1:3.arabic: الرحمن الرحيم مالك يوم الدين خالق الخير والشر خالق الجنة والنار الواحد الأحد الفرد الصمد الذي لم يتخذ صاحبة ولا ولدا الفرد الوتر عالم الغيب والشهادة الملك القدوس السلام المؤمن المهيمن العزيز الجبار المتكبر الخالق البارىء المصور الكبير المتعال المقتدر القهار الحليم الكريم أهل الثناء والمجد أعلم السر وأخفى القادر الرزاق فوق الخلق والخليقة
1:3.english: The Most Merciful (Ar-Rahman), The Especially Merciful (Ar-Rahim), Owner (Malik) of the Day of Recompense (Yawm ad-Deen), Creator (Khaliq) of good and evil, Creator (Khaliq) of Paradise and Hell, The One (Al-Wahid), The Unique (Al-Ahad), The Single (Al-Fard), The Eternal (As-Samad) who has not taken a consort nor a son, The Single (Al-Fard), The Odd (Al-Witr), Knower (Alim) of the unseen and the witnessed, The Sovereign (Al-Malik), The Holy (Al-Quddus), The Peace (As-Salam), The Faithful (Al-Mu'min), The Overseer (Al-Muhaymin), The Mighty (Al-Aziz), The Compeller (Al-Jabbar), The Supreme (Al-Mutakabbir), The Creator (Al-Khaliq), The Originator (Al-Bari'), The Fashioner (Al-Musawwir), The Great (Al-Kabir), The Exalted (Al-Muta'ali), The Powerful (Al-Muqtadir), The Subduer (Al-Qahhar), The Forbearing (Al-Halim), The Generous (Al-Karim), Possessor (Ahl) of praise and glory, Knower (A'lam) of the secret and what is more hidden, The Able (Al-Qadir), The Provider (Ar-Razzaq) above the creation and the creatures.
1:3.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter

2:16.arabic: وأما المنافقون ففروا من الزحف خوفاً من الموت فقيل لهم: "إن الموت الذين تفرون منه فإنه ملاقيكم" فإيثارهم البقاء على الشهادة استبدال الذي هو أدنى بالذي هو خير، فأولئك الذين اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى فما ربحت تجارتهم وما كانوا مهتدين، وأما المخلصون فإن الله تعالى اشترى منهم أنفسهم وأموالهم بأن لهم الجنة، فلما رأوا أنهم تركوا تمتع عشرين سنة مثلاً أو ثلاثين سنة بتمتع الأبد استبشروا ببيعهم الذي بايعوا به، فهذا بيان المزهود فيه.
2:16.english: As for the hypocrites, they fled from the battle out of fear of death, so it was said to them: "Indeed, the death from which you flee will meet you." Their preferring survival over martyrdom is exchanging that which is lower for that which is better. So those are the ones who purchased misguidance (al-ḍalālah) with guidance (al-hudā), so their trade did not profit, and they were not guided (muh'tadīn). As for the sincere ones, then Allah the Exalted purchased from them their souls (anfus) and their wealth in exchange for Paradise for them. When they saw that they left enjoyment of twenty years, for example, or thirty years for enjoyment of eternity, they rejoiced at their sale which they transacted. This is the explanation of what is renounced.
2:16.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

2:22.arabic: فانظر إلى الأرض وهى ميتة فإذا أنزل عليها الماء اهتزت وربت واخضرت وأنبتت عجائب النبات وخرجت منها أصناف الحيوانات ثم انظر كيف أحكم جوانب الأرض بالجبال الراسيات الشوامخ الصم الصلاب وكيف أودع المياه تحتها ففجر العيون وأسأل الأنهار تجرى على وجهها وأخرج من الحجارة اليابسة ومن التراب الكدر ماء رقيقا عذبا صافيا زلالا وجعل به كل شىء حى فأخرج به فنون الأشجار والنبات من حب وعنب وقضب وزيتون ونخل ورمان وفواكه كثيرة لا تحصى مختلفة الأشكال والألوان والطعوم والصفات والأرابيح يفضل بعضها على بعض فى الأكل تسقى بما
2:22.english: Then look at the Earth while it is dead, then when water is sent down upon it, it quivers, swells, and greens, and brings forth wonders of vegetation, and from it emerge various kinds of animals. Then look at how He has firmly established the sides of the Earth with the towering, lofty, solid, hard mountains, and how He has deposited waters beneath it, so He gushes forth springs, and He makes rivers flow upon its surface, and He brings forth from the dry stones and from the turbid soil water that is delicate, sweet, pure, and cool, and He makes with it every thing alive, so He brings forth with it varieties of trees and vegetation from grain, grapes, herbs, olives, date palms, pomegranates, and many fruits that cannot be enumerated, differing in shapes, colors, tastes, attributes, and fragrances, some excelling over others in eating, watered with one water and emerging from one land. If you say that their difference is due to the difference in their seeds and origins, then when was there in the seed a date palm encircled with clusters of fresh dates, and when was there in a single grain ears of corn, in each ear one hundred? Then look at the land of the deserts and search its surface and interior, and you will see it as similar soil, then when water is sent down upon it, it quivers, swells, and brings forth from every delightful pair different colors and similar vegetation and other.
2:22.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Contemplation'

2:23.arabic: وعلى الجملة فالقرآن من أوله إلى آخره محاجة مع الكفار فعمده أدلة المتكلمين في التوحيد قوله تعالى لو كان فيهما آلهة إلا الله لفسدتا وفي النبوة وإن كنتم في ريب مما نزلنا على عبدنا فأتوا بسورة من مثله وفي البعث قل يحييها الذي أنشأها أول مرة إلى غير ذلك من الآيات والأدلة ولم تزل الرسل صلوات الله عليهم يحاجون المنكرين ويجادلونهم قال تعالى: ﴿ وجادلهم بالتي هي أحسن ﴾ {} فالصحابة رضي الله عنهم أيضا كانوا يحاجون المنكرين ويجادلون ولكن عند الحاجة وكانت الحاجة إليه قليلة في زمانهم
2:23.english: And in summary, the Quran from its beginning to its end is an argumentation with the disbelievers, so the foundation of the evidences of the theologians in Oneness (Tawhid) is His saying, the Exalted: 'If there were in them (the heavens and earth) gods other than Allah, they would have been corrupted'; and in Prophethood: 'And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant, then bring a surah like it'; and in the Resurrection: 'Say: He gives them life Who created them the first time' - to other than that of the verses and evidences. And the messengers, prayers of Allah be upon them, have not ceased to argue with the deniers and debate them. He, the Exalted, said: 'And argue with them in the best manner'. So the companions, may Allah be pleased with them, also used to argue with the deniers and debate, but only when needed, and the need for it was little in their time.
2:23.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

2:25.arabic: بيان طعام أهل الجنة مذكور فى القرآن من الفواكه والطيور السمان والمن والسلوى والعسل واللبن وأصناف كثيرة لا تحصى قال الله تعالى: ﴿ كلما رزقوا فيها من ثمرة رزقا قالوا هذا الذى رزقنا من قبل وأتوا به متشابها ﴾ وذكر الله تعالى شراب أهل الجنة فى مواضع كثيرة
2:25.english: The description of the food of the people of Paradise is mentioned in the Quran from fruits and fat birds and manna and quails and honey and milk and many varieties that cannot be enumerated. Allah the Exalted said: 'Whenever they are given a provision of fruit from it, they say: "This is what we were given before." And they are given it in resemblance.' And Allah the Exalted mentioned the drink of the people of Paradise in many places.
2:25.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

2:26.arabic: وإذا قيل لهم أنفقوا مما رزقكم الله قال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا أنطعم من لو يشاء الله أطعمه ﴾ {} وقالوا أيضا ﴿ لو شاء الله ما أشركنا ولا آباؤنا ﴾ {} فانظر كيف كانوا صادقين في كلامهم وكيف هلكوا بصدقهم فسبحان من إذا شاء أهلك بالصدق وإذا شاء أسعد بالجهل يضل به كثيرا ويهدى به كثيرا فهؤلاء لما ظنوا أنهم استخدموا لأجل المساكين والفقراء أو جل الله تعالى ثم قالوا لا حظ لنا في المساكين ولا حظ لله فينا وفي أموالنا سواء أنفقنا أو أمسكنا هلكوا كما هلك الصبي لما ظن أن مقصود الوالد استخدامه لأجل العبيد ولم يشع
2:26.english: And when it is said to them: 'Spend from what Allah has provided you,' those who disbelieve say to those who believe: 'Shall we feed one whom, if Allah willed, He would have fed?' {} And they also said: 'If Allah had willed, we would not have associated partners, nor would our fathers.' {} So look how they were truthful in their speech and how they perished by their truthfulness. Glory be to the One who, when He wills, destroys with truth, and when He wills, makes happy with ignorance. He misleads many thereby and guides many thereby. So these, when they thought that they were employed for the sake of the poor and the needy, or exalted Allah, then said: 'We have no share in the poor, and Allah has no share in us or in our wealth, whether we spend or withhold,' they perished just as the boy perished when he thought that the father's purpose in employing him was for the sake of the slaves, and he did not realize that the intended purpose was the establishment of the attribute of knowledge in his self (Nafs) and its confirmation in his heart (Qalb) until that becomes the cause of his happiness in this world. Rather, that was from the father as gentleness toward him in drawing him to what contains his happiness. So this example clarifies for you the misguidance of those who went astray from this path. Therefore, this poor person who takes your wealth fulfills through the wealth the evil of miserliness and love of this world from your inner being (Batin), for it is destructive to you. He is like the cupper who extracts blood from you so that by the exit of the blood, the destructive ailment exits from your inner being (Batin). So the cupper is a servant to you, not you a servant to the cupper, nor does the cupper depart from being a servant by having a desire to do something with the blood. And since charities are purifiers for the inner beings (Bawatin) and purifiers for them from the evils of attributes, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ refrained from taking them and abstained from them[121] just as he prohibited the earnings of the cupper and called them the filth of people's wealth, and honored his household by protecting them from it[122]. And the intended purpose is that actions are effectors in the heart (Qalb) as preceded in the quarter of the destroyers, and the heart (Qalb) according to their effect is prepared to accept the...
2:26.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

2:27.arabic: ي الله عنه: ثلاث بهن ينهدم الزمان إحداهن زلة العالم. وقال ابن مسعود: سيأتي على الناس زمان تملح فيه عذوبة القلوب فلا ينتفع بالعلم يومئذ عالمه ولا متعلمه فتكون قلوب علمائهم مثل السباخ من ذوات الملح ينزل عليها قطر السماء فلا يوجد لها عذوبة وذلك إذا مالت قلوب العلماء إلى حب الدنيا وإيثارها على الآخرة فعند ذلك يسلبها الله تعالى ينابيع الحكمة ويطفىء مصابيح الهدى من قلوبهم فيخبرك عالمهم حين تلقاه أنه يخشى الله بلسانه والفجور ظاهر في عمله فما أخصب الألسن يومئذ وما أجدب القلوب فوالله الذي لا إله إلا هو م
2:27.english: From God about him: Three things by which time collapses, one of them is the slip of the scholar. And Ibn Mas'ud said: There will come upon people a time when the sweetness of hearts becomes salty, so neither its scholar nor its learner benefits from knowledge then, and the hearts of their scholars become like salt flats from those possessing salt, rain falls upon them but no sweetness is found for them, and that is when the hearts of scholars incline to love of the worldly life and prefer it over the Hereafter, then at that time God the Exalted strips them of the springs of wisdom and extinguishes the lamps of guidance from their hearts, so their scholar informs you when you meet him that he fears God with his tongue while corruption is apparent in his action, so how fertile are the tongues at that time and how barren are the hearts. By God, there is no god but Him, that is only because the teachers taught for other than God the Exalted and the learners learned for other than God the Exalted. And in the Torah and the Gospel it is written: Do not seek knowledge of what you have not known until you act upon what you have known. And Hudhayfah, may God be pleased with him, said: You are in a time where whoever leaves a tenth of what he knows perishes, and there will come a time where whoever acts upon a tenth of what he knows is saved, and that is due to the abundance of the idle. And know that the likeness of the scholar is like the judge, and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ((Judges are three: a judge who judges with truth while knowing it, that one is in Paradise; and a judge who judges with injustice while knowing or not knowing, he is in the Fire; and a judge who judges with other than what God has commanded, he is in the Fire))[161]. And Ka'b, may God have mercy on him, said: There will be in the end of time scholars who make people renounce the worldly life but do not renounce, and frighten people but do not fear, and forbid frequenting rulers but come to them, and prefer the worldly life over the Hereafter, they eat with their tongues, they draw near the rich to the exclusion of the poor, they become jealous over knowledge as women become jealous over men, one of them becomes angry at his companion if he sits with another, those are the tyrants, enemies of the Merciful. And the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ((Indeed Satan sometimes procrastinates you with knowledge, so it was said: O Messenger of God, and how is that? He said, peace and blessings be upon him: He says seek knowledge and do not act until you know, so knowledge remains saying and action remains procrastinated until he dies and has not acted))[162]. And Sari al-Saqati said: A man secluded himself for worship, he was eager in seeking outward knowledge, so I asked him and he said: I saw in a dream a speaker saying to me: Until when do you waste knowledge? May God waste you, so I said: Indeed I memorize it, so he said: Memorizing knowledge is acting upon it, so I left seeking and turned to action. And Ibn Mas'ud, may God be pleased with him, said: Knowledge is not with abundance of narration, indeed knowledge is fear (Khashyah). And al-Hasan said: Learn whatever you wish to learn, for by God God will not reward you until you act, for the foolish ones their concern is narration and the scholars their concern is guardianship (Ri'ayah). And Malik, may God have mercy on him, said:
2:27.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Book of Knowledge'

2:27.arabic: وكيف لا يبغض وهو لا ينفك عن الكذب والغيبة والغدر والخيانة والغل والحسد والنفاق والإفساد بين الناس والخديعة وهو ممن يسعون في قطع ما أمر الله به أن يوصل ويفسدون في الأرض؟ وقال تعالى "إنما السبيل على الذين يظلمون الناس ويبغون في الأرض بغير الحق" والنمام منهم. وقال ﭬ "إن من شرار الناس من اتقاه الناس لشره"[236] والنمام منهم. وقال "لا يدخل الجنة قاطع" قيل وما القاطع؟ قال "قاطع بين الناس"[237] وهو النمام وقيل قاطع الرحم.
2:27.english: And how should he not be hated when he does not desist from lying, backbiting (Ghibah), treachery, betrayal, malice, envy, hypocrisy, corruption between people, and deception? He is among those who strive to cut off what Allah has commanded to be connected and who spread corruption in the earth. And Allah the Exalted said: "Indeed, the way is only against those who wrong the people and tyrannize upon the earth without right" (Quran 42:42) - and the talebearer (Nammam) is among them. And He said: "Indeed, among the worst of people is he whom people fear for his evil" (Hadith) - and the talebearer is among them. And He said: "The cutter (Qati') will not enter Paradise." It was asked: "What is the cutter?" He said: "The one who cuts between people" - and he is the talebearer, and it is said: the one who cuts kinship ties.
2:27.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

2:29.arabic: الأصل الثاني: العلم بأنه تعالى عالم بجميع الموجودات ومحيط بكل المخلوقات لا يعزب عن علمه مثقال ذرة في الأرض ولا في السماء صادق في قوله وهو بكل شيء عليم ومرشد إلى صدقه بقوله تعالى ألا يعلم من خلق وهو اللطيف الخبير أرشدك إلى الاستدلال بالخلق على العلم بأنك لا تستريب في دلالة الخلق اللطيف والصنع المزين بالترتيب ولو في الشيء الحقير الضعيف على علم الصانع بكيفية الترتيب والترصيف فما ذكره الله سبحانه هو المنتهى في الهداية والتعريف.
2:29.english: The Second Foundation: Knowledge that He, Exalted is He, is Knower of all existents and encompasses all created beings; not even an atom's weight in the earth or in the heaven escapes His knowledge, truthful in His saying: 'And He is, of all things, Knowing (ʿAlīm).' And guiding to His truthfulness by His saying, Exalted is He: 'Does He not know, He Who created? And He is the Subtle (Al-Laṭīf), the Aware (Al-Khabīr).' He guides you to inferring from creation to knowledge that you do not doubt in the indication of the subtle (laṭīf) creation and the work adorned with arrangement, even in the insignificant, weak thing, about the Maker's knowledge of the manner of arrangement and composition. So what God, Glorified is He, has mentioned is the ultimate in guidance and definition.
2:29.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Foundations of Belief'

2:32.arabic: وقال انس حدثني رسول الله ﭬ: (إن الله عز وجل قال يا جبريل ما جزاء من سلبت كريمتيه قال سبحانك لا علم لنا الا ما علمتنا قال الله تعالى جزاؤه الخلود في داري والنظر الى وجهي[30])
2:32.english: And Anas narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: (Indeed Allah the Exalted said: O Jibril (Gabriel), what is the reward for one whose two precious things I have taken? He said: Glory be to You (Subhanaka), we have no knowledge except what You have taught us (la 'ilma lana illa ma 'allamtana). Indeed You are the All-Knowing (Al-'Alim), the All-Wise (Al-Hakim). Allah the Exalted said: His reward is eternity in My abode and gazing upon My Face[30]).
2:32.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

2:34.arabic: الآثار: قال بعض السلف: أول خطيئة هي الحسد حسد إبليس آدم عليه السلام على رتبته فأبى أن يسجد له فحمله على الحسد والمعصية. وحكي أن عون بن عبد الله دخل على الفضل بن المهلب وكان يومئذ على واسط فقال: إني أريد أن أعظك بشيء فقال: وما هو؟ قال: إياك والكبر فإنه أول ذنب عصي الله به، ثم قرأ "وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس" الآية، وإياك والحرص فإنه أخرج آدم من الجنة أمكنه الله سبحانه من جنة عرضها السموات والأرض يأكل منها إلا شجرة واحدة نهاه عنها فأكل منها فأخرجه الله تعالى منها، ثم قرأ "اهبطو
2:34.english: The Narrations: Some of the predecessors said: The first sin is envy (Hasad) - Iblis envied Adam, peace be upon him, for his rank, so he refused to prostrate to him, and it carried him to envy (Hasad) and disobedience. And it was narrated that 'Awn ibn 'Abdullah entered upon al-Fadl ibn al-Muhallab, who was then over Wasit, and said: I want to advise you with something. He said: And what is it? He said: Beware of arrogance (Kibr), for it is the first sin with which Allah was disobeyed, then he recited: "And [mention] when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam,' and they prostrated, except for Iblis; he refused and was arrogant and became of the disbelievers." And beware of greed (Hirs), for it expelled Adam from Paradise - Allah, glorified be He, had enabled him in a garden the width of the heavens and the earth, to eat from it except one tree which He forbade him from, but he ate from it, so Allah, exalted be He, expelled him from it, then he recited: "Descend from it" to the end of the verse. And beware of envy (Hasad), for indeed the son of Adam killed his brother when he envied him, then he recited: "And recite to them the story of Adam's two sons in truth," the verses. And when the companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, are mentioned, then refrain, and when predestination (Qadar) is mentioned, be silent, and when the stars are mentioned, be silent.
2:34.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

2:43.arabic: أما بعد: فإن الله تعالى جعل الزكاة إحدى مباني الإسلام وأردف بذكرها الصلاة التي هي أعلى الأعلام فقال تعالى: ﴿ وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة ﴾{البقرة: 83} وقال ﭬ: (بني الإسلام على خمس شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله وأن محمدا عبده ورسوله وإقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة[1])
2:43.english: After: Indeed Allah the Exalted made Zakah (Zakat) one of the foundations of Islam and appended to its mention the Prayer (Salah) which is the highest of the signs. So He the Exalted said: 'And establish the Prayer (Salah) and give the Zakah (Zakat)' (Al-Baqarah: 83). And He ﭬ said: 'Islam is built upon five: the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His slave and messenger, and establishing the Prayer (Salah), and giving the Zakah (Zakat)[1]'.
2:43.topic: Al-Ghazali on the outer and inner dimensions of worship, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

2:44.arabic: ومنها أن لا يخالف فعله قوله بل لا يأمر بالشيء ما لم يكن هو أول عامل به قال الله تعالى: (أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم( (البقرة: 44) وقال تعالى: (كبر مقتا عند الله أن تقولوا ما لا تفعلون( (الصف: 3) وقال تعالى في قصة شعيب: (وما أريد أن أخالفكم إلى ما أنهاكم عنه( (هود: 88) وقال تعالى: (واتقوا الله ويعلمكم الله( (البقرة: 282) وقال تعالى: (واتقوا الله واعلموا( (البقرة: 194) (واتقوا الله واسمعوا( (المائدة: 108).
2:44.english: And from them is that his action does not contradict his speech, rather he does not command something unless he is the first to act upon it. Allah the Exalted said: 'Do you command people to righteousness and forget yourselves?' (Al-Baqarah: 44) And Allah the Exalted said: 'Greatly hateful is it with Allah that you say what you do not do.' (As-Saff: 3) And Allah the Exalted said in the story of Shu'ayb: 'And I do not intend to differ from you to that which I forbid you from.' (Hud: 88) And Allah the Exalted said: 'And fear Allah (Taqwa) and Allah will teach you.' (Al-Baqarah: 282) And Allah the Exalted said: 'And fear Allah (Taqwa) and know.' (Al-Baqarah: 194) 'And fear Allah (Taqwa) and listen.' (Al-Ma'idah: 108).
2:44.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

2:44.arabic: الوظيفة الثامنة: أن يكون المعلم عاملا بعلمه فلا يكذب قوله فعله لأن العلم يدرك بالبصائر والعمل يدرك بالأبصار وأرباب الأبصار أكثر فإذا خالف العمل العلم منع الرشد وكل من تناول شيئا وقال للناس لا تتناولوه فإنه سم مهلك سخر الناس به واتهموه وزاد حرصهم على ما نهوا عنه فيقولون لولا أنه أطيب الأشياء وألذها لما كان يستأثر به ومثل المعلم المرشد من المسترشدين مثل النقش من الطين والظل من العود فكيف ينتقش الطين بما لا نقش فيه ومتى استوى الظل والعود أعوج ولذلك قيل في المعنى: لا تنه عن خلق وتأتي مثله
2:44.english: The Eighth Duty: That the teacher should act according to his knowledge, so his action does not belie his speech, because knowledge is perceived through insights (Basa'ir) and action is perceived through sights (Absar), and the people of sights are more numerous. So if action contradicts knowledge, it prevents guidance (Rushd). And whoever partakes of something and tells people not to partake of it, then it is a destroying poison; people mock him and accuse him, and their craving for what they are forbidden increases, so they say: 'If it were not the most pleasant and delightful of things, he would not monopolize it.' And the likeness of the guiding teacher from the guided is like the impression from clay and the shadow from the stick; so how can clay be impressed with what has no impression in it, and when the shadow and the stick are equal, it is crooked. Therefore, it is said in meaning: 'Do not forbid a trait and then come with its like; a great disgrace upon you if you do.' And Allah the Exalted said: 'Do you enjoin righteousness upon people and forget yourselves?' (Al-Baqarah: 44). Therefore, the burden (Wizr) of the scholar in his sins is greater than the burden of the ignorant, for many scholars stumble with his stumble and follow him ('And whoever initiates a bad practice, upon him is its burden and the burden of those who act upon it'). Therefore, said Ali, may Allah be pleased with him: 'My back is broken by two men: a scholar who is wanton and an ignorant who is ascetic.' So the ignorant deceives people with his asceticism (Tanasuk), and the scholar deceives them with his wantonness (Tahattuk). And Allah knows best.
2:44.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Book of Knowledge'

2:44.arabic: وأما الشرط الثالث وهو العدالة فقد اعتبرها قوم وقالوا ليس للفاسق أن يحتسب وربما استدلوا فيه بالنكير الوارد على من يأمر بما لا يفعله مثل قوله تعالى أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون انفسكم وقوله تعالى كبر مقتا عند الله أن تقولوا ما لا تفعلون وبما روى عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم انه قال مررت ليلة اسرى بي بقوم تقرض شفاههم بمقاريض من نار فقلت من انتم فقالوا كنا نامر بالخير ولا ناتيه وننهى عن الشر وناتيه حديث مررت ليلة أسري بي بقوم تقرض شفاههم بمقاريض من نارالحديث تقدم في العلم وبما روى أن الله تعالى أوح
2:44.english: And as for the third condition, which is righteousness (Adalah), some people have considered it and said: 'The corrupt person (Fasiq) may not perform commanding good and forbidding evil (Ihtisab).' And perhaps they argued for this with the reprimand that comes upon one who commands what he does not do, such as His saying, the Exalted: 'Do you command people to righteousness (Al-Birr) and forget yourselves while you recite the Book? Do you not then reason?' And His saying, the Exalted: 'Greatly hateful is it with Allah that you say what you do not do.' And with what was narrated from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, that he said: 'I passed by on the night of my Ascension (Isra') a people whose lips were being cut with scissors of fire, so I said: "Who are you?" They said: "We used to command good and not do it, and forbid evil and do it."' The hadith 'I passed by on the night of my Ascension a people whose lips were being cut with scissors of fire' preceded in the Book of Knowledge. And with what was narrated that Allah, the Exalted, revealed to Jesus, peace be upon him: 'Admonish yourself; if you are admonished, then admonish people, otherwise be ashamed before Me.' And perhaps they argued from the path of analogy (Qiyas) that guiding others is a branch of being guided, and likewise, rectifying others is a branch of uprightness (Istiqamah), and reform (Islah) is a purification (Zakat) from the measure of righteousness (Salah). So how can one who is not righteous (Salih) in himself reform others, and when will the shadow be straight if the stick is crooked?
2:44.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

2:45.arabic: نعم المواظبة عليه بالمجاهدة خير ولكن بالإضافة إلى تركها لا بالإضافة إلى فعلها عن طوع ولذلك قال الله تعالى "وإنها لكبيرة إلا على الخاشعين" وقال ﭬ "اعبد الله في الرضا فإن لم تستطع ففي الصبر على ما تكره خير كثير"[41] ثم لا يكن في نيل السعادة الموعودة على جسن الخلق استلذاذ الطاعة واستكراه المعصية في زمان دون زمان، بل ينبغي أن يكون ذلك على الدوام وفي جملة العمر.
2:45.english: Yes, persistence in it through struggle (Mujahadah) is good, but in comparison to abandoning it, not in comparison to performing it willingly. Therefore, Allah the Exalted said: "And indeed, it (the prayer) is burdensome except for the humble (Al-Khashi'in)" and the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Worship Allah in contentment (Rida); if you cannot, then in patience (Sabr) over what you dislike is much good." Then, in attaining the promised happiness through good character (Husn al-Khuluq), the delight (Istilthadh) in obedience and aversion (Istikrah) to sin should not be for a time only, but it should be constant and throughout the entirety of life.
2:45.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

2:48.arabic: ويوم لا تجزى نفس عن نفس شيئا
2:48.english: And a day when no soul (Nafs) will avail another soul (Nafs) anything
2:48.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

2:57.arabic: وقال تعالى في وصف الطيبات وأنزلنا عليكم المن والسلوى المن العسل والسلوى اللحم سمي سلوى لأنه يتسلى به عن جميع الإدام ولا يقوم غيره مقامه ولذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم سيد الإدام اللحم ثم قال بعد ذكر المن والسلوى كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم فاللحم والحلاوة من الطيبات
2:57.english: And Allah said in describing the good things: 'And We shaded you with clouds and sent down upon you manna and quails (al-Salwa).' The manna is honey, and the quails (al-Salwa) is meat. It is called 'salwa' because one consoles oneself (yata-salla) with it over all other dishes, and nothing else takes its place. Therefore, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'The master of dishes is meat.' Then He said after mentioning the manna and the quails (al-Salwa): 'Eat from the good things (al-Tayyibat) of what We have provided for you.' So meat and sweetness are from the good things (al-Tayyibat).
2:57.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Manners of Eating'

2:61.arabic: وأما المنافقون ففروا من الزحف خوفاً من الموت فقيل لهم: "إن الموت الذين تفرون منه فإنه ملاقيكم" فإيثارهم البقاء على الشهادة استبدال الذي هو أدنى بالذي هو خير، فأولئك الذين اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى فما ربحت تجارتهم وما كانوا مهتدين، وأما المخلصون فإن الله تعالى اشترى منهم أنفسهم وأموالهم بأن لهم الجنة، فلما رأوا أنهم تركوا تمتع عشرين سنة مثلاً أو ثلاثين سنة بتمتع الأبد استبشروا ببيعهم الذي بايعوا به، فهذا بيان المزهود فيه.
2:61.english: As for the hypocrites, they fled from the battle out of fear of death, so it was said to them: "Indeed, the death from which you flee will meet you." Their preference for survival over martyrdom is exchanging that which is lower for that which is better. Those are the ones who purchased misguidance for guidance, so their trade did not profit, and they were not guided. As for the sincere ones, Allah the Exalted purchased from them their souls (Nafs) and their wealth in exchange for Paradise for them. When they saw that they had left enjoyment of twenty years, for example, or thirty years for enjoyment of eternity, they rejoiced at their transaction which they had transacted. This is the explanation of what is renounced.
2:61.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

2:62.arabic: فختم على كل ذى حزم آمن بالله واليوم الآخر أن لا يغفل عن محاسبة نفسه والتضييق عليها في حركاتها وسكناتها وخطراتها وخطواتها فإن كل نفس من أنفاس العمر جوهرة نفيسة لا عوض لها يمكن أن يشترى بها كنز من الكنوز لا يتناهى نعيمه أبد الآباد فانقباض هذه الأنفاس ضائعة أو مصروفة إلى ما يجلب الهلاك خسران عظيم هائل لا تسمح به نفس عاقل فإذا أصبح العبد وفرغ من فريضة الصبح ينبغى أن يفرغ قلبه ساعة لمشارطه النفس كما أن التاجر عند تسليم البضاعة إلى الشريك العامل يفرغ المجلس لمشارطته فيقول للنفس ما لي بضاعة إلا العمر و
2:62.english: So it is concluded for every possessor of determination who believes in Allah and the Last Day that he should not neglect accounting his Soul (Nafs) and constraining it in its movements, stillness, fleeting thoughts, and steps. For every breath of life is a precious jewel with no substitute, through which can be purchased a treasure among treasures whose bliss is endless for all eternity. The contraction of these breaths wasted or diverted to what brings destruction is a tremendous, immense loss that no rational Soul (Nafs) would permit. When the servant wakes and finishes the obligatory dawn prayer, he should empty his Heart (Qalb) for an hour to contract with the Soul (Nafs), just as the merchant, when delivering goods to the working partner, empties the gathering to contract with him. He says to the Soul (Nafs): 'I have no merchandise except life; whenever it perishes, the capital has perished, and despair occurs regarding trade and seeking profit. This new day, Allah has granted me respite in it, postponed my term, and bestowed favor upon me. If He had taken me, I would wish to be returned to the world for a single day to work righteous deeds in it. So consider that you have died and then been returned. Beware, then beware, of wasting this day, for every breath of the breaths is a jewel of no value. And know, O Soul (Nafs), that the day and night are twenty-four hours, and it has come in the report that for the servant, with every day and night, twenty-four treasuries are spread out. He opens one of them for him, and he sees it filled with light from his good deeds that he performed in that hour, so he says: 'Indeed, those who have believed and those who were Jews and the Christians and the Sabians - whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day and does righteous deeds - they will have their reward with their Lord, and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.'
2:62.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

2:62.arabic: يفزع الناس وهم لا يفزعون ويخاف الناس وهم لا يخافون وهم أولياء الله الذين لا خوف عليهم ولاهم يحزنون فقيل من هؤلاء يا رسول الله فقال هم المتحابون في الله تعالى حديث قال أبو إدريس الخولاني لمعاذ أني احبك في الله فقال أبشر ثم أبشر فإني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول تنصب لطائفة من الناس كراسي حول العرش يوم القيامة الحديث أخرجه أحمد و الحاكم في حديث طويل أن أبا إدريس قال قلت و الله إني لأحبك في الله قال فأني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول أن المتحابين بجلال الله في ظل عرشه يوم لا ظل إ
2:62.english: The people will be terrified while they are not terrified, and the people will fear while they do not fear, and they are the allies of Allah (Awliya Allah) upon whom there is no fear nor do they grieve. It was said: 'Who are these, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'They are those who love each other for the sake of Allah, the Exalted.' A hadith: Abu Idris al-Khawlani said to Mu'adh: 'I love you for the sake of Allah.' He said: 'Rejoice, then rejoice, for I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: "Chairs will be set up for a group of people around the Throne on the Day of Resurrection."' The hadith was narrated by Ahmad and al-Hakim in a long hadith that Abu Idris said: 'I said: By Allah, I love you for the sake of Allah.' He said: 'For I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: "Those who love each other for the majesty of Allah will be in the shade of His Throne on a day when there is no shade except His shade."' Al-Hakim said: 'Authentic according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs.' And it is in al-Tirmidhi from the narration of Abu Muslim al-Khawlani from Mu'adh with the wording: 'Those who love each other for My majesty, for them are pulpits of light, and the prophets and martyrs will envy them.' He said: 'A good authentic hadith.' And in Ahmad from the hadith of Abu Malik al-Ash'ari: 'Allah has servants who are neither prophets nor martyrs, and the prophets and martyrs will envy them for their stations and their closeness to Allah.' The hadith includes: 'They love each other for the sake of Allah and are sincere to each other for His sake. Allah will place for them on the Day of Resurrection pulpits of light, making their faces light and their garments light. The people will be terrified on the Day of Resurrection, but they will not be terrified, and they are the allies of Allah (Awliya Allah) upon whom there is no fear nor do they grieve.' And in it is Shahr ibn Hawshab, who is disputed, and it was narrated by Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, and he said in it: 'Around the Throne are pulpits of light, upon them are people whose garments are light and whose faces are light. They are neither prophets nor martyrs, and the prophets and martyrs will envy them.' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, describe them to us.' He said: 'They are those who love each other for the sake of Allah, sit together for the sake of Allah, and visit each other for the sake of Allah.' The hadith of Abu Hurayrah: 'Around the Throne are pulpits of light, upon them are people whose garments are light and whose faces are light. They are neither prophets nor martyrs.' The hadith was narrated by al-Nasa'i in his Sunan al-Kubra, and its narrators are trustworthy. And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'No two people love each other for the sake of Allah except that the more beloved of them to Allah is the one with the strongest love for his companion.' The hadith: 'No two people love each other for the sake of Allah except that the more beloved of them to Allah is the one with the strongest love for his companion' was narrated by Ibn Hibban and al-Hakim from the hadith of Anas, and he said: 'Authentic chain.' And it is said: 'When two brothers in Allah, if one of them is of a higher station than the other, the other is raised with him to his station, and he joins him just as offspring join their parents and family members join each other, because brotherhood, if acquired for the sake of Allah, is not less than the brotherhood of birth.' He, the Exalted, said: 'We joined them with their descendants, and We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds.' And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'Allah, the Exalted, says: "My love is due to those who visit each other for My sake."'
2:62.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

2:68.arabic: وخمس آيات من أول الحديد[32] وثلاثا من آخر سورة الحشر[33]  وإن  قرأ  المسبعات العشر التي أهداها الخضر عليه السلام إلى إبراهيم التيمي رحمه  الله  ووصاه  أن يقولها غدوة وعشية فقد استكمل الفضل وجمع له ذلك فضيلة جملة  الأدعية  المذكورة
2:68.english: And five verses from the beginning of Al-Hadid [32] and three from the end of Surah Al-Hashr [33]. And if he recites the ten seven-times-repeated (Al-Masbi'at) that Al-Khidr (peace be upon him) gifted to Ibrahim Al-Taymi (may Allah have mercy on him) and advised him to say them morning and evening, then he has completed the virtue and gathered for himself the excellence of the entirety of the mentioned supplications.
2:68.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Book of Knowledge'

2:70.arabic: الوجه الثالث: مستنده الشك ومعناه أنا مؤمن حقا إن شاء الله إذ قال الله تعالى لقوم مخصوصين بأعيانهم: ﴿ أولئك هم المؤمنون حقا ﴾ {} فانقسموا إلى قسمين ويرجع هذا إلى الشك في كمال الإيمان لا في أصله وكل إنسان شاك في كمال إيمانه وذلك ليس بكفر والشك في كمال الإيمان حق من وجهين: أحدهما من حيث إن النفاق يزيل كمال الإيمان وهو خفي لا تتحقق البراءة منه. والثاني: أنه يكمل بأعمال الطاعات ولا يدري وجودها على الكمال أما العمل فقد قال الله تعالى: ﴿ إنما المؤمنون الذين آمنوا بالله ورسوله ثم لم يرتابوا وجاهدوا بأمو
2:70.english: The third aspect: its basis is doubt, and its meaning is 'I am truly a believer, if Allah wills (In sha' Allah)', since Allah the Exalted said to a specific people by their individuals: 'Those are the ones who are truly believers' {Quran 8:4}. They divided into two groups, and this returns to doubt in the perfection of faith (Iman), not in its foundation. Every person doubts the perfection of their faith, and that is not disbelief (Kufr). Doubt in the perfection of faith is valid from two perspectives: One, from the aspect that hypocrisy (Nifaq) removes the perfection of faith, and it is hidden—one cannot ascertain freedom from it. Two, that it is perfected by acts of obedience (Taat), and one does not know their existence in perfection. As for action, Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, the believers are those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, then have not doubted, and have struggled with their wealth and their souls (Anfus) in the cause of Allah—those are the truthful ones' {Quran 49:15}. And as for perfection, He the Exalted said: 'They said, "Call upon your Lord to make clear to us what it is. Indeed, cows look alike to us, and indeed, if Allah wills (In sha' Allah), we will be guided"' {Quran 2:70}. So His saying 'and indeed, if Allah wills (In sha' Allah), we will be guided' is an exception in guidance, even though they were guided to faith in Allah the Exalted, but they doubted the perfection of guidance, so they made an exception.
2:70.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

2:74.arabic: وقال ﭬ: (الحمد رداء الرحمن[42]) وأوحى الله تعالى الى ايوب عليه السلام: إني رضيت بالشكر مكأفاة من أوليائي في كلام طويل وأوحى الله تعالى اليه ايضا في صفة الصابرين أن دارهم دار السلام إذا دخلوها ألهمتهم الشكر وهو خير الكلام وعند الشكر استزيدهم وبالنظر إلى أزيدهم ولما نزل في الكنوز ما نزل. قال عمر رضي الله عنه: (أي المال نتخذ فقال عليه نتخذ؟ فقال عليه السلام: ليتخذ احدكم لسانا ذاكرا او قلبا شاكرا[43]). فأمر باقتناء القلب الشاكر بدلا عن المال وقال ابن مسعود الشكر نصف الايمان. (بيان حد الشكر وحقيقته)
2:74.english: And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Praise (Al-Hamd) is the garment of the Most Merciful (Ar-Rahman).' And Allah the Exalted revealed to Job (peace be upon him): 'I am pleased with gratitude (Ash-Shukr) as a reward from My friends' in a long discourse. And Allah the Exalted also revealed to him regarding the description of the patient ones that their abode is the abode of peace; when they enter it, He inspires them with gratitude (Ash-Shukr), and it is the best of speech, and through gratitude (Ash-Shukr) I increase them, and by looking at them I increase them more. And when what was revealed about treasures was revealed, Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'What wealth should we acquire?' He said to him: 'What should we acquire?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Let one of you acquire a tongue that remembers (Dhakir) or a heart that is grateful (Shaakir).' So he commanded acquiring the grateful heart (Al-Qalb Ash-Shaakir) instead of wealth. And Ibn Mas'ud said: 'Gratitude (Ash-Shukr) is half of faith (Al-Iman).' (Explanation of the limit and reality of gratitude) Know that gratitude (Ash-Shukr) is among the stations (Maqaamaat) of the travelers (As-Saalikeen), and it also consists of knowledge (Ilm), state (Haal), and action (Amal). So knowledge (Ilm) is the foundation, and it begets the state (Haal), and the state (Haal) begets the action (Amal). As for knowledge (Ilm), it is recognizing the blessing (An-Ni'mah) from the Bestower (Al-Mun'im). And the state (Haal) is the heart's (Al-Qalb) being affected by gratitude (Ash-Shukr). And the action (Amal) is affirming that with the tongue and limbs. And the heart (Al-Qalb) of the servant (Al-Abd) is like the stones or harder in hardness (Qaswa), and its hardness (Qaswa) does not depart except through weeping in the state (Haal) of fear (Al-Khawf) and gratitude (Ash-Shukr) together.
2:74.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

2:74.arabic: ولا غرو وإن كان ذلك لا يؤثر في قلبك فإن قلوب الغافلين مثل ﴿ الحجارة أو أشد قسوة وإن من الحجارة لما يتفجر منه الأنهار وإن منها لما يشقق فيخرج منه الماء وإن منها لما يهبط من خشية الله وما الله بغافل عما تعملون ﴾{}.
2:74.english: And it is not surprising if that does not affect your heart (Qalb), for the hearts (Qulub) of the heedless are like 'stones or even harder in hardness, and indeed among the stones are those from which rivers gush forth, and among them are those that split open so that water flows from them, and among them are those that fall down from fear (Khashyah) of Allah, and Allah is not unaware of what you do.'
2:74.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

2:78.arabic: وكان داخلا في معنى قوله عز وجل ﴿ ومنهم أميون لا يعلمون الكتاب إلا أمانيّ ﴾ {} يعني التلاوة المجردة وقوله عز وجل ﴿ وكأين من آية في السموات والأرض يمرون عليها وهم عنها معرضون ﴾ {} لأن القرآن هو المبين لتلك الآيات في السموات والأرض ومهما تجاوزها ولم يتأثر بها كان معرضا عنها ولذلك قيل: إن من لم يكن متصفا بأخلاق القرآن فإذا قرأ القرآن ناداه الله تعالى: مالك ولكلامي وأنت معرض عني دع عنك كلامي إن لم تتب إلي. ومثال العاصي إذا قرأ القرآن وكرره مثال من يكرر كتاب الملك في كل يوم مرات وقد كتب إليه في عمارة
2:78.english: And he was included in the meaning of His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And among them are the unlettered (Ummiyyūn) who do not know the Book except [mere] wishes (Amāniyya)' meaning mere recitation (Tilāwa) without understanding or application, and His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And how many a sign (Āya) in the heavens and the earth they pass by while they are turning away from it' because the Quran is the clarifier of those signs in the heavens and the earth, and whenever he passes by them and is not affected by them, he is turning away from them. Therefore, it is said: Indeed, whoever is not characterized by the morals of the Quran, when he recites the Quran, Allah, the Exalted, calls to him: What is your affair with My speech while you are turning away from Me? Leave My speech if you do not repent to Me. And the example of the disobedient one when he recites the Quran and repeats it is like one who repeats the king's letter every day many times, while it was written to him about building his kingdom, and he is busy destroying it and confines himself to studying his letter. Perhaps if he abandoned the study during the disobedience, he would be farther from mockery and deserving of wrath. Therefore, Yusuf ibn Asbāṭ said: I intend to recite the Quran, but when I remember what is in it, I fear the wrath, so I turn to glorification (Tasbīḥ) and seeking forgiveness (Istighfār). And the one who turns away from acting upon it is intended by His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'So they threw it behind their backs and purchased with it a small price, and wretched is that which they purchased.' Therefore, the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said: 'Recite the Quran as long as your hearts (Qulūb) are in harmony with it and your skins (Julūd) soften for it, but when you differ, you are not reciting it, and in some versions: when you differ, then rise from it.'
2:78.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

2:82.arabic: وقال أبو طالب المكي العمل بالجوارح من الإيمان ولا يتم دونه وادعى الإجماع فيه واستدل بأدلة تشعر بنقيض غرضه كقوله تعالى الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات إذ هذا يدل على أن العمل وراء الإيمان لا من نفس الإيمان وإلا فيكون العمل في حكم المعاد والعجب أنه ادعى الإجماع في هذا وهو مع ذلك ينقل قوله ﭬ: (لا يكفر أحد إلا بعد جحوده لما أقرّ به[51]) وينكر على المعتزلة قولهم بالتخليد في النار بسبب الكبائر والقائل بهذا قائل بنفس مذهب المعتزلة إذ يقال له من صدق بقلبه وشهد بلسانه ومات في الحال فهل هو في الجنة فلا بد أن
2:82.english: And Abu Talib al-Makki said: 'Action with the limbs (al-a'mal bil-jawarih) is from faith (al-iman) and it is not complete without it,' and he claimed consensus (ijma') in this and argued with evidences that suggest the opposite of his purpose, such as His saying, the Exalted: 'And those who believe and do righteous deeds (alladhina amanu wa 'amilu al-salihat)' - since this indicates that action is beyond faith, not from the essence of faith itself, otherwise action would be in the position of repetition. And it is astonishing that he claimed consensus in this while also transmitting his saying, peace be upon him: 'No one becomes an unbeliever except after denying what he affirmed,' and he denies the Mu'tazilites' statement of eternal punishment (al-takhleed) in the Fire due to major sins. And the one who says this is saying the same doctrine as the Mu'tazilites, for it is said to him: 'One who affirms with his heart (qalb) and testifies with his tongue and dies immediately - is he in Paradise?' He must necessarily say yes, and in this is a ruling on the existence of faith without action.
2:82.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

2:83.arabic: أما بعد: فإن الله تعالى جعل الزكاة إحدى مباني الإسلام وأردف بذكرها الصلاة التي هي أعلى الأعلام فقال تعالى: ﴿ وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة ﴾{البقرة: 83} وقال ﭬ: (بني الإسلام على خمس شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله وأن محمدا عبده ورسوله وإقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة[1]) وشدد الوعيد على المقصرين فيها فقال: ﴿ والذين يكنزون الذهب والفضة ولا ينفقونها في سبيل الله فبشرهم بعذاب أليم ﴾{التوبة: 34} ومعنى الإنفاق في سبيل الله إخراج حق الزكاة
2:83.english: After that: Indeed, Allah the Exalted made Zakat (obligatory almsgiving) one of the foundations of Islam and paired its mention with the Prayer (Salah) which is the highest of the signs. So He the Exalted said: 'And establish the Prayer (Salah) and give the Zakat (obligatory almsgiving)' (Al-Baqarah: 83). And He (the Prophet) said: 'Islam is built upon five: the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His slave and messenger, establishing the Prayer (Salah), giving the Zakat (obligatory almsgiving) [1].' And He intensified the threat against those who are negligent in it, saying: 'And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah, give them tidings of a painful punishment' (At-Tawbah: 34). And the meaning of spending in the way of Allah is the extraction of the right of Zakat (obligatory almsgiving).
2:83.topic: Al-Ghazali on the outer and inner dimensions of worship, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

2:86.arabic: وهؤلاء هم الذين اشتروا الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة فخسرت صفقتهم وقيل لمن قصد إرشادهم ﴿ فأعرض عمن تولى عن ذكرنا ولم يرد إلا الحياة الدنيا ذلك مبلغهم من العلم ﴾ {} وهذه الحالة علامتها اليأس والقنوط والغرور بالأماني وهو غاية الحمق كما قال ﭬ: (الكيس من دان نفسه وعمل لما بعد الموت والأحمق من اتبع نفسه هواها وتمنى على الله[17]) وصاحب هذه الحالة إذا وعظ قال أنا مشتاق إلى التوبة ولكنها قد تعذرت على فلست أطمع فيها أو لم يكن مشتاقا إلى التوبة ولكن قال إن الله غفور رحيم كريم فلا حاجة به إلى توبتي وهذا المسكين قد
2:86.english: And these are those who have purchased the worldly life (al-hayat al-dunya) with the Hereafter (al-akhirah), so their transaction has incurred loss, and it was said to the one who intended to guide them: 'So turn away from whoever turns away from Our Remembrance (Dhikr) and desires nothing but the worldly life. That is the extent of their knowledge.' And this condition's sign is despair (al-ya's) and hopelessness (al-qunut) and delusion with hopes, which is the utmost foolishness (al-hamq), as he (the Prophet) said: 'The intelligent one (al-kayyis) is he who holds his Soul (Nafs) accountable and works for what is after death, and the foolish one (al-ahmaq) is he who follows his Soul's (Nafs) desire (hawa) and makes wishes upon Allah.' And the possessor of this condition, when admonished, says: 'I am longing for repentance (tawbah), but it has become impossible for me, so I do not hope for it,' or he was not longing for repentance but said: 'Indeed, Allah is Forgiving (ghafur), Merciful (rahim), Generous (karim), so He has no need for my repentance.' And this wretched one has become his intellect (aql) weak for his lust (shahwah), so he does not employ his intellect except in deducing subtle stratagems through which he attains the fulfillment of his lust. Indeed, his intellect has become in the hands of his lusts like a Muslim captive in the hands of the disbelievers (kuffar); they enslave him in tending pigs, guarding wines, and carrying them. And his place with Allah the Exalted is the place of one who subdues a Muslim and delivers him to the disbelievers and makes him a captive among them, because by his atrocious offense, he resembles one who enslaved what had the right not to be enslaved and empowered what had the right not to be empowered over it. And indeed, the Muslim deserved to be dominant because of what is in him of knowledge of Allah and the motivator of religion (ba'ith al-din), and indeed, the disbeliever deserved to be dominated over because of what is in him of ignorance of religion and the motivator of the devils (ba'ith al-shayatin).
2:86.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

2:86.arabic: فانظر كيف انقلب الجاهلون وانكبوا على وجوههم انكباب العميان فأقبلوا على طلب كمال القدرة بالجاه والمال، وهو الكمال الذي لا يسلم وإن سلم فلا بقاء له، وأعرضوا عن كمال الحرية والعلم الذي إذا حصل كان أبدياً لا انقطاع له، وهؤلاء هم الذين اشتروا الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة فلا جرم لا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينصرون، وهم الذين لم يفهموا قوله تعالى "المال والبنون زينة الحياة الدنيا والباقيات الصالحات خير عند ربك ثواباً وخير أملاً" فالعلم والحرية هي الباقيات الصالحات التي تبقى كمالاً في النفس، والمال والجاه هو ال
2:86.english: Look how the ignorant have turned and fallen on their faces like the falling of the blind, so they turned to seeking perfection of power through status and wealth, which is the perfection that does not remain safe and even if it remains safe, it has no permanence, and they turned away from the perfection of freedom and knowledge which, when attained, is eternal with no cessation. And these are the ones who purchased the worldly life with the Hereafter, so it is no wonder that the punishment is not lightened for them nor are they helped. And they are the ones who did not understand His saying, the Exalted: 'Wealth and children are adornment of the worldly life, and the enduring righteous deeds are better with your Lord for reward and better for hope.' So knowledge and freedom are the enduring righteous deeds that remain as perfection in the soul (Nafs), and wealth and status are what perish in proximity, and it is as Allah, the Exalted, has likened it where He said: 'The likeness of the worldly life is as water which We send down from the sky...' the verse. And He, the Exalted, said: 'And strike for them the likeness of the worldly life as water which We send down from the sky...' until His saying: '...then it becomes dry stubble scattered by the winds.' And everything that the winds of death scatter is the flower of the worldly life, and everything that death does not cut off is the enduring righteous deeds.
2:86.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

2:86.arabic: المثال الأول غرور الكفار، فمنهم من غرته الحياة الدنيا ومنهم من غره بالله الغرور، أما الذين غرتهم الحياة الدنيا: فهم الذين قالوا: النقد خير من النسيئة والدنيا نقد والآخرة نيسئة فهي إذن خير فلا بد من إيثارها، وقالوا: اليقين خير من الشك ولذات الدنيا يقين ولذات الآخرة شك فلا تترك اليقين بالشك. وهذه أقيسة فاسدة تشبه قياس إبليس حيث قال "أنا خير منه خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين" وإلى هؤلاء الإشارة بقوله تعالى "أولئك الذين اشتروا الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة فلا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينصرون" وعلاج هذا الغرور
2:86.english: The first example: the delusion (Ghurur) of the disbelievers (Kuffar). Among them are those deluded by the worldly life (Al-Hayat Al-Dunya), and among them are those deluded by Allah's delusion. As for those deluded by the worldly life: they are those who said: 'Cash (Naqd) is better than credit (Nasi'ah), and the world (Al-Dunya) is cash and the Hereafter (Al-Akhirah) is credit, so it is therefore better and must be preferred.' And they said: 'Certainty (Yaqin) is better than doubt (Shakk), and the pleasures of the world are certain and the pleasures of the Hereafter are doubtful, so do not abandon certainty for doubt.' And these are corrupt analogies (Aqisah Fasidah) resembling the analogy of Iblis when he said, 'I am better than him; You created me from fire and created him from clay.' And to these is the reference in His saying, the Exalted: 'Those are the ones who have purchased the worldly life [in exchange] for the Hereafter, so the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be aided.' And the treatment for this delusion is either through affirmation of faith (Tasdiq Al-Iman) or through proof (Burhan). As for affirmation through mere faith, it is to believe Allah, the Exalted, in His saying, 'Whatever you have will end, but what Allah has is lasting,' and in His saying, the Mighty and Majestic, 'And what is with Allah is better,' and His saying, 'And the Hereafter is better and more enduring,' and His saying, 'And the worldly life is not but the enjoyment of delusion,' and His saying, 'So let not the worldly life delude you.' And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) informed groups of disbelievers of this, so they imitated him, believed him, and had faith in him without demanding proof. And among them were those who said: 'I adjure you by Allah, has Allah sent you as a messenger?' He would say, 'Yes,' so they would believe. And this is the faith of the common people, and it exits from delusion, and this is placed in the position of a child believing his father that attending the school is better than attending the playground, even though he does not know the aspect of its being better. And as for knowledge through clarification and proof, it is to know the aspect of corruption of this analogy that Satan has organized in his heart (Qalb), for every deluded person has a cause for his delusion, and that cause is evidence, and every evidence is a type of analogy that occurs in the soul (Nafs) and begets tranquility (Sukun) towards it, even if its possessor is not aware of it nor able to organize it with the words of the scholars. So the analogy that Satan has organized has two foundations: 'One of them' is that the world is cash and the Hereafter is credit, and this is correct; 'and the other' is his saying: 'Cash is better than credit,' and this is the place.
2:86.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

2:86.arabic: ثم حرمتهم السعادة أبد الآباد. فهم على فراقها يتحسرون ومن مكايدها يستغيثون ولا يغاثون. بل يقال لهم "اخسئوا فيها ولا تكلمون. أولئك الذين اشتروا الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة فلا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينصرون". وإذا عظمت غوائل الدنيا وشرورها فلا بد أولاً من معرفة حقيقة الدنيا وما هي؟ وما الحكمة في خلقها مع عداوتها؟ وما مدخل غرورها وشرورها؟ فإن من لا يعرف الشر لا يتقيه ويوشك أن يقع فيه.
2:86.english: Then it deprived them of happiness for all eternity. They lament over its departure and cry for help from its deceits, but they are not helped. Rather, it is said to them: "Be driven away therein and do not speak. Those are the ones who have purchased the worldly life (al-Dunya) in exchange for the Hereafter (al-Akhirah), so the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be aided." And when the calamities and evils of the worldly life (al-Dunya) become great, it is necessary first to know the reality of the worldly life (al-Dunya) and what it is? And what is the wisdom in creating it despite its enmity? And what is the entry point of its deception and evils? For whoever does not know evil does not guard against it and is likely to fall into it.
2:86.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of the World'

2:86.arabic: فبهذه العلامات وأمثالها تتبين سريرة الباطن. ومهما رأيت العلماء يتغايرون ويتحاسدون ولا يتوانسون ولا يتعاونون فاعلم أنهم قد اشتروا الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة فهم الخاسرون. اللهم ارحمنا بلطفك يا أرحم الراحمين.
2:86.english: Through these signs and their like, the inner secret (سريرة الباطن) becomes clear. Whenever you see scholars being hostile to each other and envying one another, and not being intimate with each other nor cooperating with each other, then know that they have purchased the life of this world (الحياة الدنيا) in exchange for the Hereafter (الآخرة), so they are the losers. O Allah, have mercy upon us with Your gentleness, O Most Merciful of the merciful.
2:86.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

2:89.arabic: قال ابن عباس: كانت اليهود قبل أن يبعث النبي ﷺ إذا قاتلوا قوماً قالوا نسألك بالنبي الذي وعدتنا أن ترسله وبالكتاب الذي تنزله إلا ما نصرتنا. فكانوا ينصرون. فلما جاء النبي ﷺ من ولد إسماعيل عليه السلام عرفوه وكفروا به بعد معرفتهم إياه فقال تعالى "وكانوا من قبل يستفتحون على الذين كفروا فلما جاءهم ما عرفوا كفروا به" إلى قوله "أن يكفروا بما أنزل الله بغياً" أي حسداً.
2:89.english: Ibn Abbas said: The Jews, before the Prophet (peace be upon him) was sent, when they fought a people, would say: 'We ask You by the Prophet whom You promised to send us and by the Book which You will reveal, unless You grant us victory.' So they would be granted victory. Then when the Prophet (peace be upon him) came from the descendants of Ishmael (upon him be peace), they recognized him and disbelieved in him after their recognition of him. So Allah the Exalted said: 'And they used to, from before, seek victory over those who disbelieved. Then when came to them what they recognized, they disbelieved in it' to His saying 'that they disbelieve in what Allah has sent down out of envy (Baghya)' meaning envy (Hasad).
2:89.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

2:89.arabic: ثم كان منهم من منعه الكبر عن الفكر والمعرفة فجهل كونه ﭬ محقاً، ومنهم من عرف ومنعه الكبر عن الاعتراف قال الله تعالى مخبراً عنهم "فلما جاءهم ما عرفوا كفروا به" وقال "وجحدوا بها واستيقنتها أنفسهم ظلماً وعلوا" وهذا الكبر قريب من التكبر على الله عز وجل وإن كان دونه، ولكنه تكبر على قبول أمر الله والتواضع لرسوله.
2:89.english: Then among them were those whom arrogance prevented from reflection and knowledge, so they were ignorant of his (peace be upon him) being truthful; and among them were those who knew but arrogance prevented them from acknowledgment. Allah the Exalted said informing about them: "And when came to them what they recognized, they disbelieved in it" and said: "And they denied them while their souls were convinced of them, out of injustice and arrogance." And this arrogance is close to arrogance against Allah the Mighty and Majestic, even if it is less than it, but it is arrogance against accepting the command of Allah and humbling oneself to His Messenger.
2:89.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

2:89.arabic: وإنما يضاعف عذاب العالم في معصيته لأنه عصى من علم ولذلك قال الله عز وجل: (إن المنافقين في الدرك الأسفل من النار( (النساء:145). لأنهم جحدوا بعد العلم وجعل اليهود شرا من النصارى مع أنهم ما جعلوا لله سبحانه ولدا ولا قالوا إنه ثالث ثلاثة إلا أنهم أنكروا بعد المعرفة إذ قال الله (يعرفونه كما يعرفون أبناءهم( (البقرة:146) (الأنعام:20). وقال تعالى: (فلما جاءهم ما عرفوا كفروا به فلعنة الله على الكافرين( (البقرة:89). وقال تعالى في قصة بلعام بن باعوراء (واتل عليهم نبأ الذي آتيناه آياتنا فانسلخ منها فأتبعه ا
2:89.english: And indeed, the punishment of the scholar in his disobedience is multiplied because he disobeyed from knowledge. Therefore, Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire' (An-Nisa: 145). Because they denied after knowledge. And He made the Jews worse than the Christians, even though they did not make for Allah, the Glorified, a son, nor did they say He is the third of three, except that they rejected after recognition (Ma'rifah), as Allah said: 'They recognize him as they recognize their sons' (Al-Baqarah: 146) (Al-An'am: 20). And He the Exalted said: 'So when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of Allah be upon the disbelievers' (Al-Baqarah: 89). And He the Exalted said in the story of Balaam son of Beor: 'And recite to them the news of him to whom We gave Our signs, but he detached himself from them; so Satan pursued him, and he became of the deviators' (Al-A'raf: 175) until He said: 'So his example is like that of the dog: if you chase him, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants' (Al-A'raf: 176). Likewise is the wicked scholar, for Balaam was given the Book of Allah the Exalted, but he inclined to desires, so he was likened to the dog, meaning whether he was given wisdom or not, he pants toward desires.
2:89.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

2:89.arabic: حديث ابن عباس قوله كانت اليهود قبل أن يبعث النبي ﭬ إذا قاتلوا قوما قالوا نسألك. بالنبي الذي وعدتنا أن ترسله الحديث في نزول قوله تعالى وكانوا من قبل يستفتحون على الذين كفروا أخرجه ابن إسحاق في السيرة فيما بلغه عن عكرمة أو عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس أن اليهود كانوا يستفتحون على الأوس والخزرج برسول الله ﭬ فذكره نحوه وهو منقطع.
2:89.english: The hadith of Ibn Abbas, his statement: The Jews, before the Prophet (peace be upon him) was sent, when they fought a people, they would say: We ask you by the Prophet whom you promised to send us. The hadith regarding the revelation of His saying, the Exalted: 'And they had been, from before, seeking victory over those who disbelieved.' It was reported by Ibn Ishaq in the Sirah (Biography) in what reached him from Ikrimah or from Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas that the Jews were seeking victory over the Aws and the Khazraj by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), and he mentioned it similarly, and it is disconnected.
2:89.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

2:90.arabic: وقال تعالى "وكانوا من يقبل يستفتحون على الذين كفروا فلما جاءهم ما عرفوا كفروا به" إلى قوله "أن يكفروا بما أنزل الله بغياً" أي حسداً.
2:90.english: And Allah said: "And they were from those who used to seek victory over those who disbelieved, but when came to them what they recognized, they disbelieved in it" up to His saying: "that they disbelieve in what Allah has sent down out of envy (Baghya)" meaning envy (Hasad).
2:90.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

2:93.arabic: وقوله تعالى ﴿ وأشربوا في قلوبهم العجل بكفرهم ﴾ {} أي حب العجل فحذف الحب
2:93.english: And His saying, the Exalted: 'And they were made to drink in their hearts the calf due to their disbelief' (Quran 2:93) {} meaning the love of the calf, so 'the love' was omitted.
2:93.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

2:94.arabic: وقال البويطي لبعض الزهاد: أتحب الموت؟ فكأنه توقف، فقال: لو كنت صادقاً لأحببته. وتلا قوله تعالى: "فتمنوا الموت إن كنتم صادقين" فقال الرجل: فقد قال النبي ﭬ: "لا يتمنين أحدكم الموت" فقال: إنما قاله لضر نزل به لأن الرضا بقضاء الله تعالى أفضل من طلب الفرار منه.
2:94.english: And Al-Buwayti said to some of the ascetics: 'Do you love death?' It was as if he hesitated, so he said: 'If you were truthful, you would love it.' And he recited the saying of Allah the Exalted: 'Then wish for death if you are truthful.' So the man said: 'But the Prophet ﷬ said: "Let none of you wish for death."' So he said: 'He only said it due to a harm that had befallen him because contentment (Rida) with the decree (Qada) of Allah the Exalted is better than seeking escape from it.'
2:94.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

2:96.arabic: اعلم أن الناس في ذلك يتفاوتون. فمنهم من يأمل البقاء ويشتهى ذلك أبدا قال الله تعالى: ﴿ يود أحدهم لو يعمر ألف سنة ﴾  {}.  ومنهم  من  يأمل  البقاء  إلى الهرم وهو أقصى العمر الذي شاهده ورآه وهو الذي  يحب  الدنيا  حبا  شديدا.  قال رسول الله ﭬ: (الشيخ شاب في حب طلب الدنيا وإن  التفت  ترقوتاه  من  الكبر  إلا الذين اتقوا وقليل ما هم[28]).
2:96.english: Know that people vary in this matter. Among them are those who hope for survival and desire that eternally. Allah the Exalted said: 'He would wish that he could be granted a life of a thousand years' (Quran 2:96). And among them are those who hope for survival until old age, which is the maximum lifespan he has witnessed and seen, and he is the one who loves the worldly life (Dunya) with intense love. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'The old man is young in the love of seeking the worldly life (Dunya), even if his collarbones have turned from old age, except those who have been God-conscious (Taqwa) and few are they.'
2:96.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Book of Repentance'

2:104.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
2:104.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Whatever is in the Quran of 'O you who have believed' is in the Torah 'O you poor ones (al-Masakin)'.
2:104.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

2:109.arabic: ولعلك تقول ليت النعمة كانت تزول عن المحسود بحسدي. وهذا غاية الجهل فإنه بلاء تشتهيه أولاً لنفسك، فإنك أيضاً لا تخلو عن عدو يحسدك، فلو كانت النعمة تزول بالحسد لم يبق لله تعالى عليك نعمة ولا على أحد من الخلق ولا نعمة الإيمان أيضاً، لأن الكفار يحسدون المؤمنين على الإيمان. قال الله تعالى "ود كثير من أهل الكتاب لو يردونكم من بعد إيمانكم كفاراً حسداً من عند أنفسهم" إذ ما يريد الحسود لا يكون. نعم هو يضل بإرادته الضلال لغيره فإن أراد الكفر كفر. فمن اشتهى أن تزول النعمة عن المحسود بالحسد فكأنما يريد أن يس
2:109.english: And perhaps you say: 'Would that the blessing (Nimah) were removed from the envied one by my envy.' This is the utmost ignorance, for it is a calamity (Bala') you first desire for yourself, since you too are not free from an enemy who envies you. If the blessing (Nimah) were removed by envy, there would remain for you no blessing (Nimah) from Allah the Exalted, nor for anyone among creation, nor even the blessing (Nimah) of faith (Iman), because the disbelievers (Kuffar) envy the believers (Mu'minun) for faith (Iman). Allah the Exalted said: 'And many of the People of the Book wish they could turn you back to disbelief after your faith, out of envy from themselves, after the truth has become clear to them. But pardon and overlook until Allah brings His command. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.' For what the envier (Hasud) desires does not come to be. Yes, he leads astray with his desire for misguidance (Dhalal) for others; if he desires disbelief (Kufr), he disbelieves. So whoever desires that the blessing (Nimah) be removed from the envied one by envy is as if he wants to strip away the blessing (Nimah) of faith (Iman) by the envy of the disbelievers (Kuffar), and likewise all other blessings (Nimam).
2:109.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

2:109.arabic: وقد تسمى المنافسة حسداً والحسد منافسة ويوضع أحد اللفظين موضع الآخر، ولا حجر في الأسامي بعد فهم المعاني: وقد قال ﭬ "إن المؤمن يغبط والمنافق يحسد"[101]. فأما الأول فهو حرام بكل حال، إلا نعمة أصابها فاجر أو كافر وهو يستعين بها على تهييج الفتنة وإفساد ذات البين وإيذاء الحق، فلا يضرك كراهتك لها ومحبتك لزوالها، فإنك لا تحب زوالها من حيث هي نعمة بل من حيث هي آلة الفساد، ولو أمنت فساده لم يغمك بنعمته، ويدل على تحريم الحسد الأخبار التي نقلناها وأن هذه الكراهة تسخط لقضاء الله في تفضيل بعض عباده على بعض، و
2:109.english: And competition may be called envy (Hasad) and envy (Hasad) may be called competition, and one of the two terms may be placed in the position of the other, and there is no restriction in names after understanding the meanings: and the Prophet ﷺ said, "The believer envies (Yagbit) and the hypocrite envies (Yahsud)"[101]. As for the first, it is forbidden in every case, except for a blessing that a wicked person or disbeliever attains, and he uses it to stir up strife (Fitnah) and corrupt relationships (Dhat al-Bayn) and harm the truth, so your dislike of it and your love for its removal does not harm you, for you do not love its removal inasmuch as it is a blessing but inasmuch as it is an instrument of corruption, and if you were secure from his corruption, his blessing would not grieve you. And what indicates the prohibition of envy (Hasad) are the reports we have transmitted and that this dislike is displeasure with the decree (Qada) of Allah in preferring some of His servants over others, and there is no excuse or concession in that, and what sin exceeds your dislike of a Muslim's comfort without you having any harm from it? And to this the Quran alluded by His saying, "If good touches you, it distresses them, and if evil befalls you, they rejoice at it," and this rejoicing is gloating (Shamatah) and envy (Hasad) and gloating (Shamatah) are concomitant. And Allah the Exalted said, "And many of the People of the Book wish they could turn you back to disbelief after your belief, out of envy (Hasad) from themselves." So Allah the Exalted informed that their love for the removal of the blessing of faith is envy (Hasad). And He the Mighty and Majestic said, "They wish you would disbelieve as they have disbelieved, so you would be equal." And Allah the Exalted mentioned the envy (Hasad) of the brothers of Joseph, peace be upon him, and expressed what was in their hearts by His saying, "When they said, 'Joseph and his brother are more beloved to our father than we, while we are a clan. Indeed, our father is in clear error. Kill Joseph or cast him out to [another] land; the countenance of your father will [then] be only for you.'" So when they disliked their father's love for him and it distressed them and they loved its removal from him, they concealed him from him. And He said, "And they will not find within their breasts any need for that which they have been given," meaning their breasts do not constrict with it nor do they grieve, so He praised them for the absence of envy (Hasad). And He said in the context of reproach, "Or do they envy (Yahsudun) people for what Allah has given them of His bounty?" And He said, "Mankind was [of] one religion," up to His saying, "Except those to whom it was given after clear proofs had come to them, out of jealousy (Baghyan) among themselves." It is said in the interpretation: envy (Hasad). And He said, "And they did not become divided until after knowledge had come to them out of jealousy (Baghyan) among themselves." So Allah sent down knowledge to gather them and unite them upon His obedience, and He commanded them to unite through knowledge, but they envied (Tahasadu) and differed when each one of them wanted to be alone with leadership (Riyasah) and acceptance of speech, so some of them refuted others. Ibn Abbas said: The Jews, before the Prophet ﷺ was sent, when they fought a people, said, 'We ask you by the Prophet who...'
2:109.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

2:110.arabic: أما بعد: فإن الله تعالى جعل الزكاة إحدى مباني الإسلام وأردف بذكرها الصلاة التي هي أعلى الأعلام فقال تعالى: ﴿ وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة ﴾{البقرة: 83} وقال ﭬ: (بني الإسلام على خمس شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله وأن محمدا عبده ورسوله وإقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة[1]) وشدد الوعيد على المقصرين فيها فقال: ﴿ والذين يكنزون الذهب والفضة ولا ينفقونها في سبيل الله فبشرهم بعذاب أليم ﴾{التوبة: 34} ومعنى الإنفاق في سبيل الله إخراج حق الزكاة
2:110.english: After that: Indeed, Allah the Exalted made Zakat (obligatory almsgiving) one of the foundations of Islam and paired its mention with the Prayer (Salah) which is the highest of the signs. So He the Exalted said: 'And establish the Prayer (Salah) and give the Zakat (obligatory almsgiving)' (Al-Baqarah: 83). And He (the Prophet) said: 'Islam is built upon five: the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His servant and messenger, and establishing the Prayer (Salah), and giving the Zakat (obligatory almsgiving).' And He intensified the threat against those who are negligent in it, saying: 'And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah, then give them tidings of a painful punishment' (At-Tawbah: 34). And the meaning of spending in the way of Allah is the extraction of the right of Zakat (obligatory almsgiving).
2:110.topic: Al-Ghazali on the outer and inner dimensions of worship, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

2:112.arabic: يفزع الناس وهم لا يفزعون ويخاف الناس وهم لا يخافون وهم أولياء الله الذين لا خوف عليهم ولاهم يحزنون فقيل من هؤلاء يا رسول الله فقال هم المتحابون في الله تعالى حديث قال أبو إدريس الخولاني لمعاذ أني احبك في الله فقال أبشر ثم أبشر فإني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول تنصب لطائفة من الناس كراسي حول العرش يوم القيامة الحديث أخرجه أحمد و الحاكم في حديث طويل أن أبا إدريس قال قلت و الله إني لأحبك في الله قال فأني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول أن المتحابين بجلال الله في ظل عرشه يوم لا ظل إ
2:112.english: The people will be terrified while they are not terrified, and the people will fear while they do not fear, and they are the allies (Awliya) of Allah upon whom there is no fear nor do they grieve. It was said: Who are these, O Messenger of Allah? He said: They are those who love one another for the sake of Allah the Exalted. Hadith: Abu Idris al-Khawlani said to Mu'adh: Indeed I love you for the sake of Allah. He said: Rejoice, then rejoice, for indeed I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: Chairs will be set up for a group of people around the Throne on the Day of Resurrection. The hadith was narrated by Ahmad and al-Hakim in a long hadith that Abu Idris said: I said: By Allah, indeed I love you for the sake of Allah. He said: For indeed I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: Those who love one another for the majesty of Allah will be in the shade of His Throne on a day when there is no shade except His shade. Al-Hakim said: Authentic according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, and it is in al-Tirmidhi from the narration of Abu Muslim al-Khawlani from Mu'adh with the wording: Those who love one another for My majesty, for them are pulpits of light, and the prophets and martyrs will envy them. He said: A good authentic hadith. And in Ahmad from the hadith of Abu Malik al-Ash'ari: Indeed Allah has servants who are neither prophets nor martyrs, and the prophets and martyrs will envy them for their stations and their nearness to Allah. The hadith includes: They love one another for the sake of Allah and are sincere with one another for His sake. Allah will place for them on the Day of Resurrection pulpits of light, making their faces light and their garments light. The people will be terrified on the Day of Resurrection while they are not terrified, and they are the allies (Awliya) of Allah upon whom there is no fear nor do they grieve. And in it is Shahr ibn Hawshab, who is disputed, and it was narrated by Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, and he said in it: Around the Throne are pulpits of light, upon them are people whose garments are light and whose faces are light, they are neither prophets nor martyrs, and the prophets and martyrs will envy them. So they said: O Messenger of Allah, describe them for us. He said: They are those who love one another for the sake of Allah, and those who sit together for the sake of Allah, and those who visit one another for the sake of Allah. Hadith of Abu Hurayrah: Indeed around the Throne are pulpits of light, upon them are people whose garments are light and whose faces are light, they are neither prophets nor martyrs. The hadith was narrated by al-Nasa'i in his Sunan al-Kubra and its narrators are trustworthy. And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: No two people love one another for the sake of Allah except that the more beloved of them to Allah is the one with the strongest love for his companion. Hadith: No two people love one another for the sake of Allah except that the more beloved of them to Allah is the one with the strongest love for his companion. Narrated by Ibn Hibban and al-Hakim from the hadith of Anas, and he said: Authentic chain. And it is said: The two brothers in Allah, if one of them is of a higher station than the other, the other is raised with him to his station, and he is attached to him just as offspring are attached to parents and family members to one another, because brotherhood, if acquired for the sake of Allah, is not less than brotherhood of birth. The Exalted said: We joined them with their descendants, and We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds. And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Indeed Allah the Exalted says: My love is due to those who visit one another for My sake and
2:112.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'
