2:116.arabic: أنه فيماذا يتفكر لم يقدر عليه  لأن  مجارى  الفكر  غير  محصورة وثمراته غير متناهية نعم نحن نجتهد في ضبط مجاريه بالإضافة  إلى  مهمات  العلوم الدينية وبالإضافة إلى الأحوال التى هى مقامات السالكين ويكون ذلك  ضبطا  جمليا فإن تفصيل ذلك يستدعى شرح العلوم كلها وجملة هذه  الكتب  كالشرح  لبعضها  فإنها مشتملة على علوم تلك العلوم تستفاد من أفكار مخصوصة فلنشر إلى ضبط الجامع  فيها ليحصل الوقوف على مجارى الفكر.                              بيان مجارى الفكر أعلم أن الفكر قد يجرى في أمر يتعلق بالدين وقد يجرى  في
2:116.english: That in what to think, he cannot encompass it because the channels of thought are not limited and its fruits are endless. Yes, we strive to regulate its channels in addition to the important matters of the religious sciences and in addition to the states which are the stations of the travelers (Salikeen), and that will be a general regulation, for detailing that requires explaining all the sciences, and the entirety of these books is like an explanation of some of them, for they contain the sciences of those sciences derived from specific thoughts. So let us proceed to regulating the comprehensive in them to achieve understanding of the channels of thought. Explanation of the Channels of Thought: Know that thought may run in a matter related to religion and may run in what is related to non-religion, and our aim is what relates to religion, so we leave the other division and concern ourselves with religion, the transaction (Mu'amalah) that is between the servant and the Lord, Exalted is He. So all the thoughts of the servant either relate to the servant and his attributes and his states, or relate to the Worshipped One and His attributes and His actions; it is not possible to go beyond these two divisions. And what relates to the servant is either a consideration of what is beloved to the Lord, Exalted is He, or of what is disliked, and there is no need for thought in other than these two divisions. And what relates to the Lord, Exalted is He, is either a consideration of His Essence and His attributes and His Beautiful Names, or it is in His actions and His dominion and His sovereignty and all that is in the heavens and the earth and what is between them. And it becomes clear to you the confinement of thought in these divisions by an example, which is that the state of those who walk to Allah, Exalted is He, and those who yearn for His meeting, relates to his Beloved or relates to himself. So if he thinks about his Beloved, then either he thinks about His beauty and the goodness of His image in His Essence to delight in thinking about Him and in witnessing Him, or he thinks about His subtle, good actions indicating His character and His attributes to be that which doubles the pleasure and strengthens his love. And if he thinks about himself, then his thought is in the attributes that drop him from the eye of his Beloved until he abstains from them, or in the attributes that bring him near to Him and make him beloved to Him until he becomes characterized by them. So if he thinks about something outside of these divisions, then that is outside the limit of love (Ishq) and it is a deficiency in it, because the complete, perfect love (Ishq) is what overwhelms the lover and fills the heart (Qalb) until it leaves no room for other than it. So the lover of Allah, Exalted is He, ought to be like that, so his view and thought do not exceed his Beloved. And whenever his thought is confined in these four divisions, it is not outside the requirement of love at all. So let us begin with the first division, which is his thinking about the attributes of himself and the actions of himself to distinguish the beloved from them from the disliked, for this thought is that which relates to the science of transaction (Mu'amalah) which is the intended purpose of this book, and as for the other division, it relates to the science of unveiling (Mukashafah), then every.
2:116.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Contemplation'

2:118.arabic: وإليه يشير قوله تعالى إن في ذلك لآيات للمتوسمين وقوله تعالى قد بينا الآيات لقوم يوقنون وروى الحسن عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال العلم علمان فعلم باطن في القلب فذلك هو العلم النافع
2:118.english: And to this points His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed in that are signs for those who discern (al-mutawassimīn)' and His saying, the Exalted: 'We have made clear the signs for a people who are certain (yūqinūn).' And al-Hasan narrated from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, that he said: 'Knowledge is two knowledges: knowledge that is inward (bāṭin) in the Heart (Qalb), and that is the beneficial knowledge.'
2:118.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

2:121.arabic: الوظيفة السابعة: أن لا يخوض في فن حتى يستوفي الفن الذي قبله فإن العلوم مرتبة ترتيبا ضروريا وبعضها طريق إلى بعض والموفق من راعى ذلك الترتيب والتدريج قال الله تعالى: (الذين آتيناهم الكتاب يتلونه حق تلاوته( (البقرة:121). أي لا يجاوزون فنا حتى يحكموه علما وعملا وليكن قصده في كل علم يتحراه الترقي إلى ما هو فوقه فينبغي ألا يحكم على علم بالفساد لوقوع الخلف بين أصحابه فيه ولا بخطأ واحد أو آحاد فيه ولا بمخالفتهم موجب علمهم بالعمل فترى جماعة تركوا النظر في العقليات والفقهيات متعللين فيها بأنها لو كان لها
2:121.english: The Seventh Duty: That one does not delve into a discipline until one has completed the discipline that precedes it, for the sciences are arranged in a necessary order and some of them are a path to others. The successful one is he who observes that order and gradual progression. Allah the Exalted said: 'Those to whom We have given the Book recite it with its true recitation (haqq tilawatihi)' (Al-Baqarah:121). That is, they do not pass beyond a discipline until they have mastered it in knowledge and action. And let his intention in every science he seeks be to ascend to what is above it. Therefore, one should not judge a science as corrupt due to the occurrence of disagreement among its practitioners, nor due to a single error or a few errors within it, nor due to their contravention of what their knowledge necessitates in action. Thus you see a group who abandoned consideration of the rational sciences and the jurisprudential sciences, making excuses in them that if they had a foundation, their masters would have attained it. The uncovering of this doubt has already passed in the book 'Mi'yar al-'Ilm'. And you see a faction who believe in the invalidity of medicine due to an error they witnessed from a physician, and a faction who believed in the correctness of astrology due to correctness that happened for one, and a faction who believed in its invalidity due to an error that happened for another—and all of that is error. Rather, one should know the thing in itself, for not every science can be encompassed by every person. And for that reason, 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: 'Do not know the truth through men; know the truth and you will know its people.'
2:121.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Book of Knowledge'

2:123.arabic: ويوم لا تجزى نفس عن نفس شيئا
2:123.english: And a day when no soul (Nafs) will avail another soul (Nafs) anything
2:123.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

2:125.arabic: الثاني: تهييج الشوق بالمفارقة لتنبعث داعية العودة فإن الله تعالى جعل البيت مثابة للناس وأمنا أي يثوبون ويعودون إليه مرة بعد أخرى ولا يقضون منه وطرا وقال بعضهم: تكون في بلد وقلبك مشتاق إلى مكة متعلق بهذا البيت خير لك من أن تكون فيه وأنت متبرم بالمقام وقلبك في بلد آخر.
2:125.english: The second: Stirring longing through separation so that the call to return may surge forth, for Allah the Exalted made the House a place of return (Mithabah) for people and a sanctuary (Amnan), meaning they return and come back to it time after time and do not have their fill of it. And some of them said: Being in a land while your heart (Qalb) yearns for Mecca, attached to this House, is better for you than being in it while you are weary of staying and your heart is in another land.
2:125.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

2:127.arabic: وتقول عند التصدق ﴿ ربنا تقبل منا إنك أنت السميع العليم ﴾ {}
2:127.english: And you say when giving charity: 'Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the All-Hearing (As-Sami'), the All-Knowing (Al-'Alim).'
2:127.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

2:128.arabic: ربنا أفرغ علينا صبرا وتوفنا مسلمين أنت ولي في الدنيا والآخرة توفنى مسلما وألحقنى بالصالحين أنت ولينا فاغفر لنا وارحمنا وأنت خير الغافرين واكتب لنا في هذه الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة إنا هدنا إليك ربنا عليك توكلنا وإليك أنبنا وإليك المصير ربنا لا تجعلنا فتنة للقوم الظالمين ربنا لا تجعلنا فتنة للذين كفروا واغفر لنا ربنا إنك أنت العزيز الحكيم ربنا اغفر لنا ذنوبنا وإسرافنا في أمرنا وثبت أقدامنا وانصرنا على القوم الكافرين ر
2:128.english: Our Lord, pour upon us patience and cause us to die as Muslims (Muslimīn). You are our Guardian (Walī) in the worldly life and the Hereafter. Cause me to die as a Muslim (Musliman) and join me with the righteous (Ṣāliḥīn). You are our Guardian (Walī), so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the best of forgivers. And decree for us in this worldly life good and in the Hereafter; indeed, we have turned to You. Our Lord, upon You we have relied and to You we have returned, and to You is the destination. Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people. Our Lord, do not make us a trial for those who have disbelieved, and forgive us, our Lord. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise. Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excess in our affair and make firm our feet and give us victory over the disbelieving people. R
2:128.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

2:128.arabic:
دنيا والآخرة[150] اللهم املأ وجوهنا منك حياء وقلوبنا  منك  فرقا  واسكن  في
نفوسنا من عظمتك ما تذلل به جوارحنا لخدمتك. واجعلك اللهم أحب إلينا  ممن  سواك
واجعلنا أخشى لك ممن سواك[151] اللهم اجعل أول يومنا هذا  صلاحا  وأوسطه  فلاحا
وآخره نجاحا اللهم اجعل أوله رحمة وأوسطه نعمة وآخره تكرمة  ومغفرة[152]  الحمد
لله الذي تواضع كل شيء لعظمته وذل كل شيء لعزته وخضع كل شيء لملكه  واستسلم  كل
شيء لقدرته والحمد لله الذي سكن كل شيء لهيبته وأظهر كل شيء بحكمته  وتصاغر  كل
شيء لكبريائه[153] اللهم صل على محمد وعلى
2:128.english: [158] Hadith: 'O Allah, by Your power over me, accept my repentance (Tawbah) upon me, indeed You are the Acceptor of Repentance (Al-Tawwab), the Most Merciful (Al-Rahim), and by Your forbearance (Hilm) over me, pardon me...' the hadith up to its saying 'Indeed You are the King (Al-Malik), the Compeller (Al-Jabbar)' - I have not found a source for it.
2:128.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

2:128.arabic: [108]  حديث كان النبي ﭬ يكثر أن يقول سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك اللهم اغفر لي إنك أنت التواب الرحيم أخرجه الحاكم من حديث ابن مسعود وقال صحيح إن كان أبو عبيدة سمع من أبيه والحديث متفق عليه من حديث عائشة أنه كان يكثر أن يقول ذلك في ركوعه وسجوده دون قوله إنك أنت التواب الرحيم.
2:128.english: Hadith: The Prophet (peace be upon him) used to frequently say: 'Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You, O Allah, forgive me, indeed You are the Oft-Returning (Al-Tawwab), the Most Merciful (Al-Rahim).' Al-Hakim reported it from the narration of Ibn Mas'ud and said it is authentic if Abu 'Ubaydah heard it from his father. The hadith is agreed upon from the narration of 'A'ishah that he used to frequently say that in his bowing (ruku') and prostration (sujud) without saying 'indeed You are the Oft-Returning (Al-Tawwab), the Most Merciful (Al-Rahim).'
2:128.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication

2:132.arabic:
تك  وإن
عدلت عنهم مقتك قال يا رب وما علامتهم؟ قال: يراعون الظلال بالنهار  كما  يراعى
الراعي غنمه ويحنون إلى غروب الشمس كما تحن الطير إلى أوكارها فإذا جنهم  الليل
واختلط الظلام وخلا كل حبيب بحبيبه نصبوا  إلىّ  أقدامهم  وافترشوا  إلىّ  وجوههم
وناجوني بكلامي وتملقوا إليّ بإنعامي فبين صارخ وباكي، وبين متأوه وشاكي،  بعيني
ما يتحملون من أجلي وبسمعي ما يشتكون من حبي أول ما أعطيهم  أقذف  من  نوري  في
قلوبهم فيخبرون عني كما أخبر عنهم، والثانية لو كانت  السموات  السبع  والأرضون
السبع وما فيهما من موازينهم
2:132.english: And if you turn away from them, your hatred said: O Lord, and what are their signs? He said: They observe the shadows during the day as the shepherd observes his sheep, and they yearn for sunset as birds yearn for their nests. When night covers them and darkness mixes and every lover is alone with their beloved, they direct their feet to Me and spread their faces to Me, and they converse with Me with My words and flatter Me with My blessings. Between one crying out and weeping, and between one sighing and complaining, with My eye what they endure for My sake and with My hearing what they complain of from My love. The first thing I give them: I cast from My light into their hearts (Qulub) so they inform about Me as I inform about them. The second: even if the seven heavens and the seven earths and what is in them were their scales, I would consider it little for them. The third: I turn My face toward them. Do you think one upon whom I turn My face knows what I want to give him? And Malik bin Dinar, may God have mercy on him, said: When the servant (Abd) rises to pray at night, the Almighty (Al-Jabbar) draws near to him, and they used to see what they find of tenderness and sweetness in their hearts (Qulub) and lights from the nearness of the Lord, the Exalted, to the heart (Qalb). This has a secret and verification; reference will come to it in the Book of Love. And in the reports from God, the Almighty: (O My servant, I am God who has drawn near to your heart (Qalb) and in the unseen seen My light). And some disciples (Muridun) complained to their teacher about the length of night vigil and sought a means to bring sleep. His teacher said: O my son, indeed God has breaths (Nafahat) in the night and day that strike the vigilant hearts (Qulub) and miss the sleeping hearts (Qulub), so expose yourself to those breaths. He said: O my master, you have left me not sleeping at night nor during the day. And know that these breaths (Nafahat) at night are more hopeful due to what is in night prayer (Qiyam al-Layl) of purity of the heart (Qalb) and removal of distractions. And in the authentic report from Jabir bin Abdullah from the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, that he said: (Indeed there is an hour of the night that no Muslim servant (Abd) meets it asking God, the Exalted, for good except that He gives it to him) and in another narration (asks God for good from the affairs of this world and the hereafter except that He gives it, and that every night). And what is sought by those who pray at night is that hour, and it is important in the entirety of the night like Laylat al-Qadr in the month of Ramadan and like the hour of Friday, and it is the hour of the mentioned breaths (Nafahat), and God knows best. Explanation of the division methods for parts of the night: Know that reviving the night in terms of amount has seven levels. The first: reviving the entire night, and this is the state of the strong ones who have devoted themselves to night worship and delighted in conversing with Him, and that became nourishment for them and life for their hearts (Qulub), so they were not tired by long standing and returned sleep to the daytime at the time of people's busyness. And that was the way of a group of the predecessors who used to pray the dawn prayer with the ablution of the evening prayer. Abu Talib al-Makki narrated that that was narrated on the basis of continuous transmission and fame from forty m
2:132.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

2:135.arabic: [232]  حديث أصبحنا على فطرة الإسلام وكلمة الإخلاص ودين نبينا محمد ﭬ وملة أبينا إبراهيم حنيفا وما كان من المشركين أخرجه النسائي في اليوم والليلة من حديث عبد الرحمن بن أبزى بسند صحيح ورواه أحمد من حديث ابن أبزى عن أبي بن كعب مرفوعا.
2:135.english: [232] The hadith: 'We have awakened upon the natural disposition (Fitrah) of Islam and the word of sincerity (Ikhlas) and the religion of our Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the creed (Millah) of our father Abraham, upright (Hanifan) and he was not of the polytheists (Mushrikin).' Al-Nasa'i transmitted it in 'Al-Yawm wa al-Laylah' from the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza with an authentic chain, and Ahmad transmitted it from the hadith of Ibn Abza from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, raised to the Prophet.
2:135.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication

2:136.arabic: ولما قال سفيان ذلك قيل له فماذا نقول قال قولوا آمنا بالله وما أنزل إلينا وأي فرق بين أن يقول آمنا بالله وما أنزل إلينا وبين أن يقول أنا مؤمن وقيل للحسن أمؤمن أنت فقال إن شاء الله فقيل له لم تستثني يا أبا سعيد في الإيمان فقال أخاف أن أقول نعم فيقول الله سبحانه كذبت يا حسن فتحق علي الكلمة وكان يقول ما يؤمنني أن يكون الله سبحانه قد اطلع علي في بعض ما يكره فمقتني وقال اذهب لا قبلت لك عملا فأنا أعمل في غير معمل وقال إبراهيم بن أدهم إذا قيل لك أمؤمن أنت فقل لا إله إلا الله وقال مرة قل أنا لا أشك في ال
2:136.english: And when Sufyan said that, he was asked: 'So what should we say?' He said: 'Say: "We believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us" (Quran 2:136). And what difference is there between saying "We believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us" and saying "I am a believer"?' And it was said to Al-Hasan: 'Are you a believer?' He said: 'If Allah wills.' It was said to him: 'Why do you make an exception, O Abu Sa'id, regarding faith?' He said: 'I fear that if I say yes, Allah the Exalted would say: "You have lied, O Hasan," and the word would be established against me.' And he used to say: 'What assures me that Allah the Exalted has not looked upon me in some matter He dislikes, so He detested me and said: "Go away, I have not accepted your deed," so I am working in vain?' And Ibrahim bin Adham said: 'If you are asked: "Are you a believer?" say: "There is no god but Allah."' And he said once: 'Say: "I do not doubt in faith," and your asking me is an innovation.' And it was said to 'Alqamah: 'Are you a believer?' He said: 'I hope, if Allah wills.' And Al-Thawri said: 'We believe in Allah, His angels, His books, and His messengers, and we do not know what we are with Allah the Exalted.' So what is the meaning of these exceptions?
2:136.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Foundations of Belief'

2:143.arabic: فقال يا أبا سعيد مالي أراك ساكتا قال ما عسيت أن أقول قال أخبرني برأيك في أبي تراب قال سمعت الله جل ذكره يقول وما جعلنا القبلة التي كنت عليها إلا لنعلم من يتبع الرسول ممن ينقلب على عقبيه وإن كانت لكبيرة إلا على الذين هدى الله وما كان الله ليضيع إيمانكم إن الله بالناس لرءوف رحيم فعلى ممن هدى الله من أهل الإيمان فأقول ابن عم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وختنه على ابنته وأحب الناس إليه وصاحب سوابق مباركات سبقت له من الله لن تستطيع أنت ولا أحد من الناس أن يحظرها عليه ولا يحول بينه وبينها وأقول إن كانت لع
2:143.english: He said: 'O Abu Sa'id, why do I see you silent?' He said: 'What could I say?' He said: 'Inform me of your opinion regarding Abu Turab.' He said: 'I heard Allah, Glorified and Majestic is He, say: "And We did not make the Qiblah (direction of prayer) which you were upon except to know who follows the Messenger from he who turns back on his heels. And indeed it was great except upon those whom Allah has guided. And Allah would not cause your faith to be lost. Indeed Allah is to the people Kind, Merciful." So upon whom from the people of faith has Allah guided? Then I say: The cousin of the Prophet (peace be upon him) and his son-in-law through his daughter, and the most beloved of people to him, and possessor of blessed precedents that have preceded for him from Allah. You will not be able, nor will any of the people, to prevent them from him or come between him and them. And I say: If there is for Ali a slip, then Allah is sufficient for him. By Allah, I do not find regarding him a statement more just than this.'
2:143.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

2:144.arabic: وأما الاكتفاء بالجهة عند تعذر المعاينة فيدل عليه الكتاب والسنة وفعل الصحابة رضي الله عنهم والقياس أما الكتاب فقوله تعالى وحيثما كنتم فولوا وجوهكم شطره أي نحوه ومن قابل جهة الكعبة يقال قد ولى وجهه شطره
2:144.english: As for the sufficiency of the direction (al-jiha) when direct observation is impossible, this is indicated by the Book (al-Kitab), the Prophetic Tradition (al-Sunnah), the actions of the Companions (al-Sahaba) - may Allah be pleased with them - and analogical reasoning (al-Qiyas). As for the Book, it is His statement, the Exalted: 'And wherever you are, turn your faces towards it (shatrahu).' That is, towards its direction. And whoever faces the direction (jiha) of the Kaaba, it is said he has turned his face towards its direction (shatraha).
2:144.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Etiquette of Travel'

2:146.arabic: وأما الآيات: فقوله عز وجل: ﴿ولينذروا قومهم إذا رجعوا إليهم لعلهم يحذرون﴾ ( سورة التوبة: الآية 122) والمراد هو التعليم والإرشاد وقوله تعالى: ﴿وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب ليبيننه للناس ولا يكتمونه﴾ ( سورة آل عمران: الآية 187) وهو إيجاب للتعليم وقوله تعالى: ﴿وإن فريقا منهم ليكتمون الحق وهم يعلمون﴾ ( سورة البقرة: الآية 146) وهو تحريم للكتمان كما قال تعالى في الشهادة: ﴿ومن يكتمها فإنه آثم قلبه﴾ ( سورة البقرة: الآية 283) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: (ما آتى الله عالما علما إلا وأخذ عليه من الميث
2:146.english: As for the verses: The saying of the Almighty: 'And to warn their people when they return to them so that they might be cautious' (Surah At-Tawbah: Verse 122) and the intended meaning is teaching and guidance. And His saying, the Exalted: 'And [mention] when Allah took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture to make it clear to the people and not conceal it' (Surah Āl 'Imrān: Verse 187) and it is an obligation for teaching. And His saying, the Exalted: 'And indeed, a party of them conceal the truth while they know' (Surah Al-Baqarah: Verse 146) and it is a prohibition of concealment as the Exalted said regarding testimony: 'And whoever conceals it, then indeed he is sinful in his heart (Qalb)' (Surah Al-Baqarah: Verse 283). And the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'Allah does not grant a scholar knowledge except that He takes from him a covenant like the covenant He took from the prophets: that he makes it clear to the people and does not conceal it.'
2:146.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

2:146.arabic: وإنما يضاعف عذاب العالم في معصيته لأنه عصى من علم ولذلك قال الله عز وجل: (إن المنافقين في الدرك الأسفل من النار( (النساء:145). لأنهم جحدوا بعد العلم وجعل اليهود شرا من النصارى مع أنهم ما جعلوا لله سبحانه ولدا ولا قالوا إنه ثالث ثلاثة إلا أنهم أنكروا بعد المعرفة إذ قال الله (يعرفونه كما يعرفون أبناءهم( (البقرة:146) (الأنعام:20). وقال تعالى: (فلما جاءهم ما عرفوا كفروا به فلعنة الله على الكافرين( (البقرة:89). وقال تعالى في قصة بلعام بن باعوراء (واتل عليهم نبأ الذي آتيناه آياتنا فانسلخ منها فأتبعه ا
2:146.english: And indeed the punishment of the scholar in his disobedience is multiplied because he disobeyed from knowledge, and therefore Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed the hypocrites are in the lowest depth of the Fire' (An-Nisa:145). Because they denied after knowledge, and He made the Jews worse than the Christians even though they did not make for Allah, glorified be He, a son nor did they say He is the third of three, except that they rejected after recognition (Ma'rifah) when Allah said: 'They recognize him as they recognize their sons' (Al-Baqarah:146) (Al-An'am:20). And He the Exalted said: 'So when came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it, so the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers' (Al-Baqarah:89). And He the Exalted said in the story of Balaam son of Ba'ura: 'And recite to them the news of him to whom We gave Our signs, but he detached himself from them, so Satan followed him, and he became of the deviators' (Al-A'raf:175) until He said: 'So his likeness is as the likeness of a dog; if you attack it, it pants, or if you leave it, it pants' (Al-A'raf:176). So likewise the wicked scholar, for Balaam was given the Book of Allah the Exalted but he clung to the desires, so he was likened to the dog, meaning whether he was given wisdom or not given, he pants toward the desires.
2:146.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

2:150.arabic: وأما الاكتفاء بالجهة عند تعذر المعاينة فيدل عليه الكتاب والسنة وفعل الصحابة رضي الله عنهم والقياس أما الكتاب فقوله تعالى وحيثما كنتم فولوا وجوهكم شطره أي نحوه ومن قابل جهة الكعبة يقال قد ولى وجهه شطرها
2:150.english: And as for sufficing with the direction (al-jihah) when direct observation (al-mu'āyanah) is impossible, it is indicated by the Book (al-Kitāb), the Sunnah, the action of the Companions (al-Ṣaḥābah) - may Allah be pleased with them - and analogy (al-qiyās). As for the Book, it is His statement, the Exalted: 'And wherever you are, turn your faces towards it (shatrahu)' meaning towards its direction (naḥwahu). And whoever faces the direction (jihah) of the Ka'bah, it is said he has turned his face towards its direction (shatraha).
2:150.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Etiquette of Travel'

2:152.arabic: اعلم ان الله تعالى قرن الشكر بالذكر في كتابه مع انه قال: ﴿ ولذكر الله اكبر ﴾ {} فقال تعالى: ﴿ فاذكروني اذكركم واشكروا لي ولا تكفرون ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ ما يفعل الله بعذابكم ان شكرتم وآمنتم ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ وسنجزي الشاكرين ﴾ {}. وقال عز وجل إخبارا عن ابليس اللعين: ﴿ لأقعدن لهم صراطك المستقيم ﴾ {} قيل هو طريق الشكر ولعلو رتبة الشكر طعن اللعين في الخلق فقال: ولا تجد أكثرهم شاكرين وقال تعالى: ﴿ وقليل من عبادي الشكور ﴾ {} وقد قطع الله تعالى بالمزيد مع الشكر ولم يستثن فقال تعالى: ﴿ لئن شكرتم لأزيدنكم
2:152.english: Know that Allah the Exalted coupled Gratitude (Shukr) with Remembrance (Dhikr) in His Book, even though He said: 'And the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah is greater' (Quran 29:45). So He the Exalted said: 'So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me' (Quran 2:152). And He the Exalted said: 'What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe?' (Quran 4:147). And He the Exalted said: 'And We will reward the grateful ones' (Quran 3:145). And He the Mighty and Majestic, informing about Satan the accursed: 'I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path' (Quran 7:16). It is said it is the path of Gratitude (Shukr), and due to the high rank of Gratitude (Shukr), the accursed one attacked the creation, saying: 'And you will not find most of them grateful' (Quran 7:17). And He the Exalted said: 'And few of My servants are grateful' (Quran 34:13). And Allah the Exalted has affirmed increase with Gratitude (Shukr) without exception, saying: 'If you are grateful, I will surely increase you' (Quran 14:7). And He made exceptions in five things: in enrichment, response, provision, forgiveness, and repentance, saying: 'Then Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills' (Quran 9:28), and said: 'He removes what you call to if He wills' (Quran 6:41), and said: 'He provides for whom He wills without account' (Quran 2:212), and said: 'And He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills' (Quran 4:48), and said: 'And Allah turns in forgiveness to whom He wills' (Quran 9:27). And it is a character from the characters of Lordship (Rububiyyah), as He the Exalted said: 'And Allah is Appreciative (Shakur) and Forbearing' (Quran 64:17). And Allah has made Gratitude (Shukr) the key to the speech of the people of Paradise, saying: 'And they will say, "Praise to Allah, who has fulfilled for us His promise"' (Quran 39:74), and said: 'And their last call will be, "Praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds"' (Quran 10:10).
2:152.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

2:153.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
2:153.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Whatever is in the Quran of 'O you who have believed' is in the Torah 'O you who are poor (Masakin)'.
2:153.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

2:156.arabic: وإذا بلغك وفاة أحد فقل إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون وإنا إلى ربنا لمنقلبون اللهم اكتبه في المحسنين واجعل كتابه في عليين واخلفه على عقبه في الغابرين اللهم لا تحرمنا أجره ولا تفتنا بعده واغفر لنا وله
2:156.english: And when you hear of someone's death, say: 'Indeed we belong to Allah and indeed to Him we will return, and indeed to our Lord we are returning. O Allah, write him among the doers of good and place his record in the highest ranks, and replace him for his descendants among the later ones. O Allah, do not deprive us of his reward and do not test us after him, and forgive us and him.'
2:156.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

2:156.arabic: [206] حديث القول إذا بلغه وفاة أحد إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون وإنا إلى ربنا لمنقلبون اللهم اكتبه من المحسنين واجعل كتابه في عليين واخلفه على عقبه في الغابرين اللهم لا تحرمنا أجره ولا تفتنا بعده واغفر لنا وله أخرجه ابن السني في اليوم والليلة وابن حبان من حديث أم سلمة إذا أصاب أحدكم مصيبة فليقل إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون ولمسلم من حديثها اللهم اغفر لأبي سلمة وارفع درجته في المهديين واخلفه في عقبه في الغابرين واغفر لنا وله يا رب العالمين وافسح له في قبره ونور له فيه.
2:156.english: [206] The saying when one hears of someone's death: 'Indeed we belong to Allah and indeed to Him we will return, and indeed to our Lord we are returning. O Allah, record him among the doers of good (al-Muhsinin) and place his record in the highest (Illiyyin), and replace him for his offspring among the later generations (al-Ghabirin). O Allah, do not deprive us of his reward and do not test us after him, and forgive us and him.' It was reported by Ibn al-Sunni in 'The Day and Night' and Ibn Hibban from the hadith of Umm Salamah: 'When a calamity (musibah) befalls one of you, let him say: Indeed we belong to Allah and indeed to Him we will return.' And in Muslim from her hadith: 'O Allah, forgive Abu Salamah and raise his rank among the guided ones (al-Mahdiyyin), and replace him for his offspring among the later generations (al-Ghabirin), and forgive us and him, O Lord of the worlds, and expand for him in his grave and illuminate it for him.'
2:156.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication

2:157.arabic: وكان عمر رضي الله عنه يقول نعم العدلان ونعمت العلاوة للصابرين يعني بالعدلين الصلاة والرحمة وبالعلاوة الهدى والعلاوة ما يحمل فوق العدلين على البعير وأشار به إلى قوله تعالى: ﴿ أولئك عليهم صلوات من ربهم ورحمة وأولئك هم المهتدون ﴾ {} وكان حبيب بن أبي حبيب إذا قرأ هذه الآية: ﴿ إنا وجدناه صابرا نعم العبد إنه أواب ﴾ {} بكى وقال واعجباه اعطى واثنى أي هو المعطي للصبر وهو المثنى
2:157.english: And Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say: 'How excellent are the two scales and how excellent is the additional load for the patient ones.' He meant by 'the two scales': the prayer and the mercy, and by 'the additional load': the guidance. And 'the additional load' is what is carried above the two scales on the camel. And he indicated by this to His saying, the Exalted: 'Those are upon them prayers from their Lord and mercy, and those are they who are the guided ones.' And when Habib ibn Abi Habib would read this verse: 'Indeed, We found him patient. How excellent the servant! Indeed, he was one who repeatedly turned back (to Allah).' he would weep and say: 'How wondrous! He gave and He praised.' That is, He is the Giver of patience and He is the Praiser.
2:157.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

2:157.arabic: وجمع للصابرين بين أمور لم يجمعها لغيرهم فقال تعالى: ﴿ أولئك عليهم صلوات من ربهم ورحمة وأولئك هم المهتدون ﴾ {} فالهدى والرحمة والصلوات مجموعة للصابرين
2:157.english: And He gathered for the patient ones between matters which He did not gather for others, so the Exalted said: 'Those are upon them prayers from their Lord and mercy, and those are the guided ones.' So the guidance and the mercy and the prayers are gathered for the patient ones.
2:157.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

2:161.arabic: وفي خبر آخر: (( من غش أمتي فعليه لعنة الله والملائكة والناس أجمعين، قيل: يا رسول الله وما غش أمتك، قال: أن يبتدع بدعة يحمل الناس عليها))[196].
2:161.english: And in another report: 'Whoever deceives my community, upon him is the curse of Allah and the angels and all the people. It was said: O Messenger of Allah, and what is deceiving your community? He said: That he innovates an innovation (bid'ah) and carries the people upon it.'[196].
2:161.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Book of Knowledge'

2:162.arabic: فانظر كيف انقلب الجاهلون وانكبوا على وجوههم انكباب العميان فأقبلوا على طلب كمال القدرة بالجاه والمال، وهو الكمال الذي لا يسلم وإن سلم فلا بقاء له، وأعرضوا عن كمال الحرية والعلم الذي إذا حصل كان أبدياً لا انقطاع له، وهؤلاء هم الذين اشتروا الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة فلا جرم لا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينصرون، وهم الذين لم يفهموا قوله تعالى "المال والبنون زينة الحياة الدنيا والباقيات الصالحات خير عند ربك ثواباً وخير أملاً" فالعلم والحرية هي الباقيات الصالحات التي تبقى كمالاً في النفس، والمال والجاه هو ال
2:162.english: Look how the ignorant have turned and fallen on their faces like the falling of the blind, so they turned to seeking perfection of power through status and wealth, which is a perfection that does not remain safe, and if it remains safe, it has no permanence, and they turned away from the perfection of freedom and knowledge which, when attained, is eternal with no cessation. And these are the ones who have purchased the worldly life in exchange for the Hereafter, so indeed no punishment is lightened for them, nor are they given respite. And they are the ones who did not understand His saying, the Exalted: 'Wealth and children are the adornment of the worldly life, but the enduring righteous deeds are better with your Lord for reward and better for hope.' So knowledge and freedom are the enduring righteous deeds which remain as perfection in the soul (Nafs), and wealth and status are what perish in proximity, and it is as Allah, the Exalted, has likened it where He said: 'The example of the worldly life is like water which We send down from the sky...' the verse.
2:162.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

2:163.arabic: من صلى المغرب في جماعة ثم صلى بعدها ركعتين ولم يتكلم بشيء فيما بين ذلك من أمر الدنيا ويقرأ في الركعة الأولى فاتحة الكتاب وعشر آيات من أول سورة البقرة وآيتين من وسطها وإلهكم إله واحد لا إله إلا هو الرحمن الرحيم إن في خلق السموات والأرض إلى آخر الآية وقل هو الله أحد خمس عشرة مرة ثم يركع ويسجد فإذا قام في الركعة الثانية قرأ فاتحة الكتاب وآية الكرسي وآيتين بعدها إلى قوله أولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون وثلاث آيات من آخر سورة البقرة من قوله لله ما في السموات وما في الأرض إلى آخرها وقل هو الله أحد خم
2:163.english: Whoever prays Maghrib in congregation then prays two rak'ahs after it and does not speak anything of worldly matters between them, and recites in the first rak'ah: The Opening (Al-Fatihah) of the Book and ten verses from the beginning of Surah Al-Baqarah and two verses from its middle: 'And your God (Ilah) is One God (Ilah Wahid); there is no god (ilah) except Him, the Most Merciful (Ar-Rahman), the Most Compassionate (Ar-Rahim). Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth...' to the end of the verse, and 'Say: He is Allah, the One' fifteen times, then bows and prostrates. When he stands for the second rak'ah, he recites: The Opening (Al-Fatihah) of the Book and the Throne Verse (Ayat al-Kursi) and two verses after it up to His saying: 'Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally,' and three verses from the end of Surah Al-Baqarah from His saying: 'To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth...' to its end, and 'Say: He is Allah, the One' fifteen times.
2:163.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Book of Knowledge'

2:163.arabic: ويستحب أن يقرأ الآيات المخصوصة مثل آية الكرسي وآخر البقرة وغيرهما وقوله تعالى: ﴿ وإلهكم إله واحد لا إله إلا هو ﴾ {} إلى قوله: ﴿ لقوم يعقلون ﴾ {} يقال إن من قرأها عند النوم حفظ الله عليه القرآن فلم ينسه ويقرأ من سورة الأعراف هذه الآية: ﴿ إن ربكم الله الذي خلق السموات والأرض في ستة أيام ﴾ {} إلى قوله: ﴿ قريب من المحسنين ﴾ {} وآخر بني إسرائيل ﴿ قل ادعوا الله ﴾ {} الآيتين فإنه يدخل في شعاره ملك يوكل بحفظه فيستغفر له ويقرأ المعوذتين وينفث بهن في يديه ويمسح بهما وجهه وسائر جسده كذلك روى من فعل رسول ال
2:163.english: And it is recommended to recite the specified verses such as the Throne Verse (Ayat al-Kursi) and the end of Al-Baqarah and others, and His saying, the Exalted: 'And your god is one god; there is no god except Him' until His saying: 'for a people who use reason.' It is said that whoever recites it at sleep, Allah preserves the Quran for him so he does not forget it. And he recites from Surah Al-A'raf this verse: 'Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and earth in six days' until His saying: 'is near to the doers of good.' And the end of Bani Isra'il 'Say, "Call upon Allah"' the two verses, for then a king enters his emblem who is entrusted with his protection, so he seeks forgiveness for him. And he recites the two surahs of seeking refuge (Al-Mu'awwidhatayn) and blows with them into his hands and wipes with them his face and the rest of his body; likewise, it is narrated from the action of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him. And let him recite ten from the beginning of Al-Kahf and ten from its end, and these verses are for awakening for the night prayer (Qiyam al-Layl). And Ali, may Allah honor his face, said: 'I do not think that a man with complete intellect sleeps before reciting the two verses from the end of Surah Al-Baqarah.' And let him say twenty-five times: 'Glory be to Allah (Subhan Allah) and praise be to Allah (Alhamdulillah) and there is no god but Allah (La ilaha illa Allah) and Allah is the greatest (Allahu Akbar)' so that the total of these four words becomes four hundred times.
2:163.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Book of Knowledge'

2:164.arabic: ثم انظر إلى عجائب الجو وما يظهر فيه من الغيوم والرعود والبروق والأمطار والثلوج والشهب والصواعق فهى عجائب ما بين السماء والأرض وقد أشار القرآن إلى جملة ذلك فى قوله تعالى وما خلقنا السموات والأرض وما بينهما لاعبين وهذا هو الذى بينهما وأشار إلى تفصيله فى مواضع شتى حيث قال تعالى والسحاب المسخر بين السماء والأرض وحيث تعرض للرعد والبرق والسحاب والمطر فإذا لم يكن لك حظ من هذه الجملة إلا أن ترى المطر بعينك وتسمع الرعد بأذنك فالبهيمة تشاركك فى هذه المعرفة فارتفع من حضيض عالم البهائم إلى عالم الملأ الأعلى
2:164.english: Then look at the wonders of the atmosphere and what appears in it of clouds, thunders, lightnings, rains, snows, meteors, and thunderbolts—these are wonders between the heaven and the earth. The Quran has pointed to the totality of this in His saying, the Exalted: 'And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play.' And this is what is between them. And He pointed to its details in various places where He said, the Exalted: 'And the clouds subjugated between the heaven and the earth,' and where He mentions the thunder, lightning, clouds, and rain. If you have no share of this totality except that you see the rain with your eye and hear the thunder with your ear, then the beast shares with you in this knowledge. So rise from the lowliness of the world of beasts to the world of the highest assembly. For you have opened your eyes and perceived its outward aspect, so close your outward eye and look with your inner insight (Batin) to see the wonders of its inward aspect and the marvels of its secrets. And this is also a door that lengthens thought in it, for there is no hope in exhausting it. So contemplate the dense, dark cloud—how you see it gather in a pure atmosphere with no turbidity in it, and how Allah, the Exalted, creates it when He wills and whenever He wills. And it, with its softness, carries the heavy water and holds it in the atmosphere of the heaven until Allah permits in sending the water and cutting the layers, every drop with the measure that Allah, the Exalted, has willed and in the form that He has desired. So you see the cloud sprinkling water upon the earth and sending it as separate drops—no drop of them catches another drop, nor does one connect with another. Rather, each one descends in the path that has been delineated for it, not deviating from it, so the later does not precede nor the earlier delay until it strikes the earth drop by drop. If the first and the last were to gather to create from it a drop or to know the number of what descends from it in a single town or village, the calculation of the jinn and mankind would be incapable.
2:164.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Contemplation'

2:164.arabic: يوم وهم يتفكرون فقال ما لكم لا تتكلمون فقالوا نتفكر في خلق الله الحديث رويناه في جزء من حديث عبد الله بن سلام وعن عطاء قال انطلقت يوما أنا وعبيد بن عمير إلى عائشة رضى الله عنها فكلمتنا وبيننا وبينها حجاب فقالت يا عبيد ما يمنعك من زيارتنا قال قول رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم زر غبا تزدد حبا قال ابن عمير فأخبرينا بأعجب شئ رأيته من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال فبكت وقالت كل أمره كان عجبا أتانى في ليلتى حتى مس جلده جلدى ثم قال ذرينى أتعبد لربى عز وجل فقام إلى القربة فتوضأ منها ثم قام يصلى فبكى ح
2:164.english: A day while they were contemplating (yatafakkarūn), so he said: 'What is with you that you do not speak?' They said: 'We contemplate (natafakkar) in the creation of Allah.' The hadith we narrated in a part of the hadith of Abdullah ibn Salam. And from Ata' he said: 'One day I and Ubaid ibn Umair went to Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, and she spoke to us while there was a curtain between us and her. She said: O Ubaid, what prevents you from visiting us? He said: The saying of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him: 'Visit infrequently, you will increase in love.' Ibn Umair said: So inform us of the most amazing thing you saw from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. He said: So she wept and said: Every matter of his was amazing. He came to me in my night until his skin touched my skin, then he said: Leave me to worship my Lord, the Mighty and Majestic. So he stood up to the water-skin and performed ablution from it, then he stood praying and wept until his beard became wet, then he prostrated until the ground became wet, then he lay on his side until Bilal came to call him to the dawn prayer. He said: O Messenger of Allah, what makes you weep when Allah has forgiven you your past and future sins? He said: Woe to you, O Bilal, and what prevents me from weeping when Allah the Exalted revealed to me in this night: 'Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding (ūlī al-albāb).' Then he said: Woe to the one who recites it and does not contemplate (yatafakkar) in it.' The hadith of Ata': 'I and Ubaid ibn Umair went to Aisha...' The hadith. Ibn Umair said: 'So inform us of the most amazing thing you saw from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.' The hadith regarding the revelation of 'Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth...' and he said: 'Woe to the one who recites it and does not contemplate (yatafakkar) in it.' It preceded in patience and gratitude that it is in Sahih Ibn Hibban from the narration of Abdul Malik ibn Abi Sulaiman from Ata'. It was said to Al-Awza'i: What is the ultimate goal of contemplation (tafakkur) in them? He said: To recite them and comprehend them.
2:164.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Contemplation'

2:164.arabic: الأصل الأول: معرفة وجوده تعالى وأول ما يستضاء به من الأنوار ويسلك من طريق الاعتبار ما أرشد إليه القرآن فليس بعد بيان الله سبحانه بيان وقد قال تعالى ألم نجعل الأرض مهادا والجبال أوتادا وخلقناكم أزواجا وجعلنا نومكم سباتا وجعلنا الليل لباسا وجعلنا النهار معاشا وبنينا فوقكم سبعا شدادا وجعلنا سراجا وهاجا وأنزلنا من المعصرات ماء ثجاجا لنخرج به حبا ونباتا وجنات ألفافا وقال تعالى إن في خلق السموات والأرض واختلاف الليل والنهار والفلك التي تجري في البحر بما ينفع الناس وما أنزل الله من السماء من ماء فأحيا
2:164.english: The First Foundation: Knowledge of His Existence, the Most High, and the first of the lights by which illumination is sought and the path of reflection that is followed is what the Quran has guided to, for there is no explanation after the explanation of Allah, the Glorified. And He, the Most High, has said: 'Have We not made the earth a resting place, and the mountains as pegs, and created you in pairs, and made your sleep a repose, and made the night a covering, and made the day for livelihood, and built above you seven firm ones, and made a blazing lamp, and sent down from the rain-clouds pouring water to bring forth thereby grain and vegetation and gardens of dense growth?' And He, the Most High, said: 'Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day and the ships that sail in the sea with that which benefits people, and what Allah has sent down from the sky of water, then He gives life thereby to the earth after its death and disperses therein every moving creature, and the directing of the winds and the clouds subjected between the heaven and the earth are signs for a people who use reason.' And He, the Most High, said: 'Have you not seen how Allah created seven heavens in layers and made the moon therein a light and made the sun a lamp? And Allah has caused you to grow from the earth a growth, then He will return you into it and bring you forth a bringing forth.' And He, the Most High, said: 'Then do you see that which you emit? Is it you who creates it, or are We the Creator?' up to His saying: 'for the grateful.' So it is not hidden from one who possesses the slightest bit of intellect, if he reflects with the least thought upon the content of these verses and turns his gaze upon the wonders of Allah's creation in the earth and the heavens and the marvels of the innate nature (Fitra) of animals and plants, that this amazing affair and precise arrangement cannot do without a Maker who manages it and an Agent who governs and determines it. Rather, the innate nature (Fitra) of the souls (Nufus) almost testifies to being subdued under His subjugation and directed according to His management. And for that reason, Allah, the Most High, said: 'Is there any doubt concerning Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth?'
2:164.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Foundations of Belief'

2:165.arabic: اعلم أن الأمة مجمعة على أن الحب لله تعالى ولرسوله ﭬ فرض، وكيف يفرض ما لا وجود له وكيف يفسر الحب بالطاعة والطاعة تبع الحب وثمرته؟ فلا بد وأن يتقدم الحب ثم بعد ذلك يطيع من أحب. ويدل على إثبات الحب لله تعالى قوله عز وجل "يحبهم ويحبونه " وقوله تعالى " والذين آمنوا أشد حباً لله " وهو دليل على إثبات الحب وإثبات التفاوت فيه.
2:165.english: Know that the community (Ummah) is unanimous that love for Allah the Exalted and His Messenger (peace be upon him) is obligatory (Fard), and how can something that does not exist be made obligatory, and how can love be interpreted as obedience when obedience follows love and is its fruit? It is necessary that love comes first, and then after that one obeys whom one loves. And what indicates the affirmation of love for Allah the Exalted is His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: "He loves them and they love Him" and His saying: "And those who believe are stronger in love for Allah." This is evidence for affirming love and affirming variation in it.
2:165.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

2:171.arabic: وبالجملة لا يخلو صاحب القلب عن وجد عند سماع القرآن فإن كان القرآن لا يؤثر فيه أصلا ف مثله كمثل الذي ينعق بما لا يسمع إلا دعاء ونداء صم بكم عمي فهم لا يعقلون بل صاحب القلب تؤثر فيه الكلمة من الحكمة يسمعها
2:171.english: In summary, the possessor of the Heart (Qalb) is not devoid of spiritual state (Wajd) upon hearing the Quran. If the Quran does not affect him at all, then his likeness is like the one who calls out to that which hears nothing but a call and a cry: deaf, dumb, blind - so they do not understand. Rather, the possessor of the Heart is affected by a word of wisdom that he hears.
2:171.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

2:172.arabic: وأن التقاط الفتات مهور الحور العين وأن يشكر الله تعالى بقلبه على ما أطعمه فيرى الطعام نعمة منه قال الله تعالى كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم واشكروا لله ومهما أكل حلالا قال الحمد لله الذي بنعمته تتم الصالحات وتنزل البركات اللهم أطعمنا طيبا واستعملنا صالحا
2:172.english: And gathering the crumbs is the dowry of the Houris (Al-Hur Al-'Ayn), and that he thanks Allah the Exalted with his heart (Qalb) for what He has fed him, so he sees the food as a blessing (Ni'mah) from Him. Allah the Exalted said: 'Eat of the good things (Tayyibat) We have provided for you and give thanks to Allah.' And whenever he eats something lawful (Halal), he says: 'Praise be to Allah by whose blessing (Ni'mah) good deeds are completed and blessings (Barakat) descend. O Allah, feed us good (Tayyib) and employ us in righteousness (Salih).'
2:172.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Manners of Eating'

2:172.arabic: وقال إن الله تعالى أمر المؤمنين بما أمر به المرسلين فقال يا أيها الذين آمنوا كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم
2:172.english: And he said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted commanded the believers with what He commanded the messengers, so He said: O you who have believed, eat from the good things (ṭayyibāt) which We have provided for you.
2:172.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Earning'

2:172.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
2:172.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Whatever is in the Quran of 'O you who have believed' is in the Torah 'O you poor ones (al-Masakin)'.
2:172.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

2:174.arabic:
هذه قد خطبها منه عبد الملك بن مروان لابنه الوليد حين ولاه العهد فأبى سعيد أن يزوجه، فلم يزل عبد الملك يحتال على سعيد حتى ضربه مائة سوط في يوم بارد وصب عليه جرة ماء وألبسه جبة صوف. فاستعجال سعيد في الزفاف تلك الليلة يعرفك غائلة الشهوة ووجوب المبادرة في الدين إلى تطفئة نارها بالنكاح رضي الله تعالى عنه ورحمه.

بيان فضيلة من يخالف شهوة الفرج والعين

اعلم أن هذه الشهوة هي أغلب الشهوات على الإنسان وأعصاها عند الهيجان على العقل، إلا أن مقتضاها قبيح يستحيا منه ويخشى من اقتحامه، وامتناع أكثر الناس عن مقت
2:174.english:
This one was proposed to him by Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan for his son al-Walid when he appointed him as heir, but Sa'id refused to marry her to him, so Abd al-Malik kept scheming against Sa'id until he struck him one hundred lashes on a cold day and poured a jar of water on him and clothed him in a woolen cloak. Sa'id's hastening in the wedding that night makes known to you the consequence of desire and the obligation in the religion to hasten to extinguish its fire with marriage, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him and have mercy on him.

Explanation of the virtue of one who opposes the desire of the private parts and the eye.

Know that this desire is the most dominant of desires upon the human and the most stubborn at arousal against the intellect, except that its requirement is ugly, one is ashamed of it and fears from plunging into it, and the abstention of most people from its requirement is either due to incapacity or fear or shame or preservation of his body, and there is no reward in any of that because it is preferring one of the shares of the soul (Nafs) over another share. Yes, from protection is that he is not able, so in these obstacles there is benefit, and it is repelling sin, for whoever leaves fornication, his sin is repelled by whatever reason he left it? And indeed the excellence and abundant reward is in leaving it out of fear of Allah the Exalted with capability and removal of obstacles and facilitation of means, especially at the sincerity of desire, and this is the rank of the truthful ones (Siddiqin). And for that reason he said, "Whoever loves, then remains chaste, then conceals, then dies, he is a martyr"[69] and he said, "Seven whom Allah will shade on the Day of Resurrection under the shade of His Throne on a day when there is no shade except His shade - and among them he mentioned" a man whom a woman of beauty and lineage called to herself, so he said, 'Indeed I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds'"[70] and the story of Yusuf, peace be upon him, and his abstention from Zulaykha with capability and with her desire is known, and Allah the Exalted praised him for that in His Mighty Book, and he is an imam for everyone who is granted success in striving against Satan in this great desire.

And it was narrated that Sulayman ibn Yasar was among the most beautiful of people in face, so a woman entered upon him and his soul (Nafs) asked him, so he abstained from her and went out fleeing from his house and left her in it. Sulayman said: So I saw that night in a dream Yusuf, peace be upon him, and as if I am saying to him, 'Are you Yusuf?' He said: 'Yes, I am Yusuf who intended, and you are Sulayman who did not intend,' pointing to His saying the Exalted, "And indeed she desired him and he desired her, had he not seen the proof of his Lord." And from him also is what is more amazing than this. And that is that he went out from al-Madinah as a pilgrim and with him was a companion of his until they alighted at al-Abwa', so his companion stood and took the food bag and set off to the market to buy something, and Sulayman sat in the tent and he was among the most beautiful of people in face and the most pious of them, so an Arab woman from the scarcity of the mountain saw him and descended to him until she stood before him - and upon her was the face veil and the gloves - so she unveiled from a face for her as if it were a piece of moon and said, 'Congratulate me;' so he thought she wanted
2:174.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Harms of the Tongue'

2:174.arabic:
وهو من قبائح الذنوب وفواحش العيوب. قال اسمعيل بن واسط: سمعت أبا  بكر  الصديق
رضي الله عنه يخطب بعد وفاة رسول الله ﭬ فقال قام فينا رسول الله ﭬ  مقامي  هذا
عام أول -ثم بكى وقال "إياكم والكذب فإنه مع الفجور وهما في  النار"[137]  وقال
أبو أمامة: قال رسول الله ﭬ "إن الكذب باب من أبواب النفاق"[138]. وقال  الحسن:
كان يقال  إن  من  النفاق  اختلاف  السر  والعلانية،  والقول  والعمل،  والمدخل
والمخرج، وإن الأصل الذي بني عليه النفاق الكذب. وقال ﭬ "كبرت  خيانة  أن  تحدث
أخاك حديثاً هو لك به مصدق وأنت له به ك
2:174.english: [144] Hadith: Three whom Allah will not speak to on the Day of Resurrection and will not look at: the one who reminds of his gift, the one who sells his merchandise with false oath, and the one who lets his garment drag. Reported by Muslim from the narration of Abu Dharr.
2:174.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

2:174.arabic: وثلاثة يشنؤهم الله: التاجر أو البياع الحلاف، والفقير المختال والبخل المنان"[146] وقال ﭬ "ويل للذي يحدث فيكذب ليضحك به القوم ويل له ويل له"[147] وقال ﭬ "رأيت كأن رجلاً جاءني فقال لي قم فقمت معه، فإذا أنا برجلين أحدهما قائم والآخر جالس، بيد القائم كلوب من حديد يلقمه في شدق الجالس فيجذبه حتى يبلغ كاهله، ثم يجذبه فليقمه الجانب الآخر فيمده فإذا مده رجع الآخر كما كان، فقلت للذي أقامني ما هذا؟ فقال: هذا رجل كذاب يعذب في قبره إلى يوم القيامة"[148] وعن عبد الله بن جراد قال: سألت رسول الله ﭬ فقلت: يا رسول
2:174.english: And three whom Allah hates: the merchant or the swearing seller, the poor person who is arrogant, and the miser who reminds of favors.[146] And he (peace be upon him) said: "Woe to the one who narrates and lies to make people laugh, woe to him, woe to him."[147] And he (peace be upon him) said: "I saw as if a man came to me and said to me: 'Get up,' so I got up with him, and behold I saw two men, one standing and the other sitting, in the hand of the standing one is an iron hook which he puts into the mouth of the sitting one and pulls it until it reaches his collarbone, then he pulls it to the other side and stretches it, and when he stretches it, the other returns as he was. I said to the one who made me stand: 'What is this?' He said: 'This is a liar being punished in his grave until the Day of Resurrection.'"[148] And from Abdullah ibn Jarad, he said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and said: O Messenger of Allah, does a believer commit adultery? He said: "That may happen." I said: O Prophet of Allah, does a believer lie? He said: "No." Then he (peace be upon him) followed it with the saying of Allah the Exalted: "Only those who do not believe in the signs of Allah fabricate falsehood."[149] And Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) supplicating and saying in his supplication: "O Allah, purify my heart (Qalb) from hypocrisy, my private parts from adultery, and my tongue from lying."[150] And he (peace be upon him) said: "Three whom Allah will not speak to, nor look at, nor purify, and for them is a painful punishment: an old adulterer, a lying king, and a poor person who is arrogant."[151]
2:174.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

2:177.arabic: والثاني: أنه يكمل بأعمال الطاعات ولا يدري وجودها على الكمال أما العمل فقد قال الله تعالى: ﴿ إنما المؤمنون الذين آمنوا بالله ورسوله ثم لم يرتابوا وجاهدوا بأموالهم وأنفسهم في سبيل الله أولئك هم الصادقون ﴾ {} فيكون الشك في هذا الصدق وكذلك قال الله تعالى: ﴿ ولكن البر من آمن بالله واليوم الآخر والملائكة والكتاب والنبيين ﴾ {} فشرط عشرين وصفا كالوفاء بالعهد والصبر على الشدائد ثم قال تعالى: ﴿ أولئك الذين صدقوا ﴾ {} وقد قال تعالى: ﴿ يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ ل
2:177.english: The second: that it (faith) is perfected by works of obedience (al-Ta'at) and one does not know their existence in perfection. As for the work, Allah the Exalted has said: 'Indeed, the believers are those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and then have not doubted and have struggled with their wealth and their selves in the path of Allah. Those are the truthful ones.' So the doubt is in this truthfulness. And likewise Allah the Exalted has said: 'But righteousness (al-Birr) is from one who believes in Allah and the Last Day and the angels and the Book and the prophets' and stipulated twenty descriptions such as fulfillment of the covenant (al-'Ahd) and patience (al-Sabr) in hardships. Then He the Exalted said: 'Those are the ones who have been truthful.' And Allah the Exalted has said: 'Allah raises those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge by degrees.' And He the Exalted has said: 'Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought' the verse. And He the Exalted has said: 'They are degrees with Allah.' And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Faith (al-Iman) is naked and its garment is God-consciousness (al-Taqwa).' And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Faith (al-Iman) has between seventy and seventy-nine branches, the lowest of them is removing harm from the road.' So this is what indicates the connection of the perfection of faith (al-Iman) with works.
2:177.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

2:178.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
2:178.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'What is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)".'
2:178.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

2:183.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
2:183.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'What is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)".'
2:183.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

2:185.arabic: ومنها التدريج في البيان كقوله عز وجل ﴿ شهر رمضان الذي أنزل فيه القرآن ﴾ {} إذ لم يظهر به أنه ليل أو نهار وبان بقوله عز وجل ﴿ إنا أنزلناه في ليلة مباركة ﴾ {} ولم يظهر به أي ليلة فظهر بقوله تعالى ﴿ إنا أنزلناه في ليلة القدر ﴾ {} وربما يظن في الظاهر الاختلاف بين هذه الآيات فهذا وأمثاله مما لا يغني فيه إلا النقل والسماع فالقرآن من أوله إلى آخره غير خال عن هذا الجنس لأنه أنزل بلغة العرب فكان مشتملا على أصناف كلامهم من إيجاز وتطويل وإضمار وحذف وإبدال وتقديم وتأخير ليكون ذلك مفحما لهم ومعجزا في حقهم فك
2:185.english: And among them is the gradual clarification in the statement, as in His Exalted saying: 'The month of Ramadan in which was revealed the Quran' {} since it did not become clear by it whether it was night or day, and it became clear by His Exalted saying: 'Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night' {} and it did not become clear by it which night, so it became clear by His saying: 'Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr)' {} and perhaps it is thought in the apparent meaning there is difference between these verses, so this and its like are matters in which nothing suffices except transmission (Naql) and hearing (Samāʿ). The Quran from its beginning to its end is not free from this type because it was revealed in the language of the Arabs, so it contained the varieties of their speech from brevity (Ījāz) and length (Taṭwīl), implication (Iḍmār) and omission (Ḥadhf), substitution (Ibdāl) and precedence (Taqdīm) and postponement (Taʾkhīr), so that would be silencing them and miraculous in their regard. So everyone who is satisfied with understanding the apparent Arabic and hastens to interpret the Quran and does not support himself with hearing and transmission in these matters, then he is among those who interpreted the Quran by his opinion, like that he understands from 'Ummah' the most famous meaning from it, so his nature and opinion incline to it. So when he hears it in another place, he inclines his opinion to what he heard from its famous meaning and abandons following transmission in many of its meanings. So this is what can be prohibited from without understanding the secrets of the meanings as preceded. So when hearing is attained with examples of these matters, the apparent interpretation is known, which is the translation of the words, and that does not suffice in understanding the realities of the meanings, and the difference between the realities of the meanings and the apparent interpretation is grasped with an example, which is that Allah Exalted is He said:
2:185.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

2:186.arabic: الحمد لله الشاملة رأفته العامة رحمته الذي جازى عباده عن ذكرهم بذكرهم فقال تعالى: ﴿ فاذكروني أذكركم ﴾ {} ورغبهم في السؤال والدعاء بأمره فقال: ﴿ ادعوني أستجب لكم ﴾ {} فأطمع المطيع والعاصي والداني والقاصي في الانبساط إلى حضرة جلاله برفع الحاجات والأماني بقوله: ﴿ فإني قريب أجيب دعوة الداع إذا دعان ﴾ {} والصلاة على محمد سيد أنبيائه وعلى آله وأصحابه خيرة أصفيائه وسلم تسليما كثيرا.
2:186.english: Praise be to Allah, whose encompassing compassion and general mercy rewards His servants for their remembrance (Dhikr) with His remembrance (Dhikr), as He the Exalted said: 'So remember Me; I will remember you' (Quran 2:152). And He encouraged them in asking and supplication (Du'a) by His command, saying: 'Call upon Me; I will respond to you' (Quran 40:60). So He gave hope to the obedient and the disobedient, the near and the far, in expanding towards the presence of His majesty by raising needs and desires with His saying: 'For indeed, I am near. I respond to the call (Du'a) of the caller when he calls upon Me' (Quran 2:186). And prayers upon Muhammad, the master of His prophets, and upon his family and companions, the best of His chosen ones, and abundant peace.
2:186.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God

2:186.arabic: (الباب الثاني في آداب الدعاء وفضله وفضل بعض الأدعية المأثورة وفضيلة الاستغفار والصلاة على رسول الله ﭬ) (فضيلة الدعاء) قال الله تعالى: ﴿ وإذا سألك عبادي عني فإني قريب أجيب دعوة الداع إذا دعان فليستجيبوا لي ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ ادعوا ربكم تضرعا وخفية إنه لا يحب المعتدين ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ وقال ربكم ادعوني أستجب لكم إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي سيدخلون جهنم داخرين ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل: ﴿ قل ادعوا الله أو ادعوا الرحمن أيا ما تدعوا فله الأسماء الحسنى ﴾ {} وروى النعمان بن بشير عن النبي ﭬ أنه قال: (إن الدعاء
2:186.english: (The Second Chapter on the Etiquettes of Supplication (Dua) and its Excellence and the Excellence of Some Transmitted Supplications and the Excellence of Seeking Forgiveness (Istighfar) and Sending Blessings upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ) (The Excellence of Supplication (Dua)) Allah the Exalted said: 'And when My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near. I respond to the call of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me...' {} And He the Exalted said: 'Call upon your Lord humbly and in secret. Indeed, He does not like transgressors.' {} And He the Exalted said: 'And your Lord said, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you. Indeed, those who disdain My worship will enter Hell [rendered] contemptible."' {} And He the Glorified and Exalted said: 'Say, "Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Merciful (Ar-Rahman). Whichever [name] you call - to Him belong the best names."' {} And An-Nu'man ibn Bashir narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: ('Supplication (Dua) is the worship (Ibadah).' Then he recited: 'Call upon Me; I will respond to you.' {}[65]) The verse. And he ﷺ said: ('Supplication (Dua) is the marrow of worship (Ibadah)[66]') And Abu Hurairah narrated that he ﷺ said: ('There is nothing more honorable to Allah the Glorified and Exalted than supplication (Dua)[67]') And he ﷺ said: ('The servant (Abd) does not miss from supplication (Dua) one of three: either a sin (Dhanb) is forgiven for him, or a good (Khayr) is hastened for him, or a good (Khayr) is stored for him[68]') And Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: 'Sufficient for supplication (Dua) with righteousness (Birr) is what suffices food from salt.' And he ﷺ said: ('Ask Allah the Exalted from His bounty, for indeed Allah the Exalted loves to be asked, and the best worship (Ibadah) is awaiting relief (Faraj)[69]').
2:186.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication

2:188.arabic: وقال تعالى ولا تأكلوا أموالكم بينكم بالباطل وقال تعالى إن الذين يأكلون أموال اليتامى ظلما الآية وقال تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وذروا ما بقي من الربا إن كنتم مؤمنين ثم قال فإن لم تفعلوا فأذنوا بحرب من الله ورسوله ثم قال وإن تبتم فلكم رءوس أموالكم ثم قال ومن عاد فأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون جعل آكل الربا أول الأمر مؤذنا بمحاربة الله وفي آخره متعرضا للنار والآيات الواردة في الحلال والحرام لا تحصى
2:188.english: And He (Allah), the Exalted, said: 'And do not consume your properties among yourselves unjustly (Bil-Batil).' And He, the Exalted, said: 'Indeed, those who consume the properties of the orphans unjustly...' the verse. And He, the Exalted, said: 'O you who have believed, fear Allah (Taqwa) and give up what remains [due to you] of interest (Riba), if you should be believers.' Then He said: 'But if you do not, then be informed of a war [against you] from Allah and His Messenger.' Then He said: 'And if you repent, then for you are your principal sums.' Then He said: 'And whoever returns [to dealing in interest] - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.' He made the consumer of interest (Riba) at the beginning of the matter announcing war against Allah and at its end exposed to the Fire. And the verses concerning the lawful (Halal) and the unlawful (Haram) are innumerable.
2:188.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

2:189.arabic: وقد نهى الله تعالى عنه وقصة عمر وعبد الرحمن بن عوف فيه مشهورة وقد أوردناها في كتاب آداب الصحبة وكذلك ما روي أن عمر رضي الله عنه تسلق دار رجل فرآه على حالة مكروهة فأنكر عليه فقال يا أمير المؤمنين إن كنت أنا قد عصيت الله من وجه واحد فأنت قد عصيته من ثلاثة أوجه فقال وما هي فقال قد قال تعالى ولا تجسسوا وقد تجسست وقال تعالى وأتوا البيوت من أبوابها وقد تسورت من السطح وقال لا تدخلوا بيوتا غير بيوتكم حتى تستأنسوا وتسلموا على أهلها وما سلمت فتركه عمر وشرط عليه التوبة
2:189.english: And Allah the Exalted has prohibited it, and the story of Umar and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf regarding it is well-known, and we have mentioned it in the Book of the Etiquettes of Companionship. Likewise, what has been narrated that Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) climbed over the wall of a man's house and saw him in a reprehensible state, so he rebuked him. The man said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, if I have disobeyed Allah in one aspect, you have disobeyed Him in three aspects.' He said: 'And what are they?' He said: 'Allah the Exalted has said: "And do not spy" (Quran 49:12), and you have spied. And He has said: "And enter the houses from their doors" (Quran 2:189), and you have climbed over from the roof. And He has said: "Do not enter houses other than your own until you have announced yourselves and greeted their inhabitants" (Quran 24:27), and you did not greet.' So Umar left him and stipulated repentance upon him.
2:189.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

2:189.arabic: وروي أن عمر رضي الله عنه كان يعس بالمدينة من الليل فسمع صوت رجل في بيت يتغنى فتسور عليه فوجده عنده امرأة وعنده خمر فقال يا عدو الله أظننت أن الله يسترك وأنت على معصيته فقال وأنت يا أمير المؤمنين فلا تعجل فإن كنت قد عصيت الله واحدة فقد عصيت الله في ثلاثا قال الله تعالى ولا تجسسوا وقد تجسست وقال الله تعالى وليس البر بأن تأتوا البيوت من ظهورها وقد تسورت علي وقد قال الله تعالى لا تدخلوا بيوتا غير بيوتكم الآية وقد دخلت بيتي بغير إذن ولا سلام فقال عمر رضي الله عنه هل عندك من خير إن عفوت عنك قال نعم وا
2:189.english: And it was narrated that Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) was patrolling in Medina at night when he heard a man's voice in a house singing, so he climbed over the wall to him and found him with a woman and with wine. He said: 'O enemy of Allah, did you think that Allah would conceal you while you are in disobedience to Him?' The man said: 'And you, O Commander of the Faithful, do not hasten. If I have disobeyed Allah in one matter, you have disobeyed Allah in three matters. Allah the Exalted said: "And do not spy" (Quran 49:12), and you have spied. And Allah the Exalted said: "And it is not righteousness (Al-Birr) that you come to the houses from their backs" (Quran 2:189), and you have climbed over the wall to me. And Allah the Exalted said: "Do not enter houses other than your own houses" (Quran 24:27), and you have entered my house without permission and without greeting.' Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'Do you have any good if I pardon you?' He said: 'Yes, by Allah, O Commander of the Faithful, if you pardon me, I will never return to the like of it ever.' So he pardoned him and left and abandoned him.
2:189.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

2:190.arabic: در  من المشركين فقال "لا تسبوا هؤلاء فإنه لا  يخلص  إليهم  شيء  مما  تقولون  وتؤذون الأحياء ألا إن البذاء لؤم"[62] وقال ﭬ "ليس المؤمن  بالطعان  ولا  اللعان  ولا الفاحش ولا البذي"[63] وقال ﭬ "الجنة حرام على كل فاحش أن يدخلها"[64]  وقال  ﭬ "أربعة يؤذون أهل النار في النار  على  ما  بهم  من  الأذى  يسعون  بين  الحميم والجحيم يدعون بالويل والثبور: رجل يسيل فوه قيحاً ودماً فيقال له ما بال  الأبعد قد آذاناً على ما بنا من الأذى؟ فيقول إن الأبعد كان  ينظر  إلى  كل  كلمة  قذعة خبيثة فيستلذها كما يستلذ الر
2:190.english: From the polytheists, he said: "Do not curse these, for nothing of what you say reaches them, and you harm the living. Indeed, obscenity is baseness."[62] And he (peace be upon him) said: "The believer is not one who slanders, nor curses, nor is obscene, nor foul-mouthed."[63] And he (peace be upon him) said: "Paradise is forbidden for every obscene person to enter."[64] And he (peace be upon him) said: "Four will harm the people of Hell in Hell, despite the harm upon them; they run between scalding water and blazing fire, calling out with woe and ruin: a man whose mouth flows with pus and blood, and it is said to him: 'What is with the distant one who has harmed us despite the harm upon us?' He says: 'The distant one used to look at every foul, vile word and delight in it as one delights in obscenity.'"[65] And he (peace be upon him) said to Aisha: "O Aisha, if obscenity were a man, he would be an evil man."[66] And he (peace be upon him) said: "Obscenity and explicit disclosure are two branches from the branches of hypocrisy."[67] It is possible that by 'explicit disclosure' is meant in matters of religion and in the attributes of God, the Exalted, for presenting that summarily to the ears of the common people is preferable to exaggeration in its explanation; since from the utmost explanation of it may arise doubts and whisperings, so if it is summarized, the hearts (Qulub) hasten to acceptance and do not become disturbed. But its mention coupled with obscenity resembles that what is intended by it is publicizing what a person is ashamed to disclose, for the better in such a case is overlooking and ignoring, not uncovering and explaining. And he (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, God does not love the obscene, excessively obscene one who shouts in the markets."[68] And Jabir ibn Samura said: I was sitting with the Prophet (peace be upon him) and my father was before me, and he (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, obscenity and excessive obscenity are not from Islam in anything, and the best of people in Islam are the best of them in character."[69] And Ibrahim ibn Maysara said: It is said that the obscene, excessively obscene one will be brought on the Day of Resurrection in the form of a dog or inside a dog. And Al-Ahnaf ibn Qais said: Shall I not inform you of the worst disease: the foul-mouthed tongue and the base character.
2:190.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

2:190.arabic: وَمَرَّ الْحَسَنُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا بِقَوْمٍ مِنَ الْمَسَاكِينِ الَّذِينَ يَسْأَلُونَ النَّاسَ عَلَى الطَّرِيقِ وَقَدْ نَشَرُوا كِسْرًا عَلَى الْأَرْضِ فِي الرَّمْلِ وَهُمْ يَأْكُلُونَ وَهُوَ عَلَى بَغْلَتِهِ فَسَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِمْ فَقَالُوا لَهُ هَلُمَّ إِلَى الْغَدَاءِ يَا ابْنَ بِنْتِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَقَالَ نَعَمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُسْتَكْبِرِينَ فَنَزَلَ وَقَعَدَ مَعَهُمْ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ وَأَكَلَ ثُمَّ سَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَرَكِ
2:190.english: And Al-Hasan ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with them both) passed by a group of the poor (Masakin) who ask people on the road, and they had spread crumbs on the ground in the sand and they were eating while he was on his mule. He greeted them, and they said to him: 'Come to lunch, O son of the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him).' He said: 'Yes, indeed Allah does not love the arrogant (Mustakbirin).' So he dismounted and sat with them on the ground and ate, then he greeted them and rode and said: 'I have answered you, so answer me.' They said: 'Yes.' So he promised them a known time, and they attended, and he presented to them the finest food and sat eating with them.
2:190.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Manners of Eating'

2:190.arabic: وَيَرْكَبُ وَيَقُولُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُسْتَكْبِرِينَ
2:190.english: And he rides and says: Indeed, Allah does not love the arrogant ones.
2:190.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Etiquette of Seclusion'

2:195.arabic: فإن قيل فما معنى قوله تعالى ولا تلقوا بأيديكم إلى التهلكة قلنا لا خلاف في أن المسلم الواحد له أن يهجم على صف الكفار ويقاتل وإن علم أنه يقتل وهذا ربما يظن أنه مخالف لموجب الآية وليس كذلك فقد قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما ليس التهلكة ذلك بل ترك النفقة في طاعة الله تعالى أي من لم يفعل ذلك فقد أهلك نفسه وقال البراء بن عازب التهلكة هو أن يذنب الذنب ثم يقول لا يتاب علي وقال أبو عبيدة هو أن يذنب ثم لا يعمل بعده خيرا حتى يهلك وإذا جاز أن يقاتل الكفار حتى يقتل جاز أيضا له ذلك في الحسبة ولكن لو علم أنه لا ن
2:195.english: If it is said: What is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: 'And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction'? We say: There is no disagreement that a single Muslim may charge into the ranks of the disbelievers and fight even if he knows he will be killed. This might be thought to contradict the requirement of the verse, but it is not so. Indeed, Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: 'That is not the destruction; rather, it is abandoning spending in obedience to Allah, the Exalted—meaning, whoever does not do that has destroyed himself.' And Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib said: 'The destruction is that one commits a sin then says: I will not be forgiven.' And Abu 'Ubaydah said: 'It is that one sins then does not do any good afterward until he perishes.' And if it is permissible to fight the disbelievers until one is killed, then it is also permissible for him in enjoining good and forbidding evil (al-Hisbah). But if he knows there is no harm from his charge against the disbelievers, like a blind man throwing himself upon the ranks or a disabled person, then that is forbidden and falls under the generality of the verse of destruction. And it is only permissible for him to advance if he knows he will fight until he is killed or knows that he will break the hearts (Qulub) of the disbelievers by their witnessing his bravery and their belief in the rest of the Muslims' lack of concern and their love for martyrdom in the path of Allah, so their strength is broken by that. Likewise, it is permissible for the enforcer of good (al-Muhtasib), indeed recommended for him, to expose himself to beating and to killing if his enforcement has an effect in lifting the evil or in breaking the prestige of the corrupt person or in strengthening the hearts (Qulub) of the people of the religion.
2:195.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

2:196.arabic: وإن أضاف إلى المشي الإحرام من دويرة أهله فقد قيل إن ذلك من إتمام الحج. قاله عمر وعلي وابن مسعود رضي الله عنهم في معنى قوله عز وجل - وإتموا الحج والعمرة لله - وقال بعض العلماء الركوب أفضل لما فيه من الإنفاق والمؤنة ولأنه أبعد عن ضجر النفس وأقل لأذاه وأقرب إلى سلامته وتمام حجه وهذا عند التحقيق ليس مخالفا للأول بل ينبغي أن يفصل ويقال من سهل عليه المشي فهو أفضل فإن كان يضعف ويؤدى به ذلك إلى سوء الخلق وقصور عن عمل فالركوب له أفضل كما أن الصوم للمسافر أفضل وللمريض ما لم يفض إلى ضعف وسوء خلق.
2:196.english: And if he adds to walking the assumption of Ihram (pilgrimage state) from the vicinity of his family, it has been said that this is from the completion of Hajj. This was said by Umar, Ali, and Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with them) regarding the meaning of His (Allah's) saying, exalted is He: 'And complete the Hajj and Umrah for Allah.
