But if you are prevented, then [offer] what can be obtained with ease of sacrificial animals. And do not shave your heads until the sacrificial animal has reached its place of slaughter. And whoever among you is ill or has an ailment of the head [making shaving necessary] must offer a ransom of fasting [three days] or charity or sacrifice. And when you are secure, then whoever performs Umrah [during the Hajj months] followed by Hajj [offers] what can be obtained with ease of sacrificial animals. And whoever cannot find [or afford such an animal] - then a fast of three days during Hajj and of seven when you have returned [home]. Those are ten complete [days]. This is for those whose family is not in the area of al-Masjid al-Haram. And fear Allah and know that Allah is severe in penalty.' And some scholars said riding is better due to the expenditure and effort involved, and because it is farther from the annoyance of the Soul (Nafs) and less for its harm and closer to its safety and the completion of his Hajj. And this, upon verification, is not contradictory to the first, but rather it should be detailed and said: whoever finds walking easy, it is better. But if he weakens and that leads him to bad character and deficiency in action, then riding is better for him, just as fasting is better for the traveler and for the sick person, as long as it does not lead to weakness and bad character.
2:196.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

2:196.arabic: الثالث التمتع وهو أن يجاوز الميقات محرما بعمرة ويتحلل بمكة ويتمتع بالمحظورات إلى وقت الحج ثم يحرم بالحج ولا يكون متمتعا إلا بخمس شرائط: أحدها أن لا يكون من حاضري المسجد الحرام وحاضره من كان منه على مسافة لا تقصر فيها الصلاة. الثاني أن يقدم العمرة على الحج. الثالث أن تكون عمرته في أشهر الحج. الرابع أن لا يرجع إلى ميقات الحج ولا إلى مثل مسافته لإحرام الحج. الخامس أن يكون حجه وعمرته عن شخص واحد فإذا وجدت هذه الأوصاف كان متمتعا ولزمه دم شاة فإن لم يجد فصيام ثلاثة أيام في الحج قبل يوم النحر متفرقة أو
2:196.english: The third is the Enjoyment (Tamattu') which is that one passes the designated point (Miqat) in the state of consecration (Ihram) for the 'Umrah and becomes free from restrictions (Tahallul) in Makkah and enjoys the prohibited things until the time of Hajj, then enters the state of consecration (Ihram) for Hajj. One is not considered a performer of Enjoyment (Tamattu') except with five conditions: First, that he not be from the residents of the Sacred Mosque (Masjid al-Haram), and its resident is one who is from it at a distance where prayer is not shortened. Second, that he perform the 'Umrah before the Hajj. Third, that his 'Umrah be in the months of Hajj. Fourth, that he not return to the designated point (Miqat) of Hajj nor to a distance equivalent to it for the consecration (Ihram) of Hajj. Fifth, that his Hajj and 'Umrah be for one person. If these descriptions are found, he is a performer of Enjoyment (Tamattu') and a sheep as sacrifice (Dam) is obligatory upon him. If he does not find [it], then fasting three days during Hajj before the Day of Sacrifice (Yawm al-Nahr), separately or consecutively, and seven when he returns to the homeland. And if he does not fast the three until he returns to the homeland, he fasts the ten consecutively or separately. The substitute (Badal) for the sacrifice (Dam) of the Combined (Qiran) and the Enjoyment (Tamattu') is the same, and the best is the Single (Ifrad), then the Enjoyment (Tamattu'), then the Combined (Qiran).
2:196.topic: Al-Ghazali on the outer and inner dimensions of worship, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

2:197.arabic: وأحسنوا رحمكم الله منها الرحلة بأحسن ما بحضرتكم من النقلة وتزودوا فإن خير الزاد التقوى إنما الدنيا كفىء ظلال قلص فذهب بينا ابن آدم في الدنيا ينافس وهو قدير العين إذ دعاه الله بقدره ورماه بيوم حتفه فسلبه آثاره ودنياه وصير لقوم آخرين مصانعه ومغناه إن الدنيا لا تسر بقدر ما تضر إنها تسر قليلا وتحزن طويلا.
2:197.english: And do well, may Allah have mercy on you, in the journey from it with the best of what is present with you of provisions, and take provision, for indeed the best of provisions is God-consciousness (Taqwa). Indeed, the world is like the shade of a cloud that receded and vanished while the son of Adam was competing in the world, and he was powerful in eye, when Allah called him by His decree and cast him with his day of death, so He stripped him of his traces and his world, and made for other people his constructions and his songs. Indeed, the world does not delight as much as it harms; it delights little and grieves long.
2:197.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Book of Repentance'

2:198.arabic: وقال تعالى: ﴿ فإذا أفضتم من عرفات فاذكروا الله عند المشعر الحرام واذكروه كما هداكم ﴾ {}
2:198.english: And He, the Exalted, said: 'And when you have departed from Arafat, then remember Allah (Dhikr) at the Sacred Monument (Mash'ar al-Haram), and remember Him as He has guided you.'
2:198.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith

2:200.arabic: وقال عز وجل: ﴿ فإذا قضيتم مناسككم فاذكروا الله كذكركم آباءكم أو أشد ذكرا ﴾ {}
2:200.english: And the Almighty said: 'So when you have completed your rites, then remember Allah (Dhikr) as you remember your fathers or with stronger remembrance (Dhikr).'
2:200.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith

2:201.arabic: ربنا آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة وقنا عذاب النار
2:201.english: Our Lord, grant us good in this world and good in the Hereafter and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.
2:201.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter

2:204.arabic: الصدق الثانى في النية والإرادة ويرجع ذلك إلى الإخلاص وهو أن لا يكون له باعث في الحركات والسكنات إلا الله تعالى فإن مازجه شوب من حظوظ النفس بطل صدق النية وصاحبه يجوز أن يسمى كاذبا كما روينا في فضيلة الإخلاص من حديث الثلاثة حين يسئل العالم ما عملت فيما علمت فقال فعلت كذا وكذا فقال الله تعالى كذبت بل أردت أن يقال فلان عالم حديث الثلاثة حين سأل العالم ماذا عملت فيما علمت الحديث تقدم فإنه لم يكذبه ولم يقل له لم تعمل ولكنه كذبه في إرادته ونيته وقد قال بعضهم الصدق صحة التوحيد في القصد وكذلك قول الله تع
2:204.english: The second truthfulness (Sidq) is in intention (Niyyah) and will (Iradah), and this returns to sincerity (Ikhlas), which is that there should be no motive (Ba'ith) in his movements (Harakat) and stillness (Sakanat) except Allah the Exalted. For if it is mixed with a taint (Shawb) of the desires (Huzuz) of the Soul (Nafs), the truthfulness of intention (Sidq al-Niyyah) is invalidated, and its possessor may be called a liar (Kadhib), as we have narrated in the virtue of sincerity (Ikhlas) from the hadith of the three when the scholar is asked, 'What did you do with what you knew?' He said, 'I did such and such.' So Allah the Exalted said, 'You have lied (Kadhabta), rather you intended that it be said, so-and-so is a scholar.' The hadith of the three when the scholar was asked, 'What did you do with what you knew?' The hadith has preceded. For He did not call him a liar and did not say to him, 'You did not do,' but He called him a liar in his will (Iradah) and intention (Niyyah). And some have said, 'Truthfulness (Sidq) is the soundness of monotheism (Tawhid) in purpose (Qasd).' Likewise, the saying of Allah the Exalted: 'And Allah bears witness that the hypocrites (Munafiqun) are indeed liars (Kadhibun).' And they had said, 'You are the Messenger of Allah,' and this is truthfulness (Sidq), but their lying (Kadhib) is not from where the tongue (Lisan) speaks, but from where the secret (Damir) of the Heart (Qalb) is. And the accusation of lying (Takdhib) pertains to the report (Khabar), and this saying includes reporting by circumstantial evidence (Qarinah al-Hal), for its possessor shows from himself that he believes what he says, so he lied in his indication by circumstantial evidence (Qarinah al-Hal) of what is in his Heart (Qalb), for he lied in that and did not lie in what he utters. So one of the meanings of truthfulness (Sidq) returns to the purity (Khalus) of intention (Niyyah), which is sincerity (Ikhlas). Thus, every truthful person (Sadiq) must necessarily be sincere (Mukhlis).
2:204.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

2:204.arabic: "الأولى" الرياء بأصل الإيمان وهذا أغلظ أبواب الرياء وصاحبه مخلد في النار، وهو الذي يظهر كلمتي الشهادة وباطنه مشحون بالتكذيب ولكنه يرائي بظاهر الإسلام، وهو الذي ذكره الله تعالى في كتابه في مواضع شتى كقوله عز وجل "إذا جاءك المنافقون قالوا نشهد إنك لرسول الله والله يعلم إنك لرسوله والله يشهد إن المنافقين لكاذبون" أي في دلالتهم بقولهم على ضمائرهم وقال تعالى "ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه وهو ألد الخصام وإذا تولى سعى في الأرض ليفسد فيها" الآية وقال تعالى "وإذا لقو
2:204.english: "The First": Ostentation (Riya) with the foundation of faith (Iman), and this is the most severe of the gates of ostentation, and its practitioner is eternally in the Fire (Nar), and he is the one who manifests the two testimonies (Shahadatayn) while his inner self (Batin) is filled with denial (Takdhib) but he shows off with the outward appearance (Zahir) of Islam, and he is the one whom Allah the Exalted mentioned in His Book in various places such as His saying, exalted is He: "When the hypocrites (Munafiqun) come to you, they say: 'We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah.' And Allah knows that you are indeed His Messenger, and Allah bears witness that the hypocrites are indeed liars" - meaning in their indication by their speech of their inner thoughts (Damair) - and He said, exalted is He: "And among the people is he whose speech pleases you in the worldly life (Al-Hayat Al-Dunya) and he calls Allah to witness as to what is in his heart (Qalb), and he is the most severe of adversaries (Aladdu Al-Khisam). And when he turns away, he strives throughout the land to cause corruption therein" - the verse - and He said, exalted is He: "And when they meet you, they say: 'We believe,' but when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you in rage" and He said, exalted is He: "They show off to the people and do not remember Allah except a little, wavering between that." And the verses about them are many. Hypocrisy (Nifaq) used to be abundant in the beginning of Islam among those who entered into the outward appearance of Islam initially for a purpose, and that is something that decreases in our time, but hypocrisy increases among those who secretly slip away from the religion inwardly, so they deny the Garden (Jannah) and the Fire (Nar) and the Abode of the Hereafter (Al-Dar Al-Akhirah) inclining toward the saying of the atheists (Mulhida), or they believe upon the basis of the Sacred Law (Al-Shar') and the rulings inclining toward the people of permissiveness (Ahl Al-Ibaha), or they believe in disbelief (Kufr) or innovation (Bid'ah) while manifesting its opposite, so these are among the hypocrites (Munafiqun) and the ostentatious ones (Mura'iun) who are eternally in the Fire (Nar), and beyond this ostentation there is no ostentation, and the state (Hal) of these is more severe than the state of the open disbelievers (Kuffar Al-Mujahirun), for they have combined the disbelief (Kufr) of the inner self (Batin) and the hypocrisy (Nifaq) of the outward appearance (Zahir).
2:204.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

2:206.arabic: الوجه الثاني: الذي تعظم به رذيلة الكبر أنه يدعو إلى مخالفة الله تعالى في أوامره، لأن المتكبر إذا سمع الحق من عبد من عباد الله استنكف عن قبوله وتشمر لجحده، ولذلك ترى المناظرين في مسائل الدين يزعمون أنهم يتباحثون عن أسرار الدين ثم إنهم يتجاحدون تجاحد المتكبرين، ومهما اتضح الحق على لسان واحد منهم أنف الآخر من قبوله، وتشمر لجحده واحتال لدفعه بما يقدر عليه من التلبيس وذلك من أخلاق الكافرين والمنافقين، إذ وصفهم الله تعالى فقال "وقال الذين كفروا لا تسمعوا لهذا القرآن والغوا فيه لعلكم تغلبون" فكل من ينا
2:206.english: The second aspect: that by which the vileness of arrogance (Kibr) is magnified is that it calls to opposing Allah the Exalted in His commands, because the arrogant one, when he hears the truth from a servant (Abd) among the servants of Allah, disdains accepting it and prepares for its denial. Therefore, you see those who debate in matters of religion claiming that they are investigating the secrets of religion, yet they deny each other with the denial of the arrogant. Whenever the truth becomes clear on the tongue of one of them, the other is too proud (Anif) to accept it, and prepares for its denial and schemes to repel it with whatever he can of deception. That is from the character traits of the disbelievers and hypocrites, as Allah the Exalted described them, saying: "And those who disbelieve say: 'Do not listen to this Quran and cause disruption in it that you may overcome.'" So everyone who debates for victory and silencing, not to seize the truth if he attains it, has shared with them in this character trait. Likewise, this is carried over to the pride (Anafah) from accepting admonition, as Allah the Exalted said: "And when it is said to him, 'Fear Allah (Ittaqi Allah),' pride (Al-'Izzah) seizes him with sin." And it is narrated from Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he recited it and said: "Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we return." A man stood up commanding good (Al-Ma'ruf) and was killed, then another stood up and said: "They kill those who command justice (Al-Qist) among the people," and the arrogant one who opposed him and the one who commanded him were killed out of arrogance. And Ibn Mas'ud said: "It is enough sin for a man when it is said to him, 'Fear Allah (Ittaqi Allah),' and he says: 'Mind your own self!'" And the Prophet, peace be upon him, said to a man: "Eat with your right hand," he said: "I cannot," so the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "May you not be able," and nothing prevented him except his arrogance (Kibr). He said: "So he did not raise it after that," meaning his hand became impaired. Therefore, his arrogance (Takabbur) over the creation is great because it will call him to be arrogant (Takabbur) over the command of Allah. Indeed, Iblis was made an example of this, and what He narrated of his states is only to take lesson from it, for he said: "I am better than him," and this arrogance (Kibr) is by lineage because he said: "I am better than him; You created me from fire and created him from clay." That carried him to refuse the prostration that Allah the Exalted commanded him, and its beginning was arrogance (Kibr) over Adam and envy for him, which dragged him to arrogance (Takabbur) over the command of Allah the Exalted, and that was the cause of his destruction forever. So this is a great affliction from the afflictions of arrogance (Kibr) over the servants. Therefore, the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, explained arrogance (Kibr) with these two afflictions when Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas asked him, saying: "O Messenger of Allah, I am a man to whom beauty has been made beloved, as you see; is that from arrogance (Kibr)?" He said, peace be upon him: "No, and"
2:206.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

2:207.arabic: فأنزل الله تعالى "ومن الناس من يشري نفسه ابتغاء مرضات الله والله رؤوف بالعباد"[103] وعن أبي الحسن الأنطاكي: أنه اجتمع عنده نيف وثلاثون نفساً -وكانوا في قرية بقرب الري- ولهم أرغفة معدودة لم تشبع جميعهم "فكسروا الرغفان وأطفئوا السراج وجلسوا للطعام، فلما رفع فإذا الطعام بحاله ولم يأكل أحد منه شيئاً إيثاراً لصاحبه على نفسه.
2:207.english: So Allah the Exalted revealed: "And among the people is he who sells his soul (Nafs) seeking the pleasure (Rida) of Allah, and Allah is Kind (Ra'uf) to the servants." [103] And from Abu al-Hasan al-Antaki: that there gathered at his place more than thirty souls (Nafs) - and they were in a village near Ray - and they had counted loaves that would not satisfy all of them, "so they broke the loaves and extinguished the lamp and sat for the food, and when it was lifted, behold the food was in its state and no one had eaten anything from it, preferring (Ithar) their companion over themselves.
2:207.book_title: Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth
2:207.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

2:207.arabic: [103]  حديث بات علي على فراش رسول الله ﭬ فأوحى الله إلى جبريل وميكائيل إني آخيت بينكما وجعلت عمر أحدكما أطول من الآخر الحديث في نزول قوله تعالى ومن الناس من يشري نفسه ابتغاء مرضات الله أخرجه أحمد مختصرا من حديث ابن عباس شرى على نفسه فلبس ثوب النبي ﭬ ثم نام مكانه الحديث وليس فيه ذكر جبريل وميكائيل ولم أقف لهذه الزيادة على أصل وفيه أبو بلج مختلف فيه والحديث منكر.
2:207.english: Hadith: Ali slept on the bed of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), so Allah revealed to Gabriel and Michael: 'I have made brotherhood between you two and made the life of one of you longer than the other.' The hadith is regarding the revelation of His saying, the Exalted: 'And among the people is he who sells (yashri) his soul (nafs) seeking the pleasure (mardat) of Allah.' It was reported by Ahmad in a concise form from the narration of Ibn Abbas: 'He sold (shara) upon his soul (nafs), so he wore the garment of the Prophet (peace be upon him) and then slept in his place.' The hadith does not contain mention of Gabriel and Michael, and I have not found a source for this addition, and in it is Abu Balj, who is disputed, and the hadith is rejected (munkar).
2:207.book_title: Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth
2:207.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

2:208.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
2:208.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Whatever is in the Quran of 'O you who have believed' is in the Torah 'O you poor ones (al-Masakin)'.
2:208.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

2:212.arabic: واستثنى في خمسة اشياء في الاغناء والاجابة والرزق والمغفرة والتوبة فقال تعالى: ﴿ فسوف يغنيكم الله من فضله ان شاء ﴾ {} وقال فيكشف ما تدعون اليه ان شاء - وقال يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب وقال: ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء وقال: ويتوب الله على من يشاء وهو خلق من اخلاق الربوبية اذ قال تعالى: ﴿ والله شكور حليم ﴾ {}
2:212.english: And He made exceptions in five things: in enrichment, in answering, in provision (Rizq), in forgiveness, and in repentance. So He, the Exalted, said: 'Then Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills' {} and He said: 'And He removes what you call to if He wills' - and He said: 'He provides (Yarzuq) to whom He wills without account' and He said: 'And He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills' and He said: 'And Allah turns in repentance (Yatūbu) to whom He wills.' And this is a character from the characters of Lordship (Rubūbiyyah), since He, the Exalted, said: 'And Allah is Appreciative (Shakūr), Forbearing (Halīm)' {}.
2:212.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

2:213.arabic: وكان إذا نزل به الأمر فوض الأمر إلى الله وتبرأ من الحول والقوة واستنزل الهدى فيقول اللهم أرني الحق حقا فأتبعه وأرني المنكر منكرا وأرزقني اجتنابه وأعذني من أن يشتبه علي فأتبع هواي بغير هدى منك واجعل هواي تبعا لطاعتك وخذ رضا نفسك من نفسي في عافية وأهدني لما اختلف فيه من الحق بإذنك إنك تهدي من تشاء إلى صراط مستقيم
2:213.english: And when a matter befell him, he would entrust the matter to Allah and absolve himself from power and strength, and he would seek guidance by saying: 'O Allah, show me the truth as truth and grant me to follow it, and show me falsehood as falsehood and grant me to avoid it, and protect me from confusion so that I follow my desire (Hawa) without guidance from You, and make my desire (Hawa) follow Your obedience, and take Your pleasure (Rida) from my soul (Nafs) in well-being, and guide me to what is differed upon of the truth by Your permission. Indeed, You guide whom You will to a straight path (Sirat Mustaqim).'
2:213.book_title: Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character
2:213.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character'

2:213.arabic: وقال تعالى في معرض الإنكار "أم يحسدون الناس على ما آتاهم الله من فضله" وقال تعالى "كان الناس أمة واحدة" إلى قوله "إلا الذين أوتوه من بعد ما جاءتهم البينات بغياً بينهم" قيل في التفسير: حسداً. وقال تعالى "وما تفرقوا إلا من بعد ما جاءهم العلم بغياً بينهم" فأنزل الله العلم ليجمعهم ويؤلف بينهم على طاعته، وأمرهم أن يتألفوا بالعلم فتحاسدوا واختلفوا إذ أراد كل واحد منهم أن ينفرد بالرياسة وقبول القول فرد بعضهم على بعض.
2:213.english: And He (Exalted) said in the context of reproach: "Or do they envy people for what Allah has given them of His bounty?" And He (Exalted) said: "Mankind was one community" to His saying: "except those who were given it after clear proofs had come to them, out of mutual envy (baghyan) between them." It is said in the interpretation: envy (hasadan). And He (Exalted) said: "And they did not become divided until after knowledge had come to them, out of mutual envy (baghyan) between them." So Allah sent down knowledge to gather them and unite them in His obedience, and commanded them to unite through knowledge, but they envied one another and differed, since each one of them wanted to monopolize leadership and acceptance of speech, so they refuted one another.
2:213.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

2:213.arabic: وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها (كان ﷺ إذا قام من الليل افتتح صلاته قال: اللهم رب جبريل وميكائيل وإسرافيل فاطر السموات والأرض عالم الغيب والشهادة أنت تحكم بين عبادك فيما كانوا فيه يختلفون اهدني لما اختلف فيه من الحق بإذنك إنك تهدي من تشاء إلى صراط مستقيم[83])
2:213.english: And Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: (When he ﷺ rose for the night prayer, he would begin his prayer by saying: O Allah, Lord of Jibril, Mika'il, and Israfil, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You judge between Your servants in that which they differed. Guide me to that which I differed in from the truth by Your permission, indeed You guide whom You will to a straight path[83]).
2:213.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Book of Knowledge'

2:216.arabic: ومهما لم ير المحب إلا المحبوب ولم ير شيئاً إلا منه لم يتأسف ولم يشك واستقبل الكل بالرضا وعلم أن المحبوب لم يقدر له إلا ما فيه خيرته، ويذكر قوله: " وعسى أن تكرهوا شيئاً وهو خير لكم ".
2:216.english: And whenever the lover (Muhibb) does not see except the Beloved (Mahbub) and does not see anything except from Him, he does not regret and does not doubt and receives everything with contentment (Rida) and knows that the Beloved has not decreed for him except what contains his goodness, and he remembers His saying: "And perhaps you dislike something while it is good for you."
2:216.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

2:216.arabic: وقال ﭬ: " أفضل الأعمال ما أكرهت عليه النفوس"[60]. فقيل: معناه ما دخل عليه من الأمراض والمصائب، وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى: " وعسى أن تكرهوا شيئاً وهو خير لكم ".
2:216.english: And He (peace be upon him) said: "The best deeds are those that the Souls (Nafs) are compelled to do." It was said: Its meaning is what befalls one of illnesses and calamities, and to this is the allusion in His saying, the Exalted: "And perhaps you dislike something while it is good for you."
2:216.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

2:218.arabic: فإذا العبد المجتهد في الطاعات المجتنب للمعاصى حقيق بإن ينتظر من فضل الله تمام النعمة وما تمام النعمة إلا بدخول الجنة وأما العاصى فإذا تاب وتدارك جميع ما فرط منه من تقصير فحقيق بأن يرجو قبول التوبة وأما قبل التوبة إذا كان كارها للمعصية تسوءه السيئة وتسره الحسنة وهو يذم نفسه ويلومها ويشتهى التوبة ويشتاق إليها فحقيق بأن يرجو منا لله التوفيق للتوبة لأن كراهيتة للمعصية وحؤصه على التوبة يجرى مجرى السبب الذى قد يفضى إلى التوبة وإما الرجاء بعد تأكد الأسباب ولذلك قال تعالى: ﴿ إن الذين آمنوا والذين هاجروا
2:218.english: So if the servant (Abd) is diligent in acts of obedience (Taat) and avoids sins (Maasi), he is worthy to expect from the bounty of Allah the completion of blessing (Nimah), and what is the completion of blessing except by entering Paradise. As for the sinner (Aasi), if he repents (Tab) and makes up for all that he has neglected of shortcomings, he is worthy to hope for the acceptance of repentance (Tawbah). And as for before repentance, if he is averse to sin (Ma'siyah), the bad deed (Sayyi'ah) displeases him and the good deed (Hasanah) pleases him, and he blames his soul (Nafs) and reproaches it, and he desires repentance (Tawbah) and yearns for it, he is worthy to hope from Allah for success (Tawfiq) in repentance, because his aversion to sin and his eagerness for repentance run as a cause (Sabab) that may lead to repentance. And as for hope (Rajaa) after the causes are confirmed, and therefore Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, those who have believed and those who have emigrated and fought in the cause of Allah - those expect the mercy of Allah' (Quran 2:218). Its meaning is: those deserve to hope for the mercy of Allah, and He did not intend to specify the existence of hope, because others may also hope, but He specified them with deserving hope. As for one who immerses himself in what Allah the Exalted dislikes and does not blame his soul (Nafs) for it nor resolves on repentance (Tawbah) and return, his hope for forgiveness (Maghfirah) is foolishness, like the hope of one who sows seed in barren land and resolves not to tend it with watering or purification.
2:218.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

2:218.arabic: فإن قلت: فأين الغلط في قول العصاة والفجار إن الله كريم وإنا نرجو رحمته ومغفرته، وقد قال أنا عند ظن عبدي بي فليظن بي خيراً، فما هذا إلا كلام صحيح مقبول الظاهر في القلوب؟ فاعلم أن الشيطان لا يغوي الإنسان إلا بكلام مقبول الظاهر مردود الباطن، ولولا حسن ظاهره لما انخدعت به القلوب، ولكن النبي ﭬ كشف عن ذلك فقال "الكيس من دان نفسه وعمل لما بعد الموت، والأحمق من اتبع نفسه هواهها وتمنى على الله" وهذا هو التمني على الله تعالى غير الشيطان اسمه فسماه: رجاء، حتى خدع به الجهال. وقد شرح الله الرجاء فقال "إن الذ
2:218.english: If you say: Where is the error in the statement of the disobedient and wicked that Allah is Generous and we hope for His Mercy and forgiveness, and He has said 'I am as My servant thinks of Me, so let him think good of Me' - is this not correct speech with an acceptable outward appearance in the hearts? Know that Satan does not misguide the human except with speech that has an acceptable outward appearance but a rejected inward reality, and were it not for the goodness of its outward appearance, hearts would not be deceived by it. But the Prophet (peace be upon him) uncovered this by saying: 'The intelligent one is he who holds his Soul (Nafs) accountable and works for what is after death, and the foolish one is he who follows his Soul's (Nafs) desires and makes wishes upon Allah.' This is making wishes upon Allah the Exalted, but Satan changed its name and called it: Hope (Rajā'), until he deceived the ignorant with it. And Allah explained Hope (Rajā') by saying: 'Indeed, those who have believed and those who have emigrated and striven in the path of Allah - those hope for the mercy of Allah.' Meaning that Hope (Rajā') is more fitting for them, and this is because He mentioned that the reward of the Hereafter is a wage and recompense for deeds. Allah the Exalted said: 'A recompense for what they used to do' and He said: 'And you will only be given your wages on the Day of Resurrection.' Do you see that one who is hired to repair vessels and is promised a wage for them, and the promiser is generous who fulfills the promise whenever he promises and does not break it but rather increases, then the hired worker comes and breaks the vessels and ruins all of them, then sits waiting for the wage and claims that the hirer is generous - do the intelligent see him in his waiting as a wishful, deceived person or as one who hopes? And this is due to ignorance of the difference between Hope (Rajā') and delusion.
2:218.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

2:222.arabic: اعلم أن شواهد القرآن متظاهرة على أن الله تعالى يحب عبده فلا بد من معرفة معنى ذلك. ولنقدم الشواهد على محبته فقد قال الله تعالى: " يحبهم ويحبونه " وقال تعالى: " إن الله يحب الذين يقاتلون في سبيله صفاً " وقال تعالى: " إن الله يحب التوابين ويحب المتطهرين " ولذلك رد سبحانه على من ادعى أنه حبيب الله فقال: " قل فلم يعذبكم بذنوبكم ".
2:222.english: Know that the evidences from the Quran are abundant in showing that Allah the Exalted loves His servant, so it is necessary to know the meaning of that. And let us present the evidences of His love, for Allah the Exalted has said: "He loves them and they love Him" and He said: "Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in ranks" and He said: "Indeed, Allah loves the repentant (Tawwabin) and loves the purified (Mutatahhirin)". And for that reason, He the Glorified responded to one who claimed that he was the beloved of Allah by saying: "Say, then why does He punish you for your sins?".
2:222.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

2:223.arabic: وقال ﭬ: (إنما فرضت الصلاة وأمر بالحج والطواف وأشعرت المناسك لإقامة ذكر الله تعالى فإذا لم يكن في قلبك للمذكور الذي هو المقصود والمبتغى عظمة ولا هيبة فما قيمة ذكرك[38]) وقال ﭬ للذي أوصاه: (وإذا صليت فصل صلاة مودع[39]) أي مودع لنفسه مودع لهواه مودع لعمره سائر إلى مولاه كما قال عز وجل: ﴿ أيها الإنسان إنك كادح إلى ربك كدحا فملاقيه ﴾ {الانشقاق: 6} وقال تعالى: ﴿ واتقوا الله ويعلمكم الله ﴾ {البقرة: 282} وقال تعالى: ﴿ واتقوا الله واعلموا أنكم ملاقوه ﴾ {البقرة: 223} وقال ﭬ: (من لم تنهه صلاته عن الفحشاء و
2:223.english: And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, prayer was prescribed, and Hajj and circumambulation were commanded, and the rituals were made apparent for establishing the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah the Exalted. So if there is not in your heart for the Remembered One (Al-Madhkūr) who is the intended and sought object any majesty nor awe, then what is the value of your remembrance?' And he (peace be upon him) said to the one he advised: 'And when you pray, pray a prayer of one bidding farewell' meaning bidding farewell to his Soul (Nafs), bidding farewell to his desire, bidding farewell to his lifespan, journeying to his Master, as the Mighty and Majestic said: 'O human, indeed you are laboring toward your Lord with labor, then you will meet Him' (Al-Inshiqāq: 6). And Allah the Exalted said: 'And fear Allah, and Allah teaches you' (Al-Baqarah: 282). And Allah the Exalted said: 'And fear Allah and know that you will meet Him' (Al-Baqarah: 223). And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever's prayer does not prevent him from immorality and wrongdoing, he only increases in distance from Allah.' And prayer is intimate conversation, so how can it be with heedlessness.
2:223.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

2:223.arabic: وأحد المعاني المذكورة في قوله تعالى فأتوا حرثكم أنى شئتم وقدموا لأنفسكم تقديم الأطفال إلى الآخرة فقد ظهر بهذه الوجوه الأربعة أن أكثر فضل النكاح لأجل كونه سببا للولد الفائدة الثانية التحصن من الشيطان وكسر التوقان ودفع غوائل الشهوة وغض البصر وحفظ الفرج وإليه الإشارة بقوله عليه السلام (من نكح فقد حصن نصف دينه فليتق الله في الشطر الآخر) وإليه الإشارة بقوله (عليكم بالباءة فمن لم يستطع فعليه بالالصوم فإن الصوم له وجاء.)
2:223.english: And one of the meanings mentioned in His saying, the Exalted: 'Your wives are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth when you like, and send ahead for your souls (Anfusikum)' is the sending ahead of children to the Hereafter. Thus, it has become clear through these four aspects that most of the virtue of marriage is due to it being a cause for children. The second benefit is protection from Satan, breaking the intense desire (Tawqan), repelling the dangers of lust (Shahwah), lowering the gaze, and guarding the private parts. To this is the allusion in his saying, peace be upon him: 'Whoever marries has protected half of his religion, so let him fear Allah in the other half.' And to this is the allusion in his saying: 'Upon you is marriage (Bā'ah); whoever is not able, then upon him is fasting, for fasting is a shield for him.'
2:223.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

2:223.arabic: وقوله تعالى (فأتوا حرثكم أنى شئتم) أي أي وقت شئتم وله أن يستمني بيديها وان يستمتع بما تحت الإزار بما يشتهي سوى الوقاع وينبغي أن تتزر المرأة بإزار من حقوها إلى فوق الركبة في حال الحيض فهذا من الأدب وله أن يؤاكل الحائض ويخالطها في المضاجعة وغيرها وليس عليه اجتنابها
2:223.english: And His saying, the Exalted (So approach your tilth when and how you will) means: at whatever time you will. And he may masturbate with her hands, and he may enjoy what is beneath the waist-wrapper with whatever he desires except for intercourse. And it is proper for the woman to wrap herself with a waist-wrapper from her waist to above the knee during the state of menstruation; this is from proper conduct. And he may eat with the menstruating woman and mix with her in bedding and other than that, and there is no obligation upon him to avoid her.
2:223.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

2:225.arabic: وكل ذلك يدل على العفو فأما ما يدل على المؤاخذة فقوله سبحانه إن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله فيغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء وقوله تعالى ولا تقف ما ليس لك به علم إن السمع والبصر والفؤاد كل أولئك كان عنه مسئولا فدل على أن عمل الفؤاد كعمل السمع والبصر فلا يعفي عنه وقوله تعالى ولا تكتموا الشهادة ومن يكتمها فإنه آثم قلبه وقوله تعالى لا يؤاخذكم الله باللغو في أيمانكم ولكن يؤاخذكم بما كسبت قلوبكم والحق عندنا في هذه المسألة لا يوقف عليه ما لم تقع الإحاطة بتفصيل أعمال القلوب من مبدأ ظهورها إل
2:225.english: And all of that indicates forgiveness. As for what indicates accountability, it is His saying, the Most High: 'If you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it, then He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills' (Quran 2:284), and His saying, the Most High: 'And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart (Fū'ād) - all of those will be questioned' (Quran 17:36), which indicates that the action of the heart (Fū'ād) is like the action of hearing and sight, so it is not forgiven, and His saying, the Most High: 'And do not conceal testimony, and whoever conceals it, then indeed his heart (Qalb) is sinful' (Quran 2:283), and His saying, the Most High: 'Allah does not hold you accountable for the vain (Laghu) in your oaths, but He holds you accountable for what your hearts (Qulūb) have earned' (Quran 2:225). And the truth in our view on this matter cannot be ascertained without encompassing the detailed actions of the hearts (Qulūb) from the beginning of their appearance until the action manifests on the limbs. So we say: The first thing that comes to the heart (Qalb) is the passing thought (Khāṭir), as if, for example, the image of a woman occurs to him and that she is behind his back on the road, if he turned to her he would see her. The second is the stirring of desire to look, which is the movement of appetite in the natural disposition (Ṭabʿ), and this is generated from the first passing thought (Khāṭir), and we call it the inclination of the natural disposition (Ṭabʿ), and the first is called the inner speech of the soul (Nafs). The third is the judgment of the heart (Qalb) that this should be done, meaning that he should look at her, for when the natural disposition (Ṭabʿ) inclines, the aspiration (Himmah) and intention (Niyyah) do not arise unless the deterrents are removed, for it may prevent him due to shame or fear from turning, and the absence of these deterrents may be due to contemplation, and in any case, it is a judgment from the side of the intellect (ʿAql), and this is called belief (Iʿtiqād), and it follows the passing thought (Khāṭir) and inclination. The fourth is the firm resolve (ʿAzm) to turn and the decisive intention (Niyyah) in it, and this we call actual determination (Hamm) and intention (Niyyah) and purpose (Qaṣd). And this determination (Hamm) may have a weak beginning, but if the heart (Qalb) listens to the first passing thought (Khāṭir) until its attraction to the soul (Nafs) prolongs, this determination (Hamm) becomes confirmed and becomes a decisive will (Irādah). And when the will (Irādah) is decided, perhaps he regrets after the decision and abandons the action, and perhaps he is distracted by an occurrence so he does not act on it and does not turn to it, and perhaps an obstacle hinders him so it becomes impossible for him.
2:225.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

2:225.arabic: بل اللهو واللغو لا يؤاخذ الله تعالى به إن عنى به أنه فعل ما لا فائدة فيه فإن الإنسان لو وظف على نفسه أن يضع يده على رأسه في اليوم مائة مرة فهذا عبث لا فائدة له ولا يحرم قال الله تعالى لا يؤاخذكم الله باللغو في أيمانكم فإذا كان ذكر اسم الله تعالى على الشيء على طريق القسم من غير عقد عليه ولا تصميم والمخالفة فيه مع أنه لا فائدة فيه لا يؤاخذ فكيف يؤاخذ به بالشعر والرقص
2:225.english: Rather, amusement (Lahw) and idle talk (Laghw) - Allah the Exalted does not hold accountable for it if what is meant by it is an action that has no benefit. For if a human being obligated upon himself to place his hand on his head one hundred times a day, this is frivolity that has no benefit and is not prohibited. Allah the Exalted said: 'Allah will not call you to account for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He will call you to account for what your hearts have earned. And Allah is Forgiving, Forbearing.' So if mentioning the name of Allah the Exalted upon something by way of oath without binding it or determination, and violating it while it has no benefit - He does not hold accountable, then how would He hold accountable for poetry and dancing?
2:225.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

2:225.arabic: وعن ابن جريج انه كان يرخص في السماع فقيل له أيؤتى يوم القيامة في جملة حسناتك أو سيئاتك فقال لا في الحسنات ولا في السيئات لأنه شبيه باللغو وقال الله تعالى لا يؤاخذكم الله باللغو في ايمانكم هذا ما نقل من الاقاويل ومن طلب الحق في التقليد فمهما استقصى تعارضت عنده هذه الاقاويل فيبقى متحيرا أومائلا إلى بعض الاقاويل بالتشهي وكل ذلك قصور بل ينبغي أن يطلب الحق بطريقه وذلك بالبحث عن مدارك الحظر والاباحة كما سنذكره بيان الدليل على إباحة السماع
2:225.english: And from Ibn Jurayj, that he used to permit listening (to spiritual music/recitation). He was asked: 'Will it come on the Day of Resurrection among your good deeds (Hasanat) or your bad deeds (Sayi'at)?' He said: 'Neither among the good deeds nor the bad deeds, because it resembles idle talk (Al-Laghw).' And Allah the Exalted said: 'Allah will not hold you accountable for the idle talk (Al-Laghw) in your oaths.' This is what has been transmitted from the sayings. And whoever seeks the truth through imitation (Al-Taqlid), whenever he exhaustively examines, these sayings conflict for him, so he remains perplexed or inclines to some of the sayings by desire, and all of that is deficiency. Rather, one should seek the truth by its method, and that is by investigating the sources of prohibition (Al-Hazr) and permissibility (Al-Ibahah), as we will mention the clarification of the evidence for the permissibility of listening (Al-Sama').
2:225.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

2:228.arabic: ولنضرب للخوف مثلا فما من عبد يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر إلا وهو خائف من الله خوفا ينطلق عليه الاسم ولكنه خوف غير صادق أى غير بالغ درجة الحقيقة أما تراه إذا خاف سلطانا أو قاطع طريق فى سفره كيف يصفر لونه وترتعد فرائصه ويتنغص عليه عيشه ويتعذر عليه أكله ونومه وينقسم عليه فكره حتى لا ينتفع به أهله وولده وقد ينزعج عن الوطن فيستبدل بالأنس الوحشة وبالراحة التعب والمشقة والتعرض للأخطار كل ذلك خوفا من درك المحذور ثم إنه يخاف النار ولا يظهر عليه شىء من ذلك عند جريان معصية عليه ولذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لم
2:228.english: And let us take Fear (Khauf) as an example, for there is no servant who believes in Allah and the Last Day except that he fears Allah with a fear that the name applies to, but it is a fear that is not truthful (Sadiq), meaning it does not reach the degree of reality. Do you not see that if he fears a ruler or a highway robber on his journey, how his color pales, his limbs tremble, his life becomes bitter, his eating and sleeping become difficult, his thought becomes divided until his family and children do not benefit from him, and he may be disturbed from his homeland, exchanging familiarity for loneliness, and rest for fatigue, hardship, and exposure to dangers—all of that out of fear of encountering the dreaded thing? Then, he fears the Fire, yet nothing of that appears upon him when a sin occurs to him. Therefore, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'I have not seen anything like the Fire whose fleeer sleeps, nor like Paradise whose seeker sleeps.' The hadith 'I have not seen anything like the Fire whose fleeer sleeps' has preceded. So, realization (Tahqiq) in these matters is very rare, and there is no end to these stations (Maqamat) until their completion is attained, but each servant has a share according to his state, either weak or strong. If it is strong, he is called truthful (Sadiq) in it, for the knowledge (Ma'rifah) of Allah the Exalted, His veneration (Ta'zim), and fear (Khauf) of Him have no end.
2:228.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

2:228.arabic: ولذلك اعتذر بعضهم من التزويج وقال أنا مبتلي بنفسي وكيف أضيف إليها نفسا أخرى كما قيل لن يسع الفأرة جحرها علقت المكنس في دبرها وكذلك اعتذر إبراهيم بن أدهم رحمه الله وقال لا أغر امرأة بنفسي ولا حاجة لي فيهن أي من القيام بحقهن وتحصينهن وإمتاعهن وأنا عاجز عنه وكذلك اعتذر بشر وقال يمنعني من النكاح قوله تعالى (ولهن مثل الذي عليهن) وكان يقول لو كنت أعول دجاجة لخفت أن أصير جلادا على الجسر.
2:228.english: Therefore, some of them excused themselves from marriage and said: 'I am afflicted with my own soul (Nafs), so how can I add another soul (Nafs) to it?' As it is said: 'The mouse's burrow will not accommodate it when it attaches the broom to its tail.' Likewise, Ibrahim ibn Adham, may Allah have mercy on him, excused himself and said: 'I will not deceive a woman with myself, nor do I have need for them,' meaning from fulfilling their rights (Huquq), protecting them, and giving them enjoyment, and I am incapable of that. Likewise, Bishr excused himself and said: 'What prevents me from marriage is the saying of Allah the Exalted: "And for them is like that which is upon them with kindness (bil-ma'ruf)."' And he used to say: 'If I were to provide for a chicken, I would fear that I would become a toll-collector on the bridge.'
2:228.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

2:228.arabic: وقال بشر بن الحرث فضل على أحمد بن حنبل بثلاث بطلب الحلال لنفسه ولغيره وأنا أطلبه لنفسي فقط ولاتساعه في النكاح وضيقي عنه ولأنه نصب إماما للعامة. ويقال إن أحمد رحمه الله تزوج في اليوم الثاني لوفاة أم ولده عبد الله وقال أكره أن أبيت عزبا وأما بشر فإنه لما قيل له إن الناس يتكلمون فيك لتركك النكاح ويقولون هو تارك للسنة فقال قولوا لهم هو مشغول بالفرض عن السنة وعوتب مرة أخرى فقال ما يمنعني من التزويج إلا قوله تعالى ولهن مثل الذي عليهن بالمعروف فذكر ذلك لأحمد فقال وأين مثل بشر إنه قعد على مثل حد السنان
2:228.english: And Bishr ibn al-Harith said: Ahmad ibn Hanbal is superior to me in three things: seeking the lawful (Halal) for himself and others, while I seek it only for myself; and in his expansiveness in marriage and my narrowness in it; and because he was appointed as an imam for the general public. And it is said that Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, married on the second day after the death of the mother of his son Abdullah and said: I dislike to spend the night unmarried. As for Bishr, when it was said to him: People are talking about you for abandoning marriage and saying he is abandoning the Sunnah, he said: Tell them he is preoccupied with the obligatory (Fard) over the Sunnah. And he was reproached another time, so he said: What prevents me from marriage is only His saying, the Exalted: 'And for them is like what is upon them in kindness (Ma'ruf).' He mentioned that to Ahmad, so he said: And where is the like of Bishr? Indeed, he sat on the edge of a spear. And despite that, it has been narrated that he was seen in a dream and it was said to him: What has Allah done with you? He said: My ranks were raised in Paradise, and I was elevated to the stations (Maqamat) of the prophets, but I did not reach the ranks of the married ones. And in another narration, he said to me: I did not like that you meet me unmarried. He said: So we said to him: What happened to Abu Nasr al-Tammar? He said: He was raised above me by seventy degrees. We said: With what? For we used to see you above him. He said: With his patience over his daughters and dependents (Ayal).
2:228.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

2:229.arabic: الثاني عشر في الطلاق وليعلم أنه مباح ولكنه أبغض المباحات إلى الله تعالى وإنما يكون مباحا إذا لم يكن فيه إيذاء بالباطل ومهما طلقها فقد آذاها ولا يباح إيذاء الغير إلا بجناية من جانبها أو بضرورة من جانبه قال الله تعالى (فإن أطعنكم فلا تبغوا عليهن سبيلا) أي لا تطلبوا حيلة للفراق وإن كرهها أبوه فليطلقها قال ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما كان تحتي امرأة أحبها وكان أبي يكرهها ويأمرني بطلاقها فراجعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال يا ابن عمر طلق امرأتك فهذا يدل على أن حق الوالد مقدم ولكن والد يكرهها لا لغرض ف
2:229.english: The twelfth [section] is on divorce (Talaq), and it should be known that it is permissible (Mubah) but it is the most detested of permissible things to Allah, the Exalted. It is only permissible when there is no harm (Itha') in falsehood, and whenever he divorces her, he has harmed her. Harming others is not permitted except due to a transgression (Jinayah) from her side or a necessity (Darurah) from his side. Allah, the Exalted, said: 'If they obey you, then do not seek a way against them' (Quran 4:34), meaning do not seek a stratagem for separation. And if her father dislikes her, let him divorce her. Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: 'I had a wife whom I loved, and my father disliked her and ordered me to divorce her. So I consulted the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said: O Ibn Umar, divorce your wife.' This indicates that the right of the parent takes precedence, but a parent who dislikes her without a corrupt purpose, like Umar. And whenever she harms her husband and exposes [faults] to his family, she is a transgressor. Likewise, if she is of bad character (Sayi'at al-Khuluq) or corrupt in religion (Fasidat al-Deen). Ibn Mas'ud said regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'And they should not leave except that they commit a clear immorality' (Quran 65:1), whenever she exposes [faults] to his family and harms her husband, that is an immorality (Fahishah). This is intended during the waiting period (Iddah), but it is an alert to the intended meaning. And if the harm is from the husband, she may redeem herself by giving wealth, and it is disliked for the man to take from her more than what he gave, for that is injustice (Ijhaf) to her and oppression (Tahammul) upon her and trading on the private part (Bid'). Allah, the Exalted, said: 'Then there is no blame upon them for what she gives to ransom herself' (Quran 2:229), returning what he took or less is suitable for the ransom (Fidya'). If she asks for divorce without any wrongdoing, she is sinful (Athimah). The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'Any woman who asks her husband for divorce without any wrongdoing will not smell the fragrance of Paradise.' In another wording: 'Paradise is forbidden to her.' In another wording: 'He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: The women who seek redemption (Mukhtali'at) are the hypocrites (Munafiqat).'
2:229.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

2:231.arabic: ولذلك أمر الله تعالى الكافة بشكر نعمة الكتاب فقال تعالى ﴿ واذكروا نعمة الله عليكم وما أنزل عليكم من الكتاب والحكمة يعظكم به ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل ﴿ لقد أنزلنا إليكم كتابا فيه ذكركم أفلا تعقلون. وأنزلنا إليك الذكر لتبين للناس ما نزل إليهم. كذلك يضرب الله للناس أمثالهم واتبعوا أحسن ما أنزل إليكم من ربكم. هذا بصائر للناس وهدى ورحمة لقوم يوقنون. هذا بيان للناس وهدى وموعظة للمتقين ﴾ {} وإذا قصد بالخطاب جميع الناس فقد قصد الآحاد فهذا القارىء الواحد مقصود فما له ولسائر الناس فليقدر أنه المقصود
2:231.english: Therefore, Allah the Exalted commanded the entirety to give thanks for the blessing of the Book, so He the Exalted said: 'And remember the blessing (Ni'mah) of Allah upon you and what He has sent down to you of the Book and the Wisdom (Hikmah) by which He admonishes you.' And He the Mighty and Majestic said: 'We have certainly sent down to you a Book in which is your Remembrance (Dhikr). Then will you not reason? And We have sent down to you the Remembrance (Dhikr) that you may make clear to the people what was sent down to them. Thus does Allah set forth for the people their examples. And follow the best of what was revealed to you from your Lord. This is insight for the people and guidance and mercy for a people who are certain. This is a clarification for the people and guidance and admonition for those who fear Allah.' And if the address is intended for all people, then the individuals are intended, so this single reader is intended, so what is for him and for the rest of the people, let him consider that he is the intended one.
2:231.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

2:231.arabic: على الندور فإنه أكثر أحوال الأنبياء والأولياء ولكن استوعروا هذا الطريق واستبطؤا ثمرته واستبعدوا استجماع شروطه وزعموا أن محو العلائق إلى ذلك الحد كالمتعذر وإن حصل في حال فثباته أبعد منه إذ أدنى وسواس وخاطر يشوش القلب وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قلب المؤمن أشد تقلبا من القدر في غليانها[25] أخرجه أحمد والحاكم وقال عليه أفضل الصلاة والسلام قلب المؤمن بين أصبعين من أصابع الرحمن[26] وفي أثناء هذه المجاهدة قد يفسد المزاج ويختلط العقل ويمرض البدن وإذا لم تتقدم رياضة النفس وتهذيبها بحقائق العلوم نش
2:231.english: On rarity, for it is the most frequent state of the Prophets and the Friends (Awliya), but they considered this path difficult, delayed its fruit, deemed gathering its conditions improbable, and claimed that erasing attachments to that extent is nearly impossible, and if it occurs in a state, its permanence is farther from it, since the slightest whisper (Waswas) and thought (Khatir) disturbs the Heart (Qalb). And the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'The Heart (Qalb) of the believer is more fluctuating than a pot in boiling.' [25] Reported by Ahmad and Al-Hakim. And he, upon him the best prayer and peace, said: 'The Heart (Qalb) of the believer is between two fingers of the fingers of the Most Merciful.' [26] And during this struggle (Mujahada), the temperament may corrupt, the intellect may become confused, and the body may fall ill. And if the training (Riyada) of the Soul (Nafs) and its refinement with the realities of knowledge do not precede, false imaginings (Khayalat) take root in the Heart (Qalb), to which the Soul (Nafs) becomes content for a long time until it vanishes, and life passes before success in it. For how many a Sufi has trodden this path, then remained in one imagining for twenty years! And if he had mastered knowledge beforehand, the aspect of confusion of that imagining would have opened to him immediately. So engagement with the path of learning is more reliable and closer to the goal. And they claimed that this resembles if a person abandoned learning jurisprudence (Fiqh) and claimed that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, did not learn that and became a jurist by revelation (Wahy) and inspiration (Ilham) without repetition and annotation. And I too perhaps reached it through training (Riyada) and persistence. And whoever thinks that has wronged himself and wasted his life. Rather, he is like one who abandons the path of earning and cultivation hoping to find a treasure among treasures, for that is possible but very distant, and likewise this. And they said: It is necessary first to acquire what the scholars have acquired and understand what they said, then there is no harm after that in awaiting what has not been unveiled to other scholars, perhaps it will be unveiled after that through struggle (Mujahada). Explanation of the difference between the two stations with a tangible example: Know that the wonders of the Heart (Qalb) are outside the perceptions of the senses, because the Heart (Qalb) is also outside the perception of sense. And what is not perceived by the senses, understandings weaken from grasping it except with a tangible example. And we bring that closer to weak understandings with two examples. One of them is that if we suppose a basin dug in the earth, it is possible that water is channeled to it from above by rivers opened into it, and it is possible that the bottom of the basin is dug and its soil is lifted until it nears the resting place of pure water, then water gushes from the bottom of the basin, and that water is clearer and more lasting, and it may be more abundant and greater. So that Heart (Qalb) is like the basin, and knowledge is like the water, and the five senses become an example of the rivers. And it is possible that knowledge is channeled to the Heart (Qalb) by means of the rivers of the senses and consideration of observations until it fills with knowledge. And it is possible that these rivers are blocked by seclusion (Khalwa), isolation (Uzla), and lowering the gaze, and one aims at the depth of the Heart (Qalb) by purifying.
2:231.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

2:231.arabic: ولنرجع إلى الغرض المطلوب فالمقصود أن غرور الشيطان بأن الآخرة شك يدفع إما بيقين تقليدي، وأما ببصيرة ومشاهدة من جهة الباطن، والمؤمنين بألسنتهم وبعقائدهم إذا ضيعوا أوامر الله تعالى وهجروا الأعمال الصالحة ولابسوا الشهوات والمعاصي فهم مشاركون للكفار في هذا الغرور من النار ولو بعد حين، ولكنهم أيضاً من المغرورين فإنهم اعترفوا بأن الآخرة خير من الدنيا ولكنهم مالوا إلى الدنيا وآثروها، ومجرد الإيمان لا يكفي للفوز قال تعالى "وإني لغفار لمن تاب
2:231.english: And let us return to the intended purpose, so the intended meaning is that the deception of the Satan that the Hereafter is doubt is repelled either by traditional certainty, or by insight and witnessing from the aspect of the inner (Batin), and the believers with their tongues and with their beliefs if they waste the commands of Allah the Exalted and abandon the righteous works and associate with the desires and the disobediences, then they are partners with the disbelievers in this deception from the Fire even if after a while, but they are also from the deceived ones for they acknowledged that the Hereafter is better than the world but they inclined to the world and preferred it, and mere faith is not sufficient for success, said the Exalted: "And indeed, I am Forgiving to whoever repents
2:231.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

2:232.arabic: ولنضرب للخوف مثلا فما من عبد يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر إلا وهو خائف من الله خوفا ينطلق عليه الاسم ولكنه خوف غير صادق أى غير بالغ درجة الحقيقة أما تراه إذا خاف سلطانا أو قاطع طريق فى سفره كيف يصفر لونه وترتعد فرائصه ويتنغص عليه عيشه ويتعذر عليه أكله ونومه وينقسم عليه فكره حتى لا ينتفع به أهله وولده وقد ينزعج عن الوطن فيستبدل بالأنس الوحشة وبالراحة التعب والمشقة والتعرض للأخطار كل ذلك خوفا من درك المحذور ثم إنه يخاف النار ولا يظهر عليه شىء من ذلك عند جريان معصية عليه ولذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لم
2:232.english: And let us take fear as an example, for there is no servant who believes in Allah and the Last Day except that he fears Allah with a fear that the name applies to, but it is a fear that is not truthful (صادق), meaning it does not reach the degree of reality. Do you not see that when he fears a ruler or a highway robber during his journey, how his color pales, his limbs tremble, his life becomes bitter, his eating and sleeping become difficult, his thought becomes divided until his family and children do not benefit from him, and he may be disturbed from his homeland, exchanging familiarity for loneliness and comfort for fatigue, hardship, and exposure to dangers, all of that out of fear of encountering the dreaded thing? Then he fears the Fire, yet nothing of that appears upon him when a sin occurs to him. Therefore, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'I have not seen anything like the Fire whose fleer sleeps, nor like Paradise whose seeker sleeps.' The hadith 'I have not seen anything like the Fire whose fleer sleeps' has preceded. So, realization (التحقيق) in these matters is very rare, and there is no end to these stations until their completion is attained, but every servant has a share according to his state, either weak or strong. When it becomes strong, he is called truthful (صادق) in it. So, the knowledge of Allah the Exalted, His veneration, and fear of Him have no end.
2:232.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

2:232.arabic: الترغيب في النكاح أما من الآيات فقد قال تعالى (وأنكحوا الأيامى منكم) وهذا أمر وقال تعالى (فلا تعضلوهن أن ينكحن أزواجهن) وهذا منع من العضل ونهي عنه وقال تعالى في وصف الرسل ومدحهم (ولقد أرسلنا رسلا من قبلك وجعلنا لهم أزواجا وذرية) فذكر ذلك في معرض الامتنان وإظهار الفضل ومدح أولياءه بسؤال ذلك في الدعاء فقال (والذين يقولون ربنا هب لنا من أزواجنا وذرياتنا قرة أعين) الآية ويقال إن الله تعالى لم يذكر في كتابه من الأنبياء إلا المتأهلين فقالوا إن يحيى صلى الله عليه وسلم قد تزوج ولم يجامع قيل إنما فعل ذلك
2:232.english: The encouragement of marriage: As for from the verses, indeed Allah the Exalted said: 'And marry the unmarried among you' - and this is a command. And He said: 'And when you divorce women and they have [nearly] fulfilled their term, do not prevent them from remarrying their [former] husbands if they agree among themselves on an acceptable basis' - and this is a prohibition of prevention (al-'adl) and a forbiddance from it. And He said in describing the messengers and praising them: 'And We have already sent messengers before you and assigned to them wives and descendants' - so He mentioned that in the context of bestowing favor and showing excellence. And He praised His allies by asking for that in supplication, so He said: 'And those who say, "Our Lord, grant us from among our wives and offspring comfort to our eyes"' - the verse. And it is said that Allah the Exalted did not mention in His Book from the prophets except the married ones, so they said: Indeed, Yahya (peace be upon him) married but did not have intercourse; it is said he did that only to attain excellence and establish the Sunnah, and it is said to lower the gaze. And as for 'Isa (peace be upon him), he will marry when he descends to the earth and will have children.
2:232.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

2:235.arabic: ولكن لا يخلو كل يوم عن مهم جديد وواقعة حادثة لها حكم جديد ولله عليه في ذلك حق ويكثر هذا على من يشتغل بشيء من أعمال الدنيا من ولاية أو تجارة أو تدريس إذ قلما يخلو يوم عن واقعة جديدة يحتاج إلى أن يقضى حق الله فيها فعليه أن يشترط على نفسه الاستقامة فيها والانقياد للحق في مجاريها ويحذرها مغبة الإهمال ويعظها كما يوعظ العبد الآبق المتمرد فإن النفس بالطبع متمردة عن الطاعات مستعصية عن العبودية ولكن الوعظ والتأديب يؤثر فيها وذكر فإن الذكرى تنفع المؤمنين فهذا وما يجرى مجراه هو أول مقام المرابطة مع النفس و
2:235.english: But no day passes without a new important matter and an occurring incident that has a new ruling, and Allah has a right upon him in that. This increases for one who is occupied with something from worldly affairs like governance, trade, or teaching, for rarely does a day pass without a new incident that requires fulfilling Allah's right in it. So he must stipulate upon himself uprightness in it and submission to the truth in its courses, and warn it of the consequence of neglect, and admonish it as a runaway rebellious slave is admonished. For the Soul (Nafs) is by nature rebellious against acts of worship, resistant to servitude, but admonition and discipline affect it, and remembrance (Dhikr), for the reminder benefits the believers. This and what runs its course is the first station of vigilance with the Soul (Nafs), which is self-accounting before action. Self-accounting is sometimes after action and sometimes before it for warning. Allah the Exalted said: 'And know that Allah knows what is in your souls (Anfusikum), so beware of Him.' This is for the future. And every looking into quantity and measure to know increase and decrease is called self-accounting. So looking into what is before the servant in his day to know his increase from his decrease is from self-accounting. And Allah the Exalted has said: 'O you who have believed, when you go forth in the cause of Allah, investigate...' and He said: 'O you who have believed, if there comes to you a disobedient one with information, investigate...' and He said: 'And We have certainly created man and know what his soul (Nafs) whispers to him.' Mentioning that as a warning and alert to guard against it in the future.
2:235.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

2:235.arabic: وقال تعالى واعلموا أن الله يعلم ما في أنفسكم فاحذروه فعرف أرباب البصائر من جملة العباد أن الله تعالى لهم بالمرصاد وأنهم سيناقشون في الحساب ويطالبون بمثاقيل الذر من الخطرات واللحظات وتحققوا أنه لا ينجيهم من هذه الأخطار إلا لزوم المحاسبة وصدق المراقبة ومطالبة النفس في الأنفاس والحركات ومحاسبتها في الخطرات واللحظات فمن حاسب نفسه قبل أن يحاسب خف في القيامة حسابه وحضر عند السؤال جوابه وحسن منقلبه ومآبه ومن لم يحاسب نفسه دامت حسراته وطالت في عرصات القيامة وقفاته وقادته إلى الخزى والمقت سيئاته فلما انك
2:235.english: And He (Exalted is He) said: 'And know that Allah knows what is in your souls (Anfusikum) so beware of Him.' So the possessors of insight from among the servants recognized that Allah (Exalted is He) is lying in wait for them and that they will be scrutinized in the accounting and will be demanded with the weight of an atom from the passing thoughts (Khatarat) and glances (Lahazat). And they realized that nothing will save them from these dangers except adhering to self-accounting (Muhasabah) and truthful self-observation (Muraqabah) and demanding from the soul (Nafs) in the breaths and movements and accounting it for the passing thoughts and glances. For whoever accounts his soul before being accounted for, his accounting on the Day of Resurrection will be lightened, and his answer will be present at the questioning, and his return and destination will be good. And whoever does not account his soul, his regrets will persist and his pauses in the arenas of the Day of Resurrection will be prolonged, and his evil deeds will lead him to disgrace and contempt. When this was unveiled to them, they knew that nothing will save them from it except obedience to Allah, and He has commanded them with patience (Sabr) and spiritual vigilance (Murabatah), so He (Mighty and Majestic is He) said: 'O you who believe, be patient and endure and be vigilant, so they made their souls vigilant first with mutual stipulation (Musharatah), then with self-observation (Muraqabah), then with self-accounting (Muhasabah), then with self-punishment (Mu'aqabah), then with spiritual struggle (Mujahadah), then with self-reproof (Mu'atabah). So there were for them in spiritual vigilance six stations, and it is necessary to explain them and clarify their reality and virtue and detail the works in them, and the foundation of that is self-accounting. But every accounting is after mutual stipulation and self-observation, and it is followed upon loss by self-reproof and self-punishment. So let us mention the explanation of these stations, and with Allah is success.'
2:235.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

2:235.arabic: وقال أبو سعيد الخراز قال دخلت المسجد الحرام فرأيت فقيرا عليه خرقتان فقلت في نفسي هذا وأشباهه كل على الناس فناداني وقال والله يعلم ما في أنفسكم فاحذروه فاستغفرت الله في سري فناداني وقال وهو الذي يقبل التوبة عن عباده ثم غاب عني ولم أره
2:235.english: And Abu Sa'id al-Kharraz said: I entered the Sacred Mosque and saw a poor man wearing two ragged garments, so I said to myself: 'This one and his like are a burden on people.' Then he called out to me and said: 'And Allah knows what is in your souls (Anfusikum), so beware of Him.' So I sought forgiveness from Allah in my secret (sirri). Then he called out to me and said: 'And He is the One who accepts repentance from His servants.' Then he disappeared from me and I did not see him.
2:235.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

2:237.arabic: ولنذكر الآن فضيلة العفو والإحسان.                            فضيلة العفو والإحسان اعلم أن معنى العفو أن يستحق حقاً فيسقطه ويبرئ عنه من قصاص أو غرامة، وهو غير الحلم وكظم الغيظ؛ فلذلك أفردناه. قال الله تعالى "خذ العفو وأمر بالعرف وأعرض عن الجاهلين" وقال الله تعالى "وأن تعفوا أقرب للتقوى" وقال رسول الله ﭬ "ثلاث والذي نفسي بيده لو كنت حلافاً لحلفت عليهن: ما نقص مال من صدقة فتصدقوا، ولا عفا رجل عن مظلمة يبتغي بها وجه الله إلا زاده الله بها عزاً يوم القيامة، ولا فتح رجل على نفسه باب مسألة إلا فتح الله
2:237.english: And now let us mention the virtue of forgiveness and benevolence. The Virtue of Forgiveness and Benevolence. Know that the meaning of forgiveness (Al-'Afw) is that one has a right due, then he drops it and absolves from it regarding retaliation or penalty, and it is different from forbearance (Al-Hilm) and suppressing anger (Kazm Al-Ghaiz); therefore, we have singled it out. Allah the Exalted said: "Take forgiveness and enjoin what is good and turn away from the ignorant." And Allah the Exalted said: "And that you forgive is nearer to piety (Al-Taqwa)." And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Three—by the One in Whose Hand is my soul (Nafs), if I were to swear an oath, I would swear upon them: No wealth decreases from charity, so give charity; and no man forgives an injustice seeking by it the Face of Allah except that Allah increases him in honor (Izz) on the Day of Resurrection; and no man opens upon himself a door of asking except that Allah opens upon him a door of poverty." And he (peace be upon him) said: "Humility does not increase the servant (Al-'Abd) except in elevation, so be humble and Allah will elevate you; and forgiveness does not increase the servant except in honor, so forgive and Allah will honor you; and charity does not increase wealth except in abundance, so give charity and Allah will have mercy on you." And 'A'isha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "I never saw the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) seeking retaliation for an injustice done to him as long as it did not violate the prohibitions of Allah, but if something from the prohibitions of Allah was violated, he was the most severe among them in anger regarding that, and he was never given a choice between two matters except he chose the easiest of them as long as it was not a sin." And 'Uqbah said: "I met the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) one day and I hastened to him and took his hand, or he hastened to me and took my hand, and he said: 'O 'Uqbah, shall I not inform you of the best character traits of the people of this world and the Hereafter: You maintain ties with one who cuts you off, you give to one who deprives you, and you forgive one who wrongs you.'" And he (peace be upon him) said: "Moses (upon him be peace) said: 'O Lord, which of Your servants is most honorable to You?' He said: 'The one who, when he has power, forgives.'" Likewise, Abu Al-Darda' was asked about the most honorable of people, and he said: "The one who forgives when he has power, so forgive and Allah will honor you." And a man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him) complaining.
2:237.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

2:237.arabic: وقال علي كرم الله وجهه في خطبته: إنه سيأتي على الناس زمان عضوض يعض الموسر على ما فيده ولم يؤمر بذلك قال الله تعالى "ولا تنسوا الفضل بينكم"
2:237.english: And Ali, may Allah honor his face, said in his sermon: 'There will come upon people a biting time when the wealthy will bite upon what is in his hand, and he was not commanded to do that.' Allah the Exalted said: 'And do not forget the favor between you.'
2:237.book_title: Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth
2:237.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

2:243.arabic: وقالت طائفة أخرى: بل ندخل ونتوكل ولا نهرب من قدر الله تعالى ولا نفر من الموت فنكون كمن قال الله تعالى فيهم: "ألم تر إلى الذين خرجوا من ديارهم وهم ألوف حذر الموت" فرجعوا إلى عمر فسألوه عن رأيه، فقال: نرجع ولا ندخل على الوباء، فقال له المخالفون في رأيه: أنفر من قدر الله تعالى، قال عمر: نعم نفر من قدر الله إلى قدر الله، ثم ضرب لهم مثلاً فقال: أرأيتم لو كان لأحدكم غنم فهبط وادياً له شعبتان إحداهما مخصبة والأخرى مجدبة، أليس إن رعى المخصبة رعاها بقدر الله تعالى وإن رعى المجدبة رعاها بقدر الله تعالى؟ ف
2:243.english: And another group said: Rather, we enter and rely (Tawakkul) and do not flee from the decree (Qadar) of Allah the Exalted and do not flee from death, so we become like those about whom Allah the Exalted said: 'Have you not seen those who left their homes while they were thousands, fearing death?' So they returned to Umar and asked him about his opinion, and he said: We return and do not enter upon the plague, and those who disagreed with his opinion said to him: Do you flee from the decree (Qadar) of Allah the Exalted? Umar said: Yes, we flee from the decree (Qadar) of Allah to the decree (Qadar) of Allah, then he gave them an example and said: What do you think if one of you had sheep and descended into a valley that has two branches, one fertile and the other barren, is it not that if he grazes the fertile one, he grazes it by the decree (Qadar) of Allah the Exalted, and if he grazes the barren one, he grazes it by the decree (Qadar) of Allah the Exalted? They said: Yes, then he sought Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf to ask him about his opinion - and he was absent - and when morning came, Abd al-Rahman came and Umar asked him about that, and he said: I have something in this matter, O Commander of the Faithful, that I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Umar said: Allah is the Greatest, and Abd al-Rahman said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'When you hear of a plague in a land, do not go forward to it, and when it occurs in a land and you are in it, do not leave it fleeing from it.' So Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, rejoiced at that and praised Allah the Exalted since it agreed with his opinion, and he returned from al-Jabiyah with the people.
2:243.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

2:245.arabic: وقد انخدع بمثل هذا الخيال طائفة وسلكوا طريق الإباحة وقالوا إن الله تعالى غنى عن عبادتنا وعن أن يستقرض منا فأي معنى لقوله: ﴿ من ذا الذي يقرض الله قرضا حسنا ﴾ {} ولو شاء الله إطعام المساكين لأطعمهم فلا حاجة بنا إلى صرف أموالنا إليهم كما قال تعالى حكاية عن الكفار: ﴿ وإذا قيل لهم أنفقوا مما رزقكم الله قال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا أنطعم من لو يشاء الله أطعمه ﴾ {} وقالوا أيضا ﴿ لو شاء الله ما أشركنا ولا آباؤنا ﴾ {} فانظر كيف كانوا صادقين في كلامهم وكيف هلكوا بصدقهم فسبحان من إذا شاء أهلك بالصدق وإذا شا
2:245.english: And a group has been deceived by such an illusion and took the path of permissiveness and said: 'Indeed Allah the Exalted is independent of our worship and of borrowing from us, so what meaning is there to His saying: "Who is it that would loan Allah a good loan (Qardan Hasan) so He may multiply it for him many times over?"' And if Allah willed to feed the poor, He would feed them, so there is no need for us to spend our wealth on them, as Allah the Exalted said narrating from the disbelievers: "And when it is said to them, 'Spend from that which Allah has provided for you,' the disbelievers say to the believers, 'Should we feed one whom, if Allah had willed, He would have fed?'" And they also said: "If Allah had willed, we would not have associated [partners with Him] nor would our fathers." So look how they were truthful in their speech and how they perished by their truthfulness. Glory be to the One who, when He wills, destroys with truth, and when He wills, makes happy with ignorance; He misleads many thereby and guides many thereby. These people, when they thought they were employed for the sake of the poor and the needy—exalted is Allah—then said: 'We have no share in the poor, and Allah has no share in us or in our wealth, whether we spend or withhold,' they perished just as the boy perished when he thought the father's purpose was to employ him for the sake of the slaves, and he did not realize that the intended purpose was the establishment of the attribute of knowledge in his self (Nafs) and its confirmation in his heart (Qalb) so that it would be the cause of his happiness in this world. And that was from the father as gentleness with him in drawing him toward what contains his happiness. So this example clarifies for you the misguidance of those who strayed from this path.
2:245.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

2:245.arabic: ولأجل محبة الله تعالى لبقاء النفوس أمر بالإطعام وحث عليه وعبر عنه بعبادة القرض فقال من ذا الذي يقرض الله قرضا حسنا فإن قلت قولك إن بقاء النسل والنفس محبوب يوهم أن فناءها مكروه عند الله وهو فرق بين الموت والحياة بالإضافة إلى إرادة الله تعالى ومعلوم أن الكل بمشيئة الله وإن الله غني عن العالمين فمن أين يتميز عنده موتهم عن حياتهم أو بقاؤهم عن فنائهم فاعلم أن هذه الكلمة حق أريد بها باطل فإن ما ذكرناه لا ينافي إضافة الكائنات كلها إلى إرادة الله خيرها وشرها ونفعها وضرها ولكن المحبة والكراهية يتضادان وك
2:245.english: And due to the love (Mahabbah) of Allah the Exalted for the preservation of souls (Nufus), He commanded feeding and urged upon it, and expressed it through the worship (Ibadah) of lending, saying: 'Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan (Qardan Hasan) so He may multiply it for him many times over?' If you say: your statement that the preservation of offspring and soul is beloved implies that their annihilation is hated before Allah, and this is a distinction between death and life in relation to the will (Iradah) of Allah the Exalted, and it is known that everything is by the decree (Mashiyyah) of Allah, and indeed Allah is free from need of the worlds, so from where is distinguished before Him their death from their life or their preservation from their annihilation? Know that this statement is truth intended by it falsehood, for what we have mentioned does not contradict attributing all existents to the will (Iradah) of Allah, their good and evil, benefit and harm, but love (Mahabbah) and hatred (Karahiyyah) are opposites, and both do not oppose the will (Iradah), for sometimes a willed thing is hated and sometimes a willed thing is beloved. Sins (Ma'asi) are hated, and they, with the hatred, are willed, and acts of obedience (Ta'at) are willed and intended to be willed, beloved, and pleasing. As for disbelief (Kufr) and evil, we do not say it is pleasing and beloved, but it is willed.
2:245.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

2:245.arabic: فإن قلت: فقد حث الشرع على الأعمال وبالغ في ذكر فضلها حتى طلب الصدقات بقوله: ﴿ من ذا الذي يقرض الله قرضا حسنا ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ ويأخذ الصدقات ﴾ {} فكيف لا يكون الفعل والإنفاق هو الأفضل. فاعلم أن الطبيب إذا أثنى على الدواء لم يدل على أن الدواء مراد لعينه أو على أنه أفضل من الصحة والشفاء الحاصل به ولكن الأعمال علاج لمرض القلوب ومرض القلوب مما لا يشعر به غالبا فهو كبرص على وجه من لا مرآة معه فإنه لا يشعر به ولو ذكر له لا يصدق به والسبيل معه المبالغة في الثناء على غسل الوجه بماء الورد مثلا إن كان ما
2:245.english: If you say: Indeed, the Sacred Law (Sharia) has urged upon works (A'mal) and exaggerated in mentioning their virtue until it sought alms (Sadaqat) by His saying: "Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan (Qardan Hasan) so He may multiply it for him many times over?" (Quran 2:245) and He the Exalted said: "And He accepts the alms (Sadaqat)" (Quran 9:104), so how can the action (Fi'l) and spending (Infaq) not be the best? Then know that when the physician praises the medicine, it does not indicate that the medicine is desired for itself or that it is better than the health (Sihha) and healing (Shifa) attained through it, but rather the works (A'mal) are a treatment (Ilaj) for the disease (Marad) of the hearts (Qulub), and the disease of the hearts is something that is mostly not felt, so it is like leprosy (Baras) on the face of one who has no mirror with him, for he does not feel it, and even if it is mentioned to him, he does not believe it. The way with him is to exaggerate in praising washing the face with rose water (Ma' al-Ward), for example, if rose water removes the leprosy, until he is incited by the excessive praise to persist in it, and thus his disease is removed. For if it were mentioned to him that the intended purpose is the removal of leprosy from your face, perhaps he would abandon the treatment and claim that his face has no defect. And let us give an example closer than this: We say: He has a child whom he taught knowledge (Ilm) and the Quran, and he wanted to establish that in his memory (Hifz) so that it does not vanish from him, and he knew that if he ordered him to repeat (Takrir) and study (Dirasa) so that it remains preserved for him, he would say, "It is preserved, and I have no need for repetition and study," because he thinks that what he memorizes at present remains so forever. And he had slaves, so he ordered the child to teach the slaves and promised him for that with goodness, so that his motivation (Da'iya) becomes abundant through much repetition by teaching. Perhaps the poor boy thinks that the intended purpose is teaching the slaves the Quran and that he has attained.
2:245.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

2:247.arabic: وقال الفقهاء: إذا تساوت درجات المصلين فأحسنهم وجها أولاهم بالإمامة. وقال تعالى ممتنا بذلك: ﴿ وزاده بسطة في العلم والجسم ﴾ {} ولسنا نعني بالجمال ما يحرك الشهوة فإن ذلك أنوثة وإنما نعني به ارتفاع القامة على الاستقامة مع الاعتدال في اللحم وتناسب الاعضاء وتناصف خلقة الوجه بحيث لا تنبو الطباع عن النظر إليه.
2:247.english: And the jurists said: If the degrees of the worshippers are equal, then the most beautiful of them in face is the most deserving of the imamate.
