And Allah the Exalted said, bestowing favor with that: 'And He increased him in expansiveness in knowledge and body' {} And we do not mean by beauty what stirs desire, for that is femininity, but rather we mean by it the height of stature with uprightness, along with moderation in flesh, proportionality of limbs, and symmetry in the creation of the face such that natures do not recoil from looking at it.
2:247.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

2:247.arabic: وقال يوم القيامة ولم يقل في الدنيا و لمسلم من حديث أبي هريرة من ستر مسلما ستره الله في الدنيا و الآخرة وللشيخين من حديث ابن عمر من ستر مسلما ستره الله يوم القيامة وفي خبر آخر فكأنم
2:247.english: And he said 'on the Day of Resurrection' and did not say 'in the world'. And Muslim reported from the hadith of Abu Huraira: 'Whoever covers a Muslim, Allah will cover him in the world and the Hereafter.' And the two Sheikhs (Bukhari and Muslim) reported from the hadith of Ibn Umar: 'Whoever covers a Muslim, Allah will cover him on the Day of Resurrection.' And in another report, as if...
2:247.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

2:249.arabic: السادس العجب بكثرة العدد من الأولاد والخدم والغلمان والعشيرة والأقارب والأنصار والأتباع كما قال الكفار "نحن أكثر أموالاً وأولاداً" وكما قال المؤمنون يوم حنين: لا نغلب اليوم من قلة، وعلاجه ما ذكرناه في الكبر وهو أن يتفكر في ضعفه وضعفهم وأن كلهم عبيد عجزة لا يملكون لأنفسهم ضراً ولا نفعاً. "كم من فئة قليلة غلبت فئة كثيرة بإذن الله" ثم كيف يعجب بهم وأنهم سيفترقون عنه إذا مات فيدفن في قبره ذليلاً معيناً وحده لا يرافقه أهل ولا ولد ولا قريب ولا حميم ولا عشير، فيسلمونه إلى البلى والحيات والعقارب والديدا
2:249.english: The sixth [form of pride] is pride in the multitude of numbers of children, servants, youths, tribe, relatives, supporters, and followers, as the disbelievers said: 'We are more in wealth and children,' and as the believers said on the day of Hunayn: 'We will not be defeated today due to fewness.' Its cure is what we mentioned regarding arrogance, which is to reflect on his weakness and their weakness, and that all of them are weak slaves who possess for themselves neither harm nor benefit. 'How many a small group has overcome a large group by the permission of Allah (Bismillah).' Then how can he be proud of them when they will separate from him when he dies, and he will be buried in his grave humbled, alone, with no family, child, relative, intimate friend, or tribesman accompanying him? They will surrender him to decay, snakes, scorpions, and worms, and they will not avail him anything in his most needy times from them. Likewise, they will flee from him on the Day of Resurrection (Yawm al-Qiyamah): 'The day when a man will flee from his brother, his mother, his father, his wife, and his sons' [the verse]. So what good is there in one who leaves you in your most severe states and flees from you? And how can you be proud of him when he does not benefit you in the grave, the Resurrection (al-Qiyamah), and on the Bridge (al-Sirat) regarding your deeds and the favor of Allah the Exalted? So how can you rely on one who does not benefit you, and forget the blessings of the One who possesses your benefit, harm, death, and life?
2:249.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

2:251.arabic: وأما العز والجاه فبه يدفع الإنسان عن نفسه الذل والضيم ولا يستغني عنه مسلم فإنه لا ينفك عن عدو يؤذيه وظالم يشوش عليه علمه وعمله وفراغه ويشغل قلبه وقلبه رأس ماله وإنما تندفع هذه الشواغل بالعز والجاه ولذلك قيل الدين والسلطان توأمان. قال تعالى: ﴿ وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ اللَّهِ النَّاسَ بَعْضَهُمْ بِبَعْضٍ لَفَسَدَتِ الْأَرْضُ ﴾ ولا معنى للجاه إلا ملك القلوب كما لا معنى للغنى إلا ملك الدراهم ومن ملك الدراهم تسخرت له أرباب القلوب لدفع الأذى عنه فكما يحتاج إلى سقف يدفع عنه المطر وجبة تدفع عنه البرد وكلب يدفع
2:251.english: As for honor (Al-'Izz) and status (Al-Jah), through them a person repels from himself humiliation (Al-Dhull) and oppression (Al-Dhaim), and no Muslim can do without it, for he is not free from an enemy who harms him and an oppressor who disturbs his knowledge (Ilm), his action (Amal), and his leisure, and occupies his heart (Qalb), and his heart is his capital. These distractions are only repelled by honor and status, and therefore it is said: religion (Al-Deen) and authority (Al-Sultan) are twins. Allah the Exalted said: 'And if Allah did not repel people, some by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted.' And the meaning of status (Al-Jah) is nothing but mastery over hearts (Qulub), just as the meaning of wealth (Al-Ghina) is nothing but mastery over dirhams, and whoever masters dirhams, the masters of hearts are subjugated to him to repel harm from him. So just as one needs a roof to repel rain from him, a garment to repel cold from him, and a dog to repel the wolf from his livestock, he also needs someone to repel evil from him through him. And with this intention, the prophets who had no kingdom or dominion would observe the rulers and seek status with them, and likewise the scholars of religion, not with the intention of taking from their treasuries and monopolizing and accumulating in the world by following them. And do not think that the favor of Allah the Exalted upon the Prophet (peace be upon him) when He gave him victory and perfected his religion and made it manifest over all his enemies and established love for him in the hearts until his honor and status expanded through it was less than His favor upon him when he was harmed and beaten until he was compelled to flee and emigrate.
2:251.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

2:251.arabic: فانظر لنفسك وكن فارغ القلب من حديث الناس، فإن الله تعالى يصلح خلقاً كثيراً بإفساد شخص واحد وأشخاص "ولولا دفع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض لفسدت الأرض" وإن الله يؤيد هذا الدين بأقوام لا خلاق لهم، فإنما يخشى أن يفسد طريق الاتعاظ، فأما تخرس ألسنة الوعاظ ووراءهم باعث الرياسة وحب الدنيا فلا يكون ذلك أبداً.
2:251.english: So look to yourself and be empty of heart (Qalb) from the talk of people, for Allah the Exalted reforms many creatures through the corruption of one person and persons. 'And were it not for Allah repelling people, some by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted.' And Allah supports this religion with people who have no share (in the Hereafter). Indeed, what is feared is that the path of taking admonition (I'tizaz) becomes corrupted. As for silencing the tongues of preachers while behind them is the motive of leadership-seeking (Riyasah) and love of the worldly life (Dunya), that will never be.
2:251.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

2:251.arabic: وقال في قوله تعالى ولولا دفع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض قال بالرغبة والرهبة والحياء والمداراة
2:251.english: And he said regarding His statement, the Exalted: 'And were it not for Allah repelling people, some by means of others' - he said: through desire (al-raghbah) and fear (al-rahbah) and modesty (al-haya') and tactful dealing (al-mudara'ah).
2:251.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

2:253.arabic: وهذه الاختلافات بعضها لاختلاف الأحوال والمقامات وبعضها لما سبق في الأزل من التفاضل والتفاوت في القسمة بين العباد، وقد قال تعالى: " ولقد فضلنا بعض النبيين على بعض "، وقد قال: " منهم من كلم الله ورفع بعضهم درجات " فكان عيسى عليه السلام من المفضلين ولإدلاله سلم على نفسه، فقال: " والسلام علي يوم ولدت ويوم أموت ويوم أبعث حياً" وهذا انبساط منه لما شاهد من اللطف في مقام الأنس.
2:253.english: And these differences, some of them are due to the differences in states (Ahwal) and stations (Maqamat), and some of them are due to what preceded in pre-eternity (Al-Azal) of preference (Tafadul) and disparity (Tafawut) in the apportionment (Qismah) among the servants (Ibad). And indeed, Allah the Exalted has said: 'And indeed, We have preferred some of the Prophets (Nabiyyin) over others.' And He has said: 'Among them are those whom Allah spoke to, and He raised some of them in degrees.' So Jesus (Isa), peace be upon him, was among the preferred ones, and due to his familiarity (Idlal), he greeted himself, saying: 'And peace be upon me the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I am raised alive.' And this is an expansion (Inbisat) from him due to what he witnessed of gentleness (Lutf) in the station (Maqam) of intimacy (Uns).
2:253.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

2:254.arabic: بل في الحديث الصحيح ما روي أنه ﭬ قال "من كانت لأخيه عنده مظلمة في عرض أو مال فليستحللها منه من قبل أن يأتي يوم ليس هناك دينار ولا درهم، إنما يؤخذ من حسناته فإن لم يكن له حسنات أخذ من سيئات صاحبه فزيدت على سيئاته"[226]
2:254.english: Rather, in the authentic hadith, it is narrated that he (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever has a grievance against his brother in honor or wealth, let him seek its resolution from him before a day comes when there is no dinar nor dirham; indeed, it will be taken from his good deeds, and if he has no good deeds, it will be taken from the bad deeds of his companion and added to his bad deeds."
2:254.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

2:254.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
2:254.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Whatever is in the Quran of 'O you who believe' is in the Torah 'O you poor ones (al-Masakin)'.
2:254.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

2:255.arabic: الأصل الثاني: سؤال منكر ونكير[40] وقد وردت به الأخبار فيجب التصديق به لأنه ممكن إذ ليس يستدعى إلا إعادة الحياة إلى جزء من الأجزاء الذي به فهم الخطاب وذلك ممكن في نفسه ولا يدفع ذلك ما يشاهد من سكون أجزاء الميت وعدم سماعنا للسؤال له فإن النائم ساكن بظاهره ويدرك بباطنه من الآلام واللذات ما يحس بتأثيره عند التنبه وقد كان رسول الله ﭬ يسمع كلام جبريل عليه السلام ويشاهده ومن حوله لا يسمعونه ولا يرونه[41] ولا يحيطون بشيء من علمه إلا بما شاء فإذا لم يخلق لهم السمع والرؤية لم يدركوه.
2:255.english: The second foundation: The questioning by Munkar and Nakir [40], and reports have come regarding it, so belief in it is obligatory because it is possible, as it only requires restoring life to a part of the parts through which understanding of the address occurs, and that is possible in itself. And what is observed of the stillness of the parts of the dead and our not hearing the questioning for him does not negate that, for the sleeper is still in his outward appearance and perceives in his inward self from pains and pleasures what he feels its effect upon awakening. And the Messenger of Allah ﭬ used to hear the speech of Jibril (Gabriel), peace be upon him, and see him, while those around him did not hear him nor see him [41], and they do not encompass anything of His knowledge except by what He wills. So if He did not create for them hearing and sight, they would not perceive it.
2:255.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Foundations of Belief'

2:255.arabic: الحياة والقدرة: وأنه تعالى حي قادر جبار قاهر لا يعتريه قصور ولا عجز ولا تأخذه سنة ولا نوم ولا يعارضه فناء ولا موت وأنه ذو الملك والملكوت والعزة والجبروت له السلطان والقهر والخلق والأمر والسموات مطويات بيمينه والخلائق مقهورون في قبضته.
2:255.english: Life and Power: And that He, the Exalted, is Living (Hayy), Powerful (Qadir), Compelling (Jabbar), Subduer (Qahir) - no deficiency or incapacity affects Him, and neither drowsiness (sinah) nor sleep (nawm) overtakes Him, nor does annihilation or death oppose Him. And He is the Possessor of Dominion (Mulk) and Sovereignty (Malakut), Might (Izzah) and Omnipotence (Jabarut) - to Him belongs Authority (Sultan), Subjugation (Qahr), Creation (Khalq), and Command (Amr). The heavens are folded in His right hand, and the creatures are subdued in His grasp.
2:255.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

2:255.arabic: وقال ﭬ: (من قال حين يأوي إلى فراشه أستغفر الله العظيم الذي لا إله إلا هو الحي القيوم وأتوب إليه ثلاث مرات غفر الله له ذنوبه وإن كانت مثل زبد البحر أو عدد رمل عالج أو عدد ورق الشجر أو عدد أيام الدنيا[112])
2:255.english: And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever says when he goes to his bed: "I seek forgiveness from Allah the Great, the One who there is no deity except Him, the Living (Al-Hayy), the Self-Sustaining (Al-Qayyum), and I repent to Him" three times, Allah will forgive him his sins, even if they were like the foam of the sea or the number of the sand of 'Alaj or the number of leaves of trees or the number of days of the world.'
2:255.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

2:255.arabic: [112] حديث من قال حين يأوي إلى فراشه أستغفر الله العظيم الذي لا إله إلا هو الحي القيوم وأتوب إليه ثلاث مرات غفر الله له ذنوبه وإن كانت مثل زبد البحر الحديث أخرجه الترمذي من حديث أبي سعيد وقال غريب لا نعرفه إلا من حديث عبد الله بن الوليد الوصافي قلت الوصافي وإن كان ضعيفا فقد تابعه عليه عصام بن قدامة وهو ثقة ورواه البخاري في التاريخ دون قوله حين يأوي إلى فراشه وقوله ثلاث مرات.
2:255.english: Hadith: Whoever says when he goes to his bed: 'I seek forgiveness from Allah the Great, who there is no god except Him, the Living, the Self-Subsisting (Al-Hayy Al-Qayyum), and I repent to Him' three times, Allah will forgive his sins even if they were like the foam of the sea. The hadith was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi from the narration of Abu Sa'id and he said: 'It is strange (gharib), we do not know it except from the narration of Abdullah ibn Al-Walid Al-Wasafi.' I said: Al-Wasafi, even though he is weak, he was followed in this by 'Issam ibn Qudamah, who is trustworthy. And Al-Bukhari narrated it in Al-Tarikh without his saying 'when he goes to his bed' and his saying 'three times'.
2:255.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication

2:256.arabic: وللطبراني من حديث سلمة بن الأكوع وألزمهم كلمة التقوى قال لا إله إلا الله وللطبراني في الدعاء عن ابن عباس كلمة طيبة قال شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله وله عنه في قوله دعوة الحق قال شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله وله عنه فقد استمسك بالعروة الوثقى قال لا إله الا الله
2:256.english: And from Al-Tabarani from the narration of Salamah ibn Al-Akwa': 'And he made them adhere to the Word of Piety (Kalimat al-Taqwa), he said: There is no god but Allah.' And from Al-Tabarani in Al-Du'a' from Ibn Abbas: 'A Good Word (Kalimah Tayyibah), he said: The testimony that there is no god but Allah.' And from him regarding His saying 'The Call of Truth (Da'wat al-Haqq)', he said: 'The testimony that there is no god but Allah.' And from him: 'He has grasped the Most Trustworthy Handhold (Al-'Urwah al-Wuthqa), he said: There is no god but Allah.'
2:256.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

2:257.arabic: الحمد لله الذي بيده مقاليد الأمور، وبقدرته مفاتيح الخيرات والشرور، مخرج أوليائه من الظلمات إلى النور، ومورد أعدائه ورطات الغرور، والصلاة على محمد مخرج الخلائق من الديجور، وعلى آله وأصحابه الذين لم تغرهم الحياة الدنيا ولم يغرهم بالله الغرور، صلاة تتوالى على ممر الدهور ومكر الساعات والشهور. أما بعد: فمفتاح السعادة التيقظ والفطنة، ومنبع الشقاوة الغرور والغفلة فلا نعمة لله على عباده أعظم من الإيمان والمعرفة، ولا وسيلة سوى انشراح الصدر بنور البصيرة، ولا نقمة أعظم من الكفر والمعصية، ولا داعي إليهما سو
2:257.english: Praise be to Allah who in His hand are the keys of affairs, and by His power are the keys of good and evil, He brings out His allies from the darknesses to the light, and brings His enemies into the pitfalls of delusion, and prayers upon Muhammad who brings out the creatures from the darkness, and upon his family and companions who were not deluded by the worldly life nor were they deluded about Allah with delusion, prayers that continue through the passage of ages and the plotting of hours and months. After that: The key to happiness is vigilance and insight, and the source of misery is delusion and heedlessness, so there is no blessing from Allah upon His servants greater than faith and knowledge, and no means except the expansion of the chest with the light of insight, and no punishment greater than disbelief and disobedience, and no caller to them except the blindness of the heart with the darkness of ignorance, so the intelligent ones and possessors of insights, their hearts are "like a niche in which is a lamp, the lamp is in a glass, the glass as if it were a brilliant star, lit from a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if untouched by fire, light upon light" and the deluded ones, their hearts are "like darknesses in a deep sea covered by waves, above which are clouds, darknesses, one above another, if he puts out his hand, he can hardly see it, and he for whom Allah has not made light, for him there is no light" so the intelligent ones are those whom Allah intended to guide, so He expanded their chests for Islam and guidance, and the deluded ones are those whom Allah intended to lead astray, so He made their chests tight and constricted as if they were climbing into the sky. And the deluded one is he whose insight has not opened to be sufficient for the guidance of his self and
2:257.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

2:257.arabic: وفيه أيضا: (إن الله تعالى شرف الكعبة وعظمها ولو أن عبدا هدمها حجرا حجرا ثم أحرقها ما بلغ جرم من استخف بولي من أولياء الله تعالى. قال الأعرابي: ومن أولياء الله تعالى؟ قال: المؤمنون كلهم أولياء الله تعالى أما سمعت قول الله عز وجل: ﴿ الله ولي الذين آمنوا يخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور ﴾ {})
2:257.english: And in it also: (Indeed, Allah the Exalted honored and magnified the Kaaba, and if a servant were to demolish it stone by stone then burn it, it would not reach the crime of one who belittles a friend (Wali) from among the friends (Awliya) of Allah the Exalted. The Bedouin said: And who are the friends (Awliya) of Allah the Exalted? He said: The believers, all of them are friends (Awliya) of Allah the Exalted. Have you not heard the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: 'Allah is the Friend (Wali) of those who believe; He brings them out from the darknesses into the light' {})
2:257.topic: Al-Ghazali on the outer and inner dimensions of worship, from 'Fear and Hope'

2:258.arabic: وقال تعالى ألم تر إلى الذي حاج إبراهيم في ربه إلى قوله فبهت الذي كفر إذ ذكر سبحانه احتجاج إبراهيم ومجادلته وإفحامه خصمه في معرض الثناء عليه
2:258.english: And He (Exalted is He) said: 'Have you not seen the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord...' up to His saying: '...so the one who disbelieved was confounded' when He (Glorified is He) mentioned Abraham's argumentation (Ihtijāj), his disputation (Mujādalah), and his silencing of his opponent in the context of praising him.
2:258.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Foundations of Belief'

2:259.arabic: يقال إن الخضر وإلياس عليهما السلام إذا التقيا في كل موسم لم يفترقا إلا عن هذه الكلمات: بسم الله ما شاء الله لا قوة إلا بالله ما شاء الله كل نعمة من الله ما شاء الله ا
2:259.english: It is said that Al-Khidr and Ilyas (peace be upon them both), whenever they meet in every season, do not part except with these words: In the name of Allah (Bismillah), what Allah wills (Mā shā'a Allāh), there is no power except with Allah (Lā quwwata illā billāh), what Allah wills (Mā shā'a Allāh), every blessing is from Allah (Kullu ni'matin min Allāh), what Allah wills (Mā shā'a Allāh)...
2:259.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

2:260.arabic: فإذن لا يتم التوكل إلا بقوة القلب وقوة اليقين جميعاً، إذ بهما يحصل سكون القلب وطمأنينته، فالسكون في القلب شيء واليقين شيء آخر فكم من يقين لا طمأنينة معه كما قال تعالى لإبراهيم عليه السلام: "أَوَلَمْ تُؤْمِنْ قَالَ بَلَىٰ وَلَٰكِنْ لِيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِي" فالتمس أن يكون مشاهداً إحياء الميت بعينه ليثبت في خياله فإن النفس تتبع الخيال وتطمئن به ولا تطمئن باليقين في ابتداء أمرها إلى أن تبلغ بالآخرة إلى درجة النفس المطمئنة؛ وذلك لا يكون في البداية أصلاً، وكم من مطمئن لا يقين له كسائر أرباب الملل والمذا
2:260.english: Therefore, Reliance (Tawakkul) is not complete except with strength of the Heart (Qalb) and strength of Certainty (Yaqeen) together, for through them the tranquility (Sukun) of the Heart (Qalb) and its peace (Itmi'nan) are attained. Tranquility (Sukun) in the Heart (Qalb) is one thing and Certainty (Yaqeen) is another thing, for how much Certainty (Yaqeen) there is without peace (Itmi'nan) with it, as Allah the Exalted said to Ibrahim, peace be upon him: 'Have you not believed? He said: Yes, but so that my Heart (Qalb) may be at peace (Yatma'inn).' So he sought to witness the revival of the dead with his own eye so that it would be established in his imagination, for the Soul (Nafs) follows the imagination and is at peace (Tatma'inn) with it, and it is not at peace (Tatma'inn) with Certainty (Yaqeen) at the beginning of its affair until it reaches in the Hereafter the degree of the Soul at Peace (Nafs al-Mutma'innah); and that does not occur at the beginning at all. And how many are at peace (Mutma'inn) without Certainty (Yaqeen) for them, like the rest of the people of religions and schools, for the Jew is at peace (Mutma'inn) in his Heart (Qalb) with his Judaism, and likewise the Christian, and they have no Certainty (Yaqeen) at all, and they only follow conjecture (Zann) and what the Souls (Anfus) desire, and indeed guidance (Huda) has come to them from their Lord, which is the cause of Certainty (Yaqeen), except that they turn away from it. Therefore, cowardice (Jubn) and boldness (Jara'ah) are instincts, and Certainty (Yaqeen) does not benefit with them, so they are one of the causes that oppose the state of Reliance (Tawakkul), just as weakness of Certainty (Yaqeen) in the four traits is one of the causes. And when these causes are gathered, Trust (Thiqah) in Allah the Exalted is attained. And it has been said: It is written in the Torah: Cursed is he whose trust (Thiqah) is in a human like him. And He, peace be upon him, said: 'Whoever seeks might through slaves, Allah the Exalted will humiliate him.' And when the meaning of Reliance (Tawakkul) is unveiled to you and you know the state that is called Reliance (Tawakkul), then know that that state has in strength and weakness three degrees: The first degree is what we mentioned: It is that his state regarding Allah the Exalted and Trust (Thiqah) in His guarantee and care is like his state in trust (Thiqah) in an agent.
2:260.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

2:261.arabic: فإن قلت إن اختلافها باختلاف بذورها وأصولها فمتى كان فى النواة نخلة مطوقة لعناقيد الرطب ومتى كان فى حبة واحدة سمع سنابل فى كل سنبلة مائة ثم أنظر إلى أرض البوادى وفتش ظاهرها وباطنها فتراها ترابا متشابها فإذا أنزل عليها الماء اهتزت وربت وأنبتت من كل زوج بهيج الوانا مختلفة ونباتا متشابها وغير متشابه لكل واحد طعم وريح ولون وشكل يخالف الآخر فانظر إلى كثرتها واختلاف أصنافها وكثرة أشكالها ثم اختلاف طبائع النبات وكثرة منافعه وكيف أودع الله تعالى العقاقير المنافع الغريبة فهذا النبات يغذى وهذا يقوى وهذا يح
2:261.english: If you say that their difference is due to the difference in their seeds and origins, then when was there in the kernel a palm tree encircled with clusters of fresh dates, and when was there in a single grain seven ears, in every ear a hundred? Then look at the land of the deserts and search its surface and interior, and you will see it as similar dust. But when water is sent down upon it, it quivers and swells and brings forth from every delightful pair different colors and plants, similar and dissimilar, each one having a taste, scent, color, and shape differing from the other. So look at their multitude, the difference in their kinds, the abundance of their forms, then the difference in the natures of plants and the abundance of their benefits, and how Allah the Exalted has deposited in them strange beneficial medicines: this plant nourishes, this strengthens, this gives life, this kills, this cools, this heats, this when it reaches the stomach suppresses the yellow bile from the depths of the veins, this transforms into yellow bile, this suppresses the phlegm and black bile, this transforms into them, this purifies the blood, this dissolves blood, this gladdens, this induces sleep, this strengthens, this weakens. Not a leaf nor a straw grows from the earth except that in it are benefits that humans cannot fully comprehend. And each one of these plants requires the farmer in its cultivation a specific action: the palm trees favor generosity, they are pruned; the crops are cleared of weeds and thickets; some of it is propagated by scattering the seed in the earth, some by planting branches, some is grafted onto trees. And if we wanted to mention the differences in the genera of plants, their types, their benefits, their states, and their wonders, the days would not suffice in describing that, so suffice it for you...
2:261.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Contemplation'

2:262.arabic: وقال بعضهم في إخلاص ساعة نجاة الأبد ولكن الإخلاص عزيز ويقال العلم بذر والعمل زرع وماؤه الإخلاص وقال بعضهم إذا أبغض الله عبدا أعطاه ثلاثا ومنعه ثلاثا أعطاه صحبة الصالحين ومنعه القبول منهم وأعطاه الأعمال الصالحة ومنعه الإخلاص فيها وأعطاه الحكمة ومنعه الصدق فيها وقال السوسي مراد الله من عمل الخلائق الإخلاص فقط وقال الجنيد إن لله عبادا عقلوا فلما عقلوا عملوا فلما عملوا أخلصوا فاستدعاهم الإخلاص إلى أبواب البر أجمع وقال محمد بن سعيد المروزي الأمر كله يرجع إلى أصلين فعل منه بك وفعل منك له فترضى ما فعل
2:262.english: And some of them said: 'In sincerity (ikhlas) of an hour is salvation of eternity, but sincerity (ikhlas) is precious.' And it is said: 'Knowledge is seed, and action is cultivation, and its water is sincerity (ikhlas).' And some of them said: 'When Allah hates a servant, He gives him three and denies him three: He gives him companionship of the righteous and denies him acceptance from them, and He gives him righteous deeds and denies him sincerity (ikhlas) in them, and He gives him wisdom and denies him truthfulness in it.' And Al-Susi said: 'What Allah wants from the actions of creatures is only sincerity (ikhlas).' And Al-Junayd said: 'Verily, Allah has servants who understood, so when they understood, they acted, and when they acted, they were sincere (akhlasu), so sincerity (ikhlas) called them to all the gates of righteousness.' And Muhammad ibn Sa'id Al-Marwazi said: 'The whole matter returns to two foundations: action from Him toward you and action from you toward Him, so be pleased with what He does and be sincere (tukhlis) in what you do, then indeed you have become happy.'
2:262.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

2:262.arabic: وقد روي أن ابن عمر سرقت ناقته فطلبها حتى أعيا، ثم قال: في سبيل الله تعالى، فدخل المسجد فصلى فيه ركعتين فجاءه رجل فقال: يا أبا عبد الرحمن، إن ناقتك في مكان كذا فلبس نعله وقام، ثم قال: أستغفر الله وجلس، فقيل له: ألا تذهب فتأخذها! فقال: إني كنت قلت في سبيل الله. وقال بعض الشيوخ: رأيت بعض إخواني في النوم بعد موته فقلت: ما فعل الله بك؟ قال: غفر لي وأدخلني الجنة وعرض علي منازلي فيها فرأيتها، قال: وهو مع ذلك كئيب حزين! فقلت: قد غفر لك ودخلت الجنة وأنت حزين! فتنفس الصعداء ثم قال: نعم إني لا أزال حزيناً
2:262.english: And it has been narrated that Ibn Umar's she-camel was stolen, so he searched for it until he became exhausted, then he said: In the path of Allah (سبيل الله) the Exalted, so he entered the mosque and prayed two units of prayer in it, then a man came to him and said: O Abu Abd al-Rahman, your she-camel is in such-and-such place, so he put on his sandal and stood up, then he said: I seek forgiveness from Allah (أستغفر الله) and sat down, so it was said to him: Will you not go and take it! He said: Indeed I had said it is in the path of Allah (سبيل الله). And some of the shaykhs said: I saw one of my brothers in a dream after his death, so I said: What has Allah done with you? He said: He forgave me and entered me into Paradise and showed me my dwellings in it, so I saw them, he said: And he with that was gloomy sad! So I said: He has forgiven you and you have entered Paradise and you are sad! So he sighed deeply then said: Yes, indeed I do not cease being sad until the Day of Resurrection. I said: And why? He said: Indeed when I saw my dwellings in Paradise, elevated for me were stations in the highest levels (عليين) what I have not seen the like of in what I saw, so I rejoiced in them, then when I intended to enter them, a caller called from above them: Turn him away from it, for this is not for him, indeed it is for the one who fulfilled the path (أمضى السبيل), so I said: And what is fulfilling the path? So it was said to me: You used to say about something that it is in the path of Allah (سبيل الله) then you would retract in it, so if you had fulfilled the path, we would have fulfilled for you. And it was narrated about some of the worshippers in Mecca that he was sleeping next to a man with his purse, so the man woke up and missed his purse, so he accused him of it, so he said to him: How much was in your purse? So he mentioned to him, so he carried it from the house and weighed it from his own, then after that his companions informed him that they had taken the purse jokingly with him, so he came and his companions with him and returned the gold, so he refused and said: Take it lawful pure, for I would not return in wealth I have expended in the path of Allah (سبيل الله) the Exalted, so he did not accept, so they insisted upon him, so he called his son and began to make it into bundles and send it to the poor until none of it remained. Thus were the character traits of the predecessors, and likewise whoever took a loaf of bread to give to a poor person and he was absent, he would dislike returning it to the house after expending it, so he would give it to another poor person, and likewise he would do with dirhams, dinars, and all other charities. Fifth: And it is the lowest of the degrees that he does not supplicate against the thief who wronged him by taking, for if he does, his reliance (توكله) becomes invalid and that indicates his dislike and regret over what has passed, and his asceticism (زهده) becomes invalid, and if he exaggerates, his reward also becomes invalid in what befell him; for in the report: "Whoever supplicates against his wrongdoer has indeed taken revenge"[37]. And it was narrated that al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym's horse was stolen and its value was twenty thousand and he was standing praying, so he did not cut off his prayer and did not become agitated to seek it, so a group of people came to him.
2:262.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

2:262.arabic: يفزع الناس وهم لا يفزعون ويخاف الناس وهم لا يخافون وهم أولياء الله الذين لا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون فقيل من هؤلاء يا رسول الله فقال هم المتحابون في الله تعالى حديث قال أبو إدريس الخولاني لمعاذ أني احبك في الله فقال أبشر ثم أبشر فإني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول تنصب لطائفة من الناس كراسي حول العرش يوم القيامة الحديث أخرجه أحمد و الحاكم في حديث طويل أن أبا إدريس قال قلت و الله إني لأحبك في الله قال فأني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول أن المتحابين بجلال الله في ظل عرشه يوم لا ظل
2:262.english: The people will be terrified while they are not terrified, and the people will fear while they do not fear, and they are the allies (Awliya) of Allah upon whom there is no fear nor do they grieve. It was said: Who are these, O Messenger of Allah? He said: They are those who love each other for the sake of Allah the Exalted. A hadith: Abu Idris al-Khawlani said to Mu'adh: I love you for the sake of Allah. He said: Rejoice, then rejoice, for I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, say: Chairs will be set up for a group of people around the Throne on the Day of Resurrection. The hadith was narrated by Ahmad and al-Hakim in a long hadith that Abu Idris said: I said: By Allah, I love you for the sake of Allah. He said: For I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, say: Those who love each other for the majesty of Allah will be in the shade of His Throne on a day when there is no shade except His shade. Al-Hakim said: Authentic according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, and it is in al-Tirmidhi from the narration of Abu Muslim al-Khawlani from Mu'adh with the wording: Those who love each other for My majesty, for them are pulpits of light, the prophets and martyrs will envy them. He said: A good authentic hadith. And in Ahmad from the hadith of Abu Malik al-Ash'ari: Allah has servants who are neither prophets nor martyrs, the prophets and martyrs will envy them for their stations and their closeness to Allah. The hadith includes: Love each other for the sake of Allah and be sincere with it, Allah will place for them on the Day of Resurrection pulpits of light, making their faces light and their garments light. The people will be terrified on the Day of Resurrection while they are not terrified, and they are the allies (Awliya) of Allah upon whom there is no fear nor do they grieve. And in it is Shahr ibn Hawshab, who is disputed, and it was narrated by Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, and he said in it: Around the Throne are pulpits of light upon which are people whose garments are light and their faces are light, they are neither prophets nor martyrs, the prophets and martyrs will envy them. They said: O Messenger of Allah, describe them for us. He said: They are those who love each other for the sake of Allah, and those who sit together for the sake of Allah, and those who visit each other for the sake of Allah. The hadith of Abu Hurayra: Around the Throne are pulpits of light upon which are people whose garments are light and their faces are light, they are neither prophets nor martyrs. The hadith was narrated by al-Nasa'i in his Sunan al-Kubra and its narrators are trustworthy. And he, peace be upon him, said: No two people love each other for the sake of Allah except that the more beloved of them to Allah is the one who loves his companion more. The hadith: No two people love each other for the sake of Allah except that the more beloved of them to Allah is the one who loves his companion more. It was narrated by Ibn Hibban and al-Hakim from the hadith of Anas and he said: Authentic chain. And it is said: The two brothers in Allah, if one of them is of higher station than the other, the other is raised with him to his station, and he joins him just as offspring join the parents and family members join each other, because brotherhood when acquired in Allah is not less than brotherhood of birth. He, the Exalted, said: We joined them with their offspring, and We did not diminish anything from their deeds. And he, peace be upon him, said: Allah the Exalted says: My love is due to those who visit each other for My sake and.
2:262.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

2:262.arabic: [7] حديث أنس في صلاة الصبح من توضأ ثم توجه إلى المسجد يصلي فيه الصلاة كان له بكل خطوة حسنة ومحى عنه سيئة والحسنة بعشر أمثالها وإذا صلى ثم انصرف عند طلوع الشمس كتب له بكل شعرة في جسده حسنة وانقلب بحجة مبرورة فإن جلس حتى يركع كتب له بكل ركعة ألفا ألف حسنة ومن صلى العتمة فله مثل ذلك وانقلب بحجة مبرورة لم أجد له أصلا بهذا السياق وفي شعب الإيمان للبيهقي من حديث أنس بسند ضعيف ومن صلى المغرب في جماعة كان له كحجة مبرورة وعمرة متقبلة.
2:262.english: [7] The hadith of Anas regarding the morning prayer: Whoever performs ablution then heads to the mosque to pray the prayer therein, for him with every step is a good deed and a sin is erased from him, and the good deed is multiplied tenfold. And if he prays then departs at sunrise, it is written for him for every hair on his body a good deed and he returns with an accepted pilgrimage. If he sits until he bows, it is written for him for every bow a thousand thousand good deeds. And whoever prays the evening prayer, for him is the same, and he returns with an accepted pilgrimage. I did not find a basis for this narration in this sequence, and in Shu'ab al-Iman by al-Bayhaqi from the hadith of Anas with a weak chain. And whoever prays the sunset prayer in congregation, for him is like an accepted pilgrimage and an accepted 'umrah.
2:262.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Book of Knowledge'

2:264.arabic: الوظيفة الخامسة: أن لا يفسد صدقته بالمن والأذى قال الله تعالى: ﴿ لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى ﴾{} واختلفوا في حقيقة المن والأذى فقيل المن أن يذكرها والأذى أن يظهرها وقال سفيان: من من فسدت صدقته، فقيل له: كيف المن؟ فقال: أن يذكره ويتحدث به. وقيل المن أن يستخدمه بالعطاء والأذى أن يعيره بالفقر وقيل المن أن يتكبر عليه لأجل عطائه والأذى أن ينتهره أو يوبخه بالمسألة وقد قال ﭬ: (لا يقبل الله صدقة منان[18]) وعندي أن المن له أصل ومغرس وهو من أحوال القلب وصفاته ثم يتفرع عليه أحوال ظاهرة على اللسان والجوا
2:264.english: The fifth duty: that he does not spoil his charity with reminding and harm. Allah the Exalted said: 'Do not invalidate your charities with reminding and harm.' And they differed regarding the reality of reminding and harm. It was said: reminding is to mention it, and harm is to display it. And Sufyan said: whoever reminds, his charity is spoiled. He was asked: How is reminding? He said: that he mentions it and speaks about it. And it was said: reminding is to employ him with the giving, and harm is to reproach him with poverty. And it was said: reminding is to be arrogant toward him because of his giving, and harm is to rebuke him or scold him with the asking. And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah does not accept the charity of a remembrancer.' And in my view, reminding has an origin and a planting place, and it is from the states (Ahwal) of the Heart (Qalb) and its attributes, then it branches out into apparent states on the tongue and the limbs. So its origin is that he sees himself as a benefactor to him and a bestower of favor upon him, and his right is to see the poor person as a benefactor to him by accepting the right of Allah the Exalted from him, which is his purification and his salvation from the Fire, and that if he were to accept it, he would remain indebted by it. So his right is that the poor person receives it from him, since he made his hand a deputy for Allah the Exalted in receiving the right of Allah the Exalted. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, charity falls into the hand of Allah the Exalted before it falls into the hand of the asker.' So let him realize that he is surrendering to Allah the Exalted his right, and the poor person is taking from Allah the Exalted his provision after its arrival to Allah the Exalted. And if he had a debt to a person and he transferred it to his servant or his attendant who is responsible for his provision, the belief that the receiver is under his favor would be foolishness and ignorance, for the benefactor to him is the one who...
2:264.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

2:264.arabic: ولنضرب للخوف مثلا فما من عبد يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر إلا وهو خائف من الله خوفا ينطلق عليه الاسم ولكنه خوف غير صادق أى غير بالغ درجة الحقيقة أما تراه إذا خاف سلطانا أو قاطع طريق فى سفره كيف يصفر لونه وترتعد فرائصه ويتنغص عليه عيشه ويتعذر عليه أكله ونومه وينقسم عليه فكره حتى لا ينتفع به أهله وولده وقد ينزعج عن الوطن فيستبدل بالأنس الوحشة وبالراحة التعب والمشقة والتعرض للأخطار كل ذلك خوفا من درك المحذور ثم إنه يخاف النار ولا يظهر عليه شىء من ذلك عند جريان معصية عليه ولذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لم
2:264.english: And let us give an example for Fear (Khauf): there is no servant who believes in Allah and the Last Day except that he fears Allah with a fear that the name applies to, but it is a fear that is not truthful (ṣādiq), meaning it does not reach the degree of reality. Do you not see when he fears a ruler or a highway robber on his journey, how his color pales, his limbs tremble, his life becomes bitter, his eating and sleeping become difficult, and his thought becomes divided so that his family and children do not benefit from him, and he may be disturbed from his homeland, exchanging familiarity for loneliness, and comfort for fatigue, hardship, and exposure to dangers—all of that out of fear of encountering the dreaded thing? Then, he fears the Fire, yet nothing of that appears upon him when a sin occurs upon him. Therefore, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'I have not seen anything like the Fire whose fleeer sleeps, nor like Paradise whose seeker sleeps'—the hadith 'I have not seen anything like the Fire whose fleeer sleeps' has preceded. So, realization (taḥqīq) in these matters is very rare, and there is no end to these stations (maqāmāt) until their completion is attained, but each servant has a share according to his state, either weak or strong; when it becomes strong, he is called truthful (ṣādiq) in it. Thus, the knowledge of Allah the Exalted, His veneration, and fear of Him have no end.
2:264.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

2:264.arabic: وقيل لعائشة رضي الله عنها: متى يكون الرجل مسيئاً: قالت؟ إذا ظن أنه محسن، وقد قال تعالى "لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى" والمن نتيجة استعظام الصدقة، واستعظام العمل هو العجب. فظهر بهذا أن العجب مذموم جداً.
2:264.english: And it was said to Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her: When is a man sinful? She said: When he thinks he is doing good. And Allah the Exalted said: "Do not invalidate your charities with reminders of favor and harm." And the reminder of favor results from magnifying the charity, and magnifying the action is self-admiration (Al-'Ujb). So it became clear by this that self-admiration (Al-'Ujb) is very blameworthy.
2:264.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

2:264.arabic: وهذه الشريطة من الزكوات تجري مجرى الخشوع من الصلاة وثبت ذلك بقوله ﭬ: (ليس للمرء من صلاته إلا ما عقل منها[20]) وهذا كقوله ﭬ لا يتقبل الله صدقة منان وكقوله عز وجل: ﴿ لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى ﴾{} وأما فتوى الفقيه بوقوعها موقعها وبراءة ذمته عنها دون هذا الشرط فحديث آخر وقد أشرنا إلى معناه في كتاب الصلاة.
2:264.english: And this condition of the Zakat (obligatory alms) flows in the course of the Khushu' (humble devotion) from the prayer, and that is established by his saying ﭬ: 'There is nothing for a person from his prayer except what he comprehends from it.' And this is like his saying ﭬ: 'Allah does not accept the charity of a Munnan (one who reminds of his favor).' And like His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Do not invalidate your charities with the Mann (reminding of favor) and the Adha (harm).' As for the fatwa (legal opinion) of the Faqih (jurist) regarding its occurrence in its place and the clearance of his responsibility from it without this condition, that is another discussion, and we have indicated its meaning in the Book of Prayer.
2:264.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

2:264.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
2:264.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Whatever is in the Quran of 'O you who have believed' is in the Torah 'O you the poor ones (al-Masakin)'.
2:264.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

2:267.arabic: الوظيفة السابعة: أن ينتقي من ماله أجوده وأحبه إليه وأجله وأطيبه فإن الله تعالى طيب لا يقبل إلا طيبا وإذا كان المخرج من شبهة فربما لا يكون ملكا له مطلقا فلا يقع الموقع وفي حديث أبان عن أنس بن مالك طوبى لعبد أنفق من مال اكتسبه من غير معصية[21] وإذا لم يكن المخرج من جيد المال فهو من سوء الأدب إذ قد يمسك الجيد لنفسه أو لعبده أو لأهله فيكون قد آثر على الله عز وجل غيره ولو فعل هذا بضيفه وقدم إليه أردأ طعام في بيته لأوغر بذلك صدره هذا إن كان نظره إلى الله عز وجل وإن كان نظره إلى نفسه وثوابه في الآخرة ف
2:267.english: The Seventh Duty: That he selects from his wealth its best, most beloved to him, most noble, and purest, for Allah the Exalted is Pure (Tayyib) and does not accept except the pure. And if the expenditure is from doubtful sources, perhaps it is not absolutely his property, so it does not achieve its proper place. In the hadith of Aban from Anas ibn Malik: 'Blessed is the servant who spends from wealth he earned without disobedience.' And if the expenditure is not from good wealth, it is from bad manners, for he may keep the good for himself, his servant, or his family, thus having preferred over Allah the Exalted others. If he did this with a guest and presented to him the worst food in his house, it would fill his chest with resentment—this if his view is towards Allah the Exalted. And if his view is towards himself and his reward in the Hereafter, then he is not rational who prefers others over himself, and he has nothing from his wealth except what he gave in charity and thus preserved or ate and thus consumed. And what he eats is satisfaction of desire in the present, so it is not from rationality to limit the view to the immediate and abandon saving. And Allah the Exalted has said: 'O you who have believed, spend from the good things which you have earned and from that which We have produced for you from the earth. And do not aim at the bad therefrom, spending [from that] while you would not take it [yourselves] except with closed eyes (Tughmidu) in it.' That is, do not take it except with dislike and shame (Haya'), which is the meaning of closing the eyes (Al-Ighmadh), so do not prefer with it your Lord. And in the report: 'A dirham preceded a hundred thousand dirhams.' That is by a person giving it out while it is from the most lawful of his wealth and its best, issuing from contentment and joy in giving. And he may give a hundred thousand dirhams from what he dislikes of his wealth, indicating that he does not prefer Allah the Exalted with anything he loves. And with that, Allah the Exalted censured a people who assigned to Allah what they dislike, so He said: 'And they assign to Allah that which they dislike, and their tongues assert the lie that they will have the best. No!' Some reciters paused at the negation to refute them, then began and said: 'Indeed, for them is the Fire.' That is, earning for them—their assigning to Allah what they dislike—the Fire.
2:267.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

2:267.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
2:267.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'Whatever is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)".'
2:267.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

2:268.arabic: فلا يكون خوف الاستقبال وقد آتاك الله قوت يومك لك ولعيالك إلا من ضعف اليقين والإصغاء إلى تخويف الشيطان، وقد قال تعالى: " فلا تخافوهم وخافونِ إن كنتم مؤمنين "، وقال عز وجل: " الشيطان يعدكم الفقر ويأمركم بالفحشاء والله يعدكم مغفرة منه وفضلاً " والسؤال من الفحشاء التي أبيحت بالضرورة، وحال من يسأل لحاجة متراخية عن يومه وإن كان مما يحتاج إليه في السنة أشد من حال من ملك مالاً موروثاً وادخره لحاجة وراء السنة، وكلاهما مباحان في الفتوى الظاهرة ولكنهما صادران عن حب الدنيا وطول الأمل وعدم الثقة بفضل الله، و
2:268.english: So the fear of the future, when Allah has given you the sustenance of your day for you and your dependents, is only from weakness of certainty (Yaqin) and listening to the frightening of Satan (Shaytan). And He, the Exalted, has said: "So do not fear them and fear Me if you are believers." And He, the Mighty and Majestic, has said: "Satan promises you poverty and commands you to indecency (Fahsha'), and Allah promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty." And asking (Sual) is from the indecency (Fahsha') that is permitted by necessity, and the state of one who asks for a need deferred beyond his day, even if it is from what is needed in the year, is more severe than the state of one who possesses inherited wealth and saves it for a need beyond the year. Both are permitted in the apparent legal opinion (Fatwa), but they stem from love of the world (Dunya) and long hope (Tul al-Amal) and lack of trust (Thiqa) in the bounty of Allah, and this characteristic is from the mothers of destroyers. We ask Allah for good success through His gentleness and generosity.
2:268.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

2:269.arabic: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: " إذا رأيتم العبد وقد أعطي صمتاً وزهداً في الدنيا فاقتربوا منه فإنه يلقى الحكمة"[77]. وقال تعالى: " ومن يؤت الحكمة فقد أوتي خيراً كثيراً " ولذلك قيل من زهد في الدنيا أربعين يوماً أجرى الله ينابيع الحكمة في قلبه وأنطق بها لسانه.
2:269.english: And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "When you see a servant who has been given silence and asceticism (Zuhd) in the worldly life (Dunya), then draw near to him, for he receives wisdom (Hikmah)." And Allah the Exalted said: "And whoever is given wisdom (Hikmah) has been given much good." Therefore, it is said: Whoever practices asceticism (Zuhd) in the worldly life (Dunya) for forty days, Allah causes springs of wisdom (Hikmah) to flow in his heart (Qalb) and makes his tongue speak with it.
2:269.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

2:271.arabic: الوظيفة الرابعة: أن يظهر حيث يعلم أن في إظهاره ترغيبا للناس في الاقتداء ويحرس سره من داعية الرياء بالطريق الذي سنذكره في معالجة الرياء في كتاب الرياء فقد قال الله عز وجل: ﴿ إن تبدوا الصدقات فنعما هي ﴾ {} وذلك حيث يقتضي الحال الإبداء إما للاقتداء وإما لأن السائل إنما سأل على ملأ من الناس فلا ينبغي أن يترك التصدق خيفة من الرياء في الإظهار بل ينبغي أن يتصدق ويحرس سره عن الرياء بقدر الإمكان وهذا لأن في الإظهار محذورا ثالثا سوى المن والرياء وهو هتك ستر الفقير فإنه ربما يتأذى بأن يرى في صورة المحتاج ف
2:271.english: The Fourth Duty: To make it apparent where he knows that in its manifestation there is encouragement for people to emulate, and to guard his secret from the incitement of showing off (Riya') through the method we will mention in treating showing off (Riya') in the Book of Showing Off (Riya'), for Allah the Exalted has said: 'If you disclose your charitable expenditures, they are good; but if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you, and He will remove from you some of your misdeeds. And Allah, of what you do, is Aware.' {} And that is where the situation necessitates the disclosure either for emulation or because the asker indeed asked in public, so it is not appropriate to abandon giving charity out of fear of showing off (Riya') in the manifestation, but rather one should give charity and guard his secret from showing off (Riya') as much as possible. And this is because in the manifestation there is a third danger besides reminding of favor (Mann) and showing off (Riya'), which is exposing the covering of the poor person, for perhaps he is harmed by being seen in the image of the needy, so whoever makes the asking apparent is the one who exposed his own covering, so one should not be cautious of this meaning in his manifestation, and it is like exposing immorality (Fisq) upon one who concealed it, for it is prohibited, and spying in it and habitual mention of it is forbidden. As for whoever exposes it, the establishment of the punishment upon him is publicizing, but he is the cause in it. And with a similar meaning, he said: 'Whoever throws off the cloak of modesty (Haya'), then there is no backbiting for him.' And Allah the Exalted has said: 'And spend from what We have provided for you secretly and publicly.' {} He encouraged to public also because of the benefit of encouragement in it, so let the servant (Abd) be precise in contemplation in weighing this benefit with the danger that is in it, for that differs with circumstances and persons. Indeed, the announcement in some circumstances for some persons may be better, and whoever knows the benefits and the dangers and does not look with the eye of desire, the most appropriate and fitting for every situation becomes clear to him.
2:271.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

2:271.arabic: الوظيفة الثالثة: الإسرار فإن ذلك أبعد عن الرياء والسمعة قال ﭬ: (أفضل الصدقة جهد المقل إلى فقير في سر[11]) وقال بعض العلماء: ثلاث من كنوز البر منها إخفاء الصدقة[12] وقد روي أيضا مسندا وقال ﭬ: (إن العبد ليعمل عملا في السر فيكتبه الله له سرا فإن أظهره نقل من السر وكتب في العلانية فإن تحدث به نقل من السر والعلانية وكتب رياء[13]) وفي الحديث المشهور (سبعة يظلهم الله يوم لا ظل إلا ظله أحدهم رجل تصدق بصدقة فلم تعلم شماله بما أعطت يمينه[14]) وفي الخبر: (صدقة السر تطفىء غضب الرب[15]) وقال تعالى: ﴿ وإن تخف
2:271.english: The third duty: Secrecy, for that is farther from ostentation (Riya) and reputation-seeking (Sum'ah). The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'The best charity (Sadaqah) is the effort of the poor person given to a poor person in secret.' And some scholars said: 'Three are from the treasures of righteousness, among them is hiding charity.' And it has also been narrated with a chain of transmission, and the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Verily, a servant performs a deed in secret, so Allah writes it for him secretly. If he reveals it, it is transferred from secrecy and written in openness. If he speaks about it, it is transferred from secrecy and openness and written as ostentation (Riya).' And in the famous hadith: 'Seven whom Allah will shade on a day when there is no shade except His shade: one of them is a man who gives charity (Sadaqah) such that his left hand does not know what his right hand has given.' And in the report: 'Charity (Sadaqah) in secret extinguishes the wrath of the Lord.' And Allah the Exalted said: 'And if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you.' And the benefit of concealment is deliverance from the afflictions of ostentation (Riya) and reputation-seeking (Sum'ah), for the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah does not accept from one who makes heard, nor from one who shows off, nor from one who reminds of his favor, and the one who speaks about his charity (Sadaqah) seeks reputation (Sum'ah), and the giver in a gathering of people aims for ostentation (Riya), and concealment and silence are the deliverance from it.'
2:271.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

2:271.arabic: اعلم أن في الأسرار للأعمال فائدة الإخلاص والنجاة من الرياء، وفي الإظهار فائدة الاقتداء وترغيب الناس في الخير ولكن فيه آفة الرياء. قال الحسن: قد علم المسلمون أن السر أحرز العملين، ولكن في الإظهار أيضاً فائدة ولذلك أثنى الله تعالى على السر والعلانية فقال "إن تبدوا الصدقات فنعما هي وإن تخفوها وتؤتوها الفقراء فهو خير لكم". والإظهار قسمان "أحدهما" في نفس العمل "والآخر" التحدث بما عمل. القسم الأول: إظهار نفس العمل كالصدقة في الملأ لترغيب الناس فيها كما روي عن الأنصاري الذي جاء بالصرة فتتابع الناس بالع
2:271.english: Know that in secrecy for deeds there is the benefit of sincerity (Ikhlas) and salvation from ostentation (Riya), and in public display there is the benefit of emulation and encouraging people toward good, but in it there is the affliction of ostentation. Al-Hasan said: The Muslims have known that secrecy is more secure for the two deeds, but in public display there is also benefit, and therefore Allah the Exalted praised both secrecy and openness, saying: "If you manifest the charities, then how excellent they are; and if you conceal them and give them to the poor, then it is better for you." And public display is of two types: "one" is in the deed itself, "and the other" is speaking about what was done. The first type: manifesting the deed itself, like charity in public to encourage people in it, as narrated regarding the Ansari who came with a purse, so people followed in giving when they saw him, and the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever establishes a good practice and acts upon it will have its reward and the reward of those who follow him," and all other deeds follow this course, such as prayer (Salah), fasting (Siyam), pilgrimage (Hajj), fighting (Ghazw), and others, but emulation in charity is more prevalent in dispositions.
2:271.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

2:273.arabic: وأما أدب ظاهره: فأن يظهر التعفف والتجمل ولا يظهر الشكوى والفقر، بل يستر فقره ويستر أنه يستره ففي الحديث " إن الله تعالى يحب الفقير المتعفف أبا العيال ". وقال تعالى: " يحسبهم الجاهل أغنياء من التعفف ". وقال سفيان: أفضل الأعمال التجمل عند المحنة. وقال بعضهم: ستر الفقر من كنوز البر.
2:273.english: And as for the etiquette of his outward appearance: that he shows self-restraint (التعفف) and adornment and does not show complaint and poverty, rather he conceals his poverty and conceals that he conceals it, as in the hadith: 'Indeed Allah the Exalted loves the poor person who practices self-restraint (المتعفف), the father of dependents.' And Allah the Exalted said: 'The ignorant one deems them wealthy due to their self-restraint (التعفف).' And Sufyan said: 'The best of deeds is adornment during calamity.' And some of them said: 'Concealing poverty is from the treasures of righteousness.'
2:273.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

2:273.arabic:
بيان فضيلة الفقر مطلقاً

أما من الآيات فيدل عليه قوله تعالى " للفقراء المهاجرين الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم وأموالهم " الآية. وقال تعالى: " للفقراء الذين أحصروا في سبيل الله لا يستطيعون ضرباً في الأرض " ساق الكلام في معرض المدح، ثم قدم وصفه بالفقر على وصفهم بالهجرة والإحصار وفيه دلالة ظاهرة على مدح الفقير.
2:273.english:
Explanation of the virtue of poverty absolutely.

As for from the verses, it indicates it by His saying, the Exalted: 'For the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their wealth' the verse. And He said, the Exalted: 'For the poor who are restricted in the path of Allah, unable to move about in the land' He directed the speech in the context of praise, then He presented their description with poverty before their description with emigration and restriction, and in it is an apparent indication of praising the poor person.
2:273.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

2:275.arabic: وقال تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وذروا ما بقي من الربا إن كنتم مؤمنين ثم قال فإن لم تفعلوا فأذنوا بحرب من الله ورسوله ثم قال وإن تبتم فلكم رءوس أموالكم ثم قال ومن عاد فأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون جعل آكل الربا أول الأمر مؤذنا بمحاربة الله وفي آخره متعرضا للنار والآيات الواردة في الحلال والحرام لا تحصى
2:275.english: And Allah the Exalted said: 'O you who have believed, fear Allah and give up what remains [due] of usury (Riba), if you should be believers.' Then He said: 'And if you do not, then be informed of a war [against you] from Allah and His Messenger.' Then He said: 'And if you repent, then for you are your principal sums.' Then He said: 'And whoever returns [to usury] - then those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.' He made the eater of usury (Riba) at the beginning of the matter announcing war from Allah and at its end exposed to the Fire. And the verses that have come regarding the lawful (Halal) and the unlawful (Haram) are innumerable.
2:275.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

2:277.arabic: يفزع الناس وهم لا يفزعون ويخاف الناس وهم لا يخافون وهم أولياء الله الذين لا خوف عليهم ولاهم يحزنون فقيل من هؤلاء يا رسول الله فقال هم المتحابون في الله تعالى حديث قال أبو إدريس الخولاني لمعاذ أني احبك في الله فقال أبشر ثم أبشر فإني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول تنصب لطائفة من الناس كراسي حول العرش يوم القيامة الحديث أخرجه أحمد و الحاكم في حديث طويل أن أبا إدريس قال قلت و الله إني لأحبك في الله قال فأني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول أن المتحابين بجلال الله في ظل عرشه يوم لا ظل إ
2:277.english: The people will be terrified while they are not terrified, and the people will fear while they do not fear, and they are the allies of Allah (Awliya' Allah) upon whom there is no fear nor do they grieve. It was said: Who are these, O Messenger of Allah? He said: They are those who love each other for the sake of Allah the Exalted. Hadith: Abu Idris al-Khawlani said to Mu'adh: I love you for the sake of Allah. He said: Rejoice, then rejoice, for I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, say: Chairs will be set up for a group of people around the Throne on the Day of Resurrection. The hadith was reported by Ahmad and al-Hakim in a long hadith that Abu Idris said: I said: By Allah, I love you for the sake of Allah. He said: For I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, say: Those who love each other for the majesty of Allah will be in the shade of His Throne on a day when there is no shade except His shade. Al-Hakim said: It is authentic according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, and it is in al-Tirmidhi from the narration of Abu Muslim al-Khawlani from Mu'adh with the wording: Those who love each other for My majesty, for them are pulpits of light, the prophets and the martyrs will envy them. He said: It is a hasan sahih hadith. And in Ahmad from the hadith of Abu Malik al-Ash'ari: Verily, Allah has servants who are neither prophets nor martyrs, the prophets and martyrs will envy them for their stations and their nearness to Allah. The hadith includes: They love each other for the sake of Allah and are sincere with it, Allah will place for them on the Day of Resurrection pulpits of light, making their faces light and their garments light. The people will be terrified on the Day of Resurrection while they are not terrified, and they are the allies of Allah (Awliya' Allah) upon whom there is no fear nor do they grieve. And in it is Shahr ibn Hawshab, who is disputed, and it was narrated by Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, and he said in it: Around the Throne are pulpits of light upon which are people whose garments are light and whose faces are light, they are neither prophets nor martyrs, the prophets and martyrs will envy them. So they said: O Messenger of Allah, describe them for us. He said: They are those who love each other for the sake of Allah, and those who sit together for the sake of Allah, and those who visit each other for the sake of Allah. Hadith of Abu Hurayra: Verily, around the Throne are pulpits of light upon which are people whose garments are light and whose faces are light, they are neither prophets nor martyrs. The hadith was reported by al-Nasa'i in his Sunan al-Kubra and its narrators are trustworthy. And he, peace be upon him, said: No two people love each other for the sake of Allah except that the more beloved of them to Allah is the one with the stronger love for his companion. Hadith: No two people love each other for the sake of Allah except that the more beloved of them to Allah is the one with the stronger love for his companion. Reported by Ibn Hibban and al-Hakim from the hadith of Anas, and he said: Its chain is authentic. And it is said: The two brothers in Allah, if one of them is of a higher station than the other, the other is raised with him to his station, and he joins him just as offspring join their parents and family members join each other, because brotherhood, when acquired for the sake of Allah, is not less than the brotherhood of birth. He, the Exalted, said: We joined them with their offspring, and We did not diminish anything from their deeds. And he, peace be upon him, said: Verily, Allah the Exalted says: My love is due to those who visit each other for My sake and
2:277.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

2:278.arabic: وقال تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وذروا ما بقي من الربا إن كنتم مؤمنين ثم قال فإن لم تفعلوا فأذنوا بحرب من الله ورسوله ثم قال وإن تبتم فلكم رءوس أموالكم ثم قال ومن عاد فأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون جعل آكل الربا أول الأمر مؤذنا بمحاربة الله وفي آخره متعرضا للنار والآيات الواردة في الحلال والحرام لا تحصى
2:278.english: And Allah the Exalted said: 'O you who have believed, fear Allah (Taqwa) and give up what remains [due to you] of usury (Riba), if you should be believers.' Then He said: 'And if you do not, then be informed of a war [against you] from Allah and His Messenger.' Then He said: 'But if you repent, you may have your principal.' Then He said: 'And whoever returns [to usury] - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.' He made the eater of usury (Riba) at the beginning of the matter announcing war from Allah, and at its end exposed to the Fire. And the verses concerning the lawful (Halal) and the unlawful (Haram) are innumerable.
2:278.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

2:278.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
2:278.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'Whatever is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)".'
2:278.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

2:279.arabic: وقال تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وذروا ما بقي من الربا إن كنتم مؤمنين ثم قال فإن لم تفعلوا فأذنوا بحرب من الله ورسوله ثم قال وإن تبتم فلكم رءوس أموالكم ثم قال ومن عاد فأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون جعل آكل الربا أول الأمر مؤذنا بمحاربة الله وفي آخره متعرضا للنار والآيات الواردة في الحلال والحرام لا تحصى
2:279.english: And He (Allah), the Exalted, said: 'O you who have believed, fear Allah (Taqwa) and give up what remains [due to you] of usury (Riba), if you should be believers.' Then He said: 'Then if you do not, then be informed of a war [against you] from Allah and His Messenger.' Then He said: 'But if you repent, you may have your principal [amounts].' Then He said: 'And whoever returns [to usury] - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide eternally therein.' He made the eater of usury (Riba) at the beginning of the matter announcing war from Allah and at its end exposed to the Fire. And the verses that have come regarding the lawful (Halal) and the unlawful (Haram) are innumerable.
2:279.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

2:281.arabic: فما الذي غركم بالله بعد أن سمعتم وعقلتم؟ "قالوا لو كنا نسمع أو نعقل ما كنا في أصحاب السعير فاعترفوا بذنبهم فسحقاً لأصحاب السعير". فإن قلت: فأين مظنة الرجاء وموضعه المحمود؟ فاعلم أنه محمود في موضعين: أحدهما: في حق العاصي المنهمك إذا خطرت له التوبة فقال له الشيطان: وأنى تقبل توبتك فيقنطه من رحمة الله تعالى "فيجب عند هذا أن يقمع القنوط بالرجاء ويتذكر "إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعاً" وأن الله كريم يقبل التوبة عن عباده وأن التوبة طاعة تكفر الذنوب قال الله تعالى "قل يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقن
2:281.english: So what deluded you about Allah after you heard and understood? "They said: If we had listened or understood, we would not have been among the companions of the Blazing Fire. So they confessed their sin, and away with the companions of the Blazing Fire." If you say: Then where is the place of hope and its praiseworthy position? Know that it is praiseworthy in two situations: The first: Regarding the immersed sinner when repentance occurs to him, and Satan says to him: How will your repentance be accepted? So he despairs of the mercy of Allah the Exalted. "At this point, he must suppress despair with hope and remember 'Indeed, Allah forgives all sins' and that Allah is generous in accepting repentance from His servants, and that repentance is an obedience that expiates sins. Allah the Exalted said: 'Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful. And turn to your Lord' - He commanded them to turn back. And He said: 'And indeed, I am Forgiving to whoever repents and believes and does righteous deeds and then remains guided.' So if he expects forgiveness with repentance, he is hopeful; but if he expects forgiveness with persistence in sin, he is deluded. Just as one for whom the time of Friday prayer becomes tight while he is in the market, and it occurs to him to hasten to the Friday prayer, and Satan says to him: You will not catch the Friday prayer, so stay in your place. So he rejects Satan and goes running while hoping to catch the Friday prayer - he is hopeful; but if he continues with trade and takes to hoping to catch the Friday prayer while staying put, he is deluded. The second: Regarding the righteous worker if he fears that his deed will not be accepted from him or that he will be sealed with evil. He must suppress fear with hope and remember His saying the Exalted: 'And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah. Then every Soul (Nafs) will be compensated for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.' For He the Exalted promised that no one will be wronged. So whoever does righteous deeds should not fear being wronged, but rather hope to be given his reward in full.
2:281.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

2:281.arabic: وقال تعالى يوم يبعثهم الله جميعا فينبئهم بما عملوا أحصاه الله ونسوه والله على كل شىء شهيد وقال تعالى يومئذ يصدر الناس أشتاتا ليروا أعمالهم فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره ومن يعمل مثقال ذرة شرا يره وقال تعالى ثم توفى كل نفس ما كسبت وهم لا يظلمون وقال تعالى يوم تجد كل نفس ما عملت من خير محضرا وما عملت من سوء تود لو أن بينها وبينه أمدا بعيدا ويحذركم الله نفسه وقال تعالى واعلموا أن الله يعلم ما في أنفسكم فاحذروه فعرف أرباب البصائر من جملة العباد أن الله تعالى لهم بالمرصاد وأنهم سيناقشون في الحساب ويطال
2:281.english: And He, the Exalted, said: 'On the day when Allah will resurrect them all together, then He will inform them of what they did. Allah has kept account of it, while they forgot it; and Allah is Witness over all things.' And He, the Exalted, said: 'On that day, the people will proceed in separate groups to be shown their deeds. So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.' And He, the Exalted, said: 'Then every Soul (Nafs) will be fully compensated for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.' And He, the Exalted, said: 'On the day when every Soul (Nafs) will find what it did of good presented, and what it did of evil, it will wish that between it and that [evil] was a great distance. And Allah warns you of Himself.' And He, the Exalted, said: 'And know that Allah knows what is in your Souls (Anfus), so beware of Him.' Then the possessors of insight (Arbab al-Basa'ir) from among the servants recognized that Allah, the Exalted, is lying in wait for them, and that they will be scrutinized in the account and demanded with the weight of an atom from the passing thoughts (Khatarat) and glances (Lahazat). And they realized that nothing will save them from these dangers except adhering to self-accounting (Muhasabah) and sincerity in self-observation (Muraqabah), and demanding from the Soul (Nafs) in breaths (Anfas) and movements (Harakat), and accounting it for passing thoughts (Khatarat) and glances (Lahazat).
2:281.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

2:282.arabic: لنفس والصبر والحلم والاحتمال والعفو والثبات والنبل والشهامة والوقار وغيرها فالقلب في حكم مرآة قد اكتنفته هذه الأمور المؤثرة فيه وهذه الآثار على التواصل واصلة إلى القلب أما الآثار المحمودة التي ذكرناها فإنها تزيد مرآة القلب جلاء وإشراقا ونورا وضياء حتى يتلألأ فيه جلية الحق وينكشف فيه حقيقة الأمر المطلوب في الدين وإلى مثل هذا القلب الإشارة بقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أراد الله بعبد خيرا جعل له واعظا من قلبه[11] وبقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم من كان له من قلبه واعظ كان عليه من الله حافظ[12] وهذا القلب
2:282.english: For the Soul (Nafs) and patience (Sabr) and forbearance (Hilm) and endurance (Ihtimal) and forgiveness (Afw) and steadfastness (Thabat) and nobility (Nabl) and courage (Shahama) and dignity (Waqar) and others, so the Heart (Qalb) is in the ruling of a mirror that has been encompassed by these influencing matters and these effects are continuously reaching the Heart. As for the praiseworthy effects that we mentioned, they increase the mirror of the Heart in clarity and radiance and light and illumination until the clarity of Truth (Haqq) sparkles in it and the reality of the matter required in religion is revealed in it. And to such a Heart is the reference in His saying, peace be upon him: 'When Allah wills good for a servant, He gives him an admonisher from his heart' [11] and in His saying, peace be upon him: 'Whoever has an admonisher from his heart, has a protector from Allah' [12]. And this Heart is the one in which the Remembrance (Dhikr) settles. Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, by the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah, hearts find tranquility.' And as for the blameworthy effects, they are like dark smoke ascending to the mirror of the Heart and it continues to accumulate upon it time after time until it blackens and darkens and becomes completely veiled from Allah the Exalted, and it is the sealing (Taba') and it is the covering (Rayn). Allah the Exalted said: 'No! Rather, what they have earned has covered their hearts' and He the Mighty and Majestic said: 'If We willed, We could strike them for their sins and seal (Taba') their hearts, so they would not hear.' So He linked the lack of hearing to the sealing (Taba') by sins, just as He linked hearing to piety (Taqwa), so He said: 'And fear Allah and listen, and fear Allah and He will teach you.' And whenever sins accumulate, the hearts are sealed (Taba'), and at that point, the Heart becomes blind from perceiving Truth (Haqq) and the rectitude of religion, and it belittles the matter of the Hereafter and magnifies the matter of the world, and its concern becomes restricted to it. So if its hearing is struck by the matter of the Hereafter and what is in it of dangers, it enters from one ear and exits from the other and does not settle in the Heart and does not move it to repentance and rectification. Those have despaired of the Hereafter as the disbelievers despair of the companions of the graves. And this is the meaning of the blackening of the Heart by sins as spoken by the Quran and the Sunnah. Maymun bin Mahran said: 'When a servant commits a sin, a black spot is marked in his heart. If he desists and repents, it is polished, but if he returns, it is increased in it until it covers his heart, and that is the covering (Rayn).' And the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: 'The heart of the believer is bare, in it is a lamp that shines, and the heart of the disbeliever is black, inverted' [13]. So obedience to Allah, glory be to Him, by opposing desires is a polisher for the Heart, and His disobediences are blackeners for it. So whoever inclines to disobediences, his heart blackens, and whoever follows a bad deed with a good one and erases its effect, his heart does not darken, but its light decreases like a mirror in which one breathes then it is wiped, and breathes then it is wiped, for it is not free from cloudiness. And he, peace be upon him, said: 'Hearts are four: a heart that is bare, in it is a lamp that shines, so that is the heart of the believer; and a heart that is black, inverted, so that is the heart of the disbeliever; and a heart that is covered, tied on its covering, so...'
2:282.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

2:282.arabic: وقال ﭬ للذي أوصاه: (وإذا صليت فصل صلاة مودع[39]) أي مودع لنفسه مودع لهواه مودع لعمره سائر إلى مولاه كما قال عز وجل: ﴿ أيها الإنسان إنك كادح إلى ربك كدحا فملاقيه ﴾ {الانشقاق: 6} وقال تعالى: ﴿ واتقوا الله ويعلمكم الله ﴾ {البقرة: 282} وقال تعالى: ﴿ واتقوا الله واعلموا أنكم ملاقوه ﴾ {البقرة: 223} وقال ﭬ: (من لم تنهه صلاته عن الفحشاء والمنكر لم يزدد من الله إلا بعدا[40]) والصلاة مناجاة فكيف تكون مع الغفلة.
2:282.english: And he (peace be upon him) said to the one he advised: (When you pray, pray the prayer of one departing[39]) meaning departing from his self (Nafs), departing from his desire (Hawa), departing from his lifespan, journeying to his Master (Mawla) as the Exalted said: ﴿ O human, you are laboring toward your Lord with labor, then you will meet Him ﴾ {Al-Inshiqaq: 6}. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿ And fear Allah (Taqwa) and Allah will teach you ﴾ {Al-Baqarah: 282}. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿ And fear Allah (Taqwa) and know that you will meet Him ﴾ {Al-Baqarah: 223}. And he (peace be upon him) said: (Whoever's prayer does not prevent him from immorality and evil, he only increases in distance from Allah[40]). And prayer (Salah) is intimate conversation (Munajah), so how can it be with heedlessness (Ghaflah).
2:282.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

2:282.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
2:282.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Whatever is in the Quran of 'O you who have believed' is in the Torah 'O you poor ones'.
2:282.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

2:282.english: And Allah the Exalted said: 'And fear Allah and Allah will teach you' (Al-Baqarah: 282)
2:282.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Book of Knowledge'

2:283.arabic: فأما ما يدل على المؤاخذة فقوله سبحانه إن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله فيغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء وقوله تعالى ولا تقف ما ليس لك به علم إن السمع والبصر والفؤاد كل أولئك كان عنه مسئولا فدل على أن عمل الفؤاد كعمل السمع والبصر فلا يعفي عنه وقوله تعالى ولا تكتموا الشهادة ومن يكتمها فإنه آثم قلبه
2:283.english: As for what indicates accountability, it is His saying, the Exalted: 'If you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it, then He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills.' And His saying, the Exalted: 'And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge; indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart (Fū'ād) - all of those will be questioned.' This indicates that the action of the heart (Fū'ād) is like the action of hearing and sight, so it is not pardoned. And His saying, the Exalted: 'And do not conceal testimony; and whoever conceals it, then indeed he is sinful in his heart (Qalb).'
2:283.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

2:283.arabic: وإن فريقا منهم ليكتمون الحق وهم يعلمون ( سورة البقرة: الآية 146) وهو تحريم للكتمان كما قال تعالى في الشهادة: ﴿ومن يكتمها فإنه آثم قلبه﴾ ( سورة البقرة: الآية 283)
2:283.english: And indeed a group among them conceal the truth while they know (Surah Al-Baqarah: Verse 146) and it is a prohibition of concealment as Allah the Exalted said regarding testimony: 'And whoever conceals it, then indeed he is sinful in his heart (Qalb)' (Surah Al-Baqarah: Verse 283)
2:283.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'
