2:284.arabic: فأما الخواطر وحديث النفس وهيجان الرغبة فكل ذلك لا يدخل تحت اختيار فالمؤاخذة به تكليف ما لا يطاق ولذلك لما نزل قوله تعالى وإن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله جاء ناس من الصحابة إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وقالوا كلفنا ما لا نطيق إن أحدنا ليحدث نفسه بما لا يحب أن يثبت في قلبه ثم يحاسب بذلك فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لعلكم تقولون كما قالت اليهود سمعنا وعصينا قولوا سمعنا وأطعنا فقالوا سمعنا وأطعنا فأنزل الله الفرج بعد سنة بقوله لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها فظهر به أن كل ما لا يدخل تحت ا
2:284.english: As for passing thoughts (Khawatir) and the inner speech (Hadith al-Nafs) and the agitation of desire, all of that does not enter under choice, so holding accountable for it is imposing what cannot be borne. Therefore, when His saying, the Exalted, descended: 'And if you disclose what is in your souls (Anfusikum) or conceal it, Allah will hold you accountable for it,' some people from the Companions came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: 'We have been imposed with what we cannot bear; indeed, one of us speaks to his soul (Nafs) with what he does not like to settle in his heart (Qalb), then he is held accountable for that.' He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'Perhaps you say as the Jews said: We hear and disobey; say: We hear and obey.' So they said: 'We hear and obey.' Then Allah sent down the relief after a year with His saying: 'Allah does not burden a soul (Nafs) except with what it can bear.' Thus, it became clear that everything from the actions of the heart (Qalb) that does not enter under capacity is what one is not held accountable for. This is the unveiling of the cover from this confusion.
2:284.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

2:284.arabic:
إلا  أنه  يشاهد
بالعين مشاهدة محققة وينفرد بمشاهدته المكاشف دون من حوله كالنائم.
 بيان ما يؤاخذ به العبد من وساوس القلوب وهمها وخواطرها وقصودها وما يعفى عنه
                                ولا يؤاخذ به
اعلم أن هذا أمر غامض وقد وردت فيه  آيات  وأخبار  متعارضة  يلتبس  طريق  الجمع
بينها إلا على سماسرة العلماء بالشرع فقد روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم  أنه
قال عفى عن أمتي ما حدثت به نفوسها ما لم تتكلم به أو  تعمل  به[77]  وقال  أبو
هريرة قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله  تعالى  يقول  للحف
2:284.english: [83] Hadith: When the saying of Allah the Exalted was revealed: 'And if you disclose what is in your souls (Anfus) or conceal it, Allah will account you for it,' some people from the Companions came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: 'We have been tasked with what we cannot bear.' The hadith was reported by Muslim from the narration of Abu Hurairah and Ibn Abbas similarly.
2:284.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

2:284.arabic: اعلم أن هذا أمر غامض وقد وردت فيه آيات وأخبار متعارضة يلتبس طريق الجمع بينها إلا على سماسرة العلماء بالشرع فقد روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال عفى عن أمتي ما حدثت به نفوسها ما لم تتكلم به أو تعمل به[77] وقال أبو هريرة قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله تعالى يقول للحفظة إذا هم عبدي بسيئة فلا تكتبوها فإن عملها فاكتبوها سيئة وإذا هم بحسنة لم يعملها فاكتبوها حسنة فإن عملها فاكتبوها عشرا[78] وقد خرجه البخاري ومسلم في الصحيحين وهو دليل على العفو عن عمل القلب وهمه بالسيئة وفي لفظ آخر من
2:284.english: Know that this is an obscure matter, and there have come in it verses and reports that are contradictory, and the way to reconcile between them is unclear except to the brokers of the scholars of the Sharia. It has been narrated from the Prophet (peace be upon him) that he said: 'My community is forgiven for what their souls (Nafs) speak to them, as long as they do not speak it or act upon it.'[77] And Abu Hurairah said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah the Exalted says to the recording angels: If My servant intends a bad deed, do not write it down; if he acts upon it, write it down as one bad deed. And if he intends a good deed but does not act upon it, write it down as one good deed; if he acts upon it, write it down as ten.'[78] And it has been extracted by Al-Bukhari and Muslim in the two Sahihs, and it is evidence for forgiveness for the action of the heart (Qalb) and its intention for bad deeds. And in another wording: 'Whoever intends a good deed but does not act upon it, it is written for him as one good deed; and whoever intends a good deed and acts upon it, it is written for him up to seven hundredfold. And whoever intends a bad deed but does not act upon it, it is not written against him; and if he acts upon it, it is written.' And in another wording: 'And if he speaks of doing a bad deed, I forgive it for him as long as he does not act upon it.' And all of that indicates forgiveness. As for what indicates accountability, it is His saying, the Exalted: 'If you disclose what is in your souls (Nafs) or conceal it, Allah will hold you accountable for it, then He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills.' And His saying, the Exalted: 'And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart (Fu'ad) - all of those will be questioned.' So it indicates that the action of the heart (Fu'ad) is like the action of hearing and sight, so it is not forgiven. And His saying, the Exalted: 'And do not conceal testimony, and whoever conceals it, then indeed his heart (Qalb) is sinful.' And His saying, the Exalted: 'Allah does not hold you accountable for the inadvertent in your oaths, but He holds you accountable for what your hearts (Qalb) have earned.' And the truth in our view on this matter cannot be determined unless there is comprehension of the details of the actions of the hearts (Qalb) from the beginning of their appearance until the action appears on the limbs. So we say: The first thing that comes to the heart (Qalb) is the thought (Khater), as if it occurs to him, for example, the image of a woman and that she is behind his back on the road, if he turned to her he would see her. The second is the agitation of desire to look, which is the movement of appetite in the nature (Tab'), and this is generated from the first thought, and we call it the inclination of the nature (Tab'), and the first is called the speech of the soul (Nafs). The third is the judgment of the heart (Qalb) that this should be done, meaning it should be looked at, for if the nature (Tab') inclines, the determination (Himmah) and intention (Niyyah) do not arise unless the deterrents are removed, for it may prevent him due to shame or fear from turning, and the absence of these deterrents may be due to contemplation, and it is in any case a judgment from the side of the intellect (Aql), and this is called belief (I'tiqad), and it follows the thought and inclination. The fourth is the firm resolve (Azm) to turn and the decisiveness of intention (Niyyah) in it, and this we call...
2:284.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

2:285.arabic: وروى أن الحسن ناظر قدريا فرجع عن القدر وناظر علي بن أبي طالب كرم الله وجهه رجلا من القدرية وناظر عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه يزيد بن عميرة في الإيمان قال عبد الله لو قلت إني مؤمن لقلت إني في الجنة فقال له يزيد بن عميرة يا صاحب رسول الله هذه زلة منك وهل الإيمان إلا أن تؤمن بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله والبعث والميزان وتقيم الصلاة والصوم والزكاة ولنا ذنوب لو نعلم أنها تغفر لنا لعلمنا أننا من أهل الجنة فمن أجل ذلك نقول إنا مؤمنون ولا نقول إنا من أهل الجنة فقال ابن مسعود صدقت والله إنها مني زلة
2:285.english: And it was narrated that Al-Hasan debated a Qadari (follower of free will doctrine) and he returned from Qadr (Divine Decree/Predestination), and Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah honor his face, debated a man from the Qadariyya, and Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, debated Yazid ibn 'Umayrah regarding Faith (Iman). Abdullah said: 'If I said I am a believer (Mu'min), I would say I am in Paradise.' So Yazid ibn 'Umayrah said to him: 'O companion of the Messenger of Allah, this is a slip from you. And is Faith (Iman) except that you believe in Allah and His Angels (Mala'ikah) and His Books (Kutub) and His Messengers (Rusul) and the Resurrection (Al-Ba'th) and the Balance (Al-Mizan), and you establish the Prayer (As-Salah) and the Fast (As-Sawm) and the Zakat (Al-Zakat)? And we have sins; if we knew they would be forgiven for us, we would know that we are from the people of Paradise. Therefore, we say we are believers (Mu'minun) and we do not say we are from the people of Paradise.' So Ibn Mas'ud said: 'You have spoken truthfully, by Allah, it is indeed a slip from me.'
2:285.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

2:285.arabic: ولما قال سفيان ذلك قيل له فماذا نقول قال قولوا آمنا بالله وما أنزل إلينا وأي فرق بين أن يقول آمنا بالله وما أنزل إلينا وبين أن يقول أنا مؤمن وقيل للحسن أمؤمن أنت فقال إن شاء الله فقيل له لم تستثني يا أبا سعيد في الإيمان فقال أخاف أن أقول نعم فيقول الله سبحانه كذبت يا حسن فتحق علي الكلمة وكان يقول ما يؤمنني أن يكون الله سبحانه قد اطلع علي في بعض ما يكره فمقتني وقال اذهب لا قبلت لك عملا فأنا أعمل في غير معمل وقال إبراهيم بن أدهم إذا قيل لك أمؤمن أنت فقل لا إله إلا الله وقال مرة قل أنا لا أشك في ال
2:285.english: And when Sufyan said that, he was asked: 'So what should we say?' He said: 'Say: "We believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us." And what difference is there between saying "We believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us" and saying "I am a believer"?' And it was said to Al-Hasan: 'Are you a believer?' He said: 'If Allah wills.' It was said to him: 'Why do you make an exception, O Abu Sa'id, in faith?' He said: 'I fear that if I say yes, Allah the Exalted would say: "You have lied, O Hasan," and the word would be established against me.' And he used to say: 'What assures me that Allah the Exalted has not looked upon me in some matter He dislikes and despised me and said: "Go away, I have not accepted your deeds," so I am working in vain?' And Ibrahim bin Adham said: 'If you are asked: "Are you a believer?" say: "There is no god but Allah."' And he said once: 'Say: "I do not doubt in faith, and your asking me is an innovation."' And it was said to 'Alqamah: 'Are you a believer?' He said: 'I hope, if Allah wills.' And Ath-Thawri said: 'We are believers in Allah, His angels, His books, and His messengers, and we do not know what we are with Allah the Exalted.' So what is the meaning of these exceptions? The answer is that this exception is correct and has four aspects: two aspects based on doubt, not in the origin of faith but in its conclusion or perfection, and two aspects not based on doubt. The first aspect: which does not rely on opposing doubt, is caution from certainty out of fear of what it contains of self-praise. Allah the Exalted said: 'So do not claim purity for yourselves' {} and said: 'Have you not seen those who claim purity for themselves?' {} and said: 'Look how they invent lies against Allah' {} and it was said to a wise man: 'What is ugly truth?' He said: 'A person's praise of himself, and faith is among the highest attributes of glory, and certainty is absolute self-praise, and the form of exception is like a weight for one who knows self-praise, as when it is said to a person: "Are you a doctor or jurist or exegete?" and he says: "Yes, if Allah wills," not in the context of doubt but to remove himself from praising himself, so the form is the form of hesitation and weakening of the news itself, and its meaning is the weakening necessary from the requisites of the news, which is self-praise, and with this interpretation, if asked about a blameworthy description, exception would not be proper. The second aspect: Adhering to etiquette by mentioning Allah the Exalted in every state and referring all matters to the will of Allah the Exalted, for Allah the Exalted taught His Prophet ﷺ etiquette, so He said: 'And do not say'
2:285.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Foundations of Belief'

2:285.arabic: [10] حديث الإيمان بالحساب وتفاوت الخلق فيه إلى مناقش في الحساب ومسامح فيه وإلى من يدخل الجنة بغير حساب أخرجه البيهقي في البعث من حديث عمر فقال يا رسول الله ما الإيمان قال أن تؤمن بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله وبالموت والبعث من بعد الموت والحساب والجنة والنار والقدر كله الحديث وهو عند مسلم دون ذكر الحساب
2:285.english: Hadith about faith in the accounting and the variation among creation in it, from one who will be scrutinized in the accounting and one who will be pardoned in it, and to one who will enter Paradise without accounting. Al-Bayhaqi transmitted it in Al-Ba'th from the hadith of 'Umar, who said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what is faith?' He said: 'That you believe in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers and in death and resurrection after death and the accounting and Paradise and Hell and all of destiny.' The hadith is in Muslim without mention of the accounting.
2:285.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

2:286.arabic: الأصل الخامس: أنه يجوز على الله سبحانه أن يكلف الخلق ما لا يطيقونه خلافا للمعتزلة ولو لم يجز ذلك لاستحال سؤال دفعه وقد سألوا ذلك فقالوا ربنا ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به ولأن الله تعالى أخبر نبيه ﭬ بأن أبا جهل لا يصدقه ثم أمره بأن يأمره بأن يصدقه في جميع أقواله وكان من جملة أقواله أنه لا يصدقه فكيف يصدقه في أنه لا يصدقه وهل هذا إلا محال وجوده.
2:286.english: The Fifth Principle: That it is permissible for Allah (Glory be to Him) to impose upon the creation what they cannot bear, contrary to the Mu'tazilites. And if that were not permissible, then the supplication for its repulsion would be impossible, and they have indeed supplicated that, saying: 'Our Lord (Rabbana), and do not burden us with what we have no capacity (Taqah) for.' And because Allah (Exalted is He) informed His Prophet (peace be upon him) that Abu Jahl would not believe him, then commanded him to command him to believe him in all his statements, and among his statements was that he does not believe him, so how would he believe him in that he does not believe him? And is this not an impossibility in existence?
2:286.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Foundations of Belief'

3:2.arabic: وقال ﭬ: (من قال حين يأوي إلى فراشه أستغفر الله العظيم الذي لا إله إلا هو الحي القيوم وأتوب إليه ثلاث مرات غفر الله له ذنوبه وإن كانت مثل زبد البحر أو عدد رمل عالج أو عدد ورق الشجر أو عدد أيام الدنيا[112])
3:2.english: And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever says when he goes to his bed: "I seek forgiveness from Allah the Great, the One who there is no deity except Him, the Living (Al-Hayy), the Self-Subsisting (Al-Qayyum), and I repent to Him" three times, Allah will forgive him his sins, even if they were like the foam of the sea or the number of the sand of 'Alaj or the number of leaves of trees or the number of days of the world.'
3:2.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

3:2.arabic: [112] حديث من قال حين يأوي إلى فراشه أستغفر الله العظيم الذي لا إله إلا هو الحي القيوم وأتوب إليه ثلاث مرات غفر الله له ذنوبه وإن كانت مثل زبد البحر الحديث أخرجه الترمذي من حديث أبي سعيد وقال غريب لا نعرفه إلا من حديث عبد الله بن الوليد الوصافي قلت الوصافي وإن كان ضعيفا فقد تابعه عليه عصام بن قدامة وهو ثقة ورواه البخاري في التاريخ دون قوله حين يأوي إلى فراشه وقوله ثلاث مرات.
3:2.english: Hadith: Whoever says when he goes to his bed: 'I seek forgiveness from Allah the Great, who there is no god except He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting (Al-Hayy Al-Qayyum), and I repent to Him' three times, Allah will forgive his sins even if they were like the foam of the sea. The hadith was reported by Al-Tirmidhi from the narration of Abu Sa'id and he said: 'It is strange (gharib), we do not know it except from the narration of Abdullah ibn Al-Walid Al-Wasafi.' I say: Al-Wasafi, even though he is weak, he was followed in this by 'Issam ibn Qudamah, and he is trustworthy. And Al-Bukhari reported it in Al-Tarikh without his saying 'when he goes to his bed' and his saying 'three times'.
3:2.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication

3:5.arabic: وعرفهم أنه لا يخفى عليه شيء مما يسرون وما يعلنون، وحذرهم أن يأخذهم بغتة وهم لا يشعرون فقال "ما ينظرون إلا صيحة واحدة تأخذهم وهم يخصمون فلا يستطيعون توصية ولا إلى أهلهم يرجعون" والصلاة والسلام على محمد رسوله الذي يسير تحت لوائه النبيون، وعلى آله وأصحابه الأئمة المهديين، والسادة المرضيين، صلاة يوازي عددها عدد ما كان من خلق الله وما سيكون، ويحظى ببركتها الأولون والآخرون، وسلم تسليماً كثيرا. أما بعد فإن الغضب شعلة نار اقتبست من نار الله الموقدة التي تطلع على الأفئدة، وإنها لمستكنة في طي الفؤاد. استك
3:5.english: And He made them know that nothing of what they conceal and what they reveal is hidden from Him, and He warned them that He might seize them suddenly while they are unaware, so He said: "They await not but a single blast which will seize them while they are disputing. Then they will not be able to make a bequest, nor will they return to their families." And prayers and peace be upon Muhammad, His messenger, under whose banner the prophets march, and upon his family and his companions, the guided leaders, and the pleased masters, a prayer whose number equals the number of what has been of Allah's creation and what will be, and the first and the last attain its blessing, and abundant peace. Then after, indeed anger is a flame of fire kindled from the fire of Allah that is ignited, which rises upon the hearts (Af'idah), and it is hidden in the folds of the heart (Fu'ad). The hiding of embers under ashes, and it is extracted by the concealed arrogance in the heart (Qalb) of every obstinate tyrant, like extracting fire from stone with iron, and it has been revealed to the observers with the light of certainty (Yaqin), that a vein in the human being extends to the accursed Satan, so whoever is provoked by the fire of anger has strengthened in him the kinship of Satan when he said: "You created me from fire and created him from clay." For the nature of clay is stillness and dignity, and the nature of fire is blazing and flaming, and movement and agitation, and from the outcomes of anger are malice (Haqd) and envy (Hasad), and by them perished whoever perished and corrupted whoever corrupted, and their source is a morsel; if it is rectified, the entire body is rectified with it, and if malice (Haqd) and envy (Hasad) and anger (Ghadd) are present.
3:5.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

3:5.arabic: [21]  حديث تكرار بسم الله الذي لا يضر مع اسمه شيء في الأرض ولا في السماء وهو السميع العليم أخرجه أصحاب السنن وابن حبان والحاكم وصححه من حديث عثمان من قال ذلك ثلاث مرات حين يمسي لم يصبه فجأة بلاء حتى يصبح ومن قالها حين يصبح ثلاث مرات لم يصبه فجأة بلاء حتى يمسي قال الترمذي حسن صحيح غريب.
3:5.english: Hadith of repeating: 'In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing can harm in the earth nor in the heaven, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.' It was reported by the authors of the Sunan, Ibn Hibban, and Al-Hakim, and he authenticated it from the hadith of 'Uthman: Whoever says that three times in the evening, no sudden calamity will befall him until morning, and whoever says it three times in the morning, no sudden calamity will befall him until evening. Al-Tirmidhi said: Good, authentic, rare.
3:5.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Book of Knowledge'

3:7.arabic: ولعلم اليقين أيضاً رتبة وإن كان دون عين اليقين، ومن خلا عن علم اليقين فهو خارج عن زمرة المؤمنين ويحشر يوم القيامة في زمرة الجاحدين المستكبرين الذين هم قتلى القلوب الضعيفة وأتباع الشياطين. فنسأل الله تعالى أن يجعلنا من الراسخين في العلم القائلين: " آمنا به كل من عند ربنا وما يذكر إلا أولو الألباب ".
3:7.english: And knowledge of certainty (Ilm al-Yaqin) also has a rank, even if it is below the eye of certainty (Ayn al-Yaqin). Whoever is devoid of knowledge of certainty (Ilm al-Yaqin) is outside the group of believers and will be resurrected on the Day of Judgment among the group of deniers, the arrogant ones who are the slain of the weak hearts (Qulub) and followers of devils. So we ask Allah the Exalted to make us among those firmly grounded in knowledge (Ar-Rasikhun fil-Ilm) who say: "We believe in it, all of it is from our Lord, and none will remember except those of understanding (Ulul-Albab)."
3:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

3:14.arabic: وقد ذكر الله تعالى في آية واحدة سبعة منها فقال: "زين للناس حب الشهوات من النساء والبنين والقناطير المقنطرة من الذهب والفضة والخيل المسومة والأنعام والحرث ذلك متاع الحياة والدنيا" ثم رده في آية أخرى إلى خمسة فقال عز وجل: "اعلموا أنما الحياة الدنيا لعب ولهو وزينة وتفاخر بينكم وتكاثر في الأموال والأولاد" ثم رده تعالى في موضع آخر إلى اثنين فقال تعالى: "وإنما الحياة الدنيا لعب ولهو" ثم رد الكل إلى واحد في موضع آخر فقال: "ونهى النفس عن الهوى فإن الجنة هي المأوى" فالهوى لفظ يجمع جميع حظوظ النفس في الدن
3:14.english: And Allah the Exalted mentioned in one verse seven of them, saying: "Adorned for people is the love of desires from women and children and heaped-up measures of gold and silver and branded horses and cattle and tilled land. That is the enjoyment of the life of the world." Then He reduced it in another verse to five, saying the Mighty and Majestic: "Know that the life of the world is play and amusement and adornment and boasting among you and increase in wealth and children." Then He reduced it in another place to two, saying the Exalted: "And the life of the world is nothing but play and amusement." Then He reduced all to one in another place, saying: "And restrain the Soul (Nafs) from desire (Hawa), for indeed Paradise is the abode." So desire (Hawa) is a term that gathers all the shares of the Soul (Nafs) in the world, and asceticism (Zuhd) should be in it.
3:14.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

3:18.arabic: وكذلك ذكر الله تعالى في القرآن من الأدلة والآيات في الأرض والسموات، ثم قال: "أو لم يكف بربك أنه على كل شيءٍ شهيد" وقال: "شهد الله أنه لا إله إلا هو" فبين أنه الدليل على نفسه وذلك ليس متناقضاً بل طرق الاستدلال مختلفة، فكم من طالب عرف الله تعالى بالنظر إلى الموجودات، وكم من طالب عرف كل الموجودات بالله تعالى كما قال بعضهم: عرفت ربي بربي، ولولا ربي لما عرفت ربي، وهو معنى قوله تعالى: "أو لم يكف بربك أنه على كل شيء شهيد"
3:18.english: And likewise, Allah the Exalted mentioned in the Quran from the proofs and signs in the earth and the heavens, then He said: "Or is it not sufficient for your Lord that He is over all things a Witness?" and said: "Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him" so He clarified that He is the proof for Himself, and that is not contradictory but rather the paths of reasoning are different. For how many seekers have known Allah the Exalted by looking at the existent things, and how many seekers have known all existent things through Allah the Exalted, as some of them said: I knew my Lord by my Lord, and were it not for my Lord, I would not have known my Lord. And that is the meaning of His saying the Exalted: "Or is it not sufficient for your Lord that He is over all things a Witness?"
3:18.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

3:18.arabic: شواهدها من القرآن قوله عز وجل: ﴿شهد الله أنه لا إله إلا هو والملائكة وأولو العلم قائما بالقسط﴾ (آل عمران 3: 18) فانظر كيف بدأ سبحانه وتعالى بنفسه وثنى بالملائكة وثلث بأهل العلم وناهيك بهذا شرفا وفضلا وجلاء ونبلا
3:18.english: Its evidences from the Quran are His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and the angels and those of knowledge (أولو العلم) [also bear witness], maintaining justice (قائما بالقسط)' (Al-Imran 3:18). So observe how He, glorified and exalted, began with Himself, followed with the angels, and thirdly with the people of knowledge (أهل العلم). And what an honor, virtue, clarity, and nobility this is.
3:18.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

3:18.arabic: والواصلون إلى هذه الرتبة ينقسمون إلى الأقوياء ويكون أول معرفتهم بالله تعالى، ثم به يعرفون غيره. وإلى الضعفاء ويكون أول معرفتهم بالأفعال ثم يترقون منها إلى الفاعل. وإلى الأول الإشارة بقوله تعالى: " أو لم يكف بربك أنه على كل شيء شهيد " وبقوله تعالى: " شهد الله أنه لا إله إلا هو " ومنه نظر بعضهم حيث قيل له: بم عرفت ربك؟ قال: عرفت ربي ولولا ربي لما عرفت ربي، وإلى الثاني بقوله تعالى: " سنريهم آياتنا في الآفاق وفي أنفسهم حتى يتبين لهم أنه الحق " الآية. وبقوله عز وجل: " أو لم ينظروا في ملكوت السموات وا
3:18.english: And those who reach this rank are divided into the strong ones, whose first knowledge (ma'rifah) is of Allah the Exalted, then through Him they know others. And into the weak ones, whose first knowledge is of the actions, then they ascend from them to the Actor. And to the first is the allusion in His saying, the Exalted: 'Or is it not sufficient for your Lord that He is over all things a Witness?' and in His saying, the Exalted: 'Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him' and from this is the view of some of them when it was said to him: By what did you know your Lord? He said: I knew my Lord, and were it not for my Lord, I would not have known my Lord. And to the second is His saying, the Exalted: 'We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth' the verse. And in His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Have they not looked into the dominion of the heavens and the earth?' and in His saying, the Exalted: 'Say, Look at what is in the heavens and the earth' and in His saying, the Exalted: 'Who created seven heavens in layers. You see no inconsistency in the creation of the Most Merciful. So return your vision; do you see any breaks? Then return your vision twice again. Your vision will return to you humbled while it is fatigued.' And this path is the easiest for most people and the widest for the travelers, and to it is most of the call of the Quran when commanding contemplation (tadabbur), reflection (tafakkur), consideration (i'tibar), and looking at signs beyond enumeration.
3:18.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

3:18.arabic: ثم يقرأ: ﴿ شهد الله أنه لا إله إلا هو والملائكة ﴾ {} إلى آخرها ثم يقول وأنا أشهد بما شهد الله به لنفسه وشهدت به ملائكته وأولو العلم من خلقه وأستودع الله هذه الشهادة وهي لي عند الله تعالى وديعة وأسأله حفظها حتى يتوفاني عليها اللهم احطط عني بها وزرا واجعلها لي عندك ذخرا واحفظها علي وتوفني عليها حتى ألقاك بها غير مبدل تبديلا
3:18.english: Then he recites: 'Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and the angels' {} to its end. Then he says: And I bear witness to what Allah has borne witness to for Himself, and His angels have borne witness, and the possessors of knowledge from His creation. And I entrust to Allah this testimony, and it is for me with Allah the Exalted a trust, and I ask Him to preserve it until He takes me while upon it. O Allah, remove from me by it a burden, and make it for me with You a treasure, and preserve it upon me, and take me while upon it until I meet You with it, not changed with change.'
3:18.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Book of Knowledge'

3:21.arabic: وإذا قيل له اتق الله أخذته العزة بالإثم وروي عن عمر رضي الله عنه أنه قرأها فقال إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون قام رجل يأمر بالمعروف فقتل فقام آخر فقال يقتلون الذين يأمرون بالقسط من الناس فقتل المتكبر الذي خالفه والذي أمره كبراً
3:21.english: And when it is said to him, 'Fear Allah (Taqwa)', arrogance (Al-'Izzah) with sin takes hold of him. And it is narrated from 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he recited it and said, 'Indeed, to Allah we belong and to Him we will return.' A man stood up commanding the good (Al-Ma'ruf) and was killed. Then another stood up and said, 'They kill those who command with justice (Al-Qist) from among the people,' and the arrogant one who opposed him and the one who commanded him out of arrogance (Kibr) were killed.
3:21.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

3:26.arabic: اللهم إن كنت تعلم أن هذا الأمر خير لي في ديني ودنياي وعاقبة أمري وعاجله وآجله فاقدره لي وبارك لي فيه ثم يسره لي وإن كنت تعلم أن هذا الأمر شر لي في ديني ودنياي وعاقبة أمري وعاجله وآجله فاصرفني عنه واصرفه عني واقدر لي الخير أينما كان إنك على كل شيء قدير[290]
3:26.english: O Allah, if You know that this matter is good for me in my religion (Deen), my worldly life (Dunya), and the outcome of my affair, its immediate and delayed consequences, then decree it for me and bless me in it, then make it easy for me. And if You know that this matter is evil for me in my religion (Deen), my worldly life (Dunya), and the outcome of my affair, its immediate and delayed consequences, then turn me away from it and turn it away from me, and decree for me the good wherever it may be, for You are over all things capable (Qadir).
3:26.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

3:26.arabic: وكان محمد بن واسع يقول كل يوم بعد صلاة الصبح اللهم إنك سلطت علينا عدوا بصيرا بعيوبنا يرانا هو وقبيله من حيث لا نراهم اللهم فآيسه منا كما آيسته من رحمتك وقنطه منا كما قنطته من عفوك وباعد بيننا وبينه كما باعدت بينه وبين رحمتك إنك على كل شيء قدير
3:26.english: And Muhammad ibn Wasīʿ used to say every day after the morning prayer: 'O Allah, You have empowered over us an enemy who sees our faults, he and his tribe see us from where we do not see them. O Allah, make him despair of us as You have made him despair of Your mercy, and make him despondent of us as You have made him despondent of Your pardon, and distance between us and him as You have distanced between him and Your mercy. Indeed, You are over all things powerful (Qadīr).'
3:26.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

3:26.arabic: [28]  حديث فضل قل اللهم مالك الملك الآيتين أخرجه المستغفري في الدعوات من حديث علي أن فاتحة الكتاب وآية الكرسي والآيتين من آل عمران شهد الله إلى قوله الإسلام وقل اللهم مالك الملك إلى قوله بغير حساب معلقات ما بينهن وبين الله حجاب الحديث وفيه فقال الله لا يقرأ كل أحد من عبادي دبر كل صلاة إلا جعلت الجنة مثواه الحديث وفيه الحارث بن عمير وفي ترجمته ذكره ابن حبان في الضعفاء وقال موضوع لا أصل له والحارث يروي عن الأثبات الموضوعات قلت وثقه حماد بن زيد وابن معين وأبو زرعة وأبو حاتم والنسائي وروى له البخاري
3:26.english: Hadith about the virtue of 'Say: O Allah, Owner of Sovereignty' (Qul Allahumma Malika al-Mulk) the two verses. Al-Mustaghfiri transmitted it in Al-Da'awat from the hadith of Ali that the Opening of the Book (Al-Fatihah) and the Throne Verse (Ayat al-Kursi) and the two verses from Al Imran: 'Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him' (Shahida Allahu annahu la ilaha illa Huwa) to His saying 'Islam' and 'Say: O Allah, Owner of Sovereignty' (Qul Allahumma Malika al-Mulk) to His saying 'without account' (bighayri hisab) are suspended curtains between them and Allah. In it, Allah said: 'No one among My servants recites after every prayer except that I make Paradise his abode.' In it is Al-Harith bin 'Umayr, and in his biography, Ibn Hibban mentioned him in Al-Du'afa' and said: 'Fabricated, without origin, and Al-Harith transmits from reliable narrators fabricated narrations.' I said: Hamad bin Zayd, Ibn Ma'in, Abu Zur'ah, Abu Hatim, and Al-Nasa'i authenticated him, and Al-Bukhari transmitted from him in a suspended (mu'allaq) manner.
3:26.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Book of Knowledge'

3:26.arabic: من صلى ليلة الأربعاء ست ركعات قرأ في ركعة بعد الفاتحة قل اللهم مالك الملك إلى آخر الآية فإذا فرغ من صلاته يقول جزى الله محمدا عنا ما هو أهله غفر له ذنوب سبعين سنة وكتب له براءة من النار[257]
3:26.english: Whoever prays on Wednesday night six rak'ahs, reciting in one rak'ah after Al-Fatihah: 'Say: O Allah, Owner of Sovereignty (Qul Allahumma Malika al-Mulk)' to the end of the verse, then when he finishes his prayer says: 'May Allah reward Muhammad on our behalf as he deserves,' his sins of seventy years will be forgiven and a certificate of freedom from the Fire will be written for him.
3:26.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

3:26.english: Say: O Allah, Owner of Sovereignty, the two verses
3:26.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Book of Knowledge'

3:28.arabic: وأما بغض الكفار والإنكار عليهم ومقتهم فما ورد فيه من شواهد القرآن والأخبار لا يحصى مثل قوله تعالى "لا يتخذ المؤمنون الكافرين أولياء من دون المؤمنين". وقال تعالى: "يا أيها الذي آمنوا لا تتخذوا اليهود والنصارى أولياء". وقال تعالى: "وكذلك نولي بعض الظالمين بعضاً". وفي الخبر: "إن الله تعالى أخذ الميثاق على كل مؤمن أن يبغض كل منافق وعلى كل منافق أن يبغض كل مؤمن". وقال عليه السلام: "المرء مع من أحب" وقال: "من أحب قوماً ووالاهم حشر معهم يوم القيامة". وقال عليه السلام: "أوثق عرى الإيمان الحب في الله وال
3:28.english: As for hating the disbelievers (Kuffar), rejecting them, and despising them, what has come regarding this from evidences of the Quran and reports (Akhbar) is innumerable, like His saying, the Exalted: "Let not the believers take the disbelievers (Kuffar) as allies (Awliya) instead of the believers." And He, the Exalted, said: "O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies (Awliya)." And He, the Exalted, said: "And thus do We make some of the wrongdoers (Zalimun) allies (Awliya) of others." And in the report (Khabar): "Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, took the covenant (Mithaq) upon every believer (Mu'min) to hate every hypocrite (Munafiq) and upon every hypocrite (Munafiq) to hate every believer (Mu'min)." And he, peace be upon him, said: "The person is with whom he loves." And he said: "Whoever loves a people and allies with them (Walahum) will be gathered with them on the Day of Resurrection." And he, peace be upon him, said: "The firmest bond of faith (Iman) is love (Hubb) for the sake of Allah and hatred (Bughd) for the sake of Allah." The evidences for this we have already mentioned in the explanation of love (Hubb) and hatred (Bughd) for the sake of Allah, the Exalted, from the Book of the Etiquettes of Companionship (Adab al-Suhba), and in the Book of Commanding Good and Forbidding Evil (al-Amr bi al-Ma'ruf wa al-Nahy 'an al-Munkar); so we do not repeat it.
3:28.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

3:30.arabic: وقال تعالى يوم تجد كل نفس ما عملت من خير محضرا وما عملت من سوء تود لو أن بينها وبينه أمدا بعيدا ويحذركم الله نفسه وقال تعالى واعلموا أن الله يعلم ما في أنفسكم فاحذروه فعرف أرباب البصائر من جملة العباد أن الله تعالى لهم بالمرصاد وأنهم سيناقشون في الحساب ويطالبون بمثاقيل الذر من الخطرات واللحظات وتحققوا أنه لا ينجيهم من هذه الأخطار إلا لزوم المحاسبة وصدق المراقبة ومطالبة النفس في الأنفاس والحركات ومحاسبتها في الخطرات واللحظات فمن حاسب نفسه قبل أن يحاسب خف في القيامة حسابه وحضر عند السؤال جوابه وحس
3:30.english: And He (Exalted) said: 'On the Day when every Soul (Nafs) will find what it did of good present, and what it did of evil, it will wish that between it and that (evil) were a distant period. And Allah warns you of His Self (Nafs).' And He (Exalted) said: 'And know that Allah knows what is in your souls (Anfus), so beware of Him.' So the possessors of insight from among the servants recognized that Allah (Exalted) is lying in wait for them, and that they will be scrutinized in the accounting and will be demanded with the weight of an atom from the passing thoughts (Khatarat) and glances. And they realized that nothing will save them from these dangers except adhering to self-accounting (Muhasaba) and sincerity in self-observation (Muraqaba) and demanding from the Soul (Nafs) in breaths and movements, and accounting it for passing thoughts (Khatarat) and glances. For whoever accounts his Soul (Nafs) before being accounted for, his accounting on the Day of Resurrection (Qiyamah) will be lightened, and his answer will be present at the questioning, and his return and outcome will be good. And whoever does not account his Soul (Nafs), his regrets will persist, and his standings in the plains of the Day of Resurrection (Qiyamah) will be prolonged, and his evil deeds will lead him to disgrace and contempt.
3:30.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

3:30.arabic: يوم تجد كل نفس ما عملت من خير محضرا وما عملت من سوء تود لو أن بينها وبينه أمدا بعيدا، يوم تعلم فيه كل نفس ما أحضرت وتشهد ما قدمت وأخرت يوم تخرس فيه الألسن وتنطق الجوارح يوم شيب ذكره سيد المرسلين إذ قال له الصديق رضى الله عنه: أراك قد شبت يا رسول الله قال: (شيبتنى هود وأخواتها[155]) وهى الواقعة والمرسلات وعم يتساءلون وإذا الشمس كورت فيا أيها القارىء العاجز إنما حظك من قراءتك أن تمجمج القرآن وتحرك به اللسان ولو كنت متفكرا فيما تقرؤه لكنت جديرا بأن تنشق مرارتك مما شاب منه شعر سيد المرسلين وإذا قنعت
3:30.english: The Day (Yawm) when every Soul (Nafs) will find what it did of good brought forth, and what it did of evil it will wish that between it and that [evil] there were a great distance. The Day (Yawm) when every Soul (Nafs) will know what it has brought forth and will testify to what it has sent ahead and left behind. The Day (Yawm) when tongues will be silenced and limbs will speak. The Day (Yawm) whose mention turned gray the hair of the Master of the Messengers (Sayyid al-Mursalin), when the Truthful One (al-Siddiq), may Allah be pleased with him, said to him: 'I see you have turned gray, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Surah Hud and its sisters turned me gray' [155], and they are al-Waqi'ah, al-Mursalat, 'Amma yatasā'alūn, and Idhā al-shamsu kuwirat. O you incapable reader, your portion from your reading is only that you mumble the Quran and move your tongue with it. If you were reflecting on what you read, you would be worthy of having your bitterness split open from what turned gray the hair of the Master of the Messengers (Sayyid al-Mursalin). And if you are content with the movement of the tongue, you have been deprived of the fruit of the Quran. The Resurrection (al-Qiyāmah) is one of what is mentioned in it, and Allah has described some of its calamities and multiplied its names so that we may stand, through the multitude of its names, upon the multitude of its meanings. The purpose of the multitude of names is not the repetition of names and titles, but rather the goal is to alert those of understanding (Ulī al-Albāb). Under every name from the names of the Resurrection (al-Qiyāmah) there is a secret, and in every attribute from its attributes there is a meaning, so strive to know their meanings, and we are now gathering its names for you.
3:30.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

3:30.arabic: وقال بعض الصالحين بينما أنا أسير في بعض جبال بيت المقدس إذ هبطت إلى واد هناك فإذا أنا بصوت قد علا وإذا تلك الجبال تجيبه لها دوى عال فاتبعت الصوت فإذا أنا بروضة عليها شجر ملتف وإذا أنا برجل قائم فيها يردد هذه الآية يوم تجد كل نفس ما عملت من خير محضرا إلى قوله ويحذركم الله نفسه قال فجلست خلفه أسمع كلامه وهو يردد هذه الآية إذ صاح صيحة خر مغشيا عليه فقلت وا أسفاه هذا لشقائى ثم انتظرت إفاقته فأفاق بعد ساعة فسمعته وهو يقول أعوذ بك من مقام الكذابين أعوذ بك من أعمال البطالين أعوذ بك من إعراض الغافلين ثم
3:30.english: And one of the righteous said: While I was walking in some of the mountains of Jerusalem, I descended into a valley there, and behold, I heard a voice that had risen, and those mountains were responding to it with a high echo. So I followed the voice, and behold, I was in a meadow with dense trees, and behold, I saw a man standing in it repeating this verse: 'On the Day when every Soul (Nafs) will find what it did of good presented, and what it did of evil, it will wish that between it and that [evil] was a great distance. And Allah warns you of Himself, and Allah is Kind to the servants.' He said: So I sat behind him listening to his speech while he was repeating this verse, when he cried out a cry and fell unconscious. I said: Woe is me, this is for my misery. Then I waited for his recovery, and he recovered after an hour, and I heard him saying: I seek refuge in You from the station of the liars, I seek refuge in You from the deeds of the idle, I seek refuge in You from the turning away of the heedless. Then he said: To You have humbled the Hearts (Qulub) of the fearful, and to You have fled the hopes of the deficient, and to Your greatness have submitted the Hearts (Qulub) of the knowers. Then he shook his hand and said: What is mine with the world, and what is the world's, and what do I have upon you, O world, with your sons of kind and thousands of your bliss to your lovers? So go, and with them deceive. Then he said: Where are the past generations and the people of the bygone eras? In the dust they decay and upon time they perish. So I called to him: O servant of Allah, I am from today behind you waiting for your leisure. He said: And how can one be at leisure who hastens the times and they hasten him, fearing their precedence by death to his Soul (Nafs), or how can one be at leisure whose days have gone and his sins remain? Then he said: You are for it and for every hardship I expect its descent, then for it from me an hour. And he recited: 'And there will appear to them from Allah what they had not taken into account.' Then he cried out another cry more severe than the first and fell unconscious. I said: His Spirit (Ruh) has departed. So I approached him, and behold, he was convulsing, then he recovered and was saying: Who am I? What is my significance? Grant me my misdeeds from Your bounty and cover me with Your veil, and pardon my sins by the generosity of Your face, if...
3:30.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

3:30.arabic: ولكن الناقد بصير فحق على كل متدين فيه أن يراقب قلبه ويعلم أن الله مطلع على باعثه وصارفه أنه الدين أو الهوى وستجد كل نفس ما عملت من سوء أو خير محضرا عند الله ولو في فلتة خاطر أو فلتة ناظر من غير ظلم وجور فما الله بظلام للعبيد
3:30.english: But the critic is insightful, so it is right for every religious person in this matter to watch over his Heart (Qalb) and know that Allah is aware of his motivator and turner, whether it is religion or desire (Hawa). And every Soul (Nafs) will find what it has done of evil or good presented before Allah, even if in a fleeting thought or a fleeting glance without injustice and oppression, for Allah is not unjust to the servants.
3:30.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

3:31.arabic: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: " إن من خيار أمتي فيما أنبأني الملأ الأعلى قوماً يضحكون جهراً من سعة رحمه الله تعالى، ويبكون سراً من خوف عذابه، مؤنتهم على الناس خفيفة وعلى أنفسهم ثقيلة، يلبسون الخلقان ويتبعون الرهبان؛ أجسامهم في الأرض وأفئدتهم عند العرش" فهذه كانت سيرة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الملابس وقد أوصى أمته عامة بإتباعه، إذا قال: " من أحبني فليستن بسنتي". وقال: " عليكم بسنتي وسنة الخلفاء الراشدين من بعدي، عضوا عليها بالنواجذ". وقال تعالى: " قل إن كنتم تحبون الله فاتبعوني يحببكم الله ".
3:31.english: And he (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, among the best of my community, as the Highest Assembly informed me, are a people who laugh openly from the vastness of the Mercy (Rahmah) of Allah the Exalted, and cry secretly from fear of His punishment; their burden upon people is light and upon themselves heavy; they wear worn-out clothes and follow the monks; their bodies are on earth and their hearts (Af'idah) are at the Throne." This was the conduct (Sirah) of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) regarding clothing, and he advised his community generally to follow him, as he said: "Whoever loves me, let him follow my tradition (Sunnah)." And he said: "Hold fast to my tradition (Sunnah) and the tradition (Sunnah) of the rightly-guided caliphs after me, cling to it with your molars." And Allah the Exalted said: "Say: If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you."
3:31.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

3:33.arabic: وقال الربيع بن سليمان رأيت الشافعي رحمة الله عليه بعد وفاته في المنام فقلت يا أبا عبد الله ما صنع الله بك قال أجلسني على كرسي من ذهب ونثر على اللؤلؤ الرطب ورأى رجل من أصحاب الحسن البصري ليلة مات الحسن كأن مناديا ينادي: ﴿ إن الله اصطفى آدم ونوحا وآل إبراهيم وآل عمران على العالمين ﴾ واصطفى الحسن البصري على أهل زمانه
3:33.english: And Rabīʿ ibn Sulaymān said: I saw al-Shāfiʿī, mercy of God upon him, after his death in a dream, and I said: O Abū ʿAbd Allāh, what has God done with you? He said: He seated me on a throne of gold and scattered upon me moist pearls. And a man from the companions of al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī saw, on the night al-Ḥasan died, as if a caller was calling out: 'Indeed, God chose Adam and Noah and the family of Abraham and the family of ʿImrān over the worlds' and chose al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī over the people of his time.
3:33.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Book of Repentance'

3:34.arabic: وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم (لابنته فاطمة عليها السلام أي شيء خير للمرأة قالت أن لا ترى رجلا ولا يراها رجل فضمها إليه وقال ذرية بعضها من بعض) فاستحسن قولها
3:34.english: And the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said (to his daughter Fatimah, peace be upon her: 'What is best for a woman?' She said: 'That she does not see a man and no man sees her.' So he embraced her and said: 'Progeny, some of them from others.') And he approved of her statement.
3:34.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

3:37.arabic: واستثنى في خمسة اشياء في الاغناء والاجابة والرزق والمغفرة والتوبة فقال تعالى: ﴿ فسوف يغنيكم الله من فضله ان شاء ﴾ {} وقال فيكشف ما تدعون اليه ان شاء - وقال يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب وقال: ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء وقال: ويتوب الله على من يشاء وهو خلق من اخلاق الربوبية اذ قال تعالى: ﴿ والله شكور حليم ﴾ {}
3:37.english: And He made exceptions in five things: in enrichment, in answering, in provision (Rizq), in forgiveness, and in repentance. So He, the Exalted, said: 'Then Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills' and said: 'And He removes what you call to if He wills' - and said: 'He provides (Yarzuqu) whom He wills without account' and said: 'And He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills' and said: 'And Allah turns in repentance (Yatūbu) to whom He wills.' And this is a character from the characters of Lordship (Rubūbiyyah), since He, the Exalted, said: 'And Allah is Appreciative (Shakūr), Forbearing (Halīm).'
3:37.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

3:53.arabic: وإنما كره بعض العلماء قراءة بعض أول السور وقطعها وقد روى أنه ﭬ قرأ بعض سورة يونس فلما انتهى إلى ذكر موسى وفرعون قطع فركع[131] وروى أنه ﭬ قرأ في الفجر آية من البقرة[132] وهي قوله: ﴿ قولوا آمنا بالله وما أنزل إلينا ﴾ {} وفي الثانية: ﴿ ربنا آمنا بما أنزلت ﴾ {} وسمع بلالا يقرأ من ههنا وههنا فسأله عن ذلك فقال: أخلط الطيب بالطيب، فقال: أحسنت[133] ويقرأ في الظهر بطوال المفصل إلى ثلاثين آية وفي العصر بنصف ذلك وفي المغرب بأواخر المفصل وآخر صلاة صلاها رسول الله ﭬ المغرب قرأ فيها سورة المرسلات ما صلى بعدها
3:53.english: And indeed some scholars disliked reading some beginnings of chapters and cutting them off, and it has been narrated that he (peace be upon him) read part of Surah Yunus, and when he reached the mention of Musa (Moses) and Fir'aun (Pharaoh), he cut it off and bowed[131]. And it has been narrated that he (peace be upon him) read in the Fajr (Dawn) prayer a verse from Al-Baqarah[132], which is His saying: 'Say: We believe in Allah and what has been sent down to us' {}, and in the second (rak'ah): 'Our Lord, we believe in what You have sent down' {}, and he heard Bilal reading from here and there, so he asked him about that, and he said: 'I mix good with good', so he said: 'You have done well'[133]. And he reads in Dhuhr (Noon) with the long ones of the Mufassal up to thirty verses, and in 'Asr (Afternoon) with half of that, and in Maghrib (Sunset) with the last ones of the Mufassal, and the last prayer that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) prayed, Maghrib, he read in it Surah Al-Mursalat, and he did not pray after it until he was taken[134].
3:53.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

3:53.arabic: [132]  حديث قرأ في الفجر  قولوا آمنا بالله الآية وفي الثانية ربنا آمنا بما أنزلت أخرجه مسلم من حديث ابن عباس كان يقرأ في ركعتي الفجر في الأولى منها قولوا آمنا بالله وما أنزل إلينا الآية التي في البقرة وفي الآخرة منها آمنا بالله واشهد بأنا مسلمون رواه أبو داود من حديث أبي هريرة قل آمنا بالله وما أنزل علينا الآية وفي الركعة الآخرة ربنا آمنا بما أنزلت أو إنا أرسلناك بالحق.
3:53.english: Hadith: He recited in the Fajr (dawn prayer) 'Say: We believe in Allah...' the verse, and in the second (rak'ah) 'Our Lord, we believe in what You have sent down...' transmitted by Muslim from the narration of Ibn Abbas: He used to recite in the two rak'ahs of Fajr, in the first of them 'Say: We believe in Allah and what has been sent down to us...' the verse which is in Al-Baqarah, and in the last of them 'We believe in Allah and bear witness that we are Muslims.' Transmitted by Abu Dawud from the narration of Abu Hurairah: 'Say: We believe in Allah and what has been sent down to us...' the verse, and in the last rak'ah 'Our Lord, we believe in what You have sent down...' or 'Indeed, We have sent you with the truth.'
3:53.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

3:54.arabic: فإن منشأ هذا الغرور والجهل بالله وبصفاته، فإن من عرفه لا يأمن مكره ولا يغتر بأمثال هذه الخيالات الفاسدة، وينظر إلى فرعون وهامان وقارون وإلى ملوك الأرض وما جرى لهم كيف أحسن الله إليهم ابتداء ثم دمرهم تدميرا! فقال تعالى "هل تحس منهم من أحد" الآية. وقد حذر الله تعالى من مكره واستدراجه فقال "فلا يأمن مكر الله إلا القوم الخاسرون" وقال تعالى "ومكروا مكراً ومكرنا مكراً وهم لا يشعرون" وقال عز وجل "ومكروا ومكر الله والله خير الماكرين" وقال تعالى "إنهم يكيدون كيداً وأكيد كيداً فمهل الكافرين أمهلهم رويداً"
3:54.english: For the origin of this delusion (Ghurur) is ignorance of Allah and His attributes, for whoever knows Him does not feel secure from His plotting (Makr) nor is deceived by such false imaginings, and looks to Pharaoh, Haman, and Korah and to the kings of the earth and what befell them—how Allah initially bestowed favors upon them then utterly destroyed them! So Allah the Exalted said: "Do you perceive any of them?" [Quran 69:8]. And Allah the Exalted has warned against His plotting (Makr) and gradual leading astray (Istidraj), saying: "So none feels secure from the plotting (Makr) of Allah except the losing people" [Quran 7:99], and He said: "And they plotted a plot, and We plotted a plot, while they perceive not" [Quran 27:50], and He the Mighty and Majestic said: "And they plotted and Allah plotted, and Allah is the best of plotters (Al-Makirin)" [Quran 3:54], and He said: "Indeed, they are planning a plan, and I am planning a plan. So allow time for the disbelievers. Leave them awhile" [Quran 86:15-17]. Just as it is not permissible for the negligent servant to infer from the master's neglect of him and enabling him with blessings that the master loves him, rather he should beware that this might be plotting (Makr) and scheming from him, even though the master did not warn him of his own plotting (Makr), then how much more must this be in the case of Allah the Exalted, with His warning of gradual leading astray (Istidraj), is more appropriate. Therefore, whoever feels secure from the plotting (Makr) of Allah is deluded (Mughtar), and the origin of this delusion (Ghurur) is that he inferred from worldly blessings that he is honorable with that Bestower, and it is possible that this is evidence of degradation, but that possibility does not agree with the desire (Hawa), so Satan, by means of the desire (Hawa), inclines the Heart (Qalb) toward what accompanies it, which is believing that it indicates honor, and this is the limit of delusion (Ghurur).
3:54.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

3:59.arabic: ويكفيه أن يعرف معنى آية واحدة في كتاب الله فإن القرآن علم الأولين والآخرين لمن فتحت بصيرته وقد قال تعالى "قتل الإنسان ما أكفره من أي شيء خلقه من نطفة خلقه فقدره ثم السبيل يسره ثم أماته فأقبره ثم إذا شاء أنشره" فقد أشارت الآية إلى أول خلق الإنسان فهو أنه لم يكن شيئاً مذكوراً وقد كان في حيز العدم دهوراً بل لم يكن لعدمه أول وأي شيء أخس وأقل من المحو والعدم؟ وقد كان كذلك في القدم، ثم خلقه الله من أرذل الأشياء، ثم من أقذرها إذ قد خلقه من تراب، ثم من نطفة، ثم من علقة، ثم من مضغة، ثم جعله عظماً، ثم كسا
3:59.english: And it suffices him to know the meaning of one verse in the Book of Allah, for the Quran is the knowledge of the first and the last for whom his insight has been opened. And He, the Exalted, has said: "Woe to man! What has made him reject? From what thing did He create him? From a sperm-drop He created him and proportioned him. Then He made the way easy for him. Then He causes him to die and puts him in a grave. Then when He wills, He will resurrect him." This verse points to the first creation of the human being, which is that he was not a thing mentioned, and he was in the realm of non-existence for ages, rather his non-existence had no beginning. And what is more vile and less than obliteration and non-existence? And he was like that in pre-eternity. Then Allah created him from the most vile of things, then from the filthiest of them, for indeed He created him from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh, then He made him bones, then He clothed the bones with flesh. This was the beginning of his existence when he became a thing mentioned. So he did not become a thing mentioned except while being upon the vilest of descriptions and attributes! For he was not created in his beginning complete, rather He created him as an inanimate dead thing that does not hear, nor see, nor feel, nor move, nor speak, nor grasp, nor perceive, nor know. So He began with his death before his life, and with his weakness before his strength, and with his ignorance before his knowledge, and with his blindness before his sight, and with his deafness before his hearing, and with his muteness before his speech, and with his misguidance before his guidance, and with his poverty before his wealth, and with his incapacity before his ability. This is the meaning of His saying: "From what thing did We create the human being? From a mixed sperm-drop." And the meaning of His saying: "Has there come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing mentioned? Indeed, We created man from a mixed sperm-drop to test him." Likewise, He created him first, then bestowed favor upon him, saying: "Then He made the way easy for him." And this points to what was facilitated for him during the period of his life until death. And likewise He said: "From a mixed sperm-drop We test him, so We made him hearing and seeing. Indeed, We guided him to the way, either grateful or ungrateful." And its meaning is that He gave him life after he was an inanimate dead thing, dust first and a sperm-drop second, and made him hear after he was deaf, and gave him sight after he was lacking vision, and strengthened him after weakness, and gave him knowledge after ignorance, and guided him after misguidance, and enriched him after poverty, and enabled him after incapacity. So if the human being knows himself with this knowledge, he knows that nothing befits him except humility, lowliness, and abasement. And if he knows his Lord, he knows that nothing befits greatness and pride except Allah. As for knowing his Lord and His majesty and glory, the discussion about it is lengthy, and it is the ultimate knowledge of unveiling (Mukashafa). And as for knowing himself, it is also lengthy, but we mention from that what benefits in arousing humility and lowliness. And it suffices him to know the meaning of one verse in the Book of Allah, for the Quran is the knowledge of the first and the last for whom his insight has been opened. And He, the Exalted, has said: "Indeed, the example of Jesus to Allah is like that of Adam. He created him from dust; then He said to him, 'Be,' and he was."
3:59.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

3:77.arabic: وقال ﭬ "ثلاثة لا يكلمهم الله ولا ينظر إليهم ولا يزكيهم ولهم عذاب أليم: شيخ زان، وملك كذاب، وعائل مستكبر"[151]
3:77.english: And he (peace be upon him) said: "Three whom Allah does not speak to, nor look at them, nor purify them, and for them is a painful punishment: an old man who commits adultery, a lying king, and a poor person who is arrogant."
3:77.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

3:77.arabic:
سوء يؤذيه فصبر على أذاه حتى يفرق بينهما موت  أو
ظعن، ورجل كان معه قوم في سفر أو سرية  فأطالوا  السرى  حتى  أعجبهم  أن  يمسوا
الأرض فنزلوا. فتنحى يصلى حتى يوقظ أصحابه للرحيل. وثلاثة يشنؤهم الله:  التاجر
أو البياع الحلاف، والفقير المختال والبخل المنان"[146] وقال ﭬ "ويل للذي  يحدث
فيكذب ليضحك به القوم ويل له ويل له"[147] وقال ﭬ "رأيت كأن  رجلاً  جاءني  فقال
لي قم فقمت معه، فإذا أنا برجلين أحدهما قائم والآخر جالس، بيد القائم كلوب  من
حديد يلقمه في شدق الجالس فيجذبه حتى  يبلغ  كاهله،  ثم  يجذبه  فلي
3:77.english: [151] Hadith: Three whom Allah will not speak to nor look at them, the hadith, and in it: and the lying Imam. Reported by Muslim from the narration of Abu Huraira.
3:77.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

3:77.arabic: فإذا كان الثناء على السلعة مع الصدق مكروها من حيث إنه فضول لا يزيد في الرزق فلا يخفى التغليظ في أمر اليمين وقد روى عن يونس بن عبيد وكان خزازا أنه طلب منه خز للشراء فأخرج غلامه سقط الخز ونشره ونظر إليه وقال اللهم ارزقنا الجنة فقال لغلامه رده إلى موضعه ولم يبعه وخاف أن يكون ذلك تعريضا بالثناء على السلعة فمثل هؤلاء الذين اتجروا في الدنيا ولم يضيعوا دينهم في تجاراتهم بل علموا أن ربح الآخرة أولى بالطلب من ربح الدنيا الثاني أن يظهر جميع عيوب المبيع خفيها وجليها ولا يكتم منها شيئا فذلك واجب فإن أخفاه ك
3:77.english: If praising the merchandise with truth is disliked because it is superfluous (Fudul) that does not increase in provision (Rizq), then the severity in the matter of the oath is not hidden. It has been narrated from Yunus bin 'Ubayd - and he was a silk merchant - that silk was requested from him for purchase, so his servant brought out the remnants of silk, spread it, looked at it and said: 'O Allah, grant us Paradise.' He said to his servant: 'Return it to its place' and did not sell it, fearing that this might be an allusion to praising the merchandise. Such are those who traded in this world (Dunya) and did not waste their religion (Deen) in their trades, but rather knew that the profit of the Hereafter (Akhirah) is more worthy of seeking than the profit of this world. The second is to reveal all defects of the sold item, both hidden and apparent, and not conceal anything from them, for that is obligatory. If he conceals it, he is an oppressor (Zalim), a deceiver (Ghash), and deception is forbidden, and he is abandoning sincerity (Nus'h) in the transaction, and sincerity is obligatory. Whenever he shows the better side of the garment and hides the other, he is a deceiver. Likewise, if he displays the garments in dark places, and likewise if he displays the better one of the pair of shoes or sandal and the like. What indicates the prohibition of deception is what has been narrated: He (peace be upon him) passed by a man selling food, and it pleased him, so he put his hand in it and saw dampness. He said: 'What is this?' He said: 'It was affected...'
3:77.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Etiquette of Earning'

3:83.arabic: الغموم وشدة الانتظار لعاقبة الأمر كما قال تعالى: ﴿ ونفخ فى الصور فصعق من فى السموات ومن فى الأرض إلا من شاء الله ثم نفخ فيه أخرى فإذا هم قيام ينظرون ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ فإذا نقر فى الناقور فذلك يومئذ يوم عسير على الكافرين غير يسير ﴾ {} وقال تعال: ﴿ ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين ما ينظرون إلا صيحة واحدة تأخذهم وهم يخصمون فلا يستطيعون توصية ولا إلى أهلهم يرجعون ونفخ فى الصور فإذا هم من الأجداث إلى ربهم ينسلون قالوا يا ويلنا من بعثنا من مرقدنا هذا ما وعد الرحمن وصدق المرسلون ﴾ {} فلو لم يكن ب
3:83.english: The sorrows and intensity of waiting for the outcome of the matter as He (Exalted is He) said: 'And the Horn is blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth falls dead except whom Allah wills. Then it is blown again, and at once they are standing, looking on.' {} And He (Exalted is He) said: 'And when the Trumpet is blown, that Day will be a difficult day for the disbelievers; not easy.' {} And He (Exalted is He) said: 'And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?" They do not await except one blast which will seize them while they are disputing. And they will not be able to make a testament, nor to their people will they return. And the Horn will be blown, and at once from the graves to their Lord they will hasten. They will say, "O woe to us! Who has raised us up from our sleeping place?" [It will be said], "This is what the Most Merciful had promised, and the messengers told the truth."' {} So if there were not before the dead except the terror of that blowing, it would be worthy to be feared, for it is a blowing and a cry by which whoever is in the heavens and the earth is struck dead, meaning they die by it except whom Allah wills, and that is some of the angels. And for that reason, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'How can I be at ease when the possessor of the Horn has taken the horn in his mouth, lowered his forehead, and inclined his ear, waiting for when he is commanded to blow?' [144] Maqatil said: The Horn is the trumpet, and that is because Israfil (upon him be peace) places his mouth on the horn like a trumpet, and the circumference of the head of the horn is like the width of the heavens and the earth, and he is gazing with his sight towards the Throne, waiting for when he is commanded to blow the first blowing. So when he blows, whoever is in the heavens and the earth is struck dead, meaning every living creature dies from the intensity of the fright except whom Allah wills, and that is Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil, and the Angel of Death. Then the Angel of Death is commanded to take the soul (Ruh) of Jibril, then the soul (Ruh) of Mika'il, then the soul (Ruh) of Israfil, then the Angel of Death is commanded and he dies. Then the creation remains after the first blowing in the Barzakh (the intermediate state) for forty years. Then Allah (Exalted is He) revives Israfil and commands him to blow the second, and that is His (Exalted is He) saying: 'Then it is blown again, and at once they are standing, looking on.' {} On their feet, looking at the Resurrection. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'When I was sent, I was sent to the possessor of the Horn, and he inclined it to his mouth, and advanced one foot and delayed another, waiting for when he is commanded to blow. So fear the blowing!' [145] So reflect upon the creatures and their humiliation, their breaking, and their submission at the resurrection out of fear from this striking dead and waiting for what is decreed upon them of happiness or misery. And you are among them broken like their breaking, perplexed like their perplexity. Rather, if you were in the world among the luxurious and the rich enjoying pleasures, then the kings of the earth on that day are the most humiliated people of the gathering ground, the smallest of them, and the most contemptible; they are trodden under feet like a grain. And at that time, the wild beasts from the deserts and the mountains come with lowered heads, mixed with the creatures after their wildness, humbled for the Day of Resurrection, without a sin that they have been defiled by, but their gathering is due to the intensity of the striking dead and the terror of the blowing and
3:83.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

3:84.arabic: حديث قرأ في الفجر  قولوا آمنا بالله الآية وفي الثانية ربنا آمنا بما أنزلت أخرجه مسلم من حديث ابن عباس كان يقرأ في ركعتي الفجر في الأولى منها قولوا آمنا بالله وما أنزل إلينا الآية التي في البقرة وفي الآخرة منها آمنا بالله واشهد بأنا مسلمون رواه أبو داود من حديث أبي هريرة قل آمنا بالله وما أنزل علينا الآية وفي الركعة الآخرة ربنا آمنا بما أنزلت أو إنا أرسلناك بالحق.
3:84.english: Hadith: He recited in the dawn prayer 'Say: We believe in Allah' verse and in the second 'Our Lord, we believe in what You have revealed.' Muslim transmitted it from the hadith of Ibn Abbas: He used to recite in the two rak'ahs of dawn prayer, in the first of them 'Say: We believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us' the verse that is in Al-Baqarah, and in the last of them 'We believe in Allah and bear witness that we are Muslims.' Abu Dawud transmitted from the hadith of Abu Hurairah: 'Say: We believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us' verse and in the second rak'ah 'Our Lord, we believe in what You have revealed' or 'Indeed, We have sent you with the truth.'
3:84.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

3:87.arabic: وفي خبر آخر: (( من غش أمتي فعليه لعنة الله والملائكة والناس أجمعين، قيل: يا رسول الله وما غش أمتك، قال: أن يبتدع بدعة يحمل الناس عليها))[196]. وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: (( إن لله عز وجل ملكا ينادى كل يوم من خالف سنة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لم تنله شفاعته ))[197]. ومثال الجاني على الدين بإبداع ما يخالف السنة بالنسبة إلى من يذنب ذنبا مثال من عصى الملك في قلب دولته بالنسبة إلى من خالف أمره في خدمة معينة وذلك قد يغفر له فأما في قلب الدولة فلا وقال بعض العلماء ما تكلم فيه السلف فالسكوت
3:87.english: And in another report: 'Whoever deceives my community, upon him is the curse of Allah and the angels and all the people. It was said: O Messenger of Allah, and what is deceiving your community? He said: That he innovates a religious innovation (bid'ah) and imposes it upon the people.' And the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'Indeed Allah the Exalted has an angel who calls out every day: Whoever opposes the tradition (sunnah) of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, will not attain his intercession.' And the example of the one who commits a crime against the religion by innovating what contradicts the tradition (sunnah) compared to one who commits a sin is like the example of one who disobeys the king in the heart of his kingdom compared to one who disobeys his command in a specific service, and that may be forgiven for him, but as for in the heart of the kingdom, no. And some scholars said: What the predecessors (salaf) spoke about, silence about it is ignorance, and what the predecessors (salaf) were silent about, speaking about it is affectation. And another said: The truth is heavy; whoever exceeds it oppresses, whoever falls short of it is deficient, and whoever stands with it is content. And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'Adhere to the middle path to which the elevated returns and from which the follower ascends.' And Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: Misguidance has sweetness in the hearts (qulub) of its people. Allah the Exalted said: 'And leave those who take their religion as play and amusement' (Al-An'am: 70). And He said: 'Is he whose evil deed is made attractive to him so that he sees it as good?' (Fatir: 8). So everything that was innovated after the companions, may Allah be pleased with them, that exceeds the measure of necessity and need is from play and amusement.
3:87.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

3:88.arabic: فانظر كيف انقلب الجاهلون وانكبوا على وجوههم انكباب العميان فأقبلوا على طلب كمال القدرة بالجاه والمال، وهو الكمال الذي لا يسلم وإن سلم فلا بقاء له، وأعرضوا عن كمال الحرية والعلم الذي إذا حصل كان أبدياً لا انقطاع له، وهؤلاء هم الذين اشتروا الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة فلا جرم لا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينصرون، وهم الذين لم يفهموا قوله تعالى "المال والبنون زينة الحياة الدنيا والباقيات الصالحات خير عند ربك ثواباً وخير أملاً" فالعلم والحرية هي الباقيات الصالحات التي تبقى كمالاً في النفس، والمال والجاه هو ال
3:88.english: Look how the ignorant have turned and fallen on their faces like the falling of the blind, so they turned to seeking perfection of power through status and wealth, which is the perfection that does not remain safe and even if it remains safe, it has no permanence, and they turned away from the perfection of freedom and knowledge which, when attained, becomes eternal with no cessation. And these are the ones who have purchased the worldly life in exchange for the Hereafter, so indeed no punishment is lightened for them nor are they given respite, and they are the ones who did not understand His saying, the Exalted: 'Wealth and children are adornment of the worldly life, but the enduring righteous deeds are better with your Lord for reward and better for hope.' So knowledge and freedom are the enduring righteous deeds which remain as perfection in the Soul (Nafs), and wealth and status are what perish in proximity, and it is as Allah, the Exalted, has likened it where He said: 'The example of worldly life is like water which We send down from the sky...' the verse. And He, the Exalted, said: 'And present to them the example of the worldly life as water which We send down from the sky...' until His saying: '...then it becomes dry debris scattered by the winds.' And everything that the winds of death scatter is the flower of the worldly life, and everything that death does not cut off is the enduring righteous deeds.
3:88.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

3:92.arabic: ولما أراد أبو طلحة أن يتصدق بحائط كان له يعجبه عملا بقوله تعالى لن تنالوا البر حتى تنفقوا مما تحبون حديث لما أراد أبو طلحة أن يتصدق بحائط له كان يعجبه عملا بقوله تعالى لن تنالوا البر حتى تنفقوا مما تحبون الحديث أخرجه البخاري وقد تقدم قال يا رسول الله هو في سبيل الله وللفقراء والمساكين فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم وجب أجرك على الله قسمه في أقاربك
3:92.english: And when Abu Talha intended to give in charity a garden that he had which pleased him, acting upon His saying, the Exalted: 'You will not attain righteousness (Al-Birr) until you spend from what you love.' The hadith: When Abu Talha intended to give in charity a garden that he had which pleased him, acting upon His saying, the Exalted: 'You will not attain righteousness (Al-Birr) until you spend from what you love.' The hadith was narrated by Al-Bukhari and it has preceded. He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, it is in the path of Allah (Fi Sabil Allah) and for the poor and the needy.' So the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: 'Your reward has become incumbent upon Allah. Distribute it among your relatives (Aqarib).'
3:92.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

3:92.arabic: وكان عبد الله بن عمر يتصدق بالسكر ويقول: سمعت الله يقول: ﴿ لن تنالوا البر حتى تنفقوا مما تحبون ﴾ والله يعلم أني أحب السكر.
3:92.english: And Abdullah ibn Umar used to give charity with sugar and say: I heard Allah say: 'You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love.' And Allah knows that I love sugar.
3:92.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

3:95.arabic:
تستجيب لي أخرجه أبو منصور الديلمي في مسند الفردوس من حديث ابن عباس
    اللهم ابعثنا في أحب الساعات إليك حتى نذكرك فتذكرنا ونسألك فتعطينا وندعوك
    فتستجيب لنا ونستغفرك فتغفر لنا وإسناده ضعيف وهو معروف من قول حبيب الطائي
                                          كما رواه ابن أبي الدنيا في الدعاء.
   [230]  حديث القول إذا استيقظ من منامه الحمد لله الذي أحيانا بعد ما أماتنا
              وإليه النشور أخرجه البخاري من حديث حذيفة ومسلم من حديث البراء.
  [231]  حديث أصبحنا وأصبح الملك لله والعظمة وال
3:95.english: [232] Hadith: We have awoken upon the natural disposition (Fitrah) of Islam and the word of sincerity (Kalimat al-Ikhlas) and the religion of our Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the way (Millah) of our father Abraham, upright (Hanifan) and not of the polytheists (Mushrikin). Al-Nasa'i transmitted it in 'Al-Yawm wa al-Laylah' from the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza with a sound chain, and Ahmad transmitted it from the hadith of Ibn Abza from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, raised to the Prophet.
3:95.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication

3:97.arabic: وأما إذا كان مال شبهة يحتمل أنه حلال فإذا لم يخرجه من يده لزمه الحج لأن كونه حلالا ممكن ولا يسقط الحج إلا بالفقر ولم يتحقق فقره وقد قال الله تعالى ولله على الناس حج البيت من استطاع إليه سبيلا وإذا وجب عليه التصدق بما يزيد على حاجته حيث يغلب على ظنه تحريمه فالزكاة أولى بالوجوب وان لزمته كفارة فليجمع بين الصوم والإعتاق ليتخلص بيقين وقد قال قوم يلزمه الصوم دون الإطعام إذ ليس له يسار معلوم وقال المحاسبي يكفيه الإطعام والذي نختاره أن كل شبهة حكمنا بوجوب اجتنابها وألزمناه إخراجها من يده لكون احتمال ال
3:97.english: And as for when there is wealth of doubtful nature (Shubha) that possibly could be permissible (Halal), if he does not remove it from his possession, the Pilgrimage (Hajj) becomes obligatory upon him because its being permissible is possible, and the Pilgrimage (Hajj) is not waived except due to poverty, and his poverty has not been confirmed. And Allah the Exalted has said: 'And to Allah is incumbent upon the people the Pilgrimage (Hajj) of the House for whoever is able to find a way to it.' And if it becomes obligatory upon him to give in charity (Sadaqah) what exceeds his need when the suspicion of its prohibition (Tahrim) predominates in his estimation, then the Obligatory Alms (Zakat) is more deserving of being obligatory. And if an expiation (Kaffarah) becomes obligatory upon him, then let him combine fasting (Sawm) and freeing a slave (Itq) to be purified with certainty. And some people have said that fasting (Sawm) becomes obligatory upon him without feeding (It'am) since he does not have known affluence. And Al-Muhasibi said that feeding (It'am) suffices him. And what we choose is that for every doubtful matter (Shubha) we have ruled the obligation of avoiding it and made obligatory upon him to remove it from his possession because the probability of prohibition (Haram) is predominant according to what we have mentioned. So upon him is combining fasting (Sawm) and feeding (It'am). As for fasting (Sawm), it is because he is legally bankrupt (Muflis). And as for feeding (It'am), it is because giving in charity (Sadaqah) of the entirety has become obligatory upon him, and it is possible that it belongs to him, so the obligation from the perspective of expiation (Kaffarah) becomes...
3:97.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

3:102.arabic: وأما خوف الأب عن بصيرة ومعرفة بصفة الحية وسمها وخاصيتها وسطوة السبع وبطشه وقلة مبالاته. وأما خوف الابن فإيمانه بمجرد التقليد لأنه يحسن الظن بأبيه ويعلم أنه لا يخاف إلا من سبب مخوف في نفسه فيعلم أن السبع مخوف ولا يعرف وجهه وإذا عرفت هذا المثال فاعلم أن الخوف من الله تعالى على مقامين أحدهما الخوف من عذابه والثاني الخوف منه فأما الخوف منه فهو خوف العلماء وأرباب القلوب العارفين من صفاته ما يقتضي الهيبة والخوف والحذر المطلعين على سر قوله تعالى: ﴿ ويحذركم الله نفسه ﴾ {} وقوله عز وجل: ﴿ اتقوا الله حق ت
3:102.english: And as for the fear of the father, it is from insight and knowledge of the snake's attribute, its poison, its characteristic, the lion's ferocity, its assault, and its lack of concern. And as for the fear of the son, it is his belief by mere imitation because he has good opinion of his father and knows that he does not fear except from a fearful cause in himself, so he knows that the lion is fearful but does not know its aspect. And if you understand this example, then know that the fear of God the Exalted is on two levels: one is the fear of His punishment, and the second is the fear from Him. As for the fear from Him, it is the fear of the scholars and the possessors of hearts (Qulub) who know from His attributes what necessitates awe, fear, and caution, those who are aware of the secret of His saying the Exalted: 'And Allah warns you of Himself' and His saying the Mighty and Majestic: 'Fear Allah as He should be feared.' And as for the first, it is the fear of the general creation, and it is attained by the foundation of belief in Paradise and Hell and that they are two recompenses for obedience and disobedience, and its weakness is due to heedlessness and the weakness of belief. And indeed, heedlessness is removed by reminding and admonition and persistence in thought about the terrors of the Day of Resurrection and the types of punishment in the Hereafter, and it is also removed by looking at those who fear and keeping their company and observing their states. And if observation is missed, then hearing is not devoid of effect. And as for the second, which is the higher, it is that God is the One to be feared, meaning that the servant fears the veil from Him and hopes for closeness to Him.
3:102.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

3:102.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
3:102.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'What is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)".'
3:102.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

3:103.arabic: ولا يخفي أن ثمرة الخلق الحسن الألفة وانقطاع الوحشة ومهما طاب المثمر طابت الثمرة وكيف وقد ورد في الثناء على نفس الألفة سيما إذا كانت الرابطة هي التقوى والدين وحب الله من الآيات والأخبار والآثار ما فيه كفاية ومقنع قال الله تعالى مظهرا عظيم منته على الخلق بنعمة الألفة لو أنفقت ما في الأرض جميعا ما ألفت بين قلوبهم ولكن الله ألف بينهم وقال فأصبحتم بنعمته إخوانا أي بالألفة ثم ذم التفرقة وزجر عنها فقال عز من قائل واعتصموا بحبل الله جميعا ولا تفرقوا إلى لعلكم تهتدون
3:103.english: And it is not hidden that the fruit of good character (Khuluq) is affection (Alfah) and the cutting off of estrangement (Wahshah), and whenever the source is good, the fruit is good. And how could it be otherwise when there has come in praise of affection (Alfah) itself, especially when the bond is piety (Taqwa) and religion (Deen) and love of Allah, from the verses (Ayah), reports (Akhbar), and traditions (Athar) what is sufficient and convincing. Allah the Exalted said, manifesting His great favor upon creation with the blessing of affection (Alfah): 'If you had spent all that is in the earth, you could not have brought their hearts together; but Allah brought them together.' And He said: 'So you became, by His favor, brothers' meaning through affection (Alfah). Then He censured division (Tafarruq) and warned against it, so He, the Mighty, the Speaker, said: 'And hold fast, all of you, to the rope (Habl) of Allah and do not be divided (Tafarraqa) so that you may be guided.'
3:103.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'
