3:103.arabic: وقال رسول الله ﷺ فى آية ﴿وَاعْتَصِمُوا بِحَبْلِ اللَّهِ جَمِيعًا وَلَا تَفَرَّقُوا ۚ وَاذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ كُنْتُمْ أَعْدَاءً فَأَلَّفَ بَيْنَ قُلُوبِكُمْ فَأَصْبَحْتُمْ بِنِعْمَتِهِ إِخْوَانًا وَكُنْتُمْ عَلَىٰ شَفَا حُفْرَةٍ مِنَ النَّارِ فَأَنْقَذَكُمْ مِنْهَا ۗ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ آيَاتِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ﴾: "إن الله يستخلص رجلا من أمتى على رءوس الخلائق يوم القيامة فينشر عليه تسعة وتسعين سجلا كل سجل منها مثل مد البصر ثم يقول أتنكر من هذا شيئا أظلم
3:103.english: And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said regarding the verse 'And hold firmly to the rope (Habl) of Allah all together and do not become divided. And remember the favor (Ni'mah) of Allah upon you - when you were enemies and He brought your hearts (Qulub) together and you became, by His favor (Ni'mah), brothers. And you were on the edge (Shafa) of a pit of the Fire and He saved you from it. Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses (Ayat) that you may be guided': 'Indeed, Allah will single out a man from my community on the Day of Resurrection before all creation. He will spread out before him ninety-nine scrolls, each scroll as far as the eye can see. Then He will say: Do you deny anything from this? Have My recording angels wronged you? He will say: No, O Lord. He will say: Do you have any excuse? He will say: No, O Lord. He will say: Yes, indeed you have with Us one good deed, and there is no injustice upon you today. Then He will bring out a card on which is written: I bear witness that there is no deity but Allah and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. He will say: O Lord, what is this card compared to these scrolls? He will say: You are not wronged. He said: Then the scrolls will be placed in one scale and the card in the other scale. He said: The scrolls will become light and the card will become heavy, for nothing is heavy alongside the name of Allah.'
3:103.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

3:104.arabic: والمذمة في إهماله وإضاعته ويدل على ذلك بعد إجماع الأمة عليه وإشارات العقول السليمة إليه الآيات والاخبار والآثار أما الآيات فقوله تعالى ولتكن منكم أمة يدعون إلى الخير ويأمرون بالمعروف وينهون عن المنكر وأولئك هم المفلحون ففي الآية بيان الإيجاب فإن قوله تعالى ولتكن أمر وظاهر الأمر الإيجاب وفيها بيان أن الفلاح منوط به إذ حصر وقال وأولئك هم المفلحون وفيها بيان أنه فرض كفاية لا فرض عين وأنه إذا قام به أمة سقط الفرض عن الآخرين إذ لم يقل كونوا كلكم آمرين بالمعروف بل قال ولتكن منكم أمة فإذا مهما قام به و
3:104.english: And the blame in neglecting and losing it, and what indicates that after the consensus of the community upon it and the indications of sound intellects toward it are the verses, reports, and traditions. As for the verses, then it is His saying, the Exalted: 'And let there be from you a community calling to the good and enjoining the recognized good (al-Ma'ruf) and forbidding the disapproved evil (al-Munkar), and those are the successful ones.' For in the verse is clarification of the obligation, for His saying, the Exalted, 'And let there be' is a command, and the apparent meaning of the command is obligation. And in it is clarification that the success (al-Falah) is tied to it, since He restricted and said, 'And those are the successful ones.' And in it is clarification that it is a collective obligation (Fard Kifayah), not an individual obligation (Fard 'Ayn), and that if a community undertakes it, the obligation falls from the others, since He did not say, 'Be all of you enjoiners of the recognized good,' but rather He said, 'And let there be from you a community.' So if, whenever one or a group undertakes it, the burden falls from the others, and the success (al-Falah) is specified for those who undertake it directly, and even if all of creation refrains from it, the burden encompasses all those capable of it without fail.
3:104.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

3:104.arabic: ليه الآيات والاخبار والآثار أما الآيات فقوله تعالى ولتكن منكم أمة يدعون إلى الخير ويأمرون بالمعروف وينهون عن المنكر وأولئك هم المفلحون ففي الآية بيان الإيجاب فإن قوله تعالى ولتكن أمر وظاهر الأمر الإيجاب وفيها بيان أن الفلاح منوط به إذ حصر وقال وأولئك هم المفلحون وفيها بيان أنه فرض كفاية لا فرض عين وأنه إذا قام به أمة سقط الفرض عن الآخرين إذ لم يقل كونوا كلكم آمرين بالمعروف بل قال ولتكن منكم أمة فإذا مهما قام به واحد أو جماعة سقط الحرج عن الآخرين واختص الفلاح بالقائمين به المباشرين وإن تقاعد عنه
3:104.english: As for the verses, the reports, and the traditions, regarding the verses, there is His statement, the Exalted: 'And let there be from you a community (Ummah) who invite to the good (Al-Khayr) and enjoin the recognized good (Al-Ma'ruf) and forbid the recognized evil (Al-Munkar), and those are the ones who are successful (Al-Mufliḥūn).' In the verse is a clarification of the obligation (Al-Ijāb), for His statement, the Exalted, 'And let there be' is a command, and the apparent meaning of the command is obligation. And in it is a clarification that success (Al-Falāḥ) is tied to it, since He specified and said, 'and those are the ones who are successful.' And in it is a clarification that it is a collective obligation (Farḍ Kifāyah), not an individual obligation (Farḍ 'Ayn), and that if a community (Ummah) undertakes it, the obligation falls away from the others, since He did not say, 'Be all of you enjoiners of the recognized good,' but rather said, 'And let there be from you a community.' So if one or a group undertakes it, the burden (Al-Ḥaraj) falls away from the others, and success is specifically for those who undertake it directly, even if all of creation (Al-Khalq) neglects it, the burden is removed from all those capable of it without doubt.
3:104.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

3:105.arabic: ذكر حجج المائلين إلى المخالطة ووجه ضعفها احتج هؤلاء بقوله تعالى ولا تكونوا كالذين تفرقوا واختلفوا الآية وبقوله تعالى فألف بين قلوبكم أمتن على الناس بالسبب المؤلف وهذا ضعيف لأن المراد به تفرق الآراء واختلاف المذاهب في معاني كتاب الله وأصول الشريعة والمراد بالألفة نزع الغوائل من الصدور وهي الأسباب المثيرة للفتن المحركة للخصومات والعزلة لا تنافي ذلك
3:105.english: Mention of the arguments of those inclined toward mixing/social interaction and the aspect of their weakness. These people argued with His saying, the Exalted: 'And do not be like those who divided and differed after the clear proofs had come to them' (the verse) and with His saying, the Exalted: 'And He united between your hearts (Qulub). You became, by His grace, brothers' (3:103). And this is weak because what is intended by it is the division of opinions and the difference of schools of thought in the meanings of the Book of Allah and the foundations of the Sharia. And what is intended by unity (Al-Ulfah) is the removal of the hidden enmities from the chests (Sudur), which are the causes that stir up seditions and move disputes. And seclusion (Al-Uzlah) does not contradict that.
3:105.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Seclusion'

3:109.arabic: وثلاث آيات من آخر سورة البقرة من قوله لله ما في السموات وما في الأرض إلى آخرها
3:109.english: And three verses from the end of Surah Al-Baqarah from His saying 'To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth' to its end
3:109.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Book of Knowledge'

3:110.arabic: وسئل ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه عن تفسير هذه الآية فقال إن هذا ليس زمانها إنها اليوم مقبولة ولكن قد اوشك أن يأتي زمانها تأمرون بالمعروف فيصنع بكم كذا وكذا وتقولون فلا يقبل منكم فحينئذ عليكم انفسكم لا يضركم من ضل إذا اهتديتم
3:110.english: And Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) was asked about the interpretation of this verse, so he said: 'This is not its time; today it is accepted, but it has nearly come that its time will come when you command the good (al-Ma'ruf) and such and such is done to you, and you say, but it is not accepted from you. Then at that time, upon yourselves (it is incumbent) - it does not harm you if someone goes astray when you are guided.'
3:110.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

3:110.arabic: وقال تعالى لعن الذين كفروا من بني إسرائيل على لسان داود وعيسى ابن مريم ذلك بما عصوا وكانوا يعتدون كانوا لا يتناهون عن منكر فعلوه لبئس ما كانوا يفعلون وهذا غاية التشديد إذ علل استحقاقهم للعنة بتركهم النهي عن المنكر وقال عز وجل كنتم خير أمة أخرجت للناس تأمرون بالمعروف وتنهون عن المنكر وهذا يدل على فضيلة الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر إذ بين أنهم كانوا به خير أمة أخرجت للناس
3:110.english: And Allah the Exalted said: 'Cursed were those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel by the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary. That was because they disobeyed and were transgressing. They used not to prevent one another from the wrongdoing that they committed. How wretched was that which they were doing.' And this is the utmost severity, as He explained their deserving of the curse by their abandonment of forbidding the wrong. And Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: 'You are the best nation brought forth for mankind, commanding what is right and forbidding what is wrong.' And this indicates the virtue of commanding what is right and forbidding what is wrong, as He made clear that they were by it the best nation brought forth for mankind.
3:110.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

3:110.arabic: وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لتأمرن بالمعروف ولتنهون عن المنكر أو ليسلطن الله عليكم شراركم ثم يدعوا خياركم فلا يستجاب لهم حديث لتأمرن بالمعروف ولتنهون عن المنكر أو ليسلطن الله عليكم شراركم ثم يدعوا خياركم فلا يستجاب لهم أخرجه البزار من حديث عمر بن الخطاب والطبراني في الأوسط من حديث أبي هريرة وكلاهما ضعيف وللترمذي من حديث حذيفة نحوه إلا انه قال أو ليوشكن الله أن يبعث عليكم عقابا منه ثم تدعونه فلا يستجيب لكم قال هذا حديث حسن معناه تسقط مهابتهم من أعين الاشرار فلا يخافونهم وقال صلى الله عليه و
3:110.english: And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'You must command the good (al-Ma'ruf) and forbid the evil (al-Munkar), or Allah will empower the worst among you over you, then the best among you will supplicate but will not be answered.' The hadith 'You must command the good (al-Ma'ruf) and forbid the evil (al-Munkar), or Allah will empower the worst among you over you, then the best among you will supplicate but will not be answered' is reported by Al-Bazzar from the hadith of Umar ibn Al-Khattab and Al-Tabarani in Al-Awsat from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, and both are weak. And Al-Tirmidhi reports from the hadith of Hudhayfah similarly, except that he said: 'Or Allah will soon send upon you a punishment from Him, then you will call upon Him but He will not respond to you.' He said this hadith is good in meaning: their awe falls from the eyes of the evildoers, so they do not fear them. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'O people, Allah says: You must command the good (al-Ma'ruf) and forbid the evil (al-Munkar) before you supplicate but are not answered.' The hadith 'O people, Allah the Exalted says: You must command the good (al-Ma'ruf) and forbid the evil (al-Munkar) before you supplicate but are not answered' is reported by Ahmad and Al-Bayhaqi from the hadith of Aisha with the wording 'Command and forbid,' and it is in Ibn Majah without attributing it to the speech of Allah the Exalted, and in its chain there is weakness. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'What are the deeds of righteousness (al-Birr) compared to striving in the path of Allah (al-Jihad fi Sabil Allah) except like a drop in a vast ocean? And what are all the deeds of righteousness (al-Birr) and striving in the path of Allah (al-Jihad fi Sabil Allah) compared to commanding the good (al-Ma'ruf) and forbidding the evil (al-Munkar) except like a drop in a vast ocean?' The hadith 'What are the deeds of righteousness (al-Birr) compared to striving in the path of Allah (al-Jihad fi Sabil Allah) except like a drop in a vast ocean? And what are all the deeds of righteousness (al-Birr) and striving in the path of Allah (al-Jihad fi Sabil Allah) compared to commanding the good (al-Ma'ruf) and forbidding the evil (al-Munkar) except like a drop in a vast ocean?' Then Allah the Exalted said: 'You are the best community (Ummah) brought forth for mankind: you command the good (al-Ma'ruf) and forbid the evil (al-Munkar), and you believe in Allah. And if the People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab) had believed, it would have been better for them. Among them are the believers (al-Mu'minun), but most of them are the defiantly disobedient (al-Fasiqun).'
3:110.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

3:110.arabic: وقال تعالى كنتم خير أمة أخرجت للناس تأمرون بالمعروف وتنهون عن المنكر وهذا يدل على فضيلة الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر إذ بين أنهم كانوا به خير أمة أخرجت للناس
3:110.english: And Allah the Exalted said: 'You are the best nation brought forth for mankind, commanding what is recognized as good (al-Ma'ruf) and forbidding what is recognized as evil (al-Munkar).' And this indicates the virtue of commanding what is recognized as good (al-Ma'ruf) and forbidding what is recognized as evil (al-Munkar), since He made clear that they were by it the best nation brought forth for mankind.
3:110.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

3:110.arabic: منكم قيل بل منهم يا رسول الله قال لا بل منكم لأنكم تجدون على الخير أعوانا ولا يجدون عليه أعوانا وسئل ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه عن تفسير هذه الآية فقال إن هذا ليس زمانها إنها اليوم مقبولة ولكن قد اوشك أن يأتي زمانها تأمرون بالمعروف فيصنع بكم كذا وكذا وتقولون فلا يقبل منكم فحينئذ عليكم انفسكم لا يضركم من ضل إذا اهتديتم وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لتأمرن بالمعروف ولتنهون عن المنكر أو ليسلطن الله عليكم شراركم ثم يدعوا خياركم فلا يستجاب لهم حديث لتأمرن بالمعروف ولتنهون عن المنكر أو ليسلطن الله علي
3:110.english: From you, it was said: 'Rather from them, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'No, rather from you, because you find helpers for the good (al-Khayr), and they do not find helpers for it.' And Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked about the interpretation (tafsir) of this verse (ayah). He said: 'This is not its time; today it is accepted, but it has nearly come that its time will come: you enjoin the good (al-Ma'ruf) and such and such will be done to you, and you say, but it is not accepted from you. Then at that time, upon yourselves, it does not harm you if someone goes astray when you are guided.' And the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'You must enjoin the good (al-Ma'ruf) and forbid the evil (al-Munkar), or Allah will empower over you the worst of you, then the best of you will supplicate, but they will not be answered.' The hadith: 'You must enjoin the good (al-Ma'ruf) and forbid the evil (al-Munkar), or Allah will empower over you the worst of you, then the best of you will supplicate, but they will not be answered.' Al-Bazzar narrated it from the hadith of Umar ibn al-Khattab, and al-Tabarani in al-Awsat from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, and both are weak. And al-Tirmidhi has from the hadith of Hudhayfah something similar, except he said: 'Or it is nearly that Allah sends upon you a punishment from Him, then you supplicate to Him, but He does not respond to you.' He said: 'This hadith is hasan; its meaning is that their awe falls from the eyes of the evildoers, so they do not fear them.' And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'O people, indeed Allah says: You must enjoin the good (al-Ma'ruf) and forbid the evil (al-Munkar) before you supplicate, then you will not be answered.' The hadith: 'O people, indeed Allah, glorified and exalted, says: You must enjoin the good (al-Ma'ruf) and forbid the evil (al-Munkar) before you supplicate, then you will not be answered.' Ahmad and al-Bayhaqi narrated it from the hadith of A'ishah with the wording: 'Command and forbid,' and it is in Ibn Majah without attributing it to the speech of Allah, the Exalted, and in its chain there is weakness.
3:110.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

3:113.arabic: وقال تعالى ليسوا سواء من أهل الكتاب أمة قائمة يتلون آيات الله آناء الليل وهم يسجدون يؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر ويأمرون بالمعروف وينهون عن المنكر ويسارعون في الخيرات وأولئك من الصالحين فلم يشهد لهم بالصلاح بمجرد الإيمان بالله واليوم الآخر حتى اضاف إليه الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر
3:113.english: And He, the Exalted, said: 'They are not all alike; among the People of the Book is a standing community who recite the verses of Allah during periods of the night, and they prostrate. They believe in Allah and the Last Day, and they command what is right (al-Ma'ruf) and forbid what is wrong (al-Munkar), and they hasten to good deeds. And those are among the righteous.' So He did not testify to their righteousness merely by their belief in Allah and the Last Day until He added to it commanding what is right (al-Ma'ruf) and forbidding what is wrong (al-Munkar).
3:113.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

3:114.arabic: وقال تعالى ليسوا سواء من أهل الكتاب أمة قائمة يتلون آيات الله آناء الليل وهم يسجدون يؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر ويأمرون بالمعروف وينهون عن المنكر ويسارعون في الخيرات وأولئك من الصالحين فلم يشهد لهم بالصلاح بمجرد الإيمان بالله واليوم الآخر حتى اضاف إليه الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر
3:114.english: And He (Exalted) said: 'They are not all alike; among the People of the Book is a standing community who recite the verses of Allah during periods of the night while they prostrate. They believe in Allah and the Last Day, and they command the recognized good (al-Ma'ruf) and forbid the recognized evil (al-Munkar), and they hasten in the good deeds, and those are among the righteous (al-Salihin).' So He did not testify to their righteousness (al-Salah) by mere belief in Allah and the Last Day until He added to it the commanding of the recognized good (al-Ma'ruf) and the forbidding of the recognized evil (al-Munkar).
3:114.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

3:116.arabic: وإلهكم إله واحد لا إله إلا هو الرحمن الرحيم إن في خلق السموات والأرض إلى آخر الآية وقل هو الله أحد خمس عشرة مرة ثم يركع ويسجد فإذا قام في الركعة الثانية قرأ فاتحة الكتاب وآية الكرسي وآيتين بعدها إلى قوله أولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون وثلاث آيات من آخر سورة البقرة من قوله لله ما في السموات وما في الأرض إلى آخرها وقل هو الله أحد خمس عشرة مرة
3:116.english: And your God is One God, there is no god but He, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth to the end of the verse, and say 'He is Allah, the One' fifteen times, then bow and prostrate. When he stands in the second unit, he recites the Opening of the Book (Al-Fatihah) and the Throne Verse (Ayat al-Kursi) and two verses after it until His saying 'Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally' and three verses from the end of Surah Al-Baqarah from His saying 'To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth' to its end, and say 'He is Allah, the One' fifteen times.
3:116.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Book of Knowledge'

3:118.arabic: وبالجملة فالحسد يلزم البغض والعداوة ولا يفارقهما، وإنما غاية التقى أن لا يبغي وأن يكره ذلك من نفسه، فأما أن يبغض إنساناً ثم يستوي عند مسرته ومساءته، فهذا غير ممكن، وهذا مما وصف الله تعالى الكفار به أعني الحسد بالعداوة إذ قال الله تعالى "وإذا لقوكم قالوا آمنا وإذا خلو عضوا عليكم الأنامل من الغيظ قل موتوا بغيظكم إن الله عليم بذات الصدور. إن تمسسكم حسنة تسؤهم" الآية. وكذلك قال "ودوا ما عنتم قد بدت البغضاء من أفواههم وما تخفي صدورهم أكبر" والحسد بسبب البغض ربما يفضي إلى التنازع والتقاتل واستغراق الع
3:118.english: In summary, envy (Hasad) necessitates hatred (Bughd) and enmity (Adawa) and does not separate from them. The utmost limit of piety (Taqwa) is not to transgress and to dislike that from one's soul (Nafs). As for hating a person and then being equal at his joy and sorrow, this is not possible. This is among what Allah the Exalted described the disbelievers with, meaning envy with enmity, when Allah the Exalted said: 'And when they meet you, they say, "We believe." But when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you in rage. Say, "Die in your rage. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of that within the chests." If good touches you, it distresses them' [the verse]. And likewise He said: 'They wish what would distress you. Hatred has already shown from their mouths, and what their chests conceal is greater.' And envy due to hatred may lead to dispute and fighting and consuming the lifetime in removing the blessing through schemes and slander and tearing the veil and what runs its course.
3:118.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

3:118.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
3:118.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'Whatever is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (Masakin)".'
3:118.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

3:119.arabic: السبب الأول: العداوة والبغضاء، وهذا أشد أسباب الحسد، فإن من آذاه شخص بسبب من الأسباب وخالفه في غرض بوجه من الوجوه أبغضه قلبه وغضب عليه ورسخ في نفسه الحقد. والحقد يقتضي التشفي والانتقام، فإن عجز المبغض عن أن يتشفى بنفسه أحب أن يتشفى منه الزمان، وربما يحيل ذلك على كرامة نفسه عند الله تعالى فمهما أصابت عدوة بلية فرح بها وظنها مكافأة له من جهة الله على بغضه وأنها لأجله، ومهما أصابته نعمة ساءه ذلك لأنه ضد مراده، وربما يخطر له أنه لا منزلة له عند الله حيث لم ينتقم له من عدوه الذي آذاه بل أنعم عليه. وب
3:119.english: The first cause: enmity and hatred, and this is the strongest cause of envy (Hasad), for whoever is harmed by a person due to some cause and is opposed in a desire in some manner, his heart hates him and becomes angry with him, and rancor (Haqd) becomes firmly rooted in his soul (Nafs). And rancor necessitates seeking revenge and retaliation; if the hater is unable to take revenge himself, he loves that time take revenge for him, and perhaps he attributes that to the honor of his self (Nafs) with Allah the Exalted. So whenever a calamity befalls his enemy, he rejoices at it and thinks it is a reward for him from Allah for his hatred and that it is for his sake; and whenever a blessing befalls him, it grieves him because it is contrary to his desire, and perhaps it occurs to him that he has no status with Allah since He did not avenge him from his enemy who harmed him but rather bestowed favor upon him. In summary, envy necessitates hatred and enmity and does not separate from them, and the utmost limit of piety (Taqwa) is not to transgress and to dislike that from his self (Nafs). As for hating a person and then being equal at his joy and sorrow, this is not possible, and this is among what Allah the Exalted described the disbelievers with, meaning envy with enmity, when Allah the Exalted said: 'And when they meet you, they say, "We believe," but when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you in rage. Say, "Die in your rage. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts." If good touches you, it distresses them' the verse. And likewise He said: 'They wish you would have hardship. Hatred has already shown from their mouths, and what their breasts conceal is greater.' And envy due to hatred may lead to dispute and fighting and consuming one's lifetime in removing the blessing through schemes, slander, and exposing secrets and what follows that course.
3:119.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

3:119.arabic: الأولى الرياء بأصل الإيمان وهذا أغلظ أبواب الرياء وصاحبه مخلد في النار، وهو الذي يظهر كلمتي الشهادة وباطنه مشحون بالتكذيب ولكنه يرائي بظاهر الإسلام، وهو الذي ذكره الله تعالى في كتابه في مواضع شتى كقوله عز وجل "إذا جاءك المنافقون قالوا نشهد إنك لرسول الله والله يعلم إنك لرسوله والله يشهد إن المنافقين لكاذبون" أي في دلالتهم بقولهم على ضمائرهم وقال تعالى "ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه وهو ألد الخصام وإذا تولى سعى في الأرض ليفسد فيها" الآية وقال تعالى "وإذا لقوكم
3:119.english: The first: Showing off (Riya) with the foundation of faith (Iman), and this is the most severe of the gates of showing off, and its practitioner is eternally in the Fire, and he is the one who manifests the two testimonies (Shahada) while his inner self (Batin) is filled with denial, but he shows off with the outward appearance (Zahir) of Islam, and he is the one whom Allah the Exalted mentioned in His Book in various places, such as His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: "When the hypocrites come to you, they say, 'We testify that you are the Messenger of Allah.' And Allah knows that you are His Messenger, and Allah testifies that the hypocrites are liars'" meaning in their indication by their speech of their inner thoughts (Damair). And He said, the Exalted: "And among the people is he whose speech pleases you in worldly life, and he calls Allah to witness as to what is in his heart (Qalb), yet he is the fiercest of opponents. And when he turns away, he strives throughout the land to cause corruption therein" the verse. And He said, the Exalted: "And when they meet you, they say, 'We have believed,' but when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you in rage." And He said, the Exalted: "They show off (Yura'un) to people and do not remember (Yadhkurun) Allah except a little, wavering between that." And the verses about them are many.
3:119.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

3:120.arabic: اعلم أن المؤذي ممقوت بالطبع، ومن آذاك فلا يمكنك أن لا تبغضه غالباً، فإذا تيسرت له نعمة فلا يمكنك أن لا تكرهها له حتى يستوي عندك حسن حال عدوك وسوء حاله، بل لا تزال تدرك في النفس بينهما تفرقة، ولا يزال الشيطان ينازعك إلى الحسد له، ولكن عن قوي ذلك فيك حتى بعثك على إظهار الحسد بقول أو فعل بحيث يعرف ذلك من ظاهرهك بأفعالك الاختيارية فأنت حسود عاص بحسدك، وإن كففت ظاهرك بالكلية إلا أنك بباطنك تحب زوال النعمة وليس في نفسك كراهة لهذه الحالة فأنت أيضاً حسود عاص، لأن الحسد صفة القلب لا صفة الفعل، قال الله ت
3:120.english: Know that the one who harms is naturally hated, and if someone harms you, you cannot help but hate them generally. So if a blessing (Ni'mah) becomes easy for them, you cannot help but dislike it for them until the good state of your enemy and his bad state become equal to you. Rather, you continuously perceive in the Soul (Nafs) a distinction between them, and Satan continuously contends with you towards envy (Hasad) for him. But if that becomes strong in you until it incites you to manifest envy (Hasad) by word or action such that it is known from your outward appearance by your voluntary actions, then you are an envious sinner by your envy (Hasad). And if you completely restrain your outward appearance, but in your inner self you love the removal of the blessing (Ni'mah) and there is no dislike in your Soul (Nafs) for this state, then you are also an envious sinner, because envy (Hasad) is an attribute of the Heart (Qalb), not an attribute of action. Allah the Exalted said: "Nor will they find in their chests a need of that which they have been given" (Quran 59:9), and He the Almighty said: "They wish that you would disbelieve as they have disbelieved, so you would be equal" (Quran 4:89), and He said: "If good touches you, it distresses them" (Quran 3:120). As for the action, it is backbiting and lying, and it is an act emanating from envy (Hasad) and is not the essence of envy (Hasad). Rather, the place of envy (Hasad) is the Heart (Qalb), not the limbs. Yes, this envy (Hasad) is not an injustice that one seeks to make permissible, but it is a sin between you and Allah the Exalted. And seeking permissibility is only required from the apparent causes on the limbs. So if you restrain your outward appearance and compel with that your Heart (Qalb) to dislike what naturally emanates from it of loving the removal of the blessing (Ni'mah) until it is as if you detest your Soul (Nafs) for what is in its nature, so that dislike is from the side of the intellect in opposition to the inclination from the side of nature, then you have fulfilled the obligation upon you. And in most cases, no more than this enters under your choice. As for changing the nature so that the one who harms and the one who does good become equal to him, and his joy or grief over what becomes easy for them of blessing (Ni'mah) or what befalls them of calamity becomes equal, this is something that nature does not comply with as long as one is attentive to the shares of the worldly life, unless one becomes absorbed in Allah the Exalted like the intoxicated, passionate one. Then his affair may end with his Heart (Qalb) not paying attention to the details of the states of the servants, but rather looking at all with one eye, which is the eye of mercy, and seeing all as servants of Allah and their actions as actions of Allah, and seeing them as subjugated. And if that is, it is like fleeting lightning that does not last. Then the Heart (Qalb) returns after that to its nature and the
3:120.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

3:120.arabic: وأي معصية تزيد على كراهتك لراحة مسلم من غير أن يكون لك منه مضرة؟ وإلى هذا أشار القرآن بقوله "إن تمسسكم حسنة تسؤهم وإن تصبكم سيئة يفرحوا بها" وهذا الفرح شماتة والحسد والشماتة يتلازمان.
3:120.english: And what sin exceeds your hatred for the comfort of a Muslim without there being any harm to you from it? And to this the Quran pointed with His saying: "If a good thing touches you, it distresses them; and if a bad thing befalls you, they rejoice at it." And this rejoicing is gloating (Schadenfreude), and envy (Hasad) and gloating (Shamata) are concomitant.
3:120.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

3:125.arabic: وعلق النصرة على الصبر فقال تعالى: ﴿ بلى إن تصبروا وتتقوا ويأتوكم من فورهم هذا يمددكم ربكم بخمسة آلاف من الملائكة مسومين ﴾ {} وجمع للصابرين بين أمور لم يجمعها لغيرهم فقال تعالى: ﴿ أولئك عليهم صلوات من ربهم ورحمة وأولئك هم المهتدون ﴾ {} فالهدى والرحمة والصلوات مجموعة للصابرين واستقصاء جميع الآيات في مقام الصبر يطول.
3:125.english: And He made victory conditional upon patience (الصبر) when He said: 'Yes, if you are patient (تصبروا) and are God-fearing (تتقوا) and they come upon you in this onslaught of theirs, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels marked (مسومين).' And He gathered for the patient (الصابرين) matters that He did not gather for others when He said: 'Those are the ones upon whom are prayers (صلوات) from their Lord and mercy (رحمة), and those are the ones who are guided (المهتدون).' So guidance (الهدى), mercy (الرحمة), and prayers (الصلوات) are gathered for the patient (الصابرين), and enumerating all the verses regarding the station of patience (الصبر) would be lengthy.
3:125.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

3:126.arabic: يصه مشدود الأزرار وربما حل الأزرار في الصلاة وغيرها حديث كان قميصه مشدود الأزرارا وربما حل الأزرار في الصلاة وغيرها أبو داود والبيهقي والترمذي في الشمائل من رواية معاوية بن قرة بن إياس عن أبيه قال أتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في رهط من مزينة وبايعناه وأن قميصه مطلق الأزرار وللبيهقي من رواية زيد بن أسلم قال رأيت ابن عمر يصلي محلولة أزراره فسألته عن ذلك فقال رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يفعله وفي العلل للترمذي أنه سأل البخاري عن هذا الحديث فقال أنا أتقي هذا الشيخ كأن حديثه موضوع يعني زهير بن
3:126.english: His garment was fastened with buttons, and sometimes he would unfasten the buttons during prayer and other times. Hadith: His shirt was fastened with buttons, and sometimes he would unfasten the buttons during prayer and other times. Abu Dawud, Al-Bayhaqi, and Al-Tirmidhi in Al-Shama'il from the narration of Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah ibn Iyas from his father who said: I came to the Prophet (peace be upon him) with a group from Muzaynah and we pledged allegiance to him, and his shirt had unfastened buttons. And for Al-Bayhaqi from the narration of Zayd ibn Aslam who said: I saw Ibn 'Umar praying with his buttons unfastened, so I asked him about that, and he said: I saw the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) doing it. And in Al-'Ilal of Al-Tirmidhi, that he asked Al-Bukhari about this hadith, and he said: I am cautious of this sheikh, as if his hadith is fabricated, meaning Zuhayr ibn Muhammad, its narrator from Zayd ibn Aslam. I said: Al-Walid ibn Muslim followed him on it from Zayd. Ibn Khuzaymah narrated it in his Sahih. And for Al-Tabarani from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas with a weak chain: I entered upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) while he was praying, sitting with his buttons unfastened. And he had a cloak dyed with saffron, and sometimes he would pray with people in it alone. Hadith: He had a cloak dyed with saffron, and sometimes he would pray with people in it. Abu Dawud and Al-Tirmidhi transmitted it from the hadith of Qaylah bint Makhramah who said: I saw the Prophet (peace be upon him) upon him were two worn-out garments that were dyed with saffron. Al-Tirmidhi said: We do not know it except from 'Abdullah ibn Hassan. I said: And its narrators are trustworthy. And Abu Dawud from the hadith of Qays ibn Sa'd: He performed ablution, then my father Sa'd handed him a cloak dyed with saffron or wars, and he wrapped himself in it. The hadith and its men are trustworthy. And sometimes not the cloak alone, what was upon him other than it. Hadith: Sometimes he wore the cloak alone, not upon him other than it. Ibn Majah and Ibn Khuzaymah narrated it from the hadith of Thabit ibn Al-Samit that the Prophet (peace be upon him) prayed in Banu 'Abd Al-Ashhal and upon him was a cloak wrapped around him. The hadith. And in the narration of Al-Bazzar: In a cloak. And he had a patched cloak that he wore and said: Indeed, I am a servant, I wear as the servant wears. Hadith: He had a patched cloak that he wore and said: I am a servant, I wear as the servant wears. The two sheikhs transmitted it from the narration of Abu Burdah who said: 'A'ishah brought out to us a patched cloak and a coarse waist-wrapper and said: In these two, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) passed away. And for Al-Bukhari from the hadith of 'Umar: Indeed, I am a servant. And for 'Abd Al-Razzaq in Al-Musannaf from the narration of Ayyub Al-Sakhtiyani, raised disconnected: Indeed, I am a servant, I eat as the servant eats, and I sit as the servant sits. And preceded from the hadith of Anas, Ibn 'Umar, and 'A'ishah connected. And he had two garments specifically for Friday other than his garments on other than Friday. Hadith: He had two garments specifically for Friday. The hadith. Al-Tabarani transmitted it in Al-Saghir and Al-Awsat from the hadith of 'A'ishah with a weak chain. He added: When he finished.
3:126.book_title: Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character
3:126.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character'

3:128.arabic: حتى إن من لم يعلم عاقبته كان يلعنه فنهى عنه إذ روي: أنه كان يلعن الذي قتلوا أصحاب بثر معونة في قنوته شهراً فنزل قوله تعالى "ليس لك من الأمر شيء أو يتوب عليهم أو يعذبهم فإنهم ظالمون" يعني أنهم ربما يسلمون فمن أين تعلم أنهم ملعونون؟
3:128.english: Until indeed, whoever did not know his ultimate outcome would curse him, so he prohibited it when it was narrated: that he used to curse those who killed the companions of Bi'r Ma'unah in his supplication (Qunut) for a month, then descended His saying, the Exalted: "Not for you is anything of the matter, or He turns to them (in forgiveness) (Yatūbu 'alayhim) or He punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers (Ẓālimūn)." Meaning that they might possibly become Muslims (Yuslimūn), so from where do you know that they are cursed?
3:128.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

3:128.arabic: ويقرب من هذا ما روى عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما (أن رسول الله ﷺ كان يقنت على المشركين ويلعنهم في صلاته فنزل عليه قوله تعالى: ﴿ ليس لك من الأمر شىء ﴾ {} الآية فترك الدعاء عليهم وهدى الله تعالى عامة أولئك للإسلام[54])
3:128.english: And close to this is what was narrated from Ibn Abbas, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with them both, (that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to supplicate against the polytheists and curse them in his prayer, then there descended upon him the saying of Allah the Exalted: 'Not for you is any part of the matter' (Quran 3:128) {} the verse, so he abandoned the supplication against them, and Allah the Exalted guided most of those to Islam[54]).
3:128.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Fear and Hope'

3:128.arabic: ولما كسرت رباعيته وشج يوم أحد فجعل الدم يسيل على وجهه وهو يمسح الدم ويقول كيف يفلح قوم خضبوا وجه نبيهم بالدم وهو يدعوهم إلى ربهم حديث كسرت رباعيته صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم أحد الحديث في نزول ليس لك من الأمر شيء أخرجه مسلم من حديث أنس وذكره البخاري تعليقا فأنزل الله تعالى ليس لك من الأمر شيء تأديبا له على ذلك وأمثال هذه التأديبات في القرآن لا تحصر وهو صلى الله عليه وسلم المقصود الأول بالتأديب والتهذيب ثم منه يشرق النور على كافة الخلق فإنه أدب بالقرآن وأدب الخلق به ولذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم بعثت
3:128.english: And when his incisor was broken and he was wounded on the day of Uhud, and the blood was flowing on his face while he was wiping the blood and saying: 'How can a people succeed who have stained the face of their Prophet with blood while he is calling them to their Lord?' The hadith of his incisor being broken (peace be upon him) on the day of Uhud - the hadith concerning the revelation of 'Not for you is any part of the matter' - Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Anas, and Bukhari mentioned it as a suspended narration. So Allah the Exalted revealed: 'Not for you is any part of the matter' as a discipline (ta'dīb) for him regarding that. And examples of these disciplines (ta'dībāt) in the Quran are countless, and he (peace be upon him) is the first intended one for discipline (ta'dīb) and refinement (tahdhīb), then from him the light shines upon all creation. For he was disciplined (adīb) by the Quran and disciplined (adīb) creation with it. And therefore he (peace be upon him) said: 'I was sent to perfect noble character traits (makārim al-akhlāq).' The hadith 'I was sent to perfect noble character traits' - Ahmad, Al-Hakim, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated it from the hadith of Abu Huraira.
3:128.book_title: Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character
3:128.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character'

3:128.arabic: حديث ابن عباس كان يقنت على المشركين ويلعنهم في صلاته فنزل قوله تعالى - ليس لك من الأمر شىء - فترك الدعاء عليهم الحديث أخرجه البخاري من حديث ابن عمر أنه كان إذا رفع راسه من الركوع في الركعة الأخيرة من الفجر يقول اللهم العن فلانا وفلانا وفلانا بعد ما يقول سمع الله لمن حمده ربنا ولك الحمد فأنزل الله عز وجل - ليس لك من الأمر شيء. إلى قوله: فإنهم ظالمون - ورواه الترمذي وسماهم أبا سفيان والحارث بن هشام وصفوان بن أمية وزاد فتاب عليهم فأسلموا فحسن إسلامهم وقال حسن غريب وفي رواية له أربعة نفر لم يسمهم وق
3:128.english: Hadith of Ibn Abbas: He used to supplicate against the polytheists and curse them in his prayer, then the saying of Allah the Exalted descended: 'Not for you is any part of the matter' - so he abandoned supplicating against them. The hadith was reported by al-Bukhari from the hadith of Ibn Umar that when he raised his head from bowing in the last unit of the dawn prayer, he would say: O Allah, curse so-and-so and so-and-so and so-and-so after saying: Allah hears those who praise Him, our Lord and to You is praise. Then Allah the Exalted revealed: 'Not for you is any part of the matter' up to His saying: 'For indeed they are wrongdoers.' And al-Tirmidhi reported it and named them: Abu Sufyan, al-Harith ibn Hisham, and Safwan ibn Umayyah, and added: Then He turned to them in forgiveness (Tawbah) so they embraced Islam and their Islam became good, and he said: Hasan Gharib. And in a narration of his: Four men without naming them, and he said: Then Allah guided them to Islam, and he said: Hasan Gharib Sahih.
3:128.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Fear and Hope'

3:128.arabic: [82] حديث أنه كان يلعن الذين قتلوا أصحاب بئر معونة في قنوته شهرا فنزل قوله تعالى ليس لك من الأمر شيء أخرجه الشيخان من حديث أنس دعا رسول الله ﭬ على الذين قتلوا أصحاب بئر معونة ثلاثين صباحا الحديث وفي رواية لهما قنت شهرا يدعو على رعل وذكوان الحديث ولهما من حديث أبي هريرة وكان يقول حين يفرغ من صلاة الفجر من القراءة ويكبر ويرفع رأسه الحديث اللهم العن لحيان ورعلا الحديث وفيه ثم بلغنا أنه ترك ذلك لما أنزل الله ليس لك من الأمر شيء بلفظ مسلم.
3:128.english: Hadith: He (the Prophet) used to curse those who killed the companions of Bi'r Ma'una in his supplication (Qunut) for a month, then the saying of the Exalted descended: 'Not for you is any part of the matter (لَيْسَ لَكَ مِنَ الْأَمْرِ شَيْءٌ)'. It was extracted by the two Sheikhs (Al-Bukhari and Muslim) from the hadith of Anas: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ supplicated against those who killed the companions of Bi'r Ma'una for thirty mornings. The hadith. And in a narration of both of them: He supplicated for a month, invoking against Ri'l and Dhakwan. The hadith. And for both of them from the hadith of Abu Huraira: And he used to say when he finished from the recitation of the Fajr prayer and said takbir and raised his head. The hadith: O Allah, curse Lihyan and Ri'l. The hadith. And in it: Then it reached us that he abandoned that when Allah revealed: 'Not for you is any part of the matter (لَيْسَ لَكَ مِنَ الْأَمْرِ شَيْءٌ)' in the wording of Muslim.
3:128.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

3:129.arabic: وثلاث آيات من آخر سورة البقرة من قوله لله ما في السموات وما في الأرض إلى آخرها
3:129.english: And three verses from the end of Surah Al-Baqarah from His saying 'To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth' to its end.
3:129.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Book of Knowledge'

3:130.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
3:130.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Whatever is in the Quran of 'O you who have believed' is in the Torah 'O you poor ones (al-Masakin)'.
3:130.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

3:131.arabic: وقال تعالى: ﴿ واتقوا النار التي أعدت للكافرين ﴾{}
3:131.english: And He, the Exalted, said: 'And fear the Fire (Nār) which has been prepared for the disbelievers (Kāfirīn).'
3:131.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Fear and Hope'

3:133.arabic: الأصل السادس: أن الجنة والنار مخلوقتان قال الله تعالى: ﴿ وسارعوا إلى مغفرة من ربكم وجنة عرضها السموات والأرض أعدت للمتقين ﴾ {} فقوله تعالى أعدت دليل على أنها مخلوقة فيجب إجراؤه على الظاهر إذ لا استحالة فيه ولا يقال لا فائدة في خلقهما قبل يوم الجزاء لأن الله تعالى: ﴿ لا يسأل عما يفعل وهم يسألون ﴾ {}.
3:133.english: The Sixth Foundation: That Paradise (Jannah) and Hellfire (Nar) are created. Allah the Exalted said: 'And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise (Jannah) whose width is the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous (Muttaqin).' So His statement 'prepared' is evidence that it is created, and it must be taken according to its apparent meaning since there is no impossibility in it. And it should not be said there is no benefit in creating them before the Day of Recompense because Allah the Exalted: 'He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned.'
3:133.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

3:134.arabic: والمطلوب في صفة الغضب حسن الحمية وذلك بأن يخلو عن التهور وعن الجبن جميعاً. وبالجملة أن يكون في نفسه قوياً ومع قوته منقاداً للعقل. ولذلك قال الله تعالى "أشداء على الكفار رحماء بينهم" وصفهم بالشدة وإنما تصدر الشدة عن الغضب ولو بطل الغضب لبطل الجهاد. وكيف يقصد قلع الشهوة والغضب بالكلية والأنبياء عليهم السلام لم ينفكوا عن ذلك، إذ قال ﭬ "إنما أنا بشر أغضب كما يغضب البشر". "وكان إذا تكلم بين يديه بما يكرهه يغضب حتى تحمر وجنتاه ولكن لا يقول إلا حقاً فكان عليه السلام لا يخرجه غضب عن الحق" وقال تعالى "وا
3:134.english: And what is required in the attribute of anger is good zeal, such that it is free from recklessness and cowardice altogether. In summary, that one be strong in his Soul (Nafs) and with his strength submissive to the intellect. Therefore, Allah the Exalted said, "Severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves." He described them with severity, and severity indeed issues from anger, and if anger were nullified, jihad would be nullified. How can one intend to uproot desire and anger completely when the Prophets, peace be upon them, were not free from that, as He (the Prophet) said, "I am only a human; I get angry as humans get angry." "And when something he disliked was said in his presence, he would get angry until his cheeks reddened, but he would only speak truth, so peace be upon him, his anger would not take him away from truth." And Allah the Exalted said, "And those who restrain anger and pardon the people." And He did not say, "And those who lack anger." So return anger and desire to the limit of moderation such that neither of them overpowers the intellect nor overcomes it, but rather the intellect is the regulator for them and the dominant over them is possible, and that is what is meant by changing the character, for sometimes desire may dominate a person such that his intellect is not strong enough to repel it, so he proceeds to indulgence in abominations. And through spiritual discipline (Riyada) it returns to the limit of moderation, so that indicates that it is possible, and experience and observation indicate that with an indication in which there is no doubt.
3:134.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

3:134.arabic: وقوله والكاظمين الغيظ والعافين عن الناس والله يحب المحسنين وقوله اجتنبوا كثيرا من الظن إن بعض الظن إثم ولا تجسسوا ولا يغتب بعضكم بعضا ولما كسرت رباعيته وشج يوم أحد فجعل الدم يسيل على وجهه وهو يمسح الدم ويقول كيف يفلح قوم خضبوا وجه نبيهم بالدم وهو يدعوهم إلى ربهم حديث كسرت رباعيته صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم أحد الحديث في نزول ليس لك من الأمر شيء أخرجه مسلم من حديث أنس وذكره البخاري تعليقا فأنزل الله تعالى ليس لك من الأمر شيء تأديبا له على ذلك وأمثال هذه التأديبات في القرآن لا تحصر وهو صلى الله عليه و
3:134.english: And His saying: 'And those who restrain anger (Al-Kazimīn al-Ghayz) and pardon people (Al-ʿĀfīn ʿan al-Nās) - and Allah loves the doers of good (Al-Muḥsinīn).' And His saying: 'Avoid much of suspicion, for indeed some suspicion is sin. And do not spy or backbite one another.' And when his incisor was broken and he was wounded on the day of Uhud, and the blood was flowing on his face while he was wiping the blood and saying: 'How can a people succeed who stain the face of their Prophet with blood while he is calling them to their Lord?' The hadith of his incisor being broken, peace and blessings be upon him, on the day of Uhud - the hadith concerning the revelation of 'Not for you is the decision' - Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Anas, and Bukhari mentioned it in a suspended form. So Allah the Exalted revealed 'Not for you is the decision' as an admonition (Taʾdīb) to him regarding that. And similar such admonitions (Taʾdībāt) in the Quran are innumerable. And he, peace and blessings be upon him, is the primary intended one for admonition (Taʾdīb) and refinement (Tahdhīb). Then from him, the light shines upon all creation. For he was refined (Uddiba) by the Quran and refined (Uddiba) creation through it. And for that reason he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'I was sent to perfect noble character traits (Makārim al-Akhlāq).' The hadith 'I was sent to perfect noble character traits' - Ahmad, Al-Hakim, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated it from the hadith of Abu Hurairah. Al-Hakim said: 'It is authentic according to the conditions of Muslim.' And it has preceded in the etiquettes of companionship. Then he encouraged creation towards beautiful character traits (Maḥāsin al-Akhlāq) with what we have presented in the book 'The Training of the Soul (Riyāḍat al-Nafs) and the Refinement of Character Traits (Tahdhīb al-Akhlāq),' so we do not repeat it. Then when Allah the Exalted perfected his creation, He praised him, saying: 'And indeed, you are of a great moral character (ʿAlā Khuluq ʿAẓīm).' So glory be to Him, how magnificent is His affair and how complete is His favor. Then look at the vastness of His gentleness and the greatness of His grace, how He gave...
3:134.book_title: Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character
3:134.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character'

3:135.arabic:
(فضيلة الاستغفار)
   قال عز وجل: ﴿  والذين  إذا  فعلوا  فاحشة  أو  ظلموا  أنفسهم  ذكروا  الله
فاستغفروا لذنوبهم ﴾ {} وقال علقمة والأسود قال عبد الله  بن  مسعود  رضي  الله
عنهم في كتاب الله عز وجل آيتان ما أذنب عبد ذنبا فقرأهما واستغفر الله عز  وجل
إلا غفر الله تعالى له: ﴿ والذين إذا فعلوا فاحشة أو ظلموا أنفسهم ﴾  {}  الآية
وقوله عز وجل: ﴿ ومن يعمل سوءا أو يظلم به  ثم  يستغفر  الله  يجد  الله  غفورا
رحيما ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل: ﴿  فسبح بحمد ربك واستغفره إنه كان توابا  ﴾
3:135.english:
(The Virtue of Seeking Forgiveness)
   The Mighty and Majestic said: "And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins" (Quran 3:135). And 'Alqamah and Al-Aswad said: 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with them, said: In the Book of Allah the Mighty and Majestic are two verses; no servant commits a sin then recites them and seeks forgiveness from Allah the Mighty and Majestic except that Allah the Exalted forgives him: "And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves" (Quran 3:135) the verse, and His saying the Mighty and Majestic: "And whoever does evil or wrongs himself then seeks forgiveness from Allah will find Allah Forgiving, Merciful" (Quran 4:110). And the Mighty and Majestic said: "So glorify with praise of your Lord and seek His forgiveness; indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance" (Quran 110:3). And the Exalted said: "And those who seek forgiveness in the pre-dawn hours" (Quran 3:17). And he (the Prophet) would frequently say: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and with Your praise. O Allah, forgive me; indeed, You are the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful." And he (the Prophet) said: "Whoever increases in seeking forgiveness, Allah the Mighty and Majestic makes for him from every worry an opening and from every difficulty a way out and provides for him from where he does not expect." And he (the Prophet) said: "Indeed, I seek forgiveness from Allah the Exalted and repent to Him seventy times a day." This despite that he (the Prophet) was forgiven what preceded of his sin and what followed. And he (the Prophet) said: "Indeed, a covering comes over my heart (Qalb) until indeed I seek forgiveness from Allah the Exalted one hundred times a day." And he (the Prophet) said: "Whoever says when he goes to his bed: 'I seek forgiveness from Allah the Great, there is no deity except Him, the Living, the Sustainer, and I repent to Him' three times, Allah forgives him his sins even if they were like the foam of the sea or the number of sand of 'Alaj or the number of leaves of trees or the number of days of the world." And he (the Prophet) said in another narration: "Whoever says that, his sins are forgiven even if he was fleeing from the battle." And Hudhayfah said: I was sharp-tongued toward my family, so I said: O Messenger of Allah, I have feared that my tongue will enter me into the Fire. So the Prophet said:
3:135.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith

3:135.arabic: وقال عليّ رضي الله عنه كنت رجلا إذا سمعت من رسول الله ﷺ حديثا نفعني الله عز وجل بما شاء أن ينفعني منه وإذا حدثني أحد من أصحابه استحلفته فإذا حلف صدقته قال وحدثني أبو بكر وصدق أبو بكر رضي الله عنه قال سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول: (ما من عبد يذنب ذنبا فيحسن الطهور ثم يقوم فيصلي ركعتين ثم يستغفر الله عز وجل إلا غفر له ثم تلا قوله عز وجل: ﴿ والذين إذا فعلوا فاحشة أو ظلموا أنفسهم ذكرُوا الله فاستغفروا لذنوبهم ومن يغفر الذنوب إلا الله ولم يُصِرُّوا على ما فعلوا وهم يعلمون ﴾ الآية.
3:135.english: And Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: I was a man who, when I heard a hadith from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), Allah (Exalted and Glorified) benefited me with what He willed to benefit me from it, and when one of his companions narrated to me, I would ask him to swear an oath, and if he swore, I would believe him. He said: And Abu Bakr narrated to me, and Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) spoke truthfully. He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: 'There is no servant who commits a sin, then performs purification well, then stands and prays two rak'ahs, then seeks forgiveness (istighfar) from Allah (Exalted and Glorified), except that He forgives him.' Then he recited His (Exalted and Glorified) saying: 'And those who, when they commit an immorality (fahisha) or wrong (zulm) themselves, remember (dhikr) Allah and seek forgiveness (istighfar) for their sins—and who can forgive sins except Allah?—and do not persist in what they have done while they know.' The verse.
3:135.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith

3:135.arabic: قال عز وجل: ﴿ والذين إذا فعلوا فاحشة أو ظلموا أنفسهم ذكروا الله فاستغفروا لذنوبهم ﴾ {} وقال علقمة والأسود قال عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنهم في كتاب الله عز وجل آيتان ما أذنب عبد ذنبا فقرأهما واستغفر الله عز وجل إلا غفر الله تعالى له: ﴿ والذين إذا فعلوا فاحشة أو ظلموا أنفسهم ﴾ {} الآية
3:135.english: The Exalted said: 'And those who, when they commit an indecency (fahisha) or wrong (zalamu) their souls (anfusihim), remember (dhakaru) Allah and seek forgiveness (istaghfaru) for their sins' {} And 'Alqamah and Al-Aswad said: 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with them, said: In the Book of Allah the Exalted are two verses: No servant commits a sin, then recites them and seeks forgiveness (istaghfar) from Allah the Exalted, except that Allah the Exalted forgives him: 'And those who, when they commit an indecency (fahisha) or wrong (zalamu) their souls (anfusihim)' {} The verse.
3:135.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith

3:138.arabic: والقرآن مصرح بأن التقوى مفتاح الهداية والكشف وذلك علم من غير تعلم وقال الله تعالى وما خلق الله في السموات والأرض لآيات لقوم يتقون خصصها بهم وقال تعالى هذا بيان للناس وهدى وموعظة للمتقين وكان أبو يزيد وغيره يقول ليس العالم الذي يحفظ من كتاب فإذا نسي ما حفظه صار جاهلا إنما العالم الذي يأخذ علمه من ربه أي وقت شاء بلا حفظ ولا درس وهذا هو العلم الرباني وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى وعلمناه من لدنا علما مع أن كل علم من لدنه ولكن بعضها بوسائط تعليم الخلق فلا يسمى ذلك علما لدنيا بل اللدني الذي ينفتح في سر ا
3:138.english: And the Quran declares that God-consciousness (Taqwa) is the key to guidance and unveiling, and that is knowledge without learning. And Allah the Exalted said: 'And We have not created the heavens and the earth and what is between them except in truth and for a specified term. But those who disbelieve, from that of which they are warned, are turning away.' (46:3) He specified it for them. And He said: 'This is a clear statement for mankind and a guidance and an admonition for the God-conscious (Mut-taqeen).' And Abu Yazid and others used to say: 'The knowledgeable one is not he who memorizes from a book, for if he forgets what he memorized, he becomes ignorant. Rather, the knowledgeable one is he who takes his knowledge from his Lord whenever he wills, without memorization or study.' And this is the divine knowledge (Al-'Ilm Ar-Rabbani), and to it points His saying: 'And We taught him from Us a knowledge.' (18:65) Although all knowledge is from Him, but some of it is through the intermediaries of teaching the creation, so that is not called divine knowledge (Ladunni). Rather, the divine (Ladunni) is that which opens in the secret of the heart (Sirr Al-Qalb) without a customary cause from the outside.
3:138.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

3:138.arabic: وإذا قصد بالخطاب جميع الناس فقد قصد الآحاد فهذا القارىء الواحد مقصود فما له ولسائر الناس فليقدر أنه المقصود قال الله تعالى ﴿ وأوحى إليّ هذا القرآن لأنذركم به ومن بلغ ﴾ {} قال محمد بن كعب القرظي من بلغه القرآن فكأنما كلمه الله وإذا قدر ذلك لم يتخذ دراسة القرآن عمله بل يقرؤه كما يقرأ العبد كتاب مولاه الذي كتبه إليه ليتأمله ويعمل بمقتضاه. ولذلك قال بعض العلماء: هذا القرآن رسائل أتتنا من قبل ربنا عز وجل بعهوده نتدبرها في الصلوات ونقف عليها في الخلوات وننفذها في الطاعات والسنن المتبعات. وكان مالك بن
3:138.english: And if the address is intended for all people, then the individuals are intended, so this single reader is intended, and what is for him and for all other people, let him consider that he is the intended one. Allah the Exalted said: 'And this Quran was revealed to me that I may warn you thereby and whoever it reaches' {}. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: Whoever the Quran reaches him, it is as if Allah has spoken to him. And if he considers that, he does not take studying the Quran as his work, but he reads it as the servant reads the book of his Master (Mawla) which He wrote to him to contemplate it and act according to its requirement. Therefore, some scholars said: This Quran is messages that came to us from our Lord (Rabb) the Exalted with His covenants; we ponder them in the prayers (Salawat) and stand upon them in the seclusions (Khalawat) and implement them in the acts of obedience (Tā'āt) and the followed traditions (Sunnan). And Malik ibn Dinar said: What has the Quran planted in your hearts (Qulūb), O people of the Quran? Indeed, the Quran is the spring (Rabi') of the believer (Mu'min) just as the rain is the spring of the earth. And Qatada said: No one sits with this Quran except he rises with an increase or decrease. Allah the Exalted said: 'It is healing (Shifā') and mercy (Rahma) for the believers (Mu'minīn) and it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss' {}. The eighth: Being affected (Ta'thīr) is that his heart (Qalb) is affected by different effects according to the difference of the verses, so he has a state (Hāl) according to each understanding. And a feeling (Wajd) that his heart (Qalb) is characterized by from sadness (Huzn), fear (Khawf), hope (Rajā'), and other than that, and whenever his knowledge is perfected, awe (Khashya) is the most prevalent of the states (Ahwāl) upon his heart (Qalb), for restriction (Tadhyīq) is prevalent in the verses of the Quran.
3:138.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

3:139.arabic: وقد قال تعالى وأنتم الأعلون إن كنتم مؤمنين تفضيلا للمؤمنين على المسلمين والمراد به المؤمن العارف دون المقلد وقال عز وجل يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات فأراد ههنا بالذين آمنوا الذين صدقوا من غير علم وميزهم عن الذين أوتوا العلم ويدل ذلك على أن اسم المؤمن يقع على المقلد وإن لم يكن تصديقه عن بصيرة وكشف
3:139.english: And Allah the Exalted has said: 'And you are the superior ones if you are believers' as a preference for the believers over the Muslims, and what is intended by it is the believing knower (al-Mu'min al-'Arif) not the imitator (al-Muqallid). And He the Mighty and Majestic said: 'Allah raises those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge by degrees.' So He intended here by 'those who have believed' those who have verified/affirmed (Sadaqu) without knowledge, and distinguished them from those who were given knowledge. And that indicates that the name 'believer' (al-Mu'min) applies to the imitator even if his verification/affirmation (Tasdiq) is not from insight (Bassirah) and unveiling (Kashf).
3:139.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

3:144.arabic: فجاء ودخل على رسول الله ﷺ فنظر إليه ثم أكب عليه فقبله ثم قال بأبي أنت وأمي يا رسول الله ما كان الله تعالى ليذيقك الموت مرتين فقد والله توفي رسول الله ﷺ ثم خرج إلى الناس فقال أيها الناس من كان يعبد محمدا فإن محمدا قد مات ومن كان يعبد رب محمد فإنه حى لا يموت قال الله تعالى: ﴿ وما محمد إلا رسول قد خلت من قبله الرسل أفإن مات أو قتل انقلبتم على أعقابكم ﴾ {}[75]) الآية فكأن الناس لم يسمعوا هذه الآية إلا يومئذ
3:144.english: Then he came and entered upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), looked at him, then leaned over him and kissed him, then said: 'May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of Allah, Allah the Exalted would not make you taste death twice. By Allah, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) has indeed passed away.' Then he went out to the people and said: 'O people, whoever worshipped Muhammad, then Muhammad has died. And whoever worshipped the Lord of Muhammad, then He is Living (Haiy) and does not die.' Allah the Exalted said: 'And Muhammad is not but a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. So if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels?' (Quran 3:144) {}[75]) The verse. It was as if the people had not heard this verse except on that day.
3:144.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

3:147.arabic: ربنا اغفر لنا ذنوبنا وإسرافنا في أمرنا وثبت أقدامنا وانصرنا على القوم الكافرين
3:147.english: Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excess in our matter and make firm our feet and grant us victory over the disbelieving people.
3:147.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

3:149.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
3:149.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Whatever is in the Quran of 'O you who have believed' is in the Torah 'O you who are poor (al-Masakin)'.
3:149.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

3:152.arabic: قال ابن مسعود رحمه الله: قال لي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " أنت منهم " - يعني من القليل - قال: وما عرفت فينا من يحب الدنيا حتى نزل قوله تعالى " منكم من يريد الدنيا ومنكم من يريد الآخرة"[75]. واعلم أن ليس من الزهد ترك المال وبذله على سبيل السخاء والفتوة وعلى سبيل استمالة القلوب وعلى سبيل الطمع، فذلك كله من محاسن العادات ولكن لا مدخل لشيء منه في العبادات؛ وإنما الزهد أن تترك الدنيا لعلمك بحقارتها بالإضافة إلى نفاسة الآخرة؛ فأما كل نوع من الترك فإنه يتصور ممن لا يؤمن بالآخرة، فذلك قد يكون مروءة
3:152.english: Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to me: "You are among them" - meaning among the few - he said: And I did not recognize among us anyone who loved the worldly life until His saying, the Exalted, was revealed: "Among you are those who desire the worldly life and among you are those who desire the Hereafter"[75]. And know that it is not from asceticism (Zuhd) to abandon wealth and spend it on the basis of generosity (Sakhā') and chivalry (Futuwwa) and on the basis of winning over hearts (Qulūb) and on the basis of greed (Tama'), for all of that is from the beauties of habits but there is no entry for any of it into acts of worship (ʿIbādāt); rather, asceticism (Zuhd) is that you abandon the worldly life due to your knowledge of its insignificance in comparison to the preciousness of the Hereafter; as for every type of abandonment, it can be imagined from one who does not believe in the Hereafter, so that may be manliness (Murū'a), chivalry (Futuwwa), generosity (Sakhā'), and good character, but it is not asceticism (Zuhd) since good remembrance (Dhikr) and the inclination of hearts (Qulūb) are from the shares of the immediate life and it is more delightful and more pleasant than wealth, and just as abandoning wealth on the basis of peace (Silm) out of greed (Tama') for compensation is not from asceticism (Zuhd), similarly abandoning it out of greed (Tama') for remembrance (Dhikr) and praise and fame for chivalry (Futuwwa) and generosity (Sakhā') and due to finding it burdensome because of the hardship and toil in preserving wealth. And the need to humble oneself before rulers and the wealthy is not from asceticism (Zuhd) at all, rather it is hastening another share for the soul (Nafs); rather, the ascetic (Zāhid) is one to whom the worldly life comes humbly, pure and freely, and he is capable of enjoying it without diminishment of status and ugliness of name and without loss of a share for the soul (Nafs), so he abandons it out of fear that he may become intimate with it, so he becomes intimate with other than Allah and a lover of what is other than Allah, and he becomes a polytheist in the love of Allah, the Exalted, other than Him. Or he abandons it out of greed (Tama') for the reward of Allah in the Hereafter so he abandons the enjoyment
3:152.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

3:152.arabic:
محظورات،  فإياك  أن  تثق
بوعدها في المباحات، والموثق الغليظ الذي تأخذه عليها، وأن تجربها مرة بعد  مرة
في حال القدرة، فإذا وفت بما وعدت  على  الدوام  مع  انتفاء  الصوارف  والأعذار
ظاهراً وباطناً فلا بأس أن تثق بها وثوقاً ما، ولكن تكون من تغيرها أيضاً على  حذر،
فإنها سريعة النقض للعهد، قريبة الرجوع إلى  مقتضى  الطبع  وبالجملة  فلا  أمان
منها إلا عند الترك بالإضافة إلى ما ترك فقط وذلك  عند  القدرة.  قال  ابن  أبي
ليلى لابن شبرمة: ألا ترى إلى ابن الحائك هذا لا نفتي في مسألة إلا رد علينا  -
يعني أبا
3:152.english: [75] Hadith of Ibn Mas'ud: 'I did not know that among us was one who loves the worldly life (Dunya)' - there descended His saying, the Exalted: 'Among you is he who desires the worldly life (Dunya)' - the verse. Al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah with a good chain (isnad).
3:152.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

3:156.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
3:156.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Whatever is in the Quran of 'O you who believe' is in the Torah 'O you poor ones (al-Masakin)'.
3:156.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

3:159.arabic: وقال سبحانه وتعالى: " إن الله يحب المتوكلين " وأعظم بمقام موسوم بمحبة الله تعالى صاحبه، ومضمون كفاية الله تعالى ملابسه، فمن الله تعالى حسبه وكافيه ومحبه ومراعيه: فقد فاز الفوز العظيم، فإن المحبوب لا يعذب ولا يبعد ولا يحجب. وقالت تعالى: " أليس الله بكاف عبده ". فطالب الكفاية من غيره والتارك للتوكل هو المكذب لهذه الآية. فإنه سؤال في معرض استنطاق بالحق، كقوله تعالى: " هل أتى على الإنسان حين من الدهر لم يكن شيئاً مذكوراً ". وقال عز وجل: " ومن يتوكل على الله فإن الله عزيز حكيم ". أي عزيز لا يذل من اس
3:159.english: And He, the Exalted and Majestic, said: "Indeed, Allah loves those who rely (upon Him) (Al-Mutawakkilin)." And how great is a station marked with the love of Allah, the Exalted, its possessor, and encompassed by the sufficiency of Allah, the Exalted, its companion. So whoever from Allah, the Exalted, is his sufficiency and his suffices and his lover and his protector: then he has attained the great success, for the beloved is not punished nor distanced nor veiled. And He, the Exalted, said: "Is not Allah sufficient for His servant?" So the seeker of sufficiency from other than Him and the abandoner of reliance (Tawakkul) is the one who denies this verse. For it is a question in the form of an interrogation with the truth, like His saying, the Exalted: "Has there not come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing mentioned?" And He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: "And whoever relies upon Allah, then indeed Allah is Mighty, Wise." Meaning Mighty, He does not humiliate the one who seeks refuge with Him, nor does He waste the one who clings to His side and resorts to His protection and sanctuary, and Wise, He does not fall short in managing the one who relies upon His management. And He, the Exalted, said: "Indeed, those whom you invoke besides Allah are servants like you." He clarifies that everything other than Allah, the Exalted, is a subjugated servant. His need is like your need, so how can one rely upon him? And He, the Exalted, said: "Indeed, those whom you worship besides Allah do not possess for you provision, so seek provision from Allah and worship Him." And He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: "And to Allah belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth, but the hypocrites do not understand." And He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: "He arranges the matter; there is no intercessor except after His permission." And everything mentioned in the Quran from the Oneness (Tawhid) is an alert to cutting off observation.
3:159.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

3:159.arabic: فالعلم من أعظم ما يتكبر به، ولذلك قال تعالى لنبيه عليه السلام "واخفض جناحك لمن اتبعك من المؤمنين" وقال عز وجل "ولو كنت فظاً غليظ القلب لانفضوا من حولك" ووصف أولياءه فقال "أذلة على المؤمنين أعزة على الكافرين" وكذلك قال ﭬ فيما رواه العباس رضي الله عنه "يكون قوم يقرؤون القرآن لا يجاور حناجرهم يقولون: قد قرأنا القرآن فمن أقرأ منها ومن أعلم منها" ثم التفت إلى أصحابه وقال "أولئك منكم أيها الأمة أولئك هم وقود النار"[51] ولذلك قال عمر رضي الله عنه لا تكونوا جبابرة العلماء فلا يفي علمكم بجهلكم.
3:159.english: Knowledge is among the greatest things by which one becomes arrogant, and therefore Allah the Exalted said to His Prophet (peace be upon him): 'And lower your wing to those who follow you among the believers' (Quran 26:215), and He the Almighty said: 'And if you had been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have dispersed from around you' (Quran 3:159), and He described His allies (awliya') saying: 'Humble (adhilla) towards the believers, mighty (a'izza) towards the disbelievers' (Quran 5:54). And likewise, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said in what was narrated by Al-'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him): 'There will be a people who recite the Quran, but it does not go beyond their throats. They say: We have recited the Quran, so who is more reciter than us and who is more knowledgeable than us?' Then he turned to his companions and said: 'Those are from among you, O Ummah, those are the fuel of the Fire' [Hadith 51]. And therefore, 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Do not be tyrants (jababira) of knowledge, lest your knowledge not suffice against your ignorance.
3:159.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

3:159.arabic: قال الله تعالى فيما رحمة من الله لنت لهم ولو كنت فظا غليظ القلب لأنفضوا من حولك ولقد كان يدعو أصحابه بكناهم إكراما لهم واستمالة لقلوبهم حديث كان يدعو أصحابه بكناهم إكراما لهم وإستمالة لقلوبهم في الصحيحين في قصة الغار من حديث أبي بكر يا أبا بكر ما ظنك باثنين الله ثالثهما وللحاكم من حديث ابن عباس أنه قال لعمر يا أبا حفص أبصرت وجه عم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال عمر إنه لأول يوم كناني فيه بأبي حفص وقال صحيح على شرط مسلم وفي الصحيحين أنه قال لعلي قم يا أبا تراب وللحاكم من حديث رفاعة بن مالك أن أ
3:159.english: Allah the Exalted said: 'By mercy from Allah, you were gentle (لنت) to them. And if you had been rude (فظا) and harsh-hearted (غليظ القلب), they would have dispersed from around you.' And indeed he used to call his companions by their kunyas (honorific names) honoring them and attracting their hearts (قلوبهم). The hadith: 'He used to call his companions by their kunyas honoring them and attracting their hearts' is in the two Sahih collections in the story of the cave from the hadith of Abu Bakr: 'O Abu Bakr, what do you think of two when Allah is the third of them?' And from Al-Hakim from the hadith of Ibn Abbas that he said to Umar: 'O Abu Hafs, have you seen the face of the uncle of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him?' Umar said: 'This is the first day he called me by my kunya Abu Hafs,' and he said it is authentic according to the conditions of Muslim. And in the two Sahih collections that he said to Ali: 'Get up, O Abu Turab.' And from Al-Hakim from the hadith of Rifa'ah ibn Malik that Abu Hasan found colic in his stomach so I stayed behind for him, meaning Ali. And from Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili from the hadith of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas: 'So he said: Who is this? Abu Ishaq? I said: Yes.' And from Al-Hakim from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud that the Prophet, peace be upon him, called him by his kunya Abu Abd al-Rahman, and no child was born to him, and he would give a kunya to one who did not have a kunya, so he would be called by what he gave him as a kunya. The hadith: 'He used to give a kunya to one who did not have a kunya and he would be called by what he gave him as a kunya' is reported by Al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Anas who said: 'He called me by my kunya with a vegetable I used to pick, meaning Abu Hamzah.' He said: A strange hadith. And Ibn Majah that Umar said to Suhayb ibn Malik: 'You take a kunya and you have no child?' He said: 'The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, called me by my kunya Abu Yahya.' And from Al-Tabarani from the hadith of Abu Bakrah: 'I descended.'
3:159.book_title: Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character
3:159.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character'

3:159.arabic: وقيل: خمس من الأخلاق هي من علامات علماء الآخرة مفهومة من خمس آيات من كتاب الله عز وجل الخشية والخشوع والتواضع وحسن الخلق وإيثار الآخرة على الدنيا وهو الزهد فأما الخشية فمن قوله تعالى: (إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء( (فاطر: 28) وأما الخشوع فمن قوله تعالى: (خاشعين لله لا يشترون بآيات الله ثمنا قليلا( (آل عمران: 199) وأما التواضع فمن قوله تعالى: (واخفض جناحك للمؤمنين( (الحج: 88) وأما حسن الخلق فمن قوله تعالى: (فبما رحمة من الله لنت لهم( (آل عمران: 159) وأما الزهد فمن قوله تعالى: (وقال الذين أوتوا
3:159.english: And it is said: Five character traits are from the signs of the scholars of the Hereafter, understood from five verses from the Book of Allah the Exalted: fear (Khushya), humility (Khushu'), humility/lowliness (Tawadu'), good character (Husn al-Khuluq), and preferring the Hereafter over the world, which is asceticism (Zuhd). As for fear, it is from His saying the Exalted: 'Only those fear Allah from among His servants who are knowledgeable' (Fatir: 28). And as for humility, it is from His saying the Exalted: 'Humble before Allah, not selling the signs of Allah for a small price' (Al 'Imran: 199). And as for humility/lowliness, it is from His saying the Exalted: 'And lower your wing to the believers' (Al-Hajj: 88). And as for good character, it is from His saying the Exalted: 'So by mercy from Allah, you were gentle with them' (Al 'Imran: 159). And as for asceticism, it is from His saying the Exalted: 'But those who were given knowledge said, "Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for he who has believed and done righteousness"' (Al-Qasas: 80).
3:159.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

3:160.arabic: وكل ذلك بقضاء من الله وقدر فمن يرد الله أن يهديه يشرح صدره للإسلام ومن يرد أن يضله يجعل صدره ضيقا حرجا كأنما يصعد في السماء إن ينصركم الله فلا غالب لكم وإن يخذلكم فمن ذا الذي ينصركم من بعده فهو الهادي والمضل يفعل ما يشاء ويحكم ما يريد لا راد لحكمه ولا معقب لقضائه خلق الجنة وخلق لها أهلا فاستعملهم بالطاعة وخلق النار وخلق لها أهلا فاستعمله بالمعاصي وعرف الخلق علامة أهل الجنة وأهل النار فقال إن الأبرار لفي نعيم وإن الفجار لفي جحيم ثم قال تعالى فيما روى عن نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم هؤلاء في الجنة ولا
3:160.english: And all of that is by the Decree (Qada) and Predestination (Qadar) of Allah. So whomever Allah wills to guide, He expands his chest for Islam, and whomever He wills to misguide, He makes his chest tight and constricted as if he were ascending into the sky. 'If Allah helps you, none can overcome you; and if He forsakes you, who is there after Him that can help you? And upon Allah let the believers rely.' He is the Guide (Al-Hadi) and the Misguider (Al-Mudill); He does what He wills and decrees what He intends. There is no repeller of His decree and no reverser of His judgment. He created Paradise and created for it its people, so He employed them with obedience, and He created Hellfire and created for it its people, so He employed them with disobedience. And He made known to the creation the sign of the people of Paradise and the people of Hellfire, so He said: 'Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss, and indeed, the wicked will be in a Blazing Fire.' Then He, the Exalted, said in what is narrated from His Prophet, peace be upon him: 'These are in Paradise, and I do not care, and these are in Hellfire, and I do not care.'
3:160.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

3:161.arabic: وقال تعالى يوم يبعثهم الله جميعا فينبئهم بما عملوا أحصاه الله ونسوه والله على كل شىء شهيد وقال تعالى يومئذ يصدر الناس أشتاتا ليروا أعمالهم فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره ومن يعمل مثقال ذرة شرا يره وقال تعالى ثم توفى كل نفس ما كسبت وهم لا يظلمون وقال تعالى يوم تجد كل نفس ما عملت من خير محضرا وما عملت من سوء تود لو أن بينها وبينه أمدا بعيدا ويحذركم الله نفسه وقال تعالى واعلموا أن الله يعلم ما في أنفسكم فاحذروه فعرف أرباب البصائر من جملة العباد أن الله تعالى لهم بالمرصاد وأنهم سيناقشون في الحساب ويطال
3:161.english: And He (Exalted) said: 'On the day when Allah will resurrect them all together, then He will inform them of what they did. Allah has kept account of it, while they forgot it; and Allah is Witness over all things.' And He (Exalted) said: 'On that day, the people will proceed in separate groups to be shown their deeds. So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.' And He (Exalted) said: 'Then every soul (Nafs) will be fully compensated for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.' And He (Exalted) said: 'On the day when every soul (Nafs) will find what it did of good present [before it], and what it did of evil, it will wish that between itself and that [evil] was a great distance. And Allah warns you of Himself.' And He (Exalted) said: 'And know that Allah knows what is within your souls (Anfus), so beware of Him.' So the possessors of insight (Arbab al-Basa'ir) from among the servants recognized that Allah (Exalted) is lying in wait for them, and that they will be scrutinized in the accounting and will be demanded for the atom's weights of the passing thoughts (Khatarat) and glances (Lahazat). And they realized that nothing will save them from these dangers except adhering to self-accounting (Muhasabah) and sincerity in self-observation (Muraqabah), and demanding from the soul (Nafs) in the breaths (Anfas) and movements, and accounting it for the passing thoughts (Khatarat) and glances (Lahazat). For whoever accounts his soul (Nafs) before being accounted for, his accounting on the Day of Resurrection (Qiyamah) will be lightened, and his answer will be present at the questioning, and his return and outcome will be good.
