And whoever does not account his soul (Nafs), his regrets will persist, and his pauses in the courtyards of the Day of Resurrection (Qiyamah) will be prolonged, and his evil deeds will lead him to disgrace and contempt.
3:161.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

3:161.arabic: فما الذي غركم بالله بعد أن سمعتم وعقلتم؟ "قالوا لو كنا نسمع أو نعقل ما كنا في أصحاب السعير فاعترفوا بذنبهم فسحقاً لأصحاب السعير"
3:161.english: So what deluded you about Allah after you heard and understood? "They said: If we had listened or understood, we would not have been among the companions of the Blazing Fire. So they confessed their sin, so destruction to the companions of the Blazing Fire."
3:161.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

3:163.arabic: وقد قال تعالى: ﴿ يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ لا يستوي منكم من أنفق من قبل الفتح وقاتل ﴾ {} الآية. وقد قال تعالى: ﴿ هم درجات عند الله ﴾ {} وقال ﭬ: (الإيمان عريان ولباسه التقوى[58]) الحديث وقال ﭬ: (الإيمان بضع وسبعون بابا أدناها إماطة الأذى عن الطريق) فهذا ما يدل على ارتباط كمال الإيمان بالأعمال وأما ارتباطه بالبراءة عن النفاق والشرك الخفي فقوله ﭬ: (أربع من كن فيه فهو منافق خالص وإن صام وصلى وزعم أنه مؤمن من إذا حدث كذب وإذا وعد أخلف وإذا اؤتمن خان وإذا خ
3:163.english: And Allah the Exalted has said: 'Allah will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge by degrees' (Quran 58:11). And Allah the Exalted has said: 'Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought' (Quran 57:10) the verse. And Allah the Exalted has said: 'They are degrees with Allah' (Quran 3:163). And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Faith (Iman) is naked and its garment is God-consciousness (Taqwa)' (Hadith). And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Faith (Iman) has seventy-odd branches, the lowest of which is removing harm from the road.' So this indicates the connection of the perfection of faith (Iman) with deeds. As for its connection with being free from hypocrisy (Nifaq) and hidden polytheism (Shirk), then his saying (peace be upon him): 'Four traits, whoever has them is a pure hypocrite (Munafiq), even if he fasts and prays and claims he is a believer (Mu'min): when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, when he is entrusted he betrays, and when he disputes he acts immorally' (Hadith).
3:163.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Foundations of Belief'

3:169.arabic: وهذه الحالة وما أشير بهذه الألفاظ إليه لا ينافي ذكر الله عز وجل وقال تعالى: ﴿ ولا تحسبن الذين قتلوا في سبيل الله أمواتا بل أحياء عند ربهم يرزقون فرحين بما آتاهم الله من فضله ويستبشرون بالذين لم يلحقوا بهم من خلفهم ﴾ {} الآية ولأجل شرف ذكر الله عز وجل عظمت رتبة الشهادة لأن المطلوب الخاتمة ونعني بالخاتمة وداع الدنيا والقدوم على الله والقلب مستغرق بالله عز وجل منقطع العلائق عن غيره فإن قدر عبد على أن يجعل همه مستغرقا بالله عز وجل فلا يقدر على أن يموت على تلك الحالة إلا في صف القتال فإنه قطع الطمع ع
3:169.english: And this state and what is indicated by these words does not contradict the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah, the Exalted. And Allah, the Exalted, said: 'And do not think of those who have been killed in the path of Allah as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for, rejoicing in what Allah has given them of His bounty, and they receive good tidings about those [to be martyred] after them who have not yet joined them.' The verse. And due to the nobility of the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah, the Exalted, the rank of martyrdom is elevated because what is sought is the conclusion (Al-Khatimah), and by the conclusion (Al-Khatimah) we mean bidding farewell to the world and arriving before Allah with the Heart (Qalb) immersed in Allah, the Exalted, severed from attachments to anything else. For if a servant is able to make his concern immersed in Allah, the Exalted, he cannot die in that state except in the ranks of combat, for he has severed hope from his soul (Nafs), his family, his wealth, his children, indeed from the entire world, for he desires it for his life, and he has made light in his Heart (Qalb) of his life out of love for Allah, the Exalted, and seeking His pleasure. There is no greater devotion (Tajarrud) for Allah than that, and for that reason the matter of martyrdom is elevated, and there has come regarding it virtues that are innumerable.
3:169.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith

3:169.arabic: حديث أرواح الشهداء في حواصل طيور خضر أخرجه مسلم من حديث ابن مسعود أنه سئل عن هذه الآية ولا تحسبن الذين قتلوا في سبيل الله أمواتا الآية قال أما إنا قد سألنا عن ذلك فقال أرواحهم في جوف طير خضر فلم يسم فيه النبي ﭬ وفي رواية الترمذي أما إنا سألنا عن ذلك فأخبرنا وذكر صاحب مسند الفردوس أن ابن منيع صرح برفعه في مسنده.
3:169.english: The hadith: 'The spirits (Arwah) of the martyrs are in the crops of green birds' was reported by Muslim from the narration of Ibn Mas'ud that he was asked about this verse: 'And do not think of those who are killed in the path of Allah as dead (Wala tahsabanna allatheena qutiloo fee sabeeli Allahi amwatan).' He said: 'As for us, we asked about that, and he said: Their spirits (Arwah) are in the belly of a green bird,' and he did not name the Prophet (peace be upon him) in it. And in the narration of Tirmidhi: 'As for us, we asked about that, and he informed us.' And the author of Musnad al-Firdaws mentioned that Ibn Mani' explicitly stated its elevation in his Musnad.
3:169.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication

3:173.arabic: ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله العلي العظيم وحسبنا الله ونعم الوكيل وصلى الله على محمد خاتم النبيين وآله وصحبه وسلم تسليما كثيرا[165].
3:173.english: And there is no power nor strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Most Great, and Allah is sufficient for us and He is the best Disposer of affairs (Wakil), and may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad, the seal of the prophets, and upon his family and companions, and grant them abundant peace[165].
3:173.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

3:175.arabic: فلا يكون خوف الاستقبال وقد آتاك الله قوت يومك لك ولعيالك إلا من ضعف اليقين والإصغاء إلى تخويف الشيطان، وقد قال تعالى: " فلا تخافوهم وخافونِ إن كنتم مؤمنين "، وقال عز وجل: " الشيطان يعدكم الفقر ويأمركم بالفحشاء والله يعدكم مغفرة منه وفضلاً " والسؤال من الفحشاء التي أبيحت بالضرورة، وحال من يسأل لحاجة متراخية عن يومه وإن كان مما يحتاج إليه في السنة أشد من حال من ملك مالاً موروثاً وادخره لحاجة وراء السنة، وكلاهما مباحان في الفتوى الظاهرة ولكنهما صادران عن حب الدنيا وطول الأمل وعدم الثقة بفضل الله، و
3:175.english: So fear of the future, when Allah has given you sustenance for your day for you and your dependents, is only from weakness of certainty (Yaqin) and listening to the intimidation of Satan (Shaytan). And Allah the Exalted has said: "So do not fear them and fear Me if you are believers." And He the Mighty and Majestic has said: "Satan promises you poverty and commands you to immorality (Fahsha), while Allah promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty." And asking (Sual) is from the immorality (Fahsha) that is permitted by necessity, and the state of one who asks for a need deferred beyond his day, even if it is from what is needed within the year, is more severe than the state of one who possesses inherited wealth and saves it for a need beyond the year. Both are permissible in the apparent legal opinion (Fatwa), but they stem from love of the world (Dunya), long hope (Tul al-Amal), and lack of trust in the bounty of Allah. And this characteristic is from the principal destroyers (Ummahat al-Muhlikat). We ask Allah for good success through His gentleness and generosity.
3:175.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

3:178.arabic: وهذا الغرور علاجه معرفة دلائل الكرامة والهوان إما بالبصيرة أو بالتقليد أما البصيرة فبأن يعرف وجه كون الالتفات إلى شهوات الدنيا مبعد عن الله ووجه كون التباعد عنها مقرباً إلى الله ويدرك ذلك بالإلهام في منازل العارفين والأولياء، وشرحه من جملة علوم المكاشفة ولا يليق بعلم المعاملة "وأما معرفته بطريق التقليد والتصديق" فهو أن يؤمن بكتاب الله تعالى ويصدق رسوله وقد قال تعالى "أيحسبون أن ما نمدهم به من مال وبنين نسارع لهم في الخيرات بل لا يشعرون" وقال تعالى "سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون" وقال تعالى "فتحنا ع
3:178.english: And the cure for this delusion is knowing the signs of honor and disgrace either through insight or through imitation. As for insight, it is by knowing how turning toward worldly desires distances from Allah and how distancing from them brings closer to Allah, and one perceives that through inspiration in the stations of the knowers (Al-Arifin) and the friends (Al-Awliya), and its explanation is among the sciences of unveiling and is not suitable for the science of transaction. "And as for knowing it through the way of imitation and belief," it is to have faith in the Book of Allah the Exalted and believe His Messenger. And He the Exalted has said: "Do they think that what We extend to them of wealth and children, We hasten for them in good things? Rather, they do not perceive." And He the Exalted said: "We will gradually lead them [to destruction] from where they do not know." And He the Exalted said: "We opened to them the gates of every thing until, when they rejoiced in that which they were given, We seized them suddenly, and at once they were in despair." And in the interpretation of His saying the Exalted "We will gradually lead them [to destruction] from where they do not know," it is that whenever they commit a sin, We grant them a blessing to increase their delusion. And He the Exalted said: "We only extend time for them that they may increase in sin." And He the Exalted said: "And never think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. He only delays them for a Day when eyes will stare [in horror]." And other than that from what has come in the Book of Allah the Exalted and the Sunnah of His Messenger. So whoever believes in it is freed from this delusion, for the origin of this delusion is ignorance of Allah and His attributes, for whoever knows Him does not feel secure from His plan nor is deluded by such false imaginings, and looks to Pharaoh and Haman and Korah and to the kings of the earth and what happened to them—how Allah was good to them initially then destroyed them utterly! So He the Exalted said: "Do you perceive of them anyone?" The verse.
3:178.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

3:178.arabic: فإن قلت: كيف أفرح وأرى جماعة ممن زادت معصيتهم على معصيتى ولم يصابوا بما اصبت به حتى الكفار. فاعلم أن الكافر قد خبىء له ما هو أكثر وإنما أمهل حتى يستكثر من الإثم ويطول عليه العقاب كما قال تعالى: ﴿ وَلَا يَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ خَيْرٌ لِأَنْفُسِهِمْ ۚ إِنَّمَا نُمْلِي لَهُمْ لِيَزْدَادُوا إِثْمًا ۚ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ مُهِينٌ ﴾ وأما المعاصى فمن أين تعلم أن في العالم من هو أعصى منه ورب خاطر بسوء أدب في حق الله تعالى وفي صفاته أعظم وأطم من شرب الخمر والزنا وسائر المعاصى ب
3:178.english: If you say: How can I rejoice when I see a group whose disobedience (ma'siyyah) has increased beyond my disobedience, yet they have not been afflicted with what I have been afflicted with, even the disbelievers (kuffar). Know that for the disbeliever, what is greater has been stored away, and he is only given respite so that he may increase in sin (ithm) and his punishment (iqab) may be prolonged, as Allah the Exalted said: 'And let not those who disbelieve think that Our granting them respite is good for themselves. We only grant them respite so that they may increase in sin, and for them is a humiliating punishment.' As for the disobediences (ma'asi), from where do you know that in the world there is one who is more disobedient than him? And perhaps a thought (khatir) with bad manners (su' adab) towards Allah the Exalted and His attributes is greater and more severe than drinking wine (khamr), fornication (zina), and all other disobediences with the limbs (jawarih). Therefore, Allah the Exalted said about its like: 'And you consider it trivial, while with Allah it is great.' So from where do you know that others are more disobedient than you? Then perhaps his punishment has been delayed to the Hereafter (Akhirah) and your punishment hastened in this world (Dunya), so why do you not thank Allah the Exalted for that? And this is the third aspect in thankfulness (shukr), which is that there is no punishment except that it could be imagined to be delayed to the Hereafter. The afflictions (masa'ib) of this world are consoled by other means that lighten the affliction, so its impact is lessened. The affliction of the Hereafter endures, and if it does not endure, there is no way to alleviate it through consolation, since the means of consolation are completely cut off in the Hereafter from the tormented ones. And whoever's punishment is hastened in this world is not punished a second time, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Indeed, when a servant (abd) commits a sin (dhanb) and is afflicted with hardship (shiddah) or trial (bala') in this world, Allah is more generous than to punish him a second time.' Fourth, that this affliction (musibah) and trial (baliyyah) were written for him in the Mother of the Book (Umm al-Kitab), and it was inevitable that it would reach him, and it has reached, and completion has occurred, and he has rested from some of it or all of it, so this is a blessing (ni'mah). Fifth, that its reward (thawab) is greater than it, for the afflictions of this world are paths to the Hereafter from one aspect.
3:178.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

3:180.arabic:
بيان ذم البخل

قال الله تعالى "ومن يوق شح نفسه فأولئك هم المفلحون" وقال  تعالى  "ولا  يحسبن
الذين يبخلون بما آتاهم الله من فضله هو خيراً لهم بل  هو  شر  لهم  سيطوقون  ما
بخلوا به يوم القيامة" وقال تعالى "الذين يبخلون ويأمرون الناس بالبخل  ويكتمون
ما آتاهم الله من فضله" وقال ﭬ "إياكم والشح فإنه أهلك  من  كان  قبلكم،  حملهم
على أن سفكوا دماءهم واستحلوا محارمهم"[75] وقال ﭬ "إياكم والشح  فإنه  دعا  من
كان قبلكم فسفكوا دماءهم ودعاهم فاستحلوا محارمهم ودعاهم  فقطعوا  أرحامهم"[76]
وقال ﭬ "لا يدخل الجنة
3:180.english:
Explanation of the Condemnation of Stinginess (Bakhil)

Allah the Exalted said: "And whoever is protected from the greed (Shuh) of his Soul (Nafs) - then those are the successful ones." And He the Exalted said: "And let not those who are stingy (Yabkhaloon) with what Allah has given them of His bounty think it is good for them. Rather, it is evil for them. They will be collared with what they were stingy with on the Day of Resurrection." And He the Exalted said: "Those who are stingy and enjoin upon people stinginess and conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty." And He (peace be upon him) said: "Beware of greed (Shuh), for it destroyed those before you. It drove them to shed their blood and make lawful their prohibitions." [75] And He (peace be upon him) said: "Beware of greed, for it called those before you and they shed their blood, and it called them and they made lawful their prohibitions, and it called them and they severed their ties of kinship." [76] And He (peace be upon him) said: "The stingy one (Bakhil), the treacherous one, and the betrayer of bad character will not enter Paradise." [77] And in a narration: "Nor the tyrant." And in a narration: "Nor the one who reminds of his favor." And He (peace be upon him) said: "Three destructive things: obeyed greed, followed desire (Hawa), and a person's admiration of himself." [78] And He (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, Allah hates three: the old fornicator, the stingy one who reminds of his favor, and the poor who is arrogant." [79] And He (peace be upon him) said: "The example of the spender and the stingy one is like two men upon whom are iron shirts from their chests to their collarbones. As for the spender, he does not spend anything except that it flows or becomes abundant over his skin until it conceals his fingertips. And as for the stingy one, he does not intend to spend anything except that it shrinks and clings to every ring of his throat until it takes hold of his collarbones, and he widens it but it does not widen." [80] And He (peace be upon him) said: "Two characteristics do not gather in a believer: stinginess and bad character." [81] And He (peace be upon him) said: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from stinginess, and I seek refuge in You from cowardice, and I seek refuge in You from being returned to the most despicable age." [82] And He (peace be upon him) said: "Beware of injustice, for
3:180.book_title: Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth
3:180.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

3:180.arabic: قال أبو هريرة قال رسول الله ﷺ: (من آتاه الله مالا فلم يؤد زكاته مثل له يوم القيامة شجاعا له زبيبتان يطوقه يوم القيامة ثم يأخذ بلهازمة يعنى أشدافه فيقول أنا مالك أنا كنزك ثم تلا قوله تعالى: ﴿ ولا يحسبن الذين يبخلون بما آتاهم الله من فضله ﴾ {} الآية[207])
3:180.english: Abu Hurairah reported that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever Allah gives wealth to and he does not pay its Zakat (obligatory alms), it will be made to appear to him on the Day of Resurrection as a serpent with two black spots, which will encircle him on the Day of Resurrection, then it will seize him by his cheekbones - meaning his flanks - and say: I am your wealth, I am your treasure.' Then he recited the saying of Allah the Exalted: 'And let not those who are stingy with what Allah has given them of His bounty think that it is better for them; rather, it is worse for them. They will be collared with what they were stingy about on the Day of Resurrection. And to Allah belongs the heritage of the heavens and the earth. And Allah, of what you do, is Aware.' (Quran 3:180)
3:180.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

3:182.arabic: وقال سعد بن بلال: يؤمر يوم القيامة بإخراج رجلين من النار فيقول الله تبارك وتعالى ذلك بما قدمت أيديكما وما أنا بظلام للعبيد ويأمر بردهما إلى النار فيعدو أحدهما فى سلاسله حتى يقتحمها ويتلكا الآخر ويأمر بردهما ويسألهما عن فعلهما فيقول الذى عدا إلى النار قد حذرت من وبال المعصية فلم أكن لأتعرض لسخطك ثانية ويقول الذى تلكا حسن ظنى بك كان يشعرنى أن لا تردنى إليها بعد ما أخرجتنى منها فيأمر بهما إلى الجنة.
3:182.english: And Sa'd ibn Bilal said: On the Day of Resurrection, two men are commanded to be brought out from the Fire, then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: 'That is because of what your hands have sent forth, and that Allah is not unjust to the servants (3:182).' And He commands them to be returned to the Fire. So one of them runs in his chains until he plunges into it, and the other delays. And He commands them to be returned and asks them about their action. The one who ran to the Fire says: 'I have been warned of the consequence of disobedience, so I would not expose myself to Your wrath a second time.' And the one who delayed says: 'My good expectation of You made me feel that You would not return me to it after You had brought me out from it.' Then He commands them to be sent to the Garden.
3:182.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

3:185.arabic: وعن ابن عمر أنه لما دخل أبو بكر البيت وصلى وأثنى عج أهل البيت عجيجا سمعه أهل المصلى كلما ذكر شيئا ازدادوا فما سكن عجيجهم إلا تسليم رجل على الباب صيت جلد قال السلام عليكم يا أهل البيت ﴿ كل نفس ذائقة الموت ﴾ {} الآية إن في الله خلفا من كل أحد ودركا لكل رغبة ونجاة من كل مخافة فالله تعالى فارجوا وبه فثقوا فاستمعوا له وأنكروه وقطعوا البكاء فلما انقطع البكاء فقد صوته فاطلع أحدهم فلم ير أحدا ثم عادوا فبكوا فناداهم مناد آخر لا يعرفون صوته يا اهل البيت اذكروا الله تعالى واحمدوه على كل حال تكونوا من المخل
3:185.english: And from Ibn Umar that when Abu Bakr entered the house and prayed and praised, the people of the house wailed a wailing heard by the people of the prayer place; whenever he mentioned something, they increased. Their wailing did not subside except by the greeting of a man at the door, strong-voiced, who said: 'Peace be upon you, O people of the house. "Every Soul (Nafs) tastes death." {} The verse. Indeed, in Allah is a successor for everyone and attainment for every desire and salvation from every fear. So Allah the Exalted, so hope in Him and in Him trust, so listen to Him and deny it and cut off the weeping.' When the weeping ceased, his voice was lost. One of them looked out and did not see anyone. Then they returned and wept. Then another caller called them whose voice they did not recognize: 'O people of the house, remember (Dhikr) Allah the Exalted and praise Him in every circumstance, that you may be among the sincere ones (Mukhlisin). Indeed, in Allah is consolation from every calamity and compensation for every loss. So Allah, so obey and by His command act.' Abu Bakr said: 'This is Al-Khidr and Al-Yasa, peace be upon them both, attended the Prophet ﷺ.'
3:185.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

3:185.arabic: وقال بعض الصوفية كنت أقرأ ليلة هذه الآية كل نفس ذائقة الموت فجعلت ارددها فإذا هاتف يهتف بي كم تردد هذه الآية فقد قتلت أربعة من الجن ما رفعوا رءوسهم إلى السماء منذ خلقوا
3:185.english: And some of the Sufis said: 'I was reciting one night this verse: "Every Soul (Nafs) tastes death," and I kept repeating it, when a caller called out to me: "How much you repeat this verse! You have killed four of the Jinn who have not raised their heads to the sky since they were created."'
3:185.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

3:185.arabic: وعلاج هذا الغرور إما بتصديق الإيمان وإما بالبرهان؛ أما التصديق بمجرد الإيمان فهو أن يصدق الله تعالى في قوله "ما عندكم ينفد وما عند الله باق" وفي قوله عز وجل "وما عند الله خير" وقوله "والآخرة خير وأبقى" وقوله "وما الحياة الدنيا إلا متاع الغرور" وقوله "فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا" وقد أخبر رسول الله ﭬ بذلك طوائف من الكفار فقلدوه وصدقوه وآمنوا به ولم يطالبوه بالبرهان
3:185.english: And the treatment of this deception (Ghurur) is either by verification through faith (Iman) or by proof; as for verification through mere faith (Iman), it is to verify Allah the Exalted in His saying 'What is with you will be exhausted, and what is with Allah is enduring' and in His saying, the Mighty and Majestic, 'And what is with Allah is better' and His saying 'And the Hereafter (Al-Akhirah) is better and more enduring' and His saying 'And the worldly life (Al-Hayah Al-Dunya) is nothing but the enjoyment of deception (Mata' Al-Ghurur)' and His saying 'So do not let the worldly life (Al-Hayah Al-Dunya) deceive you.' And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ informed groups of the disbelievers of this, so they imitated him and verified him and believed in him and did not demand proof from him.
3:185.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

3:185.arabic: وقد شرح الله الرجاء فقال "إن الذين آمنوا والذين هاجروا وجاهدوا في سبيل الله أولئك يرجون رحمة الله" يعني أن الرجاء بهم أليق وهذا لأنه ذكر أن ثواب الآخرة أجر وجزاء على الأعمال قال الله تعالى "جزاء بما كانوا يعملون" وقال تعالى "وإنما توفون أجوركم يوم القيامة" أفترى أن من استؤجر على إصلاح أوان وشرط له أجرة عليها وكان الشارط كريماً يفي بالوعد مهما وعد ولا يخلف بل يزيد، فجاء الأجير وكسر الأواني وأفسد جميعها ثم جلس ينتظر الأجر ويزعم أن المستأجر كريم، أفيراه العقلاء في انتظاره متمنياً مغروراً أو راجياً؟
3:185.english: And Allah has explained hope (al-Rajā') by saying: 'Indeed, those who have believed and those who have emigrated and striven in the path of Allah - those hope for the mercy of Allah.' This means that hope is more fitting for them, and this is because He mentioned that the reward of the Hereafter is a wage and recompense for deeds. Allah the Exalted said: 'A recompense for what they used to do,' and He the Exalted said: 'And you will only be given your wages on the Day of Resurrection.' Do you see that if someone is hired to repair vessels and is promised a wage for them, and the promiser is generous, fulfilling his promise whatever he promises without failing but rather increasing, and the hired worker comes and breaks the vessels and ruins all of them, then sits waiting for the wage and claims that the hirer is generous - would the people of intellect see him in his waiting as a deluded wisher or a hopeful one? And this is due to ignorance of the difference between hope (al-Rajā') and delusion (al-Ghurra).
3:185.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

3:185.arabic: وقال بعض الصالحين بينما أنا أسير في مسير لى إذ ملت إلى شجرة لأستريح تحتها فإذا أنا بشيخ قد أشرف على فقال لى يا هذا قم فإن الموت لم يمت ثم هام على وجه فاتبعته فسمعته وهو يقول كل نفس ذائقة الموت اللهم بارك لى في الموت فقلت وفيما بعد الموت فقال من أيقن بما بعد الموت شمر مئزر الحذر ولم يكن له في الدنيا مستقر ثم قال يا من لوجهه عنت الوجوه بيض وجهى بالنظر إليك واملأ قلبى من المحبة لك وأجرنى من ذلك التوبيخ غدا عندك فقد آن لى الحياء منك وحان لى الرجوع عن الإعراض عنك قم قال لولا حلمك لم يسعنى أجلى ولولا
3:185.english: And some of the righteous (Salihin) said: While I was walking on a journey of mine, I turned to a tree to rest under it, and behold, I saw an elder who had approached me. He said to me: O this one, rise, for death has not died. Then he wandered on his face, and I followed him, and I heard him saying: 'Every soul (Nafs) tastes death. O Allah, bless me in death.' So I said: And in what comes after death? He said: Whoever is certain of what comes after death, he rolls up the waistband of caution and does not have a resting place in this world (Dunya). Then he said: O You to whose face faces submit, whiten my face by looking at You, and fill my heart (Qalb) from the love (Mahabbah) for You, and save me from that reproach tomorrow with You, for indeed the time has come for me to feel shame (Hayā') from You, and it has become time for me to return from turning away from You. Rise, he said: Were it not for Your forbearance (Hilm), my term would not have accommodated me, and were it not for Your pardon ('Afw), my hope would not have expanded in what is with You. Then he departed and left me. And they recited in this meaning: A thin body, sorrowful of the heart (Fu'ād), you see him on a peak or in the valley's belly, lamenting over shameful sins, their weight disturbs the purity of sleep. If his fears stir and increase, then I call upon him: Help me, O my support, for You are knowledgeable of what I encounter, abundant in pardoning (Safh) from the slips of the servants (Ibad). And it was also said: More delightful than delighting in maidens when they approach in beautiful garments is a repentant one (Munib) fleeing from family and wealth, wandering from place to place to obscure his mention and live alone, and appearing in worship (Ibadah) with hopes. His delight is recitation (Tilawah), where is my protector (Wali) and remembrance (Dhikr) with the heart (Fu'ād) and with the tongue (Lisan). And at death, a herald (Bashir) comes to him, giving glad tidings (Yubashir) of salvation from humiliation, so he attains what he desired and what he wished for from comforts in the chambers of the Gardens (Jinan). And Karaz ibn Wabrah used to complete the Quran three times every day and struggle his soul (Nafs) in worship (Ibadah) to the utmost of struggle (Mujahadah). It was said to him: You have exhausted your soul (Nafs). He said: How much...
3:185.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

3:186.arabic: وقال تعالى: ﴿ ولتسمعن من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم ومن الذين أشركوا أذى كثيرا وإن تصبروا وتتقوا فإن ذلك من عزم الأمور ﴾ {} أي تصبروا عن المكافأة ولذلك مدح الله تعالى العافين عن حقوقهم في القصاص وغيره فقال تعالى: ﴿ وإن عاقبتم فعاقبوا بمثل ما عوقبتم به ولئن صبرتم لهو خير الصابرين ﴾ {}.
3:186.english: And Allah the Exalted said: 'You will certainly hear much harm from those who were given the Book before you and from those who associate partners (with Allah), but if you are patient (Sabr) and guard (Taqwa) against evil, indeed that is from the matters of determination.' Meaning: you are patient (Sabr) about retaliation. And for that reason, Allah the Exalted praised those who pardon regarding their rights in retaliation (Qisas) and other matters, as He said: 'And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were afflicted. But if you are patient (Sabr) - it is better for those who are patient (Sabr).'
3:186.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

3:187.arabic: أما الآيات: فقوله عز وجل: ﴿ولينذروا قومهم إذا رجعوا إليهم لعلهم يحذرون﴾ ( سورة التوبة: الآية 122) والمراد هو التعليم والإرشاد وقوله تعالى: ﴿وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب ليبيننه للناس ولا يكتمونه﴾ ( سورة آل عمران: الآية 187) وهو إوجاب للتعليم وقوله تعالى: ﴿وإن فريقا منهم ليكتمون الحق وهم يعلمون﴾ ( سورة البقرة: الآية 146) وهو تحريم للكتمان كما قال تعالى في الشهادة: ﴿ومن يكتمها فإنه آثم قلبه﴾ ( سورة البقرة: الآية 283)
3:187.english: As for the verses: The saying of the Almighty: 'And to warn their people when they return to them that they might be cautious' (Surah At-Tawbah: Verse 122) and the intended meaning is teaching and guidance, and His saying, the Exalted: 'And [mention] when Allah took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture that they must make it clear to the people and not conceal it' (Surah Āl 'Imrān: Verse 187) and it is an obligation for teaching, and His saying, the Exalted: 'And indeed, a party among them conceal the truth while they know [it]' (Surah Al-Baqarah: Verse 146) and it is a prohibition of concealment as He, the Exalted, said regarding testimony: 'And whoever conceals it, then indeed, he is sinful in his heart (Qalb)' (Surah Al-Baqarah: Verse 283).
3:187.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

3:187.arabic: والمعرض عن العمل به أريد بقوله عز وجل ﴿ فنبذوه وراء ظهورهم واشتروا به ثمنا قليلا فبئس ما يشترون ﴾ {} ولذلك قال رسول الله ﭬ: (اقرءوا القرآن ما ائتلفت عليه قلوبكم ولانت له جلودكم فإذا اختلفتم فلستم تقرءونه وفي بعضها فإذا اختلفتم فقوموا عنه[43])
3:187.english: And the one who turns away from acting upon it is intended by His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'So they cast it behind their backs and purchased with it a small price. So wretched is what they purchase.' {} And therefore the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Recite the Quran as long as your hearts (Qulub) are in harmony with it and your skins become soft for it. But if you differ, then you are not reciting it, and in some versions: if you differ, then rise from it.'
3:187.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

3:187.arabic: وقد وصف الله علماء السوء بأكل الدنيا بالعلم ووصف علماء الآخرة بالخشوع والزهد فقال عز وجل في علماء الدنيا (وَإِذْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ مِيثَاقَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ لَتُبَيِّنُنَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ وَلَا تَكْتُمُونَهُ فَنَبَذُوهُ وَرَاءَ ظُهُورِهِمْ وَاشْتَرَوْا بِهِ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا( (آل عمران: 187). وقال تعالى في علماء الآخرة: (وَإِنَّ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ لَمَنْ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ خَاشِعِينَ لِلَّهِ لَا يَشْتَرُونَ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ ثَمَنًا قَلِ
3:187.english: And Allah has described the scholars of evil with consuming the worldly life through knowledge and described the scholars of the Hereafter with humility (Khushuʿ) and asceticism (Zuhd). So the Almighty said regarding the scholars of the worldly life: 'And [mention, O Muhammad], when Allah took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture, [saying], "You must make it clear to the people and not conceal it." But they threw it away behind their backs and exchanged it for a small price. And wretched is that which they purchased.' (Āl ʿImrān: 187). And He said regarding the scholars of the Hereafter: 'And indeed, among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in Allah and what was revealed to you and what was revealed to them, [being] humbly submissive (Khāshiʿīn) to Allah. They do not exchange the verses of Allah for a small price. Those will have their reward with their Lord.' (Āl ʿImrān: 199)
3:187.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Book of Knowledge'

3:187.arabic: وليس كذلك أخذ الله الميثاق على العلماء قال الله تعالى وَإِذْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ مِيثَاقَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ لَتُبَيِّنُنَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ وَلَا تَكْتُمُونَهُ فَنَبَذُوهُ وَرَاءَ ظُهُورِهِمْ وَاشْتَرَوْا بِهِ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا ۖ فَبِئْسَ مَا يَشْتَرُونَ و أعلم أن أيسر ما ارتكبت واخف ما احتملت أنك آنست وحشة الظالم وسهلت سبيل البغي بدنوك ممن لم يؤد حقا ولم يترك باطلا حين أدناك اتخذوك قطبا تدور عليك رحى ظلمهم وجسرا يعبرون عليك إلى بلائهم وسلما يصعدون فيه إلى ضلالهم ويدخلون بك الشك على العلماء ويصا
3:187.english: And it is not like that, Allah took the covenant upon the scholars. Allah the Exalted said: 'And [mention, O Muhammad], when Allah took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture, [saying], "You must make it clear to the people and not conceal it." But they threw it away behind their backs and exchanged it for a small price. And wretched is that which they purchased.' And know that the easiest of what you have committed and the lightest of what you have borne is that you have comforted the loneliness of the oppressor and facilitated the path of transgression by your proximity to one who has not fulfilled a right nor abandoned falsehood. When they brought you near, they made you a pivot (Qutb) around which the millstone of their oppression revolves, and a bridge (Jisr) over which they cross to their calamity, and a ladder (Sullam) upon which they ascend to their misguidance. And they introduce doubt through you upon the scholars, and they trap with you the hearts (Qulub) of the ignorant. How little they have built in comparison to what they have destroyed upon you, and how much they have taken from you in what they have corrupted for you of your religion. So what assures you that you are not among those about whom Allah the Exalted said concerning them: 'But there came after them successors who neglected prayer...' [Quran 19:59]? And you are dealing with One who does not ignore and who preserves upon you One who does not neglect. So treat your religion, for sickness has entered it, and prepare your provision, for a distant journey has arrived.
3:187.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

3:190.arabic: والشياطين والعرش والكرسي وغير ذلك ومجال الفكر في هذه الأشياء مما يضيق ويغمض فلنعدل إلى الأقرب إلى الأفهام وهي المدركات بحس البصر وذلك هو السموات السبع والأرض وما بينهما فالسموات مشاهدة بكواكبها وشمسها وقمرها وحركتها ودورانها في طلوعها وغروبها والأرض مشاهدة بما فيها من جبالها ومعادنها وأنهارها وبحارها وحيوانها ونباتها وما بين السماء والأرض وهو الجو مدرك بغيومها وأمطارها وثلوجها ورعدها وبرقها وصواعقها وشهبها وعواصف رياحها فهذه هي الأجناس المشاهدة من السموات والأرض وما بينهما وكل جنس منها ينقسم إلى
3:190.english: And the devils (Shayatin), and the Throne (Arsh), and the Footstool (Kursi), and other than that, and the field of thought (Fikr) in these things is what constricts and obscures, so let us turn to what is closer to understandings, which are the perceived things by the sense of sight, and that is the seven heavens and the earth and what is between them. So the heavens are observed with their stars, sun, moon, movement, and rotation in their rising and setting; and the earth is observed with what is in it of its mountains, minerals, rivers, seas, animals, and plants; and what is between the sky and the earth, which is the atmosphere, is perceived with its clouds, rains, snows, thunder, lightning, thunderbolts, meteors, and stormy winds. These are the observed genera from the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and every genus of them divides into species, and every species divides into sections, and each section branches into varieties, and there is no end to the branching and division of that in the difference of its attributes, forms, and apparent and hidden meanings, and all of that is a field of thought (Fikr). So not a particle moves in the heavens and the earth from inanimate matter (Jamaad), nor plant, nor animal, nor celestial sphere, nor star, except that Allah the Exalted is its mover, and in its movement is a wisdom (Hikmah) or two wisdoms, or ten, or a thousand wisdoms, all of that is a witness for Allah the Exalted to Oneness (Tawhid) and indicative of His majesty and greatness, and they are the signs (Ayat) indicating Him. And the Quran has come with urging to reflect (Tafakkur) on these signs (Ayat), as Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs (Ayat) for those of understanding (Ulul Albab).' And as He the Exalted said: 'And among His signs (Ayat) are...' from the beginning of the Quran to its end. So let us mention the manner of thought (Fikr) in some of the signs (Ayat). So from His signs (Ayat) is the human being (Insan) created from a sperm-drop (Nutfah), and the closest thing to you is your own self (Nafs), and in you are wonders indicating the greatness of Allah the Exalted that lifetimes would end in standing upon a tenth of its tenth while you are heedless (Ghaafil) of it. So O you who is heedless (Ghaafil) of his own self (Nafs) and ignorant of it, how do you aspire to know other than you when Allah the Exalted has commanded you to ponder (Tadabbur) in your self (Nafs) in His mighty Book, so He said: 'And in yourselves, do you not see?' And He mentioned that you are created from a filthy sperm-drop (Nutfah), so He said: 'Cursed is man; how disbelieving he is! From what thing did He create him? From a sperm-drop (Nutfah) He created him and destined for him; then He eased the way for him; then He causes him to die and puts him in his grave; then when He wills, He will resurrect him.' And He the Exalted said: 'And among His signs (Ayat) is that He created you from dust, then, at once, you are human beings dispersing [throughout the earth].' And He the Exalted said: 'Was he not a sperm-drop (Nutfah) from semen emitted? Then he was a clinging clot (Alaqah), and [Allah] created [his form] and proportioned [him].' And He the Exalted said: 'Did We not create you from a despised water (Maa' Mahin)? Then We placed it in a firm lodging (Qarar Makin) for a known extent.' And He said: 'Does man not consider that We created him from a sperm-drop (Nutfah)? Then at once he is a clear adversary.' And He said: 'Indeed, We created man from a sperm-drop mixture (Nutfah Amshaj).' Then He mentioned how He made the sperm-drop (Nutfah) a clinging clot (Alaqah), and the clinging clot (Alaqah) a lump of flesh (Mudghah), and the lump of flesh (Mudghah) bones, so He the Exalted said: 'And certainly did We create man from an extract of clay. Then We placed him as a sperm-drop (Nutfah) in a firm lodging (Qarar Makin). Then We made the sperm-drop (Nutfah) into a clinging clot (Alaqah)...' the verse. So the repetition of the mention of the sperm-drop (Nutfah) then...
3:190.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Contemplation'

3:190.arabic: فقال ويحك يا بلال وما يمنعنى أن أبكى وقد أنزل الله تعالى على في هذه الليلة إن في خلق السموات والأرض واختلاف الليل والنهار لآيات لأولى الألباب ثم قال ويل لمن قرأها ولم يتفكر فيها
3:190.english: He said: 'Woe to you, O Bilal, and what prevents me from crying when Allah the Exalted has revealed to me on this night: "Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding (Ulul Albab)."' Then he said: 'Woe to the one who recites it and does not reflect (Tafakkur) upon it.'
3:190.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Contemplation'

3:191.arabic: وكثر الحث في كتاب الله تعالى على التدبر والاعتبار والنظر والافتكار ولا يخفى أن الفكر هو مفتاح الأنوار ومبدأ الاستبصار وهو شبكة العلوم ومصيدة المعارف والفهوم وأكثر الناس قد عرفوا فضله ورتبته لكن جهلوا حقيقته وثمرته ومصدره ومورده ومجراه ومسرحه وطريقه وكيفيته ولم يعلم أنه كيف يتفكر وفيماذا يتفكر ولماذا يتفكر وما الذى يطلب به أهو مراد لعينه أم لثمرة تستفاد منه فإن كان لثمرة فما تلك الثمرة أهى من العلوم أو من الأحوال أو منهما جميعا وكشف جميع ذلك مهم ونحن نذكر أولا فضيلة التفكر ثم حقيقة التفكر وثمرته
3:191.english: And the urging in the Book of Allah (God) the Exalted upon contemplation (Tadabbur) and consideration (I'tibar) and observation (Nadhar) and reflection (Iftikar) is abundant, and it is not hidden that thought (Fikr) is the key to the lights (Anwar) and the beginning of insight (Istibsar), and it is the net of sciences and the trap of knowledges and understandings. Most people have recognized its virtue and rank, but they have been ignorant of its reality (Haqiqah) and its fruit (Thamarah) and its source (Masdar) and its origin (Mawrid) and its course (Majra) and its arena (Masrah) and its path (Tariq) and its modality (Kayfiyyah), and they have not known how one reflects (Yatafakkar) and in what one reflects and why one reflects and what is sought by it—is it desired for its own sake or for a fruit that is gained from it? If it is for a fruit, then what is that fruit—is it from the sciences or from the states (Ahwal) or from both together? Uncovering all of that is important, and we will mention first the virtue of reflection (Tafakkur), then the reality of reflection and its fruit, then the courses of thought and its arenas, if Allah (God) the Exalted wills. The virtue of reflection: Allah (God) the Exalted has commanded reflection and contemplation in His Mighty Book in countless places and praised the reflectors, so He the Exalted said: 'Those who remember Allah (God) standing and sitting and on their sides and reflect in the creation of the heavens and the earth: Our Lord, You have not created this in vain.'
3:191.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Contemplation'

3:191.arabic: وأثنى على المفكرين فيه فقال ويتفكرون فى خلق السموات والأرض وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ويل لمن قرأ هذه الآية ثم مسح بها سبلته حديث ويل لمن قرأ هذه الآية ثم مسح بها سبلته أى قوله تعالى ويتفكرون فى خلق السموات والأرض تقدم أى تجاوزها من غير فكر وذم المعرضين عنها فقال وجعلنا السماء سقفا محفوظا وهم عن آياتها معرضون
3:191.english: And He praised those who contemplate in it, saying: 'And they contemplate in the creation of the heavens and the earth.' And the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'Woe to the one who reads this verse and then wipes his forehead with it.' The hadith: 'Woe to the one who reads this verse and then wipes his forehead with it' means His saying, the Exalted: 'And they contemplate in the creation of the heavens and the earth'—he passed over it, meaning he went beyond it without contemplation—and He condemned those who turn away from it, saying: 'And We made the sky a protected ceiling, but they, from its signs, are turning away.'
3:191.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Contemplation'

3:191.arabic: وقال تعالى: ﴿ الذين يذكرون الله قياما وقعودا وعلى جنوبهم ﴾ {} قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: أي بالليل والنهار في البر والبحر والسفر والحضر والغنى والفقر والمرض والصحة والسر والعلانية.
3:191.english: And He, the Exalted, said: 'Those who remember Allah (Dhikr) standing and sitting and on their sides' {} Said Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: Meaning by night and day, on land and sea, in travel and residence, in wealth and poverty, in sickness and health, in secret and openly.
3:191.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God

3:191.arabic: وتقول عند النظر إلى السماء  ﴿  ربنا  ما  خلقت  هذا  باطلا سبحانك فقنا عذاب النار ﴾ {}  ﴿ تبارك الذي جعل  في  السماء  بروجا  وجعل  فيها سراجا وقمرا منيرا ﴾ {}
3:191.english: And say when looking at the sky: 'Our Lord, You did not create this in vain, glory be to You, so protect us from the punishment of the Fire' {} 'Blessed is He who placed in the sky constellations and placed in it a lamp and a luminous moon' {}
3:191.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

3:193.arabic: ربنا إننا سمعنا مناديا ينادي للإيمان إلى قوله عز وجل إنك لا تخلف الميعاد ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا ربنا إلى آخر السورة[163]
3:193.english: Our Lord (Rabbana), indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith up to His saying, the Mighty and Majestic (Qawluhu Azza wa Jall): 'Indeed You do not fail in the promise (Al-Mi'ad).' Our Lord (Rabbana), do not hold us accountable if we forget or err. Our Lord (Rabbana) to the end of the Surah.
3:193.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

3:194.arabic: ربنا آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة وقنا عذاب النار ربنا إننا سمعنا مناديا ينادي للإيمان إلى قوله عز وجل إنك لا تخلف الميعاد ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا ربنا إلى آخر السورة[163]
3:194.english: Our Lord, grant us good in this world and good in the Hereafter and protect us from the punishment of the Fire. Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith, up to His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Indeed You do not fail in the promise.' Our Lord, do not hold us accountable if we forget or make a mistake. Our Lord, to the end of the chapter.
3:194.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

3:195.arabic: ذا فشرب منه ثم قال إنا معاشر الأنبياء أمرنا أن لا نأكل إلا طيبا ولا نعمل إلا صالحا حديث سؤاله عن اللبن والشاة وقوله إنا معاشر الأنبياء أمرنا أن لا نأكل إلا طيبا ولا نعمل إلا صالحا رواه الطبراني من حديث أم عبد الله أخت شداد بن أوس بسند ضعيف وقال إن الله تعالى أمر المؤمنين بما أمر به المرسلين فقال يا أيها الذين آمنوا كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم حديث إن الله أمر المؤمنين بما أمر به المرسلين الحديث أخرجه مسلم من حديث أبي هريرة فسأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أصل الشيء وأصل أصله ولم يزد لأن ما وراء ذلك
3:195.english: Then he drank from it and said: 'We, the community of prophets, have been commanded not to eat except what is pure (tayyib) and not to work except what is righteous (salih).' The hadith of his asking about the milk and the sheep and his saying: 'We, the community of prophets, have been commanded not to eat except what is pure (tayyib) and not to work except what is righteous (salih)' - narrated by Al-Tabarani from the hadith of Umm Abdullah, sister of Shaddad bin Aws, with a weak chain. And he said: 'Indeed, Allah the Exalted commanded the believers with what He commanded the messengers, saying: "O you who believe, eat from the pure (tayyibat) things We have provided you."' The hadith: 'Indeed, Allah commanded the believers with what He commanded the messengers' - the hadith was reported by Muslim from the hadith of Abu Hurairah. So the Prophet, peace be upon him, asked about the origin of the thing and the origin of its origin, and did not add because what is beyond that is impossible, and we will explain in the Book of the Lawful and the Prohibited the place of the obligation of this question. For he, peace be upon him, would not ask about everything that was brought to him. The hadith: 'He would not ask about everything that was brought to him' - narrated by Ahmad from the hadith of Jabir that the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, and his companions passed by a woman who slaughtered a sheep for them - the hadith - so the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, took a morsel and could not swallow it, and said: 'This is a sheep slaughtered without the permission of its owners' - the hadith. And he has from the hadith of Abu Hurairah: 'When food was brought to him from other than his family, he would ask about it' - the hadith, and their chains are good. And in this is that he would not ask about what was brought from his family, and Allah knows best. Rather, the obligation is for the merchant to look at whom he deals with, so everyone attributed to oppression (zulm) or betrayal (khianah) or theft (sariqah) or usury (riba) - he should not deal with them, and likewise the soldiers (ajnad) and the oppressors (zulama) - he should not deal with them at all, nor deal with their companions and assistants because he is thereby aiding in oppression (zulm). And it was narrated from a man that he undertook the construction of a wall for a frontier of the frontiers, he said: 'Something occurred to me about that, even though that work is from the good deeds (khayrat), rather from the obligations (fara'id) of Islam, but the commander who was in charge in his place was from the oppressors (zulama).' He said: 'So I asked Sufyan, may Allah be pleased with him, and he said: "Do not be an aid to them in little or much." So I said: "This is a wall in the path of Allah (sabil Allah) for the Muslims." He said: "Yes, but the least that enters upon you is that you love their remaining so they may pay you your wage, so you have loved the remaining of one who disobeys Allah."' And it came in the report: 'Whoever prays for an oppressor (zalim) to remain has loved that Allah be disobeyed in His earth.' The hadith: 'Whoever prays for an oppressor (zalim) to remain has loved that Allah be disobeyed in His earth' - I did not find it raised (to the Prophet), but rather Ibn Abi Al-Dunya narrated it in the Book of Silence from the saying of Al-Hasan, and the author mentioned it thus correctly in the Afflictions of the Tongue. And in the hadith: 'Indeed, Allah becomes angry when the corrupt (fasiq) is praised.' The hadith: 'Indeed, Allah becomes angry when the corrupt (fasiq) is praised' - reported by Ibn Abi Al-Dunya in Silence, Ibn Adi in Al-Kamil, Abu Ya'la, and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu'ab from the hadith of Anas with a weak chain, and in another hadith...
3:195.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Earning'

3:198.arabic: وعلاج  هذا  الغرور  إما  بتصديق  الإيمان وإما بالبرهان؛ أما التصديق بمجرد الإيمان فهو أن يصدق الله  تعالى  في  قوله "ما عندكم ينفد وما عند الله باق" وفي قوله عز وجل  "وما  عند  الله  خير" وقوله "والآخرة خير وأبقى" وقوله "وما الحياة الدنيا إلا  متاع  الغرور"  وقوله "فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا" وقد أخبر رسول الله ﭬ بذلك طوائف من الكفار  فقلدوه  وصدقوه وآمنوا به ولم يطالبوه بالبرهان[3]، ومنهم من  قال:  نشدتك  الله  أبعثك  الله رسولاً؟ فكان يقول "نعم" فيصدق[4] وهذا إيمان العامة وهو يخرج  من  الغرور،
3:198.english: And the treatment of this deception (Ghurur) is either by affirmation of faith (Iman) or by proof (Burhan); as for affirmation by mere faith (Iman), it is to believe Allah the Exalted in His saying 'What is with you will be exhausted, and what is with Allah is enduring' and in His saying, the Mighty, the Majestic, 'And what is with Allah is better' and His saying 'And the Hereafter is better and more enduring' and His saying 'And the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of deception (Ghurur)' and His saying 'So let not the life of this world deceive you.' And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) informed groups of disbelievers of this, so they followed him, believed him, and had faith in him without demanding proof from him[3], and among them were those who said: 'I adjure you by Allah, has Allah sent you as a messenger?' He would say 'Yes,' so they would believe[4]. And this is the faith (Iman) of the common people, and it exits from deception (Ghurur), and this is placed in the position of a child believing his father that attending the school is better than attending the playground, even though he does not know the aspect of its being better. And as for knowledge by explanation and proof (Burhan), it is to know the aspect of corruption of this analogy (Qiyas) that the Satan (Shaytan) has organized in his heart (Qalb), for every deceived person has a cause for his deception (Ghurur), and that cause is evidence (Dalil), and every evidence (Dalil) is a type of analogy (Qiyas) that occurs in the soul (Nafs) and produces tranquility towards it, even if its possessor is not aware of it nor able to formulate it in the words of the scholars. So the analogy (Qiyas) that the Satan (Shaytan) has organized has two foundations: 'One' is that this world is cash (Naqd) and the Hereafter is credit (Nasi'ah), and this is correct; 'and the other' is his saying: Indeed, cash (Naqd) is better than credit (Nasi'ah), and this is the place of confusion (Talbis), for the matter is not so, rather if the cash (Naqd) is equal to the credit (Nasi'ah) in amount and purpose, then it is better, and if it is less than it, then the credit (Nasi'ah) is better. For the deceived disbeliever gives in his trade a dirham to take ten on credit (Nasi'ah) and does not consider that a loss, so how can he give Paradise, which is credit (Nasi'ah) in the Hereafter, for this world, which is cash (Naqd)? And this is from the greatest loss, and to this meaning Allah the Exalted alluded in His saying: 'But those who fear (Ittaqaw) their Lord, for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever, as hospitality from Allah. And what is with Allah is better for the righteous (Al-Abrar).' So He made clear that what is with Allah is better for the righteous (Al-Abrar), and the righteous (Al-Abrar) are those who fear (Ittaqaw), so whoever fears (Ittaqa) his Lord, for him is Paradise, and whoever does not fear (Ittaqa) his Lord, for him is the Fire, and this is the difference between cash (Naqd) and credit (Nasi'ah), for cash (Naqd) is this world and credit (Nasi'ah) is the Hereafter, so whoever prefers cash (Naqd) over credit (Nasi'ah) has incurred loss, and whoever prefers credit (Nasi'ah) over cash (Naqd) has gained profit, and this is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted, 'And what is with Allah is better.'
3:198.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

3:199.arabic: وقيل: خمس من الأخلاق هي من علامات علماء الآخرة مفهومة من خمس آيات من كتاب الله عز وجل الخشية والخشوع والتواضع وحسن الخلق وإيثار الآخرة على الدنيا وهو الزهد فأما الخشية فمن قوله تعالى: (إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء( (فاطر: 28) وأما الخشوع فمن قوله تعالى: (خاشعين لله لا يشترون بآيات الله ثمنا قليلا( (آل عمران: 199) وأما التواضع فمن قوله تعالى: (واخفض جناحك للمؤمنين( (الحج: 88) وأما حسن الخلق فمن قوله تعالى: (فبما رحمة من الله لنت لهم( (آل عمران: 159) وأما الزهد فمن قوله تعالى: (وقال الذين أوتوا
3:199.english: And it is said: Five character traits are from the signs of the scholars of the Hereafter, understood from five verses from the Book of Allah the Exalted: Fear (Khashyah), Humility (Khushuʿ), Humility (Tawāḍuʿ), Good Character (Ḥusn al-Khuluq), and Preferring the Hereafter over the worldly life, which is Asceticism (Zuhd). As for Fear (Khashyah), it is from His saying the Exalted: 'Only those fear Allah from among His servants who are knowledgeable' (Fāṭir: 28). And as for Humility (Khushuʿ), it is from His saying the Exalted: 'Humble (Khāshiʿīn) before Allah, they do not sell the signs of Allah for a small price' (Āl ʿImrān: 199). And as for Humility (Tawāḍuʿ), it is from His saying the Exalted: 'And lower your wing to the believers' (Al-Ḥajj: 88). And as for Good Character (Ḥusn al-Khuluq), it is from His saying the Exalted: 'So by mercy from Allah, you were gentle with them' (Āl ʿImrān: 159). And as for Asceticism (Zuhd), it is from His saying the Exalted: 'But those who were given knowledge said, "Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for he who believes and does righteousness"' (Al-Qaṣaṣ: 80).
3:199.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Book of Knowledge'

3:199.arabic: وقد وصف الله علماء السوء بأكل الدنيا بالعلم ووصف علماء الآخرة بالخشوع والزهد فقال عز وجل في علماء الدنيا (وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب لتبيننه للناس ولا تكتمونه فنبذوه وراء ظهورهم واشتروا به ثمنا قليلا( (آل عمران: 187). وقال تعالى في علماء الآخرة: (وإن من أهل الكتاب لمن يؤمن بالله وما أنزل إليكم وما أنزل إليهم خاشعين لله لا يشترون بآيات الله ثمنا قليلا أولئك لهم أجرهم عند ربهم( (آل عمران:199) وقال بعض السلف: العلماء يحشرون في زمرة الأنبياء والقضاة يحشرون في زمرة السلاطين وفي معنى القضاة
3:199.english: And Allah has described the scholars of evil with consuming the worldly life through knowledge, and described the scholars of the Hereafter with humility (Khushuʿ) and asceticism (Zuhd). So He the Exalted said regarding the scholars of the worldly life: 'And [mention, O Muhammad], when Allah took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture, [saying], "You must make it clear to the people and not conceal it." But they threw it away behind their backs and exchanged it for a small price.' (Āl ʿImrān: 187). And He the Exalted said regarding the scholars of the Hereafter: 'And indeed, among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in Allah and what was revealed to you and what was revealed to them, being humbly submissive (Khāshiʿīn) to Allah. They do not exchange the verses of Allah for a small price. Those will have their reward with their Lord.' (Āl ʿImrān: 199). And some of the predecessors (Salaf) said: 'The scholars will be resurrected in the company of the prophets, and the judges will be resurrected in the company of the rulers.' And in the meaning of 'judges' is every jurist (Faqīh) whose intention is seeking the worldly life through his knowledge.
3:199.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Book of Knowledge'

3:200.arabic: فلما انكشف لهم ذلك علموا أنه لا ينجيهم منه إلا طاعة الله وقد أمرهم بالصبر والمرابطة فقال عز من قائل يا أيها الذين آمنو اصبروا وصابروا ورابطوا فرابطوا أنفسهم أولا بالمشارطة ثم بالمراقبة ثم بالمحاسبة ثم بالمعاقبة ثم بالمجاهدة ثم بالمعاتبة فكانت لهم في المرابطة ست مقامات ولا بد من شرحها وبيان حقيقتها وفضيلتها وتفصيل الأعمال فيها وأصل ذلك المحاسبة ولكن كل حساب فبعد مشارطة ومراقبة ويتبعه عند الخسران المعاتبة والمعاقبة فلنذكر شرح هذه المقامات وبالله التوفيق.
3:200.english: When this was unveiled to them, they knew that nothing would save them from it except obedience to Allah, and He had commanded them with patience (al-sabr) and steadfast vigilance (al-murabata). So He, the Mighty Speaker, said: 'O you who have believed, be patient (asbiru) and endure patiently (wasabiru) and remain steadfast (warabitu) and fear Allah (wattaqū Allāha) that you may be successful (laʿallakum tufliḥūn).' So they made their souls (anfus) steadfast first through mutual covenanting (al-musharata), then through vigilant observation (al-muraqaba), then through self-accounting (al-muhasaba), then through self-punishment (al-muʿaqaba), then through spiritual struggle (al-mujahada), then through self-reproach (al-muʿataba). Thus, there were for them in steadfast vigilance six stations (maqamat), and it is necessary to explain them and clarify their reality and virtue and detail the works in them. The foundation of that is self-accounting (al-muhasaba), but every accounting is after mutual covenanting (musharata) and vigilant observation (muraqaba), and it is followed, upon loss, by self-reproach (muʿataba) and self-punishment (muʿaqaba). So let us mention the explanation of these stations, and with Allah is success.
3:200.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

3:200.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
3:200.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Whatever is in the Quran of 'O you who have believed' is in the Torah 'O you poor ones (al-Masakin)'.
3:200.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

4:1.arabic: وقال تعالى إن الله كان عليكم رقيبا وقال تعالى والذين هم لأماناتهم وعهدهم راعون والذين هم بشهاداتهم قائمون وقال ابن المبارك لرجل راقب الله تعالى فسأله عن تفسيره فقال كن أبدا كأنك ترى الله عز وجل وقال عبد الواحد بن زيد إذا كان سيدي رقيبا على فلا أبالى بغيره
4:1.english: And Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed Allah was over you a Watcher (Raqib).' And Allah the Exalted said: 'And those who are to their trusts and their covenant caretakers (Ra'un), and those who are with their testimonies standing (Qa'imun).' And Ibn al-Mubarak said to a man: 'Observe (Raqib) Allah the Exalted,' and he asked him about its interpretation, so he said: 'Be always as if you see Allah, the Mighty, the Majestic.' And 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Zaid said: 'If my Master is a Watcher (Raqib) over me, then I do not care about anyone else.'
4:1.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

4:4.arabic: فمن ذلك فتواهم بأن المرأة متى أبرأت من الصدق برئ الزوج بينه وبين الله تعالى، وذلك خطأ بل الزوج قد يسيء إلى الزوجة بحيث يضيق عليها الأمور بسوء الخلق فتضطر إلى طلب الخلاص فتبرئ الزوج لتتخلص منه فهو إبراء لا على طيبة نفس وقد قال تعالى "فإن طبن لكم عن شيء منه نفساً فكلوه هنيئاً مريئاً" وطيبة النفس غير طيبة القلب، فقد يريد الإنسان بقلبه ما لا تطيب به نفسه فإنه يريد الحجامة بقلبه ولكن تكرهها نفسه، وإنما طيبة النفس أن تسمح نفسها بالإبراء لا عن ضرورة تقابله حتى إذا رددت بين ضررين اختارت أهونهما فهذه مصا
4:4.english: From that is their fatwa that when a woman absolves [her husband] from the dowry (sadaq), the husband is absolved between him and Allah the Exalted, and that is an error. Rather, the husband may mistreat the wife such that he constricts matters upon her with bad character, so she is compelled to seek deliverance and absolves the husband to be rid of him. This is an absolution not upon the contentment of the soul (nafs), and Allah the Exalted has said: 'Then if they are pleased to give you any of it, take it with good cheer and wholesome.' And the contentment of the soul (nafs) is not the contentment of the heart (qalb), for a person may will with his heart what his soul (nafs) is not content with, as he wills cupping with his heart but his soul (nafs) dislikes it. Rather, the contentment of the soul (nafs) is that it permits itself the absolution not from a necessity confronting it, such that when it is turned between two harms, it chooses the lesser of them. This is, in truth, seizure with internal compulsion.
4:4.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

4:5.arabic: وسئل بعض العلماء عن شيء فلم يجب فقال السائل: أما سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: ((من كتم علما نافعا جاء يوم القيامة ملجما بلجام من نار))[140]. فقال اترك اللجام واذهب فإن جاء من يفقه وكتمته فليلجمني فقد قال الله تعالى ولا تؤتوا السفهاء أموالكم تنبيها على أن حفظ العلم ممن يفسده ويضره أولى وليس الظلم في إعطاء غير المستحق بأقل من الظلم في منع المستحق: أأنثر دّراً بين سارحةِ النَّعمِ فأصبح مخزوناً براعيةِ الغنمْ لأنهم أمسوا بجهلٍ لقدرهِ فلا أنا أضحى أن أطوقهُ البهمْ فإن لطفَ اللهِ اللطيفُ بلط
4:5.english: And some scholar was asked about something and he did not answer, so the questioner said: Have you not heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: 'Whoever conceals beneficial knowledge will come on the Day of Resurrection bridled with a bridle of fire'? So he said: Leave the bridle and go, for if one comes who comprehends and I conceal it from him, then let him bridle me. Indeed Allah the Exalted has said: 'And do not give the foolish ones your wealth' as an indication that preserving knowledge from one who would corrupt it and harm it is more important, and injustice in giving to the undeserving is not less than injustice in withholding from the deserving: Should I scatter pearls among grazing livestock, then they become stored with a shepherd of sheep? For they have become ignorant of its value, so I am not the one who will adorn the beasts with it. If the Kindness of Allah the Gentle with His kindness and I encounter people worthy of knowledge and wisdom, I will spread what is beneficial and benefit mutually; otherwise it is stored with me and concealed. For whoever grants knowledge to the ignorant ones wastes it, and whoever withholds from the deserving ones has indeed been unjust.
4:5.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Knowledge'

4:7.arabic: وكل منتبذ مسكر والحيوانات طاهرة كلها إلا الكلب والخنزير وما تولد منهما أو من أحدهما فإذا ماتت فكلها نجسة إلا خمسة الآدمي والسمك والجراد ودود التفاح وفي معناه كل ما يستحيل من الأطعمة وكل ما ليس له نفس سائلة كالذباب والخنفساء وغيرهما فلا ينجس الماء بوقوع شيء منها فيه. وأما أجزاء الحيوانات فقسمان: أحدهما ما يقطع منه وحكمه حكم الميت والشعر لا ينجس بالجز والموت والعظم ينجس. الثاني الرطوبات الخارجة من باطنه فكل ما ليس مستحيلا ولا له مقر فهو طاهر كالدمع والعرق واللعاب والمخاط وما له مقر وهو مستحيل فنجس
4:7.english: And every intoxicating drink is forbidden, and all animals are pure except the dog and the pig and what is born from them or from one of them, so if they die, all are impure except five: the human, the fish, the locust, the apple worm, and in its meaning everything that transforms from foods and everything that does not have a flowing soul (Nafs) like the fly and the beetle and others, so water is not made impure by the falling of something from them into it. And as for parts of animals, they are two categories: one is what is cut from it and its ruling is the ruling of the dead, and hair is not made impure by shaving and death, and bone is made impure. The second is the moistures exiting from its interior, so everything that is not transformed and does not have a fixed place is pure like tears, sweat, saliva, and mucus, and what has a fixed place and is transformed is impure except what is the material of the animal like semen, eggs, pus, blood, dung, and urine are impure from all animals, and nothing of these impurities, little or much, is excused except for five: The first is the trace of excrement after cleansing with stones, it is excused as long as it does not exceed the exit. The second is street mud and dust of dung on the road, it is excused with certainty of impurity to the extent that avoidance is difficult, and it is that which is not attributed to the one soiled by it to negligence or slip. The third is what is on the bottom of the shoe from impurity that the road is not free from, so it is excused after rubbing due to need. The fourth is the blood of fleas, whether little or much, except if it exceeds the limit of habit, whether it is on your garment or on another's garment and you wear it. The fifth is the blood of pustules and what separates from them of pus and matter, and Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, rubbed a pustule on his face and blood came out from it and he prayed and did not perform the major ablution (Ghusl), and in its meaning is what oozes from the stains of boils that mostly persist, and likewise the effect of bloodletting except what occurs rarely from an abscess or other, so it is attached to the blood of irregular bleeding (Istihadah) and is not in the meaning of pustules that a human is not free from in his conditions, and the leniency of the law in these five impurities informs you that the matter of purity is on permissiveness and what is innovated in it is whisperings (Waswasah) that have no basis. (The second aspect in the remover of it) It is either solid or liquid; as for the solid, it is the stone of cleansing, and it is a purifier, purification by lightening, on condition that it be hard, pure, drying, and not respected; and as for liquids, impurities are not removed by anything from them except water, and not every water, but the pure that has not become extremely changed by mixing with what is dispensed with, and water exits from purity by changing due to contact with impurity in its taste, color, or smell. If it does not change and is close to two hundred and fifty Manna, which is five hundred Ratal by the Ratal of Iraq, it is not made impure due to His saying, peace be upon him: (If water reaches two Qullahs, it does not carry filth[7]), and if it is less, it becomes impure.
4:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Purity'

4:10.arabic: وقال تعالى إن الذين يأكلون أموال اليتامى ظلما الآية وقال تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وذروا ما بقي من الربا إن كنتم مؤمنين ثم قال فإن لم تفعلوا فأذنوا بحرب من الله ورسوله ثم قال وإن تبتم فلكم رءوس أموالكم ثم قال ومن عاد فأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون جعل آكل الربا أول الأمر مؤذنا بمحاربة الله وفي آخره متعرضا للنار والآيات الواردة في الحلال والحرام لا تحصى
4:10.english: And He (Allah), the Exalted, said: 'Indeed, those who consume the wealth of the orphans unjustly, they only consume fire into their bellies, and they will burn in a Blaze.' And He, the Exalted, said: 'O you who have believed, fear Allah and give up what remains [due to you] of interest, if you should be believers.' Then He said: 'And if you do not, then be informed of a war from Allah and His Messenger.' Then He said: 'But if you repent, you may have your principal.' Then He said: 'And whoever returns to [dealing in interest] - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.' He made the consumer of interest at the beginning of the matter announcing war from Allah, and at its end exposed to the Fire. And the verses that have come regarding the lawful (Halal) and the unlawful (Haram) are innumerable.
4:10.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

4:11.arabic: وكالذي يعطش يوم عرفة أو عاشوراء أو في الأشهر الحرم فلا يشرب خوفاً من أن يعلم الناس أنه غير صائم، فإذا ظنوا به الصوم امتنع عن الأكل لأجله، أو يدعى إلى طعام فيمتنع ليظن أنه صائم وقد لا يصرح بأن صائم ولكن يقول: لي عذر، وهو جمع بين خبيثين، فإنه يرى أنه صائم ثم يرى أنه مخلص ليس بمراء، وأنه يحترز من أن يذكر عبادته للناس فيكون مرائياً فيريد أن يقال إنه ساتر لعبادته، ثم إن اضطر إلى شرب لم يصبر عن أن يذكر لنفسه فيه عذراً تصريحاً أو تعريضاً بأن يتعلل بمرض يقتضي فرط العطش ويمنع من الصوم، أو يقول أفطرت تطيي
4:11.english: And like the one who thirsts on the day of Arafah or Ashura or in the Sacred Months, so he does not drink out of fear that people will know he is not fasting, then if they assume he is fasting, he abstains from eating for that reason, or he is invited to food so he declines so that it is thought he is fasting, and he may not explicitly state that he is fasting but says: I have an excuse, and this combines two evils, for he sees himself as fasting then sees himself as sincere (Mukhlis) not being a show-off (Mura'i), and he guards against mentioning his worship to people so as not to be a show-off, so he wants it to be said that he is concealing his worship, then if compelled to drink, he cannot bear not to mention to himself an excuse explicitly or implicitly by pretending an illness that necessitates extreme thirst and prevents fasting, or says I broke my fast to please the heart (Qalb) of so-and-so, then he may not mention that connected to his drinking so as not to be thought to be excusing himself out of show-off (Riya'), but he endures then mentions his excuse in the course of a story incidentally; such as saying: So-and-so loves the brothers and has a strong desire for a person to eat from his food and he insisted on me today and I found no alternative but to please his heart. And like saying: My mother is weak-hearted (Qalb), compassionate over me, thinking that if I fasted a day I would fall ill, so she does not let me fast. This and what runs its course from the afflictions of show-off (Riya') does not come to the tongue due to the deep-rooted vein of show-off (Riya') in the inner self (Batin). As for the sincere one (Mukhlis), he does not care how the creation views him? If he has no desire for fasting and God knows that from him, then he does not want others to believe what contradicts God's knowledge so as to be a deceiver, and if he has a desire for fasting for God, he is content with the knowledge of God the Exalted and does not associate partners with Him in it, and it may occur to him that in his showing it there is others following his example and stirring people's desire in it, and in that is trickery and deception - and the explanation of that and its conditions will come -. These are the degrees of show-off (Riya') and the ranks of the varieties of show-offs (Mura'un) and all of them are under God's wrath and anger, and it is among the most severe destroyers, and indeed from its severity is that in it are impurities that are more hidden than the crawling of ants as the report has come, in it slip the leading scholars, let alone the ignorant worshippers regarding the afflictions of the souls (Nufus) and the calamities of the hearts (Qulub), and God knows best. Explanation of the hidden show-off (Riya') that is more hidden than the crawling of ants. Know that show-off (Riya') is apparent (Jali) and hidden (Khafi), so the apparent is that which motivates the action and carries it even if reward is intended, and it is the most apparent, and slightly more hidden than it is what does not carry the action by itself alone, except that it lightens the action which is intended for the face of God, like the one who is accustomed to night prayer (Tahajjud) every night and it becomes heavy upon him, then if a guest stays with him, he becomes active for it and it becomes light upon him and he knows that were it not for the hope of reward, he would not pray merely for the show-off (Riya') of the guests, and more hidden than that is what does not affect the action nor by facilitation and lightening also, but with that it is concealed.
4:11.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

4:11.arabic: أين يناسب حاله قوله تعالى يوصيكم الله في أولادكم للذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين وقوله تعالى والذين يرمون المحصنات وكذلك جميع الآيات التي فيها بيان أحكام الميراث والطلاق والحدود وغيرها وإنما المحرك لما في القلب ما يناسبه والأبيات إنما يضعها الشعراء إعرابا بها عن أحوال القلب فلا يحتاج في فهم الحال منها إلى تكلف نعم من يستولي عليه حالة غالبة قاهرة لم تبق فيه متسعا لغيرها ومعه تيقظ وذكاء ثاقب يتفطن به للمعاني البعيدة من الألفاظ فقد يخرج وجده على كل مسموع كمن يخطر له عند ذكر قوله تعالى يوصيكم الله في أولادكم
4:11.english: Where does it suit his state the saying of the Exalted: 'Allah instructs you concerning your children: for the male is like the share of two females. But if there are [only] daughters, two or more, for them is two thirds of one's estate. And if there is only one, for her is half. And for one's parents, to each one of them is a sixth of his estate if he left children. But if he had no children and the parents [alone] inherit from him, then for his mother is one third. And if he had brothers [or sisters], for his mother is a sixth, after any bequest he [may have] made or debt. Your parents or your children - you know not which of them are nearest to you in benefit. [These shares are] an obligation [imposed] by Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.' (Quran 4:11) and His saying: 'And those who accuse chaste women...' and likewise all the verses that contain clarification of the rulings of inheritance, divorce, prescribed punishments, and others. Rather, what moves what is in the Heart (Qalb) is what suits it. And the verses, the poets only place them as expression through them of the states of the Heart (Qalb), so there is no need in understanding the state from them to forced effort. Yes, whoever is overcome by a dominating, overwhelming state that leaves no room in him for anything else, and with him is alertness and penetrating intelligence through which he perceives the distant meanings from the words, then his spiritual state (Wajd) may emerge upon everything heard, like one to whom occurs upon the mention of His saying: 'Allah instructs you concerning your children...' the state of death necessitating the will, and that every human being inevitably leaves behind his wealth and his children, and they are his two beloved things from the worldly life, so he leaves one of the two beloved for the second and abandons them both, so fear and distress overcome him. Or he hears the mention (Dhikr) of Allah in His saying: 'Allah instructs you concerning your children...' so he is astonished by the mere Name from what precedes and follows it. Or occurs to him the mercy of Allah upon His servants and His compassion by undertaking the division of their inheritances Himself, looking after them in their life and their death, so he says: 'If He looks after our children after our death, then we have no doubt that He looks after us,' so from that arises the state of hope and that bequeaths him gladness and joy. Or occurs to him from His saying: 'for the male is like the share of two females' the preference of the male by him being a man over the female, and that the excellence in the Hereafter is for men whom neither commerce nor sale distracts from the remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah, and that whoever is distracted by other than Allah, the Exalted, from Allah, the Exalted, then he is from the females, not from the men, in reality, so he fears that he may be veiled or delayed in the bliss of the Hereafter as the female was delayed in the worldly wealth. So the likes of this may move the spiritual state (Wajd), but for one in whom are two descriptions: one of them is a dominating, all-encompassing, overwhelming state, and the other is profound perception and complete, perfect alertness for alerting through the near matters to the distant meanings, and that is rare. Therefore, for that reason, he resorts to singing which is words suitable for the states so that their agitation hastens.
4:11.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

4:11.arabic: وكان أرباب البصائر إذا أقبلت عليهم الدنيا حزنوا وقالوا: ذنب عجلت عقوبته ورأوا ذلك علامة المقت والإهمال، وإذا أقبل عليهم الفقر قالوا: مرحباً بشعار الصالحين. والمغرور إذا أقبلت عليه الدنيا ظن أنها كرامة من الله، وإذا صرفت عنه ظن أنها هوان، كما أخبر الله تعالى عنه إذ قال "فأما الإنسان إذا ما ابتلاه ربه فأكرمه ونعمه فيقول ربي أكرمن وأما إذا ما ابتلاه فقدر عليه رزقه فيقول ربي أهانن" فأجاب الله عن ذلك "كلا" أي ليس كما قال إنما هو ابتلاء نعوذ بالله من شر البلاء ونسأل الله التثبيت، فبين أن ذلك غرور. قال
4:11.english: And the people of insight (أرباب البصائر) when the worldly life (الدنيا) approached them, they would grieve and say: 'A sin whose punishment has been hastened,' and they saw that as a sign of contempt and neglect. And when poverty approached them, they would say: 'Welcome to the emblem of the righteous.' And the deluded one (المغرور) when the worldly life approaches him, he thinks it is an honor from Allah, and when it is diverted from him, he thinks it is humiliation, as Allah the Exalted informed about him when He said: "As for man, when his Lord tests him by giving him honor and blessings, he says, 'My Lord has honored me.' But when He tests him by restricting his provision, he says, 'My Lord has humiliated me.'" So Allah answered that with "No!" meaning it is not as he said; rather it is a test—we seek refuge in Allah from the evil of the trial and we ask Allah for steadfastness—thus He clarified that this is delusion. Al-Hasan said: He denied them both with His saying "No!" saying: 'This is not My honoring, nor is this My humiliation, but the honored one is whom I have honored with My obedience, whether rich or poor, and the humiliated one is whom I have humiliated with My disobedience, whether rich or poor.'
4:11.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'
