Therefore, there is absolutely no absolute contentment in any of the causes of deficiency in religion except from the perspective of attributing them to the action of Allah the Exalted; as for them in themselves, there is no aspect of contentment with them in any state.
4:75.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

4:77.arabic: فالحاصل أن الزهد عبارة عن الرغبة عن حظوظ النفس كلها، ومهما رغب عن حظوظ النفس رغب عن البقاء في الدنيا فقصر أمله لا محالة، لأنه إنما يريد البقاء ليتمتع ويريد التمتع الدائم بإرادة البقاء؛ فإن من أراد شيئاً أراد دوامه، ولا معنى لحب الحياة إلا حب دوام ما هو موجود أو ممكن في هذه الحياة، فإذا رغب عنها لم يردها، ولذلك لما كتب عليهم القتال " قالوا ربنا لم كتبت علينا القتال لولا أخرتنا إلى أجلٍ قريب " فقال تعالى: " قل متاع الدنيا قليل "، أي لستم تريدون البقاء إلا لمتاع الدنيا، فظهر عند ذلك الزاهدون وانكشف
4:77.english: The conclusion is that asceticism (Zuhd) is an expression of aversion to all the desires (Hawā) of the soul (Nafs). Whenever one is averse to the desires of the soul, one is averse to remaining in this world, inevitably shortening one's hope (Amal), because one only wants to remain in order to enjoy and wants permanent enjoyment through the desire for permanence; for whoever desires something desires its continuity, and there is no meaning to the love of life except the love of the continuity of what exists or is possible in this life. So when one is averse to it, one does not desire it. Therefore, when fighting was prescribed for them, "They said, 'Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us? If only You had postponed it for us for a short while.'" Then the Almighty said: "Say, 'The enjoyment of this world is little,'" meaning you do not desire to remain except for the enjoyment of this world. Thus, at that time, the ascetics (Zāhidūn) became apparent, and the condition of the hypocrites (Munāfiqūn) was exposed.
4:77.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

4:77.arabic: وإلى تعريف خساسة الدنيا الإشارة بقوله تعالى: "قل متاع الدنيا قليل" وإلى تعريف نفاسة الآخرة الإشارة بقوله عز وجل: "وقال الذين أوتوا ويلكم ثواب الله خير" فنبه على أن العلم بنفاسة الجوهر هو المرغب عن عوضه، ولما لم يتصور الزهد إلا بمعارضة ورغبة عن المحبوب في أحب منه قال رجل في دعائه: اللهم أرني الدنيا كما تراها، فقال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا تقل هكذا" ولكن قل: أرني الدنيا كما أريتها الصالحين من عبادك" وهذا لأن الله تعالى يراها حقيرة كما هي، وكل مخلوق فهو بالإضافة إلى جلاله حقير والعبد يراها
4:77.english: And to the definition of the baseness of the worldly life (al-Dunya) is the indication by His saying, the Exalted: "Say: The enjoyment of the worldly life (al-Dunya) is little." And to the definition of the preciousness of the Hereafter (al-Akhira) is the indication by His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: "And those who were given said: Woe to you, the reward of Allah is better." So He alerted that the knowledge of the preciousness of the jewel is what urges away from its exchange, and since Asceticism (al-Zuhd) cannot be conceived except by opposition and desire away from the beloved for what is more beloved, a man said in his supplication: O Allah, show me the worldly life (al-Dunya) as You see it, so the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to him: "Do not say like this," but say: Show me the worldly life (al-Dunya) as You showed it to the righteous among Your servants. This is because Allah, the Exalted, sees it as contemptible as it is, and every created being is, in addition to His Majesty, contemptible, and the servant sees it as contemptible in himself in addition to what is better for him, and it is inconceivable that the seller of the horse, even if he desires away from his horse, sees as he sees the insects of the earth, for example, because he is originally independent of the insects and is not independent of the horse, and Allah, the Exalted, is Rich (Ghani) by His Essence from everything other than Him, so He sees everything in one degree in addition to His Majesty, and sees it as varying in addition to others, and the Ascetic (al-Zahid) is the one who sees its variation in addition to himself, not to others. As for the action emanating from the state of Asceticism (al-Zuhd), it is one abandonment because it is a sale and transaction and exchange of what is better for what is lower, so just as the action emanating from the contract of sale is abandoning the sold item and removing it from the hand and taking the exchange, so
4:77.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

4:78.arabic: وقوله عز وجل ﴿ فمال هؤلاء القوم لا يكادون يفقهون حديثا ما أصابك من حسنة فمن الله وما أصابك من سيئة فمن نفسك ﴾ {} معناه لا يفقهون حديثا يقولون ما أصابك من حسنة فمن الله فإن لم يرد هذا كان مناقضا لقوله ﴿ قل كل من عند الله ﴾ {}
4:78.english: And His saying, the Exalted: 'So what is with these people, they hardly understand any speech? Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself' - its meaning is: they do not understand any speech, they say: whatever good befalls you is from Allah. If this is not intended, it would contradict His saying: 'Say: All is from Allah'.
4:78.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

4:79.arabic: وقوله عز وجل ﴿ فمال هؤلاء القوم لا يكادون يفقهون حديثا ما أصابك من حسنة فمن الله وما أصابك من سيئة فمن نفسك ﴾ {} معناه لا يفقهون حديثا يقولون ما أصابك من حسنة فمن الله فإن لم يرد هذا كان مناقضا لقوله ﴿ قل كل من عند الله ﴾ {} وسبق إلى الفهم منه مذهب القدرية
4:79.english: And His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'So what is with these people that they hardly understand any speech? Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from your own soul (Nafs).' Its meaning is: they do not understand any speech; they say: 'Whatever good befalls you is from Allah.' For if this is not intended, it would contradict His saying: 'Say: Everything is from Allah.' And the understanding that preceded from it is the doctrine of the Qadariyyah (those who deny divine decree).
4:79.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

4:80.arabic: بأبي أنت وأمي يا رسول الله لقد بلغ من فضيلتك عنده أن جعل طاعتك طاعته فقال عز وجل: ﴿ من يطع الرسول فقد أطاع الله ﴾ {} بأبي أنت وأمي يا رسول الله لقد بلغ من فضيلتك عنده أن أخبرك بالعفو عنك قبل أن يخبرك بالذنب فقال تعالى: ﴿ عفا الله عنك لم أذنت لهم ﴾ {} بأبي أنت وأمي يا رسول الله لقد بلغ من فضيلتك عنده أن بعثك آخر الأنبياء وذكرك في أولهم فقال عز وجل: ﴿ وإذ أخذنا من النبيين ميثاقهم ومنك ومن نوح وإبراهيم ﴾ {} الآية
4:80.english: With my father and mother as ransom for you, O Messenger of Allah, your excellence with Him has reached the point that He made obedience to you obedience to Him, so the Mighty and Majestic said: 'Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah' (Quran 4:80). With my father and mother as ransom for you, O Messenger of Allah, your excellence with Him has reached the point that He informed you of forgiveness for you before informing you of the sin, so the Exalted said: 'May Allah forgive you; why did you permit them?' (Quran 9:43). With my father and mother as ransom for you, O Messenger of Allah, your excellence with Him has reached the point that He sent you as the last of the prophets and mentioned you among the first of them, so the Mighty and Majestic said: 'And [mention] when We took from the prophets their covenant and from you and from Noah and Abraham' (Quran 33:7) the verse.
4:80.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith

4:83.arabic: وقال تعالى: ﴿ولو ردوه إلى الرسول وإلى أولي الأمر منهم لعلمه الذين يستنبطونه منهم﴾ رد حكمه في الوقائع إلى استنباطهم وألحق رتبتهم برتبة الأنبياء في كشف حكم الله.
4:83.english: And He, the Exalted, said: 'And if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those of authority among them, those who draw it out (yastanbitunahu) from them would have known it.' He referred its ruling in occurrences to their drawing out (istinbat) and attached their rank to the rank of the Prophets in uncovering the ruling of Allah.
4:83.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

4:83.arabic: والرابع: أنه قال عز وجل ﴿ لعلمه الذي يستنبطونه منهم ﴾ فأثبت لأهل العلم استنباطا ومعلوم أنه وراء السماع. وجملة ما نقلناه من الآثار في فهم القرآن يناقض هذا الخيال فبطل أن يشترط السماع في التأويل وجاز لكل واحد أن يستنبط من القرآن بقدر فهمه وحد عقله.
4:83.english: And the fourth: that He, the Exalted, said: 'So that those who extract it from them would know it' (Quran 4:83), thus affirming for the people of knowledge extraction (istinbāṭ), and it is known that this is beyond mere hearing. The totality of what we have transmitted from the traditions regarding understanding the Quran contradicts this illusion, so it is invalidated to stipulate hearing in interpretation (taʾwīl), and it becomes permissible for each one to extract (yastanbiṭ) from the Quran according to the capacity of his understanding and the limit of his intellect.
4:83.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

4:86.arabic: وقال تعالى وإذا حييتم بتحية فحيوا بأحسن منها أو ردوها وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم والذي نفسي بيده لا تدخلوا الجنة حتى تؤمنوا ولا تؤمنوا حتى تحابوا أفلا أدلكم على عمل إذا عملتموه تحاببتم قالوا بلى يا رسول الله قال أفشوا السلام بينكم
4:86.english: And Allah the Exalted said: 'And when you are greeted with a greeting, then greet with better than it or return it.' And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'By the One in Whose Hand is my soul (Nafs), you will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another. Shall I not guide you to a deed which, if you do it, you will love one another?' They said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Spread the greeting of peace (Salam) among yourselves.'
4:86.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

4:86.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى "وقولوا للناس حسناً" وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: من سلم عليك من خلق الله فاردد عليه السلام وإن كان مجوسياً إن الله تعالى يقول "وإذا حييتم بتحية فحيوا بأحسَن منها أو رُدُّوها" وقال ابن عباس أيضاً: لو قال لي فرعون خيراً لرددت عليه.
4:86.english: And Allah the Exalted has said: 'And speak to people goodly (words).' And Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: 'Whoever from the creation of Allah greets you with peace, then return the greeting of peace upon him, even if he is a Magian (Zoroastrian), for Allah the Exalted says: "And when you are greeted with a greeting, then greet with one better than it or return it."' And Ibn Abbas also said: 'If Pharaoh said something good to me, I would return it to him.'
4:86.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

4:89.arabic: اعلم أن المؤذي ممقوت بالطبع، ومن آذاك فلا يمكنك أن لا تبغضه غالباً، فإذا تيسرت له نعمة فلا يمكنك أن لا تكرهها له حتى يستوي عندك حسن حال عدوك وسوء حاله، بل لا تزال تدرك في النفس بينهما تفرقة، ولا يزال الشيطان ينازعك إلى الحسد له، ولكن عن قوي ذلك فيك حتى بعثك على إظهار الحسد بقول أو فعل بحيث يعرف ذلك من ظاهرهك بأفعالك الاختيارية فأنت حسود عاص بحسدك، وإن كففت ظاهرك بالكلية إلا أنك بباطنك تحب زوال النعمة وليس في نفسك كراهة لهذه الحالة فأنت أيضاً حسود عاص، لأن الحسد صفة القلب لا صفة الفعل، قال الله ت
4:89.english: Know that the one who harms is naturally hated, and if someone harms you, you cannot help but generally dislike them. If a blessing is facilitated for them, you cannot help but resent it for them until the good state of your enemy and their bad state become equal to you. Rather, you continuously perceive in the soul (Nafs) a distinction between them, and Satan continuously contends with you toward envy (Hasad) for them. But if that becomes strong in you until it incites you to manifest envy (Hasad) by word or action such that it is known from your outward appearance through your voluntary actions, then you are an envious sinner by your envy (Hasad). And if you completely restrain your outward appearance, yet in your inner self you desire the removal of the blessing and there is no aversion in your soul (Nafs) to this state, then you are also an envious sinner, because envy (Hasad) is an attribute of the heart (Qalb), not an attribute of action. Allah the Exalted said: "Nor do they find in their breasts a need of that which they have been given" and He the Mighty and Majestic said: "They wish that you would disbelieve as they have disbelieved, so you would be equal" and He said: "If good touches you, it distresses them." As for the action, it is backbiting and lying, and it is an act emanating from envy (Hasad) and is not the essence of envy (Hasad). Rather, the place of envy (Hasad) is the heart (Qalb), not the limbs. Indeed, this envy (Hasad) is not an injustice requiring seeking permission for it, but it is a sin between you and Allah the Exalted. Seeking permission is only required for the apparent causes on the limbs. So if you restrain your outward appearance and oblige your heart (Qalb) along with that to dislike what naturally emanates from it of desiring the removal of the blessing, until it is as if you detest your soul (Nafs) for what is in its nature, so that dislike is from the side of the intellect in opposition to the inclination from the side of nature, then you have fulfilled what is obligatory upon you. And in most circumstances, no more than this enters under your choice. As for changing the nature so that the one who harms and the one who benefits become equal to him, and his joy or grief for what is facilitated for them of blessing or what befalls them of affliction becomes equal, this is something that nature does not comply with as long as one is attentive to the shares of the worldly life, unless one becomes absorbed in Allah the Exalted like the intoxicated lover. Then his affair may reach the point that his heart (Qalb) does not attend to the details of the conditions of the servants, but rather looks at all with one eye, which is the eye of mercy, and sees all as servants of Allah and their actions as actions of Allah, and sees them as subjugated. And if that occurs, it is like fleeting lightning that does not last, then the heart (Qalb) returns with
4:89.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

4:89.arabic: وقال عز وجل "ودوا لو تكفرون كما كفروا فتكونون سواء" وذكر الله تعالى حسد إخوة يوسف عليه السلام وعبر عما في قلوبهم بقوله تعالى "إذ قالوا ليوسف وأخوه أحب إلى أبينا منا ونحن عصبة إن أبانا لفي ضلال مبين. اقتلوا يوسف أو اطرحوه أرضاً يخل لكم وجه أبيكم" فلما كرهوا حب أبيهم له وساءهم ذلك وأحبوا زواله عنه غيبوه عنه وقال تعالى "ولا يجدون في صدورهم حاجة مما أوتوا" أي لا تضيق صدورهم به ولا يغتمون فأثنى عليهم بعدم الحسد.
4:89.english: And the Exalted said: "They wish that you would disbelieve as they have disbelieved so you would be equal." And Allah the Exalted mentioned the envy (Hasad) of the brothers of Yusuf (Joseph), peace be upon him, and expressed what was in their hearts (Qulub) by His saying: "When they said: 'Yusuf and his brother are more beloved to our father than we, while we are a group. Indeed, our father is in clear error. Kill Yusuf or cast him out to a land so that the face of your father may be free for you.'" So when they disliked their father's love for him and it distressed them, and they desired its removal from him, they concealed him from him. And He said: "And they will not find within their chests (Sudur) any need for what they have been given," meaning their chests (Sudur) do not constrict with it nor do they grieve, so He praised them for the absence of envy (Hasad).
4:89.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

4:93.arabic: وقوله تعالى: ﴿ ومن يقتل مؤمنا متعمدا فجزاؤه جهنم خالدا فيها ﴾ {} وهذه العمومات أيضا مخصوصة بدليل قوله تعالى: ﴿ ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء ﴾ {} فينبغي أن تبقى له مشيئة في مغفرة ما سوى الشرك وكذلك قوله ﭬ: (يخرج من النار من كان في قلبه مثقال ذرة من إيمان) وقوله تعالى: ﴿ إنا لا نضيع أجر من أحسن عملا ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ إن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين ﴾ {} فكيف يضيع أجر أصل الإيمان وجميع الطاعات بمعصية واحدة وقوله تعالى: ﴿ ومن يقتل مؤمنا متعمدا ﴾ {} أي لإيمانه وقد ورد على مثل هذا السبب.
4:93.english: And His saying, the Exalted: 'And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein forever' (Quran 4:93). And these general statements are also specified by the evidence of His saying, the Exalted: 'And He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills' (Quran 4:48). So it is necessary that His will (Mashiyyah) remains for forgiving what is besides polytheism (Shirk). And likewise His saying, peace be upon him: 'He will exit from the Fire whoever has in his heart (Qalb) an atom's weight of faith (Iman).' And His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, We do not waste the reward of one who does good deeds (Ahsan 'Amalan)' (Quran 18:30). And His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, Allah does not waste the reward of the doers of good (Muhsinin)' (Quran 9:120). So how would He waste the reward of the foundation of faith (Iman) and all acts of obedience (Tā'āt) with a single act of disobedience (Ma'siyah)? And His saying, the Exalted: 'And whoever kills a believer intentionally' (Quran 4:93), meaning because of his faith (Iman), and it has come down for a reason like this.
4:93.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

4:94.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا ضربتم في سبيل الله فتبينوا وقال تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن جاءكم فاسق بنبأ فتبينوا وقال تعالى ولقد خلقنا الإنسان ونعلم ماتوسوس به نفسه ذكر ذلك تحذيرا وتنبيها للاحتراز منه في المستقبل
4:94.english: And Allah the Exalted has said: 'O you who have believed, when you go forth [to fight] in the cause of Allah, investigate; and do not say to one who gives you [a greeting of] peace, "You are not a believer," aspiring for the goods of worldly life; for with Allah are many acquisitions. Thus you were before; but Allah conferred His favor upon you, so investigate. Indeed Allah is ever, of what you do, Aware.' (Quran 4:94) And He the Exalted has said: 'O you who have believed, if there comes to you a disobedient one with information, investigate.' (Quran 49:6) And He the Exalted has said: 'And We have certainly created man and know what his Soul (Nafs) whispers to him.' (Quran 50:16) He mentioned that as a warning and an alert for guarding against it in the future.
4:94.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

4:94.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
4:94.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Whatever is in the Quran of 'O you who have believed' is in the Torah 'O you poor ones (al-Masakin)'.
4:94.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

4:95.arabic: فصار بدنه كرباط وثغر ونفسه كمقيم فيه مرابط فإن هو جاهد عدوه وهزمه وقهره على ما يحب حمد أثره وإذا عاد إلى الحضرة كما قال الله تعالى والمجاهدون في سبيل الله بأموالهم وأنفسهم فضل الله المجاهدين بأموالهم وأنفسهم على القاعدين درجة وإن ضيع ثغره وأهمل رعيته ذم أثره فانتقم منه عند الله تعالى فيقال له يوم القيامة يا راعي السوء أكلت اللحم وشربت اللبن ولم تأو الضالة ولم تجبر الكسير اليوم أنتقم منك[4] كما ورد في الخبر وإلى هذه المجاهدة الإشارة بقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم رجعنا من الجهاد الأصغر إلى الجهاد الأكب
4:95.english: So his body became like a fortress and outpost, and his soul (Nafs) like one residing therein as a defender. If he strives (Jahada) against his enemy and defeats him and overcomes him according to what is beloved, his effect is praised, and when he returns to the presence (Al-Hadrah) as Allah the Exalted said: 'And the strivers (Mujahidun) in the path of Allah with their wealth and their souls (Anfus), Allah has preferred the strivers (Mujahidun) with their wealth and their souls (Anfus) over the sitters (Qa'idun) by a degree.' And if he neglects his outpost and disregards his subjects, his effect is blamed, so vengeance is taken from him with Allah the Exalted, and it is said to him on the Day of Resurrection: 'O evil shepherd, you ate the flesh and drank the milk, and you did not shelter the lost one nor mend the broken one; today I take vengeance from you' as reported in the tradition. And to this striving (Mujahadah) is the allusion in his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: 'We have returned from the lesser striving (Jihad) to the greater striving (Jihad).'
4:95.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

4:95.arabic: ويروى أن الله تعالى أوحى إلى داود عليه السلام يا داود حذر وأنذر أصحابك أكل الشهوات فإن القلوب المتعلقة بشهوات الدنيا عقولها عني محجوبة. وقال عيسى عليه السلام: طوبى لمن ترك شهوة حاضرة لموعود غائب لم يره وقال نبينا ﭬ لقوم قدموا من الجهاد "مرحباً بكم قدمتم من الجهاد الأصغر إلى الجهاد الأكبر" قيل يا رسول الله ومال الجهاد الأكبر؟ قال "جهاد النفس"[44] وقال ﭬ "المجاهد من جاهد نفسه في طاعة الله عز وجل"[45] وقال ﭬ "كف أذاك عن نفسك ولا تتابع هواها في معصية الله تعالى إذن تخاصمك يوم فليعن بعضك بعضاً إلا أن
4:95.english: And it is narrated that Allah the Exalted revealed to David, peace be upon him: O David, warn and caution your companions against consuming desires, for the hearts attached to worldly desires have their intellects veiled from Me. And Jesus, peace be upon him, said: Blessed is he who abandons a present desire for a promised unseen that he has not seen. And our Prophet, peace be upon him, said to a people who returned from jihad: "Welcome, you have come from the lesser jihad to the greater jihad." It was said: O Messenger of Allah, and what is the greater jihad? He said: "The jihad of the self (Nafs)."[44] And he said, peace be upon him: "The mujahid is he who wages jihad against his self (Nafs) in obedience to Allah the Exalted."[45] And he said, peace be upon him: "Restrain your harm from your self (Nafs) and do not follow its inclination (Hawa) in disobedience to Allah the Exalted, then it will dispute with you on a day when some of you will help others, except that Allah the Exalted forgives and covers."[46] And Sufyan al-Thawri said: I have not treated anything more difficult for me than my self (Nafs), sometimes it is with me and sometimes against me. And Abu al-Abbas al-Mu...
4:95.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

4:95.english: The Mujahidun (those who strive) in the path of Allah
4:95.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

4:97.arabic: فهذا يدل على أن من بلي ببلدة تكثر فيها المعاصي ويقل فيها الخير فلا عذر له في المقام بها، بل ينبغي أن يهاجر قال الله تعالى " ألم تكن أرض الله واسعة فتهاجروا فيها " فإن منعه عن ذلك عيال أو علاقة فلا ينبغي أن يكون راضياً بحاله مطمئن النفس إليه، بل ينبغي أن يكون منزعج القلب منها قائلاً على الدوام " ربنا أخرجنا من هذه القرية الظالم أهلها " وذلك لأن الظلم إذا عم نزل البلاء ودمر الجميع وشمل المطيعين، قال الله تعالى: " واتقوا فتنة لا تصيبن الذين ظلموا منكم خاصة " فإذن ليس في شيء من أسباب نقص الدين البتة
4:97.english: This indicates that whoever is afflicted with a land where sins abound and good is scarce has no excuse for remaining there; rather, he should emigrate. Allah the Exalted said: 'Was not the earth of Allah spacious so that you could emigrate therein?' If he is prevented from that by dependents or ties, he should not be content with his state, at ease in his Soul (Nafs) with it; rather, he should be disturbed in Heart (Qalb) about it, saying constantly: 'Our Lord, take us out of this town whose people are wrongdoers.' This is because when injustice becomes widespread, calamity descends and destroys everyone, encompassing the obedient. Allah the Exalted said: 'And fear a trial which will not strike those who have wronged among you exclusively.' Therefore, there is absolutely no absolute contentment in any of the causes of deficiency in religion except from the perspective of attributing them to the action of Allah the Exalted; as for them in themselves, there is no aspect of contentment with them in any state.
4:97.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

4:97.arabic: ومن كوشف بهذه الامور بعد ان ألف الجاه وانس به ورسخت فيه بالعادة مباشرة اسبابه فلا يكفيه في العلاج مجرد العلم والكشف بل لا بد وان يضيف اليه العمل وعمله في ثلاثة امور: أحدها ان يهرب عن موضع الجاه كي لا يشاهد اسبابه فيعسر عليه الصبر مع الاسباب كما يهرب من غلبته الشهوة من مشاهدة الصور المحركة ومن لم يفعل هذا فقد كفر نعمة الله في سعة الارض اذ قال تعالى: ﴿ ألم تكن أرض الله واسعة فتهاجروا فيها ﴾ {}. الثاني ان يكلف نفسه في أعماله أفعالا تخالف ما اعتاده فيبدل التكلف بالتبذل وزي الحشمة بزي التواضع وكذلك ك
4:97.english: And whoever is unveiled to these matters after becoming accustomed to status and familiarity with it, and it becomes firmly rooted in him through habit by directly engaging with its causes, then mere knowledge and unveiling are insufficient for treatment; rather, he must add to it action, and his action is in three matters: The first is that he flees from the place of status so that he does not witness its causes, making patience with the causes difficult for him, just as one flees from being overcome by desire from observing stimulating images. And whoever does not do this has disbelieved in the blessing of Allah in the vastness of the earth, as He, the Exalted, said: 'Was not the earth of Allah spacious that you might emigrate therein?' (Quran 4:97). The second is that he compels himself in his actions to deeds that contradict what he has become accustomed to, thus replacing affectation with simplicity and the attire of dignity with the attire of humility, and likewise every form, state, and action in dwelling, clothing, food, standing, and sitting that he used to practice in fulfillment of the requirements of his status, he should replace with their opposites until he becomes firmly rooted through habituation in the opposite of what he was previously rooted in through habituation of its opposite, for there is no meaning to treatment except opposition.
4:97.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

4:97.arabic: وإنما نزل قوله تعالى أن الذين توفاهم الملائكة ظالمى أنفسهم في قوم من المسلمين كانوا يكثرون جماعة المشركين بالمخالطة وقد روى أن الله تعالى أوحى إلى يوشع ابن نون أني مهلك من قومك أربعين ألفا من خيارهم وستين ألفا من شرارهم فقال ما بال الأخيار قال إنهم لا يغضبون لغضبي فكانوا يؤاكلونهم ويشاربهم وبهذا يتبين أن بعض الظلمة و الغضب لله عليهم واجب
4:97.english: And indeed, the saying of Allah the Exalted 'Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves (ظالمى أنفسهم)' was revealed regarding a group from the Muslims who used to increase the gathering of the polytheists through mixing. And it has been narrated that Allah the Exalted revealed to Joshua son of Nun: 'I will destroy from your people forty thousand from their best and sixty thousand from their worst.' He said: 'What about the good ones?' He said: 'Indeed, they do not become angry for My anger.' So they used to eat with them and drink with them. And through this, it becomes clear that some darkness (الظلمة) and anger (الغضب) for Allah upon them is obligatory.
4:97.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

4:100.arabic: تساع أسباب تصده عن التجرد لله فيؤثر الغربة والخمول ويجتنب السعة والجاه أو كمن يدعى إلى بدعة قهرا أو إلى ولاية عمل لا تحل مباشرته فيطلب الفرار منه وأما المطلوب فهو إما دنيوي كالمال والجاه أو ديني والديني إما علم وإما عمل والعلم إما علم من العلوم الدينية وإما علم بأخلاق نفسه وصفاته على سبيل التجربة وإما علم بآيات الأرض وعجائبها كسفر ذي القرنين وطوافه في نواحي الأرض والعمل إما عبادة وإما زيارة والعبادة هو الحج والعمرة والجهاد والزيارة أيضا من القربات وقد يقصد بها مكان كمكة والمدينة وبيت المقدس والث
4:100.english: The ninth reason that prevents one from Devotion (Tajarrud) to Allah, so one prefers solitude (Ghurbah) and obscurity (Khumul) and avoids abundance (Saa'ah) and status (Jah), or like one who is called to innovation (Bid'ah) by force or to a position of work that is not permissible to engage in, so he seeks to flee from it. As for what is sought, it is either worldly like wealth and status, or religious (Dini), and the religious is either knowledge (Ilm) or action (Amal). Knowledge is either knowledge from the religious sciences, or knowledge of the character traits (Akhlaq) of his soul (Nafs) and its attributes (Sifat) by way of experience (Tajribah), or knowledge of the signs (Ayaat) of the earth and its wonders, like the journey of Dhul-Qarnayn and his traveling around the regions of the earth. Action is either worship (Ibadah) or visitation (Ziyarah), and worship is Hajj, Umrah, and Jihad. Visitation is also among the acts of nearness (Qurbat), and it may be intended for a place like Makkah, Madinah, Bayt al-Maqdis, and the frontiers (Thughur), for guarding (Ribat) them is an act of nearness. It may be intended for the saints (Awliya) and scholars (Ulama), and they are either dead, so their graves are visited, or alive, so one seeks blessing (Tabarruk) by seeing them, and from looking at their states (Ahwal), strength of desire (Raghbah) in following their example (Iqtida) is gained. These are the categories of journeys, and from this division emerge the categories of the first division: travel in seeking knowledge, which is either obligatory (Wajib) or supererogatory (Nafil), and that is according to whether the knowledge is obligatory or supererogatory. That knowledge is either knowledge of matters of his religion, or of his character traits in his soul, or of Allah's signs in His earth. And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever leaves his house in seeking knowledge, he is in the path (Sabil) of Allah until he returns.' Hadith: 'Whoever leaves his house in seeking knowledge, he is in the path of Allah until he returns.' Reported by al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Anas, and he said it is good (Hasan) and rare (Gharib). And in another report: 'Whoever treads a path in which he seeks knowledge, Allah will ease for him a path to Paradise.' Hadith: 'Whoever treads a path in which he seeks knowledge...' Reported by Muslim. And it preceded in knowledge. And Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab would travel days in seeking a single hadith. And al-Sha'bi said: 'If a man traveled from Syria to the farthest Yemen for a word that guides him to guidance (Huda) or turns him away from error (Radda), his journey would not be wasted.' And Jabir ibn Abd Allah traveled from Madinah to Egypt with ten of the Companions, and they traveled for a month in a hadith that reached them from Abd Allah Unays al-Ansari, that he narrated from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), until they heard it. Hadith: 'Jabir ibn Abd Allah traveled from Madinah to a journey of a month in a hadith that reached him from Abd Allah ibn Unays.' Reported by al-Khatib in the book of travel (al-Rihlah) with a good chain (Isnad), and he did not name the Companion. And al-Bukhari said in his Sahih: 'Jabir ibn Abd Allah traveled a month's journey to Abd Allah ibn Unays for a single hadith.' And Ahmad reported it except he said to Syria, and its chain is good. And for Ahmad: 'Abu Ayyub rode to Uqbah ibn Amir to Egypt in a hadith.' And for him: 'Uqbah ibn Amir came to Salamah ibn Mukhallad while he was the governor of Egypt in another hadith.' And both are disconnected (Munqati), and every mentioned in knowledge is acquired for.
4:100.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Travel'

4:100.arabic: وإما أمر له نكاية في الدين كمن ابتلي في بلده بجاه ومال واتساع أسباب تصده عن التجرد لله فيؤثر الغربة والخمول ويجتنب السعة والجاه أو كمن يدعى إلى بدعة قهرا أو إلى ولاية عمل لا تحل مباشرته فيطلب الفرار منه وأما المطلوب فهو إما دنيوي كالمال والجاه أو ديني والديني إما علم وإما عمل والعلم إما علم من العلوم الدينية وإما علم بأخلاق نفسه وصفاته على سبيل التجربة وإما علم بآيات الأرض وعجائبها كسفر ذي القرنين وطوافه في نواحي الأرض والعمل إما عبادة وإما زيارة والعبادة هو الحج والعمرة والجهاد والزيارة أيضا من
4:100.english: Or it may be a matter that has harm in the religion, such as one afflicted in his land with power (Jāh) and wealth and expansion of means that prevent him from detachment (Tajarrud) for Allah, so he prefers exile (Ghurbah) and obscurity and avoids expansion and power (Jāh); or like one who is called to innovation (Bidʿah) by force or to a position of work whose direct handling is not permissible, so he seeks escape from it. As for what is sought, it is either worldly, like wealth and power (Jāh), or religious, and the religious is either knowledge (ʿIlm) or action (ʿAmal). Knowledge (ʿIlm) is either knowledge (ʿIlm) from the religious sciences, or knowledge (ʿIlm) of the character traits (Akhlāq) of his soul (Nafs) and its attributes by way of experience, or knowledge (ʿIlm) of the signs (Āyāt) of the earth and its wonders, like the journey of Dhul-Qarnayn and his traveling around the regions of the earth. Action (ʿAmal) is either worship (ʿIbādah) or visitation (Ziyārah), and worship (ʿIbādah) is Hajj, Umrah, Jihad, and visitation (Ziyārah) is also among the acts of nearness (Qurbāt). It may be intended for a place like Mecca, Medina, Jerusalem, and the frontiers, for guarding (Ribāṭ) them is an act of nearness (Qurbah). Or it may be intended for the saints (Awliyāʾ) and scholars (ʿUlamāʾ), and they are either dead, so their graves are visited, or alive, so one seeks blessing (Tabarruk) by seeing them, and from looking at their states (Aḥwāl) one gains strength in the desire (Raghbah) to emulate (Iqtidāʾ) them. These are the divisions of journeys, and from this division emerge the divisions of the first category: travel in seeking knowledge (ʿIlm), which is either obligatory (Wājib) or supererogatory (Nafal), and that is according to whether the knowledge (ʿIlm) is obligatory (Wājib) or supererogatory (Nafal). That knowledge (ʿIlm) is either knowledge (ʿIlm) of the matters of his religion, or of his character traits (Akhlāq) in his soul (Nafs), or of the signs (Āyāt) of Allah in His earth. And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever leaves his house in seeking knowledge (ʿIlm), he is in the path (Sabīl) of Allah until he returns.' Hadith: 'Whoever leaves his house in seeking knowledge (ʿIlm), he is in the path (Sabīl) of Allah until he returns.' Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Anas and said it is good (Ḥasan) and rare (Gharīb). And in another report: 'Whoever treads a path in which he seeks knowledge (ʿIlm), Allah will ease for him a path to Paradise.' Hadith: 'Whoever treads a path in which he seeks knowledge (ʿIlm)...' Muslim narrated it, and it preceded in the section on knowledge (ʿIlm). And Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib would travel days in seeking a single hadith. And al-Shaʿbī said: 'If a man traveled from Syria to the farthest Yemen for a word that guides him to guidance (Hudā) or turns him back from misguidance (Radā), his journey would not be wasted.' And Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh journeyed from Medina to Egypt with ten of the Companions, and they traveled for a month in a hadith that reached them from ʿAbd Allāh Unays al-Anṣārī narrating it from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) until they heard it. Hadith: 'Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh journeyed from Medina to a month's distance in a hadith that reached him from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Unays.' Al-Khaṭīb narrated it in the book 'Al-Riḥlah' with a good (Ḥasan) chain, and he did not name the Companion. And al-Bukhārī said in his Ṣaḥīḥ: 'Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh journeyed a month's distance to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Unays for a single hadith.' And Aḥmad narrated it except he said 'to Syria,' and its chain is good (Ḥasan). And Aḥmad has that Abū Ayyūb rode to ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir to Egypt for a hadith, and he has that ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir came to Salamah ibn Mukhallad, and he is...
4:100.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Travel'

4:100.arabic: وليرج أنه إن لم يصل إليه وأدركته المنية في الطريق لقي الله عز وجل وافدا إليه إذ قال جل جلاله (ومن يخرج من بيته مهاجرا إلى الله ورسوله ثم يدركه الموت فقد وقع أجره على الله(. وأما دخول البادية إلى الميقات ومشاهدة تلك العقبات فليتذكر فيها ما بين الخروج من الدنيا بالموت إلى ميقات يوم القيامة وما بينهما من الأهوال والمطالبات وليتذكر من هول قطاع الطريق هول سؤال منكر ونكير ومن سباع البوادي عقارب القبر وديدانه وما فيه من الأفاعي والحيات ومن انفراده من أهله وأقاربه وحشة القبر وكربته ووحدته وليكن في هذه ا
4:100.english: And let him hope that if he does not reach it and death overtakes him on the way, he will meet Allah (God), the Exalted and Majestic, as a visitor to Him, as He, Glory and Majesty be to Him, said: 'And whoever leaves his home emigrating to Allah and His Messenger, then death overtakes him, his reward has fallen upon Allah.' And as for entering the wilderness to the Miqat (designated station for Ihram) and witnessing those obstacles, let him remember in it what is between leaving the world by death to the Miqat (appointed time) of the Day of Resurrection and what is between them of terrors and demands, and let him remember from the terror of highway robbers the terror of the questioning of Munkar and Nakir (the two angels who question in the grave), and from the wild beasts of the deserts the scorpions of the grave and its worms, and what is in it of vipers and snakes, and from his separation from his family and relatives the loneliness of the grave, its distress, and its solitude, and let him in these fears in his actions and words be provisioned for the fears of the grave.
4:100.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

4:100.arabic: ن زارني بعد وفاتي فكأنما زارني في حياتي اخرجه الطبراني والدار قطني من حديث ابن عمر. [59] حديث من وجد سعة ولم يفد إلي فقد جفاني أخرجه ابن عدي والدار قطني في غرائب مالك وابن حبان في الضعفاء والخطيب في الرواة عن مالك في حديث ابن عمر من حج ولم يزرني فقد جفاني وذكره ابن الجوزي في الموضوعات وروى ابن النجار في تاريخ المدينة من حديث أنس ما من أحد من أمتي له سعة ثم لم يزرني فليس له عذر. [60] حديث من جاءني زائرا لا تهمه إلا زيارتي كان حقا على الله أن أكون له شفيعا أخرجه الطبراني من حديث ابن عمر وصححه ابن
4:100.english: Who visits me after my death is as if he visited me in my life - reported by Al-Tabarani and Al-Daraqutni from the hadith of Ibn Umar. [59] Hadith: Whoever finds spaciousness (Saa'a) and does not come to me has been distant from me - reported by Ibn Adi and Al-Daraqutni in the oddities of Malik, Ibn Hibban in the weak narrators, and Al-Khatib in the narrators from Malik in the hadith of Ibn Umar: Whoever performs Hajj and does not visit me has been distant from me, and Ibn Al-Jawzi mentioned it in the fabricated narrations, and Ibn Al-Najjar reported in the History of Medina from the hadith of Anas: There is no one from my community who has spaciousness (Saa'a) then does not visit me but has no excuse. [60] Hadith: Whoever comes to me as a visitor with no concern except my visitation, it is a right upon Allah that I be an intercessor for him - reported by Al-Tabarani from the hadith of Ibn Umar and authenticated by Ibn Al-Sakan. [61] Hadith: What is between my grave and my pulpit is a garden from the gardens of Paradise, and my pulpit is upon my basin - agreed upon from the hadith of Abu Huraira and Abdullah Ibn Zaid. [62] Hadith: He placed his hand upon the knob of the pulpit during the sermon - I did not find an origin for it, and Muhammad Ibn Al-Hasan Ibn Zubala mentioned in the History of Medina that the length of the two knobs of the pulpit which he used to hold with his noble hands when sitting was a span and two fingers. [63] Hadith: Whoever leaves his house until he comes to the Quba Mosque and prays in it, it is equivalent to an Umrah - reported by Al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah from the hadith of Sahl Ibn Hunayf with a sound chain. [64] Hadith: That the Prophet spat in the well of Aris - I did not find an origin for it, but it is reported that he spat in the well of Al-Bassa and the well of Ghars as will come when mentioning them. [65] Hadith: The wells from which the Prophet performed ablution, bathed, and drank, and they are seven wells - I said: They are the well of Aris, the well of Ha, the well of Ruma, the well of Ghars, the well of Bada'a, the well of Al-Bassa, and the well of Al-Saqya or Al-Ahn or the well of Jamal. The hadith of the well of Aris is reported by Muslim from the hadith of Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari in a hadith therein: Until he entered the well of Aris, he said: I sat at its door, and its door was of iron, until the Messenger of Allah fulfilled his need and performed ablution - the hadith. And the hadith of the well of Ha is agreed upon from the hadith of Anas, he said: Abu Talha was the wealthiest of the Ansar in Medina in palm trees, and the most beloved of his wealth to him was the well of Ha, and it was facing the mosque, and the Messenger of Allah would enter it and drink from its good water - the hadith. And the hadith of the well of Ruma is reported by Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa'i from the hadith of Uthman, he said: I adjure you by Allah and Islam, do you know that the Messenger of Allah arrived in Medina and there was no sweet water in it except the well of Ruma, so he said: Who will buy the well of Ruma and make.
4:100.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

4:100.arabic: [5] حديث من خرج من بيته حاجا أو معتمرا فمات أجرى الله له أجر الحاج المعتمر إلى يوم القيامة ومن مات في أحد الحرمين لم يعرض ولم يحاسب وقيل له ادخل الجنة أخرجه البيهقي في الشعب بالشطر الأول من حديث أبي هريرة وروى هو والدار قطني من حديث عائشة الشطر الثاني نحوه وكلاهما ضعيف.
4:100.english: Hadith: Whoever leaves his house as a pilgrim (Hajj) or a visitor (Umrah) and dies, Allah will grant him the reward of the pilgrim visitor until the Day of Resurrection, and whoever dies in one of the two sanctuaries (Haramayn) will not be presented and will not be accounted, and it will be said to him: Enter Paradise. Al-Bayhaqi reported it in Al-Shu'ab with the first part from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, and he and Al-Daraqutni reported from the hadith of Aishah the second part similarly, and both are weak.
4:100.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

4:103.arabic: وقال تعالى: ﴿ الذين يذكرون الله قياما وقعودا وعلى جنوبهم ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ فإذا قضيتم الصلاة فاذكروا الله قياما وقعودا وعلى جنوبكم فإذا اطمأننتم فأقيموا الصلاة إن الصلاة كانت على المؤمنين كتابا موقوتا ﴾ {} قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: أي بالليل والنهار في البر والبحر والسفر والحضر والغنى والفقر والمرض والصحة والسر والعلانية.
4:103.english: And He (Allah) said: 'Those who remember Allah standing, sitting, and on their sides' {} And He said: 'So when you have completed the prayer, remember Allah standing, sitting, and on your sides. Then when you are secure, establish the prayer. Indeed, the prayer has been upon the believers a decree at fixed times' {} Said Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both): Meaning by night and day, on land and sea, in travel and residence, in wealth and poverty, in sickness and health, in secret and openly.
4:103.topic: Al-Ghazali on the outer and inner dimensions of worship

4:104.arabic: ولا ينبغى أن نقول إن المعرض عن الدنيا متألم بالصبر عنها فإن المقبل عليها أيضا متألم بالصبر عليها وحفظها وتحصيلها ودفع اللصوص عنها وتألم المعرض يفضى إلى لذة في الآخرة وتألم المقبل يفضى إلى الألم في الآخرة فليقرأ المعرض عن الدنيا على نفسه قوله تعالى: ﴿ ولا تهنوا في ابتغاء القوم إن تكونوا تألمون فإنهم يألمون كما تألمون وترجون من الله ما لا يرجون ﴾ فإذن إنما انسد طريق الشكر على الخلق لجهلهم بضروب النعم الظاهرة والباطنة والخاصة والعامة.
4:104.english: And it should not be said that the one who turns away from the world is suffering through patience from it, for the one who inclines toward it is also suffering through patience upon it, and preserving it, and acquiring it, and repelling thieves from it. And the suffering of the one who turns away leads to pleasure in the Hereafter, and the suffering of the one who inclines leads to pain in the Hereafter. So let the one who turns away from the world recite to himself the saying of The Most High: 'And do not weaken in pursuit of the people; if you should be suffering, then indeed they are suffering as you are suffering, but you hope from Allah that which they do not hope.' So then, indeed the way of gratitude has been blocked upon the creation due to their ignorance of the varieties of blessings, the apparent and the hidden, the specific and the general.
4:104.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

4:107.arabic: وكان الحسن بن علي رضي الله عنهما يمر بالسؤال وبين أيديهم كسر فيقولون هلم إلى الغداء يا ابن رسول الله فكان ينزل ويجلس على الطريق ويأكل معهم ويركب ويقول إن الله لا يحب المستكبرين الوجه الثاني أن الذي شغل نفسه بطلب رضا الناس عنه وتحسين اعتقادهم فيه مغرور لأنه لو عرف الله حق المعرفة علم أن الخلق لا يغنون عنه من الله شيئا وأن ضرره ونفعه بيد الله ولا نافع ولا ضار سواه وأن من طلب رضا الناس ومحبتهم بسخط الله سخط الله عليه وأسخط عليه الناس بل رضا الناس غاية لا تنال فرضا الله أولى بالطلب ولذلك قال الشافعي
4:107.english: And Al-Hasan ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with them both) would pass by beggars while they had bread crumbs before them, and they would say: 'Come to lunch, O son of the Messenger of Allah.' So he would dismount, sit on the road, eat with them, then remount and say: 'Indeed Allah does not love the arrogant ones.' The second aspect is that the one who occupies his Soul (Nafs) with seeking people's pleasure about him and improving their opinion of him is deluded, because if he knew Allah with true knowledge, he would know that the creation cannot avail him anything from Allah, and that his harm and benefit are in Allah's hand, and there is no benefactor nor harmer except Him, and that whoever seeks people's pleasure and love with Allah's displeasure, Allah will be displeased with him and make people displeased with him. Rather, people's pleasure is an unattainable goal, so Allah's pleasure is more worthy of pursuit. Therefore, Al-Shafi'i said to Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la: 'By Allah, I only advise you: there is no way to safety from people, so look at what suits you and do it.' Therefore, it is said: 'Whoever watches people dies grieving, and the bold one attains pleasure.' And Sahl looked at one of his companions and said to him: 'Do such and such' regarding something he commanded him to do. He said: 'O master, I cannot do it because of people.' So he turned to his companions and said: 'A servant does not attain the reality of this matter until he is in one of two descriptions: a servant from whose eye people have fallen, so he sees in the world only his Creator, and that no one can harm him nor benefit him; and a servant whose Soul (Nafs) has fallen from his Heart (Qalb), so he does not care in what state they see him.' And Al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'There is no one except that he has a lover and a hater, so if it is like this, then be with the people of Allah's obedience.' And it was said to Al-Hasan: 'O Abu Sa'id, there are people who attend your gathering whose only aim is to follow...'
4:107.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Seclusion'

4:107.arabic: وَمَرَّ الْحَسَنُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُمَا بِقَوْمٍ مِنَ الْمَسَاكِينِ الَّذِينَ يَسْأَلُونَ النَّاسَ عَلَى الطَّرِيقِ وَقَدْ نَشَرُوا كِسْرًا عَلَى الْأَرْضِ فِي الرَّمْلِ وَهُمْ يَأْكُلُونَ وَهُوَ عَلَى بَغْلَتِهِ فَسَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِمْ فَقَالُوا لَهُ هَلُمَّ إِلَى الْغَدَاءِ يَا ابْنَ بِنْتِ رَسُولِ اللهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَقَالَ نَعَمْ إِنَّ اللهَ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُسْتَكْبِرِينَ فَنَزَلَ وَقَعَدَ مَعَهُمْ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ وَأَكَلَ ثُمَّ سَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَرَكِبَ وَقَا
4:107.english: And Al-Hasan ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with them both) passed by a group of the poor (Masakin) who ask people on the road, and they had spread crumbs on the ground in the sand and they were eating, and he was on his mule. He greeted them, and they said to him: 'Come to lunch, O son of the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him).' He said: 'Yes, indeed Allah does not love the arrogant (Mustakbirin).' So he dismounted and sat with them on the ground and ate. Then he greeted them and mounted and said: 'I have answered you, so answer me.' They said: 'Yes.' So he promised them a known time, and they attended. He presented to them the finest food and sat eating with them.
4:107.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Manners of Eating'

4:110.arabic:
(فضيلة الاستغفار)
   قال عز وجل: ﴿  والذين  إذا  فعلوا  فاحشة  أو  ظلموا  أنفسهم  ذكروا  الله
فاستغفروا لذنوبهم ﴾ {} وقال علقمة والأسود قال عبد الله  بن  مسعود  رضي  الله
عنهم في كتاب الله عز وجل آيتان ما أذنب عبد ذنبا فقرأهما واستغفر الله عز  وجل
إلا غفر الله تعالى له: ﴿ والذين إذا فعلوا فاحشة أو ظلموا أنفسهم ﴾  {}  الآية
وقوله عز وجل: ﴿ ومن يعمل سوءا أو يظلم به  ثم  يستغفر  الله  يجد  الله  غفورا
رحيما ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل: ﴿  فسبح بحمد ربك واستغفره إنه كان توابا  ﴾
4:110.english:
(The Virtue of Seeking Forgiveness)
The Mighty and Majestic said: 'And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves (ظلموا أنفسهم), remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins' {}. And 'Alqamah and Al-Aswad said: 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with them, said: In the Book of Allah the Mighty and Majestic are two verses: No servant commits a sin then recites them and seeks forgiveness from Allah the Mighty and Majestic except that Allah the Exalted forgives him: 'And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves' {} the verse, and His saying the Mighty and Majestic: 'And whoever does evil or wrongs himself (يظلم نفسه) then seeks forgiveness from Allah, he will find Allah Forgiving, Merciful' {}. And the Mighty and Majestic said: 'So glorify with praise of your Lord and seek His forgiveness; indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance' {}. And the Exalted said: 'And those who seek forgiveness in the pre-dawn hours' {}. And He (the Prophet) ﷺ would frequently say: 'Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You. O Allah, forgive me; indeed, You are the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful' [108]. And He ﷺ said: 'Whoever increases in seeking forgiveness, Allah the Mighty and Majestic makes for him from every worry an opening and from every difficulty a way out, and provides for him from where he does not expect' [109].
4:110.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith

4:113.arabic: فإن من عرف نفسه وعرف ربه عرف قطعاً أنه لا وجود له من ذاته وإنما وجود ذاته ودوام وجوده وكمال وجوده من الله وإلى الله وبالله، فهو المخترع الموجد له وهو المبقي له وهو المكمل لوجوده بخلق صفات الكمال وخلق الأسباب الموصلة إليه ذو خلق الهداية إلى استعمال الأسباب، وإلا فالعبد من حيث ذاته لا وجود له من ذاته، بل هو محو محض وعدم صرف لولا فضل الله تعالى عليه بالإيجاد، وهو هالك عقيب وجوده لولا فضل الله عليه بالإبقاء، وهو ناقص بعد الوجود لولا فضل الله عليه بالتكميل لخلقته وبالجملة فليس في الوجود شيء له بنفسه
4:113.english: For whoever knows his self (Nafs) and knows his Lord (Rabb) knows with certainty that he has no existence from his own essence, and indeed the existence of his essence, the continuity of his existence, and the perfection of his existence are from Allah, to Allah, and by Allah. He is the Creator (Al-Khaliq) who brings him into existence, He is the Sustainer who preserves him, and He is the Perfecter of his existence by creating attributes of perfection and creating the means that lead to Him, possessing the creation of guidance to utilize the means. Otherwise, the servant (Al-'Abd) from the perspective of his essence has no existence from his essence; rather, he is pure effacement and sheer non-existence were it not for the grace (Fadl) of Allah, the Exalted, upon him with creation. And he would perish immediately after his existence were it not for the grace of Allah upon him with preservation. And he would be deficient after existence were it not for the grace of Allah upon him with the completion of his creation. In summary, there is nothing in existence that has self-subsistence by itself except the Self-Subsisting (Al-Qayyum), the Living (Al-Hayy), who is self-subsistent by His essence, and everything other than Him is subsistent by Him. If the knower (Al-'Arif) loves his essence and the existence of his essence is derived from another, then by necessity he loves the one who benefits his existence and perpetuates it, if he knows Him as Creator, Originator, Inventor, Preserver, Self-Subsistent by Himself, and Sustainer of others. If he does not love Him, it is due to his ignorance of his self and his Lord. Love (Al-Mahabbah) is the fruit of knowledge (Al-Ma'rifah), so it ceases with its absence, weakens with its weakness, and strengthens with its strength. Therefore, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said: 'Whoever knows his Lord loves Him, and whoever knows the world renounces it.' How can it be conceived that a human loves his self and does not love his Lord by whom his self subsists? It is known that the one afflicted by the heat of the sun, since he loves the shade, loves by necessity the trees by which the shade subsists. And everything in existence in relation to the power of Allah, the Exalted, is like the shade in relation to the tree and the light in relation to the sun, for all are from the effects of His power, and the existence of all follows His existence, just as the existence of light follows the sun and the existence of shade follows the tree. Rather, this example is correct in relation to the delusions of the common people, for they imagined that light is an effect of the sun and emanates from it and exists by it, and this is pure error when it is unveiled to the possessors of hearts (Arbab Al-Qulub) with a manifestation clearer than the observation of the...
4:113.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

4:113.arabic: فأعظم نعمة الله على عباده هو العلم وكشف الحق والإيمان عبارة عن نوع كشف وعلم ولذلك قال تعالى امتنانا على عبده وكان فضل الله عليك عظيما وأراد به العلم
4:113.english: So the greatest blessing of Allah upon His servants is knowledge (Ilm) and unveiling (Kashf) of truth, and faith (Iman) is an expression of a type of unveiling (Kashf) and knowledge (Ilm). Therefore, Allah the Exalted said, as a favor upon His servant: 'And the favor of Allah upon you is great' (Quran 4:113), and He intended by it knowledge (Ilm).
4:113.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

4:113.arabic: وقد سمى الله عز وجل العلم فضلا في مواضع قال تعالى: ﴿ وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم وكان فضل الله عليك عظيما ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ ولقد آتينا داود منا فضلا ﴾ {} يعني العلم. فتعلم العلم في هذا اليوم وتعليمه من أفضل القربات
4:113.english: And Allah the Exalted has named knowledge as favor in places. He said: 'And He taught you what you did not know, and the favor of Allah upon you was great' (Quran 4:113). And He said: 'And We gave David from Us favor' (Quran 34:10), meaning knowledge. So learning knowledge on this day and teaching it are among the best acts of nearness (Qurbat).
4:113.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

4:114.arabic: وقال تعالى لا خير في كثير من نجواهم إلا من أمر بصدقة أو معروف أو إصلاح بين الناس ومن يفعل ذلك ابتغاء مرضاة الله فسوف نؤتيه اجرا عظيما وقال تعالى وإن طائفتان من المؤمنين اقتتلوا فأصلحوا بينهما الآية والاصلاح نهي عن البغي وإعادة إلى الطاعة فإن لم يفعل فقد أمر الله تعالى بقتاله فقال فقاتلوا التي تبغي حتى تفيء إلى أمر الله وذلك هو النهي عن المنكر
4:114.english: And Allah the Exalted said: 'There is no good in much of their secret counsels except for one who enjoins charity or good (ma'ruf) or reconciliation between people. And whoever does that seeking the pleasure (mardat) of Allah, then We will give him a great reward.' And Allah the Exalted said: 'And if two parties of the believers fight, then make peace between them...' The reconciliation is a prohibition (nahy) against aggression and a restoration to obedience. If they do not do so, then Allah the Exalted has commanded to fight them, so He said: 'Then fight the one that transgresses until it returns to the command of Allah.' And that is the prohibition (nahy) against the evil (munkar).
4:114.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

4:114.arabic: واعلم أن فضول الكلام لا ينحصر بل المهم محصور في كتاب الله تعالى قال الله عز وجل "لا خير في كثير من نجواهم إلا من أمر بصدقة أو معروف أو إصلاح بين الناس" وقال ﷺ "طوبى لمن أمسك الفضل من لسانه وأنفق الفضل من ماله" فانظر كيف قلب الناس الأمر في ذلك فأمسكوا فضل المال وأطلقوا فضل اللسان
4:114.english: And know that the excess (Fudul) of speech is not limited, but the important is confined to the Book of Allah the Exalted. Allah the Exalted said: "There is no good in much of their private conversation except for one who orders charity or good (Ma'ruf) or reconciliation between people." And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Blessed is the one who withholds the excess (Fadl) from his tongue and spends the excess (Fadl) from his wealth." So look how people have reversed the matter in that: they withhold the excess (Fadl) of wealth and release the excess (Fadl) of the tongue.
4:114.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

4:114.arabic: وكان شغل الصحابة والتابعين رضي الله عنهم في خمسة أشياء قراءة القرآن وعمارة المساجد وذكر الله تعالى والأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر وذلك لما سمعوه من قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ((كل كلام ابن آدم عليه لا له إلا ثلاثة أمر بمعروف أو نهي عن منكر أو ذكر الله تعالى))[174]. وقال تعالى: (لا خير في كثير من نجواهم إلا من أمر بصدقة أو معروف أو إصلاح بين الناس... الآية( (النساء:114) ورأى بعض العلماء بعض أصحاب الرأي من أهل الكوفة في المنام فقال ما رأيت فيما كنت عليه من الفتيا والرأي فكره وجهه وأعرض عنه وقال ما
4:114.english: And the occupation of the Companions and the Followers (may Allah be pleased with them) was in five things: reciting the Quran, building mosques, the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah the Exalted, commanding good (Ma'ruf), and forbidding evil (Munkar). This is because they heard from his saying (peace be upon him): 'Every speech of the son of Adam is against him, not for him, except three: commanding good, forbidding evil, or the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah the Exalted.' And Allah the Exalted said: 'There is no good in much of their secret counsels except for one who enjoins charity or good (Ma'ruf) or reconciliation between people... the verse' (An-Nisa:114). And some scholars saw some of the people of opinion from the people of Kufa in a dream and said: 'What did I see in what I was upon of giving legal opinions (Fatwa) and opinion?' So he disliked his face and turned away from him and said: 'We did not find it anything, and we did not praise its safety.' And Ibn Husain said: 'Indeed, one of them gives a legal opinion in a matter that if it were presented to Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), he would gather for it the people of Badr.' And silence has remained the practice of the people of knowledge except in necessity.
4:114.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

4:116.arabic: ولا حجة لهم في ذلك فإنه حيث ذكر الإيمان في هذه الآيات أريد به الإيمان مع العمل إذ بينا أن الإيمان قد يطلق ويراد به الإسلام وهو الموافقة بالقلب والقول والعمل ودليل هذا التأويل أخبار كثيرة في معاقبة العاصين ومقادير العقاب وقوله ﭬ: (يخرج من النار من كان في قلبه مثقال ذرة من إيمان) فكيف يخرج إذا لم يدخل ومن القرآن قوله تعالى: ﴿ إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء ﴾ {} والاستثناء بالمشيئة يدل على الانقسام وقوله تعالى: ﴿ ومن يعص الله ورسوله فإن له نار جهنم خالدين فيها ﴾ {}
4:116.english: And they have no proof in that, for when faith (Iman) is mentioned in these verses, it is intended as faith with action, since we have explained that faith may be used and intended as Islam, which is agreement with the heart (Qalb), speech, and action. Evidence for this interpretation is numerous reports about punishing sinners and the measures of punishment, and his saying ﭬ: (He will bring out from the Fire whoever had in his heart (Qalb) an atom's weight of faith (Iman)) - so how can he be brought out if he did not enter? And from the Quran is His saying: 'Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills' - and the exception with will (Mashiyyah) indicates division, and His saying: 'And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger - then indeed, for him is the Fire of Hell, abiding eternally therein'.
4:116.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

4:116.arabic: وهذه العمومات أيضا مخصوصة بدليل قوله تعالى: ﴿ ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء ﴾ {} فينبغي أن تبقى له مشيئة في مغفرة ما سوى الشرك وكذلك قوله ﭬ: (يخرج من النار من كان في قلبه مثقال ذرة من إيمان) وقوله تعالى: ﴿ إنا لا نضيع أجر من أحسن عملا ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ إن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين ﴾ {} فكيف يضيع أجر أصل الإيمان وجميع الطاعات بمعصية واحدة
4:116.english: And these general statements are also specified by the evidence of His saying, the Exalted: 'And He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills' (Quran 4:116), so it is appropriate that His Will (Mashiyyah) remains regarding the forgiveness of what is other than association (Shirk). And likewise His saying, peace be upon him: 'He will bring out from the Fire whoever had in his heart (Qalb) an atom's weight of faith (Iman)' and His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, We do not waste the reward of one who does good work' (Quran 18:30) and His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, Allah does not waste the reward of the doers of good' (Quran 9:120), so how could He waste the reward of the foundation of faith (Iman) and all acts of obedience (Tā'āt) with a single act of disobedience (Ma'siyah).
4:116.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

4:119.arabic: وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم (تعس عبد الزوجة)[107] وإنما قال ذلك لأنه إذا أطاعها في هواها فهو عبدها وقد تعس فإن الله ملكه المرأة فملكها نفسه فقد عكس الأمر وقلب القضية وأطاع الشيطان لما قال (ولآمرنهم فليغيرن خلق الله) إذ حق الرجل أن يكون متبوعا لا تابعا.
4:119.english: And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Wretched is the slave of the wife.' He said that because if he obeys her in her desires (hawa), he is her slave and has become wretched, for Allah made him master over the woman, but he made her master over himself—thus he reversed the matter and overturned the case, and obeyed the Satan when he said: 'And I will command them so they will change the creation (khalq) of Allah,' since it is the right of the man to be followed, not a follower.
4:119.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

4:119.arabic: ومنهم من يأمل البقاء ويشتهى ذلك أبدا قال الله تعالى: ﴿ يود أحدهم لو يعمر ألف سنة ﴾  {}.  ومنهم  من  يأمل  البقاء  إلى الهرم وهو أقصى العمر الذي شاهده ورآه وهو الذي  يحب  الدنيا  حبا  شديدا.  قال رسول الله ﭬ: (الشيخ شاب في حب طلب الدنيا وإن  التفت  ترقوتاه  من  الكبر  إلا الذين اتقوا وقليل ما هم[28]). ومنهم من يأمل إلى  سنة  فلا  يشتغل  بتدبير  ما وراءها فلا يقدر لنفسه وجودا في عام قابل ولكن هذا يستعد في الصيف  للشتاء  وفي الشتاء للصيف فإذا جمع ما
4:119.english: And among them are those who hope for permanence and desire that eternally. Allah the Exalted said: 'One of them would wish to live a thousand years' {}. And among them are those who hope for permanence until old age, which is the utmost lifespan he has witnessed and seen, and he is the one who loves the worldly life (al-Dunya) with intense love. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'The old man is young in the love of seeking the worldly life (al-Dunya), even if his collarbones have turned from old age, except those who are God-conscious (ittaqaw) and few are they [28].' And among them are those who hope for a year, so he does not occupy himself with arranging what is beyond it, thus he does not estimate for himself existence in the coming year, but this one prepares in summer for winter and in winter for summer, so when he gathers what
4:119.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Book of Repentance'

4:120.arabic: وسلط عليه أقران السوء وألقى في قلبه حكم الشيطان فإنه بأنواع الحكم يغر الحمقى بقوله إن الله رحيم فلا تبال وإن الناس كلهم ما يخافون الله فلا تخالفهم وإن العمر طويل فاصبر حتى تتوب غدا يعدهم ويمنيهم وما يعدهم الشيطان إلا غرورا يعدهم التوبة ويمنيهم المغفرة فيهلكهم بإذن الله تعالى بهذه الحيل وما يجري مجراها فيوسع قلبه لقبول الغرور ويضيقه عن قبول الحق وكل ذلك بقضاء من الله وقدر فمن يرد الله أن يهديه يشرح صدره للإسلام ومن يرد أن يضله يجعل صدره ضيقا حرجا كأنما يصعد في السماء إن ينصركم الله فلا غالب لكم و
4:120.english: And He empowered over him evil companions and cast into his heart the rule of the Satan (Shaytan), for he with various rules deceives the foolish by saying: 'Allah is Merciful, so do not care,' and 'All the people do not fear Allah, so do not oppose them,' and 'The lifespan is long, so be patient until you repent tomorrow.' He promises them and gives them false hopes, and what the Satan (Shaytan) promises them is nothing but deception (ghurur). He promises them repentance and gives them false hopes of forgiveness, thus destroying them by the permission of Allah the Exalted through these tricks and what runs in their course, so He expands his heart to accept deception (ghurur) and constricts it from accepting the truth. And all of that is by a decree (qada') from Allah and a destiny (qadar). So whom Allah wills to guide, He expands his chest for Islam; and whom He wills to mislead, He makes his chest tight and constricted as if he were climbing into the sky. If Allah helps you, none can overcome you; and if He forsakes you, who is there that can help you after Him? He is the Guide and the Misleader; He does what He wills and decrees what He desires; none can repel His decree nor reverse His destiny. He created Paradise and created for it its people, so He employed them with obedience; and He created Hell and created for it its people, so He employed them with disobedience. And He made known to the creation the sign of the people of Paradise and the people of Hell, saying: 'Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss, and indeed, the wicked will be in a Blazing Fire.'
4:120.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

4:122.arabic: وقال أبو طالب المكي العمل بالجوارح من الإيمان ولا يتم دونه وادعى الإجماع فيه واستدل بأدلة تشعر بنقيض غرضه كقوله تعالى الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات إذ هذا يدل على أن العمل وراء الإيمان لا من نفس الإيمان وإلا فيكون العمل في حكم المعاد والعجب أنه ادعى الإجماع في هذا وهو مع ذلك ينقل قوله ﭬ: (لا يكفر أحد إلا بعد جحوده لما أقرّ به[51]) وينكر على المعتزلة قولهم بالتخليد في النار بسبب الكبائر والقائل بهذا قائل بنفس مذهب المعتزلة إذ يقال له من صدق بقلبه وشهد بلسانه ومات في الحال فهل هو في الجنة فلا بد أن
4:122.english: And Abu Talib al-Makki said: 'Action with the limbs (al-Jawarih) is from faith (al-Iman) and it is not complete without it,' and he claimed consensus in this and argued with evidences that suggest the opposite of his purpose, such as the saying of the Exalted: 'And those who believe and do righteous deeds (al-Salihat),' for this indicates that action is beyond faith, not from the essence of faith itself, otherwise action would be in the position of repetition. And it is astonishing that he claimed consensus in this while also transmitting his saying ﭬ: 'No one becomes an unbeliever except after denying what they affirmed [51],' and he denies the Mu'tazilites' saying of eternal punishment in the Fire due to major sins, and the one who says this is saying the same doctrine as the Mu'tazilites, for it is said to him: 'One who affirms with their heart (Qalb) and testifies with their tongue and dies immediately, is they in Paradise?' He must say yes, and in this is a ruling on the existence of faith without action.
4:122.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

4:123.arabic:
أو دفعت عنك ما هو خير وادخرت لك عندى ما  هو  أفضل  منه  فإذا
كان يوم القيامة جىء بأهل الأعمال فوفوا أعمالهم بالميزان أهل  الصلاة  والصيام
والصدقة والحج ثم يؤتي بأهل البلاء فلا ينصب لهم ميزان ولا ينشر لهم ديوان  يصب
عليهم الأجر صبا كما كان يصب عليهم البلاء صبا فيود أهل العافية في  الدنيا  لو
أنهم كانت تقرض  أجسادهم  بالمقاريض  لما  يرون  ما  يذهب  به  أهل  البلاء  من
الثواب[102]) فذلك قوله تعالى: ﴿ إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب ﴾ {}  وعن
ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال شكا نبى من الأنبياء
4:123.english: [103] Hadith: When the saying of Allah the Exalted 'Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it' was revealed, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq said: 'How can there be joy after this verse?' So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'May Allah forgive you, O Abu Bakr. Do you not become ill?' The hadith is from the narration of an unnamed person from Abu Bakr. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from another perspective with different wording and weakened it, saying: 'It has no authentic chain of transmission.' And al-Daraqutni said: 'It was also narrated from the hadith of Umar and from the hadith of al-Zubayr,' and he said: 'There is nothing established in them.'
4:123.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

4:123.arabic: وَرُوِيَ أَنَّهُ لَمَّا نَزَلَ قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿مَنْ يَعْمَلْ سُوءًا يُجْزَ بِهِ﴾ قَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقُ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى عَنْهُ: كَيْفَ الْفَرَحُ بَعْدَ هَذِهِ الْآيَةِ؟ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: (غَفَرَ اللَّهُ لَكَ يَا أَبَا بَكْرٍ، أَلَسْتَ تَمْرَضُ؟ أَلَسْتَ يُصِيبُكَ الْأَذَى؟ أَلَسْتَ تَحْزَنُ؟ فَهَذَا مِمَّا تُجْزَوْنَ بِهِ) يَعْنِي أَنَّ جَمِيعَ مَا يُصِيبُكَ يَكُونُ كَفَّارَةً لِذُنُوبِكَ.
4:123.english: And it was narrated that when the saying of the Exalted descended: 'Whoever does evil will be recompensed with it,' Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'How can there be joy after this verse?' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'May Allah forgive you, O Abu Bakr, do you not fall ill? Do you not experience harm? Do you not grieve? So this is from what you are recompensed with,' meaning that all that befalls you becomes an expiation for your sins.
4:123.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

4:126.arabic: وثلاث آيات من آخر سورة البقرة من قوله لله ما في السموات وما في الأرض إلى آخرها
4:126.english: And three verses from the end of Surah Al-Baqarah from His saying 'To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth' to its end.
4:126.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Book of Knowledge'

4:129.arabic: وإنما عليه العدل في العطاء والمبيت وأما في الحب والوقاع فذلك لا يدخل تحت الاختيار قال الله تعالى (ولن تستطيعوا أن تعدلوا بين النساء ولو حرصتم) أي أن تعدلوا في شهوة القلب وميل النفس ويتبع ذلك التفاوت في الوقاع وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم (يعدل بينهن في العطاء والبيتوتة في الليالي ويقول اللهم هذا جهدي فيما أملك ولا طاقة لي فيما تملك ولا أملك)[131] يعني الحب وقد كانت عائشة رضي الله عنها أحب نسائه إليه[132] وسائر نسائه يعرفن ذلك وكان يطاف به محمولا في مرضه في كل يوم وكل ليلة فيبيت عند كل واحدة
4:129.english: And indeed upon him is justice in giving and overnight stay, but as for in love and sexual intercourse, that does not enter under choice. Allah the Exalted said (And you will never be able to be just between women even if you should strive [to do so]), meaning that you be just in the desire of the heart (Qalb) and inclination of the soul (Nafs), and following that is the disparity in sexual intercourse. And the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, (would be just between them in giving and staying overnight in the nights and would say: O Allah, this is my effort in what I possess, and I have no capability in what You possess and I do not possess)[131] meaning love. And indeed Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, was the most beloved of his wives to him[132], and his other wives knew that. And he would be carried around in his illness every day and every night, staying overnight with each one of them, and he would say: Where am I tomorrow? Then one of his women perceived that and said: He is only asking about the day of Aisha. So they said: O Messenger of Allah, we have permitted you to be in the house of Aisha, for it is difficult upon you to be carried every night. So he said: And have you consented to that? They said: Yes. He said: Then move me to the house of Aisha[133]. And whenever one woman gives her night to her companion and the husband consents to that, the right is established for her.
4:129.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

4:129.arabic: فمن مال غضبه إلى الفتور حتى أحس من نفسه بضعف الغيرة وخسة النفس في احتمال الذل والضيم في غير محله فينبغي أن يعالج نفسه حتى يقوى غضبه. ومن مال غضبه إلى الإفراط حتى جره إلى التهور واقتحام الفواحش فينبغي أن يعالج نفسه لينقص من سورة الغضب ويققف على الوسط الحق بين الطرفين؛ فهو الصراط المستقيم وهو أرق من الشعرة وأحد من السيف؛ فأن عجز عنه فليطلب القرب منه قال تعالى "ولن تستطيعوا أن تعدلوا بين النساء ولو حرصتم فلا تميلوا كل الميل فتذروها كالمعلقة" فليس كل من عجز عن الإتيان بالخير كله ينبغي أن يأتي بالشر
4:129.english: Whoever's anger (ghadab) inclines toward weakness until he feels from his soul (nafs) a deficiency in protective jealousy (ghayrah) and baseness of the soul (nafs) in enduring humiliation and oppression in its improper place, he should treat his soul (nafs) until his anger (ghadab) strengthens. And whoever's anger (ghadab) inclines toward excess until it drags him to recklessness and plunging into abominations, he should treat his soul (nafs) to reduce from the intensity of anger (ghadab) and stand upon the true middle between the two extremes; it is the Straight Path (al-Sirat al-Mustaqim) and it is finer than a hair and sharper than a sword; so if he is incapable of it, let him seek proximity to it. Allah the Exalted said: "And you will never be able to be just between women, even if you should strive [to do so]. So do not incline completely [toward one] and leave another hanging. And if you amend [your affairs] and fear Allah, then indeed Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful." So not everyone who is incapable of bringing all good should bring all evil; but some evil is lighter than some, and some good is higher than some. This is the reality of anger (ghadab) and its degrees. We ask Allah for good success in what pleases Him; indeed He is over all things competent.
4:129.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

4:130.arabic: والقصد من هذا بيان أن الطلاق مباح وقد وعد الله الغنى في الفراق والنكاح جميعا فقال (وأنكحوا الأيامى منكم والصالحين من عبادكم وإمائكم إن يكونوا فقراء يغنهم الله من فضله) وقال سبحانه وتعالى (وإن يتفرقا يغن الله كلا من سعته).
4:130.english: The intention from this is to clarify that divorce is permissible, and Allah has promised wealth in both separation and marriage. He said: 'And marry the unmarried among you and the righteous among your male slaves and female slaves. If they should be poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty.' And He, the Exalted, said: 'And if they separate, Allah will enrich each from His abundance.'
4:130.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

4:131.arabic: وقد خصص الله تعالى التقوى بالإضافة إلى نفسه فقال تعالى: ﴿ لن ينال الله لحومها ولا دماؤها ولكن يناله التقوى منكم ﴾ {} وإنما التقوى عبارة عن كف بمقتضى الخوف كما سبق ولذلك قال تعالى: ﴿ إن أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم ﴾ {} ولذلك أوصى الله تعالى الأولين والآخرين بالتقوى فقال تعالى: ﴿ ولقد وصينا الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم وإياكم أن اتقوا الله ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل: ﴿ وخافون إن كنتم مؤمنين ﴾ {} فأمر بالخوف وأوجبه وشرطه في الإيمان فلذلك لا يتصور أن ينفك مؤمن عن خوف وإن ضعف ويكون ضعف خوفه بحسب ضعف معرفته وإيمانه
4:131.english: And Allah the Exalted has specifically attributed piety (Taqwa) to Himself, saying: 'Neither their flesh nor their blood reaches Allah, but what reaches Him is piety (Taqwa) from you.' {} And indeed piety (Taqwa) is an expression of restraint due to fear (Khauf) as previously mentioned, and therefore He said: 'Indeed, the most noble of you with Allah is the most pious (Atqakum) among you.' {} And therefore Allah the Exalted enjoined the former and the latter with piety (Taqwa), saying: 'And We have enjoined those who were given the Scripture before you and you yourselves to fear Allah (Taqwa).' {} And He the Mighty and Majestic said: 'And fear Me, if you are believers.' {} So He commanded fear (Khauf) and made it obligatory and a condition in faith (Iman), therefore it is inconceivable that a believer (Mu'min) be free from fear (Khauf), even if weak, and the weakness of his fear (Khauf) is according to the weakness of his knowledge (Ma'rifah) and faith (Iman).
4:131.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

4:131.arabic: وثلاث آيات من آخر سورة البقرة من قوله لله ما في السموات وما في الأرض إلى آخرها
4:131.english: And three verses from the end of Surah Al-Baqarah from His saying 'To Allah belongs what is in the heavens and what is in the earth' to its end.
4:131.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Book of Knowledge'

4:132.arabic: وثلاث آيات من آخر سورة البقرة من قوله لله ما في السموات وما في الأرض إلى آخرها
4:132.english: And three verses from the end of Surah Al-Baqarah from His saying 'To Allah belongs what is in the heavens and what is in the earth' to its end.
4:132.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Book of Knowledge'

4:135.arabic: وقال تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا كونوا قوامين بالقسط شهداء لله ولو على انفسكم أو الوالدين والاقربين وذلك هو الأمر بالمعروف للوالدين والأقربين
4:135.english: And Allah the Exalted said: 'O you who have believed, be upholders of justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or your parents and relatives.' And that is the commanding of good (al-Ma'ruf) to parents and relatives.
4:135.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

4:135.arabic: أيها الناس إنه من كان يعبد محمدا فإن محمدا قد مات ومن كان يعبد الله فإن الله حي لم يمت وإن الله قد قدم إليكم في أمره فلا تدعوه جزعا فإن الله عز وجل قد اختار لنبيه ﭬ ما عنده على ما عندكم وقبضه إلى ثوابه وخلف فيكم كتابه وسنة نبيه ﭬ فمن أخذ بهما عرف ومن فرق بينهما أنكر ﴿ يا أيها الذين آمنوا كونوا قوامين بالقسط شهداء لله ولو على أنفسكم أو الوالدين والأقربين إن يكن غنيا أو فقيرا فالله أولى بهما فلا تتبعوا الهوى أن تعدلوا وإن تلووا أو تعرضوا فإن الله كان بما تعملون خبيرا ﴾ ولا يشغلنكم الشيطان بموت نبي
4:135.english: O people, whoever worships Muhammad, indeed Muhammad has died, and whoever worships Allah, indeed Allah is Living (Hayy) and does not die.
