And Allah has presented to you in His command, so do not call it despair, for Allah the Exalted has chosen for His Prophet ﷺ what is with Him over what is with you, and has taken him to His reward, and has left among you His Book and the Sunnah (Tradition) of His Prophet ﷺ. So whoever takes by them knows, and whoever separates between them denies. 'O you who have believed, be upholders of justice (Qist), witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or your parents and relatives. Whether one is rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of both. So do not follow your own desire (Hawa) lest you not be just. And if you distort [your testimony] or refuse [to give it], then indeed Allah is ever, of what you do, Aware.' And do not let Satan occupy you with the death of your Prophet, nor let him tempt you away from your religion. And treat Satan with good, you will overcome him, and do not wait for him, lest he overtake you and tempt you.
4:135.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

4:135.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
4:135.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Whatever is in the Quran of 'O you who have believed' is in the Torah 'O you the poor ones (al-Masakin).'
4:135.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

4:136.arabic: فإذن جمال صفات الصديقين الذين تحبهم القلوب طبعاً ترجع إلى ثلاثة أمور: أحدها علمهم بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله وشرائع أنبيائه. والثاني: قدرتهم على إصلاح أنفسهم وإصلاح عباد الله بالإرشاد والسياسة. والثالث: تنزههم عن الرذائل والخبائث والشهوات الغالبة الصارفة عن سنن الخير الجاذبة إلى طريق الشر، وبمثل هذا يحب الأنبياء والعلماء والخلفاء والملوك الذين هم أهل العدل والكرم فأنسب هذه الصفات إلى صفات الله تعالى. أما العلم: فأين علم الأولين والآخرين من علم الله تعالى الذي يحيط بالكل إحاطة خارجة عن النهاية حت
4:136.english: Therefore, the beauty of the attributes of the Truthful Ones (Al-Siddiqin) whom hearts naturally love returns to three matters: The first is their knowledge of Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers and the laws of His prophets. The second: their ability to reform themselves and reform the servants of Allah through guidance and governance. The third: their purity from vices, impurities, and overwhelming desires that divert from the paths of good and attract to the way of evil, and by this the prophets, scholars, caliphs, and kings who are people of justice and generosity are loved, so relate these attributes to the attributes of Allah. As for knowledge: Where is the knowledge of the first and the last compared to the knowledge of Allah which encompasses everything with an encompassing beyond limit, such that not an atom's weight in the heavens or the earth escapes Him? And He addressed all creation, saying, exalted is He: "And you have not been given of knowledge except a little." Rather, if the people of the earth and the heavens gathered to encompass His knowledge and wisdom in the details of the creation of an ant or a mosquito, they would not attain a tenth of a tenth of that. "And they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except by what He wills." And the small amount that all creatures know, they know it by His teaching, as Allah said: "He created man, taught him eloquence." If the beauty and nobility of the knowledgeable one is a beloved matter and it is in itself an adornment and perfection attributed to him, then it is not fitting to love for this reason except Allah. The knowledge of the scholars is ignorance in comparison to His knowledge. Rather, whoever knows the most knowledgeable person of his time and the most ignorant person of his time, it becomes impossible for him to be ignorant that the knowledge of Allah is not encompassed by anyone, and that no one knows from His knowledge except what Allah has taught him. And this is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: "O you who have believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger and the Book which He sent down upon His Messenger and the Scripture which He sent down before. And whoever disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day has certainly strayed into far error." For He commanded belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day, and this is the knowledge by which the Truthful Ones are adorned. So whoever does not believe in this has certainly strayed into far error.
4:136.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

4:136.arabic: الوجه الأول: الذي لا يستند إلى معارضة الشك الاحتراز من الجزم خيفة ما فيه من تزكية النفس قال الله تعالى: ﴿ فلا تزكوا أنفسكم ﴾ {} وقال: ﴿ ألم تر إلى الذين يزكون أنفسهم ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ انظر كيف يفترون على الله الكذب ﴾ {} وقيل لحكيم ما الصدق القبيح فقال ثناء المرء على نفسه والإيمان من أعلى صفات المجد والجزم تزكية مطلقة وصيغة الاستثناء كأنها ثقل من عرف التزكية كما يقال للإنسان أنت طبيب أو فقيه أو مفسر فيقول نعم إن شاء الله لا في معرض التشكيك ولكن لإخراج نفسه عن تزكية نفسه فالصيغة صيغة الترديد والت
4:136.english: The first aspect: That which is not based on opposing doubt is the caution from certainty out of fear of what it contains of self-praise (Tazkiyah). Allah the Exalted said: 'So do not claim purity for yourselves' {} and said: 'Have you not seen those who claim purity for themselves?' {} and Allah the Exalted said: 'See how they invent lies against Allah' {} and it was said to a wise man: 'What is ugly truth?' He said: 'A person's praise of himself.' And Faith (Iman) is from the highest attributes of glory, and certainty is absolute self-praise, and the formula of exception is like a burden for one who recognizes self-praise, just as when it is said to a person: 'Are you a doctor or jurist or exegete?' and he says: 'Yes, if Allah wills,' not in the context of doubt but to remove himself from praising himself. So the formula is one of hesitation and weakening of the report itself, and its meaning is the weakening required by the implications of the report, which is self-praise. By this interpretation, if asked about a blameworthy description, exception would not be appropriate. The second aspect: The etiquette of mentioning Allah the Exalted in every situation and referring all matters to the will (Mashiyyah) of Allah the Exalted, for Allah the Exalted disciplined His Prophet ﷺ, so He said: 'And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow," except [when adding], "If Allah wills."' {} and He said: 'O you who have believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger and the Book which He sent down upon His Messenger and the Scripture which He sent down before. And whoever disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day has certainly gone far astray.' So He made Faith (Iman) subject to the will (Mashiyyah), and thus our saying 'We have believed in Allah and what has been revealed to us, if Allah wills' should be.
4:136.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

4:136.arabic: [10] حديث الإيمان بالحساب وتفاوت الخلق فيه إلى مناقش في الحساب ومسامح فيه وإلى من يدخل الجنة بغير حساب أخرجه البيهقي في البعث من حديث عمر فقال يا رسول الله ما الإيمان قال أن تؤمن بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله وبالموت والبعث من بعد الموت والحساب والجنة والنار والقدر كله الحديث وهو عند مسلم دون ذكر الحساب وللشيخين من حديث عائشة من نوقش الحساب عذب قالت قلت يقول الله تعالى فسوف يحاسب حسابا يسيرا قال ذلك العرض ولهما من حديث ابن عباس عرضت علي الأمم فقيل هذه أمتك ومعهم سبعون ألفا يدخلون الجنة بغير حساب ول
4:136.english: Hadith about Belief (Iman) in the Reckoning and the variation among creation in it, from one who is scrutinized in the Reckoning and one who is pardoned in it, and to one who enters Paradise without Reckoning. Al-Bayhaqi transmitted it in Al-Ba'th from the hadith of 'Umar, who said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what is Belief (Iman)?' He said: 'That you believe in Allah and His Angels (Mala'ikah) and His Books (Kutub) and His Messengers (Rusul) and in Death and Resurrection after Death and the Reckoning and Paradise and Hell and all of Predestination (Qadar).' The hadith is in Muslim without mention of the Reckoning. And for the two Shaykhs from the hadith of 'A'ishah: 'Whoever is scrutinized in the Reckoning is punished.' She said: 'I said: Allah says: "Then he will be reckoned with an easy reckoning." He said: 'That is the Presentation.' And for them from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas: 'The nations were shown to me, and it was said: "This is your nation, and with them are seventy thousand who enter Paradise without Reckoning and without punishment."' And in Muslim from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah and 'Imran ibn Husayn: 'Seventy thousand from my nation enter Paradise without Reckoning.' Al-Bayhaqi added in Al-Ba'th from the hadith of 'Amr ibn Hazm: 'And He gave me with each one of the seventy thousand seventy thousand.' Ahmad added from the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr after this addition: 'So why didn't you ask for more?' He said: 'I did ask for more, and He gave me with each man seventy thousand.' 'Umar said: 'So why didn't you ask for more?' He said: 'I did ask for more, and He gave me like this.' And 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr spread his hands. The hadith.
4:136.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

4:136.arabic: أما الترادف ففي قوله تعالى: ﴿ فأخرجنا من كان فيها من المؤمنين. فما وجدنا فيها غير بيت من المسلمين ﴾ {} ولم يكن بالاتفاق إلا بيت واحد وقال تعالى: ﴿ يا قوم إن كنتم آمنتم بالله فعليه توكلوا إن كنتم مسلمين ﴾ {} وقال ﭬ: (بني الإسلام على خمس[45]) وسئل رسول الله ﭬ مرة عن الإيمان فأجاب بهذه الخمس[46] وأما الاختلاف فقوله تعالى: ﴿ قالت الأعراب آمنا قل لم تؤمنوا ولكن قولوا أسلمنا ﴾ {} ومعناه استسلمنا في الظاهر فأراد بالإيمان ههنا التصديق بالقلب فقط وبالإسلام الاستسلام ظاهرا باللسان والجوارح، وفي حديث جبرائ
4:136.english: As for synonymy, it is in the saying of the Exalted: 'So We brought out those who were in it of the believers. And We found not in it except one house of the Muslims' {} and it was not by agreement except one house. And the Exalted said: 'O my people, if you have believed in Allah, then upon Him rely, if you are Muslims' {} and he (peace be upon him) said: 'Islam is built upon five [45]'. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was asked once about faith (Iman), so he answered with these five [46]. And as for difference, it is the saying of the Exalted: 'The Bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not believed; but say, 'We have submitted'"' {} and its meaning is: we have submitted outwardly. So He intended by faith (Iman) here only the affirmation (Tasdiq) with the heart (Qalb), and by Islam the outward submission (Istislam) with the tongue (Lisan) and limbs (Jawarih). And in the hadith of Gabriel (upon him be peace) when he asked him about faith (Iman), he said: 'That you believe in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers and the Last Day (Al-Yawm Al-Akhir) and the resurrection after death and the reckoning and the decree (Al-Qadr), its good and its evil.' Then he said: 'What is Islam?' So he answered by mentioning the five characteristics [47].
4:136.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Foundations of Belief'

4:136.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
4:136.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'What is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)".'
4:136.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

4:140.arabic: وقال ﭬ "أعظم الناس خطايا يوم القيامة أكثرهم خوضاً في الباطل"[40] وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى "وكنا نخوض مع الخائضين" وبقوله تعالى "فلا تقعدوا معهم حتى يخوضوا في حديث غيره إنكم إذاً مثلهم" وقال سلمان: أكثر الناس ذنوباً يوم القيامة أكثرهم كلاماً في معصية الله. وقال ابن سيرين: كان رجل من الأنصار يمر بمجلس لهم فيقول لهم توضئوا فإن بعض ما تقولون شر من الحديث. فهذا هو الخوض في الباطل وهو وراء ما سيأتي من الغيبة والنميمة والفحش وغيرها، بل هو الخوض في ذكر محظورات سبق وجودها أو تدبر للتوصل إليها من غير حاج
4:140.english: And he (peace be upon him) said: "The greatest people in sins on the Day of Resurrection are those who most engage in falsehood (Bāṭil)." [40] And to this is the allusion in His saying, the Exalted: "And we used to engage with those who engage" and in His saying, the Exalted: "So do not sit with them until they engage in a talk other than it; indeed, you would then be like them." And Salmān said: "The people with the most sins on the Day of Resurrection are those who speak most in disobedience to Allah." And Ibn Sīrīn said: "A man from the Helpers (Anṣār) would pass by their gathering and say to them: 'Perform ablution (Wuḍūʾ), for some of what you say is worse than obscene talk.'" This is the engagement in falsehood (Bāṭil), and it is beyond what will come of backbiting (Ghaybah), tale-bearing (Namīmah), obscenity (Fuḥsh), and others. Rather, it is the engagement in mentioning prohibitions that have previously occurred or contemplating to reach them without a religious need to mention them.
4:140.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

4:141.arabic: فإن قيل فليجز للكافر الذمي أن يحتسب على المسلم إذا رآه يزني لأن قوله لا تزن حق في نفسه فمحال أن يكون حراما عليه بل ينبغي أن يكون مباحا أو واجبا قلنا الكافر إن منع المسلم بفعله فهو تسلط عليه فيمنع من حيث إنه تسلط وما جعل الله للكافرين على المؤمنين سبيلا وأما مجرد قوله لا تزن فليس بمحرم عليه من حيث إنه نهي عن الزنا ولكن من حيث إنه إظهار دالة الاحتكام على المسلم وفيه إذلال للمحتكم عليه والفاسق يستحق الإذلال ولكن لا من الكافر الذي هو أولى بالذل منه فهذا وجه منعنا إياه من الحسبة وإلا فلسنا نقول إن ال
4:141.english: If it is said: 'It should be permissible for the protected non-Muslim (al-Kāfir al-Dhimmi) to enjoin good (iḥtisāb) upon a Muslim if he sees him committing adultery, because his saying "Do not commit adultery" is true in itself, so it is impossible for it to be forbidden for him; rather, it should be permissible or obligatory.' We say: The non-believer (al-Kāfir), if he prevents the Muslim by his action, that is an act of domination (tasalluṭ) over him, so he is prevented because it is domination. And Allah has not made for the non-believers (al-Kāfirīn) over the believers (al-Mu'minīn) any way (sabīl). As for his mere saying "Do not commit adultery," it is not forbidden for him in terms of it being a prohibition against adultery, but in terms of it being a display of the authority (dālah) of adjudication over the Muslim, and in it is humiliation (idhlāl) for the one being adjudicated. The corrupt person (al-Fāsiq) deserves humiliation, but not from the non-believer who is more deserving of humiliation than him. This is the aspect of our preventing him from enjoining good (al-ḥisbah). Otherwise, we do not say that the non-believer is punished because of his saying "Do not commit adultery" in terms of it being a prohibition; rather, we say that if he does not say "Do not commit adultery," he is punished for it if we consider the non-believer's address regarding the branches of religion, and there is consideration in that which we have fully covered in the jurisprudential matters, and it is not suitable for our purpose now.
4:141.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

4:142.arabic: وقال تعالى في ذم المنافقين: ﴿ ولا يذكرون الله إلا قليلا ﴾ {}
4:142.english: And He, the Exalted, said in censuring the hypocrites: 'And they do not remember Allah except a little.'
4:142.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God

4:143.arabic: فإن كنت لا تشاهد هذا هكذا فما أراك إلا مخنثاً بين فحولة التنزيه وأنوثة التشبيه، مذبذباً بين هذا وذا لا إلى هؤلاء ولا إلى هؤلاء، فكيف نزهت ذاته وصفاته تعالى عن الأجسام وصفاتها؟ ونزهت كلامه عن معاني الحروف والأصوات وأخذت تتوقف في يده وقلمه ولوحه وخطه؟
4:143.english: If you do not witness this thus, then I see you only as effeminate between the masculinity of Transcendence (Tanzih) and the femininity of Anthropomorphism (Tashbih), wavering between this and that, not to these nor to these. How did you declare His Essence (Dhat) and His Attributes (Sifat) transcendent from bodies and their attributes? And declared His Speech (Kalam) transcendent from the meanings of letters and sounds, yet you began to hesitate about His Hand (Yad), His Pen (Qalam), His Tablet (Lawh), and His Writing (Khatt)?
4:143.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

4:144.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
4:144.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Whatever is in the Quran of 'O you who believe' is in the Torah 'O you poor ones (al-Masakin)'.
4:144.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

4:145.arabic: ومهما كان السلاطين ظلمة ولم يقدر القاضي على القضاء إلا بمداهنتهم وإهمال بعض الحقوق لأجلهم ولأجل المتعلقين بهم، إذ يعلم أنه لو حكم عليهم بالحق لعزلوه أو لم يطيعوه، فليس له أن يتقلد القضاء، وإن تقلد فعليه أن يطالبهم بالحقوق ولا يكون خوف العزل عذراً مرخصاً له في الإهمال أصلاً، بل إذا عزل سقطت العهدة عنه، فينبغي أن يفرح بالعزل إن كان يقضي لله، فإن لم تسمح نفسه بذلك فهو إذن يقضي لأتباع الهوى والشيطان، فكيف يرتقب عليه ثواباً؟ وهو مع الظلمة في الدرك الأسفل من النار. إِنَّ الْمُنَافِقِينَ فِي الدَّرْكِ
4:145.english: Whenever the rulers are oppressive and the judge is unable to judge except by flattering them and neglecting some rights for their sake and for the sake of those attached to them, since he knows that if he judged them with truth they would remove him or not obey him, then it is not for him to assume the judgeship. And if he assumes it, then upon him is to demand the rights from them, and fear of removal should not be an excuse permitting him in neglect at all. Rather, if he is removed, the responsibility falls from him. He should rejoice in the removal if he was judging for Allah. If his soul (Nafs) does not permit that, then he is indeed judging for following the caprice (Hawa) and the Satan (Shaytan). So how can he expect reward? And he is with the oppressors in the lowest depth (Al-Dark Al-Asfal) of the Fire. 'Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depth (Al-Dark Al-Asfal) of the Fire, and never will you find for them a helper.'
4:145.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

4:145.arabic: ما هذا من علامات الإيمان لو كان الإيمان باللسان فلم كان المنافقون في الدرك الأسفل من النار ويحك يا نفس كأنك لا تؤمنين بيوم الحساب وتظنين أنك إذا مت انفلت وتخلصت وهيهات أتحسبين أنك تتركين سدى ألم تكونى نطفة من منى يمنى ثم كنت علقة فخلق فسوى أليس ذلك بقادر على أن يحيى الموتى فإن كان هذا من إضمارك فما أكفرك وأجهلك
4:145.english: What is this from the signs of faith (Iman) if faith were by the tongue alone? Then why were the hypocrites (Al-Munafiqun) in the lowest depth (Al-Dark Al-Asfal) of the Fire? Woe to you, O Soul (Nafs)! It is as if you do not believe in the Day of Reckoning (Yawm Al-Hisab) and you think that if you die, you will escape and be freed. Far from it! Do you reckon that you will be left neglected? Were you not a drop of semen (Nutfah) emitted? Then you were a clinging clot (Alaqah), then He created and proportioned. Is not That One capable of reviving the dead? If this is from your hidden thoughts, then how disbelieving (Kafir) and ignorant you are!
4:145.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

4:145.arabic: وإنما يضاعف عذاب العالم في معصيته لأنه عصى من علم ولذلك قال الله عز وجل: (إن المنافقين في الدرك الأسفل من النار( (النساء:145). لأنهم جحدوا بعد العلم وجعل اليهود شرا من النصارى مع أنهم ما جعلوا لله سبحانه ولدا ولا قالوا إنه ثالث ثلاثة إلا أنهم أنكروا بعد المعرفة إذ قال الله (يعرفونه كما يعرفون أبناءهم( (البقرة:146) (الأنعام:20). وقال تعالى: (فلما جاءهم ما عرفوا كفروا به فلعنة الله على الكافرين( (البقرة:89). وقال تعالى في قصة بلعام بن باعوراء (واتل عليهم نبأ الذي آتيناه آياتنا فانسلخ منها فأتبعه ا
4:145.english: And indeed the punishment of the scholar in his disobedience is multiplied because he disobeyed from knowledge, and therefore Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed the hypocrites are in the lowest depth of the Fire' (An-Nisa:145). Because they denied after knowledge, and He made the Jews worse than the Christians even though they did not make for Allah the Glorified a son nor did they say He is the third of three, except that they rejected after recognition (Ma'rifah) when Allah said: 'They recognize him as they recognize their sons' (Al-Baqarah:146) (Al-An'am:20). And He the Exalted said: 'So when came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it, so the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers' (Al-Baqarah:89). And He the Exalted said in the story of Balaam son of Ba'ura: 'And recite to them the news of him to whom We gave Our signs, but he detached himself from them, so Satan followed him, and he became of the deviators' (Al-A'raf:175) until He said: 'So his likeness is as the likeness of a dog; if you attack him, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants' (Al-A'raf:176). Likewise the wicked scholar, for Balaam was given the Book of Allah the Exalted but he inclined to the desires, so he was likened to the dog, meaning whether he was given wisdom or not given, he pants to the desires.
4:145.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

4:145.arabic: ولذلك شدد أمر المنافقين فقال تعالى "إن المنافقين في الدرك الأسفل من النار" لأن الكافر كفر وأظهر وهذا كفر وستر، فكان ستره لكفره كفراً آخر لأنه استخف بنظر الله سبحانه وتعالى إلى قلبه وعظم نظر المخلوقين فمحا الكفر عن ظاهره.
4:145.english: And therefore He intensified the matter of the hypocrites, so He the Exalted said: "Indeed the hypocrites are in the lowest depth of the Fire" because the disbeliever disbelieved and manifested it, and this is disbelief and concealment, so his concealment of his disbelief became another disbelief because he belittled the gaze of God, glorified and exalted is He, upon his heart (Qalb) and magnified the gaze of the created beings, thus erasing disbelief from his outward appearance.
4:145.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Harms of the Tongue'

4:146.arabic: فضيلة الإخلاص قال الله تعالى (وما أمروا إلا ليعبدوا الله مخلصين له الدين) وقال (ألا لله الدين الخالص) وقال تعالى (إلا الذين تابوا وأصلحوا واعتصموا بالله وأخلصوا دينهم لله) وقال تعالى (فمن كان يرجو لقاء ربه فليعمل عملا صالحا ولا يشرك بعبادة ربه أحدا) نزلت فيمن يعمل لله ويحب أن يحمد عليه وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: (ثلاث لا يغل عليهن قلب رجل مسلم إخلاص العمل لله)[36] وعن مصعب بن سعد عن أبيه قال ظن أبى أن له فضلا على من هو دونه من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم
4:146.english: The Virtue of Sincerity (Ikhlas). Allah the Exalted said: 'And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, [being] sincere to Him in religion' (Quran 98:5). And He said: 'Unquestionably, for Allah is the pure religion' (Quran 39:3). And Allah the Exalted said: 'Except those who repent, correct [their affairs], hold fast to Allah, and purify their religion for Allah; for those will be with the believers. And Allah is going to give the believers a great reward' (Quran 4:146). And Allah the Exalted said: 'So whoever would hope for the meeting with his Lord - let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone' (Quran 18:110). This was revealed concerning one who acts for Allah but loves to be praised for it. And the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'Three things, the Heart (Qalb) of a Muslim man does not harbor malice regarding them: sincerity of action for Allah' [36]. And from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd from his father, he said: My father thought he had superiority over those below him among the companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, so the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'Indeed, Allah the Mighty and Majestic supports this nation through its weak ones, their supplication, and their sincerity' [37]. And from Al-Hasan, he said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'Allah the Exalted says: Sincerity (Ikhlas) is a secret from My secrets; I have deposited it in the Heart (Qalb) of whom I love from My servants' [38]. And 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah honor his face, said: 'Do not be concerned with the smallness of the action, but be concerned with acceptance, for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to Mu'adh ibn Jabal: Purify the action, and a little of it will suffice you' [39]. And he, peace be upon him, said: 'There is no servant who purifies his action for Allah for forty days except that the springs of Wisdom (Hikmah) appear from his Heart (Qalb) upon his tongue' [40]. And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'The first to be questioned on the Day of Resurrection are three: a man whom Allah gave knowledge, so Allah the Exalted says: What did you do with what you knew? He says: My Lord, I would stand [in prayer] during the night and the ends of the day. So Allah the Exalted says: You have lied, and the angels say: You have lied, rather...'
4:146.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

4:147.arabic: اعلم ان الله تعالى قرن الشكر بالذكر في كتابه مع انه قال: ﴿ ولذكر الله اكبر ﴾ {} فقال تعالى: ﴿ فاذكروني اذكركم واشكروا لي ولا تكفرون ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ ما يفعل الله بعذابكم ان شكرتم وآمنتم ﴾ {} وقال تعالى ﴿ وسنجزي الشاكرين ﴾ {}. وقال عز وجل إخبارا عن ابليس اللعين: ﴿ لأقعدن لهم صراطك المستقيم ﴾ {} قيل هو طريق الشكر ولعلو رتبة الشكر طعن اللعين في الخلق فقال: ولا تجد أكثرهم شاكرين وقال تعالى: ﴿ وقليل من عبادي الشكور ﴾ {} وقد قطع الله تعالى بالمزيد مع الشكر ولم يستثن فقال تعالى: ﴿ لئن شكرتم لأزيدنكم
4:147.english: Know that Allah the Exalted coupled Gratitude (Shukr) with Remembrance (Dhikr) in His Book, even though He said: 'And the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah is greater' (Quran 29:45). So He the Exalted said: 'So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me' (Quran 2:152). And He the Exalted said: 'What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe?' (Quran 4:147). And He the Exalted said: 'And We will reward the grateful ones' (Quran 3:145). And He the Mighty and Majestic informed about Iblis the accursed: 'I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path' (Quran 7:16). It is said it is the path of Gratitude (Shukr), and due to the high rank of Gratitude (Shukr), the accursed one disparaged the creation, saying: 'And you will not find most of them grateful' (Quran 7:17). And He the Exalted said: 'And few of My servants are grateful' (Quran 34:13). And Allah the Exalted affirmed increase with Gratitude (Shukr) without exception, saying: 'If you are grateful, I will surely increase you' (Quran 14:7). And He made exceptions in five things: in enrichment, response, provision, forgiveness, and repentance, saying: 'Then Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills' (Quran 9:28), and said: 'And He removes what you call to if He wills' (Quran 42:30), and said: 'He provides for whom He wills without account' (Quran 2:212), and said: 'And He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills' (Quran 4:48), and said: 'And Allah turns in forgiveness to whom He wills' (Quran 9:27). And it is a character from the characters of Lordship (Rububiyyah), as He the Exalted said: 'And Allah is Appreciative (Shakur) and Forbearing' (Quran 64:17). And Allah made Gratitude (Shukr) the key to the speech of the people of Paradise, saying: 'And they will say, "Praise to Allah, who has fulfilled for us His promise"' (Quran 39:74), and said: 'And their last call will be, "Praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds"' (Quran 10:10).
4:147.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

4:170.arabic: أنه فيماذا يتفكر لم يقدر عليه  لأن  مجارى  الفكر  غير  محصورة وثمراته غير متناهية نعم نحن نجتهد في ضبط مجاريه بالإضافة  إلى  مهمات  العلوم الدينية وبالإضافة إلى الأحوال التى هى مقامات السالكين ويكون ذلك  ضبطا  جمليا فإن تفصيل ذلك يستدعى شرح العلوم كلها وجملة هذه  الكتب  كالشرح  لبعضها  فإنها مشتملة على علوم تلك العلوم تستفاد من أفكار مخصوصة فلنشر إلى ضبط الجامع  فيها ليحصل الوقوف على مجارى الفكر.                              بيان مجارى الفكر أعلم أن الفكر قد يجرى في أمر يتعلق بالدين وقد يجرى  في
4:170.english: That in what he thinks about, he cannot encompass it because the channels of thought are not limited and its fruits are endless. Yes, we strive to regulate its channels in addition to the important matters of the religious sciences and in addition to the states (Ahwal) which are the stations (Maqamat) of the travelers (Salikin), and that will be a comprehensive regulation. For detailing that requires explaining all the sciences, and the entirety of these books is like an explanation for some of them, for they contain the sciences of those sciences derived from specific thoughts. So let us proceed to regulate the comprehensive in them to achieve understanding of the channels of thought.                              Explanation of the Channels of Thought Know that thought may run in a matter related to religion and may run in what is related to non-religion. Our aim is only what is related to religion, so let us leave the other division and focus on religion, the transaction (Mu'amalah) that is between the servant (Abd) and the Lord (Rabb) Almighty. So all the thoughts of the servant either relate to the servant and his attributes (Sifat) and his states (Ahwal), or relate to the Worshipped One (Ma'bud) and His attributes (Sifat) and His actions. It is not possible to go beyond these two divisions. And what relates to the servant is either a consideration of what is beloved (Mahbub) to the Lord Almighty or of what is disliked (Makruh), and there is no need for thought in other than these two divisions. And what relates to the Lord Almighty is either a consideration of His Essence (Dhat) and His attributes (Sifat) and His Beautiful Names (Asma' al-Husna), or it is in His actions and His dominion (Mulk) and His sovereignty (Malakut) and all that is in the heavens and the earth and what is between them. And it becomes clear to you the confinement of thought in these divisions by an example, which is that the state of those who travel to Allah Almighty and yearn for His meeting relates to his Beloved (Ma'shuq) or relates to himself. So if he thinks about his Beloved, then either he thinks about His beauty and the goodness of His image in His Essence to delight in thinking about Him and witnessing Him, or he thinks about His gentle, good actions indicating His character traits (Akhlaq) and attributes (Sifat) to be that which doubles the pleasure and strengthens his love (Mahabbah). And if he thinks about himself, then his thought is in his attributes (Sifat) which drop him from the eye of his Beloved so that he abstains from them, or in the attributes (Sifat) which bring him near to Him and make him beloved to Him so that he becomes characterized by them. So if he thinks about something outside of these divisions, then that is outside the limit of passionate love (Ishq) and is a deficiency in it because the complete, perfect passionate love (Ishq) is what overwhelms the lover (Ashiq) and fills the heart (Qalb) so that it does not leave in it room for other than Him. So the lover (Muhibb) of Allah Almighty should be like that, so his view and thought do not go beyond his Beloved. And whenever his thought is confined in these four divisions, it is not at all outside the requirement of love (Mahabbah). So let us begin with the first division, which is his thinking about the attributes (Sifat) of himself and the actions of himself to distinguish the beloved (Mahbub) among them from the disliked (Makruh). For this thought is that which relates to the science of transaction (Ilm al-Mu'amalah) which is the intended purpose of this book. And as for the other division, it relates to the science of unveiling (Ilm al-Mukashafah), then every.
4:170.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Contemplation'

4:171.arabic: نجز أولا أشغاله وليشد رحاله وليجعل آخر أشغاله وداع البيت ووداعه بأن يطوف به سبعا ما سبق ولكن من غير رمل واضطباع فإذا فرغ منه صلى ركعتين خلف المقام وشرب من ماء زمزم ثم يأتي الملتزم ويدعو ويتضرع ويقول اللهم إن البيت بيتك والعبد عبدك وابن عبدك وابن أمتك حملتني على ما سخرت لي من خلقك حتى سيرتني في بلادك وبلغتني بنعمتك حتى أعنتني على قضاء مناسكك فإن كنت رضيت عني فازدد عني رضا وإلا فمن الآن قبل تباعدي عن بيتك هذا أوان انصرافي إن أذنت لي غير مستبدل بك ولا ببيتك ولا راغب عنك ولا عن بيتك اللهم أصحبني الع
4:171.english: First, he should complete his affairs, prepare his journey, and make his final task the farewell to the House (the Kaaba) and his farewell by circumambulating it seven times as previously mentioned, but without the rapid walking (ramal) and uncovering the right shoulder (idhtiba'). When he finishes, he prays two rak'ahs behind the Station (of Abraham) and drinks from the water of Zamzam. Then he comes to the Multazam (the area between the Black Stone and the door of the Kaaba) and supplicates and humbly implores, saying: O Allah, indeed the House is Your House, and the servant is Your servant, and the son of Your servant, and the son of Your maidservant. You have carried me on what You have subjugated for me from Your creation until You have journeyed me in Your lands and brought me to completion with Your favor until You have aided me in performing Your rites. If You are pleased with me, then increase Your pleasure with me; otherwise, from now before my distancing from Your House, this is the time of my departure if You permit me, not substituting You nor Your House, nor desiring away from You nor from Your House. O Allah, accompany me with well-being in my body and protection (al-'ismah) in my religion, and make my return good, and grant me Your obedience always as long as You keep me alive, and gather for me the good of this world and the Hereafter. Indeed, You are over all things competent. O Allah, do not make this the last of my covenant with Your Sacred House, and if You make it the last of my covenant, then compensate me with Paradise for it. And it is preferred that he not turn his gaze away from the House until it disappears from his sight. (The Tenth Section on Visiting Medina and Its Etiquettes) He (peace be upon him) said: (Whoever visits me after my death is as if he visited me in my life[58]) and He (peace be upon him) said: (Whoever finds the means and does not come to me has been neglectful of me[59]) and He (peace be upon him) said: (Whoever comes to me as a visitor with no concern except visiting me, it is a right upon Allah, the Exalted, that I be an intercessor for him[60]). So whoever intends to visit Medina, let him send blessings upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) frequently on his way. When his sight falls upon the walls of Medina and its trees, let him say: O Allah, this is the sanctuary of Your Messenger, so make it for me a protection from the Fire and a safety from the punishment and the evil of the reckoning. And let him perform ablution before entering from the well of al-Harrah, and let him perfume himself, and let him wear his cleanest clothes. When he enters it, let him enter it humbly, honoring it, and let him say: In the name of Allah and upon the religion of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him). O Lord, cause me to enter a truthful entrance and cause me to exit a truthful exit, and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority. Then he heads to the mosque and enters it and prays beside the pulpit two rak'ahs, and he makes the pillar of the pulpit aligned with his right shoulder, and he faces the column beside which is the chest, and the circle that is in the direction of the mosque's qibla is between his eyes. That is the standing place of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) before the mosque was altered. And let him strive to pray in the first mosque before it was expanded. Then he comes to the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him) and stands at his face, which is by turning his back to the qibla and facing the wall of the grave at about four cubits from the column that is in the corner of the grave's wall, and he places the lamp above his head. And it is not from the Sunnah to touch the wall nor to kiss it; rather, standing from a distance is closer to respect. So he stands and says: Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. Peace be upon you, O Prophet of Allah. Peace be upon you, O Trustworthy...
4:171.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

4:171.arabic: ن أغر امرأة بنفسي. وقد قيل فضل المتأهل على العزب كفضل المجاهد على القاعد وركعة من متأهل افضل من سبعين ركعة من عزب وأما ما جاء في الترهيب عن النكاح فقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم (خير الناس بعد المائتين الخفيف الحاذ الذي لا أهل له ولا ولد)[12]. وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم (يأتي على الناس زمان يكون هلاك الرجل على يد زوجته وأبويه وولده يعيرونه بالفقر ويكلفونه ما لا يطيق فيدخل المداخل التي يذهب فيها دينه فيهلك.)[13] وفي الخبر قلة العيال أحد اليسارين وكثرتهم أحد الفقرين.[14] وسئل أبو سليمان الداراني عن النكا
4:171.english: I am not tempted by a woman for myself. And it has been said: The superiority of the married person over the celibate is like the superiority of the fighter over the sedentary, and one prayer cycle (rak'ah) from a married person is better than seventy prayer cycles from a celibate. As for what has come in discouragement from marriage, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'The best of people after two hundred are the light, skillful one who has no family (ahl) nor child.'[12] And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'A time will come upon people when a man's destruction will be at the hands of his wife, his parents, and his child; they reproach him with poverty and burden him with what he cannot bear, so he enters paths in which his religion (deen) goes and he perishes.'[13] And in the report: 'Few dependents are one of the two riches, and many of them are one of the two poverties.'[14] Abu Sulayman al-Darani was asked about marriage, and he said: 'Patience (sabr) away from them is better than patience with them, and patience with them is better than patience in the Fire.' And he also said: 'The solitary one finds from the sweetness of action and the emptiness of the heart (qalb) what the married person does not find.' And he said once: 'I have not seen any of our companions marry and remain at his first rank.' And he also said: 'Three things: whoever seeks them has leaned towards the world—whoever seeks a livelihood, or marries a woman, or writes hadith.' And al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'When Allah wills good for a servant, He does not busy him with family (ahl) nor wealth.' And Ibn Abi al-Hawari said: 'A group discussed this hadith, and their opinion settled that its meaning is not that he should not have them, but that he should have them and they do not busy him.' And it is an allusion to the saying of Abu Sulayman al-Darani: 'Whatever busies you from Allah of family (ahl), wealth, and child, it is ominous for you.' In summary, encouragement away from marriage has not been transmitted from anyone absolutely except accompanied by a condition, while encouragement in marriage has come absolutely and accompanied by a condition. So let us uncover the cover by enumerating the harms and benefits of marriage. Harms and Benefits of Marriage It contains five benefits: 1. The child 2. And breaking desire (shahwah) 3. And managing the household 4. And increasing the clan 5. And struggling with the soul (nafs) by undertaking them. The first benefit: The child, and it is the foundation, and for it marriage is established, and the intended purpose is preserving progeny and that the world not be empty of the human species. And indeed, desire (shahwah) was created as an instigator and inciter, like the one entrusted with the male in extracting the seed and with the female in enabling the plowing, as a gentleness with them in driving to capturing the child due to intercourse, like the gentleness with the bird in scattering the grain it desires to be driven to the net. And the eternal power (qudrah) was not incapable of creating individuals initially without cultivation and pairing, but wisdom (hikmah) necessitated arranging effects on causes while being independent of them, to manifest the power and complete the wonders of craftsmanship and realize what the will (mashiyyah) preceded with, the word (kalimah) was true with, and the pen (qalam) flowed with. And in attaining the child, there is a means of closeness m
4:171.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

4:171.arabic: اذهبوا إلى عيسى عليه السلام فيأتون عيسى فيقولون يا عيسى أنت رسول الله وكلمته ألقاها إلى مريم وروح منه وكلمت الناس فى المهد اشفع لنا إلى ربك ألا ترى ما نحن فيه فيقول عيسى عليه السلام إن ربى غضب اليوم غضبا لم يغضب قبله مثله ولن يغضب بعده مثله ولم يذكر ذنبا نفسى نفسى اذهبوا إلى غيرى اذهبوا إلى محمد ﭬ
4:171.english: Go to Jesus (Isa), peace be upon him. So they come to Jesus and say: O Jesus, you are the Messenger of Allah and His Word (Kalimah) which He cast to Mary and a Spirit (Ruh) from Him, and you spoke to people in the cradle. Intercede for us to your Lord, do you not see what we are in? Then Jesus, peace be upon him, says: Indeed my Lord has become angry today with an anger like which He has not become angry before and will not become angry after, and he does not mention a sin. Myself, myself, go to another, go to Muhammad ﷺ.
4:171.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Book of Repentance'

4:172.arabic: اعلم أن المتكبر عليه هو الله تعالى أو رسله أو سائر خلقه، وقد خلق الإنسان ظلوماً جهولاً، فتارة يتكبر على الخلق وتارة يتكبر على الخالق، فإذن التكبر باعتبار المتكبر عليه ثلاثة أقسام: الأول: التكبر على الله؛ وذلك هو أفحش أنواع الكبر، ولا مثار له إلا الجهل المحض والطغيان مثل ما كان من نمرود فإنه كان يحدث نفسه بأن يقاتل رب السماء وكما يحكي عن جماعة من الجهلة. بل ما يحكي عن كل من ادعى الربوبية مثل فرعون وغيره، فإنه لتكبره قال: أنا ربكم الأعلى، إذ استنكف أن يكون عبداً لله، ولذلك قال تعالى "إن الذين يستك
4:172.english: Know that the one upon whom arrogance is directed is Allah the Exalted, or His messengers, or the rest of His creation. And He created the human being as oppressive and ignorant. So sometimes he becomes arrogant towards the creation and sometimes towards the Creator. Therefore, arrogance, with consideration to the one upon whom it is directed, is of three divisions: The first: Arrogance towards Allah; and that is the most vile of the types of arrogance, and it has no source except pure ignorance and transgression, like what was from Nimrod, for he would converse with himself about fighting the Lord of the heavens, and as is narrated about a group of the ignorant. Rather, what is narrated about everyone who claimed lordship, like Pharaoh and others, for due to his arrogance he said: 'I am your highest lord,' since he disdained to be a slave (abd) of Allah. And for that reason, Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, those who are arrogant towards My worship will enter Hell in humiliation.' And Allah the Exalted said: 'Never will the Messiah disdain to be a slave (abd) of Allah, nor the angels brought near.' The verse. And Allah the Exalted said: 'And when it is said to them: Prostrate to the Most Merciful, they say: And what is the Most Merciful? Shall we prostrate to that which you order us?' And it increased them in aversion.
4:172.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

4:172.arabic: القسم الأول: التكبر على الله؛ وذلك هو أفحش أنواع الكبر، ولا مثار له إلا الجهل المحض والطغيان مثل ما كان من نمرود فإنه كان يحدث نفسه بأن يقاتل رب السماء وكما يحكى عن جماعة من الجهلة. بل ما يحكى عن كل من ادعى الربوبية مثل فرعون وغيره، فإنه لتكبره قال: أنا ربكم الأعلى، إذ استنكف أن يكون عبداً لله، ولذلك قال تعالى "إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي سيدخلون جهنم داخرين" وقال تعالى "لن يستنكف المسيح أن يكون عبداً لله ولا الملائكة المقربون" الآية وقال تعالى "وإذا قيل لهم اسجدوا للرحمن قالوا وما الرحمن أنسجد
4:172.english: The first division: Arrogance (Takabbur) towards Allah; and that is the most vile of types of arrogance, and its source is nothing but pure ignorance (Jahl) and transgression (Tughyan) like what was from Nimrod, for he would tell himself that he would fight the Lord of the heavens, and as is narrated about a group of the ignorant. Rather, what is narrated about everyone who claimed lordship (Rububiyyah) like Pharaoh and others, for due to his arrogance he said: 'I am your highest lord,' since he disdained (Istankafa) to be a servant (Abd) of Allah, and therefore Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, those who are arrogant (Yastakbirun) about My worship (Ibadati) will enter Hell in humiliation,' and Allah the Exalted said: 'Never will the Messiah disdain (Yastankif) to be a servant (Abd) of Allah nor the angels brought near (Al-Muqarrabun),' the verse, and Allah the Exalted said: 'And when it is said to them: Prostrate to the Most Merciful (Al-Rahman), they say: And what is the Most Merciful? Shall we prostrate to that which you order us?' and it increased them in aversion.
4:172.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

5:1.arabic: فإن اللسان سباق إلى الوعد، ثم النفس ربما لا تسمح بالوفاء فيصير الوعد خلفاً وذلك من أمارات النفاق قال الله تعالى "يا أيها الذين آمنوا أوفوا بالعقود" وقال ﭬ "العدة عطية"[128] وقال ﭬ "الوأي مثل الدين أو أفضل"[129] والوأي: الوعد. وقد أثنى الله تعالى على نبيه اسمعيل عليه السلام في كتابه العزيز فقال "إنه كان صادق الوعد" قيل إنه وعد إنساناً في موضع فلم يرجع إليه ذلك الإنسان بل نسي، فبقي اسمعيل اثنين وعشرين يوماً في انتظاره.
5:1.english: For the tongue is quick to promise, then the Soul (Nafs) perhaps does not permit fulfillment, so the promise becomes broken, and that is from the signs of hypocrisy. Allah the Exalted said: "O you who have believed, fulfill [your] contracts." And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "The promise is a gift." And he said: "The promise (al-wa'y) is like debt or better." And al-wa'y: the promise. And Allah the Exalted praised His prophet Ishmael (peace be upon him) in His Noble Book, saying: "Indeed, he was true to his promise." It is said that he promised a person in a place, but that person did not return to him; rather, he forgot, so Ishmael remained twenty-two days waiting for him.
5:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

5:1.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
5:1.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'What is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones."'
5:1.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

5:2.arabic: وقال تعالى وتعاونوا على البر والتقوى ولا تعاونوا على الإثم والعدوان وهو أمر جزم ومعنى التعاون الحث عليه وتسهيل طرق الخير وسد سبل الشر والعدوان بحسب الإمكان
5:2.english: And Allah the Exalted said: 'And cooperate upon righteousness (Al-Birr) and piety (Al-Taqwa) and do not cooperate upon sin (Al-Ithm) and aggression (Al-'Udwan).' This is a decisive command, and the meaning of cooperation is urging upon it and facilitating the paths of goodness and blocking the ways of evil and aggression according to possibility.
5:2.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

5:2.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
5:2.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'Whatever is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)".'
5:2.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

5:3.arabic: أما بعد: فإن الحج من بين أركان الإسلام ومبانيه عبادة العمر وختام الأمر وتمام الإسلام وكمال الدين فيه أنزل الله عز وجل قوله: ﴿ اليوم أكملت لكم دينكم وأتممت عليكم نعمتي ورضيت لكم الإسلام دينا ﴾ {} وفيه قال ﭬ: (من مات ولم يحج فليمت إن شاء يهوديا وإن شاء نصرانيا[1]) فأعظم بعبادة يعدم الدين بفقدها الكمال ويساوي تاركها اليهود والنصارى في الضلال وأجدر بها أن تصرف العناية إلى شرحها وتفصيل أركانها وسننها وآدابها وفضائلها وأسرارها وجملة ذلك ينكشف بتوفيق الله عز وجل في ثلاثة أبواب.
5:3.english: After: Indeed, the Pilgrimage (Hajj) is among the pillars of Islam and its foundations, the worship of a lifetime and the seal of the matter, and the completion of Islam and the perfection of the religion (Din) in it, Allah the Exalted revealed His saying: 'Today I have perfected for you your religion (Din) and completed upon you My favor and have approved for you Islam as religion (Din).' {} And in it He said ﭬ: (Whoever dies without having performed the pilgrimage, then let him die if he wishes as a Jew or if he wishes as a Christian[1]) So how great is a worship whose absence deprives the religion (Din) of perfection and equates its abandoner with the Jews and Christians in misguidance, and it is most deserving that attention be directed to explaining it and detailing its pillars, its traditions, its etiquettes, its virtues, and its secrets, and the totality of that is unveiled by the success of Allah the Exalted in three chapters.
5:3.topic: Al-Ghazali on the outer and inner dimensions of worship, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

5:3.arabic: وقال بعض السلف إذا وافق يوم عرفة يوم جمعة غفر لكل أهل عرفة وهو أفضل يوم في الدنيا وفيه. (حج رسول الله ﷺ حجة الوداع وكان واقفا إذ نزل قوله عز وجل: ﴿ الْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ وَأَتْمَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعْمَتِي وَرَضِيتُ لَكُمُ الْإِسْلَامَ دِينًا ﴾ {المائدة: 3}) قال أهل الكتاب لو أنزلت هذه الآية علينا لجعلناها يوم عيد. فقال عمر رضي الله عنه: أشهد لقد نزلت هذه الآية في يوم عيدين اثنين يوم عرفة ويوم جمعة على رسول الله ﷺ وهو واقف بعرفة.
5:3.english: And some of the predecessors said: If the Day of Arafah coincides with Friday, forgiveness is granted to all the people of Arafah, and it is the best day in the world, and in it. (The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed the Farewell Pilgrimage and was standing when the words of the Almighty descended: 'Today I have perfected for you your religion (Deen) and completed upon you My favor and have approved for you Islam as religion (Deen).' {Al-Ma'idah: 3}) The People of the Book said: If this verse had been revealed to us, we would have made it a day of celebration. Then Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: I bear witness that this verse was indeed revealed on two celebration days: the Day of Arafah and Friday, upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was standing at Arafah.
5:3.topic: Al-Ghazali on the outer and inner dimensions of worship, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

5:3.arabic: قال العلماء قد أتم الله علينا نعمته برضاه الإسلام لنا إذ قال تعالى: ﴿ وأتممت عليكم نعمتي ورضيت لكم الإسلام دينا ﴾ {} وفي الخبر: (إذا أذنب العبد ذنبا فاستغفر الله يقول الله عز وجل لملائكته انظروا إلى عبدي أذنب ذنبا فعلم أن له ربا يغفر الذنوب ويأخذ بالذنب أشهدكم أني قد غفرت له[22])
5:3.english: The scholars said: Allah has completed His favor upon us by His acceptance of Islam for us, as He said: 'And I have completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion.' {} And in the report: 'When the servant (al-'abd) commits a sin and seeks forgiveness from Allah, Allah says to His angels: Look at My servant who committed a sin but knew that he has a Lord who forgives sins and takes account of sins. I bear witness to you that I have forgiven him.'
5:3.topic: Al-Ghazali on the outer and inner dimensions of worship, from 'Fear and Hope'

5:6.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
5:6.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'What is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (Masakin)"'
5:6.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

5:7.arabic: ولذلك قال عز وجل: (لعلهم يتذكرون) ، (وليتذكر أولوا الألباب)، (واذكروا نعمة الله عليكم وميثاقه الذي واثقكم به)، (ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر فهل من مدكر)؛ وتسمية هذا النمط تذكرا ليس ببعيد فكأن التذكر ضربان أحدهما أن يذكر صورة كانت حاضرة الوجود في قلبه لكن غابت بعد الوجود الآخر. والآخر أن يذكر صورة كانت مضمنة فيه بالفطرة وهذه حقائق ظاهرة للناظر بنور البصيرة ثقيلة على من يستروجه قوله يستروجه من الرواج أي يكون السماع والتقليد رائجا عنده فتأمل اه مصححه السماع والتقليد دون الكشف والعيان ولذلك تراه يتخبط ف
5:7.english: And therefore, the Almighty said: 'Perhaps they will remember (yataḍakkarūn)', 'And let those of understanding (ūlū al-albāb) remember', 'And remember (udhkurū) the favor of Allah upon you and His covenant with which He bound you when you said, "We hear and we obey"; and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of that within the chests (dhāt al-ṣudūr)', 'And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance (dhikr), so is there any who will remember (mudakkir)?'; And naming this pattern 'remembrance (tadhakkur)' is not far-fetched, as if remembrance (tadhakkur) is of two types: one is that he remembers an image that was present in existence in his heart (qalb) but disappeared after the other existence. The other is that he remembers an image that was embedded in him by innate disposition (fiṭrah), and these are truths apparent to the one who looks with the light of insight (baṣīrah), heavy upon the one who is dominated by it—his saying 'dominated by it' is from 'rāja' meaning that hearing (samāʿ) and imitation (taqlīd) become prevalent with him, so contemplate—its corrector is hearing (samāʿ) and imitation (taqlīd) without unveiling (kashf) and direct witnessing (ʿiyān). And therefore, you see him floundering in such verses and being arbitrary, and in interpreting remembrance (tadhakkur) with the affirmation of the souls (nufūs), types of arbitrariness, and it appears to him in the reports and verses kinds of contradictions, and perhaps that overcomes him until he looks at them with an eye of contempt and believes in their incoherence. Its example is the example of the blind man who enters a house and stumbles in it with the vessels arranged in the house, so he says, 'What is with these vessels that they are not lifted from the path and returned to their places?' It is said to him, 'They are in their places, and the defect is in your sight.' So likewise, the defect of insight (baṣīrah) runs its course, and more severe and greater than it, since the soul (nafs) is like the rider and the body (badan) is like the horse, and the blindness of the rider is more harmful than the blindness of the horse. And due to the similarity of the insight (baṣīrah) of the inner (bāṭin) to the insight (baṣīrah) of the outer (ẓāhir), Allah said, 'The heart (fuʾād) did not lie [about] what it saw', and He said, 'And thus did We show Abraham...'
5:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

5:7.arabic: ولذلك أمر الله تعالى الكافة بشكر نعمة الكتاب فقال تعالى ﴿ واذكروا نعمة الله عليكم وما أنزل عليكم من الكتاب والحكمة يعظكم به ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل ﴿ لقد أنزلنا إليكم كتابا فيه ذكركم أفلا تعقلون. وأنزلنا إليك الذكر لتبين للناس ما نزل إليهم. كذلك يضرب الله للناس أمثالهم واتبعوا أحسن ما أنزل إليكم من ربكم. هذا بصائر للناس وهدى ورحمة لقوم يوقنون. هذا بيان للناس وهدى وموعظة للمتقين ﴾ {} وإذا قصد بالخطاب جميع الناس فقد قصد الآحاد فهذا القارىء الواحد مقصود فما له ولسائر الناس فليقدر أنه المقصود قال الله تعال
5:7.english: Therefore, Allah the Exalted commanded all people to be grateful for the blessing of the Book, so He said: 'And remember the blessing (Niʿmah) of Allah upon you and what He has sent down to you of the Book and the Wisdom (Ḥikmah) by which He admonishes you.' And the Mighty and Majestic said: 'We have certainly sent down to you a Book in which is your Remembrance (Dhikr) - then will you not reason? And We have sent down to you the Remembrance (Dhikr) that you may make clear to the people what was sent down to them. Thus does Allah set forth for the people their examples. And follow the best of what was revealed to you from your Lord. This is insight for the people and guidance and mercy for a people who are certain. This is a clarification for the people and guidance and admonition for those who fear Allah.' And if the address is intended for all people, then the individuals are intended, so this single reader is intended, and what is for him and for the rest of the people, let him consider that he is the intended one. Allah said: 'And it has been revealed to me this Qur'an that I may warn you thereby and whoever it reaches.' Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī said: 'Whoever the Qur'an reaches, it is as if Allah has spoken to him.' And if he considers that, he does not take studying the Qur'an as his work, but rather he reads it as the servant reads the letter of his Master which He wrote to him to contemplate it and act according to its requirement.
5:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

5:8.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
5:8.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Whatever is in the Quran of 'O you who have believed' is in the Torah 'O you poor ones (al-Masakin)'.
5:8.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

5:11.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
5:11.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'What is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)".'
5:11.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

5:13.arabic: وإنما أدبه القرآن بمثل قوله تعالى خذ العفو وأمر بالعرف وأعرض عن الجاهلين وقوله إن الله يأمر بالعدل والإحسان وإيتاء ذي القربى وينهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر والبغي وقوله واصبر على ما أصابك إن ذلك من عزم الأمور وقوله ولمن صبر وغفر إن ذلك لمن عزم الأمور وقوله فاعف عنهم واصفح إن الله يحب المحسنين
5:13.english: And indeed, the Quran disciplined him with verses like His saying: 'Take forgiveness and command what is right and turn away from the ignorant ones' and His saying: 'Indeed, Allah commands justice and excellence (Ihsan) and giving to relatives and forbids immorality and wrong and oppression' and His saying: 'And be patient over what befalls you, indeed that is of the matters of determination' and His saying: 'And for whoever is patient and forgives, indeed that is of the matters of determination' and His saying: 'So pardon them and overlook, indeed Allah loves the doers of excellence (Muhsinin).'
5:13.book_title: Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character
5:13.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character'

5:14.arabic:
ادت الحاجة أن تكون كفرا وفيه ضعف أيضا.
     [95]  حديث إنه سيصيب أمتي داء الأمم قبلكم قالوا وما داء الأمم قال الأشر
  والبطر الحديث أخرجه ابن أبي الدنيا في ذم الحسد والطبراني في الأوسط من حديث
                                                       أبي هريرة بإسناد جيد.
 [96]  حديث لا تظهر الشماتة بأخيك فيعافيه الله ويبتليك أخرجه الترمذي من حديث
         واثلة بن الأسقع وقال حسن غريب وفي رواية ابن أبي الدنيا فيرحمه الله.
 [97]  حديث أخوف ما أخاف على أمتي أن يكثر لهم المال فيتحاسدون ويقتتلون أخرجه
5:14.english: [97] Hadith: The thing I fear most for my community is that wealth will increase for them, so they will envy each other and kill each other. It was reported by Ibn Abi al-Dunya in the book 'The Condemnation of Envy' from the narration of Ibn 'Amir al-Ash'ari, and in it is Thabit ibn Abi Thabit, whom Abu Hatim considered unknown. And in the two Sahihs from the narration of Abu Sa'id: 'Indeed, among what I fear for you after me is what will be opened to you of the splendor and adornment of the worldly life.' And for both of them from the narration of 'Amr ibn 'Awf al-Badri: 'By Allah, it is not poverty that I fear for you, but I fear that the worldly life will be spread out before you.' The hadith. And in Muslim from the narration of 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr: 'When Persia and Rome are opened to you...' The hadith, and in it: 'They will compete, then they will envy each other, then they will turn away from each other.' The hadith. And in Ahmad and al-Bazzar from the narration of 'Umar: 'The worldly life is not opened to anyone except that Allah casts between them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection.'
5:14.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

5:16.arabic: وقد سماه الله نورا في قوله تعالى: (الله نور السموات والأرض مثل نوره كمشكاة( وسمى العلم المستفاد منه روحا ووحيا وحياة فقال تعالى: (وكذلك أوحينا إليك روحا من أمرنا( وقال سبحانه (أومن كان ميتا فأحييناه وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به في الناس( وحيث ذكر النور والظلمة أراد به العلم والجهل كقوله (يخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور(.
5:16.english: And Allah has called it (the intellect) light in His saying: 'Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The example of His light is like a niche...' (Quran 24:35). And He called the knowledge derived from it spirit (Ruh) and revelation (Wahy) and life (Hayat). So He said: 'And thus We have revealed to you a spirit (Ruh) from Our command...' (Quran 42:52). And He, glorified be He, said: 'Or one who was dead (Mayyit) and We gave him life (Ahyaynahu) and made for him a light (Nur) by which he walks among the people...' (Quran 6:122). And wherever He mentioned light (Nur) and darkness (Zulumat), He intended by it knowledge (Ilm) and ignorance (Jahl), like His saying: 'He brings them out from the darknesses (Zulumat) into the light (Nur).'
5:16.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

5:16.arabic: فالأكياس هم الذين أراد الله أن يهديهم فشرح صدورهم للإسلام والهدى، والمغترون هم الذين أراد الله أن يضلهم فجعل صدرهم ضيقاً حرجاً كأنما يصعد في السماء. والمغرور هو الذي لم تنفتح بصيرته ليكون بهداية نفسه كفيلاً ويهدي به الله من اتبع رضوانه سبل السلام ويخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور بإذنه ويهديهم إلى صراط مستقيم.
5:16.english: The intelligent ones are those whom Allah intended to guide, so He expanded their chests for Islam and guidance, and the deluded ones are those whom Allah intended to misguide, so He made their chests tight and constricted as if they were climbing into the sky. And the deluded person is the one whose insight (Basar) has not opened to be sufficient for the guidance of his own soul (Nafs), and Allah guides with it those who follow His pleasure to the paths of peace and brings them out from the darknesses into the light by His permission and guides them to a straight path (Sirat Mustaqim).
5:16.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

5:18.arabic: اعلم أن شواهد القرآن متظاهرة على أن الله تعالى يحب عبده فلا بد من معرفة معنى ذلك. ولنقدم الشواهد على محبته فقد قال الله تعالى: " يحبهم ويحبونه " وقال تعالى: " إن الله يحب الذين يقاتلون في سبيله صفاً " وقال تعالى: " إن الله يحب التوابين ويحب المتطهرين " ولذلك رد سبحانه على من ادعى أنه حبيب الله فقال: "وَقَالَتِ الْيَهُودُ وَالنَّصَارَىٰ نَحْنُ أَبْنَاءُ اللَّهِ وَأَحِبَّاؤُهُ ۚ قُلْ فَلِمَ يُعَذِّبُكُمْ بِذُنُوبِكُمْ ۖ بَلْ أَنْتُمْ بَشَرٌ مِمَّنْ خَلَقَ ۚ يَغْفِرُ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَنْ
5:18.english: Know that the evidences of the Quran are manifest that Allah the Exalted loves His servant, so it is necessary to know the meaning of that. And let us present the evidences of His love, for Allah the Exalted has said: "He loves them and they love Him" and He said: "Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in ranks" and He said: "Indeed, Allah loves those who repent and loves those who purify themselves." And therefore, He the Glorified responded to those who claimed to be the beloved of Allah by saying: "And the Jews and the Christians say, 'We are the children of Allah and His beloved.' Say, 'Then why does He punish you for your sins?' Rather, you are human beings from among those He created. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and to Him is the destination.'"
5:18.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

5:19.arabic: وما لي أقدر هذا وقد كان ما أقدره فلقد بعث الله نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم على فترة من الرسل وكان شرع عيسى عليه السلام قد مضى عليه قريب من ستمائة سنة والناس منقسمون إلى مكذبين له من اليهود وعبدة الأوثان وإلى مصدقين له قد شاع الفسق فيهم كما شاع في زماننا الآن والكفار مخاطبون بفروع الشريعة والأموال كانت في أيدي المكذبين له والمصدقين أما المكذبون فكانوا يتعاملون بغير شرع عيسى عليه السلام وأما المصدقون فكان يتساهلون مع أصل التصديق كما يتساهل الآن المسلمون مع أن العهد بالنبوة أقرب فكانت الأموال كلها أو
5:19.english: And why do I imagine this when what I imagine has already occurred? For indeed, Allah sent our Prophet (peace be upon him) upon a gap (fatra) from the messengers, and the law (shar') of Jesus (peace be upon him) had passed nearly six hundred years ago. The people were divided into those who denied him from the Jews and idol worshippers, and into those who believed in him, but corruption (fisq) had spread among them as it has spread in our time now. The disbelievers (kuffar) were addressed with the branches of the law (shari'a), and the wealth (amwal) was in the hands of those who denied him and those who believed. As for the deniers, they were dealing without the law of Jesus (peace be upon him), and as for the believers, they were lax with the foundation of belief (tasdiq) just as Muslims are lax now, even though the era of prophethood was closer. Thus, all the wealth, or most of it, or much of it, was unlawful (haram) (peace be upon him), and he pardoned what had passed and did not interfere with it, and he specified the owners of the hands with the wealth, and he established the law (shar'). And what was established as unlawful (tahrim) in a law does not become lawful (halal) due to the sending of a messenger, nor does it become lawful by the one who possesses the unlawful surrendering it. For we do not take in the jizya from the people of the covenant (ahl al-dhimma) what we specifically know to be the price of wine or usurious wealth (riba). Indeed, their wealth at that time was like our wealth now, and the matter of the Arabs was more severe due to the prevalence of plunder and raids among them. So it became clear that the fourth probability is definitive in the legal opinion (fatwa), and the fifth probability is the path of piety (wara'), indeed, complete piety (wara') is restricting oneself in the permissible (mubah) to the measure of need (haja) and abandoning expansion in the worldly life (dunya) entirely, and that is the path of the hereafter (akhira).
5:19.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

5:23.arabic: أما من الآيات: فقد قال تعالى: " وعلى الله فتوكلوا إن كنتم مؤمنين ". وقال عز وجل: " وعلى الله فليتوكل المتوكلون ". وقال تعالى: " ومن يتوكل على الله فهو حسبه ". وقال سبحانه وتعالى: " إن الله يحب المتوكلين " وأعظم بمقام موسوم بمحبة الله تعالى صاحبه، ومضمون كفاية الله تعالى ملابسه، فمن الله تعالى حسبه وكافيه ومحبه ومراعيه: فقد فاز الفوز العظيم، فإن المحبوب لا يعذب ولا يبعد ولا يحجب.
5:23.english: As for from the verses: Indeed, He (the Exalted) said: "And upon Allah place your trust (tawakkul) if you are believers." And He (the Mighty and Majestic) said: "And upon Allah let the ones who trust (mutawakkilun) place their trust." And He (the Exalted) said: "And whoever places trust (tawakkul) upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him." And He (the Glorified and Exalted) said: "Indeed, Allah loves the ones who place trust (mutawakkilun)." And how great is a station (maqam) marked with the love (mahabbah) of Allah (the Exalted) its possessor, and guaranteed with the sufficiency (kifayah) of Allah (the Exalted) its companion, so whoever from Allah (the Exalted) is his sufficiency (hasbuhu) and his sufficient one (kafihi) and his lover (muhhibuhu) and his caretaker (mura'ihi): then he has attained the great success (al-fawz al-'azim), for the beloved (al-mahbub) is not punished nor distanced nor veiled.
5:23.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

5:27.arabic: ولكن حال زيد وعمرو بعينه فلا ينكشف أصلا فإنا إن عولنا على إيمان زيد وعمرو فلا ندري على ماذا مات وكيف ختم له وإن عولنا على صلاحه الظاهر فالتقوى محله القلب وهو غامض يخفي على صاحب التقوى فكيف على غيره فلا حكم لظاهر الصلاح دون التقوى الباطن قال الله تعالى: ﴿ إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين ﴾ فلا يمكن معرفة حكم زيد وعمرو إلا بمشاهدته ومشاهدة ما يجري عليه وإذا مات فقد تحول من عالم الملك والشهادة إلى عالم الغيب والملكوت فلا يرى بالعين الظاهرة وإنما يرى بعين أخرى خلقت تلك العين في قلب كل إنسان ولكن جعل عليها
5:27.english: But the specific condition of Zaid and Amr is not revealed at all, for if we rely on the faith (Iman) of Zaid and Amr, we do not know upon what he died and how his end was sealed, and if we rely on his apparent righteousness, then piety (Taqwa) resides in the heart (Qalb), and it is obscure, hidden even from the possessor of piety, so how much more from others. There is no judgment for apparent righteousness without the inner piety (Taqwa). Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, Allah only accepts from the pious (Al-Muttaqin).' Therefore, it is not possible to know the judgment of Zaid and Amr except by witnessing him and observing what befalls him. And when he dies, he has transferred from the world of dominion (Al-Mulk) and the witnessed (Al-Shahadah) to the world of the unseen (Al-Ghayb) and the kingdom (Al-Malakut), so he is not seen with the apparent eye, but rather is seen with another eye created in the heart (Qalb) of every human, but a thick veil (Ghishawah) has been placed upon it from his desires (Shahawat) and worldly occupations, so he does not see with it, nor can he imagine seeing anything from the world of the kingdom (Al-Malakut) unless that veil (Ghishawah) is lifted from the eye of his heart (Qalb).
5:27.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

5:27.arabic: وإياك والحسد فإنما قتل ابن آدم أخاه حين حسده ثم قرأ "واتل عليهم نبأ ابني آدم بالحق"، الآيات
5:27.english: And beware of envy (al-Hasad), for indeed the son of Adam killed his brother when he envied him, then he recited: "And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam with truth" (Quran 5:27), the verses.
5:27.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

5:27.arabic: وبكى بعضهم عند الموت فقيل له ما يبكيك آية في كتاب الله تعالى قوله عز وجل: ﴿ إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين ﴾
5:27.english: And some of them wept at death, and it was said to him: 'What makes you weep?' He said: 'A verse in the Book of Allah, the Exalted, His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: "Indeed, Allah only accepts from the God-fearing (Al-Muttaqeen)."'
5:27.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

5:28.arabic: وإنما الفضل والثواب الجزيل في تركه خوفاً من الله تعالى مع القدرة وارتفاع الموانع وتيسر الأسباب، لا سيما عند صدق الشهوة وهذه درجة الصديقين. ولذلك قال ﭬ "من عشق فعف فكتم فمات فهو شهيد"[69] وقال ﭬ "سبعة يظلمهم الله يوم القيامة في ظل عرشه يوم لا ظل إلا ظله - وعد منهم" رجل دعته امرأة ذات جمال وحسب إلى نفسها فقال إني أخاف الله رب العالمين"[70] وقصة يوسف عليه السلام وامتناعه من زليخا مع القدرة ومع رغبتها معروفة، وقد أثنى الله تعالى عليه بذلك في كتابه العزيز، وهو إمام لكل من وفق لمجاهدة الشيطان في هذه ا
5:28.english: And indeed the virtue and great reward is in abandoning it out of fear of Allah (God) the Exalted with capability and removal of obstacles and facilitation of means, especially when the desire (Shahwa) is sincere, and this is the rank of the truthful ones (Siddiqin). Therefore he (the Prophet) said: 'Whoever loves then remains chaste then conceals then dies, he is a martyr.' And he said: 'Seven whom Allah will shade on the Day of Resurrection under the shade of His Throne on a day when there is no shade except His shade - among them is promised' a man whom a woman of beauty and lineage invited to herself, so he said: 'Indeed I fear Allah (God), Lord of the worlds.' And the story of Yusuf (Joseph) peace be upon him and his abstention from Zulaykha with capability and with her desire is known, and Allah the Exalted has praised him for that in His Noble Book, and he is an imam (leader) for everyone who is granted success in striving against the devil (Shaytan) in this great desire (Shahwa).
5:28.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Harms of the Tongue'

5:32.arabic: وقيل فكأنما قتل الناس جميعا وعن علي رضي الله عنه من احتكر الطعام أربعين يوما قسا قلبه وعنه أيضا أنه أحرق طعام محتكر بالنار وروي في فضل ترك الاحتكار عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم من جلب طعاما فباعه بسعر يومه فكأنما تصدق به وفي لفظ آخر فكأنما أعتق رقبة حديث من جلب طعاما فباعه بسعر يومه فكأنما تصدق به وفي لفظ آخر فكأنما أعتق رقبة أخرجه ابن مردويه في التفسير من حديث ابن مسعود بسند ضعيف ما من جالب يجلب طعاما إلى بلد من بلدان المسلمين فيبيعه بسعر يومه إلا كانت منزلته عند الله منزلة الشهيد وللحاكم من حديث الي
5:32.english: And it is said: 'As if he killed all people.' And from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him: 'Whoever hoards food for forty days, his heart (Qalb) hardens.' And from him also: 'He burned the food of a hoarder with fire.' And it is narrated regarding the virtue of abandoning hoarding from him, peace and blessings be upon him: 'Whoever brings food and sells it at the price of its day, it is as if he gave it in charity (Sadaqah).' And in another wording: 'It is as if he freed a slave (Raqabah).' The hadith: 'Whoever brings food and sells it at the price of its day, it is as if he gave it in charity (Sadaqah).' And in another wording: 'It is as if he freed a slave (Raqabah).' Ibn Mardawayh in the Tafsir narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud with a weak chain. 'There is no one who brings food to a town from the towns of the Muslims and sells it at the price of its day except that his status with Allah is like the status of a martyr (Shahid).' And Al-Hakim from the hadith of Al-Yasa' ibn Al-Mughirah: 'Indeed, the one who brings to a market is like a Mujahid (one who strives) in the path of Allah.' And it is disconnected. And it is said regarding His saying, the Exalted: 'And whoever intends therein deviation with injustice, We will make him taste of a painful punishment.' Indeed, hoarding is from injustice (Zulm) and falls under it in the threat.
5:32.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Earning'

5:35.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
5:35.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'What is in the Quran as "O you who have believed" is in the Torah as "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)".'
5:35.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

5:42.arabic: الثالث: كف السمع عن الإصغاء إلى كل مكروه لأن كل ما حرم قوله حرم الإصغاء إليه ولذلك سوى الله عز وجل بين المستمع وآكل السحت فقال تعالى: ﴿ سماعون للكذب أكالون للسحت ﴾{} وقال عز وجل: ﴿ لولا ينهاهم الربانيون والأحبار عن قولهم الإثم وأكلهم السحت ﴾{} فالسكوت على الغيبة حرام. وقال تعالى: ﴿ إنكم إذا مثلهم ﴾{} ولذلك قال ﭬ: (المغتاب والمستمع شريكان في الإثم[22]).
5:42.english: Third: Restraining the hearing from listening to every disliked thing because everything whose speech is forbidden, listening to it is also forbidden. Therefore, Allah the Exalted equated between the listener and the consumer of unlawful gain (Suhut) when He said: 'They are listeners to falsehood, consumers of unlawful gain (Suhut)' (Quran 5:42). And He the Exalted said: 'If only the rabbis and the scholars had forbidden them from their sinful speech and consumption of unlawful gain (Suhut)' (Quran 5:63). So remaining silent about backbiting is forbidden. And He said: 'Indeed, you then are like them' (Quran 4:140). Therefore, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'The backbiter and the listener are partners in sin' (Hadith 22).
5:42.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Mysteries of Fasting'

5:45.arabic:
بن عامر ورواه ابن أبى
                                     الدنيا في القناعة موقوفا عليه وقد تقدم.
                        [91]  حديث من أصبح آمنا في سربه الحديث تقدم غير مرة.
 [92]  حديث ما عظمت نعمة الله على عبد إلا كثرت حوائج الناس إليه الحديث أخرجه
   ابن عدى وابن حبان في الضعفاء من حديث معاذ بن جبل بلفظ إلا عظمت مؤنة الناس
   عليه فمن لم يحتمل تلك المونة الحديث ورواه ابن حبان في الضعفاء من حديث ابن
                                        عباس وقال أنه موضوع على حجاج الأعور.
  [93]  حديث إن
5:45.english: [94] Hadith: 'Indeed, when a servant commits a sin and then experiences hardship and tribulation in the worldly life, Allah is more generous than to punish him a second time.' It was reported by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah from the narration of 'Ali: 'Whoever commits a sin in the worldly life and is punished for it, Allah is more just than to impose punishment upon His servant.' The wording of Ibn Majah says: 'Whoever commits a sin and his punishment is hastened in the worldly life.' Al-Tirmidhi said it is hasan (good). And from the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) from the narration of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit: 'Whoever commits something from that and is punished for it, then it is an expiation (kafarah) for him.'
5:45.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

5:48.arabic: لملك والصدقة تدخلك  عليه.  وقال  ابن  أبي الجعد: إن الصدقة لتدفع سبعين بابا من السوء وفضل سرها على علانيتها بسبعين ضعفا وإنها لتفك لحيي سبعين شيطانا. وقال ابن  مسعود: إن رجلا عبد الله سبعين سنة ثم أصاب فاحشة فأحبط عمله ثم مر بمسكين فتصدق  عليه برغيف فغفر الله له ذنبه ورد عليه عمل السبعين  سنة.  وقال  لقمان  لابنه:  إذا أخطأت خطيئة فأعط الصدقة. وقال يحيى بن معاذ: ما أعرف حبة تزن جبال الدنيا  إلا الحبة من الصدقة: وقال عبد العزيز بن أبي رواد: كان يقال ثلاثة من  كنوز  الجنة كتمان المرض وكتمان الصدقة
5:48.english: Charity (Sadaqah) and almsgiving grant you entry to Him. And Ibn Abi Al-Ja'd said: Indeed charity repels seventy doors of evil, and the virtue of its secrecy over its openness is seventyfold, and indeed it frees seventy devils from the neck. And Ibn Mas'ud said: Indeed a man worshipped Allah for seventy years, then he committed an immorality, so his deeds were nullified, then he passed by a poor person and gave him charity with a loaf of bread, so Allah forgave his sin and restored to him the deeds of the seventy years. And Luqman said to his son: When you commit a sin, then give charity. And Yahya bin Mu'adh said: I do not know of a seed that weighs the mountains of the world except the seed of charity. And Abdul Aziz bin Abi Rawad said: It was said: Three are from the treasures of Paradise: concealing illness, concealing charity, and concealing calamities. And he narrated with a chain, and Umar bin Al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Indeed the deeds boasted, so charity said: I am the best of you. And Abdullah bin Umar used to give charity with sugar and say: I heard Allah saying: "You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love." {} And Allah knows that I love sugar.
