And Al-Nakha'i said: When something is for Allah, the Exalted, it does not please me that there be a defect in it. And Ubaid bin Umair said: People will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection the hungriest they ever were, the thirstiest they ever were, and the most naked they ever were, so whoever feeds for Allah, the Exalted, Allah will satiate him, and whoever gives drink for Allah, the Exalted, Allah will give him drink, and whoever clothes for Allah, the Exalted, Allah will clothe him. And Al-Hasan said: If Allah had willed, He would have made you all rich with no poor among you, but He tested some of you with others. And Al-Sha'bi said: Whoever does not see himself more in need of the reward of charity than the poor person is of his charity, then he has invalidated his charity and struck his face with it. And Malik said: We see no harm in the believer drinking from the water that is given as charity and given to drink in the mosque, because it was only made for the thirsty, whoever it may be, and it was not intended specifically for the people of need and poverty. And it is said: Al-Hasan passed by a slave trader with a slave girl, and he said to the slave trader: Would you be satisfied with a dirham or two dirhams for her price? He said: No. He said: Then go, for Allah, the Exalted, is satisfied with the dirham and the morsel in the houris of Paradise.
5:48.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

5:51.arabic: وأما بغض الكفار والإنكار عليهم ومقتهم فما ورد فيه من شواهد القرآن والأخبار لا يحصى مثل قوله تعالى " لا يتخذ المؤمنون الكافرين أولياء من دون المؤمنين ". وقال تعالى: " يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا اليهود والنصارى أولياء ". وقال تعالى: " وكذلك نولي بعض الظالمين بعضاً ". وفي الخبر: " إن الله تعالى أخذ الميثاق على كل مؤمن أن يبغض كل منافق وعلى كل منافق أن يبغض كل مؤمن"[69]. وقال عليه السلام: " المرء مع من أحب"[70] وقال: " من أحب قوماً ووالاهم حشر معهم يوم القيامة"[71]. وقال عليه السلام: " أوثق عرى ا
5:51.english: As for hating the disbelievers (Kuffar), rejecting them, and despising them, what has come regarding this from evidences of the Quran and reports (Akhbar) is innumerable, such as His saying, the Exalted: "Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies (Awliya) instead of the believers." And He said, the Exalted: "O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies (Awliya)." And He said, the Exalted: "And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies (Nuwalli) of others." And in the report (Khabar): "Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, took the covenant (Mithaq) upon every believer to hate every hypocrite (Munafiq) and upon every hypocrite (Munafiq) to hate every believer." And he, peace be upon him, said: "A person is with whom he loves." And he said: "Whoever loves a people and allies with them (Walahum) will be gathered with them on the Day of Resurrection." And he, peace be upon him, said: "The firmest bond of faith (Iman) is love for the sake of Allah (Al-Hubb fi Allah) and hatred for the sake of Allah (Al-Bughd fi Allah)." The evidences for this we have already mentioned in the explanation of love and hatred for the sake of Allah, the Exalted, from the Book of the Etiquettes of Companionship (Adab al-Suhba), and in the Book of Commanding Good and Forbidding Evil (Al-Amr bi al-Ma'ruf wa al-Nahy 'an al-Munkar); so we do not repeat it.
5:51.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

5:51.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
5:51.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'What is in the Quran as "O you who have believed" is in the Torah as "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)"'.
5:51.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

5:54.arabic: فهذا يدل على أن قوله: " ذلك فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء " أي مزيد ثواب الفقراء على ذكرهم. وأما قوله: إن الغني وصف الحق، فقد أجابه بعض الشيوخ فقال: أترى أن الله تعالى غني بالأسباب والأعراض، فانقطع ولم ينطق، وأجاب آخرون فقالوا: إن التكبر من صفات الحق فينبغي أن يكون أفضل من التواضع، ثم قالوا: بل هذا يدل على أن الفقر أفضل لأن صفات العبودية فضل للعبد كالخوف والرجاء، وصفات الربوبية لا ينبغي أن ينازع فيها، ولذلك قال تعالى فيما روى عنه نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم: " الكبرياء ردائي والعظمة إزاري، فمن نازعني واحد
5:54.english: This indicates that His saying: "That is the Favor (Fadl) of Allah, He gives it to whom He wills" means the increased reward of the poor over their remembrance. As for his saying: Indeed, richness is an attribute of the Truth (Al-Haqq), some shaykhs answered him by saying: Do you see that Allah the Exalted is rich through causes and accidents? He fell silent and did not speak. Others answered by saying: Indeed, arrogance is from the attributes of the Truth, so it should be better than humility. Then they said: Rather, this indicates that poverty is better because the attributes of servitude (al-'ubudiyyah) are a favor for the servant (al-'abd) like fear (al-khawf) and hope (al-raja'), and the attributes of lordship (al-rububiyyah) should not be contended over. Therefore, Allah the Exalted said in what was narrated from our Prophet, peace be upon him: "Pride (al-kibriya') is My cloak and majesty (al-'azamah) is My garment, so whoever contends with Me in one of them, I will break him." And Sahl said: Love of honor (al-'izz) and permanence (al-baqa') is polytheism (shirk) in lordship and contention in it because they are from the attributes of the Lord, the Exalted. From this category, they spoke about preferring the rich and the poor, and the essence of that is attachment to generalities that accept interpretations and deficient words whose contradiction is not far, for just as the statement of one who prefers richness because it is an attribute of the Truth with arrogance is contradicted, so too is the statement of one who criticizes richness because it is a description of the servant with knowledge (al-'ilm) and recognition (al-ma'rifah), for it is a description of the Lord, the Exalted, and ignorance (al-jahl) and heedlessness (al-ghaflah) are descriptions of the servant, and no one should prefer heedlessness over knowledge. The unveiling of the cover from this is what we mentioned in the Book of Patience (Kitab al-Sabr): which is that what is not desired for itself but is desired for other than it f
5:54.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

5:54.arabic:
ن قرأ الأخبار  والآثار  في  تفضيل
الفقر، ولا بد فيه من تفصيل فنقول إنما يتصور  الشك  في  مقامين:  أحدهما  فقير
صابر ليس بحريص على الطلب، بل هو قانع أو راض بالإضافة إلى غني  منفق  ماله  في
الخيرات ليس حريصاً على إمساك المال.

والثاني فقير حريص مع غني حريص، إذ لا يخفى أن الفقير  القانع  أفضل  من  الغني
الحريص الممسك، وأن الغني المنفق ماله في الخيرات أفضل من الفقير الحريص.

المقام الأول فقير صابر ليس بحريص على الطلب أما  الأول  فربما  يظن  أن  الغني
أفضل من الفقير، لأنهما تساويا في ضعف الحرص على ال
5:54.english: [44] Hadith: The poor complained to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) that the rich have preceded them in good deeds and charity. The hadith, and at its end he said: "That is the bounty of Allah which He gives to whom He wills." Agreed upon from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, similar.
5:54.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

5:54.arabic: فرجع إليهم فأخبرهم بما قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقالوا: رضينا رضينا[45]. فهذا يدل على أن قوله: " ذلك فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء " أي مزيد ثواب الفقراء على ذكرهم. وأما قوله: "يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَنْ يَرْتَدَّ مِنْكُمْ عَنْ دِينِهِ فَسَوْفَ يَأْتِي اللَّهُ بِقَوْمٍ يُحِبُّهُمْ وَيُحِبُّونَهُ أَذِلَّةٍ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَعِزَّةٍ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ يُجَاهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَلَا يَخَافُونَ لَوْمَةَ لَائِمٍ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ فَضْلُ اللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ ۚ وَاللَّهُ وَاس
5:54.english: He returned to them and informed them of what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, and they said: 'We are pleased, we are pleased.' This indicates that His saying: "That is the bounty of Allah which He gives to whom He wills" means the increased reward of the poor in their remembrance (Dhikr). As for His saying: "O you who have believed, whoever among you turns back from his religion - Allah will bring forth a people He will love and who will love Him, humble (Adhillah) toward the believers, mighty (A'izzah) against the disbelievers; they strive in the cause of Allah and do not fear the blame of a critic. That is the bounty of Allah which He gives to whom He wills. And Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing." It is in another meaning, which is that when Allah the Exalted wills to replace a people with another people, He replaces them with a people whom He loves and who love Him, and He makes them humble (Adhillah) toward the believers, mighty (A'izzah) against the disbelievers, not fearing in Allah the blame of a critic, and that is the bounty of Allah which He gives to whom He wills, and Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing.
5:54.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

5:54.arabic: وقد استشهد ابن عطاء أيضاً لما سئل عن ذلك فقال: الغني أفضل لأنه وصف الحق، أما دليله الأول ففيه نظر، لأن الخبر قد ورد مفصلاً تفصيلاً يدل على خلاف ذلك: وهو أن ثواب الفقير في التسبيح يزيد على ثواب الغني، وأن فوزهم بذلك الثواب فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء، فقد روى يزيد بن أسلم عن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه قال: بعثني الفقراء رسولاً إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: إني رسول الفقراء إليك؛ فقال: " مرحباً بك وبمن جئت من عندهم قوم أحبهم " قال: قالوا يا رسول الله إن الأغنياء ذهبوا بالخير يحجون ولا نقدر عليه،
5:54.english: And Ibn 'Ata' also cited as evidence when asked about that, saying: The rich person is better because he is described by the Truth (Al-Haqq), but his first evidence is questionable, because the report has come detailed in a way that indicates the opposite of that: which is that the reward of the poor person in glorification (Tasbih) increases over the reward of the rich person, and that their attainment of that reward is the favor (Fadl) of Allah, He gives it to whom He wills, for Yazid bin Aslam narrated from Anas bin Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The poor sent me as a messenger to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and I said: I am the messenger of the poor to you; so he said: "Welcome to you and to those you have come from, a people whom I love." He said: They said: O Messenger of Allah, the rich have taken away the good deeds, they perform pilgrimage (Hajj) and we are not able to do it, and they perform 'Umrah and we are not able to do it, and when they fall ill, they send ahead with the surplus of their wealth as a provision for them; so the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Convey from me to the poor that for whoever among you is patient and expects reward, there are three characteristics not for the rich: As for one characteristic: Indeed in Paradise there are chambers that the people of Paradise look at as the people of the earth look at the stars of the sky, none enters them except a poor prophet, or a poor martyr, or a poor believer, and the second: The poor enter Paradise before the rich by half a day, which is five hundred years, and the third: Glory be to Allah (Subhan Allah) and praise be to Allah (Al-Hamdulillah) and there is no god but Allah (La ilaha illa Allah) and Allah is the Greatest (Allahu Akbar), and the poor person said similarly.
5:54.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

5:57.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
5:57.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'What is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)".'
5:57.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

5:63.arabic: الثالث: كف السمع عن الإصغاء إلى كل مكروه لأن كل ما حرم قوله حرم الإصغاء إليه ولذلك سوى الله عز وجل بين المستمع وآكل السحت فقال تعالى: ﴿ سماعون للكذب أكالون للسحت ﴾{} وقال عز وجل: ﴿ لولا ينهاهم الربانيون والأحبار عن قولهم الإثم وأكلهم السحت ﴾{} فالسكوت على الغيبة حرام. وقال تعالى: ﴿ إنكم إذا مثلهم ﴾{} ولذلك قال ﭬ: (المغتاب والمستمع شريكان في الإثم[22]).
5:63.english: Third: Restraining the hearing from listening to every disliked thing, because everything whose speech is forbidden, listening to it is also forbidden. Therefore, Allah the Exalted equated between the listener and the eater of unlawful gain (Suhut), as He said: 'Listeners to falsehood, eaters of unlawful gain (Suhut)' (Quran 5:42), and He said: 'If only the rabbis (Rabbāniyyūn) and the scholars (Aḥbār) had forbidden them from their sinful speech and their eating of unlawful gain (Suhut)' (Quran 5:63). So, remaining silent about backbiting (Ghibah) is forbidden. And He said: 'Indeed, you then are like them' (Quran 4:140). Therefore, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'The backbiter (Mughtāb) and the listener (Mustamiʿ) are partners in sin.'
5:63.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Mysteries of Fasting'

5:63.arabic: وقال تعالى لولا ينهاهم الربانيون والاحبار عن قولهم الإثم وأكلهم السحت لبئس ما كانوا يصنعون فبين أنهم أثموا بترك النهي
5:63.english: And Allah the Exalted said: 'If only the Rabbis (Rabbāniyyūn) and the Scholars (Aḥbār) had forbidden them from their sinful speech and their consumption of the unlawful (Suhṭ), then how wretched was what they used to do.' So He made clear that they sinned by abandoning the forbidding.
5:63.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

5:64.arabic: [102] حديث ابن عباس قوله كانت اليهود قبل أن يبعث النبي ﭬ إذا قاتلوا قوما قالوا نسألك. بالنبي الذي وعدتنا أن ترسله الحديث في نزول قوله تعالى وكانوا من قبل يستفتحون على الذين كفروا أخرجه ابن إسحاق في السيرة فيما بلغه ع
5:64.english: [102] The hadith of Ibn Abbas, his statement: 'The Jews, before the Prophet ﷺ was sent, when they fought a people, they said: We ask you by the Prophet whom you promised to send us' - the hadith concerning the revelation of His saying, the Exalted: 'And they used to, before that, seek victory over those who disbelieved' - reported by Ibn Ishaq in the Sirah according to what reached him.
5:64.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

5:67.arabic: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يحرس حتى نزلت هذه الآية والله يعصمك من الناس فأخرج رأسه من القبة فقال انصرفوا فقد عصمني الله
5:67.english: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was being guarded until this verse was revealed: 'And Allah protects you from the people.' So he brought his head out from the tent and said: 'Depart, for Allah has protected me.'
5:67.book_title: Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character
5:67.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character'

5:69.arabic: فختم على كل ذى حزم آمن بالله واليوم الآخر أن لا يغفل عن محاسبة نفسه والتضييق عليها في حركاتها وسكناتها وخطراتها وخطواتها فإن كل نفس من أنفاس العمر جوهرة نفيسة لا عوض لها يمكن أن يشترى بها كنز من الكنوز لا يتناهى نعيمه أبد الآباد فانقباض هذه الأنفاس ضائعة أو مصروفة إلى ما يجلب الهلاك خسران عظيم هائل لا تسمح به نفس عاقل فإذا أصبح العبد وفرغ من فريضة الصبح ينبغى أن يفرغ قلبه ساعة لمشارطه النفس كما أن التاجر عند تسليم البضاعة إلى الشريك العامل يفرغ المجلس لمشارطته فيقول للنفس ما لي بضاعة إلا العمر و
5:69.english: Therefore, it is concluded for every possessor of determination who believes in Allah and the Last Day that he should not neglect accounting his Soul (Nafs) and constraining it in its movements, stillness, fleeting thoughts, and steps. For every breath of life is a precious jewel with no substitute, through which can be purchased a treasure of treasures whose bliss is endless for all eternity. The contraction of these breaths wasted or diverted to what brings destruction is a great, tremendous loss that no rational Soul (Nafs) would permit. When the servant (Abd) awakens and completes the obligatory morning prayer (Fajr), he should empty his Heart (Qalb) for an hour to contract with his Soul (Nafs), just as a merchant, when delivering goods to the working partner, empties the council for contracting with him. He says to the Soul (Nafs): 'I have no merchandise except life; whenever it perishes, the capital has perished, and despair occurs regarding trade and seeking profit. This new day, Allah has granted me respite in it, postponed my term, and bestowed favor upon me. If He had taken me, I would wish to be returned to the world for a single day to perform righteous deeds in it. Consider that you have died and then been returned. Beware, then beware, of wasting this day, for every breath of the breaths is a jewel of no value. And know, O Soul (Nafs), that the day and night are twenty-four hours, and it has been reported in the tradition that for every day and night, twenty-four treasuries are spread out for the servant, so one of them is opened for him, and he sees it filled with light from his good deeds that he performed in that hour.'
5:69.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

5:72.arabic: المؤمنين على العراق وعامله عليها ورجل مأمور على الطاعة ابتليت بالرعية ولزمني حقهم فأنا أحب حفظهم وتعهد ما يصلحهم مع النصيحة لهم وقد يبلغني عن العصابة من أهل الديار الأمر أجد عليهم فيه فأقبض طائفة من عطائهم فأضعه في بيت المال ومن نيتي أن أرده عليهم فيبلغ أمير المؤمنين أني قد قبضته على ذلك النحو فيكتب إلى أن لا ترده فلا أستطيع رد أمره ولا إنفاذ كتابه وإنما أنا رجل مأمور على الطاعة فهل على في هذا تبعة وفي أشباهه من الأمور والنية فيها على ما ذكرت قال الشعبي فقلت أصلح الله الأمير إنما السلطان والد يخ
5:72.english: The believers over Iraq and its governor over it and a man commanded to obedience, I have been tested with the subjects and their right has become incumbent upon me, so I love preserving them and overseeing what reforms them along with sincere advice for them. And sometimes news reaches me about the group from the people of the lands regarding a matter I find them at fault in, so I withhold a portion of their stipend and place it in the treasury, and my intention is to return it to them. Then the Commander of the Faithful learns that I have withheld it in that manner and writes to me not to return it, so I cannot disobey his command nor can I implement his letter, for I am merely a man commanded to obedience. Is there any sin upon me in this and in similar matters where the intention is as I mentioned? Al-Sha'bi said: So I said, 'May Allah rectify the Commander, the ruler is like a father who errs and is correct.' He said: He was pleased with my words and delighted with it, and I saw joy on his face, and he said, 'Praise be to Allah.' Then he turned to Al-Hasan and said, 'What do you say, O Abu Sa'id?' He said: I have heard the Commander's statement saying that he is the trustee of the Commander of the Faithful over Iraq and its governor over it and a man commanded to obedience, tested with the subjects, and their right has become incumbent upon him and sincere advice for them and overseeing what reforms them. And the right of the subjects is binding upon you, and it is your duty to encompass them with sincere advice. And I heard 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Samurah al-Qurashi, the companion of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, 'Whoever is entrusted with subjects and does not encompass them with sincere advice, Allah has forbidden Paradise upon him.' The hadith of Al-Hasan from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Samurah: 'Whoever is entrusted with subjects and does not encompass them with sincere advice, Allah has forbidden Paradise upon him.' Al-Baghawi narrated it in Mu'jam al-Sahabah with a weak chain, and the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) have agreed upon it similarly from the narration of Al-Hasan from Ma'qil ibn Yasar. And he says: I sometimes withhold from their stipend intending their reform and rectification and that they return to their obedience. Then the Commander of the Faithful learns that I have withheld it in that manner and writes to me not to return it, so I cannot disobey his command nor can I implement his letter. And the right of Allah is more binding than the right of the Commander of the Faithful, and Allah is more deserving to be obeyed, and there is no obedience to a created being in disobedience to the Creator. So present the letter of the Commander of the Faithful to the Book of Allah, the Exalted. If you find it conforming to the Book of Allah, then take it, and if you find it contradicting the Book of Allah, then discard it. O Ibn Hubayrah, fear Allah, for soon a messenger from the Lord of the worlds will come to you, removing you from your throne and taking you out from the spaciousness of your palace to the narrowness of your grave, so you will leave your authority and your worldly life behind your back and proceed to your Lord and descend upon your deeds. O Ibn Hubayrah, indeed Allah will prevent you from Yazid, and Yazid will not prevent you from Allah, and the command of Allah is above every command, and there is no obedience in disobedience to Allah, and I warn you of His punishment which is not averted from the criminal people. Then Ibn Hubayrah said, 'Hold back on your lameness, O elder, and refrain from mentioning the Commander of the Faithful.'
5:72.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

5:78.arabic: وقال تعالى لعن الذين كفروا من بني إسرائيل على لسان داود وعيسى ابن مريم ذلك بما عصوا وكانوا يعتدون كانوا لا يتناهون عن منكر فعلوه لبئس ما كانوا يفعلون وهذا غاية التشديد إذ علل استحقاقهم للعنة بتركهم النهي عن المنكر
5:78.english: And He (Exalted) said: 'Cursed were those who disbelieved from the Children of Israel on the tongue of David and Jesus son of Mary. That was because they disobeyed and were transgressing. They would not desist from an evil (منكر) they had committed. Evil indeed was what they used to do.' And this is the utmost severity, for He explained their deserving of the curse by their abandoning the forbidding of evil (النهي عن المنكر).
5:78.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

5:78.arabic: وَرَوَى ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ لَعَنَ عُلَمَاءَ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ إِذْ خَالَطُوا الظَّالِمِينَ فِي مَعَاشِهِمْ حَدِيثُ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ لَعَنَ اللَّهُ عُلَمَاءَ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ إِذْ خَالَطُوا الظَّالِمِينَ فِي مَعَايِشِهِمْ أَخْرَجَهُ أَبُو دَاوُدَ وَالتِّرْمِذِيُّ وَابْنُ مَاجَهْ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ لَمَّا وَقَعَتْ بَنُو إِسْرَائِيلَ فِي الْمَعَاصِي نَهَتْهُمْ عُلَمَاؤُهُمْ فَلَمْ يَنْتَهُوا فَجَالَس
5:78.english: And Ibn Mas'ud narrated from the Prophet (peace be upon him) that Allah cursed the scholars of the Children of Israel when they mingled with the wrongdoers in their livelihoods. The hadith of Ibn Mas'ud: 'Allah cursed the scholars of the Children of Israel when they mingled with the wrongdoers in their livelihoods' - reported by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'When the Children of Israel fell into sins, their scholars forbade them but they did not desist, so they sat with them in their gatherings, ate with them, and drank with them. Then Allah struck the hearts (Qulub) of some of them against others and cursed them on the tongue of David and Jesus son of Mary.' The wording is from al-Tirmidhi, who said: 'Hasan gharib (good but rare).'
5:78.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

5:82.arabic: ولأجل هذا انفرد الرهبانيون في الملل السالفة عن الخلق وانحازوا إلى قلل الجبال وآثروا التوحش عن الخلق لطلب الأنس بالله عز وجل فتركوا لله عز وجل اللذات الحاضرة وألزموا أنفسهم المجاهدات الشاقة طمعا في الآخرة وأثنى الله عز وجل عليهم في كتابه فقال: ﴿ ذلك بأن منهم قسيسين ورهبانا وأنهم لا يستكبرون ﴾ فلما اندرس ذلك وأقبل الخلق على اتباع الشهوات وهجروا التجرد لعبادة الله عز وجل وفتروا عنه بعث الله عز وجل نبيه محمدا ﭬ لإحياء طريق الآخرة وتجديد سنة المرسلين في سلوكها
5:82.english: For this reason, the monastic ones (الرهبانيون) in the past religious communities separated from creation and withdrew to mountain peaks, preferring isolation from creation to seek intimacy with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. They abandoned for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, the present pleasures and imposed upon themselves difficult struggles (المجاهدات), hoping for the Hereafter. And Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, praised them in His Book, saying: 'That is because among them are priests (قسيسين) and monks (رهبانا), and they are not arrogant.' Then when that faded and creation turned to following desires and abandoned devotion (التجرد) to the worship of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and became negligent about it, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to revive the path of the Hereafter and renew the way of the messengers in traversing it.
5:82.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

5:83.arabic: وقد أثنى الله تعالى على أهل الوجد بالقرآن فقال تعالى وإذا سمعوا ما أنزل إلى الرسول ترى أعينهم تفيض من الدمع مما عرفوا من الحق
5:83.english: And Allah the Exalted has praised the people of spiritual ecstasy (al-Wajd) through the Quran, for He said: 'And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears from what they have recognized of the Truth.'
5:83.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

5:87.arabic: وكان الحسن بن علي رضي الله عنهما يمر بالسؤال وبين أيديهم كسر فيقولون هلم إلى الغداء يا ابن رسول الله فكان ينزل ويجلس على الطريق ويأكل معهم ويركب ويقول إن الله لا يحب المستكبرين الوجه الثاني أن الذي شغل نفسه بطلب رضا الناس عنه وتحسين اعتقادهم فيه مغرور لأنه لو عرف الله حق المعرفة علم أن الخلق لا يغنون عنه من الله شيئا وأن ضرره ونفعه بيد الله ولا نافع ولا ضار سواه وأن من طلب رضا الناس ومحبتهم بسخط الله سخط الله عليه وأسخط عليه الناس بل رضا الناس غاية لا تنال فرضا الله أولى بالطلب ولذلك قال الشافعي
5:87.english: And Al-Hasan ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with them both) would pass by the beggars while they had crumbs before them, and they would say: 'Come to lunch, O son of the Messenger of Allah.' So he would dismount and sit on the road and eat with them, and then ride and say: 'Indeed, Allah does not love the arrogant ones.' The second aspect is that the one who occupies his Soul (Nafs) with seeking the pleasure of people about him and improving their belief in him is deluded, because if he knew Allah with true knowledge, he would know that the creation cannot avail him anything from Allah, and that his harm and benefit are in the hand of Allah, and there is no benefactor nor harmer except Him, and that whoever seeks the pleasure and love of people with the anger of Allah, Allah will be angry with him and make people angry with him. Rather, the pleasure of people is an unattainable goal, so the pleasure of Allah is more worthy of seeking. Therefore, Al-Shafi'i said to Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la: 'By Allah, I only advise you: there is no way to safety from people, so look at what suits you and do it.' Therefore, it is said: 'Whoever watches people dies grieving, and the bold one attains pleasure.' And Sahl looked at a man from his companions and said to him: 'Do such and such' for something he commanded him, and he said: 'O master, I cannot do it because of people.' So he turned to his companions and said: 'A servant does not attain the reality of this matter until he is in one of two descriptions: a servant from whose eye people have fallen, so he sees in the world only his Creator, and that no one can harm him nor benefit him; and a servant whose Soul (Nafs) has fallen from his Heart (Qalb), so he does not care in what state they see him.' And Al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'There is no one except that he has a lover and a hater, so if it is like this, then be with the people of obedience to Allah.' And it was said to Al-Hasan: 'O Abu Sa'id, there are people who attend your gathering whose aim is only to follow...'
5:87.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Seclusion'

5:87.arabic: وَمَرَّ الْحَسَنُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا بِقَوْمٍ مِنَ الْمَسَاكِينِ الَّذِينَ يَسْأَلُونَ النَّاسَ عَلَى الطَّرِيقِ وَقَدْ نَشَرُوا كِسَرًا عَلَى الْأَرْضِ فِي الرَّمْلِ وَهُمْ يَأْكُلُونَ وَهُوَ عَلَى بَغْلَتِهِ فَسَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِمْ فَقَالُوا لَهُ هَلُمَّ إِلَى الْغَدَاءِ يَا ابْنَ بِنْتِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَقَالَ نَعَمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُسْتَكْبِرِينَ فَنَزَلَ وَقَعَدَ مَعَهُمْ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ وَأَكَلَ ثُمَّ سَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَرَكِ
5:87.english: And Al-Hasan ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with them both) passed by a group of the poor (Masakin) who ask people on the road, and they had spread crumbs on the ground in the sand and they were eating, and he was on his mule. He greeted them, and they said to him: 'Come to lunch, O son of the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him).' He said: 'Yes, indeed Allah does not love the arrogant (Mustakbirin).' So he dismounted and sat with them on the ground and ate. Then he greeted them and rode and said: 'I have answered you, so answer me.' They said: 'Yes.' So he promised them a known time, and they attended. He presented to them the best of food and sat eating with them.
5:87.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Manners of Eating'

5:87.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
5:87.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'Whatever is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)".'
5:87.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

5:89.arabic: بل اللهو واللغو لا يؤاخذ الله تعالى به إن عنى به أنه فعل ما لا فائدة فيه فإن الإنسان لو وظف على نفسه أن يضع يده على رأسه في اليوم مائة مرة فهذا عبث لا فائدة له ولا يحرم قال الله تعالى لا يؤاخذكم الله باللغو في أيمانكم فإذا كان ذكر اسم الله تعالى على الشيء على طريق القسم من غير عقد عليه ولا تصميم والمخالفة فيه مع أنه لا فائدة فيه لا يؤاخذ فكيف يؤاخذ به بالشعر والرقص
5:89.english: Rather, amusement (Lahw) and idle talk (Laghw) - Allah the Exalted does not hold one accountable for them if what is meant by them is an action that has no benefit. For if a person were to impose upon himself to place his hand on his head one hundred times a day, this is frivolity that has no benefit and is not prohibited. Allah the Exalted said: 'Allah will not call you to account for what is futile in your oaths, but He will call you to account for your deliberate oaths; for expiation, feed ten indigent persons, on a scale of the average for the food of your families; or clothe them; or give a slave his freedom. If that is beyond your means, fast for three days. That is the expiation for the oaths you have sworn. But keep your oaths. Thus does Allah make clear to you His signs that you may be grateful.' (Quran 5:89) So if the mention of the name of Allah the Exalted upon something is by way of an oath without a binding commitment or firm resolve, and breaking it - despite it having no benefit - is not held accountable, then how can one be held accountable for it with poetry and dancing?
5:89.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

5:89.arabic: وعن ابن جريج انه كان يرخص في السماع فقيل له أيؤتى يوم القيامة في جملة حسناتك أو سيئاتك فقال لا في الحسنات ولا في السيئات لأنه شبيه باللغو وقال الله تعالى لا يؤاخذكم الله باللغو في ايمانكم هذا ما نقل من الاقاويل ومن طلب الحق في التقليد فمهما استقصى تعارضت عنده هذه الاقاويل فيبقى متحيرا أومائلا إلى بعض الاقاويل بالتشهي وكل ذلك قصور بل ينبغي أن يطلب الحق بطريقه وذلك بالبحث عن مدارك الحظر والاباحة كما سنذكره بيان الدليل على إباحة السماع
5:89.english: And from Ibn Jurayj, that he used to permit listening (to spiritual music/recitation). He was asked: 'Will it come on the Day of Resurrection among your good deeds or your bad deeds?' He said: 'Neither among the good deeds nor the bad deeds, because it resembles idle talk (al-Laghw).' And Allah the Exalted said: 'Allah will not call you to account for what is vain (al-Laghw) in your oaths...' This is what has been transmitted from the sayings. And whoever seeks the truth through imitation (taqlīd), whenever he exhaustively examines, these sayings conflict for him, so he remains perplexed or inclined to some sayings by mere desire. And all of that is deficiency. Rather, one should seek the truth by its proper way, and that is by investigating the sources of prohibition and permissibility, as we will mention the clarification of the evidence for the permissibility of listening (to spiritual music/recitation).
5:89.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

5:94.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
5:94.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'What is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)"'.
5:94.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

5:95.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
5:95.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'Whatever is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (Masakin)".'
5:95.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

5:101.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
5:101.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'What is in the Quran as "O you who have believed" is in the Torah as "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)."'
5:101.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

5:105.arabic: ومن خالط الناس فلا يخلو عن مشاهدة المنكرات فإن سكت عصى الله به وإن أنكر تعرض لأنواع من الضرر إذ ربما يجره طلب الخلاص عنها إلى معاص هي أكبر مما نهى عنه ابتداء وفي العزلة خلاص من هذا فإن الأمر في إهماله شديد والقيام به شاق وقدم قام أبو بكر رضي الله عند خطيبا وقال أيها الناس إنكم تقرءون هذه الآية يا أيها الذين آمنوا عليكم أنفسكم لا يضركم من ضل إذا اهتديتم وإنكم تضعونها في غير موضعها وإني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول إذا رأى الناس المنكر فلم يغيروه أوشك أن يعمهم الله بعقاب حديث أبي بكر إنك
5:105.english: And whoever mixes with people cannot avoid witnessing evil deeds (al-Munkarāt). If he remains silent, he disobeys Allah by it, and if he forbids it, he exposes himself to various types of harm, for perhaps seeking deliverance from them may lead him to sins that are greater than what he initially forbade. In seclusion (al-ʿUzlah) there is deliverance from this, for the matter in neglecting it is severe and performing it is burdensome. And previously, Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) stood as a preacher and said: 'O people, you recite this verse: "O you who have believed, upon you is [the care of] your own selves (Anfusakum). He who has gone astray cannot harm you when you are guided. To Allah is your return all together; then He will inform you of what you used to do." And you place it in other than its proper place. And I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: "If people see evil (al-Munkar) and do not change it, Allah is about to encompass them with punishment." The hadith of Abu Bakr: "You recite this verse: 'O you who have believed, upon you is [the care of] your own selves (Anfusakum). He who has gone astray cannot harm you when you are guided.' And you indeed place it in other than its proper place." The hadith was reported by the compilers of the Sunan. At-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan Sahih." And he (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, Allah questions the servant (al-ʿAbd) until He says to him: 'What prevented you when you saw evil (al-Munkar) from forbidding it?' Then if Allah provides the servant (al-ʿAbd) with his excuse, he says: 'O Lord, I hoped in You and feared people.'" The hadith: "Indeed, Allah questions the servant (al-ʿAbd) until He says: 'What prevented you when you saw evil (al-Munkar) in the world from forbidding it?'" The hadith was reported by Ibn Majah from the hadith of Abu Saʿid al-Khudri with a good chain. And this is if he fears from beating or a matter he cannot bear, and knowing the limits of that is problematic and in it is danger. And in seclusion (al-ʿUzlah) there is deliverance. And in commanding good (al-Amr bi-l-Maʿrūf) and forbidding evil (al-Nahy ʿan al-Munkar) there is stirring of disputes and agitation of the hidden evils of the chests (al-Ṣudūr), as it is said: 'And how many times have I driven in your traces from sincere advice?' And the sincere advisor may gain hatred. And whoever has tried commanding good (al-Amr bi-l-Maʿrūf) has regretted it mostly, for it is like a leaning wall that a person wants to straighten, and it is about to fall upon him. Then if it falls upon him, he says: 'I wish I had left it leaning.' Yes, if he found helpers who held the...
5:105.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Etiquette of Seclusion'

5:105.arabic: تأويلها يا أيها الذين آمنوا عليكم انفسكم الحديث أخرجه أصحاب السنن وتقدم في العزلة وإني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول ما من قوم عملوا بالمعاصي وفيهم من يقدر أن ينكر عليهم فلم يفعل إلا يوشك أن يعمهم الله بعذاب من عنده وروى عن أبي ثعلبة الخشنى أنه سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن تفسير قوله تعالى لا يضركم من ضل إذا اهتديتم حديث أبي ثعلبة أنه سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن تفسير قوله تعالى لا يضركم من ضل إذا اهتديتم الحديث أخرجه أبو داود والترمذي وحسنه وابن ماجه فقال يا أبا ثعلبة مر
5:105.english: Its interpretation: O you who have believed, upon you are your own selves (Anfusikum). The hadith was reported by the compilers of the Sunan and preceded in the chapter on seclusion. And I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, say: 'There is no people who commit sins while among them is one who is able to forbid them but does not do so, except that Allah is about to encompass them with punishment from Himself.' And it is narrated from Abu Tha'labah al-Khushani that he asked the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, about the interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: 'No harm will come to you from one who goes astray if you are guided.' The hadith of Abu Tha'labah that he asked the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, about the interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: 'No harm will come to you from one who goes astray if you are guided.' The hadith was reported by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi who graded it as good, and Ibn Majah. So he said: 'O Abu Tha'labah, enjoin what is good (Ma'ruf) and forbid what is evil (Munkar). But when you see stinginess obeyed, desire (Hawa) followed, the worldly life preferred, and every possessor of an opinion admiring his own opinion, then upon you is your own self (Nafs) and leave the common people. Indeed, behind you are trials like pieces of a dark night; for the one who holds fast in them to something like what you are upon, there is the reward of fifty of you.' It was said: 'Rather from them, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'No, rather from you, because you find helpers for good and they do not find helpers for it.' And Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked about the interpretation of this verse. He said: 'This is not its time; today it is accepted. But it is about to come a time when you will enjoin what is good (Ma'ruf) and such and such will be done to you, and you will say, but it will not be accepted from you. Then at that time, upon you are your own selves (Anfusikum); no harm will come to you from one who goes astray if you are guided.'
5:105.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

5:105.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
5:105.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'Whatever is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (Masakin)".'
5:105.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

5:105.arabic: وقدم قام أبو بكر رضي الله عند خطيبا وقال أيها الناس إنكم تقرءون هذه الآية يا أيها الذين آمنوا عليكم أنفسكم لا يضركم من ضل إذا اهتديتم وإنكم تضعونها في غير موضعها وإني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول إذا رأى الناس المنكر فلم يغيروه أوشك أن يعمهم الله بعقاب حديث أبي بكر إنكم تقرءون هذه الآية يا أيها الذين آمنوا عليكم أنفسكم لا يضركم من ضل إذا اهتديتم وإنكم لتضعونها في غير موضعها الحديث أخرجه أصحاب السنن قال الترمذي حسن صحيح وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله ليسأل العبد حتى يقول له ما منعك
5:105.english: And Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) stood as a preacher and said: 'O people, you recite this verse: "O you who have believed, upon you is [responsibility for] yourselves (Anfusakum). He who has strayed will not harm you when you have been guided. To Allah is your return all together; then He will inform you of what you used to do." And you place it in other than its proper place. And I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: "When people see evil (Al-Munkar) and do not change it, Allah is about to encompass them with punishment." The hadith of Abu Bakr: "You recite this verse: 'O you who have believed, upon you is [responsibility for] yourselves (Anfusakum). He who has strayed will not harm you when you have been guided.' And you indeed place it in other than its proper place." The hadith was reported by the compilers of the Sunan. At-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan Sahih." And he (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, Allah questions the servant (Al-'Abd) until He says to him: 'What prevented you when you saw evil (Al-Munkar) from forbidding it?' When Allah provides the servant (Al-'Abd) with his excuse, he says: 'O Lord, I hoped in You and feared people.'" The hadith: "Allah questions the servant (Al-'Abd) until He says: 'What prevented you when you saw evil (Al-Munkar) in the world from forbidding it?'" The hadith was reported by Ibn Majah from the narration of Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri with a good chain. And this is when he fears from beating or something unbearable, and knowing the limits of that is problematic and contains danger. And in seclusion (Al-'Uzlah) is salvation. And in enjoining good (Al-Amr bil-Ma'ruf) and forbidding evil (An-Nahy 'anil-Munkar) is the stirring of disputes and the agitation of the depths of chests (Sudur), as it is said: 'And how many times have I driven in your traces from advice?' And the advisor (Al-Munassih) may gain hatred. And whoever tries enjoining good (Al-Amr bil-Ma'ruf) regrets it mostly, for it is like a leaning wall that a person wants to straighten, and it is about to fall upon him. When it falls upon him, he says: 'I wish I had left it leaning.' Yes, if he found helpers who held the wall until he secured it with a support, it would stand straight. And you today do not find the helpers, so leave them and save yourself (Nafsak)."
5:105.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Seclusion'

5:105.arabic: وأما الأخبار فمنها ما روي عن أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه أنه قال في خطبة خطبها أيها الناس إنكم تقرءون هذه الآية وتؤولونها على خلاف تأويلها يا أيها الذين آمنوا عليكم أنفسكم لا يضركم من ضل إذا اهتديتم حديث أبي بكر أيها الناس إنكم تقرءون هذه الآية وتؤولونها على خلاف تأويلها يا أيها الذين آمنوا عليكم انفسكم الحديث أخرجه أصحاب السنن وتقدم في العزلة وإني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول ما من قوم عملوا بالمعاصي وفيهم من يقدر أن ينكر عليهم فلم يفعل إلا يوشك أن يعمهم الله بعذاب من عنده وروى عن أبي
5:105.english: And as for the narrations, among them is what was narrated from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said in a sermon he delivered: 'O people, you recite this verse and interpret it contrary to its interpretation: "O you who have believed, upon you is your own selves (Anfusikum). He who has gone astray will not harm you when you have been guided. To Allah is your return all together; then He will inform you about what you used to do."' The narration of Abu Bakr: 'O people, you recite this verse and interpret it contrary to its interpretation: "O you who have believed, upon you is your own selves (Anfusikum)..."' The narration was reported by the compilers of the Sunan and it was previously mentioned in the chapter on seclusion. And I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: 'There is no people who commit sins while among them is one who is able to forbid them, but he does not do so, except that Allah is about to encompass them with punishment from Himself.' And it was narrated from Abu Tha'labah al-Khushani that he asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) about the interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: 'He who has gone astray will not harm you when you have been guided.' The narration of Abu Tha'labah: that he asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) about the interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: 'He who has gone astray will not harm you when you have been guided.' The narration was reported by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi (who graded it as good), and Ibn Majah. So he said: 'O Abu Tha'labah, enjoin what is good (Ma'ruf) and forbid what is evil (Munkar). But if you see stinginess being obeyed, desire (Hawa) being followed, worldly life being preferred, and every possessor of an opinion being impressed with his own opinion, then upon you is your own self (Nafs) and leave the common people. Indeed, behind you are trials like pieces of a dark night. For the one who holds fast in them to something like what you are upon, there is the reward of fifty of you.' It was said: 'Rather, from among them, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'No, rather from among you, because you find helpers for good (Khayr) and they do not find helpers for it.' And Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) was asked about the interpretation of this verse, so he said: 'This is not its time; today it is accepted, but its time is about to come.'
5:105.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

5:106.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
5:106.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Whatever is in the Quran of 'O you who have believed' is in the Torah 'O you poor ones (al-Masakin)'.
5:106.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

5:109.arabic: وعند ذلك يصدق الله تعالى قوله: ﴿ فلنسألن الذين أرسل إليهم ولنسألن المرسلين فلنقصن عليهم بعلم وما كنا غائبين ﴾ {} وقوله: ﴿ فوربك لنسألنهم أجمعين عما كانوا يعملون ﴾ {} فيبدأ سبحانه بالأنبياء ﴿ يوم يجمع الله الرسل فيقول ماذا أجبتم قالوا لا علم لنا إنك أنت علام الغيوب ﴾ {} فيا لشدة يوم تذهل فيه عقول الأنبياء وتنمحى علومهم من شدة الهيبة إذ يقال لهم ما أجبتم وقد أرسلتم إلى الخلائق وكانوا قد علموا فتدهش عقولهم فلا يدرون بماذا يجيبون فيقولون من شدة الهيبة لا علم لنا إنك أنت علام الغيوب وهم فى ذلك الوقت
5:109.english: And at that time, Allah the Exalted will fulfill His saying: 'So We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent, and We will surely question the messengers. Then We will surely relate to them with knowledge, and We were not absent.' (Quran 7:6-7) and His saying: 'Then by your Lord, We will surely question them all about what they used to do.' (Quran 15:92-93) He begins, glorified is He, with the prophets: 'On the Day when Allah will assemble the messengers and say, "What was the response you received?" They will say, "We have no knowledge. Indeed, it is You who is Knower of the unseen."' (Quran 5:109) Oh, the severity of a day in which the intellects (Aql) of the prophets are bewildered and their knowledges (Ilm) are erased from the intensity of the awe (Hiba) when it is said to them, 'What was the response you received?' And they had been sent to the creation and they had known. So their intellects (Aql) are stunned, and they do not know with what to answer. So they say from the intensity of the awe (Hiba), 'We have no knowledge. Indeed, it is You who is Knower of the unseen.' And they at that time are truthful, for the intellects (Aql) have flown away from them and the knowledges (Ilm) have been erased until Allah the Exalted strengthens them.
5:109.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Repentance'

5:110.arabic: وأما التأييد فكأنه جامع للكل وهو عبارة عن تقوية أمره بالبصيرة من داخل وتقوية البطش ومساعدة الأسباب من خارج وهو المراد بقوله عز وجلّ: ﴿ إذ ايدتك بروح القدس ﴾ {} وتقرب منه العصمة وهى عبارة عن وجود إلهى يسبح في الباطن يقوى به الإنسان على تحرى الخير وتجنب الشر يصير كمانع من باطنه غير محسوس وإياه عنى بقوله تعالى: ﴿ ولقد همت به وهمّ بها لولا أن رأى برهان ربه ﴾ {} فهذه هى مجامع النعم ولن تثبت إلا بما يخوله الله من الفهم الصافى الثاقب والسمع الواعى والقلب البصير المراعى المتواضع والمعلم الناصح والمال ال
5:110.english: As for the Support (Tāʾyīd), it is as if it encompasses all, and it is an expression of strengthening his matter with insight from within and strengthening the grasp and assisting the causes from without, and this is what is intended by His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'When I supported you with the Spirit of Holiness (Rūḥ al-Quds)' {} and near to it is the Protection (ʿIṣmah), which is an expression of a divine presence that flows in the inner being, by which the human is strengthened to pursue good and avoid evil, becoming like an imperceptible barrier from his inner self, and it is this that is intended by His saying, the Exalted: 'And she certainly determined [to seduce] him, and he would have inclined to her had he not seen the proof of his Lord' {} These are the gatherings of blessings, and they will not be established except by what Allah grants of pure, penetrating understanding, attentive hearing, the seeing heart (Qalb) that is observant and humble, the advising teacher, wealth that exceeds what falls short of important matters by its scarcity, which is insufficient for what distracts from the religion by its abundance, and honor that protects him from the foolishness of the foolish and the injustice of enemies. Each one of these sixteen causes necessitates causes, and those causes necessitate causes until they end in the Hereafter with the guide of the perplexed and the refuge of the distressed, and that is the Lord of lords and the causer of causes. If these causes are lengthy and a book like this cannot bear their exhaustive treatment, then let us mention from them a model to understand by it the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: 'And if you should count the blessings of Allah, you could not enumerate them' {} And with Allah is success.
5:110.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

5:114.arabic: ورأيت في الإنجيل قال عيسى بن مريم عليه السلام لقد قيل لكم من قبل إن السن بالسن والأنف بالأنف وأنا أقول لكم لا تقاوموا بالشر بل من ضرب خدك الأيمن فحول إليه الخد الأيسر ومن اخذ رداءك فاعطه ازارك ومن سخرك لتسير معه ميلا فسر معه ميلين وكل ذلك أمر بالصبر على الاذى، فالصبر على اذى الناس من أعلى مراتب الصبر لانه يتعاون فيه باعث الدين وباعث الشهوة والغضب جميعا.
5:114.english: And I saw in the Gospel that Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him, said: 'It was said to you before: an eye for an eye and a nose for a nose, but I say to you: do not resist evil, but whoever strikes your right cheek, turn to him the left cheek, and whoever takes your cloak, give him your garment, and whoever compels you to go one mile, go with him two miles.' And all of that commands patience upon harm, for patience upon the harm of people is from the highest levels of patience because in it cooperate the motivator of religion and the motivator of desire and anger all together.
5:114.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

5:114.arabic: وقال عيسى ابن مريم عليه السلام: ويل لصاحب الدنيا كيف يموت ويتركها وما فيها، وتغره ويأمنها، ويثق بها وتخذله، وويل للمغترين كيف أرتهم ما يكرهون وفارقهم ما يحبون وجاءهم ما يوعدون؟ وويل لمن الدنيا همه والخطايا عمله كيف يفتضح غداً بذنبه؟
5:114.english: And Jesus son of Mary (peace be upon him) said: Woe to the possessor of the worldly life (Dunya) how he dies and leaves it and what is in it, and it deceives him and he feels secure in it, and he trusts it and it betrays him, and woe to the deceived ones how I showed them what they dislike and separated them from what they love and brought them what they are promised? And woe to the one whose concern is the worldly life (Dunya) and whose action is sins how he will be exposed tomorrow by his sin?
5:114.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of the World'

5:117.arabic: يستحب للمريد إذا أصبح أن يكون أحب أوراده الدعاء كما سيأتي ذكره في كتاب الأوراد فإن كنت من المريدين لحرث الآخرة المقتدين برسول الله ﭬ فيما دعا به فقل في مفتتح دعواتك[136] أعقاب صلواتك[137] سبحان ربي العلي الأعلى الوهاب لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له له الملك وله الحمد وهو على كل شيء قدير وقل رضيت بالله ربا وبالإسلام دينا وبمحمد ﭬ نبيا[138] ثلاث مرات وقل اللهم فاطر السموات والأرض عالم الغيب والشهادة رب كل شيء ومليكه أشهد أن لا إله إلا أنت أعوذ بك من شر نفسي وشر الشيطان وشركه[139] وقل اللهم إني أس
5:117.english: It is recommended for the seeker (Mureed) when morning comes that his most beloved devotional practices (Awrad) be supplication as will be mentioned in the Book of Devotional Practices. If you are among the seekers of the harvest of the Hereafter, following the Messenger of God ﷺ in what he supplicated with, then say at the beginning of your supplications[136] after your prayers[137]: 'Glory be to my Lord, the Most High, the Most Exalted, the Bestower. There is no god but God alone, without partner. To Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs praise, and He has power over all things.' And say: 'I am pleased with God as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad ﷺ as prophet'[138] three times. And say: 'O God, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, Lord of everything and its Sovereign. I bear witness that there is no god but You. I seek refuge in You from the evil of my soul (Nafs) and from the evil of Satan and his partnership'[139]. And say: 'O God, I ask You for pardon and well-being in my religion, my worldly life, my family, and my wealth. O God, cover my faults, secure my fears, remove my stumblings, and protect me from before me and from behind me, from my right and from my left, and from above me, and I seek refuge in You from being taken from beneath me'[140]. O God, do not make me feel secure from Your guile, do not entrust me to other than You, do not remove from me Your covering, do not make me forget Your remembrance (Dhikr), and do not make me...
5:117.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

5:117.arabic: وقال عليّ رضي الله عنه كنت رجلا إذا سمعت من رسول الله ﷺ حديثا نفعني الله عز وجل بما شاء أن ينفعني منه وإذا حدثني أحد من أصحابه استحلفته فإذا حلف صدقته قال وحدثني أبو بكر وصدق أبو بكر رضي الله عنه قال سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول: (ما من عبد يذنب ذنبا فيحسن الطهور ثم يقوم فيصلي ركعتين ثم يستغفر الله عز وجل إلا غفر له ثم تلا قوله عز وجل: ﴿ والذين إذا فعلوا فاحشة أو ظلموا أنفسهم ﴾ {}[117]) الآية.
5:117.english: And Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: I was a man who, when I heard a saying (Hadith) from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), Allah the Exalted benefited me with what He willed to benefit me from it, and when one of his companions narrated to me, I would make him swear an oath, and if he swore, I would believe him. He said: And Abu Bakr narrated to me, and Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) spoke truthfully. He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: 'There is no servant who commits a sin, then performs purification well, then stands and prays two units (Rak'atayn), then seeks forgiveness (Yastaghfir) from Allah the Exalted except that He forgives him.' Then he recited His saying the Exalted: 'And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves (ظلموا أنفسهم - Zalamu Anfusahum: wronged their souls/selfs (Nafs))' {}[117] the verse.
5:117.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication

5:118.arabic: ومن عرف حقيقة المعرفة قصور معرفته عن الإحاطة بكنة الأمور عظم خوفه لا محالة ولذلك قال المسيح ﭬ لما قيل له: ﴿ أأنت قلت للناس اتخذوني وأمي إلهين من دون الله قال سبحانك ما يكون لي أن أقول ما ليس لي بحق إن كنت قلته فقد علمته تعلم ما في نفسي ولا أعلم ما في نفسك ﴾ {} وقال: ﴿ إن تعذبهم فإنهم عبادك وإن تغفر لهم ﴾ {} الآية. فوض الأمر إلى المشيئة وأخرج نفسه بالكلية من البين لعلمه بأنه ليس له من الأمر شيء وأن الأمور مرتبطة بالمشيئة ارتباطا يخرج عن حد المعقولات والمألوفات فلا يمكن الحكم عليها بقياس ولا حدس و
5:118.english: And whoever knows the reality of knowledge (Ma'rifah) recognizes the deficiency of his knowledge in encompassing the essence of matters, his fear inevitably increases. Therefore, Jesus (peace be upon him) said when it was said to him: 'Did you say to people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?" He said, "Glory be to You! It is not for me to say what I have no right to. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Yourself."' And he said: 'If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them...' the verse. He delegated the matter to the Will (Mashiyyah) and completely removed himself from the affair, knowing that he has no part in the matter and that matters are connected to the Will in a connection that goes beyond the limits of rational considerations and familiar patterns. Thus, it is not possible to judge them by analogy, conjecture, or calculation, let alone by verification and certainty. This is what has broken the hearts of the knowers (Arifin), for the greatest calamity is the connection of your affair to the Will of One who does not care about you. If He destroys you, He has destroyed your like among countless others, and He has always been in the world punishing them with various pains and illnesses, and sickening their hearts (Qulub) from that with disbelief and hypocrisy, then He makes the punishment eternal upon them forever.
5:118.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

5:118.arabic: وعن أبي ذر قال: (قام رسول الله ﭬ بنا ليلة فقام بآية يرددها وهي ﴿ إن تعذبهم فإنهم عبادك وإن تغفر لهم ﴾ {}[38] الآية). وقام تميم الداري ليلة بهذه الآية ﴿ أم حسب الذين اجترحوا السيئات ﴾ {} الآية. وقام سعيد بن جبير ليلة يردد هذه الآية ﴿ وامتازوا اليوم أيها المجرمون ﴾ {}.
5:118.english: And from Abu Dharr, he said: (The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) stood with us one night, and he stood with a verse repeating it, and it is: "If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Mighty, the Wise." (Quran 5:118)). And Tamim al-Dari stood one night with this verse: "Or do those who commit evil deeds think..." (Quran 45:21). And Sa'id ibn Jubayr stood one night repeating this verse: "And be separated today, O criminals." (Quran 36:59).
5:118.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

5:118.arabic: وقال ﭬ: (أعطيت خمسا لم يعطهن أحد قبل نصرت بالرعب مسيرة شهر وأحلت لى الغنائم ولم تحل لأحد قبلى وجعلت لى الأرض مسجدا وترابها طهورا فأيما رجل من أمتى أدركته الصلاة فليصل وأعطيت الشفاعة وكل نبى بعث إلى قومه خاصة وبعثت إلى الناس عامة[176]) وقال ﭬ: (إذا كان يوم القيامة كنت إمام النبين وخطيبهم وصاحب شفاعتهم من غير فخر) وقال ﭬ: (أنا سيد ولد آدم ولا فخر وأنا أول من تنشق الأرض عنه وأنا أول شافع وأول مشفع بيدى لواء الحمد تحته آدم فمن دونه[177]) وقال ﭬ: (لكل نبى دعوة مستجابة فأريد أن أختبىء دعوتي شفاعة لأمت
5:118.english: And he (peace be upon him) said: 'I have been given five things that were not given to anyone before me: I have been aided with terror (al-Ru'b) for a month's journey, spoils of war (al-Ghana'im) have been made lawful for me and were not lawful for anyone before me, the earth has been made a place of prostration (Masjid) and its soil pure (Tahur) for me, so any man from my nation (Ummati) who is reached by the prayer (al-Salah) should pray, and I have been given intercession (al-Shafa'ah). Every prophet was sent to his people specifically, but I have been sent to all people generally.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'On the Day of Resurrection (Yawm al-Qiyamah), I will be the leader (Imam) of the prophets and their orator and the possessor of their intercession (Shafa'ah), without boasting.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'I am the master (Sayyid) of the children of Adam, without boasting, and I am the first from whom the earth will split open, and I am the first intercessor (Shafi') and the first whose intercession is accepted (Mushaffa'), in my hand is the banner of praise (Liwa' al-Hamd) under which is Adam and those after him.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Every prophet has a supplication (Da'wah) that is answered, and I want to reserve my supplication as intercession (Shafa'ah) for my nation (Ummati) on the Day of Resurrection (Yawm al-Qiyamah).' And Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Pulpits (Manabir) of gold will be erected for the prophets, and they will sit on them, but my pulpit will remain; I will not sit on it, standing before my Lord (Rabb) upright, fearing that I will be sent to Paradise and my nation (Ummati) remains after me, so I will say: O my Lord (Rabb), my nation (Ummati)! Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says:
5:118.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

5:118.arabic: حديث عمرو بن العاص أن رسول الله ﭬ تلا قول إبراهيم ﭬ - رب إنهن أضللن كثيرا من الناس فمن تبعنى فإنه منى ومن عصانى فإنك غفور رحيم - وقول عيسى ﭬ - إن تعذبهم فإنهم عبادك - ثم رفع يديه ثم قال أمتى أمتى ثم بكى الحديث وفيه يا جبريل اذهب إلى محمد فقل إنا سنرضيك ولا نسوءك فى أمتك قلت ليس هو من حديث عمرو بن العاص وإنما هو من حديث ابنه عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص كما رواه مسلم ولعله سقط من الإحياء ذكر عبد الله من بعض النساخ.
5:118.english: The hadith of 'Amr ibn al-'As that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) recited the saying of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) - 'My Lord, indeed they have led astray many of the people. So whoever follows me, then he is of me; and whoever disobeys me - indeed, You are Forgiving, Merciful' - and the saying of 'Isa (peace be upon him) - 'If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants' - then he raised his hands and then said: 'My Ummah, my Ummah' then wept. The hadith contains: 'O Jibril, go to Muhammad and say: Indeed, we will please you and not sadden you regarding your Ummah.' I said: It is not from the hadith of 'Amr ibn al-'As, but rather it is from the hadith of his son 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As as narrated by Muslim, and perhaps the mention of 'Abdullah dropped from some copyists of the Ihya'.
5:118.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Book of Repentance'

5:118.arabic: وفي رواية أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ إن تعذبهم فإنهم عبادك فبكى حديث إنه قرأ إن تعذبهم فإنهم عبادك فبكى أخرجه مسلم من حديث عبد الله بن عمرو
5:118.english: And in a narration, that the Prophet (peace be upon him) recited 'If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants' and wept. The hadith that he recited 'If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants' and wept was reported by Muslim from the narration of Abdullah ibn Amr.
5:118.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

5:119.arabic:
بيان فضيلة خصوص الفقراء من الراضين والقانعين والصادقين

قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " طوبى لمن هدي إلى الإسلام وكان عيشه كفافاً وقنع به"[36] وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: " يا معشر الفقراء أعطوا الله الرضا من قلوبكم تظفروا بثواب فقركم وإلا فلا"[37]. فالأول القانع، وهذا الراضي، ويكاد يشعر هذا بمفهومه: أن الحريص لا ثواب له على فقره ولكن العمومات الواردة في فضل الفقر تدل على أن له ثواباً كما سيأتي تحقيقه، فلعل المراد بعدم الرضا هو الكراهة لفعل الله في حبس الدنيا عنه، ورب راغبٍ في المال لا يخطر بقل
5:119.english:
Explanation of the virtue specifically of the poor who are content (Ar-Radhin), satisfied (Al-Qani'in), and truthful (As-Sadiqin).

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Blessed is the one who is guided to Islam and whose livelihood is sufficient (Kafafan) and he is satisfied (Qana'a) with it' [36]. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'O community of the poor, give Allah contentment (Ar-Rida) from your hearts so you may attain the reward of your poverty, otherwise not' [37]. The first is the satisfied one (Al-Qani'), and this is the content one (Ar-Radi), and this almost indicates by its implication: that the greedy one has no reward for his poverty, but the general texts that have come regarding the virtue of poverty indicate that he has a reward as will be clarified later. Perhaps what is meant by lack of contentment (Ar-Rida) is dislike for Allah's action in withholding the world from him, and perhaps one desirous of wealth does not have denial of Allah the Exalted or dislike for His action occur in his heart, so that dislike is what nullifies the reward of poverty.

And it is narrated from Umar ibn Al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) from the Prophet (peace be upon him) that he said: 'Indeed everything has a key, and the key to Paradise is love for the destitute and the poor due to their patience (Sabr), they are the companions (Julusa') of Allah the Exalted on the Day of Resurrection' [38].

And it is narrated from Ali (may Allah honor his face) from the Prophet (peace be upon him) that he said: 'The most beloved of servants to Allah the Exalted is the poor one who is satisfied (Al-Qani') with his provision, content (Ar-Radi) with Allah the Exalted' [39].

And he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Allah, make the sustenance of the family of Muhammad sufficient (Kafafan)' [40].

And Allah the Exalted said: 'Allah said: "This is the Day when the truthful (As-Sadiqin) will benefit from their truthfulness (Sidq). For them are gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him. That is the great attainment."' [41].

So the truthful ones (As-Sadiqun) are those who were truthful in their poverty, patience (Sabr), and contentment (Rida), so their poverty was truthful not false, and their contentment (Rida) was truthful not forced, so they were among the people of this verse. Look how Allah the Exalted combined for them between truthfulness (Sidq) and contentment (Rida), saying: 'will benefit the truthful (As-Sadiqin) from their truthfulness (Sidq)' then said: 'Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him', so He combined for them between the attribute of truthfulness (Sidq) and the attribute of contentment (Rida), and they are among the greatest attributes of the righteous poor. So whoever is truthful in his poverty and content (Radi) with the decree of Allah the Exalted, he is among those who will benefit from their truthfulness (Sidq) on the Day of Resurrection, and enters into the saying of Allah the Exalted: 'That is the great attainment.'
5:119.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

5:120.arabic: فإذا دخلت السوق فقل لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له له الملك وله الحمد يحيي ويميت وهو حي لا يموت بيده الخير وهو على كل شيء قدير
5:120.english: When you enter the market, say: There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner to Him, to Him belongs the Kingdom (al-Mulk) and to Him belongs the Praise, He gives life and causes death, and He is Living (Hayy) and does not die, in His hand is the good, and He is over all things All-Powerful (Qadir).
5:120.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter

5:120.arabic: الأصل الأول: العلم بأن صانع العالم قادر وأنه تعالى في قوله وهو على كل شيء قدير صادق لأن العالم محكم في صنعته مرتب في خلقته ومن رأى ثوبا من ديباج حسن النسج والتأليف متناسب التطريز والتطريف ثم توهم صدور نسجه عن ميت لا استطاعة له أو عن إنسان لا قدرة له كان منخلعا عن غريزة العقل ومنخرطا في سلك أهل الغباوة والجهل.
5:120.english: The First Foundation: The knowledge that the Maker of the world is Powerful (Qadir) and that He, exalted is He, in His saying 'And He is over all things Powerful (Qadir)' is truthful because the world is precise in its making, ordered in its creation. And whoever sees a garment of brocade, beautiful in its weaving and composition, harmonious in its embroidery and ornamentation, then imagines that its weaving issued from a dead thing that has no capability or from a human that has no power, has been stripped from the instinct of intellect and has been enrolled in the ranks of the people of stupidity and ignorance.
5:120.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Foundations of Belief'

5:120.arabic: يا من هو على كل شيء قدير
5:120.english: O You Who is over every thing powerful (Qadir).

5:120.arabic: [197] حديث القول عند دخول السوق لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له له الملك وله الحمد يحيي ويميت وهو حي لا يموت بيده الخير وهو على كل شيء قدير من حديث عمر وقال غريب والحاكم وقال صحيح على شرط الشيخين.
5:120.english: [197] The saying when entering the market: There is no god but Allah alone, He has no partner, to Him belongs the kingdom (al-mulk) and to Him belongs the praise, He gives life and causes death, and He is living and does not die, in His hand is the good, and He is over all things capable (qadir). From the narration of Umar, and it was said: rare (gharib), and Al-Hakim said: authentic according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs.
5:120.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication

6:1.arabic: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله الذي خلق كل شيء فأحسن خلقه وترتيبه وأدب نبيه محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم فأحسن تأديبه وزكى أوصافه وأخلاقه ثم اتخذه صفيه وحبيبه ووفق للإقتداء به من أراد تهذيبه وحرم عن التخلق بأخلاقه من أراد تخييبه صلى الله على سيدنا محمد سيد المرسلين وعلى آله الطيبين الطاهرين وسلم كثيرا أما بعد فإن آداب الظواهر عنوان آداب البواطن وحركات الجوارح ثمرات الخواطر والأعمال نتيجة الأخلاق والآداب رشح المعارف وسرائر القلوب هي مغارس الأفعال ومنابعها وأنوار السرائر هي التي تشرق على الظواهر فتز
6:1.english: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is to Allah who created everything and perfected its creation and arrangement, and educated His Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and perfected his education, purified his attributes and character, then took him as His intimate friend and beloved, and granted success in following him to whoever desired refinement, and prevented from adopting his character whoever desired corruption. May Allah send blessings upon our master Muhammad, master of the messengers, and upon his pure and purified family, and grant abundant peace. Now then, indeed the manners of outward appearances are an indicator of the manners of the inner selves, and the movements of the limbs are fruits of thoughts, and actions are the result of character traits and manners. The effusion of knowledge and the secrets of the hearts (Qulub) are the planting grounds of deeds and their sources, and the lights of the secrets are what shine upon outward appearances, thus adorning them, revealing them, and replacing their unpleasantness and faults with beauties. Whoever's heart (Qalb) does not humble itself, his limbs do not humble themselves, and whoever's chest is not a niche for the divine lights does not overflow upon his outward appearance with the beauty of the prophetic manners. I had resolved to conclude the quarter of customs in this book with a comprehensive book on the manners of living, so that it would not be difficult for the seeker to extract them from all these books. Then I saw that each book in the quarter of customs has covered a collection of manners, so I found it burdensome to repeat and reiterate them, for seeking repetition is heavy, and souls are inherently disposed to opposing repeated things. Therefore, I decided to limit myself in this book to mentioning the manners of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and...
6:1.book_title: Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character
6:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character'

6:1.arabic: الحمد لله الذي خلق الإنسان من طين لازب وصلصال ثم ركب  صورته  في  أحسن  تقويم وأتم اعتدال ثم غذاه في أول نشوه بلبن استصفاه من بين  فرث  ودم  سائغا  كالماء الزلال ثم حماه بما آتاه من طيبات الرزق  عن  دواعي  الضعف  والانحلال  ثم  قيد شهوته المعادية له عن السطوة والصيال وقهرها بما  افترضه  عليه  من  طلب  القوت الحلال وهزم بكسرها جند الشيطان المتشمر للإضلال ولقد  كان  يجري  من  ابن  آدم مجرى الدم السيال فضيق عليه عزة الحلال المجرى والمجال إذ كان  لا  يبذرقه  إلى أعماق العروق إلا الشهوة الماثلة إلى ال
6:1.english: Praise be to Allah who created the human being from sticky clay and ringing clay, then fashioned his form in the best proportion and most complete balance. Then He nourished him in his first growth with milk purified from between feces and blood, pleasant like pure water. Then He protected him with what He gave him of good provisions from the causes of weakness and dissolution. Then He restrained his appetite (Shahwa) that is hostile to him from domination and aggression, and subdued it with what He obligated upon him of seeking lawful (Halal) sustenance, and defeated by breaking it the army of Satan who is girded for misguidance. And indeed, it used to flow in the son of Adam like flowing blood, so the honor of the lawful (Halal) narrowed its channel and scope, since nothing pours it into the depths of the veins except the appetite (Shahwa) inclined to overpowering and indulgence. So he remained, when it was restrained with the rein of the lawful (Halal), disappointed and losing, with no helper or ally. And prayers upon Muhammad, the guide from misguidance, and upon his family, the best of families, and much peace.
6:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

6:1.arabic: العاشر في آداب الجماع ويستحب أن يبدأ باسم الله تعالى ويقرأ قل هو الله أحد أولا ويكبر ويهلل ويقول بسم الله العلي العظيم اللهم اجعلها ذرية طيبة إن كنت قدرت أن تخرج ذلك من صلبي وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم (لو أن أحدكم إذا أتى أهله قال اللهم جنبني الشيطان وجنب الشيطان ما رزقتنا فإن كان بينهما ولد لم يضره الشيطان)[139] وإذا قربت من الإنزال فقل في نفسك ولا تحرك شفتيك الحمد لله الذي خلق من الماء بشرا فجعله نسبا وصهرا وكان ربك قديرا وكان بعض أصحاب الحديث يكبر حتى يسمع أهل الدار صوته ثم ينحرف عن القبلة ولا ي
6:1.english: The tenth [section] is on the etiquettes of intercourse, and it is recommended to begin with the name of Allah the Exalted and to recite 'Say: He is Allah, the One' first, and to say 'Allahu Akbar' (Allah is Greatest) and 'La ilaha illa Allah' (There is no god but Allah), and to say: 'In the name of Allah, the Most High, the Most Great. O Allah, make it good offspring if You have decreed to bring that forth from my loins.' And the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'If one of you, when he approaches his wife, says: O Allah, keep me away from Satan and keep Satan away from what You have provided us, then if there is a child between them, Satan will not harm him.' And when you are close to ejaculation, say in your heart and do not move your lips: 'Praise be to Allah who created from water a human being and made him [a means of] lineage and marriage, and your Lord is ever Powerful.' And some of the companions of hadith would say 'Allahu Akbar' until the people of the house heard his voice, then he would turn away from the qiblah and not face the qiblah during intercourse out of respect for the qiblah, and to cover himself and his wife with a garment. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would cover his head, lower his voice, and say to the woman: 'Upon you is tranquility.'
6:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

6:4.arabic: ولكن ما تأتيهم من آية من آيات ربهم إلا كانوا عنها معرضين وذلك لأنّا جعلنا من بين أيديهم سدا ومن خلفهم سدا فأغشيناهم فهم لا يبصرون وسواء عليهم أأنذرتهم أم لم تنذرهم لا يؤمنون ولنرجع إلى الغرض فان هذه تلويحات تشير إلى أمور هي أعلى من علوم المعاملة.
6:4.english: But no sign (Ayat) from the signs (Ayat) of their Lord comes to them except that they turn away from it. And that is because We have placed a barrier before them and a barrier behind them and covered them, so they do not see. And it is the same to them whether you warn them or do not warn them - they will not believe. And let us return to the purpose, for these allusions point to matters that are higher than the sciences of interaction (Mu'amalat).
6:4.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

6:8.arabic: القسم الثاني: التكبر على الرسل من حيث تعزز النفس وترفعها على الانقياد لبشر مثل سائر الناس؛ وذلك تارة يصرف عن الفكر والاستبصار فيبقى في ظلمة الجهل بكبره فيمتنع عن الانقياد وهو ظان أنه محق فيه، وتارة يمتنع مع المعرفة ولكن لا تطاوعه نفسه للإنقياد للحق والتواضع للرسل، كما حكى الله قولهم "أنؤمن لبشرين مثلنا" وقولهم "إن أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا ولئن أطعتم بشراً مثلكم إنكم إذا لخاسرون" وقال الذين لا يرجون لقائنا لولا أنزل علينا الملائكة أو نرى ربنا لقد استكبروا في أنفسهم وعتوا عواً كبيراً. وقالوا لولا أنزل ع
6:8.english: The second category: Arrogance toward the messengers due to the Soul (Nafs) strengthening and elevating itself above submission to a human being like other people; this sometimes diverts from thought and insight, remaining in the darkness of ignorance through its arrogance, thus preventing submission while thinking it is correct in that, and sometimes it prevents despite knowledge but its Soul (Nafs) does not comply with submission to the Truth and humility toward the messengers, as Allah narrated their saying "Shall we believe in two humans like ourselves" and their saying "You are only humans like us, and if you obey a human like yourselves, then indeed you would be losers" and said those who do not hope for Our meeting: "If only angels were sent down to us or we see our Lord" they have certainly become arrogant within themselves and transgressed greatly. And they said: "If only a angel had been sent down to him" and Pharaoh, in what Allah informed about him, said: "Or he comes with the angels accompanying him" and Allah the Exalted said: "And he and his soldiers were arrogant in the land without right" so he was arrogant toward Allah and toward all His messengers.
6:8.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

6:13.arabic: وإذا جن عليه الليل فليقل يا أرض ربي وربك الله أعوذ بالله من شرك ومن شر ما فيك وشر ما دب عليك أعوذ بالله من شر كل أسد وأسود وحية وعقرب ومن شر ساكني البلد ووالد وما ولد وله ما سكن في الليل والنهار وهو السميع العليم
6:13.english: And when the night covers him, let him say: 'O earth, my Lord and your Lord is Allah. I seek refuge in Allah from your evil and from the evil of what is in you and the evil of what crawls upon you. I seek refuge in Allah from the evil of every lion and black one, and snake and scorpion, and from the evil of the inhabitants of the land, and the parent and what is born.'
