And to Him belongs what settles in the night and the day, and He is the All-Hearing (As-Sami'), the All-Knowing (Al-'Alim).
6:13.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Etiquette of Travel'

6:13.arabic: فإذا نزل المنزل صلى ركعتين فيه ثم قال: أعوذ بكلمات الله التامات التي لا يجاوزهن بر ولا فاجر من شر ما خلق فإذا جن عليه الليل يقول يا أرض ربي وربك الله أعوذ بالله من شرك وشر ما فيك وشر ما دب عليك أعوذ بالله من شر كل أسد وأسود وحية وعقرب ومن شر ساكن البلد ووالد وما ولد وله ما سكن في الليل والنهار وهو السميع العليم.
6:13.english: When he alights at a stopping place, he prays two rak'ahs in it, then says: 'I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah which no righteous or wicked one can surpass, from the evil of what He has created.' When night falls upon him, he says: 'O earth, my Lord and your Lord is Allah. I seek refuge in Allah from your evil and the evil of what is in you and the evil of what crawls upon you. I seek refuge in Allah from the evil of every lion, black one, snake, and scorpion, and from the evil of the inhabitant of the land, and the parent and what is born. And to Him belongs what settles in the night and the day, and He is the All-Hearing (As-Sami'), the All-Knowing (Al-'Alim).'
6:13.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

6:15.arabic: فإذا قال ﴿ إني أخاف إن عصيت ربي عذاب يوم عظيم ﴾ {} ولم يكن خائفا كان حاكيا
6:15.english: If he says, 'Indeed, I fear if I disobey my Lord the punishment of a great day' and he is not fearful, he is merely imitating.
6:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

6:19.arabic: وإذا قصد بالخطاب جميع الناس فقد قصد الآحاد فهذا القارىء الواحد مقصود فما له ولسائر الناس فليقدر أنه المقصود قال الله تعالى ﴿ وأوحى إليّ هذا القرآن لأنذركم به ومن بلغ ﴾ {} قال محمد بن كعب القرظي من بلغه القرآن فكأنما كلمه الله وإذا قدر ذلك لم يتخذ دراسة القرآن عمله بل يقرؤه كما يقرأ العبد كتاب مولاه الذي كتبه إليه ليتأمله ويعمل بمقتضاه.
6:19.english: And if the address is intended for all people, then the individuals are intended, so this single reader is intended, and what is for him and for all other people, let him consider that he is the intended one. Allah the Exalted said: 'And this Quran has been revealed to me that I may warn you thereby and whoever it reaches.' {} Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: Whoever the Quran reaches, it is as if Allah has spoken to him. And if he considers that, he does not take studying the Quran as his work, but rather he reads it as the servant reads the book of his Master which He wrote to him to contemplate it and act according to its requirements.
6:19.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

6:20.arabic: وإنما يضاعف عذاب العالم في معصيته لأنه عصى من علم ولذلك قال الله عز وجل: (إن المنافقين في الدرك الأسفل من النار( (النساء:145). لأنهم جحدوا بعد العلم وجعل اليهود شرا من النصارى مع أنهم ما جعلوا لله سبحانه ولدا ولا قالوا إنه ثالث ثلاثة إلا أنهم أنكروا بعد المعرفة إذ قال الله (يعرفونه كما يعرفون أبناءهم( (البقرة:146) (الأنعام:20). وقال تعالى: (فلما جاءهم ما عرفوا كفروا به فلعنة الله على الكافرين( (البقرة:89). وقال تعالى في قصة بلعام بن باعوراء (واتل عليهم نبأ الذي آتيناه آياتنا فانسلخ منها فأتبعه ا
6:20.english: And indeed, the punishment of the scholar in his disobedience is multiplied because he disobeyed from knowledge. And for that reason, Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire' (An-Nisa: 145). Because they denied after knowledge. And He made the Jews worse than the Christians, even though they did not make for Allah, glorified be He, a son, nor did they say He is the third of three, except that they rejected after recognition (ma'rifah), since Allah said: 'They recognize him as they recognize their sons' (Al-Baqarah: 146) (Al-An'am: 20). And He the Exalted said: 'But when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of Allah be upon the disbelievers' (Al-Baqarah: 89). And He the Exalted said in the story of Balaam son of Beor: 'And recite to them the news of him to whom We gave Our signs, but he detached himself from them; so Satan pursued him, and he became of the deviators' (Al-A'raf: 175) until He said: 'So his example is like that of the dog: if you chase him, he pants, or if you leave him, he [still] pants' (Al-A'raf: 176). Likewise is the wicked scholar, for Balaam was given the Book of Allah the Exalted, but he clung to desires, so he was likened to the dog, meaning whether he was given wisdom or not, he pants towards desires.
6:20.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

6:21.arabic: وقد سوى الله تعالى بين من افترى على الله كذبا وبين من كذب بالحق فقال تعالى: (ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بالحق لما جاءه( (العنكبوت: 68). وقال تعالى: (فمن أظلم ممن كذب على الله وكذب بالصدق إذ جاءه( (الزمر: 32).
6:21.english: And Allah the Exalted has equated between one who fabricates a lie against Allah and one who denies the truth when it comes to him, as He said: 'And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah or denies the truth when it has come to him?' (Al-Ankabut: 68). And He said: 'So who is more unjust than one who lies about Allah and denies the truth when it comes to him?' (Az-Zumar: 32).
6:21.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Book of Knowledge'

6:25.arabic: ومن لم يكن له فهم ما في القرآن ولو في أدنى الدرجات دخل في قوله تعالى: ﴿ ومنهم من يستمع إليك حتى إذا خرجوا من عندك قالوا للذين أوتوا العلم ماذا قال آنفا أولئك الذين طبع الله على قلوبهم ﴾ {} والطابع هي الموانع التي سنذكرها في موانع الفهم وقد قيل: لا يكون المريد مريدا حتى يجد في القرآن كل ما يريد ويعرف منه النقصان من المزيد ويستغني بالمولى عن العبيد. السادس: التخلي عن موانع الفهم فإن أكثر الناس منعوا عن فهم معاني القرآن لأسباب وحجب أسدلها الشيطان على قلوبهم فعميت عليهم عجائب أسرار القرآن قال ﭬ: (لو
6:25.english: And whoever does not have understanding of what is in the Quran, even in the lowest degrees, enters into His saying, the Exalted: 'And among them are those who listen to you until when they depart from you, they say to those who were given knowledge: What did he say just now? Those are the ones upon whose hearts Allah has set a seal.' {} And the seal are the barriers that we will mention in the barriers of understanding. And it has been said: The Seeker (Mureed) does not become a true seeker until he finds in the Quran everything he desires and recognizes from it the deficiency from the increase and becomes independent with the Master (Mawla) from the servants. Sixth: Abandoning the barriers of understanding, for most people are prevented from understanding the meanings of the Quran due to reasons and veils that Satan has draped over their hearts, so the wonders of the secrets of the Quran are blinded to them. He said: 'If it were not that the devils hover around the hearts of the children of Adam, they would look at the Unseen Realm (Malakoot).' And the meanings of the Quran are from the totality of the Unseen Realm (Malakoot), and everything that is absent from the senses and is not perceived except by the light of insight (Basseerah) is from the Unseen Realm (Malakoot).
6:25.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

6:30.arabic: وقرئ عند يحيى البكاء ﴿ ولو ترى إذ وقفوا على ربهم ﴾{} فصاح صيحة مكث منها مريضا أربعة أشهر يعاد من أطراف البصرة
6:30.english: And it was recited before Yahya the Weeper: "And if you could see when they are made to stand before their Lord (Rabb)" (Quran 6:30), so he cried out a cry, and he remained sick from it for four months, being visited from the outskirts of Basra.
6:30.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Fear and Hope'

6:38.arabic: وقال أبو هريرة فى قوله عز وجل ﴿ وما من دابة فى الأرض ولا طائر يطير بجناحيه إلا أمم أمثالكم ﴾ {} أنه يحشر الخلق كلهم يوم القيامة البهائم والدواب والطير وكل شىء فيبلغ من عدل الله تعالى أن يأخذ للجماء من القرناء ثم يقول كونى ترابا فذلك حين يقول الكافر يا ليتنى كنت ترابا فكنت أنت يا مسكين فى يوم ترى صحيفتك خالية عن حسنات طال فيها تعبك فتقول أين حسناتي فيقال نقلت إلى صحيفة خصمائك وترى صحيفتك مشحونة بسيئات طال فى الصبر عنها نصبك واشتد بسبب الكف عنها عناؤك فتقول يا رب هذه سيئات ما قارفتها قط فيقال هذه
6:38.english: And Abu Huraira said regarding His Exalted statement 'And there is no creature on the earth nor a bird that flies with its two wings except that they are communities like you' {} that He will gather all creation on the Day of Resurrection - the animals, the beasts, the birds, and everything - to the extent of the justice of Allah the Exalted that He will take for the hornless from the horned, then He says: 'Be dust!' That is when the disbeliever says: 'I wish I were dust!' So you, O wretched one, on a day when you see your record empty of good deeds in which your toil was prolonged, you will say: 'Where are my good deeds?' It will be said: 'They were transferred to the record of your adversaries.' And you see your record laden with bad deeds in which your exertion in abstaining from them was prolonged and your effort in refraining from them intensified, so you say: 'O Lord, these are bad deeds I never committed!' It will be said: 'These are the bad deeds of the people whom you backbit, insulted, intended with evil, and wronged in transactions, neighborliness, conversation, debate, discussion, study, and all other types of dealings.'
6:38.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

6:41.arabic: واستثنى في خمسة اشياء في الاغناء والاجابة والرزق والمغفرة والتوبة فقال تعالى: ﴿ فسوف يغنيكم الله من فضله ان شاء ﴾ {} وقال فيكشف ما تدعون اليه ان شاء - وقال يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب وقال: ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء وقال: ويتوب الله على من يشاء وهو خلق من اخلاق الربوبية اذ قال تعالى: ﴿ والله شكور حليم ﴾ {}
6:41.english: And He made an exception in five things: in enrichment, response, provision, forgiveness, and repentance. So He, the Exalted, said: 'Then Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills' (Quran 24:28). And He said: 'He removes what you call to if He wills' (Quran 6:41). And He said: 'He provides for whom He wills without measure' (Quran 2:212). And He said: 'And He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills' (Quran 4:48). And He said: 'And Allah turns in repentance to whom He wills' (Quran 9:15). And it is a character from the characters of Lordship (Rububiyyah), as He, the Exalted, said: 'And Allah is Appreciative (Shakur), Forbearing (Haleem)' (Quran 64:17).
6:41.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

6:44.arabic: وعن عقبة بن عامر عن النبي ﷺ أنه قال: (إذا رأيتم الرجل يعطيه الله ما يحب وهو مقيم على معصيته فاعلموا أن ذلك استدراج ثم قرأ قوله تعالى: ﴿ فلما نسوا ما ذكروا به فتحنا عليهم أبواب كل شىء ﴾ {}[104]) يعنى لما تركوا ما أمروا به فتحنا عليهم أبواب الخير حتى إذا فرحوا بما أوتوا أى بما أعطوا من الخير أخذناهم بغتة.
6:44.english: And from Uqbah ibn Amir from the Prophet (peace be upon him) that he said: 'When you see a man whom Allah gives what he loves while he persists in his disobedience (ma'siyyah), know that that is gradual entrapment (istidraj).' Then he recited His saying, the Exalted: 'So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened upon them the doors of every thing' (Quran 6:44). This means: when they abandoned what they were commanded with, We opened upon them the doors of good (khayr) until when they rejoiced with what they were given, that is, with what they were granted of good, We seized them suddenly.
6:44.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

6:44.arabic: وهذا الغرور علاجه معرفة دلائل الكرامة والهوان إما بالبصيرة أو بالتقليد أما البصيرة فبأن يعرف وجه كون الالتفات إلى شهوات الدنيا مبعد عن الله ووجه كون التباعد عنها مقرباً إلى الله ويدرك ذلك بالإلهام في منازل العارفين والأولياء، وشرحه من جملة علوم المكاشفة ولا يليق بعلم المعاملة "وأما معرفته بطريق التقليد والتصديق" فهو أن يؤمن بكتاب الله تعالى ويصدق رسوله وقد قال تعالى "أيحسبون أن ما نمدهم به من مال وبنين نسارع لهم في الخيرات بل لا يشعرون" وقال تعالى "سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون" وقال تعالى "فتحنا ع
6:44.english: And the cure for this delusion (Ghurur) is knowing the signs of honor (Karama) and humiliation (Hawan) either through insight (Bassira) or through imitation (Taqleed). As for insight, it is by knowing how turning toward worldly desires distances from Allah and how distancing from them brings near to Allah, and one perceives this through inspiration (Ilham) in the stations of the knowers (Arifeen) and the friends (Awliya), and its explanation is among the sciences of unveiling (Makashafa) and is not fitting for the science of transaction (Mu'amala). "And as for knowing it through the way of imitation and belief (Tasdeeq)," it is to have faith in the Book of Allah the Exalted and believe His Messenger. And He the Exalted has said: "Do they think that what We extend to them of wealth and children, We hasten for them in good things? Rather, they do not perceive." And He the Exalted has said: "We will gradually lead them [to destruction] from where they do not know." And He the Exalted has said: "So when they forgot that by which they had been reminded, We opened to them the doors of every [good] thing until, when they rejoiced in that which they were given, We seized them suddenly, and they were [then] in despair." And in the interpretation of His saying the Exalted "We will gradually lead them [to destruction] from where they do not know" is that whenever they commit a sin, We bring them a blessing to increase their delusion. And He the Exalted has said: "We only extend time for them that they may increase in sin." And He the Exalted has said: "And never think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. He only delays them for a Day when eyes will stare [in horror]." And other than that from what has come in the Book of Allah the Exalted and the Sunnah of His Messenger. So whoever believes in it is freed from this delusion, for the origin of this delusion is ignorance of Allah and His attributes, for whoever knows Him does not feel secure from His plan (Makr) nor is deceived by such false imaginings, and looks to Pharaoh, Haman, and Korah and to the kings of the earth and what happened to them—how Allah was good to them initially then destroyed them utterly! So He the Exalted said: "Do you perceive of them anyone?" the verse.
6:44.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

6:45.arabic: فَقُطِعَ دَابِرُ الْقَوْمِ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا ۚ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ
6:45.english: Then the root of the people who did wrong was cut off, and praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

6:46.arabic: فإن قلت: فما علامة عدم اتكاله على البضاعة والكفاية؟ فأقول: علامته أنه إن سرقت بضاعته أو خسرت تجارته أو تعوق أمر من أموره كان راضياً به ولم تبطل طمأنينته ولم يضطرب قلبه، بل كان حال قلبه في السكون قبله وبعده واحداً، فإن لم يسكن إلى شيء لم يضطرب لفقده، ومن اضطرب لفقد شيء فقد سكن إليه، وكان بشر يعمل المغازل فتركها، وذلك لأن البعادي كاتبه قال: بلغني أنك استعنت على رزقك بالمغازل، أرأيت إن أخذ الله سمعك وبصرك الرزق على من؟ فوقع ذلك في قلبه فأخرج آلة المغازل من يده وتركها.
6:46.english: If you say: What is the sign of not relying on merchandise and sufficiency? I say: Its sign is that if his merchandise is stolen or his trade incurs loss or some matter of his affairs is obstructed, he is content with it and his tranquility (Tuma'ninah) is not nullified and his heart (Qalb) does not become agitated. Rather, the state of his heart in stillness (Sukun) before it and after it is one. For if he does not settle upon something, he does not become agitated by its loss, and whoever becomes agitated by the loss of something has indeed settled upon it. And Bishr used to make spindles then abandoned them, and that is because Al-Ba'adi wrote to him: It has reached me that you have sought help for your provision (Rizq) through spindles. 'Tell me, if Allah takes away your hearing and your sight, upon whom is the provision?' So that settled in his heart, and he took the tool of spindles out of his hand and abandoned them.
6:46.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

6:52.arabic: وقالت قريش لرسول الله ﷺ: كيف نجلس إليك وعند هؤلاء؟ وأشاروا إلى فقراء المسلمين فازدروهم بأعينهم لفقرهم، وتكبروا عن مجالستهم فأنزل الله تعالى "ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي" إلى قوله "ما عليك من حسابهم" وقال تعالى "واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه ولا تعد عيناك عنهم تريد زينة الحياة الدنيا" ثم أخبر الله تعالى عن تعجبهم حين دخلوا جهنم إذ لم يروا الذين ازدروهم فقالوا "ما لنا لا نرى رجالاً كنا نعدهم من الأشرار" قيل يعنون عماراً وبلالاً وصهيباً والمقداد رضي الله عنه
6:52.english: And the Quraysh said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him): 'How can we sit with you while these are present?' And they pointed to the poor Muslims, and they looked down upon them with their eyes because of their poverty, and they were too proud to sit with them. So Allah the Exalted revealed: 'And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, seeking His Face (Wajhahu)' up to His saying 'You are not accountable for them.' And He said: 'And restrain your soul (Nafs) with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, seeking His Face (Wajhahu), and do not turn your eyes away from them, desiring the adornment of the worldly life.' Then Allah the Exalted informed about their astonishment when they entered Hell, as they did not see those whom they had looked down upon, so they said: 'Why do we not see men whom we used to count among the wicked?' It is said they meant Ammar, Bilal, Suhayb, and Miqdad (may Allah be pleased with them). Then among them were those whom pride prevented from reflection and knowledge, so they were ignorant of his (peace be upon him) being right, and among them were those who knew but pride prevented them from acknowledgment. Allah the Exalted said informing about them: 'So when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it,' and He said: 'And they denied them while their souls (Anfus) were convinced of them, out of injustice and arrogance.' And this pride is close to being proud against Allah the Almighty, even if it is less than that, but it is pride against accepting the command of Allah and humbling oneself to His Messenger.
6:52.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

6:52.arabic: وأما عبادة ذوي الألباب فإنها لا تجاوز ذكر الله تعالى والفكر فيه لجماله لماله وجلاله وسائر الأعمال تكون مؤكدات وروادف وهؤلاء ارفع درجة من الالتفات إلى المنكوح والمطعوم في الجنة فإنهم لم يقصدوها بل هم الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه فقط وثواب الناس بقدر نياتهم فلا جرم يتنعمون بالنظر إلى وجهه الكريم ويسخرون ممن يلتفت إلى وجه الحور العين كما يسخر المتنعم بالنظر إلى الحور العين ممن يتنعم بالنظر إلى وجه الصور المصنوعة من الطين بل أشد فإن التفاوت بين جمال حضرة الربوبية وجمال الحور العين أشد
6:52.english: As for the worship of the possessors of intellects (ذوي الألباب), it does not exceed the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah the Exalted and contemplation upon Him for His beauty, for what He possesses, and for His majesty, and all other actions are confirmations and accompaniments. These are of a higher degree than turning attention to the one to be coupled with and the food in Paradise, for they did not intend it. Rather, they are those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, desiring only His Face (وجهه). And the reward of people is according to their intentions, so it is no wonder that they delight in gazing upon His Noble Face and mock those who turn to the faces of the wide-eyed maidens (الحور العين), just as one who delights in gazing upon the wide-eyed maidens mocks one who delights in gazing upon the faces of images made from clay—indeed, more severe. For the disparity between the beauty of the Presence of Lordship (حضرة الربوبية) and the beauty of the wide-eyed maidens is more severe and much greater than the disparity between the beauty of the wide-eyed maidens and images made from clay.
6:52.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

6:52.arabic: ويجالس الفقراء حديث كان يجالس الفقراء أخرجه أبو داود من حديث أبي سعيد جلست في عصابة من ضعفاء المهاجرين وإن بعضهم ليستر بعضا من العرى الحديث وفيه فجلس رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وسطنا ليعدل بنفسه فينا الحديث وابن ماجه من حديث خباب وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يجلس معنا الحديث في نزول قوله تعالى ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه ما عليك من حسابهم من شيء وما من حسابك عليهم من شيء فتطردهم فتكون من الظالمين إسنادهما حسن ويؤاكل المساكين حديث مؤاكلته للمساكين أخرجه البخاري من
6:52.english: And he would sit with the poor (Fuqara) - a hadith that he would sit with the poor was reported by Abu Dawud from the narration of Abu Sa'id: 'I sat in a group of weak emigrants (Muhajirin), and indeed some of them would cover the nakedness of others...' In it: 'And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) sat among us to make himself equal among us...' And Ibn Majah from the narration of Khabbab: 'And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) would sit with us...' In the revelation of His saying, the Exalted: 'And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord (Rabb) in the morning and the evening, desiring His Face (Wajh). Not upon you is anything of their account, and not of your account upon them is anything, so that you would drive them away and be among the wrongdoers (Zalimin).' Their chains are good (Hasan). And he would eat with the poor (Masakin) - a hadith of his eating with the poor was reported by Bukhari from the narration of Abu Hurairah who said: 'And the People of the Suffah (Ahl al-Suffah) were the guests of Islam; they had no family or wealth to turn to. When charity (Sadaqah) came to him, he would send it to them and not take from it, and when a gift (Hadiyyah) came to him, he would send to them and take from it and share them in it.'
6:52.book_title: Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character
6:52.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character'

6:52.arabic: بيان فضيلة النية قال الله تعالى ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشى يريدون وجهه والمراد بتلك الإرادة هى النية
6:52.english: Explanation of the virtue of intention (Niyyah). Allah the Exalted said: 'And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, desiring His Face (Wajhahu).' The intended meaning of that desire is the intention (Niyyah).
6:52.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

6:52.arabic: وقال تعالى: ﴿ ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه ﴾ {}. فهذا كله يبين لك أن الطريق إلى تعالى مراقبة الأوقات وعمارتها بالأوراد على سبيل الدوام ولذلك قال ﭬ: (أحب عباد الله إلى الله الذين يراعون الشمس والقمر والأظلة لذكر الله تعالى[1]).
6:52.english: And He, the Exalted, said: 'And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, desiring His Face (Wajhahu).' {}. All of this clarifies for you that the path to the Exalted is the observance (Murāqabah) of the times and filling them with regular litanies (Awrād) on the basis of continuity, and for that reason He, peace be upon him, said: 'The most beloved of Allah's servants to Allah are those who observe the sun, the moon, and the shadows for the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah, the Exalted.'
6:52.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

6:53.arabic: السبب الثالث: الكبر؛ وهو أن يكون في طبعه أن يتكبر عليه ويستصغره ويستخدمه ويتوقع منه الانقياد له والمتابعة في أغراضه، فإذا نال نعمة خاف أن لا يحتمل تكبره ويترفع عن متابعته، أو ربما يتشوف إلى مساواته أو إلى أن يرتفع عليه فيعود متكبراً بعد أن كان متكبراً عليه. ومن التكبر والتعزز كان حسد أكثر الكفار لرسول الله ﭬ إذ قالوا: كيف يتقدم علينا غلام يتيم وكيف نطأطئ رؤوسنا؟ فقالوا "لولا نزل هذا القرآن على رجل من القريتين عظيم"[108] أي كان لا يثقل علينا أن نتواضع له ونتبعه إذا كان عظيماً وقال تعالى يصف قول ق
6:53.english: The third cause: Arrogance (Kibr); it is that it be in his nature to be arrogant toward him and belittle him and use him and expect from him submission to him and following in his purposes, so if he attains a blessing (Ni'mah) he fears that he will not bear his arrogance and rise above following him, or perhaps he aspires to equality with him or to rising above him so he returns arrogant after having been arrogant toward him. And from arrogance and self-importance (Ta'azzuz) was the envy (Hasad) of most disbelievers (Kuffar) for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when they said: How does an orphan boy advance upon us and how do we lower our heads? So they said "If only this Quran had been revealed to a man of importance from the two towns" meaning it would not be heavy upon us to humble ourselves to him and follow him if he were important. And Allah the Exalted said describing the saying of Quraysh "Are these the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us?" as belittling them and pride (Anfah) from them.
6:53.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

6:53.arabic: وقالت قريش لرسول الله ﷺ: كيف نجلس إليك وعند هؤلاء؟ وأشاروا إلى فقراء المسلمين فازدروهم بأعينهم لفقرهم، وتكبروا عن مجالستهم فأنزل الله تعالى "ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي" إلى قوله "ما عليك من حسابهم" وقال تعالى "واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه ولا تعد عيناك عنهم تريد زينة الحياة الدنيا" ثم أخبر الله تعالى عن تعجبهم حين دخلوا جهنم إذ لم يروا الذين ازدروهم فقالوا "ما لنا لا نرى رجالاً كنا نعدهم من الأشرار" قيل يعنون عماراً وبلالاً وصهيباً والمقداد رضي الله عنه
6:53.english: And the Quraysh said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him): 'How can we sit with you while these are present?' And they pointed to the poor Muslims and despised them with their eyes due to their poverty, and they were too proud to sit with them. So Allah the Exalted revealed: 'And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening' up to His saying: 'You are not accountable for them.' And He said: 'And restrain your soul (Nafs) with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, seeking His Face, and do not turn your eyes away from them, desiring the adornment of the worldly life.' Then Allah the Exalted informed about their astonishment when they entered Hellfire, as they did not see those whom they had despised, so they said: 'Why do we not see men whom we used to count among the wicked?' It is said they meant Ammar, Bilal, Suhayb, and Miqdad (may Allah be pleased with them). Then among them were those whom pride prevented from thought and knowledge, so they were ignorant that he (peace be upon him) was right; and among them were those who knew but pride prevented them from acknowledgment. Allah the Exalted said, informing about them: 'So when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it.' And He said: 'And they denied them while their souls (Anfus) were convinced of them, out of injustice and arrogance.' And this pride is close to being proud against Allah the Mighty and Majestic, even though it is less than that, but it is pride against accepting the command of Allah and humbling oneself to His Messenger. And Allah the Exalted said: 'And thus We have tried some of them by others so that they would say, "Are these the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us?" Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?' meaning despising them and considering their advancement unlikely.
6:53.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

6:53.arabic: ومرة ينظرون إلى المؤمنين؛ وهم فقراء شعث غبر فيزدرون بهم ويستحقرونهم، فيقولون "أهؤلاء من الله عليهم من بيننا" ويقولون "لو كان خيراً ما سبقونا إليه" وترتيب القياس الذي نظمه في قلوبهم أنهم يقولون: قد أحسن الله إلينا بنعيم الدنيا، وكل محسن فهو محب، وكل محب فإنه يحسن أيضاً في المستقبل كما قال الشاعر: |لقد أحسن الله  | |كذلك يحسن فيما| |فيما مضى       | |بقـي          |
6:53.english: And sometimes they look at the believers; and they are poor, disheveled, and dusty, so they disdain them and belittle them, saying "Are these the ones whom Allah has favored from among us?" and saying "If it were good, they would not have preceded us to it." And the arrangement of the analogy that He has organized in their hearts is that they say: Allah has been good to us with the enjoyment of the worldly life, and every one who is good is a lover, and every lover then he is also good in the future as the poet said: |Indeed Allah has been good| |Thus He is good in what| |in what has passed| |remains|
6:53.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

6:54.arabic: وقد عاتب الله نبيه ﭬ في الإعراض عن عبد والإقبال على عبد، وهما في العبودية سيان ولكن في الحال مختلفان، فقال: " وأما من جاءك يسعى وهو يخشى فأنت عنده تلهى "، وقال في الآخر: " أما من استغنى فأنت له تصدى " وةكذلك أمره بالقعود مع طائفة، فقال عز وجل: " وإذا جاءك الذين يؤمنون بآياتنا فقل سلام عليكم " وأمره بالإعراض عن غيرهم، فقال: " وإذا رأيت الذين يخوضون في آياتنا فأعرض عنهم " حتى قال: " فلا تقعد بعد الذكرى مع القوم الظالمين " وقال تعالى: " واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي ".
6:54.english: And Allah has reproached His Prophet (peace be upon him) regarding turning away from one servant and turning toward another servant, and they are equal in servitude but different in state. He said: "And as for he who comes to you striving while he fears, you are to him distracted." And He said regarding the other: "As for he who considers himself self-sufficient, you give him attention." And likewise, He commanded him to sit with a group, so the Mighty and Majestic said: "And when those who believe in Our signs come to you, then say: Peace be upon you." And He commanded him to turn away from others, saying: "And when you see those who engage in vain discourse about Our signs, then turn away from them" until He said: "So do not sit after the remembrance with the wrongdoing people." And Allah said: "And restrain your soul (Nafs) with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening."
6:54.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

6:59.arabic: ولا يعدو القرآن هذه الأقسام الثلاثة وهي: الإرشاد إلى معرفة ذات الله وتقديسه، أو معرفة صفاته وأسمائه، أو معرفة أفعاله وسنته مع عباده، ولما اشتملت سورة الإخلاص على أحد هذه الأقسام الثلاثة وهو التقديس وازنها رسول الله ﭬ بثلث القرآن فقال: "من قرأ سورة الإخلاص فقد قرأ ثلث القرآن"[51] لأن منتهى التقديس أن يكون واحداً في ثلاثة أمور، لا يكون حاصلاً منه من هو نظيره وشبهه، ودل عليه قوله " لم يلد " ولا يكون حاصلاً ممن هو نظيره وشبهه، ودل عليه قوله " ولم يولد " ولا يكون في درجته وإن لم يكن أصلاً له ولا فرعا
6:59.english: And the Quran does not exceed these three divisions, which are: guidance to knowledge of the Essence (Dhat) of Allah and His sanctification, or knowledge of His attributes and names, or knowledge of His actions and His way (Sunnah) with His servants. And since Surah Al-Ikhlas contains one of these three divisions, which is sanctification, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ equated it with a third of the Quran, saying: "Whoever recites Surah Al-Ikhlas has recited a third of the Quran" because the ultimate sanctification is to be one in three matters: it is not obtained from one who is His equal and likeness, indicated by His saying "He did not beget"; nor is it obtained from one who is His equal and likeness, indicated by His saying "nor was He begotten"; nor is there in His rank, even if not being His origin or branch, one who is like Him, indicated by His saying: "nor is there to Him any equivalent." And all of that is gathered in His saying, the Exalted: "Say, He is Allah, the One." And its entirety is the detailed explanation of the saying "There is no god but Allah." These are the secrets of the Quran, and examples of these secrets in the Quran are endless, "nor moist nor dry except in a clear book." And therefore, Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Illuminate the Quran and seek its wonders, for in it is the knowledge of the first and the last. And it is as he said, and none knows it except one who has prolonged in its individual words his thought and purified for it his understanding until every word of it testifies to him that it is the speech of a Mighty (Jabbar), Overpowering (Qahir), Sovereign (Malik), Powerful (Qadir), and that it is beyond the limit of human capability.
6:59.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

6:59.arabic: وقال سهل بن عبد الله التستري رحمه الله: خرج العلماء والعباد والزهاد من الدنيا وقلوبهم مقفلة ولم تفتح إلا قلوب الصديقين والشهداء ثم تلا قوله تعالى: (وعنده مفاتح الغيب لا يعلمها إلا هو... الآية( (الأنعام: 59). ولولا أن إدراك قلب من له قلب بالنور الباطن حاكم على علم الظاهر لما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم: (( استفت قلبك وإن أفتوك وأفتوك وأفتوك))[178].
6:59.english: And Sahl bin Abdullah al-Tustari, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The scholars, worshippers, and ascetics left the world with their hearts locked, and none were opened except the hearts of the truthful ones (al-Siddiqin) and the martyrs (al-Shuhada). Then he recited the saying of the Exalted: 'And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him... the verse' (Al-An'am: 59). And were it not that the perception of the heart (Qalb) of one who has a heart with the inner light (al-Nur al-Batin) is sovereign over the knowledge of the apparent (al-Zahir), He would not have said, peace and blessings be upon him: 'Consult your heart even if they give you legal opinions and give you legal opinions and give you legal opinions.'
6:59.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

6:59.arabic: وكذلك إذا سمع وصف الجنة والنار وسائر ما في القرآن فلا يمكن استقصاء ما يفهم منه لأن ذلك لا نهاية له وإنما لكل عبد بقدر رزقه فلا رطب ولا يابس إلا في كتاب مبين ﴿ قل لو كان البحر مدادا لكلمات ربي لنفد البحر قبل أن تنفد كلمات ربي ولو جئنا بمثله مددا ﴾ {} ولذلك قال علي رضي الله عنه: لو شئت لأوقرت سبعين بعيرا من تفسير فاتحة الكتاب.
6:59.english: Likewise, if he hears the description of Paradise and Hell and all that is in the Quran, it is not possible to exhaust what is understood from it because that has no end, and indeed for every servant (Abd) according to the measure of his provision (Rizq), so no moist (Rutb) nor dry (Yabis) except in a clear book (Kitab Mubin). 'Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord were exhausted, even if We brought the like of it as a supplement.' And therefore, Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'If I wished, I could load seventy camels with the interpretation of the Opening of the Book (Fatiha).'
6:59.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

6:60.arabic: اللهم إني أسألك أن تبعثنا في هذا اليوم إلى كل خير ونعوذ بك أن نجترح فيه سوءا أو نجره إلى مسلم فإنك قلت ﴿ وهو الذي يتوفاكم بالليل ويعلم ما جرحتم بالنهار ثم يبعثكم فيه ليقضي أجل مسمى ﴾ {}[234] اللهم فالق الإصباح وجاعل الليل سكنا والشمس والقمر حسبانا أسألك خير هذا اليوم وخير ما فيه وأعوذ بك من شره وشر ما فيه[235]
6:60.english: O Allah, I ask You to resurrect us on this day to every good, and we seek refuge in You from committing evil in it or bringing it upon a Muslim, for You have said: 'And He is the One who takes your souls (Nafs) at night and knows what you have earned (Jaraha) during the day, then He resurrects you in it so that a specified term (Ajal) may be fulfilled.' {}[234] O Allah, Splitter of the dawn and Maker of the night as a rest and the sun and moon as calculation, I ask You for the good of this day and the good in it, and I seek refuge in You from its evil and the evil in it.[235]
6:60.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

6:65.arabic: وسئل ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه عن تفسير هذه الآية فقال إن هذا ليس زمانها إنها اليوم مقبولة ولكن قد اوشك أن يأتي زمانها تأمرون بالمعروف فيصنع بكم كذا وكذا وتقولون فلا يقبل منكم فحينئذ عليكم انفسكم لا يضركم من ضل إذا اهتديتم
6:65.english: And Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) was asked about the interpretation of this verse. He said: 'This is not its time; today it is accepted, but its time is almost upon you. You will command the good (Ma'ruf) and such and such will be done to you, and you will speak but it will not be accepted from you. Then at that time, upon yourselves (Anfusikum) - it will not harm you if someone goes astray when you have been guided.'
6:65.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

6:68.arabic: وقد عاتب الله نبيه ﭬ في الإعراض عن عبد والإقبال على عبد، وهما في العبودية سيان ولكن في الحال مختلفان، فقال: " وأما من جاءك يسعى وهو يخشى فأنت عنده تلهى "، وقال في الآخر: " أما من استغنى فأنت له تصدى " وةكذلك أمره بالقعود مع طائفة، فقال عز وجل: " وإذا جاءك الذين يؤمنون بآياتنا فقل سلام عليكم " وأمره بالإعراض عن غيرهم، فقال: " وإذا رأيت الذين يخوضون في آياتنا فأعرض عنهم " حتى قال: " فلا تقعد بعد الذكرى مع القوم الظالمين " وقال تعالى: " واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي ".
6:68.english: And Allah has reproached His Prophet (peace be upon him) regarding turning away from one servant and turning toward another servant, while they are equal in servitude (ʿubūdiyyah) but differ in state (ḥāl). He said: "And as for he who comes to you striving while he fears, you are to him distracted." And He said regarding the other: "As for he who considers himself self-sufficient, you give him attention." And likewise, He commanded him to sit with a group, so the Mighty and Majestic said: "And when those who believe in Our signs come to you, say: Peace be upon you." And He commanded him to turn away from others, saying: "And when you see those who engage in vain discourse about Our signs, then turn away from them" until He said: "So do not sit after the Remembrance (Dhikr) with the wrongdoing people." And He said, Exalted is He: "And restrain yourself with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening."
6:68.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

6:68.arabic: ومنها كلام القصاص والوعاظ الذين يمزجون بكلامهم البدعة فالقاص إن كان يكذب في أخباره فهو فاسق والإنكار عليه واجب وكذا الواعظ المبتدع يجب منعه ولا يجوز حضور مجلسه إلا على قصد إظهار الرد عليه إما للكافة إن قدر عليه أو لبعض الحاضرين حواليه فإن لم يقدر فلا يجوز سماع البدع قال الله تعالى لنبيه فأعرض عنهم حتى يخوضوا في حديث غيره ومهما كان كلامه مائلا إلى الإرجاء وتجرئة الناس على المعاصي وكان الناس يزدادون بكلامه جراءة وبعفو الله وبرحمته وثوقا يزيد بسببه رجاؤهم على خوفهم فهو منكر ويجب منعه عنه لأن فساد ذ
6:68.english: And among them is the speech of storytellers and preachers who mix innovation (Bid'ah) into their speech. If the storyteller lies in his reports, he is corrupt (Fasiq) and it is obligatory to disapprove of him. Likewise, the innovating preacher must be prevented, and it is not permissible to attend his gathering except with the intention of showing refutation to him, either to all if capable, or to some of those present around him. If incapable, it is not permissible to listen to innovations. Allah the Exalted said to His Prophet: 'And when you see those who engage in [offensive] discourse concerning Our verses, then turn away from them until they enter into another conversation. And if Satan should cause you to forget, then do not remain after the Remembrance (Dhikr) with the wrongdoing people.' And whenever his speech inclines toward postponement (Irja') and emboldening people toward sins, and people increase in boldness through his speech and in confidence in Allah's pardon and mercy, causing their hope (Raja') to increase over their fear (Khawf), this is reprehensible (Munkar) and he must be prevented from it because its corruption is great. Rather, if their fear outweighs their hope, that is more fitting and closer to the nature of creation, for they are in greater need of fear. Indeed, justice is balancing fear and hope, as Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'If a caller called on the Day of Resurrection for all people to enter the Fire except one man, I would hope to be that man; and if a caller called for all people to enter Paradise except one man, I would fear to be that man.' And whenever the preacher is a youth adorned for women in his clothes and appearance, with much poetry, gestures, and movements, and women have attended his gathering, this is reprehensible and must be prevented, for corruption in it is more than benefit, and this is evident from him through circumstantial evidence of his states. Rather, preaching should not be entrusted except to one whose outward appearance is piety (Wara') and his demeanor is tranquility (Sakinah) and dignity (Waqar), and his attire is that of the righteous; otherwise, people only increase in persistence in misguidance. And a barrier must be placed between men and women to prevent looking, for that too is a source of corruption, and customs testify to these reprehensible acts. And women must be prevented from attending mosques for prayers and gatherings of Remembrance (Dhikr).
6:68.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

6:70.arabic: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: الضلالة لها حلاوة في قلوب أهلها. قال الله تعالى: (وذر الذين اتخذوا دينهم لعبا ولهوا وغرتهم الحياة الدنيا وذكر به أن تبسل نفس بما كسبت ليس لها من دون الله ولي ولا شفيع وإن تعدل كل عدل لا يؤخذ منها أولئك الذين أبسلوا بما كسبوا لهم شراب من حميم وعذاب أليم بما كانوا يكفرون) (الأنعام: 70) وقال تعالى: (أفمن زين له سوء عمله فرآه حسنا) (فاطر: 8) فكل ما أحدث بعد الصحابة رضي الله عنهم مما جاوز قدر الضرورة والحاجة فهو من اللعب واللهو.
6:70.english: And Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: Misguidance has sweetness in the hearts (Qulub) of its people. Allah the Exalted said: 'And leave those who have taken their religion as play and amusement and whom the worldly life has deluded. And remind with it (the Quran) lest a soul (Nafs) be seized for what it has earned - it has no protector besides Allah, nor any intercessor. And if it should offer every compensation, it would not be taken from it. Those are the ones who are seized for what they have earned. For them will be a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment because they used to disbelieve.' (Al-An'am: 70) And He the Exalted said: 'Then is one to whom the evil of his deed has been made attractive so he sees it as good?' (Fatir: 8) So everything that was innovated after the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) that exceeds the measure of necessity and need is from play and amusement.
6:70.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

6:71.arabic: والهداية الثالثة وراء الثانية وهو النور الذى يشرق في عالم النبوة والولاية بعد كمال المجاهدة فيهتدى بها إلا ما لا يهتدى إليه بالعقل الذى يحصل به التكليف وإمكان تعلم العلوم وهو الهوى المطلق وما عداه حجاب له ومقدمات وهو الذى شرفه الله تعالى بتخصيص الإضافة إليه وإن كان الكل من جهته تعالى فقال تعالى: ﴿ قل إن هدى الله هو الهدى ﴾ {} وهو المسمى حياة في قوله تعالى: ﴿ أو من كان ميتا فأحييناه وجعلنا له نورا يمشى به في الناس ﴾ {} والمعنى بقوله تعالى: ﴿ أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام فهو على نور من ربه ﴾ {}
6:71.english: And the third guidance (Hidayah) is beyond the second, and it is the light (Nur) that shines in the realm of prophethood (Nubuwwah) and sainthood (Wilayah) after the perfection of striving (Mujahadah), so one is guided by it except what cannot be guided to by the intellect (Aql) through which obligation (Taklif) and the possibility of learning sciences are attained, and it is the absolute desire (Hawa) and what is besides it is a veil (Hijab) for it and its preliminaries, and it is that which Allah the Exalted honored by specifying the attribution to Him, even though all is from His side, the Exalted, so He said, the Exalted: 'Say: Indeed, the guidance (Hidayah) of Allah is the guidance (Hidayah).' And it is called life (Hayat) in His saying, the Exalted: 'Or one who was dead (Mayyit) and We gave him life (Ahyaynah) and made for him a light (Nur) by which he walks among the people.' And the meaning in His saying, the Exalted: 'Is one whose chest Allah has expanded for Islam (Islam) then he is upon a light (Nur) from his Lord?'
6:71.topic: Al-Ghazali on the outer and inner dimensions of worship, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

6:75.arabic: فانظر إلى الملكوت لترى عجائب العز والجبروت ولا تظنن أن معنى النظر إلى الملكوت بأن تمد البصر إليه فترى زرقة السماء وضوء الكواكب وتفرقها فإن البهائم تشاركك فى هذا النظر فإن كان هذا هو المراد فلم مدح الله تعالى إبراهيم بقوله وكذلك نرى إبراهيم ملكوت السموات والأرض لا بل كل ما يدرك بحاسة البصر فالقرآن يعبر عنه بالملك والشهادة وما غاب عن الأبصار فيعبر عنه بالغيب والملكوت والله تعالى عالم الغيب والشهادة وجبار الملك والملكوت ولا يحيط أحد بشىء من علمه إلا بما شاء وهو عالم الغيب فلا يظهر على غيبه أحدا إلا
6:75.english: So look to the Dominion (al-Malakūt) to see the wonders of Might (al-ʿIzz) and Power (al-Jabarūt). And do not think that the meaning of looking to the Dominion (al-Malakūt) is by extending your sight to it so that you see the blueness of the sky, the light of the stars, and their dispersion, for the beasts share with you in this looking. If this were the intended meaning, then why did Allah the Exalted praise Abraham with His saying: 'And thus We showed Abraham the Dominion (Malakūt) of the heavens and the earth'? No, rather everything that is perceived by the sense of sight, the Quran expresses it with Kingdom (al-Mulk) and the Witnessed (al-Shahādah), and what is hidden from the sights is expressed with the Unseen (al-Ghayb) and the Dominion (al-Malakūt). And Allah the Exalted is Knower of the Unseen (al-Ghayb) and the Witnessed (al-Shahādah), and Sovereign of the Kingdom (al-Mulk) and the Dominion (al-Malakūt). And no one encompasses anything of His knowledge except by what He wills, and He is Knower of the Unseen (al-Ghayb), so He does not reveal His Unseen (Ghayb) to anyone except a messenger He has approved. So reflect, O intelligent one, upon the Dominion (al-Malakūt), perhaps the doors of the sky will open for you, and you will roam with your Heart (Qalb) in its regions until your Heart (Qalb) stands before the Throne of the Most Merciful. At that point, perhaps it may be hoped for you to reach the rank of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, where he said: 'My Heart (Qalb) saw my Lord.' And this is because reaching the utmost cannot be except after passing beyond the nearest, and the nearest thing to you is your Soul (Nafs), then the earth which is your abode, then the air enveloping you, then the plants and animals and what is on the face of the earth, then the wonders of the atmosphere, which is what is between the sky and the earth, then the seven heavens with their stars, then the Footstool (al-Kursī), then the Throne (al-ʿArsh), then the angels who are the bearers of the Throne (al-ʿArsh) and the keepers of the heavens, then from there you pass beyond to looking at the Lord of the Throne (al-ʿArsh), the Footstool (al-Kursī), the heavens, the earth, and what is between them.
6:75.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Contemplation'

6:76.arabic: وتلك الحجب أيضا مترتبة وتلك الأنوار متفاوتة في الرتب تفاوت الشمس والقمر والكواكب ويبدو في الأول أصغرها ثم ما يليه وعليه أول بعض الصوفية درجات ما كان يظهر لإبراهيم الخليل ﭬ في ترقيه وقال: ﴿ فلما جن عليه الليل ﴾ {} أي أظلم عليه الأمر ﴿ رأى كوكبا ﴾ {} أي وصل إلى حجاب من حجب النور فعبر عنه بالكوكب وما أريد به هذه الأجسام المضيئة فإن آحاد العوام لا يخفى عليهم أن الربوبية لا تليق بالأجسام بل يدركون ذلك بأوائل نظرهم فما لا يضلل العوام لا يضلل الخليل عليه السلام والحجب المسماة أنوارا ما أريد بها الضوء ا
6:76.english: And those veils are also arranged in order, and those lights are varied in rank like the variation between the sun, the moon, and the stars. In the beginning, the smallest of them appears, then what follows it. Upon this, some Sufis began the degrees of what was appearing to Abraham the Friend (Al-Khalil) ﭬ in his ascension, and He said: 'When the night covered him' {} meaning the matter became dark upon him 'he saw a star' {} meaning he reached a veil from the veils of light, so he expressed it with 'the star', and what is intended by it is not these luminous bodies, for the common people are not unaware that divinity (Ar-Rububiyyah) is not suitable for bodies; rather, they perceive that with the beginnings of their consideration. So what does not mislead the common people does not mislead the Friend (Al-Khalil) upon him peace. And the veils called lights are not intended by them the light perceived by sight; rather, what is intended by them is what is intended by His saying, the Exalted: 'Allah is the Light (Nur) of the heavens and the earth. The example of His light (Nur) is like a niche within which is a lamp' {} the verse. And let us pass over these meanings, for they are outside the knowledge of practice (Ilm Al-Mu'amalah), and none reaches their realities except the unveiling (Al-Kashf) that follows pure thought (Al-Fikr As-Safi), and few are those for whom its door opens. What is made easy for the masses of creation is thought (Al-Fikr) in what benefits in the knowledge of practice (Ilm Al-Mu'amalah), and that also is among what abounds in benefit and magnifies its usefulness.
6:76.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

6:76.arabic: وإليه الإشارة بقول إبراهيم عليه السلام إذ قال الله تعالى إخباراً عنه "فلما جن الليل رأى كوكباً قال هذا ربي" وليس المعنى به هذه الأجسام المضيئة فإنه كان يراها في الصغر ويعلم أنها ليست آلهة وهي كثيرة وليست واحداً، والجهال يعلمون أن الكوكب ليس بإله فمثل إبراهيم عليه السلام لا يغره الكوكب الذي لا يغر السوادية. ولكن المراد به أنه نور من الأنوار التي هي من حجب الله عز وجل وهي على طريق السالكين، ولا يتصور الوصول إلى الله تعالى إلا بالوصول إلى هذه الحجب، وهي حجب من نور بعضها أكبر من بعض وأصغر النيرات ال
6:76.english: And to this is alluded by the saying of Abraham (peace be upon him) when Allah the Exalted said, reporting about him: "When the night covered him, he saw a star. He said, 'This is my Lord.'" And the meaning is not these luminous bodies, for he used to see them in his youth and knew that they are not gods, and they are many and not one, and the ignorant know that the star is not a god, so one like Abraham (peace be upon him) is not deceived by a star that does not deceive the common people. But what is intended by it is that it is a light from the lights that are from the veils of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and they are on the path of the travelers (Salikin), and it is inconceivable to reach Allah the Exalted except by reaching these veils, and they are veils of light, some greater than others, and the smallest of the luminous ones is the star, so its term is borrowed for it, and the greatest of them is the sun, and between them is the rank of the moon. So Abraham (peace be upon him) did not cease when he saw the dominion (Malakut) of the heavens, as Allah the Exalted said: "And thus did We show Abraham the dominion (Malakut) of the heavens and the earth," and he reaches light after light, and it is imagined to him at first when he encounters it that he has reached, then it is unveiled to him that beyond it is a matter, so he ascends to it and says: I have reached, then it is unveiled to him what is beyond it until he reached the nearest veil beyond which there is no reaching, so he said "This is greater." Then when it became apparent to him that it, with its greatness, is not free from inclination in the depths of deficiency and decline from the peak of perfection, he said "I do not love those that set - until he said - Indeed, I have turned my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth." And the traveler (Salik) of this path may be deceived in stopping at some of these veils, and he may be deceived by the first veil, and the first veil between Allah and the servant is his own soul (Nafs), for it is also a divine matter and it is a light from the lights of Allah the Exalted; I mean the secret (Sirr) of the heart (Qalb) in which the reality (Haqiqah) of the Truth (Al-Haqq) all is manifested, so much so that it expands to encompass the whole world and surrounds it, and the form of the whole is manifested in it, and at that time its light shines a great shining, for the whole existence appears in it as it is, and in the first matter it is veiled by a niche that is like a cover for it. So when its light is manifested and the beauty (Jamal) of the heart (Qalb) is unveiled after the light of Allah shines upon it, perhaps the possessor of the heart (Qalb) turns to the heart (Qalb) and sees from its surpassing beauty (Jamal) what bewilders him, and perhaps his tongue precedes in this bewilderment, so he says: I am the Truth (Al-Haqq). Then if what is beyond that is not made clear to him, he is deceived by it and stops at it and perishes, and he had been deceived by a small star from the lights of the divine presence (Al-Hadrah Al-Ilahiyyah) and had not yet reached the moon, let alone the sun, so he is deceived, and this is the place of confusion, for the manifested (Al-Mutajalli) is confused with that in which it is manifested (Al-Mutajalla Fihi), as the color of what appears in the mirror is confused so it is thought to be the color of the mirror, and as what is in the glass is confused with the glass, as it is said: |The glass became thin| |so they resembled each other| |And the wine became thin| |so they became similar|.
6:76.topic: Al-Ghazali on the outer and inner dimensions of worship, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

6:76.arabic: وفرقة أخرى جاوزوا هؤلاء ولم يلتفتوا إلى ما يفيض عليهم من الأنوار في الطريق ولا إلا ما تيسر لهم من العطايا الجزيلة ولم يعرجوا على الفرح بها والالتفات إليها جادين في السير حتى قاربوا فوصلوا إلى حد القربة إلى الله تعالى، فظنوا أنهم قد وصلوا إلى الله فوقفوا وغلطوا فإن لله تعالى سبعين حجاباً من نور لا يصل السالك إلى حجاب من تلك الحجب في الطريق إلا ويظن أنه قد وصل. وإليه الإشارة بقول إبراهيم عليه السلام إذ قال الله تعالى إخباراً عنه "فلما جن الليل رأى كوكباً قال هذا ربي" وليس المعنى به هذه الأجسام الم
6:76.english: And another group surpassed these and did not turn to what flows upon them of lights (Anwar) on the path, nor except what was made easy for them of abundant gifts, and they did not linger over rejoicing in them and turning to them, earnest in walking until they approached and reached the limit of nearness (Qurbah) to Allah the Exalted, so they thought that they had reached Allah, so they stopped and erred, for Allah the Exalted has seventy veils (Hujub) of light; the traveler (Salik) does not reach a veil from those veils on the path except that he thinks he has reached. And to this is the allusion in the saying of Abraham, peace be upon him, when Allah the Exalted reported about him: "When the night covered him, he saw a star; he said, 'This is my Lord (Rabb).'" And the meaning is not these luminous bodies, for he used to see them in childhood and know that they are not gods, and they are many and not one, and the ignorant know that the star is not a god, so the like of Abraham, peace be upon him, is not deceived by the star that does not deceive the common people. But what is intended is that it is a light from the lights (Anwar) that are from the veils (Hujub) of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and they are on the path of the travelers (Salikin), and reaching Allah the Exalted is not conceivable except by reaching these veils (Hujub), and they are veils (Hujub) of light, some greater than others, and the smallest of the luminous ones is the star, so its term was borrowed for it, and the greatest is the sun, and between them is the rank of the moon. So Abraham, peace be upon him, did not cease when he saw the dominion (Mulkut) of the heavens, as Allah the Exalted said: "And thus We showed Abraham the dominion (Mulkut) of the heavens and the earth," and he reaches light after light, and it is imagined to him at first what he encounters that he has reached, then it is unveiled to him that beyond it is a matter, so he ascends to it and says: I have reached, then it is unveiled to him what is beyond it until he reached the nearest veil (Hijab) after which there is no reaching, so he said "This is greater," then when it became apparent to him that it, with its greatness, is not free from inclination (Hawa) in the lowliness of deficiency and decline from the peak of perfection (Kamal), "he said, 'I do not love those that set' - until he said - 'Indeed, I have turned my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth.'" And the traveler (Salik) of this path may be deceived in stopping at
6:76.topic: Al-Ghazali on the outer and inner dimensions of worship, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

6:79.arabic: وذلك كإفلاس من يصبح بكرة ويتوجه إلى القبلة ويقول: (وجهت وجهي للذي فطر السموات والأرض حنيفا( (الأنعام: 79). وهو أول كذب يفاتح الله به كل يوم إن لم يكن وجه قلبه متوجها إلى الله تعالى على الخصوص فإنه إن أراد بالوجه وجه الظاهر فما وجهه إلا إلى الكعبة وما صرفه إلا عن سائر الجهات والكعبة ليست جهة للذي فطر السموات والأرض حتى يكون المتوجه إليها متوجها إليه تعالى عن أن تحده الجهات والأقطار وإن أراد به وجه القلب وهو المطلوب المتعبد به فكيف يصدق في قوله وقلبه متردد في أوطاره وحاجاته الدنيوية ومتصرف في طلب
6:79.english: And that is like the bankruptcy (إفلاس) of one who rises in the morning and turns toward the Qibla and says: 'I have turned my face toward He Who created the heavens and the earth, as a true monotheist (حنيفا)' (Al-An'am: 79). And it is the first lie with which he addresses Allah each day if the face (وجه) of his Heart (Qalb) is not turned toward Allah, the Exalted, in particular. For if he intended by 'face' the apparent face, then his face is only toward the Ka'bah, and he has only diverted it from other directions. And the Ka'bah is not a direction for He Who created the heavens and the earth, such that one who turns toward it is turning toward Him, the Exalted, above being limited by directions and regions. And if he intended by it the face of the Heart (Qalb), which is the required object of worship, then how can he be truthful in his statement while his Heart (Qalb) is wavering in its familiar places and its worldly needs, and is engaged in seeking means to gather wealth, status, and multiplying causes, and is turned wholly toward them? So when has he turned his face toward He Who created the heavens and the earth? And this statement is a report about the reality of Monotheism (Tawhid). So the monotheist (الموحد) is the one who sees nothing but the One and does not turn his face except toward Him. And it is compliance with His statement, the Exalted: 'Say: Allah, then leave them in their discourse, playing' (Al-An'am: 91). And what is intended by it is not the statement with the tongue, for the tongue is only an interpreter that tells the truth sometimes and lies at other times. Rather, the place of Allah's, the Exalted, gaze, which is interpreted from it, is the Heart (Qalb), and it is the mine and source of Monotheism (Tawhid).
6:79.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

6:79.arabic: ولكن المراد به أنه نور من الأنوار التي هي من حجب الله عز وجل وهي على طريق السالكين، ولا يتصور الوصول إلى الله تعالى إلا بالوصول إلى هذه الحجب، وهي حجب من نور بعضها أكبر من بعض وأصغر النيرات الكوكب فاستعير له لفظه وأعظمها الشمس وبينهما رتبة القمر، فلم يزل إبراهيم عليه السلام لما رأى ملكوت السموات حيث قال تعالى "وكذلك نرى إبراهيم ملكوت السموات والأرض" ويصل إلى نور بعد نور ويتخيل إليه في أول ما كان يلقاه أنه قد وصل، ثم كان يكشف له أن وراءه أمراً فيترقى إليه ويقول: قد وصلت فيكشف له ما وراءه حتى وصل
6:79.english: But what is intended by it is that it is a light from the lights that are from the veils of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and they are upon the path of the travelers (Salikin), and reaching Allah, the Exalted, cannot be conceived except by reaching these veils, and they are veils of light, some greater than others, and the smallest of the luminous ones is the star, so its term was borrowed for it, and the greatest of them is the sun, and between them is the rank of the moon. So Abraham, peace be upon him, did not cease when he saw the dominion (Mulkut) of the heavens, as Allah, the Exalted, said: "And thus did We show Abraham the dominion (Mulkut) of the heavens and the earth," and he reaches light after light, and it appears to him at first what he encounters that he has reached, then it is unveiled to him that beyond it is a matter, so he ascends to it and says: I have reached, then it is unveiled to him what is beyond it until he reached the nearest veil beyond which there is no reaching, so he said: "This is greater." Then when it became apparent to him that despite its greatness, it is not free from inclination in the depths of deficiency and decline from the peak of perfection, "he said: I do not love those that set - until he said - Indeed, I have turned my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth." And the traveler (Salik) of this path may be deceived in stopping at some of these veils, and he may be deceived by the first veil, and the first veil between Allah and the servant is his own self (Nafs), for it is also a divine matter and a light from the lights of Allah, the Exalted; I mean the secret (Sirr) of the heart (Qalb) in which the reality (Haqiqah) of the Truth (Haqq) all is manifested, so much so that it expands to encompass the whole world and surrounds it, and the form (Surah) of the whole is manifested in it. At that time, its light shines a great shining, for the whole existence appears in it as it is, and in the first matter, it is veiled by a niche that is like a cover for it. So when its light is manifested and the beauty (Jamal) of the heart (Qalb) is unveiled after the light of Allah shines upon it, perhaps the possessor of the heart (Qalb) turns to the heart (Qalb) and sees from its surpassing beauty (Jamal) what bewilders him, and perhaps his tongue precedes in this bewilderment, so he says: I am the Truth (Haqq). Then if what is beyond that is not clarified to him, he is deceived by it and stops at it and perishes, and he had been deceived by a small star from the lights of the divine presence (Hadrah Ilahiyyah) and had not yet reached the moon, let alone the sun, so he is deceived, and this is the place of confusion, for the manifested (Mutajalli) is confused with that in which it is manifested (Mutajalla fihi), as the color of what appears in the mirror is confused so it is thought to be the color of the mirror, and as what is in the glass is confused with the glass, as it is said: |The glass became thin | |so they resembled each other | |And the wine became thin | |so they became similar | | | |The matter | |So it is as if they are wine | |And as if it has
6:79.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

6:79.arabic: والكمال الثاني أن يراعي معنى الصدق في ألفاظه التى يناجي بها ربه كقوله (وجهت وجهي للذي فطر السموات والأرض) فإن قلبه إن كان منصرفا عن الله تعالى مشغولا بأماني الدنيا وشهواته فهو كذب وكقوله (إياك نعبد) وقوله (أنا عبد الله) فإنه إذا لم يتصف بحقيقة العبودية وكان له مطلب سوى الله لم يكن كلامه صدقا ولو طولب يوم القيامة بالصدق في قوله أنا عبد الله لعجز تحقيقه فإنه إن كان عبدا لنفسه أو عبدا لدنيا أو عبدا لشهواته لم يكن صادقا في قوله.
6:79.english: And the second perfection is that one should observe the meaning of truthfulness in the words with which he converses with his Lord, such as his saying: 'I have turned my face (Wajhi) toward He who created (Fatar) the heavens and the earth' (Quran 6:79). For if his Heart (Qalb) is turned away from Allah the Exalted, preoccupied with worldly hopes and desires, then it is falsehood. And like his saying: 'You alone we worship' and his saying: 'I am a slave (Abd) of Allah.' For if he is not characterized by the reality of slavery (Ubudiyyah) and has a desire other than Allah, his speech is not truthful. And if he were demanded on the Day of Resurrection for truthfulness in his saying 'I am a slave of Allah,' he would be incapable of fulfilling it. For if he is a slave to his own self (Nafs), or a slave to the world, or a slave to his desires, he is not truthful in his statement.
6:79.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

6:79.arabic: ويصلي الإمام بهم ركعتين يكبر في الأولى سوى تكبيرة الإحرام والركوع سبع تكبيرات يقول بين كل تكبيرتين سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر ويقول وجهت وجهي للذي فطر السموات والأرض عقيب تكبيرة الافتتاح ويؤخر الاستعاذة إلى ما وراء الثامنة ويقرأ سورة ق في الأولى بعد الفاتحة واقتربت في الثانية والتكبيرات الزائدة في الثانية خمس سوى تكبيرتي القيام والركوع وبين كل تكبيرتين ما ذكرناه ثم يخطب خطبتين بينهما جلسة ومن فاتته صلاة العيد قضاها.
6:79.english: And the Imam (Imam) prays with them two units (rak'ahs), saying the magnification (takbir) in the first unit besides the magnification of commencement (takbirat al-ihram) and the bowing (ruku') seven magnifications, saying between every two magnifications: 'Glory be to Allah (Subhan Allah) and praise be to Allah (Alhamdulillah) and there is no god but Allah (La ilaha illa Allah) and Allah is the greatest (Allahu Akbar).' And he says: 'I have turned my face (wajjahtu wajhiya) to the One who created (fatar) the heavens and the earth, sincerely devoted (hanifan), and I am not of the polytheists (mushrikin)' following the magnification of opening (takbirat al-iftitah), and he delays the seeking refuge (isti'adha) until after the eighth, and he recites Surah Qaf in the first unit after the Opening (Al-Fatihah) and 'It has approached' (Iqtarabat) in the second, and the additional magnifications in the second are five besides the two magnifications of standing (qiyam) and bowing (ruku'), and between every two magnifications is what we have mentioned. Then he delivers two sermons (khutbah) with a sitting (jalsah) between them, and whoever misses the Eid prayer makes it up.
6:79.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

6:79.arabic: وأما دعاء الاستفتاح فأول كلماته قولك وجهت وجهي للذي فطر السموات والأرض وليس المراد بالوجه الوجه الظاهر فإنك إنما وجهته إلى جهة القبلة والله سبحانه يتقدس عن أن تحده الجهات حتى تقبل بوجه بدنك عليه وإنما وجه القلب هو الذي تتوجه به إلى فاطر السماوات والأرض فانظر إليه أمتوجه هو إلى أمانيه وهمه في البيت والسوق ومتبع للشهوات أو مقبل على فاطر السموات. وإياك أن تكون أول مفاتحتك للمناجاة بالكذب والاختلاق ولن ينصرف الوجه إلى الله تعالى إلا بانصرافه عما سواه فاجتهد في الحال في صرفه إليه وإن عجزت عنه على الد
6:79.english: And as for the opening supplication, its first words are your saying: 'I have turned my face (Wajh) toward the One Who created the heavens and the earth' (Quran 6:79). And what is intended by 'face' is not the apparent face, for you have only turned it toward the direction of the Qibla, and Allah, glorified be He, is sanctified from being limited by directions such that you would turn your bodily face toward Him. Rather, it is the face of the Heart (Qalb) that you turn toward the Creator (Fāṭir) of the heavens and the earth. So look at it: is it turned toward its hopes and concerns in the house and market, and following desires, or is it turned toward the Creator of the heavens? And beware that your first opening of the intimate discourse (Munājāh) be with falsehood and fabrication. And the face will not turn to Allah, exalted be He, except by turning away from all else besides Him, so strive in the present moment to turn it toward Him, and if you are incapable of that perpetually, then let your saying in the present moment be truthful. And when you say 'as a true monotheist (Ḥanīf), a submitter (Muslim)', it should occur to your mind that the submitter is the one from whose tongue and hand the submitters are safe. If you are not thus, then you are a liar, so strive to resolve upon it in the future and regret what has preceded of states. And when you say 'and I am not of the polytheists (Mushrikīn)', then bring to your mind the hidden polytheism (Shirk), for His saying, exalted be He: 'So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone' (Quran 18:110) was revealed concerning one who intends by his worship the face of Allah and the praise of people. And be cautious, fearful of this polytheism, and feel shame (Khajlah) in your heart if you describe yourself as not being from the polytheists without being free from this polytheism, for the name polytheism applies to the little...
6:79.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

6:83.arabic: وكيف تعتدل القسمة مهما وقع النقص في جهته والكمال في خلقه وصنعته أو كيف تستقيم حجة إبراهيم ﭬ على أبيه إذ كان يعبد الأصنام جهلا وغيا فقال له لم تعبد ما لا يسمع ولا يبصر ولا يغني عنك شيئا ولو انقلب ذلك عليه في معبوده لأضحت حجته داحضة ودلالته ساقطة ولم يصدق قوله تعالى وتلك حجتنا آتيناها إبراهيم على قومه نرفع درجات من نشاء إن ربك حكيم عليم وكما عقل كونه فاعلا بلا جارحة وعالما بلا قلب ودماغ فليعقل كونه بصيرا بلا حدقة وسميعا بلا أذن إذ لا فرق بينهما.
6:83.english: And how would the division be balanced whenever deficiency occurs on His side and perfection in His creation and craftsmanship? Or how would the argument of Abraham (peace be upon him) against his father be sound when he was worshipping idols out of ignorance and misguidance, and he said to him: 'Why do you worship what does not hear nor see, nor benefit you in anything?' And if that were reversed upon him regarding his worshipped one, his argument would become invalid and his proof would fall, and the saying of Allah the Exalted would not be truthful: 'And that is Our argument which We gave to Abraham against his people. We raise in degrees whom We will. Indeed, your Lord is Wise, Knowing.' And just as one comprehends His being an Actor without an organ and a Knower without a heart and brain, let him comprehend His being a Seer without a pupil and a Hearer without an ear, for there is no difference between them.
6:83.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

6:91.arabic: والمعنى الثاني أن ينزله على نفسه في حق الله تعالى فإنه إذا تفكر فمعرفته جهل إذ ما قدروا الله حق قدره وطاعته رياء إذ لا يتقي الله حق تقاته وحبه معلول إذ لا يدع شهوة من شهواته في حبه ومن أراد الله به خيرا بصره بعيوب نفسه فيرى مصداق هذا البيت في نفسه وإن كان على المرتبة بالإضافة إلى الغافلين ولذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لا أحصى ثناء عليك أنت كما أثنيت على نفسك حديث لا أحصي ثناء عليك أنت كما أثنيت على نفسك رواه مسلم وقد تقدم وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إني لاستغفر الله في اليوم والليلة سبعين مرة حديث إن
6:91.english: The second meaning is that he applies it to himself regarding Allah (God) the Exalted, for when he reflects, his knowledge is ignorance since 'they did not measure Allah (God) with His true measure' (Quran 6:91), and his obedience is hypocrisy since he does not fear Allah (God) with His true fear, and his love is caused since he does not abandon a desire from his desires in his love. And whoever Allah (God) wills good for, He shows him the faults of his Soul (Nafs), so he sees the truth of this verse in himself, even if it is at a level relative to the heedless. Therefore, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'I cannot enumerate praise upon You; You are as You have praised Yourself' (hadith: I cannot enumerate praise upon You; You are as You have praised Yourself, narrated by Muslim, and it has preceded). And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, I seek forgiveness from Allah (God) seventy times a day and night' (hadith: Indeed, I seek forgiveness from Allah (God) seventy times a day and night, preceded in the second chapter of the Remembrances (Dhikr)). And his seeking forgiveness was only about states that are degrees later relative to what comes after them, and even if they are closeness relative to what came before them, there is no closeness except that beyond it remains a closeness without end, since the path of Journeying (Suluk) to Allah (God) the Exalted is infinite, and reaching the utmost degrees of closeness is impossible.
6:91.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

6:91.arabic: حتى قال أرباب القلوب من تحركت همته بالتصرف في نهاره لتدبير ما يفطر عليه كتبت عليه خطيئة فإن ذلك من قلة الوثوق بفضل الله عز وجل وقلة اليقين برزقه الموعود وهذه رتبة الأنبياء والصديقين والمقربين ولا يطول النظر في تفصيلها قولا ولكن في تحقيقها عملا فإنه إقبال بكنه الهمة على الله عز وجل وانصراف عن غير الله سبحانه وتلبس بمعنى قوله عز وجل: ﴿ قل الله ثم ذرهم في خوضهم يلعبون ﴾{}. وأما صوم الخصوص وهو صوم الصالحين فهو كف الجوارح عن الآثام وتمامه بستة أمور:
6:91.english: Until the masters of the Hearts (Qulūb) said: 'Whoever's aspiration moves him during his day to arrange what he will break his fast with, a sin is written against him, for that is from lack of trust in the grace of Allah, the Exalted and Majestic, and lack of certainty in His promised provision.' And this is the rank of the Prophets, the Truthful Ones (Ṣiddīqīn), and the Brought-Near Ones (Muqarrabīn). And one should not prolong looking into its details in speech, but in its actualization in practice, for it is turning with the essence of aspiration toward Allah, the Exalted and Majestic, and turning away from other than Allah, the Glorified, and clothing oneself with the meaning of His saying, the Exalted and Majestic: 'Say: Allah, then leave them in their vain discourse playing.' And as for the fast of the special ones, which is the fast of the righteous, it is restraining the limbs from sins, and its perfection is with six matters:
6:91.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Fasting'

6:91.arabic: وإلى هذا التفريد والتجريد الإشارة بقوله تعالى: "قل الله ثم ذرهم في خوضهم"، وبقوله تعالى: "إن الذين قالوا ربنا الله ثم استقاموا" بل هو معنى قولك "لا إله إلا الله" أي معبود ولا محبوب سواه، فكل محبوب فإنه معبود، فإن العبد هو المقيد والمعبود هو المقيد به، وكل محب مقيد بما يحبه. ولذلك قال الله تعالى: "أرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه" وقال ﭬ: "أبغض إله عبد في الأرض الهوى" ولذلك قال عليه السلام: "من قال لا إله إلا الله مخلصاً دخل الجنة"[27] ومعنى الإخلاص أن يخلص قلبه لله فلا يبقى فيه شرك لغير الله، فيكون الله
6:91.english: And to this isolation (Tafreed) and abstraction (Tajreed) is the indication by His saying, the Exalted: "Say: Allah, then leave them in their vain discourse" (Quran 6:91), and by His saying, the Exalted: "Indeed, those who have said, 'Our Lord is Allah,' and then remained steadfast..." (Quran 41:30). Rather, it is the meaning of your saying "There is no god but Allah"—meaning there is no object of worship (Ma'bood) and no beloved (Mahboob) except Him. For every beloved is an object of worship, since the servant (Al-'Abd) is the one bound and the object of worship is what he is bound by, and every lover is bound by what he loves. Therefore, Allah, the Exalted, said: "Have you seen he who has taken as his god his [own] desire?" (Quran 25:43) and He said: "The most hated god of a servant on earth is desire (Hawa)." And therefore, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever says 'There is no god but Allah' sincerely (Mukhlisan) enters Paradise." And the meaning of sincerity (Ikhlas) is that he purifies his heart (Qalb) for Allah so that no association (Shirk) for other than Allah remains in it. Thus, Allah becomes the beloved (Mahboob) of his heart, the object of worship (Ma'bood) of his heart, and the intended (Maqsood) of his heart only. Whoever is in this state, the world is his prison because it prevents him from witnessing his beloved, and his death is liberation from the prison and arrival at the beloved. So what is the state of one who has only one beloved, and his longing for him has been prolonged, and his imprisonment from him has been extended, then he is freed from the prison and enabled to be with the beloved and given eternal security forever?
6:91.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

6:91.arabic: والطهارة في كل رتبة نصف العمل الذي فيها فإن الغاية القصوى في عمل السر أن ينكشف له جلال الله تعالى وعظمته ولن تحل معرفة الله تعالى بالحقيقة في السر ما لم يرتحل ما سوى الله تعالى عنه ولذلك قال الله عز وجل: ﴿ قل الله ثم ذرهم في خوضهم يلعبون ﴾ {} لأنهما لا يجتمعان في قلب ﴿ وما جعل الله لرجل من قلبين في جوفه﴾ {}.
6:91.english: And purification in every rank is half of the work therein, for the ultimate goal in the work of the innermost secret (Sirr) is that the majesty of Allah, the Exalted, and His greatness be unveiled to it, and the knowledge of Allah, the Exalted, in reality will not settle in the innermost secret (Sirr) until what is other than Allah, the Exalted, departs from it. And for that reason, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Say: Allah, then leave them in their vain discourse playing' (Quran 6:91) because the two do not gather in a heart (Qalb) - 'And Allah has not made for any man two hearts within his breast' (Quran 33:4).
6:91.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Purity'

6:91.arabic: وهؤلاء هم الذين يرون كل ما ليس لله حراما امتثالا لقوله تعالى قل الله ثم ذرهم في خوضهم يلعيون وهذه رتبة الموحدين المتجردين عن حظوظ أنفسهم المنفردين لله تعالى بالقصد ولا شك في أن من يتورع عما يوصل إليه أو يستعان عليه بمعصية ليتورع عما يقترن بسبب اكتسابه معصية أو كراهية
6:91.english: And these are those who see everything that is not for Allah as forbidden, in compliance with His saying, the Exalted: 'Say: Allah. Then leave them in their vain discourse playing.' And this is the rank of the monotheists (al-Muwahhidīn) who are stripped of the desires of their souls (Nafs), who are devoted exclusively to Allah, the Exalted, in intention. And there is no doubt that whoever abstains from what leads to it or is aided by it with disobedience, should abstain from what is associated with the cause of its acquisition with disobedience or dislike.
6:91.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

6:93.arabic: ومنها الاستكبار عن الحق وكراهته، والحرص على المماراة فيه حتى إن أبغض شيء إلى المناظر أن يظهر على لسان خصمه الحق ومنهما ظهر تشمر لجحده وإنكاره بأقصى جهده وبذل غاية إمكانه في المخادعة والمكر والحيلة لدفعه حتى تصير المماراة فيه عادة طبيعية فلا يسمع كلاما إلا وينبعث من طبعه داعية الاعتراض عليه حتى يغلب ذلك على قلبه في أدلة القرآن وألفاظ الشرع فيضرب البعض منها بالبعض والمراء في مقابلة الباطل محذور إذ ندب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى ترك المراء بالحق على الباطل قال صلى الله عليه وسلم : (( من ترك ا
