7:12.english: And indeed, Iblis (Satan) was made an example of this, and what was narrated of his states is only to take lesson from it, for he said: 'I am better than him,' and this pride (Kibr) is by lineage because he said: 'I am better than him, You created me from fire and created him from clay,' so that carried him to refuse the prostration (Sujood) which Allah the Exalted commanded him with, and its beginning was pride (Kibr) upon Adam and envy (Hasad) for him, which dragged him to pride (Kibr) upon the command of Allah the Exalted, so that was the cause of his destruction forever, so this is a calamity (Aafah) from the calamities (Aafaat) of pride (Kibr) upon the servants (Ibaad) great, and therefore the Messenger of Allah ﷺ explained pride (Kibr) with these two calamities (Aafaat) when Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas asked him saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, I am a man who loves beauty as you see, is that from pride (Kibr)?' He ﷺ said: 'No, but pride (Kibr) is from rejecting the truth (Haqq) and despising people (Ghams al-Naas).' And in another narration: 'from belittling the truth (Safah al-Haqq).' And his saying 'and despising people (Ghams al-Naas)' meaning looking down upon them and considering them insignificant, and they are servants (Ibaad) of Allah like him or better than him. And this first calamity (Aafah) 'and belittling the truth (Safah al-Haqq)' is rejecting it, and it is the second calamity (Aafah), so whoever sees that he is better than his brother and despises his brother and looks down upon him and looks at him with the eye of belittlement, or rejects the truth (Haqq) while he knows it, has indeed become proud (Takabbar) between him and the creation (Khalq), and whoever is too proud (Anif) to submit (Yakhda') to Allah the Exalted and humble himself (Yatawada') to Allah through His obedience (Taa'ah) and following His messengers, has indeed become proud (Takabbar) between him and Allah the Exalted and His messengers.
7:12.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

7:12.arabic: وهذه أقيسة فاسدة تشبه قياس إبليس حيث قال "أنا خير منه خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين" وإلى هؤلاء الإشارة بقوله تعالى "أولئك الذين اشتروا الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة فلا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينصرون" وعلاج هذا الغرور إما بتصديق الإيمان وإما بالبرهان؛ أما التصديق بمجرد الإيمان فهو أن يصدق الله تعالى في قوله "ما عندكم ينفد وما عند الله باق" وفي قوله عز وجل "وما عند الله خير" وقوله "والآخرة خير وأبقى" وقوله "وما الحياة الدنيا إلا متاع الغرور" وقوله "فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا" وقد أخبر رسول الله ﭬ بذلك طوائف
7:12.english: And these are corrupt analogies resembling the analogy of Iblis (Satan) when he said: "I am better than him (Adam), You created me from fire and created him from clay." And to these people is the reference in His saying, the Exalted: "Those are the ones who have purchased the worldly life for the Hereafter, so the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be aided." And the treatment for this delusion (Ghurur) is either through affirmation of faith (Iman) or through proof (Burhan); as for affirmation through mere faith (Iman), it is to believe Allah, the Exalted, in His saying: "What is with you will be exhausted, and what is with Allah is enduring," and in His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: "And what is with Allah is better," and His saying: "And the Hereafter is better and more enduring," and His saying: "And the worldly life is not but the enjoyment of delusion (Ghurur)," and His saying: "So do not let the worldly life delude you." And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) informed groups of disbelievers of this, so they followed him and believed him and had faith (Amanu) in him and did not demand proof from him[3], and among them were those who said: "I adjure you by Allah, did Allah send you as a messenger?" And he would say: "Yes," so they would believe[4]. And this is the faith (Iman) of the common people, and it removes from delusion (Ghurur), and this is placed in the position of a child believing his father that attending the school is better than attending the playground, even though he does not know the aspect of its being better. And as for knowledge through clarification and proof (Burhan), it is to know the aspect of corruption of this analogy that Satan has organized in his heart (Qalb), for every deluded person has a cause for his delusion (Ghurur), and that cause is evidence, and every evidence is a type of analogy that occurs in the soul (Nafs) and produces tranquility (Sukun) towards it, even if its possessor is not aware of it nor capable of organizing it with the words of the scholars. So the analogy that Satan organized...
7:12.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

7:12.arabic: أما بعد فإن الغضب شعلة نار اقتبست من نار الله الموقدة التي تطلع على الأفئدة، وإنها لمستكنة في طي الفؤاد. استكنان الجمر تحت الرماد، ويستخرجها الكبر الدفين في قلب كل جبار عنيد، كاستخراج الحجر النار من الحديد، وقد انكشف للناظرين بنور اليقين، أن الإنسان ينزع منه عرق إلى الشيطان اللعين، فمن استفزته نار الغضب فقد قويت فيه قرابة الشيطان حيث قال "خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين" فإن شأن الطين السكون والوقار، وشأن النار التلظي والاستعار، والحركة والاضطراب، ومن نتائج الغضب الحقد والحسد، وبهما هلك من هلك وفسد
7:12.english: Afterwards, anger is a flame of fire borrowed from the fire of Allah the kindled which rises upon the hearts (Afa'idah), and indeed it is hidden in the fold of the heart (Fu'ad). The hiding of embers under ashes, and it is extracted by the concealed arrogance in the heart of every obstinate tyrant, like extracting fire from stone with iron, and it has been revealed to the observers with the light of certainty (Yaqin), that the human being has a vein extending to the accursed Satan (Shaytan), so whoever is provoked by the fire of anger has strengthened in him the kinship of Satan when he said "I am better than him, You created me from fire and created him from clay." For the nature of clay is stillness and dignity, and the nature of fire is blazing and flaming, and movement and agitation, and from the results of anger are malice (Haqd) and envy (Hasad), and by them perished whoever perished and corrupted whoever corrupted, and their source is a morsel (Mudghah) if it becomes sound, the entire body becomes sound with it, and if malice and envy and anger are among what drives the servant (Abd) to places of destruction, how much he needs to know its harms and evils! To beware of that and avoid it, and remove it from the heart if it exists and expel it, and treat it if it becomes entrenched in his heart and cure it, for whoever does not know evil falls into it, and whoever knows it, knowledge alone does not suffice him, unless he knows the path by which he repels evil and removes it.
7:12.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

7:15.arabic: وقال سفيان بن عيينة لا يمنعن أحدكم من الدعاء ما يعلم من نفسه فإن الله عز وجل أجاب دعاء شر الخلق إبليس لعنه الله إذ قال: ﴿ رب فانظرني إلى يوم يبعثون قال إنك من المنظرين ﴾ {}.
7:15.english: And Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: Let not what one knows about himself prevent anyone from supplication, for Allah the Exalted answered the supplication of the worst of creation, Iblis (may Allah curse him), when he said: 'My Lord, grant me respite until the Day they are resurrected.' He said: 'Indeed, you are of those granted respite.'
7:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

7:16.arabic: ولأجل اكتناف الشهوات للقلب من جوانبه قال الله تعالى إخبارا عن إبليس لأقعدن لهم صراطك المستقيم ثم لآتينهم من بين أيديهم ومن خلفهم وعن إيمانهم وعن شمائلهم وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الشيطان قعد لابن آدم بطرق فقعد له بطريق الإسلام فقال أتسلم وتترك دينك ودين آبائك فعصاه وأسلم ثم قعد له بطريق الهجرة فقال أتهاجر أتدع أرضك وسمائك فعصاه وهاجر هو قعد له بطريق الجهاد فقال أتجاهد وهو تلف النفس والمال فتقاتل فتقتل فتنكح نساؤك ويقسم مالك فعصاه وجاهد[49]
7:16.english: And because the desires (Shahawat) surround the Heart (Qalb) from its sides, Allah the Exalted said, informing about Iblis: 'I will surely sit for them on Your straight path (Siraat al-Mustaqim), then I will come to them from before them and from behind them and from their right hands and from their left hands.' And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Satan sat for the son of Adam with paths, so he sat for him with the path of Islam and said: Do you become Muslim and leave your religion and the religion of your fathers? So he disobeyed him and became Muslim. Then he sat for him with the path of emigration (Hijrah) and said: Do you emigrate? Do you leave your land and your sky? So he disobeyed him and emigrated. He sat for him with the path of striving (Jihad) and said: Do you strive, and it is destruction of the self (Nafs) and wealth, so you fight and are killed, then your women are married and your wealth is divided? So he disobeyed him and strove.'
7:16.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

7:16.arabic: وقال عز وجل إخبارا عن ابليس اللعين: ﴿ لأقعدن لهم صراطك المستقيم ﴾ {} قيل هو طريق الشكر ولعلو رتبة الشكر طعن اللعين في الخلق فقال: ولا تجد أكثرهم شاكرين وقال تعالى: ﴿ وقليل من عبادي الشكور ﴾ {} وقد قطع الله تعالى بالمزيد مع الشكر ولم يستثن فقال تعالى: ﴿ لئن شكرتم لأزيدنكم ﴾ {}
7:16.english: And the Mighty and Majestic said, reporting about the cursed Iblis: 'I will surely sit in ambush for them on Your straight path' (Quran 7:16). It is said that it is the path of gratitude (Shukr), and due to the high rank of gratitude (Shukr), the cursed one attacked the creation, saying: 'And you will not find most of them grateful' (Quran 7:17). And Allah the Exalted said: 'And few of My servants are grateful' (Quran 34:13). And Allah the Exalted has affirmed increase with gratitude (Shukr) without exception, saying: 'If you are grateful, I will surely increase you' (Quran 14:7).
7:16.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

7:16.arabic: وقيل في تفسير قوله عز وجل: ﴿ لأقعدن لهم صراطك المستقيم ﴾ {} أي طريق مكة يقعد الشيطان عليها ليمنع الناس منها
7:16.english: And it is said in the interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: 'I will surely sit for them on Your straight path' (Quran 7:16), meaning: the way to Mecca; the Satan sits on it to prevent people from it.
7:16.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

7:17.arabic: وقال عز وجل إخبارا عن ابليس اللعين: ﴿ لأقعدن لهم صراطك المستقيم ﴾ {} قيل هو طريق الشكر ولعلو رتبة الشكر طعن اللعين في الخلق فقال: ولا تجد أكثرهم شاكرين وقال تعالى: ﴿ وقليل من عبادي الشكور ﴾ {}
7:17.english: And the Mighty and Majestic said, reporting from the cursed Iblis: 'I will surely sit for them on Your straight path' (Quran 7:16). It is said this is the path of gratitude (Shukr), and due to the high rank of gratitude (Shukr), the cursed one attacked the creation, saying: 'And you will not find most of them grateful (Shakirin)' (Quran 7:17). And Allah said: 'And few of My servants are grateful (Shakur)' (Quran 34:13).
7:17.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

7:17.arabic: فمن فهم حكمة الله تعالى في جميع أنواع الموجودات قدر على القيام بوظيفة الشكر واستقصاء ذلك يحتاج إلى مجلدات ثم لا تفى إلا بالقليل وإنما أوردنا هذا القدر ليعلم علة الصدق في قوله تعالى: ﴿ وقليل من عبادى الشكور ﴾ {} وفرح إبليس لعنه الله بقوله: ﴿ ولا تجد أكثرهم شاكرين ﴾ {} فلا يعرف معنى هذه الآية من لم يعرف معنى هذا كله وأمورا أخر وراء ذلك تنقضى الأعمار دون استقصاء مباديها فأما تفسير الآية ومعنى لفظها فيعرفه كل من يعرف اللغة وبهذا يتبين لك الفرق بين المعنى والتفسير.
7:17.english: So whoever understands the wisdom (Hikmah) of Allah the Exalted in all types of existents becomes capable of performing the duty of gratitude (Shukr), and exhaustively detailing that requires volumes, yet they would not suffice except with little. We have only presented this amount to know the reason for the truth in His saying the Exalted: 'And few of My servants are grateful' (Quran 34:13). And Iblis (Satan), may Allah curse him, rejoiced in His saying: 'And you will not find most of them grateful' (Quran 7:17). So one does not know the meaning of this verse who does not know the meaning of all this and other matters beyond that, whose principles lifetimes expire without exhaustive exploration. As for the interpretation (Tafsir) of the verse and the meaning of its wording, everyone who knows the language knows it, and with this the difference between meaning (Ma'na) and interpretation (Tafsir) becomes clear to you.
7:17.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

7:26.arabic: وقيل في قوله تعالى: ﴿ يا بني آدم قد أنزلنا عليكم لباسا يواري سوءاتكم﴾ يعني العلم ﴿وريشا﴾ يعني اليقين ﴿ولباس التقوى﴾ يعني الحياء.
7:26.english: And it is said regarding His statement, the Exalted: 'O children of Adam, We have sent down upon you clothing to cover your private parts' (Quran 7:26) meaning knowledge (Al-'Ilm), 'and adornment' meaning certainty (Al-Yaqeen), 'and the clothing of piety' meaning modesty (Al-Haya').
7:26.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

7:27.arabic: ولذلك حذر الله منه جميع الخلق فقال الله تعالى "يا بني آدم لا يفتننكم الشيطان كما أخرج أبويكم من الجنة" وقال عز وجل "إنه يراكم هو وقبيله من حيث لا ترونهم" والقرآن من أوله إلى آخره تحذير من الشيطان فكيف وقد أمر بالحذر من العدو كما أمر بالحذر من الكفار فقال تعالى "وليأخذوا حذرهم وأسلحتهم" وقال تعالى "وأعدوا لهم ما استطعتم من قوة ومن رباط الخيل" فإذا لزمك بأمر الله الحذر من العدو الكافر وأنت تراه فبأن يلزمك الحذر من عدو يراك ولا تراه أولى.
7:27.english: Therefore, Allah warned all creation from him, so Allah the Exalted said: "O children of Adam, let not Satan tempt you as he removed your parents from the Garden (Jannah), stripping them of their clothing to show them their private parts. Indeed, he sees you, he and his tribe, from where you do not see them." And the Quran from its beginning to its end is a warning from Satan, so how [can one be heedless] when He has commanded caution from the enemy just as He commanded caution from the disbelievers? He the Exalted said: "And let them take their precaution and their weapons," and He the Exalted said: "And prepare against them whatever you are able of power and of steeds of war." So if it is incumbent upon you by Allah's command to be cautious from the disbelieving enemy whom you see, then it is more appropriate that it be incumbent upon you to be cautious from an enemy who sees you but you do not see him.
7:27.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

7:31.arabic: وعنه عبر بقوله ﭬ "خير الأمور أوساطها"[49] وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى "وكلوا واشربوا ولا تسرفوا" ومهما لم يحس الإنسان بجوع ولا شبع تيسرت له العبادة والفكر وخف في نفسه وقوي على العمل مع خفته، ولكن هذا بعد اعتدال الطبع.
7:31.english: And from this, he expressed with his saying ﭬ "The best of matters are their middles"[49] and to it is the indication by the saying of Allah the Exalted "And eat and drink and do not be excessive (Tasrifu)" and whenever the human does not feel hunger nor satiation, worship (Ibadah) and thought (Fikr) become easy for him and it becomes light in his soul (Nafs) and he becomes strong upon work with its lightness, but this is after the moderation of the natural disposition (Tab').
7:31.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Harms of the Tongue'

7:31.arabic: وكذلك المطلوب في شهوة الطعام الاعتدال دون الشره والجمود قال الله تعالى "وكلوا واشربوا ولا تسرفوا إنه لا يحب المسرفين" وقال في الغضب "أشداء على الكفار رحماء بينهم" وقال ﭬ "خير الأمور أوساطها" وهذا له سر وتحقيق وهو أن السعادة منوطة بسلامة القلب عن عوارض هذا العالم. قال الله تعالى "إلا من أتى الله بقلب سليم" والبخل من عوارض الدنيا، والتبذير أيضاً من عوارض الدنيا، وشرط القلب أن يكون سليماً منهما أي لا يكون ملتفتاً إلى المال ولا يكون حريصاً على إنفاقه ولا على إمساكه، فإن الحريص على الإنفاق مصروف القل
7:31.english: Likewise, what is required in the appetite for food is moderation (I'tidal) without gluttony (Sharah) and rigidity (Jamud). Allah the Exalted said: "And eat and drink and do not be excessive (Tusrifu). Indeed, He does not love the excessive ones (Musrifin)." And He said regarding anger: "Firm against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves." And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "The best of matters are their middle ones." This has a secret and verification, which is that happiness is tied to the soundness of the Heart (Qalb) from the accidents of this world. Allah the Exalted said: "Except he who comes to Allah with a sound heart (Qalb Salim)." And miserliness (Bukhl) is from the accidents of the world, and wastefulness (Tabdhir) is also from the accidents of the world. The condition of the Heart (Qalb) is that it be sound from both of them, meaning it should not be attentive to wealth, nor should it be eager (Hariṣ) to spend it nor to withhold it. For the one eager (Hariṣ) to spend has his Heart (Qalb) diverted to spending, just as the one eager (Hariṣ) to withhold has his Heart (Qalb) diverted to withholding. So the perfection of the Heart (Qalb) is that it be purified (Yasfuw) from both descriptions altogether.
7:31.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

7:31.arabic: السادس الاعتدال في النفقة فلا ينبغي أن يقتر عليهن في الإنفاق ولا ينبغي أن يسرف بل يقتصد قال تعالى (وكلوا واشربوا ولا تسرفوا) وقال تعالى (ولا تجعل يدك مغلولة إلى عنقك ولا تبسطها كل البسط) وقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم (خيركم خيركم لأهله)[127] وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم (دينار أنفقته في سبيل الله ودينار أنفقته في رقبة ودينار تصدقت به على مسكين ودينار أنفقته على أهلك أعظمها أجرا الذي أنفقته على أهلك.)[128]
7:31.english: The sixth [principle] is moderation in expenditure. One should not be stingy with them in spending, nor should one be extravagant, but rather be moderate. Allah the Exalted said: 'And eat and drink, and do not be extravagant (la tusrifu).' And Allah the Exalted said: 'And do not make your hand tied to your neck, nor stretch it out completely.' And the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'The best of you is the best of you to his family.' And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'A dinar you spend in the path of Allah, a dinar you spend to free a slave, a dinar you give in charity to a poor person, and a dinar you spend on your family—the greatest in reward is the one you spend on your family.'
7:31.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

7:32.arabic: فأما ما ذكرت لي أني آكل الرقاق وألبس الدقاق وأحتجب وأجلس على الوطىء فنحن نفعل ذلك ونستغفر الله تعالى فقد قال الله تعالى قل من حرم زينة الله التي أخرج لعباده والطيبات من الرزق وإني لأعلم أن ترك ذلك خير من الدخول فيه ولا تدعنا من كتابك فلسنا ندعك من كتابنا والسلام.
7:32.english: As for what you mentioned to me - that I eat thin bread (raqiq), wear fine clothes (daqaq), seclude myself, and sit on cushions - we do that and seek forgiveness from Allah the Exalted. For Allah the Exalted has said: 'Say: Who has forbidden the adornment (zina) of Allah which He has produced for His servants and the good things (tayyibat) from the provision (rizq)?' And I know that abandoning that is better than entering into it. And do not leave us from your letter, for we will not leave you from our letter. Peace.
7:32.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

7:32.arabic: بل أقول سماع الاوتار ممن يضربها على غير وزن متناسب مستلذ حرام أيضا وبهذا يتبين انه ليست العلة في تحريمها مجرد اللذة الطيبة بل القياس تحليل الطيبات كلها إلا ما في تحليله فساد قال الله تعالى قل من حرم زينة الله التي أخرج لعباده والطيبات من الرزق فهذه الأصوات لا تحرم من حيث إنها أصوات موزونة وإنما تحرم بعارض آخر كما سيأتي في العوارض المحرمة الدرجة الثالثة الموزون والمفهوم وهو الشعر وذلك لا يخرج إلا من حنجرة الإنسان فيقطع بإباحة ذلك لأنه ما زاد إلا كونه مفهوما والكلام المفهوم غير حرام والصوت الطيب ا
7:32.english: Rather, I say that listening to strings from one who plays them without proportional rhythm that is pleasurable is also forbidden, and by this it becomes clear that the reason for their prohibition is not merely the pleasant pleasure, but the analogy is the permissibility of all good things except what in its permissibility contains corruption. Allah the Exalted said: 'Say, who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He has produced for His servants and the good things from the provision?' So these sounds are not forbidden because they are rhythmic sounds, but rather they are forbidden due to another incidental factor, as will come in the forbidden incidents of the third degree: the rhythmic and comprehensible, which is poetry, and that does not come out except from the throat of a human, so it is decisively permissible because it only increased by being comprehensible, and comprehensible speech is not forbidden, and pleasant rhythmic sound is not forbidden. So if the individual elements are not forbidden, then from where is the combination forbidden? Yes, one looks at what is understood from it; if it contains a prohibited matter, its prose and poetry are forbidden, and speaking it is forbidden whether with melodies or not. The truth in it is what Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said when he said: 'Poetry is speech, so its good is good and its bad is bad.' Whenever reciting poetry without voice and melodies is permissible, reciting it with melodies is permissible, for when permissible individual things gather, that combination is permissible, and whenever a permissible thing joins with a permissible thing, it is not forbidden except if the combination contains a prohibition that the individual elements do not contain, and there is no prohibition here. And how can reciting poetry be denied when it was recited in the presence of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him? The hadith of reciting poetry in the presence of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, is agreed upon from the narration of Abu Hurairah that 'Umar passed by Hassan while he was reciting poetry in the mosque, so he glanced at him and said: 'I used to recite, and in it is one better than you,' the hadith, and in Muslim from the narration of 'A'isha, reciting.
7:32.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

7:32.arabic: وما على الحائط ليس منسوبا إلى الذكور ولو حرم هذا لحرم تزيين الكعبة بل الأولى إباحته لموجب قوله قل من حرم زينة الله لا سيما في وقت الزينة إذا لم يتخذ عادة للتفاخر وإن تخيل أن الرجال ينتفعون بالنظر إليه ولا يحرم على الرجال الانتفاع بالنظر إلى الديباج مهما لبسه الجواري والنساء والحيطان في معنى النساء إذ لسن موصوفات بالذكورة
7:32.english: And what is on the wall is not attributed to males, and if this were prohibited, it would prohibit decorating the Kaaba. Rather, the first (opinion) is its permissibility due to the reason of His saying: 'Say, who has forbidden the adornment (Zīnah) of Allah which He has produced for His servants and the good things (Al-Ṭayyibāt) from the provision (Rizq)?' especially at the time of adornment if it is not taken as a habit for boasting. And if it is imagined that men benefit from looking at it, it is not prohibited for men to benefit from looking at silk whenever slave-girls and women wear it, and walls are in the meaning of women since they are not described with masculinity.
7:32.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Manners of Eating'

7:33.arabic: ولأجل غيرة الله تعالى حرم الفواحش ما ظهر منها وما بطن ولا أحد أحب إليه العذر من الله ولذلك بعث المنذرين والمبشرين ولا أحد أحب إليه المدح من الله ولأجل ذلك وعد الجنة.
7:33.english: And because of the jealousy (ghayrah) of Allah the Exalted, He prohibited the abominations (fawāḥish) - what is apparent of them and what is hidden - and no one is more beloved to Him than excuse, and for that reason He sent the warners and the bearers of good tidings, and no one is more beloved to Him than praise, and for that reason He promised Paradise.
7:33.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

7:37.arabic: ومنها الاستكبار عن الحق وكراهته، والحرص على المماراة فيه حتى إن أبغض شيء إلى المناظر أن يظهر على لسان خصمه الحق ومنهما ظهر تشمر لجحده وإنكاره بأقصى جهده وبذل غاية إمكانه في المخادعة والمكر والحيلة لدفعه حتى تصير المماراة فيه عادة طبيعية فلا يسمع كلاما إلا وينبعث من طبعه داعية الاعتراض عليه حتى يغلب ذلك على قلبه في أدلة القرآن وألفاظ الشرع فيضرب البعض منها بالبعض والمراء في مقابلة الباطل محذور إذ ندب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى ترك المراء بالحق على الباطل قال صلى الله عليه وسلم : (( من ترك ا
7:37.english: And among them is arrogance toward the truth (Al-Haqq) and hatred of it, and eagerness for disputation in it until indeed the most hated thing to the disputant is that the truth appears on the tongue of his opponent, and from these two emerges exertion for its denial and rejection with his utmost effort and expending the limit of his capability in deception, cunning, and trickery to repel it until disputation in it becomes a natural habit, so he does not hear speech except that there arises from his nature an urge to object to it until that overcomes his heart (Qalb) in the proofs of the Quran and the expressions of the Sharia, so he strikes some of them with others, and disputation in opposition to falsehood is cautioned against, for the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, encouraged abandoning disputation with truth against falsehood. He said, peace be upon him: 'Whoever abandons disputation while he is false, Allah builds for him a house in the outskirts of Paradise, and whoever abandons disputation while he is truthful, Allah builds for him a house in the highest Paradise.' And Allah the Exalted equated between one who fabricates a lie against Allah and one who denies the truth, for He said, the Exalted: 'And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah or denies the truth when it has come to him?' (Al-Ankabut: 68). And He said, the Exalted: 'So who is more unjust than one who lies against Allah and denies the truth when it has come to him?' (Az-Zumar: 32).
7:37.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

7:40.arabic:
قالوا: الله ورسوله أعلم قال إنه نهر وعدنيه ربى عز  وجل  فى  الجنة
عليه  خير  كثير  عليه  حوض  ترد  عليه  أمتى  يوم  القيامة  آنيته  عدد   نجوم
السماء[188]) وقال أنس: قال رسول الله ﭬ: بينما أنا أسير  فى  الجنة  إذا  بنهر
حافتاه قباب اللؤلؤ المجوف قلت: ما هذا يا جبريل؟ قال: هذا الكوثر  الذى  أعطاك
ربك فضرب الملك بيده فإذا طينه مسك أذفر[189]) وقال كان رسول الله ﭬ يقول:  (ما
بين لابتى حوضى مثل ما بين المدينة وصنعاء أو مثل ما بين  المدينة  وعمان[190])
وروى ابن عمر (أنه لما نزل قوله تعالى: ﴿ إنا أعطين
7:40.english: [77] Hadith that Hudhayfah was specifically given by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) knowledge of the hypocrites, narrated by Muslim from the hadith of Hudhayfah: 'Among my companions are twelve hypocrites, its completion: they will not enter Paradise until the camel passes through the eye of the needle' hadith.
7:40.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

7:42.arabic: وقال أبو طالب المكي العمل بالجوارح من الإيمان ولا يتم دونه وادعى الإجماع فيه واستدل بأدلة تشعر بنقيض غرضه كقوله تعالى الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات إذ هذا يدل على أن العمل وراء الإيمان لا من نفس الإيمان وإلا فيكون العمل في حكم المعاد والعجب أنه ادعى الإجماع في هذا وهو مع ذلك ينقل قوله ﭬ: (لا يكفر أحد إلا بعد جحوده لما أقرّ به[51]) وينكر على المعتزلة قولهم بالتخليد في النار بسبب الكبائر والقائل بهذا قائل بنفس مذهب المعتزلة إذ يقال له من صدق بقلبه وشهد بلسانه ومات في الحال فهل هو في الجنة فلا بد أن
7:42.english: And Abu Talib al-Makki said: 'Action with the limbs (al-Jawarih) is from faith (al-Iman) and it is not complete without it,' and he claimed consensus in this and argued with evidences that suggest the opposite of his purpose, such as His saying, the Exalted: 'And those who believe and do righteous deeds (al-Salihat)' - indeed this indicates that action is beyond faith, not from the essence of faith itself, otherwise action would be in the position of repetition. It is astonishing that he claimed consensus in this while also transmitting his saying, peace be upon him: 'No one becomes an unbeliever except after rejecting what they affirmed,' and he denies the Mu'tazilites' statement of eternal punishment in the Fire due to major sins. The one who says this is saying the same doctrine as the Mu'tazilites, for it is said to him: 'Whoever affirms with their heart (Qalb) and testifies with their tongue and dies immediately - is he in Paradise?' He must say yes, and in this is a ruling on the existence of faith without action. We add and say: If he remained alive until the time of one prayer entered upon him and he abandoned it, then died, or committed adultery then died - is he eternally punished in the Fire? If he says yes, then this is the intent of the Mu'tazilites; and if he says no, then this is a clear statement that action is not a pillar of the essence of faith, nor a condition for its existence, nor for deserving Paradise through it.
7:42.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

7:43.arabic: وهم على الدوام بين أصناف هذه النعم يترددون وهم من زوالها آمنون قال أبو هريرة: قال رسول الله ﭬ: (ينادى مناد: يا أهل الجنة إن لكم أن تصحوا فلا تسقموا أبدا وإن لكم أن تحيوا فلا تموتوا أبدا وإن لكم أن تشبوا فلا تهرموا أبدا وإن لكم أن تنعموا فلا تبأسوا أبدا فذلك قوله عز وجل: ﴿ ونودوا أن تلكم الجنة أورثتموها بما كنتم تعلمون ﴾ {}[216]) ومهما أردت أن تعرف صفة الجنة فاقرأ القرآن فليس وراء بيان الله تعالى بيان واقرأ من قوله تعالى: ﴿ لمن خاف مقام ربه جنتان ﴾ {} إلى آخر سورة الرحمن واقرأ سورة الواقعة وغيرها
7:43.english: And they are perpetually circulating among these varieties of blessings and they are secure from their disappearance. Abu Hurairah said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'A caller will call out: O people of Paradise, indeed for you is to be healthy so you will never be sick forever, and indeed for you is to live so you will never die forever, and indeed for you is to be youthful so you will never grow old forever, and indeed for you is to enjoy comfort so you will never be miserable forever. And that is His statement, the Exalted: "And they will be called: That is Paradise which you have been made to inherit for what you used to do." And whenever you want to know the description of Paradise, then read the Quran, for there is no explanation beyond the explanation of Allah, the Exalted. And read from His statement, the Exalted: "For those who feared the standing (maqām) of their Lord are two gardens" to the end of Surah Ar-Rahman, and read Surah Al-Waqi'ah and other surahs.'
7:43.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

7:43.arabic: فإذا استوى على الراحلة واستوت تحته قال سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر سبع مرات وقال الحمد لله الذي هدانا لهذا وما كنا لنهتدي لولا أن هدانا الله اللهم أنت الحامل على الظهر وأنت المستعان على الأمور.
7:43.english: When he mounts the riding animal and it becomes steady beneath him, he says: Glory be to Allah (Subhan Allah) and Praise be to Allah (Alhamdulillah) and There is no god but Allah (La ilaha illa Allah) and Allah is the Greatest (Allahu Akbar) seven times, and he says: Praise be to Allah (Alhamdulillah) who has guided us to this, and we would not have been guided had Allah not guided us. O Allah (Allahumma), You are the Carrier on the back and You are the One sought for help in matters.
7:43.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

7:43.arabic: فإذا استوت الدابة تحته فليقل الحمد لله الذي هدانا لهذا وما كنا لنهتدي لولا أن هدانا الله اللهم أنت الحامل على الظهر وأنت المستعان على الأمور
7:43.english: When the mount is steady beneath him, let him say: 'Praise be to Allah who guided us to this, and we would not have been guided had Allah not guided us. O Allah, You are the Carrier on the back, and You are the One sought for help in matters.'
7:43.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Etiquette of Travel'

7:43.arabic: ثم اتكأ فقال: ﴿ الحمد لله الذي هدانا لهذا وما كنا لنهتدى لو لا أن هدانا الله ﴾ ثم ينادى مناد تحيون فلا تموتون أبدا وتقيمون فلا تظعنون أبدا وتصحون فلا تمرضون أبدا
7:43.english: Then he reclined and said: 'Praise (Al-Hamd) be to Allah who has guided us to this, and we would not have been guided had Allah not guided us.' Then a caller calls out: 'You live and never die, you settle and never depart, you are healthy and never become ill.'
7:43.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Book of Repentance'

7:44.arabic: ولا ينكر بقاء ذكر الله عز وجل معه بعد الموت فيقول إنه أعدم فكيف يبقى معه ذكر الله عز وجل فإنه لم يعدم عدما يمنع الذكر بل عدما من الدنيا وعالم الملك والشهادة لا من عالم الملكوت وإلى ما ذكرناه الإشارة بقوله ﭬ: (القبر إما حفرة من حفر النار أو روضة من رياض الجنة[58]) وبقوله ﭬ: (أرواح الشهداء في حواصل طيور خضر[59]) وبقوله ﭬ لقتلى بدر من المشركين: (يا فلان ويا فلان وقد سماهم النبي ﭬ هل وجدتم ما وعد ربكم حقا فإني وجدت ما وعدني ربي حقا[60] فسمع عمر رضي الله عنه قوله ﭬ فقال: يا رسول الله كيف يسمعون وأنى
7:44.english: And one should not deny the remaining of the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah, the Exalted, with him after death by saying that he has been annihilated, so how can the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah remain with him? For he has not been annihilated with an annihilation that prevents remembrance, but rather with an annihilation from the worldly life and the realm of dominion and witness, not from the realm of sovereignty. And to what we have mentioned is the allusion in his saying ﭬ: (The grave is either a pit from the pits of Hell or a garden from the gardens of Paradise[58]) and in his saying ﭬ: (The spirits of the martyrs are in the crops of green birds[59]) and in his saying ﭬ to the slain of Badr from the polytheists: (O so-and-so and O so-and-so—and the Prophet ﭬ named them—'Have you found what your Lord promised you to be true? For I have found what my Lord promised me to be true.'[60] Then Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, heard his saying ﭬ and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, how do they hear and how do they respond when they have become decomposed?' He said ﭬ: 'By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, you are not more hearing of my speech than them, but they are not able to respond.') And the hadith is in the Sahih; this is his saying ﭬ regarding the polytheists. As for the believers and the martyrs, he has said ﭬ: (Their spirits are in the crops of green birds suspended beneath the Throne[61]) And this state and what is alluded to by these expressions does not contradict the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah, the Exalted. And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿ And never think of those who have been killed in the cause of Allah as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision, rejoicing in what Allah has bestowed upon them of His bounty, and they receive good tidings about those [to be martyred] after them who have not yet joined them... ﴾ {} the verse. And due to the nobility of the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah, the Exalted, the rank of martyrdom is magnified, because the sought-after is the conclusion, and by the conclusion we mean the farewell to the worldly life and the arrival before Allah, with the Heart (Qalb) immersed in Allah, the Exalted, severed from attachments to other than Him. For if a servant is able to make his concern immersed in Allah, the Exalted, he cannot die in that state except in the ranks of combat, for he has cut off hope from his soul, his family, his wealth, and his children, indeed from the entire worldly life, for he desires it for his life, and he has made light in his heart of his life in the love of Allah, the Exalted, and seeking His pleasure, so there is no greater devotion to Allah...
7:44.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter

7:50.arabic: وكذلك المخاطبات التي تجري من منكر ونكير وفي الميزان والصراط والحساب ومناظرات أهل النار وأهل الجنة في قولهم: ﴿ أفيضوا علينا من الماء أو مما رزقكم الله ﴾ { سورة الأعراف:50 } زعموا أن ذلك كله بلسان الحال وغلا آخرون في حسم الباب منهم أحمد بن حنبل رضي الله عنه حتى منع تأويل قوله: ﴿ كن فيكون ﴾ { سورة النحل: 40 } وزعموا أن ذلك خطاب بحرف وصوت يوجد من الله تعالى في كل لحظة بعدد كون مكون
7:50.english: And likewise the dialogues that occur from Munkar and Nakir (the two questioning angels in the grave) and in the Scale (Mizan), the Bridge (Sirat), and the Reckoning (Hisab), and the debates between the people of the Fire (Ahl al-Nar) and the people of the Garden (Ahl al-Jannah) in their saying: 'Pour upon us from the water or from what Allah has provided you' (Surah al-A'raf: 50). They claimed that all of that is by the tongue of the state (bi-lisan al-hal), and others went to extremes in sealing the door, among them Ahmad ibn Hanbal (may Allah be pleased with him), to the point that he prohibited the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying: 'Be, and it is' (Surah an-Nahl: 40), and they claimed that that is a discourse with letter and sound that occurs from Allah (Exalted is He) in every moment according to the number of a being being brought into existence.
7:50.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

7:52.arabic: وقال عز وجل: ﴿ولقد جئناهم بكتاب فصلناه على علم﴾ وقال تعالى: ﴿فلنقصن عليهم بعلم﴾ وقال عز وجل: ﴿بل هو آيات بينات في صدور الذين أوتوا العلم﴾ وقال تعالى: ﴿خلق الإنسان¤ علمه البيان﴾ وإنما ذكر ذلك في معرض الامتنان.
7:52.english: And the Mighty and Majestic said: 'And indeed We have brought them a Book which We have detailed with knowledge (ʿilm)' (Quran 7:52). And the Exalted said: 'So We will relate to them with knowledge (ʿilm)' (Quran 7:7). And the Mighty and Majestic said: 'Rather, it is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge (ʿilm)' (Quran 29:49). And the Exalted said: 'He created the human being, He taught him the clear expression (bayān)' (Quran 55:3-4). And indeed He mentioned that in the context of bestowing favor.
7:52.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

7:54.arabic: والثاني: الأحكام، وحاصله يرجع إلى الاستدلال على الحوادث بالأسباب وهو يضاهي استدلال الطبيب بالنبض على ما سيحدث من المرض وهو معرفة لمجاري سنة الله تعالى وعادته في خلقه ولكن قد ذمه الشرع قال صلى الله عليه وسلم: (إذا ذكر القدر فأمسكوا وإذا ذكرت النجوم فأمسكوا وإذا ذكر أصحابي فأمسكوا)[81]. وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: (أخاف على أمتي بعدي ثلاثا حيف الأئمة والإيمان بالنجوم والتكذيب بالقدر)[82]. وقال عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه: تعلموا من النجوم ما تهتدون به في البر والبحر ثم أمسكوا. وإنما زجر عنه من ثلاثة أ
7:54.english: The second: The judgments, and its essence returns to deducing events through causes, which resembles a doctor deducing from the pulse what will occur of illness, and it is knowledge of the courses of the custom (Sunnah) of Allah the Exalted and His habit in His creation, but the Law has censured it. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'When predestination (Qadar) is mentioned, refrain; when the stars are mentioned, refrain; and when my companions are mentioned, refrain.' And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'I fear for my community after me three things: the injustice of rulers, belief in the stars, and denial of predestination (Qadar).' And Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'Learn from the stars what guides you on land and sea, then refrain.' And it is prohibited for three aspects: The first: It harms most of creation, for when it is cast to them that these effects occur following the movement of the planets, it settles in their souls (Nufus) that the planets are the effectors and that they are the deities managing because they are noble celestial substances, and their impact becomes great in the hearts (Qulub), so the heart (Qalb) remains attentive to them, and good and evil are seen as feared or hoped from their direction, and the remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah the Exalted is erased from the heart (Qalb), for the weak one limits his view to the intermediaries, and the firmly established scholar is the one who perceives that the sun, the moon, and the stars are subjugated by His command, glory be to Him and exalted is He. And the example of the weak one's view to the occurrence of sunlight following sunrise is like an ant if intellect were created for it and it were on the surface of a paper, and it looks at the blackness of the line being renewed, so it believes it is the action of the pen, and it does not ascend in its view to witnessing the fingers, then from them to the hand, then from it to the moving will (Iradah) of the hand, then from it to the writer, the capable, the willing, then from him to the creator of the hand, capability, and will (Iradah). So most of the view of creation is limited to the proximate, lowly causes, cut off from ascending to the causer of causes. This is one of the reasons for prohibition regarding the stars.
7:54.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

7:54.arabic: ويستحب أن يقرأ الآيات المخصوصة مثل آية الكرسي وآخر البقرة وغيرهما وقوله تعالى: ﴿ وإلهكم إله واحد لا إله إلا هو ﴾ {} إلى قوله: ﴿ لقوم يعقلون ﴾ {} يقال إن من قرأها عند النوم حفظ الله عليه القرآن فلم ينسه ويقرأ من سورة الأعراف هذه الآية: ﴿ إن ربكم الله الذي خلق السموات والأرض في ستة أيام ﴾ {} إلى قوله: ﴿ قريب من المحسنين ﴾ {} وآخر بني إسرائيل ﴿ قل ادعوا الله ﴾ {} الآيتين فإنه يدخل في شعاره ملك يوكل بحفظه فيستغفر له ويقرأ المعوذتين وينفث بهن في يديه ويمسح بهما وجهه وسائر جسده كذلك روى من فعل رسول ال
7:54.english: And it is recommended to recite the specified verses such as the Throne Verse (Ayat al-Kursi) and the end of Surah al-Baqarah and others, and His saying, the Exalted: 'And your god is one God. There is no deity except Him' {} until His saying: 'for a people who use reason' {}. It is said that whoever recites it at sleep, Allah preserves the Quran for him so he does not forget it. And recite from Surah al-A'raf this verse: 'Indeed, your Lord is Allah who created the heavens and the earth in six days' {} until His saying: 'is near to the doers of good' {}. And the end of Bani Isra'il 'Say, Call upon Allah' {} the two verses, for then enters into his emblem an angel entrusted with his protection who seeks forgiveness for him. And recite the two seeking refuge (al-Mu'awwidhatayn) and blow with them into his hands and wipe with them his face and the rest of his body, as narrated from the action of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him[73]. And let him recite ten from the beginning of al-Kahf and ten from its end, and these verses are for awakening for the night prayer (Qiyam al-Layl). And Ali, may Allah honor his face, said: 'I do not think that a man with complete intellect sleeps before reciting the two verses from the end of Surah al-Baqarah.' And let him say twenty-five times: Glory be to Allah (Subhan Allah) and praise be to Allah (al-Hamd lillah) and there is no god but Allah (La ilaha illa Allah) and Allah is the Greatest (Allahu Akbar), so that the total of these four phrases becomes four hundred times.
7:54.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Book of Knowledge'

7:55.arabic: الرابع: خفض الصوت بين المخافتة والجهر لما روى أن أبا موسى الأشعري قال قدمنا مع رسول الله فلما دنونا من المدينة كبر وكبر الناس ورفعوا أصواتهم فقال النبي ﭬ: (يا أيها الناس إن الذي تدعون ليس بأصم ولا غائب إن الذي تدعون بينكم وبين أعناق ركابكم) وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنه في قوله عز وجل: ﴿ ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها ﴾ {} أي بدعائك وقد أثنى الله عز وجل على نبيه زكرياء عليه السلام حيث قال: ﴿ إذ نادى ربه نداء خفيا ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل: ﴿ ادعوا ربكم تضرعا وخفية ﴾ {}. الخامس: أن لا يتكلف السجع في الدعاء فإن
7:55.english: Fourth: Lowering the voice between whispering and loudness, as narrated that Abu Musa al-Ash'ari said: We arrived with the Messenger of Allah, and when we approached Medina, he said 'Allahu Akbar' and the people said 'Allahu Akbar' and raised their voices. The Prophet said: (O people, the One you call upon is not deaf nor absent; the One you call upon is between you and the necks of your mounts). And Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said regarding His saying, the Exalted: (And do not be loud in your prayer nor whisper it) meaning in your supplication. And Allah, the Exalted, praised His prophet Zakariya, peace be upon him, when He said: (When he called upon his Lord with a secret call). And the Exalted said: (Call upon your Lord humbly and secretly). Fifth: That one should not contrive rhymed prose in supplication, for the state of the supplicant should be a state of humility (mutadarriʿ), and contrivance does not suit it. He said: (There will be a people who exceed bounds in supplication). And the Exalted said: (Call upon your Lord humbly and secretly; indeed, He does not love the transgressors). It is said its meaning is contrivance for rhymed prose, and it is preferable not to go beyond the transmitted supplications, for one may transgress in his supplication and ask for what his benefit does not require, for not everyone is good at supplication. Therefore, it is narrated from Mu'adh, may Allah be pleased with him, that the scholars are needed in Paradise, for it will be said to the people of Paradise: 'Wish,' and they will not know how to wish until they learn from the scholars. And he said: (Beware of rhymed prose in supplication; it is enough for one of you to say: O Allah, I ask You for Paradise and what brings near to it of speech and action, and I seek refuge in You from the Fire and what brings near to it of speech and action). And in the report: 'There will come a people who exceed bounds in supplication and purification.' And some of the predecessors passed by a storyteller supplicating with rhymed prose and said to him: 'May Allah elevate your exaggeration, I bear witness that I saw Habib al-'Ajami supplicating, and he did not exceed saying: O Allah, make us good, O Allah, do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection, O Allah, grant us success in good,' and the people were supplicating from every direction behind him, and he was known for the blessing of his supplication. And some of them said: 'Supplicate with the tongue of humility (dhull) and neediness (iftiqar), not with the tongue of eloquence and fluency.'
7:55.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure

7:55.arabic: الرابع: خفض الصوت بين المخافتة والجهر لما روى أن أبا موسى الأشعري قال قدمنا مع رسول الله فلما دنونا من المدينة كبر وكبر الناس ورفعوا أصواتهم فقال النبي ﷺ: (يا أيها الناس إن الذي تدعون ليس بأصم ولا غائب إن الذي تدعون بينكم وبين أعناق ركابكم) وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها في قوله عز وجل: ﴿ ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها ﴾ {} أي بدعائك وقد أثنى الله عز وجل على نبيه زكرياء عليه السلام حيث قال: ﴿ إذ نادى ربه نداء خفيا ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل: ﴿ ادعوا ربكم تضرعا وخفية ﴾ {}. الخامس: أن لا يتكلف السجع في الدعاء فإن
7:55.english: Fourth: Lowering the voice between whispering and loudness, because it was narrated that Abu Musa al-Ash'ari said: 'We came with the Messenger of Allah, and when we approached Medina, he said takbir and the people said takbir and raised their voices.' The Prophet ﷺ said: 'O people, the One you are calling is not deaf nor absent; the One you are calling is between you and the necks of your mounts.' And Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said regarding His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And do not be loud in your prayer nor whisper it' - meaning in your supplication. And Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, praised His prophet Zakariya, peace be upon him, when He said: 'When he called upon his Lord with a secret call.' And the Mighty and Majestic said: 'Call upon your Lord with humility and in secret.' Fifth: That one should not force rhymed prose in supplication, for the state of the supplicant should be a state of humility, and affectation does not suit it. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'There will be a people who transgress in supplication.' And the Mighty and Majestic said: 'Call upon your Lord with humility and in secret. Indeed, He does not love the transgressors.' It is said its meaning is affectation for rhymed prose. And it is preferable not to go beyond the transmitted supplications, for one may transgress in his supplication and ask for what his benefit does not require, and not everyone is good at supplication. Therefore, it is narrated from Mu'adh, may Allah be pleased with him, that the scholars are needed in Paradise, for it will be said to the people of Paradise: 'Wish,' and they will not know how to wish until they learn from the scholars. And the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Beware of rhymed prose in supplication; it is enough for one of you to say: O Allah, I ask You for Paradise and what brings near to it of speech and action, and I seek refuge in You from the Fire and what brings near to it of speech and action.' And in the report: 'There will come a people who transgress in supplication and purification.' And some of the predecessors passed by a storyteller supplicating with rhymed prose and said to him: 'May Allah elevate your exaggeration; I bear witness that I saw Habib al-'Ajami supplicating and he did not exceed saying: O Allah, make us good, O Allah, do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection, O Allah, grant us success in good.' And the people were supplicating from every direction behind him, and he was known for the blessing of his supplication. And some of them said: 'Supplicate with the tongue of lowliness and need, not with the tongue of eloquence and fluency.' And it is said that the scholars, the substitutes, do not exceed seven words or less in supplication, and the end of Surah al-Baqarah testifies to this, for Allah, the Exalted, did not inform in any place of the supplications of worship more than that.
7:55.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure

7:55.arabic: السادس: التضرع والخشوع والرغبة والرهبة قال الله تعالى: ﴿ إنهم كانوا يسارعون في الخيرات ويدعوننا رغبا ورهبا ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل: ﴿ ادعوا ربكم تضرعا وخفية ﴾ {} وقال ﭬ: (إذا أحب الله عبدا ابتلاه حتى يسمع تضرعه[87]).
7:55.english: Sixth: Supplication (Tadarru') and Humility (Khushu') and Desire (Raghba) and Fear (Rahba). Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds and supplicate Us with desire and fear' {} and He the Mighty and Majestic said: 'Supplicate your Lord with humility (Tadarru') and in secret (Khufya)' {} and the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'When Allah loves a servant, He tests him until He hears his supplication (Tadarru')[87].'
7:55.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

7:55.arabic: قال الله تعالى: ﴿ وإذا سألك عبادي عني فإني قريب أجيب دعوة الداع إذا دعان فليستجيبوا لي ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ ادعوا ربكم تضرعا وخفية إنه لا يحب المعتدين ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ وقال ربكم ادعوني أستجب لكم إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي سيدخلون جهنم داخرين ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل: ﴿ قل ادعوا الله أو ادعوا الرحمن أيا ما تدعوا فله الأسماء الحسنى ﴾ {} وروى النعمان بن بشير عن النبي ﭬ أنه قال: (إن الدعاء هو العبادة ثم قرأ: ﴿ ادعوني أستجب لكم ﴾ {}[65]) الآية. وقال ﭬ: (الدعاء مخ العبادة[66]) وروى أبو هريرة أنه ﭬ قال: (ليس
7:55.english: Allah the Exalted said: 'And when My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me' (Quran 2:186). And He said: 'Call upon your Lord humbly (tadarru'an) and in secret (khufyatan). Indeed, He does not like the transgressors' (Quran 7:55). And He said: 'And your Lord says, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you. Indeed, those who disdain My worship will enter Hell in humiliation"' (Quran 40:60). And the Mighty and Majestic said: 'Say, "Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Merciful. Whichever [name] you call - to Him belong the best names"' (Quran 17:110). And An-Nu'man ibn Bashir narrated from the Prophet (peace be upon him) that he said: ('Supplication (Du'a) is worship (al-'Ibadah).' Then he recited: 'Call upon Me; I will respond to you' (Quran 40:60) [65]). And he (peace be upon him) said: ('Supplication (Du'a) is the marrow of worship (mukhkh al-'Ibadah) [66]'). And Abu Hurairah narrated that he (peace be upon him) said: ('Nothing is more honorable to Allah the Mighty and Majestic than supplication (Du'a) [67]'). And he (peace be upon him) said: ('The servant (al-'Abd) does not miss from supplication (Du'a) one of three things: either a sin (dhamb) is forgiven for him, or a good (khayr) is hastened for him, or a good (khayr) is stored for him [68]'). And Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'Sufficient for supplication (Du'a) with righteousness (al-Birr) is what suffices food from salt.' And he (peace be upon him) said: ('Ask Allah the Exalted from His bounty, for indeed Allah the Exalted loves to be asked, and the best worship (al-'Ibadah) is awaiting relief (al-Faraj) [69]').
7:55.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication

7:56.arabic: وحيث اقتصر ذكر شرطا جامعا فقال تعالى ﴿ إن رحمة الله قريب من المحسنين ﴾ {} فالإحسان يجمع الكل وهكذا من يتصفح القرآن من أوله إلى آخره ومن فهم ذلك فجدير بأن يكون حاله الخشية والحزن ولذلك قال الحسن: والله ما أصبح اليوم عبد يتلو القرآن يؤمن به إلا كثر حزنه وقل فرحه وكثر بكاؤه وقل ضحكه وكثر نصبه وشغله وقلت راحته وبطالته.
7:56.english: And where He limited the mention to a comprehensive condition, He said, the Most High: 'Indeed, the Mercy (Rahmah) of Allah is near to the Doers of Good (Muhsinin).' {} So the Doing of Good (Ihsan) encompasses all. And thus, whoever peruses the Quran from its beginning to its end and understands that, it is fitting that his state be one of fear (Khashyah) and sorrow. Therefore, Al-Hasan said: By Allah, no servant today recites the Quran and believes in it except that his sorrow increases and his joy decreases, his weeping increases and his laughter decreases, his toil and preoccupation increase and his rest and idleness decrease.
7:56.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

7:56.arabic: ولنرجع إلى الغرض المطلوب فالمقصود أن غرور الشيطان بأن الآخرة شك يدفع إما بيقين تقليدي، وأما ببصيرة ومشاهدة من جهة الباطن، والمؤمنين بألسنتهم وبعقائدهم إذا ضيعوا أوامر الله تعالى وهجروا الأعمال الصالحة ولابسوا الشهوات والمعاصي فهم مشاركون للكفار في هذا الغرور من النار ولو بعد حين، ولكنهم أيضاً من المغرورين فإنهم اعترفوا بأن الآخرة خير من الدنيا ولكنهم مالوا إلى الدنيا وآثروها، ومجرد الإيمان لا يكفي للفوز قال تعالى "وإني لغفار لمن تاب وآمن وعمل صالحاً ثم اهتدى" وقال تعالى "إن رحمت الله قريب من الم
7:56.english: And let us return to the intended purpose, so the intended meaning is that the deception of Satan that the Hereafter is doubt is repelled either by traditional certainty, or by insight and witnessing from the aspect of the inner (Batin), and the believers with their tongues and with their beliefs if they neglect the commands of Allah the Exalted and abandon righteous works and engage in desires and disobediences, then they are partners with the disbelievers in this deception from the Fire even if after a while, but they are also among the deceived, for they acknowledged that the Hereafter is better than the world but they inclined to the world and preferred it, and mere faith is not sufficient for success. Allah the Exalted said: "And indeed, I am Forgiving to whoever repents and believes and does righteous work then is guided" and Allah the Exalted said: "Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the doers of good (Muhsinin)" then the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Ihsan (doing good) is that you worship Allah as if you see Him" and Allah the Exalted said: "By time, indeed, mankind is in loss, except for those who have believed and done righteous works and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience." So the promise of forgiveness in all the Book of Allah the Exalted is tied to faith and righteous work together, not to faith alone, so these are also deceived, I mean those who are content with the world, joyful in it, indulgent in its pleasures, loving it. Those who hate death fearing the loss of worldly pleasures, not those who hate it fearing what comes after it, so this is an example of deception by the world from both disbelievers and believers altogether.
7:56.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

7:56.arabic: وقد أمر الله تعالى بالعدل والإحسان جميعا والعدل سبب النجاة فقط وهو يجري من التجارة مجرى رأس المال والإحسان سبب الفوز ونيل السعادة وهو يجري من التجارة مجرى الربح ولا يعد من الغفلاء من قنع في معاملات الدنيا برأس ماله فكذا في معاملات الآخرة فلا ينبغي للمتدين أن يقتصر على العدل واجتناب الظلم ويدع أبواب الإحسان وقد قال الله وأحسن كما أحسن الله إليك وقال عز وجل إن الله يأمر بالعدل والإحسان وقال سبحانه إن رحمت الله قريب من المحسنين ونعني بالإحسان فعل ما ينتفع به المعامل وهو غير واجب عليه ولكنه تفضل منه
7:56.english: And Allah the Exalted has commanded justice and excellence in conduct (Ihsan) together. Justice is only the cause of salvation, and it flows in trade like capital. Excellence in conduct (Ihsan) is the cause of triumph and attainment of happiness, and it flows in trade like profit. One is not considered among the heedless who is content in worldly transactions with his capital, likewise in the transactions of the Hereafter. So it is not fitting for the religious person to limit himself to justice and avoiding oppression and abandon the doors of excellence in conduct (Ihsan). And Allah has said: 'And do good as Allah has done good to you' (28:77). And the Mighty and Majestic said: 'Indeed, Allah commands justice and excellence in conduct (Ihsan)' (16:90). And He the Glorified said: 'Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the doers of good (Al-Muhsinin)' (7:56). And we mean by excellence in conduct (Ihsan) doing what benefits the other party in transaction, and it is not obligatory upon him, but it is a favor from him. For the obligatory enters into the category of justice and avoiding oppression, and we have mentioned it.
7:56.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Etiquette of Earning'

7:57.arabic: وقوله تعالى ﴿ فأنزلنا به الماء ﴾ {} يعني السحاب ﴿ فأخرجنا به من كل الثمرات ﴾ {} يعني الماء وأمثال هذا في القرآن لا ينحصر.
7:57.english: And His saying, the Exalted: 'And We sent down with it water' (Quran 7:57) means the cloud. 'And We brought forth with it every kind of fruit' (Quran 7:57) means the water. And examples like this in the Quran are countless.
7:57.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

7:63.arabic: السبب الرابع: التعجب، كما أخبر الله تعالى عن الأمم السالفة إذ قالوا "ما أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا" "وقالوا أنؤمن لبشرين مثلنا" "ولئن أطعتم بشراً مثلكم إنكم إذاً لخاسرون" فتعجبوا من أن يفوز برتبة الرسالة والوحي والقرب من الله تعالى بشر مثلهم فحسدوهم، وأحبوا زوال النبوة عنهم جزعاً أن يفضل عليهم من هو مثلهم في الخلقة، لا عن قصد تكبر وطلب رياسة وتقدم عداوة أو سبب آخر من سائر الأسباب، وقالوا متعجبين "أبعث الله بشراً رسولاً" وقالوا "لولا أنزل علينا الملائكة" وقال تعالى "أو عجبتم أن جاءكم ذكر من ربكم على رجل
7:63.english: The fourth cause: Astonishment (Ta'ajjub), as Allah the Exalted informed about the past nations when they said, "You are only human beings like us," "And they said, 'Shall we believe for two human beings like ourselves?'," "And if you obey a human being like yourselves, then indeed, you would be losers." So they were astonished that a human being like them would attain the rank of Messengership, Revelation, and closeness to Allah the Exalted, so they envied them, and desired the removal of Prophethood from them out of distress that one who is like them in creation would be favored over them, not from an intention of arrogance, seeking leadership, advancing enmity, or any other cause from the various causes. And they said in astonishment, "Has Allah sent a human being as a messenger?" And they said, "Why were angels not sent down to us?" And Allah the Exalted said, "Or are you astonished that a Remembrance (Dhikr) from your Lord has come to you upon a man from among you?" The verse.
7:63.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

7:69.arabic: السبب الرابع: التعجب، كما أخبر الله تعالى عن الأمم السالفة إذ قالوا "ما أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا" "وقالوا أنؤمن لبشرين مثلنا" "ولئن أطعتم بشراً مثلكم إنكم إذاً لخاسرون" فتعجبوا من أن يفوز برتبة الرسالة والوحي والقرب من الله تعالى بشر مثلهم فحسدوهم، وأحبوا زوال النبوة عنهم جزعاً أن يفضل عليهم من هو مثلهم في الخلقة، لا عن قصد تكبر وطلب رياسة وتقدم عداوة أو سبب آخر من سائر الأسباب، وقالوا متعجبين "أبعث الله بشراً رسولاً" وقالوا "لولا أنزل علينا الملائكة" وقال تعالى "أو عجبتم أن جاءكم ذكر من ربكم على رجل
7:69.english: The fourth cause: Amazement (Ta'ajjub), as Allah the Exalted informed about the past nations when they said, 'You are only human beings like us' and 'They said: Shall we believe in two human beings like ourselves?' and 'If you obey a human being like yourselves, then indeed you would be losers.' So they were amazed that a human being like them would attain the rank of Messengership, Revelation, and proximity (Qurb) to Allah the Exalted, so they envied them, and desired the removal of Prophethood from them out of distress that one who is like them in creation would be preferred over them, not from an intention of arrogance, seeking leadership, advancing enmity, or any other cause from the rest of the causes. And they said in amazement, 'Has Allah sent a human being as a messenger?' and they said, 'Why were not angels sent down to us?' And Allah the Exalted said, 'Or do you wonder that a Remembrance (Dhikr) from your Lord has come to you upon a man from among you to warn you? And remember when He made you successors after the people of Noah and increased you in creation extensively. So remember the favors of Allah that you might succeed.'
7:69.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

7:75.arabic: ومنها المكرر القاطع لوصل الكلام في الظاهر كقوله عز وجل ﴿ وما يتبع الذين يدعون من دون الله شركاء إن يتبعون إلا الظن ﴾ {} وقوله عز وجل ﴿ قال الملأ الذين استكبروا من قومه للذين استضعفوا لمن آمن منهم ﴾ {} معناه الذين استكبروا لمن آمن من الذين استضعفوا
7:75.english: And among them is the repeated [construction] that cuts off the apparent connection of speech, like His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And those whom they invoke besides Allah do not follow [anything]; they follow not except assumption' (Quran 6:148), and His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Said the chiefs who were arrogant among his people to those who were oppressed - to those who believed among them' (Quran 7:75), its meaning is: those who were arrogant [said] to those who believed from among those who were oppressed.
7:75.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

7:79.arabic: وقد وصف الله تعالى الكاذبين ببعضهم للناصحين إذ قال ولكن لا تحبون الناصحين وهذا في عيب هو غافل عنه فأما ما علمت انه يعلمه من نفسه فإنما هو مقهور عليه من طبعه فلا ينبغي أن يكشف فيه ستره إن كان يخفيه وإن كان يظهره فلا بد من التلطف في النصح بالتعريض مرة وبالتصريح أخرى إلى حد لا يؤدي إلى الإيحاش فإن علمت أن النصح غير مؤثر فيه وأنه مضطر من طبعه إلى الإصرار عليه فالسكوت عنه أولى وهذا كله فيما يتعلق بمصالح أخيك في دينه أو دنياه أما ما يتعلق بتقصيره في حقك فالواجب فيه الاحتمال والعفو والصفح والتعامى عنه
7:79.english: And Allah the Exalted has described the liars with some of them for the advisers (الناصحين) when He said: 'But you do not love the advisers (الناصحين).' And this is regarding a defect that one is heedless of. As for what you know that he knows about himself, then it is only something he is compelled to by his nature, so it is not appropriate to uncover its covering if he conceals it, and if he reveals it, then gentleness in advice (النصح) is necessary, with allusion at times and with explicit statement at others, to a limit that does not lead to alienation. If you know that the advice (النصح) is not effective in him and that he is compelled by his nature to persist in it, then silence about it is preferable. And all of this pertains to the interests of your brother in his religion or his worldly life. As for what pertains to his shortcoming in your right, then the obligation in it is forbearance, pardon, forgiveness, and turning a blind eye to it, and addressing that is not from advice (النصح) in anything. Yes, if it is such that its continuation leads to severance, then reproach in secret is better than severance, and allusion to it is better than explicit statement, and writing is better than face-to-face speech, and forbearance is better than all, for your intention from your brother should be the rectification of your soul (نفسك) by your observance of him and your fulfillment of his right and your forbearance of his shortcoming, not seeking help from him and seeking benefit from him.
7:79.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

7:87.arabic: وقال رجل لعمرو بن عبيد: إن الأسواري ما يزال يذكرك في قصصه بشر، فقال له عمرو: يا هذا ما رعيت حق مجالسة الرجل حيث نقلت إلينا حديثه، ولا أديت حقي حين أعلمتني عن أخي ما أكره ولكن أعمله أن الموت يعمنا والقبر يضمنا والقيامة تجمعنا والله تعالى يحكم بيننا وهو خير الحاكمين.
7:87.english: And a man said to Amr ibn Ubayd: Al-Aswari continues to mention you in his stories with evil, so Amr said to him: O this one, you did not observe the right of sitting with the man when you conveyed to us his speech, nor did you fulfill my right when you informed me about my brother what I dislike. But I act upon the knowledge that death encompasses us, the grave gathers us, the Resurrection (Qiyamah) assembles us, and Allah the Exalted judges between us, and He is the best of judges.
7:87.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

7:95.arabic: وحذرهم أن يأخذهم بغتة وهم لا يشعرون فقال "ما ينظرون إلا صيحة واحدة تأخذهم وهم يخصمون فلا يستطيعون توصية ولا إلى أهلهم يرجعون" والصلاة والسلام على محمد رسوله الذي يسير تحت لوائه النبيون، وعلى آله وأصحابه الأئمة المهديين، والسادة المرضيين، صلاة يوازي عددها عدد ما كان من خلق الله وما سيكون، ويحظى ببركتها الأولون والآخرون، وسلم تسليماً كثيرا. أما بعد فإن الغضب شعلة نار اقتبست من نار الله الموقدة التي تطلع على الأفئدة، وإنها لمستكنة في طي الفؤاد. استكنان الجمر تحت الرماد، ويستخرجها الكبر الدفين في قل
7:95.english: And He warned them that He might seize them suddenly while they are unaware, as He said: "They await not but a single Cry that will seize them while they are disputing. Then they will not be able to make a bequest, nor will they return to their families." And prayers and peace be upon Muhammad, His messenger, under whose banner the prophets march, and upon his family and his companions, the guided leaders, and the pleased masters, prayers equal in number to what has been of Allah's creation and what will be, and may the earlier and later ones attain its blessing, and abundant peace. After that, indeed anger is a flame of fire kindled from the fire of Allah that is ignited, which rises upon the hearts (Af'idah), and it is hidden in the recess of the heart (Fu'ad). It is like the ember hidden under ashes, and it is extracted by the concealed arrogance in the heart of every obstinate tyrant, like extracting fire from stone with iron. And it has been revealed to the observers by the light of certainty (Yaqin), that man has a vein extending to the accursed Satan (Shaytan), so whoever is provoked by the fire of anger has strengthened in him the kinship of Satan, as he said: "You created me from fire and created him from clay." For the nature of clay is stillness and dignity, and the nature of fire is blazing and flaming, and movement and agitation. And from the outcomes of anger are malice (Haqd) and envy (Hasad), and by them perished those who perished and corrupted those who corrupted, and their source is a morsel; if it is rectified, the entire body is rectified with it. And if malice (Haqd), envy (Hasad), and anger are among what drive the servant to places of destruction, then how much he needs to know the means of...
7:95.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

7:99.arabic: ومن اعتقد جزماً أنه فوق أحد من عباد الله فقد أحبط بجهله جمع عمله، فإن الجهل أفحش المعاصي وأعظم شيء يبعد العبد عن الله، وحكمه لنفسه بأنه خير من غيره جهل محض وأمن من مكر الله ولا يأمن مكر الله إلا القوم الخاسرون ولذلك روي أن رجلاً ذكر بخير للنبي ﭬ فأقبل ذات يوم فقالوا: يا رسول الله هذا الذي ذكرناه لك، فقال "إني أرى في وجهه سفعة من الشيطان، فسلم ووقف على النبي ﭬ فقال له النبي ﭬ "أسألك بالله حدثتك نفسك أن ليس في القوم أفضل منك" قال: اللهم نعم"[56] فرأى رسول الله ﭬ بنور النبوة ما استكن في قلبه سفعة ف
7:99.english: And whoever firmly believes that he is above any of the servants of Allah has nullified with his ignorance all his deeds, for ignorance is the most vile of sins and the greatest thing that distances the servant from Allah, and his judgment for himself that he is better than others is pure ignorance and security from the plotting of Allah, and none feels secure from the plotting of Allah except the people who are losers. And for that reason, it was narrated that a man was mentioned favorably to the Prophet (peace be upon him), then he came one day and they said: O Messenger of Allah, this is the one we mentioned to you, so he said: 'Indeed, I see in his face a trace from Satan.' So he greeted and stood before the Prophet (peace be upon him), and the Prophet (peace be upon him) said to him: 'I ask you by Allah, did your soul (Nafs) tell you that there is no one in the group better than you?' He said: 'O Allah, yes.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) saw with the light of prophethood what had settled in his heart as a trace on his face. And this is an affliction from which none of the servants is free except whom Allah protects.
7:99.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

7:99.arabic: وإنما كان خوف الأنبياء مع ما فاض عليهم من النعم لأنهم لم يأمنوا مكر الله تعالى ﴿ فلا يأمن مكر الله إلا القوم الخاسرون ﴾ حتى روى أن النبي وجبريل عليهما الصلاة والسلام بكيا خوفا من الله تعالى فأوحى الله إليهما لم تبكيان وقد أمنتكما فقالا ومن يأمن مكرك وكأنهما إذ علما أن الله هو علام الغيوب وأنه لا وقوف لهما على غاية الأمور لم يأمنا أن يكون قوله قد أمنتكما ابتلاء وامتحانا لهما ومكرا بهما حتى إن سكن خوفهما ظهر أنهما قد أمنا من المكر وما وفيا بقولهما
7:99.english: And the fear of the Prophets, despite the abundant blessings that flowed upon them, was because they did not feel secure from the plotting (makkara) of Allah the Exalted: 'So none feels secure from the plotting (makkara) of Allah except the people who are losers.' Until it was narrated that the Prophet and Gabriel, peace be upon them both, wept out of fear from Allah the Exalted, so Allah revealed to them: 'Why do you weep when I have given you security?' They said: 'And who feels secure from Your plotting (makkara)?' And it was as if they, since they knew that Allah is the Knower of the unseen and that they had no standing regarding the ultimate matters, did not feel secure that His saying 'I have given you security' might be a trial (ibtila') and a test (imtihana) for them and a plotting (makkara) against them, so that if their fear subsided, it would become apparent that they had felt secure from the plotting (makkara) and had not been true to their saying.
7:99.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

7:99.arabic: فمن آمن به تخلص من هذا الغرور فإن منشأ هذا الغرور والجهل بالله وبصفاته، فإن من عرفه لا يأمن مكره ولا يغتر بأمثال هذه الخيالات الفاسدة، وينظر إلى فرعون وهامان وقارون وإلى ملوك الأرض وما جرى لهم كيف أحسن الله إليهم ابتداء ثم دمرهم تدميرا! فقال تعالى "هل تحس منهم من أحد" الآية. وقد حذر الله تعالى من مكره واستدراجه فقال "فلا يأمن مكر الله إلا القوم الخاسرون" وقال تعالى "ومكروا مكراً ومكرنا مكراً وهم لا يشعرون" وقال عز وجل "ومكروا ومكر الله والله خير الماكرين" وقال تعالى "إنهم يكيدون كيداً وأكيد كيدا
7:99.english: So whoever believes in Him is saved from this delusion (Ghurur), for the origin of this delusion (Ghurur) is ignorance of Allah and His attributes. For whoever knows Him does not feel secure from His scheme (Makr) nor is deceived by such false imaginings, and looks at Pharaoh, Haman, and Korah, and at the kings of the earth and what befell them—how Allah initially bestowed favors upon them, then utterly destroyed them! So Allah the Exalted said: "Do you perceive any of them?" [Quran 19:98]. And Allah the Exalted has warned against His scheme (Makr) and gradual entrapment (Istidraj), saying: "So none feels secure from the scheme (Makr) of Allah except the losing people." [Quran 7:99] And He said: "And they devised a scheme (Makr), and We devised a scheme (Makr), while they were unaware." [Quran 27:50] And He the Mighty and Majestic said: "And they devised a scheme (Makr), and Allah devised a scheme (Makr), and Allah is the best of schemers (Makirin)." [Quran 3:54] And He said: "Indeed, they are planning a plan (Kaid), and I am planning a plan (Kaid). So give the disbelievers respite; give them respite a little." [Quran 86:15-17] Just as it is not permissible for a neglected servant to infer from the master's neglect of him and enabling him with blessings that the master loves him, rather he should beware that this might be a scheme (Makr) and plot (Kaid) from him, even though the master did not warn him of his own scheme (Makr), then how much more necessary is this regarding Allah the Exalted, with His warning of His gradual entrapment (Istidraj) being more appropriate. Therefore, whoever feels secure from the scheme (Makr) of Allah is deluded (Mughtarr), and the origin of this delusion (Ghurur) is that he infers from worldly blessings that he is honored by that Bestower, and it is possible that this is evidence of degradation, but that possibility does not accord with desire (Hawa). So Satan, through the medium of desire (Hawa), inclines the heart (Qalb) toward what accompanies it, which is believing that it indicates honor, and this is the definition of delusion (Ghurur).
7:99.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

7:100.arabic: وأما الآثار المذمومة فإنها مثل دخان مظلم يتصاعد إلى مرآة القلب ولا يزال يتراكم عليه مرة بعد أخرى إلى أن يسود ويظلم ويصير بالكلية محجوبا عن الله تعالى وهو الطبع وهو الرين قال الله تعالى كلا بل ران على قلوبهم ما كانوا يكسبون وقال عز وجل أن لو نشاء أصبناهم بذنبوهم ونطبع على قلوبهم فهم لا يسمعون فربط عدم السماع بالطبع بالذنوب كما ربط السماع بالتقوى فقال تعالى واتقوا الله واسمعوا واتقوا الله ويعلمكم الله ومهما تراكمت الذنوب طبع على القلوب وعند ذلك يعمى القلب عن إدراك الحق وصلاح الدين ويستهين بأمر الآ
7:100.english: As for the blameworthy effects, they are like dark smoke that rises to the mirror of the Heart (Qalb) and continues to accumulate upon it time after time until it blackens and darkens and becomes completely veiled from Allah the Exalted, and this is the Sealing (Al-Tab') and the Rust (Al-Rayn). Allah the Exalted said: 'No! Rather, what they have earned has rusted upon their hearts.' And He the Mighty and Majestic said: 'Or has it not been made clear to those who inherit the earth after its [former] people that if We willed, We could afflict them for their sins and seal over their hearts so they would not hear?' So He linked the lack of hearing to the sealing with sins, just as He linked hearing to God-consciousness (Taqwa), for He the Exalted said: 'And fear Allah and listen, and fear Allah, and Allah will teach you.' Whenever sins accumulate, the hearts are sealed, and at that point the Heart (Qalb) becomes blind to perceiving the Truth (Al-Haqq) and the rectitude of the religion, and it belittles the matter of the Hereafter (Al-Akhirah) and magnifies the matter of the Worldly Life (Al-Dunya), and its concern becomes restricted to it. So when its hearing is struck by the matter of the Hereafter and the dangers within it, it enters from one ear and exits from the other, and it does not settle in the Heart (Qalb) and does not move it to repentance (Al-Tawbah) and rectification. Those are the ones who have despaired of the Hereafter (Al-Akhirah) just as the disbelievers despair of the companions of the graves. And this is the meaning of the blackening of the Heart (Qalb) by sins, as articulated by the Quran and the Sunnah.
7:100.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

7:104.arabic: فإنه يوشك أن يأتيك رسول من رب العالمين يزيلك عن سريرك ويخرجك من سعة قصرك إلى ضيق قبرك
7:104.english: For indeed, it is imminent that a messenger from the Lord of the Worlds (Rabb al-'Alamin) will come to you, removing you from your throne and taking you out from the spaciousness of your palace to the narrowness of your grave.
7:104.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

7:124.arabic: وما مثال المكاشفين والمعتقدين إلا كسحرة فرعون مع أصحاب السامري؛ فإن سحرة فرعون لما كانوا مطلعين على منتهى تأثير السحر لطول مشاهدتهم وتجربتهم رأوا من موسى عليه السلام ما جاوز حدود السحر وانكشف لهم حقيقة الأمر فلم يكترثوا بقول فرعون "لأقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف" بل "قالوا لن نؤثرك على ما جاءنا من البينات والذي فطرنا فاقض ما أنت قاض إنما تقضي هذه الحياة الدنيا" فإن البيان والكشف يمنع التغيير
7:124.english: And the example of those who have spiritual unveiling (Mukāshifīn) and those who merely believe (Muʿtaqidīn) is none other than like the magicians of Pharaoh with the followers of the Sāmirī; for the magicians of Pharaoh, since they were aware of the ultimate effect of magic due to their prolonged witnessing and experience, saw from Moses, peace be upon him, what exceeded the limits of magic, and the truth of the matter was unveiled to them, so they did not heed the saying of Pharaoh: "I will surely cut off your hands and your feet from opposite sides" but rather "they said: 'We will never prefer you over what has come to us of clear proofs and He who created us. So decree whatever you are to decree. You can only decree for this worldly life.'" For clear demonstration and unveiling (Kashf) prevent change.
7:124.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

7:126.arabic: يا من لا تضره الذنوب ولا تنقصه المغفرة هب لي ما لا يضرك وأعطني ما لا ينقصك ربنا أفرغ علينا صبرا وتوفنا مسلمين أنت ولي في الدنيا والآخرة توفنى مسلما وألحقنى بالصالحين أنت ولينا فاغفر لنا وارحمنا وأنت خير الغافرين واكتب لنا في هذه الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة إنا هدنا إليك ربنا عليك توكلنا وإليك أنبنا وإليك المصير ربنا لا تجعلنا فتنة للقوم الظالمين ربنا لا تجعلنا فتنة للذين كفروا واغفر لنا ربنا إنك أنت العزيز الحكيم ربنا اغفر لنا ذنوبنا وإسرافنا في أمرنا وثبت أقدامنا وانصرنا على القوم الكافرين ربنا اغفر
7:126.english: O You whom sins do not harm and forgiveness does not diminish, grant me what does not harm You and give me what does not diminish You. Our Lord, pour upon us patience (Sabr) and cause us to die as Muslims (Muslimin). You are the Guardian (Wali) in this world and the Hereafter.
