Indeed, Allah the Exalted said in some of the ancient books: O son of Adam, remember Me when you are angry, I will remember you when I am angry, so I will not annihilate you among those I annihilate. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a servant for a need, and he delayed upon him, so when he came, he said: "Were it not for retribution, I would have hurt you"[22] meaning retribution on the Day of Resurrection. And it was said: There was no king among the Children of Israel except that with him was a wise man; when he became angry, he would give him a scroll in which was written: Have mercy on the poor, fear death, and remember the Hereafter, and he would read it until his anger subsided. The third: That he warns his Soul (Nafs) of the consequence of enmity and revenge, and the enemy prepares to confront him and strives to destroy his purposes and gloat over his calamities, and he is not free from calamities, so he frightens his Soul (Nafs) with the consequences of anger in this world if he does not fear from the Hereafter. And this returns to unleashing desire.
7:199.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

7:200.arabic: وإنه مهما دفع الوساوس كلها ورد النفس إلى هذه الكلمة جاءته الوساوس من هذه الكلمة، وأنها: ما هي؟ وما معنى قولنا: الله؟ ولأي معنى كان إلهاً وكان معبوداً؟ ويعتريه عند ذلك خواطر تفتح عليه باب الفكر وربما يرد عليه من وساوس الشيطان ما هو كفر وبدعة. ومهما كان كارهاً لذلك ومتشمراً لإماطته عن القلب لم يضره ذلك. وهي منقسمة إلى ما يعلم قطعاً أن الله تعالى منزه عنه ولكن الشيطان يلقي ذلك في قلبه ويجريه على خاطره، فشرطه أن يبالي به ويفزع إلى ذكر الله تعالى ويبتهل إليه ليدفعه عنه كما قال الله تعالى "وإما ينزغنك
7:200.english: And if he repels all the whisperings and returns the Soul (Nafs) to this word, whisperings come to him from this word, and they are: What is it? And what is the meaning of our saying: Allah? And for what meaning was He a deity (Ilah) and was worshipped? And there befalls him at that time thoughts that open upon him the door of reflection, and perhaps there comes to him from the whisperings of Satan what is disbelief and innovation. And however much he is averse to that and prepared to remove it from the Heart (Qalb), it does not harm him. And they are divided into what he knows decisively that Allah the Exalted is free from it, but Satan casts that in his heart and runs it on his thought, so his condition is that he should care about it and flee to the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah the Exalted and beseech Him to repel it from him, as Allah the Exalted said: "And if an incitement from Satan incites you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is Hearing, Knowing." And He said: "Indeed, those who fear Allah, when an impulse from Satan touches them, they remember, and at once they see clearly." And into what he doubts about, then he should present that to his spiritual guide (Shaykh), rather everything he finds in his heart from the states of slackness or vigor or attention to an attachment or truthfulness in intention, then he should manifest that to his spiritual guide (Shaykh), and conceal it from others so that he does not inform anyone about it. Then his spiritual guide (Shaykh) looks at his condition and contemplates his intelligence and cleverness, so if he knows that if he leaves him and commands him with reflection, he awakens from himself to the reality of the Truth, then he should refer him to reflection and command him to adhere to it until there is cast in his heart from the light what unveils to him its reality. And if he knows that that is from what one like him cannot bear, he returns him to the decisive belief with what his heart can bear from admonition and that is evidence close to his understanding. And it is built that the spiritual guide (Shaykh) should be meticulous and gentle with him, for these are the perils of the path and places of its dangers.
7:200.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

7:201.arabic: فحق على العبد أن يقف عند كل هم يخطر له ليعلم أنه من لمة الملك أو من لمة الشيطان وأن يمعن النظر فيه بعين البصيرة لا بهوى من الطبع ولا يطلع عليه إلا بنور التقوى والبصيرة وغزارة العلم كما قال تعالى إن الذين اتقوا إذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان تذكروا أي رجعوا إلى نور العلم فإذا هم مبصرون أي ينكشف لهم الإشكال فأما من لم يرض نفسه بالتقوى فيميل طبعه إلى الإذعان بتلبيسه بمتابعة الهوى فيكثر فيه غلطه ويتعجل فيه هلاكه وهو لا يشعر وفي مثلهم قال سبحانه وتعالى وبدا لهم من الله ما لم يكونوا يحتسبون قيل هي أعمال ظنو
7:201.english: It is incumbent upon the servant (Al-Abd) to pause at every thought that occurs to him to know whether it is from the inspiration of the angel (Lamat Al-Malak) or from the whisper of the devil (Lamat Al-Shaytan), and to examine it deeply with the eye of insight (Al-Basira) not with the desire (Hawa) of the natural disposition (Al-Tab'), nor can one perceive it except with the light of God-consciousness (Al-Taqwa) and insight (Al-Basira) and abundance of knowledge, as Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, those who are God-conscious (Al-Muttaqun) - when an impulse from Satan touches them, they remember (Tadhakkaru) [Allah] and at once they have insight (Mubsirun).' That is, they return to the light of knowledge, so then they have insight (Mubsirun), meaning the confusion is unveiled for them. As for one who does not satisfy himself with God-consciousness (Al-Taqwa), his natural disposition (Al-Tab') inclines to submitting to its deception by following desire (Al-Hawa), so his error increases in it and his destruction hastens while he is unaware. And concerning their like, He the Exalted said: 'And there will appear to them from Allah that which they had not taken into account.' It is said: they are deeds they thought were good deeds, but they are evil deeds.
7:201.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

7:201.arabic: ولذلك قال الله تعالى إن الذين اتقوا إذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان تذكروا فإذا هم مبصرون خصص بذلك المتقى فمثل الشيطان كمثل كلب جائع يقرب منك فإن لم يكن بين يديك خبز أو لحم فإنه ينزجر بأن تقول له اخسأ فمجرد الصوت يدفعه فإن كان بين يديك لحم وهو جائع فإنه يهجم على اللحم ولا يندفع بمجرد الكلام فالقلب الخالي عن قوت الشيطان ينزجر عنه بمجرد الذكر فأما الشهوة إذا غلبت على القلب دفعت حقيقة الذكر إلى حواشي القلب فلم يتمكن من سويدائه فيستقر الشيطان في سويداء القلب وأما قلوب المتقين الخالية من الهوى والصفات المذم
7:201.english: And therefore Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, those who are God-fearing (ittaqaw) when a passing thought (ta'if) from Satan touches them, they remember (tadhakkaru), then indeed they become seeing (mubsirun).' He specified that for the God-fearing (muttaqin). So the likeness of Satan is like a hungry dog that approaches you. If there is no bread or meat before you, then it is repelled by you saying to it: 'Go away!' Mere sound repels it. But if there is meat before you and it is hungry, then it attacks the meat and is not repelled by mere speech. So the Heart (Qalb) empty from the sustenance of Satan is repelled from it by mere Remembrance (Dhikr). As for the desire (shahwa) when it overcomes the Heart, it pushes the reality of the Remembrance to the peripheries of the Heart, so it does not reach its core (sawad), and Satan settles in the core of the Heart. But as for the hearts of the God-fearing (muttaqin), empty from caprice (hawa) and blameworthy traits, Satan approaches them not for desires but because of their emptiness due to heedlessness (ghafla) from the Remembrance. So when it returns to the Remembrance, Satan retreats. And evidence for that is His saying: 'So seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed,' and the rest of the reports and verses that have come regarding the Remembrance.
7:201.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

7:201.arabic: ولا يمحو وسوسة الشيطان من القلب إلا ذكر ما سوى ما يوسوس به لأنه إذا خطر في القلب ذكر شيء انعدم منه ما كان فيه من قبل ولكن كل شيء سوى الله تعالى وسوى ما يتعلق به فيجوز أيضا أن يكون مجالا للشيطان وذكر الله هو الذي يؤمن جانبه ويعلم أنه ليس للشيطان فيه مجال ولا يعالج الشيء إلا بضده وضد جميع وساوس الشيطان ذكر الله بالاستعاذة والتبري عن الحول والقوة وهو معنى قولك أعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله العلي العظيم وذلك لا يقدر عليه إلا المتقون الغالب عليهم ذكر الله تعالى وإنما الشيطان
7:201.english: And nothing erases the whispering (waswasa) of the Satan (Shaytan) from the Heart (Qalb) except the remembrance (dhikr) of something other than what he whispers about, because when the remembrance of something occurs in the Heart, what was previously in it disappears. However, everything besides Allah the Exalted and besides what is connected to Him may also be a field for the Satan, and the remembrance of Allah is what secures his side and makes known that there is no field for the Satan in it. And nothing is treated except by its opposite, and the opposite of all the whisperings of the Satan is the remembrance of Allah through seeking refuge (isti'adha) and disavowing power and strength, which is the meaning of your saying: 'I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan' and 'There is no power nor strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Most Great.' And that is not within the capability except of the God-fearing (muttaqun) upon whom the remembrance of Allah the Exalted predominates. Indeed, the Satan only circles around them at times of lapses (faltat) by way of stealth. Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, those who fear Allah (ittaqaw) - when an impulse (ta'if) from Satan touches them, they remember (tadhakkaru) and then they see clearly (mubsirun).' And Mujahid said regarding the meaning of the saying of Allah the Exalted: 'From the evil of the whisperer (waswas) who withdraws (khannas)' - he said: 'He spreads out over the Heart, so when Allah the Exalted is remembered, he withdraws (khanasa) and contracts, and when one is heedless (ghafil), he spreads out over his heart.' So the chasing away between the remembrance of Allah the Exalted and the whispering of the Satan is like the chasing away between light (nur) and darkness (zalam), and between night (layl) and day (nahar). And due to their opposition, Allah the Exalted said: 'Satan has gained mastery over them and made them forget the remembrance of Allah.'
7:201.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

7:201.arabic: ومهما كان كارهاً لذلك ومتشمراً لإماطته عن القلب لم يضره ذلك. وهي منقسمة إلى ما يعلم قطعاً أن الله تعالى منزه عنه ولكن الشيطان يلقي ذلك في قلبه ويجريه على خاطره، فشرطه أن يبالي به ويفزع إلى ذكر الله تعالى ويبتهل إليه ليدفعه عنه كما قال الله تعالى "وإما ينزغنك من الشيطان نزغ فاستعذ بالله إنه سميع عليم" وقال تعالى "إن الذين اتقوا إذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان تذكروا فإذا هم مبصرون" وإلى ما يشك فيه فينبغي أن يعرض ذلك على شيخه، بل كل ما يجد في قلبه من الأحوال من فترة أو نشاط أو التفات إلى علقة أو صدق في إ
7:201.english: And whenever he is averse to that and strives to remove it from the Heart (Qalb), it does not harm him. And it is divided into what he knows with certainty that Allah the Exalted is free from, but the Satan casts that into his Heart (Qalb) and runs it through his thought, so his condition is that he should care about it and flee to the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah the Exalted and beseech Him to repel it from him, as Allah the Exalted said: "And if an evil whisper from the Satan tries to turn you away (O Muhammad), then seek refuge in Allah. Verily, He is the All-Hearer, the All-Knower" and He said: "Indeed, those who are God-fearing (Muttaqun) when a touch from the Satan touches them, they remember, then behold, they are seeing clearly." And as for what he doubts about, then he should present that to his spiritual guide (Shaykh), rather everything he finds in his Heart (Qalb) of states from slackness or activity or attention to an attachment or sincerity in intention, he should manifest that to his spiritual guide (Shaykh), and conceal it from others so that no one becomes aware of it. Then his spiritual guide (Shaykh) looks at his condition and contemplates his intelligence and cleverness, so if he knows that if he leaves him and commands him with reflection, he will awaken from himself to the reality of the Truth (Haqq), then he should refer him to reflection and command him to adhere to it until there is cast into his Heart (Qalb) from the Light (Nur) what unveils for him its reality. And if he knows that that is something his like cannot bear, he returns him to the decisive belief with what his Heart (Qalb) can bear of admonition and that is evidence close to his understanding. And it is built that the spiritual guide (Shaykh) should be refined and gentle with him, for these are the perils of the path and the places of its dangers.
7:201.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

7:201.arabic: فمثل الإيمان فيه كمثل البقلة يمدها الماء الطيب ومثل النفاق فيه كمثل القرحة يمدها القيح والصديد فأي المادتين غلبت عليه حكم له بها وفي رواية ذهبت به قال الله تعالى إن الذين اتقوا إذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان تذكروا فإذا هم مبصرون فأخبر أن جلاء القلب وإبصاره يحصل بالذكر وأنه لا يتمكن منه إلا الذين اتقوا فالتقوى باب الذكر والذكر باب الكشف والكشف باب الفوز الأكبر وهو الفوز بلقاء الله تعالى.
7:201.english: So the likeness of faith in it is like a plant that pure water nourishes, and the likeness of hypocrisy in it is like an ulcer that pus and discharge nourish, so whichever of the two nourishments overcomes him, he is judged by it, and in a narration: it took him away. Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, those who are God-fearing (ittaqaw) when a passing thought (ta'if) from the Satan touches them, they remember (tadhakkaru), then behold, they are seeing clearly (mubsirun).' So He informed that the polishing (jala') of the heart (qalb) and its clear-sightedness (ibsar) occurs through the remembrance (dhikr), and that none can attain it except those who are God-fearing (ittaqaw). So God-fearingness (taqwa) is the gate of remembrance (dhikr), and remembrance (dhikr) is the gate of unveiling (kashf), and unveiling (kashf) is the gate of the greatest success (fawz al-akbar), which is success in meeting Allah the Exalted.
7:201.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

7:205.arabic: وقال عز وجل: ﴿ واذكر ربك في نفسك تضرّعاً وخيفةً  ودون  الجهر  من  القول  بالغدو والآصال ولا تكن من الغافلين ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ ولذكر الله أكبر ﴾ {} قال  ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: له وجهان أحدهما أن ذكر الله تعالى  لكم  أعظم  من  ذكركم إياه والآخر أن ذكر الله أعظم من كل عبادة سواه إلى غير ذلك  من  الآيات.
7:205.english: And He, the Exalted, said: 'And remember your Lord (Rabb) within your Soul (Nafs) with humility (Tadarru') and fear (Khifah) and without loudness in speech in the morning (Ghuduww) and the evening (Asal) and do not be among the heedless (Ghafilin).' And He, the Exalted, said: 'And the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah is greater.' Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: It has two aspects: one is that the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah, the Exalted, for you is greater than your remembrance of Him, and the other is that the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah is greater than every worship besides it, among other verses.
7:205.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith

8:1.arabic: ثم قال رسول الله ﷺ عند ذلك اتقوا الله وأصلحوا ذات بينكم فإن الله يصلح بين المؤمنين[170]) وهذا تنبيه على أن ذلك إنما ينال بالتخلق بأخلاق الله وهو إصلاح ذات البين وسائر الأخلاق فتفكر الآن فى نفسك إن خلت صحيفتك عن المظالم أو تلطف لك حتى عفا عنك وأيقنت بسعادة الأبد كيف يكون سرورك فى منصرفك من مفصل الفضاء وقد خلع عليك خلعة الرضا وعدت بسعادة ليس بعدها شقاء وبنعيم لا يدور بحواشيه الفناء وعند ذلك طار قلبك سرورا وفرحا وابيض وجهك واستنار وأشرق كما يشرق القمر ليلة البدر فتوهم تبخترك بين الخلائق رافعا رأسك
8:1.english: Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said at that: 'Fear Allah (Taqwa) and reconcile matters between yourselves, for indeed Allah reconciles between the believers.'[170] And this is an alert that that is only attained by adorning oneself with the character traits (Akhlaq) of Allah, and it is reconciliation of matters between (people) and the rest of the character traits. So reflect now in your soul (Nafs) if your record is free from injustices, or if you are treated with gentleness until you are forgiven and you become certain of eternal happiness (Sa'ada), how will your joy be upon your departure from the assembly of the open space, and the garment of contentment (Rida) has been bestowed upon you, and you return with a happiness after which there is no misery, and with a bliss (Na'eem) whose edges are not encircled by annihilation. And at that, your heart (Qalb) flew with joy and happiness, and your face whitened and illuminated and shone as the moon shines on the night of the full moon. So imagine yourself strutting among the creation, raising your head, your back free from burdens, and the freshness of the breeze of bliss and the coolness of contentment (Rida) gleams from your forehead, and the creation of the first and the last look at you and at your state and envy you for your goodness and beauty, and the angels walk before you and behind you and proclaim upon the heads of the assemblies: 'This is so-and-so son of so-and-so, may Allah be pleased with him and make him pleased, and he has attained a happiness after which he will never be miserable forever.' Do you think that this station is not greater than the position you attain in the hearts of the creation in the world through your ostentation (Riya'), your flattery, your affectation, and your adornment? If you know that it is better than it, indeed there is no comparison of it to it, then seek to reach this rank through pure sincerity (Ikhlas) and truthful intention (Niyya) in your dealings with Allah, for you will not attain that except through it.
8:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

8:1.arabic: وقوله عز وجل ﴿ لهم مغفرة ورزق كريم. كما أخرجك ربك من بيتك بالحق ﴾ {} فهذا الكلام غير متصل وإنما هو عائد إلى قوله السابق ﴿ قل الانفال لله والرسول. كما أخرجك ربك من بيتك بالحق ﴾ {} أي فصارت أنفال الغنائم لك إذ أنت راض بخروجك وهم كارهون فاعترض بين الكلام الأمر بالتقوى وغيره
8:1.english: And His (Allah's) saying, exalted is He: 'For them is forgiveness and a generous provision. As your Lord brought you out of your home in truth' {} this speech is not connected, but rather it refers back to His preceding saying: 'Say: The spoils (Al-Anfal) are for Allah and the Messenger. As your Lord brought you out of your home in truth' {} meaning: So the spoils of war became for you, since you were content with your departure and they were unwilling, and the command for God-consciousness (Taqwa) and other matters intervened between the speech.
8:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

8:2.arabic: اعلم أن كل إنسان جاهل بعيوب نفسه، فإذا جاهد نفسه أدنى مجاهدة حتى ترك فواحش المعاصي ربما يظن بنفسه أنه هذب نفسه وحسن خلقه واستغنى عن المجاهدة، فلا بد من إيضاح علامة حسن الخلق. فإن حسن الخلق هو الإيمان، وسوء الخلق هو النفاق. وقد ذكر الله تعالى صفات المؤمنين والمنافقين في كتابه وهي بجملتها ثمرة حسن الخلق وسوء الخلق. فلنورد جملة من ذلك لتعلم آية حسن الخلق. قال الله تعالى "قد أفلح المؤمنون الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون والذين هم عن اللغو معرضون" إلى قوله "أولئك هم الوارثون" وقال عز وجل "التائبون العابدون
8:2.english: Know that every human is ignorant of the defects of his own self (Nafs), so if he strives against his self (Nafs) with the slightest striving (Mujahadah) until he abandons the gross sins, perhaps he imagines of his self (Nafs) that he has refined his self (Nafs) and beautified his character (Khuluq) and become independent of striving (Mujahadah). Therefore, it is necessary to clarify the sign of good character (Khuluq). For good character (Khuluq) is faith (Iman), and bad character (Khuluq) is hypocrisy (Nifaq). And Allah the Exalted has mentioned the attributes of the believers (Mu'minun) and the hypocrites (Munafiqun) in His Book, and they are in their entirety the fruit of good character (Khuluq) and bad character (Khuluq). So let us present a collection of that so you may learn the sign of good character (Khuluq). Allah the Exalted said: 'Successful indeed are the believers (Mu'minun) who are humble in their prayers and who turn away from idle talk' to His saying 'Those are the inheritors.' And He the Mighty and Majestic said: 'The repentant, the worshippers, the praisers' to His saying 'and give glad tidings to the believers (Mu'minun).' And He the Mighty and Majestic said: 'Indeed, the believers (Mu'minun) are those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts (Qulub) tremble, and when His verses are recited to them, it increases them in faith (Iman) and upon their Lord they rely' to His saying 'Those are the believers (Mu'minun) in truth.' And He the Exalted said: 'And the servants of the Most Merciful who walk upon the earth easily and when the ignorant address them, they say peace' to the end of the Surah. Whoever is confused about his state, let him present his self (Nafs) to these verses, for the presence of all these attributes is a sign of good character (Khuluq), and the absence of all of them is a sign of bad character (Khuluq), and the presence of some of them without others indicates some without others, so let him occupy himself with acquiring what he lacks and preserving what he has found.
8:2.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

8:2.arabic: قال الله تعالى ﴿ الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم وإذا تليت عليهم آياته زادتهم إيمانا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون ﴾ {} وقال ﭬ: (إن أحسن الناس صوتا بالقرآن الذي إذا سمعته يقرأ رأيت أنه يخشى الله تعالى[44]) وقال ﭬ: (لا يسمع القرآن من أحد أشهى ممن يخشى الله عز وجل[45]) فالقرآن يراد لاستجلاب هذه الأحوال إلى القلب والعمل به وإلا فالمؤنة في تحريك اللسان بحروفه خفيفة
8:2.english: Allah the Exalted said: 'Those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts (Qulub) tremble with awe, and when His verses are recited to them, it increases them in faith (Iman), and upon their Lord they rely (Yatawakkalun).' And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'The best of people in voice with the Quran is the one whom, when you hear him recite, you see that he fears Allah the Exalted.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'No one hears the Quran from anyone more desirable than one who fears Allah the Mighty and Majestic.' So the Quran is intended to attract these states (Ahwal) to the heart (Qalb) and to act upon it; otherwise, the effort in moving the tongue with its letters is light.
8:2.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

8:2.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم وقال تعالى لو أنزلنا هذا القرآن على جبل لرأيته خاشعا متصدعا من خشية الله فالوجل والخشوع وجد من قبيل الأحوال وإن لم يكن من قبيل المكاشفات ولكن قد يصير سببا للمكاشفات والتنبيهات
8:2.english: And Allah the Exalted has said: 'Indeed, the believers are those whose hearts tremble (Wajilat) when Allah is mentioned (Dhikr),' and He said: 'If We had sent down this Quran upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled (Khashi'a) and split asunder from the fear (Khashyah) of Allah.' So the trembling (Wajal) and the humility (Khushu') are a state (Hal) from the category of states (Ahwal), even if it is not from the category of unveilings (Mukashafat), but it may become a cause for unveilings (Mukashafat) and alerts (Tanbihat).
8:2.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

8:4.arabic: وقد ذكر الله تعالى صفات المؤمنين والمنافقين في كتابه وهي بجملتها ثمرة حسن الخلق وسوء الخلق. فلنورد جملة من ذلك لتعلم آية حسن الخلق. قال الله تعالى "قد أفلح المؤمنون الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون والذين هم عن اللغو معرضون" إلى قوله "أولئك هم الوارثون" وقال عز وجل "التائبون العابدون الحامدون" إلى قوله "وبشر المؤمنين" وقال عز وجل "إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم" إلى قوله "أولئك هم المؤمنون حقاً" وقال تعالى "وعباد الرحمن الذين يمشون على الأرض هوناً وإذا خاطبهم الجاهلون قالوا سلاما" إلى آخر
8:4.english: And Allah the Exalted has mentioned the attributes of the believers and the hypocrites in His Book, and they are in their entirety the fruit of good character and bad character. So let us present a summary of that to know the sign of good character. Allah the Exalted said: "Successful indeed are the believers who are humble in their prayers and who turn away from idle talk" up to His saying "Those are the inheritors." And He the Mighty and Majestic said: "The repentant, the worshippers, the praisers" up to His saying "and give glad tidings to the believers." And He the Mighty and Majestic said: "The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble" up to His saying "Those are the believers in truth (أولئك هم المؤمنون حقاً)." And He the Exalted said: "And the servants of the Most Merciful who walk upon the earth easily and when the ignorant address them, they say peace" up to the end of the surah.
8:4.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

8:4.arabic: الوجه الثالث: مستنده الشك ومعناه أنا مؤمن حقا إن شاء الله إذ قال الله تعالى لقوم مخصوصين بأعيانهم: ﴿ أولئك هم المؤمنون حقا ﴾ {} فانقسموا إلى قسمين ويرجع هذا إلى الشك في كمال الإيمان لا في أصله وكل إنسان شاك في كمال إيمانه وذلك ليس بكفر والشك في كمال الإيمان حق من وجهين: أحدهما من حيث إن النفاق يزيل كمال الإيمان وهو خفي لا تتحقق البراءة منه. والثاني: أنه يكمل بأعمال الطاعات ولا يدري وجودها على الكمال أما العمل فقد قال الله تعالى: ﴿ إنما المؤمنون الذين آمنوا بالله ورسوله ثم لم يرتابوا وجاهدوا بأمو
8:4.english: The third aspect: its basis is doubt and its meaning is 'I am a true believer (Mu'min Haqqan) if Allah wills,' since Allah the Exalted said to a specific group of individuals: 'Those are the true believers (Mu'minun Haqqan)' (Quran 8:4). They divided into two categories, and this refers to doubt about the perfection of faith (Iman) not its foundation. Every person doubts the perfection of their faith (Iman), and that is not disbelief (Kufr). Doubt about the perfection of faith (Iman) is valid from two perspectives: First, because hypocrisy (Nifaq) removes the perfection of faith (Iman), and it is hidden such that one cannot ascertain freedom from it. Second, it is perfected through acts of obedience (Ta'at), and one does not know if they exist in perfection. As for action, Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, the believers (Mu'minun) are those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and then doubt not but strive with their properties and their selves in the cause of Allah. It is those who are the truthful (Sadiqun)' (Quran 49:15). Thus, doubt arises about this truthfulness (Sidq). Similarly, Allah the Exalted said: 'But righteousness (Al-Birr) is [in] one who believes in Allah, the Last Day, the angels, the Book, and the prophets' (Quran 2:177). He stipulated twenty descriptions such as fulfilling the covenant and patience in hardships, then said: 'Those are the ones who have been truthful (Sadaqu)' (Quran 2:177). And He said: 'Allah will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge by degrees' (Quran 58:11). And He said: 'Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought' (Quran 57:10) the verse. And He said: 'They are degrees with Allah' (Quran 8:4). And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Faith (Iman) is naked, and its garment is piety (Taqwa)' (Hadith). And he said: 'Faith (Iman) has seventy-odd branches, the lowest of which is removing harm from the road' (Hadith). This indicates the connection of...
8:4.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Foundations of Belief'

8:5.arabic: وقوله عز وجل ﴿ لهم مغفرة ورزق كريم. كما أخرجك ربك من بيتك بالحق ﴾ {} فهذا الكلام غير متصل وإنما هو عائد إلى قوله السابق ﴿ قل الانفال لله والرسول. كما أخرجك ربك من بيتك بالحق ﴾ {} أي فصارت أنفال الغنائم لك إذ أنت راض بخروجك وهم كارهون فاعترض بين الكلام الأمر بالتقوى وغيره
8:5.english: And His saying, the Exalted and Majestic: 'For them is forgiveness and a noble provision. As your Lord brought you out of your home with the truth' {} This speech is not connected, but rather it refers back to His previous saying: 'Say: The spoils of war are for Allah and the Messenger. As your Lord brought you out of your home with the truth' {} Meaning: So the spoils of war became for you since you were content with your departure and they were averse. The command for piety and other matters intervened between the speech.
8:5.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

8:15.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
8:15.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Whatever is in the Quran of 'O you who have believed' is in the Torah 'O you poor ones'.
8:15.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

8:17.arabic: أما صريح الحق: فهو أنك وقدرتك وإرادتك وحركتك وجميع ذلك من خلق الله واختراعه، فما عملت إذ عملت وما صليت إذ صليت "وما رميت إذ رميت ولكن الله رمى" فهذا هو الحق الذي انكشف لأرباب القلوب بمشاهدة أوضح من إبصار العين، بل خلقك وخلق أعضاءك وخلق فيها القوة والقدرة والصحة، وخلق لك العقل والعلم وخلق لك الإرادة، ولو أردت أن تنفي شيئاً من هذا عن نفسك لم تقدر عليه، ثم خلق الحركات في أعضائك مستبداً باختراعها من غير مشاركة من جهتك معه في الاختراع، إلا أنه خلقه على ترتيب فلم يخلق الحركة ما لم يخلق في العضو قوة وف
8:17.english: As for the plain truth: it is that you and your power (Qudrah) and your will (Iradah) and your movement (Harakah) and all of that are from the creation (Khalq) of Allah and His invention (Ikhtera'), so you did not act when you acted and you did not pray when you prayed "And you did not throw when you threw but Allah threw" (Quran 8:17) - this is the truth that has been unveiled to the possessors of hearts (Arbab al-Qulub) through witnessing (Mushahadah) clearer than the sight of the eye. Rather, He created you and created your limbs and created in them the strength (Quwwah) and the power (Qudrah) and the health (Sihhah), and created for you the intellect (Aql) and the knowledge (Ilm) and created for you the will (Iradah). If you wanted to deny anything of this from yourself, you would not be able to do so. Then He created the movements in your limbs, being independent in inventing them without any partnership from your side with Him in the invention, except that He created it in an order: He did not create the movement unless He created in the limb strength and in the heart (Qalb) will, and He did not create will unless He created knowledge of what is intended, and He did not create knowledge unless He created the heart which is the place (Mahall) of knowledge. So His gradual creation (Tadreej) in creation thing after thing is what deluded you into thinking that you brought your action into existence, and you have erred.
8:17.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

8:17.arabic: ركبوا في الفلك دعوا الله مخلصين له الدين فلما نجاهم إلى البر إذا هم يشركون " قيل: معناه أنهم يقولون لولا استواء الريح لما نجونا. ومن انكشف له أمر العالم كما هو عليه علم أن الريح هو الهواء والهواء لا يتحرك ما لم يحركه محرك، وكذلك محركه، وهكذا إلى أن ينتهي إلى المحرك الأول الذي لا محرك له ولا هو متحرك في نفسه عز وجل؛ فالتفات العبد في النجاة إلى الريح يضاهي التفات من أخذ لتحز رقبته فكتب الملك توقيعاً بالعفو عنه وتخليته، فأخذ يشتغل بذكر الحبر والكاغد والقلم الذي به كتب التوقيع يقول: لولا القلم لما ت
8:17.english: They embarked on the ship calling upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion, then when He saved them to the land, behold, they associate partners. It is said: Its meaning is that they say: If not for the wind being favorable, we would not have been saved. And whoever has the matter of the world unveiled to him as it truly is knows that the wind is the air, and the air does not move unless a mover moves it, and likewise its mover, and so on until it ends at the First Mover who has no mover for Him and is not moved in Himself, Glorified and Exalted; so the turning of the servant in salvation to the wind resembles the turning of one who was taken to have his neck severed, then the king wrote a decree of pardon and release for him, so he began to occupy himself with mentioning the ink, the paper, and the pen with which the decree was written, saying: If not for the pen, I would not have been freed, thus seeing his salvation from the pen, not from the mover of the pen, and this is the utmost ignorance. And whoever knows that the pen has no ruling in itself and is only subjugated in the hand of the writer does not turn to it and does not give thanks except to the writer. Rather, perhaps the joy of salvation and gratitude to the king and the writer overwhelms him from that the pen, ink, inkwell, sun, moon, stars, rain, clouds, earth, and every living being and inanimate object, all subjugated in the grasp of the Power (Qudrah) like the subjugation of the pen in the hand of the writer, come to his mind. Rather, this is an analogy regarding you due to your belief that the signing king is the writer of the decree, and the truth is that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is the Writer due to His saying, the Exalted: "And you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw." So if it is unveiled to you that all that is in the heavens and the earth is subjugated in this manner, Satan turns away from you disappointed and despairs of mixing your monotheism (Tawhid) with this association (Shirk). Then he comes to you in the second destruction, which is turning to the choice (Ikhtiyar) of animals in voluntary actions, and says: How do you see everything from Allah when this human gives you your provision by his choice; if he wills, he gives you, and if he wills, he cuts you off. And this person is the one who severs your neck with his sword, and he is capable over you; if he wills, he severs your neck, and if he wills, he pardons you, so how do you not fear him, and how do you not hope in him when your affair is in his hand and you witness that and do not doubt it? And he also says to him: Yes, if you do not see the pen because it is subjugated, then how do you not see the writer with the pen who is subjugated to it? And at this, the feet of most slip except the sincere servants (Ibad) of Allah over whom the accursed Satan has no authority, for they witnessed with the light of insights (Basa'ir) that the writer is subjugated, compelled, just as all the weak witnessed that the pen is subjugated, and they knew that the mistake of the weak in that is like the mistake of an ant, for example, if it were crawling on the paper and sees the tip of the pen blackening the paper, and its sight did not extend to the hand and fingers, let alone the possessor of the hand, so it erred and thought the pen is the one that blackens the whiteness, and that is due to the deficiency of its sight from exceeding the tip of the pen because of the narrowness of its pupil, so likewise whoever has not.
8:17.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

8:17.arabic: وإذا حصل السماع بأمثال هذه الأمور علم ظاهر التفسير وهو ترجمة الألفاظ ولا يكفى ذلك في فهم حقائق المعاني ويدرك الفرق بين حقائق المعاني وظاهر التفسير بمثال وهو أن الله عز وجل قال ﴿ وما رميت إذ رميت ولكن الله رمى ﴾ فظاهره تفسير واضح وحقيقة معناه غامض فإنه إثبات للرمي ونفي له وهما متضادان في الظاهر ما لم يفهم أنه رمى من وجه ولم يرم من وجه ومن الوجه الذي لم يرم رماه الله عز وجل وكذلك قال تعالى ﴿ قاتلوهم يعذبهم الله بأيديكم ﴾ فإذا كانوا هم المقاتلين كيف يكون الله سبحانه هو المعذب وإن كان الله تعالى هو
8:17.english: And when hearing is obtained regarding such matters, the apparent interpretation (Tafsir) is known, which is the translation of the words, and that is not sufficient for understanding the realities of the meanings. And the difference between the realities of the meanings and the apparent interpretation is understood with an example, which is that Allah the Exalted said: 'And you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw.' So its apparent meaning is a clear interpretation, but the reality of its meaning is obscure, for it is an affirmation of throwing and a denial of it, and they are contradictory in appearance unless it is understood that he threw from one aspect and did not throw from another aspect, and from the aspect from which he did not throw, Allah the Exalted threw him. And similarly, Allah the Exalted said: 'Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands.' So if they are the fighters, how can Allah the Glorified be the punisher? And if Allah the Exalted is the punisher by moving their hands, then what is the meaning of commanding them to fight? The reality of this draws from a vast ocean of the sciences of unveilings (Mukashafat), which the apparent interpretation cannot suffice for. It is to know the aspect of connection of actions with the originated power (Qudrah Hadithah) and to understand the aspect of connection of the power with the power of Allah the Exalted, until after clarifying many obscure matters, the truth of His saying the Exalted is unveiled: 'And you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw.' And perhaps if a lifetime were spent in exploring the secrets of this meaning and what is connected to its premises and consequences, the lifetime would end before completing all its consequences.
8:17.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

8:17.arabic: وقال تعالى: " قاتلوهم يعذبهم الله بأيديكم " فأضاف القتل إليهم والتعذيب إلى نفسه، والتعذيب هو عين القتل، بل صرح وقال تعالى: " فلم تقتلوهم ولكن الله قتلهم ", وقال تعالى: " وما رميت إذا رميت ولكن الله رمى " وهو جمع بين النفي والإثبات ظاهراً، ولكن معناه: وما رميت بالمعنى الذي يكون الرب به رامياً إذ رميت بالمعنى الذي يكون العبد به رامياً، إذ هما معنيان مختلفان.
8:17.english: And He (Allah), the Exalted, said: 'Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands' - thus attributing the killing to them and the punishment to Himself, and the punishment is precisely the killing. Indeed, He explicitly stated and said: 'So you did not kill them, but Allah killed them', and He said: 'And you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw' - which combines negation and affirmation in appearance, but its meaning is: And you did not throw in the sense that makes the Lord (Rabb) the thrower, when you threw in the sense that makes the servant (Abd) the thrower, for they are two different meanings.
8:17.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

8:17.arabic: وقال تعالى: " قاتلوهم يعذبهم الله بأيديكم " فأضاف القتل إليهم والتعذيب إلى نفسه، والتعذيب هو عين القتل، بل صرح وقال تعالى: " فلم تقتلوهم ولكن الله قتلهم "، وقال تعالى: " وما رميت إذا رميت ولكن الله رمى " وهو جمع بين النفي والإثبات ظاهراً، ولكن معناه: وما رميت بالمعنى الذي يكون الرب به رامياً إذ رميت بالمعنى الذي يكون العبد به رامياً، إذ هما معنيان مختلفان.
8:17.english: And He (Exalted is He) said: "Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands" - thus attributing the killing to them and the punishment to Himself, and the punishment is the very killing. Indeed, He explicitly stated and said: "So you did not kill them, but Allah killed them", and He said: "And you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw" - which combines negation and affirmation apparently, but its meaning is: And you did not throw in the sense that makes the Lord the thrower when you threw in the sense that makes the servant the thrower, for they are two different meanings.
8:17.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

8:20.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
8:20.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Whatever is in the Quran of 'O you who have believed' is in the Torah 'O you poor ones'.
8:20.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

8:24.arabic: ومن جهل قلبه فهو بغيره أجهل إذ أكثر الخلق جاهلون بقلوبهم وأنفسهم وقد حيل بينهم وبين أنفسهم فإن الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه وحيلولته بأن يمنعه عن مشاهدته ومراقبته ومعرفة صفاته وكيفية تقلبه بين أصبعين مع أصابع الرحمن وأنه كيف يهوي مرة إلى أسفل السافلين وينخفض إلى أفق الشياطين وكيف يرتفع أخرى إلى أعلى عليين ويرتقي إلى عالم الملائكة المقربين ومن لم يعرف قلبه ليراقبه ويراعيه ويترصد لما يلوح من خزائن الملكوت عليه وفيه فهو ممن قال الله تعالى فيه نسوا الله فأنساهم أنفسهم أولئك هم الفاسقون فمعرفة القلب وحق
8:24.english: And whoever is ignorant of his Heart (Qalb) is more ignorant of other things, since most of creation are ignorant of their hearts and their selves (Anfus), and a barrier has been placed between them and their selves. For indeed Allah places a barrier between the person and his heart, and His placing of a barrier is by preventing him from witnessing it, observing it, and knowing its attributes and how it fluctuates between two fingers among the fingers of the Most Merciful, and how it sometimes descends to the lowest of the low and sinks to the horizon of the devils, and how at other times it rises to the highest heights and ascends to the world of the angels brought near. And whoever does not know his heart to observe it, care for it, and watch for what appears from the treasures of the dominion upon it and within it, he is among those about whom Allah the Exalted said: 'They forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves. Those are the defiantly disobedient.' So knowledge of the Heart and the reality of its attributes is the foundation of the religion and the basis of the path of the travelers.
8:24.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

8:24.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
8:24.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'What is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)".'
8:24.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

8:25.arabic: فهذا يدل على أن من بلي ببلدة تكثر فيها المعاصي ويقل فيها الخير فلا عذر له في المقام بها، بل ينبغي أن يهاجر قال الله تعالى " ألم تكن أرض الله واسعة فتهاجروا فيها " فإن منعه عن ذلك عيال أو علاقة فلا ينبغي أن يكون راضياً بحاله مطمئن النفس إليه، بل ينبغي أن يكون منزعج القلب منها قائلاً على الدوام " ربنا أخرجنا من هذه القرية الظالم أهلها " وذلك لأن الظلم إذا عم نزل البلاء ودمر الجميع وشمل المطيعين، قال الله تعالى: " واتقوا فتنة لا تصيبن الذين ظلموا منكم خاصة " فإذن ليس في شيء من أسباب نقص الدين البتة
8:25.english: This indicates that whoever is afflicted with a town where sins are abundant and good is scarce has no excuse for residing there; rather, he should emigrate. Allah the Exalted said: 'Was not the earth of Allah spacious enough for you to emigrate therein?' If he is prevented from that by dependents or ties, he should not be content with his state, at peace in his soul (Nafs) with it; rather, he should be disturbed in his heart (Qalb) from it, saying constantly: 'Our Lord, take us out of this town whose people are wrongdoers.' This is because when injustice becomes widespread, calamity descends and destroys everyone, encompassing the obedient. Allah the Exalted said: 'And fear a trial (Fitnah) that will not afflict those who have wronged among you exclusively.' Therefore, there is absolutely no absolute contentment in any of the causes of deficiency in religion except from the perspective of attributing them to the action of Allah the Exalted; as for them in themselves, there is no aspect for contentment with them in any state.
8:25.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

8:27.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
8:27.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'What is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)".'
8:27.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

8:28.arabic: ولما فتحت ابواب الدنيا على الصحابة رضي الله عنهم قالوا ابتلينا بفتنة الضراء فصبرنا وابتلينا بفتنة السراء فلم نصبر ولذلك حذر الله عباده من فتنة المال والزوج والولد فقال تعالى: ﴿ يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تلهكم أموالكم ولا أولادكم عن ذكر الله ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل: ﴿ ان من أزواجكم وأولادكم عدوا لكم فاحذروهم ﴾ {} وقال ﭬ: (الولد مبخلة مجبنة محزنة[19]). (ولما نظر عليه السلام الى ولده الحسن رضي الله عنه يتعثر في قميصه نزل عن المنبر واحتضنه ثم قال صدق الله ﴿ إنما اموالكم واولادكم فتنة ﴾ {} اني لما رأيت ابني يت
8:28.english: And when the doors of the world were opened upon the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them), they said: 'We were tested with the trial (fitnah) of hardship, so we were patient, and we were tested with the trial (fitnah) of ease, so we were not patient.' Therefore, Allah warned His servants from the trial (fitnah) of wealth, spouse, and children, so He, the Exalted, said: 'O you who have believed, let not your wealth and your children divert you from the remembrance (dhikr) of Allah' (Quran 63:9). And He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them' (Quran 64:14). And he (the Prophet, peace be upon him) said: 'The child is a miser-maker, a coward-maker, a sorrow-maker.' And when he (the Prophet, peace be upon him) looked at his son Al-Hasan (may Allah be pleased with him) stumbling in his shirt, he descended from the pulpit and embraced him, then said: 'Allah has spoken the truth: "And know that your wealth and your children are a trial (fitnah)" (Quran 8:28). Indeed, when I saw my son stumbling, I could not control my soul (nafs) from taking him.' In that is a lesson for those of insight.
8:28.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

8:28.arabic: فإن قلت: فقد أدخلت المال والجاه والنسب والأهل والولد في حيز النعم، وقد ذم الله تعالى المال والجاه وكذا رسول ﭬ[72] وكذا العلماء قال تعالى: ﴿ إن من أزواجكم وأولادكم عدوا لكم فاحذروهم ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل: ﴿ إنما أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة ﴾ {}. وقال علي كرم الله وجهه في ذم النسب: الناس أبناء ما يحسنون وقيمة كل امرىء ما يحسنه، وقيل المرء بنفسه لا بأبيه فما معنى كونها نعمة مع كونها مذمومة شرعا. فاعلم أن من يأخذ العلوم من الألفاظ المنقولة المؤولة والعمومات المخصصة كان الضلال عليه اغلب ما لم يهتد بنور الله تعا
8:28.english: If you say: You have included wealth, status, lineage, family, and children within the realm of blessings, yet Allah the Exalted has censured wealth and status, and likewise the Messenger (peace be upon him) and the scholars. Allah said: 'Indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them' (64:14). And the Almighty said: 'And know that your wealth and your children are a trial (Fitnah)' (8:28). And Ali (may Allah honor his face) said in censuring lineage: 'People are children of what they excel at, and the value of every person is what he excels at,' and it is said: 'A person is by himself, not by his father.' So what is the meaning of them being a blessing while being censured religiously? Know that whoever takes knowledge from transmitted words that are interpreted and generalities that are specified, misguidance is more prevalent upon him unless he is guided by the light (Nur) of Allah the Exalted to comprehend the sciences as they truly are, then he applies the transmission in accordance with what has become clear to him from them through interpretation at times and specification at others. These are blessings that assist in the matter of the Hereafter, with no way to deny them except that they contain trials (Fitnah) and fears. The example of wealth is like a snake that contains beneficial antidote (Tiryaq) and beneficial poison. If it is obtained by the charmer who knows the method of precaution from its poison and the way to extract its beneficial antidote, it is a blessing. But if it is obtained by the ignorant black person, it is upon him calamity and destruction. And it is like the sea beneath which are varieties of jewels and pearls. Whoever attains the sea, if he is knowledgeable in swimming, the way of diving, and the way of precaution from the perils of the sea, he has attained its blessings. But if he enters it ignorant of that, he has perished. Therefore, Allah the Exalted praised wealth and called it good, and the Messenger (peace be upon him) praised it and said: 'What an excellent aid to the fear (Taqwa) of Allah the Exalted is wealth.' And likewise, He praised status and honor since Allah the Exalted bestowed upon His Messenger (peace be upon him) by manifesting him...
8:28.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

8:28.arabic: وإسناده صحيح وتعثر الحسن والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على منبره فنزل فحمله وقرأ قوله إنما أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة حديث عثر الحسن وهو على منبره صلى الله عليه وسلم فنزل فحمله وقرأ قوله تعالى إنما أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة أخرجه أصحاب السنن من حديث بريدة في الحسن والحسين معا يمشيان ويعثران قال الترمذي حسن غريب
8:28.english: And its chain is authentic, and Al-Hasan stumbled while the Prophet (peace be upon him) was on his pulpit, so he descended and carried him and recited His saying: 'Indeed, your wealth and your children are a trial (Fitnah).' The hadith: Al-Hasan stumbled while he (peace be upon him) was on his pulpit, so he descended and carried him and recited His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, your wealth and your children are a trial (Fitnah).' It was reported by the compilers of the Sunan from the hadith of Buraidah regarding Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn both walking and stumbling. At-Tirmidhi said: 'Hasan (good) and Gharib (rare).'
8:28.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

8:29.arabic: وقال الله تعالى ومن يتق الله يجعل له مخرجا من الإشكالات والشبه ويرزقه من حيث لا يحتسب يعلمه علما من غير تعلم ويفطنه من غير تجربة وقال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن تتقوا الله يجعل لكم فرقانا قيل نورا يفرق به بين الحق والباطل ويخرج به من الشبهات ولذلك كان صلى الله عليه وسلم يكثر في دعائه من سؤال النور فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم اللهم أعطني نورا وزدني نورا واجعل لي في قلبي نورا وفي قبري نورا وفي سمعي نورا وفي بصري نورا حتى قال في شعري وفي بشري وفي لحمي ودمي وعظامي
8:29.english: And Allah the Exalted said: 'And whoever fears Allah (Yattaqi Allah), He will make for him a way out from difficulties and doubts, and will provide for him from where he does not expect, teaching him knowledge without learning and making him discerning without experience.' And Allah the Exalted said: 'O you who have believed, if you fear Allah (Tattaqū Allāh), He will grant you a criterion (Furqānan),' it is said: a light (Nūran) by which one distinguishes between truth and falsehood and emerges from doubts. Therefore, the Prophet (peace be upon him) frequently asked for light in his supplication, saying: 'O Allah, grant me light, increase me in light, and place for me light in my heart (Qalbī), in my grave, in my hearing, in my sight,' until he said: 'in my hair, in my skin, in my flesh, blood, and bones.'
8:29.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

8:29.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
8:29.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Whatever is in the Quran of 'O you who have believed' is in the Torah 'O you poor ones (al-Masakin)'.
8:29.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

8:38.arabic: إلهنا إنك قلت في كتابك المبين لمحمد خاتم النبيين قل للذين كفروا إن ينتهوا يغفر لهم ما قد سلف فأرضاك عنهم بالإقرار بكلمة التوحيد بعد الجحود وإنا نشهد لك بالتوحيد مخبتين ولمحمد بالرسالة مخلصين فاغفر لنا بهذه الشهادة سوالف الإجرام ولا تجعل حظنا فيه أنقص من حظ من دخل في الإسلام
8:38.english: Our God, You said in Your clear Book to Muhammad, the Seal of the Prophets: 'Say to those who have disbelieved: If they desist, what has passed will be forgiven for them.' So You were pleased with them by the affirmation of the word of Oneness (Tawhid) after denial. And we bear witness to You with Oneness (Tawhid) in humility, and to Muhammad with the Messengership in sincerity. So forgive us through this testimony for past transgressions, and do not make our share in it less than the share of those who entered into Islam.
8:38.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

8:41.arabic: ليلة سبع عشرة من رمضان فهي ليلة صبيحتها يوم الفرقان يوم التقى الجمعان فيه كانت وقعة بدر وقال ابن الزبير رحمه الله هي ليلة القدر.
8:41.english: The night of the seventeenth of Ramadan is the night whose morning is the Day of Distinction (Yawm al-Furqān), the day the two hosts met, in which the Battle of Badr occurred, and Ibn al-Zubayr, may Allah have mercy on him, said it is the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr).
8:41.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

8:42.arabic: ولا يتصور أن يكون ذلك نادرا شاذا وهو مع الندور يتفاوت في القلة والكثرة وإنما تكون كثرته في الأعصار القريبة من أعصار الأنبياء عليهم السلام فلا يزال يزداد العهد طولا وتزداد مثل هذه القلوب قلة إلى أن تقرب الساعة ويقضى الله أمرا كان مفعولا وإنما وجب أن يكون هذا نادرا لأنه مبادى ملك الآخرة والملك عزيز والملوك لا يكثرون فكما لا يكون الفائق في الملك والجمال إلا نادرا وأكثر الناس من دونهم فكذا في ملك الآخرة فإن الدنيا مرآة الآخرة فإنها عبارة عن عالم الشهادة والآخرة عبارة عن عالم الغيب وعالم الشهادة تابع
8:42.english: And it is not conceivable that this would be rare and anomalous, and with the rarity it varies in scarcity and abundance, and its abundance is only in the eras close to the eras of the Prophets, peace be upon them. The interval continues to increase in length, and such hearts increase in scarcity until the Hour approaches and Allah decrees a matter that was to be done. And it was necessary for this to be rare because it is the beginnings of the kingdom of the Hereafter, and the kingdom is mighty, and kings do not abound. Just as the one who excels in kingdom and beauty is only rare, and most people are beneath them, so it is in the kingdom of the Hereafter. For the world is a mirror of the Hereafter, for it is an expression of the world of witnessing, and the Hereafter is an expression of the world of the unseen, and the world of witnessing follows the world of the unseen, just as the image in the mirror follows the image of the viewer in the mirror. And the image in the mirror, even though it is second in the rank of existence, it is foremost in the right of your vision, for you do not see yourself and you see your image in the mirror first, so you know by it your image that is established by you second, by way of imitation. So the heart that follows in existence is followed in the right of knowledge, and the heart that is delayed is advanced, and this is a type of inversion. But inversion and reversal are necessities of this world. Likewise, the world of dominion and witnessing imitates the world of the unseen and the sovereignty. So among people are those for whom the view of consideration is made easy, so he does not look at anything from the world of dominion except that he crosses with it to the world of sovereignty, so his crossing is called a lesson, and the Truth has commanded it, saying: 'So take lesson, O possessors of insight' (Quran 59:2). And among them are those whose insight is blinded, so he does not take lesson, so he is confined in the world of dominion and witnessing, and the doors of Hell will open to his confinement, and this confinement is filled with fire.
8:42.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

8:42.arabic: وقال عز وجل: ﴿ ليهلك من هلك عن بينة ويحيا من حي عن بينة ﴾ {} وقال تعالى هل عندكم من سلطان بهذا أي حجة وبرهان
8:42.english: And the Almighty said: 'So that he who perishes may perish upon a clear evidence (Bayan) and he who lives may live upon a clear evidence (Bayan).' And He said: 'Do you have any authority for this?' meaning proof (Hujjah) and evidence (Burhan).
8:42.topic: Al-Ghazali on the outer and inner dimensions of worship, from 'Foundations of Belief'

8:44.arabic: ولا يتصور أن يكون ذلك نادرا شاذا وهو مع الندور يتفاوت في القلة والكثرة وإنما تكون كثرته في الأعصار القريبة من أعصار الأنبياء عليهم السلام فلا يزال يزداد العهد طولا وتزداد مثل هذه القلوب قلة إلى أن تقرب الساعة ويقضى الله أمرا كان مفعولا وإنما وجب أن يكون هذا نادرا لأنه مبادى ملك الآخرة والملك عزيز والملوك لا يكثرون فكما لا يكون الفائق في الملك والجمال إلا نادرا وأكثر الناس من دونهم فكذا في ملك الآخرة فإن الدنيا مرآة الآخرة فإنها عبارة عن عالم الشهادة والآخرة عبارة عن عالم الغيب وعالم الشهادة تابع
8:44.english: And it is not conceivable that this be rare and exceptional, and with the rarity it varies in scarcity and abundance, and its abundance is only in the eras close to the eras of the Prophets, peace be upon them. The interval continues to increase in length, and such Hearts (Qalb) increase in scarcity until the Hour approaches and Allah decrees a matter that was to be done. And it is necessary that this be rare because it is the beginning of the kingdom of the Hereafter, and the kingdom is mighty, and kings do not abound. Just as the excellent in kingdom and beauty is only rare, and most people are beneath them, so too in the kingdom of the Hereafter. For the Worldly Life (Dunya) is a mirror of the Hereafter (Akhirah), for it is an expression of the world of Witnessing (Shahadah), and the Hereafter is an expression of the world of the Unseen (Ghayb), and the world of Witnessing follows the world of the Unseen, just as the image in the mirror follows the image of the viewer in the mirror. And the image in the mirror, even though it is second in rank of existence, is first in terms of your seeing, for you do not see yourself and you see your image in the mirror first, then you know by it your image that is established by you second, by way of imitation. So the Heart (Qalb) that is following in existence is followed in terms of knowledge, and the Heart that is delayed is advanced, and this is a type of reversal. But reversal and inversion are necessities of this world. Likewise, the world of Dominion (Mulk) and Witnessing (Shahadah) imitates the world of the Unseen (Ghayb) and the Dominion (Malakut). Among people are those for whom the gaze of consideration is made easy, so he does not look at anything from the world of Dominion except that he crosses with it to the world of Dominion, and his crossing is called a lesson. And the Truth has commanded it, saying: 'So take lesson, O you of insight' (Quran 59:2). And among them are those whose insight is blinded, so he does not take lesson, and he is confined in the world of Dominion and Witnessing, and the doors of Hell will open to his confinement, and this confinement is filled with fire.
8:44.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

8:45.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
8:45.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Whatever is in the Quran of 'O you who have believed' is in the Torah 'O you poor ones (al-Masakin)'.
8:45.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

8:46.arabic: ووعد الصابرين بأنه معهم فقال تعالى: ﴿ واصبروا إن الله مع الصابرين ﴾ {} وعلق النصرة على الصبر فقال تعالى: ﴿ بلى إن تصبروا وتتقوا ويأتوكم من فورهم هذا يمددكم ربكم بخمسة آلاف من الملائكة مسومين ﴾ {} وجمع للصابرين بين أمور لم يجمعها لغيرهم فقال تعالى: ﴿ أولئك عليهم صلوات من ربهم ورحمة وأولئك هم المهتدون ﴾ {} فالهدى والرحمة والصلوات مجموعة للصابرين واستقصاء جميع الآيات في مقام الصبر يطول.
8:46.english: And He promised the patient ones (الصابرين) that He is with them, so He said, the Exalted: 'And be patient (اصبروا), indeed Allah is with the patient ones (الصابرين).' And He made victory conditional upon patience (الصبر), so He said, the Exalted: 'Yes, if you are patient (تصبروا) and are God-conscious (تتقوا) and they come upon you in this rush, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand of the angels, marked.' And He gathered for the patient ones (الصابرين) between matters He did not gather for others, so He said, the Exalted: 'Those are upon them prayers (صلوات) from their Lord and mercy (رحمة), and those are the guided ones (المهتدون).' So guidance (الهدى), mercy (رحمة), and prayers (صلوات) are gathered for the patient ones (الصابرين), and enumerating all the verses in the station of patience (الصبر) would be lengthy.
8:46.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

8:47.arabic: وأما هؤلاء فإنهم يصدون عن سبيل الله ويجرون الخلق إلى الغرور بالله بلفظ الرجاء فيزيدهم كلامهم جرأة على المعاصي ورغبة في الدنيا، لا سيما إذا كان الواعظ متزيناً بالثياب والخيل والمراكب فإنه تشهد هيئته من فرقه إلى قدمه بشدة حرصه على الدنيا فما يفسده هذا المغرور أكثر مما يصلحه بل لا يصلح أصلاً ويضل خلقاً كثيراً ولا يخفى وجه كونه مغروراً.
8:47.english: And as for these, they turn away from the path of Allah (سبيل الله) and drag the creation into delusion (غرور) regarding Allah with words of hope, and their speech increases them in boldness toward sins and desire for the worldly life (الدنيا), especially if the preacher is adorned with clothes, horses, and vehicles, for his appearance from his head to his feet testifies to his intense craving for the worldly life. So what this deluded one corrupts is more than what he rectifies; indeed, he does not rectify at all, and he misleads many people, and the aspect of his being deluded is not hidden.
8:47.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

8:49.arabic: وقال عز وجل: " ومن يتوكل على الله فإن الله عزيز حكيم ". أي عزيز لا يذل من استجار به، ولا يضيع من لاذ بجنابه والتجأ إلى ذمامه وحماه، وحكيم لا يقصر عن تدبير من توكل على تدبيره.
8:49.english: And He, the Exalted, said: "And whoever relies (tawakkala) upon Allah, then indeed Allah is Mighty (ʿazīz), Wise (ḥakīm)." That is, Mighty (ʿazīz) — He does not humiliate whoever seeks refuge in Him, nor does He forsake whoever takes shelter in His side and seeks protection in His sanctuary and safeguard; and Wise (ḥakīm) — He does not fall short in managing the affairs of whoever relies (tawakkala) upon His management.
8:49.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

8:51.arabic: وقال سعد بن بلال: يؤمر يوم القيامة بإخراج رجلين من النار فيقول الله تبارك وتعالى ذلك بما قدمت أيديكما وما أنا بظلام للعبيد ويأمر بردهما إلى النار فيعدو أحدهما فى سلاسله حتى يقتحمها ويتلكا الآخر ويأمر بردهما ويسألهما عن فعلهما فيقول الذى عدا إلى النار قد حذرت من وبال المعصية فلم أكن لأتعرض لسخطك ثانية ويقول الذى تلكا حسن ظنى بك كان يشعرنى أن لا تردنى إليها بعد ما أخرجتنى منها فيأمر بهما إلى الجنة.
8:51.english: And Sa'd ibn Bilal said: On the Day of Resurrection, two men are ordered to be taken out from the Fire, and Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: 'That is for what your hands have sent forth, and Allah is not unjust to the servants (8:51).' And He orders them to be returned to the Fire. So one of them runs in his chains until he plunges into it, and the other delays. And He orders them to be returned and asks them about their action. The one who ran to the Fire says: 'I have been warned of the consequence of disobedience, so I would not expose myself to Your wrath a second time.' And the one who delayed says: 'My good expectation of You made me feel that You would not return me to it after You had taken me out from it.' So He orders both of them to Paradise.
8:51.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

8:58.arabic: وقال ﭬ "لا يدخل الجنة بخيل ولا خب ولا خائن لا سيئ الملكة"[77] وفي رواية "ولا جبار" وفي رواية "ولا منان" وقال ﭬ "ثلاث مهلكات؛ شح مطاع وهوى متبع وإعجاب المرء بنفسه"[78] وقال ﭬ "إن الله يبغض ثلاثة: الشيخ الزاني، والبخيل المنان، والمعيل المختال"[79]
8:58.english: And he (peace be upon him) said: "The stingy (Bakhil), the treacherous (Kha'in), and the one with bad character (Sayyi' al-Malakah) will not enter Paradise." In another narration: "nor the tyrant (Jabbar)" and in another narration: "nor the one who reminds of his favors (Mannan)." And he (peace be upon him) said: "Three destructive things: obeyed greed (Shah), followed desire (Hawa), and self-admiration (I'jab al-Mar' bi-Nafsihi)." And he (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, Allah hates three: the old fornicator (Shaykh al-Zani), the stingy one who reminds of favors (Bakhil al-Mannan), and the poor arrogant (Mu'il al-Mukhtal)."
8:58.book_title: Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth
8:58.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

8:58.arabic: وكان الحسن بن علي رضي الله عنهما يمر بالسؤال وبين أيديهم كسر فيقولون هلم إلى الغداء يا ابن رسول الله فكان ينزل ويجلس على الطريق ويأكل معهم ويركب ويقول إن الله لا يحب المستكبرين
8:58.english: And Al-Hasan ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with them both) would pass by beggars who had bread before them, and they would say: 'Come to lunch, O son of the Messenger of Allah.' So he would dismount, sit on the road, eat with them, then remount and say: 'Indeed, Allah does not love the arrogant ones.'
8:58.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Etiquette of Seclusion'

8:58.arabic: وَمَرَّ الْحَسَنُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا بِقَوْمٍ مِنَ الْمَسَاكِينِ الَّذِينَ يَسْأَلُونَ النَّاسَ عَلَى الطَّرِيقِ وَقَدْ نَشَرُوا كِسْرًا عَلَى الْأَرْضِ فِي الرَّمْلِ وَهُمْ يَأْكُلُونَ وَهُوَ عَلَى بَغْلَتِهِ فَسَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِمْ فَقَالُوا لَهُ هَلُمَّ إِلَى الْغَدَاءِ يَا ابْنَ بِنْتِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَقَالَ نَعَمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُسْتَكْبِرِينَ فَنَزَلَ وَقَعَدَ مَعَهُمْ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ وَأَكَلَ ثُمَّ سَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَرَكِ
8:58.english: And Al-Hasan ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with them both) passed by a group of the poor (Masakin) who were asking people on the road, and they had spread out crumbs on the ground in the sand and they were eating, while he was on his mule. He greeted them, and they said to him: 'Come to lunch, O son of the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him).' He said: 'Yes, indeed Allah does not love the arrogant (Mustakbirin).' So he dismounted and sat with them on the ground and ate. Then he greeted them and mounted and said: 'I have answered you, so answer me.' They said: 'Yes.' So he promised them a known time, and they attended, and he presented to them the finest food and sat eating with them.
8:58.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Manners of Eating'

8:60.arabic: فإذا لزمك بأمر الله الحذر من العدو الكافر وأنت تراه فبأن يلزمك الحذر من عدو يراك ولا تراه أولى. ولذلك قال ابن محيريز: صيد تراه ولا يراك يوشك أن تظفر به، وصيد يراك ولا تراه يوشك أن يظفر بك. فأشار إلى الشيطان، فكيف وليس في الغفلة عن عداوة الكافر إلا قتل هو شهادة وفي إهمال الحذر من الشيطان التعرض للنار والعقاب الأليم؟ فليس من الاشتغال بالله الأعراض عما حذر الله وبه يبطل مذهب الفرقة الثاني في ظنهم أن ذلك قادح في التوكل، فإن أخذ الترس والسلاح وجمع الجنود وحفر الخندق لم يقدح في توكل رسول الله ﭬ فكيف ي
8:60.english: If it is incumbent upon you by the command of Allah to be cautious of the disbelieving enemy whom you see, then it is more incumbent upon you to be cautious of an enemy who sees you while you do not see him. Therefore, Ibn Muhayriz said: 'A prey that you see but does not see you, you are likely to capture it; and a prey that sees you but you do not see it, it is likely to capture you.' He was referring to Satan (Shaytan). How can it be otherwise when neglecting the enmity of the disbeliever results only in killing, which is martyrdom (Shahadah), while neglecting caution from Satan exposes one to the Fire (Nar) and painful punishment? It is not part of being occupied with Allah to turn away from what Allah has warned against, and this invalidates the doctrine of the second group in their assumption that this detracts from Reliance (Tawakkul). For taking up the shield and weapon, gathering troops, and digging the trench did not detract from the Reliance (Tawakkul) of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), so how can caution from what Allah has warned against and being cautious from what He has commanded to be cautious from detract from Reliance (Tawakkul)? We have mentioned in the Book of Reliance (Kitab al-Tawakkul) what clarifies the error of those who claim that the meaning of Reliance (Tawakkul) is complete abandonment of means, and His saying, the Exalted, 'And prepare against them whatever you are able of power and of steeds of war by which you may terrify the enemy of Allah and your enemy and others besides them whom you do not know [but] whom Allah knows. And whatever you spend in the cause of Allah will be fully repaid to you, and you will not be wronged' does not contradict compliance with Reliance (Tawakkul), as long as the Heart (Qalb) believes that the One who harms and benefits, gives life and causes death is Allah, the Exalted. Similarly, one should be cautious of Satan (Shaytan) and believe that the Guide (Al-Hadi) and the Misleader (Al-Mudill) is Allah, and see the means as subservient intermediaries - as we have mentioned in Reliance (Tawakkul).
8:60.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

8:60.arabic: وقال عز وجل "إنه يراكم هو وقبيله من حيث لا ترونهم" والقرآن من أوله إلى آخره تحذير من الشيطان فكيف وقد أمر بالحذر من العدو كما أمر بالحذر من الكفار فقال تعالى "وليأخذوا حذرهم وأسلحتهم" وقال تعالى "وأعدوا لهم ما استطعتم من قوة ومن رباط الخيل" فإذا لزمك بأمر الله الحذر من العدو الكافر وأنت تراه فبأن يلزمك الحذر من عدو يراك ولا تراه أولى. ولذلك قال ابن محيريز: صيد تراه ولا يراك يوشك أن تظفر به، وصيد يراك ولا تراه يوشك أن يظفر بك. فأشار إلى الشيطان، فكيف وليس في الغفلة عن عداوة الكافر إلا قتل هو شهاد
8:60.english: And He (Allah), the Exalted, said: "Indeed, he sees you, he and his tribe, from where you do not see them." And the Quran from its beginning to its end is a warning from Satan, so how is it that He commanded caution from the enemy as He commanded caution from the disbelievers? He said, the Exalted: "And let them take their precaution and their weapons," and He said, the Exalted: "And prepare for them what you are able of strength and of tethering the horses, you frighten with it the enemy of Allah and your enemy and others besides them whom you do not know them, Allah knows them. And whatever you spend of anything in the path of Allah, it will be repaid to you, and you will not be wronged." So if it is incumbent upon you by the command of Allah to be cautious from the disbelieving enemy while you see him, then that it is incumbent upon you to be cautious from an enemy who sees you and you do not see him is more deserving. And for that reason, Ibn Muhayriz said: "A prey you see and it does not see you, you are likely to capture it, and a prey that sees you and you do not see it, it is likely to capture you." He pointed to Satan, so how is it that there is not in heedlessness of the enmity of the disbeliever except killing which is martyrdom, and in neglecting caution from Satan is exposure to the Fire and the painful punishment? So it is not from preoccupation with Allah to turn away from what Allah warned, and by this, the doctrine of the second group is invalidated in their assumption that this detracts from Reliance (Tawakkul). For taking the shield and weapons, gathering the soldiers, and digging the trench did not detract from the Reliance (Tawakkul) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so how can caution from what Allah warned about and caution from what He commanded to be cautious from detract from Reliance (Tawakkul)? And we have mentioned in the book of Reliance (Tawakkul) what clarifies the error of those who claim that the meaning of Reliance (Tawakkul) is complete abandonment of means, and His saying, the Exalted: "And prepare for them what you are able of strength and of tethering the horses" does not contradict compliance with Reliance (Tawakkul), as long as the Heart (Qalb) believes that the Harmful and the Beneficial, the Giver of Life (Muhyi) and the Causer of Death (Mumit) is Allah, the Exalted. Likewise, one is cautious of Satan and believes that the Guide (Hadi) and the Misleader (Mudill) is Allah, and sees the means as subjugated intermediaries - as we mentioned in Reliance (Tawakkul).
8:60.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

8:60.arabic: وقال سبحانه: "وأعدوا لهم ما استطعتم من قوة ومن رباط الخيل" والتحصن بالليل اختفاءً عن أعين الأعداء ونوع تسبب، واختفاء رسول الله ﭬ في الغار اختفاء عن أعين الأعداء دفعاً للضرر[34]، وأخذ السلاح في الصلاة فليس دافعاً قطعاً كقتل الحية والعقرب فإنه دافع قطعاً، ولكن أخذ السلاح سبب مظنون، وقد بينا أن المظنون كالمقطوع، وإنما الموهوم هو الذي يقتضي التوكل تركه.
8:60.english: And He, the Exalted, said: "And prepare for them what you are able of strength (Qūwah) and of tethering the horses (Ribāṭ al-Khayl)." And fortifying by night is concealment from the eyes of the enemies and a type of taking means (Tasabbub), and the concealment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the cave is concealment from the eyes of the enemies as a repulsion of harm[34], and taking weapons in prayer is not a repeller decisively like killing the snake and the scorpion, for that is a repeller decisively, but taking weapons is a presumed cause (Sabab Maẓnūn), and we have clarified that the presumed is like the decisive, and only the imagined (Mawhūm) is what necessitates the abandonment of reliance (Tawakkul).
8:60.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

8:63.arabic: اعلم أن هؤلاء الصناع المصلحين للأطعمة وغيرها لو تفرقت آراؤهم وتنافرت طباعهم تنافر طباع الوحش لتبددوا وتباعدوا ولم ينتفع بعضهم ببعض بل كانوا كالوحوش لا يحويهم مكان واحد ولا يجمعهم غرض واحد، فانظر كيف ألف الله تعالى بين قلوبهم وسلط الأنس والمحبة عليهم ﴿ لو أنفقت ما في الأرض جميعا ما ألفت بين قلوبهم ولكن الله ألف بينهم ﴾  {}  فلأجل الإلف وتعارف الأرواح اجتمعوا وائتلفوا وبنوا المدن والبلاد ورتبوا المساكن والدور متقاربة متجاورة ورتبوا الأسواق والخانات وسائر أصناف البقاع مما يطول إحصاؤه
8:63.english: Know that these craftsmen who rectify foods and other things, if their opinions had diverged and their natures had clashed like the natures of wild beasts, they would have scattered and distanced themselves, and none would have benefited from another. Rather, they would have been like wild beasts that no single place contains and no single purpose unites. So observe how Allah the Exalted brought affection between their hearts (Qulub) and subjected them to familiarity and love: 'If you had spent all that is in the earth, you could not have brought affection between their hearts, but Allah brought affection between them' (Quran 8:63). {} So due to affection (Ilf) and the mutual recognition of spirits (Arwah), they gathered and united, and built cities and lands, and arranged dwellings and houses close and adjacent, and arranged markets, caravanserais, and all kinds of places whose enumeration would be lengthy.
8:63.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

8:63.arabic: ولا يخفي أن ثمرة الخلق الحسن الألفة وانقطاع الوحشة ومهما طاب المثمر طابت الثمرة وكيف وقد ورد في الثناء على نفس الألفة سيما إذا كانت الرابطة هي التقوى والدين وحب الله من الآيات والأخبار والآثار ما فيه كفاية ومقنع قال الله تعالى مظهرا عظيم منته على الخلق بنعمة الألفة لو أنفقت ما في الأرض جميعا ما ألفت بين قلوبهم ولكن الله ألف بينهم وقال فأصبحتم بنعمته إخوانا أي بالألفة ثم ذم التفرقة وزجر عنها فقال عز من قائل واعتصموا بحبل الله جميعا ولا تفرقوا إلى لعلكم تهتدون
8:63.english: And it is not hidden that the fruit of good character (Khuluq al-Hasan) is affection (Alfah) and the cutting off of alienation, and whenever the fruit-bearer is good, the fruit is good. And how could it not be, when there has come in praise of affection itself, especially when the bond is piety (Taqwa) and religion (Deen) and love of Allah, from the verses (Ayat) and reports (Akhbar) and traditions (Athar) what is sufficient and convincing. Allah the Exalted said, manifesting His great favor upon creation with the blessing of affection: 'If you had spent all that is in the earth, you could not have brought their hearts together; but Allah brought them together.' And He said: 'So you became brothers by His favor,' meaning through affection. Then He censured division and warned against it, saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And hold fast, all of you together, to the rope of Allah, and be not divided among yourselves, that you may be guided.'
8:63.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

8:63.arabic: هذا هو المألوف من الصحابة رضي الله عنهم ومن زاد عليهم في الورع فهو ضال مبتدع وليس بمتبع فلن يبلغ أحد مد أحدهم ولا نصيفه ولو انفق ما في الأرض جميعا كيف وقد أكل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم طعام بريرة فقيل : إنه صدقة فقال : هو لها صدقة ولنا هدية حديث أكله طعام بريرة فقيل إنها صدقة فقال هو لها صدقة ولنا هدية متفق عليه من حديث أنس ولم يسأل على المتصدق عليها فكان مجهولا عنده ولم يمتنع
8:63.english: This is the customary practice (al-ma'lūf) of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them), and whoever exceeds them in scrupulousness (al-waraʿ) is misguided and innovating, not following. No one will reach the measure (mudd) of any of them, nor even half of it, even if he spent all that is in the earth. How could he, when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) ate the food of Burairah, and it was said: 'It is charity (ṣadaqah).' He said: 'It is charity (ṣadaqah) for her, and a gift (hadiyyah) for us.' The hadith of him eating the food of Burairah: it was said it is charity (ṣadaqah), so he said: 'It is charity (ṣadaqah) for her, and a gift (hadiyyah) for us,' agreed upon from the narration of Anas. And he did not ask about the one who gave charity upon it, so it was unknown to him, and he did not refrain.
8:63.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

8:73.arabic: فالنكاح بسبب دفع غائلة الشهوة مهم في الدين لكل من لا يؤتى عن عجز وعنة وهم غالب الخلق فإن الشهوة إذا غلبت ولم يقاومها قوة التقوى جرت إلى اقتحام الفواحش وإليه أشار بقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام عن الله تعالى (إلا تفعلوه تكن فتنة في الأرض وفساد كبير) وإن كان ملجما بلجام التقوى فغايته أن يكف الجوارح عن إجابة الشهوة فيغض البصر ويحفظ الفرج.
8:73.english: Marriage, due to repelling the danger of desire (Shahwah), is important in the religion for everyone who is not afflicted with impotence or disability, and they are the majority of creation. For if desire overpowers and is not resisted by the strength of piety (Taqwa), it leads to plunging into abominations. And to this, He (peace and blessings be upon him) referred by the saying of Allah the Exalted: 'Unless you do it, there will be trial (Fitnah) on earth and great corruption (Fasad Kabir).' And if it is bridled with the bridle of piety (Taqwa), its utmost is that it restrains the limbs from responding to the desire, so one lowers the gaze and guards the private parts.
8:73.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'
