8:73.arabic: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم (إذا أتاكم من ترضون دينه وأمانته فزوجوه إلا تفعلوه تكن فتنة في الأرض وفساد كبير)[7] وهذا أيضا تعليل الترغيب لخوف الفساد
8:73.english: And the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: 'When someone whose religion and trustworthiness you approve comes to you, marry him off; if you do not do it, there will be a trial (Fitnah) in the earth and great corruption (Fasad).' [7] And this is also an explanation of the encouragement due to fear of corruption.
8:73.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

8:73.arabic: حديث إذا أتاكم من ترضون دينه وأمانته فزوجوه إلا تفعلوه تكن فتنة في الأرض وفساد كبير أخرجه الترمذي من حديث أبي هريرة ونقل عن البخاري أنه لم يعده محفوظا وقال أبو داود إنه خطأ ورواه الترمذي أيضا من حديث أبي حاتم المزني وحسنه ورواه أبو داود في المراسيل وأعله ابن القطان بإرساله وضعف رواته.
8:73.english: The hadith: 'If there comes to you one whose religion and trustworthiness you are pleased with, then marry him off. If you do not do it, there will be tribulation (fitnah) in the earth and great corruption (fasad kabir).' Al-Tirmidhi transmitted it from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, and it is reported from Al-Bukhari that he did not consider it preserved, and Abu Dawud said it is an error. Al-Tirmidhi also transmitted it from the hadith of Abu Hatim Al-Muzani and graded it as good (hasan), and Abu Dawud transmitted it in the Marasil, and Ibn Al-Qattan criticized it due to its being disconnected (mursal) and the weakness of its narrators.
8:73.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

8:74.arabic: وقد ذكر الله تعالى صفات المؤمنين والمنافقين في كتابه وهي بجملتها ثمرة حسن الخلق وسوء الخلق. فلنورد جملة من ذلك لتعلم آية حسن الخلق. قال الله تعالى "قد أفلح المؤمنون الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون والذين هم عن اللغو معرضون" إلى قوله "أولئك هم الوارثون" وقال عز وجل "التائبون العابدون الحامدون" إلى قوله "وبشر المؤمنين" وقال عز وجل "إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم" إلى قوله "أولئك هم المؤمنون حقاً" وقال تعالى "وعباد الرحمن الذين يمشون على الأرض هوناً وإذا خاطبهم الجاهلون قالوا سلاما" إلى آخر
8:74.english: And Allah the Exalted has mentioned the attributes of the believers and the hypocrites in His Book, and they are in their entirety the fruit of good character and bad character. So let us mention a collection of that to know the sign of good character. Allah the Exalted said: "Successful indeed are the believers who are humble in their prayers and who turn away from idle talk" to His saying "Those are the inheritors." And He the Mighty and Majestic said: "The repentant, the worshippers, the praisers" to His saying "and give glad tidings to the believers." And He the Mighty and Majestic said: "The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble" to His saying "Those are the believers in truth." And He the Exalted said: "And the servants of the Most Merciful who walk upon the earth easily and when the ignorant address them, they say peace" to the end of the surah. Whoever is confused about his condition, let him present himself to these verses, for the presence of all these attributes is a sign of good character, and the absence of all of them is a sign of bad character, and the presence of some without others indicates some without others, so let him occupy himself with acquiring what he lacks and preserving what he has found.
8:74.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

8:74.arabic: وقوله عز وجل ﴿ لهم مغفرة ورزق كريم. كما أخرجك ربك من بيتك بالحق ﴾ {} فهذا الكلام غير متصل وإنما هو عائد إلى قوله السابق ﴿ قل الانفال لله والرسول. كما أخرجك ربك من بيتك بالحق ﴾ {} أي فصارت أنفال الغنائم لك إذ أنت راض بخروجك وهم كارهون فاعترض بين الكلام الأمر بالتقوى وغيره
8:74.english: And His saying, the Exalted and Majestic: 'For them is forgiveness and a generous provision. As your Lord brought you out of your home in truth' {} This speech is not connected, but rather it refers back to His previous saying: 'Say: The spoils of war are for Allah and the Messenger. As your Lord brought you out of your home in truth' {} meaning: So the spoils of war became yours since you were pleased with your departure while they were averse, so the command for piety and other matters intervened between the speech.
8:74.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

8:74.arabic: الوجه الثالث: مستنده الشك ومعناه أنا مؤمن حقا إن شاء الله إذ قال الله تعالى لقوم مخصوصين بأعيانهم: ﴿ أولئك هم المؤمنون حقا ﴾ {} فانقسموا إلى قسمين ويرجع هذا إلى الشك في كمال الإيمان لا في أصله وكل إنسان شاك في كمال إيمانه وذلك ليس بكفر والشك في كمال الإيمان حق من وجهين: أحدهما من حيث إن النفاق يزيل كمال الإيمان وهو خفي لا تتحقق البراءة منه. والثاني: أنه يكمل بأعمال الطاعات ولا يدري وجودها على الكمال أما العمل فقد قال الله تعالى: ﴿ إنما المؤمنون الذين آمنوا بالله ورسوله ثم لم يرتابوا وجاهدوا بأمو
8:74.english: The third aspect: its basis is doubt and its meaning is 'I am a true believer if Allah wills' since Allah the Exalted said to a specific group of individuals: 'Those are the true believers' {} They divided into two categories, and this returns to doubt about the perfection of faith (Iman) not about its foundation, and every person doubts about the perfection of his faith (Iman), and that is not disbelief (Kufr). Doubt about the perfection of faith (Iman) is correct from two perspectives: One of them is from the aspect that hypocrisy (Nifaq) removes the perfection of faith (Iman), and it is hidden such that one cannot ascertain freedom from it. The second: that it is perfected through acts of obedience (Taat) and one does not know their existence in perfection. As for action, Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, the believers are those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and then have not doubted and have struggled with their wealth and their selves in the way of Allah. Those are the truthful ones' {} So doubt occurs about this truthfulness. And similarly Allah the Exalted said: 'But righteousness is in one who believes in Allah, the Last Day, the angels, the Book, and the prophets' {} He stipulated twenty descriptions such as fulfillment of the covenant and patience in hardships, then said the Exalted: 'Those are the ones who have been truthful' {} And Allah the Exalted said: 'Allah will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge by degrees' {} And Allah the Exalted said: 'Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought' {} The verse. And Allah the Exalted said: 'They are degrees with Allah' {} And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Faith (Iman) is naked and its garment is piety (Taqwa)' the hadith. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Faith (Iman) has seventy-odd branches, the lowest of them is removing harm from the road.' This is what indicates the connection of...
8:74.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Foundations of Belief'

9:14.arabic: وقال تعالى: " قاتلوهم يعذبهم الله بأيديكم " فأضاف القتل إليهم والتعذيب إلى نفسه، والتعذيب هو عين القتل، بل صرح وقال تعالى: " فلم تقتلوهم ولكن الله قتلهم "، وقال تعالى: " وما رميت إذا رميت ولكن الله رمى " وهو جمع بين النفي والإثبات ظاهراً، ولكن معناه: وما رميت بالمعنى الذي يكون الرب به رامياً إذ رميت بالمعنى الذي يكون العبد به رامياً، إذ هما معنيان مختلفان.
9:14.english: And He, the Exalted, said: "Fight them; Allah will torment them by your hands" (Quran 9:14). So He attributed the killing to them and the tormenting to Himself, and the tormenting is the very killing. Indeed, He explicitly stated and said, the Exalted: "So you did not kill them, but Allah killed them" (Quran 8:17), and He, the Exalted, said: "And you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw" (Quran 8:17). This is a combination of negation and affirmation in appearance, but its meaning is: And you did not throw in the sense that makes the Lord (Rabb) the thrower when you threw in the sense that makes the servant (Abd) the thrower, for they are two different meanings.
9:14.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

9:14.arabic: ومن الوجه الذي لم يرم رماه الله عز وجل وكذلك قال تعالى ﴿ قاتلوهم يعذبهم الله بأيديكم ﴾ فإذا كانوا هم المقاتلين كيف يكون الله سبحانه هو المعذب وإن كان الله تعالى هو المعذب بتحريك أيديهم فما معنى أمرهم بالقتال فحقيقة هذا يستمد من بحر عظيم من علوم المكاشفات لا يغنى عنه ظاهر التفسير وهو أن يعلم وجه ارتباط الأفعال بالقدرة الحادثة ويفهم وجه ارتباط القدرة بقدرة الله عز وجل حتى ينكشف بعد إيضاح أمور كثيرة غامضة صدق قوله عز وجل ﴿ وما رميت إذ رميت ولكن الله رمى ﴾
9:14.english: And from the aspect in which he did not throw, Allah the Exalted threw him. And similarly, Allah the Exalted said: 'Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands' (Quran 9:14). So if they are the fighters, how can Allah the Glorified be the Punisher? And if Allah the Exalted is the Punisher by moving their hands, then what is the meaning of commanding them to fight? The reality of this draws from a vast ocean of the sciences of unveilings (Mukashafat) that the apparent interpretation (Tafsir) cannot suffice for. It is to know the aspect of connection of actions with the emergent power (Qudrah Hadithah) and to understand the aspect of connection of the power with the power of Allah the Exalted, until after clarifying many obscure matters, the truth of His saying the Exalted is unveiled: 'And you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw' (Quran 8:17).
9:14.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

9:15.arabic: واستثنى في خمسة اشياء في الاغناء والاجابة والرزق والمغفرة والتوبة فقال تعالى: ﴿ فسوف يغنيكم الله من فضله ان شاء ﴾ {} وقال فيكشف ما تدعون اليه ان شاء - وقال يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب وقال: ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء وقال: ويتوب الله على من يشاء وهو خلق من اخلاق الربوبية اذ قال تعالى: ﴿ والله شكور حليم ﴾ {}
9:15.english: And He made exceptions in five things: in enrichment, in answering, in provision, in forgiveness, and in repentance. So He, the Exalted, said: 'Then Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills' {} and He said: 'He will remove what you call to if He wills' - and He said: 'He provides for whom He wills without measure' and He said: 'And He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills' and He said: 'And Allah turns in repentance (Tawbah) upon whom He wills' and it is a character from the characters of Lordship (Rububiyyah) since He, the Exalted, said: 'And Allah is Appreciative (Shakur), Forbearing (Halim)' {}.
9:15.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

9:18.arabic: فختم على كل ذى حزم آمن بالله واليوم الآخر أن لا يغفل عن محاسبة نفسه والتضييق عليها في حركاتها وسكناتها وخطراتها وخطواتها
9:18.english: So it concludes for every possessor of determination who believes in Allah and the Last Day that he should not neglect accounting his self (Nafs) and restricting it in its movements, stillness, fleeting thoughts, and steps.
9:18.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

9:18.arabic:
(فضيلة المسجد وموضع الصلاة)
   قال الله عز وجل: ﴿ إنما يعمر مساجد الله من  آمن  بالله  واليوم  الآخر  ﴾
{التوبة: 18} وقال ﭬ: (من بنى لله مسجدا ولو كمفحص قطاة بنى الله  له  قصرا  في
الجنة[44]) وقال ﭬ: (من ألف المسجد ألفه الله  تعالى[45])  وقال  ﭬ:  (إذا  دخل
أحدكم المسجد فليركع ركعتين قبل أن يجلس[46]) وقال ﭬ:  (لا  صلاة  لجار  المسجد
إلا في المسجد[47]) وقال ﭬ: (الملائكة تصلي على أحدكم ما  دام  في  مصلاه  الذي
يصلي فيه تقول اللهم صل عليه اللهم ارحمه اللهم اغفر له ما لم يحد
9:18.english: (The Virtue of the Mosque and the Place of Prayer) Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, the ones who maintain (yaʿmuru) the mosques of Allah are those who have believed in Allah and the Last Day and established the prayer (aḳāma aṣ-ṣalāta) and given the zakah and have not feared except Allah. Then it is expected that those will be of the [rightly] guided.' (At-Tawbah: 18) And He (the Prophet) said: 'Whoever builds for Allah a mosque, even if it be like the nest of a sandgrouse, Allah will build for him a palace in Paradise.' And He said: 'Whoever frequents the mosque, Allah the Exalted will make him beloved.' And He said: 'When one of you enters the mosque, let him perform two rak'ahs before he sits.' And He said: 'There is no prayer for the neighbor of the mosque except in the mosque.' And He said: 'The angels pray upon one of you as long as he remains in his prayer place where he prays, saying: O Allah, bless him, O Allah, have mercy on him, O Allah, forgive him, as long as he does not break his ablution or leave the mosque.' And He said: 'There will come at the end of time people from my community who will come to the mosques and sit in them in circles; their remembrance (dhikr) is the worldly life and love of the worldly life. Do not sit with them, for Allah has no need of them.' And He said: 'Allah the Exalted said in some of the books: Indeed, My houses on My earth are the mosques, and My visitors in them are those who maintain them. So blessed is the servant who purifies himself in his house then visits Me in My house, for it is incumbent upon the One visited to honor His visitor.' And He said: 'If you see a man who regularly attends the mosque, then bear witness to his faith (īmān).' And Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: 'Whoever sits in the mosque, he is sitting with his Lord, so it is not fitting for him to say except good.' And it is seen in the tradition or report: 'Conversation in the mosque consumes good deeds just as livestock consume grass.' And an-Nakha'i said: 'They used to see that walking in the dark night...'
9:18.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

9:19.arabic: فختم على كل ذى حزم آمن بالله واليوم الآخر أن لا يغفل عن محاسبة نفسه والتضييق عليها في حركاتها وسكناتها وخطراتها وخطواتها فإن كل نفس من أنفاس العمر جوهرة نفيسة لا عوض لها يمكن أن يشترى بها كنز من الكنوز لا يتناهى نعيمه أبد الآباد فانقباض هذه الأنفاس ضائعة أو مصروفة إلى ما يجلب الهلاك خسران عظيم هائل لا تسمح به نفس عاقل
9:19.english: So it concludes for every possessor of determination who believes in Allah and the Last Day that he should not neglect accounting his Soul (Nafs) and constricting it in its movements, stillness, fleeting thoughts, and steps. For every breath of life is a precious jewel without substitute, with which can be purchased a treasure of treasures whose bliss is endless for eternity of eternities. The contraction of these breaths wasted or diverted to what brings destruction is a great, tremendous loss that no rational Soul (Nafs) would permit.
9:19.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

9:23.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
9:23.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'What is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)".'
9:23.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

9:24.arabic: لقلب ويقسو ويسود وتتراكم ظلمة النفوس على القلب فلا يزال يطفئ ما فيه من نور الإيمان على ضعفه حتى يصير طبعا ورينا فإذا جاءت سكرات الموت ازداد ذلك الحب أعني حب الله ضعفا لما يبدو من استشعار فراق الدنيا وهي المحبوب الغالب على القلب فيتألم القلب باستشعار فراق الدنيا ويرى ذلك من الله فيختلج ضميره بإنكار ما قدر عليه من الموت وكراهة ذلك من حيث إنه من الله فيخشى أن يثور في باطنه بغض الله تعالى بدل الحب كما أن الذي يحب ولده حبا ضعيفا إذا اخذ ولده أمواله التي هي أحب إليه من ولده وأحرقها انقلب ذلك الحب الضع
9:24.english: The Heart (Qalb) hardens and blackens, and the darkness of the Souls (Nafs) accumulates upon the Heart, so it continuously extinguishes what is in it of the light of Faith (Iman) due to its weakness, until it becomes a nature and a covering. When the agonies of death come, that love—meaning the love of Allah—increases in weakness due to what appears from sensing separation from the world, which is the beloved that dominates the Heart. So the Heart suffers from sensing separation from the world and sees that from Allah, and his conscience is agitated with denial of what has been decreed upon him of death and dislike of that from the perspective that it is from Allah. He fears that hatred of Allah the Exalted may arise in his inner self instead of love, just as one who loves his child with weak love, if his child takes his wealth, which is more beloved to him than his child, and burns it, that weak love turns into hatred. If it happens that his spirit departs at that moment when this thought occurred, then he has been sealed with evil and perishes an eternal perdition. The cause that leads to such an ending is the dominance of love of the world and reliance upon it and rejoicing in its means, along with weakness of Faith (Iman) that necessitates weakness of love of Allah the Exalted. So whoever finds in his heart the love of Allah more dominant than the love of the world, even if he also loves the world, he is farther from this danger. And love of the world is the head of every sin, and it is the chronic disease, and it has encompassed all kinds of creation. And all of that is due to lack of knowledge of Allah the Exalted, for none loves Him except one who knows Him. And for this reason, He the Exalted said: 'Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, your kinsfolk, wealth which you have acquired, commerce whose decline you fear, and dwellings with which you are pleased are more beloved to you than Allah and His Messenger and striving in His path, then wait until Allah brings His command.' Therefore, everyone whose spirit leaves him in a state of dangerous denial of Allah the Exalted in his mind, and hatred of Allah's action appears in his heart in His separating him from his family, his wealth, and all his beloved things, then his death becomes an arrival upon what he hates and a separation from what he loves. So he comes to Allah with the arrival of the hated, runaway servant when he is brought to his master by force, so it is not hidden what he deserves of disgrace and punishment. As for the one who dies upon love, then he comes to Allah the Exalted with the arrival of the good, longing servant to his master, who bore the hardships of deeds and the roughness of journeys hoping for meeting Him, so it is not hidden what he meets of joy and happiness merely from the arrival, let alone what he deserves of subtleties of honor and wonders of grace. As for the second ending, which is below the first and does not necessitate eternal abode in the Fire, it also has two causes: one is abundance of sins even if Faith (Iman) is strong, and the other is weakness of Faith (Iman) even if sins are few. That is because committing sins is caused by the dominance of desires and their firmness in the Heart due to much familiarity and habit. And all that a human has become accustomed to in his life returns its remembrance to his heart at his death. If his greater inclination is toward acts of obedience, then most of what is present to him is the remembrance of obedience to Allah. And if his greater inclination is toward sins, then their remembrance dominates his heart at death, so perhaps his spirit is seized.
9:24.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

9:24.arabic: وعلامة المعرفة المحبة فمن عرف الله تعالى أحبه وعلامة المحبة أن لا يؤثر عليه الدنيا، ولا غيرها من المحبوبات كما قال الله تعالى "قل إن كان آباؤكم وأبناؤكم وإخوانكم وأزواجكم" إلى قوله "أحب إليكم من الله ورسوله وجهاد في سبيله فتربصوا حتى يأتي الله بأمره" فمن عنده شيء أحب إليه من الله فقلبه مريض، كما أن كل معدة صار الطين أحب إليها من الخبز والماء أو سقطت شهوتها عن الخبز والماء فهي مريضة.
9:24.english: And the sign of knowledge (ma'rifah) is love (mahabba), so whoever knows Allah the Exalted loves Him, and the sign of love is that one does not prefer the worldly life (dunya) over Him, nor other beloved things, as Allah the Exalted said: 'Say: If your fathers and your sons and your brothers and your wives' to His saying 'are dearer to you than Allah and His Messenger and striving in His way, then wait until Allah brings His command.' So whoever has something dearer to him than Allah, his heart (qalb) is sick, just as every stomach for which clay becomes dearer than bread and water, or its appetite (shahwa) for bread and water falls away, it is sick.
9:24.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

9:24.arabic: وفي حديث آخر: " لا يؤمن العبد حتى أكون أحب إليه من أهله وماله والناس أجمعين"[3] وفي رواية " ومن نفسه ". كيف وقد قال تعالى " قل إن كان آباؤكم وأبناؤكم وإخوانكم " الآية. وإنما أجرى ذلك في معرض التهديد والإنكار.
9:24.english: And in another hadith: 'The servant (Abd) does not believe until I am more beloved to him than his family, his wealth, and all people' [3], and in a narration 'and than his self (Nafs)'. How [could it be otherwise] when Allah the Exalted has said: 'Say: If your fathers and your sons and your brothers and your wives and your tribe and wealth which you have acquired, and commerce whose stagnation you fear, and dwellings you are pleased with are more beloved to you than Allah and His Messenger and striving (Jihad) in His path, then wait until Allah brings His command. And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people (Al-Fasiqin).' And indeed, He has brought that forth in the context of threat and disapproval.
9:24.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

9:25.arabic: وكذلك لما اتكل أصحاب رسول الله ﷺ يوم حنين على قوتهم وكثرتهم ونسوا فضل الله تعالى عليهم وقالوا لا نغلب اليوم من قلة وكلوا إلى أنفسهم فقال تعالى "ويوم حنين إذ أعجبتكم كثرتكم فلم تغن عنكم شيئاً وضاقت عليكم الأرض بما رحبت ثم وليتم مدبرين".
9:25.english: And likewise when the companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) on the day of Hunayn relied upon their strength and their multitude and forgot the favor of Allah the Exalted upon them and said: 'We will not be defeated today due to fewness' and entrusted to themselves, then Allah the Exalted said: "And on the day of Hunayn when your multitude impressed you but it did not avail you anything and the earth became constricted upon you despite its vastness then you turned back fleeing."
9:25.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

9:25.arabic: اعلم أن العجب مذموم في كتاب الله تعالى وسنة رسوله ﭬ. قال الله تعالى "ويوم حنين إذ أعجبتكم كثرتكم فلم تغن عنكم شيئاً" ذكر ذلك في معرض الإنكار وقال عز وجل "وظنوا أنهم ما نعتهم حصونهم من الله فأتاهم الله من حيث لم يحتسبوا" فرد على الكفار في أعجابهم بحصونهم وشوكتهم وقال تعالى "وهم يحسبون أنهم يحسنون صنعاً -، وهذا أيضاً يرجع إلى العجب بالعمل. وقد يعجب الإنسان بالعمل هو مخطئ فيه كما يعجب بعمل هو مصيب فيه.
9:25.english: Know that self-conceit (Al-'Ujb) is condemned in the Book of Allah the Exalted and the Sunnah of His Messenger (peace be upon him). Allah the Exalted said: "And on the day of Hunayn, when your multitude impressed you, but it availed you nothing" - He mentioned that in the context of reproach. And He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: "And they thought that their fortresses would protect them from Allah, but Allah came upon them from where they had not expected" - He responded to the disbelievers regarding their self-conceit (I'jāb) in their fortresses and their might. And He the Exalted said: "And they think that they are doing good work" - and this also returns to self-conceit (Al-'Ujb) regarding action. And a human may be self-conceited (Ya'jabu) regarding an action in which he is mistaken, just as he may be self-conceited regarding an action in which he is correct.
9:25.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

9:25.arabic: [89] حديث قولهم يوم حنين لا نغلب اليوم من قلة أخرجه البيهقي في دلائل النبوة من رواية الربيع بن أنس مرسلا أن رجلا قال يوم حنين لن نغلب اليوم من قلة فشق ذلك على رسول الله ﷺ فأنزل الله عز وجل - ويوم حنين إذ أعجبتكم كثرتكم - ولابن مردويه في تفسيره من حديث أنس لما التقوا يوم حنين أعجبتهم كثرتهم فقالوا اليوم نقاتل ففروا فيه الفرح بن فضالة ضعفه الجمهور.
9:25.english: Hadith: Their saying on the day of Hunayn: 'We will not be defeated today due to fewness.' Al-Bayhaqi extracted it in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah from the narration of Rabi' ibn Anas as mursal: that a man said on the day of Hunayn: 'We will not be defeated today due to fewness.' That grieved the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), so Allah the Exalted revealed: 'And on the day of Hunayn when your multitude impressed you...' And Ibn Mardawayh in his Tafsir from the hadith of Anas: when they met on the day of Hunayn, their multitude impressed them, so they said: 'Today we will fight,' then they fled. In it is Al-Farrah ibn Fadalah, whom the majority weakened.
9:25.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

9:25.arabic: الوظيفة السادسة: أن يستصغر العطية فإنه إن استعظمها أعجب بها والعجب من المهلكات وهو محبط للأعمال قال تعالى: ﴿ ويوم حنين إذا أعجبتكم كثرتكم فلم تغن عنكم شيئا ﴾{} ويقال إن الطاعة كلما استصغرت عظمت عند الله عز وجل والمعصية كلما استعظمت صغرت عند الله عز وجل.
9:25.english: The sixth duty: to consider the gift small, for if he considers it great, he will become proud of it, and pride is among the destroyers and it nullifies works. Allah the Exalted said: 'And on the day of Hunayn when your multitude impressed you, but it availed you nothing.' And it is said: obedience, whenever it is considered small, becomes great with Allah the Exalted, and disobedience, whenever it is considered great, becomes small with Allah the Exalted.
9:25.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

9:28.arabic: واستثنى في خمسة اشياء في الاغناء والاجابة والرزق والمغفرة والتوبة فقال تعالى: ﴿ فسوف يغنيكم الله من فضله ان شاء ﴾ {} وقال فيكشف ما تدعون اليه ان شاء - وقال يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب وقال: ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء وقال: ويتوب الله على من يشاء وهو خلق من اخلاق الربوبية اذ قال تعالى: ﴿ والله شكور حليم ﴾ {}
9:28.english: And He made exceptions in five things: in enrichment, in answering, in provision, in forgiveness, and in repentance. So He, the Exalted, said: 'Then Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills' (Quran 9:28). And He said: 'And He removes what you call to if He wills' - and He said: 'He provides for whom He wills without measure' and He said: 'And He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills' and He said: 'And Allah turns in repentance to whom He wills'. And it is a character from the characters of Lordship (Rububiyyah), as He, the Exalted, said: 'And Allah is Appreciative (Shakur), Forbearing (Haleem)' (Quran 64:17).
9:28.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

9:28.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
9:28.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Whatever is in the Quran of 'O you who have believed' is in the Torah 'O you poor ones (al-Masakin)'.
9:28.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

9:34.arabic: وفي حديث عمر رضي الله عنه أنه قال: لما نزل قوله تعالى " والذين يكنزون الذهب والفضة ولا ينفقونها في سبيل الله " قال صلى الله عليه وسلم: " تباً للدنيا تباً للدينار والدرهم " فقلنا: يا رسول الله نهانا الله عن كنز الذهب والفضة، فأي شيء ندخر؟ فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ليتخذ أحدكم لساناً ذاكراً وقلباً شاكراً أو زوجة صالحة تعينه على أمر آخرته"[93].
9:34.english: And in the narration of Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, he said: When the saying of Allah the Exalted descended: "And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the path of Allah," the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Woe to the worldly life, woe to the dinar and dirham." So we said: O Messenger of Allah, Allah has forbidden us from hoarding gold and silver, so what should we store? He said: "Let one of you take a tongue that remembers (Dhikr) and a heart that is grateful (Shakir) or a righteous wife who helps him with the matter of his Hereafter."
9:34.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

9:34.arabic: [93] حديث عمر لما نزل قوله تعالى - والذين يكنزون الذهب والفضة - الآية قال تبا للدينار والدرهم الحديث وفيه فأي شيء ندخر أخرجه الترمذي وابن ماجه وتقدم في النكاح دون قوله تبا للدينار والدرهم والزيادة رواها الطبراني في الأوسط وهو من حديث ثوبان وإنما قال المصنف إنه حديث عمر لأن عمر هو الذي سأل النبي ﭬ أي المال يتخذ كما في رواية ابن ماجه وكما رواه البزار من حديث ابن عباس.
9:34.english: [93] The hadith of Umar: When the saying of Allah the Exalted descended - 'And those who hoard gold and silver' - the verse, he said: 'Woe to the dinar and dirham' the hadith, and in it: 'So what should we save?' It was reported by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, and it preceded in marriage without his saying 'Woe to the dinar and dirham', and the addition was narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, and it is from the hadith of Thawban. The author only said it is the hadith of Umar because Umar is the one who asked the Prophet ﷺ which wealth to take, as in the narration of Ibn Majah and as narrated by al-Bazzar from the hadith of Ibn Abbas.
9:34.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

9:35.arabic: وقد كان غيره من المسلمين يموت ويخلف أموالاً ولا يقول ذلك في حقه، وهذا يحتمل وجهين لأن حاله يحتمل حالين: أحدهما: أنه أراد كيتين من النار، كما قال تعالى "تكوى بها جباههم وجنوبهم وظهورهم" وذلك إذا كان حاله إظهار الزهد والفقر مع الإفلاس عنه فهو نوع تلبيس.
9:35.english: And others among the Muslims would die and leave behind wealth, and he (the Prophet) would not say that about them. This admits of two interpretations because his situation admits of two possibilities: The first: that he meant two brands from the Fire, as Allah the Exalted said: "They will be branded with it on their foreheads, their sides, and their backs." And that is if his situation was displaying asceticism (Zuhd) and poverty while being free from it - that is a type of deception (Talbees).
9:35.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

9:38.arabic: ولما استطار مكر الشيطان في كافة الخلق ارسل الله الملائكة الى الرسل وأوحوا إليهم ما تم على الخلق من اهلاك العدو واغوائه فاشتغلوا بدعوة الخلق الى الملك الحقيقي عن الملك المجازي الذي لا اصل له ان سلم ولا دوام له اصلا فنادوا فيهم ﴿ يا ايها الذين امنوا ما لكم اذا قيل لكم انفروا في سبيل الله اثاقلتم الى الارض أرضيتم بالحياة الدنيا من الاخرة فما متاع الحياة الدنيا في الاخرة الا قليل ﴾ {} فالتوراة والانجيل والزبور والفرقان وصحف موسى وابراهيم وكل كتاب منزل ما أنزل إلالدعوة الخلق الى الملك الدائم المخلد و
9:38.english: And when the deception (makar) of Satan spread among all creation, God sent the angels to the messengers and revealed to them what had befallen creation from the destruction of the enemy and his seduction, so they busied themselves with calling creation to the true kingdom (al-mulk al-haqīqī) over the metaphorical kingdom (al-mulk al-majāzī) which has no foundation even if it appears sound, nor any permanence at all. So they called out to them: 'O you who have believed, what is [the matter] with you that, when it is said to you, "Go forth in the path of God," you adhere heavily to the earth? Are you satisfied with the life of this world (al-ḥayāh al-dunyā) rather than the Hereafter (al-ākhirah)? But what is the enjoyment of the life of this world compared to the Hereafter except a little.' So the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, the Criterion (al-Furqān), and the scrolls of Moses and Abraham, and every revealed book was not sent except to call creation to the permanent, eternal kingdom, and what is intended for them is that they be kings in this world and kings in the Hereafter. As for kingship in this world, it is through asceticism (al-zuhd) in it and contentment (al-qanāʿah) with the little of it, and as for kingship in the Hereafter, it is through proximity (al-qurb) to God, attaining an existence (baqāʾ) in which there is no annihilation (fanāʾ), and a might (ʿizz) in which there is no humiliation (dhull), and a coolness of the eye (qurrat al-ʿayn) hidden in this world that no soul (nafs) among the souls knows. And Satan calls them to kingship in this world, knowing that kingship in the Hereafter is missed by it, for this world and the Hereafter are two rivals (ḍarratān), and knowing that this world does not remain secure for him either, and even if it were to remain secure for him, he would envy it as well. But kingship in this world is not free from disputes and disturbances, and prolonged anxieties in management, and likewise all the means of status (al-jāh). Then however much one secures and completes the means, the lifespan expires.
9:38.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

9:38.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
9:38.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'What is in the Quran as "O you who have believed" is in the Torah as "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)."'
9:38.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

9:40.arabic: حديث الرجل يقاتل لنيل مال أو أن يقال شجاع أو غير ذلك متفق عليه من حديث أبي موسى قال جاء رجل إلى النبي ﭬ فقال الرجل يقاتل للذكر والرجل يقاتل للمغنم والرجل يقاتل ليرى مكانه فمن في سبيل الله قال من قاتل لتكون كلمة الله هي العليا فهو في سبيل الله.
9:40.english: The hadith about the man who fights to obtain wealth or to be called brave or other than that, agreed upon from the narration of Abu Musa, who said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him) and said: The man fights for remembrance (Dhikr), the man fights for spoils, and the man fights to see his position. So who is in the path of Allah? He said: Whoever fights so that the word of Allah is the highest, he is in the path of Allah.
9:40.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication

9:43.arabic: بأبي أنت وأمى يا رسول الله لقد بلغ من فضيلتك عنده أن أخبرك بالعفو عنك قبل أن يخبرك بالذنب فقال تعالى: ﴿ عفا الله عنك لم أذنت لهم ﴾ {} بأبي أنت وأمي يا رسول الله لقد بلغ من فضيلتك عنده أن بعثك آخر الأنبياء وذكرك في أولهم فقال عز وجل: ﴿ وإذ أخذنا من النبيين ميثاقهم ومنك ومن نوح وإبراهيم ﴾ {} الآية
9:43.english: May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of Allah. Indeed, your excellence with Him has reached such a level that He informed you of forgiveness for you before informing you of the sin. So the Exalted said: 'Allah has forgiven you (عَفَا اللَّهُ عَنْكَ) - why did you permit them (لِمَ أَذِنْتَ لَهُمْ) until it becomes clear to you those who are truthful and you know the liars (حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَكَ الَّذِينَ صَدَقُوا وَتَعْلَمَ الْكَاذِبِينَ).' May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of Allah. Indeed, your excellence with Him has reached such a level that He sent you as the last of the prophets and mentioned you among the first of them. So the Mighty and Majestic said: 'And when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you and from Noah and Abraham...' the verse.
9:43.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith

9:52.arabic: فساد وقال تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا كونوا قوامين بالقسط شهداء لله ولو على انفسكم أو الوالدين والاقربين وذلك هو الأمر بالمعروف للوالدين والأقربين وقال تعالى لا خير في كثير من نجواهم إلا من أمر بصدقة أو معروف أو إصلاح بين الناس ومن يفعل ذلك ابتغاء مرضاة الله فسوف نؤتيه اجرا عظيما وقال تعالى وإن طائفتان من المؤمنين اقتتلوا فأصلحوا بينهما الآية والاصلاح نهي عن البغي وإعادة إلى الطاعة فإن لم يفعل فقد أمر الله تعالى بقتاله فقال فقاتلوا التي تبغي حتى تفيء إلى أمر الله وذلك هو النهي عن المنكر وأما الأخب
9:52.english: Corruption, and Allah the Exalted said: 'O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives.' And that is commanding the good (al-ma'ruf) to parents and relatives. And Allah the Exalted said: 'There is no good in most of their secret conversations except for one who orders charity or good (ma'ruf) or reconciliation between people. And whoever does that seeking the pleasure of Allah - then We are going to give him a great reward.' And Allah the Exalted said: 'And if two factions among the believers should fight, then make settlement between them...' the verse, and reconciliation is forbidding transgression and returning to obedience. If they do not do so, then Allah the Exalted has commanded to fight them, so He said: 'Then fight the one that transgresses until it returns to the command of Allah.' And that is forbidding the evil (al-munkar). As for the reports, among them is what was narrated from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said in a sermon he delivered: 'O people, you recite this verse and interpret it contrary to its interpretation: "O you who have believed, upon you is [responsibility for] yourselves. Those who have gone astray will not harm you when you have been guided."' The hadith of Abu Bakr: 'O people, you recite this verse and interpret it contrary to its interpretation: "O you who have believed, upon you is [responsibility for] yourselves..."' The hadith was reported by the compilers of the Sunan and preceded in the chapter on seclusion (al-'uzlah). And I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: 'There is no people who commit sins and among them is one who is able to forbid them but does not do so, except that Allah is about to encompass them with a punishment from Himself.' And it was narrated from Abu Tha'labah al-Khushani that he asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, about the interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: 'Those who have gone astray will not harm you when you have been guided.' The hadith of Abu Tha'labah that he asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, about the interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: 'Those who have gone astray will not harm you when you have been guided.' The hadith was reported by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi who graded it as good (hasan), and Ibn Majah. So he said: 'O Abu Tha'labah, command the good (al-ma'ruf) and forbid the evil (al-munkar). But if you see stinginess obeyed, desire (hawa) followed, worldly life given preference, and every possessor of an opinion admiring his own opinion, then upon you is yourself and leave the common people. Indeed, behind you are trials (fitan) like pieces of a dark night; for the one who holds fast in them to something like what you are upon, there is the reward of fifty of you.' It was said: 'Or from them, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'No, rather from you, because you find helpers for good (al-khayr) and they do not find helpers for it.' And Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked about the interpretation of this verse, so he said: 'Indeed, this is not its time; today it is accepted, but it is about to come a time when you command the good (al-ma'ruf) and such and such is done to you, and you say, but it is not accepted from you. Then at that time, upon you is yourselves; those who have gone astray will not harm you when you have been guided.' And the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'You must command the good (al-ma'ruf) and forbid the evil (al-munkar), or Allah will empower over you the worst of you, then the best of you will supplicate and they will not be answered.' The hadith: 'You must command the good (al-ma'ruf) and forbid the evil (al-munkar), or Allah will empower...'
9:52.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

9:60.arabic: الخامس: أن يقسم ماله بعدد الأصناف الموجودين في بلده فإن استيعاب الأصناف واجب وعليه يدل ظاهر قوله تعالى ﴿ إنما الصدقات للفقراء والمساكين ﴾ {التوبة: 60} الآية فإنه يشبه قول المريض إنما ثلث مالي للفقراء والمساكين وذلك يقتضي التشريك في التمليك والعبادات ينبغي أن يتوقى عن الهجوم فيها على الظواهر وقد عدم من الثمانية صنفان في أكثر البلاد وهم المؤلفة قلوبهم والعاملون على الزكاة ويوجد في جميع البلاد أربعة أصناف: الفقراء والمساكين والغارمون والمسافرون أعني أبناء السبيل وصنفان يوجدان في بعض البلاد دون البع
9:60.english: Fifth: That he divides his wealth according to the number of categories present in his locality, for encompassing all categories is obligatory, and upon this indicates the apparent meaning of His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, the alms (Sadaqat) are for the poor (Fuqara) and the needy (Masakin)' (At-Tawbah: 60) the verse. For it resembles the statement of a sick person: 'Indeed, one-third of my wealth is for the poor (Fuqara) and the needy (Masakin),' and that necessitates shared ownership, and acts of worship (Ibadat) should be cautious from rushing into their apparent meanings. And two categories from the eight are absent in most lands: those whose hearts are to be reconciled (Mu'allafati Qulubuhum) and those employed over the alms (Zakat). And there exist in all lands four categories: the poor (Fuqara), the needy (Masakin), the debtors (Gharimin), and the travelers (Musafirun), meaning the wayfarers (Ibn as-Sabil). And two categories exist in some lands and not others: the fighters (Ghuzat) and those in bondage (Mukatibun). So if five categories are found, for example, he divides his alms (Zakat) wealth among them into five equal or approximate portions and designates for each category a portion. Then he divides each portion into three shares or more, either equal or unequal, and it is not upon him to equalize among individuals of the category, for he may divide it among ten or twenty, decreasing each one's share. But as for the categories, they do not accept increase and decrease, so it is not appropriate to decrease in each category below three if found.
9:60.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

9:60.arabic: وبلغنا أن عبد الرحمن بن عوف قدمت عليه عير من اليمن فضجت المدينة ضجة واحدة فقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها: ما هذا؟ قيل عير قدمت لعبد الرحمن، قالت: صدق الله ورسوله ﭬ، فبلغ ذلك عبد الرحمن فسألها فقالت سمعت رسول الله ﭬ يقول: "إني رأيت الجنة فرأيت فقراء المهاجرين والمسلمين يدخلون سعياً، ولم أرد أحداً من الأغنياء يدخلها معهم إلا عبد الرحمن بن عوف يدخلها معهم حبوا"[107] فقال عبد الرحمن: إن العير وما عليها في سبيل الله، وإن إرقاءها أحراراً لعلي أدخلها معهم سعياً.
9:60.english: And it reached us that a caravan from Yemen arrived for 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, and Medina resounded with a single uproar. 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "What is this?" It was said: "A caravan has arrived for 'Abd al-Rahman." She said: "Allah and His Messenger have spoken the truth." This reached 'Abd al-Rahman, and he asked her about it. She said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: 'Indeed, I saw Paradise, and I saw the poor among the Emigrants and the Muslims entering it swiftly, and I did not desire any of the wealthy to enter it with them except 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, who enters it with them crawling.'"[107] 'Abd al-Rahman said: "The caravan and what is upon it are in the path of Allah (fi sabil Allah), and indeed, freeing its slaves (irqa'uha ahraaran) so that perhaps I may enter it with them swiftly."
9:60.book_title: Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth
9:60.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

9:60.arabic: الأخبار فقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم من الذنوب ذنوب لا يكفرها إلا الهم في طلب المعيشة حديث من الذنوب ذنوب لا يكفرها إلا الهم في طلب المعيشة تقدم في النكاح وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم التاجر الصدوق يحشر يوم القيامة مع الصديقين والشهداء حديث التاجر الصدوق يحشر يوم القيامة مع الصديقين والشهداء أخرجه الترمذي والحاكم من حديث أبي سعيد قال الترمذي حسن وقال الحاكم إنه من مراسيل الحسن ولابن ماجه والحاكم نحوه من حديث ابن عمر وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من طلب الدنيا حلالا وتعففا عن المسئلة وسعيا على عياله وتعطفا عل
9:60.english: The narrations: Indeed, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Among sins are sins that are not expiated except by the anxiety (al-hamm) in seeking livelihood (al-ma'īsha).' The hadith: 'Among sins are sins that are not expiated except by the anxiety in seeking livelihood' was previously mentioned in the chapter on marriage. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The truthful merchant (al-tājir al-ṣadūq) will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection with the truthful ones (al-ṣiddīqīn) and the martyrs (al-shuhadā').' The hadith: 'The truthful merchant will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection with the truthful ones and the martyrs' was reported by al-Tirmidhī and al-Ḥākim from the narration of Abū Sa'īd. Al-Tirmidhī said it is ḥasan, and al-Ḥākim said it is from the mursalāt of al-Ḥasan. And Ibn Mājah and al-Ḥākim have something similar from the narration of Ibn 'Umar. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever seeks the worldly life (al-dunyā) lawfully (ḥalālan) and with abstinence (ta'affufan) from begging (al-mas'ala) and striving (sa'yan) for his dependents (al-'iyāl) and compassion (ta'ṭufan) for his neighbor will meet Allah with his face like the moon on the night of the full moon (al-badr).' The hadith: 'Whoever seeks the worldly life lawfully and with abstinence from begging and striving for his dependents' was reported by Abū al-Shaykh in Kitāb al-Thawāb, Abū Nu'aym in al-Ḥilya, and al-Bayhaqī in Shu'ab al-Īmān from the narration of Abū Hurayra with a weak chain. And the Prophet (peace be upon him) was sitting with his companions one day when they looked at a young man with vigor (jild) and strength (quwwa) who had risen early striving (yas'ā). They said: 'Woe to this one, if only his youth and vigor were in the path of Allah (fī sabīl Allāh).' So the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not say this, for if he is striving for himself to suffice it (li-yakfīhā) from begging and enrich it (li-yughnīhā) from people, then he is in the path of Allah. And if he is striving for weak parents or weak offspring to enrich them and suffice them, then he is in the path of Allah. And if he is striving for boasting (tafākhuran) and rivalry (takāthuran), then he is in the path of Satan (al-shayṭān).' The hadith: 'The Prophet (peace be upon him) was sitting with his companions one day when he looked at a young man with vigor and strength who had risen early striving. They said: 'Woe to this one, if only his vigor were in the path of Allah'' was reported by al-Ṭabarānī in his three Mu'jams from the narration of Ka'b bin 'Ajra with a weak chain. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah loves the servant (al-'abd) who takes up a profession (al-mihna) to become independent (li-yastaghnī) from people, and hates the servant who learns knowledge (al-'ilm) and takes it as a profession.' The hadith: 'Indeed, Allah loves the servant who takes up a profession to become independent from people' was not found exactly like this. And Abū Manṣūr al-Daylamī reported in Musnad al-Firdaws from the narration of 'Alī: 'Indeed, Allah loves to see His servant tired (ta'aban) in seeking the lawful (al-ḥalāl),' and in it is Muḥammad bin Sahl al-'Aṭṭār. Al-Dāraquṭnī said he fabricates hadith. And in the report: 'Indeed, Allah the Exalted loves the believing craftsman (al-mu'min al-muḥtarrif).' The hadith: 'Indeed, Allah loves the believing craftsman' was reported by al-Ṭabarānī and Ibn 'Adī and they weakened it from the narration of Ibn 'Umar. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The most lawful (aḥall) thing a man eats is from his earnings (kasb), and every blessed sale (bay' mabrūr).' The hadith: 'The most lawful thing a man eats is from his earnings, and every blessed sale' was reported by Aḥmad from the narration of Rāfi' bin Khadīj. It was said: 'O Messenger of Allah, which earnings are best?' He said: 'A...'
9:60.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Earning'

9:71.arabic: وقال تعالى والمؤمنون والمؤمنات بعضهم أولياء بعض يأمرون بالمعروف وينهون عن المنكر ويقيمون الصلاة فقد نعت المؤمنين بأنهم يأمرون بالمعروف وينهون عن المنكر فالذي هجر الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر خارج عن هؤلاء المؤمنين المنعوتين في هذه الآية
9:71.english: And He, the Exalted, said: 'And the believing men and believing women are allies of one another. They enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and establish the prayer (Salah).' So He described the believers as those who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. Therefore, the one who abandons enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong is outside of these believers described in this verse.
9:71.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

9:71.arabic: قال الله تعالى والمؤمنون والمؤمنات بعضهم أولياء بعض يأمرون بالمعروف الآية وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المؤمن للمؤمن كالبنيان يشد بعضه بعضا حديث المؤمن للمؤمن كالبنيان يشد بعضه بعضا متفق عليه من حديث أبي موسى وقد تقدم في الباب الثالث من آداب الصحبة وقد مكنت في الأرض وهذا كتاب الله وسنة رسوله فإن انقدت لهما شكرت لمن أعانك لحرمتهما وإن استكبرت عنهما ولم تنقد لما لزمك منهما فإن الذي إليه أمرك وبيده عزك وذلك قد شرط أنه لا يضيع اجر من أحسن عملا فقل الآن ما شئت
9:71.english: Allah the Exalted said: 'And the believing men and believing women are allies (awliya) of one another. They enjoin what is right (al-ma'ruf) and forbid what is wrong (al-munkar) and establish prayer (al-salah) and give zakah and obey Allah and His Messenger. Those - Allah will have mercy upon them. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.' (Quran 9:71) And the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'The believer to the believer is like a building, one part strengthening another.' The hadith 'The believer to the believer is like a building, one part strengthening another' is agreed upon from the narration of Abu Musa, and it has preceded in the third chapter of the Etiquettes of Companionship. And you have been established in the earth, and this is the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger. So if you submit to them, you will be grateful to whoever assists you due to their sanctity, and if you are arrogant toward them and do not submit to what is incumbent upon you from them, then the One to whom your affair belongs and in Whose hand is your might, He has stipulated that He does not waste the reward of one who does good work. So say now whatever you wish.
9:71.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

9:72.arabic: وقال الله تعالى: " ولدينا مزيد ". قال بعض المفسرين: يأتي أهل الجنة في وقت المزيد ثلاث تحف من عند رب العالمين؛ أحداها: هدية من عند الله تعالى ليس عندهم في الجنان مثلها فذلك قوله تعالى: " فلا تعلم نفس ما أخفي لهم من قرة أعين " والثانية: السلام عليهم من ربهم، فيزيد ذلك على الهدية فضلاً وهو قوله تعالى: " سلام قولاً من رب رحيم " والثالثة: يقول الله تعالى: إني عنكم راض فيكون ذلك أفضل من الهدية والتسليم فذلك قوله تعالى: " ورضوان من الله أكبر " أي من النعيم الذي هم فيه فهذا فضل رضا الله تعالى وهو ثمرة ر
9:72.english: And Allah the Exalted said: "And with Us is more." Some interpreters said: The people of Paradise receive at the time of increase three gifts from the Lord of the worlds; the first: a gift from Allah the Exalted that they have nothing like in the Gardens, and that is His saying: "So no soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort of eyes." And the second: Peace upon them from their Lord, and that increases over the gift in favor, and that is His saying: "Peace, a word from a Merciful Lord." And the third: Allah the Exalted says: I am pleased with you, and that becomes better than the gift and the greeting, and that is His saying: "And pleasure (Ridwan) from Allah is greater," meaning than the bliss they are in, so this is the favor of Allah's pleasure (Ridwan) and it is the fruit of the servant's pleasure (Rida).
9:72.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

9:72.arabic: وقال تعالى: " ومساكن طيبة في جنات عدن ورضوان من الله أكبر " فقد رفع الله الرضا فوق جنات عدن كما رفع ذكره الصلاة حيث قال: " إن الصلاة تنهي عن الفحشاء والمنكر ولذكر الله أكبر " فكما أن مشاهدة المذكور في الصلاة أكبر من الصلاة فرضوان رب الجنة أعلى من الجنة بل هو غاية مطلب سكان الجنان.
9:72.english: And Allah the Exalted said: "And goodly dwellings in Gardens of Eden and pleasure (Ridwan) from Allah is greater." For Allah has elevated pleasure (Ridha) above the Gardens of Eden, just as He elevated its mention of prayer where He said: "Indeed, prayer prevents from immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah is greater." So just as witnessing the Remembered One in prayer is greater than prayer, the pleasure (Ridwan) of the Lord of the Garden is higher than the Garden, indeed it is the ultimate goal of the inhabitants of the Gardens.
9:72.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

9:72.arabic: [223] حديث سئل عن قوله تعالى - ومساكن طيبة فى جنات عدن - قال قصور من لؤلؤ الحديث أخرجه أبو الشيخ ابن حبان فى كتاب العظمة والآجرى فى كتاب النصيحة من رواية الحسن بن خليفة عن الحسن قال سألت أبا هريرة وعمران بن حصين فى هذه الآية ولا يصح والحسن ابن خليفة لم يعرفه ابن أبى حاتم والحسن البصرى لم يسمع من أبى هريرة على قول الجمهور.
9:72.english: [223] A hadith: He was asked about the saying of Allah the Exalted - 'and goodly dwellings in gardens of perpetual abode (Jannat 'Adn)' - he said: palaces of pearl. The hadith was reported by Abu al-Shaykh Ibn Hibban in Kitab al-'Azamah and al-Ajurri in Kitab al-Nasihah from the narration of al-Hasan ibn Khalifah from al-Hasan. He said: I asked Abu Hurayrah and 'Imran ibn Husayn about this verse, and it is not authentic (la yasihh). Al-Hasan ibn Khalifah was not known by Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Hasan al-Basri did not hear from Abu Hurayrah according to the saying of the majority (al-jumhur).
9:72.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Book of Repentance'

9:72.arabic: (وسئل رسول الله ﭬ عن قوله ﴿ ومساكن طيبة فى جنات عدن ﴾ {} قال: قصور من لؤلؤ فى كل قصر سبعون دارا من ياقوت أحمر فى كل دارسبعون بيتا من زمرد أخضر فى كل بيت سرير على كل سرير سبعون فراشا من كل لون على كل فراش زوجة من الحور العين فى كل بيت سبعون مائدة على كل مائدة سبعون لونا من الطعام فى كل بيت سبعون وصيفة ويعطى المؤمن فى كل غداة يعنى من القوة ما يأتي على ذلك أجمع[223]).
9:72.english: (And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was asked about His saying: 'And pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual abode (Jannat 'Adn)' {} He said: Palaces of pearl, in every palace seventy houses of red ruby, in every house seventy rooms of green emerald, in every room a bed, on every bed seventy couches of every color, on every couch a wife from the wide-eyed maidens (Al-Hur al-'Ayn), in every house seventy tables, on every table seventy colors of food, in every house seventy handmaidens, and the believer is given every morning - meaning from the strength - what suffices for all of that [223]).
9:72.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Book of Repentance'

9:73.arabic: أما التفريط: فبفقد هذه القوة أو ضعفها وذلك مذموم، وهو الذي يقال فيه إنه لا حمية له. ولذلك قال الشافعي رحمه الله من استغضب فلم يغضب فهو حمار. فمن فقد قوة الغضب والحمية أصلاً فهو ناقص جداً، وقد وصف الله سبحانه أصحاب النبي ﷺ بالشدة والحمية فقال "أشداء على الكفار رحماء بينهم" وقال لنبيه ﷺ "جاهد الكفار والمنافقين واغلظ عليهم" الآية وإنما الغلظة والشدة من آثار قوة الحمية وهو الغضب.
9:73.english: As for deficiency: it is by the loss of this power or its weakness, and that is blameworthy, and it is said of him that he has no zeal (Hamiyyah). Therefore, Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: 'Whoever is provoked to anger and does not get angry is a donkey.' So whoever loses the power of anger and zeal (Hamiyyah) entirely is very deficient, and Allah the Exalted has described the companions of the Prophet ﷺ with severity and zeal (Hamiyyah), saying: 'Severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves' and said to His Prophet ﷺ: 'Fight (Jahid) the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh (Ighluz) upon them' the verse, and indeed harshness (Ghilzah) and severity are from the effects of the power of zeal (Hamiyyah), which is anger.
9:73.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

9:75.arabic: فأنزل الله تعالى في ثعلبة "ومنهم من عاهد الله لئن آتانا من فضله لنصدقن ولنكونن من الصالحين، فلما آتاهم من فضله بخلوا به وتولوا وهم معرضون، فأعقبهم نفاقاً في قلوبهم إلى يوم يلقونه بما أخلفوا الله ما وعدوه وبما كانوا يكذبون" وعند رسول الله ﷺ رجل من أقارب ثعلبة، فسمع ما أنزل الله فيه، فخرج حتى أتى ثعلبة فقال: لا أم لك يا ثعلبة! قد أنزل الله فيك كذا، فخرج ثعلبة حتى أتي النبي ﷺ فسأله أن يقبل منه صدقته فقال "إن الله منعني أن أقبل منك صدقتك، فجعل يحثو على التراب على رأسه فقال رسول الله ﷺ "هذا عملك أمرت
9:75.english: Then Allah the Exalted revealed regarding Tha'labah: "And among them is he who made a covenant with Allah: 'If He gives us from His bounty, we will surely spend in charity and be among the righteous.' But when He gave them from His bounty, they withheld it and turned away while they were refusing. So He penalized them with hypocrisy in their hearts until the Day they will meet Him, because they failed Allah in what they promised Him and because they used to lie.'" And with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was a man from Tha'labah's relatives, and he heard what Allah revealed about him, so he went out until he came to Tha'labah and said: "May your mother be bereft of you, O Tha'labah! Allah has revealed such and such about you." So Tha'labah went out until he came to the Prophet (peace be upon him) and asked him to accept his charity from him, so he said: "Indeed Allah has prevented me from accepting your charity from you." So he began to scatter dust upon his head, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "This is your deed; I commanded you but you did not obey me."
9:75.book_title: Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth
9:75.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

9:75.arabic: وقال مجاهد رجلان خرجا على ملأ من الناس قعود فقالا إن رزقنا الله تعالى مالا لنتصدقن فبخلوا به فنزلت ومنهم من عاهد الله لئن آتانا من فضله لنصدقن ولنكونن من الصالحين وقال بعضهم إنما هو شىء نووه في أنفسهم لم يتكلموا به فقال ومنهم من عاهد الله لئن آتانا من فضله لنصدقن ولنكونن من الصالحين فلما آتاهم من فضله بخلوا به وتولوا وهم معرضون فأعقبهم نفاقا في قلوبهم إلى يوم يلقونه بما أخلفوا الله ما وعدوه وبما كانوا يكذبون فجعل العزم عهدا وجعل الخلف فيه كذبا والوفاء به صدقا وهذا الصدق أشد من الصدق الثالث فإن ا
9:75.english: And Mujahid said: Two men went out before a sitting crowd of people and said: 'If Allah (The Exalted) provides us with wealth, we will surely give charity.' Then they became stingy with it, so was revealed: 'And among them is he who made a covenant (ʿāhada) with Allah: "If He gives us from His bounty, we will surely spend in charity, and we will surely be among the righteous."' And some of them said: 'It is only something they resolved in their souls (anfus) without speaking it.' So He said: 'And among them is he who made a covenant (ʿāhada) with Allah: "If He gives us from His bounty, we will surely spend in charity, and we will surely be among the righteous."' Then when He gave them from His bounty, they were stingy with it and turned away while they were averse. So He penalized them with hypocrisy (nifāq) in their hearts (qulūb) until the Day they will meet Him, because they failed Allah in what they promised Him and because they used to lie. So He made the resolution (ʿazm) a covenant (ʿahd), and made breaking it a lie (kadhib), and fulfilling it truthfulness (ṣidq). And this truthfulness (ṣidq) is more severe than the third truthfulness (ṣidq), for people may be generous with resolution (ʿazm), then falter at fulfillment due to its severity upon them and due to the agitation of desire (shahwa) when capability and attainment of means occur. And for that reason, ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) made an exception, saying: 'For me to go forward and have my neck struck is more beloved to me than to command a people among whom is Abu Bakr, except, O Allah, that my soul (nafs) suggests to me at the time of killing something I do not find now, for I do not feel secure that it may become heavy upon it, so it changes from its resolution (ʿazm).' And he indicated by that to the severity of fulfilling the resolution (ʿazm).
9:75.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

9:81.arabic: وتمرغ في الرمضاء وكان يقول لنفسه: ونار جهنم أشد حرا
9:81.english: And he rolled in the hot sand and was saying to his Soul (Nafs): 'And the Fire of Hell is more severe in heat.'
9:81.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

9:82.arabic: بل أقول كل ما ورد في فضل البكاء من خشية الله فهو إظهار لفضيلة الخشية فإن البكاء ثمرة الخشية فقد قال تعالى: ﴿ فليضحكوا قليلا وليبكوا كثيرا ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ يبكون ويزيدهم خشوعا ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل: ﴿ أفمن هذا الحديث تعجبون وتضحكون ولا تبكون وأنتم سامدون ﴾ {}
9:82.english: Rather, I say: Everything that has come regarding the virtue of weeping from fear (Khashya) of Allah is a manifestation of the virtue of fear (Khashya), for weeping is the fruit of fear (Khashya). Indeed, Allah the Exalted has said: 'So let them laugh a little and weep much' (Quran 9:82). And Allah the Exalted has said: 'They weep, and it increases them in humility (Khashūʿan)' (Quran 17:109). And Allah the Mighty and Majestic has said: 'Then at this statement do you wonder? And you laugh and do not weep, while you are proudly sporting?' (Quran 53:59-61).
9:82.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Fear and Hope'

9:87.arabic: فأما الدعاء فقد تعبدنا به، وكثرت دعوات رسول الله ﭬ وسائر الأنبياء عليهم السلام - على ما نقلناه في كتاب الدعوات - تدل عليه. ولقد كان رسول الله ﭬ في أعلى المقامات من الرضا. وقد أثنى الله تعالى على بعض عباده بقوله "ويدعوننا رغباً رهباً " وأما إنكار المعاصي وكراهتها وعدم الرضا بها فقد تعبد الله به عباده وذمهم على الرضا به فقال: " ورضوا بالحياة الدنيا واطمأنوا بها "، وقال تعالى: " رضوا بأن يكونوا مع الخوالف وطبع على قلوبهم ". وفي الخبر المشهور " من شهد منكراً فرضي به فكأنه قد فعله ".
9:87.english: As for supplication (Dua), we have been commanded to perform it, and the numerous supplications of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and the other prophets (upon them be peace) - as we have transmitted in the Book of Supplications - indicate this. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was at the highest stations (Maqamat) of contentment (Rida). And Allah the Exalted has praised some of His servants by His saying: "And they call upon Us in hope and fear." As for rejecting sins (Ma'asi), disliking them, and not being content with them, Allah has commanded His servants with this and censured them for being content with it, saying: "And they were content with the worldly life and were satisfied with it," and He the Exalted said: "They were content to be with those who stay behind, and a seal was set upon their hearts (Qulub)." And in the famous report: "Whoever witnesses an evil (Munkar) and is content with it, it is as if he has done it."
9:87.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

9:91.arabic: وقال الأوزاعي: خرج الناس يستسقون فقام فيهم بلال بن سعد فحمد الله وأثنى عليه. ثم قال يا معشر من حضر ألستم مقرين بالإساءة فقالوا اللهم نعم فقال اللهم إنا قد سمعناك تقول: ﴿ ما على المحسنين من سبيل ﴾ وقد أقررنا بالإساءة فهل تكون مغفرتك إلا لمثلنا اللهم فاغفر لنا وارحمنا واسقنا فرفع يديه ورفعوا أيديهم فسقوا
9:91.english: And Al-Awza'i said: The people went out seeking rain, and Bilal ibn Sa'd stood among them, praising Allah and extolling Him. Then he said: 'O gathering of those present, are you not acknowledging wrongdoing?' They said: 'O Allah, yes.' He said: 'O Allah, we have heard You say: "There is no blame upon the doers of good (Al-Muhsinin)." And we have acknowledged wrongdoing, so would Your forgiveness be except for the likes of us? O Allah, forgive us, have mercy upon us, and give us rain.' So he raised his hands, and they raised their hands, and they were given rain.
9:91.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

9:96.arabic: فإذن نعم الله تعالى آلات يترقى العبد بها عن اسفل السافلين خلقها الله تعالى لاجل العبد حتى ينال بها سعادة القرب والله تعالى غني عنه قرب ام بعد والعبد فيها بين ان يستعملها في الطاعة فيكون قد شكر لموافقة محبة مولاه وبين ان يستعملها في معصيته فقد كفر لاقتحامه ما يكرهه مولاه ولا يرضاه له فإن الله لا يرضى لعباده الكفر والمعصية وان عطلها ولم يستعملها في طاعة ولا معصية فهو ايضا كفر كفران إن للنعمة بالتضييع وكل ما خلق في الدنيا انما خلق آلة للعبد ليتوصل به الى سعادة الاخرة ونيل القرب من الله تعالى فكل مط
9:96.english: Therefore, the blessings (Ni'am) of Allah the Exalted are instruments by which the servant (Al-'Abd) ascends from the lowest of the low. Allah the Exalted created them for the sake of the servant so that he may attain through them the happiness (Sa'ada) of closeness (Qurb) [to Allah]. Allah the Exalted is independent of him, whether near or far. The servant is in them between using them in obedience (Ta'a), in which case he has given thanks (Shukr) by conforming to the love (Mahabbah) of his Master (Mawla), and using them in disobedience (Ma'siya), in which case he has disbelieved (Kafara) by plunging into what his Master dislikes and does not approve for him. For Allah does not approve for His servants disbelief (Kufr) and disobedience (Ma'siya). And if he neglects them and does not use them in obedience or disobedience, that is also disbelief (Kufr), a denial (Kufran) of the blessing (Ni'ma) through waste. Everything created in this world is only created as an instrument for the servant to reach through it the happiness (Sa'ada) of the Hereafter and attainment of closeness (Qurb) to Allah the Exalted. Every obedient one is, according to his obedience, thankful (Shakir) for the blessing (Ni'ma) of Allah in the means (Asbab) he used in obedience. Every lazy one who abandoned use or disobedient one who used them on the path of distance (B'ud) is a disbeliever (Kafir), straying outside the love (Mahabbah) of Allah the Exalted. Disobedience (Ma'siya) and obedience (Ta'a) both encompass them the will (Mashiyya), but they do not encompass them the love (Mahabbah) and dislike (Karahah). Rather, some desired things are beloved (Mahbub) and some desired things are disliked (Makruh).
9:96.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

9:99.arabic: الصدق السادس وهو أعلى الدرجات وأعزها الصدق في مقامات الدين كالصدق في الخوف والرجاء والتعظيم والزهد والرضا والتوكل والحب وسائر هذه الأمور فإن هذه الأمور لها مباد ينطلق الاسم بظهورها ثم لها غايات وحقائق والصادق المحقق من نال حقيقتها وإذا غلب الشيء وتمت حقيقته سمى صاحبه صادقا فيه كما يقال فلان صدق القتال ويقال هذا هو الخوف الصادق وهذه هي الشهوة الصادقة وقال الله تعالى إنما المؤمنون الذين آمنوا بالله ورسوله ثم لم يرتابوا إلى قوله أولئك هم الصادقون وقال تعالى (ولكن البر من آمن بالله واليوم الآخر ...
9:99.english: The sixth truthfulness (Sidq), which is the highest of degrees and most precious, is truthfulness in the stations (Maqamat) of the religion (Deen) such as truthfulness in fear (Khawf), hope (Raja'), veneration (Ta'zim), asceticism (Zuhd), contentment (Rida), reliance (Tawakkul), love (Hubb), and all these matters. For these matters have beginnings from which the name is launched by their appearance, then they have ends and realities (Haqa'iq), and the truthful verifier (Sadiq Muhaqqiq) is the one who attains their reality. And when a thing prevails and its reality is complete, its possessor is called truthful in it, as it is said: 'So-and-so was truthful in fighting (Sadaqa al-Qital)', and it is said: 'This is the truthful fear (al-Khawf al-Sadiq)', and 'This is the truthful desire (al-Shahwah al-Sadiqah)'. And Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, the believers are those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and then have not doubted...' to His saying: '...those are the truthful ones (al-Sadiqun)'. And He said: 'But righteousness (al-Birr) is [in] one who believes in Allah, the Last Day...' to His saying: '...those are the ones who have been truthful (Sadaqu)'. And Abu Dharr was asked about faith (Iman), so he recited this verse. It was said to him: 'We asked you about faith', so he said: 'I asked the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, about faith, and he recited this verse.' [61] And let us strike an example for fear: There is no servant who believes in Allah and the Last Day except that he fears Allah with a fear that the name is launched upon, but it is a fear that is not truthful, meaning it does not reach the degree of reality. Do you not see him when he fears a ruler or a highway robber on his journey, how his color pales, his limbs tremble, his life becomes bitter, his eating and sleeping become difficult, and his thought is divided until his family and children do not benefit from him, and he may be disturbed from his homeland, substituting familiarity with loneliness, and ease with fatigue, hardship, and exposure to dangers, all that out of fear of encountering the dreaded thing? Then he fears the Fire, yet nothing of that appears upon him when a sin befalls him. Therefore, he, peace be upon him, said: 'I have not seen anything like the Fire whose fleer sleeps, nor like Paradise whose seeker sleeps.' The hadith 'I have not seen anything like the Fire whose fleer sleeps' has preceded. So verification (Tahqiq) in these matters is very rare, and there is no end to these stations until their completion is attained, but every servant has a share according to his state, either weak or strong. So when it becomes strong, he is called truthful in it. Thus, the knowledge (Ma'rifah) of Allah the Exalted, His veneration (Ta'zim), and fear (Khawf) of Him have no end.
9:99.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

9:100.arabic: أما من الآيات فقوله تعالى: " رضي الله عنهم ورضوا عنه "، وقد قال تعالى: " هل جزاء الإحسان إلا الإحسان " ومنتهى الإحسان رضا الله عن عبده وهو ثواب رضا العبد عن الله تعالى. وقال تعالى: " ومساكن طيبة في جنات عدن ورضوان من الله أكبر " فقد رفع الله الرضا فوق جنات عدن كما رفع ذكره الصلاة حيث قال: " إن الصلاة تنهي عن الفحشاء والمنكر ولذكر الله أكبر " فكما أن مشاهدة المذكور في الصلاة أكبر من الصلاة فرضوان رب الجنة أعلى من الجنة بل هو غاية مطلب سكان الجنان.
9:100.english: As for from the verses, there is His saying, the Exalted: "Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him," and He, the Exalted, has said: "Is the reward for good except good?" And the ultimate good is Allah's pleasure with His servant, and it is the reward for the servant's pleasure with Allah, the Exalted. And He, the Exalted, said: "And pleasant dwellings in Gardens of Eternity, and the pleasure (Ridwan) from Allah is greater." For Allah has elevated the pleasure (Ridwan) above the Gardens of Eternity, just as He elevated His remembrance (Dhikr) above prayer when He said: "Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah is greater." So just as witnessing the Remembered One in prayer is greater than the prayer, the pleasure (Ridwan) of the Lord of the Garden is higher than the Garden; rather, it is the ultimate goal of the inhabitants of the Gardens.
9:100.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

9:102.arabic: الحالة الثالثة أن يكون الحرب سجالا بين الجندين فتارة له اليد عليها وتارة لها عليه وهذا من المجاهدين يعد مثله لا من الظافرين وأهل هذه الحالة هم الذين خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا عسى الله ان يتوب عليهم هذا باعتبار القوة والضعف ويتطرق إليه أيضا ثلاثة أحوال باعتبار عدد ما يصبر عنه فإنه إما أن يغلب جميع الشهوات أو لا يغلب شيئا منها أو يغلب بعضها دون بعض وتنزيل قوله تعالى: ﴿ خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا ﴾ {} على من عجز عن بعض الشهوات دون بعض أولى
9:102.english: The third state is that the war is back-and-forth between the two armies, so sometimes he has the upper hand over it, and sometimes it has the upper hand over him. This one from the strugglers (Mujahidin) is considered like him, not from the victorious ones. The people of this state are those who mixed a righteous deed and another evil one; perhaps Allah will turn to them in forgiveness. This is with consideration of strength and weakness. And it also approaches three states with consideration of the number of what he abstains from, for he either overcomes all the desires (Shahawat) or does not overcome anything of them, or overcomes some of them without others. And the application of His saying, the Exalted: 'They mixed a righteous deed and another evil one' {} upon the one who is incapable regarding some of the desires (Shahawat) without others is more appropriate.
9:102.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

9:102.arabic: فمن أراد أن يدخل الجنة بغير حساب فليستغرق أوقاته في الطاعة ومن أراد أن تترجح كفة حسناته وتثقل موازين خيراته فليستوعب في الطاعة أكثر أوقاته فإن خلط عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا فأمره مخطر ولكن الرجاء غير منقطع والعفو من كرم الله منتظر فعسى الله تعالى أن يغفر له بجوده وكرمه فهذا ما انكشف للناظرين بنور البصيرة فإن لم تكن من أهله فانظر إلى خطاب الله تعالى لرسوله واقتبسه بنور الإيمان فقد قال الله تعالى لأقرب عبادة إليه وارفعهم درجة لديه: ﴿ إن لك في النهار سبحا طويلا واذكر اسم ربك وتبتل إليه تبتيلا ﴾ {} وقال
9:102.english: Whoever wishes to enter Paradise without reckoning, let him occupy his times in obedience (Taa'ah), and whoever wishes that the scale of his good deeds (Hasanat) be weighted and the balances of his goodness (Khayrat) be heavy, let him encompass in obedience (Taa'ah) most of his times. For if he mixes a righteous deed (Amal Salih) and another evil one (Sayyi'), his affair is perilous, but hope is not cut off, and forgiveness (Afw) from the generosity (Karam) of Allah is awaited. So perhaps Allah, the Exalted, will forgive him by His bounty (Jood) and generosity (Karam). This is what has been unveiled to the observers by the light of insight (Bassirah). If you are not from its people, then look at the address of Allah, the Exalted, to His Messenger and take it by the light of faith (Iman). Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, said to the closest of His worship to Him and the highest of them in degree with Him: 'Indeed, for you in the daytime is prolonged glorification, and remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself to Him with complete devotion.' And He, the Exalted, said: 'And remember the name of your Lord morning and evening, and from the night prostrate to Him and glorify Him a long night.' And He, the Exalted, said: 'And glorify with the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and from the night glorify Him and after the prostrations.' And He, the Glorified, said: 'And glorify with the praise of your Lord when you rise, and from the night glorify Him and after the stars.' And He, the Exalted, said: 'Indeed, the night prayer is more intense and more upright for speech.' And He, the Exalted, said: 'And from the hours of the night glorify and the ends of the day that you may be pleased.' And He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and nearness of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove the evil deeds.' Then see how He described the successful among His servants and with what He described them. He, the Exalted, said: 'Is one who is devoutly obedient during periods of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord? Say, "Are those who know equal to those who do not know?"' And He, the Exalted, said: 'And others have confessed their sins. They mixed a righteous deed (Amal Salih) and another evil one (Sayyi'). Perhaps Allah will turn to them in forgiveness (Tawbah). Indeed, Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.'
9:102.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

9:102.arabic: ويبقى قسم ثالث وهم الأكثرون خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا وقد يخفى عليهم ولا يخفى على الله تعالى ان الغالب حسناتهم أو سيئاتهم ولكن يأبى الله إلا أن يعرفهم ذلك ليبين فضله عند العفو وعدله عند العقاب فتتطاير الصحف والكتب منطوية على الحسنات والسيئات وينصب الميزان وتشخص الأبصار إلى الكتب أتقع فى اليمين أو فى الشمال ثم إلى لسان الميزان أيميل إلى جانب السيئات أو إلى جانب الحسنات وهذه حالة هائلة تطيش فيها عقول الخلائق.
9:102.english: And there remains a third group, and they are the majority, who have mixed a righteous deed and another evil one. And it may be hidden from them, but it is not hidden from Allah, the Exalted, whether their good deeds or their evil deeds are predominant. But Allah refuses except to make them know that, to manifest His favor at the time of pardon and His justice at the time of punishment. So the scrolls and books fly, folded upon the good deeds and the evil deeds, and the Balance (Mizan) is set up, and the gazes are fixed upon the books: will they fall in the right hand or in the left? Then upon the tongue of the Balance: will it incline to the side of the evil deeds or to the side of the good deeds? And this is a tremendous state in which the intellects of the creatures are bewildered.
9:102.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Book of Repentance'

9:102.arabic: ورجل مؤمن خلط عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا لقى العدو فصدق الله حتى قتل فذاك في الدرجة الثالثة
9:102.english: And a believer who mixed a righteous deed (Amal Salih) and another evil one (Sayyi') met the enemy and was truthful to Allah until he was killed, so that one is in the third degree.
9:102.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

9:102.arabic: وليته سلم لنا من الصلاة شطرها أو ثلثها من الوسواس لنكون ممن خلط عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا وعلى الجملة همة الدنيا وهمة الآخرة في القلب مثل الماء الذي يصب في قدح مملوء بخل فبقدر ما ندخل فيه من الماء يخرج منه من الخل لا محالة ولا يجتمعان.
9:102.english: Would that we were safe from distraction (Waswas) for half or a third of our prayer, so that we might be among those who mixed a righteous deed (Amal Salih) and another evil one (Sayyi'). In summary, the aspiration (Himmah) for this world (Dunya) and the aspiration (Himmah) for the Hereafter (Akhirah) in the heart (Qalb) are like water poured into a cup full of vinegar: inevitably, as much as we put in of water, that much vinegar comes out, and the two do not mix.
9:102.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

9:103.arabic: قال "يا ويح ثعلبة يا ويح ثعلبة يا ويح ثعلبة" قال وأنزل الله تعالى "خذ من أموالهم صدقة تطهرهم وتزكيهم بها وصل عليهم إن صلاتك سكن لهم" وأنزل الله تعالى فرائض الصدقة، فبعث رسول الله ﷺ رجلاً من جهينة ورجلاً من بني سليم على الصدقة، وكتب لهما كتاباً بأخذ الصدقة وأمرهما أن يخرجا فيأخذا من المسلمين: وقال "مرا بثعلبة بن حاطب وبفلان -رجل من بني سليم- وخذا صدقاتهما: فخرجا حتى أتيا ثعلبة، فسألاه الصدقة وأقرآه كتاب رسول الله ﷺ فقال ما هذه إلا جزية ما هذه إلا جزية ما هذه إلا أخت الجزية! انطلقا حتى تفرغا ثم تع
