9:103.english: He said, "Woe to Tha'labah, woe to Tha'labah, woe to Tha'labah." He said, and Allah the Exalted revealed, "Take from their wealth a charity (Sadaqah) to purify them and to cause them to grow (Tazkiyah) through it, and pray over them; indeed, your prayer is a tranquility (Sakan) for them." And Allah the Exalted revealed the obligations of charity (Sadaqah), so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a man from Juhaynah and a man from Banu Sulaym for the charity (Sadaqah), and wrote for them a document for taking the charity (Sadaqah) and ordered them to go out and take from the Muslims. And he said, "Go to Tha'labah ibn Hatib and so-and-so—a man from Banu Sulaym—and take their charities (Sadaqat)." So they went until they came to Tha'labah, and they asked him for the charity (Sadaqah) and recited to him the document of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said, "This is nothing but a tax (Jizyah)! This is nothing but a tax (Jizyah)! This is nothing but the sister of the tax (Jizyah)! Go until you finish, then return to me." So they went toward the Sulaymi, and he heard about them, so he rose to the best ages of his camels and prepared them for the charity (Sadaqah), then met them with them. When they saw them, they said, "It is not obligatory upon you, and we do not want to take this from you." He said, "Yes, take them." When they finished from his charities (Sadaqat), they returned until they passed by Tha'labah and asked him for the charity (Sadaqah). He said, "Show me your document." So he looked in it and said, "This is the sister of the tax (Jizyah)! Go until I see my opinion." So they went until they came to the Prophet ﷺ. When he saw them, he said, "Woe to Tha'labah," before they spoke to him, and he supplicated for the Sulaymi. They informed him of what Tha'labah did and what the Sulaymi did. So Allah the Exalted revealed regarding Tha'labah, "And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: 'If He gives us from His bounty, we will surely spend in charity (Sadaqah) and be among the righteous.' But when He gave them from His bounty, they were stingy with it and turned away while they were refusing. So He penalized them with hypocrisy (Nifaq) in their hearts (Qulub) until
9:103.book_title: Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth
9:103.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

9:104.arabic: أحدهما: في حق العاصي المنهمك إذا خطرت له التوبة فقال له الشيطان: وأنى تقبل توبتك فيقنطه من رحمة الله تعالى فيجب عند هذا أن يقمع القنوط بالرجاء ويتذكر "إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعاً" وأن الله كريم يقبل التوبة عن عباده وأن التوبة طاعة تكفر الذنوب قال الله تعالى "قل يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعاً إنه هو الغفور الرحيم وأنيبوا إلى ربكم" أمرهم بالإنابة وقال تعالى "وإني لغفار لمن تاب وآمن وعمل صالحاً ثم اهتدى" فإذا توقع المغفرة مع التوبة فهو راج، وإن توق
9:104.english: One: Regarding the immersed sinner when repentance occurs to him, and Satan says to him: 'How will your repentance be accepted?' thus making him despair of the mercy of Allah the Exalted. At this point, he must suppress despair with hope and remember 'Indeed, Allah forgives all sins' and that Allah is generous in accepting repentance from His servants and that repentance is an obedience that expiates sins. Allah the Exalted said: 'Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves [by sinning], do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful. And return [in repentance] to your Lord."' He commanded them to return [in repentance]. And He said: 'And indeed, I am Forgiving to whoever repents and believes and does righteous work then remains guided.' So if he expects forgiveness with repentance, he is hopeful; but if he expects forgiveness with persistence [in sin], he is deluded, just as one for whom the time of Friday prayer becomes tight while he is in the market, and it occurs to him to hasten to Friday prayer, and Satan says to him: 'You will not catch Friday prayer, so stay in your place.' He rejects Satan and proceeds running while hoping to catch Friday prayer—he is hopeful. But if he continues with trade and begins hoping for the Imam to delay the prayer for his sake until mid-time or for another's sake or for a reason among reasons he does not know—he is deluded.
9:104.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

9:108.arabic: [18] حديث لما نزل قوله تعالى فيه رجال يحبون أن يتطهروا الحديث في أهل قباء وجمعهم بين الحجر والماء أخرجه البزار من حديث ابن عباس بسند ضعيف ورواه ابن ماجه والحاكم وصححه من حديث أبي أيوب وجابر وأنس في الاستنجاء بالماء ليس فيه ذكر الحجر وقول النووي تبعا لابن الصلاح إن الجمع بين الماء والحجر في أهل قباء لا يعرف مردود بما تقدم.
9:108.english: Hadith: When the saying of Allah the Exalted descended: 'In it are men who love to purify themselves (yataṭahharū)'—the hadith is about the people of Quba' and their combining between stone and water. Al-Bazzar transmitted it from the narration of Ibn 'Abbas with a weak chain, and Ibn Majah and Al-Hakim transmitted it and authenticated it from the narration of Abu Ayyub, Jabir, and Anas regarding cleansing with water—there is no mention of stone in it. And the statement of Al-Nawawi, following Ibn Al-Salah, that the combining between water and stone among the people of Quba' is not known is refuted by what preceded.
9:108.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Mysteries of Purity'

9:108.arabic: والجمع بين الماء والحجر مستحب فقد روى: (أنه لما نزل قوله تعالى: ﴿ فيه رجال يحبون أن يتطهروا والله يحب المطهرين ﴾ {} قال رسول الله ﭬ لأهل قباء ما هذه الطهارة التي أثنى الله بها عليكم قالوا كنا نجمع بين الماء والحجر[18]).
9:108.english: And combining water and stone is recommended, for it has been narrated: (That when the saying of Allah, the Exalted, descended: 'In it are men who love to purify themselves, and Allah loves those who purify themselves' (Quran 9:108), the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the people of Quba: 'What is this purification (Taharah) that Allah has praised you for?' They said: 'We used to combine water and stone.'[18])
9:108.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Mysteries of Purity'

9:109.arabic: ومثل الطعامة من الدين مثل الأساس من البنيان فإذا ثبت الأساس وقوي استقام البنيان وارتفع وإذا ضعف الأساس واعوج انهار البنيان ووقع و قال الله عز وجل أفمن أسس بنيانه على تقوى من الله الآية
9:109.english: And the example of food in religion is like the foundation of a building. If the foundation is established and strong, the building becomes upright and rises. And if the foundation weakens and becomes crooked, the building collapses and falls. And Allah the Exalted said: 'Is he who founded his building upon piety (Taqwa) from Allah and [His] approval better, or he who founded his building on the edge of a crumbling, overhanging precipice so it collapsed with him into the fire of Hell? And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.'
9:109.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

9:111.arabic: فبقدر قوة اليقين والمعرفة بالتفاوت بين الدنيا والآخرة تقوى الرغبة في البيع والمعاملة، حتى إن من قوي يقينه يبيع نفسه وماله، كما قال الله تعالى: "إن الله اشترى من المؤمنين أنفسهم وأموالهم بأن لهم الجنة" ثم بين أن صفقتهم رابحة فقال تعالى: "فاستبشروا ببيعكم الذي بايعتم به" فليس يحتاج من العلم في الزهد إلا إلى هذا القدر: وهو أن الآخرة خير وأبقى وقد يعلم ذلك من لا يقدر على ترك الدنيا، إما لضعف علمه ويقينه، وإما لاستيلاء الشهوة في الحال عليه وكونه مقهوراً في يد الشيطان، وإما لاغتراره بمواعيد الشيطان في
9:111.english: According to the strength of certainty (Yaqin) and knowledge (Ma'rifah) of the disparity between this world (Dunya) and the Hereafter (Akhirah), the desire for the transaction and dealing strengthens, until indeed, whoever strengthens his certainty sells his soul (Nafs) and his wealth, as Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their souls (Anfus) and their wealth in exchange for Paradise for them.' Then He clarified that their transaction is profitable, so He the Exalted said: 'So rejoice in your transaction which you have contracted.' So what is needed from knowledge in asceticism (Zuhd) is only this amount: that the Hereafter is better and more lasting. And one may know that but not be able to abandon this world, either due to weakness of his knowledge and certainty, or due to the domination of desire (Shahwah) in the moment upon him and his being overpowered in the hand of Satan (Shaytan), or due to his deception by the promises of Satan in procrastination day after day until death snatches him and nothing remains with him except regret after the passing.
9:111.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

9:111.arabic: وأما المخلصون فإن الله تعالى اشترى منهم أنفسهم وأموالهم بأن لهم الجنة، فلما رأوا أنهم تركوا تمتع عشرين سنة مثلاً أو ثلاثين سنة بتمتع الأبد استبشروا ببيعهم الذي بايعوا به، فهذا بيان المزهود فيه.
9:111.english: As for the sincere ones (Al-Mukhlisun), then Allah the Exalted purchased from them their souls (Anfus) and their wealth (Amwal) in exchange for the Garden (Al-Jannah) for them. When they saw that they had abandoned enjoyment of twenty years, for example, or thirty years, for the enjoyment of eternity, they rejoiced in their sale (Bai') which they had transacted. This is the explanation of what is renounced (Al-Mazhud fih).
9:111.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

9:111.arabic: فأسلم الأحوال عن هذا الخطر خاتمة الشهادة إذ لم يكن قصد الشهيد نيل مال أو أن يقال شجاع أو غير ذلك[63] كما ورد به الخبر بل حب الله عز وجل وإعلاء كلمته فهذه الحالة هي التي عبر عنها: ﴿ إن الله اشترى من المؤمنين أنفسهم واموالهم بأن لهم الجنة ﴾ ومثل هذا الشخص هو البائع للدنيا بالآخرة وحالة الشهيد توافق معنى قولك لا إله إلا الله فإنه لا مقصود له سوى الله عز وجل وكل مقصود معبود وكل معبود إله فهذا الشهيد قائل بلسان حاله لا إله إلا الله إذ لا مقصود له سواه ومن يقول ذلك بلسانه ولم يساعده حاله فأمره في مشيئ
9:111.english: The safest conditions from this danger is the conclusion of martyrdom, since the martyr's intention was not to attain wealth or to be called brave or other such things[63] as the report indicates, but rather love of Allah (God) the Exalted and the elevation of His word. This condition is what is expressed by: 'Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their souls (Anfus) and their wealth in exchange for Paradise for them.' And such a person is the seller of the worldly life for the Hereafter, and the state of the martyr corresponds to the meaning of your saying 'There is no god but Allah (La ilaha illa Allah)', for he has no objective except Allah (God) the Exalted, and every objective is worshipped, and every worshipped is a god. So this martyr is saying with the tongue of his state 'There is no god but Allah (La ilaha illa Allah)', since he has no objective other than Him. And whoever says that with his tongue but his state does not assist him, his affair is in the will of Allah (God) the Exalted, and danger is not secured in his right. And for that reason, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) preferred the saying 'There is no god but Allah (La ilaha illa Allah)' over all other remembrances (Adhkar)[64].
9:111.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter

9:112.arabic: وقال أبو ذر الغفاري قال أبو بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه يا رسول الله هل من جهاد غير قتال المشركين فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم نعم يا أبا بكر إن لله تعالى مجاهدين في الأرض أفضل من الشهداء أحياء مرزوقين يمشون على الأرض يباهي الله بهم ملائكة السماء وتزين لهم الجنة كما تزينت أم سلمة لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال أبو بكر رضي الله عنه يا رسول الله ومن هم قال الآمرون بالمعروف والناهون عن المنكر والمحبون في الله والمبغضون في الله ثم قال والذي نفسي بيده إن العبد منهم ليكون في الغرفة فوق الغرفات فو
9:112.english: And Abu Dharr al-Ghifari said: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'O Messenger of Allah, is there any struggle (Jihad) other than fighting the polytheists?' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, O Abu Bakr. Verily, Allah the Exalted has strugglers (Mujahidin) on earth better than the martyrs, alive and provided for, walking on the earth; Allah boasts of them to the angels of the heavens, and Paradise is adorned for them as Umm Salamah adorned herself for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him).' Then Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'O Messenger of Allah, and who are they?' He said: 'Those who enjoin good (Al-Amirun bil-Ma'ruf) and forbid evil (Wa-N-Nahuna 'anil-Munkar), and those who love for Allah's sake (Al-Muhibbuna fi Allah) and hate for Allah's sake (Wa-l-Mubghiduna fi Allah).' Then he said: 'By the One in Whose Hand is my soul (Nafs), verily, a servant (Abd) from among them will be in a chamber above the chambers, above the chambers of the martyrs; the chamber has three hundred thousand doors, among them ruby and green emerald, on every door is light. And verily, the man from among them will be married to three hundred thousand wide-eyed houris (Hura' Qasirat at-Tarf 'Ayn); every time he turns to one of them and looks at her, she says to him: 'Do you remember such-and-such a day when you enjoined good (Amarta bil-Ma'ruf) and forbade evil (Wa-Nahayta 'anil-Munkar)?' Every time he looks at one of them, she reminds him of a station (Maqam) in which he enjoined good (Amara fihi bil-Ma'ruf) and forbade evil (Wa-Naha fihi 'anil-Munkar).' The hadith of Abu Dharr: Abu Bakr said: 'O Messenger of Allah, is there any struggle (Jihad) other than fighting the polytheists?' He said: 'Yes, O Abu Bakr. Verily, Allah the Exalted has strugglers (Mujahidin) on earth better than the martyrs.' He mentioned the hadith, and in it he said: 'They are those who enjoin good (Al-Amirun bil-Ma'ruf) and forbid evil (Wa-N-Nahuna 'anil-Munkar).'
9:112.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

9:112.arabic: وقال أبو هريرة رضى الله عنه: إن فى الجنة حوراء يقال لها العيناء إذا مشت مشى عن يمينها ويسارها سبعون ألف وصيفة وهى تقول أين الآمرون بالمعروف والناهون عن المنكر؟
9:112.english: And Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'In Paradise, there is a houri called Al-'Aynaa; when she walks, seventy thousand handmaidens walk to her right and left, and she says: Where are those who enjoin good and forbid evil?'
9:112.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

9:118.arabic: م  من خطر غيره كما أن قدره أعظم من قدر غيره، فهذا بذاك. وهو كالملك المخاطر بروحه في ملكه لكثرة أعدائه فإنه إذا أخذ وقهر اشتهى أن يكون قد كان فقيراً، فكم من عالم يشتهي في الآخرة سلامة الجهال؟ والعياذ بالله منه. فهذا الخطر يمنع من التكبر، فإنه إن كان من أهل النار فالخنزير أفضل منه، فكيف يتكبر من هذا حاله؟ فلا ينبغي أن يكون العالم عند نفسه أكبر من الصحابة رضوان الله عليهم وقد كان بعضهم يقول: يا ليتني لم تلدني أمي! ويأخذ الآخر تبنة من الأرض ويقول: يا ليتني كنت هذه التبنة! ويقول الآخر: ليتني كنت طيرا
9:118.english: From the danger of others, just as his status is greater than the status of others, so this is with that. And he is like a king who risks his soul (Ruh) in his kingdom due to the multitude of his enemies, for if he is captured and subdued, he wishes he had been poor. How many scholars wish in the Hereafter for the safety of the ignorant? And refuge with Allah from that. This danger prevents arrogance (Takabbur), for if he is from the people of the Fire, the pig is better than him, so how can one be arrogant with this condition? So the scholar should not consider himself greater than the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, and indeed some of them would say: 'O would that my mother had not given birth to me!' And another would take a straw from the earth and say: 'O would that I were this straw!' And another would say: 'Would that I were a bird that eats!' And another would say: 'Would that I had not been a thing mentioned!' All of that out of fear of the danger of the outcome, so they saw themselves as worse in condition than the bird and than the dust. Whenever he prolongs his thought (Fikr) in the danger that he is facing, his arrogance (Kibr) vanishes completely, and he sees himself as if he were the worst of creation. And its example is the example of a slave whom his master ordered with matters, so he began them, then left some of them and introduced deficiency in some of them and doubted in some of them whether he performed them as his master approves or not? Then an informer informed him that his master sent to him a messenger who will not bring him out of all that he is in naked and humiliated and cast him at his door in the heat and the sun for a long time, until when the matter became straitened upon him and the effort reached him, he ordered the raising of his account and searched all his deeds, little and much, then ordered him to a narrow prison and constant punishment that does not relieve him for an hour, and he knew that his master had done with groups of his slaves like that and pardoned some of them, and he does not know from which of the two groups he will be? So if he reflects on that, his soul (Nafs) is broken and humbled and his honor and arrogance (Kibr) are nullified and his sorrow and fear appear, and he does not become arrogant over anyone of creation, but rather he humbles himself hoping that he will be from his intercessors at the descent of the punishment. So likewise the scholar, if he reflects on what he wasted of the commands of his Lord with transgressions on his limbs and with sins in his inner self (Batin) from ostentation (Riya), malice (Haqd), envy (Hasad), pride (Ujb), hypocrisy (Nifaq), and other than that, and knows with what he is facing of the great danger, his arrogance (Kibr) leaves him inevitably. The second matter is that the scholar knows that arrogance (Kibr) is not fitting except for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, alone, and that if he becomes arrogant, he becomes hated by Allah, detested, and Allah loved from him that he humble himself and said to him: 'Indeed you have with Me status as long as you do not see for yourself status; if you see for yourself status, then you have no status with Me.' So he must impose upon himself what his Master loves from him. And this removes arrogance (Takabbur) from his heart (Qalb) even if he is certain that he has no sin, for example, or imagines that. And by this, arrogance (Takabbur) was removed from the Prophets, peace be upon them, when they knew that whoever contends with Allah, the Exalted, for the garment of arrogance (Kibr).
9:118.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

9:119.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
9:119.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Whatever is in the Quran of 'O you who have believed' is in the Torah 'O you who are poor (Masakin)'.
9:119.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

9:120.arabic: فلا دواء للرياء مثل الإخفاء، وذلك يشق في بداية المجاهدة، وإذا صبر عليه مدة بالتكلف سقط عنه ثقله وهان عليه ذلك بتواصل ألطاف الله وما يمد به عباده من حسن التوفيق والتأييد والتسديد و"إن الله لا يغير ما بقوم حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم" فمن العبد المجاهدة ومن الله الهداية، ومن العبد قرع الباب ومن الله فتح الباب "والله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين؛ وإن تك حسنة يضاعفها ويؤت من لدنه أجراً عظيماً".
9:120.english: So there is no remedy for hypocrisy (Riya') like concealment, and that is difficult at the beginning of spiritual struggle (Mujahadah), and if one endures it for a period with effort, its heaviness falls away from him and it becomes easy for him through the continuous kindnesses of Allah and what He provides His servants with of good success (Tawfiq), support (Ta'yid), and rectification (Tasdid). And "Indeed, Allah will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in their souls (Anfus)" so from the servant is the spiritual struggle (Mujahadah) and from Allah is the guidance (Hidayah), and from the servant is knocking on the door and from Allah is opening the door "And Allah does not allow to be lost the reward of the doers of good (Muhsinin); and if it is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from His presence a great reward."
9:120.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

9:120.arabic: وقوله تعالى: ﴿ إنا لا نضيع أجر من أحسن عملا ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ إن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين ﴾ {} فكيف يضيع أجر أصل الإيمان وجميع الطاعات بمعصية واحدة
9:120.english: And His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, We do not waste the reward of one who does good deeds (aḥsana ʿamalan)' and His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, Allah does not waste the reward of the doers of good (al-muḥsinīn)'. So how could He waste the reward of the foundation of faith (al-īmān) and all acts of obedience (al-ṭāʿāt) due to a single act of disobedience (maʿṣiyah)?
9:120.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Foundations of Belief'

9:122.arabic: أما الآيات: فقوله عز وجل: ﴿ولينذروا قومهم إذا رجعوا إليهم لعلهم يحذرون﴾ ( سورة التوبة: الآية 122) والمراد هو التعليم والإرشاد وقوله تعالى: ﴿وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب ليبيننه للناس ولا يكتمونه﴾ ( سورة آل عمران: الآية 187) وهو إوجاب للتعليم وقوله تعالى: ﴿وإن فريقا منهم ليكتمون الحق وهم يعلمون﴾ ( سورة البقرة: الآية 146) وهو تحريم للكتمان كما قال تعالى في الشهادة: ﴿ومن يكتمها فإنه آثم قلبه﴾ ( سورة البقرة: الآية 283) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: (ما آتى الله عالما علما إلا وأخذ عليه من الميثا
9:122.english: As for the verses: The saying of the Almighty: 'And to warn their people when they return to them so that they might be cautious' (Surah At-Tawbah: Verse 122) and the intended meaning is teaching and guidance, and His saying the Exalted: 'And when Allah took a covenant from those who were given the Book to make it clear to the people and not conceal it' (Surah Āl 'Imrān: Verse 187) and it is an obligation for teaching, and His saying the Exalted: 'And indeed, a party of them conceal the truth while they know' (Surah Al-Baqarah: Verse 146) and it is a prohibition of concealment as He the Exalted said regarding testimony: 'And whoever conceals it, then indeed he is sinful in his heart (Qalb)' (Surah Al-Baqarah: Verse 283) and the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah does not give a scholar knowledge except that He takes from him a covenant like the covenant He took from the prophets to make it clear to the people and not conceal it' [42]. And He the Exalted said: 'And who is better in speech than one who invites to Allah and does righteous work' (Surah Fuṣṣilat: Verse 33) and He the Exalted said: 'Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good admonition' (Surah An-Naḥl: Verse 125) and He the Exalted said: 'And teaches them the Book and the wisdom' (Surah Al-Baqarah: Verse 129 and Verse 151, and Surah Āl 'Imrān, Verse 164 and Surah Al-Jumu'ah, Verse 2).
9:122.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

9:122.arabic: وترك أيضاً علم تهذيب الأخلاق وترك الفقه عن الله تعالى بإدراك جلاله وعظمته وهو العلم الذي يورث الخوف والهيبة والخشوع ويحمل على التقوى، فتراه آمناً من الله مغتراً به متكلاً على أنه لا بد وأن يرحمه فإنه قوم دينه، وأنه لو لم يشتغل بالفتاوى لتعطل الحلال والحرام فقد ترك العلوم التي هي أهم وهو غافل مغرور، وسبب غروره ما سلم في الشرع من تعظيم الفقه ولم يدر أن ذلك الفقه هو الفقه عن الله ومعرفة صفاته المخوفة والمرجوة ليستشعر القلب الخوف ويلازم التقوى، إذ قال تعالى "فلولا نفر من كل فرقة منهم طائفة ليتفقهوا
9:122.english: And he also abandoned the knowledge of refining character traits (Akhlaq) and abandoned the understanding (Fahm) about Allah the Exalted through perceiving His majesty and greatness, which is the knowledge that begets fear (Khawf), awe (Haybah), and humility (Khushuʿ) and carries one to piety (Taqwa). So you see him secure from Allah, deceived by Him, relying that He must surely have mercy on him because he has established his religion, and that if he did not occupy himself with legal rulings (Fatawa), the lawful (Halal) and unlawful (Haram) would be suspended. Thus he has abandoned the knowledges that are more important while being heedless (Ghafil) and deceived (Maghrur). The cause of his deception is what he heard in the Sacred Law (Shariʿa) regarding the exaltation of understanding (Fiqh), and he did not realize that this understanding (Fiqh) is the understanding (Fiqh) about Allah and knowledge of His attributes that are feared and hoped for, so that the Heart (Qalb) may feel fear (Khawf) and adhere to piety (Taqwa), as Allah the Exalted said: "Then why did not a group from every faction among them go forth to gain understanding (Yatafaqqahu) in the religion (Deen) and to warn (Yunthiru) their people when they return to them, that they might beware (Yahdharun)?" And that by which the warning (Inthar) is achieved is other than this knowledge. For the objective of this knowledge is: preserving wealth through conditions of transactions and preserving bodies through wealth and by repelling killing and injuries. Wealth in the path of Allah is a tool (Alah) and the body is a mount (Markab).
9:122.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

9:122.arabic: اللفظ الأول: الفقه؛ فقد تصرفوا فيه بالتخصيص لا بالنقل والتحويل إذا خصصوه بمعرفة الفروع الغريبة في الفتاوى والوقوف على دقائق عللها واستكثار الكلام فيها وحفظ المقالات المتعلقة بها فمن كان أشد تعمقا فيها وأكثر اشتغالا بها يقال هو الأفقه ولقد كان اسم الفقه في العصر الأول مطلقا على علم طريق الآخرة ومعرفة دقائق آفات النفوس ومفسدات الأعمال وقوة الإحاطة بحقارة الدنيا وشدة التطلع إلى نعيم الآخرة واستيلاء الخوف على القلب ويدلك عليه قوله عز وجل: (ليتفقهوا في الدين ولينذروا قومهم إذا رجعوا إليهم( (التوبة: 1
9:122.english: The first term: Jurisprudence (Fiqh); they have dealt with it through specification, not through transmission and transformation, when they specify it to knowledge of obscure branches in legal opinions (fatwas) and standing upon the subtleties of their causes and multiplying speech about them and memorizing the treatises related to them. So whoever is more deeply immersed in them and more occupied with them is said to be the most jurisprudent. And indeed, the name Jurisprudence (Fiqh) in the first era was applied generally to knowledge of the path of the Hereafter and knowledge of the subtleties of the afflictions of the souls (Nafs) and the corrupters of deeds and the strength of encompassing the insignificance of the world and the intense aspiration to the bliss of the Hereafter and the domination of fear over the heart (Qalb). And what indicates you to that is His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'So that they may gain understanding (yatafaqqahu) in the religion and so that they may warn their people when they return to them' (At-Tawbah: 122). And what brings about the warning and the frightening is this Jurisprudence (Fiqh), not the subdivisions of divorce, manumission, imprecation, advance sale, and lease, for that does not bring about warning nor frightening. Rather, exclusive devotion to it continuously hardens the heart (Qalb) and removes reverence from it, as we witness now from those exclusively devoted to it. And He, the Exalted, said: 'For them are hearts (Qalb) with which they do not understand (yafqahuna)' (Al-A'raf: 179). And He intended by it the meanings of faith (Iman), not the legal opinions (fatwas). And by my life, indeed Jurisprudence (Fiqh) and understanding (Fahm) in the language are two names with one meaning, and only the customary usage of it is spoken about, ancient and modern.
9:122.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

9:122.arabic:
فضيلة التعلم

أما الآيات فقوله تعالى: ﴿فلولا نفر من كل فرقة منهم طائفة ليتفقهوا في  الدين﴾ (سورة التوبة: الآية 122) وقوله عز وجل ﴿فاسألوا أهل الذكر إن كنتم لا  تعلمون﴾ (سورة النحل: الآية 43، وسورة الأنبياء: الآية 7)
9:122.english:
The Virtue of Learning

As for the verses, there is His saying, the Exalted: "So why does not a group from every faction among them go forth to gain understanding (liyatafaqqahu) in the religion (al-deen)?" (Surah At-Tawbah: Verse 122) and His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: "So ask the people of the Remembrance (ahl al-dhikr) if you do not know." (Surah An-Nahl: Verse 43, and Surah Al-Anbiya: Verse 7)
9:122.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

9:123.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
9:123.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Whatever is in the Quran of 'O you who have believed' is in the Torah 'O you poor ones (al-Masakin)'.
9:123.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

9:126.arabic: وقال تعالى: " أو لا يرون أنهم يفتنون في كل عام مرة أو مرتين ثم لا يتوبون ولا هم يذكرون " قيل يفتنون بأمراض يختبرون بها. ويقال: إن العبد إذا مرض مرضتين ثم لم يتب قال له ملك الموت: يا غافل جاءك مني رسول بعد رسول فلم تجب. وقد كان السلف لذلك يستوحشون إذا خرج عام ولم يصابوا فيه بنقص في نفس أو مال. وقالوا: لا يخلو المؤمن في كل أربعين يوماً أن يروع روعة أو يصاب ببلية حتى روي أن عمار بن ياسر تزوج امرأة فلم تكن تمرض فطلقها، وأن النبي ﭬ عرض عليه امرأة فحكي من وصفها حتى هم أن يتزوجها، فقيل: وإنها ما مرضت ق
9:126.english: And Allah the Exalted said: "Or do they not see that they are tested (yuf-tanūna) in every year once or twice, then they do not repent (yatūbūna) nor do they remember (yadh-dhakkarūna)?" It is said: They are tested with illnesses by which they are examined. And it is said: When the servant (al-'abd) falls ill twice and does not repent, the Angel of Death (Malak al-Mawt) says to him: O heedless one, messenger after messenger came to you from me, and you did not respond. And for this reason, the early righteous predecessors (al-Salaf) would feel uneasy if a year passed without them being afflicted with a deficiency in their soul (nafs) or wealth. And they said: The believer (al-Mu'min) does not pass forty days without being startled by a fright or struck by a calamity, until it was narrated that 'Ammar ibn Yasir married a woman who never fell ill, so he divorced her, and that the Prophet ﷺ was presented with a woman, and her description was related until he almost married her, but it was said: And she has never been ill, so he said: "I have no need for her."
9:126.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

9:128.arabic: وقوله تعالى: ﴿ لقد جاءكم رسول من أنفسكم ﴾ {} إلى آخرها[29]
9:128.english: And His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, there has come to you a Messenger from among yourselves' {} to its end[29]
9:128.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

9:128.arabic: [29]  حديث فضل لقد جاءكم رسول من أنفسكم إلى آخرها أخرجه الطبراني في الدعاء من حديث أنس بسند ضعيف علمني رسول الله ﭬ ما أحترز به من كل شيطان رجيم ومن كل جبار عنيد فذكر حديثا وفي آخره فقل حسبي الله إلى آخر السورة وذكر أبو القاسم الغافقي في فضائل القرآن في رغائب القرآن لعبد الملك بن حبيب من رواية محمد بن بكار أن رسول الله ﭬ قال من لزم قراءة لقد جاءكم رسول من أنفسكم إلى آخر السورة لم يمت هدما ولا غرقا ولا حرقا ولا ضربا بحديدة وهو ضعيف.
9:128.english: [29] The hadith regarding the virtue of 'Lāqad jā'akum rasūlun min anfusikum' to its end was transmitted by Al-Tabarani in Al-Du'a from the narration of Anas with a weak chain: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) taught me what I guard myself with from every accursed devil and every obstinate tyrant.' He mentioned a hadith, and at its end: 'So say: Hasbiyallahu...' to the end of the surah. And Abu Al-Qasim Al-Ghafiqi mentioned in Fada'il Al-Qur'an in Raghā'ib Al-Qur'an by Abd Al-Malik ibn Habib from the narration of Muhammad ibn Bakkar that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever persists in reciting 'Lāqad jā'akum rasūlun min anfusikum' to the end of the surah will not die by demolition, drowning, burning, or being struck with iron.' And it is weak.
9:128.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Book of Knowledge'

9:129.arabic: قال محمد بن حسان قال لي معروف الكرخي رحمه الله: ألا أعلمك عشر كلمات خمس للدنيا وخمس للآخرة. من دعا الله عز وجل بهن وجد الله تعالى عندهن قلت اكتبها لي قال لا ولكن أرددها عليك كما رددها علي بكر بن خنيس رحمه الله: حسبي الله لديني حسبي الله لدنياي حسبي الله الكريم لما أهمني حسبي الله الحليم القوي لمن بغى علي حسبي الله الشديد لمن كادني بسوء حسبي الله الرحيم عند الموت حسبي الله الرؤوف عند المسألة في القبر حسبي الله الكريم عند الحساب حسبي الله اللطيف عند الميزان حسبي الله القدير عند الصراط حسبي الله لا
9:129.english: Muhammad ibn Hassan said: Ma'ruf al-Karkhi (may Allah have mercy on him) said to me: 'Shall I not teach you ten phrases - five for this world and five for the Hereafter? Whoever supplicates to Allah (the Mighty and Majestic) with them will find Allah (the Exalted) with them.' I said: 'Write them for me.' He said: 'No, but I will repeat them to you as Bakr ibn Khunays (may Allah have mercy on him) repeated them to me: Allah is sufficient for me for my religion, Allah is sufficient for me for my worldly life, Allah the Generous is sufficient for me for what concerns me, Allah the Forbearing the Strong is sufficient for me for whoever transgresses against me, Allah the Severe is sufficient for me for whoever plots evil against me, Allah the Merciful is sufficient for me at death, Allah the Compassionate is sufficient for me at the questioning in the grave, Allah the Generous is sufficient for me at the Reckoning, Allah the Subtle is sufficient for me at the Scale, Allah the Powerful is sufficient for me at the Bridge, Allah is sufficient for me, there is no deity except Him, upon Him I rely, and He is the Lord of the Great Throne.' And it has been narrated from Abu al-Darda' that he said: 'Whoever says seven times every day: "Then if they turn away, say: Allah is sufficient for me, there is no deity except Him, upon Him I rely, and He is the Lord of the Great Throne," Allah (the Mighty and Majestic) will suffice him regarding what concerns him of his Hereafter matter, whether he is truthful or lying.'
9:129.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

10:3.arabic: وقال عز وجل: " يدبر الأمر ما من شفيع إلا من بعد إذنه ". وكل ما ذكر في القرآن من التوحيد فهو تنبيه على قطع الملاحظة عن الأغيار والتوكل على الواحد القهار.
10:3.english: And He, the Almighty, said: "He manages the affair; there is no intercessor except after His permission." And everything mentioned in the Quran regarding Monotheism (Tawhid) is an alert to cut off observation from others and to rely (Tawakkul) upon the One, the Subduer (Al-Qahhar).
10:3.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

10:3.arabic: ويستحب أن يقرأ الآيات المخصوصة مثل آية الكرسي وآخر البقرة وغيرهما وقوله تعالى: ﴿ وإلهكم إله واحد لا إله إلا هو ﴾ {} إلى قوله: ﴿ لقوم يعقلون ﴾ {} يقال إن من قرأها عند النوم حفظ الله عليه القرآن فلم ينسه ويقرأ من سورة الأعراف هذه الآية: ﴿ إن ربكم الله الذي خلق السموات والأرض في ستة أيام ﴾ {} إلى قوله: ﴿ قريب من المحسنين ﴾ {} وآخر بني إسرائيل ﴿ قل ادعوا الله ﴾ {} الآيتين فإنه يدخل في شعاره ملك يوكل بحفظه فيستغفر له ويقرأ المعوذتين وينفث بهن في يديه ويمسح بهما وجهه وسائر جسده كذلك روى من فعل رسول ال
10:3.english: And it is recommended to recite the specified verses such as the Throne Verse (Ayat al-Kursi) and the end of Surah al-Baqarah and others, and His saying: 'And your god is one God; there is no deity except Him' until His saying: 'for a people who use reason.' It is said that whoever recites it at sleep, Allah preserves the Quran for him so he does not forget it. And recite from Surah al-A'raf this verse: 'Indeed, your Lord is Allah who created the heavens and the earth in six days' until His saying: 'is near to the doers of good.' And the end of Bani Isra'il 'Say, Call upon Allah' the two verses. For indeed, there enters into his emblem an angel entrusted with his protection who seeks forgiveness for him. And recite the two seeking refuge chapters (al-Mu'awwidhatayn) and blow with them into his hands and wipe with them his face and the rest of his body, as narrated from the action of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him).
10:3.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Book of Knowledge'

10:6.arabic: والقرآن مصرح بأن التقوى مفتاح الهداية والكشف وذلك علم من غير تعلم وقال الله تعالى وما خلق الله في السموات والأرض لآيات لقوم يتقون خصصها بهم وقال تعالى هذا بيان للناس وهدى وموعظة للمتقين وكان أبو يزيد وغيره يقول ليس العالم الذي يحفظ من كتاب فإذا نسي ما حفظه صار جاهلا إنما العالم الذي يأخذ علمه من ربه أي وقت شاء بلا حفظ ولا درس وهذا هو العلم الرباني وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى وعلمناه من لدنا علما مع أن كل علم من لدنه ولكن بعضها بوسائط تعليم الخلق فلا يسمى ذلك علما لدنيا بل اللدني الذي ينفتح في سر ا
10:6.english: And the Quran clarifies that God-Consciousness (Taqwa) is the key to guidance and unveiling, and that is knowledge without learning. And Allah said: 'And what Allah has created in the heavens and the earth are signs for a people who are God-Conscious (Yattaqun).' He specified it for them. And He said: 'This is a clarification for the people and guidance and admonition for the God-Conscious (Muttaqin).' And Abu Yazid and others used to say: 'The knowledgeable one is not he who memorizes from a book, for if he forgets what he memorized, he becomes ignorant. Rather, the knowledgeable one is he who takes his knowledge from his Lord whenever he wishes, without memorization or study.' And this is the Divine Knowledge (Al-Ilm Ar-Rabbani). And to it points His saying: 'And We taught him from Our Presence knowledge,' although all knowledge is from His Presence, but some of it is through intermediaries of teaching creation, so that is not called knowledge from the Presence (Ladunni). Rather, the Ladunni is that which opens in the secret of the heart (Sirr Al-Qalb) without a customary cause from outside. These are the evidences from transmission, and if all that has come regarding it from verses, reports, and traditions were gathered, it would exceed enumeration.
10:6.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

10:7.arabic: وكان أحدهم يعرض لهم المال الحلال فلا يأخذه ويقول: أخاف أن يفسد على قلبي، فمن كان له قلب فهو لا محالة يخاف من فساده، والذين أمات حب الدنيا قلوبهم فقد أخبر الله عنهم إذ قال تعالى: " ورضوا بالحياة الدنيا واطمأنوا بها والذين هم عن آياتنا غافلون ". وقال عز وجل: " ولا تطمع من أغفلنا قلبه عن ذكرنا واتبع هواه وكان أمره فرطاً ". وقال تعالى: " فأعرض عمن تولى عن ذكرنا ولم يرد إلا الحياة الدنيا، ذلك مبلغهم من العلم"، فأحال ذلك كله على الغفلة وعدم العلم، ولذلك قال رجل لعيسى عليه السلام: احملني معك في سياحتك،
10:7.english: And one of them would be offered lawful wealth but would not take it, saying: 'I fear it will corrupt my heart (Qalb).' So whoever has a heart (Qalb) inevitably fears its corruption. And those whose hearts (Qulub) have been killed by the love of the worldly life (Dunya), Allah has informed about them when He, the Exalted, said: "And they are content with the worldly life (Al-Hayat Al-Dunya) and feel secure with it, and those who are heedless of Our signs (Ayatina)." And He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: "And do not hope for [guidance from] one whose heart (Qalb) We have made heedless of Our remembrance (Dhikrina) and who follows his desire (Hawah) and whose affair is [one of] neglect." And He, the Exalted, said: "So turn away from whoever turns away from Our remembrance (Dhikrina) and desires not except the worldly life (Al-Hayat Al-Dunya). That is their extent of knowledge." So He attributed all of that to heedlessness (Al-Ghaflah) and lack of knowledge, and for that reason a man said to Jesus, peace be upon him: 'Carry me with you on your journey.' He said: 'Take out your wealth and follow me.' He said: 'I am not able.' So Jesus, peace be upon him, said: 'It is amazing that a rich man enters Paradise' - or he said: 'with difficulty.'
10:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

10:10.arabic: وقد جعل الله الشكر مفتاح كلام أهل الجنة فقال تعالى: ﴿ وقالوا الحمد لله الذي صدقنا وعده ﴾ {} وقال: ﴿ وآخر دعواهم ان الحمد لله رب العالمين ﴾ {}.
10:10.english: And Allah has made gratitude (Shukr) the key to the speech of the people of Paradise, so He the Exalted said: 'And they said: "Praise (Al-Hamd) be to Allah who has fulfilled His promise to us."' And He said: 'And the last of their supplication (Da'wah) is that: "Praise (Al-Hamd) be to Allah, Lord of the worlds."'
10:10.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

10:15.arabic: ولقد كان في الخائفين من خر مغشيا عليه عند آيات الوعيد. ومنهم من مات في سماع الآيات فمثل هذه الأحوال يخرجه عن أن يكون حاكيا في كلامه فإذا قال ﴿ إني أخاف إن عصيت ربي عذاب يوم عظيم ﴾ {} ولم يكن خائفا كان حاكيا وإذا قال ﴿ عليك توكلنا وإليك أنبنا وإليك المصير ﴾ {} ولم يكن حاله التوكل والإنابة كان حاكيا وإذا قال ﴿ ولنصبرن على ما آذيتمونا ﴾ {} فليكن حاله الصبر أو العزيمة عليه حتى يجد حلاوة التلاوة فإن لم يكن بهذه الصفات ولم يتردد قلبه بين هذه الحالات كان حظه من التلاوة حركة اللسان مع صريح اللعن على نفس
10:15.english: And indeed among those who fear (Allah) were those who fell unconscious at verses of threat. And among them were those who died while hearing the verses. Such states remove him from being merely a narrator in his speech. So if he says 'Indeed I fear if I disobey my Lord the punishment of a Great Day' and he is not fearful, he is merely narrating. And if he says 'Upon You we rely and to You we turn in repentance and to You is the final return' and his state is not one of reliance (Tawakkul) and turning in repentance (Inabah), he is merely narrating. And if he says 'And we will certainly be patient over what you harm us' then let his state be patience (Sabr) or determination upon it until he finds the sweetness of recitation. For if he does not have these qualities and his heart (Qalb) does not fluctuate between these states, his share of recitation is merely the movement of the tongue with explicit cursing upon himself in His saying, the Exalted, 'Indeed the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers'.
10:15.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

10:17.arabic: ومنها الاستكبار عن الحق وكراهته، والحرص على المماراة فيه حتى إن أبغض شيء إلى المناظر أن يظهر على لسان خصمه الحق ومنهما ظهر تشمر لجحده وإنكاره بأقصى جهده وبذل غاية إمكانه في المخادعة والمكر والحيلة لدفعه حتى تصير المماراة فيه عادة طبيعية فلا يسمع كلاما إلا وينبعث من طبعه داعية الاعتراض عليه حتى يغلب ذلك على قلبه في أدلة القرآن وألفاظ الشرع فيضرب البعض منها بالبعض والمراء في مقابلة الباطل محذور إذ ندب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى ترك المراء بالحق على الباطل قال صلى الله عليه وسلم : (( من ترك ا
10:17.english: And among them is arrogance (Istikbar) towards the truth (Haqq) and hatred of it, and eagerness for disputation (Mira') in it until indeed the most hated thing to the disputant is that the truth appears on the tongue of his opponent, and from these two emerges exertion for its denial and rejection with his utmost effort and expenditure of the ultimate of his capability in deception, cunning, and trickery to repel it until disputation in it becomes a natural habit, so he does not hear speech except that there arises from his nature an urge to object to it until that overcomes his heart (Qalb) in the proofs of the Quran and the expressions of the Sharia, so he strikes some of them with others, and disputation in opposition to falsehood is cautioned against, as the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, encouraged leaving disputation even with truth against falsehood. He said, peace be upon him: 'Whoever leaves disputation while he is false, Allah builds for him a house in the outskirts of Paradise, and whoever leaves disputation while he is truthful, Allah builds for him a house in the highest part of Paradise.' And Allah the Exalted has equated between one who fabricates a lie against Allah and one who denies the truth, as He said, the Exalted: 'And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah or denies the truth when it has come to him?' (Al-Ankabut: 68). And He said, the Exalted: 'So who is more unjust than one who lies about Allah and denies the truth when it comes to him?' (Az-Zumar: 32).
10:17.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

10:24.arabic: والشيطان يدعوهم الى ملك الدنيا لعلمه بان ملك الاخرة يفوت به اذ الدنيا والاخرة ضرتان ولعلمه بأن الدنيا لا تسلم له ايضا ولو كانت تسلم له لكان يحسده ايضا ولكن ملك الدنيا لا يخلو عن المنازعات والمكدرات وطول الهموم في التدبيرات وكذا سائر اسباب الجاه ثم مهما تسلم وتتم الاسباب ينقضي العمر ﴿ حتى اذا اخذت الارض زخرفها وازينت وظن اهلها انهم قادرون عليها اتاها امرنا ليلا او نهارا فجعلناها حصيدا كأن لم تغن بالأمس ﴾ {} فضرب الله تعالى لها مثلا فقال تعالى: ﴿ واضرب لهم مثل الحياة الدنيا كماء انزلناه من السماء
10:24.english: And Satan calls them to the kingdom of this world, knowing that the kingdom of the Hereafter is lost through it, for this world and the Hereafter are two co-wives, and knowing that this world does not remain secure for him either; even if it were to remain secure for him, he would envy it as well. But the kingdom of this world is not free from disputes, troubles, and prolonged anxieties in management, as well as all other causes of status. Then, however much one secures and completes the causes, the lifespan ends. 'Until when the earth takes on its adornment and is beautified, and its people think that they are capable over it, Our command comes to it by night or day, and We make it as a harvest, as if it had not flourished yesterday.' {} Then Allah the Exalted struck a parable for it, saying: 'And strike for them the parable of the life of this world: like water which We send down from the sky, then the vegetation of the earth mingles with it, then it becomes dry stubble scattered by the winds.' {} And asceticism (Zuhd) in this world, since it is a present kingdom, Satan envied it and turned him away from it.
10:24.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

10:24.arabic: فالعلم والحرية هي الباقيات الصالحات التي تبقى كمالاً في النفس، والمال والجاه هو الذي ينقضي على القرب وهو كما مثله الله تعالى حيث قال "إنما مثل الحياة الدنيا كماء أنزلناه من السماء فاختلط به نبات الأرض" الآية. وقال تعالى "واضرب لهم مثل الحياة الدنيا كماء أنزلناه من السماء" إلى قوله "فأصبح هشيماً تذروه الرياح" وكل ما تذروه رياح الموت فهو زهرة الحياة الدنيا، وكل ما لا يقطعه الموت فهو الباقيات الصالحات.
10:24.english: Knowledge and freedom are the righteous remaining deeds (al-baqiyat al-salihat) that remain as perfection in the soul (nafs), while wealth and status are what perish in proximity, as Allah the Exalted has likened it where He said: "Indeed, the likeness of worldly life is like water which We send down from the sky, then the vegetation of the earth mingles with it" the verse. And He said: "And strike for them the likeness of worldly life as water which We send down from the sky" to His saying: "Then it becomes dry debris scattered by the winds." And everything that the winds of death scatter is the flower of worldly life, and everything that death does not cut off is the righteous remaining deeds (al-baqiyat al-salihat).
10:24.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

10:24.arabic: وصار كأن لم يغن بالأمس حصيداً كما كان في أول أمره أمداً مديداً، وليته بقي كذلك فما أحسنه لو ترك تراباً. لا بل يحييه بعد طول البلى ليقاسي شديد البلاء، فيخرج من قبره بعد جمع أجزائه المتفرقة، ويخرج إلى أهوال القيامة فينظر إلى قيامة قائمة وسماء مشققة ممزقة وأرض مبدلة وجبال مسيرة ونجوم منكدرة وشمس منكسفة وأحوال مظلمة وملائكة غلاظ شداد وجهنم تزفر وجنة ينظر إليها المجرم فيتحسر، ويرى صحائف منشورة فيقال له اقرأ كتابك فيقول وما هو: فيقال: كان قد وكل بك في حياتك التي كنت تفرح بها وتتكبر بنعيمها وتفتخر بأسب
10:24.english: And he became as if he had not prospered yesterday, harvested as he was in the beginning of his affair for a long duration, and would that he had remained thus, how excellent it would be if he were left as dust. No, rather He (Allah) revives him after long decay to experience severe affliction, he emerges from his grave after gathering his scattered parts, and emerges to the terrors of the Resurrection, seeing a standing Resurrection and a sky split and torn, an earth changed, mountains set in motion, stars falling, a sun eclipsed, dark conditions, harsh and severe angels, Hellfire blazing, and a Paradise which the criminal looks upon and regrets, and he sees scrolls spread out, and it is said to him: Read your book, and he says: And what is it? It is said: There had been appointed over you in your life which you rejoiced in, boasted of its blessings, and prided yourself on its means, two guardian angels writing upon you what you spoke or did, little and much, small and large, eating and drinking, standing and sitting, you had forgotten that and Allah has enumerated it for you, so come to the accounting and prepare for the answer or be driven to the abode of torment, his heart (Qalb) is cut off in terror from the horror of this address before the scroll is spread and he witnesses what is in it of his disgrace, and when he witnesses it, he says: "Woe to us! What is with this book that leaves nothing small or great but enumerates it?" This is the end of his affair, and it is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: "Then when He wills, He resurrects him." So what is for one in this state and arrogance and self-aggrandizement? Rather, what is for him and joy in a single moment, let alone insolence?
10:24.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

10:24.arabic: إن ملكت واحداً منهم جميع ما طلعت عليه الشمس جعلته حصيداً كأن لم يغن بالأمس. تمنى أصحابها سروراً وتعدهم غروراً حتى يأملون كثيراً ويبنون قصورا. فتصبح قصورهم قبورا وجمعهم بورا. وسعيهم هباء منثورا ودعاؤهم ثبورا، هذه صفتها وكان أمر الله قدراً مقدورا.
10:24.english: If it possesses one of them with all that the sun has risen upon, it makes him like a harvested crop (حصيداً) as if he had not flourished yesterday. Its companions wish for joy and it promises them delusion (غروراً) until they hope much and build palaces. Then their palaces become graves and their gathering becomes barren (بورا). Their striving is scattered dust (هباء منثورا) and their supplication is woe (ثبورا). This is its description, and the command of Allah was a decree decreed (قدراً مقدورا).
10:24.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Condemnation of the World'

10:24.arabic: وكونه مقطوعاً بالموت الذي لا بد من إتيانه مهما أخذت الأرض زخرفها وازينت وظن أهلها أنهم قادرون عليها فيستعظم بالإضافة إليها لذة معرفة الله ومطالعة صفاته وأفعاله ونظام مملكته من أعلى عليين إلى أسفل السافلين، فإنها خالية من المزاحمات والمكدرات متسعة للمتواردين عليها لا تضيق عنهم بكبرها، وإنما عرضها من حيث التقدير السموات والأرض، وإذا خرج النظر عن المقدرات فلا نهاية لعرضها، فلا يزال العارف بمطالعتها في جنة عرضها السموات والأرض يرتع في رياضها ويقطف من ثمارها ويكرع من حياضها وهو آمن من انقطاعها، إذ ثم
10:24.english: And it is cut off by death which must inevitably come, no matter how the earth takes its adornment and becomes beautified and its people think they are capable upon it, so he magnifies in comparison to it the pleasure of knowing God (Ma'rifat Allah) and contemplating His attributes and actions and the system of His kingdom from the highest heights to the lowest depths, for it is free from rivalries and disturbances, spacious for those who come to it, not constricted for them by its greatness, and indeed its breadth from the perspective of estimation is the heavens and the earth, and when the gaze goes beyond estimations, there is no end to its breadth, so the knower (Al-'Arif) by contemplating it is in a garden whose breadth is the heavens and the earth, grazing in its meadows and plucking from its fruits and drinking from its pools, and he is safe from its cessation, for the fruits of this garden are not cut off nor prohibited, then it is eternal perpetual, not cut by death, for death does not destroy the place of knowing God the Exalted and its place is the spirit (Al-Ruh) which is a divine heavenly command, then it is eternal perpetual, not cut by death, for death does not destroy the place of knowing God the Exalted and its place is the spirit (Al-Ruh) which is a divine heavenly command, and indeed death changes its states and cuts off its distractions and obstacles and empties it from its imprisonment, but as for annihilating it, then no "And do not think of those who have been killed in the way of God as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision, rejoicing in what God has given them of His bounty, and they receive good tidings about those [to be martyred] after them who have not yet joined them" the verse. And do not think that this is specific to the killed in battle, for the knower (Al-'Arif) with every soul
10:24.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

10:26.arabic: وقال الله عز وجل: ﴿ هل جزاء الإحسان إلا الإحسان ﴾ {} فقيل الإحسان في الدنيا قول لا إله إلا الله وفي الآخرة الجنة. وكذا قوله تعالى: ﴿ للذين أحسنوا الحسنى وزيادة ﴾ {}
10:26.english: And Allah the Exalted said: 'Is the reward for good (Ihsan) anything but good (Ihsan)?' (Quran 55:60) It was said: The good (Ihsan) in this world is the statement 'There is no god but Allah' (La ilaha illa Allah) and in the Hereafter is Paradise. Likewise His saying: 'For those who do good (Ahsanu) is the best reward (Al-Husna) and more (Wa Ziyadah).' (Quran 10:26)
10:26.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter

10:41.arabic: وقد قال عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه لا يقيم أمر الناس إلا حصيف العقل أريب العقد لا يطلع منه على عورة ولا يخاف منه على حرة ولا تأخذه في الله لومة لائم وقال الأمراء أربعة فأمير قوي ظلف نفسه وعماله فذلك كالمجاهد في سبيل الله يد الله باسطة عليه بالرحمة وأمير فيه ضعف ظلف نفسه وأرتع عماله لضعفه فهو على شفا هلاك إلا أن يرحمه الله وأمير ظلف عماله وأرتع نفسه فذلك الحطمة الذي قال فيه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم شر الرعاة الحطمة فهو الهالك وحده حديث شر الرعاة الحطمة رواه مسلم من حديث عائذ بن عمرو المزني مت
10:41.english: And Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'No one can establish the affairs of the people except one with sound intellect (Aql) and firm resolve, from whom no private matter is exposed, from whom no free woman is feared, and whom no blamer's blame takes in the matter of Allah.' And he said: 'Rulers are four types: A ruler who is strong, restrains himself and his agents, that one is like a warrior (Mujahid) in the path of Allah, with Allah's hand extended over him in mercy. A ruler in whom there is weakness, restrains himself but lets his agents roam due to his weakness, he is on the brink of destruction unless Allah has mercy on him. A ruler who restrains his agents but lets himself roam, that is the one who crushes (Al-Hatma) about whom the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "The worst of shepherds is the one who crushes (Al-Hatma)." He is the one destroyed alone.' The hadith 'The worst of shepherds is the one who crushes' is narrated by Muslim from the hadith of A'idh ibn Amr al-Muzani connected, and it is with Ibn Abi al-Dunya from al-Awza'i disconnected as mentioned by the author. And a ruler who lets himself and his agents roam, they are all destroyed. And it has reached me, O Commander of the Faithful, that Jibril (peace be upon him) came to the Prophet (peace be upon him) and said: 'I came to you when Allah commanded the bellows of the Fire, and they were placed on the Fire to blaze for the Day of Resurrection.' He said to him: 'O Jibril, describe to me the Fire.' So he said:
10:41.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

10:48.arabic: واختلاف تركيب أعضائه أعاجيب تزيد على الأعاجيب فى بعثه وإعادته فكيف ينكر ذلك من قدرة الله تعالى وحكمته من يشاهد ذلك فى صنعته وقدرته فإن كان فى إيمانك ضعف فقو الإيمان بالنظر فى النشأة الأولى فإن الثانية مثلها وأسهل منها وإن كنت قوى الإيمان بها فأشعر قلبك تلك المخاوف والأخطار وأكثر فيها التفكر والاعتبار لتسلب عن قلبك الراحة والقرار فتشتغل بالتشمر للعرض على الجبار وتفكر أولا فيما يقرع سمع سكان القبور من شدة نفخ الصور فإنها صيحة واحدة تنفرج بها القبور عن رءوس الموتی فيثورون دفعة واحدة فتوهم نفسك وقد
10:48.english: And the differing composition of his limbs are wonders that increase upon wonders in his resurrection and restoration, so how can one deny that from the power of Allah the Exalted and His wisdom who witnesses that in His creation and power? If there is weakness in your faith, then strengthen faith by looking at the first creation, for the second is like it and easier than it. And if you are strong in faith in it, then make your heart (Qalb) feel those fears and dangers and increase in it reflection (Tafakkur) and consideration (I'tibar) to strip from your heart (Qalb) comfort and settlement, so you busy yourself with preparing for the presentation before the Compeller (Al-Jabbar). And reflect first on what strikes the hearing of the inhabitants of the graves from the intensity of the blowing of the Trumpet (As-Sur), for it is a single cry by which the graves split open from the heads of the dead, and they rise up all at once. So imagine yourself having leaped up, your face changed, your body dusty from your hair to your feet from the dust of your grave, stunned from the intensity of the blow, your eye fixed toward the call. And the creation has risen up in a single uprising from the graves in which their tribulation has been prolonged, and alarm and terror have agitated them, added to what was with them of sorrows and griefs and intense waiting for the outcome of the matter, as the Exalted said: 'And the Trumpet (As-Sur) will be blown, and all who are in the heavens and all who are on the earth will fall dead except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on.' And the Exalted said: 'And when the Horn (An-Naqur) is blown, that Day will be a difficult day for the disbelievers; not easy.' And the Exalted said: 'And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?" They do not await except one blast which will seize them while they are disputing. And they will not be able to make a testament, nor to their people will they return. And the Trumpet (As-Sur) will be blown; and at once from the graves to their Lord they will hasten. They will say, "O woe to us! Who has raised us up from our sleeping place? This is what the Most Merciful had promised, and the messengers told the truth."' So if there were not before the dead except the terror of that blowing, it would be worthy of being feared, for it is a blowing and a cry by which those in the heavens and the earth are struck dead, meaning they die by it except whom Allah wills, and that is some of the angels. And therefore the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'How can I be at ease when the possessor of the Trumpet (As-Sur) has taken the horn in his mouth, lowered his forehead, and inclined his ear, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow?' Maqatil said: The Trumpet (As-Sur) is the horn, and that is because Israfil (upon him be peace) has placed his mouth on the horn like the form of a trumpet, and the circle of the head of the horn is like the width of the heavens and the earth, and he is fixing his gaze toward the Throne, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow the first blowing. And when he blows, those in the heavens and the earth are struck dead, meaning every animal dies from the intensity of the alarm except whom Allah wills, and that is Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil, and the Angel of Death (Malak al-Mawt). Then the Angel of Death (Malak al-Mawt) is commanded to take the soul (Ruh) of Jibril, then the soul (Ruh) of Mika'il, then the soul (Ruh) of Israfil, then the Angel of Death (Malak al-Mawt) is commanded and he dies. Then the creation remains after the first blowing in the Barzakh for forty years, then Allah the Exalted revives Israfil and commands.
10:48.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

10:49.arabic: ولا يتفكر واحد منهم إلا ما شاء الله في جنازة نفسه وفي حاله إذا حمل عليها ولا سبب لهذه الغفلة إلا قسوة القلوب بكثرة المعاصي والذنوب حتى نسينا الله تعالى واليوم الآخر والأهوال التي بين أيدينا فصرنا نلهو ونغفل ونشتغل بما لا يعنينا فنسأل الله تعالى اليقظة من هذه الغفلة فإن أحسن أحوال الحاضرين على الجنائز بكاؤهم على الميت ولو عقلوا لبكوا على أنفسهم لا على الميت نظر إبراهيم الزيات إلى إناس يترحمون على الميت فقال لو ترحمون على أنفسكم لكان خيرا لكم إنه نجا من أهوال ثلاثة: وجه ملك الموت وقد رأى، ومرارة ا
10:49.english: And not one of them reflects except what Allah wills (ما شاء الله) in his own funeral procession and in his state when he is carried upon it. And there is no cause for this heedlessness (غفلة) except the hardening of the Hearts (القلوب) through abundant sins and transgressions, until we have forgotten Allah the Exalted and the Last Day (اليوم الآخر) and the terrors that are before us, so we have become diverted, heedless, and preoccupied with what does not concern us. So we ask Allah the Exalted for awakening from this heedlessness. For the best state of those present at funerals is their weeping over the deceased; if they were to use their intellect, they would weep over themselves, not over the deceased. Ibrahim al-Zayyat looked at some people offering mercy upon the deceased and said: 'If you offered mercy upon yourselves, it would be better for you. He has been saved from three terrors: the face of the Angel of Death (ملك الموت) and he has seen it, the bitterness of death and he has tasted it, and the fear of the final outcome (الخاتمة) and he has become secure.'
10:49.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

10:55.arabic: أنه فيماذا يتفكر لم يقدر عليه  لأن  مجارى  الفكر  غير  محصورة وثمراته غير متناهية نعم نحن نجتهد في ضبط مجاريه بالإضافة  إلى  مهمات  العلوم الدينية وبالإضافة إلى الأحوال التى هى مقامات السالكين ويكون ذلك  ضبطا  جمليا فإن تفصيل ذلك يستدعى شرح العلوم كلها وجملة هذه  الكتب  كالشرح  لبعضها  فإنها مشتملة على علوم تلك العلوم تستفاد من أفكار مخصوصة فلنشر إلى ضبط الجامع  فيها ليحصل الوقوف على مجارى الفكر.                              بيان مجارى الفكر أعلم أن الفكر قد يجرى في أمر يتعلق بالدين وقد يجرى  في
10:55.english: That in what to think, he cannot encompass it because the channels of thought are not limited and its fruits are endless. Yes, we strive to regulate its channels in addition to the important matters of the religious sciences and in addition to the states that are the stations of the travelers (Salikeen), and that will be a general regulation. For detailing that requires explaining all the sciences, and the entirety of these books is like an explanation for some of them, for they contain the sciences of those sciences derived from specific thoughts. So let us proceed to regulate the comprehensive in them to achieve standing upon the channels of thought. Explanation of the Channels of Thought: Know that thought may run in a matter related to religion and may run in what is related to non-religion. Our aim is only what relates to religion, so let us leave the other division and concern ourselves with religion, the transaction (Mu'amalah) that is between the servant and the Lord, the Exalted. So all the thoughts of the servant either relate to the servant and his attributes and his states, or relate to the Worshipped One and His attributes and His actions; it is not possible to go beyond these two divisions. And what relates to the servant is either a consideration of what is beloved to the Lord, the Exalted, or of what is disliked, and there is no need for thought in other than these two divisions. And what relates to the Lord, the Exalted, is either a consideration of His Essence and His attributes and His Beautiful Names, or it is in His actions and His dominion and His sovereignty and all that is in the heavens and the earth and what is between them. And it becomes clear to you the confinement of thought in these divisions by an example, which is that the state of those who walk to Allah, the Exalted, and those who yearn for meeting Him relates to his Beloved or relates to himself. So if he thinks about his Beloved, then either he thinks about His beauty and the goodness of His image in His Essence to delight in thinking about Him and in witnessing Him, or he thinks about His subtle, good actions indicating His character and His attributes to be that which doubles the pleasure and strengthens his love. And if he thinks about himself, then his thought is in his attributes that drop him from the eye of his Beloved so that he abstains from them, or in the attributes that bring him near to Him and make him beloved to Him so that he becomes characterized by them. So if he thinks about something outside of these divisions, then that is outside the limit of love (Ishq) and it is a deficiency in it because the complete, perfect love (Ishq) is what overwhelms the lover and fills the heart (Qalb) so that it does not leave in it room for other than Him. So the lover of Allah, the Exalted, ought to be like that, so his view and thought do not go beyond his Beloved. And whenever his thought is confined in these four divisions, it is not at all outside the requirement of love. So let us begin with the first division, which is his thinking about the attributes of himself and the actions of himself to distinguish the beloved from them from the disliked, for this thought is that which relates to the science of transaction (Mu'amalah) which is the intended purpose of this book. And as for the other division, it relates to the science of unveiling (Mukashafah), then every.
10:55.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Contemplation'

10:57.arabic: فيه شفاء لما في الصدور ومن خالفه من الجبابرة قصمه الله ومن ابتغى العلم في غيره أضله الله هو حبل الله المتين ونوره المبين والعروة الوثقى والمعتصم الأوفى وهو المحيط بالقليل والكثير والصغير والكبير لا تنقضي عجائبه ولا تتناهى غرائبه لا يحيط بفوائده عند أهل العلم تحديد ولا يخلقه عند أهل التلاوة كثرة الترديد هو الذي أرشد الأولين والآخرين ولما سمعه الجن لم يلبثوا أن ولوا إلى قومهم منذرين فقالوا إنا سمعنا قرآنا عجبا يهدي إلى الرشد فآمنا به ولن نشرك بربنا أحدا فكل من آمن به فقد وفق ومن قال به فقد صدق ومن
10:57.english: In it is healing (Shifa) for what is in the chests (Sudur), and whoever opposes it from the tyrants, Allah will break him, and whoever seeks knowledge in other than it, Allah will misguide him. It is the firm rope (Habl) of Allah and His clear light (Nur), and the most trustworthy handhold, and the most faithful refuge. It encompasses the little and the much, the small and the great. Its wonders do not cease, and its marvels are endless. Its benefits cannot be encompassed by the people of knowledge with limitation, nor does it become worn out by the people of recitation with frequent repetition. It is what guided the first and the last, and when the jinn heard it, they did not delay but turned to their people as warners, and they said: 'Indeed, we have heard an amazing Quran that guides to the right path, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate with our Lord anyone.' So whoever believes in it has been granted success, and whoever speaks by it has spoken truthfully, and whoever holds fast to it has been guided, and whoever acts by it has attained success. And Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, We have sent down the Remembrance (Dhikr), and indeed, We are its guardians.' And from the causes of its preservation in the hearts (Qulub) and the copies (Mushafs) is the continuity of its recitation and the persistence in its study, along with the observance of its etiquettes and conditions, and the preservation of what is in it from the inward actions (A'mal al-Batinah) and the outward etiquettes (Adab al-Zahirah). And that must be explained and detailed, and its purposes are revealed in four chapters.
10:57.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

10:58.arabic: فأما المحمود فأربعة أقسام "الأول" أن يكون قصده إخفاء الطاعة والإخلاص لله، ولكن لما اطلع عليه الخلق علم أن الله أطلعهم وأظهر الجميل من أحواله، فيستدل به على حسن صنع الله به ونظره إليه وإلطافه به، فإنه يستر الطاعة والمعصية ثم الله يستر عليه المعصية ويظهر الطاعة، ولا لطف أعظم من ستر القبيح وإظهار الجميل، فيكون فرحه بجميل نظر الله لا بحمد الناس وقيام المنزلة في قلوبهم وقد قال تعالى "قل بفضل الله وبرحمته فبذلك فليفرحوا" فكأنه ظهر له أنه عند الله مقبول ففرح به.
10:58.english: As for the praiseworthy [joy], it is of four types. The first is that his intention was to conceal the obedience and have sincerity (Ikhlas) for Allah, but when the creation became aware of it, he knew that Allah made them aware and manifested the beautiful from his states, so he deduces from this the goodness of Allah's making (صنع) concerning him, His gaze (نظر) upon him, and His gentleness (لطف) with him. For He conceals the obedience and the disobedience, then Allah conceals from him the disobedience and manifests the obedience, and there is no gentleness (لطف) greater than concealing the ugly and manifesting the beautiful. Thus, his joy is with the beautiful gaze (نظر) of Allah, not with the praise of people and the establishment of status in their hearts. And Allah the Exalted has said: "Say: In the bounty (فضل) of Allah and in His mercy (رحمة) - in that let them rejoice." So it is as if it became apparent to him that he is accepted by Allah, so he rejoiced in it.
10:58.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

10:61.arabic: العلم: وأنه عالم بجميع المعلومات محيط بما يجري من تخوم الأرضين إلى أعلى السموات وأنه عالم لا يعزب عن علمه مثقال ذرة في الأرض ولا في السماء بل يعلم دبيب النملة السوداء على الصخرة الصماء في الليلة الظلماء ويدرك حركة الذر في جو الهواء ويعلم السر وأخفى، ويطلع على هواجس الضمائر وحركات الخواطر وخفيات السرائر بعلم قديم أزلي لم يزل موصوفا به في أزل الآزال لا بعلم متجدد حاصل في ذاته بالحلول والانتقال.
10:61.english: Knowledge: And He is Knower (Alim) of all knowledges (ma'lumat), encompassing what occurs from the depths of the earths to the highest of the heavens, and He is Knower (Alim) such that not even the weight of an atom (mithqal dharrah) in the earth or in the heaven escapes His knowledge (ilm), rather He knows the crawling of the black ant on the solid rock in the dark night, and perceives the movement of the particle (dharrah) in the air's atmosphere, and knows the secret (sirr) and what is more hidden (akhfa), and gazes upon the stirrings of the consciences (damair), the movements of the thoughts (khawatir), and the hidden aspects of the innermost secrets (sara'ir) with an ancient, eternal knowledge (ilm qadim azali) that He has not ceased to be described with in the eternity of eternities (azal al-azal), not with a newly occurring knowledge (ilm mutajaddid) obtained in His essence (dhat) through indwelling (hulul) and transference (intiqal).
10:61.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

10:61.arabic: الأصل الثاني: العلم بأنه تعالى عالم بجميع الموجودات ومحيط بكل المخلوقات لا يعزب عن علمه مثقال ذرة في الأرض ولا في السماء صادق في قوله وهو بكل شيء عليم ومرشد إلى صدقه بقوله تعالى ألا يعلم من خلق وهو اللطيف الخبير أرشدك إلى الاستدلال بالخلق على العلم بأنك لا تستريب في دلالة الخلق اللطيف والصنع المزين بالترتيب ولو في الشيء الحقير الضعيف على علم الصانع بكيفية الترتيب والترصيف فما ذكره الله سبحانه هو المنتهى في الهداية والتعريف.
10:61.english: The Second Foundation: The knowledge that He, exalted is He, is Knower of all existents and encompasses every created thing; there does not escape from His knowledge the weight of an atom in the earth nor in the heaven, truthful in His saying 'And He is, of all things, Knowing' (Quran 64:11), and guiding to its truthfulness by His saying, exalted is He: 'Does He not know, He Who created? And He is the Subtle (Al-Lateef), the Aware (Al-Khabeer)' (Quran 67:14). He guides you to the deduction from the creation to the knowledge that you do not doubt in the indication of the subtle (lateef) creation and the work adorned with arrangement, even in the insignificant, weak thing, upon the knowledge of the Maker concerning the manner of arrangement and composition. So what Allah, glorified is He, has mentioned is the ultimate in guidance and definition.
10:61.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Foundations of Belief'

10:66.arabic: ومنها المكرر القاطع لوصل الكلام في الظاهر كقوله عز وجل ﴿ وما يتبع الذين يدعون من دون الله شركاء إن يتبعون إلا الظن ﴾ {}
10:66.english: And among them is the repeated [expression] that cuts off the connection of speech in appearance, like His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And what follow those who call upon besides Allah partners? They follow not except conjecture' {}
10:66.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

10:68.arabic: وقال تعالى هل عندكم من سلطان بهذا أي حجة وبرهان وقال تعالى: ﴿ قل فلله الحجة البالغة ﴾ {} وقال تعالى ألم تر إلى الذي حاج إبراهيم في ربه إلى قوله فبهت الذي كفر إذ ذكر سبحانه احتجاج إبراهيم ومجادلته وإفحامه خصمه في معرض الثناء عليه
10:68.english: And He, the Exalted, said: 'Do you have any authority (sulṭān) for this?' meaning proof (ḥujjah) and evidence (burhān). And He, the Exalted, said: 'Say: To Allah belongs the conclusive argument (al-ḥujjah al-bālighah).' And He, the Exalted, said: 'Have you not seen the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord?' up to His saying: 'So the one who disbelieved was confounded,' when He, the Glorified, mentioned Abraham's argumentation (iḥtijāj) and disputation (mujādalah) and silencing his opponent in the context of praising him.
10:68.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Foundations of Belief'

10:84.arabic: أما الترادف ففي قوله تعالى: ﴿ فأخرجنا من كان فيها من المؤمنين. فما وجدنا فيها غير بيت من المسلمين ﴾ {} ولم يكن بالاتفاق إلا بيت واحد وقال تعالى: ﴿ يا قوم إن كنتم آمنتم بالله فعليه توكلوا إن كنتم مسلمين ﴾ {} وقال ﭬ: (بني الإسلام على خمس[45]) وسئل رسول الله ﭬ مرة عن الإيمان فأجاب بهذه الخمس[46]
10:84.english: As for synonymy, it is in His saying, the Exalted: 'So We brought out those who were in it of the believers. And We found in it not but a house of the Muslims (Muslimīn)' {} and it was by agreement only one house. And He said, the Exalted: 'O my people, if you have believed in Allah, then upon Him rely, if you are Muslims (Muslimīn)' {}. And he (the Prophet) ﭬ said: 'Islam is built upon five [45]'. And the Messenger of Allah ﭬ was asked once about faith (Īmān) and he answered with these five [46].
10:84.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Foundations of Belief'

10:85.arabic: ربنا لا تجعلنا فتنة للقوم الظالمين ربنا لا تجعلنا فتنة للذين كفروا واغفر لنا ربنا إنك أنت العزيز الحكيم
10:85.english: Our Lord, do not make us a trial (Fitnah) for the oppressive people (Al-Qawm Al-Zalimin). Our Lord, do not make us a trial (Fitnah) for those who disbelieve, and forgive us, our Lord. Indeed, You are the Mighty (Al-Aziz), the Wise (Al-Hakim).
10:85.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

10:94.arabic: فإن كنتم في شك مما جاء به محمد ﭬ فائتونا لنبين لكم ولنريكم من النور ما تطمئن إليه قلوبكم!
10:94.english: If you are in doubt about what Muhammad (peace be upon him) brought, then come to us so we may clarify for you and show you from the Light (Nur) what will bring tranquility (Tuma'ninah) to your hearts (Qulub)!
10:94.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of the World'

10:101.arabic: والواصلون إلى هذه الرتبة ينقسمون إلى الأقوياء ويكون أول معرفتهم بالله تعالى، ثم به يعرفون غيره. وإلى الضعفاء ويكون أول معرفتهم بالأفعال ثم يترقون منها إلى الفاعل. وإلى الأول الإشارة بقوله تعالى: " أو لم يكف بربك أنه على كل شيء شهيد " وبقوله تعالى: " شهد الله أنه لا إله إلا هو " ومنه نظر بعضهم حيث قيل له: بم عرفت ربك؟ قال: عرفت ربي ولولا ربي لما عرفت ربي، وإلى الثاني بقوله تعالى: " سنريهم آياتنا في الآفاق وفي أنفسهم حتى يتبين لهم أنه الحق " الآية. وبقوله عز وجل: " أو لم ينظروا في ملكوت السموات وا
10:101.english: And those who reach this rank are divided into the strong ones whose first knowledge is of Allah the Exalted, then through Him they know others. And into the weak ones whose first knowledge is of the actions then they ascend from them to the Actor. And to the first is the indication by His saying the Exalted: "Or is it not sufficient for your Lord that He is over all things a Witness?" and by His saying the Exalted: "Allah witnesses that there is no deity except Him." And from it is the view of some of them when it was said to him: By what did you know your Lord? He said: I knew my Lord and were it not for my Lord I would not have known my Lord. And to the second by His saying the Exalted: "We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth." The verse. And by His saying the Mighty and Majestic: "Have they not looked into the dominion of the heavens and the earth?" And by His saying the Exalted: "Say: Look at what is in the heavens and the earth." And by His saying the Exalted: "Who created seven heavens in layers. You do not see in the creation of the Most Merciful any inconsistency. So return the vision; do you see any breaks? Then return the vision twice again. The vision will return to you humbled while it is fatigued." And this path is the easiest for most people and it is the widest for the travelers, and to it is most of the call of the Quran when commanding with contemplation (Tadabbur), reflection (Tafakkur), consideration (I'tibar), and looking (Nadhar) in signs outside of enumeration.
10:101.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

11:4.arabic: فإذا بلغك وفاة أحد فقل إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون وإنا إلى ربنا لمنقلبون ا
11:4.english: And when you hear of someone's death, say: 'Indeed we belong to Allah and indeed to Him we will return, and indeed to our Lord we are turning back.'
11:4.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter

11:4.arabic: [197]  حديث القول عند دخول السوق لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له له الملك وله الحمد يحيي ويميت وهو حي لا يموت بيده الخير وهو على كل شيء قدير من حديث عمر وقال غريب والحاكم وقال صحيح على شرط الشيخين.
11:4.english: [197] The hadith of the saying when entering the market: 'There is no god but Allah alone, He has no partner, to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs the praise, He gives life and causes death, and He is living and does not die, in His hand is the good, and He is over all things powerful (Qadīr).'
