14:1.arabic: الحمد لله الذي بيده مقاليد الأمور، وبقدرته مفاتيح الخيرات والشرور، مخرج أوليائه من الظلمات إلى النور، ومورد أعدائه ورطات الغرور، والصلاة على محمد مخرج الخلائق من الديجور، وعلى آله وأصحابه الذين لم تغرهم الحياة الدنيا ولم يغرهم بالله الغرور، صلاة تتوالى على ممر الدهور ومكر الساعات والشهور. أما بعد: فمفتاح السعادة التيقظ والفطنة، ومنبع الشقاوة الغرور والغفلة فلا نعمة لله على عباده أعظم من الإيمان والمعرفة، ولا وسيلة سوى انشراح الصدر بنور البصيرة، ولا نقمة أعظم من الكفر والمعصية، ولا داعي إليهما سو
14:1.english: Praise be to Allah who holds in His hand the keys of affairs, and by His power are the keys of good and evil, who brings out His allies from the darknesses to the light, and brings His enemies into the pitfalls of delusion, and prayers upon Muhammad, who brings out the creatures from the darkness, and upon his family and companions who were not deluded by the worldly life nor deluded by Allah's delusion, prayers that continue through the passage of ages and the plotting of hours and months. After that: The key to happiness is vigilance and insight, and the source of misery is delusion and heedlessness, so there is no blessing from Allah upon His servants greater than faith and knowledge, and no means except the expansion of the chest by the light of insight, and no punishment greater than disbelief and disobedience, and no caller to them except the blindness of the heart by the darkness of ignorance. So the intelligent ones and possessors of insight, their hearts are "like a niche in which is a lamp, the lamp is in a glass, the glass as if it were a brilliant star, lit from a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if untouched by fire - light upon light" and the deluded ones, their hearts are "like darknesses in a deep sea covered by waves, upon which are waves, above which are clouds - darknesses, one above another. If one stretches out his hand, he can hardly see it. And he for whom Allah has not made light - for him there is no light." So the intelligent ones are those whom Allah intended to guide, so He expanded their chests for Islam and guidance, and the deluded ones are those whom Allah intended to misguide, so He made their chests tight and constricted as if ascending into the sky. And the deluded one is he whose insight has not opened to be sufficient for the guidance of his soul and
14:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

14:2.arabic: فالعدل هو أن يكون أولى به، وعبر الفقراء عن هذا الترجيح بالملك، وهو مجاز محض، إذ لا ملك إلا لملك الملوك الذى له ما في السموات والأرض وكيف يكون العبد مالكا وهو في نفسه ليس يملك نفسه بل هو ملك غيره، نعم الخلق عباد الله والأرض مائدة الله وقد أذن لهم في الأكل من مائدته بقدر حاجتهم كالملك ينصب مائدة لعبيده، فمن أخذ لقمة بيمينه واحتوت عليها براجمه فجاء عبد آخر وأراد انتزاعها من يده لم يمكن منه لا لأن اللقمة صارت ملكا له بالأخذ باليد فإن اليد وصاحب اليد أيضا مملوك ولكن إذا كانت كل لقمة بعينها لا تفى بحا
14:2.english: Justice (Al-Adl) is that one should be more deserving of it, and the poor have expressed this preference as ownership (Al-Mulk), which is purely metaphorical, for there is no ownership except for the King of Kings (Malik Al-Muluk) who has what is in the heavens and the earth. How can the servant (Al-Abd) be an owner when he himself does not own himself, but rather is owned by another? Indeed, the creation (Al-Khalq) are servants of Allah (Ibad Allah) and the earth is the table of Allah (Maidat Allah), and He has permitted them to eat from His table according to their need, like a king who sets a table for his servants. So whoever takes a morsel with his right hand and encloses it with his knuckles, and then another servant comes and wants to snatch it from his hand, he cannot be prevented from it not because the morsel has become his property by taking it with the hand, for the hand and the owner of the hand are also owned. But if each specific morsel does not fulfill the need of all the servants, then justice in specification occurs when there is a kind of preference, distinction, and taking—a distinction that the servant uniquely possesses—so that those who do not present such distinction are prevented from competing with him. Thus, one should understand the command of Allah regarding His servants. Therefore, we say: whoever takes from the worldly wealth more than his need and hoards it and holds onto it, while among the servants of Allah are those who need it, he is unjust (Zalim) and is among those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend them in the path of Allah (Sabil Allah). And indeed, the path of Allah is obedience to Him (Taatuhu), and the provision for the creation in His obedience is worldly wealth, for through it their necessities are repelled and their needs are elevated. Indeed, this does not fall within the scope of legal rulings (Fatawa Al-Fiqh) because the measures of needs are hidden, and the souls (Al-Nufus) in sensing poverty in the future are different, and the ends of lifespans are unknown, so imposing this on the common people proceeds in the manner of...
14:2.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

14:3.arabic: وقال تعالى: " الذين يستحبون الحياة الدنيا على الآخرة " فوصف الكفار بذلك، فمفهومه أن المؤمن هو الذي يتصف بنقيضه وهو أن يستحب الآخرة على الحياة الدنيا.
14:3.english: And He (Allah), the Exalted, said: "Those who prefer the worldly life (al-Hayat al-Dunya) over the Hereafter (al-Akhira)" — thus He described the disbelievers (al-Kuffar) with that. The implication (mafhumuhu) is that the believer (al-Mu'min) is the one who is characterized by its opposite (bi-naqidhihi), which is that he prefers the Hereafter (al-Akhira) over the worldly life (al-Hayat al-Dunya).
14:3.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

14:5.arabic: الحمد لله الذي بيده مقاليد الأمور، وبقدرته مفاتيح الخيرات والشرور، مخرج أوليائه من الظلمات إلى النور، ومورد أعدائه ورطات الغرور، والصلاة على محمد مخرج الخلائق من الديجور، وعلى آله وأصحابه الذين لم تغرهم الحياة الدنيا ولم يغرهم بالله الغرور، صلاة تتوالى على ممر الدهور ومكر الساعات والشهور. أما بعد: فمفتاح السعادة التيقظ والفطنة، ومنبع الشقاوة الغرور والغفلة فلا نعمة لله على عباده أعظم من الإيمان والمعرفة، ولا وسيلة سوى انشراح الصدر بنور البصيرة، ولا نقمة أعظم من الكفر والمعصية، ولا داعي إليهما سو
14:5.english: Praise be to Allah who in His hand are the keys of affairs, and by His power are the keys of good and evil, who brings out His allies from the darknesses to the light, and brings His enemies into the pitfalls of delusion, and prayers upon Muhammad who brings out the creatures from the darkness, and upon his family and companions who were not deluded by the worldly life and were not deluded about Allah by delusion, prayers that continue through the passage of ages and the plotting of hours and months. After that: The key to happiness is wakefulness and insight, and the source of misery is delusion and heedlessness, so there is no blessing from Allah upon His servants greater than faith and knowledge, and no means except the expansion of the chest by the light of insight, and no punishment greater than disbelief and disobedience, and no caller to them except the blindness of the heart by the darkness of ignorance. So the intelligent ones and possessors of insights, their hearts are "like a niche in which is a lamp, the lamp is in a glass, the glass as if it were a brilliant star, lit from a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if untouched by fire, light upon light" and the deluded ones, their hearts are "like darknesses in a deep sea covered by waves, above which are clouds, darknesses, one above another, if he puts out his hand, he can hardly see it, and he for whom Allah has not made light, for him there is no light." So the intelligent ones are those whom Allah intended to guide, so He expanded their chests for Islam and guidance, and the deluded ones are those whom Allah intended to misguide, so He made their chests tight and constricted as if ascending into the sky. And the deluded one is he whose insight has not opened to be sufficient for guiding his own self and
14:5.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

14:10.arabic: القسم الثاني: التكبر على الرسل من حيث تعزز النفس وترفعها على الانقياد لبشر مثل سائر الناس؛ وذلك تارة يصرف عن الفكر والاستبصار فيبقى في ظلمة الجهل بكبره فيمتنع عن الانقياد وهو ظان أنه محق فيه، وتارة يمتنع مع المعرفة ولكن لا تطاوعه نفسه للإنقياد للحق والتواضع للرسل، كما حكى الله قولهم "أنؤمن لبشرين مثلنا" وقولهم "إن أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا ولئن أطعتم بشراً مثلكم إنكم إذا لخاسرون" وقال الذين لا يرجون لقائنا لولا أنزل علينا الملائكة أو نرى ربنا لقد استكبروا في أنفسهم وعتوا عواً كبيراً. وقالوا لولا أنزل ع
14:10.english: The second category: Arrogance (Takabbur) toward the Messengers, stemming from the Soul (Nafs) strengthening and elevating itself above submission to a human being like other people; this sometimes diverts from thought (Fikr) and insight (Istibsar), leaving one in the darkness of ignorance (Jahl) due to his arrogance, so he refuses to submit while thinking he is correct in it, and sometimes he refuses despite knowledge (Ma'rifah) but his Soul (Nafs) does not comply with submission to the Truth (Haqq) and humility toward the Messengers, as Allah narrated their saying: "Shall we believe in two humans like ourselves?" and their saying: "You are only human beings like us, and if you obey a human being like yourselves, then indeed you would be losers." And those who do not expect the meeting with Us said: "Why have not angels been sent down to us, or why do we not see our Lord?" They have certainly become arrogant within themselves and become insolent with great insolence. And they said: "Why has not an angel been sent down to him?" And Pharaoh, in what Allah informed about him, said: "Or that the angels should come with him, combined together?" And Allah said: "And he and his soldiers were arrogant in the land without right." So he was arrogant toward Allah and toward all His Messengers. Wahb said: Moses, peace be upon him, said to him: "Believe, and you will have your kingdom." He said: "Until I consult Haman." So he consulted Haman, and Haman said: "While you are a lord being worshipped, you have become a slave worshipping." So he disdained the worship (Ibadah) of Allah and from following Moses, peace be upon him. And Quraysh, in what Allah informed about them, said: "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a man from the two cities who is great?" Qatadah said: The great one of the two cities is Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughirah and Abu Mas'ud Al-Thaqafi. They demanded one who has greater leadership than the Prophet, peace be upon him, when they said: "An orphan boy, how has Allah sent him to us?" So Allah said: "Do they distribute the mercy of your Lord?" And Allah said: "So that they may say: 'Are these whom Allah has favored among us?'" meaning belittling them and considering their precedence unlikely. And Quraysh said to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him: "How can we sit with you when these are present?" And they pointed to the poor Muslims, and they looked down upon them with their eyes due to their poverty, and
14:10.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

14:10.arabic: فليس يخفى على من معه أدنى مسكة من عقل إذا تأمل بأدنى فكرة مضمون هذه الآيات وأدار نظره على عجائب خلق الله في الأرض والسموات وبدائع فطرة الحيوان والنبات أن هذا الأمر العجيب والترتيب المحكم لا يستغني عن صانع يدبره وفاعل يحكمه ويقدره بل تكاد فطرة النفوس تشهد بكونها مقهورة تحت تسخيره ومصرفة بمقتضى تدبيره ولذلك قال الله تعالى أفي الله شك فاطر السموات والأرض ولهذا بعث الأنبياء صلوات الله عليهم لدعوة الخلق إلى التوحيد ليقولوا لا إله إلا الله وما أمروا أن يقولوا لنا إله وللعالم إله فإن ذلك كان مجبولا في
14:10.english: It is not hidden from one who possesses the slightest bit of intellect, if he contemplates with the slightest thought the content of these verses and turns his gaze upon the wonders of Allah's creation in the earth and the heavens and the marvels of the natural disposition (Fitra) of animals and plants, that this amazing affair and precise arrangement cannot do without a Maker who manages it and an Agent who governs and decrees it. Rather, the natural disposition (Fitra) of the souls almost testifies to being subdued under His subjugation and directed according to His management. Therefore, Allah the Exalted said: 'Is there any doubt about Allah, the Originator (Fāṭir) of the heavens and the earth?' (Quran 14:10). And for this reason, the prophets, prayers of Allah be upon them, were sent to call the creation to Monotheism (Tawḥīd) so that they would say 'There is no god but Allah,' and they were not commanded to say to us a god and to the world a god, for that was ingrained in the natural disposition (Fitra) of their intellects from the beginning of their emergence and in the prime of their youth. Therefore, He the Exalted said: 'And if you ask them who created the heavens and the earth, they will surely say Allah' (Quran 31:25). And He the Exalted said: 'So set your face to the religion, uprightly, the natural disposition (Fitra) of Allah upon which He has created people; there is no altering the creation of Allah; that is the upright religion' (Quran 30:30). Thus, in the natural disposition (Fitra) of man and the evidences of the Quran, there is what suffices without establishing proof.
14:10.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Foundations of Belief'

14:12.arabic: ولترك الأسباب الدافعة وإن كانت مقطوعة وجه إذا ناله الضرر من إنسان، فإنه إذا أمكنه الصبر وأمكنه الدفع والتشفي فشرط التوكل الاحتمال والصبر، قال الله تعالى: " فاتخذه وكيلاً واصبر على ما يقولون ". وقال تعالى: " ولنصبرن على ما آذيتمونا وعلى الله فليتوكل المتوكلون ". وقال عز وجل: " ودع أذاهم وتوكل على الله ". وقال سبحانه وتعالى: " فاصبر كما صبر أولو العزم من الرسل ". وقال تعالى: " نعم أجر العاملين الذين صبروا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون " وهذا في أذى الناس، وأما الصبر على أذى الحيات والسباع والعقارب، فترك دفعها
14:12.english: And abandoning the repelling causes, even if they are certain, has a justification when harm comes to him from a human being, for if he is capable of patience (sabr) and capable of repelling and seeking revenge, then the condition of reliance (tawakkul) is endurance and patience (sabr). Allah the Exalted said: "So take Him as your trustee and be patient (sabr) over what they say." And He said: "And we will surely be patient (sabr) over what you harm us, and upon Allah let the reliant ones rely (tawakkul)." And He the Mighty and Majestic said: "And leave their harm and rely (tawakkul) upon Allah." And He the Blessed and Exalted said: "So be patient (sabr) as the resolute ones of the messengers were patient (sabr)." And He said: "Excellent is the reward of the workers who were patient (sabr) and upon their Lord they rely (tawakkul)." And this is regarding the harm of people. As for patience (sabr) upon the harm of snakes, beasts, and scorpions, abandoning repelling them is not from reliance (tawakkul) in anything, for there is no benefit in it, and striving is not intended nor is striving abandoned for its own sake but rather to aid in the religion (deen), and the arrangement of causes here is like their arrangement in earning and bringing benefits, so we do not prolong with repetition. Likewise, in the causes repelling from wealth, reliance (tawakkul) is not diminished by closing the door of the house when leaving nor by tying the camel, because these are causes known by the Sunnah of Allah the Exalted either certainly or presumably, and for that reason He ﷺ said to the Bedouin when he neglected the camel and said 'I have relied (tawakkul) upon Allah': 'Tie it and rely (tawakkul).'
14:12.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

14:12.arabic: القسم الثاني: مالا يرتبط هجومه باختياره وله اختيار في دفعه كما لو أوذي بفعل أو قول وجنى عليه في نفسه أو ماله، فالصبر على ذلك بترك المكافأة تارة يكون واجبا وتارة يكون فضيلة. قال بعض الصحابة رضوان الله عليهم: ما كنا نعدّ إيمان الرجل ايمانا إذا لم يصبر على الأذى، وقال تعالى: ﴿ ولنصبرنّ على ما آذيتمونا وعلى الله فليتوكل المتوكلون ﴾ {}. (وقسم رسول الله ﭬ مرة مالا، فقال بعض الأعراب من المسلمين هذه قسمة ما أريد بها وجه الله فأخبر رسول الله فاحمرت وجنتاه ثم قال يرحم الله أخي موسى لقد أوذي بأكثر من هذا ف
14:12.english: The second category: That which does not relate to its assault by one's choice, but one has a choice in repelling it, as if one is harmed by an action or speech and wronged in his self (Nafs) or wealth, so patience (Sabr) regarding that by abandoning retaliation is sometimes obligatory and sometimes a virtue. Some of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, said: We did not consider a man's faith (Iman) to be faith if he did not have patience (Sabr) with harm, and Allah the Exalted said: 'And we will certainly have patience (Sabr) with what you harm us, and upon Allah let the reliant ones (Mutawakkilun) rely.' (Quran 14:12). (And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, once distributed wealth, and some Bedouin from the Muslims said: This is a distribution not intended for the Face of Allah, so the Messenger of Allah was informed, and his cheeks reddened, then he said: May Allah have mercy on my brother Musa, he was harmed more than this and had patience (Sabr)[24]). And Allah the Exalted said: 'And leave their harm and rely (Tawakkul) upon Allah' (Quran 73:10). And Allah the Exalted said: 'And have patience (Sabr) with what they say and leave them with a beautiful leaving' (Quran 73:10). And Allah the Exalted said: 'And We certainly know that your chest (Sadr) is constrained by what they say, so glorify with the praise of your Lord' (Quran 15:97) the verse. And Allah the Exalted said: 'And you will certainly hear much harm from those who were given the Book before you and from those who associate partners, and if you have patience (Sabr) and guard (Taqwa), then indeed that is from the matters of determination' (Quran 3:186), meaning have patience (Sabr) from retaliation, and for that Allah the Exalted praised those who pardon from their rights in retaliation (Qisas) and other than it, so He the Exalted said: 'And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished, and if you have patience (Sabr), it is better for the patient ones (Sabirin)' (Quran 16:126). And he, peace be upon him, said: 'Pray for the one who cuts you off, give to the one who deprives you, and pardon the one who wrongs you[25].' And I saw in the Gospel, Isa ibn Maryam, peace be upon him, said: It was said to you before: An eye for an eye and a nose for a nose, and I say to you: Do not resist with evil, but whoever strikes your right cheek, turn to him the left cheek, and whoever takes your cloak, give him your garment, and whoever compels you to go one mile, go with him two miles, and all of that is a command for patience (Sabr).
14:12.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

14:12.arabic: وقال عز وجل: " وعلى الله فليتوكل المتوكلون ". وقال تعالى: " ومن يتوكل على الله فهو حسبه ". وقال سبحانه وتعالى: " إن الله يحب المتوكلين " وأعظم بمقام موسوم بمحبة الله تعالى صاحبه، ومضمون كفاية الله تعالى ملابسه، فمن الله تعالى حسبه وكافيه ومحبه ومراعيه: فقد فاز الفوز العظيم، فإن المحبوب لا يعذب ولا يبعد ولا يحجب. وقالت تعالى: " أليس الله بكاف عبده ". فطالب الكفاية من غيره والتارك للتوكل هو المكذب لهذه الآية. فإنه سؤال في معرض استنطاق بالحق، كقوله تعالى: " هل أتى على الإنسان حين من الدهر لم يكن شي
14:12.english: And He, the Exalted, said: "And upon Allah let the ones who trust (Mutawakkilun) rely." And He, the Exalted, said: "And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him." And He, the Glorified and Exalted, said: "Indeed, Allah loves the ones who rely (Mutawakkilun)." And how great is a station marked with the love of Allah, the Exalted, its possessor, and guaranteed the sufficiency of Allah, the Exalted, its companion. So whoever from Allah, the Exalted, is his sufficiency and his suffices and his lover and his guardian: then he has attained the great success, for the beloved is not punished nor distanced nor veiled. And He, the Exalted, said: "Is not Allah sufficient for His servant?" So the seeker of sufficiency from other than Him and the abandoner of reliance (Tawakkul) is the one who denies this verse. For it is a question in the manner of interrogation with the truth, like His saying, the Exalted: "Has there come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing mentioned?" And He, the Exalted, said: "And whoever relies upon Allah, then indeed Allah is Mighty, Wise." Meaning Mighty, He does not humiliate the one who seeks refuge in Him, nor does He waste the one who clings to His side and seeks protection in His sanctuary and His protection, and Wise, He does not fall short in managing the one who relies upon His management. And He, the Exalted, said: "Indeed, those you call upon besides Allah are servants like you." He clarified that everything besides Allah, the Exalted, is a subjugated servant. His need is like your need, so how can one rely upon him? And He, the Exalted, said: "Indeed, those you worship besides Allah do not possess for you provision, so seek provision from Allah and worship Him." And He, the Exalted, said: "And to Allah belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth, but the hypocrites do not understand." And He, the Exalted, said: "He manages the affair."
14:12.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

14:12.arabic: وإذا قال ﴿ ولنصبرن على ما آذيتمونا ﴾ {} فليكن حاله الصبر أو العزيمة عليه حتى يجد حلاوة التلاوة فإن لم يكن بهذه الصفات ولم يتردد قلبه بين هذه الحالات كان حظه من التلاوة حركة اللسان مع صريح اللعن على نفسه في قوله تعالى ﴿ ألا لعنة الله على الظالمين ﴾ {} وفي قوله تعالى ﴿ كبر مقتا عند الله أن تقولوا ما لا تفعلون ﴾ {} وفي قوله عز وجل -﴿ وهم في غفلة معرضون ﴾ {} وفي قوله ﴿ فأعرض عمن تولى عن ذكرنا ولم يرد إلا الحياة الدنيا ﴾ {} وفي قوله تعالى ﴿ ومن لم يتب فأولئك هم الظالمون ﴾ {} إلى غير ذلك من الآيات وكا
14:12.english: And when he says 'And we will certainly be patient over what you harm us' (Quran 14:12), his state should be patience (Sabr) or resolve upon it until he finds the sweetness of recitation. For if he is not with these qualities and his heart (Qalb) does not fluctuate between these states, his share of recitation is the movement of the tongue with clear curse upon himself in His saying, the Exalted, 'Indeed, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers' (Quran 11:18) and in His saying, the Exalted, 'Great is hatred in the sight of Allah that you say what you do not do' (Quran 61:3) and in His saying, the Exalted, 'And they are in heedlessness turning away' (Quran 21:1) and in His saying 'So turn away from whoever turns away from Our remembrance (Dhikr) and desires not except the worldly life' (Quran 53:29) and in His saying, the Exalted, 'And whoever does not repent - then those are the wrongdoers' (Quran 49:11) and other than that of the verses, and he was included in the meaning of His saying, the Exalted, 'And among them are unlettered ones who do not know the Scripture except [their] wishes' (Quran 2:78) meaning mere recitation, and His saying, the Exalted, 'And how many a sign in the heavens and earth they pass over while they are therefrom turning away' (Quran 12:105) because the Quran is the clarifier of those signs in the heavens and earth, and whenever he passes over them and is not affected by them, he is turning away from them. Therefore, it is said: Indeed, whoever is not characterized by the morals of the Quran, when he recites the Quran, Allah, the Exalted, calls to him: What is with you and My speech while you are turning away from Me? Leave My speech if you do not repent to Me. And the example of the disobedient when he recites the Quran and repeats it is like one who repeats the king's letter every day many times, and it has been written to him concerning the construction of a property...
14:12.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

14:14.arabic: وقد قال تعالى "ولمن خاف مقام ربه جنتان - ذلك لمن خاف مقامي وخاف وعيد" والقرآن من أوله إلى آخره تحذير وتخويف، لا يتفكر فيه متفكر إلا ويطول حزنه ويعظم خوفه إن كان مؤمناً بما فيه.
14:14.english: And Allah the Exalted has said: 'And for whoever fears the standing (maqām) of his Lord, two gardens - that is for whoever fears My standing (maqām) and fears My threat (waʿīd).' And the Quran from its beginning to its end is warning and intimidation; no one reflects upon it except that his sadness lengthens and his fear (khawf) increases if he is a believer in what is in it.
14:14.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

14:14.arabic: فذهبنا واستأذنا على ثالث فقال: ادخلوا إن لم تشغلونا عن ربنا فقرأت ﴿ ذلك لمن خاف مقامي وخاف وعيد ﴾{} فشهق شهقة فبدا الدم من منخريه وجعل يتشحط في دمه حتى يبس فتركناه على حاله وخرجنا
14:14.english: We went and sought permission from a third one. He said: 'Enter if you do not distract us from our Lord.' So I recited: 'That is for whoever fears My standing (maqāmī) and fears My threat (waʿīd).' He gasped a gasp, and blood began to flow from his nostrils, and he began to flounder in his blood until it dried. We left him in his state and departed.
14:14.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

14:15.arabic: قد ذم الله الكبر في مواضع من كتابه وذم كل جبار متكبر فقال تعالى "سأصرف عن آياتي الذين يتكبرون في الأرض بغير الحق" وقال عز وجل "كذلك يطبع الله على كل قلب متكبر جبار" وقال تعالى "واستفتحوا وخاب كل جبار عنيد" وقال تعالى "إنه لا يحب المستكبرين" وقال تعالى "لقد استكبروا في أنفسهم وعتوا عتواً كبيراً" وقال تعالى "إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي سيدخلون جهنم داخرين" وذم الكبر في القرآن كثير
14:15.english: Indeed, Allah has condemned arrogance in multiple places in His Book and condemned every tyrant who is arrogant. So He, the Exalted, said: "I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant on earth without right." And He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: "Thus does Allah seal over every heart (Qalb) of an arrogant tyrant." And He, the Exalted, said: "And they sought victory, and disappointed was every obstinate tyrant." And He, the Exalted, said: "Indeed, He does not love the arrogant." And He, the Exalted, said: "They had certainly become arrogant within themselves and transgressed a great transgression." And He, the Exalted, said: "Indeed, those who are arrogant toward My worship will enter Hell in humiliation." And the condemnation of arrogance in the Quran is abundant.
14:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

14:16.arabic: وقال أبو أمامة قال رسول الله ﷺ في قوله تعالى: ﴿ ويسقى من ماء صديد يتجرعه ولا يكاد يسيغه ﴾ قال: (يقرب إليه فيتكرهه فإذا أدنى منه شوى وجهه فوقعت فروة رأسه فإذا شربه قطع أمعاءه حتى يخرج من دبره يقول الله تعالى: ﴿ وسقوا ماء حميما فقطع أمعاءهم ﴾ وقال تعالى: ﴿ وإن يستغيثوا يغاثوا بماء كالمهل يشوى الوجوه ﴾ فهذه طعامهم وشرابهم عند جوعهم وعطشهم[206])
14:16.english: And Abu Umamah said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said regarding His (the Exalted's) statement: 'And he is given to drink from water of pus (صديد) which he gulps and can hardly swallow' (Quran 14:16-17): '(It is brought near to him and he dislikes it. When it is brought close to him, it scorches his face and the skin of his head falls off. When he drinks it, it cuts his intestines until it exits from his anus. Allah the Exalted says: "And they are given to drink boiling water (حميم) so it cuts their intestines" (Quran 47:15). And He the Exalted says: "And if they call for relief, they are relieved with water like molten metal (مهل) that scorches the faces" (Quran 18:29).) This is their food and drink during their hunger and thirst.'
14:16.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

14:16.arabic: ثم انظر بعد هذا فى نتن الصديد الذى يسيل من أبدانهم حتى يغرقون فيه وهو الغساق، قال أبو سعيد الخدرى قال رسول الله ﭬ: (لو أن دلوا من غساق جهنم ألقى فى الدنيا لأنتن أهل الأرض[202]) فهذا شرابهم إذا استغاثوا من العطش فيسقى أحرهم من ماء صديد يتجرعه ولا يكاد يسيغه ويأتيه الموت من كل مكان وما هو يميت وإن يستغيثوا يغاثوا بماء كالمهل يشوى الوجوه بئس الشراب وساءت مرتفقا.
14:16.english: Then look after this at the foulness of the pus (الصديد) that flows from their bodies until they drown in it, and it is the intensely cold pus (الغساق). Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: The Messenger of Allah ﭬ said: 'If a bucket of the intensely cold pus (غساق) of Hell were thrown into the world, it would corrupt the people of the earth.' [202] This is their drink when they cry for help from thirst, so the most intense of them is given to drink from pus water (ماء صديد) which he gulps down and can hardly swallow, and death comes to him from every place but it does not kill him. And if they cry for help, they are helped with water like molten brass that scalds the faces. Wretched is the drink and evil is the resting place.
14:16.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

14:16.arabic: [206]  حديث أبى أمامة فى قوله تعالى ويسقى من ماء صديد يتجرعه ولا يكاد يسيغه قال يقرب إليه الحديث أخرجه الترمذى وقال غريب.
14:16.english: [206] The hadith of Abu Umamah regarding His saying, the Exalted: 'And he will be given to drink from purulent water (mā' ṣadīd)' - he gulps it down and can hardly swallow it. He said: It is brought near to him. The hadith was transmitted by al-Tirmidhi and he said: It is rare (gharīb).
14:16.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Book of Repentance'

14:17.arabic: قال صالح: فبكيت وقلت في نفسي: أنا في واد وأنت في واد آخر. وقال السري السقطي: نفسي منذ ثلاثين سنة تطالبني أن أمس جزرة في دبس فما أطعمتها. وقال أبو بكر الجلاء. أعرف رجلاً تقول له نفسه أنا أصبر لك على طي عشرة أيام وأطعمني بعد ذلك شهوة أشتهيها، فيقول لها: لا أريد أن تطوى عشرة أيام ولكن اتركي هذه الشهوة. وروي أن عابداً دعا بعض إخوانه فقرب إليه رغفاناً فجعل أخوه يقلب الأرغفة ليختار أجودها فقال له العابد. مه أي شيء تصنع! أما علمت أن في الرغيف الذي رغبت عنه كذا وكذا حكمة وعمل فيه كذا وكذا صانعاً، حتى اس
14:17.english: Salih said: So I wept and said to myself: I am in one valley and you are in another valley. And Al-Sari Al-Saqati said: My Soul (Nafs) has been demanding from me for thirty years that I eat a carrot in syrup, but I have not fed it. And Abu Bakr Al-Jala' said: I know a man whose Soul (Nafs) says to him: I will endure for you the folding of ten days, then feed me after that a desire that I crave. He says to it: I do not want you to fold ten days, but leave this desire. And it is narrated that an ascetic invited some of his brothers and brought near to him two loaves of bread, so his brother began to turn over the loaves to choose the best of them. The ascetic said to him: Stop! What are you doing? Do you not know that in the loaf that you rejected is such and such wisdom, and worked in it such and such a maker, until it revolved from the cloud that carries the water and the water that irrigates the earth and the winds and the earth and the beasts and the children of Adam until it came to you, then you after this turn it over and are not satisfied with it. And in the report: "The loaf does not become round and placed between your hands until three hundred and sixty makers work in it, the first of them is Mika'il, peace be upon him, who measures the water from the treasuries of mercy, then the angels who drive the clouds and the sun and the moon and the spheres and the angels of the air and the creatures of the earth, and the last of them is the baker. "And if you count the blessings of Allah, you cannot enumerate them" [46]. And some of them said: I came to Qasim Al-Jar'i and asked him about asceticism a
14:17.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Harms of the Tongue'

14:21.arabic: قال مالك بن أنس رضى الله عنه: قال زيد بن أسلم فى قوله تعالى: ﴿ سواء علينا أجزعنا أم صبرنا ما لنا من محيص ﴾ {} قال صبروا مائة سنة ثم جزعوا مائة سنة ثم صبروا مائة سنة ثم قالوا ﴿ سواء علينا أجزعنا أم صبرنا ﴾ {}
14:21.english: Malik ibn Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Zayd ibn Aslam said regarding the saying of Allah the Exalted: 'It is equal upon us whether we despair or we are patient; there is no escape for us.' He said: They were patient for one hundred years, then they despaired for one hundred years, then they were patient for one hundred years, then they said: 'It is equal upon us whether we despair or we are patient.'
14:21.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

14:24.arabic: فيكون أول التلقين كإلقاء بذر في الصدر وتكون هذه الأسباب كالسقى والتربية له حتى ينمو ذلك البذر يقوى ويرتفع شجرة طيبة راسخة أصلها ثابت وفرعها في السماء وينبغي أن يحرس سمعه من الجدل والكلام غاية الحراسة فإن ما يشوّشه الجدل أكثر مما يمهده وما يفسده أكثر مما يصلحه بل تقويته بالجدل تضاهي ضرب الشجرة بالمدقة من الحديد رجاء تقويتها بأن تكثر أجزاؤها وربما يفتتها ذلك ويفسدها وهو الأغلب والمشاهدة تكفيك في هذا بيانا فناهيك بالعيان برهانا فقس عقيدة أهل الصلاح والتقى من عوام الناس بعقيدة المتكلمين والمجادلين ف
14:24.english: So the first teaching (Taqleed) is like planting a seed in the chest (Sadrat), and these causes are like watering and nurturing it until that seed grows, strengthens, and rises as a good (Tayyibah) tree, firmly rooted, its foundation (Asl) fixed and its branch (Far') in the sky. And one should guard his hearing from dialectics (Jadal) and theological disputation (Kalam) with utmost vigilance, for what confuses it through dialectics is more than what prepares it, and what corrupts it is more than what rectifies it. Rather, strengthening it through dialectics resembles striking a tree with an iron mallet hoping to strengthen it by increasing its parts, but perhaps that shatters it and corrupts it—and that is more likely. Observation suffices you in this as explanation, so let direct sight be your proof. Compare the belief (I'tiqad) of the people of righteousness (Salah) and piety (Taqwa) from the common folk to the belief of the theologians (Mutakallimun) and disputants (Mujadilun): you will see the common person's belief in steadfastness like a towering mountain (Tawd) that calamities (Dawahi) and thunderbolts (Sawa'iq) cannot move, while the theologian's belief, guarded by the divisions of dialectics, is like a thread sent into the air that the winds sway sometimes this way and sometimes that way—except for one who receives from them the proof of belief and accepts it through imitation (Taqleed) just as he accepted the belief itself through imitation, since there is no difference in imitation between teaching the proof or learning what is proven. Teaching the proof is one thing, and inferring through independent reasoning (Nadhar) is another thing far from it.
14:24.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

14:24.arabic: السبب الثاني: لقوة المحبة، قوة معرفة الله تعالى واتساعها واستيلاؤها على القلب، وذلك بعد تطهير القلب من جميع شواغل الدنيا وعلائقها يجري مجرى وضع البذر في الأرض بعد تنقيتها من الحشيش وهو الشطر الثاني. ثم يتولد من هذا البذر شجرة المحبة والمعرفة وهي الكلمة الطيبة التي ضرب الله بها مثلاً حيث قال: "ضرب الله مثلاً كلمة طيبة كشجرة طيبة أصلها ثابت وفرعها في السماء" وإليها الإشارة بقوله تعالى "إليه يصعد الكلم الطيب"، أي المعرفة "والعمل الصالح يرفعه" فالعمل الصالح كالجمال لهذه المعرفة وكالخادم وإنما العمل
14:24.english: The second reason: For the strength of love, the strength of knowledge of Allah the Exalted and its expansion and its domination over the heart (Qalb), and that after purifying the heart from all distractions of the world and its attachments, it proceeds like placing the seed in the earth after purifying it from weeds, which is the second half. Then from this seed is generated the tree of love and knowledge, which is the good word (Kalimah Tayyibah) that Allah struck as a parable when He said: "Allah struck a parable: a good word is like a good tree, its root is firm and its branch is in the sky." And to it is the indication by His saying the Exalted "To Him ascends the good word," meaning the knowledge "and the righteous deed raises it." So the righteous deed is like beauty for this knowledge and like a servant, and indeed all righteous deed is in purifying the heart first from the world then maintaining its purity, so the deed is not desired except for this knowledge, and as for the knowledge of how to perform the deed, it is desired for the deed, so knowledge is the first and it is the last, and indeed the first is knowledge of interaction (Ilm al-Mu'amalah) and its purpose is the deed, and the purpose of interaction is clarity of the heart and its purity so that in it becomes clear the manifestation of the truth and it becomes adorned with knowledge of knowledge (Ilm al-Ma'rifah), which is knowledge of unveiling (Ilm al-Mukashafah). And whenever this knowledge is attained, love follows it by necessity, just as one who has balanced temperament, if he sees the beautiful and perceives it with the apparent eye, loves it and inclines to it, and whenever he loves it, pleasure occurs, so pleasure follows love by necessity, and love follows knowledge by necessity, and one does not reach this knowledge after cutting off distractions of the world from the heart except with pure thought (Fikr) and constant remembrance (Dhikr) and utmost effort in seeking and continuous contemplation in Allah the Exalted and in His attributes and in the dominion of His heavens and all His creations.
14:24.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

14:24.arabic: والمحبة شجرة طيبة أصلها ثابت وفرعها في السماء وثمارها تظهر في القلب واللسان والجوارح. وتدل تلك الآثار الفائضة منها على القلب والجوارح على المحبة دلالة الدخان على النار ودلالة الثمار على الأشجار. وهي كثيرة فمنها حب لقاء الحبيب بطريق الكشف والمشاهدة في دار السلام، فلا يتصور أن يحب القلب محبوباً إلا ويحب مشاهدته ولقاءه، وإذا علم أنه لا وصول إلا بالارتحال من الدنيا ومفارقتها بالموت فينبغي أن يكون محباً للموت غير فار منه، فإن المحب لا يثقل عليه السفر عن وطنه إلى مستقر محبوبه ليتنعم بمشاهدته والموت مف
14:24.english: And love is a good tree whose root is firm and whose branch is in the sky and its fruits appear in the heart (Qalb), the tongue, and the limbs. And those overflowing effects from it upon the heart (Qalb) and the limbs indicate love with the indication of smoke upon fire and the indication of fruits upon trees. And they are many, among them is love of meeting the Beloved through unveiling (Kashf) and witnessing (Mushahada) in the Abode of Peace (Dar al-Salam), so it is inconceivable that the heart (Qalb) loves a beloved except that it loves seeing him and meeting him, and when it knows that there is no arrival except by departing from the world and leaving it through death, then it should be loving of death, not fleeing from it, for the lover is not burdened by traveling from his homeland to the abode of his beloved to delight in seeing him, and death is the key to meeting and the door to entering into witnessing (Mushahada).
14:24.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

14:27.arabic: اللهم اعصمني من فتن الدنيا ووفقني لما تحب وترضى وأصلح لي شأني كله وثبتني بالقول الثابت في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة ولا تضلني وإن كنت ظالما
14:27.english: O Allah, protect me from the trials of the worldly life (Dunya) and grant me success in what You love and are pleased with, and rectify all my affairs, and make me firm with the firm word (al-Qawl al-Thabit) in the worldly life (al-Hayat al-Dunya) and in the Hereafter (al-Akhirah), and do not lead me astray even if I am among the wrongdoers (al-Zalimin).
14:27.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure

14:31.arabic: بل في الحديث الصحيح ما روي أنه ﷺ قال "من كانت لأخيه عنده مظلمة في عرض أو مال فليستحللها منه من قبل أن يأتي يوم ليس هناك دينار ولا درهم، إنما يؤخذ من حسناته فإن لم يكن له حسنات أخذ من سيئات صاحبه فزيدت على سيئاته"[226]
14:31.english: Rather, in the authentic hadith, it is narrated that he (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever has a grievance against his brother in honor or wealth, let him seek its resolution from him before there comes a day where there is no dinar nor dirham; indeed, it will be taken from his good deeds, and if he has no good deeds, it will be taken from the bad deeds of his companion and added to his bad deeds."
14:31.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

14:34.arabic: ولذلك كان ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما يقول اللهم إني أستغفرك لظلمي وكفري فقيل له هذا الظلم فما بال الكفر فتلا قوله عز وجل إن الإنسان لظلوم كفار
14:34.english: And therefore Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) used to say: 'O Allah, I seek Your forgiveness for my injustice (ظلمي) and my ingratitude (كفري).' It was said to him: 'This is the injustice (الظلم), but what about the ingratitude (الكفر)?' So he recited His (Exalted is He) saying: 'Indeed, the human being is an unjust wrongdoer (ظلوم), a disbelieving ingrate (كفار).'
14:34.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

14:35.arabic: ولما كانت الطباع مائلة إلى اتباع الشهوات القاطعة لسبيل الله وكان المال مسهلاً لها وآلة إليها، عظم الخطر فيما يزيد على قدر الكفاية فاستعاذ الأنبياء من شره حتى قال نبينا عليه الصالة والسلام "الله اجعل قوت آل محمد كفافاً" فلم يطلب من الدنيا غلا ما يتمحض خيره وقال "الله أحيني مسكيناً وأمتني مسكيناً واحشرني في زمرة المساكين" واستعاذ إبراهيم ﭬ فقال "واجنبني وبني أن نعبد الأصنام" وعنى بها هذين الحجرين الذهب والفضة، إذ رتبة النبوة أجل من أن يخشى عليها أن تعتقد الإلهية في شيء من هذه الحجارة، إذ قد كفى قب
14:35.english: And since the natural dispositions (Tabā'i') are inclined to follow the desires (Shahawāt) that cut off the path of Allah, and wealth (Māl) facilitates them and is a tool for them, the danger in what exceeds the measure of sufficiency became great, so the prophets sought refuge from its evil. Until our Prophet (upon him be peace and blessings) said: 'O Allah, make the provision of the family of Muhammad sufficient (Kafāf).' So he did not ask from the worldly life except what is purely good, and he said: 'O Allah, make me live as a poor person (Miskīn), make me die as a poor person (Miskīn), and gather me in the company of the poor (Masākīn).' And Abraham (peace be upon him) sought refuge, saying: 'And keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols (Aṣnām).' And he meant by them these two stones: gold and silver, for the rank of prophethood (Nubuwwah) is too noble to fear that it would believe in the divinity (Ilāhiyyah) of any of these stones, since he was protected before prophethood even in childhood. Rather, the meaning of worshipping them is loving them, being deceived by them, and relying upon them. Our Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Wretched is the slave (ʿAbd) of the Dinar, wretched is the slave (ʿAbd) of the Dirham, wretched and not prosperous, and if pricked, not relieved.' So he clarified that one who loves them is a worshipper of them, and whoever worships a stone is a worshipper of an idol (Ṣanam). Rather, everyone who is a slave (ʿAbd) to other than Allah is a worshipper of an idol (Ṣanam), meaning that it cuts him off from Allah the Exalted and from fulfilling His right, so he is like a worshipper of an idol (Ṣanam), and it is association (Shirk). Except that association (Shirk) is of two types: hidden association (Shirk Khafī) that does not necessitate eternal abode in the Fire, and rarely do the believers (Mu'minūn) escape from it, for it is more hidden than the crawling of ants; and manifest association (Shirk Jalī) that necessitates eternal abode in the Fire—we seek refuge in Allah from all of it.
14:35.book_title: Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth
14:35.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

14:36.arabic: وقال ﭬ: (لكل نبى دعوة مستجابة فأريد أن أختبىء دعوتي شفاعة لأمتى يوم القيامة[178]) وقال ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما: قال رسول الله ﭬ: (ينصب للأنبياء منابر من ذهب فيجلسون عليها ويبقى منبرى لا أجلس عليه قائما بين يدى ربى منتصبا مخافة أن يبعث بى إلى الجنة وأمره مخطر فى نفسه فإن عجزت عن ذلك كله فكن محبا لرسول الله ﭬ حريصا على تعظيم سننه ومتشوقا إلى مراعاة قلوب الصالحين من أمته ومتبركا بأدعيتهم فعساك أن تنال من شفاعته أو شفاعتهم فتنجو بالشفاعة إن كنت قليل البضاعة. (صفة الشفاعة) اعلم أن إذا حق دخول النار ع
14:36.english: And He (peace be upon him) said: 'Every prophet has a supplication that is answered, and I want to conceal my supplication as intercession for my community on the Day of Resurrection.'[178] And Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Pulpits of gold will be erected for the prophets, and they will sit upon them, and my pulpit will remain; I will not sit upon it, standing before my Lord, upright, fearing that I might be sent to Paradise.' And his matter is precarious in his soul. So if you are incapable of all that, then be a lover of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), eager to magnify his traditions, longing to observe the hearts of the righteous among his community, and blessed by their supplications, so perhaps you may attain from his intercession or their intercession, and thus be saved by intercession if you are of little merchandise. (Description of Intercession) Know that if entry into the Fire becomes due for groups of the believers, then Allah the Exalted, by His grace, accepts among them the intercession of the prophets and the truthful ones, indeed the intercession of the scholars and the righteous, and everyone who has with Allah the Exalted status and good dealings, then he has intercession for his family, his relatives, his friends, and his acquaintances. So be eager to acquire for yourself with them the rank of intercession, and that is by not despising any human being at all, for Allah the Exalted has concealed His friendship (Wilayah) in His servants, so perhaps the one whom your eye looks down upon is the friend (Wali) of Allah; and do not belittle any sin at all, for Allah the Exalted has concealed His anger in His sins, so perhaps the wrath (Maqt) of Allah is in it; and do not despise any obedience at all, for Allah the Exalted has concealed His pleasure in His obedience, so perhaps His pleasure is in it, even if it be a good word or a good intention or what runs in its course. And the evidences of intercession in the Quran and the reports are many: Allah the Exalted said: 'And your Lord will give you, and you will be satisfied.' {} Narrated Amr ibn al-'As: 'That the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) recited the saying of Ibrahim (upon him be peace): "My Lord, indeed they have led astray many of the people. So whoever follows me, then indeed he is of me; and whoever disobeys me, indeed You are Forgiving, Merciful." {} And the saying of Isa (upon him be peace): "If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants." {} Then he raised his hands and said: "My community, my community," then he wept. So Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: "O Jibril, go to Muhammad and ask him what makes him weep." So Jibril came to him and asked him, and he informed him, and Allah knows best about it. Then He said: "O Jibril, go to Muhammad and say to him: 'We will satisfy you concerning your community and not grieve you.'"[175])
14:36.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

14:36.arabic:
وأمره مخطر فى نفسه فإن عجزت عن ذلك كله فكن  محبا  لرسول  الله  ﭬ  حريصا  على
تعظيم سننه ومتشوقا إلى مراعاة قلوب الصالحين من أمته ومتبركا  بأدعيتهم  فعساك
أن تنال من شفاعته أو شفاعتهم فتنجو بالشفاعة إن كنت قليل البضاعة.
                                (صفة الشفاعة)
   اعلم أن إذا حق دخول النار على طوائف من المؤمنين  فإن  الله  تعالى  بفضله
يقبل فيهم شفاعة الأنبياء والصديقين بل شفاعة العلماء والصالحين وكل من له  عند
الله تعالى جاه وحسن معاملة فإن له شفاعة فى  أهله  وقرابته  وأصدقائه  ومعارفه
فكن
14:36.english: [175] Hadith of 'Amr ibn al-'As that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) recited the saying of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) - 'My Lord (Rabb), indeed they have led astray many of the people. So whoever follows me, then indeed he is of me; and whoever disobeys me, indeed You are Forgiving (Ghafur), Merciful (Rahim)' - and the saying of 'Isa (peace be upon him) - 'If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants' - then he raised his hands and then said 'My nation (Ummati), my nation (Ummati)' then wept. The hadith contains: O Jibril, go to Muhammad and say: Indeed we will please you and not grieve you regarding your nation. I said: It is not from the hadith of 'Amr ibn al-'As, but rather it is from the hadith of his son 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As as narrated by Muslim, and perhaps the mention of 'Abdullah dropped from some copyists of the Ihya'.
14:36.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

14:38.arabic: وما يخفى على الله من شيء في الأرض ولا في السماء فهذه الأخبار والآثار تدل على ما في مخالطة السلاطين من الفتن وأنواع الفساد ولكن نفصل ذلك تفضيلا فقيها تميز فيه المحظور عن المكروه والمباح فنقول الداخل على السلطان متعرض لأن يعصي الله تعالى إما بفعله أو بسكوته وإما بقوله وإما باعتقاده فلا ينفك عن أحد هذه الأمور
14:38.english: And nothing is hidden from Allah (God) in the earth nor in the heaven. These reports and traditions indicate the trials (Fitnah) and various corruptions in associating with rulers, but we will detail that with jurisprudential distinction to differentiate between the prohibited (Muharram), the disliked (Makruh), and the permissible (Mubah). We say: The one who enters upon the ruler exposes himself to disobeying Allah (God) the Exalted, either by his action or by his silence, or by his speech, or by his belief, and he does not escape from one of these matters.
14:38.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

14:42.arabic: فبينا أنت كذلك وقد انشب الخصماء فيك مخالبهم وأحكموا فى تلابيبك أيديهم وأنت مبهوت متحير من كثرتهم حتى لم يبق فى عمرك أحد عاملته على درهم أو جالسته فى مجلس إلا وقد استحق عليك مظلمة بغيبة أو خيانة أو نظر بعين استحقار وقد ضعفت عن مقاومتهم ومددت عنق الرجاء إلى سيدك ومولاك لعله يخلصك من أيديهم إذ قرع سمعك نداء الجبار جل جلاله ﴿ اليوم تجزى كل نفس بما كسبت لا ظلم اليوم ﴾ {} فعند ذلك ينخلع قلبك من الهيبة وتوقن نفسك بالبوار وتتذكر ما أنذرك الله تعالى على لسان رسوله حيث قال ﴿ ولا تحسبن الله غافلا عما يعمل
14:42.english: While you are in that state, and the adversaries have sunk their claws into you and firmly grasped your collars with their hands, and you are bewildered and perplexed by their multitude, until there remains no one in your lifetime whom you have dealt with for a dirham or sat with in a gathering except that they have a rightful claim against you due to backbiting or betrayal or a look of contempt, and you have weakened in resisting them and stretched out the neck of hope to your Master and Lord, perhaps He may deliver you from their hands, when the call of the Almighty, majestic is His glory, strikes your hearing: 'Today every soul will be recompensed for what it earned; no injustice today.' Then at that moment, your heart (Qalb) is torn out from awe, and your soul (Nafs) becomes certain of perdition, and you remember what Allah the Exalted warned you through the tongue of His Messenger where He said: 'And never think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. He only delays them for a Day when eyes will stare [in horror], As they come forth with their heads bowed, their eyes not returning to them, and their hearts (Af'idah) void. And, warn the people.' The verse. So how great is your joy today with your rinsing of people's honors and your taking of their wealth, and how great are your regrets on that Day when your Lord stands on the carpet of justice and you are addressed with the discourse of accountability, and you are bankrupt, poor, incapable, humiliated, unable to repay a right or present an excuse. Then at that moment, your good deeds in which you toiled throughout your lifetime are taken and transferred to your adversaries as compensation for their rights.
14:42.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

14:42.arabic: وهذا الغرور علاجه معرفة دلائل الكرامة والهوان إما بالبصيرة أو بالتقليد أما البصيرة فبأن يعرف وجه كون الالتفات إلى شهوات الدنيا مبعد عن الله ووجه كون التباعد عنها مقرباً إلى الله ويدرك ذلك بالإلهام في منازل العارفين والأولياء، وشرحه من جملة علوم المكاشفة ولا يليق بعلم المعاملة "وأما معرفته بطريق التقليد والتصديق" فهو أن يؤمن بكتاب الله تعالى ويصدق رسوله وقد قال تعالى "أيحسبون أن ما نمدهم به من مال وبنين نسارع لهم في الخيرات بل لا يشعرون" وقال تعالى "سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون" وقال تعالى "فتحنا ع
14:42.english: And the cure for this delusion (Ghurur) is knowing the signs of honor (Karāmah) and disgrace (Hawān) either through insight (Bāṣīrah) or through imitation (Taqleed). As for insight, it is by knowing the aspect of turning toward the desires of the world being distant from Allah and the aspect of distancing from them being close to Allah, and one perceives that through inspiration (Ilhām) in the stations (Manāzil) of the knowers (ʿĀrifīn) and the friends (Awliyāʾ), and its explanation is from the totality of the sciences of unveiling (ʿUlūm al-Mukāshafah) and is not suitable for the science of transaction (ʿIlm al-Muʿāmalah). "And as for knowing it through the way of imitation and belief (Tasdīq)," it is that one believes in the Book of Allah the Exalted and believes His messenger. And He the Exalted has said: "Do they think that what We extend to them of wealth and children, We hasten for them in good things? Rather, they do not perceive." And He the Exalted said: "We will lead them on step by step from where they do not know." And He the Exalted said: "We opened to them the doors of every thing until when they rejoiced in what they were given, We seized them suddenly, and at once they were in despair." And in the interpretation (Tafsīr) of His saying the Exalted "We will lead them on step by step from where they do not know," it is that whenever they committed a sin, We granted them a blessing to increase their delusion. And He the Exalted said: "We only give them respite that they may increase in sin." And He the Exalted said: "And never think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. He only delays them for a Day when eyes will stare [in horror]." And other than that from what has come in the Book of Allah the Exalted and the Sunnah of His messenger. So whoever believes in it is freed from this delusion, for the origin of this delusion is ignorance of Allah and His attributes, for whoever knows Him does not feel secure from His plan (Makr) nor is deluded by such false imaginings, and looks to Pharaoh and Haman and Korah and to the kings of the earth and what happened to them—how Allah was good to them initially then destroyed them utterly! So He the Exalted said: "Do you perceive of them anyone?" the verse. And Allah the Exalted has warned of His plan and leading on step by step, so He said: "So none feels secure from the plan of Allah except the losing people." And He the Exalted said: "And they planned a plan, and We planned a plan, while they perceive not." And He the Mighty and Majestic said: "And they planned, and Allah planned, and Allah is the best of planners." And He the Exalted said: "Indeed, they are planning a plan, and I am planning a plan. So allow time for the disbelievers. Deal with them gently [for a while]." So just as it is not permissible for the neglected servant (ʿAbd) to infer from the master's (Sayyid) neglect of him and enabling him of blessings upon the master's love, rather he should be cautious that it be a plan and scheme from him, even though the master did not warn him of his own plan, so that it must be so in the right of Allah the Exalted with His warning of His leading on step by step is more appropriate. Therefore, whoever feels secure from the plan of Allah is deluded, and the origin of this delusion is that he inferred from the blessings of the world that he is honored with that Bestower, and it is possible that it be a sign of disgrace, but that possibility does not agree with the...
14:42.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

14:42.arabic: فعند ذلك ينخلع قلبك من الهيبة وتوقن نفسك بالبوار وتتذكر ما أنذرك الله تعالى على لسان رسوله حيث قال ﴿ ولا تحسبن الله غافلا عما يعمل الظالمون إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار مهطعين مقنعى رءوسهم لا يرتد إليهم طرفهم وأفئدتهم هواء وأنذر الناس ﴾ {} الآية فما أشد فرحك اليوم بتمضمضك باعراض الناس ويناولك أموالهم وما أشد حسراتك فى ذلك اليوم إذا وقف ربك على بساط العدل وشوفهت بخطاب السياسة وأنت مفلس فقير عاجز مهين لا تقدر على أن ترد حقا أو تظهر عذرا فعند ذلك تؤخذ حسناتك التى تعبت فيها عمرك وتنقل إلى خصمائ
14:42.english: At that moment, your Heart (Qalb) is torn from awe and your Soul (Nafs) becomes certain of ruin, and you remember what Allah the Exalted warned you through the tongue of His Messenger where He said: 'And do not think Allah is heedless of what the wrongdoers do. He only delays them for a Day when the eyes will stare [in horror], their heads raised, their gaze not returning to them, and their hearts (Af'idah) are void. And warn the people' {} the verse. How great is your joy today with your sipping of people's honors and your taking of their wealth, and how great are your regrets on that Day when your Lord stands on the carpet of justice and you are addressed with the speech of governance while you are bankrupt, poor, incapable, humiliated, unable to return a right or show an excuse. At that time, your good deeds which you toiled for in your lifetime are taken and transferred to your adversaries in exchange for their rights.
14:42.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

14:44.arabic: يقولون ﴿ ربنا أخرنا إلى أجل قريب نجب دعوتك ونتبع الرسل فيجيبهم الله تعالى ﴿ أو لم تكونوا أقسمتم من قبل ما لكم من زوال ﴾ {} فيقولون ﴿ ربنا أخرجنا نعمل صالحا غير الذى كنا نعمل به فيجيبهم الله تعالى أو لم نعمركم ما يتذكر فيه من تذكر وجاءكم النذير فذوقوا فما للظالمين من نصير ثم يقولون ربنا غلبت علينا شقوتنا وكنا قوما ضالين ربنا أخرجنا منها فإن عدنا فإنا ظالمون فيجيبهم الله تعالى اخسئوا فيها ولا تكلمون فلا يتكلمون بعدها أبدا وذلك غاية شدة العذاب.
14:44.english: They say: 'Our Lord, delay us to a near term, we will answer Your call and follow the messengers.' Then Allah the Exalted answers them: 'Or did you not swear before that you would have no removal?' Then they say: 'Our Lord, bring us out, we will do righteous deeds other than what we used to do.' Then Allah the Exalted answers them: 'Or did We not give you long life in which whoever would remember could remember? And the warner came to you; so taste, for the wrongdoers there is no helper.' Then they say: 'Our Lord, our misfortune overcame us, and we were a people astray. Our Lord, bring us out of it; if we return, then indeed we are wrongdoers.' Then Allah the Exalted answers them: 'Be driven into it and do not speak.' So they do not speak after that ever, and that is the utmost severity of punishment.
14:44.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Book of Repentance'

14:48.arabic: يوم ترى الأرض قد زلزلت فيه زالزالها، وأخرجت الأرض أثقالها، يومئذ يصدر الناس أشتاتا ليروا أعمالهم، يوم تحمل الأرض والجبال فدكتا دكة واحدة، فيومئذ وقعت الواقعة وانشقت السماء فهى يومئذ واهية، والملك على أرجائها، ويحمل عرش ربك فوقهم يومئذ ثمانية يومئذ تعرضون لا تخفى منكم خافية، يوم تسير الجبال وترى الأرض بارزة، يوم ترج الأرض فيه رجا وتبس الجبال بسا فكانت هباء منبثا، يوم يكون الناس كالفراش المبثوث وتكون الجبال كالعهن المنفوش، يوم تذهل فيه كل مرضعة عما أرضعت وتضع كل ذات حمل حملها وترى الناس سكارى وما
14:48.english: The day you see the earth shaken with its shaking, and the earth brings forth its burdens, then the people will emerge in scattered groups to see their deeds, the day the earth and the mountains are carried and crushed with a single crushing, then the Inevitable Event (Al-Waqi'ah) has occurred and the sky is split, so it is on that day weak, and the angels are at its edges, and the Throne (Arsh) of your Lord is carried above them on that day by eight, on that day you are presented, nothing of you is hidden, the day the mountains are set in motion and you see the earth bare, the day the earth is shaken with its shaking and the mountains are scattered as dust, so they become scattered particles, the day the people will be like scattered moths and the mountains will be like carded wool, the day every nursing mother will be distracted from what she nursed and every pregnant one will deliver her burden and you see the people intoxicated while they are not intoxicated but the punishment of Allah is severe, the day the earth is changed to other than the earth and the heavens and they appear before Allah the One, the Subduer (Al-Wahid Al-Qahhar), the day the mountains are blown away with blowing, so they leave a level plain, you see in it no crookedness nor unevenness, the day you see the mountains, you think them fixed while they pass like the passing of clouds, the day the sky is split, so it becomes like red leather, then on that day no human or jinn will be asked about his sin, the day the disobedient one is prevented from speech and is not asked therein about crimes but is seized by the forelocks and the feet, the day every soul (Nafs) will find what it did of good present and what it did of evil, it wishes that between it and it were a distant span, the day every soul (Nafs) will know what it has brought and will testify to what it has sent ahead and left behind, the day the tongues are silenced and the limbs speak, the day its mention turned grey the master of the messengers when the Truthful One (Al-Siddiq), may Allah be pleased with him, said to him: I see you have turned grey, O Messenger of Allah, he said: (Surah Hud and its sisters have turned me grey[155]) and they are Al-Waqi'ah, Al-Mursalat, 'Amma Yatasa'alun, and Idha Al-Shamsu Kuwwirat. So O incapable reader, your share from your reading is that you mumble the Quran and move with it the tongue, and if you were reflecting on what you read, you would be worthy that your bitterness splits from what turned grey from it the hair of the master of the messengers, and if you are content with the movement of the tongue, you have deprived yourself of the fruit of the Quran. So the Resurrection (Al-Qiyamah) is one of what is mentioned in it, and Allah has described some of its terrors and multiplied its names so that we may stand with the multiplicity of its names on the multiplicity of its meanings, so the purpose of the multiplicity of names is not the repetition of names and titles.
14:48.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

14:48.arabic: ولا تظنن أن تلك الأرض مثل أرض الدنيا بل لا تساويها إلا فى الاسم قال تعالى: ﴿ يوم تبدل الأرض غير الأرض والسموات ﴾ {}. قال ابن عباس: يزداد فيها وينقص وتذهب أشجارها وجبالها وأوديتها وما فيها وتمد مد الأديم العكاظى أرض بيضاء مثل الفضة لم يسفك عليها دم ولم يعمل عليها خطيئة والسموات تذهب شمسها وقمرها ونجومها فانظر يا مسكين فى هول ذلك اليوم وشدته
14:48.english: And do not think that that earth is like the earth of the world, rather it does not equal it except in name. Allah the Exalted said: 'On the Day when the earth will be changed to other than the earth and the heavens' {}. Ibn Abbas said: It increases in it and decreases, and its trees, mountains, valleys, and what is in it go away, and it stretches like the stretching of the Adim Al-Akkazi, a white earth like silver upon which no blood has been spilled and upon which no sin has been committed, and the heavens lose their sun, moon, and stars. So look, O wretched one, at the terror of that day and its severity.
14:48.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Book of Repentance'

15:2.arabic: وقال رسول الله ﷺ: (إذا اجتمع أهل النار فى النار ومن شاء الله معهم من أهل القبلة قال الكفار للمسلمين ألم تكونوا مسلمين؟ قالوا: بلى فيقولون ما أغنى عنكم إسلامكم إذ أنتم معنا فى النار فيقولون كانت لنا ذنوب فأخذنا بها فيسمع الله عز وجل ما قالوا فيأمر بإخراج من كان فى النار من أهل القبلة فيخرجون فإذا رأى ذلك الكفار قالوا يا ليتنا كنا مسلمين فنخرج كما أخرجوا ثم قرأ رسول الله ﷺ ربما يود الذين كفروا لو كانوا مسلمين)
15:2.english: And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'When the people of the Fire gather in the Fire, and whomever Allah wills from the people of the Qiblah (direction of prayer) are with them, the disbelievers say to the Muslims: "Were you not Muslims?" They say: "Yes." Then they say: "What did your Islam benefit you when you are with us in the Fire?" They say: "We had sins, so we were taken by them." Allah, the Exalted and Glorified, hears what they said, so He commands the removal of whoever was in the Fire from the people of the Qiblah, and they are removed. When the disbelievers see that, they say: "Oh, would that we were Muslims, so we could be removed as they were removed." Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) recited: "Often those who disbelieved wish that they had been Muslims."
15:2.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

15:2.arabic:
ه إن رحمتى سبقت غضبى وأنا أرحم الراحمين فيخرج  من
النار مثلا أهل الجنة[260]) وقال رسول الله ﭬ: (يتجلى  الله  عز  وجل  لنا  يوم
القيامة ضاحكا فيقول أبشروا معشر المسلمين فإنه ليس  منكم  أحد  إلا  وقد  جعلت
مكانه فى النار يهوديا أو نصرانيا[261]) وقال النبي ﭬ: (يشفع  الله  تعالى  آدم
يوم القيامة من جميع ذريته فى مائة ألف ألف وعشرة آلاف ألف[262]) وقال  ﭬ:  (إن
الله عز وجل يقول يوم القيامة للمؤمنين هل أحببتم لقائى فيقولون  نعم  يا  ربنا
فيقول لم فيقولون رجونا عفوك ومغفرتك فيقول قد أوجبت لكم مغفرتي[263
15:2.english: [265] Hadith: When the people of the Fire (Ahl al-Nar) gather in the Fire, and whomever Allah wills from the people of the Qiblah (Ahl al-Qiblah) with them, the disbelievers (Kuffar) say to the Muslims: 'Were you not Muslims?' They say: 'Yes.' Then they say: 'What did your Islam (Islam) benefit you, since you are with us in the Fire?' The hadith is about the extraction of the people of the Qiblah from the Fire. Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) recited: 'Perhaps (Rubbama) those who disbelieved (Kafarū) would wish (Yawaddu) that they had been Muslims (Muslimīn).' He extracted it in al-Nasa'i in al-Kubra from the hadith of Jabir, similar to it, with a sound chain (Isnad).
15:2.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Remembrance of Death and Afterlife'

15:5.arabic: إلى يوم من أيامها. وروي أنه انصرف الناس ذات يوم من مجلس ابن عباس وبقي شاب لم يبرح فقال له ابن عباس هل لك من حاجة قال نعم أردت أن اسأل مسألة فاستحييت من الناس وأنا الآن أهابك وأجلك فقال ابن عباس إن العالم بمنزلة الوالد فما كنت أفضيت به إلى أبيك فأفض إلي به فقال أني شاب لا زوجة لي وربما خشيت العنت على نفسي فربما استمنيت بيدي فهل في ذلك معصية فأعرض عنه ابن عباس ثم قال أف وتف نكاح الأمة خير منه وهو خير من الزنا) فهذا تنبيه على أن العزب المغتلم مردد بين ثلاثة شرور أدناها نكاح الأمة وفيه إرقاق الولد و
15:5.english: To a day of its days. And it is narrated that people departed one day from the gathering of Ibn Abbas and a young man remained who did not leave, so Ibn Abbas said to him: Do you have a need? He said: Yes, I wanted to ask a question but I was shy from the people, and I now revere and honor you. So Ibn Abbas said: The scholar is in the position of a parent, so what you would have confided to your father, confide it to me. He said: I am a young man without a wife, and perhaps I fear hardship upon my soul (Nafs), so perhaps I masturbate with my hand; is there in that disobedience? So Ibn Abbas turned away from him, then said: Ugh and pah, marriage to a slave woman is better than it, and it is better than fornication. This is an indication that the unmarried person experiencing sexual arousal is wavering between three evils: the least of them is marriage to a slave woman, and in it is the enslavement of the child; and more severe than it is masturbation with the hand; and the most abominable is fornication. And Ibn Abbas did not declare permissibility in anything of it because they are two things to be avoided that one resorts to out of fear of falling into a more severe thing to be avoided, just as one resorts to consuming carrion out of fear of the destruction of the soul (Nafs), so preferring the lesser of two evils is not in the meaning of absolute permissibility nor in the meaning of absolute good, and it is not cutting off the hand that consumes from the good things, even if it is permitted when the soul (Nafs) is on the verge of destruction. So then in marriage there is merit from this aspect, but this does not encompass everyone, rather the majority. For perhaps a person's desire weakens due to old age or illness or other, so this motive disappears in his case, and what preceded regarding the matter of the child remains, for that is general except for the one who is impotent, and he is rare. And among the temperaments are those that are overcome by desire such that one woman does not protect him, so it is recommended for its possessor to increase beyond one to four. If Allah facilitates for him affection and mercy and his heart (Qalb) is at ease with them, otherwise it is recommended for him to replace. Indeed, Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, married after the death of Fatima, peace be upon her, by seven nights, and it is said that Al-Hasan ibn Ali was much-marrying until he married more than two hundred women, and he would sometimes contract marriage with four at one time and sometimes divorce four at one time and replace them. And the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to Al-Hasan: You resemble my character and my creation. And the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Al-Hasan is from me and Al-Husayn is from Ali. So he said: The abundance of his marriage is one of the things by which he resembles the creation of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. And Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah married eighty women, and among the Companions were those who had three and four, and those who had two are uncountable. And whenever the motive is known, the treatment should be according to the ailment, so the intent is to calm the soul (Nafs), so let him look at it in abundance and scarcity. The third benefit: refreshing the soul (Nafs) and comforting it with companionship, looking, and play, as a relief for the heart (Qalb) and strengthening it for worship, for the soul (Nafs) is bored and it is averse from the truth because it is contrary to its nature, so if it were burdened
15:5.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

15:9.arabic: فكذلك فلما تجلو سنة وشهر ويوم  عن  جذبه  من  الجذبات  ونفحة  من  النفحات فينبغي ان يكون العبد قد طهر القلب عن  حشيش  الشهوات  وبذر  فيه  بذر  الارادة والاخلاص وعرضه لمهاب رياح الرحمة وكما يقوى انتظار الأمطار  في  اوقات  الربيع وعند ظهور الغيم فيقوى انتظار تلك النفحات  في  الأوقات  الشريفة  وعند  اجتماع الهمم وتساعد القلوب كما في يوم  عرفة  ويوم  الجمعة  وأيام  رمضان  فان  الهمم والأنفاس اسباب بحكم تقدير الله تعالى لاستدرار رحمته حتى  تستدر  بها  الامطار في اوقات الاستسقاء وهي لا ستدراك امطار الم
15:9.english: Similarly, when a year, month, or day passes without a pull from the pulls or a breeze from the breezes, the servant should have purified the Heart (Qalb) from the weeds of desires and sown in it the seed of will and sincerity, exposing it to the blowing winds of mercy. Just as the expectation of rain strengthens during the times of spring and when clouds appear, so does the expectation of those breezes strengthen during the noble times and when intentions gather and hearts assist each other, as on the Day of Arafah, Friday, and the days of Ramadan. For intentions and breaths are causes by the decree of Allah the Exalted to draw forth His mercy, just as rain is drawn forth during times of seeking rain. They are more suitable for drawing forth the rains of unveilings and subtleties of knowledges from the treasuries of the Dominion than for drawing forth droplets of water and pulling clouds from the corners of mountains and seas. Rather, the states and unveilings are present with you in your heart, but you are preoccupied from them by your attachments and desires, so that becomes a veil between you and them. You only need to break the desire and lift the veil, so the lights of knowledges shine from the inner Heart (Qalb). Bringing forth water from the earth by digging canals is easier and closer than reaching it from a distant place lower than it. And because it is present in the heart and forgotten due to preoccupation with it, Allah the Exalted named all the knowledges of faith Remembrance (Dhikr), so He said: 'Indeed, it is We who sent down the Remembrance (Dhikr), and indeed, We will be its guardian.' And He said: 'And that those of understanding may remember.' And He said: 'And We have certainly made the Quran easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?' This is the treatment for patience against whisperings and distractions, and it is the final degrees of patience. Indeed, patience against all attachments precedes patience against thoughts.
15:9.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

15:9.arabic: ومن أسباب حفظه في القلوب والمصاحف استدامة تلاوته والمواظبة على دراسته مع القيام بآدابه وشروطه والمحافظة على ما فيه من الأعمال الباطنة والآداب الظاهرة وذلك لا بد من بيانه وتفصيله وتنكشف مقاصده في أربعة أبواب. الباب الأول: في فضل القرآن وأهله. الباب الثاني: في آداب التلاوة في الظاهر. الباب الثالث: في الأعمال الباطنة عند التلاوة. الباب الرابع: في فهم القرآن وتفسيره بالرأي وغيره.
15:9.english: And among the means of its preservation in the hearts (Qulub) and the codices (Mushaf) is the continuity of its recitation (Tilawah) and the persistence in its study along with the observance of its manners (Adab) and conditions (Shurut) and the safeguarding of what is in it from the inward actions (A'mal al-Batinah) and the outward manners (Adab al-Zahirah). And that must be explained and detailed, and its purposes are revealed in four chapters. Chapter One: On the excellence of the Quran and its people. Chapter Two: On the manners of recitation in the outward. Chapter Three: On the inward actions during recitation. Chapter Four: On understanding the Quran and its interpretation by opinion and other.
15:9.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

15:29.arabic: وأما ما لا يجوز أن يسطر في الكتب من المناسبة الخاصة التي اختص بها الآدمي فهي التي يومئ إليها قوله تعالى: " ويسألونك عن الروح قل الروح من أمر ربي " إذ بين أنه أمر رباني خارج عن حد عقول الخلق. وأوضح من ذلك قوله تعالى: " فإذا سويته ونفخت فيه من روحي" ولذلك أسجد له ملائكته، ويشير إليه قوله تعالى: " إنا جعلنا خليفة في الأرض " إذ لم يستحق آدم خلافة الله تعالى إلا بتلك المناسبة وإليه يرمز قوله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم: " إن الله خلق آدم على صورته" حتى ظن القاصرون أن لا صورة إلا الصورة الظاهرة المدركة با
15:29.english: As for what is not permissible to be recorded in books from the special suitability that the human being (al-Ādamī) has been exclusively granted, it is that which is alluded to by His saying, the Exalted: 'And they ask you about the Spirit (al-Rūḥ). Say: The Spirit is from the command of my Lord (amr rabbī),' since He made clear that it is a lordly command (amr rabbānī) beyond the limit of the intellects of creation. And clearer than that is His saying, the Exalted: 'So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him from My Spirit (rūḥī),' and for that reason He made His angels prostrate to him. And it is indicated by His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, We have made a vicegerent (khalīfah) on the earth,' since Adam did not deserve the vicegerency (khilāfah) of Allah, the Exalted, except by that suitability. And to it points His saying, peace and blessings be upon him and his family: 'Indeed, Allah created Adam upon His image (ṣūratih),' until the deficient ones thought that there is no image (ṣūrah) except the apparent image perceived by the senses, so they likened, corporealized, and formed images. Exalted is Allah, Lord of the worlds, above what the ignorant say, a great exaltation.
15:29.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

15:29.arabic: ألم أخلقك بيدى ونفخت فيك من روحى وأسجدت لك ملائكتى فعصيت أمرى ونسيت عهدى وتعرضت لسخطى
15:29.english: Did I not create you with My Hand and blow into you from My Spirit (Ruh) and make My angels prostrate to you, then you disobeyed My command and forgot My covenant and exposed yourself to My wrath?
15:29.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

15:36.arabic: وقال سفيان بن عيينة لا يمنعن أحدكم من الدعاء ما يعلم من نفسه فإن الله عز وجل أجاب دعاء شر الخلق إبليس لعنه الله إذ قال: ﴿ رب فانظرني إلى يوم يبعثون قال إنك من المنظرين ﴾ {}.
15:36.english: And Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: Let not what one knows about himself prevent anyone from supplication, for Allah the Exalted answered the supplication of the worst of creation, Iblis (may Allah curse him), when he said: 'My Lord, then grant me respite until the Day they are resurrected. He said: Indeed, you are of those granted respite.'
15:36.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

15:40.arabic: فقال لأنك غضبت أول مرة لله وكانت نيتك الآخرة فسخرنى الله لك وهذه المرة غضبت لنفسك وللدنيا فصرعتك هذه الحكايات تصديق قوله تعالى إلا عبادك منهم المخلصين إذ لا يتخلص العبد من الشيطان إلا بالإخلاص ولذلك كان معروف الكرخى رحمه الله تعالى يضرب نفسه ويقول يا نفس أخلصى تتخلصى وقال يعقوب المكفوف المخلص من يكتم حسناته كما يكتم سيئاته وقال سليمان طوبى لمن صحت له خطوة واحدة لا يريد بها إلا الله تعالى وكتب عمر بن الخطاب رضى الله تعالى عنه إلى أبى موسى الأشعرى من خلصت نيته كفاه الله تعالى ما بينه وبين الناس وك
15:40.english: He said: 'Because you were angry the first time for Allah and your intention was for the Hereafter, so Allah subjugated me to you. And this time you were angry for your soul (Nafs) and for the worldly life, so I overpowered you.' These stories confirm His saying, the Exalted: 'Except Your servants among them, the purified ones (Al-Mukhlaseen).' For indeed the servant (Al-Abd) does not become purified (Yatakhalasu) from Satan except through sincerity (Al-Ikhlas). And for that reason, Ma'ruf Al-Karkhi, may Allah have mercy on him, would strike himself and say: 'O soul (Nafs), be sincere (Ikhlas) so you may become purified (Tatakhalasu).' And Ya'qub Al-Makfuf said: 'The sincere one (Al-Mukhlis) is he who conceals his good deeds just as he conceals his bad deeds.' And Sulaiman said: 'Blessed is he for whom a single step is sound, not desiring by it except Allah, the Exalted.'
