And Umar ibn Al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari: 'Whoever's intention (Niyyah) becomes sincere (Khalasat), Allah suffices him for what is between him and the people.' And some of the friends of Allah (Al-Awliya) wrote to his brother: 'Make sincere (Akhlas) the intention (Niyyah) in your deeds, and a little of the action will suffice you.' And Ayyub Al-Sakhtiyani said: 'Purifying (Takhlees) the intentions (Al-Niyyat) upon the doers is more severe upon them than all the actions.' And Mutarrif used to say: 'Whoever becomes pure (Safa), it becomes pure (Safa) for him, and whoever mixes (Khalata), it becomes mixed (Khalata) upon him.' And one of them was seen in a dream and it was said to him: 'How did you find your deeds?' He said: 'Everything I did for Allah, I found it, even a pomegranate seed I picked up from the road, and even a cat that died for us, I saw it in the scale of good deeds (Al-Hasanat). And there was a thread of silk in my cap, and I saw it in the scale of bad deeds (Al-Sayyi'at). And a donkey of mine had died, its value one hundred dinars, and I did not see any reward for it. So I said: "The death of a cat is in the scale of good deeds, and the death of a donkey is not in it." It was said to me: "Indeed, it has been directed where you sent it, for when it was said to you: 'It has died,' you said: 'May Allah curse it,' so your reward in it became void. And if you had said: 'In the path of Allah,' you would have found it in your good deeds."'
15:40.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

15:40.arabic: فمعرفة حقيقة الإخلاص والعمل به بحر عميق يغرق فيه الجميع إلا الشاذ النادر والفرد الفذوهو المستثنى في قوله تعالى إلا عبادك منهم المخلصين فليكن العبد شديد التفقد والمراقبة لهذه الدقائق وإلا التحق بأتباع الشياطين وهو لا يشعر.
15:40.english: For knowing the reality of Sincerity (Ikhlas) and acting upon it is a deep sea in which all drown except the rare exceptional and unique individual—he is the one excepted in His saying, the Exalted: 'Except Your servants from among them, the purified ones (al-Mukhlaseen).' So let the servant (al-Abd) be intensely vigilant and watchful of these subtleties, otherwise he will join the followers of the devils (Shayateen) without realizing.
15:40.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

15:42.arabic: ولا يمكن فتحها بعد ذلك إلا بتخلية القلب عن قوت الشيطان وهو الهوى والشهوات وعمارته بذكر الله تعالى الذي هو مطرح أثر الملائكة وقال جابر بن عبيدة العدوي شكوت إلى العلاء بن زياد ما أجد في صدري من الوسوسة فقال إنما مثل ذلك مثل البيت الذي يمر به اللصوص فإن كان فيه شيء عالجوه وإلا مضوا وتركوه يعني أن القلب الخالي عن الهوى لا يدخله الشيطان ولذلك قال الله تعالى إن عبادي ليس لك عليهم سلطان فكل من اتبع الهوى فهو عبد الهوى لا عبد الله ولذلك سلط الله عليه الشيطان وقال تعالى أفرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه وهو إشارة
15:42.english: And it is not possible to open it after that except by emptying the Heart (Qalb) from the power of Satan, which is the Passion (Hawa) and the Desires (Shahawat), and building it with the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah the Exalted, which is the place of the effect of the angels. And Jabir ibn 'Abidah al-'Adawi said: I complained to al-'Ala' ibn Ziyad about what I find in my chest of the Whisperings (Waswasah). He said: Indeed, the likeness of that is like a house that thieves pass by; if there is something in it, they treat it, otherwise they pass and leave it. Meaning that the Heart (Qalb) empty from Passion (Hawa) does not enter it Satan. And for that reason, Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, My servants (Ibad) - you have no authority over them, except those who follow you of the deviators.' So everyone who follows the Passion (Hawa) is a servant of the Passion (Hawa), not a servant of Allah. And for that reason, Allah gave authority over him to Satan. And He the Exalted said: 'Have you seen the one who takes as his god his [own] desire?' And it is an indication that whoever makes his Passion (Hawa) his god and his worshipped one, he is a servant of the Passion (Hawa), not a servant of Allah. And for that reason, 'Amr ibn al-'As said to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: O Messenger of Allah, Satan comes between me and my prayer and my recitation. He said: That is a Satan called Khanzab; when you sense him, seek refuge in Allah from him and spit to your left three times. He said: So I did that, and Allah removed him from me.
15:42.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

15:42.arabic: وإنما تحوم الشياطين على القلوب إذا كانت مشحونة بالصفات المذمومة فإنها مرعى الشيطان وجنده ومن خلص قلبه من تلك الصفات وصفاه لم يطف الشيطان حول قلبه وإليه الاشارة بقوله تعالىإلا عبادك منهم المخلصين وبقوله تعالى إن عبادي ليس لك عليهم سلطان والسماع سبب لصفاء القلب وهو شبكة للحق بواسطة الصفاء
15:42.english: And indeed, the devils only hover around the hearts (Qulub) when they are filled with blameworthy attributes (Sifat), for they are the pasture of the devil and his soldiers. And whoever purifies his heart (Qalb) from those attributes and cleanses it, the devil does not circle around his heart (Qalb). And to this is the indication by His saying, the Exalted: 'Except Your servants among them, the purified ones (Al-Mukhlaseen)' and by His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, My servants (Ibad) - you have no authority over them (Sultan).' And listening (Sama') is a cause for the purity of the heart (Qalb), and it is a net for the truth (Haqq) through the medium of purity (Safa').
15:42.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

15:43.arabic: ومن لم يسبق له من الله الحسنى بعد عن سماع كلام الله تعالى وكلام رسول الله ﭬ وكلام العلماء فاذا لم يسمع لم يعلم واذا لم يعلم لم يخف واذا لم يخف لم يترك الركون الى الدنيا واذا لم يترك الركون الى الدنيا بقى في حزب الشيطان وان جهنم لموعدهم اجمعين، فإذا عرفت هذا تعجبت من قوم يقادون الى الجنة بالسلاسل فما من احد الا وهو مقود الى الجنة بسلاسل الاسباب وهو تسليط العلم والخوف عليه وما من مخذول الا وهو مقود الى النار بالسلاسل وهو تسليط الغفلة والأمن والغرور عليه فالمتقون يساقون الى الجنة قهرا والمجرمون يقا
15:43.english: And whoever has not been preceded for him from Allah the good fortune distances himself from hearing the speech of Allah the Exalted and the speech of His Messenger (peace be upon him) and the speech of the scholars. So if he does not hear, he does not know; and if he does not know, he does not fear; and if he does not fear, he does not abandon the reliance upon the worldly life; and if he does not abandon the reliance upon the worldly life, he remains in the party of Satan, and indeed Hellfire is their promised meeting place all together. So if you comprehend this, you will be amazed at a people who are led to Paradise by chains, for there is no one except that he is led to Paradise by the chains of causes, which is the imposition of knowledge and fear upon him; and there is no forsaken one except that he is led to the Fire by chains, which is the imposition of heedlessness, security, and delusion upon him. So the God-fearing are driven to Paradise by compulsion, and the criminals are led to the Fire by compulsion, and there is no compeller except Allah the One, the Subduer, and there is no powerful one except the Sovereign, the Compeller.
15:43.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

15:43.arabic: [118] حديث ميمون بن مهران لما نزلت هذه الآية ﴿ وإن جهنم لموعدهم أجمعين ﴾ صاح سلمان الفارسي لم أقف له على أصل.
15:43.english: [118] The narration of Maymun ibn Mahran: When this verse descended: "And indeed, Hell is their appointment all together," Salman al-Farsi cried out. I have not found a basis for it.
15:43.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Fear and Hope'

15:43.arabic: وقال ميمون بن مهران لما نزلت هذه الآية ﴿ وإن جهنم لموعدهم أجمعين ﴾{} صاح سلمان الفارسي ووضع يده على رأسه وخرج هاربا ثلاثة أيام لا يقدرون عليه
15:43.english: And Maimun bin Mahran said: When this verse descended: 'And indeed, Hell is their promised place all together' (Quran 15:43), Salman Al-Farsi cried out and placed his hand on his head and went out fleeing for three days, and they could not reach him.
15:43.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Fear and Hope'

15:44.arabic: ثم ليستأنف لها وصية في أعضائه السبعة وهي العين والأذن واللسان والبطن والفرج واليد والرجل وتسليمها إليها فإنها رعايا خادمة لنفسه في هذه التجارة وبها تتم أعمال هذه التجارة وإن لجهنم سبعة أبواب لكل باب منهم جزء مقسوم وإنما تتعين تلك الأبواب لمن عصى الله تعالى بهذه الأعضاء فيوصيها بحفظها عن معاصيها
15:44.english: Then he renews for it (the Soul/Nafs) an admonition regarding its seven members, which are the eye, the ear, the tongue, the stomach, the private parts, the hand, and the foot, and he delivers them to it, for they are subjects serving his Soul (Nafs) in this trade, and through them the works of this trade are completed. And indeed, for Hell (Jahannam) there are seven gates; for every gate among them is an apportioned part. And those gates are specifically designated for whoever disobeys Allah the Exalted with these members, so he admonishes it to guard them from their sins.
15:44.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

15:47.arabic: فإن فرض كثرة في العارفين لم يكونوا متحاسدين بل كانوا كما قال فيهم رب العالمين "ونزعنا ما في صدورهم من غل إخواننا على سرر متقابلين" فهذا حالهم وهم بعد في الدنيا، فماذا يظن بهم عند انكشاف الغطاء، أمشاهدة المحبوب في العقبى؟ فإذن لا يتصور أن يكون في الجنة محاسدة ولا أن يكون بين أهل الدنيا في الجنة محاسدة، لأن الجنة لا مضايقة فيها ولا مزاحمة، ولا تنال إلا بمعرفة الله تعالى التي لا مزاحمة فيها في الدنيا أيضاً، فأهل الجنة بالضرورة برءاء من الحسد في الدنيا والآخرة جميعاً، بل الحسد من صفات المبعدين عن سع
15:47.english: For if there is an abundance of the Knowers (Al-Arifin), they would not be envious of each other; rather, they would be as their Lord, the Lord of the Worlds, said about them: 'And We will remove whatever is in their chests of rancor (Ghill) - brothers, on thrones facing each other.' This is their state while they are still in the worldly life (Al-Dunya), so what is presumed about them when the covering is unveiled, or witnessing the Beloved (Al-Mahbub) in the Hereafter (Al-Uqba)? Therefore, it is inconceivable that there would be envy in Paradise (Al-Jannah), nor that there would be envy among the people of the worldly life in Paradise, because Paradise has no constriction in it nor competition, and it is not attained except by the knowledge (Ma'rifah) of Allah, the Exalted, in which there is no competition in the worldly life also. Thus, the people of Paradise are necessarily free from envy (Al-Hasad) in the worldly life and the Hereafter altogether. Rather, envy is from the attributes of those distanced from the expanse of the highest places (Aliyyin) to the narrowness of the lowest depths (Sijjin). And for that reason, the accursed Satan (Al-Shaytan Al-La'in) was branded with it, and it was mentioned from his attributes that he envied Adam, peace be upon him, for what he was specifically chosen with from selection, and when he was called to prostrate, he became arrogant and refused, and he rebelled and disobeyed.
15:47.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

15:75.arabic: وقال بعض السلف ظن المؤمن كهانة وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أتقوا فراسة المؤمن فإنه ينظر بنور الله تعالى وإليه يشير قوله تعالى إن في ذلك لآيات للمتوسمين وقوله تعالى قد بينا الآيات لقوم يوقنون وروى الحسن عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال العلم علمان فعلم باطن في القلب فذلك هو العلم النافع
15:75.english: And some of the predecessors said: 'The believer's intuition is like divination.' And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Fear the insight (Firasa) of the believer, for he sees with the Light (Nur) of Allah the Exalted.' And to this points His saying the Exalted: 'Indeed in that are signs for those who discern (Al-Mutawassimin).' And His saying the Exalted: 'We have made clear the signs for a people who are certain (Yaqinun).' And Al-Hasan narrated from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) that he said: 'Knowledge is of two types: knowledge that is internal (Batin) in the Heart (Qalb), and that is the beneficial knowledge.'
15:75.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

15:92.arabic: وعند ذلك يصدق الله تعالى قوله: ﴿ فلنسألن الذين أرسل إليهم ولنسألن المرسلين فلنقصن عليهم بعلم وما كنا غائبين ﴾ {} وقوله: ﴿ فوربك لنسألنهم أجمعين عما كانوا يعملون ﴾ {} فيبدأ سبحانه بالأنبياء ﴿ يوم يجمع الله الرسل فيقول ماذا أجبتم قالوا لا علم لنا إنك أنت علام الغيوب ﴾ {} فيا لشدة يوم تذهل فيه عقول الأنبياء وتنمحى علومهم من شدة الهيبة إذ يقال لهم ما أجبتم وقد أرسلتم إلى الخلائق وكانوا قد علموا فتدهش عقولهم فلا يدرون بماذا يجيبون فيقولون من شدة الهيبة لا علم لنا إنك أنت علام الغيوب وهم فى ذلك الوقت
15:92.english: And at that time, Allah the Exalted will fulfill His saying: 'So We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent, and We will surely question the messengers. Then We will surely relate to them with knowledge, and We were not absent.' (Quran 7:6-7) and His saying: 'So by your Lord, We will surely question them all about what they used to do.' (Quran 15:92-93) Then He the Exalted begins with the prophets: 'On the Day when Allah will assemble the messengers and say, "What was the response you received?" They will say, "We have no knowledge. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen."' (Quran 5:109) Oh, the severity of a day in which the intellects (Aql) of the prophets are bewildered and their knowledges (Ilm) are erased from the intensity of the awe (Hiba) when it is said to them, 'What was the response you received?' And they had been sent to the creation and they had known, so their intellects (Aql) are stunned, and they do not know with what to answer, so they say from the intensity of the awe (Hiba), 'We have no knowledge. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen (Alim al-Ghuyub).' And they at that time are truthful, for their intellects (Aql) have flown away and their knowledges (Ilm) have been erased until Allah the Exalted strengthens them.
15:92.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Book of Repentance'

15:96.arabic: وقال ﭬ "يخرج من النار عنق له أذنان تسمعان وعينان تبصران ولسان ينطق يقول: وكلت بثلاثة: بكل جبار عنيد وبكل من دعا مع الله إلهاً آخر وبالمصورين"[7]
15:96.english: And He (the Prophet) said: 'There will emerge from the Fire a neck having two ears that hear and two eyes that see and a tongue that speaks, saying: I have been entrusted with three: with every arrogant obstinate one and with everyone who calls with Allah another god (ilah) and with the image-makers.'
15:96.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

15:97.arabic: وقال تعالى: ﴿ واصبر على ما يقولون واهجرهم هجرا جميلا ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ ولقد نعلم أنك يضيق صدرك بما يقولون فسبح بحمد ربك ﴾ {} الآية وقال تعالى: ﴿ ولتسمعن من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم ومن الذين أشركوا أذى كثيرا وإن تصبروا وتتقوا فإن ذلك من عزم الأمور ﴾ {} أي تصبروا عن المكأفاة ولذلك مدح الله تعالى العافين عن حقوقهم في القصاص وغيره فقال تعالى: ﴿ وإن عاقبتم فعاقبوا بمثل ما عوقبتم به ولئن صبرتم لهو خير الصابرين ﴾ {}.
15:97.english: And He (Allah) said: 'And be patient (اصبر) over what they say and leave them with a beautiful leaving (هجرا جميلا).' And He (Allah) said: 'And We certainly know that your chest (صدرك) tightens (يضيق) with what they say, so glorify (سبح) with the praise (بحمد) of your Lord (ربك).' The verse. And He (Allah) said: 'And you will certainly hear from those who were given the Book before you and from those who associate partners (أشركوا) much harm, and if you are patient (تصبروا) and are conscious (وتتقوا), then indeed that is from the matters of determination (عزم الأمور).' That is, be patient (تصبروا) from retaliation (المكأفاة). And for that reason, Allah praised those who pardon (العافين) from their rights in retaliation (القصاص) and other than it, so He (Allah) said: 'And if you punish (عاقبتم), then punish (فعاقبوا) with the like of that with which you were punished (عوقبتم), and if you are patient (صبرتم), it is better for the patient ones (الصابرين).'
15:97.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

15:98.arabic: فإن قلت فقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم ما أوحي إلي أن أجمع المال وكن من التاجرين ولكن أوحي إلي أن سبح بحمد ربك وكن من الساجدين واعبد ربك حتى يأتيك اليقين حديث ما أوحي إلي أن اجمع المال وكن من التاجرين ولكن أوحي إلي أن سبح بحمد ربك وكن من الساجدين رواه ابن مردويه في التفسير من حديث ابن مسعود بسند فيه لين وقيل لسلمان الفارسي أوصنا فقال من استطاع منكم أن يموت حاجا أو غازيا أو عامرا لمسجد ربه فليفعل ولا يموتن تاجرا ولا خائنا فالجواب أن وجه الجمع بين هذه الأخبار تفصيل الأحوال فنقول لسنا نقول التجارة أفضل
15:98.english: If you say: Indeed, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'It was not revealed to me to gather wealth and be among the traders, but it was revealed to me: "So glorify with the praise of your Lord and be among those who prostrate (in worship)" (Quran 15:98), and worship your Lord until certainty comes to you.' The hadith: 'It was not revealed to me to gather wealth and be among the traders, but it was revealed to me: "So glorify with the praise of your Lord and be among those who prostrate (in worship)" (Quran 15:98).' Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh in the Tafsir from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud with a chain containing weakness. And it was said to Salman al-Farsi: 'Advise us.' He said: 'Whoever among you is able to die as a pilgrim, or a warrior, or a builder of his Lord's mosque, let him do so, and do not die as a trader or a betrayer.' The answer is that the way to reconcile these reports is by detailing the circumstances. We say: We do not say that trade is absolutely better than everything, but trade is either sought for sufficiency, or wealth, or increase beyond sufficiency. If increase beyond sufficiency is sought from it for amassing and hoarding wealth, not to spend on good deeds and charities, then it is blameworthy because it is turning towards the worldly life (Dunya), the love of which is the head of every sin. If along with that he is oppressive and treacherous, then it is oppression and wickedness. This is what Salman meant by his saying: 'Do not die as a trader or a betrayer,' and by 'trader' he meant the seeker of increase. As for if it is sought for sufficiency for himself and his children, and he is able to provide for them through begging, then trade as abstention from begging is better. And if he does not need to beg and is given without begging, then earning is better because he is only given because he is a beggar by the tongue of his state and a proclaimer among people of his poverty, so abstention and concealment are more complete than idleness.
15:98.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Earning'

16:8.arabic: ووجود الأشياء كلها نور من أنوار ذاته تعالى وتقدس إذ قوام وجود الأشياء بذاته القيوم بنفسه كما أن قوام نور الأجسام بنور الشمس المضيئة بنفسها ومهما انكشف بعض الشمس فقد جرت العادة بأن يوضع طشت ماء حتى ترى الشمس فيه ويمكن النظر إليها فيكون الماء واسطة يغض قليلا من نور الشمس حتى يطاق النظر إليها فكذلك الأفعال واسطة نشاهد فيها صفات الفاعل ولا نبهر بأنوار الذات بعد أن تباعدنا عنها بواسطة الأفعال فهذا سر قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم تفكروا في خلق الله ولا تتفكروا في ذات الله تعالى. بيان كيفية التفكر في خلق ال
16:8.english: And the existence of all things is a light from the lights of His Essence, Exalted and Holy, since the subsistence of the existence of things is by His Self-Subsisting Essence, just as the subsistence of the light of bodies is by the light of the sun that illuminates by itself. And whenever some of the sun is uncovered, it has become customary to place a basin of water so that the sun may be seen in it and it becomes possible to look at it, so the water becomes a medium that slightly reduces the light of the sun until it can be endured to look at. Likewise, actions are a medium through which we witness the attributes of the Actor, and we are not dazzled by the lights of the Essence after we have distanced ourselves from it through the medium of actions. This is the secret of His saying, peace be upon him: 'Reflect upon the creation of Allah and do not reflect upon the Essence of Allah, Exalted.' Explanation of the manner of reflecting upon the creation of Allah, Exalted. Know that everything in existence other than Allah, Exalted, is the action and creation of Allah, and every atom of the atoms, whether substance, accident, attribute, or described thing, contains wonders and marvels through which the wisdom, power, majesty, and greatness of Allah appear. Enumerating that is not possible, for if the sea were ink for that, the sea would be exhausted before a tenth of its tenth is exhausted. But we point to a summary of it so that it may serve as an example for what is beyond it. So we say: The created existents are divided into that whose origin is not known, so we cannot reflect upon it, and how many existents are there that we do not know, as Allah, Exalted, said: 'And He creates what you do not know. Glory be to Him who created all pairs from what the earth grows and from themselves and from what they do not know.' And He said: 'And We will develop you in what you do not know.' And into that whose origin and summary is known but whose details are not known, so we can reflect upon its details. And it is divided into what we perceive by the sense of sight and into what we do not perceive by sight. As for what we do not perceive by sight, such as the angels, jinn, devils, the Throne (Al-'Arsh), the Footstool (Al-Kursi), and other than that, the field of thought in these things is narrow and obscure, so let us turn to what is closer to comprehension, which is what is perceived by the sense of sight, and that is the seven heavens and the earth and what is between them. So the heavens are observed with their stars, sun, moon, movement, and rotation in their rising and setting; and the earth is observed with what is in it of its mountains, minerals, rivers, seas, animals, and plants; and what is between the sky and the earth, which is the atmosphere, is perceived with its clouds, rains, snows, thunder, lightning, thunderbolts, meteors, and stormy winds. These are the observable genera from the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and every genus of them divides into species, and every species divides into categories, and every category branches into varieties, and there is no end to the branching and division of that in the differences of its attributes, forms, and apparent and hidden meanings, and all of that is a field for thought. So not an atom moves in the heavens...
16:8.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Contemplation'

16:9.arabic: وَعَلَى اللَّهِ قَصْدُ السَّبِيلِ وَمِنْهَا جَائِرٌ ۚ وَلَوْ شَاءَ لَهَدَاكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ وقال على كرم الله وجهه الهوى شريك العمى ومن التوفيق التوقف عند الحيرة ونعم طارد الهم اليقين وعاقبة الكذب الندم وفي الصدق السلامة رب بعيد أقرب من قريب وغريب من لم يكن له حبيب والصديق من صدق غيبه ولا يعدمك من حبيب سوء ظن نعم الخلق التكرم والحياء سبب إلى كل جميل وأوثق العرا التقوى واوثق سبب أخذت به سبب بينك وبين الله تعالى إنما لك من دنياك ما أصلحت به مثواك والرزق رزقان رزق تطلبه ورزق يطلبك فان لم تأته أتاك و
16:9.english: And upon Allah is the straightening of the path, and among them are deviant ones. And if He had willed, He would have guided you all. And Ali (may Allah honor his face) said: Desire (Hawa) is a partner of blindness. And from success (Tawfiq) is stopping at perplexity. And an excellent dispeller of worry is certainty (Yaqin). And the consequence of lying is regret. And in truthfulness is safety. A distant lord is closer than a close one, and a stranger is one who has no beloved. And the truthful friend (Sadiq) is one who is truthful in his absence. And do not let a beloved be lacking in you due to bad suspicion. An excellent character is generosity (Takrim). And modesty (Haya) is a means to every beautiful thing. And the most secure bond is piety (Taqwa). And the most secure means you have taken is a means between you and Allah. Indeed, what you have from your worldly life is what you have rectified with your abode. And provision (Rizq) is of two types: provision you seek and provision that seeks you. So if you do not come to it, it will come to you. And if you are distressed over what has befallen you from what is in your hands, then do not be distressed over what has not reached you. And infer about what has not been from what has been, for matters are similar. And a person is pleased by attaining what would not have escaped him and is displeased by missing what he would not have attained. So what reaches you from your worldly life, do not excessively rejoice in it, and what escapes you from it, do not let your soul (Nafs) follow it with regret. And let your joy be in what you have sent forth and your regret over what you have left behind. And your occupation be for your hereafter and your concern in what is after death. And our purpose in transmitting these words is his saying: And from success (Tawfiq) is stopping at perplexity.
16:9.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

16:12.arabic: والعالم الراسخ هو الذي يطلع على أن الشمس والقمر والنجوم مسخرات بأمره سبحانه وتعالى ومثال نظر الضعيف إلى حصول ضوء الشمس عقيب طلوع الشمس مثال النملة لو خلق لها عقل وكانت على سطح قرطاس وهي تنظر إلى سواد الخط يتجدد فتعتقد أنه فعل القلم ولا تترقى في نظرها إلى مشاهدة الأصابع ثم منها إلى اليد ثم منها إلى الإرادة المحركة اليد ثم منها إلى الكاتب القادر المريد ثم منه إلى خالق اليد والقدرة والإرادة فأكثر نظر الخلق مقصور على الأسباب القريبة السافلة مقطوع من الترقي إلى مسبب الأسباب فهذا أحد أسباب النهي عن ال
16:12.english: And the firmly established scholar (Alim) is the one who perceives that the sun, the moon, and the stars are subjugated by His command, glorified and exalted is He. The example of the weak person's view regarding the occurrence of sunlight following the rising of the sun is like an ant, if intellect were created for it and it were on the surface of a paper, and it looks at the blackness of the line being renewed, so it believes it is the action of the pen, and it does not ascend in its view to witnessing the fingers, then from them to the hand, then from them to the will (Iradah) that moves the hand, then from them to the writer who is capable (Qadir) and willing (Murid), then from him to the creator of the hand, the capability (Qudrah), and the will (Iradah). So most of the view of creation is restricted to the proximate, lowly causes, cut off from ascending to the causer of causes. This is one of the reasons for the prohibition regarding the stars.
16:12.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

16:18.arabic: وإذا كانت تلك الأسباب طويلة لا يحتمل مثل هذا الكتاب استقصاءها فلنذكر منها أنموذجا ليعلم به معنى قوله تعالى: ﴿ وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها ﴾ وبالله التوفيق. (بيان وجه الأنموذج في كثرة نعم الله تعالى وتسلسلها وخروجها عن الحصر والإحصاء) اعلم أنا جمعنا النعم في ستة عشر ضربا وجعلنا صحة البدن نعمة من النعم الواقعة في الرتبة المتأخرة فهذه النعمة الواحدة لو أردنا أن نستقصى الأسباب التي بها تمت هذه النعمة لم نقدر عليها ولكن الأكل أحد أسباب الصحة فلنذكر نبذة من جملة الأسباب التي بها تتم نعمة الأكل فلا ي
16:18.english: And since those causes are lengthy, a book like this cannot bear their exhaustive enumeration, so let us mention from them a model to understand by it the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: 'And if you count the blessings of Allah, you cannot enumerate them' (Quran 16:18). And by Allah is success. (Explanation of the aspect of the model in the abundance of Allah's blessings and their sequence and their departure from enumeration and counting) Know that we have gathered the blessings into sixteen types, and we made the health of the body a blessing from the blessings occurring in the later rank. So this single blessing, if we wanted to exhaustively enumerate the causes by which this blessing is completed, we would not be able to do so. But eating is one of the causes of health, so let us mention a portion from the totality of causes by which the blessing of eating is completed. It is not hidden that eating is an action, and every action of this type is a movement, and every movement necessarily has a moving body that is its instrument, and necessarily has a power (Qudrah) over the movement, and necessarily has a will (Iradah) for the movement, and necessarily has knowledge (Ilm) of what is intended and perception (Idrak) of it. And eating necessarily has food (Mā'kul), and the food necessarily has an origin from which it is obtained, and necessarily has a maker (Sāni') who prepares it. So let us mention the causes of perception, then the causes of wills, then the causes of power, then the causes of food, by way of allusion, not by way of exhaustive enumeration. (The first aspect in Allah's blessings in creating the causes of perception) Know that Allah, the Exalted, created the plant, and it is more complete in existence than the stone, the clay, the iron, the copper, and the rest of the jewels that do not grow and do not nourish, for the plant...
16:18.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

16:18.arabic: وجملة ما عرفناه وعرفه الخلق كلهم بالإضافة إلى ما لم يعرفوه من نعم الله تعالى أقل من قطرة من بحر إلا أن من علم شيئا من هذا أدرك شمة من معانى قوله تعالى: ﴿ وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها ﴾ ثم انظر كيف ربط الله تعالى قوام هذه الأعضاء وقوام منافعها وإدراكاتها وقواها ببخار لطيف يتصاعد من الأخلاط الأربعة ومستقرة القلب ويسرى في جميع البدن بواسطة العروق الضوارب فلا ينتهى إلى جزء من أجزاء البدن إلا ويحدث عند وصوله في تلك الأجزاء ما يحتاج إليه من قوة حس وإدراك وقوة حركة وغيرها كالسراج الذى يدار في أطراف ال
16:18.english: And the totality of what we have known and what all creation has known, in addition to what they have not known of the blessings of Allah the Exalted, is less than a drop from an ocean. However, whoever knows something of this perceives a whiff of the meanings of His saying the Exalted: 'And if you should count the blessings of Allah, you could not enumerate them.' Then look how Allah the Exalted has tied the uprightness of these limbs and the uprightness of their benefits, their perceptions, and their powers to a subtle vapor that ascends from the four humors and is settled in the Heart (Qalb) and flows in all the body by means of the pulsating veins. So it does not reach a part from the parts of the body except that it causes, upon its arrival in those parts, what is needed from it of sensory power, perception, power of movement, and others, like the lamp that is circulated in the corners of the house. So it does not reach a part except that there occurs, due to its arrival, light upon the parts of the house from the creation of Allah the Exalted and His invention, but He made the lamp a cause for it by His wisdom. And this subtle vapor is what the physicians call the Spirit (Ruh), and its place is the Heart (Qalb), and its example is the fiery substance of the lamp, and the Heart (Qalb) is for it like the lamp-holder, and the black blood that is in the interior of the Heart (Qalb) is for it like the wick, and the nourishment is for it like the oil, and the apparent life in the rest of the body's limbs because of it is like the light for the lamp in the entirety of the house. And just as the lamp, if its oil is cut off, is extinguished, so the lamp of the Spirit (Ruh) also is extinguished whenever its nourishment is cut off. And just as the wick may burn and become ashes such that it does not accept the oil, so the lamp is extinguished with abundance of oil, likewise the blood that this vapor clings to in the Heart (Qalb) may burn due to excessive heat of the Heart (Qalb) and is extinguished with the presence of nourishment, for it does not accept the nourishment that
16:18.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

16:18.arabic: ومنشأ كل ترتيب وتأليف وكل ذلك نعم من رب الأرباب ومسبب الأسباب ولولا فضله وكرمه إذ قال تعالى: ﴿ والذين جاهدوا فينا لنهدينهم سبلنا ﴾ لما اهتدينا إلى هذه النبذة اليسيرة من نعم الله تعالى ولولا عزله إيانا عن أن نطمح بعين الطمع إلى الإحاطة بكنه نعمه لتشوفنا إلى طلب الإحاطة والاستقصاء ولكنه تعالى عزنا بحكم القهر والقدرة فقال تعالى: ﴿ وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها ﴾ فإن تكلمنا فبإذنه انبسطنا وإن سكنا فبقهره انقبضنا، إذ لا معطى لما منع ولا مانع لما أعطى لأنا في كل لحظة من لحظات العمر قبل الموت نسمع بسمع
16:18.english: And the origin of every arrangement and composition, and all of that is blessings from the Lord of lords and the Causer of causes. And were it not for His grace and generosity when He, the Exalted, said: "And those who strive in Us, We will surely guide them to Our ways" (Quran 29:69), we would not have been guided to this small portion of the blessings of Allah, the Exalted. And were it not for His isolating us from aspiring with the eye of greed to encompass the essence of His blessings, we would have yearned to seek encompassing and exhaustive enumeration. But He, the Exalted, isolated us by the decree of overpowering and power, so He, the Exalted, said: "And if you should count the blessings of Allah, you could not enumerate them" (Quran 16:18). So if we speak, it is by His permission that we expand; and if we remain silent, it is by His overpowering that we contract, for there is no giver of what He has withheld nor withholder of what He has given. Because we, in every moment of the moments of life before death, hear with the hearing of the hearts (Qulūb) the call of the Compelling King: "To whom belongs the dominion today? To Allah, the One, the Compeller" (Quran 40:16). So praise be to Allah who distinguished us from the disbelievers and made us hear this call before the expiration of lifetimes.
16:18.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

16:18.arabic: وفي الخبر "لا يستدير الرغيف ويوضع بين يديك حتى يعمل في ثلثمائة وستون صانعاً أولهم ميكائيل عليه السلام الذي يكيل الماء من خزائن الرحمة، ثم الملائكة التي تزجي السحاب والشمس والقمر والأفلاك وملائكة الهواء ودواب الأرض، وآخرهم الخباز "وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها"[46]
16:18.english: And in the report: 'The loaf does not become round and placed before you until three hundred and sixty workers have worked on it, the first of them being Mikail (Michael), peace be upon him, who measures the water from the treasuries of mercy (Rahmah), then the angels who drive the clouds, the sun, the moon, the celestial spheres, the angels of the air, and the creatures of the earth, and the last of them is the baker.' 'And if you count the blessings (Ni'mah) of Allah, you cannot enumerate them.'
16:18.topic: Al-Ghazali on the outer and inner dimensions of worship, from 'Harms of the Tongue'

16:18.arabic: وكما عرفت أن في كل طرفة عين نعما كثيرة فاعلم أن في كل نفس ينبسط وينقبض نعمتين إذ بانبساطه يخرج الدخان المحترق من القلب ولو لم يخرج لهلك وبانقبضه يجمع روح الهواء إلى القلب ولو سد متنفسه لاحترق قلبه بانقطاع روح الهواء وبرودته عنه وهلك بل اليوم والليلة أربع وعشرون ساعة وفي كل ساعة قريب من ألف نفس وكل نفس قريب من عشر لحظات فعليك في كل لحظة آلاف آلاف نعمة في كل جزء من أجزاء بدنك بل في كل جزء من أجزاء العالم فانظر هل يتصور إحصاء ذلك أم لا، ولما انكشف لموسى عليه السلام حقيقة قوله تعالى: ﴿ وإن تعدوا نعم
16:18.english: And as you know that in every blink of an eye there are many blessings, so know that in every breath that expands and contracts there are two blessings: with its expansion, it expels the burnt smoke from the Heart (Qalb), and if it did not expel it, it would perish; and with its contraction, it gathers the spirit of air to the Heart (Qalb), and if its breathing passage were blocked, its Heart (Qalb) would burn from the cutting off of the spirit of air and its cooling from it, and it would perish. Rather, the day and night are twenty-four hours, and in every hour there are about a thousand breaths, and every breath is about ten moments, so upon you in every moment are thousands upon thousands of blessings in every part of the parts of your body, nay in every part of the parts of the world. So look: is it conceivable to enumerate that or not? And when the reality of His saying, the Exalted, was revealed to Moses, peace be upon him: 'And if you count the blessings of Allah, you cannot enumerate them' (Quran 16:18), he said: 'My God, how can I thank You when for every hair on my body there are two blessings: that You softened its root and that You blunted its tip.' And likewise, it has come in the tradition that whoever does not recognize the blessings of Allah in his food and drink, then his knowledge has diminished and his punishment has drawn near. And all that we have mentioned returns to food and drink, so consider what is other than them from the blessings by it, for the insightful one does not cast his eye in the world upon anything, nor does his thought touch upon an existent, except that he realizes that Allah has in it a blessing upon him. So let us leave exhaustive detailing, for it is aspiration in what is not attainable.
16:18.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

16:22.arabic: وشر أنواع الكبر ما يمنع من استفادة العلم وقبول الحق والانقياد له وفيه وردت الآيات التي فيها ذم الكبر والمتكبرين قال الله تعالى "والملائكة باسطو أيديهم" إلى قوله "وكنتم عن آياته تستكبرون" ثم قال "ادخلوا أبواب جهنم خالدين فيها فبئس مثوى المتكبرين" ثم أخبر أن أشد أهل النار عذاباً أشدهم عتياً على الله تعالى فقال "ثم لننزعن من كل شبعة أيهم أشد على الرحمن عتياً" وقال تعالى "فالذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة قلوبهم منكرة وهم مستكبرون" وقال عز وجل "يقول الذين استضعفوا للذين استكبروا لولا أنتم لكنا مؤمنين" وقال ت
16:22.english: And the worst types of arrogance (Kibr) are what prevent from benefiting from knowledge and accepting the truth and submitting to it. In it have come the verses which contain censure of arrogance (Kibr) and the arrogant ones. Allah the Exalted said: 'And the angels will be spreading their hands' up to His saying: 'and you were arrogant (Tastakbirun) about His signs.' Then He said: 'Enter the gates of Hell, abiding eternally therein, and wretched is the residence of the arrogant (Mutakabirin).' Then He informed that the most severely punished of the people of the Fire are the most insolent (Atiyan) against Allah the Exalted, so He said: 'Then We will surely extract from every sect those of them who were most insolent (Atiyan) against the Most Merciful.' And He the Exalted said: 'So those who do not believe in the Hereafter, their hearts (Qulub) are denying (Munkirah) and they are arrogant (Mustakbirun).' And He the Mighty and Majestic said: 'Those who were oppressed say to those who were arrogant (Istakbaru): "If not for you, we would have been believers."' And He the Exalted said: 'Indeed, those who are arrogant (Yastakbirun) about My worship will enter Hell in humiliation.' And He the Exalted said: 'I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant (Yatakabbarun) in the earth without right.' It is said in the interpretation (Tafsir): I will lift the understanding of the Quran from their hearts (Qulub). And in some interpretations (Tafsir): I will veil their hearts (Qulub) from the dominion (Malakut). And Ibn Juraij said: I will turn them away from reflecting upon them and taking admonition from them. And therefore, Jesus (Isa) peace be upon him said: Indeed, the crop grows in the plain and does not grow upon the rock, likewise wisdom (Hikmah) works in the heart (Qalb) of the humble one and does not work in the heart (Qalb) of the arrogant one (Mutakabbir). Do you not see that whoever raises his head to the ceiling strikes it, and whoever lowers it is shaded and sheltered. So this is a parable he struck for the arrogant ones (Mutakabirin) and how they are deprived of wisdom (Hikmah). And therefore, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) mentioned the rejection (Juhud) of the truth as part of the definition of arrogance (Kibr) and the uncovering of its reality, and he said: 'Whoever belittles the truth and looks down upon people.'
16:22.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

16:23.arabic: قد ذم الله الكبر في مواضع من كتابه وذم كل جبار متكبر فقال تعالى "سأصرف عن آياتي الذين يتكبرون في الأرض بغير الحق" وقال عز وجل "كذلك يطبع الله على كل قلب متكبر جبار" وقال تعالى "واستفتحوا وخاب كل جبار عنيد" وقال تعالى "إنه لا يحب المستكبرين" وقال تعالى "لقد استكبروا في أنفسهم وعتوا عتواً كبيراً" وقال تعالى "إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي سيدخلون جهنم داخرين" وذم الكبر في القرآن كثير وقد قال رسول الله ﭬ "لا يدخل الجنة من كان في قلبه مثقال حبة من خردل من كبر، ولا يدخل النار من كان في قلبه مثقال حبة من
16:23.english: Indeed, Allah has condemned arrogance in multiple places in His Book and condemned every tyrant who is arrogant. So He, the Exalted, said: "I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant on earth without right" and He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: "Thus does Allah seal over every arrogant, tyrannical heart (Qalb)" and He, the Exalted, said: "And they sought victory, and every obstinate tyrant failed" and He, the Exalted, said: "Indeed, He does not love the arrogant ones" and He, the Exalted, said: "They have certainly become arrogant within themselves and transgressed a great transgression" and He, the Exalted, said: "Indeed, those who are arrogant toward My worship will enter Hell in humiliation." And the condemnation of arrogance in the Quran is abundant. And the Messenger of Allah ﭬ said: "He will not enter Paradise who has in his heart (Qalb) the weight of a mustard seed of arrogance, and he will not enter the Fire who has in his heart (Qalb) the weight of a mustard seed of faith (Iman)."
16:23.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

16:33.arabic: فإذا عرفت أن الأخلاق الحسنة تارة تكون بالطبع والفطرة، تكون باعتياد الأفعال الجميلة، وتارة بمشاهدة أرباب الفعال الجميلة ومصاحبتهم وهم قرناء الخير وإخوان الصلاح، إذ الطبع يسرق من الطبع الشر والخير جميعاً. فمن تظاهرت في حقه الجهات الثلاث حتى صار ذا فضيلة طبعاً واعتياداً وتعلماً فهو في غاية الفضيلة، ومن كان رذلاً بالطبع واتفق له قرناء السوء فتعلم منهم وتيسرت له أسباب الشر حتى اعتادها فهو في غاية البعد من الله عز وجل، وبين الرتبتين من اختلفت فيه من هذه الجهات ولكل درجة في القرب والبعد بحسب ما تقتضيه
16:33.english: If you know that good character traits (Akhlaq) are sometimes by nature (Tab') and innate disposition (Fitrah), sometimes by habitual practice (I'tiyad) of beautiful actions, and sometimes by observing masters of beautiful deeds and accompanying them—they being companions of good (Qurana' al-Khayr) and brothers of righteousness (Ikhwan al-Salah)—since nature steals from nature both evil and good. So whoever has all three aspects manifest in his case until he becomes virtuous by nature, habit, and learning, he is at the peak of virtue. And whoever is base by nature and happens to have evil companions, learns from them, and finds the means of evil facilitated for him until he habituates them, he is at the peak of distance from Allah, the Exalted and Majestic. And between these two ranks are those who differ in these aspects, and each degree in closeness and distance is according to what his form and state necessitate: "So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it. And Allah did not wrong them, but they were wronging their own souls (Anfus)."
16:33.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

16:40.arabic: ومن هذا القبيل في كنايته عن الاقتدار قوله تعالى: ﴿ إنما قولنا لشيء إذا أردناه أن نقول له كن فيكون ﴾ {} فإن ظاهره ممتنع إذ قوله كن إن كان خطابا للشيء قبل وجوده فهو محال إذا المعدوم لا يفهم الخطاب حتى يمثل وإن كان بعد الوجود فهو مستغن عن التكوين ولكن لما كانت هذه الكناية أوقع في النفوس في تفهيم غاية الاقتدار عدل إليها.
16:40.english: And from this category in its metaphor for power (Iqtidar) is His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, Our word to a thing when We intend it is that We say to it, "Be," and it is.' For its apparent meaning is impossible, because His saying 'Be' - if it is an address to the thing before its existence, it is impossible since the non-existent does not understand the address until it is represented; and if it is after existence, it is independent of formation. But since this metaphor is more impactful in the souls (Nufus) in making understood the utmost power (Iqtidar), He turned to it.
16:40.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

16:42.arabic: وترك الأسباب الدافعة وإن كانت مقطوعة وجه إذا ناله الضرر من إنسان، فإنه إذا أمكنه الصبر وأمكنه الدفع والتشفي فشرط التوكل الاحتمال والصبر، قال الله تعالى: " فاتخذه وكيلاً واصبر على ما يقولون ". وقال تعالى: " ولنصبرن على ما آذيتمونا وعلى الله فليتوكل المتوكلون ". وقال عز وجل: " ودع أذاهم وتوكل على الله ". وقال سبحانه وتعالى: " فاصبر كما صبر أولو العزم من الرسل ". وقال تعالى: " نعم أجر العاملين الذين صبروا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون " وهذا في أذى الناس، وأما الصبر على أذى الحيات والسباع والعقارب، فترك دفعها
16:42.english: And abandoning the repelling causes, even if they are certain, is a face when harm reaches him from a human, for if patience is possible for him and repelling and retaliation are possible, then the condition of reliance (Tawakkul) is endurance and patience. Allah the Exalted said: "So take Him as a disposer of affairs (Wakil) and be patient over what they say." And He the Exalted said: "And we will be patient over what you harm us, and upon Allah let the reliant ones rely (Yatawakkal)." And He the Mighty and Majestic said: "And leave their harm and rely (Tawakkul) upon Allah." And He the Blessed and Exalted said: "So be patient as the possessors of resolve (Ulul-Azm) from the messengers were patient." And He the Exalted said: "Excellent is the reward of the doers, those who were patient (Sabaru) and upon their Lord they rely (Yatawakkalun)." And this is regarding the harm of people. As for patience over the harm of snakes, beasts, and scorpions, abandoning repelling them is not from reliance (Tawakkul) in anything, for there is no benefit in it, and the striving is not intended nor is the striving abandoned for its own sake but for aiding in the religion (Deen). And the arrangement of causes here is like their arrangement in earning and bringing benefits, so we do not prolong with repetition. And likewise in the causes repelling from wealth, reliance (Tawakkul) is not diminished by closing the door of the house when going out nor by tying the camel, because these are causes known by the Sunnah of Allah the Exalted, either certainly or presumptively. And for that reason, he ﷺ said to the Bedouin when he neglected the camel and said 'I have relied (Tawakkaltu) upon Allah': 'Tie it and rely (Tawakkul).' And He the Exalted said: 'Take your precaution.' And He said regarding the manner of the prayer of fear: 'And let them take their weapons.' And He the Blessed said: 'And prepare for them what you are able of power and of tethering horses.' And He the Exalted said to Musa, peace be upon him: 'So travel by night with My servants.' And fortifying by night is hiding from the eyes of enemies and a type of causing, and the hiding of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the cave is hiding from the eyes of enemies repelling harm. And taking weapons in prayer is not a repeller certainly like killing the snake and scorpion, for it is a repeller certainly, but taking weapons is a presumptive cause, and we have clarified that the presumptive is like the certain, and only the imagined is what reliance (Tawakkul) necessitates abandoning.
16:42.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

16:43.arabic: فإن قلت فقد قال الله تعالى: (فاسألوا أهل الذكر إن كنتم لا تعلمون( (النحل: 43). فالسؤال مأمور به فاعلم أنه كذلك ولكن فيما يأذن المعلم في السؤال عنه فإن السؤال عما لم تبلغ مرتبتك إلى فهمه مذموم ولذلك منع الخضر موسى عليه السلام من السؤال أي دع السؤال قبل أوانه فالمعلم أعلم بما أنت أهل له وبأوان الكشف وما لم يدخل أوان الكشف في كل درجة من مراقي الدرجات لا يدخل أوان السؤال عنه
16:43.english: If you say: Indeed, Allah the Exalted has said: 'So ask the people of the Remembrance (Dhikr) if you do not know' (An-Nahl: 43). So asking is commanded. Know that it is indeed so, but only regarding what the teacher permits you to ask about. For asking about what your rank has not reached to understand is blameworthy, and for that reason, Al-Khidr prevented Musa (peace be upon him) from asking, meaning: leave the question before its proper time. The teacher knows better what you are worthy of and the time of unveiling (Kashf), and what has not entered the time of unveiling in every degree of the ascending degrees (Marāqī al-Darajāt) does not enter the time of questioning about it.
16:43.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

16:43.arabic:
وقال الزهري رحمه الله العلم ذكر ولا تحبه إلا ذكران الرجال.

                                فضيلة التعلم

أما الآيات فقوله تعالى: ﴿فلولا نفر من كل فرقة منهم طائفة ليتفقهوا في الدين﴾ (سورة التوبة: الآية 122) وقوله عز وجل ﴿فاسألوا أهل الذكر إن كنتم لا تعلمون﴾ (سورة النحل: الآية 43، وسورة الأنبياء: الآية 7)
16:43.english:
And Al-Zuhri, may Allah have mercy upon him, said: Knowledge is Remembrance (Dhikr), and none love it except the men of Remembrance (Dhikr).

                                The Virtue of Learning

As for the verses, then His saying, the Exalted: 'Then why should not a party from every group of them go forth to gain understanding in the religion?' (Surah At-Tawbah: Verse 122) and His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'So ask the people of the Remembrance (Dhikr) if you do not know.' (Surah An-Nahl: Verse 43, and Surah Al-Anbiya: Verse 7)
16:43.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

16:43.arabic: والمقصود أن من قصد الخير بمعصية عن جهل فهو غير معذور إلا إذا كان قريب العهد بالإسلام ولم يجد بعد مهلة للتعلم وقد قال الله سبحانه فاسئلوا أهل الذكر إن كنتم لا تعلمون وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم (لا يعذر الجاهل على الجهل ولا يحل للجاهل أن يسكت على جهله ولا للعالم أن يسكت على علمه)[24]
16:43.english: The intended meaning is that whoever intends good through disobedience out of ignorance is not excused, except if he is newly converted to Islam and has not yet found an opportunity for learning. And Allah the Exalted has said: 'So ask the people of the Remembrance (Dhikr) if you do not know.' And the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'The ignorant one is not excused for his ignorance, nor is it permissible for the ignorant one to remain silent about his ignorance, nor for the knowledgeable one to remain silent about his knowledge.'
16:43.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

16:43.arabic: وأعظم نعمة الله على عباده هو العلم وكشف الحق والإيمان عبارة عن نوع كشف وعلم ولذلك قال تعالى امتنانا على عبده وكان فضل الله عليك عظيما وأراد به العلم وقال تعالى فاسألوا أهل الذكر إن كنتم لا تعلمون
16:43.english: And the greatest blessing of Allah upon His servants is knowledge and the unveiling of truth, and faith is an expression of a type of unveiling and knowledge. Therefore, Allah the Exalted said, as a favor upon His servant: 'And great is the grace of Allah upon you' (Quran 4:113), and He intended by it knowledge. And He said: 'So ask the people of the Remembrance (Dhikr) if you do not know' (Quran 16:43).
16:43.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

16:44.arabic: ولذلك قال تعالى ﴿ ما نثبت به فؤادك ﴾ {} فليقدر العبد أن الله ثبت فؤاده بما يقصه عليه من أحوال الأنبياء وصبرهم على الإيذاء وثباتهم في الدين لانتظار نصر الله تعالى وكيف لا يقدر هذا والقرآن ما أنزل على رسول الله ﭬ لرسول الله خاصة بل هو شفاء وهدى ورحمة ونور للعالمين ولذلك أمر الله تعالى الكافة بشكر نعمة الكتاب فقال تعالى ﴿ واذكروا نعمة الله عليكم وما أنزل عليكم من الكتاب والحكمة يعظكم به ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل ﴿ لقد أنزلنا إليكم كتابا فيه ذكركم أفلا تعقلون. وأنزلنا إليك الذكر لتبين للناس ما نزل إليهم. كذل
16:44.english: Therefore, Allah the Exalted said: 'What We strengthen with it your heart (Fūād)' {} So let the servant (ʿAbd) consider that Allah strengthened his heart (Fūād) with what He narrates to him of the conditions of the prophets and their patience upon harm and their firmness in the religion (Dīn) in anticipation of the victory of Allah the Exalted. And how can he not consider this when the Quran was not sent down upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for the Messenger of Allah alone, but it is a cure (Shifāʾ) and guidance (Hudā) and mercy (Raḥmah) and light (Nūr) for the worlds. Therefore, Allah the Exalted commanded the entirety to give thanks for the blessing of the Book, so He said: 'And remember the blessing of Allah upon you and what He sent down upon you of the Book and the Wisdom (Ḥikmah) by which He admonishes you' {} And He the Mighty and Majestic said: 'We have certainly sent down to you a Book in which is your Remembrance (Dhikr). Do you not then reason? And We sent down to you the Remembrance (Dhikr) that you may make clear to the people what was sent down to them. Thus does Allah set forth for the people their examples. And follow the best of what was sent down to you from your Lord. This is insights for the people and guidance (Hudā) and mercy (Raḥmah) for a people who are certain. This is a clarification for the people and guidance (Hudā) and admonition (Mawʿiẓah) for the God-fearing (Muttaqīn)' {} And if the address intended all people, then the individuals are intended, so this single reader is intended, so what is for him and for the rest of the people, let him consider that he is the intended one.
16:44.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

16:52.arabic: أنه فيماذا يتفكر لم يقدر عليه لأن مجارى الفكر غير محصورة وثمراته غير متناهية نعم نحن نجتهد في ضبط مجاريه بالإضافة إلى مهمات العلوم الدينية وبالإضافة إلى الأحوال التى هى مقامات السالكين ويكون ذلك ضبطا جمليا فإن تفصيل ذلك يستدعى شرح العلوم كلها وجملة هذه الكتب كالشرح لبعضها فإنها مشتملة على علوم تلك العلوم تستفاد من أفكار مخصوصة فلنشر إلى ضبط الجامع فيها ليحصل الوقوف على مجارى الفكر. بيان مجارى الفكر أعلم أن الفكر قد يجرى في أمر يتعلق بالدين وقد يجرى فيما يتعلق بغير الدين وإنما غرضنا ما يتعلق بالد
16:52.english: That in what he thinks about, he cannot encompass it because the channels of thought are not limited and its fruits are endless. Yes, we strive to control its channels in addition to the important matters of religious sciences and in addition to the states that are the stations of the travelers (Salikeen), and that will be a general control, for detailing that requires explaining all the sciences, and the entirety of these books is like an explanation for some of them, for they contain sciences of those sciences derived from specific thoughts. So let us proceed to controlling the comprehensive in them to achieve standing upon the channels of thought. Explanation of the channels of thought: Know that thought may run in a matter related to religion and may run in what is related to non-religion, and our aim is what is related to religion, so let us leave the other division and focus on religion as the transaction (Mu'amalah) that is between the servant and the Lord, the Exalted. So all the thoughts of the servant either relate to the servant and his attributes and his states, or relate to the Worshipped and His attributes and His actions; it is not possible to go beyond these two divisions. And what relates to the servant is either a consideration of what is beloved to the Lord, the Exalted, or of what is disliked, and there is no need for thought in other than these two divisions. And what relates to the Lord, the Exalted, is either a consideration of His Essence and His attributes and His beautiful names, or it is in His actions and His dominion and His sovereignty and all that is in the heavens and the earth and what is between them. And it becomes clear to you the confinement of thought in these divisions by an example, which is that the state of those who travel to Allah, the Exalted, and those who yearn for meeting Him relates to his Beloved or relates to himself. So if he thinks about his Beloved, then either he thinks about His beauty and the goodness of His image in His Essence to enjoy thinking about Him and witnessing Him, or he thinks about His gentle, good actions indicating His morals and attributes to make that a multiplier of pleasure and a strengthener of his love. And if he thinks about himself, then his thought is in his attributes that drop him from the eye of his Beloved until he abstains from them, or in the attributes that bring him near to Him and make him beloved to Him until he becomes characterized by them. So if he thinks about something outside of these divisions, then that is outside the limit of love (Ishq) and it is a deficiency in it, because the complete, perfect love is what overwhelms the lover and fulfills the heart (Qalb) until it leaves no room for other than Him. So the lover of Allah, the Exalted, should be like that, so his view and thought do not go beyond his Beloved. And as long as his thought is confined in these four divisions, it is not outside the requirement of love at all. So let us begin with the first division, which is his thinking about the attributes of himself and the actions of himself to distinguish the beloved from them from the disliked, for this thought is what relates to the science of transaction (Ilm al-Mu'amalah) which is the purpose of this book, and the other division relates to the science of unveiling (Ilm al-Mukashafah), then every.
16:52.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Contemplation'

16:62.arabic: وقد يخرج مائة ألف درهم مما يكره من ماله فيدل ذلك على أنه ليس يؤثر الله عز وجل بشيء مما يحبه وبذلك ذم الله تعالى قوما جعلوا لله ما يكرهون فقال تعالى: ﴿ ويجعلون لله ما يكرهون وتصف ألسنتهم الكذب أن لهم الحسنى لا ﴾{} وقف بعض القراء على النفي تكذيبا لهم ثم ابتدأ وقال: ﴿ جرم أن لهم النار ﴾{} أي كسب لهم جعلهم لله ما يكرهون النار.
16:62.english: And he may give one hundred thousand dirhams from what he dislikes of his wealth, which indicates that he does not prefer Allah (Exalted and Glorified) with anything that he loves. And with that, Allah (Exalted and Glorified) censured a people who made for Allah what they dislike. So He (Exalted and Glorified) said: 'And they assign to Allah what they dislike, and their tongues describe the falsehood that for them is the best. No' - some reciters paused at the negation to refute them, then began and said: 'It is earned that for them is the Fire' - meaning: their making for Allah what they dislike has earned them the Fire.
16:62.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

16:66.arabic: اعلم أن كل شىء يتصور أن يشوبه غيره فإذا صفا عن شوبه وخلص عنه سمى خالصا ويسمى الفعل المصفى المخلص إخلاصا قال الله تعالى من بين فرث ودم لبنا خالصا سائغا للشاربين فإنما خلوص اللبن أن لا يكون فيه شوب من الدم والفرث ومن كل ما يمكن أن يمتزج به والإخلاص يضاده الإشراك فمن ليس مخلصا فهو مشرك إلا أن الشرك درجات فالإخلاص في التوحيد يضاده التشريك في الإلهية والشرك منه خفي ومنه جلي وكذا الإخلاص والإخلاص وضده يتواردان على القلب فمحله القلب وإنما يكون ذلك في القصود والنيات وقد ذكر حقيقة النية وأنها ترجع إلى إج
16:66.english: Know that everything that can be imagined to be mixed with something else, when it becomes pure from its mixture and purified from it, is called pure (khalis), and the purified, purified action is called sincerity (ikhlas). Allah the Exalted said: 'From between dung and blood, pure milk, palatable to the drinkers.' For the purity of milk is that there is no mixture in it of blood and dung, and from everything that can mix with it. And sincerity (ikhlas) is opposed to association (shirk), so whoever is not sincere is an associator, except that association has degrees. Sincerity in monotheism (tawhid) is opposed to association in divinity, and association is of two kinds: hidden and apparent, and likewise sincerity. Sincerity and its opposite come upon the heart (qalb), so its place is the heart, and that only occurs in intentions and purposes. And the reality of intention has been mentioned, that it returns to responding to motives. So whenever the motive is single in detachment, the action emanating from it is called sincerity relative to what is intended. So whoever gives charity and his aim is purely ostentation (riya), he is sincere, and whoever's aim is purely drawing near to Allah the Exalted, he is sincere. But custom is established in specifying the name sincerity (ikhlas) to mean purifying the intention of drawing near to Allah the Exalted from all impurities, just as deviation (ilhad) is an expression for inclination, but custom specified it as inclination away from the truth. And whoever's motive is purely ostentation is exposed to destruction, and we are not speaking about it since we have mentioned what pertains to it in the Book of Ostentation from the quarter of destructives, and the least of its matters is what came in the report that the ostentatious will be called on the Day of Resurrection with four names: 'O ostentatious, O deceiver, O associator, O disbeliever.'
16:66.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

16:66.arabic: الحمد لله الذي خلق الإنسان من طين لازب وصلصال ثم ركب صورته في أحسن تقويم وأتم اعتدال ثم غذاه في أول نشوه بلبن استصفاه من بين فرث ودم سائغا كالماء الزلال ثم حماه بما آتاه من طيبات الرزق عن دواعي الضعف والانحلال ثم قيد شهوته المعادية له عن السطوة والصيال وقهرها بما افترضه عليه من طلب القوت الحلال وهزم بكسرها جند الشيطان المتشمر للإضلال ولقد كان يجري من ابن آدم مجرى الدم السيال فضيق عليه عزة الحلال المجرى والمجال إذ كان لا يبذرقه إلى أعماق العروق إلا الشهوة الماثلة إلى الغلبة والاسترسال فبقي لما زم
16:66.english: Praise be to Allah who created the human being from sticky clay and ringing clay, then fashioned his form in the best proportion and most perfect balance. Then He nourished him in his first growth with milk purified from between dung and blood, wholesome like pure water. Then He protected him with what He provided of goodly provisions from the causes of weakness and dissolution. Then He restrained his desire (Shahwa) that opposes him from domination and aggression, and subdued it with what He obligated upon him of seeking lawful (Halal) sustenance, and defeated by breaking it the army of Satan who is girded for misguidance. Indeed, it used to flow in the son of Adam like flowing blood, so the honor of the lawful (Halal) narrowed its channel and scope, since nothing could pour it into the depths of the veins except the desire (Shahwa) inclined to overpowering and indulgence. So he remained, when it was restrained with the rein of the lawful (Halal), disappointed and losing, with no helper or ally. And prayers upon Muhammad, the guide from misguidance, and upon his family, the best of families, and abundant salutations.
16:66.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

16:68.arabic: ثم في كل حيوان ونبات أعجوبة وأعاجيب تخصه لا يشاركه فيها غيره، فانظر إلى النحل وعجائبها وكيف أوحى الله تعالى إليها حتى اتخذت من الجبال بيوتاً ومن الشجر ومما يعرشون، وكيف استخرج من لعابها الشمع والعسل وجعل أحدهما ضياءً وجعل الآخر شفاءً، ثم لو تأملت عجائب أمرها في تناولها الأزهار والأنوار واحترازها عن النجاحات والأقذار، وطاعتها لواحد من جملتها هو أكبرها شخصاً وهو أميرها، ثم ما سخر الله تعالى له أميرها من العدل والإنصاف بينها - حتى إنه ليقتل على باب المنفذ كل ما وقع منها على نجاسة - لقضيت منها عجباً
16:68.english: Then in every animal and plant there is a wonder and wonders specific to it that no other shares in it, so look at the bees and their wonders and how Allah the Exalted inspired (awḥā) to them until they took from the mountains houses and from the trees and from what they construct, and how He extracted from their saliva wax and honey and made one of them light (ḍiyāʾ) and made the other healing (shifāʾ). Then if you contemplate the wonders of their affair in their consumption of flowers and blossoms and their avoidance of impurities and filth, and their obedience to one from among them who is the largest in body and is their commander (amīr), then what Allah the Exalted has subjugated for their commander of justice (ʿadl) and fairness (inṣāf) among them - until indeed he kills at the entrance of the passage every one of them that falls upon impurity - you would judge from them a wonder of the utmost wonder if you are insightful in your soul (nafs) and free from the concern of your stomach and your private parts and the desires (shahawāt) of your soul in hostility toward your peers and allegiance to your brothers. Then leave all of that and look at their building of their houses from wax, and their choice from among the shapes the hexagonal shape, so they do not build a house circular nor square nor pentagonal but hexagonal, due to a special property in the hexagonal shape that the understanding of the engineers falls short of grasping it, and it is that the widest shapes and the most containing: the circular and what is near to it, for the square produces from it wasted corners and the shape of the bee is circular elongated so they abandoned the square so that the corners are not wasted and remain empty, then if they built them circular there would remain outside the houses wasted gaps for the circular shapes when gathered do not come together compactly, and no shape among the shapes with corners approaches in containment the circular then they...
16:68.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

16:75.arabic: السبب الثاني: أن المدح يدل على أن قلب المادح مملوك للممدوح وأنه مريد له ومعتقد فيه ومسخر تحت مشيئته وملك القلوب محبوب والشعور بحصوله لذيذ، وبهذه العلة تعظم اللذة مهما صدر الثناء ممن تتسع قدرته وينتفع باقتناص قلبه كالملوك والأكابر، ويضعف مهما كان المادح ممن لا يؤبه له ولا يقدر على شيء، فإن القدرة عليه بملك قلبه قدرة على أمر حقير فلا يدل المدح إلا على قدرة قاصرة، وبهذه العلة أيضاً يكره الذم ويتألم به القلب، وإذا كان من الأكابر كانت نكايته أعظم لأن الفائت به أعظم.
16:75.english: The second reason: That praise indicates that the heart (Qalb) of the praiser is owned (mamlūk) by the praised one, and that he is desirous of him and believes in him and is subjugated under his will, and the ownership (mulk) of hearts is beloved and the feeling (shuʿūr) of its attainment is delightful. By this cause, the delight magnifies whenever praise issues from one whose capability expands and one benefits from capturing his heart, like kings and notables, and it weakens whenever the praiser is from those who are not heeded and has no capability (lā yaqdiru ʿalā shayʾ) over anything. For the capability over him through owning his heart is a capability over a trivial matter, so the praise indicates nothing but a deficient capability. By this cause also, blame is hated and the heart (Qalb) is pained by it, and if it is from the notables, its injury is greater because what is lost by it is greater.
16:75.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

16:75.arabic: وما كان قصدهم الرياء بإظهار الشوق وكل عبد سئل عن حال فهو بين ان يشكر او يشكو يسكت فالشكر طاعة والشكوى معصية قبيحة من اهل الدين وكيف لا تقبح الشكوى من ملك الملوك وبيده كل شيء الى عبد مملوك لا يقدر على شيء فالأحرى بالعبد ان لم يحسن الصبر على البلاء والقضاء وأفضي به الضعف الى الشكوى ان تكون شكواه الى الله تعالى فهو المبلى والقادر على ازالة البلاء وذل العبد لمولاه عز والشكوى الى غيره ذل وإظهار الذل للعبد مع كونه عبدا مثله ذل قبيح قال الله تعالى: ﴿ إن الذين تعبدون من دون الله لا يملكون لكم رزقا فابتغ
16:75.english: And their intention was not ostentation (Riya) by showing longing, and every servant (Abd) asked about his condition is between either giving thanks (Shukr) or complaining (Shakwa) or remaining silent. So giving thanks (Shukr) is obedience (Taa'a), and complaining (Shakwa) is ugly disobedience (Ma'siya) from the people of religion (Ahl al-Din). And how could complaining (Shakwa) not be ugly from the King of Kings (Malik al-Muluk) in whose hand is everything, to an owned slave (Abd Mamlook) who is not capable of anything? So it is more appropriate for the servant (Abd) that if he does not excel in patience (Sabr) upon the trial (Bala) and the decree (Qada), and weakness leads him to complaining (Shakwa), that his complaint (Shakwa) be to Allah the Exalted, for He is the One who afflicts (Al-Mubli) and is capable of removing the trial (Bala), and the humility (Dhull) of the servant (Abd) to his Master (Mawla) is glorious, and complaining (Shakwa) to other than Him is humility (Dhull), and showing humility (Dhull) to a servant (Abd) while he is a servant (Abd) like him is ugly humility (Dhull). Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, those you worship besides Allah do not possess for you [the power of] provision. So seek from Allah provision and worship Him and be grateful to Him.' {} And He said: 'Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah are servants like you.' {} So giving thanks (Shukr) by the tongue (Lisan) is from the totality of giving thanks (Shukr).
16:75.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

16:75.arabic: القسم الثالث: التكبر على العباد؛ وذلك بأن يستعظم نفسه ويستحقر غيره، فتأبى نفسه عن الانقياد لهم وتدعوه إلى الترفع عليهم فيزدريهم ويستصغرهم ويأنف عن مساواتهم، وهذا وإن كان دون الأول والثاني فهو أيضاً عظيم من وجهين؛ أحدهما: أن الكبر والعز والعظمة والعلاء لا يليق إلا بالملك القادر، فأما العبد المملوك الضعيف العاجز الذي لا يقدر على شيء فمن أين يليق بحاله الكبر؟ فمهما تكبر العبد فقد نازع الله تعالى في صفة لا تليق إلا بجلاله، ومثاله: أن يأخذ الغلام قلنسوة الملك فيضعها على رأسه ويجلس على سريره، فما أعظم
16:75.english: The third category: Arrogance (Takabbur) towards the servants (of Allah); that is by magnifying oneself and belittling others, so his soul (Nafs) refuses to submit to them and calls him to elevate himself over them, thus he despises them, considers them insignificant, and disdains equality with them. And this, even though it is less than the first and second, is also great from two aspects; one of them: that arrogance (Kibr), honor (Izz), majesty (Azamah), and loftiness (Ala') are not fitting except for the capable King (Malik), so as for the owned slave (Abd Mamlook), weak, incapable, who is not able to do anything, then from where is arrogance fitting for his condition? Whenever a slave (Abd) becomes arrogant, he has contended with Allah the Exalted in an attribute that is not fitting except for His majesty (Jalal), and its example: that a boy takes the king's cap and places it on his head and sits on his throne, so how great is his deserving of hatred and how great is his targeting for disgrace and punishment! And how severe is his audacity towards his master (Mawla) and how ugly is what he has undertaken! And to this meaning is the allusion in His saying the Exalted "Majesty (Azamah) is My lower garment and grandeur (Kibriya') is My upper garment, so whoever contends with Me in them I will break him" meaning that it is specific to My attribute and not fitting except for Me, and the contender in it contends in an attribute from My attributes, and if arrogance (Kibr) over His servants is not fitting except for Him, then whoever is arrogant over His servants has wronged Him, since the one who despises the special servants of the king and uses them and elevates himself over them and monopolizes what is the king's right to monopolize from them is contending with him in some of his affair, even if his degree does not reach the degree of one who wanted to sit on his throne and monopolize his kingdom, so all creation are servants (Ibad) of Allah and to Him belongs majesty (Azamah) and grandeur (Kibriya') over them, so whoever is arrogant over a servant (Abd) from the servants (Ibad) of Allah has contended with Allah in His right. Indeed, the difference between this contention and the contention of Nimrod and Pharaoh, is the difference between contending with the king in belittling some of his slaves and using them and contending with him in the essence of kingship.
16:75.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

16:75.arabic: فهو مضطر ذليل إن ترك بقي وإن اختطف فني، عبد مملوك لا يقدر على شيء من نفسه ولا شيء من غيره، فأي شيء أذل منه لو عرف نفسه؟ وأنى يليق الكبر به لولا جهله؟ فهذا أوسط أحواله فليتأمله. وأما آخره ومورده فهو الموت المشار إليه بقول تعالى "ثم أماته فأقبره ثم إذا شاء أنشره" ومعناه أنه يسلب روحه وسمعه وبصره وعلمه وقدرته وحسه وإدراكه وحركته، فيعود جماداً كما كان أول مرة، لا يبقى إلا شكل أعضائه وصورته لا حس فيه ولا حركة، ثم يوضع في التراب فيصير جيفة منتنة قذرة كما كان في الأول نطفة مذرة، ثم تبلى أعضاؤه وتتفتت أ
16:75.english: So he is compelled and humiliated; if left, he remains, and if snatched away, he perishes—a slave owned (abd mamluk) who cannot control anything of himself nor anything of others. What is more humiliated than him if he knew himself? And how does arrogance befit him except due to his ignorance? This is his intermediate state, so let him contemplate it. As for his end and destination, it is death, alluded to by the saying of the Exalted: 'Then He causes him to die and buries him, then when He wills, He resurrects him.' Its meaning is that He strips him of his Spirit (Ruh), hearing, sight, knowledge, power, sensation, perception, and movement, so he returns as inanimate matter as he was at first, nothing remains except the form of his limbs and his image—no sensation in it nor movement. Then he is placed in the earth and becomes a stinking, filthy corpse as he was initially a despised drop (nutfah). Then his limbs decay, his parts disintegrate, his bones rot, and he becomes scattered remains and fragments, and worms eat his parts, beginning with his pupils to pluck them out and his cheeks to cut them off, and with all his parts until he becomes dung in the bellies of worms and becomes a corpse from which animals flee and every human finds repulsive and flees from due to the intensity of the stench. The best of his states is that he returns to what he was and becomes earth from which cups are made and from which buildings are constructed, so he becomes non-existent after having been existent. And it becomes as if he had not flourished yesterday as a harvest, as he was in his first affair a long period. Would that he remained thus—how excellent if he were left as earth! No, rather He revives him after long decay to experience severe trial, so he emerges from his grave after gathering his scattered parts, and emerges.
16:75.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

16:75.arabic: وما أنت إلا عبد مملوك لا تقدر على شيء. ومن عرف ذلك لا بد وأن يزول كبره. ومثاله: أن يفتخر الغافل بقوته وجماله وماله وحريته واستقلاله وسعة منازله وكثرة خيوله وغلمانه، إذ شهد عليه شاهدان عدلان عند حاكم منصف بأنه رقيق لفلان وأن أبويه كانا مملوكين له، فعلم ذلك وحكم به الحاكم، فجاء مالكه فأخذه، وأخذ جميع ما في يده، وهو مع ذلك يخشى أن يعاقبه وينكل به لتفريطه في أمواله وتقصيره في طلب مالكه ليعرف أنه له مالكاً، ثم نظر العبد فرأى نفسه محبوساً في منزل قد أحدقت به الحيات والعقارب والهوام وهو في كل حال على و
16:75.english: And you are nothing but a slave (abd) owned (mamluk) who cannot do anything. And whoever knows that, his arrogance must vanish. Its example: that the heedless one boasts of his strength, beauty, wealth, freedom, independence, spacious dwellings, and abundance of horses and servants, when two just witnesses testify against him before a fair judge that he is a slave (riq) to so-and-so and that his parents were owned (mamluk) by him, so that is known and the judge rules by it, then his owner (malik) comes and takes him, and takes all that is in his hand, and he with that fears that he will punish him and inflict harm upon him for his wastefulness in his wealth and his shortcoming in seeking his owner (malik) to know that he has an owner (malik). Then the slave (abd) looked and saw himself imprisoned in a dwelling that has been surrounded by snakes, scorpions, and vermin, and he is in every state in fear from each one of them, and he remains not owning himself nor his wealth nor knowing any way of escape at all. Do you think one in this state boasts of his power, wealth, strength, and perfection or humbles himself and submits? And this is the state of every intelligent person who becomes, for he sees himself thus, so he does not own his neck, body, limbs, and wealth, and he with that is among afflictions, desires, illnesses, and diseases that are like scorpions and snakes from which he fears destruction. So one in this state does not become arrogant with his strength and power since he knows that he has no power and no strength. This is the way of treating arrogance with external causes, and it is easier than treating arrogance with knowledge and action, for they are two perfections in the soul (nafs) worthy of rejoicing in them. Allah struck a similitude: a slave (abd) owned (mamluk) who cannot do anything, and one whom We have provided from Us a good provision, so he spends from it secretly and openly. Are they equal? Praise be to Allah. But most of them do not know.
16:75.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

16:76.arabic: ومنها المبهم وهو اللفظ المشترك بين معن من كلمة أو حرف أما الكلمة فكالشيء والقرين والأمة والروح ونظائرها قال الله تعالى ﴿ ضرب الله مثلا عبدا مملوكا لا يقدر على شيء ﴾ {} أراد به النفقة مما رزق وقوله عز وجل ﴿ وضرب الله مثلا رجلين أحدهما أبكم لا يقدر على شيء ﴾ {} أي الأمر بالعدل والاستقامة
16:76.english: And among them is the ambiguous, which is the word shared between meanings of a word or letter. As for the word, such as 'thing' (al-shay'), 'companion' (al-qarīn), 'community' (al-ummah), 'spirit' (al-rūḥ), and their like. Allah the Exalted said: 'Allah sets forth a parable of a slave owned, unable to do anything' (Quran 16:75) – He intended by it the expenditure from what He has provided. And His saying, the Exalted: 'And Allah sets forth a parable of two men: one of them dumb, unable to do anything' (Quran 16:76) – meaning the command to justice (al-ʿadl) and uprightness (al-istiqāmah).
16:76.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

16:76.arabic: القسم الثالث: التكبر على العباد؛ وذلك بأن يستعظم نفسه ويستحقر غيره، فتأبى نفسه عن الانقياد لهم وتدعوه إلى الترفع عليهم فيزدريهم ويستصغرهم ويأنف عن مساواتهم، وهذا وإن كان دون الأول والثاني فهو أيضاً عظيم من وجهين؛ أحدهما: أن الكبر والعز والعظمة والعلاء لا يليق إلا بالملك القادر، فأما العبد المملوك الضعيف العاجز الذي لا يقدر على شيء فمن أين يليق بحاله الكبر؟ فمهما تكبر العبد فقد نازع الله تعالى في صفة لا تليق إلا بجلاله، ومثاله: أن يأخذ الغلام قلنسوة الملك فيضعها على رأسه ويجلس على سريره، فما أعظم
