16:76.english: The third category: Arrogance (Takabbur) towards the servants (of Allah); this is by magnifying oneself and belittling others, so his Soul (Nafs) refuses to submit to them and calls him to elevate himself over them, thus he despises them, considers them insignificant, and disdains equality with them. And this, even if it is less than the first and second, is also great from two aspects. The first: that arrogance (Kibr), honor (Izz), majesty (Azamah), and loftiness (Ala') are not fitting except for the King (Malik) who is capable (Qadir). As for the servant (Abd) who is owned (Mamluk), weak (Da'if), incapable (Ajiz), who cannot do anything, then from where does arrogance (Kibr) befit his state? So whenever a servant (Abd) becomes arrogant (Takabbur), he has contended with Allah the Exalted in an attribute that is not fitting except for His majesty (Jalal). Its example: that a boy (Ghulam) takes the king's cap (Qalansuwah) and places it on his head and sits on his throne (Sarir), so how great is his deserving of contempt (Maqt) and how great is his exposure to disgrace (Khizy) and punishment (Nikal)! And how severe is his audacity (Istijra') towards his master (Mawlah) and how ugly is what he has undertaken! And to this meaning is the allusion in His saying the Exalted: "Majesty (Azamah) is My lower garment (Izar) and arrogance (Kibriya') is My cloak (Rida'), so whoever contends with Me in them I will break him" meaning that it is specific to My attribute and not fitting except for Me, and the contender in it contends in an attribute from My attributes. And if arrogance (Kibr) over His servants (Ibad) is not fitting except for Him, then whoever is arrogant (Takabbur) over His servants (Ibad) has wronged Him, since the one who despises the special servants (Khawass) of the king's boys (Ghulman), uses them, elevates himself over them, and monopolizes what it is the king's right to monopolize from them, he is contending with him in some of his affair, even if his degree does not reach the degree of one who wanted to sit on his throne (Sarir) and monopolize his kingdom. So all creation (Khalq) are servants (Ibad) of Allah and to Him belongs majesty (Azamah) and arrogance (Kibriya') over them, so whoever is arrogant (Takabbur) over a servant (Abd) from the servants (Ibad) of Allah has contended with Allah in His right. Yes, the difference between this contention and the contention of Nimrod and Pharaoh is the difference between contending with the king in belittling some of his servants (Abid) and using them and contending with him in the foundation of kingship. The second aspect: by which the vileness of arrogance (Takabbur) towards the servants (of Allah) is magnified is that Allah the Exalted struck for it a parable, saying: "And Allah presents an example of two men: one of them is dumb (Abkam), unable to do anything, and he is a burden (Kall) upon his master (Mawlah) - wherever he directs him, he brings no good. Is he equal to one who commands justice (Adl) and is upon a straight path (Sirat Mustaqim)?" So the one arrogant (Mutakabbir) towards the servants (of Allah) is like the dumb (Abkam) who cannot do anything, and he is a burden (Kall) upon his master (Mawlah), meaning a heavy load upon him, wherever he directs him he brings no good. So is he equal to one who commands justice (Adl) and is upon a straight path (Sirat Mustaqim)? So the one arrogant (Mutakabbir) towards the servants (of Allah) does not command justice (Adl) nor is he upon a straight path (Sirat Mustaqim), rather he is like the dumb (Abkam) who cannot do anything, and he is a burden (Kall) upon his master (Mawlah), meaning a heavy load upon Allah the Exalted, wherever he directs him he brings no good. So is he equal to one who commands justice (Adl) and is upon a straight path (Sirat Mustaqim)? So the one arrogant (Mutakabbir) towards the servants (of Allah) does not command justice (Adl) nor is he upon a straight path (Sirat Mustaqim), rather he is like the dumb (Abkam) who cannot do anything, and he is a burden (Kall) upon his master (Mawlah), meaning a heavy load upon Allah the Exalted, wherever he directs him he brings no good. So is he equal to one who commands justice (Adl) and is upon a straight path (Sirat Mustaqim)?
16:76.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

16:77.arabic: فإن قلت: فما فائدة الدعاء والقضاء لا مرد له. فاعلم أن من القضاء رد البلاء بالدعاء فالدعاء سبب لرد البلاء واستجلاب الرحمة كما أن الترس سبب لرد السهم والماء سبب لخروج النبات من الأرض فكما أن الترس يدفع السهم فيتدافعان فكذلك الدعاء والبلاء يتعالجان وليس من شرط الاعتراف بقضاء الله تعالى أن لا يحمل السلاح وقد قال تعالى: ﴿ خذوا حذركم ﴾ {} وأن لا يسقي الأرض بعد بث البذر فيقال إن سبق القضاء بالنبات نبت البذر وإن لم يسبق لم ينبت بل ربط الأسباب بالمسببات هو القضاء الأول الذي هو كلمح البصر أو هو أقرب وترتي
16:77.english: If you say: What is the benefit of supplication (Dua) when divine decree (Qada) cannot be reversed? Know that from divine decree (Qada) is repelling affliction (Bala) through supplication (Dua), so supplication (Dua) is a cause for repelling affliction (Bala) and attracting mercy (Rahma) just as a shield is a cause for repelling an arrow and water is a cause for the emergence of plants from the earth. So just as the shield pushes the arrow and they repel each other, likewise supplication (Dua) and affliction (Bala) contend with each other. It is not a condition of acknowledging the divine decree (Qada) of Allah the Exalted to not carry weapons, and He the Exalted has said: 'Take your precautions' (Quran 4:71), and to not water the earth after sowing seeds, saying: If divine decree (Qada) preceded with growth, the seed will grow, and if it did not precede, it will not grow. Rather, linking causes (Asbab) to effects (Musabbabat) is the first divine decree (Qada) which is like the blink of an eye or it is nearer. And arranging the detailing of effects (Musabbabat) upon the details of causes (Asbab) with gradualness and measure is divine destiny (Qadar). And the One who decreed good decreed it with a cause, and the One who decreed evil decreed it to repel it with a cause. So there is no contradiction between these matters for one whose insight (Basira) has opened.
16:77.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

16:90.arabic: والطاعات تنقسم الى فرض ونفل وهو محتاج الى الصبر عليهما جميعا وقد جمعهما الله تعالى في قوله: ﴿ إن الله يأمر بالعدل والاحسان وايتاء ذي القربى ﴾ {} فالعدل هو الفرض، والإحسان هو النفل، وايتاء ذي القربى هو المروءة وصلة الرحم وكل ذلك يحتاج الى صبر. الضرب الثاني المعاصي فما أحوج العبد الى الصبر عنها، وقد جمع الله تعالى انواع المعاصي في قوله تعالى: ﴿ وينهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر والبغي ﴾ {}
16:90.english: And acts of obedience (Tā'āt) are divided into obligatory (Farḍ) and supererogatory (Nafal), and one needs patience (Ṣabr) upon both of them together. And Allah the Exalted has combined them in His saying: 'Indeed, Allah commands justice (Al-'Adl) and excellence (Al-Iḥsān) and giving to relatives (Dhī al-Qurbā)' - so justice (Al-'Adl) is the obligatory (Farḍ), and excellence (Al-Iḥsān) is the supererogatory (Nafal), and giving to relatives (Dhī al-Qurbā) is chivalry (Al-Murū'ah) and maintaining kinship ties (Ṣilat al-Raḥm), and all of that requires patience (Ṣabr). The second category is sins (Al-Ma'āṣī), so how much the servant (Al-'Abd) is in need of patience (Ṣabr) from them! And Allah the Exalted has gathered the types of sins (Al-Ma'āṣī) in His saying: 'And He forbids immorality (Al-Faḥshā') and wrong (Al-Munkar) and oppression (Al-Baghy)'.
16:90.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

16:90.arabic: قال إني سمعت اباك واجدادك يقرءون هذه الآية على المنبر إن الله يأمر بالعدل والاحسان وإيتاء ذي القربى وينهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر والبغي وأنا رأيت منكرا فغيرته فقال فغيره فوالله ما قال إلا هذا
16:90.english: He said: 'Indeed, I heard your father and your forefathers reciting this verse on the pulpit: "Indeed, Allah commands justice (al-'adl) and excellence (al-ihsan) and giving to the near of kin, and forbids indecency (al-fahsha') and the reprehensible (al-munkar) and aggression (al-baghy). He admonishes you so that you may remember." And I saw a reprehensible act (munkar) so I changed it.' So he changed it, and by Allah, he said nothing but this.
16:90.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

16:90.arabic: وإنما أدبه القرآن بمثل قوله تعالى خذ العفو وأمر بالعرف وأعرض عن الجاهلين وقوله إن الله يأمر بالعدل والإحسان وإيتاء ذي القربى وينهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر والبغي وقوله واصبر على ما أصابك إن ذلك من عزم الأمور وقوله ولمن صبر وغفر إن ذلك لمن عزم الأمور وقوله فاعف عنهم واصفح إن الله يحب المحسنين وقوله وليعفوا وليصفحوا ألا تحبون أن يغفر الله لكم وقوله ادفع بالتي هي أحسن فإذا الذي بينك وبينه عداوة كأنه ولي حميم وقوله والكاظمين الغيظ والعافين عن الناس والله يحب المحسنين وقوله اجتنبوا كثيرا من الظن إن بعض ال
16:90.english: And indeed, the Quran educated him with verses like His saying: 'Take forgiveness and command with what is recognized as good and turn away from the ignorant ones,' and His saying: 'Indeed, Allah commands with justice (al-'adl) and excellence (al-ihsan) and giving to the near of kin, and He forbids from indecency (al-fahsha') and what is disapproved (al-munkar) and aggression (al-baghy),' and His saying: 'And be patient over what befalls you; indeed, that is of the matters of determination,' and His saying: 'And for whoever is patient and forgives; indeed, that is of the matters of determination,' and His saying: 'So pardon them and overlook; indeed, Allah loves the doers of excellence (al-muhsinin),' and His saying: 'And let them pardon and overlook; do you not love that Allah should forgive you?' and His saying: 'Repel with that which is better; then indeed, the one between you and whom is enmity will be as if he was a close protector,' and His saying: 'And those who restrain anger and pardon the people; and Allah loves the doers of excellence (al-muhsinin),' and His saying: 'Avoid much of assumption; indeed, some assumption is sin, and do not spy, nor backbite one another.'
16:90.book_title: Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character
16:90.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character'

16:90.arabic: وقال الفضيل بن عياض: ينبغي لحامل القرآن أن لا يكون له إلى أحد حاجة ولا إلى الخلفاء فمن دونهم فينبغي أن تكون حوائج الخلق إليه وقال أيضا حامل القرآن حامل راية الإسلام فلا ينبغي أن يلهو مع من يلهو ولا يسهو مع من يسهو ولا يلغو مع من يلغو تعظيما لحق القرآن. وقال سفيان الثوري: إذا قرأ الرجل القرآن قبل الملك بين عينيه. وقال عمرو بن ميمون: من نشر مصحفا حين يصلي الصبح فقرأ منه مائة آية رفع الله عز وجل له مثل عمل جميع أهل الدنيا. ويروى أن (خالد بن عقبة جاء إلى رسول الله ﭬ وقال: اقرأ علي القرآن فقرأ عليه ﴿
16:90.english: And Al-Fudayl ibn Iyad said: It is fitting for the bearer of the Quran that he should have no need of anyone, nor of the caliphs or those below them; rather, the needs of creation should be directed to him. He also said: The bearer of the Quran is the bearer of the banner of Islam, so it is not fitting that he should play around with those who play around, nor be heedless with those who are heedless, nor engage in idle talk with those who engage in idle talk, out of reverence for the right of the Quran. And Sufyan al-Thawri said: When a man recites the Quran, the angel places it between his eyes. And Amr ibn Maymun said: Whoever opens a Quran when he prays the morning prayer and recites one hundred verses from it, Allah the Exalted will raise for him the equivalent of the deeds of all the people of the world. And it is narrated that (Khalid ibn Uqbah came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: Recite the Quran to me. So he recited to him: 'Indeed, Allah commands justice and excellence (Ihsan) and giving to relatives, and He forbids immorality and wrong and oppression; He admonishes you that perhaps you will be reminded.' Then he said to him: Repeat it. So he repeated it and said: By Allah, indeed it has sweetness, and indeed upon it is freshness, and indeed its lower part is verdant, and indeed its upper part is fruitful, and no human says this). And Al-Hasan said: By Allah, there is no wealth below the Quran, nor any poverty beyond it.
16:90.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

16:90.arabic: وقال معاذ أوصاني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال يا معاذ أوصيك بإتقاء الله وصدق الحديث والوفاء بالعهد وأداء الأمانة وترك الخيانة وحفظ الجار ورحمة اليتيم ولين الكلام وبذل السلام وحسن العمل وقصر الأمل ولزوم الإيمان والتفقه في القرآن وحب الآخرة والجزع من الحساب وخفض الجناح وأنهاك أن تسب حكيما أو تكذب صادقا أو تطيع آثما أو تعصي إماما عادلا أو تفسد أرضا وأوصيك باتقاء الله عند كل حجر وشجر ومدر وأن تحدث لكل ذنب توبة السر بالسر والعلانية بالعلانية حديث يا معاذ أوصيك باتقاء الله وصدق الحديث الحديث أخرج
16:90.english: And Mu'adh said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) advised me, saying: O Mu'adh, I advise you with the Fear (Taqwa) of Allah, truthful speech, fulfilling the covenant, performing the trust, abandoning treachery, protecting the neighbor, mercy to the orphan, softness in speech, giving the greeting (Salam), good action, shortening hope, adhering to faith, understanding the Quran, love of the Hereafter, dread from the accounting, lowering the wing, and I forbid you from insulting a wise person, lying to a truthful one, obeying a sinner, disobeying a just leader, or corrupting the land. And I advise you with the Fear (Taqwa) of Allah at every stone, tree, and clod, and that you initiate repentance for every sin, the secret with the secret and the public with the public. The hadith: O Mu'adh, I advise you with the Fear (Taqwa) of Allah and truthful speech. The hadith was reported by Abu Nu'aym in Al-Hilyah and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Zuhd, and it preceded in the etiquettes of companionship. Thus is the manner of the servants of Allah, and He called them to noble character traits and beautiful etiquettes. Explanation of a group of his beautiful character traits that some scholars collected and extracted from the reports, saying: He (peace be upon him) was the most forbearing of people. The hadith: He (peace be upon him) was the most forbearing of people. Reported by Abu Al-Shaykh in the book Akhlaq Rasul Allah (peace be upon him) from the narration of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was among the most forbearing of people. The hadith is mursal, and Abu Hatim ibn Hibban reported from the hadith of...

16:93.arabic: ونحن نجوز أن يقدر الله سببا يهلك به الخلق عن آخرهم فيفوت دنياهم ويضلون في دينهم فإنه يضل من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء ويميت من يشاء ويحيي من يشاء ولكنا نقدر الأمر جاريا على ما ألف من سنة الله تعالى في بعثة الأنبياء لصلاح الدين والدنيا
16:93.english: And we allow that Allah may decree a cause by which He destroys the creation entirely, so their worldly life is lost and they go astray in their religion, for He misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills, and causes death whom He wills and gives life whom He wills. But we consider the matter proceeding according to what is customary from the established way (Sunnah) of Allah the Exalted in sending the prophets for the rectification of the religion and the worldly life.
16:93.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

16:96.arabic: وأما العلم الذي هو مثمر لهذه الحال فهو العلم بكون المتروك حقيراً بالإضافة إلى المأخوذ كعلم التاجر بأن العوض خير من المبيع فيرغب فيه، وما لم يتحقق هذا العلم لم يتصور أن تزول الرغبة عن المبيع، فكذلك من عرف أن ما عند الله باق وأن الآخرة خير وأبقى، أي لذاتها خير في أنفسها وأبقى، كما تكون الجواهر خيراً وأبقى من الثلج مثلاً. ولا يعسر على مالك الثلج بيعه بالجواهر واللآلئ، فهكذا مثال الدنيا والآخرة، فالدنيا كالثلج الموضوع في الشمس لا يزال في الذوبان إلى الانقراض، والآخرة كالجوهر الذي لا فناء له، فبقدر ق
16:96.english: And as for the knowledge that is fruitful for this state, it is the knowledge that what is abandoned is insignificant in comparison to what is taken, like the knowledge of the merchant that the exchange is better than the sold item, so he desires it. And if this knowledge is not realized, it cannot be imagined that the desire for the sold item will vanish. Similarly, whoever knows that what is with Allah remains and that the Hereafter is better and more lasting, meaning its essence is better in itself and more lasting, just as jewels are better and more lasting than snow, for example. And it is not difficult for the owner of snow to sell it for jewels and pearls. Thus is the example of this world and the Hereafter: this world is like snow placed in the sun, constantly melting to extinction, and the Hereafter is like a jewel that has no perishing. So according to the strength of certainty and knowledge of the disparity between this world and the Hereafter, the desire for selling and transaction strengthens, until indeed whoever has strong certainty sells his soul (Nafs) and his wealth, as Allah the Exalted said: "Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their souls (Anfus) and their wealth in exchange for Paradise for them." Then He clarified that their transaction is profitable, so He said: "So rejoice in your transaction which you have contracted." So what is needed from knowledge in asceticism (Zuhd) is only this amount: that the Hereafter is better and more lasting. And one may know that yet not be able to abandon this world, either due to weakness in his knowledge and certainty, or due to the domination of desire (Shahwa) in the moment over him and being overpowered in the hand of Satan, or due to his deception by the promises of Satan in procrastination day after day until death snatches him and nothing remains with him except regret after the passing: and to the definition of the baseness of this world, the indication is in His saying: "Say, the enjoyment of this world is little." And to the definition of the preciousness of...
16:96.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

16:98.arabic: وخذلانا فإن المعاني المختلفة تفتقر إلى أسامي مختلفة والملك عبارة عن خلق خلقه الله تعالى شأنه إفاضة الخير وإفادة العلم وكشف الحق والوعد بالخير والأمر بالمعروف وقد خلقه وسخره لذلك والشيطان عبارة عن خلق شأنه ضد ذلك وهو الوعد بالشر والأمر بالفحشاء والتخويف عند الهم بالخير بالفقر فالوسوسة في مقابلة الإلهام والشيطان في مقابلة الملك والتوفيق في مقابلة الخذلان وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى ومن كل شيء خلقنا زوجين فإن الموجودات كلها متقابلة مزدوجة إلا الله تعالى فإنه فرد لا مقابل له بل هو الواحد الحق الخالق ل
16:98.english: And abandonment (Khudhlan). For different meanings require different names. The Angel (Malak) is an expression for a creation that Allah the Exalted created, its affair being the outpouring of good, imparting knowledge, unveiling truth, promising good, and commanding righteousness. He created it and subjugated it for that. And the Satan (Shaytan) is an expression for a creation whose affair is the opposite of that, which is promising evil, commanding indecency, and frightening when intending good with poverty. So whispering (Waswasa) is in opposition to inspiration (Ilham), and Satan is in opposition to the Angel, and success (Tawfiq) is in opposition to abandonment. To this is the allusion in His saying the Exalted: 'And of all things We created pairs' (51:49). For all existents are opposing, paired except Allah the Exalted, for He is singular with no opposite; rather, He is the One True (Al-Wahid Al-Haqq), Creator of all pairs. So the Heart (Qalb) is pulled between Satan and the Angel. And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said regarding the Heart: 'There are two promptings (Lamatayn) in the Heart: a prompting from the Angel—promising good and confirming truth—so whoever finds that, let him know it is from Allah the Exalted and let him praise Allah; and a prompting from the enemy—promising evil, denying truth, and forbidding good—so whoever finds that, let him seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.' Then he recited His saying the Exalted: 'Satan threatens you with poverty and commands you to indecency' (2:268). And Al-Hasan said: 'They are but two thoughts (Hamman) that roam in the Heart: a thought from Allah the Exalted and a thought from the enemy. May Allah have mercy on a servant who pauses at his thought: if it is from Allah the Exalted, he proceeds with it; and if it is from his enemy, he fights it.' And for the pulling of the Heart between these two dominators, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'The Heart of the believer is between two fingers from the fingers of the Most Merciful.' Allah is exalted above having a finger composed of flesh, blood, and nerves divided by fingertips. But the spirit (Ruh) of the finger is swift turning and the ability to move and change, for you do not want your finger for its entity but for its action in turning and repeating, just as you undertake actions with your fingers. And Allah the Exalted does what He does by employing the Angel and Satan, and they are subjugated by His power in turning the Hearts, just as your fingers are subjugated to you in turning bodies, for example. And the Heart, by original nature (Fitra), is suitable for accepting the effects of the Angel and for accepting the effects of Satan with equal suitability; neither outweighs the other. Rather, one of the two sides outweighs by following caprice (Hawa) and indulging in desires (Shahawat) or turning away from them and opposing them. For if a human follows the requirement of anger and desire, the domination of Satan appears through caprice, and the Heart becomes the nest and mine of Satan because
16:98.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

16:98.arabic: ولا يمحو وسوسة الشيطان من القلب إلا ذكر ما سوى ما يوسوس به لأنه إذا خطر في القلب ذكر شيء انعدم منه ما كان فيه من قبل ولكن كل شيء سوى الله تعالى وسوى ما يتعلق به فيجوز أيضا أن يكون مجالا للشيطان وذكر الله هو الذي يؤمن جانبه ويعلم أنه ليس للشيطان فيه مجال ولا يعالج الشيء إلا بضده وضد جميع وساوس الشيطان ذكر الله بالاستعاذة والتبري عن الحول والقوة وهو معنى قولك أعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله العلي العظيم وذلك لا يقدر عليه إلا المتقون الغالب عليهم ذكر الله تعالى وإنما الشيطان
16:98.english: And the whispering (Waswasah) of the Satan (Shaytan) is not erased from the Heart (Qalb) except by the Remembrance (Dhikr) of other than what he whispers about, because when the Remembrance (Dhikr) of something occurs in the Heart (Qalb), what was previously in it disappears. But everything other than Allah the Exalted and other than what is related to Him may also be a field for the Satan (Shaytan), and the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah is what secures its side and makes known that there is no field for the Satan (Shaytan) in it. And a thing is not treated except by its opposite, and the opposite of all the whisperings (Waswasah) of the Satan (Shaytan) is the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah through seeking refuge (Isti'adha) and disavowal of power and strength, and that is the meaning of your saying: 'I seek refuge (A'udhu) in Allah from the accursed Satan (Shaytan) (Al-Rajim)', and 'There is no power nor strength except with Allah the Most High, the Most Great'. And that is not within the capability except of the God-fearing (Muttaqun) upon whom the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah the Exalted predominates. And indeed, the Satan (Shaytan) circulates around them in times of lapses (Falatat) by way of stealth. Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, those who fear Allah (Yattaquna) – when an impulse (Ta'if) from the Satan (Shaytan) touches them, they remember (Tadhakkara) and at once they have insight (Mubsirun).' And Mujahid said regarding the meaning of Allah the Exalted's saying: 'From the evil of the retreating whisperer (Al-Waswas Al-Khannas)', he said: 'He is spread out over the Heart (Qalb), so when Allah the Exalted is remembered (Dhikr), he retreats (Khannasa) and contracts, and when he is heedless (Ghafla), he spreads out over his Heart (Qalb).' So the chasing away between the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah the Exalted and the whispering (Waswasah) of the Satan (Shaytan) is like the chasing away between light (Nur) and darkness (Zulmah), and between night (Layl) and day (Nahar). And due to their opposition, Allah the Exalted said: 'Satan (Shaytan) has overcome them and made them forget the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah.' And Anas said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'Indeed, the Satan (Shaytan) places his snout (Khurtum) on the Heart (Qalb) of the son of Adam, so if he remembers (Dhikr) Allah the Exalted, he retreats (Khannasa), and if he forgets (Nasiya) Allah the Exalted, he swallows (Iltqama) his Heart (Qalb).'
16:98.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

16:98.arabic: وإذا قلت أعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم فاعلم أنه عدوك ومترصد لصرف قلبك عن الله عز وجل حسدا لك على مناجاتك مع الله عز وجل وسجودك له مع أنه لعن بسبب سجدة واحدة تركها ولم يوفق لها وأن استعاذتك بالله سبحانه منه بترك ما يحبه وتبديله بما يحب الله عز وجل لا بمجرد قولك فإن من قصده سبع أو عدو ليفترسه أو يقتله فقال أعوذ منك بذلك الحصن الحصين وهو ثابت على مكانه فإن ذلك لا ينفعه بل لا يعيذه إلا تبديل المكان فكذلك من يتبع الشهوات التي هي محاب الشيطان ومكاره الرحمن فلا يغنيه مجرد القول فليقترن قوله بالعزم على
16:98.english: And when you say 'I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan (Shaytan)', know that he is your enemy and lies in wait to divert your Heart (Qalb) from Allah the Exalted, out of envy toward you for your intimate conversation (Munajat) with Allah the Exalted and your prostration (Sujud) to Him, even though he was cursed due to a single prostration he abandoned and was not granted success in it. And your seeking refuge (Isti'adha) in Allah the Glorified from him is by abandoning what he loves and replacing it with what Allah the Exalted loves, not merely by your statement. For if one whom a predator or enemy intends to devour or kill says 'I seek refuge from you with that impregnable fortress' while remaining in his place, that will not benefit him; rather, nothing will grant him refuge except changing his location. Likewise, one who follows the desires (Shahawat) that are the pleasures of Satan and the displeasures of the Most Merciful (Al-Rahman) will not be helped by mere speech. So let his statement be accompanied by the determination (Al-'Azm) to seek refuge with the fortress of Allah the Exalted from the evil of Satan, and his fortress is 'There is no god but Allah (La ilaha illa Allah)', as He the Exalted said in what our Prophet (peace be upon him) reported: 'There is no god but Allah is my fortress, so whoever enters my fortress is safe from my punishment.' And the one who takes refuge in it has no object of worship except Allah the Glorified. As for one who takes his desire (Hawa) as his god, he is in the arena of Satan, not in the fortress of Allah the Exalted. And know that among his stratagems is to distract you in your prayer (Salah) with remembrance (Dhikr) of the Hereafter and planning good deeds to prevent you from understanding what you recite. Know that everything that distracts you from understanding the meanings of your recitation is whispering (Waswas). For the movement of the tongue is not the intended goal; rather, the intended goal is their meanings.
16:98.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

16:98.arabic: [23] حديث الأمر بالتعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم عند الغيظ متفق عليه من حديث سليمان بن صرد قال كنت جالسا مع النبي ﭬ ورجلان يستبان فأحدهما أحمر وجهه وانتفخت أوداجه الحديث وفيه لو قال أعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم لذهب عنه ما يجد فقالوا له إن النبي ﭬ قال تعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم الحديث.
16:98.english: [23] The hadith about the command to seek refuge with Allah from the Accursed Satan (Al-Shaytan Al-Rajim) during anger is agreed upon from the narration of Sulayman ibn Surad who said: I was sitting with the Prophet ﷺ and two men were insulting each other, and one of them had his face reddened and his veins swollen. The hadith contains: If he had said 'I seek refuge with Allah from the Accursed Satan (Al-Shaytan Al-Rajim)', what he was experiencing would have left him. So they said to him: Indeed the Prophet ﷺ said: Seek refuge with Allah from the Accursed Satan (Al-Shaytan Al-Rajim). The hadith.
16:98.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

16:98.arabic: وأما العمل فإن تقول بلسانك أعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم. هكذا أمر رسول الله ﷺ أن يقال عند الغيظ[23] وكان رسول الله ﷺ إذا غضبت عائشة أخذ بأنفها وقال "يا عويش قولي اللهم رب النبي محمد اغفر لي ذنبي وأذهب غيظ قلبي وأجرني من مضلات الفتن"[24] فيستحب أن تقول ذلك، فإن لم يزل بذلك فاجلس إن كنت قائماً واضجع إن كنت جالساً واقرب من الأرض التي منها خلقت لتعرف بذلك ذل نفسك، واطلب بالجلوس والاضجاع السكون فإن سبب الغضب الحرارة وسبب الحرارة الحركة. فقد قال رسول الله ﷺ "إن الغضب جمرة توقد في القلب"[25] ألم تروا إ
16:98.english: As for the action, then say with your tongue: 'I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan (Shaytan).' Thus did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) command that it be said during anger [23]. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), when Aisha became angry, would take her by the nose and say: 'O little Aisha, say: O Allah, Lord of the Prophet Muhammad, forgive me my sin, remove the anger of my heart (Qalb), and deliver me from misleading trials (Fitnah)' [24]. It is recommended to say that. If it does not cease with that, then sit if you are standing, and lie down if you are sitting, and draw near to the earth from which you were created, so that you may recognize thereby the lowliness of your soul (Nafs). And seek through sitting and lying down tranquility, for the cause of anger is heat, and the cause of heat is movement. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Anger is an ember kindled in the heart (Qalb)' [25]. Have you not seen the swelling of his veins and the redness of his eyes? So if any of you finds something of that, then if he is standing, let him sit, and if he is sitting, let him lie down. If it does not cease with that, then let him perform ablution (Wudu) with cold water or bathe, for fire is not extinguished except by water. Indeed, he (peace be upon him) said: 'When one of you becomes angry, let him perform ablution (Wudu) with water, for indeed anger is from fire' [26]. And in a narration: 'Anger is from Satan (Shaytan), and Satan (Shaytan) was created from fire, and fire is only extinguished by water, so when one of you becomes angry, let him perform ablution (Wudu).' And Ibn Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'And when you become angry, be silent' [27]. And Abu Huraira said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), when he became angry while standing, would sit, and when he became angry while sitting, would lie down, and his anger would depart [28].
16:98.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

16:102.arabic: ثم أخبر أن له عبدين يحب أحدهما واسمه جبريل وروح القدس والأمين وهو عنده محبوب مطاع أمين مكين ويبغض الآخر واسمه إبليس وهو اللعين المنظر إلى يوم الدين، ثم أحال الإرشاد إلى جبريل فقال تعالى: ﴿ قل نزله روح القدس من ربك بالحق ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ يلقى الروح من أمره على من يشاء من عباده ﴾ {} وأحال الإغواء على إبليس فقال تعالى: ﴿ ليضلّ عن سبيله ﴾ {} والإغواء هو استيقاف العباد دون بلوغ غاية الحكمة فانظر كيف نسبه إلى العبد الذى غضب عليه والإرشاد سياقه لهم إلى الغاية فانظر كيف نسبه إلى العبد الذى أحبه وعندك
16:102.english: Then He informed that He has two servants: He loves one of them, and his name is Jibril and the Spirit of Holiness (Ruh al-Qudus) and the Trustworthy (Al-Amin), and he is with Him beloved, obeyed, trustworthy, and firmly established; and He detests the other, and his name is Iblis, and he is the accursed one, granted respite until the Day of Recompense (Yawm al-Din). Then He attributed guidance to Jibril, so the Exalted said: 'Say: The Spirit of Holiness (Ruh al-Qudus) has brought it down from your Lord with truth' {} and He said: 'He casts the Spirit (Ruh) from His command upon whom He wills of His servants' {} and He attributed misguidance to Iblis, so He said: 'To lead astray from His path' {} and misguidance is preventing the servants from reaching the ultimate wisdom. So see how He attributed it to the servant upon whom He is angry, and guidance is leading them to the ultimate goal, so see how He attributed it to the servant whom He loved. And you have in custom an example for it: if a king needs someone to give him drink and someone to perform cupping and clean the courtyard of his house from filth, and he has two servants, then he does not assign for cupping and cleaning except the ugliest and most base of them, and he does not entrust carrying the drink and perfume except to the best, most complete, and most beloved of them to him. And it is not fitting for you to say: 'This is my action, and was not his action without my action?' For you have erred when you attributed that to yourself; rather, it is He who directed your motivation to specify the disliked action with the disliked person and the beloved action with the beloved person, completing justice. For His justice (Adl) is sometimes accomplished through matters in which you have no involvement, and sometimes it is accomplished in you, for you are also from His actions. So your motivation, your capability, your knowledge, your action, and all the causes of your movements in expression are His action which He arranged with justice, an arrangement from which balanced actions issue, except that you see only yourself, so you think that what appears upon you in the world of witnessing (Alam al-Shahadah) has no cause.
16:102.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

16:105.arabic: وعن عبد الله بن جراد قال: سألت رسول الله ﭬ فقلت: يا رسول الله هل يزني المؤمن؟ قال "قد يكون ذلك" قال: يا نبي الله هل يكذب المؤمن؟ قال "لا" ثم أتبعها ﭬ بقول الله تعالى "إنما يفتري الكذب الذين لا يؤمنون بآيات الله"
16:105.english: And from Abdullah ibn Jarad, he said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and I said: O Messenger of Allah, does the believer (Mu'min) commit adultery? He said: "That may occur." He said: O Prophet of Allah, does the believer (Mu'min) lie? He said: "No." Then he (peace be upon him) followed it with the saying of Allah the Exalted: "Only those who do not believe in the signs (Ayat) of Allah fabricate falsehood."
16:105.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

16:107.arabic: فمهما كان القلب الغالب عليه عند الموت حب الأهل والولد والمال والمسكن والعقار والرفقاء والأصحاب فهذا رجل محابه كلها في الدنيا فالدنيا جنته إذ الجنة عبارة عن البقعة الجامعة لجميع المحاب فموته خروج من الجنة وحيلولة بينه وبين ما يشتهيه ولا يخفى حال من يحال بينه وبين ما يشتهيه فإذا لم يكن له محبوب سوى الله تعالى وسوى ذكره ومعرفته والفكر فيه والدنيا وعلائقها شاغلة له عن المحبوب فالدنيا إذن سجنه لأن السجن عبارة عن البقعة المانعة للمحبوس عن الاسترواح إلى محابه فموته قوم على محبوبه وخلاص من السجن ولا يخف
16:107.english: Whenever the Heart (Qalb) that dominates at the time of death is love of family, children, wealth, residence, property, companions, and friends, then this is a man whose loves are all in the worldly life (Dunya). Thus, the worldly life is his paradise, since paradise is an expression for the place that gathers all loves. His death is an exit from paradise and a barrier between him and what he desires, and the state of one who is barred between him and what he desires is not hidden. If he has no beloved except Allah, the Exalted, and except His Remembrance (Dhikr), knowledge of Him, and contemplation of Him, and the worldly life and its attachments distract him from the Beloved, then the worldly life is his prison, because prison is an expression for the place that prevents the imprisoned from finding relief in his loves. His death is a standing before his Beloved and a liberation from prison, and the state of one who escapes from prison and is left between him and his Beloved without any barrier or disturbance is not hidden. This is the first thing that everyone who departs from the worldly life encounters immediately after his death from reward and punishment, apart from what Allah has prepared for His righteous servants that no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived, and apart from what Allah, the Exalted, has prepared for those who preferred the worldly life over the Hereafter and were pleased with it and felt secure in it—from shackles, chains, fetters, and various kinds of disgrace and punishment. So we ask Allah, the Exalted, to cause us to die as Muslims and join us with the righteous, and there is no hope in the answer to this supplication except by acquiring the love of Allah, the Exalted, and there is no way to it except by removing the love of other than Him from the Heart (Qalb) and cutting off attachments to everything other than Allah, the Exalted, from status, wealth, and homeland. Thus, it is best to supplicate with what our Prophet ﷺ supplicated when he said: 'O Allah, grant me Your love and the love of those who love You and the love of what brings me closer to Your love, and make Your love more beloved to me than cold water.' The purpose is that the dominance of hope at the time of death is better because it is more conducive to love, and the dominance of fear before death is better because it burns the fire of desires and suppresses the love of the worldly life from the Heart (Qalb). Therefore, he ﷺ said: 'Let none of you die except while having good thoughts of his Lord,' and Allah, the Exalted, said: 'I am as My servant thinks of Me, so let him think of Me what he wills.' And when the death of Sulayman al-Taymi approached, he said to his son: 'O my son, tell me the leniencies and remind me of hope so that I meet Allah with good thoughts of Him.' Likewise, when the death of al-Thawri approached and his distress intensified, he gathered scholars around him to give him hope, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah be pleased with him, said to his son at the time of death: 'Remind me of the reports that contain hope and good thoughts.' The intended purpose of all that is that Allah, the Exalted, makes beloved...
16:107.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

16:107.arabic: وإنما تكثر الحيات والعقارب في قبور الأغنياء الذين استحبوا الحياة الدنيا على الآخرة وفرحوا بها واطمأنوا إليها فهذه مقامات الإيمان في حيات القبر وعقاربه وفي سائر أنواع عذابه.
16:107.english: And indeed, the snakes and scorpions multiply in the graves of the wealthy who preferred the worldly life (Al-Hayat Al-Dunya) over the Hereafter (Al-Akhirah) and rejoiced in it and found tranquility in it. These are the stations of faith (Iman) in the snakes of the grave and its scorpions and in all other types of its punishment.
16:107.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

16:109.arabic: رغبوا في عرض الدنيا ورفعتها وآثروها على الآخرة، وأدلوا الدين للدنيا فهم في العاجل عار وشين، وفي الآخرة هم الخاسرون أو يعفو الكريم بفضله.
16:109.english: They desired the fleeting pleasure (عرض) of this world and its elevation, and preferred it over the Hereafter (الآخرة), and they sold the religion (الدين) for this world, so they are in the immediate [life] disgrace and shame, and in the Hereafter they are the losers (الخاسرون) or the Generous One (الكريم) may pardon by His grace.
16:109.book_title: Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth
16:109.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

16:109.arabic: رغبوا في عرض الدنيا ورفعتها وآثروها على الآخرة وأذلوا الدين للدنيا، فهم في العاجل عار وشين وفي الآخرة هم لخاسرون.
16:109.english: They desired the fleeting enjoyment (عرض) of this world and its elevation, and preferred it over the Hereafter (الآخرة), and humiliated the religion (الدين) for the sake of this world (الدنيا). So they are in the immediate [life] disgrace and shame, and in the Hereafter (الآخرة) they are the losers (الخاسرون).
16:109.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

16:111.arabic: وأتى هشام برجل بلغه عنه أمر فلما أقيم بين يديه جعل يتكلم بحجته فقال له هشام: وتتكلم أيضاً؟ فقال الرجل: يا أمير المؤمنين قال الله عز وجل "يوم تأتي كل نفس تجادل عن نفسها" أفنجادل الله تعالى ولا نتكلم بين يديك كلاماً؟ قال هشام: بلى ويحك تكلم.
16:111.english: And Hisham was brought a man about whom something had reached him. When he was placed before him, he began to speak with his argument. Hisham said to him: 'And you still speak?' The man said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, Allah the Exalted said: "On the Day when every Soul (Nafs) will come disputing for itself." Shall we dispute with Allah the Exalted and not speak before you with speech?' Hisham said: 'Yes, woe to you, speak.'
16:111.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

16:111.arabic: وستجد كل نفس ما عملت من سوء أو خير محضرا عند الله ولو في فلتة خاطر أو فلتة ناظر من غير ظلم وجور فما الله بظلام للعبيد
16:111.english: And every soul (Nafs) will find what it has done of evil or good present before Allah, even if in a fleeting thought (Khatir) or a fleeting glance (Nazir), without injustice (Zulm) or oppression (Jawr), for Allah is not unjust (Zalim) to His servants.
16:111.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

16:120.arabic: وأما الأمة فتطلق على ثمانية أوجه الأمة الجماعة كقوله تعالى ﴿ وجد عليه أمة من الناس يسقون ﴾ {} وأتباع الأنبياء كقولك عن أمة محمد ﭬ، ورجل جامع للخير يقتدي به كقوله تعالى ﴿ إن إبراهيم كان أمة قانتا لله ﴾ {} والأمة الدين كقوله عز وجل ﴿ إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة ﴾ {} والأمة الحين والزمان كقوله عز وجل ﴿ إلى أمة معدودة ﴾ {} وقوله عز وجل ﴿ وادكر بعد أمة ﴾ {} والأمة القامة يقال فلان حسن الأمة أي القامة، وأمة رجل منفرد بدين لا يشركه فيه أحد قال ﭬ: (يبعث زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل أمة وحده[57]) والأمة الأم يقال هذ
16:120.english: And as for 'Ummah' (الأمة), it is applied in eight aspects: The 'Ummah' as a community, as in His saying, the Exalted: 'He found there a community (Ummah) of people watering' (Quran 28:23); and the followers of the prophets, as you say regarding the 'Ummah' of Muhammad (peace be upon him); and a man comprehensive of good who is followed, as in His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, Abraham was a community (Ummah), devoutly obedient (Qanitan) to Allah, a true monotheist (Hanifan), and he was not of the polytheists' (Quran 16:120); and the 'Ummah' as religion, as in His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, we found our fathers upon a community (Ummah)' (Quran 43:22); and the 'Ummah' as a time or period, as in His saying, the Exalted: 'Until a numbered community (Ummah)' (Quran 11:8) and His saying, the Exalted: 'And remember after a community (Ummah)' (Quran 12:45); and the 'Ummah' as stature, it is said: 'So-and-so has a good 'Ummah' meaning stature; and the 'Ummah' of a man isolated in a religion with no one sharing him in it, he (peace be upon him) said: 'Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Nufayl will be resurrected as a community (Ummah) alone' (Hadith); and the 'Ummah' as mother, it is said: 'This is the 'Ummah' of Zayd' meaning the mother of Zayd.
16:120.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

16:123.arabic:
تستجيب لي أخرجه أبو منصور الديلمي في مسند الفردوس من حديث ابن عباس
    اللهم ابعثنا في أحب الساعات إليك حتى نذكرك فتذكرنا ونسألك فتعطينا وندعوك
    فتستجيب لنا ونستغفرك فتغفر لنا وإسناده ضعيف وهو معروف من قول حبيب الطائي
                                          كما رواه ابن أبي الدنيا في الدعاء.
   [230]  حديث القول إذا استيقظ من منامه الحمد لله الذي أحيانا بعد ما أماتنا
              وإليه النشور أخرجه البخاري من حديث حذيفة ومسلم من حديث البراء.
  [231]  حديث أصبحنا وأصبح الملك لله والعظمة وال
16:123.english: [232] Hadith: We have awakened upon the natural disposition (Fitrah) of Islam and the word of sincerity (Kalimat al-Ikhlas) and the religion of our Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the way (Millah) of our father Abraham, upright (Hanifan) and he was not of the polytheists (Mushrikin). Al-Nasa'i transmitted it in Al-Yawm wa al-Laylah from the narration of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza with a sound chain, and Ahmad transmitted it from the narration of Ibn Abza from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, raised to the Prophet.
16:123.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication

16:125.arabic: ولم تزل الرسل صلوات الله عليهم يحاجون المنكرين ويجادلونهم قال تعالى: ﴿ وجادلهم بالتي هي أحسن ﴾ {} فالصحابة رضي الله عنهم أيضا كانوا يحاجون المنكرين ويجادلون ولكن عند الحاجة وكانت الحاجة إليه قليلة في زمانهم وأول من سن دعوة المبتدعة بالمجادلة إلى الحق علي ابن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه إذ بعث ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما إلى الخوارج فكلمهم فقال ما تنقمون على إمامكم قالوا قاتل ولم يسب ولم يغنم فقال ذلك في قتال الكفار أرأيتم لو سببت عائشة رضي الله عنها في سهم أحدكم أكنتم تستحلون منها ما تستحلون من ملككم وهي
16:125.english: And the Messengers, prayers of Allah be upon them, never ceased to argue with the deniers and debate with them. Allah the Exalted said: 'And debate with them in that which is best (bil-latī hiya aḥsanu).' So the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, also used to argue with the deniers and debate, but only when necessary, and the need for it was little in their time. The first to establish calling the innovators to the truth through debate was Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, when he sent Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, to the Khawarij and he spoke to them. He said: 'What do you find fault with regarding your Imam?' They said: 'He fought but did not take captives nor spoils.' He said: 'That was in fighting the disbelievers. Tell me, if Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, were among your spoils, would you consider lawful from her what you consider lawful from your property, while she is your mother according to the clear text of the Book?' They said: 'No.' So two thousand of them returned to obedience through his debate.
16:125.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Foundations of Belief'

16:125.arabic: وقال تعالى: ﴿ومن أحسن قولا ممن دعا إلى الله وعمل صالحا﴾ ( سورة فصلت: الآية 33) وقال تعالى: ﴿ادع إلى سبيل ربك بالحكمة والموعظة الحسنة﴾ ( سورة النحل: الآية 125) وقال تعالى: ﴿ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة﴾( سورة البقرة: الآية 129و الآية:151، وسورة آل عمران، الآية:164 وسورة الجمعة، الآية:2.).
16:125.english: And He (Exalted is He) said: 'And who is better in speech than one who invites to Allah and does righteous work' (Surah Fussilat: Verse 33). And He (Exalted is He) said: 'Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good admonition' (Surah An-Nahl: Verse 125). And He (Exalted is He) said: 'And teaches them the Book and the Wisdom' (Surah Al-Baqarah: Verse 129 and Verse:151, and Surah Al-Imran, Verse:164 and Surah Al-Jumu'ah, Verse:2.).
16:125.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Book of Knowledge'

16:126.arabic: وقال تعالى: ﴿ وإن عاقبتم فعاقبوا بمثل ما عوقبتم به ولئن صبرتم لهو خير الصابرين ﴾ {}. وقال ﭬ: (صل من قطعك وأعط من حرمك واعف عمن ظلمك[25]) ورأيت في الإنجيل قال عيسى بن مريم عليه السلام لقد قيل لكم من قبل إن السن بالسن والأنف بالأنف وأنا أقول لكم لا تقاوموا بالشر بل من ضرب خدك الأيمن فحول إليه الخد الأيسر ومن اخذ رداءك فاعطه ازارك ومن سخرك لتسير معه ميلا فسر معه ميلين وكل ذلك أمر بالصبر على الاذى، فالصبر على اذى الناس من أعلى مراتب الصبر لانه يتعاون فيه باعث الدين وباعث الشهوة والغضب جميعا.
16:126.english: And Allah the Exalted said: 'And if you retaliate, then retaliate with the like of that with which you were afflicted. But if you are patient, it is indeed better for the patient ones.' And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Maintain ties with the one who cuts you off, give to the one who deprives you, and pardon the one who wrongs you.' And I saw in the Gospel that Jesus son of Mary (peace be upon him) said: 'It was said to you before: An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth, but I say to you: Do not resist evil, but whoever strikes your right cheek, turn to him the other also; and whoever takes your cloak, give him your tunic; and whoever compels you to go one mile, go with him two.' And all of that commands patience upon harm, for patience upon the harm of people is from the highest levels of patience because in it the motivator of religion and the motivator of desire and anger all cooperate.
16:126.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

16:128.arabic: وهم أربعون صديقاً أو ثلاثون رجلاً قلوبهم على مثل يقين إبراهيم خليل الرحمن عليه السلام لا يموت الرجل منهم حتى يكون الله قد أنشأ من يخلفه، واعلم يا أخي أنهم لا يلعنون شيئاً ولا يؤذونه ولا يحقرونه ولا يتطاولون عليه ولا يحسدون أحداً ولا يحصرون على الدنيا، هم أطيب الناس خيراً وألينهم عريكة وأسخاهم نفساً، علامتهم السخاء وسجيتهم البشاشة وصفتهم السلامة، ليسوا اليوم في خشية وغداً في غفلة ولكن مدامين على حالهم الظاهر وهم فيما بينهم وبين ربهم لا تدركهم الرياح العواصف ولا الخيل المجراة، قلوبهم تصعد ارتياحاً
16:128.english: And they are forty righteous ones or thirty men whose hearts (Qulub) are upon the certainty (Yaqin) like Ibrahim, the intimate friend (Khalil) of the Most Merciful, peace be upon him. No man among them dies until Allah has raised up one to succeed him. And know, O my brother, that they do not curse anything, nor harm it, nor belittle it, nor act arrogantly toward it, nor envy anyone, nor are they preoccupied with the worldly life (Dunya). They are the best of people in goodness, the most gentle in disposition, and the most generous in soul (Nafs). Their sign is generosity, their nature is cheerfulness, and their attribute is safety. They are not today in fear and tomorrow in heedlessness, but rather they are constant in their outward state, and between them and their Lord, the raging winds and galloping horses do not reach them. Their hearts ascend with delight to Allah and longing for Him, and they are foremost in racing toward good deeds. "Those are the party of Allah. Indeed, the party of Allah are the successful." The narrator said: So I said: O Abu al-Darda, I have not heard of a description more difficult for me than that description, and how can I attain it? He said: Between you and being in its broadest scope is nothing except that you hate the worldly life (Dunya). For if you hate the worldly life, you turn to the love (Hubb) of the Hereafter (Akhirah), and according to the measure of your love for the Hereafter, you abstain from the worldly life, and according to that measure, you perceive what benefits you. And when Allah knows from a servant (Abd) good seeking, He pours upon him correctness and surrounds him with protection. And know, O son of my brother, that this is in the Book of Allah, the Exalted, the Revealed: "Indeed, Allah is with those who fear (Ittaqaw) and those who are doers of good (Muhsinun)." Yahya ibn Kathir said: So we reflected on that, and the delighters have not delighted in anything like the love (Hubb) of Allah and seeking His pleasure. O Allah, make us among the lovers of those who love You, O Lord of the worlds, for none is suitable for Your love except whom You have approved. And may Allah bless our master Muhammad and his family and companions and grant them peace.
16:128.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

17:12.arabic: فلا تظنن أن المقصود من سير الشمس والقمر بحسبان منظوم مرتب ومن خلق الظل والنور والنجوم أن يستعان بها على أمور الدنيا بل لتعرف بها مقادير الأوقات فتشتغل فيها بالطاعات والتجارة للدار الآخرة يدلك عليه قوله تعالى: ﴿ وهو الذي جعل الليل والنهار خلفة لمن أراد أن يذكر أو أراد شكورا ﴾ {} أي يخلف أحدهما الآخر ليتدارك في أحدهما ما فات في الآخر وبين أن ذلك للذكر والشكر لا غير وقال تعالى: ﴿ وجعلنا الليل والنهار آيتين فمحونا آية الليل وجعلنا آية النهار مبصرة لتبتغوا فضلا من ربكم ولتعلموا عدد السنين والحساب ﴾ {
17:12.english: Do not think that the purpose of the sun and moon moving in a precise, ordered calculation, and the creation of shadow and light and stars, is to be aided by them in worldly matters. Rather, it is to know by them the measures of times so that you may occupy yourself in them with acts of obedience (Taa'aat) and trade for the Abode of the Hereafter (Al-Daar Al-Aakhirah). This is indicated to you by His saying, the Exalted: 'And He is the One who made the night and the day successive for whoever desires to remember (Yadhkur) or desires to be grateful (Shakooran).' {} Meaning, one of them succeeds the other so that what was missed in one may be made up in the other, and He clarified that this is for remembrance (Dhikr) and gratitude (Shukr) only, and nothing else. And He said, the Exalted: 'And We made the night and the day two signs (Aayatayn). Then We erased the sign of the night and made the sign of the day seeing (Mubsiratan), that you may seek bounty (Fadlan) from your Lord and that you may know the number of years and the calculation (Al-Hisab).' {} And indeed, the bounty (Al-Fadl) sought is the reward (Al-Thawaab) and forgiveness (Al-Maghfirah), and we ask Allah for good success in what pleases Him.
17:12.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

17:14.arabic: وأول ما ينكشف له ما يضره وينفعه من حسناته وسيئاته وقد كان ذلك مسطورا في كتاب مطوي في سر قلبه وكان يشغله عن الاطلاع عليه شواغل الدنيا فإذا انقطعت الشواغل انكشف له جميع أعماله فلا ينظر إلى سيئه إلا ويتحسر عليها تحسرا يؤثر أن يخوض غمرة النار للخلاص من تلك الحسرة وعبد ذلك يقال له: ﴿ كفى بنفسك اليوم عليك حسيبا ﴾ {} وينكشف كل ذلك عند انقطاع النفس وقبل الدفن وتشتعل فيه نيران الفراق أعنى فراق ما كان يطمئن إليه من هذه الدنيا الفانية دون ما أراد منها لأجل الزاد والبلغة فإن من طلب الزاد للبلغة فإذا بلغ الم
17:14.english: And the first thing that is unveiled to him is what harms and benefits him from his good deeds and bad deeds, and that had been inscribed in a book folded in the secret of his heart (Qalb), and the distractions of the world (Dunya) were occupying him from observing it. So when the distractions are cut off, all his actions are unveiled to him, so he does not look at his evil except and regrets it with a regret that makes him prefer to plunge into the depths of the Fire to escape from that regret. And to that servant (Abd) it is said: 'Read your book; sufficient is yourself today as a reckoner against you' (Quran 17:14). And all that is unveiled at the cutting off of the breath (Nafs) and before burial, and the fires of separation ignite in him—meaning separation from what he used to find tranquility in from this perishing world (Dunya), except what he intended from it for the purpose of provision (Zad) and sufficiency (Balgha). For whoever seeks provision for sufficiency, when he reaches the destination, he rejoices at parting with the remainder of the provision, since he did not want the provision for its own sake. And this is the state of one who did not take from the world except according to necessity and wished that his necessity would be cut off so he could be free from it—he has obtained what he wished and become free from it. And these are types of punishment and great pains that assail him before burial.
17:14.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

17:14.arabic: قال أنس رضى الله عنه: (كنا مع رسول الله ﭬ فضحك ثم قال أتدرون مم أضحك قلنا الله ورسوله أعلم قال من مخاطبة العبد ربه يقول يا رب الم تجرنى من الظلم قال يقول بلى قال فيقول فإنى لا أجيز على نفسى إلا شاهدا منى فيقول كفى بنفسك اليوم عليك حسيبا وبالكرام الكاتبين شهودا قال فيختم على فيه ويقال لأركانه انطقى قال فتنطق بأعماله ثم يخلى بينه وبين الكلام فيقول لأعضائه بعدا لكن وسحقا فعنكن كنت أنا ضل[158])
17:14.english: Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: (We were with the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, and he laughed, then said: Do you know why I laughed? We said: Allah and His Messenger know best. He said: From the conversation of the servant (al-'abd) with his Lord (Rabb). He says: O Lord (Rabb), did You not save me from injustice (al-zulm)? He says: Yes. He says: Then I do not accept upon myself except a witness from me. He says: Sufficient is your Soul (Nafs) today against you as a reckoner (hasib) and the noble recorders as witnesses. He said: Then his mouth is sealed and it is said to his limbs: Speak! He said: So they speak with his deeds, then he is left between him and the speech, and he says to his limbs: Away with you and perish, for through you I was astray[158]).
17:14.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

17:14.arabic: وفي هذه القيامة يكون العبد وحده وعندها يقال ﴿ ولقد جئتمونا فرادى كما خلقناكم أول مرة ﴾ {} وفيها يقال ﴿ كفى بنفسك اليوم عليك حسيبا ﴾ {} أما في القيامة الكبرى الجامعة لكافة الخلائق فلا يكون وحده بل ربما يحاسب على ملأ من الخلق وفيها يساق المتقون إلى الجنة والمجرمون إلى النار زمرا لا آحادا
17:14.english: And in this resurrection, the servant (Al-'Abd) is alone, and at that time it is said: 'And you have come to Us alone as We created you the first time' (Quran 6:94). And in it, it is said: 'Read your book; sufficient is your soul (Nafs) today as a reckoner (Hasib) over you' (Quran 17:14). As for the greater resurrection (Al-Qiyamah Al-Kubra) that gathers all creation, he is not alone, but perhaps he is accounted for in the presence of the creation, and in it, the righteous (Al-Muttaqun) are driven to Paradise and the criminals (Al-Mujrimun) to the Fire in groups, not as individuals.
17:14.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

17:14.arabic: ومعنى قوله تعالى: (اقرأ كتابك كفى بنفسك اليوم عليك حسيبا( (الاسراء: 14) ومعنى قوله تعالى: (وإن الدار الآخرة لهي الحيوان لو كانوا يعلمون( (العنكبوت: 64) ومعنى لقاء الله عز وجل والنظر إلى وجهه الكريم، ومعنى القرب منه والنزول في جواره، ومعنى حصول السعادة بمرافقة الملأ الأعلى ومقارنة الملائكة والنبيين، ومعنى تفاوت درجات أهل الجنان حتى يرى بعضهم البعض كما يرى الكوكب الدري في جوف السماء إلى غير ذلك مما يطول تفصيله.
17:14.english: And the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: 'Read your book; sufficient is your Soul (Nafs) today against you as a reckoner' (Al-Isra: 14), and the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: 'And indeed, the Home of the Hereafter is truly the life, if they only knew' (Al-Ankabut: 64), and the meaning of meeting Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and looking at His Noble Face, and the meaning of proximity to Him and descending in His neighborhood, and the meaning of attaining happiness by accompanying the Highest Assembly and being in the company of the angels and the prophets, and the meaning of the varying degrees of the people of Paradise until some of them see each other as the brilliant star is seen in the depth of the sky, and other than that which would take long to detail.
17:14.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

17:15.arabic: فلا تتفكر فيما هو ممكن لغيرك بل فيما هو مخوف في حقك، فإنه لا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى، وعذاب غيرك لا يخفف شيئاً من عذابك، فإذا تفكرت في هذا الخطر كان عندك شغل شاغل عن التكبر وعن أن ترى نفسك فوق غيرك.
17:15.english: So do not contemplate what is possible for others, but rather what is feared in your own right, for indeed no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another, and the punishment of another does not alleviate anything from your punishment. If you contemplate this danger, you will have an all-engrossing preoccupation from arrogance and from seeing your soul (Nafs) above others.
17:15.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

17:15.arabic: فالتقوى فرض عين فلا يجزه فيه والد عن ولده شيئاً وكذا العكس، وعند الله جزاء التقوى "يوم يفر المرء من أخيه وأمه وأبيه" إلا على سبيل الشفاعة لمن لم يشتد غضب الله عليه فيأذن في الشفاعة له - كما سبق في كتاب الكبر والعجب. فإن قلت: فأين الغلط في قول العصاة والفجار إن الله كريم وإنا نرجو رحمته ومغفرته، وقد قال أنا عند ظن عبدي بي فليظن بي خيراً، فما هذا إلا كلام صحيح مقبول الظاهر في القلوب؟ فاعلم أن الشيطان لا يغوي الإنسان إلا بكلام مقبول الظاهر مردود الباطن، ولولا حسن ظاهره لما انخدعت به القلوب، ولكن ال
17:15.english: Piety (Taqwa) is an individual obligation (Fard 'Ayn), so a parent cannot fulfill it on behalf of their child in any way, and likewise the reverse. With Allah (God) is the reward of piety (Taqwa) "On the Day when a man will flee from his brother, his mother, and his father" except through intercession for those upon whom Allah's wrath has not intensified, so He permits intercession for them - as previously mentioned in the Book of Arrogance and Vanity. If you say: Then where is the error in the statement of the sinners and transgressors that Allah is Generous (Karim) and we hope for His mercy and forgiveness, and He has said 'I am as My servant thinks of Me, so let him think good of Me'? This is nothing but speech that is correct and acceptable in appearance to the hearts (Qulub). Know that Satan (Shaytan) does not mislead a human except with speech that is acceptable in appearance but rejected in its inner meaning (Batin), and were it not for the goodness of its outward appearance, hearts (Qulub) would not be deceived by it. But the Prophet ﷺ uncovered this by saying: 'The intelligent one is he who holds his soul (Nafs) accountable and works for what comes after death, and the fool is he who follows his soul's (Nafs) desires (Hawa) and makes wishes upon Allah.' This is making wishes upon Allah the Exalted, but Satan changed its name and called it: hope (Rajaa'), until he deceived the ignorant with it. And Allah has explained hope (Rajaa') by saying: 'Indeed, those who have believed and those who have emigrated and striven in the cause of Allah - those hope (Yarjoon) for the mercy of Allah.' Meaning that hope (Rajaa') is more fitting for them. And this is because He mentioned that "Whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] his soul (Nafs). And whoever errs only errs against it. And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And never would We punish until We sent a messenger."
17:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

17:15.arabic: وقول القائل إن الولد ربما لم يكن صالحا لا يؤثر فإنه مؤمن والصلاح هو الغالب على أولاد ذوي الدين لا سيما إذا عزم على تربيته وحمله على الصلاح وبالجملة دعاء المؤمن لأبويه مفيد برا كان أو فاجرا فهو مثاب على دعواته وحسناته فإنه من كسبه وغير مؤاخذ بسيئاته فإنه لا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى ولذلك قال تعالى ألحقنا بهم ذرياتهم وما ألتناهم من عملهم من شيء أي ما نقصناهم من أعمالهم وجعلنا أولادهم مزيدا في إحسانهم.
17:15.english: And the statement of the one who says that the child might not be righteous does not affect, for he is a believer, and righteousness is predominant among the children of people of religion, especially if he resolves to raise him and compel him to righteousness. And in summary, the supplication of the believer for his parents is beneficial, whether they are righteous or wicked, for he is rewarded for his supplications and good deeds, as they are from his earning, and he is not held accountable for their evil deeds, for 'no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another' (la taziru waziratun wizra ukhra). And therefore, Allah the Exalted said: 'We will join them with their descendants, and We will not deprive them of anything of their deeds' (Quran 52:21), meaning: We did not diminish them from their deeds, and We made their children an increase in their good deeds.
17:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

17:15.arabic: وأقيم عليه شاهدين إبراهيم وموسى ثم تلا "أم لم ينبأ بما في صحف موسى وإبراهيم الذي وفى أن لا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى" فقال زياد خلوا سبيله، هذا رجل قد لقن حجته، وقيل مكتوب في الإنجيل. من استغفر لمن ظلمه فقد هزم الشيطان.
17:15.english: And I will establish upon it two witnesses, Ibrahim (Abraham) and Musa (Moses), then he recited: 'Or has he not been informed of what is in the scrolls of Musa (Moses) and Ibrahim (Abraham) who fulfilled [his covenant]? That no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another.' So Ziyad said: Release him, this man has been taught his argument, and it is said written in the Injil (Gospel): Whoever seeks forgiveness for one who wronged him has defeated the Shaytan (Satan).
17:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on the outer and inner dimensions of worship, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

17:21.arabic: وبحر هذه المعرفة - أعني معرفة العجائب صنع الله تعالى - بحر لا ساحل له، فلا جرم تفاوت أهل المعرفة في الحب لا حصر له، ومما يتفاوت بسببه الحب اختلاف الأسباب الخمسة التي ذكرناها للحب، فإنه من يحب الله مثلاً لكونه محسناً إليه منعماً عليه ولم يحبه لذاته ضعفت محبته، إذ تتغير بتغير الإحسان فلا يكون حبه في حالة البلاء كحبه في حالة الرضا والنعماء. وأما من يحبه لذاته ولأنه مستحق للحب بسبب كماله وجماله ومجده وعظمته فإنه لا يتفاوت حبه بتفاوت الإحسان إليه. فهذا وأمثاله وهو سبب تفاوت الناس في المحبة. والتفاوت
17:21.english: And this ocean of knowledge - I mean knowledge of the wonders of Allah's creation - is an ocean without a shore, so it is no wonder that the disparity among people of knowledge in love has no limit. Among what causes disparity in love is the difference in the five reasons for love that we mentioned. For example, whoever loves Allah because He is beneficent to him and bestows favors upon him, and does not love Him for His essence, his love becomes weak, since it changes with the change of beneficence, so his love in the state of tribulation is not like his love in the state of contentment and blessings. As for whoever loves Him for His essence and because He is deserving of love due to His perfection, beauty, glory, and majesty, then his love does not vary with the variation of beneficence to him. This and its like is the cause of disparity among people in love. And the disparity in love is the cause for disparity in the happiness of the Hereafter. Therefore, Allah the Exalted said: "And for the Hereafter are greater degrees and greater preference."
17:21.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

17:21.arabic: وما أعظم الفرق بينهما وما أعظم الغبن على من يخسر حظه من ذلك وللآخرة أكبر درجات وأكبر تفضيلا. بيان شواهد الشرع على صحة طريق أهل التصوف في اكتساب المعرفة لا من التعلم ولا من الطريق المعتاد أعلم أن من انكشف له شيء ولو الشيء اليسير بطريق الإلهام والوقوع في القلب من حيث لا يدري فقد صار عارفا بصحة الطريق ومن لم يدرك ذلك من نفسه قط فينبغي أن يؤمن به فإن درجة المعرفة فيه عزيزة جدا ويشهد لذلك شواهد الشرع والتجارب والحكايات أما الشواهد فقوله تعالى والذين جاهدوا فينا لنهدينهم سبلنا فكل حكمة تظهر من القلب ب
17:21.english: And how great is the difference between them, and how great is the loss upon he who forfeits his share of that. And for the Hereafter (Al-Akhirah) are greater degrees and greater preference. Explanation of the evidences of the Sacred Law (Shari'ah) on the validity of the path of the people of Sufism (Ahl al-Tasawwuf) in acquiring knowledge (Ma'rifah) not from learning nor from the customary path. Know that whoever has something unveiled to him, even the slightest thing, through the path of inspiration (Ilham) and occurrence in the heart (Qalb) from where he does not know, has become a knower (Arif) of the validity of the path. And whoever never perceives that from himself, then he should believe in it, for the degree of knowledge (Ma'rifah) in it is very precious. And evidences of the Sacred Law (Shari'ah), experiences, and stories testify to that. As for the evidences, then His saying, the Exalted: 'And those who strive in Us, We will surely guide them to Our ways.' So every wisdom (Hikmah) that appears from the heart (Qalb) through persistence in worship (Ibadah) without learning, it is through the path of unveiling (Kashf) and inspiration (Ilham). And the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'Whoever acts upon what he knows, Allah will bequeath to him knowledge of what he did not know, and guide him in what he acts upon until he becomes deserving of Paradise. And whoever does not act upon what he knows, he will be lost in what he knows, and will not be guided in what he acts upon until he becomes deserving of the Fire.' And Allah, the Exalted, said: 'And whoever fears Allah (Yattaqi Allah), He will make for him a way out from difficulties and doubts, and provide for him from where he does not expect. He will teach him knowledge without learning, and make him discerning without experience.' And Allah, the Exalted, said: 'O you who have believed, if you fear Allah (Tattaqū Allah), He will grant you a criterion (Furqan).' It is said: a light (Nur) by which He distinguishes between truth and falsehood, and by which He exits from doubts. And for that reason, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, used to increase in
17:21.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

17:21.arabic: ثم انظر إلى تفاوت الدركات فإن الآخرة أكبر درجات وأكبر تفضيلا فكما أن إكباب الناس على الدنيا يتفاوت فمن منهمك مستكثر كالغريق فيها ومن خائض فيها إلى حد محدود فكذلك تناول النار لهم متفاوت فإن الله لا يظلم مثقال ذرة فلا تترادف أنواع العذاب على كل من فى النار كيفما كان بل لكل واحد حد معلوم على قدر عصيانه وذنبه إلا أن أقلهم عذابا لو عرضت عليه الدنيا بحذافير لافتدى بها من شدة ما هو فيه ما هو قال رسول الله ﭬ: (إن أدنى أهل النار عذابا يوم القيامة ينتعل بنعلين من نار يغلى دماغه من حرارة نعليه[198]) فانظر
17:21.english: Then look at the disparity of the degrees (darajat), for the Hereafter (al-Akhirah) is greater in degrees and greater in preferential treatment (tafdilan). Just as the people's immersion in the worldly life (al-Dunya) varies—some are deeply engrossed, accumulating it like one drowning in it, and some wade in it to a limited extent—so too is their experience of the Fire (al-Nar) varied. For Allah does not wrong even an atom's weight, so the types of punishment do not cascade upon everyone in the Fire however it may be; rather, each one has a known limit according to the measure of his disobedience (asiyan) and sin (dhanb), except that the least punished among them, if the worldly life in its entirety were presented to him, would ransom himself with it from the severity of what he is in. The Messenger of Allah ﭬ said: (Indeed, the least punished of the people of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection wears two sandals of fire, and his brain boils from the heat of his sandals[198]). So look now at the one upon whom it is lightened and take lesson from the one upon whom it is intensified.
17:21.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

17:21.arabic: ثم تأمل الآن فى غرف الجنة واختلاف درجات العلو فيها فإن الآخرة أكبر درجات وأكبر تفضيلا وكما أن بين الناس فى الطاعات الظاهرة والأخلاق الباطنة المحمودة تفاوتا ظاهرا فكذلك فيما يجازون به تفاوت ظاهر فإن كنت تطلب أعلى الدرجات فاجتهد أن لا يسبقك أحد بطاعة الله تعالى فقد أمرك الله بالمسابقة والمنافسة فيها فقال تعالى: ﴿ سابقوا إلى مغفرة من ربكم ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ وفى ذلك فليتنافس المتنافسون ﴾ {}
17:21.english: Then contemplate now the chambers of Paradise and the difference in the degrees of elevation within it, for indeed the Hereafter (Al-Akhirah) is greater in degrees and greater in preferential treatment (Tafdheelan). And just as there is an apparent disparity between people in the outward acts of obedience (Taa'aat) and the praised inward character traits (Akhlaaq), so too in what they are rewarded with there is an apparent disparity. So if you seek the highest degrees, strive that no one precedes you in obedience to Allah the Exalted, for indeed Allah has commanded you with racing and competing in it. He the Exalted said: 'Race toward forgiveness from your Lord' and He the Exalted said: 'And for that let the competitors compete.'
17:21.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

17:22.arabic: وقال ﭬ "يخرج من النار عنق له أذنان تسمعان وعينان تبصران ولسان ينطق يقول: وكلت بثلاثة: بكل جبار عنيد وبكل من دعا مع الله إلهاً آخر وبالمصورين"[7] وقال ﭬ "لا يدخل الجنة بخيل ولا جبار ولا سيئ الملكة"[8] وقال ﭬ "تحاجت الجنة والنار فقالت النار: أوثرت بالمتكبرين والمتجبرين، وقالت الجنة: ما لي لا يدخلني إلا ضعفاء الناس وسقاطهم وعجزتهم؟ فقال الله للجنة: إنما أنت رحمتي أرحم بك من أشاء من عبادي، وقال للنار: إنما أنت عذابي أعذب بك من أشاء ولكل واحدة منكما ملؤها"[9] وقال ﭬ "بئس العبد عبد تجبر واعتدى ونسى ال
17:22.english: And he (peace be upon him) said: "There emerges from the Fire a neck that has two ears that hear and two eyes that see and a tongue that speaks, saying: I have been entrusted with three: with every arrogant obstinate one and with everyone who calls upon with Allah another god (ilah) and with the image-makers."[7] And he (peace be upon him) said: "The miser, nor the arrogant one (jabbar), nor the one of bad character will not enter Paradise."[8] And he (peace be upon him) said: "Paradise and the Fire argued. The Fire said: I have been favored with the arrogant ones (mutakabbirin) and the domineering ones (mutajabbirin). And Paradise said: Why is it that none enters me except the weak of the people and their lowly and their incapable? So Allah said to Paradise: You are only My mercy; I show mercy through you to whom I will of My servants. And He said to the Fire: You are only My punishment; I punish through you whom I will. And for each one of you is its fill."[9] And he (peace be upon him) said: "Wretched is the servant (abd) who acts arrogantly (tajabbar) and transgresses and forgets the Supreme Almighty (al-Jabbar al-A'la). Wretched is the servant who acts arrogantly and becomes proud and forgets the Great, the Most High (al-Kabir al-Muta'al). Wretched is the servant who is heedless and negligent and forgets the graves and decay. Wretched is the servant who is insolent and oppressive and forgets the beginning and the end."[10]
17:22.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

17:24.arabic: رب اغفر لي ولوالدي وارحمهما كما ربياني صغيرا واغفر للمؤمنين والمؤمنات والمسلمين والمسلمات الأحياء منهم والأموات
17:24.english: Lord, forgive me and my parents and have mercy on them as they raised me small, and forgive the believing men and believing women and the submitting men and submitting women, the living among them and the dead.
17:24.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

17:24.arabic: [164]  حديث رب اغفر لي ولوالدي وارحمهما كما ربياني صغيرا واغفر للمؤمنين والمؤمنات والمسلمين والمسلمات الأحياء منهم والأموات أخرجه أبو داود وابن ماجه بإسناد حسن من حديث أبي أسيد الساعدي قال رجل من بني سلمة هل بقي علي من بر أبوي شيء قال نعم الصلاة عليهما والاستغفار لهما الحديث ولأبي الشيخ ابن حبان في الثواب والمستغفري في الدعوات من حديث أنس من استغفر للمؤمنين والمؤمنات رد الله عليه عن كل مؤمن مضى من أول الدهر أو هو كائن إلى يوم القيامة وسنده ضعيف وفي صحيح ابن حبان من حديث أبي سعيد أيما رجل مسلم لم
17:24.english: Hadith: 'O Lord, forgive me and my parents, and have mercy on them as they raised me when I was small, and forgive the believing men and believing women, and the Muslim men and Muslim women, the living among them and the dead.' It was reported by Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah with a good chain from the hadith of Abu Usayd al-Sa'idi. A man from Banu Salamah said, 'Is there anything left for me regarding dutifulness (Birr) to my parents?' He said, 'Yes, praying for them and seeking forgiveness for them.' The hadith. And for Abu al-Shaykh Ibn Hibban in al-Thawab and al-Mustaghfiri in al-Da'awat from the hadith of Anas: 'Whoever seeks forgiveness for the believing men and believing women, Allah will return to him for every believer who has passed from the beginning of time or who will be until the Day of Resurrection.' Its chain is weak. And in Sahih Ibn Hibban from the hadith of Abu Sa'id: 'Any Muslim man who does not have charity (Sadaqah) with him, let him say in his supplication: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad, Your servant and messenger, and send blessings upon the believing men and believing women, and the Muslim men and Muslim women, for it is purification (Zakah).'
17:24.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication

17:26.arabic: ومنها الإسراف في الطعام والبناء فهو منكر بل في المال منكران أحدهما الإضاعة والآخر الإسراف فالإضاعة تفويت مال بلا فائدة يعتد بها كإحراق الثوب وتمزيقه وهدم البناء من غير غرض وإلقاء المال في البحر وفي معناه صرف المال إلى النائحة والمطرب وفي أنواع الفساد لأنها فوائد محرمة شرعا فصارت كالمعدومة وأما الإسراف فقد يطلق لإرادة صرف المال إلى النائحة والمطرب والمنكرات وقد يطلق على الصرف إلى المباحات في جنسها ولكن مع المبالغة والمبالغة تختلف بالإضافة إلى الأحوال فنقول من لم يملك إلا مائة دينار مثلا ومعه عيال
17:26.english: And among them is extravagance (Israf) in food and building, which is reprehensible (Munkar). Rather, in wealth there are two reprehensible acts: one is waste (Ida'ah) and the other is extravagance (Israf). Waste is squandering wealth without any considered benefit, like burning a garment, tearing it, demolishing a building without purpose, and throwing wealth into the sea. In its meaning is spending wealth on lamentation (Naihah) and entertainment (Mutrib) and in types of corruption, because these are benefits prohibited by law (Sharia), so they become as if non-existent. As for extravagance (Israf), it may be used to intend spending wealth on lamentation (Naihah), entertainment (Mutrib), and reprehensible acts (Munkarat), and it may be used for spending on permissible things (Mubahat) in their kind, but with exaggeration (Mubalaghah). Exaggeration differs relative to circumstances. We say: whoever owns only a hundred dinars, for example, and has his dependents and children with no livelihood except it, and spends all of it on a feast, he is extravagant (Musrif) and must be prevented. Allah the Exalted said: 'And do not extend it all extension, so you sit blamed, exhausted.' This was revealed regarding a man in Medina who distributed all his wealth and left nothing for his dependents, then was demanded for maintenance and could not afford anything. And He said: 'And do not waste wastefully (Tabdhir). Indeed, the wasteful (Mubadhirin) are brothers of the devils.' And likewise, He the Mighty and Glorious said: 'And those who, when they spend, are not extravagant (Yusrifu) and are not stingy (Yaqtiru).' So whoever is extravagant with this extravagance (Israf) is censured, and it is obligatory upon the judge to impose guardianship on him, except if the man is alone and has a true strength in reliance (Tawakkul), then he may spend all his wealth in the paths of good (Abwab al-Birr). And whoever has dependents or is incapable of reliance (Tawakkul) may not give all his wealth in charity. Likewise, if he spends all his wealth on carvings of his walls and adorning his building, that is also prohibited extravagance (Israf Muharram). Doing that by one who has abundant wealth is not prohibited, because adornment is among sound purposes, and mosques have always been adorned and their doors and ceilings carved, even though carving the door and ceiling has no benefit except mere adornment, so likewise houses.
