And likewise, the statement regarding adornment with clothes and foods: that is permissible (Mubah) in its kind and becomes extravagance (Israf) considering the man's condition and wealth. And examples of these reprehensible acts (Munkarat) are many and cannot be enumerated. So judge by these reprehensible acts (Munkarat) the gatherings, courts of judges, offices of rulers, schools of jurists, retreats of Sufis (Ribatat al-Sufiyyah), and inns of markets. No place is free from a reprehensible (Munkar) disliked or cautioned against. Exhausting all reprehensible acts (Munkarat) requires encompassing all details of the law (Sharia), its principles (Usul) and branches (Furu'), so let us limit to this amount of them. The general reprehensible acts (Munkarat): know that every sitter in his house, wherever he is, is not free.
17:26.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

17:29.arabic: وبينهما وسط وهو المحمود وينبغي أن يكون السخاء والجود عبارة عنه؛ إذ لم يؤمر رسول الله ﷺ إلا بالسخاء، وقد قيل له "ولا تجعل يدك مغلولة إلى عنقك ولا تبسطها كل البسط" وقال تعالى "والذين إذا أنفقوا لم يسرفوا ولم يقتروا وكان بين ذلك قواماً" فالجود وسط بين الإسراف والإقتار وبين البسط والقبض، وهو أن يقدر بذله وإمساكه بقدر الواجب، ولا يكفي أن يفعل ذلك بجوارحه ما لم يكن قلبه طيباً به غير منازع له فيه. فإن بذل في محل وجوب البذل ونفسه تنازعه وهو يصابرها فهو متسخ وليس بسخي، بل ينبغي أن لا يكون لقلبه علاقة مع
17:29.english: And between them is a middle path which is praiseworthy, and it should be that generosity (Sakhā') and magnanimity (Jūd) are expressions for it; for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was not commanded except with generosity, and it was said to him: 'And do not make your hand chained to your neck nor stretch it forth with all stretching' (Quran 17:29), and Allah the Exalted said: 'And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy, and between that is a standing upright' (Quran 25:67). So magnanimity (Jūd) is a middle between extravagance (Isrāf) and stinginess (Iqtār) and between stretching forth (Bast) and withholding (Qabd), and it is that one measures his giving and withholding according to what is obligatory, and it is not sufficient that he does that with his limbs unless his heart (Qalb) is content with it without disputing him in it. For if he gives in the place of obligatory giving and his soul (Nafs) disputes him while he endures it, he is forcing himself and is not generous, rather it should be that his heart (Qalb) has no connection with wealth except from where wealth is intended for him, which is spending it to what it should be spent to.
17:29.book_title: Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth
17:29.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

17:29.arabic: فنقول من لم يملك إلا مائة دينار مثلا ومعه عياله وأولاده ولا معيشة لهم سواه فأنفق الجميع في وليمة فهو مسرف يجب منعه قال تعالى ولا تبسطها كل البسط فتقعد ملوما محسورا نزل هذا في رجل بالمدينة قسم جميع ماله ولم يبق شيئا لعياله فطولب بالنفقة فلم يقدر على شيء وقال تعالى ولا تبذر تبذيرا إن المبذرين كانوا إخوان الشياطين وكذلك قال عز وجل والذين إذا أنفقوا لم يسرفوا ولم يقتروا فمن يسرف هذا الإسراف ينكر عليه ويجب على القاضي أن يحجر عليه إلا إذا كان الرجل وحده وكان له قوة في التوكل صادقة فله أن ينفق جميع مال
17:29.english: We say: For example, one who possesses only one hundred dinars and has dependents and children with no livelihood for them except this, then he spends all of it on a feast - he is wasteful (Musrif) and must be prevented. Allah the Exalted said: 'And do not extend it (your hand) completely extended, so you sit blameworthy, destitute.' This was revealed regarding a man in Al-Madinah who distributed all his wealth and left nothing for his dependents, then was demanded for expenses but was unable to provide anything. And Allah the Exalted said: 'And do not squander wastefully, indeed the squanderers are brothers of the devils.' And likewise, the Mighty and Majestic said: 'And those who, when they spend, are neither wasteful nor stingy.' So whoever wastes with this wastefulness, it is denounced upon him, and it is obligatory upon the judge to impose guardianship over him, except if the man is alone and has a true strength in Reliance (Tawakkul) upon Allah - then he may spend all his wealth in the paths of righteousness. But whoever has dependents or is incapable of Reliance (Tawakkul) - then it is not for him to give charity with all his wealth.
17:29.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

17:29.arabic: والذي يدل على أن المطلوب هو الوسط في الأخلاق دون الطرفين أن السخاء خلق محمود شرعاً، وهو وسط بين طرفي التبذير والتقتير. وقد أثنى الله تعالى عليه فقال "والذين إذا أنفقوا لم يسرفوا ولم يقتروا وكان بين ذلك قواما" وقال تعالى "ولا تجعل يدك مغلولة إلى عنقك ولا تبسطها كل البسط" وكذلك المطلوب في شهوة الطعام الاعتدال دون الشره والجمود قال الله تعالى "وكلوا واشربوا ولا تسرفوا إنه لا يحب المسرفين" وقال في الغضب "أشداء على الكفار رحماء بينهم" وقال ﭬ "خير الأمور أوساطها" وهذا له سر وتحقيق وهو أن السعادة منوطة
17:29.english: And what indicates that the sought-after is the middle in character traits without the two extremes is that generosity is a praiseworthy trait legally, and it is a middle between the two extremes of wastefulness and stinginess. And Allah the Exalted has praised it, saying: 'And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy, but hold a just balance between that' (Quran 25:67). And He said: 'And do not make your hand chained to your neck nor stretch it out completely' (Quran 17:29). Likewise, the sought-after in the desire for food is moderation without gluttony and abstinence. Allah the Exalted said: 'And eat and drink, but do not be extravagant; indeed, He does not love the extravagant' (Quran 7:31). And He said regarding anger: 'Severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves' (Quran 48:29). And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'The best of matters are their middle ones.' And this has a secret and verification, which is that happiness is tied to the soundness of the heart from the afflictions of this world. Allah the Exalted said: 'Except he who comes to Allah with a sound heart' (Quran 26:89). And stinginess is from the afflictions of the worldly life, and wastefulness is also from the afflictions of the worldly life, and the condition of the heart is to be sound from both, meaning it should not be attentive to wealth, nor should it be eager to spend it nor to withhold it. For the one eager to spend has his heart diverted to spending, just as the one eager to withhold has his heart diverted to withholding. So the perfection of the heart is to be pure from both descriptions altogether.
17:29.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

17:29.arabic: السادس الاعتدال في النفقة فلا ينبغي أن يقتر عليهن في الإنفاق ولا ينبغي أن يسرف بل يقتصد قال تعالى (وكلوا واشربوا ولا تسرفوا) وقال تعالى (ولا تجعل يدك مغلولة إلى عنقك ولا تبسطها كل البسط) وقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم (خيركم خيركم لأهله)[127] وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم (دينار أنفقته في سبيل الله ودينار أنفقته في رقبة ودينار تصدقت به على مسكين ودينار أنفقته على أهلك أعظمها أجرا الذي أنفقته على أهلك.)[128]
17:29.english: Sixth: Moderation in expenditure. One should not be stingy with them in spending, nor should one be extravagant, but rather be moderate. Allah the Exalted said: 'And eat and drink, but do not be extravagant' (Quran 7:31). And He said: 'And do not make your hand tied to your neck, nor stretch it out to the utmost extent' (Quran 17:29). And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'The best of you is the best to his family' [127]. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'A dinar you spend in the path of Allah, a dinar you spend to free a slave, a dinar you give in charity to a poor person, and a dinar you spend on your family—the greatest in reward is the one you spend on your family.' [128]
17:29.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

17:36.arabic: وكيف لا يؤاخذ بأعمال القلب من الكبر والعجب والرياء والنفاق والحسد وجملة الخبائث من أعمال القلب بل السمع والبصر والفؤاد كل أولئك كان عنه مسئولا أي ما يدخل تحت الاختيار فلو وقع البصر بغير اختيار على غير ذي محرم لم يؤاخذ به فإن أتبعها نظرة ثانية كان مؤاخذا به لأنه مختار فكذا خواطر القلب تجري هذا المجرى بل القلب أولى بمؤاخذته لأنه الأصل قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم التقوى ههنا وأشار إلى القلب وقال الله تعالى لن ينال الله لحومها ولا دماؤها ولكن يناله التقوى منكم وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم الإثم حواز
17:36.english: And how could one not be held accountable for the works of the Heart (Qalb) from arrogance (Kibr), self-admiration (Ujb), ostentation (Riya), hypocrisy (Nifaq), envy (Hasad), and the entirety of evils from the works of the Heart? Rather, the Hearing (Sam') and the Sight (Basar) and the Heart (Fu'ad) - all of those will be questioned about it, meaning what enters under choice. If the sight falls without choice upon something not forbidden, one is not held accountable for it. But if one follows it with a second look, one is held accountable for it because it is chosen. Likewise, the thoughts of the Heart follow this course. Rather, the Heart is more deserving of being held accountable because it is the origin. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'God-consciousness (Taqwa) is here,' and he pointed to his Heart. And Allah the Exalted said: 'Their flesh and their blood do not reach Allah, but your God-consciousness (Taqwa) reaches Him.' And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'Sin is what wavers in the hearts.' And he said: 'Righteousness (Birr) is what the Heart finds tranquility in, even if they give you legal opinions and give you legal opinions.' So much so that we say: If the Heart of the jurist (Mufti) rules by obligating something and he is mistaken in it, he becomes rewarded for it.
17:36.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

17:36.arabic: فأما ما يدل على المؤاخذة فقوله سبحانه إن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله فيغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء وقوله تعالى ولا تقف ما ليس لك به علم إن السمع والبصر والفؤاد كل أولئك كان عنه مسئولا فدل على أن عمل الفؤاد كعمل السمع والبصر فلا يعفي عنه وقوله تعالى ولا تكتموا الشهادة ومن يكتمها فإنه آثم قلبه وقوله تعالى لا يؤاخذكم الله باللغو في أيمانكم ولكن يؤاخذكم بما كسبت قلوبكم
17:36.english: As for what indicates accountability, there is His saying, the Most High: 'If you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it, then He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills.' And His saying, the Most High: 'And do not follow that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart (Al-Fu'ād) - all of those will be questioned.' This indicates that the action of the heart (Al-Fu'ād) is like the action of hearing and sight, so it is not pardoned. And His saying, the Most High: 'And do not conceal testimony, and whoever conceals it - indeed, his heart (Qalb) is sinful.' And His saying, the Most High: 'Allah will not call you to account for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He will call you to account for what your hearts (Qulūb) have earned.'
17:36.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

17:36.arabic: فمن لم يتوقف عند الاشتباه كان متبعا لهواه معجبا برأيه وكان ممن وصفه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذ قال فإذا رأيت شحا مطاعا وهوى متبعا وإعجاب كل ذى رأى برأيه فعليك بخاصة نفسك وكل من خاض في شبهه بغير تحقيق فقد خالف قوله تعالى ولا تقف ما ليس لك به علم حديث فإذا رأيت شحا مطاعا وهوى متبعا الحديث تقدم وقوله عليه السلام إياكم والظن فإن الظن أكذب الحديث حديث إياكم والظن الحديث تقدم وأراد به ظنا بغير دليل كما يستفتى بعض العوام قلبه فيما أشكل عليه ويتبع ظنه ولصعوبة هذا الأمر وعظمة كان دعاء الصديق رضى الل
17:36.english: Whoever does not pause at ambiguity follows his desire (Hawa) and admires his own opinion, and he is among those described by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) when he said: 'When you see miserliness obeyed, desire (Hawa) followed, and every possessor of opinion admiring his opinion, then upon you is your own self.' And everyone who delves into his doubt without verification has contradicted His saying, the Exalted: 'And do not follow that of which you have no knowledge (علم). Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart (الفؤاد) - all of those will be questioned.' The hadith 'When you see miserliness obeyed...' preceded, and his saying (peace be upon him): 'Beware of conjecture (الظن), for conjecture is the most lying of speech.' The hadith 'Beware of conjecture...' preceded, and he meant by it conjecture without evidence, as some common people consult their heart (قلب) in what is ambiguous to them and follow their conjecture. Due to the difficulty of this matter and its greatness, the supplication of the Truthful One (may Allah be pleased with him) was: 'O Allah, show me the truth as truth and grant me following it, and show me falsehood as falsehood and grant me avoiding it, and do not make it ambiguous to me so I follow desire (الهوى).' And Jesus (peace be upon him) said: 'Matters are three: a matter whose right guidance becomes clear, so follow it; a matter whose misguidance becomes clear, so avoid it; and a matter that is ambiguous to you, so refer it to its knower.' The hadith 'Jesus said: Matters are three...' was reported by Al-Tabarani from the hadith of Ibn Abbas with a weak chain. And it was from the supplication of the Prophet (peace be upon him): 'O Allah, I seek refuge in You from speaking about the religion without knowledge (علم).' The hadith 'O Allah, I seek refuge in You from speaking about the religion without knowledge' I did not find.
17:36.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

17:36.arabic: فإذا لم يكن معك حفظ بقلبك ولا نسخة صحيحة استوثقت عليها لتقابل بها فمن أين تعلم أنك سمعت ذلك؟ وقد قال الله تعالى "ولا تقف ما ليس لك به علم" وقول الشيوخ كلهم في هذا الزمان إنا سمعنا ما في هذا الكتاب إذا لم يوجد الشرط الذي ذكرناه فهو كذب صريح.
17:36.english: If you do not have memorization with your heart (Qalb) nor a verified copy that you have authenticated to compare with, then from where do you know that you heard that? And Allah the Exalted has said: 'And do not follow that of which you have no knowledge.' And the statement of all the shaykhs in this time that 'we heard what is in this book'—if the condition that we mentioned is not present—then it is an outright lie.
17:36.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

17:37.arabic: فسمع ابن الأهثم فرجع يعتذر إليه فقال: لا تعتذر إلي وتب إلى ربك، أما سمعت قول الله تعالى "ولا تمش في الأرض مرحاً إنك لن تخرق الأرض ولت تبلغ الجبال طولاً"؟ ومر بالحسن شاب عليه بزة له حسنة فدعاه فقال له: ابن آدم معجب بشبابه محب لشمائله، كأن القبر قد وارى بدنك وكأنك قد لاقيت عملك، ويحك! داو قلبك فإن حاجة الله إلى العباد صلاح قلوبهم.
17:37.english: Ibn al-Ahtham heard this and returned to apologize to him. He said: 'Do not apologize to me, but repent to your Lord. Have you not heard the saying of Allah the Exalted: "And do not walk upon the earth exultantly (marahan). Indeed, you will never tear the earth apart, and you will never reach the mountains in height"?' And a youth passed by al-Hasan wearing a beautiful garment, so he called him and said to him: 'Son of Adam, admiring his youth, loving his attributes, as if the grave has already covered your body and as if you have already met your deeds. Woe to you! Treat your Heart (Qalb), for Allah's need from the servants is the rectification of their hearts.'
17:37.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

17:39.arabic: وقال ﭬ "يخرج من النار عنق له أذنان تسمعان وعينان تبصران ولسان ينطق يقول: وكلت بثلاثة: بكل جبار عنيد وبكل من دعا مع الله إلهاً آخر وبالمصورين"[7] وقال ﭬ "لا يدخل الجنة بخيل ولا جبار ولا سيئ الملكة"[8] وقال ﭬ "تحاجت الجنة والنار فقالت النار: أوثرت بالمتكبرين والمتجبرين، وقالت الجنة: ما لي لا يدخلني إلا ضعفاء الناس وسقاطهم وعجزتهم؟ فقال الله للجنة: إنما أنت رحمتي أرحم بك من أشاء من عبادي، وقال للنار: إنما أنت عذابي أعذب بك من أشاء ولكل واحدة منكما ملؤها"[9] وقال ﭬ "بئس العبد عبد تجبر واعتدى ونسى ال
17:39.english: And he (peace be upon him) said: "There will emerge from the Fire a neck having two ears that hear and two eyes that see and a tongue that speaks, saying: I have been entrusted with three: with every arrogant oppressor (jabbār ʿanīd) and with everyone who calls upon another god (ilāhan ākhar) alongside Allah and with the image-makers."[7] And he (peace be upon him) said: "The miser, the arrogant (jabbār), and the one of bad character will not enter Paradise."[8] And he (peace be upon him) said: "Paradise and Hell debated. Hell said: I have been favored with the arrogant (mutakabbirīn) and the tyrants (mutajabbirīn). And Paradise said: Why is it that none enter me except the weak of the people, their lowly, and their incapable? So Allah said to Paradise: You are only My mercy; I show mercy through you to whom I will of My servants. And He said to Hell: You are only My punishment; I punish through you whom I will, and each of you will have its fill."[9] And he (peace be upon him) said: "Wretched is the servant who acts arrogantly (tajabbar) and transgresses and forgets the Supreme Almighty (al-Jabbār al-Aʿlā). Wretched is the servant who acts arrogantly (tajabbar) and is proud and forgets the Great, the Exalted (al-Kabīr al-Mutaʿāl). Wretched is the servant who is heedless and negligent and forgets the graves and decay. Wretched is the servant who is insolent and oppressive and forgets the beginning and the end."[10] And from Thābit that he said: It reached us that it was said: O Messenger of Allah, how great is the arrogance (kibr) of so-and-so! He said: "Is there not after it death?"[11] And ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr said: Indeed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "When death approached Nūḥ (upon him be peace), he called his two sons and said: I command you with two and I forbid you from two. I forbid you from association (shirk) and arrogance (kibr), and I command you with 'There is no god but Allah.' For if the heavens and the earths and what is in them were placed on one scale of the balance and 'There is no god but Allah' were placed on the other scale, it would outweigh them. And if the heavens and the earths and what is in them were a ring and 'There is no god but Allah' were placed in its middle, it would split them. That is from what your Lord has revealed to you of wisdom. And do not set up with Allah another god, lest you be cast into Hell, blamed and banished."
17:39.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

17:44.arabic: ومن هذا قوله تعالى: ﴿ وإن من شيء إلا يسبح بحمده ﴾ {} فالبليد يفتقر فيه إلى أن يقدر للجمادات حياة وعقلا ونطقا بصوت وحرف حتى يقول سبحان الله ليتحقق تسبيحه والبصير يعلم أنه ما أريد به نطق اللسان بل كونه مسبحا بوجوده ومقدسا بذاته وشاهدا بوحدانية الله سبحانه كما يقال: وفي كل شيء له آية تدل على أنه الواحد وكما يقال هذه الصنعة المحكمة تشهد لصانعها بحسن التدبير وكمال العلم لا بمعنى أنها تقول أشهد بالقول ولكن بالذات والحال وكذلك ما من شيء إلا وهو محتاج في نفسه إلى موجد يوجده ويبقيه ويديم أوصافه ويردده في
17:44.english: And from this is His saying, the Exalted: 'And there is not a thing except that it glorifies with His praise' (Quran 17:44). The dull-witted one requires in understanding it to imagine for inanimate objects life, intellect, and speech with sound and letter until they say 'Glory be to Allah' to realize their glorification. But the insightful one knows that what is intended is not the tongue's utterance, but rather its being glorifying by its existence, sanctified by its essence, and witnessing to the Oneness (Tawhid) of Allah, the Exalted, as it is said: 'And in everything there is a sign for Him that indicates He is the One.' And as it is said: 'This precise craftsmanship testifies for its maker with good management and perfect knowledge'—not in the sense that it says 'I bear witness' with speech, but by essence and state. Likewise, there is not a thing except that it is needy in itself for a Creator who creates it, preserves it, maintains its attributes, and returns it through its stages. So by its neediness, it testifies for its Creator with sanctification. Those with insight perceive its testimony, not those rigidly adhering to appearances. And therefore, He, the Exalted, said: 'But you do not understand their glorification' (Surah Al-Isra: 44). As for the deficient ones, they do not understand it at all; and as for the close ones and firmly rooted scholars, they do not understand its reality and perfection, for everything has various testimonies to the sanctification and glorification of Allah, the Exalted, and each one perceives according to the measure of his intellect and insight. Enumerating those testimonies is not fitting for the knowledge of transaction. This art is also among that in which the masters of appearances and the masters of insight differ in their knowledge, and through it the distinction between the inner (Batin) and the outer (Zahir) becomes apparent. And in this station, for the people of stations, there is extravagance and...
17:44.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

17:44.arabic: وما من ذرة في السماوات والأرض إلا ولها أنواع شاهدات لله تعالى بالوحدانية هي توحيدها وأنواع شاهدات لصانعها بالتقدس هي تسبيحها ولكن لا يفقهون تسبيحها لأنهم لم يسافروا من مضيق سمع الظاهر إلى فضاء سمع الباطن ومن ركاكة لسان المقال إلى فصاحة لسان الحال ولو قدر كل عاجز على مثل هذا السير لما كان سليمان عليه السلام مختصا بفهم منطق الطير ولما كان موسى عليه السلام مختصا بسماع كلام الله تعالى الذي يجب تقديسه عن مشابهة الحروف والأصوات ومن يسافر ليستقرئ هذه الشهادات من الأسطر المكتوبة بالخطوط الإلهية على صفحا
17:44.english: And there is not a single particle in the heavens and the earth except that it has types of witnesses for Allah the Exalted to Oneness (Tawhid), which are its declaration of Oneness, and types of witnesses to its Creator for Holiness (Taqdis), which are its glorification (Tasbih). But they do not comprehend its glorification because they have not journeyed from the narrowness of the apparent hearing (Sama' al-Zahir) to the expanse of the inner hearing (Sama' al-Batin), and from the weakness of the tongue of speech (Lisan al-Maqal) to the eloquence of the tongue of state (Lisan al-Hal). And if every incapable one were capable of such a journey, Solomon (peace be upon him) would not have been uniquely distinguished with understanding the speech of the birds, and Moses (peace be upon him) would not have been uniquely distinguished with hearing the speech of Allah the Exalted, which must be sanctified from resemblance to letters and sounds. And whoever journeys to seek these testimonies from the lines written with the divine scripts on the pages of inanimate things, his journey with the body does not prolong; rather, he settles in a place and empties his heart (Qalb) to enjoy hearing the melodies of glorifications from individual particles. So what has he to do with wandering in the deserts? And he has sufficiency in the dominion (Malakut) of the heavens. For the sun, the moon, and the stars are subjugated by His command, and they are traveling to the sights of those with insight in the month and the year times, rather they are diligent in movement upon the succession of times. So it is among the wonders that one diligently circumambulates individual mosques when the Kaaba has been commanded to circumambulate him, and it is among the wonders that one circumambulates the corners of the earth when the regions of the sky circumambulate him. Then, as long as the traveler is in need of seeing the world of dominion (Malakut) and testimony (Shahadah) with the apparent sight (Basar al-Zahir), he is still in the first station of the stations of those who walk to Allah and journey to His presence, and it is as if he is secluded at the door of the homeland, not having entered.
17:44.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Etiquette of Travel'

17:44.arabic: وتقول السماوات كلها: عليه لعنة الله ولعنتنا وتلعنه السماوات السبع والأرض ومن فيهن
17:44.english: And all the heavens say: upon him is the curse of Allah and our curse, and the seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them curse him.
17:44.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

17:53.arabic: ومهما انقطع الوفاء بدوام المحبة شمت به الشيطان فإنه لا يحسد متعاونين على بركما يحسد متواخيين في الله ومتحابين فيه فإنه يجهد نفسه لإفساد ما بينهما قال الله تعالى وقل لعبادي يقولوا التي هي أحسن أن الشيطان ينزغ بينهم وقال مخبرا عن يوسف من بعد أن نزغ الشيطان بيني وبين إخوتي ويقال ما تواخى اثنان في الله فتفرق بينهما إلا بذنب يرتكبه أحدهما وكان بشر يقول إذا قصر العبد في طاعة الله سلبه الله من يؤنسه وذلك لأن الإخوان مسلاة للهموم وعون على الدين ولذلك قال ابن المبارك ألذ الأشياء مجالسة الإخوان والانقلاب
17:53.english: Whenever faithfulness (الوفاء) is severed from the continuity of love (المحبة), Satan (الشيطان) gloats over it, for he does not envy those cooperating in righteousness as he envies those who are brothers in Allah (الله) and those who love each other for His sake. Indeed, he exerts himself to corrupt what is between them. Allah (الله) the Exalted said: 'And say to My servants that they should speak that which is best. Indeed, Satan sows discord between them.' And He informed about Yusuf (يوسف) after Satan had sown discord between me and my brothers. And it is said: 'No two people become brothers in Allah (الله) and then separate except due to a sin committed by one of them.' And Bishr used to say: 'When a servant (العبد) falls short in obeying Allah (الله), Allah (الله) deprives him of those who would comfort him.' This is because brothers are a solace for sorrows and an aid in religion (الدين). Therefore, Ibn al-Mubarak said: 'The most delightful thing is sitting with brothers and returning to sufficiency.' Lasting affection (المودة) is that which is for Allah (الله), and whatever is for a purpose vanishes with the vanishing of that purpose. Among the fruits of affection (المودة) in Allah (الله) is that it is not accompanied by envy in religion (الدين) or worldly life (دنيا). How could he envy him when everything that belongs to his brother returns its benefit to him? And with this, Allah (الله) the Exalted described those who love in Allah (الله) the Exalted, saying: 'And they find in their chests no need for what they have been given and prefer others over themselves.' And the existence of need is envy.
17:53.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

17:55.arabic: وهذه الاختلافات بعضها لاختلاف الأحوال والمقامات وبعضها لما سبق في الأزل من التفاضل والتفاوت في القسمة بين العباد، وقد قال تعالى: " ولقد فضلنا بعض النبيين على بعض "، وقد قال: " منهم من كلم الله ورفع بعضهم درجات " فكان عيسى عليه السلام من المفضلين ولإدلاله سلم على نفسه، فقال: " والسلام علي يوم ولدت ويوم أموت ويوم أبعث حياً" وهذا انبساط منه لما شاهد من اللطف في مقام الأنس.
17:55.english: And these differences, some of them are due to differences in states (Ahwal) and stations (Maqamat), and some of them are due to what preceded in pre-eternity (Al-Azal) of preference (Tafadul) and disparity (Tafawut) in the apportionment (Qismah) among the worshippers (Al-Ibad). And indeed Allah the Exalted said: "And We have preferred some of the prophets over others." And He said: "Among them are those to whom Allah spoke and He raised some of them in degrees." So Jesus (Isa) peace be upon him was among the preferred ones, and due to his familiarity (Idlal) he greeted himself, saying: "And peace be upon me the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I am raised alive." And this is an expansion (Inbisat) from him due to what he witnessed of gentleness (Lutf) in the station of intimacy (Maqam Al-Uns).
17:55.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

17:57.arabic: فإذن الناس وإن اختلفت طرقهم في العبادة فكلهم على الصواب ﴿ أولئك الذين يدعون يبتغون إلى ربهم الوسيلة أيهم أقرب ﴾ {} وإنما يتفاوتون في درجات القرب لا في أصله وأقربهم إلى الله تعالى أعرفهم به وأعرفهم به لا بد وأن يكون أعبدهم له فمن عرفه لم يعبد غيره.
17:57.english: Therefore, the people, even if their paths in worship differ, are all upon correctness. 'Those whom they call upon seek the means of approach (al-wasīlah) to their Lord, as to which of them would be nearest' (Quran 17:57). They only differ in the degrees of nearness (al-qurb), not in its foundation. And the nearest of them to Allah the Exalted is the most knowledgeable of Him, and the most knowledgeable of Him must necessarily be the most worshipping of Him, for whoever knows Him does not worship other than Him.
17:57.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

17:59.arabic: وما لا بد فيه من السماع فنون كثيرة منها الإيجار بالحذف والإضمار كقوله تعالى ﴿ وآتينا ثمود الناقة مبصرة فظلموا بها ﴾ {} معناه آية مبصرة فظلموا أنفسهم بقتلها فالناظر إلى ظاهر العربية يظن أن المراد به أن الناقة كانت مبصرة ولم تكن عمياء ولم يدر أنهم بماذا ظلموا غيرهم أو أنفسهم
17:59.english: And what is indispensable in hearing (al-Samāʿ) are many arts, among them is the indication through omission (al-Hadhf) and implication (al-Idhmār), as in His saying, the Exalted: 'And We gave Thamūd the she-camel, clear (Mubṣirah), but they wronged (Ẓalamū) with it' (Quran 17:59). Its meaning is: a clear sign (Āyah Mubṣirah), and they wronged themselves (Ẓalamū Anfusahum) by killing it. So, the one who looks at the apparent Arabic (al-ʿArabiyyah) thinks that what is intended by it is that the she-camel was seeing (Mubṣirah) and was not blind, and does not know with what they wronged others or themselves.
17:59.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

17:61.arabic: الآثار: قال بعض السلف: أول خطيئة هي الحسد حسد إبليس آدم عليه السلام على رتبته فأبى أن يسجد له فحمله على الحسد والمعصية. وحكي أن عون بن عبد الله دخل على الفضل بن المهلب وكان يومئذ على واسط فقال: إني أريد أن أعظك بشيء فقال: وما هو؟ قال: إياك والكبر فإنه أول ذنب عصي الله به، ثم قرأ "وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس" الآية، وإياك والحرص فإنه أخرج آدم من الجنة أمكنه الله سبحانه من جنة عرضها السموات والأرض يأكل منها إلا شجرة واحدة نهاه عنها فأكل منها فأخرجه الله تعالى منها، ثم قرأ "اهبطو
17:61.english: The Narrations: Some of the predecessors said: The first sin is envy (Hasad) - Iblis envied Adam, peace be upon him, for his rank, so he refused to prostrate to him, and it carried him into envy (Hasad) and disobedience. And it is narrated that 'Awn ibn 'Abdullah entered upon al-Fadl ibn al-Muhallab, who was then in Wasit, and said: I want to advise you with something. He said: And what is it? He said: Beware of arrogance (Kibr), for it is the first sin by which Allah was disobeyed, then he recited: "And [mention] when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam,' and they prostrated, except for Iblis..." the verse, and beware of greed (Hirs), for it expelled Adam from Paradise - Allah, glorified be He, had enabled him in a garden whose width is the heavens and the earth, he could eat from it except for one tree which He forbade him from, but he ate from it, so Allah, exalted be He, expelled him from it, then he recited: "Descend from it..." to the end of the verse, and beware of envy (Hasad), for indeed the son of Adam killed his brother when he envied him, then he recited: "And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam in truth...", the verses, and when the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ are mentioned, then refrain, and when predestination (Qadar) is mentioned, then be silent, and when the stars are mentioned, then be silent.
17:61.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

17:64.arabic: قال إبليس يارب هذا العبد الذي كرمته علي إن لا تعني عليه لا أقوى عليه قال لا يولد له ولد إلا ولد لك ولد قال يارب زدني قال تجري منهم مجرى الدم وتتخذون صدورهم بيوتا قال رب زدني قال أجلب عليهم بخيلك ورجلك إلى قوله غرورا
17:64.english: Iblis said: 'O Lord, this servant whom You have honored over me, if You do not help me against him, I cannot overpower him.' He said: 'No child is born to him except that a child is born to you.' He said: 'O Lord, increase me.' He said: 'You flow through them like blood and you take their chests as homes.' He said: 'O Lord, increase me.' He said: 'And muster against them all your forces, cavalry and infantry, to the word "deception."'
17:64.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

17:65.arabic: ولا يمكن فتحها بعد ذلك إلا بتخلية القلب عن قوت الشيطان وهو الهوى والشهوات وعمارته بذكر الله تعالى الذي هو مطرح أثر الملائكة وقال جابر بن عبيدة العدوي شكوت إلى العلاء بن زياد ما أجد في صدري من الوسوسة فقال إنما مثل ذلك مثل البيت الذي يمر به اللصوص فإن كان فيه شيء عالجوه وإلا مضوا وتركوه يعني أن القلب الخالي عن الهوى لا يدخله الشيطان ولذلك قال الله تعالى إن عبادي ليس لك عليهم سلطان فكل من اتبع الهوى فهو عبد الهوى لا عبد الله ولذلك سلط الله عليه الشيطان وقال تعالى أفرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه وهو إشارة
17:65.english: And it is not possible to open it after that except by emptying the Heart (Qalb) from the strength of Satan, which is the Passion (Hawa) and the Desires (Shahawat), and building it with the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah the Exalted, which is the place of the effect of the angels. And Jabir ibn 'Abidah al-'Adawi said: I complained to al-'Ala' ibn Ziyad about what I find in my chest from the whisperings. He said: Indeed, the likeness of that is like a house that thieves pass by; if there is something in it, they treat it, otherwise they pass and leave it. Meaning that the Heart (Qalb) empty from Passion (Hawa) does not enter it Satan. And for that reason, Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, My servants, there is not for you over them any authority.' So everyone who follows the Passion (Hawa) is a servant of the Passion (Hawa), not a servant of Allah. And for that reason, Allah empowered over him Satan. And He the Exalted said: 'Have you seen the one who takes his god his passion?' And it is an indication that whoever has his Passion (Hawa) as his god and worshipped one, he is a servant of the Passion (Hawa), not a servant of Allah.
17:65.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

17:65.arabic: وإنما تحوم الشياطين على القلوب إذا كانت مشحونة بالصفات المذمومة فإنها مرعى الشيطان وجنده ومن خلص قلبه من تلك الصفات وصفاه لم يطف الشيطان حول قلبه وإليه الاشارة بقوله تعالىإلا عبادك منهم المخلصين وبقوله تعالى إن عبادي ليس لك عليهم سلطان والسماع سبب لصفاء القلب وهو شبكة للحق بواسطة الصفاء
17:65.english: And indeed, the devils only hover around the hearts (Qulub) when they are filled with blameworthy attributes (Sifat), for they are the pasture of the devil and his soldiers. And whoever purifies his heart (Qalb) from those attributes and cleanses it, the devil does not circle around his heart (Qalb). And to this points the indication by His saying, the Exalted: 'Except Your servants among them, the purified ones (Al-Mukhlaseen)' and by His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, My servants (Ibad) - you have no authority over them.' And listening (Sama') is a cause for the purity of the heart (Qalb), and it is a net for the Truth (Al-Haqq) by means of purity.
17:65.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

17:72.arabic: ولمشابهة بصيرة الباطن لبصيرة الظاهر قال الله تعالى ما كذب الفؤاد ما رأى وقال تعالى وكذلك نرى إبراهيم ملكوت السموات والأرض الآية وسمى ضده عمى فقال تعالى فإنها لا تعمى الأبصار ولكن تعمى القلوب التي في الصدور وقال تعالى ومن كان في هذه أعمى فهو في الآخرة أعمى وأضل سبيلا وهذه الأمور التي كشفت للأنبياء بعضها كان بالبصر وبعضها كان بالبصيرة وسمى الكل رؤية وبالجملة من لم تكن بصيرته الباطنة ثاقبة لم يعلق به من الدين إلا قشوره وأمثلته دون لبابه وحقائقه
17:72.english: And due to the similarity of the inner insight (Bassira) to the outer insight, Allah the Exalted said: 'The Heart (Fu'ad) did not lie about what it saw' [Quran 53:11], and He said: 'And thus We showed Abraham the dominion (Malakut) of the heavens and the earth' [Quran 6:75] the verse. And He named its opposite blindness, so He said: 'For indeed, it is not the eyes that become blind, but it is the Hearts (Qulub) in the chests that become blind' [Quran 22:46]. And He said: 'And whoever is blind in this [world] will be blind in the Hereafter and more astray in way' [Quran 17:72]. And these matters that were unveiled to the prophets, some of them were through sight (Basar) and some were through insight (Bassira), and He named all of it vision (Ru'ya). And in summary, whoever does not have their inner insight (Bassira) penetrating, nothing attaches to them from the religion except its outer shells (Qushur) and its examples without its core (Lubab) and its truths.
17:72.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

17:72.arabic: والمغرور هو الذي لم تنفتح بصيرته ليكون بهداية نفسه كفيلاً وبقي في العمى فاتخذ الهوى قائداً والشيطان دليلاً "ومن كان في هذه أعمى فهو في الآخرة أعمى وأضل سبيلا" وإذا عرف أن الغرور هو أم الشقاوات ومنبع المهلكات فلا بد من شرح مداخله ومجاريه وتفصيل ما يكثر من وقوع الغرور فيه، ليحذره المريد بعد معرفته فيتقيه، فالموفق من العباد من عرف مداخل الآفات والفساد فأخذ منها حذره وبنى على الحزم والبصيرة أمره.
17:72.english: And the deluded one (Al-Maghroor) is he whose insight (Bassirah) has not opened to be sufficient for the guidance of his soul (Nafs), and he remained in blindness (Al-'Amā), so he took desire (Al-Hawā) as a leader and Satan (Ash-Shaytān) as a guide. "And whoever is blind in this [world] will be blind in the Hereafter and more astray in way." And when it is known that delusion (Al-Ghuroor) is the mother of wretchednesses (Ash-Shaqawāt) and the source of destructions (Al-Mahlikāt), then it is necessary to explain its entrances and channels and detail what increases in the occurrence of delusion in it, so that the seeker (Al-Mureed) may beware of it after knowing it and thus avoid it. The successful one (Al-Muwaffaq) among the worshippers is he who knows the entrances of calamities (Al-Āfāt) and corruption (Al-Fasād), so he takes caution from them and builds his affair upon prudence (Al-Hazm) and insight (Al-Bassirah).
17:72.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

17:72.arabic: ولموازنة البصيرة الباطنة للبصر الظاهر سماه الله تعالى باسمه فقال ما كذب الفؤاد ما رأى سمى إدراك الفؤاد رؤية وكذلك قوله تعالى وكذلك نري إبراهيم ملكوت السموات والأرض وما أراد به الرؤية الظاهرة فإن ذلك غير مخصوص بإبراهيم عليه السلام حتى يعرض في معرض الامتنان ولذلك سمى ضد إدراكه عمى فقال تعالى فإنها لا تعمى الأبصار ولكن تعمى القلوب التي في الصدور وقال تعالى ومن كان في هذه أعمى فهو في الآخرة أعمى وأضل سبيلا فهذا بيان العلم العقلي أما العلوم الدينية فهي المأخوذة بطريق التقليد من الأنبياء صلوات الله عل
17:72.english: And due to the equivalence of the inner insight (Bassira) to the outer sight (Basar), Allah the Exalted named it with His name, saying: 'The heart (Fu'ad) did not lie about what it saw' - He called the perception of the heart (Fu'ad) 'seeing'. Likewise, His saying: 'And thus We showed Abraham the kingdom of the heavens and the earth' - and He did not intend by it the apparent vision, for that is not specific to Abraham (peace be upon him) to present in the context of favor. Therefore, He called the opposite of its perception 'blindness', saying: 'Indeed, it is not the eyes that are blind, but blind are the hearts (Qulub) which are in the breasts.' And He said: 'And whoever is blind in this [world] will be blind in the Hereafter and more astray in way.' This is the explanation of intellectual knowledge. As for religious sciences, they are taken through imitation (Taqleed) from the prophets (prayers and peace of Allah be upon them), and that is achieved by learning the Book of Allah the Exalted and the Sunnah of His Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) and understanding their meanings after hearing, and through this is the perfection of the attribute of the heart (Qalb) and its safety from ailments and diseases.
17:72.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

17:74.arabic: وقال الثوري فتنة الحديث أشد من فتنة الأهل والمال والولد وكيف لا تخاف فتنته وقد قيل لسيد المرسلين صلى الله عليه وسلم: (ولولا أن ثبتناك لقد كدت تركن إليهم شيئا قليلا( (الإسراء: 74)
17:74.english: And Thawri said: 'The trial (fitnah) of hadith is more severe than the trial of family, wealth, and children.' And how can one not fear its trial when it was said to the Master of the Messengers, peace be upon him: 'And if We had not made you firm, you would have almost inclined to them a little.' (Al-Isra: 74)
17:74.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Book of Knowledge'

17:75.arabic: وقوله عز وجل إذا لأذقناك ضعف الحياة وضعف الممات أي ضعف عذاب الأحياء وضعف عذاب الموتي فحذف العذاب وأبدل الأحياء والموتي بذكر الحياة والموت وكل ذلك جائز في فصيح اللغة
17:75.english: And His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'If [so], We would have made you taste double the life and double the death' means double the punishment of the living and double the punishment of the dead. So 'the punishment' is omitted, and 'the living' and 'the dead' are substituted with the mention of 'life' and 'death'. And all of that is permissible in eloquent language.
17:75.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

17:80.arabic: فإذا دخلها فليدخلها متواضعا معظما وليقل بسم الله وعلى ملة رسول الله ﭬ رب أدخلني مدخل صدق وأخرجني مخرج صدق واجعل لي من لدنك سلطانا نصيرا ثم يقصد المسجد ويدخله ويصلي بجنب المنبر ركعتين
17:80.english: So when he enters it, let him enter it humbly, honoring it, and let him say: 'In the name of Allah and upon the creed (Millah) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. O my Lord, cause me to enter a truthful entrance (Mudkhal Sidq) and bring me out a truthful exit (Mukhraj Sidq), and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority (Sultanan Nasiran).' Then he should head to the mosque and enter it and pray beside the pulpit two units of prayer.
17:80.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

17:82.arabic: وكان مالك بن دينار يقول: ما زرع القرآن في قلوبكم يا أهل القرآن إن القرآن ربيع المؤمن كما أن الغيث ربيع الأرض. وقال قتادة: لم يجالس أحد هذا القرآن إلا قام بزيادة أو نقصان قال تعالى ﴿ هو شفاء ورحمة للمؤمنين ولا يزيد الظالمين إلا خسارا ﴾ {}. الثامن: التأثر وهو أن يتأثر قلبه بآثار مختلفة بحسب اختلاف الآيات فيكون له بحسب كل فهم حال. ووجد يتصف به قلبه من الحزن والخوف والرجاء وغيره ومهما تمت معرفته كانت الخشية أغلب الأحوال على قلبه فإن التضييق غالب على آيات القرآن فلا يرى ذكر المغفرة والرحمة إلا مقرونا
17:82.english: And Malik bin Dinar used to say: What has the Quran planted in your hearts (Qulub), O people of the Quran? Indeed, the Quran is the spring (Rabi') of the believer (Mu'min) just as rain is the spring of the earth. And Qatada said: No one sits with this Quran except that he rises with either increase or decrease. Allah the Exalted said: 'It is healing (Shifa') and mercy (Rahmah) for the believers (Mu'minin) and it does not increase the wrongdoers (Zalimin) except in loss (Khasara).' The eighth: Being affected (Ta'aththur) - which is that his heart (Qalb) is affected by different effects according to the difference of the verses, so he has a state according to each understanding. And what is found that his heart (Qalb) is characterized by from sadness (Huzn), fear (Khawf), hope (Rajaa'), and other than that. And whenever his knowledge (Ma'rifah) is perfected, awe (Khashyah) becomes the predominant state upon his heart (Qalb), for restriction (Tadhiq) is predominant in the verses of the Quran, so he does not see the mention of forgiveness (Maghfirah) and mercy (Rahmah) except coupled with conditions that the knower (Arif) falls short of attaining, like His saying the Exalted: 'And indeed, I am Forgiving (Ghaffar)' then followed that with four conditions: 'for those who repent (Taba) and believe (Amana) and do righteous deeds (Amila Salihan) then are guided (Ihtada).'
17:82.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

17:84.arabic: وإنما يتفاوتون في درجات القرب لا في أصله وأقربهم إلى الله تعالى أعرفهم به وأعرفهم به لا بد وأن يكون أعبدهم له فمن عرفه لم يعبد غيره. والأصل في الأوراد في حق كل صنف من الناس المداومة فإن المراد منه تغيير الصفات الباطنة وآحاد الأعمال يقل آثارها بل لا يحس بآثارها وإنما يترتب الأثر على المجموع فإذا لم يعقب العمل الواحد أثرا محسوسا ولم يردف بثان وثالث على القرب انمحى الأثر الأول وكان كالفقيه يريد أن يكون فقيه النفس فإنه لا يصير فقيه النفس إلا بتكرار كثير فلو بالغ ليلة في التكرار وترك شهرا أو أسبوعا ث
17:84.english: And they only differ in degrees of closeness (Qurb), not in its essence. And the closest of them to Allah, the Exalted, is the most knowledgeable of Him, and the most knowledgeable of Him must necessarily be the most worshipful of Him, for whoever knows Him does not worship other than Him. The foundation in the spiritual litanies (Awrad) for every category of people is consistency (Mudawamah), for the intended purpose is to change the inner attributes (Sifat al-Batinah), and individual actions have little effect, indeed one does not perceive their effects. Rather, the effect is established upon the totality. So if a single action does not produce a perceptible effect and is not followed by a second and third in closeness (Qurb), the first effect is erased, and it is like the jurist who wants to be a jurist of the Soul (Nafs). For he does not become a jurist of the Soul (Nafs) except through much repetition. So if he intensifies repetition for one night and leaves it for a month or a week, then returns and intensifies for one night, this would not affect him. But if he distributed that amount over consecutive nights, it would affect him, and for this reason...
17:84.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

17:85.arabic: وجملة ما عرفوه قليل بالإضافة إلى ما عرفه محمد نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم وما عرفه الأنبياء كلهم قليل بالإضافة إلى ما عرفته الملائكة المقربون كإسرافيل وجبريل وغيرهما ثم جميع علوم الملائكة والجن والإنس إذا أضيف إلى علم الله سبحانه وتعالى لم يستحق أن يسمى علما بل هو إلى أن يسمى دهشا وحيرة وقصورا وعجزا أقرب فسبحان من عرف عباده ما عرف ثم خاطب جميعهم فقال وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا فهذا بيان معاقد الجمل التى تجول فيها فكر المتفكرين فى خلق الله تعالى وليس فيها فكر فى ذات الله تعالى ولكن يستفاد من الفك
17:85.english: And the entirety of what they knew is little in addition to what our Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) knew, and what all the Prophets knew is little in addition to what the close Angels (Al-Mala'ikah Al-Muqarrabun) like Israfil and Jibril and others knew. Then all the knowledges of the Angels, the Jinn, and the Humans, when added to the knowledge of Allah (Glory be to Him, the Exalted), do not deserve to be called knowledge; rather, it is closer to being called bewilderment (dahsh), perplexity (hayrah), deficiency (qusur), and incapacity ('ajz). So Glory be to the One who made known to His servants what He made known, then addressed all of them saying: 'And you have not been given of knowledge except a little.' This is an explanation of the nodal points of the sentences in which the thought of the thinkers wanders regarding the creation of Allah (the Exalted), and there is no thought in the Essence (Dhat) of Allah (the Exalted) in them, but from the thought in the creation inevitably comes knowledge of the Creator (Al-Khaliq) and His greatness (azamah), majesty (jalal), and power (qudrah). And whenever you increase in knowledge of the wondrous making (sana') of Allah (the Exalted), your knowledge of His majesty and greatness becomes more complete.
17:85.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Contemplation'

17:86.arabic: وكذلك الصوفية فقد كان الشبلي في مسجده ليلة من رمضان وهو يصلي خلف إمام له فقرأ الإمام ولئن شئنا لنذهبن بالذي أوحينا إليك فزعق الشبلي زعقة ظن الناس أنه قد طارت روحه واحمر وجهه وارتعدت فرائصه وكان يقول بمثل هذا يخاطب الأحباب يردد ذلك مرارا
17:86.english: And likewise the Sufis, for indeed Al-Shibli was in his mosque one night of Ramadan while he was praying behind his Imam, and the Imam recited: 'And if We willed, We could surely take away that which We have revealed to you' (Quran 17:86). So Al-Shibli cried out a cry such that the people thought his Spirit (Ruh) had flown away, and his face reddened, and his limbs trembled. And he would say: 'With such as this does He address the beloved ones,' repeating that many times.
17:86.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

17:88.arabic: وليس لنبي معجزة باقية سواه صلى الله عليه وسلم إذ تحدى بها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بلغاء الخلق وفصحاء العرب وجزيرة العرب حينئذ مملوءة بآلاف منهم والفصاحة صنعتهم وبها منافستهم ومباهاتهم وكان ينادي بين أظهرهم أن يأتوا بمثله ولو كان بعضهم لبعض ظهيرا وقال ذلك تعجيزا لهم فعجزوا عن ذلك وصرفوا عنه حتى عرضوا أنفسهم للقتل ونساءهم وذراريهم للسبي وما استطاعوا أن يعارضوا ولا أن يقدحوا في جزالته وحسنه ثم انتشر ذلك بعده في أقطار العالم شرقا وغربا قرنا بعد قرن وعصرا بعد عصر وقد انقرض اليوم قريب من خمسمائة
17:88.english: And there is no remaining miracle for any prophet except his (peace be upon him), since the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) challenged with it the eloquent of creation and the eloquent speakers of the Arabs, and the Arabian Peninsula at that time was filled with thousands of them, and eloquence was their craft, and with it was their competition and boasting. And he was proclaiming among them that they should bring the like of it, even if some of them were helpers (ظهيرا) to others, and he said that to incapacitate them, so they were incapacitated from that and turned away from it until they exposed themselves to killing and their women and children to captivity, and they were not able to oppose it nor to find fault in its strength and beauty. Then that spread after him in the regions of the world east and west, century after century and era after era, and today nearly five hundred years have passed, and no one has been able to oppose it.
17:88.book_title: Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character
17:88.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character'

17:94.arabic: السبب الرابع: التعجب، كما أخبر الله تعالى عن الأمم السالفة إذ قالوا "ما أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا" "وقالوا أنؤمن لبشرين مثلنا" "ولئن أطعتم بشراً مثلكم إنكم إذاً لخاسرون" فتعجبوا من أن يفوز برتبة الرسالة والوحي والقرب من الله تعالى بشر مثلهم فحسدوهم، وأحبوا زوال النبوة عنهم جزعاً أن يفضل عليهم من هو مثلهم في الخلقة، لا عن قصد تكبر وطلب رياسة وتقدم عداوة أو سبب آخر من سائر الأسباب، وقالوا متعجبين "أبعث الله بشراً رسولاً" وقالوا "لولا أنزل علينا الملائكة" وقال تعالى "أو عجبتم أن جاءكم ذكر من ربكم على رجل
17:94.english: The fourth cause: Astonishment (Ta'ajjub), as Allah the Exalted informed about the past nations when they said, 'You are only human beings like us' and 'They said: Shall we believe in two human beings like ourselves?' and 'And if you obey a human being like yourselves, then indeed you would be losers.' So they were astonished that a human being like them would attain the rank of Messengership, Revelation, and closeness to Allah the Exalted, so they envied them, and they desired the removal of Prophethood from them out of distress that one who is like them in creation would be favored over them, not from an intention of arrogance, seeking leadership, advancing enmity, or any other cause from the rest of the causes, and they said in astonishment, 'Has Allah sent a human being as a Messenger?' and they said, 'Why were not angels sent down to us?' and Allah the Exalted said, 'Or do you wonder that there has come to you a Remembrance (Dhikr) from your Lord upon a man from among you?' the verse.
17:94.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

17:100.arabic: وقيل رأى أيوب السختياني جنازة عاص فدخل الدهليز كيلا يصلي عليها فرأى الميت بعضهم في المنام فقيل له ما فعل الله بك قال غفر لي وقال قل لأيوب: ﴿ قل لو أنتم تملكون خزائن رحمة ربي إذا لأمسكتم خشية الإنفاق ﴾ {}
17:100.english: And it was said: Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani saw the funeral procession of 'As, so he entered the corridor so as not to pray over it. Then the deceased was seen by some of them in a dream, and it was said to him: 'What has Allah done with you?' He said: 'He forgave me, and said: Say to Ayyub: "Say: If you possessed the treasuries of the mercy of my Lord, then you would withhold out of fear of spending." {}'
17:100.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Book of Repentance'

17:108.arabic: فقال: وأنت فحياك الله يا هرم بن حيان كيف أنت يا أخي ومن دلك علي؟ قلت الله فقال: لا إله إلا الله سبحان الله "إن كان وعد ربنا لمفعولا" قال: فعجبت حين عرفني ولا والله ما رأيته قبل ذلك ولا رآني! فقلت: من أين عرفت اسمي واسم أبي وما رأيتك قبل اليوم؟ "قال نبأني العليم الخبير" وعرفت روحي روحك حين كلمت نفسي نفسك، إن الأرواح لها أنفس كأنفس الأجساد وإن المؤمنين ليعرف بعضهم بعضاً ويتحابون بروح الله وإن لم يلتقوا، يتعارفون ويتكلمون وإن نأت بهم الدار وتفرقت بهم المنازل
17:108.english: He said: And you, may Allah give you life, O Hirm ibn Hayyan, how are you, O my brother, and who guided you to me? I said: Allah. He said: There is no god but Allah, glory be to my Lord (Subhan Rabbi), "Indeed, the promise of our Lord is to be fulfilled (in kana wa'du rabbina lamaf'ulan)." He said: So I was amazed when he recognized me, and by Allah, I had not seen him before that, nor had he seen me! I said: From where did you know my name and my father's name, and I have not seen you before today? "He said: The All-Knowing, the All-Aware informed me (nabba'ni al-'alim al-khabir)." And my spirit (ruhi) recognized your spirit (ruhak) when my soul (nafsi) spoke to your soul (nafsak), for the spirits (al-arwah) have souls (anfus) like the souls of the bodies, and indeed the believers (al-mu'minun) recognize each other and love each other through the spirit of Allah (bi-ruh Allah), even if they do not meet; they become acquainted and speak, even if the abode distances them and the dwellings separate them.
17:108.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of the World'

17:109.arabic: وأكمله أن يكبر فيسجد ويدعو في سجوده بما يليق بالآية التي قرأها مثل أن يقرأ قوله تعالى: ﴿ خروا سجدا وسبحوا بحمد ربهم وهم لا يستكبرون ﴾ {} فيقول اللهم اجعلني من الساجدين لوجهك المسبحين بحمدك وأعوذ بك أن أكون من المستكبرين عن أمرك أو على أوليائك وإذا قرأ قوله تعالى: ﴿ ويخرون للأذقان يبكون ويزيدهم خشوعا ﴾ {} فيقول اللهم اجعلني من الباكين إليك الخاشعين لك وكذلك كل سجدة ويشترط في هذه السجدة شروط الصلاة من ستر العورة واستقبال القبلة وطهارة الثوب والبدن من الحدث والخبث ومن لم يكن على طهارة عند السماع فإ
17:109.english: And its perfection is that he says 'Allahu Akbar' and prostrates and supplicates in his prostration with what is appropriate to the verse he recited, such as when he recites the saying of the Exalted: 'They fall down prostrating and glorify with the praise of their Lord and they do not show arrogance' (Quran 38:24), then he says: 'O Allah, make me among those who prostrate to Your Face, those who glorify with Your praise, and I seek refuge in You from being among those who show arrogance against Your command or against Your allies.' And if he recites the saying of the Exalted: 'And they fall down on their chins weeping, and it increases them in humility (Khushu')' (Quran 17:109), then he says: 'O Allah, make me among those who weep to You, those who are humble (Khashi'un) to You.' And likewise for every prostration. And it is stipulated for this prostration the conditions of prayer: covering the private parts, facing the Qibla, and purity of the garment and the body from ritual impurity (Hadath) and filth (Khabath). And whoever is not in a state of purity at the time of hearing, then when he becomes pure, he prostrates. And it has been said regarding its perfection that he says 'Allahu Akbar' raising his hands for its prohibition, then he says 'Allahu Akbar' for the inclination to prostration, then he says 'Allahu Akbar' for rising, then he says the salutation. And some added the Tashahhud, but there is no basis for this except analogy to the prostration of prayer, and it is far-fetched, for the command has come regarding prostration, so let him follow the command therein, and the 'Allahu Akbar' for the inclination is closer to the beginning, and what is besides that has distance in it. Then the follower (Ma'mum) should prostrate at the prostration of the Imam and not prostrate for his own recitation if he is a follower.
17:109.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

17:110.arabic: الرابع: خفض الصوت بين المخافتة والجهر لما روى أن أبا موسى الأشعري قال قدمنا مع رسول الله فلما دنونا من المدينة كبر وكبر الناس ورفعوا أصواتهم فقال النبي ﷺ: (يا أيها الناس إن الذي تدعون ليس بأصم ولا غائب إن الذي تدعون بينكم وبين أعناق ركابكم) وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنه في قوله عز وجل: ﴿ ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها ﴾ {} أي بدعائك وقد أثنى الله عز وجل على نبيه زكرياء عليه السلام حيث قال: ﴿ إذ نادى ربه نداء خفيا ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل: ﴿ ادعوا ربكم تضرعا وخفية ﴾ {}.
17:110.english: Fourth: Lowering the voice between whispering and loudness, because it was narrated that Abu Musa al-Ash'ari said: 'We arrived with the Messenger of Allah, and when we approached Medina, he said takbir and the people said takbir and raised their voices.' The Prophet ﷺ said: 'O people, the One you are calling is not deaf nor absent; the One you are calling is between you and the necks of your mounts.' And Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said regarding the saying of Allah the Exalted: 'And do not be loud in your prayer (Salah) nor whisper it' {} meaning in your supplication (Du'a). And Allah the Exalted praised His prophet Zakariya, peace be upon him, when He said: 'When he called upon his Lord with a secret call' {} and Allah the Exalted said: 'Call upon your Lord humbly and secretly' {}.
17:110.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure

17:110.arabic: وقال عز وجل: ﴿ قل ادعوا الله أو ادعوا الرحمن أيا ما تدعوا فله الأسماء الحسنى ﴾ {} وروى النعمان بن بشير عن النبي ﭬ أنه قال: (إن الدعاء هو العبادة ثم قرأ: ﴿ ادعوني أستجب لكم ﴾ {}[65]) الآية. وقال ﭬ: (الدعاء مخ العبادة[66]) وروى أبو هريرة أنه ﭬ قال: (ليس شيء أكرم على الله عز وجل من الدعاء[67]) وقال ﭬ: (إن العبد لا يخطئه من الدعاء إحدى ثلاث إما ذنب يغفر له وإما خير يعجل له وإما خير يدخر له[68]) وقال أبو ذر رضي الله عنه يكفي من الدعاء مع البر ما يكفي الطعام من الملح. وقال ﭬ: (سلوا الله تعالى من فضله
17:110.english: And the Mighty and Majestic said: 'Say: Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Merciful (Ar-Rahman); whichever you call upon, to Him belong the Most Beautiful Names (Al-Asma' Al-Husna).' And Nu'man bin Bashir narrated from the Prophet (peace be upon him) that he said: 'Indeed, the Supplication (Ad-Du'a) is the Worship (Al-'Ibadah),' then he recited: 'Call upon Me, I will respond to you.' The verse. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Supplication (Ad-Du'a) is the marrow of Worship (Al-'Ibadah).' And Abu Hurairah narrated that he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing more honorable to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, than Supplication (Ad-Du'a).' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The servant (Al-'Abd) does not miss from Supplication (Ad-Du'a) one of three: either a sin (Dhanb) is forgiven for him, or a good (Khayr) is hastened for him, or a good (Khayr) is stored for him.' And Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'Sufficient for Supplication (Ad-Du'a) with righteousness (Al-Birr) is what suffices food from salt.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Ask Allah, the Exalted, from His bounty, for indeed Allah, the Exalted, loves to be asked, and the best Worship (Al-'Ibadah) is awaiting relief (Al-Faraj).'
17:110.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication

17:110.arabic: [83] حديث عائشة في قوله تعالى ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها أي بدعائك متفق عليه.
17:110.english: [83] The Hadith of Aisha regarding His saying, the Exalted: 'And do not raise your voice in your prayer (Salah) nor lower it excessively' meaning in your supplication (Du'a) - agreed upon.
17:110.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication

17:111.arabic: وقد ذكرنا أن ذلك عصيان وعدوان لا لأن طلب الدنيا حرام ولكن طلبها بأعمال الدين حرام لما فيه من الرياء وتغيير العبادة عن موضعها وأما لفظ الشركة حيث ورد فمطلق للتساوي وقد بينا أنه إذا تساوى القصدان تقاوما ولم يكن له ولا عليه فلا ينبغي أن يرجي عليه ثواب ثم إن الإنسان عند الشركة أبدا في خطر فإنه لا يدري أي الأمرين أغلب على قصده فربما يكون عليه وبالا ولذلك قال تعالى (فمن كان يرجو لقاء ربه فليعمل عملا صالحا ولا يشرك بعبادة ربه أحدا) أي لا يرجي اللقاء مع الشركة التى أحسن أحوالها التساقط.
17:111.english: And we have mentioned that that is disobedience and transgression, not because seeking the worldly life (Dunya) is forbidden, but seeking it through acts of religion is forbidden due to what it contains of showing off (Riya) and changing worship from its proper place. As for the term partnership (Shirkah) where it occurs, it is absolute for equality, and we have clarified that if the two intentions are equal, they cancel each other out, and there is neither for him nor against him, so one should not hope for reward upon it. Then indeed, the human being in partnership is always in danger, for he does not know which of the two matters is more dominant in his intention; perhaps it will be a calamity upon him. And for that reason, Allah the Exalted said: 'So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone' (Quran 18:110), meaning do not hope for the meeting with the partnership whose best state is cancellation.
17:111.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

17:111.arabic: ولنرجع الآن إلى الغرض فإن المقصود ذكر نعم الله تعالى في الأكل فقد
17:111.english: And let us return now to the purpose, for the intended is the mention of the blessings of Allah the Exalted in eating, indeed
17:111.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

17:111.arabic: وقوله سبحانه: ﴿ الحمد لله الذي لم يتخذ ولدا ﴾ {}[31] الآية
17:111.english: And His saying, the Exalted: 'Praise be to Allah who has not taken a son' {}[31] the verse
17:111.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Book of Knowledge'

17:111.arabic: [31]  حديث فضل الحمد لله الذي لم يتخذ ولدا الآية أخرجه أحمد والطبراني من حديث معاذ بن أنس آية العز الحمد لله الذي لم يتخذ ولدا الآية كلها وإسناده ضعيف.
17:111.english: Hadith of virtue: 'Al-Hamdulillahi alladhi lam yattakhidh waladan' (Praise be to Allah who has not taken a son) the verse, transmitted by Ahmad and Al-Tabarani from the narration of Mu'adh ibn Anas: 'The verse of honor: Al-Hamdulillahi alladhi lam yattakhidh waladan' (Praise be to Allah who has not taken a son) the entire verse, and its chain is weak.
17:111.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Book of Knowledge'

17:111.arabic: وَقُلِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي لَمْ يَتَّخِذْ وَلَدًا وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ شَرِيكٌ فِي الْمُلْكِ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ وَلِيٌّ مِنَ الذُّلِّ ۖ وَكَبِّرْهُ تَكْبِيرًا
17:111.english: And say: 'Praise be to Allah who has not taken a son, and there is no partner for Him in the dominion, and there is no protector for Him from humiliation, and magnify Him with magnification.'
17:111.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

18:7.arabic: وقال عز وجل: " إنا جعلنا ما على الأرض زينة لها لنبلوهم أيهم أحسن عملاً ". قيل: معناه أيهم أزهد فيها، فوصف الزهد بأنه من أحسن الأعمال.
18:7.english: And He (Allah), the Mighty and Majestic, said: "Indeed, We have made what is on the earth an adornment (zīnah) for it to test them as to which of them is best in deed." It is said: Its meaning is 'which of them is most ascetic (azhad) in it,' thus describing asceticism (al-zuhd) as being among the best of deeds.
18:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

18:7.arabic: والمقصود من هذا: أن الزيادة على قدر الحاجة إنما تأتيك ابتلاء وفتنة لينظر الله إليك ماذا تعمل فيه، وقدر الحاجة يأتيك رفقاً بك، فلا تغفل عن الفرق بين الرفق والابتلاء. قال الله تعالى: " إنا جعلنا ما على الأرض زينة لها لنبلوهم أيهم أحسن عملاً ".
18:7.english: The intended meaning from this is: That the increase beyond the measure of need only comes to you as a trial (Ibtila') and temptation (Fitnah) so that Allah may look at you [to see] what you will do with it, and the measure of need comes to you as gentleness (Rifq) with you, so do not be heedless of the difference between gentleness (Rifq) and trial (Ibtila'). Allah the Exalted said: "Indeed, We have made that which is on the earth adornment for it that We may test them [as to] which of them is best in deed."
18:7.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

18:10.arabic: وتقول عند ابتداء الأمور ﴿ ربنا آتنا من لدنك رحمة وهيىء لنا من أمرنا رشدا ﴾ {} رب اشرح لي صدري ويسر لي أمري ﴾ {}
18:10.english: And say at the beginning of matters: 'Our Lord, grant us from Your presence mercy and prepare for us from our affair right guidance (Rashd).' {} 'My Lord, expand for me my breast and ease for me my affair.' {}
18:10.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

18:10.arabic: ربنا آتنا من لدنك رحمة وهيئ لنا من أمرنا رشدا
18:10.english: Our Lord, grant us mercy from Your presence and prepare for us from our affair right guidance (Rashd).
18:10.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

18:13.arabic: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: ما آتي الله عز وجل عبدا علما إلا شابا والخير كله في الشباب ثم تلا قوله عز وجل: ﴿ قالوا سمعنا فتى يذكرهم يقال له إبراهيم ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ إنهم فتية آمنوا بربهم وزدناهم هدى ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ وآتيناه الحكم صبيا ﴾ {}
18:13.english: And Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: 'Allah the Exalted does not give knowledge to a servant except when he is young, and all good is in youth.' Then he recited the saying of the Exalted: 'They said: We heard a youth (Fata) mentioning them; he is called Ibrahim' (Quran 21:60), and His saying: 'Indeed they were youths (Fityah) who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance' (Quran 18:13), and His saying: 'And We gave him wisdom (Hukm) while a boy (Sabiyy)' (Quran 19:12).
18:13.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Purity'

18:15.arabic: وقد سوى الله تعالى بين من افترى على الله كذبا وبين من كذب بالحق فقال تعالى: (ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بالحق لما جاءه( (العنكبوت: 68). وقال تعالى: (فمن أظلم ممن كذب على الله وكذب بالصدق إذ جاءه( (الزمر: 32).
18:15.english: And Allah the Exalted has equated between one who fabricates lies against Allah and one who denies the truth, as He said: 'And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah or denies the truth when it has come to him?' (Al-Ankabut: 68). And He said: 'So who is more unjust than one who lies about Allah and denies the truth when it comes to him?' (Az-Zumar: 32).
18:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Book of Knowledge'

18:16.arabic: فهؤلاء جميع أحوالهم تصلح أن تكون سببا لازيادهم فلا تتميز عندهم عبادة عن عبادة وهم الذين فروا إلى الله عز وجل كما قال تعالى: ﴿ لعلكم تذكرون ﴾ {} ففروا إلى الله وتحقق فيهم قوله تعالى: ﴿ وإذ اعتزلتموهم وما يعبدون إلا الله فأووا إلى الكهف ينشر لكم ربكم من رحمته ﴾ {} وإليه الإشارة بقوله: ﴿ إني ذاهب إلى ربي سيهدين ﴾ {} وهذه منتهى درجات الصديقين ولا وصول إليها إلا بعد ترتيب الأوراد والمواظبة عليها دهرا طويلا فلا ينبغي أن يغتر المريد بما سمعه من ذلك فيدعيه لنفسه ويفتر عن وظائف عبادته فذلك علامته أن لا ي
18:16.english: For these people, all their states (ahwal) become suitable to be a cause for their increase, so no worship (ibadah) is distinguished from another worship for them. They are the ones who fled to Allah (Allah) the Exalted in Might, as He said: 'That you may remember' (Quran 18:24). So they fled to Allah, and His saying is realized in them: 'And when you withdraw from them and that which they worship except Allah, then take refuge in the cave; your Lord will spread for you of His mercy (rahmah) and will prepare for you from your affair a comfort (mirfaq)' (Quran 18:16). And to this is the indication by His saying: 'Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me' (Quran 37:99). And this is the utmost degrees of the truthful ones (siddiqin), and there is no reaching it except after arranging the litanies (awrad) and persisting in them for a long time. So it is not appropriate for the seeker (murid) to be deceived by what he heard of that and claim it for himself and become negligent in the duties of his worship. Its sign is that no whisper (waswas) stirs in his heart (qalb), nor does a sin (ma'siyah) occur to his heart, nor do the assaults of terrors (hawal) alarm him, nor do the great affairs (ashghal) agitate him. And how is this rank (rutbah) granted to everyone? So it is incumbent upon all to arrange the litanies as we have mentioned.
18:16.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

18:16.arabic: فإذن كيف يستدل باعتزال الكفار والأصنام على اعتزال المسلمين مع كثرة البركة فيهم واحتجوا أيضا بقول موسى عليه السلام وإن لم تؤمنوا لي فاعتزلون وأنه فزع إلى العزلة عند اليأس منهم وقال تعالى في أصحاب الكهف وإذا اعتزلتموهم وما يعبدون إلا الله فأووا إلى الكهف ينشر لكم ربكم من رحمته أمرهم بالعزلة وقد اعتزل نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم قريشا لما آذوه وجفوه ودخل الشعب وأمر أصحابه باعتزالهم والهجرة إلى أرض الحبشة
18:16.english: So then, how can one argue for seclusion from the disbelievers and idols to justify seclusion from the Muslims, given the abundance of blessing (Barakah) among them? They also cited the saying of Moses, peace be upon him: 'And if you do not believe me, then leave me alone' (Quran 7:79), and that he resorted to seclusion when he despaired of them. And Allah the Exalted said regarding the Companions of the Cave: 'And when you have withdrawn from them and that which they worship except Allah, then take refuge in the cave; your Lord will spread out for you of His mercy and will prepare for you from your affair a comfort' (Quran 18:16). He commanded them to seclusion. And indeed, our Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, withdrew from Quraysh when they harmed and shunned him, and he entered the valley (al-Shi'b), and he commanded his companions to withdraw from them and emigrate to the land of Abyssinia.
18:16.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Seclusion'

18:19.arabic: واستعمل عمر بن عبد العزيز رجلا فقيل كان عاملا للحجاج فعزله فقال الرجل إنما عملت له شيء يسير فقال له عمر حسبك بصحبته يوما أو بعض يوم شؤما وشرا
18:19.english: Umar bin Abdul Aziz appointed a man, and it was said he had worked for Al-Hajjaj, so he dismissed him. The man said, 'I only worked for him for a little thing.' Umar said to him, 'Your companionship with him for a day or part of a day is enough for misfortune and evil.'
18:19.topic: Al-Ghazali on the outer and inner dimensions of worship, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

18:23.arabic: الوجه الثاني: التأدب بذكر الله تعالى في كل حال وإحالة الأمور كلها إلى مشيئة الله سبحانه فقد أدب الله سبحانه نبيه ﭬ فقال تعالى: ﴿ ولا تقولن لشيء إني فاعل ذلك غدا إلا أن يشاء الله ﴾ {} ثم لم يقتصر على ذلك فيما لا يشك فيه بل قال تعالى: ﴿ لتدخلن المسجد الحرام إن شاء الله آمنين محلقين رءؤسكم ومقصرين ﴾ {} وكان الله سبحانه عالما بأنهم يدخلون لا محالة وأنه شاءه ولكن المقصود تعليمه ذلك فتأدب رسول الله ﭬ في ما كان يخبر عنه معلوما كان أو مشكوكا حتى قال ﭬ لما دخل المقابر: (السلام عليكم دار قوم مؤمنين وإنا إ
18:23.english: The second aspect: The etiquette of mentioning Allah (God) the Exalted in every state and referring all matters to the will of Allah (God) the Glorified. Indeed, Allah (God) the Glorified taught etiquette to His Prophet (peace be upon him) when He the Exalted said: 'And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow," except [when adding], "If Allah (God) wills."' Then He did not restrict that to matters about which there is no doubt, but rather said: 'You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if Allah (God) wills, in safety, with your heads shaved and [hair] shortened.' And Allah (God) the Glorified was knowing that they would enter inevitably and that He willed it, but the intended purpose was teaching him that. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) observed etiquette in what he would inform about, whether it was known or doubtful, until he (peace be upon him) said when he entered the graveyards: 'Peace be upon you, O abode of believing people, and we, if Allah (God) wills, will be joining you.' And joining them is not a matter of doubt, but the requirement of etiquette is mentioning Allah (God) the Exalted and linking matters to Him. And this formulation indicates that, until it became, by customary usage, an expression for showing desire and wish. So if it is said to you that so-and-so will die quickly, and you say 'If Allah (God) wills,' it is understood from it your desire, not your doubt. And if it is said to you that so-and-so's illness will depart and he will recover, and you say 'If Allah (God) wills' with the meaning of desire, then the word has shifted from the meaning of doubt to the meaning of desire, and likewise the shift to the meaning of etiquette for mentioning Allah (God) the Exalted, however the matter may be.
18:23.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

18:24.arabic: إلا أن يشاء الله فيحسدونه ويبغون عليه ويتشاءمون به فإذن الأمر أمر الله والقضاء قضاؤه وعصمه الله من كل ما تخوفت عليه من أمر الدنيا والدين
18:24.english: Except that Allah wills (Insha'Allah), so they envy him and bear malice against him and consider him an ill omen. So indeed the matter is Allah's matter and the decree is His decree, and Allah protected him from everything I feared for him regarding worldly matters and religion.
18:24.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Book of Repentance'

18:28.arabic: وكان أحدهم يعرض لهم المال الحلال فلا يأخذه ويقول: أخاف أن يفسد على قلبي، فمن كان له قلب فهو لا محالة يخاف من فساده، والذين أمات حب الدنيا قلوبهم فقد أخبر الله عنهم إذ قال تعالى: " ورضوا بالحياة الدنيا واطمأنوا بها والذين هم عن آياتنا غافلون ". وقال عز وجل: " ولا تطمع من أغفلنا قلبه عن ذكرنا واتبع هواه وكان أمره فرطاً ". وقال تعالى: " فأعرض عمن تولى عن ذكرنا ولم يرد إلا الحياة الدنيا، ذلك مبلغهم من العلم"، فأحال ذلك كله على الغفلة وعدم العلم، ولذلك قال رجل لعيسى عليه السلام: احملني معك في سياحتك،
18:28.english: And one of them would be offered lawful wealth but would not take it, saying: 'I fear it will corrupt my Heart (Qalb).' So whoever has a Heart (Qalb) inevitably fears its corruption. And those whose Hearts (Qalb) have been killed by the love of the worldly life, Allah has informed about them when He said, the Exalted: 'And they are content with the worldly life and feel secure with it, and those who are heedless of Our signs.' And He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'And do not obey one whose Heart (Qalb) We have made heedless of Our Remembrance (Dhikr) and who follows his own desire (Hawa) and whose affair is ever [in] neglect.' And He, the Exalted, said: 'So turn away from whoever turns away from Our Remembrance (Dhikr) and desires not except the worldly life. That is their extent of knowledge.' So He attributed all of that to heedlessness (Ghafala) and lack of knowledge, and for that reason a man said to Jesus, peace be upon him: 'Take me with you in your journeying.' He said: 'Bring out your wealth and follow me.' He said: 'I am not able.' So Jesus, peace be upon him, said: 'It is amazing that a rich man enters Paradise' - or he said: 'with difficulty.'
18:28.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

18:28.arabic: ولما قالت سادات العرب وأغنياؤهم للنبي صلى الله  عليه  وسلم:  اجعل  لنا  يوماً ولهم يوماً يجيئون إليك ولا نجيء، ونجيء إليك ولا يجيئون،  يعنون  بذلك  الفقراء مثل بلال وسليمان وصهيب وأبي ذر وخباب بن  الأرت  وعمار  بن  ياسر وأبي  هريرة وأصحاب الصفة من الفقراء رضي الله عنهم أجمعين  أجابهم  النبي  صلى  الله  عليه وسلم إلى ذلك، وذلك لأنهم شكوا إليه التأذي برائحتهم وكان لباس القوم الصوف  في شدة الحر؛ فإذا عرقوا فاحت الروائح من ثيابهم، فاشتد  ذلك  على  الأغنياء  منهم الأقرع بن حابس التميمي وعيينة بن حصن
18:28.english: And when the chiefs of the Arabs and the wealthy said to the Prophet (peace be upon him): 'Make for us a day and for them a day, they come to you and we do not come, and we come to you and they do not come,' meaning by that the poor like Bilal, Sulayman, Suhayb, Abu Dharr, Khabbab bin Al-Arat, Ammar bin Yasir, Abu Hurairah, and the People of the Suffah from the poor (may Allah be pleased with them all), the Prophet (peace be upon him) answered them to that, and that is because they complained to him of being harmed by their smell, and the clothing of the people was wool in intense heat; so when they sweated, the odors emanated from their clothes, and that became severe upon the wealthy among them like Al-Aqra' bin Habis At-Tamimi, Uyaynah bin Hisn Al-Fazari, Abbas bin Mirdas As-Sulami, and others. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) answered them that he would not gather them and them in one gathering; then descended His saying, the Exalted: 'And have patience (Sabr) with your Soul (Nafs) with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, desiring His Face (Wajh), and do not turn your eyes away from them' meaning the poor 'desiring the adornment (Zinah) of the worldly life (Al-Hayat Ad-Dunya)' meaning the wealthy 'and do not obey he whose Heart (Qalb) We have made heedless of Our Remembrance (Dhikr)' meaning the wealthy up to His saying: 'And say, "The truth is from your Lord, so whoever wills - let him believe; and whoever wills - let him disbelieve."' [23] the verse.
18:28.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

18:28.arabic: [23]  حديث قال سادات العرب وأغنياؤهم للنبي ﭬ اجعل لنا يوما ولهم يوما الحديث في نزول قوله تعالى - واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم - الآية تقدم من حديث خباب وليس فيه أنه كان لباسهم الصوف ويفوح ريحهم إذا عرفوا وهذه الزيادة من حديث سلمان.
18:28.english: [23] A hadith: The chiefs and wealthy of the Arabs said to the Prophet (peace be upon him): 'Appoint a day for us and a day for them.' The hadith concerns the revelation of His saying, the Exalted: 'And restrain your Soul (Nafs) with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, desiring His Face, and let not your eyes pass beyond them, desiring the adornment of the worldly life.
