And do not obey one whose Heart (Qalb) We have made heedless of Our Remembrance (Dhikr) and who follows his desire and whose affair is ever [in] neglect.' The hadith is previously mentioned from the narration of Khabbab, and it does not contain that their garment was wool and their scent would diffuse when they were known, and this addition is from the hadith of Salman.
18:28.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

18:29.arabic: ولما قالت سادات العرب وأغنياؤهم للنبي صلى الله  عليه  وسلم:  اجعل  لنا  يوماً ولهم يوماً يجيئون إليك ولا نجيء، ونجيء إليك ولا يجيئون،  يعنون  بذلك  الفقراء مثل بلال وسليمان وصهيب وأبي ذر وخباب بن  الأرت  وعمار  بن  ياسر  وأبي  هريرة وأصحاب الصفة من الفقراء رضي الله عنهم أجمعين  أجابهم  النبي  صلى  الله  عليه وسلم إلى ذلك، وذلك لأنهم شكوا إليه التأذي برائحتهم وكان لباس القوم الصوف  في شدة الحر؛ فإذا عرقوا فاحت الروائح من ثيابهم، فاشتد  ذلك  على  الأغنياء  منهم الأقرع بن حابس التميمي وعيينة بن حصن
18:29.english: And when the chiefs of the Arabs and the wealthy said to the Prophet (peace be upon him): 'Appoint for us a day and for them a day, they come to you and we do not come, and we come to you and they do not come,' meaning by that the poor like Bilal, Sulayman, Suhayb, Abu Dharr, Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, 'Ammar ibn Yasir, Abu Hurayrah, and the People of the Bench from the poor (may Allah be pleased with them all), the Prophet (peace be upon him) answered them to that, and that is because they complained to him of being harmed by their odor, and the clothing of the people was wool in intense heat; so when they sweated, the smells emanated from their clothes, and that became severe upon the wealthy among them like al-Aqra' ibn Habis al-Tamimi, 'Uyaynah ibn Hisn al-Fazari, 'Abbas ibn Mirdas al-Sulami, and others, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) answered them not to gather them and them in one assembly; then descended His saying, the Exalted: 'And restrain your Soul (Nafs) with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, desiring His Face, and do not turn your eyes away from them' meaning the poor 'desiring the adornment of the worldly life' meaning the wealthy 'and do not obey he whose Heart (Qalb) We have made heedless of Our Remembrance (Dhikr)' meaning the wealthy until His saying: 'And say, "The truth is from your Lord, so whoever wills - let him believe, and whoever wills - let him disbelieve."' the verse.
18:29.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

18:30.arabic: وقال تعالى: ﴿ إنا لا نضيع أجر من أحسن عملا ﴾ {} ولا حجة لهم في ذلك فإنه حيث ذكر الإيمان في هذه الآيات أريد به الإيمان مع العمل إذ بينا أن الإيمان قد يطلق ويراد به الإسلام وهو الموافقة بالقلب والقول والعمل ودليل هذا التأويل أخبار كثيرة في معاقبة العاصين ومقادير العقاب وقوله ﭬ: (يخرج من النار من كان في قلبه مثقال ذرة من إيمان) فكيف يخرج إذا لم يدخل ومن القرآن قوله تعالى: ﴿ إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء ﴾ {} والاستثناء بالمشيئة يدل على الانقسام
18:30.english: And He (Exalted) said: 'Indeed, We do not waste the reward of one who does good work' (Quran 18:30). And they have no proof in that, for when faith (Iman) is mentioned in these verses, what is intended is faith with action, since we have clarified that faith may be used and intended as Islam, which is agreement with the heart (Qalb), speech, and action. Evidence for this interpretation is many reports about punishing the disobedient and the measures of punishment, and His saying (peace be upon him): 'He will exit from the Fire whoever has in his heart (Qalb) an atom's weight of faith (Iman)' – so how would he exit if he did not enter? And from the Quran, His saying (Exalted): 'Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills' (Quran 4:48). The exception with will (Mashiyyah) indicates division.
18:30.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

18:30.arabic: وقوله تعالى: ﴿ إنا لا نضيع أجر من أحسن عملا ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ إن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين ﴾ {} فكيف يضيع أجر أصل الإيمان وجميع الطاعات بمعصية واحدة
18:30.english: And His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, We do not waste the reward of one who does good deeds' (Quran 18:30) and His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, Allah does not waste the reward of the doers of good' (Quran 12:90). So how can the reward of the foundation of faith (Iman) and all acts of obedience (Taa'at) be wasted by a single act of disobedience (Ma'siyah)?
18:30.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Foundations of Belief'

18:31.arabic: [234] حديث في قوله تعالى - يحلون فيها من أساور من ذهب - قال إن عليهم التيجان أدنى لؤلؤة فيها تضىء ما بين المشرق والمغرب أخرجه الترمذى من حديث أبى سعيد دون ذكر الآية وقال لا نعرفه إلا من حديث رشد بن سعد.
18:31.english: [234] A hadith regarding His statement - 'They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold' - he said: 'Upon them are crowns, the smallest pearl in them illuminates what is between the east and the west.' Al-Tirmidhi transmitted it from the narration of Abu Sa'id without mentioning the verse, and he said: 'We do not know it except from the narration of Rashid ibn Sa'd.'
18:31.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Book of Repentance'

18:31.arabic: وقال ﭬ فى قوله تعالى: ﴿ يحلون فيها من أساور من ذهب ﴾ {} قال: (إن عليهم التيجان إن أدنى لؤلؤة فيها تضىء ما بين المشرق والمغرب[234])
18:31.english: And he (the Prophet, peace be upon him) said regarding His (Allah's) statement: 'They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold' {} He said: 'Indeed upon them are crowns; the lowest pearl therein illuminates what is between the east and the west[234].'
18:31.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Book of Repentance'

18:34.arabic: الخامس الكبر بالمال؛ وذلك يجري بين الملوك في خزائنهم وبين التجار في بضائعهم وبين الدهاقين في أراضيهم وبين المتجملين في لباسهم وخيولهم ومراكبهم، فيستحقر الغني الفقير ويتكبر عليه ويقول له: أنت مد ومسكين وأنا لو أرد لاشتريت مثلك واستخدمت من هو فوقك، ومن أنت؟ وما معك وأثاث بيتي يساوي أكثر من جميع مالك؟ وأنا أنفق في اليوم ما لا تأكله في سنة؟ وكل ذلك لاستعظامه للغنى واستحقاره للفقر، وكل ذلك جهل منه بفضيلة الفقر وآفة الغنى، وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى "فقال لصاحبه وهو يحاوره أنا أكثر منك مالاً وأعز نفراً
18:34.english: Fifth: Arrogance (Kibr) through wealth; this occurs among kings regarding their treasuries, among merchants regarding their goods, among landowners regarding their lands, and among those who adorn themselves regarding their clothing, horses, and vehicles. The rich person belittles the poor person and acts arrogantly toward him, saying: You are destitute and poor, and if I wanted, I could buy someone like you and employ someone superior to you. Who are you? What do you have? The furnishings of my house are worth more than all your wealth? I spend in one day what you do not eat in a year? All of this is due to his magnifying of wealth and belittling of poverty, and all of this is ignorance on his part regarding the virtue (Fadilah) of poverty and the affliction (Afah) of wealth. To this is the allusion in His saying, the Exalted: 'And he had fruit, so he said to his companion while conversing with him: I am more than you in wealth and mightier in followers (Nafar)' until he answered him, saying: 'If you see me less than you in wealth and children, then perhaps my Lord will give me better than your garden and send upon it a reckoning from the sky, so it becomes a slippery bare plain, or its water becomes sunken, then you will never be able to seek it.' And that was from him arrogance (Takabbur) through wealth and children. Then Allah made clear the consequence of his matter with His saying: 'Oh, would that I had not associated with my Lord anyone.' And from that is the arrogance (Takabbur) of Qarun when Allah said, informing about his arrogance (Takabbur): 'So he went out to his people in his adornment. Those who desired the worldly life said: Oh, would that we had the like of what was given to Qarun. Indeed, he is one of great fortune.'
18:34.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

18:34.arabic: السابع العجب بالمال كما قال تعالى إخباراً عن صاحب الجنتين إذ قال "أنا أكثر منك مالاً وأعز نفراً" ورأى رسول الله ﭬ رجلاً غنياً جلس بجنبه فقير فانقبض عنه وجمع ثيابه فقال عليه السلام "أخشيت أن يعدو إليك فقره" وذلك للعجب بالغنى، وعلاجه أن يتفكر في آفات المال وكثرة حقوقه وعظيم غوائله، وينظر إلى فضيلة الفقراء وسبقهم إلى الجنة في القيامة، وإلى أن المال غاد ورائح ولا أصل له، وإلى أن في اليهود من يزيد عليه في المال وإلى قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام "بينما رجل يتبختر في حلة له قد أعجبته نفسه إذ أمر الله الأرض
18:34.english: The seventh: Pride (Al-'Ujb) in wealth, as Allah the Exalted said, reporting about the owner of the two gardens when he said: "I am more than you in wealth and mightier in supporters (Nafar)." And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) saw a wealthy man sitting next to a poor man, so he withdrew from him and gathered his garments. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Did you fear that his poverty (Fa-qr) would leap onto you?" That was due to pride in wealth. Its remedy is to reflect on the harms of wealth, the multitude of its obligations, and the greatness of its dangers, and to look at the virtue of the poor and their precedence to Paradise on the Day of Resurrection (Al-Qiyāmah), and that wealth comes and goes and has no foundation, and that among the Jews there are those who exceed him in wealth, and to his saying (peace be upon him): "While a man was strutting in a garment that had impressed his Soul (Nafs), Allah commanded the earth, and it seized him, and he is sinking in it until the Day of Resurrection (Al-Qiyāmah)." And he indicated by this the punishment for his pride in his wealth and his Soul (Nafs).
18:34.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

18:36.arabic: وذم الله تعالى صاحب البستان إذا دخل جنته وقال: ﴿ ما أظن تبيده هذه أبدا وما أظن الساعة قائمة ولئن رددت إلى ربى لأجدن خيرا منها منقلبا ﴾{} فإذا العبد المجتهد في الطاعات المجتنب للمعاصى حقيق بإن ينتظر من فضل الله تمام النعمة وما تمام النعمة إلا بدخول الجنة وأما العاصى فإذا تاب وتدارك جميع ما فرط منه من تقصير فحقيق بأن يرجو قبول التوبة وأما قبل التوبة إذا كان كارها للمعصية تسوءه السيئة وتسره الحسنة وهو يذم نفسه ويلومها ويشتهى التوبة ويشتاق إليها فحقيق بأن يرجو منا لله التوفيق للتوبة لأن كراهيتة للمع
18:36.english: And Allah the Exalted censured the owner of the garden when he entered his garden and said: 'I do not think this will ever perish, and I do not think the Hour (Sāʿah) is established, and if I am returned to my Lord (Rabbī), I will surely find better than it as a return.' So if the servant (ʿAbd) strives in acts of obedience (Ṭāʿāt) and avoids sins (Maʿāṣī), he is worthy to expect from the grace (Faḍl) of Allah the completion of the blessing (Niʿmah), and what is the completion of the blessing except by entering Paradise (Jannah). As for the sinner (ʿĀṣī), if he repents (Tāba) and makes up for all that he neglected from shortcomings, he is worthy to hope for the acceptance of repentance (Tawbah). And as for before repentance, if he is averse to the sin (Maʿṣiyah), the evil deed (Sayyiʾah) displeases him and the good deed (Ḥasanah) pleases him, and he blames his soul (Nafs) and reproaches it, and he desires repentance (Tawbah) and yearns for it, he is worthy to hope from Allah for success (Tawfīq) in repentance because his aversion to the sin and his eagerness for repentance runs the course of the cause (Sabab) that may lead to repentance. As for hope (Rajāʾ) after the causes are confirmed, and therefore Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, those who have believed and those who have emigrated and striven in the path (Sabīl) of Allah - those expect the mercy (Raḥmah) of Allah.' Its meaning is: those deserve to hope for the mercy of Allah, and He did not intend by it to specify the existence of hope because others also may hope, but He specified them with deserving hope.
18:36.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

18:36.arabic: ولنذكر للغرور بالله مثالين من غرور الكافرين والعاصين. فأما غرور الكفار بالله: فمثاله قول بعضهم في أنفسهم وبألسنتهم: إنه لو كان لله من معاد فنحن أحق به من غيرنا ونحن أوفر حظاً فيه وأسعد حالاً، كما أخبر الله تعالى عنه من قول الرجلين المتجاورين إذ قال "وما أظن الساعة قائمة ولئن رددت إلى ربي لأجدن خيراً منها منقلباً" وجملة أمرهما كما نقل في التفسير: أن الكافر منهما بنى قصراً بألف دينار واشترى بستاناً بألف دينار وخدماً بألف دينار وتزوج امرأة على ألف دينار، وفي ذلك كله يعظه المؤمن ويقول: اشتريت قصراً
18:36.english: And let us mention for the delusion (Ghurur) regarding Allah two examples from the delusion of the disbelievers and the disobedient. As for the delusion of the disbelievers regarding Allah: its example is the saying of some of them in themselves and with their tongues: If there is from Allah a return (Ma'ad), then we are more deserving of it than others and we have a greater share in it and a happier state, as Allah the Exalted informed about it from the saying of the two neighboring men when he said "And I do not think the Hour will be established, and if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than it as a return." And the summary of their affair as transmitted in the interpretation (Tafsir): that the disbeliever among them built a palace for a thousand dinars and bought an orchard for a thousand dinars and servants for a thousand dinars and married a woman for a thousand dinars, and in all of that the believer admonishes him and says: You bought a palace that perishes and is ruined, why did you not buy a palace in Paradise that does not perish! And you bought an orchard that is ruined and perishes, why did you not buy an orchard in Paradise that does not perish and servants who do not perish nor die and a wife from the wide-eyed maidens (Hur al-'Ayn) who does not die! And in all of that the disbeliever replies to him and says: There is nothing there and what is said of that is lies! And if it is, then surely for me in Paradise will be better than this.
18:36.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

18:39.arabic: فإن قلت: فما بال ذكر الله سبحانه مع خفته على اللسان وقلة التعب فيه صار أفضل وأنفع من جملة العبادات مع كثرة المشقات فيها؟ فاعلم أن تحقيق هذا لا يليق إلا بعلم المكاشفة والقدر الذي يسمح بذكره في علم المعاملة أن المؤثر النافع هو الذكر على الدوام مع حضور القلب فأما الذكر باللسان والقلب لاه فهو قليل الجدوى وفي الأخبار ما يدل عليه أيضا وحضور القلب في لحظة بالذكر والذهول عن الله عز وجل مع الاشتغال بالدنيا أيضا قليل الجدوى بل حضور القلب مع الله تعالى على الدوام أو في أكثر الأوقات هو المقدم على العبادات ب
18:39.english: If you say: Why is the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah, the Exalted, despite its lightness on the tongue and the little exertion in it, become better and more beneficial than the entirety of acts of worship with their many hardships in them? Then know that the realization of this is not fitting except with the knowledge of unveiling (Mukashafa) and the measure that permits mentioning it in the science of interaction (Mu'amala) that the effective, beneficial thing is the Remembrance (Dhikr) perpetually with the presence of the Heart (Qalb). As for the Remembrance (Dhikr) with the tongue while the Heart (Qalb) is heedless, it is of little benefit, and in the reports there is also what indicates this. And the presence of the Heart (Qalb) in a moment with the Remembrance (Dhikr) and the distraction from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, while being occupied with the worldly life is also of little benefit. Rather, the presence of the Heart (Qalb) with Allah, the Exalted, perpetually or in most times is what is given precedence over acts of worship. Indeed, by it all other acts of worship are ennobled, and it is the ultimate fruit of practical acts of worship. And the Remembrance (Dhikr) has a beginning and an end. Its beginning necessitates intimacy and love for Allah, and its end necessitates intimacy and love and issues from it, and what is sought is that intimacy and love. For the seeker (Murid) at the beginning of his affair may be constrained in diverting his Heart (Qalb) and tongue from the whisperings to the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. If he is granted success in persistence, he becomes intimate with it, and love for the One Remembered becomes implanted in his Heart (Qalb). And one should not be astonished at this, for from what is observed in customary matters that
18:39.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith

18:39.arabic: وقال مجاهد إذا خرج الرجل من بيته فقال بسم الله قال الملك هديت فإذا قال توكلت على الله قال الملك كفيت وإذا قال لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله قال الملك وقيت فتتفرق عنه الشياطين فيقولون ما تريدون من رجل قد هدي وكفي ووقي لا سبيل لكم إليه. فإن قلت: فما بال ذكر الله سبحانه مع خفته على اللسان وقلة التعب فيه صار أفضل وأنفع من جملة العبادات مع كثرة المشقات فيها؟ فاعلم أن تحقيق هذا لا يليق إلا بعلم المكاشفة والقدر الذي يسمح بذكره في علم المعاملة أن المؤثر النافع هو الذكر على الدوام مع حضور القلب فأما الذكر بال
18:39.english: And Mujahid said: When a man leaves his house and says 'In the name of Allah (Bismillah)', the angel says 'You are guided (Hudīta)'. And if he says 'I rely upon Allah (Tawakkaltu 'alā Allāh)', the angel says 'You are sufficed (Kufīta)'. And if he says 'There is no power nor strength except with Allah (Lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh)', the angel says 'You are protected (Waqīta)', then the devils disperse from him and say: 'What do you want from a man who has been guided, sufficed, and protected? There is no way for you to him.' If you say: Why is the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah, the Exalted, despite its lightness on the tongue and the little exertion in it, better and more beneficial than the totality of acts of worship with their many hardships in them? Then know that the realization of this is not fitting except with the knowledge of unveiling (al-Mukāshafah) and the measure that permits mentioning it in the science of interaction (al-Mu'āmalah) is that the effective, beneficial thing is the Remembrance (Dhikr) perpetually with the presence of the Heart (Qalb). As for the Remembrance (Dhikr) with the tongue while the Heart (Qalb) is heedless, it is of little benefit, and in the reports there is also what indicates that. And the presence of the Heart (Qalb) in a moment with the Remembrance (Dhikr) and the distraction from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, while being occupied with the worldly life is also of little benefit. Rather, the presence of the Heart (Qalb) with Allah, the Exalted, perpetually or in most times is what is given precedence over acts of worship; indeed, by it all other acts are ennobled.
18:39.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith

18:39.arabic: وقال رسول الله ﷺ: (الباقيات الصالحات هن لا إله إلا الله وسبحان الله والحمد لله والله أكبر ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالالله[37]) وقال ﷺ: (ما على الأرض رجل يقول لا إله إلا الله والله أكبر وسبحان الله والحمد لله ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله إلا غفرت ذنوبه ولو كانت مثل زبد البحر[38]) رواه ابن عمر وروى النعمان بن بشير عنه ﷺ أنه قال: (الذين يذكرون من جلال الله وتسبيحه وتكبيره وتحميده ينعطفن حول العرش لهن دوى كدوي النحل يذكرون بصاحبهن أو لا يحب أحدكم أن لا يزال عند الله ما يذكر به[39]) وروى أبو هريرة أنه ﷺ قال
18:39.english: And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'The enduring righteous deeds are: There is no god but Allah, and glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and Allah is the greatest, and there is no power and no strength except with Allah.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no man on earth who says: There is no god but Allah, and Allah is the greatest, and glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and there is no power and no strength except with Allah, except that his sins are forgiven, even if they were like the foam of the sea.' Narrated by Ibn Umar. And Nu'man bin Bashir narrated from him (peace be upon him) that he said: 'Those who remember from the majesty of Allah and His glorification and magnification and praise, they encircle the Throne, having a humming like the humming of bees, remembering with their companion; or does not one of you love that he always has with Allah what he is remembered by?' And Abu Hurairah narrated that he (peace be upon him) said: 'For me to say: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and there is no god but Allah, and Allah is the greatest, is more beloved to me than what the sun has risen upon.' And in another narration, he added: 'There is no power and no strength except with Allah,' and he said: 'It is better than the world and what is in it.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The most beloved speech to Allah the Exalted are four: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and there is no god but Allah, and Allah is the greatest; it does not harm you with which of them you begin.' Narrated by Samurah bin Jundub. And Abu Malik al-Ash'ari narrated that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Purity is half of faith, and praise be to Allah fills the scale, and glory be to Allah and Allah is the greatest fill what is between the heaven and the earth, and prayer is light, and charity is proof, and patience is illumination, and the Quran is an argument for you or against you; every person goes forth, so he is a seller of his soul, thus destroying it, or a purchaser of his soul, thus freeing it.'
18:39.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

18:39.arabic: [236] حديث بسم الله ما شاء الله لا قوة إلا بالله ما شاء الله كل نعمة فمن الله ما شاء الله الخير كله بيد الله ما شاء الله لا يصرف السوء إلا الله عد في الكامل من حديث ابن عباس ولا أعلمه إلا مرفوعا إلى النبي ﭬ قال يلتقي الخضر وإلياس عليهما الصلاة والسلام كل عام بالموسم بمنى فيحلق كل واحد منهما رأس صاحبه فيفترقان عن هذه الكلمات فذكره ولم يقل الخير كله بيد الله قال موضعها لا يسوق الخير إلا الله قال ابن عباس من قالهن حين يصبح وحين يمسي أمنه الله من الغرق والحرق وأحسبه قال ومن الشيطان والسطان والحية وا
18:39.english: Hadith: In the name of Allah, what Allah wills (mā shāʾa Allāh), there is no power except with Allah (lā quwwata illā bi-llāh), what Allah wills, every blessing is from Allah, what Allah wills, all good is in the hand of Allah, what Allah wills, none averts evil except Allah. Counted in Al-Kāmil from the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās, and I do not know it except as elevated to the Prophet ﷺ. He said: Al-Khiḍr and Ilyās, peace be upon them both, meet every year at the season in Minā, and each of them shaves the head of his companion, and they part with these words. He mentioned it and did not say 'all good is in the hand of Allah'. He said its place: 'None drives good except Allah'. Ibn ʿAbbās said: Whoever says them when he becomes morning and when he becomes evening, Allah secures him from drowning and burning, and I think he said: and from Satan, the Sultan, the snake, and the scorpion. He cited it in the biography of Al-Ḥusayn ibn Razīn, saying: It is not well-known, and with this chain it is rejected.
18:39.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication

18:39.arabic: وقال ﷺ فيما شهد عليه أبو هريرة وأبو سعيد الخدري: (إذا قال العبد لا إله إلا الله والله أكبر قال الله عز وجل صدق عبدي لا إله إلا أنا وأنا أكبر وإذا قال العبد لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له قال تعالى صدق عبدي لا إله إلا أنا وحدي لا شريك لي وإذا قال لا إله إلا الله ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله يقول الله سبحانه صدق عبدي لا حول ولا قوة إلا بي ومن قالهن عند الموت لم تمسه النار[51])
18:39.english: And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said, as witnessed by Abu Huraira and Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: 'When the servant says: There is no god but Allah and Allah is the Greatest, Allah Almighty says: My servant has spoken truthfully, there is no god but Me and I am the Greatest. And when the servant says: There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, Allah says: My servant has spoken truthfully, there is no god but Me alone, with no partner. And when he says: There is no god but Allah and there is no power (Hawl) and no strength (Quwwah) except with Allah, Allah says: My servant has spoken truthfully, there is no power and no strength except with Me. And whoever says these at death will not be touched by the Fire.'
18:39.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

18:41.arabic: الخامس الكبر بالمال؛ وذلك يجري بين الملوك في خزائنهم وبين التجار في بضائعهم وبين الدهاقين في أراضيهم وبين المتجملين في لباسهم وخيولهم ومراكبهم، فيستحقر الغني الفقير ويتكبر عليه ويقول له: أنت مد ومسكين وأنا لو أرد لاشتريت مثلك واستخدمت من هو فوقك، ومن أنت؟ وما معك وأثاث بيتي يساوي أكثر من جميع مالك؟ وأنا أنفق في اليوم ما لا تأكله في سنة؟ وكل ذلك لاستعظامه للغنى واستحقاره للفقر، وكل ذلك جهل منه بفضيلة الفقر وآفة الغنى، وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى "فقال لصاحبه وهو يحاوره أنا أكثر منك مالاً وأعز نفراً
18:41.english: Fifth: Arrogance (Kibr) through wealth; this occurs among kings regarding their treasuries, among merchants regarding their goods, among landowners regarding their lands, and among those who adorn themselves regarding their clothing, horses, and vehicles. Thus, the rich person despises the poor person and acts arrogantly toward him, saying: You are a pauper and destitute, and if I wished, I could buy someone like you and employ someone superior to you. Who are you? What do you possess, and the furnishings of my house are worth more than all your wealth? I spend in one day what you do not eat in a year? All of that is due to his magnifying of wealth and his belittling of poverty, and all of that is ignorance on his part regarding the virtue of poverty and the affliction of wealth. To this, the indication is in His saying, the Exalted: 'He said to his companion while conversing with him: I am more than you in wealth and mightier in men' until he answered him, saying: 'If you see me as less than you in wealth and children, then perhaps my Lord will give me better than your garden and send upon it a reckoning from the sky, so it becomes a slippery bare plain or its water becomes deep-sunken, then you will never be able to seek it.' And that was from him arrogance through wealth and children. Then Allah made clear the outcome of his affair with His saying: 'Oh, would that I had not associated with my Lord anyone.' And from that is the arrogance of Qarun when Allah said, informing about his arrogance: 'So he went out to his people in his adornment. Those who desired the worldly life said: Oh, would that we had the like of what was given to Qarun. Indeed, he is one of great fortune.'
18:41.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

18:42.arabic: الخامس الكبر بالمال؛ وذلك يجري بين الملوك في خزائنهم وبين التجار في بضائعهم وبين الدهاقين في أراضيهم وبين المتجملين في لباسهم وخيولهم ومراكبهم، فيستحقر الغني الفقير ويتكبر عليه ويقول له: أنت مد ومسكين وأنا لو أرد لاشتريت مثلك واستخدمت من هو فوقك، ومن أنت؟ وما معك وأثاث بيتي يساوي أكثر من جميع مالك؟ وأنا أنفق في اليوم ما لا تأكله في سنة؟ وكل ذلك لاستعظامه للغنى واستحقاره للفقر، وكل ذلك جهل منه بفضيلة الفقر وآفة الغنى، وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى "فقال لصاحبه وهو يحاوره أنا أكثر منك مالاً وأعز نفراً
18:42.english: Fifth: Arrogance (Kibr) through wealth; this occurs among kings regarding their treasuries, among merchants regarding their goods, among landowners regarding their lands, and among those who adorn themselves regarding their clothing, horses, and vehicles. The rich person belittles the poor person and acts arrogantly toward him, saying: 'You are destitute and poor, while I, if I wished, could purchase someone like you and employ someone superior to you. Who are you? What do you possess? The furnishings of my house are worth more than all your wealth. I spend in a day what you do not consume in a year?' All of this stems from his magnifying wealth and belittling poverty, and all of this is ignorance on his part regarding the virtue (Fadilah) of poverty and the affliction (Afa) of wealth. To this, the indication is in His saying, the Exalted: 'And he said to his companion while he was conversing with him, "I am more than you in wealth and mightier in [numbers of] men"' until he answered him, saying: 'If you see me less than you in wealth and children, then perhaps my Lord will give me better than your garden and will send upon it a calamity from the sky, and it will become a smooth, bare plain. Or its water will become sunken [into the earth], so you would never be able to seek it out.' And that was from him arrogance through wealth and children. Then Allah made clear the consequence of his affair with His saying: 'And his fruits were encompassed [by ruin], so he began to turn his hands about [in dismay] over what he had spent on it, while it had collapsed upon its trellises, and said, "Oh, I wish I had not associated with my Lord anyone."' And from that is the arrogance of Qarun, as Allah said, informing about his arrogance: 'So he came out to his people in his adornment. Those who desired the worldly life said, "Oh, would that we had like what was given to Qarun. Indeed, he is one of great fortune."'
18:42.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

18:45.arabic: ثم مهما تسلم وتتم الاسباب ينقضي العمر ﴿ حتى إذا أخذت الأرض زخرفها وازينت وظن أهلها أنهم قادرون عليها أتاها أمرنا ليلا أو نهارا فجعلناها حصيدا كأن لم تغن بالأمس ﴾ {} فضرب الله تعالى لها مثلا فقال تعالى: ﴿ واضرب لهم مثل الحياة الدنيا كماء أنزلناه من السماء فاختلط به نبات الأرض فأصبح هشيما تذروه الرياح ﴾ {} والزهد في الدنيا لما ان كان ملكا حاضرا حسده الشيطان عليه فصده عنه ومعنى الزهد ان يملك العبد شهوته وغضبه فينقادان لباعث الدين وإشارة الإيمان وهذا ملك بالاستحقاق اذ به يصير صاحبه حرا وباستيلاء الش
18:45.english: Then whenever it is secured and the means are completed, the lifespan ends. 'Until when the earth takes on its adornment and is beautified and its people think they are capable of it, Our command comes to it by night or day, and We make it a mowed field as if it had not flourished yesterday.' {} So Allah the Exalted struck a parable for it, saying the Exalted: 'And strike for them the parable of the worldly life like water We sent down from the sky, then the vegetation of the earth mixed with it, then it became dry debris scattered by the winds.' {} And asceticism (Zuhd) in the worldly life, since it is a present kingdom, the Devil (Shaytan) envied it for it, so he turned him away from it. And the meaning of asceticism (Zuhd) is that the servant (Abd) masters his desire (Shahwa) and his anger (Ghadab), so they submit to the motivator of the religion (Din) and the indication of faith (Iman). And this is a kingdom by merit, for by it its possessor becomes free, and by the domination of desire (Shahwa) over him, he becomes a slave (Abd) to his private parts (Farj) and his stomach (Batin) and his other purposes, so he becomes harnessed like a beast, owned, pulled by the reins of desire (Shahwa), taken by its throat to where it wants and desires. So how great is the deception of the human being when he thought that he attains kingdom by becoming owned and attains lordship (Rububiyya) by becoming a slave (Abd). And such as this, can it be except inverted in the worldly life, overturned in the Hereafter?
18:45.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

18:45.arabic: فالعلم والحرية هي الباقيات الصالحات التي تبقى كمالاً في النفس، والمال والجاه هو الذي ينقضي على القرب وهو كما مثله الله تعالى حيث قال "إنما مثل الحياة الدنيا كماء أنزلناه من السماء فاختلط به نبات الأرض" الآية. وقال تعالى "واضرب لهم مثل الحياة الدنيا كماء أنزلناه من السماء" إلى قوله "فأصبح هشيماً تذروه الرياح" وكل ما تذروه رياح الموت فهو زهرة الحياة الدنيا، وكل ما لا يقطعه الموت فهو الباقيات الصالحات.
18:45.english: Knowledge and freedom are the righteous remaining deeds (al-baqiyat al-salihat) that remain as perfection in the soul (nafs), while wealth and status are what perish in proximity, as Allah the Exalted has likened it where He said: 'Indeed, the likeness of worldly life is as water which We send down from the sky' until 'it becomes dry stubble scattered by the winds.' And everything that the winds of death scatter is the flower of worldly life, and everything that death does not cut off is the righteous remaining deeds (al-baqiyat al-salihat).
18:45.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

18:46.arabic: فانظر كيف انقلب الجاهلون وانكبوا على وجوههم انكباب العميان فأقبلوا على طلب كمال القدرة بالجاه والمال، وهو الكمال الذي لا يسلم وإن سلم فلا بقاء له، وأعرضوا عن كمال الحرية والعلم الذي إذا حصل كان أبدياً لا انقطاع له، وهؤلاء هم الذين اشتروا الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة فلا جرم لا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينصرون، وهم الذين لم يفهموا قوله تعالى "المال والبنون زينة الحياة الدنيا والباقيات الصالحات خير عند ربك ثواباً وخير أملاً" فالعلم والحرية هي الباقيات الصالحات التي تبقى كمالاً في النفس، والمال والجاه هو ال
18:46.english: Look how the ignorant have turned and fallen on their faces like the falling of the blind, so they turned to seeking perfection of power through status and wealth, which is a perfection that does not remain safe, and even if it remains safe, it has no permanence, and they turned away from the perfection of freedom and knowledge which, when attained, becomes eternal with no cessation. These are the ones who have purchased the worldly life in exchange for the Hereafter, so it is no wonder that the punishment is not lightened for them, nor are they helped. They are the ones who did not understand His saying, the Exalted: 'Wealth and children are the adornment of the worldly life, and the enduring righteous deeds are better with your Lord for reward and better for hope.' So knowledge and freedom are the enduring righteous deeds that remain as perfection in the soul (Nafs), and wealth and status are what perish in proximity, as Allah, the Exalted, has likened it where He said: 'The example of worldly life is like water which We send down from the sky...' the verse. And He, the Exalted, said: 'And present to them the example of the worldly life as water which We send down from the sky...' up to His saying: '...and it becomes dry debris scattered by the winds.' And everything that the winds of death scatter is the flower of the worldly life, and everything that death does not cut off is the enduring righteous deeds.
18:46.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

18:47.arabic: يوم تسير الجبال وترى الأرض بارزة، يوم ترج الأرض فيه رجا وتبس الجبال بسا فكانت هباء منبثا، يوم يكون الناس كالفراش المبثوث وتكون الجبال كالعهن المنفوش، يوم تذهل فيه كل مرضعة عما أرضعت وتضع كل ذات حمل حملها وترى الناس سكارى وما هم بسكارى ولكن عذاب الله شديد، يوم تبدل الأرض غير الأرض والسموات وبرزوا لله الواحد القهار، يوم تنسف فيه الجبال نسفا فتترك قاعا صفصفا لا ترى فيها عوجا ولا أمتا، يوم ترى الجبال تحسبها جامدة وهى تمر مر السحاب، يوم تنشق فيه السماء فتكون وردة كالدهان، فيومئذ لا يسئل عن ذنبه إنس و
18:47.english: The day when the mountains will be set in motion and you will see the earth laid bare, the day when the earth will be shaken with a shaking and the mountains will be crumbled to dust so they become scattered particles, the day when people will be like scattered moths and the mountains will be like carded wool, the day when every nursing mother will be distracted from that which she nursed and every pregnant one will abort her burden and you will see the people intoxicated while they are not intoxicated but the punishment of Allah is severe, the day when the earth will be changed to other than the earth and the heavens and they will appear before Allah the One, the Subduer, the day when the mountains will be blown away as dust leaving a level plain where you will see no crookedness nor unevenness, the day when you will see the mountains you think them firmly fixed while they pass by like the passing of clouds, the day when the sky will be split open so it becomes like red leather, then on that day no human nor jinn will be asked about his sin, the day when the disobedient will be prevented from speech and no inquiry will be made therein about crimes but they will be seized by the forelocks and the feet, the day when every soul (Nafs) will find what it did of good present and what it did of evil it will wish that between it and that were a great distance, the day when every soul (Nafs) will know what it has brought forth and will testify to what it has sent ahead and left behind, the day when the tongues will be silenced and the limbs will speak, the day whose mention turned gray the master of the messengers when the Truthful One (Al-Siddiq) may Allah be pleased with him said to him: I see you have turned gray O Messenger of Allah, he said: (Surah Hud and its sisters have turned me gray[155]) and they are Al-Waqi'ah and Al-Mursalat and 'Amma Yatasa'alun and Idha Al-Shamsu Kuwwirat. So O incapable reader, your portion from your reading is only that you mumble the Quran and move your...
18:47.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

18:49.arabic: فينقطع قلبه فزعاً من هول هذا الخطاب قبل أن تنتشر الصحيفة ويشاهد ما فيها من مخازيه، فإذا شاهده قال "يا ويلتنا ما لهذا الكتاب لا يغادر صغيرة ولا كبيرة إلا أحصاها" فهذا آخر أمره وهو معنى قوله تعالى "ثم إذا شاء أنشره" فما لمن هذا حاله والتكبر والتعظم؟ بل ما له وللفرح في لحظة واحدة فضلاً عن البطر والأشر؟ فقد ظهره له أول حاله ووسطه ولو ظهر آخره والعياذ بالله تعالى ربما اختار أن يكون كلباً أو خنزيراً ليصير مع البهائم تراباً ولا يكون إنساناً يسمع خطاباً أو يلقى عذاباً، وإن كان عند الله مستحقاً للنار فال
18:49.english: His Heart (Qalb) is severed in terror from the horror of this address before the scroll is spread open and he witnesses what is in it of his disgraceful acts. So when he witnesses it, he says, "Woe to us! What is with this book? It does not leave out a small thing nor a large thing except that it has enumerated it." This is his final affair, and it is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted, "Then when He wills, He will resurrect him." So what is for one in this state and arrogance and self-aggrandizement? Rather, what is for him and joy in a single moment, let alone insolence and extravagance? Indeed, his beginning state and middle have become apparent to him, and if his end were to appear—and refuge is sought with Allah, the Exalted—perhaps he would choose to be a dog or a pig to become with the animals as dust and not be a human who hears an address or meets punishment. And if he is, with Allah, deserving of the Fire, then the pig is more noble than him and more pleasant and higher, since its beginning is dust and its end is dust, and it is removed from the Reckoning (Hisab) and the Punishment (Adhab), and the dog and the pig, the creation does not flee from them.
18:49.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

18:49.arabic: وَقَدْ رُفِعَ الْخَلَائِقُ إِلَيْكَ أَبْصَارَهُمْ فَتَوَهَّمْ نَفْسَكَ أَنَّكَ فِي أَيْدِي الْمُوَكَّلِينَ بِكَ عَلَى هَذِهِ الصِّفَةِ حَتَّى انْتَهَى بِكَ إِلَى عَرْشِ الرَّحْمَنِ فَرَمَوْكَ مِنْ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَنَادَاكَ اللَّهُ سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى بِعَظِيمِ كَلَامِهِ يَا ابْنَ آدَمَ ادْنُ مِنِّي فَدَنَوْتَ مِنْهُ بِقَلْبٍ خَافِقٍ مَحْزُونٍ وَجِلٍ وَطَرْفٍ خَاشِعٍ ذَلِيلٍ وَفُؤَادٍ مُنْكَسِرٍ وَأُعْطِيتَ كِتَابَكَ الَّذِي لَا يُغَادِرُ صَغِيرَةً وَلَا كَبِيرَةً إِلَّا أَحْصَاهَا فَكَمْ مِنْ فَ
18:49.english: And the creatures have raised their gazes to you, so imagine yourself that you are in the hands of those entrusted with you in this state until you reached the Throne of the Most Merciful, and they threw you from their hands, and Allah, Glorified and Exalted, called you with His mighty speech: 'O son of Adam, draw near to Me.' So you drew near to Him with a fluttering, sorrowful, fearful heart (Qalb), and a humble, submissive gaze, and a broken inner self (Fu'ad), and you were given your book which does not leave a small or a large [sin] except that it has enumerated it. How many obscenities you had forgotten, then you remembered them, and how many acts of obedience you were heedless of their defects, then their faults were unveiled to you. How much shame and cowardice you have, and how much confinement and incapacity you have. I wish I knew with which foot you stand before Him, and with which tongue you answer, and with which heart (Qalb) you comprehend what you say.
18:49.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

18:49.arabic: وقال ابن عباس في قوله تعالى "يا ويلتنا ما لهذا الكتاب لا يغادر صغيرة ولا كبيرة إلا أحصاها" إن الصغيرة التبسم بالاستهزاء بالمؤمن، والكبيرة القهقهة بذلك. وهذه إشارة إلى أن الضحك على الناس من جملة الذنوب والكبائر.
18:49.english: And Ibn Abbas said regarding His (Allah's) saying, exalted is He: "Woe to us! What is this book that leaves nothing small or great but has enumerated it?" Indeed, the small (sin) is smiling in mockery of the believer, and the great (sin) is laughing loudly at that. And this is an indication that laughing at people is from the category of sins and major sins.
18:49.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

18:49.arabic: فكيف بكم لو عاينتم الأمور وبعثرت القبور وحصل ما في الصدور وأوقفتم للتحصيل بين يدي الملك الجليل فطارت القلوب لإشفاقها من سالف الذنوب وهتكت عنكم الحجب والأستار وظهرت منكم العيوب والأسرار؟ هنالك تجزى كل نفس بما كسبت إن الله عز وجل يقول "ليجزى الذي أساءوا بما عملوا ويجزى الذي أحسنوا بالحسنى" وقال تعالى "ووضع الكتاب فترى المجرمين مشفقين مما فيه" الآية جعلنا الله وإياكم عاملين بكتابة متبعين لأوليائه حتى يحلنا وإياكم دار المقامة من فضله إنه حميد مجيد.
18:49.english: How would it be for you if you witnessed the matters and the graves were overturned and what is in the chests (Sudur) was gathered and you were stood for the accounting before the Glorious King (Al-Malik Al-Jalil), so the hearts (Qulub) flew from their fear (Ishfaq) of past sins and the veils (Hujub) and curtains (Astār) were torn from you and your faults (ʿUyūb) and secrets (Asrār) appeared? There, every soul (Nafs) is recompensed for what it earned. Indeed, Allah, the Exalted and Majestic, says: "So that He may recompense those who did evil with what they did, and recompense those who did good with the best reward." And He, the Exalted, says: "And the Record (Al-Kitāb) will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful (Mushfiqīn) of what is in it, and they will say, 'Woe to us! What is this record that leaves nothing small or great but that it has enumerated it?' And they will find what they did present. And your Lord does injustice to no one." May Allah make us and you among those who act according to His writing (Kitābah), following His allies (Awliyāʾ), until He settles us and you in the Abode of Permanence (Dār Al-Maqāmah) from His bounty. Indeed, He is Praiseworthy (Hamīd), Glorious (Majīd).
18:49.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of the World'

18:49.arabic: يا أمير المؤمنين أتدري ما جاء في تأويل هذه الآية عن جدك ما لهذا الكتاب لا يغادر صغيرة ولا كبيرة إلا أحصاها قال الصغيرة التبسم والكبيرة الضحك فكيف بما عملته الأيدي وحصدته الألسن
18:49.english: O Commander of the Believers, do you know what came in the interpretation (ta'wil) of this verse from your grandfather: 'What is this book that leaves nothing small or great but has enumerated it?' He said: The small is the smile (tabassum) and the great is the laughter (dahik). So how about what the hands have done and what the tongues have harvested?
18:49.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

18:50.arabic: الآثار: قال بعض السلف: أول خطيئة هي الحسد حسد إبليس آدم عليه السلام على رتبته فأبى أن يسجد له فحمله على الحسد والمعصية. وحكي أن عون بن عبد الله دخل على الفضل بن المهلب وكان يومئذ على واسط فقال: إني أريد أن أعظك بشيء فقال: وما هو؟ قال: إياك والكبر فإنه أول ذنب عصي الله به، ثم قرأ "وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس" الآية، وإياك والحرص فإنه أخرج آدم من الجنة أمكنه الله سبحانه من جنة عرضها السموات والأرض يأكل منها إلا شجرة واحدة نهاه عنها فأكل منها فأخرجه الله تعالى منها، ثم قرأ "اهبطو
18:50.english: The Narrations: Some of the predecessors said: The first sin is envy (Hasad) - Iblis envied Adam, peace be upon him, regarding his rank, so he refused to prostrate to him, and it carried him into envy (Hasad) and disobedience. And it is narrated that 'Awn ibn 'Abd Allah entered upon al-Fadl ibn al-Muhallab, who was then in Wasit, and said: I want to advise you with something. He said: And what is it? He said: Beware of arrogance (Kibr), for it is the first sin by which Allah was disobeyed, then he recited: "And [mention] when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam,' and they prostrated, except for Iblis. He was of the jinn and departed from the command of his Lord. Then will you take him and his descendants as allies other than Me while they are enemies to you? Wretched it is for the wrongdoers as an exchange.'" And beware of greed (Hirs), for it expelled Adam from Paradise - Allah, glorified be He, had enabled him in a garden the width of the heavens and the earth, he could eat from it except for one tree which He forbade him from, so he ate from it and Allah, exalted be He, expelled him from it, then he recited: "Descend from it" to the end of the verse. And beware of envy (Hasad), for indeed the son of Adam killed his brother when he envied him, then he recited: "And recite to them the story of Adam's two sons in truth," the verses. And when the companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, are mentioned, then refrain, and when predestination (Qadar) is mentioned, then be silent, and when the stars are mentioned, then be silent.
18:50.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

18:54.arabic: وعن علي رضي الله عنه أن النبي ﷺ طرقه وفاطمة رضي الله عنهما وهما نائمان فقال: (ألا تصليان قال علي فقلت يا رسول الله إنما أنفسنا بيد الله تعالى فإذا شاء أن يبعثها بعثها فانصرف ﷺ فسمعته وهو منصرف يضرب فخذه ويقول وكان الإنسان أكثر شيء جدلا)[9]. ثم ينبغي أن يشتغل بعد ركعتي الفجر ودعائه بالاستغفار والتسبيح إلى أن تقام الصلاة فيقول أستغفر الله الذي لا إله إلا هو الحي القيوم وأتوب إليه سبعين مرةوسبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر مائة مرة ثم يصلي الفريضة مراعيا جميع ما ذكرناه من الآداب ال
18:54.english: And from Ali, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, peace be upon him, came upon him and Fatima, may God be pleased with them both, while they were sleeping and said: 'Do you not pray?' Ali said: I said, O Messenger of God, indeed our souls (Nafs) are in the hand of God Almighty, so if He wills to send them forth, He sends them forth. Then the Prophet, peace be upon him, turned away, and I heard him as he was turning away striking his thigh and saying: 'And man is the most contentious of things (Quran 18:54).' [9] Then one should occupy oneself after the two rak'ahs of Fajr and its supplication with seeking forgiveness (Istighfar) and glorification (Tasbih) until the prayer is established, saying: 'I seek forgiveness from God, there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting, and I repent to Him' seventy times, and 'Glory be to God, and praise be to God, and there is no god but God, and God is the Greatest' one hundred times, then pray the obligatory prayer, observing all that we have mentioned of the inner (Batin) and outer (Zahir) etiquettes in prayer and following the example (Qudwah). When finished with it, he sits in the mosque until sunrise in the remembrance (Dhikr) of God Almighty as we will arrange it, for he, peace be upon him, said: 'That I sit in my gathering remembering God Almighty in it from the morning prayer until sunrise is more beloved to me than freeing four slaves.' [10] And it is narrated that he, peace be upon him, when he prayed the morning prayer, would sit in his prayer place until the sun rises, and in some narrations, and pray two rak'ahs [11], meaning after the rising. And there has come regarding the virtue of that what cannot be enumerated.
18:54.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Book of Knowledge'

18:65.arabic: وكان أبو يزيد وغيره يقول ليس العالم الذي يحفظ من كتاب فإذا نسي ما حفظه صار جاهلا إنما العالم الذي يأخذ علمه من ربه أي وقت شاء بلا حفظ ولا درس وهذا هو العلم الرباني وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى وعلمناه من لدنا علما مع أن كل علم من لدنه ولكن بعضها بوسائط تعليم الخلق فلا يسمى ذلك علما لدنيا بل اللدني الذي ينفتح في سر القلب من غير سبب مألوف من خارج فهذه شواهد النقل ولو جمع كل ما ورد فيه من الآيات والأخبار والآثار لخرج عن الحصر وأما مشاهدة ذلك بالتجارب فذلك أيضا خارج عن الحصر وظهر ذلك على الصحابة والتاب
18:65.english: And Abu Yazid and others used to say: 'The knowledgeable one (Alim) is not he who memorizes from a book, for if he forgets what he has memorized, he becomes ignorant. Rather, the knowledgeable one is he who takes his knowledge from his Lord (Rabb) at any time he wishes, without memorization or study.' And this is the divine knowledge (Ilm Rabbani). And to this is the allusion in His saying, the Exalted: 'And We taught him from Our presence knowledge (Wa 'Allamnahu min ladunna 'ilma)' - although all knowledge is from His presence, but some of it comes through intermediaries of teaching the creation, so that is not called 'presence knowledge' (Ilm Laduni). Rather, the 'presence' one is that which opens up in the secret (Sirr) of the heart (Qalb) without any customary cause from outside. These are the evidences from transmission, and if all that has come regarding it from verses, reports, and traditions were gathered, it would exceed enumeration. As for witnessing that through experiences, that also exceeds enumeration, and it appeared upon the Companions (Sahaba), the Successors (Tabi'in), and those after them.
18:65.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

18:67.arabic: ومهما أشار عليه المعلم بطريق في التعلم فليقلده وليدع رأيه فإن خطأ مرشده أنفع له من صوابه في نفسه إذ التجربة تطلع على دقائق يستغرب سماعها مع أنه يعظم نفعها فكم من مريض محرور يعالجه الطبيب في بعض أوقاته بالحرارة ليزيد في قوته إلى حد يحتمل صدمة العلاج فيعجب منه من لا خبرة له به وقد نبه الله تعالى بقصة الخضر وموسى عليهما السلام حيث قال الخضر: (إنك لن تستطيع معي صبرا وكيف تصبر على ما لم تحط به خبرا( (الكهف: 67 و68). ثم شرط عليه السكوت والتسليم فقال: (فإن اتبعتني فلا تسألني عن شيء حتى أحدث لك منه ذكرا
18:67.english: And whenever the teacher indicates a path in learning, let the student follow it and abandon his own opinion, for the error of his guide is more beneficial to him than his own correctness in himself, since experience reveals subtleties whose hearing causes astonishment, while their benefit is great. How many a feverish patient is treated by the physician at some times with heat to increase his strength to a limit where he can bear the shock of treatment, and one who has no experience with this is amazed by it. And Allah the Exalted has alerted [us] with the story of Al-Khidr and Musa, peace be upon them both, where Al-Khidr said: 'Indeed, you will not be able to have patience (Sabr) with me. And how can you have patience (Sabr) over that of which you have not been given knowledge?' (Al-Kahf: 67-68). Then he stipulated upon him silence and submission (Taslim), saying: 'So if you follow me, then do not ask me about anything until I mention to you its remembrance (Dhikr).' (Al-Kahf: 70). Then he did not have patience (Sabr) and did not cease in his persistence until that became the cause of separation between them. And in summary, every student who retains for himself an opinion and choice (Ikhtiyar) apart from the choice (Ikhtiyar) of the teacher, judge him to be in failure and loss.
18:67.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

18:68.arabic: ومهما أشار عليه المعلم بطريق في التعلم فليقلده وليدع رأيه فإن خطأ مرشده أنفع له من صوابه في نفسه إذ التجربة تطلع على دقائق يستغرب سماعها مع أنه يعظم نفعها فكم من مريض محرور يعالجه الطبيب في بعض أوقاته بالحرارة ليزيد في قوته إلى حد يحتمل صدمة العلاج فيعجب منه من لا خبرة له به وقد نبه الله تعالى بقصة الخضر وموسى عليهما السلام حيث قال الخضر: (إنك لن تستطيع معي صبرا وكيف تصبر على ما لم تحط به خبرا( (الكهف: 67 و68). ثم شرط عليه السكوت والتسليم فقال: (فإن اتبعتني فلا تسألني عن شيء حتى أحدث لك منه ذكرا
18:68.english: And whenever the teacher indicates to him a path in learning, let him follow it and abandon his own opinion, for the error of his guide is more beneficial to him than his own correctness in himself, since experience reveals subtleties whose hearing is astonishing, while its benefit is great. How many a feverish patient the doctor treats at some of his times with heat to increase his strength to a limit that can bear the shock of treatment, so one who has no experience with it is amazed at it. And Allah the Exalted has alerted with the story of Al-Khidr and Moses, peace be upon them both, where Al-Khidr said: 'You will not be able to have patience with me. And how can you have patience over that which you have not encompassed in knowledge?' (Al-Kahf: 67-68). Then he stipulated upon him silence and submission, saying: 'Then if you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I mention it to you.' (Al-Kahf: 70). Then he did not have patience and did not cease in his persistence until that was the cause of separation between them. And in summary, every student who retains for himself an opinion and choice without the choice of the teacher, judge him with failure and loss.
18:68.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

18:70.arabic: وقد نبه الله تعالى بقصة الخضر وموسى عليهما السلام حيث قال الخضر: (إنك لن تستطيع معي صبرا وكيف تصبر على ما لم تحط به خبرا( (الكهف: 67 و68). ثم شرط عليه السكوت والتسليم فقال: (فإن اتبعتني فلا تسألني عن شيء حتى أحدث لك منه ذكرا( (الكهف: 70). ثم لم يصبر ولم يزل في مراودته إلى أن كان ذلك سبب الفراق بينهما وبالجملة كل متعلم استبقى لنفسه رأيا واختيارا دون اختيار المعلم فاحكم عليه بالإخفاق والخسران
18:70.english: And Allah the Exalted has alerted [us] through the story of Al-Khidr and Moses, peace be upon them both, where Al-Khidr said: 'Indeed, you will not be able to have patience with me. And how can you have patience for what you have not encompassed in knowledge?' (Al-Kahf: 67-68). Then he stipulated upon him silence and submission, saying: 'Then if you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I mention to you of it a remembrance (Dhikr).' (Al-Kahf: 70). Then he did not have patience and did not cease in his persistence until that became the cause of separation between them. And in summary, every learner who retains for himself an opinion (Ra'y) and choice (Ikhtiyar) without the choice of the teacher, then judge him with failure and loss.
18:70.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

18:70.arabic: وفي قصة موسى والخضر عليهما السلام تنبيه على المنع من السؤال قبل أوان استحقاقه إذ قال "فإن اتبعتني فلا تسألني عن شيء حتى أحدث لك منه ذكراً" فلما سأل عن السفينة أنكر عليه حتى اعتذر وقال "لا تؤاخذني بما نسيت ولا ترهقني من أمري عسراً" فلم يصبر حتى سأل ثلاثاً قال "هذا فراق بيني وبينك" وفارقه.
18:70.english: And in the story of Moses and Al-Khidr (peace be upon them both), there is a warning against asking before its due time, as He (Al-Khidr) said: "If you follow me, then do not ask me about anything until I initiate for you a Remembrance (Dhikr) from it." When he (Moses) asked about the ship, he (Al-Khidr) reproached him until he (Moses) apologized and said: "Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot, and do not burden me with hardship in my affair." He (Moses) did not have patience until he asked three times; he (Al-Khidr) said: "This is a separation between me and you," and he parted from him.
18:70.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

18:70.arabic: وقوله عز وجل ﴿ فإن اتبعتني فلا تسألني عن شيء ﴾ {} أراد به من صفات الربوبية وهو العلوم التي لا يحل السؤال عنها حتى يبتدئ بها العارف في أوان الاستحقاق
18:70.english: And His saying, the Exalted, 'If you follow me, then do not ask me about anything' (Quran 18:70) — He intended by it from the attributes of Lordship (Rububiyyah), and it is the knowledges (al-'Ulum) which it is not permissible to ask about until the knower (al-'Arif) initiates them at the time of deserving (awān al-istihqāq).
18:70.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

18:72.arabic: ومهما أشار عليه المعلم بطريق في التعلم فليقلده وليدع رأيه فإن خطأ مرشده أنفع له من صوابه في نفسه إذ التجربة تطلع على دقائق يستغرب سماعها مع أنه يعظم نفعها فكم من مريض محرور يعالجه الطبيب في بعض أوقاته بالحرارة ليزيد في قوته إلى حد يحتمل صدمة العلاج فيعجب منه من لا خبرة له به وقد نبه الله تعالى بقصة الخضر وموسى عليهما السلام حيث قال الخضر: (إنك لن تستطيع معي صبرا وكيف تصبر على ما لم تحط به خبرا( (الكهف: 67 و68). ثم شرط عليه السكوت والتسليم فقال: (فإن اتبعتني فلا تسألني عن شيء حتى أحدث لك منه ذكرا
18:72.english: And whenever the teacher indicates a path in learning, let him follow it and abandon his own opinion, for the error of his guide is more beneficial to him than his own correctness in himself, since experience reveals subtleties whose hearing is astonishing, while its benefit is great. How many a feverish patient is treated by the physician at some of his times with heat to increase his strength to a limit that can bear the shock of treatment, and one who has no experience with it is amazed at it. And Allah the Exalted has alerted with the story of Al-Khidr and Musa, peace be upon them both, where Al-Khidr said: 'Indeed, you will not be able to have patience (Sabr) with me. And how can you have patience (Tasbir) over that which you have not encompassed in knowledge?' (Al-Kahf: 67-68). Then he stipulated upon him silence and submission, saying: 'Then if you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I make to you thereof mention (Dhikr).' (Al-Kahf: 70). Then he did not have patience (Lam Yasbir) and did not cease in his persistence until that was the cause of separation between them. And in summary, every learner who retains for himself an opinion and choice without the choice of the teacher, judge him with failure and loss.
18:72.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

18:73.arabic: وفي قصة موسى والخضر عليهما السلام تنبيه على المنع من السؤال قبل أوان استحقاقه إذ قال "فإن اتبعتني فلا تسألني عن شيء حتى أحدث لك منه ذكراً" فلما سأل عن السفينة أنكر عليه حتى اعتذر وقال "لا تؤاخذني بما نسيت ولا ترهقني من أمري عسراً" فلم يصبر حتى سأل ثلاثاً قال "هذا فراق بيني وبينك" وفارقه.
18:73.english: And in the story of Moses and Al-Khidr (peace be upon them both) there is an admonition regarding the prohibition of asking before the time of its deserving, when he said: 'If you follow me, then do not ask me about anything until I mention to you its remembrance (Dhikr).' When he asked about the ship, he disapproved of him until he apologized and said: 'Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot and do not burden me with difficulty from my affair.' He did not have patience until he asked three times; he said: 'This is separation between me and you' and he parted from him.
18:73.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

18:75.arabic: ومهما أشار عليه المعلم بطريق في التعلم فليقلده وليدع رأيه فإن خطأ مرشده أنفع له من صوابه في نفسه إذ التجربة تطلع على دقائق يستغرب سماعها مع أنه يعظم نفعها فكم من مريض محرور يعالجه الطبيب في بعض أوقاته بالحرارة ليزيد في قوته إلى حد يحتمل صدمة العلاج فيعجب منه من لا خبرة له به وقد نبه الله تعالى بقصة الخضر وموسى عليهما السلام حيث قال الخضر: (إنك لن تستطيع معي صبرا وكيف تصبر على ما لم تحط به خبرا( (الكهف: 67 و68). ثم شرط عليه السكوت والتسليم فقال: (فإن اتبعتني فلا تسألني عن شيء حتى أحدث لك منه ذكرا
18:75.english: And whenever the teacher indicates to him a path in learning, let him follow it and abandon his own opinion, for the error of his guide is more beneficial to him than his own correctness in himself, since experience reveals subtleties whose hearing is astonishing, while its benefit is great. How many a feverish patient is treated by the physician at some of his times with heat to increase his strength to a limit that can bear the shock of treatment, and one who has no experience with it is amazed by it. And Allah the Exalted has alerted with the story of Al-Khidr and Musa, peace be upon them both, where Al-Khidr said: 'Indeed, you will not be able to have patience (Sabr) with me. And how can you have patience (Tasbir) over that of which you have not been given knowledge?' (Al-Kahf: 67-68). Then he stipulated upon him silence and submission, saying: 'Then if you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I mention to you its remembrance (Dhikr)' (Al-Kahf: 70). Then he did not have patience (Yasbir) and did not cease in his persistence until that was the cause of separation between them. And in summary, every learner who retains for himself an opinion and choice without the choice of the teacher, judge him with failure and loss.
18:75.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

18:75.arabic: وما حكى من تفرس المشايخ وإخبارهم عن اعتقادات الناس وضمائرهم يخرج عن الحصر بل ما حكى عنهم من مشاهدة الخضر عليه السلام والسؤال منه ومن سماع صوت الهاتف ومن فنون الكرامات خارج عن الحصر والحكاية لا تنفع الجاحد ما لم يشاهد ذلك من نفسه ومن أنكر الأصل أنكر التفصيل والدليل القاطع الذي لا يقدر أحد على جحده أمران أحدهما عجائب الرؤيا الصادقة فإنه ينكشف بها الغيب وإذا جاز ذلك في النوم فلا يستحيل أيضا في اليقظة فلم يفارق النوم اليقظة إلا في ركود الحواس وعدم اشتغالها بالمحسوسات فكم من مستيقظ غائص لا يسمع ولا ي
18:75.english: And what has been narrated regarding the insight (Tafarrus) of the shaykhs and their informing about the beliefs (I'tiqadat) of people and their inner thoughts (Dama'ir) goes beyond enumeration. Rather, what has been narrated from them regarding witnessing Al-Khidr (peace be upon him) and asking him, and hearing the voice of the caller (Al-Hatif), and various types of miracles (Karamat) is beyond enumeration. The narration does not benefit the denier unless he witnesses that from himself. Whoever denies the foundation denies the details. The decisive proof that no one can deny is two matters: one is the wonders of truthful dreams (Al-Ru'ya Al-Sadiqa), for through them the unseen (Al-Ghayb) is unveiled. If that is permissible in sleep, then it is not impossible also in wakefulness, for sleep does not differ from wakefulness except in the stillness of the senses and their lack of engagement with perceptible things. How many are awake yet submerged, not hearing nor seeing due to their engagement with themselves. The second is the informing of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) about the unseen and matters in the future, as contained in the Quran. If that is permissible for the Prophet (peace be upon him), it is permissible for others, for the Prophet is an expression for a person who is unveiled (Kushifa) with the realities of matters and occupied with reforming creation. It is not impossible that there exists in existence a person who is unveiled (Mukashaf) with the realities and not occupied with reforming creation. This is not called a prophet but is called a saint (Wali). So whoever believes...
18:75.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

18:78.arabic: وفي قصة موسى والخضر عليهما السلام تنبيه على المنع من السؤال قبل أوان استحقاقه إذ قال "فإن اتبعتني فلا تسألني عن شيء حتى أحدث لك منه ذكراً" فلما سأل عن السفينة أنكر عليه حتى اعتذر وقال "لا تؤاخذني بما نسيت ولا ترهقني من أمري عسراً" فلم يصبر حتى سأل ثلاثاً قال "هذا فراق بيني وبينك" وفارقه.
18:78.english: And in the story of Moses and Al-Khidr (peace be upon them both) there is an admonition regarding the prohibition of asking before the time of its deserving, when he said: 'If you follow me, then do not ask me about anything until I mention to you its remembrance (Dhikr).' When he asked about the ship, he reproached him until he apologized and said: 'Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot and do not burden me with difficulty in my affair.' He did not have patience (Sabr) until he asked three times. He said: 'This is separation between me and you' and he parted from him.
18:78.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

18:82.arabic: اعلم أن الله تعالى قد سمى المال خيراً في مواضع من كتابه العزيز فقل جل وعز "إن ترك خيراً" الآية وقال رسول الله ﭬ "نعم المال الصالح للرجل الصالح"[13] وكل ما جاء في ثواب الصدقة والحج فهو ثناء على المال إذ لا يمكن الوصول إليهما إلا به. وقال تعالى "ويستخرجا كنزهما رحمة من ربك" وقال تعالى ممتناً على عباده "ويمددكم بأموال وبنين ويجعل لكم جنات ويجعل لكم أنهاراً" وقال ﭬ "كاد الفقر أن يكون كفراً"[14] وهو ثناء على المال. ولا تقف على وجه الجمع بعد الذم والمدح إلا بأن تعرف حكمة المال ومقصوده وآفاته وغوائله؛
18:82.english: Know that Allah the Exalted has called wealth good in places of His Noble Book, so say He is Glorified and Exalted: "If he leaves good" the verse, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "How excellent is righteous wealth for a righteous man"[13], and all that comes regarding the reward of charity and pilgrimage is praise of wealth since it is not possible to reach them except through it. And He the Exalted said: "And they extract their treasure as a mercy from your Lord" and He the Exalted said, bestowing favor upon His servants: "And He supplies you with wealth and children and makes for you gardens and makes for you rivers" and He (peace be upon him) said: "Poverty almost becomes disbelief"[14], and this is praise of wealth. And you will not stand upon the face of the combination after blame and praise except by knowing the wisdom of wealth, its purpose, its harms, and its dangers; until it becomes clear to you that it is good from one aspect and evil from another aspect, and that it is praiseworthy from where it is good and blameworthy from where it is evil, for it is not pure good nor pure evil, but rather it is a cause for both matters, and what has this description is inevitably praised at times and blamed at others, but the discerning distinguisher perceives that the praiseworthy from it is not the blameworthy, and its clarification is by seeking support from what we mentioned in the Book of Gratitude regarding the explanation of goods and the detailing of the degrees of blessings, and the sufficient amount in it is that the purpose of the wise and the people of insight is the happiness of the Hereafter which is the everlasting bliss and the kingdom and the abiding. And aiming for this is the habit of the noble and the wise, for it was said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him): Who are the most honorable of people and the wisest of them? He said: "The most frequent in remembrance (Dhikr) of death and the most prepared for it"[15]. And this happiness is not attained except through three means in the world: they are the spiritual virtues, like knowledge and good character, the bodily virtues: like health and safety, and the virtues external to the body: like wealth and other means. And the highest of them are the spiritual, then the bodily.
18:82.book_title: Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth
18:82.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

18:84.arabic: وما هو قادر عليه من نفسه وغيره فليست قدرته من نفسه وبنفسه بل الله خالقه وخالق قدرته وخالق أسبابه والممكن له من ذلك. ولو سلط بعوضاً على أعظم ملك وأقوى شخص من الحيوانات لأهلكه، فليس للعبد قدرة إلا بتمكين مولاه كما قال في أعظم ملوك الأرض ذي القرنين إذ قال "إنا مكنا له في الأرض" فلم يكن جميع ملكه وسلطنته إلا بتمكين الله تعالى إياه في جزء من الأرض، والأرض كلها مدرة بالإضافة إلى أجسام العالم وجميع الولايات التي يحظى بها الناس من الأرض غبرة من تلك المدرة، ثم تلك الغبرة أيضاً من فضل الله تعالى وتمكينه،
18:84.english: And what he is capable of from himself and others, his capability is not from himself and by himself, but Allah is his Creator and the Creator of his capability and the Creator of his means and the Enabler for him of that. And if He were to unleash a mosquito upon the greatest king and strongest person of the animals, it would destroy him, so the servant has no capability except through the enabling of his Master, as He said regarding the greatest king of the earth, Dhul-Qarnayn, when He said: "Indeed, We enabled him in the earth." So all his kingdom and sovereignty were only through Allah the Exalted enabling him in a portion of the earth, and the entire earth is a speck of dust in comparison to the bodies of the universe, and all the dominions that people attain from the earth are a particle of that speck of dust, then that particle is also from the favor of Allah the Exalted and His enabling. Thus, it is impossible to love a servant from among the servants of Allah the Exalted for his capability, governance, enabling, dominion, and perfection of his strength and not love Allah the Exalted for that. And there is no power and no strength except with Allah the Most High, the Most Great. He is the Compeller, the Subduer, the All-Knowing, the All-Capable. The heavens are folded in His right hand, and the earth and its kingdom and what is upon it are in His grasp, and the forelocks of all creatures are in the grasp of His capability. If He were to destroy them from their last one, it would not diminish from His sovereignty and kingdom an atom. And if He were to create their like a thousand times, He would not be wearied by their creation, nor would fatigue or slackness touch Him in their invention. So there is no capability and no capable one except that he is an effect from the effects of His capability. So to Him belongs beauty, splendor, majesty, grandeur, subduing, and dominion. If it is conceivable to love a capable one for the perfection of his capability, then none deserves love for the perfection of capability except Him at all.
18:84.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

18:103.arabic: فإن اتفق زهوق روحه في هذه الخطرة قبل أن يثبت ويعود إلى أصل الإيمان فقد ختم له بالسوء وخرجت روحه على الشرك والعياذ بالله منه فهؤلاء هم المرادون بقوله تعالى: ﴿ وبدا لهم من الله ما لم يكونوا يحتسبون ﴾ وبقوله عز وجل: ﴿ قل هل ننبئكم بالأخسرين أعمالا الذين ضل سعيهم في الحياة الدنيا وهم يحسبون أنهم يحسنون صنعا ﴾ وكما أنه ينكشف في النوم ما سيكون في المستقبل وذلك بسبب خفة أشغال الدنيا عن القلب فكذلك ينكشف في سكرات الموت بعض الأمور إذ شواغل الدنيا وشهوات البدن هي المانعة للقلب من أن ينظر إلى الملكوت فيطال
18:103.english: If it happens that his spirit (Ruh) departs in this peril before he becomes firm and returns to the foundation of faith (Iman), then he has been sealed with evil and his spirit has departed upon polytheism (Shirk) - we seek refuge in Allah from it. These are the ones intended by His saying, the Exalted: 'And there will appear to them from Allah that which they had not taken into account' and by His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Say: Shall we inform you of the greatest losers in deeds? Those whose effort is lost in worldly life while they think that they are doing well in work.' And just as what will be in the future is unveiled in sleep due to the lightness of worldly occupations from the heart (Qalb), similarly some matters are unveiled in the throes of death, since the distractions of the world and the desires of the body are what prevent the heart from looking at the dominion (Malakut) to observe what is in the Preserved Tablet (Al-Lawh Al-Mahfuz) so that matters become unveiled to him as they truly are. Thus such a state becomes a cause for unveiling (Kashf), and the unveiling becomes a cause for doubt in the remaining beliefs.
18:103.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

18:103.arabic: والغافلون يرون حسناتهم كلها في الآخرة سيئات وهم المرادون بقوله تعالى (وبدا لهم من الله مالم يكونوا يحتسبون وبدا لهم سيئات ما كسبوا) وبقوله تعالى (قل هل ننبئكم بالأخسرين أعمالا الذين ضل سعيهم في الحياة الدنيا وهم يحسبون أنهم يحسنون صنعا.)
18:103.english: And the heedless ones will see all their good deeds as bad deeds in the Hereafter, and they are those intended by His saying, the Exalted: (And there will appear to them from Allah that which they had not taken into account, and there will appear to them the evils of what they earned) and by His saying, the Exalted: (Say, 'Shall we inform you of the greatest losers in respect of (their) deeds? Those whose effort is lost in worldly life, while they think that they are doing well in work.')
18:103.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

18:103.arabic: ومن لم يطع على مكايد الشيطان وآفات النفوس فأكثر عباداته تعب ضائع يفوت عليه الدنيا ويخسره في الآخرة، وفيهم قال الله تعالى "قل هل ننبئكم بالأخسرين أعمالاً الذي ضل سعيهم في الحياة الدنيا وهم يحسبون أنهم يحسنون صنعاً".
18:103.english: And whoever does not guard against the tricks of Satan and the afflictions of the Souls (Nafs) then most of his acts of worship are wasted effort that causes him to miss out on this world and lose in the Hereafter, and about them Allah the Exalted said: "Say: Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in respect of (their) deeds? Those whose effort is lost in worldly life while they think that they are doing well in work."
18:103.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

18:104.arabic: فبسوا المرقعات واتخذوا في الخانقاهات متنزهات وربما تلقفوا ألفاظا مزخرفة من أهل الطامات فينظرون إلى أنفسهم وقد تشبهوا بالقوم في خرقتهم وفي سياحتهم وفي لفظهم وعبارتهم وفي آداب ظاهرة من سيرتهم فيظنون بأنفسهم خيرا ويحسبون أنهم يحسنون صنعا ويعتقدون أن كل سوداء تمرة ويتوهمون أن المشاركة في الظاهر توجب المساهمة في الحقائق وهيهات فما أغزر حماقة من لا يميز بين الشحم والورم فهؤلاء بغضاء الله فإن الله تعالى يبغض الشاب الفارغ ولم يحملهم على السياحة إلا الشباب والفراغ إلا من سافر لحج أو عمرة في غير رياء ولا
18:104.english: They wore patched garments and made the Sufi lodges (Khanqahs) into pleasure grounds, and perhaps they picked up embellished phrases from people of false claims. They look at themselves having imitated the people in their patched garments, in their wandering, in their speech and expressions, and in apparent manners from their conduct, so they think good of themselves and reckon that they are doing good deeds (yuḥsinūna ṣunʿan), and they believe that every black thing is a date, and they imagine that participation in outward appearance necessitates sharing in realities. Far from it! How abundant is the foolishness of one who does not distinguish between fat and swelling. These are hated by Allah, for Allah the Exalted hates the idle youth. Nothing drove them to wandering except youth and idleness, except for one who travels for Hajj or Umrah without ostentation or fame-seeking, or travels to observe a shaykh to follow in his knowledge and conduct—and the lands have become empty of him now. All religious matters have become corrupt and weakened except Sufism, for it has been completely obliterated and nullified because the sciences have not yet been forgotten. The scholar, even if he is an evil scholar, his corruption is in his conduct, not in his knowledge, so he remains a scholar not acting upon his knowledge, and action is not knowledge. As for Sufism, it is an expression of the Heart's (Qalb) detachment for Allah the Exalted and belittling what is other than Allah, and its essence returns to the action of the Heart (Qalb) and the limbs. Whenever the action is corrupt, the foundation is lost. In the travels of these people, there is consideration for the jurists from the perspective that it is exhausting the Soul (Nafs) without benefit. It may be said that this is prohibited, but the correct view according to us is to rule with permissibility, for their gains are amusement from the distress of idleness by observing different lands. These gains, even if they are base, the Souls (Nufūs) of those moved by these gains are also base, and there is no harm in exhausting a base animal for a base gain that suits it and...
18:104.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Travel'

18:104.arabic: بل الأكثرون يرتكبون الجهل فيما يكرهه الله تعالى وهم يحسبون أنهم يحسنون صنعا ولا تظنن أن الجاهل بما يقدر على التعلم فيه يعذر هيهات بل طلب العلم فريضة على كل مسلم ولهذا كانت ركعتان من عالم أفضل من ألف ركعة من غير عالم لأنه يعلم آفات النفوس ومكايد الشيطان ومواضع الغرور فيتقى ذلك والجاهل لا يعرفه فكيف يحترز منه فلا يزال الجاهل في تعب والشيطان منه في فرح وشماته فنعوذ بالله من الجهل والغفلة فهو رأس كل شقاوة وأساس كل خسران فحكم الله تعالى على كل عبد أن يراقب نفسه عند همه بالفعل وسعيه بالجارحة فيتوقف عن
18:104.english: Rather, most people commit ignorance in what Allah the Exalted dislikes, and they think that they are doing good work. And do not think that the ignorant one who is capable of learning about it is excused - far from it! Rather, seeking knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim. For this reason, two units of prayer from a knowledgeable person are better than a thousand units from a non-knowledgeable person, because he knows the defects of the souls (Nafs) and the plots of Satan (Shaytan) and the places of delusion, so he avoids that, and the ignorant one does not know it, so how can he guard against it? Thus, the ignorant one remains in hardship, and Satan (Shaytan) is in joy and gloating over him, so we seek refuge in Allah from ignorance and heedlessness, for it is the head of every misery and the foundation of every loss. So Allah the Exalted has decreed upon every servant that he should watch over his soul (Nafs) at his intention (Himmah) with action and his striving (Sa'y) with the limb, so he stops from the intention (Himmah) and from the striving (Sa'y) until it becomes clear to him through the light of knowledge that it is for Allah the Exalted, so he proceeds with it, or it is for the desire of the soul (Nafs), so he avoids it and restrains the heart (Qalb) from thinking about it and from intending (Himmah) it. For the first step in falsehood, if not repelled, produces desire, and desire produces intention (Himmah), and intention (Himmah) produces firm resolve, and resolve produces action, and action produces ruin and wrath. So it is necessary to cut off the source of evil from its first origin, which is the thought (Khatir), for all that follows it follows it. And whenever that becomes ambiguous to the servant and the situation becomes dark, so it is not revealed to him, then he should reflect on that with the light of knowledge and seek refuge in Allah from the deception of Satan (Shaytan) through the mediation of desire. If he is incapable of striving and reflection by himself, then he should be illuminated by the light of the scholars of religion and flee from the scholars.
18:104.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'
