18:104.arabic: الثامن العجب بالرأي الخطأ. قال الله تعالى "أفمن زين له سوء عمله فرآه حسناً" وقال تعالى "وهم يحسبون أنهم يحسنون صنعاً" وقد أخبر رسول الله ﭬ: أن ذلك يغلب على آخر هذه الأمة[101] وبذلك هلكت الأمم السالفة إذ افترقت فرقاً فكل معجب برأيه "وكل حزب بما لديهم فرحون" وجميع أهل البدع والضلال إنما أصروا عليها لعجبهم بآرائهم والعجب بالبدعة هو استحسان ما يسوق إليه الهوى والشهوة مع ظن كونه حقاً، وعلاج هذا العجب أشد من علاج غيره لأن صاحب الرأي الخطأ جاهل بخطئه ولو عرفه لتركه، ولا يعالج الداء الذي لا يعرف والجهل
18:104.english: The eighth: Pride in erroneous opinion. Allah the Exalted said: "Is he whose evil deed is made fair-seeming unto him so that he sees it as good?" and He said: "And they think that they are doing good work." And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) informed: that this will prevail over the latter part of this nation [101], and by this the past nations perished when they split into factions, each proud of his opinion, "and every party rejoices in what they have." And all the people of innovation (Bid'ah) and misguidance only persist in it due to their pride in their opinions, and pride in innovation (Bid'ah) is the approval of what the desire (Hawa) and appetite (Shahwah) lead to with the assumption of its being truth. The treatment of this pride is more severe than the treatment of others because the possessor of erroneous opinion is ignorant (Jahil) of his error, and if he knew it, he would abandon it, and the disease that is not known is not treated, and ignorance (Jahl) is a disease that is not known, so its cure is extremely difficult. Because the knower (Arif) is able to clarify to the ignorant (Jahil) his ignorance (Jahl) and remove it from him, except if he is proud of his opinion and his ignorance (Jahl), then he does not listen to the knower (Arif) and accuses him. Indeed, Allah has imposed upon him a calamity that destroys him while he thinks it a blessing, so how can his treatment be possible and how can he seek escape from what is the cause of his happiness in his belief? And his treatment in summary is that he be suspicious of his opinion always, not being deceived by it except when a decisive proof from the Book or the Sunnah or a sound rational evidence (Daleel 'Aqli) that gathers the conditions of evidences testifies. And a person will not know the evidences of the Sacred Law (Shari'ah) and the intellect (Aql) and their conditions and the places of error in them except with a complete natural disposition (Qareehah), a penetrating intellect (Aql), diligence, and exertion in seeking, practice with the Book and the Sunnah, keeping company with the people of knowledge ('Ilm) for the length of life, and studying the sciences, and with all that, there is no security.
18:104.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

18:104.arabic: والمتنطعون هم الذين يخشى عليهم أن يكونوا ممن قيل فيهم الَّذِينَ ضَلَّ سَعْيُهُمْ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَهُمْ يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ يُحْسِنُونَ صُنْعًا وبالجملة لا ينبغي للإنسان أن يشتغل بدقائق الورع إلا بحضرة عالم متقن فإنه إذا جاوز ما رسم وتصرف بذهنه من غير سماع كان ما يفسده أكثر مما يصلحه
18:104.english: And the extremists (al-Mutanatti'ūn) are those who are feared to be among those about whom it was said: 'Those whose effort is lost in worldly life while they think that they are doing good in work (ṣunʿan).' And in summary, it is not appropriate for a person to occupy himself with the subtleties of scrupulousness (al-Waraʿ) except in the presence of a proficient scholar (ʿĀlim Mutqin), for if he exceeds what is prescribed and acts according to his own mind without hearing [from scholars], what he corrupts is more than what he rectifies.
18:104.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

18:104.arabic: ومن لم يطع على مكايد الشيطان وآفات النفوس فأكثر عباداته تعب ضائع يفوت عليه الدنيا ويخسره في الآخرة، وفيهم قال الله تعالى "قل هل ننبئكم بالأخسرين أعمالاً الذين ضل سعيهم في الحياة الدنيا وهم يحسبون أنهم يحسنون صنعاً".
18:104.english: And whoever does not guard against the tricks (maka'id) of Satan (Shaytan) and the afflictions (afat) of the Souls (Nafs), then most of his acts of worship ('ibadat) are wasted effort that causes him to miss out on this worldly life (al-dunya) and lose in the Hereafter (al-akhira). And about them, Allah the Exalted said: "Say: Shall we inform you of the greatest losers in deeds? Those whose effort (sa'y) is lost (dalla) in the worldly life (al-hayat al-dunya) while they think that they are doing good (yuhsinuna) in making (suna'an)."
18:104.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

18:109.arabic: اعلم أن كل ما في الوجود مما سوى الله تعالى فهو فعل الله وخلقه وكل ذرة من الذرات من جوهر وعرض وصفة وموصوف ففيها عجائب وغرائب تظهر بها حكمة الله وقدرته وجلاله وعظمته وإحصاء ذلك غير ممكن لأنه لو كان البحر مدادا لذلك لنفد البحر قبل أن ينفد عشر عشيره ولكنا نشير إلى جمل منه ليكون ذلك كالمثال لما عداه
18:109.english: Know that everything in existence besides Allah the Exalted is the action (Fi'l) and creation (Khalq) of Allah, and every atom of atoms from substance (Jawhar) and accident ('Arad) and attribute (Sifah) and described thing (Mawsuf) - in them are wonders and marvels through which appear the wisdom (Hikmah) of Allah and His power (Qudrah) and majesty (Jalal) and greatness ('Azamah). And enumerating that is not possible because if the sea were ink for that, the sea would be exhausted before a tenth of its tenth would be exhausted. But we point to a summary of it so that it may be like an example for what is beyond it.
18:109.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Contemplation'

18:109.arabic: وإحصاء ذلك غير ممكن لأنه لو كان البحر مدادا لذلك لنفد البحر قبل أن ينفد عشر عشيره ولكنا نشير إلى جمل منه ليكون ذلك كالمثال لماعداه
18:109.english: And enumerating that is not possible because if the sea were ink for that, the sea would be exhausted before one-tenth of it would be exhausted. But we point to a summary of it so that it may serve as an example for what is beyond it.
18:109.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Contemplation'

18:110.arabic: فضيلة الإخلاص قال الله تعالى (وما أمروا إلا ليعبدوا الله مخلصين له الدين) وقال (ألا لله الدين الخالص) وقال تعالى (إلا الذين تابوا وأصلحوا واعتصموا بالله وأخلصوا دينهم لله) وقال تعالى (فمن كان يرجو لقاء ربه فليعمل عملا صالحا ولا يشرك بعبادة ربه أحدا) نزلت فيمن يعمل لله ويحب أن يحمد عليه وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: (ثلاث لا يغل عليهن قلب رجل مسلم إخلاص العمل لله)[36] وعن مصعب بن سعد عن أبيه قال ظن أبى أن له فضلا على من هو دونه من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم
18:110.english: The Virtue of Sincerity (Ikhlas). Allah the Exalted said: 'And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, being sincere (mukhlisīn) to Him in religion' (Quran 98:5). And He said: 'Unquestionably, for Allah is the pure religion (al-dīn al-khālis)' (Quran 39:3). And the Exalted said: 'Except for those who repent, correct themselves, hold fast to Allah, and are sincere (akhlaṣū) in their religion for Allah' (Quran 4:146). And the Exalted said: 'So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, then let him do righteous work (ʿamalan ṣāliḥan) and not associate (yushrik) in the worship of his Lord anyone' (Quran 18:110). It was revealed concerning one who works for Allah and loves to be praised for it. And the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'Three things against which the Heart (Qalb) of a believing man does not harbor rancor: sincerity (ikhlāṣ) of action for Allah' [36]. And from Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd from his father, he said: My father thought he had superiority over those below him among the companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, so the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'Indeed, Allah the Mighty and Majestic gives victory to this community through its weak ones, their supplication, and their sincerity (ikhlāṣihim)' [37]. And from al-Ḥasan, he said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'Allah the Exalted says: Sincerity (al-ikhlāṣ) is a secret from My secrets which I have deposited in the Heart (Qalb) of whom I have loved from among My servants' [38]. And ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah honor his face, said: 'Do not be concerned with the smallness of the action, but be concerned with its acceptance, for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to Muʿādh ibn Jabal: Make the action sincere (akhliṣ), and a little of it will suffice you' [39]. And he, peace be upon him, said: 'There is no servant who makes his action sincere (yukhliṣ) for Allah for forty days except that the springs of Wisdom (al-Ḥikmah) will appear from his Heart (Qalb) upon his tongue' [40].
18:110.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

18:110.arabic: وقد ذكرنا أن ذلك عصيان وعدوان لا لأن طلب الدنيا حرام ولكن طلبها بأعمال الدين حرام لما فيه من الرياء وتغيير العبادة عن موضعها وأما لفظ الشركة حيث ورد فمطلق للتساوي وقد بينا أنه إذا تساوى القصدان تقاوما ولم يكن له ولا عليه فلا ينبغي أن يرجي عليه ثواب ثم إن الإنسان عند الشركة أبدا في خطر فإنه لا يدري أي الأمرين أغلب على قصده فربما يكون عليه وبالا ولذلك قال تعالى (فمن كان يرجو لقاء ربه فليعمل عملا صالحا ولا يشرك بعبادة ربه أحدا) أي لا يرجي اللقاء مع الشركة التى أحسن أحوالها التساقط.
18:110.english: And we have mentioned that that is disobedience and transgression, not because seeking the worldly life (Dunya) is forbidden, but seeking it through religious works is forbidden due to what it contains of ostentation (Riya) and changing worship from its proper place. As for the term partnership (Shirkah) where it occurs, it is absolute for equality, and we have clarified that if the two intentions are equal, they cancel each other out, and there is neither for him nor against him, so one should not hope for reward upon it. Then indeed, the human being in partnership is always in danger, for he does not know which of the two matters is predominant in his intention; perhaps it will be a calamity upon him. And therefore, Allah the Exalted said: 'So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, then let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone.' That is, do not hope for the meeting with the partnership whose best state is cancellation.
18:110.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

18:110.arabic: اعلم أن الرياء حرام والمرائي عند الله ممقوت، وقد شهدت لذلك الآيات والأخبار والآثار. أما الآيات: فقوله تعالى "فويل للمصلين الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون الذين هم يراءون" وقوله عز وجل "والذين يمكرون السيئات لهم عذاب شديد ومكر أولئك هو يبور" قال مجاهد هم أهل الرياء. وقال تعالى "إنما نعطمكم لوجه الله لا نريد منكم جزاء ولا شكورا" فمدح المخلصين ينفي كل إرادة سوى وجه الله، والرياء ضده وقال تعالى "فمن كان يرجو لقاء ربه فليعمل صالحاً ولا يشرك بعبادة ربه أحدا" نزل بعد ذلك فيمن يطلب الأجر والحمد بعباداته وأعمال
18:110.english: Know that ostentation (Riya') is forbidden and the ostentatious person is detested by Allah, and the verses, reports, and traditions testify to that. As for the verses: His saying, the Exalted, "Woe to those who pray, who are heedless of their prayer, who make show (of their deeds)" and His saying, the Mighty and Majestic, "And those who plot evil deeds, for them is a severe punishment, and the plotting of those, it will perish" said Mujahid: they are the people of ostentation (Riya'). And His saying, the Exalted, "We feed you only for the Face (Wajh) of Allah. We wish no reward nor thanks from you" so He praised the sincere ones (Mukhlisin) by negating every desire except the Face (Wajh) of Allah, and ostentation (Riya') is its opposite. And His saying, the Exalted, "So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, then let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone" was revealed after that concerning those who seek reward and praise through their acts of worship and deeds.
18:110.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

18:110.arabic: أما الآيات: فقوله تعالى "فويل للمصلين الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون الذين هم يراءون" وقوله عز وجل "والذين يمكرون السيئات لهم عذاب شديد ومكر أولئك هو يبور" قال مجاهد هم أهل الرياء. وقال تعالى "إنما نعطمكم لوجه الله لا نريد منكم جزاء ولا شكورا" فمدح المخلصين ينفي كل إرادة سوى وجه الله، والرياء ضده وقال تعالى "فمن كان يرجو لقاء ربه فليعمل صالحاً ولا يشرك بعبادة ربه أحدا" نزل بعد ذلك فيمن يطلب الأجر والحمد بعباداته وأعماله.
18:110.english: As for the verses: His statement, the Exalted: "So woe to those who pray, who are heedless of their prayer, who show off" and His statement, the Mighty and Majestic: "And those who plot evil deeds, for them is a severe punishment, and the plotting of those - it will perish" said Mujahid: they are the people of showing off (Riya'). And His statement, the Exalted: "We feed you only for the Face (Wajh) of Allah, we desire no reward nor thanks from you" so He praised the sincere ones (Mukhlisin) by negating every intention (Iradah) except the Face (Wajh) of Allah, and showing off (Riya') is its opposite. And His statement, the Exalted: "So whoever hopes for the meeting (Liqa') of his Lord, then let him do righteous work (Amalan Salihan) and not associate anyone in the worship (Ibadah) of his Lord" it was revealed after that concerning those who seek reward and praise through their acts of worship (Ibadat) and deeds (A'mal).
18:110.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

18:110.arabic: [22] حديث نزول قوله تعالى فمن كان يرجو لقاء ربه الآية فيمن يطلب الآخرة بعباداته وأعماله أخرجه الحاكم من حديث طاوس قال رجل إني أقف الموقف أبتغي وجه الله وأحب أن يرى موطني فلم يرد عليه حتى نزلت هذه الآية هكذا في نسختي من المستدرك ولعله سقط منه ابن عباس أو أبو هريرة وللبزار من حديث معاذ بسند ضعيف من صام رياء فقد أشرك الحديث وفيه أنه ﭬ تلا هذه الآية.
18:110.english: [22] A hadith about the revelation of His saying, the Exalted: 'So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord...' (Quran 18:110) concerning one who seeks the Hereafter with his acts of worship (Ibadat) and deeds (A'mal). Al-Hakim transmitted it from the hadith of Tawus: A man said, 'I stand in the position seeking the Face (Wajh) of Allah and I love that my standing place be seen.' He did not respond to him until this verse was revealed. Thus it is in my copy of Al-Mustadrak, and perhaps Ibn Abbas or Abu Huraira was omitted from it. And Al-Bazzar has from the hadith of Mu'adh with a weak chain: 'Whoever fasts for show (Riya') has committed association (Ashrak).' In it, he recited this verse.
18:110.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

19:3.arabic: وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها في قوله عز وجل: ﴿ ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها[83] ﴾ {} أي بدعائك وقد أثنى الله عز وجل على نبيه زكرياء عليه السلام حيث قال: ﴿ إذ نادى ربه نداء خفيا ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل: ﴿ ادعوا ربكم تضرعا وخفية ﴾ {}.
19:3.english: And Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said regarding His (the Exalted's) statement: 'And do not raise your voice in your prayer (Salat) nor lower it excessively' meaning in your supplication (Du'a). And Allah (the Exalted) praised His prophet Zakariya (peace be upon him) where He said: 'When he called upon his Lord (Rabb) with a hidden call (Nida'an Khafiyyan).' And He (the Exalted) said: 'Call upon your Lord (Rabb) with humility (Tadarru'an) and in secret (Khufyatan).'
19:3.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

19:12.arabic: الثالث: حضور القلب وترك حديث النفس قيل في تفسير: ﴿ يا يحيى خذ الكتاب بقوة ﴾ {} أي بجد واجتهاد وأخذه بالجد أن يكون متجردا له عند قراءته منصرف الهمة إليه عن غيره وقيل لبعضهم إذا قرأت القرآن تحدث نفسك بشيء فقال أو شيء أحب إلي من القرآن حتى أحدث به نفسي وكان بعض السلف إذا قرأ آية لم يكن قلبه فيها أعادها ثانية وهذه الصفة تتولد عما قبلها من التعظيم فإن المعظم للكلام الذي يتلوه يستبشر به وياستأنس ولا يغفل عنه ففي القرآن ما يستأنس به القلب إن كان التالي أهلا له فكيف يطلب الأنس بالفكر في غيره وهو في متنز
19:12.english: Third: Presence of the Heart (Qalb) and abandoning the talk of the Soul (Nafs). It is said in the interpretation of: 'O Yahya, take the Book with strength' meaning with seriousness and diligence, and taking it with seriousness is to be devoted to it during its recitation, diverting one's concern (Himma) to it away from other things. It was said to someone: 'When you recite the Quran, do you talk to your Soul (Nafs) about something?' He replied: 'Is there anything more beloved to me than the Quran that I would talk to my Soul (Nafs) about it?' Some of the predecessors (Salaf) would repeat a verse if their Heart (Qalb) was not in it. This quality is generated from what precedes it of veneration, for the one who venerates the speech he recites rejoices in it, finds intimacy (Uns) with it, and does not neglect it. In the Quran is what the Heart (Qalb) finds intimacy (Uns) with, if the reciter is worthy of it. So how can one seek intimacy (Uns) through thought in other than it while he is in a pleasure-garden and a place of viewing? The one who views in pleasure-gardens does not think about other than them. It has been said that in the Quran are arenas, gardens, pavilions, brides, brocades, meadows, and inns. The Mims are the arenas of the Quran, the Rās are its gardens, the Hās are its pavilions, the Musabbihat are its brides, the Hamims are its brocades, the Mufassal is its meadows, and the inns are what is besides that. So when the reciter enters the arenas, plucks from the gardens, enters the pavilions, witnesses the brides, wears the brocades, strolls in the meadows, and lodges in the rooms of the inns, that engrosses him and occupies him from other than it, so his Heart (Qalb) does not stray and his thought does not scatter.
19:12.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

19:17.arabic: وقال عز وجل: " فأرسلنا إليها روحنا فتمثل لها بشراً سوياً "، ثم قال تعالى: " فنفخنا فيها من روحنا " وكان النافخ جبريل عليه السلام، وكما قال تعالى: " فإذا قرأناه فاتبع قرآنه " قيل في التفسير: معناه إذا قرأه عليك جبريل.
19:17.english: And He (Exalted and Glorified) said: "So We sent to her Our Spirit (Ruh), and he appeared to her as a well-proportioned human (Bashar)." Then He (Exalted) said: "So We blew into her from Our Spirit (Ruh)." And the blower was Gabriel (peace be upon him). And as He (Exalted) said: "So when We have recited it, then follow its recitation." It is said in the interpretation (Tafsir): Its meaning is when Gabriel recites it to you.
19:17.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

19:33.arabic: وكان عيسى عليه السلام من المفضلين ولإدلاله سلم على نفسه، فقال: "والسلام علي يوم ولدت ويوم أموت ويوم أبعث حياً" وهذا انبساط منه لما شاهد من اللطف في مقام الأنس.
19:33.english: And Jesus (peace be upon him) was among the preferred ones, and due to his intimacy (Idlal), he greeted himself, saying: "And peace be upon me the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I am raised alive." And this is an expansion (Inbisat) from him because of what he witnessed of gentleness (Lutf) in the station (Maqam) of intimacy (Uns).
19:33.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

19:39.arabic: فانظر يا مسكين فى هذه الأهوال واعلم أن الله تعالى خلق النار بأهوالها وخلق أهلا لا يزيدون ولا ينقصون وأن هذا أمر قد قضى وفرغ منه قال الله تعالى: ﴿ وأنذرهم يوم الحسرة إذ قضى الأمر وهم فى غفلة وهم لا يؤمنون ﴾ {} ولعمرى الإشارة به يوم القيامة بل فى أزل ولكن أظهر يوم القيامة ما سبق به القضاء فالعجب منك حيث تضحك وتلهو وتشتغل بمحقرات الدنيا ولست تدرى أن القضاء بماذا سبق فى حقك؛ فإن قلت فليت شعرى ماذا موردى وإلى ماذا مآلى ومرجعى وما الذى سبق به القضاء فى حقى فلك علامة تستأنس بها وتصدق رجاءك بسببها وهى أ
19:39.english: Look, O wretched one, at these terrors and know that Allah the Exalted created the Fire with its terrors and created people who neither increase nor decrease, and that this matter has been decreed and finished with. Allah the Exalted said: 'And warn them of the Day of Regret when the matter is decreed while they are in heedlessness and they do not believe.' {} By my life, the reference is to the Day of Resurrection, but rather in pre-eternity (al-Azal), but on the Day of Resurrection what was preceded by the decree becomes manifest. So the wonder is from you where you laugh and play and busy yourself with the trivialities of the worldly life (al-Dunya) and you do not know what the decree has preceded concerning your right; if you say: 'Would that I knew what my source is and to what my end and return is, and what the decree has preceded concerning my right,' then for you is a sign by which you find comfort and confirm your hope because of it, and it is that you look at your states and your deeds, for each is facilitated for what he was created for. If the path of good has been facilitated for you, then give glad tidings, for you are kept far from the Fire. And if you do not intend good except that obstacles surround you and repel it, and you do not intend evil except that its causes are facilitated for you, then know that you are decreed against. For the indication of this upon the outcome is like the indication of rain upon vegetation and the indication of smoke upon fire. Indeed Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed the righteous are in bliss and indeed the wicked are in a Blazing Fire.' {} So present your soul (Nafs) upon the two verses and you have known your abode from the two abodes, and Allah knows best.
19:39.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

19:41.arabic: فضيلة الصدق قال الله تعالى (رجال صدقوا ما عاهدوا الله عليه) وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم (إن الصدق يهدى إلى البر والبر يهدي إلى الجنة وإن الرجل ليصدق حتى يكتب عند الله صديقا وإن الكذب يهدي إلى الفجور والفجور يهدي إلى النار وإن الرجل ليكذب حتى يكتب عند الله كذابا)[52] ويكفي في فضيلة الصدق أن الصديق مشتق منه والله تعالى وصف الأنبياء به في معرض المدح والثناء فقال (واذكر في الكتاب إبراهيم إنه كان صديقا نبيا) وقال (واذكر في الكتاب إسمعيل إنه كان صادق الوعد وكان رسولا نبيا) وقال تعالى (واذكر في الكتا
19:41.english: The virtue of Truthfulness (Sidq). Allah the Exalted said: 'Men who were true (Sadaqu) to what they promised Allah.' And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, truthfulness (Sidq) guides to righteousness (Al-Birr) and righteousness guides to Paradise. And a man may be truthful until he is recorded with Allah as a Truthful One (Siddiq). And indeed, falsehood (Kadhib) guides to wickedness (Al-Fujur) and wickedness guides to the Fire. And a man may lie until he is recorded with Allah as a liar.' And it suffices for the virtue of truthfulness that 'The Truthful One (Al-Siddiq)' is derived from it. And Allah the Exalted described the Prophets with it in the context of praise and commendation, saying: 'And mention in the Book (Al-Kitab) Ibrahim. Indeed, he was a Truthful One (Siddiq), a Prophet (Nabiyy).' And He said: 'And mention in the Book (Al-Kitab) Isma'il. Indeed, he was true to his promise (Sadiq al-Wa'd) and was a Messenger (Rasul), a Prophet (Nabiyy).' And Allah the Exalted said: 'And mention in the Book (Al-Kitab) Idris. Indeed, he was a Truthful One (Siddiq), a Prophet (Nabiyy).'
19:41.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

19:42.arabic: فانظر كيف دبره وصوره وإلى السبيل كيف يسره وإلى طغيان الإنسان ما أكفره وإلى جهل الإنسان كيف أظهره؟ فقال "إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ يَا أَبَتِ لِمَ تَعْبُدُ مَا لَا يَسْمَعُ وَلَا يُبْصِرُ وَلَا يُغْنِي عَنْكَ شَيْئًا" فقد أشارت الآية إلى أن الإنسان يعبد ما لا يسمع ولا يبصر ولا يغني عنه شيئاً، وهذا منتهى الجهل والغفلة، فإنه يعبد ما هو مثله في العجز والضعف، بل ما هو دونه، فإنه يسمع ويبصر ويغني عن نفسه بعض الإغناء، والمعبود لا يسمع ولا يبصر ولا يغني عنه شيئاً، فكيف يعبد ما هو دونه؟ وهذا منتهى الحماقة وال
19:42.english: So look how He managed him and formed him, and to the path how He made it easy for him, and to the transgression of the human being (Insān) how ungrateful he is, and to the ignorance of the human being how He manifested it? Then He said: "When he said to his father: 'O my father, why do you worship what does not hear and does not see and does not avail you anything?'" For the verse indicated that the human being worships what does not hear and does not see and does not avail him anything, and this is the utmost ignorance (Jahl) and heedlessness (Ghaflah). For he worships what is like him in incapacity and weakness, or rather what is inferior to him, for he hears and sees and avails himself some benefit, while the worshipped does not hear and does not see and does not avail him anything. So how does he worship what is inferior to him? And this is the utmost foolishness (Hamāqah) and ignorance (Jahl).
19:42.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

19:42.arabic: وكيف تعتدل القسمة مهما وقع النقص في جهته والكمال في خلقه وصنعته أو كيف تستقيم حجة إبراهيم ﭬ على أبيه إذ كان يعبد الأصنام جهلا وغيا فقال له لم تعبد ما لا يسمع ولا يبصر ولا يغني عنك شيئا ولو انقلب ذلك عليه في معبوده لأضحت حجته داحضة ودلالته ساقطة ولم يصدق قوله تعالى وتلك حجتنا آتيناها إبراهيم على قومه وكما عقل كونه فاعلا بلا جارحة وعالما بلا قلب ودماغ فليعقل كونه بصيرا بلا حدقة وسميعا بلا أذن إذ لا فرق بينهما.
19:42.english: And how can the division be balanced when deficiency occurs on His side and perfection in His creation and craftsmanship? Or how can the argument of Abraham (peace be upon him) against his father be sound when he was worshipping idols out of ignorance and error, and he said to him: 'Why do you worship what does not hear, nor see, nor avail you anything?' And if that were reversed upon him regarding his worshipped one, his argument would become invalid and his proof would fall, and the saying of Allah the Exalted would not be truthful: 'And that was Our argument which We gave Abraham against his people.' And just as one comprehends His being an Actor without a limb and a Knower without a heart and brain, let him comprehend His being a Seer without a pupil and a Hearer without an ear, for there is no difference between them.
19:42.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

19:48.arabic: ذكر حجج المائلين إلى تفضيل العزلة احتجوا بقوله تعالى حكاية عن إبراهيم عليه السلام وأعتزلكم وما تدعون من دون الله وأدعو ربي الآية ثم قال تعالى فلما اعتزلهم وما يعبدون من دون الله وهبنا له إسحق ويعقوب وكلا جعلنا نبيا إشارة إلى أن ذلك ببركة العزلة وهذا ضعيف لأن مخالطة الكفار لا فائدة فيها إلا دعوتهم إلى الدين وعند اليأس من إجابتهم فلا وجه إلا هجرهم وإنما الكلام في مخالطة المسلمين وما فيها من البركة لما روى أنه قيل يا رسول الله الوضوء من جر مخمر أحب إليك أو من هذه المطاهر التي يتطهر منها الناس فقال
19:48.english: Mentioning the arguments of those inclined toward preferring isolation, they argued with His saying, the Exalted, narrating from Abraham, peace be upon him: 'And I will withdraw from you and what you call upon besides Allah, and I will call upon my Lord. Perhaps I will not be in calling upon my Lord unhappy.' Then Allah said: 'So when he withdrew from them and what they worship besides Allah, We gave him Isaac and Jacob, and each We made a prophet.' Indicating that this was by the blessing (Barakah) of isolation. And this is weak because mixing with disbelievers has no benefit except calling them to the religion, and when despairing of their response, there is no aspect except abandoning them. Rather, the discussion is about mixing with Muslims and what is in it of blessing (Barakah), as it was narrated that it was said: 'O Messenger of Allah, ablution (Wudu) from a sealed jug is more beloved to you or from these public water sources from which people purify themselves?' He said: 'Rather from these public water sources,' seeking the blessing (Barakah) of the hands of Muslims. The hadith: It was said to him, peace be upon him: 'Ablution (Wudu) from a sealed jug is more beloved to you or from these public water sources from which people purify themselves?' He said: 'Rather from these public water sources.' The hadith was reported by Al-Tabarani in Al-Awsat from the narration of Ibn Umar, and there is weakness in it. And it was narrated that when he, peace be upon him, circumambulated the House, he turned to Zamzam to drink from it, and there was the dates soaked in leather basins, and the people had mixed it with their hands, and they were taking from it and drinking. He asked for drink from it and said: 'Give me to drink.' Al-Abbas said: 'This is a drink that has been mixed and stirred with hands. Shall I not bring you a drink cleaner than this from a sealed jug in the house?' He said: 'Give me to drink from this from which the people drink, seeking the blessing (Barakah) of the hands of Muslims.' So he drank from it. The hadith: When he circumambulated the House.
19:48.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Seclusion'

19:49.arabic: احتجوا بقوله تعالى حكاية عن إبراهيم عليه السلام وأعتزلكم وما تدعون من دون الله وأدعو ربي الآية ثم قال تعالى فلما اعتزلهم وما يعبدون من دون الله وهبنا له إسحق ويعقوب وكلا جعلنا نبيا إشارة إلى أن ذلك ببركة العزلة وهذا ضعيف لأن مخالطة الكفار لا فائدة فيها إلا دعوتهم إلى الدين وعند اليأس من إجابتهم فلا وجه إلا هجرهم وإنما الكلام في مخالطة المسلمين وما فيها من البركة لما روى أنه قيل يا رسول الله الوضوء من جر مخمر أحب إليك أو من هذه المطاهر التي يتطهر منها الناس فقال بل من هذه المطاهر التماسا لبركة أي
19:49.english: They argued with His saying, Exalted is He, narrating from Abraham, peace be upon him: 'And I will withdraw from you and what you call upon besides Allah, and I will call upon my Lord...' Then Allah said: 'So when he withdrew from them and what they worship besides Allah, We granted him Isaac and Jacob, and each We made a prophet' - indicating that this was by the blessing (barakah) of withdrawal. And this is weak because mixing with disbelievers has no benefit except calling them to the religion, and when despairing of their response, there is no aspect except abandoning them. Rather, the discussion is about mixing with Muslims and what is in it of blessing (barakah), as it was narrated that it was said: 'O Messenger of Allah, is ablution (wudu) from a sealed jar more beloved to you or from these water sources from which people purify themselves?' He said: 'Rather from these water sources' - seeking the blessing (barakah) of the hands of Muslims.
19:49.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Seclusion'

19:54.arabic: فإن اللسان سباق إلى الوعد، ثم النفس ربما لا تسمح بالوفاء فيصير الوعد خلفاً وذلك من أمارات النفاق قال الله تعالى "يا أيها الذين آمنوا أوفوا بالعقود" وقال ﭬ "العدة عطية"[128] وقال ﭬ "الوأي مثل الدين أو أفضل"[129] والوأي: الوعد. وقد أثنى الله تعالى على نبيه اسمعيل عليه السلام في كتابه العزيز فقال "إنه كان صادق الوعد" قيل إنه وعد إنساناً في موضع فلم يرجع إليه ذلك الإنسان بل نسي، فبقي اسمعيل اثنين وعشرين يوماً في انتظاره.
19:54.english: For the tongue is swift to promise, then the Soul (Nafs) perhaps does not permit fulfillment, so the promise becomes broken, and that is from the signs of hypocrisy. Allah the Exalted said: 'O you who have believed, fulfill [all] contracts' and He ﭬ said: 'The promise is a gift' and He ﭬ said: 'The promise (al-wa'y) is like debt or better' and al-wa'y: the promise. And Allah the Exalted praised His prophet Ishmael, peace be upon him, in His Noble Book, so He said: 'Indeed, he was true to his promise.' It is said that he promised a person in a place, but that person did not return to him, rather he forgot, so Ishmael remained twenty-two days awaiting him.
19:54.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

19:54.arabic: فضيلة الصدق قال الله تعالى (رجال صدقوا ما عاهدوا الله عليه) وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم (إن الصدق يهدى إلى البر والبر يهدي إلى الجنة وإن الرجل ليصدق حتى يكتب عند الله صديقا وإن الكذب يهدي إلى الفجور والفجور يهدي إلى النار وإن الرجل ليكذب حتى يكتب عند الله كذابا)[52] ويكفي في فضيلة الصدق أن الصديق مشتق منه والله تعالى وصف الأنبياء به في معرض المدح والثناء فقال (واذكر في الكتاب إبراهيم إنه كان صديقا نبيا) وقال (واذكر في الكتاب إسمعيل إنه كان صادق الوعد وكان رسولا نبيا) وقال تعالى (واذكر في الكتا
19:54.english: The virtue of truthfulness (Sidq) - Allah the Exalted said: 'Men who were true (Sadaqu) to what they promised Allah' and the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed truthfulness (Sidq) guides to righteousness (Al-Birr) and righteousness guides to Paradise, and indeed a man may be truthful (Yasduq) until he is recorded with Allah as a truthful one (Siddiq), and indeed falsehood (Al-Kidhb) guides to wickedness (Al-Fujur) and wickedness guides to the Fire, and indeed a man may lie (Yakdhib) until he is recorded with Allah as a liar (Kadhdhab).' [52] And it suffices in the virtue of truthfulness (Sidq) that 'the truthful one' (Al-Siddiq) is derived from it, and Allah the Exalted described the prophets with it in the context of praise and commendation, so He said: 'And mention in the Book Abraham; indeed, he was a truthful one (Siddiq) and a prophet.' And He said: 'And mention in the Book Ishmael; indeed, he was truthful (Sadiq) to the promise and was a messenger, a prophet.' And Allah the Exalted said: 'And mention in the Book Idris; indeed, he was a truthful one (Siddiq) and a prophet.'
19:54.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

19:56.arabic: وَكَفِي فِي فَضِيلَةِ الصِّدْقِ أَنَّ الصِّدِّيقَ مُشْتَقٌّ مِنْهُ وَاللَّهُ تَعَالَى وَصَفَ الْأَنْبِيَاءَ بِهِ فِي مَعْرَضِ الْمَدْحِ وَالثَّنَاءِ فَقَالَ (وَاذْكُرْ فِي الْكِتَابِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ إِنَّهُ كَانَ صِدِّيقًا نَبِيًّا) وَقَالَ (وَاذْكُرْ فِي الْكِتَابِ إِسْمَعِيلَ إِنَّهُ كَانَ صَادِقَ الْوَعْدِ وَكَانَ رَسُولًا نَبِيًّا) وَقَالَ تَعَالَى (وَاذْكُرْ فِي الْكِتَابِ إِدْرِيسَ إِنَّهُ كَانَ صِدِّيقًا نَبِيًّا).
19:56.english: And it suffices in the virtue of Truthfulness (Sidq) that the Truthful One (Siddiq) is derived from it, and Allah the Exalted described the Prophets with it in the context of praise and commendation, so He said: 'And mention in the Book Abraham; indeed, he was a Truthful One (Siddiq), a Prophet (Nabi).' And He said: 'And mention in the Book Ishmael; indeed, he was true to his promise (Sadiq al-Wa'd), and he was a Messenger (Rasul), a Prophet (Nabi).' And the Exalted said: 'And mention in the Book Idris; indeed, he was a Truthful One (Siddiq), a Prophet (Nabi).'
19:56.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

19:59.arabic: وإن قطع عن بذر الإيمان تعهده بماء الطاعات وترك القلب مشحونا برذائل الأخلاق وانهمك في طلب لذات الدنيا ثم انتظر المغفرة فانتظاره حمق وغرور قال صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم: (الأحمق من أتبع نفسه هواها وتمنى على الله الجنة[1]) وقال تعالى: ﴿ فخلف من بعدهم أضاعوا الصلاة واتبعوا الشهوات فسوف يلقون غيا ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ فخلف من بعدهم خلف ورثوا الكتاب يأخذون عرض هذا الأدنى ويقولون سيغفر لنا ﴾{} وذم الله تعالى صاحب البستان إذا دخل جنته وقال: ﴿ ما أظن تبيده هذه أبدا وما أظن الساعة قائمة ولئن رددت إلى ربدى لأجد
19:59.english: And if he abandons nurturing the seed of faith (Iman) with the water of acts of obedience (Taa'at) and leaves the heart (Qalb) filled with vile character traits (Akhlāq) and immerses himself in seeking the pleasures of this world (Dunya), then expects forgiveness, his expectation is foolishness and delusion. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The foolish one is he who follows his soul's (Nafs) desires (Hawa) and expects Paradise from Allah.' And Allah the Exalted said: 'Then there succeeded after them a succession who neglected the prayer (Salah) and followed the lusts (Shahawat), so they will meet misguidance (Ghayy).' And Allah the Exalted said: 'Then there succeeded after them a succession who inherited the Book, taking the gains of this lower life and saying: "It will be forgiven for us."' And Allah the Exalted censured the owner of the garden when he entered his garden and said: 'I do not think this will ever perish, and I do not think the Hour will occur. And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find a better place than this to return to.' So if the servant (Abd) strives in acts of obedience (Taa'at) and avoids sins (Ma'asi), he is worthy to expect from Allah's grace (Fadl) the completion of the blessing (Ni'mah), and the completion of the blessing is nothing but entering Paradise.
19:59.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

19:59.arabic: و أعلم أن أيسر ما ارتكبت واخف ما احتملت أنك آنست وحشة الظالم وسهلت سبيل البغي بدنوك ممن لم يؤد حقا ولم يترك باطلا حين أدناك اتخذوك قطبا تدور عليك رحى ظلمهم وجسرا يعبرون عليك إلى بلائهم وسلما يصعدون فيه إلى ضلالهم ويدخلون بك الشك على العلماء ويصادون بك قلوب الجهلاء فما أيسر ما عمروا في جنب ما خربوا عليك وما أكثر ما أخذوا منك فيما أفسدوا عليك من دينك فما يؤمنك أن تكون ممن قال الله تعالى فيهم فخلف من بعدهم خلف أضاعوا الصلاة الآية وإنك تعامل من لا يجهل ويحفظ عليك من لا يغفل فداو دينك فقد دخله سقم وه
19:59.english: And know that the easiest of what you have committed and the lightest of what you have borne is that you have comforted the loneliness of the oppressor and facilitated the path of transgression by your proximity to one who has not fulfilled a right nor abandoned falsehood. When they brought you close, they made you a pivot (Qutb) around which the millstone of their oppression revolves, and a bridge they cross over to their calamity, and a ladder they ascend in it to their misguidance, and they enter doubt upon the scholars through you, and they hunt with you the hearts (Qulub) of the ignorant. How little they have built compared to what they have destroyed upon you, and how much they have taken from you in what they have corrupted upon you of your religion (Deen). What assures you that you are not among those about whom Allah the Exalted said: 'Then there succeeded after them a succession who neglected the prayer (As-Salah) and followed the lusts, so they will meet misguidance' (Quran 19:59)? And you are dealing with One who does not ignore and who preserves upon you One who does not neglect. So treat your religion (Deen), for sickness has entered it, and prepare your provision, for a distant journey has arrived. And nothing is hidden from Allah of anything in the earth nor in the heaven. And peace. These reports and traditions indicate what is in mixing with the rulers of trials and types of corruption.
19:59.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

19:62.arabic: وإن أنهارها لتجرى على رضراض من ياقوت وزبرجد وإن عروقها ونخلها وكرمها اللؤلؤ وثمارها لا يعلم علمها إلا الله تعالى وإن ريحها ليوجد من مسيرة خمسمائة سنة وإن لهم فيها خيلا وإبلا هفافة رحالها وأزمتها وسروجها من ياقوت يتزاورون فيها وأزواجهم الحور العين كأنهن بيض مكنون وإن المرأة لتأخذ بين أصبعيها سبعين حلة فتلبسها فيرى مخ ساقها من وراء تلك السبعين حلة قد طهر الله الأخلاق من السوء والأجساد من الموت لا يمتخطون فيها ولا يبولون ولا يتغوطون وإنما هو حبشاء ورشح مسك لهم رزقهم فيها بكرة وعشيا أما إنه ليس ليل
19:62.english: And its rivers flow upon pebbles of ruby and emerald, and its roots, palms, and vines are pearls, and its fruits—none knows their knowledge except Allah the Exalted. And its fragrance is found from a journey of five hundred years. And they have therein horses and camels, light, their saddles, bridles, and saddles of ruby; they visit each other therein, and their spouses are the wide-eyed maidens, as if they were hidden pearls. And the woman takes between her two fingers seventy garments and wears them, and the marrow of her leg is seen from behind those seventy garments. Allah has purified the morals from evil and the bodies from death; they do not blow their noses therein, nor do they urinate, nor defecate, and it is only a pleasant fragrance and musk sweat. For them is their provision therein morning and evening. But indeed, there is no night; the morning alternates with the evening and the evening with the morning. And the last to enter Paradise and the lowest in rank—his sight and his dominion are extended for a journey of one hundred years in palaces of gold and silver and tents of pearl, and his sight is expanded until he sees its farthest as he sees its nearest. They are served in the morning with seventy thousand platters of gold and in the evening with the like thereof; in each platter is a color not like the other, and he finds the taste of its end as he finds the taste of its beginning. And in Paradise is a ruby containing seventy thousand dwellings, in each dwelling seventy thousand houses, with no crack or hole.
19:62.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

19:68.arabic: ثم أقبلت الشياطين المردة بعد تمردها وعتوها وأذعنت خاشعة من هيبة العرض على الله تعالى تصديقا لقوله تعالى: ﴿ فوربك لنحشرنهم والشياطين ثم لنحضرنهم حول جهنم جثيا ﴾ {} فتفكر فى حالك وحال قلبك هنالك.
19:68.english: Then the rebellious devils (Shayatin) came forward after their rebellion and arrogance, and they submitted humbly from the awe of the presentation before Allah the Exalted, confirming His saying: 'So by your Lord, We will surely gather them and the devils (Shayatin); then We will bring them around Hell on their knees (Jithiyyan).' So contemplate your state and the state of your heart (Qalb) there.
19:68.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

19:69.arabic: وشر أنواع الكبر ما يمنع من استفادة العلم وقبول الحق والانقياد له وفيه وردت الآيات التي فيها ذم الكبر والمتكبرين قال الله تعالى "والملائكة باسطو أيديهم" إلى قوله "وكنتم عن آياته تستكبرون" ثم قال "ادخلوا أبواب جهنم خالدين فيها فبئس مثوى المتكبرين" ثم أخبر أن أشد أهل النار عذاباً أشدهم عتياً على الله تعالى فقال "ثم لننزعن من كل شبعة أيهم أشد على الرحمن عتياً" وقال تعالى "فالذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة قلوبهم منكرة وهم مستكبرون" وقال عز وجل "يقول الذين استضعفوا للذين استكبروا لولا أنتم لكنا مؤمنين" وقال ت
19:69.english: And the worst type of arrogance (Kibr) is what prevents from benefiting from knowledge and accepting the truth and submitting to it, and in it came the verses which contain condemnation of arrogance (Kibr) and the arrogant ones. Allah the Exalted said: "And the angels will be spreading their hands" up to His saying: "and you were arrogant (Tastakbirun) about His signs." Then He said: "Enter the gates of Hell, abiding eternally therein, and wretched is the residence of the arrogant (Mutakabbirin)." Then He informed that the most severely punished of the people of the Fire are those most insolent (Atiyyan) against Allah the Exalted, so He said: "Then We will surely extract from every sect (Shi'ah) those of them who were most insolent (Atiyyan) against the Most Merciful." And He said: "So those who do not believe in the Hereafter - their hearts (Qulub) are denying and they are arrogant (Mustakbirun)." And He the Mighty and Majestic said: "Those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant (Istakbaru): 'If not for you, we would have been believers.'" And He said: "Indeed, those who are arrogant (Yastakbirun) about My worship will enter Hell humiliated." And He said: "I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant (Yatakabbarun) on the earth without right." It is said in the interpretation (Tafsir): I will lift the understanding of the Quran from their hearts (Qulub), and in some interpretations (Tafasir) I will veil their hearts (Qulub) from the dominion (Malakut). And Ibn Juraij said: I will turn them away from reflecting upon them and taking admonition from them.
19:69.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

19:71.arabic: يا أيها الغافل عن نفسه المغرور بما هو فيه من شواغل هذه الدنيا المشرفة على الانقضاء والزوال دع التفكر فيما أنت مرتحل عنه واصرف الفكر إلى موردك فإنك أخبرت بأن النار مورد للجميع إذ قيل: ﴿ وإن منكم إلا واردها كان على ربك حتما مقضيا ثم ننجى الذين اتقوا ونذر الظالمين فيها جثيا ﴾ {} فأنت من الورود على يقين ومن النجاة فى شك فاستشعر فى قلبك هول ذلك المورد فعساك تستعد للنجاة منه وتأمل فى حال الخلائق وقد قاسوا من دواهى القيامة ما قاسوا فبينما هم فى كربها وأهوالها وقوفا ينتظرون حقيقة أنبائها وتشفيع شفعائها
19:71.english: O you who are heedless (Ghaafil) of your Soul (Nafs), deluded by what you are in of the preoccupations of this World (Dunya) that is approaching expiration and vanishing, leave contemplating what you are departing from and direct the thought (Fikr) to your watering place (Mawrid). For you have been informed that the Fire (Nar) is a watering place for all, as it is said: 'And there is none of you but will pass over it (Hell); this is with your Lord a decree which must be accomplished. Then We shall save those who used to fear Allah and were dutiful to Him. And We shall leave the wrong-doers therein (humbled) to their knees (in Hell).' So you are of the passing over (Wurood) with certainty and of the salvation (Najaah) in doubt. So feel in your Heart (Qalb) the terror of that watering place, perhaps you may prepare for salvation from it. And contemplate the state of the creatures when they have suffered from the calamities of the Resurrection (Qiyaamah) what they suffered. While they are in its distress and terrors, standing, awaiting the reality of its tidings and the intercession (Shafaa'ah) of its intercessors (Shufa'aa'), when darknesses with branches surrounded the criminals and a fire with flame overshadowed them, and they heard for it a roaring and rumbling that expresses the intensity of rage and anger. At that, the criminals became certain of destruction, and the nations knelt on their knees until the innocent ones feared the evil of the outcome. And the caller from the guardians of Hell (Zabaniyah) came out saying: 'Where is so-and-so son of so-and-so, who prolonged his Soul (Nafs) in the World (Dunya) with long hope (Amal), wasting his life in evil work?' So they hasten to him with iron maces and confront him with great threats, and drive him to the severe punishment, and plunge him into the bottom of Hell (Jahim), and say to him: 'Taste! Indeed, you are the mighty, the noble!' - So they dwell in an abode narrow in its expanses, dark in its paths, obscure in its perils, where the captive is made to abide eternally and the blazing fire is kindled. Their drink therein is boiling water, and their abode is Hell (Jahim). The guardians of Hell (Zabaniyah) crush them, and the abyss (Haawiyah) gathers them. Their hopes (Amaaniyy) therein are destruction, and they have no escape from it. Their feet have been tied to their foreheads, and their faces have blackened from the darkness of sins. They call from its corners and cry out in its regions, and...
19:71.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

19:71.arabic: بل قوله تعالى: ﴿ وإن منكم إلا واردها ﴾ {} كالصريح في أن ذلك لا بد منه للكل إذ لا يخلو مؤمن عن ذنب يرتكبه وقوله تعالى: ﴿ لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى الذي كذب وتولى ﴾ {} أراد به من جماعة مخصوصين أو أراد بالأشقى شخصا معينا أيضا وقوله تعالى: ﴿ كلما ألقي فيها فوج سألهم خزنتها ﴾ {} أي فوج من الكفار وتخصيص العمومات قريب ومن هذه الآية وقع للأشعري وطائفة من المتكلمين إنكار صيغ العموم وأن هذه الألفاظ يتوقف فيها إلى ظهور قرينة تدل على معناها. وأما المعتزلة فشبهتهم قوله تعالى: ﴿ وإني لغفار لمن تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا
19:71.english: Rather, His (Allah's) saying, exalted is He: 'And there is not one of you except that he will enter it' is like the explicit statement that this is inevitable for all, since no believer is free from a sin he commits. And His saying, exalted is He: 'None will burn in it except the most wretched, who denied and turned away' intended by it a specific group or intended by 'the most wretched' a specific person also. And His saying, exalted is He: 'Whenever a group is thrown into it, its keepers will ask them' meaning a group from the disbelievers, and specifying the generalities is plausible. And from this verse occurred for Al-Ash'ari and a group of the theologians the denial of the forms of generality and that these expressions are suspended until the appearance of an indicator that points to their meaning. As for the Mu'tazila, their doubt is His saying, exalted is He: 'And indeed, I am Forgiving to whoever repents and believes and does righteous (ṣāliḥ) work then remains guided' and His saying, exalted is He: 'By time, indeed, mankind is in loss, except those who have believed and done righteous (ṣāliḥ) works' and His saying, exalted is He: 'And there is not one of you except that he will enter it; it has been upon your Lord an inevitable decree' then He said: 'Then We will save those who feared (ittaqā)'
19:71.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Foundations of Belief'

19:71.arabic: فالعجب أنا لا نعتبر به ولسنا على ثقة فيما نلقاه بل نحن أسراء الشهوات وقرناء المعاصي والسيئات فما بالنا لا نتعظ بمصرع محمد سيد المرسلين وإمام المتقين وحبيب رب العالمين لعلنا نظن أننا مخلدون أو نتوهم أنَّا مع سُوءِ أفعالنا عند الله مكرمون! هيهات هيهات! بل نتيقن أنا جميعا على النار واردون ثم لا ينجو منها إلا المتقون فنحن للورود مستيقنون وللصدور عنها متوهمون لا، بل ظلمنا أنفسنا إن كنا كذلك لغالب الظن منتظرين فما نحن والله من المتقين. وقد قال الله رب العالمين: ﴿ وإن منكم إلا واردها كان على ربك حتما م
19:71.english: So it is astonishing that we do not take heed from him, and we are not confident in what we will encounter. Rather, we are captives of desires (Shahawat) and companions of sins (Ma'asi) and evil deeds (Sayyi'at). So why do we not learn a lesson from the death of Muhammad, the master of the messengers (Sayyid al-Mursalin) and the leader of the God-fearing (Imam al-Muttaqin) and the beloved of the Lord of the worlds (Habib Rabb al-'Alamin)? Perhaps we think that we are immortal, or we imagine that we, with our evil actions, are honored before Allah! Far from it, far from it! Rather, we are certain that we are all entering the Fire (al-Nar) as entrants (Waridun), then none will be saved from it except the God-fearing (al-Muttaqun). So we are certain of the entering (al-Wurud) and we imagine the emerging (al-Sudur) from it. No, rather we have wronged ourselves if we are waiting for the predominant assumption (Ghalib al-Zann) in such a manner, for we are not, by Allah, from the God-fearing (al-Muttaqin). And Allah, the Lord of the worlds, has said: 'And there is none of you but will come to it (enter it). This is upon your Lord a decree (Hatm) determined (Maqdi). Then We will save those who feared (ittaqaw) and leave the wrongdoers (al-Zalimin) therein on their knees (Jithiyyan).' So let every servant (Abd) look at himself: is he closer to the wrongdoers (al-Zalimin) or to the God-fearing (al-Muttaqin)? Then look at yourself after you look at the conduct of the righteous predecessors (al-Salaf al-Salihin), for they were, with what they were granted, from the fearful (al-Kha'ifin). Then look at the master of the messengers (Sayyid al-Mursalin), for he was certain in his affair, as he was the master of the prophets (Sayyid al-Nabiyyin) and the leader of the God-fearing (Qa'id al-Muttaqin). And consider how his distress (Karb) was at the parting from the world (al-Dunya) and how his affair intensified at the turning back (al-Inqilab) to the Garden of Abode (Jannat al-Ma'wa)!
19:71.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

19:71.arabic: وقوله تعالى:  وإن منكم إلا واردها ﴾ {} الآية،
19:71.english: And His saying, the Exalted: 'And there is none of you but will pass over it (the Fire)' (Quran 19:71) {} the verse,
19:71.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Fear and Hope'

19:71.arabic: وقوله تعالى: ﴿ وإن منكم إلا واردها ﴾ {} كالصريح في أن ذلك لا بد منه للكل إذ لا يخلو مؤمن عن ذنب يرتكبه وقوله تعالى: ﴿ لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى الذي كذب وتولى ﴾ {} أراد به من جماعة مخصوصين أو أراد بالأشقى شخصا معينا أيضا وقوله تعالى: ﴿ كلما ألقي فيها فوج سألهم خزنتها ﴾ {} أي فوج من الكفار وتخصيص العمومات قريب ومن هذه الآية وقع للأشعري وطائفة من المتكلمين إنكار صيغ العموم وأن هذه الألفاظ يتوقف فيها إلى ظهور قرينة تدل على معناها. وأما المعتزلة فشبهتهم قوله تعالى: ﴿ وإني لغفار لمن تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا ثم
19:71.english: And His saying, the Exalted: 'And there is none of you except he will enter it' (Quran 19:71) is like the explicit in that this is inevitable for all since no believer is free from a sin he commits. And His saying, the Exalted: 'None will burn in it except the most wretched one who denied and turned away' (Quran 92:15-16) intended by it a specific group or intended by 'the most wretched one' a specific person also. And His saying, the Exalted: 'Whenever a group is thrown into it, its keepers will ask them' (Quran 67:8) meaning a group from the disbelievers, and specifying the generalities is close. And from this verse occurred for Al-Ash'ari and a group of the theologians the denial of the forms of generality and that these words are suspended in them until the appearance of an indication that points to their meaning. As for the Mu'tazila, their doubt is His saying, the Exalted: 'And indeed, I am Forgiving to he who repents and believes and does righteous (Sālih) work then remains rightly guided' (Quran 20:82) and His saying, the Exalted: 'By time, indeed, mankind is in loss, except those who have believed and done righteous (Sālih) works' (Quran 103:1-3) and His saying, the Exalted: 'And there is none of you except he will enter it. It has been upon your Lord a decree determined' (Quran 19:71) then He said: 'Then We will save those who feared (ittaqū)' (Quran 19:72).
19:71.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Foundations of Belief'

19:72.arabic: ثم قال: ﴿ ثم ننجي الذين اتقوا ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ ومن يعص الله ورسوله فإن له نار جهنم ﴾ {} وكل آية ذكر الله عز وجل العمل الصالح فيها مقرونا بالإيمان وقوله تعالى: ﴿ ومن يقتل مؤمنا متعمدا فجزاؤه جهنم خالدا فيها ﴾ {} وهذه العمومات أيضا مخصوصة بدليل قوله تعالى: ﴿ ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء ﴾ {} فينبغي أن تبقى له مشيئة في مغفرة ما سوى الشرك وكذلك قوله ﭬ: (يخرج من النار من كان في قلبه مثقال ذرة من إيمان) وقوله تعالى: ﴿ إنا لا نضيع أجر من أحسن عملا ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ إن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين ﴾ {} ف
19:72.english: Then He said: 'Then We will save those who feared (Allah) (ittaqaw)' and His saying, the Exalted: 'And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger - then indeed, for him is the Fire of Hell; they will abide therein forever' and every verse in which Allah, the Exalted, mentions righteous work (al-'amal al-salih) coupled with faith (iman) and His saying, the Exalted: 'And whoever kills a believer intentionally - his recompense is Hell, wherein he will abide eternally' and these generalities are also specified by the evidence of His saying, the Exalted: 'And He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills' so it is appropriate that His will (mashiyyah) remains in forgiving what is besides polytheism (shirk) and likewise His saying (peace be upon him): 'He will bring out of the Fire whoever had in his heart (qalb) an atom's weight of faith (iman)' and His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, We do not allow to be lost the reward of any who did well in deeds' and His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, Allah does not allow to be lost the reward of the doers of good (muhsinin)' so how could the reward of the foundation of faith (iman) and all acts of obedience (ta'at) be lost by a single disobedience? And His saying, the Exalted: 'And whoever kills a believer intentionally' meaning because of his faith (iman) and it has come for such a reason.
19:72.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

19:77.arabic: وكذلك وصف الله تعالى قول العاص ابن وائل إذ يقول "لأوتين مالاً وولداً" فقال الله تعالى رداً عليه "أطلع الغيب أم اتخذ عند الرحمن عهداً كلا" وروي عن خباب بن الأرت أنه قال: كان لي على العاص بن وائل دين فجئت أتقاضاه فلم يقض لي فقلت: إني آخذه في الآخرة؛ فقال لي: إذا صرت إلى الآخرة فإن لي هناك مالاً وولداً أقضيك منه. فأنزل الله تعالى قوله "أفرأيت الذي كفر بآياتنا وقال لأوتين مالاً وولداً"[6] وقال الله تعالى "ولئن أذقناه رحمة منا من بعد ضراء مسته ليقولن هذا لي وما أظن الساعة قائمة ولئن رجعت إلى ربي إن ل
19:77.english: And likewise, Allah the Exalted described the statement of Al-'As ibn Wa'il when he says "I will certainly be given wealth and children." So Allah the Exalted responded to him, saying "Has he known the unseen or taken a covenant with the Most Merciful? No!" And it is narrated from Khabbab ibn al-Aratt that he said: I had a debt upon Al-'As ibn Wa'il, so I came to demand it from him, but he did not settle it for me. So I said: I will take it in the Hereafter; he said to me: When you reach the Hereafter, then indeed I have there wealth and children, I will settle you from it. So Allah the Exalted revealed His saying "Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our signs and said, 'I will surely be given wealth and children'?"[6] And Allah the Exalted said "And if We give him a taste of mercy from Us after adversity has touched him, he will surely say, 'This is due to me, and I do not think the Hour will occur; but if I am returned to my Lord, indeed, for me there will be with Him the best.'" And all of this is from delusion (Ghurur) regarding Allah.
19:77.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

19:77.arabic: [6]  حديث خباب بن الأرت قال كان لي على العاص بن وائل دين فجئت أتقاضاه الحديث في نزول قوله تعالى - أفرأيت الذي كفر بآياتنا - الآية أخرجه البخاري ومسلم.
19:77.english: [6] The hadith of Khabbab ibn al-Aratt: He said: I had a debt owed by al-'As ibn Wa'il, so I came to collect it. The hadith regarding the revelation of His saying, the Exalted: 'Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our signs...' - the verse. Reported by al-Bukhari and Muslim.
19:77.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

19:78.arabic: وكذلك وصف الله تعالى قول العاص ابن وائل إذ يقول "لأوتين مالاً وولداً" فقال الله تعالى رداً عليه "أطلع الغيب أم اتخذ عند الرحمن عهداً كلا" وروي عن خباب بن الأرت أنه قال: كان لي على العاص بن وائل دين فجئت أتقاضاه فلم يقض لي فقلت: إني آخذه في الآخرة؛ فقال لي: إذا صرت إلى الآخرة فإن لي هناك مالاً وولداً أقضيك منه. فأنزل الله تعالى قوله "أفرأيت الذي كفر بآياتنا وقال لأوتين مالاً وولداً"[6] وقال الله تعالى "ولئن أذقناه رحمة منا من بعد ضراء مسته ليقولن هذا لي وما أظن الساعة قائمة ولئن رجعت إلى ربي إن ل
19:78.english: And likewise, Allah the Exalted described the statement of Al-'As ibn Wa'il when he says "I will certainly be given wealth and children." So Allah the Exalted responded to him: "Has he perceived the unseen (Al-Ghayb) or taken a covenant (Ahd) with the Most Merciful (Al-Rahman)? No!" And it is narrated from Khabbab ibn Al-Aratt that he said: I had a debt on Al-'As ibn Wa'il, so I came to demand it from him, but he did not settle it for me. So I said: I will take it in the Hereafter (Al-Akhirah); he said to me: When I reach the Hereafter, indeed I have there wealth and children, I will repay you from it. So Allah the Exalted revealed His saying: "Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our signs and said, 'I will certainly be given wealth and children'?" And Allah the Exalted said: "And if We give him a taste of mercy (Rahmah) from Us after hardship has touched him, he will surely say, 'This is mine, and I do not think the Hour will occur; and if I am returned to my Lord, indeed, for me there will be with Him the best.'" And all of this is from delusion (Ghurur) regarding Allah.
19:78.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

19:84.arabic: وكان الحسن يقول في موعظته المبادرة المبادرة فإنما هي الأنفاس لو حبست انقطعت عنكم أعمالكم التي تتقربون بها إلى الله عز وجل رحم الله امرأ نظر إلى نفسه وبكى على عدد ذنوبه ثم قرأ هذه الآية ﴿ إنما نعد لهم عدا ﴾ {} يعني الأنفاس آخر العدد خروج نفسك آخر العدد فراق أهلك آخر العدد دخولك في قبرك.
19:84.english: And Al-Hasan (Al-Basri) used to say in his sermon: 'Hasten, hasten, for indeed it is breaths—if they are held back, your deeds through which you draw near to Allah (God), the Mighty and Majestic, are cut off. May Allah have mercy on a person who looks at his Soul (Nafs) and weeps over the number of his sins.' Then he recited this verse: 'Indeed, We count for them a counting (ʿadadan).' {} Meaning: breaths—the last of the counting is the departure of your breath (Nafs); the last of the counting is the separation from your family; the last of the counting is your entry into your grave.
19:84.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

19:85.arabic: ثم تفكر بعد هذه الأهوال فى قول الله تعالى: ﴿ يوم نحشر المتقين إلى الرحمن وفدا ونسوق المجرمين إلى جهنم وردا ﴾ {} وفى قوله تعالى: ﴿ فاهدوهم إلى صراط الجحيم. وقفوهم إنهم مسئولون ﴾ {} فالناس من بعد هذه الأهوال يساقون إلى الصراط وهو جسر ممدود على متن النار أحد من السيف وأدق من الشعر فمن استقام فى هذا العالم على الصراط المستقيم خف على صراط الآخرة ونجا ومن عدل عن الاستقامة فى الدنيا وأثقل ظهره بالأوزار وعصى تعثر فى أول قدم من الصراط وتردى فتفكر الآن فيما يحل من الفزع بفؤادك إذا رأيت الصراط ودقته ثم وقع
19:85.english: Then reflect after these terrors upon the saying of Allah the Exalted: 'On the Day when We will gather the God-fearing (Al-Muttaqin) to the Most Merciful (Al-Rahman) as a delegation, and drive the criminals to Hell as a thirsty herd' (Quran 19:85-86) and upon His saying: 'So guide them to the path (Siraat) of Hell. And stop them; indeed, they are to be questioned' (Quran 37:23-24). The people, after these terrors, are driven to the Bridge (Al-Siraat), which is a bridge extended over the back of the Fire, sharper than the sword and finer than a hair. Whoever was upright in this world upon the Straight Path (Al-Siraat al-Mustaqim) will be light upon the Bridge of the Hereafter and be saved, and whoever deviated from uprightness in the world and burdened his back with sins (Awzar) and disobeyed will stumble at the first step of the Bridge and fall. So reflect now upon what befalls your heart (Fu'ad) of terror when you see the Bridge and its fineness, then your sight falls upon the blackness of Hell beneath it, then your hearing is struck by the roaring of the Fire and its rage, and you have been tasked to walk upon the Bridge with the weakness of your state and the agitation of your heart (Qalb) and the trembling of your foot and the burden of your back with sins (Awzar) preventing you from walking on the carpet of the earth, let alone the sharpness of the Bridge. How will it be with you when you place one of your feet upon it and feel its sharpness and are compelled to lift the second foot, and the creatures before you slip and stumble, and the guards of the Fire pull them down with hooks and grappling irons, and you look at them how they are overturned so that their heads descend toward the direction of the Fire and their legs rise. Oh, what a sight, how dreadful it is, and what an ascent, how difficult it is, and what a passage, how narrow it is. So look at your state as you crawl upon it and ascend to it while you are burdened in the back with your sins (Awzar), turning right and left.
19:85.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

19:85.arabic: وقوله تعالى: ﴿ يوم نحشر المتقين إلى الرحمن وفدا ﴾ {} الآيتين وقوله تعالى: وإن منكم إلا واردها ﴾ {} الآية، وقوله: ﴿ اعملوا ما شئتم ﴾ {} الآية، وقوله: ﴿ من كان يريد حرث الآخرة نزد له في حرثه ﴾ {} الآية، قوله: ﴿ فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره ﴾ {} الآيتين وقوله تعالى: ﴿ وقدمنا إلى ما عملوا من عمل ﴾ {} الآية، وكذلك قوله تعالى: ﴿ والعصر إن الإنسان لفي خسر ﴾ {} إلى آخر السورة فهذه أربعة شروط للخلاص من الخسران وإنما كان خوف الأنبياء مع ما فاض عليهم من النعم لأنهم لم يأمنوا مكر الله تعالى ﴿ فلا يأمن مكر ال
19:85.english: And His saying, the Exalted: 'On the Day when We will gather the God-fearing (Al-Muttaqeen) to the Most Merciful (Ar-Rahman) as a delegation' (Quran 19:85) - these two verses - and His saying, the Exalted: 'And there is none of you except he will come to it' (Quran 19:71) - the verse - and His saying: 'Do whatever you will' (Quran 41:40) - the verse - and His saying: 'Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his harvest' (Quran 42:20) - the verse - His saying: 'So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it' (Quran 99:7) - these two verses - and His saying, the Exalted: 'And We will present what they have done of deeds' (Quran 25:23) - the verse - and likewise His saying, the Exalted: 'By time, indeed, mankind is in loss' (Quran 103:1-2) - to the end of the Surah. These are four conditions for salvation from loss. And the fear of the Prophets, despite the abundant blessings that overflowed upon them, was because they did not feel secure from the plan (Makra) of Allah, the Exalted: 'So none feels secure from the plan (Makra) of Allah except the people who are the losers' (Quran 7:99). Until it was narrated that the Prophet and Gabriel, peace be upon them both, wept out of fear of Allah, the Exalted, so Allah revealed to them: 'Why do you weep when I have given you security?' They said: 'And who feels secure from Your plan (Makra)?' [90] And it was as if they, since they knew that Allah is the Knower of the unseen and that they have no standing upon the ultimate matters, did not feel secure that His saying 'I have given you security' might be a trial and a test for them and a plan (Makra) against them, so that if their fear subsided, it would become apparent that they had felt secure from the plan (Makra) and had not fulfilled their saying. Just as when Abraham, peace be upon him, was placed in the catapult, he said: 'Sufficient for me is Allah (Hasbunallahu)', and this was among the great supplications, so he was tested and confronted by Gabriel in the air until he said: 'Do you have any need?' He replied: 'As for from you, no.' That was a fulfillment of the reality of his saying 'Sufficient for me is Allah'. So Allah, the Exalted, informed about him, saying: 'And Abraham who fulfilled' - meaning, by the implication of his saying 'Sufficient for me is Allah'. And with the like of this, He informed about Moses, peace be upon him, when he said: 'Indeed, we fear that he will hasten [punishment] against us or that he will transgress.' He said: 'Fear not. Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see' (Quran 20:45-46). And despite this, when the magicians threw their magic, Moses felt fear within himself, for he did not feel secure from the plan (Makra) of Allah, and the matter became confused for him until reassurance was renewed for him and it was said to him: 'Fear not. Indeed, you are the highest' (Quran 20:68). And when the strength of the Muslims weakened on the day of Badr, he, peace be upon him, said: 'O Allah, if You destroy this group, there will remain no one on the face of the earth who worships You [91].' So Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: 'Leave off your pleading with your Lord, for He is faithful to you with what He promised you.' So the station of Al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, was the station of trust in the promise of Allah, and the station of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, was the station of fear from the plan (Makra) of Allah, and it is more complete because it does not issue except from perfection of knowledge of the secrets of Allah, the Exalted, and the hidden aspects of His actions and the meanings of His attributes, some of which are expressed as plan (Makra). And no one from mankind has the ability to stand upon the reality (Kunh) of the attributes of Allah, the Exalted. And whoever knows the reality (Haqiqah) of knowledge, the deficiency of his knowledge from encompassing the reality (Kunh) of matters, his fear inevitably becomes great. And for that reason, the Messiah, peace be upon him, said when it was said to him: 'Did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as deities besides Allah"?' He said: 'Exalted are You! It was not for me to say that to which I have no right. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Yourself' (Quran 5:116). And he said: 'If You should punish them - indeed they are Your servants; but if You forgive them - indeed it is You who is the Exalted in Might, the Wise' (Quran 5:118) - the verse. He delegated the matter to the Will (Mashiyyah) and removed himself entirely from between, knowing that he has nothing of the matter and that matters are connected to the Will (Mashiyyah) with a connection that goes beyond the limits of the intelligible and the customary, so it is not possible to judge them by analogy, conjecture, or calculation, let alone by verification and certainty. And this is what cut the hearts (Qulub) of the knowers (Al-Arifeen), for the greatest calamity is the connection of your matter to the Will (Mashiyyah) of One who does not care about you; if He destroys you, He has destroyed your like from those who cannot be enumerated, and He has not ceased in the world to punish them with types of pains and illnesses, and He sickens from that their hearts (Qulub) with disbelief and hypocrisy, then He makes the punishment eternal upon them forever. Then He informs about Himself and says: 'And if We had willed, We could have given every soul its guidance, but the word from Me will come into effect: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men all together"' (Quran 32:13). And He, the Exalted, said: 'And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: "I will surely fill Hell"' (Quran 11:119) - the verse. So how can one not fear what has been decreed from the word in pre-eternity and not hope to recover it? And if the matter were otherwise, hopes would extend to a stratagem therein, but there is only submission therein and inferring the hidden precedent (As-Sabiqah) from the apparent causes evident upon the heart (Al-Qalb) and the limbs. So for whom the causes of evil are facilitated and he is prevented from the causes of good and his attachment to the world is firmly established, it is as if the secret of the precedent (As-Sabiqah) that preceded for him with wretchedness has been unveiled to him in reality, for 'every [person] is facilitated for what he was created' (Hadith). And if all good deeds are facilitated and the heart (Al-Qalb) is completely cut off from the world and with its outward and inward turned towards Allah, this would necessitate a lessening of fear if constancy upon that were assured. But the danger of the ending (Al-Khatimah) and the difficulty of steadfastness increase the flames of fear in ignition and do not allow them to be extinguished. And how can one feel secure from a change of state when the heart (Qalb) of the believer is between two fingers of the fingers of the Most Merciful, and the heart (Al-Qalb) is more fluctuating than the pot in its boiling? And the Turner of the hearts (Muqallib Al-Qulub), Glory be to Him, has said: 'Indeed, the punishment of their Lord is not that from which one is safe' (Quran 70:28). So the most ignorant of people is he who feels secure from Him while He calls out with warning against security. And if Allah were gentle with His knower (Al-Arifeen) servants by reviving their hearts (Qulub) with the spirit (Ruh) of hope, their hearts (Qulub) would burn from the fire of fear. So the causes of hope are a mercy for the chosen ones of Allah, and the causes of heedlessness are a mercy upon the common people of creation from one aspect, for if the covering were unveiled, the souls (An-Nufus) would expire and the hearts (Al-Qulub) would be severed from fear of the Turner of the hearts (Muqallib Al-Qulub). Some of the knowers (Al-Arifeen) said: 'If there were between me and one whom I knew with Oneness (At-Tawhid) a barrier for fifty years and he died, I would not affirm for him Oneness (At-Tawhid) because I do not know what appeared to him of fluctuation.' And some of them said: 'If the testimony were at the door of the house and death upon Islam were at the door of the room, I would choose death upon Islam because I do not know what occurs to my heart (Qalbi) between the door of the room and the door of the house.' And Abu Ad-Darda' would swear by Allah that no one feels secure about his faith that it will not be stripped from him before death except that it is stripped. And Sahl would say: 'The fear of the truthful ones (As-Siddiqeen) from a bad ending (Sou' Al-Khatimah) is at every thought (Khatrah) and at every movement, and they are those whom Allah, the Exalted, described when He said: 'And their hearts (Qulubuhum) are fearful' (Quran 23:60).
19:85.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Fear and Hope'

19:85.arabic: وكان المسور بن مخرمة لا يقوى أن يسمع شيئا من القرآن لشدة خوفه ولقد كان يقرأ عنده الحرف والآية فيصيح الصحية فما يعقل أياما حتى أتي عليه رجل من خثعم فقرأ عليه ﴿ يوم نحشر المتقين إلى الرحمن وفدا ونسوق المجرمين إلى جهنم وردا ﴾{} فقال: أنا من المجرمين ولست من المتقين أعد على القول أيها القارئ فأعادها عليه فشهق شهقة فلحق بالآخرة.
19:85.english: And al-Miswar ibn Makhramah could not bear to hear anything from the Quran due to the intensity of his fear (khawf), and indeed when a letter or verse was recited near him, he would scream a scream and not regain consciousness for days, until a man from Khath'am came to him and recited to him: 'On the Day when We will gather the God-fearing (al-Muttaqin) to the Most Merciful (al-Rahman) as a delegation, and drive the criminals to Hell as a thirsty herd.' He said: 'I am from the criminals and not from the God-fearing (al-Muttaqin). Repeat the saying, O reciter.' So he repeated it to him, and he gasped a gasp, then he joined the Hereafter (al-Akhirah).
19:85.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Fear and Hope'

19:93.arabic: فلو لم يكن بين يدي الموتي إلا هول تلك النفخة لكان ذلك جديرا بأن يتقى فإنها نفخة وصيحة يصعق بها من فى السموات والأرض يعنى يموتون بها إلا من شاء الله وهو بعض الملائكة ولذلك قال رسول الله ﭬ: (كيف أنعم وصاحب الصور قد التقم القرن وحنى الجبهة وأصغى بالأذن متى يؤمر فينفخ[144]) قال مقاتل: الصور هو القرن وذلك أن إسرافيل عليه السلام واضع فاه على القرن كهيئة البوق ودائرة رأس القرن كعرض السموات والأرض وهو شاخص بصره نحو العرش ينتظر متى يؤمر فينفخ النفخة الأولى فإذا نفخ صعق من فى السموات والأرض أى مات كل حيوا
19:93.english: If there were nothing before the dead except the terror of that blowing, it would be worthy of being feared, for it is a blowing and a cry by which those in the heavens and the earth are struck unconscious, meaning they die by it, except whom Allah wills, and that is some of the angels. Therefore, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'How can I enjoy comfort when the possessor of the Trumpet (Sahib al-Sur) has taken the horn in his mouth, lowered his forehead, and listened with his ear, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow?' [144] Muqatil said: The Trumpet (al-Sur) is the horn, and that is because Israfil (upon him be peace) has placed his mouth on the horn like the form of a trumpet, and the circumference of the head of the horn is like the expanse of the heavens and the earth, and he is staring with his gaze toward the Throne, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow the first blowing. When he blows, those in the heavens and the earth are struck unconscious, meaning every living creature dies from the intensity of the terror, except whom Allah wills, and that is Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil, and the Angel of Death (Malak al-Mawt). Then the Angel of Death is commanded to take the soul (Ruh) of Jibril, then the soul (Ruh) of Mika'il, then the soul (Ruh) of Israfil, then the Angel of Death is commanded and he dies. Then the creation remains after the first blowing in the Intermediate State (al-Barzakh) for forty years. Then Allah, the Exalted, revives Israfil and commands him to blow the second blowing, and that is His saying, the Exalted: 'Then it will be blown into it another time, and behold, they are standing, looking on' [Quran 39:68], on their feet, looking at the Resurrection. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'When I was sent, I was sent to the possessor of the Trumpet (Sahib al-Sur), and he inclined it to his mouth, and advanced one foot and delayed another, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow. Indeed, fear the blowing!' [145] So reflect on the creation and their humiliation, their brokenness, and their submission at the time of resurrection, out of fear of this unconsciousness and waiting for it.
19:93.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

19:98.arabic: وينظر إلى فرعون وهامان وقارون وإلى ملوك الأرض وما جرى لهم كيف أحسن الله إليهم ابتداء ثم دمرهم تدميرا! فقال تعالى "هل تحس منهم من أحد" الآية. وقد حذر الله تعالى من مكره واستدراجه فقال "فلا يأمن مكر الله إلا القوم الخاسرون" وقال تعالى "ومكروا مكراً ومكرنا مكراً وهم لا يشعرون" وقال عز وجل "ومكروا ومكر الله والله خير الماكرين" وقال تعالى "إنهم يكيدون كيداً وأكيد كيداً فمهل الكافرين أمهلهم رويداً" فكما لا يجوز للعبد المهمل أن يستدل بإهمال السيد إياه وتمكينه من النعم على حب السيد، بل ينبغي أن يحذر أن
19:98.english: And look at Pharaoh, Haman, Korah, and the kings of the earth and what happened to them - how Allah bestowed favor upon them initially, then destroyed them utterly! So Allah the Exalted said: "Do you perceive from them anyone?" The verse. And Allah the Exalted has warned of His deception (makr) and gradual entrapment (istidrāj), saying: "So none feels secure from the deception (makr) of Allah except the people who are losers," and Allah the Exalted said: "And they planned a plan, and We planned a plan, while they perceived not," and He the Mighty and Majestic said: "And they planned, and Allah planned, and Allah is the best of planners," and Allah the Exalted said: "Indeed, they are planning a plan, and I am planning a plan. So allow time for the disbelievers. Leave them awhile." So just as it is not permissible for the neglected servant to infer from the master's neglect of him and enabling him with blessings that the master loves him, rather he should be cautious that this might be deception (makr) and plotting from him, even though the master did not warn him of his own deception (makr), then it is more incumbent regarding Allah the Exalted with His warning of His gradual entrapment (istidrāj). Therefore, whoever feels secure from the deception (makr) of Allah is deluded (maghṭūr), and the origin of this delusion (ghurūr) is that he inferred from worldly blessings that he is honorable with that Bestower, and it is possible that this is evidence of degradation, but that possibility does not agree with desire (hawā), so Satan, by means of desire (hawā), inclines the Heart (Qalb) toward what accompanies it, which is believing in its indication of honor, and this is the limit of delusion (ghurūr).
19:98.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'
