19:98.arabic: فاحسبى أن كل من على وجه الأرض سجد لك وأطاعك أفما تعرفين أنه بعد خمسين سنة لا تبقين انت ولا أحد ممن على وجه الأرض ممن عبدك وسجد لك وسيأتى زمان لا يبقى ذكرك ولا ذكر من ذكرك كما أتى على الملوك الذين كانوا من قبلك فهل تحس منهم من أحد أو تسمع لهم ركزا فكيف تبيعين يا نفس ما يبقى أبد الآباد بما لا يبقى أكثر من خمسين سنة
19:98.english: So consider that everyone on the face of the earth prostrated to you and obeyed you. Do you not know that after fifty years, you will not remain, nor will any of those on the face of the earth who worshipped you and prostrated to you remain? And a time will come when your remembrance (Dhikr) and the remembrance (Dhikr) of those who remember you will not remain, just as it came upon the kings who were before you. So do you perceive from them anyone or hear from them a whisper? So how do you sell, O Soul (Nafs), what remains for eternity of eternities for what does not remain more than fifty years?
19:98.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

19:98.arabic: فانظر هل وجدوا من الموت حصنا وعزّا، واتخذوا من دونه حجابا وحرزا، وانظر ﴿ هل تحس منهم من أحد أو تسمع لهم ركزا ﴾ فسبحان من انفرد بالقهر والاستيلاء، واستأثر باستحقاق البقاء، وأذل أصناف الخلق بما كتب عليهم من الفناء، ثم جعل الموت مخلصا للأتقياء وموعدا فى حقهم للقاء وجعل القبر سجنا للأشقياء وحبسا ضيقا عليهم إلى يوم الفصل والقضاء
19:98.english: So look: did they find from death a fortress and might, and did they take from besides it a barrier and protection, and look: 'Do you perceive from them anyone or hear for them a whisper?' So glory be to the One who is unique in overpowering and domination, and who exclusively possesses the entitlement to permanence, and who humbled the kinds of creation with what He decreed upon them of annihilation, then made death a deliverance for the pious and an appointment in their right for the meeting, and made the grave a prison for the wretched and a tight confinement upon them until the day of separation and judgment.
19:98.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

20:14.arabic: رواه عن النبي ﭬ أنه قال: (إن الله تعالى يمجد نفسه كل يوم ويقول إني أنا الله رب العالمين إني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا الحي القيوم إني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا العلي العظيم إني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا لم ألد ولم أولد إني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا العفو الغفور إني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا مبدىء كل شيء وإلي يعود العزيز الحكيم الرحمن الرحيم مالك يوم الدين خالق الخير والشر خالق الجنة والنار الواحد الأحد الفرد الصمد الذي لم يتخذ صاحبة ولا ولدا الفرد الوتر عالم الغيب والشهادة الملك القدوس السلام المؤمن المهي
20:14.english: It was narrated from the Prophet (peace be upon him) that he said: (Indeed, Allah the Exalted glorifies Himself every day and says: Indeed, I am Allah, Lord of the worlds; indeed, I am Allah, there is no god except Me, the Living, the Sustainer; indeed, I am Allah, there is no god except Me, the Most High, the Most Great; indeed, I am Allah, there is no god except Me, I have not begotten nor was I begotten; indeed, I am Allah, there is no god except Me, the Pardoner, the Forgiving; indeed, I am Allah, there is no god except Me, the Originator of everything and to Me is the return, the Almighty, the Wise, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, Master of the Day of Judgment, Creator of good and evil, Creator of Paradise and Hell, the One, the Unique, the Eternal, the Absolute, who has not taken a consort nor a son, the Single, the Odd, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Sovereign, the Holy, the Peace, the Faithful, the Guardian, the Almighty, the Compeller, the Majestic, the Creator, the Evolver, the Fashioner, the Most Great, the Most Exalted, the All-Powerful, the Subduer, the Forbearing, the Generous, Possessor of praise and glory, Knower of the secret and what is more hidden, the Able, the Provider, above the creation and the creatures[135]). And He mentioned before every word 'Indeed, I am Allah, there is no god except Me' as we have presented it in the beginning. So whoever supplicates with these names, let him say: Indeed, You are Allah, there is no god except You, such and such. So whoever supplicates with them is written among the prostrating, the humble ones who will be neighbors to Muhammad, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and the prophets (may Allah's prayers be upon them) in the abode of majesty, and for him is the reward of the worshippers in the heavens and the earths. And may Allah send prayers upon Muhammad and upon every chosen servant.
20:14.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

20:14.arabic: إني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا
20:14.english: Indeed I am Allah, there is no god except Me
20:14.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

20:14.arabic: [135] حديث علي إن الله تعالى يمجد نفسه كل يوم فيقول إني أنا الله رب العالمين إني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا الحي القيوم الحديث بطوله لم أجد له أصلا.
20:14.english: Hadith: 'Ali reported that Allah the Exalted glorifies Himself every day, saying: "Indeed I am Allah, Lord of the worlds. Indeed I am Allah, there is no god but I, the Living, the Self-Subsisting." The hadith in its full length - I did not find any basis for it.
20:14.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication

20:14.arabic: لا إله إلا الله والله أكبر
20:14.english: There is no god but Allah and Allah is greater
20:14.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

20:16.arabic: وأما الفاسق المصر على الفسق فلا فائدة في صحبته لأن من يخاف الله لا يصر على كبيرة ومن لا يخاف الله لا تؤمن غائلته ولا يوثق بصداقته بل يتغير بتغير الأغراض وقال تعالى ولا تطع من أغفلنا قلبه عن ذكرنا واتبع هواه وقال تعالى فلا يصدنك عنها من لا يؤمن بها واتبع هواه وقال تعالى فأعرض عمن تولى عن ذكرنا ولم يرد إلا الحياة الدنيا و قال واتبع سبيل من أناب إلى وفي مفهوم ذلك زجر عن الفاسق
20:16.english: As for the sinner (Fasiq) who persists in sinfulness, there is no benefit in his companionship because whoever fears Allah does not persist in major sin, and whoever does not fear Allah, his harm cannot be secured against nor can his friendship be trusted; rather, he changes with changing objectives. And Allah the Exalted said: 'And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our Remembrance (Dhikr) and who follows his desire (Hawa).' And Allah the Exalted said: 'So let not one who does not believe in it and follows his desire (Hawa) turn you away from it, lest you perish.' And Allah the Exalted said: 'And turn away from him who turns away from Our Remembrance (Dhikr) and desires not except the worldly life.' And He said: 'And follow the way of him who turns to Me.' And in the understanding of that is a prohibition from the sinner (Fasiq).
20:16.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

20:24.arabic: وتارة قد يكون له غرض صحيح فيطلب له دليلا من القرآن ويستدل عليه مما يعلم أنه ما أريد به كمن يدعو إلى الاستغفار بالأسحار فيستدل بقوله ﭬ: (تسحروا فإن في السحور بركة[56]) ويزعم أن المراد به التسحر بالذكر وهو يعلم أن المراد به الأكل وكالذي يدعو إلى مجاهدة القلب القاسي فيقول قال الله عز وجل ﴿ إذهب إلى فرعون إنه طغى ﴾  {} ويشير إلى قلبه ويومئ إلى أنه المراد بفرعون وهذا الجنس قد يستعمله بعض الوعاظ في المقاصد الصحيحة تحسينا للكلام وترغيبا للمستمع وهو ممنوع وقد تستعمله الباطنية في المقاصد الفاسدة لتغرير ا
20:24.english: And sometimes one may have a correct purpose and seeks evidence for it from the Quran, and he deduces from what he knows is not intended by it, like one who calls to seeking forgiveness (Istighfar) at the pre-dawn hours (Al-Ashar) and deduces from His saying: 'Take the pre-dawn meal (Tasahharu) for indeed in the pre-dawn meal (Al-Suhur) there is blessing' and claims that what is intended by it is taking the pre-dawn meal with remembrance (Dhikr), while he knows that what is intended by it is eating. And like one who calls to struggling against (Mujahada) the hard heart (Qalb) and says: 'Allah the Exalted said: "Go to Pharaoh, indeed he has transgressed"' and he points to his heart and indicates that it is what is intended by Pharaoh. And this type may be used by some preachers for correct purposes, beautifying the speech and encouraging the listener, and it is prohibited. And it may be used by the Batiniyya (esotericists) for corrupt purposes to deceive people and invite them to their false doctrine, so they interpret the Quran according to their opinion and doctrine regarding matters they know with certainty are not intended by it. So these arts are one aspect of the prohibition of interpretation by opinion (Tafsir bi al-Ra'y), and what is meant by opinion is the corrupt opinion that conforms to desire (Hawa) without correct independent reasoning (Ijtihad). And opinion encompasses both correct and corrupt, and what conforms to desire may be specifically named as opinion.
20:24.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

20:24.arabic: ومثال تأويل أهل الطامات قول بعضهم في تأويل قوله تعالى: (اذهب إلى فرعون إنه طغى( (طه: 24 و النازعات: 17) أنه إشارة إلى قلبه وقال هو المراد بفرعون وهو الطاغي على كل إنسان
20:24.english: And an example of the interpretation of the people of excesses is the statement of some of them in interpreting His saying, the Exalted: 'Go to Pharaoh, indeed he has transgressed' (Taha: 24 and Al-Nazi'at: 17) that it is an allusion to his heart (Qalb) and he said: it is intended by Pharaoh, and he is the transgressor over every human being.
20:24.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

20:25.arabic: وتقول عند التصدق ﴿ ربنا تقبل منا إنك أنت السميع العليم ﴾ {} وتقول عند الخسران ﴿ عسى ربنا أن يبدلنا خيرا منها إنا إلى ربنا راغبون ﴾ {} وتقول عند ابتداء الأمور ﴿ ربنا آتنا من لدنك رحمة وهيىء لنا من أمرنا رشدا ﴾ {} رب اشرح لي صدري ويسر لي أمري ﴾ {} وتقول عند النظر إلى السماء ﴿ ربنا ما خلقت هذا باطلا سبحانك فقنا عذاب النار ﴾ {} ﴿ تبارك الذي جعل في السماء بروجا وجعل فيها سراجا وقمرا منيرا ﴾ {}
20:25.english: And say when giving charity: 'Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.' And say when experiencing loss: 'Perhaps our Lord will give us better than it. Indeed, we are to our Lord desirous.' And say at the beginning of matters: 'Our Lord, grant us from Yourself mercy and prepare for us from our affair right guidance.' 'My Lord, expand for me my chest and ease for me my affair.' And say when looking at the sky: 'Our Lord, You did not create this in vain. Glory be to You, so protect us from the punishment of the Fire.' 'Blessed is He who has placed in the sky constellations and has placed therein a lamp and a luminous moon.'
20:25.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

20:27.arabic: فخر صعقاً يضطرب في غشيته، فلما أفاق قال: سبحانك ما أعظم شأنك تبت إليك وتوكلت عليك وآمنت بأنك الملك الجبار الواحد القهار، فلا أخاف غيرك ولا أرجو سواك ولا أعوذ إلا بعفوك من عقابك وبرضاك من سخطك، وما لي إلا أن أسألك وأتضرع إليك وأبتهل بين يديك، فأقول: اشرح لي صدري لأعرفك واحلل عقدة من لساني لأثني عليك، فنودي من وراء الحجاب: إياك أن تطمع في الثناء وتزيد على سيد الأنبياء، بل ارجع إليه فما آتاك فخذه وما نهاك عنه فانته عنه، وما قاله لك فقله؛ فإنه ما زاد في هذه الحضرة على أن قال: " سبحانك لا أحصي ثناء ع
20:27.english: He fell unconscious, trembling in his swoon. When he regained consciousness, he said: 'Glory be to You, how great is Your affair! I repent to You, rely upon You, and believe that You are the King, the Compeller, the One, the Subduer. So I fear none but You, hope for none but You, and seek refuge only in Your pardon from Your punishment and in Your pleasure from Your wrath. I have nothing except to ask You, supplicate to You, and implore before You. So I say: "Expand for me my chest (SADR) to know You, and untie a knot from my tongue (LISAN) to praise You." Then he was called from behind the veil: "Beware of aspiring to praise and exceeding the Master of the Prophets. Rather, return to him: what he gives you, take it; what he forbids you from, abstain from it; and what he says to you, say it. For he did not increase in this Presence (HADRA) beyond saying: 'Glory be to You, I cannot enumerate praise upon You; You are as You have praised Yourself.'" He said: 'My God, if the tongue (LISAN) has no boldness to praise You, then does the heart (QALB) have aspiration in knowing You?' Then he was called: 'Beware of overstepping the necks of the Truthful Ones (SIDDIQIN). Return to the Greatest Truthful One (SIDDIQ AL-AKBAR) and follow him. For the companions of the Master of the Prophets are like stars: by whichever you follow, you are guided. Have you not heard him say: "Inability to grasp perception (IDRAK) is perception (IDRAK)." So suffice you a portion from Our Presence (HADRA) that you know you are deprived from Our Presence (HADRA), unable to observe Our beauty (JAMAL) and majesty (JALAL).' At that, the traveler (SALIK) returned and apologized for his questions and reproaches.
20:27.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

20:44.arabic: وَدَلَّ عَلَى وُجُوبِ الرِّفْقِ مَا اسْتَدَلَّ بِهِ الْمَأْمُونُ إِذَا وَعَظَهُ وَاعِظٌ وَعَنَّفَ لَهُ فِي الْقَوْلِ فَقَالَ: يَا رَجُلُ ارْفُقْ فَقَدْ بَعَثَ اللَّهُ مِنْ هُوَ خَيْرٌ مِنْكَ إِلَى مَنْ هُوَ شَرٌّ مِنِّي وَأَمَرَهُ بِالرِّفْقِ فَقَالَ تَعَالَى: فَقُولَا لَهُ قَوْلًا لَيِّنًا لَعَلَّهُ يَتَذَكَّرُ أَوْ يَخْشَىٰ فَلْيَكُنِ اقْتِدَاءُ الْمُحْتَسِبِ فِي الرِّفْقِ بِالْأَنْبِيَاءِ صَلَوَاتُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمْ
20:44.english: And the obligation of gentleness (Rifq) is indicated by what Al-Ma'mun cited as evidence when a preacher admonished him and was harsh in speech to him, so he said: 'O man, be gentle, for Allah has sent one who is better than you to one who is worse than me and commanded him to gentleness, so the Exalted said: "So speak to him a gentle (layyinan) word, perhaps he may remember (yatadhakkar) or fear (yakhsha)."' So let the one who enjoins good and forbids evil (al-Muhtasib) follow the Prophets, prayers of Allah be upon them, in gentleness.
20:44.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

20:45.arabic: ومع هذا لما ألقى السحرة سحرهم أوجس موسى في نفسه خيفة إذا لم يأمن مكر الله والتبس الأمر عليه حتى جدد عليه الأمن وقيل له ﴿ لا تخف إنك أنت الأعلى ﴾ {} ولما ضعفت شوكة المسلمين يوم بدر قال ﭬ: (اللهم إن تهلك هذه العصابة لم يبق على وجه الأرض أحد يعبدك[91]) فقال أبو بكر رضي الله تعالى عنه دع عنك مناشدتك ربك فإنه واف لك بما وعدك فكان مقام الصديق رضي الله عنه مقام الثقة بوعد الله، وكان مقام رسول الله ﭬ مقام الخوف من مكر الله وهو أتم لأنه لا يصدر إلا عن كمال المعرفة بأسرار الله تعالى وخفايا أفعاله ومعاني ص
20:45.english: And with this, when the magicians threw their magic, Moses felt fear in his Soul (Nafs) since he did not feel secure from the plotting (Makar) of Allah, and the matter became confused for him until reassurance was renewed for him and it was said to him: 'Do not fear, indeed you are the highest.' And when the strength of the Muslims weakened on the day of Badr, he (the Prophet) said: 'O Allah, if You destroy this group, there will remain no one on the face of the earth who worships You.' So Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: 'Leave off your supplication to your Lord, for He is faithful to you with what He promised you.' So the station (Maqam) of the Truthful One (Al-Siddiq), may Allah be pleased with him, was the station of trust in the promise of Allah, and the station of the Messenger of Allah was the station of fear from the plotting (Makar) of Allah, and it is more complete because it does not issue except from the perfection of knowledge (Ma'rifah) of the secrets (Asrar) of Allah the Exalted and the hidden aspects (Khafa'ya) of His actions and the meanings (Ma'ani) of His attributes (Sifat) which some of what issues from them is expressed as plotting (Makar), and no one from humankind has the ability to stand upon the reality (Kunh) of the attributes (Sifat) of Allah the Exalted. And whoever knows the reality (Haqiqah) of knowledge (Ma'rifah) [knows] the deficiency of his knowledge (Ma'rifah) from encompassing the reality (Kunh) of matters, his fear inevitably increases. And for that reason, Jesus said when it was said to him: 'Did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as gods besides Allah"? He said, "Glory be to You! It is not for me to say what I have no right to. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is within my Soul (Nafs), and I do not know what is within Your Soul (Nafs)."' And he said: 'If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants, and if You forgive them...' the verse. He entrusted the matter to the will (Mashiyyah) and removed himself entirely.
20:45.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

20:45.arabic: فكذلك الانبساط والإدلال يحتمل من بعض العباد دون بعض. فمن انبساط الأنس قول موسى عليه السلام: "إن هي إلا فتنتك تضل بها من تشاء وتهدي من تشاء" وقوله في التعليل والاعتذار لما قيل له: "اذهب إلى فرعون"، فقال: "ولهم على ذنب" وقوله: "إني أخاف أن يكذبون ويضيق صدري ولا ينطلق لساني"، وقوله: "إننا نخاف أن يفرط علينا أو أن يطغى" وهذا من غير موسى عليه السلام من سوء الأدب لأن الذي أقيم مقام الأنس يلاطف ويحتمل، ولم يحتمل ليونس عليه السلام ما دون هذا لما أقيم مقام القبض والهيبة، فعوقب بالسجن في بطن الحوت - في ظل
20:45.english: Similarly, expansion (Inbisat) and familiarity (Idlal) are permissible for some worshippers but not others. From the expansion of intimacy (Unsiyyah) is the saying of Moses, peace be upon him: "It is only Your trial by which You lead astray whom You will and guide whom You will" and his saying in explanation and excuse when he was told: "Go to Pharaoh," so he said: "And they have upon me a sin" and his saying: "Indeed, I fear that they will deny me and my breast will tighten and my tongue will not be fluent" and his saying: "Indeed, we fear that he will exceed against us or that he will transgress." And this from other than Moses, peace be upon him, would be bad manners (Su' al-Adab) because the one who is established in the station of intimacy (Maqam al-Uns) is treated gently and is tolerated, and it was not tolerated for Jonah, peace be upon him, what is less than this because he was established in the station of contraction (Qabd) and awe (Haybah), so he was punished with imprisonment in the belly of the whale - in three darknesses - and was called upon until the Day of Resurrection: "Had it not been that a favor from his Lord reached him, he would have been thrown onto the naked shore while he was blameworthy."
20:45.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

20:50.arabic: فأما الهداية فلا سبيل لأحد إلى طلب السعادة إلا بها لأن داعية الإنسان قد تكون مائلة إلى ما فيه صلاح آخرته ولكن إذا لم يعلم ما فيه صلاح آخرته حتى يظن الفساد صلاحا فمن أين ينفعه مجرد الإرادة فلا فائدة في الإرادة والقدرة والأسباب إلا بعد الهداية ولذلك قال تعالى: ﴿ ربنا الذى أعطى كل شىء خلقه ثم هدى ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ ولو لا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته ما زكى منكم أحد أبدا ولكن الله يزكى من يشاء ﴾ {} وقال ﭬ: (ما من أحد يدخل الجنة إلا برحمة الله تعالى أى بهدايته فقيل ولا أنت يا رسول الله؟ قال ولا أنا[77]). و
20:50.english: As for guidance (Hidayah), there is no way for anyone to seek happiness except through it, because the inclination (Dā'iyah) of a human may be inclined toward what contains rectification (Salāh) of his Hereafter, but if he does not know what contains rectification of his Hereafter until he considers corruption (Fasād) as rectification, then from where will mere will (Irādah) benefit him? So there is no benefit in will, capability (Qudrah), and means (Asbāb) except after guidance (Hidayah). And therefore, Allah the Exalted said: 'Our Lord is He Who gave to each thing its creation (Khalq), then guided (Hidā)' (20:50). And He said: 'And were it not for the favor (Fadl) of Allah upon you and His mercy (Rahmah), none of you would ever have been purified (Zakkā), but Allah purifies whom He wills' (24:21). And He said (peace be upon him): 'No one enters Paradise except by the mercy (Rahmah) of Allah the Exalted, meaning by His guidance (Hidāyah).' It was said: 'Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Not even me.' And guidance (Hidāyah) has three stations (Manāzil): The first is knowledge of the path of good and evil, referred to by His saying: 'And We have guided him to the two ways (Najdayn)' (90:10). And Allah the Exalted has bestowed this upon all His servants, some of it through intellect ('Aql) and some of it upon the tongue of the messengers (Rusul). And therefore, He said: 'And as for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness ('Amā) over guidance (Hudā)' (41:17). So the means (Asbāb) of guidance (Hudā) are the Book (Kitāb), the messengers (Rusul), and the insights (Basā'ir) of intellects ('Uqūl), and they are made available, and nothing prevents from them except envy (Hasad), arrogance (Kibr), love of the worldly life (Hubb al-Dunyā), and the means (Asbāb) that blind (Tu'mī) the hearts (Qulūb) even though they do not blind the eyesights (Absār). He said: 'For indeed, it is not the eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts (Qulūb) which are within the breasts (Sudūr)' (22:46). And among the blinding things (Ma'miyyāt) are familiarity (Ilf) and habit ('Ādah) and the love of adhering to them, and from it is the expression by His saying: 'Indeed, we found our fathers upon a community (Ummah)' (43:22) the verse. And from arrogance (Kibr) and envy (Hasad) is the expression by His saying: 'And they said, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man from one of the two cities?"' (43:31) and His saying: 'Shall we follow one human being (Bashar) among us?' (54:24). So these blinding things (Ma'miyyāt) are what prevented guidance-seeking (Ihtidā') and guidance (Hidāyah).
20:50.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

20:55.arabic: فإذا صعد بروحه قيل أي رب عبدك فلان فيقول ارجعوه فأروه ما أعددت له من الكرامة فإني وعدته ﴿ منها خلقناكم وفيها نعيدكم ومنها نخرجكم تارة أخرى ﴾ {}الآية، وإنه ليسمع خفق نعالهم إذا ولوا مدبرين حتى يقال يا هذا من ربك وما دينك وما نبيك؟ فيقول ربي الله وديني الإسلام ونبي محمد ﭬ قال فينتهرأنه انتهارا شديدا وهي آخر فرصة تعرض على الميت فإذا قال ذلك نادى مناد أن قد صدقت وهي معنى قوله تعالى: ﴿ يثبت الله الذين آمنوا بالقول الثابت ﴾ {}الآية
20:55.english: When his soul (Ruh) ascends, it is said: 'O Lord, Your servant so-and-so.' He says: 'Return him, and show him what I have prepared for him of honor, for I promised him: "From it (the earth) We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will bring you out another time" (Quran 20:55).' And indeed he hears the shuffling of their sandals when they turn away departing, until it is said: 'O you, who is your Lord, and what is your religion, and who is your prophet?' He says: 'My Lord is Allah, my religion is Islam, and my prophet is Muhammad (peace be upon him).' It is said: Then he is rebuked with a severe rebuke, and it is the last opportunity presented to the deceased. If he says that, a caller calls out: 'You have spoken truthfully,' and it is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: "Allah keeps firm those who have believed with the firm word" (Quran 14:27).
20:55.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

20:55.arabic: فإذا صعد بروحه نبذ وقيل أي ربعبدك فلان لم تقبله سماء ولا ارض فيقول الله عز وجل ارجعوه فأروه ما أعدت له من الشر إني وعدته ﴿ منها خلقناكم وفيها نعيدكم ومنها نخرجكم تارة أخرى ﴾ {}الآية وأنه ليسمع خفق نعالهم إذا ولوا مدبرين
20:55.english: Then when his spirit ascends, it is cast away and it is said: 'O you, the servant of so-and-so, neither the sky nor the earth accepted you.' Then Allah, the Exalted and Majestic, says: 'Return him and show him what I have prepared for him of evil. Indeed, I promised him: "From it (the earth) We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will bring you out another time." (Quran 20:55) And indeed, he hears the flapping of their sandals when they turn away retreating.'
20:55.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

20:68.arabic: ومع هذا لما ألقى السحرة سحرهم أوجس موسى في نفسه خيفة إذا لم يأمن مكر الله والتبس الأمر عليه حتى جدد عليه الأمن وقيل له ﴿ لا تخف إنك أنت الأعلى ﴾ {} ولما ضعفت شوكة المسلمين يوم بدر قال ﭬ: (اللهم إن تهلك هذه العصابة لم يبق على وجه الأرض أحد يعبدك[91]) فقال أبو بكر رضي الله تعالى عنه دع عنك مناشدتك ربك فإنه واف لك بما وعدك فكان مقام الصديق رضي الله عنه مقام الثقة بوعد الله، وكان مقام رسول الله ﭬ مقام الخوف من مكر الله وهو أتم لأنه لا يصدر إلا عن كمال المعرفة بأسرار الله تعالى وخفايا أفعاله ومعاني ص
20:68.english: And with this, when the magicians threw their magic, Moses felt in his soul (Nafs) apprehension since he did not feel secure from the deception (Makar) of Allah and the matter became confused for him until reassurance was renewed for him and it was said to him: 'Do not fear, indeed you are the highest.' And when the strength of the Muslims weakened on the day of Badr, he (the Prophet) said: 'O Allah, if You destroy this group, there will remain on the face of the earth no one who worships You.' So Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'Leave off your supplication to your Lord, for He is faithful to you with what He promised you.' So the station (Maqam) of the Truthful One (Al-Siddiq) (may Allah be pleased with him) was the station of trust (Thiqa) in the promise of Allah, and the station of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was the station of fear (Khauf) from the deception (Makar) of Allah, and it is more complete because it does not issue except from perfection of knowledge (Ma'rifah) of the secrets (Asrar) of Allah the Exalted and the hidden aspects (Khafa'ya) of His actions and the meanings (Ma'ani) of His attributes (Sifat) which some of what issues from them is expressed as deception (Makar), and no one from humankind has the ability to stand upon the reality (Kunh) of the attributes (Sifat) of Allah the Exalted. And whoever knows the reality (Haqiqah) of knowledge (Ma'rifah) [knows] the deficiency of his knowledge (Ma'rifah) from encompassing the reality (Kunh) of matters, his fear (Khauf) necessarily becomes great. And for that reason, Jesus (peace be upon him) said when it was said to him: 'Did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as deities besides Allah?" He said, "Exalted are You! It is not for me to say that to which I have no right. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Yourself."'
20:68.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

20:72.arabic: وأما الذي شاهد الطريق وسلكه بنفسه فلا يخاف عليه شيء من ذلك بل لو كشف الغطاء لما ازداد يقيناً وإن كان يزداد وضوحاً، كما أن الذي يرى إنساناً في وقت الإسفار لا يزداد يقيناً عند طلوع الشمس بأنه إنسان ولكن يزداد وضوحاً في تفصيل خلقته، وما مثال المكاشفين والمعتقدين إلا كسحرة فرعون مع أصحاب السامري؛ فإن سحرة فرعون لما كانوا مطلعين على منتهى تأثير السحر لطول مشاهدتهم وتجربتهم رأوا من موسى عليه السلام ما جاوز حدود السحر وانكشف لهم حقيقة الأمر فلم يكترثوا بقول فرعون " لأقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف " بل "
20:72.english: As for the one who has witnessed the path and traversed it himself, nothing is to be feared for him; rather, even if the veil were lifted, he would not increase in certainty (Yaqin), though he would increase in clarity. Just as one who sees a human at dawn does not increase in certainty at sunrise that it is a human, but increases in clarity regarding the details of his form. The example of those who have spiritual unveiling (Mukashifin) and those who merely hold beliefs (Mu'taqidin) is none other than like the magicians of Pharaoh with the followers of the Samiri. For the magicians of Pharaoh, because they were aware of the ultimate effect of magic due to their long observation and experience, saw from Moses, peace be upon him, what exceeded the limits of magic, and the truth of the matter was unveiled to them. Thus, they did not heed Pharaoh's statement, 'I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides,' but rather, 'They said: "We will never prefer you over what has come to us of the clear proofs and the One who created us. So decree whatever you are to decree. You can only decree for this worldly life."' For explanation (Bayan) and unveiling (Kashf) prevent change. As for the followers of the Samiri, since their faith was from looking at the apparent serpent, when they looked at the calf of the Samiri and heard its lowing, they changed and heard his saying, 'This is your god and the god of Moses,' and they forgot that it does not respond to them with speech, nor does it possess for them harm or benefit. Thus, everyone who believes by looking at a serpent will inevitably disbelieve if he looks at a calf, because both are from the world of witnessing (Alam al-Shahadah) and difference and opposition in the world of witnessing is abundant. As for the world of the dominion (Alam al-Malakut), it is from God, the Exalted, therefore we do not find in it any difference or opposition at all.
20:72.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

20:82.arabic: فإن قلت: فأين مظنة الرجاء وموضعه المحمود؟ فاعلم أنه محمود في موضعين: أحدهما: في حق العاصي المنهمك إذا خطرت له التوبة فقال له الشيطان: وأنى تقبل توبتك فيقنطه من رحمة الله تعالى "فيجب عند هذا أن يقمع القنوط بالرجاء ويتذكر "إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعاً" وأن الله كريم يقبل التوبة عن عباده وأن التوبة طاعة تكفر الذنوب قال الله تعالى "قل يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعاً إنه هو الغفور الرحيم وأنيبوا إلى ربكم" أمرهم بالإنابة وقال تعالى "وإني لغفار لمن تاب و
20:82.english: If you say: So where is the place of hope (Rajā') and its praiseworthy location? Know that it is praiseworthy in two places: The first: Regarding the immersed sinner when repentance occurs to him, and Satan says to him: How will your repentance be accepted? So he despairs of the mercy of Allah the Exalted. "At this point, he must suppress despair with hope and remember 'Indeed, Allah forgives all sins' and that Allah is generous in accepting repentance from His servants, and that repentance is an obedience that expiates sins. Allah the Exalted said: 'Say, O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful. And turn in repentance to your Lord' - He commanded them to turn in repentance (Inābah). And He said: 'And indeed, I am Forgiving (Ghaffār) to whoever repents and believes and does righteous work (ʿAmal Ṣāliḥ) then is guided.' So if he expects forgiveness with repentance, he is hopeful (Rāj), and if he expects forgiveness with persistence (in sin), he is deluded (Maghrūr), just as one for whom the time of Friday prayer becomes tight while he is in the market, and it occurs to him to hasten to the Friday prayer, and Satan says to him: You will not catch the Friday prayer, so stay in your place. So he disbelieves Satan and goes running while hoping to catch the Friday prayer - he is hopeful. And if he continues with trade and begins to hope for the Imam to delay the prayer for his sake until the middle of the time, or for the sake of another, or for a reason among the reasons he does not know, he is deluded.
20:82.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

20:82.arabic: وَمَهْمَا تَمَّتْ مَعْرَفَتُهُ كَانَتِ الْخَشْيَةُ أَغْلَبَ الْأَحْوَالِ عَلَى قَلْبِهِ فَإِنَّ التَّضْيِيقَ غَالِبٌ عَلَى آيَاتِ الْقُرْآنِ فَلَا يَرَى ذِكْرَ الْمَغْفِرَةِ وَالرَّحْمَةِ إِلَّا مُقْرُونًا بِشُرُوطٍ يَقْصُرُ الْعَارِفُ عَنْ نَيْلِهَا كَقَوْلِهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ ﴿ وَإِنِّي لَغَفَّارٌ ﴾ {} ثُمَّ أَتْبَعَ ذَلِكَ بِأَرْبَعَةِ شُرُوطٍ ﴿ لِمَنْ تَابَ وَآمَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا ثُمَّ اهْتَدَىٰ ﴾ {}
20:82.english: And whenever his knowledge is perfected, the state of fear (Khushya) becomes predominant over his heart (Qalb), for restriction is prevalent in the verses of the Quran. He does not see the mention of forgiveness (Maghfira) and mercy (Rahma) except coupled with conditions that the knower (Al-'Arif) falls short of attaining, like His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And indeed, I am Forgiving (Ghaffar)' then followed that with four conditions: 'for whoever repents (Taba) and believes (Amana) and does righteous work (Amila Salihan) then is guided (Ihtada).'
20:82.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

20:82.arabic: ولنرجع إلى الغرض المطلوب فالمقصود أن غرور الشيطان بأن الآخرة شك يدفع إما بيقين تقليدي، وأما ببصيرة ومشاهدة من جهة الباطن، والمؤمنين بألسنتهم وبعقائدهم إذا ضيعوا أوامر الله تعالى وهجروا الأعمال الصالحة ولابسوا الشهوات والمعاصي فهم مشاركون للكفار في هذا الغرور من النار ولو بعد حين، ولكنهم أيضاً من المغرورين فإنهم اعترفوا بأن الآخرة خير من الدنيا ولكنهم مالوا إلى الدنيا وآثروها، ومجرد الإيمان لا يكفي للفوز قال تعالى "وإني لغفار لمن تاب وآمن وعمل صالحاً ثم اهتدى" وقال تعالى "إن رحمت الله قريب من الم
20:82.english: And let us return to the intended purpose, so the intended meaning is that the deception of Satan that the Hereafter is doubt is repelled either by traditional certainty, or by insight and witnessing from the aspect of the inner (Batin), and the believers with their tongues and with their beliefs if they neglect the commands of Allah the Exalted and abandon righteous works and engage in desires and disobediences, they are partners with the disbelievers in this deception from the Fire even if after a while, but they are also among the deceived, for they acknowledged that the Hereafter is better than the worldly life but they inclined to the worldly life and preferred it, and mere faith is not sufficient for success. Allah the Exalted said: "And indeed, I am Forgiving to whoever repents and believes and does righteous work then is guided." And Allah the Exalted said: "Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the doers of good." Then the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Excellence (Ihsan) is that you worship Allah as if you see Him." And Allah the Exalted said: "By time, indeed, mankind is in loss, except for those who have believed and done righteous works and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience." So the promise of forgiveness in all the Book of Allah the Exalted is tied to faith and righteous work together, not to faith alone, so these are also deceived, I mean those who are content with the worldly life, joyful in it, indulgent in its pleasures, loving it.
20:82.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

20:82.arabic: وأما المعتزلة فشبهتهم قوله تعالى: ﴿ وإني لغفار لمن تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا ثم اهتدى ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ والعصر إن الإنسان لفي خسر إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى ﴿ وإن منكم إلا واردها كان على ربك حتما مقضيا ﴾ {} ثم قال: ﴿ ثم ننجي الذين اتقوا ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ ومن يعص الله ورسوله فإن له نار جهنم ﴾ {} وكل آية ذكر الله عز وجل العمل الصالح فيها مقرونا بالإيمان
20:82.english: As for the Mu'tazilites, their evidence is His saying, the Exalted: 'And indeed, I am Forgiving (Ghaffār) to the one who repents (Tāba) and believes (Āmana) and does righteous work (ʿAmila Ṣāliḥan) then is guided (Ihtadā)' and His saying, the Exalted: 'By time, indeed, mankind is in loss, except those who have believed (Āmanū) and done righteous deeds (ʿAmilū al-Ṣāliḥāt)' and His saying, the Exalted: 'And there is none of you except he will enter it. This has been upon your Lord a decree determined' then He said: 'Then We will save those who feared (Ittaqū)' and His saying, the Exalted: 'And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger - then indeed, for him is the Fire of Hell' and every verse in which Allah, the Exalted, mentions righteous work (al-ʿAmal al-Ṣāliḥ) is coupled with faith (al-Īmān).
20:82.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Foundations of Belief'

20:82.arabic: والقرآن من أوله إلى آخره مخاوف لمن قرأه بتدبر ولو لم يكن فيه إلا قوله تعالى: ﴿ وإني لغفار لمن تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا ثم اهتدى ﴾ {} لكان كافيا إذ علق المغفرة على أربعة شروط يعجز العبد عن آحادها
20:82.english: And the Quran from its beginning to its end contains fears for whoever reads it with contemplation, and even if there were nothing in it except His saying, the Exalted: 'And indeed I am Forgiving (Ghaffar) for whoever repents (Taba) and believes (Amana) and does righteous work (Amila Salihan) then is guided (Ihtada)' {} it would be sufficient, since He made forgiveness (Maghfirah) conditional upon four conditions that the servant (Al-Abd) is incapable of fulfilling individually.
20:82.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Fear and Hope'

20:88.arabic: وأما أصحاب السامري لما كان إيمانهم عن النظر إلى ظاهر الثعبان، فلما نظروا إلى عجل السامري وسمعوا خواره تغيروا وسمعوا قوله "هذا إلهكم وإله موسى" ونسوا أنه لا يرجع إليهم قولاً ولا يملك لهم ضراً ولا نفعاً: فكل من آمن بالنظر إلى ثعبان يكفر لا محالة إذا نظر إلى عجل، لأن كليهما من عالم الشهادة والاختلاف والتضاد في عالم الشهادة كثير. وأما عالم الملكوت فهو من عند الله تعالى فلذلك لا نجد فيه اختلافاً وتضاداً أصلاً.
20:88.english: As for the companions of the Samiri, when their faith was based on looking at the apparent serpent, then when they looked at the calf of the Samiri and heard its lowing, they changed and heard his saying "This is your god and the god of Moses" and they forgot that it does not return to them any speech nor possesses for them any harm or benefit: For everyone who believes by looking at a serpent disbelieves inevitably if he looks at a calf, because both are from the world of testimony (al-Shahadah) and difference and opposition in the world of testimony (al-Shahadah) is abundant. As for the world of the dominion (al-Malakut), it is from Allah the Exalted, therefore we do not find in it any difference or opposition at all.
20:88.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

20:89.arabic: ومثاله أن يتمثل بين يدي ملك من الملوك طول النهار كما جرت عادة الخدم وإنما وقوفه لملاحظة جارية من جواري الملك أو غلام من غلمانه، فإن هذا استهزاء بالملك إذ لم يقصد التقريب إلى الملك بخدمته بل قصد بذلك عبداً من عبيده، فأي استحقار يزيد على أن يقصد العبد بطاعة الله تعالى مراءاة عبد ضعيف لا يملك له ضراً ولا نفعاً؟ وهل ذلك إلا لأنه يظن أن ذلك العبد أقدر على تحصيل أغراضه من الله؟ وأنه أولى بالتقريب إليه من الله إذ آثره على ملك الملوك فجعله مقصود عبادته؟ وأي استهزاء يزيد على رفع العبد فوق المولى؟ فهذا من
20:89.english: And its example is that one stands before a king from the kings all day long as is the custom of servants, yet his standing is only for observing a maiden from the maidens of the king or a boy from his boys. Indeed, this is mockery of the king, for he did not intend closeness to the king through his service, but rather intended by that a servant from his servants. So what contempt increases beyond that the servant intends by obedience to Allah the Exalted the showing-off (Riya') to a weak servant who does not possess for him harm nor benefit? And is that except because he thinks that that servant is more capable of attaining his objectives than Allah? And that he is more deserving of closeness to him than Allah since he preferred him over the King of Kings and made him the intended object of his worship? And what mockery increases beyond raising the servant above the Master (Mawla)? So this is from the great destructive sins, and for this the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) called it the minor polytheism (Shirk al-Asghar). Yes, some degrees of showing-off (Riya') are more severe than others - as will come its clarification in the degrees of showing-off (Riya') if Allah the Exalted wills - and nothing of it is devoid of grave or light sin according to what is in the showing-off (Riya'), and if there were not in showing-off (Riya') except that he prostrates and bows to other than Allah, it would be sufficient. For indeed, even if he did not intend closeness to Allah, he has intended other than Allah. By my life, if he magnified other than Allah with prostration, he would disbelieve with clear disbelief (Kufr Jali), except that showing-off (Riya') is the hidden disbelief (Kufr Khafi) because the show-off (Mura'i) has magnified in his heart (Qalb) the people, so that magnification necessitated that he prostrates and bows, so the people were the magnified ones by the prostration from one aspect. And whenever the intention of magnifying Allah by the prostration vanishes and the magnification of the creation (Khalq) remains, that was close to polytheism (Shirk), except that he intended the magnification of himself in the heart (Qalb) of the one magnified by him through his showing from himself the image of magnification for Allah. So from this it was hidden polytheism (Shirk Khafi), not clear polytheism (Shirk Jali), and that is the utmost ignorance, and none proceeds upon it except whom the Satan (Shaytan) has deceived and made him imagine that the servants possess from his harm and benefit.
20:89.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

20:89.arabic: وأما أصحاب السامري لما كان إيمانهم عن النظر إلى ظاهر الثعبان، فلما نظروا إلى عجل السامري وسمعوا خواره تغيروا وسمعوا قوله "هذا إلهكم وإله موسى" ونسوا أنه لا يرجع إليهم قولاً ولا يملك لهم ضراً ولا نفعاً: فكل من آمن بالنظر إلى ثعبان يكفر لا محالة إذا نظر إلى عجل، لأن كليهما من عالم الشهادة والاختلاف والتضاد في عالم الشهادة كثير. وأما عالم الملكوت فهو من عند الله تعالى فلذلك لا نجد فيه اختلافاً وتضاداً أصلاً.
20:89.english: As for the companions of the Samiri, when their faith was based on looking at the outward appearance of the serpent, then when they looked at the calf of the Samiri and heard its lowing, they changed and heard his saying "This is your god and the god of Moses" and they forgot that it does not return to them a word nor does it possess for them harm or benefit: So everyone who believed by looking at a serpent disbelieves inevitably if he looks at a calf, because both of them are from the world of witnessing (Shahadah) and difference and opposition in the world of witnessing (Shahadah) is abundant. As for the world of the dominion (Malakut), it is from Allah the Exalted, therefore we do not find in it difference or opposition at all.
20:89.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

20:98.arabic: مع أنه لا كمال في مدحهم ولا نقصان في ذمهم كما قال شاعر بني تميم: إن مدحي زين وإن ذمي شين! فقال له رسول الله ﭬ "كذبت؛ ذاك الله الذي لا إله إلا هو[48] إذ لا زين إلا في مدحه ولا شين إلا في ذمه، فأي خير لك في مدح الناس. وأنت عند الله مذموم ومن أهل النار؟ وأي شر لك من ذم الناس وأنت عند الله محمود في زمرة المقربين؟
20:98.english: With that, there is no perfection in their praise nor deficiency in their blame, as the poet of Banu Tamim said: 'Indeed my praise is adornment (zayn) and indeed my blame is disgrace (shayn)!' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'You have lied; that is Allah who has no deity except Him[48] since there is no adornment (zayn) except in His praise and no disgrace (shayn) except in His blame. So what good is there for you in the praise of people while you are blameworthy before Allah and from the people of the Fire? And what harm is there for you from the blame of people while you are praiseworthy before Allah in the company of those brought near?'
20:98.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

20:98.arabic: فقال: والله الذي لا إله إلا هو لا أراك تعرفه.
20:98.english: He said: By Allah, the One (Allah) who there is no god (ilah) except Him, I do not see that you know him.
20:98.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

20:107.arabic: يوم تنسف فيه الجبال نسفا فتترك قاعا صفصفا لا ترى فيها عوجا ولا أمتا، يوم ترى الجبال تحسبها جامدة وهى تمر مر السحاب، يوم تنشق فيه السماء فتكون وردة كالدهان، فيومئذ لا يسئل عن ذنبه إنس ولا جان، يوم يمنع فيه العاصى من الكلام ولا يسئل فيه عن الأجرام بل يؤخذ بالنواصى والأقدام، يوم تجد كل نفس ما عملت من خير محضرا وما عملت من سوء تود لو أن بينها وبينه أمدا بعيدا، يوم تعلم فيه كل نفس ما أحضرت وتشهد ما قدمت وأخرت يوم تخرس فيه الألسن وتنطق الجوارح يوم شيب ذكره سيد المرسلين إذ قال له الصديق رضى الله عنه: أ
20:107.english: The day when the mountains will be blown away, leaving a level plain where you will see no crookedness nor curvature, the day when you will see the mountains thinking them firm while they pass like clouds, the day when the sky will split open becoming like red leather, then on that day no human nor jinn will be asked about his sin, the day when the disobedient will be prevented from speech and no inquiry will be made about the bodies but they will be seized by the forelocks and the feet, the day when every soul (Nafs) will find what it did of good present and what it did of evil it will wish there were a great distance between it and that, the day when every soul (Nafs) will know what it has brought forth and will witness what it sent ahead and left behind, the day when tongues will be silenced and limbs will speak, the day whose mention turned grey the master of the messengers when the truthful one (Al-Siddiq) said to him: I see you have turned grey, O Messenger of Allah. He said: (Hud and its sisters turned me grey[155]) and they are Al-Waqi'ah, Al-Mursalat, 'Amma Yatasa'alun, and Idha Al-Shamsu Kuwwirat. So O incapable reader, your share from your reading is only that you mumble the Quran and move your tongue with it, and if you were reflecting on what you read, you would be worthy of having your bitterness split open from what turned grey the hair of the master of the messengers, and if you are content with the movement of the tongue, you have been deprived of the fruit of the Quran. The Resurrection (Al-Qiyamah) is one of what is mentioned in it, and Allah has described some of its calamities and multiplied its names so that we may stand, through the multiplicity of its names, upon the multiplicity of its meanings, for the purpose of the multiplicity of names is not the repetition of names and titles, but the aim is to alert those of understanding (Ulul Albab), for under every name of the names of the Resurrection (Al-Qiyamah) there is a secret and in it...
20:107.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

20:107.arabic: ثم انظر كيف يساقون بعد البعث والنشور حفاة عراة غرلا إلى أرض المحشر أرض بيضاء قاع صفصف لا ترى فيها عوجا ولا أمتا ولا ترى عليها ربوة يختفى الإنسان وراءها ولا وهدة ينخفض عن الأعين فيها بل هو صعيد واحد بسيط لا تفاوت فيه يساقون إليه زمرا فسبحان من جمع الخلائق على اختلاف أصنافهم من أقطار الأرض إذ ساقهم بالراجفة تتبعها الرادفة والراجفة هى النفخة الأولى والرادفة هى النفخة الثانية وحقيق لتلك القلوب أن تكون يومئذ واجفة ولتلك الأبصار أن تكون خاشعة قال رسول الله ﭬ: (يحشر الناس يوم القيامة على أرض بيضاء عفرا
20:107.english: Then look at how they are driven after the Resurrection (al-Ba'th) and the Rising (al-Nushur), barefoot, naked, uncircumcised, to the land of the Gathering (Ard al-Mahshar), a white land, a level plain, you will see in it no crookedness (la tara fiha 'iwajan) nor any depression (wa-la amtan), nor will you see upon it a hill behind which a human can hide, nor a valley that lowers from the eyes in it; rather, it is a single, simple, level ground with no variation in it; they are driven to it in groups. So glory be to the One who gathers the creatures despite the difference of their kinds from the corners of the earth when He drives them with the Shaking (al-Rajifah) followed by the Following (al-Radifah); and the Shaking is the first Blast (al-Nafkhah al-Ula) and the Following is the second Blast (al-Nafkhah al-Thaniyah). And it is fitting for those Hearts (Qulub) to be trembling (wajifah) at that time, and for those Eyes (Absar) to be humbled (khashi'ah). The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'The people will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection (Yawm al-Qiyamah) on a white, pale land like a pure loaf, with no landmark for anyone.' The narrator said: And the paleness is a whiteness that is not bright, and the pure is that which is pure from husk and bran, and landmark means no building to conceal nor variation to repel the sight. And do not think that that land is like the land of the world; rather, it does not equal it except in name. Allah the Exalted said: 'On the Day when the earth will be changed to another earth and the heavens.' Ibn Abbas said: It increases in it and decreases, and its trees, mountains, valleys, and what is in it go away, and it stretches like the stretching of the Adim al-'Akkazi, a white land like silver, upon which no blood has been spilled nor any sin committed; and the heavens, their sun, moon, and stars go away. So look, O wretched one, at the terror of that day and its severity, for when the creatures gather on this level ground, the stars of the sky scatter from above them and the sun is extinguished.
20:107.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

20:109.arabic: حتى يشفع نبينا ﭬ لمن يؤذن له فيه ﴿ لا يملكون الشفاعة إلا من أذن له الرحمن ورضى له قولا ﴾ {} فتأمل فى طول هذا اليوم وشدة الانتظار فيه حتى يخف عليك انتظار الصبر عن المعاصى فى عمرك المختصر.
20:109.english: Until our Prophet (peace be upon him) intercedes for whom permission is given to him in it: 'They do not possess intercession (Shafa'a) except for whom the Most Merciful (Al-Rahman) has given permission and has been pleased with his speech.' So contemplate in the length of this day and the severity of waiting in it until the waiting for patience from sins in your brief lifespan becomes light upon you.
20:109.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

20:113.arabic: ولذلك قيل تفكر ساعة خير من عبادة سنة فقيل هو الذى ينقل من المكاره إلى المحاب ومن الرغبة والحرص إلى الزهد والقناعة وقيل هو الذى يحدث مشاهدة وتقوى ولذلك قال تعالى لعلهم يتقون أو يحدث لهم ذكرا وإن أردت أن تفهم كيفية تغير الحال بالفكر فمثاله ما ذكرناه من أمر الآخرة فإن الفكر يعرفنا أن الآخرة أولى بالإيثار فإذا رسخت هذه المعرفة يقينا في قلوبنا تغيرت القلوب إلى الرغبة في الآخرة والزهد في الدنيا
20:113.english: And therefore it is said: 'Reflection (Tafakkur) for an hour is better than worship for a year.' It is said that it transfers from the disliked to the beloved, and from desire and greed to asceticism (Zuhd) and contentment (Qana'ah). And it is said that it brings about witnessing (Mushahadah) and piety (Taqwa). And therefore Allah the Exalted said: 'So that they may become pious (Yattaqun) or it may bring about for them a Remembrance (Dhikr).' And if you wish to understand how the state (Hal) changes through reflection (Fikr), its example is what we mentioned regarding the matter of the Hereafter. For reflection (Fikr) makes us know that the Hereafter is more deserving of preference. So when this knowledge becomes firmly established with certainty in our hearts (Qulub), the hearts (Qulub) change to desire for the Hereafter and asceticism (Zuhd) in this world.
20:113.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Contemplation'

20:114.arabic: فتعالى الله الملك الحق لا يسئل عما يفعل وهم يسئلون ولنقتصر على هذا القدر اليسير من ذكر عجائب القلب فإن استقصاءه لا يليق بعلم المعاملة وإنما ذكرنا منه ما يحتاج إليه لمعرفة أغوار علوم المعاملة وأسرارها لينتفع بها من لا يقنع بالظواهر ولا يجتزئ بالقشر عن اللباب بل يتشوق إلى معرفة دقائق حقائق الأسباب وفيما ذكرناه كفاية له ومقنع إن شاء الله تعالى والله ولي التوفيق تم كتاب عجائب القلب ولله الحمد والمنة ويتلوه كتاب رياضة النفس وتهذيب الأخلاق والحمد لله وحده وصلى الله على كل عبد مصطفى.
20:114.english: So Exalted is Allah, the True King (Al-Malik al-Haqq). He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned. And we will limit ourselves to this small amount of mentioning the wonders of the Heart (Qalb), for its exhaustive treatment is not fitting for the knowledge of spiritual practice (Ilm al-Mu'amalah). Rather, we have mentioned from it what is needed for knowing the depths of the sciences of spiritual practice and their secrets, so that those who are not satisfied with outward appearances and do not content themselves with the shell instead of the core (al-Lubab) may benefit from it, but rather yearn to know the subtleties of the realities of causes. In what we have mentioned, there is sufficiency for him and satisfaction, if Allah wills. And Allah is the Guardian of success. The book of the wonders of the Heart is completed, and praise and favor are to Allah. And following it is the book of disciplining the Soul (Nafs) and refining character. And praise is to Allah alone, and may Allah bless every chosen servant.
20:114.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

20:114.arabic: ومن أبوابه العظيمة العجلة وترك التثبت في الأمور وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم العجلة من الشيطان والتأني من الله تعالى وقال عز وجل خلق الإنسان من عجل وقال تعالى وكان الإنسان عجولا وقال لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا تعجل بالقرآن من قبل أن يقضي إليك وحيه وهذا لأن الأعمال ينبغي أن تكون بعد التبصرة والمعرفة والتبصرة تحتاج إلى تأمل وتمهل والعجلة تمنع من ذلك وعند الاستعجال يروج الشيطان شره على الإنسان من حيث لا يدري
20:114.english: And among its great gates are haste and abandoning careful consideration in matters. And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Haste is from Satan, and deliberation is from Allah the Exalted.' And the Mighty and Majestic said: 'Man was created from haste.' And He said: 'And man is hasty.' And He said to His Prophet (peace be upon him): 'And do not hasten with the Quran before its revelation is completed to you.' And this is because actions should be after insight and knowledge, and insight requires contemplation and deliberation, and haste prevents that. And during hastening, Satan spreads his evil upon the human from where he does not realize.
20:114.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

20:116.arabic: الآثار: قال بعض السلف: أول خطيئة هي الحسد حسد إبليس آدم عليه السلام على رتبته فأبى أن يسجد له فحمله على الحسد والمعصية. وحكي أن عون بن عبد الله دخل على الفضل بن المهلب وكان يومئذ على واسط فقال: إني أريد أن أعظك بشيء فقال: وما هو؟ قال: إياك والكبر فإنه أول ذنب عصي الله به، ثم قرأ "وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس" الآية، وإياك والحرص فإنه أخرج آدم من الجنة أمكنه الله سبحانه من جنة عرضها السموات والأرض يأكل منها إلا شجرة واحدة نهاه عنها فأكل منها فأخرجه الله تعالى منها، ثم قرأ "اهبطو
20:116.english: The Narrations: Some of the predecessors said: The first sin is envy (Hasad) - Iblis envied Adam, peace be upon him, regarding his rank, so he refused to prostrate to him, and it carried him into envy (Hasad) and disobedience. And it is narrated that 'Awn ibn 'Abdullah entered upon al-Fadl ibn al-Muhallab, who was then in Wasit, and said: I want to advise you with something. He said: And what is it? He said: Beware of arrogance (Kibr), for it is the first sin by which Allah was disobeyed, then he recited: "And [mention] when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam,' and they prostrated, except for Iblis" the verse, and beware of greed (Hirs), for it expelled Adam from Paradise - Allah, glorified and He, had enabled him in a Paradise the width of the heavens and the earth, he could eat from it except one tree He forbade him from, so he ate from it and Allah, exalted, expelled him from it, then he recited: "Descend from it" to the end of the verse, and beware of envy (Hasad), for indeed the son of Adam killed his brother when he envied him, then he recited: "And recite to them the story of Adam's two sons in truth," the verses, and when the companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, are mentioned, then refrain, and when predestination (Qadr) is mentioned, be silent, and when the stars are mentioned, be silent.
20:116.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

20:117.arabic: ولم يؤمنهم ذلك من كيد الشيطان ولذلك لم يسلم منه آدم وحواء في الجنة التي هي دار الأمن والسرور بعد أن قال الله لهما "إن هذا عدو لك ولزوجك فلا يخرجنكما من الجنة فتشقى إن لك أن لا تجوع فيها ولا تعرى وأنك لا تظمأ فيها ولا تضحى" ومع أنه لم ينه إلا عن شجرة واحدة وأطلق له وراء ذلك ما أراد فإذا لم يأمن نبي من الأنبياء وهو في الجنة دار الأمن والسعادة من كيد الشيطان فكيف يجوز لغيره أن يأمن في دار الدنيا وهي منبع المحن والفتن معدن الملاذ والشهوات المنهي عنها؟
20:117.english: And that did not secure them from the plotting of Satan, and therefore Adam and Eve were not safe from him in the Garden (Jannah) which is the abode of security and joy, after Allah said to them: "Indeed, this is an enemy to you and your spouse, so let him not expel you from the Garden (Jannah) lest you become wretched. Indeed, it is for you that you will not be hungry therein nor unclothed, and you will not be thirsty therein nor suffer from heat." And even though He only forbade one tree and permitted for him beyond that what he desired, if a prophet from the prophets did not feel secure from the plotting of Satan while he was in the Garden (Jannah), the abode of security and happiness, then how can it be permissible for anyone else to feel secure in the abode of the worldly life (Dunya), which is the source of trials and tribulations, the mine of pleasures and forbidden desires (Shahawat)?
20:117.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

20:118.arabic: ولم يؤمنهم ذلك من كيد الشيطان ولذلك لم يسلم منه آدم وحواء في الجنة التي هي دار الأمن والسرور بعد أن قال الله لهما "إن هذا عدو لك ولزوجك فلا يخرجنكما من الجنة فتشقى إن لك أن لا تجوع فيها ولا تعرى وأنك لا تظمأ فيها ولا تضحى" ومع أنه لم ينه إلا عن شجرة واحدة وأطلق له وراء ذلك ما أراد فإذا لم يأمن نبي من الأنبياء وهو في الجنة دار الأمن والسعادة من كيد الشيطان فكيف يجوز لغيره أن يأمن في دار الدنيا وهي منبع المحن والفتن معدن الملاذ والشهوات المنهي عنها؟
20:118.english: And that did not secure them from the plotting of Satan, and therefore Adam and Eve were not safe from him in the Garden (Jannah) which is the abode of security and joy after Allah said to them: "Indeed, this is an enemy to you and your spouse, so do not let him expel you from the Garden (Jannah) so that you become wretched. Indeed, for you is that you will not hunger therein nor be naked, and indeed, you will not thirst therein nor be exposed to the sun." And despite that He only forbade one tree and permitted for him beyond that what he desired, so if a prophet from the prophets did not feel secure while in the Garden (Jannah), the abode of security and happiness, from the plotting of Satan, then how is it permissible for anyone else to feel secure in the abode of the world (Dunya), which is the source of trials and tribulations, the mine of pleasures and forbidden desires?
20:118.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

20:121.arabic: أما بعد: فأعظم المهلكات لابن آدم شهوة البطن، فبها أخرج آدم عليه السلام وحواء من دار القرار إلى دار الذل والافتقار؛ إذ نهيا عن الشجرة فغلبتهما شهواتهما حتى أكلا منها فبدت لهما سوآتهما. والبطن على التحقيق ينبوع الشهوات ومنبت الأدواء والآفات، إذ يتبعها شهوة الفرج وشدة الشبق إلى المنكوحات؛ ثم تتبع شهوة الطعام والنكاح شدة الرغبة في الجاه والمال اللذين هما وسيلة إلى التوسع في المنكوحات والمطعومات؛ ثم يتبع استكثار المال والجاه أنواع الرعونات وضروب المنافسات والمحاسدات؛ ثم يتولد بينهما آفة الرياء وغائلة
20:121.english: Now then: The greatest destroyer for the son of Adam is the desire (shahwa) of the stomach, for through it Adam (peace be upon him) and Eve were expelled from the abode of settlement to the abode of humiliation and need; when they were forbidden from the tree, their desires overcame them until they ate from it and their shameful parts became apparent to them. The stomach, in truth, is the spring of desires (shahawat) and the source of diseases and afflictions, for it is followed by the desire (shahwa) of the private parts and intense lust (shiddat al-shabaq) for women; then following the desire (shahwa) for food and intercourse comes intense craving for status and wealth, which are means to expansion in women and foods; then following the accumulation of wealth and status come various foolishnesses and types of rivalries and envies; then between them is generated the affliction of hypocrisy (riya') and the consequence of boasting, competition, and arrogance (kibriya'), then that leads to rancor, envy, enmity, and hatred, then that brings its possessor to plunge into oppression, evil, and indecency, and all of that is the fruit of neglecting the stomach and what is generated from it of the insolence of satiety and fullness. If the servant (al-'abd) had subdued his soul (nafs) with hunger and narrowed with it the channels of Satan, it would have submitted to the obedience of Allah (the Mighty and Majestic) and not taken the path of insolence and transgression, and it would not have led to immersion in the worldly life and preferring the immediate over the hereafter, and it would not have rushed with all this rushing upon the worldly life. And if the affliction of the desire (shahwa) of the stomach has reached this extent, it is obligatory to explain its dangers and afflictions as a warning from it, and it is obligatory to clarify the way of striving (mujahada) against it and to point out its virtue as an encouragement toward it, and likewise explaining the desire (shahwa) of the private parts, for it follows it.
20:121.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Harms of the Tongue'

20:121.arabic: وإن خطر ببالك أنه لا يعاقب إلا على معصية ولا يثيب إلا على طاعة فتأمل أنه لم يمد المطيع بأسباب الطاعة حتى يطيع شاء أم أبى ولم يمد العاصي بدواعي المعصية حتى يعصي شاء أم أبى فإنه مهما خلق الغفلة والشهوة والقدرة على قضاء الشهوة كان الفعل واقعا بها بالضرورة فإن كان أبعده لأنه عصاه فلم حمله على المعصية هل ذلك لمعصية سابقة حتى يتسلسل إلى غير نهاية أو يقف لا محالة على أول لا علة له من جهة العبد بل قضى عليه في الأزل وعن هذا المعنى عبر ﭬ إذ قال: (احتج آدم موسى عليهما الصلاة والسلام عند ربهما فحج آدم موسى
20:121.english: And if it occurs to your mind that He does not punish except for disobedience (ma'siyah) and does not reward except for obedience (ta'ah), then contemplate that He did not provide the obedient one with the means of obedience so that he would obey whether he willed or not, and He did not provide the disobedient one with the motives of disobedience so that he would disobey whether he willed or not. For whenever He created heedlessness (ghaflah) and desire (shahwah) and the ability to fulfill the desire, the action occurred by necessity through them. If He distanced him because he disobeyed Him, then what compelled him to the disobedience? Is that due to a prior disobedience until it regresses to infinity, or it inevitably stops at a first cause that has no cause from the side of the servant? Rather, it was decreed for him in pre-eternity. And about this meaning, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Adam and Moses (peace be upon them both) argued before their Lord, and Adam overcame Moses (peace be upon him). Moses said: 'You are Adam whom Allah created with His Hand, breathed into you from His Spirit (Ruh), made His angels prostrate to you, and settled you in His Garden, then you caused the people to descend to the earth by your sin.' Adam said: 'You are Moses whom Allah chose with His message and His speech, gave you the Tablets in which is the explanation of everything, and brought you near as a confidant. For how long did you find that Allah wrote the Torah before I was created?' Moses said: 'Forty years.' Adam said: 'Then did you find in it: "And Adam disobeyed (عصى) his Lord and went astray (فغوى)"? He said: 'Yes.' Adam said: 'Then do you blame me for doing an act that Allah wrote upon me before I did it and before He created me by forty years?' The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'So Adam overcame Moses.' So whoever knows the cause in this matter with a knowledge emanating from the light of guidance, he is from the special knowers (al-'arifin) who are aware of the secret of divine decree (al-qadr). And whoever hears this and believes in it and affirms it by mere hearing, he is from the general believers. And fear (khawf) occurs for each one of the two groups. For if he is a servant, he is fallen into the grasp of divine power like the fall of the weak child into the claws of the lion, and the lion may be heedless by coincidence and leave him, and it may attack him and devour him, and that is according to what coincides. And that coincidence has causes arranged by a known decree. But if it is attributed to one who does not know it, it is called coincidence, and if it is attributed to the knowledge of Allah, it is not permissible to call it coincidence. And the one fallen into the claws of the lion, if his knowledge were complete, he would not fear the lion because the lion is subjugated: if hunger is imposed upon it, it devours, and if heedlessness is imposed upon it, it leaves and abandons. So indeed, one fears the Creator of the lion and the Creator of its attributes. I do not say that the example of fear from Allah the Exalted is fear from the lion, but when the veil is lifted, it is known that fear from the lion is the very fear from Allah the Exalted because the destroyer through the medium of the lion is Allah. So know that the lions of the Hereafter are like the lions of this world, and that Allah the Exalted created the causes of punishment and the causes of reward and created for each
20:121.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Fear and Hope'

20:121.arabic: فأول القصص: قصة آدم عليه السلام وإبليس أما تراهما كيف اشتركا في اسم المعصية والمخالفة ثم تباينا في الاجتباء والعصمة. أما إبليس فأبلس عن رحمته، وقيل إنه من المبعدين. وأما آدم عليه السلام فقيل فيه " وعصى آدم ربه فغوى ثم اجتباه ربه فتاب عليه وهدى ".
20:121.english: The first story: The story of Adam (peace be upon him) and Iblis. Do you not see how they shared in the name of disobedience (al-ma'siyah) and opposition (al-mukhalafah), then they diverged in selection (al-ijtibā') and protection (al-'ismah). As for Iblis, he despaired (ablasa) of His mercy, and it is said that he is among the banished (al-mub'adin). As for Adam (peace be upon him), it is said about him: "And Adam disobeyed (ʿaṣā) his Lord and went astray (faghawā), then his Lord chose him (ijtabāhu) and turned to him (tāba) and guided him (hadā)."
20:121.topic: Al-Ghazali on the outer and inner dimensions of worship, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

20:124.arabic: وأما مجرَّد حركة اللسان فقليل الجدوى بل التالي باللسان المعرض عن العمل جدير بأن يكون هو المراد بقوله تعالى ﴿ ومن أعرض عن ذكري فإن له معيشة ضنكا ونحشره يوم القيامة أعمى ﴾ {} وبقوله عز وجل ﴿ كذلك أتتك آياتنا فنسيتها وكذلك اليوم تنسى ﴾ {} أي تركها ولم تنظر إليها ولم تعبأ بها فإنَّ المُقَصِّر في الأمر يقال إنه نسي الأمر وتلاوة القرآن. حق تلاوته هو أن يشترك فيه اللسان والعقل والقلب فحظ اللسان تصحيح الحروف بالترتيل وحظ العقل تفسير المعاني وحظ القلب الاتعاظ والتأثر بالانزجار والائتمار. فاللسان يرتل وال
20:124.english: And as for mere movement of the tongue, it is of little benefit. Rather, the one who recites with the tongue while turning away from action is worthy of being what is intended by His saying, the Exalted: 'And whoever turns away from My Remembrance (Dhikr), then indeed for him is a straitened life (ma'ishatan dankan), and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind.' And by His saying, the Exalted: 'Thus Our signs came to you, and you forgot them; and thus today you are forgotten.' That is, he left them and did not look at them and did not care for them. For the one who falls short in the matter, it is said that he forgot the matter. And the recitation of the Quran, its true recitation, is that the tongue, the intellect ('Aql), and the heart (Qalb) participate in it. The portion of the tongue is correcting the letters with proper recitation (tartil), the portion of the intellect is interpreting the meanings, and the portion of the heart is taking admonition and being affected by the warning and the command. So the tongue recites properly, the intellect translates, and the heart takes admonition.
20:124.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

20:124.arabic: هل تدرون فيماذا أنزلت ﴿ فإن له معيشة ضنكا ﴾ {} قالوا الله ورسوله أعلم قال عذاب الكافر في قبره يسلط عليه تسعة وتسعون تنينا هل تدرون ما التنين؟ تسعة وتسعون حية لكل حية تسعة رؤوس يخدشونه ويلحسونه وينفخون في جسمه إلى يوم يبعثون[126]) ولا ينبغي أن يتعجب من هذا العدد على الخصوص فإن أعداد هذه الحيات والعقارب بعدد الأخلاق المذمومة من الكبر والرياء والحسد والغل والحقد وسائر الصفات فإن لها أصولا معدودة ثم تتشعب منها فروع معدودة ثم تنقسم فروعها إلى أقسام وتلك الصفات بأعيانها هي المهلكات وهي بأعيانها تنقلب
20:124.english: Do you know regarding what was revealed "For him is a straitened life (ma'ishatan dankan)"? They said: Allah and His Messenger know best. He said: The punishment of the disbeliever in his grave; there are unleashed upon him ninety-nine dragons (tinnin). Do you know what the dragon (tinnin) is? Ninety-nine snakes (hayya), each snake has nine heads, they scratch him, lick him, and blow into his body until the day they are resurrected. And one should not be astonished at this number in particular, for the numbers of these snakes and scorpions are according to the number of blameworthy character traits (akhlaq al-madhmuma) from arrogance (kibr), hypocrisy (riya'), envy (hasad), rancor (ghill), malice (hiqd), and other attributes (sifat). For they have countable roots, then branches spread from them that are countable, then their branches divide into divisions, and those attributes in their very essences are the destroyers (al-muhlikat), and in their very essences they transform into scorpions and snakes. The strong among them stings with the sting of the dragon (tinnin), and the weak stings with the sting of the scorpion (aqrab), and what is between them harms with the harm of the snake (hayya). And the possessors of hearts (arbab al-qulub) and insights (al-basa'ir) witness with the light of insight (nur al-basira) these destroyers and their branching offshoots, except that the measure of their number cannot be ascertained except by the light of prophethood (nur al-nubuwwa). So, the likes of these reports have sound outward appearances (zawahir sahiha) and hidden secrets (asrar khafiya), but they are clear to the possessors of insights (arbab al-basa'ir). So, whoever the realities (haqa'iq) of them are not unveiled to him, he should not deny their outward appearances; rather, the lowest degrees of faith (iman) are belief (tasdiq) and submission (taslim).
20:124.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Book of Repentance'

20:126.arabic: بل التالي باللسان المعرض عن العمل جدير بأن يكون هو المراد بقوله تعالى ﴿ ومن أعرض عن ذكري فإن له معيشة ضنكا ونحشره يوم القيامة أعمى ﴾ {} وبقوله عز وجل ﴿ كذلك أتتك آياتنا فنسيتها وكذلك اليوم تنسى ﴾ {} أي تركتهما ولم تنظر إليهما ولم تعبأ بهما فإنَّ المُقَصِّر في الأمر يقال إنه نسي الأمر وتلاوة القرآن. حق تلاوته هو أن يشترك فيه اللسان والعقل والقلب فحظ اللسان تصحيح الحروف بالترتيل وحظ العقل تفسير المعاني وحظ القلب الاتعاظ والتأثر بالانزجار والائتمار. فاللسان يرتل والعقل يترجم والقلب يتعظ.
20:126.english: Rather, the one who recites with the tongue while turning away from action is worthy of being what is intended by His saying, the Exalted: 'And whoever turns away from My Remembrance (Dhikr), indeed, for him is a life of hardship, and We will raise him blind on the Day of Resurrection' and by His saying, the Exalted: 'Thus Our signs came to you, and you forgot them; and thus today you are forgotten' meaning you abandoned them and did not look at them and did not care for them. For the one who falls short in the matter, it is said that he forgot the matter and the recitation of the Quran. The true recitation of it is that the tongue, the intellect (Aql), and the heart (Qalb) participate in it: the share of the tongue is correcting the letters with proper recitation (Tartil), the share of the intellect is interpreting the meanings, and the share of the heart is taking admonition and being affected by the warning and the command. So the tongue recites properly, the intellect translates, and the heart takes admonition.
20:126.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

20:129.arabic: ومنها المقدم والمؤخر وهو مظنة الغلط كقوله عز وجل ﴿ ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك لكان لزاما وأجل مسمى ﴾ {} معناه لولا الكلمة وأجل مسمى لكان لزاما ولولاه لكان نصبا كاللزام
20:129.english: And among them is the advanced and delayed [word order], which is a place of error, like His Exalted saying: 'And were it not for a word that had preceded from your Lord, it would have been inevitable and a term appointed' (Quran 20:129). Its meaning is: were it not for the word and the appointed term, it would have been inevitable, and were it not for it, it would have been a punishment like the inevitable.
20:129.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

20:130.arabic: وهو وقت شريف ويدل على شرفه وفضله إقسام الله تعالى به إذ قال: ﴿ والصبح إذا تنفس ﴾ {} وتمدحه به إذ قال: ﴿ فالق الإصباح ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ قل أعوذ برب الفلق ﴾ {} وإظهاره القدرة بقبض الظل فيه إذ قال تعالى: ﴿ ثم قبضناه إلينا قبضا يسيرا ﴾ {} وهو وقت قبض ظل الليل ببسط نور الشمس وإرشاده الناس إلى التسبيح فيه بقوله تعالى: ﴿ فسبحان الله حين تمسون وحين تصبحون ﴾ {} وبقوله تعالى: ﴿ فسبح بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها ﴾ {} وقوله عز وجل: ﴿ ومن آناء الليل فسبح وأطراف النهار لعلك ترضى ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ وا
20:130.english: And it is a noble time, and its nobility and virtue are indicated by Allah the Exalted swearing by it when He said: 'And the dawn when it breathes' and praising it when He said: 'The Cleaver of the daybreak' and Allah the Exalted said: 'Say, "I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak"' and demonstrating His power by the contraction of shadow in it when Allah the Exalted said: 'Then We drew it in to Ourselves a gentle drawing' and it is the time of contracting the shadow of the night by spreading the light of the sun and guiding people to the Glorification (Tasbīḥ) in it by His saying the Exalted: 'So exalt Allah when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning' and by His saying the Exalted: 'So be patient over what they say and glorify (Sabbih) with praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting' and His saying the Mighty and Majestic: 'And [in part] of the night exalt (Fasabbiḥ) Him and at the ends of the day, that you may be satisfied' and His saying the Exalted: 'And remember (Udhkur) the name of your Lord morning and evening'.
20:130.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

20:130.arabic: وإن قرأ المسبعات العشر التي أهداها الخضر عليه السلام إلى إبراهيم التيمي رحمه الله ووصاه أن يقولها غدوة وعشية فقد استكمل الفضل وجمع له ذلك فضيلة جملة الأدعية المذكورة فقد روي عن كرز بن وبرة رحمه الله وكان من الأبدال قال أتاني أخ لي من أهل الشام فأهدى لي هدية وقال يا كرز اقبل مني هذه الهدية فإنها نعمت الهدية فقلت يا أخي ومن أهدى لك هذه الهدية قال أعطانيها إبراهيم التيمي قلت: أفلم تسأل إبراهيم من أعطاه إياها قال: كنت جالسا في فناء الكعبة وأنا في التهليل والتسبيح والتحميد والتمجيد فجاءني رجل فسلم عل
20:130.english: And if one recites the ten sevenfold [prayers] that Al-Khidr (peace be upon him) gifted to Ibrahim Al-Taymi (may Allah have mercy on him) and advised him to say them morning and evening, then he has completed the excellence and gathered for himself the virtue of the entirety of the mentioned supplications. It has been narrated from Kurz ibn Wabrah (may Allah have mercy on him), and he was from the Substitutes (Al-Abdal), he said: 'A brother of mine from the people of Ash-Sham came to me and gifted me a gift and said: O Kurz, accept from me this gift, for it is an excellent gift. I said: O my brother, and who gifted you this gift? He said: Ibrahim Al-Taymi gave it to me. I said: Did you not ask Ibrahim who gave it to him? He said: I was sitting in the courtyard of the Ka'bah while I was in the declaration of the Oneness of Allah (Tahlil), the Glorification (Tasbih), the Praise (Tahmid), and the Magnification (Tamjid) when a man came to me, greeted me, and sat to my right. I have never seen in my time a more beautiful face than his, nor more beautiful clothes, nor more intense whiteness, nor a more pleasant scent than him. I said: O servant of Allah, who are you and from where have you come? He said: I am Al-Khidr. I said: For what have you come to me? He said: I have come to you to greet you and out of love for you for the sake of Allah, and I have a gift I want to gift to you. I said: What is it? He said: That you say before the rising of the sun and before its spreading over the earth and before the setting: Surah Al-Hamd (Al-Fatihah), and 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind' (Surah An-Nas), and 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak' (Surah Al-Falaq), and 'Say: He is Allah, the One' (Surah Al-Ikhlas), and 'Say: O you who disbelieve' (Surah Al-Kafirun), and the Verse of the Throne (Ayat Al-Kursi), each one seven times, and you say: Glory be to Allah (Subhan Allah) and Praise be to Allah (Alhamdulillah) and There is no god but Allah (La ilaha illa Allah) and Allah is the Greatest (Allahu Akbar) seven times, and you send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him) seven times, and you seek forgiveness for yourself and for your parents and for the believing men and for the believing women seven times, and you say: O Allah, do with me and with them, in the immediate and the deferred, in the religion (Ad-Deen) and the worldly life (Ad-Dunya) and the Hereafter (Al-Akhirah), what You are worthy of, and do not do with us, O our Master, what we are worthy of, for You are Forgiving, Forbearing, Generous, Noble, Compassionate, Merciful seven times, and see that you do not leave that morning and evening.' I said: I love that you inform me who gave you this great gift. He said: Muhammad (peace be upon him) gave it to me. I said: Inform me of the reward for that. He said: When you meet Muhammad (peace be upon him), ask him about its reward, for he will inform you of that.'
20:130.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

20:130.arabic: قال الله تعالى: ﴿ للذين أحسنوا الحسنى وزيادة ﴾ {} وهذه الزيادة هى النظر إلى وجه الله تعالى وهى اللذة الكبرى التى ينسى فيها نعيم أهل الجنة وقد ذكرناه حقيقتها فى كتاب المحبة وقد شهد لها الكتاب والسنة على خلاف ما يعتقده أهل البدعة قال جرير بن عبد الله البجلى: (كنا جلوسا عند رسول الله ﭬ فرأى القمر ليلة البدر فقال إنكم ترون ربكم كما ترون القمر لا تضامون فى رؤيته فإن استطعتم أن لا تغلبوا على صلاة قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها فافعلوا ثم قرأ ﴿ وسبح بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها ﴾ {}[256]) وهو مخرج ف
