20:130.english: Allah the Exalted said: 'For those who do good is the best reward and an addition' {} and this addition is the vision of the face of Allah the Exalted, and it is the greatest pleasure in which the bliss of the people of Paradise is forgotten, and we have mentioned its reality in the Book of Love, and the Book and the Sunnah have testified to it contrary to what the people of innovation believe. Jarir ibn 'Abdullah al-Bajali said: (We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he saw the moon on the night of the full moon and said: 'You will see your Lord as you see this moon, you will have no difficulty in seeing Him. So if you are able not to be overcome in prayer before the rising of the sun and before its setting, then do so.' Then he recited: 'And glorify with the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting' {}[256]) and it is reported in the two Sahihs.
20:130.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Book of Repentance'

20:130.arabic: وهي خمسة: الأول: إذا غربت الشمس صلى المغرب واشتغل بإحياء ما بين العشاءين فآخر هذا الورد عند غيبوبة الشفق أعنى الحمرة التي بغيبوبتها يدخل وقت العتمة وقد أقسم الله تعالى به فقال ﴿ فلا أقسم بالشفق ﴾ {} والصلاة فيه هي ناشئة الليل لأنه أول نشوء ساعاته وهو آن من الآناء المذكورة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ومن آناء الليل فسبح ﴾ {} وهي صلاة الأوابين. وهي المراد بقوله تعالى: ﴿ تتجافى جنوبهم عن المضاجع ﴾ {} روى ذلك عن الحسن وأسنده ابن أبي زياد إلى رسول الله ﭬ (أنه سئل عن هذه الآية فقال ﭬ: الصلاة بين العشاءين، ثم قال
20:130.english: They are five: The first: When the sun sets, he prays Maghrib and occupies himself with reviving what is between the two evening prayers (Isha), so the end of this devotional practice (Wird) is at the disappearance of the twilight, meaning the redness whose disappearance marks the entry of the time of the late evening prayer (Atama), and Allah the Exalted has sworn by it, saying: 'So I swear by the twilight' (Quran 89:1) {}, and the prayer in it is the beginning of the night because it is the first emergence of its hours, and it is a time (Anaa) from the times (Anaa) mentioned in the saying of Allah the Exalted: 'And from the times (Anaa) of the night, then glorify' (Quran 20:130) {}, and it is the prayer of the oft-returning ones (Al-Awabeen). It is what is intended by the saying of Allah the Exalted: 'Their sides forsake their beds' (Quran 32:16) {}. That was narrated from Al-Hasan and Ibn Abi Ziyad attributed it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (that he was asked about this verse and he ﷺ said: The prayer between the two evening prayers, then he ﷺ said: Upon you is the prayer between the two evening prayers, for it removes the frivolities (Malaghat) of the day and refines its end [42]). And 'Malaghat' is the plural of 'Malgha' from 'Laghw' (frivolity, idle talk). And Anas, may Allah have mercy on him, was asked about one who sleeps between the two evening prayers, and he said: Do not do it, for it is the hour intended by the saying of Allah the Exalted: 'Their sides forsake their beds' (Quran 32:16) {}. And the virtue of reviving what is between the two evening prayers will come in the second chapter. And the order of this devotional practice (Wird) is that he prays after Maghrib two units (Rak'atain) first, reciting in them 'Say, O disbelievers' (Surah Al-Kafirun) and 'Say, He is Allah, the One' (Surah Al-Ikhlas), and he prays them immediately after Maghrib without interruption of speech or occupation, then he prays four units (Arba'a) prolonging them, then he prays until the disappearance of the twilight what is easy for him, and if the mosque is near the house, then there is no harm in praying them in his house if his intention (Azm) is not to stay in the mosque, and if he intends to stay in waiting for the late evening prayer (Atama), then it is the best if he is safe from affectation (Tasannu') and showing off (Riya). And the second devotional practice (Wird): It begins with the entry of the time of the last evening prayer (Isha) to the limit of people's sleep, and it is the first establishment of darkness, and Allah the Exalted has sworn by it when He said: 'And the night and what it envelops' (Quran 92:1) {} a
20:130.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

20:130.arabic: قال جرير بن عبد الله البجلى: (كنا جلوسا عند رسول الله ﭬ فرأى القمر ليلة البدر فقال إنكم ترون ربكم كما ترون القمر لا تضامون فى رؤيته فإن استطعتم أن لا تغلبوا على صلاة قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها فافعلوا ثم قرأ ﴿ وسبح بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها ﴾ {}) وهو مخرج فى الصحيحين
20:130.english: Jarir ibn Abdullah al-Bajali said: (We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) when he saw the moon on the night of the full moon and said: 'You will see your Lord as you see this moon, without any crowding in seeing Him. So if you are able not to be overcome regarding prayer before the rising of the sun and before its setting, then do so.' Then he recited: 'And glorify with the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting' {}) and this is reported in the two Sahihs.
20:130.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Repentance'

20:131.arabic: وروي أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم مر في أصحابه بعشار من النوق حفل وهي الحوامل وكانت من أحب أموالهم إليهم وأنفسها عندهم لأنها تجمع الظهر واللحم واللبن والوبر، ولعظمها في قلوبهم قال الله تعالى: " وإذا العشار عطلت " قال: فأعرض عنها رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وغض بصره، فقيل له: يا رسول الله هذه أنفس أموالنا لم لا تنظر إليها؟ فقال: " قد نهاني الله عن ذلك " ثم تلا قوله تعالى: " ولا تمدن عينيك إلى ما متعنا به " الآية.
20:131.english: And it was narrated that he (peace be upon him) passed by his companions with a group of ten pregnant camels, and they were among their most beloved possessions and most precious to them because they combine transportation, meat, milk, and wool. Due to their greatness in their hearts, Allah the Exalted said: "And when the ten-month pregnant camels are neglected" (Quran 81:4). He said: So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) turned away from them and lowered his gaze. It was said to him: O Messenger of Allah, these are our most precious possessions, why do you not look at them? He said: "Allah has forbidden me from that." Then he recited His saying: "And do not extend your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to [some] categories of them, [its being but] the splendor of worldly life by which We test them. And the provision of your Lord is better and more enduring." (Quran 20:131).
20:131.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

20:131.arabic: وعن أبي رافع أنه قال: ورد على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ضيف فلم يجد عنده ما يصلحه، فأرسلني إلى رجل من يهود خيبر وقال: " قل له يقول لك محمد أسلفني أو بعني دقيقاً إلى هلال رجب " قال فأتيته فقال: لا والله إلا برهن، فأخبرت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بذلك فقال: " أما والله إني لأمين في أهل السماء أمين في أهل الأرض ولو باعني أو أسلفني لأديت إليه، اذهب بدرعي هذا إليه فارهنه، فلما خرجت نزلت هذه الآية " ولا تمدن عينيك إلى ما متعنا به أزواجاً منهم زهرة الحياة الدنيا" الآية. وهذه الآية تعزية لرسول الل
20:131.english: And from Abu Rafi' that he said: A guest came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and he did not find with him what would be suitable for him, so he sent me to a man from the Jews of Khaybar and said: "Tell him that Muhammad says to you: Lend me or sell me flour until the crescent of Rajab." He said: So I came to him and he said: No, by Allah, except with a pledge. So I informed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) of that, and he said: "By Allah, I am trustworthy (Amin) with the people of the heavens, trustworthy (Amin) with the people of the earth, and if he sold to me or lent to me, I would repay him. Go with this armor of mine to him and pledge it." When I went out, this verse descended: "And do not extend your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to [some] categories of them, [its being but] the splendor (Zahrah) of worldly life by which We test them. And the provision of your Lord is better and more enduring." This verse is a consolation (Ta'ziyah) for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) from the worldly life (Al-Dunya).
20:131.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

20:131.arabic: [14] حديث أبي رافع ورد على رسول الله ﭬ ضيف فلم يجد عنده ما يصلحه فأرسلنى إلى رجل من يهود خيبر الحديث في نزول قوله تعالى - ولا تمدن عينيك إلى ما متعنا به أزواجا منهم - أخرجه الطبرانى بسند ضعيف.
20:131.english: [14] The hadith of Abu Rafi': A guest came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and he did not find with him what would be suitable for him, so he sent me to a man from the Jews of Khaybar. The hadith is about the revelation of His saying, the Exalted: 'And do not extend your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to [some] categories of them.' It was reported by Al-Tabarani with a weak chain.
20:131.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

20:131.arabic: وقال تعالى: " ولا تمدن عينيك إلى ما متعنا به أزواجاً منهم زهرة الحياة الدنيا لنفتنهم فيه ورزق ربك خير وأبقى ". وقال تعالى: " الذين يستحبون الحياة الدنيا على الآخرة " فوصف الكفار بذلك، فمفهومه أن المؤمن هو الذي يتصف بنقيضه وهو أن يستحب الآخرة على الحياة الدنيا.
20:131.english: And He (Exalted is He) said: "And do not extend your eyes toward what We have given enjoyment to some pairs of them - the flower (zahrah) of the worldly life - so that We may test them in it. And the provision (rizq) of your Lord is better and more lasting." And He (Exalted is He) said: "Those who prefer the worldly life over the Hereafter" - so He described the disbelievers with that, so its implication is that the believer is the one who is characterized by its opposite, which is that he prefers the Hereafter over the worldly life.
20:131.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

20:132.arabic: ويروى عن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أنه كان إذا أصاب أهله خصاصة قال: "قوموا إلى الصلاة " ويقول: " بهذا أمرني ربي عز وجل قال عز وجل: " وأمر أهلك بالصلاة واصطبر عليها " الآية.
20:132.english: And it is narrated from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) that when poverty struck his family, he would say: "Rise to the Prayer (Salah)" and say: "With this my Lord commanded me, He (Exalted is He) said: 'And command your family to the Prayer (Salah) and be patient upon it'" the verse.
20:132.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

20:132.arabic: [5]  حديث كان إذا أصاب أهله خصاصة قال قوموا إلى الصلاة ويقول بهذا أمرني ربي قال تعالى - وأمر أهلك بالصلاة واصطبر عليها - رواه الطبراني في الأوسط من حديث محمد بن حمزة عن عبد الله بن سلام قال كان النبي ﭬ إذا نزل بأهله الضيق أمرهم بالالصلاة ثم قرأ هذه الآية ومحمد بن حمزة بن يوسف بن عبد الله بن سلام إنما ذكروا له روايته عن أبيه عن جده فيبعد سماعه من جد أبيه.
20:132.english: Hadith: When poverty (khasāṣah) afflicted his family, he would say: 'Get up for prayer (ṣalāh),' and say: 'With this my Lord has commanded me.' Allah the Exalted said: 'And command your family to prayer (ṣalāh) and be steadfast (iṣṭabir) upon it.' Narrated by Al-Ṭabarānī in Al-Awsaṭ from the ḥadīth of Muḥammad ibn Ḥamzah from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, who said: 'When distress (ḍayq) befell his family, the Prophet (peace be upon him) would command them to prayer (ṣalāh), then recite this verse.' And Muḥammad ibn Ḥamzah ibn Yūsuf ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām—they only mentioned his narration from his father from his grandfather, so it is unlikely he heard it from his grandfather's father.
20:132.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

21:1.arabic: أما تتدبرين قوله تعالى اقترب للناس حسابهم وهم في غفلة معرضون ما يأتيهم من ذكر من ربهم محدث إلا استمعوه وهم يلعبون لاهية قلوبهم ويحك يا نفس إن كانت جراءتك على معصية الله لاعتقادك أن الله لا يراك فما أعظم كفرك وإن كان مع علمك باطلاعه عليك فما أشد وقاحتك وأقل حياءك ويحك يا نفس لو واجهك عبد من عبيدك بل أخ من إخوانك بما تكرهينه كيف كان غضبك عليه ومقتك له فبأى جسارة تتعرضين لمقت الله وغضبه وشديد عقابه أفتظنين أنك تطيقين عذابه هيهات هيهات جربى نفسك إن ألهاك البطر عن أليم عذابه فاحتبسى ساعة في الشمس أو
21:1.english: Do you not contemplate His saying, the Exalted: 'The accounting of the people has drawn near while they are in heedlessness, turning away. No new Remembrance (Dhikr) comes to them from their Lord except they listen to it while they play, their Hearts (Qalb) distracted.' And woe to you, O Soul (Nafs)! If your boldness in disobeying Allah is due to your belief that Allah does not see you, then how great is your disbelief (Kufr)! And if it is with your knowledge of His awareness of you, then how severe is your insolence and how little your shame! Woe to you, O Soul (Nafs)! If a slave from your slaves, or rather a brother from your brothers, confronted you with what you dislike, how would your anger be upon him and your hatred for him? So with what audacity do you expose yourself to the hatred of Allah, His anger, and His severe punishment? Do you think you can bear His punishment? Far from it, far from it! Test yourself: if heedlessness distracts you from His painful punishment, then confine yourself for an hour in the sun, or in the bathhouse, or bring your finger near the fire to make clear the extent of your capacity. Are you deluded by the generosity of Allah and His bounty and His independence from your obedience and worship? So why do you not rely on the generosity of Allah, the Exalted, in the affairs of your worldly life? If an enemy intends you, why do you not devise means to repel him, nor entrust him to the generosity of Allah, the Exalted? And if a need for a desire from the desires of the worldly life, which does not end except with the dinar and dirham, overwhelms you, why do you exert the Spirit (Ruh) in seeking it and obtaining it through various means, not relying on the generosity of Allah, the Exalted, until He causes you to stumble upon a treasure or subjugates a slave from His slaves to carry your need to you without effort or seeking from you? Do you reckon that Allah is generous in the Hereafter but not in the worldly life? And you have known that the way of Allah has no change, and that the Lord of the Hereafter and the worldly life is One (Tawhid).
21:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

21:1.arabic: وكان داخلا في معنى قوله عز وجل ﴿ ومنهم أميون لا يعلمون الكتاب إلا أمانيّ ﴾ {} يعني التلاوة المجردة وقوله عز وجل ﴿ وكأين من آية في السموات والأرض يمرون عليها وهم عنها معرضون ﴾ {} لأن القرآن هو المبين لتلك الآيات في السموات والأرض ومهما تجاوزها ولم يتأثر بها كان معرضا عنها ولذلك قيل: إن من لم يكن متصفا بأخلاق القرآن فإذا قرأ القرآن ناداه الله تعالى: مالك ولكلامي وأنت معرض عني دع عنك كلامي إن لم تتب إلي. ومثال العاصي إذا قرأ القرآن وكرره مثال من يكرر كتاب الملك في كل يوم مرات وقد كتب إليه في عمارة
21:1.english: And he was included in the meaning of His Mighty and Majestic saying: 'And among them are unlettered ones who do not know the Book except [mere] wishes' meaning mere recitation, and His Mighty and Majestic saying: 'And how many a sign in the heavens and earth they pass over while they are turning away from it' because the Quran is the clarifier of those signs in the heavens and the earth, and whenever he passes over them and is not affected by them, he is turning away from them. Therefore, it is said: Indeed, whoever is not characterized by the morals of the Quran, then when he recites the Quran, Allah the Exalted calls to him: What is your affair with My speech while you are turning away from Me? Leave My speech if you do not repent to Me. And the example of the disobedient one when he recites the Quran and repeats it is like one who repeats the book of the king every day multiple times, while it has been written to him concerning the building of his kingdom, yet he is busy destroying it and restricts himself to studying his book. Perhaps if he left the study at the time of transgression, he would be farther from mockery and deserving of hatred. Therefore, Yusuf ibn Asbat said: Indeed, I intend to recite the Quran, but when I remember what is in it, I fear hatred, so I turn to glorification and seeking forgiveness. And the one turning away from acting upon it is intended by His Mighty and Majestic saying: 'So they threw it behind their backs and purchased with it a small price, so wretched...'
21:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

21:1.arabic: فقد قرب لما بعد الموت الرحيل فما بقي من العمر إلا القليل والخلق عنه غافلون ﴿ اقترب للناس حسابهم وهم في غفلة معرضون ﴾ {} ونحن نذكر ما يتعلق بالموت في شطرين:
21:1.english: Indeed, the departure for what is after death has drawn near, and what remains of life is but little, and the creation is heedless of it. 'The reckoning for the people has drawn near, while they are in heedlessness, turning away.' And we mention what pertains to death in two parts:
21:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

21:1.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا الْإِنْسَانُ مَا غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ الْكَرِيمِ حَيْثُ أُغْلِقَتِ الْأَبْوَابُ وَأُرْخِيَتِ السُّتُورُ وَاسْتَتَرْتَ عَنِ الْخَلَائِقِ فَقَارَفْتَ الْفُجُورَ فَمَاذَا تَفْعَلُ وَقَدْ شَهِدَتْ عَلَيْكَ جَوَارِحُكَ فَالْوَيْلُ كُلُّ الْوَيْلِ لَنَا مَعْشَرَ الْغَافِلِينَ يُرْسِلُ اللَّهُ لَنَا سَيِّدَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ وَيُنْزِلُ عَلَيْهِ الْكِتَابَ الْمُبِينَ وَيُخْبِرُنَا بِهَذِهِ الصِّفَاتِ مِنْ نُعُوتِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ ثُمَّ يُعَرِّفُنَا غَفْلَتَنَا وَيَقُولُ: ﴿ اقْتَرَبَ لِلنَّاسِ حِسَ
21:1.english: O human being, what has deceived you concerning your Generous Lord (Rabb) when the doors were closed and the curtains were lowered and you concealed yourself from the creatures, so you committed immorality? So what will you do when your limbs have testified against you? So woe, all woe to us, the community of the heedless ones (al-ghāfilīn). Allah sends to us the master of the messengers and reveals to him the Clear Book (al-Kitāb al-Mubīn) and informs us of these attributes from the descriptions of the Day of Recompense (Yawm al-Dīn). Then He makes us aware of our heedlessness (ghafla) and says: 'The reckoning for the people has drawn near, while they are in heedlessness (ghafla), turning away.' Then He makes us aware of the nearness of the Hour (al-Sāʿa) and says: 'The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split. Indeed, they see it as distant, but We see it as near.' 'And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near.' Then the best of our states is that we take the study of this Qur'an as an action, so we do not ponder its meanings, nor do we look at the multitude of descriptions and names of this Day, nor do we prepare to escape from its calamities. So we seek refuge in Allah from this heedlessness (ghafla) if Allah does not reach us with His vast mercy.
21:1.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Book of Repentance'

21:7.arabic: فإن قلت فقد قال الله تعالى: (فاسألوا أهل الذكر إن كنتم لا تعلمون( (النحل: 43). فالسؤال مأمور به فاعلم أنه كذلك ولكن فيما يأذن المعلم في السؤال عنه فإن السؤال عما لم تبلغ مرتبتك إلى فهمه مذموم ولذلك منع الخضر موسى عليه السلام من السؤال أي دع السؤال قبل أوانه فالمعلم أعلم بما أنت أهل له وبأوان الكشف وما لم يدخل أوان الكشف في كل درجة من مراقي الدرجات لا يدخل أوان السؤال عنه
21:7.english: If you say: Indeed Allah the Exalted has said: 'So ask the people of the Remembrance (Dhikr) if you do not know' (16:43). So asking is commanded. Know that it is indeed so, but only regarding what the teacher permits you to ask about. For asking about what your rank has not reached to understand is blameworthy. And for that reason, Al-Khidr prevented Moses, peace be upon them, from asking—meaning, leave the question before its proper time. For the teacher knows better what you are worthy of and the time of unveiling (Kashf). And what has not entered the time of unveiling in every degree of the ascending degrees, does not enter the time of questioning about it.
21:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

21:7.arabic: وأعظم نعمة الله على عباده هو العلم وكشف الحق والإيمان عبارة عن نوع كشف وعلم ولذلك قال تعالى امتنانا على عبده وكان فضل الله عليك عظيما وأراد به العلم وقال تعالى فاسألوا أهل الذكر إن كنتم لا تعلمون وقال تعالى إن علينا للهدى وقال ثم إن علينا بيانه وقال وعلى الله قصد السبيل
21:7.english: And the greatest blessing of Allah upon His servants is knowledge and the unveiling of truth, and faith is an expression of a type of unveiling and knowledge. Therefore, Allah said, as a favor upon His servant: 'And great is the favor of Allah upon you' (Quran 4:113), and He intended by it knowledge. And He said: 'So ask the people of the Remembrance (Dhikr) if you do not know' (Quran 21:7). And He said: 'Indeed, upon Us is guidance' (Quran 92:12). And He said: 'Then indeed, upon Us is its explanation' (Quran 75:19). And He said: 'And upon Allah is the direction of the path' (Quran 16:9).
21:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

21:7.arabic: والمقصود أن من قصد الخير بمعصية عن جهل فهو غير معذور إلا إذا كان قريب العهد بالإسلام ولم يجد بعد مهلة للتعلم وقد قال الله سبحانه فاسئلوا أهل الذكر إن كنتم لا تعلمون وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم (لا يعذر الجاهل على الجهل ولا يحل للجاهل أن يسكت على جهله ولا للعالم أن يسكت على علمه)[24]
21:7.english: The intended meaning is that whoever intends good through disobedience (ma'siyah) out of ignorance (jahl) is not excused except if he is newly converted to Islam and has not yet found an opportunity for learning. And Allah the Exalted has said: 'So ask the people of the Remembrance (Dhikr) if you do not know.' And the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'The ignorant one (al-jahil) is not excused for his ignorance, nor is it permissible for the ignorant one to remain silent about his ignorance, nor for the knowledgeable one to remain silent about his knowledge.'
21:7.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

21:7.arabic: وأما الآيات فقوله تعالى: ﴿فلولا نفر من كل فرقة منهم طائفة ليتفقهوا في الدين﴾ (سورة التوبة: الآية 122) وقوله عز وجل ﴿فاسألوا أهل الذكر إن كنتم لا تعلمون﴾ (سورة النحل: الآية 43، وسورة الأنبياء: الآية 7)
21:7.english: As for the verses, there is His saying, the Exalted: 'Why does not a group from every faction among them go forth to gain understanding in the religion?' (Surah At-Tawbah: Verse 122) and His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'So ask the people of the Remembrance (Dhikr) if you do not know.' (Surah An-Nahl: Verse 43, and Surah Al-Anbiya': Verse 7)
21:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

21:10.arabic: ولذلك قال تعالى ﴿ ما نثبت به فؤادك ﴾ {} فليقدر العبد أن الله ثبت فؤاده بما يقصه عليه من أحوال الأنبياء وصبرهم على الإيذاء وثباتهم في الدين لانتظار نصر الله تعالى وكيف لا يقدر هذا والقرآن ما أنزل على رسول الله ﭬ لرسول الله خاصة بل هو شفاء وهدى ورحمة ونور للعالمين ولذلك أمر الله تعالى الكافة بشكر نعمة الكتاب فقال تعالى ﴿ واذكروا نعمة الله عليكم وما أنزل عليكم من الكتاب والحكمة يعظكم به ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل ﴿ لقد أنزلنا إليكم كتابا فيه ذكركم أفلا تعقلون. وأنزلنا إليك الذكر لتبين للناس ما نزل إليهم. كذل
21:10.english: And therefore, Allah the Exalted said: 'What We strengthen with it your heart (Fūād)' {} So let the servant (ʿAbd) consider that Allah strengthened his heart (Fūād) with what He narrates to him of the conditions of the prophets and their patience upon harm and their steadfastness in the religion (Dīn) in anticipation of the victory of Allah the Exalted. And how can he not consider this when the Quran was not sent down upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for the Messenger of Allah specifically, but it is a healing (Shifāʾ) and guidance (Hudā) and mercy (Raḥmah) and light (Nūr) for the worlds. And therefore, Allah the Exalted commanded the entirety to be grateful for the blessing of the Book, so He the Exalted said: 'And remember the blessing of Allah upon you and what He sent down upon you of the Book and the wisdom He admonishes you with' {} And He the Mighty and Majestic said: 'Certainly, We have sent down to you a Book in which is your Remembrance (Dhikr). Then do you not reason? And We have sent down to you the Remembrance (Dhikr) that you may make clear to the people what was sent down to them. Thus does Allah strike for the people their examples. And follow the best of what was sent down to you from your Lord. This is insights for the people and guidance (Hudā) and mercy (Raḥmah) for a people who are certain. This is a clarification for the people and guidance (Hudā) and admonition (Mawʿiẓah) for the God-fearing (Muttaqīn).' {} And if the address is intended for all people, then the individuals are intended, so this single reader is intended, so what is for him and for the rest of the people, let him consider that he is the intended one. Allah the Exalted said: 'And it was revealed to me this Quran that I may warn you thereby and whoever it reaches' {} Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī said: Whoever the Quran reaches him, it is as if Allah spoke to him. And if he considers that, he does not take studying the Quran as his work, but he reads it as the servant (ʿAbd) reads the book of his master (Mawlā) which he wrote to him to contemplate it and act according to its requirement.
21:10.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

21:18.arabic: وقال ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه: أنزل القرآن ليعمل به فاتخذتم دراسته عملا وسيأتي قوم يثقفونه مثل القناة ليسوا بخياركم والعالم الذي لا يعمل كالمريض الذي يصف الدواء وكالجائع الذي يصف لذائذ الأطعمة ولا يجدها وفي مثله قوله تعالى: (ولكم الويل مما تصفون( (الأنبياء: 18). وفي الخبر: (( إنما أخاف على أمتي زلة عالم وجدال منافق في القرآن))[163].
21:18.english: And Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Quran was revealed to be acted upon, but you have taken its study as action. And there will come a people who will master it like a spear, but they are not the best of you. And the scholar who does not act is like the sick person who describes medicine, and like the hungry person who describes the delights of foods but does not find them. And in its likeness is His saying, the Exalted: 'And woe to you for what you describe' (Al-Anbiya: 18). And in the report: 'Indeed, I fear for my nation the slip of a scholar and the argumentation of a hypocrite regarding the Quran.'
21:18.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Book of Knowledge'

21:19.arabic: وما رزق تعالى الملائكة من القرب والرتبة لازم مستمر على حال واحد لا يزيد ولا ينقص لذلك أخبر الله عنهم أنهم قالوا: وما منا إلا له مقام معلوم، وفارق الإنسان الملائكة في الترقي من درجة إلى درجة فإنه لا يزال يتقرب إلى الله تعالى فيستفيد مزيد قربه وباب المزيد مسدود على الملائكة عليهم السلام وليس لكل واحد إلا رتبته التي هي وقف عليه وعبادته التي هو مشغول بها لا ينتقل إلى غيرها ولا يفتر عنها لا يستكبرون عن عبادته ولا يستحسرون يسبحون الليل والنهار لا يفترون ومفتاح مزيد الدرجات هي الصلوات.
21:19.english: And what Allah the Exalted has granted the angels of nearness (Qurb) and rank (Rutbah) is necessary, continuous, and in a single state that does not increase nor decrease. Therefore, Allah informed about them that they said: 'And there is none among us except that he has a known station.' And the human differs from the angels in ascending from one degree (Darajah) to another, for he continually draws near to Allah the Exalted and benefits from increased nearness (Mazīd Qurb), and the door of increase (Bāb al-Mazīd) is closed upon the angels, peace be upon them. And for each one there is only his rank (Rutbah) which is fixed upon him and his worship (ʿIbādah) which he is occupied with; he does not transfer to other than it nor does he cease from it. They do not grow arrogant (lā yastakbirūna) from worshipping Him, nor do they grow weary (lā yastaḥsirūna). They glorify night and day without ceasing. And the key to increased degrees (Mazīd al-Darajāt) is the prayers (Ṣalawāt).
21:19.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

21:20.arabic: وقد وصف الله تعالى الملائكة عليهم السلام مع تقدسهم عن الذنوب ومواظبتهم على العبادات على الدءوب بالإشفاق فقال تعالى مخبراً عنهم "يُسَبِّحُونَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ لَا يَفْتُرُونَ وهم من خشيته مشفقون" فمتى زال الإشفاق والحذر مما سبق به القضاء في الأزل - وينكشف عند خاتمة الأجل - غلب الأمن من مكر الله وذلك يوجب الكبر وهو سبب الهلاك.
21:20.english: And Allah the Exalted has described the angels, peace be upon them, with their sanctity from sins and their persistence in acts of worship (Ibadat) continuously, with apprehension (Ishfaq), so He the Exalted said, informing about them: "They glorify (Yusabbihuna) the night and the day, they do not cease (La Yafturuna), and they are from fear (Khashya) of Him apprehensive (Mushfiqun)." So when the apprehension (Ishfaq) and caution from what has preceded in the decree (Qada) in eternity (Al-Azal) - and is revealed at the conclusion of the term (Ajal) - is removed, security (Al-Amn) from the deception (Makr) of Allah prevails, and that necessitates arrogance (Kibr), which is the cause of destruction.
21:20.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

21:20.arabic: بل هم مجبولون على الطاعة ضي الله عنه ضي الله عنه عليه السلام ضي الله عنه ضي الله عنه ضي الله عنه لا مجال للمعصية في حقهم فلا جرم لا يعصون الله ما أمرهم ويفعلون ما يؤمرون ويسبحون الليل والنهار لا يفترون والراكع منهم راكع أبدا والساجد منهم ساجد أبدا والقائم قائم أبدا لا اختلاف في أفعالهم ولا فتور ولكل واحد مقام معلوم لا يتعداه وطاعتهم لله تعالى من حيث لا مجال للمخالفة فيهم يمكن أن تشبه بطاعة أطرافك لك، فإنك مهما جزمت الإرادة بفتح الأجفان لم يكن للجفن الصحيح تردد واختلاف في طاعتك مرة ومعصيتك أخرى ب
21:20.english: Rather, they are created upon obedience (Taa'ah) - may Allah be pleased with him, may Allah be pleased with him, peace be upon him, may Allah be pleased with him, may Allah be pleased with him, may Allah be pleased with him - there is no possibility for disobedience (Ma'siyah) in their case, so certainly they do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded, and they glorify (Yusabbihuna) the night and the day without ceasing (La Yafturuna). And the one bowing (Raki') among them is bowing forever, and the one prostrating (Sajid) among them is prostrating forever, and the one standing (Qa'im) is standing forever - there is no difference in their actions and no cessation. And for each one is a known station (Maqam) which he does not exceed, and their obedience (Taa'ah) to Allah the Exalted, from where there is no possibility for opposition in them, can be likened to the obedience of your limbs to you. For whenever you resolve the will (Iradah) to open the eyelids, there is no hesitation or difference for the sound eyelid in obeying you once and disobeying you another time; rather, it is as if it awaits your command and prohibition, opening and closing continuously at your signal. This resembles it from one aspect but differs from another aspect, since the eyelid has no knowledge of what issues from it of movement, opening and closing, while the angels are living beings (Ahya') who know (Alimun) what they do.
21:20.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

21:20.arabic: ومما يكره: التظاهر بالحب، بسبب أن المحب إن كان عارفاً - وعرف أحوال الملائكة في حبهم الدائم وشوقهم اللازم الذي به يسبحون الليل والنهار لا يفترون ولا يعصون الله ما أمرهم ويفعلون ما يؤمرون - لاستنكف من نفسه ومن إظهار حبه وعلم قطعاً أنه من أخس المحبين في مملكته وأن حبه أنقص من حب كل محب لله.
21:20.english: And from what is disliked: the ostentation of love, because if the lover is a knower - and knows the states of the angels in their perpetual love and their necessary longing by which they glorify the night and the day, they do not cease and they do not disobey Allah what He commands them and they do what they are commanded - he would disdain from himself and from showing his love and know with certainty that he is from the most base of lovers in His kingdom and that his love is less than the love of every lover for Allah.
21:20.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

21:22.arabic: فإن في عالم الشهادة أيضاً توحيداً، إذ يعلم كل أحد أن المنزل يفسد بصاحبين، والبلد يفسد بأميرين، فيقال له على حد عقله إله العالم واحد والمدبر واحد، إذ لو كان فيهما آلهة إلا الله لفسدتا، فيكون ذلك على ذوق ما رآه في عالم الشهادة، فينغرس اعتقاد التوحيد في قلبه بهذا الطريق اللائق بقدر عقله، وقد كلف الله الأنبياء أن يكلموا الناس على قدر عقولهم، ولذلك نزل القرآن بلسان العرب على حد عادتهم في المحاورة.
21:22.english: For in the world of testimony (Shahadah) there is also Oneness (Tawhid), since everyone knows that a house is corrupted by two owners, and a city is corrupted by two rulers. So it is said to him according to the limit of his intellect: The God (Ilah) of the world is one and the Manager (Mudabbir) is one, since if there were in them gods except Allah, they would have been corrupted. So that becomes according to the taste (Dhawq) of what he has seen in the world of testimony (Shahadah), and the belief (I'tiqad) in Oneness (Tawhid) becomes implanted in his heart (Qalb) by this path suitable to the measure of his intellect. And Allah has charged the Prophets to speak to people according to the measure of their intellects, and for that reason the Quran was revealed in the tongue of the Arabs according to the limit of their custom in discourse.
21:22.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

21:22.arabic: الأصل العاشر: العلم بأن الله عز وجل واحد لا شريك له فرد لا ند له انفرد بالخلق والإبداع واستند بالإيجاد والاختراع لا مثل له يساهمه ويساويه ولا ضد له فينازعه ويناويه وبرهانه قوله تعالى لو كان فيهما آلهة إلا الله لفسدتا وبيانه أنه لو كانا اثنين وأراد أحدهما أمرا فالثاني إن كان مضطرا إلى مساعدته كان هذا الثاني مقهورا عاجزا ولم يكن إلها قادرا وإن كان قادرا على مخالفته ومدافعته كان الثاني قويا قاهرا والأول ضعيفا قاصرا ولم يكن إلها قادرا.
21:22.english: The Tenth Foundation: The knowledge that Allah (Exalted and Glorified is He) is One, without partner, Unique without equal, Who alone created and originated, and relied upon bringing into existence and inventing, with none like Him to share with Him and equal Him, and no opponent to contend with Him and oppose Him. And its proof is His statement (Exalted is He): 'If there were in them (the heavens and the earth) gods besides Allah, they would have been corrupted.' And its explanation is that if there were two, and one of them willed a matter, then the second: if he were compelled to assist him, this second would be overpowered and incapable, and would not be a god capable; and if he were capable of opposing him and resisting him, the second would be strong and overpowering, and the first weak and deficient, and would not be a god capable.
21:22.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Foundations of Belief'

21:22.arabic: وعلى الجملة فالقرآن من أوله إلى آخره محاجة مع الكفار فعمده أدلة المتكلمين في التوحيد قوله تعالى لو كان فيهما آلهة إلا الله لفسدتا وفي النبوة وإن كنتم في ريب مما نزلنا على عبدنا فأتوا بسورة من مثله وفي البعث قل يحييها الذي أنشأها أول مرة إلى غير ذلك من الآيات والأدلة ولم تزل الرسل صلوات الله عليهم يحاجون المنكرين ويجادلونهم قال تعالى: ﴿ وجادلهم بالتي هي أحسن ﴾ {} فالصحابة رضي الله عنهم أيضا كانوا يحاجون المنكرين ويجادلون ولكن عند الحاجة وكانت الحاجة إليه قليلة في زمانهم
21:22.english: And in summary, the Quran from its beginning to its end is an argumentation with the disbelievers, so the foundation of the theologians' proofs in Divine Oneness (Tawhid) is His saying, the Exalted: 'If there were in them (the heavens and earth) gods other than Allah, they would have been corrupted.' And in prophethood: 'And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant, then bring a surah like it.' And in resurrection: 'Say: He gives them life Who created them the first time.' To other than that of the verses and proofs. And the messengers, prayers of Allah upon them, have not ceased arguing with the deniers and debating them. He, the Exalted, said: 'And argue with them in that which is best.' So the companions, may Allah be pleased with them, also used to argue with the deniers and debate, but when needed, and the need for it was little in their time.
21:22.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

21:22.arabic: ولا نظام إلا في الوحدة ولا فساد إلا في الكثرة وإنما انتظم أمر العالم لأن مدبر الكل واحد لو كان فيهما آلهة إلا الله لفسدتا ومهما كان المدبر واحدا انتظم أمر التدبير وإذا كثر المدبرون فسدت الأمور في الحضر والسفر
21:22.english: And there is no order except in unity (al-wahdah), and no corruption (al-fasad) except in multiplicity. And indeed, the affair of the world has become orderly because the Manager (al-mudabbir) of all is One: 'If there were in them (the heavens and earth) gods (alihah) other than Allah, they would have been corrupted (lafasadata).' And whenever the Manager (al-mudabbir) is one, the affair of management (al-tadbir) becomes orderly; and when the managers (al-mudabbirun) become many, affairs become corrupted (fasadat) in both residence and travel.
21:22.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Etiquette of Travel'

21:23.arabic: فتعالى الله الملك الحق لا يسئل عما يفعل وهم يسئلون ولنقتصر على هذا القدر اليسير من ذكر عجائب القلب فإن استقصاءه لا يليق بعلم المعاملة وإنما ذكرنا منه ما يحتاج إليه لمعرفة أغوار علوم المعاملة وأسرارها لينتفع بها من لا يقنع بالظواهر ولا يجتزئ بالقشر عن اللباب بل يتشوق إلى معرفة دقائق حقائق الأسباب وفيما ذكرناه كفاية له ومقنع إن شاء الله تعالى والله ولي التوفيق تم كتاب عجائب القلب ولله الحمد والمنة ويتلوه كتاب رياضة النفس وتهذيب الأخلاق والحمد لله وحده وصلى الله على كل عبد مصطفى.
21:23.english: So exalted is Allah, the True King, He is not questioned about what He does, and they are questioned. And we will limit ourselves to this small amount of mentioning the wonders of the Heart (Qalb), for its exhaustive treatment is not fitting for the science of spiritual practice (Mu'amalah). Rather, we have mentioned from it what is needed for knowing the depths of the sciences of spiritual practice (Mu'amalah) and their secrets, so that those who are not satisfied with appearances and do not content themselves with the shell instead of the core (Lubab) may benefit from it, but rather yearn to know the subtleties of the realities of causes. In what we have mentioned, there is sufficiency for him and satisfaction, if Allah wills. And Allah is the Guardian of success. Completed is the book of the wonders of the Heart (Qalb), and praise and favor are to Allah. And following it is the book of disciplining the Soul (Nafs) and refining the character traits. And praise is to Allah alone, and may Allah bless every chosen servant.
21:23.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

21:23.arabic: الأصل الثالث: أن فعل العبد وإن كان كسبا للعبد فلا يخرج عن كونه مرادا لله سبحانه فلا يجري في الملك والملكوت طرفة عين ولا لفتة خاطر ولا فلتة ناظر إلا بقضاء الله وقدرته وبإرادته ومشيئته ومنه الشر والخير والنفع والضر والإسلام والكفر والعرفان والنكر والفوز والخسران والغواية والرشد والطاعة والعصيان والشرك والإيمان لا راد لقضائه ولا معقب لحكمه يضل من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء لا يسئل عما يفعل وهم يسألون ويدل عليه من النقل قول الأمة قاطبة ما شاء كان وما لم يشأ لم يكن وقول الله عز وجل أن لو يشاء الله لهدى الناس
21:23.english: The Third Foundation: That the action of the servant, even though it is an acquisition (kasb) for the servant, does not depart from being willed by Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He. Thus, not a blink of an eye, nor a turn of thought, nor a glance of sight occurs in the dominion (al-mulk) and the kingdom (al-malakūt) except by the decree (qadā') of Allah and His power (qudrah) and by His will (irādah) and His volition (mashī'ah). From it [comes] evil and good, benefit and harm, submission (al-Islām) and disbelief (al-kufr), recognition (al-'irfān) and denial (al-nukr), success (al-fawz) and loss (al-khusrān), misguidance (al-ghawāyah) and right guidance (al-rushd), obedience (al-ṭā'ah) and disobedience (al-'iṣyān), polytheism (al-shirk) and faith (al-īmān). There is no averter of His decree, nor any repealer of His judgment. He misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills. He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned. Evidence for this from transmission (al-naql) is the statement of the entire community: 'What He wills occurs, and what He does not will does not occur,' and the statement of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He: 'If Allah had willed, He would have guided all the people,' and His statement, Exalted is He: 'And if We had willed, We could have given every soul its guidance.' Evidence for this from the perspective of intellect (al-'aql) is that if sins (al-ma'āṣī) and crimes (al-jarā'im) were such that Allah dislikes them and does not will them, and they only occur in accordance with the will of the enemy, Iblīs—may Allah curse him—even though he is an enemy to Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, and what occurs in accordance with the will of the enemy is more than what occurs in accordance with His will, Exalted is He, then I wonder how a Muslim permits himself to reduce the dominion of the Compeller (al-Jabbār), Possessor of Majesty and Honor, to a rank that, if the leadership of a village chief were reduced to it, he would disdain it. For if what continues for the enemy of the chief in the village were more than what is established for him, he would disdain his leadership and disavow his authority. Disobedience (al-ma'ṣiyah) is what predominates over creation, and all of that, according to the innovators (al-mubtadi'ah), occurs contrary to the will of the Truth, Exalted is He. This is the utmost weakness and incapacity—Exalted is the Lord of lords above what the wrongdoers say, greatly exalted. Then, whenever it becomes clear that the actions of the servants are created by Allah, it is correct that they are willed by Him. If it is said: 'How does He prohibit what He wills and command what He does not will?' We say: Command (al-amr) is different from will (al-irādah). Therefore, when a master strikes his servant and the ruler reproaches him for it, and he excuses himself by the rebellion of his servant against him, and the ruler disbelieves him, he wanted to manifest his proof by commanding the...
21:23.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

21:23.arabic: وعند هذا كاد أن يزيغ ويطلق بالجراءة لسان السؤال، فثبت بالقول الثابت ونودي من وراء حجاب سرادقات الحضرة "لا يسأل عما يفعل وهم يسألون" فغشيته هيبة الحضرة، فخر صعقاً يضطرب في غشيته، فلما أفاق قال: سبحانك ما أعظم شأنك تبت إليك وتوكلت عليك وآمنت بأنك الملك الجبار الواحد القهار، فلا أخاف غيرك ولا أرجو سواك ولا أعوذ إلا بعفوك من عقابك وبرضاك من سخطك، وما لي إلا أن أسألك وأتضرع إليك وأبتهل بين يديك، فأقول: اشرح لي صدري لأعرفك واحلل عقدة من لساني لأثني عليك، فنودي من وراء الحجاب: إياك أن تطمع في الثناء وت
21:23.english: And at this point, he nearly deviated and unleashed his tongue with audacity in questioning, but he was steadied by the firm statement and was called from behind the veil of the pavilions of the Presence (al-Hadrah): "He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned." Then the awe of the Presence (al-Hadrah) overwhelmed him, and he fell unconscious, trembling in his swoon. When he regained consciousness, he said: Glory be to You, how great is Your affair! I repent to You, rely on You, and believe that You are the Compelling King (al-Malik al-Jabbar), the One, the Subduer (al-Qahhar). So I fear none but You, hope for none but You, and seek refuge only in Your pardon from Your punishment and in Your pleasure from Your wrath. I have nothing except to ask You, supplicate to You, and implore before You, so I say: Expand my chest (sadr) to know You and untie a knot from my tongue to praise You. Then he was called from behind the veil: Beware of aspiring to praise and exceeding the Master of the Prophets (Sayyid al-Anbiya). Rather, return to him, for whatever he gives you, take it; whatever he forbids you from, abstain from it; and whatever he says to you, say it. For he did not increase in this Presence (al-Hadrah) beyond saying: "Glory be to You, I cannot enumerate praise upon You; You are as You have praised Yourself."
21:23.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

21:23.arabic: الأصل السابع: أنه تعالى يفعل بعباده ما يشاء فلا يجب عليه رعاية الأصلح لعباده لما ذكرناه من أنه لا يجب عليه سبحانه شيء بل لا يعقل في حقه الوجوب فإنه لا يسأل عما يفعل وهم يسألون وليت شعري بما يجيب المعتزلي في قوله إن الأصلح واجب عليه في مسألة نعرضها عليه وهو أن يفرض مناظرة في الآخرة بين صبي وبين بالغ ماتا مسلمين فإن الله سبحانه يزيد في درجات البالغ ويفضله على الصبي لأنه تعب بالإيمان والطاعات بعد البلوغ ويجب عليه ذلك عند المعتزلي فلو قال الصبي يا رب لم رفعت منزلته علي فيقول لأنه بلغ واجتهد في الطاع
21:23.english: The Seventh Foundation: That He, the Exalted, does with His servants what He wills, so it is not obligatory upon Him to observe what is most beneficial for His servants, due to what we have mentioned that nothing is obligatory upon Him, the Glorified, rather obligation is inconceivable in His regard. For He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned. And I wonder how the Mu'tazilite would answer in his claim that what is most beneficial is obligatory upon Him in a matter we present to him, which is to suppose a debate in the Hereafter between a child and an adult who both died as Muslims. For Allah, the Glorified, increases the degrees of the adult and favors him over the child because he toiled in faith and acts of obedience after puberty, and this is obligatory upon Him according to the Mu'tazilite. So if the child says: 'O Lord, why have You elevated his station above mine?' He would say: 'Because he reached puberty and strove in acts of obedience.' And the child says: 'You caused me to die in childhood, so it was obligatory upon You to prolong my life until I reached puberty so I could strive.' You have deviated from justice in favoring him with long life to my exclusion, so why have You favored him? Allah, the Exalted, says: 'Because I knew that if you had reached puberty, you would have associated partners or disobeyed, so what was most beneficial for you was death in childhood.' This is the Mu'tazilite's excuse for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. And at this, the disbelievers call from the depths of Hellfire and say: 'O Lord, did You not know that if we had reached puberty we would have associated partners? Why did You not cause us to die in childhood? For we would have been content with less than the station of the Muslim child.' With what can this be answered? And is it not necessary at this point except to affirm that divine matters are exalted by the decree of Majesty from being weighed with the scale of the people of Mu'tazila? If it is said: 'Whenever He is able to observe what is most beneficial for the servants, then He subjects them to causes of punishment, that would be ugliness unbecoming of wisdom.' We say: Ugliness is what does not conform.
21:23.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

21:23.arabic: فكان لفظ القضاء بإزاء الآمر الواحد الكلى ولفظ القدر بإزاء التفصيل المتمادى إلى غير نهاية وقيل إن شيئا من ذلك ليس خارجا عن القضاء والقدر فخطر لبعض العباد أن القسمة لماذا اقتضت هذا التفصيل وكيف انتظم العدل مع هذا التفاوت والتفضيل وكان بعضهم لقصوره لا يطيق ملاحظة كنه هذا الأمر والاحتواء على مجامعه فألجموا عما لم يطيقوا خوض غمرته بلجام المنع وقيل لهم اسكنوا فما لهذا خلقتم لا يسئل عما يفعل وهم يسئلون وامتلأت مشكاة بعضهم نورا مقتبسا من نور الله تعالى في السموات والأرض وكان زيتهم أولا صافيا يكاد يضىء و
21:23.english: So the term 'Decree (Qada)' corresponds to the single universal command, and the term 'Divine Measure (Qadar)' corresponds to the detailed specification extending without end. And it is said that nothing of that is outside of the Decree (Qada) and the Divine Measure (Qadar). Then it occurred to some servants (عباد) why the apportionment necessitated this detailed specification and how justice was organized with this disparity and preferential treatment. And some of them, due to their deficiency, could not bear to observe the reality (كنه) of this matter and encompass its totality, so they were restrained from what they could not bear to plunge into its depth by the bridle of prohibition. And it was said to them: 'Be still, for you were not created for this. He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned.' And the niche (مشكاة) of some of them was filled with light (نور) taken from the light (نور) of Allah, the Exalted, in the heavens and the earth. And their oil was at first pure, almost giving light even if no fire touched it. Then fire touched it, and it blazed with light upon light. Then the regions of the Dominion (الملكوت) shone before them with the light (نور) of their Lord, so they comprehended all matters as they truly are. Then it was said to them: 'Adorn yourselves with the manners (آداب) of Allah, the Exalted, and be still. And when the Divine Measure (القدر) is mentioned, hold back, for walls have ears, and around you are those weak in vision.'
21:23.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

21:28.arabic: فإن قلت: فقد قال ﷺ بعد قوله لفاطمة وصفية "إني لا أغني عنكما من الله شيئاً إلا أن لكم رحماً سأبلها ببلاها" وقال عليه الصلاة والسلام "أترجو سليم شفاعتي ولا يرجوها بنو عبد المطلب" فذلك يدل على أنه سيخصص قرابته بالشفاعة؟ فاعلم أن كل مسلم فهو منتظر شفاعة رسول الله ﷺ، والنسيب أيضاً جدير بأن يرجوها لكن بشرط أن يتقي الله أن يغضب عليه، فإنه إن يغضب عليه فلا يأذن لأحد في شفاعته، لأن الذنوب منقسمة إلى ما يوجب المقت فلا يؤذن في الشفاعة له، وإلى ما يعفى عنه بسبب الشفاعة، كالذنوب عند ملوك الدنيا فإن كل ذي مكا
21:28.english: If you say: Indeed, he (peace be upon him) said after his statement to Fatimah and Safiyyah, "I cannot avail you anything from Allah except that you have kinship ties which I will maintain with due maintenance," and he (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "Do you hope for Salim my intercession while the sons of Abdul-Muttalib do not hope for it?" Does that indicate that he will specifically grant his relatives intercession? Then know that every Muslim is awaiting the intercession of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), and the relative is also worthy of hoping for it, but on the condition that he fears Allah (Taqwa) that He not be angry with him. For if He is angry with him, then He does not permit anyone to intercede for him, because sins are divided into that which necessitates wrath (Maaqt), so intercession is not permitted for it, and into that which is forgiven due to intercession, like sins with the kings of the world. For every person of status with the king cannot intercede in that which the king's anger has intensified against. So among sins are those from which intercession does not save, and about it is the expression by His saying, the Most High, "Nor do they intercede except for him whom He approves" (Quran 21:28), and by His saying, "Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?" (Quran 2:255), and by His saying, "And intercession does not benefit with Him except for him whom He permits" (Quran 34:23), and by His saying, "So their intercession will not benefit them" (Quran 74:48). And when sins are divided into that in which there is intercession and into that in which there is no intercession, fear (Khawf) and apprehension (Ishfaq) become obligatory without doubt. And if there were a sin in which intercession is accepted, He would not have commanded Quraysh to obedience, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) would not have prohibited Fatimah (may Allah be pleased with her) from disobedience, and he would have permitted her to follow desires to complete her self (Dhaat) in this world, then intercede for her in the Hereafter to complete her self (Dhaat) in the Hereafter.
21:28.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

21:28.arabic: وقد وصف الله تعالى الملائكة عليهم السلام مع تقدسهم عن الذنوب ومواظبتهم على العبادات على الدءوب بالإشفاق فقال تعالى مخبراً عنهم "يَسْبَحُونَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ لا يَفْتُرُونَ وَهُمْ مِنْ خَشْيَتِهِ مُشْفِقُونَ" فمتى زال الإشفاق والحذر مما سبق به القضاء في الأزل - وينكشف عند خاتمة الأجل - غلب الأمن من مكر الله وذلك يوجب الكبر وهو سبب الهلاك.
21:28.english: And Allah the Exalted has described the angels, peace be upon them, with their sanctity from sins and their persistence in acts of worship (Ibadat) continuously, with being apprehensive (Mushfiqun), as He the Exalted said informing about them: "They glorify (Yasbahuna) night and day, they do not slacken, and they are from fear (Khashya) of Him apprehensive (Mushfiqun)." So when the apprehension (Ishfaq) and caution from what has preceded in the decree (Qada) in pre-eternity (Al-Azal) - and is revealed at the conclusion of the term (Ajal) - is removed, security (Amn) from the deception (Makr) of Allah prevails, and that necessitates arrogance (Kibr), and it is the cause of destruction.
21:28.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

21:32.arabic: وذم المعرضين عنها فقال وجعلنا السماء سقفا محفوظا وهم عن آياتها معرضون فأى نسبة لجميع البحار والأرض إلى السماء وهى متغيرات على القرب والسموات صلاب شداد محفوظات عن التغير إلى أن يبلغ الكتاب أجله ولذلك سماه الله تعالى محفوظا فقال وجعلنا السماء سقفا محفوظا
21:32.english: And He censured those who turn away from them, saying: 'And We made the sky a protected ceiling, and they are turning away from its signs.' So what is the proportion of all the seas and the earth to the sky, while they are changing in proximity, and the heavens are firm, strong, protected from change until the decree reaches its term. And for that reason, Allah the Exalted named it protected, saying: 'And We made the sky a protected ceiling.'
21:32.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Contemplation'

21:35.arabic: وعن ابن عمر أنه لما دخل أبو بكر البيت وصلى وأثنى عج أهل البيت عجيجا سمعه أهل المصلى كلما ذكر شيئا ازدادوا فما سكن عجيجهم إلا تسليم رجل على الباب صيت جلد قال السلام عليكم يا أهل البيت ﴿ كل نفس ذائقة الموت ﴾ {} الآية إن في الله خلفا من كل أحد ودركا لكل رغبة ونجاة من كل مخافة فالله تعالى فارجوا وبه فثقوا فاستمعوا له وأنكروه وقطعوا البكاء فلما انقطع البكاء فقد صوته فاطلع أحدهم فلم ير أحدا ثم عادوا فبكوا فناداهم مناد آخر لا يعرفون صوته يا اهل البيت اذكروا الله تعالى واحمدوه على كل حال تكونوا من المخل
21:35.english: And from Ibn Umar that when Abu Bakr entered the house and prayed and praised, the people of the house wailed a wailing heard by the people of the prayer place; whenever he mentioned something, they increased. Their wailing did not cease except by the greeting of a man at the door, strong-voiced, who said: 'Peace be upon you, O people of the house. "Every soul (Nafs) shall taste death" (Quran 21:35). Indeed, in Allah there is a successor (Khalaf) from everyone and attainment (Darak) for every desire and salvation (Najah) from every fear. So in Allah the Exalted, hope (Fargu), and in Him, trust (Thiq), and listen to Him and deny (Ankiruh) and cut off the weeping.' When the weeping ceased, his voice was lost. One of them looked out and did not see anyone. Then they returned and wept. Then another caller called them whose voice they did not recognize: 'O people of the house, remember (Udhkuru) Allah the Exalted and praise (Uhmaduh) Him in every state, that you may be among the sincere ones (Mukhlisin). Indeed, in Allah there is consolation (Azā') from every calamity and compensation (Iwad) from every desire. So in Allah, obey (Fati'u), and by His command, act (Fa'malu).' Abu Bakr said: 'This is Al-Khidr and Al-Yasa, peace be upon them, who attended the Prophet ﷺ.'
21:35.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

21:35.arabic: وقال بعض الصوفية كنت أقرأ ليلة هذه الآية كل نفس ذائقة الموت فجعلت ارددها فإذا هاتف يهتف بي كم تردد هذه الآية فقد قتلت أربعة من الجن ما رفعوا رءوسهم إلى السماء منذ خلقوا
21:35.english: And some of the Sufis said: I was reciting one night this verse: 'Every Soul (Nafs) tastes death (Al-Mawt)' so I kept repeating it, then a caller called out to me: 'How much you repeat this verse! You have killed four of the Jinn (Al-Jinn) who have not raised their heads to the sky since they were created.'
21:35.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

21:35.arabic: وقال بعض الصالحين بينما أنا أسير في مسير لى إذ ملت إلى شجرة لأستريح تحتها فإذا أنا بشيخ قد أشرف على فقال لى يا هذا قم فإن الموت لم يمت ثم هام على وجه فاتبعته فسمعته وهو يقول كل نفس ذائقة الموت اللهم بارك لى في الموت فقلت وفيما بعد الموت فقال من أيقن بما بعد الموت شمر مئزر الحذر ولم يكن له في الدنيا مستقر
21:35.english: And some of the righteous said: While I was walking on my journey, I inclined toward a tree to rest under it, and behold, I saw an elder who had appeared to me and said to me: O this one, rise, for death has not died. Then he wandered on his face, and I followed him, and I heard him saying: 'Every soul (Nafs) will taste death (Quran 21:35). O Allah, bless me in death.' So I said: And in what comes after death? He said: Whoever is certain of what comes after death has girded the loincloth of caution and has no abode in this world.
21:35.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

21:37.arabic: ومن أبوابه العظيمة العجلة وترك التثبت في الأمور وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم العجلة من الشيطان والتأني من الله تعالى[58] وقال عز وجل خلق الإنسان من عجل وقال تعالى وكان الإنسان عجولا وقال لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا تعجل بالقرآن من قبل أن يقضي إليك وحيه وهذا لأن الأعمال ينبغي أن تكون بعد التبصرة والمعرفة والتبصرة تحتاج إلى تأمل وتمهل والعجلة تمنع من ذلك وعند الاستعجال يروج الشيطان شره على الإنسان من حيث لا يدري
21:37.english: And from its great gates are haste and abandoning careful consideration in matters. And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Haste is from Satan, and deliberation is from Allah the Exalted.' And the Mighty and Majestic said: 'The human being (Al-Insan) is created from haste (عَجَلٍ).' And He said: 'And the human being (Al-Insan) is hasty (عَجُولًا).' And He said to His Prophet (peace be upon him): 'And do not hasten with the Quran before its revelation is completed to you.' And this is because actions should be after insight (Al-Basirah) and knowledge (Al-Ma'rifah), and insight requires contemplation (Ta'ammul) and deliberation (Tamahhul), and haste prevents from that. And during hastening, Satan promotes his evil upon the human being from where he does not realize.
21:37.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

21:38.arabic: واختلاف تركيب أعضائه أعاجيب تزيد على الأعاجيب فى بعثه وإعادته فكيف ينكر ذلك من قدرة الله تعالى وحكمته من يشاهد ذلك فى صنعته وقدرته فإن كان فى إيمانك ضعف فقو الإيمان بالنظر فى النشأة الأولى فإن الثانية مثلها وأسهل منها وإن كنت قوى الإيمان بها فأشعر قلبك تلك المخاوف والأخطار وأكثر فيها التفكر والاعتبار لتسلب عن قلبك الراحة والقرار فتشتغل بالتشمر للعرض على الجبار وتفكر أولا فيما يقرع سمع سكان القبور من شدة نفخ الصور فإنها صيحة واحدة تنفرج بها القبور عن رءوس الموتی فيثورون دفعة واحدة فتوهم نفسك وقد
21:38.english: And the differing composition of its limbs are wonders that increase over wonders in its resurrection and restoration, so how can one deny that from the power (Qudrah) of Allah the Exalted and His wisdom who witnesses that in His creation and power? If there is weakness in your faith (Iman), then strengthen the faith (Iman) by looking at the first creation, for the second is like it and easier than it. And if you are strong in faith (Iman) in it, then make your heart (Qalb) feel those fears and dangers, and increase in it reflection (Tafakkur) and consideration (I'tibar) to strip from your heart (Qalb) comfort and settlement, so you busy yourself with preparing for the presentation before the Almighty (Al-Jabbar). And reflect first on what strikes the hearing of the inhabitants of the graves from the intensity of blowing the Trumpet (As-Sur), for it is a single cry by which the graves split open from the heads of the dead, and they rise up all at once. So imagine yourself having leapt up, your face changed, your body dusty from your scalp to your feet from the dust of your grave, stunned from the intensity of the blow, your eye fixed toward the call. And the creation has risen up in one uprising from the graves in which their tribulation has been prolonged, and alarm and terror have agitated them, added to what they had of sorrows and griefs and intense waiting for the outcome of the matter, as the Exalted said: 'And the Trumpet (As-Sur) will be blown, and all who are in the heavens and all who are on the earth will fall dead except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on.' And the Exalted said: 'And when the Horn (An-Naqur) is blown, that Day will be a difficult day for the disbelievers; not easy.' And the Exalted said: 'And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?" They do not await except one blast which will seize them while they are disputing. And they will not be able to make a testament, nor to their people can they return. And the Trumpet (As-Sur) will be blown; and at once from the graves to their Lord they will hasten. They will say, "O woe to us! Who has raised us from our sleeping place? This is what the Most Merciful had promised, and the messengers told the truth."' So if there were not before the dead except the terror of that blowing, it would be worthy to be feared, for it is a blowing and a cry by which those in the heavens and the earth are struck dead, meaning they die by it except whom Allah wills, and that is some of the angels. And therefore the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'How can I be at ease when the possessor of the Trumpet (As-Sur) has taken the horn in his mouth, lowered his forehead, and inclined his ear, waiting for when he is commanded to blow?' Maqatil said: The Trumpet (As-Sur) is the horn, and that Israfil (upon him be peace) is placing his mouth on the horn like the form of a trumpet, and the circle of the horn's head is like the width of the heavens and the earth, and he is fixing his gaze toward the Throne, waiting for when he is commanded to blow the first blowing. And when he blows, those in the heavens and the earth are struck dead, meaning every animal dies from the intensity of the alarm except whom Allah wills, and that is Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil, and the Angel of Death (Malak al-Mawt). Then the Angel of Death (Malak al-Mawt) is commanded to take the soul (Ruh) of Jibril, then the soul (Ruh) of Mika'il, then the soul (Ruh) of Israfil, then the Angel of Death (Malak al-Mawt) is commanded and he dies. Then the creation remains after the first blowing in the Barzakh for forty years, then Allah the Exalted revives Israfil and commands.
21:38.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

21:47.arabic: خواطر عباده إذا اختلجت الذى لا يعزب عن علمه مثقال ذرة في السموات والأرض تحركت أو سكنت المحاسب على النقير والقطمير والقليل والكثير من الأعمال وإن خفيت المتفضل بقبول طاعات العباد وان صغرت المتطول بالعفو عن من معاصيهم وإن كثرت وإنما يحاسبهم لتعلم كل نفس ما أحضرت وتنظر فيما قدمت وأخرت فتعلم انه لولا لزومها للمراقبة والمحاسبة في الدنيا لشفيت في صعيد القيامة وهلكت وبعد المجاهدة والمحاسبة والمراقبة لولا فضله بقبول بضاعتها المزجاة لخابت وخسرت فسبحان من عمت نعمته كافة العباد وشملت واستغرقت رحمته الخلائق
21:47.english: The thoughts (Khawatir) of His servants when they stir—He from Whose knowledge not an atom's weight in the heavens or earth escapes, whether it moves or is still—the Accountant (Al-Muhasib) over the smallest and the largest of deeds, even if hidden; the Bestower of favor (Al-Mutafaddil) by accepting the acts of obedience (Taat) of the servants, even if small; the One who extends pardon (Al-Mutawwil) by forgiving their sins, even if numerous. And He only accounts them so that every soul (Nafs) may know what it has brought forth and reflect on what it has sent ahead and left behind, so it knows that were it not for its adherence to vigilance (Muraqabah) and self-accounting (Muhasabah) in this world, it would be exposed on the plain of Resurrection and perish. And after striving (Mujahadah), self-accounting, and vigilance, were it not for His grace (Fadl) in accepting their meager offering, it would fail and lose. So glory be to Him whose favor (Nimat) encompasses all servants, and whose mercy (Rahmah) embraces and pervades the creatures in this world and the next, and overwhelms. And by the breaths of His grace, the hearts (Qulub) expanded for faith (Iman) and were opened, and by the blessing of His enabling success (Tawfiq), the limbs (Jawarih) were bound to acts of worship (Ibadat) and disciplined, and by the excellence of His guidance (Hidayah), the darknesses of ignorance (Jahl) cleared from the hearts and dispersed, and by His support (Tayid) and victory (Nasr), the schemes of Satan (Shaytan) were cut off and repelled, and by the gentleness of His care (Inayah), the scale of good deeds (Hasanat) tips when heavy, and by His facilitation (Taysir), what is facilitated of acts of obedience is facilitated. From Him is the giving and the recompense, the distancing and the drawing near, the making happy and the making wretched. And prayers and peace be upon Muhammad, the master of the prophets, and upon his family, the masters of the chosen ones, and upon his companions, the leaders of the pious. Then after, Allah the Exalted said: 'And We will set up the scales of justice (Al-Mawazin Al-Qist) for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged at all. And if there is [even] the weight of a mustard seed (Habbah min Khardal), We will bring it forth. And sufficient are We as accountant (Hasib).' And He said: 'And the record [of deeds] will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of that within it, and they will say, "Oh, woe to us! What is this book that leaves nothing small or great except that it has enumerated it?" And they will find what they did present [before them]. And your Lord does injustice to no one.' And He said: 'On the Day when Allah will resurrect them all and inform them of what they did. Allah has enumerated it, and they have forgotten it; and Allah is, over all things, Witness.' And He said: 'That Day, the people will depart separated [into categories] to be shown their deeds. So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.' And He said: 'Then every soul will be compensated for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.' And He said: 'On the Day when every soul will find what it did of good present [before it] and what it did of evil, it will wish that between itself and that [evil] was a great distance. And Allah warns you of Himself.' And He said: 'And know that Allah knows what is within yourselves, so beware of Him.' So the possessors of insight (Arbab Al-Basair) from among the servants recognized that Allah the Exalted is lying in wait for them and that they will be scrutinized in the account and demanded with atom's weights of thoughts (Khawatir) and glances (Lahzat). And they realized that nothing saves them from these dangers except adherence to self-accounting, sincerity in vigilance, and demanding accountability from the soul (Nafs) in breaths (Anfas) and movements (Harakat), and accounting it for thoughts and glances. For whoever accounts his soul before being accounted, his account on the Day of Resurrection will be lightened, his answer will be present at the questioning, and his outcome and return will be good. And whoever does not account his soul, it persists.
21:47.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

21:47.arabic: وقال تعالى "وَنَضَعُ الْمَوَازِينَ الْقِسْطَ لِيَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ فَلَا تُظْلَمُ نَفْسٌ شَيْئًا ۖ وَإِنْ كَانَ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍ مِنْ خَرْدَلٍ أَتَيْنَا بِهَا ۗ وَكَفَىٰ بِنَا حَاسِبِينَ" وذم الكبر في القرآن كثير وقد قال رسول الله ﭬ "لا يدخل الجنة من كان في قلبه مثقال حبة من خردل من كبر، ولا يدخل النار من كان في قلبه مثقال حبة من خردل من إيمان"[3]
21:47.english: And He (Allah) said: "And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul (Nafs) will be wronged at all. And if there is the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth. And sufficient are We as accountant." And the condemnation of arrogance in the Quran is abundant, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "He will not enter Paradise who has in his heart (Qalb) the weight of a mustard seed of arrogance, and he will not enter the Fire who has in his heart (Qalb) the weight of a mustard seed of faith."
21:47.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

21:47.arabic: وقد قال رسول الله ﭬ "لا يدخل الجنة من كان في قلبه مثقال حبة من خردل من كبر، ولا يدخل النار من كان في قلبه مثقال حبة من خردل من إيمان"[3] وقال أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه: قال رسول الله ﭬ "يقول الله تعالى الكبرياء ردائي والعظمة إزاري فمن نازعني واحداً منهما ألقيته في جهنم ولا أبالي"[4] وعن أبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن قال: التقى عبد الله بن عمرو وعبد الله بن عمر على الصفا فتواقفا، فمضى ابن عمرو وأقام ابن عمر يبكي، فقالوا ما يبكيك يا أبا عبد الرحمن؟ فقال: هذا - يعني عبد الله بن عمرو - زعم أنه سمع رسول الله ﭬ
21:47.english: And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "He will not enter Paradise who has in his heart (Qalb) the weight of a mustard seed (Habbah min Khardal) of arrogance (Kibr), nor will he enter the Fire who has in his heart (Qalb) the weight of a mustard seed (Habbah min Khardal) of faith (Iman)." [3] And Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Allah the Exalted says: Arrogance (Kibriya') is My cloak and grandeur (Izzah) is My lower garment, so whoever contends with Me for one of them, I will cast him into Hellfire and I do not care." [4] And from Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, he said: Abdullah ibn Amr and Abdullah ibn Umar met at al-Safa and stood together, then Ibn Amr went on and Ibn Umar remained weeping. They said: What makes you weep, O Abu Abd al-Rahman? He said: This - meaning Abdullah ibn Amr - claimed that he heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: "Whoever has in his heart (Qalb) the weight of a mustard seed (Habbah min Khardal) of arrogance (Kibr), Allah will throw him on his face into the Fire." [5] And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "A man continues to go with his soul (Nafs) until he is written among the tyrants (Jabbarin), and he will be afflicted with what afflicted them of punishment." [6] And Sulayman ibn Dawud (peace be upon them both) said one day - to the birds, mankind, jinn, and beasts: Come out, so they came out in two hundred thousand of mankind and two hundred thousand of jinn, then he was raised until he heard the clamor of the angels with glorification in the heavens, then he was lowered until his feet touched the sea, and he heard a voice: If there were in the heart (Qalb) of your companion the weight of an atom (Dharr) of arrogance (Kibr), I would have caused him to sink farther than I raised him. And he (peace be upon him) said: "There will come out from the Fire a neck having two ears that hear and two eyes that see and a tongue that speaks, saying: I have been entrusted with three: with every obstinate tyrant (Jabbar Anid) and with everyone who called upon another god with Allah and with the image-makers." [7] And he (peace be upon him) said: "He will not enter Paradise a miser, nor a tyrant (Jabbar), nor one of bad character." [8] And he (peace be upon him) said: "Paradise and the Fire argued, so the Fire said: I have been favored with the arrogant (Mutakabbirin) and the tyrannical (Mutajabbirin), and Paradise said: Why is it that none enters me except the weak of the people, their lowly, and their incapable? So Allah said to Paradise: You are only My mercy, I show mercy with you to whom I will of My servants, and He said to the Fire: You are only My punishment, I punish with you whom I will, and for each of you is your fill." [9] And he (peace be upon him) said: "Wretched is the servant (Abd) who acts arrogantly (Tajabbar) and transgresses and forgets the Most High Tyrant (Al-Jabbar al-A'la), wretched is the servant (Abd) who acts arrogantly (Tajabbar) and...
21:47.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

21:47.arabic: الأصل الرابع: الميزان وهو حق قال الله تعالى: ﴿ ونضع الموازين القسط ليوم القيامة ﴾ { سورة الأنبيآء: 47 } وقال تعالى: ﴿ فمن ثقلت موازينه فأولئك هم المفلحون. ومن خفت موازينه ﴾ { سورة المؤمنون:102، 103 } ووجهها أن الله تعالى يحدث في صحائف الأعمال وزنا بحسب درجات الأعمال عند الله تعالى فتصير مقادير أعمال العباد معلومة للعباد حتى يظهر لهم العدل في العقاب أو الفضل في العفو وتضعيف الثواب.
21:47.english: The Fourth Foundation: The Balance (Mizan) is truth. Allah the Exalted said: 'And We will set up the balances of justice (al-Mawazin al-Qist) for the Day of Resurrection' (Surah Al-Anbiya: 47). And He said: 'Then as for those whose scales are heavy, they are the successful ones. And as for those whose scales are light' (Surah Al-Muminun: 102-103). And its interpretation (Wajhuha) is that Allah the Exalted creates in the scrolls of deeds a weight (Waznan) according to the degrees of deeds with Allah the Exalted, so the measures (Maqadir) of the deeds of the servants become known to the servants until justice (al-Adl) in punishment or favor (al-Fadl) in pardon and multiplication of reward becomes apparent to them.
21:47.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

21:47.arabic: [3] حديث لا يدخل الجنة من كان في قلبه مثقال حبة من خردل من كبر ولا يدخل النار رجل في قلبه مثقال حبة من خردل من إيمان أخرجه مسلم من حديث ابن مسعود.
21:47.english: Hadith: "He will not enter Paradise who has in his heart (Qalb) the weight of a mustard seed (Habbah min Khardal) of arrogance (Kibr), nor will he enter Hellfire a man who has in his heart (Qalb) the weight of a mustard seed (Habbah min Khardal) of faith (Iman)." Reported by Muslim from the narration of Ibn Mas'ud.
21:47.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

21:51.arabic: وأما الرشد فنعنى به العناية الإلهية التى تعين الإنسان عند توجهه إلى مقاصده فتقوبه على ما فيه صلاحه وتفتره عما فيه فساده ويكون ذلك من الباطن كما قال تعالى: ﴿ ولقد آتينا إبراهيم رشده من قبل وكنا به عالمين ﴾ {} فالرشد عبارة عن هداية باعثة إلى جهة السعادة محركة إليها فالصبى إذا بلغ خبيرا بحفظ المال وطرق التجارة والاستنماء ولكنه مع ذلك يبذر ولا يريد الاستنماء لا يسمى رشيدا لا لعدم هدايته بل لقصور هدايته عن تحريك داعيته فكم من شخص يقدم على ما يعلم أنه يضره فقد أعطى الهداية وميز بها عن الجاهل الذى لا ي
21:51.english: And as for the Guidance (Rushd), we mean by it the Divine Care (Al-'Inayah Al-Ilahiyyah) that assists the human when he turns toward his objectives, so it guides him to what contains his rectification (Salah) and turns him away from what contains his corruption (Fasad), and this is from the inner dimension (Al-Batin) as Allah the Exalted said: 'And verily We gave Abraham his Guidance (Rushd) from before, and We were of him Knowers.' So the Guidance (Rushd) is an expression for a guidance (Hidayah) that motivates toward the direction of happiness (Al-Sa'adah) and moves toward it. For the boy when he reaches puberty, knowledgeable about preserving wealth and ways of commerce and growth, but with that he squanders and does not desire growth, he is not called guided (Rashid), not due to absence of his guidance (Hidayah) but due to deficiency of his guidance (Hidayah) in moving his motivation (Da'iyah). For how many a person proceeds upon what he knows harms him, he has been given the guidance (Hidayah) and distinguished by it from the ignorant one who does not know that it harms him, but he has not been given the Guidance (Rushd). So the Guidance (Rushd) by this consideration is more complete than mere guidance (Hidayah) to the aspects of deeds, and it is a great blessing (Ni'mah).
21:51.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

21:56.arabic: فإذا انتهى إلى قوله إنك تقضي ولا يقضى عليك فلا يليق به التأمين وهو ثناء فيقرأ معه فيقول مثل قوله أو يقول بلى وأنا على ذلك من الشاهدين أو صدقت وبررت وما أشبه ذلك
21:56.english: When he reaches His saying 'You judge and are not judged,' it is not fitting for him to say 'Amen' as it is praise, so he recites with him and says like his saying or says 'Yes, and I am among the witnesses of that' or 'You have spoken truthfully and righteously' and what resembles that.
21:56.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

21:60.arabic: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: ما آتي الله عز وجل عبدا علما إلا شابا والخير كله في الشباب ثم تلا قوله عز وجل: ﴿ قالوا سمعنا فتى يذكرهم يقال له إبراهيم ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ إنهم فتية آمنوا بربهم وزدناهم هدى ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ وآتيناه الحكم صبيا ﴾ {} وكان أنس رضي الله عنه يقول (قبض رسول الله ﭬ وليس في رأسه ولحيته عشرون شعرة بيضاء فقيل له: يا أبا حمزة فقد أسن فقال لم يشنه الله بالشيب فقيل أهو شين فقال كلكم يكرهه[76])
21:60.english: And Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: 'Allah Almighty does not give knowledge to a servant except when he is young, and all good is in youth.' Then he recited the saying of Allah Almighty: 'They said: We heard a youth (Fata) mentioning them; he is called Abraham' (Quran 21:60), and His saying: 'Indeed, they were youths (Fityah) who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance' (Quran 18:13), and His saying: 'And We gave him wisdom (Hukm) as a boy (Sabiyyan)' (Quran 19:12). And Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say: 'The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, passed away and there were not twenty white hairs in his head and beard. It was said to him: O Abu Hamzah, you have aged. He said: Allah did not disgrace him with gray hair. It was said: Is it a disgrace? He said: All of you dislike it.'
21:60.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Purity'
