21:67.arabic: الدرجة الرابعة السب والتعنيف بالقول الغليظ الخشن وذلك يعدل إليه عند العجز عن المنع باللطف وظهور مبادىء الإصرار والاستهزاء بالوعظ والنصح وذلك مثل قول إبراهيم عليه السلام أف لكم ولما تعبدون من دون الله أفلا تعقلون ولسنا نعني بالسب والفحش بما فيه نسبة إلى الزنا ومقدماته ولا الكذب بل أن يخاطبه بما فيه مما لا يعد من جملة الفحش كقوله يا فاسق يا أحمق يا جاهل ألا تخاف الله وكقوله يا سوادي يا غبي وما يجري هذا المجرى فإن كل فاسق فهو أحمق وجاهل ولولا حمقه لما عصى الله تعالى بل كل من ليس بكيس فهو أحمق والكي
21:67.english: The fourth degree: reviling and rebuking with harsh, coarse speech, and one resorts to this when incapable of prevention with gentleness and when signs of persistence and mockery of admonition and counsel appear. This is like the saying of Abraham (peace be upon him): 'Uff (an expression of disgust) to you and to what you worship besides Allah. Do you not then understand?' And we do not mean by reviling and obscenity that which involves attribution to fornication and its preliminaries, nor lying, but rather addressing him with what is not considered among obscenities, such as saying: 'O transgressor (Fasiq), O fool (Ahmaq), O ignorant one (Jahil), do you not fear Allah?' and like saying: 'O black one (Sawadi), O stupid one (Ghabi),' and what runs in this course. For every transgressor (Fasiq) is a fool (Ahmaq) and ignorant (Jahil), and were it not for his foolishness (Hamaq), he would not disobey Allah Almighty. Rather, everyone who is not prudent (Kays) is a fool (Ahmaq), and the prudent one (Kays) is he whom the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) testified to for prudence (Kaysah) when he said: 'The prudent one (Kays) is he who holds his Soul (Nafs) accountable and works for what is after death,' and the fool (Ahmaq) is he who follows his Soul's (Nafs) desire (Hawa) and wishes upon Allah. The hadith: 'The prudent one (Kays) is he who holds his Soul (Nafs) accountable and works for what is after death'—the hadith was reported by Al-Tirmidhi who said it is hasan, and by Ibn Majah from the narration of Shaddad ibn Aws. For this rank, there are two etiquettes: one is not to proceed to it except out of necessity and incapacity for gentleness, and the second is not to speak except with truth and not to indulge in it by letting his long tongue loose with what is not needed, but rather to limit to the extent of need. If he knows that addressing him with these deterrent words does not deter him, then it is not appropriate to let it loose, but rather to limit to showing anger and contempt for him and disdain for his place due to his disobedience. And if he knows that if he speaks he will be struck, but if he frowns and shows dislike with his face he will not be struck, it is incumbent upon him, and it does not suffice him to disapprove with the Heart (Qalb), but rather it is incumbent upon him.
21:67.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

21:79.arabic: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله تعالى ﴿ ومن يؤت الحكمة فقد أوتي خيرا كثيرا ﴾ {} يعني الفهم في القرآن. وقال عز وجل ﴿ ففهمناها سليمان وكلا آتينا حكما وعلما ﴾ {} سمى ما آتاهما علما وحكما وخصص ما انفرد به سليمان بالتفطن له باسم الفهم وجعله مقدما على الحكم والعلم فهذه الأمور تدل على أن في فهم معاني القرآن مجالا رحبا ومتسعا بالغا وأن المنقول من ظاهر التفسير ليس منتهى الإدراك فيه.
21:79.english: And Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said regarding His (the Exalted's) statement: 'And whoever is given wisdom has been given much good' (Quran 2:269) - meaning understanding (Fahm) in the Quran. And He (the Exalted) said: 'So We gave Solomon understanding (Fahhamnaha) of it, and to each We gave judgment (Hukm) and knowledge (Ilm)' (Quran 21:79). He named what He gave both of them as knowledge (Ilm) and judgment (Hukm), and He specified what Solomon uniquely possessed of discernment (Tafattun) by the name 'understanding' (Fahm) and made it precede judgment (Hukm) and knowledge (Ilm). These matters indicate that in understanding (Fahm) the meanings of the Quran there is a vast and extensive scope, and that what is transmitted of the apparent interpretation (Tafsir) is not the ultimate limit of comprehension (Idrak) in it.
21:79.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

21:84.arabic: وقال الشافعي رحمه الله: (التمكين درجة الأنبياء ولا يكون التمكين إلا بعد المحنة فإذا امتحن صبر وإذا صبر مكن ألا ترى أن الله عز وجل امتحن إبراهيم عليه السلام ثم مكنه، وامتحن موسى عليه السلام ثم مكنه، وامتحن أيوب عليه السلام ثم مكنه، وامتحن سليمان عليه السلام ثم مكنه وآتاه ملكا، والتمكين أفضل الدرجات قال الله عز وجل (وكذلك مكنا ليوسف في الأرض( (يوسف: 56)، وأيوب عليه السلام بعد المحنة العظيمة مكن، قال الله تعالى (وآتيناه أهله ومثلهم معهم( (الأنبياء: 84) الآية. فهذا الكلام من الشافعي رحمه الله يدل عل
21:84.english: And Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy upon him, said: 'Empowerment (Tamkin) is the rank of the Prophets, and empowerment does not occur except after trial (Mihna). So when one is tested, he endures with patience (Sabr), and when he endures with patience, he is empowered. Do you not see that Allah, the Exalted and Majestic, tested Ibrahim, peace be upon him, then empowered him; and tested Musa, peace be upon him, then empowered him; and tested Ayyub, peace be upon him, then empowered him; and tested Sulayman, peace be upon him, then empowered him and granted him a kingdom. And empowerment is the best of ranks. Allah, the Exalted and Majestic, said: "And thus We empowered Yusuf in the land" (Yusuf: 56). And Ayyub, peace be upon him, after the great trial, was empowered. Allah, the Exalted, said: "And We gave him his family and the like of them with them" (Al-Anbiya': 84) the verse. This speech from Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy upon him, indicates his deep immersion in the secrets of the Quran and his awareness of the stations (Maqamat) of those journeying (Sa'irin) to Allah, the Exalted, from among the Prophets and the Friends (Awliya'), and all of that is from the sciences of the Hereafter (Al-Akhira).'
21:84.topic: Al-Ghazali on the outer and inner dimensions of worship, from 'Book of Knowledge'

21:87.arabic: ستغفرك وأتوب إليك آمنت اللهم بما أرسلته من رسول وآمنت اللهم بما أنزلت من كتاب وصلى الله على محمد النبي الأمي وعلى آله وسلم تسليما كثيرا خاتم كلامي ومفتاحه وعلى أنبيائه ورسله أجمعين آمين يا رب العالمين اللهم أوردنا حوض محمد واسقنا بكأسه مشربا رويا سائغا هنيا لا نظمأ بعده أبدا واحشرنا في زمرته غير خزايا ولا ناكثين للعهد ولا مرتابين ولا مفتونين ولا مغضوب علينا ولا ضالين اللهم اعصمني من فتن الدنيا ووفقني لما تحب وترضى وأصلح لي شأني كله وثبتني بالقول الثابت في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة ولا تضلني وإن ك
21:87.english: I seek Your forgiveness and repent to You. O Allah, I believe in what You have sent of Messenger, and I believe, O Allah, in what You have revealed of Book. And may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad, the unlettered Prophet, and upon his family and grant abundant peace, the seal of my speech and its key, and upon all His prophets and messengers. Amen, O Lord of the worlds. O Allah, make us arrive at the pool of Muhammad and give us to drink from his cup a drink that is quenching, pleasant, delightful, after which we shall never thirst forever. And gather us in his company, not disgraced, nor breaking the covenant, nor doubting, nor tempted, nor those upon whom is wrath, nor astray. O Allah, protect me from the trials of the world and grant me success in what You love and are pleased with, and rectify all my affairs for me, and make me firm with the firm word in the worldly life and in the Hereafter, and do not lead me astray, even if I have been unjust. Glory be to You, glory be to You, O Exalted, O Magnificent, O Creator, O Merciful, O Mighty, O Compeller. Glory be to Him for whom the heavens glorify with their expanses, and glory be to Him for whom the seas glorify with their waves, and glory be to Him for whom the mountains glorify with their echoes, and glory be to Him for whom the fish glorify with their languages, and glory be to Him for whom the stars in the sky glorify with their constellations, and glory be to Him for whom the trees glorify with their roots and fruits, and glory be to Him for whom the seven heavens and the seven earths glorify, and whoever is in them and upon them. Glory be to Him whom everything from His creatures glorifies. Blessed and Exalted are You. Glory be to You, glory be to You, O Living, O Self-Subsisting, O All-Knowing, O Forbearing. Glory be to You, there is no god but You alone, no partner to You. You give life and cause death, and You are Living, do not die. In Your hand is good, and You have power over all things.
21:87.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

21:87.arabic:

ومفتاحه وعلى أنبيائه ورسله أجمعين آمين يا رب العالمين اللهم أوردنا حوض  محمد
واسقنا بكأسه مشربا رويا سائغا هنيا لا نظمأ بعده أبدا واحشرنا  في  زمرته  غير
خزايا ولا ناكثين للعهد ولا مرتابين ولا مفتونين ولا  مغضوب  علينا  ولا  ضالين
اللهم اعصمني من فتن الدنيا ووفقني لما تحب وترضى وأصلح  لي  شأني  كله  وثبتني
بالقول الثابت في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخ
21:87.english: [159] Hadith: 'Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You, there is no god but You, I have done evil and wronged my soul (Nafs), so forgive me my sin, You are my Lord, indeed none forgives sins except You.' Al-Bayhaqi reported it in 'Al-Da'awat' from the narration of 'Ali, without the phrase 'my sin, You are my Lord,' and it has preceded in the second chapter.
21:87.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

21:90.arabic: السادس: التضرع والخشوع والرغبة والرهبة قال الله تعالى: ﴿ إنهم كانوا يسارعون في الخيرات ويدعوننا رغبا ورهبا ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل: ﴿ ادعوا ربكم تضرعا وخفية ﴾ {} وقال ﭬ: (إذا أحب الله عبدا ابتلاه حتى يسمع تضرعه[87]).
21:90.english: Sixth: Supplication (Tadarru'), Humility (Khushu'), Desire (Raghba), and Fear (Rahba). Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed they used to hasten to good deeds and call upon Us with desire and fear' (Quran 21:90). And He the Mighty and Majestic said: 'Call upon your Lord with supplication and in secret' (Quran 7:55). And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'When Allah loves a servant, He tests him until He hears his supplication.'
21:90.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

21:91.arabic: وقال عز وجل: " فأرسلنا إليها روحنا فتمثل لها بشراً سوياً "، ثم قال تعالى: " فنفخنا فيها من روحنا " وكان النافخ جبريل عليه السلام، وكما قال تعالى: " فإذا قرأناه فاتبع قرآنه " قيل في التفسير: معناه إذا قرأه عليك جبريل.
21:91.english: And He, the Exalted, said: "So We sent to her Our Spirit (Ruh), and he appeared to her as a well-proportioned man." Then He, the Exalted, said: "And she who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her from Our Spirit (Ruh), and We made her and her son a sign for the worlds." And the blower was Gabriel, peace be upon him. And as He, the Exalted, said: "So when We have recited it, then follow its recitation." It is said in the interpretation (Tafsir): its meaning is when Gabriel recites it to you.
21:91.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

21:101.arabic: فخوف الخاتمة كخوف السابقة وربما يظهر في الحال ما سبقت الكلمة بنقيضه. فمن الذي يدري أنه من الذين سبقت لهم من الله الحسنى وقيل في معنى قوله تعالى: ﴿ وجاءت سكرة الموت بالحق ﴾ {} أي بالسابقة يعني أظهرتها. وقال بعض السلف إنما يوزن من الأعمال خواتيمها وكان أبو الدرداء رضي الله عنه يحلف بالله ما من أحد يأمن أن يسلب إيممانه إلا سلبه وقيل من الذنوب ذنوب عقوبتها سوء الخاتمة، نعوذ بالله من ذلك وقيل هي عقوبات دعوى الولاية واالكرامة بالافتراء.
21:101.english: The fear of the ending (Al-Khatimah) is like the fear of the precedent (As-Sabiqah), and perhaps what appears in the present moment contradicts what the word (Al-Kalimah) preceded. So who knows that he is from those for whom the good (Al-Husna) has preceded from Allah? And it was said regarding the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: 'And the agony of death (Sakrat Al-Mawt) comes with the truth (Al-Haqq)' - meaning with the precedent (As-Sabiqah), that is, it reveals it. And some of the predecessors (As-Salaf) said: 'Only the endings (Al-Khawatim) of deeds are weighed.' And Abu Ad-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, would swear by Allah that no one feels secure from having his faith (Iman) stripped away except that it is stripped from him. And it was said: Among sins (Adh-Dhunub) are sins whose punishment is a bad ending (Su' Al-Khatimah) - we seek refuge in Allah from that. And it was said: They are punishments for claiming sainthood (Al-Wilayah) and honor (Al-Karamah) through falsehood.
21:101.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

21:101.arabic: فإنه المستصفى لقلوب الصديقين والمبعد لقلوب الجاحدين والمغرورين فلا مانع لما أعطى ولا معطي لما منع ولم يقطع التوفيق عن الكفار لجناية متقدمة ولا أمد الأنبياء عليهم السلام بتوفيقه ونور هدايته لوسيلة سابقة ولكنه قال ولقد سبقت كلمتنا لعبادنا المرسلين وقال عز وجل ولكن حق القول مني لأملأن جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين وقال تعالى إن الذين سبقت لهم منا الحسنى أولئك عنها مبعدون فإن خطر ببالك أنه لم اختلفت السابقة وهم في ربقه العبودية مشتركون نوديت من سرادقات الجلال لا تجاوز حد الأدب فإنه لا يسئل عما يفعل وه
21:101.english: For He is the One Who selects the hearts (Qulūb) of the truthful ones (Ṣiddīqīn) and distances the hearts (Qulūb) of the deniers and the deluded ones. There is no preventer for what He gives, and no giver for what He withholds. He did not cut off divine facilitation (Tawfīq) from the disbelievers due to a preceding transgression, nor did He extend to the Prophets, peace be upon them, His facilitation (Tawfīq) and light of guidance (Hidāyah) due to a prior means. Rather, He said: 'And Our word has already preceded for Our servants, the messengers' (Quran 37:171). And the Almighty said: 'But the word from Me will come true: "I will fill Hell with jinn and mankind all together."' (Quran 32:13). And the Exalted said: 'Indeed, those for whom the best [reward] has preceded from Us - they are from it [Hell] distanced' (Quran 21:101). If it occurs to your mind that the precedence has not differed while they are partners in the bond of servitude, you are called from the pavilions of majesty: 'Do not exceed the limit of etiquette, for He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned.'
21:101.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

21:101.arabic: والهالكون في التيه هم الأكثرون من ركاب هذه الطريق ولكن السائحون بنور التوفيق فازوا بالنعيم والملك المقيم وهم الذين سبقت لهم من الله الحسنى
21:101.english: And those who perish in the wilderness are the majority of the riders on this path, but those who journey with the light of Divine Success (Tawfīq) have attained bliss and the abiding kingdom, and they are those for whom the good has preceded from Allah.
21:101.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Travel'

21:101.arabic: اللهم إن أنت أمرضتني لتقبض روحي في مرضي هذا فاجعل روحي في أرواح من سبقت لهم منك الحسنى وباعدني من النار كما باعدت أولياءك الذين سبقت لهم منك الحسنى
21:101.english: O Allah, if You have made me ill to take my soul (Ruh) in this illness of mine, then place my soul (Ruh) among the souls (Arwah) of those for whom the good (Al-Husna) has preceded from You, and distance me from the Fire as You have distanced Your allies (Awliya) for whom the good (Al-Husna) has preceded from You.
21:101.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

21:104.arabic: وكما أن الأبرار يجدون المزيد في حالهم ومعرفتهم بقربهم من المقربين ومشاهدتهم لهم، فكذلك يكون حالهم في الآخرة "ما خلقكم ولا بعثكم إلا كنفس واحدة كما بدأنا أول خلق نعيده"، وكما قال تعالى: "جزاء وفاقاً" أي وافق الجزاء أعمالهم فقوبل الخالص بالصرف من الشراب وقوبل المشوب بالمشوب، وشوب كل شراب على قدر ما سبق من الشوب في حبه وأعماله
21:104.english: And just as the righteous (al-abrar) find increase in their state and knowledge through their proximity to the close ones (al-muqarrabun) and their witnessing of them, so too will be their state in the Hereafter: "We did not create you nor resurrect you except as a single soul (nafs), just as We began the first creation We repeat it," and as Allah the Exalted said: "A recompense in accordance (wafaqan)," meaning the recompense corresponded to their deeds, so the pure was met with the pure from the drink and the mixed was met with the mixed, and the mixing of each drink is according to what preceded of mixing in his love and his deeds.
21:104.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

21:104.arabic: ويحك يا نفس انزعى عن جهلك وقيسى آخرتك بدنياك فما خلقكم ولا بعثكم إلا كنفس واحدة و كما بدأنا أول خلق نعيده و كما بدأكم تعودون وسنة الله تعالى لا تجدين لها تبديلا ولا تحويلا
21:104.english: Woe to you, O Soul (Nafs)! Cast off your ignorance and measure your Hereafter (Akhirah) by your worldly life, for He did not create you nor resurrect you except as a single soul, and 'As We began the first creation, We will repeat it' (Quran 21:104), and as He began you, you will return. And the Way (Sunnah) of Allah, the Exalted, you will find no change or alteration for it.
21:104.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

22:1.arabic:
ه تعالى؟ قال: المؤمنون كلهم أولياء الله تعالى  أما سمعت  قول  الله
عز وجل: ﴿ الله ولي الذين آمنوا يخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور  ﴾  {})  وفي  بعض
الاخبار: (المؤمن أفضل من الكعبة[29]) (والمؤمن طيب  طاهر[30])  (والمؤمن  أكرم
على الله تعالى من الملائكة[31]) وفي الخبر:  (خلق  الله  تعالى  جهنم  من  فضل
رحمته سوطا يسوق به عباده إلى الجنة[32]). وفي خبر  آخر:  (يقول  الله  عز  وجل
إنما خلقت الخلق ليربحوا علي ولم أخلقهم لأربح عليهم[33]) وفي  حديث  أبي  سعيد
الخدري عن رسول الله ﭬ: (ما خلق الله تعالى شيئا إ
22:1.english: [41] Hadith: When he recited - 'Indeed, the earthquake of the Hour is a tremendous thing' - he said: 'Do you know what day this is?' The hadith was reported by al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of 'Imran ibn Husayn, and he said: 'Hasan sahih.' I say: It is from the narration of al-Hasan al-Basri from 'Imran, and he did not hear it from him, and in the two Sahihs there is something similar from the hadith of Abu Sa'id.
22:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

22:1.arabic: ولما تلا رسول الله ﭬ قوله تعالى: ﴿ إن زلزلة الساعة شيء عظيم ﴾ {} قال أتدرون أي يوم هذا هذا يوم يقال لآدم عليه الصلاة والسلام قم فابعث بعث النار من ذريتك فيقول كم فيقال من كل ألف تسعمائة وتسعة وتسعون إلى النار وواحد إلى الجنة قال فأبلس القوم وجعلوا يبكون وتعطلوا يومهم عن الإشتغال والعمل فخرج عليهم رسول الله ﭬ وقال: ما لكم لا تعملون؟ فقالوا: ومن يشتغل بعمل بعد ما حدثتنا بهذا. فقال: كم أنتم في الأمم أين تأويل وثاريث ومنسك ويأجوج ومأجوج أمم لا يحصيها إلا الله تعالى إنما أنتم في سائر الأمم كالشعرة ال
22:1.english: And when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) recited His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, the earthquake of the Hour is a tremendous thing' (Quran 22:1), he said: 'Do you know what day this is? This is a day when it will be said to Adam (upon him be peace): "Arise and send forth the contingent of the Fire from your progeny." He will say: "How many?" It will be said: "From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine to the Fire and one to Paradise."' He said: So the people despaired and began to weep, and they abandoned their day from engagement and work. Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) came out to them and said: 'What is the matter with you that you do not work?' They said: 'And who would engage in work after what you have informed us of this?' He said: 'How many are you among the nations? Where are the interpretations and the inheritances and the rites and Gog and Magog? Nations that none can enumerate except Allah, the Exalted. You are among all the nations like the white hair on the skin of a black ox and like the mark on the forearm of a beast.' So observe how he would drive the creation with the whips of fear and lead them with the reins of hope to Allah, the Exalted, for he drove them first with the whips of fear. Then when that took them beyond the limit of moderation to the excess of despair, he treated them with the medicine of hope and returned them to moderation and balance. The latter was not contradictory to the former, but he mentioned in the first what he saw as a cause for healing and confined himself to it. Then when they needed treatment with hope, he mentioned the completion of the matter. So upon the preacher to follow the example of the master of preachers and be gentle in employing the reports of fear and hope according to the need after observing the hidden ailments. And if he does not observe that, what he corrupts with his preaching...
22:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Fear and Hope'

22:2.arabic: يوم تذهل فيه كل مرضعة عما أرضعت وتضع كل ذات حمل حملها وترى الناس سكارى وما هم بسكارى ولكن عذاب الله شديد
22:2.english: A day when every nursing mother will be distracted from what she nursed, and every pregnant one will deliver her pregnancy, and you will see the people intoxicated, and they are not intoxicated, but the punishment of Allah is severe.
22:2.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

22:4.arabic: وهذا لأن القلوب كانت مطهرة عن مرعى الشيطان وقوته وهي الشهوات فمهما طمعت في أن يندفع الشيطان عنك بمجرد الذكر كما اندفع عن عمر رضي الله عنه كان محالا وكنت كمن يطمع أن يشرب دواء قبل الاحتماء والمعدة مشغولة بغليظ الأطعمة ويطمع أن ينفعه كما نفع الذي شربه بعد الاحتماء وتخلية المعدة والذكر الدواء والتقوى احتمال وهي تخلي القلب عن الشهوات فإذا نزل الذكر قلبا فارغا عن غير الذكر اندفع الشيطان كما تندفع العلة بنزول الدواء في المعدة الخالية عن الأطعمة قال الله تعالى إن في ذلك لذكرى لمن كان له قلب وقال تعالى
22:4.english: This is because the Hearts (Qalb) were purified from the pasture of Satan and his power, which is the Desires (Shahawat). So whenever you hope that Satan will be repelled from you by mere Remembrance (Dhikr) as he was repelled from Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), it is impossible, and you are like one who hopes to drink medicine before protection, with the stomach occupied by coarse foods, and hopes that it will benefit him as it benefited the one who drank it after protection and emptying the stomach. The Remembrance (Dhikr) is the medicine, and God-consciousness (Taqwa) is protection, and it empties the Heart (Qalb) from Desires (Shahawat). So if the Remembrance (Dhikr) descends upon a Heart (Qalb) empty of anything other than Remembrance (Dhikr), Satan is repelled just as an ailment is repelled by the descent of medicine into an empty stomach free from foods. Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, in that is a reminder for whoever has a Heart (Qalb).' And He the Exalted said: 'It is decreed upon him that whoever takes him as an ally, then indeed, he misleads him and guides him to the punishment of the Blaze.' And whoever assists Satan with his action is his ally, even if he remembers Allah with his tongue. And if you say the hadith has come unrestricted that Remembrance (Dhikr) repels Satan, and you do not understand that most generalities of the Sharia are specified with conditions transmitted by the scholars of the religion, then look at yourself, for the report is not like witnessing, and contemplate that the ultimate of your Remembrance (Dhikr) and worship is the Prayer (Salah), so observe your Heart (Qalb) when you are in your Prayer (Salah) how Satan pulls it towards the markets, the accounting of the worlds, and the responses to the obstinate, and how he passes you through the valleys of the world and its perils, until you do not remember what you have forgotten of the excesses of the world except in your Prayer (Salah), and Satan does not crowd upon your Heart (Qalb) except when you pray. So the Prayer (Salah) is the test of the Hearts (Qalb), for through it their virtues and faults appear. The Prayer (Salah) is not accepted from Hearts (Qalb) filled with the Desires (Shahawat) of the world, so it is no wonder that Satan is not repelled from you; rather, perhaps he increases the whisperings upon you, just as medicine before protection perhaps increases harm upon you. So if you want deliverance from Satan, then precede protection with God-consciousness (Taqwa), then follow it with the medicine of Remembrance (Dhikr); Satan flees from you as he fled from Umar (may Allah be pleased with him).
22:4.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

22:5.arabic: فانظر إلى الأرض وهى ميتة فإذا أنزل عليها الماء اهتزت وربت واخضرت وأنبتت عجائب النبات وخرجت منها أصناف الحيوانات... ثم أنظر إلى أرض البوادى وفتش ظاهرها وباطنها فتراها ترابا متشابها فإذا أنزل عليها الماء اهتزت وربت وأنبتت من كل زوج بهيج الوانا مختلفة ونباتا متشابها وغير متشابه لكل واحد طعم وريح ولون وشكل يخالف الآخر
22:5.english: Then look at the earth when it is dead (ميتة), then when We send down upon it water, it quivers (اهتزت) and swells (ربت) and becomes green (اخضرت) and brings forth wondrous plants (عجائب النبات) and brings out from it various kinds of animals... Then look at the land of the deserts (أرض البوادى) and search its surface and its interior, and you will see it as similar dust (ترابا متشابها). Then when We send down upon it water, it quivers (اهتزت) and swells (ربت) and brings forth from every beautiful pair (من كل زوج بهيج) different colors and similar and dissimilar plants, each one having a taste (طعم), scent (ريح), color (لون), and shape (شكل) that differs from the other.
22:5.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Contemplation'

22:6.arabic: نسأل الله حسن التوفيق بلطفه وكرمه إنه على كل شيء قدير والحمد لله وحده.
22:6.english: We ask Allah for good success through His gentleness and generosity, indeed He is over all things capable (Qadir), and praise be to Allah alone.
22:6.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

22:7.arabic: وإنما تفنى الدنيا بالموت في حقه إلى أن تفنى في نفسها عند بلوغ الكتاب أجله وهذا الأنس يتلذذ به العبد بعد موته إلى أن ينزل في جوار الله عز وجل ويترقى من الذكر إلى اللقاء وذلك بعد أن يبعثر ما في القبور ويحصل ما في الصدور ولا ينكر بقاء ذكر الله عز وجل معه بعد الموت فيقول إنه أعدم فكيف يبقى معه ذكر الله عز وجل فإنه لم يعدم عدما يمنع الذكر بل عدما من الدنيا وعالم الملك والشهادة لا من عالم الملكوت وإلى ما ذكرناه الإشارة بقوله ﭬ: (القبر إما حفرة من حفر النار أو روضة من رياض الجنة[58]) وبقوله ﭬ: (أرواح ا
22:7.english: And the world perishes for him through death until it perishes in itself when the Book reaches its term. And this intimacy (Anas) is enjoyed by the servant after his death until he descends in the proximity of Allah, the Exalted, and ascends from the remembrance (Dhikr) to the meeting (Liqāʾ). And that is after what is in the graves is scattered and what is in the chests is realized. And one should not deny the remaining of the remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah, the Exalted, with him after death by saying: 'He has been annihilated, so how does the remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah, the Exalted, remain with him?' For he has not been annihilated with an annihilation that prevents remembrance (Dhikr), but rather with an annihilation from the world and the realm of dominion (Mulk) and testimony (Shahādah), not from the realm of sovereignty (Malakūt). And to what we have mentioned is the allusion by his saying ﭬ: ('The grave is either a pit from the pits of the Fire or a garden from the gardens of Paradise[58]') and by his saying ﭬ: ('The spirits (Arwāḥ) of the martyrs are in the crops of green birds[59]') and by his saying ﭬ to the slain of Badr from the polytheists: ('O so-and-so and O so-and-so'—and the Prophet ﭬ named them—'Have you found what your Lord promised to be true? For I have found what my Lord promised me to be true[60].' Then ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, heard his saying ﭬ and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, how do they hear and how do they respond when they have become decomposed?' He said ﭬ: 'By the One in Whose hand is my soul (Nafs), you are not more hearing of my speech than them, but they are not able to respond.') And the ḥadīth is in the Ṣaḥīḥ. This is his saying ﭬ regarding the polytheists. As for the believers and the martyrs, he has said ﭬ: ('Their spirits (Arwāḥ) are in the crops of green birds suspended beneath the Throne[61]'). And this state and what is alluded to by these expressions does not contradict the remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah, the Exalted. And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt in it, and that Allah will resurrect whoever is in the graves.﴾ And do not think of those who have been killed in the way of Allah as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for, rejoicing in what Allah has given them of His bounty, and receiving good tidings about those who have not yet joined them from behind them.
22:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith

22:7.arabic: وأن الجنة حق وأن النار حق والحوض حق والشفاعة حق ومنكرا ونكيرا حق ووعدك حق ووعيدك حق ولقاءك حق والساعة آتية لا ريب فيها وأن الله يبعث من في القبور على ذلك أحيا وعليه أموت وعليه أبعث إن شاء الله
22:7.english: And that Paradise is true and that the Fire is true and the Basin is true and the Intercession is true and Munkar and Nakir are true and Your promise is true and Your threat is true and meeting You is true and the Hour is coming, no doubt in it, and that Allah resurrects those in the graves. Upon that I live and upon that I die and upon that I will be resurrected, if Allah wills.
22:7.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter

22:11.arabic: وشرها في أن يسميه البطالون من أبناء الدنيا فاضلا محققا عالما بالدقائق وجزاؤه من الله أن لا ينتفع في الدنيا بقبول الخلق بل يتكدر عليه صفوه بنوائب الزمان ثم يرد القيامة مفلسا متحسرا على ما يشاهده من ربح العاملين وفوز المقربين وذلك هو الخسران المبين. ولقد كان الحسن البصري رحمه الله أشبه الناس كلاما بكلام الأنبياء عليهم الصلاة والسلام وأقربهم هديا من الصحابة رضي الله عنهم اتفقت الكلمة في حقه على ذلك وكان أكثر كلامه في خواطر القلوب وفساد الأعمال ووساس النفوس والصفات الخفية الغامضة من شهوات النفس وقد
22:11.english: And its evil is that the idle ones among the children of this world call him virtuous, verified, knowledgeable in subtleties, and his reward from Allah is that he does not benefit in this world by the acceptance of creation, rather his purity becomes troubled by the calamities of time, then he arrives at the Resurrection bankrupt, regretful over what he witnesses of the profit of the workers and the success of those brought near, and that is the manifest loss. And indeed, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, was the most similar of people in speech to the speech of the Prophets, peace be upon them, and the closest of them in guidance from the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them; the word agreed upon regarding him was that. And most of his speech was about the thoughts of the Hearts (Qalb), corruption of deeds, and the whisperings of the Souls (Nafs) and the hidden, obscure attributes from the desires of the Soul (Nafs). And it was said to him: O Abu Sa'eed, you speak with speech not heard from others, so from where did you take it? He said: From Hudhayfah ibn Al-Yaman. And it was said to Hudhayfah: We see you speaking with speech not heard from others among the Companions, so from where did you take it? He said: ((The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, singled me out with it; the people used to ask him about good, and I used to ask him about evil, fearing that I would fall into it, and I knew that good would not precede me in knowledge.)) And he said once: ((So I knew that whoever does not know evil does not know good.)) And in another wording: ((They used to say: O Messenger of Allah, what is for whoever does such and such? asking him about the virtues of deeds, and I used to say: O Messenger of Allah, what corrupts such and such? So when he saw me asking him about the afflictions of deeds, he singled me out with this knowledge.)) And Hudhayfah, may Allah be pleased with him, was also singled out with the knowledge of the hypocrites and uniquely endowed with knowing the knowledge of hypocrisy and its causes and the subtleties of trials, so 'Umar and 'Uthman and the great Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, used to ask him about the general trials and the
22:11.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

22:11.arabic: فرح الهالك برجائه فلم تبق له دنياه ولم يسلم له دينه "خسر الدنيا والآخرة ذلك هو الخسران المبين" فيا لها من مصيبة ما أفظعها ورزية ما أجلها، ألا فراقبوا الله إخواني ولا يغرنكم الشيطان وأولياؤه من الآنسين بالحجج الداحضة عند الله، فإنهم يتكالبون على الدنيا ثم يطلبون لأنفسهم المعاذير والحجج، ويزعمون أن أصحاب رسول الله ﭬ كانت لهم أموال فيتزين المغرورون بذكر الصحابة ليعذرهم الناس على جمع المال، ولقد دهاهم الشيطان وما يشعرون.
22:11.english: The perished one rejoices in his hope, yet his worldly life does not remain for him, nor does his religion (Deen) remain secure for him. "He has lost the worldly life and the Hereafter; that is the manifest loss." Oh, what a calamity, how dreadful it is, and what a great disaster! Indeed, fear Allah (Taqwa), my brothers, and do not let Satan and his allies from among those who are intimate with flimsy arguments before Allah deceive you. For they scramble after the worldly life, then seek excuses and arguments for themselves, and claim that the companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) had wealth, so the deceived ones adorn themselves with the mention of the companions to excuse themselves before people for accumulating wealth. And Satan has indeed overwhelmed them, while they are unaware.
22:11.book_title: Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth
22:11.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

22:13.arabic: ومثله من الحيوانات الفأرة و العقرب كما قال تعالى يدعو لمن ضره أقرب من نفعه لبئس المولى ولبئس العشير وقال الشاعر الناس شتى إذا ما أنت ذقتهم لا يستوون كما لا يستوي الشجر هذا له ثمر حلو مذاقته وذاك ليس له طعم و لا ثمر
22:13.english: And its likeness among animals is the mouse and the scorpion, as The Exalted said: 'He calls upon one whose harm is closer than his benefit; wretched is the protector and wretched is the companion.' And the poet said: 'People are diverse when you taste them; they are not equal just as trees are not equal—this one has sweet-tasting fruit, and that one has no taste and no fruit.'
22:13.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

22:15.arabic: وقال عليه السلام من ستر عوره أخيه ستره الله تعالى في الدنيا الآخرة حديث من ستر عورة أخيه ستره الله في الدنيا الآخرة أخرجه ابن ماجه من حديث ابن عباس و قال يوم القيامة ولم يقل في الدنيا و لمسلم من حديث أبي هريرة من ستر مسلما ستره الله في الدنيا و الآخرة وللشيخين من حديث ابن عمر من ستر مسلما ستره الله يوم القيامة وفي خبر آخر فكأنما أحيا موءودة حديث فكأنما أحيا موءودة من قبرها أخرجه أبو داود والنسائي و الحاكم من حديث عقبة بن عامر من رأى عورة فسترها كان كمن أحيا موءودة زاد الحاكم من قبرها وقال صحيح ا
22:15.english: And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever covers the shame (عورة) of his brother, Allah will cover him in this world and the hereafter.' Hadith: 'Whoever covers the shame (عورة) of his brother, Allah will cover him in this world and the hereafter' - reported by Ibn Majah from the narration of Ibn Abbas, and he said 'on the Day of Resurrection' and did not say 'in this world'. And Muslim reported from the narration of Abu Hurairah: 'Whoever covers a Muslim, Allah will cover him in this world and the hereafter.' And the two Sheikhs (Bukhari and Muslim) reported from the narration of Ibn Umar: 'Whoever covers a Muslim, Allah will cover him on the Day of Resurrection.' And in another report: 'It is as if he revived a buried alive female infant (موءودة).' Hadith: 'It is as if he revived a buried alive female infant (موءودة) from her grave' - reported by Abu Dawud, Al-Nasa'i, and Al-Hakim from the narration of Uqbah bin Amir: 'Whoever sees a shame (عورة) and covers it, it is as if he revived a buried alive female infant (موءودة).' Al-Hakim added 'from her grave' and said: 'Its chain is authentic.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'If a man relates a narration and then turns away, it is a trust (أمانة).' Hadith: 'If a man relates a narration and then turns away, it is a trust (أمانة)' - reported by Abu Dawud and Al-Tirmidhi from the narration of Jabir, and he said: 'Hasan.' And he said: 'Gatherings are with trust (أمانة) except three gatherings: a gathering in which unlawful blood is shed, a gathering in which unlawful private parts (فرج) are made lawful, and a gathering in which wealth from other than its lawful source is made lawful.' Hadith: 'Gatherings are with trust (أمانة) except three gatherings' - the hadith reported by Abu Dawud from the narration of Jabir from the narration of his nephew, unnamed from him. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, two people who sit together do so with trust (أمانة), and it is not lawful for one of them to disclose about his companion what he dislikes.' Hadith: 'Indeed, two people who sit together do so with trust (أمانة); it is not lawful for one of them to disclose about his companion what he dislikes' - reported by Abu Bakr bin La.
22:15.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

22:18.arabic: فإن قلت: ليس في قولك "لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله" إلا نسبة شيئين إلى الله، فلو قال قائل: السماء والأرض خلق الله فهل يكون ثوابه مثل ثوابه؟ فأقول: لا، لأن الثواب على قدر درجة المثاب عليه ولا مساواة بين الدرجتين ولا ينظر إلى عظم السماء والأرض وصغر الحول والقوة إن جاز وصفهما بالصغر تجاوزاً، فليست الأمور بعظم الأشخاص بل كل عامي يفهم أن الأرض والسماء ليستا من جهة الآدميين بل هما من خلق الله تعالى، فأما الحول والقوة فقد أشكل أمرهما على المعتزلة والفلاسفة وطوائف كثيرة ممن يدعي أنه يدقق النظر في الرأي والم
22:18.english: If you say: In your statement "There is no power (Hawl) nor strength (Quwwah) except with Allah" there is only the attribution of two things to Allah, so if someone says: The sky and the earth are Allah's creation, would his reward be like his reward? I say: No, because the reward is according to the degree of what is rewarded upon, and there is no equality between the two degrees, and one does not look at the greatness of the sky and the earth and the smallness of power (Hawl) and strength (Quwwah) if it is permissible to describe them as small by way of concession. For matters are not by the greatness of persons, rather every common person understands that the earth and the sky are not from the aspect of humans but they are from the creation of Allah the Exalted. As for power (Hawl) and strength (Quwwah), their matter has become obscure to the Mu'tazilites, the philosophers, and many groups who claim that they scrutinize opinion and reason until they split hair with the sharpness of their insight. This is a destructive danger and a great slippery slope in which the heedless have perished when they affirmed for themselves a matter which is polytheism (Shirk) in Divine Oneness (Tawhid) and affirmation of a creator other than Allah the Exalted. So whoever crosses this obstacle by Allah's facilitation for him, his rank has risen and his degree has become great, and he is the one who truthfully says "There is no power (Hawl) nor strength (Quwwah) except with Allah." And we have mentioned that in Divine Oneness (Tawhid) there are only two obstacles: one of them is looking at the sky and the earth and the sun and the moon and the stars and the clouds and the rain and other inanimate objects, and the second is looking at the choice of animals, and it is the greater of the two obstacles and the more dangerous, and by cutting them off is the perfection of the secret of Divine Oneness (Tawhid). Therefore, the reward of this word is great, I mean the reward of witnessing (Mushahadah) which this word translates. So when the state of reliance (Tawakkul) returns to disavowal from power (Hawl) and strength (Quwwah) and reliance (Tawakkul) on the One Truth, and it will become clear when we mention the details of the works of reliance (Tawakkul), Allah willing.
22:18.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

22:19.arabic: وأما الكافر فإنه إذا كان في قبل من الآخرة وانقطاع من الدنيا نزلت إليه ملائكة غلاظ شداد معهم ثياب من نار وسرابيل من قطران فيحتوشونه فإذا خرجت نفسه لعنه كل ملك بين السماء والأرض وكل ملك في السماء وغلقت أبواب السماء فليس بها باب إلا يكره أن يدخل بروحه منه فإذا صعد بروحه نبذ وقيل أي رب عبدك فلان لم تقبله سماء ولا أرض فيقول الله عز وجل ارجعوه فأروه ما أعددت له من الشر إني وعدته ﴿ منها خلقناكم وفيها نعيدكم ومنها نخرجكم تارة أخرى ﴾ {}الآية وأنه ليسمع خفق نعالهم إذا ولوا مدبرين حتى يقال له يا هذا من ربك
22:19.english: As for the disbeliever, when he is in the approach of the Hereafter and cut off from the worldly life, harsh and severe angels descend to him with garments of fire and shirts of pitch, and they surround him. When his soul (Ruh) emerges, every angel between the heavens and the earth and every angel in the heavens curses him, and the gates of the heavens are closed—there is no gate except that it dislikes his soul (Ruh) entering through it. When his soul ascends, it is cast away, and it is said: 'O Lord, Your servant so-and-so—no heaven accepted him, nor earth.' Then Allah, the Exalted, says: 'Return him and show him what I have prepared for him of evil; indeed, I promised him: "From it (the earth) We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will bring you out another time." (Quran 20:55) And he hears the shuffling of their sandals when they turn away retreating, until it is said to him: 'O you, who is your Lord, and who is your prophet, and what is your religion?' He says: 'I do not know.' It is said: 'You did not know.' Then comes to him one with an ugly face, foul odor, and ugly garments, and says: 'Receive glad tidings of wrath from Allah and a painful, lasting punishment.' He says: 'May Allah give you evil as glad tidings—who are you?' He says: 'I am your evil deed (Amal). By Allah, you were indeed swift in disobedience to Allah and slow in obedience to Allah, so may Allah reward you with evil.' He says: 'And may Allah reward you with evil.' Then is appointed for him a blind, deaf, and dumb one with an iron club—if the two weighty ones (jinn and mankind) gathered to lift it, they would not be able—if he struck a mountain with it, it would become dust. He strikes him with it a blow, and he becomes dust. Then the soul (Ruh) returns to him, and he strikes him with it between his eyes a blow heard by those on the earths, not the two weighty ones. Then a caller calls out: 'Spread for him two slabs of fire and open for him a gate to the Fire.' So two slabs of fire are spread for him, and a gate to the Fire is opened for him.
22:19.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

22:19.arabic: ومهما دعوا بالثبور صب من فوق رءوسهم الحميم يصهر به ما في بطونهم والجلود ولهم مقامع من حديد تهشم بها جباههم فيتفجر الصديد من أفواههم وننقطع من العطش أكبادهم وتسيل على الخدود أحداقهم ويسقط من الوجنات لحومها ويتمعط من الأطراف شعورها بل جلودها وكلما نضجت جلودهم بدلوا جلودا غيرها قد عريت من اللحم عظامهم فبقيت الأرواح منوطة بالعروق وعلائق العصب وهى تنش فى لفح تلك النيران وهم مع ذلك يتمنون الموت فلا يموتون فكيف بك لو نظرت إليهم وقد سوّدت وجوههم أشد سوادا من الحميم وأعميت أبصارهم وأبكمت ألسنتهم وقصمت ظه
22:19.english: And whenever they call for destruction, boiling water is poured from above their heads, melting what is in their bellies and the skins. And they have mallets of iron that shatter their foreheads, so pus gushes from their mouths, and their livers are severed from thirst, and their eyeballs flow on the cheeks, and flesh falls from the jaws, and hair is pulled out from the extremities, indeed their skins. And whenever their skins are roasted, they are replaced with other skins, their bones have been stripped of flesh, so the spirits remain tied to the veins and nerve connections, and they are roasted in the blast of those fires, and they with that wish for death but do not die. How would it be if you saw them, and their faces have been blackened, blacker than boiling water, and their sights have been blinded, and their tongues have been silenced, and their backs have been broken, and their bones have been fractured, and their ears have been cut off, and their skins have been torn, and their hands have been shackled to their necks, and gathered between their foreheads and their feet, and they walk on the fire with their faces and tread on the thorns of iron with their eyeballs, so the flame of the fire travels in the inner parts of their components, and the snakes of the abyss and its scorpions are clinging to the outer parts of their limbs. This is some of the summary of their conditions, and look now at the detailing of their horrors, and contemplate also in the valleys of Hell and its paths, for the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: (Indeed in Hell are seventy thousand valleys, in every valley seventy thousand paths, in every path seventy thousand serpents and seventy thousand scorpions, the disbeliever and hypocrite do not cease until all that befalls them[195]), and said Ali, may Allah honor his face, said the Messenger of...
22:19.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

22:23.arabic: قال الله تعالى: ﴿ يحلون فيها من أساور من ذهب ولؤلؤا ولباسهم فيها حرير ﴾ والآيات فى ذلك كثيرة وإنما تفصيله فى الأخبار فقد روى أبو هريرة أن النبي ﭬ قال: (من يدخل الجنة ينعم لا يبأس لا تبلى ثيابه ولا يفنى شبابه فى الجنة ما لا عين رأت ولا أذن سمعت ولا خطر عن قلب بشر[231]). (وقال رجل: يا رسول الله أخبرنا عن ثياب أهل الجنة أخلق تخلق أم نسج تنسج فسكت رسول الله ﭬ وضحك بعض القوم فقال رسول الله ﭬ مم تضحكون من جاهل سأل عالما ثم قال رسول الله ﭬ: بل ينشق عنها ثمر الجنة مرتين[232]) وقال أبو هريرة قال رسول الل
22:23.english: Allah the Exalted said: 'They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their garments therein will be silk.' And the verses about that are many, but its detail is in the reports. Indeed, Abu Hurairah reported that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever enters Paradise enjoys without misery, his clothes do not wear out, nor does his youth perish in Paradise—what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has not occurred to the heart (Qalb) of a human.' And a man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, inform us about the clothes of the people of Paradise—are they created as creation or woven as weaving?' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) remained silent, and some of the people laughed. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Why do you laugh at an ignorant one asking a knowledgeable one?' Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Rather, they split from the fruit of Paradise twice.' And Abu Hurairah said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, the first group to enter Paradise, their form is like the form of the moon on the night of the full moon; they do not spit therein, nor blow their noses, nor defecate; their vessels and combs are of gold and silver, and their sweat is musk; for each of them are two wives—the marrow of her shin is seen from behind the flesh due to beauty; there is no disagreement among them nor hatred; their hearts (Qulub) are upon one heart (Qalb); they glorify Allah morning and evening (and in a narration) on each wife are seventy garments.' And he (peace be upon him) said regarding His statement: 'They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold,' he said: 'Indeed, upon them are crowns; the lowest pearl therein illuminates what is between the east and the west.'
22:23.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

22:23.arabic: (صفة لباس أهل الجنة وفرشهم وسررهم وأرائكهم وخيامهم) قال الله تعالى: ﴿ يحلون فيها من أساور من ذهب ولؤلؤا ولباسهم فيها حرير ﴾ والآيات فى ذلك كثيرة وإنما تفصيله فى الأخبار فقد روى أبو هريرة أن النبي ﭬ قال: (من يدخل الجنة ينعم لا يبأس لا تبلى ثيابه ولا يفنى شبابه فى الجنة ما لا عين رأت ولا أذن سمعت ولا خطر عن قلب بشر[231]). (وقال رجل: يا رسول الله أخبرنا عن ثياب أهل الجنة أخلق تخلق أم نسج تنسج فسكت رسول الله ﭬ وضحك بعض القوم فقال رسول الله ﭬ مم تضحكون من جاهل سأل عالما ثم قال رسول الله ﭬ: بل ينشق عن
22:23.english: (Description of the clothing of the people of Paradise and their furnishings, beds, couches, and tents) Allah the Exalted said: 'They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their garments therein will be silk.' And the verses regarding that are many, and its detail is in the narrations. Indeed, Abu Hurairah reported that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever enters Paradise enjoys bliss without misery, his clothes do not wear out, nor does his youth perish in Paradise, what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has not occurred to the heart (Qalb) of a human.' And a man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, inform us about the clothes of the people of Paradise, are they created or woven?' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) remained silent, and some of the people laughed. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Why do you laugh at an ignorant one asking a knowledgeable one?' Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Rather, it splits from the fruit of Paradise twice.' And Abu Hurairah said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, the first group to enter Paradise, their form is like the form of the moon on the night of the full moon; they do not spit in it, nor blow their noses, nor defecate; their utensils and combs are of gold and silver, and their sweat is musk; each one of them has two wives, the marrow of whose shins is seen from behind the flesh due to beauty; there is no disagreement among them nor hatred; their hearts (Qulub) are upon one heart (Qalb); they glorify Allah morning and evening (and in a narration) each wife has seventy garments.' And he (peace be upon him) said regarding His statement: 'They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold': 'Indeed, upon them are crowns; the lowest pearl among them illuminates what is between the east and the west.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The tent is a hollow pearl, its length in the sky is sixty miles; in every corner of it, for the believer, are people who do not see them.'
22:23.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

22:23.arabic: [234] حديث في قوله تعالى - يحلون فيها من أساور من ذهب - قال إن عليهم التيجان أدنى لؤلؤة فيها تضىء ما بين المشرق والمغرب أخرجه الترمذى من حديث أبى سعيد دون ذكر الآية وقال لا نعرفه إلا من حديث رشد بن سعد.
22:23.english: [234] A hadith regarding His saying, the Exalted - 'They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold' - he said: Upon them are crowns, the smallest pearl therein illuminates what is between the east and the west. It was reported by Al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Abu Sa'id without mentioning the verse, and he said: We do not know it except from the hadith of Rashid bin Sa'd.
22:23.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Book of Repentance'

22:25.arabic: فهؤلاء شياطين الإنس ضلوا وأضلوا عن سواء السبيل، فإن الأولين وإن لم يصلحوا أنفسهم فقد أصلحوا غيرهم وصححوا كلامهم ووعظهم. وأما هؤلاء فإنهم يصدون عن سبيل الله ويجرون الخلق إلى الغرور بالله بلفظ الرجاء فيزيدهم كلامهم جرأة على المعاصي ورغبة في الدنيا، لا سيما إذا كان الواعظ متزيناً بالثياب والخيل والمراكب فإنه تشهد هيئته من فرقه إلى قدمه بشدة حرصه على الدنيا فما يفسده هذا المغرور أكثر مما يصلحه بل لا يصلح أصلاً ويضل خلقاً كثيراً ولا يخفى وجه كونه مغروراً.
22:25.english: These are the devils among mankind who have gone astray and led others astray from the straight path (sawāʾ al-sabīl). For the former group, even if they did not rectify themselves, they rectified others and corrected their speech and admonition. As for these, they hinder from the path of Allah (ṣaddūna ʿan sabīl Allāh) and drag creation into delusion about Allah with words of hope, increasing their audacity toward sins and desire for the worldly life, especially if the preacher is adorned with clothes, horses, and vehicles, for his appearance from his head to his feet testifies to his intense craving for the worldly life. Thus, what this deluded one corrupts is more than what he rectifies; indeed, he does not rectify at all and misleads many people, and the aspect of his being deluded is not hidden.
22:25.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

22:25.arabic: وقال ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه: ما من بلد يؤاخذ فيه العبد بالنية قبل العمل إلا مكة وتلا قوله تعالى: ﴿ ومن يرد فيه بإلحاد بظلم نذقه من عذاب أليم ﴾ {} أي أنه على مجرد الإرادة. ويقال: إن السيئات تضاعف بها كما تضاعف الحسنات. وكان ابن عباس رضي الله عنه يقول: الاحتكار بمكة من الإلحاد في الحرم وقيل الكذب أيضا. وقال ابن عباس: لأن أذنب سبعين ذنبا بركية أحب إلي من أن أذنب ذنبا واحدا بمكة، وركية منزل بين مكة والطائف.
22:25.english: And Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: There is no city where the servant is held accountable for the intention (niyyah) before the action except Mecca, and he recited the saying of Allah the Exalted: 'And whoever intends therein deviation (ilhad) with injustice (zulm), We will make him taste of a painful punishment' (Quran 22:25) {} meaning that it is based on mere intention (iradah). And it is said: The sins are multiplied there just as the good deeds are multiplied. And Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) used to say: Hoarding (ihtikar) in Mecca is from deviation (ilhad) in the Sacred Sanctuary (haram), and lying is also said to be so. And Ibn Abbas said: For me to commit seventy sins in Rukiyah is more beloved to me than to commit one sin in Mecca, and Rukiyah is a station between Mecca and Ta'if.
22:25.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

22:25.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى سواء العاكف فيه والباد من جعل لك هذا فنظر في وجهه وكان بعرفه لأنه من مواليهم فقال أعبد الله ابن مرزوق قال نعم فأخذ فجىء به إلى بغداد فكره أن يعاقبه عقوبة يشنع بها عليه في العامة فجعله في اصطبل الدواب ليسوس الدواب وضموا إليه فرسا عضوضا سيىء الخلق ليعقره الفرس فلين الله تعالى له الفرس قال ثم صيروه إلى بيت وأغلق عليه وأخذ المهدي المفتاح عنده فإذا هو قد خرج بعد ثلاث إلى البستان يأكل البقل فأوذن به المهدي فقال له من أخرجك فقال الذي حبسني فضج المهدي وصاح وقال ما تخاف أن أقتلك فرفع ع
22:25.english: And Allah the Exalted said: 'Equal (sawāʾ) is the resident (al-ʿākif) in it and the visitor (al-bād) - who made this for you?' Then he looked at his face and recognized him because he was from their clients, so he said: 'Are you ʿAbd Allāh ibn Marzūq?' He said: 'Yes.' So he was taken and brought to Baghdad, and he disliked punishing him with a punishment that would disgrace him publicly, so he placed him in the stable of animals to manage the animals, and they assigned to him a vicious horse with bad character so that the horse would trample him, but Allah the Exalted softened the horse for him. He said: Then they confined him to a house and locked it, and al-Mahdī took the key with him, and behold, he had come out after three days to the garden eating herbs, so al-Mahdī was informed of him. He said to him: 'Who released you?' He said: 'The One who imprisoned me.' So al-Mahdī cried out and shouted and said: 'Do you not fear that I will kill you?' So ʿAbd Allāh raised his head to him laughing and saying: 'If you possessed life or death...' And he remained imprisoned until al-Mahdī died, then they released him and he returned to Mecca. He said: And he had made upon himself a vow (nadhr) that if Allah delivered him from their hands, he would slaughter one hundred camels, and he worked on that until he slaughtered them.
22:25.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

22:25.arabic: وقيل في قوله تعالى ومن يرد فيه بإلحاد بظلم نذقه من عذاب أليم إن الاحتكار من الظلم وداخل تحته في الوعيد
22:25.english: And it is said regarding His statement, the Exalted: 'And whoever intends therein deviation with injustice, We will make him taste a painful punishment' (Quran 22:25), that hoarding (Ihtikar) is from injustice (Zulm) and falls under this threat.
22:25.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Etiquette of Earning'

22:26.arabic:
قال  فقه  الأعرابي[28])  وفيه
أيضا: (إن الله تعالى شرف الكعبة وعظمها  ولو  أن  عبدا  هدمها  حجرا  حجرا  ثم
أحرقها ما بلغ جرم من استخف بولي من أولياء  الله  تعالى.  قال  الأعرابي:  ومن

عز وجل: ﴿ الله ولي الذين آمنوا يخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور  ﴾  {})  وفي  بعض
الاخبار: (المؤمن أفضل من الكعبة[29]) (والمؤمن طيب  طاهر[30])  (والمؤمن  أكرم
على الله تعالى من الملائكة[31]) وفي الخبر:  (خلق  الله  تعالى  جهنم  من  فضل
رحمته سو
22:26.english: The jurisprudence (Fiqh) of the Bedouin said [28], and in it also: (Indeed, Allah the Exalted honored and magnified the Kaaba, and if a servant were to demolish it stone by stone then burn it, it would not reach the crime of one who belittles a friend (Wali) from the friends (Awliya) of Allah the Exalted. The Bedouin said: And who are the friends (Awliya) of Allah the Exalted? He said: The believers (Mu'minun) all are friends (Awliya) of Allah the Exalted. Have you not heard the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: 'Allah is the friend (Wali) of those who believe (Amanu), He brings them out from the darknesses into the light' {}. And in some reports: (The believer (Mu'min) is better than the Kaaba [29]) (And the believer (Mu'min) is good and pure [30]) (And the believer (Mu'min) is more honored with Allah the Exalted than the angels [31]). And in the report: (Allah the Exalted created Hell from the surplus of His mercy as a whip to drive His servants to Paradise [32]). And in another report: (Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: I only created the creation so they would profit from Me, and I did not create them to profit from them [33]). And in the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: (Allah the Exalted did not create anything except He made for it what overcomes it and made His mercy overcome His anger [34]). And in the famous report: (Indeed, Allah the Exalted wrote upon Himself mercy before He created the creation: My mercy overcomes My anger [35]). And from Mu'adh ibn Jabal and Anas ibn Malik that he ﷺ said: (Whoever says 'There is no god but Allah' enters Paradise [36]). (And whoever's last words are 'There is no god but Allah', the Fire will not touch him [37]). (And whoever meets Allah not associating anything with Him, the Fire is forbidden upon him [38]). (And none enters it who has in his heart (Qalb) an atom's weight of faith (Iman) [39]). And in another report: (If the disbeliever (Kafir) knew the vastness of Allah's mercy, no one would despair of His Paradise [40]). And when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited His saying the Exalted: 'Indeed, the earthquake of the Hour is a tremendous thing' {}, he said: Do you know what day this is? This is a day when it is said to Adam, upon him be peace: Arise and send forth the dispatch to the Fire from your offspring. He says: How many? It is said: From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine to the Fire and one to Paradise. He said: So the people despaired and began to weep and became idle that day from engagement and work. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to them and said: What is with you? Why do you not work? They said: And who engages in work after what you have told us of this? He said: How many are you among the nations? Where are the interpretation and the inheritance and the ritual and Gog and Magog? Nations that none can enumerate except Allah the Exalted. You are among the other nations like the white hair on the skin of a black ox and like the mark on the forearm of a beast [41]. So look how he would drive the creation with the whips of fear and lead them with the reins of hope to Allah the Exalted, for he drove them with the whips of fear first, then when that took them beyond the limit of moderation to the excess of despair, he treated them with the medicine of hope and returned them to moderation and balance, and the latter was not contradictory to the former, but he mentioned in the first what he saw as a cause for healing and confined himself to it.
22:26.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Fear and Hope'

22:27.arabic: فأنعم الله عز وجل على هذه الأمة بأن جعل الحج رهبانية لهم فشرف البيت العتيق بالإضافة إلى نفسه تعالى ونصبه مقصدا لعباده وجعل ما حواليه حرما لبيته تفخيما لأمره وجعل عرفات كالميزاب على فناء حوضه وأكد حرمة الموضع بتحريم صيده وشجره ووضعه على مثال حضرة الملوك يقصده الزوار من كل فج عميق ومن كل أوب سحيق شعثا غبرا متواضعين لرب البيت ومستكينين له خضوعا لجلاله واستكانة لعزته مع الاعتراف بتنزيهه عن أن يحويه بيت أو يكتنفه بلد ليكون ذلك أبلغ في رقهم وعبوديتهم وأتم في إذعانهم وانقيادهم ولذلك وظف عليهم فيها أعما
22:27.english: So Allah the Exalted and Glorified bestowed favor upon this nation by making the Pilgrimage (Hajj) a monasticism (Rahbaniyyah) for them. He honored the Ancient House (Al-Bayt Al-'Atiq) by associating it with His own Self, the Exalted, and established it as a destination for His servants. He made its surroundings a sanctuary (Haram) for His House, magnifying its affair. He made 'Arafat like a spout over the courtyard of His basin. He affirmed the sanctity of the place by prohibiting its game and trees, and placed it on the model of the presence of kings, visited by pilgrims from every deep mountain pass (min kulli fajjin 'amiqin) and from every distant return, disheveled, dusty, humbling themselves to the Lord of the House and submitting to Him, in submission to His majesty and surrender to His might, while acknowledging His transcendence (Tanzih) from being contained by a house or encompassed by a land, so that this would be more profound in their servitude (Raqq) and slavery ('Ubūdiyyah) and more complete in their submission and compliance. Therefore, He prescribed for them therein actions that the Souls (Nufūs) find no comfort in, and the intellects ('Uqūl) do not grasp the meanings of, such as stoning the pillars (Jamarat) with stones and going back and forth between Safa and Marwah in repetition. Through such actions, the perfection of servitude and slavery becomes apparent.
22:27.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

22:27.arabic: وليُتذَكَّرِ المُلَبِّي عِندَ رَفْعِ الصَّوْتِ بِالتَّلْبِيَةِ فِي المِيقَاتِ إجَابَتَهُ لِنِدَاءِ اللهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ إِذْ قَالَ: وَأَذِّنْ فِي النَّاسِ بِالْحَجِّ يَأْتُوكَ رِجَالًا وَعَلَىٰ كُلِّ ضَامِرٍ يَأْتِينَ مِنْ كُلِّ فَجٍّ عَمِيقٍ، وَنِدَاءِ الخَلْقِ بِنَفْخِ الصُّورِ وَحَشْرِهِمْ مِنَ القُبُورِ وَازْدِحَامِهِمْ فِي عَرَصَاتِ القِيَامَةِ مُجِيبِينَ لِنِدَاءِ اللهِ سُبْحَانَهُ وَمُنْقَسِمِينَ إِلَى مُقَرَّبِينَ وَمَمْقُوتِينَ وَمَقْبُولِينَ وَمَرْدُودِينَ وَمُتَرَدِّدِينَ فِي أَوَّلِ ا
22:27.english: And let the one performing the talbiyah (ritual call) remember, upon raising the voice with the talbiyah at the miqat (designated station for entering ihram), his answering of the call of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, when He said: 'And proclaim to the people the pilgrimage; they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel from every distant pass.' And the call of the creation with the blowing of the trumpet (Sur) and their gathering from the graves and their crowding in the courtyards of the Resurrection, answering the call of Allah, Glorified is He, and being divided into those brought near (muqarrabin), those detested (mamqutin), those accepted (maqbulin), those rejected (mardudin), and those hesitant (mutaraddidin) at the beginning of the matter between fear (khawf) and hope (raja'), like the hesitation of the pilgrim at the miqat where they do not know whether the completion of the pilgrimage and its acceptance will be facilitated for them or not.
22:27.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

22:27.arabic: قال الله عز وجل: ﴿ وأذن في الناس بالحج يأتوك رجالا وعلى كل ضامر يأتين من كل فج عميق ﴾ {} وقال قتادة: لما أمر الله عز وجل إبراهيم ﭬ وعلى نبينا وعلى كل عبد مصطفى أن يؤذن في الناس بالحج نادى: يا أيها الناس إن الله عز وجل بنى بيتا فحجوه، وقال تعالى: ﴿ ليشهدوا منافع لهم ﴾ {} قيل التجارة في الموسم والأجر في الآخرة ولما سمع بعض السلف هذا قال غفر لهم ورب الكعبة وقيل في تفسير قوله عز وجل: ﴿ لأقعدن لهم صراطك المستقيم ﴾ {} أي طريق مكة يقعد الشيطان عليها ليمنع الناس منها وقال ﭬ: (من حج البيت فلم يرفث ولم يف
22:27.english: Allah the Exalted said: 'And proclaim to the people the Pilgrimage (Hajj); they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel; they will come from every distant pass.' And Qatadah said: When Allah the Exalted commanded Abraham (peace be upon him) and our Prophet (peace be upon him) and every chosen servant (Abd) to proclaim to the people the Pilgrimage (Hajj), he called out: O people, indeed Allah the Exalted has built a House, so perform pilgrimage to it. And He the Exalted said: 'That they may witness benefits for themselves.' It is said: trade during the season and reward in the Hereafter. And when some of the predecessors (Salaf) heard this, he said: May they be forgiven, by the Lord of the Kaaba. And it is said in the interpretation of His the Exalted's saying: 'I will surely sit in ambush for them on Your straight path (Sirat)' meaning the road to Mecca; Satan sits on it to prevent people from it. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever performs pilgrimage to the House and does not commit obscenity or sin, he emerges from his sins like the day his mother gave birth to him.' And he (peace be upon him) also said: 'Satan has never been seen on a day smaller, more defeated, more despised, or more furious than on the day of Arafah.' And that is only because of what he sees of the descent of mercy and Allah the Glorified's overlooking of great sins, as it is said: 'Indeed among sins are sins that are not expiated except by standing at Arafah.' And Ja'far ibn Muhammad attributed it to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him). And some of the unveilers (Mukashifin) from the close ones (Muqarrabin) mentioned: That Iblis, may Allah's curse be upon him, appeared to him in the form of a person at Arafah, and he was emaciated in body, yellow in color, weeping in eye, hunched in back. He said to him: What has made your eye weep? He said: The departure of the pilgrims to Him without trade; I say they have intended Him, I fear that He will not disappoint them, so it saddens me.
22:27.topic: Al-Ghazali on the outer and inner dimensions of worship, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

22:27.arabic: [81] حديث يقول الله تعالى انظروا إلى زوار بيتي قد جاءوا شعثا غبرا من كل فج عميق أخرجه الحاكم وصححه من حديث أبي هريرة دون قوله من كل فج عميق وكذا رواه أحمد من حديث عبد الله بن عمر.
22:27.english: [81] A hadith: Allah the Exalted says: 'Look at the visitors of My House; they have come disheveled (Shu'ath), dusty (Ghubar) from every deep (Amīq) path (Fajj).' Al-Hakim authenticated it from the narration of Abu Hurairah, without his saying 'from every deep path,' and similarly Ahmad narrated it from the narration of Abdullah ibn Umar.
22:27.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

22:31.arabic: وذلك من الأخبار ما روي أن أصحاب رسول الله ﷺ شكوا إليه وقالوا: تعرض لقلوبنا أشياء لأن تخر من السماء فتخطفنا الطير أو تهوي بنا الريح في مكان سحيق أحب إلينا من أن نتكلم بها، فقال عليه السلام "أو قد وجدتموه" قالوا: نعم قال "ذلك صريح الإيمان"[50] ولم يجدوا إلا الوسواس والكراهة له، ولا يمكن أن يقال أراد بصريح الإيمان الوسوسة، فلم يبق إلا حمله على الكراهة المساوقة للوسوسة، والرياء وإن كان عظيماً فهو دون الوسوسة في حق الله تعالى، فإذا اندفع ضرر الأعظم بالكراهة فبأن يندفع بها ضرر الأصغر أولى
22:31.english: And that from the reports is what was narrated that the companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) complained to him and said: 'There appear to our hearts (Qulub) things such that to fall from the sky and the birds snatch us or the wind hurls us in a far place is more beloved to us than that we speak of them.' He (upon him be peace) said: 'Or have you found it?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'That is pure faith (Iman).' And they found nothing except the whispering (Waswas) and hatred for it, and it cannot be said that he meant by pure faith the whispering, so nothing remains except to carry it on the hatred accompanying the whispering. And showing off (Riya'), even if it is great, it is less than the whispering in the right of Allah the Exalted, so if the harm of the greater is repelled by hatred, then that the harm of the smaller be repelled by it is more appropriate.
22:31.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

22:32.arabic: التاسع: أن يتقرب بإراقة دم وإن لم يكن واجبا عليه ويجتهد أن يكون من سمين النعم ونفيسه وليأكل منه إن كان تطوعا ولا يأكل منه إن كان واجبا قيل في تفسير قوله تعالى - ذلك ومن يعظم شعائر الله - إنه تحسينه وتسمينه وسوق الهدي من الميقات أفضل إن كان لا يجهده ولا يكده وليترك المكاس في شرائه فقد كانوا يغالون في ثلاث ويكرهون المكاس فيهن الهدي والأضحية والرقبة فإن أفضل ذلك أغلاه ثمنا وأنفسه عند أهله.
22:32.english: Ninth: That one draws near (to Allah) by shedding blood (sacrifice) even if it is not obligatory upon him, and he strives that it be from the fattened and precious livestock, and let him eat from it if it is voluntary, but not eat from it if it is obligatory. It is said in the interpretation of His saying, the Exalted - 'That (is so). And whoever honors the symbols (Sha'a'ir) of Allah - indeed, it is from the piety (Taqwa) of the hearts (Qulub)' - that it is its beautification and fattening, and driving the sacrificial animal (Hady) from the designated place (Miqat) is better if it does not exhaust or strain it, and let him avoid haggling in its purchase, for they used to be extravagant in three things and disliked haggling in them: the sacrificial animal (Hady), the sacrifice (Udhiyah), and the slave (Raqabah), for the best of that is the most expensive in price and the most precious to its owner.
22:32.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

22:37.arabic: وقد خصص الله تعالى التقوى بالإضافة إلى نفسه فقال تعالى: ﴿ لن ينال الله لحومها ولا دماؤها ولكن يناله التقوى منكم ﴾ {} وإنما التقوى عبارة عن كف بمقتضى الخوف كما سبق ولذلك قال تعالى: ﴿ إن أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم ﴾ {} ولذلك أوصى الله تعالى الأولين والآخرين بالتقوى فقال تعالى: ﴿ ولقد وصينا الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم وإياكم أن اتقوا الله ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل: ﴿ وخافون إن كنتم مؤمنين ﴾ {} فأمر بالخوف وأوجبه وشرطه في الإيمان فلذلك لا يتصور أن ينفك مؤمن عن خوف وإن ضعف ويكون ضعف خوفه بحسب ضعف معرفته وإيمانه
22:37.english: And Allah the Exalted has specified Piety (Taqwa) by attributing it to Himself, for He said: 'Never will their flesh nor their blood reach Allah, but what reaches Him is Piety (Taqwa) from you' (22:37). Indeed, Piety (Taqwa) is an expression of restraint due to Fear (Khauf) as previously mentioned. Therefore, He said: 'Indeed, the most noble of you with Allah is the most pious (Atqakum) among you' (49:13). And therefore, Allah the Exalted enjoined Piety (Taqwa) upon the former and the latter, for He said: 'And We had already enjoined upon those who were given the Scripture before you and upon you that you fear Allah' (4:131). And He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'And fear Me, if you are believers' (3:175). So He commanded Fear (Khauf) and made it obligatory and a condition in Faith (Iman). Therefore, it is inconceivable that a believer be devoid of Fear (Khauf), even if weak, and the weakness of his Fear (Khauf) is according to the weakness of his knowledge (Ma'rifah) and his Faith (Iman).
22:37.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

22:37.arabic: بل القلب أولى بمؤاخذته لأنه الأصل قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم التقوى ههنا وأشار إلى القلب[84] وقال الله تعالى لن ينال الله لحومها ولا دماؤها ولكن يناله التقوى منكم وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم الإثم حواز القلوب[85] وقال البر ما اطمأن إليه القلب وإن أفتوك وأفتوك[86] حتى إنا نقول إذا حكم القلب المفتي بإيجاب شيء وكان مخطئا فيه صار مثابا عليه بل من قد ظن أنه تطهر فعليه أن يصلي فإن صلى ثم تذكر أنه لم يتوضأ كان له ثواب بفعله فإن تذكر ثم تركه كان معاقبا عليه ومن وجد على فراشه امرأة فظن أنها زوجته لم يع
22:37.english: Rather, the Heart (Qalb) is more deserving of being held accountable because it is the foundation. The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said: 'God-consciousness (Taqwa) is here,' and he pointed to his Heart (Qalb). And Allah the Exalted said: 'Never will Allah reach their flesh nor their blood, but He will reach the God-consciousness (Taqwa) from you.' And the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: 'Sin is what unsettles the Hearts (Qulub).' And he said: 'Righteousness (Al-Birr) is what the Heart (Qalb) finds tranquility in, even if they give you legal opinions and give you legal opinions.' So much so that we say: if the Heart (Qalb) of the jurist rules to obligate something and he is mistaken in it, he becomes rewarded for it. Rather, whoever thought he had performed ablution, then he must pray; if he prays then remembers he did not perform ablution, he has reward for his action. If he remembers then abandons it, he is punished for it. And whoever finds a woman on his bed and thinks she is his wife, he does not sin by intercourse with her, even if she is a stranger. If he thinks she is a stranger then has intercourse with her, he sins by intercourse with her, even if she is his wife. And all of that looks to the Heart (Qalb) without regard to the limbs.
22:37.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

22:37.arabic: فليس المقصود من إراقة دم القربان الدم واللحم بل ميل القلب عن حب الدنيا وبذلها إيثارا لوجه الله تعالى وهذه الصفة قد حصلت عند جزم النية والهمة وإن عاق عن العمل عائق ف لن ينال الله لحومها ولا دماؤها ولكن يناله التقوى منكم والتقوى ههنا صفة القلب ولذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم (إن قوما بالمدينة قد شركونا في جهادنا) كما تقدم ذكره لأن قلوبهم في صدق إرادة الخير وبذل المال والنفس والرغبة في طلب الشهادة وإعلاء كلمة الله تعالى كقلوب الخارجين فى الجهاد وإنما فارقوهم بالأبدان لعوائق تخص الأسباب الخارجة عن القل
22:37.english: For the intended purpose of shedding the blood of sacrifice is not the blood and the flesh, but rather the inclination of the Heart (Qalb) away from the love of the worldly life and spending it in preference for the Face of Allah the Exalted. And this attribute has been attained at the firmness of the intention (Niyyah) and the earnest striving (Himmah), even if a hindrance prevents the action. So 'Never will Allah reach their flesh nor their blood, but He will reach the God-consciousness (Taqwa) from you.' And the God-consciousness (Taqwa) here is an attribute of the Heart (Qalb). And for that reason, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said ('Indeed, a people in Al-Madinah have shared with us in our jihad') as its mention preceded, because their hearts are in the sincerity of desiring good and spending wealth and the self (Nafs), and the desire in seeking martyrdom and raising high the word of Allah the Exalted, like the hearts of those who went out in jihad. And they only differed from them with the bodies due to hindrances specific to causes external to the Heart (Qalb), and that is not sought except for confirming these attributes. And with these meanings, you understand all the hadiths that we presented regarding the virtue of intention (Niyyah), so present them to it so that their secrets may be unveiled to you, so we will not prolong with repetition.
22:37.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

22:37.arabic: فالجوارح خادمة للقلب بتأكيد صفاتها فيه فالقلب هو المقصود والأعضاء آلات موصلة إلى المقصود ولذلك قال النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم (إن في الجسد مضغة إذا صلحت صلح لها سائر الجسد)[22] وقال عليه الصلاة والسلام (اللهم أصلح الراعى والرعية)[23] وأراد بالراعى القلب وقال الله تعالى (لن ينال لحومها ولا دماؤها ولكن يناله التقوى منكم) وهى صفة القلب فمن هذا الوجه يجب لا محالة أن تكون أعمال القلب على الجملة أفضل من حركات الجوارح ثم يجب أن تكون النية من جملتها أفضل لأنها عبارة عن ميل القلب إلى الخير وإرادته له وغرضن
22:37.english: The limbs are servants to the Heart (Qalb) by confirming its attributes within it, so the Heart is the intended goal and the limbs are instruments leading to the goal. Therefore, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, in the body there is a morsel; if it is sound, the entire body becomes sound.' And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: 'O Allah, rectify the shepherd and the flock,' intending by 'the shepherd' the Heart. And Allah the Exalted said: 'Their flesh and their blood do not reach Allah, but the God-consciousness (Taqwa) from you reaches Him.' And it is an attribute of the Heart. From this perspective, it must necessarily be that the works of the Heart, in general, are better than the movements of the limbs. Then it must be that the intention (Niyyah) is among them better, because it is an expression of the Heart's inclination toward good and its desire for it. Our purpose from works with the limbs is that the Heart returns to desiring good and confirms within it the inclination toward it, to empty it from worldly desires and to immerse it in the Remembrance (Dhikr) and reflection (Fikr). Therefore, it is necessarily better in relation to the purpose because it is established in the very intended goal.
22:37.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

22:37.arabic: بل الضحايا والقرابين التي هي مجاهدة للنفس بتنقيص المال قال الله تعالى: ﴿ لن ينال الله لحومها ولا دماؤها ولكن يناله التقوى منكم ﴾ {} أي الصفة التي استولت على القلب حتى حملته على امتثال الأوامر هي المطلوبة فكيف الأمر في الصلاة ولا أرب في أفعالها فهذا ما يدل من حيث المعنى على اشتراط حضور القلب.
22:37.english: Rather, the sacrifices and offerings that are a struggle (Mujahadah) for the Soul (Nafs) through the reduction of wealth. Allah the Exalted said: 'Never will Allah reach (Yanalu) their meats nor their bloods, but He will reach (Yanalu) the God-consciousness (Taqwa) from you.' {} That is, the attribute (Sifah) that has taken possession of the Heart (Qalb) until it compelled it to obey the commands is what is sought. So how is the matter in prayer, and there is no benefit (Arb) in its actions? This is what indicates from the perspective of meaning the requirement of the Heart's (Qalb) presence.
22:37.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

22:38.arabic: البخل ويكتمون ما آتاهم الله من فضله" وقال ﭬ "إياكم والشح فإنه أهلك من كان قبلكم، حملهم على أن سفكوا دماءهم واستحلوا محارمهم"[75] وقال ﭬ "إياكم والشح فإنه دعا من كان قبلكم فسفكوا دماءهم ودعاهم فاستحلوا محارمهم ودعاهم فقطعوا أرحامهم"[76] وقال ﭬ "لا يدخل الجنة بخيل ولا خب ولا خائن لا سيئ الملكة"[77] وفي رواية "ولا جبار" وفي رواية "ولا منان" وقال ﭬ "ثلاث مهلكات؛ شح مطاع وهوى متبع وإعجاب المرء بنفسه"[78] وقال ﭬ "إن الله يبغض ثلاثة: الشيخ الزاني، والبخيل المنان، والمعيل المختال"[79] وقال ﭬ "مثل المنفق
