22:38.english: Miserliness and they conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty" and He (peace be upon him) said: "Beware of avarice (Shuh) for it destroyed those before you, it compelled them to shed their blood and make lawful their prohibitions"[75] and He (peace be upon him) said: "Beware of avarice (Shuh) for it called those before you so they shed their blood and it called them so they made lawful their prohibitions and it called them so they severed their kinship ties"[76] and He (peace be upon him) said: "The miser (Bakhil) does not enter Paradise, nor the treacherous, nor the betrayer, nor the one of bad character"[77] and in a narration: "nor the tyrant" and in a narration: "nor the one who reminds of favors" and He (peace be upon him) said: "Three destructive things; obeyed avarice (Shuh), followed desire (Hawa), and self-admiration"[78] and He (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed Allah hates three: the old fornicator, the miser (Bakhil) who reminds of favors, and the poor arrogant"[79] and He (peace be upon him) said: "The likeness of the spender and the miser (Bakhil) is like two men upon them are iron shirts from their chests to their collarbones, as for the spender, he does not spend anything except it spreads or increases over his skin until it hides his fingertips, and as for the miser (Bakhil), he does not intend to spend anything except it shrinks and sticks to each of his throat's place until it takes hold of his collarbones, so he widens it but it does not widen"[80] and He (peace be upon him) said: "Two traits do not gather in a believer: miserliness (Bukhl) and bad character"[81] and He (peace be upon him) said: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from miserliness (Bukhl) and I seek refuge in You from cowardice and I seek refuge in You that I be returned to the most despicable age"[82] and He (peace be upon him) said: "Beware of oppression (Zulm) for oppression (Zulm) is darknesses on the Day of Resurrection, and beware of obscenity for Allah does not love the obscene nor the one who is obscene, and beware of avarice (Shuh) for indeed what destroyed those before you was avarice (Shuh) commanded them to lie so they lied and commanded them to oppress (Zulm) so they oppressed (Zulm) and commanded them to sever ties so they severed"[83] and He (peace be upon him) said: "The worst thing in a man is destructive avarice (Shuh) and stripping cowardice"[84] and a martyr was killed in the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) so a weeping woman wept for him and said: O my martyr! So He (peace be upon him) said: "And what makes you know that he is a martyr? Perhaps he used to speak about what does not concern him or be miserly (Bakhil) with what does not diminish him"[85] and Jubayr ibn Mut'im said: While we were walking with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and with him were people returning from Khaybar when the Bedouins clung to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) asking him, until they pushed him to a thorny tree and snatched his cloak, so He (peace be upon him) stood and said: "Give me my cloak, for by the One in Whose hand is my soul (Nafs), if I had the number of these sticks as camels, I would divide them among you, then you would not find me miserly (Bakhil), nor a liar, nor a coward"[86] and Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) divided a division so I said: Others were more deserving of it than them? So He said: "Indeed they give me the choice between that they ask me with obscenity or they consider me miserly (Bakhil) and I am not miserly (Bakhil)"[87] and Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: Two men entered upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and asked him for the price of a camel so He gave them two dinars; so they went out from him and Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) met them so they praised and said good and thanks for what He did for them, so Umar entered upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and informed him of
22:38.book_title: Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth
22:38.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

22:38.arabic: وقالوا له هلم إلى الغداء يا ابن بنت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال نعم إن الله لا يحب المستكبرين فنزل وقعد معهم على الأرض وأكل ثم سلم عليهم وركب وقال قد أجبتكم فأجيبوني
22:38.english: And they said to him: 'Come to lunch, O son of the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him).' He said: 'Yes, indeed Allah does not love the arrogant ones.' So he dismounted and sat with them on the ground and ate, then he greeted them and mounted and said: 'I have responded to you, so respond to me.'
22:38.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Manners of Eating'

22:38.arabic: در  من المشركين فقال "لا تسبوا هؤلاء فإنه لا  يخلص  إليهم  شيء  مما  تقولون  وتؤذون الأحياء ألا إن البذاء لؤم"[62] وقال ﭬ "ليس المؤمن  بالطعان  ولا  اللعان  ولا الفاحش ولا البذي"[63] وقال ﭬ "الجنة حرام على كل فاحش أن يدخلها"[64]  وقال  ﭬ "أربعة يؤذون أهل النار في النار  على  ما  بهم  من  الأذى  يسعون  بين  الحميم والجحيم يدعون بالويل والثبور: رجل يسيل فوه قيحاً ودماً فيقال له ما بال  الأبعد قد آذاناً على ما بنا من الأذى؟ فيقول إن الأبعد كان  ينظر  إلى  كل  كلمة  قذعة خبيثة فيستلذها كما يستلذ الر
22:38.english: From the polytheists, he said: "Do not curse these, for nothing of what you say reaches them, and you harm the living. Indeed, vulgarity is baseness."[62] And he (peace be upon him) said: "The believer is not one who slanders, nor curses, nor is obscene, nor vulgar."[63] And he (peace be upon him) said: "Paradise is forbidden for every obscene person to enter."[64] And he (peace be upon him) said: "Four will harm the people of Hell in Hell, despite the harm upon them; they run between scalding water and blazing fire, calling out woe and ruin: a man whose mouth flows with pus and blood, and it is said to him: 'What is with the distant one who has harmed us despite the harm upon us?' He says: 'The distant one used to look at every foul, vile word and relish it as one relishes obscenity.'"[65] And he (peace be upon him) said to Aisha: "O Aisha, if obscenity were a man, he would be an evil man."[66] And he (peace be upon him) said: "Vulgarity and explicit disclosure are two branches from the branches of hypocrisy."[67] It is possible that what is meant by explicit disclosure is in matters of religion and in the attributes of Allah (Exalted is He), for presenting that summarily to the ears of the common people is preferable to exaggeration in its explanation; for from the utmost explanation of it may arise doubts and whisperings, so if it is summarized, the hearts (Qulub) hasten to acceptance and do not become disturbed. But its mention coupled with vulgarity resembles that what is intended by it is public proclamation of what a person is ashamed to disclose, for the preferable in its like is overlooking and ignoring, not uncovering and explaining. And he (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, Allah does not love the obscene, excessively obscene one who shouts in the markets."[68] And Jabir ibn Samura said: I was sitting with the Prophet (peace be upon him) and my father was before me, and he (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, obscenity and excessive obscenity are not from Islam in anything, and the best of people in Islam are the best of them in character."[69] And Ibrahim ibn Maysara said: It is said that the obscene, excessively obscene one will be brought on the Day of Resurrection in the form of a dog or inside a dog. And Al-Ahnaf ibn Qais said: Shall I not inform you of the worst disease: the vulgar tongue and the lowly character.
22:38.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

22:38.arabic: وكان الحسن بن علي رضي الله عنهما يمر بالسؤال وبين أيديهم كسر فيقولون هلم إلى الغداء يا ابن رسول الله فكان ينزل ويجلس على الطريق ويأكل معهم ويركب ويقول إن الله لا يحب المستكبرين
22:38.english: And Al-Hasan ibn Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both, would pass by the beggars while they had crumbs before them, and they would say: 'Come to lunch, O son of the Messenger of Allah.' So he would dismount and sit on the road and eat with them, and then ride and say: 'Indeed, Allah does not love the arrogant ones.'
22:38.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Etiquette of Seclusion'

22:40.arabic: وبين الله عز وجل ما أحسنه وأعظم أجره  وأفضل  من  ذلك  ذكر  الله سبحانه عند ما حرم الله عز وجل ويروى أن كل نفس تخرج من الدنيا عطشى  إلا  ذاكر الله عز وجل وقال معاذ بن جبل رضي الله عنه ليس يتحسر أهل الجنة  على  شيء  إلا على ساعة مرت بهم لم يذكروا الله سبحانه فيها والله تعالى أعلم.                             (فضيلة مجالس الذكر)   قال رسول الله ﭬ (ما جلس قوم  مجلسا  يذكرون  الله  عز  وجل  إلا  حفت  بهم الملائكة وغشيتهم الرحمة وذكرهم الله تعالى فيمن عنده[12]) وقال ﭬ: (ما من  قوم اجتمعوا يذكرون الله
22:40.english: And Allah, the Exalted, has shown what is most beautiful and greatest in reward, and better than that is the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah, the Glorified, when Allah, the Exalted, has forbidden. And it is narrated that every soul leaves the world thirsty except the one who remembers Allah, the Exalted. And Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, said: 'The people of Paradise do not regret anything except an hour that passed them by in which they did not remember Allah, the Glorified.' And Allah, the Exalted, knows best. (The Virtue of Gatherings of Remembrance) The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said: 'No people sit in a gathering remembering Allah, the Exalted, except that angels surround them, mercy envelops them, and Allah, the Exalted, mentions them among those with Him.' And he, peace be upon him, said: 'No people gather remembering Allah, the Exalted, not desiring by that except His Face, except that a caller calls them from the sky: 'Rise, forgiven for you; your bad deeds have been replaced with good deeds.' And he, peace be upon him, also said: 'No people sit in a sitting in which they do not remember Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, and do not send blessings upon the Prophet, peace be upon him, except that it will be a regret for them on the Day of Resurrection.' And David, peace be upon him, said: 'My God, if You see me passing from gatherings of those who remember to gatherings of the heedless, then break my leg before them, for it is a blessing You bestow upon me.' And he, peace be upon him, said: 'A good gathering expiates for the believer two thousand gatherings of evil gatherings.' And Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: 'Indeed, the people of the sky see the houses of the people of the earth in which the Name of Allah, the Exalted, is remembered as stars are seen.' And Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, may Allah have mercy on him, said: 'When people gather remembering Allah, the Exalted, Satan and the world withdraw, and Satan says to the world: 'Do you not see what they are doing?' So the world says: 'Leave them, for when they disperse, I will take them by their necks to you.' And from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, that when he entered the market and said: 'I see you here, and the inheritance of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, is being divided in the mosque.' So the people went to the mosque and left the market, and they did not see an inheritance, so they said: 'O Abu Hurairah, we did not see an inheritance being divided in the mosque.' He said: 'So what did you see?' They said: 'We saw people remembering Allah, the Exalted, and reciting the Quran.' He said: 'That is the inheritance of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him.' And Al-A'mash narrated from Abu Salih from Abu Hurairah and Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri, from him, peace be upon him, that he said: 'Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, has angels roaming the earth besides the writers of people, so when they find people remembering Allah, the Exalted, they call out: 'Come to your desire,' so they come and surround them up to the sky, then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: 'What thing did you leave My servants doing?' So they say: 'We left them praising You, glorifying You, and declaring Your perfection.' So Allah, the Exalted, says: 'And have they seen Me?' So they say: 'No.' So He, Majestic is His Majesty, says: 'How if they saw Me?' So they say: 'If they saw You, they would be more intense in declaring Your perfection, praising, and glorifying.' So He says to them: 'From what thing...'
22:40.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith

22:41.arabic: فقال إما رفعت أو أذنت لي حتى أرفع فنظر المأمون تحت قدمه فرأى الكتاب فأخذه وقبله وخجل ثم عاد وقال لم تأمر بالمعروف وقد جعل الله ذلك إلينا أهل البيت ونحن الذين قال الله تعالى فيهم الذين إن مكناهم في الأرض أقاموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة وأمروا بالمعروف ونهوا عن المنكر فقال صدقت يا أمير المؤمنين أنت كما وصفت نفسك من السلطان والتمكن غير أنا أعوانك وأولياؤك فيه ولا ينكر ذلك إلا من جهل كتاب الله تعالى وسنة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال الله تعالى والمؤمنون والمؤمنات بعضهم أولياء بعض يأمرون بالمعروف الآي
22:41.english: He said: 'Either you lift it or permit me to lift it.' So Al-Ma'mun looked under his foot and saw the book, so he took it and kissed it and felt ashamed. Then he returned and said: 'Why do you command the good when Allah has made that for us, the People of the House, and we are those about whom Allah the Exalted said: "Those who, if We establish them in the earth, establish the prayer (Salah) and give the alms (Zakah) and command the good (Ma'ruf) and forbid the evil (Munkar). And to Allah belongs the outcome of affairs."' He said: 'You have spoken truthfully, O Commander of the Believers. You are as you have described yourself regarding authority and establishment, except that we are your helpers and allies (Awliya') in it, and none denies that except one who is ignorant of the Book of Allah the Exalted and the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him. Allah the Exalted said: "And the believing men and believing women are allies (Awliya') of one another. They command the good..." the verse. And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said: "The believer to the believer is like a building, one part strengthening another." The hadith "The believer to the believer is like a building, one part strengthening another" is agreed upon from the narration of Abu Musa, and it has preceded in the third chapter of the Etiquettes of Companionship. And you have been established in the earth, and this is the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger. So if you submit to them, you will thank the one who aided you for their sanctity, and if you are arrogant toward them and do not submit to what is incumbent upon you from them, then the One to Whom belongs your command and in Whose hand is your might, and He has stipulated that He does not waste the reward of one who does good work. So say now what you wish.'
22:41.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

22:41.arabic: وقال تعالى الذين إن مكناهم في الأرض أقاموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة وأمروا بالمعروف ونهوا عن المنكر فقرن ذلك بالصلاة والزكاة في نعت الصالحين والمؤمنين
22:41.english: And Allah the Exalted said: 'Those who, if We establish them in the earth, establish the Prayer (al-Salah) and give the Purifying Alms (al-Zakah) and command the Recognized Good (al-Ma'ruf) and forbid the Reprehensible (al-Munkar).' So He coupled that with the Prayer and the Purifying Alms in describing the Righteous (al-Salihin) and the Believers (al-Mu'minin).
22:41.topic: Al-Ghazali on the outer and inner dimensions of worship, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

22:46.arabic: ولمشابهة بصيرة الباطن لبصيرة الظاهر قال الله تعالى ما كذب الفؤاد ما رأى وقال تعالى وكذلك نرى إبراهيم ملكوت السموات والأرض الآية وسمى ضده عمى فقال تعالى فإنها لا تعمى الأبصار ولكن تعمى القلوب التي في الصدور وقال تعالى ومن كان في هذه أعمى فهو في الآخرة أعمى وأضل سبيلا وهذه الأمور التي كشفت للأنبياء بعضها كان بالبصر وبعضها كان بالبصيرة وسمى الكل رؤية وبالجملة من لم تكن بصيرته الباطنة ثاقبة لم يعلق به من الدين إلا قشوره وأمثلته دون لبابه وحقائقه
22:46.english: And due to the similarity of the inner insight (Bassira) to the outer insight, Allah the Exalted said: 'The Heart (Fu'ad) did not lie about what it saw' [Quran 53:11], and He said: 'And thus did We show Abraham the dominion (Malakut) of the heavens and the earth' [Quran 6:75] the verse. And He named its opposite blindness, so He said: 'For indeed, it is not the eyes that become blind, but it is the Hearts (Qulub) which are in the chests that become blind' [Quran 22:46], and He said: 'And whoever is blind in this [world] will be blind in the Hereafter and more astray in way' [Quran 17:72]. And these matters that were unveiled to the prophets, some of them were through sight (Basar) and some were through insight (Bassira), and He named all of it vision (Ru'ya). And in summary, whoever does not have his inner insight (Bassira) penetrating, nothing will attach to him from the religion except its outer shells and its examples, without its core and its truths.
22:46.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

22:46.arabic: ولموازنة البصيرة الباطنة للبصر الظاهر سماه الله تعالى باسمه فقال ما كذب الفؤاد ما رأى سمى إدراك الفؤاد رؤية وكذلك قوله تعالى وكذلك نري إبراهيم ملكوت السموات والأرض وما أراد به الرؤية الظاهرة فإن ذلك غير مخصوص بإبراهيم عليه السلام حتى يعرض في معرض الامتنان ولذلك سمى ضد إدراكه عمى فقال تعالى فإنها لا تعمى الأبصار ولكن تعمى القلوب التي في الصدور وقال تعالى ومن كان في هذه أعمى فهو في الآخرة أعمى وأضل سبيلا فهذا بيان العلم العقلي
22:46.english: And due to the equivalence of the inner insight (Bassira) to the outer sight (Basar), Allah the Exalted named it with His name, so He said: 'The heart (Fu'ad) did not lie about what it saw' - He called the perception of the heart (Fu'ad) 'seeing'. Likewise, His saying the Exalted: 'And thus We showed Ibrahim the dominion of the heavens and the earth' - and He did not intend by it the apparent vision, for that is not specific to Ibrahim (peace be upon him) so that it would be presented in the context of favor. Therefore, He called the opposite of its perception 'blindness', so He said the Exalted: 'For indeed, it is not the eyes that become blind, but it is the hearts (Qulub) that are in the breasts that become blind.' And He said the Exalted: 'And whoever is blind in this [world] will be blind in the Hereafter and more astray in way.' This is the explanation of intellectual knowledge.
22:46.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

22:46.arabic: فأسباب الهدى هى الكتاب والرسل وبصائر العقول وهى مبذولة ولا يمنع منها إلا الحسد والكبر وحب الدنيا والأسباب التى تعمى القلوب وإن كانت لا تعمى الأبصار قال تعالى: ﴿ فإنها لا تعمى الأبصار ولكن تعمى القلوب التى في الصدور ﴾ {} ومن جملة المعميات الإلف والعادة وحب استصحابهما وعنه العبارة بقوله تعالى: ﴿ إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة ﴾ {} الآية وعن الكبر والحسد العبارة بقوله تعالى: ﴿ وقالوا لولا نزل هذا القرآن على رجل من القريتين عظيم ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ أبشرا منا واحدا نتبعه ﴾ {} فهذه المعميات هى التى منعت الا
22:46.english: The means of guidance (Huda) are the Book (Kitab) and the Messengers (Rusul) and the insights of the intellects (Basa'ir al-'Uqul), and they are made available, and nothing prevents from them except envy (Hasad) and arrogance (Kibr) and love of the worldly life (Hubb al-Dunya) and the causes that blind the hearts (Qulub) even though they do not blind the eyesights (Absar). Allah the Exalted said: 'For indeed, it is not the eyesights (Absar) that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts (Qulub) which are within the chests (Sudur).' And among the blinding things are familiarity (Ilf) and habit ('Adah) and the love of adhering to them, and from this is the expression in His saying: 'Indeed, we found our forefathers upon a community...' the verse, and concerning arrogance (Kibr) and envy (Hasad) the expression is in His saying: 'And they said, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man from [one of] the two cities?"' and His saying: 'A human being from among us, one, that we should follow him?' So these blinding things are what prevented the attainment of guidance (Ihtida') and the second guidance (Hidayah) beyond this general guidance, and it is that which Allah the Exalted grants the servant (Abd) state after state, and it is the fruit of striving (Mujahadah) where He said: 'And those who strive (Jahadu) in Us - We will surely guide them to Our ways.' And it is what is intended by His saying: 'And those who are guided (Ihtadaw) - He increases them in guidance (Huda).'
22:46.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

22:50.arabic: وقوله عز وجل ﴿ لهم مغفرة ورزق كريم. كما أخرجك ربك من بيتك بالحق ﴾ {} فهذا الكلام غير متصل وإنما هو عائد إلى قوله السابق ﴿ قل الانفال لله والرسول. كما أخرجك ربك من بيتك بالحق ﴾ {} أي فصارت أنفال الغنائم لك إذ أنت راض بخروجك وهم كارهون فاعترض بين الكلام الأمر بالتقوى وغيره
22:50.english: And His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'For them is forgiveness and a generous provision. As your Lord brought you out from your home in truth' {} So this speech is not connected, but rather it returns to His preceding saying: 'Say: The spoils of war are for Allah and the Messenger. As your Lord brought you out from your home in truth' {} Meaning: So the spoils of war became for you since you were pleased with your departure and they were averse, so the command for piety (Taqwa) and other matters intervened between the speech.
22:50.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

22:52.arabic: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن من أمتي محدثين ومعلمين ومكلمين وإن عمر منهم وقرأ ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما وما أرسلنا من قبلك من رسول ولا نبي ولا محدث يعني الصديقين والمحدث هو الملهم والملهم هو الذي انكشف له في باطن قلبه من جهة الداخل لا من جهة المحسوسات الخارجة والقرآن مصرح بأن التقوى مفتاح الهداية والكشف وذلك علم من غير تعلم وقال الله تعالى وما خلق الله في السموات والأرض لآيات لقوم يتقون خصصها بهم وقال تعالى هذا بيان للناس وهدى وموعظة للمتقين
22:52.english: And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed among my community are those who are spoken to (Muhaddathun), those who are taught (Mu'allimun), and those who are spoken with (Mukallamun), and Umar is among them.' And Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) recited: 'And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet or one spoken to (Muhaddath)' meaning the truthful ones (Siddiqin). And the one spoken to (Muhaddath) is the inspired one (Mulham), and the inspired one (Mulham) is the one to whom is unveiled in the inner (Batin) of his heart (Qalb) from the direction of the interior, not from the direction of the external sensed things. And the Quran declares that piety (Taqwa) is the key to guidance (Hidayah) and unveiling (Kashf), and that is knowledge without learning. And Allah the Exalted said: 'And We did not create in the heavens and the earth signs for a people who are pious (Muttaqun),' specifying it for them. And He said: 'This is a clarification for the people and guidance and admonition for the pious (Muttaqun).'
22:52.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

22:52.arabic: وقالت فرقة من أهل العلم: لا بد من الحذر من الشيطان وما ذكره البصريون من أن الأقوياء قد استغنوا عن الحذر وخلت قلوبهم عن حب الدنيا بالكلية فهو وسيلة الشيطان يكاد يكون غروراً، إذ الأنبياء عليهم السلام لم يتخلصوا من وسواس الشيطان ونزغاته فكيف يتخلص غيرهم؟ وليس كل وسواس الشيطان من الشهوات وحب الدنيا، بل في صفات الله تعالى وأسمائه، وفي تحسين البدع والضلال وغير ذلك، ولا ينجو أحد من الخطر فيه ولذلك قال تعالى "وما أرسلنا من قبلك من رسول ولا نبي إلا إذا تمنى ألقي الشيطان في أمنيته فينسخ الله ما يلقى الشيط
22:52.english: And a group of the people of knowledge said: It is necessary to be cautious of the Satan (Shaytan), and what the Basrans mentioned—that the strong ones have become independent from caution and their hearts (Qulub) have become empty from the love (Hubb) of the worldly life (Dunya) completely—is a means of the Satan (Shaytan) that almost amounts to delusion (Ghurur), since the Prophets (Anbiya) upon them be peace did not become free from the whisperings (Waswas) of the Satan (Shaytan) and his incitements (Nuzghat), so how can others become free? And not every whispering (Waswas) of the Satan (Shaytan) is from the desires (Shahawat) and love (Hubb) of the worldly life (Dunya), but rather in the attributes (Sifat) of Allah the Exalted and His names (Asma), and in beautifying innovations (Bid'ah) and misguidance (Dalal) and other than that, and no one is safe from the danger in it, and for that reason Allah the Exalted said: "And We did not send before you any messenger (Rasul) or prophet (Nabi) except that when he desired (Tamanna), the Satan (Shaytan) cast into his desire (Ummniyyah), then Allah abolishes what the Satan (Shaytan) casts, then Allah makes firm His signs (Ayat)." And the Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed, it covers over my heart (Qalb)."[52] even though his Satan (Shaytan) had submitted (Aslama) and does not command him except with good[53]. So whoever thinks that his occupation with the love (Hubb) of Allah is more than the occupation of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the rest of the Prophets (Anbiya) upon them be peace, then he is deluded (Maghrur), and that did not secure them from the plotting (Kayd) of the Satan (Shaytan), and for that reason Adam and Eve did not become safe from him in the Garden (Jannah) which is the abode (Dar) of security (Amn) and joy (Surur) after Allah said to them: "Indeed, this is an enemy ('Adu) for you and your spouse, so do not let him expel you from the Garden (Jannah) so that you become wretched; indeed, for you is that you do not hunger in it nor be naked, and that you do not thirst in it nor be exposed to the sun." And even though He only forbade one tree and permitted for him beyond that what he wanted, so if a prophet (Nabi) from the Prophets (Anbiya) did not become secure while he is in the Garden (Jannah), the abode (Dar) of security (Amn) and happiness (Sa'adah), from the plotting (Kayd) of the Satan (Shaytan), then how is it permissible for others to become secure in the abode (Dar) of the worldly life (Dunya), which is the source (Manba') of trials (Mihan) and temptations (Fitna), the mine (Ma'din) of pleasures (Maladh) and forbidden desires (Shahawat)?
22:52.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

22:58.arabic: وقد روي أن ابن عمر سرقت ناقته فطلبها حتى أعيا، ثم قال: في سبيل الله تعالى، فدخل المسجد فصلى فيه ركعتين فجاءه رجل فقال: يا أبا عبد الرحمن، إن ناقتك في مكان كذا فلبس نعله وقام، ثم قال: أستغفر الله وجلس، فقيل له: ألا تذهب فتأخذها! فقال: إني كنت قلت في سبيل الله. وقال بعض الشيوخ: رأيت بعض إخواني في النوم بعد موته فقلت: ما فعل الله بك؟ قال: غفر لي وأدخلني الجنة وعرض علي منازلي فيها فرأيتها، قال: وهو مع ذلك كئيب حزين! فقلت: قد غفر لك ودخلت الجنة وأنت حزين! فتنفس الصعداء ثم قال: نعم إني لا أزال حزيناً
22:58.english: And it has been narrated that Ibn Umar's she-camel was stolen, so he searched for it until he became exhausted, then he said: 'In the path of Allah (سبيل الله) the Exalted,' so he entered the mosque and prayed two units of prayer (ركعتين) therein, then a man came to him and said: 'O Abu Abd al-Rahman, your she-camel is in such-and-such place,' so he put on his sandal and stood up, then he said: 'I seek forgiveness from Allah (أستغفر الله),' and sat down. It was said to him: 'Will you not go and take it?' He said: 'Indeed, I had said: In the path of Allah (سبيل الله).' And some of the shaykhs said: 'I saw one of my brothers in a dream after his death, so I said: What has Allah done with you? He said: He forgave me and admitted me to Paradise and showed me my dwellings therein, so I saw them,' he said: 'And he, despite that, was gloomy and sad! So I said: You have been forgiven and entered Paradise, and you are sad! He sighed deeply then said: Yes, I remain sad until the Day of Resurrection (يوم القيامة). I said: Why? He said: When I saw my dwellings in Paradise, elevated stations in the highest levels (عليين) were raised for me, the like of which I had not seen in what I saw, so I rejoiced in them. When I intended to enter them, a caller called from above them: Turn him away from it, for this is not for him; it is only for the one who fulfilled the path (أمضى السبيل). So I said: And what is fulfilling the path? It was said to me: You used to say about something that it is in the path of Allah (سبيل الله), then you would retract in it. Had you fulfilled the path, we would have fulfilled for you.' And it was narrated about some of the worshippers in Mecca that he was sleeping next to a man who had his purse with him, then the man woke up and missed his purse, so he accused him of it. He said to him: How much was in your purse? He mentioned it to him, so he brought it from the house and weighed it from his own, then after that his companions informed him that they had taken the purse as a joke with him, so he came and his companions with him and returned the gold, but he refused and said: Take it as lawful and good (حلالاً طيباً), for I would not return to wealth that I had expended in the path of Allah (سبيل الله) the Exalted. So he did not accept it, so they insisted upon him, so he called his son and began to make it into bundles and send it to the poor until none of it remained. Thus were the character traits (أخلاق) of the predecessors (السلف), and likewise, whoever took a loaf of bread to give to a poor person and he was absent, he would dislike returning it to the house after taking it out, so he would give it to another poor person, and likewise he would do with dirhams, dinars, and other charities. The fifth: And it is the lowest of the degrees that he does not invoke against the thief who wronged him by taking, for if he does, his reliance (توكله) becomes invalid and that indicates his dislike and regret over what has passed, and his asceticism (زهده) becomes invalid, and if he exaggerates, his reward (أجره) also becomes invalid in what befell him; for in the report: 'Whoever invokes against his wrongdoer has sought vengeance.' And it was narrated that al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym's horse was stolen, and its value was twenty thousand, and he was standing praying, so he did not cut off his prayer and was not agitated to seek it, then some people came to him.
22:58.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

22:65.arabic: وكان بعضهم يقول في دعائه: يا ممسك السماء أن تقع على الأرض إلا بإذنك أمسك الدنيا عني.
22:65.english: And some of them would say in his supplication: 'O You who holds back the sky from falling upon the earth except by Your permission, hold back the world (Dunya) from me.'
22:65.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Condemnation of the World'

22:73.arabic: نحمد الله حمد موحد انمحق في توحيده ما سوى الواحد الحق وتلاشر ونمجده تمجيد من يصرح بأن كل شيء ما سوى الله باطل ولا يتحاشى وأن كل من في السموات والأرض لن يخلقوا ذبابا ولو اجتمعوا له ولا فراشا ونشكره إذ رفع السماء لعباده سقفا مبنيا ومهد الأرض بساطا لهم وفراشا وكور الليل على النهار فجعل الليل لباسا والنهار معاشا لينتشروا في ابتغاء فضله وينتعشوا به عن ضراعة الحاجات انتعاشا
22:73.english: We praise Allah with the praise of one who unifies (Tawhid), annihilating in His unification (Tawhid) all besides the One Truth (Al-Haqq), and we glorify Him with the glorification of one who declares that everything besides Allah is false (Bāṭil) and does not hesitate, and that all who are in the heavens and the earth will never create a fly even if they gathered for it, nor a bed, and we thank Him for raising the sky as a built roof for His servants and spreading the earth as a carpet for them and a bed, and wrapping the night over the day, making the night a garment and the day a livelihood so they may spread out in seeking His bounty and revive from the humility of needs with revival.
22:73.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Etiquette of Earning'

22:77.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
22:77.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Whatever is in the Quran of 'O you who have believed' is in the Torah 'O you poor ones'.
22:77.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

23:1.arabic: اعلم أن كل إنسان جاهل بعيوب نفسه، فإذا جاهد نفسه أدنى مجاهدة حتى ترك فواحش المعاصي ربما يظن بنفسه أنه هذب نفسه وحسن خلقه واستغنى عن المجاهدة، فلا بد من إيضاح علامة حسن الخلق. فإن حسن الخلق هو الإيمان، وسوء الخلق هو النفاق. وقد ذكر الله تعالى صفات المؤمنين والمنافقين في كتابه وهي بجملتها ثمرة حسن الخلق وسوء الخلق. فلنورد جملة من ذلك لتعلم آية حسن الخلق. قال الله تعالى "قد أفلح المؤمنون الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون والذين هم عن اللغو معرضون" إلى قوله "أولئك هم الوارثون" وقال عز وجل "التائبون العابدون
23:1.english: Know that every human is ignorant of his own faults, so if he strives against his Soul (Nafs) with the slightest striving until he abandons the gross sins, perhaps he thinks of himself that he has refined his Soul (Nafs) and improved his character and become independent of striving, so it is necessary to clarify the sign of good character. For good character is Faith (Iman), and bad character is Hypocrisy (Nifaq). And Allah the Exalted has mentioned the attributes of the believers and the hypocrites in His Book, and they are in their entirety the fruit of good character and bad character. So let us present a summary of that to know the sign of good character. Allah the Exalted said: "Indeed, the believers have succeeded (Qad aflaha al-mu'minuna) - those who are humble in their prayer and who turn away from idle talk" to His saying "Those are the inheritors." And He the Mighty and Majestic said: "The repentant, the worshippers, the praisers" to His saying "and give good tidings to the believers." And He the Mighty and Majestic said: "The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble" to His saying "Those are the true believers." And He the Exalted said: "And the servants of the Most Merciful who walk upon the earth easily and when the ignorant address them, they say peace" to the end of the surah. Whoever is confused about his condition, let him present himself to these verses, for the presence of all these attributes is a sign of good character, and the absence of all of them is a sign of bad character, and the presence of some without others indicates some without others, so let him occupy himself with acquiring what he lacks and preserving what he has found.
23:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

23:1.arabic: ومفتاح مزيد الدرجات هي الصلوات. قال الله عز وجل: ﴿ قد أفلح المؤمنون الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون ﴾ {} فمدحهم بعد الإيمان بصلاة مخصوصة وهي المقرونة بالخشوع ثم ختم أوصاف المفلحين بالصلاة أيضا فقال تعالى: ﴿ والذين هم على صلواتهم يحافظون ﴾ {} ثم قال تعالى في ثمرة تلك الصفات: ﴿ أولئك هم الوارثون الذين يرثون الفردوس هم فيها خالدون ﴾ {} فوصفهم بالفلاح أوّلا وبوراثة الفردوس آخرا وما عندي أن هذرمة اللسان مع غفلة القلب تنتهي إلى هذا الحد ولذلك قال الله عز وجل في أضدادهم: ﴿ ما سلككم في سقر قالوا لم نك من المص
23:1.english: And the key to increased ranks are the prayers. Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, the believers have succeeded (Qad aflaha al-mu'minoona) - those who are in their prayer humbly submissive (khashi'oon)' {} So He praised them after faith with a specific prayer - that which is accompanied by humble submission (khushoo'). Then He concluded the attributes of the successful ones with prayer also, saying the Exalted: 'And those who are over their prayers guardians (muhafidhoon)' {} Then He said the Exalted regarding the fruit of those attributes: 'Those are the inheritors (al-warithoon) who will inherit Paradise (al-Firdaws) - they will abide therein eternally' {} So He described them with success (al-falah) first and with inheritance of Paradise (al-Firdaws) last. And in my view, the rapid movement of the tongue with heedlessness of the Heart (Qalb) does not reach this limit. Therefore Allah the Exalted said regarding their opposites: 'What has caused you to enter Saqar? They will say, We were not of those who prayed (al-musalleen)' {} So the ones who pray (al-musalleen) are the inheritors of Paradise (al-Firdaws), and they are the witnesses to the Light (Nur) of Allah the Exalted and those who enjoy His proximity (qurb) and nearness (dunuw) to their Hearts (Quloob).
23:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

23:1.arabic: الثاني: أن تفتر نفسه عن فضائل الأعمال ويقتصر على الفرائض فيرجى نفسه نعيم الله تعالى وما وعد به الصالحين حتى ينبعث من الرجاء نشاط العبادة فيقبل على الفضائل ويتذكر قوله تعالى "قد أفلح المؤمنون الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون" إلى قوله "أولئك هم الوارثون الذين يرثون الفردوس هم فيها خالدون" فالرجاء الأول: يقمع القنوط المانع من التوبة. الرجاء الثاني: يقمع الفتور المانع من النشاط والتشمر، فكل توقع حث على توبة أو على تشمر في العبادة فهو رجاء، وكل رجاء أوجب فتوراً في العبادة وركوناً إلى البطالة فهو غرة
23:1.english: The second: That his Soul (Nafs) becomes lax regarding virtuous deeds and restricts itself to obligatory duties, then he hopes for himself the bliss of Allah the Exalted and what He promised the righteous ones, until from the Hope (Rajā') arises the vigor of worship, so he turns toward the virtues and remembers His saying the Exalted: "Indeed, the believers have succeeded (Qad aflaḥa al-mu'minūn) - those who in their prayer are humble (khāshiʿūn)" up to His saying: "Those are the inheritors who will inherit Paradise, wherein they will abide eternally." So the first Hope (Rajā'): suppresses the despair that prevents repentance. The second Hope (Rajā'): suppresses the laxity that prevents vigor and exertion, so every expectation that urges toward repentance or toward exertion in worship is Hope (Rajā'), and every Hope (Rajā') that causes laxity in worship and leaning toward idleness is delusion.
23:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

23:2.arabic: فهذا تفصيل صلاة الخاشعين الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون والذين هم على صلواتهم يحافظون والذين هم على صلاتهم دائمون والذين هم يناجون الله على قدر استطاعتهم في العبودية فليعرض الإنسان نفسه على هذه الصلاة فبالقدر الذي يسر له منه ينبغي أن يفرح وعلى ما يفوته ينبغي أن يتحسر وفي مداراة ذلك ينبغي أن يجتهد.
23:2.english: This is the detailed explanation of the prayer of those who are humble (Khashi'un) who are in their prayer humble (Khashi'un) and those who are over their prayers preserving and those who are over their prayers constant and those who are conversing with Allah (Munajun) according to their capability in servitude (Ubudiyyah). So let the human being present himself to this prayer, for by the measure that is made easy for him from it, he should rejoice, and over what he misses from it, he should grieve, and in managing that, he should strive diligently.
23:2.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

23:8.arabic: وقال تعالى والذين هم لأماناتهم وعهدهم راعون والذين هم بشهاداتهم قائمون وقال ابن المبارك لرجل راقب الله تعالى فسأله عن تفسيره فقال كن أبدا كأنك ترى الله عز وجل
23:8.english: And Allah the Exalted said: 'And those who are guardians of their trusts and their covenants' and 'those who stand by their testimonies'. And Ibn al-Mubarak said to a man: 'Observe (raqqaba) Allah the Exalted', and he asked him about its interpretation, so he said: 'Be always as if you see Allah, the Mighty and Majestic'.
23:8.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

23:9.arabic: ومفتاح مزيد الدرجات هي الصلوات. قال الله عز وجل: ﴿ قد أفلح المؤمنون الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون ﴾ فمدحهم بعد الإيمان بصلاة مخصوصة وهي المقرونة بالخشوع ثم ختم أوصاف المفلحين بالصلاة أيضا فقال تعالى: ﴿ والذين هم على صلواتهم يحافظون ﴾ ثم قال تعالى في ثمرة تلك الصفات: ﴿ أولئك هم الوارثون الذين يرثون الفردوس هم فيها خالدون ﴾ فوصفهم بالفلاح أوّلا وبوراثة الفردوس آخرا وما عندي أن هذرمة اللسان مع غفلة القلب تنتهي إلى هذا الحد ولذلك قال الله عز وجل في أضدادهم: ﴿ ما سلككم في سقر قالوا لم نك من المصلين ﴾ فال
23:9.english: And the key to increased degrees (of closeness to Allah) are the prayers. Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, the believers have succeeded: those who are in their prayer humbly submissive (Khashaʿūn)' (Quran 23:1-2). He praised them after faith with a specific prayer, which is the one accompanied by humble submission (Khashūʿ). Then He concluded the attributes of the successful ones with prayer as well, saying: 'And those who are over their prayers guardians (Yuḥāfiẓūn)' (Quran 23:9). Then He said regarding the fruit of those attributes: 'Those are the inheritors who will inherit Paradise, wherein they will abide eternally' (Quran 23:10-11). He described them with success first and with inheriting Paradise last. And in my view, the rapid movement of the tongue with heedlessness of the heart (Qalb) does not reach this limit. Therefore, Allah the Exalted said about their opposites: 'What has caused you to enter Hell?' They will say, 'We were not of those who prayed' (Quran 74:42-43). So the ones who pray are the inheritors of Paradise, and they are the witnesses to the light of Allah the Exalted and those who enjoy His closeness and nearness to their hearts (Qulūb).
23:9.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

23:9.arabic: فهذا تفصيل صلاة الخاشعين الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون والذين هم على صلواتهم يحافظون والذين هم على صلاتهم دائمون والذين هم يناجون الله على قدر استطاعتهم في العبودية فليعرض الإنسان نفسه على هذه الصلاة فبالقدر الذي يسر له منه ينبغي أن يفرح وعلى ما يفوته ينبغي أن يتحسر وفي مداراة ذلك ينبغي أن يجتهد.
23:9.english: This is the detailed description of the prayer of those who are humble (Khashīʿūn) - those who are humble in their prayer, and those who guard (Yuḥāfiẓūn) their prayers, and those who are constant (Dāʾimūn) in their prayer, and those who converse (Yunājūn) with Allah according to their capability in servitude (ʿUbūdiyyah). So let a person examine himself against this prayer: for the portion that is made easy for him from it, he should rejoice; and for what he misses from it, he should grieve; and in striving for that, he should exert effort.
23:9.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

23:10.arabic: الثاني: أن تفتر نفسه عن فضائل الأعمال ويقتصر على الفرائض فيرجى نفسه نعيم الله تعالى وما وعد به الصالحين حتى ينبعث من الرجاء نشاط العبادة فيقبل على الفضائل ويتذكر قوله تعالى "قد أفلح المؤمنون الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون" إلى قوله "أولئك هم الوارثون الذين يرثون الفردوس هم فيها خالدون" فالرجاء الأول: يقمع القنوط المانع من التوبة. الرجاء الثاني: يقمع الفتور المانع من النشاط والتشمر، فكل توقع حث على توبة أو على تشمر في العبادة فهو رجاء، وكل رجاء أوجب فتوراً في العبادة وركوناً إلى البطالة فهو غرة، كما إ
23:10.english: The second: that his Soul (Nafs) slackens from the virtues of deeds and he restricts himself to the obligations, so he hopes for himself the bliss of Allah the Exalted and what He promised the righteous, until from the Hope (Rajā') springs the vigor of worship, so he turns to the virtues and remembers His saying the Exalted: "Indeed, the believers have succeeded—those who are humble in their prayer" to His saying: "Those are the inheritors who will inherit Paradise, wherein they will abide eternally." So the first Hope (Rajā'): suppresses the despair that prevents repentance. The second Hope (Rajā'): suppresses the slackness that prevents vigor and exertion, so every expectation that urges to repentance or to exertion in worship is Hope (Rajā'), and every Hope (Rajā') that causes slackness in worship and leaning to idleness is deception (Gharra), as if it occurs to him to abandon the sin and engage in work, so Satan says to him: What is it to you to harm your Soul (Nafs) and torment it, and you have a Lord generous, forgiving, merciful? So he slackens from that in repentance and worship—that is deception (Gharra). And at this, it is obligatory upon the servant to employ Fear (Khawf), so he frightens his Soul (Nafs) with the anger of Allah and His great punishment and says: Indeed, He, while He is the forgiver of the sin and the acceptor of repentance, is severe in punishment; and He, while He is generous, made the disbelievers abide in the Fire forever and ever, while their disbelief did not harm Him, but rather He unleashed punishment, trials, illnesses, ailments, poverty, and hunger upon a group of His servants in this world, and He is capable of removing them. So from this is His way (Sunnah) with His servants, and He has frightened me with His punishment—so how can I not fear Him, and how can I be deceived by Him?
23:10.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

23:10.arabic: ومفتاح مزيد الدرجات هي الصلوات. قال الله عز وجل: ﴿ قد أفلح المؤمنون الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون ﴾ فمدحهم بعد الإيمان بصلاة مخصوصة وهي المقرونة بالخشوع ثم ختم أوصاف المفلحين بالصلاة أيضا فقال تعالى: ﴿ والذين هم على صلواتهم يحافظون ﴾ ثم قال تعالى في ثمرة تلك الصفات: ﴿ أولئك هم الوارثون الذين يرثون الفردوس هم فيها خالدون ﴾ فوصفهم بالفلاح أوّلا وبوراثة الفردوس آخرا وما عندي أن هذرمة اللسان مع غفلة القلب تنتهي إلى هذا الحد ولذلك قال الله عز وجل في أضدادهم: ﴿ ما سلككم في سقر قالوا لم نك من المصلين ﴾ فال
23:10.english: And the key to increased degrees (of closeness to Allah) is the prayers. Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, the believers have succeeded - those who are in their prayer humbly submissive (Khashaʿūn).' So He praised them after faith with a specific prayer, which is the one accompanied by humble submission (Khashūʿ). Then He concluded the descriptions of the successful ones with prayer also, saying the Exalted: 'And those who are of their prayers guardians.' Then He said the Exalted in the fruit of those attributes: 'Those are the inheritors (Al-Wārithūn) who will inherit Paradise (Al-Firdaws); they will abide therein eternally.' So He described them with success first and with inheritance of Paradise (Al-Firdaws) last. And in my view, the rapid movement of the tongue with heedlessness of the heart (Qalb) does not reach this limit. And therefore Allah the Exalted said about their opposites: 'What has put you into Saqar?' They will say, 'We were not of those who prayed.' So the ones who pray are the inheritors of Paradise (Al-Firdaws), and they are the witnesses to the light of Allah the Exalted and those who enjoy His closeness and nearness to their hearts (Qulūb).
23:10.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

23:12.arabic: وقال تعالى ولقد خلقنا الإنسان من سلالة من طين ثم جعلناه نطفة في قرار مكين ثم خلقنا النطفة علقة الآية فتكرير ذكر النطفة في الكتاب العزيز ليس ليسمع لفظه ويترك التفكر في معناه فانظر الآن إلى النطفة وهي قطرة من الماء قذرة لو تركت ساعة ليضربها الهواء فسدت وانتنت كيف أخرجها رب الأرباب من الصلب والترائب وكيف جمع بين الذكر والأنثى وألقى الألفة والمحبة في قلوبهم وكيف قادهم بسلسلة المحبة والشهوة الى الاجتماع وكيف استخرج النطفة من الرجل بحركة الوقاع وكيف استجلب دم الحيض من أعماق العروق وجمعه في الرحم ثم كي
23:12.english: And He (Allah), the Exalted, said: 'And verily We created the human being from an extract of clay (sulālat min ṭīn), then We made him a sperm-drop (nuṭfah) in a firm resting-place (qarārin makīn), then We created the sperm-drop a clinging clot (ʿalaqah)' - the verse. So the repetition of the mention of the sperm-drop in the Noble Book is not to hear its wording and abandon reflection (tafakkur) upon its meaning. So look now at the sperm-drop: it is a drop of impure water; if left for an hour for the air to strike it, it would spoil and become foul-smelling. How did the Lord of lords (Rabb al-arbāb) bring it forth from the loins (ṣulb) and the breastbones (tarāʾib)? And how did He bring together the male and the female and cast affection (ulfah) and love (maḥabbah) into their hearts (qulūb)? And how did He lead them by the chain of love (maḥabbah) and desire (shahwah) to union? And how did He extract the sperm-drop from the man by the movement of intercourse? And how did He draw the menstrual blood from the depths of the veins and gather it in the womb? Then how did He create the newborn from the sperm-drop and water it with the menstrual water and nourish it until it grew, increased, and became large? And how did He make the sperm-drop, which is white and shining, a red clinging clot? Then how did He make it a chewed lump (muḍghah)? Then how did He divide the parts of the sperm-drop, which are equal and similar, into bones, nerves, veins, tendons, and flesh? Then how did He construct from the flesh, nerves, and veins the apparent limbs: the roundness of the head, the splitting of hearing and sight, the nose, the mouth, and the other openings? Then He extended the hand and the leg and divided their heads with fingers and divided the fingers with fingertips. Then how did He construct the internal limbs from the heart (qalb), stomach, liver, spleen, lung, womb, bladder, and intestines, each one in a specific form and specific measure for a specific function? Then how did He divide each limb from th[is]...
23:12.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Contemplation'

23:14.arabic: فإذا سجدت فقل: اللهم لك سجدت وبك آمنت ولك أسلمت سجد وجهي للذي خلقه وصوره وشق سمعه وبصره فتبارك الله أحسن الخالقين اللهم سجد لك سوادي وخيالي وآمن بك فؤادي أبوء بنعمتك علي وأبوء بذنبي وهذا ما جنيت على نفسي فاغفر لي فإنه لا يغفر الذنوب إلا أنت[193]
23:14.english: And when you prostrate, say: O Allah, to You I have prostrated, and in You I have believed, and to You I have submitted. My face has prostrated to the One who created it and formed it and split its hearing and its sight. So blessed is Allah, the best of creators. O Allah, my blackness and my imagination have prostrated to You, and my heart (Fūād) has believed in You. I acknowledge Your blessings upon me, and I acknowledge my sin, and this is what I have earned against myself, so forgive me, for none forgives sins except You.
23:14.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith

23:27.arabic: فقد روي أن نوحا عليه السلام لما ركب السفينة حمل فيها من كل زوجين اثنين كما أمره الله تعالى فرأى في السفينة شيخا لم يعرفه فقال له نوح ما أدخلك فقال دخلت لأصيب قلوب أصحابك فتكون قلوبهم معي وأبدانهم معك فقال له نوح أخرج منها يا عدو الله فإنك لعين فقال له إبليس خمس أهلك بهن الناس وسأحدثك منهم بثلاث ولا أحدثك باثنتين فأوحى الله تعالى إلى نوح أنه لا حاجة لك بالثلاث فليحدثك بالاثنين فقال له نوح ما الاثنتان فقال هما اللتان لا تكذباني هما اللتان لا تخلفاني بهما أهلك الناس الحرص والحسد فبالحسد لعنت وجعلت
23:27.english: It has been narrated that when Noah (peace be upon him) boarded the Ark, he carried therein from every pair two, as Allah the Exalted commanded him. Then he saw in the Ark an old man he did not recognize. So Noah said to him: 'What brought you in?' He said: 'I entered to capture the hearts (Qulūb) of your companions, so that their hearts would be with me and their bodies with you.' So Noah said to him: 'Get out of it, O enemy of Allah, for you are indeed an evil eye.' So Iblis said to him: 'Five [things] with which I destroy people, and I will tell you of three of them, but I will not tell you of two.' So Allah the Exalted revealed to Noah that he had no need for the three; let him tell you of the two. So Noah said to him: 'What are the two?' He said: 'They are the two about which you will not call me a liar. They are the two about which I will not fail you with them. I destroy people with greed (al-Ḥirṣ) and envy (al-Ḥasad). For by envy I was cursed and made a rejected devil (Shayṭān Rajīm). As for greed, indeed, Adam was permitted all of Paradise except the tree, so I attained my need from him through greed.'
23:27.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

23:34.arabic: القسم الثاني: التكبر على الرسل من حيث تعزز النفس وترفعها على الانقياد لبشر مثل سائر الناس؛ وذلك تارة يصرف عن الفكر والاستبصار فيبقى في ظلمة الجهل بكبره فيمتنع عن الانقياد وهو ظان أنه محق فيه، وتارة يمتنع مع المعرفة ولكن لا تطاوعه نفسه للإنقياد للحق والتواضع للرسل، كما حكى الله قولهم "أنؤمن لبشرين مثلنا" وقولهم "إن أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا ولئن أطعتم بشراً مثلكم إنكم إذا لخاسرون" وقال الذين لا يرجون لقائنا لولا أنزل علينا الملائكة أو نرى ربنا لقد استكبروا في أنفسهم وعتوا عواً كبيراً.
23:34.english: The second category: Arrogance (Takabbur) toward the Messengers, stemming from the Soul (Nafs) strengthening and elevating itself against submission to a human being like other people. This sometimes diverts from thought (Fikr) and insight (Istibsar), leaving one in the darkness of ignorance due to his arrogance, preventing submission while thinking he is correct in it. And sometimes he refuses despite knowledge, but his Soul (Nafs) does not comply with submission to the Truth (Haqq) and humility toward the Messengers, as Allah narrated their saying: "Shall we believe in two humans like ourselves?" and their saying: "You are only humans like us, and if you obey a human like yourselves, indeed you would then be losers." And those who do not expect the meeting with Us said: "Why have not angels been sent down to us, or why do we not see our Lord?" They have certainly become arrogant within themselves and transgressed a great transgression.
23:34.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

23:34.arabic: السبب الرابع: التعجب، كما أخبر الله تعالى عن الأمم السالفة إذ قالوا "ما أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا" "وقالوا أنؤمن لبشرين مثلنا" "ولئن أطعتم بشراً مثلكم إنكم إذاً لخاسرون" فتعجبوا من أن يفوز برتبة الرسالة والوحي والقرب من الله تعالى بشر مثلهم فحسدوهم، وأحبوا زوال النبوة عنهم جزعاً أن يفضل عليهم من هو مثلهم في الخلقة، لا عن قصد تكبر وطلب رياسة وتقدم عداوة أو سبب آخر من سائر الأسباب، وقالوا متعجبين "أبعث الله بشراً رسولاً" وقالوا "لولا أنزل علينا الملائكة" وقال تعالى "أو عجبتم أن جاءكم ذكر من ربكم على رجل
23:34.english: The fourth cause: Amazement (Ta'ajjub), as Allah the Exalted informed about the past nations when they said 'You are only human beings like us' and 'Shall we believe in two human beings like ourselves?' and 'And if you obey a human being like yourselves, then indeed, you would then be losers.' So they were amazed that a human being like them would attain the rank of Messengership, revelation, and closeness to Allah the Exalted, so they envied them, and they desired the removal of prophethood from them out of distress that someone like them in creation would be favored over them, not from an intention of arrogance (Takabbur) and seeking leadership and advancement of enmity or another cause from all the causes, and they said in amazement 'Has Allah sent a human being as a messenger?' and they said 'Why were not angels sent down to us?' and Allah the Exalted said 'Or do you wonder that there has come to you a reminder (Dhikr) from your Lord upon a man from among you?' the verse.
23:34.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

23:38.arabic: وقد سوى الله تعالى بين من افترى على الله كذبا وبين من كذب بالحق فقال تعالى: (ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بالحق لما جاءه( (العنكبوت: 68). وقال تعالى: (فمن أظلم ممن كذب على الله وكذب بالصدق إذ جاءه( (الزمر: 32). ومنها الرياء، وملاحظة الخلق والجهد في استمالة قلوبهم وصرف وجوههم والرياء هو الداء العضال الذي يدعو إلى أكبر الكبائر كما سيأتي في كتاب الرياء والمناظر لا يقصد إلا الظهور عند الخلق وانطلاق ألسنتهم بالثناء عليه فهذه عشر خصال من أمهات الفواحش الباطنة سوى ما يتفق لغير المتماسكين منه
23:38.english: And Allah the Exalted has equated between one who fabricates lies against Allah and one who denies the truth, as He said: 'And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah or denies the truth when it has come to him?' (Al-Ankabut: 68). And He said: 'So who is more unjust than one who lies about Allah and denies the truth when it comes to him?' (Az-Zumar: 32). And among them is ostentation (Riya'), and observing the creation and striving to attract their hearts (Qulub) and divert their faces, and ostentation (Riya') is the incurable disease that leads to the greatest major sins, as will come in the Book of Ostentation (Kitab al-Riya'), and the disputer intends nothing but appearing before the creation and the release of their tongues with praise upon him. These are ten traits from the mothers of hidden abominations, aside from what occurs to those among them who are not restrained from quarreling leading to hitting, punching, slapping, tearing clothes, grabbing beards, cursing parents, insulting teachers, and explicit slander, for those are not counted among the group of considered people. Rather, the great ones and the rational ones among them are those who do not desist from these ten traits. Yes, some of them may be safe from some of them with one who is apparently inferior to him or apparently superior to him or is distant from his land and means of livelihood, and none of them desists from it with his similar counterparts who are equal to him in rank. Then from each one of these ten traits branches out ten other vices, we have not prolonged with mentioning them and detailing their individuals, such as haughtiness, anger, hatred, and greed.
23:38.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Book of Knowledge'

23:43.arabic: إلى يوم من أيامها. وروي أنه انصرف الناس ذات يوم من مجلس ابن عباس وبقي شاب لم يبرح فقال له ابن عباس هل لك من حاجة قال نعم أردت أن اسأل مسألة فاستحييت من الناس وأنا الآن أهابك وأجلك فقال ابن عباس إن العالم بمنزلة الوالد فما كنت أفضيت به إلى أبيك فأفض إلي به فقال أني شاب لا زوجة لي وربما خشيت العنت على نفسي فربما استمنيت بيدي فهل في ذلك معصية فأعرض عنه ابن عباس ثم قال أف وتف نكاح الأمة خير منه وهو خير من الزنا) فهذا تنبيه على أن العزب المغتلم مردد بين ثلاثة شرور أدناها نكاح الأمة وفيه إرقاق الولد و
23:43.english: To a day of its days. And it is narrated that people departed one day from the council of Ibn Abbas and a young man remained who did not leave, so Ibn Abbas said to him: Do you have a need? He said: Yes, I wanted to ask a question but I was shy from the people, and I now revere and honor you. So Ibn Abbas said: The scholar is in the position of a parent, so what you would have confided to your father, confide to me with it. He said: I am a young man without a wife, and perhaps I fear hardship upon my Soul (Nafs), so perhaps I masturbate with my hand; is there in that disobedience? So Ibn Abbas turned away from him, then said: Ugh and pah, marriage to a slave woman is better than it, and it is better than fornication. This is an alert that the unmarried, sexually mature person is wavering between three evils: the least of them is marriage to a slave woman, and in it is the enslavement of the child; and more severe than it is masturbation with the hand; and the most vile is fornication. And Ibn Abbas did not declare permissibility in anything of it because they are two feared things one resorts to out of fear of falling into a more feared thing, just as one resorts to consuming carrion out of fear of the destruction of the Soul (Nafs). So preferring the lesser of two evils is not in the meaning of absolute permissibility nor in the meaning of absolute good, and cutting off the hand that is consuming from the good things, even if it is permitted when the Soul (Nafs) is on the verge of destruction. So indeed in marriage there is merit from this aspect, but this does not encompass everyone, rather the majority. For perhaps a person's desire weakens due to old age or illness or other, so this motive disappears in his case, and what preceded regarding the matter of the child remains, for that is general except for the effaced one, which is rare. And from the natures are those overcome by desire such that a single woman does not protect him, so it is recommended for its possessor to increase beyond one to four, if Allah facilitates for him affection and mercy and his Heart (Qalb) is at ease with them; otherwise, it is recommended for him to replace. Indeed, Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, married after the death of Fatimah, peace be upon her, by seven nights, and it is said that Al-Hasan ibn Ali was much-marrying until he married more than two hundred women, and he would perhaps contract on four at one time and perhaps divorce four at one time and replace them. And the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to Al-Hasan: You resemble my creation and my character. And the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Al-Hasan is from me and Al-Husayn is from Ali. So he said: The abundance of his marriage is one of what he resembled with the creation of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. And Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah married eighty women, and among the Companions were those who had three and four, and those who had two are uncountable. And whenever the motive is known, the treatment should be according to the ailment, so the intent is to calm the Soul (Nafs), so let it be looked at in abundance and scarcity. The third benefit: refreshing the Soul (Nafs) and comforting it with companionship, looking, and play, as a relief for the Heart (Qalb) and a strengthening for it upon worship, for the Soul (Nafs) is fickle and it is averse from the Truth because it is contrary to its nature, so if it were burdened
23:43.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

23:51.arabic: وعليه نبه رب العالمين بقوله وهو أصدق القائلين كلوا من الطيبات واعملوا صالحا فمن يقدم على الأكل ليستعين به على العلم والعمل ويقوى به على التقوى فلا ينبغي أن يترك نفسه مهملا سدى يسترسل في الأكل استرسال البهائم في المرعى فإن ما هو ذريعة إلى الدين ووسيلة إليه ينبغي أن تظهر أنوار الدين عليه وإنما أنوار الدين آدابه وسننه التي يزم العبد بزمامها ويلجم المتقى بلجامها حتى يتزن بميزان الشرع شهوة الطعام في إقدامها وإحجامها فيصير بسببها مدفعة للوزر ومجلبة للأجر وإن كان فيها أوفى حظ للنفس
23:51.english: And upon this, the Lord of the Worlds alerted by His saying, and He is the Most Truthful of Speakers: 'Eat from the good things and do righteous deeds.' So whoever proceeds to eat to seek assistance through it for knowledge and action, and to strengthen through it for piety (Taqwa), then it is not fitting that he leaves his self (Nafs) neglected, aimlessly, indulging in eating like the indulgence of beasts in pasture. For what is a means to the religion and a path to it, it is necessary that the lights of the religion appear upon it. And indeed, the lights of the religion are its etiquettes (Adab) and its established practices (Sunnah) which the servant (Abd) reins with its reins and bridles the pious (Muttaqi) with its bridle, until he balances with the scale of the Sharia the appetite (Shahwa) for food in its advance and retreat, so that through it becomes a repeller of sin and an attractor of reward, even if in it is the fullest share for the self (Nafs).
23:51.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Manners of Eating'

23:51.arabic: الباب الأول في فضيلة الحلال ومذمة الحرام وبيان أصناف الحلال ودرجاته وأصناف الحرام ودرجات الورع فيه فضيلة الحلال ومذمة الحرام قال الله تعالى كلوا من الطيبات واعملوا صالحا أمر بالأكل من الطيبات قبل العمل وقيل إن المراد به الحلال وقال تعالى ولا تأكلوا أموالكم بينكم بالباطل وقال تعالى إن الذين يأكلون أموال اليتامى ظلما الآية وقال تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وذروا ما بقي من الربا إن كنتم مؤمنين ثم قال فإن لم تفعلوا فأذنوا بحرب من الله ورسوله ثم قال وإن تبتم فلكم رءوس أموالكم ثم قال ومن عاد ف
23:51.english: Chapter One: On the virtue of the lawful (Halal) and the censure of the forbidden (Haram), and clarifying the types of the lawful and its degrees, and the types of the forbidden and the degrees of scrupulousness (Wara') in it. The virtue of the lawful and the censure of the forbidden. Allah the Exalted said: 'Eat from the good things and work righteousness.' He commanded eating from the good things before work, and it is said that what is intended by it is the lawful. And He the Exalted said: 'And do not consume your properties among yourselves unjustly.' And He the Exalted said: 'Indeed, those who consume the properties of the orphans unjustly...' the verse. And He the Exalted said: 'O you who have believed, fear Allah and give up what remains [due to you] of usury, if you should be believers.' Then He said: 'And if you do not, then be informed of a war [against you] from Allah and His Messenger.' Then He said: 'But if you repent, you may have your principal.' Then He said: 'And whoever returns to [dealing in usury] - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide eternally therein.' He made the consumer of usury at the beginning of the matter announcing war from Allah, and at its end exposed to the Fire. And the verses concerning the lawful and the forbidden are innumerable. And Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that he said: 'Seeking the lawful is an obligation upon every Muslim.' And when he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'Seeking knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim' - the hadith 'Seeking knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim' preceded in knowledge. Some scholars said he intended by it seeking knowledge of the lawful and the forbidden, and made the meaning of the two hadiths one. And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'Whoever strives for his dependents from his lawful (Halal) earning, he is like the warrior in the path of Allah, and whoever seeks the worldly life lawfully in chastity, he is in the rank of the martyrs.' The hadith: 'Whoever strives for his dependents from his lawful earning, he is like the warrior in the path of Allah, and whoever seeks the worldly life in chastity, he is in the rank of...
23:51.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

23:51.arabic: أما علمت أن الأكل من الدين قدمه الله تعالى على العمل الصالح فقال كلوا من الطيبات واعملوا صالحا وفي الخبر أنه مكتوب في التوراة من لم يبال من أين مطعمه لم يبال الله من أي أبواب النيران أدخله
23:51.english: Did you not know that eating is from the religion (Deen) which Allah the Exalted placed before righteous action, so He said: 'Eat from the good things and do righteous deeds.' And in the report, it is written in the Torah: 'Whoever does not care from where his food comes, Allah will not care from which gates of the Fire He enters him.'
23:51.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

23:53.arabic: الثامن العجب بالرأي الخطأ. قال الله تعالى "أفمن زين له سوء عمله فرآه حسناً" وقال تعالى "وهم يحسبون أنهم يحسنون صنعاً" وقد أخبر رسول الله ﭬ: أن ذلك يغلب على آخر هذه الأمة[101] وبذلك هلكت الأمم السالفة إذ افترقت فرقاً فكل معجب برأيه "وكل حزب بما لديهم فرحون" وجميع أهل البدع والضلال إنما أصروا عليها لعجبهم بآرائهم والعجب بالبدعة هو استحسان ما يسوق إليه الهوى والشهوة مع ظن كونه حقاً، وعلاج هذا العجب أشد من علاج غيره لأن صاحب الرأي الخطأ جاهل بخطئه ولو عرفه لتركه، ولا يعالج الداء الذي لا يعرف والجهل
23:53.english: The eighth [type of pride] is pride in erroneous opinion. Allah the Exalted said: 'Is he whose evil deed is made fair-seeming unto him so that he sees it as good?' and He said: 'And they think that they are doing well.' And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) informed: that this will prevail over the latter part of this nation. And by this, the past nations perished when they split into factions, each one proud of his opinion 'and every party rejoices in what is with them.' And all the people of innovation and misguidance only persist in them due to their pride in their opinions, and pride in innovation is the approval of what the desire (Hawa) and appetite (Shahwa) lead to with the assumption of its being truth. The treatment of this pride is more severe than the treatment of others because the possessor of erroneous opinion is ignorant (Jahil) of his error, and if he knew it, he would abandon it, and the disease that is not known is not treated, and ignorance (Jahl) is a disease that is not known, so its cure becomes extremely difficult.
23:53.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

23:53.arabic: ولا يزالون مختلفين كل حزب بما لديهم فرحون ولذلك خلقهم حكى أن أحمد بن خضرويه رأى ربه عز وجل في المنام فقال له كل الناس يطلبون مني الجنة إلا أبا يزيد فإنه يطلبني ورأى أبو يزيد ربه في المنام فقال يا رب كيف الطريق اليك فقال اترك نفسك وتعال إلي ورؤى الشبلي بعد موته في المنام فقيل له ما فعل الله بك فقال لم يطالبني على الدعاوي بالبرهان إلا على قول واحد قلت يوما أي خسارة أعظم من خسران الجنة فقال أي خسارة أعظم من خسران لقائي
23:53.english: And they will not cease to differ; every faction rejoices in what they have with them. And for that He created them. It was narrated that Ahmad ibn Khadruwayh saw his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, in a dream, and He said to him: 'All people ask Me for Paradise except Abu Yazid, for he asks for Me.' And Abu Yazid saw his Lord in a dream and said: 'O Lord, how is the path to You?' He said: 'Leave your soul (Nafs) and come to Me.' And Al-Shibli was seen after his death in a dream, and it was said to him: 'What did Allah do with you?' He said: 'He did not demand from me proof for the claims except for one statement: I said one day: What loss is greater than the loss of Paradise? He said: What loss is greater than the loss of My meeting?'
23:53.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

23:55.arabic: وهذا الغرور علاجه معرفة دلائل الكرامة والهوان إما بالبصيرة أو بالتقليد أما البصيرة فبأن يعرف وجه كون الالتفات إلى شهوات الدنيا مبعد عن الله ووجه كون التباعد عنها مقرباً إلى الله ويدرك ذلك بالإلهام في منازل العارفين والأولياء، وشرحه من جملة علوم المكاشفة ولا يليق بعلم المعاملة "وأما معرفته بطريق التقليد والتصديق" فهو أن يؤمن بكتاب الله تعالى ويصدق رسوله وقد قال تعالى "أيحسبون أن ما نمدهم به من مال وبنين نسارع لهم في الخيرات بل لا يشعرون"
23:55.english: And the cure for this delusion (Ghurur) is knowing the signs of honor (Karama) and humiliation (Hawan) either through insight (Basira) or through imitation (Taqleed). As for insight, it is by knowing how turning toward worldly desires distances one from Allah and how distancing oneself from them brings one closer to Allah, and one perceives that through inspiration (Ilham) in the stations of the knowers (Arifin) and the friends (Awliya), and its explanation is among the sciences of unveiling (Kashf) and is not suitable for the science of transaction. "And as for knowing it through the way of imitation and belief," it is to have faith in the Book of Allah the Exalted and to believe His Messenger. And He the Exalted has said: "Do they think that what We extend to them of wealth and children We hasten for them in good things? Rather, they do not perceive."
23:55.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

23:57.arabic: والذي يدل على فضيلة هذه الخصلة قوله تعالى "يؤتون ما آتوا وقلوبهم وجلة أنهم إلى ربهم راجعون" أي أنهم يؤتون الطاعات وهم على وجل عظيم من قبولها وقال تعالى "إن الذين هم من خشية ربهم مشفقون" وقال تعالى "إنا كنا قبل في أهلنا مشفقين" وقد وصف الله تعالى الملائكة عليهم السلام مع تقدسهم عن الذنوب ومواظبتهم على العبادات على الدءوب بالإشفاق فقال تعالى مخبراً عنهم "يسحبون الليل والنهار لا يفترون وهم من خشيته مشفقون" فمتى زال الإشفاق والحذر مما سبق به القضاء في الأزل - وينكشف عند خاتمة الأجل - غلب الأمن من مك
23:57.english: And that which indicates the virtue of this characteristic is His saying, the Exalted: "They give what they give while their hearts are fearful (وجلة) that they are returning to their Lord" meaning that they perform acts of obedience while in great fear (وجل) of their acceptance. And He said, the Exalted: "Indeed, those who are from the fear (خشية) of their Lord apprehensive (مشفقون)" and He said, the Exalted: "Indeed we were before among our people apprehensive (مشفقين)". And Allah, the Exalted, described the angels, peace be upon them, with their sanctity from sins and their persistence in worship diligently with apprehension (الإشفاق), so He said, the Exalted, informing about them: "They drag the night and the day without ceasing and they are from fear (خشيته) of Him apprehensive (مشفقون)". So when apprehension (الإشفاق) and caution from what has preceded in the decree in eternity (الأزل) - and is revealed at the end of the term (الأجل) - is removed, security from the deception of Allah prevails, and that necessitates arrogance, which is the cause of destruction.
23:57.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

23:60.arabic: والذي يدل على فضيلة هذه الخصلة قوله تعالى "يؤتون ما آتوا وقلوبهم وجلة أنهم إلى ربهم راجعون" أي أنهم يؤتون الطاعات وهم على وجل عظيم من قبولها وقال تعالى "إن الذين هم من خشية ربهم مشفقون" وقال تعالى "إنا كنا قبل في أهلنا مشفقين" وقد وصف الله تعالى الملائكة عليهم السلام مع تقدسهم عن الذنوب ومواظبتهم على العبادات على الدءوب بالإشفاق فقال تعالى مخبراً عنهم "يسحبون الليل والنهار لا يفترون وهم من خشيته مشفقون" فمتى زال الإشفاق والحذر مما سبق به القضاء في الأزل - وينكشف عند خاتمة الأجل - غلب الأمن من مك
23:60.english: And what indicates the virtue of this characteristic is the saying of Allah the Exalted: 'And those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful (Wajila) that they are to their Lord returning' (23:60), meaning that they give the acts of obedience while they are in great fear (Wajal) of their acceptance. And He the Exalted said: 'Indeed, those who are from fear (Khashya) of their Lord are apprehensive (Mushfiqun)' (23:57). And He the Exalted said: 'Indeed, we were before among our people apprehensive (Mushfiqun)' (52:26). And Allah the Exalted described the angels, peace be upon them, with their sanctity from sins and their persistence in acts of worship diligently, with apprehension (Ishfaq), as He the Exalted said informing about them: 'They drag the night and the day without ceasing, and they are from fear (Khashya) of Him apprehensive (Mushfiqun)' (21:20). So when the apprehension (Ishfaq) and caution from what has preceded in the decree in eternity (Al-Azal) - and is revealed at the end of the term (Al-Ajal) - is removed, security (Al-Amn) from the deception of Allah prevails, and that necessitates arrogance (Al-Kibr), which is the cause of destruction. So arrogance (Al-Kibr) is an indicator of security (Al-Amn), and security (Al-Amn) is destructive. And humility (Al-Tawadu') is an indicator of fear (Al-Khawf), and it is felicitous; therefore, what the worshipper corrupts by harboring arrogance (Al-Kibr) and despising the creation and looking at them with the eye of belittlement is more than what he rectifies with the apparent works. So these are knowledges (Ma'arif) by which the disease of arrogance (Al-Kibr) is removed from the heart (Al-Qalb) only, except that the soul (Al-Nafs) after this knowledge (Ma'rifa) may harbor humility (Al-Tawadu') and claim innocence from arrogance (Al-Kibr) while it is lying, so if it falls, it returns to its nature and forgets its promise, thus on this, it is not appropriate to suffice in the treatment with mere knowledge (Ma'rifa), but it should be completed with action (Al-'Amal) and tested with the actions of the humble in situations of the arousal of arrogance (Al-Kibr) in the soul (Al-Nafs).
23:60.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

23:60.arabic: وقد كان ما وعد به ﭬ فقد كان الناس في الأعصار الأول يواظبون على العبادات ويؤتون ما آتوا وقلوبهم وجلة أنهم إلى ربهم راجعون، يخافون على أنفسهم وهم طول الليل والنهار في طاعة الله يبالغون في التقوى والحذر من الشبهات والشهوات ويبكون على أنفسهم في الخلوات.
23:60.english: And what He (Allah) promised has come to pass, for the people in the earlier eras would consistently perform acts of worship and give what they gave while their hearts were fearful that they would return to their Lord. They would fear for their selves (Nafs) while they were throughout the night and day in obedience to Allah, they would go to extremes in piety (Taqwa) and caution from doubts and desires, and they would weep over their selves (Nafs) in seclusions.
23:60.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

23:60.arabic: [67] حديث عائشة قلت يا رسول الله - الذين يؤتون ما آتوا وقلوبهم وجلة - هو الرجل يسرق ويزني قال لا الحديث رواه الترمذي وابن ماجه والحاكم وقال صحيح الإسناد قلت بل منقطع بين عائشة وبين عبد الرحمن بن سعد بن وهب قال الترمذي وروي عن الرحمن بن حازم عن أبي هريرة.
23:60.english: Hadith: Aisha said: I said, O Messenger of Allah - 'And those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful (وَالَّذِينَ يُؤْتُونَ مَا آتَوْا وَقُلُوبُهُمْ وَجِلَةٌ)' - is this the man who steals and commits adultery? He said: No. The hadith was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, and Al-Hakim, and he said: Its chain is authentic. I said: Rather, it is disconnected between Aisha and Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'd ibn Wahb. Al-Tirmidhi said: And it was narrated from Al-Rahman ibn Hazim from Abu Huraira.
23:60.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Fear and Hope'

23:60.arabic: وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها: (قلت يا رسول الله ﴿ الذين يؤتون ما آتوا وقلوبهم وجلة ﴾ {} هو الرجل يسرق ويزني؟ قال: لا بل الرجل يصوم ويصلي ويتصدق ويخاف أن لا يقبل منه[67])
23:60.english: And Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: (I said: O Messenger of Allah, "Those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful (وَالَّذِينَ يُؤْتُونَ مَا آتَوْا وَقُلُوبُهُمْ وَجِلَةٌ)" — is it the man who steals and commits adultery? He said: No, rather it is the man who fasts, prays, gives charity, and fears that it may not be accepted from him[67]).
23:60.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

23:60.arabic: قال الحسن أجهدتهم العبادة قال الله تعالى والذين يؤتون ما آتوا وقلوبهم وجلة قال الحسن يعملون ما عملوا من أعمال البر ويخافون أن لا ينجيهم ذلك من عذاب الله
23:60.english: Al-Hasan said: 'Wearied them the worship (Ibadah).' Allah the Exalted said: 'And those who give what they give while their hearts (Qulub) are fearful that they will return to their Lord.' Al-Hasan said: 'They perform what they perform from righteous deeds (A'mal al-Birr) and they fear that it will not save them from the punishment of Allah.'
23:60.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

23:86.arabic: فإذا أصابك كرب فقل لا إله إلا الله العلي الحليم لا إله إلا الله رب العرش العظيم لا إله إلا الله رب السموات السبع ورب العرش الكريم
23:86.english: If distress befalls you, then say: There is no god but Allah, the Most High, the Forbearing; there is no god but Allah, the Lord of the Great Throne; there is no god but Allah, the Lord of the Seven Heavens and the Lord of the Noble Throne.
23:86.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

23:91.arabic: كان النخعي إذا مر بمثل قوله عز وجل: ﴿ ما اتخذ الله من ولد وما كان معه من إله ﴾ {} يخفض صوته كالمستحيي عن أن يذكره بكل شيء لا يليق به.
