23:91.english: Al-Nakha'i, when he would pass by something like His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Allah has not taken any son, nor is there any god with Him' (Quran 23:91), would lower his voice like one who is ashamed to mention Him with anything that is not befitting for Him.
23:91.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

23:91.arabic: با سعيد قال قد أسقطت عنك مائة قال له فأحسن  يا أبا سعيد فقال قد وهبت لك مائة أخرى فقبض من حقه مائتي درهم  فقيل  له  يا  أبا سعيد هذا نصف الثمن فقال هكذا يكون الإحسان وإلا فلا وفي الخبر خذ حقك في  كفاف وعفاف واف أو غير واف يحاسبك الله حسابا  يسيرا  حديث  خذ  حقك  في  عفافالحديث أخرجه ابن ماجه من حديث أبي هريرة بإسناد  حسن  دون  قوله  يحاسبك  الله  حسابا يسيرا وله ولابن حبان والحاكم وصححه نحوه من حديث ابن  عمر  وعائشة  الرابع  في توفية الدين ومن الإحسان فيه حسن القضاء وذلك  بأن  يمشي  إلى  صاحب  ا
23:91.english: O Sa'id said: I have dropped one hundred from you. He said to him: So do good (أحسن), O Abu Sa'id. So he said: I have gifted you another one hundred. So he took from his right two hundred dirhams. It was said to him: O Abu Sa'id, this is half the price. So he said: Thus is goodness (الإحسان), otherwise not. And in the report: Take your right in sufficiency (كفاف) and chastity (عفاف), sufficient or insufficient, Allah will account you an easy account. Hadith: Take your right in chastity. The hadith was reported by Ibn Majah from the hadith of Abu Hurairah with a good chain without his saying: Allah will account you an easy account. And he and Ibn Hibban and Al-Hakim and he authenticated something similar from the hadith of Ibn Umar and Aishah. The fourth in fulfilling debt and from goodness (الإحسان) in it is good repayment, and that is by walking to the possessor of the right and not burdening him to walk to him to demand it, for the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: The best of you are the best of you in repayment. Hadith: The best of you are the best of you in repayment is agreed upon from the hadith of Abu Hurairah. And whenever one is able to repay the debt, let him hasten to it even before its time, and let him give better than what was stipulated upon him and do good (أحسن), and if unable, then let him intend its repayment whenever able. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: Whoever incurs a debt while intending to repay it, Allah assigns to him angels who protect him and pray for him until he repays it. Hadith: Whoever incurs a debt while intending to repay it, Allah assigns to him angels who protect him and pray for him until he repays it was reported by Ahmad from the hadith of Aishah. There is no servant who had an intention (نية) in paying his debt except that there was with him from Allah help and protector. And in a narration of his: There did not cease to be with him from Allah a guard. And in a narration of Al-Tabarani in Al-Awsat: Except that there was with him help from Allah upon him until he repays it from him. And a group of the predecessors used to borrow without need for this report. And whenever the possessor of the right speaks to him with harsh speech, let him bear it and meet it with gentleness, following the example of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) when the possessor of the debt came to him at the due time and it had not been agreed to repay it, so the man intensified the speech against the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), so his companions became angry with him, so he said: Leave him, for the possessor of the right has a saying. Hadith: Leave him, for the possessor of the right has a saying is agreed upon from the hadith of Abu Hurairah. And whenever the speech revolves between the borrower and the lender, the goodness (الإحسان) is that the greater inclination for the mediators be to the one upon whom is the debt, for the lender lends from sufficiency (غنى) and the borrower borrows from need. And likewise, the assistance should be more for the buyer, for the seller is desirous of the commodity seeking to market it, and the buyer is in need of it. This is the best (الأحسن) except that the one upon whom is the debt exceeds his limit, so at that time, his assistance is in preventing him from transgression with it and assisting his companion, for the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: Help your brother, whether he is an oppressor or oppressed. So it was said: How do we help him as an oppressor? So he said: Your preventing him from oppression is help for him. Hadith: Help your brother, whether he is an oppressor or oppressed.
23:91.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Earning'

23:96.arabic: ومنها أنه إذا بلى بذي شر فينبغي أن يتحمله ويتقيه قال بعضهم خالص المؤمن مخالصة وخالق الفاجر مخالفة فإن الفاجر يرضى بالخلق الحسن في الظاهر وقال أبو الدرداء إنا لنبش في وجوه أقوام وإن قلوبنا لتلعنهم وهذا معنى المداراة وهي مع من يخاف شره قال الله تعالى ادفع بالتي هي أحسن السيئة قال ابن عباس في معنى قوله ويدرءون بالحسنة السيئة أي الفحش والأذى بالسلام والمداراة وقال في قوله تعالى ولولا دفع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض قال بالرغبة والرهبة والحياء والمداراة
23:96.english: And among them is that when afflicted with one possessing evil, it is necessary to bear it and be cautious of him. Some said: The sincere believer is sincere companionship, and the creator of the wicked is opposition, for the wicked is pleased with good character outwardly. And Abu al-Darda said: We indeed smile in the faces of some people while our hearts curse them. And this is the meaning of tactful dealing (Mudara'ah), and it is with whom one fears his evil. Allah the Exalted said: 'Repel with that which is better the evil.' Ibn Abbas said regarding the meaning of His saying 'And they repel with good the evil' meaning obscenity and harm with peace and tactful dealing. And he said regarding His saying 'And were it not for Allah repelling people, some by means of others' said: by desire and fear, shame and tactful dealing.
23:96.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

23:97.arabic: العاشرة: قوله أعوذ بالله السميع العليم من الشيطان الرجيم رب أعوذ بك من همزات الشياطين وأعوذ بك رب أن يحضرون[23]. فهذه العشر كلمات إذا كرر كل واحدة عشر مرات حصل له مائة مرة فهو أفضل من أن يكرر ذكرا واحدا مائة مرة لأن لكل واحدة من هؤلاء الكلمات فضلا على حياله وللقلب بكل واحد نوع تنبه وتلذذ وللنفس في الانتقال من كلمة إلى كلمة نوع استراحة وأمن من الملل
23:97.english: The tenth: His saying: 'I seek refuge with Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. My Lord, I seek refuge with You from the whisperings of the devils, and I seek refuge with You, my Lord, lest they be present with me' [23]. So these ten words, if each one is repeated ten times, it results in one hundred times for him, and it is better than repeating a single remembrance (Dhikr) one hundred times because each one of these words has merit on its own, and for the Heart (Qalb) with each one there is a kind of alertness and delight, and for the Soul (Nafs) in transitioning from one word to another there is a kind of rest and security from boredom.
23:97.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

23:97.arabic: الثامن أن يقول في مبتدأ قراءته: أعوذ بالله السميع العليم من الشيطان الرجيم ﴿ رب أعوذ بك من همزات الشياطين وأعوذ بك رب أن يحضرون ﴾ {} وليقرأ قل أعوذ برب الناس وسورة الحمد لله وليقل عند فراغه من القراءة صدق الله تعالى وبلغ رسول الله ﭬ اللهم انفعنا به وبارك لنا فيه الحمد لله رب العالمين وأستغفر الله الحي القيوم.
23:97.english: The eighth [practice] is that he should say at the beginning of his recitation: 'I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan (Shaytan).' 'My Lord (Rabb), I seek refuge in You from the whisperings (Hamazat) of the devils (Shayatin), and I seek refuge in You, my Lord, lest they be present with me.' And let him recite 'Say: I seek refuge in the Lord (Rabb) of mankind' and the Chapter of Praise (Surah Al-Fatihah) for Allah. And let him say upon completion of his recitation: 'Allah the Exalted has spoken the truth, and His Messenger has conveyed it. O Allah, benefit us by it and bless us in it. All praise is due to Allah, the Lord (Rabb) of the worlds, and I seek forgiveness from Allah, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining.'
23:97.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

23:97.arabic: [23]  حديث تكرار أعوذ بالله السميع العليم من الشيطان الرجيم أعوذ بالله من همزات الشياطين وأعوذ بك رب أن يحضرون أخرجه الترمذي من حديث معقل بن يسار من قال حين يصبح ثلاث مرات أعوذ بالله السميع العليم من الشيطان الرجيم وقرأ ثلاث آيات من آخر سورة الحشر وكل الله به سبعين ألف ملك الحديث ومن قالها حين يمسي كان بتلك المنزلة وقال حسن غريب ولابن أبي الدنيا من حديث أنس مثل حديث مقطوع قبله من قالها حين يصبح عشر مرات أجير من الشيطان إلى الصبح الحديث ولأبي الشيخ في الثواب من حديث عائشة ألا أعلمك يا خالد كلمات
23:97.english: Hadith on repeating: 'I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. I seek refuge in Allah from the whisperings (hamazat) of the devils (shayatin), and I seek refuge in You, my Lord, lest they be present.' It was reported by Al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Ma'qil ibn Yasar: Whoever says when he wakes up three times: 'I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan,' and recites three verses from the end of Surah Al-Hashr, Allah will assign to him seventy thousand angels. The hadith: And whoever says it when he sleeps will be in that station. And he said: Hasan gharib. And for Ibn Abi Al-Dunya from the hadith of Anas: Like the hadith, disconnected before it: Whoever says it when he wakes up ten times will be protected from Satan until dawn. The hadith: And for Abu Al-Sheikh in Al-Thawab from the hadith of Aisha: 'Shall I not teach you, O Khalid, words that you say three times? Say: I seek refuge in the perfect words (kalimat) of Allah from His anger and His punishment and the evil of His servants and from the whisperings (hamazat) of the devils (shayatin) and lest they be present.' And the hadith is with Abu Dawud and Al-Tirmidhi, and he graded it hasan, and Al-Hakim authenticated it in what is said during fright without repeating it three times from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr.
23:97.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Book of Knowledge'

23:97.arabic: ثم عند الفراغ من السواك يجلس للوضوء مستقبل القبلة ويقول بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم قال ﭬ: (لا وضوء لمن لم يسم الله تعالى[27]) أي لا وضوء كامل ويقول عند ذلك أعوذ بك من همزات الشياطين وأعوذ بك رب أن يحضرون ثم يغسل يديه ثلاثا قبل أن يدخلهما الإناء ويقول اللهم إني أسألك اليمن والبركة وأعوذ بك من الشؤم والهلكة
23:97.english: Then upon finishing the siwak (tooth-cleaning stick), he sits for the wudu (ritual ablution) facing the qiblah (direction of prayer) and says: 'In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.' The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no wudu for one who does not mention the name of Allah the Exalted'—meaning no complete wudu—and he says at that time: 'I seek refuge in You from the whisperings of the devils (hamazat al-shayatin), and I seek refuge in You, my Lord, that they should be present.' Then he washes his hands three times before putting them into the vessel and says: 'O Allah, I ask You for goodness and blessing, and I seek refuge in You from misfortune and destruction.'
23:97.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Mysteries of Purity'

23:99.arabic: وكان الربيع بين خيثم قد حفر في داره قبرا فكان إذا وجد في قلبه قساوة دخل فيه فاضطجع فيه ومكث ساعة ثم قال رب ارجعون لعلي أعمل صالحا فيما تركت ثم يقول يا ربيع قد أرجعت فاعمل الآن قبل أن لا ترجع
23:99.english: And Rabi' bin Khaytham had dug a grave in his house, so when he found hardness in his heart (Qalb), he would enter it and lie down in it and remain for an hour, then he would say: 'My Lord (Rabb), return me, so that I may do righteous deeds in what I have left.' Then he would say: 'O Rabi', you have been returned, so act now before you are not returned.'
23:99.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

23:99.arabic: وعن محمد بن كعب القرظي أنه كان يقرأ قوله تعالى: ﴿ حتى إذا جاء أحدهم الموت قال ربي ارجعون لعلي أعمل صالحا فيما تركت ﴾ {} قال أي شيء تريد في أي شيء ترغب أتريد أن ترجع لتجمع المال وتغرس الغراس وتبني البنيان وتشق الأنهار قال لا لعلي أعمل صالحا فيما تركت قال فيقول الجبار: ﴿ كلا أنها كلمة هو قائلها ﴾ {} أي ليقولنها عند الموت.
23:99.english: And from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, he used to recite the saying of The Exalted: 'Until when death comes to one of them, he says: "My Lord, send me back, that I might do righteousness in what I left behind."' {} He said: "What do you want? In what do you desire? Do you want to return to gather wealth, plant plantations, build buildings, and dig rivers?" He said: "No, that I might do righteousness in what I left behind." He said: Then The Compeller (al-Jabbar) says: 'No! Indeed, it is a word he is saying.' {} Meaning: He will certainly say it at death.
23:99.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

23:100.arabic: وكان الربيع بن خيثم قد حفر في داره قبرا فكان إذا وجد في قلبه قساوة دخل فيه فاضطجع ومكث ما شاء الله ثم يقول: ﴿ رب إرجعون لعلي أعمل صالحا فيما تركت ﴾ يرددها ثم يرد على نفسه يا ربيع قد رجعتك فاعمل
23:100.english: And Rabi' ibn Khaytham had dug a grave in his house, so when he found hardness in his heart (Qalb), he would enter it and lie down, and remain for as long as Allah willed, then he would say: 'My Lord, send me back, so that I may do righteous deeds in what I have left behind' (Quran 23:100), repeating it, then he would respond to himself: 'O Rabi', I have sent you back, so work.'
23:100.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

23:100.arabic: وكان ابن عباس يقول: من مات ولم يزك ولم يحج سأل الرجعة إلى الدنيا وقرأ قوله عز وجل: ﴿ رب ارجعون لعلي أعمل صالحا فيما تركت ﴾ {} قال: الحج.
23:100.english: And Ibn Abbas used to say: Whoever dies without paying Zakat (obligatory alms) and without performing Hajj (pilgrimage) will ask to return to the Worldly Life (Dunya) and he recited the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: 'My Lord, return me, that I might do righteousness (Sālih) in what I left behind' (Quran 23:100). He said: Hajj.
23:100.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

23:100.arabic: وعن محمد بن كعب القرظي أنه كان يقرأ قوله تعالى: ﴿ حتى إذا جاء أحدهم الموت قال ربي ارجعون لعلي أعمل صالحا فيما تركت ﴾ {} قال أي شيء تريد في أي شيء ترغب أتريد أن ترجع لتجمع المال وتغرس الغراس وتبني البنيان وتشق الأنهار قال لا لعلي أعمل صالحا فيما تركت قال فيقول الجبار: ﴿ كلا أنها كلمة هو قائلها ﴾ {} أي ليقولنها عند الموت.
23:100.english: And from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, he used to recite the saying of the Exalted: 'Until when death comes to one of them, he says: My Lord, send me back, that I may do righteousness (Sāliḥ) in what I left behind.' {} He said: What do you want? In what do you desire? Do you want to return to gather wealth, plant plantations, build buildings, and dig rivers? He said: No, that I may do righteousness (Sāliḥ) in what I left behind. He said: Then the Almighty (al-Jabbār) says: 'No! It is but a word he is saying.' {} Meaning: He will surely say it at the time of death.
23:100.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

23:100.arabic: هيهات هيهات "كلا إنها كلمة هو قائلها ومن ورائهم برزخ إلى يوم يبعثون" فكأن قد صرتم إلى ما صاروا إليه من البلاء والوحدة في دار المثوى وارتهنتم في ذلك المضجع وضمكم ذلك المستودع.
23:100.english: Far, far [is it] "No! Indeed, it is a word he is saying, and behind them is a barrier (Barzakh) until the Day they are resurrected." So it is as if you have already reached what they have reached of affliction and solitude in the abode of the final resting place (Dar al-Mathwa), and you have been held as security in that resting place, and that repository has encompassed you.
23:100.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of the World'

23:102.arabic: الأصل الرابع: الميزان وهو حق قال الله تعالى: ﴿ ونضع الموازين القسط ليوم القيامة ﴾ { سورة الأنبيآء: 47 } وقال تعالى: ﴿ فمن ثقلت موازينه فأولئك هم المفلحون. ومن خفت موازينه ﴾ { سورة المؤمنون:102، 103 } ووجهها أن الله تعالى يحدث في صحائف الأعمال وزنا بحسب درجات الأعمال عند الله تعالى فتصير مقادير أعمال العباد معلومة للعباد حتى يظهر لهم العدل في العقاب أو الفضل في العفو وتضعيف الثواب.
23:102.english: The Fourth Foundation: The Balance (Mizan) is true. Allah the Exalted said: 'And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection' (Surah Al-Anbiya: 47). And He said: 'So whoever's scales are heavy - those are the successful ones. And whoever's scales are light' (Surah Al-Mu'minun: 102, 103). And its meaning is that Allah the Exalted creates in the records of deeds a weight according to the degrees of deeds with Allah the Exalted, so the measures of the deeds of the servants become known to the servants until justice in punishment or favor in pardon and multiplication of reward becomes apparent to them.
23:102.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

23:106.arabic: ثم يقولون ﴿ ربنا أخرجنا نعمل صالحا غير الذى كنا نعمل به فيجيبهم الله تعالى أو لم نعمركم ما يتذكر فيه من تذكر وجاءكم النذير فذوقوا فما للظالمين من نصير ثم يقولون ربنا غلبت علينا شقوتنا وكنا قوما ضالين ربنا أخرجنا منها فإن عدنا فإنا ظالمون فيجيبهم الله تعالى اخسئوا فيها ولا تكلمون فلا يتكلمون بعدها أبدا وذلك غاية شدة العذاب.
23:106.english: Then they say, 'Our Lord, take us out so we may do righteous deeds other than what we used to do.' So Allah the Exalted answers them, 'Did We not grant you a lifespan in which one who remembers could remember, and the warner came to you? So taste, for the wrongdoers have no helper.' Then they say, 'Our Lord, our wretchedness (Shiqwah) overcame us, and we were a people astray (Dallin). Our Lord, take us out of it; if we return, then indeed we are wrongdoers.' So Allah the Exalted answers them, 'Be driven away into it, and do not speak.' So they do not speak after that ever, and that is the utmost severity of punishment.
23:106.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Book of Repentance'

23:106.arabic: فيقولون ادعوا ربكم فلا أحد خير من ربكم فيقولون ربنا غلبت علينا شقوتنا وكنا قوما ضالين ربنا أخرجنا منها فإن عدنا فإنا ظالمون قال فيجيبهم اخسئوا فيها ولا تكلمون
23:106.english: They say: 'Call upon your Lord, for there is none better than your Lord.' So they say: 'Our Lord, our wretchedness (Shiqwah) has overcome us, and we were a people astray (Dallin). Our Lord, bring us out of it; if we return [to evil], then indeed we are wrongdoers.' He says: He answers them: 'Remain despised therein and do not speak to Me.'
23:106.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Book of Repentance'

23:108.arabic: ثم حرمتهم السعادة أبد الآباد. فهم على فراقها يتحسرون ومن مكايدها يستغيثون ولا يغاثون. بل يقال لهم "اخسئوا فيها ولا تكلمون. أولئك الذين اشتروا الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة فلا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينصرون".
23:108.english: Then it deprived them of happiness for all eternity. They are in regret over its separation and from its plots they cry for help but are not helped. Rather, it is said to them: "Be driven away therein and do not speak to Me. Those are the ones who purchased the worldly life (al-Dunya) in exchange for the Hereafter (al-Akhirah), so the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be aided."
23:108.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of the World'

23:108.arabic: وعند ذلك تختطفك النيران والعياذ بالله وينادى المنادى اخسئوا فيها ولا تكلمون فلا يبقى سبيل إلا الصياح والأنين والتنفس والاستغاثة فكيف ترى الآن عقلك وهذه الأخطار بين يديك
23:108.english: And at that moment, the Fires (An-Niran) snatch you—seeking refuge with Allah—and the Caller (Al-Munadi) calls out: 'Be driven away therein and do not speak to Me.' So there remains no way except screaming, groaning, breathing, and calling for help. So how do you see now your intellect (Aql) and these dangers before you?
23:108.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Book of Repentance'

23:108.arabic: فيقولون ادعوا ربكم فلا أحد خير من ربكم فيقولون ربنا غلبت علينا شقوتنا وكنا قوما ضالين ربنا أخرجنا منها فإن عدنا فإنا ظالمون قال فيجيبهم اخسئوا فيها ولا تكلمون قال فعند ذلك يئسوا من كل خير وعند ذلك أخذوا فى الزفير والحسرة والويل
23:108.english: They say: 'Call upon your Lord, for there is none better than your Lord.' They say: 'Our Lord, our wretchedness has overcome us, and we were a people astray. Our Lord, bring us out of it; if we return [to evil], then indeed we are wrongdoers.' He responds to them: 'Remain despised in it and do not speak to Me.' At that point, they despair of all good, and at that point they begin sighing, regret, and woe.
23:108.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Book of Repentance'

23:108.arabic: ينادون من أكنافها ويصيحون فى نواحيها وأطرافها: يا مالك قد حق علينا الوعيد يا مالك قد أثقلنا الحديد يا مالك قد نضجت منا الجلود يا مالك أخرجنا منها فإنا لا نعود فتقول الزبانية هيهات لات حين أمان ولا خروج لكم من دار الهوان فاخسئوا فيها ولا تكلمون ولو أخرجتم منها لكنتم إلى ما نهيتم عنه تعودون فعند ذلك يقنطون وعلى ما فرطوا فى جنب الله يتأسفون ولا ينجيهم الندم ولا يغنيهم الأسف
23:108.english: They call from its corners and cry out in its regions and edges: 'O Malik, the threat has come true upon us; O Malik, the iron has weighed heavily upon us; O Malik, our skins have been cooked; O Malik, take us out from it, for we will not return.' Then the guardians say: 'Far be it! This is not the time for hope, nor is there any exit for you from the abode of humiliation. So be driven away (ikhsa'u) in it and do not speak. And if you were taken out from it, you would return to what you were forbidden from.' At that, they despair and over what they neglected in the side of Allah (fi janbi Allah) they regret, and regret does not save them, nor does sorrow benefit them.
23:108.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Book of Repentance'

23:108.arabic: فيقولون ﴿ ربنا غلبت علينا شقوتنا وكنا قوما ضالين ربنا أخرجنا منها فإن عدنا فإنا ظالمون فيجيبهم الله تعالى اخسئوا فيها ولا تكلمون فلا يتكلمون بعدها أبدا وذلك غاية شدة العذاب.
23:108.english: They say: 'Our Lord, our misfortune has overcome us, and we were a people astray. Our Lord, bring us out of it; then if we return, indeed we are wrongdoers.' Then Allah the Exalted answers them: 'Be driven away therein and do not speak to Me.' So they do not speak after that ever, and that is the utmost severity of punishment.
23:108.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Book of Repentance'

23:109.arabic: والاستغفار على الأسماء التي في القرآن أحب كقوله استغفر الله إنه كان غفارا أستغفر الله إنه كان توابا رب اغفر وارحم وأنت خير الراحمين فاغفر لنا وارحمنا وأنت خير الراحمين فاغفر لنا وارحمنا وأنت خير الغافرين ويستحب أن يقرأ قبل غروب الشمس: والشمس وضحاها. والليل إذا يغشى. والمعوذتين. ولتغرب الشمس عليه وهو في الاستغفار فإذا سمع الأذان قال اللهم هذا إقبال ليلك وإدبار نهارك وأصوات دعاتك كما سبق ثم يجيب المؤذن ويشتغل بصلاة المغرب وبالغروب قد انتهت أوراد النهار فينبغي أن يلاحظ العبد أحواله ويحاسب نفسه فقد
23:109.english: And seeking forgiveness (Istighfar) upon the names that are in the Quran is more beloved, such as saying: 'I seek forgiveness from Allah, indeed He is the Oft-Forgiving (Ghaffar),' 'I seek forgiveness from Allah, indeed He is the Accepter of Repentance (Tawwab),' 'Our Lord, forgive and have mercy, and You are the best of the merciful ones, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the best of the merciful ones, forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the best of the forgivers.' And it is recommended to recite before sunset: 'By the sun and its brightness,' 'By the night when it covers,' and the two chapters of seeking refuge (Al-Mu'awwidhatayn). And let the sun set upon him while he is in seeking forgiveness (Istighfar). Then when he hears the call to prayer (Adhan), he says: 'O Allah, this is the approach of Your night and the departure of Your day and the voices of Your callers,' as previously mentioned. Then he responds to the caller to prayer (Mu'adhdhin) and occupies himself with the sunset prayer (Maghrib). And with sunset, the daily litanies (Awrad) have ended, so it is incumbent upon the servant (Abd) to observe his states (Ahwal) and hold his soul (Nafs) accountable, for a stage of his path (Tariq) has passed. If his day equals his yesterday, then he is deceived; and if it is worse, then he is blameworthy, for he (the Prophet) said: 'No blessing is upon me in a day in which I do not increase in goodness.' If he sees his soul (Nafs) abundant in goodness throughout his entire day, abstaining from hardship, that is glad tidings, so let him thank Allah Almighty for His enabling (Tawfiq) and His guiding him to his path (Tariq). And if it is otherwise, then the night follows the day, so let him resolve to make up for what preceded of his negligence, for good deeds (Hasanat) erase bad deeds (Sayyi'at). And let him thank Allah Almighty for the health of his body and the remaining portion of his lifespan, the length of his night, to occupy himself with making up for his shortcomings. And let him hold in his heart (Qalb) that the day of life has an end in which the sun of life sets, so after it there is no rising for it, and at that time the door of making up and excuse is closed, for life is only numbered days that inevitably pass, their entirety by the passing of their units.
23:109.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

23:113.arabic: واستعمل عمر بن عبد العزيز رجلا فقيل كان عاملا للحجاج فعزله فقال الرجل إنما عملت له شيء يسير فقال له عمر حسبك بصحبته يوما أو بعض يوم شؤما وشرا
23:113.english: And Umar bin Abdul Aziz appointed a man, and it was said he was an agent for Al-Hajjaj, so he dismissed him. The man said: 'I only worked for him a small thing.' So Umar said to him: 'It is enough for you that accompanying him for a day or part of a day is an omen and evil.'
23:113.topic: Al-Ghazali on the outer and inner dimensions of worship, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

23:116.arabic: فتعالى الله الملك الحق لا يسئل عما يفعل وهم يسئلون ولنقتصر على هذا القدر اليسير من ذكر عجائب القلب فإن استقصاءه لا يليق بعلم المعاملة وإنما ذكرنا منه ما يحتاج إليه لمعرفة أغوار علوم المعاملة وأسرارها لينتفع بها من لا يقنع بالظواهر ولا يجتزئ بالقشر عن اللباب بل يتشوق إلى معرفة دقائق حقائق الأسباب وفيما ذكرناه كفاية له ومقنع إن شاء الله تعالى والله ولي التوفيق تم كتاب عجائب القلب ولله الحمد والمنة ويتلوه كتاب رياضة النفس وتهذيب الأخلاق والحمد لله وحده وصلى الله على كل عبد مصطفى.
23:116.english: So Exalted is Allah, the True King (Al-Malik al-Haqq), He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned. And we will limit ourselves to this small amount of mention of the wonders of the Heart (Qalb), for its exhaustive treatment is not fitting for the science of Transaction (al-Mu'amalah). Rather, we have mentioned from it what is needed for knowing the depths of the sciences of Transaction (al-Mu'amalah) and their secrets, so that those who are not satisfied with the outward appearances and do not content themselves with the shell instead of the core (al-Lubab) may benefit from it, but rather yearn to know the subtleties of the realities of the causes. In what we have mentioned, there is sufficiency for him and satisfaction, if Allah wills. And Allah is the Guardian of Success. Completed is the Book of the Wonders of the Heart (Qalb), and to Allah is praise and favor. And following it is the Book of Disciplining the Soul (Nafs) and Refining the Character (al-Akhlaq). And praise be to Allah alone, and may Allah bless every chosen servant.
23:116.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

23:117.arabic: وقال ﭬ "يخرج من النار عنق له أذنان تسمعان وعينان تبصران ولسان ينطق يقول: وكلت بثلاثة: بكل جبار عنيد وبكل من دعا مع الله إلهاً آخر وبالمصورين"[7]
23:117.english: And He (the Prophet) said: "There emerges from the Fire a neck that has two ears that hear and two eyes that see and a tongue that speaks, saying: I have been entrusted with three: with every arrogant (jabbar) stubborn one and with everyone who calls upon with Allah another god (ilah) and with the image-makers."
23:117.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

23:118.arabic: والاستغفار على الأسماء التي في القرآن أحب كقوله استغفر الله إنه كان غفارا أستغفر الله إنه كان توابا رب اغفر وارحم وأنت خير الراحمين فاغفر لنا وارحمنا وأنت خير الراحمين فاغفر لنا وارحمنا وأنت خير الغافرين ويستحب أن يقرأ قبل غروب الشمس: والشمس وضحاها. والليل إذا يغشى. والمعوذتين. ولتغرب الشمس عليه وهو في الاستغفار فإذا سمع الأذان قال اللهم هذا إقبال ليلك وإدبار نهارك وأصوات دعاتك كما سبق ثم يجيب المؤذن ويشتغل بصلاة المغرب وبالغروب قد انتهت أوراد النهار
23:118.english: And seeking forgiveness (Istighfar) according to the names (Asma) that are in the Quran is more beloved, such as saying: 'I seek forgiveness from Allah (Astaghfirullah), indeed He is the Oft-Forgiving (Ghaffar). I seek forgiveness from Allah (Astaghfirullah), indeed He is the Accepter of Repentance (Tawwab). O my Lord (Rabb), forgive and have mercy, and You are the best of those who show mercy (Khayr al-Rahimeen). So forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the best of those who show mercy (Khayr al-Rahimeen). Forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the best of those who forgive (Khayr al-Ghafireen).' And it is recommended to recite before sunset: 'By the sun and its brightness (Wa al-Shamsi wa duhaha). And by the night when it covers (Wa al-Layli idha yaghsha).' And the two chapters of seeking refuge (al-Mu'awwidhatayn). And let the sun set upon him while he is in seeking forgiveness (Istighfar). Then when he hears the call to prayer (Adhan), he says: 'O Allah, this is the approach of Your night and the departure of Your day and the voices of Your callers,' as preceded. Then he responds to the caller to prayer (Mu'adhdhin) and occupies himself with the sunset prayer (Salat al-Maghrib). And with the sunset, the daily litanies (Awrad) of the day have ended.
23:118.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

24:2.arabic: ومن ضعف الغضب الخور والسكوت عند مشاهدة المنكرات وقد قال ﭬ "خير أمتي أحداؤها"[13] يعني في الدين وقال تعالى "ولا تأخذكم بهما رأفة في دين الله" بل من فقد الغضب عجز عن رياضة نفسه، إذ لا تتم الرياضة إلا بتسليط الغضب على الشهوة، حتى يغضب على نفسه عند الميل إلى الشهوات الخسيسة. ففقد الغضب مذموم، وإنما المحمود غضب ينتظر إشارة العقل والدين، فينبعث حيث تجب الحمية وينطفئ حيث يحسن الحلم، وحفظه على حد الاعتدال هو الاستقامة التي كلف الله بها عباده وهو الوسط الذي وصفه رسول الله ﭬ حيث قال "خير الأمور أوساطها"[1
24:2.english: And from the weakness of anger (Ghadab) is cowardice (Khur) and silence when witnessing reprehensible acts (Munkarat), and the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'The best of my community are those with anger (Ahda'uha),' meaning in religion. And Allah the Exalted said: 'And let not pity (Ra'fah) for them take hold of you in the religion of Allah.' Rather, whoever loses anger is incapable of disciplining (Riyadah) his Soul (Nafs), for discipline is not accomplished except by unleashing anger upon desire (Shahwah), so that he becomes angry with himself when inclining towards base desires. Thus, the loss of anger is blameworthy, and only the praiseworthy anger is that which awaits the signal of intellect (Aql) and religion (Din), so it arises where zeal (Hamiyyah) is required and extinguishes where forbearance (Hilm) is appropriate. Maintaining it at the limit of moderation (I'tidal) is the uprightness (Istiqamah) that Allah has obligated upon His servants, and it is the middle path (Wasat) that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) described when he said: 'The best of matters are their middle ones.' So whoever's anger leans towards feebleness until he feels from himself weakness of zeal (Ghayrah) and baseness of the Soul (Nafs) in enduring humiliation (Dhull) and oppression (Daym) in its improper place, then he should treat himself until his anger strengthens.
24:2.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

24:15.arabic: فإن قلت: فإن صح هذا فينبغي أن يكون للعالم أن يرى نفسه فوق العابد لقوله عليه السلام "فضل العالم على العابد كفضلي على أدني رجل من أصحابي"؟ فاعلم أن ذلك كان ممكناً لو علم العالم عاقبة أمره، وخاتمة الأمر مشكوك فيها، فيحتمل أن يموت بحيث يكون حاله عند الله أشد من حال الجاهل الفاسق لذنب واحد كان يحسبه هيناً وهو عند الله عظيم وقد مقته به، وإذا كان هذا ممكناً كان على نفسه خائفاً، فإذا كان كل واحد من العابد والعالم خائفاً على نفسه وقد كلف أمر نفسه لا أمر غيره، فينبغي أن يكون الغالب عليه في حق نفسه الخوف و
24:15.english: If you say: If this is valid, then it should be for the scholar to see himself above the worshipper due to his saying, peace be upon him, "The superiority of the scholar over the worshipper is like my superiority over the lowest man among my companions"? Then know that that would have been possible if the scholar knew the outcome of his affair, and the conclusion of the affair is doubtful, for it is possible that he dies in a state where his condition with Allah is more severe than the condition of the ignorant sinner due to a single sin that he considered insignificant (هيناً) while it is with Allah great (عظيم) and He has despised him for it, and if this is possible, he should be fearful for himself, so if each one of the worshipper and the scholar is fearful for himself and has been charged with the affair of himself, not the affair of another, then the predominant state for him regarding himself should be fear and regarding others hope, and that prevents him from arrogance in every situation.
24:15.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

24:15.arabic: فإن قلت: كيف أفرح وأرى جماعة ممن زادت معصيتهم على معصيتى ولم يصابوا بما اصبت به حتى الكفار. فاعلم أن الكافر قد خبىء له ما هو أكثر وإنما أمهل حتى يستكثر من الإثم ويطول عليه العقاب كما قال تعالى: ﴿ إنما نملى لهم ليزدادوا إثما ﴾ {} وأما المعاصى فمن أين تعلم أن في العالم من هو أعصى منه ورب خاطر بسوء أدب في حق الله تعالى وفي صفاته أعظم وأطم من شرب الخمر والزنا وسائر المعاصى بالجوارح ولذلك قال تعالى في مثله ﴿ وتحسبونه هينا وهو عند الله عظيم ﴾ {} فمن أين تعلم أن غيرك أعصى منك ثم لعله قد أخرت عقوبته إلى
24:15.english: If you say: How can I rejoice when I see a group whose disobedience has increased beyond my disobedience, and they have not been afflicted with what I have been afflicted with, even the disbelievers? Then know that for the disbeliever, what is greater has been stored away, and he is only given respite so that he may increase in sin and his punishment may be prolonged, as Allah the Exalted said: 'We only give them respite so that they may increase in sin' (Quran 3:178). As for the disobediences, from where do you know that in the world there is one who is more disobedient than him? And perhaps a thought of bad manners (sū' adab) in the right of Allah the Exalted and in His attributes is greater and more severe than drinking wine, fornication, and all other disobediences with the limbs. And for that reason, Allah the Exalted said regarding its like: 'And you consider it trivial, while it is, with Allah, immense' (Quran 24:15). From where do you know that others are more disobedient than you? Then perhaps his punishment has been delayed to the Hereafter, and your punishment has been hastened in this world, so why do you not thank Allah the Exalted for that? And this is the third aspect in thankfulness (shukr), which is that there is no punishment except that it can be imagined to be delayed to the Hereafter. And the afflictions of this world are consoled by other means that lighten the affliction, so its impact is lessened. But the affliction of the Hereafter endures, and if it does not endure, then there is no way to alleviate it by consolation, since the means of consolation are completely cut off in the Hereafter for the tormented. And whoever's punishment is hastened in this world is not punished a second time, as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, when a servant commits a sin and then is afflicted with hardship or tribulation in this world, Allah is more noble than to punish him a second time.'
24:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

24:15.arabic: ولما حضرت ابن المنكدر الوفاة بكى فقيل له ما يبكيك فقال والله ما أبكى لذنب أعلم أني أتيته ولكن أخاف أني أتيت شيئا حسبته هينا وهو عند الله عظيم
24:15.english: And when Ibn al-Munkadir's death approached, he wept. It was said to him: 'What makes you weep?' He said: 'By Allah, I do not weep for a sin I know I committed, but I fear that I committed something I considered insignificant (hīnan), and it is with Allah great ('aẓīm).'
24:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

24:21.arabic: ولهذا قال الله تعالى "ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته ما زكا منكم من أحد أبداً" وقال النبي ﷺ لأصحابه وهم خير الناس "ما منكم من أحد ينجيه عمله" قالوا: ولا أنت يا رسول الله؟ قال "ولا أنا إلا أن يتغمدني الله برحمته" ولقد كان أصحابه من بعده يتمنون أن يكونوا تراباً وتبناً وطيراً مع صفاء أعمالهم وقلوبهم، فكيف يكون لذي بصيرة أن يعجب بعمله أو يدل به ولا يخاف على نفسه؟
24:21.english: And for this reason, Allah the Exalted said: "And were it not for the favor (Fadl) of Allah upon you and His mercy (Rahmah), not one of you would ever have been purified (Zakka) forever." And the Prophet ﷺ said to his companions, and they are the best of people: "There is not one of you whom his work (Amal) will save." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even me, except that Allah envelops me with His mercy (Rahmah)." And indeed, his companions after him wished to be dust, straw, and birds with the purity (Safa') of their works (A'mal) and hearts (Qulub), so how can one with insight (Bassirah) be amazed (Ya'jab) by his work (Amal) or rely (Yadl) on it and not fear for his soul (Nafs)?
24:21.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

24:21.arabic: فأما الهداية فلا سبيل لأحد إلى طلب السعادة إلا بها لأن داعية الإنسان قد تكون مائلة إلى ما فيه صلاح آخرته ولكن إذا لم يعلم ما فيه صلاح آخرته حتى يظن الفساد صلاحا فمن أين ينفعه مجرد الإرادة فلا فائدة في الإرادة والقدرة والأسباب إلا بعد الهداية ولذلك قال تعالى: ﴿ ربنا الذى أعطى كل شىء خلقه ثم هدى ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ ولو لا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته ما زكى منكم أحد أبدا ولكن الله يزكى من يشاء ﴾ {} وقال ﭬ: (ما من أحد يدخل الجنة إلا برحمة الله تعالى أى بهدايته فقيل ولا أنت يا رسول الله؟ قال ولا أنا[77]). و
24:21.english: As for guidance (Hidayah), there is no way for anyone to seek happiness except through it, because the inclination of the human being may be leaning toward what contains the rectification (Salah) of his Hereafter, but if he does not know what contains the rectification of his Hereafter until he thinks corruption (Fasad) is rectification, then from where will mere will benefit him? So there is no benefit in will, capability, and causes except after guidance. And for that reason, Allah the Exalted said: 'Our Lord who gave everything its creation then guided' (Quran 20:50). And He said: 'And were it not for the favor (Fadl) of Allah upon you and His mercy (Rahmah), none of you would ever have been purified (Zakka), but Allah purifies whom He wills' (Quran 24:21). And He (the Prophet) said: 'No one enters Paradise except by the mercy of Allah the Exalted, meaning by His guidance.' It was said: 'Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Not even me.' And guidance has three stations: The first is knowledge of the path of good and evil, indicated by His saying: 'And We guided him to the two ways' (Quran 90:10). And Allah the Exalted has bestowed this upon all His servants, some of it through intellect (Aql) and some of it upon the tongue of the messengers. And for that reason, He said: 'And as for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance' (Quran 41:17). So the means of guidance are the Book, the messengers, and the insights (Basa'ir) of the intellects, and they are made available, and nothing prevents from them except envy (Hasad), arrogance (Kibr), love of the worldly life (Dunya), and the causes that blind the hearts (Qulub) even though they do not blind the sights. He said: 'For indeed, it is not the eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts which are within the breasts' (Quran 22:46). And among the blinding things are familiarity (Ilf) and habit (Adah) and the love of adhering to them, and from it is the expression by His saying: 'Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion' (Quran 43:22) the verse. And from arrogance and envy is the expression by His saying: 'And they said, "Why was this Quran not sent down upon a great man from one of the two cities?"' (Quran 43:31) and His saying: 'A man from among us, one, we should follow him?' (Quran 54:24). So these blinding things are what prevented guidance, and the second guidance is beyond this general guidance, and it is that which Allah the Exalted extends to the servant.
24:21.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

24:21.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
24:21.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'What is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)".'
24:21.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

24:22.arabic: ولما حلف أبو بكر رضي الله عنه أن لا ينفق على مسطح -وكان قريبه- لكونه تكلم في واقعة الإفك نزل قوله تعالى "ولا يأتل أولوا الفضل منكم" إلى قوله "ألا تحبون أن يغفر الله لكم" فقال أبو بكر: نعم نحب ذلك وعاد إلى الإنفاق عليه[63]. والأولى أن يبقى على ما كان عليه، فإن أمكنه أن يزيد في الإحسان مجاهدة للنفس وإرغاماً للشيطان فذلك مقام الصديقين وهو من فضائل أعمال المقربين.
24:22.english: And when Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) swore not to spend on Mistah - and he was his relative - because he spoke in the incident of the slander, the saying of Allah the Exalted descended: "And let not those of virtue among you and abundance swear not to give to the relatives and the poor and the emigrants in the path of Allah, and let them pardon and overlook. Do you not love that Allah should forgive you?" So Abu Bakr said: Yes, we love that, and he returned to spending on him[63]. And the best is that he remains upon what he was upon, and if it is possible for him to increase in the good treatment (Ihsan) by struggling against the Soul (Nafs) and humiliating the Satan, then that is the station of the Truthful Ones (Siddiqin) and it is from the virtues of the deeds of the Near Ones (Muqarrabin).
24:22.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

24:22.arabic: قال عبد الله ما أدبت فأحسنت الأدب ولا سترت الحرمة إنه ينبغي للإمام إذا انتهى إليه حد أن يقيمه وإن الله عفو يحب العفو ثم قرأ وليعفوا وليصفحوا ثم قال إني لأذكر أول رجل قطعه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أتى بسارق فقطعه فكأنما أسف وجهه فقالوا يا رسول الله كأنك كرهت قطعه فقال وما يمنعني لا تكونوا عونا للشياطين على أخيكم فقالوا ألا عفوت عنه فقال إنه ينبغي للسلطان إذا انتهى إليه حد أن يقيمه إن الله عفو يجب العفو وقرأ وليعفوا وليصفحوا ألا تحبون أن يغفر الله لكم والله غفور رحيم
24:22.english: Abdullah said: 'You have neither disciplined properly nor preserved the sanctity. Indeed, it is incumbent upon the Imam when a prescribed punishment (Hadd) reaches him to implement it, and Allah is Forgiving (Afuw) and loves forgiveness (Al-'Afw).' Then he recited: 'And let them pardon and overlook. Do you not love that Allah should forgive you? And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.' Then he said: 'I remember the first man whose hand the Prophet (peace be upon him) amputated - a thief was brought and he amputated his hand, and it was as if his face was saddened. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, it seems you disliked amputating him." He said: "What prevents me? Do not be helpers to the devils against your brother." They said: "Why did you not pardon him?" He said: "It is incumbent upon the ruler when a prescribed punishment (Hadd) reaches him to implement it. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving (Afuw) and loves forgiveness (Al-'Afw)." And he recited: "And let them pardon and overlook. Do you not love that Allah should forgive you? And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful."'
24:22.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

24:22.arabic: احتجوا بما روى معاذ بن جبل أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قال إن الشيطان ذئب الإنسان كذئب الغنم يأخذ القاصية والناحية والشاردة وإياكم والشعاب وعليكم بالعامة والجماعة والمساجد حديث معاذ بن جبل الشيطان ذئب الإنسان كذئب الغنم يأخذ القاصية أخرجه أحمد والطبراني ورجاله ثقات إلا أن فيه انقطاعا وهذا إنما أراد به من اعتزل قبل تمام الغلم وسيأتي بيان ذلك وأن ذلك ينهى عنه إلا لضرورة ذكر حجج المائلين إلى تفضيل العزلة احتجوا بقوله تعالى حكاية عن إبراهيم عليه السلام وأعتزلكم وما تدعون من دون الله وأدعو ربي الآية ثم قا
24:22.english: They argued with what was narrated from Mu'adh ibn Jabal that he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Satan is the wolf of the human being like the wolf of sheep, he takes the distant one, the isolated one, and the stray one. Beware of the mountain valleys, and adhere to the general public, the congregation, and the mosques.' The hadith of Mu'adh ibn Jabal: 'Satan is the wolf of the human being like the wolf of sheep, he takes the distant one' was reported by Ahmad and Al-Tabarani, and its narrators are trustworthy except that there is a break in its chain. This only refers to one who isolates himself before the completion of maturity, and the clarification of that will come, and that it is prohibited except out of necessity. Mention of the arguments of those inclined to prefer isolation: They argued with His saying, the Exalted, narrating from Ibrahim (peace be upon him): 'And I will withdraw from you and what you invoke besides Allah, and I will invoke my Lord...' Then Allah said: 'So when he withdrew from them and what they worshipped besides Allah, We bestowed upon him Ishaq and Ya'qub, and each We made a prophet.' Indicating that this was due to the blessing of isolation. And this is weak because mixing...
24:22.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Seclusion'

24:22.arabic: وإن كانت معصيته بالجناية على حقك أو حق من يتعلق بك وفيه نزل قوله تعالى ولا يأتل أولوا الفضل منكم و السعة إلى قوله تعالى ألا تحبون أن يغفر الله لكم إذ تكلم مسطح بن أثاثة في واقعة الإفك حديث كلام مسطح في الإفك وهجر أبي بكر له حتى نزلت ولا يأتل أولوا الفضل منكم الآية متفق عليه من حديث عائشة فحلف أبو بكر أن يقطع عنه رفقه وقد كان يواسيه بالمال فنزلت الآية مع عظم معصية مسطح وأية معصية تزيد على التعرض لحرم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وإطالة اللسان في مثل عائشة رضي الله عنها إلا أن الصديق رضي الله عنه
24:22.english: And if his sin was by transgressing against your right or the right of someone connected to you, and in this context was revealed the saying of Allah the Exalted: 'And let not those of virtue among you and affluence swear against giving to the relatives and the poor and the emigrants in the path of Allah, and let them pardon and overlook. Do you not love that Allah should forgive you?' (Quran 24:22) when Mistah ibn Uthatha spoke in the incident of the Slander (al-Ifk) - the narration of Mistah's speech in the Slander and Abu Bakr's boycotting of him until 'And let not those of virtue among you and affluence...' the verse was revealed, agreed upon from the narration of Aisha. So Abu Bakr swore to cut off his kindness (Rafq) to him, and he had been supporting him with wealth, and the verse was revealed despite the enormity of Mistah's sin. And what sin increases upon exposing the sanctity of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and extending the tongue against the likes of Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her)? Except that al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) was as if wronged in himself by that incident. And pardoning (al-'Afw) from one who wronged and doing good (al-Ihsan) to one who did evil are from the character traits (Akhlaq) of the Truthful Ones (al-Siddiqin).
24:22.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

24:22.arabic: وقوله وليعفوا وليصفحوا ألا تحبون أن يغفر الله لكم
24:22.english: And His saying: 'And let them pardon and overlook. Do you not love that Allah should forgive you?'
24:22.book_title: Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character
24:22.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character'

24:27.arabic: وقد أوردناها في كتاب آداب الصحبة وكذلك ما روي أن عمر رضي الله عنه تسلق دار رجل فرآه على حالة مكروهة فأنكر عليه فقال يا أمير المؤمنين إن كنت أنا قد عصيت الله من وجه واحد فأنت قد عصيته من ثلاثة أوجه فقال وما هي فقال قد قال تعالى ولا تجسسوا وقد تجسست وقال تعالى وأتوا البيوت من أبوابها وقد تسورت من السطح وقال لا تدخلوا بيوتا غير بيوتكم حتى تستأنسوا وتسلموا على أهلها وما سلمت فتركه عمر وشرط عليه التوبة ولذلك شاور عمر الصحابة رضي الله عنهم وهو على المنبر وسألهم عن الإمام إذا شاهد بنفسه منكرا فهل له إق
24:27.english: And we have mentioned it in the Book of the Etiquettes of Companionship, and likewise what was narrated that Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) climbed over the wall of a man's house and saw him in a reprehensible state, so he rebuked him. The man said: 'O Commander of the Believers, if I have disobeyed Allah in one aspect, you have disobeyed Him in three aspects.' He said: 'And what are they?' He said: 'Allah the Exalted has said: "And do not spy" (Quran 49:12), and you have spied. And He said: "And enter houses from their doors" (Quran 2:189), and you have climbed over from the roof. And He said: "O you who have believed, do not enter houses other than your houses until you ascertain familiarity and greet their people" (Quran 24:27), and you did not greet.' So Umar left him and stipulated repentance upon him. And for that reason, Umar consulted the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) while he was on the pulpit and asked them about the Imam if he witnesses a wrong with his own eyes, does he have the right to establish the prescribed punishment for it? Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) indicated that this is dependent upon two just witnesses, so one is not sufficient for it. And we have mentioned these reports in clarifying the right of the Muslim from the Book of the Etiquettes of Companionship, so we do not repeat them.
24:27.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

24:27.arabic: وروي أن عمر رضي الله عنه كان يعس بالمدينة من الليل فسمع صوت رجل في بيت يتغنى فتسور عليه فوجده عنده امرأة وعنده خمر فقال يا عدو الله أظننت أن الله يسترك وأنت على معصيته فقال وأنت يا أمير المؤمنين فلا تعجل فإن كنت قد عصيت الله واحدة فقد عصيت الله في ثلاثا قال الله تعالى ولا تجسسوا وقد تجسست وقال الله تعالى وليس البر بأن تأتوا البيوت من ظهورها وقد تسورت علي وقد قال الله تعالى لا تدخلوا بيوتا غير بيوتكم الآية وقد دخلت بيتي بغير إذن ولا سلام فقال عمر رضي الله عنه هل عندك من خير إن عفوت عنك قال نعم وا
24:27.english: And it was narrated that Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) was patrolling in Medina at night when he heard the voice of a man in a house singing, so he climbed over the wall to him and found him with a woman and with wine. He said: 'O enemy of Allah, did you think that Allah would conceal you while you are upon disobedience?' He replied: 'And you, O Commander of the Believers, do not hasten, for if I have disobeyed Allah in one matter, you have disobeyed Allah in three matters. Allah the Exalted said: 'And do not spy' (Quran 49:12), and you have spied. And Allah the Exalted said: 'And it is not righteousness that you come to houses from their backs' (Quran 2:189), and you have climbed over the wall to me. And Allah the Exalted said: 'Do not enter houses other than your houses until you seek permission and greet their people' (Quran 24:27), and you have entered my house without permission and without greeting.' Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'Do you have any good if I pardon you?' He said: 'Yes, by Allah, O Commander of the Believers, if you pardon me, I will never return to the like of it ever.' So he pardoned him and left, abandoning him.
24:27.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

24:27.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
24:27.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'What is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)".'
24:27.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

24:30.arabic: وقال تعالى "قل للمؤمنين يغضوا من أبصارهم" الآية وقال عليه السلام "لكل ابن آدم حظ من الزنا فالعينان تزنيان وزناهما النظر، واليدان تزنيان وزناهما البطش، والرجلان تزنيان وزناهما المشي، والفم يزني وزناه القبلة، والقلب يهم أو يتمنى ويصدق ذلك الفرج أو يكذبه"
24:30.english: And Allah the Exalted said: "Say to the believing men to lower their gaze" the verse. And he (the Prophet) peace be upon him said: "Every son of Adam has a share of adultery. The two eyes commit adultery and their adultery is looking, the two hands commit adultery and their adultery is striking, the two feet commit adultery and their adultery is walking, the mouth commits adultery and its adultery is kissing, and the heart (Qalb) desires or wishes and the private part either confirms that or denies it."
24:30.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Harms of the Tongue'

24:31.arabic: وتوبوا إلى الله جميعا أيها المؤمنون لعلكم تفلحون والتوبة نظر في الفعل بعد الفراغ منه بالندم عليه وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم إنى لاستغفر الله تعالى وأتوب إليه في اليوم مائة مرة حديث اني لأستغفر الله وأتوب إليه في اليوم مائة مره تقدم غير مرة
24:31.english: And repent to Allah all of you, O you who believe, so that you may succeed. And repentance (Tawbah) is looking at the action after finishing it with regret (Nadam) upon it. And he (peace be upon him) said: Indeed I seek forgiveness from Allah the Exalted and repent to Him one hundred times in a day. The hadith: Indeed I seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Him one hundred times in a day has preceded more than once.
24:31.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

24:32.arabic: والطلاق مباح وقد وعد الله الغنى في الفراق والنكاح جميعا فقال (وأنكحوا الأيامى منكم والصالحين من عبادكم وإمائكم إن يكونوا فقراء يغنهم الله من فضله) وقال سبحانه وتعالى (وإن يتفرقا يغن الله كلا من سعته).
24:32.english: And divorce is permissible, and Allah has promised wealth in both separation and marriage, for He said: 'And marry the unmarried among you and the righteous among your male slaves and your female slaves. If they should be poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty.' And He, the Exalted, said: 'And if they separate, Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance.'
24:32.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

24:35.arabic: وإلى المثال الذي ضربناه أشار كعب الأحبار حيث قال دخلت على عائشة رضي الله عنها فقلت الإنسان عيناه هاد وأذناه قمع ولسانه ترجمان ويداه جناحان ورجلاه بريد والقلب منه ملك[10] فإذا طاب الملك طابت جنوده فقالت هكذا سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول وقال علي رضي الله عنه في تمثيل القلوب إن لله تعالى في أرضه آنية وهي القلوب فأحبها إليه تعالى أرقها وأصفاها وأصلبها ثم فسره فقال أصلبها في الدين وأصفاها في اليقين وأرقها على الإخوان وهو إشارة إلى قوله تعالى أشداء على الكفار رحماء بينهم وقوله تعالى مثل نور
24:35.english: And to the example we have given, Ka'b al-Ahbar pointed where he said: I entered upon Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, and I said: The human being, his two eyes are guides, his two ears are restrainers, his tongue is an interpreter, his two hands are two wings, his two feet are messengers, and the Heart (Qalb) from him is a king. So if the king becomes pure, his soldiers become pure. She said: Thus I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say. And Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said in the similitude of the hearts: Indeed, for Allah the Exalted in His earth are vessels, and they are the hearts, so the most beloved of them to Allah the Exalted are the most tender, the purest, and the firmest. Then he explained it, saying: The firmest in the religion, the purest in certainty, and the tenderest towards the brothers. And it is an allusion to His saying, the Exalted: 'Severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves' and His saying, the Exalted: 'The example of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp.' Ubayy ibn Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him, said its meaning is: The example of the light of the believer and his heart. And His saying, the Exalted: 'Or [they are] like darknesses within an unfathomable sea' is the example of the heart of the hypocrite. And Zayd ibn Aslam said regarding His saying, the Exalted: 'In a preserved tablet' and it is the heart of the believer. And Sahl said: The similitude of the Heart (Qalb) and the Chest (Sadr) is like the Throne and the Footstool. These are the examples of the heart.
24:35.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

24:35.arabic: ولقد كان زيته الذي في مشكاة قلبه يكاد يضيء ولو لم تمسسه نار، فلما نفخ فيه العلم بحدته اشتعل زيته فأصبح نوراً على نور، فقال له العلم: اغتنم الآن هذه الفرصة وافتح بصرك لعلك تجد على النار هدى، ففتح بصره فانكشف له القلم الإلهي، فإذا هو كما وصفه العلم في التنزيه، ما هو من خشب ولا قصب، ولا له رأس ولا ذنب، وهو يكتب على الدوام في قلوب البشر كلهم أصناف العلوم؛ وكأن له في كل قلب رأساً ولا رأس له، فقضى منه العجب وقال: نعم الرفيق العلم، فجزاه الله تعالى عني خيراً، إذ الآن ظهر لي صدق أنبائه عن أوصاف القلم؛ ف
24:35.english: And indeed, his oil which was in the niche of his heart (Qalb) was almost illuminating even if fire had not touched it. Then when knowledge (Ilm) blew into it with its intensity, his oil ignited and became light upon light. So knowledge said to him: 'Seize now this opportunity and open your sight (Basar) so that perhaps you may find guidance upon the fire.' So he opened his sight and the divine pen (Qalam) was unveiled to him. And behold, it was as knowledge had described it in transcendence (Tanzih) - not from wood nor reed, nor does it have a head nor tail, and it writes perpetually in the hearts (Qulub) of all humans all kinds of knowledge (Ulum); and as if it has in every heart a head while having no head. So he finished from it in wonder and said: 'Excellent is the companion knowledge, so may Allah reward him on my behalf with goodness, for now the truth of his reports about the attributes of the pen has become clear to me; for I see it as a pen not like pens.' At this point, he bid farewell to knowledge and thanked it, and said: 'My stay with you and my seeking from you has been long, and I am determined to travel to the presence of the pen and ask it about its affair.' So he traveled to it and said to it: 'What is with you, O pen, that you perpetually inscribe in the hearts (Qulub) from the knowledge (Ulum) what sends the intentions (Iradat) to the persons of decree (Qadar) and diverts them to the decreed matters (Maqdurat)?' It said: 'Or have you forgotten what you saw in the world of dominion (Mulk) and testimony (Shahadah) and heard from the answer of the pen when you asked it and it referred you to the hand?' He said: 'I have not forgotten that.' It said: 'So my answer is like its answer.' He said: 'How, and you do not resemble it?' The pen said: 'Have you not heard that Allah created Adam upon His image?' He said: 'Yes.' It said: 'So ask about my affair the one who is cast.'
24:35.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

24:35.arabic: فالأكياس وأرباب البصائر قلوبهم "كمشكاة فيها مصباح المصباح في زجاجة الزجاجة كأنها كوكب دري يوقد من شجرة مباركة زيتونة لا شرقية ولا غربية يكاد زيتها يضيء ولو لم تمسسه نار نور على نور" والمغترون قلوبهم "كظلمات في بحر لجي يغشاه موج من فوقه سحاب ظلمات بعضها فوق بعض إذا أخرج يده لم يكد يراها ومن لم يجعل الله له نوراً فما له من نور" فالأكياس هم الذين أراد الله أن يهديهم فشرح صدورهم للإسلام والهدى، والمغترون هم الذين أراد الله أن يضلهم فجعل صدرهم ضيقاً حرجاً كأنما يصعد في السماء.
24:35.english: The intelligent ones and possessors of insight, their hearts (Qalb) are "like a niche containing a lamp, the lamp in a glass, the glass as if it were a brilliant star, lit from a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if untouched by fire. Light upon light." And the deluded ones, their hearts (Qalb) are "like layers of darkness in a deep sea covered by waves, upon which are waves, above which are clouds; layers of darkness, one upon another. When he puts out his hand, he can hardly see it. And he for whom Allah has not made light, for him there is no light." So the intelligent ones are those whom Allah intended to guide, so He expanded their chests for Islam and guidance, and the deluded ones are those whom Allah intended to mislead, so He made their chests tight and constricted as if they were climbing into the sky.
24:35.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

24:35.arabic: ومن ظن أن عقل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مثل عقل آحاد السوادية وأجلاف البوادي فهو أخس في نفسه من آحاد السوادية وكيف ينكر تفاوت الغريزة ولولاه لما اختلف الناس في فهم العلوم ولما انقسموا إلى بليد لا يفهم بالتفهيم إلا بعد تعب طويل من المعلم وإلى ذكي يفهم بأدنى رمز وإشارة وإلى كامل تنبعث من نفسه حقائق الأمور بدون التعليم كما قال تعالى يكاد زيتها يضيء ولو لم تمسسه نار نور على نور وذلك مثل الأنبياء عليهم السلام إذ يتضح لهم في بواطنهم أمور غامضة من غير تعلم وسماع ويعبر عن ذلك بالإلهام وعن مثله عبر النبي
24:35.english: And whoever thinks that the intellect (Aql) of the Prophet (peace be upon him) is like the intellect of common townspeople and ignorant desert dwellers, he is more base in himself than the common townspeople. How can one deny the disparity in innate disposition (Ghareezah)? Were it not for this, people would not differ in understanding sciences, nor would they divide into: a dull one who only understands after long exertion from the teacher, and an intelligent one who understands with the slightest hint and indication, and a perfect one from whom the truths of matters emanate without teaching, as Allah the Exalted said: 'Its oil would almost glow even if untouched by fire. Light upon light.' And that is like the Prophets (peace be upon them), for obscure matters become clear to them in their inner selves (Bawatin) without learning and hearing, and this is expressed as inspiration (Ilham). And of its like, the Prophet (peace be upon him) expressed where he said: 'Indeed, the Holy Spirit (Ruh al-Qudus) breathed into my heart (Rawi'): Love whom you love, for you will part from them; and live as you wish, for you will die; and act as you wish, for you will be recompensed for it.'
24:35.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

24:35.arabic: وامتلأت مشكاة بعضهم نورا مقتبسا من نور الله تعالى في السموات والأرض وكان زيتهم أولا صافيا يكاد يضىء ولو لم تمسسه نار فمسته نار فاشتعل نورا على نور فأشرقت أقطار الملكوت بين أيديهم بنور ربها فأدركوا الأمور كلها كما هى عليه فقيل لهم تأدبوا بآداب الله تعالى واسكنوا وإذا ذكر القدر فأمسكوا[54] فإن للحيطان آذانا وحواليكم ضعفاء الإبصار فسيروا بسير أضعفكم ولا تكشفوا حجاب الشمس لأبصار الخفافيش فيكون ذلك سبب هلاكهم فتخلقوا بأخلاق الله تعالى وانزلوا إلى سماء الدنيا من منتهى علوكم ليأنس بكم الضعفاء ويقتبسوا
24:35.english: And the niche (mishkāh) of some of them filled with light borrowed from the light of Allah the Exalted in the heavens and the earth. And their oil was at first pure, it would almost give light even if no fire touched it. Then fire touched it and it blazed light upon light, so the regions of the dominion (malakūt) shone before them with the light of their Lord, and they comprehended all matters as they truly are. Then it was said to them: Adorn yourselves with the manners (ādāb) of Allah the Exalted and be still, and when predestination (qadar) is mentioned, hold back, for walls have ears and around you are those weak in vision. So walk with the pace of your weakest, and do not unveil the veil of the sun for the eyes of bats, for that would be the cause of their destruction. So embody the character traits (akhlāq) of Allah the Exalted, and descend to the heaven of the world from the peak of your elevation, so that the weak may find comfort in you and borrow from the remnants of your lights shining from behind your veil, just as bats borrow from the remnants of the light of the sun and the stars in the darkness of night, so that they may live by it a life that their person and state can bear, even if they do not live by it the life of those who wander in the perfection of the sun's light.
24:35.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

24:36.arabic: الثالث أن يمنعه سوق الدنيا عن سوق الآخرة وأسواق الآخرة المساجد قال الله تعالى رجال لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله وإقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة وقال الله تعالى في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع ويذكر فيها اسمه فينبغي أن يجعل أول النهار إلى وقت دخول السوق لآخرته فيلازم المسجد ويواظب على الأوراد كان عمر رضي الله عنه يقول للتجار اجعلوا أول نهاركم لآخرتكم وما بعده لدنياكم وكان صالحو السلف يجعلون أول النهار وآخره للآخرة والوسط للتجارة ولم يكن يبيع الهريسة والرءوس بكرة إلا الصبيان وأهل الذمة لأنهم كانوا في ا
24:36.english: The third is that the market of the worldly life (Dunya) prevents him from the market of the Hereafter (Akhirah), and the markets of the Hereafter are the mosques. Allah the Exalted said: 'Men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah and the establishment of prayer and giving of zakah.' And Allah the Exalted said: 'In houses which Allah has ordered to be raised and in which His Name is remembered. He is glorified therein in the mornings and the evenings.' So it is necessary to make the beginning of the day until the time of entering the market for his Hereafter, so he should frequent the mosque and be consistent in the regular litanies (Awrad). Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say to the merchants: 'Make the beginning of your day for your Hereafter, and what comes after it for your worldly life.' And the righteous predecessors (Salaf) used to make the beginning of the day and its end for the Hereafter, and the middle for trade. And none would sell porridge and heads in the morning except the children and the protected people (Dhimmis) because they were in the mosques afterwards. And in the report: 'When the angels ascend with the record of the servant, and in it at the beginning of the day and at its end is the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah and good, Allah expiates for him what is between them of evil deeds.' A hadith: 'When the angels ascend with the record of the servant, and at the beginning of the day and its end is remembrance and good, Allah expiates what is between them of evil deeds.' Abu Ya'la narrated it from the hadith of Anas with a weak chain, with its meaning. And in the report: 'The angels of the night and the angels of the day meet at the rising of dawn and at the Asr prayer, and Allah the Exalted says, and He knows best about them: "How did you leave My servants?" They say: "We left them while they were praying, and we came to them while they were praying." Then Allah, glorified and exalted, says: "I bear witness to you that I have forgiven them."' A hadith: 'The angels of the night and the angels of the day meet at the rising of dawn and at the Asr prayer, and Allah says, and He knows best: "How did you leave My servants?"'
24:36.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Etiquette of Earning'

24:37.arabic: وبالجملة سبب هلاك الناس حرصهم على الدنيا، وسبب حرصهم على الدنيا البطن والفرج، وسبب شهوة الفرج، شهوة البطن. وفي تقليل الأكل ما يحسم هذه الأحوال كلها وهي أبواب النار وفي حسمها فتح أبواب الجنة كما قال ﭬ "أديموا قرع باب الجنة بالجوع" فمن قنع برغيف في كل يوم قنع في سائر الشهوات أيضاً وصار حراً واستغنى عن الناس واستراح من التعب، وتخلى لعبادة الله عز وجل وتجارة الآخرة، فيكون من الذين لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله وإنما لا تلهيهم لاستغنائهم عنها بالقناعة، وأما المحتاج فتلهيه لا محالة.
24:37.english: In summary, the cause of people's destruction is their greed for the worldly life (Dunya), and the cause of their greed for the worldly life (Dunya) is the stomach and the private parts, and the cause of the desire of the private parts is the desire of the stomach. And in reducing eating there is what cuts off all these conditions, and they are the gates of the Fire, and in cutting them off is the opening of the gates of Paradise, as he (the Prophet) said: 'Persist in knocking on the gate of Paradise with hunger.' So whoever is content with a loaf of bread each day becomes content in all other desires as well, and becomes free, and becomes independent of people, and rests from toil, and devotes himself to the worship of Allah the Exalted and the trade of the Hereafter, thus he will be among those whom trade and sale do not distract from the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah. And they are not distracted only because of their independence from it through contentment (Qana'a), whereas the needy one is inevitably distracted by it.
24:37.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Harms of the Tongue'

24:37.arabic: فإن كنت لا تشتاق إلى معرفة الله تعالى ولم تجد لذتها وفتر عنها رأيك وضعفت فيها رغبتك فأنت في ذلك معذور؛ إذ العنين لا يشتاق إلى لذة الوقاع، والصبي لا يشتاق إلى لذة الملك، فإن هذه لذات يختص بإدراكها الرجال دون الصبيان والمخنثين فكذلك لذة المعرفة يختص بإدراكها الرجل "رجال لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله" ولا يشتاق إلى هذه اللذة غيرهم، لأن الشوق بعد الذوق، ومن لم يذق لم يعرف، ومن لم يعرف لم يشتق، ومن لم يشتق لم يطلب، ومن لم يطلب لم يدرك، ومن لم يدرك بقي مع المحرومين في أسفل السافلين "ومن يعش عن ذ
24:37.english: If you do not yearn for the knowledge (ma'rifah) of Allah the Exalted and do not find its delight, and your opinion has become lax about it and your desire has weakened in it, then you are excused in that; for the impotent man does not yearn for the pleasure of intercourse, and the child does not yearn for the pleasure of kingship, for these are pleasures that are specifically perceived by men (rijāl) apart from children and effeminate men. Likewise, the pleasure of knowledge is specifically perceived by the man (rajul) "Men (rijāl) whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah" and none yearn for this pleasure except them, because yearning (shawq) comes after tasting (dhawq), and whoever has not tasted does not know, and whoever does not know does not yearn, and whoever does not yearn does not seek, and whoever does not seek does not attain, and whoever does not attain remains with the deprived ones in the lowest of the low "And whoever turns away from the Remembrance (Dhikr) of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil, and he is to him a companion."
24:37.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

24:37.arabic: الثالث أن يمنعه سوق الدنيا عن سوق الآخرة وأسواق الآخرة المساجد قال الله تعالى رجال لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله وإقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة وقال الله تعالى في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع ويذكر فيها اسمه فينبغي أن يجعل أول النهار إلى وقت دخول السوق لآخرته فيلازم المسجد ويواظب على الأوراد كان عمر رضي الله عنه يقول للتجار اجعلوا أول نهاركم لآخرتكم وما بعده لدنياكم وكان صالحو السلف يجعلون أول النهار وآخره للآخرة والوسط للتجارة ولم يكن يبيع الهريسة والرءوس بكرة إلا الصبيان وأهل الذمة لأنهم كانوا في ا
24:37.english: The third is that the market of this world (Dunya) should not prevent him from the market of the Hereafter (Akhirah), and the markets of the Hereafter are the mosques. Allah the Exalted said: 'Men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah and establishing the prayer (Salah) and giving the alms (Zakat).' And Allah the Exalted said: 'In houses which Allah has permitted to be raised and wherein His name is remembered.' Therefore, one should make the beginning of the day until the time of entering the market for his Hereafter, so he should frequent the mosque and be consistent in the litanies (Awrad). Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say to the merchants: 'Make the beginning of your day for your Hereafter, and what comes after it for your worldly life.' And the righteous predecessors (Salaf) used to make the beginning and end of the day for the Hereafter, and the middle for trade. And only the children and the protected non-Muslims (Ahl al-Dhimmah) used to sell porridge and heads in the morning, because they were in the mosques afterwards. And in the report: 'When the angels ascend with the record of the servant, and in it at the beginning of the day and at its end is the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah and good deeds, Allah forgives him for what is between them of evil deeds.' A hadith: 'When the angels ascend with the record of the servant, and at the beginning of the day and its end is remembrance and good deeds, Allah forgives what is between them of evil deeds.' Abu Ya'la narrated it from the hadith of Anas with a weak chain, with its meaning. And in the report: 'The angels of the night and the angels of the day meet at the rising of dawn and at the Asr prayer, and Allah the Exalted says, and He knows best about them: 'How did you leave My servants?' They say: 'We left them while they were praying, and we came to them while they were praying.' Then Allah, glorified and exalted, says: 'I bear witness to you that I have forgiven them.' A hadith: 'The angels of the night and the angels of the day meet at the rising of dawn and at the Asr prayer, and Allah says, and He knows best: 'How did you leave My servants?'
24:37.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Etiquette of Earning'

24:37.arabic: وقال أبو الدرداء: ما يسرني أنني أقمت على درج مسجد دمشق أصيب كل يوم خمسين ديناراً أتصدق بها، أما إني لا أحرم البيع والشراء ولكني أريد أن أكون من الذين لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله. وقد اختلفت العلماء فقال قوم: إذا طلب الدنيا من الحلال وسلم منها وتصدق بها فهو أفضل من أن يشتغل بالعبادات والنوافل، وقال قوم: الجلوس في دوام ذكر الله أفضل، والأخذ والإعطاء يشغل عن الله وقد قال المسيح عليه السلام: يا طالب الدنيا ليبر بها، تركك لها أبر؛ وقال. أقل ما فيه أن يشغله إصلاحه عن ذكر الله وذكر الله أكبر وأ
24:37.english: And Abu al-Darda' said: 'It would not please me that I sat on the steps of the Damascus mosque earning fifty dinars every day to give in charity, for indeed I do not forbid buying and selling, but I want to be among those whom trade and sale do not distract from the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah.' And the scholars differed: some said: 'If one seeks worldly matters from what is lawful, remains safe from them, and gives charity from them, that is better than being occupied with acts of worship and supererogatory prayers.' And others said: 'Sitting in continuous Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah is better, and taking and giving distracts from Allah.' And the Messiah, peace be upon him, said: 'O seeker of the world to be righteous through it, your abandoning it is more righteous.' And he said: 'The least of it is that it distracts him from rectifying the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah, and the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah is greater and better.' And this is for one who is safe from afflictions; as for one who is exposed to the affliction of showing off, abandoning it is more righteous, and being occupied with Remembrance (Dhikr) is indisputably better.
24:37.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

24:37.arabic: أو يخطر له من قوله تعالى للذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين تفضيل الذكر بكونه رجلا على الأنثى وأن الفضل في الآخرة لرجال لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله وأن من ألهاه غير الله تعالى عن الله تعالى فهو من الإناث لا من الرجال تحقيقا فيخشى أن يحجب أو يؤخر في نعيم الآخرة كما اخرت الانثى في أموال الدنيا
24:37.english: Or it occurs to him from His saying, exalted is He, 'For the male is the equivalent of the share of two females' [Quran 4:11] the preference of the male by him being a man over the female, and that the excellence in the Hereafter is for men whom neither commerce nor sale distracts from the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah [Quran 24:37], and that whoever is distracted by other than Allah, exalted is He, from Allah, exalted is He, then he is from the females, not from the men, in reality, so he fears that he may be veiled or delayed in the bliss of the Hereafter as the female was delayed in the wealth of this world.
24:37.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

24:38.arabic: واستثنى في خمسة اشياء في الاغناء والاجابة والرزق والمغفرة والتوبة فقال تعالى: ﴿ فسوف يغنيكم الله من فضله ان شاء ﴾ {} وقال فيكشف ما تدعون اليه ان شاء - وقال يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب وقال: ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء وقال: ويتوب الله على من يشاء وهو خلق من اخلاق الربوبية اذ قال تعالى: ﴿ والله شكور حليم ﴾ {}
24:38.english: And He made an exception in five things: in enrichment, in answering, in provision, in forgiveness, and in repentance. So He, the Exalted, said: 'Then Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills' (Quran 24:32). And He said: 'He will remove what you call to if He wills' - and He said: 'He provides for whom He wills without account' (Quran 24:38). And He said: 'And He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills' (Quran 4:48). And He said: 'And Allah turns in repentance (Tawbah) to whom He wills' (Quran 9:15). And it is a character from the characters of Lordship (Rububiyyah), since He, the Exalted, said: 'And Allah is Appreciative (Shakur), Forbearing (Halim)' (Quran 64:17).
24:38.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

24:40.arabic: فالمعاصى كلها ظلمات بعضها فوق بعض فيمنحق بعضها في جنب البعض فالسيد قد يعاقب عبده إذا استعمل سكينه بغير إذنه ولكن لو قتل بتلك السكين أعز أولاده لم يبق لاستعمال السكين بغير إذنه حكم ونكاية في نفسه فكل ما راعاه الأنبياء والأولياء من الآداب وتسامحنا فيه في الفقه مع العوام فسببه هذه الضرورة وإلا فكل هذه المكاره عدول عن العدل وكفران للنعمة ونقصان عن الدرجة المبلغة للعبد إلى درجات القرب، بعضها يؤثر في العبد بنقصان القرب وانحطاط المنزلة وبعضها يخرج بالكلية عن حدود القرب إلى عالم البعد الذى هو مستقر الشي
24:40.english: For all sins are darknesses (ظُلُمَاتٌ) some above others, where some are absorbed in the side of others. The master may punish his servant if he uses his knife without permission, but if he killed with that knife his most beloved child, there would remain no consideration for using the knife without permission and no harm to himself.
