Everything that the Prophets and the Friends (الأولياء) observed of manners (الآداب) and we have been lenient about in jurisprudence (الفقه) with the common people is due to this necessity; otherwise, all these disliked matters are deviations from justice (العدل) and ingratitude for the blessing (النعمة) and a deficiency from the degree that conveys the servant to degrees of proximity (القرب). Some of them affect the servant by diminishing proximity (القرب) and lowering status, and some of them completely remove him from the boundaries of proximity (القرب) to the world of distance (البعد) which is the abode of devils. Likewise, whoever breaks a branch from a tree without an urgent important need and without a valid purposeful need has shown ingratitude for the blessing (النعمة) of Allah the Exalted in creating trees and creating the hand. As for the hand, it was not created for frivolity but for obedience (الطاعة) and works that assist in obedience (الطاعة). As for the tree, Allah the Exalted created it and created roots for it and channeled water to it and created in it the power of nourishment and growth so that it reaches the peak of its flourishing for His servants to benefit from it. Breaking it before the peak of its flourishing in a way that does not benefit His servants is contrary to the purpose of wisdom (الحكمة) and a deviation from justice (العدل). If he has a valid purpose, then he may do so, since trees and animals are made as ransom for human purposes, for they are both perishable.
24:40.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

24:40.arabic: ومن ليس معه أصل معرفة الله تعالى لم يكن له مطمع في هذا النور، فيبقى كمن مثله في الظلمات ليس بخارج منها بل "كظلمات في بحر لجى يغشاه موج من فوقه موج من فوقه سحاب ظلمات بعضها فوق بعض" فإذن لا سعادة إلا في معرفة الله تعالى وأما ما عدا ذلك من المعارف فمنها ما لا فائدة له أصلاً كمعرفة الشعر وأنساب العرب وغيرهما، ومنها ما له منفعة في الإعانة على معرفة الله تعالى كمعرفة لغة العرب والتفسير والفقه والأخبار، فإن معرفة لغة العرب تعين على معرفة تفسير القرآن، ومعرفة التفسير تعين على معرفة ما في القرآن من كيفي
24:40.english: And whoever does not have the foundation of the knowledge of Allah the Exalted has no hope in this light, so he remains like one whose likeness is in the darknesses, not exiting from them, rather "like darknesses in a deep sea covered by a wave from above it a wave from above it a cloud, darknesses some of them above others." Therefore, there is no happiness except in the knowledge of Allah the Exalted. As for what is other than that from the knowledges, among them is what has no benefit at all, like the knowledge of poetry and the lineages of the Arabs and others, and among them is what has benefit in assisting towards the knowledge of Allah the Exalted, like the knowledge of the language of the Arabs, the interpretation (Tafsir), jurisprudence (Fiqh), and reports (Akhbar). For the knowledge of the language of the Arabs assists in knowing the interpretation of the Quran, and the knowledge of the interpretation assists in knowing what is in the Quran from the manner of the acts of worship and works that benefit the purification of the Soul (Tazkiyat al-Nafs), and the knowledge of the way of purifying the Soul (Tazkiyat al-Nafs) benefits the preparedness of the Soul (Nafs) for accepting the guidance to the knowledge of Allah, the Majestic and Exalted, as He the Exalted said: "Indeed successful is he who purifies it (Zakaha)" and He the Mighty and Majestic said: "And those who strive in Us, We will surely guide them to Our ways." So the totality of these knowledges is like the means to the realization of the knowledge of Allah the Exalted, and indeed the perfection is in the knowledge of Allah and the knowledge of His attributes and His actions, and it encompasses all the knowledges surrounding the existents since all the existents are from His actions. So whoever knows them from the aspect that they are the action of Allah the Exalted, and from the aspect of their connection to the Power (Qudrah), the Will (Iradah), and the Wisdom (Hikmah), then they are from the completion of the knowledge of Allah the Exalted. And this is the ruling of the perfection of knowledge we have mentioned, even if it is not suitable for the rulings of ignorance and ostentation, but we have presented it for the completion of the divisions of perfection.
24:40.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

24:40.arabic: فالأكياس وأرباب البصائر قلوبهم "كمشكاة فيها مصباح المصباح في زجاجة الزجاجة كأنها كوكب دري يوقد من شجرة مباركة زيتونة لا شرقية ولا غربية يكاد زيتها يضيء ولو لم تمسسه نار نور على نور" والمغترون قلوبهم "كظلمات في بحر لجي يغشاه موج من فوقه سحاب ظلمات بعضها فوق بعض إذا أخرج يده لم يكد يراها ومن لم يجعل الله له نوراً فما له من نور" فالأكياس هم الذين أراد الله أن يهديهم فشرح صدورهم للإسلام والهدى، والمغترون هم الذين أراد الله أن يضلهم فجعل صدرهم ضيقاً حرجاً كأنما يصعد في السماء.
24:40.english: The wise ones and possessors of insight, their hearts (Qalb) are "like a niche containing a lamp, the lamp in a glass, the glass as if it were a brilliant star, lit from a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if untouched by fire. Light upon light." And the deluded ones, their hearts (Qalb) are "like darknesses in a deep sea covered by a wave, above which is a cloud, darknesses, some above others. When he puts out his hand, he can hardly see it. And he for whom Allah has not made light, for him there is no light." So the wise ones are those whom Allah has willed to guide, so He expanded their chests for Islam and guidance, and the deluded ones are those whom Allah has willed to misguide, so He made their chests tight and constricted as if they were climbing into the sky.
24:40.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

24:40.arabic: وقوله تعالى مثل نوره كمشكاة فيها مصباح قال أبي بن كعب رضي الله عنه معناه مثل نور المؤمن وقلبه وقوله تعالى أو كظلمات في بحر لجي مثل قلب المنافق
24:40.english: And His saying, the Exalted: 'The example of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp' - Abu ibn Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him, said its meaning is: like the light of the believer and his heart (Qalb). And His saying, the Exalted: 'Or [they are] like darknesses within an unfathomable sea' - like the heart (Qalb) of the hypocrite.
24:40.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

24:41.arabic: لعرض على الجبار  وتفكر  أولا  فيما  يقرع سمع سكان القبور من شدة نفخ الصور فإنها صيحة واحدة تنفرج بها القبور  عن  رءوس الموتي فيثورون دفعة واحدة فتوهم نفسك وقد وثبت  متغيرا  وجهك  مغبرا  بدنك  من فرقك إلى قدمك من تراب قبرك مبهوتا من شدة الصعقة شاخص العين  نحو  النداء  وقد ثار الخلق ثورة واحدة من القبور التى طال فيها بلاؤهم وقد أزعجهم الفزع  والرعب مضافا إلى ما كان عندهم من الهموم والغموم وشدة الانتظار لعاقبة الأمر كما  قال تعالى: ﴿ ونفخ فى الصور فصعق من فى السموات ومن فى الأرض إلا من  شاء  الله
24:41.english: To present to the Almighty and contemplate first what strikes the hearing of the inhabitants of the graves from the intensity of the blowing of the Horn (As-Sur), for it is a single cry by which the graves split open from the heads of the dead, and they rise up all at once. So imagine yourself having leaped up with your face altered, your body dusty from your hair to your feet from the dust of your grave, stunned from the intensity of the shock, with your eyes fixed toward the call. And the creation has risen up in a single uprising from the graves in which their tribulation has been prolonged, and alarm and terror have disturbed them, added to what they had of sorrows, griefs, and intense waiting for the outcome of the matter, as the Exalted said: 'And the Horn (As-Sur) will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on.' And the Exalted said: 'And when the Trumpet (An-Naqur) is blown, that Day will be a difficult day for the disbelievers; not easy.' And the Exalted said: 'And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?" They do not await except one blast which will seize them while they are disputing. And they will not be able to make a testament, nor to their people can they return. And the Horn (As-Sur) will be blown; and at once from the graves to their Lord they will hasten. They will say, "O woe to us! Who has raised us up from our sleeping place?" [The reply will be], "This is what the Most Merciful had promised, and the messengers told the truth."' So if there were nothing before the dead except the terror of that blowing, that would be worthy of being feared, for it is a blowing and a cry by which whoever is in the heavens and the earth is struck dead, meaning they die by it except whom Allah wills, and that is some of the angels. And for that reason, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'How can I be at ease when the possessor of the Horn (As-Sur) has taken the horn into his mouth, lowered his forehead, and inclined his ear, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow?' Maqatil said: The Horn (As-Sur) is the trumpet (Al-Qarn), and that is because Israfil (upon him be peace) places his mouth on the horn like the shape of a trumpet, and the circumference of the head of the horn is like the width of the heavens and the earth, and he is fixing his gaze toward the Throne, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow the first blowing. And when he blows, whoever is in the heavens and the earth is struck dead, meaning every animal dies from the intensity of the alarm except whom Allah wills, and that is Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil, and the Angel of Death (Malak Al-Mawt). Then the Angel of Death (Malak Al-Mawt) is commanded to take the soul (Ruh) of Jibril, then the soul (Ruh) of Mika'il, then the soul (Ruh) of Israfil, then the Angel of Death (Malak Al-Mawt) is commanded and he dies. Then the creation remains after the first blowing in the Barzakh for forty years. Then Allah the Exalted revives Israfil and commands him to blow the second, and that is His saying: 'Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on.' On their feet, looking at the Resurrection. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'When I was sent, I was sent to the possessor of the Horn (As-Sur), and he gestured with it to his mouth and advanced one foot and delayed another, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow. So fear the blowing.' So contemplate the creation and their humiliation, their breaking, and their submission at the resurrection out of fear of this shock and waiting for it.
24:41.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

24:41.arabic: الغموم وشدة الانتظار لعاقبة الأمر كما قال تعالى: ﴿ ونفخ فى الصور فصعق من فى السموات ومن فى الأرض إلا من شاء الله ثم نفخ فيه أخرى فإذا هم قيام ينظرون ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ فإذا نقر فى الناقور فذلك يومئذ يوم عسير على الكافرين غير يسير ﴾ {} وقال تعال: ﴿ ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين ما ينظرون إلا صيحة واحدة تأخذهم وهم يخصمون فلا يستطيعون توصية ولا إلى أهلهم يرجعون ونفخ فى الصور فإذا هم من الأجداث إلى ربهم ينسلون قالوا يا ويلنا من بعثنا من مرقدنا هذا ما وعد الرحمن وصدق المرسلون ﴾ {} فلو لم يكن ب
24:41.english: The sorrows and intensity of waiting for the outcome of the matter, as He (Exalted is He) said: 'And the Horn is blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth falls dead except whom Allah wills. Then it is blown again, and at once they are standing, looking on.' {} And He (Exalted is He) said: 'And when the Trumpet is blown, that Day will be a difficult day for the disbelievers; not easy.' {} And He (Exalted is He) said: 'And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?" They do not await except one blast which will seize them while they are disputing. And they will not be able to make a testament, nor to their people will they return. And the Horn will be blown, and at once from the graves to their Lord they will hasten. They will say, "O woe to us! Who has raised us up from our sleeping place?" [It will be said], "This is what the Most Merciful had promised, and the messengers told the truth."' {} So if there were nothing before the dead except the terror of that blowing, it would be worthy of being feared, for it is a blowing and a cry by which whoever is in the heavens and the earth falls dead, meaning they die by it, except whom Allah wills, and that is some of the angels. And for that reason, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'How can one be at ease when the possessor of the Horn has taken the horn in his mouth, lowered his forehead, and listened with his ear, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow?' [144] Maqatil said: The Horn is the trumpet, and that is because Israfil (upon him be peace) places his mouth on the horn like a trumpet, and the circumference of the head of the horn is like the expanse of the heavens and the earth, and he is gazing with his sight toward the Throne, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow the first blowing. And when he blows, whoever is in the heavens and the earth falls dead, meaning every living creature dies from the intensity of the fright, except whom Allah wills, and that is Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil, and the Angel of Death. Then the Angel of Death is commanded to take the spirit (Ruh) of Jibril, then the spirit (Ruh) of Mika'il, then the spirit (Ruh) of Israfil, then the Angel of Death is commanded and he dies. Then the creation remains after the first blowing in the Barzakh (the intermediate state) for forty years. Then Allah (Exalted is He) revives Israfil and commands him to blow the second, and that is His (Exalted is He) saying: 'Then it is blown again, and at once they are standing, looking on.' {} On their feet, looking at the Resurrection. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'When I was sent, I was sent to the possessor of the Horn, and he inclined it to his mouth, and put forward one leg and delayed another, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow. Indeed, fear the blowing!' [145] So reflect on the creatures and their humiliation, their brokenness, and their submission at the resurrection out of fear from this falling dead and waiting for what is decreed upon them of happiness or misery. And you are among them, broken like their brokenness, perplexed like their perplexity. Rather, if you were in the world among the luxurious and the rich enjoying comfort, then the kings of the earth on that day are the most humiliated people of the gathering place, the smallest of them, and the most contemptible; they are trodden under feet like a grain. And at that time, the wild beasts from the deserts and the mountains come with lowered heads, mixed with the creatures after their wildness, humbled for the Day of Resurrection, without any sin they have been defiled by, but their gathering is due to the intensity of the falling dead and the terror of the blowing and
24:41.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

24:44.arabic: ففي ذلك عبرة لأولى الأبصار فالرجل كل الرجل من يصبر على العافية ومعنى الصبر عليها ان لا يركن اليها ويعلم ان كل ذلك مستودع عنده وعسى ان يسترجع على القرب وان لا يرسل نفسه في الفرح بها ولا ينهمك في التنعم واللذة واللهو واللعب وان يرعى حقوق الله في ماله بالإنفاق وفي بدنه ببذل المعونة للخلق وفي لسانه ببذل الصدق وكذلك في سائر ما انعم الله به عليه وهذا الصبر متصل بالشكر فلا يتم الا بالقيام بحق الشكر كما سيأتي وانما كان الصبر على السراء اشد لأنه مقرون بالقدرة ومن العصمة ان لا تقدر والصبر على الحجامة والق
24:44.english: In that is a lesson for those of insight (أولى الأبصار). The complete man is he who is patient (يصبر) with well-being (العافية), and the meaning of patience with it is that he does not rely upon it, and knows that all of that is a trust deposited with him, and perhaps it will be taken back soon, and that he does not let his Soul (Nafs) go in rejoicing over it, nor does he immerse himself in enjoyment, pleasure, amusement, and play, and that he observes the rights of Allah in his wealth through spending, in his body through offering assistance to creation, in his tongue through offering truthfulness, and likewise in all that Allah has bestowed upon him. This patience is connected to gratitude (الشكر), and it is not complete except by fulfilling the right of gratitude as will come later. And indeed, patience with prosperity (السراء) is more severe because it is accompanied by ability, and from protection (العصمة) is not to have ability. Patience with cupping and intention when someone else performs it is easier than patience with you bleeding yourself and cupping yourself. The hungry person in the absence of food is more capable of patience than when delicious, tasty foods are present before him and he has power over them. For this reason, the trial of prosperity is great.
24:44.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

24:48.arabic: وقال ﭬ "أبغض خليقة الله إلى الله يوم القيامة الكذابون والمستكبرون والذين يكثرون البغضاء لإخوانهم في صدورهم فإذا لقوهم تملقوا لهم والذين إذا دعوا إلى الله ورسوله كانوا بكاء وإذا دعوا إلى الشيطان وأمره كانوا سراعاً"[241] وقال ابن مسعود: لا يكونن أحدكم إمعة، قالوا: وما الإمعة؟ قال الذي يجري مع كل ريح. واتفقوا على أن ملاقاة الاثنين بوجهين نفاق، وللنفاق علامات كثيرة وهذه من جملتها.
24:48.english: And He (peace be upon him) said: "The most hated creation of Allah to Allah on the Day of Resurrection are the liars and the arrogant and those who increase hatred for their brothers in their chests (Sudur) so when they meet them they flatter them and those who when they are called to Allah and His Messenger they are weeping and when they are called to Satan and his command they are swift."[241] And Ibn Mas'ud said: Let not any of you be a follower (Im'ah), they said: And what is the follower (Im'ah)? He said: The one who flows with every wind. And they agreed that meeting the two with two faces is hypocrisy (Nifaq), and hypocrisy (Nifaq) has many signs and this is among them.
24:48.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

24:52.arabic: وخطب رجل عند رسول الله ﭬ فقال: من يطع الله ورسوله فقد رشد ومن يعصهما فقد غوى" فقال "قل: ومن يعص الله ورسوله فقد غوى فكره رسول الله ﭬ قوله: ومن يعصهما، لأنه تسوية وجمع.
24:52.english: And a man delivered a sermon in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and said: 'Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has been guided, and whoever disobeys them has gone astray.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Say: And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has gone astray.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) disliked his statement: 'and whoever disobeys them,' because it implies equalization and grouping together.
24:52.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

24:52.arabic:
ي
بمقتك وأنا أشهدك على مقته. وقال علي رضي الله عنه لما أثنى عليه:  اللهم  اغفر
لي ما لا يعلمون ولا تؤاخذني بما يقولون واجعلني خيراً  مما  يظنون.  وأثنى  رجل
على عمر رضي الله عنه فقال: أتهلكني وتهلك نفسك؟ وأثنى رجل على  علي  كرم  الله
وجهه في وجهه -وكان قد بلغه أنه يقع فيه- فقال: أنا دون  ما  قلت  وفوق  ما  في
نفسك.


                              الآفة التاسعة عشر


                    الغفلة عن دقائق الخطأ في فحوى الكلام


                       لا سيما فيما يتعلق بالله وصفاته

ويرتبط بأمور الد
24:52.english: [257] Hadith: A man spoke before the Prophet (peace be upon him) and said: 'Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has been guided, and whoever disobeys them has gone astray.' The hadith was reported by Muslim from the narration of 'Adi ibn Hatim.
24:52.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

24:56.arabic: أما بعد: فإن الله تعالى جعل الزكاة إحدى مباني الإسلام وأردف بذكرها الصلاة التي هي أعلى الأعلام فقال تعالى: ﴿ وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة ﴾{البقرة: 83} وقال ﭬ: (بني الإسلام على خمس شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله وأن محمدا عبده ورسوله وإقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة[1]) وشدد الوعيد على المقصرين فيها فقال: ﴿ والذين يكنزون الذهب والفضة ولا ينفقونها في سبيل الله فبشرهم بعذاب أليم ﴾{التوبة: 34} ومعنى الإنفاق في سبيل الله إخراج حق الزكاة
24:56.english: After that: Indeed, Allah the Exalted made Zakat (obligatory almsgiving) one of the foundations of Islam and paired its mention with the Prayer (Salah) which is the highest of the signs. So He the Exalted said: 'And establish the Prayer (Salah) and give the Zakat (obligatory almsgiving)' (Al-Baqarah: 83). And He (the Prophet) said: 'Islam is built upon five: the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His servant and messenger, and establishing the Prayer (Salah), and giving the Zakat (obligatory almsgiving).' And He intensified the threat against those who are negligent in it, saying: 'And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah, then give them tidings of a painful punishment' (At-Tawbah: 34). And the meaning of spending in the way of Allah is the extraction of the right of Zakat (obligatory almsgiving).
24:56.topic: Al-Ghazali on the outer and inner dimensions of worship, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

24:58.arabic: ويحكى عن يحيى بن معاذ أنه رأى أبا يزيد - في بعض مشاهداته من بعد صلاة العشاء إلى طلوع الفجر - مستوفزاً على صدور قدميه رافعاً أخمصيه مع عقبيه عن الأرض ضارباً بذقنه على صدره شاخصاً بعينيه لا يطرف، قال: ثم سجد عند السحر فأطاله ثم قعد فقال: اللهم إن قوماً طلبوك فأعطيتهم المشي على الماء والمشي في الهواء فرضوا بذلك، وإني أعوذ بك من ذلك، وإن قوماً طلبوك فأعطيتهم طي الأرض فرضوا بذلك وإني أعوذ بك من ذلك، وإن قوماً طلبوك فأعطيتهم كنوز الأرض فرضوا بذلك وإني أعوذ بك من ذلك، حتى عد نيفاً وعشرين مقاماً من كرام
24:58.english: And it is narrated from Yahya ibn Mu'adh that he saw Abu Yazid - in some of his spiritual visions (Mushahadat) from after the Evening Prayer (Salat al-'Isha') until the rising of the Dawn (Fajr) - poised on the tops of his feet, raising the soles of his feet with his heels off the ground, striking his chin on his chest, staring with his eyes without blinking, he said: Then he prostrated at the pre-dawn time (Sahar) and prolonged it, then he sat and said: O Allah, indeed a people sought You and You granted them walking on water and walking in the air, and they were content with that, and I seek refuge in You from that, and indeed a people sought You and You granted them folding the earth, and they were content with that, and I seek refuge in You from that, and indeed a people sought You and You granted them treasures of the earth, and they were content with that, and I seek refuge in You from that, until he enumerated over twenty stations (Maqamat) of the miracles (Karamat) of the Friends (Awliya'), then he turned and saw me and said: Yahya! I said: Yes, O my master, he said: Since when have you been here? I said: Since a while, so he was silent, so I said: O my master, tell me something, so he said: I will tell you what is suitable for you, He entered me into the lower sphere (Falak) and revolved me in the lower dominion (Malakut) and showed me the earths and what is beneath them to the dust (Thara), then He entered me into the upper sphere (Falak) with me in the heavens and showed me what is in them from the Gardens (Jinan) to the Throne ('Arsh), He stood me before Him and said: Ask Me for any thing you have seen until I grant it to you? So I said: O my master, I have not seen anything that I admired so that I would ask You for it! So He said: You are truly My servant, you worship Me for My sake sincerely, I will indeed do with you and I will indeed do, and he mentioned things. Yahya said: So that overwhelmed me and I was filled with it and I was amazed at it and
24:58.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

24:58.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
24:58.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'What is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)".'
24:58.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

24:61.arabic: وكان مالك أبسط منه وأحسن خلقا فدخل الحسن وقال يا مويلك هكذا كنا لا يحتشم بعضنا بعضا حتى ظهرت أنت وأصحابك وأشار بهذا إلى أن الانبساط في بيوت الإخوان من الصفاء في الأخوة كيف وقد قال الله تعالى أو صديقكم وقال أو ما ملكتم مفاتحه إذ كان الأخ يدفع مفاتيح بيته إلى أخيه ويفوض له التصرف كما يريد وكان أخوه يتحرج عن الأكل بحكم التقوى حتى انزل الله تعالى هذه الآية وإذن لهم في الانبساط في طعام الإخوان و الأصدقاء
24:61.english: And Malik was more open (absat) and of better character than him, so Al-Hasan entered and said: 'O Muwaylik, this is how we used to be - we did not feel shy (yahtashim) with each other until you and your companions appeared.' And he indicated by this that openness (al-inbisat) in the houses of brothers (ikhwan) is from the purity (safa') in brotherhood (ukhuwwah). How could it not be, when Allah the Exalted has said: 'or your friend (sadiqikum)' and said: 'or what you possess the keys (mafatih) of it' - since a brother would give the keys (mafatih) of his house to his brother and delegate to him the disposal as he wishes, and his brother would feel constrained (yataharraj) about eating due to the ruling of piety (taqwa) until Allah the Exalted revealed this verse and permitted them in openness (al-inbisat) in the food of brothers (ikhwan) and true friends (asdiqa').
24:61.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

24:62.arabic: الفاسد  فيكون  انكشاف  بعض اعتقاداته عن الجهل سببا لبطلان بقية اعتقاداته أو لشكه  فيها  فإن  اتفق  زهوق روحه في هذه الخطرة قبل أن يثبت ويعود إلى  أصل  الإيمان  فقد  ختم  له  بالسوء وخرجت روحه على الشرك والعياذ بالله منه فهؤلاء هم  المرادون  بقوله  تعالى:  ﴿ وبدا لهم من الله ما لم يكونوا يحتسبون ﴾{} وبقوله عز  وجل:  ﴿  قل  هل  ننبئكم بالأخسرين أعمالا الذين ضل سعيهم في الحياة  الدنيا  وهم  يحسبون  أنهم  يحسنون صنعا ﴾{} وكما أنه ينكشف في النوم ما سيكون في المستقبل وذلك  بسبب  خفة  أشغال الدنيا عن ا
24:62.english: The corrupt one, so the unveiling of some of his beliefs due to ignorance becomes a cause for the invalidation of his remaining beliefs or for his doubt in them. If it happens that his spirit (Ruh) perishes in this danger before he becomes firm and returns to the foundation of faith (Iman), then he has been sealed with evil, and his spirit has departed upon polytheism (Shirk) - we seek refuge in Allah from that. These are the ones intended by His saying, the Exalted: 'And there will appear to them from Allah that which they had not taken into account' (Quran 39:47), and by His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Say, "Shall we inform you of the greatest losers as to [their] deeds? [They are] those whose effort is lost in worldly life, while they think that they are doing well in work."' (Quran 18:103-104). And just as what will be in the future is unveiled in sleep, due to the lightness of worldly occupations from the heart (Qalb), so too in the agonies of death some matters are unveiled, since the distractions of the world and the desires of the body are what prevent the heart from looking to the dominion (Malakut) to observe what is in the Preserved Tablet (Al-Lawh Al-Mahfuz), so that matters become unveiled to him as they truly are. Thus, such a state becomes a cause for unveiling (Kashf), and the unveiling becomes a cause for doubt in the remaining beliefs. And everyone who believes in Allah, the Exalted, and in His attributes and actions something contrary to what He is, whether by imitation (Taqlid) or by opinion-based reasoning (Nazar bil-Ra'i) and speculation, is in this danger, and asceticism (Zuhd) and righteousness (Salah) are not sufficient to repel this danger. Rather, nothing saves from it except true belief, and the simple-minded (Balah) are remote from this danger - I mean those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and the Last Day with a comprehensive, firm faith (Iman), like the Bedouins, the Sawad people, and the rest of the common folk who have not delved into investigation and reasoning, and have not independently embarked upon speech, nor have they inclined to the various types of theologians in imitating their differing statements. Therefore, he (the Prophet) said: 'Most of the people of Paradise are the simple-minded.' Therefore, the predecessors (Salaf) prohibited investigation, reasoning, delving into theological discourse (Kalam), and probing into these matters, and they commanded the creation to restrict themselves to believing in all that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has revealed, and in all that has come from the apparent meanings (Zawahir) while holding the belief in the negation of anthropomorphism (Tashbih), and they prohibited them from delving into interpretation (Ta'wil), because the danger in investigating the attributes is great, its obstacles are formidable, its paths are rugged, and the intellects are deficient in comprehending the majesty of Allah, the Exalted. And the guidance of Allah, the Exalted, with the light of certainty (Yaqin) is veiled from the hearts due to what they have been created with of love for the world. And what the investigators have mentioned with the merchandise of their intellects is disordered and contradictory, and the hearts are accustomed to and attached to what was cast into them at the beginning of creation. And the raging fanaticisms among the creation are nails confirming the inherited beliefs or those taken with good assumption from the teachers in the beginning. Then the dispositions are infatuated with love for the world and inclined towards it, and the desires of the world take them by the throat and divert them from complete thought. So if the door of speech about Allah and His attributes is opened with opinion and speculation...
24:62.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

24:64.arabic: أنه فيماذا يتفكر لم يقدر عليه  لأن  مجارى  الفكر  غير  محصورة وثمراته غير متناهية نعم نحن نجتهد في ضبط مجاريه بالإضافة  إلى  مهمات  العلوم الدينية وبالإضافة إلى الأحوال التى هى مقامات السالكين ويكون ذلك  ضبطا  جمليا فإن تفصيل ذلك يستدعى شرح العلوم كلها وجملة هذه  الكتب  كالشرح  لبعضها  فإنها مشتملة على علوم تلك العلوم تستفاد من أفكار مخصوصة فلنشر إلى ضبط الجامع  فيها ليحصل الوقوف على مجارى الفكر.                              بيان مجارى الفكر أعلم أن الفكر قد يجرى في أمر يتعلق بالدين وقد يجرى  في
24:64.english: That in what to think, he cannot encompass it because the channels of thought are not limited and its fruits are endless. Yes, we strive to regulate its channels in addition to the important matters of the religious sciences and in addition to the states (Ahwal) which are the stations (Maqamat) of the travelers (Salikin). And that will be a comprehensive regulation, for detailing that requires explaining all the sciences, and the entirety of these books is like an explanation for some of them, for they contain the sciences of those sciences derived from specific thoughts. So let us proceed to regulate the comprehensive in them to achieve standing upon the channels of thought.                              Clarification of the Channels of Thought Know that thought may run in a matter related to the religion and may run in what is related to other than the religion. And our aim is what is related to the religion, so let us leave the other division and concern ourselves with the religion, the transaction (Mu'amalah) that is between the servant (Abd) and the Lord (Rabb) Most High. So all the thoughts of the servant are either related to the servant and his attributes and his states, or related to the Worshipped One and His attributes and His actions; it is not possible to go beyond these two divisions. And what is related to the servant is either a looking at what is beloved (Mahbub) with the Lord Most High or at what is disliked (Makruh), and there is no need for thought in other than these two divisions. And what is related to the Lord Most High is either a looking at His Essence (Dhat) and His attributes and His Beautiful Names (Asma' al-Husna), or it is in His actions and His dominion (Mulk) and His sovereignty (Malakut) and all that is in the heavens and the earth and what is between them. And it becomes clear to you the confinement of thought in these divisions by an example, which is that the state of those who walk (Sa'irin) to Allah Most High and those who yearn (Mushtaqin) for meeting Him relates to his Beloved (Ma'shuq) or relates to himself. So if he thinks in his Beloved, then either he thinks in His beauty and the goodness of His image in His Essence to delight in thinking in Him and in witnessing Him, or he thinks in His subtle, good actions indicating His morals and His attributes to be that which doubles the pleasure and strengthens his love (Mahabbah). And if he thinks in himself, then his thought is in his attributes which drop him from the eye of his Beloved until he becomes purified from them, or in the attributes which bring him near to Him and make him beloved to Him until he becomes characterized by them. So if he thinks in something outside of these divisions, then that is outside the limit of passionate love (Ishq) and is a deficiency in it, because the complete, perfect passionate love is what overwhelms the lover (Ashiq) and fills the heart (Qalb) until it does not leave in it room for other than Him. So the lover (Muhibb) of Allah Most High should be like that, so his looking and thinking do not go beyond his Beloved. And whenever his thought is confined in these four divisions, it is not outside the requirement of love at all. So let us begin with the first division, which is his thinking in the attributes of himself and the actions of himself to distinguish the beloved from them from the disliked, for this thought is that which relates to the science of transaction (Ilm al-Mu'amalah) which is the intended purpose of this book. And as for the other division, it relates to the science of unveiling (Ilm al-Mukashafah), then every
24:64.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Contemplation'

25:3.arabic: وإن صدقوك فى مودتهم إياك فلا يملكون لك ولا لأنفسهم نفعا ولا ضرا ولا موتا ولا حياة ولا نشورا وقد يكون فى بلدك من أغنياء اليهود والنصارى من يزيد جاهه على جاهك وقد اشتغلت بهذا الغرور وغفلت عن النظر فى جمال ملكوت السموات والأرض ثم غفلت عن التنعم بالنظر إلى جلال مالك الملكوت والملك
25:3.english: And if they are truthful in their affection for you, they do not possess for you nor for themselves benefit nor harm, nor death, nor life, nor resurrection. And there may be in your land from the wealthy of the Jews and Christians whose status exceeds your status, and you have busied yourself with this delusion and neglected contemplating the beauty of the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, then neglected enjoying the gaze upon the majesty of the Owner of the kingdom and dominion.
25:3.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Contemplation'

25:12.arabic: ثم ليحضر بعد أهوال القيامة في قلبه صورة جهنم ودركاتها ومقامعها وأهوالها وسلاسلها وأغلالها وزقومها وصديدها وأنواع العذاب فيها وقبح صور الزبانية الموكلين بها وأنهم كلما نضجت جلودهم بدلوا جلودا غيرها وأنهم كلما أرادوا أن يخرجوا منها أعيدوا فيها وأنهم إذا رأوها من مكان بعيد سمعوا لها تغيظا وزفيرا وهلم جرا إلى جميع ما ورد في القرآن من شرحها
25:12.english: Then let him present in his heart (Qalb) after the terrors of the Resurrection the image of Hell and its depths, its beatings, its terrors, its chains, its shackles, its Zaqqum, its boiling water, and the types of torment in it, and the ugliness of the forms of the guardians (Zabaniyah) appointed over it, and that whenever their skins are roasted, they are replaced with other skins, and that whenever they wish to exit from it, they are returned into it, and that when they see it from a distant place, they hear for it raging and roaring, and so on to all that has come in the Quran of its explanation.
25:12.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Contemplation'

25:20.arabic: وحكى أن المزني رحمه الله خرج من باب جامع الفسطاط وقد أقبل ابن عبد الحكم في موكبه فبهره ما رأى من حسن حاله وحسن هيئته فتلا قوله تعالى وجعلنا بعضكم لبعض فتنة أتصبرون ثم قال بلى أصبر وأرضى وكان فقيرا مقلا فالذي هو في بيته لا يبتلى بمثل هذه الفتن فإن من شاهد زينة الدنيا فإما أن يقوى دينه ويقينه فيصبر إلى أن يتجرع مرارة الصبر وهو أمر من الصبر أو تنبعث رغبته فيحتال في طلب الدنيا فيهلك هلاكا مؤبدا أما في الدنيا فبالطمع الذي يخيب في أكثر الأوقات فليس كل من يطلب الدنيا تتيسر له وأما في الآخرة فإيثاره متا
25:20.english: And it is narrated that Al-Muzani, may Allah have mercy on him, exited from the gate of the Mosque of Al-Fustat, and Ibn Abd al-Hakam approached in his procession, and he was dazzled by what he saw of his good condition and fine appearance, so he recited the saying of Allah the Exalted: 'And We have made some of you a trial (fitnah) for others: will you have patience (tasbirun)?' Then he said: 'Yes, I will have patience (asbir) and be content.' And he was poor and destitute. So the one who is in his home is not tested with such trials (fitan). For whoever witnesses the adornment of the world, either his religion (din) and certainty (yaqin) strengthen, and he has patience (yasbir) until he swallows the bitterness of patience (sabr), and it is a command from patience (sabr); or his desire (raghbah) is stirred, and he schemes in seeking the world, and he perishes an eternal perishing. As for in the world, then through covetousness (tama') which fails in most times, for not everyone who seeks the world finds it facilitated for him. And as for in the Hereafter, then through his preferring the enjoyment of the world over the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah the Exalted and drawing near to Him.
25:20.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Seclusion'

25:21.arabic: القسم الثاني: التكبر على الرسل من حيث تعزز النفس وترفعها على الانقياد لبشر مثل سائر الناس؛ وذلك تارة يصرف عن الفكر والاستبصار فيبقى في ظلمة الجهل بكبره فيمتنع عن الانقياد وهو ظان أنه محق فيه، وتارة يمتنع مع المعرفة ولكن لا تطاوعه نفسه للإنقياد للحق والتواضع للرسل، كما حكى الله قولهم "أنؤمن لبشرين مثلنا" وقولهم "إن أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا ولئن أطعتم بشراً مثلكم إنكم إذا لخاسرون" وقال الذين لا يرجون لقائنا لولا أنزل علينا الملائكة أو نرى ربنا لقد استكبروا في أنفسهم وعتوا عواً كبيراً. وقالوا لولا أنزل ع
25:21.english: The second category: Arrogance (Takabbur) towards the Messengers, stemming from the Soul (Nafs) strengthening and elevating itself above submission to a human being like other people. This sometimes diverts from thought (Fikr) and insight (Istibsar), leaving one in the darkness of ignorance due to his arrogance, so he refuses submission while thinking he is correct in it. And sometimes he refuses despite knowledge, but his Soul (Nafs) does not comply with submission to the Truth (Haqq) and humility towards the Messengers, as Allah narrated their saying: "Shall we believe in two human beings like ourselves?" and their saying: "You are only human beings like us, and if you obey a human being like yourselves, then indeed you would be losers." And said those who do not hope for Our meeting: "If only the angels had been sent down to us or we could see our Lord." They have certainly become arrogant within themselves and transgressed a great transgression. And they said: "If only an angel had been sent down to him." And Pharaoh said, as Allah informed about him: "Or the angels should have come with him, accompanying him." And Allah said: "And he and his soldiers were arrogant in the land without right." So he was arrogant towards Allah and towards all His Messengers.
25:21.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

25:21.arabic: قد ذم الله الكبر في مواضع من كتابه وذم كل جبار متكبر فقال تعالى "سأصرف عن آياتي الذين يتكبرون في الأرض بغير الحق" وقال عز وجل "كذلك يطبع الله على كل قلب متكبر جبار" وقال تعالى "واستفتحوا وخاب كل جبار عنيد" وقال تعالى "إنه لا يحب المستكبرين" وقال تعالى "لقد استكبروا في أنفسهم وعتوا عتواً كبيراً" وقال تعالى "إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي سيدخلون جهنم داخرين" وذم الكبر في القرآن كثير وقد قال رسول الله ﭬ "لا يدخل الجنة من كان في قلبه مثقال حبة من خردل من كبر، ولا يدخل النار من كان في قلبه مثقال حبة من
25:21.english: Indeed, Allah has condemned arrogance in multiple places of His Book and condemned every tyrant who is arrogant. So He, the Exalted, said: "I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant on earth without right." And He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: "Thus does Allah seal over every heart of an arrogant tyrant." And He, the Exalted, said: "And they sought victory, and every obstinate tyrant was disappointed." And He, the Exalted, said: "Indeed, He does not love the arrogant." And He, the Exalted, said: "Indeed, they have become arrogant in their souls (Anfus) and transgressed a great transgression." And He, the Exalted, said: "Indeed, those who are arrogant toward My worship will enter Hell in humiliation." And the condemnation of arrogance in the Quran is abundant. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "He will not enter Paradise who has in his heart (Qalb) the weight of a mustard seed of arrogance, nor will he enter Hell who has in his heart (Qalb) the weight of a mustard seed of faith." And Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Allah, the Exalted, says: 'Grandeur (Kibriya) is My cloak and majesty (Izzah) is My garment. So whoever contends with Me for one of them, I will cast him into Hell, and I do not care.'" And from Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, he said: Abdullah ibn Amr and Abdullah ibn Umar met at al-Safa and stood together, then Ibn Amr departed and Ibn Umar remained weeping. They said: "What makes you weep, O Abu Abd al-Rahman?" He said: "This one - meaning Abdullah ibn Amr - claimed that he heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: 'Whoever has in his heart (Qalb) the weight of a mustard seed of arrogance, Allah will throw him on his face into Hell.'" And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "A man continues to go with his soul (Nafs) until he is written among the tyrants, and then befalls him what befell them of punishment." And Sulayman ibn Dawud (peace be upon them both) said one day - to the birds, humans, jinn, and beasts: "Come out," so they came out in two hundred thousand humans and two hundred thousand jinn, and he was raised until he heard the clamor of the angels glorifying in the heavens, then he was lowered until his feet touched the ground.
25:21.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

25:23.arabic: والإخلاص من غير صدق وتحقيق هباء وقد قال الله تعالى في كل عمل كان بإرادة غير الله مشوبا مغمورا وقدمنا إلى ما عملوا من عمل فجعلناه هباء منثورا وليت شعرى كيف يصحح نيته من لا يعرف حقيقة النية أو كيف يخلص من صحح النية إذا لم يعرف حقيقة الإخلاص أو كيف تطالب المخلص نفسه بالصدق إذا لم يتحقق معناه
25:23.english: And Sincerity (Ikhlas) without truthfulness (Sidq) and verification is scattered dust (Haba'). And Allah the Exalted has said regarding every deed that was with a desire other than Allah, mixed and submerged: 'And We will proceed to what they have done of deeds and make them as scattered dust (Haba' Manthuran).' And I wonder how one can correct his intention (Niyyah) who does not know the reality of intention, or how can one be sincere (Mukhlis) who has corrected the intention if he does not know the reality of sincerity (Ikhlas), or how can the sincere one (Mukhlis) demand from himself truthfulness (Sidq) if he has not verified its meaning.
25:23.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

25:26.arabic: وكذلك سمع مرة قوله تعالى الملك يومئذ الحق للرحمن فاضطرب فسأله ابن سالم وكان من أصحابه فقال قد ضعفت فقيل له فإن كان هذا من مضعف فما قوة الحال فقال أن لا يرد عليه وارد إلا وهو يلتقيه بقوة حاله فلا تغيره الواردات وإن كانت قوية
25:26.english: And similarly, he heard once the saying of the Exalted: 'The Sovereignty (al-Mulk) on that Day belongs truly to the Most Merciful (al-Rahman)' (Quran 25:26), and he became agitated. So Ibn Salim, who was from his companions, asked him, and he said: 'I have weakened.' So it was said to him: 'If this is from weakness, then what is the strength of the state (al-Hal)?' He said: 'That no incoming spiritual state (Wārid) comes upon him except that he meets it with the strength of his state (Hal), so the incoming states (Wāridāt) do not change him, even if they are strong.'
25:26.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

25:27.arabic: فكيف بك لو زلت قدمك ولم ينفعك ندمك فناديت بالويل والثبور وقلت هذا ما كنت أخافه فياليتنى قدمت لحياتي يا ليتنى اتخذت مع الرسول سبيلا يا ويلتا ليتنى لم اتخذ فلانا خليلا يا ليتنى كنت ترابا يا ليتنى كنت نسيا منسيا يا ليت أمى لم تلدنى، وعند ذلك تختطفك النيران والعياذ بالله وينادى المنادى اخسئوا فيها ولا تكلمون فلا يبقى سبيل إلا الصياح والأنين والتنفس والاستغاثة
25:27.english: How would it be for you if your foot slipped and your regret did not benefit you, then you would call out with woe and ruin and say: 'This is what I used to fear. Oh, would that I had sent ahead for my life! Oh, would that I had taken with the Messenger a way! Oh, woe to me! Would that I had not taken so-and-so as a friend! Oh, would that I had been dust! Oh, would that I had been a thing forgotten! Oh, would that my mother had not borne me!' And at that time, the fires would snatch you—we seek refuge in Allah—and the caller would call out: 'Be driven into it, and do not speak!' Then there would remain no way except screaming, groaning, breathing, and calling for help.
25:27.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Repentance'

25:28.arabic: فكيف بك لو زلت قدمك ولم ينفعك ندمك فناديت بالويل والثبور وقلت هذا ما كنت أخافه فياليتنى قدمت لحياتي يا ليتنى اتخذت مع الرسول سبيلا يا ويلتا ليتنى لم اتخذ فلانا خليلا يا ليتنى كنت ترابا يا ليتنى كنت نسيا منسيا يا ليت أمى لم تلدنى، وعند ذلك تختطفك النيران والعياذ بالله وينادى المنادى اخسئوا فيها ولا تكلمون فلا يبقى سبيل إلا الصياح والأنين والتنفس والاستغاثة
25:28.english: How would it be for you if your foot slipped and your regret did not benefit you, then you would call out with woe and destruction and say: 'This is what I used to fear! Would that I had sent forth for my life! Would that I had taken with the Messenger a way! Woe to me! Would that I had not taken so-and-so as a close friend (Khalil)! Would that I had been dust! Would that I had been a thing forgotten and out of sight! Would that my mother had not borne me!' And at that time, the fires would snatch you—we seek refuge in Allah—and the caller would call out: 'Be driven into it, and do not speak!' Then there would remain no way except screaming, groaning, breathing, and calling for help.
25:28.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Repentance'

25:34.arabic: ولو نظر إلى صورهم في النار وأنتانهم وأقذارهم لاستنكف منهم ولتبرأ من الانتساب إليهم، ولأنكر على من نسبه إليهم استقذاراً واستحقار لهم، ولو انكشف له ذلهم في القيامة وقد تعلق الخصماء بهم والملائكة آخذون بنواصيهم يجرونهم على وجوههم إلى جهنم في مظالم العباد لتبرأ إلى الله منهم، ولكان انتسابه إلى الكلب والخنزير أحب إليه من الانتساب إليهم، فحق أولاد الظلمة إن عصمهم الله من ظلمهم أن يشكروا الله تعالى على سلامة دينهم ويستغفروا لآبائهم إن كانوا مسلمين!ّ فأما العجب فجهل محض.
25:34.english: And if he were to look at their forms in the Fire and their filth and impurities, he would recoil from them and disavow association with them, and he would deny anyone who attributed him to them out of disgust and contempt for them. And if their humiliation in the Resurrection were unveiled to him, with the adversaries clinging to them and the angels taking them by their forelocks, dragging them on their faces to Hell for the injustices against the servants, he would seek refuge with Allah from them, and his association with the dog and the pig would be more beloved to him than association with them. So it is right for the children of the oppressors, if Allah protects them from their oppression, to thank Allah the Exalted for the safety of their religion and seek forgiveness for their fathers if they were Muslims! As for pride, it is pure ignorance.
25:34.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

25:38.arabic: وكان الربيع بن خثيم أصابه فالج، فقيل له: لو تداويت؟ فقال: قد هممت ثم ذكرت عاداً وثمود وأصحاب الرس وقروناً بين ذلك كثيراً وكان فيهم الأطباء، فهلك المداوي والمداوى، ولم تغن الرقي شيئاً.
25:38.english: And Ar-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym was afflicted with paralysis, so it was said to him: 'If only you would seek treatment?' He said: 'I had intended to, then I remembered 'Aad and Thamud and the Companions of the Well (Ashab ar-Rass) and generations between that many, and among them were physicians, so perished the treater and the treated, and incantations availed nothing.'
25:38.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

25:42.arabic: فكما أنه إذا نكح ووطئ وأنزل بقي متردداً في الولد يخاف ويرجو فضل الله في خلق الولد ودفع الآفات عن الرحم وعن الأم إلى أن يتم فهو كيس، فكذلك إذا آمن وعمل الصالحات وترك السيئات وبقي متردداً بين الخوف والرجاء يخاف أن لا يقبل منه وأن لا يدوم عليه وأن يختم له بالسوء، ويرجوا من الله تعالى أن يثبته بالقول الثابت ويحفظ دينه من صواعق سكرات الموت حتى يموت على التوحيد، ويحرس قلبه عن الميل إلى الشهوات بقية عمره حتى لا يميل إلى المعاصي فهو كيس، ومن عدا هؤلاء فهم المغرورون بالله "وسوف يعلمون حين يرون العذاب من
25:42.english: Just as when one marries and has intercourse and ejaculates, he remains hesitant about the child, fearing and hoping for the favor of Allah in creating the child and warding off afflictions from the womb and from the mother until it is complete, he is wise. Similarly, if one believes and does righteous deeds and abandons sins and remains hesitant between fear and hope, fearing that it will not be accepted from him and that it will not last for him and that he will be sealed with evil, and hoping from Allah the Exalted that He will establish him with the firm word and protect his religion from the thunderbolts of the agonies of death until he dies upon monotheism (Tawhid), and guards his heart (Qalb) from inclining toward desires for the remainder of his life so that he does not incline toward sins, he is wise. And whoever is other than these, they are the ones deluded by Allah "And they will know, when they see the punishment, who is more astray in way - and you will know its news after a while." And at that time they will say as Allah informed about them: "Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us; we will do righteousness. Indeed, we are certain." That is, we have learned that just as a child is not born except by intercourse and marriage, and a crop does not grow except by plowing and sowing seed, similarly, reward and recompense are not attained in the Hereafter except by righteous deed, so return us, we will do righteous deeds, for we have now learned the truth of Your saying: "And that there is not for man except that [good] for which he strives, and that his effort is going to be seen - Whenever a company is thrown into it, its keepers ask them, 'Did there not come to you a warner?' They will say, 'Yes, a warner had come to us, but we denied...'" That is, did we not hear you about the way of Allah (Sunnah) with His servants and that "Every soul will be fully repaid [for] what it earned" and that "Every soul, for what it has earned, is held in pledge"? So what deluded you about Allah after you heard and understood? "They will say, 'If only we had been listening or reasoning, we would not be among the companions of the Blaze.' And they will admit their sin, so away with the companions of the Blaze."
25:42.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

25:43.arabic: وإلى مثل هذا القلب الإشارة بقوله تعالى أرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه أفأنت تكون عليه وكيلا أم تحسب أن أكثرهم يسمعون أو يعقلون إن هم إلا كالأنعام بل هم أضل سبيلا وبقوله عز وجل لقد حق القول على أكثرهم فهم لا يؤمنون وبقوله سواء عليهم أأنذرتهم أم لم تنذرهم لا يؤمنون ورب قلب هذا حاله بالإضافة إلى بعض الشهوات كالذي يتورع عن بعض الأشياء ولكنه إذا رأى وجها حسنا لم يملك عينه وقلبه وطاش عقله وسقط مساك قلبه أو كالذي لا يملك نفسه فيما فيه الجاه والرياسة والكبر ولا يبقى معه مسكة للتثبت عند ظهور أسبابه أو كالذي لا
25:43.english: And to such a heart (Qalb) is the reference in His saying, the Exalted: 'Have you seen the one who takes his desire (Hawa) as his god? Then would you be a guardian over him?' Or do you think that most of them hear or understand? They are only like cattle, but they are more astray in way. And in His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'The word has become due upon most of them, so they do not believe.' And in His saying: 'It is the same to them whether you warn them or do not warn them—they will not believe.' And many a heart is in this state with respect to some desires (Shahawat), like one who abstains from some things, but when he sees a beautiful face, he cannot control his eye and his heart (Qalb), his intellect (Aql) becomes confused, and the reins of his heart (Qalb) fall, or like one who cannot control himself in matters of status, leadership, and arrogance, and no restraint remains with him for caution when its causes appear, or like one who cannot control himself in anger whenever he is belittled and a defect of his defects is mentioned, or like one who cannot control himself when able to take a dirham or dinar, but rushes upon it with the rush of the bewildered, heedless one, forgetting in it chivalry (Muru'ah) and piety (Taqwa). All of that is due to the rising of the smoke of desire (Hawa) to the heart (Qalb) until it darkens and its lights are extinguished from it, so the light of modesty (Haya'), chivalry (Muru'ah), and faith (Iman) is extinguished, and it strives to achieve the will of Satan.
25:43.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

25:43.arabic: وأمره مخطر فى نفسه فإن عجزت عن ذلك كله فكن محبا لرسول الله ﭬ حريصا على تعظيم سننه ومتشوقا إلى مراعاة قلوب الصالحين من أمته ومتبركا بأدعيتهم فعساك أن تنال من شفاعته أو شفاعتهم فتنجو بالشفاعة إن كنت قليل البضاعة. (صفة الشفاعة) اعلم أن إذا حق دخول النار على طوائف من المؤمنين فإن الله تعالى بفضله يقبل فيهم شفاعة الأنبياء والصديقين بل شفاعة العلماء والصالحين وكل من له عند الله تعالى جاه وحسن معاملة فإن له شفاعة فى أهله وقرابته وأصدقائه ومعارفه فكن حريصا على أن تكتسب لنفسك عندهم رتبة الشفاعة وذلك بأن
25:43.english: And his matter is precarious in his soul. If you are incapable of all that, then be a lover of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), diligent in venerating his traditions (Sunnah), yearning to observe the hearts (Qulub) of the righteous (Salihin) among his community, and seeking blessings (Tabarruk) through their supplications (Ad'iyah). Perhaps you may attain from his intercession (Shafa'ah) or their intercession, and thus be saved by intercession if you are of little stock. (Description of Intercession) Know that when entry into the Fire becomes due for groups of the believers, then Allah the Exalted, by His grace, accepts among them the intercession of the prophets and the truthful ones (Siddiqin), indeed the intercession of the scholars (Ulama) and the righteous (Salihin), and everyone who has standing (Jah) and good dealings with Allah the Exalted, then he has intercession for his family, relatives, friends, and acquaintances. So be diligent to acquire for yourself with them the rank of intercession, and that is by not despising any human being at all, for Allah the Exalted has concealed His friendship (Wilayah) in His servants; perhaps the one whom your eye belittles is the friend (Wali) of Allah. And do not deem any sin (Ma'siyah) small at all, for Allah the Exalted has concealed His anger (Ghadab) in sins; perhaps the wrath (Maqt) of Allah is in it. And do not deem any obedience (Ta'ah) insignificant at all, for Allah the Exalted has concealed His pleasure (Rida) in obedience; perhaps His pleasure is in it, even if it be a good word or a good intention (Niyyah) or what runs in its course. And the evidences for intercession in the Quran and reports (Akhbar) are many: Allah the Exalted said: 'And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be satisfied' (Quran 93:5). It is narrated from Amr ibn al-'As: (that the Messenger of Allah...
25:43.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

25:43.arabic: وإلى هذا التفريد والتجريد الإشارة بقوله تعالى: " قل الله ثم ذرهم في خوضهم"، وبقوله تعالى: " إن الذين قالوا ربنا الله ثم استقاموا " بل هو معنى قولك " لا إله إلا الله " أي معبود ولا محبوب سواه، فكل محبوب فإنه معبود، فإن العبد هو المقيد والمعبود هو المقيد به، وكل محب مقيد بما يحبه. ولذلك قال الله تعالى: " أرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه " وقال ﭬ: " أبغض إله عبد في الأرض الهوى " ولذلك قال عليه السلام: " من قال لا إله إلا الله مخلصاً دخل الجنة"[27] ومعنى الإخلاص أن يخلص قلبه لله فلا يبقى فيه شرك لغير الله، ف
25:43.english: And to this singling out and purification (Tafrīd wa-Tajrīd) points the saying of the Exalted: "Say: Allah, then leave them in their vain discourse" (Quran 6:91), and His saying: "Indeed, those who have said: 'Our Lord is Allah' and then have remained steadfast" (Quran 41:30). Rather, it is the meaning of your saying "There is no god but Allah" (Lā ilāha illā Allāh) - meaning no worshipped one and no beloved one except Him. For every beloved one is a worshipped one, since the servant (Al-ʿAbd) is the bound one and the worshipped one (Al-Maʿbūd) is that by which he is bound, and every lover is bound by what he loves. Therefore, Allah the Exalted said: "Have you seen the one who takes his desire (Hawāhu) as his god?" (Quran 25:43) and He said: "The most hated god of a servant on earth is desire (Al-Hawā)." Therefore, the Prophet (upon him be peace) said: "Whoever says 'There is no god but Allah' sincerely (Mukhlisan) enters Paradise." And the meaning of sincerity (Al-Ikhlāṣ) is that he purifies his heart (Qalb) for Allah so that no association (Shirk) for other than Allah remains in it. Thus, Allah becomes the beloved of his heart, the worshipped of his heart, and the intended of his heart alone. Whoever is in this state, the world (Al-Dunyā) is his prison because it prevents him from witnessing his beloved, and his death is liberation from the prison and arrival to the beloved. So what is the state of one who has only one beloved, and his longing for him has prolonged, and his imprisonment from him has extended, then he is freed from the prison and enabled to reach the beloved, and his soul (Rūḥ) is in security forever and ever?
25:43.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

25:43.arabic: والمتحصن به لا معبود له سوى الله سبحانه فأما من اتخذ إلهه هواه فهو في ميدان الشيطان لا في حصن الله عز وجل واعلم أن من مكايده أن يشغلك في صلاتك بذكر الآخرة وتدبير فعل الخيرات ليمنعك عن فهم ما تقرأ فاعلم أن كل ما يشغلك عن فهم معاني قراءتك فهو وسواس فإن حركة اللسان غير مقصودة بل المقصود معانيها.
25:43.english: And the one who takes refuge in it has no object of worship except Allah (God) the Exalted. As for the one who takes his desire (Hawa) as his god (Ilah), he is in the arena of Satan (Shaytan), not in the fortress of Allah (God) the Exalted. And know that among his stratagems is to distract you in your prayer with remembrance (Dhikr) of the Hereafter and planning good deeds to prevent you from understanding what you recite. Know that everything that distracts you from understanding the meanings of your recitation is whisperings (Waswas), for the movement of the tongue is not the intended goal; rather, the intended goal is their meanings.
25:43.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

25:44.arabic: وإنما خاصية الإنسان التى حجبت البهائم عنها معرفة الله تعالى بالنظر فى ملكوت السموات والأرض وعجائب الافاق والأنفس إذ بها يدخل العبد فى زمرة الملائكة المقربين ويحشر فى زمرة النبيين والصديقين مقربا من حضرة رب العالمين وليست هذه المنزلة للبهائم ولا لإنسان رضى من الدنيا بشهوات البهائم فإنه شر من البهائم بكثير إذ لا قدرة للبهيمة على ذلك وأما هو فقد خلق الله له القدرة ثم عطلها وكفر نعمة الله فيها فأولئك كالأنعام بل هم أضل سبيلا
25:44.english: And indeed, the specific characteristic of the human being that is veiled from the animals is the knowledge of Allah (God) the Exalted through contemplation in the dominion of the heavens and the earth and the wonders of the horizons and the souls (Anfus), for through it the servant enters into the ranks of the close angels and is resurrected in the ranks of the prophets and the truthful ones, brought near to the presence of the Lord of the worlds. And this station is not for the animals, nor for a human being who is content with the worldly desires of the animals, for he is worse than the animals by much, since the animal has no capability for that. But as for him, Allah created for him the capability, then he nullified it and disbelieved in the blessing of Allah in it. So those are like the cattle (Al-An'am), rather they are more astray in way (sabilan).
25:44.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Contemplation'

25:45.arabic: وقد قال تعالى: ﴿ الشمس والقمر بحسبان ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ ألم تر إلى ربك كيف مد الظل ولو شاء لجعله ساكنا ثم جعلنا الشمس عليه دليلا ثم قبضناه إلينا قبضا يسيرا ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ والقمر قدرناه منازل ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ وهو الذي جعل لكم النجوم لتهتدوا بها في ظلمات البر والبحر ﴾ {} فلا تظنن أن المقصود من سير الشمس والقمر بحسبان منظوم مرتب ومن خلق الظل والنور والنجوم أن يستعان بها على أمور الدنيا بل لتعرف بها مقادير الأوقات فتشتغل فيها بالطاعات والتجارة للدار الآخرة يدلك عليه قوله تعالى: ﴿ وهو الذي جعل
25:45.english: And He (Exalted is He) said: 'The sun and the moon are by calculation' (Quran 55:5). And He (Exalted is He) said: 'Have you not seen to your Lord how He extended the shadow? And if He willed, He would have made it stationary. Then We made the sun upon it a guide. Then We withdraw it to Us a gradual withdrawal' (Quran 25:45). And He (Exalted is He) said: 'And the moon - We have determined for it phases' (Quran 36:39). And He (Exalted is He) said: 'And He is the One who made for you the stars to guide you by them in the darknesses of the land and the sea' (Quran 6:97). So do not think that the intended purpose from the movement of the sun and the moon by a precise, ordered calculation, and from the creation of the shadow and the light and the stars, is that they be used for worldly matters. Rather, it is so that you may know by them the measures of the times, so that you may occupy yourself in them with acts of obedience (Taa'aat) and trade for the Abode of the Hereafter (Daar al-Aakhirah). This is indicated to you by His (Exalted is He) saying: 'And He is the One who made the night and the day in succession for whoever desires to remember (Yadhkur) or desires to be grateful (Shakooran)' (Quran 25:62). That is, one of them succeeds the other so that what was missed in one may be made up in the other. And He clarified that this is for Remembrance (Dhikr) and gratitude (Shukr) only, nothing else. And He (Exalted is He) said: 'And We made the night and the day two signs. Then We erased the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible, that you may seek bounty from your Lord and may know the number of years and the account' (Quran 17:12). And the bounty sought is only the reward (Thawaab) and forgiveness (Maghfirah). And we ask Allah for good success in what pleases Him.
25:45.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

25:46.arabic: وإظهاره القدرة بقبض الظل فيه إذ قال تعالى: ﴿ ثم قبضناه إلينا قبضا يسيرا ﴾ {} وهو وقت قبض ظل الليل ببسط نور الشمس وإرشاده الناس إلى التسبيح فيه بقوله تعالى: ﴿ فسبحان الله حين تمسون وحين تصبحون ﴾ {} وبقوله تعالى: ﴿ فسبح بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها ﴾ {} وقوله عز وجل: ﴿ ومن آناء الليل فسبح وأطراف النهار لعلك ترضى ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ واذكر اسم ربك بكرة وأصيلا ﴾ {}.
25:46.english: And His manifestation of power in withdrawing the shadow therein, as He the Exalted said: 'Then We withdraw it to Us, a gradual withdrawal' (Quran 25:46). And it is the time of withdrawing the shadow of the night by spreading the light of the sun, and His guiding people to glorification therein by His saying the Exalted: 'So glorify Allah when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning' (Quran 30:17), and by His saying the Exalted: 'So glorify with praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting' (Quran 50:39), and His saying the Mighty and Majestic: 'And during parts of the night glorify, and at the ends of the day, that you may be satisfied' (Quran 20:130), and His saying the Exalted: 'And remember the name of your Lord morning and evening' (Quran 76:25).
25:46.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

25:47.arabic: فانظر كيف جعل الله تعالى الليل لباسا والنوم سباتا والنهار معاشا وانظر إلى إيلاجه الليل في النهار والنهار فى الليل وإدخاله الزيادة والنقصان عليهما على ترتيب مخصوص
25:47.english: Then look at how Allah the Exalted made the night a garment (libās) and sleep a repose (subāt) and the day a livelihood (maʿāsh). And look at His interweaving the night into the day and the day into the night, and His introducing increase and decrease upon them according to a specific arrangement.
25:47.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Contemplation'

25:54.arabic: وإذا قربت من الإنزال فقل في نفسك ولا تحرك شفتيك الحمد لله الذي خلق من الماء بشرا فجعله نسبا وصهرا وكان ربك قديرا وكان بعض أصحاب الحديث يكبر حتى يسمع أهل الدار صوته ثم ينحرف عن القبلة ولا يستقبل القبلة بالوقاع إكراما للقبلة وليغط نفسه وأهله بثوب.
25:54.english: And when approaching ejaculation, say in your heart (Nafs) and do not move your lips: 'Praise be to Allah who created from water a human being (Bashar) and made him lineage (Nasab) and affinity (Sihr), and your Lord is All-Powerful (Qadir).' And some of the companions of the Hadith would say 'Allahu Akbar' until the people of the house heard his voice, then he would turn away from the Qiblah and not face the Qiblah during intercourse, out of reverence for the Qiblah, and to cover himself and his family with a garment.
25:54.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

25:54.arabic: ومن بدائع ألطافه أن خلق من الماء بشرا فجعله نسبا وصهرا وسلط على الخلق شهوة اضطرهم بها الحراثة جبرا واستبقى بهم نسلهم إقهارا وقسرا ثم عظم أمر الأنساب وجعل لها قدرا فحرم بسببها السفاح وبالغ في تقبيحه ردعا وزجرا وجعل اقتحامه جريمة فاحشة وأمر إمرا وندب إلى النكاح وحث عليه استحبابا وأمرا فسبحان من كتب الموت على عباده فأذلهم به هدما وكسرا ثم بث بذور النطف في أراضي الأرحام وأنشأ منها خلقا وجعله لكسر الموت جبرا تنبيها على أن بحار المقادير فياضة على العالمين نفعا وضرا وخيرا وشرا وعسرا ويسرا وطيا ونشرا
25:54.english: And from the wonders of His subtle favors (Al-Lata'if) is that He created from water a human being (Basharan) and made him kinship (Nasaban) and marriage alliance (Sihran), and He empowered over creation a desire (Shahwah) that compelled them to cultivation by force (Jabran), and preserved through them their progeny by overpowering (Iqhar) and coercion (Qasran). Then He magnified the matter of kinship ties (Al-Ansab) and gave them importance, so He prohibited because of them illicit sexual intercourse (Al-Sifah) and intensified in condemning it as a deterrent (Rad'an) and warning (Zajran), and made its commission a heinous crime and a command (Amran), and exhorted to marriage (Al-Nikah) and urged upon it as recommended (Istihbab) and commanded (Amran). So glory be to the One who decreed death upon His servants, thus humbling them with it as destruction (Hadman) and breaking (Kasran), then He scattered the seeds of sperm (Al-Nutaf) in the lands of wombs (Al-Arham) and brought forth from them a creation, and made it as a compensation (Jabran) for breaking death, as a reminder that the seas of destinies (Al-Maqadir) are overflowing upon the worlds with benefit (Naf'an) and harm (Darran), good (Khayran) and evil (Sharran), hardship (Usran) and ease (Yusran), folding (Tayyan) and unfolding (Nashran).
25:54.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

25:58.arabic: ورؤى مالك بن أنس فقيل ما فعل الله بك قال غفر لي بكلمة كان يقولها عثمان بن عفان رضي الله عنه عند رؤية الجنازة سبحان الحي الذي لا يموت
25:58.english: And Malik ibn Anas was seen (in a dream) and it was said: 'What has Allah done with you?' He said: 'He forgave me due to a word that Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him) used to say upon seeing a funeral: "Glory be to the Living (Al-Hayy) who does not die."'
25:58.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

25:58.arabic: وقرأ الخواص قوله تعالى: " وتوكل على الحي الذي لا يموت " إلى آخر، فقال: ما ينبغي للعبد بعد هذه الآية أن يلجأ إلى أحد غير الله تعالى.
25:58.english: And the ascetic (Al-Khawass) recited the saying of the Exalted: "And rely upon (tawakkul) the Living (Al-Hayy) who does not die" to the end, then he said: It is not fitting for the servant (al-'abd) after this verse to seek refuge in anyone other than Allah the Exalted.
25:58.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

25:60.arabic: القسم الثاني: التكبر على الرسل من حيث تعزز النفس وترفعها على الانقياد لبشر مثل سائر الناس؛ وذلك تارة يصرف عن الفكر والاستبصار فيبقى في ظلمة الجهل بكبره فيمتنع عن الانقياد وهو ظان أنه محق فيه، وتارة يمتنع مع المعرفة ولكن لا تطاوعه نفسه للإنقياد للحق والتواضع للرسل، كما حكى الله قولهم "أنؤمن لبشرين مثلنا" وقولهم "إن أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا ولئن أطعتم بشراً مثلكم إنكم إذا لخاسرون" وقال الذين لا يرجون لقائنا لولا أنزل علينا الملائكة أو نرى ربنا لقد استكبروا في أنفسهم وعتوا عواً كبيراً. وقالوا لولا أنزل ع
25:60.english: The second category: Arrogance (Takabbur) toward the Messengers, in terms of the Soul (Nafs) exalting and elevating itself above submission to a human being like other people; this sometimes diverts from thought (Fikr) and insight (Istibsar), so he remains in the darkness of ignorance (Jahl) due to his arrogance, and he refrains from submission while thinking he is right in it, and sometimes he refrains despite knowledge (Ma'rifah) but his Soul (Nafs) does not comply with submission to the Truth (Haqq) and humility (Tawadu') toward the Messengers, as Allah narrated their saying: "Shall we believe in two humans like ourselves?" and their saying: "You are only human beings like us, and if you obey a human being like yourselves, then indeed you would be losers." And those who do not expect the meeting with Us said: "Why have not angels been sent down to us, or why do we not see our Lord?" They have certainly become arrogant within themselves and become insolent with great insolence. And they said: "Why has not an angel been sent down to him?" And Pharaoh, in what Allah informed about him, said: "Or that he bring with him the angels as companions?" And Allah said: "And he and his soldiers were arrogant in the land without right." So he was arrogant toward Allah and toward all His Messengers. And Allah said: "And when it is said to them: 'Prostrate to the Most Merciful (Al-Rahman),' they say: 'And what is the Most Merciful (Al-Rahman)? Shall we prostrate to that which you order us?' And it increases them in aversion (Nufur).'"
25:60.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

25:61.arabic: وتقول عند النظر إلى السماء ﴿ ربنا ما خلقت هذا باطلا سبحانك فقنا عذاب النار ﴾ {} ﴿ تبارك الذي جعل في السماء بروجا وجعل فيها سراجا وقمرا منيرا ﴾ {} وإذا سمعت صوت الرعد فقل سبحان من يسبح الرعد بحمده والملائكة من خيفته[207]
25:61.english: And say when looking at the sky: 'Our Lord, You did not create this in vain. Glory be to You, so protect us from the punishment of the Fire.' {} 'Blessed is He who placed in the sky constellations and placed therein a lamp and a luminous moon.' {} And if you hear the sound of thunder, say: 'Glory be to the One whom the thunder glorifies with His praise and the angels from fear of Him.'
25:61.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

25:62.arabic: نحمد الله على آلائه حمدا كثيرا ونذكره ذكرا لا يغادر في القلب استكبارا ولا نفورا ونشكره إذ جعل الليل والنهار خلفه لمن أراد أن يذكر أو أراد شكورا
25:62.english: We praise Allah for His blessings with abundant praise, and we remember Him with a remembrance (Dhikr) that does not leave in the Heart (Qalb) arrogance nor aversion, and we thank Him since He made the night and the day alternating for whoever intended to remember (Yadhakkara) or intended to be thankful (Shukūran).
25:62.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

25:62.arabic: وإن لم ينم ولم يشتغل بالكسب واشتغل بالصلاة والذكر فهو أفضل أعمال النهار لأنه وقت غفلة الناس عن الله عز وجل واشتغالهم بهموم الدنيا فالقلب المتفرغ لخدمة ربه عند إعراض العبيد عن بابه جدير بأن يزكيه الله تعالى ويصطفيه لقربه ومعرفته وفضل ذلك كفضل إحياء الليل فإن الليل وقت الغفلة بالنوم وهذا وقت الغفلة باتباع الهوى والاشتغال بهموم الدنيا وأحد معنى قوله تعالى: ﴿ وهو الذي جعل الليل والنهار خلفة لمن اراد أن يذكر ﴾ {} أي يخلف أحدهما الآخر في الفضل والثاني أنه يخلفه فيتدارك فيه ما فات في أحدهما.
25:62.english: And if he does not sleep and does not occupy himself with earning and occupies himself with prayer and remembrance (Dhikr), it is the best of the daytime deeds because it is a time of heedlessness (Ghafala) of the people from Allah the Exalted and their preoccupation with worldly concerns, so the heart (Qalb) that is free to serve its Lord when the servants turn away from His door is worthy that Allah the Exalted purify him and select him for His proximity and knowledge, and the merit of that is like the merit of reviving the night, for the night is a time of heedlessness (Ghafala) through sleep, and this is a time of heedlessness (Ghafala) through following desire (Hawa) and preoccupation with worldly concerns. And one meaning of His saying the Exalted: 'And He is the One who made the night and the day successive (Khilfatan) for whoever intends to remember (Yadhakkara)' {} meaning one of them succeeds the other in merit, and the second is that it succeeds it so that what was missed in one of them is made up for in it.
25:62.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

25:62.arabic: فلا تظنن أن المقصود من سير الشمس والقمر بحسبان منظوم مرتب ومن خلق الظل والنور والنجوم أن يستعان بها على أمور الدنيا بل لتعرف بها مقادير الأوقات فتشتغل فيها بالطاعات والتجارة للدار الآخرة يدلك عليه قوله تعالى: ﴿ وهو الذي جعل الليل والنهار خلفة لمن أراد أن يذكر أو أراد شكورا ﴾ {} أي يخلف أحدهما الآخر ليتدارك في أحدهما ما فات في الآخر وبين أن ذلك للذكر والشكر لا غير
25:62.english: So do not think that the purpose of the sun and moon moving in a precise, ordered system, and the creation of shadow and light and stars, is to be aided by them in worldly matters. Rather, it is to know by them the measures of times so that you may occupy yourself therein with acts of obedience and trade for the Abode of the Hereafter. This is indicated to you by His saying, the Exalted: 'And He is the One who made the night and the day successive for whoever intends to remember (Dhikr) or intends to be grateful (Shukr).' {} Meaning, one of them succeeds the other so that what was missed in one may be made up for in the other. And He made clear that this is for Remembrance (Dhikr) and Gratitude (Shukr) only, nothing else.
25:62.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

25:63.arabic: وقد ذكر الله تعالى صفات المؤمنين والمنافقين في كتابه وهي بجملتها ثمرة حسن الخلق وسوء الخلق. فلنورد جملة من ذلك لتعلم آية حسن الخلق. قال الله تعالى "قد أفلح المؤمنون الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون والذين هم عن اللغو معرضون" إلى قوله "أولئك هم الوارثون" وقال عز وجل "التائبون العابدون الحامدون" إلى قوله "وبشر المؤمنين" وقال عز وجل "إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم" إلى قوله "أولئك هم المؤمنون حقاً" وقال تعالى "وعباد الرحمن الذين يمشون على الأرض هوناً وإذا خاطبهم الجاهلون قالوا سلاما" إلى آخر
25:63.english: And Allah the Exalted has mentioned the attributes of the believers and the hypocrites in His Book, and they are in their entirety the fruit of good character (Husn al-Khuluq) and bad character (Su' al-Khuluq). So let us present a collection of that to know the sign of good character. Allah the Exalted said: 'Successful indeed are the believers who are humble in their prayers and who turn away from idle talk' to His saying 'Those are the inheritors.' And He the Mighty and Majestic said: 'The repentant, the worshippers, the praisers' to His saying 'and give glad tidings to the believers.' And He the Mighty and Majestic said: 'The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble' to His saying 'Those are the true believers.' And He the Exalted said: 'And the servants of the Most Merciful (Ibad al-Rahman) who walk upon the earth humbly (Hawwan) and when the ignorant address them, they say peace (Salaman).' to the end of the surah. Whoever is confused about his condition, let him present himself to these verses, for the presence of all these attributes is a sign of good character, and the absence of all of them is a sign of bad character, and the presence of some without others indicates some without others, so let him occupy himself with acquiring what he lacks and preserving what he has found.
25:63.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

25:63.arabic: وقيل في قوله تعالى "ربانيين" أي حلماء علماء. وعن الحسن في قوله تعالى "وإذا خاطبهم الجاهلون قالوا سلاماً" قال حلماء إن جهل عليهم لم يجهلوا. وقال عطاء بن أبي رباح "يمشون على الأرض هوناً" أي حلماء. وقال ابن أبي حبيب في قوله عز وجل "وكهلا" قاله: الكهل منتهى الحلم. وقال مجاهد "وإذا مروا باللغو مروا كراما" أي إذا أوذوا صفحوا.
25:63.english: And it is said regarding His saying, the Exalted, "Rabbaniyyin" (Quran 3:79) meaning forbearing (Hulama') scholars (Ulama'). And from Al-Hasan regarding His saying, the Exalted, "And when the ignorant address them, they say: Peace (Salam)" (Quran 25:63), he said: Forbearing (Hulama') - if ignorance is shown towards them, they do not respond with ignorance. And said 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah: "They walk upon the earth humbly (Haw'nan)" (Quran 25:63) meaning forbearing (Hulama'). And said Ibn Abi Habib regarding His saying, the Mighty and Majestic, "And middle-aged (Kahilan)" (Quran 40:67), he said: The middle-aged (Al-Kahl) is the ultimate in forbearance (Al-Hilm). And said Mujahid: "And when they pass by futility, they pass by with dignity (Karam)" (Quran 25:72) meaning if they are harmed, they overlook (Safahu).
25:63.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'
