25:63.arabic: بل هؤلاء لا سلامة في مخالطتهم وإنما السلامة في الانقطاع عنهم قال الله تعالى وإذا خاطبهم الجاهلون قالوا سلاما أي سلامة و الألف بدل من الهاء ومعناه إنا سلمنا من إثمكم وأنتم سلمتم من شرنا
25:63.english: Rather, there is no safety in associating with them, and safety is only in cutting off from them. Allah the Exalted said: 'And when the ignorant address them, they say: Peace (Salam)' meaning safety, and the alif is a substitute for the ha, and its meaning is: 'We are safe from your sin, and you are safe from our harm.'
25:63.topic: Al-Ghazali on the outer and inner dimensions of worship, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

25:64.arabic: أما من الايات فقوله تعالى: ﴿ إن ربك يعلم أنك تقوم أدنى من ثلثي الليل ﴾ {} الاية وقوله تعالى: ﴿ إن ناشئة الليل هي أشد وطأ وأقوم قيلا ﴾ {} وقوله سبحانه وتعالى: ﴿ تتجافى جنوبهم عن المضاجع ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ أمن هو قانت آناء الليل ﴾ {} الآية وقوله عز وجل: ﴿ والذين يبيتون لربهم سجدا وقياما ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ واستعينوا بالصبر والصلاة ﴾ {} قيل هي قيام الليل يستعان بالصبر عليه على مجاهدة النفس.
25:64.english: As for from the verses, His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand (for prayer) nearly two-thirds of the night' (Quran 73:20) - the verse, and His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, the rising (Nash'ah) of the night is more intense in tread and more upright in speech' (Quran 73:6), and His saying, the Glorified and Exalted: 'Their sides forsake (Tatajafa) their beds' (Quran 32:16), and His saying, the Exalted: 'Is one who is devoutly obedient (Qanit) during periods of the night' (Quran 39:9) - the verse, and His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And those who spend the night for their Lord, prostrating and standing' (Quran 25:64), and His saying, the Exalted: 'And seek help through patience and prayer' (Quran 2:45) - it is said it is the standing of the night; one seeks help through patience upon it for struggling against the Soul (Nafs).
25:64.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

25:64.arabic: ثم انظر كيف وصف الفائزين من عباده وبماذا وصفهم فقال تعالى: ﴿ أمن هو قانت آناء الليل ساجدا وقائما يحذر الآخرة ويرجو رحمة ربه قل هل يستوي الذين يعلمون والذين لا يعلمون ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ تتجافى جنوبهم عن المضاجع يدعون ربهم خوفا وطمعا ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل: ﴿ والذين يبيتون لربهم سجدا وقياما ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل: ﴿ كانوا قليلا من الليل ما يهجعون وبالأسحار هم يستغفرون ﴾ {}
25:64.english: Then look at how He described the successful ones from His servants and with what He described them, so He, the Exalted, said: 'Is one who is devoutly obedient (Qanit) during periods of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord? Say, "Are those who know equal to those who do not know?"' And He, the Exalted, said: 'Their sides forsake their beds as they call upon their Lord in fear and hope.' And He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'And those who spend the night for their Lord, prostrating and standing.' And He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'They used to sleep but little of the night, and in the hours before dawn they would ask forgiveness.'
25:64.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

25:67.arabic: ومنها الإسراف في الطعام والبناء فهو منكر  بل  في  المال  منكران أحدهما الإضاعة والآخر الإسراف فالإضاعة تفويت مال بلا فائدة يعتد  بها  كإحراق الثوب وتمزيقه وهدم البناء من غير غرض وإلقاء المال في  البحر  وفي  معناه  صرف المال إلى النائحة والمطرب وفي أنواع الفساد  لأنها  فوائد  محرمة  شرعا  فصارت كالمعدومة وأما الإسراف  فقد  يطلق  لإرادة  صرف  المال  إلى  النائحة  والمطرب والمنكرات وقد يطلق  على  الصرف  إلى  المباحات  في  جنسها  ولكن  مع  المبالغة والمبالغة تختلف بالإضافة إلى الأحوال فنقول من لم يم
25:67.english: And among them is extravagance in food and building, which is reprehensible. Rather, in wealth there are two reprehensible acts: one is wastefulness and the other is extravagance. Wastefulness is squandering wealth without any benefit that is considered, like burning a garment, tearing it, demolishing a building without purpose, and throwing wealth into the sea. In its meaning is spending wealth on lamentation and entertainment and in types of corruption, because they are benefits prohibited by law, so they become as if non-existent. As for extravagance, it may be used to mean spending wealth on lamentation, entertainment, and reprehensible acts, and it may be used for spending on permissible things in their kind but with excessiveness. And excessiveness differs relative to circumstances. So we say: whoever owns only one hundred dinars, for example, and has his dependents and children with no livelihood for them except it, then spends it all on a feast, he is extravagant and must be prevented. Allah the Exalted said: 'And do not extend it all extension, so you sit blamed, destitute.' This was revealed regarding a man in Medina who distributed all his wealth and left nothing for his dependents, then was required for maintenance and could not afford anything. And Allah the Exalted said: 'And do not squander wastefully; indeed, the squanderers are brothers of the devils.' And likewise, Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: 'And those who, when they spend, are not extravagant and are not stingy, and it is between that a standing.' So whoever is extravagant with this extravagance is censured, and it is obligatory upon the judge to impose guardianship on him, except if the man is alone and has a true strength in reliance (Tawakkul), then he may spend all his wealth in paths of good. And whoever has dependents or is incapable of reliance (Tawakkul), it is not for him to give all his wealth in charity. And likewise, if he spends all his wealth on carvings of his walls and adorning his building, that is also prohibited extravagance. Doing that from one who has abundant wealth is not prohibited, because adornment is from sound purposes, and mosques have not ceased to be adorned and their doors and ceilings carved, even though carving the door and ceiling has no benefit except mere adornment, so likewise houses. And likewise the statement regarding beautification with garments and foods, that is permissible in its kind and becomes extravagance by consideration of the man's condition and wealth. And examples of these reprehensible acts are many and cannot be enumerated.
25:67.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

25:67.arabic: وجملة هذه الكلمات غير محيطة بحقيقة الجود والبخل، بل نقول: المال خلق لحكمة ومقصود وهو صلاحه لحاجات الخلق، ويمكن إمساكه عن الصرف إلى ما خلق للصرف إليه، ويمكن بذله بالصرف إلى ما لا يحسن الصرف إليه، ويمكن التصرف فيه بالعدل، وهو أن يحفظ حيث يجب الحفظ، ويبذل حيث يجب البذل. فالإمساك حيث يجب البذل بخل، والبذل حيث يجب الإمساك تبذير. وبينهما وسط وهو المحمود وينبغي أن يكون السخاء والجود عبارة عنه؛ إذ لم يؤمر رسول الله ﭬ إلا بالسخاء، وقد قيل له "ولا تجعل يدك مغلولة إلى عنقك ولا تبسطها كل البسط" وقال تعالى "
25:67.english: The totality of these words does not encompass the reality of generosity (al-Jood) and miserliness (al-Bukhl), rather we say: Wealth is created for a wisdom and purpose, which is its suitability for the needs of creation, and it is possible to withhold it from spending on what it was created to be spent on, and it is possible to give it by spending on what is not proper to spend on, and it is possible to manage it with justice (al-Adl), which is to preserve where preservation is obligatory, and to give where giving is obligatory. So withholding where giving is obligatory is miserliness, and giving where withholding is obligatory is wastefulness. Between them is a middle path which is praiseworthy, and it is appropriate that generosity (al-Sakhaa') and generosity (al-Jood) be an expression of it; for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was not commanded except with generosity, and it was said to him: 'And do not make your hand chained to your neck nor stretch it forth to the utmost limit' (Quran 17:29), and Allah the Exalted said: 'And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy, and there is a firmness between that' (Quran 25:67). So generosity (al-Jood) is the middle between extravagance (al-Israaf) and stinginess (al-Iqtar) and between stretching forth (al-BasT) and holding back (al-QabD), and it is to measure his giving and withholding according to what is obligatory, and it is not sufficient that he does that with his limbs unless his heart (al-Qalb) is content with it, not disputing him in it. For if he gives in a place where giving is obligatory and his soul (al-Nafs) disputes him and he endures it, he is forcing himself and is not generous, rather it should be that his heart (al-Qalb) has no connection with wealth except from where wealth is intended for him, which is spending it on what it is obligatory to spend it on.
25:67.book_title: Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth
25:67.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

25:67.arabic: والذي يدل على أن المطلوب هو الوسط في الأخلاق دون الطرفين أن السخاء خلق محمود شرعاً، وهو وسط بين طرفي التبذير والتقتير. وقد أثنى الله تعالى عليه فقال "والذين إذا أنفقوا لم يسرفوا ولم يقتروا وكان بين ذلك قواما" وقال تعالى "ولا تجعل يدك مغلولة إلى عنقك ولا تبسطها كل البسط" وكذلك المطلوب في شهوة الطعام الاعتدال دون الشره والجمود قال الله تعالى "وكلوا واشربوا ولا تسرفوا إنه لا يحب المسرفين" وقال في الغضب "أشداء على الكفار رحماء بينهم" وقال ﭬ "خير الأمور أوساطها" وهذا له سر وتحقيق وهو أن السعادة منوطة
25:67.english: And what indicates that what is sought is the middle path in character traits without the two extremes is that generosity is a praiseworthy trait religiously, and it is a middle between the two extremes of wastefulness and stinginess. And Allah the Exalted praised it by saying: "And those who, when they spend, are neither wasteful nor stingy, and there is a balance between that." And He said: "And do not make your hand chained to your neck nor extend it completely." Likewise, what is sought in the appetite for food is moderation without greed and rigidity. Allah said: "And eat and drink and do not be wasteful, indeed He does not love the wasteful." And He said regarding anger: "Severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves." And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "The best of matters are their middle ones." This has a secret and verification, which is that happiness is tied to the soundness of the Heart (Qalb) from the afflictions of this world. Allah said: "Except he who comes to Allah with a sound Heart (Qalb)." And stinginess is from the afflictions of the worldly life, and wastefulness is also from the afflictions of the worldly life, and the condition of the Heart (Qalb) is that it be sound from both of them, meaning it is not attentive to wealth nor is it eager to spend it nor to withhold it, for the one eager to spend has his Heart (Qalb) diverted to spending just as the one eager to withhold has his Heart (Qalb) diverted to withholding. So the perfection of the Heart (Qalb) is that it be purified from both descriptions altogether. And if that is not attainable in this world, we seek what is most similar to the absence of both descriptions and farthest from the extremes, which is the middle, for the lukewarm is neither hot nor cold but rather a middle between them, so it is as if it is free from both descriptions. So likewise generosity is between wastefulness and stinginess. And courage is between cowardice and recklessness. And chastity is between greed and rigidity. And likewise all other character traits, for both extremes of matters are blameworthy.
25:67.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

25:68.arabic: وقال ﭬ "يخرج من النار عنق له أذنان تسمعان وعينان تبصران ولسان ينطق يقول: وكلت بثلاثة: بكل جبار عنيد وبكل من دعا مع الله إلهاً آخر وبالمصورين"[7] وقال ﭬ "لا يدخل الجنة بخيل ولا جبار ولا سيئ الملكة"[8] وقال ﭬ "تحاجت الجنة والنار فقالت النار: أوثرت بالمتكبرين والمتجبرين، وقالت الجنة: ما لي لا يدخلني إلا ضعفاء الناس وسقاطهم وعجزتهم؟ فقال الله للجنة: إنما أنت رحمتي أرحم بك من أشاء من عبادي، وقال للنار: إنما أنت عذابي أعذب بك من أشاء ولكل واحدة منكما ملؤها"[9] وقال ﭬ "بئس العبد عبد تجبر واعتدى ونسى ال
25:68.english: And He (the Prophet) said: "There will emerge from the Fire a neck having two ears that hear and two eyes that see and a tongue that speaks saying: I have been entrusted with three: with every arrogant obstinate one and with everyone who calls upon with Allah another god and with the image-makers." [7] And He said: "The miser, nor the arrogant one, nor the one of bad character will not enter Paradise." [8] And He said: "Paradise and the Fire argued, so the Fire said: I have been favored with the arrogant ones and the tyrants, and Paradise said: Why is it that none enters me except the weak of the people and their lowly ones and their incapable ones? So Allah said to Paradise: You are only My mercy, I show mercy with you to whom I will from My servants, and He said to the Fire: You are only My punishment, I punish with you whom I will, and for each one of you is its fill." [9] And He said: "Wretched is the servant, a servant who acts arrogantly and transgresses and forgets the Supreme Almighty (Al-Jabbar Al-A'la), wretched is the servant, a servant who acts arrogantly and is proud and forgets the Great Most High (Al-Kabir Al-Muta'al), wretched is the servant, a servant who is heedless and negligent and forgets the graves and decay, wretched is the servant, a servant who is insolent and oppresses and forgets the beginning and the end." [10] And from Thabit that he said: It reached us that it was said: O Messenger of Allah, how great is the arrogance of so-and-so! So He said: "Is there not after it death?" [11] And Abdullah bin Amr said: Indeed the Messenger of Allah said: "When death approached Nuh (Noah) upon him peace, he called his two sons and said: I command you with two and I forbid you from two, I forbid you from polytheism (shirk) and arrogance (kibr), and I command you with 'There is no god but Allah.' For if the heavens and the earths and what is in them were placed in one scale of the balance and 'There is no god but Allah' were placed in the other scale, it would outweigh them, and if the heavens and the earths and what is in them were a ring and were placed
25:68.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

25:72.arabic: وقال مجاهد "وإذا مروا باللغو مروا كراما" أي إذا أوذوا صفحوا. وروي أن ابن مسعود مر بلغو معرضاً فقال رسول الله ﷺ "أصبح ابن مسعود وأمسى كريماً"[47] ثم تلا إبراهيم بن ميسرة وهو الراوي قوله تعالى "وإذا مروا باللغو مروا كراما"
25:72.english: And Mujahid said regarding His saying (Exalted is He) "And when they pass by idle talk, they pass by with dignity" meaning: if they are harmed, they overlook it. And it was narrated that Ibn Mas'ud passed by idle talk while turning away, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said "Ibn Mas'ud has become and remained noble". Then Ibrahim bin Maysarah, who is the narrator, recited the saying of Allah (Exalted is He) "And when they pass by idle talk, they pass by with dignity".
25:72.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

25:72.arabic: وقال مجاهد "وإذا مروا باللغو مروا كراما" أي إذا أوذوا صفحوا.
25:72.english: And Mujahid said regarding His saying, the Exalted, 'And when they pass by futility, they pass by with dignity (karāmā)' meaning: when they are harmed, they overlook it.
25:72.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

25:74.arabic: وقال تعالى في وصف الرسل ومدحهم (ولقد أرسلنا رسلا من قبلك وجعلنا لهم أزواجا وذرية) فذكر ذلك في معرض الامتنان وإظهار الفضل ومدح أولياءه بسؤال ذلك في الدعاء فقال (والذين يقولون ربنا هب لنا من أزواجنا وذرياتنا قرة أعين) الآية ويقال إن الله تعالى لم يذكر في كتابه من الأنبياء إلا المتأهلين فقالوا إن يحيى صلى الله عليه وسلم قد تزوج ولم يجامع قيل إنما فعل ذلك لنيل الفضل وإقامة السنة وقيل لغض البصر وأما عيسى عليه السلام فإنه سينكح إذا نزل الأرض ويولد له.
25:74.english: And Allah the Exalted said in describing the Messengers and praising them: 'And We have sent messengers before you and made for them spouses and offspring' (Quran 43:6). He mentioned that in the context of bestowing favor and showing excellence, and He praised His allies by asking for that in supplication, so He said: 'And those who say: Our Lord, grant us from our spouses and our offspring comfort of eyes (Qurrat A'yun), and make us leaders for the righteous (Imam lil-Muttaqin)' (Quran 25:74). And it is said that Allah the Exalted did not mention in His Book from the prophets except those who were married. They said: Indeed, Yahya (John) peace be upon him married but did not have intercourse; it is said he did that only to attain excellence and establish the Sunnah (tradition), and it is said for lowering the gaze. As for 'Isa (Jesus) peace be upon him, he will marry when he descends to the earth and will have children.
25:74.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

26:12.arabic: فكذلك الانبساط والإدلال يحتمل من بعض العباد دون بعض. فمن انبساط الأنس قول موسى عليه السلام: "إن هي إلا فتنتك تضل بها من تشاء وتهدي من تشاء" وقوله في التعليل والاعتذار لما قيل له: "اذهب إلى فرعون"، فقال: "ولهم على ذنب" وقوله: "إني أخاف أن يكذبون ويضيق صدري ولا ينطلق لساني"، وقوله: "إننا نخاف أن يفرط علينا أو أن يطغى" وهذا من غير موسى عليه السلام من سوء الأدب لأن الذي أقيم مقام الأنس يلاطف ويحتمل، ولم يحتمل ليونس عليه السلام ما دون هذا لما أقيم مقام القبض والهيبة، فعوقب بالسجن في بطن الحوت - في ظل
26:12.english: Similarly, expansion (Inbisat) and familiarity (Idlal) are permissible for some worshippers but not others. Among the expansion of intimacy (Unsi) is the saying of Moses, peace be upon him: "It is only Your trial by which You misguide whom You will and guide whom You will" and his saying in explanation and excuse when he was told: "Go to Pharaoh," so he said: "And they have upon me a sin" and his saying: "Indeed, I fear that they will deny me and my chest will tighten and my tongue will not be released" and his saying: "Indeed, we fear that he will hasten against us or that he will transgress." And this from other than Moses, peace be upon him, would be bad manners (Su' al-Adab) because the one who is established in the station of intimacy (Maqam al-Unsi) is indulged and tolerated, and it was not tolerated for Jonah, peace be upon him, what is less than this because he was established in the station of contraction (Maqam al-Qabd) and awe (Hibah), so he was punished with imprisonment in the belly of the whale - in three darknesses - and he was called out to until the Day of Resurrection: "Had it not been that a favor from his Lord reached him, he would have been thrown onto the naked shore while he was blameworthy."
26:12.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

26:23.arabic: وقال تعالى في قصة فرعون وما رب العالمين إلى قوله أولوا جئتك بشيء مبين
26:23.english: And He (Allah) said in the story of Pharaoh: 'And what is the Lord (Rabb) of the worlds?' up to His saying: 'Would that you had come to me with something clear?'
26:23.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Foundations of Belief'

26:42.arabic: فالعلاج الاول يضاهي اطماع المصارع بالخلعة عند الغلبة ووعده بأنواع الكرامة كما وعد فرعون سحرته عند إغرائه اياهم بموسى حيث قال ﭬ ﴿ وانكم اذا لمن المقربين ﴾  {} والثاني يضاهي تعويد الصبي الذي يراد منه المصارعة والمقاتلة بمباشرة اسباب ذلك منذ الصبا حتى يأنس به ويستجرىء عليه وتقوى فيه منته
26:42.english: The first treatment resembles tempting the wrestler with the robe of honor upon victory and promising him various honors, as Pharaoh promised his magicians when enticing them against Moses, where He said: 'And indeed you will then be among those brought near (al-Muqarrabīn).' The second resembles habituating the child who is intended for wrestling and fighting by directly engaging in its causes from childhood until he becomes accustomed to it and becomes bold in it, and his strength in it increases.
26:42.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

26:49.arabic: وما مثال المكاشفين والمعتقدين إلا كسحرة فرعون مع أصحاب السامري؛ فإن سحرة فرعون لما كانوا مطلعين على منتهى تأثير السحر لطول مشاهدتهم وتجربتهم رأوا من موسى عليه السلام ما جاوز حدود السحر وانكشف لهم حقيقة الأمر فلم يكترثوا بقول فرعون "لأقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف" بل "قالوا لن نؤثرك على ما جاءنا من البينات والذي فطرنا فاقض ما أنت قاض إنما تقضي هذه الحياة الدنيا" فإن البيان والكشف يمنع التغيير وأما أصحاب السامري لما كان إيمانهم عن النظر إلى ظاهر الثعبان، فلما نظروا إلى عجل السامري وسمعوا خواره تغير
26:49.english: And the example of those who have spiritual unveiling (Mukāshifīn) and those who merely believe (Muʿtaqidīn) is nothing but like the magicians of Pharaoh with the companions of the Samiri; for the magicians of Pharaoh, since they were aware of the ultimate effect of magic due to their prolonged witnessing and experience, saw from Moses (peace be upon him) what exceeded the limits of magic and the truth of the matter was unveiled to them, so they did not heed Pharaoh's saying "I will cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides" but rather "they said: 'We will never prefer you over what has come to us of clear proofs and He who created us. So decree whatever you are to decree. You can only decree for this worldly life.'" For clarity and unveiling prevent change. As for the companions of the Samiri, since their faith was from looking at the outward appearance of the serpent, when they looked at the calf of the Samiri and heard its lowing, they changed and heard his saying "This is your god and the god of Moses" and forgot that it does not respond to them with speech nor possesses for them harm or benefit: thus everyone who believes by looking at a serpent will inevitably disbelieve if he looks at a calf, because both are from the world of witnessing (ʿĀlam al-Shahādah) and difference and opposition in the world of witnessing is abundant. As for the world of the dominion (ʿĀlam al-Malakūt), it is from God the Exalted, therefore we do not find in it any difference or opposition at all.
26:49.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

26:80.arabic: الحمد لله المنفرد بالجلال في كبريائه وتعاليه، المستحق للتحميد والتقديس والتسبيح والتنزيه، القائم بالعدل فيما يبرمه ويقضيه، المتطول بالفضل فيما ينعم به ويسديه، المتكفل بحفظ عبده في جميع موارده ومجاريه، المنعم عليه بما يزيد على مهمات مقاصده بل بما يفي بأمانيه، فهو الذي يرشده ويهديه، وهو الذي يميتُه ويحييه، وإذا مرض فهو يشفيه، وإذا ضعف فهو يقويه، وهو الذي يوفقه للطاعة ويرتضيه، وهو الذي يطعمه ويسقيه، ويحفظه من الهلاك ويحميه، ويحرسه بالطعام والشراب عما يهلكه ويرديه، ويمكنه من القناعة بقليل القوت ويقر
26:80.english: Praise be to Allah, the One Alone in Majesty in His greatness and exaltation, deserving of praise, sanctification, glorification, and transcendence, the One who establishes justice in what He decrees and judges, the One who extends favor in what He bestows and grants, the One who undertakes the protection of His servant in all his sources and courses, the One who bestows upon him what exceeds the necessities of his aims but rather fulfills his hopes, so He is the One who guides him and directs him, and He is the One who causes him to die and gives him life, and when he is sick, He heals him, and when he is weak, He strengthens him, and He is the One who grants him success in obedience and approves of him, and He is the One who feeds him and gives him drink, and protects him from destruction and safeguards him, and guards him with food and drink from what destroys him and ruins him, and enables him with contentment with little sustenance and brings him near until the pathways of Satan who opposes him become narrow for him, and breaks with it the desire of the Soul (Nafs) which opposes him, so he repels its evil then worships his Lord and fears Him, this after He expands upon him what he delights in and desires, and increases upon him what stirs his motives and confirms his urges, all of that He tests him with and tries him, so He observes how he prefers it over what he loves and chooses, and how he preserves His commands and refrains from His prohibitions, and persists in His obedience and abstains from His disobedience.
26:80.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Harms of the Tongue'

26:88.arabic: يوم لا ينطقون ولا يؤذن لهم فيعتذرون يوم لا مرد له من الله يوم هم بارزون ويوم هم على النار يفتنون يوم لا ينفع مال ولا بنون يوم لا ينفع الظالمين معذرتهم ولهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار يوم ترد فيه المعاذير وتبلى السرائر وتظهر الضمائر وتكشف الأستار يوم تخشع فيه الأبصار وتسكن الأصوات ويقل فيه الالتفات وتبرز الخفيات وتظهر الخطيئات يوم يساق العباد ومعهم الأشهاد ويشيب الصغير ويسكر الكبير فيومئذ وضعت الموازين ونشرت الدواوين وبرزت الجحيم وأغلى الحميم وزفرت النار ويئس الكفار وسعرت النيران وتغيرت الألوان وخرس ا
26:88.english: A day when they will not speak nor be permitted to offer excuses, a day when there is no turning back from Allah, a day when they are exposed, and a day when they are tested over the Fire, a day when wealth will not benefit nor children, a day when the excuses of the wrongdoers will not benefit them, and for them is the curse and for them is the evil abode, a day when excuses are returned, secrets are tested, consciences are revealed, and veils are uncovered, a day when gazes are humbled, voices are silenced, turning away is diminished, hidden things are exposed, and sins are made apparent, a day when the servants are driven forth with their witnesses, the young turn gray-haired, and the old become intoxicated. Then on that day, the scales are set up, the records are spread out, Hellfire is made manifest, the boiling water is heated, the Fire blazes, the disbelievers despair, the fires are kindled, colors change, the tongue is silenced, and the limbs of the human being speak. O human being, what has deluded you concerning your Generous Lord, when the doors are closed, the curtains are lowered, and you are concealed from the creatures, yet you commit immorality? So what will you do when your limbs bear witness against you? So woe, all woe to us, the heedless ones.
26:88.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

26:89.arabic: وقد قرأ أبو سليمان قوله تعالى: " إلا من أتى الله بقلبٍ سليم " فقال: هو القلب الذي ليس فيه غير الله تعالى وقال: إنما زهدوا الدنيا لتفرغ قلوبهم من همومها للآخرة، فهذا بيان انقسام الزهد بالإضافة إلى أصناف المزهود فيه؛
26:89.english: And Abu Sulayman recited the saying of the Exalted: "Except he who comes to Allah with a sound heart (Qalb Salim)" and said: It is the heart (Qalb) in which there is nothing other than Allah the Exalted, and said: They only abstained from the world (Zuhd) to empty their hearts (Qalb) from its concerns for the Hereafter (Akhirah), and this is an explanation of the division of abstention (Zuhd) in relation to the categories of what is abstained from;
26:89.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

26:202.arabic: الحمد لله الذي لا يتكل على عفوه ورحمته إلا الراجون، ولا يحذر سوء غضبه وسطوته إلا الخائفون، الذي استدرج عباده من حيث لا يعلمون، وسلط عليهم الشهوات وأمرهم بترك ما يشتهون، وابتلاهم بالغضب وكلفهم كظم الغيظ فيما يغضبون، ثم حفهم بالمكاره واللذات وأملى لهم لينظر كيف يعملون، وامتحن بهم حبهم ليعلم صدقهم فيما يدعون، وعرفهم أنه لا يخفى عليه شيء مما يسرون وما يعلنون، وحذرهم أن يأخذهم بغتة وهم لا يشعرون فقال "ما ينظرون إلا صيحة واحدة تأخذهم وهم يخصمون فلا يستطيعون توصية ولا إلى أهلهم يرجعون" والصلاة والسلام
26:202.english: Praise be to Allah, upon whose forgiveness (ʿafw) and mercy (raḥmah) none rely except the hopeful (al-rājūn), and none fear the evil of His anger (ghaḍab) and His might except the fearful (al-khāʾifūn), who leads His servants astray from where they do not know, and subjects them to desires (shahawāt) and commands them to abandon what they desire, and tests them with anger (ghaḍab) and obliges them to suppress rage (kaẓm al-ghayẓ) in what angers them, then surrounds them with hardships and pleasures and grants them respite to see how they act, and tests them with their love to know their truthfulness in what they claim, and makes known to them that nothing is hidden from Him of what they conceal and what they reveal, and warns them that He may seize them suddenly while they are unaware, saying: "They await not but a single blast which will seize them while they are disputing. Then they will not be able to make a bequest, nor will they return to their families." And prayers and peace be upon Muhammad, His messenger, under whose banner the prophets march, and upon his family and his companions, the guided leaders (al-aʾimmah al-mahdiyyīn), and the pleased masters (al-sādah al-marḍiyyīn), prayers equal in number to what has been of Allah's creation and what will be, and may the first and the last attain its blessing, and grant abundant peace.
26:202.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

26:212.arabic: وأما الجاحدون والغافلون والمغترون بلامع السراب من زهرة الدنيا فإنهم لا يبصرون ولا يسمعون لأنهم عن السمع معزولون وعن آيات ربهم محجوبون يعلمون ظاهرا من الحياة الدنيا وهم عن الآخرة هم غافلون وما أريد بالسمع السمع الظاهر فإن الذين أريدوا به ما كانوا معزولين عنه وإنما أريد به السمع الباطن ولا يدرك بالسمع الظاهر إلا الأصوات ويشارك الإنسان فيه سائر الحيوانات فأما السمع الباطن فيدرك به لسان الحال الذي هو نطق وراء نطق المقال
26:212.english: As for the deniers (al-Jāhidūn) and the heedless (al-Ghāfilūn) and those deceived by the shimmering mirage of the world's adornment, they do not see and they do not hear because they are prevented from hearing (maʿzūlūn ʿan al-samʿ) and veiled from the signs of their Lord. They know the outward aspect of worldly life, and they are heedless of the Hereafter. And what is intended by 'hearing' is not the outward hearing, for those intended by it were not prevented from that. Rather, what is intended is the inward hearing (al-samʿ al-bāṭin). With the outward hearing, only sounds are perceived, and in this, humans share with all other animals. As for the inward hearing, through it is perceived the language of the state (lisān al-ḥāl), which is an utterance beyond the utterance of speech.
26:212.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Etiquette of Travel'

26:213.arabic: وقال ﭬ "يخرج من النار عنق له أذنان تسمعان وعينان تبصران ولسان ينطق يقول: وكلت بثلاثة: بكل جبار عنيد وبكل من دعا مع الله إلهاً آخر وبالمصورين"[7]
26:213.english: And He (the Prophet) said: "There will emerge from the Fire a neck having two ears that hear and two eyes that see and a tongue that speaks, saying: I have been entrusted with three: with every arrogant obstinate one and with everyone who calls upon with Allah another god and with the image-makers."
26:213.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

26:215.arabic: فالعلم من أعظم ما يتكبر به، ولذلك قال تعالى لنبيه عليه السلام "واخفض جناحك لمن اتبعك من المؤمنين" وقال عز وجل "ولو كنت فظاً غليظ القلب لانفضوا من حولك" ووصف أولياءه فقال "أذلة على المؤمنين أعزة على الكافرين" وكذلك قال ﭬ فيما رواه العباس رضي الله عنه "يكون قوم يقرؤون القرآن لا يجاور حناجرهم يقولون: قد قرأنا القرآن فمن أقرأ منها ومن أعلم منها" ثم التفت إلى أصحابه وقال "أولئك منكم أيها الأمة أولئك هم وقود النار"[51] ولذلك قال عمر رضي الله عنه لا تكونوا جبابرة العلماء فلا يفي علمكم بجهلكم.
26:215.english: Knowledge is among the greatest things through which one becomes arrogant, and therefore Allah the Exalted said to His Prophet (peace be upon him): "And lower your wing (i.e., be humble and gentle) for those who follow you from among the believers (Mu'minin)." And He the Almighty said: "And if you had been rude [in speech] and harsh in heart (Qalb), they would have dispersed from around you." And He described His allies (Awliya') saying: "Humble (Adhillah) towards the believers, mighty (A'izzah) towards the disbelievers." And likewise, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said in what was narrated by Al-'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him): "There will be a people who recite the Quran, it does not go beyond their throats; they say: 'We have recited the Quran, so who is more reciting than us and who is more knowledgeable than us?'" Then he turned to his companions and said: "Those are from among you, O Ummah; those are the fuel of the Fire." [51] And therefore, 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Do not be tyrants (Jababirah) of the scholars, lest your knowledge not suffice against your ignorance."
26:215.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

26:215.arabic: ولو كان الله سبحانه وتعالى يرضى لك ذلك لما قال لنبيه ﷺ 'واخفض جناحك لمن اتبعك من المؤمنين' وهؤلاء الذين يظهر أثر الكبر على شمائلهم فأحوالهم أخف حالاً ممن هو في الرتبة الثالثة وهو الذي يظهر الكبر على لسانه حتى يدعوه إلى الدعوى والمفاخرة والمباهاة وتزكية النفس وحكايات الأحوال والمقامات والتشمر لغلبة الغير في العلم والعمل.
26:215.english: And if Allah, the Exalted and Glorified, were pleased with that for you, He would not have said to His Prophet (peace be upon him): 'And lower your wing (i.e., show humility and gentleness) for those who follow you from among the believers.' And these are those upon whose outward demeanor the effect of arrogance appears, so their condition is lighter than the one in the third rank, who is the one who manifests arrogance upon his tongue until it calls him to claim, boasting, vainglory, self-purification (Tazkiyah al-Nafs), narrations of states (Ahwal) and stations (Maqamat), and striving to overcome others in knowledge and action.
26:215.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

26:216.arabic: وهذا التحقيق وهو أن الصداقة لحمة كلحمة النسب و القريب لا يجوز أن يهجر بالمعصية ولذلك قال الله تعالى لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم في عشيرته فإن عصوك فقل إني بريء مما تعملون ولم يقل أني بريء منكم مراعاة لحق القرابة ولحمة النسب
26:216.english: And this verification is that friendship is a bond like the bond of kinship, and the relative should not be abandoned due to sin. Therefore, Allah the Exalted said to His Prophet (peace be upon him) regarding his kin: 'If they disobey you, then say: Indeed, I am innocent of what you do.' And He did not say: 'I am innocent of you,' out of consideration for the right of kinship and the bond of lineage.
26:216.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

26:218.arabic: وقال عكرمة في قوله عز وجل: ﴿ الذي يراك حين تقوم وتقلبك في الساجدين ﴾ قال قيامه وركوعه وسجوده وجلوسه. وأما الركوع والسجود فينبغي أن تجدد عندهما ذكر كبرياء الله سبحانه وترفع يديك مستجيرا بعفو الله عز وجل من عقابه بتجديد نية ومتبعا سنة نبيه ﭬ ثم تستأنف له ذلا وتواضعا بركوعك وتجتهد في ترقيق قلبك وتجديد خشوعك وتستشعر ذلك وعز مولاك واتضاعك وعلو ربك وتستعين على تقرير ذلك في قلبك بلسانك فتسبح ربك وتشهد له بالعظمة وأنه أعظم من كل عظيم وتكرر ذلك على قلبك لتؤكده بالتكرار ثم ترتفع من ركوعك راجيا أنه راحم لك
26:218.english: And 'Ikrimah said regarding His Exalted statement: 'The One Who sees you when you stand and your turning among those who prostrate' (Quran 26:218-219), he said: 'His standing, bowing, prostration, and sitting.' As for the bowing and prostration, you should renew at them the remembrance (Dhikr) of the greatness of Allah, the Exalted, and raise your hands seeking refuge in the forgiveness of Allah, the Exalted, from His punishment by renewing intention and following the tradition (Sunnah) of His Prophet (peace be upon him). Then you begin for Him with humility and submission in your bowing, and strive to soften your heart (Qalb) and renew your reverence (Khushu'), and feel that and the might of your Master and your lowliness and the loftiness of your Lord, and you seek help in affirming that in your heart (Qalb) with your tongue, so you glorify your Lord and testify to Him of greatness and that He is greater than every great one, and you repeat that upon your heart (Qalb) to confirm it with repetition. Then you rise from your bowing hoping that He is merciful to you and confirming the hope in yourself by saying: 'Allah hears the one who praises Him,' meaning He responds to the one who thanks Him. Then you follow that thanks which demands increase, so you say: 'Our Lord, to You is praise,' and increase the praise by saying: 'As much as fills the heavens and the earth.' Then you descend to the prostration, which is the highest degrees of submission, so you place the noblest of your limbs, which is the face, upon the lowliest of things, which is the dust. And if it is possible for you not to place a barrier between them, so prostrate on the ground, then do so, for it is more conducive to reverence (Khushu') and more indicative of humility. And when you place yourself in the position of humility, know that you have placed it in its place and returned the branch to its origin, for you were created from dust and to it you return. At this, renew upon your heart (Qalb) the greatness of Allah and say: 'Glory be to my Lord, the Most High,' and confirm it with repetition, for the repetition...
26:218.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

26:218.arabic: فأنشأ يقول صغير هواك عذبني فكيف به إذا احتنكا وأنت جمعت في قلبي هوى قد كان مشتركا أما ترثى لمكتئب إذا ضحك الخلى بكى فقام ذو النون وسقط على وجهه ثم قام رجل آخر فقال ذو النون الذي يراك حين تقوم فجلس ذلك الرجل وكان ذلك اطلاعا من ذي النون على قلبه أنه متكلف متواجد فعرفه أن الذي يراه حين يقوم هو الخصم في قيامه لغير الله تعالى ولو كان الرجل صادقا لما جلس
26:218.english: He began to say: 'Small was your love, it tormented me, so how about when it becomes intense? And you have gathered in my heart (Qalb) a love that was shared. Do you not have mercy on a depressed one when the empty one laughs, he cries?' Then Dhu al-Nun stood up and fell on his face. Then another man stood up and said: 'Dhu al-Nun, the One Who sees you when you stand (Qiyam).' That man sat down, and that was an unveiling (Ittila') from Dhu al-Nun upon his heart (Qalb) that he was pretentious and affected. So he made him know that the One Who sees him when he stands (Qiyam) is the adversary in his standing (Qiyam) for other than Allah the Exalted. And if the man had been truthful, he would not have sat down.
26:218.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

26:218.arabic: فإذا خطرت فعلاجها أن يتذكر أن الناس لو عرفوا نفاقه في الباطن واطلعوا على ضميره لمقتوه، وإن الله مطلع على ضميره وهو له أشد مقتاً، كما روي عن ذي النون رحمه الله أنه قام وزعق، فقام معه شيخ آخر رأى فيه أثر التكلف فقال يا شيخ! الذي يراك حين تقوم؟ فجلس الشيخ وكل ذلك من أعمال المنافقين.
26:218.english: If these [thoughts] occur, their treatment is to remember that if people knew his hypocrisy in the inner self (Batin) and became aware of his conscience (Damir), they would despise him, and indeed Allah is aware of his conscience (Damir) and He despises him more severely. As narrated about Dhun-Nun, may Allah have mercy on him, that he stood up and cried out, so another elder stood up with him who saw in him the effect of affectation (Takalluf) and said: O elder! The One Who sees you when you stand? So the elder sat down, and all of that is from the deeds of the hypocrites (Munafiqun).
26:218.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

26:224.arabic: وأما الأشعار فتكثيرها في المواعظ مذموم قال الله تعالى والشعراء يتبعهم الغاوون ألم تر أنهم في كل واد يهيمون وقال تعالى وما علمناه الشعر وما ينبغي له وأكثر ما اعتاده الوعاظ من الأشعار ما يتعلق بالتواصف في العشق وجمال المعشوق وروح الوصال وألم الفراق والمجلس لا يحوى إلا أجلاف العوام وبواطنهم مشحونة بالشهوات وقلوبهم غير منفكة عن الالتفات إلى الصور المليحة فلا تحرك الأشعار من قلوبهم إلا ما هو مستكن فيها فتشتعل فيها نيران الشهوات فيزعقون ويتواجدون وأكثر ذلك أو كله يرجع إلى نوع فساد فلا ينبغي أن يستعمل
26:224.english: As for poetry, its abundance in admonitions is blameworthy. Allah the Exalted said: 'And the poets - the deviators follow them; Do you not see that in every valley they wander?' (Quran 26:224-225) And He said: 'And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it befitting for him.' (Quran 36:69) Most of what preachers have accustomed themselves to from poetry relates to mutual description in passionate love (al-'ishq) and the beauty of the beloved and the spirit (ruh) of union and the pain of separation. The gathering contains only the coarse common people, and their inner selves (bawatin) are filled with lusts, and their hearts (qulub) are not detached from turning attention to beautiful images. So poetry does not stir from their hearts except what lies hidden within them, thus igniting in them the fires of lusts, so they cry out and experience ecstatic states. Most or all of that returns to a type of corruption. So it is not appropriate to use from poetry except what contains admonition or wisdom on the basis of citation and familiarity. And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, in poetry there is wisdom.'
26:224.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

27:14.arabic: ثم كان منهم من منعه الكبر عن الفكر والمعرفة فجهل كونه ﭬ محقاً، ومنهم من عرف ومنعه الكبر عن الاعتراف قال الله تعالى مخبراً عنهم "فلما جاءهم ما عرفوا كفروا به" وقال "وجحدوا بها واستيقنتها أنفسهم ظلماً وعلوا" وهذا الكبر قريب من التكبر على الله عز وجل وإن كان دونه، ولكنه تكبر على قبول أمر الله والتواضع لرسوله.
27:14.english: Then among them were those whom arrogance prevented from reflection and knowledge, so they were ignorant of his (peace be upon him) being truthful; and among them were those who knew but arrogance prevented them from acknowledgment. Allah the Exalted said, informing about them: "And when came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it" and said: "And they denied them while their souls (Anfus) were convinced of them, out of wrongdoing and arrogance." And this arrogance is close to arrogance against Allah the Mighty and Majestic, even if it is less than it, but it is arrogance against accepting the command of Allah and humbling oneself to His Messenger.
27:14.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

27:25.arabic: ومن لا يطلع على أسرار باطنه وخبائث صفاته لا يقدر على تطهير القلب منها وإنما السفر هو الذي يسفر عن أخلاق الرجال وبه يخرج الله الخبء في السماوات والأرض وإنما سمى السفر سفرا لأنه يسفر عن الأخلاق ولذلك قال عمر رضي الله عنه للذي زكى عنده بعض الشهود هل صحبته في السفر الذي يستدل به على مكارم أخلاقه فقال لا فقال ما أراك تعرفه وكان بشر يقول يا معشر القراء سيحوا تطيبوا فإن الماء إذا ساح طاب وإذا طال مقامه في موضع تغير وبالجملة فإن النفس في الوطن مع مواتاة الأسباب لا تظهر خبائث أخلاقها لاستئناسها بما يوافق
27:25.english: And whoever does not become aware of the secrets of his inner self (Batin) and the hidden evils (Khuba'ith) of his traits cannot purify the Heart (Qalb) from them. Indeed, travel is what reveals the character of men, and through it Allah brings forth the hidden (Al-Khab') in the heavens and the earth. Travel is only called travel (Safar) because it reveals (Yusfiru) character. Therefore, Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said to the one who praised some witnesses before him: 'Have you accompanied him on the journey by which one discerns the noble traits of his character?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'I do not think you know him.' And Bishr used to say: 'O community of reciters, travel so that you may become pure, for when water flows (Saha), it becomes pure, and if it remains long in one place, it changes.' In summary, the Soul (Nafs) in the homeland, with the facilitation of means, does not manifest the hidden evils (Khuba'ith) of its character due to its familiarity with what agrees with its nature from accustomed habits. When it bears the hardship of travel and is diverted from its accustomed habits, and is tested by the difficulties of being a stranger, its hidden dangers are uncovered, and the recognition of its faults occurs, so one can then engage in treating them.
27:25.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Etiquette of Travel'

27:40.arabic: وقال تعالى: ﴿قل كفى بالله شهيدا بيني وبينكم ومن عنده علم الكتاب﴾ وقال تعالى: ﴿قال الذي عنده علم من الكتاب أنا آتيك به﴾ تنبيها على أنه اقتدر بقوة العلم.
27:40.english: And He, the Exalted, said: 'Say: Sufficient is Allah as a witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Book (ʿilm al-Kitāb)' (Quran 13:43). And He, the Exalted, said: 'Said the one who had knowledge from the Book (ʿilm min al-Kitāb): I will bring it to you' (Quran 27:40) – alerting that he was empowered by the strength of knowledge (ʿilm).
27:40.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Knowledge'

27:50.arabic: وقد حذر الله تعالى من مكره واستدراجه فقال "فلا يأمن مكر الله إلا القوم الخاسرون" وقال تعالى "ومكروا مكراً ومكرنا مكراً وهم لا يشعرون" وقال عز وجل "ومكروا ومكر الله والله خير الماكرين" وقال تعالى "إنهم يكيدون كيداً وأكيد كيداً فمهل الكافرين أمهلهم رويداً" فكما لا يجوز للعبد المهمل أن يستدل بإهمال السيد إياه وتمكينه من النعم على حب السيد، بل ينبغي أن يحذر أن يكون ذلك مكراً منه وكيداً مع أن السيد لم يحذره مكر نفسه، فبأن يجب ذلك في حق الله تعالى مع تحذيره استدراجه أولى، فإذن من أمن مكر الله فهو مغتر
27:50.english: And Allah the Exalted has warned of His plotting (makr) and gradual entrapment (istidrāj), saying: 'So none feels secure from the plotting (makr) of Allah except the losing people.' And He said: 'And they plotted a plot, and We plotted a plot, while they were not aware.' And the Mighty and Majestic said: 'And they plotted, and Allah plotted, and Allah is the best of plotters.' And He said: 'Indeed, they plan a plan, and I plan a plan. So give the disbelievers respite; give them respite a little.' So just as it is not permissible for the negligent servant to infer from the master's neglect of him and enabling him with blessings that the master loves him, rather he should be cautious that this might be plotting (makr) and scheming from him, even though the master did not warn him of his own plotting (makr), then how much more must this be in the case of Allah the Exalted with His warning of His gradual entrapment (istidrāj) is more deserving. Therefore, whoever feels secure from the plotting (makr) of Allah is deluded (maghṭūr), and the origin of this delusion (ghurūr) is that he inferred from worldly blessings that he is honorable with that Bestower, and it is possible that this is evidence of degradation, but that possibility does not agree with the lower self's desire (hawā), so Satan, by means of the lower self's desire (hawā), inclines the heart (qalb) toward what accompanies it, which is believing in its indication of honor, and this is the limit of delusion (ghurūr).
27:50.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

27:59.arabic: وهذه أمور ممكنة في أنفسها فمن لم يحظ بشيء منها، فلا ينبغي أن يخلو عن التصديق والإيمان بإمكانها، فإن القدرة واسعة والفضل عميم وعجائب الملك والملكوت كثيرة، ومقدورات الله تعالى لا نهاية لها وفضله على عباده الذين اصطفى لا غاية له. ولذلك كان أبو يزيد يقول: إن أعطاك مناجاة موسى وروحانية عيسى وخلة إبراهيم فاطلب ما وراء ذلك، فإن عنده فوق ذلك أضعافاً مضاعفة، فإن سكت إلى ذلك حجبك به، وهذا بلاء مثلهم ومن هو في مثل حالهم لأنهم الأمثل فالأمثل.
27:59.english: And these matters are possible in themselves, so whoever does not attain any of them should not be devoid of belief and faith in their possibility, for the Power (Qudrah) is vast and the Favor (Fadl) is abundant, and the wonders of the Dominion (Malak) and the Kingdom (Malakut) are many, and the things decreed by Allah the Exalted have no end, and His Favor upon His servants whom He has chosen has no limit. And for that reason, Abu Yazid used to say: If He gives you the intimate conversation (Munajat) of Moses and the spirituality (Ruhaniyyah) of Jesus and the friendship (Khullah) of Abraham, then seek what is beyond that, for with Him is above that multiples upon multiples, for if you remain silent to that, He will veil you with it, and this is a trial for those like them and for whoever is in a state like theirs because they are the best of the best.
27:59.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

27:59.arabic: فإذا قرب من البيت قال الحمد لله وسلام على عباده الذين اصطفى اللهم صل على محمد عبدك ورسولك وعلى إبراهيم خليلك وعلى جميع أنبيائك ورسلك وليرفع يديه وليقل اللهم إني أسألك في مقامي هذا في أول مناسكي أن تتقبل توبتي وأن تتجاوز عن خطيئتي وتضع عني وزري الحمد لله الذي بلغني بيته الحرام الذي جعله مثابة للناس وأمنا وجعله مباركا وهدى للعالمين اللهم إني عبدك والبلد بلدك والحرم حرمك والبيت بيتك جئتك أطلب رحمتك وأسألك مسألة المضطر الخائف من عقوبتك الراجي لرحمتك الطالب مرضاتك.
27:59.english: When he approaches the House (Kaaba), he should say: 'All praise is for Allah and peace upon His servants whom He has chosen. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad, Your servant and messenger, and upon Abraham, Your intimate friend, and upon all Your prophets and messengers.' And he should raise his hands and say: 'O Allah, I ask You in this station of mine at the beginning of my rites that You accept my repentance, that You overlook my sin, and that You remove my burden from me. All praise is for Allah who has brought me to His Sacred House which He made a place of return for people and a sanctuary, and made it blessed and guidance for the worlds. O Allah, I am Your servant and the land is Your land and the sanctuary is Your sanctuary and the House is Your House. I have come to You seeking Your mercy and I ask You the request of the distressed one, fearful of Your punishment, hopeful for Your mercy, seeking Your pleasure.'
27:59.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

27:71.arabic: واختلاف تركيب أعضائه أعاجيب تزيد على الأعاجيب فى بعثه وإعادته فكيف ينكر ذلك من قدرة الله تعالى وحكمته من يشاهد ذلك فى صنعته وقدرته فإن كان فى إيمانك ضعف فقو الإيمان بالنظر فى النشأة الأولى فإن الثانية مثلها وأسهل منها وإن كنت قوى الإيمان بها فأشعر قلبك تلك المخاوف والأخطار وأكثر فيها التفكر والاعتبار لتسلب عن قلبك الراحة والقرار فتشتغل بالتشمر للعرض على الجبار وتفكر أولا فيما يقرع سمع سكان القبور من شدة نفخ الصور فإنها صيحة واحدة تنفرج بها القبور عن رءوس الموتي فيثورون دفعة واحدة فتوهم نفسك وقد
27:71.english: And the differing composition of its limbs are wonders that increase over wonders in its resurrection and restoration, so how can one deny that from the power (Qudrah) of Allah the Exalted and His wisdom who witnesses that in His creation and power? If there is weakness in your faith (Iman), then strengthen the faith (Iman) by looking at the first creation, for the second is like it and easier than it. And if you are strong in faith (Iman) in it, then make your heart (Qalb) feel those fears and dangers and increase in it reflection (Tafakkur) and consideration (I'tibar) to strip from your heart (Qalb) comfort and settlement, so you busy yourself with preparing for the presentation before the Almighty (Al-Jabbar). And reflect first on what strikes the hearing of the inhabitants of the graves from the intensity of the blowing of the Trumpet (As-Sur), for it is a single cry by which the graves split open from the heads of the dead, and they rise up all at once. So imagine yourself having leaped up with your face changed, your body dusty from your scalp to your feet from the dust of your grave, stunned from the intensity of the blow, your eye fixed toward the call. And the creation has risen up in a single uprising from the graves in which their tribulation (Bala') has been prolonged, and alarm and terror have agitated them, added to what they had of sorrows (Humum) and griefs (Ghumum) and intense waiting for the outcome of the matter, as Allah the Exalted said: 'And the Trumpet (As-Sur) will be blown, and all who are in the heavens and all who are on the earth will fall dead except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on.' And Allah the Exalted said: 'And when the Trumpet (An-Naqur) is blown, that Day will be a difficult day for the disbelievers; not easy.' And Allah the Exalted said: 'And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?" They do not await except one blast which will seize them while they are disputing. And they will not be able [to give] any instruction, nor to their people can they return. And the Trumpet (As-Sur) will be blown; and at once from the graves to their Lord they will hasten. They will say, "O woe to us! Who has raised us up from our sleeping place?" [The reply will be], "This is what the Most Merciful had promised, and the messengers told the truth."' So if there were not before the dead except the terror of that blowing, it would be worthy of being feared, for it is a blowing and a cry by which those in the heavens and the earth are struck dead, meaning they die by it except whom Allah wills, and that is some of the angels. And therefore the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'How can I be at ease when the possessor of the Trumpet (As-Sur) has taken the horn in his mouth, lowered his forehead, and inclined his ear, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow?' Maqatil said: The Trumpet (As-Sur) is the horn, and that Israfil (upon him be peace) is placing his mouth on the horn like the form of a trumpet, and the circle of the head of the horn is like the width of the heavens and the earth, and he is fixing his gaze toward the Throne (Al-'Arsh), waiting for when he will be commanded to blow the first blowing. And when he blows, those in the heavens and the earth are struck dead, meaning every animal dies from the intensity of the alarm except whom Allah wills, and that is Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil, and the Angel of Death (Malak al-Mawt). Then the Angel of Death (Malak al-Mawt) is commanded to take the soul (Ruh) of Jibril, then the soul (Ruh) of Mika'il, then the soul (Ruh) of Israfil, then the Angel of Death (Malak al-Mawt) is commanded and he dies. Then the creation remains after the first blowing in the Barzakh for forty years, then Allah the Exalted revives Israfil and commands.
27:71.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

27:87.arabic: قيام ليلة إلى الصبح، وقال أيضاً: الجوع عند الله في خزائنه لا يعطيه إلا من أحبه. وكان سهل بن عبد الله التستري يطوي نيفاً وعشرين يوماً لا يأكل، وكان يكفيه لطعامه في السنة درهم، وكان يعظم الجوع ويبالغ فيه حتى قال: لا يوافى القيامة عمل بر أفضل من ترك فضول الطعام اقتداء بالنبي ﭬ في أكله. وقال: لم ير الأكياس شيئاً أنفع من الجوع للدين والدنيا. وقال: لا أعلم شيئاً أضر على طلاب الآخرة من الأكل. وقال: وضعت الحكمة والعلم في الجوع ووضعت المعصية والجهل في الشبع. وقال ما عبد الله بشيء أفضل من مخالفة الهوى في
27:87.english: Standing [in prayer] from night until dawn, and he also said: Hunger is with Allah in His treasuries, and He does not give it except to whom He loves. And Sahl ibn Abdullah al-Tustari would go over twenty-some days without eating, and a dirham sufficed him for his food in the year, and he would magnify hunger and exaggerate in it until he said: No righteous deed will meet the Resurrection better than abandoning excess food in emulation of the Prophet (peace be upon him) in his eating. And he said: The wise have not seen anything more beneficial than hunger for religion and the worldly life. And he said: I do not know anything more harmful to seekers of the Hereafter than eating. And he said: Wisdom and knowledge were placed in hunger, and disobedience and ignorance were placed in satiety. And he said: Allah has not been worshipped with anything better than opposing the desire (Hawa) in abandoning the lawful. And it has come in the hadith: "One-third for food, so whoever increases upon that, then he eats from his good deeds." And he was asked about the increase, so he said: He does not find the increase until abandonment becomes more beloved to him than eating, and when he is hungry for a night, he asks Allah to make it two nights, so when that is, he finds the increase. And he said: The Substitutes (Abdal) became substitutes only by emptying the bellies, staying awake, silence, and seclusion. And he said: The head of every righteousness that descended from the sky to the earth is hunger, and the head of every wickedness between them is satiety. And he said: Whoever hungers his soul (Nafs), the whisperings are cut off from him. And he said: The turning of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to the servant is with hunger, sickness, and affliction except whom Allah wills. And he said: Know that this is a time in which no one attains salvation except by slaughtering his soul (Nafs) and killing it with hunger, staying awake, and exertion. And he said: No one has passed on the face of the earth who drank from this water until he was quenched and was safe from disobedience - even if he thanks Allah, the Exalted - so how about satiety from food? And a wise man was asked: With what restraint do I restrain my soul (Nafs)? He said: Restrain it with hunger and thirst, humble it by lowering remembrance (Dhikr) and abandoning honor, make it small by placing it under the feet of the sons of the Hereafter, break it by abandoning the appearance of the reciters from its outward, and escape from its defects by constant bad suspicion of it, and accompany it by opposing its desire (Hawa). And Abdul Wahid ibn Zaid would swear by Allah, the Exalted, that Allah, the Exalted, has not purified anyone except with hunger, nor have they walked on water except with it, nor was the earth folded for them except with hunger, nor has Allah, the Exalted, taken charge of them except with hunger. And Abu Talib al-Makki said: The belly is like the lute, which is the hollow wood with strings - indeed its sound is beautiful due to its lightness and thinness because it is hollow and not full, and likewise the interior if it is empty is sweeter for recitation, more enduring for standing [in prayer], and less for sleep. And Abu Bakr ibn Abdullah al-Muzani said: Three whom Allah, the Exalted, loves; a man of little sleep, little eating, little rest. And it is narrated that Jesus (peace be upon him) remained conversing intimately with his Lord for sixty mornings without eating, then bread occurred to his mind, so he was cut off from the intimate conversation, so...
27:87.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Harms of the Tongue'

27:87.arabic: فلو لم يكن بين يدي الموتي إلا هول تلك النفخة لكان ذلك جديرا بأن يتقى فإنها نفخة وصيحة يصعق بها من فى السموات والأرض يعنى يموتون بها إلا من شاء الله وهو بعض الملائكة ولذلك قال رسول الله ﭬ: (كيف أنعم وصاحب الصور قد التقم القرن وحنى الجبهة وأصغى بالأذن متى يؤمر فينفخ[144]) قال مقاتل: الصور هو القرن وذلك أن إسرافيل عليه السلام واضع فاه على القرن كهيئة البوق ودائرة رأس القرن كعرض السموات والأرض وهو شاخص بصره نحو العرش ينتظر متى يؤمر فينفخ النفخة الأولى فإذا نفخ صعق من فى السموات والأرض أى مات كل حيوا
27:87.english: If there were nothing before the dead except the terror of that blowing (of the Horn), it would be worthy of being feared, for it is a blowing and a shout by which those in the heavens and the earth are struck unconscious (صعق) - meaning they die by it - except whom Allah wills, and that is some of the angels. Therefore, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'How can one enjoy comfort when the possessor of the Horn (الصور) has taken the horn into his mouth, bent his forehead, and listened with his ear, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow?' [144] Muqatil said: The Horn (الصور) is the trumpet, and that is because Israfil (upon him be peace) has placed his mouth on the horn like a trumpet, and the circumference of the horn's head is like the expanse of the heavens and the earth, and he is gazing with his sight toward the Throne, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow the first blowing. When he blows, those in the heavens and the earth are struck unconscious (صعق) - meaning every living creature dies from the intensity of the terror (الفزع) - except whom Allah wills, and that is Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil, and the Angel of Death. Then the Angel of Death is commanded to take the soul (روح) of Jibril, then the soul of Mika'il, then the soul of Israfil, then the Angel of Death is commanded and he dies. Then the creation remains after the first blowing in the Barzakh (البرزخ) for forty years. Then Allah the Exalted revives Israfil and commands him to blow the second blowing, and that is His saying: 'Then it will be blown into it another time, and behold, they are standing, looking.' [Quran 39:68] - on their feet, looking at the Resurrection. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'When I was sent, I was sent to the possessor of the Horn, and he inclined it to his mouth, and advanced one foot and delayed another, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow. So fear the blowing!' [145] So reflect upon the creatures and their humiliation (ذل), their brokenness (انكسار), and their submission (استكانة) at the time of being raised, out of fear of this striking unconscious (الصعقة) and in anticipation of what will be decreed for them of happiness (سعادة) or misery (شقاوة). And you are among them, broken like their brokenness, perplexed like their perplexity. Rather, if you were in the world among the luxurious and the rich who enjoy comfort, then the kings of the earth on that day are the most humiliated people of the gathering place, the smallest and most contemptible of them, being trodden under feet like a grain. And at that time, the wild beasts from the deserts and the mountains come with lowered heads, mixed with the creatures after their wildness, humiliated for the Day of Resurrection, without any sin by which they have been defiled, but their gathering is due to the intensity of the striking unconscious (الصعقة) and the terror of the blowing, and that preoccupies them from fleeing from the creatures and being wild toward them, and that.
27:87.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

27:87.arabic: رع سمع سكان القبور من شدة نفخ الصور فإنها صيحة واحدة تنفرج بها القبور عن رءوس الموتي فيثورون دفعة واحدة فتوهم نفسك وقد وثبت متغيرا وجهك مغبرا بدنك من فرقك إلى قدمك من تراب قبرك مبهوتا من شدة الصعقة شاخص العين نحو النداء وقد ثار الخلق ثورة واحدة من القبور التى طال فيها بلاؤهم وقد أزعجهم الفزع والرعب مضافا إلى ما كان عندهم من الهموم والغموم وشدة الانتظار لعاقبة الأمر كما قال تعالى: ﴿ ونفخ فى الصور فصعق من فى السموات ومن فى الأرض إلا من شاء الله ثم نفخ فيه أخرى فإذا هم قيام ينظرون ﴾ {} وقال تعالى:
27:87.english: Listen, the inhabitants of the graves hear from the intensity of the blowing of the Trumpet (As-Sur), for it is a single cry by which the graves split open from the heads of the dead, and they rise up all at once. So imagine yourself having leaped up, your face altered, your body dusty from your head to your feet from the dust of your grave, stunned from the intensity of the blow, your eyes fixed toward the call. And the creation has risen up in a single uprising from the graves in which their tribulation has been prolonged, and the terror and dread have agitated them, added to what they had of sorrows, griefs, and intense waiting for the outcome of the matter, as Allah the Exalted said: 'And the Trumpet (As-Sur) will be blown, and all who are in the heavens and all who are on the earth will fall dead except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on.' And Allah the Exalted said: 'And when the Trumpet (An-Naqur) is sounded, that Day will be a difficult day for the disbelievers; not easy.' And Allah the Exalted said: 'And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?" They do not await except one blast which will seize them while they are disputing. And they will not be able to make a testament, nor to their people will they return. And the Trumpet (As-Sur) will be blown; and at once from the graves to their Lord they will hasten. They will say, "O woe to us! Who has raised us from our sleeping place? This is what the Most Merciful had promised, and the messengers told the truth."' So if there were nothing before the dead except the terror of that blowing, it would be worthy of being feared, for it is a blowing and a cry by which those in the heavens and the earth are struck dead, meaning they die by it, except whom Allah wills, and that is some of the angels. And for that reason, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'How can I be at ease when the possessor of the Trumpet (As-Sur) has taken the horn in his mouth, bowed his forehead, and inclined his ear, waiting for when he is commanded to blow?' Maqatil said: The Trumpet (As-Sur) is the horn, and that is because Israfil (upon him be peace) places his mouth on the horn like the shape of a trumpet, and the circle of the head of the horn is like the expanse of the heavens and the earth, and he is fixing his gaze toward the Throne, waiting for when he is commanded to blow the first blowing. And when he blows, those in the heavens and the earth are struck dead, meaning every living creature dies from the intensity of the terror, except whom Allah wills, and that is Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil, and the Angel of Death (Malak al-Mawt). Then the Angel of Death is commanded to take the soul (Ruh) of Jibril, then the soul (Ruh) of Mika'il, then the soul (Ruh) of Israfil, then the Angel of Death is commanded and he dies. Then the creation remains after the first blowing in the Intermediate State (Al-Barzakh) for forty years. Then Allah the Exalted revives Israfil and commands him to blow the second blowing, and that is His saying the Exalted: 'Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on.' On their feet, looking at the Resurrection (Al-Ba'th). And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'When I was sent, I was sent to the possessor of the Trumpet (As-Sur), and he inclined it to his mouth, advanced one foot and delayed another, waiting for when he is commanded to blow. So fear the blowing.' So reflect on the creation and their humiliation, their brokenness, and their submission at the resurrection, out of fear from this blow and waiting for what is decreed upon them of happiness or wretchedness, and
27:87.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

27:88.arabic: يوم ترى الجبال تحسبها جامدة وهى تمر مر السحاب، يوم تنشق فيه السماء فتكون وردة كالدهان، فيومئذ لا يسئل عن ذنبه إنس ولا جان، يوم يمنع فيه العاصى من الكلام ولا يسئل فيه عن الأجرام بل يؤخذ بالنواصى والأقدام، يوم تجد كل نفس ما عملت من خير محضرا وما عملت من سوء تود لو أن بينها وبينه أمدا بعيدا، يوم تعلم فيه كل نفس ما أحضرت وتشهد ما قدمت وأخرت يوم تخرس فيه الألسن وتنطق الجوارح يوم شيب ذكره سيد المرسلين إذ قال له الصديق رضى الله عنه: أراك قد شبت يا رسول الله قال: (شيبتنى هود وأخواتها[155]) وهى الواقعة و
27:88.english: The day you see the mountains, you think them firm while they pass like the passing of clouds, the day the sky splits therein and becomes like red leather, then on that day no human or jinn will be asked about his sin, the day the disobedient is prevented from speech and therein is not asked about the crimes but is taken by the forelocks and the feet, the day every soul finds what it did of good present and what it did of evil wishes that between it and it were a distant span, the day every soul therein knows what it has brought and witnesses what it has sent ahead and left behind, the day the tongues are silenced therein and the limbs speak, the day its mention turned gray the master of the messengers when the truthful one (may Allah be pleased with him) said to him: I see you have turned gray, O Messenger of Allah. He said: (Hud and its sisters turned me gray [155]) and they are Al-Waqi'ah, Al-Mursalat, 'Amma Yatasa'alun, and Idha Ash-Shamsu Kuwwirat. So O incapable reader, your share from your reading is that you mumble the Quran and move with it the tongue, and if you were reflecting on what you read, you would be worthy that your bitterness splits from what turned gray from it the hair of the master of the messengers, and if you are content with the movement of the tongue, you have deprived yourself of the fruit of the Quran. So the Resurrection (Al-Qiyamah) is one of what is mentioned therein, and Allah has described some of its calamities and multiplied its names for us to stand with the multiplicity of its names on the multiplicity of its meanings, so the intended with the multiplicity of the names is not the repetition of the names and titles, but the purpose is alerting the possessors of intellects (Ulul Albab), so under every name from the names of the Resurrection is a secret and in every attribute from its attributes is a meaning, so strive to know their meanings and
27:88.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

27:88.arabic: فلا تظنن أن الذي يضطرب بنفسه على الأرض أتم وجدا من الساكن باضطرابه بل رب ساكن أتم وجدا من المضطرب فقد كان الجنيد يتحرك في السماع في بدايته ثم صار لا يتحرك فقيل له في ذلك فقال وترى الجبال تحسبها جامدة وهي تمر مر السحاب صنع الله الذي أتقن كل شيء إشارة إلى أن القلب مضطرب جائل في الملكوت والجوارح متأدبة في الظاهر ساكنة
27:88.english: So do not think that the one who trembles with his self (Nafs) upon the ground is more complete in spiritual ecstasy (Wajd) than the one who is still with his trembling; rather, perhaps a still one is more complete in spiritual ecstasy (Wajd) than the trembler. Indeed, Al-Junayd used to move during spiritual listening (Sama') in his beginning, then he became not moving. So it was said to him regarding that, and he said: 'And you see the mountains, you think them stationary, while they pass like the passing of the clouds. The making of Allah who perfected everything' (Quran 27:88) - an indication that the heart (Qalb) is disturbed, wandering in the dominion (Malakut), and the limbs are disciplined in the apparent, still.
27:88.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

27:89.arabic: ولقوله تعالى: ﴿ من جاء بالحسنة فله خير منها وهم من فزع يومئذ آمنون ﴾ {} فالإيمان رأس الحسنات ولقوله تعالى: ﴿ والله يحب المحسنين ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ إنا لا نضيع أجر من أحسن عملا ﴾ {} ولا حجة لهم في ذلك فإنه حيث ذكر الإيمان في هذه الآيات أريد به الإيمان مع العمل إذ بينا أن الإيمان قد يطلق ويراد به الإسلام وهو الموافقة بالقلب والقول والعمل ودليل هذا التأويل أخبار كثيرة في معاقبة العاصين ومقادير العقاب
27:89.english: And due to His saying, the Exalted: 'Whoever comes with a good deed (al-hasanah) will have better than it, and they will be secure from terror on that day' (27:89). So faith (al-iman) is the head of the good deeds (al-hasanat). And due to His saying, the Exalted: 'And Allah loves the doers of good (al-muhsinin)' (3:134). And He said, the Exalted: 'Indeed, We do not waste the reward of one who does good (ahsana) in deed' (18:30). And they have no proof in that, for when faith (al-iman) is mentioned in these verses, it is intended to be faith (al-iman) with action (al-'amal), since we have clarified that faith (al-iman) may be uttered and intended to be Islam, which is conformity with the heart (al-qalb), the speech (al-qawl), and the action (al-'amal). And the evidence for this interpretation is many reports regarding the punishment of the disobedient and the measures of punishment.
27:89.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

27:90.arabic: وقوله تعالى: ﴿ ومن جاء بالسيئة فكبت وجوههم في النار ﴾ {} فهذه العمومات في معارضة عموماتهم ولا بد من تسليط التخصص والتأويل على الجانبين لأن الأخبار مصرحة بأن العصاة يعذبون[52] بل قوله تعالى: ﴿ وإن منكم إلا واردها ﴾ {} كالصريح في أن ذلك لا بد منه للكل إذ لا يخلو مؤمن عن ذنب يرتكبه
27:90.english: And His saying, the Exalted: 'And whoever comes with the evil deed, then their faces will be turned down in the Fire' (Quran 27:90). So these general statements are in opposition to their general statements, and it is necessary to apply specification (takhṣīṣ) and interpretation (taʾwīl) to both sides because the reports explicitly state that the disobedient ones (ʿuṣāh) are punished. Rather, His saying, the Exalted: 'And there is not one of you except that he will enter it' (Quran 19:71) is like the explicit in that this is inevitable for all, since no believer is free from a sin that he commits.
27:90.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

28:15.arabic: وقال موسى عليه السلام فيما أخبر عنه الله "هذا من عمل الشيطان" ولذلك حذر الله منه جميع الخلق فقال الله تعالى "يا بني آدم لا يفتننكم الشيطان كما أخرج أبويكم من الجنة" وقال عز وجل "إنه يراكم هو وقبيله من حيث لا ترونهم" والقرآن من أوله إلى آخره تحذير من الشيطان فكيف وقد أمر بالحذر من العدو كما أمر بالحذر من الكفار فقال تعالى "وليأخذوا حذرهم وأسلحتهم" وقال تعالى "وأعدوا لهم ما استطعتم من قوة ومن رباط الخيل" فإذا لزمك بأمر الله الحذر من العدو الكافر وأنت تراه فبأن يلزمك الحذر من عدو يراك ولا تراه أولى
28:15.english: And Moses, peace be upon him, said in what Allah informed about him: "This is from the action of the Satan (Shaytan)." Therefore, Allah warned all creation from him, as Allah the Exalted said: "O children of Adam, let not Satan tempt you as he removed your parents from the Garden (Jannah)," and He the Mighty and Majestic said: "Indeed, he sees you, he and his tribe, from where you do not see them." And the Quran from its beginning to its end is a warning from Satan (Shaytan), so how [can one be heedless] when He has commanded caution from the enemy just as He commanded caution from the disbelievers? He the Exalted said: "And let them take their precaution and their weapons," and He the Exalted said: "And prepare against them whatever you are able of power and of steeds of war." So if it is incumbent upon you by Allah's command to be cautious from the disbelieving enemy whom you see, then it is more appropriate that it be incumbent upon you to be cautious from an enemy who sees you and you do not see him.
28:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

28:16.arabic: عملت سوءا وظلمت نفسي فاغفر لي فإنه لا يغفر الذنوب إلا أنت
28:16.english: I have done evil and wronged my soul (Nafs), so forgive me, for none forgives sins except You.
28:16.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith

28:16.arabic: اللهم إني ظلمت نفسي فاغفر لي ذنوبي فإنه لا يغفر الذنوب إلا أنت
28:16.english: O Allah, indeed I have wronged my Soul (Nafs), so forgive me my sins, for none forgives sins except You.
28:16.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith

28:16.arabic: سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك لا إله إلا أنت عملت سوءا وظلمت نفسي فاغفر لي ذنبي إنك أنت ربي ولا يغفر الذنوب إلا أنت
28:16.english: Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You, there is no god but You. I have done evil and wronged my soul (Nafs), so forgive me my sin, for You are my Lord, and none forgives sins except You.
28:16.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

28:16.arabic: [159] حديث سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك لا إله إلا أنت عملت سوءا وظلمت نفسي فاغفر لي ذنبي أنت ربي إنه لا يغفر الذنوب إلا أنت أخرجه البيهقي في الدعوات من حديث علي دون قوله ذنبي إنك أنت ربي وقد تقدم في الباب الثاني.
28:16.english: Hadith: 'Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You, there is no god but You, I have done evil and wronged my soul (Nafs), so forgive me my sin, You are my Lord, indeed none forgives sins except You.' Al-Bayhaqi reported it in Al-Da'awat from the narration of Ali without his saying 'my sin, You are my Lord,' and it has preceded in the second chapter.
28:16.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication

28:23.arabic: وأما الأمة فتطلق على ثمانية أوجه الأمة الجماعة كقوله تعالى ﴿ وجد عليه أمة من الناس يسقون ﴾ {} وأتباع الأنبياء كقولك عن أمة محمد ﭬ، ورجل جامع للخير يقتدي به كقوله تعالى ﴿ إن إبراهيم كان أمة قانتا لله ﴾ {} والأمة الدين كقوله عز وجل ﴿ إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة ﴾ {} والأمة الحين والزمان كقوله عز وجل ﴿ إلى أمة معدودة ﴾ {} وقوله عز وجل ﴿ وادكر بعد أمة ﴾ {} والأمة القامة يقال فلان حسن الأمة أي القامة، وأمة رجل منفرد بدين لا يشركه فيه أحد قال ﭬ: (يبعث زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل أمة وحده[57]) والأمة الأم يقال هذ
28:23.english: And as for 'Ummah' (الأمة), it is applied in eight aspects: The 'Ummah' as a community (الجماعة), as in His saying, the Exalted: 'And he found upon it a community (Ummah) of people watering' (Quran 28:23). And the followers of the prophets, as you say regarding the community (Ummah) of Muhammad (peace be upon him). And a man who gathers goodness and is followed, as in His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, Abraham was a community (Ummah), devoutly obedient to Allah' (Quran 16:120). And the 'Ummah' as religion, as in His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, we found our fathers upon a community (Ummah)' (Quran 43:22). And the 'Ummah' as a time or period, as in His saying, the Exalted: 'Until a numbered community (Ummah)' (Quran 11:8) and His saying, the Exalted: 'And remember after a community (Ummah)' (Quran 12:45). And the 'Ummah' as stature, it is said: 'So-and-so has a good 'Ummah' meaning stature. And the 'Ummah' of a man who is unique in a religion, with no one sharing it with him, as he (peace be upon him) said: 'Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Nufayl will be resurrected as a community (Ummah) alone' [57]. And the 'Ummah' as mother, it is said: 'This is the 'Ummah' of Zayd' meaning the mother of Zayd.
28:23.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

28:30.arabic: رواه عن النبي ﭬ أنه قال: (إن الله تعالى يمجد نفسه كل يوم ويقول إني أنا الله رب العالمين إني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا الحي القيوم إني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا العلي العظيم إني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا لم ألد ولم أولد إني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا العفو الغفور إني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا مبدىء كل شيء وإلي يعود العزيز الحكيم الرحمن الرحيم مالك يوم الدين خالق الخير والشر خالق الجنة والنار الواحد الأحد الفرد الصمد الذي لم يتخذ صاحبة ولا ولدا الفرد الوتر عالم الغيب والشهادة الملك القدوس السلام المؤمن المهي
28:30.english: It is narrated from the Prophet (peace be upon him) that he said: (Indeed, Allah the Exalted glorifies Himself every day and says: 'Indeed, I am Allah, Lord of the Worlds (Rabb al-'Alamin). Indeed, I am Allah, there is no god but I, the Living (Al-Hayy), the Self-Sustaining (Al-Qayyum). Indeed, I am Allah, there is no god but I, the Most High (Al-'Ali), the Most Great (Al-'Azim). Indeed, I am Allah, there is no god but I, I have not begotten nor have I been begotten. Indeed, I am Allah, there is no god but I, the Pardoner (Al-'Afuw), the Forgiving (Al-Ghafur).
