Indeed, I am Allah, there is no god but I, the Originator (Mubdi') of everything and to Me is the return, the Mighty (Al-'Aziz), the Wise (Al-Hakim), the Most Gracious (Ar-Rahman), the Most Merciful (Ar-Rahim), Master (Malik) of the Day of Judgment, Creator (Khaliq) of good and evil, Creator of Paradise and Hell, the One (Al-Wahid), the Unique (Al-Ahad), the Single (Al-Fard), the Eternal (As-Samad) who has not taken a consort nor a son, the Single (Al-Fard), the Odd (Al-Witr), Knower (Alim) of the unseen and the witnessed, the Sovereign (Al-Malik), the Holy (Al-Quddus), the Peace (As-Salam), the Faithful (Al-Mu'min), the Guardian (Al-Muhaymin), the Mighty (Al-'Aziz), the Compeller (Al-Jabbar), the Majestic (Al-Mutakabbir), the Creator (Al-Khaliq), the Maker (Al-Bari'), the Fashioner (Al-Musawwir), the Great (Al-Kabir), the Exalted (Al-Muta'ali), the Powerful (Al-Muqtadir), the Subduer (Al-Qahhar), the Forbearing (Al-Halim), the Generous (Al-Karim), Possessor (Ahl) of praise and glory, Knower (A'lam) of the secret and what is more hidden, the Able (Al-Qadir), the Provider (Ar-Razzaq) above the creation and the creatures[135]).' And He mentioned before every word 'Indeed, I am Allah, there is no god but I' as we have brought it in the beginning. So whoever supplicates with these names, let him say: 'Indeed, You are Allah, there is no god but You, such and such.' So whoever supplicates with them is written among the prostrating (As-Sajidin), the humble (Al-Mukhbitin) who will be neighbors with Muhammad, Ibrahim, Musa, 'Isa, and the prophets, prayers of Allah be upon them, in the abode of majesty, and for him is the reward of the worshippers (Al-'Abidin) in the heavens and the earths. And may Allah bless Muhammad and every chosen servant (Abd Mustafa).
28:30.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

28:34.arabic: فكذلك الانبساط والإدلال يحتمل من بعض العباد دون بعض. فمن انبساط الأنس قول موسى عليه السلام: "إن هي إلا فتنتك تضل بها من تشاء وتهدي من تشاء" وقوله في التعليل والاعتذار لما قيل له: "اذهب إلى فرعون"، فقال: "ولهم على ذنب" وقوله: "إني أخاف أن يكذبون ويضيق صدري ولا ينطلق لساني"، وقوله: "إننا نخاف أن يفرط علينا أو أن يطغى" وهذا من غير موسى عليه السلام من سوء الأدب لأن الذي أقيم مقام الأنس يلاطف ويحتمل، ولم يحتمل ليونس عليه السلام ما دون هذا لما أقيم مقام القبض والهيبة، فعوقب بالسجن في بطن الحوت - في ظل
28:34.english: Similarly, expansion (Inbisat) and familiarity (Idlal) are permissible for some worshippers but not others. From the expansion of intimacy (Unsiyyah) is the saying of Moses, peace be upon him: "It is only Your trial by which You misguide whom You will and guide whom You will" and his saying in explanation and excuse when he was told: "Go to Pharaoh," so he said: "And they have a sin against me" and his saying: "Indeed, I fear they will deny me and my chest will tighten and my tongue will not be fluent" and his saying: "Indeed, we fear he will hasten against us or transgress." And this from other than Moses, peace be upon him, would be bad manners (Su' al-Adab) because the one established in the station of intimacy (Maqam al-Uns) is indulged and tolerated, and Jonah, peace be upon him, was not tolerated for less than this when he was established in the station of contraction (Qabd) and awe (Haybah), so he was punished with imprisonment in the belly of the whale - in three darknesses - and was called out to until the Day of Resurrection: "Had it not been that a favor from his Lord reached him, he would have been cast on the barren shore while blameworthy." Al-Hasan said: The barren shore (Al-'Ara') is the Resurrection. And our Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was forbidden to be followed in this and it was said to him: "So be patient for the decree of your Lord and do not be like the companion of the fish when he called out while distressed."
28:34.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

28:38.arabic: ونظر عمر رضي الله عنه في طريق الشام إلى صرح قد بني بجص وآجر، فكبر وقال: ما كنت أظن أن يكون في هذه الأمة من يبني بنيان هامان لفرعون؛ يعني قول فرعون "فأوقد لي يا هامان على الطين" يعني به الآجر، ويقال: إن فرعون هو أول من بني له بالجص والآجر، وأول من عمله هامان، ثم تبعهما الجبابرة، وهذا هو الزخرف.
28:38.english: And Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) looked in the direction of Syria at a palace that had been built with plaster and baked bricks, so he exclaimed 'Allahu Akbar' and said: 'I did not think that there would be in this nation one who builds the building of Haman for Pharaoh'; meaning the saying of Pharaoh: 'So kindle for me, O Haman, upon the clay' meaning by it the baked bricks. And it is said: Indeed Pharaoh was the first for whom was built with plaster and baked bricks, and the first who made it was Haman, then the tyrants followed them, and this is the adornment (Zukhruf).
28:38.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

28:39.arabic: القسم الثاني: التكبر على الرسل من حيث تعزز النفس وترفعها على الانقياد لبشر مثل سائر الناس؛ وذلك تارة يصرف عن الفكر والاستبصار فيبقى في ظلمة الجهل بكبره فيمتنع عن الانقياد وهو ظان أنه محق فيه، وتارة يمتنع مع المعرفة ولكن لا تطاوعه نفسه للإنقياد للحق والتواضع للرسل، كما حكى الله قولهم "أنؤمن لبشرين مثلنا" وقولهم "إن أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا ولئن أطعتم بشراً مثلكم إنكم إذا لخاسرون" وقال الذين لا يرجون لقائنا لولا أنزل علينا الملائكة أو نرى ربنا لقد استكبروا في أنفسهم وعتوا عواً كبيراً. وقالوا لولا أنزل ع
28:39.english: The second category: Arrogance (Takabbur) toward the messengers (Rusul) in terms of the Soul (Nafs) strengthening and elevating itself above submission to a human being like other people; this sometimes diverts from thought (Fikr) and insight (Istibsar), remaining in the darkness of ignorance (Jahl) due to its arrogance (Kibr), thus preventing submission while thinking it is correct in this, and sometimes it prevents despite knowledge (Ma'rifah) but its Soul (Nafs) does not comply with submission to the Truth (Haqq) and humility toward the messengers (Rusul), as Allah narrated their saying "Shall we believe in two human beings like ourselves?" and their saying "You are only human beings like us, and if you obey a human being like yourselves, then indeed you would be losers." And said those who do not hope for Our meeting: "Why have not angels been sent down to us, or (why) do we (not) see our Lord?" Indeed, they have become arrogant within themselves and transgressed a great transgression. And they said: "Why has not an angel been sent down to him?" And Pharaoh, in what Allah informed about him, said: "Or (why) have not angels come with him, accompanying?" And Allah the Exalted said: "And he and his soldiers were arrogant in the land without right" so he was arrogant toward Allah and toward all His messengers (Rusul).
28:39.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

28:48.arabic: وفي حديث آخر " ثلاث من أوتيهن فقد أوتي مثل ما أوتي آل داود: العدل في الرضا والغضب، والقصد في الغنى والفقر، وخشية الله في السر والعلانية"[81]
28:48.english: And in another narration: 'Three [qualities] whoever is given them has been given like what was given to the family of Dawud (David): justice in pleasure and anger, moderation in wealth and poverty, and fear of Allah (Khushya Allah) in secret and openness.'[81]
28:48.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

28:50.arabic: ً  ما  سبقونا إليه" وترتيب القياس الذي نظمه في قلوبهم أنهم  يقولون:  قد  أحسن  الله  إلينا بنعيم الدنيا، وكل محسن فهو محب، وكل محب فإنه يحسن أيضاً في المستقبل  كما  قال الشاعر: |لقد أحسن الله  | |كذلك يحسن فيما| |فيما مضى       | |بقـي          | وإنما يقيس المستقبل على الماضي بواسطة الكرامة والحب إذ يقول: لولا  أني  كريم عند الله ومحبوب لما أحسن إلي. والتلبيس تحت ظنه أن كل محسن  محب،  لا  بل  تحت ظنه أن إنعامه عليه في الدنيا إحسان، فقد اغتر  بالله  إذ  ظن  أنه  كريم  عنده بدليل لا يدل على الكرا
28:50.english: What has preceded us to it, and the arrangement of analogy that He organized in their hearts is that they say: Allah has done good to us with the bliss of the worldly life, and every doer of good is a lover, and every lover then he does good also in the future as the poet said: "Allah has done good in what has passed, likewise He does good in what remains." And he only analogizes the future to the past by means of honor and love when he says: Were it not that I am honorable with Allah and beloved, He would not have done good to me. And the deception is under his assumption that every doer of good is a lover, no, rather under his assumption that His bestowing upon him in the worldly life is doing good, so he has been deluded by Allah when he thought that he is honorable with Him by evidence that does not indicate honor, but rather with the people of insight it indicates disgrace. And its example: That a man has two small servants, he hates one of them and loves the other. The one whom he loves, he prevents from playing and obliges him to the study room and confines him in it to teach him manners, and prevents him from fruits and delights of foods that harm him, and gives him medicines that benefit him. And the one whom he hates, he neglects him to live as he wishes, so he plays and does not enter the study room and eats what he desires. So this neglected servant thinks that he is with his master beloved and honorable because he enabled him for his desires and pleasures and assisted him in all his purposes, so he does not prevent him and did not restrict him, and that is pure delusion. And thus the bliss of the worldly life and its pleasure, for they are destroyers and distancers from Allah. "For indeed Allah protects His servant from the worldly life while He loves him" as one of you protects his sick person from food and drink while he loves him, thus it has come in the report from the master of humankind. And the people of insight, when the worldly life came to them, they grieved and said: A sin whose punishment was hastened, and they saw that as a sign of contempt and neglect. And when poverty came to them, they said: Welcome to the emblem of the righteous. And the deluded one, when the worldly life comes to him, he thinks it is honor from Allah, and when it is turned away from him, he thinks it is disgrace, as Allah the Exalted informed about him when He said: "As for man, when his Lord tests him and honors him and bestows favor upon him, he says, 'My Lord has honored me.' But when He tests him and restricts his provision, he says, 'My Lord has humiliated me.'" So Allah answered that with "No!" meaning not as he said, rather it is a test—we seek refuge in Allah from the evil of the test and we ask Allah for firmness—so He made clear that that is delusion. Al-Hasan said: He denied them both with His saying "No!" saying: This is not My honoring nor this is My humiliation, but rather the honorable one is whom I have honored with My obedience, whether he was rich or poor, and the humiliated one is whom I have humiliated with My disobedience, whether he was rich or poor. And this delusion, its cure is knowing the signs of honor and humiliation either by insight or by imitation. As for insight, it is by knowing the aspect of turning attention to the desires of the worldly life being a distancer from Allah and the aspect of distancing from them being a bringer closer to.
28:50.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

28:54.arabic: قال الله تعالى: " فخرج على قومه في زينته . . . إلى قوله تعالى . . . وقال الذين أوتوا العلم ويلكم ثواب الله خير لمن آمن " فنسب الزهد إلى العلماء ووصف أهله بالعلم وهو غاية الثناء، وقال تعالى: " أولئك يؤتون أجرهم مرتين بما صبروا " وجاء في التفسير على الزهد في الدنيا.
28:54.english: Allah the Exalted said: "So he went forth to his people in his adornment..." up to His saying: "...and those who were given knowledge said: 'Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for those who believe.'" Thus He attributed asceticism (Zuhd) to the scholars and described its people with knowledge, which is the utmost praise. And He said: "Those will be given their reward twice for what they patiently endured." And it came in the interpretation regarding asceticism (Zuhd) in the worldly life.
28:54.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

28:60.arabic: وأما المعرفة بالبيان والبرهان فهو أن يعرف وجه فساد هذا القياس الذي نظمه في قلبه الشيطان، فإن كل مغرور فلغروره سبب، وذلك السبب هو دليل وكل دليل فهو نوع قياس يقع في النفس ويورث السكون إليه وإن كان صاحبه لا يشعر به ولا يقدر على نظمه بألفاظ العلماء. فالقياس الذي نظمه الشيطان فيه أصلان "أحدهما" أن الدنيا نقد والآخرة نسيئة وهذا صحيح "والآخر" قوله: إن النقاد خير من النسيئة، وهذا محل التلبيس فليس الأمر كذلك، بل إن كان النقد مثل النسيئة في المقدار والمقصود فهو خير وإن كان أقل منها فالنسيئة خير، فإن الكاف
28:60.english: And as for the knowledge (Ma'rifah) through clarification and proof, it is to know the aspect of corruption of this analogy (Qiyas) that the Satan (Shaytan) organized in his heart (Qalb), for every deluded one has a cause for his delusion, and that cause is evidence and every evidence is a type of analogy that occurs in the soul (Nafs) and produces tranquility towards it even if its possessor is not aware of it nor capable of organizing it with the words of the scholars. So the analogy that the Satan organized has two foundations: "one" that the worldly life (Dunya) is cash and the Hereafter (Akhirah) is credit, and this is correct; "the other" is his statement: Indeed, cash is better than credit, and this is the place of deception, for the matter is not so, rather if the cash is like the credit in amount and purpose then it is better, but if it is less than it then the credit is better. For the deluded disbeliever (Kafir) spends in his trade a dirham to receive ten on credit, yet he does not spend a dirham to receive ten on credit in the Hereafter, and this is pure ignorance (Jahl), for if he knew that what is with Allah is better and more lasting, he would prefer credit over cash. And to this meaning Allah the Exalted pointed with His saying: "And whatever you have been given of anything, then it is the enjoyment of the worldly life and its adornment. And what is with Allah is better and more lasting. So will you not use intellect?" So He made clear that what is with Allah is better and more lasting, so whoever prefers what is inferior over what is superior has abandoned the best, and this is delusion itself.
28:60.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

28:60.arabic: فإن قلت: إنه ينتظر جوابه فليتلذذ بسماع جوابه وليس يسمع كلام الله تعالى. فاعلم أنه إن كان يعلم أنه لا يجيبه ويسكت عنه فقد بقيت له أيضا لذة في عرض أحواله عليه ورفع سريرته إليه كيف والموقن يسمع من الله تعالى كل ما يرد على خاطره في أثناء مناجاته فيتلذذ به وكذا الذي يخلو بالملك ويعرض عليه حاجاته في جنح الليل يتلذذ به في رجاء إنعامه والرجاء في حق الله تعالى أصدق وما عند الله خير وأبقى وأنفع مما عند غيره فكيف لا يتلذذ بعرض الحاجات عليه في الخلوات.
28:60.english: If you say: 'He awaits His response, so let him delight in hearing His answer, yet he does not hear the speech of Allah.' Know that even if he knows He will not respond and remains silent, there still remains for him delight in presenting his states to Him and raising his innermost secret (Sirrah) to Him. How much more so for the one certain (Muqin) who hears from Allah everything that occurs to his thought during his intimate conversation (Munajah), delighting in it. Similarly, one who secludes himself with a king and presents his needs to him in the depth of night delights in it in hope of his favor. And hope in the right of Allah is truer, and what is with Allah is better and more lasting (Abqa) and more beneficial than what is with others, so how can he not delight in presenting his needs to Him in seclusions?
28:60.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

28:67.arabic: والقرآن من أوله إلى آخره مخاوف لمن قرأه بتدبر ولو لم يكن فيه إلا قوله تعالى: ﴿ وإني لغفار لمن تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا ثم اهتدى ﴾ {} لكان كافيا إذ علق المغفرة على أربعة شروط يعجز العبد عن آحادها، وأشد منه قوله تعالى: ﴿ فأما من تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا فعسى أن يكون من المفلحين ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ ليسأل الصادقين عن صدقهم ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ سنفرغ لكم أيه الثقلان ﴾ {} وقوله عز وجلّ: ﴿ أفأمنوا مكر الله ﴾ {} الآية، وقوله: ﴿ وكذلك أخذ ربك إذا أخذ القرى وهي ظالمة إن أخذه أليم شديد ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ يوم نحشر ال
28:67.english: And the Quran from its beginning to its end contains fears for whoever reads it with contemplation, and if there were nothing in it except His saying, the Exalted: 'And indeed, I am Forgiving to whoever repents and believes and does righteous deeds then is guided' {} it would be sufficient, since He made forgiveness conditional upon four conditions that the servant is incapable of fulfilling individually, and more severe than it is His saying, the Exalted: 'So as for whoever repents and believes and does righteous deeds, then perhaps he will be among the successful ones' {} and His saying, the Exalted: 'He will ask the truthful ones about their truthfulness' {} and His saying, the Exalted: 'We will attend to you, O you two weighty ones' {} and His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Do they then feel secure from the plan of Allah' {} the verse, and His saying: 'And thus is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are wrongdoers. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe' {} and His saying, the Exalted: 'The day We will gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation' {} the two verses, and His saying, the Exalted: 'And there is not one of you except that he will come to it' {} the verse, and His saying: 'Do whatever you will' {} the verse, and His saying: 'Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter - We increase for him in his harvest' {} the verse, His saying: 'So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it' {} the two verses, and His saying, the Exalted: 'And We will present to what they did of deed' {} the verse, and likewise His saying, the Exalted: 'By time, indeed, mankind is in loss' {} to the end of the surah. These are four conditions for salvation from loss. And the fear of the prophets, despite what overflowed upon them of blessings, was because they did not feel secure from the plan of Allah, the Exalted: 'So none feels secure from the plan of Allah except the losing people' {} until it was narrated that the Prophet and Gabriel, peace be upon them both, wept out of fear from Allah, the Exalted, so Allah revealed to them: 'Why do you weep when I have given you security?' They said: 'And who feels secure from Your plan?' [90] And it is as if they, since they knew that Allah is the Knower of the unseen and that they have no standing on the ultimate matters, did not feel secure that His saying might have...
28:67.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Fear and Hope'

28:70.arabic: وله الشكر فى السموات والأرض وله الحمد فى الأولى والآخرة، والصلاة على محمد ذى المعجزات الظاهرة والآيات الباهرة وعلى آله وأصحابه وسلم تسليماً كثيراً.
28:70.english: And to Him belongs gratitude in the heavens and the earth, and to Him belongs praise in the first (life) and the last (life), and blessings upon Muhammad, possessor of the manifest miracles and the evident signs, and upon his family and his companions, with abundant peace.
28:70.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

28:76.arabic: وكان الحسن بن علي رضي الله عنهما يمر بالسؤال وبين أيديهم كسر فيقولون هلم إلى الغداء يا ابن رسول الله فكان ينزل ويجلس على الطريق ويأكل معهم ويركب ويقول إن الله لا يحب المستكبرين الوجه الثاني أن الذي شغل نفسه بطلب رضا الناس عنه وتحسين اعتقادهم فيه مغرور لأنه لو عرف الله حق المعرفة علم أن الخلق لا يغنون عنه من الله شيئا وأن ضرره ونفعه بيد الله ولا نافع ولا ضار سواه وأن من طلب رضا الناس ومحبتهم بسخط الله سخط الله عليه وأسخط عليه الناس بل رضا الناس غاية لا تنال فرضا الله أولى بالطلب ولذلك قال الشافعي
28:76.english: And Al-Hasan ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with them both) would pass by the poor people while they had bread before them, and they would say: 'Come to lunch, O son of the Messenger of Allah.' So he would dismount, sit on the road, eat with them, and then ride again, saying: 'Indeed, Allah does not love the arrogant ones.' The second aspect is that the one who occupies his Soul (Nafs) with seeking the pleasure of people about him and improving their opinion of him is deluded, because if he knew Allah with true knowledge, he would know that the creation cannot avail him anything from Allah, and that his harm and benefit are in the Hand of Allah, and there is no benefactor nor harmer except Him, and that whoever seeks the pleasure and love of people with the anger of Allah, Allah will be angry with him and make people angry with him. Rather, the pleasure of people is an unattainable goal, so the pleasure of Allah is more worthy of pursuit. Therefore, Al-Shafi'i said to Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la: 'By Allah, I only advise you that there is no way to safety from people, so look at what benefits you and do it.' Therefore, it is said: 'Whoever watches people dies grieving, and the bold one attains pleasure.' And Sahl looked at a man from his companions and said to him: 'Do such and such for something he commanded him to do.' He said: 'O teacher, I cannot do it because of people.' So he turned to his companions and said: 'A servant does not attain the reality of this matter until he is in one of two descriptions: a servant from whose eye people have fallen, so he sees in the world only his Creator, and that no one can harm him nor benefit him; and a servant whose Soul (Nafs) has fallen from his Heart (Qalb), so he does not care in what state they see him.' And Al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'There is no one except that he has a lover and a hater, so if it is like this, then be with the people of obedience to Allah.' And it was said to Al-Hasan: 'O Abu Sa'id, indeed some people attend your gathering, and their aim is only to follow...'
28:76.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Seclusion'

28:76.arabic: البخل ويكتمون ما آتاهم الله من فضله" وقال ﭬ "إياكم والشح فإنه أهلك من كان قبلكم، حملهم على أن سفكوا دماءهم واستحلوا محارمهم"[75] وقال ﭬ "إياكم والشح فإنه دعا من كان قبلكم فسفكوا دماءهم ودعاهم فاستحلوا محارمهم ودعاهم فقطعوا أرحامهم"[76] وقال ﭬ "لا يدخل الجنة بخيل ولا خب ولا خائن لا سيئ الملكة"[77] وفي رواية "ولا جبار" وفي رواية "ولا منان" وقال ﭬ "ثلاث مهلكات؛ شح مطاع وهوى متبع وإعجاب المرء بنفسه"[78] وقال ﭬ "إن الله يبغض ثلاثة: الشيخ الزاني، والبخيل المنان، والمعيل المختال"[79] وقال ﭬ "مثل المنفق
28:76.english: Miserliness and they conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty." And he (peace be upon him) said: "Beware of stinginess (Shuh) for it destroyed those before you; it drove them to shed their blood and violate their prohibitions." [75] And he (peace be upon him) said: "Beware of stinginess (Shuh) for it called those before you, so they shed their blood, and it called them, so they violated their prohibitions, and it called them, so they severed their kinship ties." [76] And he (peace be upon him) said: "A miser (Bakhil) will not enter Paradise, nor a treacherous person, nor a betrayer, nor one of bad character." [77] In a narration: "nor a tyrant (Jabbar)" and in a narration: "nor a reproacher (Mannan)." And he (peace be upon him) said: "Three destructive things: obeyed stinginess (Shuh), followed desire (Hawa), and self-admiration (I'jab al-Mar' bi-Nafsihi)." [78] And he (peace be upon him) said: "Allah hates three: the old fornicator, the miserly reproacher (Bakhil al-Mannan), and the arrogant poor person." [79] And he (peace be upon him) said: "The example of the spender and the miser (Bakhil) is like two men wearing iron shirts from their chests to their collarbones. As for the spender, whenever he spends something, it expands or increases over his skin until it hides his fingertips. As for the miser (Bakhil), whenever he intends to spend something, it shrinks and clings to each ring of his throat until it seizes his collarbones, so he tries to widen it but it does not widen." [80] And he (peace be upon him) said: "Two traits do not gather in a believer: miserliness (Bakhil) and bad character." [81] And he (peace be upon him) said: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from miserliness (Bakhil), and I seek refuge in You from cowardice, and I seek refuge in You from being returned to the most despicable age." [82] And he (peace be upon him) said: "Beware of oppression (Zulm) for oppression is darknesses on the Day of Resurrection, and beware of obscenity (Fahsh) for Allah does not love the obscene nor the one who acts obscenely, and beware of stinginess (Shuh) for indeed stinginess (Shuh) destroyed those before you; it commanded them to lie so they lied, and it commanded them to oppress so they oppressed, and it commanded them to sever ties so they severed." [83] And he (peace be upon him) said: "The worst thing in a man is destructive stinginess (Shuh Hal') and cowardice that strips away." [84] And a martyr was killed during the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), so a weeping woman mourned him and said: "O my martyr!" So he (peace be upon him) said: "What makes you know that he is a martyr? Perhaps he used to speak about what does not concern him or be miserly (Yabkhal) with what does not diminish him." [85] And Jubayr ibn Mut'im said: While we were traveling with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and the people were returning from Khaybar, some Bedouins clung to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) asking him, until they pushed him to a thorny tree and snatched his cloak, so he (peace be upon him) stood and said: "Give me my cloak, for by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if I had livestock equal to the number of these sticks, I would distribute it among you, then you would not find me miserly (Bakhilan), nor a liar, nor a coward." [86] And Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) distributed a portion, so I said: "Were others more deserving of it than them?" He said: "They give me the choice between asking me with obscenity (Fahsh) or accusing me of miserliness (Yabkhaluni), and I am not miserly (Bakhil)." [87] And Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: Two men entered upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and asked him for the price of a camel, so he gave them two dinars; they went out from him and met Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), so they praised and said good and thanks for what he did for them, so Umar entered upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and informed him of it.
28:76.book_title: Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth
28:76.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

28:76.arabic:
در  من
المشركين فقال "لا تسبوا هؤلاء فإنه لا  يخلص  إليهم  شيء  مما  تقولون  وتؤذون
الأحياء ألا إن البذاء لؤم"[62] وقال ﭬ "ليس المؤمن  بالطعان  ولا  اللعان  ولا
الفاحش ولا البذي"[63] وقال ﭬ "الجنة حرام على كل فاحش أن يدخلها"[64]  وقال  ﭬ
"أربعة يؤذون أهل النار في النار  على  ما  بهم  من  الأذى  يسعون  بين  الحميم
والجحيم يدعون بالويل والثبور: رجل يسيل فوه قيحاً ودماً فيقال له ما بال  الأبعد
قد آذاناً على ما بنا من الأذى؟ فيقول إن الأبعد كان  ينظر  إلى  كل  كلمة  قذعة
خبيثة فيستلذها كما يستلذ الر
28:76.english: [68] Hadith: 'Indeed Allah does not love the obscene (al-Fahish) nor the one who speaks obscenely (al-Mutafahhish), shouting in the markets.' Reported by Ibn Abi al-Dunya from the narration of Jabir with a weak chain, and also by him and al-Tabarani from the narration of Usamah ibn Zayd: 'Indeed Allah does not love the obscene (al-Fahish) who speaks obscenely (al-Mutafahhish),' and its chain is good.
28:76.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

28:76.arabic: وقالوا له هلم إلى الغداء يا ابن بنت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال نعم إن الله لا يحب المستكبرين
28:76.english: And they said to him: 'Come to lunch, O son of the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him).' He said: 'Yes, indeed Allah does not love the arrogant ones (al-mustakbireen).'
28:76.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Manners of Eating'

28:77.arabic: فإذا كان فارغا من الفرائض وقدر على الفضائل فينبغي أن يلتمس أفضل الأعمال ليشتغل بها فإن من فاته مزيد ربح وهو قادر على دركه فهو مغبون والأرباح تنال بمزايا الفضائل فبذلك يأخذ العبد من دنياه لآخرته كما قال تعالى ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا وكل ذلك إنما يمكن بصبر ساعة واحدة فإن الساعات ثلاث ساعة مضت لا تعب فيها على العبد كيفما انقضت في مشقة أو رفاهية وساعة مستقبلة لم تأت بعد لا يدري العبد أيعيش إليها أم لا ولا يدرى ما يقضى الله فيها وساعة راهنة ينبغي أن يجاهد فيها نفسه ويراقب فيها ربه فإن لم تأته الساعة
28:77.english: If the servant (Al-'Abd) is free from obligatory duties (Al-Fara'id) and capable of virtues (Al-Fada'il), he should seek the best deeds to occupy himself with them. For whoever misses additional profit while capable of attaining it is cheated, and profits are gained through the merits of virtues. Thus, the servant takes from his worldly life for his Hereafter, as Allah the Exalted said: 'And do not forget your share of the world (Al-Dunya).' All of this is only possible with patience for a single hour (Saa'ah). For the hours are three: a past hour that does not burden the servant however it passed, in hardship or ease; a future hour that has not yet come—the servant does not know if he will live to it or not, nor does he know what Allah decrees in it; and a present hour in which he should strive against his Soul (Nafs) and observe his Lord (Rabb) in it. If the second hour does not come to him, he will not regret the loss of this hour; and if the second hour comes to him, he fulfills his right from it as he fulfilled from the first. And he should not extend his hope for fifty years, making the resolve for observation (Al-Muraqabah) in it prolonged; rather, he should be a child of his moment as if in his last breaths, for perhaps it is his last breath and he does not know. And if it is possible to be his last breath, he should be in a state where he does not dislike that death overtakes him in that condition.
28:77.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

28:77.arabic: وقال معاذ بن جبل رضي الله عنه في وصيته إنه لا بد لك من نصيبك في الدنيا وأنت إلى نصيبك من الآخرة أحوج فابدأ بنصيبك من الآخرة فخذه فإنك ستمر على نصيبك من الدنيا فتنظمه قال الله تعالى ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا أي لا تنس في الدنيا نصيبك منها للآخرة فإنها مزرعة الآخرة وفيها تكتسب الحسنات
28:77.english: And Mu'adh ibn Jabal (may Allah be pleased with him) said in his testament: 'It is inevitable for you to have your portion (Naseeb) in the worldly life (Dunya), and you are more in need of your portion from the Hereafter (Akhirah). So begin with your portion from the Hereafter and take it, for you will pass by your portion from the worldly life and organize it.' Allah the Exalted said: 'And do not forget your portion (Naseeb) from the worldly life (Dunya)' meaning: do not forget in the worldly life your portion from it for the Hereafter, for it is the cultivation field (Mazra'ah) of the Hereafter, and in it you acquire good deeds (Hasanat).
28:77.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Etiquette of Earning'

28:77.arabic:
ي
                                                      في العلل والموقوف أصح.
  [64]  حديث الجنة حرام على كل فاحش أن يدخلها أخرجه ابن أبي الدنيا وأبو نعيم
                                         في الحلية من حديث عبد الله بن عمرو.
  [65]  حديث أربعة يؤذون أهل النار على ما بهم من الأذى الحديث وفيه إن الأبعد
 كان ينظر إلى كل كلمة خبيثة فيستلذها كما يستلذ الرفث أخرجه ابن أبي الدنيا من
    حديث شفى بن مانع واختلف في صحبته فذكره أبو نعيم في الصحابة وذكره البخاري
28:77.english: In the causes and the stopped (hadiths) is more authentic. [64] Hadith: Paradise is forbidden for every obscene person to enter it, transmitted by Ibn Abi al-Dunya and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr. [65] Hadith: Four torment the people of Hell with what they have of torment, the hadith and in it: The farthest one looks at every evil word and delights in it as one delights in obscenity, transmitted by Ibn Abi al-Dunya from the hadith of Shafi ibn Ma'ni, and there is disagreement about his companionship, so Abu Nu'aym mentioned him among the Companions, and al-Bukhari and Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the Followers. [66] Hadith: O Aisha, if obscenity were a man, he would be an evil man, transmitted by Ibn Abi al-Dunya from the narration of Ibn Lahi'ah from Abu al-Nadr from Abu Salamah from her. [67] Hadith: Vulgarity and eloquence are two branches of hypocrisy, transmitted by al-Tirmidhi and al-Hakim considered it good and authenticated it according to their conditions from the hadith of Abu Umamah, and it has preceded. [68] Hadith: Indeed, Allah does not love the obscene nor the one who shouts obscenities in the markets, transmitted by Ibn Abi al-Dunya from the hadith of Jabir with a weak chain, and for him and al-Tabarani from the hadith of Usamah ibn Zaid: Indeed, Allah does not love the obscene, the one who shouts obscenities, and its chain is good. [69] Hadith: Jabir ibn Samurah: Indeed, obscenity and shouting obscenities are not from Islam in anything, the hadith transmitted by Ahmad and Ibn Abi al-Dunya with an authentic chain. [70] Hadith: A Bedouin said: Advise me, so he said: Upon you is the fear (Taqwa) of Allah, and if a man reproaches you with something he knows in you, then do not reproach him with something you know in him, the hadith transmitted by Ahmad and al-Tabarani with a good chain from the hadith of Abu Jari al-Hujaymi, it is said his name is Jabir ibn Salim or Salim ibn Jabir. [71] Hadith: Iyad ibn Himar: I said: O Messenger of Allah, a man from my people insults me and he is beneath me, is there any harm if I retaliate against him? He said: The two insulters are two devils lying to each other and reviling each other, transmitted by Abu Dawud and al-Tayalisi and its origin is with Ahmad. [72] Hadith: Insulting a Muslim is corruption (Fisq) and fighting him is disbelief (Kufr), agreed upon from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud. [73] Hadith: The two insulters, what they said is upon the beginner until the wronged one transgresses, transmitted by Muslim from the hadith of Abu Hurairah and he said: As long as he does not transgress. [74] Hadith: Cursed is the one who insults his parents, and in a narration: From the greatest major sins is that a man insults his parents, the hadith transmitted by Ahmad, Abu Ya'la, and al-Tabarani from the hadith of...
28:77.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

28:77.arabic: وَمَرَّ الْحَسَنُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا بِقَوْمٍ مِنَ الْمَسَاكِينِ الَّذِينَ يَسْأَلُونَ النَّاسَ عَلَى الطَّرِيقِ وَقَدْ نَشَرُوا كِسْرًا عَلَى الْأَرْضِ فِي الرَّمْلِ وَهُمْ يَأْكُلُونَ وَهُوَ عَلَى بَغْلَتِهِ فَسَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِمْ فَقَالُوا لَهُ هَلُمَّ إِلَى الْغَدَاءِ يَا ابْنَ بِنْتِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَقَالَ نَعَمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُسْتَكْبِرِينَ فَنَزَلَ وَقَعَدَ مَعَهُمْ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ وَأَكَلَ ثُمَّ سَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَرَكِ
28:77.english: And Al-Hasan ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with them both) passed by a group of the poor (Masakin) who ask people on the road, and they had spread crumbs on the ground in the sand and they were eating, and he was on his mule. He greeted them, and they said to him: 'Come to lunch, O son of the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him).' He said: 'Yes, indeed Allah does not love the arrogant (Mustakbirin).' So he dismounted and sat with them on the ground and ate. Then he greeted them and mounted and said: 'I have answered you, so answer me.' They said: 'Yes.' So he promised them a known time, and they attended, and he presented to them the finest food and sat eating with them.
28:77.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Manners of Eating'

28:77.arabic: الباب الرابع في الإحسان في المعاملة وقد أمر الله تعالى بالعدل والإحسان جميعا والعدل سبب النجاة فقط وهو يجري من التجارة مجرى رأس المال والإحسان سبب الفوز ونيل السعادة وهو يجري من التجارة مجرى الربح ولا يعد من الغفلاء من قنع في معاملات الدنيا برأس ماله فكذا في معاملات الآخرة فلا ينبغي للمتدين أن يقتصر على العدل واجتناب الظلم ويدع أبواب الإحسان وقد قال الله وأحسن كما أحسن الله إليك وقال عز وجل إن الله يأمر بالعدل والإحسان وقال سبحانه إن رحمت الله قريب من المحسنين ونعني بالإحسان فعل ما ينتفع به المع
28:77.english: Chapter Four on Excellence (Ihsan) in Transactions. And Allah the Exalted has commanded justice and excellence (Ihsan) together. Justice is the cause of salvation only, and it flows in trade like capital. Excellence (Ihsan) is the cause of triumph and attainment of happiness, and it flows in trade like profit. One is not considered among the heedless who is content in worldly transactions with his capital, likewise in the transactions of the Hereafter. So it is not fitting for the religious person to limit himself to justice and avoiding oppression and abandon the doors of excellence (Ihsan). And Allah has said: 'وَأَحْسِنْ كَمَا أَحْسَنَ اللَّهُ إِلَيْكَ' (And do excellence (Ihsan) as Allah has done excellence (Ihsan) to you). And the Almighty said: 'Indeed, Allah commands justice and excellence (Ihsan).' And He, glorified be He, said: 'Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the doers of excellence (Muhsinin).' And we mean by excellence (Ihsan) doing what benefits the transactor, and it is not obligatory upon him, but it is a favor from him. For the obligatory enters into the chapter of justice and avoiding oppression, and we have mentioned it. And the rank of excellence (Ihsan) is attained by one of six matters: The first is in overcharging (Mughabana). So one should not overcharge his companion with what is not usually overcharged. As for the basis of overcharging (Mughabana), it is permitted because selling is for profit, and that is not possible except with some overcharging. But moderation is observed in it. If the buyer offers an increase over the customary profit, either due to intense desire or intense need for it at the moment, then one should refrain from accepting it, for that is from excellence (Ihsan). And as long as there is no deception, taking the increase is not oppression. Some scholars have held that overcharging by what exceeds one-third necessitates the option (Khiyar), but we do not see that. However, from excellence (Ihsan) is to reduce that overcharging. It is narrated that Yunus ibn 'Ubayd had garments of varying prices: one type valued at four hundred each, and each garment valued at two hundred. He went to prayer and left his nephew in the shop. A Bedouin came and requested a garment for four hundred, so he showed him from the two-hundred garments. He admired it and was pleased with it, so he bought it and went away with it on his hands. Yunus met him and recognized the garment.
28:77.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Earning'

28:79.arabic: وترك التزين والتجمل بزينة الدنيا طمعاً في زينة الجنة، وترك المطاعم اللذيذة طمعاً في فواكه الجنة وخوفاً من أن يقال له: " أذهبتم طيباتكم في حياتكم الدنيا" فآثر في جميع ذلك ما وعد على ما تيسر له في الدنيا عفواً صفواً لعلمه بأن ما في الآخرة خير وأبقى، وأن ما سوى هذا فمعاملات دنيوية لا جدوى لها في الآخرة أصلاً. بيان فضيلة الزهد قال الله تعالى: " فخرج على قومه في زينته . . . إلى قوله تعالى . . . وقال الذين أوتوا العلم ويلكم ثواب الله خير لمن آمن " فنسب الزهد إلى العلماء ووصف أهله بالعلم وهو غاية الثنا
28:79.english: And abandoning adornment and beautification with the adornment (zīnah) of the worldly life (al-dunyā) out of hope for the adornment (zīnah) of Paradise, and abandoning delicious foods out of hope for the fruits of Paradise and fear that it will be said to him: "You exhausted your good things in your worldly life (ḥayātukum al-dunyā)" - so he preferred in all of that what was promised over what became available to him in the worldly life (al-dunyā) freely and purely, knowing that what is in the Hereafter (al-ākhirah) is better and more lasting, and that other than this is worldly transactions that have no benefit in the Hereafter (al-ākhirah) at all. Clarification of the virtue of asceticism (al-zuhd). Allah the Exalted said: "So he went forth to his people in his adornment (zīnatihi)... up to His saying... and those who were given knowledge said: Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for one who believes" - thus He attributed asceticism (al-zuhd) to the scholars and described its people with knowledge, which is the ultimate praise. And He said: "Those will be given their reward twice for what they patiently endured" - and it came in the interpretation concerning asceticism (al-zuhd) in the worldly life (al-dunyā).
28:79.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

28:80.arabic: قال الله تعالى: " فخرج على قومه في زينته . . . إلى قوله تعالى . . . وقال الذين أوتوا العلم ويلكم ثواب الله خير لمن آمن " فنسب الزهد إلى العلماء ووصف أهله بالعلم وهو غاية الثناء، وقال تعالى: " أولئك يؤتون أجرهم مرتين بما صبروا " وجاء في التفسير على الزهد في الدنيا.
28:80.english: Allah the Exalted said: "So he went forth before his people in his adornment... until the saying of Allah the Exalted... and those who were given knowledge said: Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for he who believes." So He attributed asceticism (Zuhd) to the scholars and described its people with knowledge, and that is the utmost praise. And He the Exalted said: "Those will be given their reward twice for what they patiently endured." And it came in the interpretation regarding asceticism (Zuhd) in the worldly life.
28:80.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

28:80.arabic: وإلى تعريف نفاسة الآخرة الإشارة بقوله عز وجل: "وقال الذين أوتوا ويلكم ثواب الله خير " فنبه على أن العلم بنفاسة الجوهر هو المرغب عن عوضه، ولما لم يتصور الزهد إلا بمعارضة ورغبة عن المحبوب في أحب منه قال رجل في دعائه: اللهم أرني الدنيا كما تراها، فقال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " لا تقل هكذا " ولكن قل: أرني الدنيا كما أريتها الصالحين من عبادك" وهذا لأن الله تعالى يراها حقيرة كما هي، وكل مخلوق فهو بالإضافة إلى جلاله حقير والعبد يراها حقيرة في نفسه بالإضافة إلى ما هو خير له، ولا يتصور أن يرى بائع ا
28:80.english: And to define the preciousness (نفاسة) of the Hereafter (الآخرة), there is an indication in His Exalted saying: "And those who were given knowledge said, 'Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for he who believes and does righteous deeds, and none will receive it except the patient.'" So He alerted that knowledge of the preciousness (نفاسة) of the jewel (الجوهر) is what motivates one away from its substitute. And since asceticism (الزهد) cannot be conceived except through opposition and desire away from the beloved for what is more beloved, a man said in his supplication: 'O Allah, show me the world (الدنيا) as You see it.' So the Prophet (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Do not say like this,' but say: 'Show me the world as You showed it to the righteous among Your servants.' This is because Allah the Exalted sees it as contemptible as it is, and every creature is contemptible in relation to His majesty (جلاله), and the servant (العبد) sees it as contemptible in himself in relation to what is better for him. And it is inconceivable that the seller of a horse, even if he desires away from his horse, sees it as he sees earth insects, for example, because he is originally independent from insects but not independent from the horse. And Allah the Exalted is rich (غني) in His essence from everything other than Him, so He sees everything in one degree in relation to His majesty (جلاله), and sees it as varying in relation to others. And the ascetic (الزاهد) is the one who sees its variation in relation to himself, not to others. As for the action emanating from the state of asceticism (الزهد), it is a single abandonment because it is a sale and transaction and exchange of what is better for what is lower. So just as the action emanating from the contract of sale is abandoning the sold item and removing it from the hand and taking the substitute, likewise asceticism (الزهد) necessitates abandoning what is abstained from entirely, which is the world (الدنيا) in its entirety with its causes, preliminaries, and connections.
28:80.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

28:83.arabic: وفي قوله تعالى: "تلك الدار الآخرة نجعلها للذين لا يريدون علواً في الأرض ولا فساداً" إنه الرياسة والتطاول في البنيان.
28:83.english: And in His saying, the Exalted: "That abode of the Hereafter, We make it for those who do not desire exaltation (ʿuluwwan) in the earth nor corruption (fasādan)" — indeed, it is leadership (riyāsah) and overreaching (taṭāwulan) in building.
28:83.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

28:88.arabic: ههنا نظران نظر بعين التوحيد المحض وهذا النظر يعرفك قطعا انه الشاكر وانه المشكور وانه المحب وانه المحبوب وهذا نظر من عرف انه ليس في الوجود غيره وان كل شيء هالك إلا وجهه وان ذلك صدق في كل حال أزلا وابدا لأن الغير هو الذي يتصور ان يكون له بنفسه قوام ومثل هذا الغير لا وجود له بل هو محال أن يوجد اذ الموجود المحقق هو القائم بنفسه وما ليس له بنفسه قوام فليس له بنفسه وجود بل هو قائم بغيره فهو موجود بغيره فان اعتبر ذاته ولم يلتفت الى غيره لم يكن له وجود ألبته وإنما الموجود هو القائم بنفسه والقائم بنفسه ه
28:88.english: Here are two perspectives: a perspective with the eye of pure Oneness (Tawhid), and this perspective makes you know decisively that He is the One Who gives thanks (Shakir) and He is the One Who is thanked (Mashkur), and He is the Lover (Muhibb) and He is the Beloved (Mahbub). And this is the perspective of one who knows that there is nothing else in existence except Him, and that 'every thing is perishing except His Face (Wajh)', and that this is true in every state, eternally and forever. Because the other (Ghair) is that which is imagined to have subsistence (Qiwam) by itself, and such an other has no existence; rather, it is impossible for it to exist, since the true existent (Mawjud) is the Self-Subsisting (Al-Qa'im bi-Nafsih). And what does not have subsistence by itself has no existence by itself; rather, it subsists by another, so it exists by another. If you consider its essence and do not pay attention to another, it has no existence at all. Rather, the existent is the Self-Subsisting, and the Self-Subsisting is that which, if the absence of another were imagined, would remain existent. If, along with its self-subsistence, the existence of another subsists by its existence, then it is the Sustainer (Qayyum), and there is no Sustainer except One, and it is inconceivable to be otherwise. Therefore, there is nothing in existence except the Living, the Sustainer (Al-Hayy Al-Qayyum), and He is the One, the Eternal (Al-Wahid Al-Samad). So when you look from this station, you know that everything originates from Him and returns to Him, so He is the One Who gives thanks and He is the One Who is thanked, and He is the Lover and He is the Beloved.
28:88.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

28:88.arabic: فكان أوّل مقاماته نهاية مقامات الموحدين وهو ان لا يرى الا الله تعالى وافعاله فيستعيذ بفعل من فعل فانظر الى ماذا انتهت نهايته اذ انتهى الى الواحد الحق حتى ارتفع من نظره ومشاهدته سوى الذات الحق، ولقد كان ﭬ لا يرقى من رتبة الى اخرى الا ويرى الاولى بعدا بالإضافة الى الثانية فكان يستغفر الله من الاولى ويرى ذلك نقصا في سلوكه وتقصيرا في مقامه واليه الاشارة بقوله ﭬ: (إنه ليغان على قلبي حتى استغفر الله في اليوم والليلة سبعين مرة[49]) فكان ذلك لترقية الى سبعين مقاما بعضها فوق البعض أوّلها وان كان مجاوزا ا
28:88.english: So his first stations were the ultimate stations of the monotheists (al-Muwahhidīn), which is that he sees nothing except Allah the Exalted and His actions, so he seeks refuge with an action from an action. Look at what his ultimate end reached, for he reached the True One (al-Wāḥid al-Ḥaqq) until there rose from his sight and witnessing anything other than the True Essence (al-Dhāt al-Ḥaqq). And indeed he ﷺ would not ascend from one rank to another except that he would see the first as distance in addition to the second, so he would seek forgiveness from Allah for the first and see that as deficiency in his conduct (sulūk) and shortcoming in his station (maqām). To this is the allusion in his saying ﷺ: 'Indeed, it covers over my heart (qalb) until I seek forgiveness from Allah seventy times in a day and night.' So that was for ascending to seventy stations, some above others, the first of them even though it had surpassed the utmost limits of creation, but it was deficiency in relation to the last of them, so his seeking forgiveness was for that. And when 'Ā'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: 'Has not Allah forgiven you what preceded of your sin and what will follow? So what is this weeping in prostration and this intense effort?' He said: 'Should I not be a grateful servant ('abd shakūr)?' Its meaning is: Should I not be a seeker of increase in the stations? For gratitude (shukr) is the cause of increase, as the Exalted said: 'If you are grateful, I will surely increase you.' And if we delve into the seas of unveiling (mukāshafah), then let us rein in the bridle, and let us return to what befits the sciences of interaction (mu'āmalah), so we say: The prophets, peace be upon them, were sent for the call of the...
28:88.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

28:88.arabic: وقال ﭬ "يخرج من النار عنق له أذنان تسمعان وعينان تبصران ولسان ينطق يقول: وكلت بثلاثة: بكل جبار عنيد وبكل من دعا مع الله إلهاً آخر وبالمصورين"[7]
28:88.english: And he (the Prophet) said: "There will emerge from the Fire a neck having two ears that hear and two eyes that see and a tongue that speaks, saying: I have been entrusted with three: with every arrogant obstinate one, and with everyone who calls upon with Allah another god, and with the image-makers."
28:88.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

28:88.arabic: ومن عرفه عرف أن كل شيء ما خلا الله باطل وأن كل شيء هالك إلا وجهه لا أنه سيبطل في ثاني الحال بل هو الآن باطل إن اعتبر ذاته من حيث هو إلا أن يعتبر وجوده من حيث إنه موجود بالله عز وجل وبقدرته فيكون له بطريق التبعية ثبات وبطريق الاستقلال بطلان محض وهذا مبدأ من مبادىء علم المكاشفة
28:88.english: And whoever knows Him knows that everything except Allah is false (Bāṭil) and that everything perishes (Hālik) except His Face (Wajh), not that it will become false in a second moment, but it is now false if considered in its essence from what it is, except if its existence is considered from the perspective that it exists by Allah, the Exalted and Glorified, and by His power, so it has stability through the way of following (Tābiʿiyya) and through the way of independence (Istiqlāl) pure falsehood (Bāṭil), and this is a principle from the principles of the science of unveiling (ʿIlm al-Mukāshafa).
28:88.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

28:88.arabic: وفي بعض الروايات (وكل شيء هالك إلا وجهه له الحكم وإليه ترجعون) فينبغي أن يستعمل هذه السنة في رجوعه وإذا أشرف على مدينته يحرك الدابة ويقول اللهم اجعل لنا بها قرارا ورزقا حسنا ثم ليرسل إلى أهله من يخبرهم بقدومه كي لا يقدم عليهم بغتة فذلك هو السنة[69] ولا ينبغي أن يطرق أهله ليلا فإذا دخل البلد فليقصد المسجد أولا وليصل ركعتين فهو السنة[70] كذلك كان يفعل رسول الله ﭬ فإذا دخل بيته قال توبا توبا لربنا أوبا لا يغادر علينا حوبا فإذا استقر في منزله فلا ينبغي أن ينسى ما أنعم الله به عليه من زيارة بيته وحرم
28:88.english: And in some narrations (and everything is perishing except His Face, to Him belongs the judgment and to Him you will be returned) so it is proper to practice this Sunnah in his return, and when he approaches his city, he should urge the mount and say: O Allah, make for us in it a settlement and good provision. Then he should send to his family someone to inform them of his arrival so that he does not come upon them suddenly, for that is the Sunnah[69]. And it is not proper that he knock on his family's door at night. When he enters the town, he should head to the mosque first and pray two units of prayer, for that is the Sunnah[70]. Likewise, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to do. When he entered his house, he would say: Repentance, repentance to our Lord, returning, not leaving upon us sin. When he settles in his home, he should not forget what Allah has bestowed upon him of visiting His House, His Sanctuary, and the grave of His Prophet ﷺ, thus repaying that blessing by returning to heedlessness (Ghaflah) and amusement and delving into sins. That is not the sign of the accepted pilgrimage (Hajj al-Mabrur), rather its sign is that he returns abstaining (Zahid) from the worldly life (Dunya), desiring (Raghib) the Hereafter (Akhirah), prepared for meeting the Lord of the House after meeting the House.
28:88.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

29:7.arabic: وقال أبو طالب المكي العمل بالجوارح من الإيمان ولا يتم دونه وادعى الإجماع فيه واستدل بأدلة تشعر بنقيض غرضه كقوله تعالى الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات إذ هذا يدل على أن العمل وراء الإيمان لا من نفس الإيمان وإلا فيكون العمل في حكم المعاد
29:7.english: And Abu Talib al-Makki said: 'Action with the limbs (al-Jawarih) is from faith (al-Iman) and it is not complete without it,' and he claimed consensus in this, and he argued with evidences that suggest the opposite of his purpose, such as the saying of The Most High: 'Those who believe and do righteous deeds (al-Salihat)' since this indicates that action is beyond faith, not from the essence of faith itself, otherwise action would be in the ruling of repetition.
29:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

29:9.arabic: وقال أبو طالب المكي العمل بالجوارح من الإيمان ولا يتم دونه وادعى الإجماع فيه واستدل بأدلة تشعر بنقيض غرضه كقوله تعالى الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات إذ هذا يدل على أن العمل وراء الإيمان لا من نفس الإيمان وإلا فيكون العمل في حكم المعاد
29:9.english: And Abu Talib al-Makki said: 'Action with the limbs (al-Jawarih) is from faith (al-Iman) and it is not complete without it.' And he claimed consensus (al-Ijma') in this and argued with evidences that indicate the opposite of his purpose, such as the saying of The Most High: 'Those who believe and do righteous deeds (al-Salihat)' - since this indicates that action is beyond faith, not from the essence of faith itself, otherwise action would be in the position of repetition (al-Mu'ad).
29:9.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

29:17.arabic: وإن عملت لغيري فقد استوجبت مقتى وعقابي إذ كنت عبدا لي تأكل رزقي وتترفه بنعمتي ثم تعمل لغيري أما سمعتني أقول إن الذين تدعون من دون الله عباد أمثالكم إن الذين تعبدون من دون الله لا يملكون لكم رزقا فابتغوا عند الله الرزق واعبدوه ويحك أما سمعتني أقول ألا لله الدين الخالص فإذا عرف العبد أنه بصدد هذه المطالبات والتوبيخات طالب نفسه قبل أن تطالب وأعد للسؤال جوابا وليكن الجواب صوابا فلا يبدئ ولا يعيد إلا بعد التثبت ولايحرك جفنا ولا أنمله إلا بعد التأمل
29:17.english: And if you worked for other than Me, then you have deserved My wrath and punishment, since you were a slave to Me, eating My provision (Rizq) and enjoying My blessings, then you work for other than Me. Have you not heard Me say: 'Indeed, those whom you call upon besides Allah are slaves like yourselves. Indeed, those whom you worship besides Allah do not possess for you any provision (Rizq), so seek provision (Rizq) from Allah and worship Him.' Woe to you! Have you not heard Me say: 'Indeed, the religion (Deen) is purely for Allah.' So when the slave (Abd) knows that he is facing these demands and rebukes, he questions himself before being questioned, and prepares an answer for the questioning, and let the answer be correct. So he does not begin nor repeat except after verification, and he does not move an eyelid nor a fingertip except after contemplation.
29:17.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

29:17.arabic: فالأحرى بالعبد ان لم يحسن الصبر على البلاء والقضاء وأفضي به الضعف الى الشكوى ان تكون شكواه الى الله تعالى فهو المبلى والقادر على ازالة البلاء وذل العبد لمولاه عز والشكوى الى غيره ذل وإظهار الذل للعبد مع كونه عبدا مثله ذل قبيح قال الله تعالى: ﴿ إن الذين تعبدون من دون الله لا يملكون لكم رزقا فابتغوا عند الله الرزق واعبدوه واشكروا له ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ إن الذين تدعون من دون الله عباد امثالكم ﴾ {} فالشكر باللسان من جملة الشكر.
29:17.english: It is more appropriate for the servant (Abd) that if he cannot properly endure patience (Sabr) on the trial (Bala') and the decree (Qada'), and weakness leads him to complaint, that his complaint be to Allah the Exalted, for He is the One who afflicts and is capable of removing the trial, and the humility (Dhull) of the servant (Abd) to his Master (Mawla) is honorable, while complaint to other than Him is humiliation (Dhull), and displaying humiliation (Dhull) to a servant (Abd) while he is a servant (Abd) like him is ugly humiliation (Dhull). Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, those you worship besides Allah do not possess for you [the power of] provision. So seek from Allah provision and worship Him and be grateful (Ashkuru) to Him.' And He said: 'Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah are servants (Ibad) like you.' So gratitude (Shukr) with the tongue (Lisan) is from the totality of gratitude (Shukr).
29:17.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

29:17.arabic: وقال تعالى: " إن الذين تعبدون من دون الله لا يملكون لكم رزقاً فابتغوا عند الله الرزق واعبدوه ". وكل ما ذكر في القرآن من التوحيد فهو تنبيه على قطع الملاحظة عن الأغيار والتوكل على الواحد القهار.
29:17.english: And He, the Exalted, said: "Indeed, those whom you worship besides Allah do not possess for you provision (Rizq), so seek provision (Rizq) with Allah and worship Him." And everything mentioned in the Quran regarding Monotheism (Tawhid) is an alert to sever observation from the others (Al-Aghyar) and to rely (Tawakkul) upon the One, the Subduer (Al-Qahhar).
29:17.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

29:43.arabic: وقال تعالى: ﴿وتلك الأمثال نضربها للناس وما يعقلها إلا العالمون﴾ وقال تعالى: ﴿ولو ردوه إلى الرسول وإلى أولي الأمر منهم لعلمه الذين يستنبطونه منهم﴾ رد حكمه في الوقائع إلى استنباطهم وألحق رتبتهم برتبة الأنبياء في كشف حكم الله.
29:43.english: And He (Allah) said: 'And these examples We present them to the people, and none comprehends them except the knowledgeable ones (Al-Alimun).' And He (Allah) said: 'And if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those of authority among them, the ones who derive it (Yastanbitunahu) from them would have known it.' He referred His ruling in occurrences to their derivation (Istinbat) and attached their rank to the rank of the Prophets in uncovering the ruling of Allah.
29:43.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

29:43.arabic: وذلك ظاهر من أدلة الشرع قال ﭬ: (إن للقرآن ظاهرا وباطنا وحدا ومطلعا[22]) وقال علي رضي الله عنه وأشار إلى صدره إن ههنا علوما جمة لو وجدت لها حملة. وقال ﭬ: (نحن معاشر الأنبياء أمرنا أن نكلم الناس على قدر عقولهم[23]) وقال ﭬ: (ما حدث أحد قوما بحديث لم تبلغه عقولهم إلا كان فتنة عليهم[24]) وقال الله تعالى: ﴿ وتلك الأمثال نضربها للناس وما يعقلها إلا العالمون ﴾ {} وقال ﭬ: (إن من العلم كهيئة المكنون لا يعلمه إلا العالمون بالله تعالى[25]) الحديث إلى آخره كما أوردناه في كتاب العلم.
29:43.english: And that is evident from the proofs of the Sacred Law (Sharia). He (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, the Quran has an outward (Zahir) and an inward (Batin), a limit (Hadd) and a point of ascent (Matla').' And Ali (may God be pleased with him) said, pointing to his chest: 'Here are abundant sciences, if only I could find carriers for them.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'We, the community of prophets, have been commanded to speak to people according to the capacity of their intellects (Aql).' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever relates to a people a discourse that their intellects (Aql) have not reached, it will only be a trial (Fitnah) upon them.' And God the Exalted said: 'And these similitudes (Amthal) We strike them for the people, and none comprehends them except the knowers (Alimun).' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, from knowledge is like the form of the concealed (Maknun); none knows it except the knowers (Alimun) of God the Exalted.' The hadith to its end as we have cited it in the Book of Knowledge.
29:43.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Foundations of Belief'

29:45.arabic: وقال تعالى: " ومساكن طيبة في جنات عدن ورضوان من الله أكبر " فقد رفع الله الرضا فوق جنات عدن كما رفع ذكره الصلاة حيث قال: " إن الصلاة تنهي عن الفحشاء والمنكر ولذكر الله أكبر " فكما أن مشاهدة المذكور في الصلاة أكبر من الصلاة فرضوان رب الجنة أعلى من الجنة بل هو غاية مطلب سكان الجنان.
29:45.english: And Allah the Exalted said: "And pleasant dwellings in Gardens of Eden and pleasure (رضوان) from Allah is greater." For Allah has elevated pleasure (رضا) above the Gardens of Eden, just as He elevated its remembrance (ذكر) of prayer where He said: "Indeed, prayer prevents from immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance (ذكر) of Allah is greater." So just as witnessing the Remembered One (المذكور) in prayer is greater than prayer, the pleasure (رضوان) of the Lord of the Garden is higher than the Garden; rather, it is the ultimate goal of the inhabitants of the Gardens.
29:45.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

29:45.arabic: وإن العبد ليأكل أكلة أو يفعل فعلة فيحرم بها قيام سنة وكما أن الصلاة تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر فكذلك الفحشاء تنهى عن الصلاة وسائر الخيرات.
29:45.english: And indeed, the servant may eat a morsel or commit an act, and thereby be deprived of standing (in prayer) for a year. And just as the Prayer (As-Salah) forbids from the indecencies (Al-Fahsha') and the wrongs (Al-Munkar), so too do the indecencies forbid from the Prayer and all other good deeds.
29:45.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Book of Knowledge'

29:48.arabic: وقد تقدم بعضه وروى ابن مردويه من حديث ابن عباس في قوله وما كنت تتلو من قبله من كتاب ولا تخطه بيمينك قال كان نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أميا لا يقرأ ولا يكتب وقد تقدم في العلم
29:48.english: And some of it has preceded, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from the hadith of Ibn Abbas regarding His saying 'And you were not reciting before it from a book nor writing it with your right hand' - he said: The Prophet of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was unlettered (Ummi), not reading nor writing, and it has preceded in the knowledge.
29:48.book_title: Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character
29:48.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character'

29:49.arabic: وقال عز وجل: ﴿بل هو آيات بينات في صدور الذين أوتوا العلم﴾ وقال تعالى: ﴿خلق الإنسان¤ علمه البيان﴾ وإنما ذكر ذلك في معرض الامتنان.
29:49.english: And the Mighty and Majestic said: 'Rather, it is clear signs in the chests (Sudur) of those who have been given knowledge (Al-'Ilm).' And the Exalted said: 'He created the human being, He taught him the clear expression (Al-Bayan).' And indeed, He mentioned that in the context of bestowing favor (Al-Imtinan).
29:49.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

29:52.arabic:
أنه فيماذا يتفكر لم يقدر عليه  لأن  مجارى  الفكر  غير  محصورة
وثمراته غير متناهية نعم نحن نجتهد في ضبط مجاريه بالإضافة  إلى  مهمات  العلوم
الدينية وبالإضافة إلى الأحوال التى هى مقامات السالكين ويكون ذلك  ضبطا  جمليا
فإن تفصيل ذلك يستدعى شرح العلوم كلها وجملة هذه  الكتب  كالشرح  لبعضها  فإنها
مشتملة على علوم تلك العلوم تستفاد من أفكار مخصوصة فلنشر إلى ضبط الجامع  فيها
ليحصل الوقوف على مجارى الفكر.
                              بيان مجارى الفكر
أعلم أن الفكر قد يجرى في أمر يتعلق بالدين وقد يجرى  ف
29:52.english:
That in what he thinks about, he cannot encompass it because the channels of thought are not limited, and its fruits are endless. Yes, we strive to regulate its channels in addition to the important matters of religious sciences and in addition to the states (Ahwal) which are the stations (Maqamat) of the travelers (Salikin). And this will be a general regulation, for detailing that requires explaining all the sciences, and the entirety of these books is like an explanation for some of them, for they contain the sciences of those sciences derived from specific thoughts. So let us proceed to regulate the comprehensive in them to achieve understanding of the channels of thought.
                              Explanation of the Channels of Thought
Know that thought may run in a matter related to religion, and it may run in what is related to other than religion. Our aim is only what is related to religion, so we will leave the other division and focus on religion, the transaction (Mu'amalah) that is between the servant (Abd) and the Lord (Rabb) Almighty. So all the thoughts of the servant are either related to the servant and his attributes and his states (Ahwal), or related to the Worshipped One and His attributes and His actions; it is not possible to go beyond these two divisions. And what is related to the servant is either a consideration of what is beloved to the Lord Almighty or what is disliked, and there is no need for thought in other than these two divisions. And what is related to the Lord Almighty is either a consideration of His Essence (Dhat) and His attributes and His Beautiful Names (Asma' al-Husna), or it is in His actions and His dominion (Mulk) and His sovereignty (Malakut) and all that is in the heavens and the earth and what is between them. And it becomes clear to you the confinement of thought in these divisions by an example, which is that the state of those who walk to Allah Almighty and yearn for meeting Him relates to his Beloved or relates to himself. So if he thinks about his Beloved, then either he thinks about His beauty and the goodness of His image in His Essence to delight in thinking about Him and witnessing Him, or he thinks about His subtle, good actions indicating His character and attributes to be that which doubles the pleasure and strengthens his love. And if he thinks about himself, then his thought is in his attributes which drop him from the eye of his Beloved so that he abstains from them, or in the attributes which bring him near to Him and make him beloved to Him so that he becomes characterized by them. So if he thinks about something outside these divisions, then that is outside the limit of love (Ishq) and is a deficiency in it, because the complete, perfect love is what overwhelms the lover and fills the heart (Qalb) so that it leaves no room for other than it. So the lover of Allah Almighty should be like that, so his view and thought do not go beyond his Beloved. And as long as his thought is confined in these four divisions, it is not at all outside the requirement of love. So let us begin with the first division, which is his thinking about the attributes of himself and the actions of himself to distinguish the beloved among them from the disliked, for this thought is that which relates to the science of transaction (Ilm al-Mu'amalah) which is the purpose of this book. And the other division relates to the science of unveiling (Ilm al-Mukashafah), then every...
29:52.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Contemplation'

29:53.arabic: وحذرهم أن يأخذهم بغتة وهم لا يشعرون فقال "ما ينظرون إلا صيحة واحدة تأخذهم وهم يخصمون فلا يستطيعون توصية ولا إلى أهلهم يرجعون" والصلاة والسلام على محمد رسوله الذي يسير تحت لوائه النبيون، وعلى آله وأصحابه الأئمة المهديين، والسادة المرضيين، صلاة يوازي عددها عدد ما كان من خلق الله وما سيكون، ويحظى ببركتها الأولون والآخرون، وسلم تسليماً كثيرا. أما بعد فإن الغضب شعلة نار اقتبست من نار الله الموقدة التي تطلع على الأفئدة، وإنها لمستكنة في طي الفؤاد. استكنان الجمر تحت الرماد، ويستخرجها الكبر الدفين في قل
29:53.english: And He warned them that He might take them suddenly while they are unaware, as He said: "They await not but a single Cry (صيحة) that will seize them while they are disputing. Then they will not be able to make a bequest, nor will they return to their families." And prayers and peace be upon Muhammad, His messenger, under whose banner the prophets march, and upon his family and his companions, the guided leaders (الأئمة المهديين), and the pleased masters (السادة المرضيين), prayers equal in number to what has been of Allah's creation and what will be, and may the first and the last attain its blessing, and abundant salutations. After that, indeed anger is a flame of fire kindled from the fire of Allah that is ignited, which rises over the hearts (الأفئدة), and it is concealed within the folds of the heart (الفؤاد). Like the concealment of embers under ashes, and it is extracted by the hidden arrogance in the heart of every obstinate tyrant, like extracting fire from stone with iron, and it has been revealed to the observers by the light of certainty (اليقين), that man has a vein extending to the accursed Satan, so whoever is provoked by the fire of anger has strengthened in him the kinship of Satan, as he said: "You created me from fire and created him from clay." For the nature of clay is stillness and dignity, and the nature of fire is blazing and flaming, and movement and agitation, and from the results of anger are malice (الحقد) and envy (الحسد), and by them perished whoever perished and corrupted whoever corrupted, and their source is a morsel (مضغة) that if it is rectified, the entire body is rectified with it, and if malice and envy and anger are among what drives the servant to places of destruction, then how much he needs to know the means.
29:53.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

29:57.arabic: وعن ابن عمر أنه لما دخل أبو بكر البيت وصلى وأثنى عج أهل البيت عجيجا سمعه أهل المصلى كلما ذكر شيئا ازدادوا فما سكن عجيجهم إلا تسليم رجل على الباب صيت جلد قال السلام عليكم يا أهل البيت ﴿ كل نفس ذائقة الموت ﴾ {} الآية إن في الله خلفا من كل أحد ودركا لكل رغبة ونجاة من كل مخافة فالله تعالى فارجوا وبه فثقوا فاستمعوا له وأنكروه وقطعوا البكاء فلما انقطع البكاء فقد صوته فاطلع أحدهم فلم ير أحدا ثم عادوا فبكوا فناداهم مناد آخر لا يعرفون صوته يا اهل البيت اذكروا الله تعالى واحمدوه على كل حال تكونوا من المخل
29:57.english: And from Ibn Umar that when Abu Bakr entered the house and prayed and praised, the people of the house wailed a wailing heard by the people of the prayer place; whenever he mentioned something, they increased. Their wailing did not subside except by the greeting of a man at the door, strong-voiced, who said: Peace be upon you, O people of the house. 'Every Soul (Nafs) tastes death' (Quran 29:57). Indeed, in Allah is a successor for everyone and attainment for every desire and salvation from every fear. So in Allah the Exalted, hope, and in Him trust, and listen to Him and deny (worldly attachments) and cut off the weeping. When the weeping ceased, his voice was lost. One of them looked out and did not see anyone. Then they returned and wept. Then another caller called them whose voice they did not recognize: O people of the house, remember (Dhikr) Allah the Exalted and praise Him in every circumstance, that you may be among the sincere ones (Mukhlisin). Indeed, in Allah is consolation from every calamity and compensation for every loss. So in Allah, obey, and by His command act. Abu Bakr said: This is Al-Khidr and Al-Yasa, peace be upon them, they attended the Prophet ﷺ.
29:57.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

29:57.arabic: وقال بعض الصوفية كنت أقرأ ليلة هذه الآية كل نفس ذائقة الموت فجعلت ارددها فإذا هاتف يهتف بي كم تردد هذه الآية فقد قتلت أربعة من الجن ما رفعوا رءوسهم إلى السماء منذ خلقوا
29:57.english: And some of the Sufis said: I was reciting one night this verse: 'Every Soul (Nafs) tastes death (Mawt)', so I kept repeating it, when a caller called out to me: 'How much you repeat this verse! You have killed four of the Jinn (Jinn) who have not raised their heads to the sky since they were created.'
29:57.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

29:57.arabic: وقال بعض الصالحين بينما أنا أسير في مسير لى إذ ملت إلى شجرة لأستريح تحتها فإذا أنا بشيخ قد أشرف على فقال لى يا هذا قم فإن الموت لم يمت ثم هام على وجه فاتبعته فسمعته وهو يقول كل نفس ذائقة الموت اللهم بارك لى في الموت فقلت وفيما بعد الموت فقال من أيقن بما بعد الموت شمر مئزر الحذر ولم يكن له في الدنيا مستقر
29:57.english: And some of the righteous said: While I was walking on my journey, I turned to a tree to rest under it, and behold, I saw an elder who had appeared to me and said to me: O this one, rise, for death has not died. Then he wandered on his face, and I followed him, and I heard him saying: 'Every soul (Nafs) will taste death (Al-Mawt). O Allah, bless me in death.' So I said: And what about after death? He said: Whoever is certain of what comes after death, he rolls up the waistband of caution and does not have a resting place in this world (Al-Dunya).
29:57.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

29:58.arabic: وقال أبو طالب المكي العمل بالجوارح من الإيمان ولا يتم دونه وادعى الإجماع فيه واستدل بأدلة تشعر بنقيض غرضه كقوله تعالى الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات إذ هذا يدل على أن العمل وراء الإيمان لا من نفس الإيمان وإلا فيكون العمل في حكم المعاد
29:58.english: And Abu Talib al-Makki said: 'Action with the limbs is from faith (Iman) and is not complete without it,' and he claimed consensus in this and argued with evidences that suggest the opposite of his intent, such as the saying of the Exalted: 'And those who believe and do righteous deeds (Al-Salihat),' for this indicates that action is beyond faith, not from the essence of faith itself, otherwise action would be in the position of repetition.
29:58.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

29:59.arabic: وترك الأسباب الدافعة وإن كانت مقطوعة وجه إذا ناله الضرر من إنسان، فإنه إذا أمكنه الصبر وأمكنه الدفع والتشفي فشرط التوكل الاحتمال والصبر، قال الله تعالى: " فاتخذه وكيلاً واصبر على ما يقولون ". وقال تعالى: " ولنصبرن على ما آذيتمونا وعلى الله فليتوكل المتوكلون ". وقال عز وجل: " ودع أذاهم وتوكل على الله ". وقال سبحانه وتعالى: " فاصبر كما صبر أولو العزم من الرسل ". وقال تعالى: " نعم أجر العاملين الذين صبروا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون " وهذا في أذى الناس، وأما الصبر على أذى الحيات والسباع والعقارب، فترك دفعها
29:59.english: And abandoning the repelling causes, even if they are certain, has a justification when harm reaches him from a human being, for if patience is possible for him and repelling and retaliation are possible, then the condition of reliance (Tawakkul) is endurance and patience. Allah the Exalted said: "So take Him as a trustee and be patient over what they say." And He the Exalted said: "And we will be patient over what you harm us, and upon Allah let the reliant ones rely." And He the Mighty and Majestic said: "And leave their harm and rely upon Allah." And He the Blessed and Exalted said: "So be patient as the resolute ones from the messengers were patient." And He the Exalted said: "Excellent is the reward of the workers, those who were patient and upon their Lord they rely." And this is regarding the harm of people. As for patience over the harm of snakes, beasts, and scorpions, abandoning repelling them is not from reliance (Tawakkul) in anything, for there is no benefit in it, and striving is not intended nor is striving abandoned for its own sake but rather to aid in the religion (Deen). The arrangement of causes here is like their arrangement in earning and bringing benefits, so we do not prolong with repetition. Likewise, in the causes repelling from wealth, reliance (Tawakkul) is not diminished by closing the door of the house when leaving nor by tying the camel, because these are causes known by the Sunnah of Allah the Exalted, either certainly or conjecturally. And for that reason, he ﷺ said to the Bedouin when he neglected the camel and said 'I have relied upon Allah': 'Tie it and rely.'[33]
29:59.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

29:60.arabic: قال فوالله ما برحنا ولا قمنا حتى نزلت ﴿ وكأين من دابة لا تحمل رزقها الله يرزقها وإياكم وهو السميع العليم ﴾ {} قال فقال رسول الله ﭬ: (إن الله لم يأمركم بكنز المال ولا باتباع الشهوات من كنز دنانير يريد بها حياة فانية فإن الحياة بيد الله ألا وإني لا أكنز دينارا ولا درهما ولا أخبأ رزقا لغد[116]).
29:60.english: He said: By Allah, we did not depart nor rise until there descended: "And how many a creature (Dabbah) does not carry its provision (Rizq); Allah provides for it and for you, and He is the All-Hearing (Al-Sami'), the All-Knowing (Al-'Alim)." {} He said: Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, Allah has not commanded you to hoard wealth nor to follow desires from hoarding dinars intending by it a perishable life, for life is in the hand of Allah. Behold, I do not hoard a dinar nor a dirham, nor do I hide provision (Rizq) for tomorrow."
29:60.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Fear and Hope'

29:61.arabic: فقد رآني فإن الشيطان لا يتخيل بي متفق عليه من حديث أبي هريرة. [142] حديث ابن عيينة عن محمد بن المنكدر عن جابر ما سئل النبي ﭬ شيئا قط فقال لا رواه مسلم وقد تقدم. [143] حديث قال الله تعالى شمتنى ابن آدم وما ينبغى له أن يشتمنى وكذبنى ما ينبغى له أن يكذبنى الحديث أخرجه البخارى من حديث أبى هريرة. [144] حديث كيف أنعم وصاحب الصور قد التقم القرن وحنى الجبهة الحديث أخرجه الترمذى من حديث أبى سعيد وقال حسن ورواه ابن ماجه بلفظ إن صاحبى القرن بأيديهما أو فى أيديهما قرنان يلاحظان النظر متى يؤمران وفى رواية اب
29:61.english: He saw me, for Satan does not imagine me, agreed upon from the hadith of Abu Huraira. [142] Hadith of Ibn 'Uyaynah from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir from Jabir: The Prophet (peace be upon him) was never asked for something and said no, narrated by Muslim and previously mentioned. [143] Hadith: Allah said: The son of Adam has insulted me, and it is not befitting for him to insult me, and he has lied about me, and it is not befitting for him to lie about me, the hadith was reported by al-Bukhari from the hadith of Abu Huraira. [144] Hadith: How can I enjoy comfort when the companion of the trumpet has taken the horn and bent his forehead?
