The hadith was reported by al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Abu Sa'id and he said it is good, and Ibn Majah narrated it with the wording: Indeed my two companions of the horn have in their hands or in their hands two horns, they are observing the gaze when they will be commanded, and in the narration of Ibn Majah, al-Hajjaj ibn Artah is disputed. [145] Hadith: When he was sent to, he was sent to the companion of the trumpet, so he gestured with it to his mouth and advanced one leg and delayed another, the hadith I did not find like this, but it has been reported that Israfil from the beginning of creation is like that, as narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Tarikh and Abu al-Shaykh in Kitab al-'Azamah from the hadith of Abu Huraira: Indeed Allah, blessed and exalted, when He finished creating the heavens and the earth, created the trumpet and gave it to Israfil, so he is placing it on his mouth, staring with his sight to the Throne, waiting for when he will be commanded, al-Bukhari said: And it is not authentic, and in a narration of Abu al-Shaykh: The companion of the trumpet has not blinked since he was entrusted with it, ready, looking towards the Throne, fearing that he will be commanded before his glance returns to him, as if his two eyes are two shining stars, and its chain is good. [146] Hadith: People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection on a white, pure land like a flat loaf of bread, with no landmark for anyone, agreed upon from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd, and al-Bukhari separated his saying: With no landmark for anyone, so he made it from the saying of Sahl or others, and Muslim included it in it. [147] Hadith: People will be resurrected barefoot, naked, uncircumcised, sweat has bridled them and reached the fats of the ears, said Sawdah, the narrator of the hadith: And woe to me, the hadith was reported by al-Tha'labi and al-Baghawi and it is in the two Sahihs from the hadith of 'A'ishah and she is the one who said: And woe to me, and al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Awsat from the hadith of Umm Salamah and she is the one who said: And woe to me. [148] Hadith of Abu Huraira: People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection riding and walking and on their faces, the hadith was narrated by al-Tirmidhi and he graded it good, and in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Anas: A man said: O Prophet of Allah, how will the disbeliever be gathered on his face? He said: Is not the One who made him walk on...
29:61.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Book of Repentance'

29:64.arabic: وهذه ضرورة دائمة في هذه الحياة الفانية فلا تزال هذه اللذة منغصة إلى الموت، وإنما الحياة الطيبة بعد الموت وإنما العيش عيش الآخرة " وإن الدار الآخرة لهي الحيوان لو كانوا يعلمون " وكل من انتهى إلى هذه الرتبة فإنه يحب لقاء الله تعالى فيحب الموت، ولا يكره إلا من حيث ينتظر زيادة استكمال في المعرفة فإن المعرفة كالبذر وبحر المعرفة لا ساحل له، فالإحاطة بكنه جلال الله محال، فكلما كثرت المعرفة بالله وبصفاته وأفعاله وبأسرار مملكته وقويت، كثر النعيم في الآخرة وعظم، كما أنه كلما كثر البذر وحسن، كثر الزرع وحسن
29:64.english: And this is a permanent necessity in this perishing life, so this pleasure remains tainted until death, and indeed the good life is after death, and indeed the living is the living of the Hereafter: "And indeed the abode of the Hereafter—it is truly the life (al-hayawān), if they only knew." And everyone who reaches this rank loves meeting Allah the Exalted, so he loves death, and he only dislikes it from the perspective of expecting an increase in completion in knowledge (maʿrifah), for knowledge is like a seed, and the ocean of knowledge has no shore, so encompassing the essence of the majesty of Allah is impossible. So whenever knowledge of Allah and His attributes and His actions and the secrets of His kingdom increases and strengthens, the bliss in the Hereafter increases and becomes great, just as whenever the seed increases and improves, the crop increases and improves. And this seed cannot be obtained except in this world, and it is only sown in the soil of the heart (qalb), and there is no harvest except in the Hereafter. And for this reason, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "The best of happiness is a long life in obedience to Allah" because knowledge only completes, increases, and expands in a long life through continuous thought (fikr) and persistence in struggle (mujāhadah) and detachment from the attachments of this world and devotion to seeking, and this inevitably requires time. So whoever loves death loves it because he sees himself standing in knowledge, having reached the limit of what has been made easy for him, and whoever dislikes death dislikes it because he was hoping for additional knowledge to be attained for him through a long life and saw himself falling short of what his capacity could bear if he lived long. This is the reason for disliking and loving death among the people of knowledge.
29:64.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

29:64.arabic: ومعنى قوله تعالى: (وإن الدار الآخرة لهي الحيوان لو كانوا يعلمون(  (العنكبوت: 64) ومعنى لقاء الله عز وجل والنظر إلى وجهه الكريم، ومعنى القرب  منه  والنزول في  جواره،  ومعنى  حصول  السعادة  بمرافقة  الملأ  الأعلى  ومقارنة   الملائكة والنبيين، ومعنى تفاوت درجات أهل الجنان حتى يرى بعضهم البعض  كما  يرى  الكوكب الدري في جوف السماء إلى غير ذلك مما يطول تفصيله.
29:64.english: And the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: 'And indeed the Abode (Dar) of the Hereafter (Al-Akhirah) - it is truly the Life (Al-Hayawan) - if they only knew' (Al-Ankabut: 64), and the meaning of meeting Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and gazing upon His Noble Face (Wajh), and the meaning of proximity (Qurb) to Him and descending into His neighborhood, and the meaning of attaining happiness (Sa'adah) by accompanying the Highest Assembly (Al-Mala' Al-A'la) and being in the company of the angels (Al-Mala'ikah) and the prophets (Al-Anbiya'), and the meaning of the varying degrees of the people of the Gardens (Ahl Al-Jinan) until some of them see each other as the brilliant star is seen in the depth of the sky, and other such matters whose detailed explanation would be lengthy.
29:64.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

29:65.arabic: وأما الالتفات إلى الجمادات فكاعتمادك على المطر في خروج الزرع ونباته ونمائه، وعلى الغيم في نزول المطر، وعلى البرد في اجتماع الغيم، وعلى الريح في استواء السفينة وسيرها: وهذا كله شرك في التوحيد وجهل بحقائق الأمور، ولذلك قال تعالى: " فإذا ركبوا في الفلك دعوا الله مخلصين له الدين فلما نجاهم إلى البر إذا هم يشركون " قيل: معناه أنهم يقولون لولا استواء الريح لما نجونا. ومن انكشف له أمر العالم كما هو عليه علم أن الريح هو الهواء والهواء لا يتحرك ما لم يحركه محرك، وكذلك محركه، وهكذا إلى أن ينتهي إلى المحرك
29:65.english: And as for turning attention to inanimate objects, it is like relying on rain for the emergence of crops and their growth and increase, and on clouds for the descent of rain, and on cold for the gathering of clouds, and on wind for the stability of the ship and its sailing: all of this is associationism (shirk) in Divine Oneness (Tawhid) and ignorance of the realities of matters. Therefore, The Exalted said: "So when they ride in the ship, they call upon Allah, making their religion (deen) sincere for Him. But when He delivers them to the land, at once they associate others (with Him)." It is said: its meaning is that they say: if not for the steadiness of the wind, we would not have been saved. And whoever has the matter of the world unveiled to him as it truly is knows that the wind is air, and air does not move unless a mover moves it, and likewise its mover, and so on until it ends at the First Mover who has no mover and is not moved in Himself, Glorified and Exalted; the turning of the servant (abd) in salvation to the wind resembles the turning of one whose neck was taken to be severed, then the king wrote a decree of pardon and release for him, so he busied himself with mentioning the ink and paper and pen with which the decree was written, saying: if not for the pen, I would not have been freed, thus seeing his salvation from the pen, not from the mover of the pen, and this is the utmost ignorance. And whoever knows that the pen has no ruling in itself and is only subjugated in the hand of the writer does not turn to it and does not thank except the writer. Rather, perhaps the joy of salvation and gratitude to the king and the writer overwhelms him from that the pen and ink and inkwell and sun and moon and stars and rain and clouds and earth, and every living being and inanimate object, subjugated in the grasp of Divine Power (Qudrah), like the subjugation of the pen in the hand of the writer, should cross his mind. Indeed, this is an analogy regarding you due to your belief that the signing king is the writer of the decree, and the truth is that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is the Writer, due to His saying, The Exalted: "And you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw." So when it is unveiled to you that all that is in the heavens and
29:65.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

29:68.arabic: وقد سوى الله تعالى بين من افترى على الله كذبا وبين من كذب بالحق فقال تعالى: (ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بالحق لما جاءه( (العنكبوت: 68). وقال تعالى: (فمن أظلم ممن كذب على الله وكذب بالصدق إذ جاءه( (الزمر: 32).
29:68.english: And Allah the Exalted has equated between one who fabricates lies against Allah and one who denies the truth, for He said the Exalted: 'And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah or denies the truth when it has come to him?' (Al-Ankabut: 68). And He said the Exalted: 'So who is more unjust than one who lies about Allah and denies the truth when it has come to him?' (Az-Zumar: 32).
29:68.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Book of Knowledge'

29:69.arabic: فإن معرفة لغة العرب تعين على معرفة تفسير القرآن، ومعرفة التفسير تعين على معرفة ما في القرآن من كيفية العبادات والأعمال التي تفيد تزكية النفس، ومعرفة طريق تزكية النفس تفيد استعداد النفس لقبول الهدايا إلى معرفة الله سبحانه وتعالى كما قال تعالى "قد أفلح من زكاها" وقال عز وجل "والذين جاهدوا فينا لنهدينهم سبلنا" فتكون جملة هذه المعارف كالوسائل إلى تحقيق معرفة الله تعالى، وإنما الكمال في معرفة الله ومعرفة صفاته وأفعاله، وينطوي فيه جميع المعارف المحيطة بالموجودات إذ الموجودات كلها من أفعاله، فمن عرفها
29:69.english: For knowledge of the language of the Arabs assists in knowledge of the interpretation (Tafsir) of the Quran, and knowledge of the interpretation assists in knowledge of what is in the Quran regarding the manner of acts of worship and works that benefit the purification (Tazkiyah) of the Soul (Nafs), and knowledge of the way of purifying the Soul benefits the preparedness of the Soul for receiving the gifts leading to knowledge of Allah, the Exalted and Majestic, as He, the Exalted, said: 'Indeed, he succeeds who purifies it (Zakaha)' and He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'And those who strive (Jahadu) in Us, We will surely guide them to Our ways.' Thus, the entirety of these knowledges are like the means to the realization of knowledge of Allah, the Exalted. And indeed, the perfection is in knowledge of Allah and knowledge of His attributes and His actions, and all knowledges encompassing the existents are enfolded within it, since all existents are from His actions. So whoever knows them from the perspective that they are the action of Allah, the Exalted, and from the perspective of their connection to Power (Qudrah), Will (Iradah), and Wisdom (Hikmah), then that is from the completion of knowledge of Allah, the Exalted. And this is the ruling regarding the perfection of knowledge we have mentioned, even if it is not fitting for the rulings of status and ostentation, but we have presented it for the completion of the divisions of perfection.
29:69.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

29:69.arabic: وإن أراد أن يكون من سالكي طريق الآخرة وساعده التوفيق حتى اشتغل بالعمل ولازم التقوى ونهى النفس عن الهوى واشتغل بالرياضة والمجاهدة انفتحت له أبواب من الهداية تكشف عن حقائق هذه العقيدة بنور إلهي يقذف في قلبه بسبب المجاهدة تحقيقا لوعده عز وجل إذ قال: ﴿ والذين جاهدوا فينا لنهدينهم سبلنا وإن الله لمع المحسنين ﴾ {} وهو الجوهر النفيس الذي هو غاية إيمان الصديقين والمقربين وإليه الإشارة بالسر الذي وقر في صدر أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه حيث فضل به الخلق وانكشاف ذلك السر بل تلك الأسرار له درجات بحسب درجات ا
29:69.english: And if he wishes to be among the travelers of the path of the Hereafter and success assists him until he engages in action and adheres to piety (Taqwa) and forbids the Soul (Nafs) from desire (Hawa) and engages in spiritual discipline (Riyada) and striving (Mujahada), doors of guidance open for him that unveil the realities of this creed with a divine light cast into his Heart (Qalb) due to the striving, in fulfillment of His promise, the Exalted, when He said: 'And those who strive in Our cause, We will surely guide them to Our paths. And indeed, Allah is with the doers of good.' {} And it is the precious essence that is the ultimate goal of the faith of the truthful ones (Siddiqin) and the near ones (Muqarrabin), and to it points the secret that settled in the chest of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, by which he excelled over creation. And the unveiling of that secret, rather those secrets, has degrees according to the degrees of striving and the degrees of the inner self (Batin) in purity and cleanliness from all besides Allah, the Exalted, and in illumination with the light of certainty (Yaqin). And that is like the variation among creation in the secrets of medicine, jurisprudence, and other sciences, as it differs with the difference in exertion (Ijtihad) and the difference in innate nature (Fitrah) in intelligence and acumen. And just as those degrees are not limited, so too are these.
29:69.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

29:69.arabic: ومنشأ كل ترتيب وتأليف وكل ذلك نعم من رب الأرباب ومسبب الأسباب ولولا فضله وكرمه إذ قال تعالى: ﴿ والذين جاهدوا فينا لنهدينهم سبلنا ﴾ لما اهتدينا إلى هذه النبذة اليسيرة من نعم الله تعالى ولولا عزله إيانا عن أن نطمح بعين الطمع إلى الإحاطة بكنه نعمه لتشوفنا إلى طلب الإحاطة والاستقصاء ولكنه تعالى عزلنا بحكم القهر والقدرة فقال تعالى: ﴿ وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها ﴾ فإن تكلمنا فبإذنه انبسطنا وإن سكنا فبقهره انقبضنا، إذ لا معطى لما منع ولا مانع لما أعطى لأنا في كل لحظة من لحظات العمر قبل الموت نسمع بسم
29:69.english: And the origin of every arrangement and composition, and all of that is blessings from the Lord of lords and the Causer of causes. And were it not for His favor and generosity when He, the Exalted, said: 'And those who strive in Our cause, We will surely guide them to Our paths' (Quran 29:69), we would not have been guided to this small portion of the blessings of Allah, the Exalted. And were it not for His preventing us from aspiring with the eye of greed to encompass the essence of His blessings, we would have yearned to seek encompassing and exhaustive knowledge. But He, the Exalted, prevented us by the decree of compulsion and power, so He, the Exalted, said: 'And if you should count the blessings of Allah, you could not enumerate them' (Quran 14:34). So if we speak, it is by His permission that we expand; and if we are silent, it is by His compulsion that we contract, for there is no giver of what He withholds nor withholder of what He gives. For we, in every moment of the moments of life before death, hear with the hearing of the hearts (Qulub) the call of the Compelling King (Al-Malik Al-Jabbar): 'To whom belongs the dominion today? To Allah, the One, the Compeller' (Quran 40:16). So praise be to Allah who distinguished us from the disbelievers and made us hear this call before the expiration of lifetimes.
29:69.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

29:69.arabic: فإن قلت فقد رددت حد المتكلم إلى حراسة عقيدة العوام عن تشويش المبتدعة كما أن حد البذرقة حراسة أقمشة الحجيج عن نهب العرب ورددت حد الفقيه إلى حفظ القانون الذي به يكف السلطان شر بعض أهل العدوان عن بعض وهاتان رتبتان نازلتان بالإضافة إلى علم الدين وعلماء الأمة المشهورون بالفضل هم الفقهاء والمتكلمون وهم أفضل الخلق عند الله تعالى فكيف تنزل درجاتهم إلى هذه المنزلة السافلة بالإضافة إلى علم الدين. فاعلم أن من عرف الحق بالرجال حار في متاهات الضلال فاعرف الحق تعرف أهله إن كنت سالكا طريق الحق وإن قنعت بالتقلي
29:69.english: If you say: You have reduced the definition of the theologian to guarding the belief of the common people from the confusion of innovators, just as the definition of the guard is protecting the fabrics of the pilgrims from the plunder of the Arabs, and you have reduced the definition of the jurist to preserving the law by which the ruler restrains the harm of some people of aggression from others. These are two lowly ranks in comparison to the knowledge of religion, and the scholars of the nation famous for virtue are the jurists and theologians, and they are the best of creation before Allah the Exalted. So how do you lower their degrees to this lowly station in comparison to the knowledge of religion? Know that whoever knows the truth through men wanders in the mazes of misguidance. So know the truth, then you will know its people if you are traversing the path of truth. And if you are content with imitation and looking at what is famous among people regarding degrees of virtue, then do not neglect the Companions and the loftiness of their status. For those I have mentioned have unanimously agreed on their precedence and that none can reach their level in religion nor come close to their dust. Their precedence was not through theology and jurisprudence, but through the knowledge of the Hereafter and traversing its path. 'And Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) did not excel the people through abundant fasting nor prayer, nor through abundant narration nor legal verdicts nor speech, but through something that settled in his chest' [75]. As the Master of the Messengers (peace be upon him) testified for him. So let your eagerness be in seeking that secret, for it is the precious jewel and the valuable pearl.
29:69.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Book of Knowledge'

29:69.arabic: فالإقبال على طاعة الله والإعراض عن مقتضى الشهوات هو الذي يجلو القلب ويصفيه ولذلك قال الله تعالى والذين جاهدوا فينا لنهدينهم سبلنا وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من عمل بما علم ورثه الله علم ما لم يعلم[16] الثالث أن يكون معدولا به عن جهة الحقيقة المطلوبة فإن قلب المطيع الصالح وإن كان صافيا فإنه ليس يتضح فيه جلية الحق لأنه ليس يطلب الحق وليس محاذيا بمرآته شطر المطلوب بل ربما يكون متسوعب الهم بتفصيل الطاعات البدنية أو بتهيئة أسباب المعيشة ولا يصرف فكره إلى التأمل في حضرة الربوبية والحقائق الخفية الإلهية ف
29:69.english: Turning towards obedience to Allah and turning away from the demands of desires is what polishes and purifies the Heart (Qalb). Therefore, Allah the Exalted said: 'And those who strive in Our cause, We will surely guide them to Our paths.' And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever acts upon what he knows, Allah will bequeath to him knowledge of what he did not know.' The third [reason] is that one is diverted from the direction of the desired Truth. For the heart of the obedient righteous person, even if it is pure, the clarity of the Truth does not become apparent in it because he does not seek the Truth and does not align the mirror of his heart towards the direction of the sought object. Rather, perhaps he is preoccupied with detailing bodily acts of worship or preparing the means of livelihood, and does not direct his thought to contemplation in the presence of Lordship and the hidden divine realities. Thus, nothing is unveiled to him except what he is contemplating about, whether it be the subtleties of the defects of deeds and the hidden faults of the Soul (Nafs) if he is contemplating them, or the affairs of livelihood if he is contemplating them. And if preoccupation with deeds and detailing acts of worship prevents the unveiling of the clarity of the Truth, then what do you think of one who directs his preoccupation towards worldly desires, their pleasures, and their attachments? How could it not prevent true unveiling? The fourth is the Veil (Hijab). For the obedient one who subdues his desires, with thought detached in a reality among realities, that may not be unveiled to him because he is veiled from it by a belief that preceded him since childhood by way of blind following (Taqlid) and acceptance with good assumption. For that stands between him and the reality of the Truth and prevents from being unveiled in his heart anything contrary to what he received from the outward aspect of blind following. And this too is a great veil.
29:69.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

30:1.arabic: ولما نزل قوله تعالى ألم غلبت الروم في أدنى الأرض وهم من بعد غلبهم سيغلبون كذبه المشركون و قالوا للصحابة إلا ترون ما يقول صاحبكم يزعم أن الروم ستغلب فخاطرهم أبو بكر رضي الله عنه بإذن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فلما حقق الله صدقه وجاء أبو بكر رضي الله عنه بما قامرهم به قال عليه الصلاة و السلام هذا سحت فتصدق به وفرح المؤمنون بنصر الله و كان قد نزل تحريم القمار بعد إذن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم له في المخاطرة مع الكفار حديث مخاطرة أبي بكر المشركين بأذنه صلى الله عليه وسلم لما نزل قوله تعالى آلم
30:1.english: And when descended His saying, The Exalted: 'Alif-Lam-Mim. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land, and they, after their defeat, will be victorious' (Quran 30:1-3), the polytheists denied it and said to the companions: 'Do you not see what your companion says? He claims that the Romans will be victorious.' So Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, wagered with them by the permission of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. When Allah verified his truthfulness and Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, came with what he had gambled with them, he, upon him be peace and blessings, said: 'This is unlawful gain (Suhut), so give it in charity.' And the believers rejoiced at the victory of Allah, and the prohibition of gambling had descended after the permission of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, for him in the wager with the disbelievers. The narration of Abu Bakr's wager with the polytheists by his permission, peace and blessings be upon him, when descended His saying, The Exalted: 'Alif-Lam-Mim. The Romans have been defeated...' and in it he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'This is unlawful gain (Suhut), so give it in charity.' Al-Bayhaqi extracted it in 'Dala'il al-Nubuwwah' from the narration of Ibn Abbas, and it is not in it that that was by his permission, peace and blessings be upon him. And the narration is with Al-Tirmidhi who graded it as good (Hasan), and Al-Hakim who authenticated it, without his saying also: 'This is unlawful gain (Suhut), so give it in charity.'
30:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on the outer and inner dimensions of worship, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

30:7.arabic: وكل جمال فهو محبوب عند مدرك الجمال، فإن كان مدركاً بالقلب فهو محبوب القلب ومثال هذا في المشاهدة حب الأنبياء والعلماء وذوي المكارم السنية والأخلاق المرضية، فإن ذلك متصور مع تشوش صورة الوجه وسائر الأعضاء وهو المراد بحسن الصورة الباطنة والحس لا يدرك. نعم يدرك بحسن آثاره الصادرة منه الدالة عليه، حتى إذا دل القلب عليه مال القلب إليه فأحبه، فمن يحب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أو الصديق رضي الله تعالى عنه أو الشافعي رحمة الله عليه فلا يحبهم إلا لحسن ما ظهر منهم، وليس ذلك لحسن صورهم ولا لحسن أفعال
30:7.english: And every beauty is beloved to the perceiver of beauty. If it is perceived by the Heart (Qalb), then it is beloved to the Heart (Qalb). An example of this in observation is the love of the prophets, the scholars, and those with noble virtues and pleasing character traits, for that is conceivable even with disarray in the face's appearance and the other limbs. This is what is meant by the beauty of the inner form, which the senses do not perceive. Rather, it is perceived through the beauty of its effects emanating from it that indicate it, until when the Heart (Qalb) indicates it, the Heart (Qalb) inclines toward it and loves it. Thus, whoever loves the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him and his family), or Al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), or Al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him), loves them only for the beauty that appeared from them, and that is not for the beauty of their forms nor for the beauty of their actions. Rather, the beauty of their actions indicated the beauty of the attributes that are the source of the actions, since actions are effects emanating from them and indicating them. So whoever saw the beauty of the author's composition and the beauty of the poet's poetry, indeed the beauty of the engraver's engraving and the builder's building, was unveiled to him from these actions their inner attributes, whose essence upon investigation returns to knowledge and capability. Then, whenever the known is more noble and more complete in men and greatness, the knowledge is more noble and more beautiful. Likewise, the object of capability, whenever it is greater in rank and more majestic in station, the capability regarding it is more majestic in rank and more noble in value. And the most majestic of known things is Allah the Exalted, so it is no wonder that the most beautiful of sciences and the most noble of them is the knowledge of Him the Exalted. And the most majestic of objects of capability is Allah the Exalted, so it is no wonder that the most beautiful of capabilities and the most noble of them is the capability to know Him the Exalted. And this inner beauty is not perceived except by the possessors of Hearts (Qalb), and none shares with them in it except those who know only an outward aspect from the worldly life, and they, regarding the Hereafter, they are heedless.
30:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

30:7.arabic: وأما الجاحدون والغافلون والمغترون بلامع السراب من زهرة الدنيا فإنهم لا يبصرون ولا يسمعون لأنهم عن السمع معزولون وعن آيات ربهم محجوبون يعلمون ظاهرا من الحياة الدنيا وهم عن الآخرة هم غافلون وما أريد بالسمع السمع الظاهر فإن الذين أريدوا به ما كانوا معزولين عنه وإنما أريد به السمع الباطن ولا يدرك بالسمع الظاهر إلا الأصوات ويشارك الإنسان فيه سائر الحيوانات فأما السمع الباطن فيدرك به لسان الحال الذي هو نطق وراء نطق المقال
30:7.english: As for the deniers (Al-Jahidun) and the heedless (Al-Ghafilun) and those deceived by the shimmering mirage of the world's bloom, they do not see and they do not hear because they are isolated from hearing (As-Sam') and veiled from the signs of their Lord. They know an outward aspect (Zahiran) of the worldly life (Al-Hayat Ad-Dunya) and they are from the Hereafter (Al-Akhirah) they are heedless (Ghafilun). And what is intended by hearing (As-Sam') is not the outward hearing (As-Sam' Az-Zahir), for those intended by it were not isolated from it. Rather, what is intended is the inward hearing (As-Sam' Al-Batin). And by the outward hearing (As-Sam' Az-Zahir) only sounds are perceived, and in it, the human shares with all other animals. As for the inward hearing (As-Sam' Al-Batin), by it is perceived the tongue of the state (Lisan Al-Hal) which is an utterance beyond the utterance of speech (Nutuq Al-Maqal).
30:7.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Etiquette of Travel'

30:7.arabic: ولذلك ترى الأكياس في أمور الدنيا وفي علم الطب والحساب والهندسة والفلسفة جهالا في أمور الآخرة والأكياس في دقائق علوم الآخرة جهالا في أكثر علوم الدنيا لأن قوة العقل لا تفي بالأمرين جميعا في الغالب فيكون أحدهما مانعا من الكمال في الثاني ولذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن أكثر أهل الجنة البله[24] أي البله في أمور الدنيا وقال الحسن في بعض مواعظه لقد أدركنا أقواما لو رأيتموهم لقلتم مجانين ولو أدركوكم لقالوا شياطين فمهما سمعت أمرا غريبا من أمور الدين جحده أهل الكياسة في سائر العلوم فلا يغرنك جحودهم عن قبو
30:7.english: Therefore you see the intelligent ones in worldly matters and in the knowledge of medicine, arithmetic, geometry, and philosophy as ignorant in matters of the Hereafter, and the intelligent ones in the subtleties of the sciences of the Hereafter as ignorant in most of the sciences of this world, because the power of the intellect (Aql) does not suffice for both matters together in most cases, so one of them becomes a barrier from perfection in the second. Therefore the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Most of the people of Paradise are the simple-minded' meaning simple-minded in worldly matters. And Al-Hasan said in some of his sermons: 'We have encountered people whom if you saw them, you would say they are mad, and if they encountered you, they would say you are devils.' So whenever you hear something strange from the matters of religion, the intelligent ones in all other sciences deny it, so do not let their denial deceive you from accepting it, since it is impossible for one traveling the path of the East to attain what exists in the West. Similarly, the affair of this world and the Hereafter proceeds. Therefore Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, those who do not expect the meeting with Us and are satisfied with the life of this world and feel secure therein...' [the verse]. And He said: 'They know an outward (Zahir) from the life of this world, but they, from the Hereafter, they are heedless (Ghafilun).' And He the Mighty and Majestic said: 'So turn away from whoever turns away from Our Remembrance (Dhikr) and desires not except the life of this world. That is their extent of knowledge.' So combining perfect insight (Istibsar) into the benefits of this world and religion hardly becomes easy except for those whom Allah has firmly established to manage His servants in their livelihood (Ma'ash) and their return (Ma'ad), and they are the prophets supported by the Spirit of Holiness (Ruh al-Qudus), drawing from the divine power (Al-Quwwah al-Ilahiyyah) that expands for all matters and does not become narrow from them. As for the hearts (Qulub) of the rest of creation, when they become preoccupied with the affair of this world, they turn away from the Hereafter and fall short from attaining perfection therein.
30:7.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

30:7.arabic: ومن جملة ما يتعذر بكثرة الأكل الدوام على الطهارة وملازمة المسجد، فإنه يحتاج إلى الخروج لكثرة شرب الماء وإراقته. ومن جملته الصوم فإنه يتيسر لمن تعود الجوع، فالصوم ودوام الاعتكاف ودوام الطهارة وصرف أوقات شغله بالأكل وأسبابه إلى العبادة أرباح كثيرة، وإنما يستحقرها الغافلون الذين لم يعرفوا قدر الدين لكن رضوا بالالحياة الدنيا واطمأنوا بها "يعلمون ظاهراً من الحياة الدنيا وهم عن الآخرة هم غافلون".
30:7.english: And among what becomes difficult with excessive eating is continuity in ritual purity (Taharah) and constant presence in the mosque, for it necessitates frequent exiting due to drinking water and its elimination. And among it is fasting (Sawm), for it becomes easy for one accustomed to hunger. So fasting, continuous seclusion in the mosque (I'tikaf), continuous ritual purity (Taharah), and diverting the times occupied with eating and its causes to worship are abundant profits, but only those who are heedless (Ghafilun) who have not recognized the worth of the religion (Deen) belittle them, but they have become content with the worldly life (Al-Hayat Al-Dunya) and found tranquility in it: "They know an outward aspect of the worldly life (Al-Hayat Al-Dunya), but they, of the Hereafter (Al-Akhirah), they are heedless (Ghafilun)."
30:7.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Harms of the Tongue'

30:7.arabic: فسبحان من احتجب عن بصائر العميان غيرة على جماله وجلاله أن يطلع عليه إلا من سبقت له منه الحسنى الذين هم عن نار الحجاب مبعدون، وترك الخاسرين في ظلمات العمى يتيهون وفي مسارح المحسوسات وشهوات البهائم يترددون؛ يعملون ظاهراً من الحياة الدنيا وهم عن الآخرة هم غافلون. الحمد لله بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون.
30:7.english: So Glory be to the One who has veiled Himself from the insights of the blind out of jealousy for His Beauty (Jamal) and Majesty (Jalal), that none may perceive Him except those for whom the good has preceded from Him—those who are kept far from the fire of the veil—and He has left the losers wandering in the darknesses of blindness and lingering in the pastures of the sensibles and the lusts of the beasts; they know an outward aspect from the worldly life and they, from the Hereafter (Akhirah), they are heedless. Praise be to Allah, but most of them do not know.
30:7.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

30:17.arabic: وهو وقت شريف ويدل على شرفه وفضله إقسام الله تعالى به إذ قال: ﴿ والصبح إذا تنفس ﴾ {} وتمدحه به إذ قال: ﴿ فالق الإصباح ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ قل أعوذ برب الفلق ﴾ {} وإظهاره القدرة بقبض الظل فيه إذ قال تعالى: ﴿ ثم قبضناه إلينا قبضا يسيرا ﴾ {} وهو وقت قبض ظل الليل ببسط نور الشمس وإرشاده الناس إلى التسبيح فيه بقوله تعالى: ﴿ فسبحان الله حين تمسون وحين تصبحون ﴾ {} وبقوله تعالى: ﴿ فسبح بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها ﴾ {} وقوله عز وجل: ﴿ ومن آناء الليل فسبح وأطراف النهار لعلك ترضى ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ وا
30:17.english: And it is a noble time, and its nobility and excellence are indicated by Allah the Exalted swearing by it when He said: 'And by the morning when it breathes' (Quran 81:18), and praising it when He said: 'The Cleaver of the dawn' (Quran 6:96), and Allah the Exalted said: 'Say, "I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak"' (Quran 113:1), and demonstrating His power by the contraction of the shadow in it when Allah the Exalted said: 'Then We drew it in to Ourselves a gradual drawing in' (Quran 25:46), and it is the time of contracting the shadow of the night by spreading the light of the sun, and guiding people to the Glorification (Tasbīḥ) in it by His saying the Exalted: 'So glorify Allah when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning' (Quran 30:17), and by His saying the Exalted: 'So glorify with praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting' (Quran 50:39), and His saying the Mighty and Majestic: 'And during parts of the night exalt Him and at the ends of the day, that you may be satisfied' (Quran 20:130), and His saying the Exalted: 'And remember the name of your Lord morning and evening' (Quran 76:25).
30:17.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

30:17.arabic: الورد السابع: إذا اصفرت الشمس بأن تقرب من الأرض بحيث يغطى نورها العبارات والبخارات التي على وجه الأرض ويرى صفرة في ضوئها دخل وقت هذا الورد وهو مثل الورد الأول من طلوع الفجر إلى طلوع الشمس لأنه قبل الغروب كما أن ذلك قبل الطلوع وهو المراد بقوله تعالى: ﴿ فسبحان الله حين تمسون وحين تصبحون ﴾ {} وهذا هو الطرف الثاني المراد بقوله تعالى: ﴿ فسبح وأطراف النهار ﴾ {} قال الحسن كانوا أشد تعظيما للعشى منهم لأول النهار وقال بعض السلف كانوا يجعلون أول النهار للدنيا وآخره للآخرة فيستحب في هذا الوقت التسبيح والاس
30:17.english: The Seventh Remembrance (Wird): When the sun yellows by approaching the earth such that its light covers the expressions and vapors on the face of the earth and a yellowness is seen in its light, the time of this Remembrance (Wird) enters. It is like the first Remembrance (Wird) from the rising of dawn to the rising of the sun because it is before sunset, just as that is before sunrise. This is what is intended by His saying, the Exalted: 'So glorify Allah when you reach evening and when you reach morning.' And this is the second extremity intended by His saying, the Exalted: 'So glorify and the extremities of the day.' Al-Hasan said: They used to have greater reverence for the evening than for the beginning of the day. And some of the predecessors said: They used to make the beginning of the day for the worldly life (Dunya) and its end for the Hereafter (Akhirah). So it is recommended in this time the Glorification (Tasbih) and the Seeking of Forgiveness (Istighfar) especially, and the rest of what we mentioned in the first Remembrance (Wird), such as saying: 'I seek forgiveness from Allah, there is no god but He, the Living, the Sustainer, and I ask Him for repentance, and glory be to Allah the Great and with His praise,' taken from His saying, the Exalted: 'And seek forgiveness for your sin and glorify with the praise of your Lord in the evening and the morning.' And the Seeking of Forgiveness (Istighfar) upon the names that are in the Quran is more beloved, like His saying: 'Seek forgiveness from Allah, indeed He is Oft-Forgiving (Ghaffar),' 'I seek forgiveness from Allah, indeed He is Oft-Returning (Tawwab),' 'My Lord, forgive and have mercy, and You are the best of the merciful, so forgive us and have mercy on us, and You are the best of the forgivers.' And it is recommended to recite before the setting of the sun: 'By the sun and its brightness,' 'By the night when it covers,' and the two seeking refuge surahs. And let the sun set upon him while he is in the Seeking of Forgiveness (Istighfar). Then when he hears the call to prayer (Adhan), he says: 'O Allah, this is the approach of Your night and the departure of Your day and the voices of Your callers,' as preceded, then he responds to the caller to prayer and occupies himself with the sunset prayer (Maghrib). And with the sunset, the Remembrances (Awrad) of the day have ended, so it behooves the servant (Abd) to observe his states and account his Soul (Nafs), for a stage from his path has passed, so if the day equals...
30:17.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

30:17.arabic: الحمد لله رب العالمين ~ فسبحان الله حين تمسون وحين تصبحون وله الحمد في السموات والأرض وعشيا وحين تظهرون يخرج الحي من الميت ويخرج الميت من الحي ويحيي الأرض بعد موتها وكذلك تخرجون ومن آياته أن خلقكم من تراب ثم إذا أنتم بشر تنتشرون ~ اللهم إني أسألك إيمانا دائما ويقينا صادقا وعلما نافعا وقلبا خاشعا ولسانا ذاكرا وأسألك العفو والعافية والمعافاة الدائمة في الدنيا والآخرة ويصلي على محمد ﭬ ويدعو الله عز وجل بما شاء من حاجته عقيب هذا الدعاء
30:17.english: Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds ~ So glorify Allah when you reach the evening (tumsūn) and when you reach the morning (tuṣbiḥūn), and to Him belongs praise in the heavens and the earth, and at nightfall and when you are at noon. He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living, and He gives life to the earth after its death, and thus you will be brought forth. And among His signs is that He created you from dust, then behold, you are human beings dispersing ~ O Allah, I ask You for enduring faith (īmān) and truthful certainty (yaqīn) and beneficial knowledge and a humble heart (qalb) and a remembering tongue (lisān dhākir), and I ask You for pardon and well-being and enduring safety in this world and the Hereafter, and he sends blessings upon Muhammad ﷺ and supplicates to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, with whatever he wishes of his needs following this supplication.
30:17.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

30:17.arabic: وقال عز وجل: ﴿ كانوا قليلا من الليل ما يهجعون وبالأسحار هم يستغفرون ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل: ﴿ فسبحان الله حين تمسون وحين تصبحون ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه ﴾ {}. فهذا كله يبين لك أن الطريق إلى تعالى مراقبة الأوقات وعمارتها بالأوراد على سبيل الدوام ولذلك قال ﭬ: (أحب عباد الله إلى الله الذين يراعون الشمس والقمر والأظلة لذكر الله تعالى[1]).
30:17.english: And the Mighty and Majestic said: 'They used to sleep little of the night, and in the dawns they would seek forgiveness' (Quran 76:26-27). And the Mighty and Majestic said: 'So glory be to Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning' (Quran 30:17). And He said: 'And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, desiring His Face (Wajh)' (Quran 6:52). All of this makes clear to you that the path to the Exalted is watching over the times and populating them with regular devotional practices (Awrad) on the basis of continuity, and for that reason the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'The most beloved of Allah's servants to Allah are those who observe the sun, the moon, and the shadows for the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah the Exalted.'
30:17.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

30:20.arabic: فمن آياته الانسان المخلوق من النطفة وأقرب شيء إليك نفسك وفيك من العجائب الدالة على عظمة الله تعالى ما تنقضي الأعمار في الوقوف على عشر عشيره وأنت غافل عنه فيامن هو غافل عن نفسه وجاهل بها كيف تطمع في معرفة غيرك وقد أمرك الله تعالى بالتدبر في نفسك في كتابه العزيز فقال وفي أنفسكم أفلا تبصرون وذكر أنك مخلوق من نطفة قذرة فقال قتل الإنسان ما أكفره من أي شئ خلقه من نطفة خلقه فقدره ثم السبيل يسره ثم أماته فأقبره ثم إذا شاء أنشره وقال تعالى ومن آياته أن خلقكم من تراب ثم إذا أنتم بشر تنتشرون وقال تعالى ألم
30:20.english: From His Signs (Ayat) is the human being created from a sperm-drop (Nutfah), and the closest thing to you is your own self (Nafs). In you are wonders indicating the majesty of Allah, the Exalted, that lifetimes would not suffice to grasp a tenth of a tenth of it, while you are heedless of it. So, O you who are heedless of your own self (Nafs) and ignorant of it, how can you aspire to know others when Allah, the Exalted, has commanded you to reflect upon your self (Nafs) in His Noble Book, saying: 'And in your own selves (Anfusikum) - will you not then see?' And He mentioned that you are created from a filthy sperm-drop (Nutfah Qadhirah), saying: 'Woe to man! How ungrateful he is! From what thing did He create him? From a sperm-drop (Nutfah) He created him and then proportioned him. Then He made the way easy for him. Then He causes him to die and puts him in his grave. Then when He wills, He will resurrect him.' And He, the Exalted, said: 'And among His Signs (Ayat) is that He created you from dust, then, behold, you are human beings dispersing.' And He, the Exalted, said: 'Was he not a sperm-drop (Nutfah) from semen emitted? Then he was a clinging clot ('Alaqah), then He created and proportioned.' And He, the Exalted, said: 'Did We not create you from a despised water (Ma'in Mahin)? Then We placed it in a firm lodging (Qararin Makin) for a known term.' And He said: 'Does not man see that We created him from a sperm-drop (Nutfah)? Then, behold, he is a clear adversary.' And He said: 'Indeed, We created man from a sperm-drop mixture (Nutfatin Amshaj).' Then He mentioned how He made the sperm-drop (Nutfah) into a clinging clot ('Alaqah), and the clinging clot ('Alaqah) into a chewed lump (Mudghah), and the chewed lump (Mudghah) into bones, saying, the Exalted: 'And certainly did We create man from an extract of clay. Then We placed him as a sperm-drop (Nutfah) in a firm lodging (Qararin Makin). Then We made the sperm-drop (Nutfah) into a clinging clot ('Alaqah)...' So, the repetition of mentioning the sperm-drop (Nutfah) in the Noble Book is not merely to hear its word and neglect reflection upon its meaning. Now look at the sperm-drop (Nutfah): it is a drop of filthy water; if left for an hour to be struck by the air, it would spoil and become foul-smelling. How did the Lord of lords bring it forth from the backbone and the ribs? And how did He bring together the male and the female and cast affection (Alfah) and love (Mahabbah) into their hearts (Qulub)? And how did He lead them by the chain of love (Mahabbah) and desire (Shahwah) to union? And how did He extract the sperm-drop (Nutfah) from the man through the movement of intercourse (Waqa')? And how did He draw the menstrual blood from the depths of the veins and gather it in the womb? Then how did He create the newborn from the sperm-drop (Nutfah) and quench it with the water of menstruation and nourish it until it grew, increased, and became large? And how did He make the sperm-drop (Nutfah), which is white and shining, into a red clinging clot ('Alaqah)? Then how did He make it into a chewed lump (Mudghah)? Then how did He divide the parts of the sperm-drop (Nutfah), which are equal and similar, into the...
30:20.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Contemplation'

30:26.arabic: فلو لم يكن بين يدي الموتي إلا هول تلك النفخة لكان ذلك جديرا بأن يتقى فإنها نفخة وصيحة يصعق بها من فى السموات والأرض يعنى يموتون بها إلا من شاء الله وهو بعض الملائكة ولذلك قال رسول الله ﭬ: (كيف أنعم وصاحب الصور قد التقم القرن وحنى الجبهة وأصغى بالأذن متى يؤمر فينفخ[144]) قال مقاتل: الصور هو القرن وذلك أن إسرافيل عليه السلام واضع فاه على القرن كهيئة البوق ودائرة رأس القرن كعرض السموات والأرض وهو شاخص بصره نحو العرش ينتظر متى يؤمر فينفخ النفخة الأولى فإذا نفخ صعق من فى السموات والأرض أى مات كل حيوا
30:26.english: If there were nothing before the dead except the terror of that blowing (of the Trumpet), it would be worthy of being feared, for it is a blowing and a cry by which those in the heavens and the earth are struck unconscious (صعق), meaning they die by it except whom Allah wills, and that is some of the angels. Therefore, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'How can I be at ease when the possessor of the Trumpet has taken the horn into his mouth, lowered his forehead, and inclined his ear, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow?' [144] Muqatil said: The Trumpet (الصور) is the horn, and that is because Israfil (upon him be peace) has placed his mouth on the horn like a trumpet, and the circumference of the head of the horn is like the expanse of the heavens and the earth, and he is staring with his gaze towards the Throne, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow the first blowing. When he blows, those in the heavens and the earth are struck unconscious (صعق), meaning every living creature dies from the intensity of the fright except whom Allah wills, and that is Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil, and the Angel of Death. Then the Angel of Death is commanded to take the soul (روح) of Jibril, then the soul of Mika'il, then the soul of Israfil, then the Angel of Death is commanded and he dies. Then the creation remains after the first blowing in the Barzakh (البرزخ) for forty years. Then Allah the Exalted revives Israfil and commands him to blow the second blowing, and that is His saying the Exalted: 'Then it will be blown into it another time, and behold, they will be standing, looking on.' {} On their feet, looking at the Resurrection. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'When I was sent, I was sent to the possessor of the Trumpet, and he inclined it to his mouth, advanced one foot and delayed another, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow. Indeed, fear the blowing!' [145] So reflect upon the creatures and their humiliation, their brokenness, and their submission at the time of resurrection out of fear of this striking unconscious (الصعقة) and in anticipation of what will be decreed for them of happiness or misery. And you are among them, broken like their brokenness, perplexed like their perplexity. Rather, if you were in the world among the luxurious and the rich enjoying pleasures, then the kings of the earth on that day are the most humiliated people of the gathering place, the smallest and most contemptible of them, being trodden underfoot like a grain. And at that time, the wild beasts from the deserts and the mountains come with lowered heads, mixed with the creatures after their wildness, humbled for the Day of Resurrection (يوم النشور), without any sin they have been defiled by, but their gathering (حشرتهم) is due to the intensity of the striking unconscious (الصعقة) and the terror of the blowing.
30:26.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

30:30.arabic: ولذلك قال تعالى وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم وأشهدهم على أنفسهم ألست بربكم قالوا بلى فالمراد به إقرار نفوسهم لا إقرار الألسنة فإنهم انقسموا في إقرار الألسنة حيث وجدت الألسنة والأشخاص إلى مقر وإلى جاحد ولذلك قال تعالى: (ولئن سألتهم من خلقهم ليقولن الله( معناه إن اعتبرت أحوالهم شهدت بذلك نفوسهم وبواطنهم فطرة الله التي فطر الناس عليها أي كل آدمي فطر على الإيمان بالله عز وجل بل على معرفة الأشياء على ما هي عليه أعني أنها كالمضمنة فيها لقرب استعدادها للإدراك ثم لما كان الإيمان مركوزا في الن
30:30.english: Therefore, Allah the Exalted said: 'And [mention] when your Lord took from the children of Adam from their backs their descendants and made them testify concerning themselves, [saying to them], "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we have testified."' The intended meaning is the affirmation of their souls (Nafs), not the affirmation of tongues, for they divided in the affirmation of tongues where tongues and persons existed into affirmers and deniers. Therefore, Allah the Exalted said: 'And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "Allah."' Its meaning is that if you considered their states, their souls (Nafs) and innermost beings (Bawatin) would testify to that. The natural disposition (Fitrah) of Allah upon which He created people, meaning every human is created upon faith in Allah the Exalted, indeed upon knowledge of things as they are, meaning they are as if embedded in it due to the proximity of their preparedness for perception. Then, since faith is firmly rooted in the souls (Nafs) by natural disposition (Fitrah), people divided into two groups: those who turned away and forgot—they are the disbelievers—and those who pondered their thoughts and remembered, so they were like one who carried testimony then forgot it due to heedlessness then remembered it. Therefore, the Exalted said: 'That they may remember,' 'And that those of understanding may remember,' 'And remember the favor of Allah upon you and His covenant with which He bound you,' 'And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?'; Naming this pattern remembrance is not far-fetched, as if remembrance is of two kinds: one is to remember an image that was present in existence in his heart (Qalb) but disappeared after the other existence. The other is to remember an image that was embedded in him by natural disposition (Fitrah), and these are truths apparent to the observer by the light of insight, heavy upon one who is accustomed to it—his saying 'is accustomed to it' is from circulation, meaning hearing and imitation are prevalent with him, so reflect—his corrector is hearing and imitation without unveiling and witnessing. Therefore, you see him floundering in such verses and forcing, and in interpreting remembrance with the affirmation of souls (Nafs), types of forced interpretations, and he imagines to himself in reports and verses kinds of contradictions, and perhaps that overcomes him until he looks at them with an eye of contempt and...
30:30.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

30:30.arabic: ولهذا بعث الأنبياء صلوات الله عليهم لدعوة الخلق إلى التوحيد ليقولوا لا إله إلا الله وما أمروا أن يقولوا لنا إله وللعالم إله فإن ذلك كان مجبولا في فطرة عقولهم من مبدأ نشؤهم وفي عنفوان شبابهم ولذلك قال عز وجل ولئن سألتهم من خلق السموات والأرض ليقولن الله وقال تعالى: )فأقم وجهك للدين حنيفا فطرة الله التي فطر الناس عليها لا تبديل لخلق الله ذلك الدين القيم( فإذا في فطرة الإنسان وشواهد القرآن ما يغني عن إقامة البرهان
30:30.english: And for this reason, the Prophets (peace be upon them) were sent to call the creation to Tawhid (Oneness of God) so that they would say 'There is no god but Allah,' and they were not commanded to say 'We have a god and the world has a god,' for that was ingrained in the innate disposition (Fitrah) of their intellects from the beginning of their emergence and in the prime of their youth. Therefore, the Almighty said: 'And if you ask them who created the heavens and the earth, they will say Allah.' And He said: 'So set your face to the religion, uprightly. The innate disposition (Fitrah) of Allah upon which He created mankind. There is no alteration in the creation of Allah. That is the upright religion.' So indeed, in the innate disposition (Fitrah) of man and the evidences of the Quran, there is what suffices without establishing proof.
30:30.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Foundations of Belief'

30:32.arabic: الثامن العجب بالرأي الخطأ. قال الله تعالى "أفمن زين له سوء عمله فرآه حسناً" وقال تعالى "وهم يحسبون أنهم يحسنون صنعاً" وقد أخبر رسول الله ﭬ: أن ذلك يغلب على آخر هذه الأمة[101] وبذلك هلكت الأمم السالفة إذ افترقت فرقاً فكل معجب برأيه "وكل حزب بما لديهم فرحون" وجميع أهل البدع والضلال إنما أصروا عليها لعجبهم بآرائهم والعجب بالبدعة هو استحسان ما يسوق إليه الهوى والشهوة مع ظن كونه حقاً، وعلاج هذا العجب أشد من علاج غيره لأن صاحب الرأي الخطأ جاهل بخطئه ولو عرفه لتركه، ولا يعالج الداء الذي لا يعرف والجهل
30:32.english: The eighth: Pride in erroneous opinion. Allah the Exalted said: "Is he whose evil deed is made fair-seeming unto him so that he sees it as good?" And He said: "And they think that they are doing well." And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) informed: that this will prevail over the latter part of this nation. And by this, the past nations perished when they split into factions, each being proud of his opinion "and every party rejoices in what is with them." And all the people of innovation and misguidance only persist in them due to their pride in their opinions. And pride in innovation is the approval of what leads to desire and appetite with the assumption of its being truth. And the treatment of this pride is more severe than the treatment of others because the possessor of erroneous opinion is ignorant of his error, and if he knew it, he would abandon it. And the disease that is not known is not treated, and ignorance is a disease that is not known, so its cure becomes very difficult.
30:32.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

30:32.arabic: ولا يزالون مختلفين كل حزب بما لديهم فرحون ولذلك خلقهم حكى أن أحمد بن خضرويه رأى ربه عز وجل في المنام فقال له كل الناس يطلبون مني الجنة إلا أبا يزيد فإنه يطلبني ورأى أبو يزيد ربه في المنام فقال يا رب كيف الطريق اليك فقال اترك نفسك وتعال إلي ورؤى الشبلي بعد موته في المنام فقيل له ما فعل الله بك فقال لم يطالبني على الدعاوي بالبرهان إلا على قول واحد قلت يوما أي خسارة أعظم من خسران الجنة فقال أي خسارة أعظم من خسران لقائي والغرض أن هذه النيات متفاوتة الدرجات ومن غلب على قلبه واحدة منها ربما لا يتيسر ل
30:32.english: And they will not cease to differ; every party rejoices in what they have with them, and for that He created them. It is narrated that Ahmad ibn Khadruwayh saw his Lord (may He be exalted) in a dream, and He said to him: 'All people ask Me for Paradise except Abu Yazid, for he asks for Me.' And Abu Yazid saw his Lord in a dream and said: 'O Lord, how is the path to You?' He said: 'Leave your Soul (Nafs) and come to Me.' And al-Shibli was seen after his death in a dream, and it was said to him: 'What did Allah do with you?' He said: 'He did not demand from me proof for the claims except for one statement: I said one day: What loss is greater than the loss of Paradise? He said: What loss is greater than the loss of My meeting?' And the purpose is that these intentions are of varying degrees, and whoever is dominated in their Heart (Qalb) by one of them, perhaps it is not made easy for them to turn to another. And knowledge of these truths produces actions and deeds that the literalists among the jurists do not find strange.
30:32.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

30:39.arabic: وأما طلب الزيادة فداخل في قوله تعالى (ولا تمنن تستكثر) أي تعطي لتطلب أكثر وتحت قوله تعالى (وما آتيتم من ربا ليربوا في أموال الناس) فإن الربا هو الزيادة وهذا طلب زيادة على الجملة وإن لم يكن في الأموال الربوية فكل ذلك مكروه وبدعة في النكاح يشبه التجارة والقمار ويفسد مقاصد النكاح.
30:39.english: And as for seeking increase, it falls under His saying, the Exalted: 'And do not confer favor to acquire more' (Quran 74:6), meaning you give to seek more, and under His saying, the Exalted: 'And whatever you give of usury (riba) to increase in the wealth of people, it does not increase with Allah' (Quran 30:39). For usury (riba) is the increase, and this is seeking increase in general, even if it is not in usurious wealth. All of that is disliked (makruh) and an innovation (bid'ah) in marriage that resembles trade and gambling, and it corrupts the purposes of marriage.
30:39.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

30:43.arabic: يوم لا مرد له من الله يوم هم بارزون ويوم هم على النار يفتنون يوم لا ينفع مال ولا بنون يوم لا ينفع الظالمين معذرتهم ولهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار يوم ترد فيه المعاذير وتبلى السرائر وتظهر الضمائر وتكشف الأستار يوم تخشع فيه الأبصار وتسكن الأصوات ويقل فيه الالتفات وتبرز الخفيات وتظهر الخطيئات يوم يساق العباد ومعهم الأشهاد ويشيب الصغير ويسكر الكبير فيومئذ وضعت الموازين ونشرت الدواوين وبرزت الجحيم وأغلى الحميم وزفرت النار ويئس الكفار وسعرت النيران وتغيرت الألوان وخرس اللسان ونطقت جوارح الإنسان فيا أيها ا
30:43.english: A day when there is no turning back from Allah, a day when they are exposed, and a day when they are tested over the Fire, a day when wealth and children do not benefit, a day when the excuses of the wrongdoers do not benefit them, and for them is the curse and for them is the evil abode, a day when excuses are returned, secrets are tested, consciences are revealed, and veils are uncovered, a day when gazes are humbled, voices are silenced, turning away is reduced, hidden things are exposed, and sins are revealed, a day when the servants are driven with their witnesses, the young turn gray, and the old become intoxicated, and on that day the scales are set up, the records are spread out, Hell is exposed, the boiling water is heated, the Fire blazes, the disbelievers despair, the fires are kindled, colors change, the tongue is silenced, and the limbs of the human speak. O human, what deluded you concerning your Generous Lord, when the doors were closed, the curtains were lowered, and you concealed yourself from the creatures, yet you committed immorality? So what will you do when your limbs have testified against you? So woe, all woe to us, the heedless ones. Allah sends to us the master of the messengers and reveals to him the Clear Book, and He informs us of these attributes from the descriptions of the Day of Recompense (Yawm al-Din), then He makes us aware of our heedlessness and says: 'The reckoning of the people has drawn near, while they are in heedlessness turning away. No new reminder comes to them from their Lord except that they listen to it while they are playing, their hearts (Qulub) distracted.' {} Then He makes us aware of the nearness of the Hour and says: 'The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split.' 'Indeed, they see it as distant, but We see it as near.' {} 'And what'
30:43.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

30:43.arabic: بل في الحديث الصحيح ما روي أنه ﭬ قال "من كانت لأخيه عنده مظلمة في عرض أو مال فليستحللها منه من قبل أن يأتي يوم ليس هناك دينار ولا درهم، إنما يؤخذ من حسناته فإن لم يكن له حسنات أخذ من سيئات صاحبه فزيدت على سيئاته"[226]
30:43.english: Rather, in the authentic hadith, it is narrated that he (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever has a wrong against his brother in honor or wealth, let him seek its resolution from him before there comes a day where there is no dinar nor dirham; indeed, it will be taken from his good deeds, and if he has no good deeds, it will be taken from the bad deeds of his companion and added to his bad deeds."
30:43.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

30:50.arabic: ام فادع الله حتى أؤمن على  دعائك  قال  فدعا فتجلت السماء سحابا ثم صبت فسقوا. وقال يحيى الغساني: أصاب الناس قحط على  عهد داود عليه السلام فاختاروا ثلاثة من  علمائهم  فخرجوا  حتى  يستسقوا  بهم  فقال أحدهم اللهم إنك أنزلت في توراتك أن نعفو عمن ظلمنا اللهم إنا قد ظلمنا  أنفسنا فاعف عنا. وقال الثاني اللهم إنك أنزلت في توراتك أن نعتق  أرقاءنا  اللهم  إنا أرقاؤك فأعتقنا وقال الثالث اللهم إنك أنزلت في توراتك أن لا نرد المساكين  إذا وقفوا بأبوابنا اللهم إنا مساكينك وقفنا ببابك فلا ترد دعاءنا فسقوا وقال
30:50.english: Then call upon Allah until I believe in your supplication, he said, so he called and the sky became covered with clouds then poured, so they were watered. And Yahya al-Ghassani said: A drought afflicted people during the time of Dawud (David), peace be upon him, so they chose three from their scholars, and they went out until they sought rain through them. The first said: O Allah, You revealed in Your Torah that we forgive those who wrong us; O Allah, we have wronged ourselves, so forgive us. The second said: O Allah, You revealed in Your Torah that we free our slaves; O Allah, we are Your slaves, so free us. The third said: O Allah, You revealed in Your Torah that we do not turn away the poor when they stand at our doors; O Allah, we are Your poor, standing at Your door, so do not reject our supplication, and they were watered. And Ata al-Sulami said: We were deprived of rain, so we went out seeking rain, and behold, we found Sa'dun the Madman in the graveyards. He looked at me and said: O Ata, is this the Day of Resurrection or when what is in the graves is scattered? I said: No, but we have been deprived of rain, so we went out seeking rain. He said: O Ata, with earthly hearts (Qulub) or with heavenly hearts (Qulub)? I said: Rather with heavenly hearts (Qulub). He said: Far be it, O Ata! Tell the ostentatious not to be ostentatious, for the Critic is seeing. Then he glanced at the sky with his eye and said: My God, my Master, and my Lord, do not destroy Your lands with the sins of Your servants, but with the hidden secret from Your names and what the veils have concealed from Your bounties, except that You give us abundant, sweet water to revive with it the servants and water with it the lands, O He who is over all things powerful (Qadir). Ata said: He had not finished the speech until the sky thundered and lightninged and gave rain like the mouths of waterskins, and he turned away while saying: The ascetics (Zahidun) and worshippers (Abidun) have succeeded, for they made their bellies hungry for their Master. They kept awake the ailing eyes out of love, so their night passed while they were awake. The worship (Ibadah) of Allah preoccupied them until people thought there was madness in them. And Ibn al-Mubarak said: I arrived in Medina in a year of severe drought, and the people went out seeking rain, so I went out with them. Then a black youth approached, wearing two pieces of coarse cloth, having girded with one and thrown the other over his shoulder, and he sat next to me. I heard him say: My God, have the faces become blackened before You due to the multitude of sins and the faults of deeds, and You have withheld from us the rain of the sky to discipline Your servants with that? I ask You, O Forbearing (Halim), possessor of forbearance (Anah), O He from whom His servants know nothing but beauty, that You give them drink now, now. He did not cease saying now, now until the sky became clothed with clouds and rain came from every side. Ibn al-Mubarak said: I came to al-Fudayl, and he said: Why do I see you sad? I said: A matter that others preceded us to, so they undertook it instead of us, and I narrated the story to him. Al-Fudayl cried out and fell unconscious. And it is narrated that Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, sought rain through al-Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him. When Umar finished his supplication, al-Abbas said: O Allah, no affliction has descended from the sky except...
30:50.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

31:6.arabic: احتجوا بقوله تعالى ومن الناس من يشتري لهو الحديث قال ابن مسعود والحسن البصري والنخعي رضي الله عنهم إن لهو الحديث هو الغناء وروت عائشة رضي الله عنها أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال إن الله تعالى حرم القينة وبيعها وثمنها وتعليمها حديث عائشة إن الله حرم القينة وبيعها وثمنها وتعليمها أخرجه الطبراني في الأوسط بإسناد ضعيف قال البيهقي ليس بمحفوظ فنقول أما القينة فالمراد بها الجارية التي تغني للرجال في مجلس الشرب وقد ذكرنا أن غناء الأجنبية للفساق ومن يخاف عليهم الفتنة حرام وهم لا يقصدون بالفتنة إلا ما ه
31:6.english: They argued with His saying, the Exalted: 'And among the people is he who purchases idle talk (lahw al-hadith) to mislead from the path of Allah without knowledge and takes it in ridicule; those will have a humiliating punishment.' Ibn Mas'ud, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, and Al-Nakha'i, may Allah be pleased with them, said that idle talk (lahw al-hadith) is singing (ghina'). And 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, narrated that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, has forbidden the singing-girl (al-qayna) and her sale, her price, and her teaching.' The hadith of 'A'isha: 'Indeed, Allah has forbidden the singing-girl (al-qayna) and her sale, her price, and her teaching' was reported by Al-Tabarani in Al-Awsat with a weak chain; Al-Bayhaqi said it is not preserved. So we say: As for the singing-girl (al-qayna), what is intended by it is the female slave who sings for men in a drinking gathering, and we have mentioned that the singing of a non-mahram woman for corrupt people and those whom one fears temptation (fitna) for is forbidden, and they do not intend by temptation (fitna) except what is prohibited. As for the singing of the female slave for her owner, its prohibition is not understood from this hadith; rather, for other than her owner, listening to her in the absence of temptation (fitna) is evidenced by what is narrated in the two Sahihs from the singing of the two female slaves in the house of 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her. And as for purchasing idle talk (lahw al-hadith) with religion, exchanging it to mislead by it from the path of Allah, it is forbidden and blameworthy, and there is no dispute in it. And not every singing is an exchange for religion, purchased with it, and misleading from the path of Allah, the Exalted, and that is what is intended in the verse. And if one recited the Quran to mislead by it from the path of Allah, it would be forbidden; it is narrated about some hypocrites that he used to lead the people in prayer and would not recite except Surah 'Abasa because of what is in it of reproach with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, so 'Umar intended to kill him.
31:6.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

31:15.arabic: وَلأن مشاهدة الفسق و الفساق تهون أمر المعصية على القلب وتبطل نفرة القلب عنها قال سعيد بن المسيب لا تنظروا إلى الظلمة فتحبط أعمالكم الصالحة بل هؤلاء لا سلامة في مخالطتهم وإنما السلامة في الانقطاع عنهم قال الله تعالى وإذا خاطبهم الجاهلون قالوا سلاما أي سلامة و الألف بدل من الهاء ومعناه إنا سلمنا من إثمكم وأنتم سلمتم من شرنا فهذا ما أردنا أن نذكره من معاني الأخوة وشروطها وفوائدها فلنرجع في ذكر حقوقها ولوازمها وطرق القيام بحقها وأما الحريص على الدنيا فصحبته سم قاتل لأن الطباع مجبولة على التشبه و الا
31:15.english: And because observing immorality (Fisq) and immoral people (Fussaq) makes sin seem trivial to the Heart (Qalb) and nullifies the Heart's (Qalb) aversion from it. Said Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib: 'Do not look at the wrongdoers lest your righteous deeds be invalidated.' Rather, these people—there is no safety in associating with them, and safety is only in cutting off from them. Said Allah the Exalted: 'And when the ignorant address them, they say: Peace (Salam)' meaning safety, and the Alif is substituted for the Ha, and its meaning is: 'We are safe from your sin, and you are safe from our harm.' This is what we intended to mention of the meanings of brotherhood, its conditions, and its benefits. So let us return to mentioning its rights, necessities, and ways of fulfilling its right. As for the one greedy for the worldly life (Dunya), his companionship is deadly poison because natures are predisposed to imitation and emulation; indeed, nature steals from nature without its owner realizing. Sitting with the greedy for the worldly life (Dunya) stirs greed, and sitting with the ascetic (Zahid) makes one ascetic toward the worldly life (Dunya). Therefore, the companionship of seekers of the worldly life (Dunya) is disliked, and the companionship of those desirous of the Hereafter (Akhira) is recommended. Said Ali (upon him be peace): 'Revive acts of obedience by sitting with one from whom you feel shame.' And said Ahmad ibn Hanbal (may Allah have mercy on him): 'Nothing has landed me in tribulation except the companionship of one I do not respect.' And said Luqman: 'O my son, sit with the scholars and press close to them with your knees, for indeed Hearts (Qulub) are revived by wisdom (Hikmah) just as the dead earth is revived by abundant rain.' Chapter Two: On the Rights of Brotherhood and Companionship. Know that...
31:15.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

31:15.arabic: وقال تعالى فأعرض عمن تولى عن ذكرنا ولم يرد إلا الحياة الدنيا و قال واتبع سبيل من أناب إلى وفي مفهوم ذلك زجر عن الفاسق وأما المبتدع ففي صحبته خطر سراية البدعة وتعدي شؤمها إليه فالمبتدع مستحق للهجر و المقاطعة فكيف تؤثر صحبته
31:15.english: And Allah the Exalted said: 'So turn away from whoever turns away from Our Remembrance (Dhikr) and desires only the worldly life.' And He said: 'And follow the path of those who turn to Me.' And in the understanding of that is a prohibition from the corrupt person. As for the innovator, in his companionship there is danger of the spread of innovation and the transfer of its evil omen to him, so the innovator is deserving of abandonment and severance, so how could you prefer his companionship?
31:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

31:16.arabic: فهذا كله أخلاق الكبر وآثاره التي يثمرها التعزز بالعلم والعمل، وأين من يخلو عن جميع ذلك أو عن بعضه؟ فليت شعري من الذي عرف هذه الأخلاق من نفسه وسمع قول رسول الله ﭬ "لا يدخل الجنة من في قلبه مثقال حبة من خردل من كبر"[59] كيف يستعظم نفسه ويتكبر على غيره ورسول الله ﭬ يقول إنه من أهل النار؟ وإنما العظيم من خلا عن هذا، ومن خلا عنه لم يكن فيه تعظم وتكبر، والعالم هو الذي فهم أن الله تعالى قال له: إن لك عندنا قدراً ما لم تر لنفسك قدراً فإن رأيت لها قدراً فلا قدر لك عندنا. ومن لم يعلم هذا من الدين فاسم الع
31:16.english: All of this is the character traits of arrogance and its effects that result from pride in knowledge and action. Where is the one who is free from all of that or from some of it? I wonder, who is it that recognizes these traits in himself and hears the saying of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him): 'He will not enter Paradise who has in his heart (Qalb) the weight of a mustard seed of arrogance' [59] - how can he magnify himself and be arrogant over others while the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) says that he is from the people of the Fire? Indeed, the great one is he who is free from this, and he who is free from it has no self-magnification and arrogance in him. The knowledgeable one is he who understood that Allah the Exalted said to him: 'Indeed, you have with Us a status as long as you do not see for yourself a status. If you see for it a status, then you have no status with Us.' And whoever does not know this from the religion, then the name 'knowledgeable' upon him is false. And whoever knows it, it is incumbent upon him not to be arrogant and not to see for himself a status. This is arrogance through knowledge and action.
31:16.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

31:16.arabic: وقال رسول الله ﭬ "لا يدخل الجنة من كان في قلبه مثقال حبة من خردل من كبر، ولا يدخل النار من كان في قلبه مثقال حبة من خردل من إيمان"[3] وقال أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه: قال رسول الله ﭬ "يقول الله تعالى الكبرياء ردائي والعظمة إزاري فمن نازعني واحداً منهما ألقيته في جهنم ولا أبالي"[4] وعن أبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن قال: التقى عبد الله بن عمرو وعبد الله بن عمر على الصفا فتواقفا، فمضى ابن عمرو وأقام ابن عمر يبكي، فقالوا ما يبكيك يا أبا عبد الرحمن؟ فقال: هذا - يعني عبد الله بن عمرو - زعم أنه سمع رسول الله ﭬ يق
31:16.english: And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "He will not enter Paradise who has in his heart (Qalb) the weight of a mustard seed of arrogance (Kibr), and he will not enter the Fire who has in his heart (Qalb) the weight of a mustard seed of faith (Iman)." And Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Allah the Exalted says: 'Grandeur (Kibriya) is My cloak and majesty (Izzah) is My garment; whoever contends with Me for one of them, I will cast him into Hellfire and I do not care.'" And from Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, he said: Abdullah ibn Amr and Abdullah ibn Umar met at al-Safa and stood together, then Ibn Amr departed and Ibn Umar remained weeping. They said: "What makes you weep, O Abu Abd al-Rahman?" He said: "This one - meaning Abdullah ibn Amr - claimed that he heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: 'Whoever has in his heart (Qalb) the weight of a mustard seed of arrogance (Kibr), Allah will throw him on his face into the Fire.'" And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "A man continues to go with his soul (Nafs) until he is written among the tyrants (Jabbarin), and he is afflicted with what afflicted them of punishment." And Sulayman ibn Dawud (peace be upon them both) said one day - to the birds, mankind, jinn, and beasts: "Come out," so they came out in two hundred thousand of mankind and two hundred thousand of jinn, and he was raised until he heard the clamor of the angels with glorification in the heavens, then he was lowered until his feet touched the sea, and he heard a voice: "If there were in the heart (Qalb) of your companion the weight of an atom of arrogance (Kibr), I would have caused him to sink farther than I raised him." And he (peace be upon him) said: "There emerges from the Fire a neck that has two ears that hear and two eyes that see and a tongue that speaks."
31:16.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

31:16.arabic: [59] حديث لا يدخل الجنة من في قلبه مثقال حبة من خردل من كبر تقدم.
31:16.english: Hadith: 'He will not enter Paradise who has in his heart the weight of a mustard seed of arrogance' - previously mentioned.
31:16.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

31:16.arabic: وللشيخين من حديث أبي سعيد الخدري من وجدتم في قلبه مثقال حبة من خردل من الإيمان فأخرجوه وفي رواية من خير وفيه فيقول الله تعالى شفعت الملائكة وشفعت النبيون وشفع المؤمنون ولم يبق إلا أرحم الراحمين فيقبض قبضة من النار فيخرج منها قوما لم يعملوا خيرا قط الحديث.
31:16.english: And from the two Sheikhs (Al-Bukhari and Muslim) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri: 'Whoever you find in his heart (Qalb) the weight of a mustard seed (Habbah min Khardal) of faith (Iman), then bring him out.' And in a narration: 'of good.' And in it, Allah the Exalted says: 'The angels have interceded, and the prophets have interceded, and the believers have interceded, and none remains except the Most Merciful of the merciful.' Then He takes a handful from the Fire and brings out from it a people who never did any good at all.' The hadith.
31:16.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Foundations of Belief'

31:16.arabic: [3] حديث لا يدخل الجنة من كان في قلبه مثقال حبة من خردل من كبر ولا يدخل النار رجل في قلبه مثقال حبة من خردل من إيمان أخرجه مسلم من حديث ابن مسعود.
31:16.english: Hadith: 'He will not enter Paradise who has in his heart (Qalb) the weight of a mustard seed (Khardal) of arrogance (Kibr), nor will he enter Hellfire a man who has in his heart (Qalb) the weight of a mustard seed (Khardal) of faith (Iman).' Reported by Muslim from the narration of Ibn Mas'ud.
31:16.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

31:17.arabic: وقال ﭬ "اخزن لسانك إلا من خير فإنك بذلك تغلب الشيطان"[22] وقال ﭬ "إن الله عند لسان كل قائل فليتق الله امرؤ علم ما يقول" وقال ﭬ "إذا رأيتم المؤمن صموتا وقورا فادنوا منه فإنه يلقن الحكمة[23]" وقال ابن مسعود: قال رسول الله ﭬ "الناس ثلاثة: غانم وسالم وشاحب. فالغانم الذي يذكر الله تعالى، والسالم الساكت، والشاحب الذي يخوض في الباطل"[24] وقال عليه السلام "إن لسان المؤمن وراء قلبه فإذا أراد أن يتكلم بشيء تدبره بقلبه ثم أمضاه بلسانه، وإن لسان المنافق أمام قلبه، فإذا هم بشيء أمضاه بلسانه ولم يتدبره بقلبه"
31:17.english: And He (peace be upon him) said: "Guard your tongue except for good, for by that you overcome Satan." [22] And He (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, Allah is at the tongue of every speaker, so let a person who knows what he says fear Allah." And He (peace be upon him) said: "When you see the believer silent and dignified, approach him, for he imparts wisdom." [23] And Ibn Mas'ud said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "People are three: a gainer, a safe one, and a pale one. The gainer is the one who remembers Allah the Exalted, the safe one is the silent one, and the pale one is the one who delves into falsehood." [24] And He (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, the tongue of the believer is behind his heart (Qalb), so when he intends to speak something, he considers it with his heart (Qalb), then executes it with his tongue. And the tongue of the hypocrite is in front of his heart (Qalb), so when he intends something, he executes it with his tongue and does not consider it with his heart (Qalb)." [25] And Jesus (peace be upon him) said: "Worship (Ibadah) is ten parts: nine of them are in silence and one part is in fleeing from people." And our Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever increases his speech increases his slips, and whoever increases his slips increases his sins, and whoever increases his sins, the Fire is more deserving of him." [26] The Effects: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) would place a pebble in his mouth to prevent himself from speaking, and he would point to his tongue and say: "This is what has brought me to the watering places." And Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: "By Allah, besides whom there is no deity, nothing is more in need of long imprisonment than the tongue." And he said:
31:17.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

31:17.arabic: وكل من حملت إليه النميمة وقيل له إن فلاناً قال فيك كذا وكذا أو فعل في حقك كذا أو هو يدبر في إفساد أمرك أو في ممالأة عدوك أو تقبيح حالك أو ما يجري مجراه فعليه ستة أمور، الأول: أن لا يصدقه لأن النمام فاسق وهو مردود الشهادة قال الله تعالى "يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن جاءكم فاسق بنبأ فتبينوا أن تصيبوا قوماً بجهالة" الثاني: أن ينهاه عن ذلك وينصح له ويقبح عليه فعله قال الله تعالى "وأمر بالمعروف وانه عن المنكر" الثالث: أن يبغضه في الله تعالى فإنه بغيض عند الله تعالى ويجب بغض من يبغضه الله تعالى.
31:17.english: And whoever is brought gossip and it is said to him that so-and-so said such-and-such about you or did such-and-such against you, or is planning to corrupt your affair or to ally with your enemy or to vilify your condition or what follows its course, then upon him are six matters. First: that he not believe him because the gossip-monger is corrupt (Fasiq) and his testimony is rejected.
