Allah the Exalted said: 'O you who have believed, if there comes to you a corrupt (Fasiq) person with information, then verify, lest you harm a people out of ignorance.' Second: that he forbid him from that and advise him and deem his action ugly. Allah the Exalted said: 'And enjoin the good (Ma'ruf) and forbid the evil (Munkar).' Third: that he hate him for the sake of Allah the Exalted, for he is hateful in the sight of Allah the Exalted, and it is obligatory to hate whom Allah the Exalted hates.
31:17.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

31:17.arabic: وإنما أدبه القرآن بمثل قوله تعالى خذ العفو وأمر بالعرف وأعرض عن الجاهلين وقوله إن الله يأمر بالعدل والإحسان وإيتاء ذي القربى وينهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر والبغي وقوله واصبر على ما أصابك إن ذلك من عزم الأمور وقوله ولمن صبر وغفر إن ذلك لمن عزم الأمور
31:17.english: And the Quran disciplined him with verses like His saying: 'Take forgiveness and command with what is known (al-'urf) and turn away from the ignorant ones,' and His saying: 'Indeed, Allah commands justice and excellence (al-ihsan) and giving to relatives, and forbids immorality and what is disapproved (al-munkar) and oppression,' and His saying: 'And be patient (wa-isbir) over what has befallen you. Indeed, that is of the matters of determination (min 'azm al-umur),' and His saying: 'And for one who is patient (sabara) and forgives, indeed that is of the matters of determination.'
31:17.book_title: Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character
31:17.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character'

31:17.arabic: إذن من آداب الحسبة توطين النفس على الصبر ولذلك قرن الله تعالى الصبر بالأمر بالمعروف فقال حاكيا عن لقمان يا بني أقم الصلاة وأمر بالمعروف وانه عن المنكر واصبر على ما أصابك ومن الآداب تقليل العلائق حتى لا يكثر خوفه وقطع الطمع عن الخلائق حتى تزول عنه المداهنة
31:17.english: Therefore, from the etiquettes of enjoining good and forbidding evil (al-Hisbah) is preparing the Soul (Nafs) for patience (al-Sabr). And for this reason, Allah the Exalted coupled patience with commanding good, saying, narrating from Luqman: 'O my son, establish the prayer (al-Salah) and command good (al-Ma'ruf) and forbid evil (al-Munkar) and be patient (wa-isbir) over what befalls you.' And from the etiquettes is reducing attachments so that his fear does not increase, and cutting off hope from the creation so that hypocrisy (al-Mudahanah) is removed from him.
31:17.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

31:18.arabic: وكان الحسن بن علي رضي الله عنهما يمر بالسؤال وبين أيديهم كسر فيقولون هلم إلى الغداء يا ابن رسول الله فكان ينزل ويجلس على الطريق ويأكل معهم ويركب ويقول إن الله لا يحب المستكبرين الوجه الثاني أن الذي شغل نفسه بطلب رضا الناس عنه وتحسين اعتقادهم فيه مغرور لأنه لو عرف الله حق المعرفة علم أن الخلق لا يغنون عنه من الله شيئا وأن ضرره ونفعه بيد الله ولا نافع ولا ضار سواه وأن من طلب رضا الناس ومحبتهم بسخط الله سخط الله عليه وأسخط عليه الناس بل رضا الناس غاية لا تنال فرضا الله أولى بالطلب ولذلك قال الشافعي
31:18.english: And Al-Hasan ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with them both) would pass by the poor people while they had crumbs before them, and they would say: 'Come to lunch, O son of the Messenger of Allah.' So he would dismount, sit on the road, eat with them, and then ride again, saying: 'Indeed, Allah does not love the arrogant ones (Al-Mustakbireen).' The second aspect is that the one who occupies his Soul (Nafs) with seeking the pleasure of people about him and improving their opinion of him is deluded, because if he knew Allah with true knowledge (Ma'rifah), he would know that the creation cannot avail him anything from Allah, and that his harm and benefit are in the hand of Allah, and there is no benefactor nor harmer except Him, and that whoever seeks the pleasure and love of people with the anger of Allah, Allah will be angry with him and make people angry with him. Rather, the pleasure of people is an unattainable goal, so the pleasure of Allah is more worthy of seeking. Therefore, Al-Shafi'i said to Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la: 'By Allah, I only advise you: there is no way to safety from people, so look at what benefits you and do it.' Therefore, it is said: 'Whoever watches people dies grieving, and the bold one attains pleasure.' And Sahl looked at a man from his companions and said to him: 'Do such and such for something he commanded him to do.' He said: 'O teacher, I cannot do it because of people.' So he turned to his companions and said: 'A servant does not attain the reality (Haqiqah) of this matter until he is in one of two descriptions: a servant from whose eye people have fallen, so he sees in the world only his Creator, and that no one can harm him nor benefit him; and a servant whose Soul (Nafs) has fallen from his Heart (Qalb), so he does not care in what state they see him.' And Al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'There is no one except that he has a lover and a hater, so if it is like this, then be with the people of obedience to Allah.' And it was said to Al-Hasan: 'O Abu Sa'id, indeed some people attend your gathering, and their aim is only to follow...'
31:18.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Seclusion'

31:18.arabic: در  من المشركين فقال "لا تسبوا هؤلاء فإنه لا  يخلص  إليهم  شيء  مما  تقولون  وتؤذون الأحياء ألا إن البذاء لؤم"[62] وقال ﭬ "ليس المؤمن  بالطعان  ولا  اللعان  ولا الفاحش ولا البذي"[63] وقال ﭬ "الجنة حرام على كل فاحش أن يدخلها"[64]  وقال  ﭬ "أربعة يؤذون أهل النار في النار  على  ما  بهم  من  الأذى  يسعون  بين  الحميم والجحيم يدعون بالويل والثبور: رجل يسيل فوه قيحاً ودماً فيقال له ما بال  الأبعد قد آذاناً على ما بنا من الأذى؟ فيقول إن الأبعد كان  ينظر  إلى  كل  كلمة  قذعة خبيثة فيستلذها كما يستلذ الر
31:18.english: From the polytheists, he said: "Do not curse these, for nothing of what you say reaches them, and you harm the living. Indeed, obscenity is baseness."[62] And he (peace be upon him) said: "The believer is not one who slanders, nor curses, nor is obscene, nor foul-mouthed."[63] And he (peace be upon him) said: "Paradise is forbidden for every obscene person to enter."[64] And he (peace be upon him) said: "Four will harm the people of Hell in Hell, despite the harm upon them, they run between scalding water and blazing fire, calling out woe and ruin: a man whose mouth flows with pus and blood, and it is said to him: 'Why has the distant one harmed us despite the harm upon us?' He says: 'The distant one used to look at every foul, vile word and relish it as one relishes obscenity.'"[65] And he (peace be upon him) said to Aisha: "O Aisha, if obscenity were a man, he would be an evil man."[66] And he (peace be upon him) said: "Obscenity and explicit disclosure are two branches from the branches of hypocrisy."[67] It is possible that by 'explicit disclosure' is meant in matters of religion and in the attributes of Allah, the Exalted, for presenting that summarily to the ears of the common people is preferable to exaggeration in its explanation; since from the utmost explanation in it may arise doubts and whisperings, so if summarized, the hearts (Qulub) hasten to acceptance and do not become disturbed. But its mention coupled with obscenity resembles that what is intended by it is publicizing what a person is ashamed to disclose, for the better in such is overlooking and ignoring without uncovering and explanation. And he (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, Allah does not love the obscene, excessively obscene one shouting in the markets."[68] And Jabir ibn Samura said: I was sitting with the Prophet (peace be upon him) and my father was before me, and he (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, obscenity and excessive obscenity are not from Islam in anything, and the best of people in Islam are the best of them in character."[69] And Ibrahim ibn Maysara said: It is said the obscene, excessively obscene one will be brought on the Day of Resurrection in the form of a dog or inside a dog. And Al-Ahnaf ibn Qais said: Shall I not inform you of the worst disease: the foul-mouthed tongue and lowly character.
31:18.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

31:18.arabic: ومن المتكبرين من يجيب الأغنياء دون الفقراء وهو خلاف السنة كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يجيب دعوة العبد ودعوة المسكين حديث كان يجيب دعوة العبد ودعوة المسكين أخرجه الترمذي وابن ماجة من حديث أنس دون ذكر المسكين ضعفه الترمذي وصححه الحاكم ومر الحسن بن علي رضي الله عنهما بقوم من المساكين الذين يسألون الناس على الطريق وقد نشروا كسرا على الأرض في الرمل وهم يأكلون وهو على بغلته فسلم عليهم فقالوا له هلم إلى الغداء يا ابن بنت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال نعم إن الله لا يحب المستكبرين فنزل وقعد معه
31:18.english: And among the arrogant ones are those who accept invitations from the rich but not from the poor, and this is contrary to the Sunnah (the way of the Prophet). The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, used to accept invitations from the slave and the poor person. The hadith: 'He used to accept invitations from the slave and the poor person' was reported by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah from the narration of Anas, without mentioning the poor person; al-Tirmidhi considered it weak, and al-Hakim authenticated it. And al-Hasan ibn Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both, passed by a group of poor people who ask people on the road, and they had spread crumbs on the ground in the sand and were eating, while he was on his mule. He greeted them, and they said to him: 'Come to lunch, O son of the daughter of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him.' He said: 'Yes, for Allah does not love the arrogant ones.' So he dismounted and sat with them on the ground and ate. Then he greeted them and rode and said: 'I have accepted your invitation, so accept mine.' They said: 'Yes.' So he appointed a known time for them, and they attended, and he presented to them the best food and sat eating with them.
31:18.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Manners of Eating'

31:18.arabic: ومنها أن يتواضع لكل مسلم ولا يتكبر عليه فإن الله لا يحب كل مختال فخور قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن الله تعالى أوحى إلى أن تواضعوا حتى لا يفخر أحد على أحد حديث أن الله أوحى إلى أن تواضعوا حتى لا يفجر أحد على أحد أخرجه أبو داود وابن ماجه و اللفظ له من حديث عياض بن جماز ورجاله رجال الصحيح ثم أن تفاخر عليه غيره فليحتمل قال الله تعالى لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم خذ العفو وأمر بالعرف وأعرض عن الجاهلين وعن ابن أبي أوفى كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يتواضع لكل مسلم ولا يأنف ولا يتكبر أن يمشي مع ا
31:18.english: And from them is that he should show humility (تواضع) to every Muslim and not be arrogant (تكبر) toward him, for Allah does not love every arrogant (مختال) boaster (فخور). The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said: 'Indeed, Allah the Exalted revealed to me that you should be humble (تواضعوا) so that no one boasts (يفخر) over another.' The hadith: 'Indeed, Allah revealed to me that you should be humble so that no one transgresses (يفجر) over another' was narrated by Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah, with the wording from the hadith of Iyad bin Jumaz, and its narrators are narrators of the Sahih. Then, if others boast (تفاخر) over him, let him endure. Allah the Exalted said to His Prophet, peace be upon him: 'Take forgiveness and enjoin what is good and turn away from the ignorant.' And from Ibn Abi Awfa: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, would show humility to every Muslim and would not disdain (يأنف) nor be arrogant (يتكبر) to walk with the widow (أرملة) and the poor (مسكين) to fulfill their need. The hadith of Ibn Abi Awfa: 'He would not disdain nor be arrogant (يستكبر) to walk with the widow and the poor to fulfill their need' was narrated by Al-Nasa'i with a sound chain and Al-Hakim said it meets the conditions of the two Shaykhs.
31:18.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

31:19.arabic: وقول الله تعالى إن أنكر الأصوات لصوت الحمير يدل بمفهومه على مدح الصوت الحسن ولو جاز أن يقال إنما أبيح ذلك بشرط أن يكون في القرآن للزمه أن يحرم سماع صوت العندليب لأنه ليس من القرآن وإذا جوز سماع صوت غفل لا معنى له فلم لا يجوز سماع صوت يفهم منه الحكمة والمعاني الصحيحة وإن من الشعر لحكمة فهذا نظر في الصوت من حيث أنه طيب حسن
31:19.english: And the saying of Allah the Exalted: 'Indeed, the most repulsive of voices is the voice of the donkeys' indicates by its implication the praise of the beautiful voice. And if it were permissible to say that this is only permitted on the condition that it be in the Quran, it would necessarily follow that listening to the voice of the nightingale is forbidden because it is not from the Quran. And if listening to a voice that is heedless and has no meaning is permitted, then why should listening to a voice from which wisdom and sound meanings are understood not be permitted? And indeed, in poetry there is wisdom. This is a consideration of the voice from the perspective that it is pleasant and beautiful.
31:19.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

31:22.arabic: وله عنه فقد استمسك بالعروة الوثقى قال لا إله الا الله
31:22.english: And from him (Ibn Abbas) regarding 'He has grasped the firmest handhold (Al-'Urwah Al-Wuthqa)' said: 'There is no god but Allah (La Ilaha Illa Allah).'

31:25.arabic: وترك الخاسرين في ظلمات العمى يتيهون وفي مسارح المحسوسات وشهوات البهائم يترددون؛ يعملون ظاهراً من الحياة الدنيا وهم عن الآخرة هم غافلون. الحمد لله بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون. فالحب بهذا السبب أقوى من الحب بالإحسان لأن الإحسان يزيد وينقص.
31:25.english: And He left the losers wandering in the darknesses of blindness and wandering in the pastures of the sensibles and the lusts of the beasts; they work the outward aspect of the worldly life while they are heedless of the Hereafter. Praise be to Allah, but most of them do not know. So love by this cause is stronger than love by beneficence because beneficence increases and decreases.
31:25.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

31:25.arabic: ولهذا بعث الأنبياء صلوات الله عليهم لدعوة الخلق إلى التوحيد ليقولوا لا إله إلا الله وما أمروا أن يقولوا لنا إله وللعالم إله فإن ذلك كان مجبولا في فطرة عقولهم من مبدأ نشؤهم وفي عنفوان شبابهم ولذلك قال عز وجل ولئن سألتهم من خلق السموات والأرض ليقولن الله وقال تعالى: )فأقم وجهك للدين حنيفا فطرة الله التي فطر الناس عليها لا تبديل لخلق الله ذلك الدين القيم( فإذا في فطرة الإنسان وشواهد القرآن ما يغني عن إقامة البرهان
31:25.english: And for this reason, the Prophets (peace be upon them) were sent to call the creation to Monotheism (Tawhid) so that they would say 'There is no god but Allah,' and they were not commanded to say to us 'a god' and to the world 'a god,' for that was ingrained in the innate disposition (Fitrah) of their intellects from the beginning of their growth and in the prime of their youth. And for this reason, the Almighty said: 'And if you ask them who created the heavens and the earth, they will surely say Allah.' And He said: 'So set your face to the religion, inclining to truth. [Adhere to] the innate disposition (Fitrah) of Allah upon which He has created [all] people. No change should there be in the creation of Allah. That is the correct religion.' So indeed, in the innate disposition (Fitrah) of the human and the evidences of the Quran, there is what suffices without establishing proof.
31:25.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Foundations of Belief'

31:25.arabic: فقد رآني فإن الشيطان لا يتخيل بي متفق عليه من حديث أبي هريرة. [142] حديث ابن عيينة عن محمد بن المنكدر عن جابر ما سئل النبي ﭬ شيئا قط فقال لا رواه مسلم وقد تقدم. [143] حديث قال الله تعالى شمتنى ابن آدم وما ينبغى له أن يشتمنى وكذبنى ما ينبغى له أن يكذبنى الحديث أخرجه البخارى من حديث أبى هريرة. [144] حديث كيف أنعم وصاحب الصور قد التقم القرن وحنى الجبهة الحديث أخرجه الترمذى من حديث أبى سعيد وقال حسن ورواه ابن ماجه بلفظ إن صاحبى القرن بأيديهما أو فى أيديهما قرنان يلاحظان النظر متى يؤمران وفى رواية اب
31:25.english: He saw me, for Satan does not imagine me, agreed upon from the hadith of Abu Huraira. [142] Hadith of Ibn 'Uyaynah from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir from Jabir: The Prophet (peace be upon him) was never asked for anything and said no, narrated by Muslim and previously mentioned. [143] Hadith: Allah the Exalted said: 'Son of Adam has reviled Me, and it is not fitting for him to revile Me, and he has denied Me, and it is not fitting for him to deny Me,' the hadith was transmitted by al-Bukhari from the hadith of Abu Huraira. [144] Hadith: 'How can I enjoy comfort when the companion of the Trumpet has taken the horn and bent his forehead?' The hadith was transmitted by al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Abu Sa'id and he said it is good, and Ibn Majah narrated it with the wording: 'Indeed my two companions of the horn are in their hands or in their hands two horns, observing the gaze when they will be commanded,' and in the narration of Ibn Majah, al-Hajjaj ibn Artah is disputed. [145] Hadith: 'When he was sent to, he was sent to the companion of the Trumpet, so he gestured with it to his mouth and advanced one leg and delayed another,' the hadith I did not find like this, but it has been reported that Israfil from the beginning of creation is like that, as narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Tarikh and Abu al-Shaykh in Kitab al-'Azamah from the hadith of Abu Huraira: 'When Allah, blessed and exalted, finished creating the heavens and the earth, He created the Trumpet and gave it to Israfil, so he is placing it on his mouth, staring with his sight at the Throne, waiting for when he will be commanded,' al-Bukhari said: 'It is not authentic,' and in a narration of Abu al-Shaykh: 'The companion of the Trumpet has not blinked since he was entrusted with it, prepared, looking towards the Throne, fearing that he will be commanded before his glance returns to him, as if his two eyes are two shining stars,' and its chain is good. [146] Hadith: 'People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection on a white, pure land like a flat loaf of bread, with no landmark for anyone,' agreed upon from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd, and al-Bukhari separated his saying: 'with no landmark for anyone,' so he made it from the saying of Sahl or others, and Muslim included it in it. [147] Hadith: 'People will be resurrected barefoot, naked, uncircumcised, sweat has bridled them and reached the fats of the ears,' said Sawdah, the narrator of the hadith: 'And woe to me,' the hadith was transmitted by al-Tha'labi and al-Baghawi, and it is in the two Sahihs from the hadith of 'A'ishah, and she is the one saying: 'And woe to me,' and al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Awsat from the hadith of Umm Salamah, and she is the one saying: 'And woe to me.' [148] Hadith of Abu Huraira: 'People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection riding and walking and on their faces,' the hadith was narrated by al-Tirmidhi and he graded it good, and in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Anas: 'A man said: O Prophet of Allah, how will the disbeliever be gathered on his face? He said: Is not the One who made him walk on...'
31:25.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Book of Repentance'

31:26.arabic: وما يتعلق بالرب تعالى إما ان يكون نظرا في ذاته وصفاته وأسمائه الحسنى وإما أن يكون في أفعاله وملكه وملكوته وجميع ما في السموات والأرض وما بينهما وينكشف لك انحصار الفكر في هذه الأقسام بمثال وهو أن حال السائرين إلى الله تعالى والمشتاقين إلى لقائه يتعلق بمعشوقه أو يتعلق بنفسه فإن تفكر في معشوقه فإما أن يتفكر في جماله وحسن صورته في ذاته ليتنعم بالفكر فيه وبمشاهدته وإما ان يتفكر في أفعاله اللطيفة الحسنة الدالة على أخلاقه وصفاته ليكون ذلك مضعفا للذة ومقويا لمحبته وإن تفكر في نفسه فيكون فكره في صفاته ال
31:26.english: And what pertains to the Lord (Al-Rabb) the Exalted is either a contemplation (Nadhar) in His Essence (Dhat) and His Attributes (Sifat) and His Beautiful Names (Asma' al-Husna), or it is in His Actions (Af'al) and His Dominion (Mulk) and His Sovereignty (Malakut) and all that is in the heavens and the earth and what is between them. And it becomes clear to you the confinement of thought (Fikr) in these divisions by an example, which is that the state (Hal) of those who journey (Al-Sa'irin) to Allah the Exalted and those who yearn (Al-Mushtaqin) for meeting Him pertains to His Beloved (Ma'shuq) or pertains to himself. So if he contemplates in his Beloved, then either he contemplates in His Beauty (Jamal) and the goodness of His Form (Surah) in His Essence (Dhat) to delight in the thought (Fikr) in Him and in witnessing Him (Mushahadah), or he contemplates in His Gentle (Latif), Good (Hasan) Actions (Af'al) that indicate His Morals (Akhlaq) and Attributes (Sifat) so that this becomes a multiplier of pleasure (Ladhdhah) and a strengthener of his love (Mahabbah). And if he contemplates in himself, then his thought (Fikr) is in his attributes (Sifat) that drop him from the eye of his Beloved (Ma'shuq) until he becomes purified (Yatanazzah) from them, or in the attributes (Sifat) that bring him near to Him and make him beloved to Him until he becomes characterized (Yattasif) by them. So if he contemplates in something outside of these divisions, then that is outside the limit of passionate love (Al-'Ishq) and it is a deficiency in it, because the complete (Al-Kamil), perfect (Al-Tamm) passionate love (Al-'Ishq) is what overwhelms the lover (Al-'Ashiq) and fills the Heart (Al-Qalb) until it does not leave in it room for other than Him. So the lover (Muhibb) of Allah the Exalted ought to be like that, so his gaze (Nadhar) and thought (Fikr) do not exceed his Beloved (Ma'shuq). And as long as his thought (Fikr) is confined in these four divisions, it is not outside the requirement of love (Mahabbah) at all. So let us begin with the first division, which is his contemplation (Tafakkur) in the attributes (Sifat) of himself and the actions (Af'al) of himself to distinguish the beloved (Al-Mahbub) among them from the disliked (Al-Makruh), for this thought (Fikr) is what pertains to the knowledge of transaction (Ilm al-Mu'amalah) which is the intended purpose of this book. And as for the other division, it pertains to the knowledge of unveiling (Ilm al-Mukashafah). Then every
31:26.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Contemplation'

31:28.arabic: ويحك يا نفس انزعى عن جهلك وقيسى آخرتك بدنياك فما خلقكم ولا بعثكم إلا كنفس واحدة و كما بدأنا أول خلق نعيده و كما بدأكم تعودون وسنة الله تعالى لا تجدين لها تبديلا ولا تحويلا ويحك يا نفس ما أراك إلا ألفت الدنيا وأنست بها فعسر عليك مفارقتها وأنت مقبلة على مقاربتها وتؤكدين في نفسك مودتها فاحسن أنك غافلة عن عقاب الله وثوابه وعن أهوال القيامة وأحوالها فما أنت مؤمنة بالموت المفرق بينك وبين محابك
31:28.english: Woe to you, O Soul (Nafs)! Cast off your ignorance and measure your Hereafter (Akhirah) by your worldly life, for 'Your creation and your resurrection are not but like that of a single soul (Nafs).' And as We began the first creation, We will repeat it, and as We began you, you will return. And the Way (Sunnah) of Allah, the Exalted, you will find no change or alteration for it. Woe to you, O Soul (Nafs)! I see you only as having become accustomed to the worldly life and finding comfort in it, so parting from it has become difficult for you, while you are approaching its proximity, and you confirm in your soul (Nafs) its affection. Know well that you are heedless of the punishment (Iqab) of Allah and His reward (Thawab), and of the terrors (Ahwal) of the Resurrection (Qiyamah) and its states (Ahwal). You are not truly believing in death, which separates you from your beloved things.
31:28.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

31:28.arabic: وكما أن الأبرار يجدون المزيد في حالهم ومعرفتهم بقربهم من المقربين ومشاهدتهم لهم، فكذلك يكون حالهم في الآخرة "ما خلقكم ولا بعثكم إلا كنفس واحدة كما بدأنا أول خلق نعيده"، وكما قال تعالى: "جزاء وفاقاً" أي وافق الجزاء أعمالهم فقوبل الخالص بالصرف من الشراب وقوبل المشوب بالمشوب، وشوب كل شراب على قدر ما سبق من الشوب في حبه وأعماله
31:28.english: And just as the Righteous (Al-Abrar) find increase in their state and knowledge through their proximity to the Close Ones (Al-Muqarrabun) and their witnessing of them, so too will be their state in the Hereafter: "Your creation and your resurrection are not but like a single soul (Nafs). Just as We began the first creation, We will repeat it." And as Allah the Exalted said: "A recompense in proportion (Jaza'an Wifaqan)" meaning the recompense corresponded to their deeds, so the pure was met with the pure from the drink, and the mixed was met with the mixed, and the mixing of every drink is according to what preceded of mixing in his love and his deeds.
31:28.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

31:28.arabic: فقس الآخره بالأولى فما خلقكم ولا بعثكم الا كنفس واحدة وما النشأة الثانية إلا على قياس النشأة الأولى بل أعداد النشآت ليست محصورة في اثنتين وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى: ﴿ وننشئكم فيما لا تعلمون ﴾ {} فالمقر بالقيامتين مؤمن بعالم الغيب والشهادة وموقن بالملك والملكوت والمقر بالقيامة الصغرى دون الكبرى ناظر بالعين العوراء الى أحد العالمين وذلك هو الجهل والضلال والأقتداء بالأعور الدجال، فما اعظم غفلتك يا مسكين وكلنا ذلك المسكين وبين يديك هذه الأهوال فإن كنت لا تؤمن بالقيامة الكبرى بالجهل والضلال أفلا تكفي
31:28.english: So measure the Hereafter (Al-Akhirah) by the first, for 'Your creation and your resurrection are not but like a single Soul (Nafs)' and the second creation (Nash'ah) is only according to the measure of the first creation (Nash'ah). Rather, the numbers of creations (Nash'at) are not limited to two, and to this is the indication by His saying, the Exalted: 'And We will create you in what you do not know.' So the one who affirms the two resurrections (Qiyamatayn) is a believer in the world of the unseen (Al-Ghayb) and the witnessed (Al-Shahadah), and certain of the dominion (Al-Mulk) and the sovereignty (Al-Malakut). And the one who affirms the minor resurrection (Al-Qiyamah Al-Sughra) without the major (Al-Kubra) is looking with the one-eyed eye (Al-'Ayn Al-'Awra') to one of the two worlds, and that is ignorance (Al-Jahl) and misguidance (Al-Dalal) and following the one-eyed Dajjal. So how great is your heedlessness (Ghaflah), O wretched one, and all of us are that wretched one, and before you are these terrors. If you do not believe in the major resurrection (Al-Qiyamah Al-Kubra) due to ignorance (Al-Jahl) and misguidance (Al-Dalal), does not the indication of the minor resurrection (Al-Qiyamah Al-Sughra) suffice you? Or have you not heard the saying of the master of the prophets: 'Sufficient is death as a warner' or have you not heard Abu Bakr, upon him be peace, at death until he said: 'O Allah, make easy for Muhammad the agonies of death'? Or are you not ashamed of your delay in the assault of death, following the riffraff of the heedless (Al-Ghafilun) who do not look except at a single blast that seizes them while they are disputing, so they cannot make a will nor return to their families? Then comes to them illness as a warner from death, but they do not take warning, and comes to them gray hair as a messenger from it, but they do not take heed. So woe to the servants! There comes not to them a messenger but that they mock him. Do they think that they are in the world (Al-Dunya) immortal? Or have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them?
31:28.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

31:28.arabic: الأصل الأول: الحشر والنشر[39] وقد ورد بهما الشرع وهو حق والتصديق بهما واجب لأنه في العقل ممكن ومعناه الإعادة بعد الإفناء وذلك مقدور لله تعالى كابتداء الإنشاء قال الله تعالى: ﴿ قال من يحيي العظام وهي رميم. قل يحييها الذي أنشأها أول مرة ﴾ { سورة يس: 78، 79 } فاستدل بالابتداء على الإعادة وقال عز وجل: ﴿ ما خلقكم ولا بعثكم إلا كنفس واحدة ﴾ { سورة لقمان: 28 } والإعادة ابتداء ثان فهو ممكن كالابتداء الأول.
31:28.english: The First Foundation: The Gathering (Al-Hashr) and the Resurrection (Al-Nashr)[39]. The Sacred Law (Al-Shar') has come with them, and they are true, and believing in them is obligatory because it is rationally possible. Its meaning is the restoration after annihilation, and that is within the power of Allah, the Exalted, like the initial creation. Allah, the Exalted, said: 'He said, "Who will give life to bones while they are disintegrated?" Say, "He will give them life who produced them the first time."' {Surah Ya-Sin: 78-79}. So, He argued from the initial creation to the restoration. And He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Your creation and your resurrection are not but like that of a single Soul (Nafs).' {Surah Luqman: 28}. And the restoration is a second beginning, so it is possible like the first beginning.
31:28.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

31:33.arabic: كل ذلك رجاء أن تخلص أعمالهم الصالحة فيجازيهم الله في القيامة بإخلاصهم على ملأ من الخلص، إذ علموا أن الله لا يقبل في القيامة إلا الخالص وعلموا شدة حاجتهم وفاقتهم في القيامة وأنه يوم لا ينفع فيه مال ولا بنون ولا يجزى والد عن ولده، ويشتغل الصديقون بأنفسهم فيقول كل واحد. نفسي نفسي! فضلاً عن غيرهم فكانوا كزوار بيت الله إذا توجهوا إلى مكة فإنهم يستصحبون مع أنفسهم الذهب المغربي الخالص لعلمهم أن أرباب البوادي لا يروج عندهم الزائف والبهرج، والحاجة تشتد في البادية ولا وطن يفزع إليه ولا حميم يتمسك به فلا ي
31:33.english: All of that hoping that their righteous deeds would be purified so that Allah would reward them on the Day of Standing (Qiyamah) with their sincerity (Ikhlas) before a gathering of the pure ones, since they knew that Allah does not accept on the Day of Standing (Qiyamah) except the pure (Khalis), and they knew the severity of their need and poverty on the Day of Standing (Qiyamah) and that it is a day when wealth will not benefit, nor sons, nor will a parent be recompensed for their child, and the truthful ones (Siddiqun) will be preoccupied with themselves, each one saying: 'My soul (Nafs)! My soul (Nafs)!' let alone others. So they were like visitors to the House of Allah when they head to Mecca, for they take with themselves pure Moroccan gold, knowing that the people of the desert do not circulate the counterfeit and the flashy, and need intensifies in the desert with no homeland to flee to nor intimate friend to cling to, so only the pure (Khalis) from the currency is saved. Likewise, the possessors of hearts (Arbab al-Qulub) witness on the Day of Standing (Qiyamah) the provision (Zad) which they have prepared for it from piety (Taqwa).
31:33.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

31:33.arabic: ويحك يا نفس لا ينبغى أن تغرك الحياة الدنيا ولا يغرنك بالله الغرور فانظرى لنفسك فما أمرك بمهم لغيرك ولا تضيعى أوقاتك فالأنفاس معدودة فإذا مضى منك نفس فقد ذهب بعضك فاغتنمى الصحة قبل السقم والفراغ قبل الشغل والغنى قبل الفقر والشباب قبل الهرم والحياة قبل الموت واستعدي للآخرة على قدر بقائك فيها يا نفس أما تستعدين للشتاء بقدر طول مدته فتجمعين له القوت والكسوة والحطب وجميع الأسباب ولا تتكلين في ذلك على فضل الله وكرمه حتى يدفع عنك البرد من غير جبة ولبد وحطب وغير ذلك فإنه قادر على ذلك أفتظنين أيتها النفس
31:33.english: Woe to you, O Soul (Nafs)! It is not fitting that the worldly life should deceive you, nor should the deceiver deceive you concerning Allah. So look to your soul (Nafs), for you are not commanded with something important for others, and do not waste your times, for the breaths are counted. So when a breath passes from you, part of you has gone. So seize health before sickness, leisure before occupation, wealth before poverty, youth before old age, and life before death, and prepare for the Hereafter according to the length of your stay in it, O soul (Nafs). Do you not prepare for winter according to the length of its duration, gathering for it provisions, clothing, firewood, and all means, and do not rely in that on the bounty of Allah and His generosity until He repels the cold from you without a cloak, felt, firewood, and other than that, for He is capable of that. Do you think, O soul (Nafs), that the intense cold of Hell is lighter in cold and shorter in duration than the intense cold of winter? Or do you think that that is less than this? No, that this is so or that there is a similarity between them in severity and coldness. Do you think that the servant is saved from it without striving? Far be it! Just as the cold of winter is not repelled except by a cloak, fire, and all means, so the heat of the Fire and its cold are not repelled except by the fortress of Monotheism (Tawhid) and the trench of acts of obedience. And the generosity of Allah, the Exalted, is in that He made known to you the way of fortification and facilitated its means for you, not in that He repels the punishment from you without its fortress, just as the generosity of Allah, the Exalted, in repelling the cold of winter is that He created fire and guided you to the way of extracting it from between iron and stone so that you may repel with it the cold of winter from your soul (Nafs), and just as
31:33.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

31:33.arabic: وخطب علي كرم الله وجهه يوماً خطبة فقال فيها: اعلموا أنكم ميتون ومبعوثون من بعد الموت وموقوفون على أعمالكم ومجزيون بها، فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا فإنها بالبلاء محفوفة وبالفناء معروفة وبالغدر موصوفة، وكل ما فيها إلى زوال وهي بين أهلها دول وسجال، لا تدوم أحوالها ولا يسلم من شرها نزالها، بينا أهلها منها في رخاء وسرور إذا هم منها في بلاء وغرور. أحوال مختلفة وتارات منصرفة، العيش فها مذموم والرخاء فيها لا يدوم وإنما أهلها فيها أغراض مستهدفة. ترميهم بسهامها وتقصيهم بحمامها. وكل حتفه فيها مقدور وحظه فيها
31:33.english: And Ali, may Allah honor his face, delivered a sermon one day in which he said: Know that you will die and be resurrected after death, and you will be held accountable for your deeds and recompensed for them. So do not let the worldly life deceive you, for it is surrounded by tribulation, known for its perishability, and described with betrayal. Everything in it is destined to vanish, and it is among its inhabitants a rotating and flowing [affair]. Its conditions do not last, and its dwellers are not safe from its harm. While its people are in ease and joy from it, suddenly they are in tribulation and deception. Conditions are varied and times are passing. Living in it is blameworthy, and ease in it does not endure; rather, its people in it are targeted objectives. It shoots them with its arrows and cuts them off with its death. Every person's appointed time in it is decreed, and his share in it is fulfilled. And know, O servants of Allah, that you and what you are in of this worldly life are on the path of those who have passed away—those who had longer lifespans than you, were mightier in strength than you, built more dwellings, and left more distant traces. Their voices have become silent and extinguished after long turning [in life], their bodies have decayed, their dwellings are empty on their foundations, and their traces are effaced. They have exchanged the constructed palaces, the couches, and the spread cushions for the leaning rocks and stones in the sunken, hidden graves. Its place is near, and its inhabitant is a stranger among the inhabitants of buildings who are desolate and the inhabitants of neighborhoods who are preoccupied. They do not find comfort in civilization, nor do they communicate with the communication of neighbors and brothers despite the closeness of place, neighborhood, and nearness of dwelling. And how can there be communication between them when tribulation has ground them with its millstone and the rocks and dust have consumed them? And they have become...
31:33.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of the World'

31:33.arabic: فلذلك عدل بوجهه عن الله إليهم وأقبل بقلبه عليهم لِيَسْتَمِيلَ بذلك قلوبهم، ولو وكله الله تعالى إليهم في الدنيا والآخرة لكان ذلك أقل مكافأة له على صنيعه، فإن العباد كلهم عاجزون عن أنفسهم لا يملكون لأنفسهم نفعاً ولا ضراً فكيف يملكون لغيرهم هذا في الدنيا؟ فكيف في يوم لا يجزى والد عن ولده ولا مولود هو جاز عن والده شيئاً بل تقول الأنبياء فيه نفسي نفسي؟ فكيف يستبدل الجاهل عن ثواب الآخرة ونيل القرب عند الله ما يرتقبه بطمعه الكاذب في الدنيا من الناس؟ فلا ينبغي أن نشك في أن المرائي بطاعة الله في سخط الله
31:33.english: Therefore, he turned his face away from Allah (God) towards them and directed his heart (Qalb) towards them to attract their hearts (Qalb) with that. And if Allah (God) the Exalted were to entrust him to them in this world (Dunya) and the Hereafter (Akhirah), that would be the least reward for his action, for all servants (Ibad) are incapable regarding themselves—they possess no benefit (Naf') or harm (Darr) for themselves, so how could they possess it for others? This is in this world (Dunya), so how about on a day when a parent (Walid) will not avail his child (Walad) at all, nor will a child (Mawlud) avail his parent (Walid) anything? Rather, the Prophets (Anbiya') will say in it: 'Myself, myself!' So how does the ignorant one exchange the reward of the Hereafter (Akhirah) and attaining closeness (Qurb) with Allah (God) for what he anticipates with his false greed in this world (Dunya) from people? Thus, we should not doubt that the show-off (Mura'i) with obedience (Taa'ah) to Allah (God) is in the displeasure (Sakhat) of Allah (God) from both transmission (Naql) and analogy (Qiyas) together—this is if he did not intend the reward (Ajr); but if he intended the reward (Ajr) and praise (Hamd) together in his charity (Sadaqah) or prayer (Salah), then it is the association (Shirk) that contradicts sincerity (Ikhlas).
31:33.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

31:33.arabic: اعلم أن قوله تعالى "فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا ولا يغرنكم بالله الغرور" وقوله تعالى "ولكنكم فتنتم أنفسكم وتربضتم وارتبتم وغرتكم الأماني" الآية. كاف في ذم الغرور، وقد قال رسول الله ﭬ "حبذا نوم الأكياس وفطرهم كيف يغبنون سهر الحمقى واجتهادهم ولمثقال ذرة من صاحب تقوى ويقين أفضل من ملئ الأرض من المغترين"[1] وقال ﭬ "الكيس من دان نفسه وعمل لما بعد الموت، والأحمق من اتبع نفسه هواها وتمنى على الله"[2] وكل ما ورد في فضل العلم وذم الجهل فهو دليل على ذم الغرور، لأن الغرور عبارة عن بعض أنواع الجهل، إذ الجهل هو
31:33.english: Know that His statement, the Exalted, "So let not the worldly life (al-hayāt al-dunyā) deceive you, nor let the deceiver (al-gharūr) deceive you concerning Allah" and His statement, the Exalted, "But you tempted yourselves and hesitated and doubted, and false hopes (al-amānī) deceived you" the verse. This is sufficient in censuring deception (al-ghurūr), and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, "How excellent is the sleep of the intelligent and their breaking of fast, how they surpass the staying awake of the foolish and their striving, and a speck's weight of one possessing God-consciousness (taqwā) and certainty (yaqīn) is better than the earth filled with the deceived." And he (peace be upon him) said, "The intelligent is he who holds his Soul (Nafs) accountable and works for what is after death, and the foolish is he who follows his Soul's (Nafs) desires (hawāhā) and makes wishes upon Allah." And all that has come regarding the virtue of knowledge and the censure of ignorance is evidence for censuring deception (al-ghurūr), because deception (al-ghurūr) is an expression for some types of ignorance, since ignorance is to believe a thing and see it contrary to what it is, and deception (al-ghurūr) is ignorance except that there is ignorance that is not deception (ghurūr), rather deception (al-ghurūr) necessitates: a deceived one in something specific and a deceiver by which he is deceived. So whenever the striving believer believes something that agrees with desire (al-hawā) and the cause necessitating the ignorance is a false semblance and imagination that he thinks is evidence but is not evidence, the ignorance occurring by it is called deception (ghurūr). So deception (al-ghurūr) is the Soul's (Nafs) tranquility towards what agrees with desire (al-hawā), and the natural inclination inclines to it from a semblance and trick of Satan, so whoever believes he is upon good either in the immediate or the ultimate from a false semblance, he is deceived, and most people think of themselves good and they are mistaken in it, so most people therefore are deceived and if
31:33.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

32:7.arabic: الثاني أن يعرف نسبه الحقيقي، فيعرف أباه وجده فإن أباه القريب نطفة قذرة وجده البعيد تراب ذليل وقد عرفه الله تعالى نسبه فقال "الذين أحسن كل شيء خلقه وبدأ خلق الإنسان من طين ثم جعل نسله من سلالة من ماء مهين" فمن أصله التراب المهين الذي يداس بالأقدام ثم خمر طينة حتى صار حمأ مسنوناً كيف يتكبر؟ وأخس الأشياء ما إليه انتسابه إذ يقال يا أذل من التراب ويا أنتن من الحمأة ويا أقذر من المضغة.
32:7.english: The second is that he should know his true lineage, so he knows his father and grandfather, for his close father is a filthy drop (Nutfah) and his distant grandfather is lowly dust (Turab), and Allah the Exalted has made known his lineage when He said: "The One Who perfected everything He created and began the creation of the human being from clay, then made his progeny from an extract of a despised fluid." So from his origin being the despised dust (Turab) that is trodden under feet, then He fermented the clay until it became stinking mud (Hama'), how can he be arrogant? And the most vile things are what he traces his lineage to, for it is said: O more lowly than dust, O more foul-smelling than stinking mud, and O more filthy than a chewed lump (Mudghah).
32:7.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

32:11.arabic: ولأجل توافق ذلك وتطابقه نسب الله تعالى الأفعال في القرآن مرة إلى الملائكة ومرة إلى العباد، ونسبها بعينها مرة أخرى إلى نفسه، فقال الله تعالى في الموت " قل يتوفاكم ملك الموت " ثم قال عز وجل: " الله يتوفى الأنفس حين موتها " وقال تعالى: " أفرأيتم ما تحرثون " أضاف إلينا ثم قال تعالى: " أنا صببنا ثم شققنا الأرض شقاً فأنبتنا فيها حباً وعنباً "، وقال عز وجل: " فأرسلنا إليها روحنا فتمثل لها بشراً سوياً "، ثم قال تعالى: " فنفخنا فيها من روحنا " وكان النافخ جبريل عليه السلام، وكما قال تعالى: " فإذا قرأناه
32:11.english: And due to the correspondence and congruence of that, Allah the Exalted attributed actions in the Quran at one time to the angels and at another time to the servants, and attributed the very same actions at another time to Himself. So Allah the Exalted said regarding death: "Say: 'The Angel of Death (Malak al-Mawt) who is entrusted with you will take your souls (yatawaffākum)'" then He the Exalted said: "Allah takes the souls (yatawaffā) at the time of their death." And He the Exalted said: "Have you considered what you sow?" He attributed it to us, then He the Exalted said: "We pour down water, then We split the earth in fissures and cause to grow therein grain and grapes." And He the Exalted said: "So We sent to her Our Spirit (Rūḥ), and he represented himself to her as a well-proportioned man." Then He the Exalted said: "So We breathed into her of Our Spirit (Rūḥ)," and the one breathing was Gabriel, peace be upon him. And as He the Exalted said: "So when We have recited it, then follow its recitation," it is said in the interpretation (tafsīr): its meaning is when Gabriel recites it to you. And He the Exalted said: "Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands," so He attributed the killing to them and the punishment to Himself, and the punishment is the very killing. Indeed, He made it explicit and said: "So you did not kill them, but Allah killed them." And He the Exalted said: "And you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw," and it is a combination of negation and affirmation apparently, but its meaning is: and you did not throw by the meaning by which the Lord is a thrower, when you threw by the meaning by which the servant is a thrower, for they are two different meanings.
32:11.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

32:12.arabic: ومن عدا هؤلاء فهم المغرورون بالله "وسوف يعلمون حين يرون العذاب من أضل سبيل-ولتعلمن نبأه بعد حين" وعند ذلك يقولون كما أخبر الله عنهم "ربنا أبصرنا وسمعنا فارجعنا نعمل صالحاً إنا موقنون" أي علمنا أنه كما لا يولد إلا بوقاع ونكاح ولا ينبت زرع إلا بحراثة وبث بذر، فكذلك لا يحصل في الآخرة ثواب وأجر إلا بعمل صالح فارجعنا نعمل صالحاً فقد علمنا الآن صدقك في قولك "وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى وأن سعيه سوف يرى -كلما ألقى فيها فوج سألهم خزنتها ألم يأتكم نذير قالوا بلى قد جاءنا نذير" أي ألم نسمعكم سنة الله في عب
32:12.english: And whoever is other than these are those deluded by Allah "And they will know when they see the punishment who is more astray in way - and you will know its news after a while." And at that time they will say as Allah informed about them: "Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us, we will work righteousness, indeed we are certain." That is, we have known that just as a child is not born except by intercourse and marriage, and a crop does not grow except by plowing and sowing seed, likewise there is no attainment in the Hereafter of reward and recompense except by righteous work, so return us, we will work righteousness, for we have now known the truthfulness in Your saying: "And that for man is only what he strives for, and that his striving will be seen - whenever a group is thrown into it, its keepers ask them: 'Did there not come to you a warner?' They say: 'Yes, a warner had come to us.'" That is, did we not hear you about the Sunnah (established way) of Allah among His servants and that "He takes every soul what it has earned" and that "Every soul is a pledge for what it has earned"? So what deluded you about Allah after you heard and comprehended? "They said: 'If we had been hearing or comprehending, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze.' So they confessed their sin, so away with the companions of the Blaze."
32:12.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

32:13.arabic: ثم يخبر عنه ويقول: ﴿ ولو شئنا لآتينا كل نفس هداها ولكن حق القول مني لأملأن جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ وتمت كلمة ربك لأملأن جهنم ﴾ {} الآية، فكيف لا يخاف ما حق من القول في الأزل ولا يطمع في تداركه ولو كان الأمر أنفا لكانت الأطماع تمتد إلى حيلة فيه ولكن ليس إلا التسليم فيه واستقراء خفى السابقة من جلى الأسباب الظاهرة على القلب والجوارح فمن يسرت له أسباب الشر وحيل بينه وبين أسباب الخير وأحكمت علاقته من الدنيا فكأنه كشف له على التحقيق سر السابقة التي سبقت له بالشقاوة، إذ كل ميسر ل
32:13.english: Then He informs about it and says: 'And if We had willed, We could have given every Soul (Nafs) its guidance, but the Word (Qawl) from Me has been decreed: I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind all together.' And the Exalted said: 'And the Word (Kalimah) of your Lord has been fulfilled: I will surely fill Hell...' the verse. So how can one not fear what has been decreed from the Word (Qawl) in eternity and not hope to recover it? If the matter were otherwise, hopes would extend to a stratagem in it, but there is nothing except submission (Taslim) in it and investigating the hidden precedence from the apparent causes manifest on the Heart (Qalb) and limbs. For whoever is facilitated for him the causes of evil and is prevented between him and the causes of good, and his connection from the world is firmly established, it is as if the secret of the precedence that preceded for him with wretchedness has been revealed to him in truth, since everyone is facilitated for what he was created for. And if all good deeds are facilitated and the Heart (Qalb) is completely cut off from the world and with its outward and inward turned towards God, this would necessitate alleviation of fear if constancy upon that were trusted, but the danger of the ending and the difficulty of steadfastness increase the flames of fear in ignition and cannot be extinguished. And how can one feel secure from changing of state when the Heart (Qalb) of the believer is between two fingers of the fingers of the Most Merciful, and the Heart (Qalb) is more fluctuating than the pot in its boiling? And the Turner of Hearts (Muqallib al-Qulub), may He be glorified, said: 'Indeed, the punishment of their Lord is not to be secure from.' So the most ignorant of people is he who feels secure from it while He calls out with warning from security. And if God had been gentle with His servants, the knowers, when He revived their hearts with the spirit of hope, their hearts would have burned from the fire of fear. So the causes of hope are a mercy for the elect...
32:13.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

32:13.arabic: الحالة الثانية أن تغلب دواعي الهوى وتسقط بالكلية منازعة باعث الدين فيسلم نفسه إلى جند الشياطين ولا يجاهد ليأسه من المجاهدة وهؤلاء هم الغافلون وهم الأكثرون وهم الذين استرقتهم شهواتهم وغلبت عليهم شقوتهم فحكموا أعداء الله في قلوبهم التي هي سر من أسرار الله تعالى وأمر من أمور الله وإليهم الإشارة بقوله تعالى: ﴿ ولو شئنا لآتينا كل نفس هداها ولكن حق القول مني لأملأن جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين ﴾ {} وهؤلاء هم الذين اشتروا الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة فخسرت صفقتهم وقيل لمن قصد إرشادهم ﴿ فأعرض عمن تولى عن ذكرنا
32:13.english: The second state is that the incitements of desire (Hawa) overcome and the urging of religion (Din) completely ceases to contend, so he surrenders his soul (Nafs) to the armies of the devils and does not struggle due to his despair from struggling. These are the heedless ones (Ghaafiloon) and they are the majority, and they are those whose lusts have enslaved them and their wretchedness has overcome them, so they have given authority to the enemies of Allah in their hearts (Quloob), which are a secret (Sirr) from the secrets of Allah the Exalted and a matter (Amr) from the affairs of Allah. To them is the indication by His saying, the Exalted: 'And if We had willed, We could have given every soul (Nafs) its guidance, but the word (Qawl) from Me will come true: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind all together."' And these are those who have purchased the worldly life (Al-Hayaat Al-Dunya) with the Hereafter (Al-Aakhirah), so their transaction has incurred loss, and it is said to one who intends to guide them: 'So turn away from he who turns away from Our remembrance (Dhikr) and desires not except the worldly life. That is their extent of knowledge.' And this state's sign is despair (Yaa's) and hopelessness (Qunoot) and delusion with hopes (Amaani), which is the utmost foolishness (Hamaq), as it is said: 'The intelligent one (Al-Kayyis) is he who holds his soul (Nafs) accountable and works for what is after death, and the foolish one (Al-Ahmaq) is he who follows his soul (Nafs) its desire (Hawa) and hopes upon Allah.' And the possessor of this state, when admonished, says: 'I am longing for repentance (Tawbah), but it has become impossible for me, so I do not hope for it,' or he was not longing for repentance (Tawbah) but said: 'Indeed Allah is Forgiving, Merciful, Generous, so He has no need for my repentance.' And this wretched one has become his intellect (Aql) weak for his lust (Shahwah), so he does not use his intellect (Aql) except in deducing subtle tricks by which he attains the fulfillment of his lust (Shahwah). Indeed, his intellect (Aql) has become in the hand of his lusts (Shahawaat) like a Muslim captive in the hands of the disbelievers (Kuffaar), so they enslave him in tending pigs, guarding wines, and carrying them. And his place with Allah the Exalted is the place of one who overpowers a Muslim and delivers him to the disbelievers (Kuffaar) and makes him a captive with them, because by his atrocious crime he resembles one who enslaved what had the right not to be enslaved and gave authority to what had the right not to have authority over it. And indeed, the Muslim deserved to be dominant because of what is in him of knowledge (Ma'rifah) of Allah and the urging of religion (Din), and indeed, the disbeliever (Kaafir) deserved to be...
32:13.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

32:13.arabic: فإن قلت: فلو ترك الوعاظ الوعظ إلا عند نيل هذه الدرجة لخلت الدنيا عن الوعظ خربت القلوب؟ فأقول قد قال رسول الله ﭬ "حب الدنيا رأس كل خطيئة"[36] ولو لم يحب الناس الدنيا لهلك العالم وبطلت المعايش وهلكت القلوب والأبدان جميعاً، إلا أنه ﭬ علم أن حب الدنيا مهلك وأن ذكر كونه مهلكاً لا ينزع الحب من قلوب الأكثرين لا الأقلين الذين لا تخرب الدنيا بتركهم، فلم يترك النصح وذكر ما في حب الدنيا من الخطر ولم يترك ذكره خوفاً من أن يترك نفسه بالشهوات المهلكة التي سلطها الله على عباده ليسوقهم بها إلى جهنم تصديقاً لقول
32:13.english: If you say: If preachers were to abandon preaching except upon attaining this degree, then the world would be devoid of preaching and hearts would be ruined? I say: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, "Love of the world (Dunya) is the head of every sin." And if people did not love the world, the world would perish, livelihoods would cease, and hearts and bodies would all be destroyed. However, he (peace be upon him) knew that love of the world is destructive and that mentioning its destructiveness does not remove the love from the hearts of the majority, not the minority whose abandonment would not ruin the world. So he did not abandon advising and mentioning the danger in love of the world, nor did he abandon mentioning it out of fear that he would leave himself to the destructive desires that Allah has empowered over His servants to drive them with them to Hellfire, in confirmation of His saying, the Most High: "But the word from Me has become true: I will fill Hell with jinn and mankind all together." Likewise, the tongues of preachers remain unleashed for love of leadership, and they do not abandon it due to the saying of one who says: Preaching for love of leadership is forbidden, just as the creation does not abandon drinking, fornication, theft, hypocrisy, oppression, and other sins due to the saying of Allah, the Most High, and His Messenger that it is forbidden. So look to your own self (Nafs) and be empty-hearted (Qalb) from the talk of people, for Allah, the Most High, reforms many creation through the corruption of one person and persons: "And if Allah did not repel some people by others, the earth would be corrupted." And Allah supports this religion with people who have no share (in the Hereafter). What is feared is that the path of taking admonition is corrupted. As for silencing the tongues of preachers while behind them is the motive of leadership and love of the world, that will never be.
32:13.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

32:13.arabic: الأصل الثالث: أن فعل العبد وإن كان كسبا للعبد فلا يخرج عن كونه مرادا لله سبحانه فلا يجري في الملك والملكوت طرفة عين ولا لفتة خاطر ولا فلتة ناظر إلا بقضاء الله وقدرته وبإرادته ومشيئته ومنه الشر والخير والنفع والضر والإسلام والكفر والعرفان والنكر والفوز والخسران والغواية والرشد والطاعة والعصيان والشرك والإيمان لا راد لقضائه ولا معقب لحكمه يضل من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء لا يسئل عما يفعل وهم يسألون ويدل عليه من النقل قول الأمة قاطبة ما شاء كان وما لم يشأ لم يكن وقول الله عز وجل أن لو يشاء الله لهدى الناس
32:13.english: The third foundation: That the action of the servant (al-'abd), even if it is an acquisition (kasb) of the servant, does not depart from being willed by Allah, glorified and exalted be He. Therefore, not a blink of an eye, nor a turn of thought, nor a glance of the eye occurs in the dominion (al-mulk) and the kingdom (al-malakūt) except by the decree (qadā') of Allah and His power (qudrah) and by His will (irādah) and His volition (mashī'ah). And from Him is evil and good, benefit and harm, Islam and disbelief (kufr), recognition (ma'rifah) and denial (inkār), success and loss, misguidance (ghawāyah) and right guidance (rushd), obedience and disobedience, polytheism (shirk) and faith (īmān). There is no repeller of His decree and no reverser of His judgment. He misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills. He is not questioned about what He does, while they will be questioned. And what indicates this from transmitted tradition (al-naql) is the statement of the entire community: 'What He wills is, and what He does not will is not,' and the statement of Allah, mighty and majestic: 'If Allah had willed, He would have guided all the people,' and His statement, exalted: 'And if We had willed, We could have given every soul (nafs) its guidance (hudāhā).' And what indicates this from the perspective of intellect (al-'aql) is that sins (ma'āṣī) and crimes, if Allah dislikes them and does not will them, yet they occur in accordance with the will of the enemy, Iblīs—may Allah curse him—even though he is an enemy to Allah, glorified and exalted be He, and what occurs in accordance with the will of the enemy is more than what occurs in accordance with His will, exalted. I wonder how a Muslim permits himself to reduce the dominion of the Compeller (al-Jabbār), Possessor of Majesty and Honor, to a rank that, if the leadership of a village chief were reduced to it, he would disdain it. For if what continues for the enemy of the chief in the village were more than what is established for him, he would disdain his leadership and absolve himself of his authority. And sin is what predominates over creation, and all of that, according to the innovators (al-mubtadi'ah), occurs contrary to the will of the Truth (al-Ḥaqq), exalted. And this is the utmost weakness and incapacity—exalted is the Lord of lords above what the wrongdoers say, supremely great. Then, whenever it becomes apparent that the actions of the servants are created by Allah, it is sound that they are willed by Him. If it is said: 'How does He forbid what He wills and command what He does not will?' We say: Command (al-amr) is different from will (al-irādah). Therefore, when a master strikes his servant and the ruler reproaches him for it, and he excuses himself by the rebellion of his servant against him, and the ruler disbelieves him, so he wishes to manifest his proof by commanding the servant to do an action and he disobeys him in the presence of the ruler, so he says to him: 'Saddle this mount in the sight of the ruler.' Thus, he commands him with what he does not will his compliance with, and if he were not a commander, his excuse would not be facilitated before the ruler, and if he were...
32:13.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Foundations of Belief'

32:13.arabic: ولم يقطع التوفيق عن الكفار لجناية متقدمة ولا أمد الأنبياء عليهم السلام بتوفيقه ونور هدايته لوسيلة سابقة ولكنه قال ولقد سبقت كلمتنا لعبادنا المرسلين وقال عز وجل ولكن حق القول مني لأملأن جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين وقال تعالى إن الذين سبقت لهم منا الحسنى أولئك عنها مبعدون فإن خطر ببالك أنه لم اختلفت السابقة وهم في ربقه العبودية مشتركون نوديت من سرادقات الجلال لا تجاوز حد الأدب فإنه لا يسئل عما يفعل وهم يسئلون
32:13.english: And He did not cut off success (Tawfiq) from the disbelievers due to a preceding transgression, nor did He extend to the Prophets, peace be upon them, His success (Tawfiq) and the light (Nur) of His guidance (Hidayah) due to a prior means. Rather, He said: 'And Our word has already preceded for Our servants, the messengers.' And the Almighty said: 'But the word (Qawl) from Me has become true: I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men all together.' And the Exalted said: 'Indeed, those for whom the best (Al-Husna) from Us has preceded, they will be removed far from it.' If it occurs to your mind that the precedence (Sabiqah) did not differ while they are partners in the bond (Ribqah) of servitude (Ubudiyyah), you are called from the pavilions (Saradiqu) of majesty (Jalal): 'Do not exceed the limit of etiquette (Adab), for He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned.'
32:13.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

32:15.arabic: وأكمله أن يكبر فيسجد ويدعو في سجوده بما يليق بالآية التي قرأها مثل أن يقرأ قوله تعالى: ﴿ إِنَّمَا يُؤْمِنُ بِآيَاتِنَا الَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِّرُوا بِهَا خَرُّوا سُجَّدًا وَسَبَّحُوا بِحَمْدِ رَبِّهِمْ وَهُمْ لَا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ ﴾ فيقول اللهم اجعلني من الساجدين لوجهك المسبحين بحمدك وأعوذ بك أن أكون من المستكبرين عن أمرك أو على أوليائك
32:15.english: And its most complete form is that he says 'Allahu Akbar' and prostrates and supplicates in his prostration with what is appropriate to the verse he recited, such as when he recites the saying of Allah the Exalted: 'Only those believe in Our signs who, when they are reminded by them, fall down prostrating and glorify with praise of their Lord, and they are not arrogant.' Then he says: O Allah, make me among those who prostrate to Your Face (Wajh), those who glorify with Your praise, and I seek refuge in You from being among those who are arrogant about Your command or against Your allies.
32:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

32:16.arabic: ولهذه الصلاة فضل عظيم وقيل إنها المراد بقوله عز وجل تتجافى جنوبهم عن المضاجع وقد روى عنه ﷺ أنه قال: )من صلى بين المغرب والعشاء فإنها من صلاة الأوابين[241]) وقال ﷺ: (من عكف نفسه فيما بين المغرب والعشاء في مسجد جماعة لم يتكلم إلا بصلاة أو بقرآن كان حقا على الله أن يبني له قصرين في الجنة مسيرة كل قصر منهما مائة عام ويغرس له بينهما غراسا لوطافة أهل الأرض لوسعهم[242]) وسيأتي بقية فضائلها في كتاب الأوراد إن شاء الله تعالى.
32:16.english: And for this prayer there is great virtue, and it is said that it is what is intended by His saying, the Exalted: 'Their sides (جنوبهم) withdraw from the beds (المضاجع), calling upon their Lord in fear (خوفًا) and hope (طمعًا), and from what We have provided them they spend.' And it has been narrated from him (peace be upon him) that he said: 'Whoever prays between Maghrib and Isha, then it is from the prayer of the oft-returning ones (الأوابين).' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever confines his soul (نفسه) between Maghrib and Isha in a congregational mosque, not speaking except with prayer or Quran, it is a right upon Allah to build for him two palaces in Paradise, the journey of each palace being one hundred years, and to plant for him between them plantings that, if the delicacy of the people of the earth were to encompass them, it would suffice them.' And the remainder of its virtues will come in the Book of Regular Devotions (الأوراد), if Allah wills.
32:16.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

32:16.arabic: ولذلك جمع الله تعالى بينهما في وصف من أثنى عليهم فقال تعالى: ﴿تَتَجَافَىٰ جُنُوبُهُمْ عَنِ الْمَضَاجِعِ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ خَوْفًا وَطَمَعًا وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ﴾ وقال عز وجل: ﴿وَيَدْعُونَنَا رَغَبًا وَرَهَبًا﴾ وأين مثل عمر رضي الله عنه فالخلق الموجودة في هذا الزمان كلهم الأصلح لهم غلبة الخوف بشرط أن لا يخرجهم إلى اليأس وترك العمل وقطع الطمع من المغفرة
32:16.english: And therefore Allah the Exalted combined them in describing those He praised, so He said: 'Their sides forsake their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear (Khauf) and hope (Tama'a), and from what We have provided them they spend.' And He the Mighty and Majestic said: 'And they call upon Us in desire (Raghban) and fear (Rahban).' And where is the like of Umar, may Allah be pleased with him? The created beings existing in this time, all of them, the most appropriate for them is the predominance of fear (Khauf) on condition that it does not lead them to despair (Yas) and abandoning work (Amal) and cutting off hope (Tama'a) from forgiveness, for that is despair (Qunut) and is not fear (Khauf).
32:16.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

32:16.arabic: ثم انظر كيف وصف الفائزين من عباده وبماذا وصفهم فقال تعالى: ﴿ أمن هو قانت آناء الليل ساجدا وقائما يحذر الآخرة ويرجو رحمة ربه قل هل يستوي الذين يعلمون والذين لا يعلمون ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ تتجافى جنوبهم عن المضاجع يدعون ربهم خوفا وطمعا ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل: ﴿ والذين يبيتون لربهم سجدا وقياما ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل: ﴿ كانوا قليلا من الليل ما يهجعون وبالأسحار هم يستغفرون ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل: ﴿ فسبحان الله حين تمسون وحين تصبحون ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه ﴾ {}. فهذا كله يب
32:16.english: Then look at how He described the successful ones among His servants and with what He described them, so He the Exalted said: 'Is one who is devoutly obedient (Qānit) during periods of the night, prostrating and standing [in prayer], fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord [like one who does not]? Say, "Are those who know equal to those who do not know?"' And He the Exalted said: 'Their sides (Junūb) forsake (Tatajāfā) [their] beds as they call upon their Lord in fear (Khawf) and hope (Ṭamaʿ), and from what We have provided them, they spend.' And He the Mighty and Majestic said: 'And those who spend [part of] the night to their Lord prostrating and standing [in prayer].' And He the Mighty and Majestic said: 'They used to sleep but little of the night, and in the hours before dawn they would ask forgiveness.' And He the Mighty and Majestic said: 'So exalted is Allah when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning.' And He the Exalted said: 'And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance (Wajh).' All of this clarifies for you that the path to the Exalted is monitoring the times and populating them with regular devotional acts (Awrād) on the basis of continuity, and for that reason he (the Prophet) said: 'The most beloved of Allah's servants to Allah are those who observe the sun, the moon, and the shadows for the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah the Exalted.'
32:16.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

32:16.arabic: [42] حديث سئل عن قوله تعالى تتجافى جنوبهم عن المضاجع فقال الصلاة بين العشاءين ثم قال عليكم بالصلاة بين العشاءين فإنها تذهب بملاغات النهار وتهذب آخره قال المصنف أسنده ابن أبي الزناد [قول العراقى ابن أبى الزناد هى نسخة وقعت له وإلا ففى النسخ الصحيحة ابن أبى الزياد فليتأمل] إلى رسول الله ﭬ قلت إنما هو إسماعيل بن أبي زياد بالياء المثناة من تحت رواه أبو منصور الديلمي في مسند الفردوس من رواية إسماعيل بن أبي زياد الشامي عن الأعمش حدثنا أبو العلاء العنبري عن سلمان قال قال رسول الله ﭬ عليكم بالالصلاة بين
32:16.english: [42] A hadith: He was asked about His saying, the Most High: 'Their sides (جنوبهم) withdraw from the beds (المضاجع), they call upon their Lord in fear (خوفًا) and hope (طمعًا), and from what We have provided them they spend.' He said: The prayer between the two evening prayers (العشاءين). Then he said: Upon you is the prayer between the two evening prayers, for indeed it removes the frivolities of the day and refines its end. The author said: Ibn Abi Zinad attributed it [the commentator says: Ibn Abi Zinad is a copy that came to him, otherwise in the correct copies it is Ibn Abi Ziyad, so let it be considered] to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him. I say: Rather it is Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad with the dotted Ya. Abu Mansur al-Daylami narrated it in Musnad al-Firdaws from the narration of Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad al-Shami from al-A'mash: Abu al-'Ala al-'Anbari narrated to us from Salman, he said: The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: 'Upon you is the prayer between the two evening prayers, for indeed it removes the frivolities of the beginning of the day and refines its end.' And this Isma'il is abandoned, he fabricates hadith, al-Daraqutni said it. And the name of Abi Ziyad is Muslim. And there is disagreement about it from al-A'mash. And for Ibn Mardawayh from the hadith of Anas that it was revealed concerning the prayer between Maghrib and 'Isha'. And the hadith is with al-Tirmidhi and he graded it as good with the wording: 'It was revealed concerning waiting for the prayer which is called al-'Atmah (the late evening prayer).'
32:16.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Book of Knowledge'

32:16.arabic: ولذلك قال تعالى: ﴿ ويدعوننا رغبا ورهبا ﴾ {} وقال عز وجلّ: ﴿ يدعون ربهم خوفا وطمعا ﴾ {} ولذلك عبر العرب عن الخوف بالرجاء فقال تعالى: ﴿ ما لكم لا ترجون لله وقارا ﴾ {} أي لا تخافون وكثيرا ما ورد في القرآن الرجاء بمعنى الخوف وذلك لتلازمهما إذ عادة العرب التعبير عن الشيء بما يلازمه
32:16.english: And therefore Allah the Exalted said: 'And they call upon Us in hope and fear' (Quran 21:90) and the Almighty said: 'Their sides forsake their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and hope (طمعا)' (Quran 32:16). And therefore the Arabs expressed fear (الخوف) through hope (الرجاء) as Allah said: 'Why do you not hope (ترجون) for Allah with reverence?' (Quran 71:13) meaning 'Why do you not fear?' And often in the Quran hope (الرجاء) comes with the meaning of fear (الخوف), and that is due to their inseparability, for it is the custom of the Arabs to express a thing through what accompanies it.
32:16.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

32:17.arabic: وقيل في قوله تعالى: ﴿ فلا تعلم نفس ما أخفي لهم من قرة أعين جزاء بما كانوا يعملون ﴾ قيل كان عملهم الصيام لأنه قال: ﴿ إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب ﴾ فيفرغ للصائم جزاؤه إفراغا ويجازف جزافا فلا يدخل تحت وهم وتقدير وجدير بأن يكون كذلك لأن الصوم إنما كان له ومشرفا بالنسبة إليه وإن كانت العبادات كلها له كما شرف البيت بالنسبة إلى نفسه والأرض كلها له لمعنيين: أحدهما أن الصوم كف وترك وهو في نفسه سر ليس فيه عمل يشاهد وجميع أعمال الطاعات بمشهد من الخلق ومرأى والصوم لا يراه إلا الله عز وجل فإنه عمل في
32:17.english: And it is said regarding His statement, the Exalted: 'So no soul (Nafs) knows what has been hidden for them of delight of the eyes as reward for what they used to do' (Quran 32:17), it is said their action was fasting because He said: 'Indeed, the patient ones will be given their reward without account' (Quran 39:10). So the reward for the fasting person is poured out completely and given generously, not entering under imagination and estimation, and it is worthy to be so because fasting is specifically for Him and honored in relation to Him, even though all acts of worship are for Him, just as the House is honored in relation to Himself and all the earth is His, for two meanings: The first is that fasting is restraint (Kaf) and abandonment (Tark), and it is in itself a secret (Sirr) with no visible action, and all acts of obedience are witnessed and seen by creation, but fasting is not seen except by Allah, the Exalted, for it is an action in the inner (Batin) with pure patience (Sabr). The second is that it subdues the enemy of Allah, the Exalted, for the means of Satan, may Allah curse him, are the desires (Shahawat), and desires are strengthened by eating and drinking, and therefore the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: 'Indeed, Satan flows in the son of Adam like blood, so constrict his pathways with hunger.' And therefore the Prophet, peace be upon him, said to Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her: 'Persist in knocking on the door of Paradise.' She said: 'With what?' He said, peace be upon him: 'With hunger.' And the virtue of hunger will come in the book on the evil of food and its treatment from the quarter of the destroyers. Since fasting in particular is suppression of Satan, blocking of his paths, and constriction of his pathways, it deserves specification in relation to Allah, the Exalted, for in suppressing the enemy of Allah is victory for Allah, glory be to Him, and the supporter of Allah, the Exalted, is dependent on victory for Him, said Allah, the Exalted.
32:17.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Fasting'

32:17.arabic: ولعلها أرادت بحب الهوى: حب الله لإحسانه إليها وإنعامه عليها بحظوظ العاجلة، وبحبه لما هو أهل له: الحب لجماله وجلاله الذي انكشف لها؛ وهو أعلى الجبين وأقواهما، ولذة مطالعة جمال الربوبية هي التي عبر عنها رسول الله ﭬ حيث قال حاكياً عن ربه تعالى: "أعددت لعبادي الصالحين ما لا عين رأت ولا أذن سمعت ولا خطر على قلب بشر" وقد تعجل بعض هذه اللذات في الدنيا لمن انتهى صفاء قلبه إلى الغاية، ولذلك قال بعضهم: إني أقول يا رب يا الله فأجد ذلك على قلبي أثقل من الجبال لأن النداء يكون من وراء حجاب؛ وهل رأيت جليساً ينا
32:17.english: And perhaps she intended by love of desire (Hawa): the love of Allah for His benevolence to her and His bestowal upon her with the shares of the immediate, and by His love for that which He is worthy of: the love for His beauty and majesty which was unveiled to her; and it is the highest and strongest of the two, and the delight of contemplating the beauty of Lordship (Rububiyyah) is that which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ expressed when he said, narrating from his Lord, the Exalted: "I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has not occurred to the heart of a human." And some of these delights are hastened in this world for one whose purity of heart (Qalb) has reached the ultimate, and for that reason some of them said: I say, O Lord, O Allah, and I find that upon my heart heavier than the mountains because the call is from behind a veil; and have you seen a companion calling his companion? And he said: When a man reaches the ultimate in this knowledge, the creation pelts him with stones; meaning his speech goes beyond the limit of their intellects so they see what he says as madness or disbelief, so the aim of all the knowers (Arifin) is only His connection and meeting, so it is the coolness of the eye (Qurrat al-Ayn) which no soul (Nafs) knows what has been hidden for them of it, and when it is attained, all worries and desires are obliterated and the heart becomes immersed in its bliss, so if he were thrown into the Fire, he would not feel it due to his immersion, and if the bliss of Paradise were presented to him, he would not turn to it due to the perfection of his bliss and his reaching the ultimate which has nothing above it, and I wish I knew how one who only understands the love of tangible things believes in the delight of looking at the Face of Allah, the Exalted, when He has no image nor form? And what meaning is there to Allah's promise of it to His servants and His mention that it is the greatest of blessings? Rather, whoever knows Allah knows that the delights scattered by different desires all fold under this delight as some of them said:
32:17.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

32:17.arabic: وقد شرح الله الرجاء فقال "إن الذين آمنوا والذين هاجروا وجاهدوا في سبيل الله أولئك يرجون رحمة الله" يعني أن الرجاء بهم أليق وهذا لأنه ذكر أن ثواب الآخرة أجر وجزاء على الأعمال قال الله تعالى "جزاء بما كانوا يعملون" وقال تعالى "وإنما توفون أجوركم يوم القيامة" أفترى أن من استؤجر على إصلاح أوان وشرط له أجرة عليها وكان الشارط كريماً يفي بالوعد مهما وعد ولا يخلف بل يزيد، فجاء الأجير وكسر الأواني وأفسد جميعها ثم جلس ينتظر الأجر ويزعم أن المستأجر كريم، أفيراه العقلاء في انتظاره متمنياً مغروراً أو راجياً؟
32:17.english: And Allah has explained hope (al-raja') by saying: 'Indeed, those who have believed and those who have emigrated and striven in the path of Allah - those expect the mercy of Allah.' This means that hope (al-raja') is more appropriate for them, and this is because He mentioned that the reward of the Hereafter is a wage and recompense for deeds. Allah the Exalted said: 'As recompense for what they used to do.' And He the Exalted said: 'And you will only be given your rewards on the Day of Resurrection.' Do you think that if someone is hired to repair vessels and is promised a wage for it, and the promiser is generous, fulfilling whatever he promises without failing but rather increasing, then the hired worker comes and breaks the vessels and ruins all of them, then sits waiting for the wage and claims that the hirer is generous - would the people of intellect see him in his waiting as a wishful person (mutamannin) deluded (maghrur) or as a hopeful person (raji)?
32:17.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

32:17.arabic: وَكَمَا أَنَّ لَذَّةَ الرِّيَاسَةِ وَالْكَرَامَةِ أَغْلَبُ اللَّذَّاتِ عَلَى مَنْ جَاوَزَ نَقْصَانَ الصِّبَا وَالْعَتْهِ فَلَذَّةُ مَعْرِفَةِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى وَمُطَالَعَةِ جَمَالِ حَضْرَةِ الرُّبُوبِيَّةِ وَالنَّظَرِ إِلَى أَسْرَارِ الْأُمُورِ الْإِلَهِيَّةِ أَلَذُّ مِنَ الرِّيَاسَةِ الَّتِي هِيَ أَعْلَى اللَّذَّاتِ الْغَالِبَةِ عَلَى الْخَلْقِ، وَغَايَةُ الْعِبَارَةِ عَنْهُ أَنْ يُقَالَ "فَلَا تَعْلَمُ نَفْسٌ مَا أُخْفِيَ لَهُمْ مِنْ قُرَّةِ أَعْيُنٍ" وَأَنَّهُ أَعَدَّ لَهُمْ مَا لَا عَيْنٌ رَ
32:17.english: And just as the pleasure (Ladhdha) of leadership (Riyasah) and honor (Karāmah) is the most dominant of pleasures for one who has surpassed the deficiency of childhood (Sibā) and foolishness (Atah), so the pleasure (Ladhdha) of the knowledge (Ma'rifah) of Allah, the Exalted, and the contemplation (Mutāla'ah) of the beauty (Jamāl) of the presence (Hadhrah) of Lordship (Rubūbiyyah) and the observation (Nadhar) of the secrets (Asrār) of divine (Ilāhiyyah) matters is more pleasurable than leadership (Riyasah), which is the highest of the pleasures that dominate over creation (Khalq). The ultimate expression about it is to say: 'So no soul (Nafs) knows what has been hidden for them of the coolness (Qurrah) of eyes (A'yun) as a reward (Jazā') for what they used to do.' And that He has prepared for them what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has not occurred to the heart (Qalb) of any human (Bashar). This now is not known except by one who has tasted both pleasures, for he inevitably prefers seclusion (Tabattul) and solitude (Tafarruḍ) and reflection (Fikr) and remembrance (Dhikr) and immerses himself in the seas of knowledge (Ma'rifah) and abandons leadership (Riyasah) and considers contemptible the creation (Khalq) whom he leads, due to his knowledge ('Ilm) of the annihilation (Fanā') of his leadership and the annihilation of those over whom his leadership is, and its being mixed with the turbidities (Kadūrāt) from which freedom (Khulū) is inconceivable, and its being cut off by death (Mawt) which must inevitably come, no matter how the earth takes its adornment and becomes beautified and its people think they are capable of it. So he considers great, in comparison to it, the pleasure (Ladhdha) of the knowledge (Ma'rifah) of Allah and the contemplation (Mutāla'ah) of His attributes (Sifāt) and actions (Af'āl) and the order (Nidhām) of His kingdom (Mamlakah) from the highest 'Illiyyīn to the lowest of the low (Asfal al-Sāfilīn), for it is free from competitors (Mazāhimāt) and disturbances (Makdirāt), spacious for those who come to it, not constricted for them by its greatness. Its width ('Arḍ) in terms of estimation (Taqdīr) is the heavens and the earth, and when observation (Nadhar) goes beyond the estimated things (Muqaddarāt), there is no end to its width. So the knower ('Ārif) by contemplating it is in a garden (Jannah) whose width is the heavens and the earth, grazing in its meadows (Riyāḍ), plucking from its fruits (Thimār), and drinking from its pools (Hiyāḍ), secure from its cessation, for the fruits of this garden are not cut off nor forbidden.
