And if there were a sin in which intercession is accepted, He would not have commanded the Quraysh with obedience, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) would not have prohibited Fatimah (may Allah be pleased with her) from disobedience, and He would have permitted her to follow desires to complete her self (Nafs) in this world, then intercede for her in the Hereafter to complete her self (Nafs) in the Hereafter. So immersion in sins and abandoning piety (Taqwa) relying on the hope of intercession resembles the immersion of the sick person in his desires depending on a skilled doctor who is close and compassionate like a father or brother or other, and that is ignorance because the effort of the doctor, his diligence, and his skill benefit in removing some illnesses, not all of them. So it is not permissible to abandon precaution absolutely relying on mere medicine, rather the doctor has an effect in general but in mild illnesses and when the balance of temperament (Mizaj) predominates. Thus, you should understand the care of intercessors from the prophets and the righteous for relatives and strangers, for it is certainly like that, and that does not remove fear and caution, and how can it remove when the best of creation after the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) are his companions, and they used to wish they were beasts out of fear of the Hereafter with the perfection of their piety (Taqwa), the goodness of their deeds, the purity of their hearts (Qulub), and what they heard from the promise of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) to them of Paradise.
34:23.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

34:29.arabic: واختلاف تركيب أعضائه أعاجيب تزيد على الأعاجيب فى بعثه وإعادته فكيف ينكر ذلك من قدرة الله تعالى وحكمته من يشاهد ذلك فى صنعته وقدرته فإن كان فى إيمانك ضعف فقو الإيمان بالنظر فى النشأة الأولى فإن الثانية مثلها وأسهل منها وإن كنت قوى الإيمان بها فأشعر قلبك تلك المخاوف والأخطار وأكثر فيها التفكر والاعتبار لتسلب عن قلبك الراحة والقرار فتشتغل بالتشمر للعرض على الجبار وتفكر أولا فيما يقرع سمع سكان القبور من شدة نفخ الصور فإنها صيحة واحدة تنفرج بها القبور عن رءوس الموتي فيثورون دفعة واحدة فتوهم نفسك وقد
34:29.english: And the differing composition of its limbs are wonders that increase upon wonders in its resurrection and restoration, so how can one deny that from the power (Qudrah) of Allah the Exalted and His wisdom who witnesses that in His creation and power? If there is weakness in your faith (Iman), then strengthen the faith (Iman) by looking at the first creation, for the second is like it and easier than it. And if you are strong in faith (Iman) in it, then make your heart (Qalb) feel those fears and dangers, and increase in it contemplation (Tafakkur) and consideration (I'tibar) to strip from your heart (Qalb) comfort and settlement, so you busy yourself with preparing for the presentation before the Almighty (Al-Jabbar). And contemplate first in what strikes the hearing of the inhabitants of the graves from the intensity of the blowing of the Trumpet (As-Sur), for it is a single shout by which the graves split open from the heads of the dead, and they rise up all at once. So imagine yourself having leapt up, your face changed, your body dusty from your scalp to your feet from the dust of your grave, stunned from the intensity of the blow, your eye fixed toward the call. And the creation has risen up in one uprising from the graves in which their tribulation (Bala') has been prolonged, and alarm and terror have agitated them, added to what they had of sorrows and griefs and intense waiting for the outcome of the matter, as the Exalted said: 'And the Trumpet (As-Sur) will be blown, and all who are in the heavens and all who are on the earth will fall dead except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on.' And the Exalted said: 'And when the Horn (An-Naqur) is blown, that Day will be a difficult day for the disbelievers; not easy.' And the Exalted said: 'And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?" They do not await except one blast which will seize them while they are disputing. And they will not be able to make a testament, nor to their people will they return. And the Horn (As-Sur) will be blown; and at once from the graves to their Lord they will hasten. They will say, "O woe to us! Who has raised us from our sleeping place? This is what the Most Merciful had promised, and the messengers told the truth."' So if there were not before the dead except the terror of that blowing, it would be worthy of being guarded against, for it is a blowing and a shout by which those in the heavens and the earth are struck dead, meaning they die by it except whom Allah wills, and that is some of the angels. And for that reason, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'How can I be at ease when the possessor of the Trumpet (As-Sur) has taken the horn (Al-Qarn) in his mouth, lowered his forehead, and inclined his ear, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow?' Maqatil said: The Trumpet (As-Sur) is the horn (Al-Qarn), and that is because Israfil (upon him be peace) has placed his mouth on the horn (Al-Qarn) like the form of a trumpet, and the circle of the head of the horn (Al-Qarn) is like the expanse of the heavens and the earth, and he is fixing his gaze toward the Throne (Al-'Arsh), waiting for when he will be commanded to blow the first blowing. And when he blows, those in the heavens and the earth are struck dead, meaning every animal dies from the intensity of the alarm except whom Allah wills, and that is Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil, and the Angel of Death (Malak al-Mawt). Then the Angel of Death (Malak al-Mawt) is commanded to take the soul (Ruh) of Jibril, then the soul (Ruh) of Mika'il, then the soul (Ruh) of Israfil, then the Angel of Death (Malak al-Mawt) is commanded and he dies. Then the creation remains after the first blowing in the Barzakh for forty years, then Allah the Exalted revives Israfil and commands.
34:29.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

34:31.arabic: وشر أنواع الكبر ما يمنع من استفادة العلم وقبول الحق والانقياد له وفيه وردت الآيات التي فيها ذم الكبر والمتكبرين قال الله تعالى "والملائكة باسطو أيديهم" إلى قوله "وكنتم عن آياته تستكبرون" ثم قال "ادخلوا أبواب جهنم خالدين فيها فبئس مثوى المتكبرين" ثم أخبر أن أشد أهل النار عذاباً أشدهم عتياً على الله تعالى فقال "ثم لننزعن من كل شبعة أيهم أشد على الرحمن عتياً" وقال تعالى "فالذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة قلوبهم منكرة وهم مستكبرون" وقال عز وجل "يقول الذين استضعفوا للذين استكبروا لولا أنتم لكنا مؤمنين" وقال ت
34:31.english: And the worst type of arrogance (Kibr) is what prevents from benefiting from knowledge and accepting the truth (Haqq) and submitting to it, and in it have come the verses which contain censure of arrogance (Kibr) and the arrogant ones. Allah the Exalted said: "And the angels are stretching forth their hands" to His saying "and you were arrogant (Tastakbirun) about His signs." Then He said: "Enter the gates of Hell, abiding eternally therein, and wretched is the residence of the arrogant (Mutakabirin)." Then He informed that the most severely punished people of the Fire are the most insolent (Atiyyan) against Allah the Exalted, so He said: "Then We will surely extract from every faction those of them who were most insolent (Atiyyan) against the Most Merciful." And He the Exalted said: "So those who do not believe in the Hereafter - their hearts are denying and they are arrogant (Mustakbirun)." And He the Mighty and Majestic said: "Those who were oppressed (Mustad'afun) say to those who were arrogant (Mustakbirun), 'If not for you, we would have been believers.'" And He the Exalted said: "Indeed, those who are arrogant (Yastakbirun) about My worship will enter Hell in humiliation." And He the Exalted said: "I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant (Yatakabbarun) in the earth without right." It is said in the interpretation (Tafsir): I will lift the understanding of the Quran from their hearts (Qulub), and in some interpretations (Tafasir) I will veil their hearts (Qulub) from the dominion (Malakut). And Ibn Juraij said: I will turn them away from reflecting upon them and taking admonition from them.
34:31.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

34:35.arabic: السادس العجب بكثرة العدد من الأولاد والخدم والغلمان والعشيرة والأقارب والأنصار والأتباع كما قال الكفار "نحن أكثر أموالاً وأولاداً" وكما قال المؤمنون يوم حنين: لا نغلب اليوم من قلة، وعلاجه ما ذكرناه في الكبر وهو أن يتفكر في ضعفه وضعفهم وأن كلهم عبيد عجزة لا يملكون لأنفسهم ضراً ولا نفعاً. "كم من فئة قليلة غلبت فئة كثيرة بإذن الله" ثم كيف يعجب بهم وأنهم سيفترقون عنه إذا مات فيدفن في قبره ذليلاً معيناً وحده لا يرافقه أهل ولا ولد ولا قريب ولا حميم ولا عشير، فيسلمونه إلى البلى والحيات والعقارب والديدا
34:35.english: The sixth: Pride (Al-'Ujb) in the multitude of numbers from children and servants and young attendants and tribe and relatives and supporters and followers, as the disbelievers said: 'We are more in wealth and children' (Quran 34:35), and as the believers said on the day of Hunayn: 'We shall not be defeated today from fewness.' And its cure is what we mentioned regarding arrogance (Al-Kibr), which is that he should reflect upon his weakness and their weakness and that all of them are weak slaves ('Ibad 'Ujaza) who do not possess for themselves harm nor benefit. 'How many a small company has overcome a large company by permission of Allah' (Quran 2:249). Then how can he be proud of them when they will separate from him when he dies, so he is buried in his grave humbled, forsaken, alone—no household member accompanies him, nor child, nor relative, nor intimate friend, nor tribesman—so they deliver him to decay and snakes and scorpions and worms, and they avail him nothing at the time he is most in need of them. And likewise they flee from him on the Day of Resurrection (Yawm al-Qiyamah): 'The Day a man will flee from his brother and his mother and his father and his companion and his sons' (Quran 80:34-36), the verse. So what good is there in one who parts from you in your most severe states and flees from you? And how can you be proud of him when he does not benefit you in the grave and the Resurrection and on the Bridge (Al-Sirat) to your deeds and the favor of Allah the Exalted? So how do you rely on one who does not benefit you, and forget the favors of the One who possesses your benefit and your harm and your death and your life?
34:35.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

34:54.arabic: وأعظم العذاب أن يمنع الإنسان عن مراده كما قال الله تعالى: ﴿ وَحِيلَ بَيْنَهُمْ وَبَيْنَ مَا يَشْتَهُونَ ﴾ فكان هذا أجمع عبارة لعقوبات أهل جهنم
34:54.english: And the greatest punishment is that a human is prevented from what he desires, as Allah the Exalted said: 'And a barrier is placed between them and what they desire.' So this is the most comprehensive expression for the punishments of the people of Hellfire.
34:54.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

35:1.arabic: وأما نتفها في أول النبات تشبها بالمرد فمن المنكرات الكبار فإن اللحية زينة الرجال فإن لله سبحانه ملائكة يقسمون والذي زين بني آدم باللحى وهو من تمام الخلق وبها يتميز الرجال عن النساء. وقيل في غريب التأويل اللحية هي المراد بقوله تعالى: ﴿ يزيد في الخلق ما يشاء ﴾ {} قال أصحاب الأحنف بن قيس: وددنا أن نشتري للأحنف لحية ولو بعشرين ألفا. وقال شريح القاضي: وددت أن لي لحية ولو بعشرة آلاف وكيف تكره اللحية وفيها تعظيم الرجل والنظر إليه بعين العلم والوقار والرفع في المجالس وإقبال الوجوه إليه والتقديم على الجم
35:1.english: And as for plucking it at the beginning of growth in imitation of beardless youths, it is among the major reprehensible acts, for the beard is the adornment of men. Indeed, Allah the Exalted has angels who distribute, and He who adorned the children of Adam with beards, and it is from the completion of creation, and through it men are distinguished from women. And it is said in an unusual interpretation: the beard is what is intended by His saying, the Exalted: 'He increases in creation what He wills' {Quran 35:1}. The companions of Al-Ahnaf ibn Qais said: 'We wish we could buy a beard for Al-Ahnaf even for twenty thousand.' And Shuraih the judge said: 'I wish I had a beard even for ten thousand.' And how can the beard be disliked when in it is the magnification of the man and looking at him with the eye of knowledge and dignity, elevation in gatherings, the turning of faces toward him, precedence over the group, and protection of honor? For whoever insults makes reference to the beard if the insulted one has a beard. And it has been said that the people of Paradise are beardless except for Harun, the brother of Musa, peace be upon them both, for he has a beard to his navel, a specification and preference for him.
35:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Mysteries of Purity'

35:1.arabic: أما النص فيدل على إباحة سماع الصوت الحسن امتنان الله تعالى على عباده إذ قال يزيد في الخلق ما يشاء فقيل هو الصوت الحسن وفي الحديث ما بعث الله نبيا إلا حسن الصوت حديث ما بعث الله نبيا إلا حسن الصوت أخرجه الترمذي في الشمائل عن قتادة وزاد قوله وكان نبيكم حسن الوجه حسن الصوت ورويناه متصلا في الغيلانيات من رواية قتادة عن أنس والصواب الأول قاله الدارقطني ورواه ابن مردويه في التفسير من حديث علي بن أبي طالب وطرقه كلها ضعيفة
35:1.english: As for the textual evidence, it indicates the permissibility of listening to beautiful sound as a favor from Allah the Exalted upon His servants when He said: 'He increases in creation what He wills' and it was said it refers to beautiful sound. And in the hadith: 'Allah did not send any prophet except with a beautiful voice' - the hadith 'Allah did not send any prophet except with a beautiful voice' was reported by al-Tirmidhi in al-Shama'il from Qatadah, and he added his statement: 'And your prophet was beautiful of face and beautiful of voice.' And we reported it connected in al-Ghaylaniyat from the narration of Qatadah from Anas, and the correct is the first, said al-Daraqutni. And Ibn Mardawayh reported it in the Tafsir from the hadith of Ali ibn Abi Talib, and all its chains are weak.
35:1.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

35:2.arabic: فكذلك لا يعرف العاقل ما افتتح الله على أوليائه وأنبيائه من مزايا لطفه ورحمته ما يفتح الله للناس من رحمة فلا ممسك لها وهذه الرحمة مبذولة بحكم الجود والكرم من الله سبحانه وتعالى غير مضنون بها على أحد ولكن إنما تظهر في القلوب المتعرضه لنفحات رحمة الله تعالى كما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن لربكم في أيام دهركم لنفحات ألا فتعرضوا لها والتعرض لها بتطهير القلب وتزكيته من الخبث والكدورة الحاصلة من الأخلاق المذمومة كما سيأتي بيانه
35:2.english: Thus, the rational person does not know what Allah has opened for His saints (awliya') and prophets from the subtleties of His gentleness (lutf) and mercy (rahma). 'What Allah opens for people of mercy, there is no withholder for it' (Quran 35:2). And this mercy is bestowed by the decree of generosity (jawd) and magnanimity (karam) from Allah, the Exalted and Glorified, not being stingily withheld from anyone. However, it only appears in the hearts (qulub) that expose themselves to the breezes (nafahat) of Allah's mercy, as the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, your Lord has in the days of your time breezes, so expose yourselves to them.' And exposing oneself to them is by purifying the heart (qalb) and cleansing it from the filth (khabath) and turbidity (kadurah) resulting from blameworthy character traits, as its explanation will come later.
35:2.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

35:5.arabic: ويحك يا نفس لا ينبغى أن تغرك الحياة الدنيا ولا يغرنك بالله الغرور فانظرى لنفسك فما أمرك بمهم لغيرك ولا تضيعى أوقاتك فالأنفاس معدودة فإذا مضى منك نفس فقد ذهب بعضك فاغتنمى الصحة قبل السقم والفراغ قبل الشغل والغنى قبل الفقر والشباب قبل الهرم والحياة قبل الموت واستعدي للآخرة على قدر بقائك فيها يا نفس أما تستعدين للشتاء بقدر طول مدته فتجمعين له القوت والكسوة والحطب وجميع الأسباب ولا تتكلين في ذلك على فضل الله وكرمه حتى يدفع عنك البرد من غير جبة ولبد وحطب وغير ذلك فإنه قادر على ذلك أفتظنين أيتها النفس
35:5.english: Woe to you, O Soul (Nafs)! It is not fitting that the worldly life (al-hayat al-dunya) should deceive you, nor should the deceiver (al-gharur) deceive you concerning Allah. So look to your soul (nafs), for you are not commanded with what is important for others, and do not waste your times, for the breaths are counted. When a breath passes from you, part of you has gone. So seize health before sickness, leisure before occupation, wealth before poverty, youth before old age, and life before death, and prepare for the Hereafter (al-akhira) according to the length of your stay in it, O soul (nafs). Do you not prepare for winter according to the length of its duration, gathering for it provisions, clothing, firewood, and all means, and do not rely in that on the bounty (fadl) of Allah and His generosity (karam) until He repels the cold from you without a cloak, felt, firewood, and other than that, for He is capable of that. Do you think, O soul (nafs), that the intense cold (zamharir) of Hell (Jahannam) is lighter in cold and shorter in duration than the intense cold of winter? Or do you think that that is less than this? No, it is not so, nor is there any similarity between them in severity and coldness. Do you think that the servant (al-'abd) is saved from it without striving? Far from it! Just as the cold of winter is not repelled except by a cloak, fire, and other means, so the heat of the Fire (al-nar) and its cold are not repelled except by the fortress of Oneness (Tawhid) and the trench of acts of obedience (al-ta'at). And the generosity (karam) of Allah, the Exalted, is in that He made known to you the way of fortification and facilitated its means for you, not in that He repels the punishment from you without its fortress, just as the generosity (karam) of Allah, the Exalted, in repelling the cold of winter is that He created fire and guided you to the way of extracting it from between iron and stone so that you may repel with it the cold of winter from your soul (nafs).
35:5.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

35:5.arabic: اعلم أن قوله تعالى "فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا ولا يغرنكم بالله الغرور" وقوله تعالى "ولكنكم فتنتم أنفسكم وتربضتم وارتبتم وغرتكم الأماني" الآية. كاف في ذم الغرور، وقد قال رسول الله ﭬ "حبذا نوم الأكياس وفطرهم كيف يغبنون سهر الحمقى واجتهادهم ولمثقال ذرة من صاحب تقوى ويقين أفضل من ملئ الأرض من المغترين"[1] وقال ﭬ "الكيس من دان نفسه وعمل لما بعد الموت، والأحمق من اتبع نفسه هواها وتمنى على الله"[2] وكل ما ورد في فضل العلم وذم الجهل فهو دليل على ذم الغرور، لأن الغرور عبارة عن بعض أنواع الجهل، إذ الجهل هو
35:5.english: Know that His saying, the Exalted, "So let not the worldly life (al-hayat al-dunya) deceive you, nor let the deceiver (al-gharur) deceive you concerning Allah" and His saying, the Exalted, "But you tempted yourselves and hesitated and doubted, and false hopes (al-amani) deceived you" the verse. This is sufficient in censuring deception (al-ghurur), and the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said: "How excellent is the sleep of the intelligent and their breaking of fast, how they surpass the staying awake of the foolish and their striving, and a speck's weight of one with piety (taqwa) and certainty (yaqin) is better than the earth filled with the deceived." And he, peace be upon him, said: "The intelligent is he who holds his soul (nafs) accountable and works for what is after death, and the foolish is he who follows his soul (nafs) its desire (hawa) and hopes upon Allah." And all that has come regarding the virtue of knowledge and the censure of ignorance is evidence for censuring deception (al-ghurur), because deception (al-ghurur) is an expression for some types of ignorance, for ignorance is to believe a thing and see it contrary to what it is, and deception (al-ghurur) is ignorance except that there is ignorance that is not deception (ghurur), but it necessitates deception (al-ghurur): a deceived one in it specified and a deceived one by it which is that which deceives him. So whenever the striving one believes something that agrees with desire (al-hawa) and the cause necessitating ignorance is a false doubt and imagination he thinks is evidence but is not evidence, the ignorance occurring by it is called deception (ghurur). So deception (al-ghurur) is the settling of the soul (al-nafs) to what agrees with desire (al-hawa), and the inclination of the nature (al-tab') to it from a doubt and trick of Satan, so whoever believes he is upon good either in the immediate or in the ultimate from a false doubt is deceived, and most people think of themselves good and they are mistaken in it, so most people then are deceived and if
35:5.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

35:5.arabic: المثال الأول غرور الكفار، فمنهم من غرته الحياة الدنيا ومنهم من غره بالله الغرور، أما الذين غرتهم الحياة الدنيا: فهم الذين قالوا: النقد خير من النسيئة والدنيا نقد والآخرة نيسئة فهي إذن خير فلا بد من إيثارها، وقالوا: اليقين خير من الشك ولذات الدنيا يقين ولذات الآخرة شك فلا تترك اليقين بالشك. وهذه أقيسة فاسدة تشبه قياس إبليس حيث قال "أنا خير منه خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين" وإلى هؤلاء الإشارة بقوله تعالى "أولئك الذين اشتروا الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة فلا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينصرون" وعلاج هذا الغرور
35:5.english: The first example is the delusion (Ghurur) of the disbelievers (Kuffar), among them are those whom worldly life (Al-Hayat Al-Dunya) deluded, and among them are those whom the deluder (Al-Gharur) deluded concerning Allah. As for those whom worldly life deluded: they are those who said: 'Cash (Naqd) is better than credit (Nasi'ah), and the worldly life is cash and the Hereafter (Al-Akhirah) is credit, so it is therefore better and must be preferred.' And they said: 'Certainty (Yaqin) is better than doubt (Shakk), and the pleasures of worldly life are certain while the pleasures of the Hereafter are doubtful, so do not abandon certainty for doubt.' These are corrupt analogies resembling the analogy of Iblis when he said 'I am better than him; You created me from fire and created him from clay.' And to these is the reference in His saying, the Exalted: 'Those are the ones who have purchased the worldly life [in exchange] for the Hereafter, so the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be aided.' And the cure for this delusion is either through affirmation of faith (Iman) or through proof (Burhan). As for affirmation through mere faith, it is to believe Allah, the Exalted, in His saying: 'Whatever you have will end, but what Allah has is lasting' and in His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And what is with Allah is better' and His saying: 'And the Hereafter is better and more enduring' and His saying: 'And worldly life is not but the enjoyment of delusion' and His saying: 'So do not let the worldly life delude you.' And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ informed groups of disbelievers of this, so they followed him, believed him, and had faith in him without demanding proof. And among them were those who said: 'I adjure you by Allah, did Allah send you as a messenger?' He would say 'Yes,' so they would believe. And this is the faith of the common people, and it removes from delusion, and this is likened to the child believing his father that attending the school is better than attending the playground, even though he does not know the reason for its being better.
35:5.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

35:5.arabic: وخطب علي كرم الله وجهه يوماً خطبة فقال فيها: اعلموا أنكم ميتون ومبعوثون من بعد الموت وموقوفون على أعمالكم ومجزيون بها، فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا فإنها بالبلاء محفوفة وبالفناء معروفة وبالغدر موصوفة، وكل ما فيها إلى زوال وهي بين أهلها دول وسجال، لا تدوم أحوالها ولا يسلم من شرها نزالها، بينا أهلها منها في رخاء وسرور إذا هم منها في بلاء وغرور. أحوال مختلفة وتارات منصرفة، العيش فها مذموم والرخاء فيها لا يدوم وإنما أهلها فيها أغراض مستهدفة. ترميهم بسهامها وتقصيهم بحمامها. وكل حتفه فيها مقدور وحظه فيها
35:5.english: And Ali, may Allah honor his face, delivered a sermon one day in which he said: Know that you will die and be resurrected after death, and you will be held accountable for your deeds and rewarded for them. So do not let the worldly life deceive you, for it is surrounded by tribulation, known for annihilation, and described with betrayal. Everything in it is destined to vanish, and it circulates among its people like a bucket in a well. Its conditions do not last, and its inhabitants are not safe from its harm. While its people are in ease and joy from it, suddenly they are in tribulation and deception. Conditions vary and times pass. Life in it is blameworthy, and ease in it does not endure; rather, its people in it are targeted aims. It shoots them with its arrows and cuts them off with its death. Every person's death in it is predetermined, and his share in it is fulfilled. And know, O servants of Allah, that you and what you are in of this world are on the path of those who have passed before you, who had longer lifespans than you, were stronger in power than you, built more dwellings, and left more traces. Then their voices became silent and still after long turning, their bodies decayed, their dwellings became empty on their foundations, and their traces vanished. They exchanged the built palaces, the couches, and the spread cushions for the leaning rocks and stones in the low, hidden graves. So its place is near, and its inhabitant is a stranger among the people of buildings who are desolate and the people of neighborhoods who are preoccupied. They do not find comfort in civilization, nor do they communicate like neighbors and brothers despite the closeness of place, neighborhood, and nearness of dwelling. And how can there be communication between them when tribulation has ground them with its millstone and the stones and dust have consumed them? And they became...
35:5.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of the World'

35:5.arabic: ومن العجائب أنا إذا أردنا المال في الدنيا زرعنا وغرسنا واتجرنا وركبنا البحار والبراري وخاطرنا وإن أردنا طلب رتبة العلم فقهنا وتعبنا في حفظه وتكراره وشهرنا ونجتهد في طلب أرزاقنا ولا نثق بضمان الله لنا ولا نجلس في بيوتنا فنقول اللهم ارزقنا ثم إذا طمعت أعيننا نحو الملك الدائم المقيم قنعنا بأن نقول بألسنتنا اللهم اغفر لنا وارحمنا والذي إليه رجاؤنا وبه اعتزازنا ينادينا ويقول ﴿ وإن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى. ولا يغرنكم بالله الغرور. يا أيها الإنسان ما عزك بربك الكريم ﴾{} ثم كل ذلك لا ينبهنا ولا يخرجنا عن
35:5.english: And among the wonders is that when we want wealth in the worldly life (Dunya), we sow and plant and trade and ride the seas and deserts and take risks, and when we want to seek the rank of knowledge, we understand and toil in memorizing it and repeating it and become famous, and we strive in seeking our provisions and do not trust in God's guarantee for us, nor do we sit in our houses and say: O God, provide for us. Then when our eyes covet the permanent, abiding kingdom, we content ourselves with saying with our tongues: O God, forgive us and have mercy on us. And He to whom is our hope and by whom is our honor calls to us and says: 'And there is not for man except what he strives for. And let not the deceiver deceive you concerning God. O man, what has made you arrogant toward your Lord, the Noble?' Then all of that does not awaken us nor bring us out from the valleys of our deception (Ghurur) and our hopes. So this is nothing but a tremendous trial unless God favors us with a sincere repentance (Tawbah Nasuh) by which He rescues us and grants us refuge. So we ask God the Exalted to grant us repentance, rather we ask Him to make the innermost secrets (Sara'ir) of our hearts (Qulub) yearn for repentance, and that He not make the movement of the tongue with asking for repentance the ultimate portion of our share, so that we become among those who say and do not act, and hear and do not accept. When we hear the admonition, we weep, and when the time comes for acting upon what we have heard, we disobey—a sign of abandonment greater than this. So we ask God the Exalted to bestow upon us success (Tawfiq) and right guidance (Rushd) by His grace and favor.
35:5.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Fear and Hope'

35:6.arabic: وقد عرف الله سبحانه عداوته في مواضع كثيرة من كتابه ليؤمن به ويحترز عنه فقال تعالى إن الشيطان لكم عدو فاتخذوه عدوا إنما يدعو حزبه ليكونوا من أصحاب السعير وقال تعالى ألم أعهد إليكم يا بني آدم أن لا تعبدوا الشيطان إنه لكم عدو مبين فينبغي للعبد أن يشتغل بدفع العدو عن نفسه لا بالسؤال عن أصله ونسبه ومسكنه نعم ينبغي أن يسأل عن سلاحه ليدفعه عن نفسه وسلاح الشيطان الهوى والشهوات وذلك كاف للعالمين
35:6.english: And Allah the Exalted has made known his enmity in many places of His Book so that one may believe in it and guard against it. He said the Exalted: 'Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy. He only invites his party to be among the companions of the Blaze.' And He said the Exalted: 'Did I not enjoin upon you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan - indeed, he is to you a clear enemy?' So it is incumbent upon the servant to occupy himself with repelling the enemy from himself, not with asking about his origin, lineage, and dwelling. Yes, he should ask about his weapon to repel him from himself, and the weapon of Satan is the desire (Hawa) and the lusts (Shahawat), and that is sufficient for the knowers. As for knowing his essence, attributes, and reality - we seek refuge in Allah from him - and the reality of the angels, that is the field of the knowers (Arifin) who delve deeply into the sciences of unveilings (Mukashafat), so there is no need in the science of transaction (Mu'amalah) to know it. Yes, one should know that the thoughts (Khawatir) are divided into what is known decisively to be calling to evil - so it is not hidden that it is a whispering (Waswasa) - and into what is known to be calling to good - so there is no doubt that it is an inspiration (Ilham) - and into what is ambiguous in it - so one does not know whether it is from the prompting (Lamma) of the angel or from the prompting of Satan. For among the stratagems of Satan is that he presents evil in the guise of good, and the distinction in that is obscure, and most worshippers perish by it. For Satan is not able to call them to clear evil, so he portrays evil in the image of good, as he says to the scholar by way of admonition: 'Do you not look at the creation, and they are dead from ignorance, perished from heedlessness, they have approached the Fire? Do you not have mercy upon the servants of Allah to rescue them from the calamities with your advice and admonition? And Allah has bestowed upon you a seeing heart (Qalb Basir) and an eloquent tongue (Lisan Dhallaq) and an accepted speech.'
35:6.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

35:6.arabic: وقال تعالى إن الشيطان لكم عدوا فاتخذوه عدوا فواطأتموه على المعاصي وقلتم نخاف النار وأرهقتم أبدانكم فيها وقلتم نحب الجنة ولم تعملوا لها وإذا قمتم من فرشكم رميتم عيوبكم وراء ظهوركم وافترشتم عيوب الناس أمامكم فأسخطتم ربكم فكيف يستجيب لكم
35:6.english: And Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy.' Yet you have aligned with him in sins, and you said: 'We fear the Fire' while you exhausted your bodies in it, and you said: 'We love Paradise' but you did not work for it, and when you rose from your beds, you threw your faults behind your backs and spread the faults of others before you, thus angering your Lord—so how could He respond to you?
35:6.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

35:6.arabic: السادسة: نظرت إلى هذا الخلق يبغي بعضهم على بعض ويقاتل بعضهم بعضا فرجعت إلى قول الله عز وجل: (إن الشيطان لكم عدو فاتخذوه عدوا (فاطر: 6) فعاديته وحده واجتهدت في أخذ حذري منه لأن الله تعالى شهد عليه أنه عدو لي فتركت عداوة الخلق غيره.
35:6.english: The Sixth: I looked at this creation and saw them oppressing one another and fighting one another, so I returned to the saying of Allah the Exalted: 'Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy' (Surah Fatir: 6). So I made him alone my enemy and strove to take my precaution from him because Allah the Exalted testified against him that he is an enemy to me, so I abandoned enmity with the creation other than him.
35:6.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Book of Knowledge'

35:7.arabic: وادعى الإجماع فيه واستدل بأدلة تشعر بنقيض غرضه كقوله تعالى الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات إذ هذا يدل على أن العمل وراء الإيمان لا من نفس الإيمان وإلا فيكون العمل في حكم المعاد
35:7.english: And he claimed consensus in this and argued with evidences that suggest the opposite of his purpose, such as the saying of the Exalted: 'Those who believed and did righteous deeds', for this indicates that the deed is beyond the faith, not from the essence of the faith, otherwise the deed would be in the ruling of repetition.
35:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

35:8.arabic: الأصل الثالث: أن فعل العبد وإن كان كسبا للعبد فلا يخرج عن كونه مرادا لله سبحانه فلا يجري في الملك والملكوت طرفة عين ولا لفتة خاطر ولا فلتة ناظر إلا بقضاء الله وقدرته وبإرادته ومشيئته ومنه الشر والخير والنفع والضر والإسلام والكفر والعرفان والنكر والفوز والخسران والغواية والرشد والطاعة والعصيان والشرك والإيمان لا راد لقضائه ولا معقب لحكمه يضل من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء لا يسئل عما يفعل وهم يسألون ويدل عليه من النقل قول الأمة قاطبة ما شاء كان وما لم يشأ لم يكن وقول الله عز وجل أن لو يشاء الله لهدى الناس
35:8.english: The third principle: That the action of the servant (Al-Abd), even if it is an acquisition (Kasb) for the servant, does not depart from being willed (Murad) by Allah, the Exalted. Therefore, not a blink of an eye, nor a turn of thought (Khatir), nor a glance of the eye occurs in the dominion (Al-Mulk) and the kingdom (Al-Malakut) except by the decree (Qada) of Allah and His power (Qudrah) and by His will (Iradah) and His wish (Mashiyyah). From it comes evil (Al-Sharr) and good (Al-Khayr), benefit (Al-Naf) and harm (Al-Darr), Islam and disbelief (Al-Kufr), recognition (Al-Irfan) and denial (Al-Nukr), success (Al-Fawz) and loss (Al-Khusran), misguidance (Al-Ghawayah) and guidance (Al-Rushd), obedience (Al-Ta'ah) and disobedience (Al-Isyan), polytheism (Al-Shirk) and faith (Al-Iman). There is no repeller of His decree, nor any overturner of His judgment. He misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills. He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned. This is indicated by transmission (Al-Naql) from the unanimous saying of the community: 'What He wills happens, and what He does not will does not happen,' and by the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'If Allah had willed, He would have guided all people,' and His saying, the Exalted: 'And if We had willed, We could have given every soul (Nafs) its guidance.' It is indicated by reason (Al-Aql) that if sins (Al-Ma'asi) and crimes were something Allah dislikes and does not will, but they occur in accordance with the will of the enemy, Iblis—may Allah curse him—even though he is an enemy of Allah, the Exalted, and what occurs in accordance with the will of the enemy is more than what occurs in accordance with His will, the Exalted, then I wonder how a Muslim can permit reducing the dominion of the Compeller (Al-Jabbar), Possessor of Majesty (Al-Jalal) and Honor (Al-Ikram), to a rank that, if the leadership of a village chief were reduced to it, he would disdain it. For if what persists for the enemy of the chief in the village is more than what is established for him, he would disdain his leadership and disavow his authority. Disobedience (Al-Ma'siyah) is predominant over creation, and all of that, according to the innovators, occurs contrary to the will of the Truth (Al-Haqq), the Exalted. This is the utmost weakness and incapacity—exalted is the Lord of lords above what the wrongdoers say, high and great. Then, whenever it becomes clear that the actions of the servants are created by Allah, it follows that they are willed by Him. If it is said: 'How can He forbid what He wills and command what He does not will?' We say: Command (Al-Amr) is different from will (Al-Iradah). Therefore, if a master strikes his servant and the ruler reproaches him for it, and he excuses himself by the rebellion of his servant against him, and the ruler disbelieves him, then he shows...
35:8.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

35:8.arabic: "والثانية" أن يكون قد عرف قبح القبيح، ولكنه لم يتعود العمل الصالح بل زين له سوء عمله فتعاطاه انقياداً لشهواته وإعراضاً عن صواب رأيه لاستيلاء الشهوة عليه، ولكن علم تقصيره في عمله فأمره أصعب من الأول، إذ قد تضاعفت الوظيفة عليه؛ إذ عليه قلع ما رشه في نفسه أولاً من كثرة الاعتياد للفساد، والآخر أن يغرس في نفسه صفة الاعتياد للصلاح ولكنه بالجملة محل قابل للرياضة إن انتهض لها بجد وتشمير وحزم. "والثالثة" أن يعتقد في الأخلاق القبيحة أنها الواجبة المستحسنة وأنها حق وجميل وتربى عليها، فهذا يكاد تمتنع معالجت
35:8.english: "The second category" is that he may have recognized the ugliness of the ugly, but he has not accustomed himself to righteous work; rather, his evil deed has been adorned for him, so he undertook it in submission to his desires (Shahawat) and turning away from the correctness of his opinion due to the domination of desire (Shahwa) over him, but he knows his deficiency in his work, so his matter is more difficult than the first, for the duty has multiplied upon him; for he must uproot what was first sprinkled in his soul (Nafs) from the abundance of habituation to corruption, and the other is to implant in his soul (Nafs) the attribute of habituation to righteousness, but he is, in summary, a place receptive to spiritual discipline (Riyada) if he rises to it with earnestness, exertion, and determination. "The third category" is that he believes in the ugly morals that they are obligatory and commendable and that they are truth and beauty, and he is raised upon them, so his treatment is almost impossible and his rectification is not hoped for except rarely, due to the multiplication of the causes of misguidance. "The fourth category" is that, along with his upbringing on the corrupt opinion and his education in acting upon it, he sees virtue in the abundance of evil and the consumption of souls (Nufus) and boasts of it and thinks that this raises his status, and this is the most difficult of the levels. And concerning its like, it is said: And from the hardship is the discipline of the old man, and from the torment is the refinement of the wolf. The first: from these is ignorant only. The second: ignorant and misguided. The third: ignorant, misguided, and transgressor. The fourth: ignorant, misguided, transgressor, and wicked. As for the other illusion they argued with: which is their saying that as long as the human is alive, desire (Shahwa), anger (Ghadab), love of the world, and all these morals do not cease from him, this is an error that occurred to a group who thought that the intended
35:8.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

35:8.arabic: الثامن العجب بالرأي الخطأ. قال الله تعالى "أفمن زين له سوء عمله فرآه حسناً" وقال تعالى "وهم يحسبون أنهم يحسنون صنعاً" وقد أخبر رسول الله ﭬ: أن ذلك يغلب على آخر هذه الأمة[101] وبذلك هلكت الأمم السالفة إذ افترقت فرقاً فكل معجب برأيه "وكل حزب بما لديهم فرحون" وجميع أهل البدع والضلال إنما أصروا عليها لعجبهم بآرائهم والعجب بالبدعة هو استحسان ما يسوق إليه الهوى والشهوة مع ظن كونه حقاً، وعلاج هذا العجب أشد من علاج غيره لأن صاحب الرأي الخطأ جاهل بخطئه ولو عرفه لتركه، ولا يعالج الداء الذي لا يعرف والجهل
35:8.english: The eighth: Pride in erroneous opinion. Allah the Exalted said: "Is he whose evil deed is made fair-seeming unto him so that he sees it as good?" and He said: "And they think that they are doing well." And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) informed: that this will prevail over the latter part of this nation [101], and by this the past nations perished when they split into factions, each proud of his opinion, "and every party rejoices in what is with them." And all the people of innovation and misguidance only persist in them due to their pride in their opinions, and pride in innovation is the approval of what leads to desire and appetite with the assumption of its being truth. The treatment of this pride is more severe than the treatment of others because the possessor of erroneous opinion is ignorant of his error, and if he knew it he would abandon it, and the disease that is not known is not treated, and ignorance is a disease that is not known, so its cure is extremely difficult. Because the knower is able to clarify to the ignorant his ignorance and remove it from him, except if he is proud of his opinion and his ignorance, then he does not listen to the knower and accuses him. Indeed, Allah has imposed upon him a trial that destroys him while he thinks it a blessing, so how can his treatment be possible and how can he seek escape from what is the cause of his happiness in his belief? And his treatment in summary is that he be suspicious of his opinion always, not being deceived by it except when a decisive proof from the Book or the Sunnah or a sound rational evidence encompassing the conditions of evidences testifies, and the human will not know the evidences of the Sharia and the intellect and their conditions and the places of error in them except with a complete natural disposition and a penetrating intellect and diligence and exertion in seeking and practice with the Book and the Sunnah and sitting with the people of knowledge for a long time.
35:8.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

35:8.arabic: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: الضلالة لها حلاوة في قلوب أهلها. قال الله تعالى: (وذر الذين اتخذوا دينهم لعبا ولهوا( (الأنعام: 70) وقال تعالى: (أفمن زين له سوء عمله فرآه حسنا( (فاطر: 8) فكل ما أحدث بعد الصحابة رضي الله عنهم مما جاوز قدر الضرورة والحاجة فهو من اللعب واللهو.
35:8.english: And Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: Misguidance (Dhalalah) has sweetness in the hearts (Qulub) of its people. Allah the Exalted said: 'And leave those who take their religion as play and amusement' (Al-An'am: 70) and He said: 'Is he whose evil deed is made fair-seeming unto him so that he sees it as good?' (Fatir: 8). So everything that is innovated after the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, that exceeds the measure of necessity and need is from play and amusement.
35:8.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

35:8.arabic: فإنه يضل من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء ويميت من يشاء ويحيي من يشاء ولكنا نقدر الأمر جاريا على ما ألف من سنة الله تعالى في بعثة الأنبياء لصلاح الدين والدنيا وما لي أقدر هذا وقد كان ما أقدره فلقد بعث الله نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم على فترة من الرسل وكان شرع عيسى عليه السلام قد مضى عليه قريب من ستمائة سنة والناس منقسمون إلى مكذبين له من اليهود وعبدة الأوثان وإلى مصدقين له قد شاع الفسق فيهم كما شاع في زماننا الآن والكفار مخاطبون بفروع الشريعة والأموال كانت في أيدي المكذبين له والمصدقين أما المكذبون فكانوا يت
35:8.english: For He misleads whom He wills and guides whom He wills, and He causes death whom He wills and gives life whom He wills. But we estimate the matter proceeding according to what is customary from the established way (Sunnah) of Allah the Exalted in sending the prophets for the rectification of the religion and the worldly life. And why do I estimate this when what I estimate has already occurred? For indeed Allah sent our Prophet (peace be upon him) after an interval of messengers, and the law of Jesus (peace be upon him) had passed upon it close to six hundred years, and the people were divided into those who disbelieved in him from the Jews and idol worshippers, and into those who believed in him, and corruption had spread among them as it has spread in our time now. And the disbelievers were addressed with the branches of the law, and the wealth was in the hands of those who disbelieved in him and those who believed. As for the disbelievers, they were transacting without the law of Jesus (peace be upon him), and as for the believers, they were being lax with the foundation of belief just as Muslims are lax now, even though the era of prophethood was closer. So all the wealth, or most of it, or much of it, was unlawful (haram) (peace be upon him), and he pardoned what had passed and did not interfere with it, and he specified the possessors of hands with the wealth, and he established the law. And what is established as unlawful in a law does not become lawful due to the sending of a messenger, nor does it become lawful by the one who possesses the unlawful surrendering it, for we do not take in the jizyah from the people of the covenant what we know specifically to be the price of wine or usurious wealth, for their wealth in that time was like our wealth now and...
35:8.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

35:10.arabic: السبب الثاني: لقوة المحبة، قوة معرفة الله تعالى واتساعها واستيلاؤها على القلب، وذلك بعد تطهير القلب من جميع شواغل الدنيا وعلائقها يجري مجرى وضع البذر في الأرض بعد تنقيتها من الحشيش وهو الشطر الثاني. ثم يتولد من هذا البذر شجرة المحبة والمعرفة وهي الكلمة الطيبة التي ضرب الله بها مثلاً حيث قال: " ضرب الله مثلاً كلمة طيبة كشجرة طيبة أصلها ثابت وفرعها في السماء " وإليها الإشارة بقوله تعالى " إليه يصعد الكلم الطيب "، أي المعرفة " والعمل الصالح يرفعه " فالعمل الصالح كالجمال لهذه المعرفة وكالخادم وإنما
35:10.english: The second reason: For the strength of love (Mahabbah), the strength of knowledge (Ma'rifah) of Allah the Exalted and its expansion and its domination over the heart (Qalb), and that after purifying the heart from all distractions of the world and its attachments, it proceeds like placing the seed in the earth after purifying it from weeds, which is the second half. Then from this seed is generated the tree of love and knowledge, which is the good word (Kalimah Tayyibah) that Allah struck as a parable when He said: "Allah strikes a parable of a good word like a good tree whose root is firm and its branch is in the sky." And to it is the allusion in His saying, the Exalted: "To Him ascends the good word (Al-Kalim Al-Tayyib)", meaning the knowledge (Ma'rifah), "and the righteous deed (Al-'Amal Al-Salih) raises it." So the righteous deed is like beauty for this knowledge and like a servant, and indeed all righteous deeds are in purifying the heart first from the world then in maintaining its purity, so the deed is not intended except for this knowledge, and as for the knowledge of how to perform the deed, it is intended for the deed, so knowledge is the first and it is the last, and indeed the first is the knowledge of interaction (Ilm Al-Mu'amalah) and its purpose is the deed, and the purpose of interaction is the clarity (Safa') of the heart and its purity so that the clarity of the truth becomes evident in it and it becomes adorned with the knowledge of knowledge (Ilm Al-Ma'rifah), which is the knowledge of unveiling (Ilm Al-Mukashafah). And whenever this knowledge is attained, love follows it by necessity, just as one with a balanced temperament, if he sees beauty and perceives it with the apparent eye, loves it and inclines toward it, and whenever he loves it, pleasure (Ladhdhah) occurs, so pleasure follows love by necessity, and love follows knowledge by necessity, and one does not reach this knowledge after the cutting off of worldly distractions from the heart except with pure thought (Fikr Safi), constant remembrance (Dhikr Da'im), utmost effort in seeking, and continuous contemplation (Nadhar Mustamirr) in Allah the Exalted and in His attributes and in the dominion of His heavens and all His creatures.
35:10.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

35:10.arabic: والثالث أن يراد به العلم بالله وصفاته وأفعاله فذلك أفضل من كل عمل بل مقصود الأعمال صرف القلوب عن الخلق إلى الخالق لتنبعث بعد الانصراف إليه لمعرفته ومحبته فالعلم وعلم العمل مرادان لهذا العلم وهذا العلم غاية المريدين والعمل كالشرط له وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى إليه يصعد الكلم الطيب والعمل الصالح يرفعه فالكلم الطيب هو هذا العلم والعمل كالحمال الرافع له إلى مقصده فيكون المرفوع أفضل من الرافع وهذا كلام معترض لا يليق بهذا الكلام فلنرجع إلى المقصود
35:10.english: The third [aspect] is that what is intended by it is knowledge of Allah and His attributes and His actions, for that is better than every deed. Rather, the purpose of deeds is to divert the hearts (Qulūb) from creation to the Creator, so that they may be stirred after turning to Him for His knowledge (Maʿrifah) and His love. Thus, the deed and knowledge of the deed are intended for this knowledge, and this knowledge is the ultimate goal of the seekers (Murīdīn), and the deed is like a condition for it. And to this is the allusion in His saying, the Exalted: 'To Him ascends the good word (Al-Kalim al-Ṭayyib), and the righteous deed raises it.' So the good word (Al-Kalim al-Ṭayyib) is this knowledge, and the deed is like the carrier that raises it to its intended destination, so the raised is better than the raiser. And this is an interjected speech that is not fitting for this discourse, so let us return to the intended purpose.
35:10.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Seclusion'

35:10.arabic: وأما الآيات: فقوله تعالى "فويل للمصلين الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون الذين هم يراءون" وقوله عز وجل "والذين يمكرون السيئات لهم عذاب شديد ومكر أولئك هو يبور" قال مجاهد هم أهل الرياء. وقال تعالى "إنما نعطمكم لوجه الله لا نريد منكم جزاء ولا شكورا" فمدح المخلصين ينفي كل إرادة سوى وجه الله، والرياء ضده وقال تعالى "فمن كان يرجو لقاء ربه فليعمل صالحاً ولا يشرك بعبادة ربه أحدا" نزل بعد ذلك فيمن يطلب الأجر والحمد بعباداته وأعماله.
35:10.english: As for the verses: His statement, the Exalted, "Woe to those who pray, who are heedless of their prayer, who make show (of their deeds)" and His statement, the Mighty and Majestic, "And those who plot evil deeds, for them is a severe punishment, and the plotting of those, it will perish" said Mujahid: they are the people of ostentation (Riya'). And His statement, "We feed you only for the face (Wajh) of Allah; we desire no reward nor thanks from you" so He praised the sincere ones (Mukhlisin) by negating every desire except the face (Wajh) of Allah, and ostentation (Riya') is its opposite. And His statement, "So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone" was revealed after that concerning those who seek reward and praise through their acts of worship and deeds.
35:10.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

35:18.arabic: فكما أنه لا يبغض الأب المطيع ببغضه للولد العاصي فكذلك لا يحب الولد العاصي بحبه للأب المطيع، ولو كان الحب يسري من الأب إلى الولد لأوشك أن يسري البغض أيضاً بل الحق أن لا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى. ومن ظن أنه ينجو بتقوى أبيه كمن ظن أنه يشبع بأكل أبيه ويروى بشرب أبيه، ويصير عالماً بتعلم أبيه ويصل إلى الكعبة ويراها بمشي أبيه. فالتقوى فرض عين فلا يجزه فيه والد عن ولده شيئاً وكذا العكس، وعند الله جزاء التقوى "يوم يفر المرء من أخيه وأمه وأبيه" إلا على سبيل الشفاعة لمن لم يشتد غضب الله عليه فيأذن في الشفاعة له
35:18.english: Just as He does not hate the obedient father because of His hatred for the disobedient son, similarly He does not love the disobedient son because of His love for the obedient father. If love were to flow from the father to the son, it would be likely that hatred would also flow. Rather, the truth is that 'no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another' (Quran 35:18). And whoever thinks that he will be saved by the piety (Taqwa) of his father is like one who thinks that he will be satiated by his father's eating, quenched by his father's drinking, becomes knowledgeable by his father's learning, and reaches the Kaaba and sees it by his father's walking. Piety (Taqwa) is an individual obligation (Fard 'Ayn), so no parent can substitute for their child in it, and likewise the reverse. And with Allah is the reward of piety (Taqwa) 'on the Day when a man will flee from his brother, his mother, and his father' except by way of intercession (Shafa'a) for one upon whom Allah's anger has not intensified, so He permits intercession (Shafa'a) for him - as previously mentioned in the Book of Arrogance and Vanity.
35:18.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

35:18.arabic: فلا تتفكر فيما هو ممكن لغيرك بل فيما هو مخوف في حقك، فإنه لا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى، وعذاب غيرك لا يخفف شيئاً من عذابك، فإذا تفكرت في هذا الخطر كان عندك شغل شاغل عن التكبر وعن أن ترى نفسك فوق غيرك.
35:18.english: So do not contemplate what is possible for others, but rather what is feared in your own right, for indeed no bearer of burdens (Wazira) bears the burden (Wizr) of another, and the punishment of another does not alleviate anything from your punishment. If you contemplate this danger, you will have an all-engrossing preoccupation from arrogance and from seeing your soul (Nafs) above others.
35:18.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

35:18.arabic: وأقيم عليه شاهدين إبراهيم وموسى ثم تلا "أم لم ينبأ بما في صحف موسى وإبراهيم الذي وفى أن لا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى" فقال زياد خلوا سبيله، هذا رجل قد لقن حجته، وقيل مكتوب في الإنجيل. من استغفر لمن ظلمه فقد هزم الشيطان.
35:18.english: And he established upon it two witnesses, Ibrahim (Abraham) and Musa (Moses), then he recited: "Or has he not been informed of what is in the scriptures of Musa (Moses) and Ibrahim (Abraham) who fulfilled [his covenant]? That no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another." So Ziyad said: Release him, this man has been taught his argument, and it is said written in the Injil (Gospel): Whoever seeks forgiveness for the one who wronged him has defeated the Satan.
35:18.topic: Al-Ghazali on the outer and inner dimensions of worship, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

35:18.arabic: الوجه الثالث أن يبقى بعده ولدا صالحا يدعو له كما ورد في الخبر أن جميع عمل ابن آدم منقطع إلا ثلاثا فذكر الولد الصالح وفي الخبر إن الأدعية تعرض على الموتى على أطباق من نور وقول القائل إن الولد ربما لم يكن صالحا لا يؤثر فإنه مؤمن والصلاح هو الغالب على أولاد ذوي الدين لا سيما إذا عزم على تربيته وحمله على الصلاح وبالجملة دعاء المؤمن لأبويه مفيد برا كان أو فاجرا فهو مثاب على دعواته وحسناته فإنه من كسبه وغير مؤاخذ بسيئاته فإنه لا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى ولذلك قال تعالى ألحقنا بهم ذرياتهم وما ألتناهم من عمله
35:18.english: The third aspect is that there remains after him a righteous child who prays for him, as it is reported in the tradition that all the deeds of the son of Adam are cut off except three, and the righteous child is mentioned. And in the tradition, supplications are presented to the dead on trays of light. And the statement of the one who says that the child might not be righteous does not affect it, for he is a believer, and righteousness is predominant among the children of the people of religion, especially if he resolves to raise him and compel him to righteousness. And in summary, the supplication of the believer for his parents is beneficial, whether they are righteous or wicked, for he is rewarded for his supplications and good deeds, for they are from his earning, and he is not held accountable for their evil deeds, for no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another. And therefore, the Exalted said: 'We have joined their offspring with them, and We have not diminished anything from their deeds' meaning: We have not decreased anything from their deeds, and We have made their children an increase in their good deeds.
35:18.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

35:28.arabic: وأما الثاني وهو الأعلى فأن يكون الله هو المخوف أعني أن يخاف العبد الحجاب عنه ويرجو القرب منه. قال ذو النون رحمه الله تعالى خوف النار عند خوف الفراق كقطرة قطرت في بحر لجي وهذه خشية العلماء حيث قال تعالى: ﴿ إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء ﴾ {} ولعموم المؤمنين أيضا حظ من هذه الخشية ولكن هو بمجرد التقليد أيضا هي خوف الصبي من الحية تقليدا لأبيه وذلك لا يستند إلى بصيرة فلا جرم يضعف ويزول على قرب حتى إن الصبي ربما يرى المعزم يقدم على أخذ الحية فينظر إليه ويغتر به فيتجرأ على أخذها تقليدا له كما احترز من
35:28.english: And the second, which is the higher, is that God is the One to be feared, meaning that the servant fears the veil from Him and hopes for closeness to Him. Dhu al-Nun, may God have mercy on him, said: 'The fear of Hell compared to the fear of separation is like a drop that has fallen into a deep sea.' And this is the fear (Khashya) of the scholars, where He, the Exalted, said: 'Indeed, only those who have knowledge (Al-'Ulama') among His servants fear God.' And the general believers also have a share of this fear, but it is merely by imitation (Taqleed), like the fear of a child from a snake by imitating his father, and that is not based on insight (Bassira), so it weakens and disappears quickly. Indeed, the child might see the snake charmer proceed to take the snake, look at him, be deceived by him, and dare to take it by imitating him, just as he refrained from taking it by imitating his father. Imitative beliefs are weak in general, unless they are strengthened by witnessing their confirming causes continuously and by persisting in their requirements in increasing acts of obedience (Taa'at) and avoiding sins (Ma'asi) for a long duration consistently. Therefore, whoever ascends to the peak of knowledge (Ma'rifa) and knows God, the Exalted, fears Him necessarily, so he does not need treatment to induce fear, just as whoever knows the lion and sees himself falling into its claws does not need treatment to induce fear into his heart (Qalb), but fears it necessarily, whether he wills or not. And for that reason, God, the Exalted, revealed to David, peace be upon him: 'Fear Me as you fear the predatory lion.' And there is no means to induce fear of the predatory lion except knowledge of the lion and knowledge of falling into its claws, so he does not need any means. Similarly, whoever knows God, the Exalted, knows that He does what He wills and does not care, and decrees what He wants, and does not fear the closeness of the angels without a prior means, and He banished Iblis.
35:28.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

35:28.arabic: وأما بطريق الإقتباس من الآيات والأخبار فما ورد في فضيلة الخوف خارج عن الحصر وناهيك دلالة على فضيلته جمع الله تعالى للخائفين الهدى والرحمة والعلم والرضوان وهي مجامع مقامات أهل الجنان وقال الله تعالى: ﴿ وهدى ورحمة للذين هم لربهم يرهبون ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء ﴾ {} وصفهم بالعلم لخشيتهم وقال عز وجلّ: ﴿ رضى الله عنهم ورضوا عنه ذلك لمن خشى ربه ﴾ {} وكل ما دل على فضيلة العلم دل على فضيلة الخوف لأن الخوف ثمرة العلم ولذلك جاء في خبر موسى عليه أفضل الصلاة والسلام وأما الخائفون ف
35:28.english: And as for the method of citation from the verses and reports, what has come regarding the virtue of fear is beyond enumeration, and sufficient as an indication of its virtue is that Allah the Exalted has gathered for those who fear: guidance, mercy, knowledge, and pleasure, which are the collective stations of the people of the Gardens. And Allah the Exalted said: 'And guidance and mercy for those who are in awe of their Lord' (Quran 16:128). And He the Exalted said: 'Indeed, only those who fear Allah from among His servants are the knowledgeable ones' (Quran 35:28). He described them with knowledge due to their fear. And He the Mighty and Majestic said: 'Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him; that is for whoever fears his Lord' (Quran 98:8). And everything that indicates the virtue of knowledge indicates the virtue of fear, because fear is the fruit of knowledge. And therefore, it came in the report of Moses, upon him the best of prayers and peace: 'And as for those who fear, for them is the Highest Companion, in which they are not shared.' So see how He singled them out with the companionship of the Highest Companion, and that is because they are the knowledgeable ones, and the knowledgeable ones have a rank of companionship with the prophets, because they are the inheritors of the prophets, and the companionship of the Highest Companion is for the prophets and those who join them. And therefore (when the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, was given the choice during his terminal illness between remaining in the world and coming to Allah the Exalted, he would say: 'I ask You for the Highest Companion' [60]). So then, if one looks at its producer, it is knowledge, and if one looks at its fruit, it is piety (Wara') and God-consciousness (Taqwa). And what has come regarding their virtues is not hidden, until indeed the outcome has become marked with God-consciousness (Taqwa), specified by it, just as praise has become specified for Allah the Exalted and prayer for the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, until it is said: 'Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and the outcome is for the God-conscious ones (Mut-taqeen), and prayers upon our master Muhammad, peace be upon him, and all his family.' And Allah the Exalted has specified God-consciousness (Taqwa) with addition to Himself, so He the Exalted said: 'Their meat will not reach Allah, nor will their blood, but what reaches Him is God-consciousness (Taqwa) from you' (Quran 22:37). And indeed, God-consciousness (Taqwa) is an expression of restraint by the dictate of fear, as preceded.
35:28.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

35:28.arabic: فإن قلت: فما بال بعض الناس يزداد بالعلم كبراً وأمناً؟ فاعلم أن لذلك سببين: "أحدهما" أن يكون اشتغاله بما يسمى علماً وليس علماً حقيقياً، وإنما العلم الحقيقي ما يعرف به العبد ربه ونفسه، وخطر أمره في لقاء الله والحجاب منه، وهذا يورث الخشية والتواضع دون الكبر والأمن. قال الله تعالى "إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء" فأما ما وراء ذلك كعلم الطب والحساب واللغة والشعر والنحو وفصل الخصومات وطرق المجادلات، فإذا تجرد الإنسان لها حتى امتلأ بها كبراً ونفاقاً، وهذه بأن تسمى صناعات أولى من أن تسمى علوماً، بل الع
35:28.english: If you say: Why is it that some people increase in arrogance and false security with knowledge? Know that there are two reasons for this: "The first" is that he occupies himself with what is called knowledge but is not true knowledge, for true knowledge is that by which the servant knows his Lord and himself, and the danger of his affair in meeting Allah and being veiled from Him, and this produces fear (Khushya) and humility without arrogance and false security. Allah the Exalted said: "Indeed, only those who have knowledge (Al-'Ulama') among His servants fear Allah." As for what is beyond that, like knowledge of medicine, arithmetic, language, poetry, grammar, settling disputes, and methods of argumentation, if a person devotes himself to these until he becomes filled with arrogance and hypocrisy, these are more appropriately called crafts than called knowledge, rather knowledge is the knowledge of servitude ('Ubūdiyya) and lordship (Rubūbiyya) and the path of worship ('Ibāda), and these generally produce humility.
35:28.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

35:28.arabic: شواهدها من القرآن قوله عز وجل: ﴿شهد الله أنه لا إله إلا هو والملائكة وأولو العلم قائما بالقسط﴾ (آل عمران 3: 18) فانظر كيف بدأ سبحانه وتعالى بنفسه وثنى بالملائكة وثلث بأهل العلم وناهيك بهذا شرفا وفضلا وجلاء ونبلا وقال الله تعالى: ﴿يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات﴾ (المجادلة: 11) قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: للعلماء درجات فوق المؤمنين بسبعمائة درجة ما بين الدرجتين مسيرة خمسمائة عام. وقال عز وجل: ﴿قل هل يستوي الذين يعلمون والذين لا يعلمون﴾ وقال تعالى: ﴿إنما يخشى الله من عباده الع
35:28.english: Its evidences from the Quran are His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and [so do] the angels and those of knowledge - [that He is] maintaining [creation] in justice' (Al Imran 3:18). So observe how He, the Exalted and Majestic, began with Himself, then mentioned the angels, and thirdly mentioned the people of knowledge - and what honor, virtue, clarity, and nobility is greater than this! And Allah, the Exalted, said: 'Allah will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge by degrees' (Al-Mujadilah: 11). Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: 'For the scholars are degrees above the believers by seven hundred degrees, the distance between two degrees being a journey of five hundred years.' And the Mighty and Majestic said: 'Say, "Are those who know equal to those who do not know?"' And He, the Exalted, said: 'Only those fear Allah from among His servants who are scholars' (Quran 35:28). And He, the Exalted, said: 'Say, "Sufficient is Allah as Witness between me and you, and [from] whoever has knowledge of the Scripture."' And He, the Exalted, said: 'Said one who had knowledge from the Scripture, "I will bring it to you."' indicating that he was empowered by the strength of knowledge. And the Mighty and Majestic said: 'But those who were given knowledge said, "Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for he who believes and does righteousness."' clarifying that the greatness of the Hereafter's status is known through knowledge. And He, the Exalted, said: 'And these examples We present to the people, but none will understand them except those of knowledge.' And He, the Exalted, said: 'And if they had referred it back to the Messenger or to those of authority among them, then the ones who [can] draw correct conclusions from it would have known about it.' referring His ruling in events to their deduction and equating their rank with the rank of the prophets in uncovering Allah's ruling. And it is said regarding His saying, the Exalted: 'O children of Adam, We have bestowed upon you clothing to conceal your private parts' meaning knowledge, 'and adornment' meaning certainty (Yaqin), 'and the clothing of righteousness (Taqwa)' meaning modesty (Haya'). And the Mighty and Majestic said: 'And We had certainly brought them a Book which We detailed by knowledge.' And He, the Exalted, said: 'So We will surely relate [their deeds] to them with knowledge.' And the Mighty and Majestic said: 'Rather, it is distinct verses [preserved] within the breasts of those who have been given knowledge.' And He, the Exalted, said: 'He created man¤ [and] taught him eloquence.' And He only mentioned that in the context of bestowing favor.
35:28.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Book of Knowledge'

35:28.arabic: فمن عرف الله تعالى عرف من صفاته أنه يهلك العالمين ولا يبالي، ويعلم أنه مسخر في قدرة من لو أهلك مثله آلافاً مؤلفة وأبد عليهم العذاب أبد الآباد لم يؤثر ذلك فيه أثراً ولم تأخذه عليه رقة ولا اعتراه عليه جزع. ولذلك قال تعالى "إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء" وفاتحة الزبور "رأس الحكمة خشية الله" وقال ابن مسعود: كفى بخشية الله علماً وكفى بالاغترار بالله جهلاً.
35:28.english: For whoever knows Allah (the Exalted) knows from His attributes that He destroys the worlds and does not care, and knows that he is subjugated in the power of One who, if He destroyed thousands upon thousands like him and made the punishment eternal upon them for eternity, it would not affect Him with any effect, nor would any compassion take Him regarding it, nor would any distress afflict Him concerning it. And therefore He (the Exalted) said: "Indeed, only those who have knowledge (al-'Ulama') among His servants fear Allah." And the opening of the Psalms: "The beginning of wisdom is the fear (Khashyah) of Allah." And Ibn Mas'ud said: "Sufficient is the fear (Khashyah) of Allah as knowledge, and sufficient is delusion with Allah as ignorance."
35:28.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

35:29.arabic: الوظيفة الرابعة: أن يظهر حيث يعلم أن في إظهاره ترغيبا للناس في الاقتداء ويحرس سره من داعية الرياء بالطريق الذي سنذكره في معالجة الرياء في كتاب الرياء فقد قال الله عز وجل: ﴿ إن تبدوا الصدقات فنعما هي ﴾ {} وذلك حيث يقتضي الحال الإبداء إما للاقتداء وإما لأن السائل إنما سأل على ملأ من الناس فلا ينبغي أن يترك التصدق خيفة من الرياء في الإظهار بل ينبغي أن يتصدق ويحفظ سره عن الرياء بقدر الإمكان وهذا لأن في الإظهار محذورا ثالثا سوى المن والرياء وهو هتك ستر الفقير فإنه ربما يتأذى بأن يرى في صورة المحتاج ف
35:29.english: The Fourth Duty: That he should make it public where he knows that in its publicity there is encouragement for people to follow his example, and he should guard his secret from the prompting of hypocrisy (Riya') through the method we will mention in treating hypocrisy in the Book of Hypocrisy. For Allah the Exalted has said: 'If you disclose your charitable expenditures, they are good' (Quran 2:271) {} and that is where the situation necessitates disclosure, either for emulation or because the asker only asked in public view, so one should not refrain from giving charity out of fear of hypocrisy in publicity; rather, one should give charity and guard his secret from hypocrisy as much as possible. This is because in publicity there is a third danger besides reminding of favor and hypocrisy, which is exposing the cover of the poor person, for he might be harmed by being seen in the guise of a needy person. So whoever makes the asking public is the one who exposed his own cover, so one should not be cautious of this meaning in his publicity, and it is like exposing immorality upon one who concealed it, for that is prohibited, and spying into it and habitual mention of it is forbidden. As for whoever exposes it, the establishment of the punishment upon him is publicizing, but he is the cause in it. And with a similar meaning, the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever casts off the garment of modesty (Haya'), then there is no backbiting for him.' And Allah the Exalted has said: 'And spend from what We have provided you, secretly and openly' (Quran 35:29) {} He encouraged to openness also because of the benefit of encouragement in it. So let the servant (Abd) be precise in contemplation in weighing this benefit against the danger that is in it, for that differs by circumstances and persons. Indeed, announcement in some circumstances for some persons may be better, and whoever knows the benefits and harms and does not look with the eye of desire, the most appropriate and fitting for every situation becomes clear to him.
35:29.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

35:29.arabic: وقال تعالى: ﴿ إن الذين يتلون كتاب الله وأقاموا الصلاة وأنفقوا مما رزقناهم سرا وعلانية يرجون تجارة لن تبور ﴾ {} ولما قال ﭬ: (لو تعلمون ما أعلم لضحكتم قليلا ولبكيتم كثيرا ولخرجتم إلى الصعدات تلدمون صدروكم وتجارون إلى ربكم فهبط جبريل عليه السلام فقال إن ربك يقول لك لم تقنط عبادي فخرج عليهم ورجاهم وشوقهم[8]).
35:29.english: And Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, those who recite the Book (Kitab) of Allah and establish the Prayer (Salah) and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and openly, they hope for a trade that will never perish.' And when the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'If you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much, and you would go out to the elevated places striking your chests and trading with your Lord.' Then Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended and said: 'Indeed, your Lord says to you: Why do you cause My servants to despair?' So he went out to them and gave them hope (Rajaa) and aroused their longing (Shawq).
35:29.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Fear and Hope'

35:33.arabic: قال الله تعالى: ﴿ يحلون فيها من أساور من ذهب ولؤلؤا ولباسهم فيها حرير ﴾ {} والآيات فى ذلك كثيرة وإنما تفصيله فى الأخبار فقد روى أبو هريرة  أن  النبي ﭬ قال: (من يدخل الجنة ينعم لا يبأس لا تبلى ثيابه ولا يفنى شبابه فى الجنة  ما لا عين رأت ولا أذن سمعت ولا خطر عن قلب بشر[231]). (وقال رجل:  يا  رسول  الله أخبرنا عن ثياب أهل الجنة أخلق تخلق أم نسج تنسج فسكت رسول  الله  ﭬ  وضحك  بعض القوم فقال رسول الله ﭬ مم تضحكون من جاهل سأل عالما ثم قال رسول  الله  ﭬ:  بل ينشق عنها ثمر الجنة مرتين[232]) وقال أبو هر
35:33.english: Allah the Exalted said: 'They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their garments therein will be silk.' {} And the verses regarding that are many, but its detail is in the reports. Indeed, Abu Hurairah reported that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever enters Paradise enjoys bliss without misery; his clothes do not wear out, nor does his youth perish in Paradise—what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has not occurred to the heart (Qalb) of any human [231].' (And a man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, inform us about the clothes of the people of Paradise—are they created as creation or woven as weaving?' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) remained silent, and some of the people laughed. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Why do you laugh at an ignorant one asking a knowledgeable one?' Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Rather, they split from the fruit of Paradise twice [232].') And Abu Hurairah said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, the first group to enter Paradise, their form is like the form of the moon on the night of the full moon; they do not spit therein, nor blow their noses, nor defecate; their utensils and combs are of gold and silver, and their sweat is musk; each one of them has two wives—the marrow of their shins is seen from behind the flesh due to beauty; there is no disagreement among them nor hatred; their hearts (Qulub) are upon one heart (Qalb); they glorify Allah morning and evening (and in a narration) each wife has seventy garments [233].' And he (peace be upon him) said regarding His statement: 'They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold' {} said: 'Indeed, upon them are crowns; the lowest pearl therein illuminates what is between the east and the west [234].'
35:33.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

35:33.arabic: (صفة لباس أهل الجنة وفرشهم وسررهم وأرائكهم وخيامهم) قال الله تعالى: ﴿ يحلون فيها من أساور من ذهب ولؤلؤا ولباسهم فيها حرير ﴾ والآيات فى ذلك كثيرة وإنما تفصيله فى الأخبار فقد روى أبو هريرة أن النبي ﭬ قال: (من يدخل الجنة ينعم لا يبأس لا تبلى ثيابه ولا يفنى شبابه فى الجنة ما لا عين رأت ولا أذن سمعت ولا خطر عن قلب بشر[231]). (وقال رجل: يا رسول الله أخبرنا عن ثياب أهل الجنة أخلق تخلق أم نسج تنسج فسكت رسول الله ﭬ وضحك بعض القوم فقال رسول الله ﭬ مم تضحكون من جاهل سأل عالما ثم قال رسول الله ﭬ: بل ينشق عن
35:33.english: (Description of the clothing of the people of Paradise and their furnishings, beds, couches, and tents) Allah the Exalted said: "They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their garments therein will be silk." And the verses in that are many, and its detail is in the reports. Indeed, Abu Hurairah reported that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever enters Paradise enjoys, does not despair, his clothes do not wear out, nor does his youth perish in Paradise, what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, nor has it occurred to the heart (Qalb) of a human." (And a man said: O Messenger of Allah, inform us about the clothes of the people of Paradise, are they created creation or woven weaving? The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) remained silent, and some of the people laughed. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: Why are you laughing at an ignorant one asking a knowledgeable one? Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: Rather, it splits from it the fruit of Paradise twice.) And Abu Hurairah said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, the first group to enter Paradise, their image is like the image of the moon on the night of the full moon, they do not spit in it, nor do they blow their noses, nor do they defecate, their utensils and their combs are of gold and silver, and their sweat is musk, for each one of them are two wives, the marrow of her shin is seen from behind the flesh from the beauty, there is no difference between them and no mutual hatred, their hearts (Qulub) are upon one heart (Qalb), they glorify Allah morning and evening (and in a narration) on each wife are seventy garments." And he (peace be upon him) said regarding His statement the Exalted: "They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold": "Indeed, upon them are the crowns, the lowest pearl in it illuminates what is between the east and the west." And he (peace be upon him) said: "The tent is a hollow pearl, its length in the sky is sixty miles, in every corner of it for the believer are people he does not see."
35:33.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

35:33.arabic: [234] حديث في قوله تعالى - يحلون فيها من أساور من ذهب - قال إن عليهم التيجان أدنى لؤلؤة فيها تضىء ما بين المشرق والمغرب أخرجه الترمذى من حديث أبى سعيد دون ذكر الآية وقال لا نعرفه إلا من حديث رشد بن سعد.
35:33.english: [234] A hadith regarding His (Allah's) saying - 'They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold' - he said: 'Upon them are crowns, the smallest pearl in them illuminates what is between the East and the West.' Al-Tirmidhi transmitted it from the hadith of Abu Sa'id without mentioning the verse and said: 'We do not know it except from the hadith of Rashid ibn Sa'd.'
35:33.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Book of Repentance'

35:34.arabic: وقال ﷺ: (ليس على أهل لا إله إلا الله وحشة في قبورهم ولا في نشورهم كأني أنظر إليهم عند الصيحة ينفضون رؤوسهم من التراب ويقولون الحمد لله الذي أذهب عنا الحزن إن ربنا لغفور شكور[21]).
35:34.english: And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no loneliness upon the people of "There is no god but Allah" in their graves nor in their resurrection, as if I am looking at them at the blast (of the trumpet) shaking their heads from the dust and saying: "Praise be to Allah who has removed from us the grief; indeed, our Lord is Forgiving (Ghafur), Appreciative (Shakur)."'
35:34.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

35:35.arabic: فكأن قد صرتم إلى ما صاروا إليه من البلاء والوحدة في دار المثوى وارتهنتم في ذلك المضجع وضمكم ذلك المستودع. فكيف بكم لو عاينتم الأمور وبعثرت القبور وحصل ما في الصدور وأوقفتم للتحصيل بين يدي الملك الجليل فطارت القلوب لإشفاقها من سالف الذنوب وهتكت عنكم الحجب والأستار وظهرت منكم العيوب والأسرار؟ هنالك تجزى كل نفس بما كسبت إن الله عز وجل يقول "ليجزى الذي أساءوا بما عملوا ويجزى الذي أحسنوا بالحسنى" وقال تعالى "ووضع الكتاب فترى المجرمين مشفقين مما فيه" الآية جعلنا الله وإياكم عاملين بكتابة متبعين لأوليا
35:35.english: As if you have already reached what they have reached of affliction and solitude in the abode of the final resting place (Dar al-Mathwa), and you have been held as security in that resting place and that repository has encompassed you.
