37:64.english: Then look at their food, which is the Zaqqum (Zaqqum) as Allah the Exalted said: 'Then indeed you, O those astray and deniers, will eat from a tree of Zaqqum and fill your bellies with it, then drink on top of it from boiling water, drinking like thirsty camels.' And He the Exalted said: 'Indeed it is a tree that emerges in the foundation of the Hellfire (al-Jahim), its fruit as if it were heads of devils. Then indeed they will eat from it and fill their bellies with it, then indeed for them upon it is a mixture of boiling water, then indeed their return is to the Hellfire (al-Jahim).'
37:64.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

37:74.arabic: وعند هذا زل أقدام الأكثرون إلا عباد الله المخلصين الذين لا سلطان عليهم للشيطان اللعين فشاهدوا بنور البصائر كون الكاتب مسخراً مضطراً، كما شاهد جميع الضعفاء كون القلم مسخراً، وعرفوا أن غلط الضعفاء في ذلك كغلط النملة مثلاً لو كانت تدب على الكاغد فترى رأس القلم يسود الكاغد، ولم يمتد بصرها إلى اليد والأصابع فضلاً عن صاحب اليد فغلطت وظنت القلم هو المسود للبياض، وذلك لقصور بصرها عن مجاوزة رأس القلم لضيق حدقتها، فكذلك من لم ينشرح بنور الله تعالى صدره للإسلام قصرت عن ملاحظة جبار السموات والأرض ومشاهدة كو
37:74.english: And at this point, the feet of most people slipped except the purified servants (Ibad Allah al-Mukhlaseen) of Allah upon whom the accursed Satan has no authority, for they witnessed with the light of insights (Basa'ir) that the writer is a compelled instrument (Musakhkhar), just as all the weak witnessed that the pen is an instrument. And they knew that the error of the weak in this is like the error of an ant, for example, if it were crawling on the paper and saw the tip of the pen blackening the paper, and its sight did not extend to the hand and fingers, let alone the possessor of the hand, so it erred and thought the pen was the one blackening the whiteness, and that is due to the deficiency of its sight from surpassing the tip of the pen because of the narrowness of its pupil. Similarly, whoever's chest (Sadr) was not expanded by the light of Allah, the Exalted, for Islam (Islam), his sight fell short from observing the Compeller (Jabbar) of the heavens and the earth and witnessing His being the Dominator (Qahir) behind everything, so he stopped on the path at the writer, and that is pure ignorance. Rather, the possessors of hearts (Qulub) and spiritual visions (Mushahadat) - Allah, the Exalted, has made every particle in the heavens and the earth speak in their regard by His power (Qudrah) through which everything speaks, until they heard its glorification (Tasbih) and sanctification (Taqdis) for Allah, the Exalted, and its testimony against itself of incapacity (Ajz) with a fluent tongue (Lisan Dhalq) that speaks without letter (Harf) or sound (Sawt), which those who are isolated from hearing (Sam') do not hear. And I do not mean by it the apparent hearing (Sam' al-Dhahir) that does not transcend sounds, for the donkey shares in it, and there is no value in what the beasts share in. Rather, I intend by it a hearing (Sam') that perceives a speech (Kalam) that is not by letter nor sound, nor is it Arabic nor non-Arabic.
37:74.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

37:96.arabic: الأصل الأول: العلم بأن كل حادث في العالم فهو فعله وخلقه واختراعه لا خالق له سواه ولا محدث له إلا إياه خلق الخلق وصنعهم وأوجد قدرتهم وحركتهم فجميع أفعال عباده مخلوقة له ومتعلقة بقدرته تصديقا له في قوله تعالى الله خالق كل شيء وفي قوله تعالى والله خلقكم وما تعملون وفي قوله تعالى وأسروا قولكم أو اجهروا به إنه عليم بذات الصدور ألا يعلم من خلق وهو اللطيف الخبير أمر العباد بالتحرز في أقوالهم وأفعالهم وإسرارهم وإضمارهم لعلمه بموارد أفعالهم واستدل على العلم بالخلق وكيف لا يكون خالقا لفعل العبد وقدرته تام
37:96.english: The First Principle: The knowledge that every occurrence in the world is His action, His creation, and His invention; there is no creator for it other than Him, and no one brings it into existence except Him. He created the creation and fashioned them, brought into existence their power (Qudrah) and their movement, so all the actions of His servants are created by Him and connected to His power (Qudrah), confirming Him in His saying, the Exalted: 'Allah is the Creator of everything' and in His saying: 'And Allah created you and what you do' and in His saying: 'And conceal your speech or proclaim it, indeed He is Knowing of what is within the chests. Does He not know who He created? And He is the Subtle, the Aware.' He commanded the servants to be cautious in their statements and their actions, their secrets and their hidden thoughts due to His knowledge of the sources of their actions, and He argued for the knowledge of creation. And how could He not be the creator of the servant's action when His power (Qudrah) is complete with no deficiency in it, and it is connected to the movement of the bodies of the servants, and the movements are similar, and the connection of the power (Qudrah) to them is for their essence. So what is it that restricts its connection from some movements without others despite their similarity? Or how could the animal be independent in invention when there issues from the spider, the bee, and all the animals from subtle crafts what bewilders the intellects of those of understanding? So how did they become isolated in their invention without the Lord of lords, and they are not knowing of the details of what issues from them of acquisition? Far, far be it! The creations have been humbled, and He is unique in sovereignty and dominion, the Compeller of the earth and the heavens.
37:96.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Foundations of Belief'

37:99.arabic: فهؤلاء جميع أحوالهم تصلح أن تكون سببا لازيادهم فلا تتميز عندهم عبادة عن عبادة وهم الذين فروا إلى الله عز وجل كما قال تعالى: ﴿ لعلكم تذكرون ﴾ {} ففروا إلى الله وتحقق فيهم قوله تعالى: ﴿ وإذ اعتزلتموهم وما يعبدون إلا الله فأووا إلى الكهف ينشر لكم ربكم من رحمته ﴾ {} وإليه الإشارة بقوله: ﴿ إني ذاهب إلى ربي سيهدين ﴾ {} وهذه منتهى درجات الصديقين ولا وصول إليها إلا بعد ترتيب الأوراد والمواظبة عليها دهرا طويلا فلا ينبغي أن يغتر المريد بما سمعه من ذلك فيدعيه لنفسه ويفتر عن وظائف عبادته فذلك علامته أن لا ي
37:99.english: For these people, all their states become a cause for their increase, so no worship is distinguished from another worship for them, and they are those who have fled to Allah the Exalted, as He said: 'That you may remember' (Quran 2:203), so flee to Allah. And His saying is realized in them: 'And when you withdraw from them and that which they worship except Allah, then take refuge in the cave; your Lord will spread for you of His mercy' (Quran 18:16). And to this is the indication by His saying: 'Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me' (Quran 37:99). And this is the utmost degree of the truthful ones (Siddiqin), and there is no reaching it except after arranging the litanies (Awrad) and persisting in them for a long time. So it is not fitting for the seeker (Murid) to be deceived by what he hears of that and claim it for himself and slacken from the duties of his worship. Its sign is that no whisper (Waswas) occurs in his heart (Qalb), and no sin (Ma'siyah) crosses his heart (Qalb), and the assaults of terrors (Hawal) do not agitate him, nor do great affairs (Ashghal) startle him. And how is this rank granted to everyone? So it is incumbent upon all to arrange the litanies (Awrad) as we have mentioned.
37:99.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

37:128.arabic: وعند هذا زل أقدام الأكثرون إلا عباد الله المخلصين الذين لا سلطان عليهم للشيطان اللعين فشاهدوا بنور البصائر كون الكاتب مسخراً مضطراً، كما شاهد جميع الضعفاء كون القلم مسخراً، وعرفوا أن غلط الضعفاء في ذلك كغلط النملة مثلاً لو كانت تدب على الكاغد فترى رأس القلم يسود الكاغد، ولم يمتد بصرها إلى اليد والأصابع فضلاً عن صاحب اليد فغلطت وظنت القلم هو المسود للبياض، وذلك لقصور بصرها عن مجاوزة رأس القلم لضيق حدقتها، فكذلك من لم ينشرح بنور الله تعالى صدره للإسلام قصرت عن ملاحظة جبار السموات والأرض ومشاهدة كو
37:128.english: At this point, the feet of most people slipped except the purified servants (Ibad Allah al-Mukhlaseen) of Allah upon whom the accursed Satan has no authority, for they witnessed with the light of insight (Basa'ir) that the writer is a compelled instrument (Musakhkhar), just as all the weak witnessed that the pen is an instrument. They recognized that the error of the weak in this is like the error of an ant, for example, if it were crawling on the paper and saw the tip of the pen blackening the paper, and its sight did not extend to the hand and fingers, let alone the owner of the hand, so it erred and thought the pen was the one blackening the whiteness, due to the deficiency of its sight from exceeding the tip of the pen because of the narrowness of its pupil. Similarly, whoever's chest (Sadr) has not expanded with the light of Allah the Exalted for Islam (Islam), their sight fell short from observing the Compeller (Jabbar) of the heavens and the earth and witnessing His being the Dominant (Qahir) behind everything, so they stopped on the path at the writer, which is pure ignorance. Rather, the possessors of hearts (Qulub) and spiritual visions (Mushahadat) - Allah the Exalted has made every particle in the heavens and the earth speak in their regard by His power (Qudrah) through which everything speaks, until they heard its glorification (Tasbih) and sanctification (Taqdis) for Allah the Exalted and its testimony against itself of incapacity with a fluent tongue (Lisan Dhalq) that speaks without letter (Harf) or sound (Sawt), which those who are isolated from hearing (Sam') do not hear. I do not mean by it the apparent hearing (Sam' al-Zahir) that does not exceed sounds, for the donkey shares in it, and there is no value in what the beasts share in. Rather, I intend by it a hearing (Sam') that perceives a speech (Kalam) that is not by letter nor sound, nor is it Arabic nor non-Arabic.
37:128.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

37:130.arabic: ومنها المنقول المنقلب كقوله تعالى ﴿ وطور سينين ﴾ {} أي طور سيناء ﴿ سلام على إل ياسين ﴾ {} أي على الياس وقيل إدريس لأن في حرف ابن مسعود سلام على إدراسين
37:130.english: And among them is the transferred and reversed, like His saying, the Exalted: 'And Mount Sinai (Ṭūr Sīnīn)' meaning Mount Sinai (Ṭūr Sīnā'), 'Peace be upon the family of Yasin (Salam 'alā Āl Yāsīn)' meaning upon Elias (Ilyās), and it is said Idris (Idrīs) because in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is 'Peace be upon Idrasin (Salam 'alā Idrāsīn)'.
37:130.topic: Al-Ghazali on the outer and inner dimensions of worship, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

37:137.arabic: وعلى القعود عن هذا السفر وقع الإنكار بقوله تعالى وإنكم لتمرون عليهم مصبحين وبالليل أفلا تعقلون وبقوله سبحانه وكأين من آية في السماوات والأرض يمرون عليها وهم عنها معرضون
37:137.english: And upon the abstention from this journey falls the reproach by His saying, the Exalted: 'And indeed, you pass by them in the morning and by night - will you not then use intellect?' and by His saying, the Glorified: 'And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by while they are turning away from it?'
37:137.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Etiquette of Travel'

37:147.arabic: وقال أبو هريرة لو كان فى المسجد مائة ألف أو يزيدون ثم تنفس رجل من أهل النار لماتوا وقد قال بعض العلماء فى قوله: ﴿ تلفح وجوههم النار ﴾ {} إنها لفحتهم لفحة واحدة فما أبقت لحما على عظم إلا ألقته عند أعقابهم
37:147.english: And Abu Huraira said: 'If there were in the mosque one hundred thousand or more (mā'at alf aw yazīdūn), then a man from the people of the Fire breathed, they would die.' And some scholars said regarding His saying: 'The Fire will scorch their faces' {} that it scorches them with one scorching, and it leaves no flesh upon a bone except that it casts it at their heels.'
37:147.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

37:160.arabic: وعند هذا زل أقدام الأكثرون إلا عباد الله المخلصين الذين لا سلطان عليهم للشيطان اللعين فشاهدوا بنور البصائر كون الكاتب مسخراً مضطراً، كما شاهد جميع الضعفاء كون القلم مسخراً، وعرفوا أن غلط الضعفاء في ذلك كغلط النملة مثلاً لو كانت تدب على الكاغد فترى رأس القلم يسود الكاغد، ولم يمتد بصرها إلى اليد والأصابع فضلاً عن صاحب اليد فغلطت وظنت القلم هو المسود للبياض، وذلك لقصور بصرها عن مجاوزة رأس القلم لضيق حدقتها، فكذلك من لم ينشرح بنور الله تعالى صدره للإسلام قصرت عن ملاحظة جبار السموات والأرض ومشاهدة كو
37:160.english: And at this point, the feet of most people slipped except the purified servants (Ibad Allah al-Mukhlaseen) of Allah upon whom the accursed Satan has no authority, so they witnessed with the light of insight (Basa'ir) that the writer is a compelled and subjugated one, just as all the weak ones witnessed that the pen is subjugated. And they knew that the mistake of the weak ones in that is like the mistake of an ant, for example, if it were crawling on the paper and sees the tip of the pen blackening the paper, and its sight did not extend to the hand and the fingers, let alone the possessor of the hand, so it erred and thought the pen is the one that blackens the whiteness, and that is due to the deficiency of its sight from surpassing the tip of the pen because of the narrowness of its pupil. Likewise, he whose chest (Sadr) has not expanded with the light of Allah the Exalted for Islam (Islam), his sight fell short from observing the Compeller of the heavens and the earth and witnessing His being the Dominant behind everything, so he stopped on the way at the writer, and that is pure ignorance. Rather, the possessors of hearts (Qulub) and spiritual visions (Mushahadat) - Allah the Exalted has made every particle in the heavens and the earth speak on their behalf by His power (Qudrah) with which everything speaks, until they heard its glorification and its praise (Tasbih) of Allah the Exalted and its testimony against itself of incapacity with a fluent tongue that speaks without letter (Harf) or sound (Sawt) that is not heard by those who are isolated from hearing (Sam'). And I do not mean by it the apparent hearing (Sam' al-Zahir) that does not go beyond sounds, for the donkey shares in it, and there is no value for that in which beasts share. Rather, I intend by it a hearing (Sam') that perceives thereby a speech (Kalam) that is not by letter nor sound, nor is it Arabic nor non-Arabic.
37:160.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

37:164.arabic: فإن ما رزق تعالى الملائكة من القرب والرتبة لازم مستمر على حال واحد لا يزيد ولا ينقص لذلك أخبر الله عنهم أنهم قالوا: وما منا إلا له مقام معلوم، وفارق الإنسان الملائكة في الترقي من درجة إلى درجة فإنه لا يزال يتقرب إلى الله تعالى فيستفيد مزيد قربه وباب المزيد مسدود على الملائكة عليهم السلام وليس لكل واحد إلا رتبته التي هي وقف عليه وعبادته التي هو مشغول بها لا ينتقل إلى غيرها ولا يفتر عنها لا يستكبرون عن عبادته ولا يستحسرون يسبحون الليل والنهار لا يفترون ومفتاح مزيد الدرجات هي الصلوات.
37:164.english: For what Allah the Exalted has granted the angels of nearness and rank is constant and continuous in a single state that does not increase nor decrease; therefore, Allah informed about them that they said: 'And there is not among us except that he has a known station (maqām maʿlūm).' And the human differs from the angels in ascending from one degree to another, for he continuously draws nearer to Allah the Exalted and thus gains increased nearness, and the door of increase is closed upon the angels, peace be upon them. And for each one there is only his rank that is fixed upon him and his worship that he is occupied with; he does not transfer to other than it nor does he cease from it; they do not grow arrogant about worshipping Him nor do they become weary; they glorify night and day without ceasing, and the key to increased degrees is the prayers.
37:164.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

37:164.arabic: فاعلم أن خلقه الملائكة تخالف خلقة الإنس وما من واحد منهم إلا وهو وحدانى الصفة ليس فيه خلط وتركيب ألبتة فلا يكون لكل واحد منهم إلا فعل واحد، وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى: ﴿ وما منا إلا له مقام معلوم ﴾ {} فلذلك ليس بينهم تنافس وتقاتل بل مثالهم في تعين مرتبة كل واحد منهم وفعله مثال الحواس الخمس فإن البصر لا يزاحم السمع في إدراك الأصوات ولا الشم يزاحمها ولا هما يتنازعان الشم وليس كاليد والرجل فإنك قد تبطش بأصابع الرجل بطشا ضعيفا فتزاحم به اليد وقد تضرب غيرك برأسك فتزاحم اليد التى هى آلة الضرب ولا كالإن
37:164.english: Know that the creation of the angels differs from the creation of humans, and there is not one of them except that he is singular in attribute (وحدانى الصفة), with no mixing or composition whatsoever. Therefore, each one of them has only one action, and to this is the indication by His saying, the Exalted: 'And there is not among us except that he has a known station (مقام معلوم)' (Quran 37:164). Thus, there is no competition or fighting between them. Rather, their example in determining the rank of each one of them and his action is like the example of the five senses, for sight does not compete with hearing in perceiving sounds, nor does smell compete with them, nor do they dispute over smell. And it is not like the hand and the foot, for you may strike with the toes of the foot a weak strike, thus competing with the hand, and you may strike another with your head, thus competing with the hand which is the instrument of striking. Nor is it like the single human who undertakes by himself grinding, kneading, and baking, for this is a kind of deviation and departure from justice, its cause being the difference in the attributes (صفات) of the human and the difference in his motives (دواعيه). For he is not singular in attribute, so he is not singular in action. Therefore, we see the human obeying God at one time and disobeying Him at another due to the difference in his motives and attributes, and that is not possible in the nature (طباع) of the angels. Rather, they are molded upon obedience, peace be upon him, peace be upon him, peace be upon him, peace be upon him, peace be upon him. There is no room for disobedience in their right, so indeed they do not disobey God in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded, and they glorify night and day without ceasing. The one bowing among them is bowing forever, the one prostrating among them is prostrating forever, and the one standing is standing forever. There is no difference in their actions nor slackness, and for each one there is a known station (مقام معلوم) which he does not exceed, and their obedience to God, the Exalted, from where there is no room for opposition in them, can be likened.
37:164.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

37:171.arabic: والمغرورين فلا مانع لما أعطى ولا معطي لما منع ولم يقطع التوفيق عن الكفار لجناية متقدمة ولا أمد الأنبياء عليهم السلام بتوفيقه ونور هدايته لوسيلة سابقة ولكنه قال ولقد سبقت كلمتنا لعبادنا المرسلين وقال عز وجل ولكن حق القول مني لأملأن جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين وقال تعالى إن الذين سبقت لهم منا الحسنى أولئك عنها مبعدون فإن خطر ببالك أنه لم اختلفت السابقة وهم في ربقه العبودية مشتركون نوديت من سرادقات الجلال لا تجاوز حد الأدب فإنه لا يسئل عما يفعل وهم يسئلون
37:171.english: And the deluded ones, so there is no preventer for what He gives and no giver for what He withholds, and He did not cut off the Success (Tawfiq) from the disbelievers due to a preceding transgression, nor did He extend the Prophets, peace be upon them, with His Success (Tawfiq) and the light of His guidance due to a preceding means, but He said: 'And indeed Our Word (Kalimatuna) has preceded for Our servants, the messengers (al-Mursalin).' And He, the Exalted, said: 'But the true Word (al-Qawl) from Me is: I will fill Hell with jinn and mankind together.' And He, the Exalted, said: 'Indeed, those for whom the best (al-Husna) from Us has preceded, those are from it far removed.' So if it occurs to your mind that the preceding has not differed while they are in the bond of servitude (al-'ubudiyyah) sharing, you are called from the pavilions of Majesty: 'Do not exceed the limit of etiquette (al-Adab), for He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned.'
37:171.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

37:182.arabic: نجز كتاب الأذكار والدعوات بكماله يتلوه إن شاء الله تعالى كتاب الأوراد والحمد لله رب العالمين وصلى الله على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وصحبه وسلم.
37:182.english: The Book of Remembrances (Adhkar) and Supplications (Dua'at) is completed in its entirety, to be followed, if Allah wills, by the Book of Regular Devotions (Awrad). And all praise (Al-Hamd) is for Allah, Lord (Rabb) of the worlds, and may Allah send blessings upon our master Muhammad and upon his family and companions and grant them peace.
37:182.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

38:26.arabic: يا أمير المؤمنين أتدري ما جاء في تأويل هذه الآية عن جدك يا داود إنا جعلناك خليفة في الأرض فاحكم بين الناس بالحق ولا تتبع الهوى فيضلك عن سبيل الله قال الله تعالى في الزبور يا داود إذا قعد الخصمان بين يديك فكان لك في أحدهما هوى فلا تتمنين في نفسك أن يكون الحق له فيفلح على صاحبه فأمحوك عن نبوتي ثم لا تكون خلفتي ولا كرامة يا داود إنما جعلت رسلي إلى عبادي رعاء كرعاء الإبل لعلمهم بالرعاية ورفقهم بالسياسة ليجبروا الكسير ويدلوا الهزيل على الكلأ والماء
38:26.english: O Commander of the Believers, do you know what came in the interpretation of this verse from your grandfather? 'O David, indeed We have made you a successor (Khalifah) in the earth, so judge between the people in truth and do not follow the desire (Hawa) lest it mislead you from the path of Allah.' Allah the Exalted said in the Zabur: 'O David, when two disputants sit before you and you have desire (Hawa) for one of them, do not wish in your soul (Nafs) that the truth be for him so he prevails over his opponent, for I will erase you from My prophethood, then you will not be My successor (Khalifah) nor have honor. O David, I only made My messengers to My servants as shepherds like shepherds of camels, for their knowledge of shepherding and their gentleness in governance, to mend the broken and guide the weak to pasture and water.'
38:26.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

38:30.arabic: الثانية: أن يشكر المعطى ويدعو له ويثني عليه ويكون شكره ودعاؤه بحيث لا يخرجه عن كونه واسطة ولكنه طريق وصول نعمة الله سبحانه إليه وللطريق حق من حيث جعله الله طريقا وواسطة وذلك لا ينافي رؤية النعمة من الله سبحانه فقد قال ﭬ: (من لم يشكر الناس لم يشكر الله[31]) وقد أثنى الله عز وجل على عباده في مواضع على أعمالهم وهو خالقها وفاطر القدرة عليها نحو قوله تعالى: ﴿ نعم العبد إنه أواب ﴾ {} إلى غير ذلك وليقل القابض في دعائه طهر الله قلبك في قلوب الأبرار وزكى عملك في عمل الأخيار وصلى على روحك في أرواح الشهداء
38:30.english: The second: That he thanks the giver and prays for him and praises him, and his thanks and prayer should be such that it does not remove him from being an intermediary, but it is the path of arrival of the blessing (Ni'mah) of Allah سبحانه to him, and the path has a right from where Allah made it a path and intermediary, and that does not contradict seeing the blessing (Ni'mah) from Allah سبحانه, for he ﭬ said: (Whoever does not thank people has not thanked Allah[31]), and Allah عز وجل has praised His servants in places for their deeds while He is their Creator and Originator of the capability for them, like His saying تعالى: ﴿ Excellent is the servant (Abd), indeed he is oft-returning (Awwab) ﴾ {} and so on. And let the receiver say in his prayer: May Allah purify your heart (Qalb) among the hearts (Qulub) of the righteous and make your deeds pure among the deeds of the good-doers and send blessings upon your spirit (Ruh) among the spirits (Arwah) of the martyrs. And he ﭬ said: (Whoever does you a favor, then reward him, and if you are unable, then pray for him until you know that you have rewarded him[32]). And from the completeness of thanks is that he conceals the defects of the gift if there is a defect in it, and does not belittle it, nor disparage it, nor reproach him with withholding if he withholds, and magnifies his deed to himself and to people. So the function of the giver is to consider it small, and the function of the receiver is to assume the favor and magnify it, and upon every servant (Abd) is to fulfill his right, and there is no contradiction in that, for the causes of belittling and magnifying are opposed, and what benefits the giver is observing the causes of belittling, and harms him its opposite, and the taker is the opposite of that, and all of that does not contradict seeing the blessing (Ni'mah) from Allah عز وجل, for whoever does not see the intermediary as an intermediary has been ignorant, and indeed the denial is to see the intermediary as an origin.
38:30.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

38:44.arabic: الثانية: أن يشكر المعطى ويدعو له ويثني عليه ويكون شكره ودعاؤه بحيث لا يخرجه عن كونه واسطة ولكنه طريق وصول نعمة الله سبحانه إليه وللطريق حق من حيث جعله الله طريقا وواسطة وذلك لا ينافي رؤية النعمة من الله سبحانه فقد قال ﭬ: (من لم يشكر الناس لم يشكر الله[31]) وقد أثنى الله عز وجل على عباده في مواضع على أعمالهم وهو خالقها وفاطر القدرة عليها نحو قوله تعالى: ﴿ نعم العبد إنه أواب ﴾ {} إلى غير ذلك وليقل القابض في دعائه طهر الله قلبك في قلوب الأبرار وزكى عملك في عمل الأخيار وصلى على روحك في أرواح الشهداء
38:44.english: The second: that he thanks the giver and prays for him and praises him, and his thanks and prayer should be such that it does not remove him from being an intermediary, but it is the path of arrival of the blessing (Ni'mah) of Allah, the Exalted, to him, and the path has a right from the aspect that Allah made it a path and an intermediary, and that does not contradict seeing the blessing (Ni'mah) from Allah, the Exalted, for indeed the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever does not thank people has not thanked Allah.' And Allah, the Exalted, has praised His servants in places for their deeds while He is the Creator of them and the Originator of the ability upon them, such as His saying, the Exalted: 'Excellent is the servant (Abd); indeed, he is one who repeatedly turns (Awwab).' and so on. And let the receiver say in his supplication: 'May Allah purify your heart (Qalb) among the hearts of the righteous and make your deeds pure among the deeds of the good-doers and send blessings upon your spirit (Ruh) among the spirits of the martyrs.' And indeed the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever does you a favor, then reward him, and if you are unable, then pray for him until you know that you have rewarded him.' And from the completeness of thanks is that he conceals the defects of the gift if there is a defect in it, and he does not belittle it, nor does he blame it, nor does he reproach with withholding if he withholds, and he magnifies his deed to himself and to the people. So the duty of the giver is to consider it small, and the duty of the receiver is to assume the favor and consider it great, and upon every servant (Abd) is to fulfill his right, and there is no contradiction in that, for the causes of making small and making great are opposed, and what benefits the giver is observing the causes of making small, and what harms him is the opposite of that, and the receiver is the opposite of that, and all of that does not contradict seeing the blessing (Ni'mah) from Allah, the Exalted, for whoever does not see the intermediary as an intermediary has indeed been ignorant, and what is denied is to see the intermediary as an origin.
38:44.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

38:44.arabic: وكان حبيب بن أبي حبيب إذا قرأ هذه الآية: ﴿ إنا وجدناه صابرا نعم العبد إنه أواب ﴾ {} بكى وقال واعجباه اعطى واثنى أي هو المعطي للصبر وهو المثنى وقال أبو الدرداء ذروة الايمان الصبر للحكم والرضا بالقدر هذا بيان فضيلة الصبر من حيث النقل وأما من حيث النظر بعين الاعتبار فلا تفهمه الا بعد فهم حقيقة الصبر ومعناه اذ معرفة الفضيلة والرتبة معرفة صفة فلا تحصل قبل معرفة الموصوف فلنذكر حقيقته ومعناه وبالله التوفيق.
38:44.english: And Habib ibn Abi Habib, when he recited this verse: 'Indeed, We found him patient (صابرا). Excellent is the servant (العبد). Indeed, he was one who repeatedly turned [to Allah] (أواب).' {}, he wept and said: 'How wondrous! He gave and praised,' meaning He is the Giver of patience (الصبر) and the Praiser. And Abu al-Darda' said: 'The pinnacle of faith (الإيمان) is patience (الصبر) for the decree and contentment with destiny (القدر).' This is the clarification of the virtue of patience (الصبر) from the perspective of transmitted tradition, and as for from the perspective of consideration with the eye of insight, you will not understand it except after understanding the reality (حقيقة) of patience (الصبر) and its meaning, for knowledge of virtue and rank is knowledge of an attribute, so it is not attained before knowledge of the described. So let us mention its reality (حقيقة) and meaning, and with Allah is success.
38:44.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

38:44.arabic: ومن ههنا نظر حبيب بن ابي حبيب حيث قرأ ﴿ إنا وجدناه صابرا نعم العبد إنه اواب ﴾  {}  فقال  واعجباه  أعطى  واثنى اشارة الى انه اذا اثنى على اعطائه فعلى نفسه اثنى فهو المثنى وهو المثنى عليه
38:44.english: And from here is the perspective of Habib ibn Abi Habib when he recited: 'Indeed, We found him patient. Excellent is the servant (Abd). Indeed, he was one who repeatedly turned [to Allah] (Awwab).' Then he said: 'How wondrous! He gave and praised,' indicating that when He praises His giving, He praises Himself, for He is the Praiser (Al-Muthna) and the One Praised (Al-Muthna 'Alayh).
38:44.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

38:62.arabic: وقالت قريش لرسول الله ﭬ: كيف نجلس إليك وعند هؤلاء؟ وأشاروا إلى فقراء المسلمين فازدروهم بأعينهم لفقرهم، وتكبروا عن مجالستهم فأنزل الله تعالى "ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي" إلى قوله "ما عليك من حسابهم" وقال تعالى "واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه ولا تعد عيناك عنهم تريد زينة الحياة الدنيا" ثم أخبر الله تعالى عن تعجبهم حين دخلوا جهنم إذ لم يروا الذين ازدروهم فقالوا "ما لنا لا نرى رجالاً كنا نعدهم من الأشرار" قيل يعنون عماراً وبلالاً وصهيباً والمقداد رضي الله عنه
38:62.english: And the Quraysh said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him): 'How can we sit with you while these are present?' And they pointed to the poor Muslims, and they looked down upon them with their eyes due to their poverty, and they were too proud to sit with them. So Allah the Exalted revealed: 'And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord (Rabb) in the morning and the evening' up to His saying: 'You are not accountable for them.' And He said: 'And restrain your soul (Nafs) with those who call upon their Lord (Rabb) in the morning and the evening, seeking His Face, and do not turn your eyes away from them, desiring the adornment of the worldly life.' Then Allah the Exalted informed about their astonishment when they entered Hellfire, as they did not see those whom they had looked down upon, so they said: 'What is wrong with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the wicked?' It is said they mean 'Ammar, Bilal, Suhayb, and Al-Miqdad (may Allah be pleased with them). Then among them were those whom pride prevented from thought and knowledge, so they were ignorant of his (peace be upon him) being right; and among them were those who knew but pride prevented them from acknowledgment. Allah the Exalted said informing about them: 'So when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it,' and He said: 'And they denied them while their souls (Anfus) were convinced of them, out of injustice and arrogance.' And this pride is close to being proud against Allah the Almighty, even if it is less than that, but it is pride against accepting the command of Allah and humbling oneself to His Messenger.
38:62.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

38:65.arabic: ولا قاهر الا الله الواحد القهار ولا قادر الا الملك الجبار واذا انكشفت الغطاء عن اعين الغافلين فشاهدوا الامر كذلك سمعوا عند ذلك نداء المنادي ﴿ لمن الملك اليوم لله الواحد القهار ﴾ {} ولقد كان الملك لله الواحد القهار كل يوم لا ذلك على الخصوص ولكن الغافلين لا يسمعون هذا النداء الا ذلك اليوم، فهو نبأ عما يتجدد للغافلين من كشف الاحوال حيث لا ينفعهم الكشف فنعوذ بالله الحليم الكريم من الجهل والعمى فانه اصل اسباب الهلاك.
38:65.english: And there is no Subduer (Qahir) except Allah, The One (Al-Wahid), The Subduer (Al-Qahhar), and there is no Powerful (Qadir) except The King (Al-Malik), The Compeller (Al-Jabbar). And when the veil (Ghita') is lifted from the eyes of the heedless (Ghafilin) and they witness the matter thus, they hear at that time the call of the caller: 'To whom belongs the dominion today? To Allah, The One (Al-Wahid), The Subduer (Al-Qahhar).' And indeed, the dominion belongs to Allah, The One (Al-Wahid), The Subduer (Al-Qahhar) every day, not that specifically, but the heedless (Ghafilin) do not hear this call except on that day. So it is news (Naba') about what is renewed for the heedless (Ghafilin) from the unveiling (Kashf) of states (Ahwal) where the unveiling (Kashf) does not benefit them. So we seek refuge in Allah, The Forbearing (Al-Halim), The Generous (Al-Karim), from ignorance (Jahl) and blindness ('Ama), for it is the root (Asl) of the causes (Asbab) of destruction (Halak).
38:65.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

38:66.arabic: العاشر الدعاء عن التنبه فليقل في تيقظاته وتقلباته مهما تنبه ما كان يقوله رسول الله ﷺ: (لا إله إلا الله الواحد القهار رب السموات والأرض وما بينهما العزيز الغفار[75]) وليجتهد أن يكون آخر ما يجري على قلبه عند النوم ذكر الله تعالى وأول ما يرد على قلبه عند التيقظ ذكر الله تعالى فهو علامة الحب ولا يلازم القلب في هاتين الحالتين إلا ما هو الغالب عليه فليجرب قلبه به فهو علامة الحب فإنها علامة تكشف من باطن القلب وإنما استحبت هذه الأذكار لتستجر القلب إلى ذكر الله تعالى فإذا استيقظ ليقوم قال الحمد لله الذي
38:66.english: The tenth: The supplication upon awakening, so let him say in his awakenings and tossings whenever he awakens what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say: (There is no god but Allah, the One, the Subduer (Al-Qahhar), Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, the Mighty (Al-Aziz), the Forgiving (Al-Ghaffar)[75]). And let him strive that the last thing that flows upon his heart (Qalb) at sleep be the remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah the Exalted and the first thing that comes to his heart (Qalb) upon awakening be the remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah the Exalted, for it is a sign of love. And nothing accompanies the heart (Qalb) in these two states except what is predominant over it, so let him test his heart (Qalb) with it, for it is a sign of love, for it is a sign that reveals from the inner heart (Qalb). And these remembrances (Adhkar) are recommended only to draw the heart (Qalb) to the remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah the Exalted. So when he awakens to rise, he says: Praise be to Allah who gave us life after He caused us to die, and to Him is the resurrection, to the end of what we have mentioned of the supplications of awakening.
38:66.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

38:66.arabic:
ا أن المستيقظ تنكشف له  مشاهدات  لا  تناسب  أحواله  في  النوم
فكذلك المبعوث يرى ما لم يخطر قط بباله ولا شاهده حسه ومثل  النوم  بين  الحياة
والموت مثل البزخ بين الدنيا والآخرة. وقال لقمان لابنه: يا بني إن كنت تشك  في
الموت فلا تنم فكما أنك تنام كذلك تموت وإن كنت تشك في البعث  فلا  تنتبه  فكما
أنك تنتبه بعد نومك فكذلك تبعث بعد موتك. وقال كعب  الأحبار:  إذا  نمت  فاضطجع
على شقك الأيمن واستقبل القبلة بوجهك فإنها وفاة. وقالت عائشة  رضي  الله  عنها
كان رسول الله ﭬ آخر ما يقول حين ينام وهو واضع خده على
38:66.english: [75] Hadith: He used to say upon awakening: 'There is no god but Allah, the One, the Subduer (Al-Qahhar), Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, the Mighty (Al-Aziz), the Forgiving (Al-Ghaffar).' Reported by Ibn al-Sunni and Abu Nu'aym in their two books 'The Practice of Day and Night' from the narration of 'A'ishah.
38:66.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Arrangement of Litanies'

38:71.arabic: فنقول: الخلق والخلق عبارتان مستعملتان معاً، يقال: فلان حسن الخلق والخلق - أي حسن الباطن والظاهر- فيراد بالخلق الصورة الظاهرة، ويراد بالخلق الصورة الباطنة. وذلك لأن الإنسان مركب من جسد مدرك بالبصر ومن روح ونفس مدرك بالبصيرة. ولكل واحد منهما هيئة وصورة إما قبيحة وإما جميلة. فالنفس المدركة بالبصيرة أعظم قدراً من الجسد المدرك بالبصر. ولذلك عظم الله أمره بإضافته إليه إذ قال تعالى "إني خالق بشراً من طين فإذا سويته ونفخت فيه من روحي فقعوا له ساجدين" فنبه على أن الجسد منسوب إلى الطين والروح إلى رب العال
38:71.english: We say: Al-Khalq and al-Khuluq are two expressions used together. It is said: So-and-so has good al-Khuluq and al-Khalq - meaning good inner and outer - so al-Khalq is intended as the outward form, and al-Khuluq is intended as the inward form. This is because the human is composed of a body perceived by sight and of a spirit (Ruh) and soul (Nafs) perceived by insight. For each of them there is a state and form, either ugly or beautiful. The soul (Nafs) perceived by insight is greater in status than the body perceived by sight. Therefore, Allah magnified its matter by attributing it to Himself when He, the Exalted, said: "Indeed, I am creating a human from clay. So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit (Ruh), then fall down to him in prostration." Thus, He alerted that the body is attributed to clay and the spirit (Ruh) to the Lord of the worlds. What is meant by spirit (Ruh) and soul (Nafs) in this context is one; so al-Khuluq is an expression for a firmly established state in the soul (Nafs), from which actions issue forth with ease and facility without need for thought and deliberation. If the state is such that beautiful actions praised by reason and law issue forth from it, that state is called good character (Khuluq hasan), and if what issues forth from it is ugly actions, the state that is the source is called something character.
38:71.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

38:72.arabic: وأما ما لا يجوز أن يسطر في الكتب من المناسبة الخاصة التي اختص بها الآدمي فهي التي يومئ إليها قوله تعالى: " ويسألونك عن الروح قل الروح من أمر ربي " إذ بين أنه أمر رباني خارج عن حد عقول الخلق. وأوضح من ذلك قوله تعالى: " فإذا سويته ونفخت فيه من روحي" ولذلك أسجد له ملائكته، ويشير إليه قوله تعالى: " إنا جعلنا خليفة في الأرض " إذ لم يستحق آدم خلافة الله تعالى إلا بتلك المناسبة وإليه يرمز قوله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم: " إن الله خلق آدم على صورته" حتى ظن القاصرون أن لا صورة إلا الصورة الظاهرة المدركة با
38:72.english: As for what is not permissible to be recorded in books from the special suitability (munāsabah) that the human being (al-ādami) has been exclusively granted, it is that which is alluded to by His saying, the Exalted: 'And they ask you about the Spirit (al-rūḥ). Say: The Spirit is from the command (amr) of my Lord' (Quran 17:85), since He clarified that it is a lordly command (amr rabbānī) beyond the limit of the intellects of creation. And clearer than that is His saying, the Exalted: 'So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him from My Spirit (rūḥī)' (Quran 38:72), and for that reason He made His angels prostrate to him. And it is indicated by His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successor (khalīfah)' (Quran 2:30), since Adam did not deserve the vicegerency (khilāfah) of Allah, the Exalted, except by that suitability (munāsabah). And to it points His saying, peace and blessings be upon him and his family: 'Indeed, Allah created Adam upon His image (ṣūratihi)' (Hadith), until the deficient ones thought that there is no image (ṣūrah) except the apparent image perceived by the senses, so they likened (shabbahū), corporealized (jassamū), and imagined (ṣawwarū). Exalted is Allah, Lord of the worlds, above what the ignorant say, a great exaltation.
38:72.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

38:72.arabic: ألم أخلقك بيدى ونفخت فيك من روحى وأسجدت لك ملائكتى فعصيت أمرى ونسيت عهدى وتعرضت لسخطى
38:72.english: Did I not create you with My Hand and blow into you from My Spirit (Ruh) and make My angels prostrate to you, then you disobeyed My command and forgot My covenant and exposed yourself to My wrath?
38:72.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

38:76.arabic: فإذن تكبره على الخلق عظيم لأنه سيدعوه إلى التكبر على أمر الله، وإنما ضرب إبليس مثلاً لهذا، وما حكاه من أحواله إلا ليعتبر به، فإنه قال: أنا خير منه، وهذا الكبر بالنسب لأنه قال: أنا خير منه خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين، فحمله ذلك على أن يمتنع من السجود الذي أمره الله تعالى به، وكان مبدؤه الكبر على آدم والحسد له فجره ذلك إلى التكبر على أمر الله تعالى، فكان ذلك سبب هلاكه أبد الآباد، فهذه آفة من آفات الكبر على العباد عظيمة، ولذلك شرح رسول الله ﷺ الكبر بهاتين الآفتين إذ سأله ثابت بن قيس بن شماس فقال: ي
38:76.english: Therefore, his arrogance toward the creation is great because it will call him to arrogance toward the command of Allah. Indeed, Iblis (Satan) was made an example of this, and what He narrated of his states is only to take lesson from it, for he said: 'I am better than him,' and this arrogance is by lineage because he said: 'I am better than him, You created me from fire and created him from clay.' This carried him to refuse the prostration that Allah the Exalted commanded him with. Its beginning was arrogance toward Adam and envy of him, which dragged him to arrogance toward the command of Allah the Exalted, and that was the cause of his destruction forever. This is a great affliction from the afflictions of arrogance upon the servants. Therefore, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ explained arrogance with these two afflictions when Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas asked him: 'O Messenger of Allah, I am a man to whom beauty has been made beloved as you see, is it from arrogance?' He ﷺ said: 'No, but arrogance is from rejecting the truth (battar al-haqq) and despising people (ghamṣ al-nās).' And in another narration: 'from belittling the truth (safaha al-haqq).' And his saying 'and despising people' means looking down upon them and considering them insignificant, and they are servants of Allah like him or better than him. And this first affliction 'and belittling the truth' is rejecting it, and it is the second affliction. So whoever sees that he is better than his brother and despises his brother, looks down upon him, and looks at him with the eye of belittlement, or rejects the truth while knowing it, has become arrogant between himself and the creation. And whoever is too proud to submit to Allah the Exalted and humble himself to Allah through His obedience and following His messengers has become arrogant between himself and Allah the Exalted and His messengers.
38:76.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

38:76.arabic: وهذه أقيسة فاسدة تشبه قياس إبليس حيث قال "أنا خير منه خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين" وإلى هؤلاء الإشارة بقوله تعالى "أولئك الذين اشتروا الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة فلا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينصرون" وعلاج هذا الغرور إما بتصديق الإيمان وإما بالبرهان؛ أما التصديق بمجرد الإيمان فهو أن يصدق الله تعالى في قوله "ما عندكم ينفد وما عند الله باق" وفي قوله عز وجل "وما عند الله خير" وقوله "والآخرة خير وأبقى" وقوله "وما الحياة الدنيا إلا متاع الغرور" وقوله "فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا" وقد أخبر رسول الله ﭬ بذلك طوائف
38:76.english: And these are corrupt analogies resembling the analogy of Iblis (Satan) when he said "I am better than him; You created me from fire and created him from clay." And to these people is the reference in the saying of the Exalted: "Those are the ones who have purchased the worldly life for the Hereafter, so the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be aided." And the treatment for this delusion (Ghurur) is either through verification of faith (Iman) or through proof; as for verification through mere faith, it is to believe Allah the Exalted in His saying "What is with you will be exhausted, and what is with Allah is enduring" and in His saying, the Mighty and Majestic, "And what is with Allah is better" and His saying "And the Hereafter is better and more enduring" and His saying "And the worldly life is not but the enjoyment of delusion (Ghurur)" and His saying "So do not let the worldly life delude you." And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) informed groups of the disbelievers of this, so they followed him and believed him and had faith in him and did not demand proof from him[3], and among them were those who said: I adjure you by Allah, did Allah send you as a messenger? And he would say "Yes" so they would believe[4]. And this is the faith (Iman) of the common people, and it removes from delusion (Ghurur), and this is placed in the position of a child believing his father that attending the school is better than attending the playground even though he does not know the aspect of its being better. And as for knowledge through clarification and proof, it is to know the aspect of corruption of this analogy that Satan organized in his heart (Qalb), for every deluded person has a cause for his delusion (Ghurur), and that cause is evidence, and every evidence is a type of analogy that occurs in the soul (Nafs) and begets tranquility towards it even if its possessor is not aware of it nor capable of organizing it with the words of the scholars. So the analogy that Satan organized...
38:76.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

38:76.arabic: وَهَذَا لِأَنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ خُلِقَ مِنَ النَّارِ وَخُلِقَ الْإِنْسَانُ مِنْ صَلْصَالٍ كَالْفَخَّارِ وَالْفَخَّارُ قَدِ اجْتَمَعَ فِيهِ مَعَ النَّارِ الطِّينُ وَالطِّينُ طَبِيعَتُهُ السُّكُونُ وَالنَّارُ طَبِيعَتُهَا الْحَرَكَةُ فَلَا يَتَصَوَّرُ نَارٌ مُشْتَعِلَةٌ لَا تَتَحَرَّكُ بَلْ لَا تَزَالُ تَتَحَرَّكُ بِطَبْعِهَا وَقَدْ كُلِّفَ الْمَلْعُونُ الْمَخْلُوقُ مِنَ النَّارِ أَنْ يَطْمَئِنَّ عَنْ حَرَكَتِهِ سَاجِدًا لِمَا خَلَقَ اللَّهُ مِنَ الطِّينِ فَأَبَى وَاسْتَكْبَرَ وَاسْتَعْصَى وَعَبَّرَ
38:76.english: And this is because the Satan (Shaytan) was created from fire and the human (Insan) was created from clay like pottery, and pottery has gathered in it with fire the clay, and the clay its nature is stillness and fire its nature is movement, so it is not conceivable that a burning fire does not move, rather it does not cease moving by its nature. And the accursed one (Mal'un), created from fire, was commanded to settle from his movement prostrating (Sajdan) to what Allah created from clay, but he refused and was arrogant (Istakbara) and disobeyed (Ist'asa), and he expressed the reason for his disobedience by saying: 'I am better than him, You created me from fire and created him from clay.' Therefore, since the accursed one did not prostrate to our father Adam (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), it is not fitting to hope for his prostration to his children.
38:76.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

38:76.arabic: أما بعد فإن الغضب شعلة نار اقتبست من نار الله الموقدة التي تطلع على الأفئدة، وإنها لمستكنة في طي الفؤاد. استكنان الجمر تحت الرماد، ويستخرجها الكبر الدفين في قلب كل جبار عنيد، كاستخراج الحجر النار من الحديد، وقد انكشف للناظرين بنور اليقين، أن الإنسان ينزع منه عرق إلى الشيطان اللعين، فمن استفزته نار الغضب فقد قويت فيه قرابة الشيطان حيث قال "خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين" فإن شأن الطين السكون والوقار، وشأن النار التلظي والاستعار، والحركة والاضطراب، ومن نتائج الغضب الحقد والحسد، وبهما هلك من هلك وفسد
38:76.english: Now then, anger is a flame of fire borrowed from the fire of Allah the kindled which rises upon the hearts (Af'idah), and indeed it is hidden in the fold of the heart (Fu'ad). The hiding of embers under ashes, and it is extracted by the concealed arrogance in the heart of every obstinate tyrant, like extracting fire from stone with iron, and it has been revealed to the observers by the light of certainty (Yaqin), that the human being has a vein extending to the accursed Satan (Shaytan), so whoever is provoked by the fire of anger has strengthened in him the kinship of Satan when he said "You created me from fire and You created him from clay." For the nature of clay is stillness and dignity, and the nature of fire is blazing and kindling, and movement and agitation, and from the results of anger are malice (Haqd) and envy (Hasad), and by them perished whoever perished and corrupted whoever corrupted, and their source is a morsel (Mudghah) which if it becomes sound, the entire body becomes sound with it, and if malice and envy and anger are among what drives the servant (Abd) to places of destruction, how much he needs to know its harms and evils! So that he may beware of it and guard against it, and remove it from the heart if it is there and expel it, and treat it if it becomes firmly rooted in his heart and cure it, for whoever does not know evil falls into it, and whoever knows it, knowledge alone does not suffice him, unless he knows the path by which he repels evil and removes it.
38:76.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

38:79.arabic: وقال سفيان بن عيينة لا يمنعن أحدكم من الدعاء ما يعلم من نفسه فإن الله عز وجل أجاب دعاء شر الخلق إبليس لعنه الله إذ قال: ﴿ رب فانظرني إلى يوم يبعثون قال إنك من المنظرين ﴾ {}.
38:79.english: And Sufyan bin 'Uyaynah said: Let not what one knows about himself prevent anyone from supplication, for Allah the Exalted answered the supplication of the worst of creation, Iblis (may Allah curse him), when he said: 'My Lord, then grant me respite until the Day they are resurrected. He said: Indeed, you are of those granted respite.'
38:79.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

38:83.arabic: هذه الحكايات تصديق قوله تعالى إلا عبادك منهم المخلصين إذ لا يتخلص العبد من الشيطان إلا بالإخلاص ولذلك كان معروف الكرخى رحمه الله تعالى يضرب نفسه ويقول يا نفس أخلصى تتخلصى وقال يعقوب المكفوف المخلص من يكتم حسناته كما يكتم سيئاته وقال سليمان طوبى لمن صحت له خطوة واحدة لا يريد بها إلا الله تعالى وكتب عمر بن الخطاب رضى الله تعالى عنه إلى أبى موسى الأشعرى من خلصت نيته كفاه الله تعالى ما بينه وبين الناس وكتب بعض الأولياء إلى أخ له أخلص النية في أعمالك يكفك القليل من العمل وقال أيوب السختيانى تخليص الن
38:83.english: These stories confirm His saying, the Exalted: 'Except Your servants among them, the purified ones (al-mukhlaseen).' For the servant (al-'abd) does not purify himself from Satan except through sincerity (al-ikhlas). Therefore, Ma'ruf al-Karkhi, may Allah have mercy on him, would strike himself and say: 'O soul (nafs), purify yourself (akhlesi) and you will be purified (tatakhlasee).' And Ya'qub al-Makfuf said: 'The purified one (al-mukhlis) is he who conceals his good deeds as he conceals his bad deeds.' And Sulaiman said: 'Blessed is he for whom one step is sound, not wanting by it except Allah, the Exalted.' And 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to Abu Musa al-Ash'ari: 'Whoever's intention (niyyah) is purified (khalasat), Allah suffices him for what is between him and the people.' And some of the friends (al-awliya') wrote to his brother: 'Purify the intention (niyyah) in your deeds, and a little of the deed will suffice you.' And Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani said: 'Purifying intentions (takhlees al-niyyat) upon the doers is more severe upon them than all the deeds.' And Mutarrif would say: 'Whoever is pure (safa), it is made pure for him; and whoever mixes (khalata), it is mixed upon him.' And one of them was seen in a dream and it was said to him: 'How did you find your deeds?' He said: 'Everything I did for Allah, I found it, even a pomegranate seed I picked from the road, and even a cat that died for us, I saw it in the scale of good deeds (hasanat). And in my cap was a thread of silk, and I saw it in the scale of bad deeds (sayi'at). And a donkey of mine had died, its value one hundred dinars, and I did not see reward for it. So I said: "The death of a cat in the scale of good deeds, and the death of a donkey not in it?" It was said to me: "Indeed, it has been directed where you sent it, for when it was said to you: 'It has died,' you said: 'May Allah curse it,' so your reward in it became void. And if you had said: 'In the path of Allah,' you would have found it in your good deeds."'
38:83.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

38:83.arabic: فمعرفة حقيقة الإخلاص والعمل به بحر عميق يغرق فيه الجميع إلا الشاذ النادر والفرد الفذوهو المستثنى في قوله تعالى إلا عبادك منهم المخلصين فليكن العبد شديد التفقد والمراقبة لهذه الدقائق وإلا التحق بأتباع الشياطين وهو لا يشعر.
38:83.english: For knowing the reality of Sincerity (Ikhlas) and acting upon it is a deep sea in which all drown except the rare and exceptional and the unique individual—he is the one excepted in His saying, the Exalted: 'Except Your servants among them, the purified ones (Al-Mukhlaseen).' So let the servant be intensely watchful and observant of these subtleties, otherwise he will join the followers of the devils without realizing it.
38:83.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

38:88.arabic: فكانت سلامة الخلق في أن يشتغلوا بالأعمال الصالحة ولا يتعرضوا لما هو خارج عن حد طاقتهم ولكن الآن قد استرخى العنان وفشا الهذيان ونزل كل جاهل على ما وافق طبعه بظن وحسبان وهو يعتقد أن ذلك علم واستيقان وأنه صفو الإيمان ويظن أن ما وقع به من حدس وتخمين علم اليقين وعين اليقين ﴿ وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ نَبَأَهُ بَعْدَ حِينٍ ﴾ وينبغي أن ينشد في هؤلاء عند كشف الغطاء: أحسنت ظنك بالأيام إذ حسنت ولم تخف سوء ما يأتي به القدر وسالمتك الليالي فاغتررت بها وعند صفو الليالي يحدث الكدر
38:88.english: The safety of the creation was in occupying themselves with righteous deeds and not exposing themselves to what is beyond the limit of their capacity. But now the reins have slackened and delirium has spread, and every ignorant person has descended upon what agrees with his nature with conjecture and supposition, and he believes that this is knowledge and certainty, and that it is the purest faith, and he thinks that what he has arrived at through guesswork and speculation is the knowledge of certainty (Ilm al-Yaqeen) and the essence of certainty (Ayn al-Yaqeen). 'And you will surely know its news after a time' (Quran 38:88). And it is fitting to recite about these people when the veil is lifted: 'You thought well of the days when they were good, and you did not fear the evil that fate brings, and the nights were safe for you, so you were deceived by them, and during the serenity of the nights, disturbance occurs.'
38:88.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

39:3.arabic: فضيلة الإخلاص قال الله تعالى (وما أمروا إلا ليعبدوا الله مخلصين له الدين) وقال (ألا لله الدين الخالص) وقال تعالى (إلا الذين تابوا وأصلحوا واعتصموا بالله وأخلصوا دينهم لله) وقال تعالى (فمن كان يرجو لقاء ربه فليعمل عملا صالحا ولا يشرك بعبادة ربه أحدا) نزلت فيمن يعمل لله ويحب أن يحمد عليه وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: (ثلاث لا يغل عليهن قلب رجل مسلم إخلاص العمل لله)[36] وعن مصعب بن سعد عن أبيه قال ظن أبى أن له فضلا على من هو دونه من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم
39:3.english: The Virtue of Sincerity (Ikhlas). Allah the Exalted said: (And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, being sincere (mukhlisīn) to Him in the religion) and He said: (Indeed, for Allah is the pure religion (al-dīn al-khālis)) and He the Exalted said: (Except those who repented and reformed and held fast to Allah and made their religion (dīn) sincere (akhlaṣū) for Allah) and He the Exalted said: (So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone). It was revealed concerning one who works for Allah and loves to be praised for it. And the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: (Three things, the heart (qalb) of a Muslim man is not treacherous regarding them: sincerity (ikhlāṣ) of the deed for Allah)[36]. And from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd from his father, he said: My father thought he had superiority over those below him from the companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, so the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: (Indeed, Allah the Mighty and Majestic gives victory to this nation through its weak ones and their supplication and their sincerity (ikhlāṣihim))[37]. And from Al-Hasan, he said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: (Allah the Exalted says: Sincerity (al-ikhlāṣ) is a secret from My secrets; I have deposited it in the heart (qalb) of whom I have loved from My servants)[38]. And 'Ali ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah honor his face, said: (Do not be concerned with the smallness of the deed and be concerned with acceptance, for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to Mu'ādh ibn Jabal: Make the deed sincere (akhliṣ), and a little of it will suffice you)[39]. And he, peace be upon him, said: (There is no servant who makes the deed sincere (yukhlis) for Allah for forty days except that the springs of wisdom (ḥikmah) appear from his heart (qalb) upon his tongue)[40]. And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: (The first to be questioned on the Day of Resurrection are three: a man whom Allah gave knowledge, so Allah says: What did you do with what you knew? He says: O my Lord, I used to stand...)
39:3.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

39:3.arabic: اذ عبدة الأوثان قالوا ﴿ ما نعبدهم الا ليقربونا إلى الله زلفى ﴾ فكانوا داخلين في اوائل ابواب التوحيد دخولا ضعيفا والمتوسطون هم الاكثرون وفيهم من تنفتح بصيرته في بعض الاحوال فتلوح له حقائق التوحيد ولكن كالبرق الخاطف لا يثبت وفيهم من يلوح له ذلك ويثبت زمانا ولكن لا يدوم والدوام فيه عزيز: لكل إلى شأو العلا حركات ولكن عزيز في الرجال ثبات
39:3.english: For the idol-worshippers said: 'We do not worship them except to bring us closer to Allah in nearness (Zulfa).' So they were entering into the beginnings of the doors of Monotheism (Tawhid) with a weak entry, and the intermediate ones are the majority. Among them are those whose insight (Basirah) opens in some states, so the realities of Monotheism (Tawhid) appear to him, but like a fleeting lightning bolt, it does not remain firm. And among them are those to whom that appears and remains for a time, but it does not endure, and endurance in it is rare: For every one there are movements toward the heights of elevation, but rare among men is steadfastness.
39:3.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

39:3.arabic: أما سمعتني أقول ألا لله الدين الخالص فإذا عرف العبد أنه بصدد هذه المطالبات والتوبيخات طالب نفسه قبل أن تطالب وأعد للسؤال جوابا وليكن الجواب صوابا فلا يبدئ ولا يعيد إلا بعد التثبت ولايحرك جفنا ولا أنمله إلا بعد التأمل
39:3.english: Have you not heard Me say: 'Indeed, for Allah is the pure religion (Al-Din Al-Khalis).' So when the servant (Al-Abd) knows that he is facing these demands and rebukes, he questions his soul (Nafs) before being questioned, and prepares an answer for the questioning, and let the answer be correct, so he does not begin nor repeat except after verification, and does not move an eyelid nor a fingertip except after contemplation.
39:3.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

39:3.arabic: وقوله تعالى ﴿ والذين اتخذوا من دونه أولياء ما نعبدهم إلا ليقربونا إلى الله زلفى ﴾ {} أي يقولون ما نعبدهم
39:3.english: And His saying, the Exalted: 'And those who take besides Him allies, we do not worship them except to bring us nearer to Allah in closeness' {} meaning they say 'we do not worship them'
39:3.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

39:7.arabic: فإن قلت: فأين الغلط في قول العصاة والفجار إن الله كريم وإنا نرجو رحمته ومغفرته، وقد قال أنا عند ظن عبدي بي فليظن بي خيراً، فما هذا إلا كلام صحيح مقبول الظاهر في القلوب؟ فاعلم أن الشيطان لا يغوي الإنسان إلا بكلام مقبول الظاهر مردود الباطن، ولولا حسن ظاهره لما انخدعت به القلوب، ولكن النبي ﭬ كشف عن ذلك فقال "الكيس من دان نفسه وعمل لما بعد الموت، والأحمق من اتبع نفسه هواها وتمنى على الله" وهذا هو التمني على الله تعالى غير الشيطان اسمه فسماه: رجاء، حتى خدع به الجهال. وقد شرح الله الرجاء فقال "إن الذي
39:7.english: If you say: Where is the error in the statement of the sinners and the wicked that Allah is generous and we hope for His mercy and forgiveness, and He has said 'I am as My servant thinks of Me, so let him think good of Me'? This is nothing but speech that is correct and acceptable in appearance to the hearts. Know that Satan does not misguide the human except with speech that is acceptable in appearance but rejected in its inner meaning, and were it not for the goodness of its appearance, the hearts would not be deceived by it. But the Prophet (peace be upon him) uncovered that by saying: 'The intelligent one is he who holds his Soul (Nafs) accountable and works for what is after death, and the fool is he who follows his Soul's (Nafs) desires and wishes upon Allah.' This is wishing upon Allah, the Exalted, but Satan changed its name and called it: hope, until he deceived the ignorant with it. And Allah has explained hope by saying: 'Indeed, those who have believed and those who have emigrated and striven in the path of Allah - those hope for the mercy of Allah.' Meaning that hope is more fitting for them, and this is because He mentioned that: 'If you disbelieve - indeed, Allah is Free from need of you. And He does not approve for His servants disbelief. And if you are grateful, He approves it for you. And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you about what you used to do. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the chests.'
39:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

39:7.arabic: ولكن المحبة والكراهية يتضادان وكلاهما لا يضادان الإرادة فرب مراد مكروه ورب مراد محبوب فالمعاصي مكروهة وهي مع الكراهة مرادة والطاعات مرادة ومزمع كونها مرادة محبوبة ومرضية أما الكفر والشر فلا نقول إنه مرضي ومحبوب بل هو مراد. وقد قال الله تعالى ولا يرضى لعباده الكفر فكيف يكون الفناء بالإضافة إلى محبة الله وكراهته كالبقاء فإنه تعالى يقول (ما ترددت في شيء كترددي في قبض روح عبدي المسلم هو يكره الموت وأنا أكره مساءته ولا بد له من الموت)[15] فقوله لا بد له من الموت إشارة إلى سبق الإرادة والتقدير المذكور
39:7.english: But love (al-Mahabbah) and hatred (al-Karahiyyah) are opposites, and both do not oppose the Will (al-Iradah). For sometimes what is willed is hated, and sometimes what is willed is loved. Sins (al-Ma'asi) are hated, yet with that hatred they are willed, and acts of obedience (al-Ta'at) are willed and intended to be willed, loved, and pleasing. As for disbelief (al-Kufr) and evil (al-Sharr), we do not say they are pleasing and loved, but they are willed. And Allah the Exalted has said: 'And He does not approve for His servants disbelief (al-Kufr).' So how can annihilation, in relation to Allah's love and hatred, be like permanence? For He the Exalted says: 'I have not hesitated in anything as I hesitate in taking the soul (al-Ruh) of My believing servant (al-'Abd al-Muslim); he hates death, and I hate to harm him, but death is inevitable for him.' [15] His statement 'death is inevitable for him' points to the precedence of the Will and the decree mentioned in His saying: 'We have decreed death among you' and in His saying: 'The Creator of death and life.' And there is no contradiction between His saying: 'We have decreed death among you' and His saying: 'and I hate to harm him,' but clarifying the truth in this requires verifying the meaning of the Will (al-Iradah), love (al-Mahabbah), and hatred (al-Karahiyyah), and explaining their realities.
39:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

39:7.arabic: الوجه الثالث أن يبقى بعده ولدا صالحا يدعو له كما ورد في الخبر أن جميع عمل ابن آدم منقطع إلا ثلاثا فذكر الولد الصالح وفي الخبر إن الأدعية تعرض على الموتى على أطباق من نور[19] وقول القائل إن الولد ربما لم يكن صالحا لا يؤثر فإنه مؤمن والصلاح هو الغالب على أولاد ذوي الدين لا سيما إذا عزم على تربيته وحمله على الصلاح وبالجملة دعاء المؤمن لأبويه مفيد برا كان أو فاجرا فهو مثاب على دعواته وحسناته فإنه من كسبه وغير مؤاخذ بسيئاته فإنه لا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى ولذلك قال تعالى ألحقنا بهم ذرياتهم وما ألتناهم من
39:7.english: The third aspect is that there remains after him a righteous child who prays for him, as mentioned in the report that all the deeds of the son of Adam are cut off except three, and among them is mentioned the righteous child. And in the report, supplications are presented to the dead on plates of light. The statement of the one who says that the child might not be righteous does not affect it, for he is a believer, and righteousness is predominant among the children of people of religion, especially if one resolves to raise him and guide him to righteousness. In summary, the supplication of a believer for his parents is beneficial, whether they are righteous or wicked; he is rewarded for his supplications and good deeds, for they are from his earnings, and he is not held accountable for their evil deeds, for no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another. Therefore, Allah the Exalted said: 'We joined their descendants with them, and We did not diminish anything from their deeds' meaning We did not reduce them from their deeds, and We made their children an increase in their good deeds.
39:7.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

39:7.arabic: وأتى عبد الملك بن مروان بأسارى ابن الأشعث فقال لرجاء بن حيوة. ما ترى؟ قال إن الله تعالى قد أعطاك ما تحب من الظفر فأعط الله ما يحب من العفو فعفا عنهم. وروي أن زياداً أخذ رجلاً من الخوارج فأفلت منه فأخذ أخاً له فقال له: إن جئت بأخيك وإلا ضربت عنقك، فقال: أرأيت إن جئتك بكتاب من أمير المؤمنين تخلي سبيلي؟ قال نعم قال فأنا آتيك بكتاب من العزيز الحكيم وأقيم عليه شاهدين إبراهيم وموسى ثم تلا "أم لم ينبأ بما في صحف موسى وإبراهيم الذي وفى أن لا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى" فقال زياد خلوا سبيله، هذا رجل قد لقن حجته،
39:7.english: And Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan was brought captives from Ibn al-Ash'ath, so he said to Raja' ibn Haywah: What do you see? He said: Indeed Allah the Exalted has given you what you love of victory, so give Allah what He loves of forgiveness. So he forgave them. And it is narrated that Ziyad took a man from the Kharijites who escaped from him, so he took his brother and said to him: If you bring me your brother, otherwise I will strike your neck. He said: What do you think if I bring you a letter from the Commander of the Faithful, will you release me? He said: Yes. He said: Then I will bring you a letter from the Mighty, the Wise and establish upon it two witnesses, Ibrahim and Musa, then he recited: "Or has he not been informed of what is in the scriptures of Musa and Ibrahim who fulfilled [his covenant] that no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another." So Ziyad said: Release him, this man has been taught his argument. And it is said written in the Gospel: Whoever seeks forgiveness for one who wronged him has defeated Satan.
39:7.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

39:7.arabic: فلا تتفكر فيما هو ممكن لغيرك بل فيما هو مخوف في حقك، فإنه لا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى، وعذاب غيرك لا يخفف شيئاً من عذابك، فإذا تفكرت في هذا الخطر كان عندك شغل شاغل عن التكبر وعن أن ترى نفسك فوق غيرك.
39:7.english: So do not contemplate what is possible for others, but rather what is feared in your own right, for indeed no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another, and the punishment of another does not alleviate anything from your punishment. If you contemplate this danger, you will have an all-engrossing preoccupation from arrogance and from seeing yourself above others.
39:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

39:9.arabic: وقال تعالى ﴿ إنما يتذكر أولوا الألباب ﴾ {} فالذي آثر غرور الدنيا على نعيم الآخرة فليس من ذوي الألباب ولذلك لا تنكشف له أسرار الكتاب.
39:9.english: And the Exalted said: 'Only those possessing intellects (أولوا الألباب) take heed.' So the one who prefers the deception (غرور) of this world over the bliss (نعيم) of the Hereafter is not among those possessing intellects (ذوي الألباب), and therefore the secrets (أسرار) of the Book are not unveiled to him.
39:9.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

39:9.arabic: السبب السابع: التكبر بالورع والعبادة، وذلك أيضاً فتنة عظيمة على العباد، وسبيله أن يلزم قلبه التواضع لسائر العباد وهو أن يعلم أن من يتقدم عليه بالعلم لا ينبغي أن يتكبر عليه كيفما كان "لما عرفه من فضيلة العلم، وقد قال تعالى "هل يستوي الذين يعلمون والذين لا يعلمون" وقال ﭬ "فضل العالم على العابد كفضلي على أدنى رجل من أصحابي"[80] إلى غير ذلك مما ورد في فضل العلم.
39:9.english: The seventh cause: Arrogance through piety and worship, and that is also a great trial upon the worshippers, and its way is that he must oblige his heart (Qalb) to humility toward all worshippers, which is that he knows that whoever precedes him in knowledge should not be arrogantly looked down upon in any way "because of what he recognizes from the virtue of knowledge, and Allah the Exalted has said: 'Are those who know equal to those who do not know?' and the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'The superiority of the knowledgeable one over the worshipper is like my superiority over the lowest man among my companions' [80] and other than that which has come regarding the virtue of knowledge.
39:9.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

39:9.arabic: أما من الايات فقوله تعالى: ﴿ إن ربك يعلم أنك تقوم أدنى من ثلثي الليل ﴾ {} الاية وقوله تعالى: ﴿ إن ناشئة الليل هي أشد وطأ وأقوم قيلا ﴾ {} وقوله سبحانه وتعالى: ﴿ تتجافى جنوبهم عن المضاجع ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ أمن هو قانت آناء الليل ﴾ {} الآية وقوله عز وجل: ﴿ والذين يبيتون لربهم سجدا وقياما ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ واستعينوا بالصبر والصلاة ﴾ {} قيل هي قيام الليل يستعان بالصبر عليه على مجاهدة النفس.
39:9.english: As for from the verses, His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand (in prayer) for nearly two-thirds of the night' (Quran 73:20) the verse, and His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, the rising (Nashia) of the night is more intense in tread and more upright in speech' (Quran 73:6), and His saying, the Exalted and Majestic: 'Their sides forsake (Tatajafa) their beds' (Quran 32:16), and His saying, the Exalted: 'Is one who is devoutly obedient (Qanit) during periods of the night' (Quran 39:9) the verse, and His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And those who spend the night for their Lord prostrating and standing' (Quran 25:64), and His saying, the Exalted: 'And seek help through patience and prayer' (Quran 2:45). It is said: it is the standing (Qiyam) of the night; help is sought through patience upon it for striving against the Soul (Nafs).
39:9.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

39:9.arabic: شواهدها من القرآن قوله عز وجل: ﴿شهد الله أنه لا إله إلا هو والملائكة وأولو العلم قائما بالقسط﴾ (آل عمران 3: 18) فانظر كيف بدأ سبحانه وتعالى بنفسه وثنى بالملائكة وثلث بأهل العلم وناهيك بهذا شرفا وفضلا وجلاء ونبلا وقال الله تعالى: ﴿يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات﴾ (المجادلة: 11) قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: للعلماء درجات فوق المؤمنين بسبعمائة درجة ما بين الدرجتين مسيرة خمسمائة عام. وقال عز وجل: ﴿قل هل يستوي الذين يعلمون والذين لا يعلمون﴾ وقال تعالى: ﴿إنما يخشى الله من عباده الع
39:9.english: Its evidences from the Quran are His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and [so do] the angels and those of knowledge - [that He is] maintaining [creation] in justice' (Al Imran 3:18). So observe how He, the Exalted, began with Himself, then mentioned the angels, and thirdly mentioned the people of knowledge - and what honor, excellence, clarity, and nobility is greater than this! And Allah, the Exalted, says: 'Allah will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge by degrees' (Al-Mujadilah: 11). Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: 'For the scholars are degrees above the believers by seven hundred degrees, the distance between each two degrees being a journey of five hundred years.' And the Mighty and Majestic says: 'Say, "Are those who know equal to those who do not know?"' And He, the Exalted, says: 'Only those fear Allah from among His servants who are knowledgeable.' And He, the Exalted, says: 'Say, "Sufficient is Allah as Witness between me and you, and [by] whoever has knowledge of the Scripture."' And He, the Exalted, says: 'Said one who had knowledge from the Scripture, "I will bring it to you."' indicating that he was able through the power of knowledge. And the Mighty and Majestic says: 'But those who were given knowledge said, "Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for he who believes and does righteousness."' clarifying that the greatness of the Hereafter's value is known through knowledge. And He, the Exalted, says: 'And these examples We present to the people, but none will understand them except those of knowledge.' And He, the Exalted, says: 'And if they had referred it back to the Messenger or to those of authority among them, then the ones who [can] draw correct conclusions from it would have known about it.' He referred its ruling in matters to their deduction and equated their rank with the rank of the prophets in uncovering Allah's ruling. And it is said regarding His saying, the Exalted: 'O children of Adam, We have bestowed upon you clothing to conceal your private parts' meaning knowledge, 'and adornment' meaning certainty (Yaqin), 'but the clothing of righteousness' meaning modesty (Haya). And the Mighty and Majestic says: 'And We had certainly brought them a Book which We detailed by knowledge.' And He, the Exalted, says: 'So We will surely relate [their deeds] to them with knowledge.' And the Mighty and Majestic says: 'Rather, it is distinct verses [preserved] in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge.' And He, the Exalted, says: 'He created man, [and] taught him eloquence.' And He mentioned that in the context of favor.
39:9.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Book of Knowledge'

39:9.arabic: ثم انظر كيف وصف الفائزين من عباده وبماذا وصفهم فقال تعالى: ﴿ أمن هو قانت آناء الليل ساجدا وقائما يحذر الآخرة ويرجو رحمة ربه قل هل يستوي الذين يعلمون والذين لا يعلمون ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ تتجافى جنوبهم عن المضاجع يدعون ربهم خوفا وطمعا ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل: ﴿ والذين يبيتون لربهم سجدا وقياما ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل: ﴿ كانوا قليلا من الليل ما يهجعون وبالأسحار هم يستغفرون ﴾ {}
39:9.english: Then look at how He described the successful ones from His servants and with what He described them, so He the Exalted said: 'Is one who is devoutly obedient (Qānit) during periods of the night, prostrating and standing [in prayer], fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord? Say, "Are those who know equal to those who do not know?"' And He the Exalted said: 'Their sides forsake their beds, they supplicate their Lord in fear (Khawf) and hope (Tamaʿ).' And He the Mighty and Majestic said: 'And those who spend [part of] the night to their Lord prostrating and standing.' And He the Mighty and Majestic said: 'They used to sleep but little of the night, and in the hours before dawn they would ask forgiveness.'
39:9.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

39:10.arabic: وقال عمر بن عبد العزيز رحمه الله في خطبته ما أنعم الله على عبد نعمة فانتزعها منه وعوضه منها الصبر الا كان ما عوضه منها أفضل مما انتزع منه وقرا ﴿ انما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب ﴾ {} وسئل فضيل عن الصبر، فقال: هو الرضا بقضاء الله قيل: وكيف ذلك؟ قال: الراضي لا يتمنى فوق منزلته، وقيل حبس الشبلى رحمة الله في المارستان فدخل عليه جماعة فقال: من أنتم؟ قالوا: أحباؤك جاءوك زائرين فأخذ يرميهم بالحجاره فأخذوا يهربون فقال لو كنتم أحبائي لصبرتم على بلائي، وكان بعض العارفين في جيبه رقعة يخرجها كل ساعة ويطال
39:10.english: And Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his sermon: 'Allah has not bestowed a blessing upon a servant then withdrawn it from him and compensated him with Patience (Sabr) except that what He compensated him with was better than what He withdrew from him.' And he recited: 'Indeed, the Patient ones (As-Sabirun) will be given their reward without account.' And Fudayl was asked about Patience (Sabr), so he said: 'It is being Pleased (Rida) with the Decree (Qada) of Allah.' It was said: 'And how is that?' He said: 'The Pleased one (Ar-Radi) does not wish for more than his station.' And it was said: Al-Shibli, may Allah have mercy on him, was confined in the hospital, and a group entered upon him, so he said: 'Who are you?' They said: 'Your lovers have come to visit you.' So he began throwing stones at them, and they began fleeing. So he said: 'If you were my lovers, you would have been Patient (Sabirun) with my affliction.' And some of the Knowers (Al-Arifun) had in his pocket a note that he would take out every hour and look at it, and in it was: 'And be Patient (Wasbir) for the Judgment (Hukm) of your Lord, for indeed you are in Our Eyes.' And it is said that a woman, Fatih al-Mawsili, stumbled and her nail was cut off, so she laughed. So it was said to her: 'Do you not feel the pain?' So she said: 'The delight of its reward has removed from my Heart (Qalb) the bitterness of its pain.' And Dawud said to Sulayman, peace be upon them both: 'The God-consciousness (Taqwa) of the believer is known by three things: good Reliance (Tawakkul) in what has not been attained, good Pleasure (Rida) in what has been attained, and good Patience (Sabr) in what has passed.'
39:10.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

39:10.arabic: فنقول: هذا المقام في البيان يأبى البحث والتفصيل ومقتضاه النظر إلى الظاهر المفهوم من موارد الشرع وذلك يقتضى تفضيل الصبر فإن الشكر وإن وردت أخبار كثيرة في فضله فإذا أضيف إليه ما ورد في فضيلة الصبر كانت فضائل الصبر أكثر بل فيه ألفاظ صريحة في التفضيل كقوله ﭬ: (من أفضل ما أوتيتم اليقين وعزيمة الصبر[113]) وفي الخبر: (يؤتي بأشكر أهل الأرض فيجزيه الله جزاء الشاكرين ويؤتي بأصبر أهل الأرض فيقال له: أما ترضى أن يجزيك كما جزينا هذا الشاكر، فيقول نعم يا رب فيقول الله تعالى: كلا أنعمت عليه فشكر وابتليتك فصبرت
39:10.english: We say: This station in explanation rejects investigation and detail, and its requirement is looking at the apparent understood from the sources of the Sharia, and that necessitates preferring Patience (Sabr).
