39:67.arabic: والمعنى الثاني أن ينزله على نفسه في حق الله تعالى فإنه إذا تفكر فمعرفته جهل إذ ما قدروا الله حق قدره وطاعته رياء إذ لا يتقي الله حق تقاته وحبه معلول إذ لا يدع شهوة من شهواته في حبه ومن أراد الله به خيرا بصره بعيوب نفسه فيرى مصداق هذا البيت في نفسه وإن كان على المرتبة بالإضافة إلى الغافلين ولذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لا أحصى ثناء عليك أنت كما أثنيت على نفسك حديث لا أحصي ثناء عليك أنت كما أثنيت على نفسك رواه مسلم وقد تقدم وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إني لاستغفر الله في اليوم والليلة سبعين مرة حديث إن
39:67.english: The second meaning is that he applies it to himself regarding Allah (God) the Exalted, for when he reflects, his knowledge is ignorance since 'what they have not measured Allah (God) with His true measure' (Quran 39:67), and his obedience is hypocrisy since he does not fear Allah (God) with His true fear, and his love is caused since he does not abandon a desire from his desires in his love. And whoever Allah (God) wills good for, He shows him the defects of his Soul (Nafs), so he sees the truth of this verse in himself, even if it is at the level relative to the heedless. Therefore, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'I cannot enumerate praise upon You; You are as You have praised Yourself' (hadith: I cannot enumerate praise upon You; You are as You have praised Yourself, narrated by Muslim, and it preceded). And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, I seek forgiveness from Allah (God) seventy times a day and night' (hadith: Indeed, I seek forgiveness from Allah (God) seventy times a day and night, preceded in the second chapter of the Remembrances (Dhikr)). And his seeking forgiveness was only about states that are degrees after relative to what is after them, and if they are closeness relative to what is before them, then there is no closeness except that beyond it remains closeness without end, since the path of journeying (Suluk) to Allah (God) the Exalted is infinite, and reaching the utmost degrees of closeness is impossible.
39:67.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

39:68.arabic: وتفكر أولا فيما يقرع سمع سكان القبور من شدة نفخ الصور فإنها صيحة واحدة تنفرج بها القبور عن رءوس الموتى فيثورون دفعة واحدة فتوهم نفسك وقد وثبت متغيرا وجهك مغبرا بدنك من فرقك إلى قدمك من تراب قبرك مبهوتا من شدة الصعقة شاخص العين نحو النداء وقد ثار الخلق ثورة واحدة من القبور التي طال فيها بلاؤهم وقد أزعجهم الفزع والرعب مضافا إلى ما كان عندهم من الهموم والغموم وشدة الانتظار لعاقبة الأمر كما قال تعالى: ﴿ ونفخ فى الصور فصعق من فى السموات ومن فى الأرض إلا من شاء الله ثم نفخ فيه أخرى فإذا هم قيام ينظرون
39:68.english: And contemplate first in what strikes the hearing of the inhabitants of the graves from the intensity of the blowing of the Trumpet (Al-Sur), for it is a single cry by which the graves split open from the heads of the dead, and they rise up all at once. So imagine yourself having leaped up, your face altered, your body dust-covered from your scalp to your feet from the dust of your grave, stunned from the intensity of the blow (Al-Sa'qa), your eye fixed toward the call. And the creation has risen up in a single uprising from the graves in which their tribulation (Bala') has been prolonged, and the terror (Faza') and dread (Ra'b) has disturbed them, added to what was with them of sorrows (Humum) and griefs (Ghumum) and intense waiting for the outcome of the matter, as Allah the Exalted said: 'And the Trumpet (Al-Sur) will be blown, and all who are in the heavens and all who are on the earth will fall dead except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on.' And Allah the Exalted said: 'And when the Trumpet (Al-Naqur) is blown, that Day will be a difficult day for the disbelievers; not easy.' And Allah the Exalted said: 'And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?" They do not await except one blast which will seize them while they are disputing. And they will not be able to make a testament, nor to their people will they return. And the Trumpet (Al-Sur) will be blown, and at once from the graves to their Lord they will hasten. They will say, "O woe to us! Who has raised us from our sleeping place? This is what the Most Merciful had promised, and the messengers told the truth."' So if there were not before the dead except the horror of that blowing, it would be worthy of being feared, for it is a blowing and a cry by which those in the heavens and the earth are struck dead (Yus'aq), meaning they die by it except whom Allah wills, and that is some of the angels. And for that reason, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'How can I be at ease when the possessor of the Trumpet (Sahib Al-Sur) has taken the horn (Al-Qarn) into his mouth and bent his forehead and inclined his ear, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow?' Maqatil said: The Trumpet (Al-Sur) is the horn (Al-Qarn), and that is because Israfil (upon him be peace) is placing his mouth on the horn like the form of a trumpet, and the circle of the head of the horn is like the expanse of the heavens and the earth, and he is fixing his gaze toward the Throne (Al-'Arsh), waiting for when he will be commanded to blow the first blowing. So when he blows, those in the heavens and the earth are struck dead (Yus'aq), meaning every animal dies from the intensity of the terror (Faza') except whom Allah wills, and that is Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil, and the Angel of Death (Malak Al-Mawt). Then the Angel of Death is commanded to take the soul (Ruh) of Jibril, then
39:68.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

39:68.arabic: فلو لم يكن بين يدي الموتي إلا هول تلك النفخة لكان ذلك جديرا بأن يتقى فإنها نفخة وصيحة يصعق بها من فى السموات والأرض يعنى يموتون بها إلا من شاء الله وهو بعض الملائكة ولذلك قال رسول الله ﭬ: (كيف أنعم وصاحب الصور قد التقم القرن وحنى الجبهة وأصغى بالأذن متى يؤمر فينفخ[144]) قال مقاتل: الصور هو القرن وذلك أن إسرافيل عليه السلام واضع فاه على القرن كهيئة البوق ودائرة رأس القرن كعرض السموات والأرض وهو شاخص بصره نحو العرش ينتظر متى يؤمر فينفخ النفخة الأولى فإذا نفخ صعق من فى السموات والأرض أى مات كل حيوا
39:68.english: If there were nothing before the dead except the terror of that blowing, it would be worthy of being feared, for it is a blowing and a cry by which those in the heavens and the earth are struck unconscious, meaning they die by it, except whom Allah wills, and that is some of the angels. Therefore, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'How can I be at ease when the possessor of the Trumpet (Soor) has taken the Horn (Qarn) into his mouth, lowered his forehead, and inclined his ear, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow?' [144] Maqatil said: The Trumpet (Soor) is the Horn (Qarn), and that Israfil (upon him be peace) is placing his mouth on the Horn like a trumpet, and the circumference of the head of the Horn is like the expanse of the heavens and the earth, and he is fixing his gaze toward the Throne, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow the first blowing. When he blows, those in the heavens and the earth are struck unconscious, meaning every living creature dies from the intensity of the terror, except whom Allah wills, and that is Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil, and the Angel of Death (Malak al-Mawt). Then the Angel of Death is commanded to take the soul (Ruh) of Jibril, then the soul (Ruh) of Mika'il, then the soul (Ruh) of Israfil, then the Angel of Death is commanded and he dies. Then the creation remains after the first blowing in the Barzakh (the intermediate state) for forty years. Then Allah the Exalted revives Israfil and commands him to blow the second blowing, and that is His saying the Exalted: 'Then it will be blown into it another time, and behold, they are standing, looking.' On their feet, looking at the Resurrection (al-Ba'th). And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'When I was sent, I was sent to the possessor of the Trumpet (Soor), and he inclined it to his mouth, and advanced one leg and delayed another, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow. Indeed, fear the blowing!' [145]
39:68.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

39:68.arabic: رع سمع سكان القبور من شدة نفخ الصور فإنها صيحة واحدة تنفرج بها القبور عن رءوس الموتي فيثورون دفعة واحدة فتوهم نفسك وقد وثبت متغيرا وجهك مغبرا بدنك من فرقك إلى قدمك من تراب قبرك مبهوتا من شدة الصعقة شاخص العين نحو النداء وقد ثار الخلق ثورة واحدة من القبور التى طال فيها بلاؤهم وقد أزعجهم الفزع والرعب مضافا إلى ما كان عندهم من الهموم والغموم وشدة الانتظار لعاقبة الأمر كما قال تعالى: ﴿ ونفخ فى الصور فصعق من فى السموات ومن فى الأرض إلا من شاء الله ثم نفخ فيه أخرى فإذا هم قيام ينظرون ﴾ {} وقال تعالى:
39:68.english: The inhabitants of the graves hear from the intensity of the blowing of the Trumpet (Al-Sur), for it is a single cry by which the graves split open from the heads of the dead, and they rise up all at once. So imagine yourself having leaped up, your face altered, your body dusty from your hair to your feet from the dust of your grave, stunned from the intensity of the blow, your eyes fixed toward the call. And the creation has risen up in a single uprising from the graves in which their tribulation has been prolonged, and alarm and terror have disturbed them, added to what they had of sorrows, griefs, and intense waiting for the outcome of the matter, as Allah the Exalted said: 'And the Trumpet (Al-Sur) will be blown, and all who are in the heavens and all who are on the earth will fall dead except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on.' And Allah the Exalted said: 'And when the Trumpet (Al-Naqur) is blown, that Day will be a difficult day for the disbelievers; not easy.' And Allah the Exalted said: 'And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?" They do not await except one blast which will seize them while they are disputing. And they will not be able to make a testament, nor to their people can they return. And the Trumpet (Al-Sur) will be blown, and at once from the graves to their Lord they will hasten. They will say, "O woe to us! Who has raised us up from our sleeping place?" [The reply will be], "This is what the Most Merciful had promised, and the messengers told the truth."' So if there were not before the dead except the terror of that blowing, it would be worthy of being feared, for it is a blowing and a cry by which those in the heavens and the earth are struck dead, meaning they die by it, except whom Allah wills, and that is some of the angels. And for that reason, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'How can I be at ease when the possessor of the Trumpet (Al-Sur) has taken the horn in his mouth, bowed his forehead, and inclined his ear, waiting for when he is commanded to blow?' Maqatil said: The Trumpet (Al-Sur) is the horn, and that is because Israfil (upon him be peace) places his mouth on the horn like the form of a trumpet, and the circle of the head of the horn is like the expanse of the heavens and the earth, and he is fixing his gaze toward the Throne, waiting for when he is commanded to blow the first blowing. And when he blows, those in the heavens and the earth are struck dead, meaning every living creature dies from the intensity of the alarm, except whom Allah wills, and that is Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil, and the Angel of Death (Malak al-Mawt). Then the Angel of Death is commanded to take the soul (Ruh) of Jibril, then the soul (Ruh) of Mika'il, then the soul (Ruh) of Israfil, then the Angel of Death is commanded and he dies. Then the creation remains after the first blowing in the Intermediate State (Al-Barzakh) for forty years. Then Allah the Exalted revives Israfil and commands him to blow the second time, and that is His saying the Exalted: 'Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on.' On their feet, looking at the Resurrection (Al-Ba'th). And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'When I was sent, I was sent to the possessor of the Trumpet (Al-Sur), and he brought it to his mouth, advanced one foot and delayed another, waiting for when he is commanded to blow. So fear the blowing.' So reflect on the creatures and their humiliation, brokenness, and submission at the resurrection, fearing from this blow and waiting for what is decreed upon them of happiness or wretchedness, and
39:68.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

39:69.arabic: وقبل الابتداء بالسؤال يظهر نور العرش ﴿ وأشرقت الأرض بنور ربها ﴾ {} وأيقن كل عبد بإقبال الجبار لمساءلة العباد وظن كل واحد أنه ما يراه أحد سواه وأنه المأخوذ بالأخذ والسؤال دون من عداه فيقول الجبار سبحانه وتعالى عند ذلك: يا جبريل ائتى بالنار فيجىء لها جبريل ويقول يا جهنم أجيبي خالقك ومليكك فيصادفها جبريل على غيظها وغضبها فلم يلبث بعد ندائها أن ثارت وفارت وزفرت إلى الخلائق وشهقت وسمع الخلائق تغيظها وزفيرها وانتهضت خزنتها متوثبة إلى الخلائق غضبا على من عصى الله تعالى وخالف أمره فأخطر ببالك وأحضر فى ق
39:69.english: And before the beginning of the questioning, the light of the Throne appears: 'And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord' (Quran 39:69). And every servant (Abd) became certain of the approach of the Almighty (Al-Jabbar) for questioning the servants, and each one thought that no one sees him except Him and that he is the one taken for taking and questioning, not anyone else. Then the Almighty (Al-Jabbar), glorified and exalted, says at that time: 'O Gabriel, bring the Fire.' So Gabriel comes for it and says: 'O Hell, respond to your Creator and your Sovereign.' Gabriel finds it in its rage and anger, and it did not linger after his call before it erupted, boiled, and snorted towards the creatures, and it gasped, and the creatures heard its rage and snorting, and its keepers rose up, leaping towards the creatures in anger at those who disobeyed Allah, exalted is He, and opposed His command. So imagine in your mind and present in your heart (Qalb) the state of the hearts (Qulub) of the servants, which have filled with terror and dread, so they fell prostrate on their knees and turned away fleeing: 'On the Day you will see every nation kneeling' (Quran 45:28). And some of them fell on their faces, prostrate, and the sinners and wrongdoers call out with woe and ruin, and the truthful ones call out: 'Myself, myself!' While they are like that, the people snorted its second snort, so their fear multiplied and their strengths weakened, and they thought they were being taken. Then it snorted the third time, so the creatures fell on their faces and stared with their eyes, looking from a hidden, humble corner, and at that, the hearts (Qulub) of the wrongdoers were crushed, reaching the throats, suppressing, and the minds (Aql) of the fortunate and the wretched all were bewildered. And after that, Allah, exalted is He, turned to the messengers and said: 'What did you answer?' So when they saw...
39:69.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Book of Repentance'

39:69.arabic: ثم تبلغك صيحة الحشر ونفخ الصور وقيام الجبار لفصل قضاء الخلائق وخلاء الأرض من أهلها والسماوات من سكانها فباحت الأسرار وأسعرت النار ووضعت الموازين وجىء بالنبيين والشهداء وقضى بينهم بالحق وقيل الحمد لله رب العالمين
39:69.english: Then will reach you the cry of the Gathering and the blowing of the Horn and the rising of the Almighty for the separation of the judgment of the creatures and the emptying of the Earth from its inhabitants and the heavens from their dwellers, so the secrets will be exposed and the Fire will be kindled and the Scales will be placed and the Prophets and the Witnesses will be brought and judgment will be passed between them with the Truth and it will be said: 'Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds'.
39:69.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

39:70.arabic: وستجد كل نفس ما عملت من سوء أو خير محضرا عند الله ولو في فلتة خاطر أو فلتة ناظر من غير ظلم وجور فما الله بظلام للعبيد
39:70.english: And every soul (Nafs) will find what it has done of evil or good present before Allah (Allah), even if in a fleeting thought (Khatir) or a fleeting glance (Nazir) without oppression (Zulm) and injustice (Jawr), for Allah (Allah) is not an oppressor (Zallam) to the servants (Ibad).
39:70.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

39:72.arabic: والأخلاق الذميمة متلازمة والبعض منها داع إلى البعض لا محالة. وشر أنواع الكبر ما يمنع من استفادة العلم وقبول الحق والانقياد له وفيه وردت الآيات التي فيها ذم الكبر والمتكبرين قال الله تعالى "والملائكة باسطو أيديهم" إلى قوله "وكنتم عن آياته تستكبرون" ثم قال "ادخلوا أبواب جهنم خالدين فيها فبئس مثوى المتكبرين" ثم أخبر أن أشد أهل النار عذاباً أشدهم عتياً على الله تعالى فقال "ثم لننزعن من كل شبعة أيهم أشد على الرحمن عتياً" وقال تعالى "فالذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة قلوبهم منكرة وهم مستكبرون" وقال عز وجل "يقو
39:72.english: And the blameworthy character traits are interconnected, and some of them inevitably lead to others. The worst type of arrogance (Kibr) is what prevents benefiting from knowledge and accepting the truth and submitting to it, and in this context came the verses that contain condemnation of arrogance (Kibr) and the arrogant ones (Mutakabbirun). Allah the Exalted said: "And the angels will be spreading their hands" up to His saying: "and you were arrogant (Tastakbirun) towards His signs." Then He said: "Enter the gates of Hell (Jahannam), abiding therein. So wretched is the abode of the arrogant (Mutakabbirun)." Then He informed that the most severely punished people of the Fire (Nar) are those most insolent (Atiyyan) against Allah the Exalted, so He said: "Then We will surely extract from every sect those of them who were most insolent (Atiyyan) against the Most Merciful." And He the Exalted said: "So those who do not believe in the Hereafter (Akhirah) - their hearts (Qulub) are denying, and they are arrogant (Mustakbirun)." And He the Mighty and Majestic said: "Those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant (Istakbaru): 'If not for you, we would have been believers.'" And He the Exalted said: "Indeed, those who are arrogant (Yastakbirun) towards My worship will enter Hell (Jahannam) debased." And He the Exalted said: "I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant (Yatakabbarun) on the earth without right." It is said in the interpretation (Tafsir): I will lift the understanding of the Quran from their hearts (Qulub), and in some interpretations (Tafasir): I will veil their hearts (Qulub) from the dominion (Malakut). And Ibn Juraij said: I will turn them away from reflecting upon them and taking admonition from them. And therefore, Jesus (Al-Masih) peace be upon him said: Indeed, crops grow in the plain and do not grow on the hard rock, likewise wisdom (Hikmah) works in the heart (Qalb) of the humble (Mutawadi') and does not work in the heart (Qalb) of the arrogant (Mutakabbir). Do you not see that whoever raises his head to the ceiling injures it, and whoever lowers it is shaded and sheltered. So this is a parable he struck for the arrogant ones (Mutakabbirun) and how they are deprived of wisdom (Hikmah). And therefore, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned the denial of truth as part of the definition of arrogance (Kibr) and uncovering its reality and said: "Whoever belittles the truth and looks down upon people."
39:72.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

39:73.arabic: وعن عاصم بن ضمرة عن على كرم الله وجهه أنه ذكر النار فعظم أمرها ذكرا لا أحفظه ثم قال ﴿ وسيق الذين اتقوا ربهم إلى الجنة زمرا ﴾ {} حتى إذا انتهوا إلى باب من أبوابها وجدوا عنده شجرة يخرج من تحت ساقها عينان تجريان فعمدوا إلى إحداهما كما أمروا به فشربوا منها فأذهبت ما فى بطونهم من أذى أو بأس ثم عمدوا إلى الأخرى فتطهروا منها فجرت عليهم نضرة النعيم فلم تتغير أشعارهم بعدها أبدا ولا تشعث رءوسهم كأنما دهنوا بالدهان ثم انتهوا إلى الجنة فقال لهم خزنتها سلام عليكم طبتم فادخلوها خالدين ثم تلقاهم الولدان يطيفون
39:73.english: And from Asim bin Damrah from Ali, may God honor his face, that he mentioned the Fire and magnified its matter with a mention I do not memorize, then he said: 'And those who feared (ittaqaw) their Lord will be led to the Garden in groups' until when they reached a gate from its gates, they found near it a tree from under its trunk two springs flowing. So they proceeded to one of them as they were commanded and drank from it, and it removed what was in their bellies of harm or distress. Then they proceeded to the other and purified themselves from it, and the freshness of bliss flowed upon them, so their hairs never changed after that forever, nor did their heads become disheveled as if they were anointed with ointment. Then they reached the Garden, and its keepers said to them: 'Peace be upon you, you have done well, so enter it abiding forever.' Then the youths meet them, circulating around them as the youths of the people of the world circulate around the beloved who comes to them from an absence, saying to him: 'Rejoice, God has prepared for you such and such honor,' as he said. Then a boy from those youths speaks to some of his wives from the wide-eyed maidens (al-hoor al-ʿeen) and says: 'So-and-so has come by the name he was called by in the world.' She says: 'You saw him?' He says: 'I saw him, and he is behind me.' Joy overwhelms her until she rises to the threshold of its gate. When he reaches his dwelling, he looks at the foundation of its structure, and behold, pearls upon it, a palace red, green, and yellow from every color. Then he raises his head and looks at its ceiling, and behold, like lightning, and were it not that God the Exalted had decreed it, it would have pained him to take away his sight. Then he lowers his head, and behold, his wives 'and cups placed and cushions arranged and carpets spread.' Then he reclined and said: 'Praise be to God who guided us to this, and we would not have been guided had God not guided us.' Then a caller calls out: 'You live, so you never die; you settle, so you never depart; you are healthy, so you never become ill.'
39:73.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

39:74.arabic: وقد جعل الله الشكر مفتاح كلام أهل الجنة فقال تعالى: ﴿ وقالوا الحمد لله الذي صدقنا وعده ﴾ {} وقال: ﴿ وآخر دعواهم ان الحمد لله رب العالمين ﴾ {}.
39:74.english: And Allah has made thankfulness (Shukr) the key to the speech of the people of Paradise, so He, the Exalted, said: 'And they said: "All praise is due to Allah Who has fulfilled His promise to us and made us inherit the earth; we may settle in Paradise wherever we will. And excellent is the reward of the workers."' And He said: 'And the last of their call will be, "Praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds."'
39:74.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

39:75.arabic: الثاني شعر الشارب وقد قال ﭬ: (قصوا الشارب) وفي لفظ آخر (جزوا الشوارب) وفي لفظ آخر (حفوا الشوارب وأعفوا اللحى[62]) أي اجعلوها حفاف الشفة أي حولها وحفاف الشيء حوله ومنه ﴿ وترى الملائكة حافين من حول العرش ﴾ {} وفي لفظ آخر احفوا وهذا يشعر بالاستئصال وقوله حفوا يدل على ما دون ذلك
39:75.english: The second: The hair of the mustache. And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Trim the mustache.' In another wording: 'Cut the mustaches.' And in another wording: 'Make the mustaches short (hufū al-shawārib) and let the beards grow (a'fū al-liḥā).' That is, make them the edge (ḥafāf) of the lip, meaning around it, and the edge (ḥafāf) of a thing is its surrounding. And from this is: 'And you will see the angels surrounding (ḥāffīn) from around the Throne.' And in another wording: 'Make them short (iḥfū).' And this indicates complete removal, and his saying 'make them short (ḥufū)' indicates less than that.
39:75.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Mysteries of Purity'

39:75.arabic: فباحت الأسرار وأسعرت النار ووضعت الموازين وجىء بالنبيين والشهداء وقضى بينهم بالحق وقيل الحمد لله رب العالمين فكم من مفتضح ومستور وكم من هالك وناج وكم من معذب ومرحوم فيا ليت شعري مالى وحالك يومئذ ففي هذا ما هدم اللذات وأسلى عن الشهوات وقصر عن الأمل وأيقظ النائمين وحذر الغافلين
39:75.english: Then the secrets were revealed, and the Fire was kindled, and the Scales were set up, and the Prophets and the witnesses were brought, and judgment was passed between them with truth, and it was said: 'Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.' So how many will be exposed and concealed, and how many will perish and be saved, and how many will be tormented and shown mercy? Oh, I wonder what my state and your state will be on that day. For in this is what demolishes pleasures, consoles from desires, shortens hope, awakens the sleepers, and warns the heedless.
39:75.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Book of Repentance'

40:1.arabic: و في حديث عمر وقد سأل عن أخ كان آخاه فخرج إلى الشام فسأل عنه بعض من قدم عليه وقال ما فعل أخي قال ذلك أخو الشيطان قال مه قال إنه قارف الكبائر حتى وقع في الخمر قال إذا أردت الخروج فآذني فكتب عند خروجه إليه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم حم تنزيل الكتاب من الله العزيز العليم غافر الذنب وقابل التوب شديد العقاب الآية ثم عاتبه تحت ذلك وعذله فلما قرأ الكتاب بكى و قال صدق الله ونصح لي عمر فتاب ورجع
40:1.english: And in the narration of Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), when he asked about a brother whom he had taken as a brother, and he had gone out to Syria, he asked about him from some of those who had arrived and said: 'What has my brother done?' He said: 'That is the brother of Satan.' He said: 'Enough!' He said: 'He has committed major sins until he fell into wine.' He said: 'When you intend to depart, inform me.' So he wrote at his departure to him: 'In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Ha Mim. The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Knowing, Forgiver of sin and Acceptor of repentance, severe in punishment...' the verse. Then he reproached him beneath that and admonished him. When he read the letter, he wept and said: 'Allah has spoken the truth, and Umar has advised me.' So he repented and returned.
40:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

40:1.arabic: الثاني: الاستعانة على تغيير المنكر ورد العاصي إلى منهج الصلاح، كما روي أن عمر رضي الله عنه مر على عثمان -وقيل على طلحة- رضي الله عنه فسلم عليه فلم يرد السلام. فذهب إلى أبي بكر رضي الله عنه فذكر له ذلك، فجاء أبو بكر إليه ليصلح ذلك ولم يكن ذلك غيبة عندهم. وكذلك لما بلغ عمر رضي الله عنه أن أبا جندل قا عاقر الخمر بالشام كتب إليه "بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم حم تنزيل الكتاب من الله العزيز العليم غافر الذنب وقابل التوب شديد العقاب" الآية فتاب، ولم ير ذلك عمر ممن أبلغه غيبة، إذ كان قصده أن ينكر عليه ذلك فين
40:1.english: Second: Seeking assistance to change the wrong (al-Munkar) and return the disobedient (al-'Asi) to the path of righteousness (al-Salah), as it is narrated that 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) passed by 'Uthman - or it is said Talha - (may Allah be pleased with him) and greeted him, but he did not return the greeting. So he went to Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) and mentioned that to him, and Abu Bakr came to him to rectify that, and that was not considered backbiting (Ghibah) among them. Likewise, when it reached 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) that Abu Jandal was a persistent drinker of wine in Syria, he wrote to him: "In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Ha, Meem. The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Knowing, the Forgiver of sin, the Acceptor of repentance, severe in punishment" the verse, so he repented, and 'Umar did not consider that from the one who informed him as backbiting (Ghibah), since his intention (Qasd) was to censure him for that, so his advice (Nush) benefits him what the advice of others does not benefit him, and the permissibility of this is with the correct intention (al-Qasd al-Sahih); if that is not the intended purpose (al-Maqsud), it was forbidden (Haram).
40:1.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

40:3.arabic: وعند هذا واجب على العبد أن يستعمل الخوف فيخوف نفسه بغضب الله وعظيم عقابه ويقول: إنه مع أنه غافر الذنب وقابل التوب شديد العقاب، وإنه مع أنه كريم خلد الكفار في النار أبد الآباد، مع أنه لم يضره كفرهم، بل سلط العذاب والمحن والأمراض والعلل والفقر والجوع على جملة من عباده في الدنيا وهو قادر على إزالتها، فمن هذه سنته في عباده وقد خوفني عقابه فكيف لا أخافه وكيف أغتر به؟
40:3.english: And at this point, it is obligatory upon the servant (Abd) to employ fear (Khauf) and frighten himself with the anger of Allah and His great punishment, and say: Indeed, He, while He is the Forgiver of sin (Ghafir al-Dhanb) and the Accepter of repentance (Qabil al-Tawb), is severe in punishment (Shadid al-Iqab); and indeed, He, while He is generous (Karim), has made the disbelievers (Kuffar) dwell in the Fire (Nar) forever and ever, even though their disbelief (Kufr) did not harm Him, but rather He has subjected a group of His servants (Ibad) in this world to punishment (Adhab), trials (Mihan), diseases (Amrad), ailments (Ilal), poverty (Faqr), and hunger (Ju'), while He is capable of removing them. So from this is His way (Sunnah) with His servants, and He has warned me of His punishment, so how can I not fear Him and how can I be deceived by Him?
40:3.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

40:11.arabic: قال محمد بن كعب: لأهل النار خمس دعوات يجيبهم الله عز وجل فى أربعة فإذا كانت الخامسة لم يتكلموا بعدها أبدا يقولون ﴿ ربنا أمتنا اثنتين وأحييتنا اثنتين فاعترفنا بذنوبنا فهل إلى خروج من سبيل ﴾ {} فيقول الله تعالى مجيبا لهم ﴿ ذلكم بأنه إذا دعى الله وحده كفرتم وإن يشرك به تؤمنوا فالحكم لله العلى الكبير ﴾ {} ثم يقولون ﴿ ربنا أخرنا إلى أجل قريب نجب دعوتك ونتبع الرسل فيجيبهم الله تعالى ﴿ أو لم تكونوا أقسمتم من قبل ما لكم من زوال ﴾ {} فيقولون ﴿ ربنا أخرجنا نعمل صالحا غير الذى كنا نعمل به فيجيبهم الله تعال
40:11.english: Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: The people of the Fire have five supplications to which Allah the Exalted responds in four, and when it comes to the fifth, they will never speak after it. They say: "Our Lord, You have caused us to die twice and given us life twice, so we have confessed our sins; is there any way out?" Then Allah the Exalted responds to them: "That is because when Allah alone was invoked, you disbelieved, but if others are associated with Him, you believe. So the judgment is with Allah, the Most High, the Most Great." Then they say: "Our Lord, delay us for a near term so that we may respond to Your call and follow the messengers." Allah the Exalted responds: "Did you not swear before that you would never cease?" Then they say: "Our Lord, bring us out so that we may do righteous deeds other than what we used to do." Allah the Exalted responds: "Did We not give you long enough life that whoever would be reminded could be reminded? And the warner came to you. So taste [the punishment], for the wrongdoers have no helper." Then they say: "Our Lord, our misfortune has overcome us, and we were a people astray. Our Lord, remove us from it; and if we return [to evil], we will be wrongdoers." Allah the Exalted responds: "Remain despised therein and do not speak to Me." So they will never speak after that, and that is the utmost severity of the punishment.
40:11.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Book of Repentance'

40:12.arabic: قال محمد بن كعب: لأهل النار خمس دعوات يجيبهم الله عز وجل فى أربعة فإذا كانت الخامسة لم يتكلموا بعدها أبدا يقولون ﴿ ربنا أمتنا اثنتين وأحييتنا اثنتين فاعترفنا بذنوبنا فهل إلى خروج من سبيل ﴾ {} فيقول الله تعالى مجيبا لهم ﴿ ذلكم بأنه إذا دعى الله وحده كفرتم وإن يشرك به تؤمنوا فالحكم لله العلى الكبير ﴾ {} ثم يقولون ﴿ ربنا أخرنا إلى أجل قريب نجب دعوتك ونتبع الرسل فيجيبهم الله تعالى ﴿ أو لم تكونوا أقسمتم من قبل ما لكم من زوال ﴾ {} فيقولون ﴿ ربنا أخرجنا نعمل صالحا غير الذى كنا نعمل به فيجيبهم الله تعال
40:12.english: Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: The people of the Fire have five supplications, and Allah the Exalted answers them in four; when it comes to the fifth, they will never speak after it. They say: 'Our Lord, You have caused us to die twice and given us life twice, and we have confessed our sins; is there any way out?' Then Allah the Exalted answers them: 'That is because when Allah alone was invoked, you disbelieved; but if others are associated with Him, you believe. So the judgment belongs to Allah, the Most High, the Most Great.' Then they say: 'Our Lord, delay us for a brief term; we will answer Your call and follow the messengers.' Allah the Exalted answers them: 'Did you not swear before that there would be no end for you?' Then they say: 'Our Lord, take us out; we will do righteous deeds other than what we used to do.' Allah the Exalted answers them: 'Did We not give you long enough life that whoever would be reminded therein could be reminded? And the warner came to you. So taste [the punishment], for there is not for the wrongdoers any helper.' Then they say: 'Our Lord, our misfortune has overcome us, and we were a people astray. Our Lord, remove us from it; and if we were to return [to evil], we would indeed be wrongdoers.' Allah the Exalted answers them: 'Remain despised therein and do not speak to Me.' So they will never speak after it, and that is the utmost severity of the punishment.
40:12.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Book of Repentance'

40:13.arabic: وقد شرط الله عز وجل الإنابة في الفهم والتذكير فقال تعالى ﴿ تبصرة وذكرى لكل عبد منيب ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل ﴿ وما يتذكر إلا من ينيب ﴾ {} وقال تعالى ﴿ إنما يتذكر أولوا الألباب ﴾ {} فالذي آثر غرور الدنيا على نعيم الآخرة فليس من ذوي الألباب ولذلك لا تنكشف له أسرار الكتاب.
40:13.english: And Allah the Exalted has made turning in repentance (al-Inabah) a condition for understanding and remembrance (al-Tadhkir), for He said: 'An insight and a reminder for every servant who turns in repentance (Muneeb)' (Quran 50:8). And the Exalted said: 'And none will remember except he who turns in repentance (Yuneeb)' (Quran 40:13). And He said: 'Only those of understanding (Ulul-Albab) will remember' (Quran 13:19). So whoever prefers the deception of this world over the bliss of the Hereafter is not among those of understanding (Dhawil-Albab), and therefore the secrets of the Book are not unveiled to him.
40:13.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

40:14.arabic: ينبغي أن يراعى فيها سبعة أمور، الأول: التكبير ثلاثا نسقا فيقول الله أكبر الله أكبرالله أكبر كبيرا والحمد لله كثيرا وسبحان الله بكرة وأصيلا لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له مخلصين له الدين ولو كره الكافرون يفتتح بالتكبير ليلة الفطر إلى الشروع في صلاة العيد وفي العيد الثاني يفتتح التكبير عقيب الصبح يوم عرفة إلى آخر النهار يوم الثالث عشر وهذا أكمل الأقاويل ويكبر عقيب الصلوات المفروضة وعقيب النوافل وهو عقيب الفرائض آكد.
40:14.english: Seven matters should be observed in it. The first: The magnification (Takbir) three times consecutively, saying: 'Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest greatly, and praise be to Allah abundantly, and glory be to Allah morning and evening. There is no god but Allah alone, He has no partner, being sincere (mukhliṣīn) to Him in the religion (al-dīn), even if the disbelievers dislike it.' He begins with the magnification on the night of Fitr until the commencement of the Eid prayer, and in the second Eid, he begins the magnification after the dawn prayer on the day of Arafah until the end of the day on the thirteenth, and this is the most complete of the sayings. And he magnifies after the obligatory prayers and after the supererogatory prayers, and it is more emphasized after the obligations.
40:14.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

40:14.arabic: ثم يفتتح الدعاء بما كان يفتتح به رسول الله ﭬ وهو قوله سبحان ربي العلي الأعلى الوهاب لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له له الملك وله الحمد يحيي ويميت وهو حي لا يموت بيده الخير وهو على كل شيء قدير لا إله إلا الله أهل النعمة والفضل والثناء الحسن لا إله إلا الله ولا نعبد إلا إياه مخلصين له الدين ولو كره الكافرون[13] ثم يبدأ بالأدعية التي أوردناها في الباب الثالث والرابع من كتاب الأدعية فيدعو بجميعها إن قدر عليه أو يحفظ من جملتها ما يراه أوفق بحاله وأرق لقلبه وأخف على لسانه.
40:14.english: Then he should begin the supplication with what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) used to begin with, which is his saying: 'Glory be to my Lord, the Most High, the Most Exalted, the Bestower. There is no god but Allah alone, without partner. To Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs praise. He gives life and causes death, and He is Living and does not die. In His hand is good, and He has power over all things. There is no god but Allah, the Possessor of bounty, excellence, and beautiful praise. There is no god but Allah, and we worship none but Him, making the religion (Deen) sincere for Him alone, even if the disbelievers dislike it.' Then he should begin with the supplications that we mentioned in the third and fourth chapters of the Book of Supplications, and supplicate with all of them if he is able, or memorize from among them what he sees as most suitable for his state, most tender for his heart (Qalb), and easiest on his tongue.
40:14.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Book of Knowledge'

40:14.arabic: لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له له الملك وله الحمد يحيي ويميت بيده الخير وهو على كل شيء قدير لا إله إلا الله وحده صدق وعده ونصر عبده وأعز جنده وهزم الأحزاب وحده لا إله إلا الله مخلصين له الدين ولو كره الكافرون لا إله إلا الله مخلصين له الدين الحمد لله رب العالمين
40:14.english: There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner to Him, to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs the praise, He gives life and causes death, in His hand is the good and He is over all things capable. There is no god but Allah alone, He fulfilled His promise and aided His servant and honored His soldiers and defeated the confederates alone. There is no god but Allah, making the religion (Deen) purely for Him (mukhlisīn lahu al-dīn) even if the disbelievers dislike it. There is no god but Allah, making the religion (Deen) purely for Him (mukhlisīn lahu al-dīn). Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
40:14.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

40:14.arabic: لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له مخلصين له الدين ولو كره الكافرون لا إله إلا الله وحده صدق وعده ونصر عبده وهزم الأحزاب وحده لا إله إلا الله والله أكبر
40:14.english: There is no god but Allah alone, no partner has He, making the religion (Deen) sincere (mukhlisīn) for Him even if the disbelievers (kāfirūn) hate it. There is no god but Allah alone, He fulfilled His promise and aided His servant and defeated the confederates alone. There is no god but Allah and Allah is greater.
40:14.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

40:15.arabic: ضرب الله تعالى مثلا لذلك تقريبا إلى أفهام الخلق إذ عرف أنه ما خلق الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدوه فكانت عبادتهم غاية الحكمة في حقهم ثم أخبر أن له عبدين يحب أحدهما واسمه جبريل وروح القدس والأمين وهو عنده محبوب مطاع أمين مكين ويبغض الآخر واسمه إبليس وهو اللعين المنظر إلى يوم الدين، ثم أحال الإرشاد إلى جبريل فقال تعالى: ﴿ قل نزله روح القدس من ربك بالحق ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ يلقى الروح من أمره على من يشاء من عباده ﴾ {} وأحال الإغواء على إبليس فقال تعالى: ﴿ ليضلّ عن سبيله ﴾ {} والإغواء هو استيقاف العباد دون بلو
40:15.english: Allah the Exalted struck an example of that to bring it closer to the understandings of the creation, since He knew that He did not create the Jinn and mankind except to worship Him, so their worship became the ultimate wisdom (Hikmah) in their regard. Then He informed that He has two servants: He loves one of them, and his name is Gabriel and the Holy Spirit (Ruh al-Qudus) and the Trustworthy (Al-Amin), and he is with Him beloved, obeyed, trustworthy, and firmly established; and He hates the other, and his name is Iblis, and he is the accursed one, granted respite until the Day of Recompense (Yawm al-Din). Then He delegated the guidance (Irshad) to Gabriel, so He the Exalted said: 'Say: The Holy Spirit (Ruh al-Qudus) has brought it down from your Lord in truth' (Quran 16:102), and He the Exalted said: 'He casts the Spirit (Ruh) from His command upon whom He wills of His servants' (Quran 40:15). And He delegated the misguidance (Ighwa') to Iblis, so He the Exalted said: 'To lead astray from His path' (Quran 4:60). And the misguidance is preventing the servants from reaching the ultimate wisdom (Hikmah). So look how He attributed it to the servant upon whom He is angry, and the guidance is leading them to the ultimate goal (Ghayah), so look how He attributed it to the servant whom He loved. And you have in custom an example for it: if a king is in need of someone to give him drink and someone to perform cupping (Hijamah) and clean the courtyard of his house from filth, and he has two servants, then he does not assign for the cupping and cleaning except the ugliest and most vile of them, and he does not entrust carrying the drink and perfume except to the best, most complete, and most beloved of them to him. And it is not fitting for you to say: 'This is my action, and was his action not without my action?' For you have erred when you attributed that to yourself. Rather, it is He who directed your motive (Da'iyah) to specify the hated action with the hated person and the beloved action with the beloved person, completing the justice ('Adl). For His justice ('Adl) is sometimes completed with matters in which you have no entry, and sometimes it is completed in you, for you are also from His actions. So your motive (Da'iyah), your ability (Qudrah), your knowledge ('Ilm), your action ('Amal), and all the causes of your movements in expression are His action which He arranged with justice ('Adl) in an arrangement from which issue the moderate actions, except that you see only yourself, so you think that what appears upon you in the world of witnessing ('Alam al-Shahadah) has no cause from the world of the unseen and dominion ('Alam al-Ghayb wal-Malakut), therefore you attribute it to yourself. And you are only like the...
40:15.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

40:16.arabic: ولا قاهر الا الله الواحد القهار ولا قادر الا الملك الجبار واذا انكشفت الغطاء عن اعين الغافلين فشاهدوا الامر كذلك سمعوا عند ذلك نداء المنادي ﴿ لمن الملك اليوم لله الواحد القهار ﴾ {} ولقد كان الملك لله الواحد القهار كل يوم لا ذلك على الخصوص ولكن الغافلين لا يسمعون هذا النداء الا ذلك اليوم، فهو نبأ عما يتجدد للغافلين من كشف الاحوال حيث لا ينفعهم الكشف فنعوذ بالله الحليم الكريم من الجهل والعمى فانه اصل اسباب الهلاك.
40:16.english: And there is no Subduer (Qahir) except Allah the One, the Subduer (Al-Wahid Al-Qahhar), and no Powerful (Qadir) except the King, the Compeller (Al-Jabbar). And when the veil (Ghita') is lifted from the eyes of the heedless (Ghafilin) and they witness the matter as such, they hear at that time the call of the caller: 'To whom belongs the dominion today? To Allah, the One, the Subduer (Al-Wahid Al-Qahhar).' {} And indeed the dominion belonged to Allah the One, the Subduer (Al-Wahid Al-Qahhar) every day, not specifically that day, but the heedless (Ghafilin) do not hear this call except on that day. So it is news of what is renewed for the heedless (Ghafilin) from the unveiling (Kashf) of states (Ahwal) where the unveiling (Kashf) does not benefit them. So we seek refuge with Allah, the Forbearing (Al-Halim), the Generous (Al-Karim), from ignorance (Jahl) and blindness ('Ama), for it is the root (Asl) of the causes (Asbab) of destruction (Halak).
40:16.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

40:16.arabic: ثم لا تغفل عن الفكر فى الميزان وتطاير الكتب إلى الأيمان والشمائل فإن الناس بعد السؤال ثلاث فرق فرقة ليس لهم حسنة فيخرج من النار عنق أسود فيلقطهم لقط الطير الحب وينطوى عليهم ويلقيهم فى النار فتبتلعهم النار وينادى عليهم شقاوة لا سعادة بعدها وقسم آخر لا سيئة لهم فينادى مناد ليقم الحمادون لله على كل حال فيقومون ويسرحون إلى الجنة ثم يفعل ذلك بأهل قيام الليل ثم بمن لم تشغله تجارة الدنيا ولا بيعها عن ذكر الله تعالى وينادى عليهم سعادة لا شقاوة بعدها ويبقى قسم ثالث وهم الأكثرون خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا
40:16.english: Then do not neglect the thought (Fikr) in the Balance (Mizan) and the flying of the books to the right hands and the left hands, for the people after the questioning are three groups: a group that has no good deed, so a black neck emerges from the Fire and picks them up like the picking of birds for grain, and it folds over them and throws them into the Fire, and the Fire swallows them, and it is proclaimed upon them: misery (Shiqawah) with no happiness (Sa'adah) after it ever. And another division has no evil deed for them, so a caller calls out: 'Let those who praise Allah (Al-Hamadun Lillah) in every circumstance rise,' so they rise and are sent forth to Paradise. Then that is done with the people of standing in prayer at night (Qiyam al-Layl), then with those whom the trade of the worldly life (Dunya) and its sale do not distract from the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah, the Exalted, and it is proclaimed upon them: happiness (Sa'adah) with no misery (Shiqawah) after it ever. And a third division remains, and they are the majority, who mixed a righteous deed and another evil deed, and it may be hidden from them, and it is not hidden from Allah, the Exalted, whether the predominant is their good deeds or their evil deeds, but Allah refuses except to make them know that to manifest His favor (Fadl) at the time of pardon (Afw) and His justice (Adl) at the time of punishment (Iqab). So the scrolls and books fly, folded upon the good deeds and the evil deeds, and the Balance (Mizan) is set up, and the gazes become fixed upon the books: will they fall into the right hand or into the left? Then to the tongue of the Balance (Mizan): does it incline to the side of the evil deeds or to the side of the good deeds? And this is an awesome state in which the intellects (Uqul) of the creatures are bewildered.
40:16.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

40:16.arabic: فإن تكلمنا فبإذنه انبسطنا وإن سكنا فبقهره انقبضنا، إذ لا معطى لما منع ولا مانع لما أعطى لأنا في كل لحظة من لحظات العمر قبل الموت نسمع بسمع القلوب نداء الملك الجبار ﴿ لمن الملك اليوم لله الواحد القهار ﴾ فالحمد لله الذى ميزنا عن الكفار وأسمعنا هذا النداء قبل انقضاء الأعمار.
40:16.english: For if we speak, it is by His permission that we expand; and if we are silent, it is by His overpowering that we contract, since there is no giver of what He has withheld nor withholder of what He has given. For we, in every moment of the moments of life before death, hear with the hearing of the Hearts (Qulub) the call of the Compelling King: 'To whom belongs the dominion today? To Allah, the One, the Subduer.' So praise be to Allah who distinguished us from the disbelievers and made us hear this call before the expiration of the lifespans.
40:16.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

40:17.arabic: فكيف بكم لو عاينتم الأمور وبعثرت القبور وحصل ما في الصدور وأوقفتم للتحصيل بين يدي الملك الجليل فطارت القلوب لإشفاقها من سالف الذنوب وهتكت عنكم الحجب والأستار وظهرت منكم العيوب والأسرار؟ هنالك تجزى كل نفس بما كسبت إن الله عز وجل يقول "ليجزى الذي أساءوا بما عملوا ويجزى الذي أحسنوا بالحسنى" وقال تعالى "ووضع الكتاب فترى المجرمين مشفقين مما فيه" الآية جعلنا الله وإياكم عاملين بكتابة متبعين لأوليائه حتى يحلنا وإياكم دار المقامة من فضله إنه حميد مجيد.
40:17.english: How would it be for you if you witnessed the matters and the graves were overturned and what is in the chests (Sudur) was gathered and you were stood for the accounting before the Glorious King (Al-Malik Al-Jalil), and the hearts (Qulub) flew from their fear of past sins, and the veils (Hujub) and curtains (Astār) were torn from you, and your faults (ʿUyūb) and secrets (Asrār) appeared? There, every soul (Nafs) will be recompensed for what it earned. Indeed, Allah (Allah), the Exalted and Majestic, says: "So that He may recompense those who did evil for what they did and recompense those who did good with the best." And He, the Exalted, said: "And the Record will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it." The verse. May Allah make us and you doers of His book, followers of His allies, until He settles us and you in the Abode of Permanence (Dār Al-Maqāmah) from His bounty. Indeed, He is Praiseworthy, Glorious.
40:17.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of the World'

40:17.arabic: وقد ضعفت عن مقاومتهم ومددت عنق الرجاء إلى سيدك ومولاك لعله يخلصك من أيديهم إذ قرع سمعك نداء الجبار جل جلاله ﴿ اليوم تجزى كل نفس بما كسبت لا ظلم اليوم ﴾ {} فعند ذلك ينخلع قلبك من الهيبة وتوقن نفسك بالبوار وتتذكر ما أنذرك الله تعالى على لسان رسوله حيث قال ﴿ ولا تحسبن الله غافلا عما يعمل الظالمون إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار مهطعين مقنعى رءوسهم لا يرتد إليهم طرفهم وأفئدتهم هواء وأنذر الناس ﴾ {} الآية
40:17.english: And you have weakened in resisting them and extended the neck of hope to your Master and Lord, perhaps He will deliver you from their hands when the call of the Almighty, majestic is His glory, strikes your hearing: 'Today every soul (Nafs) will be recompensed for what it earned; no injustice today' (Quran 40:17). Then at that moment, your heart (Qalb) is torn out from awe and your soul (Nafs) becomes certain of perdition, and you remember what Allah the Exalted warned you through the tongue of His Messenger where He said: 'And do not think Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. He only delays them for a Day when eyes will stare [in horror], racing ahead, their heads raised up, their glance not returning to them, and their hearts (Af'idah) void. And warn the people' (Quran 14:42-44).
40:17.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

40:18.arabic: فإن كان ما ذكرت باطلاً فإني أذكرك يوماً تكون السماء فيه كالمهل وتصير الجبال كالعهن وتجثوا الأمم لصولة الجبار العظيم، وإني والله قد ضعفت عن إصلاح نفسي فكيف بإصلاح غيري؟ وإن كان ما ذكرت حقاً فإني أدلك على طبيب هدى يداوي الكلوم الممرضة والأوجاع المرمضة ذلك الله رب العالمين فاقصديه بصدق المسألة فإني مشغول عنك بقوله تعالى "وأنذرهم يوم الآزفة إذ القلوب لدى الحناجر كاظمين ما للظالمين من حميم ولا شفيع يطاع. يعلم خائنة الأعين وما تخفي الصدور" فأين المهرب من هذه الآية؟
40:18.english: If what you mentioned is false, then I remind you of a day when the sky will be like molten brass and the mountains will become like carded wool, and the nations will kneel before the onslaught of the Great Compeller (Al-Jabbar). And I, by Allah, have weakened in reforming my own self (Nafs), so how about reforming others? And if what you mentioned is true, then I direct you to a guiding physician who heals the sick wounds and the chronic pains - that is Allah, Lord of the Worlds. So seek Him with sincere supplication, for I am preoccupied from you with His saying, the Exalted: 'And warn them of the Approaching Day (Al-Azifah) when the Hearts (Qulub) will be at the throats, choking. The wrongdoers will have no close friend nor any intercessor who could be obeyed. He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the chests conceal.' So where is the escape from this verse?
40:18.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Harms of the Tongue'

40:24.arabic: وينظر إلى فرعون وهامان وقارون وإلى ملوك الأرض وما جرى لهم كيف أحسن الله إليهم ابتداء ثم دمرهم تدميرا! فقال تعالى "هل تحس منهم من أحد" الآية. وقد حذر الله تعالى من مكره واستدراجه فقال "فلا يأمن مكر الله إلا القوم الخاسرون" وقال تعالى "ومكروا مكراً ومكرنا مكراً وهم لا يشعرون" وقال عز وجل "ومكروا ومكر الله والله خير الماكرين" وقال تعالى "إنهم يكيدون كيداً وأكيد كيداً فمهل الكافرين أمهلهم رويداً" فكما لا يجوز للعبد المهمل أن يستدل بإهمال السيد إياه وتمكينه من النعم على حب السيد، بل ينبغي أن يحذر أن
40:24.english: And he looks at Pharaoh and Haman and Korah and at the kings of the earth and what happened to them—how Allah bestowed favor upon them initially, then destroyed them utterly! So Allah the Exalted said: "Do you perceive any of them?" The verse. And Allah the Exalted warned of His deception (makr) and gradual entrapment (istidrāj), saying: "So none feels secure from the deception (makr) of Allah except the people who are losers," and He said: "And they planned a plan, and We planned a plan, while they perceived not," and He the Mighty and Majestic said: "And they planned, and Allah planned, and Allah is the best of planners," and He said: "Indeed, they are planning a plan, and I am planning a plan. So allow time for the disbelievers. Leave them awhile." So just as it is not permissible for the neglected servant to infer from the master's neglect of him and enabling him with blessings that the master loves him, rather he should be cautious that this might be deception (makr) and plotting from him, even though the master did not warn him of his own deception (makr), then how much more must this be in the right of Allah the Exalted with His warning of His gradual entrapment (istidrāj) is more appropriate. Therefore, whoever feels secure from the deception (makr) of Allah is deluded (maghṭūr), and the origin of this delusion (ghurūr) is that he inferred from worldly blessings that he is honorable with that Bestower, and it is possible that this is evidence of degradation, but that possibility does not agree with desire (hawā), so Satan, by means of desire (hawā), inclines the Heart (Qalb) toward what accompanies it, which is belief in its indication of honor, and this is the limit of delusion (ghurūr).
40:24.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

40:28.arabic: وقام أبو بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه دونه يقول وهو يبكي ويلكم أتقتلون رجلا أن يقول ربي الله ثم انصرفوا عنه وإن ذلك لأشد ما رأيت قريشا بلغت منه حديث عروة قلت لعبد الله بن عمرو ما أكثر ما رأيت قريشا نالت من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فيما كانت تظهر من عداوته الحديث أخرجه بطوله البخاري مختصرا وابن حبان بتمامه وفي رواية أخرى عن عبد الله بن عمرو رضي الله عنهما قال بينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بفناء الكعبة إذ أقبل عقبة بن أبي معيط فأخذ بمنكب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فلف ثوبه في عنقه فخنقه خنقا
40:28.english: And Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) stood up in his defense saying while crying: 'Woe to you, would you kill a man for saying my Lord is Allah?' Then they turned away from him, and that was the most severe thing I saw Quraysh reach against him. The narration of Urwah: I said to Abdullah ibn Amr: 'What is the most I saw Quraysh inflict upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) in what they showed of enmity?' The hadith was transmitted at length by al-Bukhari in abbreviated form and by Ibn Hibban in full. And in another narration from Abdullah ibn Amr (may Allah be pleased with them both), he said: 'While the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was in the courtyard of the Kaaba, Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt approached and took the shoulder of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and twisted his garment around his neck and choked him severely. Then Abu Bakr came and took his shoulder and pushed him away from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and said: "Would you kill a man for saying my Lord is Allah, when he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord?" The narration of Abdullah ibn Amr: While the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was in the courtyard of the Kaaba, Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt approached and took the shoulder of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him).' The hadith was narrated by al-Bukhari.
40:28.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

40:28.arabic: عوا في الحجر وأنا معهم فقال بعضهم لبعض ذكرتم ما بلغ منكم وما بلغكم عنه حتى إذا بادأكم بما تكرهون تركتموه فبينما هم في ذلك إذ طلع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فوثبوا إليه وثبة رجل واحد فأحاطوا به يقولون أنت الذي تقول كذا أنت الذي تقول كذا لما كان قد بلغهم من عيب آلهتهم ودينهم قال فيقول رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم نعم أنا الذي أقول ذلك قال فلقد رأيت رجل منهم أخذ بمجامع ردائه قال وقام أبو بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه دونه يقول وهو يبكي ويلكم أتقتلون رجلا أن يقول ربي الله ثم انصرفوا عنه وإن ذلك لأشد ما
40:28.english: They gathered in the Hijr (the semi-circular area near the Kaaba) and I was with them, and some of them said to each other: 'You mentioned what has reached you about him and what has reached him about you, until when he initiated with what you dislike, you abandoned him.' While they were in that state, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) appeared, and they rushed to him with the rush of one man, surrounding him, saying: 'Are you the one who says such-and-such? Are you the one who says such-and-such?' regarding what had reached them about his criticism of their gods and their religion. He said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Yes, I am the one who says that."' He said: 'I indeed saw a man among them take hold of the collar of his garment.' He said: 'And Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) stood in front of him, saying while crying: "Woe to you! Would you kill a man because he says: 'My Lord is Allah'?" Then they turned away from him, and that was the most severe thing I saw Quraysh inflict upon him.' The hadith of Urwah: I said to Abdullah ibn Amr: 'What is the most I saw Quraysh inflict upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) in what they showed of enmity?' The hadith is narrated at length by al-Bukhari in abbreviated form and by Ibn Hibban in full. And in another narration from Abdullah ibn Amr (may Allah be pleased with them both), he said: 'While the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was in the courtyard of the Kaaba, Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt approached and took hold of the shoulder of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), then twisted his garment around his neck and choked him severely. Abu Bakr came and took hold of his shoulder and pushed him away from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and said: "Would you kill a man because he says: 'My Lord is Allah' and he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord?"' The hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr: 'While the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was in the courtyard of the Kaaba, Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt approached and took hold of the shoulder of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him)...' The hadith is narrated by al-Bukhari. And it is narrated that Mu'awiyah (may Allah be pleased with him) withheld the stipend, so Abu Muslim al-Khawlani stood up to him and said to him: 'O Mu'awiyah, it is not from your effort (kad) nor from the effort of your father nor from the effort of your mother.' He said: 'So Mu'awiyah became angry and descended from the pulpit and said to them: 'Stay in your places,' and disappeared from their sight for a while, then came out to them having performed ablution (ightasala), and said: 'Abu Muslim spoke to me with words that angered me, and I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: "Anger (al-ghadab) is from Satan (al-Shaytan), and Satan was created from fire (al-nar), and fire is only extinguished with water, so when one of you becomes angry, let him perform ablution (falyaghtasil)."' The hadith of Mu'awiyah: 'Anger is from Satan...' The hadith, and at its beginning is a story narrated by Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah, and in it is one whom I do not know, and I entered and performed ablution, and Abu Muslim spoke truthfully that it is not from my effort nor from the effort of my father, so come to your stipends.' And it is narrated from Dabah ibn Muhsin al-Anazi, who said: 'Abu Musa al-Ash'ari was our governor in Basra, and when he would address us, he would praise Allah and extol Him and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him) and begin to supplicate for Umar (may Allah be pleased with him).' He said: 'That angered me from him, so I stood up to him and said to him: 'Where are you from his companion, preferring him over him?' He did that a number of times, then wrote.'
40:28.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

40:28.arabic: وللبزار وأبي يعلى من حديث أنس قال لقد ضربوا رسول الله ﭬ حتى غشي عليه فقام أبو بكر فجعل ينادي ويلكم أتقتلون رجلا أن يقول ربي الله وإسناده صحيح على شرط مسلم.
40:28.english: And from Al-Bazzar and Abu Ya'la from the hadith of Anas, he said: 'They struck the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) until he fainted, then Abu Bakr stood up and began to call out: "Woe to you! Do you kill a man because he says: My Lord is Allah?" And its chain is authentic according to the conditions of Muslim.'
40:28.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

40:33.arabic: ومن لم يفهم أن القديم عبارة عما ليس قبله شيء وأن الباء قبل السين في قولك بسم الله فلا يكون السين المتأخر عن الباء قديما فنزه عن الالتفات إليه قلبك فلله سبحانه سر في إبعاد بعض العباد ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد ومن استبعد أن يسمع موسى عليه السلام في الدنيا كلاما ليس بصوت ولا حرف فليستنكر أن يرى في الآخرة موجودا ليس بجسم ولا لون وإن عقل أن يرى ما ليس بلون ولا جسم ولا قدر ولا كمية وهو إلى الآن لم ير غيره فليعقل في حاسة السمع ما عقله في حاسة البصر وإن عقل على أن يكون له علم واحد هو علم بجميع الموجود
40:33.english: And whoever does not understand that 'the Eternal (Al-Qadim)' is an expression for that which has nothing before it, and that the 'Ba' (ب) comes before the 'Seen' (س) in your saying 'Bismillah' (In the name of Allah), then the 'Seen' which follows the 'Ba' cannot be eternal, so purify your Heart (Qalb) from turning attention to him. For Allah, glorified be He, has a secret in distancing some of the servants, and 'whom Allah misguides, for him there is no guide (wa man yudlil Allahu fama lahu min hadin).' And whoever finds it far-fetched that Moses, peace be upon him, heard in this world a Speech (Kalam) that is not sound nor letter, let him find it strange that he will see in the Hereafter an existent that is not body nor color. And if he comprehends that he can see what has no color, nor body, nor measure, nor quantity—and he has not yet seen anything else—then let him comprehend in the sense of hearing what he comprehended in the sense of sight. And if he comprehends that He has one Knowledge (Ilm) which is knowledge of all existents, then let him comprehend one attribute of the Essence (Dhat) which is Speech (Kalam) encompassing all that is indicated by expressions. And if he comprehends the existence of the seven heavens and the existence of Paradise and Hell being written on a small paper and preserved in the measure of an atom of the Heart (Qalb), and that all of that is visible in the measure of a lens of the pupil without the essence of the heavens, the earth, Paradise, and Hell residing in the pupil, the Heart (Qalb), and the paper, then let him comprehend the existence of the Speech (Kalam) being recited by tongues, preserved in hearts, written in copies of the Quran without the essence of the Speech (Kalam) residing in them. For if the essence of the Speech (Kalam) of Allah's Book resided in the paper, then the essence of Allah, exalted be He, would reside by writing His name on the paper, and the essence of Hell would reside by writing its name on the paper, and it would burn.
40:33.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

40:35.arabic: قد ذم الله الكبر في مواضع من كتابه وذم كل جبار متكبر فقال تعالى "سأصرف عن آياتي الذين يتكبرون في الأرض بغير الحق" وقال عز وجل "كذلك يطبع الله على كل قلب متكبر جبار" وقال تعالى "واستفتحوا وخاب كل جبار عنيد" وقال تعالى "إنه لا يحب المستكبرين" وقال تعالى "لقد استكبروا في أنفسهم وعتوا عتواً كبيراً" وقال تعالى "إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي سيدخلون جهنم داخرين" وذم الكبر في القرآن كثير وقد قال رسول الله ﭬ "لا يدخل الجنة من كان في قلبه مثقال حبة من خردل من كبر، ولا يدخل النار من كان في قلبه مثقال حبة من
40:35.english: Allah has condemned arrogance in multiple places in His Book and condemned every arrogant tyrant. So He, the Exalted, said: "I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant on earth without right." And He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: "Thus does Allah seal over every arrogant, oppressive heart (Qalb)." And He, the Exalted, said: "And they sought victory, and disappointed was every obstinate tyrant." And He, the Exalted, said: "Indeed, He does not love the arrogant." And He, the Exalted, said: "They had certainly become arrogant within themselves and transgressed a great transgression." And He, the Exalted, said: "Indeed, those who are arrogant toward My worship will enter Hell in humiliation." And the condemnation of arrogance in the Quran is abundant. And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said: "He will not enter Paradise who has in his heart (Qalb) an atom's weight of arrogance, and he will not enter the Fire who has in his heart (Qalb) an atom's weight of faith."
40:35.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

40:43.arabic: وذلك لاستمداده من عرق خفي في النفس وطبيعة مستكنة في الطبع لا يكاد يقف عليها إلا الغواصون. فأما السبب الأول: فهو دفع ألم الخوف، لأن الشفيق بسوء الظن مولع، والإنسان وإن كان مكفياً في الحال فإنه طويل الأمل ويخطر بباله أن المال فيه كفايته ربما يتلف فيحتاج إلى غيره، فإذا خطر ذلك بباله هاج الخوف من قلبه ولا يدفع ألم الخوف إلا الأمن الحاصل بوجود مال آخر يفزغ إليه إن أصابت هذا المال جائحة، فهو أبدا لشفقته على نفسه وحبه للحياة يقدر طول الحياة؛ ويقدر هجوم الحاجات؛ ويقدر إمكان تطرق الآفات إلى الأموال، ويست
40:43.english: And that is because it draws from a hidden vein in the Soul (Nafs) and a nature concealed in the innate disposition (Tab') that hardly anyone can discern except the deep divers. As for the first cause: it is the repulsion of the pain of fear, because the one who is anxious with bad suspicion is addicted, and the human being, even if he is sufficient in the present, is long in hope and it occurs to his mind that the wealth in which his sufficiency lies might perish, so he needs another. When that occurs to his mind, fear stirs from his Heart (Qalb), and the pain of fear is not repelled except by the security obtained through the existence of other wealth to resort to if a calamity befalls this wealth. So he is always, due to his anxiety for himself and his love for life, estimating the length of life; and estimating the assault of needs; and estimating the possibility of afflictions befalling wealth, and he senses fear from that, so he seeks what repels his fear, which is abundance of wealth, so that if he is afflicted with a portion of his wealth, he is enriched by the other. And this fear has no specific amount of wealth to stop at, therefore there is no stopping point for its like until he owns all that is in the world, and for that reason the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Two greedy ones are never satisfied: the greedy one for knowledge and the greedy one for wealth." And such a cause applies in the love of status, for he fears the humiliation of poverty and the humiliation of obscurity, so he seeks status to repel his fear with it, and this fear has no limit to stop at, therefore the love of status does not stop at a limit. And this love has no benefit in it, not in this world nor in the Hereafter, as Allah the Exalted said: "Undoubtedly, what you call me to has no call in this world nor in the Hereafter, and that our return is to Allah, and that the extravagant ones are the companions of the Fire." So the intended meaning is that this love does not detach from the Hearts (Qulub), and it is among the afflictions that befall the Heart (Qalb), and none is saved from it except whom Allah the Exalted protects.
40:43.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

40:43.arabic: وقوله سبحانه وتعالى: "نورهم يسعى بين أيديهم وبإيمانهم يقولون ربنا أتمم لنا نورنا " محتمل لهذا المعنى، وهو أن ينعم عليه بإتمام النور مهما تزود من الدنيا أصل النور، ويحتمل أن يكون المراد به إتمام النور في غير ما استنار في الدنيا استنارة محتاجة إلى مزيد الاستكمال والإشراق، فيكون
40:43.english: And His saying, the Exalted: "Their light runs before them and on their right hands, and they say: 'Our Lord, perfect for us our light'" is susceptible to this meaning, which is that He bestows upon him the completion of the light however much he provisioned from the world the origin of the light, and it is susceptible that the intended by it is the completion of the light in other than what was illuminated in the world, an illumination needing increased completion and radiance, so it becomes
40:43.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

40:46.arabic: الأصل الثالث: عذاب القبر وقد ورد الشرع به قال الله تعالى: ﴿ النار يعرضون عليها غدوا وعشيا ويوم تقوم الساعة أدخلوا آل فرعون أشد العذاب ﴾ { سورة غافر: 46 } واشتهر عن رسول الله ﭬ والسلف الصالح الاستعاذة من عذاب القبر[42] وهو ممكن فيجب التصديق به ولا يمنع من التصديق به تفرق أجزاء الميت في بطون السباع وحواصل الطيور فإن المدرك لألم العذاب من الحيوان أجزاء مخصوصة يقدر الله تعالى على إعادة الإدراك إليها.
40:46.english: The Third Foundation: The Punishment of the Grave, and the Sacred Law has come with it. Allah the Exalted said: 'The Fire, they are presented to it morning and evening, and on the Day the Hour is established [it will be said], "Enter the people of Pharaoh into the severest punishment."' {Surah Ghafir: 46}. And it is well-known from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and the righteous predecessors seeking refuge from the punishment of the grave. And it is possible, so believing in it is obligatory. And the scattering of the parts of the deceased in the bellies of beasts and the crops of birds does not prevent belief in it, for the perceiver of the pain of punishment from the living creature is specific parts; Allah the Exalted is capable of restoring perception to them.
40:46.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

40:48.arabic: ويكفيك تنبيها على كمال الرتبة في ستر القبيح و إظهار الجميل أن الله تعالى
40:48.english: And it suffices you as an indication of the perfection of the rank in concealing the ugly and manifesting the beautiful that Allah, the Exalted,
40:48.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

40:49.arabic: وقال أبو الدرداء قال رسول الله ﭬ: (يلقى على أهل النار الجوع حتى يعدل ما هم فيه من العذاب فيستغيثون بالطعام فيغاثون بطعام من ضريع لا يسمن ولا يغنى من جوع ويستغيثون بالطعام فيغاثون بطعام ذى غصة فيذكرون كما كانوا يجيزون الغصص فى الدنيا بشراب فيستغيثون بشراب فيرفع إليهم الحميم بكلاليب الحديد فإذا دنت من وجوههم شوت وجوههم فإذا دخل الشراب بطونهم قطع ما فى بطونهم فيقولون ادعوا خزنة جهنم قال فيدعون خزنة جهنم أن ادعوا ربكم يخفف عنا يوما من العذاب فيقولون أو لم تك تأتيكم رسلكم بالبينات قالوا بلى قالوا فاد
40:49.english: And Abu al-Darda' said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Hunger is cast upon the people of the Fire until it equals what they are in of punishment, so they cry out for food and are given food of bitter thorn that neither fattens nor satisfies from hunger, and they cry out for food and are given food that causes choking, so they remember how they used to pass choking in the world with drink, so they cry out for drink and the boiling water is raised to them with iron hooks. When it approaches their faces, it scorches their faces, and when the drink enters their bellies, it cuts what is in their bellies. So they say: Call the keepers of Hell. He said: So they call the keepers of Hell to call your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment. They say: Did not your messengers come to you with clear proofs? They say: Yes. They say: So call, and the call of the disbelievers is only in error. He said: So they say: Call Malik. So they call, and they say: O Malik, let our Lord decide for us. He said: So He answers them: You are abiding.'
40:49.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

40:50.arabic: فيقولون ادعوا خزنة جهنم قال فيدعون خزنة جهنم أن ادعوا ربكم يخفف عنا يوما من العذاب فيقولون أو لم تك تأتيكم رسلكم بالبينات قالوا بلى قالوا فادعوا وما دعاء الكافرين إلا فى ضلال قال فيقولون ادعوا مالكا فيدعون فيقولون يا مالك ليقض علينا ربك قال فيجيبهم إنكم ماكثون[205]
40:50.english: So they say: 'Call the keepers of Hellfire.' He said: So they call the keepers of Hellfire to call your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment. So they say: 'Did not your messengers come to you with clear proofs?' They said: 'Yes.' They said: 'So call, and the call of the disbelievers is only in misguidance.' He said: So they say: 'Call Malik.' So they call, and they say: 'O Malik, let our Lord decide upon us.' He said: So He answers them: 'You will remain.'
40:50.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

40:52.arabic: يوم لا ينفع الظالمين معذرتهم ولهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار
40:52.english: A day when the excuse of the wrongdoers will not benefit them, and for them is the curse, and for them is the evil abode.
40:52.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Book of Repentance'

40:55.arabic: وسائر ما ذكرناه في الورد الأول مثل أن يقول أستغفر الله الذي لا إله إلا هو الحي القيوم وأسأله التوبة وسبحان الله العظيم وبحمده مأخوذ من قوله تعالى: ﴿ واستغفر لذنبك وسبح بحمد ربك بالعشي والإبكار ﴾ والاستغفار على الأسماء التي في القرآن أحب كقوله استغفر الله إنه كان غفارا أستغفر الله إنه كان توابا رب اغفر وارحم وأنت خير الراحمين فاغفر لنا وارحمنا وأنت خير الراحمين فاغفر لنا وارحمنا وأنت خير الغافرين ويستحب أن يقرأ قبل غروب الشمس: والشمس وضحاها. والليل إذا يغشى. والمعوذتين. ولتغرب الشمس عليه وهو في ا
40:55.english: And all that we have mentioned in the first spiritual practice (Wird) is like saying: 'I seek forgiveness from Allah, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer (Al-Qayyum), and I ask Him for repentance, and glory be to Allah the Great and with His praise'—taken from His saying, the Exalted: 'So be patient, indeed the promise of Allah is true, and seek forgiveness for your sin and glorify with the praise of your Lord in the evening and the morning.' And seeking forgiveness (Istighfar) with the names that are in the Quran is more beloved, like His saying: 'Seek forgiveness from Allah, indeed He is Oft-Forgiving (Ghaffar),' 'I seek forgiveness from Allah, indeed He is Oft-Returning (Tawwab),' 'My Lord, forgive and have mercy, and You are the best of the merciful, so forgive us and have mercy on us, and You are the best of the forgivers.' And it is recommended to recite before sunset: 'By the sun and its brightness,' 'By the night when it covers,' and the two chapters of seeking refuge (Al-Mu'awwidhatayn). And let the sun set upon him while he is in seeking forgiveness. Then, when he hears the call to prayer (Adhan), he says: 'O Allah, this is the approach of Your night and the departure of Your day and the voices of Your callers,' as preceded. Then he responds to the caller to prayer and occupies himself with the sunset prayer (Maghrib), and with the sunset, the spiritual practices (Awrad) of the day have ended.
40:55.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Book of Knowledge'

40:56.arabic: فالكبر عبارة عن الحالة الحاصلة في النفس من هذه الاعتقادات، وتسمى أيضاً عزة وتعظماً، ولذلك قال ابن عباس في قوله تعالى "إن في صدوركم إلا كبر ما هم ببالغيه" قال عظمة لم يبلغوها، ففسر الكبر بتلك العظمة. ثم هذه العزة تقتضي أعمالاً في الظاهر والباطن هي ثمرات ويسمى ذلك تكبراً، فإنه مهما عظم عنده قدره بالإضافة إلى غيره حقر من دونه وازدراه وأقصاه عن نفسه وأبعده وترفع عن مجالسته ومؤاكلته، ورأى أن حقه أن يقوم ماثلاً بين يديه إن اشتد كبره فإن كان أشد من ذلك استنكف عن استخدامه ولم يجعله أهلاً للقيام بين يديه
40:56.english: So arrogance (Kibr) is an expression for the state occurring in the Soul (Nafs) from these beliefs, and it is also called pride (Izza) and self-glorification (Ta'azzum). Therefore, Ibn Abbas said regarding His saying, the Exalted: "Indeed, in their chests is nothing but arrogance (Kibr) which they will never attain" - he said: a greatness (Azama) they have not reached. Thus, he interpreted arrogance (Kibr) as that greatness (Azama). Then this pride (Izza) necessitates actions in the outward and inward which are fruits and that is called arrogance (Takabbur). For whenever his worth becomes great in his estimation relative to others, he belittles those beneath him, despises them, excludes them from himself, distances them, and elevates himself above sitting with them and eating with them. He sees that it is his right that they stand before him if his arrogance intensifies. If it is more severe than that, he disdains from employing them and does not deem them worthy to stand before him nor to serve his threshold. If it is less than that, then he scorns equality with them, precedes them in narrow paths, rises above them in gatherings, waits for them to initiate the greeting, considers their deficiency in fulfilling his needs improbable, and is amazed by it. If he argues or debates, he scorns responding to them; if admonished, he disdains acceptance; if he admonishes, he is harsh in advice; if something of his statement is refuted, he becomes angry; if he teaches, he does not show gentleness to the learners, humiliates them, rebukes them, imposes favors upon them, and uses them. He looks at the common people as if he looks at donkeys, considering them ignorant and belittling them.
40:56.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

40:58.arabic: جدنا فيها غير بيت من المسلمين ﴾ {}. البحث الثالث: عن الحكم الشرعي والإسلام والإيمان حكمان أخروي ودنيوي. أما الأخروي فهو الإخراج من النار ومنع التخليد إذ قال رسول الله ﭬ: (يخرج من النار من كان في قلبه مثقال ذرة من إيمان[50]) وقد اختلفوا في أن هذا الحكم على ماذا يترتب وعبروا عنه بأن الإيمان ماذا هو فمن قائل إنه مجرد العقد ومن قائل يقول إنه عقد بالقلب وشهادة باللسان ومن قائل يزيد ثالثا وهو العمل بالأركان ونحن نكشف الغطاء عنه ونقول من جمع بين هذه الثلاثة فلا خلاف في أن مستقره الجنة وهذه درجة الدرجة
40:58.english: We found in it other than a house of the Muslims. The third investigation: concerning the legal ruling and Islam and Faith (Iman) are two rulings: otherworldly and worldly. As for the otherworldly, it is the removal from the Fire and prevention of eternal abiding, as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'He will be removed from the Fire who has in his heart an atom's weight of faith.' And they have differed regarding what this ruling is based upon, and they expressed it by saying: what is faith? For some say it is merely the belief (al-'aqd), and some say it is belief in the heart and testimony with the tongue, and some add a third, which is action with the limbs. And we unveil the cover from it and say: whoever combines these three, there is no disagreement that his abode is Paradise. And this is the first degree. The second degree is that two and some of the third exist, which is the saying and the belief and some of the actions, but its possessor committed a major sin or some major sins.
