At this point, the Mu'tazilites said: he has exited from faith by this and has not entered into disbelief, rather his name is transgressor (fasiq), and he is in a station between the two stations, and he is eternally abiding in the Fire. And this is false, as we will mention. The third degree is that the affirmation (tasdiq) with the heart and the testimony with the tongue exist without the actions with the limbs. And they have differed regarding its ruling. Abu Talib al-Makki said: action with the limbs is from faith and is not complete without it, and he claimed consensus in this and argued with evidences that suggest the opposite of his purpose, such as His saying, the Exalted: 'those who believed and did righteous deeds,' for this indicates that action is beyond faith, not from the essence of faith, otherwise action would be in the ruling of repetition. And it is astonishing that he claimed consensus in this while he also transmits his saying (peace be upon him): 'No one becomes a disbeliever except after denying what he affirmed.' And he denies the Mu'tazilites' saying of eternal abiding in the Fire due to major sins, and the one who says this is saying with the same doctrine as the Mu'tazilites, for it is said to him: one who affirmed with his heart and testified with his tongue and died immediately, is he in Paradise? He must say yes, and in it is a ruling of the existence of faith without action. Then we add and say: if he remained alive until one prayer time entered upon him and he left it, then died, or fornicated then died, is he eternally abiding in the Fire? If he says yes, then it is the intent of the Mu'tazilites, and if he says no, then it is an explicit statement that action is not a pillar from the essence of faith nor a condition in its existence nor in deserving Paradise by it. And if he says: I intended by it that he lives a long time and does not pray nor proceeds to any of the lawful actions, then we say: so what defines that duration and what is the number of those acts of obedience (ta'at) by leaving which faith is invalidated, and what is the number of major sins by committing which faith is invalidated? And this cannot be arbitrarily determined, and no one has proceeded to it at all. The fourth degree is that the affirmation with the heart exists before he speaks with the tongue or engages in actions and died, so do we say he died as a believer?
40:58.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

40:60.arabic: (فضيلة الدعاء) قال الله تعالى: ﴿ وإذا سألك عبادي عني فإني قريب أجيب دعوة الداع إذا دعان فليستجيبوا لي ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ ادعوا ربكم تضرعا وخفية إنه لا يحب المعتدين ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ وقال ربكم ادعوني أستجب لكم إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي سيدخلون جهنم داخرين ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل: ﴿ قل ادعوا الله أو ادعوا الرحمن أيا ما تدعوا فله الأسماء الحسنى ﴾ {} وروى النعمان بن بشير عن النبي ﭬ أنه قال: (إن الدعاء هو العبادة ثم قرأ: ﴿ ادعوني أستجب لكم ﴾ {}[65]) الآية. وقال ﭬ: (الدعاء مخ العبادة[66]) وروى أبو هريرة أ
40:60.english: (The Excellence of Supplication) Allah the Exalted said: 'And when My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me' (Quran 2:186). And He said: 'Invoke your Lord in humility and secretly; indeed, He does not like transgressors' (Quran 7:55). And He said: 'And your Lord said, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you. Indeed, those who disdain My worship will enter Hell in humiliation"' (Quran 40:60). And the Mighty and Majestic said: 'Say, "Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Merciful. Whichever [name] you call - to Him belong the best names"' (Quran 17:110). And Nu'man ibn Bashir reported from the Prophet (peace be upon him) that he said: 'Supplication (Dua) is worship (Ibadah), then he recited: "Call upon Me; I will respond to you" (Quran 40:60).' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Supplication (Dua) is the marrow of worship (Ibadah).' And Abu Hurairah reported that he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing more honorable to Allah the Exalted than supplication (Dua).' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The servant (Abd) does not miss from supplication (Dua) one of three things: either a sin (Dhanb) is forgiven for him, or a good (Khayr) is hastened for him, or a good (Khayr) is stored for him.' And Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'Sufficient for supplication (Dua) with righteousness (Birr) is what suffices food from salt.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Ask Allah the Exalted from His bounty, for Allah the Exalted loves to be asked, and the best worship (Ibadah) is awaiting relief (Faraj).'
40:60.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication

40:62.arabic: وكما يقال هذه الصنعة المحكمة تشهد لصانعها بحسن التدبير وكمال العلم لا بمعنى أنها تقول أشهد بالقول ولكن بالذات والحال وكذلك ما من شيء إلا وهو محتاج في نفسه إلى موجد يوجده ويبقيه ويديم أوصافه ويردده في أطواره فهو بحاجته يشهد لخالقه بالتقديس يدرك شهادته ذوو البصائر دون الجامدين على الظواهر ولذلك قال تعالى: ﴿ ولكن لا تفقهون تسبيحهم ﴾ { سورة الإسرآء: 44}. وأما القاصرون فلا يفقهون أصلا وأما المقربون والعلماء الراسخون فلا يفقهون كنهه وكماله إذ لكل شيء شهادات شتى على تقديس الله سبحانه وتسبيحه ويدرك كل و
40:62.english: And as it is said: 'This precise craftsmanship bears witness for its maker through good management and perfect knowledge' - not meaning that it says 'I bear witness' through speech, but through essence (Dhāt) and state (Hāl). Likewise, there is nothing except that it is needy in its very self (Nafs) to a bringer-into-existence (Mūjid) who brings it into existence, preserves it, perpetuates its attributes, and returns it in its stages. So through its neediness, it bears witness for its Creator (Khāliq) through sanctification (Taqdīs). Those possessing insight (Dhū al-Baṣā'ir) perceive its testimony, not those rigidly adhering to outward appearances (Ẓawāhir). And therefore, the Exalted said: 'But you do not understand their glorification' (Surah Al-Isrā': 44). As for the deficient ones, they do not understand it at all. As for the close ones (Muqarrabūn) and firmly-rooted scholars (ʿUlamā' al-Rāsikhūn), they do not understand its reality (Kunh) and perfection, for everything has various testimonies (Shahādāt) regarding the sanctification (Taqdīs) of Allah, the Exalted, and His glorification (Tasbīḥ). And each one perceives according to the measure of his intellect (ʿAql) and insight (Baṣīrah). Enumerating those testimonies is not fitting for the knowledge of transaction (ʿIlm al-Muʿāmalah). This art is also among that in which the masters of outward appearances (Arbāb al-Ẓawāhir) and the masters of insight (Arbāb al-Baṣā'ir) differ in their knowledge of it, and through it appears the divergence of the inward (Bāṭin) from the outward (Ẓāhir). And in this station (Maqām) for the people of stations (Arbāb al-Maqāmāt) there is extravagance (Isrāf) and moderation (Iqtiṣād). So whoever is extravagant in elevating outward appearances ends up changing all outward appearances and proofs, or most of them, until they took the saying of the Exalted: 'And We shall cause their hands to speak to Us, and their feet to bear witness' (Surah Yā Sīn: 65) and His saying: 'And they will say to their skins, "Why did you testify against us?" They will say, "We were made to speak by Allah, who has made everything speak"' (Surah Fuṣṣilat: 21) and His saying: 'That is Allah, your Lord, Creator (Khāliq) of everything; there is no deity except Him, so how are you averted?' (Surah Ghāfir: 62) according to their outward meaning (Ẓāhir), so they did not understand that that is the tongue of state (Lisān al-Ḥāl), not the tongue of speech (Lisān al-Maqāl).
40:62.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Foundations of Belief'

40:65.arabic: لا إله إلا الله مخلصين له الدين الحمد لله رب العالمين ~ فسبحان الله حين تمسون وحين تصبحون وله الحمد في السموات والأرض وعشيا وحين تظهرون يخرج الحي من الميت ويخرج الميت من الحي ويحيي الأرض بعد موتها وكذلك تخرجون ومن آياته أن خلقكم من تراب ثم إذا أنتم بشر تنتشرون ~ اللهم إني أسألك إيمانا دائما ويقينا صادقا وعلما نافعا وقلبا خاشعا ولسانا ذاكرا وأسألك العفو والعافية والمعافاة الدائمة في الدنيا والآخرة ويصلي على محمد ﭬ ويدعو الله عز وجل بما شاء من حاجته عقيب هذا الدعاء
40:65.english: There is no god but Allah, dedicating the religion (Din) sincerely to Him. All praise is to Allah, Lord of the worlds ~ So glorify Allah when you reach evening and when you reach morning, and to Him is praise in the heavens and the earth, and at nightfall and when you are at noon. He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living, and He gives life to the earth after its death; and thus you will be brought forth. And among His signs is that He created you from dust, then behold, you are human beings dispersing ~ O Allah, I ask You for enduring faith (Iman) and truthful certainty (Yaqin) and beneficial knowledge and a humble heart (Qalb) and a remembering tongue (Lisan), and I ask You for pardon and well-being and enduring safety in this world and the Hereafter, and he sends prayers upon Muhammad ﭬ and supplicates to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, with whatever he wishes of his need following this supplication.
40:65.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

40:71.arabic: وذهبنا واستأذنا على ثالث فقال: ادخلوا إن لم تشغلونا عن ربنا فقرأت ﴿ ذلك لمن خاف مقامي وخاف وعيد ﴾{} فشهق شهقة فبدا الدم من منخريه وجعل يتشحط في دمه حتى يبس فتركناه على حاله وخرجنا فأدرته على ستة أنفس كل نخرج من عنده ونتركه مغشيا عليه ثم أتيت به إلى السابع فاستأذنا فإذا امرأة من داخل الخص تقول ادخلوا فدخلنا فإذا شيخ فان جالس في مصلاه فسلمنا عليه فلم يشعر بسلامنا فقلت بصوت عال ألا إن للخلق غدا مقاما فقال الشيخ بين يدي من ويحك ثم بقي مبهوتا فاتحا فاه شاخصا بصره يصيح بصوت له ضعيف أوه أوه حتى انقطع ذ
40:71.english: And we went and sought permission from a third, and he said: 'Enter if you do not distract us from our Lord (Rabb).' So I recited: 'That is for whoever fears My standing (Mawqif) and fears My threat (Wa'īd).' Then he gasped a gasp, and blood appeared from his nostrils, and he began to flail in his blood until it dried, and we left him in his state and went out. Then I took him to six individuals, each time we left from him and left him unconscious. Then I brought him to the seventh, and we sought permission, and behold, a woman from inside the enclosure said: 'Enter.' So we entered, and behold, an old man sitting in his prayer place (Musallā). We greeted him, but he did not perceive our greeting. So I said in a loud voice: 'Indeed, the creation (Khalq) has a standing (Maqām) tomorrow.' Then the old man said: 'Before whom, woe to you?' Then he remained stunned, with his mouth open, his gaze fixed, crying out with a weak voice: 'Oh, oh,' until that voice ceased. Then his wife said: 'Go out, for you will not benefit from him now.' Then after that, I inquired about the people, and behold, three had recovered, and three had joined Allah the Exalted. As for the old man, he remained for three days in his state, stunned and bewildered, not performing our obligation (Farḍ). Then after three, he regained his intellect (ʿAql). And Yazīd ibn al-Aswad considered him to be among the Substitutes (Abdāl), and he had sworn never to laugh, never to sleep reclining, and never to eat clarified butter (Samm).'
40:71.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

40:76.arabic: وشر أنواع الكبر ما يمنع من استفادة العلم وقبول الحق والانقياد له وفيه وردت الآيات التي فيها ذم الكبر والمتكبرين قال الله تعالى "والملائكة باسطو أيديهم" إلى قوله "وكنتم عن آياته تستكبرون" ثم قال "ادخلوا أبواب جهنم خالدين فيها فبئس مثوى المتكبرين" ثم أخبر أن أشد أهل النار عذاباً أشدهم عتياً على الله تعالى فقال "ثم لننزعن من كل شبعة أيهم أشد على الرحمن عتياً" وقال تعالى "فالذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة قلوبهم منكرة وهم مستكبرون" وقال عز وجل "يقول الذين استضعفوا للذين استكبروا لولا أنتم لكنا مؤمنين" وقال ت
40:76.english: And the worst type of arrogance (Kibr) is what prevents from benefiting from knowledge and accepting the truth and submitting to it, and in it came the verses which contain censure of arrogance (Kibr) and the arrogant ones (Mutakabbirun). Allah the Exalted said: "And the angels stretching forth their hands" up to His saying: "and you were arrogant (Tastakbirun) about His signs." Then He said: "Enter the gates of Hell (Jahannam), abiding therein. How wretched is the settlement of the arrogant ones (Mutakabbirun)." Then He informed that the most severely punished of the people of the Fire are the most insolent (Atiyyan) against Allah the Exalted, so He said: "Then We will surely extract from every faction those of them who were most insolent (Atiyyan) against the Most Merciful." And He said: "So those who do not believe in the Hereafter - their hearts are denying and they are arrogant (Mustakbirun)." And He the Mighty and Majestic said: "Those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant (Istakbaru): 'If not for you, we would have been believers.'" And He said: "Indeed, those who are arrogant (Yastakbirun) about My worship will enter Hell (Jahannam) humiliated." And He said: "I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant (Yatakabbarun) in the earth without right." It is said in the interpretation (Tafsir): I will lift the understanding of the Quran from their hearts (Qulub), and in some interpretations (Tafasir) I will veil their hearts (Qulub) from the dominion (Malakut). And Ibn Juraij said: I will turn them away from reflecting upon them and taking admonition from them.
40:76.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

41:11.arabic: الأصل الثامن: العلم بأنه تعالى مستو على عرشه بالمعنى الذي أراد الله تعالى بالاستواء وهو الذي لا ينافي وصف الكبرياء ولا يتطرق إليه سمات الحدوث والفناء وهو الذي أريد بالاستواء إلى السماء حيث قال في القرآن ثم استوى إلى السماء وهي دخان وليس ذلك إلا بطريق القهر والاستيلاء كما قال الشاعر: قد استوى بشر على العراق من غير سيف ودم مهراق واضطرّ أهل الحق إلى هذا التأويل كما التأويل كما اضطر أهل الباطن إلى تأويل قوله تعالى وهو معكم أينما كنتم إذ حمل ذلك بالاتفاق على الإحاطة والعلم وحمل قوله ﭬ قلب المؤمن بين
41:11.english: The Eighth Foundation: Knowledge that He (Exalted is He) is established upon His Throne with the meaning that Allah (Exalted is He) intended by 'istawa' (establishment), which is that which does not contradict the attribute of Majesty (al-Kibriya) nor is it subject to marks of origination (al-Huduth) and annihilation (al-Fana). And this is what is intended by 'istawa' (He established Himself) towards the heaven, where He said in the Quran: 'Then He established Himself (istawa) towards the heaven while it was smoke' (Quran 41:11). And that is only by way of domination (al-Qahr) and mastery (al-Istila), as the poet said: 'Bishr has established himself over Iraq without sword or spilled blood.' And the people of truth (Ahl al-Haqq) were compelled to this interpretation (ta'wil), just as the people of esotericism (Ahl al-Batin) were compelled to interpret His saying (Exalted is He): 'And He is with you wherever you are' (Quran 57:4), since that was unanimously understood as encompassing (al-Ihata) and knowledge (al-'Ilm). And they interpreted His saying (peace be upon him): 'The heart (Qalb) of the believer is between two fingers of the fingers of the Most Merciful' as power (al-Qudra) and strength (al-Quwwa). And they interpreted His saying (peace be upon him): 'The Black Stone is the right hand (Yamin) of Allah in His earth' as honor (al-Tashrif) and respect (al-Ikram). Because if it were taken according to its apparent meaning, impossibility (al-Muhal) would necessarily follow from it. Likewise, if 'istawa' (establishment) were taken according to settling (al-Istiqrar) and taking position (al-Tamakkun), it would necessarily follow that the one taking position is a body (Jism) in contact with the Throne, either equal to it, larger than it, or smaller than it, and that is impossible (Muhal). And whatever leads to impossibility is impossible.
41:11.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

41:11.arabic: القسم الخامس: أن يعبر بلسان المقال عن لسان الحال فالقاصر الفهم يقف على الظاهر ويعتقده نطقا والبصير بالحقائق يدرك السر فيه وهذا كقول القائل قال الجدار للوتد لم تشقني قال سل من يدقني فلم يتركني ورائي الحجر الذي ورائي فهذا تعبير عن لسان الحال بلسان المقال، ومن هذا قوله تعالى: ﴿ ثم استوى إلى السماء وهي دخان فقال لها وللأرض ائتيا طوعا أو كرها قالتا أتينا طائعين ﴾ {} فالبليد يفتقر في فهمه إلى أن يقدر لهما حياة وعقلا وفهما للخطاب وخطابا هو صوت وحرف تسمعه السماء والأرض فتجيبان بحرف وصوت وتقولان أتينا طا
41:11.english: The Fifth Category: That which expresses the tongue of the state (Lisan al-Hal) through the tongue of speech (Lisan al-Maqal). The deficient in understanding stops at the apparent and believes it to be literal speech, while the insightful into realities perceives the secret within it. This is like the saying of the speaker: 'The wall said to the peg: Why do you split me? It said: Ask the one who hammers me, for he did not leave behind me the stone that is behind me.' This is an expression of the tongue of the state (Lisan al-Hal) through the tongue of speech (Lisan al-Maqal). And from this is His saying, the Exalted: 'Then He directed Himself to the heaven while it was smoke and said to it and to the earth: Come both of you willingly or unwillingly. They said: We come willingly.' {} So the dull requires in his understanding to imagine for them life, intellect, and comprehension of the address, and an address that is sound and letter which the heaven and earth hear, then they respond with letter and sound and say: We come willingly. But the insightful knows that this is the tongue of the state (Lisan al-Hal) and that it is a declaration of their being compelled by necessity and forced into subjugation.
41:11.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Foundations of Belief'

41:15.arabic: الثاني البطش والقوة كما حكي عن قوم عاد حين قالوا فيما أخبر الله عنهم "من أشد منا قوة" وكما اتكل عوج على قوته وأعجب بها فاقتلع جبلاً ليطبقه على عسكر موسى عليه السلام، فثقب الله تعالى تلك القطعة من الجبل بنقر هدهد ضعيف المنقار حتى صارت في عنقه، وقد يتكل المؤمن أيضاً على قوته كما روي عن سليمان عليه السلام أنه قال: لأطوفن الليلة على مائة امرأة! ولم يقل إن شاء الله تعالى، فحرم ما أراد من الولد[91]. وكذلك قول داود عليه السلام: إن ابتليتني صبرت، وكان إعجاباً منه بالقوة، فلما ابتلي بالمرأة لم يصبر. ويور
41:15.english: The second: Pride in physical strength and power, as narrated about the people of 'Ad when they said, as Allah informed about them: "Who is mightier than us in strength?" And as 'Uj relied on his strength and became proud of it, so he uprooted a mountain to crush the army of Musa (peace be upon him), but Allah pierced that piece of the mountain with the pecking of a weak-beaked hoopoe until it became around his neck. And the believer may also rely on his strength, as narrated about Sulayman (peace be upon him) that he said: 'I will go around tonight to one hundred women!' and he did not say 'if Allah wills,' so he was deprived of the offspring he desired. Likewise, the saying of Dawud (peace be upon him): 'If You test me, I will be patient,' and it was pride from him in strength, so when he was tested with the woman, he was not patient. And pride in strength begets rushing into battles, throwing oneself into destruction, and hastening to strike and kill everyone who intends harm to him. Its remedy is what we mentioned, which is to know that there will come a day when his strength weakens! And that if he becomes proud of it, perhaps Allah will strip it from him with the slightest affliction He sends upon him.
41:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

41:17.arabic: وللهداية ثلاث منازل: الأولى معرفة طريق الخير والشر المشار إليه بقوله تعالى: ﴿ وهديناه النجدين ﴾ {} وقد أنعم الله تعالى به على كافة عباده بعضه بالعقل وبعضه على لسان الرسل ولذلك قال تعالى: ﴿ وأما ثمود فهديناهم فاستحبوا العمى على الهدى ﴾ {} فأسباب الهدى هى الكتاب والرسل وبصائر العقول وهى مبذولة ولا يمنع منها إلا الحسد والكبر وحب الدنيا والأسباب التى تعمى القلوب وإن كانت لا تعمى الأبصار قال تعالى: ﴿ فإنها لا تعمى الأبصار ولكن تعمى القلوب التى في الصدور ﴾ {} ومن جملة المعميات الإلف والعادة وحب استصحا
41:17.english: And for guidance (Hidayah) there are three stations: The first is knowledge of the path of good and evil, indicated by His saying, the Exalted: 'And We have shown him the two ways (of good and evil)' (Quran 90:10). And Allah, the Exalted, has bestowed this upon all His servants, some of it through the intellect (Aql) and some of it upon the tongue of the messengers. And therefore He, the Exalted, said: 'And as for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance' (Quran 41:17). So the means of guidance are the Book and the messengers and the insights of the intellects, and they are made available, and nothing prevents from them except envy (Hasad) and arrogance (Kibr) and love of the worldly life (Dunya) and the causes that blind the hearts (Qulub), even though they do not blind the eyesights. He, the Exalted, said: 'For indeed, it is not the eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts which are within the breasts' (Quran 22:46). And among the blinding things are familiarity (Ilf) and habit (Adah) and the love of adhering to them, and from it is the expression by His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion' (Quran 43:23) the verse. And from arrogance and envy is the expression by His saying, the Exalted: 'And they said, "Why was this Quran not sent down upon a great man from [one of] the two cities?"' (Quran 43:31) and His saying, the Exalted: 'Shall we follow a human being from among ourselves?' (Quran 54:24). So these blinding things are what prevented the attainment of guidance.
41:17.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

41:21.arabic: فمن مسرف في رفع الظواهر انتهى إلى تغيير جميع الظواهر والبراهين أو أكثرها حتى حملوا قوله تعالى: ﴿ وتكلمنا أيديهم وتشهد أرجلهم ﴾ { سورة يس:65 } وقوله تعالى: ﴿ وقالوا لجلودهم لم شهدتم علينا قالوا أنطقنا الله الذي أنطق كل شيء ﴾ { سورة فصلت:21 } وكذلك المخاطبات التي تجري من منكر ونكير وفي الميزان والصراط والحساب ومناظرات أهل النار وأهل الجنة في قولهم: ﴿ أفيضوا علينا من الماء أو مما رزقكم الله ﴾ { سورة الأعراف:50 } زعموا أن ذلك كله بلسان الحال
41:21.english: And from those who are excessive in elevating appearances, they ended up changing all appearances and proofs or most of them, until they interpreted His saying, the Exalted: 'And their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will bear witness' (Surah Ya-Sin: 65) and His saying, the Exalted: 'And they will say to their skins, "Why did you testify against us?" They will say, "Allah has caused us to speak - He who causes everything to speak"' (Surah Fussilat: 41:21) and likewise the dialogues that occur from Munkar and Nakir and in the Balance (Mizan) and the Path (Sirat) and the Reckoning (Hisab) and the debates of the people of the Fire and the people of the Garden in their saying: 'Pour upon us of water or from what Allah has provided you' (Surah Al-A'raf: 50). They claimed that all of that is by the tongue of the state (lisan al-hal).
41:21.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

41:23.arabic: وقال سفيان: من أذنب ذنبا فعلم أن الله تعالى قدره عليه ورجاء غفرانه غفر الله له ذنبه قال: لأن الله عز وجل عير قوما فقال: ﴿ وذلكم ظنكم الذي ظننتم بربكم أرداكم ﴾{} وقال تعالى: ﴿ وظننتم ظن السوء وكنتم قوما بورا ﴾ {}
41:23.english: And Sufyan said: Whoever commits a sin and knows that Allah the Exalted decreed it upon him and hopes for His forgiveness, Allah will forgive him his sin. He said: Because Allah the Mighty and Majestic reproached a people, saying: 'And that was your assumption (Zann) which you assumed about your Lord that has ruined you' (Quran 41:23). And He the Exalted said: 'And you assumed an evil assumption (Zann al-Sū') and you became a ruined people' (Quran 48:12).
41:23.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

41:26.arabic: الوجه الثاني: الذي تعظم به رذيلة الكبر أنه يدعو إلى مخالفة الله تعالى في أوامره، لأن المتكبر إذا سمع الحق من عبد من عباد الله استنكف عن قبوله وتشمر لجحده، ولذلك ترى المناظرين في مسائل الدين يزعمون أنهم يتباحثون عن أسرار الدين ثم إنهم يتجاحدون تجاحد المتكبرين، ومهما اتضح الحق على لسان واحد منهم أنف الآخر من قبوله، وتشمر لجحده واحتال لدفعه بما يقدر عليه من التلبيس وذلك من أخلاق الكافرين والمنافقين، إذ وصفهم الله تعالى فقال "وقال الذين كفروا لا تسمعوا لهذا القرآن والغوا فيه لعلكم تغلبون" فكل من ينا
41:26.english: The second aspect: That by which the baseness of arrogance is magnified is that it calls to opposing Allah the Exalted in His commands, because the arrogant one, when he hears the truth from a servant among the servants of Allah, disdains accepting it and prepares for its denial. Therefore, you see those who debate in matters of religion claiming that they investigate the secrets of religion, then they deny each other with the denial of the arrogant ones. Whenever the truth becomes clear on the tongue of one of them, the other disdains accepting it, prepares for its denial, and schemes to repel it with what he is capable of from deception. That is from the character traits of the disbelievers and hypocrites, as Allah the Exalted described them, saying: "And those who disbelieved said, 'Do not listen to this Quran and cause disruption in it that you might overcome.'" So everyone who debates for victory and silencing, not to seize the truth if he attains it, has shared with them in this character trait. Likewise, this carries over to the pride from accepting admonition, as Allah the Exalted said: "And when it is said to him, 'Fear Allah,' pride takes him to sin." And it is narrated from Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he recited it and said, "Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we return." A man stood commanding good and was killed, then another stood and said: They kill those who command justice among the people, so the arrogant one who opposed him and the one who commanded him out of arrogance were killed. And Ibn Mas'ud said: It is enough sin for a man when it is said to him, 'Fear Allah,' that he says: Mind your own self! And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said to a man, "Eat with your right hand." He said: I cannot. So the Prophet (peace be upon him) said, "May you not be able," and nothing prevented him except his arrogance. He said: So he did not raise it after that, meaning his hand became impaired. Therefore, his arrogance toward creation is great because it will call him to arrogance toward the command of Allah. And indeed, Iblis (Satan) was made an example of this, and what is narrated of his states is only to take lesson from it, for he said: I am better than him, and this arrogance is by lineage because he said: I am better than him, You created me from fire and created him from clay. That carried him to refrain from the prostration that Allah the Exalted commanded him with, and its beginning was arrogance toward Adam and envy for him. That dragged him to arrogance toward the command of Allah the Exalted, so that was the cause of his destruction for all eternity. This is a calamity from the calamities of arroganc
41:26.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

41:30.arabic: اعلم أنّ باعث الدين بالإضافة إلى باعث الهوى له ثلاثة أحوال: أحدها أن يقهر داعي الهوى فلا تبقى له قوة المنازعة ويتوصل إليه بدوام الصبر وعند هذا يقال من صبر ظفر والواصلون الى هذه الرتبة هم الأقلون فلا جرم هم الصديقون المقربون الذين قالوا ربنا الله ثم استقاموا فهؤلاء لازموا الطريق المستقيم واستووا على الصراط القويم واطمأنت نفوسهم على مقتضى باعث الدين وإياهم ينادي المنادي ﴿ يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة ارجعي الى ربك راضية مرضية ﴾ {}.
41:30.english: Know that the motivator of religion (bāʿith al-dīn) in relation to the motivator of desire (bāʿith al-hawā) has three states: The first is that it overcomes the caller of desire so that no strength of contention remains, and one attains it through persistence in patience (ṣabr), and at this point it is said: 'Whoever is patient prevails.' Those who reach this rank are the fewest, so undoubtedly they are the truthful ones (al-ṣiddīqūn) brought near (al-muqarrabūn) who said: 'Our Lord is Allah' then remained steadfast (istaqāmū). These have adhered to the straight path (al-ṭarīq al-mustaqīm) and stood firm on the upright path (al-ṣirāṭ al-qawīm), and their souls (nufūs) have become tranquil upon the requirement of the motivator of religion. To them the caller calls: 'O tranquil soul (al-nafs al-muṭmaʾinnah), return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing.'
41:30.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

41:30.arabic: وإلى هذا التفريد والتجريد الإشارة بقوله تعالى: " قل الله ثم ذرهم في خوضهم"، وبقوله تعالى: " إن الذين قالوا ربنا الله ثم استقاموا " بل هو معنى قولك " لا إله إلا الله " أي معبود ولا محبوب سواه، فكل محبوب فإنه معبود، فإن العبد هو المقيد والمعبود هو المقيد به، وكل محب مقيد بما يحبه. ولذلك قال الله تعالى: " أرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه " وقال ﭬ: " أبغض إله عبد في الأرض الهوى " ولذلك قال عليه السلام: " من قال لا إله إلا الله مخلصاً دخل الجنة"[27] ومعنى الإخلاص أن يخلص قلبه لله فلا يبقى فيه شرك لغير الله، ف
41:30.english: And to this singling out and purification is the indication by His saying, the Exalted: "Say: Allah, then leave them in their vain discourse," and by His saying, the Exalted: "Indeed, those who said: 'Our Lord is Allah,' then remained steadfast" - rather, it is the meaning of your saying "There is no god but Allah," meaning no worshipped one and no beloved one except Him, for every beloved one is worshipped, for the servant (al-'abd) is the bound one and the worshipped one (al-ma'būd) is what he is bound by, and every lover is bound by what he loves. Therefore, Allah, the Exalted, said: "Have you seen he who has taken his desire as his god?" and He said: "The most hated god of a servant on earth is desire." Therefore, upon him be peace, said: "Whoever says 'There is no god but Allah' sincerely enters Paradise," and the meaning of sincerity (al-ikhlāṣ) is that he purifies his heart (qalb) for Allah so that no partnership for other than Allah remains in it, thus Allah becomes the beloved of his heart and the worshipped of his heart and the intended of his heart only. Whoever is in this state, the world is his prison because it prevents him from witnessing his beloved, and his death is liberation from the prison and arrival at the beloved. So what is the state of one who has only one beloved and his longing for him has been prolonged and his imprisonment from him has extended, then he is freed from the prison and enabled with the beloved and enlivened with security forever and ever,
41:30.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

41:33.arabic: وقال ﭬ: (لا يسمع نداء المؤذن جن ولا إنس ولا شيء إلا شهد له يوم القيامة[2]) وقال ﭬ: (يد الرحمن على رأس المؤذن حتى يفرغ من أذانه[3]) وقيل في تفسير قوله عز وجل: ﴿ ومن أحسن قولا ممن دعا إلى الله وعمل صالحا ﴾ {فصلت: 33} نزلت في المؤذنين.
41:33.english: And he (peace be upon him) said: 'No jinn, human, or thing hears the call of the mu'adhdhin (caller to prayer) except that it testifies for him on the Day of Resurrection.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Hand of the Most Merciful is upon the head of the mu'adhdhin until he finishes his call.' And it is said in the interpretation of His (Exalted is He) saying: 'And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah and does righteous work?' {Fussilat: 41:33} it was revealed concerning the mu'adhdhins.
41:33.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

41:33.arabic: وقال تعالى: ﴿ومن أحسن قولا ممن دعا إلى الله وعمل صالحا﴾ ( سورة فصلت: الآية 33) وقال تعالى: ﴿ادع إلى سبيل ربك بالحكمة والموعظة الحسنة﴾ ( سورة النحل: الآية 125) وقال تعالى: ﴿ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة﴾( سورة البقرة: الآية 129و الآية:151، وسورة آل عمران، الآية:164 وسورة الجمعة، الآية:2.).
41:33.english: And He (Exalted is He) said: 'And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah and does righteous deeds' (Surah Fussilat: Verse 33). And He (Exalted is He) said: 'Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good admonition' (Surah An-Nahl: Verse 125). And He (Exalted is He) said: 'And teaches them the Book and the Wisdom' (Surah Al-Baqarah: Verse 129 and Verse 151, and Surah Al-Imran, Verse 164 and Surah Al-Jumu'ah, Verse 2).
41:33.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Book of Knowledge'

41:34.arabic: وقال أنس بن مالك في قوله تعالى "فإذا الذي بينك وبينه عداوة كأنه ولي حميم" إلى قوله "عظيم" هو الرجل يشتمه أخوه فيقول: إن كنت كاذباً فغفر الله لك وإن كنت صادقاً فغفر الله لي.
41:34.english: And Anas ibn Malik said regarding His (Allah's) saying, the Exalted: "Then the one between you and him is enmity as if he were a close friend (Wali Hameem)" to His saying "great" is the man whose brother insults him, so he says: If you are lying, may Allah forgive you, and if you are truthful, may Allah forgive me.
41:34.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

41:34.arabic: وقوله ادفع بالتي هي أحسن فإذا الذي بينك وبينه عداوة كأنه ولي حميم
41:34.english: And His saying: 'Repel with that which is better, then indeed he between whom and you was enmity will become as though he was a close friend (Wali Hameem).'
41:34.book_title: Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character
41:34.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character'

41:39.arabic: فانظر إلى الأرض وهى ميتة فإذا أنزل عليها الماء اهتزت وربت واخضرت وأنبتت عجائب النبات وخرجت منها أصناف الحيوانات ثم انظر كيف أحكم جوانب الأرض بالجبال الراسيات الشوامخ الصم الصلاب وكيف أودع المياه تحتها ففجر العيون وأسأل الأنهار تجرى على وجهها وأخرج من الحجارة اليابسة ومن التراب الكدر ماء رقيقا عذبا صافيا زلالا وجعل به كل شىء حى فأخرج به فنون الأشجار والنبات من حب وعنب وقضب وزيتون ونخل ورمان وفواكه كثيرة لا تحصى مختلفة الأشكال والألوان والطعوم والصفات والأرابيح يفضل بعضها على بعض فى الأكل تسقى بما
41:39.english: Then look at the earth while it is dead, then when We send down upon it water, it quivers and swells and greens and brings forth wonders of vegetation, and from it emerge varieties of animals. Then look how He has made firm the sides of the earth with the firmly fixed mountains, the lofty, deaf, hard ones, and how He has deposited waters beneath it, so He gushes forth springs and makes rivers flow upon its surface, and brings forth from the dry stones and from the turbid dust water, thin, sweet, pure, cool, and makes with it every thing alive, so He brings forth with it kinds of trees and vegetation from grain and grapes and herbs and olives and date palms and pomegranates and fruits many, not countable, differing in forms and colors and tastes and attributes and scents, some excelling over others in eating, watered with one water and emerging from one earth. If you say: Their difference is due to the difference of their seeds and origins, then when was there in the seed a date palm encircled with clusters of fresh dates, and when was there in one grain ears of corn, in every ear a hundred? Then look at the land of the deserts and search its exterior and interior, and you will see it as similar dust, then when water is sent down upon it, it quivers and swells and brings forth from every delightful pair colors different and vegetation similar and dissimilar, for each one a taste and scent and color and form differing from the other. Then look at its abundance and the difference of its varieties and the abundance of its forms, then the difference of the natures of vegetation and the abundance of its benefits and how Allah the Exalted has deposited in the remedies the strange benefits, so this vegetation nourishes and this...
41:39.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Contemplation'

41:42.arabic: الحمد لله الذي امتن على عباده بنبيه المرسل ﭬ وكتابه المنزل الذي لا يأتيه الباطل من بين يديه ولا من خلفه تنزيل من حكيم حميد حتى اتسع على أهل الأفكار طريق الاعتبار بما فيه من القصص والأخبار واتضح به سلوك المنهج القويم والصراط المستقيم بما فصل فيه من الأحكام وفرق بين الحلال والحرام فهو الضياء والنور وبه النجاة من الغرور وفيه شفاء لما في الصدور ومن خالفه من الجبابرة قصمه الله ومن ابتغى العلم في غيره أضله الله هو حبل الله المتين ونوره المبين والعروة الوثقى والمعتصم الأوفى وهو المحيط بالقليل والكثير و
41:42.english: Praise be to Allah who bestowed favor upon His servants with His sent Prophet (peace be upon him) and His revealed Book which falsehood does not approach from before it nor from behind it, a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy, until it expanded for the people of thoughts the path of consideration with what is in it of stories and reports, and became clear through it the traversing of the straight path and the upright way with what He detailed in it of rulings and distinguished between the lawful and the forbidden. It is the illumination and the light, and through it is salvation from delusion, and in it is healing for what is in the chests. And whoever opposes it from the tyrants, Allah breaks him, and whoever seeks knowledge in other than it, Allah misguides him. It is the firm rope of Allah and His clear light, and the trustworthy handhold and the most faithful refuge, and it encompasses the little and the much, the small and the great. Its wonders do not cease, and its marvels do not end. Its benefits cannot be encompassed by the people of knowledge with limitation, nor does it become worn out for the people of recitation with much repetition. It is the one that guided the first and the last. And when the jinn heard it, they did not delay but turned to their people as warners, and they said: 'Indeed, we have heard an amazing Qur'an that guides to right conduct, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate with our Lord anyone.' So everyone who believes in it has been granted success, and whoever speaks by it has spoken truthfully, and whoever holds fast to it has been guided, and whoever acts by it has attained success. And Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, it is We who sent down the Remembrance (Dhikr), and indeed, We will be its guardian.' And from the causes of its preservation in the hearts and the copies is the continuity of its recitation and the persistence in its study along with the performance of its manners and conditions, and the preservation of what is in it of the inward actions and the outward manners, and that must be explained.
41:42.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

41:46.arabic: وكما ان شراه الحطب والجبة مما يستغنى عنه خالقك ومولاك وإنما تشترينه لنفسك إذ خلقه سببا لاستراحتك فطاعاتك ومجاهداتك أيضا هو مستغن عنها وإنما هى طريقك إلى نجاتك فمن أحسن فلنفسه ومن أساء فعليها والله غنى عن العالمين ويحك يا نفس انزعى عن جهلك وقيسى آخرتك بدنياك فما خلقكم ولا بعثكم إلا كنفس واحدة و كما بدأنا أول خلق نعيده و كما بدأكم تعودون وسنة الله تعالى لا تجدين لها تبديلا ولا تحويلا
41:46.english: And just as the purchase of firewood and a cloak is something your Creator (Khaliq) and Master (Mawlā) is independent of, but you buy it for your own self (Nafs), since He created it as a means for your comfort, so too your acts of obedience (Tā'āt) and spiritual struggles (Mujāhadāt) - He is also independent of them, but they are your path to your salvation. So whoever does good, it is for his own self (Nafs), and whoever does evil, it is against it, and Allah is independent of the worlds. Woe to you, O self (Nafs)! Cast off your ignorance and measure your Hereafter (Ākhirah) by your worldly life (Dunyā), for He did not create you nor resurrect you except as a single soul (Nafs), and as We began the first creation, We will repeat it, and as He began you, you will return, and the established way (Sunnah) of Allah you will find no change or alteration for it.
41:46.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

41:50.arabic: وقال الله تعالى "ولئن أذقناه رحمة منا من بعد ضراء مسته ليقولن هذا لي وما أظن الساعة قائمة ولئن رجعت إلى ربي إن لي عند للحسنى" وهذا كله من الغرور بالله. وسببه قياس من أقيسة إبليس نعوذ بالله منه، وذلك أنهم ينظرون مرة إلى نعم الله عليهم في الدنيا فيقيسون عليهم نعمة الآخرة، وينظرون مرة إلى تأخير العذاب عنهم فيقيسون عليه عذاب الآخرة كما قال تعالى "ويقولون في أنفسهم لولا يعذبنا الله بما نقول" فقال تعالى جواباً لقولهم "حسبهم جهنم يصلونها فبئس المصير" ومرة ينظرون إلى المؤمنين؛ وهم فقراء شعث غبر فيزدرون
41:50.english: And Allah the Exalted said: "And if We give him a mercy (Rahmah) from Us after hardship (Darra') has touched him, he will surely say, 'This is due to me, and I do not think the Hour (As-Sa'ah) will occur; but if I am returned to my Lord (Rabb), indeed, for me there will be with Him the best (Al-Husna).'" And all of this is from delusion (Ghurur) with Allah. And its cause is a syllogism (Qiyas) from the syllogisms of Iblis (Satan) - we seek refuge in Allah from him - and that is that they look sometimes at the blessings (Ni'am) of Allah upon them in this world (Ad-Dunya) and analogize (Yaqisun) upon them the blessing (Ni'mah) of the Hereafter (Al-Akhirah), and they look sometimes at the delay (Ta'khir) of punishment (Adhab) from them and analogize upon it the punishment (Adhab) of the Hereafter (Al-Akhirah) as Allah the Exalted said: "And they say within themselves, 'Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?'" So Allah the Exalted said in response to their saying: "Sufficient for them is Hell (Jahannam), which they will [enter to] burn, and wretched is the destination (Al-Masir)." And sometimes they look at the believers (Al-Mu'minun); and they are poor (Fuqara'), disheveled (Shu'ath), dusty (Ghubar), so they disdain (Yazdarun) them and belittle (Yastahqirun) them, and they say: "Are these whom Allah has favored among us?" And they say: "If it were [any] good, they would not have preceded us to it." And the arrangement (Tartib) of the syllogism (Al-Qiyas) that He organized (Nazzamahu) in their hearts (Qulub) is that they say: Allah has done good (Ahsana) to us with the enjoyment (Na'im) of this world (Ad-Dunya), and every doer of good (Muhsin) is a lover (Muhibb), and every lover (Muhibb) then he does good (Yuhsinu) also in the future (Al-Mustaqbal) as the poet said: "Indeed Allah has done good (Ahsana) in what has passed, likewise He does good (Yuhsinu) in what remains." And indeed he analogizes (Yaqis) the future (Al-Mustaqbal) upon the past (Al-Madi) by means of honor (Al-Karamah) and love (Al-Hubb) when he says: Were it not that I am honorable (Karim) with Allah and beloved (Mahbub), He would not have done good (Ahsana) to me. And the deception (At-Talbis) is under his assumption (Zann) that every doer of good (Muhsin) is a lover (Muhibb), no, rather under his assumption (Zann) that His bestowing favor (In'am) upon him in this world (Ad-Dunya) is doing good (Ihsan), so he has been deluded (Ightarra) with Allah when he assumed (Zanna) that he is honorable (Karim) with Him by evidence (Dalil) that does not indicate (Yadullu) honor (Al-Karamah) except with the possessors of insight (Dhawu Al-Basa'ir).
41:50.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

41:51.arabic: والغالب على الخلق أنه لا تنصرف قلوبهم إلى ذكر الله عز وجل إلا عند إلمام حاجة وإرهاق ملمة فإن الإنسان إذا مسه الشر فذو دعاء عريض فالحاجة تحوج إلى الدعاء والدعاء يرد القلب إلى الله عز وجل بالتضرع والاستكانة فيحصل به الذكر الذي هو أشرف العبادات ولذلك صار البلاء موكلا بالأنبياء عليهم السلام ثم الأولياء ثم الأمثل فالأمثل لأنه يرد القلب بالافتقار والتضرع إلى الله عز وجل ويمنع من نسيانه وأما الغنى فسبب للبطر في غالب الأمور فإن الإنسان ليطغى أن رآه استغنى
41:51.english: And the predominant condition among creation is that their hearts (Qulub) do not turn to the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah, the Exalted, except when a need approaches and a calamity overwhelms. For indeed, when evil touches the human being, he is one of extensive supplication. The need compels to supplication, and supplication returns the heart (Qalb) to Allah, the Exalted, through humble entreaty and submission, thereby attaining the Remembrance (Dhikr) which is the most noble of acts of worship. Therefore, calamity has been entrusted to the Prophets, peace be upon them, then to the saints (Awliya), then to the most excellent among them, because it returns the heart (Qalb) through neediness and humble entreaty to Allah, the Exalted, and prevents from forgetting Him. As for wealth, it is a cause for arrogance in most matters, for indeed the human being transgresses when he sees himself self-sufficient.
41:51.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith

41:53.arabic: وإليه دعا الله سبحانه بقوله سنريهم آياتنا في الآفاق وفي أنفسهم وبقوله تعالى وفي الأرض آيات للموقنين وفي أنفسكم أفلا تبصرون وعلى القعود عن هذا السفر وقع الإنكار بقوله تعالى وإنكم لتمرون عليهم مصبحين وبالليل أفلا تعقلون وبقوله سبحانه وكأين من آية في السماوات والأرض يمرون عليها وهم عنها معرضون
41:53.english: And to this [journey] Allah the Exalted called with His saying: 'We will show them Our signs in the horizons and in themselves' and with His saying the Exalted: 'And on the earth are signs for those who have certainty (al-Mūqinīn) and in yourselves. Will you not then see?' And upon the abstention from this journey occurred the reproach with His saying the Exalted: 'And indeed, you pass by them in the morning and at night. Will you not then use intellect?' and with His saying the Exalted: 'And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by while they are turning away from it?'
41:53.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Travel'

41:53.arabic: وكذلك ذكر الله تعالى في القرآن من الأدلة والآيات في الأرض والسموات، ثم قال: "أو لم يكف بربك أنه على كل شيءٍ شهيد" وقال: "شهد الله أنه لا إله إلا هو" فبين أنه الدليل على نفسه وذلك ليس متناقضاً بل طرق الاستدلال مختلفة، فكم من طالب عرف الله تعالى بالنظر إلى الموجودات، وكم من طالب عرف كل الموجودات بالله تعالى كما قال بعضهم: عرفت ربي بربي، ولولا ربي لما عرفت ربي، وهو معنى قوله تعالى: "أو لم يكف بربك أنه على كل شيء شهيد"
41:53.english: And likewise, Allah the Exalted mentioned in the Quran from the proofs and signs in the earth and the heavens, then He said: "Or is it not sufficient for your Lord that He is over all things a Witness?" and He said: "Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him" so He clarified that He is the proof for Himself, and that is not contradictory, rather the paths of reasoning are different. For how many seekers have known Allah the Exalted by looking at the existent things, and how many seekers have known all the existent things through Allah the Exalted, as some of them said: I knew my Lord by my Lord, and were it not for my Lord, I would not have known my Lord. And this is the meaning of His saying the Exalted: "Or is it not sufficient for your Lord that He is over all things a Witness?"
41:53.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

41:53.arabic: والواصلون إلى هذه الرتبة ينقسمون إلى الأقوياء ويكون أول معرفتهم بالله تعالى، ثم به يعرفون غيره. وإلى الضعفاء ويكون أول معرفتهم بالأفعال ثم يترقون منها إلى الفاعل. وإلى الأول الإشارة بقوله تعالى: " أو لم يكف بربك أنه على كل شيء شهيد " وبقوله تعالى: " شهد الله أنه لا إله إلا هو " ومنه نظر بعضهم حيث قيل له: بم عرفت ربك؟ قال: عرفت ربي ولولا ربي لما عرفت ربي، وإلى الثاني بقوله تعالى: " سنريهم آياتنا في الآفاق وفي أنفسهم حتى يتبين لهم أنه الحق " الآية. وبقوله عز وجل: " أو لم ينظروا في ملكوت السموات وا
41:53.english: And those who reach this rank are divided into the strong ones whose first knowledge is of Allah the Exalted, then through Him they know others. And into the weak ones whose first knowledge is of the actions then they ascend from them to the Actor. And to the first is the indication by His saying the Exalted: "Or is it not sufficient for your Lord that He is over all things a Witness?" and by His saying: "Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him." And from this is the view of some of them when it was said to him: By what did you know your Lord? He said: I knew my Lord and were it not for my Lord I would not have known my Lord. And to the second by His saying the Exalted: "We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth." The verse. And by His saying the Mighty and Majestic: "Have they not looked into the dominion of the heavens and the earth?" And by His saying the Exalted: "Say, 'Look at what is in the heavens and the earth.'" And by His saying the Exalted: "[He] who created seven heavens in layers. You do not see in the creation of the Most Merciful any inconsistency. So return [your] vision; do you see any breaks? Then return [your] vision twice again. [Your] vision will return to you humbled while it is fatigued." And this path is the easiest for most people and it is the widest for the travelers, and to it is most of the call of the Quran when commanding contemplation (tadabbur), reflection (tafakkur), consideration (i'tibar), and looking at signs beyond enumeration.
41:53.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

42:5.arabic: الفن الثاني: استقراء الآيات والأخبار فما ورد في الرجاء خارج عن الحصر أما الآيات فقد قال تعالى: ﴿ قل يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا إنه هو الغفور الرحيم ﴾ {} وفي قراءة رسول الله ﭬ ولا يبالي إنه هو الغفور الرحيم[12] وقال تعالى: ﴿ والملائكة يسبحون بحمد ربهم ويستغفرون لمن في الأرض ﴾ {} وأخبر تعالى أن النار أعدها لإعدائه وإنما خوف بها أولياءه فقال: ﴿ لهم من فوقهم ظلل من النار ومن تحتهم ظلل ذلك يخوف الله به عباده ﴾{} وقال تعالى: ﴿ واتقوا النار التي أع
42:5.english: The Second Art: The examination of verses and reports, for what has come regarding hope is beyond enumeration. As for the verses, the Exalted has said: 'Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful."' {} And in the recitation of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him): 'And He does not care, indeed He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.' [12] And the Exalted said: 'The heavens almost break apart from above them, and the angels glorify with the praise of their Lord and seek forgiveness for those on the earth.' {} And the Exalted informed that the Fire He prepared for His enemies, and He only frightens His allies with it, so He said: 'For them are shades from the Fire above them and shades from beneath them. That is how Allah frightens His servants.' {} And the Exalted said: 'And fear the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers.' {} And the Exalted said: 'So I have warned you of a Fire that blazes fiercely; none will enter it except the most wretched, who denied and turned away.' {} And the Mighty and Majestic said: 'And indeed, your Lord is full of forgiveness for the people despite their wrongdoing.' {} And it is said: (Indeed, the Prophet (peace be upon him) kept asking for his nation until it was said to him, "Are you not satisfied, and this verse has been revealed to you: 'And indeed, your Lord is full of forgiveness for the people despite their wrongdoing.'" {} [13])
42:5.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

42:9.arabic: ام فادع الله حتى أؤمن على  دعائك  قال  فدعا فتجلت السماء سحابا ثم صبت فسقوا. وقال يحيى الغساني: أصاب الناس قحط على  عهد داود عليه السلام فاختاروا ثلاثة من  علمائهم  فخرجوا  حتى  يستسقوا  بهم  فقال أحدهم اللهم إنك أنزلت في توراتك أن نعفو عمن ظلمنا اللهم إنا قد ظلمنا  أنفسنا فاعف عنا. وقال الثاني اللهم إنك أنزلت في توراتك أن نعتق  أرقاءنا  اللهم  إنا أرقاؤك فأعتقنا وقال الثالث اللهم إنك أنزلت في توراتك أن لا نرد المساكين  إذا وقفوا بأبوابنا اللهم إنا مساكينك وقفنا ببابك فلا ترد دعاءنا فسقوا وقال
42:9.english: Or call upon Allah until I believe in your supplication, he said, so he called and the sky became covered with clouds then poured, so they were watered. And Yahya al-Ghassani said: The people were struck by drought during the time of Dawud (David), peace be upon him, so they chose three from their scholars and they went out until they sought rain through them. The first one said: O Allah, You revealed in Your Torah that we forgive those who wrong us, O Allah, we have wronged our souls (Anfus), so forgive us. The second said: O Allah, You revealed in Your Torah that we free our slaves, O Allah, we are Your slaves, so free us. The third said: O Allah, You revealed in Your Torah that we do not turn away the poor when they stand at our doors, O Allah, we are Your poor, standing at Your door, so do not reject our supplication, and they were watered. And 'Ata' al-Sulami said: We were deprived of rain, so we went out to seek rain, and behold we were with Sa'dun the Madman in the graveyards. He looked at me and said: O 'Ata', is this the Day of Resurrection (Yawm al-Nushur) or when what is in the graves is scattered? I said: No, but we were deprived of rain, so we went out to seek rain. He said: O 'Ata', with earthly hearts (Qulub) or with heavenly hearts (Qulub)? I said: Rather with heavenly hearts (Qulub). He said: Far be it, O 'Ata'! Tell the ostentatious ones not to be ostentatious, for the Critic is seeing. Then he glanced at the sky with his eye and said: My God, my Master, and my Protector (Mawla), do not destroy Your lands with the sins of Your servants, but with the hidden secret of Your names and what the veils have concealed of Your bounties, except that You give us abundant, sweet water to revive with it the servants and water with it the lands, O He who is over all things powerful (Qadir). 'Ata' said: He had not completed the speech until the sky thundered and lightninged and gave rain like the mouths of waterskins, and he turned away while saying: The ascetics (Zahidun) and worshippers ('Abidun) have succeeded, for they made their bellies hungry for their Protector (Mawla). They kept awake the sick eyes out of love, so their night passed while they were awake. The worship ('Ibadah) of Allah preoccupied them until people thought there was madness in them. And Ibn al-Mubarak said: I arrived in Medina in a year of severe drought, so the people went out to seek rain, and I went out with them. Then a black youth came wearing two pieces of coarse cloth, having girded with one of them and thrown the other over his shoulder, and he sat next to me. I heard him saying: My God, You have made the faces at You numerous with sins and bad deeds, and You have withheld from us the rain of the sky to discipline Your servants with that. I ask You, O Forbearing (Halim), possessor of forbearance (Ana), O He from whom His servants know nothing but beauty, that You give them drink now, now. He did not cease saying now, now until the sky became clothed with clouds and rain came from every side. Ibn al-Mubarak said: I came to al-Fudayl and he said: Why do I see you sad? I said: A matter that others preceded us to, so they undertook it instead of us, and I narrated to him the story. Al-Fudayl cried out and fell unconscious. And it is narrated that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, sought rain through al-'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him. When 'Umar finished his supplication, al-'Abbas said: O Allah, no calamity has descended from the sky except...
42:9.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

42:9.arabic: [197]  حديث القول عند دخول السوق لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له له الملك وله الحمد يحيي ويميت وهو حي لا يموت بيده الخير وهو على كل شيء قدير من حديث عمر وقال غريب والحاكم وقال صحيح على شرط الشيخين.
42:9.english: [197] The hadith about the saying when entering the market: 'There is no god but Allah alone, He has no partner, to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs the praise, He gives life and causes death, and He is the Living who does not die, in His hand is the good, and He is over all things capable (Qadir)' from the narration of Umar, and it was said to be rare (Gharib), and Al-Hakim said it is authentic according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs.
42:9.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication

42:11.arabic: أما صفات الله عز وجل فكقوله تعالى: ﴿ ليس كمثله شيء وهو السميع البصير ﴾ {} وكقوله تعالى ﴿ الملك القدوس السلام المؤمن المهيمن العزيز الجبار المتكبر ﴾ {} فليتأمل معاني هذه الأسماء والصفات لينكشف له أسرارها فتتح معان مدفونة لا تنكشف إلا للموفقين وإليه أشار علي رضي الله عنه بقوله ما أسر إلى رسول الله ﭬ شيئا كتمه عن الناس إلا أن يؤتي الله عز وجل عبدا فهما في كتابه فليكن حريصا على طلب ذلك الفهم[39] وقال ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه: من أراد علم الأولين والآخرين فليثور القرآن وأعظم علوم القرآن تحت أسماء الله
42:11.english: As for the attributes of Allah the Exalted, such as His saying: 'There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing (As-Sami'), the All-Seeing (Al-Basir)' (Quran 42:11), and His saying: 'The Sovereign (Al-Malik), the Holy (Al-Quddus), the Source of Peace (As-Salam), the Guardian of Faith (Al-Mu'min), the Overseer (Al-Muhaymin), the Almighty (Al-Aziz), the Compeller (Al-Jabbar), the Supreme (Al-Mutakabbir)' (Quran 59:23). So let him contemplate the meanings of these names and attributes so that their secrets may be unveiled to him, and hidden meanings may open up that are not unveiled except to those who are granted success (Al-Muwaffaqun). And to this, Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) alluded with his saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) did not conceal anything from the people that he confided to me, except that Allah the Exalted grants a servant understanding (Fahm) in His Book, so let him be eager in seeking that understanding.' And Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'Whoever desires the knowledge of the former and the latter, let him delve into the Quran, and the greatest knowledge of the Quran lies beneath the names of Allah the Exalted and His attributes, for most of creation has not grasped from them except matters suitable to their understandings, and they have not stumbled upon their depths.'
42:11.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

42:11.arabic: ولكن يعتقد أن الله تعالى واحد لا شريك له وأنه "ليس كمثله شيء وهو السميع البصير" وأن رسوله صادق فيما أخبر به ويتبع سنة السلف، ويؤمن بجملة ما جاء به الكتاب والسنة من غير بحث وتنقير وسؤال عن تفصيل، بل يقول آمناً وصدقنا ويشتغل بالتقوى واجتناب المعاصي وأداء الطاعات والشفقة على المسلمين وسائر الأعمال، فإن خاض في المذاهب والبدع والتعصب في العقائد هلك من حيث لا يشعر.
42:11.english: But he should believe that Allah the Exalted is One with no partner and that 'There is nothing like Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing' and that His Messenger is truthful in what he informed, and he follows the way of the predecessors, and he believes in the entirety of what came in the Book and the Sunnah without investigation, scrutiny, or asking for details, rather he says 'We believe and affirm' and occupies himself with piety (Taqwa) and avoiding sins (Ma'asi) and performing acts of obedience (Taa'at) and compassion (Shafaqa) towards the Muslims and other deeds, for if he delves into schools of thought, innovations (Bida'), and fanaticism in beliefs, he will perish without realizing it.
42:11.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

42:14.arabic: وقال تعالى في معرض الإنكار "أم يحسدون الناس على ما آتاهم الله من فضله" وقال تعالى "كان الناس أمة واحدة" إلى قوله "إلا الذين أوتوه من بعد ما جاءتهم البينات بغياً بينهم" قيل في التفسير: حسداً. وقال تعالى "وما تفرقوا إلا من بعد ما جاءهم العلم بغياً بينهم" فأنزل الله العلم ليجمعهم ويؤلف بينهم على طاعته، وأمرهم أن يتألفوا بالعلم فتحاسدوا واختلفوا إذ أراد كل واحد منهم أن ينفرد بالرياسة وقبول القول فرد بعضهم على بعض.
42:14.english: And the Exalted said in the context of reproach: "Or do they envy (yahsudūna) people for what Allah has given them of His bounty?" And the Exalted said: "Mankind was one community..." up to His saying: "...except those who were given it after clear proofs had come to them out of envy (baghyan) among themselves." It is said in the interpretation: envy (hasadan). And the Exalted said: "And they did not become divided except after knowledge had come to them out of envy (baghyan) among themselves." So Allah sent down knowledge to gather them and unite them in obedience to Him, and commanded them to unite through knowledge, but they envied (tahāsadū) and differed when each one of them wanted to monopolize leadership and acceptance of speech, so they rejected one another.
42:14.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

42:20.arabic: وقال تعالى: " من كان يريد حرث الآخرة نزد له في حرثه، ومن كان يريد حرث الدنيا نؤته منها وما له في الآخرة من نصيب ".
42:20.english: And He, the Exalted, said: "Whoever desires the cultivation (harvest) of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his cultivation (harvest); and whoever desires the cultivation (harvest) of the world, We give him thereof, but he has no share in the Hereafter."
42:20.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

42:22.arabic:
جدنا فيها غير بيت من  المسلمين
﴾ {}. البحث الثالث: عن الحكم الشرعي والإسلام والإيمان  حكمان  أخروي  ودنيوي.
أما الأخروي فهو الإخراج من النار ومنع التخليد إذ قال رسول الله ﭬ:  (يخرج  من
النار من كان في قلبه مثقال ذرة من إيمان[50]) وقد اختلفوا  في  أن  هذا  الحكم
على ماذا يترتب وعبروا عنه بأن الإيمان ماذا هو فمن قائل إنه  مجرد  العقد  ومن
قائل يقول إنه عقد بالقلب وشهادة  باللسان  ومن  قائل  يزيد  ثالثا  وهو  العمل
بالأركان ونحن نكشف الغطاء عنه ونقول من جمع بين هذه الثلاثة فلا  خلاف  في  أن
مستقره
42:22.english: We found in it other than a house from the Muslims. The third investigation: concerning the legal ruling and Islam and Faith (Iman) are two rulings: otherworldly and worldly. As for the otherworldly, it is the extraction from the Fire and prevention of eternal abiding, as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'He will be extracted from the Fire whoever has in his heart (Qalb) an atom's weight of faith (Iman).' And they differed regarding what this ruling depends upon, and they expressed it by saying: what is faith (Iman)? So from among them is one who says it is merely the belief (Aqid), and from among them is one who says it is belief (Aqid) with the heart (Qalb) and testimony (Shahadah) with the tongue, and from among them is one who adds a third, which is action (Amal) with the limbs. And we unveil the cover from it and say: whoever combines these three, there is no disagreement that his abode is Paradise. And this is the degree. The second degree is that two exist and some of the third, which is the saying and the belief (Aqid) and some actions (A'mal), but its possessor committed a major sin or some major sins. At this, the Mu'tazilites said: he exited from faith (Iman) by this and did not enter into disbelief (Kufr), rather his name is transgressor (Fasiq), and he is upon a station between the two stations, and he is eternally abiding in the Fire. And this is false as we will mention. The third degree is that the affirmation (Tasdiq) with the heart (Qalb) and testimony (Shahadah) with the tongue exist without actions (A'mal) with the limbs. And they differed regarding its ruling. So Abu Talib al-Makki said: action (Amal) with the limbs is from faith (Iman) and it is not complete without it, and he claimed consensus (Ijma') in it, and he argued with evidences that indicate the opposite of his purpose, such as His saying, the Exalted: 'Those who believed and did righteous deeds (Salihat)' since this indicates that action (Amal) is beyond faith (Iman), not from the essence of faith (Iman), otherwise action (Amal) would be in the ruling of repetition. And the wonder is that he claimed consensus (Ijma') in this, and he with that transmits his saying (peace be upon him): 'No one becomes a disbeliever (Kafir) except after his denial of what he affirmed.' And he denies upon the Mu'tazilites their saying of eternal abiding in the Fire due to major sins. And the one who says this is saying with the same doctrine of the Mu'tazilites, since it is said to him: whoever affirmed with his heart (Qalb) and testified with his tongue and died immediately, is he in Paradise? So he must say yes, and in it is a ruling of the existence of faith (Iman) without action (Amal). So we add and say: if he remained alive until one prayer time entered upon him and he abandoned it then died, or fornicated then died, is he eternally abiding in the Fire? So if he says yes, then it is the intent of the Mu'tazilites, and if he says no, then it is a clear statement that action (Amal) is not a pillar from the essence of faith (Iman) nor a condition in its existence nor in deserving Paradise by it. And if he says: I intended by it that he lives a long period and does not pray nor advances upon anything from the lawful actions (A'mal), then we say: so what defines that period and what is the number of those acts of obedience (Taa'at) that by abandoning them faith (Iman) becomes invalid, and what is the number of major sins that by committing them faith (Iman) becomes invalid? And this cannot be arbitrarily determined, and no one has proceeded to it at all. The fourth degree is that the affirmation (Tasdiq) with the heart (Qalb) exists before he speaks with the tongue or engages in actions (A'mal) and died, so do we say he died as a believer (Mu'min)?
42:22.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

42:24.arabic: وقد سوى الله تعالى بين من افترى على الله كذبا وبين من كذب بالحق فقال تعالى: (ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بالحق لما جاءه( (العنكبوت: 68). وقال تعالى: (فمن أظلم ممن كذب على الله وكذب بالصدق إذ جاءه( (الزمر: 32).
42:24.english: And Allah the Exalted equated between one who fabricates lies against Allah and one who denies the truth, as He said: 'And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah or denies the truth when it has come to him?' (Al-Ankabut: 68). And He said: 'So who is more unjust than one who lies about Allah and denies the truth when it comes to him?' (Az-Zumar: 32).
42:24.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Book of Knowledge'

42:25.arabic: فإن قلت: فأين مظنة الرجاء وموضعه المحمود؟ فاعلم أنه محمود في موضعين: أحدهما: في حق العاصي المنهمك إذا خطرت له التوبة فقال له الشيطان: وأنى تقبل توبتك فيقنطه من رحمة الله تعالى فيجب عند هذا أن يقمع القنوط بالرجاء ويتذكر "إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعاً" وأن الله كريم يقبل التوبة عن عباده وأن التوبة طاعة تكفر الذنوب قال الله تعالى "قل يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعاً إنه هو الغفور الرحيم وأنيبوا إلى ربكم" أمرهم بالإنابة وقال تعالى "وإني لغفار لمن تاب وآ
42:25.english: If you say: Where then is the place of hope (Rajā') and its praiseworthy location? Know that it is praiseworthy in two situations: The first: Regarding the immersed sinner when repentance (Tawbah) occurs to him, and Satan says to him: How will your repentance be accepted? So he despairs of the mercy of Allah the Exalted. At this point, he must suppress despair (Qunūṭ) with hope (Rajā') and remember "Indeed, Allah forgives all sins" and that Allah is generous, accepts repentance (Tawbah) from His servants, and that repentance (Tawbah) is an obedience that expiates sins. Allah the Exalted said: "Say, 'O My servants who have transgressed against themselves [by sinning], do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful. And return [in repentance] to your Lord.'" He commanded them with turning back (Inābah). And He said: "And indeed, I am Forgiving to whoever repents and believes and does righteousness and then continues in guidance." So if he expects forgiveness with repentance (Tawbah), he is hopeful (Rājī), but if he expects forgiveness with persistence [in sin], he is deluded (Maghrūr). Just as one for whom the time of Friday prayer becomes tight while he is in the market, and it occurs to him to hasten to the Friday prayer, and Satan says to him: You will not catch the Friday prayer, so stay in your place. He disbelieves Satan and goes running, hoping to catch the Friday prayer—he is hopeful (Rājī). But if he continues with trade and begins to hope that the Imam will delay the prayer for him until the middle of the time, or for others, or for some reason among the reasons he does not know—he is deluded (Maghrūr).
42:25.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

42:25.arabic: وعن أبي سعيد الخراز قال دخلت المسجد الحرام فرأيت فقيرا عليه خرقتان فقلت في نفسي هذا وأشباهه كل على الناس فناداني وقال والله يعلم ما في أنفسكم فاحذروه فاستغفرت الله في سري فناداني وقال وهو الذي يقبل التوبة عن عباده ثم غاب عني ولم أره
42:25.english: And from Abu Sa'id al-Kharraz, he said: I entered the Sacred Mosque (Masjid al-Haram) and saw a poor man wearing two ragged garments, so I said in my self (Nafs): 'This one and his likes are a burden on people.' Then he called out to me and said: 'And Allah knows what is in your souls (Anfusikum), so beware of Him.' So I sought forgiveness from Allah in my secret (inner self). Then he called out to me and said: 'And He is the One who accepts repentance (Tawbah) from His servants.' Then he disappeared from me and I did not see him.
42:25.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

42:26.arabic: ومنها انتظار الشفاعة في الآخرة فقد قال السلف استكثروا من الإخوان فإن لكل مؤمن شفاعة فلعلك تدخل في شفاعة أخيك وروى في غريب التفسير في قوله تعالى ويستجيب الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات ويزيدهم من فضله قال يشفعهم في إخوانهم فيدخلهم الجنة معهم ويقال إذا غفر الله للعبد شفت في إخوانه ولذلك حث جماعة من السلف على الصحبة و الألفة و المخالطة وكرهوا العزلة و الانفراد فهذه فوائد تستدعى كل فائدة شروطا لا تحصل إلا بها ونحن نفصلها
42:26.english: And among them is awaiting intercession in the Hereafter, for the predecessors said: 'Multiply brothers, for every believer has intercession; perhaps you will enter through the intercession of your brother.' And it was narrated in the rare interpretation regarding His saying, the Exalted: 'And He responds to those who have believed and done righteous deeds and increases them from His bounty' (Quran 42:26) - it said: 'He makes them intercede for their brothers, so He admits them to Paradise with them.' And it is said: 'When Allah forgives a servant, he intercedes for his brothers.' Therefore, a group of the predecessors urged companionship, affection, and mixing, and they disliked isolation and seclusion. These benefits each require conditions that are not attained except through them, and we will detail them.
42:26.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

42:27.arabic: فرب عبد تكون الخيرة له في الفقر والمرض ولو صح بدنه وكثر ماله لبطر وبغى قال الله تعالى: ﴿ ولو بسط الله الرزق لعباده لبغوا في الأرض ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ كلا إن الإنسان ليطغى أن رآه استغنى ﴾ {} وقال ﭬ: (إن الله ليحمى عبده المؤمن من الدنيا وهو يحبه كما يحمى أحدكم مريضه[93])
42:27.english: For indeed a servant (Abd) may have what is best for him in poverty and illness, and if his body were healthy and his wealth abundant, he would become arrogant and transgress. Allah the Exalted said: 'And if Allah were to expand the provision (Rizq) for His servants, they would surely transgress in the earth' (42:27). And He said: 'No! Indeed, man transgresses when he sees himself self-sufficient' (96:6-7). And He said: 'Indeed, Allah protects His believing servant (Abd) from the worldly life while He loves him, just as one of you protects his sick person' (Hadith).
42:27.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

42:30.arabic: وقال على كرم الله وجهه ألا أخبركم بأرجى آية في القرآن قالوا بلى فقرأ عليهم ﴿ وما أصابكم من مصيبة فبما كسبت أيديكم ويعفو عن كثير ﴾ {} فالمصائب في الدنيا بكسب الأوزار فإذا عاقبه الله في الدنيا فالله أكرم من أن يعذبه ثانيا وإن عفا عنه في الدنيا فالله أكرم من أن يعذبه يوم القيامة
42:30.english: And Ali (may Allah honor his face) said: 'Shall I not inform you of the most hopeful verse in the Quran?' They said: 'Yes.' So he recited to them: 'And whatever affliction befalls you is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much.' So the afflictions in the worldly life are due to earning sins. If Allah punishes him in the worldly life, then Allah is more generous than to punish him a second time. And if He pardons him in the worldly life, then Allah is more generous than to punish him on the Day of Resurrection.
42:30.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

42:36.arabic: وأما المعرفة بالبيان والبرهان فهو أن يعرف وجه فساد هذا القياس الذي نظمه في قلبه الشيطان، فإن كل مغرور فلغروره سبب، وذلك السبب هو دليل وكل دليل فهو نوع قياس يقع في النفس ويورث السكون إليه وإن كان صاحبه لا يشعر به ولا يقدر على نظمه بألفاظ العلماء. فالقياس الذي نظمه الشيطان فيه أصلان "أحدهما" أن الدنيا نقد والآخرة نسيئة وهذا صحيح "والآخر" قوله: إن النقاد خير من النسيئة، وهذا محل التلبيس فليس الأمر كذلك، بل إن كان النقد مثل النسيئة في المقدار والمقصود فهو خير وإن كان أقل منها فالنسيئة خير، فإن الكاف
42:36.english: And as for the knowledge (Ma'rifah) through clarification and proof, it is to know the aspect of the corruption of this analogy (Qiyas) that the Satan (Shaytan) has organized in his heart (Qalb), for every deluded one has a cause for his delusion, and that cause is evidence and every evidence is a type of analogy that occurs in the soul (Nafs) and produces tranquility (Sukun) towards it even if its possessor does not perceive it nor is able to formulate it with the words of the scholars. So the analogy that the Satan has organized has two principles: "the first" that the worldly life (Dunya) is cash and the Hereafter (Akhirah) is credit, and this is correct, "and the other" his saying: Indeed cash is better than credit, and this is the place of deception (Talbees), for the matter is not so, rather if the cash is like the credit in amount and purpose then it is better, and if it is less than it then the credit is better, for the deluded disbeliever (Kafir) spends in his trade a dirham to receive ten on credit and does not spend a dirham to receive ten in cash, so how does he spend the Hereafter which is better and more lasting for the worldly life which is lesser and more perishing? And this is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: "So whatever you have been given of anything, it is the enjoyment of the worldly life, and what is with Allah is better and more lasting for those who have believed and upon their Lord they rely (Tawakkul)." So whoever is deluded by the worldly life and does not know that what is with Allah is better and more lasting, then he is deluded.
42:36.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

42:36.arabic: فإن قلت: إنه ينتظر جوابه فليتلذذ بسماع جوابه وليس يسمع كلام الله تعالى. فاعلم أنه إن كان يعلم أنه لا يجيبه ويسكت عنه فقد بقيت له أيضا لذة في عرض أحواله عليه ورفع سريرته إليه كيف والموقن يسمع من الله تعالى كل ما يرد على خاطره في أثناء مناجاته فيتلذذ به وكذا الذي يخلو بالملك ويعرض عليه حاجاته في جنح الليل يتلذذ به في رجاء إنعامه والرجاء في حق الله تعالى أصدق وما عند الله خير وأبقى وأنفع مما عند غيره فكيف لا يتلذذ بعرض الحاجات عليه في الخلوات.
42:36.english: If you say: 'He awaits His response, so let him delight in hearing His answer, yet he does not hear the speech (Kalam) of Allah, the Exalted.' Know that even if he knows He will not respond and remains silent, there still remains for him a delight in presenting his states (Ahwal) to Him and raising his innermost secret (Sirrah) to Him. How much more so for the one who is certain (Mūqin) that he hears from Allah, the Exalted, everything that comes to his mind during his intimate conversation (Munājāh), and delights in it. Similarly, the one who secludes himself with a king and presents his needs to him in the depth of the night delights in it in hope (Rajā') of his favor. And hope in the right of Allah, the Exalted, is truer, and what is with Allah is better and more lasting and more beneficial than what is with others, so how can he not delight in presenting his needs to Him in seclusions?
42:36.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

42:38.arabic: وأما الرتبة العليا فهي التي وصف الله تعالى المؤمنين بها في قوله وأمرهم شورى بينهم ومما رزقناهم ينفقون أي كانوا خلطاء في الأموال لا يميز بعضهم رحله عن بعض وكان منهم من لا يصحب من قال نعلى لأنه أضافه إلى نفسه
42:38.english: And as for the highest rank, it is that which Allah the Exalted described the believers with in His saying: 'And their affair is consultation (Shura) between them, and from what We have provided them they spend.' Meaning they were partners in wealth, not distinguishing some of their belongings from others. And among them was he who would not accompany one who said 'mine' because he attributed it to himself.
42:38.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

42:42.arabic: وقال الحسن من نم إليك نم عليك. وهذه إشارة إلى أن النمام ينبغي أن يبغض ولا يوثق بقوله ولا بصداقته. وكيف لا يبغض وهو لا ينفك عن الكذب والغيبة والغدر والخيانة والغل والحسد والنفاق والإفساد بين الناس والخديعة وهو ممن يسعون في قطع ما أمر الله به أن يوصل ويفسدون في الأرض؟ وقال تعالى "إنما السبيل على الذين يظلمون الناس ويبغون في الأرض بغير الحق" والنمام منهم. وقال ﭬ "إن من شرار الناس من اتقاه الناس لشره"[236] والنمام منهم. وقال "لا يدخل الجنة قاطع" قيل وما القاطع؟ قال "قاطع بين الناس"[237] وهو النمام و
42:42.english: And Al-Hasan said: 'Whoever backbites (nam) to you will backbite about you.' This is an indication that the backbiter (namam) should be hated and not trusted in his speech nor in his friendship. And how could he not be hated when he does not cease from lying, backbiting (ghibah), treachery, betrayal, malice, envy, hypocrisy, corruption between people, and deception? And he is among those who strive to sever what Allah has commanded to be joined and corrupt in the earth? And Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, the way is only against those who wrong the people and tyrannize upon the earth without right' and the backbiter is among them. And He said: 'Indeed, among the worst of people is he whom people fear for his evil' and the backbiter is among them. And He said: 'The cutter will not enter Paradise.' It was said: 'What is the cutter?' He said: 'The one who cuts between people' and he is the backbiter, and it is said: the cutter of kinship ties.
42:42.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'
