42:43.arabic: وإنما أدبه القرآن بمثل قوله تعالى خذ العفو وأمر بالعرف وأعرض عن الجاهلين وقوله إن الله يأمر بالعدل والإحسان وإيتاء ذي القربى وينهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر والبغي وقوله واصبر على ما أصابك إن ذلك من عزم الأمور وقوله ولمن صبر وغفر إن ذلك لمن عزم الأمور وقوله فاعف عنهم واصفح إن الله يحب المحسنين وقوله وليعفوا وليصفحوا ألا تحبون أن يغفر الله لكم وقوله ادفع بالتي هي أحسن فإذا الذي بينك وبينه عداوة كأنه ولي حميم وقوله والكاظمين الغيظ والعافين عن الناس والله يحب المحسنين وقوله اجتنبوا كثيرا من الظن إن بعض ال
42:43.english: And indeed, the Quran educated him (the Prophet) with verses like His saying: 'Take forgiveness and command what is good and turn away from the ignorant ones' (Quran 7:199), and His saying: 'Indeed, Allah commands justice and good conduct and giving to relatives and forbids immorality and bad conduct and oppression' (Quran 16:90), and His saying: 'And be patient over what befalls you. Indeed, that is of the matters of determination (min 'azm al-umur)' (Quran 31:17), and His saying: 'And whoever is patient and forgives - indeed, that is of the matters of determination (min 'azm al-umur)' (Quran 42:43), and His saying: 'So pardon them and overlook. Indeed, Allah loves the doers of good' (Quran 5:13), and His saying: 'And let them pardon and overlook. Would you not like that Allah should forgive you?' (Quran 24:22), and His saying: 'Repel [evil] by that [deed] which is better; and thereupon the one whom between you and him is enmity [will become] as though he was a devoted friend' (Quran 41:34), and His saying: 'And those who restrain anger and pardon the people - and Allah loves the doers of good' (Quran 3:134), and His saying: 'Avoid much [negative] assumption. Indeed, some assumption is sin. And do not spy or backbite each other' (Quran 49:12).
42:43.book_title: Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character
42:43.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character'

42:45.arabic: وَيَنْظُرُونَ مِنْ طَرْفٍ خَفِيٍّ خَاشِعٍ وَانْهَضَمَتْ عِنْدَ ذَلِكَ قُلُوبُ الظَّالِمِينَ فَبَلَغَتِ الْحَنَاجِرَ كَاظِمِينَ وَذَهَلَتِ الْعُقُولُ مِنَ السُّعَدَاءِ وَالأَشْقِيَاءِ أَجْمَعِينَ
42:45.english: And they look from a hidden glance (طَرْفٍ خَفِيٍّ), humbled (خَاشِعٍ), and at that moment the hearts (قلوب) of the wrongdoers (الظَّالِمِينَ) were crushed, reaching the throats (الحَنَاجِرَ) while suppressing (كَاظِمِينَ), and the intellects (العُقُولُ) of the fortunate (السُّعَدَاءِ) and the wretched (الأَشْقِيَاءِ) all were bewildered.
42:45.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

42:45.arabic: وقوله تعالى: ﴿ ألا إن الظالمين في عذاب مقيم ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ ومن جاء بالسيئة فكبت وجوههم في النار ﴾ {} فهذه العمومات في معارضة عموماتهم ولا بد من تسليط التخصص والتأويل على الجانبين لأن الأخبار مصرحة بأن العصاة يعذبون[52] بل قوله تعالى: ﴿ وإن منكم إلا واردها ﴾ {} كالصريح في أن ذلك لا بد منه للكل إذ لا يخلو مؤمن عن ذنب يرتكبه
42:45.english: And His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, the wrongdoers (al-ẓālimīn) are in an enduring punishment (ʿadhāb muqīm)' (Quran 42:45). And His saying, the Exalted: 'And whoever comes with an evil deed, their faces will be thrust into the Fire' (Quran 27:90). These general statements (ʿumūmāt) are in opposition to their general statements, and it is necessary to apply specification (takhṣīṣ) and interpretation (taʾwīl) to both sides because the reports explicitly state that the disobedient (al-ʿuṣāh) are punished. Indeed, His saying, the Exalted: 'And there is none of you but will pass over it (Hell)' (Quran 19:71) is like the explicit in that this is inevitable for all, since no believer (muʾmin) is free from a sin (dhanb) he commits.
42:45.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

42:47.arabic: الذين يغلب على قلوبهم ما ليس مكروها لذاته بل لغيره كالذين يغلب عليهم خوف الموت قبل التوبة أو خوف نقض التوبة ونكث العهد أو خوف ضعف القوة عن الوفاء بتمام حقوق الله تعالى أو خوف زوال رقة القلب وتبدلها بالقساوة أو خوف الميل عن الإستقامة أو خوف إستيلاء العادة في اتباع الشهوات المألوفة أو خوف أن يكله الله تعالى إلى حسناته التي أتكل عليها وتعزز بها في عباد الله أو خوف البطر بكثرة نعم الله عليه أو خوف الإشتغال عن الله بغير الله أو خوف الإستدراج بتواتبر النعم أو خوف إنكشاف غوائل طاعاته حيث يبدو له من الل
42:47.english: Those upon whose hearts predominates what is not disliked in itself but for something else, such as those upon whom predominates the fear of death before repentance, or the fear of breaking repentance and violating the covenant, or the fear of weakness of strength in fulfilling the complete rights of Allah the Exalted, or the fear of the removal of tenderness of the Heart (Qalb) and its replacement with hardness, or the fear of deviation from uprightness, or the fear of the domination of habit in following accustomed lusts, or the fear that Allah the Exalted will abandon him to his good deeds upon which he relied and took pride in before the servants of Allah, or the fear of arrogance due to the abundance of Allah's blessings upon him, or the fear of being occupied with other than Allah instead of Allah, or the fear of being lured by the succession of blessings, or the fear of the exposure of the hidden dangers of his acts of obedience when there appears to him from Allah what he had not reckoned, or the fear of the consequences of people with him in backbiting, betrayal, deceit, and harboring evil, or the fear of what he does not know will occur in the remainder of his lifespan, or the fear of the hastening of punishment in this world and exposure before death, or the fear of being deceived by the adornments of this world, or the fear of Allah's awareness of his secret thoughts in his state of heedlessness of Him, or the fear of being sealed at death with a bad ending, or the fear of the precedent that was decreed for him in pre-eternity. All of these are fears, and each one has a specific benefit, which is treading the path of caution from what leads to the feared thing. So whoever fears the domination of habit upon him persists in weaning from the habit, and whoever fears Allah the Exalted's awareness of his secret thoughts occupies himself with purifying his Heart (Qalb) from whisperings, and so on for the remaining categories. Most of these fears, with certainty, is the fear of the ending, for the matter in it is perilous. The highest of the categories and most indicative of the perfection of knowledge is the fear of the precedent, because the ending follows the precedent and is a branch that branches from it after the interposition of many causes. Thus the ending reveals what was decreed by the judgment in the Mother of the Book. The one who fears the ending in comparison to the one who fears the precedent is like two men for whom the king issued a decree that could contain beheading or could contain the handing over of the ministry to him, and the decree has not yet reached them, so the heart of one of them becomes attached.
42:47.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

42:47.arabic: بل في الحديث الصحيح ما روي أنه ﭬ قال "من كانت لأخيه عنده مظلمة في عرض أو مال فليستحللها منه من قبل أن يأتي يوم ليس هناك دينار ولا درهم، إنما يؤخذ من حسناته فإن لم يكن له حسنات أخذ من سيئات صاحبه فزيدت على سيئاته"[226]
42:47.english: Rather, in the authentic hadith, it is narrated that he (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever has a grievance against his brother in honor or wealth, let him seek its resolution from him before there comes a day where there is no dinar nor dirham; indeed, it will be taken from his good deeds, and if he has no good deeds, it will be taken from the bad deeds of his companion and added to his bad deeds."
42:47.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

42:51.arabic: فلم يفارق الإلهام الاكتساب في نفس العلم ولا في محله ولا في سببه ولكن يفارقه من جهة زوال الحجاب فإن ذلك ليس باختيار العبد ولم يفارق الوحي الإلهام في شيء من ذلك بل في مشاهدة الملك المفيد للعلم فإن العلم إنما يحصل في قلوبنا بواسطة الملائكة وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى وما كان لبشر أن يكلمه الله إلا وحيا أو من وراء حجاب أو يرسل رسولا فيوحي بإذنه ما يشاء فإذا عرفت هذا فاعلم أن ميل أهل التصوف إلى العلوم الإلهامية دون التعليمية فلذلك لم يحرصوا على دراسة العلم وتحصيل ما صنفه المصنفون والبحث عن الأقاويل وال
42:51.english: Inspiration (Ilham) does not differ from acquisition in the essence of knowledge, nor in its place, nor in its cause, but it differs from it in terms of the removal of the veil (Hijab), for that is not by the choice of the servant. And revelation (Wahy) does not differ from inspiration in any of that, but in witnessing the angel who conveys knowledge, for knowledge only occurs in our hearts through the mediation of angels, and to this is the indication by His saying, the Exalted: 'And it is not for any human being that Allah should speak to him except by revelation (Wahy) or from behind a veil (Hijab) or that He sends a messenger to reveal, by His permission, what He wills.' So if you know this, then know that the inclination of the people of Sufism (Tasawwuf) is towards inspirational sciences (Ulum Ilhamiyyah) rather than instructional ones, therefore they did not strive to study knowledge and acquire what the authors have compiled and research the mentioned statements and proofs, but they said: The path is to prioritize struggle (Mujahadah) and erase blameworthy attributes and cut off all attachments and turn with the core of aspiration (Himmah) towards Allah, the Exalted. And whenever that occurs, Allah is the one who takes charge of the heart (Qalb) of His servant and undertakes to illuminate it with the lights of knowledge. And when Allah takes charge of the matter of the heart, mercy (Rahmah) overflows upon it, and light (Nur) shines in the heart, and the chest expands, and the secret of the dominion (Malakut) is unveiled to him, and the veil of heedlessness (Ghurrah) is lifted from the face of the heart by the gentleness of mercy, and the realities (Haqa'iq) of divine matters gleam in it. So upon the servant is only preparation through pure purification (Tasfiyah) and bringing aspiration with sincere intention (Iradah) and complete thirst and constant anticipation in waiting for what Allah, the Exalted, opens of mercy. So the prophets and the saints (Awliya), the matter was unveiled to them and light overflowed upon their chests, not by learning and studying and writing books, but by asceticism (Zuhd) in the world and disengagement from its attachments and emptying the heart from its distractions and turning with the core of aspiration towards Allah, the Exalted. So whoever is for Allah, Allah is for him. And they claimed that the path in that is first by completely cutting off attachments of the world and emptying the heart from it.
42:51.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

42:51.arabic: والقلب بيت هو منزل الملائكة ومهبط أثرهم ومحل استقرارهم والصفات الرديئة مثل والغضب والشهوة والحقد والحسد والكبر والعجب وأخواتها كلاب نابحة فأنى تدخله الملائكة وهو مشحون بالكلاب ونور العلم لا يقذفه الله تعالى في القلب إلا بواسطة الملائكة (وما كان لبشر أن يكلمه الله إلا وحيا أو من وراء حجاب أو يرسل رسولا فيوحي بإذنه ما يشاء( (الشورى: 51). وهكذا ما يرسل من رحمة العلوم إلى القلوب إنما تتولاها الملائكة الموكلون بها وهم المقدسون المطهرون المبرءون عن الصفات المذمومات فلا يلاحظون إلا طيبا ولا يعمرون بما
42:51.english: And the Heart (Qalb) is a house that is the abode of the angels, the descent place of their effect, and the location of their settlement. And the blameworthy attributes such as anger, desire, malice, envy, arrogance, self-admiration, and their sisters are barking dogs. So how can the angels enter it when it is filled with dogs? And the light of knowledge, Allah the Exalted does not cast it into the heart except through the intermediary of the angels: 'And it is not for any human that Allah should speak to him except by revelation or from behind a partition or that He sends a messenger and he reveals by His permission what He wills' (Ash-Shura: 51). And thus, what is sent from the mercy of knowledges to the hearts, indeed the angels entrusted with them take charge of it, and they are the sanctified, purified, and absolved from the blameworthy attributes. So they do not observe except what is pure, and they do not populate with what they have from the treasuries of Allah's mercy except what is pure and clean. And I do not say that the intended meaning of the word 'house' is the heart and of 'dog' is anger and the blameworthy attributes, but I say it is an alerting to it. And there is a difference between expressing the apparent to the inner realities and alerting the inner realities from mentioning the apparent while affirming the apparent. So the esotericists differ in this subtlety, for this is the way of consideration, and it is the path of the scholars and the righteous. For the meaning of consideration is to cross over from what is mentioned to something else, not restricting oneself to it. Just as the intelligent person sees a calamity for someone else, then there is for him in it a lesson by crossing over from it to being alerted that he too is exposed to calamities and that the world is on the verge of reversal. So his crossing over from someone else to himself and from himself to the origin of the world is a praiseworthy lesson. So cross over you also from the house that is the construction of creation to the heart that is a house from the construction of Allah the Exalted, and from the dog that is blamed for its attribute, not its form, which is what is in it of beastliness and impurity, to the canine spirit, which is the beastliness.
42:51.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Book of Knowledge'

42:51.arabic: استماعه من المرأة التي ليست بمحرم له لا يجوز عند أصحاب الشافعي رحمه الله بحال سواء كانت مكشوفة أو من وراء حجاب وسواء كانت حرة أو مملوكة
42:51.english: Listening to it from a woman who is not a mahram (unmarriageable relative) for him is not permissible according to the companions of Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, in any case, whether she is uncovered or from behind a veil (hijab), and whether she is free or enslaved.
42:51.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

42:52.arabic: وقد سماه الله نورا في قوله تعالى: (الله نور السموات والأرض مثل نوره كمشكاة( وسمى العلم المستفاد منه روحا ووحيا وحياة فقال تعالى: (وكذلك أوحينا إليك روحا من أمرنا( وقال سبحانه (أومن كان ميتا فأحييناه وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به في الناس( وحيث ذكر النور والظلمة أراد به العلم والجهل كقوله (يخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور(.
42:52.english: And Allah has named it (the intellect) light in His saying: 'Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The example of His light is like a niche...' (Quran 24:35). And He named the knowledge derived from it spirit (Ruh) and revelation (Wahy) and life (Hayat). So He said: 'And thus We have revealed to you a spirit (Ruh) from Our command...' (Quran 42:52). And He said, glorified be He: 'Or is one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people...' (Quran 6:122). And wherever He mentioned light (Nur) and darkness (Zulmah), He intended by it knowledge (Ilm) and ignorance (Jahl), like His saying: 'He brings them out from darknesses into the light...' (Quran 2:257).
42:52.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

42:53.arabic: وأما الشجر فإنه خلقه الله تعالى وخلق له العروق وساق إليه الماء  وخلق فيه قوة الاغتذاء والنماء ليبلغ منتهى نشوه فينتفع به عباده  فكسره  قبل  منتهى نشوة لا على وجه ينتفع به عباده مخالفة لمقصود الحكمة وعدول عن العدل  فإن  كان له غرض صحيح فله ذلك إذ الشجر والحيوان جعلا فداء لأغراض الإنسان فإنهما  جميعا فانيان هالكان فإفناء الأخس في بقاء الأشرف مدة ما أقرب إلى العدل من  تضييعهما جميعا وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى: ﴿ وسخر لكم  ما  في  السموات  وما  في  الأرض جميعا منه ﴾ {} نعم إذا كسر ذلك من ملك غيره فهو
42:53.english: As for the tree, indeed Allah the Exalted created it and created for it roots and directed water to it, and created in it the power of nourishment and growth so that it reaches the peak of its maturity to benefit His servants (عباده). Breaking it before the peak of maturity in a way that does not benefit His servants is contrary to the purpose of wisdom and a deviation from justice (العدل). If there is a valid purpose for it, then that is permissible, since trees and animals are made as ransom for human purposes, for both are perishable, vanishing. The perishing of the lower in the survival of the nobler for a period is closer to justice than wasting both. To this is the allusion in His saying the Exalted: 'And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, all from Him' {}. Yes, if one breaks that from the property of another, he is also unjust even if needy, because each specific tree does not fulfill the needs of all the servants of Allah but fulfills one need. If one is specified with it without preference and specification, it is injustice. The one with specification is the one who obtained the seed and placed it in the earth and directed water to it and undertook care, so he is more entitled to it than others, and his side returns with that. If that grows in barren land without human effort, it is specified by its planting place or by planting it, so another specification must be sought, which is precedence in taking it, for the precedent has the characteristic of precedence. Justice is that one be more entitled to it. The poor expressed this preference as ownership, and it is purely metaphorical, for there is no ownership except for the King of kings who has what is in the heavens and the earth. How can the servant be an owner when he himself does not own himself but is owned by another? Yes, the creation are the servants of Allah and the earth is the table of Allah, and He has permitted them to eat from His table according to their need, like a king who sets a table for his servants. If one takes a morsel with his right hand and encloses it with his knuckles, and another servant comes and wants to snatch it from his hand, it cannot be taken from him, not because the morsel has become his property by taking with the hand, for the hand and its owner are also owned. But if each specific morsel does not fulfill the need of all the servants, justice in specification occurs when there is a kind of preference and specification, and taking is a specification that the servant uniquely has, so preventing one who does not present that specification from competing with him. Thus should the command of Allah in His servants be understood. Therefore, we say: whoever takes from the wealth of the world more than his need and hoards it and holds it back while among the servants of Allah is one who needs it, he is unjust and is among those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the path of Allah (سبيل الله). And the path of Allah is obedience to Him, and the provision for the creation in His obedience is the wealth of the world, for with it their necessities are repelled and their needs are raised. Yes, this does not enter into the scope of legal rulings because the measures of needs are hidden, and the souls in sensing poverty in the future are different, and the ends of lifespans are unknown, so imposing that on the common people runs the course.
42:53.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

42:53.english: And to Allah return the matters.
42:53.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Condemnation of the World'

43:9.arabic: فقد رآني فإن الشيطان لا يتخيل بي متفق عليه من حديث أبي هريرة. [142] حديث ابن عيينة عن محمد بن المنكدر عن جابر ما سئل النبي ﭬ شيئا قط فقال لا رواه مسلم وقد تقدم. [143] حديث قال الله تعالى شمتنى ابن آدم وما ينبغى له أن يشتمنى وكذبنى ما ينبغى له أن يكذبنى الحديث أخرجه البخارى من حديث أبى هريرة. [144] حديث كيف أنعم وصاحب الصور قد التقم القرن وحنى الجبهة الحديث أخرجه الترمذى من حديث أبى سعيد وقال حسن ورواه ابن ماجه بلفظ إن صاحبى القرن بأيديهما أو فى أيديهما قرنان يلاحظان النظر متى يؤمران وفى رواية اب
43:9.english: He saw me, for Satan does not imagine me, agreed upon from the hadith of Abu Huraira. [142] Hadith of Ibn 'Uyaynah from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir from Jabir: The Prophet (peace be upon him) was never asked for something and said no, narrated by Muslim and it has preceded. [143] Hadith: Allah the Exalted said: The son of Adam has insulted me, and it is not befitting for him to insult me, and he has lied about me, and it is not befitting for him to lie about me, the hadith was extracted by al-Bukhari from the hadith of Abu Huraira. [144] Hadith: How can I enjoy comfort when the companion of the trumpet has taken the horn and bent his forehead? The hadith was extracted by al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Abu Sa'id and he said it is good, and Ibn Majah narrated it with the wording: Indeed my two companions of the horn are in their hands or in their hands two horns, they are observing the look when they will be commanded, and in the narration of Ibn Majah, al-Hajjaj ibn Artah is disputed. [145] Hadith: When he was sent to, he was sent to the companion of the trumpet, so he gestured with it to his mouth and advanced one leg and delayed another, the hadith I did not find it like this, but it has been reported that Israfil from the beginning of creation is like that, as narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Tarikh and Abu al-Shaykh in Kitab al-'Azamah from the hadith of Abu Huraira: Indeed Allah, blessed and exalted, when He finished creating the heavens and the earth, created the trumpet and gave it to Israfil, so he is placing it on his mouth, staring with his sight to the Throne, waiting for when he will be commanded, al-Bukhari said: And it is not authentic, and in a narration of Abu al-Shaykh: The companion of the trumpet has not blinked since he was entrusted with it, prepared, looking towards the Throne, fearing that he will be commanded before his glance returns to him, as if his two eyes are two shining stars, and its chain is good. [146] Hadith: People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection on a white, pure earth like a flat bread, with no landmark for anyone, agreed upon from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd, and al-Bukhari separated his saying: With no landmark for anyone, so he made it from the saying of Sahl or others, and Muslim included it in it. [147] Hadith: People will be resurrected barefoot, naked, uncircumcised, sweat has bridled them and reached the fats of the ears, said Sawdah, the narrator of the hadith: And woe to me, the hadith was extracted by al-Tha'labi and al-Baghawi and it is in the two Sahihs from the hadith of 'A'ishah and she is the one who said: And woe to me, and al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Awsat from the hadith of Umm Salamah and she is the one who said: And woe to me. [148] Hadith of Abu Huraira: People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection riding and walking and on their faces, the hadith was narrated by al-Tirmidhi and he deemed it good, and in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Anas: A man said: O Prophet of Allah, how will the disbeliever be gathered on his face? He said: Is not the One who made him walk on...
43:9.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Book of Repentance'

43:13.arabic: الخامسة: في الركوب فإذا ركب الراحلة يقول بسم الله وبالله والله أكبر توكلت على الله ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله العلي العظيم ما شاء الله كان وما لم يشأ لم يكن سبحان الذي سخر لنا هذا وما كنا له مقرنين وإنا إلى ربنا لمنقلبون اللهم إني وجهت وجهي إليك وفوضت أمري كله إليك وتوكلت في جميع أموري عليك أنت حسبي ونعم الوكيل. فإذا استوى على الراحلة واستوت تحته قال سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر سبع مرات وقال الحمد لله الذي هدانا لهذا وما كنا لنهتدي لولا أن هدانا الله اللهم أنت الحامل على الظ
43:13.english: Fifth: Regarding riding. When he mounts the riding animal, he says: In the name of Allah, and by Allah, and Allah is the Greatest. I have placed my trust in Allah, and there is no power nor strength except by Allah, the Most High, the Most Great. What Allah wills occurs, and what He does not will does not occur. Glory be to the One who has subjected this for us, and we could not have subdued it. And indeed, to our Lord we will return. O Allah, I have directed my face towards You, and I have entrusted all my affairs to You, and I have placed my trust in all my matters upon You. You are sufficient for me, and You are the best Disposer of affairs. Then, when he is firmly seated upon the riding animal and it is steady beneath him, he says: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and there is no deity except Allah, and Allah is the Greatest, seven times. And he says: Praise be to Allah who has guided us to this, and we would not have been guided had Allah not guided us. O Allah, You are the Carrier upon the back, and You are the One sought for help in affairs.
43:13.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

43:14.arabic: وإذا بلغك وفاة أحد فقل إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون وإنا إلى ربنا لمنقلبون اللهم اكتبه في المحسنين واجعل كتابه في عليين واخلفه على عقبه في الغابرين اللهم لا تحرمنا أجره ولا تفتنا بعده واغفر لنا وله
43:14.english: And when you hear of someone's death, say: 'Indeed we belong to Allah and indeed to Him we will return, and indeed to our Lord we are returning (munqalibūn). O Allah, write him among the doers of good (al-muḥsinīn) and place his record in the highest (ʿilliyyīn), and replace him for his offspring among the later ones. O Allah, do not deprive us of his reward and do not test us after him, and forgive us and him.'
43:14.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

43:14.arabic: حديث القول إذا بلغه وفاة أحد إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون وإنا إلى ربنا لمنقلبون اللهم اكتبه من المحسنين واجعل كتابه في عليين واخلفه على عقبه في الغابرين اللهم لا تحرمنا أجره ولا تفتنا بعده واغفر لنا وله أخرجه ابن السني في اليوم والليلة وابن حبان من حديث أم سلمة إذا أصاب أحدكم مصيبة فليقل إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون ولمسلم من حديثها اللهم اغفر لأبي سلمة وارفع درجته في المهديين واخلفه في عقبه في الغابرين واغفر لنا وله يا رب العالمين وافسح له في قبره ونور له فيه.
43:14.english: The saying when news of someone's death reaches one: 'Indeed we belong to Allah and indeed to Him we will return (إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون), and indeed to our Lord we are returning (وَإِنَّا إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا لَمُنْقَلِبُونَ). O Allah, record him among the doers of good (المحسنين), and place his record in the highest (عليين), and replace him for his offspring among the later ones (الغابرين). O Allah, do not deprive us of his reward and do not test us after him, and forgive us and him.' Ibn al-Sunni in 'al-Yawm wa al-Laylah' and Ibn Hibban extracted it from the hadith of Umm Salamah: 'When calamity befalls one of you, let him say: Indeed we belong to Allah and indeed to Him we will return.' And Muslim from her hadith: 'O Allah, forgive Abu Salamah and raise his rank among the guided ones (المهديين), and replace him for his offspring among the later ones, and forgive us and him, O Lord of the worlds, and widen for him in his grave and illuminate it for him.'
43:14.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication

43:22.arabic: ومن جملة المعميات الإلف والعادة وحب استصحابهما وعنه العبارة بقوله تعالى: ﴿ إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة ﴾ {} الآية وعن الكبر والحسد العبارة بقوله تعالى: ﴿ وقالوا لولا نزل هذا القرآن على رجل من القريتين عظيم ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ أبشرا منا واحدا نتبعه ﴾ {} فهذه المعميات هى التى منعت الاهتداء
43:22.english: And among the blinding things are familiarity and habit and the love of adhering to them, and about this is the expression by His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed we found our fathers upon a community' (Quran 43:22) the verse, and about arrogance and envy is the expression by His saying, the Exalted: 'And they said: Why was this Quran not sent down upon a man from the two towns who is great?' (Quran 43:31) and His saying, the Exalted: 'Shall we follow a single human being from among us?' (Quran 54:24). So these blinding things are what prevented guidance.
43:22.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

43:22.arabic: وأما الأمة فتطلق على ثمانية أوجه الأمة الجماعة كقوله تعالى ﴿ وجد عليه أمة من الناس يسقون ﴾ {} وأتباع الأنبياء كقولك عن أمة محمد ﭬ، ورجل جامع للخير يقتدي به كقوله تعالى ﴿ إن إبراهيم كان أمة قانتا لله ﴾ {} والأمة الدين كقوله عز وجل ﴿ إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة ﴾ {} والأمة الحين والزمان كقوله عز وجل ﴿ إلى أمة معدودة ﴾ {} وقوله عز وجل ﴿ وادكر بعد أمة ﴾ {} والأمة القامة يقال فلان حسن الأمة أي القامة، وأمة رجل منفرد بدين لا يشركه فيه أحد قال ﭬ: (يبعث زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل أمة وحده[57]) والأمة الأم يقال هذ
43:22.english: And as for 'Ummah' (Community/Nation), it is applied in eight aspects: The 'Ummah' (Community) as a group, as in His saying, the Exalted: 'He found upon it a community (Ummah) of people watering' (Quran 28:23); and the followers of the prophets, as you say regarding the community (Ummah) of Muhammad (peace be upon him); and a man comprehensive of good who is followed, as in His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, Abraham was a community (Ummah), devoutly obedient to Allah' (Quran 16:120); and the 'Ummah' (Religion) as a way of life, as in His saying, the Exalted: 'Rather they said: Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion (Ummah)' (Quran 43:22); and the 'Ummah' (Time/Period) as an era, as in His saying, the Exalted: 'Until a numbered time (Ummah)' (Quran 11:8) and His saying, the Exalted: 'And remember after a time (Ummah)' (Quran 12:45); and the 'Ummah' (Stature) as physique, it is said: So-and-so has a good 'Ummah' (Stature), meaning physique; and an 'Ummah' (Individual) as a man isolated in a religion with no one sharing him in it, he (peace be upon him) said: 'Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Nufayl will be resurrected as an individual (Ummah) alone'; and the 'Ummah' (Mother) as parent, it is said: This is the 'Ummah' (Mother) of Zayd, meaning the mother of Zayd.
43:22.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

43:23.arabic: ولم يهلك الكفار إلا بموافقة أهل زمانهم حيث قالو إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة وإنا على آثارهم مقتدون فعليك إذا اشتغلت بمعاتبة نفسك وحملها على الاجتهاد فاستعصت أن لا تترك معاتبتها وتوبيخها وتعريفها سوء نظرها لنفسها فعساها تنزجر عن طغيانها المرابطة السادسة في توبيخ النفس ومعاتبتها أعلم أن أعدى عدوك نفسك التى بين جنبيك وقد خلقت أمارة بالسوء ميالة إلى الشر فرارة من الخير وأمرت بتزكيتها وتقويمها وقودها بسلاسل القهر إلى عبادة ربها وخالقها ومنعها عن شهواتها وفطامها عن لذاتها فإن أهملتها جمحت وشردت ولم تظفر
43:23.english: And the disbelievers were not destroyed except by following the people of their time, where they said: 'Indeed we found our forefathers upon a community (Ummah) and indeed we are upon their footsteps following.' So upon you, when you busy yourself with rebuking your Soul (Nafs) and compelling it to exertion (Ijtihad), if it resists, do not abandon rebuking it and reproaching it and making it recognize the evil of its view for itself, so perhaps it will desist from its transgression. The sixth station in rebuking the Soul (Nafs) and admonishing it: Know that your most hostile enemy is your Soul (Nafs) that is between your two sides, and it was created commanding to evil, inclined to wickedness, fleeing from good, and you were commanded to purify it and straighten it and drive it with the chains of coercion to the worship of its Lord and Creator, and prevent it from its desires and wean it from its pleasures. If you neglect it, it will bolt and stray, and you will not capture it after that. And if you persist with it through rebuke and admonishment and censure and blame, then your Soul (Nafs) becomes the blaming Soul (Nafs al-Lawwāmah) that Allah swore by, and you hope that it will become the tranquil Soul (Nafs al-Muṭmaʾinnah) called to enter into the company of Allah's servants, pleased and pleasing.
43:23.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

43:23.arabic: ومن جملة المعميات الإلف والعادة وحب استصحابهما وعنه العبارة بقوله تعالى: ﴿ إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة ﴾ {} الآية وعن الكبر والحسد العبارة بقوله تعالى: ﴿ وقالوا لولا نزل هذا القرآن على رجل من القريتين عظيم ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ أبشرا منا واحدا نتبعه ﴾ {} فهذه المعميات هى التى منعت الاهتداء
43:23.english: And among the blinding factors are familiarity and habit and the love of adhering to them, and about this is the expression by His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed we found our forefathers upon a community (Ummah)' (Quran 43:23) the verse, and about arrogance and envy is the expression by His saying, the Exalted: 'And they said: Why was this Quran not sent down upon a man from the two towns who is great?' (Quran 43:31) and His saying, the Exalted: 'Shall we follow a human being from among us, one?' (Quran 54:24). These blinding factors are what prevented guidance.
43:23.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

43:23.arabic: وأتباع الأنبياء كقولك عن أمة محمد ﭬ، ورجل جامع للخير يقتدي به كقوله تعالى ﴿ إن إبراهيم كان أمة قانتا لله ﴾ {} والأمة الدين كقوله عز وجل ﴿ إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة ﴾ {} والأمة الحين والزمان كقوله عز وجل ﴿ إلى أمة معدودة ﴾ {} وقوله عز وجل ﴿ وادكر بعد أمة ﴾ {} والأمة القامة يقال فلان حسن الأمة أي القامة، وأمة رجل منفرد بدين لا يشركه فيه أحد قال ﭬ: (يبعث زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل أمة وحده[57]) والأمة الأم يقال هذه أمة زيد أي أم زيد.
43:23.english: And the followers of the prophets, as you say about the community (Ummah) of Muhammad (peace be upon him), and a man who gathers goodness and is followed, as in His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, Abraham was a community (Ummah), devoutly obedient to Allah' (Quran 16:120), and the community (Ummah) as religion, as in His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, we found our fathers upon a community (Ummah)' (Quran 43:23), and the community (Ummah) as time or period, as in His saying, the Exalted: 'until a numbered community (Ummah)' (Quran 11:8), and His saying, the Exalted: 'and remember after a community (Ummah)' (Quran 12:45), and the community (Ummah) as stature, it is said: so-and-so has a good community (Ummah), meaning stature, and a community (Ummah) of a man isolated in a religion with no one sharing in it, he (peace be upon him) said: 'Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl will be resurrected as a community (Ummah) alone' [57], and the community (Ummah) as mother, it is said: this is the community (Ummah) of Zayd, meaning the mother of Zayd.
43:23.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

43:31.arabic: ومن التكبر والتعزز كان حسد أكثر الكفار لرسول الله ﭬ إذ قالوا: كيف يتقدم علينا غلام يتيم وكيف نطأطئ رؤوسنا؟ فقالوا "لولا نزل هذا القرآن على رجل من القريتين عظيم"[108] أي كان لا يثقل علينا أن نتواضع له ونتبعه إذا كان عظيماً وقال تعالى يصف قول قريش "أهؤلاء من الله عليهم من بيننا" كالاستحقار لهم والأنفة منهم.
43:31.english: And from arrogance (Takabbur) and self-importance (Ta'azzuz) was the envy of most of the disbelievers for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), when they said: How does an orphan boy advance over us, and how do we lower our heads? So they said: "If only this Quran had been sent down upon a great man from the two towns (Makkah and Ta'if)." That is, it would not have been burdensome for us to humble ourselves before him and follow him if he were great. And Allah the Exalted describes the saying of Quraysh: "Are these the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us?" as belittling them and feeling aversion from them.
43:31.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

43:31.arabic: ومن جملة المعميات الإلف والعادة وحب استصحابهما وعنه العبارة بقوله تعالى: ﴿ إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة ﴾ {} الآية وعن الكبر والحسد العبارة بقوله تعالى: ﴿ وقالوا لولا نزل هذا القرآن على رجل من القريتين عظيم ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ أبشرا منا واحدا نتبعه ﴾ {} فهذه المعميات هى التى منعت الاهتداء
43:31.english: And from among the things that blind (the hearts) are familiarity and habit and the love of adhering to them, and concerning this is the expression by His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, we found our forefathers upon a community' (Quran 43:23) the verse. And concerning arrogance and envy is the expression by His saying, the Exalted: 'And they said: "Why was this Quran not sent down upon a great man from the two towns?"' (Quran 43:31) and His saying, the Exalted: 'A human being from among us, one, we would follow him?' (Quran 54:24). So these things that blind are what prevented guidance.
43:31.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

43:31.arabic: وقالت قريش فيما أخبر الله تعالى عنهم "لولا أنزل هذا القرآن على رجل من القريتين عظيم" قال قتادة: عظيم القريتين هو الوليد بن المغيرة وأبو مسعود الثقفي، طلبوا من هو أعظم رياسة من النبي ﷺ إذ قالوا غلام يتيم كيف بعثه الله إلينا؟ فقال تعالى "أهم يقسمون رحمة ربك" وقال الله تعالى "ليقولوا أهؤلاء من الله عليهم من بيننا" أي استحقاراً لهم واستبعاداً لتقدمهم.
43:31.english: And the Quraysh said, as Allah the Exalted informed about them: "Why was this Quran not sent down upon a man from the two towns who is great?" Qatadah said: The great one of the two towns is Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughirah and Abu Mas'ud Al-Thaqafi. They sought one who is greater in leadership than the Prophet (peace be upon him), when they said: An orphan boy, how did Allah send him to us? So the Exalted said: "Do they distribute the Mercy (Rahmah) of your Lord?" And Allah the Exalted said: "So that they may say: Are these whom Allah has favored among us?" meaning belittling them and considering their precedence unlikely.
43:31.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

43:31.arabic: [108]  حديث سبب نزول قوله تعالى ﴿ لولا نزل هذا القرآن على رجل من القريتين عظيم ﴾ {} ذكره ابن إسحاق في السيرة وإن قائل ذلك الوليد بن المغيرة قال أينزل على محمد وأترك وأنا كبير قريش وسيدهما ويترك أبو مسعود عمرو بن عمير الثقفي سيد ثقيف فنحن عظماء القريتين فأنزل الله فيما بلغني هذه الآية ورواه أبو محمد بن أبي حاتم وابن مردويه في تفسيريهما من حديث ابن عباس إلا أنهما قالا مسعود بن عمرو وفي رواية لابن مردويه حبيب بن عمير الثقفي وهو ضعيف.
43:31.english: Hadith about the reason for the revelation of His saying, the Exalted: 'Why was this Quran not sent down upon a man from the two towns who is great?' {} Ibn Ishaq mentioned it in the Sirah (Biography), and indeed the one who said that was Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughirah. He said: 'Is it revealed upon Muhammad while I am left, and I am the elder of Quraysh and its chief? And Abu Mas'ud 'Amr ibn 'Umayr Al-Thaqafi, the chief of Thaqif, is left? So we are the great ones of the two towns.' So Allah revealed, according to what reached me, this verse. And Abu Muhammad ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in their two Tafsirs (Exegeses) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, except that they said: Mas'ud ibn 'Amr. And in a narration of Ibn Mardawayh: Habib ibn 'Umayr Al-Thaqafi, and it is weak.
43:31.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

43:32.arabic: فالمحترفون إنما سخروا لينتظم الملك للملوك وكذلك المقبلون على الدنيا سخروا ليسلم طريق الدين لذوي الدين وهو ملك الآخرة ولولاه لما سلم لذوي الدين أيضا دينهم فشرط سلامة الدين لهم أن يعرض الأكثرون عن طريقهم ويشتغلوا بأمور الدنيا وذلك قسمة سبقت بها المشيئة الأزلية وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى : نحن قسمنا بينهم معيشتهم في الحياة الدنيا ورفعنا بعضهم فوق بعض درجات ليتخذ بعضهم بعضا سخريا فإن قيل : لا حاجة إلى تقدير عموم التحريم حتى لا يبقى حلال فإن ذلك غير واقع وهو معلوم ولا شك في أن البعض حرام وذلك البعض هو
43:32.english: The professionals are only made subservient so that the kingdom may be organized for the kings, and likewise those who turn towards the worldly life are made subservient so that the path of religion may be safe for the people of religion, which is the kingdom of the Hereafter. Without it, the religion of the people of religion would not be safe either. The condition for the safety of their religion is that the majority turn away from their path and busy themselves with worldly matters. That is a division that was preceded by the Eternal Will (Mashiyyah), and to this is the allusion in His saying, the Exalted: 'We have divided among them their livelihood in the worldly life, and We have raised some of them above others in degrees so that some may take others in subservience.' If it is said: There is no need to presume universal prohibition so that no lawful remains, for that is not actual and is known, and there is no doubt that some is prohibited, and that some is the lesser or the greater—there is consideration in that. What you mentioned that it is the lesser in relation to the whole is clear, but there must be a conclusive evidence for its permissibility that is not from the unrestricted interests (al-Masāliḥ al-Mursalah), and what you mentioned of the divisions are all unrestricted interests, so they must have a specific witness to be analogized upon so that the evidence is accepted by agreement, for some scholars do not accept unrestricted interests. I say: If it is conceded that the prohibited is the lesser, then the era of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and the Companions suffices us as proof, with the existence of usury, theft, misappropriation, and plunder. And if a time is considered where the greater is prohibited, then consumption is also permissible. Its proof is three matters: First, the division that we have limited and invalidated four from it and affirmed the fifth division, for if that is applied when all is prohibited, it is more so when the prohibited is the greater or the lesser. And the statement of the one who says it is an unrestricted interest: it is nonsense, for that is only imagined by one who imagines it in matters of conjecture, and this is certain, for we do not doubt that the interest of religion and the worldly life is intended by the Lawgiver, and it is known by necessity, and it is not conjectural, and there is no doubt that the rejection
43:32.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

43:32.arabic: وقالت قريش فيما أخبر الله تعالى عنهم "لولا أنزل هذا القرآن على رجل من القريتين عظيم" قال قتادة: عظيم القريتين هو الوليد بن المغيرة وأبو مسعود الثقفي، طلبوا من هو أعظم رياسة من النبي ﷺ إذ قالوا غلام يتيم كيف بعثه الله إلينا؟ فقال تعالى "أَهُمْ يَقْسِمُونَ رَحْمَتَ رَبِّكَ ۚ نَحْنُ قَسَمْنَا بَيْنَهُمْ مَعِيشَتَهُمْ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا ۚ وَرَفَعْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ دَرَجَاتٍ لِيَتَّخِذَ بَعْضُهُمْ بَعْضًا سُخْرِيًّا ۗ وَرَحْمَتُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ مِمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ" وقال الله تعالى "لي
43:32.english: And the Quraysh said, as Allah the Exalted informed about them: "Why was this Quran not sent down upon a man of great status from the two towns?" Qatadah said: The great one of the two towns is Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughirah and Abu Mas'ud Al-Thaqafi. They demanded someone of greater leadership than the Prophet (peace be upon him), when they said: An orphan boy, how did Allah send him to us? So Allah the Exalted said: "Do they distribute the Mercy (Rahmah) of your Lord? We have distributed among them their livelihood in the worldly life, and We have raised some of them above others in degrees so that some may take others in service. And the Mercy (Rahmah) of your Lord is better than what they accumulate." And Allah the Exalted said: "So that they may say: Are these whom Allah has favored among us?" meaning belittling them and rejecting their precedence.
43:32.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

43:32.arabic: الخامسة: أني نظرت إلى هذا الخلق وهم يطعن بعضهم في بعض ويلعن بعضهم بعضا وأصل هذا كله الحسد ثم نظرت إلى قول الله عز وجل: (نحن قسمنا بينهم معيشتهم في الحياة الدنيا( (الزخرف: 32) فتركت الحسد واجتنبت الخلق وعلمت أن القسمة من عند الله سبحانه وتعالى فتركت عداوة الخلق عني.
43:32.english: The fifth: I looked at this creation and they stab each other and curse each other, and the origin of all this is envy (Hasad). Then I looked at the saying of Allah the Almighty: 'Do they distribute the mercy of your Lord? We have distributed among them their livelihood in the worldly life, and We have raised some of them above others in degrees so that some may take others in service. But the mercy of your Lord is better than what they accumulate.' (Az-Zukhruf: 32) So I abandoned envy (Hasad) and avoided the creation, and I knew that the distribution is from Allah, glory be to Him, the Most High, so I left the enmity of the creation from me.
43:32.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Book of Knowledge'

43:35.arabic: قالوا أليس: العاقل من تمت مروءته وظهرت فصاحته وجادت كفه وعظمت منزلته، فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: (وإن كل ذلك لما متاع الحياة الدنيا والآخرة عند ربك للمتقين( إن العاقل هو المتقي وإن كان في الدنيا خسيسا ذليلا)[217].
43:35.english: They said: Is not the intelligent one (Al-Aqil) he whose nobility (Muru'ah) is complete, whose eloquence (Fasahah) is apparent, whose hand is generous, and whose status is great? So the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: (And all that is but the enjoyment of the life of the world (Al-Dunya), and the Hereafter (Al-Akhirah) is with your Lord for the God-fearing (Al-Muttaqin). Indeed, the intelligent one is the God-fearing one, even if he is in the world (Al-Dunya) lowly and humble.)
43:35.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Book of Knowledge'

43:36.arabic: فكذلك القلب المشغول بفكر مهم في الدين لا يخلو عن جولان الشيطان والا فمن غفل عن الله تعالى ولو في لحظة فليس له في تلك اللحظة قرين الا الشيطان ولذلك قال تعالى: ﴿ ومن يعش عن ذكر الرحمن نقيض له شيطانا فهو له قرين ﴾ {} وقال ﭬ: (ان الله تعالى يبغض الشاب الفارغ[34]) وهذا لان الشاب اذا تعطل عن عمل يشغل باطنه بمباح يستعين به على دينه كان ظاهرة فارغا ولم يبق قلبه فارغا بل يعشش فيه الشيطان ويبيض ويفرخ ثم تزدوج افراخه ايضا وتبيض مرة اخرى وتفرخ وهكذا يتوالد نسل الشيطان توالدا أسرع من توالد سائر الحيوانات لان
43:36.english: Thus, the Heart (Qalb) occupied with important thought in religion is not free from the roaming of the Satan (Shaytan), otherwise, whoever is heedless of Allah the Exalted, even for a moment, has in that moment no companion except the Satan. Therefore, Allah the Exalted said: 'And whoever turns away from the Remembrance (Dhikr) of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a Satan, and he is to him a companion.' And He said: 'Indeed, Allah the Exalted hates the idle youth.' This is because when the youth is idle from work that occupies his inner self (Batin) with something permissible to aid him in his religion, he appears idle, but his Heart (Qalb) does not remain empty; rather, the Satan nests in it, lays eggs, and hatches, then its hatchlings also pair, lay eggs again, and hatch, and thus the offspring of the Satan multiplies faster than the multiplication of other animals because its nature is from fire, and when it finds dry fuel, its multiplication increases, so the fire continually multiplies from fire and does not cease entirely, but spreads gradually in succession. The desire (Shahwa) in the Soul (Nafs) of the youth is for the Satan like dry fuel for fire, and just as fire does not remain if there is no sustenance for it, which is firewood, so the Satan has no scope if there is no desire. Therefore, if you contemplate, you know that your fiercest enemy is your desire, and it is an attribute of your Soul (Nafs). Therefore, Al-Husayn ibn Mansur al-Hallaj said when he was crucified and was asked about Sufism (Tasawwuf), what is it? He said: 'It is your Soul (Nafs); if you do not occupy it, it occupies you.' Therefore, the reality of patience (Sabr) and its perfection is patience from every blameworthy movement, and the movement of the inner self (Batin) is more deserving of patience from that, and this is a continuous patience that is not cut off except by death. We ask Allah for good success by His grace and generosity.
43:36.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

43:36.arabic: فإن كنت لا تشتاق إلى معرفة الله تعالى ولم تجد لذتها وفتر عنها رأيك وضعفت فيها رغبتك فأنت في ذلك معذور؛ إذ العنين لا يشتاق إلى لذة الوقاع، والصبي لا يشتاق إلى لذة الملك، فإن هذه لذات يختص بإدراكها الرجال دون الصبيان والمخنثين فكذلك لذة المعرفة يختص بإدراكها الرجل "رجال لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله" ولا يشتاق إلى هذه اللذة غيرهم، لأن الشوق بعد الذوق، ومن لم يذق لم يعرف، ومن لم يعرف لم يشتق، ومن لم يشتق لم يطلب، ومن لم يطلب لم يدرك، ومن لم يدرك بقي مع المحرومين في أسفل السافلين "ومن يعش عن ذ
43:36.english: If you do not yearn for the knowledge (ma'rifah) of Allah the Exalted and do not find its delight, and your opinion has become lax about it and your desire has weakened in it, then you are excused in that; for the impotent man does not yearn for the delight of intercourse, and the child does not yearn for the delight of kingship, for these are delights that are specifically perceived by men, not by children and effeminate ones. Likewise, the delight of knowledge (ma'rifah) is specifically perceived by the man 'men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah' (Quran 24:37), and none yearn for this delight except them, because yearning comes after tasting, and whoever has not tasted does not know, and whoever does not know does not yearn, and whoever does not yearn does not seek, and whoever does not seek does not attain, and whoever does not attain remains with the deprived ones in the lowest of the low. 'And whoever turns away from the Remembrance (Dhikr) of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil, and he is to him a companion' (Quran 43:36).
43:36.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

43:53.arabic: وقال الذين لا يرجون لقائنا لولا أنزل علينا الملائكة أو نرى ربنا لقد استكبروا في أنفسهم وعتوا عواً كبيراً. وقالوا لولا أنزل عليه ملك" وقال فرعون فيما أخبر الله عنه "أو جاء معه الملائكة مقترنين" وقال الله تعالى "واستكبر هو وجنوده في الأرض بغير الحق" فتكبر هو على الله وعلى رسله جميعاً.
43:53.english: And those who do not hope for Our meeting said: 'If only the angels were sent down upon us or we see our Lord.' They have indeed become arrogant in their selves (Anfus) and transgressed a great transgression. And they said: 'If only an angel had been sent down upon him.' And Pharaoh, in what Allah informed about him, said: 'Or came with him the angels accompanying (Muqtarinin).' And Allah the Exalted said: 'And he and his soldiers became arrogant in the earth without right.' So he became arrogant against Allah and against all His messengers.
43:53.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

43:58.arabic: وفي الحديث: (( ما ضل قوم بعد هدى كانوا عليه إلا أوتوا الجدل))[113] . ثم قرأ: (ما ضربوه لك إلا جدلا بل هم قوم خصمون( (الزخرف: 58) وفي الحديث في معنى قوله تعالى: ( فأما الذين في قلوبهم زيغ ( الآية (آل عمران: 7) (( هم أهل الجدل الذين عناهم الله بقوله تعالى ((فاحذرهم))[114]. وقال بعض السلف: يكون في آخر الزمان قوم يغلق عليهم باب العمل ويفتح لهم باب الجدل. وفي بعض الأخبار: (( إنكم في زمان ألهمتم فيه العمل وسيأتي قوم يلهمون الجدل))[115]. وفي الخبر المشهور: (( أبغض الخلق إلى الله تعالى الألد الخصم))[116
43:58.english: And in the hadith: 'No people strayed after guidance they were upon except they were given disputation (al-Jadal).' Then he recited: 'They did not strike it for you except as disputation (Jadalan); rather, they are a contentious people (Qawmun Khasimun)' (Az-Zukhruf: 58). And in the hadith regarding the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: 'So as for those in whose hearts is deviation (Zaygh)' (the verse from Al-Imran: 7): 'They are the people of disputation (Ahl al-Jadal) whom Allah meant by His saying, the Exalted: "So beware of them."' And some of the predecessors (al-Salaf) said: 'There will be at the end of time a people for whom the door of action (al-'Amal) is closed and the door of disputation (al-Jadal) is opened for them.' And in some reports: 'Indeed, you are in a time in which you are inspired with action (al-'Amal), and there will come a people who are inspired with disputation (al-Jadal).' And in the famous report: 'The most hated of creation to Allah, the Exalted, is the obstinate disputant (al-Ald al-Khasim).' And in the report: 'No people came to logic (al-Mantiq) except they were prevented from action (al-'Amal).' And Allah knows best.
43:58.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Book of Knowledge'

43:66.arabic: الحمد لله الذي لا يتكل على عفوه ورحمته إلا الراجون، ولا يحذر سوء غضبه وسطوته إلا الخائفون، الذي استدرج عباده من حيث لا يعلمون، وسلط عليهم الشهوات وأمرهم بترك ما يشتهون، وابتلاهم بالغضب وكلفهم كظم الغيظ فيما يغضبون، ثم حفهم بالمكاره واللذات وأملى لهم لينظر كيف يعملون، وامتحن بهم حبهم ليعلم صدقهم فيما يدعون، وعرفهم أنه لا يخفى عليه شيء مما يسرون وما يعلنون، وحذرهم أن يأخذهم بغتة وهم لا يشعرون فقال "ما ينظرون إلا صيحة واحدة تأخذهم وهم يخصمون فلا يستطيعون توصية ولا إلى أهلهم يرجعون" والصلاة والسلام
43:66.english: Praise be to Allah, upon whose forgiveness and mercy none rely except the hopeful, and none fear the evil of His anger and His might except the fearful, who leads His servants astray from where they do not know, and subjects them to desires and commands them to abandon what they desire, and tests them with anger and obliges them to suppress rage in what angers them, then surrounds them with hardships and pleasures and grants them respite to see how they act, and tests them with their love to know their truthfulness in what they claim, and makes known to them that nothing is hidden from Him of what they conceal and what they reveal, and warns them that He may seize them suddenly while they are unaware, so He said: "They await not but a single blast that will seize them while they are disputing. Then they will not be able to make a bequest, nor will they return to their families." And prayers and peace be upon Muhammad, His messenger, under whose banner the prophets march, and upon his family and his companions, the guided leaders, and the pleased masters, prayers equal in number to what has been of Allah's creation and what will be, and may the first and the last attain its blessing, and abundant peace.
43:66.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

43:67.arabic: والعادلون إلى طلب الرياسة بالعلوم خارجون عن موجب قوله تعالى: (إنما المؤمنون إخوة ( (الحجرات: 10) وداخلون في مقتضى قوله تعالى: (الأخلاء يومئذ بعضهم لبعض عدو إلا المتقين( (الزخرف: 67).
43:67.english: And those who turn to seeking leadership through knowledge are outside the scope of His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, the believers are brothers' (Al-Hujurat: 10) and enter into the requirement of His saying, the Exalted: 'The close friends (Al-Akhillā') on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the God-fearing (Al-Muttaqīn)' (Az-Zukhruf: 67).
43:67.topic: Al-Ghazali on the outer and inner dimensions of worship, from 'Book of Knowledge'

43:77.arabic: فيقولون ادعوا مالكا فيدعون فيقولون يا مالك ليقض علينا ربك قال فيجيبهم إنكم ماكثون[205]) قال الأعمش أنبئت أن بين دعائهم وبين إجابة مالك إياهم ألف عام قال فيقولون ادعوا ربكم فلا أحد خير من ربكم فيقولون ربنا غلبت علينا شقوتنا وكنا قوما ضالين ربنا أخرجنا منها فإن عدنا فإنا ظالمون قال فيجيبهم اخسئوا فيها ولا تكلمون قال فعند ذلك يئسوا من كل خير وعند ذلك أخذوا فى الزفير والحسرة والويل
43:77.english: They say: 'Call upon Malik (the keeper of Hell).' So they call, and they say: 'O Malik, let your Lord decree upon us.' He answers them: 'Indeed, you are abiding (ماكثون).' [205] Al-A'mash reported: I was informed that between their call and Malik's answer to them is a thousand years. They say: 'Call upon your Lord, for there is none better than your Lord.' They say: 'Our Lord, our wretchedness has overcome us, and we were a people astray. Our Lord, bring us out of it; if we return [to evil], then indeed we are wrongdoers.' He answers them: 'Remain despised therein and do not speak to Me.' At that, they despair of all good, and at that they begin sighing and regret and woe.
43:77.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Book of Repentance'

43:87.arabic: ولذلك قال تعالى: (ولئن سألتهم من خلقهم ليقولن الله( معناه إن اعتبرت أحوالهم شهدت بذلك نفوسهم وبواطنهم فطرة الله التي فطر الناس عليها أي كل آدمي فطر على الإيمان بالله عز وجل بل على معرفة الأشياء على ما هي عليه أعني أنها كالمضمنة فيها لقرب استعدادها للإدراك ثم لما كان الإيمان مركوزا في النفوس بالفطرة انقسم الناس إلى قسمين إلى من أعرض فنسي وهم الكفار وإلى من أجال خاطره فتذكر فكان كمن حمل شهادة فنسيها بغفلة ثم تذكرها ولذلك قال عز وجل: (لعلهم يتذكرون) ، (وليتذكر أولوا الألباب)، (واذكروا نعمة الله علي
43:87.english: And therefore, Allah the Exalted said: 'And if you ask them who created them, they will surely say, Allah' (Quran 43:87) – its meaning is that if you consider their states, their souls (Nafs) and their innermost beings (Bawatin) bear witness to that by the innate disposition (Fitrah) of Allah with which He created the people upon; meaning every human is created upon faith (Iman) in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, indeed upon knowledge of things as they truly are – I mean that it is as if it is embedded within them due to the proximity of their preparedness for perception. Then, since faith is firmly rooted in the souls (Nafs) by innate disposition (Fitrah), people divided into two groups: those who turned away and forgot – they are the disbelievers (Kuffar) – and those who pondered with their thoughts and remembered, so they became like one who carried a testimony then forgot it due to heedlessness (Ghaflah) then remembered it. And therefore, the Exalted said: 'That they may remember' (Quran 7:57), 'And that those of understanding may remember' (Quran 38:29), 'And remember the favor of Allah upon you and His covenant with which He bound you' (Quran 5:7), 'And We have certainly made the Quran easy for remembrance (Dhikr), so is there any who will remember?' (Quran 54:17); and naming this pattern 'remembrance' (Tadhakkur) is not far-fetched, as if remembrance (Tadhakkur) is of two kinds: one is that he remembers an image that was present in existence in his heart (Qalb) but disappeared after the other existence.
43:87.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

44:3.arabic: ومنها التدريج في البيان كقوله عز وجل ﴿ شهر رمضان الذي أنزل فيه القرآن ﴾ {} إذ لم يظهر به أنه ليل أو نهار وبان بقوله عز وجل ﴿ إنا أنزلناه في ليلة مباركة ﴾ {} ولم يظهر به أي ليلة فظهر بقوله تعالى ﴿ إنا أنزلناه في ليلة القدر ﴾ {} وربما يظن في الظاهر الاختلاف بين هذه الآيات فهذا وأمثاله مما لا يغني فيه إلا النقل والسماع فالقرآن من أوله إلى آخره غير خال عن هذا الجنس لأنه أنزل بلغة العرب فكان مشتملا على أصناف كلامهم من إيجاز وتطويل وإضمار وحذف وإبدال وتقديم وتأخير ليكون ذلك مفحما لهم ومعجزا في حقهم فك
44:3.english: And among them is the gradual clarification in the explanation, as in His saying, the Exalted, 'The month of Ramadan in which the Quran was revealed' (2:185), as it did not become clear by it whether it was night or day, and it became clear by His saying, the Exalted, 'Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night' (44:3), and it did not become clear by it which night, so it became clear by His saying, the Exalted, 'Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree' (97:1). And perhaps it is thought in the apparent meaning there is contradiction between these verses, so this and its like are matters in which nothing avails except transmission (Naql) and hearing (Sama'). The Quran from its beginning to its end is not devoid of this type because it was revealed in the language of the Arabs, so it encompassed the varieties of their speech from conciseness (Ijaz) and elaboration (Tatwil), implication (Idmar) and omission (Hadhf), substitution (Ibdal) and precedence (Taqdim) and postponement (Ta'khir), so that would be silencing them and miraculous in their regard. So everyone who is satisfied with understanding the apparent Arabic and hastens to interpret the Quran and does not seek support with hearing and transmission in these matters, then he is among those who interpret the Quran by his opinion.
44:3.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

44:21.arabic: فإذن كيف يستدل باعتزال الكفار والأصنام على اعتزال المسلمين مع كثرة البركة فيهم واحتجوا أيضا بقول موسى عليه السلام وإن لم تؤمنوا لي فاعتزلون وأنه فزع إلى العزلة عند اليأس منهم وقال تعالى في أصحاب الكهف وإذا اعتزلتموهم وما يعبدون إلا الله فأووا إلى الكهف ينشر لكم ربكم من رحمته أمرهم بالعزلة وقد اعتزل نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم قريشا لما آذوه وجفوه ودخل الشعب وأمر أصحابه باعتزالهم والهجرة إلى أرض الحبشة
44:21.english: So then how can one argue for seclusion from disbelievers and idols to justify seclusion from Muslims when there is abundant blessing (Barakah) among them? They also argued with the saying of Moses, peace be upon him: 'And if you do not believe in me, then keep away from me (fa'taziloon)' and that he resorted to seclusion (al-'Uzlah) when he despaired of them. And Allah the Exalted said regarding the Companions of the Cave: 'And when you withdraw from them and what they worship except Allah, then take refuge in the cave; your Lord will spread out for you of His mercy.' He commanded them to seclusion. And indeed our Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, withdrew from Quraysh when they harmed and shunned him, and he entered the valley (al-Shi'b) and commanded his companions to withdraw from them and emigrate to the land of Abyssinia.
44:21.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Seclusion'

44:29.arabic: وقال علي كرم الله وجهه: إذا مات العبد يبكي عليه مصلاه من الأرض ومصعد عمله من السماء ثم قرأ فما بكت عليهم السماء والأرض وما كانوا منظرين. وقال ابن عباس: تبكي عليه الأرض أربعين صباحا. وقال عطاء الخراساني: ما من عبد يسجد لله سجدة في بقعة من بقاع الأرض إلا شهدت له يوم القيامة وبكت عليه يوم يموت.
44:29.english: And Ali, may Allah honor his face, said: When a servant dies, his prayer place from the earth and the ascent of his deeds from the sky weep for him. Then he recited: 'So the sky and the earth did not weep for them, nor were they given respite.' And Ibn Abbas said: The earth weeps for him for forty mornings. And Ata al-Khurasani said: There is no servant who prostrates to Allah with a prostration in a spot from the spots of the earth except that it testifies for him on the Day of Resurrection and weeps for him on the day he dies.
44:29.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

44:38.arabic: ثم انظر إلى عجائب الجو وما يظهر فيه من الغيوم والرعود والبروق والأمطار والثلوج والشهب والصواعق فهى عجائب ما بين السماء والأرض وقد أشار القرآن إلى جملة ذلك فى قوله تعالى وما خلقنا السموات والأرض وما بينهما لاعبين وهذا هو الذى بينهما وأشار إلى تفصيله فى مواضع شتى حيث قال تعالى والسحاب المسخر بين السماء والأرض وحيث تعرض للرعد والبرق والسحاب والمطر فإذا لم يكن لك حظ من هذه الجملة إلا أن ترى المطر بعينك وتسمع الرعد بأذنك فالبهيمة تشاركك فى هذه المعرفة فارتفع من حضيض عالم البهائم إلى عالم الملأ الأعلى
44:38.english: Then look at the wonders of the atmosphere and what appears in it of clouds, thunders, lightnings, rains, snows, meteors, and thunderbolts. These are wonders between the heaven and the earth. And the Quran has pointed to the totality of that in His saying, the Most High: 'And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play (لاعبين).' And this is that which is between them. And He pointed to its details in various places where He said, the Most High: 'And the clouds, subjected between the heaven and the earth,' and where He mentions the thunder, the lightning, the clouds, and the rain. So if you have no share of this totality except that you see the rain with your eye and hear the thunder with your ear, then the beast shares with you in this knowledge. So rise from the lowliness of the world of beasts to the world of the highest assembly. For you have opened your eyes, so you have perceived its outward aspect. So close your outward eye and look with your inward insight (البصيرة الباطنة) to see the wonders of its inward aspect and the marvels of its secrets. And this also is a door that lengthens thought in it, for there is no hope in exhausting it.
44:38.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Contemplation'

44:38.arabic: فلم تنبت من الأرض ورقة ولا تبنة إلا وفيها منافع لا يقوى البشر على الوقوف على كنهها وكل واحد من هذا النبات يحتاج الفلاح فى تربيته إلى عمل مخصوص فالنخل تؤثر الكرم يكسح والزرع ينقى عنه الحشيش والدغل وبعض ذلك يستنبت ببث البذر فى الأرض وبعضه بغرس الأغصان وبعضه يركب فى الشجر ولو أردنا أن نذكر اختلاف أجناس النبات وأنواعة ومنافعه وأحواله وعجائبه لا نقضت الأيام فى وصف ذلك فيكفيك من كل جنس نبذة يسيرة تدلك على طريق الفكر فهذه عجائب النبات ومن أياته الجواهر المودعة تحت الجبال والمعادن الحاصلة من الأرض ففى ا
44:38.english: No leaf or straw grows from the earth except that in it are benefits that humans cannot fully comprehend. Each one of these plants requires the farmer in its cultivation to a specific action: the date palm prefers generosity to be cleared, the crop is purified from weeds and thickets, some of that is propagated by scattering seeds in the earth, some by planting branches, and some is grafted onto trees. If we wanted to mention the differences of plant genera and their types, their benefits, their states, and their wonders, the days would not suffice in describing that. So suffice for you from each genus a small sample that guides you to the way of reflection. These are the wonders of plants. And from His signs are the jewels deposited beneath the mountains and the minerals obtained from the earth. For in the earth are adjacent pieces that are different. So look at the mountains: how from them emerge precious jewels of gold, silver, turquoise, ruby, and others; some are malleable under hammers like gold, silver, copper, lead, and iron, and some are not malleable like turquoise and ruby; and how Allah guided people to extract them, purify them, and make vessels, tools, coins, and ornaments from them. Then look at the minerals of the earth from petroleum, sulfur, tar, and others, and the least of them is salt, which is needed only to season food. If a land were devoid of it, destruction would hasten to it. So look at the mercy of Allah, how He created some lands salty in their essence such that pure water from rain collects in them and turns into salt, salty, burning, such that one cannot consume a grain of it, so that it becomes seasoning for your food when you eat it, and your life becomes pleasant. And there is no inanimate thing, animal, or plant except that in it is wisdom and judgment of this kind. He did not create anything of them in vain, nor in play, nor in jest. Rather, He created all with truth as it should be, and in the manner that should be, and as befits His majesty, generosity, and gentleness. And for that reason, He, the Exalted, said: 'And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play. We did not create them except with truth.' And from His signs are the kinds of animals and their division into what flies and what walks, and the division of what walks into what walks on two legs, and into what walks on four, and on ten, and on a hundred as is observed in some insects. Then their division in benefits, forms, shapes, morals, and natures. So look at the birds of the air and at the wild beasts of the land and the domestic animals: you see in them wonders, and you do not doubt with it the greatness of their Creator, the power of their Determiner, and the wisdom of their Fashioner. And how can that be fully enumerated? Rather, if we wanted to mention the wonders of the flea, or the ant, or the date palm, or the spider—and it is among the small animals—in its building its house, in its gathering its food, in its affection for its mate, in its storing for itself, in its skill in the geometry of its house, and in its guidance to its needs, we would not be able to do that. So you see the spider building its house on the edge of a river: it first seeks two close places between them a gap of about an arm's length or less so that it can connect with thread between its two ends. Then it begins and casts the saliva, which is its thread, on one side to adhere to it. Then it goes to the other side and secures the other end of the thread. Then likewise it goes back and forth a second and third time and makes the distance between them proportional in a geometric proportion until, when it has secured the knots of the ropes and arranged the threads like the warp, it engages in the weft by placing.
44:38.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Contemplation'

44:38.arabic: وما من جماد ولا حيوان ولا نبات إلا وفيه حكمة وحكم من هذا الجنس ما خلق شىء منها عبثا ولا لعبا ولا هزلا بل خلق الكل بالحق كما ينبغى وعلى الوجه الذى ينبغى وكما يليق بجلاله وكرمه ولطفه ولذلك قال تعالى وما خلقنا السموات والأرض وما بينهما لاعبين ما خلقنهما إلا بالحق ومن آياته أصناف الحيوانات وانقسمها إلى ما يطير وإلى ما يمشى وانقسام ما يمشى إلى ما يمشى على رجلين وإلى ما يمشى على أربع وعلى عشر وعلى مائة كما يشاهد فى بعض الحشرات ثم انقسامها فى المنافع والصور والأشكال والأخلاق والطباع فانظر إلى طيور الجو
44:38.english: And there is no inanimate object, nor animal, nor plant except that in it is wisdom and rulings of this kind; He did not create anything of them in vain, nor for play, nor in jest. Rather, He created all with truth (al-Haqq) as it should be and in the manner that should be, and as befits His majesty, generosity, and subtlety. And therefore, He, the Exalted, said: 'And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play. We did not create them except with truth (al-Haqq).' And from His signs are the varieties of animals and their division into what flies and into what walks, and the division of what walks into what walks on two legs, and into what walks on four, and on ten, and on a hundred as is witnessed in some insects. Then their division in benefits, forms, shapes, morals (Akhlaq), and dispositions (Taba'i'). So look at the birds of the air and at the wild beasts of the land and the domestic animals; you will see in them wonders, and you will not doubt with it in the greatness of their Creator, the power of their Determiner, and the wisdom of their Fashioner. And how can that be exhaustively enumerated?
44:38.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Contemplation'

44:41.arabic: ويوم لا يغنى مولى عن مولى شيئا
44:41.english: And a day when a master will not avail a master anything
44:41.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Book of Repentance'

44:42.arabic: هذا إلى جملة الحقوق التي ذكرناها لعامة المسلمين وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم أتدرون ما حق الجار إن استعان بك أعنته وإن استنصرك نصرته وإن استقرضك أقرضته وإن افتقر عدت عليه وإن مرض عدته وإن مات تبعت جنازته وإن أصابه خير هنأته وإن أصابته مصيبة عزيته ولا تستعل عليه بالبناء فتحجب عنه الريح إلا بإذنه وإذا اشتريت فاكهة فأهد له فإن لم تفعل فأدخلها سرا ولا يخرج بها ولدك ليغيظ بها ولده ولا تؤذه بقتار قدرك إلا أن تغرف له منها ثم قال أتدرون ما حق الجار والذي نفسي بيده لا يبلغ حق الجار إلا من رحمه الله حديث عم
44:42.english: This is in addition to the totality of rights that we have mentioned for the general Muslims. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you know what the right of the neighbor is? If he seeks your help, help him. If he seeks your support, support him. If he seeks a loan from you, lend to him. If he becomes poor, visit him. If he becomes ill, visit him. If he dies, follow his funeral procession. If good befalls him, congratulate him. If a calamity befalls him, console him. And do not build higher than him, blocking the wind from him, except with his permission. And when you buy fruit, gift it to him. If you do not do that, then bring it in secretly. And do not let your child take it out to anger his child. And do not harm him with the smoke of your cooking pot except that you ladle out for him from it.' Then he said: 'Do you know what the right of the neighbor is? By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, none attains the right of the neighbor except whom Allah has shown mercy (raḥima).' The ḥadīth of 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb from his father from his grandfather: 'Do you know what the right of the neighbor is? If he seeks your help, help him. If he seeks a loan from you, lend to him.' The ḥadīth was reported by Al-Kharā'iṭī in Makārim al-Akhlāq and Ibn 'Adī in Al-Kāmil, and it is weak. Thus narrated 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb from his father from his grandfather from the Prophet (peace be upon him).
44:42.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

44:42.arabic: ولما سمعه من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من التشديدات في الأموال السلطانية حتى قال صلى الله عليه وسلم حين بعث عبادة بن الصامت إلى الصدقة اتق الله يا أبا الوليد لا تجيء يوم القيامة ببعير تحمله على رقبتك له رغاء أو بقرة لها خوار أو شاة لها تؤاج فقال يا رسول الله أهكذا يكون قال نعم والذي نفسي بيده إلا من رحم الله قال فوالذي بعثك بالحق لا اعمل على شيء أبدا
44:42.english: And when he heard from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) the severe warnings regarding the wealth of the rulers, until he (peace be upon him) said when he sent 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit to collect charity: 'Fear Allah, O Abu al-Walid, do not come on the Day of Resurrection carrying a camel on your neck that is bellowing, or a cow that is lowing, or a sheep that is bleating.' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, is it like this?' He said: 'Yes, by the One in Whose Hand is my soul (Nafs), except whom Allah has mercy upon (إِلَّا مَنْ رَحِمَ اللَّهُ).' He said: 'Then by the One Who sent you with the truth, I will never work for anything ever again.'
44:42.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

44:49.arabic: وينكسونه فى قعر الجحيم ويقولون له ذق إنك أنت العزيز الكريم - فأسكنوا دارا ضيقة الأرجاء مظلمة المسالك مبهمة المهالك يخلد فيها الأسير ويوقد فيها السعير شرابهم فيها الحميم ومستقرهم الجحيم الزبانية تقمعهم والهاوية تجمعهم أمانيهم فيها الهلاك وما لهم منها فكاك قد شدت أقدامهم إلى النواصى واسودت وجوههم من ظلمة المعاصى ينادون من أكنافها ويصيحون فى نواحيها وأطرافها: يا مالك قد حق علينا الوعيد يا مالك قد أثقلنا الحديد يا مالك قد نضجت منا الجلود يا مالك أخرجنا منها فإنا لا نعود فتقول الزبانية هيهات لات حين
44:49.english: And they cast him down into the depths of Hellfire and say to him: 'Taste! Indeed, you are the Mighty (Al-'Aziz), the Noble (Al-Karim).' - So they settle in an abode of narrow expanses, dark pathways, obscure perils, where the captive abides eternally and the Blaze is kindled. Their drink therein is scalding water and their abode is Hellfire. The Guardians (Al-Zabaniyah) crush them and the Abyss (Al-Hawiyah) gathers them. Their hopes therein are destruction, and they have no escape from it. Their feet are bound to their foreheads, and their faces have blackened from the darkness of sins (Al-Ma'asi). They call out from its corners and cry in its regions and extremities: 'O Malik, the threat has become true upon us! O Malik, the iron has become heavy upon us! O Malik, our skins have roasted! O Malik, take us out from it, for we will not return!' Then the Guardians (Al-Zabaniyah) say: 'Far be it! Not now is the time of hope, nor is there exit for you from the abode of disgrace. So be driven away therein and do not speak. And if you were taken out from it, you would return to what you were forbidden from.' At that, they despair and regret what they neglected in the side of Allah, but remorse does not save them, nor does regret avail them. Rather, they are thrown upon their faces, bound, with the Fire above them and the Fire beneath them, and the Fire to their right and the Fire to their left. So they are drowned in the Fire: their food is fire, their drink is fire, their clothing is fire, and their bedding is fire. They are amidst the severities of the fires and garments of pitch, and the striking of maces and the weight of chains. They are tossed in its narrow passages and shattered in its depths, and they are agitated among its coverings. The Fire boils with them like the boiling of cauldrons, and they cry out with...
44:49.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

44:51.arabic: فى مقام أمين فى جنات وعيون فى جنات ونهر فى مقعد صدق عند مليك مقتدر ينظرون فيها إلى وجه الملك الكريم وقد أشرقت فى وجوههم نضرة النعيم لا يرهقهم فتر ولا ذلة بل عباد مكرمون وبأنواع التحف من ربهم يتعاهدون فهم فيما اشتهيت أنفسهم خالدون لا يخافون فيها ولا يحزنون وهم من ريب المنون آمنون
44:51.english: In a secure abode (مقام أمين) in gardens and springs, in gardens and a river, in a seat of truthfulness (مقعد صدق) near an Omnipotent Sovereign (مليك مقتدر). They look therein at the face of the Noble King (الملك الكريم), and the radiance of bliss (نضرة النعيم) has shone upon their faces. Neither weariness nor humiliation afflicts them; rather, they are honored servants (عباد مكرمون), and with various gifts from their Lord they are attended. They are in what their souls (أنفسهم) desired, abiding eternally (خالدون). They neither fear therein nor grieve, and they are secure from the doubt of death (ريب المنون).
44:51.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

45:13.arabic: ز أولاده لم يبق لاستعمال السكين بغير إذنه حكم ونكاية في نفسه فكل ما راعاه الأنبياء والأولياء من الآداب وتسامحنا فيه في الفقه مع العوام فسببه هذه الضرورة وإلا فكل هذه المكاره عدول عن العدل وكفران للنعمة ونقصان عن الدرجة المبلغة للعبد إلى درجات القرب، بعضها يؤثر في العبد بنقصان القرب وانحطاط المنزلة وبعضها يخرج بالكلية عن حدود القرب إلى عالم البعد الذى هو مستقر الشياطين وكذلك من كسر غصنا من شجرة من غير حاجة ناجزة مهمة ومن غير حاجة غرض صحيح فقد كفر نعمة الله تعالى في خلق الأشجار وخلق اليد. أما اليد
45:13.english: And his children did not remain for using the knife without his permission, a ruling and harm to himself, so all that the Prophets and the Friends (Awliya) observed of etiquettes and we were lenient in it in jurisprudence with the common people, its cause is this necessity, otherwise all these dislikes are a deviation from justice (al-'Adl) and ingratitude for the blessing (Ni'mah) and a deficiency from the degree that brings the servant (al-'Abd) to the degrees of proximity (al-Qurb), some of it affects the servant (al-'Abd) by diminishing the proximity (al-Qurb) and lowering the station (al-Manazilah), and some of it completely exits the boundaries of proximity (al-Qurb) to the world of distance (al-Bu'd) which is the abode of the devils. And likewise, whoever breaks a branch from a tree without an urgent, important need and without a valid purpose has disbelieved in the blessing (Ni'mah) of Allah the Exalted in creating the trees and creating the hand. As for the hand, it was not created for futility but for obedience (al-Ta'ah) and works that assist in obedience (al-Ta'ah).
