And as for the tree, Allah the Exalted created it and created for it roots and directed water to it and created in it the power of nourishment and growth so that it reaches the peak of its maturity, then His servants (al-'Ibad) benefit from it, so breaking it before the peak of its maturity not in a manner that His servants (al-'Ibad) benefit from it is contrary to the purpose of wisdom (al-Hikmah) and a deviation from justice (al-'Adl). If he has a valid purpose, then he has that, for the tree and the animal were made as ransom for human purposes, for they are both perishable, vanishing, so the perishing of the lower in the survival of the nobler for a period is closer to justice (al-'Adl) than wasting them both, and to this is the allusion by His saying the Exalted: 'And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth - all from Him.' {} Yes, if he breaks that from the property of another, he is also an oppressor even if he is needy, because each specific tree does not fulfill the needs of all the servants (al-'Ibad) of Allah but fulfills one need, and if one is specified with it without preference and specification, it would be injustice, so the one with specification is the one who obtained the seed and placed it in the earth and directed water to it and undertook the care, so he is more entitled to it than others, and his side returns with that. If that grew in barren land without human effort, it is specified by its planting place or by planting it, so there must be seeking another specification, which is precedence in taking it, for the precedent has the characteristic of precedence. So justice (al-'Adl) is that he be more entitled to it, and the poor expressed this preference as ownership, and it is purely metaphorical, for there is no ownership except for the King of Kings (Malik al-Muluk) who has what is in the heavens and the earth, and how can the servant (al-'Abd) be an owner when he himself does not own himself but is owned by another? Yes, the creation are the servants (al-'Ibad) of Allah and the earth is the table of Allah, and He has permitted them to eat from His table according to their need, like a king who sets a table for his servants (al-'Ibad), so whoever takes a morsel with his right hand and his knuckles contain it, then another servant (al-'Abd) comes and wants to snatch it from his hand, it cannot be taken from him, not because the morsel became his property by taking with the hand, for the hand and the owner of the hand are also owned, but if each specific morsel does not fulfill the need of all the servants (al-'Ibad), then justice (al-'Adl) in specification occurs upon obtaining a kind of...
45:13.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

45:15.arabic: وكما ان شراه الحطب والجبة مما يستغنى عنه خالقك ومولاك وإنما تشترينه لنفسك إذ خلقه سببا لاستراحتك فطاعاتك ومجاهداتك أيضا هو مستغن عنها وإنما هى طريقك إلى نجاتك فمن أحسن فلنفسه ومن أساء فعليها والله غنى عن العالمين ويحك يا نفس انزعى عن جهلك وقيسى آخرتك بدنياك فما خلقكم ولا بعثكم إلا كنفس واحدة و كما بدأنا أول خلق نعيده و كما بدأكم تعودون وسنة الله تعالى لا تجدين لها تبديلا ولا تحويلا
45:15.english: And just as the purchase of firewood and the cloak is something your Creator (Khaliq) and Master (Mawlā) is independent of, but you purchase it for your own self (Nafs) since He created it as a means for your comfort, so too your acts of obedience (Tā'āt) and spiritual struggles (Mujāhadāt) - He is also independent of them, but they are your path to your salvation. So whoever does good, it is for his own self (Nafs), and whoever does evil, it is against it, and Allah is independent of the worlds. Woe to you, O self (Nafs)! Cast off your ignorance and measure your Hereafter (Ākhirah) by your worldly life (Dunyā), for He did not create you nor resurrect you except as a single soul (Nafs). And as We began the first creation, We will repeat it, and as He began you, you will return, and the established way (Sunnah) of Allah you will find no change or alteration for it.
45:15.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

45:17.arabic: الورد الخامس: السدس الأخير من الليل وهو وقت السحر فإن الله تعالى قال: ﴿ وبالأسحار هم يستغفرون ﴾ {} قيل يصلون لما فيها من الاستغفار وهو مقارب
45:17.english: The fifth portion (Wird): The last sixth of the night, which is the time of the pre-dawn (Sahar), for Allah the Exalted said: 'And in the hours before dawn they ask forgiveness' (Quran 51:18). It is said they pray because of the seeking forgiveness (Istighfar) in it, and it is approximate.
45:17.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

45:19.arabic: وأما قصدك المباهاة وتزكية النفس بزيادة الفضل بأن تقدح في غيرك فينبغي أن تعلم أنك بما ذكرته به أبطلت فضلك عند الله وأنت من اعتقاد الناس فضلك على خطر، وربما نقص اعتقادهم فيك إذا عرفوك بثلب الناس فتكون قد بعت ما عند الخالق يقيناً بما عند المخلوقين وهما، ولو حصل لك من المخلوقين اعتقاد الفضل لكانوا لا يغنون عنك من الله شيئاً.
45:19.english: And as for your intention of boasting and purifying the self (Nafs) by increasing virtue through criticizing others, you should know that by what you have mentioned, you have invalidated your virtue with Allah, and you are in danger regarding people's belief in your virtue. Perhaps their belief in you will decrease if they know you for slandering people, so you would have sold what is with the Creator with certainty for what is with the created ones in delusion. And even if you obtained from the created ones belief in virtue, they would not avail you against Allah anything.
45:19.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

45:19.arabic: فرفع سعيد صوته وقال يا أيها المصلي إن كنت تريد الله عز وجل بصلاتك فاخفض صوتك وإن كنت تريد الناس فإنهم لن يغنوا عنك من الله شيئا فسكت عمر بن عبد العزيز وخفف ركعته فلما سلم أخذ نعليه وانصرف وهو يومئذ أمير المدينة
45:19.english: So Sa'id raised his voice and said: 'O you who are praying, if you intend Allah the Exalted with your prayer, then lower your voice, and if you intend people, then they will not avail you anything from Allah.' So 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz fell silent and lightened his rak'ah (prayer unit), and when he gave the salutation (of peace ending the prayer), he took his sandals and departed while he was at that time the governor of Medina.
45:19.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

45:20.arabic: وأنزلنا إليك الذكر لتبين للناس ما نزل إليهم. كذلك يضرب الله للناس أمثالهم واتبعوا أحسن ما أنزل إليكم من ربكم. هذا بصائر للناس وهدى ورحمة لقوم يوقنون. هذا بيان للناس وهدى وموعظة للمتقين ﴾ {} وإذا قصد بالخطاب جميع الناس فقد قصد الآحاد فهذا القارىء الواحد مقصود فما له ولسائر الناس فليقدر أنه المقصود
45:20.english: And We have sent down to you the Remembrance (Dhikr) to clarify to the people what was sent down to them. Thus Allah strikes for the people their examples, and follow the best of what has been sent down to you from your Lord. This is insights for the people and guidance and mercy for a people who are certain (Yūqinūn). This is clarification for the people and guidance and admonition for the God-fearing (Muttaqīn). And if the address is intended for all people, then the individuals are intended, so this single reader is intended, so what is for him and for the rest of the people, let him consider that he is the intended one.
45:20.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

45:21.arabic: وقال مالك بن دينار رضي الله عنه بات يردد هذه الآية ليلة حتى أصبح ﴿أَمْ حَسِبَ الَّذِينَ اجْتَرَحُوا السَّيِّئَاتِ أَنْ نَجْعَلَهُمْ كَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ سَوَاءً مَحْيَاهُمْ وَمَمَاتُهُمْ ۚ سَاءَ مَا يَحْكُمُونَ﴾ الآية.
45:21.english: And Malik bin Dinar (may Allah be pleased with him) spent the night repeating this verse until morning: 'Do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them like those who have believed and done righteous deeds - equal in their life and their death? How wretched is that which they judge!' (the verse).
45:21.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Knowledge'

45:21.arabic: وقام تميم الداري ليلة بهذه الآية ﴿ أم حسب الذين اجترحوا السيئات ﴾ {} الآية.
45:21.english: And Tamim al-Dari stood for a night with this verse: 'Do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds, equal in their life and their death? How wretched is their judgment!' (Quran 45:21).
45:21.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

45:23.arabic: والثالث: وهو اللباب أن يرى الأمور كلها من الله تعالى رؤية تقطع التفاته عن الوسائط وأن يعبده عبادة يفرده بها فلا يعبد غيره ويخرج عن هذا التوحيد أتباع الهوى فكل متبع هواه فقد اتخذ هواه معبوده قال الله تعالى: (أفرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه( (الجاثية: 23). وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: (أبغض إله عبد في الأرض عند الله تعالى هو الهوى)[92]. وعلى التحقيق من تأمل عرف أن عابد الصنم ليس يعبد الصنم وإنما يعبد هواه إذ نفسه مائلة إلى دين آبائه فيتبع ذلك الميل وميل النفس إلى المألوفات أحد المعاني التي يعبر عنها بالهوى و
45:23.english: The third: which is the core (Lubāb) is to see all matters as from Allah the Exalted with a vision (Ru'yah) that cuts off one's attention from intermediaries, and to worship Him with a worship (ʿIbādah) that singles Him out, so he does not worship other than Him. And those who follow their desires (Hawā) exit from this monotheism (Tawḥīd), for every follower of his desire has taken his desire as his god. Allah the Exalted said: 'Have you seen he who has taken his desire as his god?' (Al-Jāthiyah: 23). And the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: 'The most hated god worshipped on earth to Allah the Exalted is the desire.' And in truth, whoever contemplates knows that the idol-worshipper does not worship the idol but rather worships his desire, for his soul (Nafs) is inclined to the religion of his forefathers, so he follows that inclination, and the inclination of the soul to familiar things is one of the meanings expressed by 'desire' (Hawā). And from this monotheism exits discontent with creation and turning attention to them, for how can one who sees everything as from Allah the Mighty and Majestic be discontent with other than Him? Indeed, monotheism is an expression of this station (Maqām), which is the station of the truthful ones (Ṣiddīqīn). So look at what he has turned to and with which shell (Qishr) he has contented himself, and how they have taken this as a refuge in boasting and pride with what is named praiseworthy while being bankrupt of the meaning that deserves true praise. That is like the bankruptcy of one who rises in the morning and turns to the qiblah and says: 'I have turned my face to He who created the heavens and the earth, inclining to truth' (Al-Anʿām: 79). And it is the first lie he opens with to Allah every day if the face of his heart (Qalb) is not turned to Allah the Exalted in particular, for if he intends by 'face' the apparent face, then his face is only to the Kaaba, and he has only diverted it from other directions, and the Kaaba is not a direction for He who created the heavens and the earth, so that the one turning to it is turning to Him, exalted is He above being limited by directions and regions, and
45:23.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

45:23.arabic: ومن عدل عن هذه الطريقة كان كمن قال الله تعالى فيه أفرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه وأضله الله على علم وقال تعالى واتبع هواه فمثله كمثل الكلب إن تحمل عليه يلهث أو تتركه يلهث وقال عز وجل فيمن نهى النفس عن الهوى وأما من خاف مقام ربه ونهى النفس عن الهوى فإن الجنة هي المأوى وسيأتي كيفية مجاهدة هذه الجنود وتسليط بعضها على بعض في كتاب رياضة النفس إن شاء الله تعالى
45:23.english: And whoever deviates from this method is like the one about whom Allah the Exalted said: 'Have you seen the one who takes his desire (Hawa) as his god (Ilah), and Allah has led him astray despite knowledge, and sealed his hearing and his heart, and placed a covering over his sight? So who will guide him after Allah? Will you not then remember?' (Quran 45:23). And He said: 'And he followed his desire (Hawa), so his likeness is as the likeness of a dog: if you attack it, it pants, or if you leave it, it pants' (Quran 7:176). And He the Almighty said regarding the one who forbids the Soul (Nafs) from desire (Hawa): 'But as for he who feared the standing before his Lord and forbade the Soul (Nafs) from desire (Hawa), then indeed, Paradise will be [his] refuge' (Quran 79:40-41). And the method of struggling (Mujahadah) against these troops and setting some of them against others will come in the Book of Disciplining the Soul (Riyadat al-Nafs), if Allah the Exalted wills.
45:23.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

45:23.arabic: وقال جابر بن عبيدة العدوي شكوت إلى العلاء بن زياد ما أجد في صدري من الوسوسة فقال إنما مثل ذلك مثل البيت الذي يمر به اللصوص فإن كان فيه شيء عالجوه وإلا مضوا وتركوه يعني أن القلب الخالي عن الهوى لا يدخله الشيطان ولذلك قال الله تعالى إن عبادي ليس لك عليهم سلطان فكل من اتبع الهوى فهو عبد الهوى لا عبد الله ولذلك سلط الله عليه الشيطان وقال تعالى أفرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه وهو إشارة إلى أن من الهوى إلهه ومعبوده فهو عبد الهوى لا عبد الله ولذلك قال عمرو ابن العاص للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يا رسول الله حال ا
45:23.english: And Jabir ibn 'Ubaydah al-'Adawi said: I complained to al-'Ala' ibn Ziyad about what I find in my chest (Sadrat) from the whispering (Waswasah), so he said: Indeed, the likeness of that is like a house that thieves pass by; if there is something in it, they treat it (i.e., attempt to steal), otherwise they pass and leave it. Meaning that the Heart (Qalb) empty from the Passion (Hawa) does not enter it the Satan (Shaytan). And for that reason, Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them.' So everyone who follows the Passion (Hawa) is a servant of the Passion (Hawa), not a servant of Allah. And for that reason, Allah empowered over him the Satan (Shaytan). And He the Exalted said: 'Have you seen the one who takes his god his passion (Hawa)?' And it is an indication that whoever makes his passion (Hawa) his god and his worshipped one, he is a servant of the passion (Hawa), not a servant of Allah. And for that reason, 'Amr ibn al-'As said to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: O Messenger of Allah, the Satan (Shaytan) comes between me and my prayer and my recitation. So he said: That is a Satan (Shaytan) called Khanzab; when you sense him, seek refuge in Allah from him and spit to your left three times. He said: So I did that, and Allah removed him from me. [44] And in the report: Indeed, for ablution (Wudu') there is a Satan (Shaytan) called al-Walhan, so seek refuge in Allah from him. [45] And it does not erase the whispering (Waswasah) of the Satan (Shaytan) from the Heart (Qalb) except the remembrance (Dhikr) of other than what he whispers with, because if there occurs in the Heart (Qalb) the remembrance (Dhikr) of something, what was in it before disappears from it. But everything other than Allah the Exalted and other than what is related to Him, it is also permissible to be a field for the Satan (Shaytan). And the remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah is that which secures his side and he knows that there is no field for the Satan (Shaytan) in it. And the thing is not treated except by its opposite, and the opposite of all the whisperings (Waswasah) of the Satan (Shaytan) is the remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah with seeking refuge and disavowal from power and strength, and it is the meaning of your saying: 'I seek refuge in Allah from the Satan (Shaytan), the accursed,' and 'There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Most Great.' And that is not capable of it except the God-fearing (Muttaqun) who are predominant over them the remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah the Exalted. And indeed, the Satan (Shaytan) circulates around them in times of slips (Falatat) on the way of stealth (Khalsah). Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, those who fear (Ittaqaw) when a touch from the Satan (Shaytan) touches them, they remember (Tadhakkara), then they are seeing (Mubsirun).'
45:23.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

45:23.arabic: والمتحصن به لا معبود له سوى الله سبحانه فأما من اتخذ إلهه هواه فهو في ميدان الشيطان لا في حصن الله عز وجل واعلم أن من مكايده أن يشغلك في صلاتك بذكر الآخرة وتدبير فعل الخيرات ليمنعك عن فهم ما تقرأ فاعلم أن كل ما يشغلك عن فهم معاني قراءتك فهو وسواس فإن حركة اللسان غير مقصودة بل المقصود معانيها.
45:23.english: And the one who takes refuge in it has no object of worship except Allah (God) the Exalted. As for the one who takes his desire (Hawa) as his god (Ilah), he is in the arena of Satan (Shaytan), not in the fortress of Allah (God) the Exalted. And know that among his stratagems is to distract you in your prayer with remembrance (Dhikr) of the Hereafter and planning good deeds to prevent you from understanding what you recite. Know that everything that distracts you from understanding the meanings of your recitation is whispering (Waswas), for the movement of the tongue is not intended; rather, the intended is its meanings.
45:23.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

45:23.arabic: وأمره مخطر فى نفسه فإن عجزت عن ذلك كله فكن محبا لرسول الله ﭬ حريصا على تعظيم سننه ومتشوقا إلى مراعاة قلوب الصالحين من أمته ومتبركا بأدعيتهم فعساك أن تنال من شفاعته أو شفاعتهم فتنجو بالشفاعة إن كنت قليل البضاعة. (صفة الشفاعة) اعلم أن إذا حق دخول النار على طوائف من المؤمنين فإن الله تعالى بفضله يقبل فيهم شفاعة الأنبياء والصديقين بل شفاعة العلماء والصالحين وكل من له عند الله تعالى جاه وحسن معاملة فإن له شفاعة فى أهله وقرابته وأصدقائه ومعارفه فكن حريصا على أن تكتسب لنفسك عندهم رتبة الشفاعة وذلك بأن
45:23.english: And his matter is precarious in his soul. If you are incapable of all that, then be a lover of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), diligent in venerating his traditions (Sunnah), yearning to observe the hearts (Qulub) of the righteous (Salihin) from his community, and seeking blessings (Tabarruk) through their supplications. Perhaps you will attain from his intercession (Shafa'ah) or their intercession, and thus be saved by intercession if you are of little merchandise. (Description of Intercession) Know that when entry into the Fire becomes due for groups of the believers, then Allah the Exalted, by His grace, accepts among them the intercession of the Prophets and the Truthful Ones (Siddiqin), indeed the intercession of the scholars and the righteous, and everyone who has status (Jah) and good dealings with Allah the Exalted, then he has intercession for his family, relatives, friends, and acquaintances. So be diligent to acquire for yourself with them the rank of intercession, and that is by not despising any human being at all, for Allah the Exalted has concealed His friendship (Wilayah) in His servants, so perhaps the one whom your eye belittles is the friend (Wali) of Allah. And do not deem any sin small at all, for Allah the Exalted has concealed His anger in His prohibitions (Ma'asi), so perhaps the wrath (Maqt) of Allah is in it. And do not deem any obedience small at all, for Allah the Exalted has concealed His pleasure (Rida) in His obedience, so perhaps His pleasure is in it, even if it be a good word or a good intention or what runs its course. And the evidences for intercession in the Quran and reports are many: Allah the Exalted said: 'And your Lord will give you, and you will be satisfied' {93:5}. It was narrated by 'Amr ibn al-'As: (that the Messenger of Allah
45:23.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

45:28.arabic: فأخطر ببالك وأحضر فى قلبك حالة قلوب العباد وقد امتلأت فزعا ورعبا فتساقطوا جثيا على الركب وولوا مدبرين ﴿ يوم ترى كل أمة جاثية ﴾ {} وسقط بعضهم على الوجوه منكبين وينادى العصاة والظالمون بالويل والثبور وينادى الصديقون نفسى نفسى فبينما هم كذلك إذ زفرت الناس زفرتها الثانية فتضاعف خوفهم وتخاذلت قواهم وظنوا أنهم مأخوذون ثم زفرت الثالثة فتساقط الخلائق على وجوههم وشخصوا بأبصارهم ينظرون من طرف خفى خاشع وانهضمت عند ذلك قلوب الظالمين فبلغت الحناجر كاظمين وذهلت العقول من السعداء والأشقياء أجمعين
45:28.english: So imagine in your mind and bring to your heart (Qalb) the state of the hearts (Qulub) of the servants (Ibad) which have become filled with terror and dread, so they fell down kneeling on their knees and turned away fleeing. 'On the day you will see every community kneeling' (Quran 45:28). And some of them fell on their faces prostrate, and the sinners and wrongdoers call out with woe and destruction, and the truthful ones call out 'myself, myself'. While they are thus, the people let out their second gasp, so their fear multiplied and their strengths weakened and they thought they were being seized. Then they let out the third gasp, so the creatures fell on their faces and they stared with their eyes looking from a hidden, humble corner, and at that moment the hearts (Qulub) of the wrongdoers were crushed so they reached the throats suppressing, and the minds (Uqul) of the fortunate and the wretched altogether were bewildered.
45:28.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

45:29.arabic: وقال موسى بن مسعود كنا إذا جلسنا إلى الثوري كأن النار قد أحاطت بنا لما نرى من خوفه وجزعه وقرأ مضر القارئ يوما ﴿ هذا كتابنا ينطق عليكم بالحق ﴾{} الآية فبكى عبد الواحد بن زيد حتى غشي عليه فلما أفاق قال وعزتك لأعصيتك جهدي أبدا فأعني بتوفيقك على طاعتك
45:29.english: And Musa ibn Mas'ud said: 'When we sat with al-Thawri, it was as if fire had surrounded us due to what we saw of his fear (khawf) and dread (jaz'). And one day, Mudar the reciter recited: "This is Our Book that speaks the truth against you" (Quran 45:29) - the verse. Then Abd al-Wahid ibn Zaid wept until he fainted. When he regained consciousness, he said: 'By Your might, I have disobeyed You with all my effort forever, so help me with Your success (tawfiq) in Your obedience (ta'ah).'
45:29.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

45:36.arabic: فإذا استيقظت من نومك عند الصباح فقل الحمد لله الذي أحيانا بعدما أماتنا وإليه النشور[230] أ
45:36.english: And if you wake up from your sleep in the morning, then say: 'Praise be to Allah who gave us life after He caused us to die, and to Him is the resurrection.'
45:36.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter

46:11.arabic: الوظيفة الخامسة أن لا يدع طالب العلم فنا من العلوم المحمودة ولا نوعا من أنواعه إلا وينظر فيه نظرا يطلع به على مقصده وغايته ثم إن ساعده العمر طلب التبحر فيه وإلا اشتغل بالأهم منه واستوفاه وتطرف من البقية فإن العلوم متعاونة وبعضها مرتبط ببعض ويستفيد منه في الحال الانفكاك عن عداوة ذلك العلم بسبب جهله فإن الناس أعداء ما جهلوا قال تعالى: (وإذا لم يهتدوا به فسيقولون هذا إفك قديم( (الأحقاف: 11). قال الشاعر: ومن يكُ ذا فم مر مريضٍ يجد مرا به الماء الزلالا فالعلوم على درجاتها إما سالكة بالعبد إلى الله تع
46:11.english: The fifth duty is that the seeker of knowledge should not leave any branch of praiseworthy sciences nor any type of them except that he looks into it with a look that makes him aware of its purpose and goal. Then if his lifespan assists him, he seeks depth in it; otherwise, he occupies himself with the most important of it and completes it, and takes a taste from the remainder. For the sciences are cooperative and some of them are connected to others, and he benefits from it immediately by disengaging from enmity toward that science due to ignorance of it, for people are enemies of what they do not know. Allah the Exalted said: 'And when they are not guided by it, they will say: This is an ancient falsehood' (Al-Ahqaf: 11). The poet said: 'And whoever has a bitter, sick mouth finds bitter with it the pure water.' So the sciences, according to their degrees, are either leading the servant to Allah the Exalted or assisting in the path (Suluk) with a type of assistance, and they have arranged stations in proximity and distance from the intended goal, and their maintainers are like the guardians of the fortresses and frontiers, and each one has a rank and has according to his degree a reward in the Hereafter if he intends by it the Face of Allah the Exalted.
46:11.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

46:11.arabic: ومرة ينظرون إلى المؤمنين؛ وهم فقراء شعث غبر فيزدرون بهم ويستحقرونهم، فيقولون "أهؤلاء من الله عليهم من بيننا" ويقولون "لو كان خيراً ما سبقونا إليه" وترتيب القياس الذي نظمه في قلوبهم أنهم يقولون: قد أحسن الله إلينا بنعيم الدنيا، وكل محسن فهو محب، وكل محب فإنه يحسن أيضاً في المستقبل كما قال الشاعر: |لقد أحسن الله  | |كذلك يحسن فيما| |فيما مضى       | |بقـي          |
46:11.english: And sometimes they look at the believers; and they are poor, disheveled, and dusty, so they disdain them and belittle them, saying "Are these the ones whom Allah has favored from among us?" and saying "If it were good, they would not have preceded us to it." And the arrangement of the analogy that He has organized in their hearts (Qulub) is that they say: Allah has been good to us with the enjoyment of the worldly life, and every doer of good is a lover, and every lover then he does good also in the future as the poet said: |Indeed Allah has been good| |Thus He does good in what| |in what has passed| |remains|
46:11.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

46:13.arabic: اعلم أنّ باعث الدين بالإضافة إلى باعث الهوى له ثلاثة أحوال: أحدها أن يقهر داعي الهوى فلا تبقى له قوة المنازعة ويتوصل إليه بدوام الصبر وعند هذا يقال من صبر ظفر والواصلون الى هذه الرتبة هم الأقلون فلا جرم هم الصديقون المقربون الذين قالوا ربنا الله ثم استقاموا فهؤلاء لازموا الطريق المستقيم واستووا على الصراط القويم واطمأنت نفوسهم على مقتضى باعث الدين وإياهم ينادي المنادي ﴿ يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة ارجعي الى ربك راضية مرضية ﴾ {}.
46:13.english: Know that the motivator of religion (bāʿith al-dīn) in relation to the motivator of desire (bāʿith al-hawā) has three states: The first is that it overcomes the caller of desire (dāʿī al-hawā) so that no strength of contention remains, and one attains it through constant patience (ṣabr). At this point, it is said: 'Whoever is patient prevails.' Those who reach this rank are the fewest, so they are indeed the truthful ones brought near (al-ṣiddīqūn al-muqarrabūn) who said: 'Our Lord is Allah' then remained steadfast (istaqāmū). These have adhered to the straight path (al-ṭarīq al-mustaqīm) and stood firm on the right way (al-ṣirāṭ al-qawīm), and their souls (nufūs) have become tranquil (iṭmaʾannat) upon the requirement of the motivator of religion. To them the caller calls: 'O tranquil soul (al-nafs al-muṭmaʾinnah), return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him].'
46:13.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

46:13.arabic: وإلى هذا التفريد والتجريد الإشارة بقوله تعالى: " قل الله ثم ذرهم في خوضهم"، وبقوله تعالى: " إن الذين قالوا ربنا الله ثم استقاموا " بل هو معنى قولك " لا إله إلا الله " أي معبود ولا محبوب سواه، فكل محبوب فإنه معبود، فإن العبد هو المقيد والمعبود هو المقيد به، وكل محب مقيد بما يحبه. ولذلك قال الله تعالى: " أرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه " وقال ﭬ: " أبغض إله عبد في الأرض الهوى " ولذلك قال عليه السلام: " من قال لا إله إلا الله مخلصاً دخل الجنة"[27] ومعنى الإخلاص أن يخلص قلبه لله فلا يبقى فيه شرك لغير الله، ف
46:13.english: And to this singling out (Tafreed) and purification (Tajreed) is the indication by His saying, the Exalted: "Say: Allah, then leave them in their vain discourse," and by His saying, the Exalted: "Indeed, those who have said: 'Our Lord is Allah,' then have remained steadfast (Istaqamoo)," rather it is the meaning of your saying: "There is no god but Allah," meaning there is no object of worship (Ma'bood) nor beloved (Mahboob) except Him, for every beloved is an object of worship, for the servant (Al-'Abd) is the one bound and the object of worship is what binds him, and every lover is bound by what he loves. And for that reason Allah, the Exalted, said: "Have you seen he who has taken his desire (Hawaa) as his god?" and He said: "The most hated god of a servant on earth is desire (Hawa)." And for that reason the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever says: 'There is no god but Allah' with sincerity (Mukhlisan) enters Paradise." And the meaning of sincerity (Ikhlaas) is that he purifies his heart (Qalb) for Allah so that no partnership (Shirk) for other than Allah remains in it, thus Allah becomes the beloved (Mahboob) of his heart, the object of worship (Ma'bood) of his heart, and the intended goal (Maqsood) of his heart only. And whoever is in this state, the world (Al-Dunya) is his prison because it prevents him from witnessing his beloved, and his death is liberation from the prison and arrival to the beloved. So what is the state of one who has only one beloved and his longing for him has been prolonged and his imprisonment from him has been extended, then he is freed from the prison and enabled with the beloved and given life with security forever and ever,
46:13.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

46:14.arabic: وقد شرح الله الرجاء فقال "إن الذين آمنوا والذين هاجروا وجاهدوا في سبيل الله أولئك يرجون رحمة الله" يعني أن الرجاء بهم أليق وهذا لأنه ذكر أن ثواب الآخرة أجر وجزاء على الأعمال قال الله تعالى "جزاء بما كانوا يعملون" وقال تعالى "وإنما توفون أجوركم يوم القيامة" أفترى أن من استؤجر على إصلاح أوان وشرط له أجرة عليها وكان الشارط كريماً يفي بالوعد مهما وعد ولا يخلف بل يزيد، فجاء الأجير وكسر الأواني وأفسد جميعها ثم جلس ينتظر الأجر ويزعم أن المستأجر كريم، أفيراه العقلاء في انتظاره متمنياً مغروراً أو راجياً؟
46:14.english: And Allah has explained hope (al-raja') by saying: 'Indeed, those who have believed and those who have emigrated and striven in the path of Allah - those hope for the mercy of Allah.' This means that hope is more fitting for them, and this is because He mentioned that the reward of the Hereafter is a wage and recompense for deeds. Allah the Exalted said: 'A recompense for what they used to do (جزاء بما كانوا يعملون).' And He the Exalted said: 'And you will only be given your wages on the Day of Resurrection.' Do you see that if someone is hired to repair vessels and is promised a wage for it, and the promiser is generous, fulfilling the promise whenever he promises and does not break it but rather increases, then the hired worker comes and breaks the vessels and ruins all of them, then sits waiting for the wage and claims that the hirer is generous - would the people of intellect see him in his waiting as a deluded wisher or a hopeful one?
46:14.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

46:19.arabic: ولكل درجات مما عملوا فحظ كل واحد من صلاته بقدر خوفه وخشوعه وتعظيمه فإن موضع نظر الله سبحانه القلوب دون ظاهر الحركات ولذلك قال بعض الصحابة رضي الله عنهم يحشر الناس يوم القيامة على مثال هيئتهم في الصلاة من الطمأنينة والهُدُوء ومن وجود النعيم بها واللذة ولقد صدق فإنه يحشر كل على ما مات عليه ويموت على ما عاش عليه ويراعى في ذلك حال قلبه لا حال شخصه فمن صفات القلوب تصاغ الصور في الدار الآخرة ولا ينجو إلا من أتي الله بقلب سليم، نسأل الله حسن التوفيق بلطفه وكرمه.
46:19.english: And for each are degrees from what they have done, so the portion of each one from his prayer is according to his fear (Khawf) and his humility (Khushu') and his reverence (Ta'zim). For the place of Allah's (Subhanahu) gaze is the Hearts (Qulub) not the outward movements. And therefore some of the Companions (Sahaba) (Radhi Allahu 'Anhum) said: The people will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection according to the likeness of their state in prayer from tranquility (Tuma'nina) and calmness (Hudu') and from the presence of bliss (Na'im) in it and pleasure (Ladhdha). And he has spoken truth, for indeed each will be resurrected upon what he died upon and dies upon what he lived upon, and consideration in that is given to the state of his Heart (Qalb) not the state of his person. So from the attributes (Sifat) of the Hearts (Qulub) are fashioned the forms (Suwar) in the Abode of the Hereafter (Al-Dar Al-Akhira), and none is saved except he who comes to Allah with a sound Heart (Qalb Salim). We ask Allah for good success through His gentleness and generosity.
46:19.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

46:20.arabic: وترك المطاعم اللذيذة طمعاً في فواكه الجنة وخوفاً من أن يقال له: "أذهبتم طيباتكم في حياتكم الدنيا" فآثر في جميع ذلك ما وعد على ما تيسر له في الدنيا عفواً صفواً لعلمه بأن ما في الآخرة خير وأبقى، وأن ما سوى هذا فمعاملات دنيوية لا جدوى لها في الآخرة أصلاً.
46:20.english: And he abandons delicious foods out of hope for the fruits of Paradise and fear that it will be said to him: "You have exhausted your good things in your worldly life." So he prefers in all of that what is promised over what became available to him in the world easily and purely, knowing that what is in the Hereafter is better and more lasting, and that other than this are worldly transactions that have no benefit in the Hereafter at all.
46:20.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

46:29.arabic: هو الذي أرشد الأولين والآخرين ولما سمعه الجن لم يلبثوا أن ولوا إلى قومهم منذرين فقالوا إنا سمعنا قرآنا عجبا يهدي إلى الرشد فآمنا به ولن نشرك بربنا أحدا فكل من آمن به فقد وفق ومن قال به فقد صدق ومن تمسك به فقد هدي ومن عمل به فقد فاز
46:29.english: It is that which guided the first ones and the last ones, and when the Jinn heard it, they did not delay before turning to their people as warners, saying: 'Indeed we have heard a wondrous Quran that guides to the right path (Rushd), so we have believed in it and we will not associate with our Lord anyone.' So everyone who has believed in it has been granted success (Waffaqa), and everyone who has spoken by it has spoken truth, and everyone who has held fast to it has been guided, and everyone who has acted by it has attained triumph.
46:29.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

46:35.arabic: وروى مسروق عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: قلت يا رسول الله ألا تستطعم الله فيطعمك؟ قالت: وبكيت لما رأيت به من الجوع؛ فقال يا عائشة والذي نفسي بيده لو سألت ربي أن يجري معي جبال الدنيا ذهباً لأجراها حيث شئت من الأرض؛ ولكن اخترت جوع الدنيا على شبعها وفقر الدنيا على غناها وحزن الدنيا على فرحها؛ يا عائشة إن الدنيا لا تنبغي لمحمد ولا لآل محمد؛ يا عائشة إن الله لم يرض لأولي العزم من الرسل إلا الصبر على مكروه الدنيا والصبر عن محبوبها، ثم لم يرض إلا أن يكلفني ما كلفهم، فقال: "فاصبر كما صبر أولو العزم من ال
46:35.english: And Masruq narrated from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: I said, O Messenger of Allah, do you not ask Allah to feed you? She said: And I cried because of the hunger I saw in him; so he said, O Aisha, by the One in whose hand is my soul (Nafs), if I asked my Lord to make the mountains of the world flow with gold for me, He would make them flow wherever I wished on the earth; but I have chosen the hunger of the world over its satiety, the poverty of the world over its wealth, and the sorrow of the world over its joy; O Aisha, the world is not fitting for Muhammad nor for the family of Muhammad; O Aisha, Allah was not pleased for the possessors of determination (Ulu al-Azm) among the messengers except with patience (Sabr) upon the disliked of the world and patience (Sabr) from its beloved, then He was not pleased except to charge me with what He charged them, so He said: "So be patient (Fasbir) as the possessors of determination (Ulu al-Azm) among the messengers were patient (Sabaru)" and by Allah, I have no alternative but to obey Him, and by Allah, I will be patient (La-asbiranna) as they were patient (Sabaru) with my effort, and there is no power except by Allah.
46:35.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

46:35.arabic: يا عائشة إن الله لم يرض من أولى العزم من الرسل إلا الصبر على مكروهها والصبر عن محبوبها ثم لم يرض إلا أن كلفني ما كلفهم فقال تعالى - فاصبر كما صبر أولوا العزم من الرسل - ومجالد مختلف في الاحتجاج به.
46:35.english: O Aisha, indeed Allah was not pleased from the possessors of firm resolve (أولى العزم) from the messengers except patience (الصبر) upon its disliked aspects and patience away from its beloved aspects. Then He was not pleased except that He charged me with what He charged them, so He said, the Exalted: 'So be patient as were patient the possessors of firm resolve (أولوا العزم) from the messengers.' And Majalid is differed upon in reliance upon him.
46:35.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

47:2.arabic: وادعى الإجماع فيه واستدل بأدلة تشعر بنقيض غرضه كقوله تعالى الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات إذ هذا يدل على أن العمل وراء الإيمان لا من نفس الإيمان وإلا فيكون العمل في حكم المعاد
47:2.english: And he claimed consensus in this and argued with evidences that suggest the opposite of his purpose, such as the saying of the Exalted: 'Those who believed and did righteous deeds' since this indicates that the deed is beyond faith, not from the essence of faith itself, otherwise the deed would be in the ruling of repetition.
47:2.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

47:3.arabic: وأنزلنا إليك الذكر لتبين للناس ما نزل إليهم. كذلك يضرب الله للناس أمثالهم واتبعوا أحسن ما أنزل إليكم من ربكم. هذا بصائر للناس وهدى ورحمة لقوم يوقنون. هذا بيان للناس وهدى وموعظة للمتقين ﴾ {} وإذا قصد بالخطاب جميع الناس فقد قصد الآحاد فهذا القارىء الواحد مقصود فما له ولسائر الناس فليقدر أنه المقصود
47:3.english: And We have sent down to you the Remembrance (Dhikr) to clarify for the people what was sent down to them. Likewise, Allah strikes for the people their examples, and follow the best of what has been sent down to you from your Lord. This is insights for the people and guidance and mercy for a people who are certain. This is clarification for the people and guidance and admonition for the God-fearing (Mutqin). And if the address is intended for all people, then the individuals are intended, so this single reader is intended, so what is for him and for the rest of the people, let him consider that he is the intended one.
47:3.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

47:4.arabic: وما أجدر ذلك بأن يكون منتهى النعيم واللذات وأكل اللذات للشهداء الذين قتلوا في سبيل الله لأنهم ما أقدموا على القتال إلا قاطعين التفاتهم عن علائق الدنيا مشتاقين إلى لقاء الله راضين بالقتل في طلب مرضاته فإن نظر إلى الدنيا فقد باعها طوعا بالآخرة والبائع لا يلتفت قلبه إلى المبيع وإن نظر إلى الآخرة فقد اشتراها وتشوق إليها فما أعظم فرحه بما اشتراه إذا رآه وما أقل التفاته إلى ما باعه إذا فارقه وتجرد القلب لحب الله تعالى قد يتفق في بعض الأحوال ولكن لا يدركه الموت عليه فيتغير والقتال سبب للموت فكان سببا ل
47:4.english: And how deserving is that to be the ultimate bliss (Naim) and pleasures, and the consumption of pleasures for the martyrs (Shuhada) who were killed in the path (Sabil) of Allah because they only advanced to fighting while cutting off their attention from the attachments of the worldly life (Dunya), longing for the meeting (Liqa) with Allah, content with being killed in seeking His pleasure. If he looks at the worldly life, he has sold it willingly for the Hereafter (Akhira), and the seller does not turn his heart (Qalb) to what he sold. And if he looks at the Hereafter, he has purchased it and yearned for it, so how great is his joy with what he purchased when he sees it, and how little is his attention to what he sold when he parts from it. And the purification of the heart (Tajrid al-Qalb) for the love (Hubb) of Allah the Exalted may occur in some states, but death (Mawt) does not reach him upon it, so it changes. And fighting (Qital) is a cause for death, so it was a cause for attaining death in such a state. Therefore, the bliss is immense, for the meaning of bliss is that the human attains what he desires. Allah the Exalted said: 'And for them is what they desire' {} So this was the most comprehensive expression for the meanings of the pleasures of Paradise (Jannah). And the greatest torment (Adhab) is that the human is prevented from his desire, as Allah the Exalted said: 'And a barrier is placed between them and what they desire' {} So this was the most comprehensive expression for the punishments of the people of Hell (Jahannam). And this bliss is attained by the martyr as his soul (Nafs) is cut off without delay. And this matter is revealed to the possessors of hearts (Arbab al-Qulub) by the light (Nur) of certainty (Yaqin). And if you want testimony for it from the side of hearing (Sam'), then all the narrations (Ahadith) of the martyrs indicate it, and every narration that encompasses expressing the ultimate of their bliss with another expression, for it has been narrated from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that he
47:4.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

47:7.arabic: فإنه عمل في الباطن بالصبر المجرد. والثاني أنه قهر لعدو الله عز وجل فإن وسيلة الشيطان لعنه الله الشهوات وإنما تقوى الشهوات بالأكل والشرب ولذلك قال ﭬ: (إن الشيطان ليجري من ابن آدم مجرى الدم فضيقوا مجاريه بالجوع[12]) ولذلك قال ﭬ لعائشة رضي الله عنها: (داومي قرع باب الجنة قالت: بماذا؟ قال ﭬ بالجوع[13]) وسيأتي فضل الجوع في كتاب شره الطعام وعلاجه من ربع المهلكات فلما كان الصوم على الخصوص قمعا للشيطان وسدا لمسالكه وتضييقا لمجاريه استحق التخصيص بالنسبة إلى الله عز وجل ففي قمع عدو الله نصرة لله سبحانه ون
47:7.english: For it is an action in the inner realm (Batin) through pure patience (Sabr). The second is that it is a subduing of the enemy of Allah, the Exalted, for the means of Satan, may Allah curse him, are the desires (Shahawat), and the desires are only strengthened by eating and drinking. Therefore, the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: 'Indeed, Satan flows in the son of Adam like blood, so constrict his pathways with hunger.' And therefore, the Prophet, peace be upon him, said to Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her: 'Persist in knocking on the door of Paradise.' She said: 'With what?' He said: 'With hunger.' And the virtue of hunger will come in the book on the greed for food and its treatment from the quarter of the destructive matters. Since fasting, in particular, is a suppression of Satan, a blocking of his paths, and a constriction of his channels, it deserves specification in relation to Allah, the Exalted. For in suppressing the enemy of Allah, there is victory for Allah, the Glorified, and the supporter of Allah, the Exalted, is dependent on victory for Him. Allah, the Exalted, said: 'If you support Allah, He will support you and make firm your feet.' So the beginning is with effort from the servant (Abd), and the recompense is with guidance from Allah, the Exalted. And therefore, He, the Exalted, said: 'And those who strive in Us, We will surely guide them to Our ways.' And He, the Exalted, said: 'Indeed, Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in their souls (Anfus).' And the change is only the increase of desires, for they are the pasture of the devils (Shayatin) and their grazing ground. As long as they are fertile, their frequenting does not cease, and as long as they frequent, the majesty of Allah, the Glorified, is not unveiled to the servant, and he remains veiled from meeting Him. And the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: 'Were it not that the devils hover over the hearts (Qulub) of the children of Adam, they would look at the dominion of the heavens.' From this perspective, fasting became the gate of worship and became a shield, and since its virtue has reached this extent, it is necessary to clarify its apparent and hidden conditions by mentioning its pillars, its recommended practices, and its hidden conditions, and we will explain that in three chapters.
47:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Fasting'

47:7.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
47:7.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'What is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)".'
47:7.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

47:12.arabic: وطائفة أخرى زعموا أنهم تفطنوا الأمر وهو أنه ليس المقصود أن يشقى الإنسان بالعمل ولا يتنعم في الدنيا؛ بل السعادة في أن يقضي وطره من شهوة الدنيا وهي شهوة البطن والفرج، فهؤلاء نسوا أنفسهم وصرفوا هممهم إلى اتباع النسوان وجمع لذائذ الأطعمة يأكلون كما تأكل الأنعام ويظنون أنهم إذا نالوا ذلك فقد أدركوا غاية السعادة فشغلهم ذلك عن الله تعالى وعن اليوم الآخر.
47:12.english: And another group claimed that they had discerned the matter, which is that the purpose is not for the human to toil in work nor to indulge in the worldly life; rather, happiness is in satisfying his desire from the worldly desire, which is the desire of the belly and the private parts. These people forgot their own souls (Anfus) and directed their aspirations to following women and gathering pleasures of foods; they eat as the cattle eat, and they think that if they attain that, they have reached the ultimate happiness. So that preoccupied them from Allah the Exalted and from the Last Day.
47:12.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of the World'

47:14.arabic: "والثانية" أن يكون قد عرف قبح القبيح، ولكنه لم يتعود العمل الصالح بل زين له سوء عمله فتعاطاه انقياداً لشهواته وإعراضاً عن صواب رأيه لاستيلاء الشهوة عليه، ولكن علم تقصيره في عمله فأمره أصعب من الأول، إذ قد تضاعفت الوظيفة عليه؛ إذ عليه قلع ما رشه في نفسه أولاً من كثرة الاعتياد للفساد، والآخر أن يغرس في نفسه صفة الاعتياد للصلاح ولكنه بالجملة محل قابل للرياضة إن انتهض لها بجد وتشمير وحزم.
47:14.english: "The second" is that he may have recognized the ugliness of the ugly, but he has not accustomed himself to righteous work; rather, his evil work has been adorned for him, so he engaged in it in submission to his desires (Shahawat) and turning away from the correctness of his opinion due to the domination of desire (Shahwa) over him, but he knows his deficiency in his work, so his matter is more difficult than the first, for the duty has multiplied upon him; upon him is to uproot what was implanted in his soul (Nafs) initially from the abundance of habituation to corruption, and the other is to implant in his soul (Nafs) the attribute of habituation to righteousness, but he is, in summary, a place receptive to spiritual discipline (Riyada) if he rises to it with earnestness, exertion, and determination.
47:14.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

47:15.arabic: وقد ذكر الحسن البصري رحمه الله جملتها فقال: إن رمانها مثل الدلاء وإن أنهارها لمن ماء غير آسن وأنهار من لبن لم يتغير طعمه وأنهار من عسل مصفى لم يصفه الرجال وأنها من خمر لذة للشاربين لا تسفه الأحلام ولا تصدع منها الرءوس
47:15.english: And Al-Hasan Al-Basri, may Allah have mercy upon him, mentioned its entirety and said: 'Indeed its pomegranates are like buckets, and indeed its rivers are of water not stagnant (ghayr āsin), and rivers of milk whose taste has not changed (lam yataghayyar taʿmuhu), and rivers of purified honey (ʿasal muṣaffan) which men have not purified, and it is of wine (khamr) a delight (ladhdha) for the drinkers, which does not befuddle the minds (lā tusfihu al-aḥlām) nor cause headaches from it (lā taṣdaʿu minhā al-ruʾūs).'
47:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Repentance'

47:15.arabic: ام ذى غصة فيذكرون كما كانوا يجيزون الغصص فى الدنيا بشراب فيستغيثون بشراب فيرفع إليهم الحميم بكلاليب الحديد فإذا دنت من وجوههم شوت وجوههم فإذا دخل الشراب بطونهم قطع ما فى بطونهم فيقولون ادعوا خزنة جهنم قال فيدعون خزنة جهنم أن ادعوا ربكم يخفف عنا يوما من العذاب فيقولون أو لم تك تأتيكم رسلكم بالبينات قالوا بلى قالوا فادعوا وما دعاء الكافرين إلا فى ضلال قال فيقولون ادعوا مالكا فيدعون فيقولون يا مالك ليقض علينا ربك قال فيجيبهم إنكم ماكثون[205]) قال الأعمش أنبئت أن بين دعائهم وبين إجابة مالك إياهم ألف
47:15.english: Or one with a choking (ghussa) - they remember as they used to pass through chokings in the world with drink, so they call for help with drink, and the scalding water (al-hamim) is raised to them with iron hooks. When it approaches their faces, it scorches their faces, and when the drink enters their bellies, it cuts what is in their bellies. They say: Call the keepers of Hell. He said: So they call the keepers of Hell: Call your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment. They say: Did not your messengers come to you with clear proofs? They say: Yes. They say: Then call, and the call of the disbelievers is only in error. He said: So they say: Call Malik. So they call, and they say: O Malik, let your Lord decide upon us. He said: So He answers them: You will remain. [205] Al-A'mash said: I was informed that between their call and Malik's answer to them is a thousand years. He said: So they say: Call your Lord, for no one is better than your Lord. They say: Our Lord, our wretchedness has overcome us, and we were a people astray. Our Lord, bring us out of it; if we return, then indeed we are wrongdoers. He said: So He answers them: Be driven into it and do not speak. He said: So at that, they despair of every good, and at that, they begin sighing and regret and woe. And Abu Umamah said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said regarding His saying, the Exalted: 'And he will be given drink from purulent water, which he will gulp and can hardly swallow' [Quran 14:16-17] - He said: It is brought near to him, and he dislikes it, and when it is brought near to him, it scorches his face, and the skin of his head falls off, and when he drinks it, it cuts his intestines until it exits from his anus. Allah, the Exalted, says: 'And they will be given drink scalding water that will cut their intestines' [Quran 47:15]. And He, the Exalted, says: 'And if they call for relief, they will be relieved with water like molten brass that will scald the faces' [Quran 18:29]. So this is their food and drink when they are hungry and thirsty. [206] Then look now at the snakes of Hell and its scorpions, and at the intensity of its poisonous winds and the greatness of its figures and the harshness of its appearance, and it has been given authority over its people and incited against them, so it does not cease from biting and stinging for a single hour. Abu Hurairah said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: Whoever Allah gives wealth and he does not pay its Zakat (obligatory alms), it will be made to appear to him on the Day of Resurrection as a bald snake with two fangs that will encircle him on the Day of Resurrection, then it will take by its cheek, meaning its flanks, and say: I am your wealth, I am your treasure. Then he recited His saying, the Exalted: 'And let not those who are stingy with what Allah has given them of His bounty think' [Quran 3:180] the verse. [207] And the Messenger (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, in the Fire are snakes like the necks of Bactrian camels that sting a sting, and one finds its heat for forty autumns, and indeed in it are scorpions like mules with loads that sting a sting, and one finds its heat for forty autumns. And these snakes and scorpions are only given authority over those who were given authority in the world over stinginess and bad character and harming people, and whoever is protected from that is protected from these snakes, so they do not appear to him. [208] Then reflect after all this on the magnification of the bodies of the people of the Fire, for Allah, the Exalted, increases in their bodies length and width until their punishment increases because of it, and they feel the scorching of the Fire and the stinging of the scorpions and snakes from all.
47:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

47:16.arabic: ومن لم يكن له فهم ما في القرآن ولو في أدنى الدرجات دخل في قوله تعالى: ﴿ ومنهم من يستمع إليك حتى إذا خرجوا من عندك قالوا للذين أوتوا العلم ماذا قال آنفا أولئك الذين طبع الله على قلوبهم ﴾ والطابع هي الموانع التي سنذكرها في موانع الفهم وقد قيل: لا يكون المريد مريدا حتى يجد في القرآن كل ما يريد ويعرف منه النقصان من المزيد ويستغني بالمولى عن العبيد.
47:16.english: And whoever does not have understanding of what is in the Quran, even in the lowest degrees, enters into His saying, the Exalted: 'And among them are those who listen to you until when they depart from your presence, they say to those who were given knowledge: What did he say just now? Those are the ones upon whose hearts Allah has set a seal.' And the seal (Taba') are the obstacles that we will mention in the obstacles of understanding. And it has been said: The Seeker (Murid) does not become a true seeker until he finds in the Quran everything he desires and recognizes from it the deficiency from the increase and becomes independent with the Master (Mawla) from the servants.
47:16.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

47:17.arabic: والهداية الثانية وراء هذه الهداية العامة وهى التى يمد الله تعالى بها العبد حالا بعد حال وهى ثمرة المجاهدة حيث قال تعالى: ﴿ والذين جاهدوا فينا لنهدينهم سبلنا ﴾ {} وهو المراد بقوله تعالى: ﴿ والذين اهتدوا زادهم هدى ﴾ {} والهداية الثالثة وراء الثانية وهو النور الذى يشرق في عالم النبوة والولاية بعد كمال المجاهدة فيهتدى بها إلا ما لا يهتدى إليه بالعقل الذى يحصل به التكليف وإمكان تعلم العلوم وهو الهوى المطلق وما عداه حجاب له ومقدمات وهو الذى شرفه الله تعالى بتخصيص الإضافة إليه وإن كان الكل من جهته تعال
47:17.english: And the second guidance is beyond this general guidance, and it is that which Allah the Exalted provides to the servant state after state, and it is the fruit of striving (Mujahadah) where He the Exalted said: 'And those who strive in Us, We will surely guide them to Our ways' (29:69). And it is what is intended by His the Exalted saying: 'And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance' (47:17). And the third guidance is beyond the second, and it is the light (Nur) that shines in the world of prophethood (Nubuwwah) and sainthood (Wilayah) after the perfection of striving (Mujahadah), so one is guided by it except what cannot be guided to by the intellect (Aql) through which obligation (Taklif) and the possibility of learning sciences is attained, and it is the absolute desire (Hawa al-Mutlaq), and what is besides it is a veil (Hijab) for it and preliminaries, and it is that which Allah the Exalted honored by specifying the attribution to Him, even though all is from His side the Exalted, so He the Exalted said: 'Say, Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the guidance' (6:71). And it is named life (Hayat) in His the Exalted saying: 'Or one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light (Nur) by which he walks among the people' (6:122). And the meaning in His the Exalted saying: 'So is one whose breast Allah has expanded to Islam, then he is upon a light (Nur) from his Lord' (39:22).
47:17.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

47:19.arabic: وذكر ذلك مطلقا في مواضع الترغيب ثم ذكر في بعض المواضع الترغيب ثم ذكر في بعض المواضع الصدق والإخلاص فقال مرة من قال لا إله إلا الله مخلصا ومعنى الإخلاص مساعدة الحال للمقال. فنسأل الله تعالى أن يجعلنا في الخاتمة من أهل لا إله إلا الله حالا ومقالا ظاهرا وباطنا حتى نودع الدنيا غير متلفتين إليها بل متبرمين بها ومحبين للقاء الله فإن من أحب لقاء الله تعالى أحب الله لقاءه ومن كره لقاء الله كره الله لقاءه فهذه مرامز إلى معاني الذكر التي لا يمكن الزيادة عليها في علم المعاملة. (الباب الثاني في آداب الدعاء
47:19.english: And he mentioned that absolutely in places of encouragement, then he mentioned in some places of encouragement, then he mentioned in some places sincerity (Sidq) and devotion (Ikhlas), saying once: 'Whoever says "There is no god but Allah" with devotion (Ikhlas),' and the meaning of devotion (Ikhlas) is the state (Hal) assisting the statement (Maqal). So we ask Allah the Exalted to make us in the conclusion among the people of "There is no god but Allah" in state (Hal) and statement (Maqal), outwardly and inwardly, until we bid farewell to the world not turning towards it but rather weary of it and loving the meeting with Allah. For whoever loves the meeting with Allah the Exalted, Allah loves meeting him, and whoever hates the meeting with Allah, Allah hates meeting him. These are indicators to the meanings of the Remembrance (Dhikr) that cannot be increased upon in the knowledge of interaction. (The Second Chapter on the Etiquettes of Supplication and Its Virtue and the Virtue of Some Transmitted Supplications and the Virtue of Seeking Forgiveness and Prayers upon the Messenger of Allah ﭬ) (The Virtue of Supplication) Allah the Exalted said: 'And when My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me.' {} And He said: 'Invoke your Lord in humility and secretly; indeed, He does not like transgressors.' {} And
47:19.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith

47:19.arabic: ومثل هذا الشخص هو البائع للدنيا بالآخرة وحالة الشهيد توافق معنى قولك لا إله إلا الله فإنه لا مقصود له سوى الله عز وجل وكل مقصود معبود وكل معبود إله فهذا الشهيد قائل بلسان حاله لا إله إلا الله إذ لا مقصود له سواه ومن يقول ذلك بلسانه ولم يساعده حاله فأمره في مشيئة الله عز وجل ولا يؤمن في حقه الخطر ولذلك فضل رسول الله ﭬ قول لا إله إلا الله على سائر الأذكار وذكر ذلك مطلقا في مواضع الترغيب ثم ذكر في بعض المواضع الصدق والإخلاص فقال مرة من قال لا إله إلا الله مخلصا ومعنى الإخلاص مساعدة الحال للمقال. فن
47:19.english: And such a person is the seller of the worldly life (Dunya) for the Hereafter (Akhirah), and the state of the martyr (Shahid) corresponds to the meaning of your saying 'There is no god but Allah' (La ilaha illa Allah), for he has no objective (Maqsud) except Allah the Exalted, and every objective is worshipped (Ma'bud), and every worshipped one is a god (Ilah). So this martyr is saying with the tongue of his state (Lisan al-Hal) 'There is no god but Allah', since he has no objective other than Him. And whoever says that with his tongue but his state (Hal) does not assist his statement (Maqal), his affair is in the will (Mashiyyah) of Allah the Exalted, and danger (Khatar) is not secured in his right. And for that reason, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) preferred the saying 'There is no god but Allah' over all other remembrances (Adhkar), and he mentioned that absolutely in places of encouragement (Targhib). Then he mentioned in some places sincerity (Sidq) and purity of intention (Ikhlas), saying once: 'Whoever says "There is no god but Allah" with purity of intention (Mukhlisan).' And the meaning of purity of intention (Ikhlas) is the assistance of the state (Hal) to the statement (Maqal). So we ask Allah the Exalted to make us in the ending (Khatimah) among the people of 'There is no god but Allah' in state (Hal) and statement (Maqal), outwardly (Zahiran) and inwardly (Batinan), until we bid farewell to the worldly life (Dunya) not turning back to it, but rather being weary of it and loving the meeting (Liqa') with Allah. For whoever loves the meeting with Allah the Exalted, Allah loves meeting him, and whoever hates the meeting with Allah, Allah hates meeting him. These are indications (Maramiz) to the meanings of the remembrance (Dhikr) that cannot be increased upon in the science of interaction (Ilm al-Mu'amalah). (Chapter Two on the Etiquettes of Supplication (Adab al-Du'a) and its virtue and the virtue of some transmitted supplications and the virtue of seeking forgiveness (Istighfar) and sending prayers upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him)) (The Virtue of Supplication (Fadilat al-Du'a)) Allah the Exalted said: 'And when My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me and believe in Me that they may be guided.' And He said: 'So know that there is no god but Allah and ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women. And Allah knows your movements and your resting place.'
47:19.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith

47:19.arabic: وأما الآثار؛ فقد جاء في الأثر: لا تزال لا إله إلا الله تدفع عن العباد سخط الله عز وجل ما لم يسألوا ما نقص من دنياهم. وفي لفظ آخر: ما لم يؤثروا صفقة دنياهم على دينهم، فإذا فعلوا ذلك وقالوا: لا إله إلا الله، قال الله تعالى: كذبتم، لستم بها صادقين.
47:19.english: As for the narrations; it has come in a narration: 'There is no god but Allah' continues to repel from the servants the wrath of Allah the Exalted as long as they do not ask for what diminishes from their worldly life. And in another wording: as long as they do not prefer the transaction of their worldly life over their religion, so if they do that and say: 'There is no god but Allah', Allah the Exalted says: 'You have lied, you are not truthful in it.'
47:19.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

47:19.arabic: توضع في ميزان لأنها لو وضعت في ميزان من قالها صادقا ووضعت السموات السبع والأرضون السبع وما فيهن كان لا إله إلا الله أرجح من ذلك[22]) وقال ﭬ: (لو جاء قائل لا إله إلا الله صادقا بقراب الأرض ذنوبا لغفر الله له ذلك[23]) وقال ﭬ: (يا أبا هريرة لقن الموتي شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله فإنها تهدم الذنوب هدما. قلت: يا رسول الله هذا للموتي فكيف للأحياء؟ قال ﭬ: هي أهدم وأهدم[24]) وقال ﭬ: (من قال لا إله إلا الله مخلصا دخل الجنة[25]) وقال ﭬ : (لتدخلن الجنة كلكم إلا من أبى وشرد عن الله عز وجل شراد البعير عن أهله.
47:19.english: It is placed in the scale because if it were placed in the scale of one who says it truthfully and the seven heavens and the seven earths and what is in them were placed, 'There is no god but Allah' would outweigh that [22]. And he (peace be upon him) said: (If a person comes saying 'There is no god but Allah' truthfully with sins as much as the earth, Allah would forgive him that [23]). And he (peace be upon him) said: (O Abu Hurairah, teach the dead the testimony that there is no god but Allah, for it demolishes sins completely. I said: O Messenger of Allah, this is for the dead, so how about for the living? He (peace be upon him) said: It is more demolishing and more demolishing [24]). And he (peace be upon him) said: (Whoever says 'There is no god but Allah' sincerely enters Paradise [25]). And he (peace be upon him) said: (You will all enter Paradise except whoever refuses and strays from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, like the straying of a camel from its people. It was said: O Messenger of Allah, who is the one who refuses and strays from Allah? He said: Whoever does not say 'There is no god but Allah' [26], so increase in saying 'There is no god but Allah' before a barrier is placed between you and it, for it is the word of Monotheism (Tawhid) and it is the word of Sincerity (Ikhlas) and it is the word of Piety (Taqwa) and it is a good word and it is the call of truth and it is the firmest handhold and it is the price of Paradise). And Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: {Is the reward for good [anything] but good?} {} It was said: The good in this world is saying 'There is no god but Allah' and in the Hereafter is Paradise. And likewise His saying, the Exalted: {For those who do good is the best [reward] and extra} {}. And Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib narrated that he (peace be upon him) said: (Whoever says 'There is no god but Allah, alone, with no partner, to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs praise, and He is over all things competent' ten times, it will be for him equal to freeing a neck or he said a soul [27]). And 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb narrated from his father from his grandfather that he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: (Whoever says in a day two hundred times 'There is no god but Allah, alone, with no partner, to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs praise, and He is over all things competent', no one before him will precede him and no one after him will catch him except whoever acts with better than his action [28]). And he (peace be upon him) said: (Whoever says in a market from the markets 'There is no god but Allah, alone, with no partner, to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs praise, He gives life and causes death, and He is over all things competent', Allah writes for him a thousand thousand good deeds and erases from him a thousand thousand bad deeds and builds for him a house in Paradise). And it is narrated: (Indeed, when the servant (Abd) says 'There is no god but Allah', it comes to his record and does not pass by a sin except it erases it until it finds a good deed like it and sits next to it [29]). And in the authentic from Ayyub from the Prophet (peace be upon him) that he said: (Whoever says 'There is no god but Allah, alone, with no partner, to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs praise, and He is over all things competent' ten times, it is as if he freed four persons from the children of Ishmael (peace be upon him) [30]). And in the authentic also from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit from the Prophet (peace be upon him) that he said: (Whoever wakes up from the night and says 'There is no god but Allah, alone, with no partner, to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs praise, and He is over all things
47:19.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter

47:19.arabic: فر الله له ذلك[23]) وقال ﭬ: (يا أبا هريرة لقن الموتي شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله فإنها تهدم الذنوب هدما. قلت: يا رسول الله هذا للموتي فكيف للأحياء؟ قال ﭬ: هي أهدم وأهدم[24]) وقال ﭬ: (من قال لا إله إلا الله مخلصا دخل الجنة[25]) وقال ﭬ : (لتدخلن الجنة كلكم إلا من أبى وشرد عن الله عز وجل شراد البعير عن أهله. فقيل: يا رسول الله من الذي يأبى ويشرد عن الله؟ قال: من لم يقل لا إله إلا الله [26]، فأكثروا من قول لا إله إلا الله قبل أن يحال بينكم وبينها فإنها كلمة التوحيد وهي كلمة الإخلاص وهي كلمة التقوى وهي
47:19.english: So Allah forgave him that[23]) and He (the Prophet) said: (O Abu Huraira, teach the dying the testimony that there is no god but Allah, for it demolishes sins completely. I said: O Messenger of Allah, this is for the dying, so how about for the living? He said: It is more demolishing and more demolishing[24]) and He said: (Whoever says there is no god but Allah sincerely enters Paradise[25]) and He said: (You will all enter Paradise except whoever refuses and flees from Allah the Almighty like the camel flees from its owner. It was said: O Messenger of Allah, who is the one who refuses and flees from Allah? He said: Whoever does not say there is no god but Allah [26], so increase in saying there is no god but Allah before a barrier is placed between you and it, for it is the word of Monotheism (Tawhid) and it is the word of Sincerity (Ikhlas) and it is the word of Piety (Taqwa) and it is a good word and it is the call of Truth and it is the firmest handhold and it is the price of Paradise). And Allah the Almighty said: 'Is the reward for good (Ihsan) anything but good (Ihsan)?' {} It was said: The good (Ihsan) in this world is saying there is no god but Allah and in the Hereafter is Paradise. And likewise His saying the Exalted: 'For those who do good (Ahsanu) is the best reward and an increase' {} and Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib narrated that He said: (Whoever says there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs praise, and He is over all things competent ten times, it will be for him equal to freeing a neck or he said a soul[27]) and 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb narrated from his father from his grandfather that he said: The Messenger of Allah said: (Whoever says in a day two hundred times there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs praise, and He is over all things competent, no one before him will precede him and no one after him will catch up to him except whoever acts with better than his action[28]) and He said: (Whoever says in a market from the markets there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs praise, He gives life and causes death and He is over all things competent, Allah writes for him a thousand thousand good deeds and erases from him a thousand thousand bad deeds and builds for him a house in Paradise) and it is narrated: (Indeed the servant when he says there is no god but Allah, it comes to his record and does not pass by a sin except it erases it until it finds a good deed like it and sits beside it[29]) and in the authentic from Ayyub from the Prophet that he said: (Whoever says there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs praise, and He is over all things competent ten times, he is like whoever freed four persons from the children of Ishmael[30]) and in the authentic also from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit from the Prophet that he said: (Whoever wakes up from the night and says there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs praise, and He is over all things competent, glory be to Allah and praise be to Allah and there is no god but Allah and Allah is greater and there is no power and no strength except with Allah the Most High the Most Great then says O Allah forgive me, he is forgiven or he supplicates, he is answered, then if he performs ablution and prays, his prayer is accepted[31]). (Virtue
47:19.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

47:22.arabic: وأوصي المهاجرين فيما بينهم فإن الله عز وجلّ قال: ﴿ والعصر إن الإنسان لفي خسر إلا الذين آمنوا ﴾{} إلى آخرها وإن الأمور تجري بإذن الله فلا يحملنكم استبطاء أمر على استعجاله فإن الله عز وجل لا يعجل لعجلة أحد ومن غالب الله غلبه ومن خادع الله خدعه ﴿ فهل عسيتم إن توليتم أن تفسدوا في الأرض وتقطعوا أرحامكم ﴾{} وأوصيكم بالأنصار خيرا فإنهم الذين تبوءوا الدار والإيمان من قبلكم أن تحسنوا إليهم ألم يشاطروكم الثمار ألم يوسعوا عليكم في الديار ألم يؤثروكم على أنفسهم وبهم الخصاصة ألا فمن ولي أن يحكم بين رجلين فلي
47:22.english: And I advise the Emigrants (Muhajirun) among themselves, for Allah the Exalted said: 'By time, indeed, mankind is in loss, except for those who have believed...' to its end. And matters proceed by the permission of Allah, so do not let the delay of a matter lead you to hasten it, for Allah the Exalted does not hasten due to anyone's haste. And whoever contends with Allah, He overcomes him, and whoever deceives Allah, He deceives him. 'Then, would you perhaps, if you turned away, cause corruption on earth and sever your [ties of] kinship?' And I advise you regarding the Helpers (Ansar) with goodness, for they are those who settled the Home and Faith before you, that you treat them well. Did they not share the fruits with you? Did they not make room for you in the dwellings? Did they not prefer you over themselves while they were in need? Indeed, whoever is appointed to judge between two men, let him accept from their doer of good and overlook their wrongdoer. Indeed, and do not monopolize over them. Indeed, I am a forerunner for you, and you will follow me. Indeed, your appointment is the Pool—my Pool is wider than what is between Busra in Syria and Sana'a in Yemen—into which pours the spout of Al-Kawthar. Its water is whiter than milk, softer than foam, and sweeter than honey. Whoever drinks from it will never thirst again. Its pebbles are pearls, and its ground is musk. Whoever is deprived of it on the Day of Standing (Yawm al-Qiyamah) tomorrow is deprived of all good. Indeed, whoever loves to meet me tomorrow, let him restrain his tongue and hand except from what is appropriate.
47:22.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

47:31.arabic: وكان الفضيل بن عياض إذا قرأ (ولنبلونكم حتى نعلم المجاهدين منكم والصابرين ونبلو أخباركم) يبكي ويرددها ويقول إنك إن بلوتنا فضحتنا وهتكت أستارنا.
47:31.english: And Fudayl ibn Iyad, when he recited (And We will surely test you until We know those who strive among you and those who are patient, and We will test your reports), would weep and repeat it, saying: 'If You test us, You expose us and tear our veils.'
47:31.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

47:33.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
47:33.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'What is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)".'
47:33.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

47:36.arabic: ثم رده تعالى في موضع آخر إلى اثنين فقال تعالى: " وإنما الحياة الدنيا لعب ولهو " ثم رد الكل إلى واحد في موضع آخر فقال: " ونهى النفس عن الهوى فإن الجنة هي المأوى " فالهوى لفظ يجمع جميع حظوظ النفس في الدنيا، فينبغي أن يكون الزهد فيه.
47:36.english: Then He (Exalted) reduced it in another place to two, saying (Exalted): "And indeed the life of the world is play and amusement." Then He reduced the whole to one in another place, saying: "And restrain the Soul (Nafs) from desire (Hawa), for indeed Paradise is the abode." So desire (Hawa) is a term that gathers all the shares/portions (Huzuz) of the Soul (Nafs) in the world, therefore asceticism (Zuhd) should be in it.
47:36.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

47:37.arabic: وقد أشار القرآن إليه إذ قال تعالى: ﴿ إن يسألكموها فيحفكم تبخلوا ﴾ {} بل الحق الذى لا كدورة فيه والعدل الذى لا ظلم فيه أن لا يأخذ أحد من عباد الله من مال الله إلا بقدر زاد الراكب فكل عباد الله ركاب لمطايا الأبدان إلى حضرة الملك الديان. فمن أخذ زيادة عليه ثم منعه عن راكب آخر محتاج إليه فهو ظالم تارك للعدو وخارج عن مقصود الحكمة وكافر نعمة الله تعالى عليه بالقرآن والرسول والعقل وسائر الأسباب التى بها عرف ان ما سوى زاد الراكب وبال عليه في الدنيا والآخرة
47:37.english: And the Quran has indicated to it when He, the Exalted, said: 'If He were to ask you for it and press you, you would withhold and your grudges would emerge' (Quran 47:37). Rather, the truth (Haqq) that has no turbidity in it and the justice (Adl) that has no oppression (Zulm) in it is that no one from the servants (Ibad) of Allah takes from the wealth (Mal) of Allah except according to the measure of the provision of the traveler (Zad al-Rakib). For all the servants (Ibad) of Allah are travelers (Rukab) on the mounts of the bodies (Abdan) to the presence (Hudur) of the King (Malik), the Judge (Dayyan). So whoever takes an increase beyond that, then prevents it from another traveler (Rakib) who is in need of it, he is an oppressor (Zalim), abandoning justice (Adl), and outside the intended wisdom (Hikmah), and ungrateful (Kafir) for the blessing (Nimah) of Allah, the Exalted, upon him through the Quran, the Messenger, the intellect (Aql), and all the other means through which he knew that whatever is beyond the provision of the traveler (Zad al-Rakib) is a burden upon him in this world (Dunya) and the hereafter (Akhirah).
47:37.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

47:37.arabic: القسم الثالث الذين يقتصرون على أداء الواجب فلا يزيدون عليه ولا ينقصون عنه وهي أقل الرتب وقد اقتصر جميع العوام عليه لبخلهم بالمال وميلهم إليه وضعف حبهم للآخرة قال الله تعالى: ﴿ إن يسألكموها فيحفكم تبخلوا ﴾ {} يحفكم أي يستقصّ عليكم فكم بين عبد اشترى منه ماله ونفسه بأن له الجنة وبين عبد لا يستقصى عليه لبخله فهذا أحد معاني أمر الله سبحانه عبادة ببذل الأموال. المعنى الثاني التطهير من صفة البخل فإنه من المهلكات قال ﭬ: (ثلاث مهلكات شح مطاع وهوى متبع وإعجاب المرء بنفسه[9]) وقال تعالى: ﴿ ومن يوق شح نفسه
47:37.english: The third category: those who limit themselves to performing the obligatory duty, neither increasing upon it nor decreasing from it, and this is the lowest rank. All common people have limited themselves to this due to their stinginess with wealth, their inclination toward it, and their weak love for the Hereafter. Allah the Exalted said: 'If He were to ask you for it and press you, you would withhold and He would expose your grudges.' {} 'Yuhfikum' means He would exact it from you completely. How great is the difference between a servant from whom his wealth and his soul were purchased in exchange for Paradise, and a servant who is not exacted from due to his stinginess. This is one of the meanings of Allah's command to worship Him by spending wealth. The second meaning: purification from the attribute of stinginess, for it is among the destroyers. He (the Prophet) said: 'Three destroyers: obeyed greed, followed desire, and a person's admiration of himself.' And Allah the Exalted said: 'And whoever is protected from the greed (Shuh) of his soul, then those are the successful ones.' {} And it will come in the quarter of the destroyers how it is a destroyer and the method of cleansing from it. The attribute of stinginess only disappears by accustoming oneself to spending wealth, for love of something does not cease except by compelling the soul (Nafs) to abandon it until that becomes habitual. Thus, Zakah in this meaning is a purification (Taharah), meaning it purifies its possessor from the filth of destructive stinginess. Its purification is according to the measure of his spending and according to the measure of his joy in giving it out and his gladness in directing it to Allah the Exalted.
47:37.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

47:37.arabic: الثاني شعر الشارب وقد قال ﭬ: (قصوا الشارب) وفي لفظ آخر (جزوا الشوارب) وفي لفظ آخر (حفوا الشوارب وأعفوا اللحى[62]) أي اجعلوها حفاف الشفة أي حولها وحفاف الشيء حوله ومنه ﴿ وترى الملائكة حافين من حول العرش ﴾ {} وفي لفظ آخر احفوا وهذا يشعر بالاستئصال وقوله حفوا يدل على ما دون ذلك وقال الله عز وجل: ﴿ إن يسئلكموها فيحفكم تبخلوا ﴾ {} أي يستقصي عليكم وأما الحلق فلم يرد والإحفاء القريب من الحلق نقل عن الصحابة نظر بعض التابعين إلى رجل أحفى شاربه فقال ذكرتني أصحاب رسول الله ﭬ.
47:37.english: The second: The hair of the mustache. And He (peace be upon him) said: 'Trim the mustache.' And in another wording: 'Cut the mustaches.' And in another wording: 'Trim the mustaches and let the beards grow.' That is, make them the trimming (hafaf) of the lip, meaning around it, and the trimming (hafaf) of a thing is around it, and from it: 'And you see the angels surrounding (hafeen) from around the Throne.' And in another wording: 'Trim (ahfoo).' And this indicates complete removal, and His saying 'trim (hafoo)' indicates less than that. And Allah the Exalted said: 'If He asks you for it and exhausts (yuhfikum) you, you would withhold.' That is, He would demand from you completely. And as for shaving, it was not mentioned. And the trimming (al-ihfaa) close to shaving was transmitted from the Companions: Some of the Followers looked at a man who trimmed (ahfaa) his mustache and said: 'You reminded me of the companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him).'
47:37.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Mysteries of Purity'
