47:38.arabic: اعلم أن الفقر عبارة عن فقد ما هو محتاج إليه، أما فقد ما لا حاجة إليه فلا يسمى فقراً، وإن كان المحتاج إليه موجوداً مقدوراً عليه لم يكن المحتاج فقيراً، وإذا فهمت هذا لم تشك في أن كل موجود سوى الله تعالى فهو فقير لأنه محتاج إلى دوام الوجود في ثاني الحال ودوام وجود مستفاد من فضل الله تعالى وجوده؛ فإن كان في الوجود موجود ليس وجوده مستفاد له من غيره فهو الغني المطلق، ولا يتصور أن يكون مثل هذا الموجود إلا واحداً، فليس في الوجود إلا غني واحد، وكل من عداه فإنهم محتاجون إليه ليمدوا وجودهم بالدوام، وإلى هذ
47:38.english: Know that poverty (al-faqr) is an expression for the loss of what one is in need of, whereas the loss of what one has no need for is not called poverty. If what is needed exists and is attainable, the one in need is not poor. If you understand this, you will not doubt that every existent besides Allah the Exalted is poor because it is in need of the continuation of existence in the next moment, and the continuation of existence is obtained from the grace of Allah the Exalted for its existence. If there exists in existence an existent whose existence is not obtained from another, then He is the Absolutely Rich (al-Ghani al-Mutlaq), and it is inconceivable that such an existent could be except one. Thus, there is in existence only one Rich (Ghani), and everyone besides Him is in need of Him to extend their existence with continuation. To this exclusivity is the allusion in His saying, the Exalted: "And Allah is the Rich (al-Ghani) and you are the poor (al-fuqara')." This is the meaning of poverty absolutely. However, we do not intend to explain absolute poverty but poverty from wealth in particular, otherwise the poverty of the servant (al-'abd) in relation to the varieties of his needs is not limited, because his needs are without limit.
47:38.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

48:2.arabic: هذا مع أنه ﷺ غفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه وما تأخر وقال ﷺ: (إنه ليغان على قلبي حتى إني لأستغفر الله تعالى في كل يوم مائة مرة[111])
48:2.english: This is despite that the Prophet (peace be upon him) was forgiven for what preceded of his sin and what followed, and he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, a covering (Ghayan) comes over my Heart (Qalb) until I seek forgiveness from Allah the Exalted one hundred times every day.'
48:2.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith

48:2.arabic: فقال يا رسول الله ما يبكيك وقد غفر الله لك ما تقدم من ذنبك وما تأخر فقال ويحك يا بلال وما يمنعنى أن أبكى وقد أنزل الله تعالى على في هذه الليلة إن في خلق السموات والأرض واختلاف الليل والنهار لآيات لأولى الألباب ثم قال ويل لمن قرأها ولم يتفكر فيها
48:2.english: He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what makes you weep when Allah has forgiven you what preceded of your sin and what followed?' He said: 'Woe to you, O Bilal, and what prevents me from weeping when Allah the Exalted has revealed to me in this night: "Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding (أولى الألباب - ulul-albab)."' Then he said: 'Woe to whoever reads it and does not reflect upon it.'
48:2.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Contemplation'

48:4.arabic: والسنن فهذا تصريح بأن الإيمان له وجود ثم بعد الوجود يختلف حاله بالزيادة والنقصان. فإن قلت: فالإشكال قائم في أن التصديق كيف يزيد وينقص وهو خصلة واحدة فأقول إذا تركنا المداهنة ولم نكترث بتشغيب من تشغب وكشفنا الغطاء ارتفع الإشكال فنقول الإيمان اسم مشترك يطلق من ثلاثة أوجه: الأول أنه أنه يطلق للتصديق بالقلب على سبيل الاعتقاد والتقليد من غير كشف وانشراح صدر وهو إيمان العوام بل إيمان الخلق كلهم إلا الخواص وهذا الاعتقاد عقدة عن القلب تارة تشتد وتقوى وتارة تضعف وتسترخي كالعقدة على الخيط مثلا ولا تستبعد
48:4.english: And the traditions, this is an explicit statement that faith (Iman) has existence, then after existence, its condition varies by increase and decrease. If you say: The difficulty remains in how belief (Tasdiq) increases and decreases while it is a single trait, I say: If we abandon hypocrisy (Mudahana) and do not care about the objections of those who object, and we remove the veil, the difficulty is lifted. So we say: Faith (Iman) is a shared name applied in three aspects: The first is that it is applied for belief (Tasdiq) with the heart (Qalb) on the basis of conviction (I'tiqad) and imitation (Taqlid) without unveiling (Kashf) and expansion of the chest (Inshirah Sadr), and this is the faith (Iman) of the common people, indeed the faith (Iman) of all creation except the elite. And this conviction (I'tiqad) is a knot from the heart (Qalb) that sometimes strengthens and becomes firm, and sometimes weakens and slackens, like a knot on a thread, for example. Do not reject this, and consider it with the Jew and his firmness in his conviction (I'tiqad) from which he cannot be diverted by intimidation and warning, nor by illusion and admonition, nor by verification and proof. Likewise the Christian and the innovators, and among them are those who can be doubted with the slightest speech and can be drawn away from their conviction (I'tiqad) with the slightest enticement or intimidation, even though he is not doubting in his knot like the first, but they differ in the intensity of determination. And this exists in the true conviction (I'tiqad) as well, and action ('Amal) affects the growth of this determination and its increase, just as watering affects the growth of trees. Therefore, Allah the Exalted said: 'So it increased them in faith (Iman)' {} and He the Exalted said: 'هُوَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ السَّكِينَةَ فِي قُلُوبِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ لِيَزْدَادُوا إِيمَانًا مَعَ إِيمَانِهِمْ ۗ وَلِلَّهِ جُنُودُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۚ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًا' (He is the One who sent down tranquility (Sakinah) into the hearts (Qulub) of the believers so that they may increase in faith (Iman) with their faith (Iman). And to Allah belong the hosts of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.) {} and He said in what is narrated in some reports: 'Faith (Iman) increases and decreases' [54], and that is due to the effect of acts of obedience (Taa'at) on the heart (Qalb). And this is not perceived except by one who observes the states of his soul (Nafs) in times of persistence in worship ('Ibadah) and devotion to it with presence of the heart (Qalb) compared to times of slackness, and perceives the difference in tranquility (Sukun) to the convictions (Aqa'id) of faith (Iman) in these states, until his knot increases in resistance to one who wants to untie it by doubt. Rather, one who believes in the orphan the meaning of mercy (Rahmah), if he acts according to his belief (I'tiqad) by stroking his head and being gentle with him, perceives from his inner self (Batin) the confirmation of mercy (Rahmah) and its multiplication due to the action ('Amal). Likewise, one who believes in humility (Tawadu'), if he acts according to it by an act of bowing or prostrating to another, feels from his heart (Qalb) humility (Tawadu') upon embarking on service. And thus all attributes of the heart (Qalb) issue from them actions of the limbs, then the effect of the actions returns upon them, confirming and increasing them. And this will come in the quarter of the salvations and the destroyers when explaining the aspect of the connection of the inner (Batin) with the outer (Zahir) and the actions ('A'mal) with the convictions (Aqa'id) and the hearts (Qulub), for that is of the kind of connection of the kingdom (Mulk) with the dominion (Malakut). And I mean by the kingdom (Mulk) the world of testimony (Shahadah) perceived by the senses, and by the dominion (Malakut) the world of the unseen (Ghayb) perceived by the light of insight (Basirah). And the heart (Qalb) is from the world of the dominion (Malakut), and the limbs and their actions are from the world of the kingdom (Mulk). And the subtlety and precision of the connection between the two worlds reaches to the extent that some people thought the union of one of them.
48:4.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

48:5.arabic: زيادة ولكني أقول  الأمر  اليقيني  الذي  لا  شك  فيه  تختلف طمأنينة النفس إليه  فليس  طمأنينة  النفس  إلى  أن  الاثنين  أكثر  من  الواحد كطمأنينتها إلى أن العالم مصنوع  حادث  وإن  كان  لا  شك  في  واحد  منهما  فإن اليقينيات تختلف في درجات الإيضاح ودرجات طمأنينة النفس إليها وقد تعرضنا  لهذا في فصل اليقين من كتاب العلم في باب علامات علماء الآخرة فلا حاجة إلى  الإعادة وقد ظهر في جميع الإطلاقات أن ما قالوه من زيادة الإيمان ونقصانه حق  وكيف  وفي الأخبار (أنه يخرج من النار من كان في  قلبه  مثقال  ذرة
48:5.english: Increase, but I say: The certain matter (الأمر اليقيني) that has no doubt in it differs in the tranquility of the Soul (النفس) towards it. For the tranquility of the Soul (النفس) that two is more than one is not like its tranquility that the world is created, originated, even though there is no doubt in one of them. For certainties differ in degrees of clarification and degrees of tranquility of the Soul (النفس) towards them. We have addressed this in the chapter of Certainty (اليقين) from the Book of Knowledge in the section on signs of the scholars of the Hereafter, so there is no need for repetition. And it has appeared in all the statements that what they said about the increase and decrease of faith is true, and how? And in the reports: 'He will be taken out of the Fire who has in his Heart (قلب) an atom's weight of faith.' And in some places in another report: 'A dinar's weight.' So what is the meaning of the difference in its measures if what is in the Heart (قلب) does not vary? [Question] If you say: What is the aspect of the saying of the predecessors: 'I am a believer, if Allah wills,' and the exception is doubt, and doubt in faith is disbelief? And they all used to refrain from giving a definitive answer with faith and guard against it. So Sufyan al-Thawri, may Allah have mercy on him, said: 'Whoever says I am a believer with Allah, he is among the liars, and whoever says I am a true believer, it is an innovation.' How can he be a liar when he knows he is a believer in himself? And whoever is a believer in himself is a believer with Allah, just as whoever is tall or generous in himself and knows that, is so with Allah, and likewise whoever is joyful or sad, or hearing or seeing. And if it were said to a person: 'Are you an animal?' it would not be proper to say 'I am an animal, if Allah wills.' And when Sufyan said that, it was said to him: 'So what do we say?' He said: 'Say: We believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us.' And what difference is there between saying 'We believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us' and saying 'I am a believer'? And it was said to al-Hasan: 'Are you a believer?' He said: 'If Allah wills.' It was said to him: 'Why do you make an exception, O Abu Sa'id, in faith?' He said: 'I fear to say yes, then Allah, glorified and exalted, would say: You have lied, O Hasan, so the word would be established against me.' And he used to say: 'What assures me that Allah, glorified and exalted, has looked upon me in some of what He dislikes, so He detested me and said: Go, I have not accepted any deed from you, so I am working in a non-work?' And Ibrahim ibn Adham said: 'If it is said to you: Are you a believer? Say: There is no god but Allah.' And once he said: 'Say: I do not doubt in faith, and your asking me is an innovation.' And it was said to 'Alqamah: 'Are you a believer?' He said: 'I hope, if Allah wills.' And al-Thawri said: 'We are believers in Allah, His angels, His books, and His messengers, and we do not know what we are with Allah, the Exalted.' So what is the meaning of these exceptions? The answer is that this exception is correct and has four aspects: two aspects relying on doubt not in the origin of faith but in its conclusion or perfection, and two aspects not relying on doubt. The first aspect: which does not rely on opposition.
48:5.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

48:12.arabic: وقال تعالى: ﴿ وظننتم ظن السوء وكنتم قوما بورا ﴾ {} وقال ﭬ: (إن الله تعالى يقول للعبد يوم القيامة ما منعك إذ رأيت المنكر أن تنكره فإن لقنه الله حجته قال يا رب رجوتك وخفت الناس قال فيقول الله تعالى قد غفرته لك)[6].
48:12.english: And He (Allah), the Exalted, said: 'And you thought evil thought (ظن السوء) and you were a people ruined (بورا).' And he (the Prophet, peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, says to the servant on the Day of Resurrection: What prevented you when you saw the evil (المنكر) from forbidding it? Then if Allah grants him his argument, he says: O my Lord, I hoped in You (رجوتك) and I feared the people. Then Allah, the Exalted, says: I have forgiven it for you.'
48:12.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Fear and Hope'

48:13.arabic: وقد ساواهم في النسب وشاركهم في القبائل من لم يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر، وكانوا عند الله شراً من الكلاب وأخس من الخنازير، ولذلك قال تعالى "وَمَنْ لَمْ يُؤْمِنْ بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ فَإِنَّا أَعْتَدْنَا لِلْكَافِرِينَ سَعِيرًا"
48:13.english: And those who did not believe in Allah and the Last Day have equaled them in lineage and shared with them in the tribes, and they were with Allah worse than dogs and more base than swine. Therefore, Allah the Exalted said: "And whoever does not believe in Allah and His Messenger - then indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers a Blaze (Sa'ir)."
48:13.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

48:17.arabic: وخطب رجل عند رسول الله ﭬ فقال: من يطع الله ورسوله فقد رشد ومن يعصهما فقد غوى"[257] فقال "قل: ومن يعص الله ورسوله فقد غوى فكره رسول الله ﭬ قوله: ومن يعصهما، لأنه تسوية وجمع.
48:17.english: And a man delivered a sermon in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and said: 'Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has been guided, and whoever disobeys them has gone astray.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Say: and whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has gone astray.' And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) disliked his saying: 'and whoever disobeys them,' because it is an equalization and a grouping together.
48:17.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

48:23.arabic: وكما أن دوام الوجود محبوب فكمال الوجود أيضاً فاقد للكمال، والنقص عدم بالإضافة إلى القدر المفقود وهو هلاك بالنسبة إليه. والهلاك والعدم ممقوت في الصفات، وكمال الوجود كما أنه ممقوت في أصل الذات ووجود صفات الكمال محبوب، كما أن دوام أصل الوجود محبوب، وهذه غريزة في الطباع بحكم سنة الله تعالى "ولن تجد لسنة الله تبديلاً ".
48:23.english: And just as the permanence of existence is beloved, so too is the perfection of existence, and deficiency is non-existence in relation to the missing measure, and it is destruction relative to it. And destruction and non-existence are detested in attributes, and the perfection of existence, as it is detested in the essence of the self (Dhāt), the existence of attributes of perfection is beloved, just as the permanence of the essence of existence is beloved. And this is an instinct in the natural dispositions (Tabā'i') by the decree of the Sunnah (Sunnah) of Allah the Exalted: "And you will never find for the Sunnah (Sunnah) of Allah any change."
48:23.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

48:26.arabic: قال الله تعالى "إذ جعل الذين كفروا في قلوبهم الحمية حمية الجاهلية فأنزل الله سكينته على رسوله وعلى المؤمنين" الآية. ذم الكفار بما تظاهروا به من الحمية الصادرة عن الغضب بالباطل، ومدح المؤمنين بما أنزل الله عليهم من السكينة
48:26.english: Allah the Exalted said: "When those who disbelieved placed in their hearts the zealotry (hamiyyah), the zealotry of ignorance (jahiliyyah), then Allah sent down His tranquility (sakinah) upon His Messenger and upon the believers" the verse. He censured the disbelievers for what they displayed of zealotry emanating from anger (ghadab) in falsehood, and praised the believers for what Allah sent down upon them of tranquility (sakinah).
48:26.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

48:27.arabic: ومهما صفا الباطن انكشف في حدقة القلب ما سيكون في المستقبل كما انكشف دخول مكة لرسول الله ﷺ في النوم حتى نزل قوله تعالى: ﴿ لَقَدْ صَدَقَ اللَّهُ رَسُولَهُ الرُّؤْيَا بِالْحَقِّ ۖ لَتَدْخُلُنَّ الْمَسْجِدَ الْحَرَامَ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ آمِنِينَ مُحَلِّقِينَ رُءُوسَكُمْ وَمُقَصِّرِينَ لَا تَخَافُونَ ۖ فَعَلِمَ مَا لَمْ تَعْلَمُوا فَجَعَلَ مِنْ دُونِ ذَٰلِكَ فَتْحًا قَرِيبًا ﴾ وقلما يخلوا الإنسان عن منامات دلت على أمور فوجدها صحيحة والرؤيا ومعرفة الغيب في النوم من عجائب صنع الله تعالى وبدائع فطرة الآ
48:27.english: Whenever the inner self (Batin) becomes purified, what will happen in the future is unveiled in the pupil of the heart (Qalb), just as the entry into Mecca was unveiled to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in sleep until His saying, the Exalted, descended: 'Certainly has Allah shown to His Messenger the vision (Ru'ya) in truth. You will surely enter al-Masjid al-Haram, if Allah wills, in safety, with your heads shaved and [hair] shortened, not fearing. But He knew what you did not know and has arranged before that a conquest near [at hand].' And rarely is a human being free from dreams that indicated matters and he found them correct, and the vision (Ru'ya) and knowledge of the unseen (Ghayb) in sleep are from the wonders of Allah's creation and the marvels of the human primordial nature (Fitrah), and it is among the clearest proofs of the world of dominion (Malakut), while the creation are heedless of it as they are heedless of the rest of the wonders of the heart (Qalb) and the wonders of the world.
48:27.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

48:27.arabic: الوجه الثاني: التأدب بذكر الله تعالى في كل حال وإحالة الأمور كلها إلى مشيئة الله سبحانه فقد أدب الله سبحانه نبيه ﭬ فقال تعالى: ﴿ ولا تقولن لشيء إني فاعل ذلك غدا إلا أن يشاء الله ﴾ {} ثم لم يقتصر على ذلك فيما لا يشك فيه بل قال تعالى: ﴿ لتدخلن المسجد الحرام إن شاء الله آمنين محلقين رءؤسكم ومقصرين ﴾ {} وكان الله سبحانه عالما بأنهم يدخلون لا محالة وأنه شاءه ولكن المقصود تعليمه ذلك فتأدب رسول الله ﭬ في ما كان يخبر عنه معلوما كان أو مشكوكا حتى قال ﭬ لما دخل المقابر: (السلام عليكم دار قوم مؤمنين وإنا إ
48:27.english: The second aspect: The etiquette (Adab) of mentioning Allah the Exalted in every situation and referring all matters to the will (Mashiyyah) of Allah the Blessed and Exalted. Indeed Allah the Blessed and Exalted taught His Prophet (peace be upon him) etiquette, as He said: 'And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow," except [when adding], "If Allah wills."' Then He did not limit this to matters of doubt, but said: 'You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque (Al-Masjid Al-Haram), if Allah wills, in safety, with your heads shaved and [hair] shortened, not fearing.' And Allah the Blessed and Exalted knew that they would enter inevitably and that He willed it, but the purpose was to teach him that. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) observed etiquette in what he informed about, whether known or doubted, until he said (peace be upon him) when he entered the graveyards: 'Peace be upon you, O abode of believing people, and we, if Allah wills, will join you.' And joining them is not doubted, but the requirement of etiquette is mentioning Allah the Exalted and connecting matters to Him. This formulation indicates that until it became, by customary usage, an expression of showing desire (Raghbah) and wish (Tamanni). So if it is said to you that so-and-so will die quickly, and you say 'If Allah wills,' it is understood from it your desire, not your doubt. And if it is said to you that so-and-so's illness will depart and he will recover, and you say 'If Allah wills' meaning desire, then the word has shifted from the meaning of doubt to the meaning of desire, and likewise the shift to the meaning of etiquette for mentioning Allah the Exalted, however the matter was.
48:27.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

48:27.arabic: [30] حديث فضل لقد صدق الله رسوله الرؤيا بالحق لم أجد فيه حديثا يخصها لكن في فضل سورة الفتح ما رواه أبو الشيخ في كتاب من حديث أبي بن كعب من قرأ سورة الفتح فكأنما شهد فتح مكة مع النبي ﭬ وهو حديث موضوع.
48:27.english: [30] Narration regarding the virtue of 'Certainly Allah has fulfilled His Messenger's vision in truth...' I did not find in it a narration that specifically addresses it, but regarding the virtue of Surah Al-Fath (The Victory), what Abu Al-Sheikh reported in his book from the narration of Ubayy ibn Ka'b: 'Whoever recites Surah Al-Fath, it is as if he witnessed the conquest of Mecca with the Prophet ﷬,' and this is a fabricated narration.
48:27.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Book of Knowledge'

48:27.arabic: ومن آياته الظاهرة التي تحدى بها مع كافة العرب القرآن العظيم فإنهم مع تمييزهم بالفصاحة والبلاغة تهدفوا لسبه ونهيه وقتله وإخراجه كما أخبر الله عز وجل عنهم ولم يقدروا على معارضته بمثل القرآن إذ لم يكن في قدرة البشر الجمع بين جزالة القرآن ونظمه هذا مع ما فيه من أخبار الأولين مع كونه أميا غير ممارس للكتب والإنباء عن الغيب في أمور تحقق صدقه فيها في الاستقبال كقوله تعالى لتدخلن المسجد الحرام إن شاء الله آمنين محلقين رؤوسكم ومقصرين وكقوله ألم غلبت الروم في أدنى الأرض وهم من بعد غلبهم سيغلبون في بضع سنين
48:27.english: And from His clear signs with which He challenged all the Arabs is the Great Quran. For they, despite their distinction in eloquence and rhetoric, aimed to insult him, forbid him, kill him, and expel him as Allah the Exalted informed about them, and they were unable to oppose it with the like of the Quran, since it was not within human capability to combine the majesty of the Quran and its composition with what it contains of news of the ancients while he was unlettered, not practiced in books, and informing of the unseen in matters that proved his truthfulness in the future, such as His saying: 'You will certainly enter the Sacred Mosque, if Allah wills, secure, shaving your heads and shortening [your hair],' and such as His saying: 'Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land, and they, after their defeat, will overcome within a few years.' And the aspect of the miracle's indication of the truthfulness of the messengers is that everything humans are incapable of is only an act of Allah the Exalted, so whenever it is accompanied by the challenge of the Prophet ﷺ, it takes the place of His saying 'You have spoken truthfully.' That is like the one who says before the king, claiming to his subjects that he is the king's messenger to them. For whenever he says to him, 'If you are truthful, then stand on your bed three times and sit contrary to your habit,' and the king does that, the attendees attain necessary knowledge that this takes the place of his saying 'You have spoken truthfully.'
48:27.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Foundations of Belief'

48:27.arabic: وقوله تعالى: ﴿ لقد صدق الله رسوله الرؤيا بالحق ﴾ {} إلى آخرها[30]
48:27.english: And His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, Allah has fulfilled His Messenger's vision in truth' {} to its end [30]
48:27.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Book of Knowledge'

48:29.arabic: ثم فسره فقال أصلبها في الدين وأصفاها في اليقين وأرقها على الإخوان وهو إشارة إلى قوله تعالى أشداء على الكفار رحماء بينهم وقوله تعالى مثل نوره كمشكاة فيها مصباح قال أبي بن كعب رضي الله عنه معناه مثل نور المؤمن وقلبه وقوله تعالى أو كظلمات في بحر لجي مثل قلب المنافق وقال زيد بن أسلم في قوله تعالى في لوح محفوظ وهو قلب المؤمن وقال سهل مثل القلب والصدر مثل العرش والكرسي فهذه أمثلة القلب.
48:29.english: Then he explained it, saying: 'The firmest in religion, the purest in certainty (Yaqin), and the most tender toward the brothers.' This is an allusion to His saying, the Exalted: 'Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are firm against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating, seeking bounty from Allah and pleasure. Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration. That is their description in the Torah. And their description in the Gospel is as a seed which sends forth its shoot, then strengthens it, then it becomes thick and stands straight upon its stalk, pleasing the sowers - that He may enrage the disbelievers thereby. Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds among them forgiveness and a great reward.' And His saying, the Exalted: 'The example of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp...' Abu bin Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him, said its meaning is: 'The example of the light of the believer and his heart (Qalb).' And His saying, the Exalted: 'Or [they are] like darknesses within an unfathomable sea...' is the example of the heart of the hypocrite. And Zaid bin Aslam said regarding His saying, the Exalted: 'In a Preserved Slate...' that it is the heart of the believer. And Sahl said: 'The example of the heart and the chest is like the Throne and the Footstool.' These are the examples of the heart.
48:29.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

48:29.arabic: وقال في الغضب "أشداء على الكفار رحماء بينهم" وقال ﭬ "خير الأمور أوساطها" وهذا له سر وتحقيق وهو أن السعادة منوطة بسلامة القلب عن عوارض هذا العالم. قال الله تعالى "إلا من أتى الله بقلب سليم" والبخل من عوارض الدنيا، والتبذير أيضاً من عوارض الدنيا، وشرط القلب أن يكون سليماً منهما أي لا يكون ملتفتاً إلى المال ولا يكون حريصاً على إنفاقه ولا على إمساكه، فإن الحريص على الإنفاق مصروف القلب إلى الإنفاق كما أن الحريص على الإمساك مصروف القلب إلى الإمساك فكان كمال القلب أن يصفوا عن الوصفين جميعاً. وإذا لم يك
48:29.english: And He said regarding anger "Severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves" and He (peace be upon him) said "The best of matters are their middle ones." And this has a secret and verification, which is that happiness is tied to the soundness of the Heart (Qalb) from the accidents of this world. Allah the Exalted said "Except he who comes to Allah with a sound heart." And miserliness is from the accidents of the worldly life, and extravagance is also from the accidents of the worldly life, and the condition of the Heart (Qalb) is that it be sound from both of them, meaning it should not be attentive to wealth nor should it be eager for spending it nor for withholding it, for the one eager for spending has his Heart (Qalb) diverted to spending just as the one eager for withholding has his Heart (Qalb) diverted to withholding. So the perfection of the Heart (Qalb) is that it be purified from both descriptions altogether. And if that is not attainable in this world, we seek what is most similar to the absence of both descriptions and farthest from the two extremes, which is the middle, for the lukewarm is neither hot nor cold but rather is middle between them, as if it is free from both descriptions. Likewise, generosity is between extravagance and stinginess. And courage is between cowardice and recklessness. And chastity is between greed and abstinence. And likewise all other character traits, for both extremes of matters are blameworthy; this is what is sought and it is possible.
48:29.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

48:29.arabic: ومنها أن يكون مشفقاً على جميع عباد الله رحيماً بهم شديداً على جميع أعداء الله وعلى كل من يقارف شيئاً مما يكرهه كما قال الله تعالى: "أشداء على الكفار رحماء بينهم" ولا تأخذه لومة لائم ولا يصرفه عن الغضب لله صارف، وبه وصف الله أولياؤه إذ قال الذين يكلفون بحبي كما يكلف الصبي بالشيء ويأوون إلى ذكري كما يأوي النسر إلى وكره، ويغضبون لمحارمه كما يغضب النمر إذا حرد فإنه لا يبالي قل الناس أو كثروا، فانظر إلى هذا المثال فإن الصبي إذا كلف بالشيء لم يفارقه أصلاً، وإن أخذ منه لم يكن له شغل إلا البكاء والصياح
48:29.english: And among them is that he be compassionate toward all the servants of Allah, merciful to them, severe toward all the enemies of Allah and toward everyone who commits something that He dislikes, as Allah the Exalted said: "Severe upon the disbelievers, merciful among themselves." And the blame of a blamer does not take him, nor does any turner turn him away from anger for Allah. And with this, Allah described His allies (awliya'), as He said: Those who are charged with My love (hubb) as a child is charged with something, and they take refuge in My remembrance (dhikr) as an eagle takes refuge in its nest, and they become angry for My prohibitions as a tiger becomes angry when enraged, for he does not care whether people are few or many. So look at this example: For the child, when charged with something, does not leave it at all, and if it is taken from him, he has no occupation except crying and shouting until it is returned to him. If he sleeps, he takes it with him in his clothes, and when he awakens, he returns and clings to it. Whenever he is separated from it, he cries, and whenever he finds it, he laughs. Whoever disputes with him about it, he hates him, and whoever gives it to him, he loves him. As for the tiger, he does not control himself when angry until he reaches such intensity of his anger that he destroys himself. These are the signs of love (mahabba). So whoever has these signs completed in him, then his love (muhabbah) has been completed and his affection (hubb) has become pure, so his drink becomes clear in the Hereafter and his watering place sweet. And whoever mixes with his love (hubb) love for other than Allah enjoys in the Hereafter according to his love (hubb), for his drink is mixed with a portion of the drink of the brought-near ones (muqarrabun), as Allah said concerning the righteous (abrar): "Indeed, the righteous will be in pleasure." Then He said: "They will be given to drink of a sealed pure wine. Its seal is musk - so for that let the competitors compete - and its mixture is of Tasnim, a spring from which those brought near drink." So the drink of the righteous becomes pleasant due to the mixing of the pure drink that is for the brought-near ones.
48:29.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

48:29.arabic: وقيل إن أقرب ما يكون العبد من الله تعالى أن يكون ساجدا وهو معنى قوله عز وجل: ﴿ واسجد واقترب ﴾ {العلق: 19} وقال عز وجل: ﴿ سيماهم في وجوههم من أثر السجود ﴾ {الفتح: 29} فقيل هو ما يلتصق بوجوههم من الأرض عند السجود وقيل هو نور الخشوع فإنه يشرق من الباطن على الظاهر وهو الأصح وقيل هي الغرر التي تكون في وجوههم يوم القيامة من أثر الوضوء.
48:29.english: And it is said that the closest the servant (Al-'Abd) can be to God the Exalted is when he is prostrating, and this is the meaning of His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And prostrate and draw near' (Al-'Alaq: 19). And He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration' (Al-Fath: 29). So it is said it is what sticks to their faces from the earth during prostration, and it is said it is the light of humility (Al-Khushu') for it shines from the inner (Al-Batin) to the outer (Al-Zahir), and this is the most correct, and it is said it is the radiance (Al-Ghurrah) that will be on their faces on the Day of Resurrection from the trace of ablution.
48:29.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

48:29.arabic: فقد وصف الله تعالى الصحابة فقال "أشداء على الكفار رحماء بينهم" إشارة إلى أن للشدة موضعاً وللرحمة موضعاً، فليس الكمال في الشدة بكل حال ولا في الرحمة بكل حال. فهذا بيان معنى الخلق وحسنه وقبحه وبيان أركانه وثمراته وفروعه.
48:29.english: Indeed, Allah the Exalted described the Companions (of the Prophet) by saying: "They are severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves" (Quran 48:29), indicating that severity has its place and mercy has its place. Perfection is not in severity in every situation nor in mercy in every situation. This is an explanation of the meaning of character (Khuluq) and its goodness and ugliness, and an explanation of its pillars, fruits, and branches.
48:29.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

49:1.arabic: قدم ركب من بني تميم على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال أبو بكر أمر القعقاع بن معبد وقال عمر بل أمر الأقرع بن حابس فقال أبو بكر ما أردت إلا خلافي وقال عمر ما أردت خلافك فتماريا حتى ارتفعت أصواتهما فنزلت يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تقدموا بين يدي الله ورسوله
49:1.english: A delegation from Banu Tamim came to the Prophet (peace be upon him). Abu Bakr said: 'Appoint Al-Qa'qa' bin Ma'bad.' And Umar said: 'Rather appoint Al-Aqra' bin Habis.' Abu Bakr said: 'You only intended to oppose me.' And Umar said: 'I did not intend to oppose you.' They disputed until their voices were raised, so was revealed: 'O you who have believed (Amanu), do not put yourselves forward (Taqaddimu) before Allah and His Messenger.'
49:1.book_title: Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character
49:1.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character'

49:1.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
49:1.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'Whatever is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" (Ya ayyuha alladhina amanu), it is in the Torah "O you who are poor" (Ya ayyuha al-masakiin).'
49:1.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

49:2.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
49:2.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'Whatever is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" (Ya ayyuha alladhina amanu), it is in the Torah "O you who are poor" (Ya ayyuha al-masakiin).'
49:2.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

49:3.arabic: والذي يقتضي الإيمان بهذا الأمر في القرآن والسنة وأقاويل العلماء أكثر من أن يحصر. قال الله تعالى "ونهى النفس عن الهوى فإن الجنة هي المأوى" وقال تعالى "أولئك الذين امتحن الله قلوبهم للتقوى" قيل نزع منها محبة الشهوات. وقال ﭬ "المؤمن بين خمس شدائد: مؤمن يحسده ومنافق يبغضه وكافر يقاتله وشيطان يضله ونفس تنازعه"[43] فبين أن النفس عدو منازع يجب عليه مجاهدته.
49:3.english: And that which necessitates faith in this matter from the Quran, the Sunnah, and the sayings of the scholars is too numerous to enumerate. Allah the Exalted said: 'And he who restrains the Soul (Nafs) from desire (Hawa), then Paradise is the abode.' And He the Exalted said: 'Those are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for piety (Taqwa).' It is said: He extracted from them the love of desires. And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'The believer is between five hardships: a believer who envies him, a hypocrite who hates him, an unbeliever who fights him, a devil who misguides him, and a soul (Nafs) that contends with him.' [43] Thus, he clarified that the soul (Nafs) is a contending enemy that must be struggled against.
49:3.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

49:6.arabic: فلا يجوز تصديق إبليس، وإن كان ثم مخيلة تدل على فساد واحتمل خلافه لم يجز أن تصدق به، لأن الفاسق يتصور أن بصدق في خيره ولكن لا يجوز لك أن تصدق به، حتى إن من استنكه فوجد منه رائحة الخمر لا يجوز أن يحد، إذ يقال يمكن أن يكون قد تمضمض بالخمر ومجها وما شربها، أو حمل عليه قهراً، فكل ذلك لا محالة دلالة محتملة فلا يجوز تصديقها بالقلب وإساءة الظن بالمسلم بها، وقد قال ﭬ "إن الله حرم من المسلم دمه وماله وأن يظن به ظن السوء"[216] فلا يستباح ظن السوء إلا بما يستباح به المال وهو نفس مشاهدته أو بينة عادلة، فإذا
49:6.english: So it is not permissible to believe Iblis (Satan), and if there is an imagination that indicates corruption and it admits the opposite, it is not permissible to believe it, because the corrupt one (Fasiq) may imagine that he is truthful in his goodness, but it is not permissible for you to believe him. Even if someone smells from him and finds the scent of wine, it is not permissible to punish him, as it is said: it is possible that he gargled with wine and spat it out and did not drink it, or he was forced upon it. All of that is inevitably a probable indication, so it is not permissible to believe it with the heart (Qalb) and have bad suspicion (Sū' al-Zann) of the Muslim with it. And he (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, Allah has made sacred from the Muslim his blood, his wealth, and that he be suspected with bad suspicion." So bad suspicion is not permitted except with what permits wealth, which is witnessing it oneself or just testimony. If it is not so, and the whisper (Waswās) of bad suspicion occurs to you, then you should repel it from yourself and affirm upon it that his state with you is concealed as it was, and that what you saw from him admits good and evil.
49:6.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

49:6.arabic: وذكر فإن الذكرى تنفع المؤمنين فهذا وما يجرى مجراه هو أول مقام المرابطة مع النفس وهي محاسبة قبل العمل والمحاسبة تارة تكون بعد العمل وتارة قبله للتحذير قال الله تعالى واعلموا أن الله يعلم ما في أنفسكم فاحذروه وهذا للمستقبل وكل نظر في كثرة ومقدار لمعرفة زيادة ونقصان فإنه يسمى محاسبة فالنظر فيما بين يدي العبد في نهاره ليعرف زيادته من نقصانه من المحاسبة وقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا ضربتم في سبيل الله فتبينوا وقال تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن جاءكم فاسق بنبأ فتبينوا وقال تعالى ولقد خلقنا
49:6.english: And remembrance (Dhikr), for the reminder benefits the believers. This and what runs its course is the first station of vigilance (Murabatah) with the Soul (Nafs), and it is accountability (Muhasabah) before action. Accountability is sometimes after action and sometimes before it for warning. Allah the Exalted said: 'And know that Allah knows what is in your souls (Anfusikum), so beware of Him.' This is for the future. And every looking into quantity and measure to know increase and decrease, then it is called accountability. So the looking at what is before the servant during his day to know his increase from his decrease is from accountability. And Allah the Exalted has said: 'O you who have believed, when you go forth in the path of Allah, then verify.' And He said: 'O you who have believed, if there comes to you a wicked person with information, then verify.' And He said: 'And We have certainly created man and know what his soul (Nafs) whispers to him.' Mentioning that as a warning and alerting to guard against it in the future.
49:6.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

49:6.arabic: فعليه ستة أمور، الأول: أن لا يصدقه لأن النمام فاسق وهو مردود الشهادة قال الله تعالى "يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن جاءكم فاسق بنبأ فتبينوا أن تصيبوا قوماً بجهالة" الثاني: أن ينهاه عن ذلك وينصح له ويقبح عليه فعله قال الله تعالى "وأمر بالمعروف وانه عن المنكر" الثالث: أن يبغضه في الله تعالى فإنه بغيض عند الله تعالى ويجب بغض من يبغضه الله تعالى. والرابع: أن لا تظن بأخيك الغائب السوء لقول الله تعالى "اجتنبوا كثيراً من الظن إن بعض الظن إثم" الخامس: أن لا يحملك ما حكى لك على التجسس والبحث لتحقق، اتباعاً لقول
49:6.english: Upon him are six matters: First: That he should not believe him because the talebearer is a transgressor (Fāsiq) and his testimony is rejected. Allah the Exalted said: "O you who have believed, if there comes to you a transgressor (Fāsiq) with information, then verify, lest you harm a people out of ignorance and become, over what you have done, regretful." Second: That he should forbid him from that and advise him and deem his action ugly, following the saying of Allah the Exalted: "And enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong." Third: That he should hate him for the sake of Allah the Exalted, for he is hateful to Allah the Exalted, and it is obligatory to hate whom Allah hates. Fourth: That he should not suspect evil of his absent brother, according to the saying of Allah the Exalted: "Avoid much suspicion, indeed some suspicion is sin." Fifth: That what he narrated to you should not drive you to spy and investigate to verify, following the saying of Allah the Exalted: "And do not spy." Sixth: That you should not accept for yourself what you forbade the talebearer from, nor narrate his talebearing by saying: So-and-so narrated to me such-and-such, for then you would become by it a talebearer and a backbiter, and you might have committed what you forbade him from. And it has been narrated from 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Azīz, may Allah be pleased with him, that a man entered upon him and mentioned something to him about a man, so 'Umar said to him: If you wish, we will look into your matter; if you are lying, then you are among the people of this verse: "If there comes to you a transgressor (Fāsiq) with information, then verify," and if you are truthful, then you are among the people of this verse: "Slanderer, going about with malicious gossip," and if you wish, we pardon you? He said: Pardon, O Commander of the Believers, I will never return to it.
49:6.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

49:6.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
49:6.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'What is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)".'
49:6.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

49:6.arabic: وكل من حملت إليه النميمة وقيل له إن فلاناً قال فيك كذا وكذا أو فعل في حقك كذا أو هو يدبر في إفساد أمرك أو في ممالأة عدوك أو تقبيح حالك أو ما يجري مجراه فعليه ستة أمور، الأول: أن لا يصدقه لأن النمام فاسق وهو مردود الشهادة قال الله تعالى "يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن جاءكم فاسق بنبأ فتبينوا أن تصيبوا قوماً بجهالة" الثاني: أن ينهاه عن ذلك وينصح له ويقبح عليه فعله قال الله تعالى "وأمر بالمعروف وانه عن المنكر" الثالث: أن يبغضه في الله تعالى فإنه بغيض عند الله تعالى ويجب بغض من يبغضه الله تعالى. والرابع: أن
49:6.english: And for everyone to whom backbiting (Namima) is brought and it is said to him that so-and-so said such-and-such about you or did such-and-such against your right or is plotting to corrupt your affair or in siding with your enemy or defaming your condition or what runs its course, upon him are six matters: First: That he should not believe him because the backbiter (Namim) is a transgressor (Fasiq) and his testimony is rejected. Allah the Exalted said: 'O you who have believed, if there comes to you a transgressor (Fasiq) with information, then verify, lest you harm a people in ignorance and become, over what you have done, regretful.' Second: That he should forbid him from that and advise him and deem his action ugly. Allah the Exalted said: 'And enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong.' Third: That he should hate him for the sake of Allah the Exalted, for he is hateful in the sight of Allah the Exalted, and it is obligatory to hate whom Allah the Exalted hates. Fourth: That you should not suspect evil of your absent brother, according to the saying of Allah the Exalted: 'Avoid much suspicion, indeed some suspicion is sin.' Fifth: That what he narrated to you should not compel you to spy and investigate to verify, following the saying of Allah the Exalted: 'And do not spy.' Sixth: That you should not be pleased for yourself with what you forbade the backbiter from, nor should you narrate his backbiting by saying so-and-so narrated to me such-and-such, for then you would become by it a backbiter and a slanderer, and you might have done what you forbade him from. And it has been narrated from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, may Allah be pleased with him, that a man entered upon him and mentioned to him something about a man, so Umar said to him: If you wish, we will look into your matter; if you are lying, then you are among the people of this verse: 'If there comes to you a transgressor (Fasiq) with information, then verify,' and if you are truthful, then you are among the people of this verse: 'Slanderer, going about with backbiting (Namim),' and if you wish, we pardon you? He said: Pardon, O Commander of the Believers, I will never return to it again.
49:6.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

49:9.arabic: وقال تعالى لا خير في كثير من نجواهم إلا من أمر بصدقة أو معروف أو إصلاح بين الناس ومن يفعل ذلك ابتغاء مرضاة الله فسوف نؤتيه اجرا عظيما وقال تعالى وإن طائفتان من المؤمنين اقتتلوا فأصلحوا بينهما الآية والاصلاح نهي عن البغي وإعادة إلى الطاعة فإن لم يفعل فقد أمر الله تعالى بقتاله فقال فقاتلوا التي تبغي حتى تفيء إلى أمر الله وذلك هو النهي عن المنكر
49:9.english: And Allah the Exalted said: 'There is no good in much of their secret talk, except for one who enjoins charity or good (Ma'ruf) or reconciliation between people. And whoever does that seeking the pleasure of Allah, then We will give him a great reward.' And Allah the Exalted said: 'And if two parties of the believers fight, then make peace between them...' the verse. And the reconciliation is forbidding from transgression (Baghy) and returning to obedience. If they do not do so, then Allah the Exalted has commanded to fight them, so He said: 'Then fight the one that transgresses until it returns to the command of Allah.' And that is the forbidding from evil (Munkar).
49:9.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

49:11.arabic: الآفة الحادية عشر السخرية والاستهزاء وهذا محرم مهما كان مؤذياً كما قال تعالى "يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا يسخر قوم من قوم عسى أن يكونوا خيراً منهم ولا نساء من نساء عسى أن يكن خيراً منهن" ومعنى السخرية الاستهانة والتحقير والتنبيه على العيوب والنقائص على وجه يضحك منه: وقد يكون ذلك بالمحاكاة في الفعل والقول، وقد يكون بالإشارة والإيماء، وإذا كان بحضرة المستهزأ به لم يسم ذلك غيبة وفيه معنى الغيبة. قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها: حاكيت إنساناً فقال لي النبي ﭬ "والله ما أحب أني حاكيت إنساناً ولي كذا وكذا"[122] وق
49:11.english: The eleventh affliction: Mockery and derision. And this is forbidden however harmful it may be, as Allah the Exalted said: "O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people; perhaps they may be better than them; nor let women ridicule [other] women; perhaps they may be better than them." And the meaning of mockery is belittling, contempt, and pointing out faults and deficiencies in a manner that causes laughter from it: and that may be through imitation in action and speech, and it may be through indication and gesture, and if it is in the presence of the one being mocked, it is not called backbiting, yet it contains the meaning of backbiting. Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: I imitated a person, so the Prophet ﭬ said to me: "By Allah, I do not love that I imitated a person and I have such and such." And Ibn Abbas said regarding His saying the Exalted: "Woe to us! What is with this Book that leaves nothing small or great but it has enumerated it?" Indeed, the small is smiling in mockery of the believer, and the great is loud laughter at that. And this is an indication that laughing at people is among the sins and major sins. And from Abdullah ibn Zam'ah that he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﭬ while he was preaching, and he admonished them regarding their laughing at flatulence, so he said: "Why does one of you laugh at what he does?" And he ﭬ said: "Indeed, those who mock people, a gate of Paradise is opened for one of them, and it is said: Come, come, so he comes with his distress and grief, and when he reaches it, it is closed upon him, then another gate is opened for him, and it is said: Come, come, so he comes with his distress and grief, and when he reaches it, it is closed upon him, and it continues like that until indeed a man has a gate opened for him, and it is said to him: Come, come, but he does not come to it." And Mu'adh ibn Jabal said: The Prophet ﭬ said: "Whoever reproaches his brother for a sin from which he has repented, not
49:11.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

49:11.arabic: وفي قوله عز وجل -﴿ وهم في غفلة معرضون ﴾ {} وفي قوله ﴿ فأعرض عمن تولى عن ذكرنا ولم يرد إلا الحياة الدنيا ﴾ {} وفي قوله تعالى ﴿ ومن لم يتب فأولئك هم الظالمون ﴾ {} إلى غير ذلك من الآيات وكان داخلا في معنى قوله عز وجل ﴿ ومنهم أميون لا يعلمون الكتاب إلا أمانيّ ﴾ {}
49:11.english: And in His saying, the Mighty and Majestic - 'And they are in heedlessness (ghaflah) turning away (mu'ridun)' {} and in His saying 'So turn away from him who turns away from Our Remembrance (Dhikr) and desires not except the worldly life' {} and in His saying, the Exalted 'And whoever does not repent, then those are the wrongdoers (al-zalimun)' {} to other than that of the verses, and he was included in the meaning of His saying, the Mighty and Majestic 'And among them are unlettered ones who do not know the Book except [mere] wishes' {}
49:11.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

49:11.arabic: وكل هذا يرجع إلى استحقار الغير والضحك عليها استهانة به واستصغاراً له. وعليه قوله تعالى "يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا يَسْخَرْ قَوْمٌ مِنْ قَوْمٍ عَسَىٰ أَنْ يَكُونُوا خَيْرًا مِنْهُمْ وَلَا نِسَاءٌ مِنْ نِسَاءٍ عَسَىٰ أَنْ يَكُنَّ خَيْرًا مِنْهُنَّ ۖ وَلَا تَلْمِزُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ وَلَا تَنَابَزُوا بِالْأَلْقَابِ ۖ بِئْسَ الِاسْمُ الْفُسُوقُ بَعْدَ الْإِيمَانِ ۚ وَمَنْ لَمْ يَتُبْ فَأُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ" "عسى أن يكونوا خيراً منهم" أي لا تستحقره استصغاراً فلعله خير منك.
49:11.english: And all of this returns to belittling others and laughing at them in contempt and looking down upon them. And upon this is the saying of the Exalted: "O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people; perhaps they may be better than them; nor let women ridicule [other] women; perhaps they may be better than them. And do not insult one another and do not call each other by [offensive] nicknames. Wretched is the name of disobedience after [one's] faith. And whoever does not repent - then it is those who are the wrongdoers." "Perhaps they may be better than them" meaning do not belittle him by looking down upon him, for perhaps he is better than you.
49:11.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

49:11.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
49:11.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Whatever is in the Quran of 'O you who have believed' is in the Torah 'O you poor ones (al-Masakin)'.
49:11.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

49:12.arabic: اعلم أن سوء الظن حرام مثل سوء القول، فكما يحرم عليك أن تحدث غيرك بلسانك بمساوئ الغير فليس لك أن تحدث نفسك تسيء الظن بأخيك، ولست أعني به إلا عقد القلب وحكه على غيره بالسوء. فأما الخواطر وحديث النفس فهو معفو عنه بل الشك أيضاً معفو عنه، ولكن المنهي عنه أن يظن، والظن عبارة عما تركن إليه النفس ويميل إليه القلب. فقد قال الله تعالى "يا أيها الذين آمنوا اجتنبوا كثيراً من الظن إن بعض الظن إثم" وسبب تحريمه أن أسرار القلوب لا يعلمها إلا علام الغيوب، فليس لك أن تعتقد في غيرك سوءاً إلا إذا انكشف لك بعيان لا
49:12.english: Know that bad suspicion (sūʾ al-ẓann) is forbidden like bad speech, so just as it is forbidden for you to inform others with your tongue about the faults of others, it is not for you to inform yourself by suspecting evil of your brother, and I do not mean by this except the binding of the heart (ʿaqd al-qalb) and its scratching against others with evil. As for thoughts (khawāṭir) and the speech of the soul (nafs), it is forgiven, even doubt (shakk) is also forgiven, but what is prohibited is to suspect (yaẓunn), and suspicion (al-ẓann) is an expression for what the soul (nafs) leans toward and the heart (qalb) inclines to. For Allah the Exalted has said: "O you who have believed, avoid much [negative] assumption. Indeed, some assumption is sin." And the reason for its prohibition is that the secrets of the hearts (asrār al-qulūb) are not known except by the Knower of the unseen (ʿallām al-ghuyūb), so it is not for you to believe evil about another except if it is revealed to you with an eyewitness account that does not accept interpretation, then at that point you cannot but believe what you have known and witnessed, and what you have not witnessed with your eye nor heard with your ear, then it occurs in your heart, then it is only Satan who casts it to you, so you should deny him for he is the most wicked of the wicked, and Allah the Exalted has said: "O you who have believed, if there comes to you a wicked person with information, investigate, lest you harm a people out of ignorance." So it is not permissible to believe Iblīs, and if there is then an imagination that indicates corruption and its opposite is possible, it is not permissible to believe it, because the wicked one may appear to be truthful in his good but it is not permissible for you to believe him, even if someone smells him and finds from him the smell of wine, it is not permissible to punish him, for it is said it is possible that he gargled with wine and spat it out and did not drink it, or it was forced upon him, so all of that is inevitably a probable indication, so it is not permissible to believe it with the heart and to have bad suspicion (isāʾat al-ẓann) of a Muslim with it, and he ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah has forbidden from the Muslim his blood, his wealth, and that he be suspected of bad suspicion (ẓann al-sūʾ)." So bad suspicion is not permitted except by what permits wealth, which is its actual witnessing or just testimony, so if it is not like that and the whisper of bad suspicion occurs to you, then you should repel it from yourself and affirm upon it that...
49:12.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

49:12.arabic: وإن سأل من حيث لا يدرى هو ففيه إساءة ظن وهتك ستر وفيه تجسس وفيه تشبث بالغيبة وإن لم يكن ذلك صريحا وكل ذلك منهي عنه في آية عليه السلام واحدة قال الله تعالى اجتنبوا كثيرا من الظن إن بعض الظن إثم ولا تجسسوا ولا يغتب بعضكم بعضا وكم زاهد جاهل يوحش القلوب في التفتيش ويتكلم الكلام الخشن المؤذى وإنما يحسن الشزمطان ذلك عنده طلبا للشهرة بأكل الحلال ولو كان باعثه محض الدين لكان خوفه على قلب مسلم أن يتأذى أشد من خوفه على بطنه أن يدخله ما لا يدرى وهو غير مؤاخذ بما لا يدري إذ لم يكن ثم علامة توجب الاجتناب فلي
49:12.english: And if he asks from a place where he does not know, then in that is bad assumption (ظن) and tearing of the veil, and in that is spying (تجسس), and in that is clinging to backbiting (غيبة) even if that is not explicit. And all of that is prohibited in one verse of the Prophet (peace be upon him). Allah the Exalted said: 'O you who have believed, avoid much [negative] assumption (ظن). Indeed, some assumption (ظن) is sin. And do not spy (تجسس) or backbite (يغتب) each other. Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his brother when dead? You would detest it. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Accepting of repentance and Merciful.' And how many ignorant ascetics (زاهد) who alienate the Hearts (قلوب) in investigation and speak harsh, harmful speech. And indeed, the Devil (الشيطان) beautifies that for him seeking fame by eating the lawful. And if his motivation was purely religion, his fear for the Heart (قلب) of a Muslim to be harmed would be stronger than his fear for his stomach to enter what he does not know. And he is not held accountable for what he does not know since there was no sign necessitating avoidance. So let it be known that the path of scrupulousness (ورع) is abstention without spying (تجسس). And if there is no alternative to eating, then the scrupulousness (ورع) is eating and good assumption (ظن). This is what is customary from the Companions (الصحابة) (may Allah be pleased with them). And whoever increases beyond them in scrupulousness (ورع) is misguided, innovating, and not following. No one will reach the measure of one of them nor half of it even if he spent all that is in the earth. How could it be otherwise when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) ate the food of Burairah? It was said: 'It is charity.' He said: 'It is charity for her and a gift for us.' The hadith of him eating the food of Burairah: it was said it is charity, he said it is charity for her and a gift for us, agreed upon from the narration of Anas. And he did not ask about the one who gave charity upon her, so it was unknown to him, and he did not abstain.
49:12.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

49:12.arabic: وإن بعض الظن إثم وهذا المسلم يستحق بإسلامه عليك أن لا تسيء الظن به فإن أسأت الظن به في عينه لأنك رأيت فسادا من غيره فقد جنيت عليه وأثمت به في الحال نقدا من غير شك ولو أخذت المال لكان كونه حراما مشكوكا فيه ويدل عليه أنا نعلم أن الصحابة رضي الله عنهم في غزواتهم وأسفارهم كانوا ينزلون في القرى ولا يردون القرى ويدخلون البلاد ولا يحترزون من الأسواق وكان الحرام أيضا موجودا في زمانهم وما نقل عنهم سؤال إلا عن ريبة إذ كان صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يسأل عن كل ما يحمل إليه بل سأل في أول قدومه إلى المدينة عما يح
49:12.english: And indeed some suspicion (Zann) is sin, and this Muslim deserves by his Islam that you do not suspect him. If you suspect him specifically because you saw corruption from others, then you have wronged him and sinned against him immediately without doubt. And if you took the wealth, its being forbidden would be doubtful. Evidence for this is that we know the Companions (Sahaba), may Allah be pleased with them, in their military expeditions and travels would stay in villages and not reject villages, and enter lands and not avoid markets, while forbidden things also existed in their time. Nothing is reported from them asking except about suspicion (Riba), for the Prophet, peace be upon him, did not ask about everything brought to him, but asked upon his first arrival in Medina about what was brought to him: is it charity (Sadaqa) or a gift? The narration of his asking upon his first arrival in Medina about what was brought to him: charity (Sadaqa) or a gift? Reported by Ahmad and Al-Hakim who said its chain is authentic, from the narration of Salman that when the Prophet, peace be upon him, arrived in Medina, Salman brought him food and he asked about it: charity (Sadaqa) or a gift? The narration preceded in the previous chapter from the narration of Abu Hurairah because the context indicates—the entry of the emigrants into Medina while they were poor—so suspicion (Zann) prevailed that what was brought to them was by way of charity (Sadaqa). Then the giver's Islam and his hand do not indicate it is not charity (Sadaqa). And he was invited to feasts and would accept without asking: charity (Sadaqa) or not? Narration.
49:12.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

49:12.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
49:12.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Whatever is in the Quran of 'O you who have believed' is in the Torah 'O you poor ones'.
49:12.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

49:12.arabic: ومكايد الشيطان فيما يتعلق بالعقائد والمذاهب لا تحصر وإنما أردنا بما أوردناه المثال ومن أبوابه سوء الظن بالمسلمين قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا اجتنبوا كثيرا من الظن إن بعض الظن إثم فمن يحكم بشر على غيره بالظن بعثه الشيطان على أن يطول فيه اللسان بالغيبة فيهلك أو يقصر في القيام بحقوقه أو يتوانى في إكرامه وينظر إليه بعين الاحتقار ويرى نفسه خيرا منه وكل ذلك من المهلكات ولأجل ذلك منع الشرع من التعرض للتهم فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم اتقوا مواضع التهم[63] حتى احترز هو صلى الله عليه وسلم من ذلك روي عن
49:12.english: And the wiles of Satan concerning beliefs and doctrines are innumerable, and we only intended with what we presented as an example, and among its doors is bad suspicion (sūʾ al-ẓann) toward Muslims. Allah the Exalted said: 'O you who have believed, avoid much [negative] assumption (al-ẓann). Indeed, some assumption (al-ẓann) is sin.' So whoever judges evil upon another based on assumption (al-ẓann), Satan incites him to lengthen the tongue in backbiting (al-ghībah) and thus perish, or to fall short in fulfilling his rights, or to be negligent in honoring him, and to look at him with the eye of contempt and see himself as better than him, and all of that is among the destructive things. For that reason, the Sacred Law (al-sharʿ) prohibited exposure to suspicions (al-tuhum), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Avoid places of suspicion (al-tuhum).' [63] Until he (peace be upon him) himself was cautious of that. It is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Ḥusayn that Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab informed him that the Prophet (peace be upon him) was in seclusion (iʿtikāf) in the mosque. She said: 'So I came to him and conversed with him, and when evening came, I departed, and he stood walking with me. Then two men from the Helpers (al-Anṣār) passed by him, and they greeted, then departed. So he called them and said: "She is Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, we do not think (naẓunn) of you except good." He said: "Indeed, Satan flows in the son of Adam like the flow of blood in the body, and I feared that he might enter upon you."' [64] So look how he (peace be upon him) showed compassion for their religion (dīn) and guarded them, and how he showed compassion for his community (ummah) and taught them the way of caution from suspicion (al-tuhmah), so that the pious scholar (al-ʿālim al-warīʿ) known for religion (al-dīn) in his states does not become negligent in his affairs, saying: 'One like me is not thought (yuẓann) of except good,' out of admiration for his own soul (nafs). For the most pious of people (awraʿ al-nās), the most God-fearing (atqāhum), and the most knowledgeable (aʿlamuhum) – not all people look at him with one eye, but rather some with the eye of contentment (bi-ʿayn al-riḍā) and others with the eye of displeasure (bi-ʿayn al-sakhaṭ).
49:12.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

49:13.arabic: وإنما التقوى عبارة عن كف بمقتضى الخوف كما سبق ولذلك قال تعالى: ﴿ إن أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم ﴾ {} ولذلك أوصى الله تعالى الأولين والآخرين بالتقوى فقال تعالى: ﴿ ولقد وصينا الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم وإياكم أن اتقوا الله ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل: ﴿ وخافون إن كنتم مؤمنين ﴾ {} فأمر بالخوف وأوجبه وشرطه في الإيمان فلذلك لا يتصور أن ينفك مؤمن عن خوف وإن ضعف ويكون ضعف خوفه بحسب ضعف معرفته وإيمانه وقال رسول الله ﭬ في فضيلة التقوى: (إذا جمع الله الأولين والآخرين لميقات يوم معلوم فإذا هم بصوت يسمع أقصاهم كما يسمع أد
49:13.english: And indeed, God-Consciousness (Taqwa) is an expression of restraint due to fear as previously mentioned, and therefore Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, the most noble of you with Allah is the most God-Conscious (Atqakum) among you.' And therefore, Allah the Exalted enjoined the former and the latter with God-Consciousness (Taqwa), so He said: 'And We have enjoined upon those who were given the Scripture before you and upon you that you fear Allah.' And He the Mighty and Majestic said: 'And fear Me, if you should be believers.' So He commanded fear and made it obligatory and stipulated it in faith, therefore it is inconceivable that a believer be free from fear even if weak, and the weakness of his fear is according to the weakness of his knowledge and faith. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said regarding the virtue of God-Consciousness (Taqwa): 'When Allah gathers the former and the latter for an appointed day, then they hear a voice that the farthest among them hears just as the nearest hears, and He says: O people, I have indeed listened to you since I created you until this day of yours, so listen to Me today. Indeed, it is your deeds that are returned to you. O people, I have indeed made lineage and you have made lineage, so you have lowered My lineage and raised your lineage. I said: "Indeed, the most noble of you with Allah is the most God-Conscious (Atqakum) among you." And you refused except to say: So-and-so son of so-and-so and so-and-so is richer than so-and-so. So today I lower your lineage and raise My lineage. Where are the God-Conscious (Muttaqun)?' Then a banner is raised for the people, and the people follow their banner to their dwellings, and they enter Paradise without reckoning.'
49:13.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

49:13.arabic: ولذلك قال تعالى "يا أيها الناس إنا خلقناكم من ذكر وأنثى" أي لا تفاوت في أنسابكم لاجتماعكم في أصل واحد، ثم ذكر فائدة النسب فقال "وجعلناكم شعوباً وقبائل لتعارفوا" ثم بين أن الشرف بالتقوى لا بالنسب فقال "إن أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم" ولما قيل لرسول الله ﭬ من أكرم الناس؟ من أكيس الناس؟ لم يقل: من ينتمي إلى نسبي ولكن قال "أكرمهم أكثرهم للموت ذكراً وأشدهم له استعداداً"[92] وإنما نزلت هذه الآية حين أذن بلال يوم الفتح على الكعبة: فقال الحرث بن هشام وسهيل بن عمرو وخالد بن أسيد: هذا العبد الأسود يؤذن على الك
49:13.english: Therefore, Allah the Exalted said: "O people, indeed We created you from a male and a female" meaning there is no disparity in your lineages due to your gathering in a single origin. Then He mentioned the benefit of lineage, saying: "and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another." Then He clarified that nobility is through God-consciousness (Taqwa) not through lineage, saying: "Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you." And when it was said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him): 'Who is the noblest of people? Who is the wisest of people?' He did not say: 'He who belongs to my lineage,' but rather said: "The noblest among them is the one who most remembers death and is most prepared for it." [92] And indeed, this verse was revealed when Bilal gave the call to prayer (Adhan) on the Kaaba on the Day of Conquest: Al-Harith ibn Hisham, Suhayl ibn Amr, and Khalid ibn Asid said: 'This black slave gives the call to prayer on the Kaaba?' So Allah the Exalted said: "Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you." And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, Allah has removed from you the boastful pride of the Age of Ignorance (Jahiliyyah) - meaning its major aspect - all of you are children of Adam, and Adam was from dust." [93] And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "O assembly of Quraysh, do not come to the people with deeds on the Day of Resurrection while you bring the worldly life carrying it on your necks, saying: 'O Muhammad, O Muhammad,' so I will say like this - meaning I will turn away from you [94] - thus clarifying that if they incline towards the worldly life, their lineage of Quraysh will not benefit them."
49:13.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

49:13.arabic: الرابع العجب بالنسب الشريف كعجب الهاشمية، حتى يظن بعضهم أنه ينجو بشرف نسبه ونجاة آبائه وأنه مغفور له، ويتخيل بعضهم أن جميع الخلق له موال وعبيد، وعلاجه أن يعلم أنه مهما خالف آباءه في أفعالهم وأخلاقهم وظن أنه ملحق بهم فقد جهل، وإن اقتدى بآبائه فما كان من أخلاقهم العجب بل الخوف والازدراء على النفس واستعظام الخلق ومذمة النفس، ولقد شرفوا بالطاعة والعلم والخصال الحميدة لا بالنسب، فليتشرف بما شرفوا به، وقد ساواهم في النسب وشاركهم في القبائل من لم يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر، وكانوا عند الله شراً من الكلاب
49:13.english: The fourth [type of pride] is pride in noble lineage, like the pride of the Hashimites, to the point that some think they will be saved by the nobility of their lineage and the salvation of their ancestors, and that they are forgiven, and some imagine that all creation are their masters and slaves. Its cure is that he should know that however much he differs from his ancestors in their actions and character traits and thinks he is attached to them, he has been ignorant. And if he follows his ancestors, then what was from their character traits was not pride but rather fear and contempt for the Soul (Nafs) and magnifying the creation and blaming the Soul (Nafs). And indeed they were ennobled by obedience and knowledge and praiseworthy qualities, not by lineage, so let him ennoble himself with what they ennobled themselves. And those who did not believe in Allah and the Last Day have equaled them in lineage and shared with them in the tribes, and they were with Allah worse than dogs and more vile than pigs. And for that reason, Allah the Exalted said: 'O people, indeed We created you from a male and a female' meaning there is no disparity in your lineages due to your gathering in a single origin. Then He mentioned the benefit of lineage, saying: 'and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another.' Then He clarified that nobility is through God-consciousness (Taqwa) not through lineage, saying: 'Indeed, the most noble of you with Allah is the most God-conscious (Atqakum) of you.' And when it was said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him): 'Who are the most noble of people? Who are the most prudent of people?' He did not say: 'He who belongs to my lineage,' but rather said: 'The most noble of them are those who have the most Remembrance (Dhikr) of death and are the most prepared for it.'[92] And indeed this verse was revealed when Bilal gave the call to prayer on the day of the Conquest on the Kaaba: So Al-Harith ibn Hisham, Suhayl ibn Amr, and Khalid ibn Asid said: 'This black slave gives the call to prayer on the Kaaba?' So Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, the most noble of you with Allah is the most God-conscious (Atqakum) of you.' And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah has removed from you the boastfulness of ignorance - meaning its major part - all of you are children of Adam, and Adam was from dust.'[93] And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'O assembly of Quraysh, do not come to the people with deeds on the Day of Resurrection and you come with the world carrying it on your necks saying: O Muhammad, O Muhammad, so I will say like this - meaning I will turn away from you[94] - thus clarifying that if they incline to the world, their lineage of Quraysh will not benefit them. And when His saying the Exalted descended: 'And warn, [O Muhammad], your closest kindred' he called them clan after clan, until he said: 'O Fatimah daughter of Muhammad, O Safiyyah daughter of Abdul-Muttalib, aunt of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), work for yourselves, for I cannot avail you anything from Allah.'
49:13.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

49:13.arabic: وسئل ابن عباس: ما الكرم؟ فقال: هو ما بين الله في كتابه العزيز "إن أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم" قيل فما الحسب؟ قال: أحسنكم خلقاً أفضلكم حسباً.
49:13.english: And Ibn Abbas was asked: 'What is nobility (al-Karam)?' He said: 'It is what Allah has clarified in His Mighty Book: "Indeed, the most noble of you with Allah is the most righteous (Atqakum) among you."' It was said: 'Then what is lineage (al-Hasab)?' He said: 'The best of you in character (Khuluq) is the most excellent of you in lineage.'
49:13.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

49:13.arabic: الرابعة: أني نظرت إلى هذا الخلق فرأيت كل واحد منهم يرجع إلى المال وإلى الحسب والشرف والنسب فنظرت فيها فإذا هي لا شيء ثم نظرت إلى قول الله تعالى (إن أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم( (الحجرات: 13) فعملت في التقوى حتى أكون عند الله كريما.
49:13.english: The fourth: I looked at this creation and saw that each one of them refers back to wealth, lineage, honor, and ancestry. I looked into these and found them to be nothing. Then I looked at the saying of Allah the Exalted: 'Indeed, the most noble of you with Allah is the most God-fearing (Atqa)' (Al-Hujurat: 13). So I worked in God-fearingness (Taqwa) until I would be noble with Allah.
49:13.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

49:14.arabic: وأما الاختلاف فهو أن يجعل الإيمان عبارة عن التصديق بالقلب فقط وهو موافق للغة والإسلام عبارة عن التسليم ظاهرا وهو أيضا موافق للغة فإن التسليم ببعض محال التسليم ينطلق عليه اسم التسليم فليس من شرط حصول الاسم عموم المعنى لكل محل يمكن أن يوجد المعنى فيه فإن من لمس غيره ببعض بدنه يسمى لامسا وإن لم يستغرق جميع بدنه فإطلاق اسم الإسلام على التسليم الظاهر عند عدم تسليم الباطن مطابق للسان وعلى هذا الوجه جرى قوله تعالى: ﴿ قالت الأعراب آمنا قل لم تؤمنوا ولكن قولوا أسلمنا ﴾ {} وقوله ﭬ في حديث سعد (أو مسلم) لأ
49:14.english: As for the difference, it is that faith (Iman) is made to mean affirmation (Tasdiq) with the heart (Qalb) only, which conforms to the language, and Islam is made to mean outward submission (Taslim), which also conforms to the language. For submission in some places of submission is applied to it the name submission, so it is not a condition for obtaining the name that the meaning be general to every place where the meaning can exist. For whoever touches another with some part of his body is called a toucher even if it does not encompass all of his body. So applying the name Islam to outward submission when there is no submission of the inner self (Batin) is consistent with the tongue (Lisan). And upon this aspect proceeds His saying, the Exalted: 'The Bedouins said, "We have believed." Say, "You have not [yet] believed; but say [instead], 'We have submitted,'"' and His saying, peace be upon him, in the hadith of Sa'd ('or Muslim') because he preferred one over the other, and he intends by the difference the superiority of the two named things.
49:14.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

49:14.arabic: وأما الاختلاف فقوله تعالى: ﴿ قالت الأعراب آمنا قل لم تؤمنوا ولكن قولوا أسلمنا ﴾ {} ومعناه استسلمنا في الظاهر فأراد بالإيمان ههنا التصديق بالقلب فقط وبالإسلام الاستسلام ظاهرا باللسان والجوارح، وفي حديث جبرائيل عليه السلام لما سأله عن الإيمان فقال: (أن تؤمن بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله واليوم الآخر وبالبعث بعد الموت وبالحساب وبالقدر خيره وشره فقال فما الإسلام فأجاب بذكر الخصال الخمس[47]) فعبر بالإسلام عن تسليم الظاهر بالقول والعمل وفي الحديث عن سعد أنه ﭬ (أعطى رجلا عطاء ولم يعط الآخر فقال له سعد: يا
49:14.english: As for the difference, it is in His saying, the Exalted: 'The Bedouins said, "We have believed." Say, "You have not believed; but say [instead], 'We have submitted,' for faith (Iman) has not yet entered your hearts.' And if you obey Allah and His Messenger, He will not deprive you from your deeds of anything. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.' (Quran 49:14) And its meaning is: we have submitted outwardly. So He intended by faith (Iman) here only the affirmation (Tasdiq) with the heart (Qalb), and by Islam the outward submission (Istislam) with the tongue (Lisan) and limbs (Jawarih). And in the hadith of Gabriel, peace be upon him, when he asked him about faith (Iman), he said: 'That you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and resurrection after death, and the accounting, and the decree (Qadr), its good and its evil.' Then he said: 'What is Islam?' So he answered by mentioning the five pillars. So he expressed by Islam the outward submission (Taslim) with speech and action. And in the hadith about Sa'd that he, peace be upon him, gave a man a gift and did not give another. So Sa'd said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, you left so-and-so, you did not give him, and he is a believer (Mu'min).' So he, peace be upon him, said: 'Or a Muslim (Muslim).' So he repeated it to him, and the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, repeated. And as for the overlap, it is what was also narrated that he was asked: 'Which deeds are best?' So he, peace be upon him, said: 'Islam.' So he said: 'Which Islam is best?' So he, peace be upon him, said: 'Faith (Iman).' And this is evidence of the difference and of the overlap, and it is the most appropriate of the usages in language because faith (Iman) is an action from the actions and it is the best of them, and Islam is submission (Taslim), either with the heart (Qalb), or with the tongue (Lisan), or with the limbs (Jawarih), and the best of it is that with the heart (Qalb), which is the affirmation (Tasdiq) that is called faith (Iman). And the usage of them on the way of difference and on the way of overlap and on the way of synonymity is all not outside the path of metaphorical usage in language. As for the difference, it is
49:14.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

49:15.arabic: الصدق السادس وهو أعلى الدرجات وأعزها الصدق في مقامات الدين كالصدق في الخوف والرجاء والتعظيم والزهد والرضا والتوكل والحب وسائر هذه الأمور فإن هذه الأمور لها مباد ينطلق الاسم بظهورها ثم لها غايات وحقائق والصادق المحقق من نال حقيقتها وإذا غلب الشيء وتمت حقيقته سمى صاحبه صادقا فيه كما يقال فلان صدق القتال ويقال هذا هو الخوف الصادق وهذه هي الشهوة الصادقة وقال الله تعالى إنما المؤمنون الذين آمنوا بالله ورسوله ثم لم يرتابوا إلى قوله أولئك هم الصادقون وقال تعالى (ولكن البر من آمن بالله واليوم الآخر ...
49:15.english: The sixth truthfulness (Sidq), which is the highest of the degrees and the most precious, is truthfulness in the stations (Maqamat) of the religion, such as truthfulness in fear (Khawf), hope (Raja'), veneration (Ta'zim), asceticism (Zuhd), contentment (Rida), reliance (Tawakkul), love (Hubb), and the rest of these matters. For these matters have beginnings from which the name is launched by their appearance, then they have ends and realities (Haqa'iq). And the truthful (Sadiq) verifier (Muhaqqiq) is the one who attains their reality. And when a thing prevails and its reality is complete, its possessor is called truthful in it, as it is said: 'So-and-so was truthful in fighting (Qital),' and it is said: 'This is the truthful fear (Khawf), and this is the truthful desire (Shahwah).' And Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, the believers are those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and then do not doubt...' to His saying: '...those are the truthful ones (Sadiqun).' And He the Exalted said: (But righteousness is [in] one who believes in Allah, the Last Day... to His saying... those are the ones who have been truthful). And Abu Dharr was asked about faith (Iman), so he recited this verse. It was said to him: 'We asked you about faith.' He said: 'I asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, about faith, and he recited this verse.' And let us strike an example for fear: There is no servant who believes in Allah and the Last Day except that he fears Allah with a fear upon which the name is launched, but it is a fear that is not truthful, meaning it does not reach the degree of reality. Do you not see him when he fears a ruler or a highway robber on his journey, how his color pales and his limbs tremble, and his life becomes bitter, and his eating and sleeping become difficult, and his thought becomes divided until his family and children do not benefit from him, and he may be agitated away from his homeland, exchanging familiarity for loneliness and ease for fatigue, hardship, and exposure to dangers, all of that out of fear of encountering the dreaded thing? Then, he fears the Fire, yet nothing of that appears upon him when a sin flows upon him. And for that reason, he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'I have not seen anything like the Fire whose fleer sleeps, nor like Paradise whose seeker sleeps.' The hadith 'I have not seen anything like the Fire whose fleer sleeps' has preceded. So, verification (Tahqiq) in these matters is very rare, and there is no end to these stations until their perfection is attained, but every servant has a share according to his state, either weak or strong.
