And the accursed one, created from fire, was commanded to settle from his movement by prostrating to what Allah created from clay, but he refused, became arrogant, and rebelled, expressing the reason for his rebellion by saying: 'You created me from fire and created him from clay' (Quran 55:14). Therefore, since the accursed one did not prostrate to our father Adam, prayers and peace of Allah be upon him, one should not hope for his prostration to his children. And whenever he refrains from the whisperings (Waswas), aggression, flying, and wandering of the heart (al-Qalb), he has shown his submission (Inqiyad) and compliance (Idh'an), and his submission through compliance is a prostration from him; it is the spirit (Ruh) of prostration. And placing the forehead on the ground is its form (Qalb) and sign indicating it by convention.
55:14.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

55:26.arabic: ثم إذا حصل الأنس بذكر الله سبحانه انقطع عن غير ذكر الله وما سوى الله عز وجل هو الذي يفارقه عند الموت فلا يبقى معه في القبر أهل ولا مال ولا ولد ولا ولاية ولا يبقى إلا ذكر الله عز وجل فإن كان قد أنس به تمتع به وتلذذ بانقطاع العوائق الصارفة عنه إذ ضرورات الحاجات في الحياة الدنيا تصد عن ذكر الله عز وجل ولا يبقى بعد الموت عائق فكأنه خلى بينه وبين محبوبه فعظمت غبطته وتخلص من السجن الذي كان ممنوعا فيه عما به أنسه ولذلك قال ﭬ: (إن روح القدس نفث في روعي أحبب من أحببت فإنك مفارقه[57]) أراد به كل ما يتعلق
55:26.english: Then when the intimacy (Anas) with the remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is attained, he becomes cut off from other than the remembrance of Allah, and what is besides Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is what he parts with at death, so there does not remain with him in the grave family, nor wealth, nor child, nor authority, and there does not remain except the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So if he had become intimate with it, he enjoys it and delights in the removal of the obstacles that divert from it, since the necessities of needs in the worldly life (Al-Hayat Al-Dunya) divert from the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and after death there does not remain an obstacle, so it is as if he is left alone between him and his beloved, thus his bliss becomes great and he is freed from the prison in which he was prevented from that with which he had intimacy. And for that reason, he (the Prophet) said: 'Indeed, the Holy Spirit (Ruh Al-Qudus) inspired in my heart: Love whom you love, for you will part with him' [57]. He intended by that everything that pertains to the worldly life (Al-Dunya), for that perishes in his regard by death, so 'Everything upon it will perish (Kullu man 'alayha fanin), and there will remain the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor' (Quran 55:26-27). And the worldly life (Al-Dunya) only perishes by death in his regard until it perishes in itself when the term of the Book reaches its end. And this intimacy (Anas) is what the servant (Al-'Abd) delights in after his death until he descends in the proximity of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and ascends from the remembrance (Dhikr) to the meeting (Al-Liqa'), and that is after what is in the graves is scattered and what is in the chests is realized. And one should not deny the permanence of the remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, with him after death by saying that he is annihilated, so how does the remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, remain with him? For he has not been annihilated with an annihilation that prevents remembrance (Dhikr), but rather an annihilation from the worldly life (Al-Dunya) and the world of dominion and witness (Alam Al-Mulk wa Al-Shahadah), not from the world of sovereignty (Alam Al-Malakut).
55:26.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith

55:27.arabic: واذا كان كل من عليها فان فلا يبقى الا وجه ربك ذو الجلال والاكرام. الفريق الثاني ليس بهم عمى ولكن بهم عور لانهم يبصرون باحدى العينين وجود الموجود الحق فلا ينكرونه والعين الأخرى ان تم عماها لم يبصر بها فناء غير الموجود الحق فاثبت موجودا اخر مع الله تعالى وهذا مشرك تحقيقا كما ان الذى قبله جاحد تحقيقا فان جاوز حد العمى الى العمش ادرك تفاوتا بين الموجودين فأثبت عبدا وربا فبهذا القدر من إثبات التفاوت والنقص من الموجود الاخر دخل في حد التوحيد ثم إن كحل بصره بما يزيد في أنواره فيقل عمشه وبقدر ما يزيد في
55:27.english: And when everything upon it perishes, nothing remains except the Face (Wajh) of your Lord, Possessor of Majesty and Honor. The second group does not have blindness but they have one-eyed vision because they see with one eye the existence of the True Existent (al-Mawjūd al-Ḥaqq) so they do not deny it, and the other eye, if its blindness is complete, does not see with it the annihilation (Fanā') of other than the True Existent, so they affirm another existent alongside Allah the Exalted, and this is truly a polytheist (Mushrik) just as the one before it is truly a denier (Jāḥid). If it surpasses the limit of blindness to dim-sightedness, it perceives a disparity between the existents, so it affirms a servant (ʿAbd) and a lord (Rabb), so with this measure of affirming disparity and deficiency from the other existent, it enters the limit of Monotheism (Tawḥīd). Then if it applies kohl to its sight with what increases its lights, its dim-sightedness decreases, and according to what increases in its sight, the deficiency of what it affirmed besides Allah the Exalted becomes apparent to it. If it remains in its spiritual journey (Sulūk) thus, then the deficiency continuously leads it to effacement (Maḥw), so it becomes effaced from seeing what is besides Allah, so it sees nothing except Allah, so that it may have reached the perfection of Monotheism. And where it perceived deficiency in the existence of what is besides Allah the Exalted, it entered the beginnings of Monotheism, and between them are degrees that cannot be enumerated. Thus, the degrees of the monotheists (Muwaḥḥidīn) vary. And the revealed Books of Allah upon the tongues of His messengers are the kohl with which the lights of insights are attained, and the prophets are the kohl-appliers, and they came calling to pure Monotheism, and its translation is the statement 'There is no god but Allah,' and its meaning is that nothing is seen except the One True, and those who reach the perfection of Monotheism are the few and the denier.
55:27.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

55:29.arabic: فلو لم يكن بين يدي الموتي إلا هول تلك النفخة لكان ذلك جديرا بأن يتقى فإنها نفخة وصيحة يصعق بها من فى السموات والأرض يعنى يموتون بها إلا من شاء الله وهو بعض الملائكة ولذلك قال رسول الله ﭬ: (كيف أنعم وصاحب الصور قد التقم القرن وحنى الجبهة وأصغى بالأذن متى يؤمر فينفخ[144]) قال مقاتل: الصور هو القرن وذلك أن إسرافيل عليه السلام واضع فاه على القرن كهيئة البوق ودائرة رأس القرن كعرض السموات والأرض وهو شاخص بصره نحو العرش ينتظر متى يؤمر فينفخ النفخة الأولى فإذا نفخ صعق من فى السموات والأرض أى مات كل حيوا
55:29.english: If there were nothing before the dead except the terror of that blowing (of the Trumpet), it would be worthy of being feared, for it is a blowing and a cry by which those in the heavens and the earth are struck unconscious, meaning they die by it except whom Allah wills, and that is some of the angels. And therefore the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'How can I enjoy comfort when the possessor of the Trumpet has taken the horn in his mouth, lowered his forehead, and listened with his ear, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow?' [144] Maqatil said: The Trumpet (As-Sur) is the horn, and that is because Israfil (upon him be peace) has placed his mouth on the horn like the form of a trumpet, and the circumference of the head of the horn is like the expanse of the heavens and the earth, and he is staring with his gaze toward the Throne, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow the first blowing. And when he blows, those in the heavens and the earth are struck unconscious, meaning every living creature dies from the intensity of the terror except whom Allah wills, and that is Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil, and the Angel of Death. Then the Angel of Death is commanded to take the soul (Ruh) of Jibril, then the soul (Ruh) of Mika'il, then the soul (Ruh) of Israfil, then the Angel of Death is commanded and he dies. Then the creation remains after the first blowing in the Barzakh (the intermediate state) for forty years. Then Allah the Exalted revives Israfil and commands him to blow the second blowing, and that is His saying the Exalted: 'Then it will be blown into it another time, and behold, they are standing, looking on' [Quran 39:68] on their feet, looking at the Resurrection. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'When I was sent, I was sent to the possessor of the Trumpet, and he inclined it to his mouth, and advanced one foot and delayed another, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow. Indeed, fear the blowing!' [145] So reflect on the creation and their humiliation, their brokenness, and their submission at the resurrection out of fear of this unconsciousness and waiting for...
55:29.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

55:31.arabic: وقوله تعالى: ﴿ سنفرغ لكم أيه الثقلان ﴾ {}
55:31.english: And His saying, the Exalted: "We will attend to you, O you two weighty ones" (Quran 55:31) {}
55:31.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Fear and Hope'

55:39.arabic: يوم تبدل الأرض غير الأرض والسموات وبرزوا لله الواحد القهار، يوم تنسف فيه الجبال نسفا فتترك قاعا صفصفا لا ترى فيها عوجا ولا أمتا، يوم ترى الجبال تحسبها جامدة وهى تمر مر السحاب، يوم تنشق فيه السماء فتكون وردة كالدهان، فيومئذ لا يسئل عن ذنبه إنس ولا جان، يوم يمنع فيه العاصى من الكلام ولا يسئل فيه عن الأجرام بل يؤخذ بالنواصى والأقدام، يوم تجد كل نفس ما عملت من خير محضرا وما عملت من سوء تود لو أن بينها وبينه أمدا بعيدا، يوم تعلم فيه كل نفس ما أحضرت وتشهد ما قدمت وأخرت يوم تخرس فيه الألسن وتنطق الجوار
55:39.english: The day the Earth (Al-Ard) will be changed to a different Earth and the heavens, and they will appear before Allah (Al-Wahid Al-Qahhar), the One, the Subduer. The day the mountains will be blown away, leaving a level plain where you see no crookedness nor unevenness. The day you see the mountains, thinking them firm, while they pass like clouds. The day the sky will split open, becoming like red leather. Then on that day, no human (Ins) nor jinn (Jann) will be asked about their sin. The day the disobedient will be prevented from speech, and no inquiry will be made about the crimes, but they will be seized by the forelocks and the feet. The day every soul (Nafs) will find what it did of good present, and what it did of evil, it will wish there were a great distance between it and that. The day every soul (Nafs) will know what it has brought forth and will witness what it has sent ahead and left behind. The day the tongues will be silenced and the limbs will speak.
55:39.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

55:46.arabic: وقال أبو الدرداء (قرأ رسول الله ﭬ ﴿ ولمن خاف مقام ربه جنتان ﴾ {} فقلت: وإن سرق وإن زنى يا رسول الله فقال ﴿ ولمن خاف مقام ربه جنتان ﴾ {} فقلت: وإن سرق وإن زنى فقال: ولمن خاف مقام ربه جنتان فقلت: وإنى سرق وإن زنى يا رسول الله؟ قال: وإن رغم أنف أبى الدرداء[274])
55:46.english: And Abu al-Darda' said: (The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: 'And for he who fears the standing (maqam) of his Lord, two gardens' {Quran 55:46} so I said: Even if he steals and commits adultery, O Messenger of Allah? He said: 'And for he who fears the standing (maqam) of his Lord, two gardens' {Quran 55:46} so I said: Even if he steals and commits adultery? He said: And for he who fears the standing (maqam) of his Lord, two gardens. So I said: Even if I steal and commit adultery, O Messenger of Allah? He said: Even if it displeases Abu al-Darda' [274]).
55:46.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

55:46.arabic: وقد قال تعالى "ولمن خاف مقام ربه جنتان - ذلك لمن خاف مقامي وخاف وعبد" والقرآن من أوله إلى آخره تحذير وتخويف، لا يتفكر فيه متفكر إلا ويطول حزنه ويعظم خوفه إن كان مؤمناً بما فيه.
55:46.english: And Allah the Exalted has said: 'And for whoever fears the standing (maqām) of his Lord, two gardens - that is for whoever fears My standing (maqāmī) and fears and worships.' And the Quran from its beginning to its end is warning and intimidation (takhwīf), no one reflects (yatafakkir) in it except that his sadness (ḥuzn) lengthens and his fear (khawf) magnifies if he is a believer (muʾmin) in what is in it.
55:46.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

55:46.arabic: ومهما أردت أن تعرف صفة الجنة فاقرأ القرآن فليس وراء بيان الله تعالى بيان واقرأ من قوله تعالى: ﴿ ولمن خاف مقام ربه جنتان ﴾ {} إلى آخر سورة الرحمن واقرأ سورة الواقعة وغيرها من السور وإن أردت أن تعرف تفصيل صفاتها من الأخبار فتأمل الآن تفصليها بعد أن اطلعت على جملتها وتأمل أولا عدد الجنان قال رسول الله ﭬ فى قوله تعالى: ﴿ ولمن خاف مقام ربه جنتان ﴾ {} قال: (جنتان من فضة آنيتهما وما فيهما وجنتان من ذهب آنيتهما وما فيهما وما بين القوم وبين أن ينظروا إلى ربهم إلا رداء الكبرياء على وجهه فى جنة عدن[217])
55:46.english: And whenever you want to know the description of Paradise, read the Quran, for there is no explanation beyond the explanation of Allah, the Exalted. And read from His saying, the Exalted: 'And for the one who feared the standing (maqām) of his Lord, two gardens' {} to the end of Surah Ar-Rahman, and read Surah Al-Waqi'ah and other surahs. And if you want to know the detailed descriptions of it from the reports, then contemplate now my detailing of it after you have grasped its summary. And contemplate first the number of the gardens. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said regarding His saying, the Exalted: 'And for the one who feared the standing (maqām) of his Lord, two gardens' {} said: 'Two gardens of silver, their vessels and what is in them, and two gardens of gold, their vessels and what is in them, and nothing is between the people and their looking at their Lord except the garment of majesty upon His face in the garden of Eden.'
55:46.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

55:46.arabic: [274] حديث أبى الدرداء قرأ رسول الله ﭬ - ولمن خاف مقام ربه جنتان - فقلت وإن زنى وإن سرق الحديث رواه أحمد بإسناد صحيح.
55:46.english: [274] The narration of Abu al-Darda': The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) recited: 'And for he who fears (khafa) the standing (maqam) of his Lord (Rabb), two gardens (jannatan)' - so I said: 'Even if he commits adultery and even if he steals?' The narration is reported by Ahmad with an authentic chain.
55:46.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Book of Repentance'

55:46.arabic: وقال تعالى: ﴿ ولِمَنْ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِ جَنَّتَانِ ﴾ وقال ﭬ: (قال الله عز وجل وعزتي لا أجمع على عبدي خوفين ولا أجمع له أمنين فإن أمنني في الدنيا أخفته يوم القيامة وإن خافتي في الدنيا أمنته يوم القيامة[64])
55:46.english: And He (Allah), the Exalted, said: 'And for whoever fears the standing (maqām) of his Lord (Rabb), two gardens (jannatān).' And he (the Prophet) said: 'Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: By My might, I do not combine two fears upon My servant, nor do I combine two securities for him. If he feels secure (amn) from Me in the world, I will make him fearful (khawf) on the Day of Resurrection, and if he fears Me in the world, I will make him secure on the Day of Resurrection.'
55:46.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Fear and Hope'

55:56.arabic: فى خيام من اللؤلؤ الرطب الأبيض فيها بسط من العبقرى الأخضر متكئين على أرائك منصوبة على أطراف أنهار مطردة بالخمر والعسل محفوفة بالغلمان والولدان مزينة بالحور العين من الخيرات الحسان كأنهن الياقوت والمرجان لم يطمثهن إنس قبلهم ولا جان يمشين فى درجات الجنان إذا اختالت إحداهن فى مشيها حمل أعطافها سبعون ألفا من الولدان عليها من طرائف الحرير الأبيض ما تتحير فيه الأبصار مكللات بالتيجان المرصعة باللؤلؤ والمرجان شكلات غنجات عطرات آمنات من الهرم والبؤس مقصورات فى الخيام فى قصور من الياقوت بنيت وسط روضات الج
55:56.english: In tents of moist white pearl, with spreads of green brocade, reclining on couches set at the edges of rivers flowing with wine and honey, surrounded by youths and young boys, adorned with the wide-eyed houris (Al-Hur Al-'Ayn) from the beautiful maidens, as if they were ruby and coral, whom no human (Ins) has touched before them, nor any jinn (Jann), walking in the degrees of Paradise; when one of them sways in her walk, seventy thousand young boys carry her flanks, upon her are fine white silks that dazzle the eyes, crowned with tiaras studded with pearl and coral, shapely, coquettish, fragrant, secure from aging and misery, secluded in the tents in palaces of ruby built amidst the meadows of Paradise, restraining their gaze (Qasirat Al-Tarf), then they are served, and upon them, with cups and ewers and a cup from a flowing spring, white, a delight for the drinkers, and servants and young boys like hidden pearls circulate among them, a reward for what they used to do, in a secure station, in gardens and springs, in gardens and a river, in a seat of truth near an Omnipotent Sovereign (Malik Muqtadir); they look therein at the face of the Noble King (Al-Malik Al-Karim), and the radiance of bliss has shone upon their faces, no weariness nor humiliation afflicts them, but rather honored servants (Ibad Mukramun), and with various gifts from their Lord they are attended, so they are in what their souls (Anfus) desire, abiding forever, they fear not therein nor grieve, and they are secure from the doubt of death, so they therein enjoy bliss and eat from its foods and drink from its rivers milk and wine and honey, in rivers of its lands of silver and its gravel is coral, and upon its ground its dust is fragrant musk and its plants are saffron, and they are rained upon from clouds therein from water of narcissus upon dunes of camphor, and they are brought cups, and what cups, cups of silver studded.
55:56.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

55:60.arabic: وقال الله عز وجل: ﴿ هل جزاء الإحسان إلا الإحسان ﴾ {} فقيل الإحسان في الدنيا قول لا إله إلا الله وفي الآخرة الجنة. وكذا قوله تعالى: ﴿ للذين أحسنوا الحسنى وزيادة ﴾ {}
55:60.english: And Allah the Exalted said: 'Is the reward for excellence (Ihsan) except excellence (Ihsan)?' So it was said: The excellence (Ihsan) in this world is the saying 'There is no god but Allah' and in the Hereafter is Paradise. And likewise His saying the Exalted: 'For those who have done excellence (Ahsanu) is the best reward and increase.'
55:60.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter

55:72.arabic: وقال أنس: قال رسول الله ﷺ: (لما أسرى بى دخلت فى الجنة موضعا يسمى البيدخ عليه خيام اللؤلؤ والزبرجد الأخضر والياقوت الأحمر فقلن السلام عليك يا رسول الله فقلت يا جبريل ما هذا النداء قال هؤلاء المقصورات فى الخيام استأذن ربهن فى السلام عليك فأذن لهن فطفقن يقلن نحن الراضيات فلا نسخط أبدا ونحن الخالدات فلا نظعن أبدا، وقرأ رسول الله ﷺ قوله تعالى: ﴿ حور مقصورات فى الخيام ﴾ {}[243])
55:72.english: And Anas said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'When I was taken on the Night Journey, I entered a place in Paradise called Al-Baydakh, upon which were tents of pearl, green emerald, and red ruby. They said: Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. I said: O Gabriel, what is this call? He said: These are the ones secluded in the tents; they sought permission from their Lord to greet you, and He permitted them. Then they began to say: We are the contented ones, so we never become displeased; and we are the eternal ones, so we never depart. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) recited the saying of Allah the Exalted: "Houris secluded in tents." {}[243]'
55:72.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

55:74.arabic: فى خيام من اللؤلؤ الرطب الأبيض فيها بسط من العبقرى الأخضر متكئين على أرائك منصوبة على أطراف أنهار مطردة بالخمر والعسل محفوفة بالغلمان والولدان مزينة بالحور العين من الخيرات الحسان كأنهن الياقوت والمرجان لم يطمثهن إنس قبلهم ولا جان يمشين فى درجات الجنان إذا اختالت إحداهن فى مشيها حمل أعطافها سبعون ألفا من الولدان عليها من طرائف الحرير الأبيض ما تتحير فيه الأبصار مكللات بالتيجان المرصعة باللؤلؤ والمرجان شكلات غنجات عطرات آمنات من الهرم والبؤس مقصورات فى الخيام فى قصور من الياقوت بنيت وسط روضات الج
55:74.english: In tents of moist white pearl, within them spreads of green brocade, reclining on couches set up on the banks of rivers flowing with wine and honey, surrounded by servants and youths, adorned with the wide-eyed houris (Al-Hur Al-'Ayn) from the beautiful ones, as if they were ruby and coral, whom no human (Ins) has touched before them, nor any jinn (Jann). They walk in the degrees of the Gardens; when one of them sways in her walking, seventy thousand youths carry her flanks, upon her from the finest white silk that bewilders the gazes, crowned with tiaras studded with pearl and coral, shapely, coquettish, fragrant, secure from aging and misery, secluded in the tents, in palaces of ruby built amidst the meadows of the Gardens, restraining their glances (Qasirat At-Tarf). Then they are served, and upon them, with cups and ewers and a cup from a flowing spring, white, a delight for the drinkers, and servants and youths like hidden pearls circulate upon them, a reward for what they used to do, in a secure station, in gardens and springs, in gardens and a river, in a seat of truth near an Omnipotent Sovereign. They look therein at the face of the Noble King, and the radiance of bliss has shone upon their faces; neither weariness nor humiliation afflicts them, but rather honored servants, and with various gifts from their Lord they are attended. Thus, in what their souls (Anfus) desire, they abide eternally; they neither fear therein nor grieve, and they are secure from the doubt of death. Thus, they enjoy therein and eat from its foods and drink from its rivers milk and wine and honey, in rivers whose beds are of silver and whose gravel is coral, and upon its ground, its dust is fragrant musk and its vegetation is saffron, and they are rained upon from clouds therein from rosewater upon dunes of camphor, and they are brought cups, and what cups! Cups of silver studded.
55:74.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

56:2.arabic: وفي سورة الواقعة ﴿ ليس لوقعتها كاذبة، خافضة رافعة ﴾ {} أي جف القلم بما هو كائن وتمت السابقة حتى نزلت الواقعة إما خافضة قوما كانوا مرفوعين في الدنيا وإما رافعة قوما كانوا مخفوضين في الدنيا
56:2.english: And in Surah Al-Waqi'ah: 'There is no denying its occurrence, lowering, raising' {} meaning the pen has dried with what is to be, and the precedent has been completed until Al-Waqi'ah descended, either lowering a people who were elevated in the worldly life or raising a people who were lowered in the worldly life.
56:2.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Fear and Hope'

56:15.arabic: فالملك لا ينال بالحديث وحركة اللسان حديث وعقد القلب أيضاً حديث ولكنه حديث نفس، وإنما الصدق والإخلاص وراءهما، ولا ينصب سرير الملك إلا للمقربين وهم المخلصون، نعم لمن يقرب منهم في الرتبة من أصحاب اليمين أيضاً درجات عند الله تعالى وإن كانت لا تنتهي إلا بالملك، أما ترى أن الله سبحانه وتعالى لما ذكر في سورة الواقعة المقربين السابقين تعرض لسرير الملك فقال: "على سرر موضونة متكئين عليها متقابلين" ولما انتهى إلى أصحاب اليمين ما زاد في ذكر الماء والظل والفواكه والأشجار والحور العين، وكل ذلك من لذات المنظور
56:15.english: The Kingdom (al-Mulk) is not attained by speech and movement of the tongue; speech and the heart's conviction are also speech, but it is speech of the Soul (Nafs). Rather, Truthfulness (al-Sidq) and Sincerity (al-Ikhlas) are behind them, and the Throne of the Kingdom (Sarīr al-Mulk) is only erected for the Brought-Near Ones (al-Muqarrabūn), and they are the Sincere Ones (al-Mukhliṣūn). Yes, for those who are close to them in rank from the Companions of the Right (Aṣḥāb al-Yamīn), there are also degrees with Allah the Exalted, even though they do not culminate except in the Kingdom. Do you not see that Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, when He mentioned in Surah al-Wāqi'ah the Brought-Near Ones, the Foremost Ones (al-Sābiqūn), He addressed the Throne of the Kingdom (Sarīr al-Mulk) and said: "Upon couches woven (ʿalā sururin mawḍūnatin), reclining upon them, facing one another." And when He concluded with the Companions of the Right (Aṣḥāb al-Yamīn), He did not increase in mentioning water, shade, fruits, trees, and wide-eyed maidens (al-Ḥūr al-ʿĪn), and all of that is from the pleasures of the seen, the drunk, the eaten, and the married, and that is conceivable for beasts perpetually. And where are the pleasures of beasts from the pleasure of the Kingdom (al-Mulk), and the descent in the Highest Heights (Aʿlā ʿIlliyyīn) in the proximity of the Worlds (al-ʿĀlamīn)? And if these pleasures had value, they would not encompass beasts, and the degree of the Angels (al-Malāʾikah) would not be elevated above them. Do you think that the states of beasts—which are let loose in meadows, enjoying water, trees, and varieties of foods, indulging in lust and corruption—are higher, more pleasurable, more noble, and more deserving to be envied by those of perfection than the states of the Angels (al-Malāʾikah) in their joy with the proximity to the Lord of the Worlds (Rabb al-ʿĀlamīn) in the Highest Heights (Aʿlā ʿIlliyyīn)? Far, far is it from attainment for one who, if given the choice between being a donkey or being in the degree of Gabriel, peace be upon him, chooses the degree of the donkey over the degree of Gabriel, peace be upon him!
56:15.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

56:18.arabic: ثم يطاف عليهم وعليهن بأكواب وأباريق وكأس من معين بيضاء لذة للشاربين ويطوف عليهم خدام وولدان كأمثال اللؤلؤ المكنون جزاء بما كانوا يعملون فى مقام أمين فى جنات وعيون فى جنات ونهر فى مقعد صدق عند مليك مقتدر ينظرون فيها إلى وجه الملك الكريم وقد أشرقت فى وجوههم نضرة النعيم لا يرهقهم فتر ولا ذلة بل عباد مكرمون وبأنواع التحف من ربهم يتعاهدون فهم فيما اشتهيت أنفسهم خالدون لا يخافون فيها ولا يحزنون وهم من ريب المنون آمنون فهم فيها يتنعمون ويأكلون من أطعمتها ويشربون من أنهارها لبنا وخمرا وعسلا فى أنهار أرا
56:18.english: Then they are served, and upon them, with cups and ewers and a cup from a flowing spring, white, a delight for the drinkers, and there serve them servants and youths like hidden pearls, a reward for what they used to do, in a secure station, in gardens and springs, in gardens and a river, in a seat of truth near an Omnipotent Sovereign. They look therein at the face of the Noble King, and the radiance of bliss has shone upon their faces; neither fatigue nor humiliation afflicts them, but rather honored servants, and with various gifts from their Lord they are attended. They are in what their souls (Nafs) desire, abiding forever; they fear not therein, nor do they grieve, and they are secure from the doubt of death. They therein enjoy bliss and eat from its foods and drink from its rivers milk and wine and honey, in rivers whose beds are of silver and whose gravel is coral, and upon its ground its dust is fragrant musk and its vegetation is saffron, and they are rained upon from clouds therein from water of narcissus upon dunes of camphor. And they are brought cups, and what cups! Cups of silver adorned with pearls and rubies and coral; a cup containing sealed pure wine mixed with the sweet Salsabil; a cup whose light shines from the purity of its jewel, the drink appears from behind it with its clarity and redness; no human made it, so he would fall short in perfecting its making and beautifying its craftsmanship, in the hand of a servant whose face's radiance resembles the sun in its shining, but from where does the sun have sweetness like the sweetness of his form and the beauty of his temples and the loveliness of his eyes? So wonder at one who believes in an abode of this description and is certain of
56:18.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

56:21.arabic: وفي القرآن تنبيه على تقديم الفاكهة في قوله تعالى وفاكهة مما يتخيرون ثم قال ولحم طير مما يشتهون ثم أفضل ما يقدم بعد الفاكهة اللحم والثريد فقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم فضل عائشة على النساء كفضل الثريد على سائر الطعام فإن جمع إليه حلاوة بعده فقد جمع الطيبات ودل على حصول الإكرام باللحم قوله تعالى في ضيف إبراهيم إذ أحضر العجل الحنيذ أي المحنوذ وهو الذي أجيد نضجه وهو أحد معنى الإكرام أعني تقديم اللحم وقال تعالى في وصف الطيبات وأنزلنا عليكم المن والسلوى المن العسل والسلوى اللحم سمي سلوى لأنه يتسلى به عن
56:21.english: And in the Quran there is an indication regarding presenting fruit first in His saying, the Exalted: 'And fruit of what they choose' then He said: 'And flesh of fowl of what they desire.' Then the best thing to present after the fruit is meat and tharid (bread soaked in broth), for he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: 'The excellence of Aisha over women is like the excellence of tharid over all other foods.' If sweetness is gathered to it afterward, then the good things have been gathered. And it indicates the attainment of honor through meat, His saying, the Exalted, regarding the guests of Ibrahim when he presented the roasted calf, meaning the roasted one, which is that which is excellently cooked, and it is one meaning of honor, I mean presenting meat. And He, the Exalted, said in describing the good things: 'And We sent down upon you the manna and the quails.' The manna is honey and the quails are meat. It is called salwa (quail) because one consoles oneself with it from all other dishes, and nothing else takes its place. And for that reason he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: 'The master of dishes is meat.' Then He said after mentioning the manna and the quails: 'Eat of the good things We have provided for you.' So meat and sweetness are from the good things.
56:21.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Manners of Eating'

56:23.arabic: ويطوف عليهم خدام وولدان كأمثال اللؤلؤ المكنون جزاء بما كانوا يعملون فى مقام أمين فى جنات وعيون فى جنات ونهر فى مقعد صدق عند مليك مقتدر
56:23.english: And there will circulate among them servants and youths like the likeness of the concealed pearl (ka-amthal al-lu'lu' al-maknun) as a reward for what they used to do, in a secure station (maqam amin), in gardens and springs, in gardens and a river, in a seat of truth (maq'ad sidq) near a Sovereign, All-Powerful (Malik Muqtadir).
56:23.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

56:24.arabic: وقد شرح الله الرجاء فقال "إن الذين آمنوا والذين هاجروا وجاهدوا في سبيل الله أولئك يرجون رحمة الله" يعني أن الرجاء بهم أليق وهذا لأنه ذكر أن ثواب الآخرة أجر وجزاء على الأعمال قال الله تعالى "جزاء بما كانوا يعملون" وقال تعالى "وإنما توفون أجوركم يوم القيامة" أفترى أن من استؤجر على إصلاح أوان وشرط له أجرة عليها وكان الشارط كريماً يفي بالوعد مهما وعد ولا يخلف بل يزيد، فجاء الأجير وكسر الأواني وأفسد جميعها ثم جلس ينتظر الأجر ويزعم أن المستأجر كريم، أفيراه العقلاء في انتظاره متمنياً مغروراً أو راجياً؟
56:24.english: And Allah has explained hope (al-raja') by saying: 'Indeed, those who have believed and those who have emigrated and striven in the path of Allah - those expect the mercy of Allah.' This means that hope (al-raja') is more fitting for them, and this is because He mentioned that the reward of the Hereafter is a wage and recompense for deeds. Allah the Exalted said: 'As recompense for what they used to do.' And He the Exalted said: 'And you will only be given your wages on the Day of Resurrection.' Do you see that one who is hired to repair vessels and is promised a wage for them, and the promiser is generous, fulfills the promise whenever he promises and does not break it but rather increases, then the hired worker comes and breaks the vessels and ruins all of them, then sits waiting for the wage and claims that the hirer is generous - would the people of intellect see him in his waiting as a deluded wisher or as a hopeful one?
56:24.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

56:33.arabic: وَمَرَّ أَبُو حَازِمٍ يَوْماً فِي السُّوقِ فَرَأَى الْفَاكِهَةَ فَاشْتَرَاهَا، فَقَالَ لِابْنِهِ: اشْتَرِ لَنَا مِنْ هَذِهِ الْفَاكِهَةِ الْمَقْطُوعَةِ الْمَمْنُوعَةِ لَعَلَّنَا نَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْفَاكِهَةِ الَّتِي لَا مَقْطُوعَةٍ وَلَا مَمْنُوعَةٍ، فَلَمَّا اشْتَرَاهَا وَأَتَى بِهَا إِلَيْهِ قَالَ لِنَفْسِهِ: قَدْ خَدَعْتِنِي حَتَّى نَظَرْتُ وَاشْتَهَيْتُ وَغَلَبْتِينِي حَتَّى اشْتَرَيْتُ وَاللَّهِ لَأُذِيقَنَّهَا فَبَعَثَ بِهَا إِلَى يَتَامَى مِنَ الْفُقَرَاءِ
56:33.english: And Abu Hazim passed one day in the market and saw the fruit and bought it, then he said to his son: 'Buy for us from this fruit that is cut off and forbidden, perhaps we may go to the fruit that is not cut off (la maqtu'atin) nor forbidden (la mamnu'atin).' When he bought it and brought it to him, he said to his Soul (Nafs): 'You have deceived me until I looked and desired and overpowered me until I bought, and by Allah I will make it taste.' Then he sent it to orphans from the poor.
56:33.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Harms of the Tongue'

56:51.arabic: ثُمَّ انْظُرْ إِلَى طَعَامِهِمْ وَهُوَ الزَّقُومُ كَمَا قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿ ثُمَّ إِنَّكُمْ أَيُّهَا الضَّالُّونَ الْمُكَذِّبُونَ لَآكِلُونَ مِنْ شَجَرٍ مِنْ زَقُومٍ فَمَالِئُونَ مِنْهَا الْبُطُونَ فَشَارِبُونَ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْحَمِيمِ فَشَارِبُونَ شُرْبَ الْهِيمِ ﴾ {} وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿ إِنَّهَا شَجَرَةٌ تَخْرُجُ فِي أَصْلِ الْجَحِيمِ طَلْعُهَا كَأَنَّهُ رُءُوسُ الشَّيَاطِينِ فَإِنَّهُمْ لَآكِلُونَ مِنْهَا فَمَالِئُونَ مِنْهَا الْبُطُونَ ثُمَّ إِنَّ لَهُمْ عَلَيْهَا لَشُوبًا مِنْ حَمِيمٍ
56:51.english: Then look at their food, and it is the Zaqqum tree as Allah the Exalted said: 'Then indeed you, O those who are astray and deniers, will be eating from a tree of Zaqqum, and filling with it the bellies, and drinking on top of it from boiling water, drinking like thirsty camels drink.' And He the Exalted said: 'Indeed it is a tree that emerges in the foundation of Hellfire, its fruit as if it were heads of devils, so indeed they will be eating from it and filling with it the bellies, then indeed for them upon it is a mixture of boiling water, then indeed their return is to Hellfire.'
56:51.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

56:58.arabic: وقال تعالى أفرأيتم ما تمنون أأنتم تخلقونه أم نحن الخالقون إلى قوله للمقوين فليس يخفى على من معه أدنى مسكة من عقل إذا تأمل بأدنى فكرة مضمون هذه الآيات وأدار نظره على عجائب خلق الله في الأرض والسموات وبدائع فطرة الحيوان والنبات أن هذا الأمر العجيب والترتيب المحكم لا يستغني عن صانع يدبره وفاعل يحكمه ويقدره بل تكاد فطرة النفوس تشهد بكونها مقهورة تحت تسخيره ومصرفة بمقتضى تدبيره
56:58.english: And He, the Exalted, said: 'Have you seen what you emit? Is it you who create it, or are We the Creator?' up to His saying: 'for the grateful.' So it is not hidden from one who possesses the slightest measure of intellect, if he reflects with the slightest thought upon the content of these verses and directs his gaze upon the wonders of Allah's creation in the earth and the heavens and the marvels of the innate nature (Fitra) of animals and plants, that this amazing affair and precise arrangement cannot do without a Maker who manages it and an Agent who governs and determines it. Rather, the innate nature (Fitra) of the souls (Nufus) almost testifies to being subdued under His subjugation and directed according to the requirement of His management.
56:58.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

56:58.arabic: وقال: "أفرأيتم ما تمنون؟ أأنتم تخلقونه أم نحن الخالقون" ثم قال رسول الله ﭬ في وصف ملك الأرحام: "إنه يدخل الرحم فيأخذ النطفة في يده ثم يصورها جسداً، فيقول: يا رب، أذكر أم أنثى أسوي أم معوج؟ فيقول الله تعالى ما شاء ويخلق الملك"[13] وفي لفظ آخر: "ويصور الملك ثم ينفخ فيه الروح بالسعادة أو بالشقاوة".
56:58.english: And He said: "Have you seen what you emit? Is it you who create it, or are We the Creators?" Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said in describing the angel of the wombs: "He enters the womb and takes the sperm-drop in his hand, then he forms it into a body, and says: O Lord, male or female, straight or crooked? Then Allah the Exalted says what He wills and the angel creates." And in another wording: "And the angel forms it, then blows into it the Soul (Ruh) with happiness or misery."
56:58.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

56:60.arabic: وقد قال الله تعالى ولا يرضى لعباده الكفر فكيف يكون الفناء بالإضافة إلى محبة الله وكراهته كالبقاء فإنه تعالى يقول (ما ترددت في شيء كترددي في قبض روح عبدي المسلم هو يكره الموت وأنا أكره مساءته ولا بد له من الموت)[15] فقوله لا بد له من الموت إشارة إلى سبق الإرادة والتقدير المذكور في قوله تعالى (نحن قدرنا بينكم الموت) وفي قوله تعالى (الذي خلق الموت والحياة) ولا مناقضة بين قوله تعالى (نحن قدرنا بينكم الموت) وبين قوله (وأنا أكره مساءته) ولكن إيضاح الحق في هذا يستدعي تحقيق معنى الإرادة والمحبة والكراهة
56:60.english: And Allah the Exalted has said: 'And He does not approve for His servants disbelief' so how can annihilation (Fana') in relation to Allah's love (Mahabbah) and dislike (Karahah) be like permanence (Baqa')? For He the Exalted says: 'I have not hesitated in anything as I hesitate in taking the soul (Ruh) of My believing servant (Abd): he dislikes death and I dislike displeasing him, yet death is inevitable for him.' So His statement 'death is inevitable for him' points to the precedence of will (Iradah) and decree (Taqdir) mentioned in His statement the Exalted: 'We have decreed among you death' and in His statement the Exalted: 'Who created death and life.' And there is no contradiction between His statement the Exalted: 'We have decreed among you death' and His statement: 'And I dislike displeasing him.' But clarifying the truth in this requires verifying the meaning of will (Iradah), love (Mahabbah), and dislike (Karahah), and explaining their realities.
56:60.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

56:68.arabic: ولهذا ينبغي إذا قرأ التالي قوله عز وجل: ﴿ أفرأيتم ما تحرثون، أفرأيتم ما تمنون، أفرأيتم الماء الذي تشربون أفرأيتم النار التي تورون ﴾ {} فلا يقصر نظره على الماء والنار والحرث والمني بل يتأمل في المني وهو نطفة متشابهة الأجزاء ثم ينظر في كيفية انقسامها إلى اللحم والعظم والعروق والعصب وكيفية تشكل أعضائها بالأشكال المختلفة من الرأس واليد والرجل والكبد والقلب وغيرها ثم إلى ما ظهر فيها من الصفات الشريفة من السمع والبصر والعقل وغيرها ثم إلى ما ظهر فيها من الصفات المذمومة من الغضب والشهوة والكبر والجهل وا
56:68.english: And for this reason, it is necessary when the reader reads His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Have you then considered the seed that you sow? Have you then considered the water that you drink? Have you then considered the fire that you kindle?' {} that he should not restrict his gaze to the water and the fire and the cultivation and the semen, but rather he should contemplate in the semen, which is a drop of fluid with similar parts, then look at how it divides into flesh and bone and veins and nerves and how its organs are formed into different shapes of the head and the hand and the leg and the liver and the heart (Qalb) and others, then to what has appeared in it of noble attributes (Sifat) of hearing and sight and intellect (Aql) and others, then to what has appeared in it of blameworthy attributes (Sifat) of anger (Ghadab) and desire (Shahwa) and arrogance (Kibr) and ignorance (Jahl) and denial (Takdhib) and argumentation (Mujadala) as He, the Exalted, said: 'Has not man considered that We created him from a sperm-drop? Then at once he is a clear adversary.' {} So let him contemplate these wonders to ascend from them to the wonder of wonders, which is the attribute (Sifat) from which these wonders issued forth, so he continuously looks at the creation (Sina'a) and sees the Creator (Sani').
56:68.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

56:71.arabic: ولهذا ينبغي إذا قرأ التالي قوله عز وجل: ﴿ أفرأيتم ما تحرثون، أفرأيتم ما تمنون، أفرأيتم الماء الذي تشربون أفرأيتم النار التي تورون ﴾ {} فلا يقصر نظره على الماء والنار والحرث والمني بل يتأمل في المني وهو نطفة متشابهة الأجزاء ثم ينظر في كيفية انقسامها إلى اللحم والعظم والعروق والعصب وكيفية تشكل أعضائها بالأشكال المختلفة من الرأس واليد والرجل والكبد والقلب وغيرها ثم إلى ما ظهر فيها من الصفات الشريفة من السمع والبصر والعقل وغيرها ثم إلى ما ظهر فيها من الصفات المذمومة من الغضب والشهوة والكبر والجهل وا
56:71.english: Therefore, when the reciter reads His Exalted saying: 'Have you considered what you sow? Have you considered what you emit? Have you considered the water which you drink? Have you considered the fire which you kindle?' {}, he should not restrict his view to the water and the fire and the sowing and the semen, but rather he should contemplate in the semen, which is a drop (nutfah) with similar parts, then look at how it divides into flesh and bone and veins and nerves, and how its organs are formed into different shapes of the head and the hand and the leg and the liver and the heart (qalb) and others, then to what appears in it of noble attributes (sifat) from hearing and sight and intellect ('aql) and others, then to what appears in it of blameworthy attributes (sifat) from anger (ghadab) and desire (shahwah) and arrogance (kibr) and ignorance (jahl) and denial (takdhib) and argumentation (mujadalah), as He Exalted said: 'Has not man considered that We created him from a drop (nutfah), then behold, he is a clear adversary?' {} So let him contemplate these wonders to ascend from them to the wonder of wonders, which is the attribute (sifah) from which these wonders issued, so he continuously looks at the creation (sana'ah) and sees the Creator (sani').
56:71.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

56:75.arabic: ثم انظر كيف عظم الله أمر السموات والنجوم فى كتابه فما من سورة إلا وتشتمل على تفخيمها فى مواضع وكم من قسم فى القرآن بها كقوله تعالى والسماء ذات البروج والسماء والطارق والسماء ذات الحبك والسماء وما بناها وكقوله تعالى والشمس وضحاها والقمر إذا تلاها وكقوله تعالى فلا أقسم بالخنس الجوار الكنس وقوله تعالى والنجم إذا هوى فلا أقسم بمواقع النجوم وإنه لقسم لو تعلمون عظيم فقد علمت أن عجائب النطفة القذرة عجز عن معرفتها الأولون والآخرون وما أقسم الله بها فما ظنك بما اقسم الله تعالى به وأحال الأرزاق عليه وأضاف
56:75.english: Then look at how Allah magnified the matter of the heavens and the stars in His Book, for there is no surah except that it contains their glorification in places, and how many oaths in the Quran are by them, like His saying, the Exalted: 'And by the sky with its constellations' and 'And by the sky and the night-comer' and 'And by the sky with its paths' and 'And by the sky and He who built it' and like His saying, the Exalted: 'By the sun and its brightness' and 'And by the moon when it follows it' and like His saying, the Exalted: 'So I swear by the retreating stars' and His saying, the Exalted: 'And by the star when it sets, so I swear by the positions of the stars, and indeed, it is an oath - if you only knew - great.' You have known that the wonders of the filthy drop (Nutfah) have baffled the knowledge of the former and the latter, and Allah did not swear by it, so what do you think of that by which Allah, the Exalted, swore and referred the provisions (Arzaq) to it and attributed them to it, saying, the Exalted: 'And in the heaven is your provision and what you are promised' and He praised those who contemplate (Mutafakkirun) in it, saying: 'And they contemplate in the creation of the heavens and the earth' and the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'Woe to whoever reads this verse then wipes his forehead with it' - a hadith: 'Woe to whoever reads this verse then wipes his forehead with it' meaning His saying, the Exalted: 'And they contemplate in the creation of the heavens and the earth' - he passed over it, meaning he exceeded it without contemplation (Fikr) - and He condemned those who turn away from it, saying: 'And We made the sky a protected ceiling, but they, from its signs, are turning away.'
56:75.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Contemplation'

56:79.arabic: الثاني: التعظيم للمتكلم: فالقارئ عند البداية بتلاوة القرآن ينبغي أن يحضر في قلبه عظمة المتكلم ويعلم أن ما يقرؤه ليس من كلام البشر وإن في تلاوة كلام الله عز وجل غاية الخطر فإنه تعالى قال: ﴿ لا يمسه إلا المطهرون ﴾ وكما أن ظاهر جلد المصحف وورقه محروس عن ظاهر بشرة اللامس إلا إذا كان متطهرا فباطن معناه أيضا بحكم عزه وجلاله محجوب عن باطن القلب إلا إذا كان متطهرا عن كل رجس ومستنيرا بنور التعظيم والتوقير وكما لا يصلح لمس جلد المصحف كل يد فلا يصلح لتلاوة حروفه كل لسان ولا لنيل معانيه كل قلب ولمثل هذا الت
56:79.english: Second: The Magnification (Ta'zim) of the Speaker: The reciter at the beginning of reciting the Quran should bring to his Heart (Qalb) the majesty of the Speaker and know that what he recites is not from the speech of humans, and indeed in reciting the speech of Allah, the Exalted and Majestic, there is the utmost danger. For He, the Exalted, said: 'None touch it except the purified ones.' And just as the external skin of the Mushaf and its paper are guarded from the external skin of the toucher except if he is purified, so too its inner meaning, by the ruling of His might and majesty, is veiled from the inner Heart (Qalb) except if it is purified from every impurity and illuminated by the light of magnification and reverence. And just as touching the skin of the Mushaf is not suitable for every hand, so too reciting its letters is not suitable for every tongue, nor attaining its meanings for every Heart (Qalb). And for such magnification, 'Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, when he would open the Mushaf, would faint and say: 'It is the speech of my Lord, it is the speech of my Lord.' So magnifying the speech is magnifying the Speaker. And the majesty of the Speaker will not be present to him unless he reflects upon His attributes and His majesty and His actions. So when there comes to his mind the Throne (Arsh) and the Footstool (Kursi) and the heavens and the earth and what is between them of the Jinn and humans and animals and trees, and he knows that the Creator of all of them and the One Able over them and the Provider for them is One, and that all are in the grasp of His power, oscillating between His favor and His mercy and between His punishment and His severity—if He bestows, it is by His favor; and if He punishes, it is by His justice—and that He is the One who says: 'These to Paradise, and I do not care, and these to the Fire, and I do not care.' And this is the utmost majesty and exaltation. So by reflecting upon examples like this, the magnification of the Speaker is present, then the magnification of the speech.
56:79.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

56:82.arabic: وقوله تعالى ﴿ وتجعلون رزقكم أنكم تكذبون ﴾ {} أي شكر رزقكم
56:82.english: And His saying, the Exalted: 'And you make your provision that you deny' (Quran 56:82) means the gratitude (Shukr) for your provision.
56:82.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

56:88.arabic: واعلم أن المؤمنين مشتركون في أصل الحب لاشتراكهم في أصل المحبة، ولكنهم متفاوتون لتفاوتهم في المعرفة وفي حب الدنيا، إذ الأشياء إنما تتفاوت بتفاوت أسبابه، وأكثر الناس ليس لهم من الله تعالى إلا الصفات والأسماء التي قرعت سمعهم فتلقنوها وحفظوها، وربما تخيلوا لها معاني يتعالى عنها رب الأرباب، وربما لم يطلعوا على حقيقتها ولا تخيلوا لها معنى فاسداً بل آمنوا بها إيمان تسليم وتصديق واشتغلوا بالعمل وتركوا البحث، وهؤلاء هم أهل السلامة من أصحاب اليمين، والمتخيلون هم الضالون، والعارفون بالحقائق هم المقربون. وق
56:88.english: And know that the believers share in the root of love (Hubb) due to their sharing in the root of affection (Mahabbah), but they differ due to their difference in knowledge (Ma'rifah) and in love of the world (Dunya), for things only differ due to the difference in their causes, and most people have from Allah the Exalted only the attributes and names that struck their hearing so they received them and memorized them, and perhaps they imagined for them meanings that the Lord of Lords is exalted above, and perhaps they did not become aware of their reality nor imagine for them a corrupt meaning but rather believed in them with a faith (Iman) of submission (Taslim) and affirmation (Tasdiq) and busied themselves with action ('Amal) and abandoned investigation (Bahth), and these are the people of safety (Salamah) from the companions of the right hand (Ashab al-Yamin), and the imaginers are the strayers (Dallun), and the knowers of the realities (Arifun bi-l-Haqa'iq) are the brought-near ones (Muqarrabun). And Allah has mentioned the state of the three categories in His saying the Exalted: "Then if he is from the brought-near ones (Muqarrabun), then rest (Ruh) and fragrance (Rayhan) and a garden (Jannah) of bliss (Na'im)" the verse.
56:88.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

56:88.arabic: وأما الفوز بالسعادة فلا يناله إلا العارفون بالله تعالى، وهم المقربون المنعمون في جوار الله تعالى بالروح والريحان وجنة النعيم وأما الممنوعون دون ذروة الكمال فلهم النجاة والسلامة كما قال الله عز وجل فأما إن كان من المقربين فروح وريحان وجنة نعيم وأما إن كان من أصحاب اليمين فسلام لك من أصحاب اليمين وكل من لم يتوجه إلى المقصد ولم ينتهض له أو انتهض إلى جهته لا على قصد الامتثال والعبودية بل لغرض عاجل فهو من أصحاب الشمال ومن الضالين فله نزل من حميم وتصلية جحيم.
56:88.english: As for attaining the happiness (al-Sa'adah), it is not reached except by those who know (al-'Arifun) Allah the Exalted, and they are the ones brought near (al-Muqarrabun), those bestowed favor upon in the proximity (Jawar) of Allah the Exalted with the Spirit (al-Ruh) and sweet basil (al-Rayhan) and the Garden of Bliss (Jannat al-Na'im). As for those prevented from the peak of perfection, for them is salvation (al-Najat) and safety (al-Salamah) as Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: 'So if he is of those brought near (al-Muqarrabin), then [for him is] rest and bounty and a Garden of Bliss. And if he is of the companions of the right, then [he will be greeted with], "Peace for you from the companions of the right."' And whoever does not turn toward the objective and does not rise up for it, or rises up toward its direction not with the intention of compliance (al-Imtithal) and servitude (al-'Ubudiyyah) but for a transient purpose, then he is of the companions of the left and of the misguided, for him is a drink of scalding water and roasting in Hellfire.
56:88.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

56:95.arabic: واعلم أن هذا هو حق اليقين عند العلماء الراسخين أعني أنهم أدركوه بمشاهدة من الباطن هي أقوى وأجلى من مشاهدة الأبصار وترقوا فيه عن حد التقليد لمجرد السماع وحالهم حال من أخبر فصدق ثم شاهد فحقق وحال غيرهم حال من قبل بحسن التصديق والإيمان ولم يحظ بالمشاهدة والعيان فالسعادة وراء علم المكاشفة وعلم المكاشفة وراء علم المعاملة التي هي سلوك طريق الآخرة وقطع عقبات الصفات وسلوك طريق محو الصفات المذمومة وراء علم الصفات وعلم طريق المعالجة وكيفية السلوك في ذلك وراء علم سلامة البدن ومساعدة أسباب الصحة وسلامة البد
56:95.english: And know that this is the Truth of Certainty (Haqq al-Yaqīn) among the firmly rooted scholars (al-ʿulamāʾ al-rāsikhīn) - I mean that they attained it through witnessing (mushāhadah) from the inward (al-bāṭin) that is stronger and clearer than the witnessing of the eyes, and they ascended in it beyond the limit of imitation (taqlīd) for mere hearing. Their state is like the state of one who was informed, then believed, then witnessed, then verified; and the state of others is like the state of one who accepted with good affirmation (taṣdīq) and faith (īmān) but did not attain witnessing (mushāhadah) and direct vision (ʿiyān). So happiness (al-saʿādah) is beyond the knowledge of unveiling (ʿilm al-mukāshafah), and the knowledge of unveiling is beyond the knowledge of transaction (ʿilm al-muʿāmalah) which is traversing the path of the Hereafter and cutting the obstacles of attributes (ṣifāt), and traversing the path of erasing blameworthy attributes is beyond the knowledge of attributes, and the knowledge of the path of treatment (muʿālagah) and how to traverse in that is beyond the knowledge of the safety of the body (salāmat al-badan) and assisting the causes of health, and the safety of the body through gathering, mutual support, and cooperation by which one attains clothing, food, and shelter is tied to the authority (al-sulṭān) and its law in restraining people upon the method of justice and governance in the domain of the jurist (al-faqīh). As for the causes of health, they are in the domain of the physician. And whoever said knowledge is two knowledges: knowledge of bodies (ʿilm al-abdān) and knowledge of religions (ʿilm al-adyān), and pointed by that to jurisprudence (al-fiqh), intended by it the apparent, widespread sciences, not the precious, inward sciences.
56:95.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

57:1.arabic: أنه فيماذا يتفكر لم يقدر عليه لأن مجارى الفكر غير محصورة وثمراته غير متناهية نعم نحن نجتهد في ضبط مجاريه بالإضافة إلى مهمات العلوم الدينية وبالإضافة إلى الأحوال التى هى مقامات السالكين ويكون ذلك ضبطا جمليا فإن تفصيل ذلك يستدعى شرح العلوم كلها وجملة هذه الكتب كالشرح لبعضها فإنها مشتملة على علوم تلك العلوم تستفاد من أفكار مخصوصة فلنشر إلى ضبط الجامع فيها ليحصل الوقوف على مجارى الفكر. بيان مجارى الفكر أعلم أن الفكر قد يجرى في أمر يتعلق بالدين وقد يجرى فيما يتعلق بغير الدين وإنما غرضنا ما يتعلق بالد
57:1.english: That in what he thinks about, he cannot encompass it because the channels of thought are not limited and its fruits are endless. Yes, we strive to control its channels in addition to the important matters of religious sciences and in addition to the states (Ahwal) which are the stations (Maqamat) of the travelers (Salikin), and that will be a general control, for detailing that requires explaining all the sciences, and the entirety of these books is like an explanation of some of them, for they contain sciences of those sciences derived from specific thoughts. So let us proceed to controlling the comprehensive in them to achieve understanding of the channels of thought. Explanation of the channels of thought: Know that thought may run in a matter related to religion and may run in what is related to non-religion, and our aim is what is related to religion, so we leave the other division and concern ourselves with religion as the transaction (Mu'amalah) that is between the servant (Abd) and the Lord (Rabb) Almighty. So all the thoughts of the servant are either related to the servant and his attributes and his states (Ahwal), or related to the Worshipped One (Ma'bud) and His attributes and His actions; it is not possible to go beyond these two divisions. And what is related to the servant is either a view in what is beloved (Mahbub) to the Lord Almighty or in what is disliked (Makruh), and there is no need for thought in other than these two divisions. And what is related to the Lord Almighty is either a view in His Essence (Dhat) and His attributes and His Beautiful Names (Asma' al-Husna), or in His actions and His dominion (Mulk) and His sovereignty (Malakut) and all that is in the heavens and the earth and what is between them. And it becomes clear to you the confinement of thought in these divisions with an example, which is that the state of those who walk to Allah Almighty and yearn for His meeting relates to His Beloved (Ma'shuq) or relates to himself. So if he thinks about His Beloved, then either he thinks about His beauty and the goodness of His image in His Essence to enjoy thinking about Him and witnessing Him, or he thinks about His gentle, good actions indicating His morals and attributes to make that a multiplier of pleasure and a strengthener of his love (Mahabbah). And if he thinks about himself, then his thought is in his attributes that drop him from the eye of his Beloved so that he abstains from them, or in the attributes that bring him near to Him and make him beloved to Him so that he becomes characterized by them. So if he thinks about something outside of these divisions, then that is outside the limit of love (Ishq) and is a deficiency in it, because the complete, perfect love (Ishq) is what overwhelms the lover (Ashiq) and fills the heart (Qalb) so that it leaves no room for other than it. So the lover (Muhibb) of Allah Almighty should be like that, so his view and thought do not go beyond his Beloved. And as long as his thought is confined in these four divisions, it is not outside the requirement of love (Mahabbah) at all. So let us begin with the first division, which is his thinking about the attributes of himself and the actions of himself to distinguish the beloved from them from the disliked, for this thought is what relates to the science of transaction (Ilm al-Mu'amalah) which is the intended purpose of this book. And as for the other division, it relates to the science of unveiling (Ilm al-Mukashafah), then every.
57:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Contemplation'

57:2.arabic: فإذا دخلت السوق فقل لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له له الملك وله الحمد يحيي ويميت وهو حي لا يموت بيده الخير وهو على كل شيء قدير
57:2.english: When you enter the market, say: There is no god but Allah alone, He has no partner, to Him belongs the dominion (al-Mulk) and to Him belongs the praise, He gives life (Yuhyi) and causes death (Yumit), and He is living (Hayy) who does not die, in His hand is the good, and He is over all things capable (Qadir).
57:2.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter

57:2.arabic: حديث القول عند دخول السوق لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له له الملك وله الحمد يحيي ويميت وهو حي لا يموت بيده الخير وهو على كل شيء قدير من حديث عمر وقال غريب والحاكم وقال صحيح على شرط الشيخين.
57:2.english: The hadith of the saying upon entering the market: 'There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner to Him, to Him belongs the Kingdom (Mulk) and to Him belongs the Praise, He gives life (Yuhyi) and He causes death (Yumit), and He is Living (Hayy) and does not die, in His hand is the good, and He is over every thing All-Powerful (Qadir).' From the hadith of Umar, and he said: 'It is rare (Gharib),' and Al-Hakim said: 'It is authentic according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs.'
57:2.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication

57:2.arabic: يا من هو على كل شيء قدير
57:2.english: O You Who is over every thing powerful (Qadir).

57:3.arabic: الأصل الثالث: العلم بأنه تعالى مع كونه أزليا أبديا ليس لوجوده آخر فهو الأول والآخر والظاهر والباطن لأن ما ثبت قدمه استحال عدمه وبرهانه أنه لو انعدم لكان لا يخلو إما أن ينعدم بنفسه أو بمعدم يضاده ولو جاز أن ينعدم شيء يتصور دوامه لجاز أن يوجد شيء يتصور عدمه بنفسه فكما يحتاج طريان الوجود إلى سبب فكذلك يحتاج طريان العدم إلى سبب وباطل أن ينعدم بمعدم يضاده لأن ذلك المعدم لو كان قديما لما تصور الوجود معه وقد ظهر بالأصلين السابقين وجوده وقدمه فكيف كان وجوده في القدم ومعه ضده فإن كان الضد المعدم حادثا كا
57:3.english: The Third Foundation: The knowledge that He, exalted is He, while being eternal (Azali) everlasting (Abadi), has no end to His existence, so He is the First (Al-Awwal) and the Last (Al-Akhir) and the Manifest (Al-Zahir) and the Hidden (Al-Batin) because what has been established as eternal (Qidm) is impossible to be non-existent. Its proof is that if He were to become non-existent, it would not be free from either becoming non-existent by Himself or by a nullifier that opposes Him. And if it were permissible for something whose continuity is conceivable to become non-existent, then it would be permissible for something whose non-existence is conceivable to exist by itself. Just as the coming into being (Turyan) of existence needs a cause, similarly the coming into being of non-existence needs a cause. And it is false that He becomes non-existent by a nullifier that opposes Him because that nullifier, if it were eternal (Qadim), existence with it would not be conceivable. And it has become clear through the two previous foundations His existence and His eternity (Qidm), so how could His existence be in eternity (Qidm) while with Him is His opposite? If the opposing nullifier is originated (Hadith), it is impossible, for the originated (Hadith) is not in opposing the eternal (Qadim) so as to cut off His existence more deserving than the eternal (Qadim) in opposing the originated (Hadith) so as to repel its existence. Rather, repelling is easier than cutting off, and the eternal (Qadim) is stronger and more deserving than the originated (Hadith).
57:3.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

57:3.arabic: فلما ذكر ذلك عالم الشهادة استبعد منه ذلك وقيل له: كيف يكون هو الأول والاخر وهما وصفان متناقضان، وكيف يكون هو الظاهر والباطن؛ فالأول ليس بآخر، والظاهر ليس بباطن؛ فقال: هو الأول بالإضافة إلى الموجودات، إذ صدر منه الكل على ترتيبه واحداً بعد واحد، وهو الآخر بالإضافة إلى سير السائرين إليه فإنهم لا يزالون مترقين من منزل إلى منزل إلى أن يقع الانتهاء إلى تلك الحضرة، فيكون ذلك آخر السفر، فهو آخر في المشاهدة أول في الوجود، وهو باطن بالإضافة إلى العاكفين في عالم الشهادة الطالبين لإدراكه بالحواس الخمس، ظاهر
57:3.english: When the witness of the visible world mentioned that, it was rejected from him and it was said to him: How can He be the First (Al-Awwal) and the Last (Al-Akhir) when they are two contradictory attributes, and how can He be the Manifest (Al-Zahir) and the Hidden (Al-Batin); for the First is not the Last, and the Manifest is not the Hidden. He said: He is the First in relation to the existents, since the whole issued from Him in its order one after another, and He is the Last in relation to the journey of the travelers (Al-Sa'irin) to Him, for they do not cease ascending from one station (Manzil) to another until the termination occurs to that presence (Hadhra), so that becomes the end of the journey. Thus, He is the Last in witnessing (Mushahada) and the First in existence (Wujud). And He is Hidden in relation to those who dwell in the world of the visible (Alam Al-Shahada) seeking to perceive Him with the five senses, Manifest in relation to those who seek Him in the lamp that has ignited in his heart (Qalb) with the inner insight (Al-Basira Al-Batina) penetrating into the world of the dominion (Alam Al-Malakut). This was the unification (Tawhid) of the travelers (Al-Salikin) on the path of unification in action: I mean those to whom it was revealed that the Doer (Al-Fa'il) is one.
57:3.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

57:3.arabic: الأصل الثاني: العلم بأنه تعالى عالم بجميع الموجودات ومحيط بكل المخلوقات لا يعزب عن علمه مثقال ذرة في الأرض ولا في السماء صادق في قوله وهو بكل شيء عليم ومرشد إلى صدقه بقوله تعالى ألا يعلم من خلق وهو اللطيف الخبير أرشدك إلى الاستدلال بالخلق على العلم بأنك لا تستريب في دلالة الخلق اللطيف والصنع المزين بالترتيب ولو في الشيء الحقير الضعيف على علم الصانع بكيفية الترتيب والترصيف فما ذكره الله سبحانه هو المنتهى في الهداية والتعريف.
57:3.english: The Second Foundation: The knowledge that He, exalted is He, is Knower (ʿĀlim) of all existents and encompasses every created thing; not even an atom's weight in the earth or in the heavens escapes His knowledge, truthful in His saying: 'And He is, of all things, Knowing (ʿAlīm).' And a guide to its truthfulness is His saying, exalted is He: 'Does He not know, He Who created? And He is the Subtle (Al-Laṭīf), the Aware (Al-Khabīr).' He guides you to the deduction from creation to the knowledge that you do not doubt in the indication of the subtle creation and the work adorned with arrangement, even in the insignificant, weak thing, regarding the knowledge of the Maker concerning the manner of arrangement and composition. So what God, glorified is He, has mentioned is the ultimate in guidance and definition.
57:3.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Foundations of Belief'

57:3.arabic: وأنه واحد قديم لا أول له أزلي لا بداية له مستمر الوجود لا آخر له أبدي لا نهاية له قيوم لا انقطاع له دائم لا انصرام له لم يزل ولا يزال موصوفا بنعوت الجلال لا يقضي عليه بالانقضاء والانفصال بتصرم الآباد وانقراض الآجال بل "هُوَ الْأَوَّلُ وَالْآخِرُ وَالظَّاهِرُ وَالْبَاطِنُ ۖ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ". التنزيه: وأنه ليس بجسم مصور ولا جوهر محدود مقدر وأنه لا يماثل والأجسام ولا في التقدير ولا في قبول الانقسام وأنه ليس بجوهر ولا تحله الجواهر ولا بعرض ولا تحله الأعراض بل لا يماثل موجوداً ولا يماثل
57:3.english: And He is One, Ancient (Qadim) without beginning, Eternal (Azali) without commencement, continuous in existence without end, Everlasting (Abadi) without termination, Self-Subsisting (Qayyum) without interruption, perpetual without cessation. He has not ceased and will not cease being described with attributes of majesty; He is not subject to extinction or separation by the passing of ages and the extinction of terms. Rather, "He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden, and He is, of all things, Knowing." The Transcendence (Tanzih): And He is not a formed body nor a limited, measured substance, and He does not resemble bodies, neither in measurement nor in accepting division. And He is not a substance nor do substances inhere in Him, nor an accident nor do accidents inhere in Him. Rather, He does not resemble any existent, nor does any existent resemble Him. "There is nothing like unto Him," nor is He like anything.
57:3.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Foundations of Belief'

57:9.arabic: فالأكياس وأرباب البصائر قلوبهم "كمشكاة فيها مصباح المصباح في زجاجة الزجاجة كأنها كوكب دري يوقد من شجرة مباركة زيتونة لا شرقية ولا غربية يكاد زيتها يضيء ولو لم تمسسه نار نور على نور" والمغترون قلوبهم "كظلمات في بحر لجي يغشاه موج من فوقه سحاب ظلمات بعضها فوق بعض إذا أخرج يده لم يكد يراها ومن لم يجعل الله له نوراً فما له من نور" فالأكياس هم الذين أراد الله أن يهديهم فشرح صدورهم للإسلام والهدى، والمغترون هم الذين أراد الله أن يضلهم فجعل صدرهم ضيقاً حرجاً كأنما يصعد في السماء. والمغرور هو الذي لم تنف
57:9.english: The wise and possessors of insight (Basa'ir), their hearts (Qulub) are "like a niche containing a lamp, the lamp in a glass, the glass as if it were a brilliant star, lit from a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if untouched by fire. Light upon light." And the deluded, their hearts (Qulub) are "like layers of darkness in a deep sea covered by waves, upon which are waves, above which are clouds; layers of darkness, one above another. When one puts out his hand, he can hardly see it. And he for whom Allah has not appointed light, for him there is no light." So the wise are those whom Allah intended to guide, so He expanded their chests (Sudur) for Islam and guidance (Huda). And the deluded are those whom Allah intended to lead astray, so He made their chests (Sudur) tight and constricted, as if they were climbing into the sky. And the deluded one is he whose insight (Basirah) has not opened to be sufficient for the guidance (Hidayah) of his self (Nafs) and
57:9.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

57:10.arabic: والذي يقتضي الإيمان بهذا الأمر في القرآن والسنة وأقاويل العلماء أكثر من أن يحصر. قال الله تعالى "ونهى النفس عن الهوى فإن الجنة هي المأوى" وقال تعالى "أولئك الذين امتحن الله قلوبهم للتقوى" قيل نزع منها محبة الشهوات. وقال ﭬ "المؤمن بين خمس شدائد: مؤمن يحسده ومنافق يبغضه وكافر يقاتله وشيطان يضله ونفس تنازعه"[43] فبين أن النفس عدو منازع يجب عليه مجاهدته. ويروى أن الله تعالى أوحى إلى داود عليه السلام يا داود حذر وأنذر أصحابك أكل الشهوات فإن القلوب المتعلقة بشهوات الدنيا عقولها عني محجوبة. وقال عيسى ع
57:10.english: And that which necessitates faith in this matter from the Quran, the Sunnah, and the sayings of the scholars is more than can be enumerated. Allah the Exalted said: 'And he who restrains the Soul (Nafs) from desire (Hawa), indeed Paradise will be his refuge.' And He the Exalted said: 'Those are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for piety (Taqwa).' It is said: He removed from them the love of desires. And he (the Prophet, peace be upon him) said: 'The believer is between five hardships: a believer who envies him, a hypocrite who hates him, a disbeliever who fights him, a devil who misguides him, and a Soul (Nafs) that contends with him.' [43] Thus, he clarified that the Soul (Nafs) is a contentious enemy that must be struggled against. And it is narrated that Allah the Exalted revealed to David, peace be upon him: 'O David, warn and admonish your companions against consuming desires, for the hearts attached to the desires of the world have their intellects veiled from Me.' And Jesus, peace be upon him, said: 'Blessed is he who leaves a present desire for a promised unseen that he has not seen.' And our Prophet (peace be upon him) said to a people who returned from military struggle (Jihad): 'Welcome, you have come from the lesser struggle (Jihad) to the greater struggle (Jihad).' It was said: 'O Messenger of Allah, and what is the greater struggle?' He said: 'The struggle against the Soul (Nafs).' [44] And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The struggler (Mujahid) is he who struggles against his Soul (Nafs) in obedience to Allah the Exalted.' [45] And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Restrain your harm from your Soul (Nafs) and do not follow its desire (Hawa) in disobedience to Allah the Exalted, lest it dispute with you on a day when some of you will help others, except that Allah the Exalted forgives and covers.' [46] And Sufyan al-Thawri said: 'I have not treated anything more difficult for me than my Soul (Nafs); sometimes it is for me and sometimes against me.' And Abu al-Abbas al-Mu...
57:10.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

57:10.arabic: وقد قال تعالى: ﴿ لا يستوي منكم من أنفق من قبل الفتح وقاتل ﴾ {} الآية.
57:10.english: And Allah the Exalted has said: 'Not equal among you are those who spent before the Conquest and fought' {} the verse.
57:10.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Foundations of Belief'

57:11.arabic: وقد انخدع بمثل هذا الخيال طائفة وسلكوا طريق الإباحة وقالوا إن الله تعالى غنى عن عبادتنا وعن أن يستقرض منا فأي معنى لقوله: ﴿ من ذا الذي يقرض الله قرضا حسنا ﴾ {} ولو شاء الله إطعام المساكين لأطعمهم فلا حاجة بنا إلى صرف أموالنا إليهم كما قال تعالى حكاية عن الكفار: ﴿ وإذا قيل لهم أنفقوا مما رزقكم الله قال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا أنطعم من لو يشاء الله أطعمه ﴾ {} وقالوا أيضا ﴿ لو شاء الله ما أشركنا ولا آباؤنا ﴾ {} فانظر كيف كانوا صادقين في كلامهم وكيف هلكوا بصدقهم فسبحان من إذا شاء أهلك بالصدق وإذا شا
57:11.english: And a group has been deceived by such imagination and took the path of permissiveness and said: 'Indeed Allah the Exalted is independent of our worship and of borrowing from us, so what meaning is there to His saying: "Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him and he will have a noble reward?" (Quran 57:11) And if Allah willed to feed the poor, He would feed them, so there is no need for us to spend our wealth on them, as Allah the Exalted said narrating from the disbelievers: "And when it is said to them, 'Spend from that which Allah has provided for you,' those who disbelieve say to those who believe, 'Should we feed one whom, if Allah had willed, He would have fed?" (Quran 36:47) And they also said: "If Allah had willed, we would not have associated [anything with Him] nor would our fathers." (Quran 6:148) So look how they were truthful in their speech and how they perished by their truthfulness. Glory be to the One who, when He wills, destroys with truthfulness and when He wills, makes happy with ignorance; He misleads many thereby and guides many thereby. So these, when they thought that they were employed for the sake of the poor and the needy, exalted is Allah, then said: 'There is no share for us in the poor, and there is no share for Allah in us and in our wealth, whether we spend or withhold,' they perished just as the boy perished when he thought that the father's intention was to employ him for the sake of the slaves, and he did not realize that the intended purpose was the establishment of the attribute of knowledge in his self (Nafs) and its confirmation in his heart (Qalb) so that it would be the cause of his happiness in this world. And that was from the father only as gentleness with him in drawing him to what contains his happiness. So this example clarifies for you the misguidance of those who went astray from this path.
57:11.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

57:11.arabic: ولأجل محبة الله تعالى لبقاء النفوس أمر بالإطعام وحث عليه وعبر عنه بعبادة القرض فقال من ذا الذي يقرض الله قرضا حسنا فإن قلت قولك إن بقاء النسل والنفس محبوب يوهم أن فناءها مكروه عند الله وهو فرق بين الموت والحياة بالإضافة إلى إرادة الله تعالى ومعلوم أن الكل بمشيئة الله وإن الله غني عن العالمين فمن أين يتميز عنده موتهم عن حياتهم أو بقاؤهم عن فنائهم فاعلم أن هذه الكلمة حق أريد بها باطل فإن ما ذكرناه لا ينافي إضافة الكائنات كلها إلى إرادة الله خيرها وشرها ونفعها وضرها ولكن المحبة والكراهية يتضادان وك
57:11.english: And due to the Love (Mahabbah) of Allah, the Exalted, for the preservation of the Souls (Nafs), He commanded feeding and urged upon it, and expressed it through the worship (Ibadah) of the Loan (Qard), saying: 'Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan?' (Quran 57:11). If you say: your statement that the preservation of progeny and the Soul (Nafs) is beloved implies that its annihilation is hated before Allah, and this is a distinction between death and life in relation to the Will (Iradah) of Allah, the Exalted. And it is known that everything is by the Decree (Mashiyyah) of Allah, and indeed Allah is Free of need from the worlds. So from where is distinguished before Him their death from their life, or their preservation from their annihilation? Know that this statement is truth intended by it falsehood, for what we have mentioned does not contradict attributing all existents entirely to the Will (Iradah) of Allah—their good and evil, their benefit and harm. But Love (Mahabbah) and Hatred (Karāhiyyah) are opposites, and both do not oppose the Will (Iradah). For sometimes a thing willed is hated, and sometimes a thing willed is beloved. Sins (Ma'asi) are hated, and they, with the hatred, are willed. Obediences (Ta'at) are willed, and it is intended that they be willed, beloved, and pleasing. As for disbelief (Kufr) and evil, we do not say it is pleasing and beloved, but it is willed.
57:11.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

57:11.arabic: فإن قلت: فقد حث الشرع على الأعمال وبالغ في ذكر فضلها حتى طلب الصدقات بقوله: ﴿ من ذا الذي يقرض الله قرضا حسنا ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ ويأخذ الصدقات ﴾ {} فكيف لا يكون الفعل والإنفاق هو الأفضل. فاعلم أن الطبيب إذا أثنى على الدواء لم يدل على أن الدواء مراد لعينه أو على أنه أفضل من الصحة والشفاء الحاصل به ولكن الأعمال علاج لمرض القلوب ومرض القلوب مما لا يشعر به غالبا فهو كبرص على وجه من لا مرآة معه فإنه لا يشعر به ولو ذكر له لا يصدق به والسبيل معه المبالغة في الثناء على غسل الوجه بماء الورد مثلا إن كان ما
57:11.english: If you say: Indeed, the Sacred Law (Sharia) has urged upon works (A'mal) and exaggerated in mentioning their virtue until it sought alms (Sadaqat) by His saying: "Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan (Qardan Hasan) so He may multiply it for him and he will have a noble reward?" (Quran 57:11) and He the Exalted said: "And He takes the alms (Sadaqat)" (Quran 9:104), so how can the action (Fi'l) and spending (Infaq) not be the best? Then know that when the physician praises the medicine, it does not indicate that the medicine is desired for itself or that it is better than the health (Sihha) and healing (Shifa) attained through it. Rather, works (A'mal) are a treatment (Ilaj) for the disease (Marad) of the hearts (Qulub), and the disease of the hearts is something that most do not perceive. It is like leprosy (Baras) on the face of one who has no mirror with him, for he does not perceive it, and even if it is mentioned to him, he does not believe it. The way with him is to exaggerate in praising washing the face with rosewater (Ma' al-Ward), for example, if rosewater removes the leprosy, until excessive praise spurs him to persist in it, and his disease is removed. For if it were mentioned to him that the intended purpose is the removal of leprosy from your face, perhaps he would abandon the treatment and claim that his face has no defect. And let us give an example closer than this: We say: He has a son whom he taught knowledge (Ilm) and the Quran, and he wanted to establish that in his memory (Hifz) so that it would not depart from him. And he knew that if he ordered him to repeat (Takrir) and study (Dirasa) so that it would remain preserved for him, he would say, "It is preserved, and I have no need for repetition and study," because he thinks that what he memorizes at present remains so forever. And he had slaves, so he ordered the boy to teach the slaves and promised him for that with goodness, so that his motivation (Da'iya) would be abundant for much repetition through teaching. Perhaps the wretched boy thinks that the intended purpose is teaching the slaves the Quran and that he has...
57:11.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

57:12.arabic: فإذا لم يكن في معرفة الله تعالى إثبات صورة وجهه فلا يكون في استكمال تلك المعرفة بعينها وترقيها في الوضوح إلى غاية الكشف أيضاً جهة وصورة لأنها هي بعينها لا تفترق منها إلا في زيادة الكشف، كما أن الصورة المرئية هي المتخيلة بعينها إلا في زيادة الكشف، وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى: " يسعى نورهم بين أيديهم وبأيمانهم يقولون ربنا أتمم لنا نورنا " إذ تمام النور لا يؤثر إلا في زيادة التكشف، ولهذا لا يفوز بدرجة النظر والرؤية إلا العارفون في الدنيا، لأن المعرفة هي البذر الذي ينقلب في الآخرة مشاهدة كما تنقلب الن
57:12.english: If there is no affirmation of the image of His Face in the knowledge of Allah the Exalted, then there is also no direction or image in the completion of that very knowledge and its elevation in clarity to the utmost unveiling, because it is the very same, not differing from it except in increase of unveiling, just as the visible image is the very same as the imagined one except in increase of unveiling. And to this is the allusion in His saying the Exalted: "Their light runs before them and on their right hands; they say: Our Lord! Perfect our light for us" since the perfection of the light does not affect except in increase of unveiling. And for this reason, none attains the degree of seeing and vision except the knowers in this world, because the knowledge is the seed that transforms in the Hereafter into witnessing, just as the kernel transforms into a tree and the seed into a crop.
