And he who has no kernel in his land, how can he obtain a palm tree? And he who does not sow the seed, how can he harvest the crop? Likewise, he who does not know Allah the Exalted in this world, how can he see Him in the Hereafter? And since the knowledge is on varying degrees, the manifestation was also on varying degrees, so the difference of the manifestation in relation to the difference of the knowledges is like the difference of the plant in relation to the difference of the seed, differing inevitably in their abundance and scarcity, goodness and strength, and weakness. And for this reason, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Indeed, Allah manifests to people in general and to Abu Bakr in particular." So it should not be thought that other than Abu Bakr, from those who are below him, finds from the pleasure of seeing and witnessing what Abu Bakr finds, but he finds only a tenth of his tenth if his knowledge in this world is a tenth of his tenth. And when He favored among people with a secret settled in his chest, He favored inevitably with a manifestation that he alone possessed. And just as you see in this world one who prefers the pleasure of leadership over food and marriage, and you see one who prefers the pleasure of knowledge and the unveiling of the problems of the kingdom of the heavens.
57:12.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

57:12.arabic: فالعلم بالله تعالى وصفاته وأفعاله وحكمته في ملكوت السموات والأرض وترتيب الدنيا والآخرة ومايتعلق به هو الكمال الحقيقي الذي يقرب من يتصف به من الله تعالى، ويبقى كمالاً للنفس بعد الموت، وتكون هذه المعرفة نور للعارفين بعد الموت "يسعى نورهم بين أيديهم وبأيمانهم يقولون ربنا أتمم لنا نورنا" أي تكون هذه المعرفة رأس مال يوصل إلى كشف ما لم ينكشف في الدنيا، كما أنه معه سراج خفي فإنه يجوز أن يصير ذلك سبباً لزيادة النور بسراج آخر يقتبس منه، فيكمل النور الخفي على سبيل الاستتمام، ومن ليس معه أصل السراج فلا مطم
57:12.english: The knowledge of Allah the Exalted and His attributes and His actions and His wisdom in the dominion of the heavens and the earth and the arrangement of this world and the hereafter and what pertains to it is the true perfection that brings closer to Allah the Exalted whoever is characterized by it, and it remains a perfection for the Soul (Nafs) after death, and this knowledge becomes a light for the knowers after death: 'Their light runs before them and on their right hands; they say: Our Lord! Perfect our light for us' meaning this knowledge becomes capital that leads to the unveiling of what was not unveiled in this world, just as with it is a hidden lamp, for it is permissible that this becomes a cause for increasing the light with another lamp that is kindled from it, thus completing the hidden light by way of completion, and whoever does not have the original lamp has no hope in that, so whoever does not have the original knowledge of Allah the Exalted has no hope in this light, thus he remains like one whose likeness is in darknesses not exiting from them but 'like darknesses in a deep sea covered by a wave, above which is a wave, above which are clouds; darknesses, one above another.' Therefore, there is no happiness except in the knowledge of Allah the Exalted.
57:12.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

57:12.arabic: فالمعارف أنوار ولا يسعى المؤمنون إلى لقاء الله تعالى إلا بأنوارهم قال الله تعالى يسعى نورهم بين أيديهم وبأيمانهم وقد روي في الخبر إن بعضهم يعطي نورا مثل الجبل وبعضهم أصغر حتى يكون آخرهم رجلا يعطي نورا على إبهام قدميه فيضيء مرة وينطفيء أخرى فإذا أضاء قدم قدميه فمشى وإذا طفيء قام ومرورهم على الصراط على قدر نورهم فمنهم من يمر كطرف العين ومنهم من يمر كالبرق ومنهم من يمر كالسحاب ومنه من يمر كانقضاض الكواكب ومنهم من يمر كالفرس إذا اشتد في ميدانه والذي أعطى نورا على إبهام قدمه يحبوحبوا على وجهه ويديه و
57:12.english: The Knowledges (Ma'arif) are lights, and the believers do not hasten to meet Allah the Exalted except with their lights. Allah the Exalted said: 'Their light runs before them and on their right hands.' And it has been narrated in the report that some of them are given a light like a mountain, and some smaller, until the last of them is a man given a light on the tip of his toe; it lights up once and extinguishes another. So when it lights up his foot, he walks, and when it extinguishes, he stands. And their crossing on the Path (Sirat) is according to the measure of their light: among them is one who passes like the blink of an eye, among them is one who passes like lightning, among them is one who passes like clouds, among them is one who passes like the falling of stars, and among them is one who passes like a horse when it speeds in its arena. And the one given a light on the tip of his toe crawls on his face, hands, and legs, dragging one hand and hanging another, and his sides are struck by the Fire, and he does not cease thus until he is saved.
57:12.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

57:13.arabic: وقوله تعالى: " انظرونا نقتبس من نوركم - قيل ارجعوا وراءكم فالتمسوا نوراً" يدل على أن الأنوار لا بد وأن يتزود أصلها في الدنيا ثم يزداد في الآخرة إشراقاً. فأما أن يتجدد نور فلا، والحكم في هذا برجم الظنون مخطر، ولم ينكشف لنا فيه بعد ما يوثق به، فنسأل الله تعالى أن يزيدنا علماً ورشداً ويرينا الحق حقاً. فهذا القدر من أنوار البصائر كاشف لحقائق الشوق ومعانيه.
57:13.english: And His saying, the Exalted: "Look at us, let us borrow from your light - it is said: Go back behind you and seek light" indicates that the lights (Anwar) must have their foundation (Asl) acquired in this world (Dunya), then they increase in radiance (Ishraq) in the Hereafter (Akhira). As for a light (Nur) being newly created, no, and judgment in this matter by conjecturing assumptions is dangerous, and nothing reliable has been revealed to us about it yet, so we ask Allah, the Exalted, to increase us in knowledge (Ilm) and guidance (Rushd) and show us the truth as truth. This amount from the lights of insights (Anwar al-Basa'ir) is revealing of the realities (Haqa'iq) of longing (Shawq) and its meanings.
57:13.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

57:14.arabic: اعلم أن قوله تعالى "فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا ولا يغرنكم بالله الغرور" وقوله تعالى "ولكنكم فتنتم أنفسكم وتربضتم وارتبتم وغرتكم الأماني" الآية. كاف في ذم الغرور، وقد قال رسول الله ﭬ "حبذا نوم الأكياس وفطرهم كيف يغبنون سهر الحمقى واجتهادهم ولمثقال ذرة من صاحب تقوى ويقين أفضل من ملئ الأرض من المغترين"[1] وقال ﭬ "الكيس من دان نفسه وعمل لما بعد الموت، والأحمق من اتبع نفسه هواها وتمنى على الله"[2] وكل ما ورد في فضل العلم وذم الجهل فهو دليل على ذم الغرور، لأن الغرور عبارة عن بعض أنواع الجهل، إذ الجهل هو
57:14.english: Know that the saying of the Exalted "So let not the worldly life deceive you, nor let the Deceiver (Al-Ghuroor) deceive you concerning Allah" and His saying "But you tempted your own selves (Anfusakum) and you waited and doubted and the hopes (Al-Amani) deceived you until the command of Allah came and the Deceiver (Al-Ghuroor) deceived you concerning Allah" the verse. It is sufficient in censuring deception (Al-Ghuroor), and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said "How excellent is the sleep of the intelligent and their breaking of fast, how they surpass the staying awake of the foolish and their striving, and a speck's weight of one with piety (Taqwa) and certainty (Yaqeen) is better than the earth filled with the deceived ones"[1] and he ﷺ said "The intelligent is he who holds his self (Nafs) accountable and works for what is after death, and the foolish is he who follows his self (Nafs) its desire (Hawa) and hopes upon Allah"[2] and all that has come regarding the virtue of knowledge and the censure of ignorance is evidence for censuring deception (Al-Ghuroor), because deception (Al-Ghuroor) is an expression for some types of ignorance, since ignorance is to believe a thing and see it contrary to what it is, and deception (Al-Ghuroor) is ignorance except that there is ignorance that is not deception (Al-Ghuroor), rather it necessitates deception (Al-Ghuroor): a deceived one in it specified and a deceived one by it which is that which deceives him. So whenever the striving one believes something that agrees with desire (Hawa) and the cause necessitating ignorance is a false doubt and imagination that he thinks is evidence and it is not evidence, the ignorance occurring by it is called deception (Al-Ghuroor). So deception (Al-Ghuroor) is the settling of the self (Nafs) to what agrees with desire (Hawa), and inclines to it the natural disposition from a doubt and trick of Satan, so whoever believes that he is upon good either in the immediate or in the ultimate from a false doubt, then he is deceived, and most people think of themselves good and they are mistaken in it, so most people therefore are deceived even if the types of their deception differ and their degrees differ, until the deception of some of them is more apparent and more
57:14.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

57:14.arabic: وقال بعض المفسرين في قوله تعالى: ﴿ فتنتم أنفسكم ﴾ {} قال بالشهوات واللذات ﴿ وتربصتم ﴾ {} قال بالتوبة ﴿ وارتبتم ﴾ {} قال شككتم ﴿ حتى جاء أمر الله ﴾ {} قال الموت ﴿ وغركم بالله الغرور ﴾ {} قال الشيطان.
57:14.english: And some interpreters said regarding His saying, the Exalted: 'You tempted yourselves (Nafs)' {} He said: with desires and pleasures 'And you awaited' {} He said: with repentance 'And you doubted' {} He said: you doubted 'Until came the command of Allah' {} He said: death 'And deceived you regarding Allah the deceiver' {} He said: Satan.
57:14.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

57:15.arabic: فلما كان في آخر عمره قرأ رجل بين يديه فاليوم لا يؤخذ منكم فدية الآية فرأيته قد ارتعد وكاد يسقط فلما عاد إلى حاله سألته عن ذلك فقال نعم يا حبيبي قد ضعفنا وكذلك سمع مرة قوله تعالى الملك يومئذ الحق للرحمن فاضطرب فسأله ابن سالم وكان من أصحابه فقال قد ضعفت فقيل له فإن كان هذا من مضعف فما قوة الحال فقال أن لا يرد عليه وارد إلا وهو يلتقيه بقوة حاله فلا تغيره الواردات وإن كانت قوية
57:15.english: When he was at the end of his life, a man recited before him 'So today no ransom will be taken from you' the verse, and I saw him tremble and almost fall. When he returned to his state, I asked him about that, and he said: 'Yes, my beloved, we have weakened.' And similarly, he once heard His saying, the Exalted: 'The Sovereignty that Day is the true (sovereignty), belonging to the Most Merciful' and he became agitated. Ibn Salim, who was from his companions, asked him, and he said: 'I have weakened.' So it was said to him: 'If this is from weakness, then what is the strength of the state (Hāl)?' He said: 'That no incoming spiritual state (Wārid) comes upon him except that he meets it with the strength of his state (Hāl), so the incoming states (Wāridāt) do not change him, even if they are strong.'
57:15.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

57:19.arabic: وقد قال أبو بكر الوراق (الصدق ثلاثة صدق التوحيد وصدق الطاعة وصدق المعرفة فصدق التوحيد لعامة المؤمنين قال الله تعالى والذين آمنوا بالله ورسله أولئك هم الصديقون وصدق الطاعة لأهل العلم والورع وصدق المعرفة لأهل الولاية الذين هم أوتاد الأرض) وكل هذا يدور على ما ذكرناه في الصدق السادس ولكنه ذكر أقسام ما فيه الصدق وهو أيضا غير محيط بجميع الأقسام.
57:19.english: And Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: 'Truthfulness (Sidq) is three: truthfulness in Oneness (Tawhid), truthfulness in obedience (Taa'ah), and truthfulness in knowledge (Ma'rifah). Truthfulness in Oneness is for the general believers. Allah the Exalted said: 'And those who believe in Allah and His messengers - those are the truthful ones (al-Siddiqun).' And truthfulness in obedience is for the people of knowledge and piety, and truthfulness in knowledge is for the people of sainthood (Wilayah) who are the pegs of the earth.' And all of this revolves around what we mentioned in the sixth truthfulness, but he mentioned the divisions of what contains truthfulness, and it is also not encompassing all the divisions.
57:19.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

57:19.arabic: فإن قلت: فما شبهة المعتزلة والمرجئة وما حجة بطلان قولهم. فأقول شبهتهم عمومات القرآن أما المرجئة فقالوا لا يدخل المؤمن النار وإن أتي بكل المعاصي لقوله عز وجل: ﴿ فمن يؤمن بربه فلا يخاف بخسا ولا رهقا ﴾ {} ولقوله سبحانه وتعالى: ﴿ والذين آمنوا بالله ورسله أولئك هم الصديقون ﴾ {} الآية ولقوله تعالى: ﴿ كلما ألقي فيها فوج سألهم خزنتها. ﴾ {} إلى قوله: ﴿ فكذبنا وقلنا ما نزل الله من شيء ﴾ {} فقوله كلما ألقي فيها فوج عام فينبغي أن يكون من ألقي في النار مكذبا ولقوله تعالى: ﴿ لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى الذي كذب وتول
57:19.english: If you say: Then what is the doubt of the Mu'tazila and the Murji'a and what is the proof of the falsity of their statement? I say: Their doubt is the generalities of the Quran. As for the Murji'a, they said: The believer does not enter the Fire even if he commits all sins, due to His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'So whoever believes in his Lord, he fears neither loss nor tyranny' and due to His saying, the Exalted: 'And those who believe in Allah and His messengers - those are the Truthful Ones (al-Siddiqun)' the verse, and due to His saying: 'Whenever a group is thrown into it, its keepers will ask them...' until His saying: 'So we denied and said: Allah has not sent down anything.' So His saying 'Whenever a group is thrown into it' is general, so it should be that whoever is thrown into the Fire is a denier, and due to His saying: 'None will burn in it except the most wretched, who denied and turned away' and this is restriction, affirmation, and negation, and due to His saying: 'Whoever comes with a good deed will have better than it, and they, from the terror of that Day, will be secure' so Faith (Iman) is the head of good deeds, and due to His saying: 'And Allah loves the Doers of Good (al-Muhsinin)' and He said: 'Indeed, We do not allow to be lost the reward of any who does good in deed.' And they have no proof in that, for when Faith (Iman) is mentioned in these verses, what is intended by it is Faith (Iman) with action, since we have clarified that Faith (Iman) may be used and what is intended by it is Islam, which is agreement with the Heart (Qalb), speech, and action. The evidence for this interpretation is many reports about punishing the disobedient and the measures of punishment, and his saying (peace be upon him): 'He will be brought out of the Fire whoever had in his heart an atom's weight of Faith (Iman)' so how can he be brought out if he did not enter? And from the Quran, His saying: 'Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills' and the exception with will indicates division, and His saying: 'And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger - then indeed, for him is the Fire of Hell, abiding eternally therein' and specifying it with disbelief is arbitrary.
57:19.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Foundations of Belief'

57:20.arabic: وقد ذكر الله تعالى في آية واحدة سبعة منها فقال: " زين للناس حب الشهوات من النساء والبنين والقناطير المقنطرة من الذهب والفضة والخيل المسومة والأنعام والحرث ذلك متاع الحياة والدنيا " ثم رده في آية أخرى إلى خمسة فقال عز وجل: " اعلموا أنما الحياة الدنيا لعب ولهو وزينة وتفاخر بينكم وتكاثر في الأموال والأولاد " ثم رده تعالى في موضع آخر إلى اثنين فقال تعالى: " وإنما الحياة الدنيا لعب ولهو " ثم رد الكل إلى واحد في موضع آخر فقال: " ونهى النفس عن الهوى فإن الجنة هي المأوى " فالهوى لفظ يجمع جميع حظوظ النفس
57:20.english: And Allah the Exalted mentioned in one verse seven of them, saying: 'Adorned for people is the love of desires from women and sons and heaped-up measures of gold and silver and branded horses and cattle and tilled land. That is the enjoyment of the life of the world.' Then He reduced it in another verse to five, saying the Mighty and Majestic: 'Know that the life of the world is play and amusement and adornment and boasting among you and competition in increase of wealth and children.' Then He reduced it the Exalted in another place to two, saying the Exalted: 'And the life of the world is not but play and amusement.' Then He reduced the whole to one in another place, saying: 'And restrain the Soul (Nafs) from the passion (Hawa), for indeed Paradise is the abode.' So passion (Hawa) is a term that gathers all the shares of the Soul (Nafs) in the world, so it is necessary that asceticism (Zuhd) be in it.
57:20.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

57:20.arabic: ثم رده في آية أخرى إلى خمسة فقال عز وجل: "اعلموا أنما الحياة الدنيا لعب ولهو وزينة وتفاخر بينكم وتكاثر في الأموال والأولاد" ثم رده تعالى في موضع آخر إلى اثنين فقال تعالى: "وإنما الحياة الدنيا لعب ولهو" ثم رد الكل إلى واحد في موضع آخر فقال: "ونهى النفس عن الهوى فإن الجنة هي المأوى" فالهوى لفظ يجمع جميع حظوظ النفس في الدنيا، فينبغي أن يكون الزهد فيه.
57:20.english: Then He reduced it in another verse to five, saying, the Almighty: "Know that the life of the world is play and amusement and adornment and boasting among you and competition in wealth and children." Then He reduced it, the Exalted, in another place to two, saying, the Exalted: "And the life of the world is nothing but play and amusement." Then He reduced the whole to one in another place, saying: "And restrain the Soul (Nafs) from desire (Hawa), for Paradise is the abode." For desire (Hawa) is a term that gathers all the shares of the Soul (Nafs) in the world, so asceticism (Zuhd) should be in it.
57:20.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

57:21.arabic: فهذا يدل على أن قوله: " ذلك فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء " أي مزيد ثواب الفقراء على ذكرهم. وأما قوله: إن الغني وصف الحق، فقد أجابه بعض الشيوخ فقال: أترى أن الله تعالى غني بالأسباب والأعراض، فانقطع ولم ينطق، وأجاب آخرون فقالوا: إن التكبر من صفات الحق فينبغي أن يكون أفضل من التواضع، ثم قالوا: بل هذا يدل على أن الفقر أفضل لأن صفات العبودية فضل للعبد كالخوف والرجاء، وصفات الربوبية لا ينبغي أن ينازع فيها، ولذلك قال تعالى فيما روى عنه نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم: " الكبرياء ردائي والعظمة إزاري، فمن نازعني واحد
57:21.english: This indicates that His saying: "That is the Grace (Fadl) of Allah, He bestows it upon whom He wills" means the increased reward of the poor over their remembrance (Dhikr). As for the statement that richness is an attribute of the Truth (Al-Haqq), some shaykhs responded to it by saying: Do you see that Allah the Exalted is rich (Ghani) through causes and accidents? He fell silent and did not speak. Others answered by saying: Indeed, arrogance (Takabbur) is from the attributes of the Truth, so it should be better than humility (Tawadu'). Then they said: Rather, this indicates that poverty is better because the attributes of servitude (Ubudiyyah) are a grace (Fadl) for the servant (Abd) like fear (Khawf) and hope (Raja'), and the attributes of lordship (Rububiyyah) should not be contended over. Therefore, Allah the Exalted said in what was narrated from our Prophet, peace be upon him: "Pride (Kibriya') is My cloak and majesty (Izzah) is My garment, so whoever contends with Me in one of them, I will break him." And Sahl said: Love of honor (Izz) and permanence (Baqa') is polytheism (Shirk) in lordship and contention in it because they are from the attributes of the Lord, the Exalted. From this category, they spoke about preferring the rich and the poor, and the essence of that is attachment to generalities that accept interpretations and deficient words whose contradiction is not far, for just as the statement of one who prefers richness because it is an attribute of the Truth through arrogance is contradicted, likewise the statement of one who censures richness because it is a description of the servant with knowledge (Ilm) and recognition (Ma'rifah) is contradicted, for it is a description of the Lord, the Exalted, and ignorance (Jahl) and heedlessness (Ghaflah) are descriptions of the servant, and no one should prefer heedlessness over knowledge. The unveiling of the veil from this is what we mentioned in the Book of Patience (Kitab al-Sabr): which is that what is not intended for itself but is intended for something else then
57:21.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

57:21.arabic:
ن قرأ الأخبار  والآثار  في  تفضيل
الفقر، ولا بد فيه من تفصيل فنقول إنما يتصور  الشك  في  مقامين:  أحدهما  فقير
صابر ليس بحريص على الطلب، بل هو قانع أو راض بالإضافة إلى غني  منفق  ماله  في
الخيرات ليس حريصاً على إمساك المال.

والثاني فقير حريص مع غني حريص، إذ لا يخفى أن الفقير  القانع  أفضل  من  الغني
الحريص الممسك، وأن الغني المنفق ماله في الخيرات أفضل من الفقير الحريص.

المقام الأول فقير صابر ليس بحريص على الطلب أما  الأول  فربما  يظن  أن  الغني
أفضل من الفقير، لأنهما تساويا في ضعف الحرص على ال
57:21.english: [44] Hadith: The poor complained to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) that the rich have preceded them in good deeds and charity. The hadith and at the end he said: "That is the bounty of Allah which He gives to whom He wills." Agreed upon from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, similar.
57:21.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

57:21.arabic: وقد استشهد ابن عطاء أيضاً لما سئل عن ذلك فقال: الغني أفضل لأنه وصف الحق، أما دليله الأول ففيه نظر، لأن الخبر قد ورد مفصلاً تفصيلاً يدل على خلاف ذلك: وهو أن ثواب الفقير في التسبيح يزيد على ثواب الغني، وأن فوزهم بذلك الثواب فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء، فقد روى يزيد بن أسلم عن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه قال: بعثني الفقراء رسولاً إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: إني رسول الفقراء إليك؛ فقال: " مرحباً بك وبمن جئت من عندهم قوم أحبهم " قال: قالوا يا رسول الله إن الأغنياء ذهبوا بالخير يحجون ولا نقدر عليه،
57:21.english: And Ibn 'Ata' also cited as evidence when he was asked about that, saying: The rich person is better because he is described by the Truth (Al-Haqq, referring to Allah), but his first proof is questionable, because the report has come detailed in a way that indicates the opposite of that: which is that the reward of the poor person in glorification (Tasbih) increases over the reward of the rich person, and that their attainment of that reward is the bounty (Fadl) of Allah which He gives to whom He wills, for Yazid bin Aslam narrated from Anas bin Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The poor sent me as a messenger to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and I said: I am the messenger of the poor to you; he said: "Welcome to you and to those you have come from, a people I love." He said: They said, O Messenger of Allah, the rich have taken away the good deeds: they perform Hajj and we cannot afford it, and they perform 'Umrah and we cannot afford it, and when they fall ill, they send ahead with the surplus of their wealth as a provision for them; so the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Convey from me to the poor that for those among you who are patient and seek reward, there are three characteristics not for the rich: As for one characteristic: Indeed in Paradise there are chambers that the inhabitants of Paradise look at as the inhabitants of the earth look at the stars of the sky, none enters them except a poor prophet, or a poor martyr, or a poor believer, and the second: The poor enter Paradise before the rich by half a day, which is five hundred years, and the third: Glory be to Allah (Subhan Allah) and praise be to Allah (Al-Hamdulillah) and there is no god but Allah (La ilaha illa Allah) and Allah is the Greatest (Allahu Akbar), and the poor person said similarly
57:21.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

57:23.arabic: وينبغي أن يعول في باطنه على ثلاث علامات: العلامة الأولى: أن لا يفرح بموجود ولا يحزن على مفقود، كما قال تعالى: " لكيلا تأسوا على ما فاتكم ولا تفرحوا بما آتاكم " بل ينبغي أن يكون بالضد من ذلك: وهو أن يحزن بوجود المال ويفرح بفقده.
57:23.english: And it is necessary to rely in his inner self (Batin) on three signs: The first sign: That he does not rejoice in what is present nor grieve over what is lost, as Allah the Exalted said: "So that you may not grieve over what has escaped you nor rejoice over what He has given you." Rather, it is necessary to be the opposite of that: Which is that he grieves at the presence of wealth and rejoices at its loss.
57:23.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

57:28.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
57:28.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'Whatever is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)".'
57:28.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

58:6.arabic: وقال تعالى يوم يبعثهم الله جميعا فينبئهم بما عملوا أحصاه الله ونسوه والله على كل شىء شهيد وقال تعالى يومئذ يصدر الناس أشتاتا ليروا أعمالهم فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره ومن يعمل مثقال ذرة شرا يره وقال تعالى ثم توفى كل نفس ما كسبت وهم لا يظلمون وقال تعالى يوم تجد كل نفس ما عملت من خير محضرا وما عملت من سوء تود لو أن بينها وبينه أمدا بعيدا ويحذركم الله نفسه وقال تعالى واعلموا أن الله يعلم ما في أنفسكم فاحذروه فعرف أرباب البصائر من جملة العباد أن الله تعالى لهم بالمرصاد وأنهم سيناقشون في الحساب ويطال
58:6.english: And He, the Exalted, said: 'On the Day when Allah will resurrect them all and inform them of what they did. Allah has recorded it, while they forgot it; and Allah is Witness over all things.' And He, the Exalted, said: 'On that Day, the people will proceed in separate groups to be shown their deeds. So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.' And He, the Exalted, said: 'Then every soul will be fully compensated for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.' And He, the Exalted, said: 'On the Day when every soul will find what it did of good present [before it] and what it did of evil, it will wish that between itself and that [evil] was a great distance. And Allah warns you of Himself.' And He, the Exalted, said: 'And know that Allah knows what is in your souls (Anfus), so beware of Him.' So the possessors of insight (Arbab al-Basa'ir) from among the servants recognized that Allah, the Exalted, is lying in wait for them and that they will be scrutinized in the account and demanded with the weight of an atom from the passing thoughts (Khatarat) and glances (Lahazat). And they realized that nothing will save them from these dangers except adherence to self-accounting (Muhasaba) and sincerity in self-observation (Muraqaba), and demanding from the Soul (Nafs) in breaths and movements, and accounting it for passing thoughts and glances.
58:6.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

58:8.arabic: وسببه قياس من أقيسة إبليس نعوذ بالله منه، وذلك أنهم ينظرون مرة إلى نعم الله عليهم في الدنيا فيقيسون عليهم نعمة الآخرة، وينظرون مرة إلى تأخير العذاب عنهم فيقيسون عليه عذاب الآخرة كما قال تعالى "ويقولون في أنفسهم لولا يعذبنا الله بما نقول" فقال تعالى جواباً لقولهم "حسبهم جهنم يصلونها فبئس المصير"
58:8.english: And its cause is a syllogism from the syllogisms of Iblis (Satan) - we seek refuge in Allah from him - and that is that they look sometimes at Allah's blessings upon them in this world and analogize from them the blessing of the Hereafter, and they look sometimes at the delay of punishment from them and analogize from it the punishment of the Hereafter as Allah the Exalted said: "And they say within themselves: 'Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?'" So Allah the Exalted said in response to their saying: "Sufficient for them is Hell, which they will [enter to] burn, and wretched is the destination."
58:8.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

58:9.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
58:9.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'What is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)".'
58:9.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

58:11.arabic: اعلم أن ما ذكرناه إن تأملته بعين الاعتبار انفتحت بصيرتك وانكشف لك علل القلوب وأمراضها وأدويتها بنور العلم واليقين، فإن عجزت عن ذلك فلا ينبغي أن يفوتك التصديق والإيمان على سبيل التلقي والتقليد لمن يستحق التقليد، فإن للإيمان درجة كما أن للعلم درجة، والعلم يحصل بعد الإيمان وهو وراءه قال الله تعالى "يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات" فمن صدق بأن مخالفة الشهوات هي الطريق إلى الله عز وجل ولم يطلع على سببه وسره فهو من الذين آمنوا، وإذا اطلع على ما ذكرناه من أعوان الشهوات فهو من الذين
58:11.english: Know that if you contemplate what we have mentioned with the eye of consideration, your insight (Basarah) will open and the ailments of the Hearts (Qulub) and their diseases and their remedies will be unveiled to you by the light of knowledge and certainty. If you are incapable of that, then it is not fitting for you to miss out on belief and faith by way of reception and imitation of one who deserves imitation, for faith has a degree just as knowledge has a degree, and knowledge is attained after faith and is beyond it. Allah the Exalted said: "Allah will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge by degrees." So whoever affirms that opposing the desires is the path to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and has not become aware of its cause and secret, he is from those who have believed. And if he becomes aware of what we have mentioned regarding the helpers of the desires, he is from those who were given knowledge, and both are promised the best by Allah.
58:11.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

58:11.arabic: وقد قال تعالى وأنتم الأعلون إن كنتم مؤمنين تفضيلا للمؤمنين على المسلمين والمراد به المؤمن العارف دون المقلد وقال عز وجل يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات فأراد ههنا بالذين آمنوا الذين صدقوا من غير علم وميزهم عن الذين أوتوا العلم ويدل ذلك على أن اسم المؤمن يقع على المقلد وإن لم يكن تصديقه عن بصيرة وكشف وفسر ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قوله تعالى والذين أوتوا العلم درجات فقال يرفع الله العالم فوق المؤمن بسبعمائة درجة بين كل درجتين كما بين السماء والأرض
58:11.english: And Allah the Exalted has said: 'And you are the superior ones if you are believers' (Quran 3:139), as a preference for the believers over the Muslims, and the intended meaning here is the believer who is a knower (al-ʿĀrif) not the imitator (al-Muqallid). And He the Almighty said: 'Allah will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge by degrees' (Quran 58:11). So He intended here by 'those who have believed' those who affirmed truth without knowledge, and distinguished them from 'those who were given knowledge'. And this indicates that the name 'believer' applies to the imitator even if his affirmation is not based on insight (baṣīrah) and unveiling (kashf). And Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, interpreted His saying the Exalted: 'and those who were given knowledge by degrees', saying: 'Allah raises the knower (al-ʿĀlim) above the believer by seven hundred degrees, between every two degrees is like the distance between the heaven and the earth.'
58:11.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

58:11.arabic: فالمتكفلون بالعلوم كالمتكفلين بالثغور والمرابطين بها والغزاة المجاهدين في سبيل الله فمنهم المقاتل ومنهم الردء ومنهم الذي يسقيهم الماء ومنهم الذي يحفظ دوابهم ويتعهدهم ولا ينفك أحد منهم عن أجر إذا كان قصده إعلاء كلمة الله تعالى دون حيازة الغنائم فكذلك العلماء قال الله تعالى يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات وقال تعالى هم درجات عند الله والفضيلة نسبية واستحقارنا للصيارفة عند قياسهم بالملوك لا يدل على حقارتهم إذا قيسوا بالكناسين فلا تظن أن ما نزل عن الرتبة القصوى ساقط القدر بل الرت
58:11.english: Those who undertake the sciences are like those who undertake the frontiers and those who garrison them and the warriors who strive (Mujahidun) in the path of Allah. Among them is the fighter, among them is the supporter, among them is the one who gives them water to drink, and among them is the one who guards their mounts and tends to them. Not one of them is deprived of reward if his intention is to exalt the word of Allah the Exalted, without seizing spoils. Likewise are the scholars. Allah the Exalted said: 'Allah will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge, by degrees.' And He the Exalted said: 'They are degrees with Allah.' And virtue is relative. Our belittling of the money-changers when comparing them to kings does not indicate their lowliness when they are compared to the sweepers. So do not think that what falls below the highest rank is of fallen worth. Rather, the highest rank is for the prophets, then the friends (Awliya'), then the scholars firmly grounded in knowledge, then for the righteous according to the disparity of their degrees. And in summary, whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it. And whoever intends Allah the Exalted with knowledge, whatever knowledge it may be, his benefit and elevation are inevitable.
58:11.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Book of Knowledge'

58:11.arabic: شواهدها من القرآن قوله عز وجل: ﴿شهد الله أنه لا إله إلا هو والملائكة وأولو العلم قائما بالقسط﴾ (آل عمران 3: 18) فانظر كيف بدأ سبحانه وتعالى بنفسه وثنى بالملائكة وثلث بأهل العلم وناهيك بهذا شرفا وفضلا وجلاء ونبلا وقال الله تعالى: ﴿يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات﴾ (المجادلة: 11) قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: للعلماء درجات فوق المؤمنين بسبعمائة درجة ما بين الدرجتين مسيرة خمسمائة عام.
58:11.english: Its evidences from the Quran are His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and [so do] the angels and those of knowledge (أولو العلم), [that He is] maintaining [creation] in justice' (Al Imran 3:18). So observe how He, the Exalted and Most High, began with Himself, then mentioned the angels second, and third with the people of knowledge (أهل العلم) - and what an honor, virtue, clarity, and nobility this is! And Allah, the Exalted, said: 'Allah will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge (أوتوا العلم) by degrees' (Al-Mujadilah: 11). Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: 'For the scholars (العلماء) there are degrees above the believers by seven hundred degrees; between each two degrees is a distance of five hundred years' journey.'
58:11.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Book of Knowledge'

58:11.arabic: ولكنا نشرح لك إن أردت أن ترتقي من درجة الإيمان إلى درجة العلم قال الله تعالى "يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات" فنقول: في الجوع عشر فوائد.
58:11.english: But we explain to you if you wish to ascend from the level of Faith (Iman) to the level of Knowledge (Ilm), Allah the Exalted said: "Allah will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge by degrees." So we say: In hunger there are ten benefits.
58:11.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Harms of the Tongue'

58:12.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
58:12.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Whatever is in the Quran of 'O you who have believed' is in the Torah 'O you poor ones'.
58:12.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

58:19.arabic: والتطارد بين ذكر الله تعالى ووسوسة الشيطان كالتطارد بين النور والظلام وبين الليل والنهار ولتضادهما قال الله تعالى استحوذ عليهم الشيطان فأنساهم ذكر الله وقال أنس قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الشيطان واضع خرطومه على قلب ابن آدم فإن هو ذكر الله تعالى خنس وإن نسي الله تعالى التقم قلبه
58:19.english: And the chasing between the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah the Exalted and the whispering of the Satan is like the chasing between the light and the darkness and between the night and the day. And due to their opposition, Allah the Exalted said: 'The Satan has gained mastery over them, so he has made them forget the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah. Those are the party of the Satan. Unquestionably, indeed the party of the Satan - they will be the losers.' And He said: 'He made them forget.' The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'Indeed the Satan places his snout upon the heart of the son of Adam. So if he remembers Allah the Exalted, he withdraws; and if he forgets Allah the Exalted, he swallows his heart.'
58:19.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

58:21.arabic: فإن قصده عدو أو سبع في ليل أو نهار فليقرأ آية الكرسي وشهد الله والإخلاص والمعوذتين وليقل بسم الله ما شاء الله لا قوة إلا بالله حسبي الله توكلت على الله ما شاء الله لا يأتي بالخير إلا الله ما شاء الله لا يصرف السوء إلا الله حسبي الله وكفى سمع الله لمن دعا ليس وراء الله منتهى ولا دون الله ملجأ ~ ﴿كتب الله لأغلبن أنا ورسلي إن الله قوي عزيز﴾ ~ تحصنت بالله العظيم واستغثت بالحي الذي لا يموت اللهم احرسنا بعينك التي لا تنام واكنفنا بركنك الذي لا يرام اللهم ارحمنا بقدرتك علينا فلا نهلك وأنت ثقتنا ورجاؤنا
58:21.english: If an enemy or beast approaches him by night or day, let him recite the Throne Verse (Ayat al-Kursi), 'Allah bears witness...' (Surah al-Ikhlas), and the two Surahs of Refuge (al-Mu'awwidhatayn), and let him say: In the name of Allah, what Allah wills, there is no power except with Allah, Allah is sufficient for me, I have placed my trust in Allah, what Allah wills, none brings good except Allah, what Allah wills, none repels evil except Allah, Allah is sufficient for me and enough, Allah hears whoever calls, there is no limit beyond Allah and no refuge below Allah ~ 'Allah has decreed: "I will surely prevail, I and My messengers. Indeed, Allah is Powerful, Mighty."' ~ I have fortified myself with Allah the Great and sought help from the Living (al-Hayy) who does not die. O Allah, guard us with Your eye that does not sleep and shelter us with Your stronghold that cannot be breached. O Allah, have mercy on us by Your power over us so we do not perish, and You are our trust and hope. O Allah, incline towards us the hearts (Qulub) of Your male servants and female servants with compassion and mercy, indeed You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.
58:21.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

58:21.arabic: فإذا نام واحد حرس آخر حديث تناوب الرفقاء في الحراسة تقدم في الحج في الباب الثاني فهذه السنة ومهما قصده عدو أو سبع في ليل أو نهار فليقرأ آية الكرسي وشهد الله وسور الإخلاص والمعوذتين وليقل بسم الله ما شاء الله لا قوة إلا بالله حسبي الله توكلت على الله ما شاء الله لا يأتي بالخيرات إلا الله ما شاء الله لا يصرف السوء إلا الله حسبي الله وكفى سمع الله لمن دعا ليس وراء الله منتهى ولا دون الله ملجأ كتب الله لأغلبن أنا ورسلي إن الله قوي عزيز تحصنت بالله العظيم واستعنت بالحي القيوم الذي لا يموت اللهم احرسن
58:21.english: If one sleeps, another guards. The hadith about companions taking turns in guarding has been mentioned previously in Hajj in the second chapter. This is the Sunnah. And whenever an enemy or predator intends him in night or day, let him recite the Throne Verse (Ayat al-Kursi) and 'Allah bears witness' and the chapters of Sincerity (al-Ikhlas) and the two seeking refuge (al-Mu'awwidhatayn), and let him say: In the name of Allah, what Allah wills, there is no power except with Allah, Allah is sufficient for me, I rely upon Allah, what Allah wills, none brings the good things except Allah, what Allah wills, none repels the evil except Allah, Allah is sufficient for me and enough, Allah hears whoever calls, there is no limit beyond Allah, and there is no refuge below Allah. Allah has written: 'I will surely overcome, I and My messengers. Indeed, Allah is Powerful, Mighty.' I have fortified myself with Allah the Great, and I have sought help from the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence (al-Qayyum) who does not die. O Allah, guard us with Your eye that does not sleep, and shelter us with Your stronghold that cannot be reached. O Allah, have mercy on us with Your power over us, so do not destroy us while You are our trust and our hope. O Allah, turn towards us the hearts (Qulub) of Your male servants and female servants with compassion and mercy, indeed You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.
58:21.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Etiquette of Travel'

58:22.arabic: هم أطيب الناس خيراً وألينهم عريكة وأسخاهم نفساً، علامتهم السخاء وسجيتهم البشاشة صفتهم السلامة، ليسوا اليوم في خشية وغداً في غفلة ولكن مدامين على حالهم الظاهر وهم فيما بينهم وبين ربهم لا تدركهم الرياح العواصف ولا الخيل المجراة، قلوبهم تصعد ارتياحاً إلى الله واشتياقاً إليه وقدماً في استباق الخيرات "أولئك حزب الله ألا إن حزب الله هم المفلحون" قال الراوي: فقلت: يا أبا الدرداء ما سمعت بصفة أشد علي من تلك الصفة وكيف لي أن أبلغها؟ فقال: ما بينك وبين أن تكون في أوسعها إلا أن تكون تبغض الدنيا، فإنك إذا أ
58:22.english: They are the best of people in goodness and the softest in disposition and the most generous in soul (Nafs). Their sign is generosity and their nature is cheerfulness and their attribute is safety. They are not today in fear and tomorrow in heedlessness, but they are constant in their apparent state and between them and their Lord, the stormy winds and the galloping horses do not reach them. Their hearts ascend with delight (Irtiyāḥ) to Allah and longing for Him and with precedence in racing to good deeds: "Those are the party of Allah. Indeed, the party of Allah are the successful ones." The narrator said: I said: O Abu Darda, I have not heard of a description more difficult for me than that description, and how can I attain it? He said: Between you and being in its widest expanse is only that you hate the worldly life (Dunyā), for if you hate the worldly life, you turn to the love of the Hereafter (Ākhirah), and according to the measure of your love for the Hereafter, you abstain from the worldly life, and according to that measure, you see what benefits you. And when Allah knows from a servant (ʿAbd) good seeking, He pours upon him correctness and surrounds him with protection. And know, O my nephew, that this is in the Book of Allah, the Revealed: "Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good."
58:22.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

58:22.arabic: أما من الآيات فقوله تعالى: " رضي الله عنهم ورضوا عنه "، وقد قال تعالى: " هل جزاء الإحسان إلا الإحسان " ومنتهى الإحسان رضا الله عن عبده وهو ثواب رضا العبد عن الله تعالى. وقال تعالى: " ومساكن طيبة في جنات عدن ورضوان من الله أكبر " فقد رفع الله الرضا فوق جنات عدن كما رفع ذكره الصلاة حيث قال: " إن الصلاة تنهي عن الفحشاء والمنكر ولذكر الله أكبر " فكما أن مشاهدة المذكور في الصلاة أكبر من الصلاة فرضوان رب الجنة أعلى من الجنة بل هو غاية مطلب سكان الجنان.
58:22.english: As for from the verses, His saying, the Exalted: "Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him" (Quran 58:22), and He, the Exalted, has said: "Is the reward for good [anything] but good?" (Quran 55:60) and the ultimate good is Allah's pleasure (Rida) with His servant, and it is the reward for the servant's pleasure (Rida) with Allah, the Exalted. And He, the Exalted, said: "And pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence; but approval from Allah is greater" (Quran 9:72). Indeed, Allah has elevated pleasure (Rida) above the gardens of Eden, just as He elevated the mention (Dhikr) of prayer when He said: "Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah is greater" (Quran 29:45). So just as witnessing the Remembered One (Al-Madhkur) in prayer is greater than the prayer, the pleasure (Ridwan) of the Lord of the Garden is higher than the Garden; rather, it is the ultimate goal of the inhabitants of the Gardens.
58:22.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

58:22.arabic: وأما الانبساط معه والاسترسال إليه كما يسترسل إلى الأصدقاء فهو مكروه كراهة شديدة يكاد ينتهي ما يقوى منها إلى حد التحريم قال تعالى لا تجد قوما يؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر يوادون من حاد الله ورسوله ولو كانوا آباءهم أو أبناءهم الآية وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم المسلم والمشرك لا تتراءى ناراهما حديث المؤمن والمشرك لا تتراءى ناراهما رواه أبو داود والترمذي من حديث جرير أنا بريء من كل مسلم يقيم بين أظهر المشركين قالوا يا رسول الله ولم قال لا تراءى ناراهما رواه النسائي مرسلا وقال البخاري الصحيح أنه مرسل وقال عز
58:22.english: And as for being open with him and relaxing with him as one relaxes with friends, it is disliked with a strong dislike that almost reaches the limit of prohibition. Allah the Exalted said: 'You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers or their sons...' the verse. And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'The Muslim and the polytheist - their fires should not be visible to each other' - the hadith: 'The believer and the polytheist - their fires should not be visible to each other' - narrated by Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi from the narration of Jarir: 'I am free from every Muslim who resides among the polytheists.' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, why?' He said: 'Their fires should not be visible to each other' - narrated by al-Nasa'i as mursal, and al-Bukhari said the correct is that it is mursal. And the Mighty and Majestic said: 'O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies...' the verse.
58:22.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

59:2.arabic: اعلم أن العجب مذموم في كتاب الله تعالى وسنة رسوله ﭬ. قال الله تعالى "ويوم حنين إذ أعجبتكم كثرتكم فلم تغن عنكم شيئاً" ذكر ذلك في معرض الإنكار وقال عز وجل "وظنوا أنهم ما نعتهم حصونهم من الله فأتاهم الله من حيث لم يحتسبوا" فرد على الكفار في أعجابهم بحصونهم وشوكتهم وقال تعالى "وهم يحسبون أنهم يحسنون صنعاً -، وهذا أيضاً يرجع إلى العجب بالعمل. وقد يعجب الإنسان بالعمل هو مخطئ فيه كما يعجب بعمل هو مصيب فيه.
59:2.english: Know that self-conceit (Al-'Ujb) is condemned in the Book of Allah the Exalted and the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ. Allah the Exalted said: "And on the day of Hunayn when your multitude made you self-conceited (A'jabatkum) but it availed you nothing" - He mentioned that in the context of reproach. And He the Glorified said: "And they thought that their fortresses would protect them from Allah, but Allah came upon them from where they did not expect" - He refuted the disbelievers in their self-conceit (A'jabihim) regarding their fortresses and their might. And He the Exalted said: "And they think that they are doing good work" - and this also returns to self-conceit (Al-'Ujb) in action. And a person may be self-conceited (Yu'jab) about an action in which he is mistaken, just as he may be self-conceited about an action in which he is correct.
59:2.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

59:2.arabic: فمن الناس من يسر له نظر الاعتبار فلا ينظر في شىء من عالم الملك إلا ويعبر به إلى عالم الملكوت فيسمى عبوره عبرة وقد أمر الحق به فقال: ﴿ فاعتبروا يا أولى الأبصار ﴾ {} ومنهم من عميت بصيرته فلم يعتبر فاحتبس في عالم الملك والشهادة وستنفتح إلى حبسه أبواب جهنم وهذا الحبس مملوء نارا من شأنها أن تطلع على الأفئدة إلا أن بينه وبين إدراك ألمها حجابا فإذا رفع ذلك الحجاب بالموت أدرك وعن هذا أظهر الله تعالى الحق على لسان قوم استنطقهم بالحق فقالوا الجنة والنار مخلوقتان ولكن الجحيم تدرك مرة بإدراك يسمى علم اليقين
59:2.english: Among people, there is one for whom the gaze of consideration (nazar al-i'tibar) is made easy, so he does not look at anything from the world of dominion (alam al-mulk) except that he crosses over with it to the world of sovereignty (alam al-malakut), and his crossing is called a lesson (ibrah). And the Truth (al-Haqq) has commanded it, saying: 'So take lesson (i'tabiru), O you of insight (uli al-absar).' {} And among them is one whose insight (basirah) is blinded, so he does not take lesson, and he is confined in the world of dominion (alam al-mulk) and the witnessed world (alam al-shahadah), and the gates of Hell will open to his confinement. And this confinement is filled with a fire whose nature is to rise upon the hearts (af'idah), except that between him and the perception of its pain is a veil (hijab). So when that veil is lifted by death, he perceives. And from this, Allah the Exalted manifested the truth upon the tongue of a people whom He made speak with the truth, and they said: 'Paradise and Hell are created, but the Blazing Fire (al-Jahim) is perceived once with a perception called the knowledge of certainty (ilm al-yaqin), and once with another perception called the eye of certainty (ayn al-yaqin). And the eye of certainty (ayn al-yaqin) does not occur except in the Hereafter, and the knowledge of certainty (ilm al-yaqin) may occur in this world, but for those who have fulfilled their share of the light of certainty (nur al-yaqin). Therefore, Allah the Exalted said: 'No! If you knew with the knowledge of certainty (ilm al-yaqin), you would see the Blazing Fire (al-Jahim).' {} That is, in this world. 'Then you will see it with the eye of certainty (ayn al-yaqin).' {} That is, in the Hereafter. So then, it has become clear that the sound heart (al-qalb al-salih) for the dominion of the Hereafter is only noble, like the sound person for the dominion of this world.
59:2.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

59:8.arabic: أما من الآيات فيدل عليه قوله تعالى " للفقراء المهاجرين الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم وأموالهم " الآية. وقال تعالى: " للفقراء الذين أحصروا في سبيل الله لا يستطيعون ضرباً في الأرض " ساق الكلام في معرض المدح، ثم قدم وصفه بالفقر على وصفهم بالهجرة والإحصار وفيه دلالة ظاهرة على مدح الفقير.
59:8.english: As for from the verses, it indicates His saying, the Exalted: 'For the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their properties' the verse. And He said, the Exalted: 'For the poor who were restricted in the path of Allah, unable to move about in the land' He directed the speech in the context of praise, then He presented their description with poverty before their description with emigration and restriction, and in it is an apparent indication of praising the poor person.
59:8.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

59:9.arabic: ومنها أن يكون مؤثراً ما أحبه الله تعالى على ما يحبه في ظاهره وباطنه فيلزم مشاق العمل ويجتنب إتباع الهوى ويعرض عنه دعة الكسل، ولا يزال مواظباً على طاعة الله ومتقرباً إليه بالنوافل وطالباً عنده مزايا الدرجات كما يطلب المحب مزيد القرب في قلب محبوبه، وقد وصف الله تعالى المحبين بالإيثار فقال: "يحبون من هاجر إليهم ولا يجدون في صدورهم حاجة مما أوتوا ويؤثرون على أنفسهم ولو كان بهم خصاصة" ومن بقي مستقراً على متابعة الهوى فمحبوبه ما يهواه، بل يترك المحب هوى نفسه كما قيل: |أريد وصاله   | |فأترك ما   | |وير
59:9.english: And among them is that one prefers what Allah the Exalted loves over what he loves in his outward and inward state, so he adheres to the hardships of work and avoids following the desire (Hawa) and turns away from the ease of laziness, and he remains constant in obedience to Allah and drawing near to Him through supererogatory acts and seeking with Him the merits of degrees as the lover seeks increased closeness in the heart of his beloved, and Allah the Exalted has described the lovers with preference (Ithar) saying: "They love those who emigrated to them and do not find in their chests any need of what they were given and they prefer over themselves even if there is poverty with them." And whoever remains settled upon following the desire (Hawa), his beloved is what he desires, rather the lover abandons the desire (Hawa) of his soul (Nafs) as it is said: |I want his union   | |so I abandon what   | |and he wants my abandonment   | |I want for what  | |             | |he wants       |
59:9.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

59:9.arabic: اعلم أن المؤذي ممقوت بالطبع، ومن آذاك فلا يمكنك أن لا تبغضه غالباً، فإذا تيسرت له نعمة فلا يمكنك أن لا تكرهها له حتى يستوي عندك حسن حال عدوك وسوء حاله، بل لا تزال تدرك في النفس بينهما تفرقة، ولا يزال الشيطان ينازعك إلى الحسد له، ولكن عن قوي ذلك فيك حتى بعثك على إظهار الحسد بقول أو فعل بحيث يعرف ذلك من ظاهرهك بأفعالك الاختيارية فأنت حسود عاص بحسدك، وإن كففت ظاهرك بالكلية إلا أنك بباطنك تحب زوال النعمة وليس في نفسك كراهة لهذه الحالة فأنت أيضاً حسود عاص، لأن الحسد صفة القلب لا صفة الفعل، قال الله ت
59:9.english: Know that the one who harms is naturally hated, and if someone harms you, you cannot help but generally hate them. If a blessing is facilitated for them, you cannot help but dislike it for them until the good state of your enemy and their bad state become equal to you. Rather, you continuously perceive in the Soul (Nafs) a distinction between them, and Satan continuously contends with you towards envying them. But if that becomes strong in you until it incites you to manifest envy by word or deed such that it is known from your outward appearance through your voluntary actions, then you are an envious sinner with your envy. And if you completely restrain your outward appearance, yet in your inner self you desire the removal of the blessing and there is no aversion in your Soul (Nafs) to this state, then you are also an envious sinner, because envy is an attribute of the Heart (Qalb), not an attribute of action. Allah the Exalted said: "And they find in their chests no need of what they have been given" and He the Mighty and Majestic said: "They wish that you would disbelieve as they have disbelieved so you would be equal" and He said: "If good touches you, it distresses them." As for the action, it is backbiting and lying, and it is an act emanating from envy and is not the essence of envy. Rather, the place of envy is the Heart (Qalb), not the limbs. Indeed, this envy is not an injustice requiring seeking permission for it, but it is a sin between you and Allah the Exalted. And seeking permission is only required for the apparent causes upon the limbs. So if you restrain your outward appearance and compel along with that your Heart (Qalb) to aversion to what naturally emanates from it of desiring the removal of the blessing, until it is as if you detest your Soul (Nafs) for what is in its nature, so that aversion is from the side of the intellect in opposition to the inclination from the side of nature, then you have fulfilled what is obligatory upon you. And in most circumstances, no more than this enters under your choice. As for changing the nature so that the one who harms and the one who does good become equal to him, and his joy or grief over what is facilitated for them of blessing or what befalls them of affliction becomes equal, this is something that nature does not comply with as long as one is attentive to worldly interests, except that one becomes absorbed in Allah the Exalted like the intoxicated, passionate one. Then his affair may reach the point that his Heart (Qalb) does not attend to the details of the conditions of the servants, rather he looks at all with one eye, and it is the eye of mercy, and he sees all as servants of Allah and their actions as actions of Allah, and he sees them as compelled and...
59:9.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

59:9.arabic: اعلم أن السخاء والبخل كل منهما ينقسم إلى درجات. فأرفع درجة السخاء الإيثار، وهو أن يجود بالمال مع الحاجة. وإنما السخاء عبارة عن بذل ما لا يحتاج إليه لمحتاج أو لغير محتاج، والبذل مع الحاجة أشد. وكما أن السخاوة قد تنتهي إلى أن يسخو الإنسان على غيره مع الحاجة فالبخل قد ينتهي إلى أن يبخل على نفسه مع الحاجة، فكم من بخيل يمسك المال ويمرض فلا يتداوى، ويشتهي الشهوة فلا يمنعه منها إلا البخل بالثمن؛ ولو وجدها مجاناً لأكلها. فهذا بخيل على نفسه مع الحاجة؛ وذلك يؤثر على نفسه غيره مع أنه محتاج إليه. فانظر ما ب
59:9.english: Know that generosity (Sakhā') and miserliness (Bukhl) each divide into degrees. The highest degree of generosity is altruistic preference (Īthār), which is to give wealth while in need. Indeed, generosity is an expression of giving what one does not need to one in need or not in need, but giving while in need is more intense. Just as generosity may culminate in a person being generous to others while in need, miserliness may culminate in a person being miserly toward himself while in need, for how many misers hold onto wealth and fall ill yet do not seek treatment, and desire a craving yet nothing prevents them except miserliness with the price; if they found it for free, they would consume it. This is a miser toward himself while in need; that one prefers others over himself while he is in need of it. So look at the difference between the two men? For character traits are gifts that Allah places where He wills, and there is no degree in generosity beyond altruistic preference. And Allah praised the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, with it, saying: "And they prefer others over themselves even if there is poverty (khaṣāṣah) upon them." And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Any person who desires a craving and repels his craving and prefers others over himself, he is forgiven." [100] And 'Ā'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) did not eat his fill for three consecutive days until he departed the world, and if we wished, we could have eaten our fill, but we used to prefer others over ourselves." [101] And a guest came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and he found nothing with his family, so a man from the Helpers (Anṣār) entered upon him and took the guest to his family, then placed food before him and ordered his wife to extinguish the lamp, and he began extending his hand to the food as if he were eating but not eating, until the guest ate. When morning came, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said to him: "Indeed, Allah was amazed at your action toward your guest," and was revealed: "And they prefer others over themselves even if there is poverty (khaṣāṣah) upon them." [102] So generosity is a character trait from the character traits of Allah the Exalted; and altruistic preference is the highest degree of generosity.
59:9.book_title: Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth
59:9.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

59:9.arabic: [102] حديث نزل به ضيف فلم يجد عند أهله شيئا فدخل عليه رجل من الأنصار فذهب به إلى أهله الحديث في نزول قوله تعالى ويؤثرون على أنفسهم ولو كان بهم خصاصة متفق عليه من حديث أبي هريرة.
59:9.english: [102] A hadith: A guest came to him and he did not find anything with his family, so a man from the Ansar (Helpers) entered upon him and took him to his family. The hadith is about the revelation of His saying, the Exalted: 'And they give preference over themselves, even though they are in need (خصاصة).' Agreed upon from the hadith of Abu Huraira.
59:9.book_title: Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth
59:9.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

59:9.arabic: المعنى الثاني التطهير من صفة البخل فإنه من المهلكات قال ﭬ: (ثلاث مهلكات شح مطاع وهوى متبع وإعجاب المرء بنفسه[9]) وقال تعالى: ﴿ ومن يوق شح نفسه فأولئك هم المفلحون ﴾ {} وسيأتي في ربع المهلكات وجه كونه مهلكا وكيفية التقصي منه وإنما تزول صفة البخل بأن تتعود بذل المال فحب الشيء لا ينقطع إلا بقهر النفس على مفارقته حتى يصير ذلك اعتيادا فالزكاة بهذا المعنى طهرة أي تطهر صاحبها عن خبث البخل المهلك وإنما طهارته بقدر بذله وبقدر فرحه بإخراجه واستبشاره بصرفه إلى الله تعالى.
59:9.english: The second meaning: purification from the attribute of miserliness (Bakhl), for it is among the destroyers. He (the Prophet) said: 'Three destroyers: obeyed greed (Shuhh), followed desire (Hawā), and self-admiration of a person.' And Allah the Exalted said: 'And whoever is protected from the greed (Shuhh) of his Soul (Nafs), then those are the successful ones.' And it will come in the quarter of the destroyers the aspect of its being a destroyer and how to be cautious from it. And the attribute of miserliness only vanishes by accustoming oneself to giving wealth, for the love of something does not cease except by compelling the Soul (Nafs) to part from it until that becomes habitual. So Zakat in this meaning is a purification (Taharah), meaning it purifies its possessor from the filth of the destructive miserliness. And its purification is according to the measure of his giving and according to the measure of his joy in expending it and his gladness in directing it to Allah the Exalted.
59:9.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

59:10.arabic: ربنا اغفر لنا ولإخواننا الذين سبقونا بالإيمان ولا تجعل في قلوبنا غلا للذين آمنوا ربنا إنك رؤوف رحيم
59:10.english: Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and do not place in our hearts any rancor (Ghilla) toward those who have believed. Our Lord, indeed You are Kind (Ra'uf), Merciful (Rahim).
59:10.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

59:13.arabic: قال تعالى: (لأنتم أشد رهبة في صدورهم من الله( (الحشر: 13) الآية. فأحال قلة خوفهم من الله واستعظامهم سطوة الخلق على قلة الفقه فانظر إن كان ذلك نتيجة عدم الحفظ لتفريعات الفتاوى أو هو نتيجة عدم ما ذكرناه من العلوم
59:13.english: Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, you are more feared in their chests (hearts) than Allah' (Al-Hashr: 13) the verse. So He attributed their lack of fear from Allah and their magnification of the might of creation to lack of understanding (Fiqh). So consider whether that is the result of not memorizing the subdivisions of legal opinions (Fatāwā) or it is the result of lacking what we have mentioned of the sciences.
59:13.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

59:16.arabic: فأتاه الشيطان فقال أنا الذي خنقتها وأنا الذي ألقيت في قلوب أهلها فأطعني تنج وأخلصك منهم قال بماذا قال اسجد لي سجدتين فسجد له سجدتين فقال له الشيطان إني برىء منك فهو الذي قال الله تعالى فيه كمثل الشيطان إذ قال للإنسان اكفر فلما كفر قال إني بريء منك[55] فانظر الآن إلى حيله واضطراره الراهب إلى هذه الكبائر وكل ذلك لطاعته له في قبول الجارية للمعالجة وهو أمر هين وربما يظن صاحبه أنه خير وحسنة فيحسن ذلك في قلبه بخفي الهوى فيقدم عليه كالراغب في الخير فيخرج الأمر بعد ذلك عن اختياره ويجره البعض إلى البعض ب
59:16.english: Then the Devil (Shaytan) came to him and said: 'I am the one who strangled her, and I am the one who cast into the hearts of her family. So obey me, you will be saved and I will deliver you from them.' He said: 'With what?' He said: 'Prostrate to me two prostrations.' So he prostrated to him two prostrations. Then the Devil (Shaytan) said to him: 'I am free from you.' He is the one about whom Allah the Exalted said: 'Like the example of the Devil (Shaytan) when he said to the human: Disbelieve. So when he disbelieved, he said: Indeed, I am free from you.' [55] So look now at his tricks and his forcing the monk to these major sins, and all of that for his obedience to him in accepting the slave girl for treatment, and it is a trivial matter, and perhaps its doer thinks that it is good and a good deed, so it becomes pleasing in his heart (Qalb) by the hidden desire (Hawa), so he proceeds upon it like one desiring good, then the matter after that goes beyond his choice, and it drags some to some until he finds no escape. So we seek refuge with Allah from wasting the beginnings of matters, and to it is the indication by his saying, peace be upon him: 'Whoever hovers around the forbidden area, he is about to fall into it.' [56].
59:16.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

59:16.arabic: وإنما الفضل والثواب الجزيل في تركه خوفاً من الله تعالى مع القدرة وارتفاع الموانع وتيسر الأسباب، لا سيما عند صدق الشهوة وهذه درجة الصديقين. ولذلك قال ﭬ "من عشق فعف فكتم فمات فهو شهيد"[69] وقال ﭬ "سبعة يظلمهم الله يوم القيامة في ظل عرشه يوم لا ظل إلا ظله - وعد منهم" رجل دعته امرأة ذات جمال وحسب إلى نفسها فقال إني أخاف الله رب العالمين"[70] وقصة يوسف عليه السلام وامتناعه من زليخا مع القدرة ومع رغبتها معروفة، وقد أثنى الله تعالى عليه بذلك في كتابه العزيز، وهو إمام لكل من وفق لمجاهدة الشيطان في هذه ا
59:16.english: And indeed the virtue and great reward is in abandoning it out of fear of Allah (The Exalted) with capability and removal of obstacles and facilitation of means, especially at the time of genuine desire (Shahwah), and this is the rank of the Truthful Ones (Al-Siddiqin). Therefore, he (the Prophet) said: 'Whoever loves then remains chaste then conceals then dies, he is a martyr.' And he said: 'Seven whom Allah will shade on the Day of Resurrection under the shade of His Throne on a day when there is no shade except His shade - among them is' a man whom a woman of beauty and lineage invited to herself, so he said: 'Indeed I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds.' And the story of Yusuf (upon him be peace) and his refusal from Zulaykha with capability and with her desire is known, and Allah (The Exalted) praised him for that in His Noble Book, and he is an Imam (leader) for everyone who is granted success in struggling against the Satan (Shaytan) in this great desire (Shahwah). Then Allah (The Exalted) said: 'Like the example of the Satan (Shaytan) when he said to the human: Disbelieve! Then when he disbelieved, he said: Indeed I am free from you; indeed I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds.' So Allah (The Exalted) likened the Satan (Shaytan) to the woman who invites to immorality then absolves herself from the invited one when he falls into sin, just as the Satan (Shaytan) invites the human to disbelief then absolves himself from him when he disbelieves, and this is an eloquent similitude in warning against following forbidden desires (Shahawat).
59:16.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Harms of the Tongue'

59:16.arabic: حديث كان راهب في بني إسرائيل فأخذ الشيطان جارية فخنقها وألقى في قلوب أهلها أن دواءها عند الراهب الحديث بطوله في قوله تعالى كمثل الشيطان إذ قال للإنسان اكفر رواه ابن أبي الدنيا في مكايد الشيطان وابن مردويه في تفسيره في حديث عبيد بن أبي رفاعة مرسلا وللحاكم نحوه موقوفا على علي بن أبي طالب وقال صحيح الإسناد ووصله بطين في مسنده من حديث علي
59:16.english: Hadith: There was a monk among the Children of Israel, then the Devil (Shaytan) took a young girl and strangled her, and cast into the hearts of her family that her cure was with the monk. The hadith in its length is in His saying, the Exalted: 'Like the example of the Devil (Shaytan) when he said to the human, disbelieve (kufr).' Narrated by Ibn Abi al-Dunya in 'The Stratagems of the Devil (Makayid al-Shaytan)' and Ibn Mardawayh in his Tafsir (interpretation) in the hadith of 'Ubayd ibn Abi Rafa'ah as mursal (interrupted chain), and al-Hakim has something similar as mawquf (attributed to a companion) on 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, and he said: 'Its chain is authentic (sahih al-isnad),' and he connected it with al-Tayalisi in his Musnad from the hadith of 'Ali.
59:16.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

59:18.arabic: المرابطة الثالثة محاسبة النفس بعد العمل ولنذكر فضيلة المحاسبة ثم حقيقتها أما الفضيلة فقد قال الله تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله ولتنظر نفس ما قدمت لغد وهذه إشارة إلى المحاسبة على ما مضى من الأعمال ولذلك قال عمر رضى الله تعالى عنه حاسبوا أنفسكم قبل أن تحاسبوا وزنوها قبل أن توزنوا وفي الخبر انه عليه السلام جاءه رجل فقال يا رسول الله أوصنى فقال أمستوص أنت فقال نعم قال إذا هممت بأمر فتتدبر عاقبته فإن كان رشدا فامضه وإن كان غيا فانته عنه وفي الخبر وينبغى للعاقل أن يكون له أربع ساعات ساعة يحاسب
59:18.english: The third spiritual station (Marabata) is the accounting of the Soul (Nafs) after the action. And let us mention the virtue of accounting, then its reality. As for the virtue, Allah the Exalted has said: 'O you who have believed, fear Allah (Taqwa) and let every Soul (Nafs) look at what it has put forth for tomorrow.' And this is an indication to the accounting for what has passed of deeds. And for that reason, Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: 'Account your souls before you are accounted, and weigh them before they are weighed.' And in the report, that upon him be peace, a man came to him and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, advise me.' He said: 'Are you seeking advice?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'When you intend a matter, then consider its consequence; if it is guidance (Rushd), then proceed with it, and if it is error (Ghayy), then desist from it.' And in the report: 'And it behooves the intelligent one to have four hours: an hour in which he accounts his soul.' And He the Exalted said: 'And turn in repentance (Tawbah) to Allah all together, O you who believe, that you may succeed.' And repentance (Tawbah) is looking at the action after finishing it with regret (Nadam) over it. And he, peace be upon him, said: 'Indeed, I seek forgiveness from Allah the Exalted and repent (Atubu) to Him one hundred times a day.' The report: 'Indeed, I seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Him one hundred times a day' has preceded more than once. And He the Exalted said: 'Indeed, those who fear Allah (Taqwa), when an impulse from Satan touches them, they remember (Tadhakkuru), then at once they are seeing clearly.' And from Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he would strike his feet with a whip when night covered him and say to his soul: 'What have you done today?' And from Maymun ibn Mihran that he said: 'The servant does not become from those who fear Allah (Al-Muttaqin) until he accounts his soul more severely than the accounting of his partner, and the two partners account each other after the action.' And it is narrated from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that Abu Bakr, may Allah's pleasure be upon him, said to her: '...'
59:18.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

59:18.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
59:18.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Whatever is in the Quran of 'O you who have believed' is in the Torah 'O you poor ones (al-Masakin)'.
59:18.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

59:19.arabic: وأنه أمر رباني وحنينه إلى جواب الرب تعالى له طبعي ذاتي، إلا أن يصرفه عن مقتضى طبعه عوارض العالم الغريب من ذاته فينسى عند ذلك نفسه وربه. ومهما فعل ذلك فقد ظلم نفسه إذ قيل له "ولا تكونوا كالذين نسوا الله فأنساهم أنفسهم أولئك هم الفاسقون" أي الخارجون عن مقتضى طبعهم ومظنة استحقاقهم. يقال: فسقت الرطبة عن كمامها؛ إذا خرجت عن معدنها الفطري. وهذه إشارة إلى أسرار يهتز لاستنشاق روائحها العارفون وتشمئز من سماع ألفاظها القاصرون فإنهم تضر بهم كما تضر رياح الورد بالجعل، وتبهر أعينهم الضعيفة كما تبهر الشمس أبص
59:19.english: And it is a divine command (Amr Rabbani) and its yearning for the response of the Lord, the Exalted, is natural and intrinsic, except that it is diverted from the requirement of its nature by the alien occurrences of the world from its essence, so it forgets at that time itself and its Lord. And whenever it does that, it has wronged itself, as it is said to it: "And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves. Those are the defiantly disobedient (Al-Fasiqun)" meaning those who have exited from the requirement of their nature and the place of their deserving. It is said: The moist date (Al-Rutbah) has exited (Fasaqat) from its sheath (Kummaha); when it has exited from its natural mine. And this is an allusion to secrets that the knowers (Al-Arifun) tremble at inhaling their fragrances, and the deficient ones recoil from hearing their words, for they harm them just as the winds of the rose harm the beetle, and dazzle their weak eyes just as the sun dazzles the eyes of bats.
59:19.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

59:19.arabic: ومن لم يعرف قلبه ليراقبه ويراعيه ويترصد لما يلوح من خزائن الملكوت عليه وفيه فهو ممن قال الله تعالى فيه نسوا الله فأنساهم أنفسهم أولئك هم الفاسقون فمعرفة القلب وحقيقة أوصافه أصل الدين وأساس طريق السالكين
59:19.english: And whoever does not know his Heart (Qalb) to observe it, guard it, and watch for what appears from the treasures of the Dominion (Malakūt) upon it and within it, he is among those about whom Allah the Exalted said: 'They forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves; those are the defiantly disobedient (Fāsiqūn).' So knowledge of the Heart (Qalb) and the reality of its attributes is the foundation of the Religion (Dīn) and the basis of the path of the travelers (Sālikīn).
59:19.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

59:21.arabic: فإن قلت فما بال هؤلاء لا يظهر وجدهم عند سماع القرآن وهو كلام الله ويظهر عند الغناء وهو كلام الشعراء فلو كان ذلك حقا من لطف الله تعالى ولم يكن باطلا من غرور الشيطان لكان القرآن أولى به من الغناء فنقول الوجد الحق هو ما ينشأ من فرط حب الله تعالى وصدق إرادته والشوق إلى لقائه وذلك يهيج بسماع القرآن أيضا وإنما الذي لا يهيج بسماع القرآن حب الخلق وعشق المخلوق ويدل على ذلك قوله تعالى ألا بذكر الله تطمئن القلوب وقوله تعالى مثاني تقشعر منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم ثم تلين جلودهم وقلوبهم إلى ذكر الله وكل ما يو
59:21.english: If you say: Why do these people not manifest spiritual state (Wajd) upon hearing the Quran, which is the Speech (Kalam) of Allah, while they manifest it upon hearing singing, which is the speech of poets? If that were truly from the grace (Lutf) of Allah the Exalted and not falsehood from the deception (Ghurur) of Satan, then the Quran would be more deserving of it than singing. We say: The true spiritual state (Wajd) is what arises from excessive love (Hubb) of Allah the Exalted and sincerity (Sidq) of His intention (Iradah) and longing (Shawq) for meeting Him, and that is also stirred by hearing the Quran. Rather, what is not stirred by hearing the Quran is love (Hubb) of creation and passion (Ishaq) for the created. Evidence for that is His saying the Exalted: 'Indeed, in the remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah do hearts find rest (Tatma'innu).' And His saying the Exalted: 'Verses (Mathani) at which the skins of those who fear their Lord shiver (Taqsha'irru), then their skins and their hearts soften (Talinna) at the remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah.' And everything that occurs in the soul (Nafs) following hearing is spiritual state (Wajd). So tranquility (Tuma'ninah), shivering (Iqsha'irrar), fear (Khashyah), and softening (Layn) of the heart (Qalb) - all of that is spiritual state (Wajd). And Allah the Exalted has said: 'The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble (Wajilat).' And He said: 'Had We sent down this Quran upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled (Khashia'an), split asunder (Mutassadi'an) from fear (Khashyah) of Allah.' So trembling (Wajal) and humility (Khashu') are spiritual state (Wajd) from the category of states (Ahwal), even if not from the category of unveilings (Mukashafat), but they may become a cause for unveilings (Mukashafat) and alerts (Tanbihat).
59:21.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

59:21.arabic: حديث فضل خمس آيات من أول الحديد ذكر أبو القاسم الغافقي في فضائل القرآن من حديث علي إذا أردت أن تسأل الله حاجة فاقرأ خمس آيات من أول سورة الحديد إلى قوله عليم بذات الصدور ومن آخر سورة الحشر من قوله لو أنزلنا هذا القرآن على جبل إلى آخر السورة ثم تقول يا من هو كذا افعل بي كذا وتدعو بما تريد.
59:21.english: The narration regarding the virtue of five verses from the beginning of Al-Hadid (The Iron) - Abu Al-Qasim Al-Ghafiqi mentioned in the virtues of the Quran from the narration of Ali: 'If you wish to ask Allah for a need, then recite five verses from the beginning of Surah Al-Hadid up to His saying: 'All-Knowing of what is in the breasts (Alim bi-dhat al-sudur)' and from the end of Surah Al-Hashr (The Gathering) from His saying: 'Had We sent down this Quran upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and split asunder from the fear of Allah (Law anzalna hadha al-qur'ana 'ala jabalin la-ra'aytahu khashi'an mutasaddi'an min khashyati Allah). And these examples We present to the people that they might give thought (wa tilka al-amthalu nadribuha lil-nasi la'allahum yatafakkarun).' Then you say: 'O He who is such-and-such, do with me such-and-such' and supplicate with what you desire.
59:21.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Book of Knowledge'

59:22.arabic: وإلى الله فقيرا وعلى الله متكلا وإلى الله منيبا أشهد الله وأشهد ملائكته وأنبيائه ورسله وحملة عرشه ومن خَلقه ومن هو خالقه بأنه هو الله الذي لا إله إلا هو وحده لا شريك له وأن محمدا عبده ورسوله ﭬ وأن الجنة حق وأن النار حق والحوض حق والشفاعة حق ومنكرا ونكيرا حق ووعدك حق ووعيدك حق ولقاءك حق والساعة آتية لا ريب فيها وأن الله يبعث من في القبور على ذلك أحيا وعليه أموت وعليه أبعث إن شاء الله اللهم أنت ربي لا إله إلا أنت خلقتني وأنا عبدك وأنا على عهدك ووعدك ما استطعت أعوذ بك اللهم من شر ما صنعت ومن شر كل
59:22.english: And to Allah poor (Faqir) and upon Allah reliant (Mutakkil) and to Allah returning (Munib). I bear witness to Allah and I bear witness to His angels, His prophets, His messengers, the bearers of His Throne, and from His creation and from He who is its Creator, that He is Allah, there is no god except Him alone, no partner to Him, and that Muhammad is His servant and His messenger, and that Paradise is true, and that the Fire is true, and the Pool is true, and intercession is true, and Munkar and Nakir are true, and Your promise is true, and Your threat is true, and meeting You is true, and the Hour is coming, no doubt in it, and that Allah will resurrect those in the graves. Upon that I live, and upon it I die, and upon it I will be resurrected, if Allah wills. O Allah, You are my Lord, there is no god except You, You created me and I am Your servant, and I am upon Your covenant and Your promise as much as I am able. I seek refuge in You, O Allah, from the evil of what I have done and from the evil of every possessor of evil. O Allah, indeed I have wronged my soul (Nafs), so forgive me my sins, for indeed none forgives sins except You. And guide me to the best of character traits (Akhlaq), for indeed none guides to the best of them except You. And turn away from me the bad of them, for indeed none turns away the bad of them except You. At Your service and Your aid, and all good is in Your hands. I am Yours and to You I seek forgiveness and I repent to You. I have believed, O Allah, in what You have sent of a messenger, and I have believed, O Allah, in what You have revealed of a Book. And may Allah send prayers upon Muhammad, the unlettered Prophet, and upon his family and grant abundant peace. The seal of my speech and its key, and upon His prophets and His messengers all. Amen, O Lord of the worlds. O Allah, cause us to arrive at the Pool of Muhammad and give us to drink from his cup a drink, plentiful, pleasant, delightful, after which we will never thirst forever.
