And gather us in his company, not disgraced, nor breaking the covenant, nor doubting, nor afflicted by trials (Fitnah), nor those upon whom is anger, nor astray. O Allah, protect me from the trials (Fitnah) of the world and grant me success in what You love.
59:22.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

59:23.arabic: وإلى الله فقيرا وعلى الله متكلا وإلى الله منيبا أشهد الله وأشهد ملائكته وأنبيائه ورسله وحملة عرشه ومن خلقه ومن هو خالقه بأنه هو الله الذي لا إله إلا هو وحده لا شريك له وأن محمدا عبده ورسوله ﭬ وأن الجنة حق وأن النار حق والحوض حق والشفاعة حق ومنكرا ونكيرا حق ووعدك حق ووعيدك حق ولقاءك حق والساعة آتية لا ريب فيها وأن الله يبعث من في القبور على ذلك أحيا وعليه أموت وعليه أبعث إن شاء الله
59:23.english: And to Allah poor, and upon Allah reliant, and to Allah repentant. I bear witness to Allah and I bear witness to His angels, His prophets, His messengers, the bearers of His Throne, and from His creation and from He who is His Creator, that He is Allah who there is no god except Him alone, no partner to Him, and that Muhammad is His servant and His messenger, and that Paradise is true, and that the Fire is true, and the Basin is true, and intercession is true, and Munkar and Nakir are true, and Your promise is true, and Your threat is true, and meeting You is true, and the Hour is coming, no doubt in it, and that Allah will resurrect those in the graves. Upon that I live, and upon that I die, and upon that I will be resurrected, if Allah wills.
59:23.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter

59:24.arabic: وما يتعلق بالرب تعالى إما ان يكون نظرا في ذاته وصفاته وأسمائه الحسنى وإما أن يكون في أفعاله وملكه وملكوته وجميع ما في السموات والأرض وما بينهما
59:24.english: And what pertains to the Lord (Rabb) the Exalted is either a consideration of His Essence (Dhat) and His Attributes (Sifat) and His Beautiful Names (Asma' al-Husna), or it is in His Actions (Af'al) and His Dominion (Mulk) and His Sovereignty (Malakut) and all that is in the heavens and the earth and what is between them.
59:24.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Contemplation'

60:1.arabic: وأما الانبساط معه والاسترسال إليه كما يسترسل إلى الأصدقاء فهو مكروه كراهة شديدة يكاد ينتهي ما يقوى منها إلى حد التحريم قال تعالى لا تجد قوما يؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر يوادون من حاد الله ورسوله ولو كانوا آباءهم أو أبناءهم الآية وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم المسلم والمشرك لا تتراءى ناراهما حديث المؤمن والمشرك لا تتراءى ناراهما رواه أبو داود والترمذي من حديث جرير أنا بريء من كل مسلم يقيم بين أظهر المشركين قالوا يا رسول الله ولم قال لا تراءى ناراهما رواه النسائي مرسلا وقال البخاري الصحيح أنه مرسل وقال عز
60:1.english: And as for being expansive with him and freely conversing with him as one converses freely with friends, it is disliked with a severe dislike that almost reaches the limit of prohibition. Allah the Exalted said: 'You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers or their sons...' the verse. And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'The Muslim and the polytheist - their fires should not be visible to one another.' The hadith: 'The believer and the polytheist - their fires should not be visible to one another' was narrated by Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Jarir: 'I am free from every Muslim who resides among the polytheists.' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, why?' He said: 'Their fires should not be visible to one another.' It was narrated by al-Nasa'i as mursal, and al-Bukhari said the authentic is that it is mursal. And Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: 'O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies...' the verse.
60:1.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

60:1.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
60:1.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'What is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)".'
60:1.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

60:4.arabic: رضيت بالله ربا وبالإسلام دينا وبمحمد ﭬ نبيا ﴿ ربنا عليك توكلنا وإليك أنبنا وإليك المصير ﴾ {}[237] وإذا أمسى قال ذلك إلا أنه يقول أمسينا ويقول مع ذلك أعوذ بكلمات الله التامات وأسمائه كلها من شر ما ذرأ وبرأ ومن شر كل ذي شر ومن شر كل دابة أنت آخذ بناصيتها إن ربي على صراط مستقيم[238]
60:4.english: I am pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad (peace be upon him) as prophet. 'Our Lord, upon You we have relied, and to You we have turned, and to You is the final destination.' And when evening comes, he says that except he says 'we have entered evening' and says with that: 'I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah and all His names from the evil of what He has created and brought forth, and from the evil of every possessor of evil, and from the evil of every creature whose forelock You take hold of; indeed my Lord is upon a straight path.'
60:4.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

60:7.arabic: وينبغي أن لا يبالغ في البغضة عند الوقيعة قال الله تعالى عسى الله أن يجعل بينكم وبين الذين عاديتم منهم مودة و قال عليه السلام أحبب حبيبك هونا ما عسى أن يكون بغيضك يوما ما وأبغض بغيضك هونا ما عسى أن يكون حبيبك يوما ما
60:7.english: And it is necessary that one should not exaggerate in hatred during enmity. Allah the Exalted said: 'Perhaps Allah will place between you and those whom you have been enemies among them affection.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Love your beloved moderately, for perhaps he may become your enemy one day; and hate your enemy moderately, for perhaps he may become your beloved one day.'
60:7.topic: Al-Ghazali on the outer and inner dimensions of worship, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

60:10.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
60:10.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'What is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (Masakin)"'.
60:10.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

60:13.arabic: ومهما تراكمت الذنوب طبع على القلوب وعند ذلك يعمى القلب عن إدراك الحق وصلاح الدين ويستهين بأمر الآخرة ويستعظم أمر الدنيا ويصير مقصور الهم عليها فإذا قرع سمعه أمر الآخرة وما فيها من الأخطار دخل من أذن وخرج من أذن ولم يستقر في القلب ولم يحركه إلى التوبة والتدارك أولئك يئسوا من الآخرة كما يئس الكفار من أصحاب القبور وهذا هو معنى اسوداد القلب بالذنوب كما نطق به القرآن والسنة
60:13.english: And whenever sins accumulate, a seal (Taba') is placed upon the hearts (Qulub), and at that point the heart (Qalb) becomes blind to perceiving the truth (Haqq) and the rectification of religion (Deen), and it belittles the matter of the Hereafter (Akhirah) and magnifies the matter of the world (Dunya), and its concern becomes restricted to it. So when the matter of the Hereafter (Akhirah) and what it contains of dangers strikes his hearing, it enters from one ear and exits from the other, and it does not settle in the heart (Qalb) and does not move him to repentance (Tawbah) and rectification. Those have despaired of the Hereafter (Akhirah) as the disbelievers (Kuffar) have despaired of the companions of the graves. And this is the meaning of the blackening of the heart (Qalb) by sins as the Quran and Sunnah have articulated.
60:13.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

60:13.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
60:13.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'Whatever is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (Masakin)".'
60:13.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

61:2.arabic: وأما الآيات التي استدلوا بها فهو إنكار عليهم من حيث تركهم المعروف لا من حيث أمرهم ولكن أمرهم دل على قوة علمهم وعقاب العالم أشد لأنه لا عذر له مع قوة علمه وقوله تعالى لم تقولون ما لا تفعلون المراد به الوعد الكاذب وقوله عز وجل وتنسون انفسكم إنكار من حيث إنهم نسوا أنفسهم لا من حيث إنهم أمروا غيرهم ولكن ذكر أمر الغير استدلالا به على علمهم وتأكيدا للحجة عليهم
61:2.english: As for the verses they cited as evidence, it is a rebuke against them for abandoning the recognized good (Ma'ruf), not for commanding others. But their commanding others indicates the strength of their knowledge, and the punishment of the knowledgeable one is more severe because he has no excuse with the strength of his knowledge. And His saying, the Exalted: 'Why do you say what you do not do?' (Quran 61:2) - the intended meaning is the false promise. And His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And you forget yourselves' - it is a rebuke from the perspective that they forgot themselves, not from the perspective that they commanded others. But mentioning the commanding of others serves as evidence of their knowledge and as confirmation of the argument against them.
61:2.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

61:2.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
61:2.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'What is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)".'
61:2.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

61:3.arabic: ومنها أن لا يخالف فعله قوله بل لا يأمر بالشيء ما لم يكن هو أول عامل به قال الله تعالى: (أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم( (البقرة: 44) وقال تعالى: (كبر مقتا عند الله أن تقولوا ما لا تفعلون( (الصف: 3) وقال تعالى في قصة شعيب: (وما أريد أن أخالفكم إلى ما أنهاكم عنه( (هود: 88) وقال تعالى: (واتقوا الله ويعلمكم الله( (البقرة: 282) وقال تعالى: (واتقوا الله واعلموا( (البقرة: 194) (واتقوا الله واسمعوا( (المائدة: 108). وقال تعالى لعيسى عليه السلام: ((يا ابن مريم عظ نفسك فإن اتعظت فعظ الناس وإلا فاستحي من
61:3.english: And from them is that his action does not contradict his speech, rather he does not command something unless he is the first doer of it. Allah the Exalted said: 'Do you enjoin righteousness upon people while you forget yourselves?' (Al-Baqarah: 44). And He the Exalted said: 'Great is hatred (maktan) in the sight of Allah that you say what you do not do' (As-Saff: 3). And He the Exalted said in the story of Shu'ayb: 'And I do not intend to differ from you to that which I forbid you' (Hud: 88). And He the Exalted said: 'And fear (ittaqū) Allah and Allah will teach you' (Al-Baqarah: 282). And He the Exalted said: 'And fear (ittaqū) Allah and know' (Al-Baqarah: 194). 'And fear (ittaqū) Allah and listen' (Al-Ma'idah: 108). And He the Exalted said to 'Isa, peace be upon him: 'O son of Maryam, admonish yourself; if you are admonished, then admonish people, otherwise be ashamed before Me.' And the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'On the night I was taken on the night journey (isrā'), I passed by people whose lips were being cut with scissors of fire. I said: Who are you? They said: We used to command good and not do it, and forbid evil and do it.' [158].
61:3.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

61:3.arabic: فإن لم يكن بهذه الصفات ولم يتردد قلبه بين هذه الحالات كان حظه من التلاوة حركة اللسان مع صريح اللعن على نفسه في قوله تعالى ﴿ ألا لعنة الله على الظالمين ﴾ {} وفي قوله تعالى ﴿ كبر مقتا عند الله أن تقولوا ما لا تفعلون ﴾ {} وفي قوله عز وجل -﴿ وهم في غفلة معرضون ﴾ {} وفي قوله ﴿ فأعرض عمن تولى عن ذكرنا ولم يرد إلا الحياة الدنيا ﴾ {} وفي قوله تعالى ﴿ ومن لم يتب فأولئك هم الظالمون ﴾ {} إلى غير ذلك من الآيات وكان داخلا في معنى قوله عز وجل ﴿ ومنهم أميون لا يعلمون الكتاب إلا أمانيّ ﴾ {} يعني التلاوة المجردة
61:3.english: If he does not possess these qualities and his heart (Qalb) does not fluctuate between these states, his share of recitation is merely the movement of the tongue with explicit curse upon himself in the saying of Allah the Exalted: 'Indeed, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers' and in His saying: 'Great is hatred (Māqit) in the sight of Allah that you say what you do not do' and in His saying the Mighty and Majestic: 'And they are in heedlessness turning away' and in His saying: 'So turn away from whoever turns away from Our Remembrance (Dhikr) and desires not except the worldly life' and in His saying the Exalted: 'And whoever does not repent - then those are the wrongdoers' and other similar verses, and he falls within the meaning of His saying the Mighty and Majestic: 'And among them are unlettered ones who do not know the Scripture except [their] wishful thinking' meaning mere recitation.
61:3.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

61:3.arabic: وأما الشرط الثالث وهو العدالة فقد اعتبرها قوم وقالوا ليس للفاسق أن يحتسب وربما استدلوا فيه بالنكير الوارد على من يأمر بما لا يفعله مثل قوله تعالى أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون انفسكم وقوله تعالى كبر مقتا عند الله أن تقولوا ما لا تفعلون وبما روى عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم انه قال مررت ليلة اسرى بي بقوم تقرض شفاههم بمقاريض من نار فقلت من انتم فقالوا كنا نامر بالخير ولا ناتيه وننهى عن الشر وناتيه حديث مررت ليلة أسري بي بقوم تقرض شفاههم بمقاريض من نارالحديث تقدم في العلم وبما روى أن الله تعالى أوح
61:3.english: As for the third condition, which is righteousness (Adalah), some people have considered it and said: 'The sinner (Fasiq) cannot perform enjoining good and forbidding evil (Ihtisab).' And perhaps they argued for this with the rebuke directed at those who command what they do not do, such as His saying, the Exalted: 'Do you enjoin righteousness upon people and forget yourselves?' and His saying, the Exalted: 'Great is hatred (Maqt) in the sight of Allah that you say what you do not do.' And with what was narrated from the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, that he said: 'On the night I was taken on the journey (Isra), I passed by a people whose lips were being cut with scissors of fire. I said: Who are you? They said: We used to enjoin good and not do it, and we used to forbid evil and do it.' The hadith of 'I passed by a people whose lips were being cut with scissors of fire on the night I was taken on the journey' was previously mentioned in the Book of Knowledge. And with what was narrated that Allah, the Exalted, revealed to Jesus, peace be upon him: 'Admonish yourself; if you are admonished, then admonish people; otherwise, be ashamed before Me.' And perhaps they argued through analogy (Qiyas) that guiding others is a branch of being guided, and likewise, rectifying others is a branch of being upright, and reform (Islah) is a purification (Zakat) from the standard (Nisab) of righteousness. So how can one who is not righteous in himself reform others? And when will the shadow be straight if the stick is crooked? All that they mentioned are illusions, and the truth is that the sinner (Fasiq) can perform enjoining good and forbidding evil (Ihtisab). Its proof is that we say: Is it a condition for enjoining good and forbidding evil (Ihtisab) that its practitioner be infallible (Ma'sum) from all sins? If that is a condition, then it is a breach of consensus (Ijma'), then it seals the door of enjoining good and forbidding evil (Ihtisab), for there is no infallibility (Ismah) for the Companions, let alone those below them, and the Prophets, peace be upon them, have differed regarding their infallibility (Ismah) from errors, and the Noble Quran indicates the attribution of Adam, peace be upon him, to sin (Ma'siyah), and likewise a group of the Prophets. For this reason, Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: 'If only one who has no sin in him enjoins good and forbids evil...'
61:3.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil'

61:4.arabic: اعلم أن شواهد القرآن متظاهرة على أن الله تعالى يحب عبده فلا بد من معرفة معنى ذلك. ولنقدم الشواهد على محبته فقد قال الله تعالى: " يحبهم ويحبونه " وقال تعالى: " إن الله يحب الذين يقاتلون في سبيله صفاً " وقال تعالى: " إن الله يحب التوابين ويحب المتطهرين " ولذلك رد سبحانه على من ادعى أنه حبيب الله فقال: " قل فلم يعذبكم بذنوبكم ".
61:4.english: Know that the evidences of the Quran are abundant in showing that Allah the Exalted loves His servant, so it is necessary to know the meaning of that. And let us present the evidences of His love, for Allah the Exalted has said: "He loves them and they love Him" and He said: "Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in ranks" and He said: "Indeed, Allah loves those who repent and He loves those who purify themselves." And for that reason, He the Glorious refuted those who claimed to be the beloved of Allah by saying: "Say, then why does He punish you for your sins?"
61:4.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

61:4.arabic: وقد شرط الله سبحانه لحقيقته الصدق في الحب القتل في سبيل الله، حيث قالوا إنا نحب الله فجعل القتل في سبيل الله وطلب الشهادة علامته فقال تعالى: " إن الله يحب الذين يقاتلون في سبيله صفاً " وقال عز وجل: " يقاتلون في سبيل الله فيقتلون ويقتلون ".
61:4.english: And Allah, may He be exalted, has stipulated for its reality the truthfulness in love the killing in the path of Allah, when they said 'Indeed we love Allah' so He made the killing in the path of Allah and seeking martyrdom its sign. He said, the Exalted: "Indeed Allah loves those who fight in His path in ranks" and He said, the Mighty and Majestic: "They fight in the path of Allah so they kill and are killed."
61:4.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

61:5.arabic: فغنائمه دائمة غير ممنوعة وثمراته متزايدة غير مقطوعة إلا إذا بدا للمسافر فترة في سفره ووقفة في حركته فإن الله لا يغير ما بقوم حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم وإذا زاغوا أزاغ الله قلوبهم وما الله بظلام للعبيد ولكنهم يظلمون أنفسهم
61:5.english: Its spoils are permanent, not prohibited, and its fruits are increasing, not cut off, except if a period appears for the traveler in his journey and a pause in his movement. For Allah does not change what is with a people until they change what is with their souls (Anfus). And when they deviate (zāghū), Allah deviates (azāgha) their hearts (Qulūb). And Allah is not unjust to the servants, but they wrong their own souls (Anfus).
61:5.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Travel'

61:6.arabic: العمى ويجعله بصيراً: ألا  إنه  من  رغب في الدنيا وطال أمله فيها أعمى الله قلبه على قدر ذلك، ومن زهد في الدنيا  وقصر فيها أمله أعطاه الله علماً بغير تعلم، وهدى بغير هداية: ألا  أنه  سيكون  بعدكم قوم لا يستقيم لهم الملك إلا بالقتل والتجبر، ولا  الغنى  إلا  بالفخر  والبخل، ولا المحبة إلا باتباع الهوى؛ إلا فمن أدرك ذلك الزمان  منكم  فصبر  على  الفقر وهو يقدر على الغنى، وصبر على البغضاء وهو يقدر على المحبة، وصبر على الذل  وهو يقدر على العز لا يريد  بذلك  إلا  وجه  الله  تعالى  أعطاه  الله  ثواب  خمسي
61:6.english: Blindness and He makes him seeing: Indeed, whoever desires the worldly life and prolongs his hope in it, Allah blinds his heart (Qalb) according to that measure, and whoever renounces the worldly life and shortens his hope in it, Allah gives him knowledge without learning, and guidance without guidance: Indeed, there will be after you a people for whom authority will not be established except through killing and tyranny, nor wealth except through pride and miserliness, nor love except by following desire; except whoever among you reaches that time and endures poverty while capable of wealth, and endures enmity while capable of love, and endures humiliation while capable of honor, desiring by that only the Face of Allah the Exalted, Allah will give him the reward of fifty truthful ones."[19] And it is narrated that Jesus, peace be upon him, was severely afflicted by rain, thunder, and lightning one day, so he sought something to take refuge in, and his eye fell on a tent from afar, so he went to it, and behold, there was a woman in it, so he turned away from it, and behold, he was at a cave in a mountain, so he went to it, and behold, there was a lion in it, so he placed his hand on it and said: My God, You have made for everything a refuge and have not made for me a refuge, so Allah the Exalted revealed to him: Your refuge is in the abode of My mercy, I will marry you on the Day of Resurrection to a hundred houris whom I created with My hand, and I will feed at your wedding for four thousand years, a day of which is like the lifespan of the worldly life, and I will command a caller to call: Where are the renouncers of the worldly life? Visit the wedding of the renouncer of the worldly life, Jesus son of Mary. And Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him, said: Woe to the possessor of the worldly life, how he dies and leaves it and what is in it, and it deceives him and he feels secure in it, and he trusts it and it betrays him, and woe to the deceived, how I show them what they dislike and separate them from what they love and bring them what they are promised? And woe to him whose concern is the worldly life and whose action is sins, how he will be exposed tomorrow by his sin? And it is said Allah the Exalted revealed to Moses, peace be upon him: O Moses, what is with you and the abode of the wrongdoers? Indeed, it is not an abode for you, remove from it your concern and separate from it with your intellect, so wretched is the abode except for a worker who works in it, then excellent is the abode it is, O Moses, I am lying in wait for the wrongdoer until I take from him for the wronged." And it is narrated that the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, sent Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, and he came with wealth from Bahrain; and the Ansar heard of Abu Ubaydah's arrival, so they met for the Fajr prayer with the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, and when the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, prayed, he turned away, and they presented themselves to him, so the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, smiled when he saw them and then said: "I think you have heard that Abu Ubaydah has arrived with something." They said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: "Then receive good news and hope for what pleases you, for by Allah, it is not poverty I fear for you, but I fear for you that the worldly life will be spread out for you as it was spread out for those before you, and you compete for it as they competed for it, and it destroys you as it destroyed them."[20] And Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed, the most I fear for you is what Allah brings out for you from the blessings of the earth." So it was said.
61:6.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of the World'

61:6.arabic: ورأيت في الإنجيل قال عيسى بن مريم عليه السلام لقد قيل لكم من قبل إن السن بالسن والأنف بالأنف وأنا أقول لكم لا تقاوموا بالشر بل من ضرب خدك الأيمن فحول إليه الخد الأيسر ومن اخذ رداءك فاعطه ازارك ومن سخرك لتسير معه ميلا فسر معه ميلين وكل ذلك أمر بالصبر على الاذى، فالصبر على اذى الناس من أعلى مراتب الصبر لانه يتعاون فيه باعث الدين وباعث الشهوة والغضب جميعا.
61:6.english: And I saw in the Gospel, Jesus son of Mary (peace be upon him) said: 'It was said to you before: an eye for an eye and a nose for a nose, but I say to you: do not resist evil, but whoever strikes your right cheek, turn to him the left cheek, and whoever takes your cloak, give him your garment, and whoever compels you to go one mile, go with him two miles.' And all of that is a command for patience (Sabr) upon harm, for patience (Sabr) upon the harm of people is from the highest levels of patience (Sabr) because in it the motivator of religion (Deen) and the motivator of desire (Shahwah) and anger (Ghadab) all cooperate.
61:6.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

61:10.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
61:10.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'What is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)".'
61:10.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

61:12.arabic: [223] حديث سئل عن قوله تعالى - ومساكن طيبة فى جنات عدن - قال قصور من لؤلؤ الحديث أخرجه أبو الشيخ ابن حبان فى كتاب العظمة والآجرى فى كتاب النصيحة من رواية الحسن بن خليفة عن الحسن قال سألت أبا هريرة وعمران بن حصين فى هذه الآية ولا يصح والحسن ابن خليفة لم يعرفه ابن أبى حاتم والحسن البصرى لم يسمع من أبى هريرة على قول الجمهور.
61:12.english: [223] A hadith: He was asked about the saying of Allah the Exalted - 'and goodly dwellings in gardens of eternity (Jannat 'Adn)' - He said: Palaces of pearl. The hadith was transmitted by Abu al-Shaykh Ibn Hibban in Kitab al-'Azamah and al-Ajurri in Kitab al-Nasihah from the narration of al-Hasan ibn Khalifah from al-Hasan. He said: I asked Abu Hurayrah and 'Imran ibn Husayn about this verse, and it is not authentic. Al-Hasan ibn Khalifah was not known by Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Hasan al-Basri did not hear from Abu Hurayrah according to the majority opinion.
61:12.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Book of Repentance'

61:12.arabic: (وسئل رسول الله ﭬ عن قوله ﴿ ومساكن طيبة فى جنات عدن ﴾ {} قال: قصور من لؤلؤ فى كل قصر سبعون دارا من ياقوت أحمر فى كل دارسبعون بيتا من زمرد أخضر فى كل بيت سرير على كل سرير سبعون فراشا من كل لون على كل فراش زوجة من الحور العين فى كل بيت سبعون مائدة على كل مائدة سبعون لونا من الطعام فى كل بيت سبعون وصيفة ويعطى المؤمن فى كل غداة يعنى من القوة ما يأتي على ذلك أجمع[223]).
61:12.english: (And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was asked about His saying: 'And pleasant dwellings in gardens of eternity (Jannat 'Adn)' (Quran 61:12). He said: Palaces of pearl, in every palace seventy houses of red ruby, in every house seventy rooms of green emerald, in every room a bed, on every bed seventy couches of every color, on every couch a wife from the wide-eyed maidens (Al-Hur al-'Ayn), in every house seventy tables, on every table seventy varieties of food, in every house seventy handmaidens, and the believer is given every morning, meaning from the strength (Al-Quwwah), what suffices for all of that together[223]).
61:12.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Book of Repentance'

61:14.arabic: ورأيت في الإنجيل قال عيسى بن مريم عليه السلام لقد قيل لكم من قبل إن السن بالسن والأنف بالأنف وأنا أقول لكم لا تقاوموا بالشر بل من ضرب خدك الأيمن فحول إليه الخد الأيسر ومن اخذ رداءك فاعطه ازارك ومن سخرك لتسير معه ميلا فسر معه ميلين وكل ذلك أمر بالصبر على الاذى، فالصبر على اذى الناس من أعلى مراتب الصبر لانه يتعاون فيه باعث الدين وباعث الشهوة والغضب جميعا.
61:14.english: And I saw in the Gospel that Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him, said: 'It was said to you before: an eye for an eye and a nose for a nose, but I say to you: do not resist evil, but whoever strikes your right cheek, turn to him the left cheek, and whoever takes your cloak, give him your garment, and whoever compels you to go one mile, go with him two miles.' And all of that is a command for patience (Sabr) upon harm, so patience (Sabr) upon the harm of people is from the highest ranks of patience (Sabr) because in it the motivator of religion (Deen) and the motivator of desire (Shahwa) and anger (Ghadab) all cooperate.
61:14.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

61:14.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
61:14.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'Whatever is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)".'
61:14.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

62:4.arabic: فهذا يدل على أن قوله: " ذلك فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء " أي مزيد ثواب الفقراء على ذكرهم. وأما قوله: إن الغني وصف الحق، فقد أجابه بعض الشيوخ فقال: أترى أن الله تعالى غني بالأسباب والأعراض، فانقطع ولم ينطق، وأجاب آخرون فقالوا: إن التكبر من صفات الحق فينبغي أن يكون أفضل من التواضع، ثم قالوا: بل هذا يدل على أن الفقر أفضل لأن صفات العبودية فضل للعبد كالخوف والرجاء، وصفات الربوبية لا ينبغي أن ينازع فيها، ولذلك قال تعالى فيما روى عنه نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم: " الكبرياء ردائي والعظمة إزاري، فمن نازعني واحد
62:4.english: This indicates that His saying: "That is the Favor (Fadl) of Allah, He gives it to whom He wills" means the increased reward of the poor over their remembrance. As for his saying: Indeed, wealth is an attribute of the Truth (Al-Haqq), some shaykhs answered him by saying: Do you see that Allah the Exalted is rich (Ghani) through causes and accidents? So he fell silent and did not speak. Others answered by saying: Indeed, arrogance (Al-Takabbur) is from the attributes of the Truth (Al-Haqq), so it should be better than humility (Al-Tawadu'). Then they said: Rather, this indicates that poverty (Al-Faqr) is better because the attributes of servitude (Al-'Ubudiyyah) are a favor (Fadl) for the servant (Al-'Abd) like fear (Al-Khawf) and hope (Al-Raja'), and the attributes of lordship (Al-Rububiyyah) should not be contended over. Therefore, Allah the Exalted said in what was narrated from our Prophet, peace be upon him: "Pride (Al-Kibriya') is My cloak and majesty (Al-'Azamah) is My garment, so whoever contends with Me in one of them, I will break him."
62:4.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

62:4.arabic: وقد استشهد ابن عطاء أيضاً لما سئل عن ذلك فقال: الغني أفضل لأنه وصف الحق، أما دليله الأول ففيه نظر، لأن الخبر قد ورد مفصلاً تفصيلاً يدل على خلاف ذلك: وهو أن ثواب الفقير في التسبيح يزيد على ثواب الغني، وأن فوزهم بذلك الثواب فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء، فقد روى يزيد بن أسلم عن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه قال: بعثني الفقراء رسولاً إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: إني رسول الفقراء إليك؛ فقال: " مرحباً بك وبمن جئت من عندهم قوم أحبهم " قال: قالوا يا رسول الله إن الأغنياء ذهبوا بالخير يحجون ولا نقدر عليه،
62:4.english: And Ibn 'Ata' also cited as evidence when he was asked about that, saying: The rich person is better because he is described as truthful. As for his first evidence, there is consideration in it, because the report has come detailed in a manner that indicates the contrary: which is that the reward of the poor person in glorification increases over the reward of the rich person, and that their attainment of that reward is the favor of Allah (Fadl Allah) which He gives to whom He wills (Yū'tīhi man yashā'), for Yazid ibn Aslam narrated from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The poor sent me as a messenger to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and I said: I am the messenger of the poor to you; he said: "Welcome to you and to those you have come from, a people I love." He said: They said: O Messenger of Allah, the rich have taken the good deeds—they perform pilgrimage (Hajj) and we are unable to do it, and they perform 'Umrah and we are unable to do it, and when they fall ill, they send ahead the surplus of their wealth as a provision for them; so the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Convey from me to the poor that for whoever among you is patient and expects reward, there are three characteristics not for the rich: As for one characteristic: Indeed, in Paradise there are chambers that the inhabitants of Paradise look at as the inhabitants of the earth look at the stars of the sky, none enters them except a poor prophet, or a poor martyr, or a poor believer. And the second: The poor enter Paradise before the rich by half a day, which is five hundred years. And the third: Glory be to Allah (Subḥān Allāh) and praise be to Allah (Al-Ḥamdu lillāh) and there is no god but Allah (Lā ilāha illā Allāh) and Allah is the greatest (Allāhu Akbar)." And the poor person said similarly.
62:4.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

62:4.arabic: [44] حديث شكى الفقراء إلى رسول الله ﭬ سبق الأغنياء بالخيرات والصدقات الحديث وفي آخر فقال ذلك فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء متفق عليه من حديث أبي هريرة نحوه.
62:4.english: [44] A hadith: The poor complained to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) that the rich have preceded them in good deeds and charitable acts. The hadith, and at its end he said: "That is the grace of Allah (Fadl Allah) - He grants it to whom He wills." Agreed upon from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, similar to it.
62:4.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

62:5.arabic: وقد مثل الله سبحانه وتعالى من يعلم ولا يعمل بالحمار والكلب فقال عز وجل "مثل الذين حملوا التوراة ثم لم يحملوها كمثل الحمار يحمل أسفاراً" أراد به علماء اليهود. وقال في بلعم بن باعوراء "واتل عليهم نبأ الذي آتيناه آياتنا فانسلخ منها" حتى بلغ "فمثله كمثل الكلب إن تحمل عليه يلهث أو تتركه يلهث" قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: أوتي بعلم كتاباً فأخلد إلى شهوات الأرض أي سكن حبه العالم هذا الخطر فأي عالم لم يتبع شهوته وأي عالم لم يأمر بالخير الذي لا يأتيه؟
62:5.english: And Allah the Exalted has likened those who know but do not act to the donkey and the dog, for He said, the Mighty and Majestic: "The likeness of those who were entrusted with the Torah then did not carry it is like the likeness of a donkey carrying books." He intended by this the scholars of the Jews. And He said regarding Balaam son of Beor: "And recite to them the news of him to whom We gave Our signs, but he detached himself from them" until reaching "So his likeness is like the likeness of a dog: if you attack him, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants." Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: He was given knowledge of a book, but he inclined to the desires of the earth, meaning his love settled in this danger. So which scholar has not followed his desire, and which scholar has not commanded good which he does not come to?
62:5.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

62:5.arabic: وعند هذا يقول له الشيطان: لا يغرنك هذا المثال فإن العلم بالدواء لا يزيل المرض، وإنما مطلبك القرب من الله وثوابه والعلم يجلب الثواب، ويتلو عليه الأخبار الواردة في فضل العلم. فإن كان المسكين معتوهاً مغروراً وافق ذلك مراده وهواه فاطمأن إليه وأهمل العمل، وإن كان كيساً فيقول للشيطان: أتذكرني فضائل العالم وتنسيني ما ورد في العالم الفاجر الذي لا يعمل بعلمه كقوله تعالى "فمثله كمثل الكلب" وكقوله تعالى "مثل الذين حملوا التوراة ثم لم يحملوها كمثل الحمار يحمل أسفاراً" فأي خزي أعظم من التمثيل بالكلب والحمار؟
62:5.english: At this point, the Devil (Shaytan) says to him: Do not let this example deceive you, for knowledge of the medicine does not remove the illness, and indeed your objective is nearness to Allah and His reward, and knowledge brings reward, and he recites to him the reports that have come regarding the virtue of knowledge. If the poor one is foolish and deceived, it agrees with his desire and his passion (Hawa), so he becomes content with it and neglects the action (Amal), and if he is intelligent, he says to the Devil: Do you remind me of the virtues of the scholar and make me forget what has come regarding the wicked scholar who does not act upon his knowledge, like His saying, the Exalted: "His likeness is like the dog" and like His saying, the Exalted: "The likeness of those who were entrusted with the Torah then did not carry it is like the likeness of the donkey carrying books." So what disgrace is greater than being likened to the dog and the donkey? And He, may He be glorified, said: "Whoever increases in knowledge and does not increase in guidance does not increase from Allah except in distance." And He also said: "The scholar is thrown into the Fire, and his intestines spill out, and he circles with them in the Fire as the donkey circles in the mill." And like His saying, upon him be prayers and peace: "The worst of people are the wicked scholars." And the saying of Abu al-Darda': Woe to the one who does not know once, and if Allah had willed, He would have taught him, and woe to the one who knows and does not act seven times, meaning that knowledge is a proof against him, for it is said to him: What have you done with what you knew, and how have you fulfilled the gratitude (Shukr) to Allah?
62:5.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

62:6.arabic: وقال البويطي لبعض الزهاد: أتحب الموت؟ فكأنه توقف، فقال: لو كنت صادقاً لأحببته. وتلا قوله تعالى: "قُلْ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ هَادُوا إِنْ زَعَمْتُمْ أَنَّكُمْ أَوْلِيَاءُ لِلَّهِ مِنْ دُونِ النَّاسِ فَتَمَنَّوُا الْمَوْتَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ" فقال الرجل: فقد قال النبي ﷺ: "لا يتمنين أحدكم الموت" فقال: إنما قاله لضر نزل به لأن الرضا بقضاء الله تعالى أفضل من طلب الفرار منه.
62:6.english: And Al-Buwayti said to some ascetics: 'Do you love death?' It was as if he hesitated, so he said: 'If you were truthful, you would love it.' And he recited the saying of Allah the Exalted: "Say: 'O you who are Jews, if you claim that you are allies of Allah to the exclusion of [other] people, then wish for death, if you should be truthful.'" Then the man said: 'But the Prophet ﷺ said: "Let none of you wish for death."' So he said: 'He only said it due to a harm that had befallen him, because contentment with the decree (Qada) of Allah the Exalted is better than seeking escape from it.'
62:6.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

62:8.arabic: وأما المنافقون ففروا من الزحف خوفاً من الموت فقيل لهم: "إن الموت الذين تفرون منه فإنه ملاقيكم" فإيثارهم البقاء على الشهادة استبدال الذي هو أدنى بالذي هو خير، فأولئك الذين اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى فما ربحت تجارتهم وما كانوا مهتدين، وأما المخلصون فإن الله تعالى اشترى منهم أنفسهم وأموالهم بأن لهم الجنة، فلما رأوا أنهم تركوا تمتع عشرين سنة مثلاً أو ثلاثين سنة بتمتع الأبد استبشروا ببيعهم الذي بايعوا به، فهذا بيان المزهود فيه.
62:8.english: And as for the hypocrites, they fled from the battle out of fear of death, so it was said to them: "Indeed, the death from which you flee will meet you." Their preferring survival over martyrdom is exchanging what is lower for what is better. Those are the ones who purchased misguidance with guidance, so their transaction did not profit them, and they were not guided. And as for the sincere ones, Allah the Exalted purchased from them their souls (Nafs) and their wealth in exchange for Paradise for them. When they saw that they left enjoyment of twenty years, for example, or thirty years for enjoyment of eternity, they rejoiced at their transaction with which they transacted. This is the explanation of what is renounced.
62:8.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

62:9.arabic: اعلم أن هذا يوم عظيم عظم الله به الإسلام وخصص به المسلمين قال الله تعالى ﴿ إذا نودي للصلاة من يوم الجمعة فاسعوا إلى ذكر الله وذروا البيع ﴾  {}  فحرم الاشتغال بأمور الدنيا وبكل صارف عن السعي إلى الجمعة، وقال ﭬ: (إن الله عز وجل فرض عليكم الجمعة في يومي هذا في مقامي هذا[145]) وقال ﭬ: (من ترك الجمعة ثلاثا من غير عذر طبع الله على قلبه[146]) وفي لفظ آخر: (فقد نبذ الإسلام وراء ظهره[147]) واختلف رجل إلى ابن عباس يسأله عن رجل مات لم يكن يشهد جمعة ولا جماعة، فقال: في النار. فلم يزل يتردد إليه شهرا يسأله ع
62:9.english: Know that this is a great day which Allah has magnified through Islam and has specifically designated for the Muslims. Allah the Exalted said: 'O you who have believed, when the call is made for the prayer on the day of Friday, then hasten to the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah and leave off trade.' {} So He prohibited preoccupation with worldly matters and every distraction from hastening to Friday. And He (the Prophet) said: 'Indeed Allah the Mighty and Majestic has made Friday obligatory upon you on this day of mine in this place of mine.' And He (the Prophet) said: 'Whoever abandons Friday three times without an excuse, Allah will seal his heart.' And in another wording: 'He has indeed cast Islam behind his back.' And a man repeatedly went to Ibn Abbas asking him about a man who died without having attended Friday or congregational prayer, and he said: 'In the Fire.' And he kept returning to him for a month asking about that while he said: 'In the Fire.' And in the report: Indeed the People of the Two Books were given Friday but they differed concerning it, so it was diverted from them, and Allah the Exalted guided us to it and postponed it for this community and made it a festival for them, so they are the most deserving people of it by precedence, and the People of the Two Books are followers after them. And in the hadith of Anas from the Prophet that he said: 'Jibril (Gabriel) peace be upon him came to me with a white mirror in his hand and said: This is Friday which your Lord makes obligatory upon you to be a festival for you and for your community after you. I said: So what is for us in it? He said: For you in it is a good hour; whoever supplicates in it for a good thing that is apportioned for him, Allah the Exalted gives it to him, or if it is not apportioned for him, He stores for him what is greater than it; or whoever seeks refuge from an evil that is written against him, except that Allah the Mighty and Majestic grants him refuge from what is greater than it. And it is the master of days with us, and we call it in the Hereafter the Day of Increase. I said: And why? He said: Indeed your Lord the Mighty
62:9.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

62:9.arabic: لقوله تعالى: ﴿ إذا نودي للصلاة من يوم الجمعة فاسعوا إلى ذكر الله وذروا البيع ﴾ {} ويرخص لهؤلاء في ترك الجمعة لعذر المطر والوحل والفزع والمرض والتمريض إذا لم يكن للمريض قيم غيره ثم يستحب لهم أعني أصحاب الأعذار تأخير الظهر إلى أن يفرغ الناس من الجمعة فإن حضر الجمعة مريض أو مسافر أو عبد أو امرأة صحت جمعتهم وأجزأت عن الظهر والله أعلم.
62:9.english: Due to His saying, the Most High: 'O you who have believed, when the call is made for the prayer of the day of Friday, then hasten to the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah and leave off trade.' And concession is granted to these [people] in abandoning the Friday [prayer] due to the excuse of rain, mud, fear, illness, and nursing [the sick] if there is no other caretaker for the sick person besides him. Then it is recommended for them—I mean the people with excuses—to delay the noon [prayer] until the people finish from the Friday [prayer]. For if a sick person, traveler, slave, or woman attends the Friday [prayer], their Friday [prayer] is valid and suffices for the noon [prayer]. And Allah knows best.
62:9.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

62:9.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
62:9.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'Whatever is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)".'
62:9.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

62:10.arabic: قال أنس بن مالك في قوله تعالى: ﴿ فإذا قضيت الصلاة فانتشروا في الأرض وابتغوا من فضل الله ﴾ {} أما إنه ليس بطلب دنيا لكن عيادة مريض وشهود جنازة وتعلم علم وزيارة أخ في الله عز وجل وقد سمى الله عز وجل العلم فضلا في مواضع قال تعالى: ﴿ وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم وكان فضل الله عليك عظيما ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ ولقد آتينا داود منا فضلا ﴾ {} يعني العلم. فتعلم العلم في هذا اليوم وتعليمه من أفضل القربات
62:10.english: Anas bin Malik said regarding the saying of Allah the Exalted: 'So when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land and seek from the bounty (Fadl) of Allah' {} Indeed, it is not for seeking worldly matters, but rather visiting a sick person, attending a funeral, learning knowledge (Ilm), and visiting a brother in Allah the Mighty and Majestic. And Allah the Mighty and Majestic has named knowledge (Ilm) as bounty (Fadl) in places. He said: 'And taught you what you did not know, and ever has the bounty (Fadl) of Allah upon you been great' {} And He said: 'And We gave David from Us bounty (Fadl)' {} meaning knowledge (Ilm). So learning knowledge (Ilm) on this day and teaching it are among the best acts of nearness (Qurbat).
62:10.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

62:10.arabic: وقال تعالى وآخرون يضربون في الأرض يبتغون من فضل الله وقال تعالى فانتشروا في الأرض وابتغوا من فضل الله وأما الأخبار فقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم من الذنوب ذنوب لا يكفرها إلا الهم في طلب المعيشة حديث من الذنوب ذنوب لا يكفرها إلا الهم في طلب المعيشة تقدم في النكاح وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم التاجر الصدوق يحشر يوم القيامة مع الصديقين والشهداء حديث التاجر الصدوق يحشر يوم القيامة مع الصديقين والشهداء أخرجه الترمذي والحاكم من حديث أبي سعيد قال الترمذي حسن وقال الحاكم إنه من مراسيل الحسن ولابن ماجه والحاكم ن
62:10.english: And He (Exalted) said: 'And others travel through the earth seeking from the bounty (Fadl) of Allah.' And He (Exalted) said: 'So disperse in the earth and seek from the bounty (Fadl) of Allah.' As for the reports (Akhbar), the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'From the sins are sins that are not expiated except by the anxiety (Al-Hamm) in seeking livelihood (Al-Ma'ishah).' The hadith 'From the sins are sins that are not expiated except by the anxiety in seeking livelihood' was previously mentioned in marriage. And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'The truthful merchant (Al-Tajir Al-Saduq) will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection with the truthful ones (Al-Siddiqin) and the martyrs (Al-Shuhada).' The hadith 'The truthful merchant will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection with the truthful ones and the martyrs' was reported by Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Hakim from the narration of Abu Sa'id. Al-Tirmidhi said it is good (Hasan), and Al-Hakim said it is from the mursal narrations of Al-Hasan. Ibn Majah and Al-Hakim have something similar from the narration of Ibn Umar. And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever seeks the worldly life (Al-Dunya) lawfully (Halan) and with abstinence (Ta'affuf) from begging, striving (Sa'yan) for his dependents, and compassion (Ta'atuf) for his neighbor, will meet Allah with his face like the moon on the night of the full moon.' The hadith 'Whoever seeks the worldly life lawfully and with abstinence from begging and striving for his dependents' was reported by Abu Al-Shaykh in the book of reward, Abu Nu'aym in Al-Hilyah, and Al-Bayhaqi in the branches of faith from the narration of Abu Hurairah with a weak chain. And the Prophet (peace be upon him) was sitting with his companions one day when they saw a young man with vigor and strength who had risen early striving. They said: 'Woe to this one, if only his youth and strength were in the path of Allah.' The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not say this, for if he is striving for himself to restrain it from begging and to enrich it from people...'
62:10.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Earning'

63:1.arabic: الصدق الثانى في النية والإرادة ويرجع ذلك إلى الإخلاص وهو أن لا يكون له باعث في الحركات والسكنات إلا الله تعالى فإن مازجه شوب من حظوظ النفس بطل صدق النية وصاحبه يجوز أن يسمى كاذبا كما روينا في فضيلة الإخلاص من حديث الثلاثة حين يسئل العالم ما عملت فيما علمت فقال فعلت كذا وكذا فقال الله تعالى كذبت بل أردت أن يقال فلان عالم حديث الثلاثة حين سأل العالم ماذا عملت فيما علمت الحديث تقدم فإنه لم يكذبه ولم يقل له لم تعمل ولكنه كذبه في إرادته ونيته وقد قال بعضهم الصدق صحة التوحيد في القصد وكذلك قول الله تع
63:1.english: The second truthfulness (Sidq) is in intention (Niyyah) and will (Iradah), and this returns to sincerity (Ikhlas), which is that there should be no motive in movements and stillness except Allah the Exalted. If it is mixed with a taint of the desires of the Soul (Nafs), the truthfulness of intention is invalidated, and its possessor may be called a liar, as we have narrated in the virtue of sincerity (Ikhlas) from the Hadith of the Three when the scholar is asked: 'What did you do with what you knew?' He said: 'I did such and such.' Allah the Exalted said: 'You have lied, rather you intended that it be said: So-and-so is a scholar.' The Hadith of the Three when the scholar was asked: 'What did you do with what you knew?' The Hadith has preceded, for He did not call him a liar and did not say to him: 'You did not act,' but He called him a liar in his will (Iradah) and intention (Niyyah). And some have said: 'Truthfulness (Sidq) is the soundness of monotheism (Tawhid) in purpose (Qasd).' Likewise, the saying of Allah the Exalted: 'And Allah bears witness that the hypocrites are liars.' And they said: 'Indeed, you are the Messenger of Allah.' And this is truthfulness, but their lying is not from the aspect of tongue utterance, but from the aspect of the heart's conscience (Damir Al-Qalb). And the calling liar pertains to the report, and this saying includes reporting by circumstantial evidence (Qarinah Al-Hal), since its possessor shows from himself that he believes what he says, so he lied in his indication by circumstantial evidence (Qarinah Al-Hal) to what is in his heart, for he lied in that and did not lie in what he utters. Thus, one of the meanings of truthfulness (Sidq) returns to the purity of intention (Niyyah), which is sincerity (Ikhlas), so every truthful one must be sincere (Mukhlis).
63:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

63:1.arabic: "الأولى" الرياء بأصل الإيمان وهذا أغلظ أبواب الرياء وصاحبه مخلد في النار، وهو الذي يظهر كلمتي الشهادة وباطنه مشحون بالتكذيب ولكنه يرائي بظاهر الإسلام، وهو الذي ذكره الله تعالى في كتابه في مواضع شتى كقوله عز وجل "إذا جاءك المنافقون قالوا نشهد إنك لرسول الله والله يعلم إنك لرسوله والله يشهد إن المنافقين لكاذبون" أي في دلالتهم بقولهم على ضمائرهم وقال تعالى "ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه وهو ألد الخصام وإذا تولى سعى في الأرض ليفسد فيها" الآية وقال تعالى "وإذا لقو
63:1.english: "The First" The Showing-off (Riya') with the foundation of Faith (Iman) and this is the most severe of the doors of showing-off and its possessor is eternally in the Fire, and it is the one who manifests the two testimonies (Kalimat al-Shahadah) and his inner being (Batin) is filled with denial but he shows off with the outward appearance (Zahir) of Islam, and it is the one whom Allah the Exalted mentioned in His Book in various places such as His saying the Mighty and Majestic: "When the hypocrites come to you, they say: 'We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah.' And Allah knows that you are His Messenger, and Allah bears witness that the hypocrites are indeed liars." That is, in their indication by their saying to their inner consciences (Damair). And He the Exalted said: "And among the people is he whose speech pleases you in the worldly life, and he calls Allah to witness as to what is in his heart (Qalb), yet he is the fiercest of opponents. And when he turns away, he strives throughout the land to cause corruption therein." The verse. And He the Exalted said: "And when they meet you, they say, 'We believe,' but when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you in rage." And He the Exalted said: "They show off to the people and do not remember Allah except a little, wavering between that." And the verses about them are many.
63:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

63:4.arabic: ولا شك أن من اختلط بالناس وشاركهم في أعمالهم لا ينفك من حاسد وعدو يسيء الظن به ويتوهم أنه يستعد لمعاداته ونصب المكيدة عليه وتدسيس غائلة وراءه فالناس مهما اشتد حرصهم على أمر يحسبون كل صيحة عليهم هم العدو فاحذرهم وقد اشتد حرصهم على الدنيا فلا يظنون بغيرهم إلا الحرص عليها
63:4.english: And there is no doubt that whoever mixes with people and participates in their affairs does not escape from an envier and enemy who thinks ill of him and imagines that he is preparing for hostility against him and setting up a plot against him and planting calamity behind him. So people, whenever their greed for a matter intensifies, they consider every cry against them—they are the enemy, so beware of them. And their greed for the worldly life has intensified, so they do not think of others except with greed for it.
63:4.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Etiquette of Seclusion'

63:7.arabic: وقال تعالى: " إن الذين تعبدون من دون الله لا يملكون لكم رزقاً فابتغوا عند الله الرزق واعبدوه ". وقال عز وجل: " ولله خزائن السموات والأرض ولكن المنافقين لا يفقهون ". وقال عز وجل: " يدبر الأمر ما من شفيع إلا من بعد إذنه ". وكل ما ذكر في القرآن من التوحيد فهو تنبيه على قطع الملاحظة عن الأغيار والتوكل على الواحد القهار.
63:7.english: And He (Exalted is He) said: "Indeed, those you worship besides Allah do not possess for you provision, so seek provision from Allah and worship Him." And He (Mighty and Majestic) said: "And to Allah belong the treasuries of the heavens and the earth, but the hypocrites do not comprehend." And He (Mighty and Majestic) said: "He arranges the affair; there is no intercessor except after His permission." And everything mentioned in the Quran regarding Tawhid (Oneness of God) is an alert to sever observation from others (Al-Aghyar) and to rely upon (Tawakkul) the One, the Subduer (Al-Qahhar).
63:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

63:9.arabic: ولذلك حذر الله عباده من فتنة المال والزوج والولد فقال تعالى: ﴿ يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تلهكم أموالكم ولا أولادكم عن ذكر الله ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل: ﴿ ان من أزواجكم وأولادكم عدوا لكم فاحذروهم ﴾ {} وقال ﭬ: (الولد مبخلة مجبنة محزنة[19]). (ولما نظر عليه السلام الى ولده الحسن رضي الله عنه يتعثر في قميصه نزل عن المنبر واحتضنه ثم قال صدق الله ﴿ إنما اموالكم واولادكم فتنة ﴾ {} اني لما رأيت ابني يتعثر لم املك نفسي ان اخذته[20]) ففي ذلك عبرة لأولى الأبصار فالرجل كل الرجل من يصبر على العافية ومعنى الصبر عليها ان
63:9.english: Therefore, Allah warned His servants from the trial of wealth, spouse, and children, so He the Exalted said: 'O you who have believed, let not your wealth and your children divert you from the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah' {} and He the Mighty and Majestic said: 'Indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them' {} and he (the Prophet) said: 'The child is a miser-maker, a coward-maker, a sorrow-maker[19].' (And when the peace be upon him saw his son Al-Hasan, may Allah be pleased with him, stumbling in his shirt, he descended from the pulpit and embraced him, then said: 'Allah has spoken the truth: "Your wealth and your children are but a trial" {} for when I saw my son stumbling, I could not control my soul (Nafs) from taking him[20].') In that is a lesson for those of insight. The man, every man, is he who is patient upon well-being, and the meaning of patience upon it is that he does not rely upon it and knows that all of that is a deposit with him, and perhaps it will be reclaimed soon, and that he does not release his soul (Nafs) in rejoicing in it, nor does he immerse himself in enjoyment, pleasure, amusement, and play, and that he observes the rights of Allah in his wealth through spending, in his body through offering assistance to creation, in his tongue through offering truth, and likewise in all that Allah has bestowed upon him. And this patience is connected to gratitude, so it is not complete except by fulfilling the right of gratitude as will come later. And patience upon prosperity is more severe only because it is accompanied by ability, and from protection is that you are not able. And patience upon cupping and intention when someone else undertakes it is easier than patience upon bleeding yourself and cupping yourself, and the hungry person in the absence of food is more capable of patience than when delicious, tasty foods are present to him and he has ability over them, then...
63:9.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

63:9.arabic:
بيان ذم المال وكراهة حبه

قال الله تعالى "يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تلهكم أموالكم ولا أولادكم عن ذكر الله ومن يفعل ذلك فأولئك هم الخاسرون" وقال تعالى "إنما أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة والله عنده أجر عظيم" فمن اختار ماله وولده على ما عند الله فقد خسر وغبن خسراناً عظيماً.
63:9.english:
Explanation of the condemnation of wealth and the dislike of loving it.

Allah the Exalted said: "O you who have believed, do not let your wealth and your children divert you from the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah. And whoever does that - then those are the losers." And He the Exalted said: "Your wealth and your children are only a trial, and Allah has with Him a great reward." So whoever chooses his wealth and his child over what is with Allah has lost and been cheated a great loss.
63:9.book_title: Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth
63:9.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

63:9.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
63:9.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'Whatever is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)".'
63:9.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

64:1.arabic: وقال عطاء السلمي منعنا الغيث فخرجنا نستسقي فإذا نحن بسعدون المجنون في المقابر فنظر إلي فقال يا عطاء أهذا يوم النشور أوبعثر ما في القبور فقلت لا ولكنا منعنا الغيث فخرجنا نستسقي فقال يا عطاء بقلوب أرضية أم بقلوب سماوية فقلت بل بقلوب سماوية فقال هيهات يا عطاء قل للمتبهرجين لا تتبهرجوا فإن الناقد بصير ثم رمق السماء بطرفه وقال إلهي وسيدي ومولاي لا تهلك بلادك بذنوب عبادك ولكن بالسر المكنون من أسمائك وما وارت الحجب من آلائك إلا ما سقيتنا ماء غدقا فراتا تحيي به العباد وتروي به البلاد يا من هو على كل شيء
64:1.english: And Ata al-Sulami said: We were deprived of rain, so we went out to pray for rain, and behold we found Sa'dun the Madman in the graveyards. He looked at me and said: O Ata, is this the Day of Resurrection, or has what is in the graves been scattered? I said: No, but we have been deprived of rain, so we went out to pray for rain. He said: O Ata, with earthly hearts (Qulub) or with heavenly hearts (Qulub)? I said: Rather with heavenly hearts (Qulub). He said: Far be it, O Ata! Tell the ostentatious ones not to be ostentatious, for the Critic is seeing. Then he glanced at the sky with his eye and said: My God (Ilahi), my Master (Sayyidi), and my Lord (Mawlaya), do not destroy Your lands with the sins of Your servants, but with the hidden secret of Your names and what the veils have concealed of Your blessings, except that You give us to drink abundant, sweet water by which You revive the servants and water the lands, O He who is over all things powerful (Qadir). Ata said: He had not completed the speech until the sky thundered and lightning flashed and poured forth rain like the mouths of waterskins. Then he departed while saying: The ascetics (Zahidun) and worshippers (Abiduna) have succeeded, for they made their bellies hungry for their Lord (Mawlaha). They kept awake the sick eyes out of love, so their night passed while they were keeping awake. The worship (Ibadah) of God preoccupied them until people thought there was madness in them.
64:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter

64:1.arabic: علي يا عظيم يا بارىء يا رحيم يا عزيز يا  جبار  سبحان  من  سبحت  له السموات بأكنافها وسبحان من سبحت له البحار بأمواجها وسبحان من سبحت له  الجبال بأصدائها وسبحان من سبحت له الحيتان بلغاتها  وسبحان  من  سبحت  له  النجوم  في السماء بأبراجها وسبحان من سبحت له الأشجار بأصولها وثمارها وسبحان من سبحت  له السموات السبع والأرضون السبع ومن فيهن ومن عليهن سبحان من سبح له  كل  شيء  من مخلوقاته تباركت وتعاليت سبحانك سبحانك يا حي يا قيوم يا عليم يا  حليم  سبحانك لا إله إلا أنت وحدك لا شريك لك تحيي وتميت وأنت ح
64:1.english: O High One, O Great One, O Creator, O Merciful, O Mighty, O Compeller. Glory be to the One for whom the heavens with their expanses glorify, and glory be to the One for whom the seas with their waves glorify, and glory be to the One for whom the mountains with their echoes glorify, and glory be to the One for whom the fish with their languages glorify, and glory be to the One for whom the stars in the sky with their constellations glorify, and glory be to the One for whom the trees with their roots and fruits glorify, and glory be to the One for whom the seven heavens and the seven earths and those in them and upon them glorify, glory be to the One for whom every thing from His creations glorifies. Blessed and Exalted are You, glory be to You, glory be to You, O Living, O Self-Subsisting, O All-Knowing, O Forbearing, glory be to You, there is no god but You alone, no partner to You, You give life and cause death, and You are Living, You do not die, in Your hand is the good, and You are over every thing powerful.
64:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

64:1.arabic: [197]  حديث القول عند دخول السوق لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له له الملك وله الحمد يحيي ويميت وهو حي لا يموت بيده الخير وهو على كل شيء قدير من حديث عمر وقال غريب والحاكم وقال صحيح على شرط الشيخين.
64:1.english: [197] The hadith of the saying when entering the market: 'There is no god but Allah alone, He has no partner, to Him belongs the kingdom and to Him belongs the praise, He gives life and causes death, and He is living and does not die, in His hand is the good, and He has power over everything' from the narration of Umar, and he said it is rare, and Al-Hakim said it is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs.
64:1.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication

64:1.arabic: ن الأسواق لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، له الملك وله الحمد يحيى ويميت وهو على كل شيء قدير كتب الله له ألف ألف حسنة ومحا عنه ألف ألف سيئة وبنى له بيتا في الجنة) ويروى: (إن العبد إذا قال لا إله إلا الله أتت إلى صحيفته فلا تمر على خطيئه إلى محتها حتى تجد حسنة مثلها فتجلس إلى جنبها[29]) وفي الصحيح عن أيوب عن النبي ﭬ أنه قال: (من قال لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، له الملك وله الحمد وهو على كل شيء قدير عشر مرات كان كمن أعتق أربعة أنفس من ولد إسماعيل ﭬ[30]) وفي الصحيح أيضا عن عبادة بن الصامت عن ا
64:1.english: From the markets: There is no god but Allah alone, no partner to Him, to Him belongs the Kingdom (Al-Mulk) and to Him belongs the Praise (Al-Hamd), He gives life and causes death, and He is over all things Powerful (Qadir). Allah writes for him a thousand thousand good deeds and erases from him a thousand thousand bad deeds and builds for him a house in Paradise. And it is narrated: (Indeed, when the servant (Al-Abd) says 'There is no god but Allah,' it comes to his record and does not pass by a sin without erasing it until it finds a good deed like it and sits beside it [29]). And in the authentic (hadith) from Ayyub from the Prophet (peace be upon him) that he said: (Whoever says 'There is no god but Allah alone, no partner to Him, to Him belongs the Kingdom and to Him belongs the Praise, and He is over all things Powerful' ten times, it is as if he freed four souls from the descendants of Ishmael (peace be upon him) [30]). And in the authentic also from Ubada ibn al-Samit from the Prophet (peace be upon him) that he said: (Whoever wakes up at night and says 'There is no god but Allah alone, no partner to Him, to Him belongs the Kingdom and to Him belongs the Praise, and He is over all things Powerful, Glory be to Allah (Subhan Allah) and Praise be to Allah (Al-Hamdulillah) and there is no god but Allah and Allah is the Greatest (Allahu Akbar) and there is no power and no strength except by Allah, the Most High, the Most Great,' then says 'O Allah, forgive me,' he is forgiven or if he supplicates, it is answered for him, then if he performs ablution (Wudu) and prays, his prayer is accepted [31]). (The virtue of glorification (Tasbih) and praise (Tahmid) and the rest of the remembrances (Adhkar)) He (peace be upon him) said: (Whoever glorifies (Yusabbih) after every prayer thirty-three times and praises (Yuhammid) thirty-three times and magnifies (Yukabbir) thirty-three times and concludes the hundred with 'There is no god but Allah, no partner to Him, to Him belongs the Kingdom and to Him belongs the Praise, and He is over all things Powerful,' his sins are forgiven even if they were like the foam of the sea [32]). And he (peace be upon him) said: (Whoever says 'Glory be to Allah and Praise be to Him (Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi)' in a day one hundred times, his sins are removed even if they were like the foam of the sea [33]). And it is narrated: (That a man came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and said: The world has turned away from me and my hands are empty, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: Then where are you from the prayer of the angels and the glorification (Tasbih) of the creatures and by it they are provided? He said: So I said: And what, O Messenger of Allah? He said: Say 'Glory be to Allah and Praise be to Him, Glory be to Allah the Most Great, I seek forgiveness from Allah (Astaghfirullah)' one hundred times between the rising of dawn until the morning prayer is prayed, the world will come to you humbly and submissively, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, creates from every word an angel who glorifies (Yusabbih) Allah, the Exalted, until the Day of Resurrection for you its reward [34]). And he (peace be upon him) said: (When the servant (Al-Abd) says 'Praise be to Allah (Al-Hamdulillah),' it fills what is between the heaven and the earth, and when he says 'Praise be to Allah' the second time, it fills what is between the seventh heaven to the lowest earth, and when he says 'Praise be to Allah' the third time, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: Ask and you will be given [35]). And Rifa'ah al-Zarqi said: (We were one day praying behind the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), so when he raised his head from the bowing (Ruku) and said 'Allah hears those who praise Him (Sami' Allahu liman hamidah),' a man behind the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: Our Lord, to You is the Praise, much, good, blessed praise, so when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) finished his prayer, he said: Who was the speaker just now? He said: I, O Messenger of Allah, so he (peace be upon him) said: I saw thirty-some angels).
64:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

64:1.arabic: ب أنه ﭬ قال: (من قال لا إله  إلا الله وحده لا شريك له له الملك وله الحمد وهو على كل شيء قدير  عشر  مرات  كانت له عدل رقبة أو قال نسمة[27]) وروى عمرو بن شعيب عن أبيه عن جده أنه  قال:  قال رسول الله ﭬ: (من قال في يوم مائتي مرة لا إله إلا الله وحده  لا  شريك  له  له الملك وله الحمد وهو على كل شيء قدير لم يسبقه أحد  كان  قبله  ولا  يدركه  أحد بعده إلا من عمل بأفضل من عمله[28]) وقال ﭬ: (من قال في سوق من الأسواق لا  إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، له الملك وله الحمد يحيى ويميت وهو على كل شيء  قدير كتب ا
64:1.english: That he (peace be upon him) said: (Whoever says 'There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner to Him, to Him belongs the Dominion (Al-Mulk) and to Him belongs the Praise (Al-Hamd), and He is over all things Powerful (Qadir)' ten times, it will be for him equal to freeing a neck or he said a soul[27]). And Amr ibn Shu'ayb narrated from his father from his grandfather that he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: (Whoever says in a day two hundred times 'There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner to Him, to Him belongs the Dominion (Al-Mulk) and to Him belongs the Praise (Al-Hamd), and He is over all things Powerful (Qadir)', no one who was before him will precede him, nor will anyone after him overtake him, except one who acts with better than his action[28]). And he (peace be upon him) said: (Whoever says in a market from the markets 'There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner to Him, to Him belongs the Dominion (Al-Mulk) and to Him belongs the Praise (Al-Hamd), He gives life and causes death, and He is over all things Powerful (Qadir)', Allah will write for him a thousand thousand good deeds and erase from him a thousand thousand bad deeds and build for him a house in Paradise). And it is narrated: (Indeed, when the servant (Al-'Abd) says 'There is no god but Allah', it comes to his record and does not pass by a sin except it erases it until it finds a good deed like it, then it sits beside it[29]). And in the authentic (hadith) from Ayyub from the Prophet (peace be upon him) that he said: (Whoever says 'There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner to Him, to Him belongs the Dominion (Al-Mulk) and to Him belongs the Praise (Al-Hamd), and He is over all things Powerful (Qadir)' ten times, it is as if he freed four souls from the children of Ishmael (peace be upon him)[30]). And in the authentic also from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit from the Prophet (peace be upon him) that he said: (Whoever wakes up from the night and says 'There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner to Him, to Him belongs the Dominion (Al-Mulk) and to Him belongs the Praise (Al-Hamd), and He is over all things Powerful (Qadir), Glory be to Allah (Subhan Allah) and Praise be to Allah (Al-Hamd lillah) and there is no god but Allah and Allah is the Greatest (Allahu Akbar) and there is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Most Great', then says 'O Allah, forgive me', he will be forgiven, or if he supplicates, it will be answered for him, then if he performs ablution and prays, his prayer will be accepted[31]). (The Virtue of Glorification (Tasbih) and Praise (Tahmid) and the Rest of the Remembrances (Adhkar)) He (peace be upon him) said: (Whoever glorifies (Subbaha) after every prayer thirty-three times and praises (Hammada) thirty-three times and magnifies (Kabbara) thirty-three times and concludes the hundred with 'There is no god but Allah, with no partner to Him, to Him belongs the Dominion (Al-Mulk) and to Him belongs the Praise (Al-Hamd), and He is over all things Powerful (Qadir)', his sins will be forgiven even if they were like the foam of the sea[32]). And he (peace be upon him) said: (Whoever says 'Glory be to Allah and with His Praise (Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi)' in the day a hundred times, his sins will be removed even if they were like the foam of the sea[33]). And it is narrated: (That a man came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and said: The world has turned away from me and my means have become few, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: So where are you from the prayer of the angels and the glorification (Tasbih) of the creatures, and by it they are provided? He said: So I said: And what, O Messenger of Allah? He said: Say 'Glory be to Allah and with His Praise (Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi), Glory be to Allah the Most Great (Subhan Allah al-'Adhim), I seek forgiveness from Allah (Astaghfir Allah)' a hundred times between the rising of dawn until the morning prayer is prayed, the world will come to you humbly submissive, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will create from every word an angel who glorifies Allah, Exalted, until the Day of Resurrection (Yawm al-Qiyamah) for you its reward[34]). And he (peace be upon him) said: (When the servant (Al-'Abd) says 'Praise be to Allah (Al-Hamd lillah)', it fills what is between the heaven and the earth, then when he says 'The Praise...'

64:4.arabic: جميع ما في السموات والأرض وما بينهما
64:4.english: All that is in the heavens and the earth and what is between them
64:4.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Contemplation'

64:9.arabic: وناهيك به حسرة وغبنا وهكذا تعرض عليه خزائن أوقاته طول عمره فيقول لنفسه اجتهدى اليوم في أن تعمرى خزانتك ولا تدعيها فارغة عن كنوزك التي هي أسباب ملكك ولا تميلى إلى الكسل والدعه والاستراحة فيفوتك من درجات عليين ما يدركه غيرك وتبقى عندك حسرة لا تفارقك وإن دخلت الجنة فألم الغبن وحسرته لا يطاق وإن كان دون ألم النار وقد قال بعضهم هب أن المسىء قد عفى عنه أليس قد فاته ثواب المحسنين أشار به إلى الغبن والحسرة وقال الله تعالى يوم يجمعكم ليوم الجمع ذلك يوم التغابن فهذه وصيته لنفسه في أوقاته ثم ليستأنف لها وص
64:9.english: And how great is its regret and loss (ghubn). And thus are presented to him the treasuries of his times throughout his lifespan, so he says to his Soul (Nafs): 'Strive today to fill your treasury and do not leave it empty of your treasures which are the causes of your kingdom, and do not incline to laziness, relaxation, and rest, lest you miss from the degrees of the highest (ʿilliyyīn) what others attain, and there remains with you a regret that does not leave you, even if you enter Paradise, for the pain of loss (ghubn) and its regret is unbearable, even if it is less than the pain of the Fire.' And some have said: 'Suppose the sinner is forgiven, has he not missed the reward of the doers of good?' He indicated by this the loss (ghubn) and regret. And Allah the Exalted said: 'The Day He will assemble you for the Day of Assembly - that is the Day of Mutual Loss (al-Taghābun).' So this is his advice to his Soul (Nafs) regarding his times. Then he renews for it advice concerning its seven members, which are the eye, the ear, the tongue, the stomach, the private part, the hand, and the foot, and entrusts them to it, for they are subjects serving his Soul (Nafs) in this trade, and through them the works of this trade are completed. And indeed, Hell has seven gates, for each gate of them a portion is allotted, and those gates are specified for whoever disobeys Allah the Exalted with these members, so he advises it to guard them from their sins.
64:9.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

64:14.arabic: ولذلك حذر الله عباده من فتنة المال والزوج والولد فقال تعالى: ﴿ يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تلهكم أموالكم ولا أولادكم عن ذكر الله ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل: ﴿ ان من أزواجكم وأولادكم عدوا لكم فاحذروهم ﴾ {} وقال ﭬ: (الولد مبخلة مجبنة محزنة[19]). (ولما نظر عليه السلام الى ولده الحسن رضي الله عنه يتعثر في قميصه نزل عن المنبر واحتضنه ثم قال صدق الله ﴿ إنما اموالكم واولادكم فتنة ﴾ {} اني لما رأيت ابني يتعثر لم املك نفسي ان اخذته[20]) ففي ذلك عبرة لأولى الأبصار فالرجل كل الرجل من يصبر على العافية ومعنى الصبر عليها ان
64:14.english: Therefore, Allah warned His servants from the trial of wealth, spouse, and children, so He the Exalted said: 'O you who have believed, let not your wealth and your children divert you from the remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah' (Quran 63:9). And He the Mighty and Majestic said: 'Indeed, from your spouses and your children is an enemy to you, so beware of them' (Quran 64:14). And he (the Prophet, peace be upon him) said: 'The child is a miser-maker, a coward-maker, a sorrow-maker' (Hadith). (And when he (the Prophet, peace be upon him) saw his son Al-Hasan, may Allah be pleased with him, stumbling in his shirt, he descended from the pulpit and embraced him, then said: 'Allah has spoken the truth: "Your wealth and your children are but a trial"' (Quran 8:28). Indeed, when I saw my son stumbling, I could not control myself from taking him.) In that is a lesson for those of insight. The man, every man, is he who is patient upon well-being, and the meaning of patience upon it is that he does not rely on it and knows that all of that is a deposit with him, and perhaps it will be taken back soon, and that he does not let his soul (Nafs) go in rejoicing in it, nor does he immerse himself in enjoyment, pleasure, amusement, and play, and that he observes the rights of Allah in his wealth through spending, in his body through offering assistance to creation, in his tongue through offering truthfulness, and likewise in all that Allah has bestowed upon him. And this patience is connected to gratitude, so it is not complete except by fulfilling the right of gratitude as will come. And indeed, patience upon prosperity is more severe because it is accompanied by ability, and from protection is that you are not able. And patience upon cupping and intention when someone else undertakes it is easier than patience upon bleeding yourself and cupping yourself. And the hungry person in the absence of food is more capable of patience than when delicious, tasty foods are present to him and he has ability over them. For this reason, the trial of prosperity is great.
64:14.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

64:14.arabic: فإن قلت: فقد أدخلت المال والجاه والنسب والأهل والولد في حيز النعم، وقد ذم الله تعالى المال والجاه وكذا رسول ﭬ[72] وكذا العلماء قال تعالى: ﴿ إن من أزواجكم وأولادكم عدوا لكم فاحذروهم ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل: ﴿ إنما أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة ﴾ {}. وقال علي كرم الله وجهه في ذم النسب: الناس أبناء ما يحسنون وقيمة كل امرىء ما يحسنه، وقيل المرء بنفسه لا بأبيه فما معنى كونها نعمة مع كونها مذمومة شرعا. فاعلم أن من يأخذ العلوم من الألفاظ المنقولة المؤولة والعمومات المخصصة كان الضلال عليه اغلب ما لم يهتد بنور الله تعا
64:14.english: If you say: You have included wealth, status, lineage, family, and children in the category of blessings (Ni'am), yet Allah the Exalted has censured wealth and status, and likewise the Messenger (peace be upon him) and the scholars. Allah said: 'Indeed, among your spouses and your children is an enemy to you, so beware of them' (Quran 64:14). And He the Almighty said: 'Your wealth and your children are only a trial (Fitnah)' (Quran 8:28). And Ali (may Allah honor his face) said in censuring lineage: 'People are children of what they excel at, and the value of every person is what he excels at,' and it is said: 'A person is by himself, not by his father.' So what is the meaning of them being a blessing while being censured religiously (Shar'an)? Know that whoever takes knowledge from transmitted words that are interpreted (Mu'awwalah) and generalities that are specified (Makhsusah), misguidance (Dhalal) is more prevalent upon him unless he is guided by the light (Nur) of Allah the Exalted to comprehend the sciences as they truly are, then he applies the transmission in accordance with what has become clear to him from them, sometimes through interpretation (Ta'wil) and other times through specification (Takhsis). These are blessings (Ni'am) that assist in the matter of the Hereafter (Akhirah), with no way to deny them except that they contain trials (Fitnah) and dangers (Makhawif). The example of wealth is like a snake that contains beneficial antidote (Tiryaq) and beneficial poison (Samm). If it is obtained by the charmer (Al-Mu'azzim) who knows the method of precaution (Ihtiraz) from its poison and the way to extract its beneficial antidote, it becomes a blessing. But if it is obtained by the ignorant black one (Al-Sawadi Al-Ghar), it is upon him affliction (Bala') and destruction (Halak). It is like the sea beneath which are varieties of jewels (Jawahir) and pearls (La'ali). Whoever attains the sea, if he is knowledgeable about swimming (Sibahah), the method of diving (Ghawas), and the method of precaution from the destructive aspects of the sea, he has attained its blessings. But if he enters it ignorant of that, he has perished. Therefore, Allah the Exalted praised wealth and called it good (Khayr), and the Messenger (peace be upon him) praised it and said: 'What a good aid (A'un) for the God-consciousness (Taqwa) of Allah the Exalted is wealth.'
64:14.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

64:14.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
64:14.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: 'Whatever is in the Quran of "O you who have believed" is in the Torah "O you poor ones (al-Masakin)"'.
