64:14.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

64:15.arabic: ولما نظر عليه السلام الى ولده الحسن رضي الله عنه يتعثر في قميصه نزل عن المنبر واحتضنه ثم قال صدق الله ﴿ إنما اموالكم واولادكم فتنة ﴾ {} اني لما رأيت ابني يتعثر لم املك نفسي ان اخذته[20]) ففي ذلك عبرة لأولى الأبصار
64:15.english: And when the Prophet (peace be upon him) saw his son Al-Hasan (may Allah be pleased with him) stumbling in his shirt, he descended from the pulpit and embraced him, then said: 'Allah has spoken the truth: "Indeed, your wealth and your children are a trial (Fitnah)." I, when I saw my son stumbling, could not control my soul (Nafs) from taking him.' In that is a lesson for those of insight.
64:15.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

64:15.arabic: قال الله تعالى "يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تلهكم أموالكم ولا أولادكم عن ذكر الله ومن يفعل ذلك فأولئك هم الخاسرون" وقال تعالى "إنما أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة والله عنده أجر عظيم" فمن اختار ماله وولده على ما عند الله فقد خسر وغبن خسراناً عظيماً.
64:15.english: Allah the Exalted said: "O you who have believed, let not your wealth and your children divert you from the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah. And whoever does that - then those are the losers." And He the Exalted said: "Indeed, your wealth and your children are a trial (Fitnah). And Allah - with Him is a great reward." So whoever chooses his wealth and his child over what is with Allah has lost and been cheated a great loss.
64:15.book_title: Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth
64:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

64:15.arabic: فإن قلت: فقد أدخلت المال والجاه والنسب والأهل والولد في حيز النعم، وقد ذم الله تعالى المال والجاه وكذا رسول ﭬ[72] وكذا العلماء قال تعالى: ﴿ إن من أزواجكم وأولادكم عدوا لكم فاحذروهم ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل: ﴿ إنما أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة ﴾ {}. وقال علي كرم الله وجهه في ذم النسب: الناس أبناء ما يحسنون وقيمة كل امرىء ما يحسنه، وقيل المرء بنفسه لا بأبيه فما معنى كونها نعمة مع كونها مذمومة شرعا. فاعلم أن من يأخذ العلوم من الألفاظ المنقولة المؤولة والعمومات المخصصة كان الضلال عليه اغلب ما لم يهتد بنور الله تعا
64:15.english: If you say: You have included wealth, status, lineage, family, and children within the realm of blessings, yet Allah the Exalted has censured wealth and status, and likewise the Messenger (peace be upon him) and the scholars. Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them' (64:14). And He the Almighty said: 'Indeed, your wealth and your children are a trial (Fitnah)' (64:15). And Ali (may Allah honor his face) said in censuring lineage: People are children of what they excel at, and the value of every person is what he excels at, and it is said a person is by himself, not by his father. So what is the meaning of them being a blessing while being censured religiously? Know that whoever takes knowledge from transmitted words that are interpreted and generalities that are specified, misguidance is more prevalent upon him unless he is guided by the light (Nur) of Allah the Exalted to comprehend the sciences as they truly are, then he applies the transmission in accordance with what has become clear to him from them through interpretation at times and specification at others. These are blessings aiding in the matter of the Hereafter, with no way to deny them except that within them are trials (Fitnah) and fears. The example of wealth is like a snake that contains beneficial antidote and beneficial poison. If it is obtained by the charmer who knows the method of precaution from its poison and the way to extract its beneficial antidote, it is a blessing. But if it is obtained by the ignorant commoner, it is upon him affliction and destruction. And it is like the sea beneath which are varieties of jewels and pearls. Whoever attains the sea, if he is knowledgeable in swimming, the way of diving, and the way of precaution from the perils of the sea, he has attained its blessings. But if he enters it ignorant of that, he has perished. Therefore, Allah the Exalted praised wealth and called it good, and the Messenger (peace be upon him) praised it and said: 'What an excellent aid to the God-consciousness (Taqwa) of Allah the Exalted is wealth.' And likewise, He praised status and honor, as Allah the Exalted bestowed upon His Messenger (peace be upon him) by manifesting him...
64:15.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

64:15.arabic: وإسناده صحيح وتعثر الحسن والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على منبره فنزل فحمله وقرأ قوله إنما أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة حديث عثر الحسن وهو على منبره صلى الله عليه وسلم فنزل فحمله وقرأ قوله تعالى إنما أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة أخرجه أصحاب السنن من حديث بريدة في الحسن والحسين معا يمشيان ويعثران قال الترمذي حسن غريب
64:15.english: And its chain of transmission is authentic. And Al-Hasan stumbled while the Prophet (peace be upon him) was on his pulpit, so he descended and carried him and recited His saying: 'Indeed, your wealth and your children are a trial (Fitnah).' The hadith: Al-Hasan stumbled while he (peace be upon him) was on his pulpit, so he descended and carried him and recited the saying of Allah the Exalted: 'Indeed, your wealth and your children are a trial (Fitnah).' It was reported by the compilers of the Sunan from the hadith of Buraidah concerning Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn together walking and stumbling. At-Tirmidhi said: 'Hasan (good) Gharib (rare).'
64:15.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

64:16.arabic:
بيان ذم البخل
قال الله تعالى "ومن يوق شح نفسه فأولئك هم المفلحون" وقال تعالى "ولا يحسبن الذين يبخلون بما آتاهم الله من فضله هو خيراً لهم بل هو شر لهم سيطوقون ما بخلوا به يوم القيامة" وقال تعالى "الذين يبخلون ويأمرون الناس بالبخل ويكتمون ما آتاهم الله من فضله" وقال ﭬ "إياكم والشح فإنه أهلك من كان قبلكم، حملهم على أن سفكوا دماءهم واستحلوا محارمهم"[75] وقال ﭬ "إياكم والشح فإنه دعا من كان قبلكم فسفكوا دماءهم ودعاهم فاستحلوا محارمهم ودعاهم فقطعوا أرحامهم"[76] وقال ﭬ "لا يدخل الجنة بخيل ولا خب ولا خائ
64:16.english: Explanation of the condemnation of miserliness. Allah the Exalted said: "And whoever is protected from the greed (Shuh) of his Soul (Nafs), then those are the successful ones." And Allah the Exalted said: "And let not those who are miserly with what Allah has given them of His bounty think it is good for them; rather, it is bad for them. They will be made to wear what they were miserly with on the Day of Resurrection." And Allah the Exalted said: "Those who are miserly and enjoin miserliness upon people and conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty." And he (the Prophet) ﷺ said: "Beware of greed (Shuh), for it destroyed those before you; it drove them to shed their blood and make lawful what was forbidden to them." [75] And he ﷺ said: "Beware of greed (Shuh), for it called those before you, so they shed their blood, and it called them, so they made lawful what was forbidden to them, and it called them, so they severed their kinship ties." [76] And he ﷺ said: "The miser (Bakhil), the treacherous, the betrayer, and the one of bad character will not enter Paradise." [77] In a narration: "Nor the tyrant." In a narration: "Nor the one who reminds of his favors." And he ﷺ said: "Three destructive things: obeyed greed (Shuh), followed desire (Hawa), and a person's admiration of himself." [78] And he ﷺ said: "Indeed, Allah hates three: the old fornicator, the miser (Bakhil) who reminds of his favors, and the poor arrogant." [79] And he ﷺ said: "The example of the spender and the miser (Bakhil) is like two men wearing iron shirts from their chests to their collarbones. As for the spender, he does not spend anything except that it spreads or increases over his skin until it hides his fingertips. As for the miser (Bakhil), he does not intend to spend anything except that it shrinks and sticks to every part of his throat until it takes hold of his collarbones, and he widens it but it does not widen." [80] And he ﷺ said: "Two traits do not combine in a believer: miserliness (Bukhl) and bad character." [8
64:16.book_title: Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth
64:16.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

64:16.arabic: المعنى الثاني التطهير من صفة البخل فإنه من المهلكات قال ﭬ: (ثلاث مهلكات شح مطاع وهوى متبع وإعجاب المرء بنفسه[9]) وقال تعالى: ﴿ ومن يوق شح نفسه فأولئك هم المفلحون ﴾ {} وسيأتي في ربع المهلكات وجه كونه مهلكا وكيفية التقصي منه وإنما تزول صفة البخل بأن تتعود بذل المال فحب الشيء لا ينقطع إلا بقهر النفس على مفارقته حتى يصير ذلك اعتيادا فالزكاة بهذا المعنى طهرة أي تطهر صاحبها عن خبث البخل المهلك وإنما طهارته بقدر بذله وبقدر فرحه بإخراجه واستبشاره بصرفه إلى الله تعالى.
64:16.english: The second meaning: The purification from the attribute of miserliness, for it is among the destroyers. He (the Prophet) said: 'Three destroyers: obeyed miserliness, followed desire, and self-admiration.' And Allah the Exalted said: 'And whoever is protected from the miserliness of his soul (Nafs), then those are the successful ones.' And it will come in the quarter of the destroyers the aspect of it being a destroyer and how to be cautious from it. And indeed, the attribute of miserliness only vanishes by accustoming oneself to giving wealth, for the love of something does not cease except by forcing the soul (Nafs) to part with it until that becomes a habit. So, Zakat in this meaning is a purification, meaning it purifies its possessor from the filth of the destroying miserliness. And its purification is according to the measure of his giving and according to the measure of his joy in expending it and his gladness in directing it to Allah the Exalted.
64:16.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

64:16.arabic: ويحك! أما علمت أن البخل كفر وأن الكفر في النار، ويحك! أما علم أن الله تعالى يقول "ومن يبخل فإنما يبخل عن نفسه... ومن يوق شح نفسه فأولئك هم المفلحون"[98].
64:16.english: Woe to you! Do you not know that miserliness (Bakhl) is disbelief (Kufr) and that disbelief is in the Fire? Woe to you! Do you not know that Allah the Exalted says: "And whoever is miserly is only miserly against his own soul... And whoever is protected from the greed (Shuhh) of his own soul (Nafs), then those are the successful ones."
64:16.book_title: Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth
64:16.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

65:1.arabic: ولذلك قال الله تعالى: ﴿ ومن يتعد حدود الله فقد ظلم نفسه ﴾ {} ولأن أصول هذه المعانى لا تختلف فيها الشرائع وإنما تختلف في وجوه التحديد كما يحد شرع عيسى ابن مريم عليه السلام تحريم الخمر بالسكر وقد حده شرعنا بكونه من جنس المسكر لأن قليله يدعو إلى كثير والداخل في الحدود داخل في التحريم بحكم الجنس كما دخل أصل المعنى بالجملة الأصلية فهذا مثال واحد لحكمه خفية من حكم النقدين فينبغى أن يعتبر شكر النعمة وكفرانها بهذا المثال فكل ما خلق لحكمة فينبغى أن يصرف عنها ولا يعرف هذا إلا من قد عرف الحكمة - ومن يؤت ال
65:1.english: Therefore, Allah the Exalted said: 'And whoever transgresses the boundaries (hudud) of Allah has indeed wronged his own soul (nafs).' {} Because the foundations of these meanings do not differ among the divine laws (shara'i'), but they differ in the aspects of specification (tahdid), just as the law (shar') of Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him, specified the prohibition of wine (khamr) by intoxication (sukr), while our law (shar') specified it by being of the intoxicating kind (jins al-muskir) because a little of it leads to much. And what falls within the boundaries (hudud) falls within the prohibition by the ruling of the kind (jins), just as the original meaning entered in the original totality. This is one example of its hidden ruling from the ruling of the two currencies. Therefore, one should consider gratitude (shukr) for the blessing (ni'mah) and ingratitude (kufran) with this example, for everything created for a wisdom (hikmah) should be directed away from it, and none knows this except one who has known the wisdom (hikmah) - 'And whoever is given wisdom (hikmah) has been given much good' - but the jewels of wisdom (hikmah) do not encounter hearts (qulub) that are dunghills of desires (shahawat) and playgrounds of devils (shayatin); rather, none remember except those of understanding (ulu al-albab). And therefore, He said: 'Were it not that the devils (shayatin) hover around the hearts (qulub) of the children of Adam, they would look at the dominion (malakut) of the heavens.' And when you have known this example, then measure against it your movement and stillness, your speech and silence, and every action issuing from you, for it is either gratitude (shukr) or ingratitude (kufr), as it is inconceivable to be free from them. And some of that is described in the language of jurisprudence (fiqh) that the common people speak with as disliked (makruh) and some as dangerous (khatr), and all of that is described as dangerous (khatr) by the possessors of hearts (arbab al-qulub).
65:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

65:1.arabic: ولكل واحد من ذلك حدود لابد من مراعاتها بدوام المراقبة ومن يتعد حدود الله فقد ظلم نفسه فينبغي أن يتفقد العبد نفسه في جميع أوقاته في هذه الأقسام الثلاثة
65:1.english: And for each one of these there are limits that must be observed through constant vigilance (Muraqaba), and whoever transgresses the limits of Allah has wronged his own soul (Nafs). Therefore, the servant (Abd) should examine himself in all his times within these three divisions.
65:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

65:1.arabic: الثاني عشر في الطلاق وليعلم أنه مباح ولكنه أبغض المباحات إلى الله تعالى وإنما يكون مباحا إذا لم يكن فيه إيذاء بالباطل ومهما طلقها فقد آذاها ولا يباح إيذاء الغير إلا بجناية من جانبها أو بضرورة من جانبه قال الله تعالى (فإن أطعنكم فلا تبغوا عليهن سبيلا) أي لا تطلبوا حيلة للفراق وإن كرهها أبوه فليطلقها قال ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما كان تحتي امرأة أحبها وكان أبي يكرهها ويأمرني بطلاقها فراجعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال يا ابن عمر طلق امرأتك فهذا يدل على أن حق الوالد مقدم ولكن والد يكرهها لا لغرض ف
65:1.english: The twelfth [chapter] is on divorce, and it should be known that it is permissible but it is the most detested of permissible things to Allah the Exalted. It is only permissible if there is no harm without right, and whenever he divorces her, he has harmed her. It is not permissible to harm others except due to a transgression from her side or a necessity from his side. Allah the Exalted said: (Then if they obey you, do not seek a way against them) meaning do not seek a stratagem for separation. And if her father dislikes her, let him divorce her. Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: I had a wife whom I loved, and my father disliked her and ordered me to divorce her, so I consulted the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said: O Ibn Umar, divorce your wife. This indicates that the right of the parent takes precedence, but a parent who dislikes her without a corrupt purpose like Umar. And whenever she harms her husband and is insolent toward his family, she is a transgressor. Likewise, if she is of bad character or corrupt in religion. Ibn Mas'ud said regarding His statement, the Exalted: 'nor should they leave except that they commit a clear immorality' - whenever she is insolent toward his family and harms her husband, that is an immorality. This is intended for the waiting period, but it is an indication of the intended meaning. And if the harm is from the husband, she may ransom herself by giving wealth; it is disliked for the man to take from her more than what he gave, for that is injustice against her and oppression upon her and trading on the private part. He, the Exalted, said: 'Then there is no blame upon them for what she gives back.' So returning what he took or less is suitable for the ransom. If she asks for divorce without any wrongdoing, she is sinful. He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: (Any woman who asks her husband for divorce without any wrongdoing will not smell the fragrance of Paradise). In another wording: 'Paradise is forbidden to her.' And in another wording: He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: (The women who seek khul' are the hypocrites). Then the husband should observe four matters in divorce: The first is that he divorce her in a state of purity in which he has not had intercourse with her, for divorce during menstruation or the purity in which he had intercourse is called forbidden, even if it occurs, due to what it contains of prolonging the waiting period upon her. If he does that, let him take her back. Ibn Umar divorced his wife during menstruation, so He, peace and blessings be upon him, said to Umar: Command him to take her back until she becomes pure, then she menstruates, then she becomes pure, then if he wishes, he divorces her, and if he wishes, he retains her. That is the waiting period which Allah commanded to divorce women for. And He commanded him to be patient after taking her back for two purity periods so that the purpose of taking back is not...
65:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

65:2.arabic: الثالثة: أن ينظر فيما يأخذه فإن لم يكن من حل تورع عنه ومن يتق الله يجعل له مخرجا ويرزقه من حيث لا يحتسب ولن يعدم المتورع عن الحرام فتوحا من الحلال فلا يأخذ من أموال الأتراك والجنود وعمال السلاطين ومن أكثر كسبه من الحرام إلا إذا ضاق الأمر عليه وكان ما يسلم إليه لا يعرف له مالكا معينا فله أن يأخذ بقدر الحاجة فإن فتوى الشرع في مثل هذا أن يتصدق به على ما سيأتي بيانه في كتاب الحلال والحرام وذلك إذا عجز عن الحلال فإذا أخذ لم يكن أخذه أخذ زكاة إذ لا يقع زكاة عن مؤديه وهو حرام.
65:2.english: The third: That he looks at what he takes; if it is not from lawful (Halal) sources, he should abstain from it. And whoever is God-fearing (Yattaqi Allah) [i.e., practices God-consciousness (Taqwa)], He will make for him a way out and provide for him from where he does not expect. And the one who abstains from the forbidden (Haram) will not lack openings from the lawful (Halal). So he should not take from the wealth of the Turks, soldiers, and the agents of sultans, and from those whose earnings are mostly from the forbidden (Haram), except when the matter becomes tight for him and what is handed to him has no known specific owner; then he may take according to need. For the legal ruling (Fatwa) in such a case is that he should give it in charity (Tasaddaqa), as will be explained in the book of the lawful (Halal) and the forbidden (Haram). And that is when he is unable to find lawful (Halal) means. If he takes it, his taking is not considered taking of alms (Zakat), since alms (Zakat) does not apply to one who gives it, and it is forbidden (Haram).
65:2.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

65:2.arabic: فإذن عليك بالقناعة بالنزر القليل والرضا بالقوت فإنه يأتيك لا محالة وإن فررت منه، وعند ذلك على الله أن يبعث إليك رزقك على يدي من لا تحتسب، فإن اشتغلت بالتقوى شاهدت بالتجربة مصداق قوله تعالى: " ومن يتق الله يجعل له مخرجاً ويرزقه من حيث لا يحتسب " الآية، إلا أنه لم يتكفل له أن يرزقه لحم الطير ولذائذ الأطعمة، فما ضمن إلا الرزق الذي تدوم به حياته، وهذا المضمون مبذول كل من اشتغل بالضامن واطمأن إلى ضمانه؛ فإن الذي أحاط به تدبير الله من الأسباب الخفية للرزق أعظم مما ظهر للخلق، بل مداخل الرزق لا تحصى ومج
65:2.english: Therefore, upon you is contentment with the little amount and satisfaction with the sustenance, for it will come to you inevitably even if you flee from it, and at that point, it is upon Allah to send to you your provision at the hands of one you do not expect. If you occupy yourself with God-consciousness (Taqwa), you will witness through experience the truth of His saying, the Exalted: 'And whoever is conscious of Allah (Yattaqi Allah), He will make for him a way out and provide for him from where he does not expect' (Quran 65:2-3), except that He has not guaranteed to provide him with the meat of birds and delights of foods, but only guaranteed the provision by which his life continues, and this guarantee is granted to everyone who occupies themselves with the Guarantor and is reassured by His guarantee; for what encompasses it from the hidden causes of provision by the arrangement of Allah is greater than what has appeared to creation, indeed the entrances of provision cannot be counted and its channels cannot be guided to, and that is because its appearance is on earth and its cause is in the heaven, Allah the Exalted said: 'And in the heaven is your provision and what you are promised' (Quran 51:22), and the secrets of the heaven are not disclosed, and for this reason a group entered upon Al-Junayd and he said: What do you seek? They said: We seek provision. He said: If you know in which place it is, then seek it. They said: We ask Allah. He said: If you know that He forgets you, then remind Him. They said: We enter the house and rely (Natawakkal) and see what will be. He said: Reliance (Tawakkul) based on experience is doubt. They said: So what is the remedy? He said: Abandoning the remedy.
65:2.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

65:2.arabic: ق  الجوار  اعلم  أن الجوار يقضي حقا وراء ما تقتضيه أخوة الإسلام فيستحق الجار  المسلم  ما  يستحقه كل مسلم وزيادة إذ قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الجيران ثلاثة جار له حق  واحد وجار له حقان وجار له ثلاثة حقوق فالجار الذي له ثلاثة حقوق  الجار  المسلم  ذو الرحم فله حق الجوار وحق الإسلام وحق الرحم وأما الذي له  حقان  فالجار  المسلم له حق الجوار وحق الإسلام وأما الذي له حق واحد  فالجار  المشرك  حديث  الجيران ثلاثة جار له حق وجار له حقان وجار له ثلاثة حقوق الحديث أخرجه الحسن بن  سفيان والبزار في مسنديهم
65:2.english: Chapter on Neighbors. Know that neighborliness imposes a right beyond what the brotherhood of Islam requires, so the Muslim neighbor deserves what every Muslim deserves and more, for the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Neighbors are three: a neighbor with one right, a neighbor with two rights, and a neighbor with three rights. The neighbor with three rights is the Muslim neighbor who is a relative, so he has the right of neighborliness, the right of Islam, and the right of kinship. As for the one with two rights, it is the Muslim neighbor who has the right of neighborliness and the right of Islam. As for the one with one right, it is the polytheist neighbor.' The hadith 'Neighbors are three: a neighbor with one right, a neighbor with two rights, and a neighbor with three rights' was reported by Al-Hasan bin Sufyan and Al-Bazzar in their Musnads, Abu Al-Sheikh in Kitab Al-Thawab, and Abu Nu'aym in Al-Hilyah from the narration of Jabir, and Ibn 'Adi from the narration of 'Abdullah bin 'Umar, and both are weak. See how he affirmed a right for the polytheist merely due to neighborliness. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Be the best neighbor to whoever neighbors you, and you will be a Muslim.' The hadith 'Be the best neighbor to whoever neighbors you, and you will be a Muslim' was mentioned earlier. And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Jibril kept advising me about the neighbor until I thought he would make him an heir.' The hadith 'Jibril kept advising me about the neighbor until I thought he would make him an heir' is agreed upon from the narration of 'A'ishah and Ibn 'Umar. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his neighbor.' The hadith 'Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his neighbor' is agreed upon from the narration of Abu Shuraih. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'A servant does not believe until his neighbor is safe from his harms.' The hadith 'A servant does not believe until his neighbor is safe from his harms' was reported by Al-Bukhari from the narration of Abu Shuraih as well. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The first two disputants on the Day of Resurrection will be two neighbors.' The hadith 'The first two disputants on the Day of Resurrection will be two neighbors' was reported by Ahmad and Al-Tabarani from the narration of 'Uqbah bin 'Amir with a weak chain. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'If you throw a stone at your neighbor's dog, you have harmed him.' The hadith 'If you throw a stone at your neighbor's dog, you have harmed him' I did not find a source for. And it is narrated that a man came to Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) and said to him: 'I have a neighbor who harms me, insults me, and makes things difficult for me.' He said: 'Go, and if he disobeys Allah regarding you, then obey Allah regarding him.' And it was said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him): 'So-and-so woman fasts during the day and prays at night, but she harms her neighbors.' He said: 'She is in the Fire.' The hadith 'So-and-so woman fasts during the day and prays at night, but she harms her neighbors, so he said: She is in the Fire' was reported by Ahmad and Al-Hakim from the narration of Abu Hurairah, and he said its chain is authentic. And a man came to him (peace be upon him) complaining about his neighbor, so the Prophet (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Be patient.' Then he said to him on the third or fourth time: 'Put your belongings in the road.' He said: So people passed by him and said: 'What is this?'
65:2.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

65:2.arabic: وقال الله تعالى ومن يتق الله يجعل له مخرجا من الإشكالات والشبه ويرزقه من حيث لا يحتسب يعلمه علما من غير تعلم ويفطنه من غير تجربة
65:2.english: And Allah the Exalted said: 'And whoever is God-fearing (Yattaqi Allah) makes for him a way out from the difficulties and doubts, and provides for him from where he does not reckon, teaches him knowledge without learning, and makes him discerning without experience.'
65:2.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

65:2.arabic: ولا ينفك الإنسان عن الحرص إلا بحسن ثقته بتدبير الله تعالى في تقدير أرزاق العباد، وأن ذلك يحصل لا محالة مع الإجمال في الطلب، بل ينبغي أن يعلم أن رزق الله للعبد من حيث لا يحتسب أكثر قال الله تعالى "ومن يتق الله يجعل له مخرجاً ويرزقه من حيث لا يحتسب" فإذا انسد عليه الباب كان ينتظر الرزق منه فلا ينبغي أن يضطرب قلبه لأجله، وقال ﷺ "أبى الله أن يرزق عبده المؤمن إلا من حيث لا يحتسب"[44] وقال سفيان: اتق الله فما رأيت تقياً محتاجاً. أي لا يترك التقى فاقداً لضرورته، بل يلقى الله في قلوب المسلمين أن يوصلوا
65:2.english: And the human being does not break free from greed except through good trust in the arrangement (tadbir) of Allah the Exalted in the apportioning of the provisions (arzaq) of the servants, and that this occurs inevitably with moderation in seeking. Rather, it is necessary to know that the provision (rizq) of Allah for the servant from where he does not reckon is greater. Allah the Exalted said: "And whoever is God-fearing (yattaqi) Allah, He makes for him a way out and provides for him from where he does not reckon." So if the door is closed upon him, he should expect the provision (rizq) from it, and it is not appropriate for his heart (qalb) to be agitated because of it. And the Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah refuses to provide for His believing servant except from where he does not reckon." And Sufyan said: Be God-fearing (ittaqi) Allah, for I have not seen a God-fearing (taqiyyan) person in need. Meaning, He does not leave the God-fearing (taqwa) one lacking his necessity, but rather Allah casts into the hearts (qulub) of the Muslims that they convey to him his provision (rizq).
65:2.book_title: Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth
65:2.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

65:3.arabic:
شاة المسمومة رواه أبو داود من حديث جابر وفيه انقطاع وحديث أنه دمى
     وجهه وكسرت رباعيته متفق عليه من حديث سهل بن سعد في غزوة أحد وحديث اللهم
   اغفر لقومي فإنهم لا يعلمون رواه البيهقي في دلائل النبوة والحديث في الصحيح
   من حديث ابن مسعود أنه ﭬ حكاه عن نبي من الأنبياء ضربه قومه وحديث لبس الصوف
  رواه الطيالسي من حديث سهل بن سعد وحديث ركوبه الحمار وإردافه خلفه متفق عليه
      من حديث أسامة بن زيد وحديث وضع طعامه بالأرض رواه أحمد في الزهد من حديث
  الحسن مرسلا وللبخاري من حديث أنس ما أكل رسول ال
65:3.english: [109] Hadith: Whoever increases in seeking forgiveness (Istighfar), Allah makes for him from every distress a relief and from every grief an exit, and provides for him from where he does not reckon. Reported by Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i in al-Yawm wa al-Laylah, Ibn Majah, and al-Hakim, who said its chain is authentic (Sahih al-Isnad) from the narration of Ibn 'Abbas, and Ibn Hibban weakened it.
65:3.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication

65:7.arabic: ومن كان غرضه الرفق وطلب الثواب به فله أن يستقرض على حسن الظن بالله لا على اعتماد السلاطين الظلمة، فإن رزقه الله من حلال قضاه. وغن مات قبل القضاء قضاه الله تعالى عنه وأرضى غرماءه، وذلك بشرط أن يكون مكشوف الحال عند من يقرضه فلا يغر المقرض ولا يخدعه بالمواعيد بل يكشف حاله عنده ليقدم على إقراضه على بصيرة، ودين مثل هذا الرجل واجب أن يقضى من مال بيت المال ومن الزكاة، وقد قال تعالى: " ومن قدر عليه رزقه فلينفق مما آتاه الله " قيل معناه: ليبع أحد ثوبيه. وقيل معناه: فليستقرض بجاهه، فذلك مما آتاه الله. وقا
65:7.english: And whoever intends kindness and seeks reward through it, he may borrow based on good expectation (husn al-zann) of Allah, not relying on oppressive rulers. If Allah provides him from lawful means, he repays it. And if he dies before repayment, Allah repays it on his behalf and satisfies his creditors, provided that his situation is disclosed to the one who lends to him, so he does not deceive the lender nor trick him with promises, but reveals his situation to him so that he proceeds with lending with insight. The debt of such a man is obligatory to be repaid from the treasury (bayt al-mal) and from alms (zakah). And Allah the Exalted said: "And whoever is constrained in his provision, let him spend from what Allah has given him." It is said its meaning: let him sell one of his two garments. And it is said its meaning: let him borrow through his status, for that is from what Allah has given him. And some of them said: Verily, Allah the Exalted has servants who spend according to the measure of their goods, and Allah has servants who spend according to the measure of good expectation (husn al-zann) of Allah the Exalted.
65:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

65:11.arabic: الحمد لله الذي بيده مقاليد الأمور، وبقدرته مفاتيح الخيرات والشرور، مخرج أوليائه من الظلمات إلى النور، ومورد أعدائه ورطات الغرور، والصلاة على محمد مخرج الخلائق من الديجور، وعلى آله وأصحابه الذين لم تغرهم الحياة الدنيا ولم يغرهم بالله الغرور، صلاة تتوالى على ممر الدهور ومكر الساعات والشهور. أما بعد: فمفتاح السعادة التيقظ والفطنة، ومنبع الشقاوة الغرور والغفلة فلا نعمة لله على عباده أعظم من الإيمان والمعرفة، ولا وسيلة سوى انشراح الصدر بنور البصيرة، ولا نقمة أعظم من الكفر والمعصية، ولا داعي إليهما سو
65:11.english: Praise be to Allah who in His hand are the keys of affairs, and by His power are the keys of good and evil, who brings out His allies from the darknesses to the light, and brings His enemies into the pits of delusion, and prayers upon Muhammad, the bringer out of creation from the darkness, and upon his family and companions who were not deluded by the worldly life and were not deluded about Allah by delusion, prayers that continue through the passage of ages and the plotting of hours and months. After: The key to happiness is vigilance and insight, and the source of misery is delusion and heedlessness, so there is no blessing from Allah upon His servants greater than faith and knowledge, and no means except the expansion of the chest with the light of insight, and no punishment greater than disbelief and disobedience, and no caller to them except the blindness of the heart with the darkness of ignorance. The intelligent ones and possessors of insights, their hearts are "like a niche containing a lamp, the lamp in a glass, the glass as if it were a brilliant star, lit from a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if untouched by fire - light upon light" (Quran 24:35). And the deluded ones, their hearts are "like darknesses in a deep sea covered by waves, upon which are waves, above which are clouds - darknesses, one above another. If one stretches out his hand, he can hardly see it. And he for whom Allah has not made light - for him there is no light" (Quran 24:40). The intelligent ones are those whom Allah intended to guide, so He expanded their chests for Islam and guidance. And the deluded ones are those whom Allah intended to misguide, so He made their chests tight and constricted as if they were climbing into the sky. And the deluded person is the one whose insight has not opened to be sufficient for the guidance of his soul and
65:11.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

65:12.arabic: ما شاء الله كان وما لم يشأ لم يكن أعلم أن الله على كل شيء قدير وأن الله قد أحاط بكل شيء علما وأحصى كل شيء عددا اللهم إني أعوذ بك من شر نفسي ومن شر كل دابة أنت آخذ بناصيتها إن ربي على صراط مستقيم[134]
65:12.english: What Allah wills happens, and what He does not will does not happen. I know that Allah is over every thing powerful (Qadir) and that Allah has encompassed every thing in knowledge ('Ilm) and has counted every thing in number. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of my soul (Nafs) and from the evil of every creature You take by its forelock. Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path (Sirat Mustaqim).
65:12.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith

66:3.arabic: فقلت: من أين عرفت اسمي واسم أبي وما رأيتك قبل اليوم؟ "قال نبأني العليم الخبير" وعرفت روحي روحك حين كلمت نفسي نفسك، إن الأرواح لها أنفس كأنفس الأجساد وإن المؤمنين ليعرف بعضهم بعضاً ويتحابون بروح الله وإن لم يلتقوا، يتعارفون ويتكلمون وإن نأت بهم الدار وتفرقت بهم المنازل
66:3.english: I said: From where did you know my name and my father's name when I have not seen you before today? "He said: The All-Knowing, the All-Aware informed me" and my spirit (Ruh) recognized your spirit (Ruh) when my soul (Nafs) spoke to your soul (Nafs). Indeed, the spirits (Arwah) have souls (Anfus) like the souls (Anfus) of the bodies, and indeed the believers recognize one another and love one another through the spirit (Ruh) of Allah even if they do not meet; they become acquainted and speak even if the abode distances them and the dwellings scatter them.
66:3.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of the World'

66:3.arabic: وقال علي كرم الله وجهه والله ما استقصى كريم قط حقه. قال الله تعالى "عرف بعضه وأعرض عن بعض" وقال الجاحظ: ما بقي من اللذات إلا ثلث ذم البخلاء، وأكل القديد، وحك الجرب.
66:3.english: And Ali, may Allah honor his face, said: By Allah, a generous person never exacts his full right. Allah the Exalted said: "He acknowledged some of it and turned away from some." And Al-Jahiz said: Nothing remains of pleasures except three: condemning the miserly, eating dried meat, and scratching scabies.
66:3.book_title: Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth
66:3.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

66:4.arabic:
فكسري العظام بسيفه فإن  سكت  فاجعلي  الإكاف  على  ظهره  وامتطيه
فإنما هو حمارك.
وعلى الجملة فبالعدل قامت السموات والأرض  فكل  ما  جاوز  حده  انعكس  على  ضده
فينبغي أن تسلك سبيل الاقتصاد في المخالفة والموافقة وتتبع الحق  في  جميع  ذلك
لتسلم من شرهن فإن (كيدهن عظيم) وشرهن فاش  والغالب  عليهن  سوء  الخلق  وركاكة
العقل ولا يعتدل ذلك منهن إلا بنوع لطف ممزوج بسياسة. وقال صلى الله عليه  وسلم
 (مثل المرأة الصالحة في  النساء  كمثل  الغراب  الأعصم  بين  مائة  غراب)[108]
والاعصم يعني الأبيض البطن وفي وصية
66:4.english: [111] Hadith: The revelation of His saying, the Exalted: 'If you both turn to Allah, your hearts have indeed inclined...' regarding the best of his wives. Agreed upon from the narration of Umar.
66:4.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

66:4.arabic: وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم في خيرات النساء (إنكن صواحبات يوسف)[110] يعني أن صرفكن أبا بكر عن التقدم في الصلاة ميل منكن عن الحق إلى الهوى قال الله تعالى حين أفشين سر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم (إن تتوبا إلى الله فقد صغت قلوبكما) أي مالت وقال ذلك في خير أزواجه[111] والمرأتان عائشة وحفصة.
66:4.english: And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said regarding the good women: 'You are the companions of Yusuf (Joseph),'[110] meaning that your turning Abu Bakr away from leading the prayer is a deviation from you from the Truth (al-Haqq) to the Desire (al-Hawa). Allah the Exalted said when they disclosed the secret of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him): 'If you both turn in repentance to Allah, your hearts (Qulub) have indeed inclined (صغت),' meaning they have deviated. And He said that regarding the best of his wives[111]—the two women being Aisha and Hafsa.
66:4.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

66:6.arabic: وإنما يفترقان في شيء وهو أن الملائكة عليهم السلام عالمة بطاعتها وامتثالها والأجفان تطيع القلب في الانفتاح والانطباق على سبيل التسخير ولا خبر لها من نفسها ومن طاعتها للقلب وإنما افتقر القلب إلى هذه الجنود من حيث افتقاره إلى المركب والزاد لسفره الذي لأجله خلق وهو السفر إلى الله سبحانه وقطع المنازل إلى لقائه فلأجله خلقت القلوب قال الله تعالى وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون وإنما مركبه البدن وزاده العلم وإنما الأسباب التي توصله إلى الزاد وتُمكِّنه من التزود منه هو العمل الصالح وليس يمكن العبد أن يص
66:6.english: And they differ in one thing, which is that the angels, peace be upon them, are aware of their obedience and compliance, while the eyelids obey the Heart (Qalb) in opening and closing by way of subjugation, and they have no awareness of themselves or of their obedience to the Heart. And the Heart only needs these soldiers due to its need for the vehicle and provision for its journey for which it was created, which is the journey to Allah, the Exalted, and traversing the stations to meet Him. For this purpose, the hearts were created. Allah, the Exalted, said: 'And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me.' And its vehicle is the body, and its provision is knowledge. And the means that lead it to the provision and enable it to take provision from it is righteous action. And it is not possible for the servant to reach Allah, the Exalted, unless he settles the body and transcends the world, for the lower station must be traversed to reach the farthest station. The world is the cultivation field of the Hereafter, and it is a station among the stations of guidance. And it is called 'dunya' because it is the lower of the two stations. So he was compelled to take provision from this world. Thus, the body is his vehicle by which he reaches this world, so he needed to attend to the body and preserve it. And the body is only preserved by bringing to it what suits it, like nourishment and other things, and by repelling from it what opposes it, like causes of destruction. So, for the purpose of bringing nourishment, he needed two soldiers: an inner one, which is desire (Shahwah), and an outward one, which is the hand.
66:6.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

66:6.arabic: وأهم ما يجب عليه مراعاته في الإنفاق أن يطعمها من الحلال ولا يدخل مداخل السوء لأجلها فإن ذلك جناية عليها لا مراعاة لها وقد أوردنا الأخبار الواردة في ذلك عند ذكر آفات النكاح السابع أن يتعلم المتزوج من علم الحيض وأحكامه ما يحترز به الاحتراز الواجب ويعلم زوجته أحكام الصلاة وما يقضى منها في الحيض وما لا يقضى فإنه أمر بأن يقيها النار بقوله تعالى قوا أنفسكم وأهليكم نارا فعليه أن يلقنها اعتقاد أهل السنة ويزيل عن قلبها كل بدعة إن استمعت إليها ويخوفها في الله إن تساهلت في أمر الدين ويعلمها من أحكام الحيض
66:6.english: And the most important thing that must be observed in expenditure is that he feeds her from the lawful (Halal) and does not enter paths of evil for her sake, for that is a crime against her, not consideration for her. And we have mentioned the narrations concerning that when mentioning the harms of marriage. Seventh: that the married person learns from the knowledge of menstruation and its rulings what to guard against with the obligatory precaution, and teaches his wife the rulings of prayer and what is made up from it during menstruation and what is not made up. For he is commanded to protect her from the Fire by His saying, the Exalted: 'Protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones, over which are angels, harsh and severe, who do not disobey Allah in what He commands them and do what they are commanded.' So upon him is to instill in her the creed of the People of the Sunnah (Ahl al-Sunnah) and remove from her heart (Qalb) every innovation (Bid'ah) if she listens to it, and make her fear in Allah if she is negligent in the matter of religion, and teach her from the rulings of menstruation and irregular bleeding (Istihadah) what she needs. And the knowledge of irregular bleeding (Istihadah) is lengthy. As for what is indispensable to guide women to concerning the matter of menstruation: clarifying the prayers that she makes up. For whenever her blood stops before Maghrib by the amount of one rak'ah, then upon her is to make up Dhuhr and 'Asr. And if it stops before Fajr by the amount of one rak'ah, then upon her is to make up Maghrib and 'Isha'. And this is the minimum that women observe. If the man is undertaking teaching her, then she has no right to go out to ask the scholars. And if the man's knowledge is deficient, but he acts on her behalf in asking and informs her of the answer of the mufti, then she has no going out. If that is not the case, then she may go out to ask, rather she must do that, and the man disobeys by preventing her. And whenever she learns what is from the obligations upon her, then she has no right to go out to a gathering of remembrance (Dhikr) nor to learn excellence except with his permission. And whenever the woman neglects a ruling from the rulings of menstruation and irregular bleeding (Istihadah) and the man does not teach her, the man is burdened with her and shares with her in the sin.
66:6.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

66:6.arabic: بل هم مجبولون على الطاعة ضي الله عنه ضي الله عنه عليه السلام ضي الله عنه ضي الله عنه ضي الله عنه لا مجال للمعصية في حقهم فلا جرم لا يعصون الله ما أمرهم ويفعلون ما يؤمرون ويسبحون الليل والنهار لا يفترون والراكع منهم راكع أبدا والساجد منهم ساجد أبدا والقائم قائم أبدا لا اختلاف في أفعالهم ولا فتور ولكل واحد مقام معلوم لا يتعداه وطاعتهم لله تعالى من حيث لا مجال للمخالفة فيهم يمكن أن تشبه بطاعة أطرافك لك، فإنك مهما جزمت الإرادة بفتح الأجفان لم يكن للجفن الصحيح تردد واختلاف في طاعتك مرة ومعصيتك أخرى ب
66:6.english: Rather, they are created upon obedience, may Allah be pleased with him, may Allah be pleased with him, peace be upon him, may Allah be pleased with him, may Allah be pleased with him, may Allah be pleased with him. There is no room for disobedience in their right, so indeed they do not disobey Allah what He commands them and they do what they are commanded, and they glorify night and day without ceasing. The one bowing among them is bowing forever, and the one prostrating among them is prostrating forever, and the one standing is standing forever. There is no difference in their actions nor slackness, and for each one is a known station that he does not exceed. Their obedience to Allah the Exalted, from where there is no room for opposition in them, can be likened to the obedience of your limbs to you. For whenever you resolve the will (Iradah) to open the eyelids, there is no hesitation or difference for the healthy eyelid in obeying you once and disobeying you another time. Rather, it is as if it awaits your command and prohibition, opening and closing continuously at your signal. This resembles it from one aspect but differs from it from another aspect, since the eyelid has no knowledge of what issues from it of movement, opening and closing, while the angels are living beings knowing what they do. So then, this is Allah's blessing upon you in the earthly and heavenly angels, and your need for them is only in the purpose of eating, apart from all other movements and needs. For we have not prolonged in mentioning them, so this is another layer from the layers of blessings, and the gatherings of layers cannot be enumerated, so how about the individuals that enter under the gatherings of layers? So then, Allah the Exalted has poured His blessings upon you, apparent and hidden, then He said: 'And leave apparent sin and its hidden.' So leaving hidden sin, which the creation does not know, from envy (Hasad), bad suspicion (Su' al-Zann), innovation (Bid'ah), and harboring evil for people, to other than that from the sins of the hearts (Qulub), is the gratitude (Shukr).
66:6.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

66:6.arabic: اعلم أن الطريق في رياضة الصبيان من أهم الأمور وأوكدها والصبيان أمانة عند والديه، وقلبه الطاهر جوهرة نفيسة ساذجة خالية عن كل نقش وصورة، وهو قابل لكل ما نقش ومائل إلى كل ما يمال به إليه، فإن عود الخير وعلمه نشأ عليه وسعد في الدنيا والآخرة وشاركه في ثوابه أبوه وكل معلم له ومؤدب؛ وإن عود الشر وأهمل إهمال البهائم شقي وهلك وكان الوزر في رقبة القيم عليه والوالي له. وقد قال الله عز وجل "يا أيها الذين آمنوا قوا أنفسكم وأهليكم ناراً" ومهما كان الأب يصونه عن نار الدنيا فبأن يصونه عن نار الآخرة أولى؛ وصيانت
66:6.english: Know that the method in disciplining children is among the most important and most emphasized matters, and children are a trust (Amanah) upon their parents. Their pure heart (Qalb) is a precious, simple jewel, empty of every engraving and image, and it is receptive to everything that is engraved upon it and inclined to everything it is directed toward. If he is accustomed to good and taught it, he grows up upon it and becomes fortunate in this world and the Hereafter, and his father and every teacher and educator share in his reward. But if he is accustomed to evil and neglected like animals, he becomes wretched and perishes, and the burden is upon the neck of the one responsible for him and his guardian. And Allah the Exalted has said: "O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire (Nar) whose fuel is people and stones, over which are [appointed] angels, harsh and severe; they do not disobey Allah in what He commands them but do what they are commanded." And whatever the father does to protect him from the fire of this world, it is more appropriate to protect him from the Fire (Nar) of the Hereafter. And his protection is by disciplining him, refining him, teaching him the beauties of character, protecting him from bad companions, not accustoming him to luxury, and not making adornment and comfort beloved to him, lest he waste his life seeking them when he grows up and thus perish eternally. Rather, he should be monitored from the very beginning, so that only a religious woman who eats lawful (Halal) food is employed in his nursing and breastfeeding, for the milk obtained from unlawful (Haram) sources has no blessing (Barakah) in it. If the child's growth occurs upon it, his clay is kneaded from the impure, and his nature inclines toward what corresponds to impurities.
66:6.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

66:6.arabic: ثم شاهدوا رءوس تلك الخيوط في مناطات لها هى معلقة بها وشاهدوا لتلك المناطات مقابض هى في أيدي الملائكة المحركين للسموات وشاهدوا أيضا ملائكة السموات مصروفة إلى حملة العرش ينتظرون منهم ما ينزل عليهم من الأمر من حضرة الربوبية كى لا يعصوا الله ما أمرهم ويفعلون ما يؤمرون وعبر عن هذه المشاهدات في القرآن وقيل: ﴿ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا قُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ وَأَهْلِيكُمْ نَارًا وَقُودُهَا النَّاسُ وَالْحِجَارَةُ عَلَيْهَا مَلَائِكَةٌ غِلَاظٌ شِدَادٌ لَا يَعْصُونَ اللَّهَ مَا أَمَرَهُمْ وَيَفْعَلُونَ م
66:6.english: Then they saw the heads of those threads in their supports that are suspended from them, and they saw for those supports handles that are in the hands of the angels who move the heavens, and they also saw the angels of the heavens directed to the bearers of the Throne, awaiting from them what descends upon them of the command from the presence of Lordship so that they do not disobey Allah what He commands them and they do what they are commanded. And these visions were expressed in the Quran, and it was said: 'O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones, over which are [appointed] angels, harsh and severe; they do not disobey Allah in what He commands them but do what they are commanded.'
66:6.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

66:8.arabic: فإذا لم يكن في معرفة الله تعالى إثبات صورة وجهه فلا يكون في استكمال تلك المعرفة بعينها وترقيها في الوضوح إلى غاية الكشف أيضاً جهة وصورة لأنها هي بعينها لا تفترق منها إلا في زيادة الكشف، كما أن الصورة المرئية هي المتخيلة بعينها إلا في زيادة الكشف، وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى: " يسعى نورهم بين أيديهم وبأيمانهم يقولون ربنا أتمم لنا نورنا " إذ تمام النور لا يؤثر إلا في زيادة التكشف، ولهذا لا يفوز بدرجة النظر والرؤية إلا العارفون في الدنيا، لأن المعرفة هي البذر الذي ينقلب في الآخرة مشاهدة كما تنقلب الن
66:8.english: If there is no affirmation of the image of His Face in the knowledge (ma'rifah) of Allah the Exalted, then there is no direction or image in the completion of that very knowledge and its ascension in clarity to the ultimate unveiling (kashf), because it is exactly the same except for the increase in unveiling, just as the visible image is exactly the imagined one except for the increase in unveiling. To this is the allusion in His saying the Exalted: "Their Light (Nur) runs before them and on their right hands; they say: 'Our Lord, perfect for us our Light (Nur) and forgive us'" since the perfection of the Light (Nur) only affects the increase in unveiling (takashshuf). Therefore, none attain the degree of vision (nazar) and seeing (ru'yah) except those who have knowledge (al-'arifun) in this world, because knowledge (ma'rifah) is the seed that transforms in the Hereafter into witnessing (mushahadah) just as the kernel transforms into a tree and the seed into a crop. How can one who has no kernel in his land obtain a palm tree? How can one who does not sow the seed harvest the crop? Likewise, how can one who does not know (ya'rif) Allah the Exalted in this world see Him in the Hereafter?
66:8.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

66:8.arabic: ولا يزال العبد عالماً بأنه بقي من الجمال والجلال ما لم يتضح له فلا يسكن قط شوقه، لا سيما من يرى فوق درجته درجات كثيرة، إلا أنه تشوق إلى استكمال الوصال مع حصول أصل الوصال، فهو يجد لذلك شوقاً لذيذاً لا يظهر فيه ألم ولا يبعد أن تكون ألطاف الكشف والنظر متوالية إلى غير نهاية، فلا يزال النعيم واللذة متزايداً أبد الآباد، وتكون لذة ما يتجدد من لطائف النعيم شاغلة عن الإحساس بالشوق إلى ما لم يحصل، وهذا بشرط أن يمكن حصول الكشف فيما لم يحصل فيه كشف في الدنيا أصلاً، فإن كان ذلك غير مبذول فيكون النعيم واقفاً
66:8.english: And the servant (Abd) continues knowing that there remains from the Beauty (Jamaal) and Majesty (Jalaal) what has not become clear to him, so his longing (Shawq) never settles, especially for one who sees above his level many levels, except that he longs for the completion of union (Wisal) while having obtained the foundation of union, so he finds for that a delightful longing in which no pain appears, and it is not far-fetched that the graces (Altaaf) of unveiling (Kashf) and vision (Nadhr) would be successive without end, so bliss (Naeem) and pleasure (Ladhdhah) continue increasing forever and ever, and the pleasure of what renews from the subtleties (Lataaif) of bliss preoccupies from sensing the longing for what has not been attained, and this is on condition that unveiling (Kashf) can occur in what had no unveiling in the worldly life (Dunya) at all, for if that is not granted then bliss stops at a limit that does not multiply but remains continuous perpetually. And His saying, the Exalted: 'Their light (Noor) runs before them and on their right hands; they say: Our Lord! Perfect for us our light (Noor)' is susceptible to this meaning, which is that He bestows upon him with the completion of the light (Noor) however much he provisioned from the worldly life (Dunya) the foundation of the light (Noor), and it is susceptible that the intended by it is the completion of the light (Noor) in other than what was illuminated in the worldly life (Dunya) with an illumination (Istinaarah) needing more completion and radiance (Ishraaq), so that is what is intended by its perfection. And His saying, the Exalted: 'Look on us that we may borrow from your light (Noor) - it was said: Turn back behind you and seek a light (Noor)' indicates that the lights (Anwaar) must have their foundation provisioned in the worldly life (Dunya) then increase in radiance (Ishraaq) in the hereafter (Aakhirah). As for a light (Noor) being renewed, no, and judgment in this by conjecturing assumptions is perilous, and what can be trusted in it has not been unveiled to us yet, so we ask Allah, the Exalted, to increase us in knowledge (Ilm) and guidance (Rushd) and show us the truth (Haqq) as truth (Haqq). This amount from the lights (Anwaar) of insights (Basaair) is revealing of the realities (Haqaaq) of longing (Shawq) and its meanings.
66:8.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

66:8.arabic: [17] حديث إن الله أوحى إلى نبيه ﭬ إني أجعل حساب أمتك إليك فقال لا يارب أنت خير لهم مني الحديث في تفسير قوله تعالى - يوم لا يخزى الله النبي - أخرجه ابن ابي الدنيا في كتاب حسن الظن بالله.
66:8.english: Hadith: Indeed, Allah revealed to His Prophet (peace be upon him): 'I will make the accounting of your nation to you.' He said: 'No, O Lord, You are better for them than me.' The hadith is in the interpretation (Tafsir) of His saying, the Exalted: 'The day Allah will not disgrace the Prophet...' It was transmitted by Ibn Abi al-Dunya in the book 'Good Opinion of Allah (Husn al-Zann bi-Allah).'
66:8.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Fear and Hope'

66:8.arabic: وقال كعب الأحبار ما في القرآن من يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو في التوراة يا أيها المساكين
66:8.english: And Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Whatever is in the Quran of 'O you who have believed' is in the Torah 'O you poor ones (al-Masakin)'.
66:8.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

66:8.arabic: ومايتعلق به هو الكمال الحقيقي الذي يقرب من يتصف به من الله تعالى، ويبقى كمالاً للنفس بعد الموت، وتكون هذه المعرفة نور للعارفين بعد الموت "يسعى نورهم بين أيديهم وبأيمانهم يقولون ربنا أتمم لنا نورنا" أي تكون هذه المعرفة رأس مال يوصل إلى كشف ما لم ينكشف في الدنيا، كما أنه معه سراج خفي فإنه يجوز أن يصير ذلك سبباً لزيادة النور بسراج آخر يقتبس منه، فيكمل النور الخفي على سبيل الاستتمام، ومن ليس معه أصل السراج فلا مطمع له في ذلك، فمن ليس معه أصل معرفة الله تعالى لم يكن له مطمع في هذا النور، فيبقى كمن مث
66:8.english: And what pertains to it is the true perfection that brings closer to Allah (the Exalted) the one who is characterized by it, and it remains a perfection for the Soul (Nafs) after death, and this knowledge becomes a light for the knowers after death: "Their light runs before them and on their right hands; they say: Our Lord! Perfect our light for us" (Quran 24:40). That is, this knowledge becomes capital that leads to the unveiling of what was not unveiled in this world, just as with it is a hidden lamp, for it is permissible that it becomes a cause for increasing the light with another lamp that is kindled from it, thus completing the hidden light on the path of completion. And whoever does not have the original lamp has no hope in that, so whoever does not have the original knowledge of Allah (the Exalted) has no hope in this light, and remains like one whose likeness is in darkness, not emerging from it, but "like darkness in a deep sea covered by a wave, above which is a wave, above which are clouds; darkness, one above another" (Quran 24:40). Therefore, there is no happiness except in the knowledge of Allah (the Exalted). As for other than that from the knowledges, some have no benefit at all, such as knowledge of poetry and Arab genealogies and others, and some have benefit in assisting towards the knowledge of Allah (the Exalted), such as knowledge of the Arabic language, interpretation (Tafsir), jurisprudence (Fiqh), and reports (Akhbar). For knowledge of the Arabic language assists in knowing the interpretation of the Quran, and knowledge of interpretation assists in knowing what is in the Quran regarding the manner of worships and works that benefit the purification of the Soul (Nafs), and knowledge of the way of purifying the Soul (Nafs) benefits the preparedness of the Soul (Nafs) to accept the gifts towards the knowledge of Allah (the Glorified and Exalted), as He (the Exalted) said: "Indeed he succeeds who purifies it" (Quran 91:9) and He (the Mighty and Majestic) said: "And those who strive in Us, We will surely guide them to Our ways" (Quran 29:69). Thus, the entirety of these...
66:8.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

66:9.arabic: أما التفريط: فبفقد هذه القوة أو ضعفها وذلك مذموم، وهو الذي يقال فيه إنه لا حمية له. ولذلك قال الشافعي رحمه الله من استغضب فلم يغضب فهو حمار. فمن فقد قوة الغضب والحمية أصلاً فهو ناقص جداً، وقد وصف الله سبحانه أصحاب النبي ﷺ بالشدة والحمية فقال "أشداء على الكفار رحماء بينهم" وقال لنبيه ﷺ "جاهد الكفار والمنافقين واغلظ عليهم" الآية وإنما الغلظة والشدة من آثار قوة الحمية وهو الغضب.
66:9.english: As for deficiency: it is by losing this power or its weakness, and that is blameworthy, and it is said about him that he has no zeal (Hamiyyah). Therefore, Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: 'Whoever is provoked to anger and does not get angry is a donkey.' So whoever loses the power of anger and zeal (Hamiyyah) entirely is very deficient. And Allah the Exalted has described the companions of the Prophet ﷺ with severity and zeal (Hamiyyah), saying: 'Severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves' and said to His Prophet ﷺ: 'O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh upon them' the verse. And indeed, harshness and severity are from the effects of the power of zeal (Hamiyyah), which is anger.
66:9.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

66:10.arabic: وقال تعالى "فخانتاهما فلم يغنيا عنهما من الله شيئاً" قيل كانت امرأة لوط تخبر بالضيفان وامرأة نوح تخبر أنه مجنون وقد قال ﭬ "لا يدخل الجنة نمام"[229] وفي حديث آخر "لا يدخل الجنة قتات" والقتات هو النمام
66:10.english: And Allah the Exalted said: "They betrayed them, so they availed them not against Allah at all." It is said: Lot's wife used to inform about the guests, and Noah's wife used to inform that he was mad. And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "The talebearer (Nammam) will not enter Paradise." [229] And in another hadith: "The slanderer (Qatat) will not enter Paradise." And the slanderer (Qatat) is the talebearer (Nammam).
66:10.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

67:1.arabic: فإذا دخلت السوق فقل لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له له الملك وله الحمد يحيي ويميت وهو حي لا يموت بيده الخير وهو على كل شيء قدير
67:1.english: When you enter the market, say: There is no god but Allah alone, He has no partner, to Him belongs the dominion (al-Mulk) and to Him belongs the praise, He gives life and causes death, and He is living, does not die, in His hand is the good, and He is over all things capable (Qadir).
67:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter

67:1.arabic: [197] حديث القول عند دخول السوق لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له له الملك وله الحمد يحيي ويميت وهو حي لا يموت بيده الخير وهو على كل شيء قدير من حديث عمر وقال غريب والحاكم وقال صحيح على شرط الشيخين.
67:1.english: [197] The hadith of the saying when entering the market: 'There is no god but Allah alone, He has no partner, to Him belongs the Kingdom (al-Mulk) and to Him belongs the Praise, He gives life and causes death, and He is Living and does not die, in His Hand is the Good, and He is over all things Powerful (Qadir).' From the narration of Umar, and it was said: 'Rare (Gharib),' and Al-Hakim said: 'Authentic according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs.'
67:1.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication

67:1.arabic: يا من هو على كل شيء قدير
67:1.english: O You Who is over every thing powerful (Qadir).

67:2.arabic: ولا مناقضة بين قوله تعالى (نحن قدرنا بينكم الموت) وبين قوله (وأنا أكره مساءته) ولكن إيضاح الحق في هذا يستدعي تحقيق معنى الإرادة والمحبة والكراهة وبيان حقائقها. فإن السابق إلى الأفهام منها أمور تناسب إرادة الخلق ومحبتهم وكراهتهم وهيهات فبين صفات الله تعالى وصفات الخلق من البعد ما بين ذاته العزيز وذاتهم وكما أن ذوات الخلق جوهر وعرض وذات الله مقدس عنه ولا يناسب ما ليس بجوهر وعرض الجوهر والعرض فكذا صفاته لا تناسب صفات الخلق وهذه الحقائق داخلة في علم المكاشفة ووراء سر القدر الذي منع من إفشائه فلنقصر
67:2.english: And there is no contradiction between His saying, the Exalted, ('We have decreed death among you') and His saying ('And I dislike displeasing him'), but clarifying the truth in this requires verifying the meaning of Will (Irada), Love (Mahabba), and Dislike (Karaha) and explaining their realities. For what first comes to minds from them are matters that correspond to the will, love, and dislike of creation—far be it! For between the attributes of Allah, the Exalted, and the attributes of creation is a distance like that between His Mighty Essence (Dhat Al-Aziz) and their essence. And just as the essences of creation are substance and accident, and the Essence of Allah is sanctified from that and does not correspond to what is not substance and accident—substance and accident—so too His attributes do not correspond to the attributes of creation. And these realities are included in the knowledge of unveiling (Ilm Al-Mukashafa) and beyond the secret of divine decree (Sirr Al-Qadr) which is prohibited from divulging, so we will refrain from mentioning it and limit ourselves to what we have pointed out regarding the difference between proceeding to marriage and refraining from it.
67:2.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

67:2.arabic: وقال السدي ﴿ الذي خلق الموت والحياة ليبلوكم أيكم احسن عملا ﴾ {} أي أيكم أكثرللموت ذكرا وأحسن له استعدادا وأشد منه خوفا وحذرا.
67:2.english: And Al-Suddi said: "The One Who created death and life to test you as to which of you is best in deed" (Quran 67:2) meaning: which of you has more remembrance (Dhikr) of death, better preparation for it, and greater fear and caution from it.
67:2.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

67:3.arabic: وبقوله تعالى: " الذي خلق سبع سموات طباقاً ما ترى في خلق الرحمن من تفاوت فارجع البصر هل ترى من فطور ثم ارجع البصر كرتين ينقلب إليك البصر خاسئاً وهو حسير " وهذا الطريق هو الأسهل على الأكثرين وهو الأوسع على السالكين، وإليه أكثر دعوة القرآن عند الأمر بالتدبر والتفكر والاعتبار والنظر في آيات خارجة عن الحصر.
67:3.english: And by His saying, the Exalted: "The One Who created seven heavens in layers, you see no inconsistency in the creation of the Most Merciful (Ar-Rahman). So return the gaze; do you see any fissure? Then return the gaze twice; the gaze will return to you humbled and weary." And this path is the easiest for most people and the widest for the travelers (Salikun), and to it belongs most of the Quran's call when commanding contemplation (Tadabbur), reflection (Tafakkur), consideration (I'tibar), and looking at signs (Ayat) beyond enumeration.
67:3.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

67:8.arabic: و جامع ولم ينزل! فهو معتوه فكذلك من رجا رحمة الله وهو لم يؤمن أو آمن لم يعمل صالحاً أو عمل ولم يترك المعاصي فهو مغرور. فكما أنه إذا نكح ووطئ وأنزل بقي متردداً في الولد يخاف ويرجو فضل الله في خلق الولد ودفع الآفات عن الرحم وعن الأم إلى أن يتم فهو كيس، فكذلك إذا آمن وعمل الصالحات وترك السيئات وبقي متردداً بين الخوف والرجاء يخاف أن لا يقبل منه وأن لا يدوم عليه وأن يختم له بالسوء، ويرجوا من الله تعالى أن يثبته بالقول الثابت ويحفظ دينه من صواعق سكرات الموت حتى يموت على التوحيد، ويحرس قلبه عن الميل إل
67:8.english: And he who has intercourse but does not ejaculate! He is foolish, and likewise is he who hopes for the mercy of Allah while he has not believed, or believed but did not do righteous deeds, or did but did not abandon sins—he is deluded. Just as when one marries and has intercourse and ejaculates, he remains hesitant about the child, fearing and hoping for Allah's favor in creating the child and warding off afflictions from the womb and from the mother until it is complete, he is wise; similarly, if he believes and does righteous deeds and abandons evil deeds and remains hesitant between fear and hope, fearing that it will not be accepted from him and that it will not last upon him and that he will be sealed with evil, and hopes from Allah the Exalted that He will establish him with the firm word and protect his religion from the lightning bolts of the agonies of death until he dies upon monotheism (Tawhid), and guards his heart (Qalb) from inclining toward desires for the remainder of his life so that he does not incline toward sins, he is wise. And besides these, they are the ones deluded by Allah: "And they will know when they see the punishment who is most astray from the path—and you will know its news after a while." And at that time, they will say as Allah informed about them: "Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us that we may do righteous deeds; indeed, we are certain." That is, we learned that just as a child is not born except by intercourse and marriage, and crops do not grow except by plowing and sowing seeds, so likewise reward and recompense are not attained in the Hereafter except by righteous deeds—so return us that we may do righteous deeds, for we have now learned the truth of Your saying: "And that there is not for man except what he has striven for, and that his striving is going to be seen—every time a company is thrown into it, its keepers will ask them, 'Did there not come to you a warner?' They will say, 'Yes, a warner had come to us.'" That is, did we not hear you about the way of Allah with His servants and that "He will take account of every soul for what it earned" and that "Every soul, for what it has earned, is held in pledge"? So what deluded you about Allah after you heard and understood? "They will say, 'If only we had been listening or reasoning, we would not be among the companions of the Blaze.' So they will admit their sin, and [it is] alienation for the companions of the Blaze."
67:8.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

67:8.arabic: فإن قلت: فما شبهة المعتزلة والمرجئة وما حجة بطلان قولهم. فأقول شبهتهم عمومات القرآن أما المرجئة فقالوا لا يدخل المؤمن النار وإن أتي بكل المعاصي لقوله عز وجل: ﴿ فمن يؤمن بربه فلا يخاف بخسا ولا رهقا ﴾ {} ولقوله سبحانه وتعالى: ﴿ والذين آمنوا بالله ورسله أولئك هم الصديقون ﴾ {} الآية ولقوله تعالى: ﴿ كلما ألقي فيها فوج سألهم خزنتها. ﴾ {} إلى قوله: ﴿ فكذبنا وقلنا ما نزل الله من شيء ﴾ {} فقوله كلما ألقي فيها فوج عام فينبغي أن يكون من ألقي في النار مكذبا ولقوله تعالى: ﴿ لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى الذي كذب وتول
67:8.english: If you say: What is the doubt of the Mu'tazila and the Murji'a and what is the proof of the invalidity of their statement? I say their doubt is from generalities of the Quran. As for the Murji'a, they said the believer does not enter the Fire even if he commits all sins, due to His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'So whoever believes in his Lord, he fears not loss nor oppression' and due to His saying, the Exalted: 'And those who believe in Allah and His messengers, those are the truthful ones' the verse, and due to His saying: 'Every time a group is cast into it, its keepers will ask them' to His saying: 'So we denied and said: Allah has not sent down anything.' So His saying 'Every time a group is cast into it' is general, so it should be that whoever is cast into the Fire is a denier, and due to His saying: 'None will burn in it except the most wretched, who denied and turned away' and this is restriction, affirmation, and negation, and due to His saying: 'Whoever comes with a good deed, for him is better than it, and they are from the terror of that Day secure' so Faith (Iman) is the head of good deeds, and due to His saying: 'And Allah loves the doers of good (Muhsinin)' and He said: 'Indeed, We do not waste the reward of one who does good work.' And they have no proof in that, for where Faith (Iman) is mentioned in these verses, it is intended as Faith (Iman) with action, since we have clarified that Faith (Iman) may be used and intended as Islam, which is agreement with the Heart (Qalb), speech, and action. The evidence for this interpretation is many reports about punishing the disobedient and the measures of punishment, and his saying ﷺ: 'He will be taken out of the Fire whoever has in his Heart (Qalb) an atom's weight of Faith (Iman)' so how can he be taken out if he did not enter? And from the Quran, His saying: 'Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills' and the exception with will indicates division, and His saying: 'And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, then indeed, for him is the Fire of Hell, abiding therein forever' and specifying it with disbelief is arbitrary, and His saying: 'Unquestionably, the wrongdoers are in enduring punishment'
67:8.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Foundations of Belief'

67:8.arabic: وقوله تعالى: ﴿ كلما ألقي فيها فوج سألهم خزنتها ﴾ {} أي فوج من الكفار وتخصيص العمومات قريب ومن هذه الآية وقع للأشعري وطائفة من المتكلمين إنكار صيغ العموم وأن هذه الألفاظ يتوقف فيها إلى ظهور قرينة تدل على معناها.
67:8.english: And His saying, the Exalted: 'Whenever a group is thrown into it, its keepers will ask them' {} meaning a group from the disbelievers, and the specification of generalities is plausible. And from this verse, it occurred to Al-Ash'ari and a group of theologians to deny the forms of generality and that these expressions are suspended until the appearance of an indication that points to their meaning.
67:8.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Foundations of Belief'

67:9.arabic: فإن قلت: فما شبهة المعتزلة والمرجئة وما حجة بطلان قولهم. فأقول شبهتهم عمومات القرآن أما المرجئة فقالوا لا يدخل المؤمن النار وإن أتي بكل المعاصي لقوله عز وجل: ﴿ فمن يؤمن بربه فلا يخاف بخسا ولا رهقا ﴾ {} ولقوله سبحانه وتعالى: ﴿ والذين آمنوا بالله ورسله أولئك هم الصديقون ﴾ {} الآية ولقوله تعالى: ﴿ كلما ألقي فيها فوج سألهم خزنتها. ﴾ {} إلى قوله: ﴿ فكذبنا وقلنا ما نزل الله من شيء ﴾ {} فقوله كلما ألقي فيها فوج عام فينبغي أن يكون من ألقي في النار مكذبا ولقوله تعالى: ﴿ لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى الذي كذب وتول
67:9.english: If you say: What is the doubt of the Mu'tazila and the Murji'a and what is the proof of the invalidity of their statement? I say: Their doubt is the generalities of the Quran. As for the Murji'a, they said: The believer does not enter the Fire even if he commits all sins, due to His saying, the Exalted: 'So whoever believes in his Lord, he fears no loss nor any injustice' and due to His saying, the Most High: 'And those who believe in Allah and His messengers - those are the truthful ones' the verse, and due to His saying: 'Every time a group is cast into it, its keepers will ask them' to His saying: 'So we denied and said: Allah has not sent down anything' so His saying 'Every time a group is cast into it' is general, so it should be that whoever is cast into the Fire is a denier, and due to His saying: 'None will burn in it except the most wretched one who denied and turned away' and this is restriction, affirmation, and negation, and due to His saying: 'Whoever comes with a good deed will have better than it, and they will be safe from terror that Day' so Faith (Iman) is the head of good deeds, and due to His saying: 'And Allah loves the doers of good' and He said: 'Indeed, We do not allow to be lost the reward of any who does good work' and they have no proof in that, for when Faith (Iman) is mentioned in these verses, it is intended to be Faith (Iman) with action, since we have clarified that Faith (Iman) may be used and intended to mean Islam, which is agreement with the Heart (Qalb), speech, and action. The evidence for this interpretation is many reports about punishing the disobedient and the measures of punishment, and his saying ﭬ: 'He will be brought out of the Fire who had in his Heart (Qalb) an atom's weight of Faith (Iman)' so how can he be brought out if he did not enter? And from the Quran, His saying: 'Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills' and the exception with will indicates division, and His saying: 'And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger - then indeed, for him is the Fire of Hell, wherein they will abide eternally' and specifying it with disbelief is arbitrary, and His saying: 'Unquestionably, the wrongdoers are in an enduring punishment' and He said: 'And whoever comes with an evil deed - their faces will be overturned into the Fire' so these generalities in...
67:9.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Foundations of Belief'

67:10.arabic: وأن "كل نفس بما كسبت رهينة" فما الذي غركم بالله بعد أن سمعتم وعقلتم؟ "قالوا لو كنا نسمع أو نعقل ما كنا في أصحاب السعير فاعترفوا بذنبهم فسحقاً لأصحاب السعير"
67:10.english: And that "Every Soul (Nafs) is held in pledge for what it has earned" so what deluded you about Allah after you heard and understood? "They said: Had we but listened or had sense (Aql), we would not have been among the dwellers of the Blazing Fire (Sa'ir). So they acknowledged their sin; and far removed (from mercy) are the dwellers of the Blazing Fire (Sa'ir)."
67:10.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

67:10.arabic: وعن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : (( لكل شيء دعامة ودعامة المؤمن عقله فبقدر عقله تكون عبادته أما سمعتم قول الفجار في النار: (لو كنا نسمع أو نعقل ما كنا في أصحاب السعير( (الملك: 10) ))[205].
67:10.english: And from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'Everything has a pillar, and the pillar of the believer is his intellect (Aql). According to the measure of his intellect (Aql) will be his worship. Have you not heard the saying of the wicked in the Fire: "If we had listened or used our intellect (Na'qil), we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze" (Al-Mulk: 10)?'
67:10.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Knowledge'

67:13.arabic: الأصل الأول: العلم بأن كل حادث في العالم فهو فعله وخلقه واختراعه لا خالق له سواه ولا محدث له إلا إياه خلق الخلق وصنعهم وأوجد قدرتهم وحركتهم فجميع أفعال عباده مخلوقة له ومتعلقة بقدرته تصديقا له في قوله تعالى الله خالق كل شيء وفي قوله تعالى والله خلقكم وما تعملون وفي قوله تعالى وأسروا قولكم أو اجهروا به إنه عليم بذات الصدور ألا يعلم من خلق وهو اللطيف الخبير أمر العباد بالتحرز في أقوالهم وأفعالهم وإسرارهم وإضمارهم لعلمه بموارد أفعالهم واستدل على العلم بالخلق وكيف لا يكون خالقا لفعل العبد وقدرته تام
67:13.english: The First Principle: The knowledge that every occurrence in the world is His action, His creation, and His invention; there is no creator for it other than Him, and no originator for it except Him. He created the creation and fashioned them, and brought into existence their power and their movement. Thus, all the actions of His servants are created by Him and connected to His power, confirming Him in His saying, the Exalted: 'Allah is the Creator of everything' (Quran 39:62), and in His saying: 'And Allah created you and what you do' (Quran 37:96), and in His saying: 'And conceal your speech or proclaim it; indeed, He is Knowing of that within the chests (ذات الصدور)' (Quran 67:13). Does He not know what He created? And He is the Subtle, the Acquainted. He commanded the servants to be cautious in their statements and their actions, and in their secrets and their hidden thoughts, due to His knowledge of the sources of their actions. And He argued for knowledge through creation. And how could He not be the creator of the servant's action when His power is complete, with no deficiency in it, and it is connected to the movement of the bodies of the servants? And the movements are similar, and the connection of the power to them is for their own essence. So what is it that restricts its connection from some movements without others despite their similarity? Or how could the animal be independent in invention when there emanates from the spider, the bee, and all the animals from subtle crafts what bewilders the intellects of those of understanding? So how did they become isolated in their invention without the Lord of lords, while they are not knowing of the details of what emanates from them from acquisition? Far, far be it! The created beings are humbled, and He is singled out with the dominion and the sovereignty, the Compeller of the earth and the heavens.
67:13.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Foundations of Belief'

67:14.arabic: الأصل الثاني: العلم بأنه تعالى عالم بجميع الموجودات ومحيط بكل المخلوقات لا يعزب عن علمه مثقال ذرة في الأرض ولا في السماء صادق في قوله وهو بكل شيء عليم ومرشد إلى صدقه بقوله تعالى ألا يعلم من خلق وهو اللطيف الخبير أرشدك إلى الاستدلال بالخلق على العلم بأنك لا تستريب في دلالة الخلق اللطيف والصنع المزين بالترتيب ولو في الشيء الحقير الضعيف على علم الصانع بكيفية الترتيب والترصيف فما ذكره الله سبحانه هو المنتهى في الهداية والتعريف.
67:14.english: The Second Foundation: The knowledge that He, the Exalted, is Knower of all existents and encompasses all created beings; not even an atom's weight in the earth or in the heavens escapes His knowledge, truthful in His saying 'and He is, of all things, Knowing.' And a guide to its truthfulness is His saying, the Exalted: 'Does He not know, He Who created? And He is the Subtle, the Aware.' He guides you to inferring from creation to knowledge, that you should not doubt in the indication of the subtle creation and the work adorned with arrangement, even in the insignificant, weak thing, regarding the knowledge of the Maker concerning the manner of arrangement and composition. So what Allah, glory be to Him, has mentioned is the ultimate in guidance and definition.
67:14.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'
