67:15.arabic: وإذا عرفت طريق الفكر فى نفسك فتفكر فى الأرض التى هى مقرك ثم فى أنهارها وجبالها ومعادتها ثم ارتفع منها إلى ملكوت السموات أما الأرض فمن آياته أن خلق الأرض فراشا ومهادا وسلك فيها سبلا فجاجا وجعلها ذلولا لتمشوا فى مناكبها وجعلها قارة لا تتحرك وأرسى فيها الجبال أوتادا لها تمنعها من أن تميد ثم وسع أكنافها حتى عجز الآدميون عن بلوغ جميع جوانبها وإن طالت إعمارهم وكثر تطوافهم فقال تعالى والسماء بنيناها بأيد وإنا لموسعون والأرض فرشناها فنعم الماهدون وقال تعالى هو الذى جعل لكم الأرض ذلولا فامشوا فى مناكبها
67:15.english: And when you know the path of thought (Fikr) in your self (Nafs), then contemplate the earth which is your abode, then in its rivers and mountains and its plains, then ascend from it to the dominion (Malakut) of the heavens. As for the earth, from His signs is that He created the earth as a bed (Firash) and a resting place (Mahad), and made in it wide paths, and made it submissive (Dhulul) so that you may walk in its tracts, and made it stable so it does not move, and set in it mountains as pegs for it to prevent it from shaking, then expanded its expanses until the sons of Adam (Adam) were unable to reach all its sides even if their lifespans were long and their travels abundant. So He, the Exalted, said: 'And the heaven We constructed with strength, and indeed, We are [its] expander. And the earth We have spread out, and excellent is the preparer.' And He, the Exalted, said: 'He is the one who made for you the earth submissive (Dhulul), so walk in its tracts.' And He, the Exalted, said: 'The one who made for you the earth a bed (Firash).' And He has frequently mentioned the earth in His mighty book so that one may contemplate its wonders: its surface is an abode for the living and its interior is a resting place for the dead. He, the Exalted, said: 'Have We not made the earth a container, for the living and the dead?' So look at the earth when it is dead, then when water is sent down upon it, it quivers and swells and greens and produces wonders of plants, and from it emerge various kinds of animals.
67:15.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Contemplation'

67:22.arabic: ومن يأخذ المعاني من الأسامي يظن أن هذه الأحوال مختلفة في ذواتها وحقائقها من حيث رأي الأسامي مختلفة والذي يسلك الطريق المستقيم وينظر بنور الله تعالى يلحظ المعاني أولا فيطلع على حقائقها ثم يلاحظ الأسامي فإنها وضعت دالة على المعاني فالمعاني هي الأصول والالفاظ هي التوابع ومن يطلب الأصول من التوابع لا بد وأن يزل وإلى الفريقين الإشارة بقوله تعالى: ﴿ أفمن يمشي مكبا على وجهه أهدى أمن يمشي سويا على صراط مستقيم ﴾ {} فإن الكفار لم يغلطوا فيما غلطوا فيه إلا بمثل هذه الانعكاسات، نسأل الله حسن التوفيق بكرمه و
67:22.english: And whoever takes the meanings from the names thinks that these states are different in their essences and realities because the names appear different. But the one who follows the straight path and looks with the light of Allah (God) observes the meanings first, then perceives their realities, then notices the names, for they were established as indicators of the meanings. Thus, the meanings are the foundations and the words are the followers. And whoever seeks the foundations from the followers must inevitably slip. To these two groups is the allusion in His saying, the Exalted: 'Is he who walks prone upon his face better guided, or he who walks upright on a straight path?' For the disbelievers did not err in what they erred in except by such reversals. We ask Allah for good success through His generosity and kindness.
67:22.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

67:25.arabic: واختلاف تركيب أعضائه أعاجيب تزيد على الأعاجيب فى بعثه وإعادته فكيف ينكر ذلك من قدرة الله تعالى وحكمته من يشاهد ذلك فى صنعته وقدرته فإن كان فى إيمانك ضعف فقو الإيمان بالنظر فى النشأة الأولى فإن الثانية مثلها وأسهل منها وإن كنت قوى الإيمان بها فأشعر قلبك تلك المخاوف والأخطار وأكثر فيها التفكر والاعتبار لتسلب عن قلبك الراحة والقرار فتشتغل بالتشمر للعرض على الجبار وتفكر أولا فيما يقرع سمع سكان القبور من شدة نفخ الصور فإنها صيحة واحدة تنفرج بها القبور عن رءوس الموتي فيثورون دفعة واحدة فتوهم نفسك وقد
67:25.english: And the variation in the composition of its limbs is wonders that increase upon wonders in its resurrection and restoration, so how can one deny that from the power (Qudrah) of Allah the Exalted and His wisdom who witnesses that in His creation and power? If there is weakness in your faith (Iman), then strengthen the faith (Iman) by looking at the first creation, for the second is like it and easier than it. And if you are strong in faith (Iman) in it, then make your heart (Qalb) feel those fears and dangers, and increase in it reflection (Tafakkur) and consideration (I'tibar) to strip from your heart (Qalb) comfort and settlement, so you become occupied with preparing for the presentation before the Compeller (Al-Jabbar). And reflect first on what strikes the hearing of the inhabitants of the graves from the intensity of the blowing of the Trumpet (As-Sur), for it is a single cry by which the graves split open from the heads of the dead, and they rise up all at once. So imagine yourself having sprung up with your face changed, your body dusty from the parting of your hair to your feet from the dust of your grave, bewildered from the intensity of the shock, with your eye fixed toward the call. And the creation has risen up in a single uprising from the graves in which their tribulation (Bala') has been prolonged, and they have been agitated by terror (Faza') and dread (Ru'b), added to what was with them of sorrows (Humum) and griefs (Ghumum) and intense waiting for the outcome of the matter, as Allah the Exalted said: 'And the Trumpet (As-Sur) will be blown, and all who are in the heavens and all who are on the earth will fall dead except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on.' And Allah the Exalted said: 'And when the Trumpet (An-Naqur) is blown, that Day will be a difficult day for the disbelievers; not easy.' And Allah the Exalted said: 'And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?" They do not await except one blast which will seize them while they are disputing. And they will not be able to make a testament, nor to their people can they return. And the Trumpet (As-Sur) will be blown, and at once from the graves to their Lord they will hasten. They will say, "O woe to us! Who has raised us from our sleeping place? This is what the Most Merciful had promised, and the messengers told the truth."' So if there were not before the dead except the terror of that blowing, it would be worthy of being feared, for it is a blowing and a cry by which those in the heavens and the earth are struck dead, meaning they die by it except whom Allah wills, and that is some of the angels. And therefore the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'How can I be at ease when the possessor of the Trumpet (As-Sur) has taken the horn in his mouth, lowered his forehead, and inclined his ear, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow?' Maqatil said: The Trumpet (As-Sur) is the horn, and that is because Israfil (upon him be peace) has placed his mouth on the horn like the form of a trumpet, and the circle of the head of the horn is like the expanse of the heavens and the earth, and he is fixing his gaze toward the Throne (Al-'Arsh), waiting for when he will be commanded to blow the first blowing. And when he blows, those in the heavens and the earth are struck dead, meaning every animal dies from the intensity of the terror except whom Allah wills, and that is Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil, and the Angel of Death (Malak al-Mawt). Then the Angel of Death (Malak al-Mawt) is commanded to take the soul (Ruh) of Jibril, then the soul (Ruh) of Mika'il, then the soul (Ruh) of Israfil, then the Angel of Death (Malak al-Mawt) is commanded and he dies. Then the creation remains after the first blowing in the Intermediate State (Al-Barzakh) for forty years, then Allah the Exalted revives Israfil and commands.
67:25.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

68:4.arabic: فالسخاء خلق من أخلاق الله تعالى؛ والإيثار أعلى درجات السخاء. وكان ذلك من أدب رسول الله ﷺ حتى سماه الله تعالى عظيماً فقال تعالى "وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم" وقلا سهل بن عبد الله التستري قال موسى عليه السلام، يا رب أرني بعض درجات محمد ﷺ وأمته! فقال يا موسى إنك لن تطيق ذلك، ولكن أريك منزلة من منازله جليلة عظيمة فضلته بها عليك وعلى جميع خلقي، قال فكشف له عن ملكوت السموات فنظر إلى منزلة كادت تتلف نفسه من أنوارها وقربها من الله تعالى، فقال: يا رب بماذا بلغت به إلى هذه الكرامة؟ قال: بخلق اختصصته به من بينهم وه
68:4.english: Generosity (Sakhā') is a character trait from the character traits of Allah the Exalted; and preferring others over oneself (Īthār) is the highest degree of generosity. And that was from the refined character (Adab) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until Allah the Exalted called him great, so He the Exalted said: "And indeed, you are upon a great character (Khuluq 'Aẓīm)." And Sahl ibn 'Abdillah al-Tustarī said: Mūsā, peace be upon him, said: O Lord, show me some of the degrees of Muḥammad ﷺ and his community! He said: O Mūsā, you will not be able to bear that, but I will show you a station from his stations, magnificent and great, with which I have favored him over you and over all My creation. He said: So He unveiled for him the dominion (Malakūt) of the heavens, and he looked at a station that almost destroyed his soul (Nafs) from its lights and its nearness to Allah the Exalted. He said: O Lord, by what did You bring him to this honor? He said: By a character trait with which I singled him out from among them, and it is preferring others over oneself (Īthār). O Mūsā, none of them comes to Me having acted upon it for a period of his life except that I feel ashamed (Istahyaytu) from calling him to account, and I settle him in My Garden (Jannah) wherever he wishes.
68:4.book_title: Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth
68:4.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

68:4.arabic:
بيان فضيلة حسن الخلق ومذمة سوء الخلق

قال الله تعالى لنبيه وحبيبه مثنياً عليه ومظهراً نعمته لديه "وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم" وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها كان رسول الله ﭬ خلقه القرآن"[1] وسأل رجل رسول الله ﭬ عن حسن الخلق فتلا قوله تعالى "خذ العفو وأمر بالعرف واعرض عن الجاهلين" ثم قال ﭬ "هو أن تصل قطعك وتعطي من حرمك وتعفو ظلمك"[2] وقال ﭬ: "إنما بعثت لأتمم مكارم الأخلاق"[3] وقال ﭬ "أُقل ما يوضع في الميزان يوم القيامة تقوى الله وحسن الخلق"[4] وجاء رجل إلى رسول الله ﭬ من بين يديه فقال: يا رسول الله ما الدين؟ ق
68:4.english:
Explanation of the virtue of good character (Khuluq) and the censure of bad character (Khuluq).

Allah the Exalted said to His Prophet and beloved, praising him and manifesting His favor upon him: "And indeed, you are upon a great character (Khuluq)" (Quran 68:4). And Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "The Messenger of Allah's character (Khuluq) was the Quran."[1] And a man asked the Messenger of Allah about good character (Khuluq), so he recited the saying of Allah the Exalted: "Take what is given freely, enjoin what is recognized (Ma'ruf), and turn away from the ignorant." Then he said: "It is that you join what is severed from you, give to one who deprives you, and pardon one who wrongs you."[2] And he said: "I was only sent to perfect noble character (Akhlaq)."[3] And he said: "The least that is placed in the scale on the Day of Resurrection is the God-consciousness (Taqwa) of Allah and good character (Khuluq)."[4] And a man came to the Messenger of Allah from before him and said: O Messenger of Allah, what is religion (Deen)? He said: "Good character (Khuluq)." Then he came to him from his right side and said: O Messenger of Allah, what is religion (Deen)? He said: "Good character (Khuluq)." Then he came to him from his left side and said: What is religion (Deen)? He said: "Good character (Khuluq)." Then he came to him from behind him and said: O Messenger of Allah, what is religion (Deen)? He turned to him and said: "Do you not understand? It is that you do not become angry."[5] And it was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is misfortune? He said: "Bad character (Khuluq)."[6] And a man said to the Messenger of Allah: Advise me. He said: "Fear Allah wherever you are." He said: Increase me. He said: "Follow a bad deed with a good deed that erases it." He said: Increase me. He said: "Treat people with good character (Khuluq)."[7] And he was asked, peace be upon him: Which deeds are best? He said: "Good character (Khuluq)." And he said: "Allah does not beautify the creation (Khalq) and character (Khuluq) of a servant and then feed him to the Fire."[8] And Al-Fudayl said: It was said to the Messenger of Allah, prayers and peace be upon him and his family: Indeed, then.
68:4.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

68:4.arabic: وأولى ما يمتحن به حسن الخلق الصبر على الأذى واحتمال الجفاء، ومن شكا من سوء خلق غيره دل ذلك على سوء خلقه، فإن حسن الخلق احتمال الأذى فقد روي أن رسول الله ﭬ كان يوماً يمشي ومعه أنس فأدركه أعرابي فجذبه جذباً شديداً وكان عليه برد نجراني غليظ الحاشية، قال أنس رضي الله عنه: حتى نظرت إلى عنق رسول الله ﭬ قد أثرت فيه حاشية البرد من شدة جذبه، فقال: يا محمد هب لي من مال الله الذي عندك، فالتفت إليه رسول الله ﭬ وضحك، ثم أمر بإعطائه[58] ولما أكثرت قريش إيذاءه وضربه قال: اللهم اغفر لقومي فإنهم لا يعلمون"[59] ق
68:4.english: And the foremost thing by which good character (Khuluq) is tested is patience (Sabr) upon harm and enduring harshness, and whoever complains of the bad character of another indicates thereby his own bad character, for good character is enduring harm. It has been narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was walking one day with Anas when a Bedouin caught up to him and pulled him with a strong pull, and he was wearing a thick-edged Najrani cloak. Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'Until I looked at the neck of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and saw the mark of the cloak's edge upon it from the severity of his pulling.' He said: 'O Muhammad, grant me from the wealth of Allah that is with you.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned to him and smiled, then ordered that he be given. And when the Quraysh increased in harming him and striking him, he said: 'O Allah, forgive my people for they do not know.' It is said that this was on the day of Uhud, therefore Allah the Exalted revealed: 'And indeed, you are upon a great character (Khuluq).'
68:4.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

68:4.arabic: ثم لما أكمل الله تعالى خلقه أثنى عليه فقال تعالى وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم فسبحانه ما أعظم شأنه وأتم امتنانه ثم انظر إلى عميم لطفه وعظيم فضله كيف أعطى ثم أثنى فهو الذي زينه بالخلق الكريم ثم أضاف إليه ذلك فقال وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم
68:4.english: Then when Allah the Exalted perfected his creation, He praised him, saying: 'And indeed, you are upon a great character (Khuluq 'Adheem).' So glory be to Him, how great is His affair and how complete is His favor. Then look at the vastness of His gentleness and the greatness of His grace—how He gave and then praised. For He is the One who adorned him with the noble character (Khuluq Kareem), then attributed that to him, saying: 'And indeed, you are upon a great character (Khuluq 'Adheem).'
68:4.book_title: Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character
68:4.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Etiquette of Living and Prophetic Character'

68:4.arabic: فضيلة الألفة والأخوة أعلم أن الألفة ثمرة حسن الخلق والتفرق ثمرة سوء الخلق فحسن الخلق يوجب التحاب والتآلف والتوافق وسوء الخلق يثمر التباغض والتحاسد والتدابر ومهما كان المثمر محمودا كانت الثمرة محمودة وحسن الخلق لا تخفى في الدين فضيلته وهو الذي مدح الله سبحانه به نبيه عليه السلام إذ قال وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أكثر ما يدخل الناس الجنة تقوى الله وحسن الخلق حديث أول ما يدخل الجنة تقوى الله وحسن الخلق أخرجه الترمذي والحاكم من حديث أبي هريرة وقال صحيح الإسناد وقد تقدم
68:4.english: The virtue of affection and brotherhood: Know that affection is the fruit of good character (Khuluq) and separation is the fruit of bad character (Khuluq). Good character necessitates mutual love, affection, and harmony, while bad character produces mutual hatred, envy, and turning away. Whenever the producer is praiseworthy, the fruit is praiseworthy. The virtue of good character in the religion is not hidden, and it is that with which Allah, glorified be He, praised His Prophet, peace be upon him, when He said: 'And indeed, you are upon a great character (Khuluq).' And the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'The most that causes people to enter Paradise is the God-consciousness (Taqwa) of Allah and good character (Khuluq).' The hadith: 'The first to enter Paradise is the God-consciousness (Taqwa) of Allah and good character (Khuluq).' Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Hakim transmitted it from the narration of Abu Hurairah and said its chain is authentic, and it has preceded.
68:4.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

68:13.arabic: قال الله تعالى "هماز مشاء بنميم" ثم قال "عتل بعد ذلك زنيم" قال عبد الله بن المبارك: الزنيم ولد الزنا الذي لا يكتم الحديث، وأشار به إلى أن كل من لم يكتم الحديث ومشى بالنميمة دل على أنه ولد زنا استنباطاً من قوله عز وجل "عتل بعد ذلك زنيم" والزنيم هو الدعى
68:13.english: Allah the Exalted said: "A slanderer, going about with calumny" then said: "Cruel, after that, base-born." Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: The base-born (Zanim) is the child of fornication who does not conceal speech, and he indicated by this that everyone who does not conceal speech and goes about with talebearing shows that he is a child of fornication, derived from His saying the Exalted: "Cruel, after that, base-born." And the base-born (Zanim) is the one attributed falsely.
68:13.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

68:32.arabic: وتقول عند الخسران ﴿ عسى ربنا أن يبدلنا خيرا منها إنا إلى ربنا راغبون ﴾
68:32.english: And say at the time of loss: 'Perhaps our Lord will exchange for us better than it. Indeed, we are to our Lord desirous.'
68:32.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

68:35.arabic: فلو خرجت من مكمن الغرور وأنصفت نفسك يا رجل وكلنا ذلك الرجل لعلمت أنك من حين تصبح إلى حين تمسي لا تسعى إلا في الحظوظ العاجلة ولا تتحرك ولا تسكن إلا لعاجل الدنيا ثم تطمع أن تكون غدا من أمته وأتباعه وما أبعد ظنك وما أبرد طمعك ﴿ أفنجعل المسلمين كالمجرمين ما لكم كيف تحكمون ﴾ {} ولنرجع إلى ما كنا فيه وبصدده فقد امتد عنان الكلام إلى غير مقصده ولنذكر الآن من المنامات الكاشفة لأحوال الموتي ما يعظم الانتفاع به إذ ذهبت النبوة وبقيت المبشرات وليس ذلك إلا المنامات.
68:35.english: If you were to emerge from the abode of delusion and be just to your soul (Nafs), O man—and all of us are that man—you would know that from morning until evening you strive only for immediate gains, and you neither move nor rest except for the immediate worldly life. Then you hope to be tomorrow from his community (Ummah) and followers, and how distant is your assumption and how cold is your hope! 'Shall We then treat the Muslims like the criminals? What is [wrong] with you? How do you judge?' (Quran 68:35-36). And let us return to what we were in and concerning, for the reins of speech have extended beyond its intended purpose. And let us now mention from the dreams that reveal the states of the dead what greatly benefits from it, since prophethood has gone and the glad tidings remain, and that is nothing but the dreams.
68:35.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Book of Repentance'

68:44.arabic: وهذا الغرور علاجه معرفة دلائل الكرامة والهوان إما بالبصيرة أو بالتقليد أما البصيرة فبأن يعرف وجه كون الالتفات إلى شهوات الدنيا مبعد عن الله ووجه كون التباعد عنها مقرباً إلى الله ويدرك ذلك بالإلهام في منازل العارفين والأولياء، وشرحه من جملة علوم المكاشفة ولا يليق بعلم المعاملة "وأما معرفته بطريق التقليد والتصديق" فهو أن يؤمن بكتاب الله تعالى ويصدق رسوله وقد قال تعالى "أيحسبون أن ما نمدهم به من مال وبنين نسارع لهم في الخيرات بل لا يشعرون" وقال تعالى "سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون" وقال تعالى "فتحنا ع
68:44.english: And the cure for this delusion (Ghurur) is knowing the signs of honor (Karama) and humiliation (Hawan) either through insight (Bassira) or through imitation (Taqleed). As for insight, it is by knowing how turning toward the desires of the world distances from Allah and how distancing from them brings near to Allah, and one perceives that through inspiration (Ilham) in the stations of the knowers (Arifeen) and the friends (Awliya), and its explanation is among the sciences of unveiling (Mukashafa) and is not suitable for the science of transaction. "And as for knowing it through the way of imitation and belief," it is to have faith in the Book of Allah the Exalted and believe His Messenger. And He the Exalted has said: "Do they think that what We extend to them of wealth and children, We hasten for them in good things? Rather, they do not perceive." And He the Exalted has said: "So leave Me with [the matter of] whoever denies this statement. We will progressively lead them [to destruction] from where they do not know." And He the Exalted has said: "We opened to them the gates of every thing until, when they rejoiced in that which they were given, We seized them suddenly, and at once they were in despair." And in the interpretation of His saying the Exalted "We will progressively lead them [to destruction] from where they do not know," it is that whenever they commit a sin, We grant them a blessing to increase their delusion. And He the Exalted has said: "We only give them respite that they may increase in sin." And He the Exalted has said: "And never think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. He only delays them for a Day when eyes will stare [in horror]." And other than that which has come in the Book of Allah the Exalted and the Sunnah of His Messenger. So whoever believes in it is freed from this delusion, for the origin of this delusion is ignorance of Allah and His attributes, for whoever knows Him does not feel secure from His plan (Makr) nor is deceived by such false imaginings, and looks at Pharaoh, Haman, and Korah and at the kings of the earth and what happened to them—how Allah was good to them initially then destroyed them utterly! So He the Exalted said: "Do you perceive of them anyone?" the verse. And Allah the Exalted has warned of His plan and gradual leading, saying: "So none feels secure from the plan of Allah except the losing people." And He the Exalted has said: "And they planned a plan, and We planned a plan, while they perceived not." And He the Mighty and Majestic has said: "And they planned, and Allah planned. And Allah is the best of planners." And He the Exalted has said: "Indeed, they are planning a plan, and I am planning a plan. So allow time for the disbelievers. Deal with them gently [for a while]." So just as it is not permissible for the neglected servant to infer from the master's neglect of him and enabling.
68:44.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

68:44.arabic: الحمد لله الذي لا يتكل على عفوه ورحمته إلا الراجون، ولا يحذر سوء غضبه وسطوته إلا الخائفون، الذي استدرج عباده من حيث لا يعلمون، وسلط عليهم الشهوات وأمرهم بترك ما يشتهون، وابتلاهم بالغضب وكلفهم كظم الغيظ فيما يغضبون، ثم حفهم بالمكاره واللذات وأملى لهم لينظر كيف يعملون، وامتحن بهم حبهم ليعلم صدقهم فيما يدعون، وعرفهم أنه لا يخفى عليه شيء مما يسرون وما يعلنون، وحذرهم أن يأخذهم بغتة وهم لا يشعرون فقال "ما ينظرون إلا صيحة واحدة تأخذهم وهم يخصمون فلا يستطيعون توصية ولا إلى أهلهم يرجعون" والصلاة والسلام
68:44.english: Praise be to Allah who none rely upon His pardon and His mercy except the hopeful ones, and none fear the evil of His anger and His might except the fearful ones, who gradually leads His servants from where they do not know, and empowered over them the desires and commanded them to abandon what they desire, and tested them with anger and obligated them to suppress rage in what angers them, then surrounded them with hardships and pleasures and gave them respite to see how they act, and tested through them their love to know their truthfulness in what they claim, and made known to them that nothing is hidden from Him of what they conceal and what they reveal, and warned them that He may seize them suddenly while they are unaware, so He said: "They await not but a single blast which will seize them while they are disputing. Then they will not be able to make a bequest, nor will they return to their families." And prayers and peace be upon Muhammad His messenger under whose banner the prophets march, and upon his family and his companions the guided leaders, and the pleased masters, prayers equal in number to what has been of Allah's creation and what will be, and may the first and the last attain its blessing, and grant abundant peace.
68:44.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

68:44.arabic: ولذلك قال الله عز وجل: (ولا تطع من أغفلنا قلبه عن ذكرنا واتبع هواه وكان أمره فرط
68:44.english: And therefore Allah the Exalted said: (And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our Remembrance (Dhikr) and who follows his desire (Hawa) and whose affair is ever [in] neglect
68:44.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

68:48.arabic: ولم يحتمل ليونس عليه السلام ما دون هذا لما أقيم مقام القبض والهيبة، فعوقب بالسجن في بطن الحوت - في ظلمات ثلاث - ونودي عليه إلى يوم القيامة " لولا أن تداركه نعمة من ربه لنبذ بالعراء وهو مذموم ". قال الحسن: العراء هو القيامة. ونهى نبينا ﭬ أن يقتدى به وقيل له: " فاصبر لحكم ربك ولا تكن كصاحب الحوت إذ نادى وهو مكظوم ".
68:48.english: And it was not endured for Yunus (Jonah), peace be upon him, what was less than this because he was placed in the position of contraction (Qabd) and awe (Hibah), so he was punished with imprisonment in the belly of the whale - in three darknesses - and he was called upon until the Day of Resurrection: "Had it not been that a favor from his Lord reached him, he would have been cast on the barren shore while he was blameworthy." Al-Hasan said: The barren shore (Al-'Ara') is the Resurrection. And our Prophet, peace be upon him, was prohibited from being followed in this, and it was said to him: "So be patient for the decree of your Lord and do not be like the companion of the whale when he called out while he was suppressed."
68:48.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

68:49.arabic: ولكن في الحال مختلفان، فقال: " وأما من جاءك يسعى  وهو  يخشى  فأنت  عنده تلهى "، وقال في الآخر: " أما من استغنى فأنت له تصدى "  وةكذلك  أمره  بالقعود مع طائفة، فقال عز وجل: " وإذا جاءك الذين يؤمنون بآياتنا  فقل  سلام  عليكم  " وأمره بالإعراض عن غيرهم، فقال: " وإذا رأيت  الذين  يخوضون  في  آياتنا  فأعرض عنهم " حتى قال: " فلا تقعد بعد الذكرى مع القوم  الظالمين  "  وقال  تعالى:  " واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي ". فكذلك الانبساط والإدلال يحتمل من بعض العباد دون بعض. فمن  انبساط  الأنس
68:49.english: But in the state (Hāl) they differ, so He said: "And as for he who comes to you striving while he fears, you are to him diverted," and in the other: "As for he who considers himself self-sufficient, to him you give attention." And likewise He commanded him to sit with a group, so the Mighty and Majestic said: "And when those who believe in Our signs come to you, say: Peace be upon you." And He commanded him to turn away from others, saying: "And when you see those who engage in vain discourse concerning Our signs, then turn away from them" until He said: "Then do not sit after the Remembrance (Dhikr) with the wrongdoing people." And He said: "And restrain yourself with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening." Similarly, expansion (Inbisāt) and familiarity (Idlāl) are permissible for some worshippers and not others. From the expansion of intimacy (Uns) is the saying of Moses, peace be upon him: "It is not except Your trial; You misguide with it whom You will and guide whom You will," and his saying in explanation and excuse when it was said to him: "Go to Pharaoh," so he said: "And they have upon me a sin," and his saying: "Indeed, I fear that they will deny me and that my breast will tighten and my tongue will not be fluent," and his saying: "Indeed, we fear that he will hasten against us or that he will transgress." And this from other than Moses, peace be upon him, would be from bad manners (Sū' al-Adab) because the one who is placed in the station (Maqām) of intimacy (Uns) is indulged and tolerated. And it was not tolerated for Jonah, peace be upon him, what is less than this because he was placed in the station of contraction (Qabd) and awe (Hībah), so he was punished with imprisonment in the belly of the whale - in three darknesses - and he was called out to until the Day of Resurrection: "Had it not been that a favor (Ni'mah) from his Lord reached him, he would have been cast onto the open land (Al-'Arā') while he was blameworthy." Al-Hasan said: Al-'Arā' is the Resurrection. And our Prophet, peace be upon him, was prohibited from being followed in this, and it was said to him: "So be patient for the decree of your Lord and do not be like the companion of the whale when he called out while he was distressed."
68:49.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

69:14.arabic: يوم ترى الأرض قد زلزلت فيه زالزالها، وأخرجت الأرض أثقالها، يومئذ يصدر الناس أشتاتا ليروا أعمالهم، يوم تحمل الأرض والجبال فدكتا دكة واحدة، فيومئذ وقعت الواقعة وانشقت السماء فهى يومئذ واهية، والملك على أرجائها، ويحمل عرش ربك فوقهم يومئذ ثمانية يومئذ تعرضون لا تخفى منكم خافية، يوم تسير الجبال وترى الأرض بارزة، يوم ترج الأرض فيه رجا وتبس الجبال بسا فكانت هباء منبثا، يوم يكون الناس كالفراش المبثوث وتكون الجبال كالعهن المنفوش، يوم تذهل فيه كل مرضعة عما أرضعت وتضع كل ذات حمل حملها وترى الناس سكارى وما
69:14.english: On that day you will see the earth shaken with its shaking, and the earth will cast out its burdens, then the people will emerge in groups to see their deeds. On the day the earth and the mountains are carried and crushed with a single crushing, then the Event (al-Waqi'ah) will occur and the sky will split, so it will be frail on that day, and the angels will be on its edges, and the Throne (Arsh) of your Lord will be carried above them on that day by eight. On that day you will be presented, nothing hidden from you will be concealed. On the day the mountains will move and you will see the earth bare, on the day the earth will be shaken with a shaking and the mountains will be pulverized with a pulverization so they become scattered dust, on the day the people will be like scattered moths and the mountains will be like carded wool, on the day every nursing mother will be distracted from what she nursed and every pregnant one will deliver her burden and you will see the people intoxicated while they are not intoxicated but the punishment of Allah is severe, on the day the earth will be changed to another earth and the heavens and they will appear before Allah the One, the Subduer (al-Qahhar), on the day the mountains will be blown away with a blowing so they leave a level plain where you see no crookedness nor unevenness, on the day you will see the mountains, you think them fixed while they pass like the passing of clouds, on the day the sky will split so it becomes like red leather, then on that day no human nor jinn will be asked about his sin, on the day the disobedient will be prevented from speech and no inquiry will be made about crimes but they will be seized by the forelocks and the feet, on the day every soul (Nafs) will find what it did of good present and what it did of evil it wishes there were a great distance between it and that, on the day every soul (Nafs) will know what it has brought and will testify to what it sent ahead and left behind, on the day the tongues will be silenced and the limbs will speak.
69:14.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

69:24.arabic: وعلى الجملة لا سبيل إلى إهمال النفس في الشهوات المباحات وأتباعها بكل حال فبقدر ما يستوفي العبد من شهوته يخشى أن يقال له يوم القيامة "أذهبتم طيباتكم في حياتكم الدنيا واستمتعتم بها" وبقدر ما يجاهد نفسه ويترك شهوته يتمتع في الدار الآخر بشهواته. قال بعض أهل البصرة: نازعتني نفسي خبز أرز وسمكاً فمنعتها، فقويت مطالبتها واشتدت مجاهدتي لها عشرين سنة، فلما مات قال بعضهم: رأيته في المنام فقلت ماذا فعل الله بك؟ قال: لا أحسن أن أصف ما تلقاني به ربي من النعم والكرامات، وكان أول شيء استقبلني به خبز أرز وسمكاً.
69:24.english: In summary, there is no way to neglect the Soul (Nafs) in permissible desires and follow it in every circumstance. To the extent that the servant fulfills his desire, he fears that it will be said to him on the Day of Resurrection: 'You exhausted your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them.' And to the extent that he struggles against his Soul (Nafs) and abandons his desire, he will enjoy in the Abode of the Hereafter with his desires. Some people of Basra said: My Soul (Nafs) contended with me for rice bread and fish, so I prevented it. Its demand strengthened and my struggle against it intensified for twenty years. When he died, some of them said: I saw him in a dream and said: What did Allah do with you? He said: I cannot describe what my Lord met me with of blessings and honors, and the first thing that welcomed me was rice bread and fish. And He said: Eat today your desire pleasantly without account. And Allah the Exalted said: 'Eat and drink pleasantly for what you sent ahead in the past days.' And they had sent ahead the abandonment of desires. And for that reason, Abu Sulayman said: Abandoning one desire from the desires is more beneficial for the Heart (Qalb) than fasting a year and standing in prayer during it. May Allah grant us success in what pleases Him.
69:24.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Harms of the Tongue'

69:24.arabic: وقال وكيع في قوله تعال:ى ﴿ كلوا واشربوا هنيئا بما أسلفتم في الأيام الخالية ﴾{} هي أيام الصيام إذ تركوا فيها الأكل والشرب وقد جمع رسول الله ﭬ في رتبة المباهاة بين الزهد في الدنيا وبين الصوم فقال: (إن الله تعالى يباهي ملائكته بالشاب العابد فيقول: أيها الشاب التارك شهوته لأجلي المبذل شبابه لي أنت عندي كبعض ملائكتي[10]) وقال ﭬ في الصائم: (يقول الله عز وجل: انظروا يا ملائكتي إلى عبدي ترك شهوته ولذته وطعامه وشرابه من أجلي[11])
69:24.english: And Waki' said regarding His statement, the Exalted: 'Eat and drink pleasantly for what you sent ahead in the days that have passed' (Quran 69:24) - they are the days of fasting since they abandoned in them eating and drinking. And the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) gathered in the rank of boasting between asceticism (Zuhd) in the worldly life and fasting, saying: 'Indeed God, the Exalted, boasts to His angels about the worshipping youth, saying: O youth who abandoned his desire for My sake, who expended his youth for Me, you are with Me like some of My angels.' And he (peace be upon him) said regarding the fasting person: 'God, the Mighty and Majestic, says: Look, O My angels, at My servant who abandoned his desire, his pleasure, his food, and his drink for My sake.'
69:24.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Mysteries of Fasting'

69:28.arabic: وحكى عن هرون الرشيد أنه انتقى أكفانه بيده عند الموت وكان ينظر إليها ويقول ما أغنى عني ماليه هلك عني سلطانيه وفرش المأمون رمادا واضطجع عليه وكان يقول يا من لا يزول ملكه ارحم من قد زال ملكه.
69:28.english: And it was narrated about Harun al-Rashid that he selected his burial shrouds with his own hand at the time of death, and he was looking at them and saying: 'My wealth (Mali) has not availed me (Ma Aghna 'Anni Maliyah) - my authority has perished from me.' And al-Ma'mun spread ashes and lay upon them, and he was saying: 'O You whose dominion does not vanish, have mercy upon one whose dominion has vanished.'
69:28.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

70:4.arabic: وكان كرز بن وبرة يختم القرآن في كل يوم ثلاث مرات ويجاهد نفسه في العبادات غاية المجاهدة فقيل له قد أجهدت نفسك فقال كم عمر الدنيا فقيل سبعة آلاف سنة فقال كم مقدار يوم القيامة فقيل خمسون ألف سنة فقال كيف يعجز أحدكم أن يعمل سبع يوم حتى يأمن ذلك اليوم يعنى أنك لو عشت عمر الدنيا واجتهدت سبعة آلاف سنة وتخلصت من يوم واحد كان مقداره خمسين ألف سنة لكان ربحك كثيرا وكنت بالرغبة فيه جديرا فكيف وعمرك قصير والآخرة لا غاية لها
70:4.english: And Karaz ibn Wabra used to complete the Quran three times every day and strive against his soul (Nafs) in acts of worship to the utmost striving (Mujahada). It was said to him: 'You have exhausted your soul (Nafs).' He said: 'How long is the lifespan of the world?' It was said: 'Seven thousand years.' He said: 'What is the measure of the Day of Resurrection?' It was said: 'Fifty thousand years.' He said: 'How can one of you be incapable of working for a seventh of a day until he is secure from that Day?' Meaning: If you lived the lifespan of the world and strove for seven thousand years and were saved from one day whose measure is fifty thousand years, your profit would be great and you would be worthy of desire for it. So how [can this be] when your lifespan is short and the Hereafter has no limit?
70:4.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

70:6.arabic: ثم يعرفنا قرب القيامة فيقول اقتربت الساعة وانشق القمر ﴿ إنهم يرونه بعيدا ونراه قريبا ﴾ {} ﴿ وما يدريك لعل الساعة تكون قريبا ﴾ {} ثم يكون أحسن أحوالنا أن نتخذ دراسة هذا القرآن عملا فلا نتدبر معانيه ولا ننظر فى كثرة أوصاف هذا اليوم وأساميه ولا نستعد للتخلص من دواهيه فنعوذ بالله من هذه الغفلة إن لم يداركنا الله بواسع رحمته.
70:6.english: Then He makes known to us the nearness of the Resurrection (Qiyamah) and says: 'The Hour (Saa'ah) has drawn near and the moon has split' (Quran 54:1). 'Indeed, they see it as distant, but We see it as near' (Quran 70:6-7). 'And what will make you perceive? Perhaps the Hour (Saa'ah) is near' (Quran 33:63). Then the best of our states becomes that we take the study of this Quran as an action, yet we do not ponder its meanings, nor do we look at the multitude of descriptions of this Day (Yawm) and its names, nor do we prepare to be delivered from its calamities. So we seek refuge in Allah from this heedlessness (Ghaflah) if Allah does not reach us with His vast mercy.
70:6.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

70:23.arabic: فهذا تفصيل صلاة الخاشعين الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون والذين هم على صلواتهم يحافظون والذين هم على صلاتهم دائمون والذين هم يناجون الله على قدر استطاعتهم في العبودية فليعرض الإنسان نفسه على هذه الصلاة فبالقدر الذي يسر له منه ينبغي أن يفرح وعلى ما يفوته ينبغي أن يتحسر وفي مداراة ذلك ينبغي أن يجتهد.
70:23.english: This is the detailed description of the prayer of the humble ones (Al-Khashi'un) who are in their prayer humble, and those who are over their prayers preserving, and those who are over their prayer constant (Da'imun), and those who are conversing with Allah (Munajun) according to their capability in servitude (Al-'Ubudiyyah). So let a person present himself to this prayer; for the amount that is made easy for him from it, he should rejoice, and for what he misses, he should grieve, and in managing that, he should strive.
70:23.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

70:28.arabic: وكيف يؤمن تغير الحال وقلب المؤمن بين أصبعين من أصابع الرحمن وأن القلب أشد تقلبا من القدر في غليانها وقد قال مقلب القلوب عز وجل: ﴿ إن عذاب ربهم غير مأمون ﴾ {} فأجهل الناس من أمنه وهو ينادي بالتحذير من الأمن ولو أن الله لطف بعباده العارفين إذ روح قلوبهم بروح الرجاء لاحترقت قلوبهم من نار الخوف.
70:28.english: And how can one feel secure about the changing of states when the heart (Qalb) of the believer is between two fingers of the fingers of the Most Merciful (Ar-Rahman), and the heart is more fluctuating than a pot in its boiling? And the Turner of Hearts (Muqallib al-Qulub), may He be glorified and exalted, has said: 'Indeed, the punishment of their Lord is not to be felt secure from.' So the most ignorant of people is he who feels secure from it while He calls out with warning against feeling secure. And if Allah had been gentle with His servants, the knowers (al-'Arifin), by reviving their hearts with the spirit (Ruh) of hope, their hearts would have burned from the fire of fear.
70:28.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

70:32.arabic: وقال تعالى والذين هم لأماناتهم وعهدهم راعون والذين هم بشهاداتهم قائمون وقال ابن المبارك لرجل راقب الله تعالى فسأله عن تفسيره فقال كن أبدا كأنك ترى الله عز وجل
70:32.english: And Allah the Exalted said: 'And those who are for their trusts (Amanat) and their covenants (Ahd) caretakers (Ra'un), and those who are for their testimonies upright.' And Ibn Al-Mubarak said to a man: 'Observe (Raqib) Allah the Exalted,' and he asked him about its interpretation, so he said: 'Be always as if you see Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.'
70:32.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

71:12.arabic: اعلم أن الله تعالى قد سمى المال خيراً في مواضع من كتابه العزيز فقل جل وعز "إن ترك خيراً" الآية وقال رسول الله ﭬ "نعم المال الصالح للرجل الصالح"[13] وكل ما جاء في ثواب الصدقة والحج فهو ثناء على المال إذ لا يمكن الوصول إليهما إلا به. وقال تعالى "ويسخر لكم ما في السموات وما في الأرض جميعاً منه" وقال تعالى ممتناً على عباده "ويمددكم بأموال وبنين ويجعل لكم جنات ويجعل لكم أنهاراً" وقال ﭬ "كاد الفقر أن يكون كفراً"[14] وهو ثناء على المال. ولا تقف على وجه الجمع بعد الذم والمدح إلا بأن تعرف حكمة المال ومقص
71:12.english: Know that Allah the Exalted has called wealth good in places in His Noble Book, so say He is Glorified and Exalted: "If he leaves good" the verse, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "How good is righteous wealth for a righteous man"[13], and all that comes regarding the reward of charity and pilgrimage is praise for wealth since it is not possible to reach them except through it. And He the Exalted said: "And He subjects for you what is in the heavens and what is on earth all from Him", and He the Exalted said, bestowing favor upon His servants: "And He will aid you with wealth and children and make for you gardens and make for you rivers", and He (peace be upon him) said: "Poverty almost becomes disbelief"[14], and this is praise for wealth. And you will not comprehend the aspect of reconciliation after blame and praise except by knowing the wisdom of wealth, its purpose, its harms, and its dangers; until it becomes clear to you that it is good from one aspect and evil from another aspect, and that it is praiseworthy from where it is good and blameworthy from where it is evil, for it is not pure good nor pure evil, but rather it is a cause for both matters, and what has this description is inevitably praised at times and blamed at others, but the discerning distinguisher perceives that the praiseworthy from it is not the blameworthy, and its clarification is by deriving from what we mentioned in the Book of Gratitude regarding the explanation of goods and the detailing of the degrees of blessings, and the sufficient amount in it is that the aim of the wise and the people of insight is the happiness of the Hereafter which is the everlasting bliss and the kingdom and the abiding. And aiming for this is the constant practice of the noble and the wise, for it was said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him): Who are the most honorable of people and the wisest of them? He said: "The most frequent in remembrance (Dhikr) of death and the most prepared for it"[15]. And this happiness is not attained except through three means in the world, and they are the spiritual virtues, like knowledge and good character, and the bodily virtues: like health and safety, and the virtues external to the body: like wealth and other means. And the highest of them are the spiritual, then the bodily, then the external.
71:12.book_title: Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth
71:12.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

71:13.arabic: ولذلك عبر العرب عن الخوف بالرجاء فقال تعالى: ﴿ ما لكم لا ترجون لله وقارا ﴾ {} أي لا تخافون وكثيرا ما ورد في القرآن الرجاء بمعنى الخوف وذلك لتلازمهما إذ عادة العرب التعبير عن الشيء بما يلازمه
71:13.english: And therefore the Arabs expressed the Fear (Khauf) through Hope (Raja') as Allah the Exalted said: 'What is the matter with you that you do not hope for Allah with awe (Waqar)?' meaning you do not fear. And often in the Quran, Hope (Raja') comes with the meaning of Fear (Khauf), and that is due to their inseparability, as it is the custom of the Arabs to express a thing through what accompanies it.
71:13.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

71:15.arabic: وقال تعالى ألم تروا كيف خلق الله سبع سموات طباقا وجعل القمر فيهن نورا وجعل الشمس سراجا والله أنبتكم من الأرض نباتا ثم يعيدكم فيها ويخرجكم إخراجا وقال تعالى أفرأيتم ما تمنون أأنتم تخلقونه أم نحن الخالقون إلى قوله للمقوين فليس يخفى على من معه أدنى مسكة من عقل إذا تأمل بأدنى فكرة مضمون هذه الآيات وأدار نظره على عجائب خلق الله في الأرض والسموات وبدائع فطرة الحيوان والنبات أن هذا الأمر العجيب والترتيب المحكم لا يستغني عن صانع يدبره وفاعل يحكمه ويقدره بل تكاد فطرة النفوس تشهد بكونها مقهورة تحت تسخيره
71:15.english: And He (Exalted) said: 'Have you not seen how Allah created seven heavens in layers and made the moon therein a light and made the sun a lamp? And Allah has caused you to grow from the earth a growth. Then He will return you into it and extract you an extraction.' And He (Exalted) said: 'Then do you see what you emit? Is it you who creates it, or are We the Creator?' up to His saying: 'for the grateful.' So it is not hidden from one who possesses the slightest bit of intellect, if he contemplates with the least thought the content of these verses and directs his gaze upon the wonders of Allah's creation in the earth and the heavens and the marvels of the innate disposition (Fitra) of animals and plants, that this amazing affair and precise arrangement cannot do without a Maker who manages it and an Agent who governs it and determines it. Rather, the innate disposition (Fitra) of the souls (Nufus) almost testifies to being subdued under His subjugation and directed according to the requirement of His management. And for that reason Allah (Exalted) said: 'Is there doubt concerning Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth?'
71:15.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

71:26.arabic: بأبي أنت وأمي يا رسول الله لقد دعا نوح على قومه فقال رب لا تذر على الأرض من الكافرين ديارا ولو دعوت علينا بمثلها لهلكنا فلقد وطىء ظهرك وأدمى وجهك وكسرت رباعيتك فأبيت أن تقول إلا خيرا فقلت اللهم اغفر لقومي فإنهم لا يعلمون
71:26.english: By my father and mother, O Messenger of Allah, indeed Noah invoked against his people, saying: 'My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from the disbelievers a single dweller (Quran 71:26).' And if you had invoked against us with its like, we would have perished. For indeed your back was trampled, your face was bloodied, and your incisor was broken, yet you refused to say except good, so you said: 'O Allah, forgive my people, for they do not know.'
71:26.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

71:28.arabic: رب اغفر لي ولوالدي وارحمهما كما ربياني صغيرا واغفر للمؤمنين والمؤمنات والمسلمين والمسلمات الأحياء منهم والأموات
71:28.english: Lord, forgive me and my parents and have mercy on them as they raised me when I was small, and forgive the believing men and believing women and the submitting men and submitting women, the living among them and the dead.
71:28.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

71:28.arabic: [164] حديث رب اغفر لي ولوالدي وارحمهما كما ربياني صغيرا واغفر للمؤمنين والمؤمنات والمسلمين والمسلمات الأحياء منهم والأموات أخرجه أبو داود وابن ماجه بإسناد حسن من حديث أبي أسيد الساعدي قال رجل من بني سلمة هل بقي علي من بر أبوي شيء قال نعم الصلاة عليهما والاستغفار لهما الحديث ولأبي الشيخ ابن حبان في الثواب والمستغفري في الدعوات من حديث أنس من استغفر للمؤمنين والمؤمنات رد الله عليه عن كل مؤمن مضى من أول الدهر أو هو كائن إلى يوم القيامة وسنده ضعيف وفي صحيح ابن حبان من حديث أبي سعيد أيما رجل مسلم لم
71:28.english: Hadith: 'My Lord (Rabb), forgive me and my parents and have mercy upon them as they raised me when I was small, and forgive the believing men (al-mu'minin) and the believing women (al-mu'minat) and the submitting men (al-muslimin) and the submitting women (al-muslimat), the living among them and the dead.' Reported by Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah with a good chain (isnad) from the narration of Abu Usayd al-Sa'idi. A man from Banu Salamah said: 'Is there anything left upon me of dutifulness (birr) to my parents?' He said: 'Yes, praying for them and seeking forgiveness (istighfar) for them.' The hadith. And for Abu al-Shaykh Ibn Hibban in 'al-Thawab' and al-Mustaghfiri in 'al-Da'awat' from the narration of Anas: 'Whoever seeks forgiveness (istaghfara) for the believing men (al-mu'minin) and the believing women (al-mu'minat), Allah will return to him for every believer who has passed from the beginning of time or who will be until the Day of Resurrection (Yawm al-Qiyamah).' Its chain is weak. And in the Sahih of Ibn Hibban from the narration of Abu Sa'id: 'Any Muslim man who does not have charity (sadaqah) with him, let him say in his supplication (du'a'): O Allah, send blessings (salli) upon Muhammad, Your servant ('abd) and Your messenger (rasul), and send blessings upon the believing men (al-mu'minin) and the believing women (al-mu'minat) and the submitting men (al-muslimin) and the submitting women (al-muslimat), for it is purification (zakah).'
71:28.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication

72:1.arabic: هو الذي أرشد الأولين والآخرين ولما سمعه الجن لم يلبثوا أن ولوا إلى قومهم منذرين فقالوا إنا سمعنا قرآنا عجبا يهدي إلى الرشد فآمنا به ولن نشرك بربنا أحدا فكل من آمن به فقد وفق ومن قال به فقد صدق ومن تمسك به فقد هدي ومن عمل به فقد فاز
72:1.english: It is the one that guided the first and the last, and when the Jinn heard it, they did not delay in turning back to their people as warners, and they said: 'Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Quran that guides to the right path (Rushd), so we have believed in it, and we will not associate with our Lord anyone.' So everyone who believes in it has been granted success (Waffaqa), and everyone who speaks by it has spoken truthfully, and everyone who holds fast to it has been guided, and everyone who acts by it has attained success.
72:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

72:13.arabic: فإن قلت: فما شبهة المعتزلة والمرجئة وما حجة بطلان قولهم. فأقول شبهتهم عمومات القرآن أما المرجئة فقالوا لا يدخل المؤمن النار وإن أتي بكل المعاصي لقوله عز وجل: ﴿ فمن يؤمن بربه فلا يخاف بخسا ولا رهقا ﴾ {} ولقوله سبحانه وتعالى: ﴿ والذين آمنوا بالله ورسله أولئك هم الصديقون ﴾ {} الآية ولقوله تعالى: ﴿ كلما ألقي فيها فوج سألهم خزنتها. ﴾ {} إلى قوله: ﴿ فكذبنا وقلنا ما نزل الله من شيء ﴾ {} فقوله كلما ألقي فيها فوج عام فينبغي أن يكون من ألقي في النار مكذبا ولقوله تعالى: ﴿ لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى الذي كذب وتول
72:13.english: If you say: What is the doubt of the Mu'tazila and the Murji'a and what is the proof of the invalidity of their statement? I say: Their doubt is generalities of the Quran. As for the Murji'a, they said: The believer does not enter the Fire even if he commits all sins, due to His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'So whoever believes in his Lord, he does not fear loss (bakhsan) nor oppression (rahqan).' And due to His saying, the Blessed and Exalted: 'And those who believe in Allah and His messengers - those are the truthful ones.' The verse. And due to His saying: 'Every time a group is thrown into it, its keepers will ask them...' until His saying: 'So we denied and said: Allah has not sent down anything.' So His saying 'Every time a group is thrown into it' is general, so it should be that whoever is thrown into the Fire is a denier. And due to His saying: 'None will burn in it except the most wretched, who denied and turned away.' And this is restriction, affirmation, and negation. And due to His saying: 'Whoever comes with a good deed will have better than it, and they will be safe from fear that Day.' So faith (Iman) is the head of good deeds. And due to His saying: 'And Allah loves the doers of good (Muhsinin).' And He said: 'Indeed, We do not waste the reward of one who does good work.' And they have no proof in that, for wherever faith (Iman) is mentioned in these verses, it is intended to be faith (Iman) with action, since we have clarified that faith (Iman) may be used and intended to mean Islam, which is agreement with the heart (Qalb), speech, and action. The evidence for this interpretation is many reports about punishing the disobedient and the measures of punishment, and his saying (peace be upon him): 'He will be taken out of the Fire whoever has in his heart (Qalb) an atom's weight of faith (Iman).' So how can he be taken out if he did not enter? And from the Quran, His saying: 'Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills.' And the exception with will indicates division.
72:13.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Foundations of Belief'

72:23.arabic: وأما المعتزلة فشبهتهم قوله تعالى: ﴿ وإني لغفار لمن تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا ثم اهتدى ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ والعصر إن الإنسان لفي خسر إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى ﴿ وإن منكم إلا واردها كان على ربك حتما مقضيا ﴾ {} ثم قال: ﴿ ثم ننجي الذين اتقوا ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ ومن يعص الله ورسوله فإن له نار جهنم ﴾ {} وكل آية ذكر الله عز وجل العمل الصالح فيها مقرونا بالإيمان وقوله تعالى: ﴿ ومن يقتل مؤمنا متعمدا فجزاؤه جهنم خالدا فيها ﴾ {} وهذه العمومات أيضا مخصوصة بدليل قوله تعالى: ﴿ ويغفر ما دون ذل
72:23.english: As for the Mu'tazilites, their evidence is His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, I am Forgiving to whoever repents and believes and does righteous deeds then remains guided' and His saying, the Exalted: 'By time, indeed, mankind is in loss, except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds' and His saying, the Exalted: 'And there is none of you except he will enter it; it has been upon your Lord a decree determined' then He said: 'Then We will save those who feared' and His saying, the Exalted: 'And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, then indeed, for him is the Fire of Hell' and every verse in which Allah, the Exalted, mentions righteous deeds coupled with faith and His saying, the Exalted: 'And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein eternally' and these generalities are also specified by the evidence of His saying, the Exalted: 'And He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills' so it is appropriate that His will remains in forgiving what is besides polytheism and likewise His saying: 'He will bring out of the Fire whoever had in his heart an atom's weight of faith' and His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, We do not waste the reward of one who does good deeds' and His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, Allah does not waste the reward of the doers of good' so how would He waste the reward of the foundation of faith and all acts of obedience with a single disobedience and His saying, the Exalted: 'And whoever kills a believer intentionally' meaning because of his faith and it has come regarding such a cause.
72:23.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Foundations of Belief'

72:23.arabic: وخطب رجل عند رسول الله ﭬ فقال: من يطع الله ورسوله فقد رشد ومن يعصهما فقد غوى"[257] فقال "قل: ومن يعص الله ورسوله فقد غوى فكره رسول الله ﭬ قوله: ومن يعصهما، لأنه تسوية وجمع.
72:23.english: And a man delivered a sermon in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and said: 'Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has been guided, and whoever disobeys them has gone astray.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Say: And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has gone astray.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) disliked his saying: 'and whoever disobeys them,' because it is an equalization and a joining together.
72:23.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

72:23.arabic: وقوله تعالى: ﴿ ومن يعص الله ورسوله فإن له نار جهنم خالدين فيها ﴾ {} وتخصيصه بالكفر تحكم
72:23.english: And His saying, the Exalted: 'And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, then for him is the Fire of Hell, abiding therein eternally' {} and specifying it as disbelief is arbitrary judgment.
72:23.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Foundations of Belief'

72:26.arabic: وما غاب عن الأبصار فيعبر عنه بالغيب والملكوت والله تعالى عالم الغيب والشهادة وجبار الملك والملكوت ولا يحيط أحد بشىء من علمه إلا بما شاء وهو عالم الغيب فلا يظهر على غيبه أحدا إلا من ارتضى من رسول فأجل أيها العاقل فكر فى الملكوت فعسى يفتح لك ابواب السماء فتجول بقلبك فى أقطارها إلى أن يقوم قلبك بين يدي عرش الرحمن
72:26.english: And what is hidden from the sights is expressed as the Unseen (Al-Ghayb) and the Dominion (Al-Malakut), and Allah the Exalted is the Knower of the Unseen (Al-Ghayb) and the Witnessed (Al-Shahadah), and the Compeller of the Kingdom (Al-Mulk) and the Dominion (Al-Malakut). And no one encompasses anything of His knowledge except by what He wills, and He is the Knower of the Unseen (Al-Ghayb), so He does not reveal His Unseen (Ghayb) to anyone except to a messenger whom He has approved. Therefore, O intelligent one, contemplate in the Dominion (Al-Malakut), so perhaps the doors of the heaven will be opened for you, and you will wander with your Heart (Qalb) in its regions until your Heart (Qalb) stands before the Throne of the Most Merciful.
72:26.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Contemplation'

72:28.arabic: اللهم إني أعوذ بك من شر نفسي ومن شر كل دابة أنت آخذ بناصيتها إن ربي على صراط مستقيم
72:28.english: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of my soul (Nafs) and from the evil of every creature whose forelock You hold. Indeed, my Lord is upon a straight path.
72:28.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith

73:6.arabic: أما من الايات فقوله تعالى: ﴿ إن ربك يعلم أنك تقوم أدنى من ثلثي الليل ﴾ {} الاية وقوله تعالى: ﴿ إن ناشئة الليل هي أشد وطأ وأقوم قيلا ﴾ {} وقوله سبحانه وتعالى: ﴿ تتجافى جنوبهم عن المضاجع ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ أمن هو قانت آناء الليل ﴾ {} الآية وقوله عز وجل: ﴿ والذين يبيتون لربهم سجدا وقياما ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ واستعينوا بالصبر والصلاة ﴾ {} قيل هي قيام الليل يستعان بالصبر عليه على مجاهدة النفس.
73:6.english: As for from the verses, His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand (for prayer) nearly two-thirds of the night' (Quran 73:20) the verse, and His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, the rising (Nashia) of the night is more intense in treading (Wata'an) and more upright in speech (Qilan)' (Quran 73:6), and His saying, the Exalted and Majestic: 'Their sides forsake their beds' (Quran 32:16), and His saying, the Exalted: 'Is one who is devoutly obedient (Qanit) during periods of the night' (Quran 39:9) the verse, and His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And those who spend the night for their Lord prostrating and standing' (Quran 25:64), and His saying, the Exalted: 'And seek help through patience and prayer' (Quran 2:45). It is said: it is the standing of the night; one seeks help through patience upon it in striving against the Soul (Nafs).
73:6.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

73:6.arabic: وقال تعالى: ﴿ إن ناشئة الليل هي أشد وطأ وأقوم قيلا ﴾ {}
73:6.english: And He (Allah), the Exalted, said: 'Indeed, the rising (Nashia) of the night is more intense in treading (Wata'an) and more upright in speech (Qilan).'
73:6.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

73:7.arabic: فإن لم تكن من أهله فانظر إلى خطاب الله تعالى لرسوله واقتبسه بنور الإيمان فقد قال الله تعالى لأقرب عبادة إليه وارفعهم درجة لديه: ﴿ إن لك في النهار سبحا طويلا واذكر اسم ربك وتبتل إليه تبتيلا ﴾ {}
73:7.english: If you are not from its people, then look at the address of Allah the Exalted to His Messenger and take it with the light of faith. Indeed, Allah the Exalted said to the closest worship to Him and the highest of them in degree with Him: 'Indeed, for you in the day is a long course (سبحا طويلا) and remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself to Him with complete devotion (تبتيلا).'
73:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

73:10.arabic: ولترك الأسباب الدافعة وإن كانت مقطوعة وجه إذا ناله الضرر من إنسان، فإنه إذا أمكنه الصبر وأمكنه الدفع والتشفي فشرط التوكل الاحتمال والصبر، قال الله تعالى: " فاتخذه وكيلاً واصبر على ما يقولون ". وقال تعالى: " ولنصبرن على ما آذيتمونا وعلى الله فليتوكل المتوكلون ". وقال عز وجل: " ودع أذاهم وتوكل على الله ". وقال سبحانه وتعالى: " فاصبر كما صبر أولو العزم من الرسل ". وقال تعالى: " نعم أجر العاملين الذين صبروا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون " وهذا في أذى الناس، وأما الصبر على أذى الحيات والسباع والعقارب، فترك دفعها
73:10.english: And abandoning the repelling causes, even if they are certain, has a justification when harm reaches him from a human being, for if he is able to have patience (Sabr) and is able to repel and seek revenge, then the condition of reliance (Tawakkul) is endurance and patience (Sabr). Allah the Exalted said: "So take Him as your trustee and have patience (Sabr) upon what they say." And He said: "And we will have patience (Sabr) upon what you harm us, and upon Allah let the reliant ones rely (Tawakkul)." And He the Mighty and Majestic said: "And leave their harm and rely (Tawakkul) upon Allah." And He the Blessed and Exalted said: "So have patience (Sabr) as the possessors of resolve from the messengers had patience (Sabr)." And He said: "Excellent is the reward of the workers who had patience (Sabr) and upon their Lord they rely (Tawakkul)." And this is regarding the harm of people. As for having patience (Sabr) upon the harm of snakes, beasts, and scorpions, abandoning repelling them is not from reliance (Tawakkul) in anything, for there is no benefit in it, and striving is not intended nor is striving abandoned for its own sake but to aid in the religion (Deen). The arrangement of causes here is like their arrangement in earning and bringing benefits, so we do not prolong with repetition. Likewise, in the causes repelling from wealth, reliance (Tawakkul) is not diminished by closing the door of the house when leaving nor by tying the camel, because these are causes known by the Sunnah of Allah the Exalted, either certainly or presumably. And for that reason, he ﷺ said to the Bedouin when he neglected the camel and said 'I have relied (Tawakkul) upon Allah': 'Tie it and rely (Tawakkul).' And He said: 'Take your precaution.' And He said regarding the manner of the prayer of fear: 'And let them take their weapons.' And He the Blessed said: 'And prepare for them what you are able of strength and of tying the horses.' And He said to Musa, peace be upon him: 'So travel by night with My servants.' And fortifying by night is hiding from the eyes of the enemies and a type of causation, and the hiding of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in
73:10.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

73:10.arabic: القسم الثاني: مالا يرتبط هجومه باختياره وله اختيار في دفعه كما لو أوذي بفعل أو قول وجنى عليه في نفسه أو ماله، فالصبر على ذلك بترك المكافأة تارة يكون واجبا وتارة يكون فضيلة. قال بعض الصحابة رضوان الله عليهم: ما كنا نعدّ إيمان الرجل ايمانا إذا لم يصبر على الأذى، وقال تعالى: ﴿ ولنصبرنّ على ما آذيتمونا وعلى الله فليتوكل المتوكلون ﴾ {}. (وقسم رسول الله ﭬ مرة مالا، فقال بعض الأعراب من المسلمين هذه قسمة ما أريد بها وجه الله فأخبر رسول الله فاحمرت وجنتاه ثم قال يرحم الله أخي موسى لقد أوذي بأكثر من هذا ف
73:10.english: The second category: That which does not relate to the assault by his choice, but he has a choice in repelling it, as if he is harmed by an action or saying and is wronged in his self (Nafs) or his wealth. Patience (Sabr) regarding that by abandoning retaliation is sometimes obligatory and sometimes a virtue. Some of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, said: 'We did not consider a man's faith (Iman) to be faith if he did not have patience (Sabr) upon harm.' And Allah the Exalted said: 'And we will certainly have patience (Sabr) upon what you harm us, and upon Allah let the reliant ones rely.' (Quran 14:12). (And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, once distributed wealth, so some of the Bedouin Muslims said: 'This is a distribution not intended by it the Face of Allah,' so the Messenger of Allah was informed, and his cheeks reddened, then he said: 'May Allah have mercy on my brother Musa; he was harmed more than this and had patience (Sabr).' [24]). And Allah the Exalted said: 'And leave their harm and rely upon Allah.' (Quran 73:10). And Allah the Exalted said: 'And have patience (Sabr) upon what they say and abandon them with a beautiful abandonment.' (Quran 73:10). And Allah the Exalted said: 'And indeed We know that your chest is constrained by what they say, so glorify with the praise of your Lord.' (Quran 15:97) the verse. And Allah the Exalted said: 'And you will certainly hear from those who were given the Book before you and from those who associate partners much harm, and if you have patience (Sabr) and are God-fearing (Taqwa), then indeed that is from the matters of determination.' (Quran 3:186) meaning have patience (Sabr) from retaliation. And for that reason, Allah the Exalted praised those who pardon from their rights in retaliation (Qisas) and other than it, so He the Exalted said: 'And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished, but if you have patience (Sabr), it is better for the patient ones (Sabirin).' (Quran 16:126). And he, peace be upon him, said: 'Maintain ties with the one who cuts you off, give to the one who deprives you, and pardon the one who wrongs you.' [25] And I saw in the Gospel, Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him, said: 'Indeed it was said to you before: An eye for an eye and a nose for a nose, but I say to you: Do not resist evil, but whoever strikes your right cheek, turn to him the left cheek, and whoever takes your cloak, give him your garment, and whoever compels you to go one mile, go with him two miles.' And all of that is a command to have patience (Sabr) upon harm. So patience (Sabr) upon the harm of people is from the highest levels of patience (Sabr) because in it cooperate the motivator of the religion (Din) and the motivator of desire (Shahwa) and anger (Ghadab) all together.
73:10.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

73:12.arabic: وقال تعالى: ﴿ إن لدينا أنكالا وجحيما وطعاما ذا غصة وعذابا أليما ﴾ {} وقال ابن عباس قال رسول الله ﭬ: (لو أن قطرة من الزقوم قطرت فى بحار الدنيا أفسدت على أهل الدنيا معايشهم فكيف من يكون طعامه ذلك؟[203])
73:12.english: And Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, with Us are shackles (Ankāl) and a Blazing Fire (Jahīm) and food that causes choking (Ghusṣah) and a painful punishment.' And Ibn Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'If a drop of the Zaqqum tree were to drip into the seas of the world, it would spoil the livelihoods of the people of the world, so how about one whose food is that?'
73:12.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Book of Repentance'

73:12.arabic: وفي رواية أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ هذا الآية أو قرئ عنده إن لدينا أنكالا وجحيما وطعاما ذا غصة وعذابا أليما فصعق حديث أنه قرئ عنده إن لدينا انكالا وجحيما وطعام ذا غصة وعذابا أليما فصعق رواه ابن عدي في الكامل والبيهقي في الشعب من طريقه من حديث أبي حرب بن أبي الأسود مرسلا
73:12.english: And in a narration, that the Prophet (peace be upon him) recited this verse or it was recited in his presence: 'Indeed, with Us are shackles (Ankāl) and a Blazing Fire (Jahīm), and food that chokes (ghuṣṣah) and a painful punishment (ʿadhāb alīm).' Then he fell unconscious (fa-ṣaʿaqa). The narration that it was recited in his presence: 'Indeed, with Us are shackles (Ankāl) and a Blazing Fire (Jahīm), and food that chokes (ghuṣṣah) and a painful punishment (ʿadhāb alīm).' Then he fell unconscious (fa-ṣaʿaqa). Reported by Ibn ʿAdī in Al-Kāmil and Al-Bayhaqī in Al-Shuʿab through his chain from the ḥadīth of Abū Ḥarb ibn Abī al-Aswad, mursalan.
73:12.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

73:12.arabic: [111]  حديث قرأ في سورة الحاقة فصعق المعروف فيما يروى من هذه القصة أنه قرئ عنده إن لدينا أنكالا وجحيما وطعاما ذا غصة وعذابا أليما فصعق كما رواه ابن عدي والبيهقي في الشعب مرسلا وهكذا ذكره المصنف على الصواب في تاب السماع كما تقدم.
73:12.english: [111] A hadith: He recited in Surah Al-Haqqah and fainted. What is known in what is narrated from this story is that it was recited to him: "Indeed, with Us are shackles (Ankalan) and a Blazing Fire (Jahiman), and food that chokes (Dha Ghussatin) and a painful punishment (Adhaban Aliman)." So he fainted, as narrated by Ibn 'Adi and Al-Bayhaqi in Al-Shu'ab with a broken chain, and thus the author mentioned it correctly in the chapter of Listening, as previously mentioned.
73:12.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Fear and Hope'

73:13.arabic: وفي رواية أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ هذا الآية أو قرئ عنده إن لدينا أنكالا وجحيما وطعاما ذا غصة وعذابا أليما فصعق حديث أنه قرئ عنده إن لدينا انكالا وجحيما وطعام ذا غصة وعذابا أليما فصعق رواه ابن عدي في الكامل والبيهقي في الشعب من طريقه من حديث أبي حرب بن أبي الأسود مرسلا
73:13.english: And in a narration, that the Prophet (peace be upon him) recited this verse or it was recited in his presence: 'Indeed, We have shackles and Hellfire and food that causes choking (ghuṣṣah) and painful punishment (ʿadhāb alīm).' Then he fell unconscious (faṣaʿaqa). The hadith that it was recited in his presence: 'Indeed, We have shackles and Hellfire and food that causes choking (ghuṣṣah) and painful punishment (ʿadhāb alīm).' Then he fell unconscious (faṣaʿaqa). Reported by Ibn ʿAdī in Al-Kāmil and Al-Bayhaqī in Al-Shuʿab through his chain from the hadith of Abī Ḥarb ibn Abī al-Aswad, mursalan.
73:13.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

73:20.arabic: أما من الايات فقوله تعالى: ﴿ إن ربك يعلم أنك تقوم أدنى من ثلثي  الليل  ﴾ {} الاية وقوله تعالى: ﴿ إن ناشئة الليل هي أشد وطأ  وأقوم  قيلا  ﴾  {}  وقوله سبحانه وتعالى: ﴿ تتجافى جنوبهم عن المضاجع ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿  أمن  هو  قانت آناء الليل ﴾ {} الآية وقوله عز وجل: ﴿ والذين يبيتون لربهم سجدا وقياما  ﴾  {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ واستعينوا بالصبر والصلاة  ﴾  {}  قيل  هي  قيام  الليل  يستعان بالصبر عليه على مجاهدة النفس.
73:20.english: As for from the verses, His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand (in prayer) for nearly two-thirds of the night, or half of it, or a third of it, and a group of those with you (also do so). And Allah determines the night and the day. He knew that you would not be able to keep count of it, so He turned to you in forgiveness. So recite what is easy from the Quran. He knew that there would be among you those who are ill, and others traveling throughout the land seeking from the bounty of Allah, and others fighting in the cause of Allah. So recite what is easy from it. And establish prayer and give zakah and lend to Allah a good loan. And whatever good you put forward for yourselves - you will find it with Allah. It is better and greater in reward. And seek forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.' (Quran 73:20) and His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, the rising (Nashia) of the night is more intense and more upright in speech.' (Quran 73:6) and His saying, the Exalted and Majestic: 'Their sides forsake their beds.' (Quran 32:16) and His saying, the Exalted: 'Is one who is devoutly obedient (Qanit) during periods of the night...' (Quran 39:9) the verse, and His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And those who spend the night for their Lord prostrating and standing.' (Quran 25:64) and His saying, the Exalted: 'And seek help through patience and prayer.' (Quran 2:45) It is said: it is the standing (Qiyam) of the night; one seeks help through patience upon it for the struggle (Mujahada) against the Soul (Nafs).
73:20.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

73:20.arabic: وأما قيام رسول الله ﷺ من حيث المقدار فلم يكن على ترتيب واحد بل ربما كان يقوم نصف الليل أو ثلثه أو سدسه[131] يختلف ذلك في الليالي ودلّ عليه قوله تعالى في الموضعين من سورة المزمل ﴿ إن ربك يعلم أنك تقوم أدنى من ثلثي الليل ونصفه وثلثه ﴾ {} فأدنى من ثلثي الليل كأنه بصفه ونصف سدسه فإن كسر قوله ونصفه وثلثه كان نصف الثلثين فيقرب من الثلث والربع وإن نصب كان نصف الليل وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها كان ﷺ يقوم إذا سمع الصارخ[132] يعني الديك وهذا يكون السدس فما دونه
73:20.english: And as for the standing (in prayer) of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) in terms of quantity, it was not on a single arrangement, but perhaps he would stand half the night, or a third of it, or a sixth of it[131], differing in the nights, and indicated by the saying of the Exalted in the two places from Surah Al-Muzzammil: 'Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand (in prayer) less than two-thirds of the night, and half of it, and a third of it' {} So 'less than two-thirds of the night' is as if describing it and half of its sixth, for if his saying 'and half of it and a third of it' is broken, it was half of the two-thirds, approaching the third and the quarter, and if it is in the accusative case, it was half the night. And Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: 'He (peace be upon him) would stand when he heard the crier[132]' meaning the rooster, and this is the sixth or less of it.
73:20.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

73:20.arabic: وأردف بذكرها الصلاة التي هي أعلى الأعلام فقال تعالى: ﴿ وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة ﴾{البقرة: 83} وقال ﭬ: (بني الإسلام على خمس شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله وأن محمدا عبده ورسوله وإقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة[1]) وشدد الوعيد على المقصرين فيها فقال: ﴿ والذين يكنزون الذهب والفضة ولا ينفقونها في سبيل الله فبشرهم بعذاب أليم ﴾{التوبة: 34} ومعنى الإنفاق في سبيل الله إخراج حق الزكاة
73:20.english: And He followed its mention with the Prayer (Salah) which is the highest of the signs, so He the Exalted said: 'And establish the Prayer (Salah) and give the Zakat (Zakah)' {Al-Baqarah: 83}. And He ﭬ said: 'Islam is built upon five: the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His slave and messenger, and establishing the Prayer (Salah), and giving the Zakat (Zakah)[1]'. And He intensified the threat against those who are negligent in it, so He said: 'And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah, then give them tidings of a painful punishment' {At-Tawbah: 34}. And the meaning of spending in the way of Allah is the extraction of the right of Zakat (Zakah).
73:20.topic: Al-Ghazali on the outer and inner dimensions of worship, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

73:20.arabic: وقال تعالى وآخرون يضربون في الأرض يبتغون من فضل الله وقال تعالى فانتشروا في الأرض وابتغوا من فضل الله
73:20.english: And He (Exalted is He) said: 'And others travel through the earth seeking from the bounty of Allah.' And He (Exalted is He) said: 'And disperse through the earth and seek from the bounty of Allah.'
73:20.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Etiquette of Earning'

74:8.arabic: وروى أن زرارة بن أوفى لما انتهى إلى قوله تعالى: ﴿ فإذا نقر في الناقور ﴾ {} خر ميتا. وكان إبراهيم النخعي إذا سمع قوله تعالى ﴿ إذا السماء انشقت ﴾ {} اضطرب حتى تضطرب أوصاله. وقال عبد الله بن واقد: رأيت ابن عمر يصلي مغلوبا عليه. وحق له أن يحترق قلبه بوعد سيده ووعيده فإنه عبد مذنب ذليل بين يدي جبار قاهر وتكون هذه المعاني بحسب درجات الفهم ويكون الفهم بحسب وفور العلم وصفاء القلب ودرجات ذلك لا تنحصر والصلاة مفتاح القلوب فيها تنكشف أسرار الكلمات فهذا حق القراءة وهو حق الأذكار والتسبيحات أيضا ثم يراعى اله
74:8.english: And it is narrated that when Zurarah bin Awfa reached the saying of Allah the Exalted: 'So when the Trumpet (An-Naqur) is blown (Naqira)' (Quran 74:8), he fell dead. And Ibrahim An-Nakha'i, when he heard the saying of Allah the Exalted 'When the sky is split asunder' (Quran 84:1), would tremble until his limbs trembled. And Abdullah bin Waqid said: I saw Ibn Umar praying overwhelmed. And it is right for him that his Heart (Qalb) burns with the promise of his Master and His threat, for he is a sinful servant, humble before a Compelling, Overpowering One. And these meanings are according to the degrees of understanding, and understanding is according to the abundance of knowledge and the purity of the Heart (Qalb), and the degrees of that are not limited. And prayer is the key to the Hearts (Qulub); in it the secrets of the words are unveiled. This is the right of recitation, and it is also the right of the Remembrances (Adhkar) and Glorifications (Tasbihat). Then awe is observed in the recitation, so he recites slowly and deliberately, not rapidly, for that is easier for contemplation, and he differentiates between its tones in the verse of mercy and punishment, promise and threat, praise, magnification, and exaltation.
74:8.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

74:8.arabic: فلو لم يكن بين يدي الموتي إلا هول تلك النفخة لكان ذلك جديرا بأن يتقى فإنها نفخة وصيحة يصعق بها من فى السموات والأرض يعنى يموتون بها إلا من شاء الله وهو بعض الملائكة ولذلك قال رسول الله ﭬ: (كيف أنعم وصاحب الصور قد التقم القرن وحنى الجبهة وأصغى بالأذن متى يؤمر فينفخ[144]) قال مقاتل: الصور هو القرن وذلك أن إسرافيل عليه السلام واضع فاه على القرن كهيئة البوق ودائرة رأس القرن كعرض السموات والأرض وهو شاخص بصره نحو العرش ينتظر متى يؤمر فينفخ النفخة الأولى فإذا نفخ صعق من فى السموات والأرض أى مات كل حيوا
74:8.english: If there were nothing before the dead except the terror of that blowing (of the Horn), it would be worthy of being feared, for it is a blowing and a cry by which those in the heavens and the earth are struck unconscious (صعق), meaning they die by it except whom Allah wills, and that is some of the angels. And for that reason, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'How can I enjoy comfort when the possessor of the Horn (الصور) has taken the Horn into his mouth, lowered his forehead, and inclined his ear, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow?' [144] Maqatil said: The Horn (الصور) is the trumpet (القرن), and that is because Israfil (upon him be peace) places his mouth on the Horn like the form of a trumpet, and the circumference of the head of the Horn is like the expanse of the heavens and the earth, and he is fixing his gaze toward the Throne (العرش), waiting for when he will be commanded to blow the first blowing.
