80:1.english: And Ibn Umm Maktum sought permission to enter upon the Prophet (peace be upon him) while there was with him a man from the nobles of Quraysh, and that became difficult upon the Prophet (peace be upon him), so Allah the Exalted revealed: "He frowned and turned away because the blind man came to him, and what would make you know that perhaps he might purify himself, or he might remember and the remembrance (Dhikr) benefit him" meaning Ibn Maktum "But as for he who considers himself self-sufficient, to him you give attention" meaning this nobleman.
80:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

80:8.arabic: وقد عاتب الله نبيه ﭬ في الإعراض عن عبد والإقبال على عبد، وهما في العبودية سيان ولكن في الحال مختلفان، فقال: " وأما من جاءك يسعى وهو يخشى فأنت عنده تلهى "، وقال في الآخر: " أما من استغنى فأنت له تصدى "
80:8.english: And Allah reproached His Prophet (peace be upon him) for turning away from one servant and turning toward another servant, and they are equal in servitude (ʿubūdiyyah) but different in state (ḥāl). So He said: "And as for the one who comes to you striving (yasʿā) while he fears (yakhshā), you are distracted from him." And He said regarding the other: "As for the one who is self-sufficient, you attend to him."
80:8.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

80:17.arabic: وذكر أنك مخلوق من نطفة قذرة فقال قتل الإنسان ما أكفره من أي شئ خلقه من نطفة خلقه فقدره ثم السبيل يسره ثم أماته فأقبره ثم إذا شاء أنشره
80:17.english: And He mentioned that you are created from a filthy drop (Nutfah), so He said: 'Killed is the human (Al-Insan) - what makes him reject faith (Kafara)? From what thing He created him? From a drop (Nutfah) He created him, then proportioned him. Then He made the way easy for him. Then He caused him to die and buried him. Then when He wills, He will resurrect him.'
80:17.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Contemplation'

80:19.arabic: فمن آياته الانسان المخلوق من النطفة وأقرب شيء إليك نفسك وفيك من العجائب الدالة على عظمة الله تعالى ما تنقضي الأعمار في الوقوف على عشر عشيره وأنت غافل عنه فيامن هو غافل عن نفسه وجاهل بها كيف تطمع في معرفة غيرك وقد أمرك الله تعالى بالتدبر في نفسك في كتابه العزيز فقال وفي أنفسكم أفلا تبصرون وذكر أنك مخلوق من نطفة قذرة فقال قتل الإنسان ما أكفره من أي شئ خلقه من نطفة خلقه فقدره ثم السبيل يسره ثم أماته فأقبره ثم إذا شاء أنشره
80:19.english: From His signs is the human being created from the sperm-drop (Nutfah), and the closest thing to you is your own self, and within you are wonders indicating the majesty of Allah the Exalted that lifetimes would end in standing upon a tenth of its tenth while you are heedless of it. So, O one who is heedless of his own self and ignorant of it, how do you aspire to know others when Allah the Exalted has commanded you to contemplate in your self in His Noble Book, saying: 'And in your selves, will you not then see?' And He mentioned that you are created from a filthy sperm-drop (Nutfah Qadhirah), saying: 'Cursed is man; how disbelieving he is! From what thing did He create him? From a sperm-drop (Nutfah) He created him, then proportioned him (Faqaddarahu). Then He made the way easy for him. Then He caused him to die and buried him. Then when He wills, He will resurrect him.'
80:19.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Contemplation'

80:21.arabic: وأما آخره ومورده فهو الموت المشار إليه بقول تعالى "ثم أماته فأقبره ثم إذا شاء أنشره" ومعناه أنه يسلب روحه وسمعه وبصره وعلمه وقدرته وحسه وإدراكه وحركته، فيعود جماداً كما كان أول مرة، لا يبقى إلا شكل أعضائه وصورته لا حس فيه ولا حركة، ثم يوضع في التراب فيصير جيفة منتنة قذرة كما كان في الأول نطفة مذرة، ثم تبلى أعضاؤه وتتفتت أجزاؤه وتنخر عظامه ويصير رميماً رفاتاً، ويأكل الدود أجزاءه فيبتدئ بحدقتيه فيقلعهما وبخديه فيقطعهما، وبسائر أجزائه فيصير روثاً في أجواف الديدان ويكون جيفة يهرب منه الحيوان ويستقذر
80:21.english: And as for its end and destination, it is death, indicated by the saying of the Exalted: "Then He causes him to die and buries him, then when He wills, He resurrects him." And its meaning is that He strips him of his Spirit (Ruh), his hearing, his sight, his knowledge, his power, his sensation, his perception, and his movement, so he returns to being inanimate matter as he was the first time. Nothing remains except the form of his limbs and his image, with no sensation in it nor movement. Then he is placed in the earth and becomes a stinking, filthy corpse, just as he was in the beginning a despised drop of fluid. Then his limbs decay, his parts disintegrate, his bones become hollow, and he becomes scattered remains and fragments. And the worms eat his parts, beginning with his pupils, plucking them out, and his cheeks, cutting them off, and with all his other parts, until he becomes dung in the bellies of the worms and becomes a corpse from which animals flee and which every human finds repulsive and flees from due to the intensity of the stench. And the best of his states is that he returns to what he was and becomes earth from which cups are made and from which buildings are constructed, so he becomes non-existent after having been existent. And it is as if he had not been reaped yesterday, just as he was in his first state a long duration. And would that he remained thus, how excellent it would be if he were left as earth. No, rather He revives him after a long decay to experience severe torment. He emerges from his grave after the gathering of his scattered parts, and he emerges to the terrors of the Resurrection, and he sees a standing Resurrection and a sky split and torn, and an earth changed, and mountains set in motion, and stars falling, and a sun eclipsed, and dark conditions, and harsh, severe angels, and Hellfire blazing, and a Paradise which the criminal looks upon and regrets, and he sees the records.
80:21.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

80:22.arabic: فينقطع قلبه فزعاً من هول هذا الخطاب قبل أن تنتشر الصحيفة ويشاهد ما فيها من مخازيه، فإذا شاهده قال "يا ويلتنا ما لهذا الكتاب لا يغادر صغيرة ولا كبيرة إلا أحصاها" فهذا آخر أمره وهو معنى قوله تعالى "ثم إذا شاء أنشره" فما لمن هذا حاله والتكبر والتعظم؟ بل ما له وللفرح في لحظة واحدة فضلاً عن البطر والأشر؟ فقد ظهره له أول حاله ووسطه ولو ظهر آخره والعياذ بالله تعالى ربما اختار أن يكون كلباً أو خنزيراً ليصير مع البهائم تراباً ولا يكون إنساناً يسمع خطاباً أو يلقى عذاباً، وإن كان عند الله مستحقاً للنار فال
80:22.english: His heart (Qalb) is severed in terror from the horror of this address before the record is spread open and he witnesses what is in it of his disgraceful acts. When he witnesses it, he says, "Woe to us! What is with this book that does not leave out small or great except that it has enumerated it?" This is the end of his affair, and it is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted, "Then when He wills, He will resurrect him." So what is for one in this state and arrogance and self-aggrandizement? Rather, what is for him and joy in a single moment, let alone insolence and extravagance? Indeed, his first state and middle have become apparent to him, and if his end were to appear—and refuge is sought with Allah, the Exalted—perhaps he would choose to be a dog or a pig to become with the animals as dust and not be a human who hears an address or meets punishment. And if he is with Allah deserving of the Fire, then the pig is more noble than him and more pleasant and higher, since its beginning is dust and its end is dust, and it is removed from the accounting and the punishment. And the dog and the pig, the creation does not flee from them.
80:22.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

80:22.arabic: أفتكذبينه في قوله ثم إذا شاء أنشرك فإن لم تكونى مكذبة فما لك لا تأخذين حذرك ولو أن يهوديا أخبرك في ألذ أطعمتك بأنه يضرك في مرضك لصبرت عنه وتركته وجاهدت نفسك فيه
80:22.english: Do you then disbelieve Him in His saying: 'Then when He wills, He will resurrect you'? If you are not a disbeliever, then why do you not take your precaution? Even if a Jew informed you about your most delicious food that it would harm you in your illness, you would endure from it and leave it and struggle against your Soul (Nafs) in it.
80:22.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

80:24.arabic: ولسنا نطنب في ذكر آلات النبات في اجتذاب الغذاء إلى نفسه ولكن نشير إلى غذائه. فنقول: كما أن الخشب والتراب لا يغذيك بل تحتاج إلى طعام مخصوص فكذلك الحبة لا تغتذى بكل شىء بل تحتاج إلى شىء مخصوص بدليل أنك لو تركتها في البيت لم تزد لأنه ليس يحيط بها إلا هواء ومجرد الهواء لا يصلح لغذائها ولو تركنها في الماء لم تزد ولو تركنها في أرض لا ماء فيها لم تزد بل لا بد من أرض فيها ماء يمتزج ماؤها بالأرض فيصير طينا وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى: ﴿ فلينظر الإنسان إلى طعامه أنا صببنا الماء صبا ثم شققنا الأرض شقا فأنبتن
80:24.english: And we do not elaborate on mentioning the instruments of the plant in attracting nourishment to itself, but we point to its nourishment. So we say: Just as wood and soil do not nourish you, rather you need specific food, likewise the grain does not nourish itself with everything, rather it needs something specific, as evidence that if you leave it in the house, it does not increase because nothing surrounds it except air, and mere air is not suitable for its nourishment; and if you leave it in water, it does not increase; and if you leave it in land with no water in it, it does not increase. Rather, it must be in land with water that mixes its water with the land, becoming mud. And to this is the allusion in His saying, the Exalted: 'Then let man look at his food: We poured down water in abundance, then We split the earth in fissures, and caused to grow therein grain, and grapes and fresh vegetation, and olives and date-palms' (Quran 80:24-29). Then water and soil are not sufficient, for if it is left in damp, solid, compacted land, it does not sprout due to lack of air, so it needs to be placed in loose, porous land where air penetrates to it. Then air does not move to it by itself, so it needs a wind that moves the air and strikes it with force and violence upon the land until it penetrates into it. And to this is the allusion in His saying, the Exalted: 'And We send the winds fertilizing' (Quran 15:22). And its fertilization is in effecting the coupling between air, water, and land. Then all of that does not benefit you if it is in excessive cold and harsh winter, so you need the heat of spring and summer. Thus, the need of its nourishment for these four has become clear. So look at what each one needs: water needs to flow to the land of cultivation from seas, springs, rivers, and canals. So look how Allah created the seas, gushed forth the springs, and made rivers flow from them. Then the land may be elevated, and waters do not rise to it, so look how Allah, the Exalted, created the clouds and how He subjected the winds to them to drive them by His permission to the regions of the earth, and they are heavy clouds bearing water. Then look how He sends it pouring down upon the lands in the time of spring and autumn according to the need. And look how He created the mountains as preservers of waters, from which springs gush forth gradually; if they came out all at once, they would flood.
80:24.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

80:24.arabic: وقال الحسن: قد رأيتهم يطيبونه بالأفاويه والطيب ثم يرمون به حيث رأيتم وقد قال الله عز وجل "فلينظر الإنسان إلى طعامه" قال ابن عباس إلى رجيعه وقال رجل لابن عمر إني أريد أن أسألك وأستحي قال فلا تستحي واسأل قال إذا قضى أحدنا حاجته فقام ينظر إلى ذلك منه قال نعم إن الملك يقول له انظر إلى ما بخلت به انظر إلى ماذا صار. وكان بشر بن كعب يقول انطلقوا حتى أريكم الدنيا فيذهب بهم إلى مزبلة فيقول انظروا إلى ثمارهم ودجاجهم وعسلهم وسمنهم.
80:24.english: And Al-Hasan said: I have seen them perfume it with spices and fragrance, then they throw it where you have seen. And Allah the Exalted has said: "Let the human being (Al-Insan) look at his food (Ta'am)." Ibn Abbas said: To its excrement. And a man said to Ibn Umar: I want to ask you, but I am ashamed. He said: Do not be ashamed, and ask. He said: When one of us relieves himself, then stands looking at that from it? He said: Yes, indeed the angel says to him: Look at what you were stingy with, look at what it has become. And Bishr ibn Ka'b used to say: Come, so that I may show you the world (Al-Dunya). And he would take them to a garbage dump and say: Look at their fruits, their chickens, their honey, and their clarified butter.
80:24.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of the World'

80:25.arabic: وقد انطوى القرآن على جملة من الحكم الجليلة التي تحتملها افهام الخلق دون الدقيق الذي يقصرون عن فهمه اذ قال تعالى: ﴿ أنا صببنا الماء صبا ثم شققنا الارض شقا فأنبتنا فيها حبا وعنبا ﴾ {} الآية. وأما الحكمة في سائر الكواكب السيارة منها والثوابت فخفية لا يطلع عليها كافة الخلق والقدر الذي يحتمله فهم الخلق انها زينة للسماء لتستلذ العين بالنظر اليها وأشار اليه قوله تعالى: ﴿ إنا زينا السماء الدنيا بزينة الكواكب ﴾ {} فجميع اجزاء العالم سماؤه وكواكبه ورياحه وبحاره وجباله ومعادنه ونباته وحيواناته وأعظاء حيوان
80:25.english: And the Quran encompasses a collection of manifest wisdoms that the understandings of creation can bear, unlike the subtle ones they fall short of comprehending, as He, the Exalted, said: 'Indeed, We poured down the water (Al-Ma') in a pouring (Sabb), then We split the earth (Al-Ard) in a splitting (Shaqq), and We caused to grow therein grain and grapes' (the verse). As for the wisdom in the rest of the moving and fixed stars, it is hidden, not accessible to all of creation, and the extent that the understanding of creation can bear is that they are an adornment for the sky so that the eye may delight in looking at them, and He alluded to this in His saying: 'Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with an adornment of stars' (the verse). So all parts of the world—its sky, stars, winds, seas, mountains, minerals, plants, animals, and the limbs of animals—not a single atom of its atoms is devoid of many wisdoms, from one wisdom to ten, to a thousand, to ten thousand. Likewise, the limbs of animals are divided except for what is known of their wisdom, such as knowing that the eye is for sight (Al-Ibsar) not for striking, the hand is for striking not for walking, and the leg is for walking not for smelling. As for the internal organs like the intestines, gallbladder, liver, kidney, and individual veins, nerves, muscles, and what they contain of cavities, convolutions, intertwinings, deviations, fineness, thickness, and other attributes, most people do not know the wisdom in them, and those who know them know only a small amount in comparison to what is in the knowledge of God, the Exalted: 'And you have not been given of knowledge except a little' (the verse).
80:25.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

80:26.arabic: ولأجل توافق ذلك وتطابقه نسب الله تعالى الأفعال في القرآن مرة إلى الملائكة ومرة إلى العباد، ونسبها بعينها مرة أخرى إلى نفسه، فقال الله تعالى في الموت " قل يتوفاكم ملك الموت " ثم قال عز وجل: " الله يتوفى الأنفس حين موتها " وقال تعالى: " أفرأيتم ما تحرثون " أضاف إلينا ثم قال تعالى: " أنا صببنا ثم شققنا الأرض شقاً فأنبتنا فيها حباً وعنباً "، وقال عز وجل: " فأرسلنا إليها روحنا فتمثل لها بشراً سوياً "، ثم قال تعالى: " فنفخنا فيها من روحنا " وكان النافخ جبريل عليه السلام، وكما قال تعالى: " فإذا قرأناه
80:26.english: And due to the correspondence and congruence of that, Allah the Exalted attributed actions in the Quran once to the angels and once to the servants, and attributed them in their very essence once again to Himself. So Allah the Exalted said regarding death: 'Say: The Angel of Death will take your souls,' then He the Glorified and Exalted said: 'Allah takes the souls at the time of their death.' And He the Exalted said: 'Have you considered what you sow?' He attributed it to us, then He the Exalted said: 'We poured down water, then We split the earth splitting, and We caused to grow therein grain and grapes.' And He the Glorified and Exalted said: 'So We sent to her Our Spirit, and he represented himself to her as a well-proportioned man.' Then He the Exalted said: 'So We breathed into her from Our Spirit,' and the breather was Gabriel, peace be upon him. And as He the Exalted said: 'So when We have recited it, then follow its recitation,' it is said in the interpretation: its meaning is when Gabriel recites it to you.
80:26.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

80:34.arabic: ويوم لا يجزى والد عن ولده ويوم يفر المرء من أخيه وأمه وأبيه ويوم لا ينطقون ولا يؤذن لهم فيعتذرون يوم لا مرد له من الله يوم هم بارزون ويوم هم على النار يفتنون يوم لا ينفع مال ولا بنون يوم لا ينفع الظالمين معذرتهم ولهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار يوم ترد فيه المعاذير وتبلى السرائر وتظهر الضمائر وتكشف الأستار يوم تخشع فيه الأبصار وتسكن الأصوات ويقل فيه الالتفات وتبرز الخفيات وتظهر الخطيئات يوم يساق العباد ومعهم الأشهاد ويشيب الصغير ويسكر الكبير فيومئذ وضعت الموازين ونشرت الدواوين وبرزت الجحيم وأغلى الحمي
80:34.english: And the day when a parent will not avail their child, and the day when a person (Al-Mar') flees from their brother (Akhih) and their mother and their father, and the day when they will not speak nor be permitted to offer excuses; a day when there is no repelling from Allah; a day when they are exposed; and a day when they are tested over the Fire; a day when wealth and children will not benefit; a day when the excuses of the wrongdoers will not benefit them, and for them is the curse and for them is the evil abode; a day when excuses are returned, secrets are tested, consciences are revealed, and veils are uncovered; a day when gazes are humbled, voices are silenced, turning away is reduced, hidden things are exposed, and sins are made apparent; a day when the servants are driven with their witnesses, the young turn gray, and the old become intoxicated; then on that day the scales are set up, the records are spread out, Hell is made manifest, the boiling water is heated, the Fire blazes, the disbelievers despair, the fires are kindled, colors change, the tongue is silenced, and the limbs of the human being speak. O human being, what has deluded you concerning your Generous Lord, when the doors are closed, the curtains are lowered, and you are concealed from the creatures, yet you commit immorality? So what will you do when your limbs bear witness against you? So woe, all woe to us, the heedless ones. Allah sends to us the master of the messengers and reveals to him the Clear Book, and He informs us of these attributes from the descriptions of the Day of Reckoning (Yawm Al-Din), then He makes us aware of our heedlessness and says: 'The reckoning of the people has drawn near, while they are in heedlessness turning away. No new reminder comes to them from their Lord except that they listen to it while they are playing, their hearts (Qulub) distracted.' Then He makes us aware of the nearness of the Hour and says: 'The Hour has drawn near...'
80:34.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

80:34.arabic: ومن ظن أنه ينجو بتقوى أبيه كمن ظن أنه يشبع بأكل أبيه ويروى بشرب أبيه، ويصير عالماً بتعلم أبيه ويصل إلى الكعبة ويراها بمشي أبيه. فالتقوى فرض عين فلا يجزه فيه والد عن ولده شيئاً وكذا العكس، وعند الله جزاء التقوى "يوم يفر المرء من أخيه وأمه وأبيه" إلا على سبيل الشفاعة لمن لم يشتد غضب الله عليه فيأذن في الشفاعة له - كما سبق في كتاب الكبر والعجب.
80:34.english: And whoever thinks that he will be saved by the piety (تقوى) of his father is like one who thinks that he will be satiated by the eating of his father and quenched by the drinking of his father, and becomes knowledgeable by the learning of his father and reaches the Kaaba and sees it by the walking of his father. So piety (تقوى) is an individual obligation (فرض عين) - nothing of it suffices for a parent regarding his child, and likewise the opposite - and with Allah is the reward of piety (تقوى): 'The Day when a person will flee from his brother, and his mother, and his father' except by way of intercession (الشفاعة) for one upon whom the anger of Allah has not intensified, so He permits intercession (الشفاعة) for him - as preceded in the Book of Arrogance and Vanity.
80:34.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

80:34.arabic: ثم كيف يعجب بهم وأنهم سيفترقون عنه إذا مات فيدفن في قبره ذليلاً معيناً وحده لا يرافقه أهل ولا ولد ولا قريب ولا حميم ولا عشير، فيسلمونه إلى البلى والحيات والعقارب والديدان ولا يغنون عنه شيئاً وفي أحوج أوقاته إليهم، وكذلك يهربون منه يوم القيامة "يوم يفر المرء من أخيه وأمه وأبيه وصاحبته وبنيه" الآية. فأي خير فيمن يفارقك في أشد أحوالك ويهرب منك؟ وكيف تعجب به ولا ينفعك في القبر والقيامة وعلى الصراط إلى عملك وفضل الله تعالى؟ فكيف تتكل على من لا ينفعك، وتنسى نعم من يملك نفعك وضرك وموتك وحياتك.
80:34.english: Then how can he be amazed by them when they will separate from him when he dies, and he will be buried in his grave humiliated, alone, with no family, child, relative, intimate friend, or tribesman accompanying him; they will surrender him to decay, snakes, scorpions, and worms, and they will not avail him anything at the time he needs them most. Likewise, they will flee from him on the Day of Resurrection (Yawm al-Qiyāmah): "The day when a person flees from his brother, his mother, his father, his companion, and his sons" (the verse). So what good is there in those who leave you in your most severe states and flee from you? And how can you be amazed by them when they do not benefit you in the grave, the Resurrection (al-Qiyāmah), and on the Bridge (al-Ṣirāṭ) regarding your deeds and the favor of Allah the Exalted? So how can you rely on those who do not benefit you, and forget the blessings of the One who possesses your benefit, harm, death, and life?
80:34.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

81:12.arabic: وفي سورة التكوير أهوال يوم القيامة وانكشاف الخاتمة وهو قوله تعالى: ﴿ وإذا الجحيم سعرت وإذا الجنة أزلفت علمت نفس ما أحضرت ﴾ {} وفي عم يتساءلون ﴿ يوم ينظر المرء ما قدمت يداه ﴾ {} الآية، وقوله تعالى: ﴿ لا يتكلمون إلا من أذن له الرحمن وقال صوابا ﴾ {} والقرآن من أوله إلى آخره مخاوف لمن قرأه بتدبر
81:12.english: And in Surah At-Takwir (The Folding Up), the terrors of the Day of Resurrection and the unveiling of the final outcome, and that is His saying, the Exalted: 'And when the Hellfire (Al-Jahim) is kindled (su'irat), and when Paradise is brought near, a soul (Nafs) will know what it has prepared.' And in 'Amma Yatasa'alun (Surah An-Naba'), 'The Day when a person will see what his hands have sent forth' - the verse, and His saying, the Exalted: 'They will not speak except whom the Most Merciful (Ar-Rahman) has permitted and says what is correct.' And the Quran from its beginning to its end is fears for whoever reads it with contemplation.
81:12.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Fear and Hope'

81:15.arabic: ثم انظر كيف عظم الله أمر السموات والنجوم فى كتابه فما من سورة إلا وتشتمل على تفخيمها فى مواضع وكم من قسم فى القرآن بها كقوله تعالى والسماء ذات البروج والسماء والطارق والسماء ذات الحبك والسماء وما بناها وكقوله تعالى والشمس وضحاها والقمر إذا تلاها وكقوله تعالى فلا أقسم بالخنس الجوار الكنس وقوله تعالى والنجم إذا هوى فلا أقسم بمواقع النجوم وإنه لقسم لو تعلمون عظيم فقد علمت أن عجائب النطفة القذرة عجز عن معرفتها الأولون والآخرون وما أقسم الله بها فما ظنك بما اقسم الله تعالى به وأحال الأرزاق عليه وأضاف
81:15.english: Then look at how Allah has magnified the matter of the heavens and the stars in His Book, for there is no surah except that it contains their glorification in places, and how many oaths in the Quran are by them, such as His saying, the Exalted: 'And by the heaven with its constellations' (85:1), and 'And by the heaven and the night-comer' (86:1), and 'And by the heaven with its paths' (51:7), and 'And by the heaven and He who built it' (91:5), and His saying, the Exalted: 'By the sun and its brightness' (91:1), and 'And by the moon when it follows it' (91:2), and His saying, the Exalted: 'So I swear by the receding ones (al-Khunnas), the moving ones (al-Jawār), the hiding ones (al-Kunnas)' (81:15-16), and His saying: 'And by the star when it sets' (53:1), 'So I swear by the positions of the stars' (56:75), 'And indeed, it is an oath, if you only knew, great' (56:76). You have known that the wonders of the filthy drop (an-Nutfa) have baffled the knowledge of the former and the latter, and Allah did not swear by it, so what do you think of that by which Allah, the Exalted, has sworn and referred the provisions (al-Arzāq) to it and attributed them to it, saying, the Exalted: 'And in the heaven is your provision (Rizq) and what you are promised' (51:22), and He praised those who contemplate (al-Mufakkirīn) in it, saying: 'And they contemplate (Yatafakkarūn) in the creation of the heavens and the earth' (3:191).
81:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Contemplation'

81:29.arabic: إذن الأمر أمر الله والقضاء قضاؤه وعصمه الله من كل ما تخوفت عليه من أمر الدنيا والدين
81:29.english: Then the matter is Allah's matter and the decree is His decree, and Allah protected him from everything I feared for him regarding worldly and religious affairs.
81:29.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Book of Repentance'

82:6.arabic: يوم يساق العباد ومعهم الأشهاد ويشيب الصغير ويسكر الكبير فيومئذ وضعت الموازين ونشرت الدواوين وبرزت الجحيم وأغلى الحميم وزفرت النار ويئس الكفار وسعرت النيران وتغيرت الألوان وخرس اللسان ونطقت جوارح الإنسان فيا أيها الإنسان ما غرك بربك الكريم حيث أغلقت الأبواب وأرخيت الستور واستترت عن الخلائق فقارفت الفجور فماذا تفعل وقد شهدت عليك جوارحك فالويل كل الويل لنا معشر الغافلين
82:6.english: The day when the servants (of Allah) are driven forth, and with them are the witnesses, and the young turn gray-haired and the old become intoxicated. Then on that day, the scales are set up, the records are spread open, Hellfire is made manifest, the boiling water is heated, the Fire blazes forth, the disbelievers despair, the fires are kindled, the colors change, the tongue falls silent, and the limbs of the human being speak. 'O human being! What has deluded you concerning your Generous Lord (Rabbika al-Karim)?' For the doors have been closed, the curtains have been lowered, and you have concealed yourself from the creatures, yet you committed immorality. So what will you do when your limbs bear witness against you? Then woe upon woe to us, the heedless ones.
82:6.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Book of Repentance'

82:10.arabic: قال عطاء بن أبي رباح: إن من كان قبلكم كانوا يكرهون فضول الكلام وكانوا يعدون فضول الكلام ما عدا كتاب الله تعالى وسنة رسول الله ﭬ، أو أمراً بمعروف أو نهياً عن منكر، أو أن تنطق بحاجتك في معيشتك التي لا بد لك منها، أتنكرون أن عليكم حافظين كراماً كاتبين عن اليمين وعن الشمال قعيد ما يلفظ من قول إلا لديه رقيب عتيد، أما يستحي أحدكم إذا نشرت صحيفته التي أملاها صدر نهاره كان أكثر ما فيها ليس من أمر دينه ولا دنياه.
82:10.english: Ata ibn Abi Rabah said: Those who came before you used to hate superfluous speech, and they considered superfluous speech to be anything except the Book of Allah the Exalted and the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), or commanding good or forbidding evil, or speaking of your need in your livelihood which is indispensable for you. Do you deny that upon you are noble guardians (Hafizin) writing from the right and from the left seated? Not a word is uttered except that with him is a ready observer. Does not one of you feel ashamed when his record is spread out which he dictated at the beginning of his day, and most of what is in it is not from the matter of his religion nor his worldly life?
82:10.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

82:13.arabic: فهذه علامات المحبة، فمن تمت فيه هذه العلامات فقد تمت محبته وخلص حبه فصفا في الآخرة شرابه وعذب مشربه، ومن امتزج بحبه حب غير الله تنعم في الآخرة بقدر حبه، إذ يمزج شرابه بقدر من شراب المقربين كما قال تعالى في الأبرار: "إن الأبرار لفي نعيم" ثم قال: "يسقون من رحيق مختوم مسك وفي ذلك فليتنافس المتنافسون ومزاجه من تسنيم عيناً يشرب بها المقربون" فإذا طاب شراب الأبرار لشوب الشراب الصرف الذي هو للمقربين. والشراب عبارة عن جملة نعيم الجنان، كما أن الكتاب عبر به عن جميع الأعمال فقال: "إن كتاب الأبرار لفي عليي
82:13.english: These are the signs of love (Mahabbah), so whoever has these signs completed in him, then his love has been completed and his love has been purified, so his drink (Sharab) in the Hereafter becomes pure and his drinking place sweet. And whoever mixes with his love love for other than Allah, he enjoys in the Hereafter according to his love, since his drink is mixed with a measure of the drink of the Close Ones (Muqarrabun) as Allah the Exalted said regarding the Righteous (Al-Abrar): 'Indeed the Righteous (Al-Abrar) are in Bliss (Na'im)' then He said: 'They are given to drink of a sealed pure wine (Rahiq), its seal is musk - and for this let the competitors compete - and its mixture is of Tasnim, a spring from which drink those brought near (Muqarrabun).' So if the drink of the Righteous (Al-Abrar) becomes pleasant due to the mixing of the pure drink which is for the Close Ones (Muqarrabun). And the drink (Sharab) is an expression for the totality of the bliss (Na'im) of Paradise (Jinan), just as the Book (Kitab) expressed by it all the deeds, so He said: 'Indeed the record of the Righteous (Al-Abrar) is in Illiyyun' then He said: 'Witnessed by those brought near (Muqarrabun)' so it was a sign of the cause of their record that it rose to where it is witnessed by the Close Ones (Muqarrabun). And just as the Righteous (Al-Abrar) find increase in their state and their knowledge by their closeness to the Close Ones (Muqarrabun) and their witnessing of them, so will be their state in the Hereafter: 'He did not create you nor resurrect you except as a single soul (Nafs), as We began the first creation, We will repeat it' and as Allah the Exalted said: 'A recompense in proportion' meaning the recompense corresponded to their deeds, so the pure was met with the pure from the drink and the mixed was met with the mixed, and the mixing of every drink is according to what preceded of mixing in his love and his deeds: 'So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it - and indeed Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves - Indeed Allah does not do injustice to the weight of an atom, and if it is a good deed He multiplies it - and if it is the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth, and sufficient are We as accountants.' So whoever his love in the world is his hope for the bliss (Na'im) of Paradise (Jannah) and the Houris (Hur al-'Ayn).
82:13.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

82:13.arabic: قال أبو حازم اعرض نفسك على كتاب الله تعالى حيث قال إن الأبرار لفي نعيم وان الفجار لفي جحيم قال فأين رحمة الله قال قريب من المحسنين
82:13.english: Abu Hazim said: Present yourself to the Book of Allah (the Quran) where He said: 'Indeed the Righteous (Al-Abrar) are in Bliss (Na'im)' and 'Indeed the Wicked (Al-Fujjar) are in Blazing Fire (Jahim).' He (Sulayman) said: Then where is the Mercy (Rahmah) of Allah? He said: Close to the Doers of Good (Al-Muhsinin).
82:13.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

82:13.arabic: فإن كان قد يسر لك سبيل الخير فأبشر فإنك مبعد عن النار وإن كنت لا تقصد خيرا إلا وتحيط بك العوائق فتدفعه ولا تقصد شرا إلا ويتيسر لك أسبابه فاعلم أنك مقضى عليك فإن دلالة هذا على العاقبة كدلالة المطر على النبات ودلالة الدخان على النار فقد قال الله تعالى: ﴿ إن الأبرار لفى نعيم وإن الفجار لفى جحيم ﴾ {} فاعرض نفسك على الآيتين وقد عرفت مستقرك من الدارين والله أعلم.
82:13.english: If the path of good has been made easy for you, then rejoice, for you are kept far from the Fire. And if you do not intend good except that obstacles surround you and repel it, and you do not intend evil except that its causes are made easy for you, then know that you are decreed against. For the indication of this upon the outcome is like the indication of rain upon vegetation and the indication of smoke upon fire. Indeed, Allah the Exalted has said: 'Indeed, the Righteous (Al-Abrar) are in Bliss (Na'eem), and indeed, the Wicked (Al-Fujjar) are in Blazing Fire (Jahim).' So present yourself upon the two verses, and you have known your abode from the two abodes. And Allah knows best.
82:13.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

82:13.arabic: خلق الجنة وخلق لها أهلا فاستعملهم بالطاعة وخلق النار وخلق لها أهلا فاستعمله بالمعاصي وعرف الخلق علامة أهل الجنة وأهل النار فقال إن الأبرار لفي نعيم وإن الفجار لفي جحيم ثم قال تعالى فيما روى عن نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم هؤلاء في الجنة ولا أبالي وهؤلاء في النار ولا أبالي
82:13.english: He created Paradise and created for it people, so He employed them with obedience, and He created Hell and created for it people, so He employed them with disobedience. And He made known to the creation the sign of the people of Paradise and the people of Hell, so He said: 'Indeed, the righteous (Al-Abrar) are in bliss (Na'im), and indeed, the wicked (Al-Fujjar) are in a Blazing Fire (Jahim).' Then He, the Exalted, said in what is narrated from His Prophet (peace be upon him): 'These are in Paradise, and I do not care, and these are in Hell, and I do not care.'
82:13.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

82:19.arabic: يوم لا تجزى نفس عن نفس شيئا ويوم تشخص فيه الأبصار ويوم لا يغنى مولى عن مولى شيئا ويوم لا تملك نفس لنفس شيئا ويوم يدعون إلى نار جهنم دعا ويوم يسحبون فى النار على وجوههم ويوم تقلب وجوههم فى النار ويوم لا يجزى والد عن ولده ويوم يفر المرء من أخيه وأمه وأبيه ويوم لا ينطقون ولا يؤذن لهم فيعتذرون يوم لا مرد له من الله يوم هم بارزون ويوم هم على النار يفتنون يوم لا ينفع مال ولا بنون يوم لا ينفع الظالمين معذرتهم ولهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار يوم ترد فيه المعاذير وتبلى السرائر وتظهر الضمائر وتكشف الأستار يوم
82:19.english: A day when no soul (Nafs) will be recompensed for another soul (Nafs) anything, and a day when the eyes will stare, and a day when a protector (Mawlā) will not avail a protector (Mawlā) anything, and a day when no soul (Nafs) will possess for another soul (Nafs) anything, and a day when they will be called to the fire of Hell with a call, and a day when they will be dragged in the Fire on their faces, and a day when their faces will be turned over in the Fire, and a day when a parent will not be recompensed for his child, and a day when a man will flee from his brother and his mother and his father, and a day when they will not speak nor will they be permitted so they may apologize, a day when there is no repelling it from Allah, a day when they are exposed, and a day when they are over the Fire being tested, a day when wealth will not benefit nor children, a day when the excuses of the wrongdoers will not benefit them, and for them is the curse and for them is the evil abode, a day when the excuses will be returned and the secrets will be tested and the consciences will appear and the veils will be uncovered, a day when the eyes will be humbled and the voices will be stilled and the turning will be little in it and the hidden things will be exposed and the sins will appear, a day when the servants will be driven and with them the witnesses, and the young will turn gray and the old will be intoxicated, so on that day the scales will be set up and the records will be spread out and Hell will be made manifest and the boiling water will be heated and the Fire will roar and the disbelievers will despair and the fires will be kindled and the colors will change and the tongue will be silenced and the limbs of the human being will speak, so O human being, what has deluded you concerning your Lord (Rabb) the Generous, when the doors were closed and the curtains were lowered and you concealed yourself from the creatures so you committed immorality, so what will you do when your limbs have testified against you? So woe, all woe to us, the company of the heedless ones. Allah sends to us the master of the messengers and sends down upon him the clear Book and informs us with these attributes from the descriptions of the Day of Recompense (Yawm al-Dīn), then He makes us recognize our heedlessness and says: "Say..."
82:19.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

83:1.arabic: وويل له في نص كتاب الله تعالى حيث قال ويل للمطففين الذين إذا أكتالوا على الناس يستوفون وإذا كالوهم أو وزنوهم يخسرون وكل من يلتمس من الإنصاف اكثر مما تسمح به نفسه فهو داخل تحت مقتضى هذه الآية ومنشأ التقصير في ستر العورة أو السعي في كشفها الداء الدفين في الباطن وهو الحقد والحسن فإن الحقود الحسود يملأ باطنه بالخبث ولكن يحبسه في باطنه ويخفيه ولا يبديه مهما لم يجد له مجالا وإذا وجد فرصة انحلت الرابطة وارتفع الحياء ويترشح الباطن بخبثه الدفين ومهما انطوى الباطن على حقد وحسد فالانقطاع أولى
83:1.english: And woe to him in the explicit text of the Book of Allah (the Quran) where He said: 'Woe to the defrauders (Al-Mutaffifin) who, when they take by measure from people, take in full, but when they measure to them or weigh for them, they give less.' And everyone who seeks from justice more than what his soul (Nafs) permits is included under the implication of this verse. The origin of deficiency in covering faults (Satr Al-Awrah) or striving to uncover them is the hidden disease in the inner self (Al-Batin), which is rancor (Al-Hiqd) and envy (Al-Hasad). For the rancorous envier fills his inner self (Batin) with wickedness but restrains it within his inner self (Batin) and conceals it and does not manifest it as long as he does not find an opportunity for it. And when he finds an opportunity, the bond is dissolved and modesty (Al-Haya) is lifted, and the inner self (Al-Batin) seeps with its hidden wickedness. And whenever the inner self (Al-Batin) contains rancor and envy, then severance is preferable.
83:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Duties of Brotherhood'

83:1.arabic: وبالجملة كل من ينتصف لنفسه من غيره ولو في كلمة ولا ينصف بمثل ما ينتصف فهو داخل تحت قوله تعالى ويل للمطففين الذين إذا اكتالوا على الناس يستوفون الآيات فإن تحريم ذلك في المكيل ليس لكونه مكيلا بل لكونه أمرا مقصودا ترك العدل والنصفة فيه فهو جار في جميع الأعمال فصاحب الميزان في خطر الويل وكل مكلف فهو صاحب موازين في أفعاله وأقواله وخطراته فالويل له إن عدل عن العدل ومال عن الاستقامة ولولا تعذر هذا واستحالته لما ورد قوله تعالى وإن منكم إلا واردها كان على ربك حتما مقضيا فلا ينفك عبد ليس معصوما عن الميل ع
83:1.english: In summary, everyone who demands justice for himself from others, even in a single word, but does not give justice in the same measure as he demands, falls under His saying, exalted is He: 'Woe to the defrauders (Al-Mutaffifin) who, when they take measure from people, take in full.' For the prohibition of that in measuring is not because it is measuring, but because it is an intended matter of abandoning justice (Al-Adl) and fairness (An-Nisfah) in it, so it applies to all actions. The possessor of the scale is in danger of the woe, and every legally responsible person (Mukallaf) is a possessor of scales in his actions, his words, and his thoughts. So woe to him if he deviates from justice (Al-Adl) and inclines away from uprightness (Al-Istiqamah). Were it not for the difficulty and impossibility of this, His saying, exalted is He, would not have come: 'And there is none of you except he will come to it; it is upon your Lord a decree determined.' So no servant (Abd) who is not infallible (Ma'sum) is free from inclination away from uprightness (Al-Istiqamah), except that the degrees of inclination vary with great variation. Therefore, the duration of their stay in the Fire varies until the time of deliverance, so that some of them remain only for the duration of fulfilling the oath, and some of them remain for a thousand and thousands of years. So we ask Allah, exalted is He, to bring us closer to uprightness (Al-Istiqamah) and justice (Al-Adl), for strict adherence to the path of the straight (As-Sirat Al-Mustaqim) without deviation from it is not to be hoped for, for it is finer than a hair and sharper than a sword. Were it not for that, the one upright (Mustaqim) upon it would not be able to cross the bridge (As-Sirat) stretched over the surface of the Fire, whose attribute is that it is finer than a hair and sharper than a sword. And according to the uprightness (Al-Istiqamah) on this straight path (As-Sirat Al-Mustaqim), the servant (Abd) is lightened on the Day of Resurrection on the bridge (As-Sirat). And everyone who mixes dust or other with food then measures it, he is among the defrauders (Al-Mutaffifin) in measuring, and every butcher who weighs bone with meat when the custom...
83:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Etiquette of Earning'

83:1.arabic: الثالث إلا يكتم في المقدار شيئا وذلك بتعديل الميزان والاحتياط فيه وفي الكيل فينبغي أن يكيل كما يكتال قال الله تعالى ويل للمطففين الذين إذا اكتالوا على الناس يستوفون وإذا كالوهم أو وزنوهم يخسرون ولا يخلص من هذا إلا بأن يرجع إذا أعطي وينقص إذا أخذ إذ العدل الحقيقي قلما يتصور فليستظهر بظهور الزيادة والنقصان فإن من استقصى حقه بكماله يوشك أن يتعداه وكان بعضهم يقول لا أشتري الويل من الله بحبة فكان إذا أخذ نقص نصف حبة وإذا أعطى زاد حبة وكان يقول ويل لمن باع بحبة جنة عرضها السموات والأرض وما أخسر من باع
83:1.english: The third [principle] is not to conceal anything in the measure, and that is by adjusting the scale and being cautious in it and in measuring. One should measure as one would be measured. Allah the Exalted said: 'Woe to the defrauders (Al-Mutaffifin) who, when they take by measure from people, take in full, but when they measure to them or weigh to them, they give less.' And one is not free from this except by returning when given and decreasing when taking, since true justice (Al-Adl) is rarely conceivable. So let him seek evidence through the appearance of increase and decrease, for whoever exacts his right in its entirety is likely to transgress it. And some of them would say: 'I do not buy the Woe from Allah for a grain.' So when he would take, he would decrease half a grain, and when he would give, he would increase a grain. And he would say: 'Woe to him who sells for a grain a garden whose width is the heavens and the earth. And how great is the loss of him who sells bliss for woe.' And they only exaggerated in guarding against this and its like because they are injustices from which repentance is not possible, since the owners of the grains are not known until they are gathered and their rights are fulfilled. And for that reason, when the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, bought something, he said to the weigher when he was weighing its price: 'Weigh and give more.' The hadith: 'He said to the weigher: Weigh and give more' was narrated by the compilers of the Sunan and Al-Hakim from the hadith of Suwayd ibn Qays. At-Tirmidhi said: 'Hasan Sahih,' and Al-Hakim said: 'Sahih according to the conditions of Muslim.'
83:1.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Earning'

83:6.arabic: ثم تفكر فى ازدحام الخلائق واجتماعهم حتى ازدحم على الموقف أهل السموات السبع والأرضين السبع من ملك وجن وإنس وشيطان ووحش وسبع وطير فأشرقت عليهم الشمس وقد تضاعف حرها وتبدلت عما كانت عليه من خفة أمرها ثم أدنيت من رءوس العالمين كقاب قوسين فلم يبق على الأرض ظل إلا ظل رب العالمين ولم يمكن من الاستظلال به إلا المقربون فمن بين مستظل بالعرش وبين مضح لحر الشمس قد صهرته بحرها واشتد كربه وغمه من وهجها ثم تدافعت الخلائق ودفع بعضهم بعضا لشدة الزحام واختلاف الأقدام وانضاف إليه شدة الخجلة والحياء من الافتضاح والا
83:6.english: Then contemplate the crowding of the creatures and their gathering until the inhabitants of the seven heavens and the seven earths crowded upon the standing place (al-Mawqif) from angels, jinn, humans, devils, beasts, predators, and birds. The sun shone upon them, and its heat had multiplied and changed from what it was in lightness of its matter. Then it was brought near to the heads of the worlds like the distance of two bow-lengths, so there remained on the earth no shade except the shade of the Lord of the Worlds (Rabb al-'Alamin), and none could take shade in it except the ones brought near (al-Muqarrabun). So between one taking shade under the Throne (al-'Arsh) and one exposed to the sun's heat, which has melted him with its heat, and his distress and grief have intensified from its blaze. Then the creatures pushed one another and some pushed others due to the severity of the crowding and the difference in feet, and added to it is the severity of shame and modesty (al-Haya') from exposure and shrinking back at the presentation before the Compeller of the sky. So the blaze of the sun, the heat of breaths, and the burning of the hearts (al-Qulub) with the fire of modesty (al-Haya') and fear (al-Khawf) gathered, so sweat flowed from the root of every hair until it streamed on the plain of the Resurrection (al-Qiyamah). Then it rose on their bodies according to the measure of their stations (al-Manzilat) with Allah. For some, the sweat reached his knees; for some, his waist; for some, to the lobe of his ears; and for some, he almost drowned in it. Ibn 'Umar said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'The Day when the people will stand before the Lord of the Worlds (Yawma yaqumu al-nasu li-Rabb al-'Alamin) until one of them drowns in his sweat up to half his ears.'
83:6.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

83:6.arabic: يوم تقف فيه الخلائق شاخصة أبصارهم منفطرة قلوبهم لا يكلمون ولا ينظر فى أمورهم يقفون ثلثمائة عام لا يأكلون فيه أكله ولا يشربون فيه شربة ولا يجدون فيه روح نسيم. قال كعب وقتادة ﴿ يوم يقوم الناس لرب العلمين ﴾ {} قال يقومون مقدار ثلثمائة عام بل قال عبد الله بن عمرو تلا رسول الله ﭬ هذه الآية ثم قال: (كيف بكم إنه جمعكم الله كما تجمع النبل فى الكنانة خمسين ألف سنة ولا ينظر إليكم؟[153]) وقال الحسن ما ظنك بيوم قاموا فيه على أقدامهم مقدار خمسين ألف سنة لا يأكلون فيها أكلة ولا يشربون فيها شربة حتى إذا انقطعت
83:6.english: A day when the creatures will stand with their eyes staring, their hearts (Qalb) shattered, not speaking nor having their affairs looked into; they will stand for three hundred years, not eating a meal in it nor drinking a drink in it, nor finding in it a breath of breeze. Ka'b and Qatadah said: 'On the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds' (Quran 83:6). They said: They will stand for the measure of three hundred years. Rather, Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) recited this verse then said: 'How will you be when Allah gathers you as arrows are gathered in a quiver for fifty thousand years and does not look at you?' And Al-Hasan said: What do you think of a day when they stood on their feet for the measure of fifty thousand years, not eating a meal in it nor drinking a drink in it, until when their necks were cut off from thirst and their bellies burned from hunger, they were turned to the Fire and given to drink from a spring whose heat had come and its blaze intensified. When their exertion reached what they had no power for, some of them spoke to each other seeking one honored by his Master to intercede for their right, but they did not cling to any prophet except he pushed them away and said: Leave me, my soul (Nafs), my soul (Nafs), my affair has preoccupied me from the affair of others. And each one excused himself with the intensity of the anger of Allah the Exalted, saying: Today our Lord has become angry with an anger like which He has not become angry before nor will become angry after it, until our Prophet (peace be upon him) intercedes for whom permission is given to him in it: 'They will not possess intercession except for whom the Most Merciful has given permission and is pleased with his speech' (Quran 20:109). So contemplate in the length of this day and the intensity of waiting in it, so that waiting for patience from sins in your short life becomes light for you.
83:6.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

83:6.arabic: [153] حديث ابن عمر تلا هذه الآية يوم يقوم الناس لرب العالمين ثم قال كيف بكم إذا جمعكم الله كما يجمع النبل فى الكنانة خمسين ألف سنة لا ينظر إليكم قلت إنما هو عبد الله بن عمر ورواه الطبرانى فى الكبير وفيه عبد الرحمن بن ميسرة ولم يذكر له ابن أبى حاتم راويا غير ابن وهب ولهم غير عبد الرحمن بن ميسرة الحضرمى أربعة هذا أحدهم مصرى والثلاثة الآخرون شاميون.
83:6.english: [153] The hadith of Ibn 'Umar: He recited this verse 'The Day when the people will stand before the Lord of the worlds (Rabb al-'Alamin)' then said: How will you be when Allah gathers you as arrows are gathered in a quiver for fifty thousand years without looking at you? I said: It is only 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar. And Al-Tabarani narrated it in Al-Kabir, and in it is 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Maysarah, and Ibn Abi Hatim did not mention for him a narrator other than Ibn Wahb. And they have other than 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Maysarah al-Hadrami four; this one is Egyptian and the other three are Syrians.
83:6.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Book of Repentance'

83:6.arabic: وسمع على بن الفضيل قارئا يقرأ يوم يقوم الناس لرب العالمين فسقط مغشيا عليه فقال الفضيل شكر الله لك ما قد علمه منك وكذلك نقل عن جماعة منهم وكذلك الصوفية
83:6.english: And 'Ali ibn al-Fudayl heard a reciter reciting 'The Day when the people will stand before the Lord of the worlds (Rabb al-'Alamin)', so he fell unconscious. Al-Fudayl said: 'May Allah thank you for what He knows from you.' And likewise was narrated from a group among them, and likewise the Sufis.
83:6.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

83:6.arabic: [149] حديث ابن عمر يوم يقوم الناس لرب العالمين حتى يغيب أحدهم فى رشحه إلى أنصاف أذنيه متفق عليه.
83:6.english: Hadith of Ibn Umar: 'On the Day when the people will stand before the Lord of the worlds (Yawma yaqūmu al-nāsu li-rabbi al-ʿālamīna) until one of them is submerged in his sweat up to half of his ears.' Agreed upon.
83:6.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Book of Repentance'

83:14.arabic: وروى أبو هريرة عن النبي ﭬ أنه قال: (إن المؤمن إذا أذنب ذنبا كانت نكتة سوداء في قلبه فإن تاب ونزع واستغفر صقل قلبه منها فإن زاد زادت حتى تغلف قلبه[118] فذلك الران الذي ذكره الله عز وجل في كتابه ﴿ كلا بل ران على قلوبهم ما كانوا يكسبون ﴾ {}).
83:14.english: And Abu Hurairah narrated from the Prophet (peace be upon him) that he said: 'Verily, when a believer commits a sin, a black spot appears in his Heart (Qalb). If he repents, desists, and seeks forgiveness, his Heart (Qalb) is polished from it. But if he increases (in sin), it increases until it covers his Heart (Qalb). That is the covering (Raan) which Allah the Exalted mentioned in His Book: "No! Rather, what they have earned has covered their hearts."'
83:14.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith

83:15.arabic: فبالنزوع إلى الدنيا يحجب عن لقاء الله تعالى، وعند الحجاب تتسلط عليه نار جهنم، إذ النار غير مسلطة إلا على محجوب. قال الله تعالى: " كلا إنهم عن ربهم يومئذ لمحجوبون، ثم إنهم لصالو الجحيم "، فرتب العذاب بالنار على ألم الحجاب، وألم الحجاب كاف من غير علاوة النار، فكيف إذا أضيفت العلاوة إليه؟
83:15.english: By inclining towards the worldly life (Dunya), one is veiled from meeting Allah the Exalted, and at the time of the veil (Hijab), the fire of Hell (Jahannam) gains power over him, for the fire is not empowered except over one who is veiled. Allah the Exalted said: "No indeed! They will be veiled from their Lord on that day. Then indeed they will enter the Blazing Fire." So He arranged the punishment by fire upon the pain of the veil (Hijab), and the pain of the veil (Hijab) is sufficient without the addition of the fire, so how when the addition is appended to it?
83:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

83:18.arabic: والشراب عبارة عن جملة نعيم الجنان، كما أن الكتاب عبر به عن جميع الأعمال فقال: "إن كتاب الأبرار لفي عليين" ثم قال: "يشهده المقربون" فكان أمارة علة كتابهم أنه ارتفع إلى حيث يشهده المقربون، وكما أن الأبرار يجدون المزيد في حالهم ومعرفتهم بقربهم من المقربين ومشاهدتهم لهم، فكذلك يكون حالهم في الآخرة
83:18.english: And the drink is an expression for the entirety of the bliss of Paradise, just as the book was expressed by it for all the deeds. He said: "Indeed, the book of the righteous is in 'Illiyyin (the highest register)" then He said: "Witnessed by those brought near (al-Muqarrabun)". So it was a sign of the reason for their book that it rose to where those brought near (al-Muqarrabun) witness it. And just as the righteous find increase in their state and knowledge by their nearness to those brought near (al-Muqarrabun) and their witnessing of them, so will be their state in the Hereafter.
83:18.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

83:19.arabic: ولما قصرت الأفهام عن درك معنى عليين عظم أمره فقال: " وما أدراك ما عليون " كما قال تعالى: " القارعة ما القارعة وما أدراك ما القارعة ".
83:19.english: And when understandings fell short of comprehending the meaning of 'Illiyyun (عليين)', He magnified its matter and said: "And what will make you know what 'Illiyyun (عليين) is?" just as The Exalted said: "The Striking Calamity (Al-Qari'ah) - what is the Striking Calamity (Al-Qari'ah)? And what will make you know what the Striking Calamity (Al-Qari'ah) is?"
83:19.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

83:22.arabic: فإن قلت فليت شعرى ماذا موردى وإلى ماذا مآلى ومرجعى وما الذى سبق به القضاء فى حقى فلك علامة تستأنس بها وتصدق رجاءك بسببها وهى أن تنظر إلى أحوالك وأعمالك فإن كلا ميسر لما خلق له فإن كان قد يسر لك سبيل الخير فأبشر فإنك مبعد عن النار وإن كنت لا تقصد خيرا إلا وتحيط بك العوائق فتدفعه ولا تقصد شرا إلا ويتيسر لك أسبابه فاعلم أنك مقضى عليك فإن دلالة هذا على العاقبة كدلالة المطر على النبات ودلالة الدخان على النار فقد قال الله تعالى: ﴿ إن الأبرار لفى نعيم وإن الفجار لفى جحيم ﴾ {} فاعرض نفسك على الآيتين وقد
83:22.english: If you say: 'Would that I knew what my source is, and to what my end and return is, and what has preceded in the decree concerning me,' then you have a sign to find comfort in and to confirm your hope because of it, which is to look at your states and your deeds. For each is facilitated for what he was created for. If the path of good has been facilitated for you, then rejoice, for you are distanced from the Fire. And if you do not intend good except that obstacles surround you and repel it, and you do not intend evil except that its causes are facilitated for you, then know that you are decreed against. For the indication of this on the outcome is like the indication of rain on vegetation and the indication of smoke on fire. Indeed, Allah the Exalted has said: 'Indeed, the Righteous (Al-Abrar) are in Bliss (Na'im), and indeed, the Wicked (Al-Fujjar) are in Blazing Fire (Jahim).' So present yourself to the two verses, and you have known your abode from the two abodes, and Allah knows best.
83:22.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

83:22.arabic: ومنها أن يكون مشفقاً على جميع عباد الله رحيماً بهم شديداً على جميع أعداء الله وعلى كل من يقارف شيئاً مما يكرهه كما قال الله تعالى: "أشداء على الكفار رحماء بينهم" ولا تأخذه لومة لائم ولا يصرفه عن الغضب لله صارف، وبه وصف الله أولياؤه إذ قال الذين يكلفون بحبي كما يكلف الصبي بالشيء ويأوون إلى ذكري كما يأوي النسر إلى وكره، ويغضبون لمحارمه كما يغضب النمر إذا حرد فإنه لا يبالي قل الناس أو كثروا، فانظر إلى هذا المثال فإن الصبي إذا كلف بالشيء لم يفارقه أصلاً، وإن أخذ منه لم يكن له شغل إلا البكاء والصياح
83:22.english: And among them is that he be compassionate toward all the servants of Allah, merciful to them, severe against all the enemies of Allah and against everyone who commits something that He dislikes, as Allah the Exalted said: "Severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves." And no blame of a blamer takes him, nor does any deterrent divert him from anger for Allah. And with this, Allah described His allies (awliya') when He said: Those who are burdened with My love as a child is burdened with a thing, and they take refuge in My remembrance (dhikr) as an eagle takes refuge in its nest, and they become angry for My prohibitions as a tiger becomes angry when enraged, for he does not care whether people are few or many. So look at this example: For the child, if burdened with a thing, does not leave it at all, and if it is taken from him, he has no occupation except crying and shouting until it is returned to him. If he sleeps, he takes it with him in his clothes, and when he wakes, he returns and clings to it. Whenever he is separated from it, he cries, and whenever he finds it, he laughs. Whoever disputes him in it, he hates him, and whoever gives it to him, he loves him. As for the tiger, he cannot control himself when angry until he reaches such intensity of anger that he destroys himself. These are the signs of love (muhabbah). So whoever has these signs completed in him, then his love has been completed and his love has become pure, so his drink (sharab) becomes pure in the Hereafter and his drink becomes sweet. And whoever mixes with his love love for other than Allah, he enjoys in the Hereafter according to his love, for his drink is mixed with a measure of the drink of the close ones (al-muqarrabun), as Allah the Exalted said concerning the righteous (al-abrar): "Indeed, the righteous are in delight (na'im)." Then He said: "They will be given to drink from a pure wine sealed with musk, and for this let the competitors compete. And its mixture is of Tasnim, a spring from which those near to Allah will drink." So if the drink of the righteous becomes pleasant due to the mixing of the pure drink that is for the close ones. And the drink is an expression for the entirety of the delight of Paradise (al-jinan), just as the Book expressed by it all the deeds, saying: "Indeed, the record of the righteous is in 'Illiyyun." Then He said: "Witnessed by those brought near." So it was a sign of the cause of their record that it rose to where those brought near witness it. And just as the righteous find increase in their state and knowledge by their proximity to the close ones and their witnessing of them, so will be their state in the Hereafter: "He did not create you nor resurrect you except as a single soul, as We began the first creation, We will repeat it." And as Allah the Exalted said: "A reward matching." That is, the reward matched their deeds, so the pure was met with the pure from the drink, and the mixed was met with the mixed, and the mixing of every drink is according to what preceded of mixing in his love and his deeds: "So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it - And Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves - Indeed, Allah does not do injustice, [even] as much as an atom's weight. And if there is [any] good, He multiplies it - And if it should be the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth, and sufficient are We as accountant." So whoever his love in this world is his hope for the delight of Paradise and the houris.
83:22.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

83:22.arabic: خلق الجنة وخلق لها أهلا فاستعملهم بالطاعة وخلق النار وخلق لها أهلا فاستعمله بالمعاصي وعرف الخلق علامة أهل الجنة وأهل النار فقال إن الأبرار لفي نعيم وإن الفجار لفي جحيم ثم قال تعالى فيما روى عن نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم هؤلاء في الجنة ولا أبالي وهؤلاء في النار ولا أبالي[97]
83:22.english: He created Paradise and created its people, then employed them in obedience, and He created Hell and created its people, then employed them in disobedience. And He made known to creation the sign of the people of Paradise and the people of Hell, so He said: 'Indeed, the righteous (Al-Abrar) are in bliss (Na'eem), and indeed, the wicked (Al-Fujjar) are in a Blaze (Jahim).' Then He, the Exalted, said in what has been narrated from His Prophet (peace be upon him): 'These are in Paradise, and I do not care, and these are in Hell, and I do not care.'
83:22.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

83:22.arabic: قال أبو حازم اعرض نفسك على كتاب الله تعالى حيث قال إن الأبرار لفي نعيم وان الفجار لفي جحيم قال فأين رحمة الله قال قريب من المحسنين
83:22.english: Abu Hazim said: 'Present yourself to the Book of Allah (the Quran) where He said: "Indeed, the Righteous (Al-Abrar) are in Bliss (Na'eem), and indeed, the Wicked (Al-Fujjar) are in Blazing Fire (Jahim)."' He said: 'So where is the Mercy (Rahma) of Allah?' He said: 'Close to the Doers of Good (Al-Muhsinin).'
83:22.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

83:24.arabic: فاستثر الخوف من قلبك بطول الفكر فى أهوال الجحيم واستثر الرجاء بطول الفكر فى النعيم المقيم الموعود لأهل الجنان وسق نفسك بسوط الخوف وقدها بزمام الرجاء إلى الصراط المستقيم فبذلك تنال الملك العظيم وتسلم من العذاب الأليم فتفكر فى أهل الجنة وفى وجوههم نضرة النعيم يسقون من رحيق مختوم جالسين على منابر الياقوت الأحمر فى خيام من اللؤلؤ الرطب الأبيض فيها بسط من العبقرى الأخضر متكئين على أرائك منصوبة على أطراف أنهار مطردة بالخمر والعسل محفوفة بالغلمان والولدان مزينة بالحور العين من الخيرات الحسان كأنهن اليا
83:24.english: So extract the Fear (Khauf) from your Heart (Qalb) through prolonged contemplation of the terrors of Hellfire, and extract the Hope (Rajaa) through prolonged contemplation of the abiding Bliss (Na'eem) promised to the people of the Gardens. Drive your Soul (Nafs) with the whip of Fear and guide it with the reins of Hope to the Straight Path (Sirat al-Mustaqeem), for by that you will attain the great dominion and be saved from the painful punishment. So contemplate the people of Paradise, and in their faces is the radiance of Bliss (Nadhrat an-Na'eem). They are given to drink of a sealed pure wine, sitting on thrones of red ruby, in tents of moist white pearl, therein spreads of green brocade, reclining on couches set up on the banks of rivers flowing with wine and honey, surrounded by youths and boys, adorned with wide-eyed maidens of beautiful goodness, as if they were ruby and coral. No man has touched them before them, nor jinn. They walk in the degrees of the Gardens; when one of them sways in her walk, seventy thousand boys carry her flanks. Upon her are fine white silks that dazzle the eyes, crowned with tiaras studded with pearl and coral, coquettish, fragrant, secure from old age and misery, secluded in the tents, in palaces of ruby built amidst the meadows of the Gardens, with restrained glances. Then they are served, and upon them, with cups and ewers and a cup from a flowing spring, white, a delight to the drinkers. And there circulate upon them servants and boys like hidden pearls, as a reward for what they used to do, in a secure station, in Gardens and springs, in Gardens and a river, in a seat of truth near an Omnipotent Sovereign. They look therein at the face of the Noble King, and the radiance of Bliss (Nadhrat an-Na'eem) has shone in their faces. No fatigue touches them, nor humiliation, but they are honored servants, and with various gifts from their Lord they are attended. They are in what their Souls (Anfus) desire, abiding forever; they fear not therein, nor do they grieve, and they are secure from the doubt of death.
83:24.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

83:24.arabic: فبذلك تنال الملك العظيم وتسلم من العذاب الأليم فتفكر فى أهل الجنة وفى وجوههم نضرة النعيم يسقون من رحيق مختوم جالسين على منابر الياقوت الأحمر فى خيام من اللؤلؤ الرطب الأبيض فيها بسط من العبقرى الأخضر متكئين على أرائك منصوبة على أطراف أنهار مطردة بالخمر والعسل محفوفة بالغلمان والولدان مزينة بالحور العين من الخيرات الحسان كأنهن الياقوت والمرجان لم يطمثهن إنس قبلهم ولا جان يمشين فى درجات الجنان إذا اختالت إحداهن فى مشيها حمل أعطافها سبعون ألفا من الولدان عليها من طرائف الحرير الأبيض ما تتحير فيه الأ
83:24.english: By that, you attain the great dominion and are saved from the painful punishment. So contemplate the people of Paradise, and in their faces is the radiance of bliss (نضرة النعيم). They are given to drink from a sealed pure wine, sitting on thrones of red ruby, in tents of moist white pearl, therein are spreads of green brocade, reclining on couches set up on the banks of rivers flowing with wine and honey, surrounded by youths and young boys, adorned with wide-eyed maidens (الحور العين) of beautiful good deeds, as if they were ruby and coral. No human has touched them before them, nor jinn. They walk in the degrees of Paradise; when one of them sways in her walk, seventy thousand young boys carry her flanks. Upon her are fine white silks that bewilder the eyes, crowned with crowns studded with pearl and coral, coquettish, flirtatious, fragrant, secure from old age and misery, secluded in the tents in palaces of ruby built amidst the meadows of Paradise, with restrained glances, chaste. Then they are served, and upon them, with cups and pitchers and a cup from a flowing spring, white, a delight for the drinkers, and there serve them servants and young boys like hidden pearls, as a reward for what they used to do, in a secure station, in gardens and springs, in gardens and a river, in a seat of truth near an Omnipotent Sovereign. They look therein at the face of the Noble King, and has shone in their faces the radiance of bliss (نضرة النعيم). No fatigue touches them, nor humiliation, but they are honored servants, and with various gifts from their Lord they are attended to. They are in what their souls (أنفسهم) desire, abiding forever; they do not fear therein, nor do they grieve, and they are secure from the doubt of death. They are therein enjoying bliss, and they eat from its foods and drink from its rivers milk and wine and honey, in rivers whose beds are of silver and whose gravel is coral, and on its ground its dust is fragrant musk and its plants are saffron, and they are rained upon from clouds therein from water of narcissus upon dunes of camphor, and they are brought cups, and what cups! Cups of silver studded with pearls and ruby and coral, a cup in it from the sealed pure wine mixed with it the sweet Salsabil, a cup whose light shines from the purity of its jewel, the drink appears from behind it with its thinness and redness; no human made it, so he falls short in leveling its making and beautifying its craftsmanship, in the hand of a servant whose brightness of his face resembles the sun in its radiance, but from where does the sun have sweetness like the sweetness of his form and the beauty of his temples and the loveliness of his pupils? So wonder at one who believes in an abode of this description and is certain that its people do not die, nor do calamities befall one who settles in its courtyard, nor do events look with the eye of change at its people, how he finds comfort in an abode that God has decreed its ruin and delights in a life below it? By God, if there were not in it except the soundness of the bodies with security from death, hunger, and thirst, and...
83:24.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

83:25.arabic: فهذه علامات المحبة، فمن تمت فيه هذه العلامات فقد تمت محبته وخلص حبه فصفا في الآخرة شرابه وعذب مشربه، ومن امتزج بحبه حب غير الله تنعم في الآخرة بقدر حبه، إذ يمزج شرابه بقدر من شراب المقربين كما قال تعالى في الأبرار: "إن الأبرار لفي نعيم" ثم قال: "يسقون من رحيق مختوم مسك وفي ذلك فليتنافس المتنافسون ومزاجه من تسنيم عيناً يشرب بها المقربون" فإذا طاب شراب الأبرار لشوب الشراب الصرف الذي هو للمقربين. والشراب عبارة عن جملة نعيم الجنان، كما أن الكتاب عبر به عن جميع الأعمال فقال: "إن كتاب الأبرار لفي عليي
83:25.english: These are the signs of love (Mahabbah), so whoever has these signs completed in him, then his love has been perfected and his affection has been purified, so his drink becomes pure in the Hereafter and his source of drink becomes sweet. And whoever mixes with his love the love of other than Allah, he will enjoy in the Hereafter according to the measure of his love, since his drink is mixed with a measure of the drink of the close ones (Muqarrabun) as Allah the Exalted said regarding the righteous (Al-Abrar): 'Indeed, the righteous are in pleasure' then He said: 'They are given to drink from a pure wine which was sealed. Its seal is musk - so for this let the competitors compete. And its mixture is of Tasnim. A spring from which those near [to Allah] drink.' So if the drink of the righteous becomes pleasant due to the mixing of the pure drink which is for the close ones (Muqarrabun). And the drink is an expression for the totality of the bliss of Paradise (Jinan), just as the Book expressed by it all the deeds, saying: 'Indeed, the record of the righteous is in 'illiyyun' then He said: 'Witnessed by those brought near [to Allah]' so it was a sign that the reason for their record is that it rose to where the close ones (Muqarrabun) witness it. And just as the righteous find increase in their state and their knowledge of their proximity to the close ones (Muqarrabun) and their witnessing of them, so will be their state in the Hereafter.
83:25.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

83:26.arabic: والمنافسة في اللغة مشتقة من النفاسة والذي يدل على إباحة المنافسة قوله تعالى "وفي ذلك فليتنافس المتنافسون" وقال تعالى "سابقوا إلى مغفرة من ربكم" وإنما المسابقة عند خوف الفوت وهو كالعبدين يتسابقان إلى خدمة مولاهما؛ إذ يجزع كل واحد أن يسبقه صاحبه فيحظى عند مولاه بمنزلة لا يحظى هو بها، فكيف وقد صرح رسول الله ﷺ بذلك فقال "لا حسد إلا في اثنتين: رجل آتاه الله مالاً فسلطه على هلكته في الحق، ورجل آتاه الله تعالى علماً فهو يعمل به ويعلمه الناس" ثم فسر ذلك في حديث أبي كبشة الأتماري فقال "مثل هذه الأمة مثل
83:26.english: And competition (Al-Munafasah) in language is derived from preciousness (An-Nafasah), and what indicates the permissibility of competition is His saying, the Exalted: "And in that let the competitors compete (فليتنافس المتنافسون)" and His saying, the Exalted: "Race toward forgiveness from your Lord (سابقوا إلى مغفرة من ربكم)". Indeed, the race is when fearing loss, and it is like two servants racing to serve their master; for each one grieves that his companion precedes him and attains with his master a status that he does not attain. How much more so when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ explicitly stated that, saying: "There is no envy (Hasad) except in two: a man whom Allah has given wealth and empowered him to spend it in truth, and a man whom Allah, the Exalted, has given knowledge and he acts upon it and teaches it to the people." Then he explained that in the hadith of Abu Kabshah Al-Atmari, saying: "The likeness of this nation is like four: a man whom Allah has given wealth and knowledge, so he acts upon his knowledge with his wealth; and a man whom Allah has given knowledge but has not given him wealth, so he says: 'O Lord, if I had wealth like the wealth of so-and-so, I would act in it with the like of his action' - so they are equal in reward. And this is from him a love to have the like of his wealth to act as he acts, without love for the removal of the blessing from him, he said - and a man whom Allah has given wealth but has not given him knowledge, so he spends it in disobedience to Allah; and a man whom He has not given knowledge and has not given him wealth, so he says: 'If I had the like of the wealth of so-and-so, I would spend it in the like of what he spends it in of disobedience' - so they are equal in sin." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ censured him from the aspect of his wishing for disobedience, not from the aspect of his love to have from the blessing the like of what he has. Therefore, there is no blame on one who admires another in
83:26.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

83:26.arabic: فإن كنت تطلب أعلى الدرجات فاجتهد أن لا يسبقك أحد بطاعة الله تعالى فقد أمرك الله بالمسابقة والمنافسة فيها فقال تعالى: ﴿ سابقوا إلى مغفرة من ربكم ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ وفى ذلك فليتنافس المتنافسون ﴾ {} والعجب أنه لو تقدم عليك أقرانك أو جيرانك بزيادة درهم أو بعلو بناء ثقل عليك ذلك وضاق به صدرك وتنغص بسبب الحسد عيشك وأحسن أحوالك أن تستقر فى الجنة وأنت لا تسلم فيها من أقوام يسبقونك بلطائف لا توازيها الدنيا بحذافيرها
83:26.english: If you seek the highest degrees (darajat), then strive that no one precedes you in obedience (ta'ah) to Allah the Exalted, for Allah has commanded you with racing (musabaqah) and competition (munafasah) in it. He the Exalted said: 'Race toward forgiveness from your Lord' and He the Exalted said: 'And in that let the competitors compete.' And it is astonishing that if your peers or neighbors advance over you with an increase of a dirham or with a higher building, that weighs heavily upon you and your chest constricts from it, and your life becomes bitter due to envy (hasad). And the best of your states is that you settle in Paradise (Jannah) while you are not safe in it from people who precede you with subtleties (lata'if) that the world (dunya) does not equal with all its entirety.
83:26.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Book of Repentance'

83:26.arabic: وقد أمر الله تعالى بالحسد والمنافسة في الخيرات وتوقي الشرور فقال تعالى: "وفي ذلك فليتنافس المتنافسون". وقال النبي ﭬ: "لا حسد إلا في اثنتين رجل آتاه الله حكمة فهو يبثها في الناس ويعلمها ورجل آتاه الله مالاً فسلطه على هلكته في الحق". وفي لفظ آخر "ورجل آتاه الله القرآن فهو يقوم به آناء الليل والنهار فيقول الرجل لو آتاني الله مثل هذا لفعلت مثل ما يفعل".
83:26.english: And Allah the Exalted has commanded envy (Hasad) and competition (Munafasah) in good deeds and avoiding evils, so He said: "And in that let the competitors compete." And the Prophet ﭬ said: "There is no envy except in two: a man whom Allah has given wisdom so he disseminates it among people and teaches it, and a man whom Allah has given wealth so he empowers it in its destruction in truth." And in another wording: "And a man whom Allah has given the Quran so he stands with it during the night and day, and a man says: If Allah had given me like this, I would have done like what he does."
83:26.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

83:29.arabic: ومن لم يفهم هذا ينكر عليهم ويقول كيف فنى وطول ظله أربعة اذرع ولعله يأكل في كل يوم أرطالا من الخبز فيضحك عليهم الجهال لجهلهم بمعاني كلامهم وضرورة قول العارفين ان يكونوا ضحكة للجاهلين واليه الاشارة بقوله تعالى: ﴿ ان الذين اجرموا كانوا من الذين امنوا يضحكون واذا مروا بهم يتغامزون واذا انقلبوا الى اهلهم انقلبوا فكهين وإذ رأوهم قالوا ان هؤلاء لضالون وما ارسلوا عليهم حافظين ﴾ {} ثم بين أن ضحك العارفين عليهم غدا اعظم اذ قال تعالى: ﴿ فاليوم الذين آمنوا من الكفار يضحكون على الأرائك ينظرون ﴾ {} وكذلك امة
83:29.english: And whoever does not understand this denies them and says: How has he annihilated while his shadow's length is four cubits, and perhaps he eats pounds of bread every day? So the ignorant ones laugh at them due to their ignorance of the meanings of their speech, and it is necessary for the Knowers (Al-Arifin) to be a laughingstock for the ignorant ones. And to this is the allusion by His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed. And when they passed by them, they would wink at each other. And when they returned to their people, they would return jesting. And when they saw them, they would say, "Indeed, these are truly lost." But they were not sent as guardians over them.' Then He clarified that the laughter of the Knowers (Al-Arifin) upon them tomorrow is greater, when He said, the Exalted: 'So today those who believed are laughing at the disbelievers, on couches, observing.' And likewise, the people of Nuh (Noah), peace be upon him, used to laugh at him when he was occupied with making the ship. He said: 'If you ridicule us, then indeed we will ridicule you just as you ridicule.' So this is one of the two perspectives.
83:29.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

83:32.arabic: وضرورة قول العارفين ان يكونوا ضحكة للجاهلين واليه الاشارة بقوله تعالى: ﴿ ان الذين اجرموا كانوا من الذين امنوا يضحكون واذا مروا بهم يتغامزون واذا انقلبوا الى اهلهم انقلبوا فكهين وإذ رأوهم قالوا ان هؤلاء لضالون وما ارسلوا عليهم حافظين ﴾ {} ثم بين أن ضحك العارفين عليهم غدا اعظم اذ قال تعالى: ﴿ فاليوم الذين آمنوا من الكفار يضحكون على الأرائك ينظرون ﴾ {} وكذلك امة نوح عليه السلام كانوا يضحكون عليه عند اشتغاله بعمل السفينة قال: ﴿ إن تسخروا منا فإنا نسخر منكم كما تسخرون ﴾ {} فهذا احد النظرين.
83:32.english: And it is necessary for the Knowers (Al-Arifin) to be a laughingstock for the ignorant, and to this is the allusion by His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed, and when they passed by them, they would wink at one another, and when they returned to their people, they would return jesting, and when they saw them, they would say: Indeed, these are astray, and they were not sent as guardians over them.' Then He clarified that the laughter of the Knowers (Al-Arifin) upon them tomorrow is greater, as He said, the Exalted: 'So today those who believed from the disbelievers are laughing upon the couches, looking.' And likewise, the people of Noah, peace be upon him, used to laugh at him when he was occupied with the work of the ship. He said: 'If you mock us, then indeed we mock you as you mock.' So this is one of the two perspectives.
83:32.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

83:34.arabic: وضرورة قول العارفين ان يكونوا ضحكة للجاهلين واليه الاشارة بقوله تعالى: ﴿ ان الذين اجرموا كانوا من الذين امنوا يضحكون واذا مروا بهم يتغامزون واذا انقلبوا الى اهلهم انقلبوا فكهين وإذ رأوهم قالوا ان هؤلاء لضالون وما ارسلوا عليهم حافظين ﴾ {} ثم بين أن ضحك العارفين عليهم غدا اعظم اذ قال تعالى: ﴿ فاليوم الذين آمنوا من الكفار يضحكون على الأرائك ينظرون ﴾ {} وكذلك امة نوح عليه السلام كانوا يضحكون عليه عند اشتغاله بعمل السفينة قال: ﴿ إن تسخروا مننا فإنا نسخر منكم كما تسخرون ﴾ {} فهذا احد النظرين.
83:34.english: And it is necessary for the Knowers (Al-Arifin) to be a laughingstock for the ignorant ones, and to this is the allusion by His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed, and when they passed by them, they would wink at one another, and when they returned to their people, they would return jesting, and when they saw them, they would say, "Indeed, these are truly astray," and they were not sent over them as guardians.'
