Then He clarified that the laughter of the Knowers (Al-Arifin) upon them tomorrow is greater, as He said, the Exalted: 'So today those who believed from the disbelievers are laughing, upon couches, looking.' And likewise, the people of Noah, peace be upon him, used to laugh at him when he was occupied with making the ship. He said: 'If you ridicule us, then indeed we will ridicule you just as you ridicule.' So this is one of the two perspectives.
83:34.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

84:4.arabic: فإذا فارقت الروح الجسد فقد حملت الأرض فمدت حتى ألقت ما فيها وتخلت ولست أطول بجميع موازنة الأحوال والأهوال ولكني أقول بمجرد الموت تقوم عليك هذه القيامة الصغرى ولا يفوتك من القيامة الكبرى شيء مما يخصك بل ما يخص غيرك
84:4.english: When the Spirit (Ruh) separates from the body, then the earth has been burdened and stretched until it cast forth what was within it and became empty. I will not elaborate on all the balancing of states and terrors, but I say: upon death alone, this minor resurrection (Qiyamah) stands against you, and nothing of the major resurrection (Qiyamah) that pertains to you will escape you, but rather what pertains to others.
84:4.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

84:6.arabic: وقال ﭬ للذي أوصاه: (وإذا صليت فصل صلاة مودع[39]) أي مودع لنفسه مودع لهواه مودع لعمره سائر إلى مولاه كما قال عز وجل: ﴿ أيها الإنسان إنك كادح إلى ربك كدحا فملاقيه ﴾ {الانشقاق: 6}
84:6.english: And he (peace be upon him) said to the one he advised: 'When you pray, pray the prayer of one departing (Muwaddi').' That is, departing from his Soul (Nafs), departing from his desire (Hawa), departing from his lifespan, journeying to his Master (Mawla) as the Exalted said: 'O human being, indeed you are laboring (Kadih) toward your Lord (Rabb) with labor (Kadhan), then you will meet Him.'
84:6.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

84:8.arabic: وللشيخين من حديث عائشة من نوقش الحساب عذب قالت قلت يقول الله تعالى فسوف يحاسب حسابا يسيرا قال ذلك العرض
84:8.english: And from the two Sheikhs (Al-Bukhari and Muslim) from the hadith of Aisha: 'Whoever is questioned in the accounting (hisab) is punished.' She said: 'I said: Allah the Exalted says: "Then he will be accounted with an easy accounting (hisaban yasiran)."' He said: 'That is the presentation (al-'ard).'
84:8.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Foundations of Belief'

86:15.arabic: وقال عز وجل "ومكروا ومكر الله والله خير الماكرين" وقال تعالى "إنهم يكيدون كيداً وأكيد كيداً فمهل الكافرين أمهلهم رويداً" فكما لا يجوز للعبد المهمل أن يستدل بإهمال السيد إياه وتمكينه من النعم على حب السيد، بل ينبغي أن يحذر أن يكون ذلك مكراً منه وكيداً مع أن السيد لم يحذره مكر نفسه، فبأن يجب ذلك في حق الله تعالى مع تحذيره استدراجه أولى، فإذن من أمن مكر الله فهو مغتر، ومنشأ هذا الغرور أنه استدل بنعم الدنيا على أنه كريم عند ذلك المنعم، واحتمل أن يكون ذلك دليل الهوان ولكن ذلك الاحتمال لا يوافق الهوى،
86:15.english: And the Exalted said: "And they plotted and Allah plotted, and Allah is the best of plotters." And He said: "Indeed, they plan a plan, and I plan a plan. So give the disbelievers respite; give them respite a little." So just as it is not permissible for the neglected servant to infer from the master's neglect of him and enabling him with blessings that the master loves him, rather he should be cautious that this might be plotting and scheming from him, even though the master did not warn him of his own plotting, then how much more necessary is this regarding Allah the Exalted with His warning of His gradual entrapment? Therefore, whoever feels secure from Allah's plotting is deluded. The origin of this delusion is that he inferred from worldly blessings that he is honorable with that Bestower, and it is possible that this is evidence of degradation, but that possibility does not agree with the desire (Hawa). So Satan, through the medium of desire (Hawa), inclines the Heart (Qalb) toward what accompanies it, which is believing in its indication of honor, and this is the limit of delusion.
86:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

87:1.arabic: السادسة: الوتر قال أنس بن مالك كان رسول الله ﷺ يوتر بعد العشاء بثلاث ركعات يقرأ في الأولى سبح اسم ربك الأعلى وفي الثانية قل يا أيها الكافرون وفي الثالثة قل هو الله أحد[225] وجاء في الخبر أنه ﷺ كان يصلي بعد الوتر ركعتين جالسا وفي بعضها متربعا[226] وفي بعض الأخبار: (إذا أراد أن يدخل فراشه زحف إليه وصلى فوقه ركعتين قبل أن يرقد يقراء فيهما إذا زلزلت الأرض وسورة التكاثر[227]) وفي رواية أخرى قل يا أيها الكافرون ويجوز الوتر مفصولا وموصولا بتسليمة واحدةوتسليمتين وقد أوتر رسول الله ﷺ بركعة[228] وثلاث[229
87:1.english: The Sixth: The Odd-Numbered Prayer (Al-Witr). Anas bin Malik said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to perform the Odd-Numbered Prayer (Al-Witr) after the Evening Prayer (Al-'Isha) with three units of prayer (Rak'at). He would recite in the first: 'Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High (Sabbih isma rabbika al-a'la)' and in the second: 'Say: O you who disbelieve (Qul ya ayyuha al-kafirun)' and in the third: 'Say: He is Allah, the One (Qul huwa Allahu ahad).' [225] And it came in the report that he ﷺ used to pray after the Odd-Numbered Prayer (Al-Witr) two units of prayer (Rak'at) sitting, and in some of them cross-legged. [226] And in some reports: 'When he wanted to enter his bed, he would crawl to it and pray upon it two units of prayer (Rak'at) before lying down, reciting in them: 'When the earth is shaken (Idha zulzilat al-ard)' and the chapter of Abundance (Surat al-Takathur).' [227] And in another narration: 'Say: O you who disbelieve (Qul ya ayyuha al-kafirun).' And it is permissible for the Odd-Numbered Prayer (Al-Witr) to be separated and connected with one salutation (Taslimah) and two salutations (Taslimat). And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed the Odd-Numbered Prayer (Al-Witr) with one unit of prayer (Rak'ah) [228], and three [229], and five [230], and thus with the odd-numbered prayers (Al-Awtar) up to eleven units of prayer (Rak'at) [232]. And the narration is uncertain about thirteen [233], and in a rare hadith, seventeen units of prayer (Rak'at) [234]. And these units of prayer (Rak'at), meaning what we have named in total as the Odd-Numbered Prayer (Al-Witr), are prayer at night, and it is the Vigil Prayer (Al-Tahajjud), and the Vigil Prayer (Al-Tahajjud) at night is a confirmed Sunnah, and its virtues will be mentioned in the Book of Regular Devotions (Kitab al-Awrad). And regarding the best, there is a difference of opinion. It is said that performing the Odd-Numbered Prayer (Al-Witr) with a single unit of prayer (Rak'ah) is best, since it is confirmed that he ﷺ used to consistently perform the Odd-Numbered Prayer (Al-I'tar) with a single unit of prayer (Rak'ah). And it is said that the connected one is best to avoid the suspicion of disagreement, especially for the Imam, since one who does not consider the single unit of prayer (Rak'ah) as prayer may follow him. If he prays connectedly, he intends with all of them the Odd-Numbered Prayer (Al-Witr), and if he limits himself to one unit of prayer (Rak'ah) after the two units of prayer (Rak'at) of the Evening Prayer (Al-'Isha) or after the obligatory Evening Prayer (Fard al-'Isha), he intends the Odd-Numbered Prayer (Al-Witr) and it is valid because the condition of the Odd-Numbered Prayer (Al-Witr) is that it be.
87:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

87:1.arabic:
يل
وتستوسق ظلمته. وترتيب هذا الورد بمراءة ثلاثة أمور: الأول  أن  يصلي  سوى  فرض
العشاء عشر ركعات أربعا قبل الفرض إحياء  لما  بين  الأذانين  وستا  بعد  الفرض
ركعتين ثم أربعا ويقرأ فيها  من  القرآن  الآيات  المخصوصة  كآخر  البقرة  وآية
الكرسي وأول الحديد وآخر الحشر وغيرها. والثاني أن يصلي ثلاث عشرة  ركعة  آخرهن
الوتر فإنه أكثر ما روى أن النبي ﭬ  صلى  بها  من  الليل[43]  والأكياس  يأخذون
أوقاتهم من أول الليل والأقوياء من آخره والحزم التقديم فإنه  ربما  لا  يستيقظ
أو يثقل عليه القيام إلا إذا صار ذلك
87:1.english: [48] Hadith: He (the Prophet) loved 'Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High' (Sabbih isma rabbika al-a'la). It was reported by Ahmad and Al-Bazzar from the narration of Ali with a weak chain.
87:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Arrangement of Litanies'

87:1.arabic: وكان العلماء يجعلونها ستا فيزيدون سبح اسم ربك الأعلى إذ في الخبر (أنه ﭬ كان يحب سبح اسم ربك الأعلى، وكان يقرأ في ثلاث ركعات الوتر ثلاث سور سبح اسم ربك الأعلى[48] وقل يا أيها الكافرون والإخلاص[49] فإذا فرغ قال سبحان الملك القدوس ثلاث مرات).
87:1.english: And the scholars would make them six by adding 'Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High (سبح اسم ربك الأعلى)' since in the report (that he ﭬ loved 'Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High (سبح اسم ربك الأعلى)', and he would recite in the three rak'ahs of the Witr prayer three surahs: 'Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High (سبح اسم ربك الأعلى)'[48] and 'Say: O you who disbelieve (قل يا أيها الكافرون)' and 'Sincerity (الإخلاص)'[49], then when he finished he would say 'Glory be to the King, the Holy (سبحان الملك القدوس)' three times).
87:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Book of Knowledge'

87:7.arabic: ولا يتفكر واحد منهم إلا ما شاء الله في جنازة نفسه وفي حاله إذا حمل عليها ولا سبب لهذه الغفلة إلا قسوة القلوب بكثرة المعاصي والذنوب حتى نسينا الله تعالى واليوم الآخر والأهوال التي بين أيدينا فصرنا نلهو ونغفل ونشتغل بما لا يعنينا فنسأل الله تعالى اليقظة من هذه الغفلة فإن أحسن أحوال الحاضرين على الجنائز بكاؤهم على الميت ولو عقلوا لبكوا على أنفسهم لا على الميت
87:7.english: And not one of them reflects except what Allah wills (إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ) regarding his own funeral procession and his state when carried upon it. And there is no cause for this heedlessness except the hardening of the Hearts (Qulūb) due to the abundance of sins and transgressions, until we have forgotten Allah the Exalted and the Last Day and the terrors that are before us, so we have become diverted, heedless, and occupied with what does not concern us. So we ask Allah the Exalted for awakening from this heedlessness, for the best state of those present at funerals is their weeping over the deceased; if they had intellect, they would weep over themselves, not over the deceased.
87:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

87:7.arabic: فهذه علامات المرض وبهذا يعرف أن القلوب كلها مريضة إلا ما شاء الله إلا أن من الأمراض ما لا يعرفها صاحبها، ومرض القلب مما لا يعرفه صاحبه، فلذلك يغفل عنه.
87:7.english: These are the signs of illness, and through this it is known that all hearts are sick except what Allah wills (إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ), except that among illnesses are those that their owner does not recognize, and the sickness of the heart is from what its owner does not recognize, therefore he is heedless of it.
87:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

87:16.arabic: وأبصار أكثر الخلق ضعيفة مقصورة على العاجلة لا يمتد نورها إلى مشاهدة العواقب، ولذلك قال تعالى "بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا والآخرة خير وأبقى" وقال عز وجل "كلا بل تحبون العاجلة، وتذرون الآخرة" فمن هذا حده فينبغي أن يعالج قلبه من حب الجاه بالعلم بالآفات العاجلة، وهو أن يتفكر في الأخطار التي يستهدف لها أرباب الجاه في الدنيا، فإن كل ذي جاه محسود ومقصود بالإيذاء وخائف على الدوام على جاهه ومحترز من أن تتغير منزلته في القلوب، والقلوب أشد تغيراً من القدر في غليانها وهي مترددة بين الإقبال والإعراض، فكل ما يبن
87:16.english: And the vision (Basar) of most of creation is weak, restricted to the immediate (Al-'Ajilah) and does not extend its light to witnessing the consequences (Al-'Awaqib). Therefore, the Exalted said: 'Rather, you prefer the life of this world (Al-Hayah Al-Dunya), while the Hereafter (Al-Akhirah) is better and more lasting.' And the Mighty and Majestic said: 'No! But you love the immediate (Al-'Ajilah) and neglect the Hereafter (Al-Akhirah).' So whoever is at this limit, it is necessary to treat his heart (Qalb) from the love of status (Al-Jah) with knowledge of the immediate harms (Al-Afat Al-'Ajilah), which is to reflect on the dangers that the possessors of status (Arbab Al-Jah) are targeted with in this world (Al-Dunya). For every possessor of status is envied, intended for harm, and constantly fearful for his status and cautious lest his standing in the hearts (Qulub) changes. And hearts are more changeable than a boiling pot, wavering between acceptance (Al-Iqbal) and turning away (Al-I'rad). So whatever is built upon the hearts of creation resembles what is built upon the waves of the sea, for it has no stability. And preoccupation with observing hearts, preserving status, repelling the plotting of the envious, and preventing the harm of enemies—all of that is immediate sorrows (Ghumum 'Ajilah) and disturbs the pleasure of status. So in this world, its hoped-for does not compensate for its feared, let alone what is lost in the Hereafter. With this, the weak insight (Al-Basirah Al-Da'ifah) should be treated.
87:16.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

87:16.arabic: فإن إيثار الحياة الدنيا طبع غالب على الإنسان ولذلك قال الله تعالى "بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا" ثم بين أن الشر قديم في الطباع وأن ذلك مذكور في الكتب السالفة فقال "إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى صحف إبراهيم وموسى" فهذا منهاج رياضة المريد وتربيته في التدريج إلى لقاء الله تعالى.
87:16.english: For preferring the worldly life (al-hayat al-dunya) is a dominant nature (tab') upon the human being, and therefore Allah the Exalted said: 'Rather, you prefer the worldly life (al-hayat al-dunya).' Then He clarified that evil is ancient in the natures (taba'i') and that this is mentioned in the previous scriptures, so He said: 'Indeed, this is in the earlier scriptures, the scriptures of Ibrahim and Musa.' This is the methodology (minhaj) of disciplining (riyada) the seeker (murid) and his upbringing (tarbiya) in gradual progression to the meeting (liqa') of Allah the Exalted.
87:16.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

87:18.arabic: فإن إيثار الحياة الدنيا طبع غالب على الإنسان ولذلك قال الله تعالى "بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا" ثم بين أن الشر قديم في الطباع وأن ذلك مذكور في الكتب السالفة فقال "إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى صحف إبراهيم وموسى" فهذا منهاج رياضة المريد وتربيته في التدريج إلى لقاء الله تعالى.
87:18.english: For preferring the worldly life (Hayat al-Dunya) is a dominant nature (Tab') upon the human being, and therefore Allah the Exalted said: "Rather, you prefer the worldly life." Then He clarified that evil (Sharr) is ancient in the natures (Taba'i') and that this is mentioned in the previous scriptures (Kutub Salifa), so He said: "Indeed, this is in the former scriptures (Suhuf al-Ula), the scriptures of Ibrahim and Musa." This is the methodology (Manhaj) of disciplining (Riyada) the seeker (Murid) and his upbringing (Tarbiya) in gradual progression to the meeting (Liqa') with Allah the Exalted.
87:18.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

88:4.arabic: ثم انظر إلى طعامهم وهو الزقوم كما قال الله تعالى: ﴿ ثم إنكم إيها الضالون المكذبون لآكلون من شجر من زقوم فمالئون منها البطون فشاربون عليه من الحميم فشاربون شرب الهيم ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ إنها شجرة تخرج فى أصل الجحيم طلعها كأنه رءوس الشياطين فإنهم لآكلون منها فمالئون منها البطون ثم إن لهم عليها لشوبا من حميم ثم إن مرجعهم لإلى الجحيم ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ تصلى نارا حامية تسقى من عين آنية ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ إن لدينا أنكالا وجحيما وطعاما ذا غصة وعذابا أليما ﴾ {} وقال ابن عباس قال رسول الله ﭬ: (لو أن قطرة
88:4.english: Then look at their food, which is the Zaqqum (Zaqqum) as Allah the Exalted said: 'Then indeed you, O those astray (al-Dalun) and deniers (al-Mukadhibun), will eat from a tree of Zaqqum (Zaqqum) and fill your bellies from it, then drink on top of it from boiling water (al-Hamim), drinking like thirsty camels (al-Him).' And He the Exalted said: 'Indeed it is a tree that emerges from the base of Hell (al-Jahim), its fruit as if it were heads of devils (al-Shayatin). Then indeed they will eat from it and fill their bellies from it, then indeed for them upon it is a mixture of boiling water (Hamim), then indeed their return is to Hell (al-Jahim).' And He the Exalted said: 'They will roast (Tasla) in a blazing fire (Naran Hamiyah), given drink from a boiling spring (Aynin Aniyah).' And He the Exalted said: 'Indeed with Us are shackles (Ankalan) and Hell (Jahiman) and food with choking (Ghusatan) and painful punishment (Adhaban Aliman).' And Ibn Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'If a drop of Zaqqum (Zaqqum) were dripped into the seas of the world, it would corrupt the livelihoods of the people of the world, so how about one whose food is that?'
88:4.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

88:7.arabic: وقال أبو الدرداء قال رسول الله ﭬ: (يلقى على أهل النار الجوع حتى يعدل ما هم فيه من العذاب فيستغيثون بالطعام فيغاثون بطعام من ضريع لا يسمن ولا يغنى من جوع ويستغيثون بالطعام فيغاثون بطعام ذى غصة فيذكرون كما كانوا يجيزون الغصص فى الدنيا بشراب فيستغيثون بشراب فيرفع إليهم الحميم بكلاليب الحديد فإذا دنت من وجوههم شوت وجوههم فإذا دخل الشراب بطونهم قطع ما فى بطونهم فيقولون ادعوا خزنة جهنم قال فيدعون خزنة جهنم أن ادعوا ربكم يخفف عنا يوما من العذاب فيقولون أو لم تك تأتيكم رسلكم بالبينات قالوا بلى قالوا فاد
88:7.english: And Abu al-Darda' said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Hunger is cast upon the people of the Fire until it equals what they are in of punishment, so they cry out for food and are given food from dhari' (a thorny, bitter plant) that does not fatten nor satisfy from hunger (la yusminu wa la yughni min ju'in). And they cry out for food and are given food that causes choking, so they remember how they used to pass choking in the world with drink, so they cry out for drink and boiling water is raised to them with iron hooks. When it approaches their faces, it scorches their faces, and when the drink enters their bellies, it cuts what is in their bellies. So they say: Call the keepers of Hell. He said: So they call the keepers of Hell to call your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment. They say: Did not your messengers come to you with clear proofs? They say: Yes. They say: So call, and the call of the disbelievers is only in error. He said: So they say: Call Malik. So they call and say: O Malik, let our Lord decide for us. He said: So He answers them: You are abiding.'
88:7.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

88:14.arabic: ثم يطأطىء رأسه فإذا أزواجه ﴿ وأكواب موضوعة ونمارق مصفوفة وزرابى مبثوثة ﴾ {} ثم اتكأ فقال: ﴿ الحمد لله الذي هدانا لهذا وما كنا لنهتدي لو لا أن هدانا الله ﴾ {} ثم ينادى مناد تحيون فلا تموتون أبدا وتقيمون فلا تظعنون أبدا وتصحون فلا تمرضون أبدا)
88:14.english: Then he lowers his head, and behold his spouses (wives) and cups placed (وَأَكْوَابٌ مَوْضُوعَةٌ) and cushions arranged and carpets spread out. Then he reclined and said: 'All praise is for Allah who has guided us to this, and we would not have been guided if Allah had not guided us.' Then a caller calls out: 'You live and never die, you settle and never depart, you are healthy and never become sick.'
88:14.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Book of Repentance'

89:6.arabic: وهذه القصص وردت في القرآن لتعرف بها سنة الله في عباده الذي خلوا من قبل، فما في القرآن شيء إلا وهو هدى ونور وتعرف من الله تعالى إلى خلقه، فتارة يتعرف إليهم بالتقديس فيقول: " قل هو الله أحد الله الصمد لم يلد ولم يولد ولم يكن له كفواً أحد " وتارة يتعرف إليهم بصفات جلاله فيقول: " الملك القدوس السلام المؤمن المهيمن العزيز الجبار المتكبر " وتارة يتعرف إليهم في أفعاله المخوفة والمرجوة فيتلو عليهم سنته في أعدائه وفي أنبيائه فيقول: " ألم تر كيف فعل ربك بعاد إرم ذات العماد - ألم تر كيف فعل ربك بأصحاب الفي
89:6.english: And these stories came in the Quran to know through them the Way (Sunnah) of Allah in His servants who passed before. There is nothing in the Quran except that it is guidance and light and recognition from Allah the Exalted to His creation. Sometimes He makes Himself known to them through Sanctification (Taqdis) when He says: "Say: He is Allah, the One, Allah the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born, nor is there to Him any equivalent." And sometimes He makes Himself known to them through His attributes of Majesty (Jalal) when He says: "The Sovereign, the Holy, the Peace, the Faithful, the Overseer, the Exalted in Might, the Compeller, the Superior." And sometimes He makes Himself known to them in His fearful and hoped-for actions, and He recites to them His Way (Sunnah) with His enemies and with His prophets when He says: "Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with 'Aad - Iram of the pillars? Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?"
89:6.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

89:15.arabic: وكان أرباب البصائر إذا أقبلت عليهم الدنيا حزنوا وقالوا: ذنب عجلت عقوبته ورأوا ذلك علامة المقت والإهمال، وإذا أقبل عليهم الفقر قالوا: مرحباً بشعار الصالحين. والمغرور إذا أقبلت عليه الدنيا ظن أنها كرامة من الله، وإذا صرفت عنه ظن أنها هوان، كما أخبر الله تعالى عنه إذ قال "فأما الإنسان إذا ما ابتلاه ربه فأكرمه ونعمه فيقول ربي أكرمن وأما إذا ما ابتلاه فقدر عليه رزقه فيقول ربي أهانن" فأجاب الله عن ذلك "كلا" أي ليس كما قال إنما هو ابتلاء نعوذ بالله من شر البلاء ونسأل الله التثبيت، فبين أن ذلك غرور. قال
89:15.english: And the possessors of insight (أرباب البصائر) when the worldly life (الدنيا) approached them, they would grieve and say: 'A sin whose punishment has been hastened,' and they saw that as a sign of contempt and neglect. And when poverty approached them, they would say: 'Welcome to the emblem of the righteous.' And the deluded one (المغرور) when the worldly life approaches him, he thinks it is an honor from Allah, and when it is diverted from him, he thinks it is humiliation, as Allah the Exalted informed about him when He said: 'So as for man when his Lord tests him and honors him and bestows favor upon him, he says: My Lord has honored me. And as for when He tests him and restricts his provision, he says: My Lord has humiliated me.' So Allah responded to that with 'No' (كلا), meaning it is not as he said; rather it is a test—we seek refuge in Allah from the evil of the test and we ask Allah for steadfastness—thus He clarified that this is delusion. Al-Hasan said: He denied them both with His saying 'No' (كلا), saying: 'This is not My honoring, nor is this My humiliation. But the honored one is whom I have honored with My obedience, whether rich or poor, and the humiliated one is whom I have humiliated with My disobedience, whether rich or poor.'
89:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

89:27.arabic: المعنى الثاني هي اللطيفة التي ذكرناها التي هي الإنسان بالحقيقة وهي نفس الإنسان وذاته ولكنها توصف بأوصاف مختلفة بحسب اختلاف أحوالها فإذا سكنت تحت الأمر وزايلها الاضطراب بسبب معارضة الشهوات سميت النفس المطمئنة قال الله تعالى في مثلها يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة ارجعي إلى ربك راضية مرضية والنفس بالمعنى الأول لا يتصور رجوعها إلى الله تعالى فإنها مبعدة عن الله وهي من حزب الشيطان وإذا لم يتم سكونها ولكنها صارت مدافعة للنفس الشهوانية ومعترضة عليها سميت النفس اللوامة لأنها تلوم صاحبها عند تقصيره في عبادة مو
89:27.english: The second meaning is the subtle essence (Lafīfa) that we mentioned, which is the human being in reality, and it is the soul (Nafs) of the human being and their essence (Dhāt). However, it is described with different attributes according to the variation of its states. If it settles under the command (Amr) and disturbance leaves it due to opposing desires (Shahawāt), it is called the tranquil soul (Nafs al-Muṭmaʾinna). Allah the Exalted said regarding its example: 'O tranquil soul (Nafs al-Muṭmaʾinna), return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing.' And the soul (Nafs) in the first meaning cannot be conceived as returning to Allah the Exalted, for it is distanced from Allah and is from the party of Satan (Shayṭān). If its settling is not complete, but it becomes resistant to the desiring soul (Nafs al-Shahwāniyya) and objects to it, it is called the blaming soul (Nafs al-Lawwāma) because it blames its owner when they fall short in worshiping their Master (Mawlā). Allah the Exalted said: 'And I swear by the blaming soul (Nafs al-Lawwāma).' And if it abandons objection and submits and obeys the demands of desires (Shahawāt) and the incitements of Satan (Shayṭān), it is called the soul that commands to evil (Nafs al-Ammāra bi-l-Sūʾ). Allah the Exalted said, informing about Joseph, peace be upon him: 'Or the wife of al-ʿAzīz, and I do not acquit myself. Indeed, the soul (Nafs) commands to evil (Ammāra bi-l-Sūʾ).' And it may be permissible to say that what is intended by 'commands to evil' is the soul (Nafs) in the first meaning. Therefore, the soul (Nafs) in the first meaning is blameworthy to the utmost blame, and in the second meaning it is praiseworthy because it is the soul (Nafs) of the human being, meaning their essence (Dhāt) and reality (Ḥaqīqa), knowing Allah the Exalted and all other known things.
89:27.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

89:27.arabic: الواصلون الى هذه الرتبة هم الأقلون فلا جرم هم الصديقون المقربون الذين قالوا ربنا الله ثم استقاموا فهؤلاء لازموا الطريق المستقيم واستووا على الصراط القويم واطمأنت نفوسهم على مقتضى باعث الدين وإياهم ينادي المنادي ﴿ يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة ارجعي الى ربك راضية مرضية ﴾ {}.
89:27.english: Those who reach this rank are the fewest, so they are the Truthful Ones (Siddiqun) and the Brought-Near Ones (Muqarrabun) who said, 'Our Lord is Allah,' then remained steadfast. These have adhered to the Straight Path (Tariq al-Mustaqim) and have become firmly established on the Right Path (Sirat al-Qawim), and their Souls (Nafs) have become tranquil (Mutma'innah) upon the dictates of the religious impulse. It is to them that the Caller calls: 'O tranquil Soul (Nafs al-Mutma'innah), return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing.'
89:27.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

89:27.arabic: وسمع رجل من أهل التصوف قارئا يقرأ يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة ارجعي إلى ربك راضية مرضية فاستعادها من القارىء وقال كم أقول لها ارجعي وليست ترجع وتواجد وزعق زعقة فخرجت روحه
89:27.english: And a man from the people of Sufism heard a reciter reciting: 'O you Soul (Nafs) at peace (Mutma'innah), return to your Lord (Rabb), well-pleased (Radiyah) and well-pleasing (Mardiyyah).' He asked the reciter to repeat it and said: 'How many times do I say to it: Return! And it does not return.' And he experienced spiritual ecstasy (Tawajud) and let out a cry (Za'qah), then his spirit (Ruh) departed.
89:27.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Audition and Ecstasy'

89:27.arabic: وهو القلب الذي أقبل الله عز وجل بوجهه عليه وهو القلب المطمئن المراد بقوله تعالى ألا بذكر الله تطمئن القلوب وبقوله عز وجل يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة
89:27.english: And it is the Heart (Qalb) that Allah the Exalted has turned His Face toward, and it is the Tranquil Heart (Qalb al-Mutma'inn) intended by His saying the Exalted: 'Indeed, in the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah do hearts find tranquility' and by His saying the Exalted: 'O you Tranquil Soul (Nafs al-Mutma'innah)'.
89:27.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

89:28.arabic: ولما كانت العقول التى بها يحصل التكليف وبها تدرك مصالح الدنيا عقولا قاصرة عن ملاحظة كنه هذا الأمر لم يأذن الله تعالى لرسول ﭬ أن يتحدث عنه بل أمره أن يكلم الناس على قدر عقولهم ولم يذكر الله تعالى في كتابه من حقيقة هذا الأمر شيئا ولكن ذكر نسبته وفعله ولم يذكر ذاته أما نسبته ففى قوله تعالى: ﴿ من أمر ربى ﴾ {} وأما فعله فقد ذكر في قوله تعالى: ﴿ ياأيها النفس المطمئنة ارجعى إلى ربك راضية مرضية فادخلى في عبادى وادخلى جنتى ﴾ {} ولنرجع الآن إلى الغرض فإن المقصود ذكر نعم الله تعالى في الأكل فقد ذكرنا بعض ن
89:28.english: And since the intellects (Aql) through which religious obligation (Taklif) occurs and through which worldly benefits are perceived are intellects deficient in observing the essence (Kunh) of this matter, Allah the Exalted did not permit His Messenger (peace be upon him) to speak about it, rather He commanded him to speak to people according to the capacity of their intellects. And Allah the Exalted did not mention in His Book anything of the reality (Haqiqah) of this matter, but He mentioned its attribution (Nisbah) and its action (Fi'l), and did not mention its essence (Dhat). As for its attribution, it is in His saying the Exalted: 'From the command of my Lord' (Quran 17:85). And as for its action, it has been mentioned in His saying the Exalted: 'O Soul (Nafs) at peace (Mutma'innah), return to your Lord, well-pleased (Radiyah) and well-pleasing (Mardhiyyah). Then enter among My servants, and enter My Paradise' (Quran 89:27-30). And let us now return to the purpose, for the intended is mentioning the blessings (Ni'am) of Allah the Exalted in eating, and we have mentioned some of the blessings of Allah the Exalted in the instruments of eating.
89:28.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

90:8.arabic: فانظر إلى نعمة الله عليه كيف نقله من تلك الذلة والقلة والخسة والقذارة إلى هذه الرفعة والكرامة فصار موجوداً بعد العدم وحياً بعد الموت وناطقاً بعد البكم وبصيراً بعد العمى وقوياً بعد الضعف وعالماً بعد الجهل ومهدياً بعد الضلال وقادراً بعد العجز وغنيّاً بعد الفقر؟ فكان في ذاته لا شيء وأي شيء أخس من لا شيء؟ وأي قلة أقل من العدم المحض؟ ثم صار بالله شيئاً. وإنما خلقه من التراب الذليل الذي يوطأ بالأقدام والنطفة القذرة بعد العدم المحض أيضاً ليعرفه خسة ذاته فيعرف به نفسه، وإنما أكمل النعمة عليه ليعرف بها ر
90:8.english: Look at the blessing (Ni'mah) of Allah upon him, how He transferred him from that humiliation (Dhullah) and scarcity (Qillah) and baseness (Khasah) and filth (Qadharah) to this elevation (Rif'ah) and honor (Karāmah), so he became existent after non-existence, alive after death, speaking after muteness, seeing after blindness, strong after weakness, knowing after ignorance, guided after misguidance, capable after incapacity, and rich after poverty? He was in his essence nothing, and what thing is baser than nothing? And what scarcity is less than pure non-existence? Then he became through Allah something. And He only created him from the lowly (Dhaleel) dust that is trodden under feet and the filthy (Qadirah) sperm-drop after pure non-existence also to make him know the baseness of his essence so he may know himself by it, and He only perfected the blessing (Ni'mah) upon him so he may know by it his Lord and know by it His greatness and majesty and that grandeur (Kibriyā') is not fitting except for Him, exalted and sublime. And for that reason, He bestowed favor upon him, saying: "Have We not made for him two eyes, and a tongue, and two lips? And guided him to the two paths?" And He made known his baseness first, saying: "Was he not a sperm-drop from semen emitted? Then he became a clinging clot." Then He mentioned His favor upon him, saying: "Then He created and proportioned, and made from him the two sexes, male and female," so that his existence may continue through reproduction as his existence first occurred through origination.
90:8.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Condemnation of Pride and Conceit'

91:1.arabic: ثم انظر كيف عظم الله أمر السموات والنجوم فى كتابه فما من سورة إلا وتشتمل على تفخيمها فى مواضع وكم من قسم فى القرآن بها كقوله تعالى والسماء ذات البروج والسماء والطارق والسماء ذات الحبك والسماء وما بناها وكقوله تعالى والشمس وضحاها والقمر إذا تلاها وكقوله تعالى فلا أقسم بالخنس الجوار الكنس وقوله تعالى والنجم إذا هوى فلا أقسم بمواقع النجوم وإنه لقسم لو تعلمون عظيم فقد علمت أن عجائب النطفة القذرة عجز عن معرفتها الأولون والآخرون وما أقسم الله بها فما ظنك بما اقسم الله تعالى به وأحال الأرزاق عليه وأضاف
91:1.english: Then look at how Allah has magnified the matter of the heavens and the stars in His Book, for there is no chapter except that it contains their glorification in places, and how many oaths in the Quran are by them, such as His saying, the Exalted: 'By the sky containing constellations' and 'By the sky and the night visitor' and 'By the sky with its pathways' and 'By the sky and He who built it', and such as His saying, the Exalted: 'By the sun and its brightness and the moon when it follows it', and such as His saying, the Exalted: 'So I swear by the retreating stars, those that run and hide', and His saying, the Exalted: 'By the star when it descends, I swear by the positions of the stars - and indeed, it is an oath, if you only knew, great'. You have known that the wonders of the filthy drop (sperm) have been beyond the knowledge of the first and the last, and Allah did not swear by it, so what do you think of that by which Allah, the Exalted, has sworn and referred the provisions (Arzaq) to it and attributed them to it? He said, the Exalted: 'And in the sky is your provision and what you are promised', and He praised those who contemplate (Mutafakkirin) in it, saying: 'And they contemplate (Yatafakkarun) in the creation of the heavens and the earth'.
91:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Contemplation'

91:9.arabic: فإن معرفة لغة العرب تعين على معرفة تفسير القرآن، ومعرفة التفسير تعين على معرفة ما في القرآن من كيفية العبادات والأعمال التي تفيد تزكية النفس، ومعرفة طريق تزكية النفس تفيد استعداد النفس لقبول الهدايا إلى معرفة الله سبحانه وتعالى كما قال تعالى "قد أفلح من زكاها" وقال عز وجل "والذين جاهدوا فينا لنهدينهم سبلنا" فتكون جملة هذه المعارف كالوسائل إلى تحقيق معرفة الله تعالى، وإنما الكمال في معرفة الله ومعرفة صفاته وأفعاله، وينطوي فيه جميع المعارف المحيطة بالموجودات إذ الموجودات كلها من أفعاله، فمن عرفها
91:9.english: For knowledge of the language of the Arabs assists in knowing the interpretation (Tafsir) of the Quran, and knowledge of the interpretation assists in knowing what is in the Quran regarding the manner of acts of worship and works that benefit the purification (Tazkiyah) of the Soul (Nafs), and knowledge of the path of purifying the Soul (Nafs) benefits the preparedness of the Soul (Nafs) to accept the gifts leading to knowledge of Allah, the Exalted and Majestic, as He, the Exalted, said: "Indeed, he has succeeded who purifies it (Zakkaha)" and He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: "And those who strive in Us, We will surely guide them to Our ways." So the totality of these knowledges becomes like the means to the realization of knowledge of Allah, the Exalted. And indeed, perfection is in knowledge of Allah and knowledge of His attributes and His actions, and it encompasses all knowledges surrounding the existents, since all existents are from His actions. So whoever knows them from the perspective that they are the action of Allah, the Exalted, and from the perspective of their connection to power (Qudrah) and will (Iradah) and wisdom (Hikmah), then that is from the completion of knowledge of Allah, the Exalted. And this is the ruling of the perfection of knowledge we have mentioned, even if it is not fitting for the rulings of ignorance (Jahl) and ostentation (Riya'), but we have presented it to complete the categories of perfection.
91:9.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

91:9.arabic: وإنما مراد الطاعات وأعمال الجوارح كلها تصفية القلب وتزكيته وجلاؤه قد أفلح من زكاها ومراد تزكيته حصول أنوار الإيمان فيه أعني إشراق نور المعرفة وهو المراد بقوله تعالى فمن يرد الله أن يهديه يشرح صدره للإسلام أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام فهو على نور من ربه نعم هذا التجلي وهذا الإيمان له ثلاث مراتب المرتبة الأولى إيمان العوام وهو إيمان التقليد المحض والثانية إيمان المتكلمين وهو ممزوج بنوع استدلال ودرجته قريبة من درجة إيمان العوام والثالثة إيمان العارفين وهو المشاهد بنور اليقين ونبين لك هذه المراتب بمثا
91:9.english: And indeed, the purpose of acts of obedience and works of the limbs all is the purification of the Heart (Qalb) and its purification (tazkiyah) and its polishing. 'Indeed, he has succeeded who purifies it (Qad aflaha man zakkaha).' And the meaning of its purification is the attainment of the lights of Faith (Iman) in it, I mean the shining of the light of knowledge (ma'rifah), and that is what is intended by His saying, the Exalted: 'So whoever Allah wants to guide - He expands his breast to Islam. And whoever He wants to send astray - He makes his breast tight and constricted as though he were climbing into the sky. Thus does Allah place defilement upon those who do not believe. And this is the path of your Lord, straight. We have detailed the verses for a people who remember.' (Quran 6:125-126) 'So is one whose breast Allah has expanded to [accept] Islam and he is upon a light from his Lord [like one whose heart rejects it]?' (Quran 39:22) Yes, this manifestation and this Faith (Iman) has three levels: The first level is the faith of the common people, and it is faith of pure imitation (taqlid). The second is the faith of the theologians (mutakallimun), and it is mixed with a kind of reasoning, and its degree is close to the degree of the faith of the common people. The third is the faith of the knowers (arifun), and it is witnessed with the light of certainty (yaqin). And we explain to you these levels with an example, which is that your belief in Zayd being, for example, in the house has three degrees: The first is that one whom you have experienced as truthful informs you, and you do not know him to lie nor suspect him in speech, so your Heart (Qalb) finds tranquility in him and is reassured by his report merely by hearing. And this faith is by mere imitation, and it is like the faith of the common people, for when they reached the age of discernment, they heard from their fathers and mothers the existence of Allah, the Exalted, and His knowledge, His will, His power, and His other attributes, and the sending of the messengers and their truthfulness and what they brought, and as they heard it, they accepted it, adhered to it, and were reassured by it, and it did not occur to their minds to oppose what was said to them due to their good opinion of their fathers, mothers, and teachers. And this faith is the cause of salvation in the Hereafter, and its people are from the foremost ranks of the companions of the right hand, and it is not...
91:9.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

91:9.arabic: وهكذا الفقيه الذي أحكم علم الطاعات ولم يعملها وأحكم علم المعاصي ولم يجتنبها وأحكم علم الأخلاق المذمومة وما زكى نفسه منها وأحكم على الأخلاق المحمودة ولم يتصف بها فهو مغرور، إذ قال تعالى "قد افلح من زكاها" ولم يقل قد أفلح من تعلم كيفية تزكيتها وكتب علم ذلك وعلمه الناس! وعند هذا يقول له الشيطان: لا يغرنك هذا المثال فإن العلم بالدواء لا يزيل المرض، وإنما مطلبك القرب من الله وثوابه والعلم يجلب الثواب، ويتلو عليه الأخبار الواردة في فضل العلم. فإن كان المسكين معتوهاً مغروراً وافق ذلك مراده وهواه فاطمأن
91:9.english: And thus the jurist who has mastered knowledge of acts of obedience (Taa'aat) and did not perform them, and mastered knowledge of sins (Ma'aasi) and did not avoid them, and mastered knowledge of blameworthy character traits (Akhlāq Madhmūmah) and did not purify his Soul (Nafs) from them, and mastered knowledge of praiseworthy character traits (Akhlāq Mahmūdah) and did not embody them—he is deluded, for Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, he succeeds who purifies it (Zakkāhā)' and He did not say: Indeed, he succeeds who learns how to purify it and writes knowledge of that and teaches it to people! At this point, Satan says to him: Do not let this example delude you, for knowledge of the medicine does not remove the illness; rather, your objective is nearness to Allah and His reward, and knowledge brings reward, and he recites to him the reports that have come regarding the virtue of knowledge. If the wretched one is foolish and deluded, he agrees with that according to his desire and inclination, so he becomes content with it and neglects action; but if he is intelligent, he says to Satan: Do you remind me of the virtues of the scholar and make me forget what has come regarding the wicked scholar who does not act upon his knowledge, such as His saying the Exalted: 'His likeness is that of a dog' and His saying the Exalted: 'The likeness of those who were entrusted with the Torah and then did not uphold it is that of a donkey carrying books'—so what disgrace is greater than being likened to a dog and a donkey? And He ﭬ said: 'Whoever increases in knowledge and does not increase in guidance does not increase from Allah except in distance.' And He also said: 'The scholar is thrown into the Fire, and his intestines spill out, and he circles with them in the Fire as the donkey circles in the mill.' And like His saying, upon him be prayers and peace: 'The worst of people are the evil scholars.' And the saying of Abu al-Darda': Woe to the one who does not know once—and if Allah willed, He would have taught him—and woe to the one who knows and does not act seven times, meaning that knowledge is a proof against him, for it is said to him: What have you done with what you knew, and how have you fulfilled gratitude to Allah?'
91:9.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

91:9.arabic: اعلم أن مطالب المتعاملين في التجارات المشتركين في البضائع عند المحاسبة سلامة الربح وكما أن التاجر يستعين بشريكه فيسلم إليه المال حتى يتجر ثم يحاسبه فكذلك العقل هو التاجر في طريق الآخرة وإنما مطالبة وربحه تزكية النفس لأن بذلك فلاحها قال الله تعالى قد أفلح من زكاها وقد خاب من دساها وإنما فلاحها بالأعمال الصالحة والعقل يستعين بالنفس في هذه التجارة إذ يستعملها ويستسخرها فيما يزكيها كما يستعين التاجر بشريكه وغلامه الذي يتجر في ماله
91:9.english: Know that the demand of partners dealing in trade and sharing in goods during accounting is the safety of profit. And just as the merchant seeks assistance from his partner by entrusting him with the capital so that he may trade, then accounts with him, similarly the Intellect (Al-'Aql) is the merchant on the path of the Hereafter. Its demand and profit is the Purification (Tazkiyah) of the Soul (Nafs) because through that is its success. Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, he has succeeded who purifies it (Qad aflaha man zakkaha), and he has failed who corrupts it (Wa qad khaba man dassaha).' And its success is only through righteous deeds. And the Intellect (Al-'Aql) seeks assistance from the Soul (Nafs) in this trade, as it employs it and subjugates it in that which purifies it, just as the merchant seeks assistance from his partner and his servant who trades with his wealth.
91:9.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

91:9.arabic: فمعالجتها هو المراد بقوله تعالى "قد أفلح من زكاها" وإهمالها هو المراد بقوله "وقد خاب من دساها" ونحن نشير في هذا الكتاب إلى جمل من أمراض القلوب وكيفية القول في معالجتها على الجملة من غير تفصيل علاج خصوص الأمراض، فإن ذلك يأتي في بقية الكتب من هذا الربع وغرضنا الآن النظر الكلي في تهذيب الأخلاق وتمهيد منهاجها.
91:9.english: Treating them is what is intended by His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, he has succeeded who purifies it (Zakka-ha)' and neglecting them is what is intended by His saying: 'And indeed, he has failed who corrupts it (Dassa-ha)'. And we point in this book to a summary of the diseases of the Hearts (Qulub) and how to speak about treating them in summary without detailing the treatment of specific diseases, for that will come in the remaining books of this quarter, and our aim now is the comprehensive view in refining the morals and establishing its methodology.
91:9.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

91:10.arabic: فمعالجتها هو المراد بقوله تعالى "قد أفلح من زكاها" وإهمالها هو المراد بقوله "وقد خاب من دساها" ونحن نشير في هذا الكتاب إلى جمل من أمراض القلوب وكيفية القول في معالجتها على الجملة من غير تفصيل علاج خصوص الأمراض، فإن ذلك يأتي في بقية الكتب من هذا الربع وغرضنا الآن النظر الكلي في تهذيب الأخلاق وتمهيد منهاجها.
91:10.english: Treating them is what is intended by His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, he succeeds who purifies it (Zakaha)' and neglecting them is what is intended by His saying: 'And indeed, he fails who corrupts it (Dassaha)'. And we point in this book to a summary of the diseases of the Hearts (Qulub) and the manner of speech about treating them in summary without detailing the treatment of specific diseases, for that will come in the remaining books of this quarter, and our purpose now is the comprehensive consideration in refining the morals and establishing its methodology.
91:10.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

92:5.arabic: وينقسم الصبر أيضا باعتبار اليسر والعسر إلى ما يشق على النفس فلا يمكن الدوام عليه إلا بجهد جهيد وتعب شديد ويسمى ذلك تصبرا وإلى ما يكون من غير شدة تعب بل يحصل بأدنى تحامل على النفس ويخص ذلك باسم الصبر وإذا دامت التقوى وقوى التصديق بما في العاقبة من الحسنى تيسر الصبر ولذلك قال تعالى: ﴿ فأما من أعطى واتقى وصدق بالحسنى فسنيسره لليسرى ﴾ {} ومثال هذه القسمة قدرة المصارع على غيره فإن الرجل القوي يقدر على أن يصرع الضعيف بأدنى حملة وأيسر قوة بحيث لا يلقاه في مصارعته إعياء ولا لغوب ولا تضطرب فيه نفسه ولا ي
92:5.english: And patience (الصبر) is also divided according to ease and hardship into that which is difficult for the Soul (النفس) such that continuity upon it is not possible except with intense effort and severe exertion, and that is called 'perseverance' (تصبرا), and into that which occurs without severity of exertion but is attained with the slightest exertion upon the Soul (النفس), and that is specifically named 'patience' (الصبر). And when God-consciousness (التقوى) persists and the affirmation (التصديق) of what is in the outcome from the best reward (الحسنى) strengthens, patience (الصبر) becomes facilitated. And for that reason, Allah the Exalted said: 'So as for he who gives and is God-conscious (واتقى) and affirms the best reward (الحسنى), We will facilitate for him the ease (لليسرى).' And an example of this division is the ability of the wrestler over his opponent, for the strong man is able to throw down the weak with the slightest attack and easiest strength such that he does not encounter in his wrestling fatigue nor weariness, nor does his Soul (النفس) become agitated nor bewildered, and he is not able to throw down the strong except with exertion and increased effort and sweat of the brow. Thus is the wrestling between the motivator of religion (الدين) and the motivator of desire (الهوى), for it is in truth a struggle between the soldiers of the angels and the soldiers of the devils. Whenever the desires (الشهوات) submit and are suppressed, and the motivator of religion (الدين) dominates and takes control, and patience (الصبر) becomes facilitated through prolonged persistence, that bequeaths the station of contentment (الرضا) as will come in the Book of Contentment, so contentment (الرضا) is higher than patience (الصبر).
92:5.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

92:5.arabic: وهذه التقلبات وعجائب صنع الله تعالى في تقلبها من حيث لا تهدي إليه المعرفة لا يعرفها إلا المراقبون والمراعون لأحوالهم مع الله تعالى والقلوب في الثبات على الخير والشر والتردد بينهما ثلاثة قلب عمر بالتقوى وزكا بالرياضة وطهر عن خبائث الأخلاق تنقدح فيه خواطر الخير من خزائن الغيب ومداخل الملكوت فينصرف العقل إلى التفكر فيما خطر له ليعرف دقائق الخير فيه ويطلع على أسرار فوائده فينكشف له بنور البصيرة وجهه فيحكم بأنه لا بد من فعله فيستحثه عليه ويدعوه إلى العمل به وينظر الملك إلى القلب فيجده طيبا في جوهره ط
92:5.english: And these fluctuations and wonders of the creation of God the Exalted in their fluctuation from where knowledge does not guide to it, none know them except the observers and those who watch over their states with God the Exalted. And the hearts in steadfastness upon the good and the evil and the hesitation between them are three: a heart that has been inhabited by piety (Taqwa) and purified by spiritual discipline (Riyada) and cleansed from the impurities of character traits (Akhlaq), sparks of good from the treasuries of the unseen (Ghayb) and the entrances of the dominion (Malakut) ignite in it, so the intellect (Aql) turns to reflecting upon what has occurred to it to know the subtleties of the good in it and to become aware of the secrets of its benefits, so its aspect is unveiled to it by the light of insight (Basira), so it judges that it must be done, so it urges it upon it and calls it to act by it. And the angel (Malak) looks at the heart and finds it good in its essence, pure by its piety (Taqwa), illuminated by the radiance of the intellect (Aql), inhabited by the lights of knowledge (Ma'rifa), so he sees it suitable to be for him a dwelling and a descent, so at that time he supplies it with unseen troops and guides it to other goodnesses until good leads to good, and likewise perpetually, and his supply with encouragement to good and facilitation of the matter for it does not cease. And to it is the allusion by His saying the Exalted: 'So as for he who gave and was pious (Taqwa) and believed in the best, We will ease him to the ease.' And in such a heart shines the light of the lamp from the niche of lordship (Rububiyya) until the hidden polytheism (Shirk) which is more hidden than the crawling of the black ant on a dark night is not concealed in it, so nothing hidden is concealed from this light, and nothing from the tricks of Satan (Shaytan) deceives it, rather Satan stands and inspires adorned speech as delusion, so it does not pay attention to it. And this heart after its purification from the destructive things becomes, in proximity, inhabited by the saving things which we will mention: gratitude (Shukr), patience (Sabr), fear (Khawf), hope (Raja'), poverty (Faqr), asceticism (Zuhd), love (Mahabbah), contentment (Rida'), longing (Shawq), reliance (Tawakkul), reflection (Tafakkur), self-accounting (Muhasabah), and others. And it is the heart upon which God the Mighty and Majestic has turned His face, and it is the contented heart intended by His saying the Exalted: 'Unquestionably, by the remembrance (Dhikr) of God hearts are contented,' and by His saying the Mighty and Majestic: 'O contented soul (Nafs).'
92:5.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

92:14.arabic: وقال تعالى: ﴿ فأنذرتكم نارا تلظى لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى الذي كذب وتولى ﴾{}
92:14.english: And He, the Exalted, said: 'So I have warned you of a Fire that blazes fiercely; none shall burn in it except the most wretched one who denied and turned away.'
92:14.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Fear and Hope'

92:15.arabic: فإن قلت: فما شبهة المعتزلة والمرجئة وما حجة بطلان قولهم. فأقول شبهتهم عمومات القرآن أما المرجئة فقالوا لا يدخل المؤمن النار وإن أتي بكل المعاصي لقوله عز وجل: ﴿ فمن يؤمن بربه فلا يخاف بخسا ولا رهقا ﴾ {} ولقوله سبحانه وتعالى: ﴿ والذين آمنوا بالله ورسله أولئك هم الصديقون ﴾ {} الآية ولقوله تعالى: ﴿ كلما ألقي فيها فوج سألهم خزنتها. ﴾ {} إلى قوله: ﴿ فكذبنا وقلنا ما نزل الله من شيء ﴾ {} فقوله كلما ألقي فيها فوج عام فينبغي أن يكون من ألقي في النار مكذبا ولقوله تعالى: ﴿ لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى الذي كذب وتول
92:15.english: If you say: What is the doubt of the Mu'tazila and Murji'a and what is the proof of the invalidity of their statement? I say: Their doubt is the generalities of the Quran. As for the Murji'a, they said: The believer does not enter the Fire even if he commits all sins, due to His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'So whoever believes in his Lord, he fears no loss nor any injustice' and due to His saying, the Blessed and Exalted: 'And those who believe in Allah and His messengers - those are the truthful ones' the verse, and due to His saying: 'Whenever a group is thrown into it, its keepers will ask them' until His saying: 'So we denied and said: Allah has not sent down anything' so His saying 'Whenever a group is thrown into it' is general, so it should be that whoever is thrown into the Fire is a denier, and due to His saying: 'None will burn in it except the most wretched, who denied and turned away' and this is restriction, affirmation, and negation, and due to His saying: 'Whoever comes with a good deed will have better than it, and they will be safe from terror that Day' so Faith (Iman) is the head of good deeds, and due to His saying: 'And Allah loves the doers of good' and He said: 'Indeed, We do not allow to be lost the reward of any who does good deeds' and they have no proof in that, for wherever Faith (Iman) is mentioned in these verses, it is intended as Faith (Iman) with action, since we have clarified that Faith (Iman) may be used and intended as Islam, which is agreement with the Heart (Qalb), speech, and action. The evidence for this interpretation is many reports about punishing the disobedient and the measures of punishment, and his saying: 'He will be brought out of the Fire whoever had in his heart an atom's weight of faith (Iman)' so how can he be brought out if he did not enter? And from the Quran, His saying: 'Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills' and the exception with will indicates division, and His saying: 'And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger - then indeed, for him is the Fire of Hell, wherein they will abide eternally' and specifying it with disbelief is arbitrary, and His saying: 'Unquestionably, the wrongdoers are in an enduring punishment' and He said: 'And whoever comes with an evil deed - their faces will be overturned into the Fire' so these generalities are in opposition to their generalities, and it is necessary to apply specification and interpretation to both sides because the reports are explicit that the disobedient are punished.
92:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Foundations of Belief'

92:15.arabic: بل قوله تعالى: ﴿ وإن منكم إلا واردها ﴾ {} كالصريح في أن ذلك لا بد منه للكل إذ لا يخلو مؤمن عن ذنب يرتكبه وقوله تعالى: ﴿ لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى الذي كذب وتولى ﴾ {} أراد به من جماعة مخصوصين أو أراد بالأشقى شخصا معينا أيضا وقوله تعالى: ﴿ كلما ألقي فيها فوج سألهم خزنتها ﴾ {} أي فوج من الكفار وتخصيص العمومات قريب ومن هذه الآية وقع للأشعري وطائفة من المتكلمين إنكار صيغ العموم وأن هذه الألفاظ يتوقف فيها إلى ظهور قرينة تدل على معناها.
92:15.english: Rather His statement, the Exalted: 'And there is not one of you except that he will enter it' is like the explicit in that this is inevitable for all since no believer is free from a sin he commits. And His statement, the Exalted: 'None will burn in it except the most wretched, who denied and turned away' intended by it from a specific group or intended by 'the most wretched' a specific person also. And His statement, the Exalted: 'Whenever a group is thrown into it, its keepers will ask them' meaning a group from the disbelievers. And specifying the generalities is near. And from this verse occurred for Al-Ash'ari and a group of the theologians the denial of the forms of generality and that these expressions are suspended in them until the appearance of an indication that points to their meaning.
92:15.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Foundations of Belief'

93:5.arabic: وفي تفسير قوله تعالى: ﴿ ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى ﴾ {} قال لا يرضى محمد وواحد من أمته في النار. وكان أبو جعفر محمد بن علي يقول أنتم أهل العراق تقولون أرجى آية في كتاب الله عز وجل قوله: ﴿ قل يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله ﴾ {} الآية. ونحن أهل البيت نقول أرجى آية في كتاب الله تعالى قوله تعالى: ﴿ ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى ﴾ {}.
93:5.english: And in the interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: 'And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be satisfied' (Quran 93:5), it is said: Muhammad will not be satisfied while one from his community (Ummah) is in the Fire. And Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali used to say: You, the people of Iraq, say the most hopeful verse in the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is His saying: 'Say, O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah' (Quran 39:53) the verse. And we, the People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt), say the most hopeful verse in the Book of Allah, the Exalted, is His saying, the Exalted: 'And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be satisfied' (Quran 93:5).
93:5.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Fear and Hope'

93:5.arabic: وشواهد الشفاعة فى القرآن والأخبار كثيرة: قال الله تعالى: ﴿ ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى ﴾ {} روى عمرو ابن العاص: (أن رسول الله ﭬ تلا قول إبراهيم عليه السلام ﴿ رب إنهن أضللن كثيرا من الناس فمن تبعنى فإنه منى ومن عصانى فإنك غفور رحيم ﴾ {} وقول عيسى عليه السلام ﴿ إن تعذبهم فإنهم عبادك ﴾ {} ثم رفع يديه وقال: أمتى أمتى ثم بكى، فقال الله عز وجل: يا جبريل اذهب إلى محمد فسله ما يبكيك فأتاه جبريل فسأله فأخبره والله أعلم به فقال يا جبريل اذهب إلى محمد فقل له إنا سنرضيك فى أمتك ولا نسوءك[175])
93:5.english: And evidences of intercession (Shafa'ah) in the Quran and reports are many: Allah the Exalted said: 'And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be satisfied' (93:5). {} It was narrated by 'Amr ibn al-'As: (That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited the saying of Ibrahim, peace be upon him: 'My Lord, indeed they have led astray many of the people. So whoever follows me, then he is of me; and whoever disobeys me - indeed, You are Forgiving (Ghafur), Merciful (Rahim)' (14:36) {} and the saying of 'Isa, peace be upon him: 'If You should punish them - indeed they are Your servants' (5:118) {} then he raised his hands and said: My nation, my nation, then he wept. So Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: O Jibril, go to Muhammad and ask him what makes him weep. So Jibril came to him and asked him, and he informed him - and Allah knows best about it - then He said: O Jibril, go to Muhammad and say to him: Indeed, We will satisfy you concerning your nation and will not grieve you[175]).
93:5.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Book of Repentance'

93:11.arabic: الرابع أن الإظهار إقامة لسنة الشكر وقد قال تعالى: ﴿ وأما بنعمة ربك فحدث ﴾ {} والكتمان كفران النعمة وقد ذم الله عز وجل من كتم ما آتاه الله عز وجل وقرنه بالبخل فقال تعالى: ﴿ الذين يبخلون ويأمرون الناس بالبخل ويكتمون ما آتاهم الله من فضله ﴾ {} وقال ﭬ: (إذا أنعم الله على عبد نعمة أحب أن ترى نعمته عليه[57]) وأعطى رجل بعض الصالحين شيئا في السر فرفع به يده وقال: هذا من الدنيا والعلانية فيها أفضل والسر في أمور الآخرة أفضل. ولذلك قال بعضهم: إذا أعطيت في الملأ فخذ ثم اردد في السر والشكر فيه محثوث عليه. قا
93:11.english: Fourth: That manifestation is the establishment of the Sunnah (tradition) of Gratitude (Shukr), and Allah the Exalted has said: 'And as for the favor of your Lord, then speak of it (Wa-ammā bi-niʿmati rabbika fa-ḥaddith)' {} and concealment is ingratitude for the favor, and Allah the Exalted has censured those who conceal what Allah the Exalted has given them and coupled it with stinginess, saying: 'Those who are stingy and enjoin stinginess upon people and conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty' {} and He ﷺ said: (When Allah bestows a favor upon a servant, He loves to see His favor upon him[57]) and a man gave something in secret to one of the righteous, so he raised his hand with it and said: This is from the worldly life, and manifestation in it is better, and secrecy in matters of the Hereafter is better. Therefore, some said: If you are given in public, then take, then return in secret, and gratitude (Shukr) is urged upon in it. He ﷺ said: (Whoever does not thank people has not thanked Allah the Exalted[58]) and gratitude (Shukr) stands in place of recompense until He ﷺ said: (Whoever does you a kindness, then recompense him, and if you are unable, then praise him well for it and pray for him until you know that you have recompensed him) and when the Emigrants said regarding gratitude (Shukr) (O Messenger of Allah, we have not seen better than a people with whom we stayed who shared their wealth with us until we feared they would take all the reward, so He ﷺ said: All that you thank them for and praise them with is recompense[59]) So now, if you have understood these meanings, then know that what is transmitted of the difference among people in it is not a difference in the issue, but rather it is a difference of state (ḥāl), so the removal of the veil in this is that we do not issue an absolute ruling that concealment is better in every state or
93:11.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Mysteries of Zakat'

95:4.arabic: وَكَذَلِكَ خَلَقَ اللهُ سُبْحَانَهُ الْخَلْقَ وَهُمْ فِي ابْتِدَاءِ فِطْرَتِهِمْ يَحْتَاجُونَ إِلَى اسْتِعْمَالِ الشَّهَوَاتِ لِتُكْمَلَ بِهَا أَبْدَانُهُمْ فَيَبْعُدُونَ بِهَا عَنْ حَضْرَتِهِ وَإِنَّمَا سَعَادَتُهُمْ فِي الْقُرْبِ مِنْهُ فَأَعْدَلَهُمْ مِنَ النِّعَمِ مَا يَقْدِرُونَ عَلَى اسْتِعْمَالِهِ فِي نَيْلِ دَرَجَةِ الْقُرْبِ وَعَنْ بُعْدِهِمْ وَقُرْبِهِمْ عَبَّرَ اللهُ تَعَالَى إِذْ قَالَ: ﴿ لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ فِي أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ ثُمَّ رَدَدْنَاهُ أَسْفَلَ سَافِلِينَ إِلَّ
95:4.english: And similarly, Allah (the Exalted) created the creation, and they in the beginning of their innate disposition (Fitrah) need to use the desires (Shahawat) to perfect their bodies with them, so they distance themselves with them from His presence (Hudur). And indeed their happiness (Sa'adah) is in proximity (Qurb) to Him. So He provided them with the blessings (Ni'am) that they are capable of using to attain the degree of proximity. And concerning their distance and proximity, Allah (the Exalted) expressed when He said: 'Indeed, We created the human being (Al-Insan) in the best form (Ahsan Taqwim), then We return him to the lowest of the low (Asfal Safilin), except those who believe.' Therefore, the blessings (Ni'am) of Allah (the Exalted) are instruments (Alat) by which the servant (Abd) ascends from the lowest of the low. Allah (the Exalted) created them for the sake of the servant so that he may attain with them the happiness (Sa'adah) of proximity (Qurb). And Allah (the Exalted) is independent of him, whether proximity or distance. And the servant (Abd) in them is between using them in obedience (Taa'ah), so he would have given thanks (Shakar) for conforming to the love (Mahabbah) of his Master (Mawla), and between using them in his disobedience (Ma'siyah), so he has disbelieved (Kafar) for plunging into what his Master (Mawla) dislikes and does not approve for him. For indeed Allah does not approve for His servants disbelief (Kufr) and disobedience (Ma'siyah). And if he neglects them and does not use them in obedience (Taa'ah) nor disobedience (Ma'siyah), then it is also disbelief (Kufr), a denial (Kufran) of the blessing (Ni'mah) through waste. And everything created in the world is only created as an instrument (Alah) for the servant (Abd) so that he may connect with it to the happiness (Sa'adah) of the Hereafter and attainment of proximity (Qurb) from Allah (the Exalted). So every obedient one (Muti') is, according to his obedience (Taa'ah), giving thanks (Shakir) for the blessing (Ni'mah) of Allah in the means (Asbab) which he used in obedience (Taa'ah). And every lazy one (Kaslan) who abandoned the use or disobedient one (Asi) who used them in the way of distance (B'ud) is a disbeliever (Kafir) straying in other than the love (Mahabbah) of Allah (the Exalted). So disobedience (Ma'siyah) and obedience (Taa'ah) encompass them both the will (Mashiyyah), but they do not encompass them both the love (Mahabbah) and dislike (Karaha). Rather, perhaps a desired thing (Murad) is beloved (Mahbub) and perhaps a desired thing (Murad) is disliked (Makruh).
95:4.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

96:3.arabic: أما ترى أن النبي ﭬ في أول أمره كوشف بالقلم إذ أنزل عليه " اقرأ وربك الأكرم، الذي علم بالقلم، علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم " فقال السالك: لقد فتحت بصري وحدقته، فوالله ما أرى قصباً ولا خشباً، ولا أعلم قلماً إلا كذلك، فقال العلم: لقد أبعدت النجعة، أما سمعت أن متاع البيت يشبه رب البيت، أما علمت أن الله تعالى لا تشبه ذاته سوائر الذوات، فكذلك لا تشبه يده الأيدي ولا قلمه الأقلام ولا كلامه سائر الكلام ولا خطه سائر الخطوط، وهذه أمور إلهية من عالم الملكوت، فليس الله تعالى في ذاته بجسم ولا هو في مكان بخلاف غيره،
96:3.english: Do you not see that the Prophet (peace be upon him) in the beginning of his affair was unveiled with the Pen (Qalam) when there was revealed to him "Read (Iqra') and your Lord (Rabb) is the Most Generous (Al-Akram), Who taught by the Pen (Qalam), taught the human (Insan) what he did not know." So the traveler (Salik) said: I have opened my sight and focused it, and by Allah I do not see a reed nor wood, nor do I know a pen except like that. So the knowledge (Ilm) said: You have indeed strayed far. Have you not heard that the furnishings of the house resemble the lord of the house? Do you not know that Allah the Exalted, His Essence (Dhat) does not resemble other essences? Likewise, His Hand (Yad) does not resemble hands, nor His Pen (Qalam) pens, nor His Speech (Kalam) other speech, nor His Writing (Khatt) other writings. And these are divine matters from the world of the Kingdom (Malakut). So Allah the Exalted is not in His Essence (Dhat) a body (Jism), nor is He in a place unlike others, nor is His Hand (Yad) flesh and bone and blood unlike hands, nor is His Pen (Qalam) from reed, nor His Tablet (Lawh) from wood, nor His Speech (Kalam) with voice and letter, nor His Writing (Khatt) number and form, nor His Ink (Hibr) vitriol and gallnut. If you do not witness this thus, then I see you only as effeminate between the masculinity of Transcendence (Tanzih) and the femininity of Anthropomorphism (Tashbih), wavering between this and that, not to these nor to those. How have you declared His Essence (Dhat) and His Attributes (Sifat) the Exalted transcendent from bodies (Ajsam) and their attributes? And declared His Speech (Kalam) transcendent from the meanings of letters and sounds, yet you hesitate regarding His Hand (Yad) and His Pen (Qalam) and His Tablet (Lawh) and His Writing (Khatt)?
96:3.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

96:4.arabic: والقلم الذي سطر الله به العلوم على صفحات القلوب يجرى مجرى قرص الشمس وإنما لم يحصل العلم في قلب الصبي قبل التمييز لأن لوح قلبه لم يتهيأ بعد لقبول نفس العلم والقلم عبارة عن خلق من خلق الله تعالى جعله سببا لحصول نقش العلوم في قلوب البشر قال الله تعالى الذي علم بالقلم علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم وقلم الله تعالى لا يشبه قلم خلقه كما لا يشبه وصفه وصف خلقه فليس قلمه من قصب ولا خشب كما أنه تعالى ليس من جوهر ولا عرض
96:4.english: And the Pen (Qalam) with which Allah inscribed the sciences upon the pages of the Hearts (Qulub) runs the course of the sun's disc. And knowledge did not occur in the heart of the child before discernment because the tablet of his heart had not yet prepared to receive the essence of knowledge. And the Pen is an expression for a creation from the creations of Allah the Exalted, which He made a cause for the occurrence of the inscription of sciences in the hearts of humans. Allah the Exalted said: 'The One Who taught by the Pen (Qalam), taught the human what he did not know.' And the Pen of Allah the Exalted does not resemble the pen of His creation, just as His description does not resemble the description of His creation. So His Pen is not from reed nor wood, just as He the Exalted is not from substance nor accident.
96:4.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'

96:5.arabic: وقال الله تعالى: " الذي علم بالقلم على الإنسان ما لم يعلم " ثم قال: " الرحمن علم القرآن " وقال: "علمه البيان "، وقال: " ثم إن علينا بيانه "
96:5.english: And Allah the Exalted said: "Who taught by the pen, taught the human being (Al-Insan) what he did not know." Then He said: "The Most Merciful (Ar-Rahman) taught the Quran." And He said: "He taught him the clear expression (Al-Bayan)." And He said: "Then indeed upon Us is its explanation."
96:5.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

96:6.arabic: فما من نعمة من هذه النعم الدنيوية إلا ويجوز أن تصير بلاء ولكن بالإضافة إليه فكذلك ما من بلاء إلا ويجوز أن يصير نعمة ولكن بالإضافة إلى حالة فرب عبد تكون الخيرة له في الفقر والمرض ولو صح بدنه وكثر ماله لبطر وبغى قال الله تعالى: ﴿ ولو بسط الله الرزق لعباده لبغوا في الأرض ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ كلا إن الإنسان ليطغى أن رآه استغنى ﴾ {} وقال ﭬ: (إن الله ليحمى عبده المؤمن من الدنيا وهو يحبه كما يحمى أحدكم مريضه[93])
96:6.english: For there is no blessing from these worldly blessings except that it may become an affliction, but in relation to him; likewise, there is no affliction except that it may become a blessing, but in relation to a state. For perhaps a servant has what is best for him in poverty and illness, and if his body were healthy and his wealth abundant, he would become arrogant and transgress. Allah the Exalted said: 'And if Allah were to extend provision to His servants, they would certainly transgress in the earth' (42:27). And He said: 'No indeed! Verily, the human being (Al-Insan) transgresses (Layutgha) when he sees himself self-sufficient (Istaghna)' (96:6-7). And He said (in a hadith): 'Indeed, Allah protects His believing servant from the world while He loves him, just as one of you protects his sick person' (93).
96:6.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

96:6.arabic: وقال عز وجل "من كان يريد الحياة الدنيا وزينتها" الآية. وقال تعالى "إن الإنسان ليطغى إن رآه استغنى" فلا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله العلي العظيم وقال تعالى "ألهاكم التكاثر".
96:6.english: And the Mighty and Majestic said: "Whoever desires the worldly life and its adornment" the verse. And the Exalted said: "Indeed, the human being transgresses (la-yatgha) when he sees himself self-sufficient (istaghna)" so there is no power nor strength except by Allah, the Most High, the Most Great. And the Exalted said: "The competition in increase distracts you."
96:6.book_title: Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth
96:6.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Miserliness and Love of Wealth'

96:6.arabic: وقال تعالى: " من بعد ما أراكم ما تحبون " قيل العوافي " إن الإنسان ليطغى أن رآه استغنى " وكذلك إذا استغنى بالعافية.
96:6.english: And Allah the Exalted said: "After He has shown you what you love" it is said: the health and well-being (Al-Awafi) "Indeed, the human being (Al-Insan) transgresses (Layutgha) when he sees himself self-sufficient (Istaghna)" and likewise when he becomes self-sufficient (Istaghna) through health and well-being (Al-Afiyah).
96:6.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Monotheism and Reliance'

96:14.arabic: وقال عليه السلام أعبد الله كأنك تراه فإن لم تكن تراه فإنه يراك حديث اعبد الله كأنك تراه الحديث تقدم وقد قال تعالى أفمن هو قائم على كل نفس بما كسبت وقال تعالى ألم يعلم بأن الله يرى وقال الله تعالى إن الله كان عليكم رقيبا وقال تعالى والذين هم لأماناتهم وعهدهم راعون والذين هم بشهاداتهم قائمون
96:14.english: And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Worship Allah as if you see Him, for if you do not see Him, indeed He sees you' - the hadith 'Worship Allah as if you see Him' has preceded. And Allah the Exalted has said: 'Is He who is standing over every soul (Nafs) by what it has earned?' And Allah the Exalted has said: 'Does he not know that Allah sees?' And Allah the Exalted has said: 'Indeed, Allah has been over you a Watcher (Raqib).' And Allah the Exalted has said: 'And those who are to their trusts (Amanat) and their covenants (Ahd) caretakers (Ra'un), and those who are to their testimonies (Shahadat) standing (Qa'imun).'
96:14.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

97:1.arabic: ومنها التدريج في البيان كقوله عز وجل ﴿ شهر رمضان الذي أنزل فيه القرآن ﴾ {} إذ لم يظهر به أنه ليل أو نهار وبان بقوله عز وجل ﴿ إنا أنزلناه في ليلة مباركة ﴾ {} ولم يظهر به أي ليلة فظهر بقوله تعالى ﴿ إنا أنزلناه في ليلة القدر ﴾ {} وربما يظن في الظاهر الاختلاف بين هذه الآيات فهذا وأمثاله مما لا يغني فيه إلا النقل والسماع
97:1.english: And among them is the gradual clarification in the explanation, as in His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'The month of Ramadan in which the Quran was revealed' (2:185), since it did not become clear by it whether it was night or day, and it became clear by His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night' (44:3), and it did not become clear by it which night, so it became clear by His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr)' (97:1). And perhaps it is thought in the apparent meaning that there is a difference between these verses, so this and its like are matters in which nothing avails except transmission (al-Naql) and hearing (al-Samāʿ).
97:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

97:1.arabic: فعسى الشيطان أن لا يحوم على قلبه فينظر إلى ملكوت السماء وليلة القدر عبارة عن الليلة التي ينكشف فيها شيء من الملكوت وهو المراد بقوله تعالى: ﴿ إنا أنزلناه في ليلة القدر ﴾{} ومن جعل بين قلبه وبين صدره مخلاة من الطعام فهو عنه محجوب ومن أخلى معدته فلا يكفيه ذلك لرفع الحجاب ما لم يخل همته عن غير الله عز وجل وذلك هو الأمر كله ومبدأ جميع ذلك تقليل الطعام
97:1.english: Perhaps Satan will not hover over his heart so he may gaze upon the Kingdom of the Heavens (Malakut al-Sama'), and the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr) is an expression for the night in which something of the Kingdom (Malakut) is unveiled, and this is what is intended by His saying, the Exalted: "Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr)." And whoever places between his heart (Qalb) and his chest a feedbag of food is veiled from it, and whoever empties his stomach, that does not suffice him to lift the veil unless he empties his aspiration (Himmah) from other than God, the Mighty and Majestic, and that is the entire matter, and the beginning of all of that is reducing food.
97:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Mysteries of Fasting'

97:1.arabic: يقرأ في كل ركعة بفاتحة الكتاب مرة وإنا أنزلناه في ليلة القدر ثلاث مرات وقل هو الله أحد اثنتي عشرة مرة
97:1.english: He recites in each unit of prayer (rak'ah) the Opening (Al-Fatihah) of the Book once and 'Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr)' three times and 'Say: He is Allah, the One' twelve times.
97:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

97:1.arabic: وقوله تعالى ﴿ إنا أنزلناه في ليلة القدر ﴾ {} أراد القرآن وما سبق له ذكر
97:1.english: And His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr)' {} He intended the Quran and what preceded it of mention.
97:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

98:4.arabic: فلو لم يكن بين يدي الموتي إلا هول تلك النفخة لكان ذلك جديرا بأن يتقى فإنها نفخة وصيحة يصعق بها من فى السموات والأرض يعنى يموتون بها إلا من شاء الله وهو بعض الملائكة ولذلك قال رسول الله ﭬ: (كيف أنعم وصاحب الصور قد التقم القرن وحنى الجبهة وأصغى بالأذن متى يؤمر فينفخ[144]) قال مقاتل: الصور هو القرن وذلك أن إسرافيل عليه السلام واضع فاه على القرن كهيئة البوق ودائرة رأس القرن كعرض السموات والأرض وهو شاخص بصره نحو العرش ينتظر متى يؤمر فينفخ النفخة الأولى فإذا نفخ صعق من فى السموات والأرض أى مات كل حيوا
98:4.english: If there were nothing before the dead except the terror of that blowing, it would be worthy of being feared, for it is a blowing and a cry by which those in the heavens and the earth are struck unconscious, meaning they die by it, except whom Allah wills, and that is some of the angels. Therefore, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'How can I enjoy comfort when the possessor of the Trumpet (Soor) has taken the horn in his mouth, lowered his forehead, and inclined his ear, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow?' [144] Muqatil said: The Trumpet (Soor) is the horn, and that is because Israfil (upon him be peace) has placed his mouth on the horn like the shape of a trumpet, and the circumference of the head of the horn is like the expanse of the heavens and the earth, and he is fixing his gaze toward the Throne (Arsh), waiting for when he will be commanded to blow the first blowing. When he blows, those in the heavens and the earth are struck unconscious, meaning every living creature dies from the intensity of the terror, except whom Allah wills, and that is Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil, and the Angel of Death (Malak al-Mawt). Then the Angel of Death is commanded to take the soul (Ruh) of Jibril, then the soul (Ruh) of Mika'il, then the soul (Ruh) of Israfil, then the Angel of Death is commanded and he dies. Then the creation remains after the first blowing in the Intermediate State (Barzakh) for forty years. Then Allah, the Exalted, revives Israfil and commands him to blow the second blowing, and that is His saying, the Exalted: 'Then it will be blown into it another time, and behold, they are standing, looking.' [Quran 39:68] On their feet, looking at the Resurrection (Ba'ath). And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'When I was sent, I was sent to the possessor of the Trumpet (Soor), and he brought it to his mouth, advanced one foot and delayed another, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow. Indeed, fear the blowing!' [145] So reflect on the creation and their humiliation, their brokenness, and their submission at the time of being raised, out of fear of this striking unconscious and waiting for it.
98:4.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

98:4.arabic: الغموم وشدة الانتظار لعاقبة الأمر كما قال تعالى: ﴿ ونفخ فى الصور فصعق من فى السموات ومن فى الأرض إلا من شاء الله ثم نفخ فيه أخرى فإذا هم قيام ينظرون ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ فإذا نقر فى الناقور فذلك يومئذ يوم عسير على الكافرين غير يسير ﴾ {} وقال تعال: ﴿ ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين ما ينظرون إلا صيحة واحدة تأخذهم وهم يخصمون فلا يستطيعون توصية ولا إلى أهلهم يرجعون ونفخ فى الصور فإذا هم من الأجداث إلى ربهم ينسلون قالوا يا ويلنا من بعثنا من مرقدنا هذا ما وعد الرحمن وصدق المرسلون ﴾ {} فلو لم يكن ب
98:4.english: The sorrows and intensity of waiting for the outcome of the matter, as Allah the Exalted said: 'And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on.' And Allah the Exalted said: 'And when the Trumpet is blown, that Day will be a difficult day for the disbelievers; not easy.' And Allah the Exalted said: 'And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?" They do not await except one blast which will seize them while they are disputing. And they will not be able to make a testament, nor to their people will they return. And the Horn will be blown, and at once from the graves to their Lord they will hasten.
