They will say, "O woe to us! Who has raised us up from our sleeping place?" [It will be said], "This is what the Most Merciful had promised, and the messengers told the truth."' So if there were nothing before the dead except the terror of that blowing, it would be worthy of being feared, for it is a blowing and a cry by which whoever is in the heavens and the earth will fall dead, meaning they die by it, except whom Allah wills, and that is some of the angels. And for that reason, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'How can I be at ease when the possessor of the Horn has taken the horn in his mouth, lowered his forehead, and inclined his ear, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow?' Maqatil said: The Horn is the trumpet, and that is because Israfil (upon him be peace) has placed his mouth on the horn like a trumpet, and the circle of the horn's head is like the width of the heavens and the earth, and he is gazing with his sight toward the Throne, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow the first blowing. And when he blows, whoever is in the heavens and the earth will fall dead, meaning every living creature dies from the intensity of the fright, except whom Allah wills, and that is Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil, and the Angel of Death. Then the Angel of Death will be commanded to take the soul (Ruh) of Jibril, then the soul (Ruh) of Mika'il, then the soul (Ruh) of Israfil, then the Angel of Death will be commanded and he will die. Then the creation will remain after the first blowing in the Barzakh (intermediate state) for forty years. Then Allah the Exalted will revive Israfil and command him to blow the second blowing, and that is His saying: 'Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on.' On their feet, looking at the Resurrection. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'When I was sent, I was sent to the possessor of the Horn, and he brought it to his mouth, and advanced one foot and delayed another, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow. So fear the blowing!' So reflect on the creatures and their humiliation, their breaking, and their submission at the resurrection out of fear of this falling dead and waiting for what will be decreed upon them of happiness or misery. And you are among them broken like their breaking, perplexed like their perplexity. Rather, if you were in the world among the luxurious and the rich enjoying pleasures, then the kings of the earth on that day are the most humiliated people of the gathering place, the smallest and most insignificant of them, being trodden under feet like a mustard seed. And at that time, the wild beasts from the deserts and the mountains will come with lowered heads, mixed with the creatures after their wildness, humbled for the Day of Resurrection, without any sin they have been defiled by, but their gathering is due to the intensity of the falling dead and the terror of the blowing and.
98:4.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

98:5.arabic: فضيلة الإخلاص قال الله تعالى (وما أمروا إلا ليعبدوا الله مخلصين له الدين) وقال (ألا لله الدين الخالص) وقال تعالى (إلا الذين تابوا وأصلحوا واعتصموا بالله وأخلصوا دينهم لله) وقال تعالى (فمن كان يرجو لقاء ربه فليعمل عملا صالحا ولا يشرك بعبادة ربه أحدا) نزلت فيمن يعمل لله ويحب أن يحمد عليه وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: (ثلاث لا يغل عليهن قلب رجل مسلم إخلاص العمل لله)[36] وعن مصعب بن سعد عن أبيه قال ظن أبى أن له فضلا على من هو دونه من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم
98:5.english: The virtue of sincerity (Ikhlas). Allah the Exalted said: (And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, being sincere (mukhlisīn) to Him in religion) and He said: (Indeed, for Allah is the pure religion) and He the Exalted said: (Except those who repent and reform and hold fast to Allah and make their religion sincere (akhlaṣū) for Allah) and He the Exalted said: (So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone) - it was revealed concerning one who works for Allah and loves to be praised for it. And the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: (Three things do not cause the heart (qalb) of a Muslim man to be treacherous: sincerity (ikhlas) of action for Allah)[36]. And from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd from his father, he said: My father thought he had superiority over those below him among the companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, so the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: (Indeed, Allah the Mighty and Majestic supports this nation through its weak ones and their supplication and their sincerity (ikhlas))[37]. And from al-Hasan, he said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: (Allah the Exalted says: Sincerity (al-Ikhlas) is a secret from My secrets which I have deposited in the heart (qalb) of whom I love from My servants)[38]. And 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah honor his face, said: (Do not be concerned with the smallness of action, but be concerned with acceptance, for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to Mu'adh ibn Jabal: Make the action sincere (akhliṣ), and a little of it will suffice you)[39]. And he, peace be upon him, said: (There is no servant who makes his action sincere (yukhliṣ) for Allah for forty days except that the springs of wisdom appear from his heart (qalb) upon his tongue)[40].
98:5.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

98:5.arabic: فالصبر على الطاعة صبر على الشدائد ويحتاج المطيع إلى الصبر على طاعته في ثلاث أحوال: الأولى قبل الطاعة وذلك في تصحيح النية والاخلاص والصبر عن شوائب الرياء ودواعي الآفات وعقد العزم على الاخلاص والوفاء وذلك من الصبر الشديد عند من يعرف حقيقة النية والاخلاص وآفات الرياء ومكايد النفس، وقد نبه ﭬ اذ قال ﭬ: (إنما الاعمال بالنيات وانما لكل امرىء ما نوى[21]) وقال تعالى: ﴿ وما أمروا إلا ليعبدوا الله مخلصين له الدين ﴾ {} ولهذا قدم الله تعالى الصبر على العمل، فقال تعالى: ﴿ الا الذين صبروا وعملوا الصالحات ﴾ {}.
98:5.english: Patience (Sabr) upon obedience is patience upon hardships, and the obedient one needs patience upon his obedience in three states: The first is before the obedience, and that is in correcting the intention (Niyyah) and sincerity (Ikhlas) and patience from the impurities of showing off (Riya) and the motives of afflictions, and resolving upon sincerity (Ikhlas) and fulfillment. That is from the severe patience for one who knows the reality of the intention (Niyyah) and sincerity (Ikhlas) and the afflictions of showing off (Riya) and the tricks of the Soul (Nafs). And He (peace be upon him) alerted when he said (peace be upon him): 'Indeed, deeds are by intentions, and for every person is what he intended.' And Allah the Exalted said: 'And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, being sincere (Mukhlisin) to Him in the religion (Deen), upright (Hunafa'), and to establish the prayer (Salah) and give the charity (Zakah). And that is the religion (Deen) of the straightness (Al-Qayyimah).' And for this reason, Allah the Exalted gave precedence to patience (Sabr) over the deed, so He the Exalted said: 'Except those who are patient (Sabaru) and do righteous deeds.'
98:5.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

98:5.arabic: نحمد الله حمد الشاكرين ونؤمن به إيمان الموقنين ونقر بوحدانيته إقرار الصادقين ونشهد أن لا إله إلا الله رب العالمين وخالق السموات والأرضين ومكلف الجن والإنس والملائكة المقربين أن يعبدوه عبادة المخلصين فقال تعالى وما أمروا إلا ليعبدوا الله مخلصين له الدين فما لله إلا الدين الخالص المتين فإنه أغنى الأغنياء عن شركة المشاركين والصلاة على نبيه محمد سيد المرسلين وعلى جميع النبيين وعلى آله وأصحابه الطيبين الطاهرين أما بعد فقد انكشف لأرباب القلوب ببصيرة الإيمان وأنوار القرآن أن لا وصول إلى السعادة إلا بال
98:5.english: We praise Allah with the praise of the thankful ones, and we believe in Him with the belief of the certain ones, and we affirm His Oneness (Tawhid) with the affirmation of the truthful ones, and we testify that there is no god but Allah, Lord of the worlds, Creator of the heavens and the earths, and He has obligated the jinn, mankind, and the close angels to worship Him with the worship of the sincere ones. So He, the Exalted, said: 'And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, [being] sincere to Him in religion, inclining to truth, and to establish prayer and to give zakah. And that is the correct religion.' (Quran 98:5) So for Allah is only the pure, firm religion, for He is the richest of the rich from partnership of associates. And prayers upon His Prophet Muhammad, master of the messengers, and upon all the prophets, and upon his family and his pure, purified companions. Now then, it has been revealed to the possessors of hearts (Qulub) through the insight of faith and the lights of the Quran that there is no attainment of happiness except through knowledge and worship. So all people are perished except the knowers, and all the knowers are perished except the doers, and all the doers are perished except the sincere ones, and the sincere ones are in great danger.
98:5.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

98:8.arabic: وروي عن علي كرم الله وجهه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: " أحب العباد إلى الله تعالى الفقير القانع برزقه الراضي عن الله تعالى"[39]. وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: " اللهم اجعل قوت آل محمد كفافا"[
98:8.english: And it was narrated from Ali, may Allah honor his face, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that he said: "The most beloved of servants to Allah, the Exalted, is the poor person who is content (Qani') with his provision, the one who is pleased (Radi) with Allah, the Exalted." And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "O Allah, make the sustenance of the family of Muhammad sufficient (Kafafan)."
98:8.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Poverty and Abstinence'

99:6.arabic: وقال تعالى يومئذ يصدر الناس أشتاتا ليروا أعمالهم فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره ومن يعمل مثقال ذرة شرا يره وقال تعالى ثم توفى كل نفس ما كسبت وهم لا يظلمون وقال تعالى يوم تجد كل نفس ما عملت من خير محضرا وما عملت من سوء تود لو أن بينها وبينه أمدا بعيدا ويحذركم الله نفسه وقال تعالى واعلموا أن الله يعلم ما في أنفسكم فاحذروه فعرف أرباب البصائر من جملة العباد أن الله تعالى لهم بالمرصاد وأنهم سيناقشون في الحساب ويطالبون بمثاقيل الذر من الخطرات واللحظات وتحققوا أنه لا ينجيهم من هذه الأخطار إلا لزوم المحاسب
99:6.english: And He (Exalted) said: 'On that day, the people will emerge in scattered groups to be shown their deeds. So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.' And He (Exalted) said: 'Then every soul (Nafs) will be fully compensated for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.' And He (Exalted) said: 'On the day when every soul (Nafs) will find what it did of good present [before it], and what it did of evil, it will wish that between it and that [evil] was a great distance. And Allah warns you of Himself.' And He (Exalted) said: 'And know that Allah knows what is in your souls (Anfus), so beware of Him.' So the possessors of insight (Arbab al-Basa'ir) from among the servants recognized that Allah (Exalted) is lying in wait for them, and that they will be scrutinized in the accounting and held accountable for atom's weights of thoughts (Khatarat) and glances (Lahazat). And they realized that nothing will save them from these dangers except adhering to self-accounting (Muhasabah) and sincere self-observation (Muraqabah), and demanding from the soul (Nafs) in breaths (Anfas) and movements (Harakat), and accounting it for thoughts (Khatarat) and glances (Lahazat). For whoever accounts his soul (Nafs) before being accounted for, his accounting on the Day of Resurrection (Qiyamah) will be lightened, and his answer will be present at the questioning, and his return and outcome will be good. And whoever does not account his soul (Nafs), his regrets will persist, and his pauses in the gathering places of the Day of Resurrection (Qiyamah) will be prolonged, and his evil deeds will lead him to disgrace and contempt.
99:6.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Monitoring and Accounting'

99:6.arabic: فاستعد يا مسكين لهذا اليوم العظيم شأنه المديد زمانه القاهر سلطانه القريب أوانه، يوم ترى السماء فيه قد انفطرت، والكواكب من هوله قد انتثرت، والنجوم الزواهر قد انكدرت، والشمس قد كورت، والجبال قد سيرت، والعشار قد عطلت، والوحوش قد حشرت، والبحار قد سجرت والنفوس إلى الأبدان قد زوجت، والجحيم قد سعرت، والجنة قد أزلفت، والجبال قد نسفت، والأرض قد مدت، يوم ترى الأرض قد زلزلت فيه زالزالها، وأخرجت الأرض أثقالها، يومئذ يصدر الناس أشتاتا ليروا أعمالهم، يوم تحمل الأرض والجبال فدكتا دكة واحدة، فيومئذ وقعت الواقعة
99:6.english: Prepare, O wretched one, for this day of great affair, long in its time, overpowering in its dominion, near in its occurrence, a day when you will see the sky therein has split, and the planets from its terror have scattered, and the shining stars have been extinguished, and the sun has been rolled up, and the mountains have been set in motion, and the pregnant camels have been neglected, and the wild beasts have been gathered, and the seas have been set ablaze, and the souls (Nafs) to the bodies have been paired, and Hell has been kindled, and Paradise has been brought near, and the mountains have been blown away, and the earth has been stretched out, a day when you will see the earth has quaked with its quaking, and the earth has brought forth its burdens, on that day the people will issue forth in scattered groups to be shown their deeds, a day when the earth and the mountains will be lifted and crushed with a single crushing, and then the Inevitable Event will occur and the sky will be split, so it is on that day frail, and the angels are at its edges, and the Throne of your Lord will be carried above them on that day by eight, on that day you will be presented, nothing of you will be hidden, a day when the mountains will move and you will see the earth bare, a day when the earth will be shaken with its shaking and the mountains will be pulverized with pulverization so they become scattered dust, a day when the people will be like scattered moths and the mountains will be like carded wool, a day when every nursing mother will be distracted from what she nursed and every pregnant one will deliver her burden and you will see the people intoxicated yet they are not intoxicated but the punishment of Allah is severe, a day when the earth will be changed to other than the earth and the heavens and they will appear before Allah the One, the Subduer, a day when the mountains will be blown away with blowing so they leave a level plain, you will see in it no crookedness nor unevenness, a day when you will see the mountains, you think them fixed while they pass like the passing of clouds, a day when the sky will be split so it becomes like red leather, and on that day no human or jinn will be asked about his sin, a day when the disobedient will be prevented from speech and in it there will be no inquiry about crimes but they will be seized by the forelocks and the feet, a day when every soul (Nafs) will find what it did of good present and what it did of evil it wishes that between it and it were a distant span, a day when every soul (Nafs) will know what it has brought and will witness what it sent ahead and left behind, a day when the tongues will be silenced and the limbs will speak, a day whose mention has turned gray, O master of the...
99:6.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

99:7.arabic: فإذا طاب شراب الأبرار لشوب الشراب الصرف الذي هو للمقربين. والشراب عبارة عن جملة نعيم الجنان، كما أن الكتاب عبر به عن جميع الأعمال فقال: "إن كتاب الأبرار لفي عليين" ثم قال: "يشهده المقربون" فكان أمارة علة كتابهم أنه ارتفع إلى حيث يشهده المقربون، وكما أن الأبرار يجدون المزيد في حالهم ومعرفتهم بقربهم من المقربين ومشاهدتهم لهم، فكذلك يكون حالهم في الآخرة "ما خلقكم ولا بعثكم إلا كنفس واحدة كما بدأنا أول خلق نعيده"، وكما قال تعالى: "جزاء وفاقاً" أي وافق الجزاء أعمالهم فقوبل الخالص بالصرف من الشراب وقو
99:7.english: So if the drink of the righteous becomes pleasant due to the mixing of the pure drink which is for the close ones. And the drink is an expression for the entirety of the bliss of the Gardens, just as the Book expressed by it all the deeds saying: "Indeed, the record of the righteous is in 'Illiyyun" then said: "Witnessed by those brought near" so it was a sign of the reason for their record that it rose to where those brought near witness it, and just as the righteous find increase in their state and knowledge by their closeness to those brought near and their witnessing of them, so will be their state in the Hereafter "He did not create you nor resurrect you except as a single soul as We began the first creation We will repeat it", and as Allah the Exalted said: "A reward matching" meaning the reward corresponded to their deeds, so the pure was met with the pure from the drink and the mixed was met with the mixed, and the mixing of every drink is according to what preceded of mixing in his love and his deeds "So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it - and Allah does not change what is in a people until they change what is in their souls - Indeed, Allah does not do injustice, [even] as much as an atom's weight; and if there is a good deed, He multiplies it - and if it is the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth, and sufficient are We as accountant" So whoever his love in the world was his hope for the bliss of the Garden and the wide-eyed maidens and palaces, he is enabled in the Garden to settle wherever he wishes to play with the eternal youths and enjoy the women; there his pleasure ends in the Hereafter because indeed every human is given in love what his soul (Nafs) desires and his eye delights in.
99:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

99:7.arabic: اعلم أن العمل إذا لم يكن خالصا لوجه الله تعالى بل امتزج به شوب من الرياء أو حظوظ النفس فقد اختلف الناس في أن ذلك هل يقتضي ثوابا أم يقتضي عقابا أم لا يقتضي شيئا أصلا فلا يكون له ولا عليه أما الذي لم يرد به إلا الرياء فهو عليه قطعا وهو سبب المقت والعقاب وأما الخالص لوجه الله تعالى فهو سبب الثواب وإنما النظر في المشوب وظاهر الأخبار تدل على أنه لا ثواب له[45] وليس تخلو الأخبار عن تعارض فيه والذي ينقدح لما فيه والعلم عند الله أن ينظر إلى قدر قوة الباعث فإن كان الباعث الديني مساويا للباعث النفسي تقاوم
99:7.english: Know that if the deed is not purely for the Face (Wajh) of Allah the Exalted, but rather mixed with a taint of showing off (Riya') or desires of the Soul (Nafs), then people have differed regarding whether that necessitates reward or necessitates punishment or necessitates nothing at all, so it is neither for him nor against him. As for that which was intended only with showing off (Riya'), it is against him decisively and is a cause of wrath and punishment. And as for that which is purely for the Face (Wajh) of Allah the Exalted, it is a cause of reward. The consideration is regarding the mixed [deed]. The apparent reports indicate that there is no reward for it, and the reports are not free from contradiction in this matter. What becomes clear regarding it—and knowledge is with Allah—is to look at the measure of the strength of the motivator. If the religious motivator is equal to the soul (Nafs) motivator, they counterbalance and cancel each other out, and the deed becomes neither for him nor against him. And if the motivator of showing off (Riya') is predominant and stronger, then it is not beneficial, and it is moreover harmful and leads to punishment—yes, the punishment in it is lighter than the punishment of the deed that was purely for showing off (Riya') and not mixed with any taint of drawing near (Taqarrub). And if the intention of drawing near (Taqarrub) is predominant in comparison to the other motivator, then he has reward according to what remains of the strength of the religious motivator. And this is due to His saying, the Exalted: 'So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it' (Quran 99:7-8), and due to His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, Allah does not do injustice, [even] as much as an atom's weight; and if there is a good deed, He multiplies it' (Quran 4:40). So it is not fitting that the intention of good be wasted. Rather, if it is predominant over the intention of showing off (Riya'), the amount that equals it is invalidated, and the increase remains. And if it is overcome, something of the punishment of the corrupt intention falls away because of it.
99:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Intention, Sincerity and Truthfulness'

99:7.arabic: والفضيلة نسبية واستحقارنا للصيارفة عند قياسهم بالملوك لا يدل على حقارتهم إذا قيسوا بالكناسين فلا تظن أن ما نزل عن الرتبة القصوى ساقط القدر بل الرتبة العليا للأنبياء ثم الأولياء ثم العلماء الراسخين في العلم ثم للصالحين على تفاوت درجاتهم وبالجملة فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره ومن يعمل مثقال ذرة شرا يره ومن قصد الله تعالى بالعلم أي علم كان نفعه ورفعه لا محالة.
99:7.english: And virtue is relative, and our belittling of money-changers when comparing them to kings does not indicate their lowliness when compared to sweepers. So do not think that what falls below the highest rank is of diminished worth, but rather the highest rank is for the Prophets, then the Friends (Awliya), then the firmly-grounded scholars in knowledge, then for the righteous with varying degrees among them. And in summary: 'So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it' (Quran 99:7-8). And whoever intends Allah the Exalted with knowledge, whatever knowledge it may be, his benefit and elevation are inevitable.
99:7.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Book of Knowledge'

99:7.arabic: فأما إذا كان بحيث لولا الناس أيضاً لكان يصلي إلا أنه ظهر له الرغبة في المحمدة أيضاً فاجتمع الباعثان، فهذا إما أن يكون في صدقة وقراءة وما ليس فيه تحليل وتحريم أو في عقد صلاة وحج، فإن كان في صدقة فقد عصى بإجابة باعث الرياء وأطاع بإجابة باعث الثواب "فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة خيراً يره ومن يعمل مثقال ذرة شراً يره" فله ثواب بقدر قصده الصحيح وعقاب بقدر قصده الفاسد ولا يحبط أحدهما الآخر.
99:7.english: As for if he was such that even without people he would still pray, except that the desire for praise also appeared to him, so the two motivators combined - this is either in charity and recitation and what does not involve permissibility and prohibition, or in the contract of prayer and pilgrimage. If it was in charity, then he has disobeyed by responding to the motivator of showing off (Riya') and obeyed by responding to the motivator of reward. "So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it." So for him is reward according to the measure of his correct intention (Qasd) and punishment according to the measure of his corrupt intention, and one does not nullify the other.
99:7.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

99:7.arabic: حديث الرجل الذي جاء ليتعلم فانتهى إلى قوله تعالى فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره ومن يعمل مثقال ذرة شرا يره فقال يكفني هذا وانصرف فقال النبي ﷺ انصرف الرجل وهو فقيه أخرجه أبو داود والنسائي في الكبرى وابن حبان والحاكم وصححه من حديث عبد الله بن عمرو قال أتى رجل رسول الله ﷺ فقال أقرئني يا رسول الله الحديث وفيه فأقرأه رسول الله ﷺ إذا زلزلت حتى فرغ منها فقال الرجل والذي بعثك بالحق لا أزيد عليهما أبدا ثم أدبر الرجل فقال رسول الله ﷺ أفلح الرويجل أفلح الرويجل ولأحمد والنسائي في الكبرى من حديث صعصعة عم الفرزد
99:7.english: The narration of the man who came to learn and reached the saying of Allah the Exalted: 'So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.' He said: 'This is sufficient for me,' and departed. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'The man departed as a jurist (faqih).' Reported by Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i in al-Kubra, Ibn Hibban, and al-Hakim who authenticated it from the narration of Abdullah ibn Amr who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and said: 'Recite to me, O Messenger of Allah...' In it: So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) recited to him 'When the earth is shaken' until he finished it. The man said: 'By the One who sent you with the truth, I will never add to these two.' Then the man turned away. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'The man has succeeded, the man has succeeded.' And for Ahmad and al-Nasa'i in al-Kubra from the narration of Sa'sa'ah, the uncle of al-Farazdaq, that he was the companion of the verse (an-nassah) and said: 'It is enough for me, I do not care to hear other than it.'
99:7.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

99:8.arabic: ومن ذلك أن يغلب على قلبه أن (من يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يرهُ  (  ومن  يعمل  مثقال ذرة شرا يره( (الزلزة: 8،7) وهو اليقين بالثواب والعقاب حتى يرى  نسبة  الطاعات إلى الثواب كنسبة الخبز إلى الشبع  ونسبة  المعاصي  إلى  العقاب  كنسبة  السموم والأفاعي إلى الهلاك فكما يحرص على  التحصيل  للخبز  طلبا  للشبع  فيحفظ  قليله وكثيره فكذلك يحرص على الطاعات كلها قليلها وكثيرها  وكما  يجتنب  قليل  السموم وكثيرها فكذلك يجتنب المعاصي قليلها وكثيرها وصغيرها وكبيرها  فاليقين  بالمعنى الأول قد يوجد لعموم المؤمنين أما بالم
99:8.english: And from that is that there overcomes upon his Heart (Qalb) that 'Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it' (Az-Zalzalah: 7-8). And it is the Certainty (Yaqeen) in reward and punishment until he sees the proportion of acts of obedience to reward like the proportion of bread to satiety, and the proportion of sins to punishment like the proportion of poisons and snakes to destruction. So just as he is eager for the acquisition of bread seeking satiety, and thus preserves its little and its much, likewise he is eager for all acts of obedience, their little and their much. And just as he avoids little poisons and their much, likewise he avoids sins, their little and their much, their small and their great. So the Certainty (Yaqeen) in the first meaning may exist for the generality of the believers, but as for the second meaning, it is specific to those brought near. And the fruit of this Certainty (Yaqeen) is the sincerity of self-observation (Muraqabah) in movements and stillness, in passing thoughts, and the utmost in God-consciousness (Taqwa) and guarding against every evil. And whenever the Certainty (Yaqeen) is more dominant, the guarding is more severe and the exertion is more complete.
99:8.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

99:8.arabic: وليس من أمله مقصور على شهر كمن أمله شهر ويوم بل بينهما تفاوت في الدرجة عند الله فإن الله لا يظلم مثقال ذرة ﴿ وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًا يَرَهُ ﴾ {} ثم يظهر أثر قصر الأمل في المبادرة إلى العمل وكل إنسان يدعى أنه قصير الأمل وهو كاذب، إنما يظهر ذلك بأعماله.
99:8.english: And it is not that his hope is limited to a month like one whose hope is for a month and a day, but between them there is a difference in degree with Allah, for Allah does not wrong (even) the weight of an atom (mithqāla dharratin). 'And whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it' (Quran 99:8). Then the effect of shortening hope appears in hastening to work, and every person claims that he has short hope, but he is lying; it only appears through his deeds.
99:8.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Book of Repentance'

100:4.arabic: والروح أيضا ورد في القرآن على معان كثيرة فلا نطول بإيرادها وكذلك قد يقع الأبهام في الحروف مثل قوله عز وجل ﴿ فأثرن به نقعا فوسطن به جمعا ﴾ {} فالهاء الأولى كناية عن الحوافر وهي الموريات أي أثرن بالحوافر نقعا. والثانية كناية عن الإغارة وهي المغيرات صبحا فوسطن به جمعا جمع المشركون فأغاروا بجمعهم
100:4.english: And the Spirit (Ruh) also comes in the Quran with many meanings, so we will not prolong by mentioning them. Likewise, ambiguity may occur in the letters, like His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: 'So they raise with it dust, then penetrate with it the gathering' (Quran 100:4-5). The first 'it' (hi) is a metaphor for the hooves, and they are the ones that kindle (al-muriyat), meaning they raise with the hooves dust. And the second 'it' (hi) is a metaphor for the raid, and they are the raiders at dawn (al-mughirat subhan), so they penetrate with it the gathering, the gathering of the polytheists, and they raided with their gathering.
100:4.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

100:10.arabic: فكيف بكم لو عاينتم الأمور وبعثرت القبور وحصل ما في الصدور وأوقفتم للتحصيل بين يدي الملك الجليل فطارت القلوب لإشفاقها من سالف الذنوب وهتكت عنكم الحجب والأستار وظهرت منكم العيوب والأسرار؟ هنالك تجزى كل نفس بما كسبت إن الله عز وجل يقول "ليجزى الذي أساءوا بما عملوا ويجزى الذي أحسنوا بالحسنى" وقال تعالى "ووضع الكتاب فترى المجرمين مشفقين مما فيه" الآية جعلنا الله وإياكم عاملين بكتابة متبعين لأوليائه حتى يحلنا وإياكم دار المقامة من فضله إنه حميد مجيد.
100:10.english: So how would you be if you witnessed the matters and the graves were overturned and what is in the chests (Sudur) was extracted and you were stopped for the accounting before the Majestic King (Al-Malik Al-Jalil), and the hearts (Qulub) flew from their fear of past sins, and the veils (Hujub) and curtains (Astār) were torn from you, and your faults (ʿUyūb) and secrets (Asrār) appeared? There, every soul (Nafs) will be recompensed for what it earned. Indeed, Allah, the Exalted and Majestic, says: "That He may recompense those who did evil with what they did, and recompense those who did good with the best reward" (Quran 53:31), and He, the Exalted, says: "And the Record will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it" (Quran 83:20). May Allah make us and you doers of His Book, followers of His allies, until He settles us and you in the Abode of Permanence (Dār al-Maqāmah) from His bounty. Indeed, He is Praiseworthy, Glorious.
100:10.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Condemnation of the World'

101:1.arabic: ولما قصرت الأفهام عن درك معنى عليين عظم أمره فقال: " وما أدراك ما عليون " كما قال تعالى: " القارعة ما القارعة وما أدراك ما القارعة ".
101:1.english: And when understandings fell short of grasping the meaning of 'Illiyyun' (the highest paradise), He magnified its matter by saying: "And what will make you know what 'Illiyyun' is?" just as The Exalted said: "The Striking Calamity (Al-Qari'ah) - what is the Striking Calamity (Al-Qari'ah)? And what will make you know what the Striking Calamity (Al-Qari'ah) is?".
101:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

101:4.arabic: يوم ترى الأرض قد زلزلت فيه زالزالها، وأخرجت الأرض أثقالها، يومئذ يصدر الناس أشتاتا ليروا أعمالهم، يوم تحمل الأرض والجبال فدكتا دكة واحدة، فيومئذ وقعت الواقعة وانشقت السماء فهى يومئذ واهية، والملك على أرجائها، ويحمل عرش ربك فوقهم يومئذ ثمانية يومئذ تعرضون لا تخفى منكم خافية، يوم تسير الجبال وترى الأرض بارزة، يوم ترج الأرض فيه رجا وتبس الجبال بسا فكانت هباء منبثا، يوم يكون الناس كالفراش المبثوث وتكون الجبال كالعهن المنفوش، يوم تذهل فيه كل مرضعة عما أرضعت وتضع كل ذات حمل حملها وترى الناس سكارى وما
101:4.english: A day when you see the earth shaken with its shaking, and the earth brings forth its burdens, then the people will issue forth in groups to see their deeds. A day when the earth and the mountains are carried and crushed with a single crushing, then the Event (Al-Waqi'ah) has occurred and the sky is split, so it is on that day weak, and the angels are on its edges, and the Throne (Arsh) of your Lord is carried above them on that day by eight. On that day you will be presented, nothing hidden from you will be concealed. A day when the mountains will move and you see the earth bare. A day when the earth will be shaken with its shaking and the mountains will be scattered with scattering, so they become scattered dust. A day when the people will be like scattered moths (Al-Farash Al-Mabthuth) and the mountains will be like carded wool. A day when every nursing mother will be distracted from what she nursed, and every pregnant one will deliver her pregnancy, and you see the people intoxicated, yet they are not intoxicated, but the punishment of Allah is severe. A day when the earth will be changed to other than the earth and the heavens, and they will appear before Allah, the One, the Subduer (Al-Qahhar). A day when the mountains will be blown away with blowing, leaving a level plain where you see no crookedness nor unevenness. A day when you see the mountains, you think them fixed, yet they pass like the passing of clouds. A day when the sky is split, so it becomes like red leather. Then on that day, no human or jinn will be asked about his sin. A day when the disobedient will be prevented from speech, and no one will be asked about crimes, but they will be seized by the forelocks and the feet. A day when every soul (Nafs) will find what it did of good present, and what it did of evil, it wishes there were a great distance between it and that. A day when every soul (Nafs) will know what it has brought and will testify to what it sent ahead and left behind. A day when the tongues will be silenced and the limbs will speak. A day whose mention turned gray the Master of the Messengers (Sayyid Al-Mursalin) when the Truthful One (Al-Siddiq), may Allah be pleased with him, said to him: 'I see you have turned gray, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Surah Hud and its sisters have turned me gray [155]'—and they are Al-Waqi'ah, Al-Mursalat, 'Amma Yatasa'alun, and 'Idha Al-Shamsu Kuwwirat.
101:4.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Repentance'

101:6.arabic: قد عرفت هول الميزان وخطره وأن الأعين شاخصة إلى لسان الميزان ﴿ فأما من ثقلت موازينه فهو فى عيشة راضية وأما من خفت موازينه فأمه هاوية وما أدراك ماهيه نار حامية ﴾ {} واعلم أنه لا ينجو من خطر الميزان إلا من حاسب فى الدنيا نفسه ووزن فيها بميزان الشرع أعماله وأقواله وخطراته ولحظاته كما قال عمر رضى الله عنه: حاسبوا أنفسكم قبل أن تحاسبوا وزنوها قبل أن توزنوا وإنما حسابه لنفسه أن يتوب عن كل معصية قبل الموت توبة نصوحا ويتدارك ما فرط من تقصيره فى فرائض الله تعالى ويرد المظالم حبة بعد حبة ويستحل كل من تعرض
101:6.english: You have known the terror of the Scale (Mizan) and its danger, and that eyes are staring at the tongue of the Scale: 'So as for he whose scales are heavy, he will be in a pleasing life. And as for he whose scales are light, his mother is Hāwiyah. And what can make you know what that is? It is a Fire, intensely hot.' And know that none is saved from the danger of the Scale except he who accounts in the world his Soul (Nafs) and weighs therein with the scale of the Law (Sharia) his deeds and his words and his thoughts and his glances, as 'Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: 'Account your souls before you are accounted, and weigh them before you are weighed.' And his accounting for his Soul (Nafs) is that he repents from every disobedience before death with a sincere repentance (Tawbah Nasuh) and makes up what he neglected from his shortcomings in the obligations (Fara'id) of God, the Exalted, and returns the wrongs grain by grain, and seeks forgiveness from everyone he wronged with his tongue and his hand and his bad suspicion with his Heart (Qalb), and with the purity of their hearts until he dies and there remains upon him no wrong nor obligation; this one enters the Garden (Jannah) without account.
101:6.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

101:6.arabic: واعلم إن لله حقا في النهار لا يقبله في الليل وأن لله حقا في الليل لا يقبله في النهار وأنه لا يقبل النافلة حتى تؤدى الفريضة وإنما ثقلت موازين من ثقلت موازينهم يوم القيامة باتباعهم الحق في الدنيا وثقله عليهم وحق لميزان لا يوضع فيه إلا الحق أن يثقل وإنما خفت موازين من خفت موزاينهم يوم القيامة باتباع الباطل وخفته عليهم وحق لميزان لا يوضع فيه إلا الباطل أن يخف
101:6.english: And know that Allah has a right in the daytime that He does not accept in the night, and Allah has a right in the night that He does not accept in the daytime, and He does not accept the supererogatory (Nawafil) until the obligatory (Fara'id) is performed. And indeed, the scales (Mawazin) of those whose scales are heavy on the Day of Resurrection are heavy because they followed the truth (Haqq) in the world and it was heavy upon them, and it is right for a scale in which nothing is placed except the truth to be heavy. And indeed, the scales of those whose scales are light on the Day of Resurrection are light because they followed falsehood (Batil) and it was light upon them, and it is right for a scale in which nothing is placed except falsehood to be light.
101:6.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Book of Repentance'

102:5.arabic: ولكن الانعكاس والانتكاس ضرورة هذا العالم فكذلك عالم الملك والشهادة محاك لعالم الغيب والملكوت فمن الناس من يسر له نظر الاعتبار فلا ينظر في شىء من عالم الملك إلا ويعبر به إلى عالم الملكوت فيسمى عبوره عبرة وقد أمر الحق به فقال: ﴿ فاعتبروا يا أولى الأبصار ﴾ {} ومنهم من عميت بصيرته فلم يعتبر فاحتبس في عالم الملك والشهادة وستنفتح إلى حبسه أبواب جهنم وهذا الحبس مملوء نارا من شأنها أن تطلع على الأفئدة إلا أن بينه وبين إدراك ألمها حجابا فإذا رفع ذلك الحجاب بالموت أدرك وعن هذا أظهر الله تعالى الحق على لسا
102:5.english: But inversion and reversal are necessities of this world, and likewise the world of dominion (al-Mulk) and witnessing (al-Shahadah) imitates the world of the unseen (al-Ghayb) and the kingdom (al-Malakut). Among people, some are granted the vision of consideration, so they do not look at anything from the world of dominion except that they cross with it to the world of the kingdom, and their crossing is called a lesson. And the Truth has commanded this, saying: 'So take lesson, O possessors of insight' (Quran 59:2). And among them are those whose insight (Basarah) is blinded, so they do not take lesson, and they are confined in the world of dominion and witnessing, and the gates of Hell will open to their confinement. And this confinement is filled with a fire whose nature is to rise upon the hearts (al-Af'idah), except that between it and the perception of its pain is a veil. So when that veil is lifted by death, they perceive. And from this, Allah the Exalted manifested the truth upon the tongue of a people whom He made speak with the truth, and they said: 'Paradise and Hell are created, but Hell is perceived once with a perception called the knowledge of certainty (Ilm al-Yaqin), and once with another perception called the eye of certainty (Ayn al-Yaqin). And the eye of certainty (Ayn al-Yaqin) does not occur except in the Hereafter, and the knowledge of certainty (Ilm al-Yaqin) can occur in this world, but only for those who have fulfilled their share of the light of certainty (Nur al-Yaqin). Therefore, Allah the Exalted said: 'No! If you knew with the knowledge of certainty (Ilm al-Yaqin), you would surely see Hell' (Quran 102:5), meaning in this world, 'Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty (Ayn al-Yaqin)' (Quran 102:7), meaning in the Hereafter. So then it has become clear that the sound heart (al-Qalb al-Salih) for the kingdom of the Hereafter cannot be except noble, like the sound person for the kingdom of this world.
102:5.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Patience and Gratitude'

103:1.arabic: وَمَهْمَا تَمَّتْ مَعْرِفَتُهُ كَانَتِ الْخَشْيَةُ أَغْلَبَ الْأَحْوَالِ عَلَى قَلْبِهِ فَإِنَّ التَّضْيِيقَ غَالِبٌ عَلَى آيَاتِ الْقُرْآنِ فَلَا يَرَى ذِكْرَ الْمَغْفِرَةِ وَالرَّحْمَةِ إِلَّا مُقْرُونًا بِشُرُوطٍ يَقْصُرُ الْعَارِفُ عَنْ نَيْلِهَا كَقَوْلِهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ ﴿ وَإِنِّي لَغَفَّارٌ ﴾  {}  ثُمَّ أَتْبَعَ ذَلِكَ بِأَرْبَعَةِ شُرُوطٍ ﴿ لِمَنْ تَابَ وَآمَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا ثُمَّ اهْتَدَى ﴾  {} وَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى ﴿ وَالْعَصْرِ إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا
103:1.english: And whenever his knowledge is perfected, the Fear (Khushya) becomes the most dominant state upon his Heart (Qalb), for the restriction is predominant over the verses of the Quran, so he does not see the mention of Forgiveness (Maghfira) and Mercy (Rahma) except coupled with conditions that the Knower (Arif) falls short of attaining, like His saying, Mighty and Majestic: 'And indeed, I am Forgiving (Ghaffar)' {} then He followed that with four conditions: 'For whoever repents and believes and does righteous deeds then is guided' {} and His saying, Exalted: 'By the Time (Al-Asr), indeed, mankind is in loss, except those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience' {} He mentioned four conditions, and where He restricted the mention to a comprehensive condition, He said, Exalted: 'Indeed, the Mercy (Rahma) of Allah is near to the Doers of Good (Muhsinin)' {} so Doing Good (Ihsan) encompasses all, and thus whoever peruses the Quran from its beginning to its end, and whoever understands that, is worthy that his state be Fear (Khushya) and Sorrow (Huzn).
103:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

103:1.arabic: ولنرجع إلى الغرض المطلوب فالمقصود أن غرور الشيطان بأن الآخرة شك يدفع إما بيقين تقليدي، وأما ببصيرة ومشاهدة من جهة الباطن، والمؤمنين بألسنتهم وبعقائدهم إذا ضيعوا أوامر الله تعالى وهجروا الأعمال الصالحة ولابسوا الشهوات والمعاصي فهم مشاركون للكفار في هذا الغرور من النار ولو بعد حين، ولكنهم أيضاً من المغرورين فإنهم اعترفوا بأن الآخرة خير من الدنيا ولكنهم مالوا إلى الدنيا وآثروها، ومجرد الإيمان لا يكفي للفوز قال تعالى "وإني لغفار لمن تاب وآمن وعمل صالحاً ثم اهتدى" وقال تعالى "إن رحمت الله قريب من الم
103:1.english: And let us return to the intended purpose, so the intended meaning is that the deception of Satan that the Hereafter is doubt is repelled either by traditional certainty, or by insight and witnessing from the aspect of the inner dimension, and the believers with their tongues and with their beliefs if they neglect the commands of Allah the Exalted and abandon righteous works and associate with desires and disobediences, they are partners with the disbelievers in this deception from the Fire even if after a while, but they are also among the deceived for they acknowledged that the Hereafter is better than the worldly life but they inclined to the worldly life and preferred it, and mere faith is not sufficient for success. Allah the Exalted said: "And indeed, I am Forgiving to whoever repents and believes and does righteous work then is guided" and Allah the Exalted said: "Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the doers of good" then the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Excellence (Ihsan) is that you worship Allah as if you see Him"[5] and Allah the Exalted said: "By the time (Al-Asr), indeed, mankind is in loss, except those who have believed and done righteous works and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience." So the promise of forgiveness in all the Book of Allah the Exalted is conditional upon faith and righteous work together, not upon faith alone, so these are also deceived, I mean those who are content with the worldly life, joyful in it, luxuriating in its pleasures, loving it. Those who hate death fearing the loss of the delights of the worldly life, not those who hate it fearing what comes after it, so this is an example of deception by the worldly life from the disbelievers and the believers altogether.
103:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Delusion'

103:1.arabic: وأما المعتزلة فشبهتهم قوله تعالى: ﴿ وإني لغفار لمن تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا ثم اهتدى ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ والعصر إن الإنسان لفي خسر إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى ﴿ وإن منكم إلا واردها كان على ربك حتما مقضيا ﴾ {} ثم قال: ﴿ ثم ننجي الذين اتقوا ﴾ {} وقوله تعالى: ﴿ ومن يعص الله ورسوله فإن له نار جهنم ﴾ {} وكل آية ذكر الله عز وجل العمل الصالح فيها مقرونا بالإيمان
103:1.english: As for the Mu'tazilites, their evidence is His saying, the Exalted: 'Indeed, I am Forgiving to whoever repents and believes and does righteous deeds then remains guided' and His saying, the Exalted: 'By the Time (Al-'Asr), indeed, the human being (Al-Insan) is in loss (Khusr) except those who have believed and done righteous deeds' and His saying, the Exalted: 'And there is none of you except he will enter it; it has been upon your Lord a decree determined' then He said: 'Then We will save those who feared (Allah) (Ittaqaw)' and His saying, the Exalted: 'And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, then indeed, for him is the Fire of Hell' and every verse in which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, mentions righteous deeds (Al-'Amal Al-Salih) therein coupled with faith (Al-Iman).
103:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Foundations of Belief'

103:1.arabic: وإن الله عز وجلّ قال: ﴿ والعصر إن الإنسان لفي خسر إلا الذين آمنوا ﴾{} إلى آخرها وإن الأمور تجري بإذن الله فلا يحملنكم استبطاء أمر على استعجاله فإن الله عز وجل لا يعجل لعجلة أحد ومن غالب الله غلبه ومن خادع الله خدعه
103:1.english: And Allah the Exalted said: 'By the time (Al-Asr), indeed, mankind is in loss (Khusr), except those who have believed (Amanu)' to its end. And matters proceed by the permission of Allah, so do not let the delay of a matter lead you to hasten it, for Allah the Exalted does not hasten for anyone's haste, and whoever contends with Allah is overcome, and whoever deceives Allah is deceived.
103:1.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Book of Repentance'

104:1.arabic: قال الله تعالى "هماز مشاء بنميم" ثم قال "عتل بعد ذلك زنيم" قال عبد الله بن المبارك: الزنيم ولد الزنا الذي لا يكتم الحديث، وأشار به إلى أن كل من لم يكتم الحديث ومشى بالنميمة دل على أنه ولد زنا استنباطاً من قوله عز وجل "عتل بعد ذلك زنيم" والزنيم هو الدعى وقال تعالى "ويل لكل همزة لمزة" قيل الهمزة: النمام، وقال تعالى "حمالة الحطب" قيل إنها كانت نمامة حمالة للحديث وقال تعالى "فخانتاهما فلم يغنيا عنهما من الله شيئاً" قيل كانت امرأة لوط تخبر بالضيفان وامرأة نوح تخبر أنه مجنون وقد قال ﭬ "لا يدخل الجنة ن
104:1.english: Allah the Exalted said: "A slanderer, going about with calumny" then said: "Surly, after that, a bastard." Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: The bastard (Zanim) is the child of fornication who does not conceal speech, and he indicated by this that everyone who does not conceal speech and goes about with talebearing shows that he is a child of fornication, derived from His saying the Exalted: "Surly, after that, a bastard" and the bastard (Zanim) is the one claimed [as son]. And He the Exalted said: "Woe to every slanderer, fault-finder" it was said the slanderer (Humazah): the talebearer (Nammam), and He the Exalted said: "Bearer of firewood" it was said she was a talebearer (Nammamah), bearer of speech, and He the Exalted said: "So they betrayed them, and they availed them not against Allah aught" it was said the wife of Lot informed about the guests and the wife of Noah informed that he was mad. And he ﭬ said: "The talebearer (Nammam) does not enter Paradise"[229] and in another hadith: "The talebearer (Qatat) does not enter Paradise" and the talebearer (Qatat) is the talebearer (Nammam).
104:1.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

104:1.arabic: وعن مجاهد أنه قال في "ويل لكل همزة لمزة" الهمزة: الطعان في الناس، واللمزة: الذي يأكل لحوم الناس.
104:1.english: And from Mujahid, he said regarding "Woe to every slanderer and backbiter (Quran 104:1)": The slanderer (Al-Hammaz): The one who reviles people, and the backbiter (Al-Lummaz): The one who eats the flesh of people.
104:1.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Condemnation of Anger and Hatred'

104:6.arabic: أما بعد فإن الغضب شعلة نار اقتبست من نار الله الموقدة التي تطلع على الأفئدة، وإنها لمستكنة في طي الفؤاد. استكنان الجمر تحت الرماد، ويستخرجها الكبر الدفين في قلب كل جبار عنيد، كاستخراج الحجر النار من الحديد، وقد انكشف للناظرين بنور اليقين، أن الإنسان ينزع منه عرق إلى الشيطان اللعين، فمن استفزته نار الغضب فقد قويت فيه قرابة الشيطان حيث قال "خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين" فإن شأن الطين السكون والوقار، وشأن النار التلظي والاستعار، والحركة والاضطراب، ومن نتائج الغضب الحقد والحسد، وبهما هلك من هلك وفسد
104:6.english: Now then, indeed anger is a flame of fire kindled from the Fire of Allah (Nār Allāh) the Kindled (al-Mūqadah) which rises over the hearts (al-af'idah), and indeed it is hidden in the recess of the heart (al-fu'ād). It is the concealment of embers beneath ashes, and it is extracted by the hidden arrogance in the heart (qalb) of every obstinate tyrant, like extracting fire from stone with iron. And it has been revealed to those who see with the light of certainty (yaqīn), that from man extends a vein to the accursed Satan (al-Shayṭān al-la'īn). So whoever is provoked by the fire of anger has strengthened in him the kinship of Satan, where he said: "You created me from fire and created him from clay." For the nature of clay is stillness and dignity, and the nature of fire is blazing and flaming, and movement and agitation. And from the results of anger are malice (al-ḥiqd) and envy (al-ḥasad), and by them perished whoever perished and corrupted whoever corrupted. And their source is a morsel (muḍghah) that if it becomes sound, the entire body becomes sound with it. And if malice, envy, and anger are among what drives the servant (al-'abd) to places of destruction, then how much he needs to know their harms and evils! So that he may beware of that and guard against it, and remove it from the heart (qalb) if it exists and expel it, and treat it if it becomes firmly rooted in his heart (qalb) and cure it. For whoever does not know evil falls into it, and whoever knows it, knowledge alone does not suffice him, unless he knows the path by which he repels evil and drives it away.
104:6.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Envy'

104:7.arabic: والأخلاق السيئة هي السموم القاتلة والمهلكات الدامغة والمخازي الفاضحة والرذائل الواضحة والخبائث المبعدة عن جوار رب العالمين، المنخرطة بصاحبها في سلك الشياطين، وهي الأبواب المفتوحة إلى نار الله تعالى الموقدة التي تطلع على الأفئدة، كما أن الأخلاق الجميلة هي الأبواب المفتوحة من القلب إلى نعيم الجنان وجوار الرحمن، والأخلاق الخبيثة أمراض القلوب وأسقام النفوس إلا أنه مرض يفوت حياة الأبد، وأين منه المرض الذي لا يفوت إلا حياة الجسد؟
104:7.english: And bad character traits are the killing poisons, the destructive calamities, the exposing disgraces, the clear vices, and the evils that distance from the proximity of the Lord of the Worlds, entangled with their possessor in the chain of the devils, and they are the open doors to the Fire of Allah the Exalted, the kindled one that looks upon the hearts (Al-Af'idah), just as beautiful character traits are the open doors from the heart (Qalb) to the bliss of Paradise and the proximity of the Most Merciful, and evil character traits are diseases of the hearts (Qulub) and ailments of the souls (Nufus) except that it is a disease that causes the loss of eternal life, and how far is it from the disease that only causes the loss of bodily life?
104:7.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Breaking the Two Desires'

105:1.arabic: وهذه القصص وردت في القرآن لتعرف بها سنة الله في عباده الذي خلوا من قبل، فما في القرآن شيء إلا وهو هدى ونور وتعرف من الله تعالى إلى خلقه، فتارة يتعرف إليهم بالتقديس فيقول: " قل هو الله أحد الله الصمد لم يلد ولم يولد ولم يكن له كفواً أحد " وتارة يتعرف إليهم بصفات جلاله فيقول: " الملك القدوس السلام المؤمن المهيمن العزيز الجبار المتكبر " وتارة يتعرف إليهم في أفعاله المخوفة والمرجوة فيتلو عليهم سنته في أعدائه وفي أنبيائه فيقول: " ألم تر كيف فعل ربك بعاد إرم ذات العماد - ألم تر كيف فعل ربك بأصحاب الفي
105:1.english: And these stories have come in the Quran so that you may know through them the Way (Sunnah) of Allah in His servants who have passed before. There is nothing in the Quran except that it is guidance and light and a recognition from Allah the Exalted to His creation. At times He makes Himself known to them through Sanctification (Taqdis) when He says: "Say: He is Allah, the One, Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born, nor is there to Him any equivalent." And at times He makes Himself known to them through His attributes of Majesty (Jalal) when He says: "The Sovereign, the Holy, the Peace, the Faithful, the Overseer, the Exalted in Might, the Compeller, the Superior." And at times He makes Himself known to them in His actions that are feared and hoped for, and He recites to them His Way (Sunnah) regarding His enemies and His prophets when He says: "Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with 'Aad of Iram - of the great pillars? Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?"
105:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

107:4.arabic: اعلم أن الرياء حرام والمرائي عند الله ممقوت، وقد شهدت لذلك الآيات والأخبار والآثار. أما الآيات: فقوله تعالى "فويل للمصلين الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون الذين هم يراءون" وقوله عز وجل "والذين يمكرون السيئات لهم عذاب شديد ومكر أولئك هو يبور" قال مجاهد هم أهل الرياء. وقال تعالى "إنما نعطمكم لوجه الله لا نريد منكم جزاء ولا شكورا" فمدح المخلصين ينفي كل إرادة سوى وجه الله، والرياء ضده وقال تعالى "فمن كان يرجو لقاء ربه فليعمل صالحاً ولا يشرك بعبادة ربه أحدا" نزل بعد ذلك فيمن يطلب الأجر والحمد بعباداته وأعمال
107:4.english: Know that hypocrisy (Riya') is forbidden and the hypocrite (Mura'i) is detested by Allah, and the verses, reports, and traditions testify to that. As for the verses: then His saying, the Exalted, "So woe to those who pray, who are heedless of their prayer, who make show (of their deeds)" and His saying, the Mighty and Majestic, "And those who plot evil deeds, for them is a severe punishment, and the plotting of those, it will perish" said Mujahid: they are the people of hypocrisy (Riya'). And He said, the Exalted, "We feed you only for the Face (Wajh) of Allah. We wish no reward nor thanks from you" so He praised the sincere ones (Mukhlisin) by negating every intention (Iradah) except the Face (Wajh) of Allah, and hypocrisy (Riya') is its opposite. And He said, the Exalted, "So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone" it was revealed after that concerning those who seek reward and praise with their acts of worship and deeds.
107:4.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Condemnation of Status and Ostentation'

107:5.arabic: وسئل أبو العالية عن قوله تعالى: ﴿ الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون ﴾ قال هو الذي يسهو في صلاته فلا يدري على كم ينصرف أعلى شفع أم على وتر. وقال الحسن: هو الذي يسهو عن وقت الصلاة حتى تخرج. وقال بعضهم: هو الذي إن صلاها في أول الوقت لم يفرح وإن أخرها عن الوقت لم يحزن فلا يرى تعجيلها خيرا ولا تأخيرا إثما.
107:5.english: And Abu Al-'Aliyah was asked about the saying of Allah the Exalted: 'Those who are heedless (Sahoon) of their prayer' (Quran 107:5). He said: 'It is the one who is heedless (Yas-haw) in his prayer, so he does not know upon how many he concludes - upon an even (Shaf') or upon an odd (Watr).' And Al-Hasan said: 'It is the one who is heedless (Yas-haw) of the time of prayer until it passes.' And some of them said: 'It is the one who, if he prays it at the beginning of its time, does not rejoice, and if he delays it beyond its time, does not grieve, so he does not see hastening it as good nor delaying it as sin.'
107:5.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

109:1.arabic: ولمن يتردد في استيقاظه تلطف استحسنه بعض العلماء وهو أن يصلي بعد الوتر ركعتين جالسا على فراشه عند النوم كان رسول الله ﷺ يزحف إلى فراشه ويصليهما ويقرأ فيهما إذا زلزلت وألهاكم لما فيهما من التحذير والوعيد وفي رواية قل يا أيها الكافرون لما فيها من التبرئة وإفراد العبادة لله تعالى فقيل إن استيقظ قامتا مقام ركعة واحدة وكان له أن يوتر بواحدة في آخر صلاة الليل وكأنه صار ما مضى شفعا بهما وحسن استئناف الوتر واستحسن هذا أبو طالب المكي وقال فيه ثلاثة أعمال قصر الأمل وتحصيل الوتر والوتر آخر الليل وهو كماذكره
109:1.english: For one who hesitates in awakening, a gentle practice that some scholars considered good is to pray after the Witr (odd-numbered prayer) two rak'ahs sitting on his bed at sleep time. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) would crawl to his bed and pray them and recite in them 'When the earth is shaken' (Surah Al-Zalzalah) and 'The mutual rivalry diverts you' (Surah At-Takathur) because of the warning and threat in them. And in a narration, 'Say: O you who disbelieve' (Qul ya ayyuha al-kafirun) because of the disavowal and singling out worship for Allah alone in it. So it was said: If he awakens, they stand in place of one rak'ah, and he could perform Witr with one in the last night prayer, and it is as if what passed became even-numbered with them, and renewing the Witr is good. Abu Talib al-Makki considered this good and said in it are three deeds: shortening hope, securing the Witr, and the Witr at the end of the night, as mentioned. But perhaps it occurs that if they made even what passed, it would be likewise, and if he does not awaken and invalidates his first Witr, then its being even-numbered if he awakens is not even-numbered if he sleeps, so there is consideration in this unless it is confirmed from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) his performing Witr before them and repeating the Witr, from which it is understood that the two rak'ahs are even-numbered in their form and odd-numbered in their meaning, so it is counted as Witr if he does not awaken and even-numbered if he awakens.
109:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Book of Knowledge'

109:1.arabic: وكان العلماء يجعلونها ستا فيزيدون سبح اسم ربك الأعلى إذ في الخبر (أنه ﷺ كان يحب سبح اسم ربك الأعلى، وكان يقرأ في ثلاث ركعات الوتر ثلاث سور سبح اسم ربك الأعلى وقل يا أيها الكافرون والإخلاص فإذا فرغ قال سبحان الملك القدوس ثلاث مرات).
109:1.english: And the scholars would make them six by adding 'Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High' (Surah Al-A'la) since in the report (that he ﷺ loved 'Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High', and he would recite in the three rak'ahs of Witr three surahs: 'Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High' and 'Say: O you who disbelieve' (Surah Al-Kafirun) and 'Say: He is Allah, the One' (Surah Al-Ikhlas). When he finished, he would say 'Glory be to the King, the Holy' three times).
109:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

109:1.arabic: السادس: إذا فرغ من ذلك ينبغي أن يصلي خلف المقام ركعتين يقرأ في الأولى قل يا أيها الكافرون وفي الثانية الإخلاص وهما ركعتا الطواف. قال الزهري مضت السنة أن يصلي لكل سبع ركعتين[46] وإن قرن بين أسابيع وصلى ركعتين جاز[47] فعل ذلك رسول الله ﭬ وكل أسبوع طواف وليدع بعد ركعتي الطواف وليقل اللهم يسر لي اليسرى وجنبني العسرى واغفر لي في الآخرة والأولى واعصمني بألطافك حتى لا أعصيك وأعني على طاعتك بتوفيقك وجنبني معاصيك واجعلني ممن يحبك ويحب ملائكتك ورسلك ويحب عبادك الصالحين اللهم حببني إلى ملائكتك ورسلك وإلى ع
109:1.english: Sixth: When he finishes that, he should pray behind the Maqam two rak'ahs; he recites in the first 'Say: O you who disbelieve' (Qul ya ayyuha al-kafirun) and in the second 'Sincerity' (Al-Ikhlas), and they are the two rak'ahs of the Tawaf. Al-Zuhri said: The Sunnah has passed that he prays for every seven two rak'ahs, and if he combines between circuits and prays two rak'ahs, it is permissible; the Messenger of Allah did that, and every circuit is a Tawaf. And let him supplicate after the two rak'ahs of Tawaf and say: O Allah, make easy for me the easy and keep me away from the difficult, and forgive me in the Hereafter and the first, and protect me with Your graces so that I do not disobey You, and help me in Your obedience with Your success, and keep me away from Your disobediences, and make me among those who love You and love Your angels and Your messengers and love Your righteous servants. O Allah, make me beloved to Your angels and Your messengers and to Your righteous servants. O Allah, just as You guided me to Islam, so make me firm upon it with Your graces and Your guardianship, and employ me for Your obedience and the obedience of Your messenger, and save me from the misguidances of trials. Then let him return to the Black Stone and touch it and conclude with it the Tawaf. He said: 'Whoever performs Tawaf around the House a circuit and prays two rak'ahs, for him is the reward like freeing a neck.' And this is the manner of Tawaf, and the obligatory from its totality after the conditions of prayer is that he completes the number of Tawaf seven with all the House, and that he begins with the Black Stone and makes the House on his left, and that he performs Tawaf inside the mosque and outside the House, not on the Shadharwan nor in the Hijr, and that he makes consecutive the circuits and does not separate them with a separation outside the customary, and what is besides this is Sunnahs and etiquettes.
109:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Mysteries of Hajj'

109:1.arabic: [195] حديث القراءة في المغرب ليلة الجمعة قل يا أيها الكافرون وقل هو الله أحد وفي عشائها الجمعة والمنافقين أخرجه ابن حبان والبيهقي من حديث سمرة وفي ثقات ابن حبان المحفوظ عن سماك مرسلا قلت لا يصح مسندا ولا مرسلا.
109:1.english: [195] The hadith about reciting in the Maghrib prayer on Friday night: 'Say (Qul) O you who disbelieve (ya ayyuha al-kafirun)' and 'Say (Qul) He is Allah, the One (huwa Allahu ahad)', and in its evening prayer: 'The Friday (al-Jumu'ah)' and 'The Hypocrites (al-Munafiqun)'. It was reported by Ibn Hibban and Al-Bayhaqi from the narration of Samurah, and in the reliable narrators of Ibn Hibban, it is preserved from Samak as a mursal (interrupted chain). I say: It is not authentic, neither with a connected chain (musnad) nor as an interrupted chain (mursal).
109:1.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'
Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Book of Knowledge'

110:3.arabic: قال عز وجل: ﴿ والذين إذا فعلوا فاحشة أو ظلموا أنفسهم ذكروا الله فاستغفروا لذنوبهم ﴾ {} وقال علقمة والأسود قال عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنهم في كتاب الله عز وجل آيتان ما أذنب عبد ذنبا فقرأهما واستغفر الله عز وجل إلا غفر الله تعالى له: ﴿ والذين إذا فعلوا فاحشة أو ظلموا أنفسهم ﴾ {} الآية وقوله عز وجل: ﴿ ومن يعمل سوءا أو يظلم به ثم يستغفر الله يجد الله غفورا رحيما ﴾ {} وقال عز وجل: ﴿ فسبح بحمد ربك واستغفره إنه كان توابا ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ والمستغفرين بالأسحار ﴾ {} وكان ﭬ يكثر أن يقول (سبحانك اللهم
110:3.english: Allah the Exalted said: 'And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins' {}. And 'Alqamah and Al-Aswad said: 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with them, said: In the Book of Allah the Exalted are two verses: No servant commits a sin then recites them and seeks forgiveness from Allah the Exalted except that Allah the Exalted forgives him: 'And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves' {} the verse, and His saying the Exalted: 'And whoever does evil or wrongs himself then seeks forgiveness from Allah will find Allah Forgiving, Merciful' {}. And He the Exalted said: 'So glorify with praise of your Lord and seek His forgiveness. Indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance' {}. And He the Exalted said: 'And those who seek forgiveness in the pre-dawn hours' {}. And He (the Prophet) ﷺ used to frequently say: 'Glory be to You, O Allah, and with Your praise. O Allah, forgive me. Indeed, You are the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful' [108]. And He ﷺ said: 'Whoever increases in seeking forgiveness, Allah the Exalted makes for him from every worry an opening and from every difficulty a way out and provides for him from where he does not expect' [109].
110:3.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith

111:1.arabic: وأما قولك لم تكنني فإن الله تعالى سمى أنبياءه وأولياءه فقال يا يحيى يا عيسى وكنى أعداءه فقال تبت يدا أبي لهب
111:1.english: And as for your statement that I did not use your kunya (honorific nickname), then indeed Allah the Exalted named His prophets and His allies (awliya) by saying 'O Yahya, O Isa,' and He used the kunya for His enemies by saying 'May the hands of Abu Lahab be ruined (tabbat yada abi lahab).'
111:1.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'The Lawful and Prohibited'

112:1.arabic: فتارة يتعرف إليهم بالتقديس فيقول: " قل هو الله أحد الله الصمد لم يلد ولم يولد ولم يكن له كفواً أحد " وتارة يتعرف إليهم بصفات جلاله فيقول: " الملك القدوس السلام المؤمن المهيمن العزيز الجبار المتكبر " وتارة يتعرف إليهم في أفعاله المخوفة والمرجوة فيتلو عليهم سنته في أعدائه وفي أنبيائه فيقول: " ألم تر كيف فعل ربك بعاد إرم ذات العماد - ألم تر كيف فعل ربك بأصحاب الفيل ". ولا يعدو القرآن هذه الأقسام الثلاثة وهي: الإرشاد إلى معرفة ذات الله وتقديسه، أو معرفة صفاته وأسمائه، أو معرفة أفعاله وسنته مع عباده،
112:1.english: And sometimes He makes Himself known to them through Sanctification (Taqdis) and says: "Say: He is Allah, the One, Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born, Nor is there to Him any equivalent." And sometimes He makes Himself known to them through the attributes of His Majesty and says: "The Sovereign, the Holy, the Peace, the Faithful, the Guardian, the Exalted in Might, the Compeller, the Superior." And sometimes He makes Himself known to them in His fearful and hoped-for actions, and He recites to them His established way (Sunnah) with His enemies and with His prophets, and says: "Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with 'Aad - [With] Iram - who had lofty pillars, The likes of whom had never been created in the land? And [with] Thamud, who carved out the rocks in the valley? And [with] Pharaoh, owner of the stakes? - [All of] whom oppressed within the lands And increased therein the corruption. So your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment. Indeed, your Lord is in observation." And the Quran does not exceed these three divisions, which are: Guidance to the knowledge of the Essence (Dhat) of Allah and His Sanctification (Taqdis), or knowledge of His attributes and His names, or knowledge of His actions and His established way (Sunnah) with His servants. And since Surah Al-Ikhlas contains one of these three divisions, which is Sanctification (Taqdis), the Messenger of Allah ﷺ equated it with a third of the Quran and said: "Whoever recites Surah Al-Ikhlas has recited a third of the Quran"[51] because the ultimate Sanctification (Taqdis) is to be One in three matters: He does not have from Him one who is His equal and likeness, and His statement "He neither begets" indicates this; and He is not from one who is His equal and likeness, and His statement "nor is born" indicates this; and there is not in His rank, even if not being an origin for Him nor a branch, one who is like Him, and His statement: "Nor is there to Him any equivalent" indicates this. And all of that is gathered by His statement, the Exalted: "Say: He is Allah, the One" and its totality is the elaboration of the statement "There is no deity except Allah." These are the secrets of the Quran, and the likes of these secrets do not end.
112:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

112:1.arabic: ولما اشتملت سورة الإخلاص على أحد هذه الأقسام الثلاثة وهو التقديس وازنها رسول الله ﭬ بثلث القرآن فقال: "من قرأ سورة الإخلاص فقد قرأ ثلث القرآن"[51] لأن منتهى التقديس أن يكون واحداً في ثلاثة أمور، لا يكون حاصلاً منه من هو نظيره وشبهه، ودل عليه قوله " لم يلد " ولا يكون حاصلاً ممن هو نظيره وشبهه، ودل عليه قوله " ولم يولد " ولا يكون في درجته وإن لم يكن أصلاً له ولا فرعاً من هو مثله، ودل عليه قوله: " ولم يكن له كفواً أحد " ويجمع جميع ذلك قوله تعالى: " قل هو الله أحد " وجملته تفصيل قول " لا إله إلا الل
112:1.english: And since Surah Al-Ikhlas contains one of these three divisions, which is Sanctification (Taqdis), the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) equated it with one-third of the Quran, saying: 'Whoever recites Surah Al-Ikhlas has recited one-third of the Quran' [51] because the ultimate Sanctification (Taqdis) is to be One (Ahad) in three matters: there is no one who is His equal and likeness originating from Him, and this is indicated by His saying 'He begets not'; and there is no one who is His equal and likeness originating from whom He originates, and this is indicated by His saying 'nor is He begotten'; and there is no one who is His equal in rank, even if not being an origin for Him nor a branch, and this is indicated by His saying: 'And there is none comparable to Him.' And all of that is gathered by His saying, the Exalted: 'Say: He is Allah, the One (Ahad).' And its entirety is the elaboration of the statement 'There is no god but Allah.' These are the secrets (Asrar) of the Quran, and the likes of these secrets in the Quran are endless, 'nor is there anything fresh or dry but is in a Clear Book.' Therefore, Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Illuminate the Quran and seek its wonders, for in it is the knowledge of the former and the latter, and it is as he said. And none knows it except one who has prolonged in pondering its individual words, and his intellect (Fikr) has become pure for his understanding (Fahm) of it, until every word of it testifies to him that it is the speech of a Mighty (Jabbar), Subduing (Qahir), Sovereign (Malik), Powerful (Qadir), and that it is beyond the limit of human capability.
112:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

112:1.arabic: وقال ﭬ: (من صلى المغرب في جماعة ثم صلى بعدها ركعتين ولم يتكلم بشيء فيما بين ذلك من أمر الدنيا ويقرأ في الركعة الأولى فاتحة الكتاب وعشر آيات من أول سورة البقرة وآيتين من وسطها وإلهكم إله واحد لا إله إلا هو الرحمن الرحيم إن في خلق السموات والأرض إلى آخر الآية وقل هو الله أحد خمس عشرة مرة ثم يركع ويسجد فإذا قام في الركعة الثانية قرأ فاتحة الكتاب وآية الكرسي وآيتين بعدها إلى قوله أولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون وثلاث آيات من آخر سورة البقرة من قوله لله ما في السموات وما في الأرض إلى آخرها وقل هو ال
112:1.english: And he (the Prophet) said: 'Whoever prays Maghrib in congregation then prays after it two rak'ahs and does not speak anything between them from worldly matters, and recites in the first rak'ah: The Opening (Al-Fatihah) of the Book and ten verses from the beginning of Surah Al-Baqarah and two verses from its middle: "And your God is One God, there is no god but He, the Most Merciful (Ar-Rahman), the Most Compassionate (Ar-Rahim)" and "Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth" to the end of the verse, and "Say: He is Allah, the One (Ahad)" fifteen times, then bows and prostrates. When he stands in the second rak'ah, he recites: The Opening (Al-Fatihah) of the Book and the Throne Verse (Ayat al-Kursi) and two verses after it to His saying: "Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally" and three verses from the end of Surah Al-Baqarah from His saying: "To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth" to its end, and "Say: He is Allah, the One (Ahad)" fifteen times.' He described from its reward in the hadith what exceeds enumeration.
112:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on the diseases of the heart and their cure, from 'Book of Knowledge'

112:1.arabic: فقد روى عن وهيب بن الورد أنه قال إن من الدعاء الذي لا يرد أن يصلي العبد ثنتي عشرة ركعة يقرأ في كل ركعة بأم الكتاب وآية الكرسي وقل هو الله أحد فإذا فرغ خر ساجدا ثم قال سبحان الذي لبس العز وقال به سبحان الذي تعطف بالمجد وتكرم به سبحان الذي أحصى كل شيء بعلمه سبحان الذي لا ينبغي التسبيح إلا له سبحان ذي المن والفضل سبحان ذي العز والكرم سبحان ذي الطول أسألك بمعاقد العز من عرشك ومنتهى الرحمة من كتابك وباسمك الأعظم وجدك الأعلى وكلماتك التامات العامات التي لا يجاوزهن بر ولا فاجر أن تصلى على محمد وعلى آل
112:1.english: It has been narrated from Wahib ibn al-Ward that he said: Among the supplication (Dua) that is not rejected is that the servant (Abd) prays twelve units (Rak'ah), reciting in each unit the Mother of the Book (Umm al-Kitab) and the Throne Verse (Ayat al-Kursi) and 'Say: He is Allah, the One (Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad).' When he finishes, he falls prostrate (Sajda) and then says: 'Glory be to the One who wears majesty and says with it. Glory be to the One who wraps Himself in glory and honors with it. Glory be to the One who enumerates everything with His knowledge. Glory be to the One to whom glorification is not fitting except for Him. Glory be to the Possessor of favor and grace. Glory be to the Possessor of might and generosity. Glory be to the Possessor of abundance. I ask You by the bonds of might from Your Throne (Arsh) and the utmost of mercy from Your Book, and by Your Greatest Name (Ism al-A'zam) and Your Highest Majesty (Jadd al-A'la) and Your perfect, comprehensive words that no righteous or wicked one surpasses, that You send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad.' Then he asks for his need that contains no disobedience, and he is answered, if Allah the Exalted wills.
112:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

112:1.arabic: التاسع أن يراعى في قدوة الجمعة ما ذكرناه في غيرها فإذا سمع قراءة الإمام لم يقرأ سوى الفاتحة فإذا فرغ من الجمعة قرأ الحمد لله سبع مرات قبل أن يتكلم وقل هو الله أحد والمعوذتين سبعا سبعا وروى بعض السلف: أن من فعله عصم من الجمعة إلى الجمعة وكان حرزا له من الشيطان ويستحب أن يقول بعد الجمعة: اللهم يا غني يا حميد يا مبدىء يا معيد يا رحيم يا ودود أغنني بحلالك عن حرامك وبفضلك عمن سواك. يقال من داوم على هذا الدعاء أغناه الله سبحانه عن خلقه ورزقه من حيث لا يحتسب ثم يصلي بعد الجمعة ست ركعات.
112:1.english: Ninth: One should observe in the Friday prayer leader what we have mentioned in others. When he hears the Imam's recitation, he should not recite except the Opening (Al-Fatihah). When he finishes the Friday prayer, he should read 'Praise be to Allah' seven times before speaking, and 'Say: He is Allah, the One' (Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad) and the two seeking refuge surahs (Al-Mu'awwidhatayn) seven times each. Some of the predecessors (Salaf) narrated: Whoever does this is protected from one Friday to the next and it becomes a shield for him from Satan. It is recommended to say after the Friday prayer: O Allah, O Rich (Al-Ghani), O Praiseworthy (Al-Hamid), O Originator (Al-Mubdi'), O Restorer (Al-Mu'id), O Merciful (Al-Rahim), O Loving (Al-Wadud), enrich me with Your lawful provision over Your unlawful, and with Your bounty over whoever besides You. It is said: Whoever persists in this supplication, Allah the Exalted enriches him from His creation and provides for him from where he does not expect. Then he prays after the Friday prayer six units of prayer.
112:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

112:3.arabic: رواه عن النبي ﭬ أنه قال: (إن الله تعالى يمجد نفسه كل يوم ويقول إني أنا الله رب العالمين إني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا الحي القيوم إني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا العلي العظيم إني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا لم ألد ولم أولد إني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا العفو الغفور إني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا مبدىء كل شيء وإلي يعود العزيز الحكيم الرحمن الرحيم مالك يوم الدين خالق الخير والشر خالق الجنة والنار الواحد الأحد الفرد الصمد الذي لم يتخذ صاحبة ولا ولدا الفرد الوتر عالم الغيب والشهادة الملك القدوس السلام المؤمن المهي
112:3.english: It is narrated from the Prophet (peace be upon him) that he said: (Indeed, Allah the Exalted glorifies Himself every day and says: I am Allah, Lord of the worlds; I am Allah, there is no god but I, the Living, the Self-Sustaining; I am Allah, there is no god but I, the Most High, the Most Great; I am Allah, there is no god but I, I did not beget nor was I begotten; I am Allah, there is no god but I, the Pardoner, the Forgiving; I am Allah, there is no god but I, the Originator of every thing and to Me it returns, the Mighty, the Wise, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, Master of the Day of Judgment, Creator of good and evil, Creator of Paradise and Hell, the One, the Unique, the Single, the Eternal, who has not taken a companion nor a son, the Single, the Odd, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the King, the Holy, the Peace, the Faithful, the Guardian, the Mighty, the Compeller, the Majestic, the Creator, the Maker, the Fashioner, the Great, the Exalted, the Powerful, the Subduer, the Forbearing, the Generous, Possessor of praise and glory, Knower of the secret and the more hidden, the Able, the Provider, above the creation and the creatures[135]). And He mentioned before every word 'I am Allah, there is no god but I' as we have brought it in the first. So whoever supplicates with these names, let him say: You are Allah, there is no god but You, such and such. So whoever supplicates with them is written among the prostrating, the humble ones who will be neighbors to Muhammad, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and the prophets (prayers of Allah be upon them) in the abode of majesty, and for him is the reward of the worshippers in the heavens and the earths. And may Allah bless Muhammad and every chosen servant.
112:3.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance

112:4.arabic: قرآن شيء إلا وهو هدى ونور وتعرف من الله تعالى إلى خلقه، فتارة يتعرف إليهم بالتقديس فيقول: "قل هو الله أحد الله الصمد لم يلد ولم يولد ولم يكن له كفواً أحد" وتارة يتعرف إليهم بصفات جلاله فيقول: "الملك القدوس السلام المؤمن المهيمن العزيز الجبار المتكبر" وتارة يتعرف إليهم في أفعاله المخوفة والمرجوة فيتلو عليهم سنته في أعدائه وفي أنبيائه فيقول: "ألم تر كيف فعل ربك بعاد إرم ذات العماد - ألم تر كيف فعل ربك بأصحاب الفيل". ولا يعدو القرآن هذه الأقسام الثلاثة وهي: الإرشاد إلى معرفة ذات الله وتقديسه، أو مع
112:4.english: The Quran is nothing except it is guidance and light and a making-known from Allah the Exalted to His creation, so at times He makes Himself known to them through sanctification (Taqdis) when He says: "Say: He is Allah, the One, Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born, nor is there to Him any equivalent (Kufuwan) one." And at times He makes Himself known to them through attributes of His majesty when He says: "The Sovereign, the Holy, the Peace, the Faithful, the Guardian, the Exalted in Might, the Compeller, the Superior." And at times He makes Himself known to them in His actions that are feared and hoped for, and He recites to them His way (Sunnah) with His enemies and with His prophets when He says: "Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with 'Aad - Iram of the pillars? Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?" And the Quran does not exceed these three divisions, which are: guidance to knowledge of the essence (Dhat) of Allah and His sanctification (Taqdis), or knowledge of His attributes and His names, or knowledge of His actions and His way (Sunnah) with His servants.
