And since Surah Al-Ikhlas contained one of these three divisions, which is sanctification (Taqdis), the Messenger of Allah ﷺ equated it with a third of the Quran, saying: "Whoever recites Surah Al-Ikhlas has recited a third of the Quran" because the utmost sanctification (Taqdis) is to be one in three matters: there is not originating from Him one who is His counterpart and likeness, and His statement "He neither begets" indicates this; and there is not originating from one who is His counterpart and likeness, and His statement "nor is born" indicates this; and there is not in His rank, even if not being an origin for Him nor a branch, one who is His like, and His statement indicates this: "nor is there to Him any equivalent (Kufuwan) one." And all of that is gathered by His statement the Exalted: "Say: He is Allah, the One" and its entirety is the detailing of the saying "There is no god but Allah." These are the secrets of the Quran, and examples of these secrets in the Quran do not end, "and not a moist thing nor a dry thing except in a clear Book." And for that reason Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Illuminate the Quran and seek its wonders, for in it is the knowledge of the first and the last, and it is as he said, and none knows it except one who prolonged in the individual words his thought (Fikr) and purified for it his understanding until every word of it testifies for him that it is the speech of a Compeller, a Subduer, a Sovereign, a Powerful, and that it is outside the limit of human capability.
112:4.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Love, Longing, Intimacy and Contentment'

113:1.arabic: الورد الأول: ما بين طلوع الصبح إلى طلوع الشمس وهو وقت شريف ويدل على شرفه وفضله إقسام الله تعالى به إذ قال: ﴿ والصبح إذا تنفس ﴾ {} وتمدحه به إذ قال: ﴿ فالق الإصباح ﴾ {} وقال تعالى: ﴿ قل أعوذ برب الفلق ﴾ {} وإظهاره القدرة بقبض الظل فيه إذ قال تعالى: ﴿ ثم قبضناه إلينا قبضا يسيرا ﴾ {} وهو وقت قبض ظل الليل ببسط نور الشمس وإرشاده الناس إلى التسبيح فيه بقوله تعالى: ﴿ فسبحان الله حين تمسون وحين تصبحون ﴾ {} وبقوله تعالى: ﴿ فسبح بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها ﴾ {} وقوله عز وجل: ﴿ ومن آناء الليل فسبح
113:1.english: The first devotional period (Wird): what is between the rising of dawn (Fajr) and the rising of the sun, and it is a noble time, and its nobility and merit are indicated by Allah the Exalted swearing by it when He said: 'By the morning when it breathes' (Quran 81:18), and praising it when He said: 'The Cleaver of the dawn' (Quran 6:96), and He said: 'Say, "I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak"' (Quran 113:1), and His manifestation of power in the contraction of the shadow therein when He said: 'Then We withdraw it to Us a gradual withdrawal' (Quran 25:46), and it is the time of contracting the shadow of the night by spreading the light of the sun, and His guiding people to glorification (Tasbīḥ) therein by His saying: 'So exalt Allah when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning' (Quran 30:17), and by His saying: 'So exalt Allah with praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting' (Quran 50:39), and His saying: 'And exalt Him during the night and at the ends of the day, that you may be satisfied' (Quran 20:130), and His saying: 'And remember the name of your Lord morning and evening' (Quran 76:25).
113:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

113:1.arabic: ليلة الأربعاء: روت فاطمة رضي الله عنها عن النبي ﭬ أنه قال: (من صلى ليلة الأربعاء ركعتين يقرأ في الأول فاتحة الكتاب وقل أعوذ برب الفلق عشر مرات وفي الثانية بعد الفاتحة قل أعوذ برب الناس عشر مرات ثم إذا سلم استغفر الله عشر مرات ثم يصلي على محمد ﭬ عشر مرات نزل من كل سماء سبعون ألف ملك يكتبون ثوابه إلى يوم القيامة[256])
113:1.english: Wednesday night: Fatimah (may Allah be pleased with her) narrated from the Prophet (peace be upon him) that he said: (Whoever prays on Wednesday night two units of prayer, recites in the first unit the Opening (Al-Fatihah) of the Book and 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the Daybreak (Qul A'udhu bi-Rabb al-Falaq)' ten times, and in the second unit after the Opening (Al-Fatihah) 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of Mankind (Qul A'udhu bi-Rabb al-Nas)' ten times, then when he gives the salutation (Salam) he seeks forgiveness (Istighfar) from Allah ten times, then sends prayers (Salah) upon Muhammad (peace be upon him) ten times, seventy thousand angels descend from every heaven writing his reward until the Day of Resurrection (Yawm al-Qiyamah)[256]).
113:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

113:1.arabic: أن تقول قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل انبساطها على الأرض وقبل الغروب سورة الحمد وقل أعوذ برب الناس وقل أعوذ برب الفلق وقل هو الله أحد وقل يا أيها الكافرون وآية الكرسي كل واحدة سبع مرات
113:1.english: That you say before sunrise and before it spreads over the earth and before sunset: Surah Al-Fatihah (The Opening) and 'Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind' and 'Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak' and 'Say: He is Allah, the One' and 'Say: O you disbelievers' and Ayat al-Kursi (The Throne Verse), each one seven times.
113:1.topic: Commentary from Al-Ghazali's Ihya 'Ulum al-Din, from 'Book of Knowledge'

113:2.arabic: أعوذ بكلمات الله التامات وأسمائه كلها من شر ما ذرأ وبرأ ومن شر كل ذي شر ومن شر كل دابة أنت آخذ بناصيتها إن ربي على صراط مستقيم أخرجه أبو الشيخ في كتاب الثواب من حديث عبد الرحمن بن عوف من قال حين يصبح أعوذ بكلمات التامات الله التي لا يجاوزهن بر ولا فاجر من شر ما خلق وبرأ وذرأ اعتصم من شر الثقلين الحديث وفيه وإن قالهن حين يمسي كن له كذلك حتى يصبح وفيه ابن لهيعة ولأحمد من حديث عبد الرحمن بن حسن في حديث إن جبريل قال يا محمد قل أعوذ بكلمات الله التامات من شر ما خلق وذرأ وبرأ ومن شر ما ينزل من السماء
113:2.english: I seek refuge in the complete words (Kalamat) of Allah and all His names from the evil (Sharr) of what He has created (Khalaqa) and brought forth, and from the evil of every possessor of evil, and from the evil of every creature (Dabbah) whose forelock You take hold of. Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path (Sirat Mustaqim). Abu al-Sheikh extracted it in the Book of Reward from the narration of Abd al-Rahman bin Awf: Whoever says when morning comes: 'I seek refuge in the complete words of Allah which no righteous or wicked person can surpass, from the evil of what He has created (Khalaqa) and brought forth and originated,' he is protected from the evil of the two weighty ones (Thaqalayn). In the narration: And if he says them when evening comes, it will be so for him until morning. And in it is Ibn Lahi'ah. And for Ahmad from the narration of Abd al-Rahman bin Hasan in the narration: Indeed, Gabriel said: O Muhammad, say: 'I seek refuge in the complete words of Allah from the evil of what He has created (Khalaqa) and originated and brought forth, and from the evil of what descends from the sky.' The narration, and its chain is good.
113:2.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication

113:3.arabic: وفي نوادر التفسير عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما (ومن شر غاسق إذا وقب) قال (قيام الذكر) وهذه يلية غالبة إذا هاجت لا يقاومها عقل ولا دين. وهي مع أنها صالحة لأن تكون باعثة على الحياتين كما سبق فهي أقوى آلة الشيطان على بني آدم وإليه أشار صلى الله عليه وسلم بقوله (ما رأيت من ناقصات عقل ودين أغلب لذوي الألباب منكن.)[27] وإنما ذلك لهيجان الشهوة.
113:3.english: And in the rare interpretations from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, regarding the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: 'And from the evil of the darkening (ghāsiq) when it settles (waqab)' (Quran 113:3), he said: 'The rising of the male organ (dhakar).' And this is a dominant affliction when it surges; neither intellect nor religion can resist it. And although it is suitable to be an incentive for both lives as previously mentioned, it is the strongest tool of Satan against the children of Adam, and to this the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, alluded in his saying: 'I have not seen anyone more overpowering to men of understanding than you women.'[27] And that is only due to the agitation of desire.
113:3.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Etiquette of Marriage'

113:3.arabic: الفائدة الثانية: بقاء النسل ودوام الوجود فهذه فائدتها. ولكن فيها من الآفات ما يهلك الدين والدنيا إن لم تضبط ولم تقهر ولم ترد إلى حد الاعتدال. وقد قيل في تأويل قوله تعالى "ربنا ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به" معناه شدة الغلبة، وعن ابن عباس: في قوله تعالى "ومن شر غاسق إذا وقب" قال: هو قيام الذكر. وقد أسنده بعض الرواة إلى رسول الله ﭬ إلا أنه قال في تفسيره: الذكر إذا دخل. وقد قيل: إذا قام ذكر الرجل ذهب ثلثا عقله"[55]. وكان ﭬ يقول في دعائه "اللهم إني أعوذ بك من شر سمعي وبصري وقلبي وهني ومني"[56] وقال ع
113:3.english: The second benefit: the preservation of progeny and the continuity of existence, this is its benefit. But in it are harms that destroy religion and the worldly life if it is not controlled, not subdued, and not returned to the limit of moderation. And it has been said in the interpretation of His saying, the Exalted, "Our Lord, do not burden us with what we have no strength for" its meaning is severe overpowering, and from Ibn Abbas: regarding His saying, the Exalted, "And from the evil of the darkening (ghāsiq) when it enters (waqab)" he said: it is the rising of the male organ (al-dhikr). And some narrators attributed it to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) except that he said in its interpretation: the male organ (al-dhikr) when it enters. And it has been said: when the male organ (dhikr) of a man rises, two-thirds of his intellect goes away. And he (peace be upon him) used to say in his supplication "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of my hearing and my sight and my heart (qalb) and my strength and my semen" and he (peace be upon him) said "Women are the snares of Satan and were it not for this desire, women would not have dominion over men."
113:3.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Harms of the Tongue'

113:3.arabic: [55] حديث ابن عباس موقوفا مسندا في قوله تعالى ومن شر غاسق إذا وقب قال هو قيام الذكر وقال الذي أسنده الذكر إذا دخل هذا حديث لا أصل له.
113:3.english: [55] A tradition from Ibn Abbas, stopped and transmitted in chain regarding His saying, the Exalted: 'And from the evil of the dark when it enters' - he said: It is the rising of the remembrance (Dhikr). And the one who transmitted it said: The remembrance (Dhikr) when it enters - this tradition has no origin.
113:3.topic: Prophetic traditions cited by Al-Ghazali with scholarly authentication, from 'Harms of the Tongue'

114:1.arabic: فإذا استوى قيامه واستقباله وإطراقه كذلك فليقرأ قل أعوذ برب الناس تحصنا به من الشيطان. ثم ليأت بالإقامة وإن كان يرجو حضور من يقتدي به فليؤذن أولا ثم ليحضر النية وهو أن ينوي في الظهر مثلا ويقول بقلبه أؤدي فريضة الظهر لله ليميزها بقوله أؤدي عن القضاء وبالفريضة عن النفل وبالظهر عن العصر وغيره ولتكن معاني هذه الألفاظ حاضرة في قلبه فإنه هو النية والألفاظ مذكرات وأسباب لحضورها.
114:1.english: If his standing, facing (the Qibla), and bowing his head have become balanced in this manner, then let him recite 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind (Qul a'udhu bi-rabbi al-nas)' as a fortification with it from Satan. Then let him come with the Iqamah (call to commence prayer), and if he hopes for the presence of someone who will follow him, let him give the Adhan (call to prayer) first. Then let him bring forth the intention (Niyyah), which is that he intends for the Dhuhr (noon prayer), for example, and says in his heart (Qalb): 'I perform the obligatory (Fard) prayer of Dhuhr for Allah,' to distinguish it by his saying 'I perform' from making up a missed prayer (Qada'), and by 'obligatory' from voluntary (Nafl), and by 'Dhuhr' from 'Asr (afternoon prayer) and others. And let the meanings of these words be present in his heart (Qalb), for that is the intention (Niyyah), and the words are reminders (Mudhakkirat) and causes for their presence.
114:1.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

114:1.arabic: وإن قرأ المسبعات العشر التي أهداها الخضر عليه السلام إلى إبراهيم التيمي رحمه الله ووصاه أن يقولها غدوة وعشية فقد استكمل الفضل وجمع له ذلك فضيلة جملة الأدعية المذكورة فقد روي عن كرز بن وبرة رحمه الله وكان من الأبدال قال أتاني أخ لي من أهل الشام فأهدى لي هدية وقال يا كرز اقبل مني هذه الهدية فإنها نعمت الهدية فقلت يا أخي ومن أهدى لك هذه الهدية قال أعطانيها إبراهيم التيمي قلت: أفلم تسأل إبراهيم من أعطاه إياها قال: كنت جالسا في فناء الكعبة وأنا في التهليل والتسبيح والتحميد والتمجيد فجاءني رجل فسلم عل
114:1.english: And if one recites the ten seven-times-repeated [verses] that Al-Khidr (peace be upon him) gifted to Ibrahim Al-Taymi (may Allah have mercy on him) and advised him to say them morning and evening, then he has attained complete virtue and gathered for himself the excellence of all the mentioned supplications. It has been narrated from Kurz ibn Wabrah (may Allah have mercy on him), who was among the Substitutes (Al-Abdal), that he said: A brother of mine from the people of Ash-Sham came to me and gifted me a gift and said: O Kurz, accept from me this gift, for it is an excellent gift. I said: O my brother, and who gifted you this gift? He said: Ibrahim Al-Taymi gave it to me. I said: Did you not ask Ibrahim who gave it to him? He said: I was sitting in the courtyard of the Kaaba while I was engaged in declaring the Oneness (At-Tahlil), glorification (At-Tasbih), praise (At-Tahmid), and magnification (At-Tamjid) of Allah. A man came to me, greeted me with peace, and sat to my right. I have never seen in my time anyone with a more beautiful face, nor more beautiful clothes, nor more intense whiteness, nor more pleasant fragrance than him. I said: O servant of Allah, who are you and from where have you come? He said: I am Al-Khidr. I said: For what have you come to me? He said: I have come to you to greet you with peace and out of love for you for the sake of Allah, and I have a gift I wish to present to you. I said: What is it? He said: That you say before the rising of the sun, before its spreading over the earth, and before sunset: Surah Al-Hamd (Al-Fatihah), and 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind (Qul A'udhu bi-Rabbi an-Nas)', and 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak (Qul A'udhu bi-Rabbi al-Falaq)', and 'Say: He is Allah, the One (Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad)', and 'Say: O you who disbelieve (Qul Ya Ayyuha al-Kafirun)', and the Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi), each one seven times. And you say: Glory be to Allah (Subhan Allah), and praise be to Allah (Al-Hamdu Lillah), and there is no god but Allah (La Ilaha Illa Allah), and Allah is the Greatest (Allahu Akbar) seven times. And you send prayers upon the Prophet (peace be upon him) seven times. And you seek forgiveness for yourself, your parents, the believing men, and the believing women seven times. And you say: O Allah, do with me and with them, immediately and later, in religion, this world, and the Hereafter, what You are worthy of, and do not do with us, O our Master, what we are worthy of, for You are Forgiving, Forbearing, Generous, Noble, Compassionate, Merciful seven times. And see that you do not abandon that morning and evening.
114:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on the virtue and practice of remembering God, from 'Book of Knowledge'

114:1.arabic: الثامن أن يقول في مبتدأ قراءته: أعوذ بالله السميع العليم من الشيطان الرجيم ﴿ رب أعوذ بك من همزات الشياطين وأعوذ بك رب أن يحضرون ﴾ {} وليقرأ قل أعوذ برب الناس وسورة الحمد لله وليقل عند فراغه من القراءة صدق الله تعالى وبلغ رسول الله ﭬ اللهم انفعنا به وبارك لنا فيه الحمد لله رب العالمين وأستغفر الله الحي القيوم.
114:1.english: The eighth [practice] is that he should say at the beginning of his recitation: 'I seek refuge with Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan (Shaytan).' 'My Lord (Rabb), I seek refuge with You from the whisperings of the devils (Shayateen), and I seek refuge with You, my Lord (Rabb), lest they be present with me.' And let him recite 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord (Rabb) of mankind' and the Chapter of Praise (Surah Al-Fatihah) for Allah. And let him say upon completing his recitation: 'Allah the Exalted has spoken the truth, and His Messenger has conveyed it. O Allah, benefit us by it and bless us in it. All praise is due to Allah, the Lord (Rabb) of the worlds, and I seek forgiveness from Allah, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining.'
114:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on supplications and their spiritual significance, from 'Etiquette of Quran Recitation'

114:1.arabic: من صلى ليلة الأربعاء ركعتين يقرأ في الأول فاتحة الكتاب وقل أعوذ برب الفلق عشر مرات وفي الثانية بعد الفاتحة قل أعوذ برب الناس عشر مرات ثم إذا سلم استغفر الله عشر مرات ثم يصلي على محمد ﭬ عشر مرات نزل من كل سماء سبعون ألف ملك يكتبون ثوابه إلى يوم القيامة
114:1.english: Whoever prays on Wednesday night two rak'ahs, recites in the first: The Opening (Al-Fatihah) of the Book and 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the Dawn (Qul A'udhu bi-Rabb al-Falaq)' ten times, and in the second after The Opening (Al-Fatihah): 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of Mankind (Qul A'udhu bi-Rabb al-Nas)' ten times, then when he gives the salutation (salam), seeks forgiveness (istighfar) from Allah ten times, then sends prayers (salawat) upon Muhammad ﷺ ten times, seventy thousand angels descend from every heaven writing his reward until the Day of Resurrection.
114:1.topic: Al-Ghazali on death, the grave, and preparation for the Hereafter, from 'Mysteries of Prayer'

114:4.arabic: وذكر الله هو الذي يؤمن جانبه ويعلم أنه ليس للشيطان فيه مجال ولا يعالج الشيء إلا بضده وضد جميع وساوس الشيطان ذكر الله بالاستعاذة والتبري عن الحول والقوة وهو معنى قولك أعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله العلي العظيم وذلك لا يقدر عليه إلا المتقون الغالب عليهم ذكر الله تعالى وإنما الشيطان يطوف عليهم في أوقات الفلتات على سبيل الخلسة قال الله تعالى أن الذين اتقوا إذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان تذكروا فإذا هم مبصرون وقال مجاهد في معنى قول الله تعالى من شر الوسواس الخناس قال هو منبسط على ا
114:4.english: And the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah is what secures its side and one knows that there is no opportunity for the Devil (Shaytan) in it, and a thing is not treated except by its opposite, and the opposite of all the whisperings (Waswas) of the Devil (Shaytan) is the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah through seeking refuge (Isti'adha) and disavowing power and strength, and that is the meaning of your saying: 'I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Devil (Shaytan)' and 'There is no power nor strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Most Great.' And that is not capable of it except the God-fearing (Muttaqun) upon whom the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah predominates. Indeed, the Devil (Shaytan) only circles around them in times of lapses (Falatat) by way of stealth. Allah the Exalted said: 'Indeed, those who fear Allah, when an impulse from the Devil (Shaytan) touches them, they remember, and at once they have insight.' And Mujahid said regarding the meaning of the saying of Allah the Exalted: 'From the evil of the whisperer (Waswas) who withdraws (Khannas),' he said: 'He is spread out upon the Heart (Qalb), so when Allah is remembered, he withdraws (Khannasa) and contracts, and when one is heedless, he spreads out upon his Heart (Qalb).' So the chasing away between the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah and the whispering (Waswas) of the Devil (Shaytan) is like the chasing away between light and darkness and between night and day. And due to their opposition, Allah the Exalted said: 'The Devil (Shaytan) has gained mastery over them and made them forget the Remembrance (Dhikr) of Allah.'
114:4.topic: Al-Ghazali's insights on the inner dimensions of faith, from 'Disciplining the Soul'
